title: Ownership and running-policy refusals keep --json and other presentation flags in fix_argv
description:
## Background

Every fix and alternative argv is meant to be runnable as-is and free of presentation flags: `src/cli.rs` `fix_argv` strips `--json`, `--robot`, `--format`, `--no-color`, `--progress` and the rest (`PRESENTATION_FLAGS`), and `with_target` uses it. Three refusal sites build their retry argv from the raw `ctx.argv` instead, so the presentation flags of the failing run are carried into `error.fix`/`error.fix_argv`:

- `src/engine/ownership.rs` `refusal()` (around line 261): the `--force` retry for `ownership_conflict` and `unmanaged_folder`;
- `src/engine/ownership.rs` `unmanaged_fix()` (around line 359);
- `src/engine/running.rs` (around line 153): the `--while-running` retry for `game_running`.

The fix becomes, for example, `omaddons install ./oldthing.zip -t retail --json --force`, while every other fix in the contract omits `--json`. The contract suite (`tests/contract/`) checks that each fix argv round-trips through shell quoting but not that presentation flags are absent, so this passed.

Found while auditing the CLI surface for the README rewrite.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. A target with an unmanaged folder `OldThing` in its AddOns.
2. `omaddons install ./OldThing -t retail --json`
3. `error.fix_argv` is `["omaddons","install","./OldThing","-t","retail","--json","--force"]`; expected `[..., "-t","retail","--force"]`.

The same with a running client and `remove` gives `--json --while-running`.

## Technical Approach

- Build every retry argv with `crate::cli::fix_argv(argv)` before pushing the extra flag, in all three sites.
- Grep `src/` for other `argv.to_vec()` / `ctx.argv.to_vec()` sites that build a `Suggestion::command` and route them through the same helper.
- Contract suite: assert that no `fix_argv`, `alternatives[].argv` or `commands[].argv` contains a presentation flag, for every envelope it already produces.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `fix_argv` for `ownership_conflict`, `unmanaged_folder` and `game_running` contains no presentation flag, under `--json`, `--robot`, `--format json` and `--no-color`.
- A contract-suite assertion fails if any suggestion argv in any envelope carries a presentation flag.
- `argc gate` passes, with any affected contract snapshots updated.

## Test Plan

- Unit: the three refusals built from an argv containing `--json --no-color` yield fixes without them.
- Contract: the new presentation-flag assertion over the whole matrix.
- Contract: the `remove` while-running case (fake `/proc`) and an unmanaged-folder install under `--json`.

## Considerations

- The human fix string is built from the same argv, so it also changes; that is intended.
- Keep the corrected-token behavior of `fix_argv_keeping` intact.
acceptance_criteria: fix_argv for ownership_conflict, unmanaged_folder and game_running carries no presentation flag; a contract assertion rejects presentation flags in every suggestion argv; argc gate passes
close_reason: Refusal retries no longer carry the failing run's presentation flags

comments.author: CrimsonJasper
comments.text: done: the --force retry of ownership refusals (engine::ownership::refusal), the --while-running retry (engine::running) and the same-name takeover refusal (engine::plan::takeover_refused, a fourth site this bead did not list) build their argv with cli::fix_argv; sync's settle_failures compares against the same stripped argv so its install --force rewrite still fires. The contract harness now asserts that no fix, alternative or commands[] argv in any envelope carries --json, --robot, --format, --progress, --no-color or --no-progress; the install_unmanaged snapshot had pinned the bug (its --force alternative carried --json) and is updated. Unit tests in ownership.rs and running.rs build the refusals from an argv with --json --no-color / --json --format json. README Known issues line removed. (unmanaged_fix, named in the bead, no longer builds an argv: the adopt fix replaced it.)

title: A timed-out Omarchy tool's children keep running
description:
## Background

`src/omarchy/shell.rs` runs Omarchy's own tools (`omarchy-plugin-validate`, `omarchy-shell`, `omarchy-bar`, `omarchy-plugin-disable`) with `OMARCHY_COMMAND_TIMEOUT` (10 s; the ping 2 s), and on timeout it kills the child with `child.kill()`: the direct process only. These tools are shell scripts that start children (`jq`, `find`, `hyprctl`), which keep running after the kill when the script hangs. The git subprocess (`src/sources/git_hosts.rs`) runs in its own process group and kills the group. Found by G2 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.7.2`).

## Steps to Reproduce

1. A stub `omarchy-plugin-validate` on `PATH` that runs `sleep 30 &` and then `sleep 30` (a child that outlives the script's kill).
2. `omaddons omarchy install --dry-run` with `PATH` holding that stub (as `tests/omarchy.rs` does).
3. After omaddons returns, the background `sleep` is still running.

## Technical Approach

- Start each Omarchy tool in its own process group (`process_group(0)`, as `git_hosts.rs` does) and kill the group on timeout, SIGTERM then SIGKILL after a short grace, reaping the child.
- Keep the user's environment (M3-D6: the tools need the desktop session's variables).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A timed-out Omarchy tool leaves no process of its group behind.
- The existing `tests/omarchy.rs` scenes (hang, silent, ok) pass, with the ping still bounded at 2 s.

## Test Plan

- `tests/omarchy.rs`: a stub that forks a long-lived child and hangs; after the command returns, no process of that group exists (check by a pid file the stub writes).

## Considerations

- `tests/single_writer.rs` names this module as a subprocess starter; its reason text stays accurate.
acceptance_criteria: A timed-out Omarchy tool leaves no process of its group behind; tests/omarchy.rs scenes pass with the ping bounded at 2 s.
close_reason: Omarchy tools run in their own process group; a timeout stops the group (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after OMARCHY_KILL_GRACE) and reaps it

comments.author: FierceWren
comments.text: claim: src/omarchy/shell.rs process groups; tests/omarchy.rs

comments.author: FierceWren
comments.text: done: argc gate passed; tests/omarchy.rs a_timed_out_tool_leaves_no_process_of_its_own_behind (fails on the old kill), ping still 2-5 s · found: none

title: Test: errors dismiss reports each read warning once when a database moves while it waits
description:
## Background
`errors dismiss` (`dismiss` in `src/app/errors.rs`) observes each client's BugGrabber databases, checks `--if-match`, then takes the global lock. If a database file changed while it waited (the game ended a session), it observes again under the lock and binds to that. The re-observation used to append its read warnings to the list that already held the first read's warnings, so every read warning (an unreadable database, a truncated walk) was reported twice. The review pass made it truncate back to the warnings from before the first read, then re-observe. No test covers the path: it only runs when a file moves between the first look and the lock.

## Technical Approach
- Add a failpoint in `dismiss` between the first `observe` and `GlobalLock::acquire`, for example `failpoint::hit("errors.dismiss.observed")`. Failpoints already pause and resume through marker files (`<name>.reached`, `<name>.resume`); see `tests/fsx_lock.rs` (`spawn_holder`) and `tests/engine_concurrency.rs` (`Pause`).
- Integration test: a client with a BugGrabber database that yields one read warning (for example, a second account's database that does not parse). Spawn `omaddons errors dismiss --json` with `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS=errors.dismiss.observed=pause`. When it reaches the failpoint, rewrite the readable database with one more session, then resume.
- Expect exit 0, the read warning exactly once in `warnings`, and the dismissal bound to the rewritten file (`targets[].errors` counts the added session's errors).

## Acceptance Criteria
- The re-observe path is exercised by a test that changes a database while `dismiss` waits.
- Each read warning appears once in the envelope.
- Removing the `warnings.truncate(before_read)` line makes the test fail (checked by hand once, noted in the close reason).

## Test Plan
- Integration: the paused dismiss above.
- Also assert that `--if-match` with the first read's token is refused (`plan_stale`) after the file moved, since the re-observation is checked again.

## Considerations
- The failpoint name joins the documented failpoint list if there is one (grep `failpoint::hit` and the failpoint docs in the vision bead).
- Use the file stamp the code compares (`FileStamp`): the rewrite must change size or mtime, so write different content rather than touching the same bytes.
acceptance_criteria: A test rewrites a BugGrabber database while dismiss is paused before the lock; the envelope holds each read warning once and the dismissal binds to the rewritten file; the test fails without warnings.truncate(before_read).
close_reason: Failpoint errors.dismiss.observed (src/app/errors.rs, after the first read and its --if-match check, before the lock). tests/errors_dismiss.rs a_session_ending_while_a_dismissal_waits_is_read_again: a first-read token is refused as plan_stale (details.changed observed) when the file moves meanwhile; without a token the dismissal binds to the rewritten file (session 12, 3 new errors where the first look had 2) and a second account's partial database is warned about once. Acceptance note: that test alone cannot fail without warnings.truncate(before_read), because the read also notes its warnings and the envelope de-duplicates against the notes; the companion test from omad-he63 (a database finished while the dismissal waits) fails without the truncate, checked by hand. argc gate passed.

comments.author: PlushDelta
comments.text: claim: src/app/errors.rs (a pause failpoint between the first read and the lock), tests/errors_dismiss.rs. Noted before starting: observe() also puts each read's warnings into ctx.notes, which emit_to merges first and de-duplicates, so a warning only the first read had may still reach the envelope after the re-read; testing that case too

comments.author: PlushDelta
comments.text: done: re-read path pinned with a pause failpoint; the truncate is pinned by the omad-he63 test · found: omad-he63

title: Human progress is never cut to the terminal width: the run's reporter does not measure it
description:
## Background
Human progress (`--progress human`, the default on a terminal) is one line on stderr that each update overwrites: `\r`, "erase line", then the text. Erasing clears only the row the cursor is on, so a line wider than the terminal wraps and leaves its first rows behind. The third review pass (c9f6a33, "progress fits the terminal width") added `fit_width` to `Reporter` (`src/output/stderr.rs`): when set, `progress` measures the terminal (`tcgetwinsize` on stderr) and cuts the message with `…` so `{phase}: {message}{count}` fits `columns - 1` characters.

Only `Reporter::stderr` sets `fit_width`. That constructor serves the paths that never draw progress: help, a usage error, `render_error` and the panic path in `src/cli.rs`. The run's own reporter, the one every `ProgressSink` draws through, is `output::shared_stderr`, which builds `Reporter::new(Box<stderr>, cfg)` with `fit_width: false`. So no progress line is ever cut, and a long one (a local zip's path, `gh:WeakAuras/WeakAuras2@… on retail`) wraps on a narrow terminal and leaves debris rows.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. A retail client and a local zip whose path is longer than 40 characters.
2. Run `omaddons install <zip> -t retail` with stderr on a pseudo-terminal 40 columns wide (`TERM=xterm`).
3. The progress lines read back from the terminal are wider than 39 characters and hold no `…`.

## Technical Approach
- `shared_stderr` writes to the real stderr, so it measures the terminal too: build its reporter with `fit_width: true` (a struct update over `Reporter::new` inside `stderr.rs`, where the field is visible).
- Keep `Reporter::new` unmeasured for the `Vec<u8>` sinks the unit tests use.

## Acceptance Criteria
- On a 40-column pseudo-terminal, every progress line of an install is at most 39 characters, and the one that would be wider is cut with `…`.
- The test fails with `shared_stderr`'s reporter unmeasured.
- NDJSON progress and JSON output are unchanged.

## Test Plan
- Integration (`tests/terminal.rs`, with omad-aco1's pseudo-terminal helper): the install above, every progress line measured.
- Unit: `fit` already has its own (`a_progress_message_is_cut_to_the_terminal`).

## Considerations
- `terminal_width` asks stderr, so a reporter whose sink is not stderr must stay unmeasured; only `shared_stderr` and `Reporter::stderr` write to stderr.
- The pseudo-terminal test skips, saying so, where `/dev/ptmx` cannot be opened.
acceptance_criteria: On a 40-column pseudo-terminal every progress line of an install is at most 39 characters and a too-wide one is cut with an ellipsis; the test fails with shared_stderr's reporter unmeasured; NDJSON and JSON output unchanged.
close_reason: Fixed: output::shared_stderr (the reporter every ProgressSink draws through) now measures the terminal (fit_width), as Reporter::stderr does. tests/terminal.rs progress_lines_fit_the_terminal: an install on a 40-column pseudo-terminal; it failed on HEAD with 100-character fetch and verify lines, and passes with every progress line at most 39 characters and the wide ones cut with an ellipsis. Not a terminal: tcgetwinsize fails, nothing is cut. Vision comment 1295. argc gate --all passed (cargo deny ok).

comments.author: PlushDelta
comments.text: claim: src/output/stderr.rs shared_stderr measures the terminal; proved by tests/terminal.rs with omad-aco1

comments.author: PlushDelta
comments.text: done: the run's progress reporter measures the terminal; proved on a pseudo-terminal · found: none

title: Correct the catalog description of client-specific TOC evidence
description:
## Background

The README catalog introduction says RaiderIO is refused on vanilla and mists because its release metadata declares only mainline. The load-rules section and the regression `the_addons_own_toc_for_this_client_outweighs_metadata_for_others` instead allow client-specific suffixed TOCs in range to prove publisher support. The two explanations contradict each other.

## Steps to Reproduce

Read the catalog introduction and compare it with the archive evidence rules and `tests/install_multi_flavor.rs` around the RaiderIO fixture. The catalog sentence promises a refusal where the regression expects successful installs on Classic Era and Mists.

## Technical Approach

Correct the catalog sentence to describe the suffixed-TOC exception, keeping the dated publisher observation and the separate Titan example. No behavior changes.

Keep the distinction between a publisher declaration and evidence of support in the actual archive; a plain compatible TOC alone still does not override explicit other-client metadata.

title: Titan clients load no _Wrath TOCs and match no game type, so publishers' Titan builds are refused
description:
## Background

The `titan` client-rules row in `src/rules.rs` (Wrath Titan-Reforged, China, 3.80.x, interface 38002) lists no game types and no game suffixes. Both were marked UNVERIFIED, and `tests/toc_matrix.rs` asserted the empty row. So a Titan client loads only a plain `Folder.toc` or a `_Classic` family TOC, and every `AllowLoadGameType` directive excludes it.

The catalog probe (omad-classic-forever-gaps-xud.7) found three addons whose publishers declare Titan but which omaddons refuses there: WeakAuras, Questie and Plater. Evidence from the live archives, 2026-10-15:
- WeakAuras 5.22.1 declares `titan:38002`. Its only TOC for Titan is `WeakAuras_Wrath.toc` with `## Interface: 38002`, which is Titan's interface (Wrath Classic is 30405), and `## AllowLoadGameType: wrath, titan`. So the Titan client loads `_Wrath` TOCs, and its game type is `titan`.
- Questie declares `wrath:38002` for the same reason.
- Plater v661 declares `titan:38001` but ships no TOC with a 38xxx interface. That is a publisher mismatch, not this bug.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Build a synthetic Battle.net tree with `wow_classic_titan` (3.80.2).
2. `omaddons install weakauras -t titan --dry-run --json`.
3. Result: `no_compatible_release`, with every WeakAuras folder `no_loadable_toc`, although release.json declares titan.

## Technical Approach

- `titan` row: `game_types = ["titan"]`, `game_suffixes = ["Wrath"]`; the family suffix stays `Classic`.
- Record the evidence (and its date) in the row's doc comment in place of the UNVERIFIED note. `_Titan` stays out; nothing shows a client reads it.
- Update the TOC matrix comment and add curated rows.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A `_Wrath.toc` with Interface 38002 is the loaded, compatible TOC on titan.
- `AllowLoadGameType: wrath, titan` loads on titan; `AllowLoadGameType: wrath` alone does not.
- `install weakauras -t titan` installs on a synthetic Titan client, as release.json declares.
- The catalog probe's titan column agrees with every publisher except listed publisher mismatches.
- `argc gate` passes, with the builtin rules-table snapshot updated.

## Test Plan

- TOC matrix rows on titan: a `_Wrath` TOC with 38002 is compatible; `_Wrath` with 30405 is `interface_not_in_family`; game type `titan` is allowed; `AllowLoadGameType: wrath` is excluded.
- The suffix sweep follows the row automatically.
- Live: `catalog_matches_declared_flavors` titan column.

## Considerations

- Titan is a China-only client and not on the development machine; this rests on publisher archives, which ship what Titan players actually use.
- If a publisher later ships `_Titan.toc`, add the suffix with that evidence.
acceptance_criteria: _Wrath.toc with Interface 38002 loads and is compatible on titan; AllowLoadGameType wrath, titan loads on titan and wrath alone does not; weakauras installs on a synthetic titan client; the catalog probe titan column agrees except listed publisher mismatches; argc gate passes with the rules snapshot updated
close_reason: The titan rules row now has game type titan and game suffix Wrath, from publishers' archives: WeakAuras 5.22.1 ships WeakAuras_Wrath.toc with Interface 38002 (Titan's alone) and AllowLoadGameType wrath, titan; Questie declares wrath:38002. The UNVERIFIED notes in src/rules.rs and tests/toc_matrix.rs are replaced by that evidence.

comments.author: RustyDolphin
comments.text: claim: src/rules.rs titan row, tests/toc_matrix.rs, tests/fixtures/toc/matrix/cases.toml

comments.author: RustyDolphin
comments.text: done: argc gate passes; TOC matrix rows on titan (_Wrath 38002 loaded and compatible over _Vanilla; _Wrath 30405 interface_not_in_family; AllowLoadGameType wrath alone game_type_excluded; Wrath Classic rejects the 38002 _Wrath TOC); the suffix sweep follows the row; tests/install_multi_flavor.rs installs a WeakAuras-shaped release (with its _Wrath TOC) on a synthetic titan client; builtin rules snapshot updated; live catalog probe titan column now agrees for WeakAuras and Questie (Plater's titan:38001 is a listed publisher mismatch: no 38xxx TOC). decided: no _Titan suffix until a publisher ships one · found: none

title: archive_too_large details take three shapes
description:
## Background

`archive_too_large` carries the bound it hit in `details`, but three shapes exist:

- M2 (archives, downloads, git checkouts): `details.limit` is the value, plus `config_key` when `config.toml` can raise it;
- the `WTF/` walk (`src/backup/tree.rs`) and `backup import` (`src/backup/import.rs`): `details.limit` is the constant's name and `details.max` its value;
- WowAce (`src/sources/wowace.rs`): `details.limit` is the value and `details.constant` the name.

README documents only `details.limit` and `config_key`. An agent reading `details.limit` gets a number from one command and a name from another. The contract freezes at the first tag (milestone 4), so the shapes should agree before then. Found by G2 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.7.2`).

## Steps to Reproduce

- `tests/backup_create.rs` / `src/backup/tree.rs:1029` asserts `details["limit"] == "BACKUP_TREE_MAX_DEPTH"` (a name); `src/sources/wowace.rs:968` asserts `details["constant"] == "WOWACE_TREE_MAX_DIRS"` with the value in `limit`.

## Technical Approach

- One shape for every `archive_too_large`: `details.limit` the numeric bound, `details.constant` the constant's name when it is a named constant, `details.config_key` when `config.toml` can raise it. Change `tree.rs` and `import.rs` to it (DEC-4 is additive before the freeze, but a value changing type is a change: record it on the vision as a pre-freeze correction).
- README's error table documents the three keys.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every `archive_too_large` site emits `limit` as a number, with `constant` and `config_key` as applicable.
- README and the vision record the shape.

## Test Plan

- Update the tree, import and WowAce bound tests; a contract matrix row for one backup bound asserting the shape.

## Considerations

- The human messages already name the bound; only `details` changes.
acceptance_criteria: Every archive_too_large site emits limit as a number, with constant and config_key as applicable; README and the vision record the shape.
close_reason: every archive_too_large gives details.limit as the number, with config_key when config can raise it, else constant (the fixed bound's name)

comments.author: FierceWren
comments.text: claim: archive_too_large details in src/backup/tree.rs, src/backup/import.rs, src/sources/wowace.rs; README error table; their tests

comments.author: FierceWren
comments.text: done: argc gate passed; contract row backup_import_archive_too_large, tree, import and API bound tests updated; vision records the pre-freeze change · found: none

title: A plan its token refuses forgets the archives it downloaded, so the re-preview downloads them again
description:
## Background

M4-D20: `apply` revalidates every source, so a release that landed since the preview makes the plan `plan_stale` (`selection`). Planning downloads every candidate before the token check (`src/engine/tx.rs`, `plan::plan` then `binding.plan(&plan)`), so the stale `apply` has already downloaded the newer archive into the blob cache when it refuses. The design (and D7's subtask omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.7.1) relies on the next run finding that archive "by expected hash or by the candidate fact its download recorded", so the re-preview that follows a stale `apply` downloads nothing.

It does not: when the binding refuses, `tx::run` returns the error and drops the plan, and with it `plan.facts` (each downloaded candidate's hash and verdict). The commands' error paths then call `cache.remember(&[])` (update, copy) or `remember` with only earlier facts (install, sync, pin), so the memo never learns the archive's hash. A blob is found by its hash, so the re-preview downloads the same archive again. The same holds for a typed `--if-match` run refused by its token.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. A retail client with Foo v1 of `gh:o/foo` installed; v2 published; the memo aged a day.
2. `omaddons update -t retail --dry-run --json` stores plan P (Foo to v2).
3. Publish v3.
4. `omaddons apply P --json`: `plan_stale`, `changed: ["selection"]`. `net.log` shows it downloaded `v3/Foo.zip`.
5. `omaddons update -t retail --dry-run --json`: shows v3, asks no source (the memo answers), but `net.log` gains another `asset` line for `v3/Foo.zip`.

Seen for GitHub, git, WoWInterface and Tukui in `tests/apply/releases.rs` (`drift_update_<source>`, step "re-preview inside the window").

## Technical Approach

- `ReleaseCache::learn(&self, facts: &[CandidateFact])` in `src/resolve/cache.rs`: adds `facts` to what this run learned (`learned.candidates`), which `remember` writes with the rest.
- In `tx::run` (`src/engine/tx.rs`), when the binding refuses the plan, hand `plan.facts` to the run's cache (`cache.learn(&plan.facts)`) before cleaning up and returning the refusal. Every engine command already writes the memo after a failed run, so no command changes.
- Nothing else changes: a refused run still stages and commits nothing; the facts are true whatever the binding says (a hash of bytes downloaded, a verdict of TOCs judged).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A run refused by its binding (a stale `apply`, a stale typed `--if-match`) leaves the candidate facts of every archive its planning downloaded in the release memo.
- After a stale `apply`, the re-preview inside the memo window makes no `asset` request for an archive the stale `apply` downloaded (GitHub, git, WoWInterface, Tukui).
- `ReleaseCache::learn` has a unit test: facts learned before `remember(&[])` are written to the memo.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit: `src/resolve/cache.rs`, facts given to `learn` are in the memo `remember(&[])` writes, beside the facts `remember` itself is given.
- E2E: `tests/apply/releases.rs` `drift_update_github`, `drift_update_git`, `drift_update_wowi`, `drift_update_tukui` (no `asset` request on the re-preview), all logged through `TestLog`.

## Considerations

- The memo caps known releases and candidate facts (`MEMO_KNOWN_RELEASES`); learning a refused plan's facts adds at most what that plan downloaded.
- A transient cache (an engine run without one) learns and forgets: harmless.
- Only the binding-refusal path is in scope: a plan that fails in planning has no complete plan to take facts from.
acceptance_criteria: A run refused by its binding leaves the candidate facts of every archive its planning downloaded in the release memo; after a stale apply the re-preview inside the window makes no asset request for those archives (GitHub, git, WoWInterface, Tukui); ReleaseCache::learn has a unit test; argc gate passes.
close_reason: done: ReleaseCache::learn (src/resolve/cache.rs) adds facts to what the run learned; tx::run hands a binding-refused plan's facts to the run's cache before returning the refusal (src/engine/tx.rs), and each engine command's existing remember writes them. Unit: facts_learned_during_the_run_are_remembered. E2E: drift_update_{github,git,wowi,tukui} re-preview after a stale apply now adds no request (before: one asset request each). README apply bullet says the check's fetches and downloads are remembered. No wire names changed; no journal, recovery, binding or deletion rule changed (common rule 14 does not apply).

comments.author: SleepyCedar
comments.text: claim: src/resolve/cache.rs (ReleaseCache::learn), src/engine/tx.rs (the binding-refusal path)

comments.author: SleepyCedar
comments.text: done: fixed and proven by the release-landing matrix, gate green

title: Prose fixes that name an omaddons command: <placeholder> rule, read-only alternatives, and a contract guard
description:
## Background

Part (b) of omad-m2-audit-yegz.5.11, split as that bead's Considerations allow. Part (a) landed: the nine runnable prose fixes became argv (git_hosts host_blocked → config set git_hosts with the merged TOML array, also for git:http refs; missing_dependency → search <folder> or the command without --no-deps; remove ref_ambiguous → list -t <id> with one remove per candidate), and the command boundary (Out::boundary_fix) now gives a retryable plan_stale and locked the failing argv, and offline the argv without --offline when the flag alone made the run offline. What remains:

- **Placeholder rule (decided in 5.11).** A fix that needs a value only the user can supply stays Suggestion::text, and its display is the exact command with each missing value as a lowercase <placeholder> (`omaddons targets add <path>`). Census sites (5.11's class P): src/app/adopt/apply.rs, copy.rs (both --from/--to given: the argv without -t, which is runnable), install.rs, status.rs (journal_pending), sync.rs, targets.rs, discover/registry.rs, update.rs, discover/battlenet.rs and custom.rs unknown_flavor (now built in discover::unknown_flavor: display `omaddons config set targets.<id>.family <family>` with the id filled in), discover/mod.rs, engine/plan.rs (no_compatible_release, alternative `omaddons info <ref> -t <id>`), resolve/updates.rs, sources/git_hosts.rs, github.rs, github_rest.rs, url.rs.
- **Read-only alternatives** for P sites where one exists (search <folder>, help sync, info <ref> -t <id>).
- **stale_check warnings**' offline fix at the boundary, like offline errors (src/sources/wowi/index.rs).
- **Guard the prose side.** tests/contract/main.rs: a null-argv display passes only if it has no `omaddons ` word, has a <placeholder>, or is on a short explicit allowlist (the echo "$TOKEN" | omaddons auth github set pipeline and its gh variant, the GitHub rate-limit 'store a token with omaddons auth github set', the --dry-run reminders, sync's 'regenerate the file with omaddons export'); shrink TEXT_FIXES to that. A source scan in tests/contract/exit_sites.rs: every string literal passed to Suggestion::text( in src/ (outside test code) that contains `omaddons ` must contain '<' or be on that allowlist; it must reject a planted Suggestion::text("omaddons status").
- **README**: Fields error row and For coding agents: fix_argv is null when the fix is prose or needs a value only you can supply; such a fix shows the command with <placeholders>. Vision comment on the placeholder rule and the boundary retry rule.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every P display follows the <placeholder> rule; the listed alternatives exist.
- The contract check and the source scan pass and reject a planted Suggestion::text("omaddons status").
- stale_check's offline fix is the argv without --offline when the flag alone set it.
- README and vision comment updated; argc gate passes.

title: `cargo build --release --tests` fails: engine_multi_target calls the debug-only `fsx::with_spec`
description:
## Background

The milestone checkpoints run some suites in release builds (`cargo test --release --test perf -- --ignored`, per README "Milestone checkpoints"). Failpoints exist only in debug builds: `src/fsx/mod.rs` re-exports `failpoint::{with_spec, with_spec_in}` under `#[cfg(debug_assertions)]` (DEC-7, test hooks are debug-only).

`tests/engine_multi_target.rs`, in the test `a_failed_commit_on_one_target_leaves_the_others_committed_and_undoable`, calls `omaddons::fsx::with_spec(...)` without a cfg guard. So that test binary does not compile in a release build, and any release build of every test target fails. Today only `--test perf` is built in release, so nothing breaks yet. But a checkpoint or a contributor running `cargo test --release` (or `cargo build --release --tests`) hits a compile error unrelated to their change. This was found while measuring `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.7`'s perf budget.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `cargo build --release --tests`
2. It fails with `error[E0425]: cannot find function with_spec in module omaddons::fsx` at `tests/engine_multi_target.rs`, and the note "found an item that was configured out" (`src/fsx/mod.rs`).

## Technical Approach

- Put `#[cfg(debug_assertions)]` on that test, the way debug-only hooks are gated elsewhere, with a one-line comment saying failpoints exist only in debug builds.
- Check that no other test calls a debug-only item unguarded: `cargo build --release --tests` must succeed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `cargo build --release --tests` succeeds.
- The test still runs, and passes, in the gate's debug build (`cargo test --test engine_multi_target`).
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Build: `cargo build --release --tests` exits 0.
- Debug: `cargo test --test engine_multi_target` still runs the guarded test (it appears in `-- --list`).

## Considerations

- Gate the test, never the failpoint export: failpoints must stay out of release binaries (DEC-7).
- If more unguarded uses turn up, guard each test, not whole files, so the release build still compiles and runs the rest.
acceptance_criteria: cargo build --release --tests succeeds; the guarded test still runs and passes in the gate's debug build (cargo test --test engine_multi_target lists and runs it); argc gate passes
close_reason: cargo build --release --tests succeeds with no warnings: debug-only failpoint users are gated

title: omaddons help with a nested command (help targets add) is a usage error
description:
## Background

`omaddons help <command>` is the documented way to see a command's flags, and `src/app/help.rs` `for_command` already resolves nested paths such as `targets add` and `config set`. But the clap definition (`src/cli.rs`, `Help { command: Option<String> }`, around line 124) takes a single positional, so `omaddons help targets add` fails at parse time: a usage error, exit 2, whose fix is `omaddons help help`. Only the quoted form `omaddons help "targets add"` or `omaddons targets add --help` works.

Bead omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.1.1 (grouped bare help) lists `help <nested path>` as unchanged behavior, so it assumes this already works.

Found while capturing every command's help for the README rewrite.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `omaddons help targets add` → exit 2, `usage`, fix `omaddons help help`.
2. Same for `help targets rm|rename|default` and `help config get|set|path`.
3. `omaddons help "targets add"` → exit 0 with the subcommand's help.

## Technical Approach

- Make the positional `command: Vec<String>` (`num_args = 0..`) and join it with a space before passing it to `for_command`.
- An unknown path keeps today's `usage` error with the closest-command suggestion.
- Under `--json`, the envelope `command` stays `help`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `omaddons help targets add` (and every other nested path) exits 0 with the same text as `omaddons targets add --help`.
- `omaddons help targets nosuch` is a usage error naming `targets` subcommands.
- `omaddons help` and `omaddons help install` are unchanged (snapshots untouched).
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- `tests/cli_skeleton.rs`: every nested path through `help` matches `<path> --help`, human and `--json`.
- An unknown nested path gives exit 2 with a suggestion.

## Considerations

- clap's own `help` subcommand is disabled in favor of ours; keep it disabled.
- README.md lists this under Known issues; remove that line when fixed.
acceptance_criteria: help <nested path> exits 0 with the same text as <path> --help; an unknown nested path is a usage error with a suggestion; bare help and help install unchanged; argc gate passes
close_reason: help takes a nested command path: omaddons help targets add

comments.author: CrimsonJasper
comments.text: done: Help's positional is now Vec<String> (num_args 0..), joined by a space for help::for_command; for_command walks the path word by word and, for an unknown word past the first, names the parent's subcommands and fixes to omaddons help <parent> (a close match still suggests itself: help config st → help config set). Envelope command stays help; data.command keeps naming the subcommand, as the quoted form did. tests/cli_skeleton.rs help_walks_a_nested_path: every targets/config subcommand through help equals <path> --help, plus the two unknown-path cases; bare help and help install snapshots unchanged; README Known issues line removed and the help section shows help targets add.

title: Usage errors ignore --no-color, misreport meta.offline, and build incomplete or circular fixes
description:
## Background

When argument parsing fails, `src/cli.rs` renders the usage error with a default-flags fallback configuration (around lines 278-288), because the real flags could not be parsed. Several usage-error fixes are also built from too little of the original argv. Together:

1. `--no-color` (and `NO_COLOR`) is ignored, so the human error is colored on a terminal.
2. `meta.offline` in the JSON envelope is `false` even with `OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1` or `--offline` in argv. Agents that check `meta.offline` to confirm an offline run get a wrong answer.
3. `omaddons install http://github.com/a/b -t retail` fails with `ref_invalid`, and its fix (the https form) drops `-t retail`.
4. `omaddons status --version` is a usage error whose suggested fix is the identical command: the suggestion candidates include the root-only `--version`.

Found while auditing the CLI surface for the README rewrite. README.md lists these under Known issues.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1 omaddons nosuch --json` → `meta.offline: false`.
2. In a terminal: `omaddons nosuch --no-color` → the `error[usage]` prefix is still colored.
3. `omaddons install http://github.com/a/b -t retail --json` → `fix_argv` lacks `-t retail`.
4. `omaddons status --version` → fix `omaddons status --version`.

## Technical Approach

- On a parse failure, pre-scan the raw argv and environment for the few flags that affect rendering and meta: `--json`/`--robot`/`--format`, `--no-color`/`NO_COLOR`, `--offline`/`OMADDONS_OFFLINE`, `--quiet`. The JSON flags are presumably already scanned this way, since usage errors produce envelopes; extend that scan.
- The `ref_invalid` http→https fix replaces only the offending token in the full argv (`fix_argv_keeping` already supports keeping a corrected token).
- Exclude root-only flags (`-V`, `--version`) from subcommand suggestion candidates, and never suggest the failing argv itself.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Usage errors honor `--no-color` and `NO_COLOR`.
- `meta.offline` is true on usage errors when `--offline` or `OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1` is present.
- The http→https fix keeps every other argument, `-t` included.
- No usage error suggests its own argv.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- `tests/contract/special.rs`: a usage error with `OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1` has `meta.offline: true`.
- `tests/cli_skeleton.rs`: a usage error under a pty with `--no-color` contains no ANSI escape; `status --version` suggests something other than itself.
- Contract matrix: an `http://` ref with `-t` yields a fix with `-t`.
- A property over the usage-error paths: `fix_argv != argv`.

## Considerations

- `OMADDONS_OFFLINE` counts only when exactly `1`; keep that rule in the pre-scan.
acceptance_criteria: usage errors honor --no-color and NO_COLOR; meta.offline is true when offline; the http to https fix keeps -t and every other argument; no usage error suggests its own argv; argc gate passes
close_reason: Usage errors render and report as their argv asks, and their fixes keep the command

comments.author: CrimsonJasper
comments.text: claim: src/cli.rs usage-error path, src/main.rs/app pre-scan, tests/cli_skeleton.rs, tests/contract

comments.author: CrimsonJasper
comments.text: done: (1,2) output::flags_from_argv reads every presentation flag of an argv that did not parse (--json/--robot/--format, --no-color, --quiet, --progress, --no-progress, -v…; stops at --), and cli::fallback_output resolves it (NO_COLOR already came through TermEnv); output::offline_from_argv (--offline before --, or OMADDONS_OFFLINE exactly 1) feeds meta.offline of usage errors, help-on-error, the cli.panic failpoint, Context errors and the panic hook (PanicState.offline). (3) resolve_args::aimed_at turns the ref parser's 'omaddons install <ref>' fixes (the https form and each ambiguity candidate) into the argv that ran with only that argument replaced (cli::fix_argv_replacing), at install and info: install keeps -t and every other ref; info now suggests info, not install. (4) usage_error: under a subcommand only global root flags are candidates; --version/-V there fixes to 'omaddons --version' with that command's help as the alternative; a final guard replaces any fix equal to the failing argv (presentation flags dropped) with help and drops such alternatives. Tests: cli a_usage_error_never_suggests_itself (status --version/-V, and every command × 8 bad tokens, >100 cases: no fix or alternative is the argv), a_usage_error_renders_as_its_argv_asks (tty: --no-color and NO_COLOR uncolored, --quiet --json); term raw_argv_finds_every_presentation_flag_and_offline; contract special a_usage_error_reports_an_offline_run_as_offline, an_http_ref_is_fixed_to_https_keeping_every_other_argument. decided: no pty test (no harness in the tree); the fallback config is unit-tested against a tty TermEnv, which is exactly what run_with renders with. README Known issues entry removed. Gate green (1283).

title: Render the guide's {{exit_doctor}} block from doctor::Exit
description:
## Background

The agent guide (M4-D7) is rendered by `src/contract/guide/render.rs` from the template `src/contract/guide/guide.md`. One of its twelve placeholders, `{{exit_doctor}}`, renders the doctor tree's own exit dictionary (M4-D40). `GuideInputs.exit_doctor` is `Option<Vec<ExitRow>>`:
- `Some(rows)`: the block prints "Every `doctor` command uses its own exit dictionary:", a blank line, and a `Code | Name | Meaning` table.
- `None`: it prints the holding line "This build has no doctor, and so no doctor exit dictionary."

When omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1.1 (the renderer) landed, E3 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3, `doctor diagnose`, which adds `doctor::Exit`) was not on `main`. So `GuideInputs::live()` sets `exit_doctor: None`, with the comment "The doctor's dictionary (E3) is not in this build yet." This task gives that wiring an owner. Without it, the guide would keep telling agents that there is no doctor after the doctor ships.

## Technical Approach

- In `GuideInputs::live()` (`src/contract/guide/render.rs`), set `exit_doctor` to `Some(rows)`: one `ExitRow` per `doctor::Exit::ALL` entry, in that order.
  - `code`, `name` and `meaning` come from the doctor `Exit`'s own accessors, the same ones E3 publishes.
  - `retryable` is any `Retry` value: the doctor table has no Retryable column.
- Remove the "not in this build yet" comment.
- Update `live_inputs_cover_the_registries`: today it asserts `live.exit_doctor == None`. Make it assert one row per `doctor::Exit::ALL` entry, in order, with each code and name.
- Regenerate `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` under common rule 17, once `robot-docs guide` and `tests/skill.rs` exist (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1.2 and later): `OMADDONS_UPDATE_SKILL=1 cargo test --test skill`. Commit it in the same commit. If those have not landed yet, there is nothing to regenerate.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `GuideInputs::live().exit_doctor` holds one row per `doctor::Exit::ALL` entry, in order, with the doctor exits' codes, names and meanings.
- The rendered guide's "Exit codes" section shows the doctor table and no longer the holding line.
- `live_inputs_cover_the_registries` asserts the rows. `exit_doctor_block_table` and `exit_doctor_block_holding_line` still pass.
- `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` is regenerated in the same commit when `tests/skill.rs` exists.
- `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files.

## Test Plan

- **Unit:** `live_inputs_cover_the_registries` (`src/contract/guide/render.rs`) checks the doctor rows against `doctor::Exit::ALL`: count, order, code and name.
- **Unit:** the existing block tests `exit_doctor_block_table` and `exit_doctor_block_holding_line` keep pinning both renderings.
- **E2E:** none of its own. `tests/skill.rs`'s `skill_md_is_the_guide` (once it exists) holds the committed `SKILL.md` equal to the rendered guide, so a missed regeneration fails the gate.

## Considerations

- Blocked by E3 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3): `doctor::Exit` must exist first.
- No other code changes. The renderer, the block format and the template are fixed by omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1.1.
- Expect `SKILL.md` churn: it is the binary's own output committed as an embedded asset, not a script editing code.
acceptance_criteria: GuideInputs::live().exit_doctor holds one row per doctor::Exit::ALL entry in order; the rendered guide shows the doctor table, not the holding line; live_inputs_cover_the_registries asserts the rows; SKILL.md regenerated in the same commit when tests/skill.rs exists; argc gate passes and ubs is clean

title: Group commit, derived writes and deferred directory fsyncs (`omad-7ccp`)
description:
## How to work this bead

This bead is worked through its 7 subtasks, listed below in work order. Claim a subtask, not this bead (`br ready --parent omad-7ccp` lists the ready ones). The agent that closes the last open subtask then verifies every acceptance criterion of this bead (they are the leaf's, not any one subtask's), and closes this bead with `br close omad-7ccp --reason "done: <evidence> · found: <ids>"`. Until this bead is closed, every bead it blocks stays blocked.

1. `omad-7ccp.1` Count first: each commit window's fsync count and its attribution by file kind on `-v` and `-vv`, the pinned "before" table, the btrfs report, and the design gate (derived targets and the written ordering argument). Starts at once.
2. `omad-7ccp.2` Group commit of the action log: `WriteSession` buffering, `sync_actions()` at the transaction's end, `finish()`, and the dropped-session assertion. After s1; its claimer first reviews s1's design-gate record.
3. `omad-7ccp.3` Derived writes: `Durability::Derived` for `history_tail.json`, `backups.json` and the doorbell, and the history projection's follow-up moved after the lock. After s2.
4. `omad-7ccp.4` `fsx::CommitWindow`: owned directory handles, deduplication by identity, `DIRTY_DIRS_MAX`, explicit barriers, `fsx.barrier.sync`, and the directory sinks in `fsx::sys` (no window opened yet, so nothing changes). After s2; can be worked beside s3.
5. `omad-7ccp.5` Deferred directory fsyncs in every commit window: a barrier at every ordering point, the final barrier before release, and the failure rules. After s3 and s4.
6. `omad-7ccp.6` E2E: the adversarial matrix (an injected sync failure and a crash at every barrier of every commit window, repeated recovery, the WTF privacy case, the oversized window, every crash matrix rerun). After s5.
7. `omad-7ccp.7` Measurement on btrfs, the power-loss campaign where an unprivileged tool allows one, README's figures and the before/after tables. After s5; can be worked beside s6.

**Size L, kept as one leaf for closure.** The three changes (group commit, derived writes, deferred directory fsyncs) share one counted table and one written ordering argument: landing them as separate leaves would re-derive the argument three times and let a dependent see a commit window whose durability had been argued for only part of its writes. The subtasks split the work into commits that each pass `argc gate` and leave `main` consistent; the closure stays whole: this bead closes only when all seven subtasks are closed, so H4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`, the README final pass) and T4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4`, the slice-3 end-to-end suite) never see half of it.

**Design gate (common rule 14).** This leaf changes a durability rule, so it is one of M4's ten design-gate leaves. A crash matrix cannot prove fsync placement (a killed process keeps the page cache, so every placement passes it), so the gate has two halves: the written power-loss argument per ordering point, posted and reviewed in `omad-7ccp.1` before any code changes durability, and the adversarial matrix of `omad-7ccp.6` (injected sync failures and crashes at every barrier, repeated recovery). The design gate is passed only when `omad-7ccp.1`'s record has been reviewed and `omad-7ccp.6` is closed. If the gate changes this leaf's size or edges, record the change in a comment on the milestone epic `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm` and rerun the delivery computation there (critical path, slack, lanes), as the milestone epic's delivery comment asks.

**This bead was `omad-7ccp` before M4** (M4-D59): the filing step undeferred it, re-parented it under the G area epic and replaced its body with this one. Its earlier comments stay; comment 1167 on this bead is the measurement this work starts from (restated below), and it is the "before" of the close comment's per-file table.

## Background

### The problem

Every commit window of omaddons (the time the global lock is held while a transaction changes the disk) is a sequence of durable writes, each made durable on its own:

- each tracked `mutate()` appends its line to the transaction's audit log, `actions.jsonl`, with one `fsync` per line (`log_action` → `sys::append_durable`, `src/fsx/mutate.rs:863-871`, `src/fsx/sys.rs:205-217`);
- every temp-plus-rename write fsyncs its file and then its parent directory (`sys::write_atomic_to`, `src/fsx/sys.rs:166-203`);
- every rename fsyncs both parent directories (`src/fsx/mutate.rs:843-845`);
- the history projection `history_tail.json`, a cache rebuilt from `history.jsonl`, is rewritten with the same full durability inside the window (`history::append_line` calls `history_tail::appended`, `src/state/history.rs:318-321`, which writes through `history_tail::write`, `src/state/history_tail.rs:339-358`).

On tmpfs, where every lock budget of `tests/perf.rs` is measured, an fsync costs nothing, which is why the M1 to M3 checkpoints recorded 0 to 2 ms. On a real disk it is the whole cost. M3's D12 measured the same commits on btrfs on an NVMe drive, release build: a whole restore of a 500 MiB `WTF/` in 5,000 files held the lock 134 to 146 ms (0 to 1 ms on tmpfs), and an install of a one-file addon onto that home 127 and 180 ms. `strace -f -e trace=flock,fsync` showed 51 fsyncs inside the restore's window and 62 inside the install's, about 3.3 ms each.

Comment 1167 on this bead attributes the install's 62 fsyncs (release build, btrfs on NVMe, `strace -y` of an install that replaced an installed version, `lock_held_ms` 165) by file: 15 `actions.jsonl` (one per `mutate()` action), 5 the journal, then pairs per temp-plus-rename write: snapshot dir 4, `targets/` record 4, `history_tail` cache 4, trash 3, journal dir 2, stage 2, client snapshot 2–3, files index pieces 4, in-flight 2, `history.jsonl` 1, AddOns 1, state root 1. It estimated about 44 after group-committing the action log (15 → 1, about 40 ms) and taking the cache writes out of the window (about 4), and showed that the original acceptance ("at least halved", 62 → 31) needs a durability redesign beyond that. The bead was deferred to M4 because group-committing the action log changes vision §5.5 step 7 ("an fsync'd `actions.jsonl` line"), which the doctor's run folder and undo build on.

A second terminal, an agent and the bar widget wait for that lock (up to 5 s, `LOCK_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT`). 165 ms is not a failure, but the budget's intent, a commit window short enough that concurrent work never notices, holds only on tmpfs today.

### What this bead does

It makes each commit window as durable as today with fewer syncs, and proves where it cannot be proven by a test:

1. **Count first.** The window's fsync count and its attribution by file kind are printed under `-v`/`-vv` and pinned per window shape in a gate test, before anything changes.
2. **Group commit of `actions.jsonl`:** the audit lines of a tracked session are buffered and synced at the transaction's end, not per line.
3. **Derived writes:** `history_tail.json`, `backups.json` and the doorbell are written without fsync (`Durability::Derived`), and the history projection's follow-up leaves the window.
4. **Deferred directory fsyncs** through owned directory handles held by an explicit durability context, `fsx::CommitWindow`, synced at explicit barriers at every ordering point and once more before the lock is released; a barrier's error fails the command.
5. **The ordering argument:** one written paragraph per ordering point, reviewed before code, because failpoint kills cannot test fsync placement.
6. **The adversarial matrix:** an injected sync failure and a crash at every barrier of every commit window, each recovered by the next lock-taking command.
7. **Measurement:** the btrfs figures, the per-file table before and after, and a power-loss campaign where an unprivileged tool allows one.

### Milestone goals it serves

- **G-M4-6, no new risk to the engine's guarantees:** "every new write goes through fsx, and every repair is a journaled transaction that recovers like any other"; "the global lock is still held only for commit windows". This bead shortens every commit window without weakening what recovery can rely on, and where it cannot argue that, keeps today's immediate fsync.
- **G-M4-4, diagnosable and repairable (in part):** the audit log the doctor contract requires (`actions.jsonl`, the trail users and agents reconstruct runs from) stays, written once per transaction instead of once per action. Repairs (E5, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`, the repair transaction), set-asides (F2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.2`, the journal fixers) and reactivations (E7, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7`, undo of repairs) run through the same commit window and gain the same barriers.
- **G-M4-3, what was previewed is what runs (indirectly):** D8's under-lock witness check (D8, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8`, the approval checked again under the commit lock) made the commit window do more; this bead counts that work and keeps the window short for the agents and the widget that wait on it.

### Checkpoint criteria it is responsible for

**§3.2 criterion 13, durability** (this bead owns it whole):

### The decisions that shape it

- **M4-D54: `actions.jsonl` is group-committed; derived files are not fsynced; directory fsyncs are deferred to ordering points.** Three changes, in this order, each landing with the counts table, after the protocols they touch have settled (the approval witness, the repair primitives, the barriers and gc), so the durability work optimizes the final protocol rather than a moving one.
  1. *Group commit.* A tracked `WriteSession` buffers its `ActionRecord` lines. `WriteSession::sync_actions()` writes and syncs the buffer, at the transaction's end, not before every journal step: before the journal line that closes the transaction's changes (a folder journal's `swapped`, a repair's `done` or `rolled_back`), before the history line, and at `WriteSession::finish()`, a new explicit method that returns errors. A tracked session dropped without `finish()` fails a debug assertion. Why it is safe: recovery reads only the journal, never `actions.jsonl`, and a repair's undo reads the history line's primitives (M4-D46); the audit log matters for a transaction that committed, so it must be durable by the line that closes that transaction's changes. A crash before that line loses at most the audit lines of an attempt that recovery then rolls back. The journal stays write-ahead per step, exactly as today.
  2. *Derived files are not fsynced.* `history_tail.json`, `backups.json` and the doorbell are rebuilt from durable state when missing or stale (M3-D37), so they are written with a new `Durability::Derived`: temp-plus-rename atomicity, no fsync, and no later `syncfs`. `Durability::Deferred` (`src/fsx/sys.rs:131-140`) promises a later `syncfs`, so it is the wrong contract for them.
  3. *Deferred directory fsyncs through owned handles and explicit barriers.* Syncing a file does not make its directory entry durable (Linux `fsync(2)` requires syncing the directory), so the deferral keeps every one of those syncs, deduplicated and moved to ordering points. The window owns a durability context, `fsx::CommitWindow`, created with the lock and passed explicitly; each `mutate()` that changes a directory records an open directory handle (`O_RDONLY | O_DIRECTORY | O_CLOEXEC`), the parent of a write or create and both parents of a rename, deduplicated by the handle's `fstat` identity; a handle keeps naming its directory after a rename, and nothing ever reopens a path to find what to sync. At most `DIRTY_DIRS_MAX` (64) handles are held; past that, the context syncs and closes them at once. `barrier()` syncs and closes every handle and returns the first error; it runs before every journal phase line and the history line, before every step line that follows a rename, and as a final barrier before success and before the lock is released. A barrier error fails the command; `Drop` is defensive cleanup only. File-data fsyncs are not deferred, and where the written argument cannot justify deferring a directory's sync, that directory keeps its immediate fsync.
  - *Pinned counts:* regression evidence, never a reason to accept an unsafe boundary. *The target follows the proven implementation:* the design gate fixes it from the counted boundaries; the forecast (at most 44) is revised there if the count says otherwise. *Power loss:* the written argument stays the evidence; a power-loss campaign runs if an unprivileged tool that drops unsynced writes can be used on the machine, else README says the ordering is argued and crash-tested, not power-loss-tested.
  - **Rejected, and why an implementer must not reach for them:** (i) per-line fsync, the status quo: about 40 ms per install on btrfs for durability nothing reads; (ii) dropping `actions.jsonl` for engine transactions: it is the doctor contract's audit trail; (iii) skipping a parent fsync "when the directory is unchanged since its last fsync": every directory fsync follows a change, so it saves almost nothing, and as first written it ignored renames out of a directory, which would have left a removal non-durable; (iv) promising a halving: no measurement supports it; (v) a per-thread map of inode keys to paths flushed when the lock guard drops (the plan's earlier draft): a later rename can make a stored path vanish or name another directory, and a flush in `Drop` cannot return its I/O error; (vi) syncing the action log before every journal append: it keeps roughly one log sync per step, so it cannot produce the estimate it was quoted with.
  - **Departure:** it amends vision §5.5 step 7.
- **M4-D59: the deferred beads.** `omad-7ccp` becomes this leaf; it is not filed twice, and its measurement comments stay.
- **M4-D60 (context): the approval witness is checked again under the commit lock.** "Cost is measured, not avoided. The under-lock re-read is one `stat` per witnessed entry. D8 reports what it adds to `lock_held_ms` on the realistic home (5,040 files), and G3's pinned counts include it." D8's checks add no fsync; this bead pins a bound run's window so a future fsync there shows.
- **M3-D37 (context): derived projections are checked before they are believed.** `history_tail::fresh` believes the projection only while `history.jsonl` is exactly as long as it covers and ends with its last line (`src/state/history_tail.rs:126-133`); `backups.json` is validated against one `read_dir` of the backups and snapshots (`src/backup/inventory.rs:1-11`). That is what makes losing them to a power cut harmless.
- **M4-D17 (context): verbosity has three levels.** `-v` keeps its meaning (debug log events), `-vv` adds `trace` events (A8, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.8`, verbosity levels). The window's count goes on the existing `-v` line; the per-kind attribution is a trace event.
- **M4-D46 and M4-D38 (context):** a repair's undo reads the history line, never the action log; a reactivation's activation rename is the repair's last primitive, provisional journal name first (E14, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14`, fences and activation barriers). Both are why the action log may be group-committed and why every rename of a reactivation must be durable before the next step line.

**How this serves the vision.** The thesis is that omaddons stays the sole, safe, undoable authority over what it manages. Its durability is the foundation of that: every guarantee recovery gives rests on what was on disk when the power went. This bead buys back the lock time the durable-write pattern costs on real disks without moving any guarantee, by making each ordering point explicit, arguing each one in writing, failing loudly when a sync fails, and keeping the old immediate fsync wherever the argument cannot be made.

### 1. Count first (s1)

**The window's counts.** `GlobalLockGuard` records `sys::sync_counts()` when the lock is acquired (`syncs_at`) and starts a per-thread tally of durability calls by file kind; `GlobalLockGuard::window_syncs(&self) -> WindowSyncs` returns the difference since acquisition and the tally:

```rust
/// What a lock window made durable: counted, never serialized.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct WindowSyncs {
    /// fsync(2) and fdatasync(2) calls, files and directories.
    pub fsyncs: u64,
    pub syncfs: u64,
    /// The same calls by file kind (`sync_kind`), zero counts absent.
    pub by_kind: BTreeMap<&'static str, u64>,
}
```

Every durability call in `fsx::sys` names the path it makes durable, and the tally adds one under `sync_kind(path, is_dir)`. **Decided while writing this bead:** the kinds are a fixed vocabulary of static names, computed from omaddons-controlled path components only (file names such as `actions.jsonl`, `history_tail.json`, and directory names such as `journal`, `targets`, `snapshots`, `stage`, `.omaddons`, `AddOns`, `WTF`), never a component copied from disk, so no account, realm, character or addon name can reach the output. The vocabulary (first match wins; files, then the `_dir` form for a directory): `actions_log`, `quarantine`, `repair_run`, `journal`/`journal_dir`, `history`, `history_tail`, `backup_inventory`, `doorbell`, `status`, `registry`, `files_index`, `record`/`targets_dir`, `backup_copy` (fsx's verbatim backups under a snapshot's `files/`), `client_snapshot`/`client_snapshot_dir`, `stage`/`stage_dir`, `state_snapshot`/`state_snapshot_dir`, `trash`/`trash_dir`, `inflight`/`inflight_dir`, `credential`, `wtf`/`wtf_dir`, `addons`/`addons_dir`, `state_root`, `cache_root`, `other_file`/`other_dir`. The implementer may refine the rules (s1's unit table is the contract); a new kind is a new row of that table. `fdatasync` (s2) counts as an `fsync` (**decided while writing this bead:** the counter's purpose is durability calls per window, and comment 1167's "before" counted every such call).

**The `-v` and `-vv` lines.** Wherever the engine takes `millis(&guard)` today (`src/engine/tx.rs:1159`, `:1348`; `src/engine/undo.rs:583`; `src/engine/restore.rs:983`; `src/engine/restore_addons.rs:1017`), it also takes `guard.window_syncs()` and carries it to the command layer beside `lock_held_ms`, as a `window_syncs: Option<WindowSyncs>` field (`#[serde(skip)]` in a serialized type, like `lock_held_ms`). ### 2. The design gate (s1, after the counting commit)
