title: Group commit of the action log: buffered `actions.jsonl` lines synced at the transaction's end, `WriteSession::finish()` and the dropped-session assertion
description:
Part 2 of 7 of omad-7ccp (Group commit, derived writes and deferred directory fsyncs (`omad-7ccp`)). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

G3 (`omad-7ccp`) makes every commit window of omaddons as durable as today with far fewer syncs, under M4-D54, and owns §3.2 checkpoint criterion 13 (durability). On btrfs an install held the global lock 165 ms for 62 fsyncs, and 15 of them were the transaction's audit log, `actions.jsonl`, fsynced once per `mutate()` action (comment 1167 on G3). It serves G-M4-6 ("no new risk to the engine's guarantees") and keeps the doctor contract's audit trail (G-M4-4).

This part is M4-D54's first change, **group commit of the action log**: a tracked `WriteSession` buffers its `ActionRecord` lines and syncs them at the transaction's end, before the journal line that closes the transaction's changes (a folder journal's `swapped`, a repair's `done` or `rolled_back`), before the history line, and at a new `WriteSession::finish()`, with a debug assertion on a tracked session dropped unfinished. It is its own step because M4-D54 orders the three changes and lands each with its counts, and because it changes the `mutate()` contract (vision §5.5 step 7, "an fsync'd `actions.jsonl` line"), which M4-D54 amends.

**Why it is safe (M4-D54).** Nothing reads `actions.jsonl` back: recovery reads only the journal, and a repair's undo reads the history line's primitives (M4-D46). The audit log matters for a transaction that committed, so it must be durable by the line that closes that transaction's changes, not per line. A crash before that line loses at most the audit lines of an attempt that recovery then rolls back. The journal itself stays write-ahead per step, exactly as today: journal step → mutate → (buffered action line) → next journal step. **Rejected:** keeping one fsync per line (about 40 ms per install for durability nothing reads); dropping the log for engine transactions (it is the doctor contract's audit trail); syncing the log before every journal append (about one log sync per step, so it cannot deliver the estimate).

**Before you start: review the design gate.** `omad-7ccp.1` posted a comment on G3 titled "Design gate: commit-window durability (M4-D54)" with the derived targets and one power-loss paragraph per ordering point. Read every paragraph and record, in your claim comment, "agreed" or a challenge per point (J1–J7, R1–R7, X). A challenged point keeps its immediate fsync until the challenge is answered in a comment on G3. This is the review M4-D54 requires before code.

**Facts this part relies on** (as of `c0ab5e9`):
- `log_action` (`src/fsx/mutate.rs:863-871`) serializes the `ActionRecord`, creates the log's directory with `sys::create_dir_all` and appends with `sys::append_durable` (one `fsync`, plus one of the directory when it created the file, `src/fsx/sys.rs:205-217`). It is called at step 7 of a tracked `mutate_with` (`src/fsx/mutate.rs:467-485`), for failed operations too (`ok: false`), before `executed?` returns the operation's error and before the failpoint `fsx.mutate.logged`.
- `TxState { tx, snapshot_roots, actions_log, next_seq }` (`src/fsx/session.rs:56-69`); `SessionKind::{Tx, Untracked}` (`:71-74`); `WriteSession` has no `Drop` (`:77-152`).
- Every journal line is appended by `journal::append_line` (`src/engine/journal.rs:442-448`) through `mutate(.., Op::AppendFile)` in the given session; in a commit window that session is the tracked one, so each journal line is itself a tracked action. `mark_swapped` (`:422-424`) is called by `swap()` (`src/engine/swap.rs:764`), `restore::Window::commit` (`src/engine/restore.rs:944`) and `restore_addons` (`src/engine/restore_addons.rs:978`).
- `history::append_line` (`src/state/history.rs:294-322`) appends the history line through the caller's session.
- The owners of a tracked session in production: `tx::commit_target` (`src/engine/tx.rs:998-1004`, created before the lock and used there by `prestage_saved_variables`, `:1013`), `undo::commit` (`src/engine/undo.rs:391`, used before the lock by `prestage_saved_variables` and `prestage_restores`, `:395-397`, rebound with `with_owned_folders` at `:499`), `restore::Window::commit` (`src/engine/restore.rs:866-872`, inside the window), `restore_addons` commit (`src/engine/restore_addons.rs:893`), and E5's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`) `engine::repair::commit` (`src/engine/repair/commit.rs`; its tracked `Writer::Doctor` session holds only the primitives and writes `<run>/actions.jsonl`, and E5 left a comment where "G3 later inserts `session.finish()` … immediately before `done`"). Each closes over the session in a commit closure and, on an error, runs in-process recovery in another session (`src/engine/tx.rs:1273-1300`, `src/engine/undo.rs:551-582`, `src/engine/restore.rs:961-982`, `src/engine/restore_addons.rs:995-1016`).
- Unit tests that build tracked sessions: `Fixture::tx_session` in `src/fsx/mutate.rs` (`:1010-1018`, about 13 uses, with `Fixture::actions` reading the log at `:1024-1030`), `Scene::session` in `src/engine/testing.rs` (`:143-151`, used by `src/engine/journal.rs` and `src/engine/swap.rs` tests), and test-only constructions such as `src/engine/swap.rs:1404-1410`. `tests/engine_crash.rs::a_torn_actions_log_never_stops_recovery` (`:1580-1620`) cuts the log mid-line itself and must keep passing.
- `fsx` has no logging channel; commands log through `Out` (`src/app/mod.rs:301-303`).
- `-v` prints each window's `fsyncs` and `-vv` its kinds (`omad-7ccp.1`); `tests/engine_durability.rs::PINNED` holds today's counts.

## Technical Approach

### 1. The buffer (`src/fsx/session.rs`, `src/fsx/mutate.rs`)

- `TxState` gains `buffer: Vec<u8>` (serialized lines, each ending in `\n`) and `buffered: usize` (lines in it).
- `log_action(state, record)` serializes as today and appends to `state.buffer` (and increments `buffered`) instead of calling `append_durable`; a serialization error is still an `FsxError::Io` on the log path. The line format is unchanged; lines for failed operations are buffered too, so a failed step's `ok: false` line still reaches the log at the next sync.
- The module documentation of `src/fsx/mutate.rs` (`:1-8`) changes step 7 to "(7) an `actions.jsonl` line, buffered in the session and synced at the transaction's end (M4-D54)"; `src/fsx/session.rs`'s module doc says the same of a transaction session.

### 2. `sync_actions`, `finish` and `Drop`

```rust
impl WriteSession<'_> {
    /// Appends every buffered action line with one write and one fdatasync, then clears
    /// the buffer. A no-op for an untracked session or an empty buffer.
    pub fn sync_actions(&mut self) -> Result<(), FsxError>;
    /// Syncs what is left and ends the session. Every owner of a tracked session calls
    /// it on every path: Drop cannot report an error.
    pub fn finish(self) -> Result<(), FsxError>;
}
```

- `sync_actions`: `sys::create_dir_all(parent)` as `log_action` does today, then `sys::append_synced(path, &buffer)`: open with `O_APPEND | O_CREAT`, one `write_all`, one `File::sync_data()` (`fdatasync`, counted as an `fsync` with kind `actions_log`), and when it created the file, a sync of its directory (immediate in this part; `omad-7ccp.4` routes it through a sink). It clears the buffer on success and on error alike (a partial append leaves at most a torn last line, which every reader tolerates) and returns the error as `FsxError::Io` on the log path.
- `finish`: `sync_actions`, then marks the session finished (a field `finished: bool` in `TxState`).
- `impl Drop for WriteSession<'_>`: for a tracked session with buffered lines, a best-effort `sync_actions` (its error ignored), then:
  - debug builds, unless `std::thread::panicking()`: `panic!("a tracked session (tx {tx}) was dropped with {n} unsynced action lines: call finish()")`;
  - release builds: increments a process-wide `AtomicU64` in `fsx` (`fsx::take_unsynced_drops() -> u64` reads and resets it); the command boundary (`src/app/mod.rs`, after the outcome is rendered) logs `fsx_unsynced_actions: <n> tracked sessions were dropped without finish()` at debug level when it is non-zero. **Decided while writing this bead:** fsx has no logging channel, so a counter drained by the command layer carries the plan's "debug event"; the message is a `log` event's text, not a new NDJSON event name.
  - A session whose buffer is empty drops silently, finished or not.

### 3. The sync points

- **Before the closing line.** `journal::append_line` (`src/engine/journal.rs:442-448`) calls `s.sync_actions()?` before appending a `JournalLine::Swapped`. (The repair family's `done` and `rolled_back` are appended by E5's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`) code; see §4.)
- **Before the history line.** `history::append_line` (`src/state/history.rs:294-322`) calls `s.sync_actions()?` before the history line's `mutate`. In an untracked session (settings commands, recovery's roll-forward, `append_once`) it is a no-op.
- **At `finish()`.** Every owner, §4.

### 4. The owners

Each owner of a tracked session finishes it on every path, so the debug assertion never fires in production code:

- `tx::commit_target`, `undo::commit`: the session is created before the lock and used before it. Restructure the locked part into an inner function (or a closure returning `Result`) that borrows the session; after it returns, still under the lock, call `s.finish()`. On the success path an error from `finish()` fails the command (below); on an error path `finish()` runs best-effort and the primary error is returned. Every early return between the session's creation and the lock (a failed prestage, a lock timeout) finishes the session best-effort first; a small helper `finish_then<T>(s, result: Result<T>) -> Result<T>` keeps that to one line per site.
- `restore::Window::commit`, `restore_addons` commit: the session is created inside the window; the same rule from its creation to the release.
- E5's `engine::repair::commit`: the tracked session's `finish()` runs immediately before `done` is appended (the position E5 commented); its error is a failed step before `done`, handled as E5 handles any failed step. The untracked session that writes the repair journal and the history line has nothing to buffer.
- **Decided while writing this bead:** the folder owners finish the tracked session after `committed`, under the lock. An error from `finish()` after `committed` fails the command with `io` (`details.path` the actions log), message "transaction <tx> committed, but its audit log could not be made durable: <err>", not retryable, fix `omaddons status`: M4-D54 says a sync failure prevents success, and the transaction stands, which the message says. (`omad-7ccp.5` adds the window's final barrier after `finish()`.)
- **The counts this gives.** With the three sync points, a folder window syncs the log up to three times (before `swapped`: every step and rename line; before the history line: the `swapped` append, the record and the files index; at `finish()`: the history and `committed` appends), each one `fdatasync`, plus one directory sync when the log is created. Update `tests/engine_durability.rs::PINNED` in this commit: `actions_log` drops from one per action to the number of non-empty sync points per window; the commit body lists the before and after of each changed row and the reason ("group commit, M4-D54 change 1").

### 5. Tests that build tracked sessions

- Every unit test that builds a tracked session and mutates through it ends with `s.finish().unwrap()` (or `sync_actions` then a deliberate drop in the tests of the assertion itself). Tests that read `actions.jsonl` (`Fixture::actions`, `src/engine/undo.rs:2956-2966`, `src/engine/restore.rs:2024`) call `s.sync_actions().unwrap()` first, or read after the owner finished.
- Integration and crash tests run the binary, whose owners finish their sessions; their oracles are unchanged. If a test asserts the content of `actions.jsonl` after a crash, it encodes the per-line fsync M4-D54 removes: change it to the group-commit rule (lines of an attempt that crashed before its closing line may be absent) with the reason in the commit body, and list it in the close comment. Crash-matrix oracles (the recovered state) must pass unchanged.

### 6. README

Safety model → Transactions gains a **Durability** bullet after **Concurrency**: "Each transaction's audit log (`actions.jsonl`, one line per filesystem operation) is written once at the end of its changes: synced before the journal line that closes them and before the history line, instead of once per operation. Recovery reads only the journal, never the audit log, and the journal is still written ahead, one synced line per step, so a crash before that line loses at most the audit lines of an attempt recovery then rolls back." (`omad-7ccp.3`, `omad-7ccp.5` and `omad-7ccp.7` extend it.)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A tracked session buffers its action lines; `sync_actions()` appends them with one write and one `fdatasync` (one more sync of the directory when it created the log) and clears the buffer; `finish()` syncs and ends the session; untracked sessions never buffer.
- [ ] The log is synced before every `swapped` line, before every history line written in a tracked session, at E5's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`) `finish()` before `done`, and at every owner's `finish()`; the journal is still appended and synced one line per step, before each step's operation.
- [ ] Every production owner finishes its tracked session on every path; a `finish()` error after `committed` fails the command with `io`, saying the transaction committed.
- [ ] `dropping_a_tracked_session_with_unsynced_lines_fails_a_debug_assertion` passes (`#[should_panic]`); a dropped session still writes its lines (best effort); release builds report dropped sessions as the debug line `fsx_unsynced_actions: …`.
- [ ] `the_audit_log_is_durable_by_the_closing_line` and `the_audit_log_holds_every_action_after_each_window` pass.
- [ ] `tests/engine_durability.rs::PINNED` is updated in this commit, each changed row's before and after and reason in the commit body; no row rises.
- [ ] Every crash matrix passes unchanged (`tests/engine_crash.rs`, `tests/journal.rs`, `tests/doctor_repair.rs`, `tests/doctor_harness.rs`); any test changed for the group-commit rule is listed in the close comment with its reason.
- [ ] The claim comment records the review of every design-gate paragraph (agreed or challenged).
- [ ] README's Durability bullet says what landed, in the same commit; `mutate.rs`'s step 7 documentation is rewritten.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files; `br lint` is clean for this subtask.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

- `src/fsx/mutate.rs` (with `Fixture`):
  - `a_tracked_session_buffers_its_lines_until_sync`: two `WriteFile`s; the log does not exist (first) and `SyncCounts::fsync` grew only by the writes' own syncs; `sync_actions()` → the log holds two lines with `seq` 1 and 2, and `fsync` grew by 2 (one `fdatasync`, one directory sync for the new file); a third op and a second `sync_actions()` → three lines, `fsync` +1.
  - `sync_actions_with_nothing_buffered_does_nothing`: no file, no count.
  - `finish_syncs_and_consumes`: the lines are in the log after `finish()`.
  - `a_failed_operation_logs_its_line_at_sync`: a `Rename` whose target exists (`NoReplace`) fails; after `sync_actions()` its line has `ok: false`.
  - `dropping_a_tracked_session_with_unsynced_lines_fails_a_debug_assertion` (`#[cfg(debug_assertions)]`, `#[should_panic(expected = "unsynced action lines")]`).
  - `a_dropped_session_still_writes_its_lines`: `std::panic::catch_unwind(|| drop(session))` (debug) or a plain drop (release), then the log holds the lines.
  - `dropping_an_empty_or_finished_session_is_silent`.
  - `untracked_sessions_never_buffer` (extends `untracked_sessions_record_nothing`, `:1448`).
  - `#[cfg(not(debug_assertions))] a_dropped_session_counts_an_unsynced_drop` (runs under `cargo test --release`).
- `src/fsx/sys.rs`: `append_synced_writes_once_and_syncs_once` (two calls: two `fdatasync`s; the directory synced only by the first, which created the file; the content is the two buffers in order).
- `src/engine/journal.rs` (with `src/engine/testing.rs`'s `Scene`): `a_swapped_line_syncs_the_action_log_first` (create a journal, two steps and their renames through the scene's tracked session, then `mark_swapped`: right after it returns, the log on disk holds a line for `prepared`, each step and each rename, and not yet the `swapped` append's own line).
- `src/state/history.rs`: `a_history_line_syncs_the_action_log_first` (a tracked session's two writes, then `history::append`: the log holds the two writes' lines before the history append's).
- Every existing unit test that builds a tracked session is updated as §5 says; the gate fails until each is.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

- `tests/engine_durability.rs`:
  - `the_audit_log_is_durable_by_the_closing_line`: a `Scene` with `Foo` v1 installed; step `crash after swapped`: `install_replace` with `.failpoints("engine.swapped=abort")` → `Ran::aborted()`; step `audit`: read `<state>/snapshots/<tx>/actions.jsonl` (the tx from the journal's `prepared`): every journal step has a matching `rename` line (`op`, `path`, `to`), `seq` contiguous from 1; step `recover`: `install --file bar.zip -t retail --offline` exits 0 with `journal_recovered`; `scene.folders()` equals the v2 state (rolled forward).
  - `the_audit_log_holds_every_action_after_each_window`: for `install_replace`, `undo`, `whole_restore` and `repair_write` (E6's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`) test fixer with `OMADDONS_TEST_FIXERS=1`): after the command, the transaction's log (`<state>/snapshots/<tx>/actions.jsonl`, `<state>/snapshots/<tx>.wtf/actions.jsonl`, `<run>/actions.jsonl`) has contiguous `seq` 1..n, every line `ok: true`, and for the folder families a last line that appended `committed` to the journal.
  - `pinned_fsync_counts_per_commit_window`: the updated rows.
- Reruns, unchanged: `tests/engine_crash.rs`, `tests/journal.rs`, `tests/doctor_repair.rs`, `tests/doctor_harness.rs`.

### Logging

Integration scenarios use T1's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`) `TestLog`: steps as named above, every command through `log.run` or `log.cmd(..).failpoints(..)`, `log.json("audit", lines)` with the parsed log lines, `log.json("journal", steps)`, and on a mismatch the first missing step and the transcript path. Unit tests name their case in every assertion message and show the log's content on failure.

## Considerations

- **Compatibility.** The line format is unchanged; only the timing of the writes moves. The M3 build never reads `actions.jsonl`. A crash may now leave fewer lines of an attempt that recovery rolls back, which M4-D54 accepts.
- **E5's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`) failpoints.** `fsx.mutate.logged@k` keeps its position (after step 7, which now buffers); a crash there loses the unsynced lines, which recovery never reads. E5's crash matrix oracles do not read the log; if one of its tests reads `<run>/actions.jsonl` after a crash, apply §5's rule.
- **The structure of the owners.** Restructuring `commit_target` and `undo::commit` into "session → inner → finish" is the largest edit; keep the inner bodies as they are (move, do not rewrite), so the diff is reviewable, and rebase on the latest `main` first (hot spots: `src/engine/tx.rs` "G3 last", `src/fsx/` "E13 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.13`) first, G3 last").
- **What could go wrong:** an owner path that returns before `finish()` (the debug assertion fires in tests; run the whole gate); a test that reads the log too early (it sees fewer lines; sync first); a sync point missed (`a_swapped_line_syncs_the_action_log_first` pins it).
- **Decided while writing this bead** (confirm or adjust in the close comment): the unsynced-drop counter drained by the command layer; clearing the buffer on a failed sync; `finish()` after `committed` under the lock, its error failing the command; the `finish_then` helper.

## Dependencies

- Parent: G3 (`omad-7ccp`, group commit, derived writes and deferred directory fsyncs).
- Before it: `omad-7ccp.1` (the counts to update, the `-v` lines that show the change, and the design-gate record this part's claimer reviews).
- After it: `omad-7ccp.3` (derived writes; it edits `history::append_line` too, so it rebases on this), `omad-7ccp.4` (the durability context routes `append_synced`'s directory sync and shares `session.rs` and `mutate.rs`).
- This part writes integration tests, so it carries an edge from T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs).

title: Derived writes: `Durability::Derived` for the history projection, the backup inventory and the doorbell, and the projection's follow-up moved after the lock
description:
Part 3 of 7 of omad-7ccp (Group commit, derived writes and deferred directory fsyncs (`omad-7ccp`)). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

G3 (`omad-7ccp`) makes every commit window of omaddons as durable as today with far fewer syncs, under M4-D54, and owns §3.2 checkpoint criterion 13 (durability). Comment 1167 on G3 counted 4 of an install's 62 fsyncs on the history projection `history_tail.json`, a cache rewritten with full durability inside the window. It serves G-M4-6 ("no new risk to the engine's guarantees"; "the global lock is still held only for commit windows").

This part is M4-D54's second change, **derived files are not fsynced**: `history_tail.json`, `backups.json` and the doorbell are rebuilt from durable state when missing or stale (M3-D37), so they are written with a new `Durability::Derived` (temp-plus-rename atomicity, no fsync, no later `syncfs`), and the commit windows' one derived write under the lock, the history projection's follow-up of the window's history line, moves after the lock is released. It is its own step because M4-D54 orders the three changes and lands each with its counts. **Rejected:** `Durability::Deferred` for them (`src/fsx/sys.rs:131-140`): it promises a later `syncfs`, so it is the wrong contract; keeping them in the window with full durability (four fsyncs of an install for files nothing needs to be durable).

**Why it is safe (M3-D37).** Each derived file is checked before it is believed: `history_tail::fresh` believes the projection only while `history.jsonl` is exactly as long as it covers and ends with its last line; `backups.json` is validated against one `read_dir` of the backups and snapshots; the doorbell is only a signal that makes the widget re-read `status --cached`. A power cut can leave an unsynced file absent, empty, cut short, or at an older version; every reader treats each of those as missing or stale and rebuilds.

**Facts this part relies on** (as of `c0ab5e9`):
- `Durability::{Immediate, Deferred}` (`src/fsx/sys.rs:131-140`); every primitive skips its fsyncs for any value but `Immediate` (`write_atomic_to`, `:189-201`). `mutate_with` admits `Deferred` only for `WriteFile`, `CreateDir` and `CloneFile` in untracked sessions on a stage path (`src/fsx/mutate.rs:359-371`).
- `history_tail::write` (`src/state/history_tail.rs:339-358`), `inventory::write` (`src/backup/inventory.rs:332-350`) and `doorbell::write` (`src/state/doorbell.rs:49-61`) each make an untracked `Writer::Derived` session, `ensure_dir_all(cache_dir)`, and `mutate(.., WriteFile)` with full durability.
- `history::append_line` (`src/state/history.rs:294-322`) appends the line and then calls `history_tail::appended(paths, before, &line)` (`:321`; `src/state/history_tail.rs:158-180`): a projection that covered exactly the history before takes the line, any other is marked stale (`covers.bytes: null`), best effort.
- `history::append` is called inside the commit windows at `src/engine/tx.rs:1266`, `src/engine/undo.rs:544`, `src/engine/restore.rs:954` and `src/engine/restore_addons.rs:988`, and by `append_once` (`src/engine/tx.rs:620-635`) for an automatic or `before_restore` backup's line under the window's lock; E5's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`) repair commit appends its history line through its untracked session. Outside commit windows it is called by settings commands (`history::record_setting`, `:269-292`), recovery's roll-forward (`src/engine/journal.rs:1548`), `backup create` (`src/app/backup.rs:1452`) and `append_alone` (`src/engine/tx.rs:640-652`).
- The doorbell and `backups.json` are already written after the lock in the folder windows (`ring_after_window`, `src/engine/tx.rs:895-906`; the inventory rebuilds after a restore and its undo, `src/engine/restore.rs:574-589`, `:1224-1235`); under a lock only recovery writes them (`src/engine/preserve.rs:72-77`; `recover_under`'s ring, `src/engine/journal.rs:889-894`). After a command, `history_tail::rebuild_if_stale` runs once the lock is released (`src/app/mod.rs:368`; `src/state/history_tail.rs:316-328`).
- Readers: `history_tail::load` returns `None` for a missing, unreadable or newer file (`src/state/history_tail.rs:331-336`) and `fresh` validates (`:126-133`); `inventory::load_file` returns the default for any of those (`src/backup/inventory.rs:159-161`, `:324-329`) and `load_validated` compares with the directories (`:153`).
- `omad-7ccp.2` landed the group commit and updated `tests/engine_durability.rs::PINNED`.

## Technical Approach

### 1. `Durability::Derived` (`src/fsx/sys.rs`, `src/fsx/mutate.rs`)

```rust
pub enum Durability {
    #[default]
    Immediate,
    /// … a `syncfs` follows (staging only).
    Deferred,
    /// Temp + rename atomicity, no fsync, and no later `syncfs`: for a file rebuilt from
    /// durable state when it is missing or stale (M3-D37): the history projection, the
    /// backup inventory, the doorbell (M4-D54).
    Derived,
}
```

- The primitives need no change: every fsync is guarded by `durability == Durability::Immediate`.
- `mutate_with`'s admission (`src/fsx/mutate.rs:359-371`) gains: `Durability::Derived` is admitted only for `Op::WriteFile` by `Writer::Derived` in an untracked session; anything else fails with `FsxError::Precondition("derived durability is only for derived files written by Writer::Derived, not {wire} on {path}")`, before any check of the target.

### 2. The three writers

- `history_tail::write`, `inventory::write` and `doorbell::write` call `mutate_with(&mut s, &path, op, MutateOpts { durability: Durability::Derived, ..MutateOpts::default() })`. Their `ensure_dir_all(cache_dir)` keeps immediate durability (it creates the cache directory at most once per home).
- Nothing else changes: their loads, their best-effort error handling and their rings stay.

### 3. The projection's follow-up leaves the commit window (`src/state/history.rs`, `src/state/history_tail.rs`, the owners)

```rust
/// What a history append left for the projection to follow, after the lock.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct TailFollow { pub before: u64, pub line: Vec<u8> }

/// `append`, without following the line in the projection: for a commit window, whose
/// owner applies the follow-up after it releases the lock.
pub fn append_in_window(s: &mut WriteSession<'_>, paths: &Paths, entry: &HistoryEntry)
    -> Result<TailFollow>;

/// Applies follow-ups in order, after the lock (each is today's `appended`); best effort.
pub fn follow(paths: &Paths, follows: &[TailFollow]);
```

- `append_line` is split: the append part returns the `(before, line)` it wrote; `append` (and `append_setting`) then call `history_tail::appended` inline as today, now with derived durability; `append_in_window` returns the follow-up instead.
- The commit windows use `append_in_window`: `src/engine/tx.rs:1266`, `src/engine/undo.rs:544`, `src/engine/restore.rs:954`, `src/engine/restore_addons.rs:988`, `append_once` when it runs inside a window (it returns its `TailFollow` to the window's owner), and E5's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`) repair history line. Each owner collects the follow-ups in order (the backup's line first, then the transaction's) and, after it releases the lock and before `write_status`, calls `history_tail::follow` **only when the window committed** (or was rolled forward in process). **Decided while writing this bead:** a window that failed leaves the projection alone; `fresh()` then sees the history longer than the projection and the command's `rebuild_if_stale` rebuilds it.
- Applying a follow-up after the lock is safe against a concurrent writer: `appended` follows only a projection that covered exactly the history before this line and ends with its last line; if another process appended in between, the projection is marked stale and rebuilt, never wrong (`fresh` checks the length and the last line).
- Recovery's roll-forward, settings commands, `backup create` and `append_alone` keep the inline follow (they are not commit windows), now without fsyncs.

### 4. The counts and README

- Update `tests/engine_durability.rs::PINNED` in this commit: no window has a `history_tail`, `backup_inventory` or `doorbell` kind; the commit body lists each changed row's before and after with the reason ("derived writes, M4-D54 change 2").
- README: the transaction diagram's last line (`README.md:1992`) becomes "then: the history projection, status.json, cleanup, doorbell, retention"; the **Durability** bullet (added by `omad-7ccp.2`) gains: "Its derived caches (`history_tail.json`, `backups.json`, `doorbell.json`) are written atomically but never synced, after the lock is released; each is checked against what it summarizes before it is believed, so one a power cut loses or cuts short is rebuilt."

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `Durability::Derived` exists, documented as atomic and never synced; `mutate_with` admits it only for `WriteFile` by `Writer::Derived` in an untracked session and refuses every other combination before touching the target.
- [ ] `history_tail.json`, `backups.json` and `doorbell.json` are written with it, so a write of each makes no fsync.
- [ ] No commit window writes a derived file under the lock: the history projection's follow-ups of a window are applied after release, only when the window committed; `-vv` shows no `history_tail`, `backup_inventory` or `doorbell` kind in any window.
- [ ] An empty, cut-short, garbage or older projection or inventory is read as stale and rebuilt (unit tests); a follow-up applied after another process's append marks the projection stale rather than wrong.
- [ ] `tests/engine_durability.rs::PINNED` is updated in this commit with each changed row's reason; no row rises.
- [ ] `derived_files_are_written_after_the_lock` passes; every crash matrix passes unchanged.
- [ ] README's diagram and Durability bullet say what landed, in the same commit.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files; `br lint` is clean for this subtask.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

- `src/fsx/mutate.rs`: `derived_durability_is_admitted_only_for_derived_writes`, a table of `(case, writer, session, op, admitted)`: `derived_write` (`Writer::Derived`, untracked, `WriteFile`) admitted, `SyncCounts::fsync` unchanged by the write; `mutating_writer` (`Writer::Mutating`) refused; `create_dir` (`CreateDir`) refused; `append` (`AppendFile`) refused; `tracked` (a tracked session) refused; each refusal is `FsxError::Precondition` and leaves the target untouched (absent or byte-identical).
- `src/fsx/mutate.rs`: `a_derived_write_replaces_atomically_and_syncs_nothing` (old content replaced, no `.omaddons-*` temp left, `fsync` count unchanged).
- `src/state/history_tail.rs`:
  - `a_projection_cut_short_or_emptied_reads_as_stale`, cases `empty`, `cut_mid_json`, `garbage_bytes`, `older_covers` (a valid projection that covers fewer bytes than the history): `fresh()` is `None`, and `rebuild_if_stale` rewrites it to equal `build()`.
  - `follow_applies_appends_in_order` (two `TailFollow`s from two appends, applied in order: the projection is fresh and holds both lines).
  - `a_follow_after_another_append_marks_it_stale` (append A in window (no follow), append B inline by "another process", then follow A: `covers.bytes` is `None`, then rebuilt).
- `src/backup/inventory.rs`: `an_inventory_cut_short_or_emptied_is_rebuilt` (cases `empty`, `cut_mid_json`, `garbage_bytes`: `load_file` gives the default, `load_validated` reports it stale, `rebuild` rewrites it).
- `src/state/doorbell.rs`: `a_ring_syncs_nothing` (`SyncCounts` unchanged by `ring`, the file written).
- `src/state/history.rs`: `append_in_window_leaves_the_projection_alone` (the projection unchanged after the append; the returned follow-up's `before` equals the history's length before and `line` the bytes written).

### Integration and end-to-end tests

- `tests/engine_durability.rs`:
  - `derived_files_are_written_after_the_lock`: steps `install_replace` and `whole_restore` with `-vv --progress json` → no window's kinds include `history_tail`, `backup_inventory` or `doorbell`; then `status --cached --json` → its last change is the install's transaction (the projection was followed after the lock); after the restore, `backup list -t retail --json` and `status --cached --json` agree on the backup count.
  - `pinned_fsync_counts_per_commit_window`: the updated rows.
- Reruns, unchanged: `tests/engine_crash.rs`, `tests/journal.rs`, `tests/doctor_repair.rs`, `tests/doctor_harness.rs`, `tests/doorbell.rs`, `tests/status.rs`.

### Logging

T1's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`) `TestLog`: steps `build`, `run`, `kinds` (`log.json("windows", observed)`), `status --cached` (the envelope recorded by `log.run`). Unit tests name their case in every assertion message and print the projection's content and `covers` on failure.

## Considerations

- **The derived files' formats are unchanged**, so the M3 build reads them exactly as before; it validates them the same way.
- **Filesystems.** Without an fsync, a rename over an existing file may leave an empty or old file after a power cut (ext4 without `auto_da_alloc`, for example); that is the case the readers' validation covers, and the unit tests prove it.
- **Other caches** (`releases.json`, the discovery cache, the wowi index, the errors memo, `net.log`) are outside commit windows and keep their durability; M4-D54 names only the three files.

title: Deferred directory fsyncs in every commit window: a barrier at every ordering point, the final barrier before release, and the failure rules
description:
Part 5 of 7 of omad-7ccp (Group commit, derived writes and deferred directory fsyncs (`omad-7ccp`)). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

G3 (`omad-7ccp`) makes every commit window of omaddons as durable as today with far fewer syncs, under M4-D54, and owns §3.2 checkpoint criterion 13 (durability). It serves G-M4-6 ("no new risk to the engine's guarantees"; "the global lock is still held only for commit windows").

This part is the change that defers: it **opens a `CommitWindow` in every commit window**, places a barrier at every ordering point of the design gate (and a final barrier before the lock is released), so every directory sync a window makes moves from "at once" to "at the next ordering point, once per directory", and it adds **the failure rules**: a barrier's error fails the command and leaves the journal for the next lock-taking command; any other failure syncs the window before in-process recovery starts. It is its own step because it is the one change that moves durability: everything before it either counts (`omad-7ccp.1`), keeps today's ordering (`omad-7ccp.2`, `omad-7ccp.3`) or adds machinery with no caller (`omad-7ccp.4`). `omad-7ccp.6` then proves every barrier by injecting at it.

**The decision this part implements (M4-D54, change 3, its ordering half).** "Ordering points are explicit barriers. `CommitWindow::barrier()` … runs before every journal phase line (a folder journal's `prepared`, `swapped`, `committed`, `preserve` and `preserved`; a repair journal's `prepared`, `done`, `committed` and `rolled_back`) and the history line, before every step line that follows a rename, and as a final barrier before the command acknowledges success or releases the lock. Every namespace change recovery needs is durable before the journal or history boundary that assumes it." "A sync failure prevents success. A barrier error fails the command at that point: the journal and the backups recovery needs stay, exactly as for any other failure inside the window, and the next lock-taking command recovers." "Where the written ordering argument cannot justify deferring a directory's sync, that directory keeps its immediate fsync."

**Before you start: re-check the design gate.** Read the "Design gate: commit-window durability (M4-D54)" comment on G3 and `omad-7ccp.2`'s review of it. Check each paragraph (J1–J7, R1–R7, X) against the code you are about to change, and record in your claim comment that you did, with any point you challenge. A challenged point keeps its immediate fsync (place no deferral before it) until the challenge is answered in a comment on G3.

**Facts this part relies on** (as of `c0ab5e9`, plus `omad-7ccp.1` to `omad-7ccp.4` and the earlier M4 leaves):
- The folder windows: `tx::commit_target` (session `src/engine/tx.rs:998-1004`, lock `:1015`, `recover_all` `:1025`, `append_once` `:1030-1032`, the registry's untracked session `:1038-1043`, journal `:1226`, the commit closure `:1230-1272`, the failure handler `:1273-1300`, release `:1348-1350`); `undo::commit` (`src/engine/undo.rs:391`, lock `:400`, journal `:500`, closure `:502-550`, failure `:551-582`, release `:583-585`); `restore::Window::commit` (`src/engine/restore.rs:728-988`; lock `:739`; `append_once` `:755-761`; registry `:765-770`; session `:866-872`; journal `:873`; closure `:875-960`; failure `:961-982`; release `:983-985`); `restore_addons` commit (`src/engine/restore_addons.rs:741-1020`, lock `:753`, session `:893`, journal `:900`, failure `:995-1016`, release `:1017-1018`). `append_alone` takes a short lock of its own (`src/engine/tx.rs:640-652`).
- Every folder journal line goes through `journal::append_line` (`src/engine/journal.rs:442-448`): `Journal::create` (`:376-394`, which ensures the journal directory and appends `prepared`, creating the file), `Journal::step` (`:406-419`), `mark_swapped`, `mark_committed` (`:422-429`), roll-forward's `committed` (`:1555`), preservation's `preserve` (`:1266`) and `preserved` (`src/engine/preserve.rs:71`).
- Recovery: `recover_all` (`src/engine/journal.rs:811`), `recover_under` (`:858`), `recover_tx`, the preservation protocol (`src/engine/preserve.rs`), E5's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`) shared rollback and recovery routine (`src/engine/repair/inverse.rs` in E5's layout) and E14's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14`) three passes; each builds its own sessions. `cleanup` (`src/engine/tx.rs:1649-1700`) prunes the journal, in-flight lock and stages only when the journal is finished (`journal::unfinished`).
- `recovery_failed` (`src/engine/tx.rs:573-591`) is the existing pattern for an error that leaves its journal: `details.journal_pending`, `details.recovery_error`, not retryable, fix `omaddons status`; A9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9`) declares `journal_pending` in `COMMON` for every code. `io` is exit 1, not retryable (`src/error.rs:202`).
- E5's repair commit (`src/engine/repair/commit.rs`): revalidate, the roots (untracked session), `prepared`, each primitive's `step` then `mutate_with` in the tracked session, `finish()` (from `omad-7ccp.2`) then `done`, the history line, `committed`; on a failed step before `done`, the shared rollback in an untracked session then `rolled_back`; E5 commented the positions of this bead's barriers. E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`) maps "E5's in-process rollback of a failed step (its predicate, an I/O error, a barrier error)" to `DONE_FAILED`, exit 3, and an `Err` that leaves the journal (its `corrupt_rollback` row) to the code's exit (74 for `io` in the doctor's dictionary), `DONE_FAILED` and a `journal_pending` warning.
- E8's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.8`) gc retargets `latest` with `SymlinkAtomic` in an untracked session, then calls `prune(.., LockUse::HandOff(guard))`, which takes the guard by value and releases it between the renames into trash and the deletions.
- M3's privacy redactor for paths below `WTF/` (`privacy::WtfPathRedactor`, M3's A5) is what every path below `WTF/` passes through before it reaches output.
- `omad-7ccp.4`: `CommitWindow::{open, barrier, barrier_after_rename, failed, finish}`, `WriteSession::{attach, with_window, barrier, barrier_after_rename}`, the `DirSink`s.

## Technical Approach

### 1. The shape of every commit window

Each owner takes this shape (the inner body is moved, not rewritten):

```text
let guard = GlobalLock::acquire(..)?;
let window = CommitWindow::open(&guard);
s.attach(&window);                        // or: the session is created with with_window
let result = locked(&mut s, &window, …);  // recover, register, revalidate, journal, undo data,
                                          // steps, record, history, committed (as today)
let result = match result {
    Err(e) if window.failed() => Err(durability_failed(e, tx)),      // §3
    Err(e) => match window.barrier() {                               // §3
        Err(b) => Err(durability_failed(b, tx)),
        Ok(()) => in_process_recovery(e),                            // as today
    },
    ok => ok,
};
let finished = s.finish();                // the action log's last sync (omad-7ccp.2)
let last = window.finish();               // X: the final barrier
let (held, syncs) = (millis(&guard), guard.window_syncs());
drop(guard);
// after release, only when committed: the projection follow-ups (omad-7ccp.3), then as today
```

- Owners: `tx::commit_target`, `undo::commit`, `restore::Window::commit`, `restore_addons` commit, E5's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`) `repair::commit` (which receives the caller's `&GlobalLockGuard`, opens and finishes its own window before returning, so E6's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`) runtime is unchanged), and `append_alone`'s short lock (a window holding only the line's append).
- Every session of the window gets it: the tracked session (`attach`), the registry's untracked session and `append_once`'s (`with_window`; `append_once` takes `&CommitWindow` instead of `&GlobalLockGuard`, the window proving the lock), and E5's untracked journal session.
- **Recovery's sessions never get it.** `recover_all`, `recover_under`, `recover_tx`, preservation and E5's rollback and recovery routine build their own sessions without a window, so they keep immediate durability. **Decided while writing this bead:** recovery prunes journals right after its renames, and a prune is not an ordering point, so deferring recovery's directory syncs would let a power loss keep a journal's deletion and lose the renames it recorded; recovery is also rare and outside the pinned shapes' steady state (M4-D54: where the argument cannot be made, the immediate fsync stays). Prune's sessions never get it either.
- **gc gets none.** **Decided while writing this bead:** E8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.8`) hands its guard to `prune` by value, so a window borrowing the guard cannot span the deletions, and its one mutation, the `latest` retarget, must be durable before the first deletion, which its immediate fsync gives at the same cost. gc's row in the pinned table stays as `omad-7ccp.3` left it.
- The borrow checker enforces the order: a session borrows the window and the window the guard, and all three implement `Drop`, so a path that drops the guard first does not compile.

### 2. The barriers (the ordering points of the design gate)

Labels: J for a folder journal, R for a repair journal, X for the final barrier (points, not beads).

| # | Hook | Code |
|---|---|---|
| J1 | before `prepared` | `journal::append_line`: `s.barrier()?` before a `JournalLine::Prepared` |
| J2 | after `prepared` | `journal::append_line`: `s.barrier()?` right after appending `Prepared` (the journal file's creation). **Not in the plan's list; decided while writing this bead:** without it a power loss could keep step 1's rename and lose the journal file's directory entry (today `append_durable` syncs it at once, `src/fsx/sys.rs:213-215`) |
| J3 | before a step line that follows a rename | `journal::append_line`: `s.barrier_after_rename()?` before a `JournalLine::Step`. **Decided while writing this bead:** "follows a rename" means an `Op::Rename` executed in the window since the last barrier (the window's `renamed` flag) |
| J4 | before `swapped` | `journal::append_line`: `s.sync_actions()?` (from `omad-7ccp.2`), then `s.barrier()?` |
| J5 | before the history line | `history::append_in_window` (from `omad-7ccp.3`): `s.sync_actions()?`, then `s.barrier()?` |
| J6 | before `committed` | `journal::append_line`: `s.barrier()?` before a `JournalLine::Committed` |
| J7 | `preserve`, `preserved` | `journal::append_line`: `s.barrier()?`; a no-op, since only recovery (no window) writes them |
| R1 | before a repair's `prepared` | E5's commit, at its comment: `window.barrier()?` |
| R2 | after `prepared` | E5's commit: `window.barrier()?` |
| R3 | before step k+1 after a rename primitive | E5's commit: `window.barrier_after_rename()?` before each `step` line |
| R4 | before `done` | E5's commit: the tracked session's `finish()?` (from `omad-7ccp.2`), then `window.barrier()?` |
| R5 | before the history line | E5's commit: `window.barrier()?` (or through `append_in_window` if E5's history append uses it) |
| R6 | before `committed` | E5's commit: `window.barrier()?` |
| R7 | before `rolled_back` | E5's in-process rollback path: `window.barrier()?` before appending `rolled_back` |
| X | the final barrier | every owner: `window.finish()` after `s.finish()`, before the guard drops |

- Each call site carries a one-line comment naming its point (`// J4: every rename durable before swapped (src/fsx/window.rs)`); `src/fsx/window.rs`'s module documentation carries the paragraphs of the design-gate comment, kept in step with it.
- A point the design gate could not argue keeps its immediate fsync: implement it by calling `window.barrier()` right after the operation it covers instead of deferring to the next point, and say so at the call site.

### 3. The failure rules

- **A barrier error is never answered by in-process recovery.** **Decided while writing this bead:** when a barrier fails (or the failure path's own barrier fails), the owner writes nothing more to the journal, runs no in-process rollback or roll-forward, and returns `durability_failed(error, tx)`: the `io` error with `details.path` (the directory, through the `WTF/` redactor), `details.journal_pending` (the transaction), not retryable, message "<dir>: making the commit durable failed (<err>); its journal is kept and the next omaddons command that commits a change finishes it", fix `omaddons status`. The journal, the in-flight lock, the stage and every snapshot half stay (`cleanup` keeps them while the journal is unfinished); the projection follow-ups and retention are skipped; the doorbell still rings (`ring_after_window`), because the widget must learn that a journal now waits. Why: §3.2 criterion 13 and §6.17's test say the command fails, the journal and backups remain, and the next lock-taking command recovers; the folder engine's failure handler would otherwise roll forward in process after `swapped` and report success (`src/engine/tx.rs:1273-1299`); and a filesystem that just failed to commit a directory is not one to keep writing to (a real `EIO` on a directory sync usually leaves the filesystem read-only, where in-process recovery would fail too). The plan's "before `done` it triggers the in-process rollback" happens, by the next lock-taking command.
- **Any other failure inside the window** (a step's predicate, an I/O error of an operation) first runs `window.barrier()`, so in-process recovery starts from a durable namespace; if that barrier fails, the rule above applies; otherwise in-process recovery runs exactly as today, in its own sessions with immediate durability. E5's in-process rollback (before `done`) does the same: barrier, then rollback, then R7, then `rolled_back`.
- **After `committed`**, an error from `s.finish()` or from the final barrier fails the command with `io`, the message saying the transaction committed and what could not be made durable ("transaction <tx> committed, but making it durable failed: <dir>: <err>"), `details.path`, not retryable, fix `omaddons status`. **Decided while writing this bead:** when the locked work already failed for another reason and the final barrier fails too, the primary error is returned and the barrier's is logged at `-v`.
- **E6's mapping.** A barrier error reaches E6 as an `Err` with `details.journal_pending`: its `corrupt_rollback` row (the code's exit, `DONE_FAILED`, one `journal_pending` warning naming the transaction). Correct E6's documentation (`src/doctor/` runtime) and any of its tests that say a barrier error rolls back in process, in this commit, and say so in the close comment.

### 4. The counts

- Update `tests/engine_durability.rs::PINNED` in this commit: directory kinds (`*_dir`, `state_root`) fall to one per distinct directory per barrier interval; compare every row with the design gate's derived target and explain any difference in the commit body and in a comment on G3 that updates the gate record (the derived figure is the target; a count above it is a bug or a point the gate must revise).
- `omad-7ccp.7` measures the same on btrfs and asserts `install_replace`'s target.

### 5. README

- The transaction diagram: before "journal: committed → release the lock", add "sync the window's directories (one barrier at each journal line)"; or, if the diagram reads better, a line "every journal line: its directories synced first".
- The **Durability** bullet: "Directory entries are made durable once per directory at each journal line instead of after every write and rename: the commit holds an open handle to each directory it changed and syncs them before the journal or history line that relies on them, and once more before it releases the lock. If such a sync fails, the command fails (`io`, with `journal_pending`), and the next command that commits a change finishes or rolls back the transaction from its journal. Recovery itself still syncs every change at once."

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every folder commit window (`commit_target`, `undo::commit`, the whole restore and its undo, the `--addon` restore and its undo, `append_alone`) and E5's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`) repair commit opens a `CommitWindow`, gives it to every session of the window except recovery's and prune's, and finishes the tracked session and then the window before releasing the lock, on every path.
- [ ] Barriers run at J1–J7 and R1–R7 and the final barrier X, each call site naming its point; `a_journal_barriers_at_each_ordering_point` pins the sequence for a folder journal and `a_repair_barriers_at_each_ordering_point` for a repair journal.
- [ ] Recovery, preservation, E5's rollback routine, prune and gc keep immediate durability (unit test `recovery_runs_without_the_window`).
- [ ] A barrier error fails the command with `io`, `details.path` (redacted below `WTF/`) and `details.journal_pending`, runs no in-process recovery, and leaves the journal, the in-flight lock, the stage and the snapshot halves; any other failure syncs the window before in-process recovery; an error at `finish()` or the final barrier after `committed` fails the command and says the transaction committed.
- [ ] E6's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`) documentation and tests treat a barrier error as its `corrupt_rollback` case.

- [ ] Every crash matrix passes unchanged (`tests/engine_crash.rs`, `tests/journal.rs`, `tests/doctor_repair.rs`, `tests/doctor_harness.rs`).
- [ ] README's diagram and Durability bullet say what landed, in the same commit.
- [ ] The claim comment records the re-check of every design-gate paragraph.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

With `src/engine/testing.rs`'s scenes (a guard, a window, a tracked session attached) and a `#[cfg(test)]` barrier log in `CommitWindow` (each barrier call records its caller's point label, passed as a `&'static str` argument to a test-only `barrier_at(point)` wrapper, or inferred from the line being appended):

  - `a_journal_barriers_at_each_ordering_point`: `Journal::create` → step 1 → rename 1 → step 2 → rename 2 → `mark_swapped` → a history append → `mark_committed`; the barrier log is `J1, J2, J3 (before step 2), J4, J5, J6`, and no barrier ran before step 1.
  - `a_first_step_after_no_rename_needs_no_barrier`: steps after only writes (no `Op::Rename`) → no J3 barrier; the writes' directories are synced at J4.

  - `a_failed_step_syncs_the_window_before_recovering`: `fsx.mutate.executed=error@3` → the barrier log shows a failure barrier before the in-process rollback, and the rollback's renames sync at once.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

## Considerations

- **What could go wrong, and how to notice.** A missing barrier fails no crash test (a killed process keeps the page cache): the barrier-sequence unit tests pin each family's points, and `omad-7ccp.6` injects at every barrier that does work. A barrier in the wrong place (after the line instead of before) shows in the same sequence tests. A session left without the window shows as a count that did not fall in the pinned table.
- **Restructuring the owners** is the largest edit of G3: keep each inner body as it is, move it, and review the diff as a move; rebase first (hot spots: `src/engine/tx.rs` and `swap.rs` "G3 last", `src/engine/journal.rs` after E11 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.11`), E13 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.13`), E5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`), E14 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14`) and F1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1`), `src/fsx/` "G3 last", `src/engine/repair/commit.rs` after E5, E14 and E7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7`)).
- **E14's activation barrier** is a recovery-order rule (pass 1 settles a reactivating repair before pass 2 may recover the folder journal it exposed); this part's barriers are durability barriers. R3 makes every rename of a reactivation durable before the next step line, which E14's crash cases assume and `omad-7ccp.6` reruns.
- **The plan's own phrasing disagrees with its test** (§6.17: "before `done` it triggers the in-process rollback" vs "the command fails, the journal and the backups remain, and the next lock-taking command recovers"); §3's rule satisfies the test and the criterion, and is recorded as decided.
- **Decided while writing this bead** (confirm or adjust in the close comment): J2 and R2 (a barrier after `prepared`); "follows a rename" as an `Op::Rename` since the last barrier; recovery, rollback, prune and gc without a window; no in-process recovery after a barrier error; a barrier before in-process recovery of any other failure; the primary error winning over a later final-barrier failure; E6's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`) mapping.

## Dependencies

- Parent: G3 (`omad-7ccp`, group commit, derived writes and deferred directory fsyncs).
- Before it: `omad-7ccp.3` (derived writes: `append_in_window` is where J5's barrier goes, and M4-D54's order puts the deferral last) and `omad-7ccp.4` (the context and the sinks).
- After it: `omad-7ccp.6` (the adversarial matrix) and `omad-7ccp.7` (the btrfs measurement and README's figures).

- [ ] Recovery, preservation, E5's rollback routine, prune and gc keep immediate durability (unit test `recovery_runs_without_the_window`).

title: E2E: the durability design gate's adversarial matrix: an injected sync failure and a crash at every barrier of every commit window, repeated recovery, privacy, the oversized window and every crash matrix rerun
description:
Part 6 of 7 of omad-7ccp (Group commit, derived writes and deferred directory fsyncs (`omad-7ccp`)). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

G3 (`omad-7ccp`) makes every commit window of omaddons as durable as today with far fewer syncs, under M4-D54: the audit log group-committed, derived caches never synced, directory syncs deferred through owned handles to explicit barriers at every ordering point, a barrier's error failing the command. It owns §3.2 checkpoint criterion 13 (durability) and serves G-M4-6 ("no new risk to the engine's guarantees").

This part is **the adversarial matrix of G3's design gate** (common rule 14: a leaf that changes a durability rule closes only when its own matrix passes: every failpoint it adds, repeated recovery, and injected I/O failure where it writes). G3 adds one failpoint, `fsx.barrier.sync`, at every barrier of every commit window; this part injects a sync failure and a crash at each of them, in every window shape, and proves that each command fails or dies, that the journal and what recovery needs stay, and that the next lock-taking command recovers to a whole state, twice repeated. It also proves the privacy of a barrier's error below `WTF/`, the oversized window, and reruns every crash matrix of the milestone unchanged. It is its own subtask because the guide of this milestone makes a design gate's matrix its own piece of work, and because a crash matrix cannot prove fsync placement: what it can prove is that every barrier exists, fails loudly and is recovered, which complements the written argument of `omad-7ccp.1`. G3's design gate is passed only when this subtask is closed.

**What the plan asks, restated** (§3.2 criterion 13, §6.17): "a sync failure injected (`fsx.barrier.sync`, a debug failpoint returning `EIO`) at every explicit barrier of an install, an undo and a repair: the command fails, the journal and the backups remain, and the next lock-taking command recovers to a consistent state"; "every crash matrix in `tests/engine_crash.rs` passes unchanged"; "rerun every crash matrix, including E5's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`) repair matrix and E14's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14`) barrier cases, as a regression check". This part covers those three shapes and every other commit window G3 changed.

**Facts this part relies on** (after `omad-7ccp.5`):
- `fsx.barrier.sync` is hit once per barrier that holds at least one handle, so `@N` addresses the Nth barrier that does work; `error` makes it fail with `EIO`, `abort` kills the process (not dumpable), as every failpoint (`src/fsx/failpoint.rs:1-12`, `:114-138`).
- A barrier error fails the command with `io`, `details.path` (redacted below `WTF/`) and `details.journal_pending` (the transaction), runs no in-process recovery, and leaves the journal, the in-flight lock, the stage and the snapshot halves (`omad-7ccp.5`). The doctor's commands report it through E6's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`) `corrupt_rollback` case: the code's exit in the doctor's dictionary (74 for `io`), `DONE_FAILED`, and one `journal_pending` warning naming the transaction.
- The closing line of a folder journal is `swapped` (recovery rolls forward from it, back before it); of a repair journal, `done`. Recovery is run by every lock-taking command: `install`, `update`, `config set`, `targets`, `auth github`, `export --write` and the doctor's repairs (`recover_all`, `recover_under`).
- `common::engine::Scene` (`tests/common/engine.rs:51-160`) and its oracle views: `folders()` (each Foo folder's tree hash), `generation()`, `record(addon)`, `view()`, `journals()`, `history_txs()`, `wtf()` (the client's `WTF/` tree hash); `shapes::update_many` (`:441-460`). `tests/engine_crash.rs` already sweeps failpoints over these scenes (`crash_matrix_install`, `:903`, and the restore and preservation sections), and E5 and E14 added the repair-family and barrier sections.
- E6's test fixers (`fm-test-write`, `fm-test-quarantine`, debug builds with `OMADDONS_TEST_FIXERS=1`) with their planting helpers; F2's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.2`) set-aside fixtures in `tests/doctor/fixtures/` and its oracle (the suspended set's artifacts present or absent, byte-identical); E7's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7`) `doctor undo <run>` of a set-aside (the reactivation) and its oracle.
- T1's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`) `TestLog` API: `log.case(name)`, `log.run(&scene, &argv)`, `log.cmd(&scene, &argv).failpoints(spec).env(k, v).run()`, `Ran::{ok, fails, aborted, envelope, warnings, events, assert_private}`, `log.tree`, `log.assert_unchanged`, `log.json`.
- `common::privacy::assert_private_all(stdout, stderr)` with the fake names `FAKEACCT`, `FakeRealm`, `FakeChar` (M3's A5).

## Technical Approach

### 1. The shapes and their oracles

| Shape | Build (fresh per case) | Command | Subject set and its "after" | Closing line |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `first_install` | `Scene::new().with_saved_variables(&["Foo"])` | `install gh:o/foo --file v1.zip -t retail --offline` | `folders()`, `generation()`; after = the reference run's | `swapped` |
| `install_replace` | `first_install` committed | `install … --file v2.zip …` | the same | `swapped` |
| `update_three` | `shapes::update_many` | its argv | the three folders, `generation()` | `swapped` |
| `undo` | `install_replace` committed, `scene.play(&["Foo"])` | `undo` | `folders()`, `generation()`, `wtf()` | `swapped` |
| `whole_restore` | a backup, then a play | `backup restore <id> -t retail` | `wtf()`, `generation()` | `swapped` |
| `partial_restore` | the same | `backup restore <id> -t retail --addon Foo` | `wtf()`, `generation()` | `swapped` |
| `repair_write` | `OMADDONS_TEST_FIXERS=1`, a `.write` subject | `doctor fix --only fm-test-write` | the subjects' tree (`<state>/doctor-test`, modes included) | `done` |
| `repair_quarantine` | a `.quarantine` subject | `doctor fix --only fm-test-quarantine` | the subjects' tree | `done` |
| `set_aside` | F2's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.2`) `journal-unreadable` fixture | `doctor fix --only fm-concurrency_primitives-journal-unreadable --force --yes` | the suspended set's live locations (journal, in-flight lock, snapshot halves): present and byte-identical (before) or absent (after) | `done` |
| `reactivation` | `set_aside` committed | `doctor undo <run>` | the same locations: absent (before) or present byte-identical with the pre-set-aside hashes (after) | `done` |

- The "after" of the folder, restore and repair shapes is taken from a **reference run** of the same command on an identical fresh home with no failpoint (tree hashes compare content and modes, so they match across homes). The set-aside and reactivation oracles compare live locations by name and content, never the quarantine's paths (which hold run ids).
- **Every case builds its home fresh.** A copied home changes inode numbers and birth times, which journals, endpoint predicates and suspension guards record.

### 2. Injected sync failures (`tests/engine_durability.rs`)

`an_injected_barrier_failure_fails_the_command_and_the_next_command_recovers`, one `#[test]` per shape (so the gate runs them in parallel), each a sweep:

```text
for N in 1.. :
  case "<shape> error@N": fresh home; tree(subjects) → before
  run the command with fsx.barrier.sync=error@N (-v --json --progress json)
  if it exits 0: N - 1 is the number of barriers that do work in this shape; stop
  assert: folder shapes fail(1, "io"), error.details.journal_pending = the tx, error.details.path present;
          doctor shapes exit with the doctor dictionary's code for io, report state DONE_FAILED,
          and one journal_pending warning naming the tx
  read the journal's lines (phase reached) before anything else touches it
  status --json: a journal_pending warning for that tx, and nothing written
  recover: install --file bar.zip -t retail --offline (set_aside, reactivation: config set check_interval_hours 6):
           exit 0, a journal_recovered warning
  assert: no journal of that tx is left; subjects == before if the phase was before the closing line,
          == the reference run's after from it on; never a mixture (per folder, per file)
  repeat recovery: config set check_interval_hours 6, twice: exit 0, no journal_recovered, subjects unchanged
assert: the number of failing positions ≥ MIN_BARRIERS[shape]
```

- `MIN_BARRIERS` is a per-shape constant in the test, set from the design gate's table (the ordering points that hold work in that shape: for `install_replace` at least J1/J2, J3, J4, J5 and J6 or X), so a barrier that silently stopped doing work fails the test.
- `status` must report the pending journal and write nothing (`log.tree("state", env.state())` before and `log.assert_unchanged` after it).
- For a whole or partial restore the recovering command needs the client not running (the scenes run no game).

### 3. Crashes at every barrier (`tests/engine_crash.rs`)

A new section at the end, `a_crash_at_every_durability_barrier_<shape>` for the same ten shapes: the same sweep with `fsx.barrier.sync=abort@N`, each run `Ran::aborted()` (`SIGABRT`), then the same reads, `status`, recovery, oracle and repeated recovery. A crash at a barrier happens before that barrier's syncs, with the page cache intact, so this proves that every barrier position is a recoverable crash point, exactly like the engine's other failpoints.

### 4. Privacy (`tests/engine_durability.rs`)

`a_barrier_failure_below_wtf_names_no_account`: a scene whose SavedVariables live at `WTF/Account/FAKEACCT/FakeRealm/FakeChar/SavedVariables/Foo.lua` (and the account-wide `WTF/Account/FAKEACCT/SavedVariables/Foo.lua`); `install_replace`, a play, then `undo` swept with `fsx.barrier.sync=error@N` under `--progress json`. Every failing run passes `assert_private_all(stdout, stderr)`; at least one failing run's `details.path` lies below the client's `WTF/` (in its redacted form), proving the case was reached.

### 5. The oversized window (`tests/engine_durability.rs`)

`a_window_over_dirty_dirs_max_directories_commits_and_recovers`: SavedVariables of `Foo` in 70 character directories (`WTF/Account/FAKEACCT/FakeRealm/FakeChar<i>/SavedVariables/Foo.lua`); `install_replace`, a play, `undo -vv --progress json`: exit 0, every file restored (tree hash of `WTF/` equals the pre-install one); the window's kinds show at least 65 directory syncs below `WTF/` and the client snapshot (more than `DIRTY_DIRS_MAX`, so an early flush ran); `assert_private_all`. Then the same undo on a fresh scene crashed at its last barrier (`fsx.barrier.sync=abort@<last>`, the last found by a first sweep run) recovers to the whole after state.

### 6. Every crash matrix rerun

In the gate, unchanged: `tests/engine_crash.rs` (every section: the engine failpoints, every journaled rename, recovery crashed, the restore and preservation sections, E5's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`) repair-family matrix, E14's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14`) barrier cases, D8's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8`) predicates), `tests/journal.rs` (E11's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.11`) differential, extended by E5 and E14), `tests/doctor_repair.rs`, `tests/doctor_harness.rs`, `tests/engine_concurrency.rs`, `tests/preconditions.rs`, `tests/apply.rs`. Once, by hand, the exhaustive harness: `cargo test --test doctor_harness -- --ignored`; the close comment quotes its summary line and run time.

### 7. README

- The **Crash testing** bullet (`README.md:2004`) gains: "Every durability barrier of every commit window (installs, updates, undos, restores, repairs, set-asides and reactivations) is also failed with an injected `EIO` and crashed in turn: the command fails or dies, its journal stays, and the next command finishes or rolls back the transaction to a whole state."
- The Tests table's `tests/engine_crash.rs` row (`README.md:2626`) adds "the durability barriers"; the `tests/engine_durability.rs` row (from `omad-7ccp.1`) adds "injected sync failures at every barrier".

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] For each of the ten shapes, an injected sync failure at every barrier that does work (`fsx.barrier.sync=error@N`, N from 1 until the run succeeds) fails the command as §2 states, keeps its journal, is reported by `status` without a write, and is recovered by the next lock-taking command to the whole before state (journal before its closing line) or the whole after state (from it on); two more lock-taking commands change nothing; the number of failing positions is at least the shape's `MIN_BARRIERS`.
- [ ] For each of the ten shapes, a crash at every barrier (`fsx.barrier.sync=abort@N`) is recovered to the same oracle, with the same repeated recovery.
- [ ] A barrier failure below `WTF/` names no account, realm or character on any channel, and the case is shown to have been reached.
- [ ] A window over `DIRTY_DIRS_MAX` directories commits, restores every file, flushes early, and recovers from a crash at its last barrier.
- [ ] Every crash matrix and harness suite listed in §6 passes unchanged in the gate, and the exhaustive harness ran once by hand; the close comment quotes it.
- [ ] Each sweep logs its number of failing positions and its run time; the suites stay within the gate's budget by running shapes as separate tests, never by skipping a position.
- [ ] README's Crash testing bullet and Tests table say what landed, in the same commit.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `argc e2e engine_durability` and `argc e2e engine_crash` run the new sections with verbose logs; `br lint` is clean for this subtask.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

None new: the barrier sequences and the window's own cases are unit-tested in `omad-7ccp.4` and `omad-7ccp.5`. This part is integration and end-to-end only.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

- `tests/engine_durability.rs`: `an_injected_barrier_failure_…_<shape>` (ten tests, §2), `a_barrier_failure_below_wtf_names_no_account` (§4), `a_window_over_dirty_dirs_max_directories_commits_and_recovers` (§5).
- `tests/engine_crash.rs`: `a_crash_at_every_durability_barrier_<shape>` (ten tests, §3).
- The reruns of §6.

### Logging

Each sweep is a `tlog!()` log with one `log.case("<shape> error@N")` (or `abort@N`) per position: steps `build`, `before` (`log.tree("subjects", …)`), `inject` (`log.cmd(..).failpoints(spec)`, recording the spec, the exit or signal, the envelope and every stderr event), `journal` (`log.json("journal", lines)` with the phase reached), `status`, `recover`, `oracle` (`log.json("expected", before or after)`, the actual hashes, and on a difference the first differing paths), `repeat recovery` (two runs, `log.assert_unchanged("subjects", …)`). The parent log records, per shape, the number of failing positions and the elapsed time. A failure prints the case's transcript path and the last 20 steps (T1's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`) guard).

## Considerations

- **What this matrix can and cannot prove.** It proves every barrier exists, does work, fails loudly and is recovered from, and that no barrier position leaves a state recovery cannot settle. It cannot prove that the barrier placement survives a power loss (a killed process keeps the page cache); that is the written argument's job (`omad-7ccp.1`) and the power-loss campaign's where one can run (`omad-7ccp.7`).
- **Run time.** About ten shapes × eight barriers × two injections × six commands: a few minutes of debug-binary runs, spread over twenty parallel tests. Build homes with the existing builders, never with `cargo` or copies; if the gate's budget is exceeded, make building faster, never sweep fewer positions.
- **Doctor exits.** Take the doctor's exit for `io` and its report state from E6's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`) dictionary in the code (`doctor::Exit`), not from a literal, so a dictionary change cannot make the test pass for the wrong reason.
- **Hot spots:** `tests/engine_crash.rs` (shared with E5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`), E14 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14`) and D8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8`): add the section at the end and rebase); `tests/engine_durability.rs` (G3's own).
- **Decided while writing this bead** (confirm or adjust in the close comment): the ten shapes; the reference-run "after"; `MIN_BARRIERS` per shape from the gate's table; `install --file bar.zip` as the recovering command (`config set check_interval_hours 6` for `set_aside` and `reactivation`, whose client an `install` would refuse while the stuck journal they handle is in place) and `config set check_interval_hours 6` for repeated recovery; one test per shape.

## Dependencies

- Parent: G3 (`omad-7ccp`, group commit, derived writes and deferred directory fsyncs).
- Before it: `omad-7ccp.5` (the barriers and the failure rules it injects at).
- Beside it: `omad-7ccp.7` (measurement and README figures; different files).
- After it: none within G3; closing it passes G3's design gate.
- This part writes integration and end-to-end tests, so it carries an edge from T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs).

- [ ] For each of the ten shapes, an injected sync failure at every barrier that does work (`fsx.barrier.sync=error@N`, N from 1 until the run succeeds) fails the command as §2 states, keeps its journal, is reported by `status` without a write, and is recovered by the next lock-taking command to the whole before state (journal before its closing line) or the whole after state (from it on); two more lock-taking commands change nothing; the number of failing positions is at least the shape's `MIN_BARRIERS`.
- [ ] For each of the ten shapes, a crash at every barrier (`fsx.barrier.sync=abort@N`) is recovered to the same oracle, with the same repeated recovery.
- [ ] A barrier failure below `WTF/` names no account, realm or character on any channel, and the case is shown to have been reached.
- [ ] A window over `DIRTY_DIRS_MAX` directories commits, restores every file, flushes early, and recovers from a crash at its last barrier.
- [ ] Every crash matrix and harness suite listed in §6 passes unchanged in the gate, and the exhaustive harness ran once by hand; the close comment quotes it.
- [ ] Each sweep logs its number of failing positions and its run time; the suites stay within the gate's budget by running shapes as separate tests, never by skipping a position.
- [ ] README's Crash testing bullet and Tests table say what landed, in the same commit.
