title: Measurement on btrfs, the power-loss campaign where an unprivileged tool allows one, README's figures and the per-file table before and after
description:
Part 7 of 7 of omad-7ccp (Group commit, derived writes and deferred directory fsyncs (`omad-7ccp`)). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

G3 (`omad-7ccp`) makes every commit window of omaddons as durable as today with far fewer syncs, under M4-D54: the audit log group-committed, derived caches never synced, directory syncs deferred through owned handles to explicit barriers. It owns §3.2 checkpoint criterion 13 (durability) and serves G-M4-6 ("no new risk to the engine's guarantees"; "the global lock is still held only for commit windows").

This part is **the measurement and the close-out evidence**: the btrfs report becomes the check of criterion 13 (an install's window at the design gate's derived target), the per-file table after is printed beside the "before" (comment 1167 on G3 and `omad-7ccp.1`'s re-measurement), the deferred directory fsyncs' further cut is reported, a **power-loss campaign** runs if an unprivileged tool that drops unsynced writes is usable on the development machine, and README's **Concurrency** figures and **Durability** bullet are finished. It is its own step because the measurement needs the final code (`omad-7ccp.5`), runs on a real disk in a release build outside the gate, and its README figures must quote what was measured, not what was forecast.

**What criterion 13 asks, restated:** "On btrfs (release build, measured beside `backups_of_500_mb_meet_their_budgets`), an install's lock hold and a whole restore's lock hold are reported. An install's fsyncs under the lock drop from 62 to the count G3's design gate derives from the boundaries it counted first. The forecast is at most 44 … Whatever the gate derives is the pinned target. The deferred directory fsyncs' further cut is reported, whatever it is, with the per-file table before and after." And M4-D54: "If neither [LazyFS nor `dm-log-writes`] can be used without privileges, README's durability paragraph says the ordering is argued and crash-tested, not power-loss-tested." The plan rejected promising a halving (no measurement supports it).

**Facts this part relies on** (after `omad-7ccp.1` to `omad-7ccp.5`):
- `tests/perf.rs::commit_windows_on_a_real_disk` (from `omad-7ccp.1`, report only): a release, ignored test on a home under a tempdir in `target/` (btrfs on the development machine; `common::checkpoint::skip` otherwise), `auto_backup = "off"`, the 500 MiB `WTF/` of 5,000 files, twenty `install_replace` runs and one whole restore with `-vv --progress json`, printing `lock_held_ms`, `fsyncs` and the per-kind table through `measured(…)`. It shares `HALF_GIB` with `backups_of_500_mb_meet_their_budgets` (`tests/perf.rs:1012-1109`).
- The design-gate comment on G3 holds the derived target per shape (and any revision `omad-7ccp.5` recorded); `tests/engine_durability.rs::PINNED` holds the final counts.
- Comment 1167 on G3 (the "before" at an older build): 62 fsyncs, `lock_held_ms` 165, by file 15 `actions.jsonl`, 5 journal, snapshot dir 4, `targets/` record 4, `history_tail` cache 4, trash 3, journal dir 2, stage 2, client snapshot 2–3, files index pieces 4, in-flight 2, `history.jsonl` 1, AddOns 1, state root 1. The original measurement of M3's D12: a whole restore 134 to 146 ms (51 fsyncs), an install 127 and 180 ms.
- README: the **Concurrency** bullet (`README.md:1997`) says "On a real disk, a commit's fsyncs set the hold: on btrfs on an NVMe drive each costs about 3 ms, and an install or a whole restore held the lock 130 to 180 ms"; the **Durability** bullet was added by `omad-7ccp.2` and extended by `omad-7ccp.3` and `omad-7ccp.5`.
- `common::checkpoint::skip(test, reason)` prints `SKIP <test>: <reason>` and fails unless `OMADDONS_ALLOW_SKIP` names the test (`tests/common/checkpoint.rs`); only the `SKIP`s listed in §3.2 are pre-accepted, and this one is not.
- FUSE: a user can mount a FUSE filesystem without root when `/dev/fuse` is readable and writable and the setuid helper `fusermount3` is installed. LazyFS (a FUSE filesystem that keeps unsynced writes in its own cache and can drop them on command) is not packaged with this project; `dm-log-writes` is a device-mapper target and needs root.

## Technical Approach

### 1. The check of criterion 13 (`tests/perf.rs`)

- `commit_windows_on_a_real_disk` gains a constant `INSTALL_FSYNCS_TARGET: u64` (the design gate's derived figure for `install_replace`, with a comment naming the gate comment and its date) and asserts that the median install's window holds at most that many fsyncs (counts are deterministic, so every run should equal it; the assertion is on every run), and that the whole restore's window equals its gate figure (a constant too).
- It prints, through `measured(…)`:
  - `install (replace), btrfs: lock_held_ms median <m> max <x>; fsyncs <n> (target <t>, before 62)`;
  - `whole restore of 500 MiB in 5000 files, btrfs: lock_held_ms <m>; fsyncs <n> (before 51)`;
  - the per-kind table of the median install, in comment 1167's format, and the same for the restore;
  - the further cut of the deferred directory fsyncs: the directory kinds' total in `omad-7ccp.3`'s pinned row (before the deferral) against now.
- Run: `cargo test --release --test perf commit_windows_on_a_real_disk -- --ignored --nocapture --test-threads=1`. H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`) runs the whole suite later (`cargo test --release --test perf -- --ignored --skip bench_home --skip live_home --test-threads=1`).

### 2. The power-loss campaign, when practical

- **Probe** (record its output in the close comment): `command -v lazyfs`; `test -r /dev/fuse -a -w /dev/fuse`; `command -v fusermount3`; and note that `dm-log-writes` needs root (`dmsetup` is not run). **Decided while writing this bead:** the campaign runs only if a LazyFS binary is already installed and FUSE is usable without root; this bead downloads, builds and installs nothing (a third-party C++ build is not a dependency this project takes, and nothing in the gate may depend on it), and does not attempt `dm-log-writes`.
- **If usable:** `tests/power_loss.rs`, one ignored test per window (`a_power_cut_at_every_barrier_of_<install_replace|whole_restore|repair_write>`), following the `SKIP` rule when LazyFS is absent. Each mounts LazyFS (its documented configuration: a cache that keeps unsynced data and a control FIFO) over a directory under `target/`, builds a `TestEnv` home inside it, and for N = 1 … until the run succeeds: runs the command with `fsx.barrier.sync=pause@N` and `OMADDONS_FAILPOINT_DIR` (the child stops at the Nth barrier, before its syncs), asks LazyFS to drop its unsynced data (the simulated power cut), kills the child, unmounts and remounts, runs the recovering command (`install --file bar.zip -t retail --offline`), and asserts `omad-7ccp.6`'s oracle (whole before or whole after by the journal's phase, no journal left). The test spawns `lazyfs` and `fusermount3`: test code, not `src/`, so `tests/single_writer.rs`'s spawner allowlist (which scans `src/`) is not involved. The close comment quotes every case's result and the run time.
- **If not usable:** no test file is added. README's Durability bullet gains: "The order of these syncs is argued in writing and crash-tested (a crash at every barrier, and an injected sync failure at each, are recovered); it is not power-loss-tested, because no tool that drops unsynced writes can run here without root." The close comment quotes the probe.

### 3. README

- **Concurrency** (`README.md:1997`): replace "an install or a whole restore held the lock 130 to 180 ms" with the measured figures: the install's and the whole restore's `lock_held_ms` and their fsyncs before → after (for example "an install now makes N fsyncs under the lock (62 before M4) and holds it about M ms; a whole restore of a 500 MiB `WTF/` N fsyncs (51) in about M ms"), keeping "each costs about 3 ms" if the measurement still says so. The tmpfs budget sentence stays.
- **Durability**: the power-loss sentence of §2.
- Nothing else: H4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`) reconciles the whole README later.

### 4. The leaf's close-out evidence

This part's close comment (and, when it is the last open subtask, the leaf's close comment) carries:
- the per-file table **before** (comment 1167, and `omad-7ccp.1`'s btrfs re-measurement at this milestone's code) and **after** (this part's run), side by side, for the install and the whole restore;
- the derived targets, the pinned counts, and the further cut of the deferred directory fsyncs;
- `lock_held_ms` before and after on btrfs;
- the power-loss campaign's result or the probe;
- the exhaustive harness run of `omad-7ccp.6`;
- every "Decided while writing this bead" item of G3, confirmed or adjusted;
- the statement that no wire name was added or changed, with the internal names (G3's Technical Approach §10).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `commit_windows_on_a_real_disk` asserts the install's window at no more than the design gate's derived target and the whole restore's at its gate figure, and passes on btrfs in a release build; it calls `common::checkpoint::skip` off btrfs.
- [ ] It prints the install's and the whole restore's `lock_held_ms`, fsyncs (with the before figures) and per-kind tables, and the deferred directory fsyncs' further cut.
- [ ] The close comment carries the per-file table before and after, the targets, the further cut and the `lock_held_ms` figures.
- [ ] The power-loss probe ran and its output is in the close comment; if LazyFS was usable without root, `tests/power_loss.rs` ran a cut at every barrier of the install, the whole restore and a repair, each recovered to a whole state; otherwise no test was added and README says the ordering is argued and crash-tested, not power-loss-tested.
- [ ] README's Concurrency bullet quotes the new btrfs figures, and the Durability bullet is complete, in the same commit as the test change.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files; `br lint` is clean for this subtask.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

None: this part changes a checkpoint test and README.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

- `tests/perf.rs::commit_windows_on_a_real_disk` (release, ignored, checkpoint): as §1. Its scenario uses T1's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`) `TestLog` for the measured runs (`log.run` records each run's argv, exit and stderr events, so a failing assertion points at the run's transcript), and `measured(…)` for the printed report.
- `tests/power_loss.rs` (only if LazyFS is usable): as §2, each position a `log.case`.

### Logging

The perf test logs each run (`log.run`), the parsed windows (`log.json("windows", …)`) and the per-kind tables; on a failed assertion it prints the observed count, the target, the gate comment it came from and the transcript path. The power-loss test logs, per position, the pause reached, the cut, the remount, the recovering command and the oracle's hashes.

### Checkpoint-only

`cargo test --release --test perf commit_windows_on_a_real_disk -- --ignored --nocapture --test-threads=1` here; H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`) runs the perf suite with `cargo test --release --test perf -- --ignored --skip bench_home --skip live_home --test-threads=1`. Its `SKIP` (no btrfs under `target/`) is not pre-accepted: criterion 13 is then unmet and H6 records it. `tests/power_loss.rs`, if added, runs by hand with `cargo test --test power_loss -- --ignored --nocapture --test-threads=1`; H6 does not run it (it is not one of §3.2's runs).

## Considerations

- **Figures are measurements, not budgets.** btrfs on NVMe on the development machine; ext4 with `data=ordered` or a SATA SSD may differ several-fold. README says where they were measured; no real-disk budget is added.
- **The target is the derived one.** If the run shows more fsyncs than the gate derived, that is a defect in `omad-7ccp.5` or a revision the gate must record (a comment on G3 with the reason), never a loosened constant.
- **A busy machine** changes `lock_held_ms`, not the counts; report the median and the maximum of twenty runs, and rerun on a quiet machine before quoting.
- **Privacy:** the perf home uses the fake names of `common::wtf::Wtf`; the printed tables hold kinds and numbers only.
- **Hot spots:** `tests/perf.rs` (append and rebase); README (the two bullets named).
- **Decided while writing this bead** (confirm or adjust in the close comment): the campaign only with an installed LazyFS and unprivileged FUSE; no `dm-log-writes`; the restore's count asserted too; the before/after table format.

## Dependencies

- Parent: G3 (`omad-7ccp`, group commit, derived writes and deferred directory fsyncs).
- Before it: `omad-7ccp.5` (the final code to measure).
- Beside it: `omad-7ccp.6` (the adversarial matrix; different files).
- After it: none within G3. Through G3, H4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`, the README final pass) reconciles the figures this part writes, and T4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4`, slice 3 end to end) quotes the pinned table.
- This part writes an integration test (the perf scenario, and possibly the power-loss test), so it carries an edge from T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs).

title: Per-item game_running drops details.running and details.reason, so a multi-target run cannot say why or whether the client may be running
description:
## Background

README's error table promises for game_running: 'details.running: "unknown" when /proc could not be read and the client may be running', and the planner sets details.reason (loaded_toc, legacy_client, policy_refuse, saved_variables) with target and ops (src/engine/running.rs evaluate). But a per-item error keeps only a whitelist of details (src/app/outcome.rs item_details: within_transaction conflicts, reset_at, required_by). So in sync, update and copy (multi-target, per-item failures, M2-D24) data.targets[].items[].error has no details at all for game_running, and when every item fails, all_failed() rebuilds the top-level error from that item error, so its details hold only items[] and lose running and reason too. An agent cannot tell an unreadable /proc (running: unknown) from a running client, or a legacy-client refusal from a loaded-TOC one, except by parsing the message. Found while writing omad-m2-audit-yegz.2.7's tests.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. tests/sync.rs sync_fails_closed_when_the_process_table_cannot_be_read: OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT at a chmod-000 dir, sync --prune dropping a loaded addon.
2. The item's error is {code: game_running, message, fix, fix_argv}: no details.running, no details.reason.
3. a_legacy_client_refuses_every_change_while_it_runs: the all-failed top-level game_running has details {items: [...]} only.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A per-item game_running error carries details.reason and, when /proc could not be read, details.running "unknown" (decide whether to whitelist the keys for game_running only or reason/running for every code, and record it in README Fields and the vision bead).
- all_failed() keeps them on the top-level error beside items[].
- tests/sync.rs and tests/copy.rs running cases assert details.reason / details.running instead of message text; argc gate passes.
close_reason: A failed item's game_running keeps details.reason and details.running, and the run's error when every item failed keeps them beside items[].

comments.text: done: src/app/outcome.rs item_details(code, details) adds reason and running to the kept keys for GameRunning only; ItemError::error() returns the kept details, and all_failed() inserts items[] into them instead of replacing them. Evidence: unit a_running_refusal_keeps_its_reason_on_the_item_and_the_run (game_running keeps reason+running, not_found keeps none, all_failed keeps both beside items); tests/sync.rs running cases now assert details {reason: loaded_toc}, {reason: loaded_toc, running: unknown}, and the legacy all-failed error's details.reason legacy_client; tests/update.rs running_clients_follow_the_running_policy asserts legacy_client on the item. README error table: game_running's details.reason values and that a failed item carries both. argc gate passes. decided: scoped to game_running rather than keeping reason for every code; no evidence other codes' item details are needed, and it keeps every other item error's shape unchanged. · found: none

title: Retention fixture dates commits from a fixed day but runs on the real clock: pruning test fails after 2026-10-19T10:00Z
description:
## Background

src/engine/retention.rs tests: Fixture::commit_as stamps entries with ago(age), relative to the fixed now() = 2026-10-14T12:00Z, while Fixture::run passes the real clock plus two hours (needed so orphans made now are past ORPHAN_MIN_AGE). From 2026-10-19T10:00Z the 'kept' commit (2 days before the fixed day) is over seven days old by the run's clock, so pruning_removes_both_halves_and_keeps_history fails every run (pruned 2, kept 1), and argc gate fails for everyone.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The fixture has one clock: commits are aged from the same instant run() uses.
- pruning_removes_both_halves_and_keeps_history passes regardless of the date; the other fixture tests still pass.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On or after 2026-10-19T10:00Z, run `cargo test --lib -- engine::retention::tests::pruning_removes_both_halves_and_keeps_history`.
2. It fails every run with `left: (2, 1) right: (1, 2)`: the 'kept' commit is pruned.
close_reason: Both fixtures that dated data from a fixed day while the code compared it with the real clock now age it from the clock: retention's Fixture has one clock for commits and run; the WoWInterface file list's default date is 30 days before now.

title: status --cached with a 20 MB history runs within 0.2 ms of its 5 ms budget
description:
## Background

`status --cached` is the bar widget's one call on every refresh, with a 5 ms median budget (milestone checkpoint criterion 10; `tests/perf.rs::status_cached_stays_under_5_ms_with_a_realistic_memo`, a release-build test run by hand). Its second half reads a home whose history is 20 MB of interleaved runs, after the change that rebuilt the history projection. On the development machine that case measures medians of 4.82–4.98 ms (p95 up to 5.22 ms), and one run hit 5.11 ms. An earlier record had 4.85 ms ("met, narrowly"). The heavy home without the large history sits at 4.40–4.60 ms.

E4 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.5.4`) measured this while adding the widget block. Interleaved A/B runs, with the block stubbed against the real one, put the block at +0.03–0.05 ms. The thin margin is therefore not the widget's; it is the 20 MB case's own cost.

## Technical Approach

- Profile the 20 MB case in release on the fixture home the perf test builds: `perf record` over 21 runs, or timing spans behind a debug env switch. Find where the extra ~0.4 ms over the heavy home goes: the projection read (`history_tail.json`), the discovery cache, the errors probe, the backups listing, or process start.
- Take the biggest avoidable cost out, keeping `--cached`'s rules: it writes nothing, makes no request, and is never wrong about `last_change_state` (`unknown` rather than a guess).
- Record before and after numbers (median, p95, cold) in the close comment.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The 20 MB-history half of `status_cached_stays_under_5_ms_with_a_realistic_memo` has a median at or under 4.5 ms over three consecutive runs on the development machine, with the widget block present.
- No `--cached` behaviour changes: `tests/status.rs` and the contract snapshots pass unchanged.

## Test Plan

- The perf test, three runs, before and after; the numbers go in the close comment.
- `argc gate`.

## Considerations

- The budget is a median of 21 runs of the binary, so process start counts. A gain inside one function may not show; measure end to end.
- Do not loosen the budget to make room. If nothing avoidable remains, record the profile and decide with the evidence in the bead.
acceptance_criteria: The 20 MB-history half of status_cached_stays_under_5_ms_with_a_realistic_memo has a median at or under 4.5 ms over three consecutive runs with the widget block present; --cached behaviour unchanged (tests/status.rs and the contract snapshots pass unchanged).
close_reason: status --cached with a 20 MB history: median 4.23/4.23/4.27 ms over three runs (was 4.74-4.99), heavy home 4.04-4.12 (was 4.46-4.60): the projection reads only the selected run whole, and store::load decodes current documents directly

title: Rollback stops on a step whose stage path a later undo reused
description:
## Background

A replace in the addon swap is two journaled steps that share a path: step 1 exchanges `<meta>/stage/<tx>/<Folder>` with `AddOns/<Folder>`, and step 2 moves the old folder on from that same stage path to `<meta>/snapshots/<tx>/AddOns/<Folder>`. A whole `WTF/` restore (D5) has the same shape: exchange `<meta>/stage/<tx>/WTF` with `<client dir>/WTF`, then move the old tree from the stage path to `WTF.previous`.

`roll_back` (`src/engine/journal.rs`) undoes steps last first, deciding each one from the identities now at its paths (`ran`). When a recovery undoes step 2 and then step 1 and dies before pruning the journal, the staged folder is back at the stage path. The next recovery checks step 2 first and finds the staged folder's identity at its `from`, which is neither its recorded before state nor its after state. It stops with "matches neither its before nor its after state; leaving it for manual repair", and every later change on that client fails, although nothing unexpected happened.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install Foo v1, then update to v2 with `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS=engine.swap.before_rename=abort@3`. The update dies after its exchange and its move to the snapshot.
2. Run any change with `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS=engine.recover.step=abort@3`. Its recovery undoes both renames and dies.
3. Run any change: it fails `internal`, "journal step 2 (…/stage/<tx>/Foo → …/snapshots/<tx>/AddOns/Foo) matches neither its before nor its after state".

No existing crash scene reached it: no failpoint lies between the move to the snapshot and `swapped`, and the recovery matrix arms `engine.swap.before_rename` only at its first hit. D5's restore scenes reached it through `engine.restore.snapshotted`.

## Technical Approach

Steps run first to last and roll back last first. So while any earlier step is in its before state, a later step either never ran or was undone already. `roll_back` now decides each step with `ran_after(step, earlier)`: a step in neither state counts as not run when an earlier step is in its before state. Anything else in neither state still stops, including a foreign tree at a live path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A rollback repeated after a recovery died having undone every step completes, for an addon replace and for a whole restore.
- A step in neither state with no earlier step in its before state still stops (`unexpected_state` for a restore, manual repair otherwise), and the live path is not touched.

## Test Plan

- Unit: `engine::journal::tests::a_rollback_repeated_after_both_steps_were_undone_skips_them` (the re-run skips both steps; a foreign tree at the live path still stops).
- Crash: `a_rollback_that_died_after_undoing_an_exchange_is_finished` (an update crashed after its second rename, recovery crashed after each undo in turn) and `a_crash_during_recovery_of_a_restore` (the same for a restore). Both fail on the old rule.

## Considerations

- The inference rests on step order and on inode identity: an earlier step's paths can look like its before state while it ran only if a later step put the exact recorded inodes back, which no transaction shape does.
- Fixed in the D5 commit that found it.
acceptance_criteria: A rollback repeated after a recovery died having undone every step completes, for an addon replace and for a whole restore; a step in neither state with no earlier step in its before state still stops and the live path is not touched.
close_reason: Fixed in the D5 commit that found it: roll_back decides each step with ran_after, so a step in neither state counts as not run while an earlier step is in its before state.

title: A pasted release-asset link ignores the named file when picking the asset
description:
## Background

A pasted GitHub release-asset link, `https://github.com/o/r/releases/download/<tag>/<file>`, is parsed into `gh:o/r` with a version hint (the tag) and an asset hint (the file name) in `src/sources/refs.rs`. Only `version_hint` is used (`src/app/install.rs` around lines 360 and 378); `asset_hint` is never read. So the user names one exact zip, and omaddons may install a different asset from that release: whichever ranks first for the client, e.g. the `-nolib` build or another flavor's zip that also loads.

Found while auditing the ref grammar for the README rewrite.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. A release with two assets that both load on the client, e.g. `Addon-1.0.zip` and `Addon-1.0-nolib.zip`.
2. `omaddons install https://github.com/o/r/releases/download/1.0/Addon-1.0-nolib.zip -t retail --dry-run --json`
3. The plan selects `Addon-1.0.zip`, the non-nolib asset that ranks first.

## Technical Approach

- Thread `asset_hint` into selection. When set, the candidate list is exactly the asset with that file name (case-sensitive, as GitHub serves it). If the release has no such asset, the result is `not_found` naming the release's assets.
- TOC verification still applies: a named asset that does not load on the client is `wrong_flavor` (exit 4), not a silent fallback to another asset.
- Record the asset name in the item so a later update can prefer the same variant (nolib or not). That part may be deferred to M2 update work; note it there if so.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An asset link installs exactly that asset, or fails with `not_found` or `wrong_flavor`; it never installs a different asset.
- A release-tag link (`/releases/tag/T`) keeps today's ranking.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- `tests/sources_github.rs` or `tests/install.rs` with replayed fixtures: two loadable assets, and a link naming the lower-ranked one installs it; a link naming a missing asset gives `not_found`; a link naming an asset for another flavor gives `wrong_flavor`.
- Unit (`refs.rs`): the round trip keeps the hint.

## Considerations

- `release.json` lists file names; REST lists assets. Both paths need the filter.
acceptance_criteria: an asset link installs exactly that asset or fails with not_found or wrong_flavor, never another asset; a release-tag link keeps todays ranking; argc gate passes
close_reason: A pasted release-asset link installs exactly that asset, or nothing

comments.author: CrimsonJasper
comments.text: done: RequestedChange::Install and InstallIntent gain asset (the link's file name; install sets it from ParsedRef.asset_hint, every other constructor None); prepare_install keeps only candidates whose asset file name equals it, after selection, so TOC verification still judges it. A release without that file is not_found naming the release's assets (details {asset, assets}), fix omaddons install <ref> --version <tag>. decided: a named asset that does not load is install's usual refusal (no_compatible_release, exit 3, with tried naming only that asset, reason wrong_flavor) rather than a separate wrong_flavor path, so a refused link reads like any refused install; never a fallback to another asset. Want::Install's intent is boxed (clippy large_enum_variant). Test tests/install.rs an_asset_link_installs_that_asset_or_nothing (three assets: missing name → not_found with the list; classic-only asset on retail → refused, tried = [Foo-classic.zip], nothing installed; the lower-ranked loadable nolib asset installs exactly). Recording the asset for later updates is not done (updates keep ranking). README sources row and Known issues updated.

title: Running-process discovery hints are implemented and tested but never wired into World
description:
## Background

Discovery has a process route: `src/discover/running.rs` `running_prefixes` (around lines 80-89) reads the `WINEPREFIX` and exe paths of running WoW and Battle.net processes. `ExtraPrefix` and `DiscoverySource::Process` carry them into discovery, and `tests/discover_scan.rs` (around lines 305-330) tests the path. But `World` (`src/app/world.rs` around lines 78-85) never sets `extra_prefixes` or `launcher_hints`, so in production a running client in a prefix that no launcher config names and that is not a direct child of the home directory's `Games` folder is never found. The module docs claim it is.

Typical case: a client in a nested prefix under the home directory, such as `Games/umu/umu-default` or `Games/Heroic/Prefixes/<game>`, launched by hand or by a script.

Found while auditing discovery for the README rewrite.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. A Wine prefix at `<home>/Games/nested/pfx` with a Battle.net WoW install, not named by any launcher config.
2. Start a process whose `comm` is `Wow.exe` with `WINEPREFIX` pointing there (tests: a fake `/proc` via `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT`).
3. `omaddons status` does not list the client.

## Technical Approach

- In `World`, call `running_prefixes` and pass the result as `extra_prefixes`. Rank stays as defined (`Process` after launchers, before extra roots).
- Respect the existing bounds: only the user's own processes and the same scan budget.
- Decide whether a client found only while running is registered on first change like any other (yes: the marker then finds it after the process exits).

## Acceptance Criteria

- With the fake `/proc` above, `status` lists the client with `found_by` process, and its qualifier follows the documented rules.
- With no WoW process running, discovery output is unchanged, and the snapshot tests still pass.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- `tests/discover_scan.rs`: extend the existing process-hint test to go through `World` end to end with `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT`.
- Real machine (checkpoint): run a client from a nested prefix and check `status`.

## Considerations

- Reading `/proc/<pid>/environ` is already done for running detection; reuse it rather than reading `/proc` twice.
- The alternative is removing the dead route and the doc claims. Wiring it is preferred, because nested prefixes are common with umu.
acceptance_criteria: with a fake /proc, a running client in an unnamed nested prefix is listed with found_by process; with no WoW process, discovery output is unchanged; argc gate passes
close_reason: Running clients' prefixes feed discovery, and registered roots stay found

title: Running detection's PrefixOnly fallback never matches under umu: WINEPREFIX <prefix>/pfx/ is compared raw
description:
## Background

README "Running clients" promises that running clients are detected live from `/proc`, and the `safe` policy refuses removing a loaded folder (and every legacy change) while a client runs. Detection in `src/discover/running.rs` `detect` has two kinds of evidence:

- `ExePath`: an argv entry whose base name is the exe, mapped through the prefix's `dosdevices` to a client dir.
- `PrefixOnly`: when no argv entry maps, every target with that exe name whose `install_root` starts with the process's `WINEPREFIX`.

umu-launcher (Omarchy's default runner, and how the 3.3.5a client runs on the development machine) sets `WINEPREFIX` to `<prefix>/pfx/`, where `pfx` is a symlink to `.` (observed 2026-10-20, omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.1). Commit 22b0a37 canonicalizes it in `running_prefixes` (discovery's process route) but not in `detect`. There, `install_root.starts_with("<prefix>/pfx/")` compares path components, and `<prefix>/drive_c/...` never starts with `<prefix>/pfx`. So under umu the `PrefixOnly` fallback never matches, and a running client whose argv names its exe without a mappable path is reported not running: detection fails open.

Every observed launch so far carried a mappable Windows argv[0], so `ExePath` caught it. The gap is latent, but it is on the safety path.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. A Battle.net prefix with `pfx -> .` holding retail, Classic Era and Anniversary (the last two share `WoWClassic.exe`).
2. A fake `/proc` process with `comm` `WoWClassic.exe`, argv `["WoWClassic.exe"]` (no path), `WINEPREFIX=<prefix>/pfx/`.
3. `detect_running_in` returns nothing (`tests/running.rs` `an_unresolved_exe_under_umus_pfx_link_marks_the_prefix_targets`, written 2026-10-21, fails). With `WINEPREFIX=<prefix>` the same shape returns each Classic target as `PrefixOnly` (`an_unresolved_exe_marks_every_matching_target_in_the_prefix`).

## Technical Approach

In `detect`, canonicalize the process's `WINEPREFIX` before both uses (the `dosdevices` mapping and the `PrefixOnly` comparison), falling back to the raw value when it cannot be canonicalized, as `running_prefixes` does. Compare against the target's `install_root` canonicalized too (or through `same_dir`-style component comparison) so a non-canonical install root still matches. Keep one helper for the canonical prefix so the two call sites cannot drift.

## Acceptance Criteria

- With `WINEPREFIX=<prefix>/pfx/` (a symlink to the prefix), a process whose argv does not map to a client dir marks every target with that exe in the prefix as `PrefixOnly`, exactly as with `WINEPREFIX=<prefix>`.
- `ExePath` results are unchanged (`observed_proton_shapes_map_to_the_played_client` stays green).
- A `WINEPREFIX` that does not exist still behaves as before (raw value, no panic).

## Test Plan

- Integration (`tests/running.rs`): the reproduction above, asserting `PrefixOnly` for each Classic target with the `pfx/` prefix.
- Existing running tests stay green.

## Considerations

- Canonicalizing reads the filesystem per matched process only (processes are filtered by `comm` first), so the cost is a few syscalls.
- The `~/.wine` default (no `WINEPREFIX`) goes through the same helper.
acceptance_criteria: with WINEPREFIX=<prefix>/pfx/ (a symlink to the prefix), a process whose argv maps to no client dir marks every target with its exe in the prefix as PrefixOnly, as with WINEPREFIX=<prefix>; ExePath results unchanged; a WINEPREFIX that does not exist behaves as before; tests/running.rs covers the pfx case
close_reason: detect canonicalizes the process's WINEPREFIX (one canonical helper shared with running_prefixes) and the target's install root before the PrefixOnly comparison, so umu's <prefix>/pfx/ marks the prefix's targets as the prefix itself does; ExePath unchanged; an unresolvable prefix is used as spelled.

title: Undo refuses a transaction after a later one that was itself undone
description:
## Background

Found by the real-machine suite (omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.5) on era with Dominos:
1. `install dominos --version 11.4.4 -t era` (tx A, pinned);
2. `unpin Dominos -t era` (tx B, records only);
3. `update Dominos -t era` (tx C, to 11.4.5);
4. `undo C` (tx U) succeeds;
5. `undo B` fails `undo_conflict`: "2 later transaction(s) changed the folders of B", listing C and U.

C and U cancel out: U restored exactly the state C started from. Undo's conflict check (`check_conflicts` in `src/engine/undo.rs`) counts every later transaction that touches the folders, including one that a later undo reverted and that undo itself. So a script that undoes its own transactions newest first (the documented way) cannot get past the first undo whenever two of its transactions touch the same folders. The same applies to folder transactions: install A, update B, undo B, then undo A is refused.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `omaddons install dominos --version 11.4.4 -t era` (tx A)
2. `omaddons unpin Dominos -t era` (tx B)
3. `omaddons update Dominos -t era` (tx C)
4. `omaddons undo C` succeeds
5. `omaddons undo B` fails `undo_conflict`, listing C and the undo of C.

In the engine: install, update, undo the update, then undo the install fails the same way.

## Technical Approach

In `check_conflicts`, walk the transactions after the reverted one newest first. A later transaction reverted by a later undo that is itself still in effect is cancelled together with that undo. An undo that was undone in turn cancels nothing: its own undo cancels it, and the transaction it reverted counts again. Cancelled transactions are not conflicts. An undo of the reverted transaction itself still reports "already undone".

## Acceptance Criteria

- Undoing B after C and undo-of-C succeeds and restores B's record (the pin).
- Install A, update B, undo B, undo A succeeds and leaves the folders as before A.
- When the undo of C is itself undone (C back in effect), undoing B is still `undo_conflict`.
- An undo of an already-undone transaction still says so.

## Test Plan

Unit tests in `src/engine/undo.rs` over TxScene; the real-machine era scenario passes.
close_reason: undo's conflict check ignores later transactions cancelled by a later undo still in effect; unit-tested; real-machine era scenario passes; gate green

comments.author: CrimsonJasper
comments.text:
**done:** Undo no longer counts a later transaction that was itself undone. `argc gate` passes: 1206 tests, ubs 0 critical.

**Fix (`src/engine/undo.rs`):** `check_conflicts` now skips the transactions `cancelled_after` returns.
- It walks the later history newest first.
- A later transaction reverted by a later undo that is still in effect is cancelled together with that undo.
- An undo undone in turn cancels nothing: its own undo cancels it, so the transaction it reverted counts again.
- An undo of the reverted transaction itself still reports "already undone".

**Tests:** unit test `a_later_transaction_undone_in_turn_is_no_conflict`:
- Install, update, undo the update, undo the install: AddOns is empty again.
- Pin, unpin, update, undo the update, undo the unpin: the pin is back and the folders are as the update's undo left them. This is the real-machine shape.
- With the update's undo undone in turn: still `undo_conflict`.
- The existing conflict tests are unchanged and pass.

**Real machine:** the era scenario (install pinned, unpin, update, three undos by id newest first) now passes on the real Classic Era client.

**Cleanup:** the failing run had left Dominos 11.4.4 on era, after the update was undone but the unpin and install were not. `remove Dominos -t era` cleaned it at once. None of Dominos's folders existed before the test (the unforced install would have refused them), so era's AddOns is as before, and the Forever guard was unchanged (5 addons, 12 folders, generation 7).

**Docs:** README's undo section says that a later transaction undone in turn no longer counts.

title: Test: a panic after human progress starts on a cleared line
description:
## Background
Human progress (`--progress human`, the default on a terminal) draws a single line on stderr that each update overwrites, and the reporter clears it before the next real line. The panic hook in `src/cli.rs` builds a fresh `Reporter::stderr` after the run's own reporter was dropped while unwinding. The fresh one did not know a progress line was on screen, so the panic message was written onto the end of the half-drawn progress line. The review pass added `PROGRESS_ON_SCREEN` (`src/output/stderr.rs`), a process-wide flag that progress sets, `clear_progress` resets, and `Reporter::stderr` starts from. Human progress only draws on a terminal, so no test covers it: the existing output tests write to a `Vec<u8>` sink, where the static is never read.

## Technical Approach
- Unit test (cheap, partial): drive two `Reporter::stderr` instances in one test, in a child process of its own (as `src/fsx/lock.rs` runs `child_holds_a_dir_lock`), since the flag is global and the repo has no serial-test crate. After the first draws progress and is dropped without clearing, the second starts with `progress_line == true`. This proves the hand-off, not the bytes.
- Integration test (the real proof): run the binary with stderr on a pseudo-terminal. rustix is already a dependency; its `pty` feature gives `openpt`, `grantpt`, `unlockpt` and `ptsname` without a new crate (enabling the feature needs `argc gate --all`). Trigger a panic after progress has drawn: the `cli.panic` failpoint fires before any progress, so arm a failpoint with the `panic` action at a later step instead (a fetch or stage failpoint during an install that reports progress; see `src/fsx/failpoint.rs` for the action syntax). Read the master side and assert that the clear sequence the reporter uses for a progress line comes before the panic text.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A test fails when `Reporter::stderr` starts from `false` instead of `PROGRESS_ON_SCREEN`.
- On a pty, the panic message starts on a cleared line, never after leftover progress text.
- No new crate; a rustix feature, if added, passes `cargo deny`.

## Test Plan
- Unit: the reporter hand-off above.
- Integration: the pty run above, skipped with a message where `/dev/ptmx` cannot be opened.

## Considerations
- The flag is process-global, so a unit test that sets it must not share a process with other reporter tests that read it; prefer the integration test.
- Width fitting (`fit_width`, `terminal_width` via `tcgetwinsize`) also only runs on a terminal; the pty test can set a window size and cover it too.
acceptance_criteria: On a pseudo-terminal, a panic after a progress line is drawn prints the clear sequence before the panic text; a test fails when Reporter::stderr starts from false instead of PROGRESS_ON_SCREEN; no new crate.
close_reason: tests/terminal.rs: the binary with stderr on a pseudo-terminal (rustix pty feature, dev-dependency only, cargo deny ok; no new crate). a_panic_after_progress_starts_on_a_cleared_line (debug builds): engine.lock.acquired=panic after the stage progress drew; the clear sequence comes right before error[internal]. Mutation checked by hand: with Reporter::stderr starting from false instead of PROGRESS_ON_SCREEN the terminal reads 'stage: retail 1/1error[internal]: …' and the test fails. The window-size part of the bead (fit_width) found omad-1afl, fixed in the same commit. Unit hand-off test not added: the bead's Considerations prefer the integration test, which covers the acceptance criteria. Skips through common::checkpoint::skip where /dev/ptmx cannot be opened. argc gate --all passed.

title: A pre-M3 build's orphan sweep can delete a crashed restore's replaced WTF/
description:
## Background

M3 names a restore's journal and stage `<tx>.wtf` so that the last M2 build (`af10e34`), which lists only journals and stages named by a bare id, never sees them (M3-D45; README "Known limitations"). The restore's undo snapshot is not renamed: it lives in `<meta>/snapshots/<tx>/`, with the replaced tree at `WTF.previous`.

The M2 build's orphan sweep removes the snapshot folder of a transaction it believes never committed once it is an hour old, and its only-copy check looks at `AddOns/` only. It cannot see the `.wtf` journal, so it treats a crashed restore's snapshot folder as an orphan. `tests/compat_m2.rs` crashes each restore shape right after its `prepared` line (step 1), when `snapshots/<tx>/` is still empty, so the test passes. After a crash past the first rename, that folder holds `WTF.previous`, the only copy of the pre-restore `WTF/` unless a `before_restore` backup exists (none on filesystems that cannot clone). An M2 change an hour later deletes it, and M3's recovery then stops with `unexpected_state`. README says each shape recovers "including when the M2 build ran two hours later", which holds only for the crash point tested.

Running a pre-M3 build to change state M3 wrote is already documented as unsupported; this closes the gap the documentation's own characterization claims is closed. Found by G2 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.7.2`).

## Steps to Reproduce

1. A restore crashed after its first journaled rename (debug build, `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS` at `engine.restore.exchanged`), on a client whose filesystem cannot clone (no `before_restore` backup).
2. Advance the clock past an hour and run an `af10e34` install on the same client.
3. `<meta>/snapshots/<tx>/WTF.previous` is gone; the next M3 change reports `journal_pending` with `unexpected_state`.

## Technical Approach

- Name a settings transaction's client-side snapshot folder `<meta>/snapshots/<tx>.wtf/` (as its journal and stage already are), so a build that lists bare ids never sees it; the state-side half too if the M2 sweep reaches it.
- Readers: recovery, undo, retention and `status`'s `snapshot_bytes` find the folder by the journal's or history line's kind; keep reading `snapshots/<tx>/` for restores committed before the change (both names, one transaction).
- Extend `tests/compat_m2.rs`: crash each restore shape after each of its renames, run the M2 build two hours later, and require the next M3 change to recover with the replaced tree kept.
- README: correct the characterization in Known limitations to what the extended test shows.

## Acceptance Criteria

- After a crash at any journaled step of a whole restore, an `--addon` restore or the undo of either, an `af10e34` change two hours later leaves the transaction's snapshot intact, and the next M3 change recovers it (`WTF.previous` kept).
- Restores committed before the rename stay undoable (old folder name read).
- `tests/compat_m2.rs` covers every crash point; the engine crash matrix still passes.

## Test Plan

- `tests/compat_m2.rs` (checkpoint test): the extended matrix above.
- `tests/engine_crash.rs`: the restore shapes with the new folder name, and an undo of a restore committed under the old name.

## Considerations

- This changes an on-disk name inside a protocol: common rule 14 applies (its own crash and recovery matrix).
- Retention and the orphan sweep in M3 must treat `<tx>.wtf` snapshot folders exactly as `<tx>` ones (only-copy rules for `WTF.previous`).
acceptance_criteria: After a crash at any journaled step of a restore, an --addon restore or the undo of either, an af10e34 change two hours later leaves the snapshot intact and the next M3 change recovers it; restores committed earlier stay undoable; compat_m2 covers every crash point.
close_reason: settings transactions keep both snapshot halves as <tx>.wtf, which the M2 build never lists; readers find either name, so older restores stay undoable

title: A multi-target command refused by a stopped journal drops details.journal_pending and details.reason
description:
## Background

When every item of a multi-target command fails (`update`, `sync`, `copy`, `pin`, `unpin`, `adopt` when it adopts), `TargetsData::all_failed` (`src/app/outcome.rs`) builds the command's one error. It keeps a target's own error body, with its `details`, only when that error is `plan_stale`. For any other code it rebuilds the error from the first failed item's `ItemError`, which carries no `details`, then adds `details.items`. Every key the target's error carried is lost.

That breaks README's contract for a journal stopped for repair. README's `journal_pending` troubleshooting says: "Every later change on that client then fails until it is fixed (`error.details.journal_pending` names the transaction, `error.details.reason` why)". The error registry lists `internal` with `details.reason: "step_unrecognized"`, `details.journal_pending`, and `state_corrupt` with `journal_unreadable`, `preservation_incomplete` and others. A single-target command such as `install` keeps them. `pin` and the other multi-target commands report the right code and message, but `details` holds only `items`. An agent then cannot read which transaction to repair from the error.

`TargetResult.error` is documented as "Nothing of this target committed (its items say `failed` with this error)" and holds the full `ErrorBody`.

Found while writing omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8.4 (`tests/engine_witness.rs::residual_after_the_step_line_*`, whose `pin` asserts only code and message, and whose `install` asserts the details).

## Steps to Reproduce

1. A debug build. A retail client with Alpha, Beta and Gamma installed at v1, and v2 released (`common::engine::shapes::update_many`).
2. Preview `omaddons update -t retail --refresh --dry-run --json` and take its token.
3. Run the bound update with `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS=engine.swap.before_rename=pause@2` (and `OMADDONS_FAILPOINT_DIR`). At the pause, move `AddOns/Beta` aside, put an exact copy in its place, then resume. The run stops for repair (`details.journal_pending`, `recovery_error.code: "internal"`).
4. `omaddons pin Gamma -t retail --json` exits 1 with `internal`, "journal step 2 (…) matches neither its before nor its after state; leaving it for manual repair". Its `error.details` is `{"items": [...]}`: no `reason`, no `journal_pending`.
5. `omaddons install gh:o/bar --file <bar.zip> -t retail --offline --json` exits 1 with `details.reason: "step_unrecognized"` and `details.journal_pending`.

## Technical Approach

- In `all_failed`, when the first failed item's target carries an error (`TargetResult.error`, the error every item of that target failed with), build the command's error from that body whatever its code, as `error_of(body)` already does for `plan_stale`. Fall back to the item's error only when the target has none (an item failed on its own).
- Keep `details.items` beside the target's own details, as today.
- Check every caller that builds a target-level error with `details` (journal stops, `game_running` with `details.reason` and `details.running`, `state_too_new`, `scope_denied` with `marker_mismatch`) and confirm that each now reaches the envelope.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] After the steps above, `pin Gamma -t retail --json` fails `internal` with `details.reason: "step_unrecognized"` and `details.journal_pending` naming the transaction, plus `details.items`.
- [ ] The same holds for `update`, `sync`, `copy`, `unpin` and an adopting `adopt` refused by a stopped journal (one row per command in a table test).
- [ ] An all-failed multi-target run whose items failed on their own (no target-level error) is unchanged.
- [ ] Every `details` an envelope now gains validates against its code's `DetailSpec` (A3's strict schema validation).
- [ ] Contract snapshots that change are reviewed and re-accepted; the close comment lists every `details` key that now appears where it did not (DEC-4).
- [ ] `tests/engine_witness.rs::residual_after_the_step_line_*` asserts the details on `pin` too; README's Known issues entry for this bead is removed.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files.

## Test Plan

- Unit (`src/app/outcome.rs`): `all_failed` with a target error of each code keeps that error's `details` and adds `items`; with item-only failures it is unchanged.
- E2E (`tests/engine_witness.rs`, `TestLog`): the residual scene, with each multi-target command run after the stop, asserting `details.reason` and `details.journal_pending`.
- Contract (`tests/contract/`): snapshots of multi-target refusals re-accepted after review.

## Considerations

- Additive on the wire: keys appear in `details` that the registry already declares for these codes. No code changes and no key is renamed.
- The widget reads `error.code`, `message` and `fix`. Confirm in `omarchy/Model.js` that nothing breaks on richer `details`.
- A command whose items failed on several targets for different reasons takes the first target's error, as today: the first failure decides, and `details.items` lists them all.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] After the steps above, `pin Gamma -t retail --json` fails `internal` with `details.reason: "step_unrecognized"` and `details.journal_pending` naming the transaction, plus `details.items`.
- [ ] The same holds for `update`, `sync`, `copy`, `unpin` and an adopting `adopt` refused by a stopped journal (one row per command in a table test).
- [ ] An all-failed multi-target run whose items failed on their own (no target-level error) is unchanged.
- [ ] Every `details` an envelope now gains validates against its code's `DetailSpec` (A3's strict schema validation).
- [ ] Contract snapshots that change are reviewed and re-accepted; the close comment lists every `details` key that now appears where it did not (DEC-4).
- [ ] `tests/engine_witness.rs::residual_after_the_step_line_*` asserts the details on `pin` too; README's Known issues entry for this bead is removed.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files.
close_reason: done: TargetsData::all_failed keeps the target error's details whatever its code; the residual cells assert reason and journal_pending on install, pin, sync, adopt and update; argc gate passed (3353 passed, 0 failed)

title: Epic: Install what the author built for this client
description:
## Background

omaddons verifies every archive against the target client's TOC load rules before writing anything (README "How omaddons decides what loads"). That check mixes two questions: which download is this client's, and which of its folders load. `accepts` (`src/engine/inspect.rs:1007`) answers the first with a clue about one folder. Without a publisher `release.json` that declares the client, a side folder that merely lists another client's interface marks the whole archive as another client's build, and the archive is refused.

The keyless-coverage study (omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.7, comment 868) and a prior-art review of other addon managers (2026-10-23) found the following.

- **The rule refuses real addons whose main addon is built for the client.** ArkInventory 3.12.17 (`wowi:6488`) is refused on Mists Classic, Classic Era and Forever. Titan Panel 9.3.5 (`wowi:8092`) is refused on Anniversary, Carbonite All-in-One on retail, and BlizzMove 3.8.5 (`wowi:23875`) on Forever. A scan of 35 popular multi-folder WoWInterface projects on 6 clients found one more such case and no case where a side folder correctly marked another client's build.
- **The game does not skip such folders.** warcraft.wiki.gg, TOC format: "If an addon doesn't set an interface version that matches the client's, then it's classified as out-of-date." Such a folder loads when the player enables "Load out of date AddOns". The only documented hard floor is on retail: "Mainline addons that don't have an interface version of 120000 or higher are not allowed to load in 12.0.0+ builds at all" (warcraft.wiki.gg, Patch 12.0.0 API change notes). "What the game would load" therefore cannot decide which build to install: with that option on, the game loads almost anything.
- **Publisher metadata is ignored whenever the TOCs look clean.** The BigWigs packager run with `-g <type>` builds one flavor: keyword preprocessing strips the other flavors' code, and only that flavor's interfaces enter `release.json` (`set_build_version` in BigWigsMods/packager `release.sh`), even when the zip still carries other flavors' TOCs. omaddons ranks such a file `MetadataMismatch` on another client and installs it there whenever its TOCs load. That is a silent install of another client's build.
- **No other manager judges folders.** WowUp, instawow, strongbox, Ajour and CurseBreaker install every folder of the zip. Their reported failures are wrong-flavor files, from WoWInterface's single retail file and from file-name guessing: WowUp #1238 and #1283, Ajour #371 (Classic GatherMate2 updated to the retail build, Lua errors), instawow #75. instawow (`any_flavour`) and CurseBreaker (`IgnoreClientVersion`) keep a per-addon "any flavor" setting that persists across updates. WowUp's one-shot "Install at your own risk" dialog led to #1283.
- **A per-flavor GitHub project's latest release may be another client's.** Such projects publish one release per flavor, so `releases/latest` is whichever shipped last. VuhDo's latest is its Cataclysm Classic build, so it installs on no live client. The other managers look back 5 to 15 releases. omaddons promises it never falls back to an older release (README line 520).

The owner decided (2026-10-23) two points: a file whose publisher labels it for other clients only is refused, and omaddons looks back through recent releases for this client's newest build.

## Goals

- **Principle: install what the author built for this client.** Each folder is judged by the author's own declarations. The game's rules are a floor (never install what the client cannot load), not the decider.
- **Per folder.** A folder is built for this client when it has a TOC with this client's suffix, an interface in this client's range, or an `AllowLoadGameType` that names this client's game type. It is out of date when its interface does not match the client's. A folder built only for other clients is left out, recorded, and explained truthfully.
- **Per download.** The main folder must be built for this client, and a file whose `release.json` or file name names only other clients is refused. Among the rest, a clean file wins as today. Otherwise a file whose only leftovers are folders for other clients installs, with those folders left out.
- **Every outcome can be explained later.** Left-out folders are recorded on the addon and shown by `info` and `list -v`. A refusal names the folder or the evidence that decided it.
- **An override instead of `--force`.** A deliberate per-addon, per-client `--any-flavor` setting that persists across updates.
- **Look-back on GitHub** for the newest release that declares a build for this client.

## Success Criteria

- Every child bead is closed.
- Fixtures shaped like ArkInventory 3.12.17, Titan Panel 9.3.5, Carbonite and BlizzMove 3.8.5 install as their beads describe.
- A clean file whose `release.json` names only other clients is refused, and the message names the evidence.
- A VuhDo-shaped per-flavor repository installs its newest build for each client.
- The coverage re-measure explains every changed cell of comment 868's matrix.
- README "How omaddons decides what loads" states the new rules.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Non-Goals

- Treating Tukui's patch list or WoWInterface's compatibility tags as evidence. README says they only rank, and that stays.
- Look-back on WoWInterface, Tukui, WowAce, `git:`, `url:` or local sources: each serves one stream or names its file explicitly.
- Changing the fail-closed reading of an `AllowLoadGameType` that names no known game type (`src/toc.rs:180-183`). That choice is deliberate and fits this epic's principle.
- Confirming the out-of-date behaviour in a running client. README cites warcraft.wiki.gg for it.

## Considerations

- **The change is monotonic except for one tightening.** Every file accepted today that carries no evidence against this client is accepted as today. Refusals become installs only for files whose leftovers are folders for other clients. The one new refusal is a clean file whose `release.json` or file name names only other clients, and the coverage re-measure counts those.
- **Name hints become evidence, so they must not misfire.** The file-name hint bead lands before the evidence rule.
- **Related bugs are filed beside this epic, not under it:** the retail 12.0 floor (P1) and newer-only interfaces (P3). The coverage re-measure depends on both.
- When a child lands, record it with a comment on omad-vision-8qa, as other landed work does.
acceptance_criteria: All children closed; ArkInventory 3.12.17-, Titan Panel 9.3.5-, Carbonite- and BlizzMove 3.8.5-shaped fixtures install as their beads describe; a clean file whose release.json names only other clients is refused naming the evidence; a VuhDo-shaped per-flavor repository installs each client's newest build; the coverage re-measure explains every changed cell of omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.7 comment 868; README 'How omaddons decides what loads' states the new rules; argc gate passes
close_reason: All 18 children closed: archive grading with left-out folders, AllowLoadGameType admission, the evidence rule (with the own-TOC exemption), --any-flavor, GitHub look-back on every channel (feed, sibling probe, REST listing, same-track stop), and the coverage re-measure explaining every changed cell

title: A folder whose AllowLoadGameType names the client is built for it: an off-range interface is out of date
description:
## Background

`judge` (`src/toc/loaded.rs:369`) gives a folder `WrongFlavor { InterfaceNotInFamily }` when none of its TOC interfaces lies in the client's family range, even when its `AllowLoadGameType` names this client's game type. Titan Panel 9.3.5 (`wowi:8092`) ships `TitanAmmo/TitanAmmo.toc`:

```
## Interface: 11509, 16001, 205056
## AllowLoadGameType: camelot, tbc, vanilla
## Notes: Adds an ammo monitor to Titan Panel - Classic versions only
## Dependencies: Titan
```

205056 is a typo for a 2.5.x interface. On Anniversary (the `tbc` row, range 20500 to 20599) no value is in range, so the folder counts as another client's, and through `accepts` the whole of Titan Panel is refused there. Yet the author built this folder for tbc and says so.

The game passes the game-type line and then lists the folder as out of date. warcraft.wiki.gg, TOC format: "If an addon doesn't set an interface version that matches the client's, then it's classified as out-of-date." It loads when "Load out of date AddOns" is on. The epic's principle is to install what the author built for this client, and an `AllowLoadGameType` that names the client is the author saying so.

## Technical Approach

- In `judge`, after the game-type check passes and before `InterfaceNotInFamily`, check the loaded TOC's effective `AllowLoadGameType` (inline directives included, as `game_type_excluded` at `src/toc/loaded.rs:457` reads it). When it names one of this client's own game types, the folder is `Compatible { out_of_date: true }`. Those are the row's game types from the README rows table: `standard`, `forever`/`camelot`, `vanilla`, `tbc`, `wrath`/`titan`, `cata`, `mists`.
- **Family-level names do not count.** `classic` and `mainline` are too broad to show that the author meant this client. A folder with `AllowLoadGameType: classic` and only a retail interface stays another client's.
- **Legacy rows ignore game types**, as today (`!rules.legacy`).
- **The `out_of_date` warning says what is off.** For example: "TitanAmmo: TitanAmmo.toc targets interface 205056, not one of this client's (20505); the client lists it as out of date and loads it only with "Load out of date AddOns" enabled". Today's message says "older than the client's", which is wrong here.
- **The verdict applies wherever `judge` runs:** install, update checks, `info`, `status --unmanaged` load verdicts and `adopt`.
- README: steps 3 and 4 of "How omaddons decides what loads".

## Acceptance Criteria

- A TitanAmmo-shaped folder (the TOC above) is `Compatible { out_of_date: true }` on Anniversary, with an `out_of_date` warning naming 205056.
- On retail and Mists Classic the same folder is still `GameTypeExcluded`.
- A folder with `AllowLoadGameType: classic` and only `## Interface: 120105` is still `InterfaceNotInFamily` on Classic Era.
- README states the rule.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

The companion test bead holds the cases: unit tests on `judge`, plus TOC-matrix rows (`tests/fixtures/toc/matrix/cases.toml`) for this folder on every client row.

## Considerations

- `best_in_family` and `primary_interface` return `None` for such a folder because no value is in range. Callers already handle `None` (update status, the M2-D42 floor), but check each one.
- **The M2-D42 adopted floor.** In `try_candidate`, an `out_of_date: true` main folder is treated as below the floor (`out_of_date || below`). A build whose main folder is admitted only by game type therefore never replaces an adopted one, which is conservative and intended.
- An `ExcludeLoadGameType` that names the client still wins, as today.
acceptance_criteria: A TitanAmmo-shaped folder (Interface 11509, 16001, 205056; AllowLoadGameType camelot, tbc, vanilla) is Compatible{out_of_date:true} on Anniversary with an out_of_date warning naming 205056, and still GameTypeExcluded on retail and Mists Classic; AllowLoadGameType classic with only 120105 stays InterfaceNotInFamily on Era; README states the rule; argc gate passes
close_reason: An AllowLoadGameType naming the client's own game type admits a folder with no in-range interface as out of date (floor still wins, legacy ignores, exclude wins); Titan Panel 9.3.5 installs on Anniversary

comments.author: CobaltOak
comments.text: claim: src/toc/loaded.rs judge (game-type admission), README load-rule steps 3-4, TitanPanel catalog note. Taking the test companion .7 with it.

comments.author: CobaltOak
comments.text:
What landed, and the decisions taken where the bead left a choice.

**Rule.** `judge` (`src/toc/loaded.rs`) now admits a folder before it would give `interface_not_in_family`, when two things hold: the row is not legacy, and the loaded TOC's effective `AllowLoadGameType` (inline directives already applied by `Toc::for_client`) names one of the row's own `game_types`. A new helper, `names_own_game_type`, checks this. Only the row's game types count, never the family suffixes `classic` or `mainline`. Such a folder is `Compatible { out_of_date: true }`. Its `out_of_date` warning says, for example: "TitanAmmo: TitanAmmo.toc targets interfaces 11509, 16001, 205056, none of them this client's 20506; the client lists it as out of date …". It keeps the usual "Load out of date AddOns" fix and never says "older than".

**Decided: the warning lists every interface.** 205056 lies in mainline's range (60000 and up), so no rule could pick it out as "the one meant for this client". Listing them all names 205056 and stays true.

**Decided: the floor still wins.** On a client with an active `interface_floor`, an admitted folder has every value below the floor, because a value of 120000 or more would be in mainline's range and so never reach this path. It is therefore `below_client_floor`, never out of date: no player setting loads it there.

**Decided: game types shared between rows admit on each.** Titan and Wrath Classic both answer to `wrath`. A Titan build gated `AllowLoadGameType: wrath, titan` (WeakAuras 5.22.1's `_Wrath` TOC, 38002) is therefore listed as out of date on a Wrath Classic 3.4.3 client, which is how that client lists it. The matrix case `wrath-rejects-titan-interface` became `wrath-lists-a-titan-build-gated-to-wrath-as-out-of-date`, and the old name now covers the same TOC without the gate (`interface_not_in_family`). Wrath Classic has no live product, so this reaches only custom 3.4.x clients.

**Checked live (2026-10-24).** A dry run of `install titanpanel` (wowi:8092, 9.3.5) on a synthetic Anniversary 2.5.6 client installs all 16 folders, with the one `out_of_date` warning for TitanAmmo. The catalog entry now lists `tbc`, and its note, README's catalog row and README's Known limitations (only ArkInventory is still refused whole) say so.

**README.** Step 4 of "How omaddons decides what loads" states the rule, with the TitanAmmo example, the legacy exception and the exclusion that still wins. The `out_of_date` warning row covers this case.

**Callers.** `best_in_family` and `primary_interface` return `None` for such a folder, and `FolderVerdict.interface` is `None`. In `try_candidate`, M2-D42's floor treats `out_of_date: true` as below the floor, so a build admitted only by game type never replaces an adopted one. That is conservative and intended. `DepFacts.out_of_date` reports it as an out-of-date dependency.

description:
## Background

This is the test companion of omad-author-built-loading-5po6.3: the addon record keeps the folders an install left out, with their reasons, and `info` and `list -v` show them. The goal is that the answer to "why is this module missing?" outlives the run's output, so the tests follow the record through install, update and undo.

## Technical Approach

- Integration tests next to the multi-flavor install tests (`tests/install_multi_flavor.rs`, using `serve_boss_mods` for the DBM and BigWigs shapes).

- Contract snapshots for `info` and `list -v` JSON.

title: Test: --any-flavor persists where it should and never installs what the client refuses
description:
## Background

This is the test companion of omad-author-built-loading-5po6.5: the per-addon, per-client `--any-flavor` setting. It loosens the safety check on purpose, so the tests must prove two things. It persists exactly where it should (record, update, sync, export) and clears when asked. It never installs what the client itself refuses.

## Technical Approach

- Integration tests with the HTTP fixture server and `Home`, in a new `tests/install_any_flavor.rs` or next to the multi-flavor tests.
- An `addons.toml` parse and render unit test in `src/state/desired.rs`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each case below is a test.
- Removing the record field fails the update case.
- Making the alternative a `fix_argv` fails the refusal-shape case.

## Test Plan

- **A retail-only addon** (plain TOC, `## Interface: 120105`) on Mists Classic:
  1. Refused without the setting.
  2. With `--any-flavor`, installed with `out_of_date` and an `any_flavor` warning.
  3. A newer release installs through `update` with the setting kept.
  4. `export` writes `any_flavor = true`, and `sync` from that file installs it.
  5. `--no-any-flavor` clears the setting, and the next `update` refuses.
- **Evidence ignored:** a file whose `release.json` lists only mainline installs on Mists Classic under the setting, with the warning naming `release.json`.
- **Limits that still hold:**
  - a folder with `AllowLoadGameType: standard` is left out on Mists Classic;
  - an addon with only `_Mainline.toc` is refused on Mists Classic (`no_loadable_toc`);
  - a retail 12.x client refuses a TOC below 120000 (needs omad-retail-12-floor-e5a0).
- **Visibility:** `status`, `list` and `info` show the setting.
- **Refusal shape:** a refusal's `alternatives` hold the `--any-flavor` argv, and `fix_argv` does not.
- **Undo** of the install that set it restores the record without it.
- **`copy`** to another client does not carry it.
- **`addons.toml`:** `any_flavor = true` parses on a table entry and renders back unchanged.

## Considerations

- Dependencies of an addon with the setting are judged without it. Add one case where a dependency is refused and reported as today.
acceptance_criteria: Tests cover refusal without the setting, install, update, export and sync with it, clearing it, release.json evidence ignored, GameTypeExcluded, NoLoadableToc and the 12.0 floor still refusing, status, list and info showing it, alternatives but never fix_argv, undo, copy not carrying it, and addons.toml round-trip
close_reason: Every case is a test: tests/install_any_flavor.rs (refusal shape, install, update, export and sync, clearing, release.json ignored, game-type gate, no_loadable_toc and the floor still refusing, status, list and info, undo, copy, a dependency judged without it) and the addons.toml round trip in src/state/desired.rs

title: Test: look-back finds this client's newest GitHub build within the feed and says so
description:
## Background

This is the test companion of omad-author-built-loading-5po6.4: GitHub look-back through `releases.atom` for the newest release whose `release.json` declares the client. It changes a README promise ("never falls back to an older release") and adds requests, so the tests pin when it runs, what it installs, and how many requests it sends.

## Technical Approach

- Integration tests with the HTTP fixture server serving `releases/latest`, `releases.atom` and per-tag `release.json` and zips.
- Assertions on the throwaway home's net log for the requests.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each case below is a test.
- Disabling the look-back fails the Mists Classic case.
- Removing the memo fails the request-count case.

## Test Plan

- **VuhDo shape.**
  - Fixture: tags `v3.218-catac` (newest, `release.json` declares `cata`), `v3.217-mists` (declares `mists`) and `v3.216-bcc` (declares `bcc`).
  - Mists Classic installs `v3.217-mists` with `older_release_for_client`.
  - Cataclysm Classic installs `v3.218-catac` with no warning.
  - Anniversary installs `v3.216-bcc`.
  - Classic Era: `no_compatible_release`, with `tried` naming each release looked at.
- **No downgrade:** with `v3.219-mists` installed and that release gone from the feed, `update` makes no change.
- **Memo:** a second `outdated` with the newest tag unchanged sends no `release.json` request.
- **REST use:** the net log shows no `api.github.com` request on the stable look-back, or exactly one for the chosen release if the prerelease decision needs it.
- **Prereleases:** a prerelease in the feed is never installed on stable, per the recorded decision.
- **No look-back:** a pinned addon (`--version`) and a pasted asset link never look back.

## Considerations

- Use tag names and `release.json` shaped as the BigWigs packager writes them (`releases[{name, version, filename, nolib, metadata[{flavor, interface}]}]`).
acceptance_criteria: Fixture-server tests cover a VuhDo-shaped repository on Mists, Cata, Anniversary and Era, no downgrade, the memo sending no release.json on an unchanged tag, REST use per the recorded prerelease decision, prerelease exclusion on stable, and no look-back for pinned addons or pasted asset links
close_reason: Fixture-server tests for the look-back: VuhDo shape on Titan (for Cata, which has no client), Mists, Anniversary and Era; no downgrade (feed-less and feed-ordered); memo request counts; REST counts; prerelease exclusion (flagged and named); no look-back for --version or a pasted asset link; a spent API budget

title: GitHub look-back on the beta and alpha channels, within the REST listing's 20 releases
description:
## Background

omad-author-built-loading-5po6.4 added a GitHub look-back on the stable channel: when the newest release has no build for the client, omaddons installs the newest older release whose `release.json` declares it (README "A release per client (GitHub look-back)"). The beta and alpha channels were left out on purpose, and README says they never look back.

On those channels, `GithubRest::list` (`src/sources/github_rest.rs`) already fetches the 20 most recent releases in one REST request. `choose` then takes the newest non-draft release. A per-client repository on beta (VuhDo ships five prereleases per build, one per client) therefore installs whichever client's prerelease came last, and refuses on every other client.

## Technical Approach

- On beta and alpha, when every candidate of the chosen release is refused `wrong_flavor`, take the next non-draft release from the same listing whose `release.json` asset declares the client. Use the predicate the stable look-back uses (`declares_client` in `src/engine/plan.rs`). Releases without `release.json` are judged by their zip assets' names, as today.
- The listing is already in hand, so no extra REST request is needed. Each candidate's `release.json` is fetched from its `browser_download_url` (github.com), one at a time, stopping at the first match, at most `LOOK_BACK_MAX_RELEASES`.
- Reuse the stable look-back's memo (`ReleaseMemo.look_backs`, keyed by ref, channel and family against the newest tag), its `older_release_for_client` warning and its never-downgrade ordering (the listing's order).
- README: Channels and the look-back section.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A fixture repository whose 20 newest releases are prereleases for several clients installs on `--channel beta` the newest prerelease declared for each client, with `older_release_for_client` on all but the newest.
- No REST request beyond the one listing.
- A client that no listed release declares is refused `no_compatible_release`, with `tried[]` naming each release looked at.
- An unchanged newest tag fetches no `release.json` again.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Integration tests in `tests/install_look_back.rs` with the fixture server: the REST listing (`api.github.com/repos/o/r/releases?per_page=20`), per-tag `release.json` and zips.
- Net-log assertions on request counts.

## Considerations

- The listing's order is by creation date, which `choose` already handles. The look-back must use the same order for its never-downgrade comparison.
- Alpha behaves like beta on GitHub (README Channels).
acceptance_criteria: On --channel beta/alpha, a per-client repository installs the newest non-draft release of the one 20-release REST listing whose release.json declares the client, with older_release_for_client, no REST request beyond the listing, tried[] naming each release looked at when none does, the look-back memo reused on an unchanged newest tag, and argc gate passing
close_reason: Beta and alpha look back through the REST listing their fetch made (kept per ref for the command), newest first, prereleases admitted by the listing's flags, with the shared walk's same-track stop; no REST request beyond the listing
