title: Reach per-client stable releases the GitHub feed does not hold, by probing the newest stable tag's siblings
description:
## Background

The stable GitHub look-back (omad-author-built-loading-5po6.4) reads `releases.atom`, which holds the 10 newest releases and does not page (`?page=2` returns the same entries).

Observed on 2026-10-24 on `gh:vuhdo-io/VuhDo`:

- `releases/latest` is `v3.218-catac` (Cataclysm only).
- The feed's 10 entries, and the 100 newest releases through the REST API, are all v3.219 alphas and betas, five per build (`-vanilla`, `-tbcc`, `-mopc`, `-catac`, none for retail).
- The stable siblings `v3.218-mopc` (Mists, `release.json` flavor `mists`, interface 50504), `-tbcc`, `-vanilla` and `v3.218` exist, but are beyond any keyless or single-request listing.

So VuhDo installs only on a Cataclysm client until its next stable releases. README Known limitations says so.

## Technical Approach

Probe the siblings of the newest stable tag, keyless:

1. Split the newest stable tag into a version and a suffix (`v3.218` + `-catac`).
2. Learn the repository's suffix vocabulary from the feed's tags. Strip a prerelease mark and the version: `v3.219-mopc-beta-3` gives `-mopc`, and `v3.219-beta-3` gives the empty suffix.
3. For each suffix other than the newest's, fetch `releases/download/<version><suffix>/release.json` from github.com. A 404 means no such release, and costs no REST.
4. The first sibling whose metadata declares the client is the release found. Confirm it is no prerelease with the existing one REST request.

Run the probe only when the feed walk found nothing and every feed entry was named like a prerelease (the feed could not reach a stable release). Bound the probes by the suffix count and `LOOK_BACK_MAX_RELEASES`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A fixture shaped like VuhDo on 2026-10-24 (latest `v3.218-catac`; a feed of 10 `v3.219-*-alpha/beta` tags; stable `v3.218-mopc`, `v3.218-tbcc`, `v3.218-vanilla` and `v3.218`) installs `v3.218-mopc` on Mists Classic and `v3.218-tbcc` on Anniversary, with `older_release_for_client`.
- At most one REST request on the stable path.
- A repository whose feed holds stable releases never probes siblings.
- The memo answers an unchanged newest tag with no request.
- README Known limitations is updated.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Fixture-server tests in `tests/install_look_back.rs`, with net-log counts.
- A unit test of the tag split and of suffix learning (`v3.219-mopc-beta-3` gives `-mopc`; `v3.219-alpha-18` gives the empty suffix; `2.0.0-rc1` gives the empty suffix).

## Considerations

- This is a heuristic. A repository that names per-client tags some other way (a prefix, `mists-v3.218`) is not reached. It never installs anything a `release.json` does not declare, so a wrong guess only costs a 404.
- Deeper REST paging was considered and rejected: VuhDo's stable releases are beyond 100 entries, and unauthenticated REST allows 60 requests an hour.
acceptance_criteria: A VuhDo-shaped fixture (latest v3.218-catac, a feed of 10 v3.219 prereleases, stable v3.218-mopc/-tbcc/-vanilla/v3.218 siblings) installs v3.218-mopc on Mists Classic and v3.218-tbcc on Anniversary with older_release_for_client and at most one REST request; a feed holding stable releases never probes; the memo answers an unchanged newest tag; README Known limitations updated; argc gate passes
close_reason: When every older feed release is named like a prerelease, the look-back probes the newest stable tag's siblings (its version with each suffix the feed's tags use); a look-back never downgrades, placing tags by feed position or else dotted version

title: GitHub look-back runs when the newest release already declares the client, and the refusal then names an older release
description:
## Background

The GitHub look-back (omad-author-built-loading-5po6.4, README "A release per client (GitHub look-back)") exists for repositories whose newest release has no build for the client. It runs whenever some candidate of the newest stable release is refused `wrong_flavor` (`Refusal.wrong_flavor` in `src/engine/plan.rs`).

That trigger is wider than the purpose. A newest release whose `release.json` *does* declare the client, but whose build does not load (below retail 12's interface floor, a game-type gate, TOCs out of range), also starts a look-back. The look-back then finds an older release declaring the same client, which is refused for the same reason.

The coverage re-measure (omad-author-built-loading-5po6.6, 2026-10-24) found 7 such look-backs among 15 hits. On retail, OmniCC 11.2.8 → 11.2.7, Carbonite v11.1.0.1 → v11.0.5.2, Quartz 3.7.17 → 3.7.16a, Cell r274 → r273, OmniBar v34 → v33 and ClassicCastbars v1.9.1 → v1.8.10. On Titan, Plater v661 → v660. Each one:

- spends one REST request (the prerelease check) and downloads the older release;
- changes the refusal so it names the older release: "gh:tullamods/OmniCC: no candidate loads on this client: OmniCC-11.2.7.zip: … below 120000" while the newest is 11.2.8. That misleads anyone reading it.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. A fixture repository with `v2` (newest; `release.json` declares `mainline` 110207; TOC `## Interface: 110207`) and `v1` (`mainline` 110205; TOC 110205), and `releases.atom` listing both.
2. `omaddons install gh:o/foo -t retail --json` on a 12.1.5 client.
3. Today: `releases.atom`, `v1/release.json`, one `api.github.com` request and `v1`'s zip are fetched, and the error names `Foo-v1.zip`.
4. Expected: no look-back. The refusal names `v2`'s asset (`below_client_floor`), and no feed, `release.json` or REST request is made beyond the newest release.

## Technical Approach

- Look back only when the newest release's own metadata declares no build for the client: no asset of the newest set has a `release.json` entry that `declares_client` accepts for this family.
- When the newest release has no `release.json` at all (assets listed through REST), keep today's trigger: nothing says whether it targets the client.
- Keep the look-back's other conditions.
- README, look-back section: "when the newest release declares no build for the client" replaces "when no candidate … installs".

## Acceptance Criteria

- The steps above make no look-back request, and the refusal names the newest release's asset.
- The VuhDo-shaped cases in `tests/install_look_back.rs` still pass. There the newest release declares only another client.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- A new case in `tests/install_look_back.rs`: the newest release declares the client but its TOC is below the floor. Assert no `releases-atom`, no older `release.json` and no `api.github.com` request in the net log, and an error naming the newest asset.
- A planner unit test is not needed beyond the integration case.

## Considerations

- A repository whose newest release declares the client but whose build is broken in some other way gets no fallback. That is deliberate: the look-back answers "no build for this client", not "a build that works".
acceptance_criteria: A newest release whose release.json declares the client but whose build does not load (e.g. below retail 12's floor) starts no look-back: no releases.atom, no older release.json, no api.github.com request, and the refusal names the newest release's asset; VuhDo-shaped look-back cases still pass; argc gate passes
close_reason: Look-back now requires the newest release's own release.json to declare no build for the client; a newest that declares it but does not load is refused by name with no look-back

title: Evidence refusal ignores the archive's own TOC for this client: Raider.IO refused on Mists Classic and Classic Era
description:
## Background

The evidence rule (README "archive grading", omad-author-built-loading epic) refuses a candidate whose `release.json` entries name only other clients, even when its TOCs would load. README Known limitations names Raider.IO on Classic Era and Mists Classic as an example.

The coverage re-measure (omad-author-built-loading-5po6.6, 2026-10-24) found these to be the only two evidence refusals among 1,519 dry runs, and the publisher does build for both clients. `RaiderIO-v202610240600.zip` (`gh:RaiderIO/raiderio-addon`, also the catalog's `RaiderIO`) ships:

- `RaiderIO/RaiderIO_Classic.toc` with `## Interface: 50504` (Mists Classic);
- `RaiderIO/RaiderIO_Vanilla.toc` with `## Interface: 11509` (Classic Era);
- `RaiderIO/RaiderIO.toc` with `120100, 120105`;
- per-region database folders with `_Classic` and `_Vanilla` TOCs too.

Its `release.json` lists the file for `mainline` only, so the metadata is incomplete, not a statement that the build is for retail alone. Under the bead's rule (a refusal of an addon whose publisher targets the client is a defect), these two refusals are defects. They also cost coverage: the build before the rule (b252319) installed Raider.IO on both.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. A Mists Classic 5.5.4 client.
2. `omaddons install RaiderIO -t classic --dry-run --json`.
3. Today: `no_compatible_release`, `tried[0].reason` "wrong_flavor: release.json lists RaiderIO-v202610240600.zip for mainline only".
4. Expected: installs. The archive carries a TOC named for this client (`_Classic` is Mists Classic's family suffix) at the client's interface.

## Technical Approach

- In `evidence_against` (`src/engine/plan.rs`), metadata naming no client is not evidence when the archive's addon folder (the primary folder) itself carries a TOC named for this client. That means a `<Folder>_<suffix>.toc` or `-<suffix>` with a suffix from the client's row (game suffixes, then the family suffix), whose effective interfaces include one in the client's family range.
- A client-specific TOC is the author building for the client, as the `AllowLoadGameType` admission already reasons (README step 4).
- A plain `<Folder>.toc` alone does not count: multi-client base TOCs are exactly what `release.json` disambiguates.
- Name evidence (`its file name … names … only`) follows the same exemption.
- README: drop the Raider.IO example from Known limitations and state the exemption under the evidence rule.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Raider.IO's archive shape installs on Mists Classic and Classic Era with no `wrong_flavor` evidence refusal.
- An archive whose `release.json` names only mainline and whose folder has only a plain TOC listing several clients' interfaces is still refused on a Classic client.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- A fixture in `tests/install_multi_flavor.rs` shaped like Raider.IO (primary folder with `_Classic` and `_Vanilla` TOCs, `release.json` naming mainline only), on Mists Classic, Era and retail.
- The existing evidence-refusal tests keep passing unchanged.

## Considerations

- A per-client TOC whose interface is out of range (a stale `_Classic.toc`) grants no exemption; the interface must be in the client's range.
- Folders other than the primary one do not grant the exemption: a module pack shipping one client-specific folder is not the addon targeting the client.
acceptance_criteria: A release.json naming only other clients is not evidence against when the primary folder carries a TOC named for this client (row suffix) with an in-range interface: Raider.IO's shape installs on Mists Classic and Era; a plain multi-client TOC with release.json naming mainline is still refused on Classic; README updated; argc gate passes
close_reason: Evidence against is waived when the primary folder's loaded TOC is suffixed for this client (game or family suffix) at an in-range interface; Raider.IO installs on Mists Classic and Era, plain multi-client TOCs under metadata for others stay refused

title: GitHub look-back reads the whole feed on single-track repositories: stop after K releases declaring the newest's flavors
description:
## Background

The GitHub look-back (omad-author-built-loading-5po6.4) reads up to `LOOK_BACK_MAX_RELEASES` (10) older releases' `release.json`, sequentially, stopping at the first that declares the client. Each one is two requests: a github.com redirect and the release-assets fetch. Answers are remembered per ref, channel and family against the newest tag.

The coverage re-measure (omad-author-built-loading-5po6.6, 2026-10-24: 217 refs on 7 clients) counted 153 look-backs. 136 found nothing, and every one of those read 9 or 10 releases. They were almost all single-track repositories, such as a retail-only addon on a Classic client, where every release declares the same clients as the newest.

Per family, that is 864 `release.json` reads ("declares no build for this client"), about 1,900 of the run's 3,762 requests. A user with several retail-only GitHub addons and a few Classic clients pays this once per addon and family each time a newest tag changes.

The hits were found early behind same-flavor releases:

- GatherMate2 at depth 2, behind one retail-only release;
- ClassicCastbars on Titan at depth 1;
- Decursive at depth 3, behind two prerelease-named tags that cost nothing.

## Technical Approach

- Stop a look-back after K consecutive older releases whose `release.json` declares exactly the newest release's set of flavors (and no build for this client): the repository publishes one track.
  - Default K = 3, a named constant in `src/politeness.rs`.
  - Prerelease-named tags and releases without `release.json` do not count toward K, and do not reset it.
- Record the stop as a ruled-out entry ("the repository publishes one track: …"), so `tried[]` says why it stopped.
- README: the look-back section and the request costs.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A fixture repository whose 10 releases all declare only `mainline` stops after K `release.json` reads on a Classic client, with the stop in `tried[]`.
- The VuhDo-shaped and GatherMate2-shaped cases (a per-client release behind one same-flavor release) still find their release.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Cases in `tests/install_look_back.rs` with net-log counts of `release-json` requests.

## Considerations

- A per-client repository that published more than K releases for one client in a row is missed until it publishes for this client again. The data above suggests that is rare; K is a constant so it can be tuned.
- The memo already prevents repeats while the newest tag is unchanged; this bounds the first look-back.
acceptance_criteria: A look-back stops after K (politeness constant, default 3) consecutive older releases whose release.json declares exactly the newest release's flavors, recording why in tried[]; a 10-release mainline-only repository costs K release.json reads on a Classic client; VuhDo- and GatherMate2-shaped cases still find their release; argc gate passes
close_reason: A look-back stops after LOOK_BACK_SAME_TRACK (3) consecutive older releases declaring the same other clients, recording the stop in tried[]; prerelease names and missing release.json neither count nor reset

title: Record each folder an install leaves out, with why, and show it in info and list -v
description:
## Background

An install's item lists the folders this client does not load in `folders.skipped`: for example DBM's retail-only boss modules on Classic, and, under the epic's evidence rule, ArkInventory's rules example on Mists Classic. The commit that introduced skipping (77a4127) says: "Skipped folders are never staged, swapped, recorded, indexed or snapshotted." So once the run's output is gone, nothing says what an addon left out or why:

- `update --all` and `sync` scroll the warning away;
- `info` and `list` show only installed folders.

A player who later notices a missing module gets no answer from omaddons. The epic's goal is that every outcome can be explained later.

## Technical Approach

- **The record.** Add `left_out: Vec<SkippedFolder>` to `AddonRecord` (`src/model.rs:569`), with each folder's name and reason serialized as in `folders.skipped` today. Use `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]`, so existing records read unchanged.
- **Every committing install or update replaces it** with the winner's `loadable.skipped`. Folders are re-judged per release, as the partition already is.
- **Undo restores it** with the rest of the record.
- **`info <addon> -t <id>` and `list -v` show it,** for example: "left out: ArkInventoryRules_Example (lists only interface 120105: retail)". In JSON it is a field on the addon object.
- **A release that loads a folder left out before installs it** (already true) and drops it from the record.
- Update the contract snapshots and the JSON schema (`JsonSchema` derives), the README `info` and `list` sections, and the JSON field tables.
- **No `status` attention.** A left-out folder needs no action.

## Acceptance Criteria

- After a DBM-shaped install on Classic Era, `info dbm -t era --json` lists the gated modules with `game_type_excluded`, and `list -v` shows them.
- An update whose release loads a previously left-out folder installs it and removes it from the record. Undo restores the previous record.
- A record written before this change reads without error or warning.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

The companion test bead covers recording, display, re-judging on update, undo and old records.

## Considerations

- `copy` and `export` do not carry `left_out`: it is a fact about one client's install, not a request.
- Keep the reason wire names the same as `folders.skipped`. They are already part of the output contract (vision D21).
acceptance_criteria: AddonRecord carries left_out (name and reason, serde default); every committing install or update replaces it and undo restores it; info and list -v show it; a DBM-shaped install on Era lists its gated modules; an update that newly loads a left-out folder installs it and drops it; records written before the change read without error; argc gate passes
close_reason: AddonRecord.left_out keeps each folder an install left out with why, replaced by every install and update, restored by undo; info shows it, list -v shows it, export and copy never carry it

title: Look back through a GitHub repository's recent releases for the newest build declared for this client
description:
## Background

Per-flavor GitHub projects publish one release per flavor, so `releases/latest` points to whichever flavor shipped last. VuhDo's latest is its Cataclysm Classic build (`VuhDo-v3.218-catac.zip`, with a `release.json` naming `cata` only), so `gh:` VuhDo installs on no live client.

The stable path (`src/sources/github.rs`, D28) reads only `releases/latest` and that tag's `release.json`. README promises "omaddons never falls back to an older release" (line 520).

The other managers look back, per the prior-art review (2026-10-23): WowUp 5 releases, instawow 10, CurseBreaker 15, and strongbox groups every release by game track. The owner decided (2026-10-23) that omaddons looks back too.

## Technical Approach

- **When.** All of these hold:
  - the ref is `gh:`;
  - there is no `--version`, and no pasted release or asset link;
  - the newest release for the channel has no candidate that wins on this client under the loading rules.
- **How, on the stable channel, without the REST API:**
  - Read `releases.atom`, which `GithubSource::recent_tags` already decodes: one conditional request, holding the 10 newest releases.
  - Go newest first, skipping the newest release.
  - For each tag, fetch `releases/download/<tag>/release.json`. That is a github.com web request, with no REST limit.
  - The first release whose `release.json` declares an asset for this client's flavor is the candidate release, judged as usual.
  - Releases without `release.json` are not considered, because their asset names need the REST API.
- **Bound.** The feed's 10 entries, in a named constant in `src/politeness.rs`. Requests are sequential and stop at the first match.
- **Prereleases.** The stable channel never installs a prerelease, and the feed does not mark them. Decide how to tell, and record the decision in a comment here before closing. Two options: one REST request for the chosen release, within `GITHUB_REST_RESERVE`, or another keyless signal.
- **Beta and alpha channels** already list 20 releases through REST (README Channels). Install the newest of them that has a build for this client.
- **Never downgrade.** A look-back result older than the installed release is no update.
- **Existing rules still apply:** pinning, M2-D42's adopted floor, and the release memo. Remember each look-back result per repository and client flavor, keyed by the newest tag. An unchanged newest tag then answers `outdated` without fetching any `release.json`, as the M2-D2 tag-first probe does today.
- **Output.** A warning `older_release_for_client` with no fix, for example: "VuhDo: the newest release v3.218-catac has no build for Mists Classic; installed v3.217-mists, the newest that has". `outdated` and `update` treat that release as the latest for this client.
- **README:** replace the "never falls back" sentence, and update the GitHub row of the Sources table, Channels and the warnings table.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A fixture repository whose newest release declares only `cata` and whose older release declares `mists`:
  - Mists Classic installs the older release, with `older_release_for_client`;
  - Cataclysm Classic installs the newest.
- No release in the feed declares the client: `no_compatible_release`, with `tried` naming each release looked at.
- An installed release newer than the look-back result is not downgraded.
- `outdated` with an unchanged newest tag sends no `release.json` request.
- The net log of a stable look-back shows no `api.github.com` request, or exactly one for the chosen release if the prerelease decision needs it.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

The companion test bead covers the cases above with the HTTP fixture server, and checks the net log.

## Considerations

- The look-back may find a build that is years old for a client the project stopped supporting. It is still the newest the publisher made for that client. The warning says how old the release is, and the usual `out_of_date` verdicts apply.
- Repositories whose per-flavor releases lack `release.json` stay refused. The refusal says the newest release has no build for this client and suggests `info`.
- `outdated` across many per-flavor repositories adds at most one `releases.atom` request and a few `release.json` requests each, and only when the newest tag changed.
acceptance_criteria: When the newest gh: release has no winning candidate for the client, omaddons looks back through releases.atom (10 entries) for the newest release whose release.json declares the client, warns older_release_for_client, never downgrades, never installs a prerelease on stable (decision recorded), memoizes by newest tag, and sends no REST request beyond the recorded prerelease check; README replaces 'never falls back to an older release'; argc gate passes
close_reason: Stable GitHub look-back through releases.atom: newest older release whose release.json declares the client, one REST prerelease check for the release found, memo keyed by newest tag per family, never downgrades, older_release_for_client warning, README updated

comments.text:
Design, before code (claim note). Decisions are marked.

**When.** In `TargetPlanner::prepare_install` (`src/engine/plan.rs`), after the candidate loop finds no winner. All of these must hold:
- a `gh:` ref on the stable channel;
- no `--version`, no pasted asset (`intent.asset`), no `--file`, no rankless cached candidate (`local`);
- the candidates came from the source's set;
- this is not already a look-back (`InstallIntent.looked_back`).

**Decided:** beta and alpha keep today's REST path. A follow-up bead covers looking back within those 20 releases.

**Source** (`Source::look_back`, a default method returning `None`, implemented by `GithubSource`):
1. Read `releases.atom` (`recent_tags`, conditional).
2. Go newest first, skipping the newest tag, at most `LOOK_BACK_MAX_RELEASES` (10, `src/politeness.rs`).
3. Fetch each tag's `release.json` (github.com, no REST). A tag without a usable one is passed over.
4. The first whose metadata names the client wins. The predicate is the evidence rule's: an entry's interface lies in the family's range, else its flavor names the family.
5. It returns `LookBack { found: Option<ReleaseSet>, passed: [(tag, why)], order: [tags newest first] }`.

**Decided: telling a prerelease.** The feed does not mark prereleases, and GitHub flags them only in its REST API. So the chosen tag is confirmed with exactly one REST request: the fallback's `releases/tags/<tag>` maps `prerelease` onto the channel. A prerelease is passed over and the look-back continues. A tag named like a prerelease (`-alpha`, `-beta`, `-rc`, `-pre`) is passed over without asking. When the REST request fails (no budget, rate limited), the look-back stops and the refusal says why. Zero REST when the newest fits; one for a look-back hit.

**Memo** (`ReleaseMemo.look_backs`, keyed by the memo key of the ref and channel plus the client family): `{newest, found, passed, order, at}`, the later `at` winning on merge. `ReleaseCache::look_back` answers from the memo while `newest` is unchanged, so no `release.json` is fetched again. Otherwise it asks the source and remembers the answer.

**Planner.**
- When found, check for a downgrade against the installed record. Install only when there is no record, or when the installed tag is in `order` and older than the found tag.
- If the installed tag is the found one or newer, or not in the feed at all, nothing changes (no downgrade).
- Otherwise prepare again from the found set, with `looked_back: Some(newest)`. The winner warns `older_release_for_client` (new code): "<addon>: the newest release <newest> has no build for <id> (<family>); installed <tag> (<date>), the newest that has". It has no fix.
- When not found, `tried` gains one entry per release looked at (`{asset: "<tag>/release.json", reason: "look_back: …"}`), and the refusal stands.

**Update statuses** (`resolve/updates.rs::evaluate`). This is where facts prove that the newest release does not load here. The memo's look-back for this client, at the same newest tag, is used before `blocked`:
- the installed release is the found one: `current`;
- the installed one is older in `order`: `update_available` (latest = the found release, confidence `declared`);
- otherwise: `current`.

There is no network on this path. `statuses` gains the look-back lookup, and its callers in `outdated`, `update` and `remembered` pass one.

**README.** Replace "omaddons never falls back to an older release". Also update the Sources table's GitHub row, Channels, the warnings table, and the request costs.

title: A per-addon, per-client --any-flavor setting for builds the publisher did not make for this client
description:
## Background

With the evidence rule (omad-mixed-archive-single-file-skk1), omaddons refuses two kinds of file:

- a file whose `release.json` or file name names only other clients;
- an addon whose main folder's TOC targets only other clients.

Some of those still work. Many small addons run unchanged across clients while their TOC lists only retail, and players have long used "Load out of date AddOns" for them. The owner asked that the user, or the user's agent, be able to decide.

`--force` is the wrong tool:

- It already authorizes taking over another addon's folder, replacing an unmanaged one (README line 769) and importing a backup across families (line 1251).
- Agents apply suggested fixes mechanically, and README's agent rules say "--force only after reading the refusal" (line 2740).
- `update` has no `--force` (line 858), so a one-shot override at install would be refused again at the next update.

**Prior art** (prior-art review, 2026-10-23):

- instawow's per-addon `any_flavour` strategy is stored with the package and reapplied on update.
- CurseBreaker's `IgnoreClientVersion` is stored per URL.
- WowUp's "Install at your own risk" dialog is not saved anywhere, and it led to WowUp #1283: a user clicked through and got retail LittleWigs on TBC.

## Technical Approach

- **Flags.** `install --any-flavor` sets the setting on the addon's record for that client, and `--no-any-flavor` clears it. Every other install, update and sync keeps it, as `channel` is kept.
- **Where it is stored:**
  - the record: `AddonRecord.any_flavor: bool`, with serde default `false`;
  - `addons.toml`: the table-form entry key `any_flavor = true` (`Entry`, `src/state/desired.rs:81`), written by `export` and applied by `sync`, `--locked` included.
- **Judgement under the setting:**
  - Evidence against is ignored.
  - A folder whose TOC the client reads, but whose interfaces are off-range or missing (`InterfaceNotInFamily`, `NoInterface`), is `Compatible { out_of_date: true }` with the `out_of_date` warning, as the game lists it. The main folder may be such a folder.
  - Still left out or refused: `GameTypeExcluded` (the author excluded this client), `NoLoadableToc` (the client reads no TOC), the retail floor of omad-retail-12-floor-e5a0 (the client never loads it), and `DependencySkipped` on any of those.
  - The ownership, `Blizzard_*` and symlink rules are unchanged.
- **Visibility.** `status` shows every addon with the setting: an attention reason `any_flavor` at the lowest severity, or whatever the status contract offers for a standing note. `list` and `info` mark it. Each install under the setting warns `any_flavor`, naming what it allowed: the evidence, or the off-range folders.
- **How it is offered.** Refusals from the evidence rule, and from an off-range main folder, carry an `alternatives` entry with the `--any-flavor` argv, never `fix` or `fix_argv`. README's agent guidance: use it only when the user asks for that addon on that client.
- **`copy` does not carry it** to another client: it is a per-client decision.
- **README:** the flags table, the `addons.toml` keys, "How omaddons decides what loads", and the warnings and attention tables.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **A retail-only addon** (plain TOC, `## Interface: 120105`) on Mists Classic:
  - refused without the setting;
  - with `--any-flavor`, installed with `out_of_date`;
  - `update` and `sync` keep it, and `export` writes `any_flavor = true`;
  - `--no-any-flavor` clears it, and the next update refuses.
- A file whose `release.json` names only mainline installs on Mists Classic under the setting, with an `any_flavor` warning naming `release.json`.
- Under the setting, a folder with `AllowLoadGameType: standard` is still left out on Mists Classic.
- Under the setting, a retail 12.x client still refuses a TOC below 120000.
- A refusal's `alternatives` include the `--any-flavor` retry; `fix_argv` does not.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

The companion test bead covers setting, keeping and clearing it through install, update, sync, export and undo, the limits that still apply, `status` and the shape of the refusal.

## Considerations

- **Undo** of the install that set it restores the record without it.
- **Pinned addons** keep the setting. Pinning and `--any-flavor` are independent.
- **Dependencies** installed for such an addon do not inherit the setting. Each is judged on its own, and a refused dependency is reported as today.
- `--dry-run --any-flavor` shows what would install and records nothing.
acceptance_criteria: install --any-flavor sets a recorded per-addon per-client setting (record and addons.toml any_flavor), kept by update and sync and cleared by --no-any-flavor; under it evidence against is ignored and off-range or missing interfaces install as out_of_date, while GameTypeExcluded, NoLoadableToc and the retail 12.0 floor still refuse; status, list and info show it; refusals offer it under alternatives, never fix_argv; README updated; argc gate passes
close_reason: install --any-flavor sets a recorded per-addon, per-client setting (record and addons.toml), kept by update, sync and reinstall and cleared by --no-any-flavor; under it evidence is ignored and off-range folders install out of date, while game-type gates, TOCs the client never reads and the retail floor still refuse; status, list and info show it; refusals offer it among alternatives only

comments.text: claim: install/--no-any-flavor flags (src/cli.rs, src/app/install.rs), AddonRecord.any_flavor, InstallIntent and carry_over, judging under the setting (src/engine/plan.rs), update statuses, addons.toml (src/state/desired.rs, export, sync), status/list/info, refusal alternatives, README. Test companion .11 follows.

comments.author: CobaltOak
comments.text:
What landed, and the decisions taken where the bead left a choice.

**Stored.**
- `AddonRecord.any_flavor` (serde default false, written only when true).
- `addons.toml` `any_flavor = true` on a table entry (`Entry.any_flavor`; parse, render, the round-trip proptest).
- `export` writes it, and its family-section "alike" key now includes it.
- `sync` sets or clears it to match the file. When only it differs, a records-only `RecordEdit::SetAnyFlavor`. When the pin differs too, one install that keeps the release.

**Flags.** `install --any-flavor` / `--no-any-flavor` (they conflict) become `AnyFlavorIntent::{Set, Clear}` on `RequestedChange::Install` and `InstallIntent`. Every other caller keeps `Keep`, `copy` included. `carry_over` takes the intent, or the record when the resolver installs.
- On an installed addon at its release it is an `edited` item with `fields: ["any_flavor"]` (new `EditField::AnyFlavor`), which undo takes back.
- **Decided:** on a pinned addon it is also records-only (`pinned_setting_only`). It never moves the release, and it needs no fetch.

**Judgement** (`try_candidate(…, any_flavor)`). The setting is on when the intent applies to the record, never for a dependency (`!from_resolver()`). The candidate is first graded by the client's own rules, and `learn` records that verdict whatever the setting, so the memo stays one client's truth. Under the setting:
- evidence against is dropped;
- `InterfaceNotInFamily` and `NoInterface` folders become `Compatible { out_of_date: true }`, each with an `out_of_date` warning;
- partition and grade run again;
- one `any_flavor` warning (new code, 51) names everything it allowed.

`GameTypeExcluded`, `NoLoadableToc`, `BelowClientFloor` and `DependencySkipped` on those are unchanged. **Decided:** update statuses ignore "verified not loading" facts for an addon with the setting (`resolve/updates.rs`), so `update` still installs its newer releases. `check_release` (adopt's verify) never applies it.

**Offered.** `Refusal.overridable` is true for evidence, or when the deciding folder is off-range or missing an interface. The `no_compatible_release` and `wrong_flavor` errors then gain the alternative `omaddons install <ref> -t <id> --any-flavor`. It is never the fix, and it is not offered for the floor, a game-type gate or a folder with no TOC this client loads.

**Decided: status visibility is a fact, not attention.** `status --check` exits 6 on any attention, so attention would fail it forever for a deliberate choice. `status` instead carries `targets[].any_flavor: [names]` (live and missing clients) and a human line, `any flavor: Foo (builds not made for this client, by --any-flavor)`. `list` (`any_flavor`, marked `any-flavor`) and `info` (`installed[].any_flavor`, ` · any flavor (--any-flavor)`) mark it.

**README.** The install flags table and a new "A build not made for this client: `--any-flavor`" section. Also: `sync`'s table keys, `copy`, `status`, `list`, `info`, the warnings table (51), Known limitations, and the agent rules ("only when the user asks for that addon on that client").

**Tests (with .11).**
- `tests/install_any_flavor.rs` (5 tests): refused with the alternative and never the fix; installed with `out_of_date` and `any_flavor`; visible in list, info and status (and `status --check` still exits 0); kept by `update --refresh`; written by export and reapplied by sync after a remove; cleared by `--no-any-flavor` (`edited`), after which the next update is `blocked`; `release.json` evidence ignored and named; a game-type gate, a `_Mainline`-only folder and the retail floor still refusing (the floor without an alternative); undo of a records-only set; copy not carrying it; a retail-only dependency not installed for it.
- `src/state/desired.rs`: an explicit round trip.

Four contract snapshots gained the keys `any_flavor` (list) and `any_flavor` (status, info).

title: Re-measure keyless coverage under the new loading rules and explain every changed cell
description:
## Background

The report of omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.7 (comment 868) measured keyless coverage on seven clients (mainline, mists, tbc, vanilla, forever, titan, wrath-legacy) for two lists: the WoWInterface top 100 by total downloads, and a 66-name CurseForge-only composite.

Several changes alter what installs:

- the epic omad-author-built-loading-5po6: left-out folders, the `AllowLoadGameType` rule, the evidence refusal (its one tightening) and GitHub look-back;
- the related bugs: the retail 12.0 floor (omad-retail-12-floor-e5a0) and newer-only interfaces (omad-newer-interface-out-of-date-9550).

Before README rests on these, the same measurement must show what moved and why.

## Technical Approach

- **Rebuild the study's harness**, since its scripts were not kept:
  - a throwaway `HOME` with a synthetic Battle.net root holding the seven clients;
  - the same lists (comment 868 names their sources), with the WoWInterface file list fetched again;
  - `omaddons install --dry-run --json` for each addon on each client;
  - the study's outcome definitions (current, out of date, refused).
- **Diff against comment 868's per-addon tables,** and name the rule behind every changed cell.
- **List every new refusal from the evidence rule,** with the file and the evidence, and say whether the publisher builds for that client.
  - Any refusal of an addon whose publisher targets the client is a defect, and so is any install of a build that metadata labels for another client.
  - File each defect with `--deps discovered-from:<this bead>`.
- **Politeness as in the study:** no requests to `api.curseforge.com`, and REST stays under its limit. Report the request counts by host.
- Post the report as a comment here, then close.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A comment holds the new matrix, the diff with the rule behind each changed cell, the evidence refusals with a verdict on each, and the request counts.
- Each defect found is filed as discovered-from this bead.

## Test Plan

No code changes. The check is the diff: every changed cell has a named cause.

## Considerations

- Release state moves between runs (new uploads, new tags). Report cells that changed for that reason separately from cells changed by rules.
- Run the release binary built at the last code commit, and say which commit it is.

report: keyless coverage re-measured under the new loading rules, 2026-10-24 (UTC), omaddons 3c764b0

## Method

- **Binaries.** Release builds of `3c764b0` (the last code commit, "new") and of `b252319`, the study's own commit (omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.7 comment 868, "old"). Both ran against today's releases, so:
  - old-today vs the 2026-10-20 study isolates release movement;
  - new vs old-today isolates rule changes.
- **Home.** One throwaway home, built by the new ignored test `tests/perf.rs::coverage_home` (`COVERAGE_HOME=<dir> cargo test --test perf coverage_home -- --ignored`), which keeps the harness this time. It holds the study's seven clients: retail 12.1.5, Mists Classic 5.5.4, Anniversary 2.5.6, Classic Era 1.15.9, Forever 1.60.1, Titan 3.80.2, and a custom 3.3.5a. Every run was `env -i` with that home's `coverage.env` only; nothing was written outside it, and no real client was touched. All runs were dry runs.
- **Refs.** Exactly the 217 refs of comment 868's per-addon tables, the two lists' "Keyless sources found" columns: 124 `wowi:`, 70 `gh:` (three as `@beta`, run with `--channel beta`), 36 catalog names, 10 `git:`. There was no GitHub search this time.
- **Runs.** One `install <ref> -t <id> --dry-run --no-deps --json` per ref and client: 1,519 runs per binary. The old binary ran first (16:07–16:12Z), then the new one (16:12–16:18Z). The new binary reads the old memo (1.0), but not the reverse.
- **Outcomes, as the study defined them.**
  - *Installs*: every loaded TOC is current. A lag within the client's major.minor counts as current (an `out_of_date` warning for 20505 on 2.5.6 does not demote a cell).
  - *Out of date*: a TOC from an older major.minor, or one the client loads only as out of date (`AllowLoadGameType` admission).
  - *Refused*: nothing installs.

The three `@beta` refs (Bagnon, ArkInventory, DynamicCam) changed message only ("no published beta release among the newest 20" → "has no published releases", omad-github-no-releases-message-wvw1). Their cells did not change.

- **`RaiderIO` on classic (Mists) and era**, "release.json lists RaiderIO-v202610240600.zip for mainline only".

Of the 120 GitHub installs whose newest release carries `release.json` metadata (look-back installs excluded, as their release declares the client by construction), none installed a release whose metadata names only other clients.

## The look-back in numbers

- 151 look-backs (153 `releases.atom` requests): 15 found a release and 136 found none. Every miss read 9 or 10 releases, ruling them out as 864 "declares no build for this client", 220 "publishes no release.json" and 150 "named like a prerelease".
- **7 of the 15 hits are spurious.** OmniCC, Carbonite, Quartz, Cell, OmniBar and ClassicCastbars on mainline, and Plater on Titan: the newest release already declares the client but does not load (mostly the floor). Each look-back found an older release that fails the same way, spent a REST request and a download, and made the refusal name the older release. Filed: omad-author-built-loading-5po6.15.
- **The misses cost about 1,900 requests.** They are single-track repositories, such as retail-only addons on Classic clients. Filed: omad-author-built-loading-5po6.17, which stops after K releases declaring the newest's flavors; the hits above were all found within depth 3.

- Its extra github.com and release-assets lines are the look-back: `release-json` went 119 → 2,021, `releases-atom` 0 → 153.
- REST stayed far under 60 an hour: 43 calls in 6 minutes.
  - 15 were prerelease checks, one per look-back hit.
  - 21 were beta listings and 7 were Details!'s tag lookup, as in the old phase.
  - The old phase's four zip-only tag lookups (Narcissus, Plumber, Pawn, Prat) did not recur.
- **The harness's own cost.** One `install` per ref and client re-fetches each ref seven times (install always fetches fresh). That puts `api.mmoui.com` at 868 requests per phase, where the study's one `sync` per source made 5. This is the harness, not the product; a re-run should batch per source as the study did.
- No request went to `api.curseforge.com`, `forgecdn.net` or `wago.io`.

title: Test: an AllowLoadGameType naming the client makes an off-range interface out of date
description:
## Background

This is the test companion of omad-author-built-loading-5po6.1: an `AllowLoadGameType` that names the client's own game type makes the folder this client's build, out of date when its interface is off-range. Without these tests a regression would quietly refuse Titan Panel 9.3.5 on Anniversary again, through the archive rule of omad-mixed-archive-single-file-skk1.

## Technical Approach

- **Unit tests** in the `src/toc/loaded.rs` test module, using its in-memory `Memory` folder and `judge`, with the TitanAmmo TOC verbatim:

  ```
  ## Interface: 11509, 16001, 205056
  ## AllowLoadGameType: camelot, tbc, vanilla
  ## Dependencies: Titan
  ```

- **TOC-matrix rows** in `tests/fixtures/toc/matrix/cases.toml` for that folder on every client row, with the matrix snapshot updated.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each case below is a test.
- With the admission removed from `judge`, the Anniversary case fails.

## Test Plan

- Anniversary (`tbc`): `Compatible { out_of_date: true }`. The `out_of_date` warning names 205056 and does not say "older than".
- Classic Era (`vanilla`) and Forever (`camelot`): judged by their in-range values (11509, 16001), as today.
- Retail and Mists Classic: `GameTypeExcluded`.
- A legacy 2.4.3 client: game types ignored, verdict as today.
- `AllowLoadGameType: classic` with only `## Interface: 120105` on Classic Era: `InterfaceNotInFamily`.
- `ExcludeLoadGameType: tbc` together with `AllowLoadGameType: tbc` on Anniversary: `GameTypeExcluded`.
- An `AllowLoadGameType` reached only through an inline directive admits only where that directive applies.

## Considerations

- Keep the TitanAmmo TOC verbatim in the fixture: the typo is the point.

title: Test: download choice by evidence on real archive shapes
description:
## Background

This is the test companion of omad-mixed-archive-single-file-skk1: grading downloads Clean, LeftOut or Refused, evidence against from `release.json` and the file name, and refusals that name their reason. It replaces the old rule ("a folder that merely lists another client's interface refuses the archive"), so the tests pin the new outcomes on the real archive shapes that motivated it, and pin the one tightening.

## Technical Approach

- Integration tests in `tests/install_multi_flavor.rs`, using its helpers (`Home`, `folder`, `release`, `skipped`, `on_disk`, `strings`) and the HTTP fixture server.
- Archives are built from TOC text. Shapes are taken from the real releases, with the TOC lines that matter kept verbatim.
- Update the "ungated-sibling" scenario of `without_metadata_only_gated_folders_are_skipped` (around line 420): it now installs `Foo` with `FooRetail` left out.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each scenario below is a test.
- Removing the evidence check fails the `release.json` and file-name cases.
- Treating LeftOut as Refused fails the ArkInventory case.
- Ignoring Clean-before-LeftOut fails the rank case.

## Test Plan

- **ArkInventory 3.12.17 shape.**
  - Fixture: ArkInventory, ArkInventoryConfig, ArkInventoryRules and ArkInventorySearch, each with plain (120105), `_Mists`, `_Vanilla`, `_BCC` and `_Camelot` TOCs, plus `ArkInventoryRules_Example` with a plain TOC holding only 120105, `## DefaultState: Disabled` and `## RequiredDeps: ArkInventoryRules`.
  - On Mists Classic, Classic Era and Forever: 4 folders added, `ArkInventoryRules_Example=interface_not_in_family` skipped, one `folder_left_out` warning, and the folders on disk match.
  - On retail: all 5 folders.
- **Titan Panel 9.3.5 shape:** Titan plus plugins, with the TitanAmmo TOC verbatim. On Anniversary every folder installs and TitanAmmo carries `out_of_date`. Needs omad-author-built-loading-5po6.1.
- **Carbonite shape:** `Carbonite.Info` lists only classic and Forever interfaces. On retail it is left out and the rest installs.
- **BlizzMove 3.8.5 shape:** `BlizzMove_Debug` omits 16001. On Forever it is left out and the rest installs.
- **Clean beats LeftOut whatever the rank:** a release with `Foo-classic.zip` (name hint for classic, LeftOut on Classic Era) and `Foo.zip` (unannotated, Clean). Classic Era installs `Foo.zip`.
- **`release.json` evidence:** a release whose `release.json` lists `Foo.zip` for mainline only, with a clean TOC (`120105, 50504`). On Mists Classic: `no_compatible_release`, and both the human message and `tried` name `release.json`.
- **File-name evidence:** the single asset `Foo-1.0-retail.zip`, clean on Classic Era. Refused, naming the file name.
- **Sources that are never evidence:**
  - a Tukui list without the client (the ElvUI-on-Forever case) still installs as today;
  - WoWInterface compatibility tags never refuse.
- **A legacy client** (custom 3.3.5a) with a `release.json`-annotated asset: the metadata says nothing, so it is judged by TOCs as today.
- **The update check:** `outdated` reports an update whose only winning candidate is LeftOut, and `info` shows it loading.
- **Cached reinstall:** `install --reinstall` of a LeftOut install asks the source for the release (the net log shows the request) and installs the same folders.
- **The human refusal:** a retail-only addon on Classic Era. The message names the folder and says it lists only interface 120105 (retail). Snapshot test on the human output.

## Considerations

- Fixtures stay small (a TOC and one Lua file per folder) but keep each real TOC line that drives the verdict.
- Each scenario is its own release, so the archive memo (keyed by hash) does not cross scenarios.

title: A stored undo --run R -t X forgets its client, so the plan can never apply
description:
## Background

`omaddons undo --run <run> -t <client>` reverts only that run's transaction on that client (README "undo": "`--run RUN` ... with `-t`, only its transaction on that client"). Its `--dry-run` stores a plan (D4, the plan store), and the plan's typed intent is what `omaddons apply <plan_id>` will execute (D5, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`).

`UndoIntent` (`src/app/intent.rs`) holds only `selection: UndoSelection` (`Tx(tx)` or `Run(run)`), `saved_variables` and `while_running`; it names no client. `undo::resolved_selection` (`src/app/undo.rs`) returns `Run(run)` whenever `data.reverted_run` is set, and `select` sets `reverted_run: Some(run)` for `--run` with or without `-t`. So the stored intent of `undo --run R -t retail` is `Run(R)` with no client: the client narrowing is lost.

Found while building `StoredIntent::target_selector` for D5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5.3`): an undo intent has no client to hand back, so the applied run gets no `-t`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On a test home with two clients, make one run that commits on both (for example `omaddons update` with an update on each).
2. `omaddons history --json`: note the run id `R` shared by the two transactions.
3. `omaddons undo --run R -t retail --dry-run --json`: the preview reverts one transaction (retail's), and `data.plan_id` names the stored plan.
4. Read the plan file under `<cache>/plans/<plan_id>.json`: `intent` is `{"command":"undo","selection":{"run":"R"},…}` and `display_argv` is `["omaddons","undo","--run","R"]`, without `-t`.

Today nothing applies plans, so the effect is a stored plan and `display_argv` that describe a different undo (the whole run). Once `apply` exists, applying it runs `undo --run R` without a client: its preview covers two transactions, its token differs from the stored one, and the run is refused with `plan_stale` every time. It never undoes the wrong thing, but the plan can never apply.

## Technical Approach

Store what the preview resolved, as `UndoSelection::Tx` when `-t` narrowed a run to one client:

- A run commits at most one transaction per client, so `--run R -t X` selects exactly one transaction. In `undo::run`, when `ctx.target` is set and the selection came from `--run`, store `UndoSelection::Tx(<that transaction>)` instead of `Run(R)`. Do it where the `StorableArgs::Undo` selection is built (or in `resolved_selection`, given whether `-t` narrowed it), without changing `UndoData` (its `reverted_run` stays as today: it is wire output).
- `display_argv` then reads `omaddons undo <tx>`, which a person can run and which reverts exactly that transaction; its token is the same (one planned undo of that tx on that key).
- No plan-format change: `UndoIntent` keeps its fields (D4's type). The rejected alternative is adding an optional `target` to `UndoIntent`, which changes the plan file's schema for a case `Tx` already expresses.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `undo --run R -t X --dry-run` stores an intent whose selection is `Tx(<X's transaction of R>)`, and `display_argv` is `omaddons undo <tx>`.
- [ ] `undo --run R --dry-run` (no `-t`) still stores `Run(R)`; `undo <tx>`, bare `undo`, `undo -t X` and `undo --last-by A` store what they do today.
- [ ] `UndoData` (including `reverted_run`) and every existing snapshot are unchanged.
- [ ] The stored token equals the token a direct `undo <tx> --dry-run` returns for the same home.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files.

## Test Plan

- Unit (`src/app/undo.rs`, beside `resolved_selection`'s table): a case for a run narrowed by `-t` resolving to `Tx`, and the existing cases unchanged.
- Integration (`tests/apply.rs` stored-preview suite, or `tests/undo_history.rs`): a two-client run; `undo --run R -t retail --dry-run --json` stores a plan whose intent is `Tx` and whose `display_argv` has no `--run`; its `data.precondition` equals `undo <tx> --dry-run --json`'s.
- Once D5's `apply` exists, its round-trip E2E (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5.6`) should include `undo --run R -t X`.

## Considerations

- `undo --run R -t X` where X has no transaction of R is already `not_found` ("run R has nothing to undo here"); unchanged.
- An undo transaction committed later in the same run is not a concern: the selection is resolved at preview time and the token binds it.
- Hot spot `src/app/undo.rs`: D4 and D5 touch it; keep the change to where the selection is stored.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] undo --run R -t X --dry-run stores an intent whose selection is Tx(<X's transaction of R>), and display_argv is omaddons undo <tx>.
- [ ] undo --run R --dry-run (no -t) still stores Run(R); undo <tx>, bare undo, undo -t X and undo --last-by A store what they do today.
- [ ] UndoData (including reverted_run) and every existing snapshot are unchanged.
- [ ] The stored token equals the token a direct undo <tx> --dry-run returns for the same home.
- [ ] argc gate passes; ubs is clean on the changed files.
close_reason: done: undo --run R -t X stores its client's transaction (Tx), so its plan applies and reverts that client only; argc gate passed

The test fails without the fix (stored {run: R}), checked by stashing src/app/undo.rs. decided: narrowed is ctx.target.is_some(), the same -t that selected the run's transaction on that client. title: M4 common rules for every leaf and subtask
description:
# M4 common rules

These rules apply to every M4 leaf and subtask under the milestone epic `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`. Each of those beads has a comment pointing here instead of carrying its own copy. Read this once per session (and again after a context compaction), not once per bead. A bead cites a rule by number, as "common rule N"; for example common rule 14 is the design gate.

## The rules (M4 plan §8.0)

Plan keys (A1 … H6) map to bead ids in the first comment on the milestone epic.

1. **The gate.** `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code: `*.rs`, `Cargo.*`, `rust-toolchain.toml`, `deny.toml`, lint config, embedded assets (`omarchy/**`, `catalog/**`, `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md`, `src/contract/guide/*.md`), fixtures or snapshots (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). Run `ubs` on the changed files. `argc gate --all` (cargo deny) is required when `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` or `deny.toml` changed.
2. **One writer.** Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`).
   - A new subprocess needs a named entry in that test's spawner allowlist, with its reason.
   - A new `prune()` caller needs a `PRUNE_CALLERS` entry. In `src/doctor/`, only `gc.rs` may prune (M4-D36).
3. **Commands never print.** They return an `Outcome` that `src/output/` renders. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests, and no `unsafe`.
4. **DEC-1, no stubs.** A command leaf adds, in the same commit:
   1. its clap variant;
   2. its `COMMANDS` row, with every M4 field (`dictionary`, `exits`, `data`, `stores_plan`, `network`; A1);
   3. its `command_name` and dispatch arms;
   4. the help-layout update;
   5. contract matrix rows (one success, one failure, with snapshots);
   6. the `special.rs` read-only invocation for any `mutates: false` path;
   7. `cli_skeleton` literals;
   8. its `CLI_PATHS` row in `omarchy/Model.js`;
   9. its README section.
5. **DEC-3, wire shapes.** Every `data` and report struct derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`. Field order is rendering order (deterministic, but not contract: M4-D56), maps are `BTreeMap`, and no `HashMap` or `HashSet` appears in a serialized type (M4-D18).
6. **DEC-4, the contract.** List every new or changed wire name (codes, `details` keys, data keys, actions, events, kinds, files) in the close comment.
   - Add by default. A leaf may rename, retype or remove a name only on a surface it owns, to correct a known pre-release inconsistency: it records the change with a compatibility note in its close comment and updates the widget, the guide, the snapshots and the corpus in the same commit (M4-D55). Any other rename waits for H1.
   - Every new shape passes A3's rule test; never add to `tests/contract/rules_allowlist.txt`.
   - Declare every new error's `DetailSpec` (M4-D10) and every new code's `meaning` (A9).
   - Declare every new volatile key in `contract::VOLATILE` (M4-D18).
   - `schema_version` stays "1.0".
7. **D22, constants.** New constants go in `src/limits.rs` or `src/politeness.rs`, each with a `REGISTRY` row and a `LIMIT_NAMES` entry, and the `limit_registries` snapshot is re-accepted (review the diff).
8. **Fixes.** Every error carries a `fix`, and a `fix_argv` when the fix is a complete omaddons command. A usage error found from the arguments (a misplaced client, a bad value) is raised before planning, recovery or any commit, so the wrong invocation changes nothing. A prose fix may not name a runnable omaddons command (`PROSE_COMMANDS`, `names_a_command` in `tests/contract/main.rs`). A fix that keeps the user's verb is marked `UsageFix::UserVerb` (M4-D12).
9. **Privacy, on every channel.** No output names an account, realm or character. Tests that create `WTF/` run `assert_private_all(stdout, stderr)` with `--progress json`. Doctor evidence never carries file content (M4-D42).
10. **Real machine.** Real-machine tests never change the Forever client (`forever_guard()`), undo every change before asserting, quote every `SKIP` line, and never write under a `WTF/`.
11. **README is the product contract.** A leaf that ships a user-visible surface updates its README section in the same commit.
12. **Beads.**
    - Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`.
    - File found work with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`.
    - Run `br lint <ids> --json` clean.
    - Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`.
    - Bead text never contains home paths, host names or people's names; use the placeholders of §0.2.
13. **Time.** Code that uses local time takes `jiff::tz::TimeZone::system()`. Tests set `TZ=UTC` and, where expiry matters, `OMADDONS_NOW`.
14. **A protocol change lands with its own crash tests.** A leaf that adds or changes a journal shape, a recovery rule, a binding rule, a deletion rule or a durability rule closes only when its own adversarial matrix passes: every failpoint it adds, every journaled step, repeated recovery, and injected I/O failure where it writes. These leaves are D1, D2, D5, D8, E5, E7, E8, E11, E14 and G3. F9 integrates across fixers. It never discovers whether a leaf's own protocol works.
15. **Bounded work.** A leaf that reads an untrusted or user-sized input bounds it with a named constant, and reports exhaustion as truncated or incomplete, never as a clean result. A store a leaf writes has a hard quota, and a full store declines the write rather than evicting live data.
16. **Previews bind.** A leaf that adds or changes a mutating command path either binds it (`app::precondition`, `--if-match`, and a test that changes state between preview and run) or records in its close comment why it does not, citing M4-D22.
17. **The guide stays the skill** (M4-D7). Once B1 has landed, a leaf that changes anything the guide's generated blocks show (a command, a code, an action, an env var) regenerates `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` with `OMADDONS_UPDATE_SKILL=1 cargo test --test skill` and commits it. That renders from a hermetic `TestEnv`, never the developer's real `HOME` or config, and no shell redirect writes a gated asset. `tests/skill.rs` fails until it does.
18. **The corpus grows with the surface.** Once C4 has landed, a leaf that adds a command or an intent hook adds its corpus rows to `tests/contract/intent_corpus.rs`. Whichever of C4 and the command leaf lands second adds them.
19. **The doctor's catalog is code.** A leaf that adds a failure mode adds its `FAILURE_MODES` row, its fixture (M4-D47), its row in README's doctor table, and its Appendix B line in the close comment.

## Defaults for questions a bead does not answer (M4 plan §8.1)

When a leaf or subtask meets a question its bead does not settle, apply these defaults in order, record the choice in a `decided:` comment on the bead, and extend README if the choice changes a promise:

1. Prefer an existing error code, warning code, action or key to a new one.
2. Additive JSON, token-frugal by default. Detail goes behind `-v`.
3. Stable order: sorted by target id, then name, then path.
4. No network on a read path, except for commands whose job is upstream (`outdated`, `search`, `info`, `doctor --online`).
5. Every write through fsx, and every mutation through a transaction or a recorded settings line.
6. Fail closed on anything persisted that cannot be fully read.
7. Never ask the owner. Decide, write `decided: … because …`, and move on (CLAUDE.md "Blocked on a Human").

title: Doctor journal findings name the repair a journal waits behind (behind_barrier evidence)
description:
## Background

E14's third part (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14.3) makes recovery run in three passes and leaves a journal behind a repair it could not settle: a folder or repair journal a stuck set-aside (or its undo) names, or every journal behind a repair whose `prepared` line cannot be read. `journal::diagnose` then gives that journal `JournalVerdict::BehindBarrier { owner, stop }` and keeps the verdict it would have reached on its own in `JournalEvidence.held`.

That bead's "Interfaces for the dependents" says: F1 reports a journal behind a barrier under its own state, with `behind_barrier: <owner>` in its evidence. F1 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1, the journal and lock detectors) was already closed, so 5.14.3 did the half that needs no wire change: `src/doctor/detectors/concurrency.rs` maps a `BehindBarrier` diagnosis by its `evidence.held` verdict, so the finding names the journal's own failure mode, title and reason. The finding does not yet say what holds the journal back. An agent reading `doctor` output sees "An interrupted change waits to be finished" with a remediation ("quit the game and run any changing command") that will not settle it: the next change fails with the owner repair's error until that repair is settled.

## Technical Approach

- `src/doctor/finding.rs`: add `behind_barrier: Option<TxId>` to `Evidence` (serialized only when set, `skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"`, like its neighbours), placed after `tx`.
- `src/doctor/detectors/concurrency.rs` (`journal_observation`): when `d.verdict` is `JournalVerdict::BehindBarrier { owner, .. }`, set `evidence.behind_barrier = Some(owner)`. Keep the row, title and reason of the held verdict (already done).
- Decide (and record in a `decided:` comment) whether the remediation of a held journal should be the owner's `doctor explain` (`fence::explain_fix` of the owner's stop reason) instead of its own row's. The owner's own finding already carries that remediation, so the default is to keep the journal's own remediation and only add the evidence key; prefer the default unless README promises otherwise.
- README: the doctor section's "What it reports" evidence list names `behind_barrier` (common rule 11).
- DEC-4 (common rule 6): `behind_barrier` is a new wire name on doctor evidence; list it in the close comment. It must pass A3's rule test (snake case, a string ULID) with no allowlist line, and the doctor report schema snapshot is re-accepted after review.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A folder journal behind a stuck set-aside, and a journal behind an unreadable repair, each give one finding under the journal's own failure mode, whose evidence carries `behind_barrier` equal to the owner's transaction id.
- No other finding gains the key; a journal not behind a barrier serializes exactly as before (snapshots of existing findings unchanged).
- The doctor report schema declares `behind_barrier`; A3's rule test passes with no allowlist line.
- README's doctor evidence list names the key.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit (`src/doctor/detectors/concurrency.rs`): table-driven over diagnoses built by hand: `BehindBarrier` with each held verdict kind (recoverable, unreadable, unattributed) gives the held verdict's row and `behind_barrier: Some(owner)`; a diagnosis with no barrier gives `None`.
- Integration: one `doctor --json` run on a home with a stuck set-aside in front of an install journal (the plant `stuck_set_aside` in `src/engine/fence.rs`'s tests shows how) asserts the finding's evidence key, under `TestLog`.

## Considerations

- `evidence.held` is `None` only if a `BehindBarrier` diagnosis were built without `held()`; the detector already falls back to the pending row then.
- Doctor evidence must never carry file content or a path below `WTF/` (M4-D42); a transaction id is neither.
- No new failure mode, error code, warning code or constant.
acceptance_criteria: A journal behind a stuck set-aside, and one behind an unreadable repair, each give one finding under the journal's own failure mode with evidence behind_barrier = the owner's tx; no other finding gains the key and existing snapshots are unchanged; the doctor report schema declares it and A3's rule test passes with no allowlist line; README's doctor evidence list names it; argc gate passes.

title: The process route never sees the Battle.net app: under GE-Proton it runs as CrBrowserMain, not Battle.net.exe
description:
## Background

README discovery route list: "the prefixes of **running WoW and Battle.net processes** (their `WINEPREFIX`, your own processes only) …: a client in a nested prefix … is found while it runs". `src/discover/running.rs::process_prefixes` matches `comm` against every product exe plus `Wow.exe`, `Wow-64.exe` and `Battle.net.exe`.

omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.1 recorded the real process shapes on 2026-10-20 (Battle.net 2.53.5.17932 under umu-launcher and GE-Proton 11-11). The Battle.net app's processes all run `C:\Program Files (x86)\Battle.net\Battle.net.exe`, but their `comm` values are Chromium thread names: `CrBrowserMain` (the main process), `CrGpuMain`, `CrUtilityMain`, `CrRendererMain`. No process had `comm` `Battle.net.exe`. The other Battle.net-side processes were `Agent.exe` (argv[0] `C:/ProgramData/Battle.net/Agent/Agent.<n>/Agent.exe`, forward slashes) and `umu.exe` (argv[1] the Linux path of `Battle.net Launcher.exe`).

So the "Battle.net process" half of the route never fires: with only the launcher open (no game client), a WoW install in a nested prefix is not found. The WoW-client half works (observed for retail, Era, Anniversary and 3.3.5a). README's Known limitations now says so (added by omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.1).

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Put a Battle.net WoW install in a nested prefix no launcher names (for example `~/Games/umu/umu-default`), Battle.net running under umu/GE-Proton, no game client open.
2. `omaddons targets --json`: the nested install is not listed.
3. Fake-/proc form: a process with `comm` `CrBrowserMain`, `cmdline` `C:\Program Files (x86)\Battle.net\Battle.net.exe --from-launcher` (plus Wine's trailing empty arguments) and `WINEPREFIX=<nested>/pfx/` yields no prefix from `running_prefixes`.

## Technical Approach

Choose one, and record the decision (`decided:`) in this bead:
1. **Match `Agent.exe`** (comm, case-insensitive) and confirm through `cmdline` that argv[0] lies under `ProgramData/Battle.net/Agent/`. `Agent.exe` is a generic name, but the confirmation keeps false positives out, and environ is still read only after the match.
2. **Match `CrBrowserMain`** and confirm argv[0]'s basename is `Battle.net.exe`. This reads the `cmdline` of every Chromium/Electron browser process the user runs (not environ), which widens what the detector reads. Weigh it against the module's "read only for a match" rule.
3. **Reword README** to promise only WoW client processes, and drop `Battle.net.exe` from the names.

Prefer 1: it is specific to Blizzard's agent and keeps the read surface small. Running detection (`detect`) is unaffected: it matches target exe names only.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Either the launcher-only case finds the nested prefix (options 1/2) with a fake-/proc test built from the recorded shapes, or README and the names list no longer promise it (option 3).
- `environ` is still read only for matched processes (`environ_and_cmdline_only_for_matches` stays green, extended if the matcher changes).
- README's discovery route list and Known limitations agree with the code.

## Test Plan

- `tests/running.rs`: launcher-only fake /proc (`CrBrowserMain`, `Agent.exe`, `umu.exe`, `wineserver`) → `running_prefixes` returns the canonical prefix (options 1/2), or nothing (option 3).
- `tests/discover_scan.rs`: the nested-prefix process-route test gains a launcher-only step.
- Unit: the recorded-reader test asserts no environ read for unmatched Chromium processes.

## Considerations

- The `WINEPREFIX` is `<prefix>/pfx/` under umu; `running_prefixes` canonicalizes it since omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.1.
- `Agent.exe`'s directory carries a build number (`Agent.9824`); do not hard-code it.
- Chromium thread names are not specific to Battle.net: native Chrome, Electron apps and Steam's web helper use them too.
acceptance_criteria: the launcher-only case finds a nested prefix with a fake-/proc test built from the recorded shapes, or README and the matched names stop promising it; environ is still read only for matched processes; README route list and Known limitations agree with the code
close_reason: Option 1: the process route recognizes the Battle.net app by its agent, Agent.exe counted only when argv[0] lies under ProgramData/Battle.net/Agent/, checked before environ is read; names in one constant PROCESS_ROUTE_EXES; README route list, route 8 and Known limitations updated (the agent's WINEPREFIX marked not yet observed; omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.2 asks the next session to observe it).

Why not 2: CrBrowserMain would read the cmdline of every Chromium and Electron process the user runs. Why not 3: the route would lose the launcher-only case README promised. title: Catalog proposals A: TellMeWhen, Threat Plates, SilverDragon, Capping, IceHUD, Quartz, Mapster, BadBoy, NPCScan, ClassicCastbars
description:
## Background

The keyless-coverage study (omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.7, report in its comments, 2026-10-20) dry-ran the most popular addons on one synthetic client per live family. The addons below have a keyless source that installs on at least one family. None is in the 21-entry catalog, so `omaddons install <name>` misses them (`not_found`). This bead proposes them as catalog entries: batch A, ten GitHub publishers from the WoWInterface top 100.

| Name | Ref | Installed in the study's dry run on | Release seen | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TellMeWhen | `gh:ascott18/TellMeWhen` | tbc, mists, vanilla, forever, mainline | 12.1.5 | WoWI #83 |
| Threat Plates | `gh:Backupiseasy/ThreatPlates` | tbc, mists, vanilla, forever, mainline | 13.3.1 | WoWI #86 |
| SilverDragon | `gh:kemayo/wow-silverdragon` | tbc, mists, vanilla, forever, mainline | v2026.40 | WoWI #90 |
| Capping | `gh:BigWigsMods/Capping` | tbc, mists, vanilla, forever, mainline, titan | v12.1.6 | WoWI #64; its TOC links this repository |
| IceHUD | `gh:parnic/ice-hud` | tbc, mists, vanilla, mainline, titan | v1.17.26 | WoWI #62 |
| Quartz | `gh:Nevcairiel/Quartz` | tbc, mists, vanilla (out of date: mainline) | 3.7.17 | WoWI #33 |
| Mapster | `gh:Nevcairiel/Mapster` | forever, mainline | 1.14.0 | WoWI #69 |
| BadBoy | `gh:funkydude/BadBoy` | tbc, mists, vanilla, mainline, titan | v12.0.3 | WoWI #100 |
| NPCScan | `gh:Torhal/NPCScan` | mainline | 12.1.0.2 | WoWI #26 |
| ClassicCastbars | `gh:wardz/ClassicCastbars` | tbc, mists, vanilla | v1.9.1 | WoWI #45 |

## Technical Approach

For each entry, verify it as README "The built-in catalog" requires, on the day of the change. Do not reuse the study's results.

1. The publisher's `releases/latest` tag. The repository must be the publisher's own, not a fork or mirror. Check the owner against the addon's author on its WoWInterface or CurseForge page, or against the TOC's `## Author`.
2. Its `release.json`: the flavors it declares become `families`. When there is no `release.json` (zip assets only), take `families` from the TOCs' interfaces, and say so in `notes`.
3. The addon roots inside the release zip become `folders`.
4. Check names and aliases against existing entries. An entry is never matched across generations, but names must stay unique.

Then add the entry to `catalog/catalog.toml` under its section. Record its fixtures with `OMADDONS_RECORD=1 cargo test --test catalog -- --ignored record`. Update README "The built-in catalog": the entry count, the verification date, and the table.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each entry above is verified on the day by the steps above, and is either added or dropped with the reason recorded in a comment here.
- `tests/catalog.rs` covers every added entry with recorded fixtures.
- The live catalog × declared-flavor probe (`live_probes::catalog_matches_declared_flavors`, omad-classic-forever-gaps-xud.7) passes with the new entries at the next checkpoint. A publisher whose TOCs disagree with its declaration gets a dated row in `KNOWN_PUBLISHER_MISMATCHES`, and a README sentence.
- README "The built-in catalog" matches `catalog/catalog.toml`: count, date and table.

## Test Plan

- `OMADDONS_RECORD=1 cargo test --test catalog -- --ignored record`, then `cargo test --test catalog`.
- The live probe at the next checkpoint.
- `argc gate`.

## Considerations

- The study's dry runs are evidence that a source works, not the verification itself. Releases move.
- Propose aliases only for names players actually type (the study's names are the listing's display names).
- Drop an entry whose source turns out to be a fork, a mirror, or a release for one dead flavor only.
acceptance_criteria: every entry is verified on the day by README 'The built-in catalog' rules and added or dropped with a recorded reason; tests/catalog.rs covers each added entry with recorded fixtures; the live catalog x declared-flavor probe passes at the next checkpoint; README's catalog count, date and table match catalog.toml
close_reason: Added 10 catalog entries verified 2026-10-20: TellMeWhen (tmw), ThreatPlates, SilverDragon, Capping, IceHUD, Quartz, Mapster, BadBoy, NPCScan, ClassicCastbars. Each was checked against its releases/latest tag, release.json flavors (→ families) and the release zip's addon roots (→ folders), with publisher identity from the zip TOCs' Author/X-WoWI-ID. README's catalog count, date and table are updated.
