Undefer only when the owner asks an agent to work this bead with them.

title: Raising limits.download_max_bytes above 512 MiB has no effect: the blob cache keeps the compiled-in cap
description:
## Background

`limits.download_max_bytes` in `config.toml` is documented as the largest download (default 512 MiB, `src/limits.rs`). The network layer honors the configured value (`src/app/engine.rs` passes it to `Guarded::new`, `src/net/mod.rs`). But every asset download is also streamed through `BlobCache::store_stream` (`src/engine/blobs.rs`, called from `src/engine/plan.rs` around line 1134), whose cap is fixed at construction: `BlobCache::new` sets `max_download: DOWNLOAD_MAX_BYTES`, and `with_max_download` is only called from tests.

So lowering the limit works (the guard trips first), but raising it above 512 MiB has no effect: the blob cache refuses the download with `archive_too_large`, and its fix tells the user to raise the very key they already raised.

Found while auditing the engine for the README rewrite.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `omaddons config set limits.download_max_bytes 1GiB`
2. Install a release whose asset is larger than 512 MiB (in tests: a replayed or local stream of 600 MiB of zeros through the URL path).
3. Result: `archive_too_large` from the blob cache, although the configured limit is 1 GiB.

## Technical Approach

- Construct the production `BlobCache` with the effective limit: `BlobCache::new(paths).with_max_download(limits.download_max_bytes)` where the engine context is built (`src/app/engine.rs`), or pass `EffectiveLimits` into `BlobCache::new`.
- Rename or re-document `with_max_download` ("tests; production uses DOWNLOAD_MAX_BYTES") accordingly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- With `limits.download_max_bytes` raised, a download between 512 MiB and the new limit is stored; past the new limit it fails with `archive_too_large`.
- With the limit lowered, behavior is unchanged.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit (`src/engine/blobs.rs`): a cache built from an `EffectiveLimits` with a raised cap accepts a stream past the default and refuses one past the raised cap (use small numbers: default overridden to 1,000 and raised to 2,000 bytes).
- Integration: the engine wiring uses the configured value (assert on the constructed cache's cap, or a replayed oversized asset).

## Considerations

- The local-file path (`file:` zips) does not go through the network guard; check whether it hits the blob cache cap too and make both agree.
- README.md lists this under Known issues and in the config example; update both when fixed.
acceptance_criteria: a raised download_max_bytes admits downloads between 512 MiB and the new cap and refuses past it; a lowered one behaves as today; argc gate passes
close_reason: limits.download_max_bytes is honoured when raised: the blob cache takes the configured cap

comments.author: CrimsonJasper
comments.text: done: ArchiveLimits gains max_download (default DOWNLOAD_MAX_BYTES, from EffectiveLimits.download_max_bytes), which EngineCtx already carries from config; both BlobCache constructions in engine::tx use with_max_download(ctx.limits.max_download), so raising the key past 512 MiB lets such a download store and lowering it behaves as before (the guard trips first). with_max_download's doc no longer says tests only. Unit test blobs::a_raised_download_cap_from_config_is_honoured (cap 2,000 from EffectiveLimits: 1,500 stored, 2,001 archive_too_large); oversized_downloads_leave_nothing unchanged. README Known issues line removed. The retention eviction's BlobCache::new needs no download cap (it never downloads).

title: readers_report_without_writing races a sibling test's forked child holding the lock
description:
## Background

`tests/journal.rs::readers_report_without_writing` checks that a reader (`journal::pending_warnings`) reports an interrupted journal as `journal_pending` while nobody holds the global lock, and as `tx_in_progress` while another process holds it. The test binary runs its tests on parallel threads, and several of its tests fork child processes. A `fork` copies every open file descriptor of the process, the test's global-lock descriptor included, and flock locks belong to the open file description, so a child forked while this test holds (or briefly re-takes) its lock keeps that lock held until its `exec` closes the descriptor. The test already waits that window out once (`drop(GlobalLock::acquire(..))` before reading), but its own acquire can be inherited the same way, so the read right after it can see the lock held and get `tx_in_progress`. It failed this way once in an `argc gate` run (left: TxInProgress, right: JournalPending) while the machine was loaded, and passed three times in isolation.

Found while running the gate for omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.8.1 (prune's gc locations), which does not touch the journal reader or this test binary.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `argc gate` (or `cargo test --test journal`) on a loaded machine.
2. Occasionally `readers_report_without_writing` fails at its first `assert_eq!(free[0].code, WarningCode::JournalPending)` with `TxInProgress`.

## Technical Approach

Test-only: read the free-lock state in a bounded retry. Each attempt takes and drops the lock (waiting out any inherited copy), reads `pending_warnings`, and checks that the read wrote nothing; it stops at the first `journal_pending` answer, and fails after 2 seconds of `tx_in_progress` answers. The held-lock half of the test is unchanged. No product code changes: a reader that sees an inherited lock as held is right to say `tx_in_progress`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `readers_report_without_writing` retries its free-lock read, bounded (2 s), asserting every attempt writes nothing, and asserts `journal_pending` exactly as before.
- The held-lock assertions are unchanged.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit/integration: the test itself, run repeatedly (`cargo test --test journal readers_report_without_writing` in a loop) and in the full gate.

## Considerations

- The bound must not hide a real regression: a reader that always says `tx_in_progress` with the lock free still fails after 2 seconds.
- Other tests that read lock state right after forking siblings may share the race; none has failed so far.
acceptance_criteria:
- readers_report_without_writing retries its free-lock read, bounded (2 s), asserting every attempt writes nothing, and asserts journal_pending exactly as before.
- The held-lock assertions are unchanged.
- argc gate passes.
close_reason: readers_report_without_writing retries its free-lock read, bounded, each read checked to write nothing.

comments.author: FrostyJasper
comments.text: claim: tests/journal.rs readers_report_without_writing (test-only retry)

comments.author: FrostyJasper
comments.text: done: argc gate passed; cargo test --test journal 3/3 green after the fix. The free read now retries up to 2 s: take and drop the lock, hash the state, read, assert nothing was written, stop at the first answer that is not tx_in_progress; the held-lock half is unchanged, and a reader that always says held still fails after the bound.

title: recover_under drops the journal_recovered warnings and the doorbell ring of journals it settled before an unattributed one
description:
## Background

`journal::recover_under` (`src/engine/journal.rs`) runs recovery for commands that take the global lock without committing a target (`config set`, `targets …`, `auth github set`, `export --write`, `errors dismiss`, a change command with nothing to commit through `recover_waiting`). It calls `recover_all(&env).unwrap_or_else(left)`, where `left` turns any error into one `journal_pending` warning ("unfinished transactions could not be recovered: …").

`recover_all` walks the folder journals in transaction order and returns early with `Err(unattributed(..))` when it meets a journal no target owns (`journal.rs`, the `(None, _) if owner_unknown` arm). The `journal_recovered` warnings it collected for the journals it already rolled back or forward are local to `recover_all` and are dropped with that early return. `recover_under` then sees no `journal_recovered` warning, so:

1. the command's envelope does not say that those journals were recovered (their journals are gone, so nothing will say it later);
2. the doorbell is not rung, although recovery changed what `status --cached` reports, so the bar widget does not refresh until something else rings it.

Found while doing omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14.2 (which made a stuck repair journal a warning instead of an error, so repairs no longer reach this path; folder journals with no readable target still do).

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In a synthetic home with one client, crash an install after `prepared` so its folder journal is recoverable (any engine failpoint before `swapped`), giving transaction A.
2. Plant a second folder journal B with a greater transaction id whose first line does not name a target (for example `{"line":"prepared"}`), its in-flight lock free.
3. Run `omaddons config set check_interval_hours 6 --json`.
4. Observe: A's journal is gone (rolled back), but `warnings` holds only the `journal_pending` "unfinished transactions could not be recovered" text and no `journal_recovered` for A; `<cache>/doorbell.json` was not rewritten.

## Technical Approach

- Keep the warnings recovery produced before the failure. Either `recover_all` returns them beside the error (for example a `Recovery { warnings, error: Option<Error> }`, or an error that carries them in a field), or `recover_under` gets them through a variant of `recover_all` that keeps them.
- `recover_under` reports those warnings followed by the `left` warning, and rings the doorbell when any of them is `journal_recovered`.
- Committing callers keep failing exactly as today (their `?` on `recover_all` is unchanged in behaviour); only what is reported changes, and a committing caller may append the kept warnings to its notes before failing if that is simple (decide, and record why).
- No new error code, warning code or wire key.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] With a recoverable journal followed by an unattributed one, `recover_under` returns A's `journal_recovered` warning and then the `journal_pending` warning, and rings the doorbell once.
- [ ] With only an unattributed journal, its result is unchanged (one `journal_pending` warning, no doorbell).
- [ ] Committing commands still fail with the same error code, `details` and exit as before.
- [ ] E11's differential (`tests/common/differential.rs`) and every crash matrix pass unchanged, or the differential is updated to read the kept warnings, with the reason in the close comment.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit (`src/engine/journal.rs`): the two-journal case above in process, asserting the warnings in order and the doorbell file's write; the single-unattributed case unchanged.
- Integration: the same scene through the binary (`config set`), asserting the envelope's warnings, with `TestLog`.

## Considerations

- The early return is deliberate (a journal no target owns fails every committing command, and later journals must not be recovered past it); keep that order, change only what is reported.
- The doorbell is a signal, never state: ringing it once more is harmless, missing a ring leaves the widget stale.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] With a recoverable journal followed by an unattributed one, recover_under returns the first journal's journal_recovered warning, then the journal_pending warning, and rings the doorbell once.
- [ ] With only an unattributed journal, the result is unchanged.
- [ ] Committing commands still fail with the same error code, details and exit.
- [ ] E11's differential and every crash matrix pass (or the differential reads the kept warnings, with the reason in the close comment).
- [ ] argc gate passes.

title: Failpoint aborts dump core: thousands of core dumps and desktop crash notifications per gate run
description:
## Background

The `abort` failpoint action (`src/fsx/failpoint.rs`, debug builds only) simulates a crash with `std::process::abort()`. On a desktop with systemd-coredump, each one is a real core dump. The crash matrices abort thousands of times per gate run, so on the development machine `coredumpctl` listed 28,238 dumps in 12 hours: a `systemd-coredump` run for each, about half storing a ~156 KB core, and Omarchy's "Process crashed: … Click to diagnose" notification stacking on the desktop for `omaddons` and the test binaries (`fsx_prune-…`). Found by the M3 checkpoint (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.7.3`) on the live desktop.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `coredumpctl list --since -1h | wc -l`.
2. `cargo test --test engine_crash` (or `argc gate`).
3. The same count grows by thousands, and the desktop shows "Process crashed" notifications.

## Technical Approach

- Before the simulated crash, mark the process not dumpable (`rustix::process::set_dumpable_behavior(NotDumpable)`, `prctl(PR_SET_DUMPABLE, 0)`): the kernel then writes no core and starts no coredump handler. The abort itself is unchanged (`SIGABRT`, exit by signal), so every crash scene's oracle holds.
- Only the failpoint's abort changes; a real crash still dumps core.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A failpoint abort leaves no core dump and no coredump journal entry.
- Every crash matrix passes unchanged.

## Test Plan

- A unit or integration test that runs a child with an `abort` failpoint and checks it died by `SIGABRT`; `/proc/<pid>/` dumpability cannot be observed after death, so the check is `coredumpctl` on the development machine, recorded in the close comment (count before and after a gate run).
- `argc gate`.

## Considerations

- `PR_SET_DUMPABLE` 0 also makes `/proc/self` root-owned; the process dies on the next line, so nothing reads it.
acceptance_criteria: A failpoint abort leaves no core dump and no coredump journal entry; every crash matrix passes unchanged.
close_reason: a failpoint abort marks the process not dumpable first: no core dump, no coredump handler, no desktop notification; the abort itself is unchanged

comments.author: FierceWren
comments.text: claim: src/fsx/failpoint.rs abort action

comments.author: FierceWren
comments.text: done: argc gate passed; engine_crash 72 passed with 0 new core dumps (coredumpctl last hour 1814 before and after, and after a full gate run); the suite ran in 13.7 s against 37 s with dumps · found: none

title: Human output says 1 folders, and file: refs keep a ./ component
description:
## Background

Two small blemishes in human output that the README now shows verbatim:

1. **Plurals.** `install` and `undo` print `(1 folders)` and `restored 1 folders` (`src/app/install.rs` around line 249, and the undo renderer in `src/app/undo.rs`). `remove` already prints `(1 folder)`. Unit tests in `src/app/install.rs` pin the wrong text.
2. **`file:` refs keep `./`.** A local install records and prints `file:/abs/path/./HelloWorld` instead of `file:/abs/path/HelloWorld`: the relative request is joined to the cwd without normalizing the `.` component (`src/sources/refs.rs`, the `file:` and path branches).

Found while capturing real output for the README rewrite.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `omaddons install ./HelloWorld -t retail` → `retail: installed HelloWorld 1.0.0 (1 folders)`.
2. `omaddons list -t retail` → ref `file:/…/./HelloWorld`.
3. `omaddons undo` → `restored 1 folders, removed 0`.

## Technical Approach

- One small plural helper in `src/output/human.rs` (or wherever remove's singular lives), used by install, undo and remove.
- Normalize `.` components (lexically, without resolving symlinks) when the path ref becomes a canonical `file:` ref. Existing records keep their stored ref; only new refs change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `1 folder` / `2 folders` in install, undo and remove human output.
- New `file:` refs contain no `/./` component; existing records still match their folders.
- `argc gate` passes with the pinned texts updated.

## Test Plan

- Unit: the renderers with 1 and 2 folders.
- Unit (`refs.rs`): `./x`, `././x` and `a/./b` normalize; `../x` keeps working.
- Re-run the README's session example and update its output.

## Considerations

- Changing the canonical form of new `file:` refs means a re-install of the same path written the old way must still resolve to the existing record. Compare normalized forms when matching.
acceptance_criteria: 1 folder and 2 folders in install, undo and remove output; new file: refs carry no /./ component and existing records still match; argc gate passes
close_reason: 1 folder / 2 folders everywhere, and new file: refs carry no . component

comments.author: CrimsonJasper
comments.text: done: output::count(n, noun) (1 folder / 2 folders) used by install, undo and remove human output; refs::absolute collects path components, so ./Bar.zip and a/./b become <cwd>/Bar.zip and a/b (.. kept: lexical resolution is wrong past a symlink); Ref::identity compares a file: path without . components, so a record written file:/x/./Bar is still the same addon as file:/x/Bar (stored spelling kept). Tests: refs unit cases (./, ././, a/./b, .. kept), model a_recorded_file_ref_with_a_dot_component_is_the_same_addon, install renderer texts, deps.rs text and three deps human snapshots (1 folders → 1 folder, reviewed). README session output, the dependency example and Known issues updated.

title: Widget: backup times shown in UTC beside a local clock
description:
## Background

The widget's restore confirmation says "Restore … from the backup of 2026-10-23 05:31" with the backup's capture time in UTC, sliced from the ISO string (`dateText` in `omarchy/Model.js`), while the bar's clock and every "N min ago" are local. 2. In the panel's Backups view, Enter on that backup, choose one addon's settings and an addon.
3. The confirmation's "from the backup of …" shows the UTC hour.

## Technical Approach

- `dateText` formats the instant in the local time zone ("YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM"), as the bar's clock shows it; a text that does not parse is shown as it is.

## Acceptance Criteria

## Considerations

- QML's JavaScript `Date` uses the session's zone, the same as the bar's clock.

title: Errors probe in `status --cached` re-lists the same parent folders once per account
description:
## Background

`status --cached` must stay under 5 ms at the median (release, median of 21; `tests/perf.rs::status_cached_stays_under_5_ms_with_a_realistic_memo`). The errors block that `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.7` added re-runs `errors::locate::locate_in` on every call. That walk lstats the BugGrabber files the memo recorded and lists each account's `SavedVariables/` to compare listing fingerprints (`src/app/errors_status.rs`, `cached`).

Measured while closing 2.7 (release build, the perf test's heavy home: 16 accounts, each with a 2 MB `!BugGrabber.lua` and 40 other SavedVariables files, plus a memo and a dismissal), using an A/B run with the probe stubbed out:

- with the probe: median 4.04 ms and 4.57 ms with the 20 MB history (p95 4.73 ms);
- without it: median 3.78 ms and 4.17 ms (p95 4.38 ms).

So the probe costs about 0.3–0.4 ms of a 5 ms budget, and with the 20 MB history about 0.4 ms of headroom is left. D11 (backups in `status`) and E4 (the widget's fields) still have to add their own blocks to `status --cached`.

Most of that cost is redundant syscalls. For every account, `locate_in` calls `engine::swap::sv_skip(client, sv)`, which:

- runs `spelled_twice`. That re-reads the client dir, `WTF/`, `Account/` and the account dir (four `read_dir`s) to look for case-variant siblings, although `locate_in` has just listed exactly those directories through `find_children` and `dirs`;
- canonicalizes the client dir. That is about ten lstats, repeated per account for the same answer.

With 16 accounts that comes to roughly 64 redundant `read_dir`s and about 160 redundant lstats per call.

## Technical Approach

Keep one rule. `locate`'s skip decision must stay exactly undo's (`sv_skip`), because the listing fingerprints `errors` records and the ones `status --cached` recomputes must come from the same walk. Do not fork the logic into `locate`.

- In `src/engine/swap.rs`, split `sv_skip` into the decision and its inputs: a `SvScope` (or similar) built once per client holds the canonical client dir, and `sv_skip_in(&SvScope, sv)` uses it. `sv_skip(client, sv)` becomes `sv_skip_in(&SvScope::of(client), sv)` for its existing callers, so undo is unchanged.
- In `locate_in`, build the scope once. Answer the case-variant question for the WTF, Account, account and SavedVariables components from the listings `locate_in` already holds: a component is spelled twice when its parent's `find_children` returned more than one match, or when the account names contain two that are equal ignoring case. Then call into the shared decision instead of re-listing.
- Measure before and after with the same A/B as above, and record the numbers in the close comment.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `locate_in` lists each directory at most once per call, and canonicalizes the client dir once per call.
- Its results are unchanged: `src/errors/locate.rs`'s unit tests (symlinked and two-spelled folders skipped and counted, bounds, fingerprints) and `src/engine` undo tests pass without edits, and a new unit test shows `sv_skip` and the hoisted path agree on symlinked, two-spelled and plain folders.
- `tests/perf.rs::status_cached_stays_under_5_ms_with_a_realistic_memo` (release) shows the errors probe's share reduced, with the before/after medians recorded in the close comment.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit (`src/engine/swap.rs`): `sv_skip` and `sv_skip_in` agree on a plain folder, a folder reached through a symlink leading outside the client, and a folder whose ancestor is spelled two ways.
- Unit (`src/errors/locate.rs`): the existing tests, unchanged.
- E2E: `tests/status_errors.rs` and `tests/errors.rs`, unchanged.
- Perf: the release perf test, medians and p95 quoted.

## Considerations

- Undo's rule is a safety boundary (it decides which SavedVariables undo may write). Any refactor must leave undo's behaviour byte-for-byte the same, so keep `sv_skip`'s signature for its callers.
- Do not cache across calls or in a file: `status` writes nothing (M3-D20), and the probe must see the disk as it is now.
- If the measured gain is under about 0.1 ms, close this as not worth the risk, with the numbers.
acceptance_criteria: locate_in lists each directory at most once and canonicalizes the client dir once per call; its results are unchanged (locate unit tests and undo tests pass without edits, plus a unit test that sv_skip and the hoisted path agree on symlinked, two-spelled and plain folders); the release perf test status_cached_stays_under_5_ms_with_a_realistic_memo shows the errors probe's share reduced, before/after medians in the close comment; argc gate passes
close_reason: not worth the risk: removing sv_skip from the errors probe entirely (the upper bound of any hoisting) saves 0.07-0.10 ms, under the bead's 0.1 ms threshold, and the refactor would touch undo's safety boundary

comments.author: FierceWren
comments.text: claim: src/engine/swap.rs sv_skip, src/errors/locate.rs locate_in, perf measurement

comments.author: FierceWren
comments.text: measured, release, perf heavy home with 200 backups, --test-threads=1, two runs each: baseline status --cached median 4.29/4.28 ms (p95 4.48/4.61), 20 MB history 4.65/4.70 ms (p95 4.93/5.00); with sv_skip stubbed to None (upper bound: a hoisted sv_skip_in still canonicalizes each SavedVariables dir) 4.18/4.19 ms (p95 4.40/4.32), 20 MB history 4.58/4.62 ms (p95 4.75/4.91). Gain <= 0.10 ms and <= 0.07 ms with the large history, so per the bead's own rule this closes without code changes; undo's sv_skip stays untouched. The stub was reverted (no diff). G3's perf run remains the binding measurement for criterion 10 · found: none

title: Expired plan pruning must check leases omitted from the victim list
description:
## Background
The plan-store sweep lists plans and leases before pruning. An applier can create and hold a lease after that listing. fsx currently checks only lease paths explicitly passed as victims, so it can delete a plan whose late lease is held.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Plant an expired plan and list it without a lease.
2. Acquire its lease.
3. Prune only the plan under LockUse::Expired.
4. The plan is removed while its lease is held.

## Technical Approach
Have fsx check and hold the lease for every expired plan as well as explicitly supplied orphan leases. Deduplicate lease paths and acquire each once. A missing lease is created through the existing fsx Lease API and left for the bounded orphan sweep if it was not a victim.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A held lease protects its plan even when omitted from the victim list.
- An initially missing lease is acquired before pruning.
- Existing expired-plan and orphan-lease cases still pass; no global lock is needed.
- argc gate and UBS pass.

## Test Plan
Extend the fsx expired-plan table with a held lease absent from victims, and test a lease created after a store listing. Check the new absent-lease guard and existing refusal cases.

## Considerations
Lease files created while guarding deletion can remain as orphans, which the existing bounded sweep removes. This closes a deletion precondition gap without changing file formats, wire names, or crash recovery.
acceptance_criteria: Held omitted leases prevent deletion; absent leases are guarded; late-lease store regression and existing pruning tests pass; argc gate and UBS pass.
close_reason: Expired plan deletion now guards every corresponding lease, including leases omitted from a prior listing.

Unit regressions cover omitted held leases and newly created guards; subprocess tests cover guarding through deletion, abort and I/O failure before rename and at both prune boundaries, followed by repeated cleanup. New guard-only lease files can remain as orphans until the next bounded sweep; no persisted format or wire name changes.

title: Memo verdict facts outlive the judge that made them: a rules change leaves outdated and info reporting old verdicts
description:
## Background

The release memo (`src/state/memo.rs`) remembers what downloading a candidate taught: a `VerdictFact {rules, interface, loads, out_of_date, primary_interface, at}` per client-rules row and client interface. `outdated`, `update`'s statuses (`src/resolve/updates.rs`, `evaluate`) and `info`'s load hints (`src/app/info.rs`) believe such a fact without downloading again.

A fact is keyed by the row's name and the client's interface, not by the rules that judged it. When a build changes how a TOC is judged, facts an older build recorded keep their old answer. omad-retail-12-floor-e5a0 is the first such change: retail 12.0 and later now refuse a Mainline TOC below 120000. A fact recorded before it says such an asset `loads: true, out_of_date: true` on (`mainline`, 120105). Until something downloads that asset again, `outdated` shows it as an update with `confidence: verified`, and `info` lists retail among the clients it loads on. Installs and updates always verify again, so nothing wrong is ever installed: the plan refuses it and records a new fact. Only the reports are wrong, until then.

A `[client_rules]` override that changes how a row judges has the same effect today. The discovery cache already guards against this: it records the rules and the omaddons version it was built with, and re-parses every root when either changes.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. With a build before omad-retail-12-floor-e5a0, a retail 12.1.5 client has `gh:o/foo` v1 (interface 120105) installed, and v2 ships only `## Interface: 110207`.
2. `omaddons outdated --verify -t retail` records v2 as loading, out of date.
3. Switch to the current build and run `omaddons outdated -t retail`: v2 shows as `update_available` with `confidence: verified`.
4. `omaddons update -t retail` refuses it (`blocked`), and only then does `outdated` agree.

## Technical Approach

- Give every `VerdictFact` the judge it was made under: a digest of what judging reads (the row as applied, the family ranges, and a `JUDGE_VERSION` constant next to `judge` in `src/toc/loaded.rs` that is bumped whenever the verdict rules change), or the omaddons version together with a digest of the rules table, as the discovery cache does.
- `FactIndex::verdict` ignores a fact from another judge. The fact stays in the memo until a new verdict replaces it (merge as today).
- Facts with no judge recorded (written before this change) count as another judge's.
- The memo's `schema_version` gets a minor bump; older facts still decode (`#[serde(default)]`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A fact recorded under another judge digest (or none) is not believed: `outdated` treats that candidate as unverified, and `info` does not count it as verified.
- A fact recorded under the current judge is believed as today, so a warm `outdated` still makes no download (the bench's warm runs add no `net.log` line).
- A `[client_rules]` override that changes how a row judges also invalidates the facts made under the old rules.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit (`src/state/memo.rs`): a fact with another digest, or none, is absent from `verdict`; a fact with the current digest is returned.
- Integration (`tests/outdated.rs`): seed the memo with an old-judge fact saying a 110207 asset loads on retail 12.1.5; `outdated` does not report it as a verified update, and `outdated --verify` records the refusal.
- The request-economy checks in `tests/perf.rs` still pass.

## Considerations

- Do not key facts on the full omaddons version alone: every release would then download every candidate again on its first `outdated`. A digest of what judging reads changes only when verdicts can change.
- Facts also carry `primary_interface`, which M2-D42's floor reads. It comes from the same judge and must follow the same rule.
acceptance_criteria: A VerdictFact made under another judge digest (or none) is not believed by outdated, update statuses or info; one made under the current judge is, so warm outdated still downloads nothing; a client_rules override that changes judging invalidates old facts; argc gate passes
close_reason: VerdictFact records the judge digest (JUDGE_VERSION, the applied rules row, every family range); FactIndex::verdict believes a fact only under the target's current digest; facts without one are another judge's; memo schema 1.1

comments.author: CobaltOak
comments.text: done: argc gate passes; unit tests memo::a_verdict_from_another_judge_is_not_believed (none, other, current; a client_rules floor patch changes the digest, a products patch does not) and outdated::a_verdict_from_another_judge_is_not_believed (old-judge 'loads' fact on a below-floor v2 is not a verified update; --verify re-judges and records it blocked); removing the judge filter fails both; warm --verify still downloads nothing (outdated::verify_downloads_unverified_updates_only_and_remembers_the_verdicts, tests/perf.rs) · found: none

title: A fence's refusal was swallowed or re-coded by candidate selection, the SavedVariables snapshot, the backup copier and item errors
description:
## Background

omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14.2 made the one writer refuse a write that overlaps what a stuck repair protects, with the fencing journal's own stop (code, `details.reason`, `tx`, `resource`, fix `omaddons doctor explain …`). omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14.4's end-to-end scenarios found four callers that swallowed or re-coded that refusal before it reached the user:

1. **Candidate selection** (`src/engine/plan.rs`, the candidate loop): every download error is recorded in `tried[]` and the next candidate is tried, so a fenced blob write ended as `no_compatible_release` (exit 3). On `update` that is a `blocked` addon, whose verdict is remembered as "does not load".
2. **The SavedVariables snapshot** (`src/engine/swap.rs`, `private`): every error is re-wrapped as "a SavedVariables file could not be snapshotted", losing the fence's details (`remove` under a closed set).
3. **The backup copier** (`src/backup/tree.rs`, `fsx_error`): a fenced write became `io`, "copying WTF/ failed at …", with the fence's text only as its cause (`backup create`).
4. **Item errors** (`src/app/outcome.rs`, `item_details`): an engine command whose every item failed kept the first item's code, message and fix but none of the fence's details (`update` under a closed set).

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Plant a repair journal whose `prepared` line does not decode (`common::repairs::plant_undecodable_prepared`), its in-flight lock free.
2. Run `omaddons install gh:o/bar -t retail --json` against a recorded release: exit 3 `no_compatible_release`, `details.tried[0].reason` naming the fence. Run `remove`, `update` and `backup create`: their errors lack `details.tx` and `details.resource` (and `backup create` reports `io`).

## Technical Approach

- `ErrorData.fenced: Option<Fencing>` (`Path` or `Closed`, never serialized), set only by `FsxError::Fenced`'s conversion: a reliable mark that the error is a fence's refusal.
- The candidate loop returns a fenced error at once: no verdict on this candidate nor the next.
- `swap::private` passes a fenced error through whole (it names only what its journal protects, cut at `WTF/`).
- `CloneError::Fenced` carries the fence, and `CloneError::error` returns the fence's own error.
- `item_details` keeps a fence's `{journal_pending, reason, target, tx, resource}` (the one refusal whose details name a `resource`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Under a closed set, `install`, `install --dry-run`, `update`, `remove`, `config set`, `auth github set`, `targets rename` and `backup create` fail with the planted journal's code, `details.reason`, `details.tx` and `details.resource`.
- [ ] A fenced blob download fails `install` with the stuck repair's stop, not `no_compatible_release`.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- `tests/doctor_repair_fences.rs`: `fence_an_unreadable_prepared_fails_every_committing_command_closed` (both cases) and `fence_a_stuck_blob_quarantine_guards_that_blob_only`.
- Unit: `item_details_keep_a_fences_stop_and_nothing_more` (`src/app/outcome.rs`); `fenced_error_has_the_stops_code_details_and_fix` asserts the mark (`src/fsx/mutate.rs`).

## Considerations

- A path fence stays an item failure: it refuses one addon's write, and the client's other addons may still commit. Escalating a closed fence to a target-level plan failure was tried and rejected: `install`'s own result building then reported the item `unchanged` with exit 0.
- Fixed in the same commit as omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14.4, which found it.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] Under a closed set, install, install --dry-run, update, remove, config set, auth github set, targets rename and backup create fail with the planted journal's code, details.reason, details.tx and details.resource.
- [ ] A fenced blob download fails install with the stuck repair's stop, not no_compatible_release.
- [ ] argc gate passes.
close_reason: Fixed: a fence's refusal reaches the user as the fencing journal's stop through candidate selection, the SavedVariables snapshot, the backup copier and item errors

comments.author: WildFerret
comments.text: done: ErrorData.fenced (Option<Fencing>, set only by FsxError::Fenced's conversion); the candidate loop returns a fenced error at once; swap::private and the backup copier (CloneError::Fenced) pass it whole; item_details keeps a fence's stop. Proven by tests/doctor_repair_fences.rs (the closed-set scenario's eight commands, the blob scenario) and the unit tests item_details_keep_a_fences_stop_and_nothing_more and fenced_error_has_the_stops_code_details_and_fix; argc gate passes (4,032 passed). Rejected: escalating a closed fence to a target-level plan failure, which made install report the item unchanged with exit 0. found: none

title: A stored plan whose local path held .. is stale on every apply: the preview's token covers the path as typed
description:
## Background

A stored plan's intent holds every local path absolute and normalized (`AbsPath::resolve` in `src/app/intent.rs`: joined to the working directory, a remaining `..` resolved through the filesystem), so the plan names the same file wherever `apply` runs (M4-D23; D5's criterion "a plan stored in one working directory applies from another, and after that directory is deleted"). `apply` then runs the command with those absolute paths, bound to the preview's token.

The preview itself plans with the path as typed, not the normalized one:

- `install --file <zip>` plans with `cwd.join(file)` (`src/app/install.rs`, `run`), which keeps `..`, and the engine's input witness records that path as its `source` (`engine::witness::input_of`, "the path as given");
- a positional local ref (`install ../zips/foo.zip`) becomes `Ref::File` through `sources::refs::absolute`, which deliberately keeps `..`.

So whenever the typed path holds `..` (any path relative to a sibling directory), the preview's token covers `<cwd>/../zips/foo.zip` while `apply` plans `<root>/zips/foo.zip`: the observed part differs and every such plan is `plan_stale` (`observed`) on every apply. Found by `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5.6`'s scenario `apply_works_from_another_directory_after_the_preview_directory_is_gone`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On a home with a retail client, put `foo.zip` (a retail addon) in `<root>/zips/` and make `<root>/a`.
2. From `<root>/a`: `omaddons install gh:o/foo --file ../zips/foo.zip -t retail --dry-run --json`; note `data.plan_id`. The plan's `intent.file` is `<root>/zips/foo.zip`.
3. `omaddons apply <plan_id> --json` (from any directory): exit 1, `plan_stale`, "this install is no longer what its preview showed (observed changed)", although nothing changed.
4. The same with a positional ref (`omaddons install ../zips/foo.zip -t retail --dry-run`) is refused the same way.

## Technical Approach

- One normalization: `sources::refs::absolute(cwd, path)` joins `path` to `cwd`, drops `.` components and, when a `..` remains, resolves it through the filesystem (`canonicalize`), keeping the joined path when that fails (a missing file then fails later with its usual error, naming the path as typed). Resolving through the filesystem is right past a symlink, which is why the lexical resolution was avoided.
- `install --file` plans with `refs::absolute(cwd, file)` instead of `cwd.join(file)`, so the witness, the records and the stored intent hold the same path.
- `AbsPath::resolve` builds on `refs::absolute` and then checks the result, so the stored form is by construction the planned one.
- No wire change: a typed path without `..` normalizes exactly as before (`./Foo.zip` is `<cwd>/Foo.zip`); a path with `..` is now recorded resolved (`file:<root>/zips/foo.zip`, not `file:<root>/a/../zips/foo.zip`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A plan previewed from a directory with `--file ../zips/foo.zip`, and one with the positional ref `../zips/foo.zip`, each applies (`committed`) from another directory after the preview's directory was deleted.
- The token of such a preview equals the token of the same preview typed with the absolute path.
- `install ../missing/../x.zip` (a path that does not exist) still fails as it did, naming the path.
- `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files.

## Test Plan

- Unit (`src/sources/refs.rs`): `absolute` keeps a path without `..` lexical (`./Bar.zip`, an absolute path), resolves `..` through an existing directory, and keeps the joined path when the target is missing.
- Unit (`src/app/intent.rs`): the existing `AbsPath::resolve` table still passes (absolute input, `..` through an existing directory, a missing `..` path refused).
- E2E (`tests/apply.rs`, 4.5.6's scenario): the two cases above, through `TestLog`.

## Considerations

- `refs::absolute` is also how `sync` resolves an entry relative to its file, and how `adopt --ref` and `copy` read local refs: their `..` paths are now recorded resolved too, which is the same file.
- Canonicalizing resolves symlinks in the whole path, not only at the `..`; that form is what the plan stores already, so preview and apply agree.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A plan previewed with --file ../zips/foo.zip, and one with the positional ref ../zips/foo.zip, each applies (committed) from another directory after the preview's directory was deleted.
- [ ] The token of such a preview equals the token of the same preview typed with the absolute path.
- [ ] install of a missing path with .. still fails as it did, naming the path.
- [ ] argc gate passes; ubs is clean on the changed files.
close_reason: done: refs::absolute resolves a remaining .. through the filesystem and is the one normalization install --file, local refs and AbsPath::resolve share; a relative plan applies from anywhere; argc gate passed

comments.text: claim: src/sources/refs.rs (absolute resolves .. through the filesystem), src/app/install.rs (--file planned with it), src/app/intent.rs (AbsPath::resolve built on it); found mid omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5.6, which stays claimed

comments.author: ElectricKoala
comments.text: done: argc gate passed (3,417 tests, widget pipeline, ubs critical 0). src/sources/refs.rs: absolute(cwd, path) joins and drops '.', and when a '..' remains canonicalizes the directory holding the last component (a symlinked input stays itself), keeping the joined path when that fails; it is now pub(crate). src/app/install.rs plans --file with it (was cwd.join(file)); src/app/intent.rs AbsPath::resolve builds on it, so the stored form is the planned one by construction. Tests: unit a_local_path_is_absolute_and_its_dot_dot_resolved (dot, plain, absolute, dot dot, dot dot with a symlink kept, a missing directory kept as joined, dot dot last); local_paths_and_collisions updated, since its pinned rule ('..' kept lexically) is the one this bead changes; e2e tests/apply.rs applying::apply_works_from_another_directory_after_the_preview_directory_is_gone (lands with omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5.6's next commit): --file ../zips/foo.zip and the positional ref ../zips/foo.zip each store the absolute path, give the same token as the absolute spelling, and apply from another directory after the preview's directory is deleted; a missing ../nowhere path still fails naming it. Without the fix the e2e fails on the token (checked by stashing the three source files). decided: canonicalize the parent and keep the last component, not the whole path as AbsPath::resolve did, so a symlink named by the user is the entry recorded. Wire names: none; a typed local path with '..' is now recorded resolved (file:<root>/zips/foo.zip). · found: none

title: install --dry-run creates inflight/ and trash/ in the state directory
description:
## Background

`--dry-run` promises to show the plan without changing anything. `install --dry-run` on a fresh state directory nevertheless creates empty `inflight/` and `trash/` directories under the state directory. The plan-level in-flight lock is taken during planning (`src/engine/tx.rs` around lines 159-160), and the prune/trash setup runs regardless of dry-run.

Nothing in a game directory is written, so this does not break the vision's "read commands never write to game directories". But it does contradict "changes nothing" and makes a dry run non-hermetic for agents that diff the state directory.

Found while exercising dry runs for the README rewrite.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Fresh `XDG_STATE_HOME`.
2. `omaddons install ./HelloWorld -t retail --dry-run`
3. `ls "$XDG_STATE_HOME/omaddons"` shows `inflight/` and `trash/`.

## Technical Approach

- Skip the plan-level in-flight lock, and any directory creation it implies, when the run is a dry run. Or create the directories lazily on first real use.
- Keep the derived discovery cache write (`<cache>/omaddons/discovery.json`), which is documented as derived data.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `install --dry-run`, `remove --dry-run`, `undo --dry-run`, `targets … --dry-run` and `config set --dry-run` create nothing under the state directory on a fresh home.
- A real run after a dry run still works and cleans up as before.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Integration: for each mutating command, snapshot the state directory tree before and after a dry run on a fresh home; assert they are equal.

## Considerations

- The in-flight lock exists so recovery can tell live transactions from dead ones. A dry run commits nothing, so it needs none, but planning code that assumes the lock exists must be checked.
acceptance_criteria: every mutating command with --dry-run leaves a fresh state directory unchanged; real runs after a dry run behave as before; argc gate passes
close_reason: Dry runs, planning and release checks leave the state directory alone

comments.author: CrimsonJasper
comments.text: Also seen from `sync --dry-run` (6.3.1): the empty <state>/omaddons/trash/ comes from cleanup() pruning the plan's in-flight lock file into the state trash. tests/sync.rs a_dry_run_writes_only_the_cache_the_net_log_and_inflight allows inflight/ and trash/ until this bead lands; tighten it then.

comments.author: CrimsonJasper
comments.text: Analysis (2026-10-16, while closing M2): both directories follow from deliberate designs, so the fix is not a quick skip. (1) inflight/: engine::tx::run takes a plan-level InflightLock before planning because a dry run still downloads and inspects archives into <cache>/omaddons/tmp/<tx>; the lock is what keeps a concurrent retention sweep from deleting that scratch (tests/sync.rs a_dry_run_writes_only_the_cache_the_net_log_and_inflight pins this). Skipping the lock under --dry-run would open that race. (2) trash/: cleanup() removes the run's own lock file through fsx::prune, which always moves through trash/ (M2-D23, the single deletion path). A hermetic dry run therefore needs the dry run's lock (and its prune) somewhere the sweep also honours, e.g. a lock beside the cache tmp dir that the cache sweep checks, with crash and concurrency coverage. Not done in the M2 checkpoint; README Known issues keeps the line.

comments.author: CrimsonJasper
comments.text: done: InflightLock::create_scratch puts a lock that guards only cache scratch at <cache>/inflight/<tx>.lock (Paths::cache_inflight_dir/lock); tx::run's plan-level lock and check_releases (adopt's checks) use it, for real runs too, since planning only writes <cache>/tmp/<tx>; each target's transaction keeps its state lock. InflightLock::is_live checks both places, so the blob tmp sweep, retention's orphans (now listing both dirs) and journal recovery honour scratch locks; fsx::prune accepts <cache>/inflight/<tx>.lock (Kind::Inflight, the cache's trash), and cleanup() prunes whichever lock exists. This keeps the analysis's race closed: a dry run's downloads stay locked against a concurrent sweep. Tests: contract special a_dry_run_leaves_the_state_directory_as_it_was (fresh home: install local, from the network and from the catalog, targets default; after an install: reinstall, remove, update --all, undo <tx>, undo, pin; byte-identical state tree but net.log); sync a_dry_run_writes_only_the_cache_and_the_net_log tightened (no inflight/trash exemption); the state_files helpers of adopt, outdated and sources_wowi drop their inflight exemption; prune every_reason_reaches_only_its_locations and a_transaction_prunes_its_own_artifacts… cover the cache lock (no state trash); retention dead_orphans… sweeps a dead scratch lock and keeps a held one's cache tmp; tx/undo leftovers include the cache lock dir. Planning detection in concurrency tests uses Home::planning_locks(). README: Known issues now 'None open', the cache row lists inflight/, and three stale Known-issues references (nested help, meta.offline, download cap) corrected. Gate green (1285).

title: A GitHub repository with no releases is reported as prerelease-only, and its --channel beta fix fails in turn
description:
## Background

The keyless-coverage study (omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.7, 2026-10-20) installed `gh:Jaliborc/Bagnon`, `gh:arkayenro/arkinventory` and `gh:LudiusMaximus/DynamicCam`. All three repositories exist and have no GitHub releases at all: `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/releases` answered `200` with `[]` (2 bytes in `net.log`). Their `releases/latest` redirects to `/{o}/{r}/releases`.

`latest_tag` in `src/sources/github.rs:337` reads that redirect as "has releases but no stable one (only prereleases)". It answers `no_compatible_release` with the fix `omaddons install <ref> --channel beta`. Following that fix fails too, now with "no published beta release among the newest 20" (`src/sources/github_rest.rs:198`, the same fix again). A user, or an agent following `fix_argv`, is sent in a circle. Nothing tells them that the repository simply publishes no releases.

GitHub redirects `releases/latest` to `/releases` whenever there is no latest release: when every release is a prerelease or draft, and also when there are none. A missing repository is a 404, which omaddons already reports as "has no GitHub releases (or the repository does not exist)", with a `git:` fix.

## Technical Approach

- On the `/releases` redirect, do not claim prereleases exist. Say the repository has no stable release ("no published release, or only prereleases"). The fix stays `--channel beta`, and add the `git:` form of the ref as an alternative (`git:https://github.com/{o}/{r}`).
- In `github_rest.rs`, when the release list is empty, say "has no published releases". Make the fix the `git:` ref, not `--channel beta`, because beta cannot help an empty list.
- Keep the error codes: `no_compatible_release` and `not_found` as now.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A repository whose `releases/latest` redirects to `/releases` gets a message that does not assert prereleases exist, with `--channel beta` as the fix and the `git:` ref as an alternative.
- A REST release list that is empty gets "has no published releases" and the `git:` ref as the fix. A non-empty list with no match on the channel keeps today's message.
- No fix offered on either path leads back to the other path's same error.

## Test Plan

- Unit tests in `src/sources/github.rs` and `github_rest.rs` with replayed responses: the `/releases` redirect, and a `200 []` list.
- The contract test for `fix_argv` keeps passing (each fix names a runnable command).
- `argc gate`.

## Considerations

- Whether a `git:` install of such a repository works depends on its layout. Bagnon's branch zip was not tried in the study. The alternative is a suggestion, and `install` still verifies every TOC.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `omaddons install gh:Jaliborc/Bagnon -t retail --dry-run --json` answers `no_compatible_release`, "gh:Jaliborc/Bagnon has releases but no stable one (only prereleases)", with fix `omaddons install gh:Jaliborc/Bagnon --channel beta`.
2. Running that fix answers "gh:Jaliborc/Bagnon: no published beta release among the newest 20", with the same fix again.
3. `net.log` shows `GET /repos/Jaliborc/Bagnon/releases` → 200, 2 bytes (`[]`). The repository has no releases. The same happens for `gh:arkayenro/arkinventory` and `gh:LudiusMaximus/DynamicCam` (2026-10-20).
acceptance_criteria: the /releases redirect no longer asserts prereleases exist and offers the git: ref as an alternative; an empty REST release list says the repository has no published releases with the git: ref as the fix; no fix leads back to the same error; argc gate passes
close_reason: The releases/latest → /releases redirect now says 'has no stable release (only prereleases, or none published)' with --channel beta as the fix and the git: ref as an alternative; an empty REST release list says 'has no published releases' with the git: ref as the fix, so neither path sends the user back to the other's error.

title: errors dismiss reports the first read's warnings after reading again under the lock
description:
## Background
`errors dismiss` (`dismiss` in `src/app/errors.rs`) reads each client's BugGrabber databases, checks `--if-match`, takes the global lock, and reads again when a database file moved meanwhile, binding to that second read (README `errors dismiss`; the review pass's "dismiss reports the read it binds to"). The second read replaces the first in the outcome's own warnings (`warnings.truncate(before_read)`), but `observe` also puts every read's warnings into the run's notes (`ctx.notes.warn_all`), and `output::emit_to` starts the envelope from the notes. So a warning only the first read had stays in the envelope after the dismissal bound to a read that no longer has it.

The visible case: a database the game was still writing at the first look (`errors_partial`, "could not be read completely … Counts are from what was read") and finished before the lock. The dismissal acknowledges it whole, and the envelope still says it could not be read. An agent following the warning's fix reads errors that are already dismissed.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. A retail client with BugGrabber whose `!BugGrabber.lua` ends early (cut 20 bytes short).
2. `omaddons errors dismiss -t retail --json` with `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS=errors.dismiss.observed=pause` (the failpoint omad-0jrj adds between the first read and the lock).
3. While it waits, write the whole file; resume.
4. The envelope: `partial: false`, `acknowledged: [{db-1, session 10}]`, `skipped: []`, and `warnings: [errors_partial …]` for that same database.

## Technical Approach
- `RunNotes::withdraw(&[Warning])` (`src/output/notes.rs`): take back warnings a step found and then superseded.
- In `dismiss`, when it reads again: withdraw the first read's warnings (those in `warnings[before_read..]` that were not already in `warnings[..before_read]`), truncate, then read again, which notes the second read's warnings as usual.
- A failure before the second read (the lock timing out, a stale `--if-match` at the first check) still reports the first read's warnings, which then describe the read that was made.

## Acceptance Criteria
- In the scenario above, the envelope has no `errors_partial` warning, and the dismissal acknowledges the database.
- Each warning of the bound read appears once (a second account's database still being written: one `errors_partial`).
- Removing the withdrawal, or the `truncate`, makes the test fail.

## Test Plan
- Integration (`tests/errors_dismiss.rs`): the scenario above; and a database that moves while the dismissal waits beside a second account's database still being written (one warning, bound to the second read, a first-read token refused as `plan_stale`).
- Unit (`src/output/notes.rs`): `withdraw` removes exactly the warnings given and keeps the others in order.

## Considerations
- A warning the run had found before the read (from `World::load`) must stay even if a read yields an equal one; the withdrawal is limited to the first read's own.
- Only `dismiss` reads twice; `errors` reads once and is unaffected.
acceptance_criteria: A database finished while dismiss waits for the lock is acknowledged and the envelope carries no errors_partial for it; each warning of the bound read appears once; removing the notes withdrawal or the truncate makes the test fail.
close_reason: Fixed: RunNotes::withdraw (src/output/notes.rs) takes back the first read's own warnings when dismiss reads again under the lock, then truncates and reads again. tests/errors_dismiss.rs a_database_finished_while_a_dismissal_waits_is_acknowledged_without_a_stale_warning failed on HEAD (envelope held errors_partial for a database it acknowledged whole) and passes now; removing the withdrawal or the truncate makes it fail again (both checked by hand). Unit: a_withdrawn_warning_leaves_the_others_in_order. Vision comment 1290. argc gate passed.

title: A release whose every candidate fails its published hash surfaces hash_mismatch, not no_compatible_release
description:
## Background

When every candidate of a wanted release fails its published hash (`hash_mismatch` after the one retry), the planner reports `no_compatible_release` (exit 3, not retryable). The `hash_mismatch` survives only as a string inside `details.tried[].reason`. The cause is `TargetPlanner::prepare_install` in `src/engine/plan.rs`, which records `Err(error)` from `try_candidate` as a tried entry and falls through to `no_release`. A user-supplied archive returns the unreadable error instead.

Found while doing 1.7 (MD5 expected hashes): `tests/plan.rs::a_published_hash_of_either_algorithm_is_checked_and_shown_in_the_plan` asserts today's shape. The M2 checkpoint for D3 says "a tampered WoWI fixture fails with `hash_mismatch`", and an agent should see a retryable download failure, not "no compatible release". SHA-256 expectations (GitHub REST digests) behave the same way today.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Plan an install of a ref whose source publishes an MD5 (or SHA-256) for its only asset, while the served zip differs. `tests/plan.rs` does this with a stand-in `wowi:` source.
2. The download fails its hash, is retried once, and fails again.
3. The plan failure is `no_compatible_release` (exit 3); `details.tried[0].reason` starts with `hash_mismatch:`.

## Technical Approach

- In `prepare_install`, when no candidate won and every tried entry failed with an error (none with a verdict refusal), return the first error itself, such as `hash_mismatch` (its retryability as the download left it), with `details.tried` added. Keep `no_compatible_release` when any candidate was judged and refused.
- Keep the M2-D41 rule in `update` intact: `blocked` stays for verification refusals only (`app::update::blocked` inspects `tried` reasons).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A release whose only candidate fails its MD5 or SHA-256 twice is an item failure with code `hash_mismatch`, `retryable: false`, and `details.tried`.
- A release with one candidate refused for flavor and one failing its hash stays `no_compatible_release`.
- `update`'s blocked mapping is unchanged (tests/update.rs passes unchanged).

## Test Plan

- Update `tests/plan.rs::a_published_hash_of_either_algorithm_is_checked_and_shown_in_the_plan` to assert `hash_mismatch`.
- Add a mixed-candidate case asserting `no_compatible_release`.
close_reason: hash_mismatch surfaces when every candidate fails its hash and none was judged

comments.author: CrimsonJasper
comments.text: claim: src/engine/plan.rs (prepare_install: surface a hash_mismatch every candidate shares), tests/plan.rs

comments.author: CrimsonJasper
comments.text: done: prepare_install tracks whether any candidate was judged and refused (try_candidate's Ok(Err)); when none was and the first failure is hash_mismatch, that error is returned (retryability as the download left it: false after the retry) with details.tried added beside expected/actual. A candidate judged not to load keeps the run no_compatible_release. update's blocked mapping is unchanged (hash_mismatch was never blocked). Tests: tests/plan.rs a_published_hash_of_either_algorithm_is_checked_and_shown_in_the_plan asserts hash_mismatch, retryable false, MD5 in the message, details.tried and expected, 2 downloads; a mixed release (a vanilla-only candidate plus a tampered one) stays no_compatible_release. Gate: 975 passed, 0 failed, ubs 0 critical. · found: none

title: Failure envelopes drop the `catalog_override_invalid` warning found before the failure
description:
## Background

The closing check of the post-M2 audit (omad-m2-audit-yegz) found that a failing command drops the `catalog_override_invalid` warning it found before failing.

README's Fields table says a failure's `warnings` "holds what the run found before it failed (a `journal_pending`, a `config_unknown_key`), and stderr carries each as a `warning` event before the `error` event". omad-m2-audit-yegz.5.3 made that true for what `World::load` finds: vision comment 680 on omad-vision-8qa records that `Context.notes` (`output::RunNotes`, src/output/notes.rs) collects a run's warnings as they are found, and `output::emit` puts them in the failure envelope and on stderr.

`Catalog::load` (src/resolve/catalog.rs:105-150) never fails: a broken built-in catalog or a broken `catalog.d` override becomes a `catalog_override_invalid` warning (lines 108-114 and 139-148). Its callers put those warnings only into a local `warnings` vector that ends up in the success outcome, never into `ctx.notes`:

- src/app/info.rs:317-318
- src/app/install.rs:405-406
- src/app/pin.rs:135-136 (pin and unpin)
- src/app/update.rs:133-134
- src/app/sync.rs:603-604
- src/app/copy.rs:183-184
- src/app/adopt.rs:473-474
- src/app/search.rs:326-327 and src/app/status.rs:486-487 (same pattern; a later failure in those commands loses it too)

So when the command then fails (`not_found`, `not_managed`, `offline`, …), the envelope's `warnings` is empty and stderr has only the `error` event. The broken override can be the very reason the command failed: a user's catalog.d entry that fails to parse makes their custom name unknown, and `install <that name>` fails `not_found` without saying the override was ignored. By contrast a `config_unknown_key` (found by `World::load`) does appear in the same failure envelope.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Fresh HOME with one synthetic retail client, `OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1`.
2. In that HOME's config directory (`$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, by default `.config` in HOME), write `omaddons/catalog.d/90-broken.toml` containing `schema_version = "1.0"` and `bogus_key = 1`.
3. `omaddons info foo --json` (a name the catalog knows): exit 0, `warnings` holds `catalog_override_invalid` ("90-broken.toml is ignored: … unknown field `bogus_key`"), and stderr has the `warning` event.
4. `omaddons info nosuchaddonxyz --json`: exit 3 `not_found`, `warnings: []`, stderr has only the `error` event.
5. `omaddons install nosuchaddonxyz -t retail --json`: exit 3 `not_found`, `warnings: []`.
6. `omaddons pin nosuchaddonxyz -t retail --json`: exit 3 `not_managed`, `warnings: []`.
7. Contrast: with `bogus_cfg = 1` in config.toml instead, step 4's envelope carries `config_unknown_key`.

## Technical Approach

- Report catalog warnings through `ctx.notes` as soon as they are found, as `World::load` does for its warnings. The smallest change is `ctx.notes.warn_all(&catalog_warnings)` next to each `Catalog::load` call listed above (keeping the `warnings.extend` for the success outcome; `RunNotes::warn_all` de-duplicates and `emit` merges them, as it already does for `World::load`'s warnings that are also cloned into outcomes).
- Better, to keep the pattern from being forgotten at the next call site: add one helper, e.g. `World::catalog(&self, ctx) -> Catalog` or `app::load_catalog(ctx, paths)`, that calls `Catalog::load`, pushes the warnings to `ctx.notes`, and returns the catalog plus the warnings; switch every call site to it.
- Call sites that discard the warnings on purpose (`Catalog::load(..).0` in src/app/engine.rs:88, src/app/status.rs:727 and src/app/adopt/hints.rs:63) load the catalog a second time in a run that already reported it; leave them as they are.
- No new warning code, no envelope change: this makes an existing promise true.

## Acceptance Criteria

- With a broken catalog.d file, `info`, `install`, `pin`/`unpin`, `update`, `sync`, `copy` and `adopt` failures carry `catalog_override_invalid` in the envelope's `warnings` and as a stderr `warning` event before the `error` event.
- Successful runs still report it exactly once (no duplicate in `warnings`).
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- E2E (tests/catalog.rs): with a broken catalog.d file, `info nosuchaddonxyz --json` and `install nosuchaddonxyz -t <id> --json` fail `not_found` and their `warnings` hold exactly one `catalog_override_invalid`; stderr shows the `warning` event before the `error` event.
- E2E: `pin nosuchaddonxyz -t <id>` fails `not_managed` with the warning.
- E2E: `info <catalog name>` succeeds with the warning exactly once (de-duplication).
- Contract: if tests/contract/ has a "failure keeps warnings" check from yegz.5.3, add a broken-catalog case to it.

## Considerations

- The warning message holds the override file's full path; that is the existing message and not changed here.
- `search` and `status` already succeed in most cases, but routing their catalog warnings through the same helper costs nothing and covers their failure paths.
- If the helper approach is taken, consider a test (like tests/single_writer.rs scans for writes) that fails when `Catalog::load` is called from src/app/ outside the helper; optional.
acceptance_criteria: with a broken catalog.d file, failing info, install, pin/unpin, update, sync, copy and adopt carry catalog_override_invalid in warnings and as a stderr warning event before the error event; successful runs report it exactly once; argc gate passes
close_reason: Catalog warnings go to the run's notes as soon as they are found (World::catalog), so a failing command reports a broken override too

title: errors dismiss --dry-run with a stale --if-match refuses instead of previewing afresh
description:
## Background

README's "Previews and `--if-match`" section promises: "A `--dry-run` that is given one previews afresh and returns the current token." `remove` and `undo` keep that promise (the engine ignores the binding on a dry run), and `backup prune` keeps it (D4). `errors dismiss` does not: `src/app/errors.rs` `dismiss()` calls `check(ctx.if_match, …)` before its `if ctx.dry_run` branch, so a dry run given a stale token fails with `plan_stale` instead of returning the current token. A widget that re-previews with the token it last held (as a confirm dialog refreshing itself may) gets a refusal instead of a fresh preview.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On a client with BugGrabber errors, `omaddons errors --json`: note `targets[0].dismiss.precondition` (token A).
2. Let a session end (the game rewrites the BugGrabber database), so the observation changes.
3. `omaddons errors dismiss -t retail --dry-run --if-match <A> --json`.
4. Today: exit 1, `plan_stale`. README: exit 0, `data.precondition` the current token, nothing written.

## Technical Approach

In `dismiss()`, return the dry-run outcome before calling `check`, as `backup prune` does (`src/app/backup.rs`, `prune_backups`): the dry run computes `bound(&seen).token()` from what it reads now. Keep the real-run check and the re-check under the lock unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `errors dismiss --dry-run --if-match <stale token>` exits 0, returns the current token, writes nothing (no acks file change, no doorbell ring).
- `errors dismiss --if-match <stale token>` (no `--dry-run`) still fails `plan_stale` and writes nothing.
- Gate green.

## Test Plan

- E2E in `tests/errors_dismiss.rs`: the stale-token scene already there, plus a `--dry-run` run with the stale token asserting exit 0, `data.precondition` equal to a fresh `errors dismiss --dry-run` token, and the acks file unchanged.

## Considerations

- Nothing else changes: the token format and parts stay as A4 defined them.
- Check `tests/preconditions.rs` `a_dry_run_with_if_match_previews_afresh` for the pattern used for `remove`.
acceptance_criteria: errors dismiss --dry-run --if-match <stale> exits 0 with the current token and writes nothing; without --dry-run a stale token still fails plan_stale; gate green
close_reason: errors dismiss --dry-run previews afresh whatever token it is given: the dry-run return comes before the --if-match check

title: Allow replacements of loaded folders on a running 3.3.5a client under safe, with reload_required: reload
description:
## Background

omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.6 observed the real 3.3.5a client (3.3.5.12340, under umu/GE-Proton, local server) on 2026-10-20 with probe addons that log their own load times:
- **A new folder is not seen without a restart.** A probe installed into the running client (T1) never loaded across three `/reload`s and an exit of that process: no SavedVariables file appeared until the client was restarted, and its first `loads` entry is 14 s after the restart.
- **A loaded addon's TOC is re-read on `/reload`.** With the restarted client running, the probe was replaced by a version whose TOC adds `b.lua` (T2). After one `/reload`, `b.lua` had run: `b` = the reload time, 12 s after T2. The `loads` list gained an entry at the same second.
- `checkAddonVersion` read `"1"` in game, and a TOC with `## Interface: 30300, 30400` loaded.

The `safe` running policy refuses every change on a legacy client (`src/engine/running.rs:~136`, `(RunningPolicy::Safe, false) if rules.legacy => …, "legacy_client"`), with the message "this client needs a restart to pick up any addon change". For a replacement of an already-loaded folder on 3.3.5a that is wrong: the player only needs `/reload`. For an add it is right.

omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.6 decided not to change the policy itself (its Technical Approach: "Do not make that change in this bead").

## Technical Approach

decided: relax only what was observed, on the `wrath-legacy` row only.
- Under `safe`, on a running `wrath-legacy` client:
  - `ReplaceFolder` that keeps or changes a loaded folder's TOC contents but keeps its loaded TOC *file* (`!op.drops_loaded_toc()`): allowed, `reload_required: reload`;
  - `AddFolder`: still refused (`legacy_client`), message changed to "this client needs a restart to see a new addon folder";
  - `RemoveFolder` of a loaded folder and any op that drops a loaded TOC: refused as today (`loaded_toc`).
- Other legacy rows (1.12.1, 2.4.3, 4.3.4, 5.4.8) keep refusing everything until observed (omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.5 covers detection only; runtime behaviour there is unobserved).
- A data-driven switch on the rules row (for example `reload_rereads_toc: bool`, true only for `wrath-legacy`) is better than matching the family name in `running.rs`. Constants live in `src/rules.rs`.
- This is a behaviour change (DEC-4): add a vision comment, and update README "Running clients", the legacy-client paragraph ("While a legacy client runs, the default running policy refuses every change") and FAQ "Is it safe to use while WoW is running?". Do it before the M4 freeze.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `the_policy_table` in `src/engine/running.rs` has rows for a running `wrath-legacy` client: replace (TOC kept) → `Ok(Reload)`; add → `legacy_client`; remove loaded → `loaded_toc`; and a running other-legacy client still refusing all three.
- An integration test installs over a managed folder on a running fake 3.3.5a target under `safe` and succeeds with `reload_required: reload`; a new addon on the same target is refused with the new message.
- README and FAQ match; the vision comment exists.
- argc gate passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit: the policy table rows above.
- Integration: `tests/running*.rs` with a fake `/proc` running a 3.3.5a client (`Wow.exe`), install update and fresh install under `safe`.
- Regression: modern-client rows unchanged.

## Considerations

- The observation is one client build and one server. 3.3.5a private-server clients are usually the stock 12340 build, but a patched `Wow.exe` might differ; the row covers the stock behaviour.
- "TOC re-read" was shown for an added Lua file. A replacement whose TOC changes `## SavedVariables` mid-session is not tested; the client writes SavedVariables at logout from what it loaded, which the reload covers.
- Keep `--while-running` as the override for adds.
acceptance_criteria: under safe, a running wrath-legacy client allows TOC-file-preserving replacements with reload_required reload, refuses adds with a restart message and removals as today; other legacy rows unchanged; policy table and integration tests cover it; README Running clients, legacy paragraph and FAQ updated with a vision comment (DEC-4); argc gate passes
close_reason: ClientRules.reload_rereads_toc (true for modern rows and wrath-legacy) drives the safe policy: on a running 3.3.5a client a replacement keeping its loaded TOC lands with reload_required reload; adds and removes are refused legacy_client with a restart message naming the folder; a dropped loaded TOC is loaded_toc; other legacy rows refuse everything as before. README Running clients, legacy paragraph, troubleshooting, Known limitations, FAQ and client_rules fields updated; vision comment added (DEC-4).

title: An undo reactivates at most one journal, so a repair that sets aside two cannot be undone
description:
## Background

M4-D46 promises that every doctor repair can be undone. A set-aside (F2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.2`, M4-D38) suspends a stuck journal's set into quarantine, and its undo reactivates the journal through E14's activation barrier: the journal comes back under its provisional name `<tx>.reactivating.jsonl` first, and the undo's last primitive renames it to its own name (`activation: true`).

E14 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14`, closed) fixed the activation rules in `src/engine/barrier.rs::validate`. Rule 1 says a repair has **at most one** activation, and it is the repair's last primitive. But `doctor fix` lowers every selected fix of a run into **one** repair transaction (E5, E6), and a forced `doctor fix --only <fm> --force --yes` selects every instance of that failure mode. Two stuck journals (two clients, or two journals on one client for the unattributed row) therefore set aside in one repair whose undo needs two activations, which rule 1 forbids.

E7's planning half (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7.1`, `src/engine/repair/undo.rs::plan_undo`) refuses such a line with `state_corrupt` ("it set aside 2 journals, and an undo reactivates at most one"), so nothing unsafe can run. The repair is then not undoable at all, which breaks M4-D46 for that case. No production fixer emits a set-aside yet (F2 is open), so no user can reach this today.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `cargo test --lib engine::repair::undo::tests::two_suspended_journals_in_one_repair_cannot_be_undone`.
2. The test commits one real repair that sets aside two journals (two `Fix::Suspend`), then plans its undo.
3. `plan_undo` returns `state_corrupt` today, and the test asserts that refusal.

## Technical Approach

Decided while filing this bead: widen rule 1 rather than split runs. `--only` names failure modes, not instances, so splitting a run cannot separate two stuck journals of one failure mode on one client. The barrier already handles a set of names (`Barrier.names`), and pass 1 settles a barrier's owner before any journal it names.

1. **`barrier::validate`.** Rule 1 becomes: the activations are the repair's last primitives, at most one per journal, and nothing that is not an activation follows the first of them. Rules 2 to 4 apply to each activation and its journal. In particular rule 3 holds per journal: its provisional restore is the first primitive that names it. Update the doc comment and the ten `validate_refuses_each_malformed_activation` cases, and add accepted cases for two and three activations.
2. **Recovery and `journal::diagnose`.** Check that a rollback of a repair crashed between two activations inverts the second-done activation first, hiding that journal under its provisional name. Each journal is then whole: before (provisional, invisible) or after (its own name, behind the settled owner). `Passes` already orders owners by naming, and its pass-1 settling must treat every name the same.
3. **E7.** Remove `plan_undo`'s "at most one" refusal. The activation-aware order already puts every provisional restore first and every activation last. Turn the unit test into one that plans two activations, both last, that `barrier::validate` accepts.
4. **README.** The Safety model ("Interrupted runs") says "the activation rename last". Make it "the activations last, one per journal".

## Acceptance Criteria

- `barrier::validate` accepts a repair whose last k primitives are activations of k distinct journals, each preceded by exactly one provisional restore that is the first primitive naming it. It refuses an activation followed by a non-activation, two activations of one journal, and every case it refused before.
- `plan_undo` of a set-aside of two journals plans both provisional restores first and both activations last, and `barrier::validate` accepts the steps.
- The crash matrix (common rule 14, `tests/barrier_crash.rs`) covers a reactivation of two journals: a crash at every primitive boundary, including between the two activations, then recovery by three lock-taking commands. Recovery itself is crashed at every inverse and repeated. Neither journal is ever recovered ahead of the repair, and each end state is wholly before or wholly after. E11's differential agrees.
- Every existing barrier, journal and crash test passes unchanged except the rule-1 cases this bead rewrites.
- `argc gate` passes, `ubs` is clean on the changed files, and README says "activations last, one per journal".

## Test Plan

- Unit (`src/engine/barrier.rs`): accepted and refused cases for multi-activation repairs, each named, each message showing the steps.
- Unit (`src/engine/repair/undo.rs`): the two-journal set-aside plans and validates.
- Crash (`tests/barrier_crash.rs`): the two-journal reactivation matrix above, logged through `TestLog`.

## Considerations

- This is a protocol change to a closed design gate, so it lands with its own adversarial matrix (common rule 14).
- Older builds: the provisional name is invisible to the M3 build, whatever the number of journals. E9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9`) characterizes a crash mid-reactivation, and a second journal adds no new shape there.
- F2 must not ship a set-aside run of several journals before this lands, or that repair is not undoable. This bead blocks F2 for that reason.
acceptance_criteria:
- barrier::validate accepts k trailing activations of k distinct journals (each preceded by exactly one provisional restore, the first primitive naming it) and refuses an activation followed by a non-activation, two activations of one journal, and every case it refused before.
- plan_undo of a set-aside of two journals plans both provisional restores first and both activations last, and barrier::validate accepts the steps.
- tests/barrier_crash.rs covers a two-journal reactivation crashed at every primitive boundary (between the activations included) and in recovery, with E11's differential agreeing; every end state wholly before or after.
- Existing barrier, journal and crash tests pass unchanged except the rewritten rule-1 cases; argc gate passes; ubs clean; README says activations last, one per journal.
close_reason: An undo reactivates every journal a set-aside suspended, one activation per journal, all last: barrier::validate's rule 1 widened, plan_undo's refusal removed, proved by a two-journal crash matrix (118 cases, 69/69 boundaries) and an end-to-end forced fix of two journals
