title: Error and warning code registries, Error/Warning/Suggestion types in src/error.rs
description:
## Background

The CLI contract (vision omad-vision-8qa §5.9, D17, D18, D31) requires:

- every failure to be a typed error with a stable snake_case `code`, a human `message`, a `fix` that is never empty, and `fix_argv`, the argv that runs the fix;
- every error code to map to exactly one exit code in the general exit dictionary, with a published retryability;
- every executable suggestion (the `fix`, each `alternatives[]` entry, each `commands[]` entry) to carry `argv`, so programs execute argv and never shell-parse a display string. The widget executes only entries whose `argv[0]` is `omaddons`. Non-CLI fixes such as `/reload in game` carry `argv: null`.

Warnings use a second registry. The reference implementation this project replaces printed a traceback and no JSON on an unexpected error (vision §3 R3). The registry exists so that every failure path has a code, an exit status and a fix.

This bead builds both registries and the error, warning and suggestion types in `src/error.rs`. It has no open dependencies; the output-envelope bead renders these types.

## Technical Approach

**Exit dictionary.** `Exit` is the general dictionary, used by every command except the M4 `doctor` tree:

| Code | Name | Meaning | Retryable |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `ok` | Success, including partial success: per-item failures are listed in `data`, mirrored in `warnings`, and flagged `partial: true` | — |
| 1 | `failed` | Runtime failure: network, source, archive integrity, I/O, state, internal | per `error.retryable` |
| 2 | `usage` | Unknown command or flag, bad argument, bad ref syntax | no |
| 3 | `not_found` | Target, ref, addon, plan or transaction not found, or ambiguous | no |
| 4 | `refused` | Safety refusal: running client, protected folder, ownership or case conflict, unsafe archive, wrong flavor, undo conflict, blocked host | no (`fix` names the flag or command) |
| 5 | `locked` | Another omaddons process held the lock past the acquire timeout | yes |
| 6 | `check_failed` | An opt-in assertion failed (`--check`, `--strict`) | no |

`Exit` provides `code() -> u8`, `name() -> &'static str`, `meaning() -> &'static str`, `ALL: &[Exit]` (M4's capabilities publishes it) and `impl From<Exit> for std::process::ExitCode`. Decided: the process exit status is only ever derived from an `Exit` value; no literal integer passed to `std::process::exit`/`ExitCode::from` appears anywhere else, which the E7 contract suite's exit-site test enforces.

**Error codes.** `ErrorCode` is a closed enum. Each variant provides `wire() -> &'static str`, `exit() -> Exit`, `default_retryable() -> bool` and `ALL: &[ErrorCode]`. The table, copied from vision §5.9 plus the DEC-4 additions:

| Code | Exit | Retryable |
|---|---|---|
| `usage`, `ref_invalid` | 2 | no |
| `target_not_found`, `target_ambiguous`, `ref_ambiguous`, `not_found`, `not_managed`, `plan_not_found`, `no_compatible_release` | 3 | no |
| `game_running`, `protected_folder`, `ownership_conflict`, `unmanaged_folder`, `case_collision`, `wrong_flavor`, `unsafe_archive`, `archive_too_large`, `undo_conflict`, `host_blocked` | 4 | no |
| `scope_denied` (DEC-4: fsx refused a write outside the write-scope table or onto the deny-list, other than a protected folder, which stays `protected_folder`) | 4 | no |
| `state_too_new` (DEC-4: a state file's `schema_version` is newer than this binary; writes refused; fix display "upgrade omaddons", `argv: null`) | 4 | no |
| `locked` | 5 | yes |
| `check_failed` | 6 | no |
| `network`, `rate_limited` (details carry the reset time), `download_failed` | 1 | yes |
| `http_status` | 1 | yes for 5xx only |
| `hash_mismatch` | 1 | yes, once |
| `plan_stale` | 1 | yes when raised by engine step-6 re-planning; no when raised by `apply` (M4; fix = the stored dry-run argv) |
| `offline`, `bad_archive`, `distribution_disabled`, `source_disabled`, `auth_required`, `auth_rejected`, `state_corrupt`, `io`, `internal` | 1 | no |

Per-instance retryability: `Error.retryable` starts from `default_retryable()` and is set by dedicated constructors where the table says it depends on context:
- `Error::http_status(status, …)` sets `retryable = status >= 500`;
- `Error::plan_stale(raised_by: Replan | Apply, …)`;
- `Error::hash_mismatch(attempt: u8, …)` is retryable only on the first attempt.

**Suggestions.**
- `Suggestion { display: String, argv: Option<Vec<String>> }`.
- `Suggestion::command<I, S>(argv: I)` (argv[0] must be `"omaddons"`, checked by `debug_assert!`) sets `display = shell_words::join(&argv)`, so display strings are shell-quoted.
- `Suggestion::text(display)` is for non-CLI fixes (`/reload in game`, "upgrade omaddons") and sets `argv: None`.
- A display can never be empty: an empty `text` falls back to the DEC-5 fix.

**Command hints.** `CommandHint { action: String, command: String, argv: Vec<String>, destructive: bool }`, built by `CommandHint::new(action, argv, destructive)` with `command = shell_words::join(argv)`. The wire field order matches the vision envelope example: `{"action":"undo","command":"omaddons undo 01JB…","argv":["omaddons","undo","01JB…"],"destructive":false}`.

**Errors.**
- `Error { code: ErrorCode, message: String, fix: Suggestion, alternatives: Vec<Suggestion>, retryable: bool, details: serde_json::Value }`, derived with `thiserror::Error`, displaying as `error[<code>]: <message>`.
- Constructors: `Error::new(code, message, fix)`, builder methods `.alternative(Suggestion)`, `.details(serde_json::Value)` and `.retryable(bool)`, and per-domain helpers where useful (`Error::internal(msg)`, `Error::io(path, &std::io::Error, fix)`).
- `details` defaults to an empty JSON object `{}`.
- `type Result<T> = std::result::Result<T, Error>`.
- DEC-5: until `doctor` exists (M4), `Error::internal` uses fix `omaddons status`, argv `["omaddons","status"]`. M4 switches it to `omaddons doctor`. Keep this in one function, `internal_fix()`.
- Decided: no blanket `From<std::io::Error> for Error`. Every I/O failure goes through `Error::io` with the path and a fix, because a bare conversion would lose the context the fix needs.

**Wire serialization** (an `ErrorBody` view, field order exactly as the vision failure example): `{"code","message","fix","fix_argv","alternatives":[{"display","argv"}],"retryable","details"}`. `fix` is the display string, `fix_argv` the argv or `null`.

**Warnings.**
- `WarningCode` is a closed enum with `wire()` and `ALL`.
- `Warning { code, message, fix: Option<Suggestion> }` serializes as `{"code","message","fix","fix_argv"}`. Decided: both `fix` and `fix_argv` are always present, `null` when absent, so the shape is stable for consumers.
- The initial codes from vision §5.9: `journal_recovered`, `journal_pending`, `tx_in_progress`, `atomic_swap_unavailable`, `reload_required`, `saved_variables_deferred`, `snapshot_cap_exceeded`, `out_of_date`, `missing_dependency`, `toc_comma_on_legacy`, `client_not_launched_since_patch`, `widget_outdated`.
- DEC-4 adds `state_version_older` (state is migrated forward on the next write) and `state_version_newer` (writes refused).
- Other M1 beads add the warning codes they introduce here, in the same file, keeping the enum closed. Codes already claimed by M1 beads: `config_unknown_key` (config), `unknown_flavor`, `discovery_truncated`, `target_key_duplicate` (discovery and registry), `catalog_override_invalid` (catalog), `ownership_transferred` (ownership). This bead may add them all up front so later beads only use them. The contract is not frozen until M4, and each addition is listed in the comment recorded on the vision bead.
- Decided: a per-item failure that is mirrored into `warnings` during partial success (exit 0, `partial: true`) uses the item's error code as its warning code. `WarningCode` has a variant `Item(ErrorCode)` whose `wire()` is the error's wire name, so `install a b` where `b` has no compatible release yields a warning `{"code":"no_compatible_release",…}` alongside the per-item entry in `data`. Wire names stay unique: no plain warning code may reuse an error code's name.

All public wire types derive `serde::Serialize` and `schemars::JsonSchema` (DEC-3).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `ErrorCode::ALL` contains exactly the 38 codes in the table above (the 36 vision §5.9 codes plus `scope_denied` and `state_too_new`). A table-driven test asserts each code's `wire()`, `exit().code()` and `default_retryable()`.
- `Exit::ALL` lists codes 0–6 with the names `ok, failed, usage, not_found, refused, locked, check_failed`.
- Every wire name (errors and warnings) is unique and matches `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`.
- `Error::http_status(503, …).retryable` is true and `Error::http_status(404, …).retryable` is false. `plan_stale` raised by re-planning is retryable and raised by apply is not. `hash_mismatch` is retryable on attempt 1 only.
- `Suggestion::command(["omaddons","install","my addon","-t","retail"]).display == "omaddons install 'my addon' -t retail"`, and `shell_words::split(display)` returns the argv unchanged, for argv containing spaces, `!`, `$(…)`, quotes and backslashes.
- No `Suggestion` can carry an empty display. `Error::internal(…)` has fix `omaddons status` with argv `["omaddons","status"]`.
- An `Error` serializes with keys in the order `code, message, fix, fix_argv, alternatives, retryable, details`, and a `Warning` as `code, message, fix, fix_argv`.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit (`src/error.rs`):
  - a table test that iterates a hand-written copy of the table above and compares it to `ErrorCode::ALL` (catches a code missing from either side);
  - wire-name uniqueness and format;
  - the retryability constructors;
  - `Suggestion` quoting round trips through `shell_words::split`, including argv `["omaddons","install","a b","$(rm -rf x)","it's","!x"]`;
  - empty-display fallback.
- Snapshot: insta JSON snapshots of a `target_ambiguous` error with one alternative and `details.candidates`, and of a `reload_required` warning with a text fix (`fix_argv: null`).
- Property: proptest over arbitrary argv vectors checks that `shell_words::split(Suggestion::command(argv).display) == argv`.
- Log test inputs and outputs on failure.

## Considerations

- This bead fixes wire names that M4 freezes and the wire-name golden test pins. Choose spellings exactly as in the tables above.
- Not here: the M4 doctor dictionary (0–6 plus 64/66/73/74) and finding ids `fm-<subsystem>-<slug>`; rendering of errors and warnings (output-envelope bead); the exit-site enforcement test (E7 contract suite).
- `rate_limited` errors put the reset time in `details.reset_at` (RFC 3339). Name the key here so the net beads use it.
- Where a refusal can be overridden, its `fix` must name the overriding flag or command (exit-dictionary row 4), e.g. `game_running` → `--while-running`, or `unmanaged_folder` → `--force` until M2's `adopt`.
acceptance_criteria: ErrorCode::ALL contains exactly 38 codes (the 36 vision §5.9 codes plus scope_denied and state_too_new), and a table-driven test checks each wire name, exit code and default retryability; Exit::ALL lists 0-6 named ok, failed, usage, not_found, refused, locked, check_failed; all error and warning wire names are unique and match ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$; http_status is retryable for 5xx only, plan_stale is retryable from re-planning but not from apply, and hash_mismatch is retryable on the first attempt only; Suggestion::command display strings are shell-quoted and round-trip through shell_words::split for argv with spaces, !, $(...), quotes and backslashes; no Suggestion has an empty display and Error::internal has fix omaddons status with argv ["omaddons","status"]; Error serializes as code, message, fix, fix_argv, alternatives, retryable, details and Warning as code, message, fix, fix_argv; argc gate passes
close_reason: src/error.rs holds the general exit dictionary, the 38-code error registry and the 20-code warning registry (plus Item(ErrorCode)), Suggestion/CommandHint with shell-quoted displays and argv, and the Error/Warning types with their wire bodies; all acceptance criteria are covered by tests

comments.author: BoldKettle
comments.text: claim: src/error.rs (+ src/snapshots/ for error/warning snapshots). Building Exit, ErrorCode, WarningCode registries, Suggestion, CommandHint, Error, Warning.

comments.author: BoldKettle
comments.text: **Implementation decisions (src/error.rs).** (1) Each registry is one `macro_rules!` table (`error_codes!`, `warning_codes!`), so a code's wire name, serde rename, exit and default retryability come from a single row. (2) Default retryability for context-dependent codes: `http_status` false, `hash_mismatch` true, `plan_stale` true. Their constructors decide per instance: `Error::http_status(status, …)` (also sets details.status), `Error::hash_mismatch(attempt, …)` (attempts count from 1), `Error::plan_stale(PlanStaleSource::{Replan,Apply}, …)`. (3) Added `Error::rate_limited(reset_at: jiff::Timestamp, …)`, which writes `details.reset_at` (RFC 3339) as the bead asks; `Error::io` puts the path in `details.path`. (4) `Suggestion` and `CommandHint` keep their fields private behind accessors, so an empty display is unconstructible; `argv[0] == omaddons` is a debug_assert. Suggestion has no Deserialize, since that would bypass the invariant. (5) schemars derives the deserialize contract by default, so `#[serde(into = "ErrorBody")]` did not shape Error's schema; `JsonSchema for Error` is written by hand and delegates to ErrorBody. (6) `Warning` derives Deserialize through WarningBody, because the discovery cache persists warnings; a blank fix loads as None. Added `Warning::with_fix` and `Warning::item(&Error)` for partial-success mirroring. (7) All six later-claimed warning codes are added up front (config_unknown_key, unknown_flavor, discovery_truncated, target_key_duplicate, catalog_override_invalid, ownership_transferred): 20 plain codes plus `Item(ErrorCode)`.

comments.author: BoldKettle
comments.text: done: argc gate passes (62 lib tests incl. argv round-trip proptest; snapshots target_ambiguous_error and reload_required_warning match the vision envelope example; strict cargo doc clean; ubs 0 critical); decisions in comment above; notes on 1.5, 5.2, 2.4, 5.5 · found: none

comments.author: BoldKettle
comments.text: **Post-close change (found while doing paths, ejl.2.6):** `Error` was 136 bytes, so clippy's default `result_large_err` (128-byte threshold) rejected every function returning `error::Result<T>`. Error is now `pub struct Error(Box<ErrorData>)` with `Deref`/`DerefMut` to `ErrorData { code, message, fix, alternatives, retryable, details }`, so `err.code` and `err.message` still work and `Result<T>` is one pointer wide (guarded by the test `errors_stay_one_pointer_wide`). Constructors, builders, Display and the wire shape (ErrorBody) are unchanged; struct-literal construction and destructuring of Error are no longer possible.

title: Define the core domain types in src/model.rs
description:
## Background

Every M1 subsystem (fsx, state, discovery, sources, resolution, the engine, the commands) passes the same domain values around: targets, folder names, transaction and plan ids, actors, refs, release sets, candidates and addon records (vision omad-vision-8qa §5.1). Several safety invariants are meant to be enforced by these types rather than by checks scattered through the code (vision §3 language note, D14, D27):

- a folder name can never escape `Interface/AddOns/`: no `/`, `\`, `..`, leading `.`, empty name or NUL;
- folder identity is case-insensitive, because Wine resolves names case-insensitively, so `Blizzard_AuctionUI` and `blizzard_auctionui` are the same folder;
- a folder whose case-folded key starts with `blizzard_` is protected and can never enter the mutable namespace, even with `--force`.

DEC-13: `Family`, `InstallKind`, `TargetKind`, `ClientRules` and the client version type live in `src/rules.rs` (the rules-tables bead, which depends on nothing). This bead depends on rules-tables and defines everything else in `src/model.rs`.

## Technical Approach

All types live in `src/model.rs`. Data types derive `Debug, Clone, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize, schemars::JsonSchema` (DEC-3). Struct field order is the wire order. Maps are `BTreeMap`. Wire names are snake_case lowercase. Use `#[schemars(with = "String")]` for ULIDs, timestamps and paths, because schemars does not know those types without extra features.

**Folder names**
- `FolderName`: a validated `AddOns/<Name>` entry name that keeps its original spelling. `FolderName::new(&str) -> Result<FolderName, FolderNameError>` rejects:
  - empty names, `.` and `..`, and names with a leading `.`;
  - names containing `/`, `\` or NUL, or any ASCII control character (0x00–0x1F, 0x7F);
  - names longer than 255 bytes (NAME_MAX).
- `key(&self) -> &str` returns the ASCII case-folded name (`to_ascii_lowercase`), computed once at construction. `as_str()` returns the original spelling.
- `PartialEq`, `Eq`, `Hash` and `Ord` compare by key, so `BTreeMap<FolderName, _>` treats case variants as one folder. Code that must detect two on-disk spellings of one key (the inventory) collects into a `Vec` and groups by key.
- `is_protected()` is true when `key()` starts with `blizzard_`.
- `MutableFolderName`: a newtype that only `FolderName::into_mutable(self) -> Result<MutableFolderName, FolderName>` can construct, and only when the name is not protected. Every API that creates, replaces, renames or removes an AddOns folder (fsx scope checks, engine ops, ownership) takes `MutableFolderName`. Decided: two types rather than one checked type (D14), so a protected folder cannot reach a mutation API without a compile error.
- Serialize as a plain string. Deserialize through `FolderName::new`, so a persisted record holding an invalid name fails to load (`state_corrupt`).

**Ids**
- `TargetKey(Ulid)`, `TxId(Ulid)` and `PlanId(Ulid)`, each with `new()` (`Ulid::new()`), `Display`, `FromStr`, and serde as the 26-character Crockford base32 string (the ulid crate's `serde` feature is enabled). The JSON Schema is a string with pattern `^[0-9A-HJKMNP-TV-Z]{26}$`.
- Keys are immutable once assigned; the registry bead owns assignment.

**Small enums** (lowercase wire names):
- `Actor { Human, Agent, Widget }`, plus a pure `Actor::resolve(flag: Option<&str>, env: Option<&str>, stdin_is_tty: bool) -> Result<Actor, ActorError>`. Precedence: the `--actor` flag, then `OMADDONS_ACTOR`, then `human` when stdin is a terminal and `agent` otherwise. An invalid value is an error that the CLI maps to `usage`. Decided: stdin, not stdout, decides the default, because a human piping `omaddons list | jq` still has a TTY on stdin while agents run with no TTY on any stream.
- `Channel { Stable, Beta, Alpha }`, default `Stable`, ordered so `Stable < Beta < Alpha`. `Channel::includes(release_channel)`: beta includes stable, alpha includes everything.
- `TxKind { Install, Update, Remove, Undo, Adopt, Sync, Restore, Repair, Backup }`, with `is_undoable()` false only for `Backup`. The history records WTF backup creation as `kind: backup` (M3); the variant exists now so the history schema does not change later.
- `ReloadRequired { None, Reload, Restart }`, ordered so `max()` merges per-op requirements into a per-target value.
- `VersionConfidence { Release, Toc }`, `AddonReason { Explicit, Dependency }`, `AddonState { Ok, Degraded }`.

**`Target`** (vision §5.1), one client dir plus its identity:
- fields in this order: `key: Option<TargetKey>` (None until registered), `id: String` (human alias), `install_root: PathBuf`, `client_dir: PathBuf`, `flavor_dir: Option<String>` (e.g. `_retail_`; None for custom roots), `product: Option<String>` (e.g. `wow_classic_era`), `install_kind`, `family`, `kind` (`live|test`), `version` (the rules client-version type), `interface: u32`, `exe_name: String`, `label: Option<String>` (e.g. `localhost` from realmlist), `rules: ClientRules`;
- `rules` is `#[serde(skip)]` and excluded from the schema. Decided: the row is large and not useful in token-frugal output; commands that need rules data build their own view;
- helper `addons_dir()` returns `client_dir/Interface/AddOns`. Paths are produced here and never created here.

**`AddonRecord`** (vision §5.1), fields in order: `ref` (serialized as its canonical string), `name`, `version: String`, `version_confidence`, `release_id: Option<String>`, `channel`, `pinned: bool`, `reason`, `required_by: Vec<String>`, `folders: Vec<FolderName>`, `state`, `installed_at` (`jiff::Timestamp`, RFC 3339), `tx_id: TxId`. The per-file index is not part of the record; it lives in `targets/<key>.files.json` (state-records bead).

**`Ref`**, the canonical `source:id`:
- `GitHub { owner, repo }` ↔ `gh:Owner/Repo`
- `Wowi { id: u64 }` ↔ `wowi:5108`
- `Tukui { slug }` ↔ `tukui:elvui`
- `CurseForge { id: u64 }` ↔ `cf:61284`
- `Wago { id }` ↔ `wago:<id>`
- `Git { url, rev: Option<String> }` ↔ `git:<https-url>[#<rev>]`
- `Url { url }` ↔ `url:<https-url>`
- `File { path }` ↔ `file:<path>`

Behavior:
- `Display` and `FromStr` handle only these canonical forms. Pasted URLs, catalog names and installed names are the refs bead's job.
- `FromStr` errors are typed, and the refs bead maps them to `ref_invalid` (exit 2). Checks: GitHub owner and repo match `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+` and are not `.`/`..`; wowi and cf ids are decimal; git and url schemes must be `https`; file paths are non-empty.
- `RefKind` (`Gh, Wowi, Tukui, Cf, Wago, Git, Url, File`) with `prefix()`. The sources layer maps kinds to sources.
- Equality and hashing for `GitHub` compare owner and repo ASCII-case-insensitively, because GitHub treats them that way and the fetch-once orchestrator must not fetch `gh:weakauras/weakauras2` twice. Display keeps the given spelling. Serialize as the canonical string.

**Release types** (vision §5.1; field lists are the minimum, and later beads may add `Option` fields):
- `ReleaseSet { ref, releases: Vec<Release> }`: everything one fetch learned about one ref.
- `Release { release_id, version, channel, published_at: Option<Timestamp>, assets: Vec<Asset>, changelog_url: Option<String> }`.
- `Asset { filename, location: AssetLocation, size: Option<u64>, expected_hash: Option<ExpectedHash>, flavors: Vec<AssetFlavor>, name_flavors: Vec<FlavorHint>, nolib: bool }`.
- `AssetLocation { Url(String) | LocalZip(PathBuf) | LocalDir(PathBuf) | GitCheckout { url: String, rev: String, sha: String } }`. Decided here, once, because four source beads and three engine beads route on it: `Url` is downloaded into the blob cache; `LocalZip` is hashed and opened in place (user files are not copied into the cache); `LocalDir` is read through a directory `FolderView`; `GitCheckout` is materialized by the git-hosts source into a temp dir and then treated like `LocalDir`.
- `AssetFlavor { flavor: String, interface: Option<u32> }` (release.json metadata).
- `FlavorHint { Mainline, Classic, Bcc, Wrath, Cata, Mists, Titan, Forever, ClassicAny }`: flavor guesses from asset file names, filled by the GitHub REST source's name heuristics for repos without `release.json`. Variant names follow the packager's release.json flavor names.
- `ExpectedHash { Sha256(String) }`, lowercase hex. Decided: M1 has only SHA-256; the MD5 (WoWInterface, M2) and SHA-1 (CurseForge, M5) variants and their crates arrive with those sources.
- `Candidate { release_id, version, channel, asset: Asset, rank: RankReason }`, where `RankReason { MetadataInterface, MetadataFlavor, NameHint, Unannotated, NameHintMismatch, MetadataMismatch }` records which tier of the select bead's ranking proposed it. Selection logic is the select bead's job.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `src/model.rs` defines every type above. `cargo doc` shows each with a one-line doc comment.
- `FolderName::new` rejects `""`, `"."`, `".."`, `".hidden"`, `"a/b"`, `"a\\b"`, `"a\0b"`, names with control characters and names over 255 bytes, and accepts `"WeakAuras"`, `"!BugGrabber"` and `"Blizzard_AuctionUI"`.
- `FolderName::new("Blizzard_AuctionUI").key() == "blizzard_auctionui"`, and that name `is_protected()`. `into_mutable()` fails for it and for `"BLIZZARD_x"`, and succeeds for `"WeakAuras"`.
- Two `FolderName`s differing only in ASCII case are equal and hash equally. `as_str()` keeps the original spelling.
- Every canonical `Ref` form round-trips through `Display` and `FromStr`. `gh:WeakAuras/WeakAuras2 == gh:weakauras/weakauras2`. `git:http://…` and `url:http://…` are rejected.
- `Actor::resolve` follows flag > env > TTY default, and rejects unknown values.
- ULID ids serialize as 26-character strings and parse back.
- Every data type derives `JsonSchema`, and `schemars::schema_for!` succeeds for `Target`, `AddonRecord`, `ReleaseSet` and `Candidate`.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit (in `src/model.rs` `#[cfg(test)]`):
  - table tests for `FolderName` accept and reject cases, `key()`, `is_protected()` and `into_mutable()`;
  - `Ref` round trip for each variant, plus rejection cases;
  - `Actor::resolve` precedence matrix;
  - `Channel::includes` matrix;
  - `ReloadRequired` max-merge.
- Property (proptest):
  - for arbitrary strings, `FolderName::new` never returns a name containing `/`, `\`, NUL or `..` as a component, and never one starting with `.`;
  - `key()` is idempotent and case-insensitive (`new(s.to_uppercase())` and `new(s)` have equal keys when both are valid ASCII);
  - every `Ref` built from generated valid parts round-trips.
- Serde: insta JSON snapshots of a sample `Target` (`rules` absent) and an `AddonRecord`; deserializing a record with folder `"../x"` fails.
- Log test inputs and outputs on failure (proptest prints the minimal failing case).

## Considerations

- `key()` folds ASCII only, as the vision specifies ("ASCII case-folded"). Wine folds non-ASCII case too, so two non-ASCII names differing in case are treated as distinct here. Addon folder names are ASCII in practice; revisit only if a real collision appears.
- Trailing dots and spaces are legal on Linux, but Windows path semantics may strip them under Wine. They are accepted for now; the archive-inspect bead's case-folded collision check is the place to tighten this if needed.
- `Target.version` is `rules::ClientVersion { major, minor, patch, build: Option<u32> }` from the rules-tables bead; do not define a second version type here.
- Out of scope: Ref parsing beyond canonical forms (refs bead), id/alias assignment (registry bead), plan, journal and history types (engine and state beads), `Finding` (M4 doctor).
- Dependency: rules-tables provides `Family`, `InstallKind`, `TargetKind`, `ClientRules` and the version type.

title: JSON envelope, human rendering and stderr event stream in src/output/
description:
## Background

The CLI contract (vision omad-vision-8qa §5.9, D17) separates data from diagnostics with no exceptions:

- **stdout is data.** Under `--json`, `--format json`, `--robot` or `OMADDONS_FORMAT=json`, stdout carries exactly one envelope, on success and on failure. Otherwise it carries human-formatted data, and it is empty on error. Help and `robot-docs` output count as data.
- **stderr is diagnostics.** It is NDJSON when stderr is not a TTY, when `CI` is set, or when `TERM=dumb`; every line is then an object with `event` ∈ `progress|log|warning|error`. On an interactive TTY it carries human lines (`warning: …`, `error[<code>]: <message>` then `fix: <fix>`, progress bars). Every error is mirrored to stderr as one line in whichever form applies.

D17 records why failures must reach stdout too: a silent empty stdout made `cmd --json | jq` pipelines succeed on failure, and the house IO contract requires both a JSON-parsing consumer and a stderr-only consumer to see errors.

Commands never print (lint-enforced: `print_stdout`, `print_stderr` denied). They return a typed outcome or an `Error` (error-registry bead), and this module renders it. This bead builds `src/output/`. It depends on error-registry.

## Technical Approach

**Files:** `src/output/mod.rs` (the `emit` entry point and mode types), `envelope.rs`, `human.rs`, `stderr.rs` (the `Reporter`), and `term.rs` (TTY, color and environment detection).

**Envelope** (`envelope.rs`). One shape for success and failure, with field order exactly as in the vision examples:

```json
{"ok":true,"schema_version":"1.0","tool_version":"0.1.0","command":"update","exit_code":0,"partial":false,"data":{},"warnings":[{"code":"reload_required","message":"…","fix":"/reload in game","fix_argv":null}],"commands":[{"action":"undo","command":"omaddons undo 01JB…","argv":["omaddons","undo","01JB…"],"destructive":false}],"meta":{"elapsed_ms":412,"offline":false}}
{"ok":false,"schema_version":"1.0","tool_version":"0.1.0","command":"install","exit_code":3,"error":{"code":"target_ambiguous","message":"weakauras is compatible with 2 targets","fix":"omaddons install weakauras -t retail","fix_argv":["omaddons","install","weakauras","-t","retail"],"alternatives":[{"display":"omaddons install weakauras -t forever","argv":["omaddons","install","weakauras","-t","forever"]}],"retryable":false,"details":{"candidates":["retail","forever"]}},"warnings":[],"commands":[],"meta":{"elapsed_ms":9,"offline":false}}
```

- `struct Envelope<'a, D: Serialize>` with fields in this order: `ok`, `schema_version` (const `SCHEMA_VERSION = "1.0"`), `tool_version` (`CARGO_PKG_VERSION`), `command`, `exit_code`, `partial: Option<bool>`, `data: Option<&'a D>`, `error: Option<ErrorBody>`, `warnings`, `commands`, `meta: Meta { elapsed_ms, offline }`.
- Decided: `partial` and `data` are present whenever the command produced data: always on success, and on failure only for `check_failed` (`--check`/`--strict`, exit 6, where the vision requires `data` to stay populated). `error` is present iff `ok == false`. `None` fields are skipped. This matches both vision examples exactly.
- Determinism: serialize `D` generically. Never convert data to `serde_json::Value` first: without serde_json's `preserve_order` feature a `Value` object sorts its keys and breaks the declaration-order rule. Volatile fields (`elapsed_ms` and any future timing) live only in `meta`. Output is compact, single-line JSON followed by `\n`.
- `--json` output is one `serde_json::to_writer` call on a locked stdout, then a flush.
- Decided: the envelope's `command` is the space-joined subcommand path as typed in canonical form, e.g. `"install"`, `"targets add"`, `"config get"`, `"help"`. Aliases resolve to the canonical name (M4 adds aliases). `Outcome::command()` returns that string.

**Outcome trait** (`mod.rs`):

```rust
pub trait Outcome {
    type Data: Serialize + schemars::JsonSchema;
    fn command(&self) -> &'static str;
    fn data(&self) -> &Self::Data;
    fn warnings(&self) -> &[Warning] { &[] }
    fn commands(&self) -> &[CommandHint] { &[] }
    fn partial(&self) -> bool { false }
    /// --check / --strict: Some(check_failed error) turns the result into ok:false, exit 6, data kept.
    fn assertion_failure(&self) -> Option<Error> { None }
    fn render_human(&self, w: &mut dyn std::io::Write, style: &Style) -> std::io::Result<()>;
}
```

**Modes** (`term.rs`, resolved once into an `OutputConfig`; the CLI-skeleton bead stores it in `Context`):
- `OutputMode { Json, Human }`: `--json`, `--robot` and `--format json` select Json, and `--format human` selects Human. Flags beat `OMADDONS_FORMAT=json|human`. The default is Human. `resolve_output_mode_from_argv(&[OsString])` also works on raw argv, because the CLI must know the mode even when clap fails to parse.
- `StderrMode { Ndjson, Human }`: Ndjson when stderr is not a TTY (`std::io::IsTerminal`), when `CI` is set and non-empty, or when `TERM=dumb`; otherwise Human.
- `ProgressMode { Json, Human, None }`: an explicit `--progress json|human|none` always wins (the widget passes `--json --progress json`). Otherwise `--no-progress`, `--json`, a set `CI`, or a non-TTY stderr give None, and anything else gives Human.
- Color is off when `NO_COLOR` is set and non-empty, with `--no-color`, `--json`, `TERM=dumb`, a set `CI`, or a non-TTY stderr. `Style` carries the color flag and the verbosity (`-v` count, `--quiet`).

**emit** (`mod.rs`): `pub fn emit<O: Outcome>(cfg: &OutputConfig, reporter: &mut Reporter, started: Instant, offline: bool, result: Result<O, Error>) -> Exit`.
- Ok with no assertion failure → exit 0. In Json mode, write the success envelope to stdout. In Human mode, call `render_human` on stdout. Warnings go to the reporter (stderr) in both modes.
- Ok with an assertion failure → exit 6. In Json mode, the envelope has `ok:false`, `data` and `error`. In Human mode, render the data on stdout and the error on stderr.
- Err → exit = `error.code.exit()`. In Json mode, write the failure envelope to stdout. In Human mode, stdout stays empty. Either way, mirror the error to stderr once.
- `--quiet` suppresses `log`, `progress` and `warning` lines on stderr, never errors, and never changes stdout.
- `emit_help<D>` provides the same path for help data (the CLI-skeleton bead renders help through it).

**Reporter** (`stderr.rs`): the only stderr writer. NDJSON event shapes (wire names; M4 pins them):
- `{"event":"progress","phase":"download","message":"…","current":123,"total":456}` (current and total optional)
- `{"event":"log","level":"info|debug","message":"…"}` (`debug` lines only with `-v`)
- `{"event":"warning","code":"…","message":"…","fix":"…","fix_argv":[…]|null}`
- `{"event":"error","code":"…","message":"…","fix":"…","fix_argv":[…]|null,"retryable":false,"exit_code":3}`

In Human stderr mode:
- warnings render as `warning: <message>`, plus `  fix: <fix>` when present;
- errors render as `error[<code>]: <message>`, then `fix: <fix>`, then `  or: <alternative>` for each alternative;
- progress renders as a single updating line only when ProgressMode is Human.

**Human rendering helpers** (`human.rs`): `Style::bold/dim/warn` that are no-ops without color, a table formatter for aligned columns, and a `paths_visible()` check (`-v`) for token-frugal output.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `src/output/` exports `Envelope`, `Outcome`, `OutputMode`, `StderrMode`, `ProgressMode`, `OutputConfig`, `Style`, `Reporter` and `emit`.
- A success envelope serializes with keys in the order `ok, schema_version, tool_version, command, exit_code, partial, data, warnings, commands, meta`, and a failure envelope in the order `ok, schema_version, tool_version, command, exit_code, error, warnings, commands, meta`. A `check_failed` envelope has `ok:false`, `exit_code:6`, `partial`, `data` and `error`.
- A data struct with fields declared `zeta, alpha` serializes in that order, and a `BTreeMap` inside it serializes with sorted keys.
- In Json mode stdout contains exactly one JSON document and a newline, for success, for every failure and for `check_failed`. In Human mode stdout is empty on failure.
- With stderr not a TTY, every stderr line produced by `emit` parses as JSON with an `event` key in `progress|log|warning|error`, and each error appears exactly once.
- Mode resolution follows the precedence above. Each of `NO_COLOR`, `CI`, `TERM=dumb`, `--no-color` and non-TTY detection disables color. `--progress json` overrides the `--json` implication. `--quiet` drops warning, log and progress events but never errors.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit:
  - mode-resolution truth tables, with environment variables and TTY flags injected through a `TermEnv` struct rather than read globally, so tests stay hermetic;
  - envelope key order;
  - `check_failed` shape;
  - generic serialization keeps declaration order;
  - `Reporter` line format in both stderr modes, writing into `Vec<u8>` sinks.
- Snapshot: insta JSON snapshots of success, failure, `check_failed` and partial-success envelopes. Strip `meta` with an insta redaction (`".meta" => "[meta]"`), matching how M4's golden diffs will ignore volatile fields.
- E2E: deferred to the CLI-skeleton bead, which runs the binary. This bead's tests call `emit` with in-memory writers (stdout and stderr are `&mut dyn Write` parameters internally).
- Log test inputs and outputs on failure.

## Considerations

- Broken pipe: writing to a closed stdout (e.g. `| head`) must not panic. Treat `ErrorKind::BrokenPipe` as success for stdout writes.
- The panic hook (CLI-skeleton bead) reuses the failure-envelope path. It must never emit a second stdout document if the success envelope was already written, so `emit` exposes an "stdout written" flag that the hook can check.
- No ANSI escape codes ever reach stdout in Json mode, and none reach stderr in Ndjson mode.
- Out of scope: the doctor's top-level report shapes (M4), `robot-docs` formats (M4), the progress events the engine emits (engine and command beads call `Reporter::progress`), and NDJSON `--progress json` coverage of long operations (M3).
acceptance_criteria: src/output/ exports Envelope, Outcome, OutputMode, StderrMode, ProgressMode, OutputConfig, Style, Reporter and emit; success envelopes serialize ok, schema_version, tool_version, command, exit_code, partial, data, warnings, commands, meta in that order and failure envelopes ok, schema_version, tool_version, command, exit_code, error, warnings, commands, meta, while check_failed envelopes carry ok:false, exit_code 6, partial, data and error; struct data keeps declaration order and BTreeMap keys are sorted; in Json mode stdout holds exactly one JSON document plus newline for success, failure and check_failed, and in Human mode stdout is empty on failure; with a non-TTY stderr every stderr line is JSON with event in progress|log|warning|error and each error appears exactly once; mode resolution honors flags over OMADDONS_FORMAT, NO_COLOR/CI/TERM=dumb/--no-color/non-TTY disable color, --progress json overrides the --json implication, and --quiet drops warning, log and progress events but never errors; argc gate passes
close_reason: src/output renders every command result: the stdout envelope (one document under JSON, success/failure/check_failed with the vision's key order, declaration-order data), human rendering helpers, the Reporter (NDJSON or human stderr, each error mirrored once, --quiet), and hermetic mode resolution for output, stderr, progress and color

comments.text: **error-registry landed (src/error.rs): notes for the envelope.** Key order: serde_json has no `preserve_order`, so routing a struct through `serde_json::Value` sorts its keys alphabetically. Serialize envelope structs directly with `to_writer`/`to_string` to keep declaration order (D17 determinism), and keep `data: serde_json::Value` only for already-ordered payloads, or make `data` generic. A `top_level_keys(text)` test helper in src/error.rs reads keys in serialized order. Types to render: `Error` serializes as ErrorBody `{code,message,fix,fix_argv,alternatives,retryable,details}`; `Warning` as `{code,message,fix,fix_argv}` with nulls; `CommandHint` as `{action,command,argv,destructive}`. Use `Error::exit()` → `Exit` → `ExitCode::from(exit)` for the process status, and `internal_fix()` for the panic hook's fix (DEC-5).

comments.author: BoldKettle
comments.text: **Implementation decisions (src/output/{mod,envelope,human,stderr,term,tests}.rs).** (1) `emit(cfg, reporter, command, started, offline, result)` takes the canonical `command`: a failure has no Outcome to ask for one. `emit_to(..)` takes an explicit stdout (tests); `emit` locks the real stdout. `emit_help(cfg, stdout, started, data, text)` renders help as data. (2) Output precedence: `--format` > `--json`/`--robot` > `OMADDONS_FORMAT` > human. Raw-argv resolution (`resolve_output_mode_from_argv`) applies the same rules and ignores arguments after `--`. (3) Color: the base conditions are NO_COLOR, --no-color, JSON output, TERM=dumb, CI, or a non-TTY stderr. Stdout color (`Style.color`) also needs a TTY stdout, and stderr color (`OutputConfig.stderr_color`) only applies in human stderr mode. (4) Progress rendering follows ProgressMode alone, so `--progress json` writes JSON progress lines even when other stderr lines are human. Debug log lines need -v. --quiet drops warning, log and progress but never error. (5) Every stdout write error, not just BrokenPipe, is ignored and the exit status stands, since there is nowhere to report it. `output::stdout_written()` tells the panic hook whether a document already went out. (6) The envelope snapshots use a fixed Meta and a masked tool_version instead of insta redactions, so no new insta feature was needed and version bumps do not churn them. (7) `OutputFlags` (json, robot, format, progress, no_color, no_progress, quiet, verbose) is what the CLI fills; `TermEnv::from_process()` reads the environment once; `resolve(&flags, &env)` → OutputConfig.

title: Epic: M1 fsx single writer, locks and state
description:
## Background

omaddons promises that no operation can leave an addon half-installed, that crashes recover, and that the widget, a terminal and an agent can mutate concurrently (vision G3, D23–D26). Those promises rest on three foundations this epic delivers:

1. **fsx, the single writer** (`src/fsx/`). Every filesystem mutation in the program goes through one module with a closed `Op` enum, a write-scope table, a deny-list, a `mutate()` pipeline that hashes, backs up and logs each action, and a separate `prune()` that is the only deletion path. A test fails if `std::fs` write, rename, remove or create calls appear anywhere else in `src/`.
2. **Locks** (`src/fsx/lock.rs`). One global flock held only for the commit window (milliseconds), plus a per-transaction in-flight flock that proves a transaction is alive. A held flock is the only proof of liveness anywhere in the program (D23). The lock file is immutable: never renamed, truncated away or deleted, because a re-created file is a new inode and therefore a second, independent lock.
3. **State** (`src/state/`). XDG paths, schema-versioned JSON state files with forward migration and a newer-version guard, target records with generations, the per-file index, the append-only `history.jsonl`, the monotonic `status.json`, and `config.toml` with `config get|set|path`.

Placeholders used in this epic and its children: `<home>` is the user's home directory; `<config>` is `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME` (default `.config` under the home directory); `<state>` is `$XDG_STATE_HOME` (default `.local/state`); `<cache>` is `$XDG_CACHE_HOME` (default `.cache`); `<client dir>` is the directory holding a client's `Interface/` and `WTF/`.

## Goals

- `paths`: one place that names every file in vision §5.6 and every client-dir path under `Interface/.omaddons/`.
- `fsx-primitives`: atomic write (unique temp + fsync + rename), `renameat2` with `RENAME_EXCHANGE`/`RENAME_NOREPLACE` and an honest fallback signal, reflink clone with byte-copy fallback, atomic symlink, directory fsync, and the debug-only failpoint facility (DEC-7).
- `fsx-mutate`: the closed `Op` enum, the write-scope table, the deny-list, `WriteSession` (transaction vs untracked, DEC-10) and the `mutate()` pipeline with `actions.jsonl`.
- `fsx-prune-guard`: `prune()` with a closed set of reasons and the single-writer enforcement test.
- `fsx-lock`: the global lock and in-flight locks.
- `state-store`: `StateFile<T>` with `schema_version`, migrations, `state_version_older`/`state_version_newer` warnings and the `state_too_new` refusal (DEC-4).
- `state-records`: `targets/<key>.json`, `targets/<key>.files.json`, `history.jsonl`, `status.json`.
- `config`: `config.toml` typed loading, `config get|set|path`, credential references and limit overrides.

## Success Criteria

When every child is closed:
- `tests/single_writer.rs` passes: no file under `src/` outside `src/fsx/` calls a `std::fs` mutation API, and `prune(` is called only from allowlisted modules.
- Every `Op` variant is exercised by unit tests, and a write outside the scope table or onto the deny-list is refused with exit 4 (`scope_denied` or `protected_folder`).
- Two processes contending for the global lock serialize; a third times out after `LOCK_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT` (5 s) with `locked` (exit 5); killing the holder with SIGKILL frees the lock; the lock file's inode never changes.
- A state file written by a newer schema is read but never written (`state_too_new`, exit 4); an older one migrates forward on the next save.
- `history.jsonl` survives a torn last line; `status.json` is never overwritten by a writer with older generations.
- `omaddons config set <k> <v>` preserves comments and key order in `config.toml`.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Non-Goals

- The transaction engine itself (journal, swap, commit, undo) — epic E6. This epic gives it the writer, the locks and the state files.
- Stored plans (`plans/<plan_id>.json`) — M4. The path is named here; nothing reads or writes it in M1.
- Doctor run artifacts and doctor fixers — M4. `WriteSession::tx` is designed so a doctor `repair` transaction can use it later.
- Credential use by sources (CurseForge, Wago) — M5. `config` resolves credential references; nothing in M1 sends them.
- `net.log` content and rotation — epic E5 (`net-core`), which appends through an untracked fsx session.

## Considerations

- fsx is on the hot path of every mutation, including the lock-hold window that must stay under 50 ms on fixtures. Hashing and backups for large folders happen before the lock is taken wherever possible (the engine computes per-file indexes during extraction, so directory ops reuse them).
- `RENAME_EXCHANGE` and reflink are unavailable on some filesystems (NTFS via ntfs-3g, some FUSE). Primitives must report "unsupported" rather than silently degrade, so the engine can report `atomic_swap: false`.
- The development machine's game, state and config directories are all btrfs; tests must also pass on tmpfs (test tempdirs often live there), where reflink falls back to byte copy.
- The single-writer test is a grep over source text. It must be strict enough to catch aliases (`use std::fs as f`) but must not flag reads (`fs::read`, `fs::metadata`).
acceptance_criteria: tests/single_writer.rs passes and prune( is called only from allowlisted modules; every Op variant is unit-tested and out-of-scope or deny-listed writes are refused with exit 4 (scope_denied or protected_folder); global lock contention serializes, times out with locked (exit 5) after 5 s, is freed by SIGKILL of the holder, and the lock file inode never changes; newer-schema state files are never written (state_too_new, exit 4) and older ones migrate forward on save; history.jsonl tolerates a torn last line and status.json is never overwritten by older generations; config set preserves comments and key order; argc gate passes
close_reason: All eight children closed: paths, fsx primitives, mutate, prune guard, locks, state store, state records and config; the single-writer test, lock contention, state migration guards, history and status rules and comment-preserving config set are each covered by their child's tests

title: config.toml loading, config get/set/path command, and credential/limit references
description:
## Background

`<config>/omaddons/config.toml` holds the product configuration (vision §5.6): extra discovery roots, target overrides, the default target and channel, the running policy, `auto_backup`, per-source enable flags, the check interval, the archive and retention limits that are marked "config" in §5.13, and credentials **by reference** (an environment variable name, a file path, or a `key_command` argv run without a shell — never the secret itself). The widget never duplicates any of it (vision §5.11).

It is read with the `toml` crate into a typed struct, and `omaddons config set` edits it with `toml_edit`, so a user's comments and key order survive. The CLI surface is `omaddons config [get <k> | set <k> <v> | path]` (vision §5.9), every form with `--json`.

Placeholders: `<config>` = `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME` (default `.config` under the home directory).

## Technical Approach

Files: `src/state/config.rs` (model, load, set, credential resolution) and `src/app/config.rs` + the `config` clap subcommand in `src/cli.rs` (DEC-1: this bead adds its own subcommand).

### Keys (typed `Config` struct, all optional, defaults applied in code)

```toml
extra_roots = ["<path to a WoW root>"] # extra discovery roots (absolute paths)
default_target = "retail"             # id, key or any -t form
default_channel = "stable"            # stable | beta | alpha
running_policy = "safe"               # safe | refuse | allow
auto_backup = "off"                   # off | daily  (stored now, used in M3)
check_interval_hours = 6              # 0–48; DEFAULT_CHECK_INTERVAL; 0 = only on panel open (widget, M3)
git_hosts = []                        # extra https git hosts allowed for git: refs (source-git-hosts)

[limits]                              # only the constants marked "config" in src/limits.rs
archive_max_entries = 20000
archive_max_uncompressed = "1GiB"     # integer bytes or a KiB/MiB/GiB string
archive_max_ratio = 200
download_max_bytes = "512MiB"
tx_retention_count = 10               # TX_RETENTION: last N per target within the window
tx_retention_days = 7                 # the 24 h age protection is not configurable
snapshot_max_bytes = "2GiB"
blob_cache_max_bytes = "1GiB"

[sources.github]                      # per-source enable flags; keyless sources default to enabled
enabled = true
[sources.curseforge]                  # optional sources default to disabled (M5)
enabled = false
credential = { env = "OMADDONS_CURSEFORGE_KEY" }        # or { file = "…" } or { command = ["pass", "show", "curseforge"] }

[targets.retail]                      # target overrides, keyed by id or key
label = "Main"
family = "mainline"                   # override a misdetected family (selects the ClientRules row)

[client_rules.<row-id>]               # ClientRules row overrides (field subset), see rules-tables
```

- Decided: `git_hosts` is defined here now (the `source-git-hosts` bead consumes it) so the config schema is complete in M1.
- Decided: `[targets.<id>]` overrides are limited to `label` and `family` in M1; the vision names "target overrides" without fields, and these two cover misdetection and naming. Other fields are rejected as unknown keys.
- `[client_rules.*]` deserializes into `rules::ClientRulesOverride` (defined by `rules-tables`) and is applied through `RulesTable::with_overrides`. The version→family table override uses the same mechanism if `rules-tables` exposes one.
- Size values accept an integer (bytes) or a string with a `KiB`/`MiB`/`GiB` suffix; ranges are validated (`archive_max_ratio` ≥ 1, `check_interval_hours` 0–48, sizes > 0).

### Loading

- `Config::load(paths) -> Result<(Config, Vec<Warning>)>`: a missing file is the default config. Invalid TOML or a wrongly typed value → `state_corrupt` (exit 1) with `details: {path, line, column}` and a message citing the line, fix display "edit <path>" with `argv: null`. Decided: a broken config fails commands loudly rather than being ignored, except `help` and `config path`, which never load it.
- Unknown keys produce a warning `config_unknown_key` (new warning code, recorded with DEC-4's additions) naming the key and the closest known key; they never fail the load.
- `EffectiveLimits::from(&Config)` merges `[limits]` over the `src/limits.rs` constants, using the constants bead's `LimitInfo` registry so only constants marked config-overridable can be set. The engine and archive inspection read limits from here, never from constants directly.
- The app layer loads config once per invocation and passes it through `Context` consumers (discovery gets `extra_roots`; the running policy gets `running_policy`; install gets `default_target`/`default_channel`).

### `config set <k> <v>`

- Keys are dotted paths (`limits.snapshot_max_bytes`, `sources.github.enabled`, `targets.retail.label`). Unknown key → `usage` (exit 2) with fix = the closest valid key (Levenshtein ≤ 2) or `omaddons config` to list keys.
- The value is parsed according to the key's type (bool, integer, size, enum, string, string list given as a TOML array literal such as `'["codeberg.org"]'`); invalid → `usage` naming the accepted values.
- Edit with `toml_edit::DocumentMut`: change only the target item, creating tables as needed, preserving comments, whitespace and key order elsewhere.
- Concurrency: decided — hold the global lock (`fsx::lock`) for the read-modify-write (milliseconds), so two concurrent `config set` calls cannot lose an update.
- Write via `fsx::mutate` in an untracked `WriteSession` with `Writer::Config` (DEC-10); create `<config>/omaddons/` with `ensure_dir_all` if missing. `config set` is not a transaction and is not recorded in history.
- `--dry-run` returns the same data with `dry_run: true` and writes nothing.

### `config get <k>`, bare `config`, `config path`

- `get`: `data = {key, value, source: "file"|"default", default}`.
- bare `config`: `data = {path, exists, settings: [{key, value, source}]}`, sorted by key; credentials are shown as their reference (`{"env": "OMADDONS_CURSEFORGE_KEY"}`), never resolved.
- `path`: `data = {path, exists}`.
- Human renderers print `key = value` lines.

### Credential references

- `resolve_credential(&CredentialRef) -> Result<Secret>`: `env` → read the variable (missing → `auth_required`); `file` → read and trim (warn if the mode is not 0600 — the doctor's `credential-file-mode` fixer arrives in M5); `command` → `std::process::Command::new(argv[0]).args(&argv[1..])` with no shell, stdin null, stdout captured and trimmed, stderr discarded, a 10 s timeout, non-zero exit → `auth_rejected` with the exit status (never the output).
- `Secret` wraps a `String` with `Debug`/`Display` that print `<redacted>`, no `Serialize`. Secrets are never logged, printed, or passed in a child process's argv.
- No M1 source consumes credentials (CurseForge and Wago are M5; the GitHub token comes from `OMADDONS_GITHUB_TOKEN` directly), so this is tested in isolation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A missing config file yields defaults; every key above round-trips through load.
- `omaddons config set limits.snapshot_max_bytes 3GiB` on a file with comments and custom key order changes only that value; comments and order are preserved byte-for-byte elsewhere.
- `config set` with an unknown key fails with `usage` (exit 2) and a fix naming the closest key; an invalid value fails with `usage` naming the accepted values; neither writes.
- Invalid TOML makes ordinary commands fail with `state_corrupt` citing line and column, while `omaddons config path` and `omaddons help` still work.
- An unknown key in the file produces a `config_unknown_key` warning, not a failure.
- `config get`, bare `config`, `config path` and `config set` all support `--json` with one envelope; `config set --dry-run` writes nothing.
- `EffectiveLimits` reflects `[limits]` overrides and only exposes config-overridable constants.
- `key_command = ["echo", "s3cret"]` resolves to `s3cret` without a shell; the secret never appears in any `Debug`/`Display` output or in the envelope.
- `config set` writes through `fsx::mutate` (single-writer test green) while holding the global lock.

## Test Plan

- Unit (`src/state/config.rs`): typed load of a full example file; size parsing (`"1GiB"`, `1073741824`, `"12MB"` rejected); enum validation; unknown-key warnings; `EffectiveLimits` merge; `toml_edit` set on fixtures with comments (insta snapshot of the resulting file); `Secret` redaction; credential resolution for `env`, `file`, `command` (using `echo` and `false`).
- E2E (`tests/cli_config.rs`, HOME and XDG_* set to tempdirs per DEC-6): `config path --json`, `config set` + `config get` round trip, comment preservation, unknown key and bad value failures with exit 2 and non-empty `fix`/`fix_argv`, broken TOML → other commands exit 1 with `state_corrupt` while `config path` exits 0, `--dry-run` leaves the file unchanged.
- Log test inputs and outputs on failure.

## Considerations

- Dependency note: `fsx-lock` (global lock during `config set`), `rules-tables` (`ClientRulesOverride`) and `model` (`Channel`) were added to the plan's deps for this bead.
- The new warning code `config_unknown_key` must be added to `src/error.rs` alongside DEC-4's additions and recorded in the vision comment listing contract additions.
- `extra_roots` paths are user data; tests use tempdir paths only.
- `auth <source> set|status|clear` (M5) writes credential files under `<config>/omaddons/credentials/`; this bead only reads references.
- Keep the key list in one table in code (name, type, default, description) so `config` output, validation, the closest-key suggestion and M4's capabilities all derive from it.
acceptance_criteria: a missing config file yields defaults and every documented key round-trips through load; config set on a commented file changes only the target value and preserves comments and key order elsewhere; config set with an unknown key or invalid value fails with usage (exit 2), a fix naming the closest key or accepted values, and no write; invalid TOML makes ordinary commands fail with state_corrupt citing line and column while config path and help still work; unknown keys in the file produce a config_unknown_key warning, not a failure; config, config get, config path and config set support --json with one envelope and config set --dry-run writes nothing; EffectiveLimits reflects [limits] overrides for config-overridable constants only; key_command argv resolves without a shell and the secret never appears in Debug, Display or the envelope; config set writes through fsx::mutate while holding the global lock
close_reason: config.toml loads into a typed Config (defaults, unknown-key warnings, state_corrupt with line and column), feeds discovery, the rules table and target overrides, and is read and edited by omaddons config [get|set|path]: set preserves comments and order, validates fully, writes under the lock through fsx, and supports --dry-run. Credential references resolve without a shell and secrets never print

title: Global lock and per-transaction in-flight locks in src/fsx/lock.rs
description:
## Background

omaddons lets the widget, a terminal and an agent mutate concurrently (G3). Two lock kinds make that safe (vision §5.5, D23, D24):

- **The global lock** `<state>/omaddons/lock` serializes the commit window of every transaction: revalidate → journal → swap → commit. It is held for milliseconds, never across network I/O (plan, download and stage happen without it), so `locked` (exit 5) is practically unreachable.
- **In-flight locks** `<state>/omaddons/inflight/<tx>.lock` are held by each transaction from planning until cleanup. Stage dirs, temporary blobs and stored plans carry the tx or plan id; an artifact is orphaned only if its in-flight lock is free or missing.

D23, the rule this bead enforces: **liveness is proven only by held flocks.** A flock is tied to an open file description of one inode and the kernel releases it when the holder exits, so "lock free" proves the writer is gone and "lock held" proves it is alive. Journal recovery therefore happens only by a process holding the global lock, and readers merely probe it. The lock file is **immutable**: created once and never renamed, truncated away, quarantined or deleted by anything, including `gc` — renaming or deleting a locked file and re-creating it yields a new inode and therefore a second, independent lock, which would let two writers commit at once. The reference design had a `lock-orphaned` fixer that quarantined the lock file; revision 2 removed it for exactly this reason.

DEC-9: the lock code lives in `src/fsx/lock.rs`. fsx owns every byte written, including the holder info written in place through the locked handle, and the lock file is on fsx's deny-list for every `Op`.

Placeholder: `<state>` = `$XDG_STATE_HOME` (default `.local/state` under the home directory).

## Technical Approach

File: `src/fsx/lock.rs`, using `fs4` (feature `sync`, already in `Cargo.toml`) for `flock`, `Paths` (paths bead) and `LOCK_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT` (constants bead, 5 s).

```rust
pub struct GlobalLock;                       // namespace
pub struct GlobalLockGuard { file: File, acquired_at: Instant }   // releases on drop
impl GlobalLock {
    pub fn acquire(paths: &Paths, command: &str) -> Result<GlobalLockGuard>;     // waits up to LOCK_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT
    pub fn acquire_with_timeout(paths: &Paths, command: &str, t: Duration) -> Result<GlobalLockGuard>;
}
pub fn probe_global(paths: &Paths) -> Result<LockState>;   // non-blocking; never creates, never writes
pub enum LockState { Free, Held { holder: Option<HolderInfo> }, Missing }
pub struct HolderInfo { pub pid: u32, pub command: String, pub started_at: jiff::Timestamp }

pub struct InflightLock { file: File, tx: TxId }   // releases on drop
impl InflightLock {
    pub fn create(paths: &Paths, tx: &TxId) -> Result<InflightLock>;  // creates inflight/<tx>.lock, takes it exclusively
    pub fn is_live(paths: &Paths, tx: &TxId) -> Result<bool>;          // true iff someone holds it (try_lock fails)
}
```

Global lock rules:
- **Open, never replace.** `acquire` opens `<state>/omaddons/lock` with read+write and `create(true)` but without truncation (`OpenOptions::new().read(true).write(true).create(true)`, mode 0644). Missing parent directories (`<state>/omaddons/`) are created with `fsx::sys::create_dir` one level at a time; this is fsx-internal code, so it does not need a `WriteSession`, and it keeps this bead independent of `fsx-mutate`. The file is never opened with `truncate`, never renamed, never unlinked by any code path.
- **Acquire with timeout.** Poll `try_lock_exclusive` with short sleeps (start 5 ms, cap 50 ms) until `LOCK_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT`; on timeout return `Error { code: locked, … }` (exit 5, retryable) with `details: {holder: {pid, command, started_at}}` read from the file (best effort) and fix = the same argv retried (the caller's argv from `Context`).
- **Holder info in place.** After acquiring, write `{"pid":…,"command":"install","started_at":"…"}` + newline at offset 0 through the locked handle (`set_len(0)` then `write_all`, same inode). This is for diagnosis only (doctor's `lock-held-long` in M4 reports it); nothing trusts it for liveness. It is the one write in the program that does not go through `mutate()`, and it is allowed because it lives inside `src/fsx/` and only touches the lock file through the handle that holds the lock.
- **Release** on `Drop` (and an explicit `release()`); holder info is left as is (stale info is harmless; the flock is the truth). Record `acquired_at` so callers can log hold time (the engine targets < 50 ms per commit on fixtures).
- **Probe for readers** (`probe_global`): open read-only if the file exists (`Missing` otherwise, without creating it — read commands never write), `try_lock_shared`; if that fails the lock is `Held` (read holder info); if it succeeds, release immediately and report `Free`. Readers use this to choose between the warnings `journal_pending` (lock free, journals exist) and `tx_in_progress` (lock held).

In-flight lock rules:
- `create` makes `inflight/` if needed (`fsx::sys::create_dir`), creates `<tx>.lock` exclusively (`create_new`), takes an exclusive flock and keeps the handle in the returned guard for the whole transaction (planning through cleanup).
- `is_live(tx)`: missing file → `false`; `try_lock_exclusive` fails → `true` (held by a live process); succeeds → release, `false`. Orphan detection elsewhere (stage dirs, temp blobs, plans) calls this.
- Deleting `<tx>.lock` after the transaction is `prune(PostCommitCleanup)`'s job, after the guard is dropped.

Re-entrancy: flocks are per open file description, so acquiring the global lock twice in one process deadlocks against itself until timeout. The API makes this hard: the engine passes `&GlobalLockGuard` down instead of re-acquiring (see `prune(…, LockUse::Held(&guard))`). Document it on `acquire`.

Failpoints (DEC-7): `fsx.lock.acquired` (after the flock, before the holder write) and `fsx.lock.holder_written`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Two processes calling `GlobalLock::acquire` serialize: the second waits and acquires after the first releases.
- With the lock held by another process, `acquire_with_timeout(…, 200 ms)` returns `locked` (exit 5, retryable) after about 200 ms, with holder pid and command in `details`.
- Killing the holder with SIGKILL frees the lock immediately for the next acquirer.
- The lock file's inode (`st_ino`, `st_dev`) is identical before and after many acquire/release cycles, crashes and holder-info writes.
- `probe_global` reports `Held` while another process holds the lock, `Free` otherwise, and `Missing` without creating the file when it does not exist.
- `InflightLock::is_live` is `true` while the creating process holds it and `false` after that process exits (including by SIGKILL).
- No code path opens the lock file with truncate, renames it or unlinks it (grep-asserted in a unit test over `src/`).

## Test Plan

- Unit (`src/fsx/lock.rs`): holder-info JSON round trip; probe on missing file creates nothing.
- Integration (`tests/fsx_lock.rs`): use child processes (re-exec the test binary selecting an `#[ignore]`d helper test by name, or `std::process::Command` on the built `omaddons` binary once a debug-only helper exists) so locks are held by a different open file description:
  - contention + serialization (timestamps show non-overlapping hold windows);
  - timeout → `locked` with details;
  - SIGKILL of the holder → immediate acquisition;
  - inode stability across 100 cycles;
  - `is_live` before/after holder exit;
  - `fsx.lock.acquired=sleep:500` in a child while the parent probes → `Held`.
- Log test inputs and outputs on failure.

## Considerations

- Dependency note: `model` was added to this bead's blocking deps (the plan listed only primitives, paths and constants) because `InflightLock` is keyed by `TxId`.
- Threads in one process sharing one `File` share one flock; tests must use separate processes (or at least separately opened files) to model real contention.
- NFS and some FUSE filesystems emulate flock poorly. `<state>` is local on the supported setups (the development machine uses btrfs); do not add workarounds.
- `locked` should almost never happen because the lock is held only for the commit window; if it shows up in practice, look for something holding the lock across I/O.
- The doctor's `lock-held-long` (M4) reads holder info and reports it; it never touches the file. Keep the holder-info format stable (it is pinned by the wire-name golden in M4).
acceptance_criteria: two processes acquiring the global lock serialize; with the lock held elsewhere acquire_with_timeout returns locked (exit 5, retryable) with holder pid and command in details; SIGKILL of the holder frees the lock immediately; the lock file's inode is unchanged across many acquire/release cycles, crashes and holder writes; probe_global reports Held, Free, or Missing without creating the file; InflightLock::is_live is true while held and false after the holder exits, including by SIGKILL; no code path opens the lock file with truncate, renames it or unlinks it
close_reason: src/fsx/lock.rs provides the immutable global flock with in-place holder info and timeout → locked (exit 5), a read-only probe (Missing/Free/Held), and per-transaction in-flight locks with is_live; no code path truncates, renames or unlinks the lock file

comments.author: BoldKettle
comments.text: **Implementation decisions (src/fsx/lock.rs).** (1) Locking uses std's `File::lock`/`try_lock`/`try_lock_shared`/`unlock` (stable since 1.89, flock(2) on Linux, so locks belong to the open file description as D23 needs) instead of fs4. fs4 1.1 only mirrors that API, and std's inherent methods would shadow it anyway, so fs4 is removed from Cargo.toml (gate --all, cargo deny ok). (2) `locked`'s fix is text (wait, then retry). The command layer replaces it with the caller's exact argv via `err.fix = Suggestion::command(argv)` (Error derefs mutably). details.holder carries {pid, command, started_at} or null. (3) The lock file opens with read+write+create+`truncate(false)`, mode 0644. Holder info is rewritten in place (`set_len(0)`, seek, write) through the locked handle; it is never fsynced, being diagnosis only. (4) `probe_global` opens read-only without creating and uses `try_lock_shared`, returning Missing/Free/Held{holder}. `InflightLock::create` uses create_new (one lock per tx) and `is_live` uses try_lock (missing → false). (5) The bookkeeping mkdir helper moved to `fsx::sys::create_dir_all`, shared by the lock and mutate. (6) Failpoints: `fsx.lock.acquired` and `fsx.lock.holder_written`. (7) A unit test reads the non-test part of src/ and asserts that only src/fsx/lock.rs, src/fsx/scope.rs (deny-list) and src/state/paths.rs mention lock_file, and that lock.rs never truncates on open, removes, renames or prunes. (8) tests/fsx_lock.rs re-execs the test binary as the lock holder (helpers live in a cfg(test) module so clippy's unwrap-in-tests exemption applies). It covers serialization, the 200 ms timeout with holder details, SIGKILL release in < 500 ms, inode stability over 100 cycles plus a crash, Missing/Held/Free with the env failpoint holding the lock, and in-flight liveness across SIGKILL.
