title: Epic: M1 commands and checkpoint verification
description:
## Background

M1 ("working slice", vision omad-vision-8qa §7) ends when a user or an agent can install, reinstall-to-update, remove and undo addons from keyless GitHub, git, URL and local sources into every discovered target, including WoW: Forever and legacy private-server clients, through the final transaction engine and the core CLI contract. The other M1 epics build the parts: the contract core and domain model (E1), fsx, locks and state (E2), discovery and target identity (E3), ClientRules and the TOC engine (E4), the network layer and sources (E5), and the transaction engine (E6). This epic turns those parts into the commands people and agents actually run, then proves the milestone against its checkpoint list.

The M1 command set (vision §7 M1 "Commands"): `install` (including reinstall-to-update), `remove`, `undo`, `history`, `status` (offline triage: targets, records, running state, warnings), `list`, `targets`, `info` (no changelog), `config` (owned by the E2 config bead), `net-log`, and `--dry-run` on every mutating command (plan output only; stored plans and `apply` are M4).

Every command follows the contract core from E1: under `--json` (or `--format json`, `--robot`, `OMADDONS_FORMAT=json`) stdout carries exactly one envelope, success or failure; stderr carries NDJSON events when it is not a TTY; every error has a non-empty `fix` plus `fix_argv`; exit codes come from the general dictionary (0 ok, 1 failed, 2 usage, 3 not_found, 4 refused, 5 locked, 6 check_failed). Each command bead adds its own clap subcommand and `src/app/<cmd>.rs` (DEC-1); commands receive a `Context` and return an `Outcome`, and never print (DEC-2).

WoW: Forever launches 2026-11-04. M1 is scoped to land before it, so the Forever-critical commands (`install`, `remove`, `undo`, `status`) are P1.

## Goals

- Ship `install`, `remove`, `undo`, `history`, `status`, `list`, `targets`, `info` and `net-log` with defined `--json` `data` schemas and human renderers.
- Make the target-default rules concrete: read commands default to all targets; `install` uses the configured default target, else the single compatible live target, else `target_ambiguous` with exact fix commands.
- Prove the CLI contract across every M1 command with one conformance suite (one stdout envelope, `fix` + `fix_argv`, NDJSON stderr, exit codes match the dictionary, every exit site maps to a published code).
- Fuzz every M1 parser and the archive inspector.
- Run the M1 checkpoint list from the vision against fixtures, synthetic trees, live endpoints and the development machine, and update README.md to describe exactly what exists.

## Success Criteria

When every child is closed:
- Every vision §7 M1 checkpoint is checked off with recorded evidence (test names, command output, timings) in the m1-checkpoint bead's close reason and a comment on omad-vision-8qa.
- `omaddons <cmd> --json | jq -e .ok` distinguishes success from failure for every M1 command.
- The contract suite, discovery matrix, TOC matrix and engine failure-injection suite pass inside `argc gate`.
- Each fuzz target has run for at least 10 minutes without a crash.
- README.md describes the M1 command set as it exists, and nothing more.

## Non-Goals

- `outdated`, `update`, `pin`/`unpin`, `adopt`, `search`, `export`/`sync`/`copy`, dependency installs, WoWInterface and Tukui sources, `info --changelog` (M2).
- The Omarchy widget, `errors`, `backup`, `--progress json` streaming for long operations (M3).
- `capabilities`, `robot-docs`, verb aliases and intent inference beyond the CLI-skeleton's closest-command fix, stored plans and `apply`, the wire-name golden, the `doctor` surface (M4).
- CurseForge, Wago, `auth`, release engineering (M5).

## Considerations

- Commands are thin: resolution, planning, locking and committing live in the engine (E6); the command layer parses arguments, resolves targets through the registry, calls the engine, and shapes the outcome. Logic that belongs in the engine must not be duplicated in a command.
- `data` structs derive `Serialize` and `schemars::JsonSchema` from day one (DEC-3), so M4's `robot-docs schema` and the wire-name golden need no retrofit. Field order is wire order; maps are `BTreeMap`.
- The contract freezes at M4's first tag. Until then, renaming a `data` key is allowed but must update the insta snapshots and the bead that owns the schema.
- Real-machine checks touch the development machine's real AddOns folders. They must undo every transaction they create and leave the machine as they found it, apart from target keys and markers, which M1 expects to be written on first mutation.
- Public-safe bead text: paths are written with placeholders (`<home>`, `<config>`, `<state>`, `<cache>`, `<client dir>`).
acceptance_criteria: Every vision §7 M1 checkpoint is checked off with recorded evidence in the m1-checkpoint close reason and a comment on omad-vision-8qa; omaddons <cmd> --json | jq -e .ok distinguishes success from failure for every M1 command; the contract suite, discovery matrix, TOC matrix and engine failure-injection suite pass inside argc gate; each fuzz target has run at least 10 minutes without a crash; README.md describes exactly the M1 command set that exists
close_reason: All children completed

title: Implement the info and net-log commands
description:
## Background

Two small read commands round out M1:

- `info <ref|addon>` answers "what is this addon and what would I get?": the installed records across targets, the catalog entry, and the latest stable release from its source. Changelogs (`--changelog`) arrive in M2 with the WoWInterface and Tukui sources (vision §7 M1 "Commands": `info` without changelog).
- `net-log` makes the privacy claim verifiable by the user rather than asserted (vision G5, D13, §5.7): every HTTP request and git subprocess omaddons makes is logged to `<state>/omaddons/net.log`, with credentials and query secrets stripped at write time, and `omaddons net-log [--since]` renders it.

Placeholders: `<state>` = `$XDG_STATE_HOME` (default `.local/state` under the home directory).

## Technical Approach

Files: `src/app/info.rs`, `src/app/net_log.rs`, `Info` and `NetLog` subcommands in `src/cli.rs` (DEC-1).

### info

Synopsis (vision §5.9, minus M2's flag): `omaddons info <ref|addon> [-t T]`.

- Resolution through the refs bead: canonical refs, pasted URLs, installed addon names, catalog names and aliases. Bad syntax → `ref_invalid` (2); ambiguity → `ref_ambiguous` (3, candidates); nothing matches → `not_found` (3) with fix `omaddons list` (argv form).
- Installed: every managed record matching the resolved ref or name, across all targets (or the `-t` target): target id/key, version, `version_confidence`, channel, pinned, state, folders, `installed_at`, `tx`.
- Catalog: the catalog entry if the ref or name is in the catalog (name, aliases, families, folders, notes).
- Latest: one fetch through the source (`fetch_once` with a single ref), then `select` per target to report which targets have a metadata candidate. Metadata only: no archive download, no verification (so `targets` here means "has a candidate", not "verified"; the install path verifies).
- `--offline`: decided — no fetch is attempted; `latest` is null and `data.offline` is true, exit 0 (why: info's local part is still useful offline, and `offline` errors are for commands that need the network).
- Fetch failure (network, `rate_limited`, `source_disabled` for `wowi:`/`tukui:`/`cf:`/`wago:` per DEC-12): decided — partial success: exit 0, `partial: true`, `latest: null`, and the error mirrored in `warnings` with the error's own code and fix (same rule as install's per-item failures). If the ref resolves to nothing local and the fetch fails, the fetch error is the command's error.

`--json` `data` schema (`InfoData`):

```
{
  "query": string,
  "ref": string,
  "name": string | null,
  "catalog": {"name": string, "aliases": [string], "families": [string], "folders": [string], "notes": string | null} | null,
  "installed": [
    {"target": {"id": string, "key": string}, "version": string, "version_confidence": "release" | "toc",
     "channel": string, "pinned": bool, "state": "ok" | "degraded", "folders": [string], "installed_at": string, "tx": string}
  ],
  "latest": {"version": string, "release_id": string, "channel": "stable", "flavors": [string], "targets": [string]} | null,
  "offline": bool
}
```

`flavors` are the release.json flavor names (`mainline`, `classic`, `bcc`, `wrath`, `cata`, `mists`, `titan`, `forever`) when present; `targets` are ids of targets with a candidate. `-v` adds asset URLs and record paths.

Human output:

```
WeakAuras  gh:WeakAuras/WeakAuras2
  catalog: folders WeakAuras, WeakAurasOptions, … · families mainline, mists, vanilla, …
  retail: 5.19.1 (release, stable) installed 2026-10-20
  latest: 5.19.2 · candidates for retail, forever
```

Exit codes: 0, 1, 2, 3.

### net-log

Synopsis: `omaddons net-log [--since D]`.

- Reads `<state>/omaddons/net.log` and the one rotated previous file kept by the net-core bead (rotation at `NET_LOG_MAX_BYTES` = 10 MiB, keep one previous; use the file name net-core defines), oldest first.
- Each line is one JSON object written by net-core: `{time, method, host, path, status, bytes, duration_ms, purpose, via}` where `via` is `"http"` or `"git"`. Secrets were stripped at write time; this command adds no filtering of its own beyond parsing.
- `--since D`: a duration (`30m`, `12h`, `1d`, `2w`) or RFC 3339 timestamp (jiff). Invalid → `usage` (2) with fix `omaddons net-log --since 1d`. Without `--since`, every entry in both files is returned (bounded by the two 10 MiB files).
- Unparseable lines are skipped and counted (`skipped`), never fatal. A missing log is an empty result, not an error.
- `summary`: request counts per host and per `via`, so "did anything talk to a host I did not expect?" is one glance.
- Never performs network I/O; works under `--offline`.

`--json` `data` schema (`NetLogData`):

```
{
  "entries": [{"time": string, "method": string, "host": string, "path": string, "status": int | null,
               "bytes": int, "duration_ms": int, "purpose": string, "via": "http" | "git"}],
  "summary": {"by_host": {string: int}, "by_via": {string: int}},
  "skipped": int,
  "since": string | null
}
```

Human output: one line per entry (`2026-10-20T14:02:11Z  GET 302  github.com  /WeakAuras/WeakAuras2/releases/latest  0 B  85 ms  latest-tag`), then the summary.

Exit codes: 0, 2.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `omaddons info weakauras --json` with HTTP replay fixtures returns the catalog entry, `latest.version` from the fixture's release tag, `latest.flavors` from its release.json, and `latest.targets` listing the synthetic targets that have candidates.
- After installing it, `installed` lists the record for that target.
- `info weakauras --offline` returns `latest: null`, `offline: true`, exit 0, and net.log is unchanged.
- `info wowi:5108` with no local match exits 1 `source_disabled` (DEC-12) with fix `omaddons help install`.
- For an installed addon whose latest fetch fails (a replay fixture returning 503 on every retry), `info` exits 0 with `partial: true`, `latest: null`, the installed record, and the `http_status` error mirrored in `warnings`.
- `info nosuchaddon` exits 3 `not_found` with a fix.
- After a fixture install, `omaddons net-log --json` lists the GitHub requests with `via: "http"`, `summary.by_host` counts them, and no entry contains a token, `api-key`, `access_token` or an Authorization value (the test plants one in the request and asserts it is absent).
- `net-log --since 1h` filters by time; `--since nonsense` exits 2; a log with a corrupt line reports `skipped: 1`.
- `net-log` reads the rotated previous file too.

## Test Plan

- Unit: `--since` parsing (shared helper with history); net.log line decoding; summary aggregation; info partial-success folding.
- Integration (`tests/info_netlog.rs`, `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES` replay, synthetic trees, HOME/XDG_* tempdirs): the cases above; a rotated log pair written by the test.
- E2E contract: one stdout envelope per case.

## Considerations

- Added deps beyond the plan's list: `source-github-stable` (fetching `latest` for `gh:` refs needs a real source) and `select` (per-target candidates). Both are P1 beads; this bead stays P2.
- `info --changelog` (GitHub release body, WoWI `UIChangeLog`, Tukui `changelog_url`) is M2.
- `net-log` output can be long; agents should pass `--since`. Pagination is not in the M1 contract.
- Verb alias `show` → info is M4.
acceptance_criteria: info weakauras --json with replay fixtures returns the catalog entry, latest.version from the fixture tag, latest.flavors from its release.json and latest.targets listing synthetic targets with candidates; after installing it, installed lists the record; info weakauras --offline returns latest null, offline true, exit 0 and leaves net.log unchanged; info wowi:5108 with no local match exits 1 source_disabled with fix omaddons help install; an installed addon whose latest fetch fails on every retry gives exit 0 partial true, latest null, the record, and the http_status error mirrored in warnings; info nosuchaddon exits 3 not_found with a fix; after a fixture install net-log --json lists the GitHub requests with via http, summary.by_host counts them, and no entry contains a planted token, api-key, access_token or Authorization value; net-log --since 1h filters by time, --since nonsense exits 2, a corrupt line reports skipped 1, and the rotated previous file is read too
close_reason: info and net-log commands

comments.author: BoldKettle
comments.text: **net-core landed.** `net-log` reads with `NetLog::new(&paths)?.read(since)` → Vec<NetLogEntry> (net.log.1 then net.log; torn and unparseable lines skipped). Fields in wire order: time, method, host, path, status, bytes, duration_ms, purpose, via, error.

comments.author: BoldKettle
comments.text: **cli-skeleton landed: how to add this command (DEC-1).** (1) Add a variant to `cli::Command`; its doc comment becomes the 'about' in bare help, which lists commands automatically, ordered by `app::help::COMMON_VERBS`. (2) Add its canonical name to `app::COMMANDS`, so usage errors name it. (3) Add arms to `app::command_name` and `app::dispatch` that call `src/app/<cmd>.rs`, returning `Result<impl output::Outcome, Error>`; dispatch renders it with `output::emit`. `Context` provides: output, actor, reason, argv (argv[0] = omaddons, for history and fix_argv), offline (flag or OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1), dry_run (read-only commands ignore it), while_running, target (raw -t value), started. Command-specific flags go on the variant. Global flags are already accepted before or after the subcommand. tests/cli_skeleton.rs has an isolated-HOME runner (`support::run_env`) that checks every stderr line is NDJSON.

comments.author: BoldKettle
comments.text: **registry landed (src/discover/registry.rs, src/state/registry.rs).** Pipeline for a command: `discover(&input, &table)`, then `reconcile(&load_registry(&paths)?.value, &found.targets)` gives `Resolved { targets (key and id filled, key None when unregistered), warnings, missing }`. Then `resolve_one(selector, &resolved.targets, &ctx.argv)` gives target_not_found / target_ambiguous with argv fixes. To register (mutating commands, inside the transaction): `GlobalLock::acquire`, then `LockedRegistry::load(&guard, &paths)?`, then `.ensure_registered(&mut session, &target)?`. The session's ScopeTable must include the target's client dir. Read paths never write.

comments.author: BoldKettle
comments.text: **Implementation decisions (src/app/info.rs, src/app/net_log.rs, net::log::read_log).** info resolves through the same parser as install (install::parse_ref, now shared); an unknown name becomes not_found with fix argv 'omaddons list' (the parser's own fix points at install). installed = records with that ref on every discovered registered target (or -t). catalog = the entry with that ref, else by name. latest = one fetch_once of Wanted::stable, then select::newest (now pub) for version/release_id/channel, release.json flavor names deduplicated and sorted, and the ids of targets where select() returns any candidate (metadata only, as the bead says: on the dev machine 'info dbm' lists wotlk because DBM's release.json has a wrath asset; install's verification rejects it). --offline skips the fetch (latest null, offline true). A fetch error with a local match (installed or catalog) is partial (Warning::item, e.g. http_status); without one it is the command's error (wowi:5108 → source_disabled, exit 1, fix 'omaddons help install'). -v adds asset URLs and record paths. net-log uses a new read-only net::log::read_log(paths, since) → NetLogRead { entries (net.log.1 then net.log), skipped (unparseable lines) }; summary.by_host/by_via; --since shares history::parse_since. Live on the dev machine: 30 requests in the last day, all github.com/release-assets over http.

comments.author: BoldKettle
comments.text: done: argc gate passes; tests/info_netlog.rs 4 E2E (catalog + latest version/flavors/targets from replayed release.json, installed record after install, --offline leaves net.log unchanged, wowi:5108 source_disabled exit 1, 503-every-retry fetch → partial with http_status warning, nosuchaddon not_found with 'omaddons list', net-log by_host/by_via, planted access_token/api-key/token never logged while the request is, --since 1h/future/nonsense, corrupt line skipped 1, rotated file read first, no writes) + unit summary · found: none

title: Verify the M1 checkpoints: real-machine smoke, keyless installs, fuzz, probes and README
description:
## Background

Each milestone ends in a usable state: the local gate passes, README.md describes exactly what exists, and contract snapshots are updated (vision §7). This bead closes M1 by running every M1 checkpoint from the vision, recording evidence, adding the real-machine smoke tests, running the checkpoint-only checks that are not part of the per-commit gate (fuzz runs, coverage, live probes, real-machine smoke tests, benchmarks; vision §5.12), and updating README.md.

WoW: Forever launches 2026-11-04; M1 is scoped to land before it. M1 alone delivers keyless Forever support: the `release.json` flavor `forever`, the `_Forever`/`_Camelot` TOC suffixes, the Forever-loads-`_Mainline` guard, and 1.60.x family detection for both `_forever_` and `_classic_beta_`.

Placeholders: `<home>` = the user's home directory; `<state>` = `$XDG_STATE_HOME` (default `.local/state` under `<home>`).

## Technical Approach

### Development machine facts (vision §4.7, the real-world oracle)

- Retail: `<home>/Games/battlenet/drive_c/Program Files (x86)/World of Warcraft/` (Omarchy's Battle.net prefix, installed with umu-launcher and GE-Proton). `product.db` and `.build.info` both report product `wow`, version `12.1.0.69933` (interface 120100; live is 12.1.5). Only `_retail_` is installed, and its AddOns folder is empty. `dosdevices` maps `c:`, `s:`, `w:`, `x:`, `z:`.
- Custom: `<home>/Games/wow-335/drive_c/WoW/`. Wow.exe is 3.3.5a. `Interface/AddOns` holds 23 `Blizzard_*` folders and nothing else. `Data/enUS/realmlist.wtf` is `set realmlist 127.0.0.1`, a local AzerothCore server.
- Filesystems: the games directory, the XDG state dir and the XDG config dir are btrfs (reflink and `RENAME_EXCHANGE` capable).
- Toolchain present: cargo/rustc (stable pinned by the repo, nightly installed), cargo-deny, cargo-audit, cargo-llvm-cov, cargo-fuzz, hyperfine, ubs.

### Real-machine smoke tests

- `tests/real_machine.rs`, every test `#[ignore]` and additionally gated on `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE=1` (decided name; vision §5.12 says "ignored by default, enabled by an environment variable"). These tests use the real HOME and XDG dirs, never tempdirs.
- They must leave the machine as they found it: every transaction they create is undone at the end (`omaddons undo` per tx, newest first), and the test asserts each touched AddOns folder's tree hash equals its value before the test. Target keys and markers written on first mutation are expected and stay.
- Live network: the keyless install checks run with `OMADDONS_LIVE=1` against real endpoints, once, at the checkpoint.

### M1 checkpoint list (vision §7 M1, copied verbatim; each item is checked off with evidence)

- [ ] On the development machine, `omaddons status --json` reports:
  - `retail` (from `product.db` and `.build.info`; 12.1.x);
  - the 3.3.5a target (`wrath-legacy`, interface 30300, label "localhost") with 23 protected folders.

  Both receive stable keys and markers on their first mutation.
- [ ] Synthetic trees resolve correctly:
  - every product in §4.1, including `_forever_` and `_classic_beta_` at 1.60.x;
  - every legacy `ClientRules` row;
  - a game on a mapped drive letter outside `drive_c`;
  - a custom client outside any prefix;
  - each launcher config;
  - an unknown `_xyz_` folder (yields a usable `unknown` target).

A legacy addon installs into the 3.3.5a target from a git repo and from a GitHub release. `Blizzard_*` folders are untouched.

  - a failure injected at every engine step leaves each folder wholly old or wholly new;

title: Implement the install command with target defaulting, partial success, --strict and --dry-run
description:
## Background

`install` is the command M1 exists for: put an addon from a keyless source into a target, verified against that client's own TOC load rules, through the journaled transaction engine, reversible with `omaddons undo`. In M1 it also covers updating: installing an addon that is already installed, when the source has a newer release, replaces it (`kind: update`). `outdated`/`update` arrive in M2.

The engine (E6: `plan` → `stage` → `commit`) does the work. This bead is the command layer: argument parsing, target defaulting and registration, calling the engine, partial-success semantics, `--strict`, `--dry-run`, the `data` schema and the human renderer. Vision references: §5.9 (contract, behavior), §5.4 (refs, selection), §5.5 (engine), §5.1 (records).

Placeholders: `<client dir>` = the directory holding `Interface/` and `WTF/` for a target; `<state>` = `$XDG_STATE_HOME` (default `.local/state` under the home directory).

## Technical Approach

Files: `src/app/install.rs` (command), a `Install` subcommand added to `src/cli.rs` (DEC-1), human renderer in the same module or `src/output/human/install.rs`.

Synopsis (vision §5.9):

```
omaddons install <ref|url|path>... [-t T] [--channel C] [--version V] [--file <zip>] [--no-deps] [--force] [--strict]
global flags that apply: --dry-run --actor --reason --offline --while-running --json/--format/--robot -v --quiet
```

Arguments:
- Each positional is parsed by the refs bead (`src/sources/refs.rs`): canonical refs (`gh:WeakAuras/WeakAuras2`, `git:<url>[#rev]`, `url:<https-zip>`, `file:<path>`), pasted GitHub URLs, https zip URLs, local paths, installed addon names, and catalog names/aliases (`omaddons install weakauras`). `wowi:`/`tukui:`/`cf:`/`wago:` refs parse but fail at fetch with `source_disabled` (DEC-12). Bad syntax → `ref_invalid` (exit 2); ambiguity → `ref_ambiguous` (exit 3, candidates in `details`).
- `--channel stable|beta|alpha` (default: the addon's recorded channel, else config `default_channel`, else `stable`). The chosen channel is stored on the record. beta/alpha for `gh:` refs use REST (source-github-rest); until that bead lands the GitHub source reports the limitation as its own error.
- `--version V`: install that exact release. Honored for `gh:` (tag) and `git:` (rev); for `url:`/`file:` it is a `usage` error (exit 2). An unknown tag → `not_found` (exit 3).
- `--file <zip>`: install a manually obtained archive as the release of the single given ref. Decided: exactly one positional ref is allowed with `--file` (more → `usage`). In M1 no source provides an expected hash for manual files, so the archive is verified by TOC load rules only; the record keeps the ref, takes its version from the TOC `## Version` (`version_confidence: "toc"`) and sets `release_id` to null. When a later source provides an expected hash (CurseForge, M5), a mismatch is `hash_mismatch`.
- `--no-deps`: accepted and ignored in M1 (dependency resolution is M2), with no warning.
- `--force`: overrides `ownership_conflict` (moves the folder to the new addon, previous owner becomes `degraded`, warning `ownership_transferred`) and `unmanaged_folder` (snapshots and replaces the unmanaged folder). It never overrides `protected_folder` or `case_collision` (vision §5.5 step 4, D14).
- `--strict`: a partial success becomes exit 6 `check_failed` with `ok: false` and `data` still populated.

Target defaulting (vision §5.9 "Target defaults"):
1. `-t T` given → resolve through the registry's `-t` resolver (id, key, family name, product code, flavor folder name, install root, AddOns path). Not found → `target_not_found` (3); more than one match → `target_ambiguous` (3).
2. Else the configured default target (config `default_target` or the registry default).
3. Else the single compatible target. Decided: compatibility is decided by planning each requested ref against every discovered `live` target (fetch once, select, download into the blob cache, inspect, verify); `test` targets (PTR/XPTR/beta) are only ever chosen with an explicit `-t` (why: otherwise every machine with a PTR installed would make every install ambiguous; this matches `sync`'s rule that test targets are addressed only explicitly).
4. More than one compatible live target → `target_ambiguous` (3) with `details.candidates` (ids), `fix` = the original argv with `-t <first candidate>` appended, `alternatives` = the same for each other candidate. Example: `{"code":"target_ambiguous","message":"weakauras is compatible with 2 targets","fix":"omaddons install weakauras -t retail","fix_argv":["omaddons","install","weakauras","-t","retail"],"alternatives":[{"display":"omaddons install weakauras -t forever","argv":["omaddons","install","weakauras","-t","forever"]}]}`.
5. No discovered targets → `target_not_found` (3) with fix `omaddons targets add <path>` (argv null because `<path>` must be filled in). No compatible live target → `no_compatible_release` (3) listing the targets checked.

Execution:
- One transaction per command run (one target). Per-item failures discovered during planning (fetch, select, verify, ownership) are excluded; the remaining items commit atomically in one transaction. Decided: the transaction kind is `update` when every changed item is an update, else `install`.
- Registration: the first mutating run on an unregistered target assigns its key and writes its marker under the global lock (registry bead API, called from the commit path). `--dry-run` never registers.
- Idempotent: an already-current addon is `status: "unchanged"` with an empty folder change list. If nothing changes at all, no transaction is created (`tx: null`), exit 0.
- `--dry-run` (DEC-15, DEC-16): runs fetch, select, download, inspect, verify and ownership; writes only derived data (blob cache, HTTP validators); never stages into the client dir, never takes the global lock, never writes state. Output is the same `data` schema with `dry_run: true` and `tx: null`.
- Partial success (vision §5.9 exit dictionary): if at least one item succeeded or was unchanged and at least one failed, exit 0 with `partial: true`; each failure appears in `data.items[].error` and is mirrored in `warnings`. Decided: a mirrored per-item failure is a warning whose `code` is the failing item's error code (for example `no_compatible_release`) and whose `fix`/`fix_argv` are that error's fix; the `Warning` type must accept an error code as its code (coordinate with the error-registry bead; add the variant here if it is missing). If every item fails, the command fails with the first failing item's error (argument order), `details.items` listing every item's error, and that error's exit code.
- Outcome extras: when a transaction committed, `commands` contains `{"action":"undo","command":"omaddons undo <tx>","argv":["omaddons","undo","<tx>"],"destructive":false}`. When `reload_required` is `reload`, add warning `reload_required` with fix display `/reload in game` and `fix_argv: null`; when `restart`, the same warning with fix display `restart the game client`. If the engine reported `atomic_swap: false`, the engine's `atomic_swap_unavailable` warning passes through. Engine warnings (`journal_recovered`, `out_of_date`, `toc_comma_on_legacy`, `ownership_transferred`) pass through unchanged.

`--json` `data` schema (`InstallData`, field order is wire order):

```
{
  "dry_run": bool,
  "target": {"id": string, "key": string | null},   // key null only under --dry-run on an unregistered target
  "tx": string | null,                                // ULID of the committed transaction
  "kind": "install" | "update" | null,                // null when nothing changed
  "items": [
    {
      "request": string,                              // the positional exactly as given
      "ref": string | null,                           // canonical ref, null if parsing failed
      "name": string | null,                          // addon name (record key)
      "status": "installed" | "updated" | "unchanged" | "failed",
      "from_version": string | null,
      "to_version": string | null,
      "version_confidence": "release" | "toc" | null,
      "channel": "stable" | "beta" | "alpha" | null,
      "folders": {"added": [string], "replaced": [string], "removed": [string]},
      "error": {"code": string, "message": string, "fix": string, "fix_argv": [string] | null} | null
    }
  ],
  "reload_required": "none" | "reload" | "restart",
  "atomic_swap": bool | null                          // null when no swap happened
}
```

Folder lists are sorted by key; `items` keep argument order. `-v` adds `paths` (client dir) and the release asset URL per item; default output stays token-frugal.

Human output (stdout):

```
retail: installed WeakAuras 5.19.2 (3 folders)
retail: DBM-Core unchanged (11.2.5)
retail: failed BigWigs: no_compatible_release: no release verifies for mainline 120105
tx 01JB… · /reload in game · undo: omaddons undo 01JB…
```

Errors in human mode leave stdout empty; the error goes to stderr per the output bead.

Exit codes this command can return: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `omaddons install <ref> -t <id> --json` against fixtures installs the addon, prints exactly one envelope with `ok: true`, `data.tx` set and `data.items[0].status == "installed"`, and the folders exist in `<client dir>/Interface/AddOns`.
- Re-running the same install prints `status: "unchanged"`, `tx: null`, exit 0, and changes nothing on disk.
- With a newer fixture release, the same install reports `status: "updated"`, `kind: "update"`, `from_version`/`to_version` set.
- With two compatible live targets and no default, the command exits 3 `target_ambiguous` with `fix_argv` ending in `-t <id>` and one `alternatives` entry per other candidate; running that `fix_argv` succeeds.
- A `test`-kind target is never chosen implicitly.
- Mixed success and failure exits 0 with `partial: true`, the failure in `data.items[].error` and mirrored in `warnings`; with `--strict` the same run exits 6, `ok: false`, `error.code == "check_failed"`, `data` populated.
- When every item fails, the envelope is the first item's error with its exit code.
- `--dry-run` returns the same schema with `dry_run: true`, `tx: null`, writes nothing under the client dir or `<state>/omaddons`, and does not register the target.
- `--file <zip>` installs a local archive under the given ref with `version_confidence: "toc"`.
- `protected_folder`, `case_collision`, `ownership_conflict`, `unmanaged_folder`, `wrong_flavor`, `game_running` each produce exit 4 with a non-empty `fix`; `--force` resolves only the two documented cases.
- `commands` contains an undo hint with argv after every committed transaction; a `reload_required` warning appears when the engine reports reload or restart.
- The first mutating install on an unregistered target writes its registry entry and marker; key and id are stable on later runs.
- Insta snapshots cover the success, unchanged, partial and ambiguous envelopes (meta stripped).

## Test Plan

- Unit: target defaulting (default target set, single compatible live target, two compatible → ambiguous with exact argv, test targets skipped, no targets); partial-success folding (some fail, all fail, all unchanged); `--strict` mapping; transaction kind selection; argument validation (`--file` with two refs, `--version` with `url:`).
- Integration (`tests/install.rs`, synthetic trees from `tests/common/trees.rs`, archives from `tests/common/archives.rs`, HTTP replay via `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES`): install from `file:` zip; install from `gh:` with release.json fixtures (WeakAuras2 without a mainline entry must pick a verified build or fail with `no_compatible_release`, never a wrong-flavor build); reinstall-to-update; idempotent re-run; `--dry-run` writes nothing (hash the client dir and state dir before and after); `--file`; `--force` on an unmanaged folder then `omaddons undo` restores it; `blizzard_auctionui` vs `Blizzard_AuctionUI` refused.
- E2E contract: every case above run with `--json` asserts exactly one stdout JSON document and the exit code; stderr lines parse as NDJSON.
- Log test inputs (argv, env) and full stdout/stderr on failure.

## Considerations

- The compatibility probe for implicit targets downloads candidate archives for every live target. It is bounded by fetch-once and the blob cache; with many targets it is slower than an explicit `-t`, which the ambiguous-target fix steers users toward.
- `--file` with a ref whose source later provides hashes must switch to hash verification; keep the verification step behind the source's `expected_hash` so M5 only supplies the hash.
- The `<home>/Downloads` lookup after `distribution_disabled` is CurseForge-only (M5); out of scope here.
- Verb aliases (`add` → install) are M4.

title: Implement the list command over records and folder inventory
description:
## Background

`list` shows what is in each target's AddOns folder: the managed addons with their versions and sources, and, on request, the folders omaddons does not manage. The reference project only listed unmanaged folders and exposed `Blizzard_*` folders of custom clients as if they were mutable (vision §3, R9); omaddons classifies every folder by its case-folded key and never offers protected or linked folders for mutation.

The inventory bead (E4) does the classification and TOC reading. This bead is the command layer: argument parsing, per-target assembly from records plus inventory, the `data` schema and human output.

Placeholders: `<client dir>` = a target's directory holding `Interface/` and `WTF/`; `<state>` = `$XDG_STATE_HOME` (default `.local/state` under the home directory).

## Technical Approach

Files: `src/app/list.rs`, a `List` subcommand in `src/cli.rs` (DEC-1).

Synopsis (vision §5.9): `omaddons list [-t T] [--unmanaged] [--protected]`. Read-only: no lock, no writes, no network.

- Targets: all discovered targets by default (read commands default to all targets), including unregistered ones (`key: null`, provisional id, no managed addons). `-t T` narrows to one via the registry resolver (`target_not_found` / `target_ambiguous`, exit 3).
- Managed addons come from `<state>/omaddons/targets/<key>.json`: name, version, `version_confidence` (`release` | `toc`), canonical ref, channel, pinned, state (`ok` | `degraded`), folders.
- Folder classes come from the inventory bead, by `FolderName::key()` (ASCII case-fold, matching Wine's case-insensitive lookup):
  - `protected`: key starts with `blizzard_`;
  - `managed`: owned by exactly one managed addon;
  - `linked`: a symlink (for example a developer's working copy); listed, never mutated, never followed outside AddOns;
  - `unmanaged`: everything else;
  - `invalid`: an entry whose name fails `FolderName` validation; listed, never mutated.
  Two folders whose names differ only in case are flagged `case_duplicate: true` on both entries (which one the client loads is undefined under Wine).
- Default output: managed addons per target plus counts of every class. `--unmanaged` adds the `unmanaged`, `linked` and `invalid` entries. Decided: linked and invalid entries ride on `--unmanaged` (why: they are not managed, and a separate flag per class would bloat the surface). `--protected` adds the `protected` entries.
- Unmanaged entries carry the TOC metadata the inventory reads (Title, Version, Interface, and the TOC-load verdict against the target: `compatible`, `out_of_date`, `wrong_flavor` or `no_toc`), so an agent can see what an unmanaged folder is before M2's `adopt`. Protected entries carry only the folder name (token-frugal; a 3.3.5a client pack has 23 of them).
- A managed record whose folder is missing on disk is reported with `missing_folders: [..]` on that addon (the doctor finding `record-folder-missing` arrives in M4).
- Token-frugal by default (vision §5.9): ids, names, versions and counts. `-v` adds folder lists per addon, `client_dir`, and TOC metadata for managed folders.

`--json` `data` schema (`ListData`):

```
{
  "targets": [
    {
      "id": string,
      "key": string | null,
      "addons": [
        {
          "name": string,
          "version": string,
          "version_confidence": "release" | "toc",
          "ref": string,
          "channel": "stable" | "beta" | "alpha",
          "pinned": bool,
          "state": "ok" | "degraded",
          "folders": int,                       // -v: [string]
          "missing_folders": [string]
        }
      ],
      "counts": {"managed": int, "unmanaged": int, "protected": int, "linked": int, "invalid": int},
      "unmanaged": [ {"folder": string, "class": "unmanaged" | "linked" | "invalid", "title": string | null, "version": string | null, "interface": int | null, "verdict": "compatible" | "out_of_date" | "wrong_flavor" | "no_toc" | null, "case_duplicate": bool} ] | null,
      "protected": [ {"folder": string} ] | null
    }
  ]
}
```

`unmanaged` is null without `--unmanaged`; `protected` is null without `--protected`. Targets sort by id; addons by name (case-insensitive); folders by key.

Human output:

```
retail (12.1.0.69933, mainline)
  WeakAuras   5.19.2   gh:WeakAuras/WeakAuras2   stable
  DBM-Core    11.2.5   gh:DeadlyBossMods/DeadlyBossMods  stable  degraded
  2 managed · 1 unmanaged · 0 protected · 0 linked
wotlk (3.3.5.12340, wrath-legacy, localhost)
  0 managed · 0 unmanaged · 23 protected · 0 linked
```

Exit codes: 0, 1, 3.

## Acceptance Criteria

- On a synthetic retail target with two installed addons, one unmanaged folder and one symlinked folder, `omaddons list --json` reports both addons with name, version, ref and channel, and counts `managed 2, unmanaged 1, protected 0, linked 1`; `unmanaged` and `protected` are null.
- `--unmanaged` adds the unmanaged folder with its TOC Title, Version, Interface and verdict, and the linked folder with `class: "linked"`.
- On a synthetic 3.3.5a target, `--protected` lists 23 `Blizzard_*` folders; a lowercase `blizzard_custom` folder is also classified protected.
- Folders `Foo` and `foo` side by side are both flagged `case_duplicate: true`.
- A record whose folder was deleted reports it in `missing_folders`.
- `list` writes nothing and performs no network I/O (hash check of state, cache and client dirs; net.log unchanged).
- `-t unknown` exits 3 `target_not_found` with a fix.

## Test Plan

- Unit: assembly of records plus inventory into `ListData`; flag handling (`unmanaged`/`protected` null vs populated); sorting.
- Integration (`tests/list.rs`, synthetic trees, `file:` installs for managed records, a symlink created in the test, a 3.3.5a tree with 23 `Blizzard_*` folders): the cases above, plus `-v` output containing folder lists.
- E2E contract: one stdout envelope per case.

## Considerations

- `adopt` (bringing unmanaged folders under management by confidence tier) is M2; the verdict and TOC metadata shown here are what M2's adoption will build on.
- Reading TOCs for many unmanaged folders costs a little I/O; it happens only with `--unmanaged` or `-v`.
- Verb alias `ls` → list is M4.
- Symlinks are never followed outside AddOns; a symlink pointing at a non-directory is still `linked`.
acceptance_criteria: On a synthetic retail target with two installed addons, one unmanaged and one symlinked folder, list --json reports both addons with name, version, ref and channel and counts managed 2, unmanaged 1, protected 0, linked 1 with unmanaged and protected null; --unmanaged adds the unmanaged folder with TOC Title, Version, Interface and verdict and the linked folder with class linked; --protected on a synthetic 3.3.5a target lists 23 Blizzard_* folders and a lowercase blizzard_custom folder is protected too; Foo and foo side by side are both flagged case_duplicate; a record whose folder was deleted reports it in missing_folders; list writes nothing and performs no network I/O; -t unknown exits 3 target_not_found with a fix
close_reason: omaddons list shows each target's managed addons (name, version, ref, channel, state, missing folders) and counts of every folder class; --unmanaged adds unmanaged, linked and invalid folders with TOC title, version, interface and verdict; --protected adds Blizzard_* folders; -v adds folder lists and paths. Read-only, over a shared World pipeline (discover, reconcile, -t)

title: Implement the remove command as an undoable transaction
description:
## Background

`remove` takes managed addons out of a target. Like every mutation it is a journaled, snapshotted transaction (kind `remove`) attributed to an actor and reversible with `omaddons undo` (vision §5.5, §5.9). Removal never deletes: the engine renames each live folder into the transaction's snapshot directory (`<client dir>/Interface/.omaddons/snapshots/<tx>/AddOns/`), so undo can rename it back. SavedVariables are not touched by remove; the engine still snapshots the touched folders' SavedVariables so undo can apply its policy.

This bead is the command layer on top of the engine (E6 `commit`): argument parsing, resolving names to a target and its records, calling the engine with remove ops, partial-success semantics, `--dry-run`, the `data` schema and the human renderer.

Placeholders: `<client dir>` = the directory holding `Interface/` and `WTF/` for a target.

## Technical Approach

Files: `src/app/remove.rs`, a `Remove` subcommand in `src/cli.rs` (DEC-1).

Synopsis (vision §5.9): `omaddons remove <addon>... [-t T]`, plus the global `--dry-run`, `--actor`, `--reason`, `--while-running`, `--json`.

Name resolution:
- Each positional matches a managed addon record by record name (ASCII case-insensitive), by canonical ref (`gh:Owner/Repo`), or by the key of a folder the addon owns (removing `DBM-Core` removes the addon that owns it). Two addons matching one positional inside a target → `ref_ambiguous` (exit 3) with candidates.
- With `-t T`: resolve the target with the registry's `-t` resolver (`target_not_found` / `target_ambiguous`, exit 3); names are looked up in that target only.
- Without `-t`: each name is looked up across all registered targets. Decided: all names must resolve to one target. If a name is managed in more than one target, or the names span targets, fail with `target_ambiguous` (exit 3), `fix` = the original argv with `-t <first candidate>` appended and `alternatives` for the rest (why: a removal is one transaction on one target; silently picking a target, or fanning out, would surprise people).
- A name not managed anywhere (or not in the given target) → item error `not_managed` (exit 3). Unregistered targets have no records, so nothing there is removable.
- Protected (`Blizzard_*`), linked (symlink) and unmanaged folders are never removable by this command; naming one yields `not_managed` with a message saying which class the folder is.

Execution:
- One transaction per run on the resolved target, containing a remove op for every folder of every resolved addon. The engine applies the running policy: while the target's client runs, removing a folder whose TOC is loaded is refused with `game_running` (exit 4) under the default `safe` policy unless `--while-running`; on a `legacy` client any mutation while running is refused. `reload_required` comes from the engine (removing a loaded TOC means `restart`).
- The engine deletes the addon records, increments the target's `generation`, updates the per-file index, appends `history.jsonl` (`kind: remove`, actor, reason, argv), and rewrites `status.json`.
- Dependents warnings and orphan reporting arrive with dependency resolution in M2; M1 removes exactly what was named.
- Partial success: at least one addon removed and at least one item failed → exit 0, `partial: true`, failures in `data.items[].error`, mirrored in `warnings` (warning `code` = the item's error code, as decided in the install bead). Every item failing → the first item's error and exit code, `details.items` listing all. `--strict` is not offered on remove (vision lists it on install, update, sync and copy only).
- `--dry-run`: resolves names and computes the ops and the running-policy verdict; takes no lock, writes nothing. Same schema with `dry_run: true`, `tx: null` (DEC-16).
- After a commit, `commands` holds the undo hint `{"action":"undo","command":"omaddons undo <tx>","argv":["omaddons","undo","<tx>"],"destructive":false}`, and a `reload_required` warning is added when reload or restart is needed (fix display `/reload in game` or `restart the game client`, `fix_argv: null`).

`--json` `data` schema (`RemoveData`):

```
{
  "dry_run": bool,
  "target": {"id": string, "key": string},
  "tx": string | null,
  "items": [
    {
      "request": string,
      "name": string | null,
      "ref": string | null,
      "status": "removed" | "failed",
      "version": string | null,
      "folders": [string],                         // folders moved into the snapshot, sorted by key
      "error": {"code": string, "message": string, "fix": string, "fix_argv": [string] | null} | null
    }
  ],
  "reload_required": "none" | "reload" | "restart",
  "atomic_swap": bool | null
}
```

Human output:

```
retail: removed Bartender4 4.15.2 (1 folder)
retail: failed Questie: not_managed: Questie is not managed in retail
tx 01JB… · restart the game client · undo: omaddons undo 01JB…
```

Exit codes: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `omaddons remove <addon> -t <id> --json` removes every folder of the addon from `<client dir>/Interface/AddOns`, moves them under `Interface/.omaddons/snapshots/<tx>/AddOns/`, deletes the record, increments `generation`, appends a `kind: remove` history entry, and prints one envelope with `status: "removed"` and an undo hint with argv.
- `omaddons undo` immediately afterwards restores the folders byte-for-byte and the record.
- Removing by folder key (for example `DBM-Core`) removes the owning addon; removing by canonical ref works.
- A name that is not managed yields `not_managed` (exit 3) with a non-empty fix; naming a `Blizzard_*`, linked or unmanaged folder yields `not_managed` and never touches it.
- Without `-t`, a name managed in two targets fails with `target_ambiguous` (exit 3) whose `fix_argv` adds `-t <id>`.
- Mixed results exit 0 with `partial: true` and mirrored warnings; all failing returns the first item's error.
- While the client runs (fake /proc), removing a loaded folder is refused with `game_running` (exit 4) under `safe`; `--while-running` allows it and reports `reload_required: "restart"`.
- `--dry-run` reports the ops with `tx: null` and leaves the client dir and state untouched.

## Test Plan

- Unit: name resolution (record name case-insensitive, ref, owned folder key, ambiguous within a target, spans targets without `-t`, not managed, protected/linked/unmanaged folder named), partial-success folding.
- Integration (`tests/remove.rs`, synthetic trees, `file:` installs to set up records, fake /proc tree for the running client): remove then undo round-trip comparing folder hashes; remove by folder key; refused removal while running; `--while-running`; `--dry-run` writes nothing (hash before/after).
- E2E contract: every case under `--json` has exactly one stdout document and the documented exit code.
- Log argv, env and full stdout/stderr on failure.

## Considerations

- Removing a required dependency, dependents warnings and `orphan` reporting are M2.
- Verb aliases (`uninstall`, `rm`, `delete`) are M4.
- SavedVariables of the removed addon stay in `WTF/` (the client owns them); removal does not offer to delete them, and backups are M3.
- Retention eventually prunes the snapshot holding removed folders (24 h minimum); after that, undo of the removal is impossible, and the undo bead reports it as `not_found` for the snapshot.

title: Implement the status command as offline triage with --cached and --check
description:
## Background

`status` is the triage command and the first call for orientation (vision §5.8, §5.10, D19). The full version reports every target, pending update counts, doctor findings by severity, recent Lua error counts, live running state, journal warnings and a `commands` list of recommended next actions. Updates arrive in M2, Lua errors in M3 and doctor findings in M4, so the M1 version is offline triage only: targets, records, folder counts, live running state, journal and state-version warnings.

`status --cached` is the Omarchy widget's authority from M3 onward (`omaddons status --json --cached`): local state only, under 5 ms, no network. M1 sets that contract now so the widget can rely on it later. The first M1 checkpoint is also a `status --json` run on the development machine.

Placeholders: `<state>` = `$XDG_STATE_HOME` (default `.local/state` under the home directory); `<cache>` = `$XDG_CACHE_HOME` (default `.cache`); `<client dir>` = a target's directory holding `Interface/` and `WTF/`.

## Technical Approach

Files: `src/app/status.rs`, a `Status` subcommand in `src/cli.rs` (DEC-1).

Synopsis (vision §5.9): `omaddons status [-t T] [--cached] [--check]`. Default: all targets (read commands default to all targets). `-t T` narrows to one (registry resolver; unknown → `target_not_found`, exit 3).

Sources of truth:
- Targets: discovery (`discover()`, E3) merged with the registry (`<state>/omaddons/registry.json`). Registered targets carry their ULID `key`; discovered-but-unregistered targets carry `key: null` and the deterministic provisional id from the registry bead. Registered targets whose client dir no longer exists are listed with `missing: true`.
- Records: `<state>/omaddons/targets/<key>.json` (managed addons, `generation`, addon `state: ok|degraded`).
- Folder counts: the inventory bead's classification of `<client dir>/Interface/AddOns` by case-folded key: `managed`, `unmanaged`, `protected` (`blizzard_` prefix), `linked` (symlinks), `invalid` (names that fail `FolderName` validation). Status uses classification only, without reading TOC metadata: call the inventory with `Depth::Classes`, which opens no TOC files, to stay inside the 5 ms `--cached` budget.
- Running state: computed live on every call, including `--cached`, by the running-detection bead (reads `/proc`, ~1–2 ms).
- Journal: the journal bead's reader API: list `<state>/omaddons/journal/`, probe the global lock without blocking, and produce `journal_pending` (lock free) or `tx_in_progress` (lock held) warnings with their fixes. Status never recovers journals.
- State versions: loading state files may yield `state_version_older` or `state_version_newer` warnings (state-store bead); status passes them through.

`--cached` (vision §5.8): reads local state only and never scans. It uses the registry, the discovery cache (`<cache>/omaddons/discovery.json`, discover-cache bead) and the records; it never runs the bounded scan and never reads TOCs. Decided: when the discovery cache is absent, `--cached` lists registered targets only and adds a `commands` entry `omaddons status` (why: the full scan costs more than the 5 ms budget, and the widget must never block on it). Budget: under 5 ms on a warm machine with a handful of targets (hyperfine at the checkpoint).

Decided: status never writes, with or without `--cached` (it is a read command). `status.json` is written by commits only.

Without `--cached` M1 status is still fully offline: it runs discovery (which uses the discovery cache when valid) and inventory classification. No network in M1 at all.

Attention (per target, M1 definition): a target needs attention when any of these hold, listed in `attention` as a status-local enum (pinned in M4's wire-name golden):
- `journal_pending` — an unrecovered journal touches this target (lock free);
- `state_version_newer` — the target record is newer than this binary (writes refused, `state_too_new`);
- `target_missing` — registered, but the client dir is gone;
- `addon_degraded` — at least one addon record has `state: degraded` (for example after `--force` transferred a folder).

`tx_in_progress` is a warning, not attention: another process is working.

`--check` (vision §5.9): exits 6 when any target needs attention, returning `ok: false`, `error.code = "check_failed"`, `data` still populated. The `fix` is the fix of the first attention item in target order (journal pending → the journal bead's fix; target missing → `omaddons targets rm <id>`; degraded → `omaddons list -t <id> -v`; state newer → display "upgrade omaddons", `fix_argv: null`).

`commands` (recommended next actions, deterministic order): one entry per attention item using the fixes above; for a target with unmanaged folders, `omaddons list -t <id> --unmanaged` (`destructive: false`). M2 adds update and adoption recommendations.

`--json` `data` schema (`StatusData`):

```
{
  "cached": bool,
  "targets": [
    {
      "id": string,
      "key": string | null,
      "registered": bool,
      "default": bool,
      "family": string,                       // e.g. "mainline", "forever", "wrath-legacy", "unknown"
      "kind": "live" | "test",
      "install_kind": "battlenet" | "custom",
      "product": string | null,               // e.g. "wow", "wowf"; null for custom clients
      "version": string,                      // e.g. "12.1.0.69933", "3.3.5.12340"
      "interface": int,                        // e.g. 120100, 30300
      "label": string | null,                 // e.g. "localhost" from realmlist
      "running": bool,
      "missing": bool,
      "folders": {"managed": int, "unmanaged": int, "protected": int, "linked": int, "invalid": int},
      "addons": {"total": int, "degraded": int},
      "attention": [string]
    }
  ],
  "journal": {"pending": int, "in_progress": bool},
  "needs_attention": bool
}
```

Targets sort by id. `-v` adds `client_dir`, `install_root` and `exe_name` per target (paths are verbose-only, vision §5.9 "token-frugal").

Human output:

```
retail   mainline      12.1.0.69933  live  running    0 managed · 0 unmanaged · 0 protected
wotlk    wrath-legacy  3.3.5.12340   live  localhost  0 managed · 0 unmanaged · 23 protected
warning: journal_pending: an interrupted transaction for retail awaits recovery
```

Exit codes: 0, 1, 3, 6.

## Acceptance Criteria

- On a synthetic machine with a Battle.net root (`_retail_` 12.1.0.69933) and a custom 3.3.5a root with 23 `Blizzard_*` folders and `set realmlist 127.0.0.1`, `omaddons status --json` reports `retail` (family `mainline`, interface 120100) and the 3.3.5a target (family `wrath-legacy`, interface 30300, label `localhost`, `folders.protected == 23`), both with `key: null` before any mutation.
- After one install into each, both report stable keys on every later run.
- `status` writes nothing: hashes of `<state>/omaddons`, `<cache>/omaddons` and every client dir are identical before and after, with and without `--cached`.
- `status --cached` never runs the bounded scan (asserted via a debug log event or a scan counter) and performs no network I/O (net.log unchanged; works with `--offline`); with no discovery cache it lists registered targets only and recommends `omaddons status`.
- Running state is live under `--cached`: starting and stopping a fake process in a fake /proc tree flips `running` without any other change.
- A leftover journal with the lock free yields warning `journal_pending`, `attention` containing `journal_pending`, and `status --check` exits 6 with `ok: false`, `error.code == "check_failed"`, `data` populated and a non-empty fix; with the lock held (failpoint sleep in another process) status reports `tx_in_progress` and changes nothing.
- A registered target whose client dir was deleted shows `missing: true` and attention `target_missing`.
- `--cached` completes in under 5 ms on the fixture machine (measured at the checkpoint with hyperfine; recorded, not asserted in the gate).

## Test Plan

- Unit: attention computation per condition; `--check` fix selection; `commands` ordering; target merge of discovered and registered (registered missing, unregistered provisional, default flag).
- Integration (`tests/status.rs`, synthetic trees from `tests/common/trees.rs`, fake /proc tree, HOME/XDG_* tempdirs per DEC-6): the two-target machine above; registration after install; leftover journal (write a `prepared` journal fixture); lock held by a second process using `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS=engine.swapped=sleep:2000`; deleted client dir; `--cached` with and without a discovery cache; write-nothing hash check.
- E2E contract: one stdout envelope per case, exit codes 0/3/6 as documented.
- Log argv, env and outputs on failure.

## Considerations

- Added deps beyond the plan's list: `inventory` (folder counts come from its classification) and `discover-cache` (`--cached` reads the discovery cache). discover-cache is P2 while this bead is P1; it is size S, so the inversion costs little, and the plan owner may want to raise its priority.
- Pending update counts, `outdated` results, drift results (M2), Lua error counts (M3) and doctor findings by severity (M4) are added to this schema by those milestones as additive keys.
- The provisional id for unregistered targets must be deterministic across runs (registry bead), or agents will chase changing ids.
- Account, realm and character names never appear; status does not read `WTF/` beyond what discovery needs (`Config.wtf` on legacy targets).
acceptance_criteria: On a synthetic machine with _retail_ 12.1.0.69933 and a custom 3.3.5a root with 23 Blizzard_* folders and realmlist 127.0.0.1, status --json reports retail (mainline, 120100) and the 3.3.5a target (wrath-legacy, 30300, label localhost, folders.protected 23), both key null before any mutation; after one install into each both report stable keys; status writes nothing (hashes of <state>/omaddons, <cache>/omaddons and client dirs unchanged, with and without --cached); status --cached never runs the bounded scan, performs no network I/O and with no discovery cache lists registered targets only and recommends omaddons status; running state flips live under --cached with a fake /proc; a leftover journal with the lock free yields journal_pending, attention journal_pending, and status --check exits 6 with ok false, error.code check_failed, data populated and a non-empty fix; with the lock held status reports tx_in_progress and changes nothing; a registered target whose client dir was deleted shows missing true and attention target_missing; --cached runs under 5 ms on the fixture machine (measured at the checkpoint)
close_reason: status: offline triage with live running state, attention, --cached without scanning, --check

title: Implement the targets command: list, add, rm, rename, default and --rescan
description:
## Background

A target is one WoW client directory (the directory holding `Interface/` and `WTF/`) plus its identity: an immutable ULID `key`, a human `id` alias, family, kind, version, interface and `ClientRules` (vision §5.1). Discovery finds targets with no setup (§5.2); the registry (`<state>/omaddons/registry.json`) remembers registered ones, and a marker at `<client dir>/Interface/.omaddons/target.json` lets a moved install be re-linked. `omaddons targets` is the user-facing surface over all of that: list what exists, add a client discovery cannot find, remove, rename, choose a default, and force a rescan.

The registry bead (E3) owns keys, aliases, markers, registration under the lock and `-t` resolution; the discover-cache bead owns the cache that `--rescan` bypasses. This bead is the command layer.

Placeholders: `<state>` = `$XDG_STATE_HOME` (default `.local/state` under the home directory); `<config>` = `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME` (default `.config`); `<client dir>` as above; `<root>` = a WoW install root.

## Technical Approach

Files: `src/app/targets.rs`, a `Targets` subcommand with `add`, `rm`, `rename`, `default` sub-subcommands in `src/cli.rs` (DEC-1).

Synopsis (vision §5.9): `omaddons targets [add <path> [--name N] | rm <id> | rename <id> <new> | default <id>] [--rescan]`.

Decided: the envelope `command` for sub-subcommands is the space-joined path (`"targets add"`, `"targets rm"`, `"targets rename"`, `"targets default"`); bare listing is `"targets"` (why: one string per distinct `data` schema keeps envelopes self-describing; coordinate with the output-envelope bead so every command family follows it).

### targets (list)

- Runs discovery (using the discovery cache when valid; `--rescan` bypasses and refreshes it) and merges registered targets. Read-only apart from the derived discovery cache.
- Each target reports: `id`, `key` (null when unregistered), `registered`, `default`, `family`, `kind` (`live` | `test`), `install_kind` (`battlenet` | `custom`), `product` (null for custom), `version`, `interface`, `label`, `client_dir`, `missing` (registered but the directory is gone), `found_by` (`product_db` | `scan` | `launcher:<lutris|heroic|steam|bottles>` | `extra_root` | `manual`).
- Decided: `client_dir` is always included, unlike other commands where paths are verbose-only (why: a target is its client dir; a target list without it is useless). `-v` adds `install_root`, `flavor_dir`, `exe_name`, the `ClientRules` row name, and the alias list.
- Discovery warnings (unknown flavor folders, version/interface disagreement, `client_not_launched_since_patch`, `DISCOVERY_MAX_DIRS` reached) pass through as warnings.

### targets add <path> [--name N]

- Accepts a Battle.net root, a flavor folder (`<root>/_retail_`), a custom client root, an `Interface` directory or an `Interface/AddOns` directory, and normalizes to client dir(s) by running the discovery recognizers on that path.
- Decided: a Battle.net root registers every flavor folder under it (one target each); `--name` is then allowed only when exactly one target results, otherwise `usage` (exit 2) with fix naming the flavor-folder form (why: one name cannot label several clients).
- A path that does not exist, or contains no recognizable client → `target_not_found` (exit 3), message saying what was looked for (`.build.info`, `Wow*.exe` + `Interface/`), fix `omaddons targets` (argv form).
- The path is stored in the registry as a manual root so later discovery includes it even outside the bounded scan.
- `--name N`: Decided: ids match `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]{0,31}$`, must not parse as a ULID, must not contain `@` (reserved for qualified collisions such as `retail@steam`), and must not already be taken; violations → `usage` (exit 2) naming the target that holds the id and suggesting `omaddons targets rename`.
- Already registered → idempotent, `changed: false`, exit 0.
- Registration (key assignment, registry write, marker write) happens under the global lock via the registry API.

### targets rm <id>

- Decided: removes the registry entry and leaves the client dir untouched, marker included, so a later `add` (or the next mutation touching it) re-links the same key. State files `targets/<key>.json` and `.files.json` are kept for the same reason.
- If it was the default target, the default is cleared.
- Data reports how many managed addons the target had (`managed_addons`) so a caller notices it unregistered a target with content. No warning code.
- Unknown id → `target_not_found` (3).

### targets rename <id> <new>

- Gives the target a new primary id; the old id is released. Same validation as `--name`. Renaming an unregistered target registers it first (vision §5.1: keys are assigned by the first mutating command or by `targets add|rename|default`).

### targets default <id>

- Sets the default target in the registry (registering it if needed). The default is used by `install` when `-t` is absent.
- Decided: config `default_target` in `<config>/omaddons/config.toml`, when set, overrides the registry default (explicit configuration wins); `targets default` still writes the registry and reports `overridden_by_config: true` so the caller knows why nothing changed in behavior. Flagged to the plan owner as a two-sources-of-truth problem worth revisiting.

Mutating sub-subcommands take the global lock (`LOCK_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT` 5 s → `locked`, exit 5) and write through fsx via the registry API. They are not transactions (they are not in the transaction kind list) and are not undoable; they are idempotent and cheap to reverse by hand. `--dry-run` reports what would change and writes nothing.

`--json` `data` schemas:

```
targets:          {"targets": [Target], "default": string | null, "rescanned": bool}
targets add:      {"changed": bool, "targets": [Target]}
targets rm:       {"id": string, "key": string, "managed_addons": int, "was_default": bool}
targets rename:   {"key": string, "from": string, "to": string}
targets default:  {"id": string, "key": string, "overridden_by_config": bool}

Target = {"id": string, "key": string | null, "registered": bool, "default": bool, "family": string,
          "kind": "live" | "test", "install_kind": "battlenet" | "custom", "product": string | null,
          "version": string, "interface": int, "label": string | null, "client_dir": string,
          "missing": bool, "found_by": string}
```

Human output (list):

```
* retail   01JB…  mainline      12.1.0.69933  live  <client dir>
  wotlk    01JC…  wrath-legacy  3.3.5.12340   live  localhost  <client dir>
  ptr      -      mainline      12.1.0        test  (unregistered)  <client dir>
```

(`*` marks the default; in real output `<client dir>` is the actual path.)

Exit codes: 0, 1, 2, 3, 5.

## Acceptance Criteria

- On a synthetic machine, bare `omaddons targets --json` lists every discovered target with `client_dir`, `found_by`, `registered: false` and `key: null` before any mutation.
- `targets add <custom root> --name pserver` registers it with a ULID key, writes `<client dir>/Interface/.omaddons/target.json` containing that key, and a second identical call returns `changed: false`.
- `targets add <Battle.net root>` with two flavor folders registers both; adding `--name` there exits 2.
- `targets add` on a directory with no client exits 3 `target_not_found` with a fix.
- `targets rename retail main` makes `-t main` resolve and `-t retail` fail; invalid ids (`Main`, a ULID, `a@b`, a taken id) exit 2.
- `targets rm <id>` removes the registry entry, leaves the marker and state files in place; `targets add` of the same path restores the same key.
- `targets default <id>` makes `install` without `-t` use that target; with config `default_target` set to another id, the output reports `overridden_by_config: true`.
- `--rescan` ignores the discovery cache: with a cache entry whose stored target data was edited in place by the test (stat keys left valid), bare `targets` shows the cached data, `targets --rescan` shows the on-disk truth with `rescanned: true` and rewrites the cache.
- A mutating sub-subcommand with the lock held by another process for longer than 5 s exits 5 `locked` with `retryable: true`.
- `--dry-run` on add/rm/rename/default writes nothing.

## Test Plan

- Unit: path normalization (root, flavor folder, custom root, `Interface`, `Interface/AddOns`); id validation; default precedence (config vs registry).
- Integration (`tests/targets.rs`, synthetic trees, HOME/XDG_* tempdirs per DEC-6): the cases above; lock contention using a second process holding the lock via `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS=engine.swapped=sleep:<ms>` (or the fsx-lock test helper); marker contents checked as JSON.
- E2E contract: one stdout envelope per sub-subcommand, success and failure, with the documented `command` string.

## Considerations

- Two live markers with one key (a copied install) are handled by the registry: the original path keeps the key, the copy gets a new one; `targets` surfaces the registry's warning.
- `extra_roots` in config and `targets add` overlap: config is declarative (dotfiles), `add` is imperative and recorded in the registry. Both feed discovery.
- Family names, product codes and flavor folder names are also accepted by `-t`; an id equal to one of those could be confusing. The registry bead defines resolution precedence; this bead only rejects ids that are already taken.
- Removing a target never deletes anything in the client dir.
acceptance_criteria: Bare targets --json lists every discovered target with client_dir, found_by, registered false and key null before any mutation; targets add <custom root> --name pserver registers a ULID key, writes Interface/.omaddons/target.json with that key, and repeating it returns changed false; add on a Battle.net root with two flavor folders registers both and --name there exits 2; add on a directory with no client exits 3 target_not_found with a fix; rename makes the new id resolve and the old fail, and invalid ids (uppercase, ULID-shaped, containing @, taken) exit 2; rm removes the registry entry but leaves marker and state files, and re-adding the path restores the same key; default <id> makes install without -t use it and reports overridden_by_config true when config default_target differs; --rescan ignores the discovery cache (an in-place edited cache entry is shown by bare targets, while --rescan shows on-disk truth with rescanned true and rewrites the cache); a mutating sub-subcommand with the lock held past 5 s exits 5 locked retryable; --dry-run on add/rm/rename/default writes nothing
close_reason: omaddons targets lists every client (registered or provisional, with found_by, missing and default) and adds, removes, renames and chooses targets under the global lock; --rescan bypasses the discovery cache; --dry-run writes nothing; nested help and usage errors work for its subcommands
