**Architecture, part 1 of 2 (§6.1–§6.8): the whole picture, the contract registry and `capabilities`, the guide and the skill, schemas and declared details, intent inference, completions and verbosity, the semantic manifest and the freeze, determinism (M4 plan, 2026-10-24).**

## §6 Architecture

### §6.1 The whole picture

```text
                       ┌──────────────── agents ───────────────────┐      ┌──── humans ────┐
                       │ skill (SKILL.md) · capabilities · schemas │      │ terminal · bar │
                       └───────────────┬───────────────────────────┘      └───────┬────────┘
                                       │ argv … --json                            │ argv (widget: apply <plan_id>)
 ┌─────────────────────────────────────▼──────────────────────────────────────────▼────────────────────┐
 │ cli.rs (clap) ── usage_error + intent inference (TargetVocabulary: rules builtin + registry.json)    │
 │       │                                                                                             │
 │ src/contract/  Registry ◄── app::COMMANDS (+ facts) · error/warning/exit tables · Action · events ·  │
 │       │                     env vars · features · limits · politeness · rules · sources · doctor     │
 │       ├─► capabilities ─► robot-docs guide (= SKILL.md) / schema / errors ─► manifest.json (golden)  │
 │       └─► help (discovery line) · completions (clap_complete) · doctor capabilities                 │
 │                                                                                                     │
 │ app/<command> ─► engine::tx::run ─ plan() ─ Binding::plan(token+witness) ─ commit_target(lock):     │
 │       ▲            generations · witness · re-judged ops == approved ─► swap (endpoint predicates)  │
 │       │  dry run: precondition + approval + StoredPlan{intent} ─► <cache>/plans/<id>.json           │
 │       └── apply <id>: lease ─ load intent ─ expiry/build/inputs/applied ─ execute intent bound      │
 │                                                                                                     │
 │ doctor/ registry(FailureMode: tier, detector, fixer) ◄── DoctorView (tolerant: config·registry·     │
 │       │                                                   discovery·records·journals·caches·…)       │
 │       ├─ status (cached + quick tiers) ─► issues[]                                                  │
 │       ├─ diagnose ─► <state>/doctor/runs/<run>/report.json, latest                                  │
 │       └─ fix ─► engine::repair: fixes lowered to primitives ─ .repair journal (write-ahead per      │
 │                 primitive) ─ fsx tracked session (run backups, per-FS quarantine) ─ history kind    │
 │                 repair ─ undo via engine::undo ─ fences and activation barriers (resource sets)     │
 │                                                                                                     │
 │ fsx (single writer): endpoint predicates · group commit · CommitWindow barriers · Writer::{Doctor,…}│
 └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Three data flows are new:

1. **Describe.** The registry (§6.2) is the one source for every description of the CLI, rendered five ways: `capabilities`, the guide, the schemas, the semantic manifest and its readable names list.
2. **Preview, then run exactly, target by target.** The engine's existing `Binding` seam carries a token computed from the engine's own plan, including an approval witness of everything the plan reads, replaces or removes (§6.9). Under the commit lock the witness is checked again and the re-judged operations must equal the approved ones. A stored plan is that token plus a typed intent. `apply` executes the intent bound to it, holding the plan's lease.
3. **Diagnose, then repair.** One registry of failure modes (§6.13) feeds `status` and `doctor`. A repair is a transaction of a new family (§6.14), made of primitive steps, which recovery, history, undo and retention all understand, and whose unfinished journals fence exactly the resources they protect.

### §6.2 The contract registry and `capabilities`

#### §6.2.1 Module layout

```text
src/contract/
  mod.rs          Registry::build() -> Registry  (cheap: no I/O but config.toml, read once)
  commands.rs     walks Cli::command() + app::COMMANDS → CommandInfo { path, about, group, mutates,
                  dictionary, exits, args[], flags[], aliases[], stores_plan, binds, network }
  actions.rs      enum Action { Undo, UndoRun, Update, …, Apply, InstallSkill, DoctorFix, DoctorExplain, DoctorGc }
                  with wire(), description(), destructive()
  events.rs       NDJSON event names and fields; Phase::ALL; LogLevel::ALL
  env.rs          ENV_VARS: [(name, Kind::{Release, Debug, Harness}, description, mirrors_flag)]
  features.rs     FEATURES: ["json_envelope", "ndjson_stderr", "dry_run_everywhere", "preconditions",
                  "stored_plans", "doctor", "offline", "progress_ndjson", "undo", "backups", "lua_errors",
                  "omarchy_widget", "completions", "agent_skill"]   (stable feature words, never removed)
  volatile.rs     VOLATILE: [(key path pattern, reason)]   (§6.8)
  manifest.rs     build(&Registry) -> Manifest; classify(&baseline, &current) -> Changes   (§6.7, A10)
  wire.rs         names(&Manifest) -> Vec<String>          (the readable projection, §6.7)
  guide/          guide.md (template), doctor.md (template), render.rs     (§6.3)
  schema.rs       schemas: envelope, events, commands, files (for_serialize)   (§6.4)
```

`app::CommandEntry` gains five fields, each declared once beside the command, in the same `COMMANDS` table:

```rust
pub struct CommandEntry {
    pub name: &'static str,            // canonical path, = envelope `command`
    pub group: Group,
    pub mutates: bool,
    pub dictionary: Dictionary,        // General | Doctor
    pub exits: &'static [u8],          // M4-D5: declared, verified by the matrix
    pub data: fn(&mut schemars::SchemaGenerator) -> schemars::Schema,  // its Outcome::Data
    pub stores_plan: bool,             // M4-D22
    pub network: Network,              // None | Optional | Required
}
```

`binds` is not a field. It is derived from `precondition::BINDING_COMMANDS`, which stays the single list.

**Why a `fn` pointer for `data`.** `schemars::schema_for!` needs the type at compile time. A function pointer per entry (for example `|g| g.root_schema_for::<InstallData>()`) keeps the command → type mapping in the one table, instead of in `run_command`'s match. A test asserts that every path's declared schema equals the schema of the `Outcome` its dispatch arm returns. The mechanism: each `Outcome` impl exposes `fn schema(g)` via a blanket helper, and a dispatch-table test runs each command once in the matrix and checks that the envelope's `data` validates against `entry.data`.

#### §6.2.2 `capabilities` data

`omaddons capabilities --json` returns `data` with these keys, in this order:

```text
version            tool version (CARGO_PKG_VERSION)
contract_version   = output::SCHEMA_VERSION ("1.0")
build_id           the execution build id (§6.9.1)
guide_digest       the guide's expected stamp digest, OMADDONS_GUIDE_SHA256 (M4-D7)
features           [feature words]
commands           [{path, description, group, mutates, json: true, dictionary, exit_codes, stores_plan,
                     binds, network, aliases, args[{name, value_name, required, multiple, default,
                     possible_values}], flags[{long, short, aliases, value_name, takes_value, multiple,
                     default, possible_values, conflicts_with, requires, global, description}],
                     data_schema: "omaddons robot-docs schema <path>"}]
exit_codes         {general: [{code, name, meaning, retryable}], doctor: [{code, name, meaning}]}
env_vars           [{name, description, mirrors}]                 (release kind only)
limits             [{name, value, unit, config_key, source: builtin|config}]   (limits + politeness REGISTRY)
sources            [{id, enabled, requires_credential, credential_configured, hosts[]}]
families           [{name, interface_min, interface_max, legacy}]
client_rules       [{row, family, install_kind, version_min, version_max, game_types, …, source}]
target_id_forms    ["key", "id", "product_code", "flavor_folder", "game_mode", "family", "path", "all"]
error_codes        [{code, exit, doctor_exit, retryable, meaning, details_schema}]   (M4-D10's DetailSpec as JSON Schema)
warning_codes      [{code, meaning}]
actions            [{action, description, destructive}]
failure_modes      {count, subsystems, command: "omaddons doctor capabilities --json"}
schemas_uri        "omaddons robot-docs schema"
robot_docs_uri     "omaddons robot-docs guide"
config_error       null | {path, line, column, message}           (M4-D4)
```

**Rules:**

- **Generated, never hand-kept.**
  - `commands` walks `Cli::command().build()` (globals propagated) and joins each path with its `CommandEntry`. `about` is clap's.
  - `possible_values` comes from clap where clap validates. For the flags validated in app code (`--actor`, `--by`, `--last-by`, `--since` forms), it comes from a declared `ValueSet` beside the flag's parser: one list, used by both the parser and capabilities.
- **`aliases`** lists clap's visible aliases and nothing else. The usage-fix synonyms (`targets remove` → `targets rm`) are intent, not aliases, and the guide documents them.
- **`requires_credential`** is a new field on each source's registration (`sources/mod.rs`): `false` for every keyless source, and `true` only for `cf`/`wago`, which are parsed and disabled until M5.
- **Per-source hosts.** The allowlist is re-keyed by source (`net::allowlist::hosts_for(SourceId)`, the flat `ALWAYS` list becoming the union). `capabilities` lists each source's hosts.
- **`credential_configured`** says whether a credential is configured, never what it is, and runs no credential command (the M2 rule for `auth github` offline).
- **The human form** (≤ 40 lines): version and contract, command count by group, the exit dictionaries, sources with their states, and the closing pointer to `--json`.

#### §6.2.3 Tests

- **Round trip.** For every `commands[]` entry: `omaddons <path> --help` parses, every flag parses with a sample value, and every alias resolves to the same path.
- **Completeness.** Every `ErrorCode::ALL`, `WarningCode::ALL`, `Action` variant and `ENV_VARS` `release` entry appears exactly once. Failure modes appear as a summary whose `count` equals the registry's, and `doctor capabilities` lists every id exactly once (E4).
- **Purity.** One run on a synthetic home leaves the tree hashes of `<state>`, `<cache>`, `<config>` and the clients unchanged, and adds no `net.log` line.
- **Broken config.** A broken `config.toml` gives exit 0 with `config_error`.
- **Perf.** Under 20 ms, median of 21 (`tests/perf.rs`, release, ignored like the other budgets).

### §6.3 The guide, `SKILL.md` and `install-skill`

#### §6.3.1 The renderer

- `src/contract/guide/guide.md` is the hand-written template, embedded with `include_str!`. Placeholders are `{{name}}` on a line of their own (block) or inline (`{{command_count}}`). The renderer replaces each with a block generated from the registry. An unknown placeholder is a test failure.
- The generated blocks, each rendered at a fixed width (no terminal measurement) so output is byte-stable:

  | Placeholder | Content |
  |---|---|
  | `{{stamp}}` | `<!-- omaddons guide sha256:<hex> -->`, filled last: the renderer renders everything else, hashes the document with this line omitted, and writes the digest (M4-D7). It must sit on the line right after the frontmatter. |
  | `{{commands}}` | one line per command path: `path` — description (mutates · stores plan) |
  | `{{exit_general}}`, `{{exit_doctor}}` | the two dictionaries |
  | `{{errors_common}}` | the 15 error codes agents meet most, with exit, retryability and the fix pattern; then "the rest: `omaddons robot-docs errors`" |
  | `{{never}}` | the "will never do" list, from a `NEVER` table in `contract/guide/render.rs`, also used by `doctor robot-docs` |
  | `{{env}}` | the `release` env vars |
  | `{{targets}}` | the `-t` forms with examples from the built-in rules (`retail`, `era`, `sod`, `wotlk`) |

#### §6.3.2 The guide's structure (Appendix C has the full outline)

1. Frontmatter:

   ```yaml
   ---
   name: omaddons
   description: Manage World of Warcraft addons on Linux with the omaddons CLI — install, update, preview and apply exactly, undo, back up WTF/, read Lua errors, and run `omaddons doctor`. Use whenever the user mentions WoW addons, a WoW client (retail, Classic Era, Anniversary, Mists Classic, Forever, a private server), BugGrabber/Lua errors, or addon backups.
   ---
   ```

2. `{{stamp}}`.
3. **What omaddons is**, in five lines, plus the discovery trio.
4. **The core loop** (§4.1's six steps, the reconcile step included).
5. **Reading the envelope**: keys, `fix_argv`, `alternatives`, `commands[]`, `partial`, and never parsing display strings.
6. **Exit codes**: both dictionaries.
7. **Targets and refs.**
8. **The safety model**: transactions, undo, running clients, SavedVariables, previews and plans, the doctor's repairs.
9. **Things omaddons will NEVER do** (`{{never}}`).
10. **Recipes**: the eight canonical intents (§6.3.4).
11. **Errors you will meet** (`{{errors_common}}`).
12. **The doctor loop**: robot-triage, then fix or explain, then undo.
13. **Where to look for more**: `capabilities`, `robot-docs schema`, `robot-docs errors`, `doctor robot-docs`, README.

#### §6.3.3 `install-skill`

- `omaddons robot-docs install-skill [--dir <DIR>]` resolves the directory (default `<skills>`, which is `Paths::skill_dir()`), checks the scope (M4-D8) and renders the guide.
- **Unchanged.** If `<DIR>/SKILL.md` exists with the same bytes, the whole file compared, it writes nothing: `{dir, file, written: "unchanged", tool_version}`.
- **Otherwise** it takes the global lock and writes atomically through `Writer::Skill`, creating `<DIR>` (0755) if needed. The file is 0644, readable as any skill is.
- **Records** a settings history line of kind `skill` with `dir`.
- **`commands[]`** offers `install-skill --dir <root>/omaddons` (action `install_skill`) for each other existing skill root: `$HOME/.codex/skills` and `$HOME/.agents/skills`, a fixed list in `contract/guide/render.rs`.
- `--dry-run` reports what it would write.
- **Data:** `{dry_run, dir, file, written: fresh|replaced|unchanged, bytes, tool_version}`.

#### §6.3.4 Recipes: the eight canonical intents, each at most two commands

Each recipe is a fenced block with the info string `sh recipe=<id> expect=<exit>[,<exit>]`. `tests/skill_recipes.rs` extracts every block from the rendered guide, runs its commands in order on a synthetic home with recorded HTTP fixtures (`tests/fixtures/http/skill_recipes/`), and asserts each command's exit against `expect` plus the per-recipe assertion its doc comment names. Placeholders like `<plan_id>` are filled from the previous command's JSON by a declared rule (`plan_id ← data.plan_id`).

| Id | Intent | Commands |
|---|---|---|
| `update-everything` | update everything | `omaddons update --json --actor agent --reason "…"` |
| `whats-broken` | what is broken | `omaddons status --json`; then `omaddons doctor --robot-triage --json` |
| `install-for-target` | install X for target Y | `omaddons install weakauras -t era --json --actor agent` |
| `legacy-from-git` | add a legacy addon from a git repo | `omaddons install git:https://github.com/fondlez/GroupBulletinBoard#main -t wotlk --json` |
| `preview-then-apply` | preview, then apply exactly | `omaddons install dbm -t retail --dry-run --json`; then `omaddons apply <plan_id> --json` |
| `undo-agent-today` | undo what the agent did today | `omaddons history --actor agent --since 1d --json`; then `omaddons undo --last-by agent --json` |
| `explain-updates` | explain pending updates with changelogs | `omaddons outdated --changelog --json` |
| `fresh-machine` | restore a fresh machine | `omaddons sync addons.toml --locked --json` |

**Why a test runs them.** The vision's checkpoint ("the `SKILL.md` recipes run as e2e tests") and the guide's credibility: an agent copies these lines verbatim.

### §6.4 Schemas, the error catalog and declared details

- **`omaddons robot-docs schema [<command>]`**
  - `--json` gives `{envelope, events, commands, files}`, each entry a draft 2020-12 schema built in its own `SchemaGenerator` with `for_serialize()`.
  - The human form prints the same JSON, pretty, because a schema has no better human rendering.
  - `<command>` is a path (`"backup restore"` as two words, `backup restore`); an unknown path is `usage` with the closest path.
  - `files` covers every `store::KINDS` row (each `Versioned` impl exposes its schema), the journal line types (folder and repair families), `plan`, `doctor_report` (the doctor report) and `addons.toml` (`DesiredStateSchema`).
- **`omaddons robot-docs errors`**
  - `--json` gives `{error_codes: [{code, exit, doctor_exit, retryable, meaning, details_schema, fix_pattern}], warning_codes: [{code, meaning, fix_pattern}]}`. `details_schema` is the code's `DetailSpec` (M4-D10) rendered as a JSON Schema fragment.
  - `fix_pattern` is a short prose description of what the fix is, for example "the same command with `-t <candidate>`".
  - The human form is a table.
- **`meaning` texts** are added to every error and warning row in `error_codes!` and `warning_codes!` (A9): one sentence each, the README table's text made the single source. README's code tables then quote `robot-docs errors`; H4 checks they agree.
- **Typed details** (M4-D10): a `DetailSpec` per error row (A9). The error schema is a union discriminated by `code`: each variant fixes `code` with `const` and carries that code's details schema. `support::check` validates every failure envelope's `details` against its code's variant, so a retyped value, an unknown key or an undeclared `reason` value fails. A test lists declared keys that no test observes, and H1 makes that list empty.
- **Live validation.** `support::check` validates `data` against `entry.data`, `error` against its code's variant, `warnings[]` against `Warning`, `commands[]` against `CommandHint`, and each stderr line against its event schema. A validation failure prints the instance path and the schema path.
- **Strict in tests, permissive when published.** schemars emits `additionalProperties: false` only for types with `deny_unknown_fields` (`schemars_derive` 1.2.3, `schema_exprs.rs:85, 264`), so a plain validation never notices a key the schema lacks.
  - The test-side generator applies a transform that adds `unevaluatedProperties: false` at every **instance position** (the root, each `properties` value, `items`, `prefixItems` and `additionalProperties`), beside that position's in-place applicators (`allOf`, `anyOf`, `oneOf`, `$ref`), wherever those positions occur, inside `$defs` entries included. It never adds it at the root of a branch applied in place or at the root of a `$defs` entry (which is only ever reached through a `$ref`), because in draft 2020-12 a branch's `unevaluatedProperties` sees only its own annotations and would reject a sibling branch's valid fields. An emitted key missing from the schema then fails validation, and every valid variant field still passes.
  - The transform has its own tests: a `$ref` used both as a property and inside `allOf`, a map (`additionalProperties`), an internally tagged enum, a flattened struct, and `oneOf` with shared fields. In each, an unknown field fails and every valid field passes.
  - The published schemas (`robot-docs schema`) stay open, so a newer minor's additions do not break an older consumer's validator.
- **Opaque values.** A few fields are deliberately unconstrained application values: config values (`config.rs:65-93`) and `outcome.rs:180`'s details.
  - A new registry `contract::OPAQUE` lists each such path with its reason. The strict transform leaves those subtrees open, and the manifest records them as `opaque`.
  - A test fails on any `Value` field in a serialized type under `src/app`, `src/output`, `src/contract` or `src/doctor` that `OPAQUE` does not list.
  - **`apply`'s data is not opaque.** `ApplyData.result` is the executed command's typed data, and `approved` is the typed approval summary (M4-D24). Its schema is a union of complete wrapper variants, one per storable command, each fixing `applied.command` with `const` and attaching that command's data schema to `result` (§6.9.3). A union on `result` alone would not tie it to its sibling `applied.command`.
- **Every snapshot, not only the matrix.** The vision's checkpoint is "validates every snapshot-tested JSON response". The repository has 159 `.snap` files (140 under `tests/`, 19 under `src/`); the matrix covers 105 of them.
  - A walker test reads every `.snap` file in the repository, keeps each whose body parses as a JSON envelope, and validates it against its `command`'s schema.
  - Redaction placeholders (`<ulid>`, `<path>`) are strings like any other, and the schemas carry no `pattern` or `format` on ids, so redacted snapshots validate.
- **Observed keys ⊆ the golden.** Once the golden exists (H2), the contract suite collects every key path it observes in `data` and checks that each appears in the manifest, as it validates `details` against their specs (M4-D10). Together with the strict transform, the manifest is complete by construction.

### §6.5 Intent inference

- **`TargetVocabulary`** (`src/vocabulary.rs`, new; `cli.rs` stays one file) is built lazily in the usage path only.
  - It holds the built-in rules table's product default ids, product codes, flavor folders, game-mode ids and aliases, and family names, plus the ids in `registry.json`.
  - `registry.json` is read with a bounded read (at most `DISCOVERY_FILE_MAX_BYTES`, `limits.rs:65`) and decoded with `store::load_bytes` (`store.rs:250`), read-only, and errors are ignored. There is no `store::load_bounded`; E2's tolerant view uses the same two calls.
  - `fn classify(word) -> Option<TargetWord{kind, canonical}>` matches case-insensitively, in `-t`'s resolution order.
- **Hook 1** (`cli.rs:676-688`, before `subcommand_fix`): `InvalidSubcommand(w)`, where `w` classifies and the next token is a subcommand path. The fix is the argv minus `w`, plus `-t <w>` appended at the end. The message is "'<w>' is a client, not a command; the client goes in -t". `details: {target, command}`.
- **Hook 2** (`cli.rs:689`): `UnknownArgument(tok)`, where `tok` has no leading dash and classifies. The fix is the argv with `tok` replaced by `-t tok`. It covers two cases:
  - a command with no positional (`status retail`);
  - a command whose positionals are already filled, so clap rejects one more (`info dbm era`, where `info` takes exactly one positional, `info.rs:50-51`; `pin dbm retail`).

  In both, the extra word is the last positional-looking token and it names a client.
- **Hook 3** (app level, a preflight). The commands that take several names (`install`, `update`, `remove`; `pin`, `unpin` and `info` take one, so an extra word is hook 2's) classify every positional of the invocation **before planning, recovery or any commit**, in one helper, `resolve_args::misplaced_clients`. A word that classifies as a client and matches no installed addon on the selected targets (for `update` and `remove`), no catalog name, alias or ref form (for `install`) and no local path rejects the whole invocation.
  - The result is `usage`, as for hooks 1 and 2, with `fix_argv` moving the word to `-t` and `details {target, command}`. Nothing else in the invocation runs.
  - With other positionals present (`update dbm retail`), the fix keeps them (`update dbm -t retail`).
  - It must run first. `remove` commits the names it recognized on the one target they agree on, and only afterwards turns the others into warnings (`remove.rs:163-275`); without `-t` it searches every managed target. Built into the not-found path, `remove dbm retail` would remove DBM before explaining that `retail` belongs in `-t`, possibly from `era`, and the corrected command would not undo it.
  - Ordinary partial success is unchanged: a name that is simply unknown fails alone while the others proceed. Only a recognized misplaced client invalidates the invocation.
  - A word that is both a client and an addon (a catalog entry named like a mode) is never moved: the addon wins, as today.
- **`-t all`** (M4-D13): resolved in `discover::registry::resolve` as a keyword before the id step, unless a registered id equals `all` (that id wins, and `target_id_reserved` warns once per command). `World::select_many` returns every target. `resolve_one` gives `target_ambiguous`.
- **Target typos** (M4-D14): in `resolve`'s not-found branch, the closest vocabulary word within distance 2 becomes the fix, keeping the rest of the argv.
- **The verb exemption.** `usage_error`'s rule "a mutating guess becomes `help <it>`" applies to guessed *verbs*. Fixes from hooks 1–3 and from target typos keep the user's verb, and are marked `UsageFix::UserVerb` so the final filter does not demote them. They must still parse.
- **`apply` hints** (M4-D27) live in `apply`'s argument handling and in `usage_error`'s `adopt apply` synonym.
- **The corpus** (`tests/contract/intent_corpus.rs`): rows of `(argv, code, fix_exit)`, run on `common::intent_home()` (two Battle.net clients, `retail` and `era`; one legacy client, `wotlk`; managed DBM on `retail` and `era`, and Questie; HTTP fixtures for their sources). Each wrong argv runs on one copy of the home, which must hash unchanged when the row is an error, and its fix on an independent copy. C4 lands the 56 starting rows of Appendix C.2 that name existing surfaces; D5, D9, E3 and E6 add 11 more; H4 checks at least 60.

### §6.6 Completions, verbosity and the discovery line

- **`omaddons completions <SHELL>`** (`src/app/completions.rs`). `clap_complete::generate(shell, &mut Cli::command(), "omaddons", &mut buf)` writes into a `Vec<u8>`. The `Outcome`'s human form writes the script raw, and its JSON form is `{shell, script}`.
  - The supported shells are clap_complete's five.
  - Generation uses `Cli::command()` with a fixed `term_width(100)` and `max_term_width(100)`, so the script is stable.
- **Verbosity** (M4-D17). `term::Style` gains `detail() -> bool` (level ≥ 1) and `trace() -> bool` (level ≥ 2). `paths_visible()` is renamed `detail()`, and every caller keeps level-1 behaviour.
  - New `trace` log events (`{"event":"log","level":"trace",…}`) are emitted at three places: the release memo's cache decisions (`resolve/cache.rs`), discovery route decisions (`discover/mod.rs`) and the lock wait (`fsx/lock.rs`).
  - `LogLevel` gains `Trace`, an additive wire name.
- **Bare help** gains one line, after "Start with…": `Agents: omaddons capabilities --json · omaddons robot-docs guide · omaddons doctor --json`. The "Start with" line is wrapped to `MAX_WIDTH` like the group lines (it is 117 columns today, §2.1). The test keeps bare help under 30 lines.
  - `help --json` gains `discovery: [{command, argv, purpose}]` (additive).

### §6.7 The semantic manifest, the released baseline and the freeze

**The manifest** (`contract::manifest::build`, A10) is the enforcement artifact (M4-D56). Generation:

1. **Outputs.** For each schema of §6.4 (every command's `data` or report, the envelope, each error code's variant, each event), resolve `$ref`s and normalize: `$defs` names never appear, and an object reached by two routes is recorded once per route. Walk:
   - `properties` give `.<key>`; `items` give `[]`; `additionalProperties` give `{}`;
   - a tagged union records each variant under its tag value (`<view=triage>`), with the fields that variant holds, so a field moving between variants is a change and never hides in a merged path list.

   Each node records its **type** (`string`, `integer`, `number`, `boolean`, `object`, `array`, `null` unions kept explicit, integer and number distinct), **required** (present in every instance of its parent variant) and **nullable** as separate facts, its **bounds** where the schema states them (`minimum`, `maximum`, `minItems`, `maxItems`, `pattern`), its **enum values**, and `opaque` for a `contract::OPAQUE` subtree.
2. **Inputs.** From the built clap tree (`Cli::command().build()`, globals propagated) joined with `COMMANDS` (A1): every canonical command path and its aliases; for every argument (flag or positional), its long and short names and aliases, `default`, value grammar (possible values, value parser kind, range), arity (`num_args`), repeatability, `conflicts_with`, `requires`, and whether it is required; plus the command's exit dictionary and declared exits, whether it binds and whether it stores a plan. Then `state::config::KEYS` with their value types, and the `addons.toml` key paths.
3. **Registries.** Error and warning codes (exits, doctor exit, retryability), actions, failure-mode ids, events and their fields, phases, the two exit dictionaries, `release` env vars.
4. **Persisted formats.** Every `store::KINDS` row, the journal families, `plan` and `doctor_report`, each with its own kind version and its schema's normalized form, tagged so the classifier applies persisted-format rules to them.
5. Serialize as canonical JSON: sorted keys, sorted arrays where order is not meaningful, one trailing newline.

**The readable projection** (`contract::wire::names`) prints the manifest one name per line, sorted, in typed sections, for review:

- `envelope`; `output <command> <dotted path> <type>[?][!]` (`?` nullable, `!` required), with `<tag=value>` for variants; `enum <command> <path> <values>`;
- `input <command> --<flag>|<POSITIONAL> <grammar> default=<v> arity=<n..m> [repeat] [required] [conflicts=<…>] [requires=<…>]`;
- `error <code> exit=<n> doctor_exit=<n> retryable=<true|false|conditional> details=<k:type,…>`;
- `opaque <command> <dotted path>`; `warning <code>`, `action <name>`, `fm <id>`, `event <name> <fields>`; `phase`, `file <kind> <version>`, `config <key> <type>`, `desired <path>`, `env <name>`; `exit general|doctor <n> <name>`; `doctor-ops <op>`.

**The classifier** (`contract::manifest::classify(&baseline, &current)`, A10) compares two manifests node by node and labels each change `additive`, `breaking` or `unclassified`, in the right direction (M4-D56): for outputs, emitting more is additive and emitting less, or less predictably, is breaking; for inputs, accepting more is additive and accepting less, or changing a default, is breaking. `unclassified` counts as breaking pending review. Persisted-format nodes demand their own kind's version bump instead of a wire bump. Member order is never compared.

**The two comparisons** (H2's `tests/contract/wire_names.rs`):

1. **With the released baseline**, `tests/contract/released/<version>.json`, whenever one exists. Any breaking or unclassified change requires `major(SCHEMA_VERSION) > major(baseline)`; additive changes only require the same major and a higher minor. The failure message names the changes, the required version and the vision-comment duty (§4.8). This comparison reads no header of the current golden, so nothing written there can switch it off.
2. **With the current golden**: the generated manifest and projection must equal the committed `manifest.json` and `wire_names.txt`.

**The variables.** `OMADDONS_UPDATE_WIRE_NAMES=1` rewrites the current golden only. `OMADDONS_ADVANCE_RELEASED_BASELINE=<version>` writes a new released baseline, and refuses unless the current golden is at exactly `<version>` and passes comparison 1 against the previous baseline when there is one; only the release procedure uses it (H6 for `1.0`). Both are harness variables (`ENV_VARS` kind `harness`), never read by the binary.

**Tests of the workflow itself** (H2): with a synthetic baseline in a temporary directory, change the contract, run the documented updater without a version bump, and assert that comparison 1 still fails. Cases: an added output field, a removed one, a field made optional, a field made nullable, an integer turned number, a removed flag, a changed default, a new required positional, and an attempt to unfreeze by editing the current golden's header. Unit tests of the classifier (A10) cover each direction rule with synthetic manifests.

### §6.8 Determinism

- **`contract::VOLATILE`** declares every key whose value changes between identical runs, with its reason:

  | Key pattern | Reason |
  |---|---|
  | `meta.*` | the envelope's volatile block |
  | `data.**.duration_ms`, `data.**.lock_held_ms` | timings |
  | `data.**.plan_id`, `data.**.plan_expires_at` | a new plan per dry run |
  | the doctor's top-level `run_id`, `run_dir`, `started_at`, `finished_at`, and `summary.duration_ms` | a new run per invocation |
  | `data.**.tx`, `data.**.run` on real runs | new transactions |
  | `checked_at`-style memo times | wall clock |

- **The repeat test** (`tests/contract/special.rs`, extended) runs every matrix row twice from a fresh copy of its home (so real runs repeat too, not just reads), strips only declared keys, and compares stdout bytes.
  - Equal bytes also mean equal key order, which keeps output deterministic and diffs readable. Key order is a rendering property, not wire semantics: the manifest does not record it (M4-D56), and consumers must not depend on it.
- **The coverage test** fails a `COMMANDS` path with no success row or no failure row in the matrix.
- **The `HashMap` scan** (`tests/determinism.rs`, using `source_scan`) fails a `HashMap<` or `HashSet<` field in any `struct` or `enum` that derives `Serialize` under `src/app`, `src/output`, `src/contract` or `src/doctor`.

comments.text:
**Architecture, part 2 of 2 (§6.9–§6.18): previews and stored plans, the doctor (layout, surface, runtime, view and detectors), the repair transaction, the safety harness, the widget, durability, and the invariants M4 must keep (M4 plan, 2026-10-24).**

### §6.9 Previews and stored plans

#### §6.9.1 `of_plan` and the approval witness: the token of an engine command

```rust
// src/app/precondition.rs
pub struct PlanExtras<'a> {
    pub copy_source: Option<(TargetKey, u64)>,      // copy: --from's key and generation
    pub desired_sha256: Option<Sha256>,             // sync: the addons.toml bytes
    pub update_skips: &'a [(TargetRef, AddonName, SkipReason)], // update: what it chose not to touch
}
pub enum TargetRef { Key(TargetKey), Provisional(String) }   // serialized as the plain string
pub fn of_plan(command: &'static str, plan: &plan::Plan, witnesses: &[ApprovalWitness],
               extras: &PlanExtras) -> Precondition

// src/engine/witness.rs (new, D1; checked under the lock by D8)
pub struct ApprovalWitness {
    pub target: TargetRef,
    pub marker: Sha256,                       // the client marker's bytes: the target's identity
    pub folders: Vec<FolderWitness>,          // see below
    pub absent: Vec<String>,                  // every name the plan creates (folder keys; `AddOns` itself)
    pub inputs: Vec<InputWitness>,            // a --file zip's sha256, a --file <dir>'s listing hash,
                                              // the sync file's sha256, a git checkout's commit
    pub dependencies: Vec<DependencyChoice>,  // which addon satisfies which requirement
    pub judge: JudgeDigest,                   // model.rs:546-550
    stamps: Vec<(PathBuf, TreeStamp)>,        // in memory only: the stamps taken while computing the
                                              // folders' digests; never serialized, never hashed
}
pub struct FolderWitness {
    pub role: WitnessRole,                    // Replaced | Removed | CopySource | Adopted
    pub key: String,                          // the folder key (`FolderName::key()`)
    pub digest: EntryDigest,                  // see below
}
```

**What the witness covers** (M4-D60). Every live folder a replace or remove will move, managed or not, edited or clean; every source folder a `copy` copies; every folder an `adopt` records. Its `EntryDigest` is a SHA-256 over the folder's sorted entries: each regular file as `(path, size, sha256)`, each symlink as `(path, target)`, each directory as `(path)`. Unlike `TreeDigest` (`mutate.rs:119-122`), it counts symlinks and empty directories, so adding either is a change.

**How it is computed, cheaply.** `witness::collect(&plan, &ctx)` runs at the end of `plan::plan`, once the folder plan is known, and before the bound check. For each witnessed folder:

1. Read its `TreeStamp` (`fsx/stamp.rs:112`): one `lstat` per entry.
2. For each regular file whose stamp is racy-clean against the files index (the same test `drift::check` uses in its quick mode), take its `(size, sha256)` from the index. Hash every other file: an unindexed folder, a changed stamp, a file the index does not know.
3. Read the stamp again. If it is unchanged and settled, keep it in the witness's private `stamps` for the under-lock check. If it moved while hashing, or is within the racy slack, keep the digest without a stamp, as `predigest` does for such folders (`swap.rs:583-610`): the under-lock check then always re-hashes that folder.

A clean file therefore costs a `stat`, and a file that was clean at preview and edited afterwards is caught because its stamp moved. Nothing hashes only the files already known to be modified.

**The token's four parts:**

- **`targets`:** one entry per `TargetPlan`: `{key: <key or provisional id>, generation}`. `Precondition.targets` is `Vec<(TargetKey, …)>` today (`precondition.rs:73`) and cannot hold a provisional id; it becomes `Vec<(TargetRef, u64)>`. Tokens of registered targets serialize exactly as before, so M3's `remove` tokens do not change. The provisional id comes from `World`'s deterministic provisional ids (comment 321). A target that registers between the preview and the run changes from provisional id to key and is stale (`targets`). That is correct: registration writes a marker the preview did not.
- **`selection`:** per target, sorted by key. Each element is canonical JSON with sorted keys and sorted id arrays:
  - `ops` (`PlannedOp`, sorted by folder key, then op);
  - `changes` (`{addon, ref, kind, fields, from_version, to_version, folders{added, replaced, removed, skipped[{name, reason}], recorded}}`, sorted by addon);
  - `releases`, sorted by `release_id`. A release with a direct URL is `{release_id, url, expected_hash, blob_sha256}`. A **deferred** asset (Tukui, and any source that resolves the download at fetch time) is `{source, key, release_id, expected_hash, blob_sha256}`, without the URL. Its `PlannedRelease.url` is the resolved address on a fresh download and `None` on a cache hit (`plan.rs:3862-3870`, `4833-4861`), so including it would make every second run of a Tukui plan stale;
  - `creates_addons_dir`.

  Text a human reads (messages, warnings) is excluded.
- **`observed`:**
  - per target, the witness's canonical digest: its marker, folders (role, key, digest), absent names, inputs, dependency choices and judge, in that order. The private stamps are excluded: they are proof of "unchanged since", not content;
  - globally, `build_id` (below), not `tool_version`;
  - `copy_source`, `desired_sha256` and `update_skips` from `extras`.

  `local_changes`, the reviewed draft's choice, is gone from the token: `LocalChanges` is a ten-path warning sample with no digest (§2.7). The `local_changes_replaced` warning is unchanged; it is for people.
- **`command`:** the command path, as in M3.

**`--file <dir>`:** `plan.rs:5444` changes to compute the release id from the directory's listing hash. That is `local::listing_hash` (`sources/local.rs:120`, private today, made `pub(crate)`), whose ids read `listing:<hash>` as `file:` directories' do. An unchanged directory then gives the same id.

**`build_id`.** `tool_version` is `CARGO_PKG_VERSION`, which stays `0.1.0` for every build until M5 (M4-D57), so it cannot tell builds apart. `build.rs`, which already stamps the widget digest, also stamps `OMADDONS_BUILD_ID`: the first 16 hex digits of a SHA-256 over an **explicit input manifest**, `BUILD_ID_INPUTS`, a constant list in `build.rs`:

- `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, `build.rs`, `rust-toolchain.toml` and `.cargo/config.toml` when it exists;
- every file under `src/`, `catalog/` and `omarchy/`, in sorted path order;
- the compiler's version (`rustc -V`, from the `RUSTC` build.rs receives), the target triple, the profile, and the enabled features (`CARGO_FEATURE_*`).

It never includes `skills/`, whose committed guide is generated output with its own identity (M4-D7), so rebuilding never changes the guide and regenerating the guide never changes the build id. `rerun-if-changed` covers each listed path. A test lists every tracked top-level path and asserts each is either in `BUILD_ID_INPUTS` or in an explicit exclusion list (`README.md`, `tests/`, `skills/`, `.beads/`, `docs/`…), so a new build-affecting file cannot be forgotten. `build_id` enters the token's `observed`, the stored plan's `build_id` and `capabilities.build_id`, and `binary_changed` compares it.

**Where it runs.** A bound command must reach a token check on every path, so the check is in three places.

1. **In the engine, before staging.** `engine::tx::run` calls `binding.plan(&plan)` after `plan::plan`. Today it skips that in a dry run (`tx.rs:404`: `Some(binding) if !req.dry_run`). M4 drops the condition, so a bound dry run (`apply --dry-run`, or `--dry-run --if-match`) compares too. A new `PlanBinding { expected: Option<String>, extras }` computes `of_plan` (witnesses included) and calls `precondition::check(expected, &actual, dry_run_argv)`:
   - **`expected: None` (no `--if-match`):** it only computes the token for the dry run's `data.precondition` and the stored plan.
   - **`Some`:** a mismatch is `plan_stale` (`PlanStaleSource::Apply`, not retryable, `details.changed`), before anything is staged.
2. **In the engine, under the commit lock, before the first managed mutation** (D8). In `locked()`, after `refuse_newer_state`:
   1. the generations: `Binding::moved` (generation changed) is `plan_stale`, as for `remove` today;
   2. the witness: `Binding::witness(&target)` re-reads each witnessed folder's `TreeStamp`. Equal to the private stamp and settled: unchanged. Otherwise (no private stamp, or a different one) the folder's `EntryDigest` is recomputed and compared with the token's. Every name in `absent` must still be absent, and the marker's digest must be unchanged. Generation equality alone is never taken as proof;
   3. the re-judge runs, as today (`tx.rs:1104-1139`);
   4. the operations: `Binding::operations(&target, &works)` puts the re-judged works in `selection`'s canonical form for that target and compares them with the run's own pre-lock selection for that target, which check 1 proved equal to the token. A mismatch is `plan_stale` (`selection`);
   5. a `copy`'s staged tree digest must equal its witnessed source digest (checked after staging, before the lock), so a source edit between check 1 and staging is caught too.

   Any failure leaves the target untouched: nothing has moved yet.
3. **At each operation.** The swap's renames carry fsx endpoint predicates (E13): the folder being moved must have the identity the under-lock check saw, and the destination must be absent (or, for an exchange, hold its recorded identity). A folder replaced in the last moment fails its operation, and the engine's existing in-process rollback restores the target. Content is not re-hashed per operation.

The M3 bindings (`remove`, `undo`, `backup restore`, `backup prune`, `errors dismiss`) keep their tokens byte for byte. The under-lock operation comparison (check 2.4) also applies to `remove`, because it changes no token.

**What the checks guarantee.** Other omaddons processes are serialized by the global lock (and by a plan's lease, M4-D61). Every change to a witnessed resource made before check 2 is caught, whoever made it. After check 2, only the identity of what each operation moves is checked. omaddons promises no compare-and-swap against an arbitrary writer saving into `AddOns` during that last interval, because no filesystem primitive it can use offers one. README's "Previews, plans and --if-match" states exactly this scope.

**What the checks cost.** Check 2.2 is one `lstat` per witnessed entry, plus a hash only for what changed. D8 measures it on the realistic home (an update of every addon, 5,040 files) and records the added `lock_held_ms`. The engine already pays the same kind of cost under the lock for unindexed folders (`with_predigests`).

**On each command's no-op path.** `update` (`update.rs:312-314`), `sync` (`sync.rs:673-675`), `copy` (`copy.rs:288-289`), `pin` (`pin.rs:245, 306`) and `adopt` (`adopt/apply.rs:753-777`) never call the engine when they have nothing to change. When bound, each computes `of_plan` over an empty plan of its in-scope targets (with their generations and witnesses) plus its extras, and checks it.

- So the loser of two concurrent typed runs that planned after the winner committed is `plan_stale` rather than a quiet "unchanged". The loser that planned before is stopped by check 2.
- A shared helper, `precondition::check_noop(ctx, command, targets, extras)`, keeps the five call sites to one line each. A test calls every storable command bound to a stale token on a home where it has nothing to do, and expects `plan_stale`.

**Each command's outcome** carries the token into its dry-run data: `InstallData.precondition`, `TargetsData.precondition` (one token for the whole run), `AdoptData.precondition`. Real runs carry `null`. `BINDING_COMMANDS` becomes the twelve paths of M4-D19 plus `doctor fix` and `doctor gc`.

**`TargetsData` commands with an app-level selection** (`update`'s skips, `copy`'s source records) compute their extras before calling the engine, and pass them through `Engine` (`src/app/engine.rs`) to `tx::run`.

#### §6.9.2 The stored plan

```rust
// src/state/plans.rs (new)
#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]
pub struct StoredPlan {
    pub schema_version: String,          // "1.0"
    pub plan_id: PlanId,                 // ULID
    pub created_at: Timestamp,
    pub expires_at: Timestamp,           // created_at + PLAN_TTL
    pub tool_version: String,
    pub build_id: String,                // OMADDONS_BUILD_ID (§6.9.1); binary_changed compares it
    pub intent: StoredIntent,            // M4-D23: the only execution authority
    pub display_argv: Vec<String>,       // derived from intent; never parsed or dispatched; checked on load
    pub actor: Actor,                    // the previewer
    pub reason: Option<String>,
    pub precondition: StoredPrecondition, // {token, parts: {command, targets, selection, observed}};
                                          // the token must be the digest of its parts, checked on load
    pub releases: Vec<PlannedRelease>,   // for blob pins and display
    pub approval: Approval,              // the typed approval summary (M4-D24, M4-D28)
    pub summary: Vec<String>,            // the human lines the dry run printed
}
impl Versioned for StoredPlan { const KIND: &str = "plan"; const VERSION: &str = "1.0"; … }

// src/app/intent.rs (new)
#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
#[serde(tag = "command", rename_all = "snake_case", deny_unknown_fields)]
pub enum StoredIntent {
    Install(InstallIntent), Update(UpdateIntent), Pin(PinIntent), Unpin(PinIntent),
    Adopt(AdoptIntent), Sync(SyncIntent), Copy(CopyIntent), Remove(RemoveIntent),
    Undo(UndoIntent), BackupRestore(RestoreIntent), BackupPrune(PruneIntent),
}
// One example; every variant follows the same rules.
pub struct InstallIntent {
    pub refs: Vec<NormalizedRef>,        // file: refs absolute; catalog names as resolved names
    pub target: TargetRef,               // the selector resolved to a key (or provisional id)
    pub channel: Option<Channel>,
    pub version: Option<String>,
    pub file: Option<AbsPath>,           // AbsPath decodes only absolute, normalized paths
    pub reinstall: bool, pub force: bool, pub no_deps: bool, pub while_running: bool,
}

// src/app/approval.rs (new)
pub struct Approval {
    pub routine: bool,                   // true only when `reasons` is empty
    pub reasons: Vec<ApprovalReason>,    // closed set: dependency_added, folders_removed,
                                         // local_changes_replaced, source_changed, channel_changed,
                                         // while_running, reinstall, force, downgrade
    pub selection: Vec<ApprovedItem>,    // {target_key, target_id, addon, source, channel, release_id,
                                         //  asset, from_version, to_version, op}
    pub scope: ApprovalScope,            // {dependencies_added[], folders_removed[],
                                         //  local_changes_replaced: {count, folders[]},
                                         //  source_changed[], while_running}

```

- **The intent is built once, at preview** (D4), by `StoredIntent::from_args(&ctx, &args)`. It makes every path absolute with `std::path::absolute` against the process directory and normalizes it, resolves each target selector to its key (or provisional id), resolves catalog names, and records each effective safety option as a typed field. The commands' own working-directory reads (`install.rs:408`, `adopt/apply.rs:125`, `sync.rs:389`, `info.rs:360`, `targets.rs:373`, `inspect.rs:507`) then see only absolute paths at `apply` time, so no `base_dir` plumbing is needed.
- `display_argv` is `intent.display_argv()`: the argv a person would type for that intent. On load, a stored `display_argv` that is not the intent's own is a sign of a hand edit, and the plan is `plan_not_found` (`unreadable`).
- **`approval`** is computed by every storable dry run (D4) from the engine plan and the command's outcome, and returned as `data.approval` too (`null` on real runs). `routine` is false whenever any reason applies.
- **Written** by the dry run of every storable command (M4-D22) **that would change something**, through `fsx` with `Writer::Derived`, at `<cache>/plans/<plan_id>.json` (0600, since the intent and `reason` are the user's).
  - A dry run with nothing to do stores no plan: `plan_id: null`, no `apply` hint, no warning (M4-D61). Its token is still returned.
  - Written after the outcome is computed and before it renders, so `data.plan_id` names a file that exists.
  - A write failure, or a full store, is the warning `plan_not_stored` (fix: prose about the cache directory), with `plan_id: null`. It never fails the dry run, whose preview and token stand.
- **`data` gains three keys** (additive) on every storable command, `null` on real runs: `plan_id`, `plan_expires_at` and `approval`.
- **`commands[]`** gains `{action: "apply", command: "omaddons apply <id>", argv: ["omaddons","apply","<id>"], destructive: <the command's CLI_PATHS destructive flag>}` when a plan was stored.
- **The human form** adds one line, and a second under `-v`:

  ```text
  Plan <id> stored for 24 hours. Run exactly this: omaddons apply <id>
  (-v) Or bind a typed run to it: --if-match <token>
  ```

  The token is in the JSON regardless; a human rarely needs it, and on every dry run it is noise.

- **Admission, cleanup and dedupe** (M4-D24). The writer takes `<cache>/plans/.lock`, an `fsx::lock::Lease` (a named advisory lock D4 adds, since it uses one first; D5 reuses it for the plan lease), never the global commit lock. Under it:
  1. It lists `<cache>/plans/` (bounded: at most `PLANS_MAX_FILES` + `PLANS_SWEEP_MAX` entries are read; a directory holding more is itself a finding, row 45) and prunes at most `PLANS_SWEEP_MAX` expired plans with their leases, oldest first (`fsx::prune(PruneReason::PlanExpiry)`, caller `src/state/plans.rs`, added to `PRUNE_CALLERS`).
  2. It looks for an unexpired plan with the same intent and token. If one exists, it returns that plan's id and its original expiry, and writes nothing.
  3. It writes the new plan only if the store is then within `PLANS_MAX_FILES` and `PLANS_MAX_BYTES`, and the plan within `PLAN_MAX_BYTES`. Otherwise it writes nothing and warns `plan_not_stored`.
  - It never evicts an unexpired plan.
  - **No global lock is needed.** `apply` reads its plan once, under its lease, and refuses an expired plan itself, so deleting an expired plan races with nothing that matters.
  - prune's lock modes do not fit: `Own` refuses a victim that is not the caller's transaction (`prune.rs:104-118`), and `Acquire` takes the global lock, which dry runs never take (`prune.rs:57-61`). fsx gains `LockUse::Expired`, accepted only for `Kind::Plan` victims whose `expires_at` (read by fsx from the file, bounded by `PLAN_MAX_BYTES`) has passed, and for `Kind::PlanLease` victims whose plan is such a victim and whose lease fsx can take itself at that moment. Any other kind under it is `scope_denied`, by a unit test.
  - prune's `Kind::Plan` moves from `<state>/plans/` (`prune.rs:371-373`) to `<cache>/plans/`, and `Kind::PlanLease` is new.
  - Retention runs the same bounded sweep after each commit (`engine/retention.rs`), so repeated batches converge on a store with no expired plan.
- **Reading** is bounded and fail-closed: a file larger than `PLAN_MAX_BYTES`, a newer major, an undecodable file, an unknown intent variant or option, a relative or non-normalized path, a `display_argv` that is not the intent's, or a token that is not its parts' digest is `plan_not_found` with `details.reason: "unreadable"` and the path (M4-D23 step 2). A plan is never acted on unless it decodes and agrees with itself.

#### §6.9.3 `apply`

```text
omaddons apply <PLAN_ID> [--dry-run]      (global flags as usual; --if-match is a usage error here)
```

1. **Resolve the id.** A prefix of at least 8 characters matching one file. None is `plan_not_found` (fix `omaddons help apply`, alternative `omaddons adopt --apply` per M4-D27). Several is `ref_ambiguous`, with one `apply <id>` alternative per candidate.
2. **Load** fail-closed (§6.9.2).
3. **Take the lease** (M4-D61), unless `--dry-run`: `fsx::lock::Lease::acquire(<cache>/plans/<plan_id>.lease, PLAN_LEASE_TIMEOUT)`. The file is opened or created through fsx, never with `create_new`, and the lock is a `flock`, so a dead holder leaves nothing behind that blocks. A timeout is `locked` (5, retryable) with `details.lease: <plan_id>` and the holder's `{pid, command, age_s}`. The lease is held until step 7 has every target's outcome. After acquiring it, `apply` reloads the plan file, since the holder before it may have finished.
4. **Check.** Each failure is `plan_stale`, not retryable, with `fix_argv` = the intent's `display_argv` plus `--dry-run`:
   - `expires_at` has passed → `details.reason: "expired"`;
   - `build_id` differs from this binary's → `"binary_changed"`;
   - an absolute input the intent names is gone → `"input_missing"`, with `details.path`;
   - history holds a committed transaction whose `plan` is this id (a bounded backward scan, as `plans show`'s, §6.9.3a) → `"already_applied"`, with `details.txs`. This covers a partial first application too: `apply` never resumes one on its own.
5. **Build the `Context`.**
   - The intent's `while_running` holds: it is part of what was approved.
   - Offline-ness is `apply`'s own (`--offline` or `OMADDONS_OFFLINE`), never the preview's. A plan previewed offline and applied online revalidates like any other, and a release found since is `plan_stale`. An offline `apply` of a plan with network sources cannot revalidate, so it is `offline` (fix: rerun without `--offline`). A plan with only local and cached-blob sources applies offline.
   - `actor` and `reason` follow M4-D25.
   - `if_match: Some(stored token)`, `force_revalidate: true` (M4-D20) and `applying: Some(plan_id)`, which the engine copies into history (`plan`) and into the doorbell's `command` (`"apply"`).
6. **Execute.** `StoredIntent::execute(&ctx) -> Result<StorableOutcome>` converts the intent into the command's own argument struct (`impl From<&InstallIntent> for InstallArgs`, and so on) and calls its `run` (`install::run`, `update::run`, …). Each already returns its typed outcome (§2.7). Nothing is re-parsed. The debug notes and `lock_released` events each dispatch arm emits today move into one helper, `app::emit_side_events(out, &outcome)`, which the arm and `apply` both call.
7. **Wrap the result:** `ApplyData {plan_id, applied: {command, display_argv}, approved?, result, outcomes[]}`, rendered once. The envelope's exit code is the executed command's.
   - `outcomes[]` is `StorableOutcome::target_outcomes()`: one `{target, key, status: committed | unchanged | stale | failed, tx, error_code}` per target of the approval, in target order (M4-D61).
   - `--dry-run` runs steps 1, 2 and 4–6 with `dry_run: true`, takes no lease, takes no global lock, and stores nothing. Its `result` is the fresh dry run (with its own `approval`), and `approved` is the stored `approval`, so a client can show "approved: … / now: …".

**`ApplyData`'s schema** is a union of complete wrapper variants, generated from a serde enum with one variant per storable command. Each variant fixes `applied.command` with `const` and gives `result` that command's data schema; `approved` is the shared `Approval` schema. A union on `result` alone would not tie it to its sibling `applied.command`, so the contract suite rejects a mismatched command/result pair and an unknown nested result field (A3's strict transform). The manifest lists each variant under its tag (`output apply <command=install> result.…`).

#### §6.9.3a `plans show` (D9, M4-D63)

```text
omaddons plans show <PLAN_ID> [--json]       (read-only: mutates false, group Look; no lock, no network)
```

1. **Resolve the id** as `apply` does. A prefix that matches no file is not yet an error: the history scan below may still find the plan.
2. **Read the plan** if the file exists, with the same bounded, fail-closed load. An unreadable file is reported as `stored: true, readable: false`, never acted on.
3. **Scan history backwards** for lines whose `plan` is this id, stopping at the first line older than the plan's `created_at` (or than `PLAN_TTL` before now, when the file is gone), and at most `PLAN_EVIDENCE_LINES_MAX` lines. The scan reads the raw file in reverse in bounded blocks; it never loads the whole history.
4. **Judge the state:**
   - `pending`: stored, unexpired, no commit recorded;
   - `completed`: a committed transaction for every target in `approval.selection`;
   - `partial`: some, not all;
   - `expired`: past `expires_at`, no commit recorded;
   - `unknown`: the file is gone or unreadable, so the approved targets are not known, or the scan stopped at its bound before reaching `created_at`.
   Current addon versions are never consulted: matching versions are not evidence.
5. **Data:** `{plan_id, state, stored, readable, created_at?, expires_at?, build_id?, build_matches?, intent?: {command, display_argv}, approval?, inputs[], evidence: {targets[{target, key, tx, result, at}], complete}}`. A missing file with no evidence at all is `plan_not_found`.

The guide's core loop (Appendix C.1) tells an agent that lost an `apply`'s output to run `plans show` before it previews again or changes anything.

#### §6.9.4 Retention and pins

- `engine::retention::run`'s pin closure gains `plans::unexpired_blob_pins(&paths)`: every `releases[].blob_sha256` of plans whose `expires_at` is in the future, read under the eviction lock. It reads at most `PLANS_MAX_FILES` files of at most `PLAN_MAX_BYTES` each. An unreadable file pins nothing.
- **Local zips.** A local zip's release (`file:` refs and `--file <zip>`) records its archive digest (`@sha256:`) as today. At `apply`, re-planning re-hashes the file, and a changed file changes `selection`; a missing one is `input_missing`.

#### §6.9.5 Freshness at `apply`

- `Freshness::Revalidate` already exists (`resolve/cache.rs:36`), and `install`, `copy` and `pin` already use it (`copy.rs:285`, `pin.rs:250`). `update` and `sync` use `Window(SOURCE_RECHECK_MIN_INTERVAL)`. What is new is a `Context.force_revalidate` flag that `apply` sets: each command's freshness choice yields `Revalidate` when it is set (and `OfflineOnly` still wins when `apply` itself is offline). The memo's 15-minute window does not apply, and each ref is probed exactly as `install` probes today.
  - A GitHub stable ref costs one `releases/latest`, plus `release.json` only if the tag moved.
  - A git ref costs one commits-feed request, usually a 304.
  - WoWInterface and Tukui use one `filedetails` or list call.
  - WowAce uses one `PROPFIND`.
- Everything else (downloads, verification) reuses the blob cache by expected hash. A plan applied within its TTL typically downloads nothing.
- Every probe writes the release memo, including one that ends in `plan_stale` (M4-D20). The re-preview a client runs after a stale `apply` then shows the new release.

#### §6.9.6 Tests (D7, with D8's and D9's own)

**The release-landing scenarios.** Each is an HTTP fixture sequence (`common::http::fixture_seq`) in which the second `releases/latest` answers a newer tag:

| Command | Expected result |
|---|---|
| `install` | `plan_stale` with `selection`; nothing installed (tree hash unchanged) |
| `update` (inside the 15-minute window, so a typed `--if-match` still succeeds) | the typed `--if-match` run succeeds; `apply` is stale; the next `update --dry-run`, still inside the window, shows the new release (the memo refresh) |
| `sync` | stale |
| `copy` (already revalidates, so a typed `--if-match` is stale too) | stale |
| a Tukui `install` whose first dry run downloads and whose `apply` hits the cache, with no release change | **succeeds** (deferred releases are keyed without their URL) |

**The witness scenarios** (D8), each for `install`, `update` and `copy`, and each asserting that the target is unchanged (tree hash) after the stale run:

- a file edited between the preview and the bound run;
- a late edit: the bound run paused at `engine.snapshot.prestaged` (after its first check, before its lock), a file edited, the run resumed: `plan_stale` from the under-lock check;
- the eleventh changed file of a folder edited (the warning names ten);
- a same-size content edit (the stamp moves, the size does not);
- a file that was clean at preview edited afterwards;
- a file deleted, and a file replaced by another of the same name;
- a symlink or an empty directory added inside a replaced folder;
- a folder created at a name the plan creates;
- a `copy` source folder edited while its record is unchanged;
- the re-judged operations differing from the approved ones (a dependency's requirement satisfied by hand in between): `plan_stale`, `selection`;
- the folder being moved replaced by another directory at a pause at `engine.revalidated`: the operation's identity predicate fails and the target rolls back.

And one cost record: the under-lock check's `lock_held_ms` on the realistic home, printed by the perf suite (a report, not a budget).

**The no-op scenarios**, one per storable command: bind to a stale token on a home where the command has nothing to do, and expect `plan_stale` (§6.9.1). A preview with nothing to do stores no plan and offers no `apply`.

**The concurrent-change scenarios**, run for every storable command: between the dry run and `apply`, another process commits on an affected target. The result is `plan_stale` with `targets`.

- For `copy`, the source client changes.
- For `sync`, the file is edited (`observed`).
- For `adopt`, a folder is touched (`observed`).
- For `undo`, `remove`, `backup restore` and `backup prune`, the M3 scenarios run through `apply`.

**The two-applier scenarios** (M4-D61), on a two-client home:

- **Split:** two `apply`s of one plan, each paused between target commits (at `engine.cleanup.done`). Exactly one holds the lease and runs; the other waits, then reports `already_applied` with the first one's transactions. The plan's targets are never split between the two invocations.
- **Lease timeout:** the first holder paused past `PLAN_LEASE_TIMEOUT`: the second exits `locked` with `details.lease`.
- **Interference:** while one `apply` is paused between targets, a different command commits on its second target. The `apply` reports the first target `committed` and the second `stale`, with accurate transaction ids, and `plans show` reports `partial`.

**The lifecycle scenarios:**

- expired: `OMADDONS_NOW` advanced past `expires_at`;
- binary changed: the file's `build_id` edited, and the test asserts the reason;
- a plan file truncated, oversized, given an unknown intent variant or option, a relative path, a `display_argv` that disagrees with its intent, or a token that disagrees with its parts: `plan_not_found` with `reason: "unreadable"`;
- `input_missing`: the `--file` zip deleted;
- the working directory of the preview deleted: `apply` still succeeds (absolute intent);
- unknown id: `plan_not_found`;
- an ambiguous prefix;
- a second `apply` of the same plan: `already_applied`;
- `apply --dry-run`, which writes nothing (tree hash) and takes no lock;
- `LockUse::Expired` given a record file, a blob, an unexpired plan or a held lease: `scope_denied`.

**The quota scenarios** (D4):

- 600 expired plans: one dry run's cleanup deletes at most `PLANS_SWEEP_MAX`; while the store is above `PLANS_MAX_FILES`, dry runs store nothing (`plan_not_stored`) and each deletes another batch; repeated dry runs converge to no expired plan, and once within quota the store never grows past it;
- a store full of live plans: the next dry run returns its preview and token with `plan_id: null` and `plan_not_stored`, and every live plan survives;
- a preview repeated with an unchanged world: the same `plan_id` comes back, with its original expiry;
- concurrent dry runs: the admission lock keeps the store within both quotas;
- an oversized plan file: pin discovery and `apply` both fail closed on it.

**The reconciliation scenarios** (D9):

- a successful `apply` whose stdout was closed before it rendered: `plans show` reports `completed` with the transactions;
- a partial multi-target `apply` (a failpoint error on the second target): `partial`;
- an expired plan with no commit: `expired`;
- the cache deleted after a successful `apply`: `stored: false`, the evidence, `state: unknown`;
- no recorded commit and no file: `plan_not_found`;
- a history longer than `PLAN_EVIDENCE_LINES_MAX` since the plan: `evidence.complete: false`, `state: unknown`;
- `plans show` writes nothing and makes no request (tree hash, `net.log`).

**The `<state>` rule.** Every dry run still leaves `<state>` untouched (`special.rs:251`, now covering every storable command).

```text
  gc.rs           doctor gc: the retention plan and its deletions (the only doctor file that may call
                  fsx::prune; M4-D36)
src/engine/resource.rs Resource, ResourceSet, overlap (M4-D62; E13)
src/engine/repair.rs   the repair transaction: fixes lowered to primitives → prepared → steps → done →
                       history → committed; recovery; fences; activation barriers; undo (§6.14)
src/app/doctor.rs      CLI wiring: the doctor command tree, outcomes, the doctor envelope
```

**The failure-mode row:**

```rust
pub struct FailureMode {
    pub id: &'static str,                 // "fm-concurrency_primitives-journal-pending"
    pub subsystem: Subsystem,             // closed enum of the 13 doctor-contract subsystems
    pub severity: Severity,               // P0–P3, fixed per failure mode
    pub title: &'static str,              // "an interrupted change waits to be finished"
    pub description: &'static str,        // what the state is
    pub why: &'static str,                // why it matters
    pub tier: Tier,                       // Cached | Quick | Default | Deep
    pub online: bool,
    pub cost_ms: u32,                     // declared estimate, for --budget's refusal and capabilities.cost_summary
    pub requires: &'static [Layer],       // Config | Registry | Discovery | Records | Inventory
    pub detect: fn(&DoctorView, &Selection, &mut Budget) -> Detected,  // findings, plus `incomplete` if cut short
    pub fix: Option<FixerSpec>,
    pub manual: Option<fn(&Finding) -> Remediation>,
}
pub struct FixerSpec {
    pub plan: fn(&DoctorView, &Finding) -> Result<Vec<Fix>, Refusal>,   // presentation-level fixes (§6.14.1)
    pub writes_to: &'static [ScopeName],  // for capabilities: State, Config, Cache, ClientMeta, AddOns, Skill
    pub ops: &'static [FixKind],          // write | chmod | quarantine | flatten | delegate
    pub enabled: bool,                    // M4-D39
    pub needs_force: bool,                // M4-D38
    pub cardinality: Cardinality,         // Low (≤ 10 paths) | High
    pub preconditions: &'static [Precondition], // LockHeld | InflightFree | ClientNotRunning | Online | SameFs
}
```

- **Severity is fixed per failure mode.** One instance of a failure mode is as bad as another, and a fixed severity lets the widget and `--severity` filter without reading evidence.
- **`Subsystem`** is the doctor contract's thirteen names: `state_files, configs, schemas, caches, sockets, hooks, plugins, secrets, permissions, external_artifacts, concurrency_primitives, network, userland_state`. `sockets` and `hooks` have no failure modes in omaddons, and capabilities lists them as `applicable: false`.
- **A finding** carries `instance` (the stable, resource-specific key of M4-D30: `<fm-id>@<target key | machine>[:<discriminator>]`) and `label` (its human form), beside its evidence. `--since` and `explain` use `instance`; nothing compares `label`.

### §6.11 The doctor's surface

```text
omaddons doctor [diagnose]   [--only <ids>] [--skip <ids>] [--severity P0|P1|P2|P3] [--quick] [--include-deep]
                             [--online] [--budget <dur>] [--since <run>] [--robot-triage] [-t <targets>]
omaddons doctor fix          [the selection flags above] [--dry-run] [--if-match <token>] [--force --yes]
omaddons doctor undo [<run>] [--dry-run]    (no run: the newest fix run whose repair is not yet undone)
omaddons doctor explain <fm-id | instance key> [-t <target>]
omaddons doctor health
omaddons doctor ls [--limit N]
omaddons doctor diff [<run>]                (no ref: what fix would change; with a run: findings since it)
omaddons doctor gc --before <date | age> [--dry-run] [--if-match <token>] [--yes]
omaddons doctor capabilities
omaddons doctor robot-docs
```

- **One path, one meaning.** `doctor` and `doctor diagnose` never mutate. Only `doctor fix`, `doctor undo` and `doctor gc` do, and each is its own command path with `mutates: true`.
  - The doctor contract's `doctor --fix` and `doctor --explain <id>` are not flags here. Typed anyway, they are intent hints (C.2): a usage error whose fix is `omaddons doctor fix …` or `omaddons doctor explain <id>`.
  - So a typo such as `omaddons doctr --fix --force --yes` can never get a runnable fix: `subcommand_fix` turns a guessed mutating path into `help` (`cli.rs:879`), and no read-only path accepts a mutating flag.
- **Global flags apply as everywhere.** `--json`, `--robot`, `--quiet`, `-v`, `--no-color`, `--no-progress`, `--actor` and `--reason` work as for every command. `--reason` and `--actor` are recorded on the repair's history line. `--dry-run` is global (as everywhere): on the read-only verbs it changes nothing, as `special.rs`'s read-only test expects.
- **`--force` requires `--yes`.** `requires = "yes"` is set at the clap level (exit 64 otherwise).
- **`gc`** requires `--before`. A real run requires `--yes`; `--dry-run` does not. `--before` takes a date or an age (`30d`, `12h`), parsed by the same function as `history --since`. `DOCTOR_GC_SUGGESTED_AGE` (30 days, `limits.rs`) is the age remediations suggest. `--if-match` binds a real run to the deletion set a `--dry-run` showed (§6.14.5).
- **`undo`.** Without a run, it selects the newest run of kind `fix` whose committed repair is not yet undone. It never selects a diagnose, which has no transaction. The word `latest` is not accepted as a run: it is a usage error whose fix is `omaddons doctor undo` (the `latest` symlink is for reading reports, and may point at a diagnose).
- **`--only` and `--skip`** take comma lists of failure-mode ids or subsystem names (M4-D30). An unknown id is `usage` (64), with the closest id as the fix.
- **`--severity P2`** reports P0–P2 and hides P3.
- **`--budget 500ms`** refuses to start (exit 4, `doctor_refused`, reason `over_budget`) when the selected detectors' declared `cost_ms` sum exceeds it, and otherwise is also the run's deadline: each detector's `Budget` gets its share, and one that runs out stops and reports `check-incomplete` (M4-D43). Without `--budget`, each tier's default deadline applies (`QUICK_DETECTOR_BUDGET` for `quick`; `DOCTOR_DETECTOR_DEADLINE` for the others).
- **An online-only selection.** `--only` naming only online failure modes without `--online` is `online_required` (exit 6). A mixed selection runs the offline ones and lists the rest in `skipped`.
- **`--since <run>`** adds to the report a `since: {run, new[], resolved[], unchanged}` comparison of finding **instance keys** with that run's `report.json`. Two stuck journals on retail are two instances, so resolving one shows as one resolved and one unchanged.
- **`-t`** narrows target-scoped detectors to the selected targets. Machine-level findings (journals with no target, the lock, the widget, the skill, credentials, caches) are always included unless `--only` excludes them.
- **The human output** of `diagnose`:
  - a summary line ("6 clients · 42 checks (3 online checks skipped) · 2 findings (1 P0, 1 P3)");
  - one block per finding, by severity: the id, its label, a one-line explanation, and `→ <remediation>`;
  - skipped checks, as a count with reasons, and in full under `-v`;
  - the run id, and `omaddons doctor explain <id>` for detail.
- **The human output** of `fix`: what was repaired, what was delegated, what needs `--force --yes`, what is manual, then the run, the transaction and the undo command.

**JSON report keys, by verb** (Appendix A has the full shapes):

| Verb | Report keys (between `exit_code` and `warnings`) |
|---|---|
| `diagnose` | `view: "full"`, `doctor_contract_version, run_id, run_dir, started_at, finished_at, state, summary{total_findings, by_severity, auto_fixable, needs_force, manual, online_required, skipped, incomplete, duration_ms}, findings[], skipped[], since?, next_steps[]` |
| `diagnose --robot-triage` | `view: "triage"`, `summary{ok, total_findings, auto_fixable}, quick_ref[], findings[], actions_planned[], recommended_command, recommended_argv, capabilities_command, robot_docs_command` |
| `fix` | the diagnose keys plus `actions[]`, `delegated[]`, `tx`, `summary{findings_before, findings_after, actions_taken, actions_failed, bytes_backed_up, backups_restored}`, `actions_jsonl_path, backups_dir, undo_command, undo_argv`; under `--dry-run`, `precondition`, `actions_planned[]` and `delegated_planned[]` |
| `undo` | `run_id` (the undo's own run), `reverted_run, tx, undo_tx, state, actions_taken, already_undone`; under `--dry-run`, `actions_planned[]`, with `commands[]` offering `omaddons undo <tx> --dry-run` for a preview that stores a bindable plan |
| `explain` | `failure_mode{id, subsystem, severity, title, description, why, tier, fixer{…}|null, manual}, instances[]` |
| `health` | `status (ok|findings|unsafe|concurrency), findings, by_severity, last_run, run_id` (and the one-line human form) |
| `ls` | `runs[{run_id, kind, started_at, state, exit_code, action_count, tx, reverted_run, undo_complete}]` |
| `diff` | `actions_planned[]` and `precondition`, or `since{…}` |
| `gc` | `dry_run, before, deletions[{kind, run_id?, target?, tx?, path, bytes, may_hold_only_copy}], excluded[{kind, run_id?, path, pin}], undo_lost[], latest{from, to}`, and `precondition` under `--dry-run` |
| `capabilities` | the doctor contract's shape (§6.11.1) |
| `robot-docs` | `{format: "markdown", content}` |

**One schema per path.** `doctor diagnose` has two report shapes, so its schema is one `oneOf` tagged by `view` (`full` or `triage`), generated from a serde enum with `#[serde(tag = "view")]`. Every other path has one shape. `doctor_contract_version` is the revision of the external doctor contract the shapes implement ("1.0"); the wire names themselves follow `schema_version`'s bump rule like every envelope (M4-D3, M4-D56). There is no separate `doctor_version`.
