| `src/app/mod.rs` (`COMMANDS`, dispatch, `emit_side_events`) | A1, A4, A5, A7, B1, B3, D5, D9, E3, E4, E6, E7, E8 | **A1 first** (it adds fields to every row); each command leaf adds its own rows afterwards and rebases |
| `src/error.rs` (code rows) | A9, A3, D4, D5, E3, E10, F*, H1 | **A9, then A3** (both touch every row); later leaves append rows with their specs |
| `src/cli.rs` | A1 (`auth github`), A8, C1, C2, D5, E3 | keep each hook in its own function; A1's subcommand first; C1's hooks before D5's `Context` fields |
| `src/engine/journal.rs` | E11, E13 (`FileId::same` moves out), E5, E14, F1 | **E11 (`LiveView`, the classifier) → E13 → E5 (the second family's entry points) → E14 (the barrier order) → F1 (detectors read only)** |
| `src/engine/tx.rs`, `src/engine/swap.rs` | D2 (`Binding`, the dry-run check), D8 (the under-lock checks, swap predicates), E5 (recovery entry points), G3 (append hooks, `CommitWindow`) | **D2 → D8**; E5 touches recovery calls only; **G3 last** |
| `src/fsx/` (`session.rs`, `mutate.rs`, `sys.rs`, `scope.rs`, `prune.rs`, `lock.rs`) | E13 (`Expect` predicates), D4 (`Lease`, `LockUse::Expired`), D8, E3 (`untracked_logged`), E5 (the symlink rename, `with_skill_dirs`, `RepairJournal`), E14 (`with_fences`), E7, E8 (prune kinds), G3 (buffering, `Durability::Derived`, `CommitWindow`), B3 (History row) | **E13 first, G3 last**; E5 before E14, E7 and E8, each later one rebasing; E3, D4 and B3 touch separate functions |
| `src/engine/undo.rs` | E7 | one leaf |
| `src/engine/repair.rs` | E5, E14, E7, F2 | **E5 → E14 → E7**; F2 adds a fixer, not engine code |
| `src/app/status.rs`, `src/app/issues.rs` | E1 (move), F1 (journal titles), F8 (registry), E10 (fixes), G1 (update entries) | **E1 → F1 → F8**, then E10 and G1 rebase |
| `src/app/precondition.rs` | D1, D2, D3, D8, E6, E7 | **D1 first** |
| `src/app/{update,sync,copy,pin,install,remove}.rs`, `adopt/apply.rs` | C2 (the preflight), D2, D3 (no-op checks), D4 (`from_args`) | C2 touches argument handling only; D2 and D3 before D4 |
| `src/resolve/cache.rs` | D5 (`force_revalidate`) | one leaf |
| `src/state/history.rs`, `history_tail.rs` | E12 (target-less lines), D5 (`plan`), D9 (the backward scan), E5 (repair lines), E7 (selection), B3 (`skill_dirs[]`) | **E12 → E5 → E7**; D5, D9 and B3 are additive and rebase |
| `build.rs` | D1 (`OMADDONS_BUILD_ID`, `BUILD_ID_INPUTS`), B1 (`OMADDONS_GUIDE_SHA256`) | **D1 first**; B1 adds one block |
| `src/limits.rs` and its snapshot | B3, D4, D5, D9, E3, E6, E8, F1, G3 | append rows; re-accept the snapshot in the same commit |
| `omarchy/Model.js`, `Service.qml` | G1, G2 (and `CLI_PATHS` rows from every command leaf) | **G1 → G2**; command leaves add only `CLI_PATHS` rows |
| `tests/contract/matrix.rs` and snapshots | every command leaf | append rows; one snapshot file per row, so conflicts are rare |
| `tests/contract/rules_allowlist.txt` | A3 (creates it), H1 (empties it), owning leaves that fix a listed violation | only ever remove lines |
| `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` | every leaf after B1 (common rule 17) | regenerate with `OMADDONS_UPDATE_SKILL=1 cargo test --test skill` after rebasing, never merge by hand |

**How to work in parallel.**

- Claim a leaf with its file list.
- Keep commits small, and rebase before each gate run.
- Coordinate through `SendMessage` and `ListAgents`.
- Treat unrecognized working-tree changes as a peer's work (CLAUDE.md).

### §10.6 Slices

Progress is judged by four slices, each with a demonstrable exit. When a slice's last leaf closes, the agent closing it runs the slice's demo and records it as a comment on the milestone epic in the `[x] … : evidence` style. A slice whose demo fails reopens the leaf responsible (`--deps discovered-from`). M3 did not record its slice demos as they landed (§2.6). The closing agent of each slice owns its demo. H6 checks that the demos of slices 1–3 exist before it starts; slice 4 contains H6 itself, so H6 verifies slice 4's pre-tag parts during the checkpoint and records its completed demo after the tag exists (§11.3).

| `slice-2` Preview, then apply exactly | D1–D9, E13, G1 | install, then update `--dry-run` then `apply`; a release landing in between gives `plan_stale`, and the re-preview shows it; a late hand edit is caught under the lock; a second `apply` is `already_applied`; two appliers never split a plan; `plans show` reconciles a lost output; a Tukui plan applies from the cache; the widget's Update with a routine matching plan (no dialog), one that adds a dependency (dialog) and a moved one (dialog), in QML scenarios | 6, 7, 8 (updates) |
| `slice-3` Diagnose and repair | E1–E12, E14, F1–F10, G2, G3 | `doctor` on a home with each §2.3 stuck state planted; a set-aside with `--force --yes`, then `doctor undo`; a set-aside, a later install, and the refused undo; a stuck repair that fences only its own resources; a bound gc; the credential fix from the Issues view (QML) and Undo last; the harness green at every primitive boundary; the fsync counts table | 8 (doctor), 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 16 |
| `slice-4` Freeze and close | A6, B2, B4, H1–H6 | the recipes pass; the audit's change list and the empty allowlist; the golden and the updater tests; README; the tag and the released baseline | 3, 4, 14, 17, 18 |

## §11 Testing strategy, the checkpoint protocol and risks

### §11.1 What runs where

| Layer | Runs in | New in M4 |
|---|---|---|
| Unit tests | the gate | the registries, `DetailSpec`s, `of_plan` canonicalization and its pinned token, the witness's collection, `StoredIntent` round trips and rejections, the approval reasons, resource overlap, the fsx endpoint predicates, the renderer and its stamp, `TargetVocabulary`, the lowering and the repair inverses, `LockUse::Expired`'s refusals, the total `exit_for`, the manifest's classifier, `selectionMatches` and the routine rule (bun) |
| Contract suite (`tests/contract/`) | the gate | strict schema validation (with its own composition tests) of every envelope, event and envelope snapshot; `OPAQUE`; typed `details`; `apply`'s wrapper variants; exit observation; the doctor envelope mode; the rule test and its allowlist; the intent corpus (runs fixes, and proves wrong invocations change nothing); the manifest and its comparisons with the current golden and, once one exists, the released baseline; the updater tests; observed keys ⊆ manifest; the coverage and repeat tests over every path |
| Differential (`tests/journal.rs`) | the gate | `journal::diagnose` against real recovery over every crash-matrix state (E11, extended by E5 and E14's barrier cases) |
| End-to-end (`tests/*.rs`) | the gate | capabilities, robot-docs, skill (and its fixed point), recipes, completions, apply (witness, lease, quotas), plans show, doctor, doctor repair (fences, reactivation, gc), determinism, durability counts and barrier failures |
| Crash matrices (`tests/engine_crash.rs`) | the gate | the repair family at every primitive boundary; the barrier cases; every existing matrix rerun under D8's predicates and G3's group commit |
| Safety harness (`tests/doctor_harness.rs`) | the gate | the 14 properties of §6.15, every primitive boundary witnessed |
| Widget pipeline (`scripts/widget-test.sh`) | the gate | the plan runner and its routine rule, the doctor reducer, the new templates' argv, the output-cap test for `apply` and doctor envelopes |
| Exhaustive harness (`tests/doctor_harness.rs`, ignored) | the checkpoint | boundaries crossed with the declared pairs and repeated-recovery depths |
| Perf budgets (`tests/perf.rs`, release, ignored) | the checkpoint | `capabilities` < 20 ms, `doctor health` < 200 ms, `quick` detectors < 5 ms each, `status --cached` < 5 ms with the cached tier, the btrfs commit windows; reports (not budgets) of the under-lock witness check's cost |
| Compat (`tests/compat_m2.rs`, `tests/compat_m3.rs`, debug, ignored) | the checkpoint | the M3 build against M4 state, built with its recorded toolchain; never a pre-accepted `SKIP` |
| Fuzz (`argc fuzz-all`) | the checkpoint | the `journal` target (both families), 30 min; every other target 10 min |
| Live probes (`OMADDONS_LIVE=1`) | the checkpoint | `doctor --online` against the real hosts (one request per source); the skill-recipes fixtures re-recorded and compared |
| Real machine (`OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE=1`) | the checkpoint, under the plan's approval (§3.3) | `doctor` on the real home (reviewed finding by finding); `doctor fix --dry-run`; `update --dry-run` → `apply` on one addon of a non-Forever client, undone; `install-skill --dry-run` against the real home, and a real install into a tempdir only |

### §11.2 How each new protocol is proven

| Protocol | Proof |
|---|---|
| Tokens and witnesses on engine commands (D1–D3) | the covered-input table (one row per input, every witnessed resource included); the pinned token; a cache hit equals a download, per source; a `touch` without a content change does not move the token; state changed between preview and run for every command (`pause` failpoints); the no-op and dry-run checks; stale runs change nothing (tree hash) |
| The approval under the commit lock (D8) | the witness scenarios, late edits after the first check among them; the re-judged operations compared; a folder replaced at the last moment fails its operation's predicate; every crash matrix unchanged; the cost reported |
| Stored plans and `apply` (D4–D7) | the release-landing fixture sequences per source; the memo refresh; the lifecycle refusals, hand-edited plan files among them; the quotas; the split, lease-timeout and interference races; repeated applies (`already_applied`); dry runs leave `<state>` untouched and take no lock |
| Reconciliation (D9) | a lost-output `apply`, a partial one, an expired plan, a deleted cache with retained history, a bounded scan; no write, no request |
| Resource sets and predicates (E13) | overlap unit cases (ancestors, descendants, rename destinations, canonicalization); every predicate part refusing its own kind of change; identity across a device-number change |
| The journal classifier (E11) | the differential test: its verdict equals what recovery then does, for every crash-matrix state |
| The repair journal (E5) | the crash matrix at every failpoint and every primitive boundary; the whole subject set before or after by phase; recovery crashed at every inverse; triple recovery; injected I/O failure; triple recovery by different lock-taking commands; older builds never touch it (E9) |
| Fences and barriers (E14) | a stuck journal fencing only its resources (a credential against `auth github set`, an unrelated blob, a skill file); an undecodable journal failing closed; reactivations crashed at every primitive, never recovered ahead of their repair; the differential test over these cases |
| Undo of repairs (E7) | round trip and round trip of the undo for every fix kind; the strict checks and the guards; a previewed and applied undo; conflicts by resource overlap |
| gc (E8) | races with fix and undo; reachability pins (an old backup a newer crashed undo needs); a changed bound set refused; an interrupted gc; `latest` retargeted |
| The doctor runtime (E3, E6) | each terminal state reached by the test fixers; a preview bound across processes; a stale bound run touching nothing, recoveries included; conflicting fixes refused; detector panics and budgets; unique run ids under a frozen clock; exit sites |
| Detectors and fixers (F*) | each fixture's true positive and no false positive on the realistic home; fix and verify in the leaf; the harness for every round trip; the set-aside's refused reactivation and its attribution of misleading payloads |
| Group commit and deferred fsyncs (G3) | the written power-loss argument per ordering point (failpoint kills cannot test fsync placement); a power-loss campaign where an unprivileged tool allows one; every crash matrix unchanged; injected barrier failures; renamed and replaced dirty directories; the pinned counts; the btrfs measurement |
| The freeze (A10, H2) | the classifier over synthetic manifests; the updater tests against a synthetic released baseline; the first baseline at H6 |

### §11.3 The checkpoint protocol (H6)

1. **Freeze.**
   - Every leaf but H6 is closed.
   - The demos of slices 1–3 are recorded on the milestone epic. Slice 4 includes H6 and its tag, so H6 verifies slice 4's pre-tag parts here (the recipes, the audit's change list and empty allowlist, the golden and its updater tests, README) and records slice 4's completed demo in step 7, after the tag exists.
   - `br epic close-eligible` shows only the milestone epic waiting on H6.
2. **Machine-local runs, in this order:**
   1. `argc gate --all` from a **clean checkout** (`git clone` of `main` into a tempdir on disk, not tmpfs: M3's gate ran out of tmpfs space with a 22 GiB target dir).
   2. `cargo test --release --test perf -- --ignored --skip bench_home --skip live_home --test-threads=1`.
   3. `argc bench`.
   4. `argc fuzz-all --time 600 --toolchain <nightly ≥ rust-version>`, then `argc fuzz journal --time 1800`.
   5. `cargo test --test compat_m2 -- --ignored --nocapture` and `cargo test --test compat_m3 -- --ignored --nocapture`. Both are debug builds: **no `--release`**, which M3's plan got wrong. Each builds its old commit with the toolchain that commit records (`1.97.1`); a build failure is a failed criterion, not a `SKIP` (§3.2).
   6. `cargo test --test doctor_harness -- --ignored` (the exhaustive combination suite).
   7. **The guide's fixed point:** `OMADDONS_UPDATE_SKILL=1 cargo test --test skill`, `cargo build`, the same regeneration again, then `git diff --exit-code skills/`.
   8. `OMADDONS_LIVE=1 cargo test --test live_probes -- --ignored`.
   9. `cargo llvm-cov --summary-only` (record the line coverage).
3. **Real machine and desktop**, under the plan's approval (§3.3), each step read-only or undone:
   1. `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE=1 OMADDONS_LIVE=1 OMADDONS_ALLOW_SKIP=keyless_installs_forever cargo test --test real_machine -- --ignored --test-threads=1`. M4 adds `doctor_on_the_real_home`, `apply_one_update_and_undo` and `install_skill_round_trip` to it. M3 lacked owners for its real-machine tests (§2.6), so here every named test has an owner: D7, E6 and B3 each add theirs, and H6 only runs them. A missing one is a reopened leaf, not something H6 writes.
   2. **Desktop:**
      - the widget's Update on a matching plan (no dialog), with the screenshot and IPC `state()`;
      - an Update whose plan moved (a fixture server is not available on the live bar, so this is recorded from the QML scenario, and the live check is the matching case);
      - a doctor repair from Issues (the credential mode), with Undo last;
      - `omarchy install` after the M4 build, so the widget is current.
4. **Record.**
   - The close reason, in the `[x] N` format.
   - The vision comment "§10 Milestone status: M4 … is done (date)".
   - The README flips H4 prepared.
5. **Freeze the contract and tag.** The golden's header with `frozen: true` and the first released baseline (`OMADDONS_ADVANCE_RELEASED_BASELINE=1.0` writes `tests/contract/released/1.0.json` with its provenance), in the same commit as the README flips and `.beads/`. That commit changes a test fixture, so `argc gate` runs on it first, with the baseline in place (CLAUDE.md D16). `git tag -a v0.1.0`, then push.
6. **Close.** `br epic close-eligible` until nothing more closes. `br sync --flush-only`, then commit and push `.beads/`.
7. **Record slice 4's demo** on the milestone epic: the recipes, the change list, the golden, README, the tag and the released baseline, each with its evidence.

### §11.4 Risks

Numbered in the order they were identified, each with its likelihood (L) and impact (I): low, medium or high. Each has an owner leaf.

| # | Risk | L | I | Mitigation | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **The repair journal has a recovery bug** that loses or corrupts a repaired file after a crash | M | H | fixes lowered to primitives, each one filesystem operation with its own write-ahead step; endpoint predicates known at plan time; a crash matrix at every primitive boundary with the whole-subject assertion, recovery crashed at every inverse, plus triple recovery (common rule 14); the repair engine is a separate family, so folder transactions are untouched | E5 |
| 2 | **Live validation finds many schema/output mismatches** and A3 balloons | M | M | each mismatch is a real bug, fixed in A3 and listed; if A3 passes 2× its size, file the remainder as bugs `discovered-from` A3 and gate on them before H1 | A3 |
| 3 | **Doctor false positives** on real homes (a detector too eager) erode trust | M | M | every detector has a no-false-positive test on the realistic home; H6 reviews every real-home finding; severities are conservative | F*, H6 |
| 4 | **`status --cached` slows past 5 ms** with the cached tier | M | M | tier contracts (§6.13); the perf test with plans and run dirs present; cached detectors limited to what status already reads | F8 |
| 5 | **The pre-freeze audit breaks the widget or scripts** | M | M | widget updated in the same commit; every change listed; the audit happens once | H1 |
| 6 | **Tokens too sensitive** (a rules edit, a binary upgrade or a judge digest stales every preview) | M | L | intentional (M4-D19: a verdict is as good as its rules), and the fix is one re-preview; `details.changed` says which part | D1 |
| 7 | **Widget update previews feel slow** (a dry run downloads and verifies) | M | L | the dry run is the same work the real run did before (the blobs are then cached, so `apply` downloads nothing); the footer shows progress; no dialog when matching | G1 |
| 8 | **Group commit or deferred directory fsyncs weaken durability** somewhere recovery depends on, invisibly, because failpoint kills keep the page cache | L | H | journal untouched; the action log synced before each transaction's closing line; directories synced through owned handles at explicit barriers that report their errors before success; derived files only lose durability when rebuilt from durable state; a written power-loss argument per ordering point at the design gate, and an immediate fsync wherever the argument fails; a power-loss campaign where practical; every crash matrix rerun; G3 lands last, on settled protocols | G3 |
| 9 | **The M3 build destroys M4 artifacts** (orphan sweep, journal listing) | L | H | `.repair` names; the compat test (E9) before the tag; rename families if touched | E9 |
| 10 | **Retention exemption grows disk use** (quarantines kept until gc) | L | M | `doctor-runs-accumulated` reports past 200 runs or 1 GiB; set-asides are rare; README documents `doctor gc` and its retention plan | E8 |
| 11 | **Target-less repair history lines confuse readers** (projection, `last_change`, undo selection; about 33 readers) | M | M | a leaf of its own (E12) that moves every reader to an explicit `Option` arm, with a grep test against `.target.unwrap`; tests over `history`, `status`, `undo` with repair lines; older builds skip them (fail closed) | E12, E7 |
| 12 | **Misplaced-client fixes misfire** (a word that is both a client and an addon, `omaddons sod update` where `sod` names a catalog entry) | L | M | the addon wins; the corpus includes the collision cases | C1, C2 |
| 13 | **The guide drifts from behaviour** | L | M | generated tables; every command in the guide parses (test); recipes run (B4); byte identity with `SKILL.md` | B2, B4 |
| 14 | **The milestone is large** (60 leaves) and the critical path is long (25 units), with two chains one unit behind it | M | M | six agents reach the critical path (computed); slices demo progress; the intent area (C, 14+ units of slack) absorbs slips; the plans chain and the repair-protocol chain (slack 1) are claimed early; the graph is recomputed after every design gate that moves a size or an edge (§10) | all |
| 15 | **`jsonschema` violates `deny.toml`** (pulls `reqwest` or a TLS backend) | L | L | default features off, version pinned, both `cargo tree -i` checks recorded; fallback `boon` | A3 |
| 16 | **A `-t all` collides with a user's target named `all`** | L | L | the registered id wins, with a warning and a rename hint | C2 |
| 17 | **Forever launches mid-milestone (2026-11-04)** and changes the client layout | M | L | M4 touches no discovery or rules code; `omad-wez` handles it outside M4 | — |
| 18 | **The classifier's `LiveView` refactor changes recovery** | L | H | recovery's tests unchanged; the differential test over every crash-matrix state; E11 lands before E5 touches `journal.rs` | E11 |
| 19 | **A token stales for no reason** (a field that differs between two runs of an unchanged world, as the deferred URL did, or a stamp that moved without a content change) | M | M | the "cache hit equals download" rows per source; two dry runs of an unchanged home give equal tokens; the witness hashes content and keeps stamps only as private proof of "unchanged since"; the token holds only stable digests (M4-D44) | D1, E6 |
| 20 | **The under-lock witness check lengthens the commit window** on large folders | M | L | a `stat` per entry, a hash only for what changed (the `predigest` pattern); the cost measured on the realistic home and reported; G3's counts include it | D8 |
| 21 | **Fences are scoped wrong**: too wide blocks unrelated work, too narrow leaves a resource unprotected | M | M | one resource model for conflicts, fences, undo and gc (E13); overlap unit cases; E14's cases on a credential, a blob and a skill file; unreadable journals fail closed rather than guess | E13, E14 |
| 22 | **The compatibility classifier mislabels a change** (a breaking change passed as additive) | L | H | conservative default (an unclassified change is breaking); unit cases per direction rule; the updater tests against a synthetic baseline; H1's final walk | A10, H2 |
| 23 | **Guarded reactivation refuses more often than users expect** (any later install on that client blocks undo of a set-aside) | M | L | intended (M4-D38): the refusal names what changed, and the suspended set stays inspectable in quarantine; `explain` says so before the user consents to the set-aside | F2, E7 |

**Appendix A: the binding JSON shapes (M4 plan, 2026-10-24).**

## Appendix A: JSON shapes

These are the binding shapes: key names, nesting, types and which keys are always present. Key order is deterministic and shown as rendered, but it is not part of the compatibility contract (JSON objects are unordered; M4-D56). Values are illustrative.

### A.1 `capabilities` (data, abbreviated: one element per list)

```json
{"version":"0.1.0","contract_version":"1.0","build_id":"9c41e0b7a2d35f18",
 "guide_digest":"sha256:5e0c…",
 "features":["json_envelope","ndjson_stderr","dry_run_everywhere","preconditions","stored_plans","doctor","offline",
             "progress_ndjson","undo","backups","lua_errors","omarchy_widget","completions","agent_skill"],
 "commands":[{"path":"install","description":"Install or update addons in one target","group":"change","mutates":true,
   "json":true,"dictionary":"general","exit_codes":[0,1,2,3,4,5,6],"stores_plan":true,"binds":true,"network":"optional",
   "aliases":["add"],"args":[{"name":"REF","value_name":"REF","required":true,"multiple":true,"default":null,
                              "possible_values":null}],
   "flags":[{"long":"channel","short":null,"aliases":[],"value_name":"CHANNEL","takes_value":true,"multiple":false,
             "default":null,"possible_values":["stable","beta","alpha"],"conflicts_with":["version"],"requires":[],
             "global":false,"description":"Release channel"}],
   "data_schema":"omaddons robot-docs schema install"}],
 "exit_codes":{"general":[{"code":0,"name":"ok","meaning":"…","retryable":null}],
               "doctor":[{"code":1,"name":"findings_present","meaning":"…"}]},
 "env_vars":[{"name":"OMADDONS_OFFLINE","description":"1 means --offline","mirrors":"--offline"}],
 "limits":[{"name":"DOWNLOAD_MAX_BYTES","value":536870912,"unit":"bytes","config_key":"limits.download_max_bytes",
            "source":"builtin"}],
 "sources":[{"id":"github","enabled":true,"requires_credential":false,"credential_configured":false,
             "hosts":["github.com","api.github.com","codeload.github.com","objects.githubusercontent.com",
                      "release-assets.githubusercontent.com"]}],
 "families":[{"name":"mainline","interface_min":60000,"interface_max":null,"legacy":false}],
 "client_rules":[{"row":"mainline","family":"mainline","install_kind":"battlenet","version_min":"12.1.5",
                  "version_max":null,"game_types":["standard"],"source":"builtin"}],
 "target_id_forms":["key","id","product_code","flavor_folder","game_mode","family","path","all"],
 "error_codes":[{"code":"plan_stale","exit":1,"doctor_exit":4,"retryable":"conditional","meaning":"…",
                 "details_schema":{"type":"object","properties":{
                   "changed":{"type":"array","items":{"enum":["targets","selection","observed","command"]}},
                   "reason":{"enum":["expired","binary_changed","input_missing","already_applied"]},
                   "cause":{"type":"string"},"cause_message":{"type":"string"},"path":{"type":"string"},
                   "txs":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}}},
                 "required":["changed"]}}],
 "warning_codes":[{"code":"plan_not_stored","meaning":"…"}],
 "actions":[{"action":"apply","description":"Run the stored plan the dry run made","destructive":false}],
 "failure_modes":{"count":46,"subsystems":["concurrency_primitives","schemas","state_files","configs",
                  "external_artifacts","caches","plugins","secrets","permissions","userland_state","network"],
                  "command":"omaddons doctor capabilities --json"},
 "schemas_uri":"omaddons robot-docs schema","robot_docs_uri":"omaddons robot-docs guide","config_error":null}
```

**`retryable`, per code,** is `true`, `false` or `"conditional"`. The last is for `plan_stale`, `http_status` and `hash_mismatch`, whose instances decide (`hash_mismatch` is retryable on its first attempt only, `error.rs:598`); `meaning` says when. *Decided while writing this appendix:* a boolean would lie for those three.

- Every error **instance** keeps a boolean `error.retryable`, as today. The tri-state appears only in the code registry (`capabilities`, `robot-docs errors`, the manifest's `error` nodes).
- `plan_stale` is registered retryable (`error.rs:194`), and each instance decides by its source (`error.rs:592`): M3's re-planned staleness (`PlanStaleSource::Replan`) is retryable; every `plan_stale` a bound run or `apply` raises (`PlanStaleSource::Apply`, all of M4's) is not. Hence "not retryable" wherever this plan describes a bound run's refusal.
- Its readable golden line is `error <code> exit=<n> doctor_exit=<n> retryable=<true|false|conditional> details=<k:type,…>` (§6.7).

### A.2 A storable dry run's additions, and `apply`

```json
{"…InstallData…":"…","precondition":"pc1:3f9a…","plan_id":"01M8Q2…","plan_expires_at":"2026-10-31T18:02:11Z",
 "approval":{"routine":false,"reasons":["dependency_added"],
   "selection":[{"target_key":"01M5…","target_id":"era","addon":"weakauras","source":"github","channel":"stable",
                 "release_id":"gh:…@v5.22.1","asset":"WeakAuras-5.22.1.zip","from_version":null,
                 "to_version":"5.22.1","op":"install"}],
   "scope":{"dependencies_added":["libdeflate"],"folders_removed":[],
            "local_changes_replaced":{"count":0,"folders":[]},"source_changed":[],"while_running":false}}}
```

A dry run that would change nothing has `"plan_id":null`, `"plan_expires_at":null`, its `precondition` and an empty `approval.selection`, and offers no `apply`.

`commands[]` includes, when a plan was stored:

```json
{"action":"apply","command":"omaddons apply 01M8Q2…","argv":["omaddons","apply","01M8Q2…"],"destructive":false}
```

`apply`'s data (the `install` wrapper variant):

```json
{"plan_id":"01M8Q2…","applied":{"command":"install","display_argv":["omaddons","install","weakauras","dbm","-t","era"]},
 "result":{"dry_run":false,"target":{"id":"era","key":"01M5…"},"tx":"01M8Q3…","kind":"install","items":["…"],
           "reload_required":"none","atomic_swap":true,"creates_addons_dir":false,"precondition":null,
           "plan_id":null,"plan_expires_at":null,"approval":null},
 "outcomes":[{"target":"era","key":"01M5…","status":"committed","tx":"01M8Q3…","error_code":null}]}
```

`apply --dry-run` adds `"approved": { …the stored approval… }` before `result`, and `result` is the fresh dry run with its own `approval`.

### A.3 The stored plan file

```json
{"schema_version":"1.0","plan_id":"01M8Q2…","created_at":"…","expires_at":"…","tool_version":"0.1.0",
 "build_id":"9c41e0b7a2d35f18",
 "intent":{"command":"install","refs":["weakauras","dbm"],"target":"01M5…","channel":null,"version":null,"file":null,
           "reinstall":false,"force":false,"no_deps":false,"while_running":false},
 "display_argv":["omaddons","install","weakauras","dbm","-t","era"],
 "actor":"agent","reason":"user asked for boss mods",
```

A deferred release (Tukui) is stored as `{"release_id":"tukui:elvui@13.82","source":"tukui","key":"elvui","url":null,"expected_hash":null,"blob_sha256":"…"}`. The token keys it without a URL (§6.9.1). The plan holds no working directory: the intent's paths are absolute.

### A.4 `doctor diagnose` (the whole envelope)

```json
{"ok":false,"schema_version":"1.0","tool_version":"0.1.0","command":"doctor diagnose","exit_code":1,
 "view":"full","doctor_contract_version":"1.0","run_id":"2026-10-30T18-02-11Z__01M8R…",
 "run_dir":"<state>/doctor/runs/2026-10-30T18-02-11Z__01M8R…",
 "started_at":"2026-10-30T18:02:11Z","finished_at":"2026-10-30T18:02:11.412Z","state":"DONE_FINDINGS",
 "summary":{"total_findings":2,"by_severity":{"P0":1,"P1":0,"P2":0,"P3":1},"auto_fixable":1,"needs_force":1,
            "manual":0,"online_required":3,"skipped":3,"incomplete":0,"duration_ms":412},

   "instance":"fm-concurrency_primitives-journal-too-new@01M5…:tx=01M7…","label":"retail · tx 01M7…",
```

`run_dir` is printed absolute. The placeholder above is for this document only.

### A.5 `doctor fix` additions

```json
{"…diagnose keys…":"…","state":"DONE_OK","tx":"01M9…",
 "summary":{"findings_before":2,"findings_after":1,"actions_taken":1,"actions_failed":0,"bytes_backed_up":0,
            "backups_restored":0,"duration_ms":38},
 "actions":[{"seq":1,"fix":1,"fm":"fm-secrets-credential-file-mode","op":"chmod","path":"<config>/credentials/github",
             "pre":{"kind":"file","identity":{"ino":"…","born_ns":"…"},"mode":"0644"},
             "post":{"kind":"file","identity":{"ino":"…","born_ns":"…"},"mode":"0600"},"backup":null,"ok":true}],
 "delegated":[],
 "actions_jsonl_path":"…/actions.jsonl","backups_dir":"…/backups",
 "undo_command":"omaddons doctor undo 2026-10-30T18-03-40Z__01M8S…","undo_argv":["omaddons","doctor","undo","…"]}
```

Under `--dry-run` there is no `tx`. `actions_planned` replaces `actions` (the same primitive shape, without `ok`, plus `bytes`), `delegated_planned` lists the recoveries the run would perform (`{tx, family, phase, direction}`), and `precondition` is added.

### A.6 `--robot-triage`

```json
{"ok":false,"schema_version":"1.0","tool_version":"0.1.0","command":"doctor diagnose","exit_code":1,
 "view":"triage","summary":{"ok":false,"total_findings":2,"auto_fixable":1},"quick_ref":["P0: 1 finding (needs --force --yes)","P3: 1 auto-fixable"],
 "findings":["…as A.4…"],
 "actions_planned":[{"fixer_id":"fm-plugins-skill-version-drift","writes_to":["<skills>/SKILL.md"],"estimated_bytes":24576}],
 "recommended_command":"omaddons doctor fix --only fm-plugins-skill-version-drift","recommended_argv":["…"],
 "capabilities_command":"omaddons doctor capabilities --json","robot_docs_command":"omaddons doctor robot-docs",
 "warnings":[],"commands":["…"],"meta":{"…":"…"}}
```

The doctor contract's `capabilities_url` becomes `capabilities_command`, because omaddons has no URL to give. That is decided here and recorded by H5. `view` is the tag of `doctor diagnose`'s one schema (`oneOf` over `full` and `triage`, §6.11).

### A.7 `health`

```text
findings  omaddons=0.1.0 doctor=1.0 findings=2 P0=1 P3=1 last_run=2026-10-30T18:02:11Z run_id=2026-10-30T18-02-11Z__01M8R…
```

Its JSON form:

```json
{"…envelope keys…":"…","status":"findings","findings":2,"by_severity":{"P0":1,"P1":0,"P2":0,"P3":1},
 "last_run":"2026-10-30T18:02:11Z","run_id":"…"}
```

### A.8 `ls`, `explain`, `undo`, `gc`

```json
{"runs":[{"run_id":"…","kind":"fix","started_at":"…","state":"DONE_OK","exit_code":0,"action_count":1,"tx":"01M9…",
          "reverted_run":null,"undo_complete":false}]}
{"failure_mode":{"id":"…","subsystem":"…","severity":"P2","title":"…","description":"…","why":"…","tier":"cached",
  "fixer":{"ops":["chmod"],"writes_to":["config"],"enabled":true,"needs_force":false,"reversible":true},"manual":null},
 "instances":["…findings…"]}
{"run_id":"…(the undo's own run)","reverted_run":"2026-10-30T18-03-40Z__01M8S…","tx":"01M9…","undo_tx":"01MA…",
 "state":"DONE_OK","actions_taken":1,"already_undone":false}
{"dry_run":true,"before":"2026-09-30T00:00:00Z",
 "deletions":[{"kind":"run","run_id":"…","target":null,"tx":null,"path":"…","bytes":4096,"may_hold_only_copy":false}],
 "excluded":[{"kind":"backup","run_id":"…","path":"…/backups/3","pin":"active_undo"}],
 "undo_lost":["01M9…"],"latest":{"from":"…","to":"…"},"precondition":"pc1:…"}
```

### A.9 The repair journal

```text
{"type":"prepared","format":"1.0","tx":"01M9…","run":"01M9…","doctor_run_id":"2026-10-30T18-03-40Z__01M8S…",
 "actor":"human","reason":null,"argv":["…"],"at":"…","targets":["01M5…"],
 "client_dirs":[{"dir":"/abs/…/_retail_","target":"01M5…"}],
 "resources":{"reads":["…"],"writes":["/abs/…/X","/abs/…/quarantine/…"]},
 "fixes":[{"fix":1,"fm":"fm-external_artifacts-nested-addon-folder","kind":"flatten"}],
 "primitives":[
   {"seq":1,"fix":1,"fm":"fm-external_artifacts-nested-addon-folder","op":"rename_noreplace","path":"/abs/…/AddOns/X/Y","to":"/abs/…/AddOns/Y",
    "pre":{"path":{"kind":"dir","identity":{"ino":"…","born_ns":"…"},"stamp":"stamp:sha256:…"},"to":{"kind":"absent"}},
    "post":{"path":{"kind":"absent"},"to":{"kind":"dir","identity":{"ino":"…","born_ns":"…"}}}},
   {"seq":2,"fix":1,"fm":"fm-external_artifacts-nested-addon-folder","op":"rename_noreplace","path":"/abs/…/AddOns/X","to":"/abs/…/quarantine/…/X",
    "pre":{"…":"…"},"post":{"…":"…"}}]}
{"type":"step","seq":1}
{"type":"step","seq":2}
{"type":"done"}
{"type":"committed"}
```

`rolled_back` replaces `done` and `committed` on an in-process rollback. The tag key is `"type"`, as in folder journals (`journal.rs:50`), because fsx's prune safeguard reads exactly that key (`prune.rs:412-425`). The journal's `to` is absolute; the token's `to_rel` is relative to the quarantine root (M4-D44). A set-aside's primitives also carry `guards` (the suspension manifest), and an undo's activation primitive carries `"activation":true`.

### A.10 The repair history line

As §6.14.4, with `repairs[]` holding the primitives as the journal recorded them. An undo of a repair is a line of kind `undo` with `reverts`, `target: null`, `targets`, `repairs` holding the inverse primitives, and `doctor_run_id` naming the undo's own run directory (kind `undo`).

### A.11 `status` issue additions

```json
{"id":"fm-secrets-credential-file-mode","severity":"P2","title":"…","addon":null,
 "remediation":{"command":"omaddons doctor fix --only fm-secrets-credential-file-mode","argv":["…"],"destructive":false},
 "auto_fixable":true,"explain":{"command":"omaddons doctor explain fm-secrets-credential-file-mode","argv":["…"]}}
```

### A.12 `plans show`

```json
{"plan_id":"01M8Q2…","state":"partial","stored":true,"readable":true,
 "created_at":"2026-10-30T18:02:11Z","expires_at":"2026-10-31T18:02:11Z","build_id":"9c41e0b7a2d35f18","build_matches":true,
 "intent":{"command":"update","display_argv":["omaddons","update"]},
 "approval":{"…":"as A.2"},
 "inputs":[],
 "evidence":{"targets":[{"target":"classic","key":"01M4…","tx":"01M8T…","result":"committed","at":"…"}],
             "complete":true}}
```

With the plan file gone: `"stored":false`, `"intent":null`, `"approval":null`, the evidence, and `"state":"unknown"`.

**Contract additions (§7): commands and flags, data keys, new shapes, error and warning codes, kinds, ops, actions and events, files, config and environment, constants (M4 plan, 2026-10-24).**

## §7 Contract additions

Additions are the default (DEC-4). The few pre-release corrections M4 makes are made by the leaf that owns the surface, recorded in its close comment with a compatibility note (M4-D55), and H1 audits the rest. Each leaf lists the wire names it actually added or changed in its close comment (common rule 6). H5 reconciles them into one vision comment, and the golden pins them at H2. `schema_version` stays "1.0" through the tag.

### §7.1 Commands and flags

| Path | Group | Mutates | Dictionary | Stores plan | Leaf |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `capabilities` | Setup | no | general | no | A4 |
| `robot-docs` (bare = `guide`), `robot-docs guide`, `robot-docs schema [<command>]`, `robot-docs errors` | Setup | no | general | no | A5, B1 |
| `robot-docs install-skill [--dir <DIR>]` | Setup | yes | general | no | B3 |
| `completions <SHELL>` | Setup | no | general | no | A7 |
| `apply <PLAN_ID> [--dry-run]` | Change | yes | general | no | D5 |
| `plans show <PLAN_ID>` | Look | no | general | no | D9 |
| `doctor` (bare = `doctor diagnose`), `doctor diagnose`, `doctor explain <id>` | Look | no (diagnose writes only its run dir, M4-D33) | doctor | no | E3 |
| `doctor health`, `doctor ls`, `doctor capabilities`, `doctor robot-docs` | Look | no | doctor | no | E4 |
| `doctor diff [<run>]` | Look | no | doctor | no | E6 |
| `doctor fix` | Change | yes | doctor | no (binds) | E6 |
| `doctor undo [<run>]` | Change | yes | doctor | no | E7 |
| `doctor gc --before <date or age> [--dry-run] [--if-match <token>] [--yes]` | Change | yes | doctor | no (binds) | E8 |
| `auth github [set|clear|status]` (restructured, same argv) | Setup | yes | general | no | A1 |

**Doctor flags.** On `diagnose`: `--only`, `--skip`, `--since`, `--online`, `--severity`, `--budget`, `--quick`, `--include-deep`, `--robot-triage` and `-t`. On `fix`: the selection flags plus `--dry-run`, `--if-match`, `--force` (requires `--yes`) and `--yes`. On `gc`: `--before`, `--dry-run`, `--if-match` and `--yes`. On `ls`: `--limit`. There is no `--fix` or `--explain` flag (§6.11): typed anyway, each is an intent hint to its subcommand.

**Global flag changes:**
- `--if-match` is accepted by the twelve paths of M4-D19 plus `doctor fix` and `doctor gc`.
- `-v` gains level 2.
- `-t` accepts `all` (M4-D13).

**Aliases:** none new. Help gains the discovery line (A6).

### §7.2 Data keys on existing commands

- **`install`, `update`, `pin`, `unpin`, `adopt` (when adopting), `sync`, `copy`:** `data.precondition`, a token under `--dry-run` and `null` on real runs (D2, D3).
- **Every storable command** (M4-D22): `data.plan_id`, `data.plan_expires_at` and `data.approval` (the typed approval summary, M4-D24), all `null` on real runs (D4). `plan_id` is also `null` on a dry run that would change nothing, or when the plan store is full. The `apply` action appears in `commands[]` only when a plan was stored.
- **`status`:**
  - `targets[].issues[]` and `data.issues[]` gain `auto_fixable` and `explain{command, argv}` (F8);
  - `summary.issues` counts the registry's findings;
  - every failure mode's id may appear (Appendix B);
  - update entries gain `source` and `release_id` where they lack them (G1), so a widget row carries its release identity.
- **`help --json` (bare):** `discovery[{command, argv, purpose}]` (A6).
- **`history`:** `entries[].plan` (D5); for `kind: repair` lines, `entries[].targets`, `entries[].doctor_run_id`, `entries[].repairs[]` (the primitives, E5, E12), with `target: null`; for `kind: skill` lines, `entries[].dir` (B3).
- **`undo`:** reverting a repair, `data.kind: "repair"` with `data.repairs_reverted` and `data.doctor_run_id` (the undo's own run, E7); under `--dry-run`, `data.precondition` covers it.
- **`capabilities`:** `build_id` (D1) and `guide_digest` (B1); per command, flags and positionals gain `default`, `conflicts_with` and `requires` (A4); per error code, `details_schema` replaces a key list (A9).

### §7.3 New data shapes (Appendix A has them in full)

| Shape | Keys |
|---|---|
| `capabilities` | §6.2.2 |
| `robot-docs guide` | `{format: "markdown", content}` |
| `robot-docs schema` | `{envelope, events, commands, files}` |
| `robot-docs errors` | `{error_codes, warning_codes}` |
| `install-skill` | `{dry_run, dir, file, written, bytes, tool_version}` |
| `completions` | `{shell, script}` |
| `apply` | `{plan_id, applied{command, display_argv}, approved?, result, outcomes[]}`, one wrapper variant per storable command (§6.9.3) |
| `plans show` | `{plan_id, state, stored, readable, created_at?, expires_at?, build_id?, build_matches?, intent?, approval?, inputs[], evidence{targets[], complete}}` (§6.9.3a) |
| `approval` (inside every storable dry run) | `{routine, reasons[], selection[], scope}` |
| the doctor's reports | §6.11 and Appendix A (top level, not under `data`, M4-D34) |

### §7.4 Error codes (41 → 43)

- **New:**
  - `online_required` (general exit 1, doctor exit 6, not retryable). A `doctor --only` or `doctor fix --only` selection holds only online failure modes, and `--online` is absent. `details {fms}`.
  - `doctor_refused` (general exit 4, doctor exit 4, not retryable). The error of every `REFUSING` run. `details.reason` is one of `force_required`, `fixer_conflict`, `too_many_actions`, `over_budget`, `filesystem_mismatch`, `client_running`, `not_enabled` and `edited_locally`, with `details.fm` when one failure mode is concerned, and `details.resources` for `fixer_conflict`.
- **First used:** `plan_not_found` (exit 3), reserved since M1, raised by `apply` and `plans show`.
- **Reused, with new details:**
  - `plan_stale` gains `details.reason` (`expired`, `binary_changed`, `input_missing`, `already_applied`) for `apply`, with `details.path` for `input_missing` and `details.txs` for `already_applied`. `details.changed` keeps its fixed set, and a witness or operation mismatch under the lock reports `observed` or `selection` there. Its doctor exit is 4 (M4-D40). It is also `doctor gc --if-match`'s refusal of a changed deletion set.
  - `locked` gains `details.lease` (the plan id) when a second `apply` timed out waiting for a plan's lease, with the holder's `{pid, command, age_s}`.
  - `undo_conflict` gains `details.reason: "changed_since_repair"` with `details.paths`, and `"changed_since_suspension"` with `details.changed`.
  - `usage` gains `details.target`/`command` (misplaced clients, from all three hooks; hook 3's misplaced name is now a `usage` error, not `not_found`) and `details.flag` (a `--force` without `--yes`).
  - `plan_not_found` also covers an unreadable or oversized plan file (`details.reason: "unreadable"`, `details.path`); `state_corrupt` stays for `<state>`.
  - `hash_mismatch` covers a damaged cached blob (`details.blob`, fix `omaddons doctor --include-deep`).
  - `scope_denied` gains `details.reason: "skill_dir"` for a refused `install-skill --dir`, and `"symlink"` for a symlinked `SKILL.md`.
  - `not_found` covers a missing `install-skill --dir` parent, or a missing `$HOME/.claude` for the default (`details.path`).
  - `usage` covers `undo --run <a doctor run id>`, with the fix `omaddons doctor undo <id>`, and `doctor undo latest`, with the fix `omaddons doctor undo`.
  - **A command refused by a fence** (a stuck repair journal protecting the resource it would write, M4-D62) fails with the fencing journal's own stop error, which gains `details.tx` and `details.resource`.
- **Every code gains** `meaning` and a typed `DetailSpec` (A9, validated by A3). These are part of the contract from H2.

### §7.5 Warning codes (52 → 55)

| Code | Leaf | When |
|---|---|---|
| `plan_not_stored` | D4 | a dry run did not store its plan (a write failure, or the store at its quota); the preview and its token stand |
| `target_id_reserved` | C2 | a registered target is named `all` |
| `delegated_recovery` | F2 | `doctor fix` recovered an interrupted transaction (names the tx and the outcome; fix `omaddons undo <tx>` when rolled forward) |

The reviewed draft's `plans_crowded` is gone: the store has hard quotas, so it is never "crowded" past a bound; a full store is `plan_not_stored`, and `fm-state_files-plan-store-crowded` reports it (row 45).

### §7.6 Kinds, ops, actions, phases, events and purposes

- **`TxKind`:** `skill` (a settings kind; B3). `repair` is now written (E5).
- **History:** the fields `targets`, `doctor_run_id`, `repairs[]` and `plan`, and `target: null` for `repair` lines (E12).
- **Repair journal lines** are tagged by `"type"`: `prepared`, `step`, `done`, `rolled_back`, `committed`. Fix kinds (`prepared.fixes[].kind`, capabilities' `ops`): `write`, `chmod`, `quarantine`, `flatten`, `suspend`, `delegate`. Primitive ops (`prepared.primitives[].op`, `history.repairs[].op`): `write_file`, `chmod`, `rename_noreplace`. Predicate kinds: `absent`, `file`, `dir`, `symlink`.
- **Run kinds** (`report.json`'s `kind`, `doctor ls`): `diagnose`, `fix`, `undo`.
- **Report views** (`doctor diagnose`'s `view`): `full`, `triage`.
- **Approval reasons** (`approval.reasons[]`): `dependency_added`, `folders_removed`, `local_changes_replaced`, `source_changed`, `channel_changed`, `while_running`, `reinstall`, `force`, `downgrade`.
- **`apply` outcomes** (`outcomes[].status`): `committed`, `unchanged`, `stale`, `failed`. **`plans show` states:** `pending`, `completed`, `partial`, `expired`, `unknown`.
- **gc pins** (`excluded[].pin`): `active_run`, `unfinished_journal`, `active_undo`, `recovery_dependency`.
- **Recommendation actions (`commands[].action`):** `apply`, `install_skill`, `doctor_fix`, `doctor_explain`, `doctor_gc`. M4-D11 and §6.2.1 list the same five.
- **`LogLevel`:** `trace` (A8).
- **`net.log` purpose:** `doctor-probe` (F7).
- **Doctor failpoints** (debug only), eleven in all: the abort points `doctor.run.staged`, `doctor.run.published`, `doctor.repair.prepared`, `doctor.repair.step`, `doctor.repair.done`, `doctor.repair.history`, `doctor.repair.committed` and `doctor.recover.step`; the pause points `doctor.fix.planned` and `doctor.gc.planned`; and `doctor.detector.panic`. `engine::tx::FAILPOINTS` is unchanged; `doctor::FAILPOINTS` is new and scanned the same way. fsx gains one debug error-injection point, `fsx.barrier.sync` (G3), beside its `fsx.mutate.*` points.
- **fsx (internal, not wire):** `Expect::{Absent, Present(Predicate)}` with `FileId::same` (E13), `LockUse::Expired`, `lock::Lease` (D4), `Durability::Derived`, `CommitWindow` (G3), prune kinds `RepairJournal`, `ClientRepair`, `CacheQuarantine`, `PlanLease` and `DoctorLatest`, `ScopeTable::with_skill_dirs` and `with_fences`, `WriteSession::untracked_logged`.

### §7.7 Files

| Path | Kind and version | Leaf |
|---|---|---|
| `<cache>/plans/<plan_id>.json` | `plan` 1.0 | D4 |
| `<cache>/plans/<plan_id>.lease`, `<cache>/plans/.lock` | empty lock files (flock), swept with their expired plans | D4, D5 |
| `<state>/doctor/runs/<run>/report.json` | `doctor_report` 1.0 (`kind: diagnose | fix | undo`) | E3 |
| `<state>/doctor/runs/<run>/runtime.jsonl` | the fsx actions line, for the runtime's own writes | E3 |
| `<state>/doctor/runs/<run>/actions.jsonl` | the fsx actions line (unchanged format), the repair's primitives only | E5 |
| `<state>/doctor/runs/<run>/backups/<seq>` | verbatim copies | E5 |
| `<state>/doctor/runs/<run>/quarantine/{state,config}/…` | moved victims | E5 |
| `<state>/doctor/runs/<run>/undo.sh` | POSIX script, 0500 | E6 |
| `<state>/doctor/latest` | symlink | E3 |
| `<state>/journal/<tx>.repair.jsonl` | `repair_journal` 1.0 | E5 |
| `<state>/journal/<tx>.reactivating.jsonl` | a suspended folder journal while its reactivation is unfinished (M4-D38) | E14 |
| `<meta>/snapshots/<tx>.repair/{files,quarantine}/` | client-side backups and quarantine | E5 |
| `<cache>/quarantine/<run id>/…` | cache-side quarantine | E5, F6 |
| `<skills>/SKILL.md` (and other `--dir`s) | the guide | B3 |
| `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` (repository) | the guide | B1, B2 |
| `tests/contract/manifest.json`, `tests/contract/wire_names.txt` (repository) | the current golden: the semantic manifest and its readable projection | A10, H2 |
| `tests/contract/released/1.0.json` (repository) | the released baseline, with provenance | H6 |
| `tests/contract/rules_allowlist.txt` (repository) | pre-existing rule violations, which may only shrink; empty after H1 | A3, H1 |

`store::KINDS` gains `plan`, `doctor_report` and `repair_journal` (the last for documentation and schema listing; the journal reader, not `store`, reads it).

### §7.8 Config and environment

- **No new `config.toml` keys.**
  - The doctor has no configuration. Its policy (which fixers run, their gates) is code, as the doctor contract wants: capabilities must describe one behaviour, not a configurable family.
  - `limits` gains no configurable entry. The plan and doctor bounds are safety limits, not preferences.
- **Release environment:** none new.
- **Harness:** `OMADDONS_UPDATE_WIRE_NAMES` (H2: rewrites the current golden only), `OMADDONS_ADVANCE_RELEASED_BASELINE` (H2: the release procedure's baseline step), `OMADDONS_UPDATE_SKILL` (B1), `OMADDONS_TEST_FIXERS` (E6; debug builds only).
- **Build:** `OMADDONS_BUILD_ID` (D1) and `OMADDONS_GUIDE_SHA256` (B1), set by `build.rs`, never read from the environment at run time.
- **Debug:** the doctor failpoints and `fsx.barrier.sync` (above), read through the existing `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS`.

### §7.9 Constants (`src/limits.rs`; each with a `REGISTRY` row and a `LIMIT_NAMES` entry, and the `limit_registries` snapshot re-accepted)

| Constant | Value | Config | Purpose | Leaf |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `PLANS_MAX_FILES` | 512 | no | hard cap on stored plans; at it, a dry run stores nothing (`plan_not_stored`) | D4 |
| `PLANS_MAX_BYTES` | 32 MiB | no | hard cap on the plan store's total size | D4 |
| `PLAN_MAX_BYTES` | 256 KiB | no | one plan file at most, on write and on every read | D4 |
| `PLANS_SWEEP_MAX` | 64 | no | expired plans one cleanup batch deletes at most | D4 |
| `PLAN_LEASE_TIMEOUT` | 30 s | no | how long a second `apply` of one plan waits for its lease | D5 |
| `PLAN_EVIDENCE_LINES_MAX` | 20,000 | no | history lines `plans show` and `already_applied` scan backwards at most | D9 |
| `LOCK_HELD_LONG` | 10 min | no | a global-lock holder older than this is `fm-concurrency_primitives-lock-held-long` | F1 |
| `DOCTOR_RUNS_SOFT_MAX` | 200 | no | `fix` and `undo` run directories past which `doctor-runs-accumulated` reports (diagnose runs do not count) | E8 |
| `DOCTOR_GC_SUGGESTED_AGE` | 30 days | no | the `--before` age remediations suggest (`doctor gc --before 30d --dry-run`) | E8 |
| `DOCTOR_GC_MAX_DELETIONS` | 1,000 | no | victims one `doctor gc` deletes at most; the report says how many remain | E8 |
| `DOCTOR_QUARANTINE_SOFT_MAX` | 1 GiB | no | quarantine bytes past which it reports | E8 |
| `DOCTOR_FIX_MAX_ACTIONS` | 1,000 | no | primitives one repair may plan; past it, `REFUSING` (`too_many_actions`); a fixer with `cardinality: high` discloses it in `--dry-run` | E6 |
| `DOCTOR_SCAN_MAX_ENTRIES` | 20,000 | no | entries one detector's walks visit per run; past it the detector stops and reports `check-incomplete` | E3 |
| `DOCTOR_DETECTOR_DEADLINE` | 2 s | no | a `default` or `deep` detector's run-time deadline without `--budget`; past it, `check-incomplete` | E3 |
| `SKILL_DIRS_MAX` | 8 | no | skill directories `history_tail.skill_dirs[]` keeps and the drift check follows | B3 |
| `DIRTY_DIRS_MAX` | 64 | no | directory handles a commit window holds before it syncs them early | G3 |
| `RUN_ID_RETRY` | 2 | no | fresh ULIDs drawn after a run-directory name collision | E3 |

The existing `QUICK_DETECTOR_BUDGET` (5 ms), `PLAN_TTL` (24 h), `LOCK_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT` (5 s) and `ORPHAN_MIN_AGE` (1 h) start being used by the doctor and the plan store.

Not constants (test budgets, `tests/perf.rs`): `capabilities` < 20 ms, `doctor health` < 200 ms, the guide under 500 lines and 32 KiB, the harness under 60 s.

**Rules every leaf follows (§8): the common rules every leaf bead carries, and the defaults for questions the plan does not answer (M4 plan, 2026-10-24).**

## §8 Rules every leaf follows

### §8.0 Common rules for every M4 leaf

Every leaf bead carries this block verbatim, as M3's leaves carried theirs. Plan keys (A1 … H6) map to bead ids in the first comment on the milestone epic.

1. **The gate.** `argc gate` passes before any commit that changes code: `*.rs`, `Cargo.*`, `rust-toolchain.toml`, `deny.toml`, lint config, embedded assets (`omarchy/**`, `catalog/**`, `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md`, `src/contract/guide/*.md`), fixtures or snapshots (vision D16: a local gate, no CI). Run `ubs` on the changed files. `argc gate --all` (cargo deny) is required when `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` or `deny.toml` changed.
2. **One writer.** Every filesystem mutation goes through `src/fsx/` (enforced by `tests/single_writer.rs`).
   - A new subprocess needs a named entry in that test's spawner allowlist, with its reason.
   - A new `prune()` caller needs a `PRUNE_CALLERS` entry. In `src/doctor/`, only `gc.rs` may prune (M4-D36).
3. **Commands never print.** They return an `Outcome` that `src/output/` renders. No `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests, and no `unsafe`.
4. **DEC-1, no stubs.** A command leaf adds, in the same commit:
   1. its clap variant;
   2. its `COMMANDS` row, with every M4 field (`dictionary`, `exits`, `data`, `stores_plan`, `network`; A1);
   3. its `command_name` and dispatch arms;
   4. the help-layout update;
   5. contract matrix rows (one success, one failure, with snapshots);
   6. the `special.rs` read-only invocation for any `mutates: false` path;
   7. `cli_skeleton` literals;
   8. its `CLI_PATHS` row in `omarchy/Model.js`;
   9. its README section.
5. **DEC-3, wire shapes.** Every `data` and report struct derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`. Field order is rendering order (deterministic, but not contract: M4-D56), maps are `BTreeMap`, and no `HashMap` or `HashSet` appears in a serialized type (M4-D18).
6. **DEC-4, the contract.** List every new or changed wire name (codes, `details` keys, data keys, actions, events, kinds, files) in the close comment.
   - Add by default. A leaf may rename, retype or remove a name only on a surface it owns, to correct a known pre-release inconsistency: it records the change with a compatibility note in its close comment and updates the widget, the guide, the snapshots and the corpus in the same commit (M4-D55). Any other rename waits for H1.
   - Every new shape passes A3's rule test; never add to `tests/contract/rules_allowlist.txt`.
   - Declare every new error's `DetailSpec` (M4-D10) and every new code's `meaning` (A9).
   - Declare every new volatile key in `contract::VOLATILE` (M4-D18).
   - `schema_version` stays "1.0".
7. **D22, constants.** New constants go in `src/limits.rs` or `src/politeness.rs`, each with a `REGISTRY` row and a `LIMIT_NAMES` entry, and the `limit_registries` snapshot is re-accepted (review the diff).
8. **Fixes.** Every error carries a `fix`, and a `fix_argv` when the fix is a complete omaddons command. A usage error found from the arguments (a misplaced client, a bad value) is raised before planning, recovery or any commit, so the wrong invocation changes nothing. A prose fix may not name a runnable omaddons command (`PROSE_COMMANDS`, `names_a_command` in `tests/contract/main.rs`). A fix that keeps the user's verb is marked `UsageFix::UserVerb` (M4-D12).
9. **Privacy, on every channel.** No output names an account, realm or character. Tests that create `WTF/` run `assert_private_all(stdout, stderr)` with `--progress json`. Doctor evidence never carries file content (M4-D42).
10. **Real machine.** Real-machine tests never change the Forever client (`forever_guard()`), undo every change before asserting, quote every `SKIP` line, and never write under a `WTF/`.
11. **README is the product contract.** A leaf that ships a user-visible surface updates its README section in the same commit.
12. **Beads.**
    - Work on `main`. Claim with `br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`.
    - File found work with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`.
    - Run `br lint <ids> --json` clean.
    - Commit code and `.beads/` together after `br sync --flush-only`.
    - Bead text never contains home paths, host names or people's names; use the placeholders of §0.2.
13. **Time.** Code that uses local time takes `jiff::tz::TimeZone::system()`. Tests set `TZ=UTC` and, where expiry matters, `OMADDONS_NOW`.
14. **A protocol change lands with its own crash tests.** A leaf that adds or changes a journal shape, a recovery rule, a binding rule, a deletion rule or a durability rule closes only when its own adversarial matrix passes: every failpoint it adds, every journaled step, repeated recovery, and injected I/O failure where it writes. These leaves are D1, D2, D5, D8, E5, E7, E8, E11, E14 and G3. F9 integrates across fixers. It never discovers whether a leaf's own protocol works.
15. **Bounded work.** A leaf that reads an untrusted or user-sized input bounds it with a named constant, and reports exhaustion as truncated or incomplete, never as a clean result. A store a leaf writes has a hard quota, and a full store declines the write rather than evicting live data.
16. **Previews bind.** A leaf that adds or changes a mutating command path either binds it (`app::precondition`, `--if-match`, and a test that changes state between preview and run) or records in its close comment why it does not, citing M4-D22.
17. **The guide stays the skill** (M4-D7). Once B1 has landed, a leaf that changes anything the guide's generated blocks show (a command, a code, an action, an env var) regenerates `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` with `OMADDONS_UPDATE_SKILL=1 cargo test --test skill` and commits it. That renders from a hermetic `TestEnv`, never the developer's real `HOME` or config, and no shell redirect writes a gated asset. `tests/skill.rs` fails until it does.
18. **The corpus grows with the surface.** Once C4 has landed, a leaf that adds a command or an intent hook adds its corpus rows to `tests/contract/intent_corpus.rs`. Whichever of C4 and the command leaf lands second adds them.
19. **The doctor's catalog is code.** A leaf that adds a failure mode adds its `FAILURE_MODES` row, its fixture (M4-D47), its row in README's doctor table, and its Appendix B line in the close comment.

### §8.1 Defaults for questions this plan does not answer

When a leaf meets a question the plan does not settle, it applies these defaults in order, records the choice in a `decided:` comment on the leaf, and extends README if the choice changes a promise:

1. Prefer an existing error code, warning code, action or key to a new one.
2. Additive JSON, token-frugal by default. Detail goes behind `-v`.
3. Stable order: sorted by target id, then name, then path.
4. No network on a read path, except for commands whose job is upstream (`outdated`, `search`, `info`, `doctor --online`).
5. Every write through fsx, and every mutation through a transaction or a recorded settings line.
6. Fail closed on anything persisted that cannot be fully read.
7. Never ask the owner. Decide, write `decided: … because …`, and move on (CLAUDE.md "Blocked on a Human").

## Appendix B: the doctor's catalog

46 failure modes: ids, severities, tiers, what detects each, its repair, and the owning leaf. "Exists" means a detector or repair exists today (§2.5). "Delegate" is M4-D37, disclosed in the preview and run only after the token check. "Set-aside" is M4-D38: a suspension (`needs_force`, never default) whose undo reactivates the journal only while nothing it depends on has changed. The `status` column says whether `status` reports it: C for `--cached` and plain `status`, Q for plain `status` only, and — when only the doctor reports it.

Row 1 covers both journal families. A `.repair` journal a crash left is `journal-pending` too, its evidence says `family: "repair"`, and the delegation recovers it like any other (M4-D37). A repair journal recovery cannot settle (row 6, `family: "repair"`) fences only the resources it protects, and its evidence lists them (M4-D62); one whose `prepared` line cannot be decoded (row 4 or 3, `family: "repair"`) fails every committing command closed until its set-aside. - 2 delegations (rows 1 and 9);
- 6 set-asides, sharing one suspending fixer (rows 3–8); for rows 3 and 4 it moves only what it can attribute without the payload (M4-D38);
- 1 quarantine of temp files (16);
- 1 flatten (36);
- 1 blob quarantine (37);
- 1 rewrite (40);
- 1 chmod (41).

That is 13 repairable rows, 6 of them gated behind `--force --yes` and 1 disabled by default. The other 33 are reports with an exact remediation. Every repair is lowered to primitive steps (§6.14.1); a flatten is two or three renames.

| `orphan-snapshot-dir*` | same; row 35 covers the kept only-copy case |
| `state-version-older*` | every authoritative kind is 1.0; caches migrate on their next write (§2.3) |
| `status-stale*` | `status.json` is no longer anyone's signal (M3-D4); it is rewritten after every commit |
| `history-torn-line*` | torn tails are closed by the next append; rewriting history is forbidden by README (M4-D49). Row 15 reports unreadable lines |
| `validator-orphan*` | a missing or orphaned HTTP validator is simply no validator: harmless derived data |
| `client-version-changed*` | the next full discovery re-parses a changed client (the cache's stamps) |
| `target-key-duplicate*` fixer | the copy is re-keyed at its first registration; row 23 reports it |
| `duplicate-addon` | no identity rule detects "the same addon twice under different folders" without false positives; `adopt`'s evidence already flags contested groups |

| `nested-addon-folder*` as a default fix | shipped disabled (M4-D39) |

**Appendix C: the guide's outline, the never-do list and the intent corpus's starting set (M4 plan, 2026-10-24).**

## Appendix C: the guide, and the intent corpus

### C.1 The guide's outline (B2 writes the prose; B1 places the blocks)

```markdown
---
name: omaddons
description: <the trigger sentence of §6.3.2>
---
{{stamp}}

# omaddons for agents

What it is (5 lines): one binary for every WoW client on this Linux machine; every change a journaled,
undoable transaction; every command one JSON envelope with fixes as argv. Learn more from the tool itself:
`omaddons capabilities --json` · `omaddons robot-docs schema <command>` · `omaddons robot-docs errors`.

## The core loop                      (§4.1's six steps; step 4: an apply whose result is unknown → `omaddons plans show <plan_id>` before anything else)
## Reading the envelope               (keys; fix_argv / alternatives / commands[].argv; partial; never parse display text)
## Exit codes
{{exit_general}}
The doctor tree uses its own dictionary:
{{exit_doctor}}
## Targets and refs
{{targets}}
Refs: catalog name | gh:Owner/Repo | wowi:<id> | tukui:<slug> | wowace:<slug> | git:https://…#rev | url:https://… | ./zip
## The safety model
- transactions and undo (bare undo = the last run; --last-by agent)
- running clients (/reload; SavedVariables never written while running)
- previews: --dry-run → plan_id → apply; or --if-match <precondition>; plan_stale means "preview again"; the guarantee is per target, and `outcomes[]` says what happened on each; `already_applied` and a lost output are answered by `plans show`
- the doctor: read-only by default; fix with consent; every repair undoable while nothing it touched has changed since (undo refuses, before moving anything, once something has)
- tolerate unknown fields and enum values: additions arrive in minor versions
- two kinds of "run": history's `run` (an invocation, `undo --run <ULID>`) and a doctor run (a directory, `doctor undo <run id>`); the shapes differ, and each command refuses the other's with the right fix
## Things omaddons will NEVER do
{{never}}
## Recipes                            (§6.3.4's eight, as `sh recipe=… expect=…` blocks)
## Errors you will meet
{{errors_common}}
## The doctor loop
`omaddons doctor --robot-triage --json` → auto-fixable? `omaddons doctor fix --only <id>` : `omaddons doctor explain <id>`
→ P0 and not auto-fixable: tell the user before anything else → `omaddons undo --last-by agent` reverts a repair too.
## Commands
{{commands}}
## Environment
{{env}}
## Where to look next
```

The `{{never}}` table (M4-D7; shared with `doctor robot-docs`):

1. Delete your files during a change. Removals go into undo snapshots or a quarantine, and only `backup prune`, `doctor gc --before --yes` and retention delete, by their documented rules.
2. Write into `Interface/AddOns` outside a transaction, touch a `Blizzard_*` folder, or follow a symlinked folder.
3. Write SavedVariables while the client runs, or parse or edit them, except reading BugGrabber's.
4. Rewrite `history.jsonl`, `config.toml` or `addons.toml` behind your back (`config set` and `export --write` edit them only when asked).
5. Contact a host outside the allowlist, make a request under `--offline`, or send a credential anywhere but its own service.
6. Run a shell, or interpret a string as a command: argv only.
7. Prompt for input, or print ANSI under `--json`.
8. Act on state it cannot read (a newer or damaged journal, record or history line): it refuses and says why.

### C.2 The intent corpus's starting set (C4; D5, D9, E3, E6 and E7 add theirs; at least 60 at H4)

Each row is `wrong argv → error code → the fix's expected exit`, on `intent_home()`.

- **Who adds a row.** Rows naming a surface that does not exist yet (`capabilities`, `robot-docs`, `completions`, `apply`, the doctor verbs) are added by whichever of the two leaves lands second, the surface's leaf or C4 (common rule 18). C4 lands the rest.
- **Who owns the count.** H4 checks that the corpus holds at least 60 rows (criterion 5). The set below has 56 rows, and the later leaves add 11 more.
- **Erroring rows change nothing.** Each wrong argv runs on its own copy of `intent_home()`, whose records and client trees must hash unchanged when the row is an error; the fix runs on an independent copy (C4).

| Wrong | Code | Fix | Fix exit |
|---|---|---|---|
| `omaddons retail update` | `usage` | `omaddons update -t retail` | 0 |
| `omaddons era status` | `usage` | `omaddons status -t era` | 0 |
| `omaddons wotlk list` | `usage` | `omaddons list -t wotlk` | 0 |
| `omaddons sod install questie` | `usage` | `omaddons install questie -t sod` | 0 |
| `omaddons status retail` | `usage` | `omaddons status -t retail` | 0 |

**Appendix E: the vision comments H5 writes (M4 plan, 2026-10-24).**

## Appendix E: vision comments (H5)

Each is added with `br comments add omad-vision-8qa -f <file>`, in the house style. The body is not edited. The section numbers in this list are the vision's own (§5.5, §5.8–§5.12, §7, §10), naming the part of the vision body each comment amends.

1. **§7 M4 as decomposed and shipped**: the decomposition record (the epic, eight areas, 60 leaves, 153 edges, changes during M4, every recomputation after a design gate), and every departure of §5.6, each with what the vision said, what M4 does and why.
2. **§5.10 discovery surfaces as shipped**: capabilities, robot-docs, the skill, intent inference, completions, verbosity.
3. **§5.9 previews, plans and `apply` as shipped**: tokens with approval witnesses on twelve commands, the under-lock checks and their stated scope, the per-target guarantee, stored typed intents in the cache with quotas, the lease, the lifecycle, `plans show`, and the widget's routine rule.
4. **§5.8 doctor as shipped**: the surface, the runtime, run directories, the envelope, the exit dictionary, the catalog of Appendix B with the dropped list.
5. **§5.5 the repair transaction**: the second journal family of primitive steps, endpoint predicates, recovery and its barrier order, fences by resource set, guarded reactivation of a set-aside, undo, retention exemption, `doctor gc`'s retention plan, quarantine per filesystem.
6. **§5.5 step 7 durability**: group commit at each transaction's end, derived writes without fsync, deferred directory fsyncs through owned handles and explicit barriers with their ordering arguments, the counted target and the measured counts before and after (supersedes comment 53's per-action fsync and closes `omad-7ccp`).
7. **§5.12 wire names and the freeze**: the semantic manifest and its readable projection, the released baseline and its provenance, the bump rule in both directions, the tag, the rule test that held from slice 1, and the pre-freeze audit's change list.
8. **Every wire name M4 added** (DEC-4, D21), reconciled with every leaf's close comment, as M3's comment 1240 was.
9. **The constants M4 added** (D22).
10. **External facts observed during M4**, if any (real-home doctor findings, compat observations).
11. **An index** of comments 1–10.

H6 adds the last: "§10 Milestone status: M4 … is done (date)", with the checkpoint's outcomes, departures and limits, and "M5 (accounts and release engineering) is next".
