comments.text:
**Filing record: how the M4 beads were made (M4 plan, 2026-10-24; filed 2026-10-25).**

## How the beads were written

- The source is the M4 plan (5,973 lines), verified against commit `c0ab5e9`. Its sections are filed verbatim as the comments above on this epic, so nothing in the plan is lost; the beads are the elaborated, authoritative version.
- One designer agent per leaf and per epic read the plan's entry for its bead, every decision and section that entry cites, every other plan line that names it, the entries of the leaves it blocks and is blocked by, and the code it touches at `c0ab5e9`. It then wrote the description, the acceptance criteria, the planning rationale (the first comment on each leaf) and the subtasks. The plan's entry for each leaf is the second comment on it, verbatim, as provenance.
- Each designer decided the open questions it met and marked them "Decided while writing this bead" in the description (1,781 such decisions across the beads). Where the plan disagreed with the code at `c0ab5e9`, the bead follows the code and says so (588 places, indexed below).
- **The beads were not adversarially reviewed.** A review-and-revise pass was planned and dropped, so that implementation starts sooner; its cost was out of proportion to what it would catch before the code exists. They passed only the mechanical checks listed below. Expect some defects. When a bead disagrees with the plan's comments, with a neighbouring bead or with the code, the implementer decides by the bead's common rules and the plan's §8.1 defaults (restated in this epic's Considerations), records it as a `decided: …` comment on the bead being worked, fixes the neighbouring bead's text with a comment when an interface they share changes, and files anything outside the bead's scope with `--deps discovered-from:<id>`.

## What was added at filing

- **Area T** (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9`): T1 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1` (structured test logs, `tests/common/tlog.rs`, and the `argc e2e` runner), and T2–T4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.2`, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.3`, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4`), the slice 1–3 exit demos as end-to-end suites. They change no product behaviour. T1 is a root; T2–T4 wait for every leaf of their slice and block H4 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`, so the plan's critical path of 25 units does not grow. The plan's §10.6 duty to record slices 1–3's demos moves to T2–T4; H6 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6` still records slice 4's.
- **Subtasks**: 283 under the 64 leaves (216 tasks, 63 features, 4 docs), each one coherent commit that passes the gate. 102 of them are test subtasks (label `tests`, titles starting `Tests:` or `E2E:`), placed after what they test.
- **The closing protocol** for a leaf with subtasks: work the subtasks in their order; the agent that closes the last one checks the leaf's own acceptance criteria and closes the leaf. A subtask is not ready while its leaf has an open blocker.

## Counts

| What | Count |
|---|---|
| Milestone epic | 1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`) |
| Area epics | 9 (A–H from the plan, T added at filing) |
| Leaves | 64 (the plan's 60 and area T's 4); 63 new, G3 reuses `omad-7ccp` (M4-D59), undeferred and re-parented |
| Subtasks | 283 |
| Leaf-level `blocks` edges | 210: the plan's 153 and area T's 57 (T1 → T2–T4; the 15 slice-1 leaves → T2; the 11 slice-2 leaves → T3; the 25 slice-3 leaves → T4; T2–T4 → H4) |
| T1 edges | 132: T1 blocks every leaf or subtask that writes an integration or end-to-end test (`uses_test_log`), except the 6 leaves already downstream of T1 |
| Sibling order edges | 262, between subtasks of the same leaf |
| Description text | about 14 MB |

## Ids, placeholders and labels

- Ids follow the hierarchy: area epics are `<epic>.1` … `<epic>.9` in the order A–H, T; leaves are `<area>.<n>` in key order within their area (G3 keeps its own id); subtasks are `<leaf>.<n>` in their order. The first comment on this epic maps every plan key and subtask key to its id.
- Descriptions were written with placeholders (the plan key in double braces) and filed with the ids substituted.
- Labels: `m4` on every bead; one `size-S`, `size-M` or `size-L` and one `slice-1` … `slice-4` on every leaf and subtask (no subtask is `size-L`); `tests` on test subtasks and on area T's leaves; `milestone` on this epic.

## Checks run

Before filing, on every spec: the sections present and in order; the common rules block verbatim in every leaf and subtask; the acceptance criteria field equal to the description's checklist; type, priority, size, slice and title equal to the plan's; every blocker and dependent named in Dependencies with its id; valid placeholders only; subtask numbering, labels and order edges; public-safe text (no machine paths, hosts, addresses, names or secrets). After filing: `br lint`, `br dep cycles` (none), `bv --robot-insights`, `--robot-plan`, `--robot-triage` and `--robot-label-health`; anything they flagged is in a later comment on this epic.

## Where the beads follow the code instead of the plan

Each item below is restated in its bead, where the implementer will meet it; this index collects them. Items for epics concern their descriptions.

### AREA-A (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1`)

- Plan §2.1 and M4-D11 count 31 recommendation actions. A2's bead counts 22 distinct names at c0ab5e9; the epic uses 22.
- §2.1 places the event structs at src/output/stderr.rs:298, 328, 365, 401. At c0ab5e9 the struct lines are :299, :329, :366, :402; the epic cites the struct lines.
- §2.1 says the bare-help 'Start with' line is 117 columns. It measures 116 characters at src/app/help.rs:181 against MAX_WIDTH 80 (src/app/help.rs:19).
- M4-D4 says capabilities reads only the registries and config.toml. credential_configured also needs a metadata-only presence check of the GitHub credential file (A4's bead); the epic notes this exception.
- §10.5 does not list A7 under src/cli.rs, or A8 under src/resolve/cache.rs, src/discover/ and src/fsx/lock.rs (found by A7's and A8's beads); both added to the epic's hot-spot table.
- The plan gives no edge between A4 and A10, although both need src/contract/commands.rs, and none between A4 and A5, although both need the three-valued retryability. The epic states the leaf beads' 'whichever lands first creates it as A4's bead specifies' rules.
- A4's and A5's beads hold the doctor_exit place differently: capabilities keeps it present with null and exit_codes.doctor as [], while robot-docs errors leaves it out until E3's dictionary exists. The epic states both, and whichever of them and E3 lands second makes the key real.

### AREA-B (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2`)

- The History scope row is at src/fsx/scope.rs:114-117 at c0ab5e9, not :112-115 as the plan cites (two-line drift, also found by B3's bead). It still admits no Writer::Skill.
- Checked and still true at c0ab5e9: no robot-docs command, no src/contract/ module and no skills/ directory; Paths::skill_dir() at src/state/paths.rs:263-265; Writer::Skill at src/fsx/scope.rs:39 and Scope::Skill at :95/:126/:526; ScopeTable::new at :238-251; README 'For coding agents' at README.md:2743. The recipe flags exist (outdated --changelog at src/app/outdated.rs:66, sync --locked at src/app/sync.rs:56, history --since at src/app/history.rs:37, undo --last-by at src/app/undo.rs:48). history reads an explicit global --actor as a filter (src/app/history.rs:5-6), so the undo-agent-today recipe's 'history --actor agent' works as written.

### AREA-C (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3`)

- The plan's 'final filter' (src/cli.rs:756-763) only replaces a fix that does not parse or repeats the failing argv. The demotion of a mutating guess to `help <it>` is in subcommand_fix (src/cli.rs:876-885), and no UsageFix type exists. Per C1's bead, the hooks run before subcommand_fix and apply both checks to their own fix.
- Observed at c0ab5e9 with the debug binary on an empty synthetic home: `omaddons era status` gets 'the closest command is remove' with fix `omaddons help remove`, because the alias `rm` is within distance 2. The plan only mentions `retail update` falling to `help`. Hook 1 now handles this case first.
- The plan cites remove.rs:163-275 for 'remove commits before it reports'. At c0ab5e9, remove's run spans src/app/remove.rs:163-321, with the engine call at :254-258 and the unknown names turned into warnings at :273-280. The behaviour is the same.
- Bare `update` already selects every discovered target, test clients included (src/app/update.rs:135), so `-t all` does not widen update's selection as M4-D13 assumes. Per C2's bead, the human line states how many of the selected clients are test clients.
- `resolve` has no argv (src/discover/registry.rs:642-646). Per C3's bead, resolve records the ranked words in process and the command boundary (src/app/mod.rs:284-300) builds the fix.
- registry.json stores absolute client paths (src/state/registry.rs:33-47), so the plan's 'copy the corpus home twice' cannot give independent copies. Per C4's bead, one home is restored byte for byte at the same path from a pristine snapshot.
- The custom-client default id `wotlk` lives in the FAMILIES rows (src/rules.rs:1158-1173, wotlk at :1169), not in PRODUCTS. Per C1's bead, family-row default ids are client words.

### AREA-D (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4`)

- Precondition.targets is at src/app/precondition.rs:72 (the plan cites :73). The plan's Vec<(TargetRef, u64)> becomes Vec<(TargetRef, Option<u64>)>, because errors dismiss and backup prune bind keys only (D1).
- Line drift in the plan's citations: the generation check is src/engine/tx.rs:1050-1056 (plan :1049-1056); the re-judge loop is :1105-1141 (plan :1104-1139); prune's Kind::Plan arm is src/fsx/prune.rs:368-374 (plan :371-373).
- Plan step D2.7 (the M4-D55 errors dismiss precondition presence fix) was already made by omad-q585 at c0ab5e9. D2 adds a presence-rule guard test instead of a wire change.
- copy never reads --from's folders; it installs from refs (src/app/copy.rs:1-11). So D8's step 'the staged tree digest must equal the witnessed source digest' cannot hold. D8 re-checks the witnessed source folders under the lock instead (found by both D1 and D8).
- §7.9 assigns PLAN_EVIDENCE_LINES_MAX and the backward scan to D9, but D5's already_applied check needs them first and D9 is blocked by D5. D5 adds them and D9 generalizes them.
- §7.7 calls the .lease and .lock files empty, but D5's locked details need the holder's {pid, command, age_s}. The lease file carries a holder line, as the global lock file does (src/fsx/lock.rs:125-159).
- M4-D19 spells the stable --file <dir> id @dir:<hash>, but the code's form is listing:<hash> (src/sources/local.rs). The beads follow the code, and resolve::updates::is_static learns the new prefix.

### AREA-E (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5`)

- The plan's hot-spot table (§10.5) lists src/engine/undo.rs for E7 alone. The leaf beads have two more leaves touching it: E12 (the refusal of a target-less line via engine::undo::target_of, and the AddOns-folder repair rule in check_conflicts at src/engine/undo.rs:964) and E14 (an under-lock fence-gate call beside refuse_newer_state at src/engine/undo.rs:243 and :417; also in tx.rs, restore.rs:454/773/1177 and restore_addons.rs:777). The epic's hot-spot table records all three, ordered E12 and E14 before E7 by edges.
- §2.4 cites issues_for at src/app/issues.rs:80-208. At c0ab5e9 the ids module is :17-33, machine_issues starts at :95 and issues_for at :125. The epic cites :17-33.
- The plan has no E4 -> E10 edge, although E10's `doctor ...` fix names E4's `doctor health` (from E10's bead).
- E14's fence refusal names E3's `doctor explain`, but E3 is not an ancestor of E14 (from E14's bead).
- E7's acceptance needs a stored, applied undo, but D4 and D5 are not ancestors of E7 (from E7's bead).

### AREA-F (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6`)

- Slack: §10.3 gives F9 2 units, but that was computed without area T. Recomputed with area T's edges, F9 has slack 0 on a second 25-unit path: E1 → E2 → E3 → E6 → E7 → F2 → F9 → T4 → H4 → H5 → H6. G3 also drops to 0 on that path. Every other F leaf's slack is unchanged (F1 3; F4 and F6 4; F3, F5, F7, F8 and F10 2; F2 0).
- Row ownership: Appendix B gives rows 19 and 12 to F4 and F3, but E2's bead registers them (fm-configs-config-parse-error and fm-schemas-state-corrupt), and E1 registers the 7 published ids. So area F adds 34 registry rows and completes the other 9 of the 43 it owns.
- Line references that drifted at c0ab5e9, corrected in the body: probe_global is src/fsx/lock.rs:161-191 (the plan says 126-191); BlobCache::get is src/engine/blobs.rs:307-326 (the plan says 308-325); status's reason pass-through is src/app/status.rs:884-892 (the plan says 885-891); the credential-mode warning is src/state/config.rs:980-991 (the plan says 982-990); issues_for starts at src/app/issues.rs:125.
- Plan facts that differ from the code, carried over from the leaf beads' own notes and summarized in the epic's 'What the leaf beads found against the plan' section: local_blob_candidate already re-hashes (src/engine/plan.rs:5341-5376), and only fetch_blob's cache hits (:4839-4852) and the download memo are unchecked; journal::Unrecoverable has only TooNew and Unreadable (src/engine/journal.rs:489-494), so only 2 of MANUAL_REPAIR's 4 reasons can reach status; status fails closed on a broken config before computing issues, so row 19's 'C (machine)' status column surfaces as that refusal.

### AREA-G (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7`)

- Plan sections 6.16, 7.2 and 10.5 put G1's row identity on `status`'s update entries and list G1 in the `src/app/status.rs` hot spot. Per G1's bead, the Updates rows come from `list -v` (`omarchy/Model.js:946-982`, `:1653-1675`), so the keys go on `list`'s `latest` (`src/app/list.rs:94-95`, `:112-118`), with an `asset` key added. The H1 edge's 'update entries' new keys' therefore means `latest.source`, `latest.release_id` and `latest.asset`.
- The plan cites `tests/omarchy_widget.rs:44-48` for the binds rule. At c0ab5e9 it is `:42-46` (G1's bead).
- Plan section 6.16 lists an `undo` template, but none exists (`omarchy/Model.js:99-127`). Undo last runs `status.last_change.undo.argv` (`omarchy/PanelView.qml:247-250`).
- `classifyCliArgv` (`omarchy/Model.js:384-420`) has no rule for `--force`, `--yes` or any path. Until E8 adds its row, `doctor gc` classifies as the read path `doctor`, so G2's refusal checks the argv's leading words.
- G3's forecast of 44 assumes a single action-log sync, but M4-D54's three sync points each find buffered lines in the folder engine (`src/engine/tx.rs:1226-1269`), so about 46 is expected before the directory change.
- Plan section 6.17 says a barrier error before `done` triggers an in-process rollback. G3's bead instead leaves the journal for the next lock-taking command, because the folder engine's failure handler would roll forward after `swapped` and report success (`src/engine/tx.rs:1273-1299`). It also adds a barrier after `prepared` (`src/fsx/sys.rs:213-215`) and makes `barrier(&self)` take `&self`, not `&mut self`.
- Plan section 10.4's six-lane schedule (lane 4: G1 12-14, G3 15-18, G2 18-20) no longer fits once area T is added, because G2's latest finish is now t = 18.
- The plan's section 10.5 row for `src/state/history.rs` and `history_tail.rs` does not list G3, but G3's bead adds `history::append_in_window` and `history_tail::follow`. D5, D9 and B3 also edit those files and are not G3's ancestors, so G3 rebases onto them.

### AREA-H (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8`)

- H1: timestamps publish a plain string schema (#[schemars(with = "String")], e.g. src/app/status.rs:155-156), so name heuristics miss instants under other names (net-log's since, src/app/net_log.rs:47; errors' dismissed, src/app/errors.rs:430). H1 adds format date-time and a type-based checker.
- H1: only the bound-run refusal sets plan_stale.details.changed (src/app/precondition.rs:214-225), although M4-D10's example declares the key required.
- H1: help --json names a nested command by clap's leaf name (src/app/help.rs:341), so 'help targets add --json' says 'add'.
- H1: rule 4 as written would rename user-typed vocabularies (kebab-case Family at src/rules.rs:148, daily-copy at src/state/config.rs:79) and the doctor contract's P0-P3 severities (src/app/issues.rs:44-51). They become EXCEPTIONS rows.
- H2: support::check asserts schema_version == "1.0" as a literal (tests/contract/main.rs:136), and the envelope snapshots embed the same string, so the plan's bump remedy also trips them.
- H3: the existing repeats compare through serde_json::Value (tests/contract/main.rs:507-514; serde_json is built without preserve_order), so member order was never compared. The matrix is scenarios, not rows. src/source_scan.rs is #[cfg(test)] and crate-private (src/lib.rs:37-38).
- H4: README's warning summary says 51 over 52 rows (README.md:1872). The general exit table differs from Exit::meaning() (src/error.rs:81). No test reads README.
- H5: the per-action fsync the plan attributes to vision comment 53 is in the vision body's section 5.5 step 7. The plan's counts of 60 leaves and 153 edges differ from the tracker as filed (64 leaves, plus subtasks and area T's edges).
- H6: keyless_installs_forever installs into the Forever client when that client manages no addons (tests/real_machine.rs:753-762). The approved checkpoint runs forbid that, so in that case the test is excluded.

But the gate runs the QML step only when omarchy/ changed or with --all (scripts/gate.sh:35-40). A WTF journal with a step waits only while its client runs or may run (journal.rs:1037-1046). The plan's own wording ('the next change command', §2.5) matches the code. title: Epic: M4 the contract registry and the discovery surfaces
description:
## Background

This is area A of M4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`, the milestone epic "the agent surface, the doctor and the first tag"). It builds the contract registry, a new module `src/contract/`, and the discovery surfaces that read it: `omaddons capabilities`, `omaddons robot-docs schema` and `robot-docs errors`, bare help's discovery line, `omaddons completions <SHELL>`, three verbosity levels, a meaning and a typed `details` specification for every code, and the semantic contract manifest with its compatibility classifier. It has ten leaves. Nine are in slice 1 ("Self-describing"); A6, the discovery line, is in slice 4 because it may only name commands that already exist.

The leaves: A1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1`, per-command facts in `COMMANDS`, and canonical names), A2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.2`, registries for actions, events, env vars, features and per-source facts), A3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`, schemas with the serialize contract, declared `details`, and live validation), A4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`, `omaddons capabilities`), A5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5`, `robot-docs schema` and `robot-docs errors`), A6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.6`, bare help's discovery line and `help --json` `discovery`), A7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.7`, `omaddons completions <SHELL>`), A8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.8`, verbosity levels), A9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9`, a meaning and a typed `DetailSpec` for every code) and A10 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.10`, the semantic contract manifest and its compatibility classifier).

It serves two of the milestone's goals directly:

- **G-M4-1 Self-describing:** an agent with no prior knowledge learns everything it needs from the binary itself, in at most three calls (`omaddons capabilities --json`, `omaddons robot-docs guide`, `omaddons status --json`); every fact in those outputs is generated from the code, so it cannot drift from what the code does; every command's output has a published JSON Schema, and the contract suite validates real output against it.
- **G-M4-5 Frozen and enforced:** at the first tag the contract is consistent, complete (a semantic manifest of every input the CLI accepts and every output it emits, with a readable names list beside it) and enforced: every later change is compared with the released baseline, and one without the version bump it needs fails the gate. This area builds the manifest and the classifier; area H (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8`, freeze and close) commits the golden, wires the comparisons and makes the tag.

It also serves the vision's G4 ("the first command an agent guesses works"; "discovery via `capabilities`, `doctor` and `robot-docs`") and vision §5.10's rule that `capabilities` is "generated from the live clap tree and the registries, never maintained by hand". That rule only works once the registries exist, which is most of this area's work.

### What is true today (at `c0ab5e9`)

- **There is no `src/contract/` module**, no `capabilities`, no `robot-docs`, no completions, and no schema published for any command's `data`. An agent learns omaddons from a 2,800-line README or by trial and error.
- **`app::COMMANDS`** (`src/app/mod.rs:121-165`) holds 42 paths, each only `{name, group, mutates}`. No exit set, no exit dictionary, no plan storage and no network use is declared anywhere; the command-to-data-type mapping exists only in `run_command`'s match (`src/app/mod.rs:374-587`).
- **`auth`'s names disagree:** its `COMMANDS` row says `auth` (`src/app/mod.rs:159`), while `command_name` returns `"auth github"` for the envelope (`src/app/mod.rs:231`). `auth` takes positional value-enums (`src/app/auth.rs:37-46`), not a subcommand.
- **Error and warning codes:** `error_codes!` (`src/error.rs:150`) registers 41 error codes with wire name, exit and retryability; only 9 have doc text, so there is no `meaning`. `warning_codes!` (`src/error.rs:246`) registers 52. `error.details` is an untyped `serde_json::Value` (`src/error.rs:512`, `:625`), with no declared keys, types or enums.
- **Scattered registries with no enumerable source:** recommendation actions are `CommandHint::new("…")` string literals in about 15 files (A2's bead counts 22 distinct names at `c0ab5e9`; the plan's 31 was an overcount); NDJSON event structs are defined inside functions in `src/output/stderr.rs` (`:299`, `:329`, `:366`, `:402`) with literal names and no `JsonSchema`; environment variables have no list except README's table (`README.md:2251`); the `-t` forms are implicit in `discover::registry::resolve`'s step order; per-source hosts are one flat `ALWAYS` list (`src/net/allowlist.rs:8`); `requires_credential` is modelled nowhere.
- **Schema hazards:** every `data` type derives `JsonSchema` (`trait Outcome`, `src/output/mod.rs:34-35`), but schemars derives the deserialize contract by default, and 96 `skip_serializing_if` sites for `-v`-only fields would then be marked `required`. schemars names duplicate types by generation order (`Summary2`), so `$defs` names are not stable. `Envelope`, `Meta`, the event structs, `Phase` and `LogLevel` derive no schema. There is no JSON Schema validator among the dev-dependencies (`Cargo.toml:43-53`) and no wire-name list or golden.
- **Verbosity:** `-v` is counted (`src/cli.rs:111-112`, `ArgAction::Count`) but every consumer tests `> 0` (`Style::paths_visible`, `src/output/human.rs:26`, and about 17 sites), so there are no levels.
- **Help:** bare help is 19 lines: the groups Look, Change and Setup, a "Start with `omaddons status`" sentence (`src/app/help.rs:181`, one line of 116 columns, wider than help's `MAX_WIDTH` of 80 at `src/app/help.rs:19`) and the 0–6 exit table. The discovery trio vision §5.9 asks it to list (`capabilities`, `robot-docs`, `doctor`) does not exist.
- **Neither `clap_complete` nor `clap_mangen` is a dependency.** `deny.toml` bans tokio, reqwest, native-tls, openssl-sys and aws-lc, and checks dev-dependencies too.

### The decisions that shape this area

Each is in full, with its rejected alternatives, in the decision-log comments on the milestone epic; what an implementer needs is restated here.

- **M4-D2, one contract registry.** `src/contract/` assembles a `Registry` from the live clap tree, `app::COMMANDS` with its new facts, the error, warning and exit tables, the new action, event, env-var and feature registries, the limits and politeness registries, the rules table, the sources and the doctor's failure-mode registry. `capabilities`, `robot-docs`, the golden, help's discovery line and `doctor capabilities` all read it. A fact clap cannot give is declared exactly once, beside the command or code it describes, and a test checks it against behaviour. Rejected: a hand-written `capabilities.json` (it drifts, which is what capabilities exists to prevent); deriving every fact from observed behaviour (a command's exits are a promise and need a declaration); proc-macro attributes on clap structs (a dependency and compile time for no gain over a table).
- **M4-D3, one contract version.** The envelope's `schema_version` ("1.0") is the contract version; `capabilities.contract_version` and the golden's header repeat it. Persisted files keep their own versions, the doctor carries `doctor_contract_version`, and `tool_version` is independent.
- **M4-D4, capabilities is offline, scan-free and write-free, and reports effective values.** It reads the binary's registries and `config.toml` only: no discovery, no network, no writes. (A4's bead adds one exception the code forces: `credential_configured` checks only the presence of the credential file, never its content.) Config-changeable values carry `source: "builtin" | "config"`. A broken `config.toml` gives the built-in values and a `config_error` object, never a failure. Human form at most 40 lines; under 20 ms.
- **M4-D5, exits declared beside the command and verified.** `CommandEntry` gains `dictionary` (`General` | `Doctor`), `exits`, `data` (a schema function), `stores_plan` and `network` (`None` | `Optional` | `Required`). Static rules: `--check`/`--strict` lists 6, a mutating command lists 5, every general command lists 0, 1 and 2. The contract matrix records every exit each path produced and fails on an undeclared one.
- **M4-D6, an env-var registry held complete by a scan.** `ENV_VARS` with kinds `release`, `debug` and `harness`; a source scan fails on an unregistered name, and `harness` names appear only in test code. Capabilities publishes the `release` ones only.
- **M4-D9, schemas with the serialize contract.** `SchemaSettings::draft2020_12().for_serialize()`, a fresh generator per command and event (stable `$defs`), validated against live envelopes in the contract suite (snapshots are redacted). The validator is the `jsonschema` dev-dependency with default features off and an exact version; `boon` is the fallback if `cargo deny` refuses it. Rejected: one generator for everything, validating snapshots only, a hand-written validator, `serde_json/preserve_order`.
- **M4-D10, typed `details`.** Each error code carries a `DetailSpec`, a recursive description of its `details` (keys, value types, nesting, required or optional, nullable, closed enums such as `reason` and `changed`). Emitters keep building `serde_json::Value`; the spec is the contract, published as JSON Schema and validated against every observed `details`. Rejected: free-form details after the freeze, a struct per code now, a key list (it misses every type change).
- **M4-D11, enumerable actions and events.** `CommandHint::new` takes an `Action` enum with `wire()`, `description()` and `destructive()`; event names, `Phase` and `LogLevel` gain `ALL` and `wire()`. Rejected: a scan for literals, which freezes a convention instead of making it impossible to break.
- **M4-D16, static completions.** `clap_complete` for bash, zsh, fish, elvish and powershell, generated in memory (commands never print); `--json` gives `{shell, script}`. Rejected: dynamic completion of client ids and addon names (unstable, and every Tab would run discovery).
- **M4-D17, three verbosity levels.** Level 0 is token-frugal, level 1 (`-v`) is exactly today's behaviour, level 2 (`-vv`) adds `trace` log events on stderr only. Rejected: moving debug logs to `-vv`, a silent change for scripts that use `-v`.
- **M4-D55, the contract's rules hold from slice 1.** Six rules: timestamps (`_at`, RFC 3339 UTC; durations with unit suffixes), null versus omitted (always present, `null` when empty; omission only for `-v` additions), names (snake case, plural arrays, `id` and `key`), enumerations (snake case, closed sets), command names (the envelope `command` is the canonical clap path) and `details` (every observed `details` validates against its spec). A1 fixes rule 5 (`auth github`); A3's rule test enforces rules 1–4 and 6 from slice 1, with today's violations on a shrink-only allowlist; a known pre-release inconsistency is fixed by the leaf that owns the surface, widget and snapshots in the same commit; H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, the pre-freeze contract audit) is the final audit. Rejected: freezing as is; one late breaking window.
- **M4-D56, a semantic manifest pins the contract (owner-visible).** The manifest records outputs (type, integer versus number, required, nullable, bounds, enums, tagged variants), inputs (paths, flags, defaults, grammars, arity, conflicts, requirements, exits, binding, plan storage), registries and persisted formats, as canonical JSON; a readable names projection sits beside it. The classifier labels each change additive, breaking or unclassified, in the right direction for outputs and for inputs; unclassified counts as breaking; persisted formats follow their own kind-version rules; member order is not contract. A10 builds the manifest and the classifier; H2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.2`, the golden and the released-baseline mechanism) adds the golden and the released-baseline comparison; H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the M4 checkpoint and the first tag) writes the first baseline. Rejected: insta snapshots of schemas (noisy, no bump rule); a names-only type alphabet (loses requiredness, integer versus number and variants); one file as both snapshot and baseline (it erases its own evidence).
- **M4-D18 (context), determinism per command path.** Volatile keys are declared in `contract::VOLATILE`; H3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3`, the determinism audit) enforces it over every `COMMANDS` path, which A1 makes complete.

### How this area connects to the others

- **Area B** (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2`, the guide and the skill): the guide's generated blocks render A1's command facts, A2's env-var and action tables and A9's meanings; B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`, the guide renderer and `robot-docs guide`) adds `guide` to the `robot-docs` tree that A5 creates, and is blocked by A2, A5 and A9. A6 waits for B1.
- **Area C** (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3`, intent inference): C2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.2`, a client named as an addon and `-t all`) adds `all` to the target-id forms that A2's `target_id_forms()` reads; C4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4`, the run-the-fix corpus) receives corpus rows for this area's new commands (common rule 18).
- **Area D** (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4`, previews and stored plans): A1's `stores_plan` field is set by D4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`, the plan store) for the eleven storable commands; D1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1`, `precondition::of_plan` and the approval witness) supplies the execution `build_id` capabilities publishes; D5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`, `omaddons apply`) builds `apply`'s wrapper-variant schema and proves it with A3's strict validation.
- **Area E** (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5`, the doctor core): E1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`, the failure-mode registry) feeds capabilities' failure-mode summary and blocks A4; E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, `doctor diagnose`) adds the doctor rows with A1's `Doctor` dictionary, the doctor exit dictionary that capabilities and `robot-docs errors` publish, and the `doctor` command A6's line names; E4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4`, `doctor health`, `ls`, `--robot-triage`, `capabilities` and `robot-docs`) builds `doctor capabilities` on the same registry.
- **Area H** (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8`, freeze and close): H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, the pre-freeze audit) waits for A4, A5, A6, A7 and A8, empties A3's allowlist and turns A3's unobserved-`details` report into an assertion; H2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.2`, the golden and the released baseline) waits for A10; H3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3`, the determinism audit) walks A1's `COMMANDS`; H4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`, README's final pass) waits for A6, A7 and A8.
- **Area T** (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9`, test infrastructure, added at filing): T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs) blocks every bead of this area that writes an integration or end-to-end test; T2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.2`, slice 1 end to end) waits for A1–A5 and A7–A10 and records the slice-1 demo.
- **Area G** (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7`, the widget and durability): the widget's `CLI_PATHS` table gains a row for each command this area adds, and A1 moves `auth` to `auth github` there.

**How the leaves are worked:** each leaf with subtasks is worked through them (claim a ready subtask with `br ready --parent <leaf id>`, never the leaf; the agent that closes a leaf's last subtask verifies the leaf's acceptance criteria and closes the leaf), and a leaf filed without subtasks, such as A8, is claimed and closed itself.

## Goals

- **A1** `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1` (Per-command facts in `COMMANDS`, and canonical names, size-M, slice-1): gives every `COMMANDS` row the five facts `dictionary`, `exits`, `data`, `stores_plan` and `network`, checked by the static exit rules and by the exits the contract matrix observes, and gives every parsed command one canonical path, making `auth github` a real clap subcommand so the clap path, `COMMANDS` and the envelope agree. Every surface that describes commands reads these facts, so it lands before any command leaf adds a row.
- **A2** `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.2` (Registries for actions, events, env vars, features and per-source facts, size-M, slice-1): replaces scattered literals with enumerable registries: the `Action` enum that `CommandHint::new` takes, the NDJSON event types with `Phase::ALL`, `LogLevel::ALL` and `EventName::ALL`, `ENV_VARS` held complete by source scans, the stable feature words, `requires_credential` and `net::allowlist::hosts_for` per source, and `contract::target_id_forms()`. It changes no output byte; capabilities, the schemas and the guide's tables list these registries.
- **A3** `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3` (Schemas with the serialize contract, declared `details`, and live validation, size-L, slice-1): builds a draft 2020-12 schema for every command's `data`, the envelope, the error union discriminated by `code`, the events and the persisted files; adds the `jsonschema` dev-dependency and validates every live envelope, stderr event and envelope snapshot strictly in tests; and starts M4-D55's rule test with its shrink-only allowlist. It is the invariant that makes every published schema true, and the base of `robot-docs schema`, capabilities' `details_schema` and the manifest.
- **A4** `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4` (`omaddons capabilities`, size-M, slice-1): the agent's first call, one offline, scan-free and write-free description of every command, flag, alias, exit, error and warning code, action, env var, limit, source, family, rules row, `-t` form and the failure-mode summary, generated from the live clap tree and the registries in under 20 ms, and answering with `config_error` when `config.toml` is broken. It is checkpoint criterion 1.
- **A5** `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5` (`robot-docs schema` and `robot-docs errors`, size-S, slice-1): creates the `robot-docs` command tree with `schema [<command>]` (A3's schemas as `{envelope, events, commands, files}`) and `errors` (every error and warning code with meaning, exit, retryability, typed `details` and a fix pattern), deterministic byte for byte. ### Coordination rules between this area's leaves

The leaf beads decided these where two leaves without an edge between them touch the same thing. Each rule is in the beads that decided it; it is collected here so it is visible at the area level, and a leaf that finds its partner's bead silent on the rule follows it as written here.

- **`src/contract/` does not exist at `c0ab5e9`.** The first leaf that needs it creates `src/contract/mod.rs` (in practice one of A2's subtasks, which are roots). `src/contract/commands.rs` (`CommandInfo`, `Registry` with `builtin()`) is created by whichever of A4 and A10 lands first, exactly as A4's bead specifies; the other builds on it. The manifest is built from `Registry::builtin()` and never reads config-derived fields.
- **Three-valued retryability** (`ErrorCode::retryability()` returning `Retryability { Fixed(bool), Conditional(…) }`, with five conditional codes: `plan_stale`, `http_status`, `hash_mismatch`, `network` and `io`) is added by whichever of A4 and A5 lands first, held by A5's scan of `.retryable(…)` call sites; A10 reads it and adds no third definition.
- **Keys whose producer is outside the area** are published by whichever of the two leaves lands second, and the one that lands first leaves a comment on the other bead handing the duty over:
  - capabilities' `build_id` (D1) and `guide_digest` (B1) are absent until their producer has landed;
  - capabilities' `exit_codes.doctor` and `error_codes[].doctor_exit` are always present, `[]` and `null` until E3's doctor dictionary exists;
  - `robot-docs errors` leaves `doctor_exit` out of its rows until E3's dictionary exists (A5's bead). The two beads hold the place differently (present and `null` in capabilities, absent in `robot-docs errors`); whichever of them and E3 lands second makes the key real.
- **Actions and feature words.** A2 registers the actions that exist at `c0ab5e9`; their descriptions are A2's, and A9's one-sentence check over `Action::ALL` is run by whichever of A2 and A9 lands second. `FEATURES` holds only words whose surface exists; A7 adds `completions`.
- **Codes added later.** A9 writes meanings and specs for the 41 error and 52 warning codes present when it lands; E3 writes those of `online_required` and `doctor_refused` (43 error codes at the tag), and D4, C2 and F2, which add the three new warnings, write their meanings (55 warning codes at the tag), whichever of A9 and each of them lands second.
- **`OMADDONS_TEST_LOG`** is registered in `ENV_VARS` as `harness` by whichever of A2 and T1 lands second.

### Collision hot spots

| File | Leaves of this area (others) | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| `src/app/mod.rs` (`COMMANDS`, `command_name`, dispatch) | A1, A4, A5, A7 (B1, B3, D5, D9, E3, E4, E6, E7, E8) | **A1 first**, because it adds fields to every row; each command leaf adds its own rows afterwards and rebases |
| `src/error.rs` (code rows, meanings, specs, retryability) | A9, A3, A4 or A5 (D4, D5, E3, E10, the F leaves, H1) | **A9, then A3**, both touching every row; the retryability change (A4 or A5) and A5's fix patterns land after A9 and A3, which both wait for; later leaves append rows with their specs and meanings |
| `src/cli.rs` | A1 (`auth github`), A7 (one `Command` variant), A8 (C1, C2, D5, E3) | A1's subcommand first; keep each hook in its own function; C1's hooks before D5's `Context` fields. The plan's table omits A7, which adds one variant there |
| `src/output/stderr.rs`, `envelope.rs`, `mod.rs` | A2 (event structs to module scope), A3 (`JsonSchema` on `Envelope` and `Meta`), A8 (`LogLevel::Trace`) (E3) | additive changes in separate items; rebase before the gate |
| `src/resolve/cache.rs`, `src/discover/`, `src/fsx/lock.rs` | A8 (one trace call each) (D5's `force_revalidate`; the fsx leaves) | one-line additive calls; the plan's table lists `src/resolve/cache.rs` for D5 alone, so rebase over D5 rather than editing around it |
| `tests/contract/` (`main.rs`'s `support::check`, `matrix.rs`, snapshots) | A1 (exit observation, `auth github` rows), A3 (validation), A4, A5, A7 (rows) (every command leaf; E3, H2) | append rows, one snapshot file per row; A1 before A3 by edge |
| `tests/contract/rules_allowlist.txt` | A3 creates it (H1 empties it) | only ever remove lines; no leaf adds one |
| `omarchy/Model.js` `CLI_PATHS` | A1 (`auth` → `auth github`), A4, A5, A7 (rows) (G1, G2) | command leaves add or move only their `CLI_PATHS` rows |
| `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` | every leaf that lands after B1 and changes what the guide's generated blocks show (a command, a code, an action, an env var): A4 and A7 add a command; A6 and A8 run `cargo test --test skill` and regenerate only if it reports a difference | regenerate with `OMADDONS_UPDATE_SKILL=1 cargo test --test skill` after rebasing, never merge by hand (common rule 17) |
| `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, `deny.toml` | A3 (`jsonschema`, dev), A7 (`clap_complete`) | each runs `argc gate --all` in its own commit |
| `README.md` | every user-visible leaf (H4 reconciles) | edit only your own section |

Claim with the file list (`br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`), keep commits small, rebase before each gate run, coordinate through `SendMessage` and `ListAgents`, and treat unrecognized working-tree changes as a peer's work.

### Design gates

None of the milestone's ten design-gate leaves is in this area: area A adds no journal shape, recovery rule, binding rule, deletion rule or durability rule. Its correctness proofs are of another kind:

- A3's strict validation of every live envelope, event and envelope snapshot, and the transform's own composition tests (a `$ref` used two ways, a map, an internally tagged enum, a flattened struct, `oneOf` with shared fields);
- the cross-checks of every declared fact against behaviour (observed exits ⊆ declared, the env-var scan, registry completeness, `robot-docs errors` equal to `ErrorCode::ALL` and `WarningCode::ALL`);
- for the freeze, A10's classifier over synthetic manifests, then H2's updater tests against a synthetic released baseline, then H6's first baseline.

### Slices and demos

- **Slice share.** `slice-1` ("Self-describing"): A1, A2, A3, A4, A5, A7, A8, A9 and A10, nine of the slice's 17 leaves. `slice-4` ("Freeze and close"): A6, one of nine.
- **Slice 1's demo** items fed by this area: "`capabilities --json` round-trips" (A4, on A1, A2 and A9); "`robot-docs schema` validates the whole matrix and every envelope snapshot, `details` included" (A3, A5, A9); "the manifest's report prints" (A10); "`completions bash` passes `bash -n`" (A7). The other items (the guide equals `SKILL.md`, `install-skill`, the misplaced-client fixes and the corpus) are areas B's and C's. Slice 1 pre-checks criteria 1, 2, 3 (part), 5 and 15.
- **Who records it.** T2 runs the slice-1 demo as a test (`tests/e2e_slice1.rs`), calling the owning leaves' own helpers, and records the comment "**Slice demo 1. Self-describing**" on the milestone epic. No leaf of this area records a demo itself. A demo item that fails is a defect in the owning leaf: reopen it, or file a bug `discovered-from` T2 and block T2 on it.
- **Slice 4's demo** (recorded by H6 after the tag) includes "the audit's change list and the empty allowlist" (A3's allowlist, emptied by H1) and "the golden and the updater tests" (A10's manifest and classifier, through H2). A6's `discovery[]` is one of the shapes H1 audits.

### Risks

- **Risk 2, live validation finds many schema and output mismatches and A3 balloons** (likelihood M, impact M). Each mismatch is a real bug, fixed in A3 and listed in its close comment. If A3 passes twice its size, the remainder is filed as bugs `discovered-from` A3 and gated before H1 (each added as H1's blocker), so A3 can close with its invariant in place.
- **Risk 15, `jsonschema` violates `deny.toml`** by pulling `reqwest` or a TLS backend (L, L). Default features off, an exact version, both `cargo tree -i` checks recorded, `argc gate --all`; the fallback is `boon`, recorded as `decided:`.
- **Risk 22, the compatibility classifier mislabels a change**, passing a breaking change as additive (L, H). Conservative default (an unclassified change is breaking), unit cases per direction rule, H2's updater tests against a synthetic baseline, and H1's final walk. Confidence in A10 is medium for this reason; capabilities, `robot-docs`, schemas, completions and verbosity are high-confidence work on existing seams.
- **Risk 5, a contract correction breaks the widget or scripts** (M, M; H1 owns the risk for the audit). In this area, A1's `auth github` correction and A3's cheap allowlist fixes change surfaces the widget reads; the widget's `CLI_PATHS` and the snapshots move in the same commit, and each change is listed with a compatibility note.
- **Risk 14, the milestone is large** (M, M). This area's 2-unit chain and its T1 dependency are why A9, A1 and A2 are claimed first.
- **Where the plan and the code disagree.** The leaf beads record each place the plan was wrong against `c0ab5e9` and how the implementer adapts. Examples that span leaves: the plan's 31 actions are 22 in the code (A2); ULID ids carry a schema `pattern` that redacted snapshots fail, which A3 adapts for; clap 4.6.7 has no public getter for an argument's `requires`, so A4 and A10 declare requirements beside the command; `src/contract/commands.rs` has no edge between its two users (A4, A10), hence the creation rule above. Read the leaf's "Facts this bead relies on" before starting.

### Two new crates

M4 adds exactly two crates, both in this area: `clap_complete` as a runtime dependency (A7, pinned to the version matching clap 4.6.x) and `jsonschema` as a dev-dependency with default features off (A3, fallback `boon`). Each leaf runs `argc gate --all` (cargo deny) and records the result in its close comment.

title: Per-command facts in `COMMANDS`, and canonical names
description:
## How to work this bead

This bead is worked through its 3 subtasks, listed below in work order. Claim a subtask, not this bead (`br ready --parent omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1` lists the ready ones). The agent that closes the last open subtask then verifies every acceptance criterion of this bead (they are the leaf's, not any one subtask's), and closes this bead with `br close omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1 --reason "done: <evidence> · found: <ids>"`. Until this bead is closed, every bead it blocks stays blocked.

1. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1.1 `auth github` as a real subcommand, and one canonical path per parsed command: the clap restructure with every argv unchanged, `app::canonical_path`, the clap-path bijection test, the `auth` row and the widget's `CLI_PATHS` row renamed to `auth github`, and the contract suite's check that every envelope names its canonical path.
2. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1.2 The five per-command facts on every `COMMANDS` row, held by their static rules and the contract matrix: `dictionary`, `exits`, `data`, `stores_plan` and `network` on all 42 rows, the static exit rules, the two envelope names that are no clap path, and the contract suite's exit observation.
3. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1.3 E2E: every `auth` spelling and every bare parent answers under its canonical name: two `TestLog` scenarios that prove the names, the declared exits and the unchanged argv end to end.

Order: subtask 1 first, because it lands the `src/cli.rs` change that the other root leaves editing that file (A8, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.8`, verbosity levels; C1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.1`, misplaced clients) rebase on, and it renames the one row that subtask 2 then fills. Subtask 2 follows on the same `COMMANDS` table. Subtask 3 needs both, and the `TestLog` of T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs).

## Background

### What this is for

omaddons M4 makes the CLI describe itself: `capabilities --json` (A4, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`), the per-command JSON Schemas (A3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`), the semantic contract manifest that freezes the contract at the first tag (A10, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.10`), the plan store's set of storable commands (D4, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`) and the determinism audit's coverage test (H3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3`) are all generated from one registry (M4-D2). Several facts those surfaces need about each command are facts clap cannot provide:

- which exit codes the command can return, and from which exit dictionary (the general one, or the doctor's that E3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, adds);
- the JSON Schema of its `data`;
- whether its dry run stores a plan (D4);
- whether it uses the network.

At `c0ab5e9` these facts live nowhere, or only implicitly in `run_command`'s match. This bead declares each of them exactly once, beside the command, in the `app::COMMANDS` table that help, usage fixes and the widget already read, and adds the tests that keep the declarations honest.

It also fixes the canonical command paths before any surface is generated from them (M4-D55 rule 5). One command breaks the rule today: `auth` is not a subcommand tree but a command taking the positional value `github`, so `COMMANDS` and the widget's `CLI_PATHS` say `auth` while its envelope says `auth github`. Fixed here, the mistake is never copied into the guide, the capabilities output, the schemas, the manifest, the snapshots or the intent corpus.

Everything that describes commands starts here: this bead is a root of the M4 graph, at the head of lane 6 (t = 0–2), and seven leaves wait for it.

### Goals served

- **G-M4-1 Self-describing:** an agent with no prior knowledge learns everything it needs from the binary itself, in at most three calls; every fact in those outputs is generated from the code, so it cannot drift; every command's output has a published JSON Schema that the contract suite validates real output against. The rows of this bead are the source of `capabilities.commands[]`'s `dictionary`, `exit_codes`, `stores_plan` and `network`, and of each command's schema function.
- **G-M4-5 Frozen and enforced:** at the first tag the contract is complete (a semantic manifest of every input the CLI accepts and every output it emits) and every exit site maps to a published code in the right dictionary. A10's manifest joins the clap tree with these rows (paths, declared exits, exit dictionary, plan storage); the declared exits are what capabilities publishes per command.
- **G-M4-2 The first guess works:** a plausible wrong invocation yields a usage error whose fix is the command the user meant, and a fix never turns the user's verb into a different command that changes something. The M2-decided fix for a mistyped service (`omaddons auth gihub` → `omaddons auth github`) survives the restructure.

Vision goal G4, agent ergonomics ("the first command an agent guesses works"): after this bead a command has one name, the same in its argv, in help, in the registry, in the widget and in its envelope.

### Checkpoint criteria this bead feeds

- **1, Capabilities:** `omaddons capabilities --json` carries `commands` (each entry with `exit_codes`, `dictionary`, `stores_plan`, `binds`, `network`) and round-trips: every command entry, every flag of it and every alias parses. A4 builds that list from these rows.
- **2, Schemas:** `omaddons robot-docs schema` gives a JSON Schema for every command path in `app::COMMANDS`, and the contract suite validates the `data` of every live envelope against its command's schema. A3 builds each schema from the row's `data` function.
- **14, The contract is frozen:** the golden is a semantic manifest of the CLI's paths, flags, positionals, defaults, value grammars and exits, plus every output. A10 reads paths and facts from these rows.

### The decisions that shape it

- **M4-D2, one contract registry feeds every description of the CLI.** A new `src/contract/` module assembles a `Registry` from the live clap tree, `app::COMMANDS` extended with per-command facts, the error, warning and exit registries and the other registries; `capabilities`, `robot-docs`, the golden, bare help's discovery line and `doctor capabilities` all read it. A fact clap cannot provide is declared exactly once, beside the command it describes, and a test cross-checks it against behaviour (whether a command mutates, its exit codes, the schema of its data, whether it stores a plan). Why: the vision's rule that `capabilities` is "generated from the live clap tree and the registries, never maintained by hand" only works if the registries exist. Rejected: a hand-written `capabilities.json` (it drifts, the failure capabilities exists to prevent); deriving every fact from runtime behaviour, for example exits observed by tests (a command's exits are a promise and need a declaration, which tests then verify); proc-macro attributes on the clap structs (a new dependency and compile time for no gain over a table).
- **M4-D5, per-command exit codes are declared beside the command and verified.** `CommandEntry` gains five fields: `dictionary` (`General` or `Doctor`), `exits: &'static [u8]`, `data` (a `fn(&mut SchemaGenerator) -> Schema`), `stores_plan: bool` and `network` (`None`, `Optional` or `Required`). Static rules check the declarations: a command with `--check` or `--strict` lists 6; a mutating command lists 5; every general command lists 0, 1 and 2. The contract suite records every exit code each command path produced across the matrix and fails if one is not declared. The doctor tree declares the doctor dictionary. Why: clap knows nothing about exits, so the vision's "each command's capabilities entry lists the exit codes it can return" needs a declaration, and the cross-check makes it honest. Rejected: deriving exits from the error codes a command can raise (not statically knowable without whole-program analysis); every command declaring all of 0–6 (true, but useless to an agent). Do not be tempted by the second: declare what a command can return, nothing more.
- **M4-D55, the contract's rules hold from slice 1.** Six rules govern every shape; rule 5 is this bead's: **the envelope `command` equals the canonical clap path.** `auth github` versus `auth` is resolved here: `github` becomes a real clap subcommand of `auth`, so the clap path, `COMMANDS` and the envelope all say `auth github`; the argv users type (`auth github`, `auth github set`, `auth github clear`, `auth github --from-gh`) is unchanged. A known pre-release inconsistency is fixed by the leaf that owns the surface, with a compatibility note in its close comment and the widget, guide and snapshot changes in the same commit. Why: after the tag every such fix costs a major `schema_version` bump (M4-D56); before it, a commit and a widget update, and less the earlier it lands. Rejected: freezing as is (it would freeze `auth`'s path mismatch); one late breaking-change window in H1 (it propagates known mistakes through every consumer). H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, the pre-freeze audit) only confirms this correction.
- **M4-D22 (context for `stores_plan`).** The dry runs of eleven commands will store a plan: `install`, `update`, `pin`, `unpin`, `adopt` (when it adopts), `sync`, `copy`, `remove`, `undo`, `backup restore`, `backup prune`. D4 sets `stores_plan: true` on those rows; this bead declares `false` everywhere.
- **`binds` is not a field** (§6.2.1): whether a command binds with `--if-match` stays derived from `app::precondition::BINDING_COMMANDS` (`src/app/precondition.rs:25-31`), the single list. Do not add a `binds` column.
- **M4-D40 (context for `dictionary`).** The doctor tree gets its own exit dictionary (`0 healthy` … `74 io_error`), added by E3 with the doctor's rows. This bead adds the `Dictionary::Doctor` variant so E3's rows can declare it; no row uses it yet.
- **DEC-1, no stubs (context).** From this bead on, every command leaf adds its `COMMANDS` row with every M4 field in the commit that adds its clap variant (common rule 4.2). This bead adds no command; it changes one command's path, and every touch point of that path changes in one subtask (subtask 1).

### Facts this bead relies on (verified at `c0ab5e9`)

- `app::COMMANDS` (`src/app/mod.rs:121-165`) holds 42 rows of `CommandEntry { name, group, mutates }` (`:99-108`), built by `const fn entry` (`:110-116`). `CommandEntry` derives `Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq` (`:100`); nothing compares two entries (every reader matches on `.name`, `.group` or `.mutates`).
- The only command → outcome mapping is `run_command`'s match (`src/app/mod.rs:374-587`). Every `Outcome` type is `pub`; `targets` and `config` use a generic `Done<D>` (`src/app/targets.rs:179-187`, `src/app/config.rs:106-114`).
- `command_name(Option<&Command>)` (`src/app/mod.rs:195-237`) gives the envelope name of a parsed invocation; bare `omaddons` is `help`, bare `backup` is `backup list`, bare `omarchy` is `omarchy status`, and `Command::Auth` is `"auth github"` (`:231`) while the row says `auth` (`:159`).
- `canonical(name)` (`:177-183`) maps a path string to its row's static name, else `"omaddons"`; `cli::command_of` (`src/cli.rs:461-467`) uses it for the envelope of a usage error whose argv did not parse. `group_of(name)` (`:186-192`) places bare help's top-level names (`src/app/help.rs:203`). `mutates(path)` (`:169-174`) counts an unknown path as mutating.
- On success the envelope's `command` is the outcome's own `Outcome::command()` (`src/output/mod.rs:133-151`); on failure it is the name dispatch passed (`:249`, `:272`). The two are written separately, and no test compares them for every command (a few matrix rows and the alias tests check single names).
- `auth` (`src/app/auth.rs:36-61`): `AuthArgs { service: AuthService (value enum, only github), action: Option<AuthAction> (status, set, clear), from_gh: bool }`; `AuthOutcome::command()` is `"auth github"` (`:97-99`); `Command::Auth` (`src/cli.rs:208-210`) carries `after_long_help = AUTH_HELP` (`src/cli.rs:547-557`).
- Help resolves a positional value as a path word (`src/app/help.rs:253-321`), which is how `help auth github` showed `auth`'s help (test `src/app/help.rs:538-594`; `tests/cli_skeleton.rs:263-299`).
- `value_fix` (`src/cli.rs:892-938`) special-cases `auth`'s ACTION (`:904`): a mistyped `set`/`clear` gets the help of the path, `show` means `status`. `subcommand_fix` (`src/cli.rs:849-890`) suggests the help of any mutating guess (`:876-885`).
- The M2-decided fix of `auth gihub` is `omaddons auth github` (`tests/contract/usage_fixes.rs:150`), produced today by `value_fix` correcting the SERVICE value in place.
- The widget's `CLI_PATHS` (`omarchy/Model.js:133-178`, row `"auth"` at `:171`) is held equal to `COMMANDS` by `tests/omarchy_widget.rs:30-51`.
- `help.rs`'s `every_subcommand_has_exactly_one_registry_entry` (`src/app/help.rs:479-516`) checks top-level names only.

- The plan does not mention the two envelope names that are no clap path (`version`, `omaddons`), nor the two readers that break when the `auth` row goes (`group_of` for bare help, `canonical` for usage-error envelopes), nor that the decided `auth gihub` fix would turn into a help fix once `github` is a subcommand, nor clap derive's implicit `arg_required_else_help`. Each is handled below.

### How it serves the vision

omaddons stays the sole, safe, undoable authority over what it manages only if what it says about itself is true. This bead makes the per-command promises (exits, schema, network, plan storage) declarations that tests hold against behaviour, and it makes a command's name one thing everywhere, so an agent that learns a path from `capabilities` can type it, find it in help, and match it in the envelope.

#### 2.1 Types

In `src/app/mod.rs`, beside `Group`:

```rust
/// Which exit dictionary a command's process exit comes from (M4-D5, M4-D40).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, JsonSchema)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum Dictionary { General, Doctor }   // ALL: [General, Doctor]

/// Whether a command uses the network.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, JsonSchema)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum Network {
    /// No path of the command sends a request (it may read the release memo).
    None,
    /// Some path may send a request (a release, an archive, a listing, the rate limit);
    /// under --offline the command still does its local work, from caches, or refuses
    /// only what needs the network.
    Optional,
    /// Its purpose is an upstream answer (search, outdated): it asks by default, and
    /// offline it answers only from what is remembered, marking the rest unchecked.
    Required,
}   // ALL: [None, Optional, Required]

/// A command path this build has, with every fact clap cannot provide (M4-D2, M4-D5).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct CommandEntry {
    pub name: &'static str,            // canonical path, = envelope `command`
    pub group: Group,
    pub mutates: bool,
    pub dictionary: Dictionary,        // General | Doctor
    pub exits: &'static [u8],          // ascending; declared, verified by the matrix
    pub data: fn(&mut schemars::SchemaGenerator) -> schemars::Schema,  // its Outcome::Data
    pub stores_plan: bool,             // M4-D22; false until D4
    pub network: Network,
}

/// The schema of `O`'s data: a row's `data`, naming the outcome its dispatch arm returns.
pub fn data_schema<O: crate::output::Outcome>(g: &mut schemars::SchemaGenerator) -> schemars::Schema {
    g.root_schema_for::<O::Data>()
}
```

- `PartialEq, Eq` are dropped from `CommandEntry`: comparing function pointers is unreliable (rustc's `unpredictable_function_pointer_comparisons`), and nothing compares entries. Never glob-import `Network::*` (its `None` would shadow `Option::None`).
- Rows are built with `const fn entry(name, group, mutates, exits, data, network) -> CommandEntry`, which sets `dictionary: Dictionary::General` and `stores_plan: false`, plus two `const fn` modifiers for later leaves: `doctor(self)` (E3's rows) and `storing_plan(self)` (D4's eleven). Six arguments stay under clippy's `too_many_arguments` limit of seven, and the defaults are honest: every command at `c0ab5e9` uses the general dictionary and stores no plan.
- `data` names the `Outcome` type the row's dispatch arm returns (`data_schema::<install::InstallOutcome>`), not its data type, because several outcomes share one data type (`TargetsData`) and the outcome is what `run_command` returns. That keeps the command → type mapping in the one table (§6.2.1). A3 calls it with its own `SchemaSettings::draft2020_12().for_serialize()` generator and validates live output against it; this bead only declares it.
- These types derive `Serialize + JsonSchema` with snake_case values (`general`, `doctor`; `none`, `optional`, `required`) so A4 can publish them unchanged. Nothing in this bead serializes them.

#### 2.3 How each row's exits are derived

Declare an exit when some path of the command constructs a code of that exit, by reading the command's run path and the shared helpers it calls (`World::load`, `World::select*`, `World::records`, the engine, fsx):

- **0, 1, 2:** every general row (success; any runtime failure, `internal` included; any usage error).
- **3:** the command resolves a `-t` selector, an id, a ref, an addon name or a user-given file (`target_not_found`, `target_ambiguous`, `ref_ambiguous`, `not_found`, `not_managed`, `no_compatible_release`, `plan_not_found`).
- **4:** the command can refuse: every mutating row (fsx refuses any write outside its scope with `scope_denied`), and any row whose path loads a versioned state file (`state_too_new` from `store::load_bytes`), plus the specific refusals (`game_running`, `protected_folder`, `ownership_conflict`, `undo_conflict`, `file_exists`, `filesystem_unsupported`, the archive rules, `host_blocked`).
- **5:** every mutating row (static rule), and any read row that acquires the global lock (none known; check `GlobalLock::acquire`'s callers, `src/fsx/lock.rs:72`).
- **6:** exactly the rows whose clap command has `--check` or `--strict`.

Never declare an exit "to be safe": M4-D5 rejects declaring all of 0–6. The contract matrix catches an under-declared exit on every path it exercises (2.6); a path it does not exercise is caught by H3's coverage test later. Record in the close comment every row whose final exits differ from the floor above, with the construction site that justifies each added code.

#### 2.4 Network, as decided

- `Required`: `search`, `outdated` (the plan).
- `Optional`: `install`, `update`, `pin`, `unpin`, `adopt`, `sync`, `copy` (they resolve releases and download through the engine), `info` (the newest release), `auth github` (`status` makes one request to `/rate_limit`).
- `None`: every other row, including `remove`, `undo` and the backup commands, which run engine transactions but never send a request, and `status`, `list` and `errors`, which read the release memo and never fetch (`src/app/remembered.rs:1-2`).

#### 2.5 The envelope names that are no clap path

```rust
/// An envelope `command` that is no clap path: it never appears in help, in
/// capabilities' commands or in the widget's CLI_PATHS.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct EnvelopeOnly { pub name: &'static str, pub exits: &'static [u8],
                          pub data: fn(&mut schemars::SchemaGenerator) -> schemars::Schema, pub why: &'static str }

pub const ENVELOPE_ONLY: &[EnvelopeOnly] = &[
    // exits [1, 2]: a usage error before any subcommand, or a panic before parsing.
    EnvelopeOnly { name: "omaddons", exits: &[1, 2], data: data_schema::<help::HelpOutcome>, why: "no command could be read from the arguments" },
    // exits [0]: -V before any subcommand.
    EnvelopeOnly { name: "version", exits: &[0], data: data_schema::<help::HelpOutcome>, why: "--version" },
];
```

Both carry `HelpOutcome`'s schema: `version` emits `HelpData::Version`, and `omaddons` envelopes are errors rendered through `HelpOutcome` (`src/cli.rs:440-447`). The static rules apply to commands only, not to these two. A3 validates `version` envelopes through it; A4 and A10 decide whether to publish them.

- `pub fn command_entry(path: &str) -> Option<&'static CommandEntry>`.
- `pub fn declared_exits(name: &str) -> Option<&'static [u8]>`: a row's exits, else an `ENVELOPE_ONLY` name's, else `None`.

#### 2.7 The static rules, as a pure checker

`fn exit_rule_violations(entry: &CommandEntry, has_check_or_strict: bool) -> Vec<String>` (test module), so the rules are tested on planted entries as well as on the table:

1. `exits` is strictly ascending (sorted, no duplicates) and non-empty;
2. a `General` row: every code is a general exit (`Exit::ALL`), and 0, 1 and 2 are listed;
3. `mutates` ⇒ 4 and 5 are listed;

#### 2.8 The exit observation in the contract suite

In `tests/contract/main.rs`'s `support`:

```rust
/// Every (command, exit) the contract suite produced in this process.
static OBSERVED: Mutex<BTreeMap<String, BTreeSet<i32>>> = Mutex::new(BTreeMap::new());

/// Records `code` for `command`, and fails unless the command declares it.
pub fn observe_exit(command: &str, code: i32, ctx: &str)
/// A copy of the table, for logs.
pub fn observed() -> BTreeMap<String, BTreeSet<i32>>
```

`check` calls `observe_exit(envelope.command, code, ctx)` right after it verifies `ok`, `exit_code` and the registered exit. It fails when the name is neither a `COMMANDS` path nor an `ENVELOPE_ONLY` name ("envelope command \"auth\" is neither a COMMANDS path nor an ENVELOPE_ONLY name"), and when the exit is not declared ("help exited 4, which its COMMANDS row does not declare: declared [0, 1, 2], observed so far {…}; add the code to the row's exits if the command can return it"). It tolerates a poisoned lock (`PoisonError::into_inner`) and drops the guard before asserting. The assertion is inline because the contract tests run in parallel threads in no fixed order, so no test can run "after the matrix"; inline, every envelope of every contract test is checked whatever the order, which is strictly stronger. Every envelope the matrix, `special.rs`, `recommendations.rs` and `usage_fixes.rs` produce goes through `check`.

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M4 plan, 2026-10-24).**

**Why this bead.** M4 makes omaddons describe itself from its own code: `capabilities --json`, a JSON Schema per command, the semantic manifest that freezes the contract at the first tag, and the plan store's set of storable commands all read one registry. At `c0ab5e9` the registry's command table, `app::COMMANDS`, knows only each path's name, group and whether it mutates; which exits a command can return, which exit dictionary it uses, what its data looks like, whether it stores a plan and whether it touches the network live nowhere, or only in `run_command`'s match. And one path is wrong: `auth`'s registry row and the widget's `CLI_PATHS` say `auth` while its envelope says `auth github`. This bead declares each missing fact once, beside the command, with tests that hold it against behaviour, and makes every command's name one thing in its argv, help, the registry, the widget and its envelope, before anything is generated from those names. It is a root, at the head of lane 6 (t = 0–2), and seven leaves (A3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`; A4, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`; A7, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.7`; A10, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.10`; D4, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`; E3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`; H3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3`) plus the slice-1 suite T2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.2`) wait for it: everything that describes commands starts here.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M4-D2:** one contract registry; a fact clap cannot provide is declared exactly once beside the command and cross-checked by a test.
- **M4-D5:** `CommandEntry` gains `dictionary`, `exits`, `data`, `stores_plan` and `network`; static rules (general ⇒ 0, 1, 2; mutating ⇒ 5; `--check`/`--strict` ⇒ 6); the contract suite fails an exit that is not declared.
- **M4-D55 rule 5:** the envelope `command` is the canonical clap path; `github` becomes a real subcommand of `auth`, argv unchanged; the correction is recorded with a compatibility note and the widget changes in the same commit.
- **M4-D22 (context):** `stores_plan` is `false` everywhere until D4 marks the eleven storable commands.
- **M4-D40 (context):** the `Doctor` dictionary variant exists for E3's rows; no row uses it yet.
- **DEC-1 (context):** every command leaf after this one adds its row with all five fields.
- `binds` stays derived from `precondition::BINDING_COMMANDS`, the single list (§6.2.1).

**Alternatives rejected that matter here.**
- A hand-written `capabilities.json` (it drifts, the failure capabilities exists to prevent).
- Deriving exits from runtime observation alone: exits are a promise and need a declaration, which the matrix then verifies.
- Deriving exits from the error codes a command can raise: not statically knowable without whole-program analysis.
- Declaring all of 0–6 on every command: true, but useless to an agent.
- Proc-macro attributes on the clap structs: a dependency and compile time for no gain over a table.
- Leaving `auth` as it is until H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, the pre-freeze audit): the mismatch would be copied into capabilities, the schemas, the manifest, the guide, the snapshots and the corpus first; after the tag it would cost a major bump.
- Making `auth github set|clear|status` subcommands too: it would change the envelope's `command` of every `auth` run, which the plan keeps as `auth github`.
- Accepting `omaddons help auth github` as the fix of `auth gihub` (what a plain subcommand restructure gives): it would silently change a fix decided in M2.

**Facts verified while writing this bead (at `c0ab5e9`), and where the plan disagreed with the code.**
- `COMMANDS` has 42 rows (`src/app/mod.rs:121-165`); `command_name` says `auth github` (`:231`) while the row says `auth` (`:159`).
- `network`: the plan's "`Optional` for engine commands, `None` for the rest" does not match the code. `info`, `auth github` status and `adopt`'s report send requests; `remove` ("A remove fetches nothing", `src/app/remove.rs:246`), `undo` and the backup commands send none. The declarations follow the code.
- `errors` is a fifth parent whose bare form runs, besides the plan's `backup`, `targets`, `config` and `omarchy`.
- "A test run after the matrix" cannot be ordered (the contract tests run in parallel threads); the assertion runs inside `support::check` on every envelope.
- `version` (`-V`) and `omaddons` (no command readable) are envelope names that are no clap path; they are declared in `ENVELOPE_ONLY`.
- Removing the `auth` row would break bare help's placement (`group_of`, `src/app/help.rs:203`) and the usage-error envelope's name (`canonical`, `src/cli.rs:461-467`); both get a rule for a parent without a row.
- clap derive's implicit `arg_required_else_help(true)` for a required subcommand (`clap_derive` 4.6.7 `derives/args.rs:204-210`) would make bare `omaddons auth` print its help as an error; the bead overrides it.
- `CommandEntry` derives `PartialEq, Eq` (`src/app/mod.rs:100`), unreliable with a function-pointer field; nothing compares entries, so the derives go.

**Risks and how they are watched.** No risk in the plan's table is owned by this bead. Its own:
- An under-declared exit on a path no contract test exercises: the inline observation catches every exercised path; H3's coverage test (a success and a failure row per path) closes the rest.
- An over-declared exit: the derivation rules, and the close comment's list of rows whose exits differ from the evidence floor, reviewed.
- clap derive surprises in the restructure (the global `--from-gh`'s value, the bare-parent error): unit tests on every argv that parsed before and on bare `auth`.
- The widget breaking on the renamed row: `CLI_PATHS` changes in the same commit, held by `tests/omarchy_widget.rs` and the widget pipeline in the gate.

**What it unblocks, and why they wait.**
- A3 needs each row's `data` to build the command schemas it validates live output against.
- A4 publishes every field, and the canonical paths, in `capabilities.commands[]`.
- A7 adds the first new row, which needs the fields to exist.
- A10's manifest inputs join the clap tree with these rows.
- D4 marks the storable commands' rows and reads them.
- E3 adds the doctor rows and the doctor's exit rules.
- H3's coverage test walks these paths.
- T2's slice-1 demo reads every one of these facts.

**How it serves the milestone.** G-M4-1 (every fact in the self-description is generated from the code), G-M4-5 (every exit site maps to a published code in the right dictionary; the manifest records the CLI's canonical paths and exits) and G-M4-2 (the first guess under `auth` still lands on the command meant). It feeds checkpoint criteria 1, 2 and 14, and keeps the thesis honest: omaddons can stay the sole, safe, undoable authority over what it manages only if what it says about itself is true.

- **Type** task · **P1** · **size-M** · **slice-1**

Capabilities, the schema registry and the golden need each fact once (M4-D2, M4-D5). The canonical command-path rule (M4-D55 rule 5) is established here, before any surface is generated from the paths.
- **Technical approach.**
  1. Extend `CommandEntry` with `dictionary`, `exits`, `data: fn(&mut SchemaGenerator) -> Schema`, `stores_plan` and `network` (§6.2.1). Fill every existing row.
     - `exits`: from what each command can return today. The matrix check (step 4) verifies it.
     - `stores_plan`: `false` everywhere until D4 sets the eleven storable commands.
     - `network`: `Required` for `search`/`outdated`, `Optional` for engine commands, `None` for the rest.
  2. Add `Dictionary { General, Doctor }`, `Network { None, Optional, Required }`, and the static exit rules: `--check`/`--strict` ⇒ 6; `mutates` ⇒ 5; every general command ⇒ 0, 1, 2.
  3. **Canonical names.** One function, `app::canonical_path(&Command) -> &'static str`, used by `command_name`, the envelope and capabilities. It covers bare `backup` → `backup list` and bare `omarchy` → `omarchy status`.
  4. **`auth github` as a real subcommand** (M4-D55 rule 5, fixed here rather than in H1): `github` becomes a clap subcommand of `auth`, so the clap path, `COMMANDS` and the envelope all say `auth github`. The argv users type is unchanged. The close comment records it as a pre-release correction (the envelope's `command` was already `"auth github"`; `COMMANDS` said `auth`), and the widget's `CLI_PATHS` row and any snapshot move in the same commit.
  5. **Exit observation.** `tests/contract/support::check` records `(command, exit_code)` for every envelope into a per-process table. A test run after the matrix asserts every observed exit is declared.
  6. A test that every clap leaf path has exactly one `COMMANDS` row, and that every `COMMANDS` row names a real clap path, leaf or parent. `COMMANDS` also holds rows for parents that run as commands (`backup`, `targets`, `config`, `omarchy`), so a strict leaf-to-row bijection would be false. It replaces `help.rs:480-516`'s narrower check.
- **Acceptance criteria.**
  - Every row carries the five fields.
  - The static rules hold.
  - Observed exits ⊆ declared, over the whole contract matrix.
  - Every clap leaf has a row, and every row is a clap path; every envelope `command` equals its canonical path, `auth github` included.
  - No other behaviour or output changes (snapshots unchanged except `auth github`'s `COMMANDS`-derived ones).
- **Test plan.** Unit tests in `src/app/mod.rs` for the static rules and the path bijection. Contract: the exit-observation assertion; the `auth github` rows.
- **Considerations.** `data`'s schema function per row is verified by A3, which validates live output against it. A1 only declares it. Hot spot: `src/app/mod.rs`, `src/cli.rs` (the `auth` subcommand). Land A1 before any command leaf adds a row.
