title: `auth github` as a real subcommand, and one canonical path per parsed command
description:
Part 1 of 3 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1 (Per-command facts in `COMMANDS`, and canonical names). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

A1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1`) is the root of omaddons M4's contract registry. M4 generates every description of the CLI (`capabilities --json`, the per-command JSON Schemas, the semantic manifest that freezes the contract at the first tag) from one registry built on the clap tree and `app::COMMANDS` (M4-D2). Before anything is generated from command paths, the paths must be canonical: **M4-D55 rule 5 says the envelope `command` equals the canonical clap path**, and that the clap path, `COMMANDS` and the envelope all say the same thing.

One command breaks the rule at `c0ab5e9`. `auth` is not a subcommand tree: it takes positional value-enums `<SERVICE> [ACTION]` (`src/app/auth.rs:36-61`, SERVICE accepting only `github`), so `COMMANDS` (`src/app/mod.rs:159`) and the widget's `CLI_PATHS` (`omarchy/Model.js:171`) say `auth` while every `auth github` envelope says `auth github` (`src/app/mod.rs:231`, `src/app/auth.rs:97-99`). M4-D55 fixes this in A1 rather than in the final audit (H1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`): `github` becomes a real clap subcommand of `auth`, and the argv users type (`auth github`, `auth github set`, `auth github clear`, `auth github --from-gh`) is unchanged. A known pre-release inconsistency is corrected by the leaf that owns the surface, with a compatibility note in its close comment and the widget and snapshot changes in the same commit, because after the tag such a fix costs a major `schema_version` bump (M4-D56) and before it a commit. Rejected: freezing as is (it would freeze `auth`'s path mismatch), and one late breaking-change window in H1 (it copies the mistake into the guide, the widget, the snapshots and the corpus first).

This subtask does all of the path work: the clap restructure, one function that names every parsed command (`app::canonical_path`), the readers that the restructure would otherwise break, the usage fixes under `auth`, the renamed `COMMANDS` and `CLI_PATHS` rows, a test that every clap path and every row correspond, and a contract-suite check that every envelope's `command` is its canonical path. It is its own step, and the first, because:

- it lands the `src/cli.rs` change that other root leaves editing that file (A8, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.8`; C1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.1`) rebase on (hot-spot rule: "A1's subcommand first");
- it renames the one row that subtask 2 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1.2) then fills with the five new facts;
- every touch point of a command path (DEC-1: clap variant, `COMMANDS` row, `command_name` arm, help layout, contract rows, `cli_skeleton` literals, `CLI_PATHS` row, README section) must change in one commit.

Goals served: G-M4-1 (self-describing: every fact generated from the code, so a command's name cannot drift between its argv, help, the registry and the envelope), G-M4-2 (the first guess works: the M2-decided fix for a mistyped service survives), and checkpoint criterion 14 (the frozen manifest records the CLI's canonical paths).

**Facts this subtask relies on (verified at `c0ab5e9`):**

- `command_name(Option<&Command>)` (`src/app/mod.rs:195-237`) names a parsed invocation: bare `omaddons` is `help`, bare `backup` is `backup list`, bare `omarchy` is `omarchy status`, bare `targets`, `config` and `errors` are themselves, nested actions use their `command()` helpers (`BackupAction::command`, `src/app/backup.rs:100`; `TargetsAction::command`, `src/app/targets.rs:75`; `ConfigAction::command`, `src/app/config.rs:52`; `OmarchyAction::command`, `src/app/omarchy.rs:49`).
- `canonical(name)` (`src/app/mod.rs:177-183`) maps a path string to its row's name, else `"omaddons"`; `cli::command_of` (`src/cli.rs:461-467`) uses it to name the envelope of a usage error whose argv did not parse. `group_of(name)` (`src/app/mod.rs:186-192`) gives bare help its group and order (`src/app/help.rs:203`). `mutates(path)` (`src/app/mod.rs:169-174`) counts an unknown path as mutating.
- On success, the envelope's `command` is the outcome's own `Outcome::command()` literal (`src/output/mod.rs:133-151`); on failure, the name dispatch passed (`src/output/mod.rs:249`, `:272`). No test compares the two for every command (a few matrix rows and the alias tests check single names).
- `Command::Auth` (`src/cli.rs:208-210`) has the about "Store, check or clear the opt-in GitHub token (5,000 REST requests an hour)", which bare help's JSON lists (snapshot `tests/snapshots/cli_skeleton__bare_help_json.snap`), and `after_long_help = AUTH_HELP` (`src/cli.rs:547-557`).
- `help::for_command` (`src/app/help.rs:249-349`) walks subcommands, then possible values of the next positional, which is how `help auth github` showed `auth`'s help (`src/app/help.rs:538-594`, `tests/cli_skeleton.rs:263-299`). Help's `data.command` is clap's leaf name for nested commands (`help targets add` gives `"add"`, `tests/cli_skeleton.rs:235-240`).
- `subcommand_fix` (`src/cli.rs:849-890`) offers the help of any mutating guess (`:876-885`); `value_fix` (`src/cli.rs:892-938`) corrects a value in place except `auth`'s ACTION (`:904`), whose `set`/`clear` get the help of the path and whose `show` means `status`. The M2-decided fix `auth gihub` → `omaddons auth github` (`tests/contract/usage_fixes.rs:150`) comes today from `value_fix` correcting SERVICE in place.
- clap 4.6.7: `disable_help_subcommand` is a global setting (`clap_builder` `command.rs:1647-1653`), so `auth` gets no implicit `help` subcommand. clap derive gives a non-`Option` subcommand field both `subcommand_required(true)` and `arg_required_else_help(true)` (`clap_derive` `derives/args.rs:204-210`); the second makes a bare parent print its help as an error. An unknown word where only subcommands are allowed is `ErrorKind::InvalidSubcommand` with the word in `ContextKind::InvalidSubcommand` (`clap_builder` `error/mod.rs:484-545`).
- `help.rs`'s `every_subcommand_has_exactly_one_registry_entry` (`src/app/help.rs:479-516`) checks top-level names only.
- `support::check` (`tests/contract/main.rs:114-225`) checks every contract run; `Run.argv` excludes the program name (`tests/common/home.rs:196-217`).
- `CLI_PATHS` (`omarchy/Model.js:133-178`) is held equal to `COMMANDS` by `tests/omarchy_widget.rs:30-51`.

## Technical Approach

### 1. `auth github` as a real subcommand, every argv unchanged

`src/app/auth.rs`:

```rust
/// `auth`'s arguments: the service, and `--from-gh` before or after it.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, clap::Args)]
pub struct AuthArgs {
    /// Store the token `gh auth token` prints (the only time omaddons asks gh)
    #[arg(long, global = true)]
    pub from_gh: bool,
    #[command(subcommand)]
    pub service: AuthService,
}

/// The services a token can be stored for.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, clap::Subcommand)]
pub enum AuthService {
    /// The GitHub token: status (the default), set (from standard input) or clear
    #[command(after_long_help = AUTH_HELP)]
    Github(GithubArgs),
}

/// `auth github`'s own arguments.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, clap::Args)]
pub struct GithubArgs {
    /// status (the default), set (the token from standard input) or clear
    #[arg(value_enum, value_name = "ACTION")]
    pub action: Option<AuthAction>,
}

impl AuthService {
    /// The envelope `command`.
    pub const fn command(&self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Github(_) => "auth github",
        }
    }
}
```

- Move `AUTH_HELP` from `src/cli.rs:547-557` to `src/app/auth.rs`, text unchanged: its examples are `auth github`'s.
- `Command::Auth` keeps its doc comment exactly (bare help's JSON lists it; the snapshot must not change), loses `after_long_help`, and gains `#[command(subcommand_required = true, arg_required_else_help = false)]`, so bare `omaddons auth` is clap's `MissingSubcommand`, which `usage_error`'s default arm turns into `usage` with the fix `omaddons help auth` and a one-sentence message (as today, when the missing SERVICE was the error). If the derive applies the variant's attributes before `AuthArgs::augment_args` and the implicit `arg_required_else_help(true)` wins, put the two settings on `AuthArgs`; the unit test `bare_auth_is_a_one_sentence_usage_error` decides.
- `auth::run` takes `args.from_gh` and `match &args.service { AuthService::Github(github) => github.action }`; the rest is unchanged (`(Some(Status | Clear), true)` stays the usage error whose fix is `omaddons auth github set --from-gh`).
- `--from-gh` is a global of `auth` so that an argv with the flag before the service, which parsed at `c0ab5e9`, still parses; clap propagates a global's value to the parent's matches when it is given after the subcommand, as the root's global flags already work.

Every argv that parsed at `c0ab5e9` parses to the same action:

| argv after `omaddons` | action, `--from-gh` |
|---|---|
| `auth github` | none (status), false |
| `auth github status`, `auth github set`, `auth github clear` | that action, false |
| `auth github --from-gh` | none (set), true |
| `auth github set --from-gh` | set, true |
| `auth --from-gh github` | none (set), true |
| `auth github status --from-gh` | status, true (parses; `run` refuses with `usage`, as before) |
| `--offline auth github`, `auth github --offline --json` | none (status), false |

### 2. One canonical path per parsed command

`src/app/mod.rs`:

- Add `pub fn canonical_path(command: &Command) -> &'static str`: the exhaustive match that is now `command_name`'s body, with `Command::Auth(args) => args.service.command()`. It is the one mapping from a parsed command to its name (the envelope's `command` and `Context::command` through `command_name`, capabilities' paths through A4, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`, `omaddons capabilities`).
- `command_name(command: Option<&Command>)` keeps its signature (callers `src/cli.rs:395`, `dispatch`) and becomes `command.map_or("help", canonical_path)`.
- `canonical(name: &str)`, the lookup for an argv that did not parse, gains a rule for a parent without a row: the path's own row; else the only row strictly under the path, when exactly one exists; else `"omaddons"`. So every usage error under `auth` (bare `auth`, `auth --bogus`, `auth gihub`) names `auth github`, the only command the user can have meant.
- `group_of(name)`: a top-level name without a row takes the group and the place of the first row under it, so bare help lists `auth` in Setup between `config` and `omarchy`, byte for byte as today.
- Rename the row `entry("auth", Group::Setup, true)` (`:159`) to `entry("auth github", Group::Setup, true)` in place; update `CommandEntry::mutates`'s doc ("`auth github` with `set`").

The rule the tests now enforce: **`COMMANDS` has one row per runnable path**: every clap leaf, plus every parent whose bare form runs (at `c0ab5e9`: `backup`, `config`, `errors`, `omarchy`, `targets`). A parent that requires a subcommand (`auth`) has no row.

### 3. Usage fixes under `auth`

`src/cli.rs`, in a function of its own (hot-spot rule: each hook in its own function):

```rust
/// Command paths whose subcommands name a service (a noun), not a verb. A mistyped
/// service is corrected in place: the verb after it (its ACTION, or none for status) is
/// the user's own, so the fix keeps the user's command (`auth gihub` → `auth github`).
pub const SERVICE_PARENTS: &[&str] = &["auth"];
```

- `subcommand_fix`: when `path` is a service parent, apply each close subcommand in place (`fix_argv_replacing(argv, bad, name)`) instead of offering a mutating guess's help. `auth gihub` → `omaddons auth github` (the decided fix, unchanged); `auth gihub set` → `omaddons auth github set` (as before). Without this, the guess `auth github` (a mutating row, conservatively) would become `omaddons help auth github` and change a decided fix. `usage_error`'s final filter (every suggestion parses, none is the failing argv) still applies.
- `value_fix` needs no code change: `path.first() == "auth"` and the ACTION check still hold, and `help_for(path)` now gives `omaddons help auth github`, the help that lists the actions (it gave `omaddons help auth`). Update its doc comment ("`set` and `clear` are suggested as `auth github`'s help").
- `tests/contract/usage_fixes.rs`: `CORPUS` rows become `(["auth", "gihub"], Some("auth github"))` and `(["auth", "github", "show"], Some("auth github"))`; `DECIDED` is unchanged; the sweep `every_one_edit_typo_of_every_command_gets_a_fix_that_runs` (`:257-311`), which now also sweeps `auth`'s subcommand, passes the row as the typed command for a row whose parent is in `omaddons::cli::SERVICE_PARENTS`, and `None` for every other row.

### 4. Help

No code change in `help::for_command`. What its tests now state:

- `help auth` is `auth`'s help and lists `github`; `auth --help` is the same text.
- `help auth github`, `help auth github set`, `auth github --help` and `auth github set --help` are one text, `github`'s, with usage `omaddons auth github [OPTIONS] [ACTION]`.
- `help auth github --json` has `data.command: "github"`, clap's leaf name, as for every nested command. Left as is (it is help's data, not the envelope `command`); listed in the close comment for the final walk of H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, the pre-freeze audit).
- `help auth gihub` is `usage`, "there is no command \"auth gihub\": auth has github", fix `omaddons help auth github` (unchanged fix; new message).
- Update the walk's comment examples at `src/app/help.rs:253-256` (`auth github set` is still a positional value; `auth github` is now a subcommand).

### 5. The widget

`omarchy/Model.js:171`: rename `"auth"` to `"auth github"`, same values (`mutates: true, destructive: false, binds: false`). `tests/omarchy_widget.rs`'s mirror test then holds. The widget never runs `auth`.

### 6. The contract suite checks every envelope's name

`tests/contract/main.rs`, `support` module:

```rust
/// The envelope `command` an argv that parses must carry: `version` for -V, `help` for
/// -h, else the canonical path of the parsed command.
pub fn canonical_name(argv: &[String]) -> Option<&'static str>
```

It parses `std::iter::once("omaddons").chain(argv)` with `Cli::try_parse_from` and returns `None` when that fails. In `check`, when the envelope's error code is not `internal` (a panic is reported under the name known when it struck) and `canonical_name` is `Some(expected)`, assert `envelope["command"] == expected` with the message "envelope command {got:?} is not the canonical path {expected:?} of {argv:?}" and the run's context. On success this compares each `Outcome::command()` literal with `canonical_path`, so a drifted literal fails the matrix; if one is found, fix the literal here and list it.

Harness self-test `the_harness_rejects_broken_envelopes` (`tests/contract/main.rs:546-581`): add a helper that runs `check` under `catch_unwind` and asserts the panic message (downcast to `String`) contains a given phrase, and use it for every negative case, so no case passes because an earlier check fired. New case: an otherwise valid envelope with `command: "status"` for argv `["list", "--json"]` → "canonical path".

### 7. The contract matrix

`tests/contract/matrix.rs::auth` (`:254-265`): add

- `s.json(&["auth"], 2)` → snapshot `auth_usage` (`command: "auth github"`, `code: "usage"`, `fix_argv: ["omaddons", "help", "auth"]`, a one-sentence `message`);
- `s.json(&["auth", "gihub"], 2)` → assert `command == "auth github"` and `fix_argv == ["omaddons", "auth", "github"]`.

The four existing `auth_*` snapshots and every other `.snap` file stay byte-identical. A diff anywhere else is a regression to investigate, never to accept.

### 8. README, in the same commit

- `### auth github`, its last line (README.md:1644): "`omaddons help auth` lists `auth`'s one subcommand, `github`; `omaddons help auth github` (or `omaddons auth github --help`) explains it: its actions and `--from-gh`."

### 9. The compatibility note for the leaf's close comment

- `COMMANDS` and `CLI_PATHS` name `auth github` (they named `auth`); every `auth github` run's envelope already said `auth github`, unchanged.

Under a service parent a close subcommand is corrected in place (`auth gihub` → `omaddons auth github`, `auth gihub set` → `omaddons auth github set`) instead of offered as its help. `value_fix` is unchanged in code; its ACTION help is now `omaddons help auth github`.

The whole suite passed it at once: **no `Outcome::command()` literal had drifted**. title: The five per-command facts on every `COMMANDS` row, held by their static rules and the contract matrix
description:
Part 2 of 3 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1 (Per-command facts in `COMMANDS`, and canonical names). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

A1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1`) is the root of omaddons M4's contract registry: M4 generates every description of the CLI (`capabilities --json`, the per-command JSON Schemas, the semantic manifest that freezes the contract at the first tag, the plan store's set of storable commands) from one registry built on the clap tree and `app::COMMANDS` (M4-D2). Subtask 1 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1.1) made every command path canonical. This subtask adds to every `COMMANDS` row the five facts clap cannot provide, declared once beside the command, and the tests that hold each declaration against behaviour. It is its own step because it rewrites every row of one table, with its own rule tests and its own contract-suite cross-check; it follows subtask 1 because both edit that table (subtask 1 renamed `auth` to `auth github`).

**The decisions this subtask implements:**

- **M4-D5, per-command exit codes are declared beside the command and verified.** `CommandEntry` gains `dictionary` (`General` or `Doctor`), `exits: &'static [u8]`, `data` (a `fn(&mut SchemaGenerator) -> Schema`), `stores_plan: bool` and `network` (`None`, `Optional` or `Required`). Static rules check the declarations: a command with `--check` or `--strict` lists 6; a mutating command lists 5; every general command lists 0, 1 and 2. The contract suite records every exit code each command path produced and fails if one is not declared. Why: clap knows nothing about exits, so the vision's "each command's capabilities entry lists the exit codes it can return" needs a declaration, and the cross-check makes it honest. Rejected: deriving exits from the error codes a command can raise (not statically knowable without whole-program analysis); every command declaring all of 0–6 (true, but useless to an agent). Do not be tempted by the second.
- **M4-D2, one registry; a fact clap cannot provide is declared exactly once, beside the command, and a test cross-checks it against behaviour.** Rejected: a hand-written `capabilities.json` (it drifts); deriving every fact from runtime behaviour (exits observed by tests: a command's exits are a promise and need a declaration, which tests then verify); proc-macro attributes on clap structs (a dependency and compile time for no gain over a table).
- **M4-D22, context for `stores_plan`:** eleven commands will store a plan on a dry run (`install`, `update`, `pin`, `unpin`, `adopt` when it adopts, `sync`, `copy`, `remove`, `undo`, `backup restore`, `backup prune`). D4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`) sets them; here every row declares `false`.
- **M4-D40, context for `dictionary`:** the doctor tree gets its own exit dictionary, added by E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`) with its rows. This subtask adds the `Doctor` variant so those rows can say so; no row uses it yet.
- **`binds` is not a field:** it stays derived from `app::precondition::BINDING_COMMANDS` (`src/app/precondition.rs:25-31`), the single list.

Who reads these facts next: A3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`) builds each command's schema from `data` and validates live output against it; A4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`) publishes every field in `capabilities.commands[]`; A10 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.10`) records them in the manifest's inputs; D4 sets `stores_plan`; E3 adds doctor rows; H3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3`) walks the paths for its coverage test; A7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.7`) adds the first new row with every field.

Goals served: G-M4-1 (self-describing: every fact in capabilities is generated from the code and cannot drift) and G-M4-5 (frozen and enforced: every exit site maps to a published code in the right dictionary); checkpoint criteria 1 (capabilities lists each command's exit codes, dictionary, plan storage and network) and 2 (a schema for every `COMMANDS` path).

**Facts this subtask relies on (verified at `c0ab5e9`):**

- `CommandEntry { name, group, mutates }` (`src/app/mod.rs:99-108`) derives `Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq`; nothing compares two entries. Rows are built by `const fn entry` (`:110-116`); `COMMANDS` is at `:121-165` (42 rows).
- The command → outcome mapping is `run_command`'s match (`src/app/mod.rs:374-587`). Every `Outcome` type is `pub`; `targets` and `config` use a generic `Done<D>` (`src/app/targets.rs:179-187`, `src/app/config.rs:106-114`). The `Outcome` trait requires `Data: Serialize + JsonSchema` (`src/output/mod.rs:34-35`).
- `check_failed` (exit 6) is constructed only by the three commands with `--check` (`status`, `outdated`, `errors`) and the four with `--strict` (`install`, `update`, `sync`, `copy`).
- fsx checks the write scope on every mutation (`src/fsx/mutate.rs:343-354`) and refuses with `scope_denied`, exit 4 (`src/fsx/scope.rs:276`, `:293`). `store::load_bytes` returns `state_too_new`, exit 4, for a newer state file that does not decode, on read paths too (`src/state/store.rs:250-273`); `World::records` propagates it (`src/app/world.rs:164-172`).
- `remove` fetches nothing (`src/app/remove.rs:246`); `undo` and the backup commands send no request; `info` builds a network stack for the newest release (`src/app/info.rs:509-516`); `auth github` status makes one request to `/rate_limit` (`src/app/auth.rs:355-376`); `status`, `list` and `errors` read the release memo and never fetch (`src/app/remembered.rs:1-2`).
- Two envelope names are no clap path: `version` (`-V`, `src/app/help.rs:352-359`, dispatched at `src/app/mod.rs:343-345`) and `omaddons` (no command could be read: `src/cli.rs:461-467`, and the panic state before parsing, `src/cli.rs:370`); their envelopes render through `HelpOutcome` (`src/cli.rs:440-447`).
- `support::check` (`tests/contract/main.rs:114-225`) runs on every envelope of the matrix, `special.rs`, `recommendations.rs` and `usage_fixes.rs`; the contract tests run in parallel threads of one process in no fixed order. Subtask 1 added its canonical-name check there.
- schemars 1.2.3: `SchemaGenerator::root_schema_for::<T>()` returns a self-contained root schema with `title` (`generate.rs:450-470`); `SchemaSettings::draft2020_12().for_serialize().into_generator()` exists (`generate.rs:108-183`).

The plan disagreed with the code in two places, and this subtask follows the code: the plan's "`network`: `Optional` for engine commands, `None` for the rest" (`info`, `auth github` and `adopt`'s report make requests; `remove`, `undo` and the backup commands make none), and "a test run after the matrix" (no such order exists; the assertion runs inside `check`).

## Technical Approach

Leaves named in this section: A3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`, schemas and live validation), A4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`, `capabilities`), A10 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.10`, the semantic manifest), D4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`, the plan store), E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, the doctor's diagnose runtime and exit dictionary).

### 1. Types (`src/app/mod.rs`, beside `Group`)

```rust
/// Which exit dictionary a command's process exit comes from (M4-D5, M4-D40).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, JsonSchema)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum Dictionary { General, Doctor }          // with ALL: [General, Doctor]

/// Whether a command uses the network.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, JsonSchema)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum Network {
    /// No path of the command sends a request (it may read the release memo).
    None,
    /// Some path may send a request (a release, an archive, a listing, the rate limit);
    /// under --offline the command still does its local work, from caches, or refuses
    /// only what needs the network.
    Optional,
    /// Its purpose is an upstream answer (search, outdated): it asks by default, and
    /// offline it answers only from what is remembered, marking the rest unchecked.
    Required,
}                                                 // with ALL: [None, Optional, Required]

/// A command path this build has, with every fact clap cannot provide (M4-D2, M4-D5).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct CommandEntry {
    pub name: &'static str,            // canonical path, = envelope `command`
    pub group: Group,
    pub mutates: bool,
    pub dictionary: Dictionary,        // General | Doctor
    pub exits: &'static [u8],          // ascending; declared, verified by the matrix
    pub data: fn(&mut schemars::SchemaGenerator) -> schemars::Schema,  // its Outcome::Data
    pub stores_plan: bool,             // M4-D22; false until D4
    pub network: Network,
}

/// The schema of `O`'s data: what a row's `data` points at, naming the outcome its
/// dispatch arm returns.
pub fn data_schema<O: crate::output::Outcome>(g: &mut schemars::SchemaGenerator) -> schemars::Schema {
    g.root_schema_for::<O::Data>()
}

const fn entry(name: &'static str, group: Group, mutates: bool, exits: &'static [u8],
               data: fn(&mut schemars::SchemaGenerator) -> schemars::Schema,
               network: Network) -> CommandEntry  // dictionary: General, stores_plan: false

impl CommandEntry {
    /// A doctor-tree command (E3): its exits come from the doctor dictionary.
    pub const fn doctor(self) -> Self
    /// A command whose dry run stores a plan (D4, M4-D22).
    pub const fn storing_plan(self) -> Self
}
```

- Drop `PartialEq, Eq` from `CommandEntry`: comparing function pointers is unreliable (rustc's `unpredictable_function_pointer_comparisons`), and nothing compares entries.
- Six arguments keep `entry` under clippy's `too_many_arguments` limit (seven). The defaults are honest at `c0ab5e9`: every command uses the general dictionary and none stores a plan. E3 and D4 use the modifiers.
- `data` names the `Outcome` its dispatch arm returns, not the data type, because several outcomes share one data type (`TargetsData`), and the outcome is what `run_command` returns: the command → type mapping moves into the table. A3 calls it with its own `for_serialize` generator; this subtask only declares it.
- `Dictionary` and `Network` derive `Serialize + JsonSchema` with snake_case values (`general`, `doctor`; `none`, `optional`, `required`) so A4 publishes them as they are. Never glob-import `Network::*`: its `None` would shadow `Option::None`. `#[rustfmt::skip]` on `COMMANDS`, as `src/error.rs` does for its code table, is allowed if one row per line reads better.

### 2. The rows

Fill all 42 rows by hand (no script). `group` and `mutates` are today's. `network` is section 4's. The exits floor is the static rules plus what the contract snapshots and matrix assertions show at `c0ab5e9`; the last column is what to check in the code before declaring the row (section 3).

| Row | Group | Mutates | Network | `data` (the outcome its arm returns) | Exits floor | Check in the code |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `status` | Look | no | None | `status::StatusOutcome` | 0 1 2 3 6 | 4 (a newer record or registry) |
| `list` | Look | no | None | `list::ListOutcome` | 0 1 2 3 | 4 |
| `outdated` | Look | no | Required | `outdated::OutdatedOutcome` | 0 1 2 6 | 3 (`-t`), 4 |
| `info` | Look | no | Optional | `info::InfoOutcome` | 0 1 2 3 | 4 |
| `search` | Look | no | Required | `search::SearchOutcome` | 0 1 2 | 3, 4 |

| `help` | Setup | no | None | `help::HelpOutcome` | 0 1 2 | — |

### 3. How each row's exits are derived

Declare an exit when some path of the command constructs a code of that exit class. Read the command's run path and the shared helpers it calls (`World::load`, `World::select*`, `World::records`, `Engine`, fsx):

- **0, 1, 2:** every general row (success; a runtime failure, `internal` included; a usage error).
- **3:** the command resolves a `-t` selector, an id, a ref, an addon name or a user-given file (`target_not_found`, `target_ambiguous`, `ref_ambiguous`, `not_found`, `not_managed`, `no_compatible_release`, `plan_not_found`).
- **4:** every mutating row (`scope_denied` can refuse any fsx write); a row whose path loads a versioned state file (`state_too_new`); and the specific refusals (`game_running`, `protected_folder`, `ownership_conflict`, `unmanaged_folder`, `case_collision`, `wrong_flavor`, the archive rules, `undo_conflict`, `host_blocked`, `filesystem_unsupported`, `file_exists`).
- **5:** every mutating row (static rule), and any read row that acquires the global lock (none known; check `GlobalLock::acquire`'s callers, `src/fsx/lock.rs:72`).
- **6:** exactly the rows whose clap command has `--check` or `--strict`.

Never declare an exit "to be safe" (M4-D5 rejected declaring all of 0–6). Record in the leaf's close comment each row whose final exits differ from section 2's floor, with the construction site that justifies each added code.

### 4. Network, as decided

- `Required`: `search`, `outdated`.
- `Optional`: `install`, `update`, `pin`, `unpin`, `adopt`, `sync`, `copy` (they resolve releases and download through the engine; `pin` and `unpin` revalidate the release cache), `info` (the newest release) and `auth github` (status's one request to `/rate_limit`).
- `None`: every other row, including `remove`, `undo` and the backup commands (engine transactions that send no request) and `status`, `list` and `errors` (the memo only).

### 5. The envelope names that are no clap path

```rust
/// An envelope `command` that is no clap path: it never appears in help, in
/// capabilities' commands or in the widget's CLI_PATHS.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
pub struct EnvelopeOnly {
    pub name: &'static str,
    pub exits: &'static [u8],
    pub data: fn(&mut schemars::SchemaGenerator) -> schemars::Schema,
    pub why: &'static str,
}

pub const ENVELOPE_ONLY: &[EnvelopeOnly] = &[
    EnvelopeOnly { name: "omaddons", exits: &[1, 2], data: data_schema::<help::HelpOutcome>,
                   why: "no command could be read from the arguments: a usage error before any subcommand, or a panic before parsing" },
    EnvelopeOnly { name: "version", exits: &[0], data: data_schema::<help::HelpOutcome>,
                   why: "-V or --version before any subcommand" },
];
```

The static rules apply to commands, not to these. A3 validates `version` envelopes through `data`; A4 and A10 decide whether to publish them.

### 6. Lookups

- `pub fn command_entry(path: &str) -> Option<&'static CommandEntry>`.
- `pub fn declared_exits(name: &str) -> Option<&'static [u8]>`: a row's exits, else an `ENVELOPE_ONLY` name's, else `None`.

### 7. The static rules, as a pure checker (test module of `src/app/mod.rs`)

`fn exit_rule_violations(entry: &CommandEntry, has_check_or_strict: bool) -> Vec<String>`, one message per broken rule:

1. `exits` is non-empty and strictly ascending (sorted, no duplicates);
2. a `General` row: every code is a general exit (`Exit::ALL`'s codes), and 0, 1 and 2 are listed;
3. `mutates` ⇒ 4 and 5 are listed;
4. 6 is listed exactly when `has_check_or_strict` (computed from the clap tree: `Cli::command()`, built, walked to the row's path, any argument whose long name is `check` or `strict`);
5. `stores_plan` ⇒ `mutates`;
6. a `Doctor` row: "the doctor dictionary is E3's: extend these rules with `doctor::Exit`", until E3 extends the checker with its dictionary.

### 8. The exit observation in the contract suite (`tests/contract/main.rs`, `support`)

```rust
/// Every (command, exit) the contract suite produced in this process.
static OBSERVED: Mutex<BTreeMap<String, BTreeSet<i32>>> = Mutex::new(BTreeMap::new());

/// Records `code` for `command`, and fails unless the command declares it.
pub fn observe_exit(command: &str, code: i32, ctx: &str)

/// A copy of the table, for logs.
pub fn observed() -> BTreeMap<String, BTreeSet<i32>>
```

- `check` calls `observe_exit` right after verifying `ok`, `exit_code` and the registered exit.
- An unknown name fails: "envelope command \"auth\" is neither a COMMANDS path nor an ENVELOPE_ONLY name".
- An undeclared exit fails: "help exited 4, which its COMMANDS row does not declare: declared [0, 1, 2], observed so far {…}; add the code to the row's exits if the command can return it".
- Recover a poisoned lock (`PoisonError::into_inner`), and drop the guard before asserting.
- Why inline: the contract tests run in parallel threads in no fixed order, so no test can run "after the matrix". Checked inside `check`, every envelope of every contract test is checked whatever the order, which is strictly stronger than one test reading a table that may be half full.

Harness self-test `the_harness_rejects_broken_envelopes` (subtask 1 gave it a helper that asserts each panic's message):

- the good envelope becomes `command: "help"` with argv `["--json"]` (it was `"t"`, which no longer passes);
- the empty-fix and unparsable-fix cases use `command: "info"` with argv `["info", "x", "--json"]` (a row declaring 3), so they still fail for their own reason; the key-order case uses `command: "help"`;
- new: `command: "auth"` (a valid success envelope otherwise) → "neither a COMMANDS path";
- new: `command: "help"`, `exit_code: 4`, error `game_running` (registered exit 4) with the prose fix "quit the game client, then rerun" and one stderr `error` event → "does not declare".

**Files:** `src/app/mod.rs`; `tests/contract/main.rs`.

title: E2E: every `auth` spelling and every bare parent answers under its canonical name
description:
Part 3 of 3 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1 (Per-command facts in `COMMANDS`, and canonical names). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

A1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1`) declares, beside every command in `app::COMMANDS`, the facts clap cannot provide (its exit dictionary, its exits, its data schema, whether it stores a plan, whether it uses the network; M4-D2, M4-D5), and makes every command path canonical (M4-D55 rule 5: the envelope `command` equals the canonical clap path). Subtask 1 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1.1) turned `auth`'s positional service into a real `github` subcommand with every argv unchanged, added `app::canonical_path`, and made the contract suite check that every parsed argv's envelope names its canonical path. Subtask 2 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1.2) filled the five facts on every row, declared the two envelope names that are no clap path (`omaddons`, `version`), and made the contract suite fail any envelope whose exit its command does not declare.

This subtask is the end-to-end proof, as two logged scenarios that a developer can read step by step when something regresses: every `auth` spelling a user or agent may type answers as `auth github` with a declared exit and the same behaviour as before, and every bare parent, alias and envelope-only name answers under the name the registry gives it. It is its own step because it is new integration code that exercises the whole surface the first two subtasks changed, and it uses T1's `TestLog` (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`), which the first two do not need.

Goals served: G-M4-1 (a command's name is the same in its argv, in help, in the registry and in its envelope, so an agent that learns a path can type it and match it) and G-M4-2 (the decided fix for a mistyped service, `omaddons auth gihub` → `omaddons auth github`, still works).

**What the scenarios rely on (as established by subtasks 1 and 2):**

- `app::command_name` and `app::canonical_path` name every parsed command; `app::declared_exits(name)` answers for every `COMMANDS` row and the `ENVELOPE_ONLY` names `omaddons` (exits 1, 2) and `version` (exit 0).
- `support::check` (`tests/contract/main.rs`) asserts, on every envelope it is given, the canonical name of a parsed argv and the declared exit, and records `(command, exit)` in a per-process table that `support::observed()` returns.
- `cli::SERVICE_PARENTS` is `["auth"]`: a mistyped service is corrected in place.
- The contract suite's `Scene` (`tests/contract/main.rs:366-505`) is a home with a retail and a Mists Classic client and replayed GitHub releases; its `Home::std_command` (`tests/common/home.rs:254-266`) adds `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES` and `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT` to the `TestEnv`'s variables, so no run reads the development machine's `/proc` or network.
- T1's `TestLog`: `tlog!()`, `log.step(label)`, `log.note(text)`, `log.json(label, &value)`, `log.run(&env, &argv) -> Ran` (records argv, environment overrides, cwd, timing, exit, the parsed envelope, stderr events, `net.log` lines added, failpoints), `Ran::{ok(), exit(n), envelope(), data(), error_code(), warnings(), commands()}`, `log.tree(label, root)`, `log.assert_unchanged(label, root)`, the drop guard that prints `test log: <path>` and the last 20 steps on a panic, and `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG=verbose`.

## Technical Approach

New module `tests/contract/canonical_names.rs`, declared in `tests/contract/main.rs` beside `matrix`, `special` and the others, so it shares `support` and `Scene`.

- Run every step through `log.run` with the scene's `TestEnv` plus the two variables `Home::std_command` adds; if the `log.run` of T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`) takes the extra variables through another call, use that one. Then hand the result to `support::check` (it takes a `common::home::Run { argv, code, stdout, stderr }`; build it from the `Ran`, and add a small test-only conversion such as `Ran::to_run()` to `tests/common/tlog.rs` if T1 did not provide one). `check` asserts the canonical name and the declared exit; the scenario then asserts the step's own facts.
- No step needs standard input: `auth github set` with nothing to read is refused with `usage` whether its standard input is empty or a terminal, both with the same fix, which is what the step asserts. If `log.run` inherits the test's standard input rather than closing it, give that one step an explicitly empty standard input (as `Home::exec_input` does with `b""`), so the child can never wait on an open pipe.

### Scenario 1: `auth_answers_as_auth_github_on_every_path`

`let s = Scene::new(); let log = tlog!();`, then `log.tree("config", s.home.env.config())` (`TestEnv::config()` is the home's `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME`; `<config>` is its `omaddons/` directory, so the credentials file is `s.home.env.config().join("omaddons/credentials/github")`). Steps, in order:

| Step label | argv (each with `--json`) | Exit | Asserted beyond `check` |
|---|---|---|---|
| status, offline | `auth github --offline` | 0 | `command: "auth github"`; `data.configured: false`, `data.source: "none"`, `data.rate_limit: null`, `data.dry_run: false` |
| status spelled out | `auth github status --offline` | 0 | `data` equal to the first step's |
| flags before the command | `--offline auth github` | 0 | `data` equal to the first step's |
| set with nothing to read | `auth github set` | 2 | `error.code: "usage"`, `error.fix` the standard-input prose fix (below), `error.fix_argv: null` |
| clear with nothing stored | `auth github clear` | 0 | `command: "auth github"`, `data.configured: false`; no file `<config>/credentials/github` afterwards |
| from-gh with status | `auth github status --from-gh` | 2 | `error.code: "usage"`, `error.fix_argv: ["omaddons", "auth", "github", "set", "--from-gh"]` |
| from-gh before the service | `auth --from-gh github clear` | 2 | the same code and `fix_argv` (the global flag reaches the same check) |
| bare auth | `auth` | 2 | `command: "auth github"`, `error.code: "usage"`, `error.fix_argv: ["omaddons", "help", "auth"]`, `error.message` without a newline |
| mistyped service | `auth gihub` | 2 | `command: "auth github"`, `error.fix_argv: ["omaddons", "auth", "github"]` |
| mistyped action | `auth github st` | 2 | `command: "auth github"`, `error.fix_argv: ["omaddons", "help", "auth", "github"]` |
| help of github, three spellings | `help auth github`; `auth github --help`; `auth github set --help` | 0 each | `command: "help"`, `data.command: "github"`, the three `data` objects equal |
| help of the parent | `help auth` | 0 | `data.command: "auth"`; and a human run of `help auth` (no `--json`) whose stdout contains `github` |

The standard-input prose fix asserted at "set with nothing to read" is exactly the string `echo "$TOKEN" | omaddons auth github set` (a `PROSE_COMMANDS` entry, so it carries no argv).

At the end: `log.assert_unchanged("config", s.home.env.config())`; `<config>/credentials/github` does not exist; `common::netlog::net_log(&s.home).is_empty()` (no step sent a request). `log.note` each fact as it is checked.

### Scenario 2: `bare_parents_and_envelope_only_names_answer_under_their_canonical_names`

`let s = Scene::new(); let log = tlog!();`, then `log.tree("state", s.home.env.state())` and `log.tree("cache", s.home.env.cache())` for diagnosis only (no assertion on them: listing commands may write derived caches).

| Step label | argv (each with `--json`) and environment | Expected `command` | Exit |
|---|---|---|---|
| bare backup is backup list | `backup`, `OMADDONS_FS_FREE_MB=1024` | `backup list` | 0 |
| a usage error at backup's level names backup | `backup --bogus` | `backup` | 2 |
| bare omarchy is omarchy status | `omarchy`, `PATH` set to an empty directory under the scene root | `omarchy status` | the run's exit, declared |
| bare targets is targets | `targets` | `targets` | 0 |
| bare config is config | `config` | `config` | 0 |
| bare errors is errors | `errors` | `errors` | the run's exit, declared |
| bare auth names auth github | `auth` | `auth github` | 2 |
| bare omaddons is help | (none) | `help` | 0 |
| -V is version | `-V` | `version` | 0 |
| an unknown command is omaddons | `nosuch` | `omaddons` | 2 |
| an alias answers as its command | `ls`; `log` | `list`; `history` | the run's exit, declared |

"The run's exit, declared" means: assert the name, and pass the run's own exit to `support::check`, which then asserts that the command declares it. The scenario ends with `log.json("observed exits", &support::observed())`, so the transcript shows every name and exit this process saw.

**Files:** `tests/contract/canonical_names.rs` (new), `tests/contract/main.rs` (the `mod` line), and `tests/common/tlog.rs` only if a `Ran` → `Run` conversion is missing.

Decided while writing this bead (confirm or adjust in the leaf's close comment): the scenarios live in the contract test binary so they share `support::check` and `Scene`; the steps avoid standard input; exits that depend on the scene's contents are asserted only as declared.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `auth_answers_as_auth_github_on_every_path` passes: every step's envelope names `auth github` (or `help` for the help steps) with its listed exit and facts, including bare `auth` (fix `omaddons help auth`), `auth gihub` (fix `omaddons auth github`), `auth github st` (fix `omaddons help auth github`) and `auth --from-gh github clear`; at the end `<config>` is unchanged, no credentials file exists and `net.log` is empty.
- [ ] `bare_parents_and_envelope_only_names_answer_under_their_canonical_names` passes: bare `backup` → `backup list`, `backup --bogus` → `backup`, bare `omarchy` → `omarchy status`, `targets`, `config`, `errors` → themselves, bare `auth` → `auth github`, bare `omaddons` → `help`, `-V` → `version`, `nosuch` → `omaddons`, `ls` → `list`, `log` → `history`, each with a declared exit.
- [ ] Both scenarios write a `TestLog` transcript with one step per table row, and a deliberately broken assertion (tried locally, not committed) prints `test log: <path>` and the last steps.
- [ ] `argc e2e canonical_names` runs both with verbose logs.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes and `ubs` is clean on the changed files.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

None: this subtask adds integration scenarios only. A `Ran` → `Run` conversion added to `tests/common/tlog.rs`, if any, is covered by both scenarios' use of it.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

`tests/contract/canonical_names.rs`, the two scenarios above, on a fresh `Scene` each (tempdir homes, `TZ=UTC` and the other `TestEnv` settings, recorded HTTP fixtures, an empty fake `/proc`). Commands in the order of each table; after each, `support::check` (name, declared exit, the whole envelope contract) and the row's own assertions. Scenario 1 hashes `<config>` before the first step and asserts it unchanged after the last.

### Logging

- One `log.step` per table row, labelled as in the table, so a failure reads "step 'mistyped service' …".
- `log.run` records each argv, the environment overrides (`OMADDONS_FS_FREE_MB`, `PATH`, the fixture and proc variables), the exit, the parsed envelope and the stderr events.
- `log.tree("config", …)` / `log.assert_unchanged("config", …)` in scenario 1, logging the first differing paths on a difference; `log.tree` of `<state>` and `<cache>` in scenario 2 for diagnosis.
- `log.json("observed exits", &support::observed())` at the end of scenario 2.
- On a panic the drop guard prints `test log: <path>` and the last 20 steps; `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG=verbose` (as `argc e2e` sets it) echoes every step live.

## Considerations

- **It owns no product code.** A step that fails is a defect in subtask 1 or 2 (or a fact of the scene); fix it there and say so in the close comment, or file a bug `discovered-from` omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1.
- **Keep it cheap:** about 25 short runs, none online.
- **Privacy:** synthetic homes only; the scene never reads the real `HOME`; the transcript holds no token (no step stores one).
- **The contract suite runs its tests in parallel:** these scenarios depend on nothing another test does, and `observed()` is only logged, never asserted complete.

## Dependencies

Parent: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1 (Per-command facts in `COMMANDS`, and canonical names).

- Before it: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1.1 (the canonical paths, the `auth github` restructure and the name check) and omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1.2 (the declared exits, `ENVELOPE_ONLY` and the exit observation), whose behaviour it proves; and T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs and the `argc e2e` runner), whose `TestLog` it uses.
- After it: nothing inside A1. Closing it, if it is the last open subtask, closes omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1 after its acceptance criteria are verified.

title: The semantic contract manifest and its compatibility classifier
description:
## How to work this bead

This bead is worked through its 6 subtasks, listed below in work order. Claim a subtask, not this bead (`br ready --parent omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.10` lists the ready ones). The agent that closes the last open subtask then verifies every acceptance criterion of this bead (they are the leaf's, not any one subtask's), and closes this bead with `br close omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.10 --reason "done: <evidence> · found: <ids>"`. Until this bead is closed, every bead it blocks stays blocked.

1. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.10.1 The manifest's node model, canonical form and entry point: `Manifest`, `Node`, `Fact`, `NodeKind`, node ids and paths, the canonical JSON layout, `render`/`parse`, `build(&Registry)`, and A4's `Registry`/`CommandInfo` if A4 has not created them yet.
2. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.10.2 Outputs, persisted positions and `addons.toml`: every published schema normalized into nodes: the schema normalizer (types, requiredness, nullability, bounds, enums, tagged and untagged variants, opaque subtrees, the error union, recursion) applied to every command's data, the envelope, every event, every error code's variant, every persisted kind and `addons.toml`.
3. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.10.3 Inputs and registries: the CLI tree, `config.toml` keys, the declared requirements, and every registry with its facts: commands, flags and positionals from `CommandInfo` and the `command_facts`/`arg_facts` helpers with every fact the classifier compares, `KeyKind::name`, `REQUIRES` (A4's, or created here) and the default-missing scan, error and warning codes with the tri-state retryability, actions, events, phases, log levels, exit dictionaries, `release` env vars, persisted kinds and their versions.
4. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.10.4 The compatibility classifier: direction rules, persisted-kind bumps and the change report: `classify(&baseline, &current) -> Changes`, the rules table, `Bump`, `KindBump`, `Changes::render`, and the unit-test matrix over synthetic manifests.
5. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.10.5 The readable projection, the report and instance matching: `contract::wire::names`, `section_counts`, `report`, and `unmatched` (an observed JSON instance located in the manifest).
6. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.10.6 Tests: the report test, and the manifest checked against the live binary: `tests/contract/manifest_report.rs` and `tests/e2e_manifest.rs`, with `TestLog` transcripts.

Subtasks 2, 3 and 4 each need only subtask 1's model and touch different files: work them in parallel. Subtask 5 needs all three. Subtask 6 needs subtask 5.

**Size L, kept as one leaf.** Generation and classification share one node model; one without the other is untestable (a classifier with nothing real to classify proves only its synthetic cases; a manifest without a classifier enforces nothing). The subtasks split the **work** into commits that each pass `argc gate`; they do not split the **closure**. This bead closes only when all six are done, so H2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.2`, the golden and the released-baseline mechanism) and T2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.2`, the slice-1 end-to-end demo) never see half of it.

## Background

**What this bead is.** At the first tag (`v0.1.0`, made by H6, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the M4 checkpoint) omaddons' contract freezes: from then on every change to what a program can rely on (the JSON envelope, each command's `data` keys and their types, error and warning codes and each code's typed `details`, actions, failure-mode ids, NDJSON events and their fields, exit codes, flags with their defaults and value grammars, the keys of persisted files) must carry the version bump it needs, checked by the gate. This bead builds the two pieces that check is made of:

- **the semantic manifest** (`contract::manifest::build(&Registry) -> Manifest`): one deterministic, canonical record of every fact of the contract a consumer can depend on, generated from the code (the clap tree, `app::COMMANDS`, the registries, the schemas), with implementation details normalized away;
- **the compatibility classifier** (`contract::manifest::classify(&baseline, &current) -> Changes`): compares two manifests node by node and labels each change `additive`, `breaking` or `unclassified`, in the right direction for outputs and for inputs, and routes persisted-format changes to their own kind's version rule;

plus the readable projection (`contract::wire::names`), a report test that prints the manifest's section counts and the classifier's verdict, and a matcher that locates an observed JSON instance in the manifest. It commits **no** golden: H2 commits `tests/contract/manifest.json` and `tests/contract/wire_names.txt`, wires the two comparisons into the gate and tests the documented updater; H6 writes the first released baseline. This bead is built early (slice 1) so that every later leaf of the milestone can see its own change semantically, and so that the freeze has a tested enforcement long before it is switched on.

**What is true today** (verified at `c0ab5e9`; the full list is under "Facts this bead relies on"): there is no `src/contract/` module, no generated schema, no wire-name list and no compatibility check of any kind. The closest things are the `limit_registries` snapshot and a hand table of error codes (`src/error.rs:744-762`). Snapshots and the byte-identical repeat tests go through `serde_json::Value`, which sorts keys, so nothing pins key order or types today.

**Why a semantic manifest, not a names list** (M4-D56's reasoning, restated because it is the reason this bead exists). The reviewed draft of the plan froze the contract with a names file and a one-letter type alphabet (`s n b o a ?`). That freezes too little:

- it loses **requiredness** (a field that may now be absent looks the same), **integer versus number** (a number where an integer was looks the same), and **tagged-variant relations** (a field moving from one variant to another hides in a merged path list, and flattening unions hid incompatible combinations);
- requiredness and nullability are distinct schema properties and need distinct records;
- walking the schema of `capabilities.commands` records that object's *shape*, not that `update` accepts `--if-match` or that a positional is optional, so removing a flag or changing a default would have left the golden unchanged.

The manifest therefore records outputs with their types, requiredness, nullability, bounds, enum values and variants, and inputs from the CLI itself: every path, alias, flag, positional, default, grammar, arity, repeatability, conflict and requirement.

**What it serves.**

- **G-M4-5, frozen and enforced:** "At the first tag the contract is consistent (audited), complete (a semantic manifest of every input the CLI accepts and every output it emits, with a readable names list beside it) and enforced: every later change is compared with the released baseline, and one that does not carry its version bump fails the gate, however the current golden was regenerated." This bead is the "complete" and the classifier the enforcement uses.
- **G-M4-1, self-describing (context):** every fact in the manifest is generated from the code, never kept by hand, so it cannot drift from what the binary does.
- **Vision D21:** "contract changes become deliberate (`schema_version` bump plus a recorded comment), never accidental". After H2 and H6, the gate makes this true, with this bead's classifier deciding which bump a change needs.
- **Vision G4, agent ergonomics** ("the first command an agent guesses works") over time: an agent written against contract 1.0 keeps working on every 1.x, because nothing that could break it lands without a major bump.

**Checkpoint criteria it is responsible for** (§3.2 of the plan; H6 records the evidence):

- **Criterion 14, the contract is frozen** (with H1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, the pre-freeze audit, H2 and H6): "The golden test passes: the semantic manifest (inputs and outputs, with requiredness, nullability, integer versus number, bounds, tagged variants, and the CLI's paths, flags, positionals, defaults, value grammars, arity, conflicts and requirements) and its readable names projection. … A test exercises the documented updater: a contract change regenerated into the current golden without a version bump still fails against the released baseline, for an addition, a removal, a requiredness change, a removed flag and a changed default. … JSON member order is deterministic but is not compared as contract; reordering keys needs no version bump." This bead supplies the manifest, the projection and the classifier those tests run; H2 supplies the golden and the updater tests.
- **Criterion 17, gate and checkpoint runs:** `argc gate --all` passes from a clean checkout with this bead's tests in it.
- **Slice 1's exit demo** (run and recorded by T2, not here): "the manifest's report prints".

**The decisions that shape it** (the full decision log is filed as comments on the milestone epic omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm):

- **M4-D56: a semantic manifest pins the contract, and every change is compared with the released baseline (owner-visible).**
  - *Two generated artifacts, one enforcement.* `tests/contract/manifest.json` is the semantic manifest, generated by `contract::manifest::build(&Registry)`: the enforcement artifact, canonical JSON with sorted keys and implementation details normalized away (no `$defs` names, references resolved). It records **outputs** (every command's `data` or report, the envelope, `error` per code with its `DetailSpec`, every NDJSON event: each field's path, type with integer and number distinct, requiredness, nullability, meaningful bounds such as `minimum` and `maxItems`, enum values, and tagged-variant relations, with `opaque` subtrees marked); **inputs** (every canonical command path and its aliases, every flag and positional with its default, value grammar, arity, repeatability, conflicts and requirements, plus each command's exit dictionary and declared exits, binding support and plan storage; the `config.toml` keys and `addons.toml` paths); **registries** (error and warning codes with exits and retryability, actions, failure-mode ids, events, phases, env vars, the two exit dictionaries); **persisted formats** with their own kind versions (`store::KINDS`, the journal families, `plan`, `doctor_report`). `tests/contract/wire_names.txt` is the readable projection, one name per line, sorted, in typed sections; it exists for review and enforces nothing on its own.
  - *The current golden and the released baseline are separate.* The golden carries an informational header (`# contract <v>`, `# frozen: true|false`; `"header": {"contract": …, "frozen": …}`) that **no comparison reads**. The released baseline `tests/contract/released/<version>.json` is a copy of the last released manifest with provenance, advanced only by the release procedure.
  - *The gate compares twice* (H2's): with the released baseline whenever one exists, through **this bead's classifier**: additions only need a higher minor; anything breaking or unclassified needs a higher major; and with the current golden (generated output must equal the committed files).
  - *Direction.* For outputs, adding a field, an enum value or a tagged variant, making an optional field always present, or narrowing a bound is additive; removing anything, making a field optional or nullable, widening a type (integer to number) or a bound, or moving a field between variants is breaking. For inputs the reverse holds: accepting more (a new flag, alias, value or optional positional) is additive; accepting less (a removed flag or value, a new requirement or conflict, a required positional, a narrower grammar) or a changed default is breaking. A change the classifier cannot place is breaking, pending review. The guide tells consumers to tolerate unknown enum values and fields.
  - *Persisted formats keep their own rules.* A file kind's schema change requires that kind's own version bump under its migration rules (M2-D36, M3-D45); it does not by itself force a wire major.
  - *Member order is not contract.* Rendering stays deterministic (declaration order, byte-identical repeats, M4-D18) so diffs are readable, but JSON objects are unordered (RFC 8259 §4): the manifest ignores member order, and reordering keys needs no bump.
  - *Why:* a golden that is both the current snapshot and the previous contract cannot enforce anything (regenerating after a breaking change erases the evidence the gate needs); names alone freeze too little (above); classifying in the right direction matters (accepting a new flag is safe, emitting one less field is not).
  - *Rejected:* insta snapshots of each schema (noisy diffs, and no bump rule); enforcing from day one of M4 (M4 adds most of the names); the reviewed draft's single names file as both snapshot and baseline (self-erasing); treating member order as contract (a bump for a meaningless change).
  - *Owner-visible:* after the tag, an added JSON key needs a minor bump, and the comparison is with the released contract. README's "Stability" section says so (H2 writes it).
- **M4-D2: one contract registry feeds every description of the CLI.** `src/contract/` assembles a `Registry` from the live clap tree, `app::COMMANDS` with its per-command facts, the error, warning and exit registries, the action, event, env-var and feature registries, the limits and politeness registries, the rules table and the sources registry, and the doctor's failure-mode registry; `capabilities`, `robot-docs`, the wire-name golden, bare help's discovery line and `doctor capabilities` all read it. A fact clap cannot provide is declared exactly once, beside the command or code it describes. *Why:* one registry means the guide, `capabilities` and the golden cannot disagree; all are views of the same data. *Rejected:* a hand-written `capabilities.json` (it drifts); deriving every fact from runtime behaviour (a declaration is a promise, which tests then verify); proc-macro attributes on clap structs (a dependency and compile time for no gain). **For this bead:** the manifest is one more view of that registry. It reads every fact from the registry and the tables it is built from, and declares no fact of its own except where clap offers no public way to read one (the `REQUIRES` table, below).
- **M4-D3 (context): the envelope's `schema_version` is the contract version** (`output::SCHEMA_VERSION`, "1.0"). Persisted files keep their own versions (`store::KINDS`, the journal, `addons.toml`), which the contract lists but does not tie to its own. This is why the classifier reports a persisted-format change as a demand on that kind's version, not on `schema_version`.
- **M4-D55 (context): the contract's rules hold from slice 1; the pre-freeze audit is their final pass.** A1 and A3 enforce the naming and nullability rules from slice 1; H1 empties A3's allowlist and walks the contract once more. **This bead may land after H1** (§10.2 of the plan lists it among the leaves that may): it adds no wire shape, so the audit never needs to see it, and when it lands after H1 its manifest records the post-audit contract.
- **M4-D9 and M4-D10 (context):** every schema is generated with the serialize contract (`SchemaSettings::draft2020_12().for_serialize()`), one fresh generator per command, event, file or error variant, so `$defs` names depend only on one type but are still not stable identifiers (schemars disambiguates duplicate names by generation order: `Summary`, `Summary2`, …). `error.details` is typed per code by A9's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9`, meanings and `DetailSpec`s) recursive `DetailSpec`, rendered as each error variant's `details` schema by A3. The manifest normalizes these schemas, so it inherits their truth and must not depend on their `$defs` names.
- **M4-D18 (context): determinism.** Maps are `BTreeMap`, no `HashMap` or `HashSet` appears in a serialized type, and key order is a rendering property, not wire semantics: the manifest does not record it.
- **Appendix A.1 (context): `retryable` per code is `true`, `false` or `"conditional"`.** It is `"conditional"` for `plan_stale`, `http_status` and `hash_mismatch`, whose instances decide; every error instance keeps a boolean `error.retryable`; the tri-state appears only in the code registry (`capabilities`, `robot-docs errors`, **the manifest's `error` nodes**).

**Facts this bead relies on** (as of `c0ab5e9`, each checked in the source):

- There is no `src/contract/` directory. A2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.2`, the action, event, env-var and feature registries) creates `src/contract/mod.rs` with `actions.rs`, `events.rs`, `env.rs`, `features.rs`; A3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`, schemas and live validation) adds `schema.rs` and `opaque.rs`; A4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`, `omaddons capabilities`) adds `Registry` (`builtin()`, `build()`) in `mod.rs` and `commands.rs` with `CommandInfo`, `Values`, `REQUIRES` and `values.rs` with the app-validated value sets (§6.2.1 of the plan; A4's bead gives the exact shapes, restated in TA 2).
- `app::COMMANDS` (`src/app/mod.rs:121-165`) holds 42 rows, each `{name, group, mutates}` (`CommandEntry`, `:101-108`). A1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1`, per-command facts) extends each row with `dictionary`, `exits` (ascending), `data: fn(&mut SchemaGenerator) -> Schema`, `stores_plan` and `network`, renames the `auth` row to `auth github` (a real clap subcommand of `auth`, which then has no row), and adds `ENVELOPE_ONLY`: the two envelope `command` names that are no clap path, `omaddons` (exits 1, 2) and `version` (exit 0), both with `HelpOutcome`'s data schema; A1 left it to A4 and this bead to decide whether to publish them.
- The clap tree: `Cli` (`src/cli.rs:25-41`) with `disable_help_flag`, `disable_version_flag`, `disable_help_subcommand` and `args_override_self`; `GlobalArgs` (`:44-119`) declares 16 global arguments (`--json --robot --format -t/--target --dry-run --actor --reason --offline --while-running --if-match --no-color --no-progress --progress --quiet -v/--verbose -h/--help`) and the root-only `-V/--version` (not global; §2.1 of the plan counts it among "17 global flags"); `Command` (`:137-213`) with visible aliases (`add`, `upgrade`, `uninstall`/`rm`/`delete`, `revert`/`rollback`, `log`, `check`, `show`, `find`, `ls`); `-t` has `visible_alias = "flavor"` (`:62-71`); `--format` and `--progress` use string `value_parser` lists with `ignore_case = true` (`:53-60`, `:98-105`); `-v` is `ArgAction::Count` (`:111`); `errors` sets `args_conflicts_with_subcommands = true` (`:194`).
- Conflicts declared at `c0ab5e9`: `install --any-flavor` with `--no-any-flavor` (`src/app/install.rs:86`); `status --deep` with `--cached` (`src/app/status.rs:75`); `backup create --auto` with `--verify` (`src/app/backup.rs:214`); `backup prune --keep` and `--older-than` with the `ID` positionals (`:250`, `:254`); `undo --last-by` with the `TX` positional (`src/app/undo.rs:45`) and `undo --run` with `TX` and `--last-by` (`:50`). clap enforces each conflict in both directions.
- **No argument declares a requirement** at `c0ab5e9`: no `requires`, `requires_if`, `required_unless_present*` or `required_if_eq*` appears in `src/`, and no `#[arg(env = …)]` (`OMADDONS_ACTOR` and `OMADDONS_OFFLINE` are read by hand in `Context::new`, `src/cli.rs:247-296`, at `:258` and `:291-292`). ### 2. What the manifest reads, and the registry precondition

`pub fn build(registry: &Registry) -> Manifest` is the entry point (§6.7), called with `Registry::builtin()`. The manifest is one more view of the one contract registry (M4-D2): it reads every fact from `Registry` and `contract::commands` where they expose it, and otherwise from the static table they are built from (`COMMANDS`, `ENVELOPE_ONLY`, `ErrorCode::ALL`, `WarningCode::ALL`, `Exit::ALL`, `Action::ALL`, `EventName::ALL`, `Phase::ALL`, `LogLevel::ALL`, `ENV_VARS`, `KINDS`, `config::KEYS`, A3's schema functions). Those are the same data, so the two paths cannot disagree.

**The manifest never depends on anything read at run time.** It reads no environment variable, no file, no clock and no `config.toml`. A4's design separates `Registry::builtin()` ("the binary alone: no I/O and no environment at all", which the golden, the guide and `robot-docs` read) from `Registry::build()` (`builtin` plus `config.toml`, which only `capabilities` reads); the manifest is built from `builtin()` and never reads the config-derived fields (`effective`, `config_error`, `warnings`). Limits, sources, families, client rules, target-id forms and feature words are capabilities *values*, not contract shapes, and §6.7 does not list them (their *shapes* are recorded through `capabilities`' own data schema). A source scan holds this (`manifest_modules_read_no_environment`, subtask 1). Without it, `cargo test` on a development machine with a customized `config.toml` could produce a different manifest than the gate on a clean checkout.

**What A4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`, `omaddons capabilities`) provides, as its bead specifies it** (and what this bead builds on, or creates first, below):

- `src/contract/commands.rs`, "the one place the CLI's inputs are extracted": `CommandInfo { path: &'static str, about, group, mutates, dictionary, exits, args: Vec<ArgInfo>, flags: Vec<FlagInfo>, aliases, stores_plan, binds, network }`, one per `COMMANDS` row, from the built tree (`Cli::command().build()`); `ArgInfo { id, value_name, required, multiple, default, values: Values, help, conflicts_with, requires }` (positionals, in index order); `FlagInfo { long, short, aliases, value_name, takes_value, multiple, default, values, conflicts_with, requires, global, help }` (the command's own flags in declaration order, then the propagated globals with `global: true`); `pub enum Values { Any, Words(Vec<&'static str>), DurationOrTime(&'static [DurationUnit]) }`; `pub fn commands() -> Vec<CommandInfo>` (in `COMMANDS` order), `pub fn command(path) -> Option<CommandInfo>`, `pub fn command_info(entry, cmd) -> CommandInfo`. Its rules: hidden arguments and hidden possible values are left out; the root-only `-V/--version` is not published; `--if-match` is listed only on binding paths (clap propagates it everywhere, but `cli::check_if_match` refuses it elsewhere); `values` is an `APP_VALIDATED` row's `ValueSet` (`Words` for actors, `DurationOrTime` for `--since`; `src/contract/values.rs`) when the flag has one, else clap's possible values, else `Any`; `conflicts_with` is the **symmetric closure** of clap's records (clap enforces conflicts both ways), each named by its long name or positional id; `requires` comes from `REQUIRES`.
- `pub const REQUIRES: &[Requirement]` with `pub struct Requirement { pub path: &'static str, pub long: &'static str, pub requires: &'static [&'static str] }`, empty at `c0ab5e9` (E6, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`, adds `doctor fix --force` → `yes`), and `pub fn requirement_violations(path, cmd, table) -> Vec<String>`, a behavioural probe: each flag is parsed alone (with samples for required positionals and its value); an undeclared `MissingRequiredArgument` is a violation, and so is a declared requirement under which the flag parses alone.
- `src/contract/mod.rs`: `pub struct Registry { pub commands: Vec<commands::CommandInfo>, … }` with `builtin()`, `build()` and `from_parts(…)`.
