### 3. The node model and the canonical form (subtask 1)

#### 3.1 Types

```rust
/// The node model's own version. Two manifests of different formats are never compared
/// fact by fact: the classifier reports the difference as one unclassified change.
pub const FORMAT: u32 = 1;

/// The semantic manifest (M4-D56): every fact of the contract a consumer can depend on.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Manifest { pub format: u32, pub nodes: BTreeMap<String, Node> }

/// One node: its kind (the classifier's routing) and its facts.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct Node {
    pub kind: String,                       // a NodeKind's wire name, or an unknown one read from a file
    #[serde(flatten)]
    pub facts: BTreeMap<String, Fact>,
}

/// A fact's value. Set-valued facts are sorted and deduplicated; an empty set is never
/// recorded (absence is the empty set); an absent boolean is false.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Serialize, Deserialize)]
#[serde(untagged)]
pub enum Fact { Bool(bool), Int(i64), Text(String), List(Vec<String>), Ints(Vec<i64>) }
```

- `Node.kind` is a `String`, not the enum, so a manifest read from a file written by a newer build keeps a node kind this build does not know, and the classifier labels its changes `unclassified` instead of failing to parse (the acceptance case "an unknown node kind"). `Node::kind()` returns `Option<NodeKind>`.
- `pub enum NodeKind` (with `ALL`, `wire()`, `from_wire()`), wire names in snake_case: `command`, `flag`, `positional`, `output_position`, `output_variant`, `file_kind`, `file_position`, `file_variant`, `config_key`, `desired_position`, `desired_variant`, `env_var`, `error_code`, `warning_code`, `action`, `failure_mode`, `event`, `phase`, `log_level`, `exit_code`, `doctor_op`.
- `pub mod fact` holds one `pub const` per fact name (`TYPES = "types"`, `REQUIRED = "required"`, …, the full list in TA 4.3, 5.1, 5.2, 6 and 7), so subtasks 2, 3 and 4 agree on spelling at compile time. No fact is named `kind` (it would collide with `Node.kind` under `flatten`).
- `Fact::list(items)` sorts and deduplicates; `Fact::ints(items)` likewise. Constructors return `None` for an empty input so a caller cannot record an empty set.
- The untagged order (`Bool`, `Int`, `Text`, `List`, `Ints`) makes every recorded value round-trip: a JSON array of strings is `List`, of integers `Ints`; empty arrays are never written.
- Integer facts are `i64`. A numeric schema bound that is not an `i64` (a fraction, or beyond `i64`) is recorded as `Text` holding its JSON number text, and the classifier treats a `Text` bound as unclassifiable when it changes.
- No serialized type in `src/contract/manifest*` holds `serde_json::Value` (A3's `OPAQUE` scan of `src/contract` would flag it), `HashMap` or `HashSet`.

#### 3.2 Node ids and paths

Every node has a string id whose first token is its **section**. Decided while writing this bead: these ids, because they are also the projection's leading tokens (readable diffs) and they make `parent(id)` computable without a schema.

| Node | Id | Kind |
|---|---|---|
| a command path: a clap path, a `COMMANDS` row, or an `ENVELOPE_ONLY` name | `command <path>`; the root is `command omaddons` | `command` |
| a flag of that path | `input <path> --<long>` (globals only under `input omaddons`) | `flag` |
| a positional | `input <path> @<index>` (clap's 1-based index) | `positional` |
| a command's data (rows and `ENVELOPE_ONLY`) | `output <path> data`, `output <path> data.items[].status`, … | `output_position`, `output_variant` |
| the envelope frame | `envelope .`, `envelope meta.elapsed_ms`, … | `output_position`, `output_variant` |
| an event | `event <name>` (registry); `event <name> .`, `event <name> phase`, … | `event`; `output_position`, `output_variant` |
| an error code | `error <code>` (registry); `error <code> .`, `error <code> details.changed[]`, … | `error_code`; `output_position`, `output_variant` |
| a persisted kind | `file <kind>`; `file <kind> .`, `file <kind> generation`, … | `file_kind`; `file_position`, `file_variant` |
| a `config.toml` key | `config <key>` (`config sources.*.enabled`) | `config_key` |
| `addons.toml` | `desired .`, `desired family`, `desired family.mainline.addon[].name`, … | `desired_position`, `desired_variant` |
| a `release` env var | `env <NAME>` | `env_var` |
| other registries | `warning <code>`, `action <name>`, `fm <id>`, `phase <name>`, `log-level <name>`, `exit general <n>`, `exit doctor <n>`, `doctor-ops <op>` | `warning_code`, `action`, `failure_mode`, `phase`, `log_level`, `exit_code`, `doctor_op` |

**Path syntax** (shared with A3's walk where they overlap: `a.b`, `a[]`, `a{}`):

- A position's path is its root token followed by segments. The root token is `data` for a command's data (it is the envelope key the data lives under, so paths read as in §0.3 of the plan: `output install data.items[].status`), and `.` for every other surface.
- Segments: `.key` for a property (for a `.`-rooted path the first key is written bare: `envelope meta`, not `envelope ..meta`); `[]` for array items; `[0]`, `[1]`, … for `prefixItems` positions; `{}` for map values; `<tag=value>` for a tagged variant; `<untagged=k1,k2>` for an untagged variant (TA 4.4).
- A key or tag value matching `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$` is written bare; any other is written as a JSON string (`."a.b"`, `<type="x y">`). Decided while writing this bead: the quoting rule, so no key can forge a segment.
- `ids::parent(id) -> Option<String>`: the id with its last segment removed; a surface root's parent is its anchor (`output <path> data` → `command <path>`, `event <name> .` → `event <name>`, `error <code> .` → `error <code>`, `file <kind> .` → `file <kind>`); an argument's parent is `command <path>`; `desired .`, `command omaddons` and registry nodes have none. The classifier (TA 8.2) and the renderer's folding (TA 8.6) use it.
- `ids::section(id) -> &str`: the first token.

#### 3.3 The canonical JSON

`pub fn render(&self, extra: &[(&str, &serde_json::Value)]) -> String` writes, exactly:

```text
{
  "format": 1,
  "nodes": {
    "action apply": {"destructive":false,"kind":"action"},
    "action undo": {"destructive":false,"kind":"action"},
    "command install": {"aliases":["add"],"binds":false,"dictionary":"general","exits":[0,1,2,3,4,5,6],"kind":"command","mutates":true,"network":"optional","stores_plan":false}
  }
}
```

- Top-level keys sorted (`format`, `nodes`, and any `extra` key such as H2's `header` or the baseline's `provenance`), one per line, two-space indent; each extra value compact on its line.
- `nodes`: one node per line, four-space indent, sorted by id (byte order), each node compact with sorted keys (serialize the `Node` to a `serde_json::Value` without `preserve_order`, whose maps sort, then `serde_json::to_string`). Commas between entries; one trailing newline at the end of the document.
- Decided while writing this bead: one node per line, because the golden is thousands of nodes and a line-per-node diff is what a reviewer reads (H2: "review the first commit by section counts and A10's report").
- `pub fn parse(text: &str) -> Result<Manifest, ParseError>` reads `format` and `nodes` and **ignores every other top-level key** (`header`, `provenance`): the comparison with the released baseline must not be switchable by anything written in a header (M4-D56), and it cannot be when the parser never keeps the header. It fails, naming the node id where it can, on: text that is not JSON; a missing or non-integer `format`; `nodes` not an object; a node that is not an object or has no string `kind`; a fact whose value is `null`, an object, a float, a mixed or empty array. `ParseError` is a plain error type (`thiserror`), not an omaddons `Error`: no command returns it.
- `Manifest::empty()` is `FORMAT` with no nodes (the report's empty baseline, the classifier's tests).

#### 3.4 Building

`pub fn build_checked(registry: &Registry) -> (Manifest, Vec<String>)` collects every section into a builder and returns the manifest with its **id conflicts**: an id produced twice with different facts or kinds (a normalizer bug, such as two branches producing one variant id). An identical duplicate is a no-op. `pub fn build(registry: &Registry) -> Manifest` returns the first half. Decided while writing this bead: conflicts are returned, not panicked on (no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!` outside tests) and not silently merged; a unit test asserts the real contract has none. `build` is infallible: anything a normalizer cannot model becomes a `keywords` fact (TA 4.7) that the classifier treats as unclassified, so no input can make it fail or panic.

|---|---|---|
| each `COMMANDS` row | `command_schema(entry)` | `output <path> data` |
| each `ENVELOPE_ONLY` name (`omaddons`, `version`) | `data_schema_for(name)` | `output <name> data` |
| the envelope frame | `envelope_schema()` | `envelope .` |
| each event | `event_schemas()[wire]` | `event <name> .` |
| each error code | `error_variant(code)` | `error <code> .` |
| each persisted kind except `desired_state` | `file_schemas()[kind]` | `file <kind> .` (kinds `file_position`, `file_variant`) |
| `addons.toml` | `file_schemas()["desired_state"]` | `desired .` (kinds `desired_position`, `desired_variant`) |

Decided while writing this bead: the `ENVELOPE_ONLY` names are recorded (their `command` values and data appear on the wire, and their exits are declared); `addons.toml` is recorded as an **input** (§6.7 step 2 lists "the `addons.toml` key paths" among inputs: users write it and `sync` reads it), so its positions take input-direction rules although A3 publishes its schema among the files. Every surface's schema comes from A3's functions, so each was generated with the serialize contract and a fresh generator.

The normalizer works on the root schema as a `serde_json::Value` (a local value, never a field of a serialized type), resolving `$ref`s against that root's `$defs`.

#### 4.2 The walk

- `properties` give `.<key>` positions; `items` gives `[]`; `prefixItems` give `[0]`, `[1]`, …; `additionalProperties` (when a schema) gives `{}`; `patternProperties` give `{}` (TA 4.5).
- `$ref: "#/$defs/<name>"` and `$ref: "#"` are resolved inline: the position takes the referenced schema's facts and children, merged with any sibling keywords (draft 2020-12 allows them) as `allOf` merges. **`$defs` names never appear** in an id or a fact.
- **An object reached by two routes is recorded once per route** (§6.7): a `$ref` used by two properties yields two full subtrees. This is what makes a field that changes under one route and not the other visible.
- **Recursion:** a `$defs` entry already being resolved on the current route is not entered again; the position gets `same_as: "<the ancestor's node id>"`. No recursive type is known in omaddons' outputs at `c0ab5e9`; the rule keeps the walk finite whatever a later type does.

#### 4.3 Facts per position

| Fact | Value | Recorded when |
|---|---|---|
| `types` | sorted list of `string`, `integer`, `number`, `boolean`, `object`, `array` (never `null`; integer and number distinct) | the position constrains its type (a `type` keyword, a `const`, an `enum`, or a union of them) |
| `nullable` | `true`/`false` | every non-root position: `true` when `null` is a type, an `enum`/`const` value, or an `anyOf`/`oneOf` branch `{"type":"null"}` |
| `required` | `true`/`false` | every property position: `true` when the key is in its object's `required` (after merging in-place branches) |
| `enum` | sorted list of the allowed values: a string value as itself, any other value as `json:<canonical JSON>` (`json:1`, `json:true`); a string beginning `json:` is written `json:"json:…"` | `enum` or `const` (const is an enum of one); `null` moves to `nullable` |
| `minimum`, `maximum`, `exclusive_minimum`, `exclusive_maximum`, `multiple_of` | `Int` (else `Text` of the JSON number) | the keyword is present |
| `min_items`, `max_items`, `min_length`, `max_length`, `min_properties`, `max_properties` | `Int` | the keyword is present |
| `pattern` | `Text` | the keyword is present (ULID ids carry one; A3 kept it as contract information) |
| `unique_items` | `true` | `uniqueItems: true` (sets) |
| `key_patterns` | sorted list | a map with `patternProperties` (TA 4.5) |
| `opaque` | `true` | the position is open (TA 4.6) |
| `tag` | the discriminating property's name | a tagged union position (TA 4.4) |
| `same_as` | a node id | recursion (TA 4.2) |
| `union_of` | `"error"` | the error union (TA 4.6) |
| `keywords` | sorted list of unmodelled keywords | TA 4.7 |

**Ignored, never recorded** (annotations and presentation, changes to which are not compatibility changes): `title`, `description`, `$comment`, `examples`, `default`, `deprecated`, `readOnly`, `writeOnly`, `format` (schemars' `uint64`, `int64`, `double` are annotations; the integer width shows in `minimum`/`maximum`), `$schema`, `$id`, `$anchor`, `additionalProperties: false` and `unevaluatedProperties: false` (closedness is a test-side property of A3's strict transform; published schemas are open). Decided while writing this bead: ignoring `format`, because a width change already changes a bound, and a `format` change alone (say `uint32` → `uint64` without a bound) cannot break a JSON consumer that reads integers.

Root positions (`data`, `.`) carry neither `required` nor `nullable` (they have no parent object); array, tuple and map value positions carry `nullable` but not `required`.

#### 4.4 Unions

At a position whose schema has `anyOf` or `oneOf` (after `$ref` resolution), the branches are sorted into three groups:

1. **Null branches** (`{"type":"null"}`) set `nullable: true`.
2. **Scalar branches** (no `object` type) merge into the position: `types` is the union of their types; `enum` is the union of their values when every scalar branch is enumerated (`const` or `enum`), and absent if any scalar branch is open (an open string absorbs the enumerated ones); a bound is kept only when every scalar branch carries the same one. This is how a doc-commented unit enum (`oneOf` of `const` strings) becomes one `enum` fact, and how `WarningCode`'s `anyOf` of the warning codes and the error codes (its untagged `Item` variant) becomes one string position whose `enum` is both sets.
3. **Object branches** become **variants**:
   - **Tagged:** a property `p` such that every object branch lists `p` in `required` and gives it a single string value (`const`, or a one-value `enum`), with distinct values across branches, is the tag. The position records `tag: "p"` and `types` gains `object`; each branch is the variant `<p=value>` (kind `output_variant`, no facts), and its properties are positions below it (`data.result<command=install>.items[]`). The tag property itself is not repeated inside the variant (the variant's id states it). If several properties qualify, the first in byte order is the tag and the others are recorded as ordinary single-value `enum` positions. If none qualifies at the top level, the tag is searched one level down (a required object `a` whose required `b` has a single string value): `apply`'s data, D5's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`) `oneOf` of complete wrappers, is discriminated by `applied.command`, giving `tag: "applied.command"` and variants `<applied.command=install>`, … (Decided while writing this bead: the dotted path, where the plan's illustration writes `<command=install>`, so a nested tag never reads as a top-level one). A union that is part tagged, part not, is treated as untagged.
   - **Untagged:** each branch is the variant `<untagged=k1,k2,…>`, named by its sorted `required` keys; if two branches share that name, by `<untagged=k1,k2|o1,o2>` (required keys, then optional ones); two identical branches are one variant. Decided while writing this bead: naming untagged variants by their keys, because there is no tag value and the `$defs` name may not be used; a field moving between untagged branches renames both variants, which the classifier then reports as a removal plus an addition, i.e. breaking, which is the conservative answer. Examples at `c0ab5e9`: `HelpData` (`src/app/help.rs:31`: `<untagged=commands,exit_codes,global_flags,name,usage,version>`, `<untagged=about,args,command,flags,usage>`, `<untagged=version>`), and the untagged types A3 listed for review (`src/app/adopt.rs:79`, `src/app/list.rs:122`, `src/backup/mod.rs:147`, `src/state/config.rs:142`, `:168`).
   - An externally tagged enum's data variants (one required property named after the variant) are untagged variants by this rule (`<untagged=Install>`); its unit variants are scalar branches.
4. **A field in two variants is recorded in each** (`…<type=a>.x` and `…<type=b>.x`), so moving a field between variants is a removal from one and an addition to the other.

#### 4.5 `allOf`, flatten and maps

- `allOf` branches (and `$ref` with sibling keywords) merge into one position: properties united, `required` united, `types` intersected (a branch without `type` does not constrain), `enum` intersected, the tighter of two bounds kept.
- An `allOf` branch that is itself a union contributes its variants at the position; two such unions (schemars wraps two flattened unions as `allOf: [{oneOf}, {oneOf}]`) contribute two variant sets side by side, each under its own tag (`<a=x>`, `<b=y>`). Decided while writing this bead: side-by-side variant sets, never their cross product, which would multiply the node count for no information.
- Maps: `additionalProperties: <schema>` gives the `{}` position. `patternProperties` whose values normalize identically give one `{}` position plus `key_patterns` (sorted) on the map's own node; differing values are recorded as `keywords: ["patternProperties"]` (unmodelled, TA 4.7). An enum-keyed map (schemars: one optional `properties` entry per enum value, `additionalProperties: false`) is recorded as those optional properties, which is exactly what it guarantees.

#### 4.6 Opaque positions, the error union

- **Open positions are opaque.** A position whose schema (or any in-place branch at it) is `true`, `{}`, or an object with `additionalProperties: true` or `unevaluatedProperties: true` gets `opaque: true`; for `true` and `{}` nothing is walked below it; for an open object with listed properties (a flattened map, such as `LeftOutFolder.details` at `src/model.rs:624-630`), the listed properties are still walked. A3's tests guarantee that the open positions are exactly `contract::OPAQUE`'s rows, so the manifest's `opaque` nodes are `OPAQUE`'s (§6.7: "`opaque` for a `contract::OPAQUE` subtree"); subtask 2 adds a test that the two agree.
- **The error union is recorded once per code, and referenced elsewhere.** Each code's variant is its own section (`error <code> .`, from `error_variant(code)`), as §6.7 asks ("each error code's variant"). Every other position whose union is *the error union* (the envelope's `error`, `TargetResult.error` in every multi-target command's data, any `Error` field) records `union_of: "error"` (plus its own `required`/`nullable`) and is not walked further. "The error union" is recognized structurally: a tagged union whose tag is `code` and whose tag values are exactly `ErrorCode::ALL`'s wire names, each variant normalizing exactly as that code's own section does. A union tagged by `code` that differs in any way (a subset of codes, an extra field) is walked in full like any union, so no difference can hide behind the reference. Decided while writing this bead: the reference, because recording the union per route would repeat every code's variant in every multi-target command (thousands of identical nodes) while adding no fact the `error` sections do not already pin.

#### 4.7 Unmodelled keywords

Any keyword not listed in TA 4.2–4.6 (for example `not`, `if`/`then`/`else`, `contains`, `dependentSchemas`, `propertyNames`, `unevaluatedItems`, `additionalItems`, a `$ref` that is not `#` or `#/$defs/…`, the boolean schema `false`, differing `patternProperties`) is recorded in the position's `keywords` list (its name; for a `$ref`, `$ref:<target>`), and the position is still walked as far as the modelled keywords allow. The classifier labels any change of `keywords` `unclassified`. A unit test asserts that the real contract carries no `keywords` fact at landing, so each future one is a deliberate review item. Decided while writing this bead: recording rather than failing, so `build` stays infallible and nothing is ever silently dropped.

### 5. Inputs (§6.7 step 2; subtask 3)

The inputs collector walks `Cli::command().build()` once, path by path (the root `omaddons`, every subcommand, every nested subcommand, pure parents such as `auth` included). For each path it takes the row facts from `contract::commands::command(path)` (A4's `CommandInfo`, for paths with a `COMMANDS` row), and the clap facts from `command_facts(cmd)` and `arg_facts(path, cmd, arg)` (TA 2).

#### 5.1 Command nodes

One `command <path>` node per built clap path, plus one per `ENVELOPE_ONLY` name that is no clap path (`version`):

| Fact | Value | From |
|---|---|---|
| `aliases` | sorted list of every alias clap accepts (`get_all_aliases()`, hidden ones included: they parse) | `command_facts` |
| `subcommand_required`, `args_conflict_with_subcommands` | `true` when set | `command_facts` |
| `exits` | sorted `Ints` | `CommandInfo.exits`, or `ENVELOPE_ONLY` (A1) |
| `dictionary` | `general` or `doctor` | `CommandInfo` |
| `mutates`, `stores_plan` | booleans, explicit | `CommandInfo` |
| `network` | `none`, `optional`, `required` | `CommandInfo` |
| `binds` | boolean, explicit | `CommandInfo.binds` (membership in `precondition::BINDING_COMMANDS`) |
| `envelope_only` | `true` | `ENVELOPE_ONLY` names (`omaddons` and `version`) |

A path without a `COMMANDS` row (a parent that cannot run bare) records no row facts. The root `command omaddons` carries both its clap facts and its `ENVELOPE_ONLY` facts (exits `[1, 2]`). Not recorded: `about`, help text, `after_long_help`, `group` and display order (presentation; `capabilities` publishes `group` as a value, and its shape is recorded through `capabilities`' data schema).

#### 5.2 Argument nodes

Globals are recorded **once**, under the root: `input omaddons --json` with `global: true`; the root-only `-V/--version` is `input omaddons --version` without `global`. A subcommand's nodes are only the arguments it declares itself (`is_global_set()` arguments are skipped there; `build()` propagates every global to every path uniformly, and clap rejects a local argument that shadows one). Decided while writing this bead: once, under the root, because a global flag's change is then one change and not one per path, and §6.7's "globals propagated" is satisfied by the `global` fact plus that uniformity; a unit test asserts every global is present on every built path. (`--if-match` is a global; where it binds is the `binds` fact of each command, which is exactly what `cli::check_if_match` enforces.)

Flags are identified by their long name (`input install --channel`); every omaddons flag has one. A flag without a long name, if one is ever added, is identified as `input <path> -<short>`. Positionals are identified by clap's 1-based index (`input install @1`), with their value name as a presentation fact. Decided while writing this bead: index identity for positionals, because a positional's name is help text only (renaming `<REF>` to `<ADDON>` changes nothing that parses and must not demand a bump), while its position is what an argv depends on.

Hidden arguments and hidden possible values are recorded (they parse; `capabilities` leaves them out as help does; none exist at `c0ab5e9`).

| Fact | Value | From (`arg_facts`, on the built tree) |
|---|---|---|
| `short` | `-c` | `get_short()` |
| `short_aliases` | sorted list | `get_all_short_aliases()` |
| `aliases` | sorted long aliases (`flavor` for `-t`) | `get_all_aliases()` |
| `grammar` | `flag` (`SetTrue`, `SetFalse`, `Help*`, `Version`), `count` (`Count`), `enum` (`Values::Words`), `duration_or_time` (`Values::DurationOrTime`), `path` (`PathBuf`, `OsString`), `integer` (`u8`…`u64`, `usize`, `i8`…`i64`, `isize`), `string` (`String`), else `other` | `get_action()`, `values_of`, `get_value_parser().type_id()` compared with `TypeId::of::<T>()` |
| `values` | sorted: the words (with each clap possible value's aliases), or a `DurationOrTime` set's unit suffixes (`d`, `h`, `m`, `w`) | `values_of` (clap's `get_possible_values()` with `get_name_and_aliases()`, or the `APP_VALIDATED` set) |
| `ignore_case` | `true` | `is_ignore_case_set()` |
| `default` | the recorded default values joined by `,` (after `build()` clap gives `SetTrue` flags `false` and `Count` `0`); absent when none | `get_default_values()` |
| `arity_min`, `arity_max` | `Int`; `arity_max` absent when unbounded | `get_num_args()` (`min_values()`, `max_values()`; `usize::MAX` means unbounded) |
| `repeat` | `true` | action `Append` or `Count` |
| `required` | boolean, explicit | `is_required_set()` |
| `global` | `true` | root arguments with `is_global_set()` |
| `conflicts` | sorted identities (`--last-by`, `@1`), **symmetric** | `conflicts_of` (the closure `command_info` publishes), renamed from long names and positional ids to identities |
| `requires` | sorted identities | `requires_of` (`REQUIRES`, TA 5.3) |
| `action` | `set`, `append`, `set_true`, `set_false`, `count`, `help`, `help_short`, `help_long`, `version` | `get_action()` |
| `value_name` | `REF` | positionals only; presentation, never compared |
| `env` | the variable name | `get_env()`, when set |
| `allow_hyphen_values`, `allow_negative_numbers`, `trailing_var_arg`, `require_equals`, `exclusive`, `last` | `true` | the matching `is_*_set()`, when set |
| `value_delimiter` | the character | `get_value_delimiter()`, when set |

- **The grammar** decided while writing this bead: a closed vocabulary from `Values` and `TypeId` comparison, because clap exposes no stable parser name in release builds (`AnyValueId` debug-prints only a `TypeId` there). An argument whose parser is none of the listed types is `other`, and the classifier treats a change involving `other` as unclassified. **Ranges** are not recorded: no omaddons argument uses a ranged parser at `c0ab5e9`, and clap does not expose a range's bounds; a later leaf that adds one declares the bounds beside the parser and records them as `minimum`/`maximum` facts on the argument (that leaf's change, with the classifier's existing bound rules).
- **The app-validated flags** (`--actor`, `--by`, `--last-by`, `--since`): `values_of` returns A4's `ValueSet` for them, so the manifest records `enum` with the actor words and `duration_or_time` with the units, as A4's bead expects ("A10 records the grammar itself from `Values::DurationOrTime`"). Before A4 lands they are what clap says (`string`; `enum` for `undo --last-by`), and A4's later sets reach the manifest through the shared helper without a change here.
- **Conflicts are symmetric** because clap enforces them both ways: `undo @1` lists `--last-by` and `--run`; `undo --run` lists `--last-by` and `@1`.

#### 5.3 Requirements: `REQUIRES`

clap 4.6.7 keeps an argument's requirements private (`Arg::requires` is `pub(crate)`), so they are declared: A4's `REQUIRES` table (`Requirement { path, long, requires }`, empty at `c0ab5e9`; E6 adds `doctor fix --force` → `yes`) held true by A4's behavioural probe `requirement_violations` (every flag parsed alone: an undeclared `MissingRequiredArgument` fails, and so does a declared requirement the flag parses without), run over every `COMMANDS` path by A4's unit test `requirements_are_declared_and_true`. The manifest records `requires` from it through `requires_of`.

- If A4 has not landed when subtask 3 starts, subtask 3 adds `Requirement`, `REQUIRES` (empty), `requirement_violations` and that unit test exactly as described (whichever of A4 and this bead lands first).
- **Default-missing values are private too** (`default_missing_vals`), and no argument uses one. A source scan (unit test over the production code of `src/`) refuses `default_missing_value`/`default_missing_values` outright: "clap keeps default-missing values private, so the manifest cannot record them: declare them beside the argument in a `contract::commands` table first". A leaf that needs one adds that table and its manifest fact (an `equal` rule) in the same commit. Decided while writing this bead.

#### 5.4 `config.toml` keys

One `config <key>` node per `state::config::KEYS` row (`*` patterns kept as written), with `config_type: <KeyKind::name()>`. `KeyKind::name(self) -> &'static str` is added in `src/state/config.rs` (`path_list`, `text`, `channel`, `running_policy`, `auto_backup`, `hours`, `host_list`, `count`, `size`, `mebibytes`, `bool`, `credential`, `family`, `rules_field`), with a unit test that the names are distinct, snake case, and cover every variant through an exhaustive `match`. ### 8. The classifier (subtask 4)

#### 8.1 API

```rust
pub fn classify(baseline: &Manifest, current: &Manifest) -> Changes;

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Changes { pub changes: Vec<Change>, pub kinds: Vec<KindBump> }   // sorted by (node, fact); kinds by kind

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Change {
    pub node: String,                 // the node id
    pub kind: ChangeKind,             // Added | Removed | Changed
    pub fact: Option<String>,         // the fact, for Changed
    pub before: Option<String>,       // a rendered value or fact summary
    pub after: Option<String>,
    pub label: Label,                 // Additive | Breaking | Unclassified
    pub rule: &'static str,           // why, one phrase: "output field removed"
    pub persisted: Option<String>,    // the persisted kind this change belongs to, if any
}

pub enum Label { Additive, Breaking, Unclassified }
pub enum Bump { None, Minor, Major }   // ordered

pub struct KindBump {
    pub kind: String,
    pub baseline: Option<String>,     // version strings as recorded
    pub current: Option<String>,
    pub required: Bump,
    pub satisfied: bool,
}

impl Changes {
    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool;
    pub fn wire_bump(&self) -> Bump;               // over changes with persisted == None
    pub fn unsatisfied_kinds(&self) -> Vec<&KindBump>;
    pub fn counts(&self) -> (usize, usize, usize); // additive, breaking, unclassified
    pub fn render(&self) -> String;
}

impl Bump {
    /// Whether moving from `baseline` to `current` carries this bump: Major needs a higher
    /// major; Minor a higher minor in the same major, or a higher major; None anything.
    pub fn is_satisfied(self, baseline: SchemaVersion, current: SchemaVersion) -> bool;
}
```

- `classify` reads only `format` and `nodes`: a header cannot reach it (TA 3.3).
- **Member order is never compared**: nodes are a sorted map and every set fact is a sorted list, so reordering a struct's fields, an enum's variants, a command's aliases or the `COMMANDS` table changes no byte (acceptance case "reordered members").
- **Different formats:** when `baseline.format != current.format`, the result is one `unclassified` change on the node id `format` (rule "manifest format changed; a migration of the older format is needed to compare"), and nothing else. Decided while writing this bead: one unclassified change rather than an error, so the signature stays the plan's and the answer stays "breaking, pending review". Changing the node model after the tag therefore requires a `migrate(old) -> Manifest` function here, tested, never an edit of the released baseline.
- `classify` is total and pure: it never panics, reads nothing else, and returns the same result for the same inputs.

#### 8.2 Nodes added, removed, re-kinded

| Kind | Added | Removed |
|---|---|---|
| `output_position`, `output_variant` | additive | breaking |
| `command` | additive | breaking |
| `flag`, `positional` | additive; **breaking** when it is `required` and its command existed in the baseline | breaking |
| `desired_position` | additive; **breaking** when it is `required` and its parent existed in the baseline | breaking |
| `desired_variant` | additive | breaking |
| `config_key`, `env_var` | additive | breaking |
| `error_code`, `warning_code`, `action`, `failure_mode`, `event`, `phase`, `log_level`, `exit_code`, `doctor_op`, `file_kind` | additive | breaking |
| `file_position`, `file_variant` | additive, persisted (TA 8.4) | breaking, persisted (TA 8.4) |
| an unknown kind | unclassified | unclassified |

A node whose kind differs between the two manifests is one `unclassified` change. Decided while writing this bead: a required argument or `addons.toml` key added **together with its parent** is additive (a new command's required positional breaks no existing invocation; a new optional table's required key breaks no existing file), which is the only refinement over "a new requirement is breaking".

#### 8.3 Facts changed

A fact is compared only when a node exists on both sides. An absent boolean is `false`; an absent set is empty; an absent bound or text is "none". The rule shapes:

| Rule | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **more is additive** (set) | elements added → additive; removed → breaking |
| **more is breaking** (set) | elements added → breaking; removed → additive |
| **true is additive** (bool) | false → true additive; true → false breaking |
| **true is breaking** (bool) | false → true breaking; true → false additive |
| **lower bound, output** | raised or added → additive; lowered or removed → breaking |
| **upper bound, output** | lowered or added → additive; raised or removed → breaking |
| **lower bound, input** | raised or added → breaking; lowered or removed → additive |
| **upper bound, input** | lowered or added → breaking; raised or removed → additive |
| **pattern, output** | added → additive; removed → breaking; changed → unclassified |
| **pattern, input** | added → breaking; removed → additive; changed → unclassified |
| **added is additive** (text) | none → value additive; value → none or another value breaking |
| **equal** | any change breaking |
| **grammar** | to `string` from `enum`, `duration_or_time`, `path` or `integer` → additive; from `string` to anything else → breaking; any other change (between non-`string` kinds, `other` included, or from `other` to `string`) → unclassified |
| **types, output** | a type not in the baseline → breaking, except `integer` where the baseline has `number`; a type removed → additive |
| **types, input** | a type added → additive; a type removed → breaking, except `integer` where the current has `number` |
| **presentation** | never a change |
| **unclassifiable** | any change unclassified |

Which rule applies to which fact:

| Kinds | Fact | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| output positions (`output_position`, and `file_position` under TA 8.4) | `types` | types, output |
| | `required` | true is additive (an optional field made always present is additive) |
| | `nullable`, `opaque` | true is breaking |
| | `enum` | more is additive (consumers tolerate unknown values; removing one is breaking); an `enum` fact that disappears (the field became an open string) → breaking, one that appears → additive |
| | `minimum`, `exclusive_minimum`, `min_items`, `min_length`, `min_properties` | lower bound, output |
| | `maximum`, `exclusive_maximum`, `max_items`, `max_length`, `max_properties` | upper bound, output |
| | `pattern` | pattern, output |
| | `unique_items` | true is additive |
| | `key_patterns` | more is breaking |
| | `tag`, `same_as`, `union_of` | equal |
| | `multiple_of` | unclassifiable |
| `desired_position` | `types` | types, input |
| | `required` | true is breaking |
| | `nullable`, `opaque` | true is additive |
| | `enum`, `key_patterns` | more is additive (an `enum` fact that disappears → additive, one that appears → breaking) |
| | lower and upper bounds | lower bound, input; upper bound, input |
| | `pattern` | pattern, input |
| | `unique_items` | true is breaking |
| | `tag`, `same_as` | equal |
| `command` | `aliases`, `exits` | more is additive |
| | `binds`, `stores_plan` | true is additive |
| | `subcommand_required`, `args_conflict_with_subcommands` | true is breaking |
| | `dictionary`, `network`, `mutates`, `envelope_only` | equal (an agent decides whether to preview, and whether it may go offline, by these) |
| `flag`, `positional` | `values`, `aliases`, `short_aliases` | more is additive |
| | `conflicts`, `requires` | more is breaking |
| | `repeat`, `ignore_case`, `global`, `allow_hyphen_values`, `allow_negative_numbers`, `trailing_var_arg` | true is additive |
| | `required`, `require_equals`, `exclusive`, `last` | true is breaking |
| | `arity_min` | lower bound, input |
| | `arity_max` | upper bound, input (absent = unbounded, so becoming unbounded is "removed" = additive) |
| | `short`, `env` | added is additive |
| | `default`, `value_delimiter` | equal (a changed default is breaking, M4-D56) |
| | `grammar` | grammar |
| | `action` | unclassifiable |
| | `value_name` | presentation |
| `config_key` | `config_type` | equal |
| `env_var` | `mirrors` | equal |
| `error_code` | `exit`, `doctor_exit`, `retryable` | equal; `doctor_exit` appearing where it was absent (E3 landing) → additive |
| `action` | `destructive` | equal |
| `exit_code` | `name`, `retryable` | equal |
| `file_kind` | `version` | consumed by TA 8.4; lowered → breaking; raised → no change of its own |
| any kind | `keywords` | unclassifiable |
| any kind | a fact not in this table for that kind | unclassifiable |

Each `Change` carries a `rule` phrase naming the rule that fired ("output field removed", "output type widened", "flag became required", "default changed", "unknown fact", …), so a reviewer never has to reverse-engineer a label.

#### 8.4 Persisted kinds

- Every change on a `file <kind> …` position or variant is labelled by the output rules (a persisted file is output that a later reader, possibly an older build, reads) and carries `persisted: Some(kind)`. It never counts toward `wire_bump()`.
- For each kind with persisted changes, `KindBump.required` is `Major` when any of them is breaking or unclassified, else `Minor`. `satisfied` is `required.is_satisfied(baseline version, current version)`; versions that do not parse as `SchemaVersion` make `satisfied` false.
- Decided while writing this bead: additive → a higher minor, breaking → a higher major, because that is the rule omaddons' readers already apply (README: a journal of a newer minor version and unknown fields is recovered as usual; one of a newer major is `journal_too_new` and never acted on; `store` reads a newer file only if it still decodes, and never writes it). H2's comparison fails on `unsatisfied_kinds()` with the kind, its versions and the bump it needs.
- A kind present on one side only is a `file_kind` addition or removal (a wire change, TA 8.2); its positions are reported as persisted changes without a `KindBump` (a new kind needs no bump of its own).

#### 8.5 The wire bump

`wire_bump()` over every change with `persisted == None`: `Major` if any is breaking or unclassified ("`unclassified` counts as breaking pending review", §6.7), else `Minor` if any is additive, else `None`. H2 compares it with `output::SCHEMA_VERSION` against the baseline's version through `Bump::is_satisfied`.

#### 8.6 Rendering

`Changes::render()` groups by label, breaking first:

```text
breaking (2):
  - input install --channel  enum (alpha|beta|stable), arity 1..1  (flag removed)
  ~ output install data.items[].size  types: integer -> number  (output type widened)
unclassified (1):
  ~ input install --file  grammar: path -> integer  (grammar changed)
additive (1):
  + output install data.items[].size_bytes  integer, required, minimum 0
persisted file target_record (1.3 -> 1.3) needs a minor bump (1 change):
  + file target_record installed_by  string, required
```

- `+` added, `-` removed, `~` changed. An added or removed node prints its facts summary (types joined by `|`, then `required`, `nullable`, bounds as `minimum 0`, `enum (a|b)`, `opaque`; for arguments the grammar, values, arity and markers), matching the plan's §4.8 example line `+ output install data.items[].size_bytes  integer, required, minimum 0`.
- Changes below a node that was itself added or removed fold into its line as `(and N nodes below)`, so a removed command reads as one line; `Changes.changes` keeps every change.
- H2 writes the surrounding message (the baseline's version and tag, the required `schema_version`, the regeneration command and the vision-comment duty, §4.8 of the plan).

### 9. The readable projection (`contract::wire::names`; subtask 5)

`pub fn names(manifest: &Manifest) -> Vec<String>`: one line per name, sorted bytewise, deduplicated, generated only from the manifest (H2 writes them under its two header lines). The section word leads every line, so sorting groups sections. Decided while writing this bead: the exact forms below, following §6.7's list; `<surface>` is the command path for command data (it may contain a space; the path that follows always starts with `data`), and `envelope`, `event:<name>`, `error:<code>`, `file:<kind>` or `desired` otherwise.

| Line | From |
|---|---|
| `command <path> aliases=<a,…> exits=<n,…> dictionary=<d> mutates=<b> binds=<b> stores_plan=<b> network=<n>[ subcommand_required][ args_conflict_with_subcommands][ envelope_only]` (absent facts omitted) | `command` |
| `input <path> --<long> <grammar>[(<v|…>)] default=<v> arity=<min>..<max> [repeat] [required] [global] [ignore_case] [short=-c] [aliases=…] [conflicts=…] [requires=…] [<other set switches>]` (`arity=1..` when unbounded; `default=` empty when none) | `flag` |
| `input <path> @<i> <<VALUE_NAME>> <grammar>…` (same tokens) | `positional` |
| `output <command path> <path> <types>[?][!][ <bound>=<v>…][ ref=<same_as or union_of>][ tag=<p>]` (`?` nullable, `!` required, `variant` for a variant node) | command data positions |
| `envelope <path> <types>[?][!]…` | envelope positions |
| `enum <surface> <path> <v,…>`; `opaque <surface> <path>` | the `enum` and `opaque` facts of any output or desired position |
| `event <name> <path:types[?][!],…>` (every position of the event, one line) | `event` and its positions |
| `error <code> exit=<n> doctor_exit=<n> retryable=<true|false|conditional> details=<path:types[?][!],…>` (every position under `details`) | `error_code` and its positions |
| `file <kind> <version>`; `file <kind> <path> <types>[?][!]…` | `file_kind` and its positions |
| `config <key> <type>`; `desired <path> <types>[?][!]…`; `env <NAME>[ mirrors=<flag>]` | inputs |
| `warning <code>`; `action <name> destructive=<b>`; `fm <id>`; `phase <name>`; `log-level <name>`; `exit general <n> <name>[ retryable=<b>]`; `exit doctor <n> <name>`; `doctor-ops <op>` | registries |
| `unknown <id> <fact>=<value>…` | a node of an unknown kind (read from a file) |

The error frame's own positions (`code`, `message`, `fix`, `fix_argv`, `alternatives`, `retryable`) are pinned by the manifest under every `error <code>` section but are not printed per code (they are generated identically for every code by A3's `error_variant`); `envelope error object! ref=error` points at them.

### 10. The report and instance matching (subtask 5)

- `pub fn section_counts(manifest: &Manifest) -> BTreeMap<String, usize>`: nodes per section word, plus derived counts (`commands with data`, `error codes`, `events`, `file kinds`, `flags`, `positionals`). H1's inventory compares its counts with these when this bead has landed.
- `pub fn report(current: &Manifest, baseline: Option<&Manifest>) -> String`: the format version and node total; a two-column table of `section_counts`; the classification against `baseline` (or `Manifest::empty()` when `None`): its `counts()`, `wire_bump()`, `unsatisfied_kinds()` and, for a real baseline, `Changes::render()`. Against the empty baseline every node is new (required arguments of new commands are additive by TA 8.2), which is the sanity check §6.7's report asks for. T2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.2`) calls `report(&build(&Registry::builtin()), None)` for its demo item "the manifest's report prints".
- `pub fn unmatched(manifest: &Manifest, anchor: &str, instance: &serde_json::Value) -> Vec<String>`: walks an observed JSON value from the node `anchor` (`output install data`, `envelope .`, `event progress .`, `error plan_stale .`) and returns every instance path with no manifest node, in the manifest's path syntax. At an object, each key `k` must be a child `.k` (or a `{}` map position); at an array, `[]` or `[n]`; at a tagged union, the instance's tag value selects `<tag=value>` (an unknown tag value is itself unmatched); at an untagged union, the first variant (in id order) under which the whole sub-instance matches; at `opaque`, everything below matches; at `union_of: "error"`, matching continues at `error <instance.code> .`; at `same_as`, at the named node. It checks paths, not values (A3's validation checks values). H2 reuses it for its observed-keys check (§6.4 of the plan: every key path the contract suite observes in `data` appears in the manifest).

### 12. What does not change, and what not to do

- No command, flag, envelope, `data` key, error, warning, action, event or file changes. No `.snap` file changes. If A4 has landed, `capabilities --json` is byte-identical before and after (its contract snapshot does not move).
- Nothing is committed under `tests/contract/` but test code: `manifest.json`, `wire_names.txt` and `released/` are H2's and H6's. The report test writes only under `CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR`.
- Do not read a `$defs` name to recognize a type (the error union is recognized structurally); do not use `serde_json/preserve_order`; do not add a `HashMap`/`HashSet` to the manifest modules (iteration order would differ per process); do not read the environment, a file, the clock or `config.toml` in `manifest*` or `wire.rs`.
- Do not change A3's schema functions to suit the manifest; if a schema cannot be normalized faithfully, record `keywords` and file the shape as found work against A3's surface.
- No constant goes to `src/limits.rs`: `manifest::FORMAT` is a format version and lives with its format, as `output::SCHEMA_VERSION` and `journal::CURRENT` do; this bead adds no safety limit or politeness constant (common rule 7 has nothing to register). It reads no untrusted or user-sized input (the schemas are generated from the code, and `parse` reads repository files the updater wrote), so common rule 15 adds no bound.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `contract::manifest::build(&Registry) -> Manifest` records the four parts of §6.7: **outputs** (every `COMMANDS` row's data, both `ENVELOPE_ONLY` names' data, the envelope frame, every event, every error code's variant with its typed `details`), **inputs** (every clap path with its aliases and row facts, every flag and positional with its facts, every `config.toml` key with its type, every `addons.toml` path), **registries** (error codes with exit and tri-state retryability, warning codes, actions, events, phases, log levels, the general exit dictionary, `release` env vars; and failure-mode ids, the doctor dictionary with each code's `doctor_exit` and doctor ops when their registries exist), and **persisted formats** (every `store::KINDS` row and the folder journal, each with its version and normalized schema).
- [ ] The manifest is deterministic: two builds give byte-identical canonical JSON, also when built on different threads; `Manifest::parse(&m.render(&[]))` equals `m`; the layout is the one of TA 3.3 (sorted top-level keys, one node per line sorted by id, compact sorted node objects, one trailing newline).
- [ ] The manifest is independent of `$defs` naming and of documentation: a test renames a type with `#[schemars(rename = …)]` and another edits a doc comment, and each sees no change; no node id or fact contains a `$defs` name.
- [ ] Outputs keep the distinctions M4-D56 requires: integer and number distinct; `required` and `nullable` as separate facts; bounds (`minimum`, `maximum`, `minItems`, `maxItems`, `pattern`, …) recorded; enum values recorded; tagged variants recorded under their tag value with their own fields; an object reached by two routes recorded once per route; open positions recorded as `opaque`, and the opaque nodes agree with `contract::OPAQUE`; the error union recorded once per code and referenced (`union_of: "error"`) from every other position that holds it.
- [ ] Every `COMMANDS` path, flag and positional appears in the manifest with its facts (aliases, exits, dictionary, mutates, binds, stores plan, network; long and short names and aliases, default, grammar and values, arity, repeatability, requiredness, globality, conflicts and requirements), checked by an independent walk of `Cli::command().build()`, and against `omaddons help <path> --json` for every path end to end.
- [ ] Every key path of the live envelopes, `data`, error `details` and stderr events produced by the end-to-end scenario is located in the manifest (`unmatched` returns nothing), on a home with clients, with `assert_private_all` over every step's stdout and stderr with `--progress json`.
- [ ] The classifier's unit tests, over synthetic manifests, label each case correctly: added and removed output fields; optional, nullable, integer-to-number and bound changes (each direction); variant additions, removals and moves; enum values added and removed; added and removed flags, values and aliases; changed defaults; new conflicts and requirements; a required positional (and one added with its new command, additive); grammar, arity, repeatability and globality changes; command facts; config keys, `addons.toml` keys and env vars in input direction; registry changes; an unknown node kind and an unknown fact (unclassified); a persisted-format change (kind rule: a minor or major bump of that kind, satisfied or not, never a wire bump); a format mismatch (one unclassified change); reordered members and a differing header (no change).
- [ ] Property tests hold: classifying a manifest against itself is empty; render then parse round-trips; shuffled insertion and list order give identical bytes; for every monotone fact rule, a change labelled additive one way is labelled breaking the other way.
- [ ] `Changes::wire_bump()`, `unsatisfied_kinds()` and `Bump::is_satisfied` give the bumps of TA 8.4–8.5, and `Changes::render()` prints TA 8.6's form, folding changes below an added or removed node.

- `every_command_and_envelope_only_name_has_data`, `every_event_and_error_code_has_its_positions`, `every_persisted_kind_has_positions`, `desired_state_is_recorded_as_input` (its nodes are `desired_*`), `envelope_error_and_target_errors_reference_the_error_sections` (on the real contract: `envelope error` has `union_of: "error"`; so does every `…targets[].error`), `opaque_nodes_agree_with_contract_opaque` (every `opaque` node is matched by an `OPAQUE` row, by scope then path with `**.` matching at any depth, and every row matches at least one node), `real_contract_has_no_unmodelled_keyword`, `real_contract_has_no_id_conflict`.

**`src/contract/manifest/inputs.rs`, `registries.rs`, `src/contract/commands.rs`, `src/state/config.rs`** (subtask 3):

- `every_commands_path_flag_and_positional_appears_with_its_facts`: an independent walk of `Cli::command().build()` (not through `CommandInfo`) asserts, for every path, a `command` node with the row's `exits`, `dictionary`, `mutates`, `stores_plan`, `network` and `binds`, and for every argument a node with clap's default, arity, requiredness, repeatability, globality, short name and aliases, values and `ignore_case`.
- `globals_are_recorded_once_on_the_root`: 16 `global` flags under `input omaddons`, `--version` without `global`, and no `input <path> --json` for any other path; every global is present on every built path (asserted on clap's tree).
- `grammar_kinds`, cases: `json_is_flag` (`--json`: `flag`, default `false`, arity 0..0), `verbose_is_count` (`-v`: `count`, `repeat`), `format_is_enum_ignoring_case` (`--format`: `enum` `human,json`, `ignore_case`), `channel_is_enum` (`install --channel`: `alpha,beta,stable`), `target_has_alias` (`--target`: `string`, `short=-t`, `aliases=flavor`), `install_file_is_path`, `sync_file_positional_is_path_and_optional`, `net_log_limit_is_integer`, `install_refs_are_required_repeatable` (`install @1`: `string`, `required`, `repeat`, arity `1..`), `help_command_positional_is_optional` (`help @1`), `auth_service_values` (A1's `auth github` shape: its action values), `last_by_is_enum` (`undo --last-by`: `agent,human,widget`), and, once A4's value sets exist, `actor_is_enum` (`input omaddons --actor`) and `since_is_duration_or_time` (`input history --since`: values `d,h,m,w`).
- `conflicts_are_symmetric`, cases: `undo_tx` (`@1`: `--last-by`, `--run`), `undo_run` (`--last-by`, `@1`), `install_any_flavor`, `status_deep`, `backup_create_auto`, `backup_prune_keep` (`@1`), `errors_args_conflict_with_subcommands` (the command fact).
- `manifest_requires_equal_the_requires_table` (every `REQUIRES` row appears as the `requires` fact of its flag, and no other flag has one); A4's `requirements_are_declared_and_true` and `requirement_violations_finds_each_fault`, added here only if A4 has not landed; `default_missing_scan_catches_planted_text` (a synthetic text with `default_missing_value = "x"` is flagged; a commented one and a string literal are not) and `no_argument_sets_a_default_missing_value` (the scan over `src/`).
- `key_kind_names_are_distinct_snake_case_and_total`; `every_config_key_has_its_node` (23 nodes at `c0ab5e9`, each with its `config_type`).
- `every_error_code_has_its_node` (exit, `retryable` equal to `retryability()`'s wire form, `doctor_exit` when E3 has landed), `every_warning_code_action_event_phase_and_log_level_has_its_node`, `general_exit_dictionary_is_recorded` (7 nodes, names and retryability), `only_release_env_vars_are_recorded` (every `release` row, with its `mirrors`; no `debug` or `harness` name), `failure_modes_are_recorded` and `doctor_dictionary_is_recorded` (each when its registry exists), `every_kinds_row_and_the_journal_has_a_file_node` (count `KINDS.len() + 1`, versions equal), `persisted_versions_cover_every_file_schema`.

**`src/contract/manifest/classify.rs`** (subtask 4):

- `classifies_each_case`: one row per case, a synthetic baseline and current (a small builder `m(&[(id, kind, &[(fact, value)])])`), and the expected `(node, fact, label)` list and `wire_bump()`. The full case list is in subtask 4's Test Plan (about 70 cases covering every row of TA 8.2 and 8.3, the persisted rule and the meta cases).
- `bump_is_satisfied`, cases: `none_any`, `minor_needs_higher_minor` (1.0→1.1 yes, 1.0→1.0 no), `major_satisfies_minor` (1.3→2.0), `major_needs_higher_major` (1.0→1.9 no, 1.0→2.0 yes), `lower_never_satisfies`.
- `render_groups_labels_and_folds_children`: a removed command with three arguments renders as one `-` line with `(and 3 nodes below)`; an added field renders the plan's §4.8 line exactly.
- Property tests (`proptest`): `classify_identity_is_empty`, `render_parse_round_trip`, `order_never_matters`, `monotone_rules_reverse`.

**`src/contract/wire.rs`, `report.rs`, `locate.rs`** (subtask 5):

- `names_formats_each_node_kind`: one synthetic node per kind → its exact line.
- `names_are_sorted_unique_and_deterministic`; `names_of_unknown_kind_are_printed`.
- `section_counts_match_a_synthetic_manifest`; `report_against_empty_baseline_counts_every_node`; `report_against_a_baseline_renders_changes`.
- `unmatched_cases`: `object_keys`, `array_items`, `map_values`, `tagged_variant`, `unknown_tag_value`, `untagged_variant`, `opaque_subtree`, `error_union_jumps_to_code`, `same_as_recursion`, `missing_key_reported_with_path`.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

**`tests/contract/manifest_report.rs`** (subtask 6; `mod manifest_report;` in `tests/contract/main.rs`), test `manifest_report`:

1. Build the manifest (`build_checked(&Registry::builtin())`) on the test thread and on two spawned threads; assert the three canonical texts are byte-identical and there are no id conflicts.
2. Assert `parse(render) == manifest`.
3. Assert section counts against the registries, computed independently: `command` = built clap paths + `ENVELOPE_ONLY` names that are no clap path; `error` registry nodes = `ErrorCode::ALL.len()`; `warning` = `WarningCode::ALL.len()`; `action` = `Action::ALL.len()`; `event` registry nodes = `EventName::ALL.len()`; `phase`, `log-level`; `exit general` = `Exit::ALL.len()`; `env` = `ENV_VARS` release rows; `file` kind nodes = `KINDS.len() + 1`; `config` = `KEYS.len()`; `output <path> data` roots = `COMMANDS.len() + ENVELOPE_ONLY.len()`.
4. Print `report(&manifest, None)`.
5. If `<CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR>/contract-manifest/manifest.json` exists from an earlier run, parse it (a failure is printed as a note, never a test failure), and print `report(&manifest, Some(&previous))`: a developer runs the test before and after a change and reads that change's semantic diff.
6. Write `manifest.json`, `wire_names.txt` and `report.txt` there (each to a temporary name, then renamed), and print their paths.

**`tests/e2e_manifest.rs`** (subtask 6; picked up by `argc e2e`):

- `help_json_agrees_with_the_manifest_inputs` on `TestEnv::new()`: `help --json` (bare: every `global_flags[]` name is `input omaddons --<name>`, global except `version`; every `commands[]` is a `command` node with its aliases), then `help <path> --json` for every `COMMANDS` path: every `flags[]` entry is a flag node of that path or a global, with the same short name, and `takes_value` exactly when its grammar is neither `flag` nor `count`; every `args[i]` is `@<i+1>` with the same `required`; and conversely every non-global flag and positional node of the path appears in help's output.
- `live_envelopes_are_in_the_manifest` on `Home::new(&["wow", "wow_classic"])`, every step with `--json --offline --progress json`: reads that succeed (`targets`, `status`, `list`, `history`, `config`, `config path`, `net-log`, `backup list`, `errors`, `help`, `help install`, `-V`), and failures with `details` (`targets rm nosuch`, `info nosuchaddon`, `install x -t nosuch`, `undo 01ZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZ`, `--frobnicate`): for each, `unmatched` from `envelope .` over the whole envelope (the error through `union_of`), from `output <command> data` over `data` when present, and from `event <name> .` over every stderr line, are all empty; `assert_private_all` holds on every step.

Both scenarios are detailed, step by step, in subtask 6.

### Logging

- Unit tests: case names and assertion messages as above; the classifier's failures print the case name, both manifests' relevant nodes and the full `Changes::render()`.
- `manifest_report`: through `TestLog` (`tlog!()`): `log.step("build")`, `log.json("section_counts", …)`, `log.note(<report text>)`, `log.json("previous_run", {path, parsed, changes: counts})`, `log.note(<artifact paths>)`. The printed report is the review aid H2 asks for.
- `tests/e2e_manifest.rs`: every command through `log.run` (argv, exit, envelope, stderr events, timing recorded by T1's log); one `log.step` per command path or per read; before each assertion, `log.json("unmatched", {anchor, paths})` or `log.json("help_vs_manifest", {path, in_help_only, in_manifest_only})`; a failure prints the step, the unmatched paths, an excerpt of the instance (at most 2 KiB) and the transcript path (T1's drop guard prints `test log: <path>` and the last 20 steps).
- `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG=verbose argc e2e manifest` echoes every step live.

No checkpoint-only test: nothing here needs the real machine, a release build or the network.

## Considerations

- **Risk #22 (likelihood low, impact high; owners this bead and H2): the compatibility classifier mislabels a change** (a breaking change passed as additive). Mitigations: the conservative default (an unknown kind, an unknown fact, an unmodelled keyword, a grammar change it cannot place and a format mismatch are all `unclassified`, which counts as breaking); unit cases for every row of the rules tables in both directions; the property test that every monotone rule reverses; H2's updater tests against a synthetic released baseline; H1's final walk, which reports nodes with surprising facts to this bead's tests while it is open. A rule found wrong after the tag is fixed by making it *more* conservative, never less, without a vision comment.
- **The normalizer is the other place a fact can hide.** A schema shape it merges wrongly (two variants collapsed, a nullable lost in a union) would make the classifier blind to a change there. Mitigations: the synthetic shape table, the `$defs`-rename and doc-comment tests, `build_checked`'s conflicts, the `keywords` record for anything unmodelled, and the end-to-end check that every observed key path is located (a lost variant shows as unmatched keys).
- **Size L, kept as one leaf** (the plan): generation and classification share one node model. The vocabulary of node kinds and fact names is fixed in subtask 1 so subtasks 2–4 can run in parallel without disagreeing on spelling.
- **The registry precondition.** A4 and this bead may run at the same time. Whoever lands second rebases onto the other's `Registry` and `CommandInfo`; the manifest-only facts never become serialized fields (`capabilities`' snapshot is the check).
- **What could go wrong, and how it shows.**
  - A `HashMap` introduced somewhere upstream of a schema (a registry built from one) makes the manifest differ per process: the cross-thread repeat in the report test and H3's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3`, the determinism audit) `HashMap` scan catch it.
  - schemars changes its output shape in an update (a new keyword, a different union encoding): `keywords` facts appear and the `real_contract_has_no_unmodelled_keyword` test fails, naming the position, before any golden is regenerated.
  - A3's `error_variant` and the union inside `ErrorBody` drift apart: the error union stops being recognized and is expanded in full at every route, so the node count jumps; the section counts in the report make it visible, and `envelope_error_and_target_errors_reference_the_error_sections` fails.
  - A global flag gains a local twin on one path: clap refuses it at build time in debug, and the "every global on every path" test fails.
  - The report test's previous-run file belongs to another agent's checkout sharing the target directory: the diff it prints is then meaningless but harmless (it never fails the test); the printed path says which file was read.
- **Hot spots (§10.5 of the plan):**
  - `src/contract/mod.rs` (A2–A5, A9, this bead, H2, H3): one `pub mod` line each; rebase and keep the lines in alphabetical order.
  - `src/contract/commands.rs` (A4 and this bead): if A4 is in flight, coordinate through `SendMessage`/`ListAgents`; this bead adds only the pure helpers `command_facts`/`arg_facts` with their types (and, when A4 is absent, A4's types exactly as A4 specifies); `capabilities`' output must not move.
  - `src/error.rs`: not touched (the tri-state is A4's or A5's).
  - `src/state/config.rs`: one method on `KeyKind`.
  - `tests/contract/main.rs`: one `mod` line.
  - `README.md`: the Tests table row only (A3 also edits that row; rebase, never overwrite).
- **Performance.** Building the manifest generates every schema once (about 45 command schemas, 41+ error variants, 4 events, 20+ files) and walks them: expected well under two seconds in a debug build. The report test measures and prints the build time (in test code: the library modules read no clock); nothing asserts it (no flaky timing test).
- **Compatibility with older builds.** Nothing persisted or printed changes; there is nothing for an older build to misread.
- **Privacy.** The manifest is derived from code and holds no user data. The end-to-end scenario's home has `WTF/` directories, so every step runs `assert_private_all` with `--progress json`.
- **After H1.** This bead may land after H1; if a manifest fact it records shows a shape that breaks M4-D55's rules, that is a defect against H1 (fixed before H2's last regeneration), not something this bead changes.
- **Defaults applied (§8.1 of the plan):** no new error or warning code (1); additive and token-frugal (2: the manifest adds nothing to any output); stable sorted order everywhere (3); nothing read from the network or the environment (4); no write outside the test's temp directory (5); fail closed (6: unknown kinds, facts and keywords are unclassified, never ignored); every open question decided here (7).
- **Decided defaults, collected:** every "Decided while writing this bead" above. The implementer confirms or adjusts each in the close comment.

## Dependencies

Parent: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1 (the contract registry and the discovery surfaces).

**Blocked by:**

- A1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1`, per-command facts in `COMMANDS`, and canonical names): the facts the manifest's command nodes record (`dictionary`, `exits`, `stores_plan`, `network`, the `data` schema function), `ENVELOPE_ONLY`, and the canonical paths (`auth github`) that make each command node's id the envelope's `command`.
- A3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`, schemas with the serialize contract, declared `details`, and live validation): every schema the outputs are normalized from (`command_schema`, `data_schema_for`, `envelope_schema`, `event_schemas`, `error_variant`, `file_schemas`), the error union whose variants carry A9's typed `details`, `KindRow` with each kind's schema, `DesiredStateSchema`, and `contract::OPAQUE` with its guarantee that open positions are exactly its rows.

The subtask that writes integration tests (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.10.6) is also blocked by T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs, and the `argc e2e` runner), whose `TestLog` it uses.

**Unblocks:**

- H2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.2`, the golden and the released-baseline mechanism): it commits this bead's canonical manifest and projection as the current golden (with its informational header, written through `render`'s extra keys), compares with the released baseline through `classify` and `Bump::is_satisfied`, fails on `unsatisfied_kinds()`, reuses `unmatched` for the observed-keys check, and reviews its first commit by this bead's report and section counts.
- T2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.2`, slice 1 end to end): its demo item "the manifest's report prints" calls `report`.

**Slice:** `slice-1`, "Self-describing". Its exit demo (run and recorded by T2, not here): "`capabilities --json` round-trips; `robot-docs schema` validates the whole matrix and every envelope snapshot, `details` included; the manifest's report prints; `robot-docs guide` equals `SKILL.md`, frontmatter first; `install-skill` into a throwaway `HOME`; `omaddons retail update` suggests `update -t retail`, `remove dbm retail` changes nothing, and the corpus runs; `completions bash` passes `bash -n`". It pre-checks checkpoint criteria 1, 2, 3 (part), 5 and 15.

**Related, not edges:** A2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.2`) for the action, event and env-var registries the manifest reads (through A3); A4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`), which creates or reuses `Registry` and `CommandInfo` with this bead (whichever lands second adapts); A9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9`) for the `DetailSpec`s inside every error variant; E1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`), E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`) and E4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4`) for the doctor registries of TA 11; D2, D3 (`BINDING_COMMANDS`), D4 (`stores_plan`, the `plan` kind) and A8 (`trace`), whose changes reach the manifest without touching it; H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`), which may land before or after this bead and compares its inventory's counts with this bead's report when it can; H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`), which writes the first released baseline from this bead's manifest. Lane guidance: the plan's six-lane schedule puts this bead in lane 2 at t = 15–18; it has 10 units of slack, so it never delays the critical path.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `contract::manifest::build(&Registry) -> Manifest` records the four parts of §6.7: **outputs** (every `COMMANDS` row's data, both `ENVELOPE_ONLY` names' data, the envelope frame, every event, every error code's variant with its typed `details`), **inputs** (every clap path with its aliases and row facts, every flag and positional with its facts, every `config.toml` key with its type, every `addons.toml` path), **registries** (error codes with exit and tri-state retryability, warning codes, actions, events, phases, log levels, the general exit dictionary, `release` env vars; and failure-mode ids, the doctor dictionary with each code's `doctor_exit` and doctor ops when their registries exist), and **persisted formats** (every `store::KINDS` row and the folder journal, each with its version and normalized schema).
- [ ] The manifest is deterministic: two builds give byte-identical canonical JSON, also when built on different threads; `Manifest::parse(&m.render(&[]))` equals `m`; the layout is the one of TA 3.3 (sorted top-level keys, one node per line sorted by id, compact sorted node objects, one trailing newline).
- [ ] The manifest is independent of `$defs` naming and of documentation: a test renames a type with `#[schemars(rename = …)]` and another edits a doc comment, and each sees no change; no node id or fact contains a `$defs` name.
- [ ] Outputs keep the distinctions M4-D56 requires: integer and number distinct; `required` and `nullable` as separate facts; bounds (`minimum`, `maximum`, `minItems`, `maxItems`, `pattern`, …) recorded; enum values recorded; tagged variants recorded under their tag value with their own fields; an object reached by two routes recorded once per route; open positions recorded as `opaque`, and the opaque nodes agree with `contract::OPAQUE`; the error union recorded once per code and referenced (`union_of: "error"`) from every other position that holds it.
- [ ] Every `COMMANDS` path, flag and positional appears in the manifest with its facts (aliases, exits, dictionary, mutates, binds, stores plan, network; long and short names and aliases, default, grammar and values, arity, repeatability, requiredness, globality, conflicts and requirements), checked by an independent walk of `Cli::command().build()`, and against `omaddons help <path> --json` for every path end to end.
- [ ] Every key path of the live envelopes, `data`, error `details` and stderr events produced by the end-to-end scenario is located in the manifest (`unmatched` returns nothing), on a home with clients, with `assert_private_all` over every step's stdout and stderr with `--progress json`.
- [ ] The classifier's unit tests, over synthetic manifests, label each case correctly: added and removed output fields; optional, nullable, integer-to-number and bound changes (each direction); variant additions, removals and moves; enum values added and removed; added and removed flags, values and aliases; changed defaults; new conflicts and requirements; a required positional (and one added with its new command, additive); grammar, arity, repeatability and globality changes; command facts; config keys, `addons.toml` keys and env vars in input direction; registry changes; an unknown node kind and an unknown fact (unclassified); a persisted-format change (kind rule: a minor or major bump of that kind, satisfied or not, never a wire bump); a format mismatch (one unclassified change); reordered members and a differing header (no change).
- [ ] Property tests hold: classifying a manifest against itself is empty; render then parse round-trips; shuffled insertion and list order give identical bytes; for every monotone fact rule, a change labelled additive one way is labelled breaking the other way.
- [ ] `Changes::wire_bump()`, `unsatisfied_kinds()` and `Bump::is_satisfied` give the bumps of TA 8.4–8.5, and `Changes::render()` prints TA 8.6's form, folding changes below an added or removed node.
- [ ] `contract::wire::names` prints every node kind in the line forms of TA 9, sorted, deduplicated and deterministic, from the manifest alone.
- [ ] The report test (`cargo test --test contract manifest_report -- --nocapture`) prints the manifest's section counts and the classifier's verdict against an empty baseline, and against the previous run's manifest when one exists; it asserts the section counts equal their registries' lengths; it writes the manifest, its projection and the report under `CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR`.
- [ ] Requirements are recorded from `REQUIRES` (A4's, or created here with `requirement_violations`), which the probe holds true over every path; the default-missing scan passes on `src/` and fails a planted `default_missing_value`.
- [ ] The manifest modules read no environment variable, file, clock or `config.toml`, and use no `HashMap`/`HashSet` (source scans); `build_checked` reports no id conflict on the real contract; the real contract carries no `keywords` fact.
- [ ] No wire key and no output change: no existing `.snap` file changes; `capabilities --json`, if A4 has landed, is byte-identical; nothing is committed under `tests/contract/` but test code.
- [ ] Every section of §6.7 whose registry had not landed when this bead closed is named in the close comment, with its follow-up bead filed `discovered-from` this bead, blocked by the registry's leaf and blocking H2.
- [ ] README's Tests table row for `tests/contract/` names the report test and how to read it, in the commit that adds it.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes for every subtask's commit, and `ubs` is clean on the changed files.
- [ ] The close comment states that this bead adds no wire name (common rule 6: "none"), says whether this bead or A4 created `Registry`, `CommandInfo` and `REQUIRES`, whether the tri-state retryability was read or (absent) deferred to a follow-up, and confirms or adjusts every "Decided while writing this bead" item.
- [ ] `br lint` is clean for this bead and its subtasks.
