title: The `Action` registry, and `CommandHint` takes it
description:
Part 1 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.2 (Registries for actions, events, env vars, features and per-source facts). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

A2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.2`) is the M4 leaf that turns the facts omaddons' self-descriptions need into enumerable registries in a new module, `src/contract/`, without changing any output. M4's `capabilities` (A4, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`), the guide that is also the agent skill (B1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`), the schemas (A3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`) and the frozen contract manifest (A10, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.10`, and H2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.2`) are generated from those registries, never kept by hand (M4-D2: one contract registry feeds every description of the CLI; a hand-written description drifts, which is the failure capabilities exists to prevent).

This part does the recommendation actions. Every envelope carries `commands[]`, each `{action, command, argv, destructive}`, and agents switch on `action`. Today `action` is a string literal passed to `CommandHint::new` at 36 production call sites in 15 files, and only hand lists in tests know the set. **M4-D11** decided: `CommandHint::new` takes an `Action` enum instead of a string; `contract::actions::Action` has one variant per action name, each with a wire name, a description and whether it is destructive by default. M4-D11 rejected a scan for `CommandHint::new("…")` literals, because that would freeze a convention instead of making a mistake impossible: with a typed parameter a string does not compile. This is its own step because it is the widest change of the leaf (about 17 files, each by one argument) and touches no file the other parts touch, except one line in `src/contract/mod.rs`.

The decisions it obeys, restated:
- **M4-D2:** a fact clap cannot provide (here: an action's meaning and destructiveness) is declared exactly once, beside what it describes, and a test cross-checks it against behaviour.
- **DEC-3 and M4-D18:** `Action` derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`; serde's name for each variant is its wire name; no `HashMap` in any serialized type.
- **M4-D55:** every new name is snake_case from slice 1 on, so A3's rule test, which every later shape must pass, has nothing to allowlist here.

**Facts this part relies on** (verified at `c0ab5e9`):
- `CommandHint` (`src/error.rs:440-483`): fields `action: String, command: String, argv: Vec<String>, destructive: bool`, derives `Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, JsonSchema`; `new(action: impl Into<String>, argv, destructive: bool)` at `:451` (debug-asserts that `argv` starts with `omaddons` and sets `command` to `shell_words::join(&argv)`); `action(&self) -> &str` at `:469`. Its JSON test, `command_hints_carry_argv_and_display` (`:956-968`), expects `{"action":"undo","command":"omaddons undo 01JB8Q2VA00000000000000000","argv":["omaddons","undo","01JB8Q2VA00000000000000000"],"destructive":false}`.
- **22 distinct action names exist, not the 31 the plan counted.** 21 are literals; `install_hints` (`src/app/install.rs:1304-1332`) labels each hint by its argv's verb (`let verb = argv.get(1).cloned().unwrap_or_default(); CommandHint::new(verb, argv, false)`), which yields `install` or `search`. README's `commands` row (`README.md:1803`) documents the same 22. Only `remove_orphans` and `forget_target` pass `destructive: true`.
- The 36 production call sites: `src/app/drift.rs:89`; `src/app/backups_status.rs:113`, `:120`; `src/app/errors.rs:1162`, `:1170`, `:1181`; `src/app/remove.rs:312`; `src/app/adopt.rs:752`, `:759`, `:767`; `src/app/undo.rs:660`, `:672`; `src/app/outcome.rs:630`, `:642`; `src/app/install.rs:728`, `:752`, `:1329`; `src/app/search.rs:618`; `src/app/outdated.rs:830`; `src/app/restore_addons.rs:164`; `src/app/backup.rs:563`, `:1945`; `src/app/status.rs:924`, `:1011`, `:1203`, `:1208`, `:1226`, `:1250`, `:1255`, `:1263`, `:1271`, `:1290`, `:1297`; `src/omarchy/status.rs:123`, `:135`; `src/engine/tx.rs:213`. In unit tests: `src/error.rs:958`, `src/output/tests.rs:71`, `src/app/status.rs:1497`, `:1610`, `:1611`, `:1612`. Nothing under `tests/` constructs a `CommandHint`.
- Code that compares `action()` with a string: `src/app/adopt.rs:282` (`== "adopt"`), `src/app/errors.rs:663` (`"update"`) and `:672` (`"install_buggrabber"`), `src/app/outdated.rs:269-277` (`match hint.action() { "update" => …, "adopt" => …, _ => {} }`), `src/app/status.rs:1108` (`"check_updates"`) and `:1224` (`"update"`); unit tests `src/app/backups_status.rs:305`, `src/app/outcome.rs:1378`, `src/app/status.rs:1602` collect `action().to_owned()`.
- `src/contract/` does not exist; `src/lib.rs:11-35` declares the modules. `src/source_scan.rs` (test builds only) gives `production_code(text, Literals::Blank)` (comments, literal contents and `#[cfg(test)]` items blanked, char for char) and `sources(dir)`.
- `error_codes!` (`src/error.rs:111-148`) is the house pattern for a registry enum: one macro row per code, `#[serde(rename = $wire)]` per variant, `ALL`, `wire()`.

## Technical Approach

1. **The module.** If `src/contract/mod.rs` does not exist yet, create it with the module doc "The contract registry (M4-D2): every description of the CLI (`capabilities`, the guide, the schemas, the semantic manifest) is generated from the tables here and from the registries they join, never kept by hand." and add `pub mod contract;` to `src/lib.rs` (alphabetical, after `pub mod cli;`). Add `pub mod actions;`.

2. **`src/contract/actions.rs`.** A macro in the style of `error_codes!`:

   ```rust
   macro_rules! actions {
       ($($(#[$doc:meta])* $variant:ident = $wire:literal, $destructive:literal, $description:literal;)+) => {
           /// A recommended next command's `action` (`commands[].action`, M4-D11).
           #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash, Serialize, JsonSchema)]
           pub enum Action { $($(#[$doc])* #[serde(rename = $wire)] $variant,)+ }

           impl Action {
               /// Every action, in declaration order.
               pub const ALL: &[Action] = &[$(Self::$variant,)+];
               /// The snake_case wire name.
               pub const fn wire(self) -> &'static str { match self { $(Self::$variant => $wire,)+ } }
               /// One line of plain text, no trailing period.
               pub const fn description(self) -> &'static str { match self { $(Self::$variant => $description,)+ } }
               /// Whether a hint with this action is destructive by default.
               pub const fn destructive(self) -> bool { match self { $(Self::$variant => $destructive,)+ } }
               /// The action named `name`, if one is.
               pub fn from_wire(name: &str) -> Option<Self> { Self::ALL.iter().copied().find(|a| a.wire() == name) }
               /// The variant's Rust name, for the usage scan.
               #[cfg(test)]
               const fn rust_name(self) -> &'static str { match self { $(Self::$variant => stringify!($variant),)+ } }
           }
       };
   }
   ```

   plus `impl fmt::Display for Action` (writes `wire()`). The rows, in README's order, each with a doc comment naming who offers it:

   | Variant | Wire | Destructive | Offered today by | Description |
   |---|---|---|---|---|
   | `Undo` | `undo` | false | every committed change (`undo <tx>`) | Undo one transaction |
   | `UndoRun` | `undo_run` | false | a change on several clients (`undo --run <run>`) | Undo every transaction of one run |
   | `Update` | `update` | false | `status`, `outdated`, `errors` | Install the available updates |
   | `CheckUpdates` | `check_updates` | false | `status` (`outdated`) | Check every client for updates |
   | `Adopt` | `adopt` | false | `status`, `install`, `adopt`'s report | Adopt folders installed by hand |
   | `AdoptFolder` | `adopt_folder` | false | `adopt`'s report, per guess | Adopt one folder identified only by a guess |
   | `AdoptWithRef` | `adopt_with_ref` | false | `adopt`'s report, per guess with rivals | Adopt one folder from a chosen source |
   | `Install` | `install` | false | `search` results; `install`'s unresolved and bridge dependencies | Install an addon |
   | `Search` | `search` | false | `install`, for a bridge dependency nothing resolves | Search the sources for an addon |
   | `Reinstall` | `reinstall` | false | drift (`install --reinstall`) | Reinstall an addon whose files were changed |
   | `Inspect` | `inspect` | false | `status`, for degraded addons (`list -t <id> -v`) | Show a client's addons in detail |
   | `Status` | `status` | false | `status --cached` with no cache | Run a full status, which builds the cache |
   | `RemoveOrphans` | `remove_orphans` | true | `status` | Remove dependencies nothing requires any more |
   | `ListUnmanaged` | `list_unmanaged` | false | `status` | List the folders omaddons does not manage |
   | `ForgetTarget` | `forget_target` | true | `status`, for a client gone from the machine (`targets rm`) | Forget a client that is no longer on this machine |
   | `BackupCreate` | `backup_create` | false | `status`, `backup list` | Back up a client's settings |
   | `RefreshBackups` | `refresh_backups` | false | `status` (`backup list -t <id>`) | Refresh a client's backup summary |
   | `CheckErrors` | `check_errors` | false | `status --cached` (`errors`) | Read a client's Lua errors |
   | `DismissErrors` | `dismiss_errors` | false | `errors` | Dismiss a client's current Lua errors |
   | `InstallBuggrabber` | `install_buggrabber` | false | `errors` | Install BugGrabber so Lua errors are captured |
   | `ReinstallWidget` | `reinstall_widget` | false | `status`, `omarchy status` | Bring the bar widget up to date |
   | `EnableWidget` | `enable_widget` | false | `omarchy status` | Put the omaddons widget on the bar |

   The descriptions may be polished (one line, plain text, no trailing period, as the capabilities shape's example `"Run the stored plan the dry run made"` reads); the wire names and the destructive flags may not change.

3. **`CommandHint`** (`src/error.rs`): the field becomes `action: Action` (same position, so the JSON key order is unchanged). The constructor and accessor become:

   ```rust
   /// `argv` must start with `omaddons`; `command` is its shell-quoted display and
   /// `destructive` the action's default.
   pub fn new<I, S>(action: Action, argv: I) -> Self
   where I: IntoIterator<Item = S>, S: Into<String>;
   pub fn action(&self) -> Action;
   ```

   `command()`, `argv()` and `destructive()` are unchanged. Import `crate::contract::actions::Action` in `src/error.rs`.

4. **Every call site, by hand** (CLAUDE.md forbids script-based code changes): `CommandHint::new("undo", argv, false)` becomes `CommandHint::new(Action::Undo, argv)`, and so on for the 36 production and 6 test sites listed above. `install_hints` (`src/app/install.rs:1304-1332`) chooses the action with `match argv.get(1).map(String::as_str) { Some("search") => Action::Search, _ => Action::Install }`, which labels exactly as today: unresolved candidates build `install` argvs, and a `bridge_dependency` fix is an `install` or a `search` argv (`README.md:859`: "Each is labelled by the verb it runs, action `install` or `search`").

5. **Every reader** compares the enum: `c.action() == Action::Adopt` (`src/app/adopt.rs:282`), `Action::Update` and `Action::InstallBuggrabber` (`src/app/errors.rs:663`, `:672`), `match hint.action() { Action::Update => …, Action::Adopt => …, _ => {} }` (`src/app/outdated.rs:269-277`), `Action::CheckUpdates` (`src/app/status.rs:1108`), `Action::Update` (`:1224`). Unit tests that collected `action().to_owned()` collect `action()` and compare with variants, or `action().wire()` where they compare with strings; their expected values do not change.

6. **README.** No change: README's `commands` row already lists the 22 names. A test (below) holds it to `Action::ALL` from now on.

Decided while writing this bead (confirm or adjust in the close reason):
- **`destructive` comes from the action.** `CommandHint::new(action, argv)` sets `destructive = action.destructive()`. M4-D11 calls the flag each action's default; a per-call flag would let a hint contradict its action's published default. Every call site at `c0ab5e9` passes exactly the default, so no output changes. D4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`, the plan store), whose `apply` hint is destructive exactly when the stored command is, adds `CommandHint::with_destructive(self, bool) -> Self` in its own commit; this part adds no method nobody calls.
- **Only the 22 existing actions.** M4-D11 also lists five M4 actions: `apply` (D4), `install_skill` (B3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3`), `doctor_explain` (E3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`), `doctor_fix` (E6, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`) and `doctor_gc` (E8, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.8`, offered only as a `--dry-run` preview, M4-D36). Each is added by the leaf that first emits it, with its description, default and README mention, so `capabilities` never advertises an action no command offers. The leaf cannot forget: without a variant it cannot emit the action. The usage scan below fails on a variant nothing constructs.
- **This part writes the descriptions.** A9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9`, meanings and detail specs) mentions "`Action` (A2) gets its description" beside its error meanings, but A9 and A2 are both roots with no edge between them; the bead that creates the enum gives every variant its description. A9 may polish wording later, keeping the one-line shape.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `src/contract/actions.rs` declares `Action` through one macro, with exactly the 22 variants of the table, `ALL`, `wire()`, `description()`, `destructive()`, `from_wire()` and `Display`; `src/contract/mod.rs` declares `pub mod actions;` and `src/lib.rs` declares `pub mod contract;`.
- [ ] `CommandHint::new` takes `(Action, argv)` and `CommandHint::action()` returns `Action`; `grep -rn 'CommandHint::new("' src tests` prints nothing, and `grep -rn 'action() == "' src` prints nothing.
- [ ] `install_hints` labels `search` argvs `Action::Search` and every other argv `Action::Install`.
- [ ] `command_hints_carry_argv_and_display` passes with its expected JSON string unchanged; no snapshot anywhere is re-accepted; the whole contract suite, `tests/contract/recommendations.rs` included, passes unchanged.
- [ ] The unit tests below pass.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes and `ubs` is clean on the changed files; the commit message and close reason list the 22 registered action names and confirm or adjust the three decided items.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

In `src/contract/actions.rs` (`#[cfg(test)] mod tests`), each assertion message naming the variant and the value seen:

- `every_action_has_a_unique_snake_case_wire_name`: for every `Action::ALL` entry, `wire()` is non-empty and every char is `a-z`, `0-9` or `_`, starting with a letter; the set of wires has `ALL.len()` members; `ALL.len() == 22`.
- `serde_and_schema_names_equal_wire`: for every variant, `serde_json::to_value(a)` is `Value::String(a.wire())`; the schema from `SchemaSettings::draft2020_12().for_serialize().into_generator().root_schema_for::<Action>()` has an `enum` (or `oneOf` of `const`s, whichever schemars emits) whose values are exactly the 22 wires.
- `from_wire_round_trips_and_rejects_unknown`: every wire maps back to its variant; cases `empty` (`""`), `capitalized` (`"Undo"`), `trailing_space` (`"undo "`), `unknown` (`"no_such_action"`) and `future_action` (`"apply"`, until D4 adds it) give `None`.
- `descriptions_are_one_plain_line`: every description is non-empty, at most 80 characters, has no newline, no backtick, does not end with `.`, and starts with an ASCII capital letter.
- `destructive_defaults_are_pinned`: a table of all 22 `(Action, bool)` pairs as above, compared with `destructive()`; the table and `ALL` have the same members, so a new variant without a row fails with "add Action::<name>'s destructive default to destructive_defaults_are_pinned".
- `every_action_is_constructed_by_production_code`: over `crate::source_scan::sources(src/)`, the production code (`Literals::Blank`) of every file except `src/contract/actions.rs` contains `Action::<rust_name>` followed by a non-identifier character, for every variant; a miss fails with "Action::<name> is never constructed outside src/contract/actions.rs: remove it, or emit it from the command that offers it".
- `every_action_is_documented_in_readme`: `README.md`'s line that starts with ``| `commands` |`` contains `` `<wire>` `` for every variant; a miss names the action and says to document it there.

In `src/error.rs`:
- `command_hints_carry_argv_and_display`: `CommandHint::new(Action::Undo, ["omaddons", "undo", "01JB8Q2VA00000000000000000"])` serializes to the same string as today.
- `a_hint_takes_its_destructiveness_from_its_action`: cases `remove_orphans` (`["omaddons","remove","Foo","-t","retail"]` → `destructive() == true`), `forget_target` (`["omaddons","targets","rm","classic"]` → true) and `undo` (→ false); `action()` returns the variant given.

Existing unit tests that change only their construction or comparison, keeping every expected value: `src/output/tests.rs:71`, `src/app/status.rs:1497` and `:1602-1615`, `src/app/backups_status.rs:305`, `src/app/outcome.rs:1378`.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

None new in this part. The existing integration suites that read `commands[].action` as JSON (`tests/contract/` and about fifteen others, for example `tests/status.rs`, `tests/adopt.rs`, `tests/drift_surfaces.rs`, `tests/outdated.rs`) must pass unchanged: they prove the wire bytes did not move. Subtask 5 switches the contract suite's hand lists to `Action`.

### Logging

Unit tests only: table-driven, one name per case, every assertion message naming the case, the input and the value seen (for the scan: the variant and the files searched).

## Considerations

- **The change is wide and mechanical.** The compiler lists every site once `new`'s signature changes; convert them file by file, by hand. Do not add a `From<&str>` for `Action` to make the old calls compile: it would bring the string API back.
- **The schema of `commands[].action` changes** from `{"type":"string"}` to the 22-value enum. No snapshot records a schema (none exists before A3), and the JSON bytes are identical, so this is not a wire change; the close reason says so.
- **Hot spots.** `src/error.rs` (A9 then A3 rewrite every code row): this part touches only `CommandHint` (`:440-483`) and its test; rebase on whichever lands first. `src/app/status.rs` and `src/app/issues.rs` (E1 → F1 → F8, then E10 and G1): only hint construction and two comparisons change; landing early keeps those leaves on the enum. Every leaf that adds a hint after this part uses `Action`; coordinate through `SendMessage`/`ListAgents` with any leaf in flight that adds a `CommandHint::new` call.
- **The usage scan and later leaves.** When D4 adds `Action::Apply`, it must also emit it, document it in README's `commands` row and add its row to `destructive_defaults_are_pinned`; each test's failure message says so.
- **Privacy, performance:** nothing here reads or prints user data; `Action` is a `Copy` enum and every method is `const`.

## Dependencies

- Parent: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.2 (Registries for actions, events, env vars, features and per-source facts).
- Before it: none. It does not depend on subtasks 2, 3 or 4 and can run in parallel with them; whichever lands first creates `src/contract/mod.rs`, the others add their line.
- After it: subtask 5 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.2.5, Tests: the registries agree with live output) switches `tests/contract/main.rs`'s `check()` and `tests/contract/recommendations.rs` to `Action`, which needs this part's enum.

title: NDJSON event types, `Phase::ALL`, `LogLevel::ALL` and `EventName::ALL`
description:
Part 2 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.2 (Registries for actions, events, env vars, features and per-source facts). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

A2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.2`) is the M4 leaf that turns the facts omaddons' self-descriptions need into enumerable registries in a new module, `src/contract/`, without changing any output. M4's `capabilities` (A4, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`), the guide (B1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`), the schemas (A3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`) and the frozen contract manifest (A10, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.10`) are generated from those registries, never kept by hand (M4-D2).

This part does the stderr event vocabulary. In NDJSON mode every stderr line is one object whose `event` is `progress`, `log`, `warning` or `error`. Today those names are literals inside four structs declared in the bodies of `Reporter`'s methods, which derive no schema, and `Phase` and `LogLevel` have no list of their values. Two decisions require the change:
- **M4-D11:** NDJSON event names, `Phase` and `LogLevel` gain `ALL` arrays and `wire()` methods, and the literals in `stderr.rs` go, because these names are contract (agents switch on `event` and `phase`) and only test hand lists cover them today.
- **M4-D9 (the part A2 carries):** the four event structs leave function scope and derive `JsonSchema`, so A3 can publish one schema per event, built with `SchemaSettings::draft2020_12().for_serialize()` and a fresh generator per event, and validate every stderr line of the contract suite against it. The serialize contract matters because it describes what is written: a field with `skip_serializing_if` is optional and an `Option` that is always written (as `null`, like a warning's `fix`) is required. schemars' default contract describes input instead: it marks a skipped field that is not an `Option` (the 96 `-v`-only fields of command data) as required, so real output would fail validation, and it marks an always-written `Option` as optional. One shared generator would make `$defs` names depend on generation order.

Checkpoint criterion 2 needs this: "`robot-docs schema` gives a JSON Schema for … every NDJSON event", and "the contract suite validates … every stderr event against its event schema". It is its own step because it touches only the output layer and the new `events.rs`, and must change no byte of stderr.

**Facts this part relies on** (verified at `c0ab5e9`):
- `src/output/stderr.rs:37-68`: `Phase { Fetch, Download, Verify, Stage, Commit, Copy }`, deriving `Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash, Serialize` with `rename_all = "lowercase"`, each variant documented, `pub const fn wire(self)` at `:57-67`. `ProgressSink` keys a `BTreeMap<Phase, PhaseCount>` by it (`:79-82`), so `Ord` must stay.
- `:212-219`: `LogLevel { Info, Debug }` (`Debug` "shown only with `-v`"), deriving `Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize`, `rename_all = "lowercase"`. No `wire()`, no `ALL`.
- The event structs, declared inside methods, with their fields in serialization order:
  - warning (`:298-305`): `event: &'static str, code: &'static str, message: &'a str, fix: Option<&'a str>, fix_argv: Option<&'a [String]>`, built with `event: "warning"` (`:307`);
  - error (`:328-337`): `event, code, message, fix: &'a str, fix_argv: Option<&'a [String]>, retryable: bool, exit_code: u8` (`event: "error"`, `:339`; `exit_code: error.exit().code()`);
  - log (`:365-370`): `event, level: LogLevel, message: &'a str` (`event: "log"`, `:372`);
  - progress (`:401-410`): `event, phase: &'a str, message: &'a str, current: Option<u64>, total: Option<u64>`, the last two `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]` (`event: "progress"`, `:412`).
- `Reporter::progress(&mut self, phase: &str, message: &str, current: Option<u64>, total: Option<u64>)` (`:388-437`) prints `{phase}: {message}{count}` in human mode; `ProgressSink` calls it with `phase.wire()` (`:157`, `:179`, `:194`). The human log label is a `match` giving `"info:"`/`"debug:"` (`:378-381`).
- Byte-exact tests: `ndjson_lines_are_events` (`:705-728`: the warning line `{"event":"warning","code":"reload_required","message":"retail needs a /reload","fix":"/reload in game","fix_argv":null}` and the progress line `{"event":"progress","phase":"download","message":"WeakAuras","current":1,"total":3}`), `human_lines_read_naturally` (`:730-740`), `quiet_drops_everything_but_errors` (`:742-747`), the progress tests at `:549-690`, and `a_progress_line_is_erased_before_the_result` (`src/output/tests.rs:157-185`), which calls `reporter.progress("fetch", …)`. The helper `run` (`:695-703`) calls `r.progress("download", …)`.
- `src/output/mod.rs:25` re-exports `LogLevel, Phase`; ten modules import `Phase` from `crate::output` (`src/app/{adopt,outdated,search,backup}.rs`, `src/engine/{tx,plan}.rs`, `src/resolve/cache.rs`, `src/backup/{export,import,tree}.rs`), and `src/app/mod.rs` and `src/cli.rs:1340` name `output::LogLevel`.
- `schemars = "1.2.3"` (`Cargo.toml:24`) has `SchemaSettings::draft2020_12()`, `for_serialize()`, `into_generator()` and `SchemaGenerator::root_schema_for::<T>()`; under the serialize contract an `Option` field without `skip_serializing_if` is required (it is always written, as `null`), and a field with it is optional.
- `src/contract/` does not exist at `c0ab5e9`; whichever of A2's subtasks 1–4 lands first creates it.

## Technical Approach

1. **The module.** If `src/contract/mod.rs` does not exist, create it with its module doc ("The contract registry (M4-D2): every description of the CLI is generated from the tables here and from the registries they join, never kept by hand.") and add `pub mod contract;` to `src/lib.rs`. Add `pub mod events;`.

2. **`src/contract/events.rs`.** A local macro builds each name enum from one list, so `ALL` cannot miss a variant and serde's name is the wire name by construction:

   ```rust
   macro_rules! wire_enum {
       ($(#[$meta:meta])* pub enum $name:ident { $($(#[$doc:meta])* $variant:ident = $wire:literal,)+ }) => {
           $(#[$meta])*
           pub enum $name { $($(#[$doc])* #[serde(rename = $wire)] $variant,)+ }
           impl $name {
               pub const ALL: &[$name] = &[$(Self::$variant,)+];
               pub const fn wire(self) -> &'static str { match self { $(Self::$variant => $wire,)+ } }
           }
       };
   }
   ```

   - `EventName { Progress = "progress", Log = "log", Warning = "warning", Error = "error" }`, deriving `Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash, Serialize, JsonSchema`, with `pub fn schema(self, g: &mut schemars::SchemaGenerator) -> schemars::Schema` mapping each name to `g.root_schema_for::<…Event<'static>>()` of its struct.
   - `Phase` moves here unchanged (variants, doc comments, derives, wire names `fetch`, `download`, `verify`, `stage`, `commit`, `copy`), gaining `JsonSchema` and `ALL`.
   - `LogLevel` moves here (`Info = "info"`, `Debug = "debug"`), gaining `JsonSchema`, `ALL` and `wire()`. A8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.8`, verbosity levels) adds `Trace` here later.

   `ALL` is `&[Self]` as for `ErrorCode::ALL`; tests that need a count use `.len()`.

3. **The event structs**, at module scope, field for field and in today's order (serde writes fields in declaration order, so the order is the bytes), each deriving `Debug, Serialize, JsonSchema`, fields private, `event` set by the constructor:

   ```rust
   pub struct ProgressEvent<'a> { event: EventName, phase: Phase, message: &'a str,
       #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")] current: Option<u64>,
       #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")] total: Option<u64> }
   pub struct LogEvent<'a> { event: EventName, level: LogLevel, message: &'a str }
   pub struct WarningEvent<'a> { event: EventName, code: &'static str, message: &'a str,
       fix: Option<&'a str>, fix_argv: Option<&'a [String]> }
   pub struct ErrorEvent<'a> { event: EventName, code: &'static str, message: &'a str, fix: &'a str,
       fix_argv: Option<&'a [String]>, retryable: bool, exit_code: u8 }

   impl<'a> ProgressEvent<'a> { pub(crate) fn new(phase: Phase, message: &'a str, current: Option<u64>, total: Option<u64>) -> Self }
   impl<'a> LogEvent<'a> { pub(crate) fn new(level: LogLevel, message: &'a str) -> Self }
   impl<'a> WarningEvent<'a> { pub(crate) fn of(warning: &'a Warning) -> Self } // code: warning.code.wire(), fix: warning.fix.as_ref().map(|f| f.display()), fix_argv: …argv()
   impl<'a> ErrorEvent<'a> { pub(crate) fn of(error: &'a Error) -> Self }       // code, message, fix.display(), fix.argv(), retryable, exit().code()
   ```

   Each struct's doc comment states the event (for the schema's description), for example "A `warning` event: one per warning, mirroring the envelope's `warnings[]`."

4. **`src/output/stderr.rs`** loses `Phase`, `LogLevel` and the four local structs, and re-exports the two enums (`pub use crate::contract::events::{LogLevel, Phase};`), so `src/output/mod.rs:25` and every importer stay as they are. `Reporter::warning`, `error`, `log` and `progress` write `WarningEvent::of(w)`, `ErrorEvent::of(e)`, `LogEvent::new(level, message)` and `ProgressEvent::new(phase, message, current, total)` through the existing `json()`. `Reporter::progress` takes `phase: Phase` (its human line prints `phase.wire()`); `ProgressSink` passes `phase` instead of `phase.wire()`; the human log label becomes `format!("{}:", level.wire())`, which prints the same `info:` and `debug:`. After this, the production code of `stderr.rs` holds no event, phase or level name as a string literal.

5. **The two test call sites** of `Reporter::progress` (`src/output/stderr.rs:700`, `src/output/tests.rs:168`) pass `Phase::Download` and `Phase::Fetch`; their expected output is unchanged.

Decided while writing this bead (confirm or adjust in the close reason):
- **The structs live in `src/contract/events.rs`**, as A2's plan entry says, although M4-D9's text says "module scope in `src/output/stderr.rs`": both meet the decision (out of function scope, with schemas), and A3, A4 and A10 read the event vocabulary from the contract module beside the other registries.
- **`event` is typed `EventName`**, so a constructor cannot write the wrong name, and the schema's `event` property is the four-value enum. A3 may pin it to a `const` per event when it builds `event_schemas()`.
- **`EventName::schema` is declared here**, mapping each event to its type once, beside the types (as A1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1`, declares each command's `data` schema beside its `COMMANDS` row).
- **`Reporter::progress` takes `Phase`**, so the phase literal does not merely move to its callers.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `src/contract/events.rs` defines `EventName`, `Phase` and `LogLevel` through `wire_enum!`, each with `ALL` and `wire()` and deriving `JsonSchema`; `EventName::schema` returns each event's schema; `src/contract/mod.rs` declares `pub mod events;`.
- [ ] `ProgressEvent`, `LogEvent`, `WarningEvent` and `ErrorEvent` are at module scope with today's fields in today's order, deriving `Serialize + JsonSchema`, built only through their constructors.
- [ ] `src/output/stderr.rs` writes those types, re-exports `Phase` and `LogLevel`, and its production code holds none of the twelve name literals (four events, six phases, two levels); `Reporter::progress` takes `Phase`.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

In `src/contract/events.rs` (`#[cfg(test)] mod tests`):

- `all_lists_are_complete_and_ordered`: `EventName::ALL` wires are `["progress", "log", "warning", "error"]`, `Phase::ALL` wires `["fetch", "download", "verify", "stage", "commit", "copy"]`, `LogLevel::ALL` wires `["info", "debug"]`; for every entry of the three lists, `serde_json::to_value(x)` is `Value::String(x.wire())`; no list has a duplicate.

  - `warning_with_text_fix`: `reload_required`, "retail needs a /reload", fix text "/reload in game" → `{"event":"warning","code":"reload_required","message":"retail needs a /reload","fix":"/reload in game","fix_argv":null}`;

- `the_event_name_matches_the_struct`: each constructor's output has `event` equal to its own `EventName`'s wire (`ProgressEvent::new` → `progress`, and so on).
- `stderr_holds_no_event_name_literal`: `crate::source_scan::production_code(include_str!("../output/stderr.rs"), Literals::Keep)` contains none of `"progress"`, `"log"`, `"warning"`, `"error"`, `"fetch"`, `"download"`, `"verify"`, `"stage"`, `"commit"`, `"copy"`, `"info"`, `"debug"` as a whole string literal (quotes included); the message names the literal found.

## Considerations

- **Bytes are the contract here.** Field order, `skip_serializing_if` and every `Option` must stay exactly as today; never re-accept a snapshot or edit an expected string in this part. If a byte test fails, the move changed something.
- **Hot spot:** `src/output/stderr.rs`, `envelope.rs`, `mod.rs` are shared with A3 (envelope and `Meta` schemas), A8 (`LogLevel::Trace` and verbosity levels) and E3 (the doctor envelope). A8 adds `Trace` to `src/contract/events.rs` once this part has landed, with `wire()`, `ALL` and the `log` gate change; rebase on whichever lands first.

title: The environment-variable registry, held complete by source scans
description:
Part 3 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.2 (Registries for actions, events, env vars, features and per-source facts). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

A2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.2`) is the M4 leaf that turns the facts omaddons' self-descriptions need into enumerable registries in a new module, `src/contract/`, without changing any output. M4's `capabilities` (A4, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`) and the guide that is also the agent skill (B1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`) are generated from those registries, never kept by hand (M4-D2: one contract registry feeds every description of the CLI).

This part does the environment variables. **M4-D6** decided: `contract::env::ENV_VARS` lists every environment variable the binary reads, each with a name, a kind, a description and the flag it mirrors, if any. The kinds are `release` (read by every build), `debug` (read by debug builds only: failpoints, fixtures, clocks) and `harness` (read only by the test harness, never by the binary). A test scans `src/` for reads and fails on any unregistered name; a second scan checks that no `harness` name is read by the binary. `capabilities.env_vars` publishes the `release` rows (as `[{name, description, mirrors}]`), and `robot-docs guide` lists them. Why: README's table is the only list today, and nothing would notice a new variable; the vision requires `env_vars` in capabilities (checkpoint criterion 1 names `env_vars` among capabilities' six required keys). Rejected: publishing debug variables in capabilities (release builds ignore them, so listing them would mislead); wrapping every read in a macro (a scan is enough, and it also catches reads that a macro would hide). This is its own step because the scan is the part of A2 that needs the most care: it must see every way this crate reads a variable, and nothing else.

**Facts this part relies on** (verified at `c0ab5e9`):
- **Most reads are not `env::var("…")` literals.** Only 9 of the 23 variables the production code reads are passed as a literal to `std::env::var`/`var_os`: `OMADDONS_NOW` (`src/clock.rs:10`), `HOME` (`src/discover/running.rs:86`), `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT` (`:88`, `:177`), `OMADDONS_FAILPOINT_DIR` (`src/fsx/failpoint.rs:167`), `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS` (`:195`), `OMADDONS_FS_CLONE` (`src/backup/fs.rs:26`), `OMADDONS_FS_FREE_MB` (`:45`), `OMARCHY_PATH` (`src/omarchy/install.rs:592`) and `PATH` (`src/app/auth.rs:259`, `src/omarchy/shell.rs:66`, `src/sources/git_hosts.rs:219`). The other 14 go through lookup closures injected so tests need not touch the process environment:
  - `src/cli.rs:353`: `let env = |name: &str| std::env::var(name).ok();`, passed as `&dyn Fn(&str) -> Option<String>`; callers call `env("OMADDONS_ACTOR")` (`:258`) and `env("OMADDONS_OFFLINE")` (`:291-292`, and `src/output/term.rs:234` in `offline_from_argv`);
  - `src/output/term.rs:83`: `let var = |name: &str| std::env::var(name).ok();` then `var("NO_COLOR")`, `var("CI")`, `var("TERM")`, `var("OMADDONS_FORMAT")` (`:87-90`);
  - `src/net/mod.rs:320`: `env`, read by `choose_transport` as `env("OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES")` and `env("OMADDONS_RECORD")` (`:337-338`);
  - `src/state/paths.rs:68`: `Self::from_lookup(|name| std::env::var_os(name))`, then `lookup("HOME")` (`:74-75`), `xdg("XDG_CONFIG_HOME", ".config")` and the other XDG names through a local `xdg` helper (`:88-95`), and `lookup("OMADDONS_WIDGET_ID")` (`:98`);
  - `src/sources/github_token.rs:79`: `resolve_with(&|name| std::env::var(name).ok(), …)`, whose name is the constant `TOKEN_VAR = "OMADDONS_GITHUB_TOKEN"` (`src/sources/github_rest.rs:36`), read by `token_from` as `lookup(TOKEN_VAR)` (`:420-421`).
- `src/state/config.rs:960`: `CredentialRef::Env { env } => std::env::var(env)` reads the variable a source's `credential = { env = "…" }` in `config.toml` names: a user's choice, which no registry can list.
- `cmd.env("GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT", "0")`, `.env("HOME", …)`, `.env("LC_ALL", "C")` and the like (`src/sources/git_hosts.rs:216-232`) set a git child's environment; they are not reads.
- Harness names appear in unit-test code under `src/`: `OMADDONS_LIVE` in `src/net/tests.rs:646` (a `#![cfg(test)]` file) and `OMADDONS_FSX_TEST_PATH` in test modules of `src/fsx/sys.rs` and `src/fsx/lock.rs`. Neither is read by the binary.
- Every debug read is in a file that gates on `debug_assertions` (`cfg!(debug_assertions)` or `#[cfg(debug_assertions)]`): `src/clock.rs`, `src/discover/running.rs`, `src/fsx/failpoint.rs`, `src/net/mod.rs`, `src/backup/fs.rs`, `src/state/paths.rs`.
- `clap` is built with its `env` feature (`Cargo.toml:17`), but no `#[arg(env = …)]` is used.
- `src/source_scan.rs` (test builds only): `production_code(text, Literals::Keep | Literals::Blank) -> Option<String>` blanks comments and every `#[cfg(test)]` item (and, with `Blank`, the contents of string and char literals, quotes kept), char for char with newlines kept, and returns `None` for a `#![cfg(test)]` file; `sources(dir)` lists every `.rs` file with its text, sorted. The two views have the same number of chars as the source but not the same number of bytes when a literal holds a non-ASCII character such as `…`.
- README's Environment variables section (`README.md:2251-2265`): a table of 13 release names, then one sentence listing 8 debug names, then one listing 7 harness names (`OMADDONS_ALLOW_SKIP`, `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE`, `OMADDONS_LIVE`, `OMADDONS_REAL_CUSTOM_ROOT`, `OMADDONS_WRITE_SEEDS`, `BENCH_HOME`, `LIVE_HOME`). It lacks `PATH`, `OMADDONS_WIDGET_ID`, `OMADDONS_WIDGET_OUT` (set by `scripts/widget-test.sh:45-46`, read by `tests/omarchy_widget.rs:744`) and `COVERAGE_HOME` (`tests/perf.rs:286`).
- `tests/common/env.rs:10-21`, `:118-145`: `TestEnv` gives every child `HOME`, the four XDG variables, `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT`, `TZ=UTC`, `OMADDONS_FS_CLONE=no` and `OMADDONS_FS_FREE_MB=65536`, and removes `CI`, `NO_COLOR`, `TERM` and every other `OMADDONS_*` variable of the test process.
- The global flags `--actor`, `--offline` and `--json` exist (`src/cli.rs:44-119`); `OMADDONS_FORMAT=json` means `--json` (`src/output/term.rs:161-174`); a non-terminal stdin makes the actor `agent` by default (`src/model.rs:330-356`).

## Technical Approach

1. **The module.** If `src/contract/mod.rs` does not exist, create it with its module doc ("The contract registry (M4-D2): every description of the CLI is generated from the tables here and from the registries they join, never kept by hand.") and add `pub mod contract;` to `src/lib.rs`. Add `pub mod env;`.

2. **`src/contract/env.rs`:**

   ```rust
   /// When a variable is read (M4-D6).
   #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, JsonSchema)]
   #[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
   pub enum EnvKind {
       /// Read by every build.
       Release,
       /// Read by debug builds only (failpoints, fixtures, clocks); release builds ignore it.
       Debug,
       /// Read only by the test harness, never by the binary.
       Harness,
   }

   /// One environment variable.
   #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, JsonSchema)]
   pub struct EnvVar {
       pub name: &'static str,
       pub kind: EnvKind,
       /// One line of plain text, no trailing period.
       pub description: &'static str,
       /// The global flag it stands for (`--offline`), if any.
       pub mirrors: Option<&'static str>,
   }

   const fn var(name: &'static str, kind: EnvKind, description: &'static str, mirrors: Option<&'static str>) -> EnvVar;

   /// Every environment variable omaddons reads, release rows first, then debug, then harness.
   pub const ENV_VARS: &[EnvVar] = &[ … ];

   /// The rows `capabilities.env_vars` publishes.
   pub fn release() -> impl Iterator<Item = &'static EnvVar>;
   /// The row named `name`.
   pub fn get(name: &str) -> Option<&'static EnvVar>;
   ```

3. **The rows** (descriptions may be polished, one line each; names, kinds and mirrors may not change):

   | Name | Kind | Mirrors | Description |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | `OMADDONS_ACTOR` | release | `--actor` | Default --actor: human, agent or widget |
   | `OMADDONS_OFFLINE` | release | `--offline` | 1 (exactly) means --offline |
   | `OMADDONS_FORMAT` | release | `--json` | json means --json |
   | `OMADDONS_GITHUB_TOKEN` | release | | Bearer token sent to api.github.com only |
   | `NO_COLOR` | release | | Set and non-empty: no color |
   | `CI` | release | | Set and non-empty: no color, and NDJSON on stderr |
   | `TERM` | release | | dumb: no color, and NDJSON on stderr |
   | `HOME` | release | | Required and absolute: every path omaddons derives starts here |
   | `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` | release | | Moves omaddons' config when absolute; also the Lutris and Heroic config lookups |
   | `XDG_STATE_HOME` | release | | Moves omaddons' state when absolute |
   | `XDG_CACHE_HOME` | release | | Moves omaddons' cache when absolute |
   | `XDG_DATA_HOME` | release | | Moves the Lutris, Steam and Bottles data lookups; omaddons keeps no files there |
   | `OMARCHY_PATH` | release | | Where omarchy install also looks for Omarchy's shell ($OMARCHY_PATH/shell) |
   | `PATH` | release | | Where gh, git and omarchy-shell are found; git runs with only PATH from the caller's environment |
   | `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS` | debug | | Failpoints to arm: name or name=action[@N], comma-separated |
   | `OMADDONS_FAILPOINT_DIR` | debug | | Absolute directory where pause failpoints meet the test that resumes them |
   | `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES` | debug | | Directory of recorded HTTP responses to replay instead of the network |
   | `OMADDONS_RECORD` | debug | | 1 with OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES: record real responses into it |
   | `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT` | debug | | A fake /proc that running-client detection reads |
   | `OMADDONS_NOW` | debug | | An RFC 3339 time that freezes the clock |
   | `OMADDONS_FS_CLONE` | debug | | yes or no: whether the filesystem under a client clones files |
   | `OMADDONS_FS_FREE_MB` | debug | | The free space, in MiB, that backups see |
   | `OMADDONS_WIDGET_ID` | debug | | A suffix that installs a separate copy of the bar widget |
   | `OMADDONS_ALLOW_SKIP` | harness | | Checkpoint tests allowed to print SKIP, as a comma list of test names |
   | `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE` | harness | | 1 runs the real-machine tests |
   | `OMADDONS_LIVE` | harness | | 1 runs the live network probes |
   | `OMADDONS_REAL_CUSTOM_ROOT` | harness | | A real custom client root for the custom-discovery checkpoint test |
   | `OMADDONS_WRITE_SEEDS` | harness | | 1 rewrites the fuzz seeds |
   | `OMADDONS_WIDGET_OUT` | harness | | The widget pipeline's output directory, set by scripts/widget-test.sh |
   | `BENCH_HOME` | harness | | Where argc bench builds its home |
   | `LIVE_HOME` | harness | | Where the live run's home is built |
   | `COVERAGE_HOME` | harness | | Where the coverage study's home is built |

   **`OMADDONS_TEST_LOG`:** T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs and `argc e2e`) adds it, a harness variable read by `tests/common/tlog.rs`. Whichever of T1 and this bead lands second registers it. If `tests/common/tlog.rs` exists when this part lands, add the harness row "verbose echoes every test-log record to stderr as it happens; unset writes the logs only, read by tests/common/tlog.rs". Before closing, read this bead's comments (`br comments list omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.2 --json`): if T1 landed first, it left the row's text there. If T1 has not landed, add no row (the stale-row check would fail on a name nothing uses) and say so in the close reason.

4. **The scan** (unit tests in `src/contract/env.rs`). A pure function scans one file, so the same code runs over the tree and over planted text:

   ```rust
   #[cfg(test)]
   struct Scanned { reads: Vec<(String, usize)>, non_literal: Vec<usize>, literals: Vec<(String, usize)> } // (name, line)
   #[cfg(test)]
   fn scan(text: &str) -> Option<Scanned>; // None for a #![cfg(test)] file
   ```

   It takes `production_code(text, Literals::Keep)` and `production_code(text, Literals::Blank)` as `Vec<char>` and works in char indices (never byte offsets: the views differ in bytes after a literal holding `…`). A call is found in the Blank view, so a name inside a comment or a string is never mistaken for a read, and its argument is read from the Keep view at the same index. The line is the count of `\n` before the index, plus one. It records:

   1. **Direct reads:** each `env::var(` or `env::var_os(` (with any path before `env`). When the first non-space char after `(` is `"`, the literal's content is a read; otherwise the line is a non-literal read.
   2. **Lookup calls:** each `env(`, `var(`, `lookup(` or `xdg(` whose preceding char is not an identifier char, `.` or `:` (so `cmd.env("GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT", "0")`, which sets a child's variable, and `std::env::var(` are excluded), with a string-literal first argument: a read. These four are the names this crate's injected lookups go by (`src/cli.rs`, `src/net/mod.rs` and `src/sources/github_rest.rs` call theirs `env` or `lookup`; `src/output/term.rs` `var`; `src/state/paths.rs` `lookup` and `xdg`).
   3. **Owned names:** each string literal (found as a pair of `"` in the Blank view, where every literal's contents are blank) whose whole content matches `OMADDONS_[A-Z0-9_]+`: a read, unless the text before its opening quote, spaces skipped, ends with `env!(` or `option_env!(` (compile-time values, set by `build.rs`). This catches a name kept in a constant (`TOKEN_VAR`) or passed through a variable.
   4. **clap:** each `env = "NAME"` inside an `#[arg(` attribute: a read.

   Every string literal's content is also kept in `literals`, for the harness check.

   `LOOKUP_SEAMS: &[(&str, &str)]` (test-side, path and reason) lists the files allowed a non-literal read: `src/cli.rs` ("the run's env lookup, passed to Context::new and offline_from_argv"), `src/output/term.rs` ("TermEnv::from_process's var"), `src/net/mod.rs` ("the transport's env lookup"), `src/state/paths.rs` ("Paths::from_env's lookup, and xdg over it"), `src/sources/github_token.rs` ("the token lookup; the name is github_rest::TOKEN_VAR") and `src/state/config.rs` ("a credential variable named by config.toml: a user's choice, never a registry row").

5. **The checks**, over every `.rs` file of `crate::source_scan::sources(<manifest dir>/src)` except `src/contract/env.rs` itself (which holds the names as data); each failure names the file and line and says what to do:

   - **Complete:** every read is an `ENV_VARS` row of any kind. "src/net/mod.rs:337 reads OMADDONS_X, which ENV_VARS does not list: add a row (release, debug or harness) to src/contract/env.rs."
   - **Harness never in the binary:** no read is a `harness` row, and no `harness` row's name is the whole content of any string literal in production code. "harness variable OMADDONS_LIVE appears in production code at src/…:N: the binary must never read it; if it does, make it a debug row."
   - **Seams are declared:** the set of files with a non-literal read equals the set of `LOOKUP_SEAMS` paths. A new file names itself ("src/new.rs:12 reads a variable whose name is not a literal: declare it in LOOKUP_SEAMS with its reason, and add the lookup's name to the scan's lookup names if it is new"); a seam that no longer reads names itself too.
   - **No stale rows:** every `release` and `debug` row is read somewhere ("ENV_VARS lists X but nothing in src/ reads it: remove the row"); every `harness` row's name occurs in some file under `tests/` (`.rs`), in `Argcfile.sh` or under `scripts/`.
   - **Debug rows are debug-gated:** every file with a read of a `debug` row contains `debug_assertions` in its production code. The test's doc comment says this is a heuristic: it shows the file has a debug gate, not that the gate covers the read; the existing per-variable tests (for example `omaddons_now_freezes_debug_builds_only`, `src/clock.rs`) prove the behaviour.
   - **Rows are well formed:** names unique and each `[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*`; kinds in groups, all release rows, then all debug rows, then all harness rows; descriptions non-empty, one line, at most 120 characters, no trailing period, no backtick; only `release` rows have `mirrors`, and each `mirrors` value is the long name of a global argument of the built `Cli::command()` (`--actor`, `--offline`, `--json`).
   - **README agrees:** in `README.md`, the text from the line `### Environment variables` to the next line starting with `---` or `## `: every backticked span, cut at its first `=`, that matches `[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]+` is a name (`TERM=dumb` counts as `TERM`; `$OMARCHY_PATH/shell`, `--actor` and `1` do not). That set equals the `ENV_VARS` names; a failure prints the missing and the extra names.

6. **README.** In the Environment variables section: add a `PATH` row to the table ("Where `gh`, `git` and `omarchy-shell` are found; `git` runs with only `PATH` from your environment"); add `OMADDONS_WIDGET_ID` (a suffix of up to 32 lowercase letters, digits and `-` that installs a separate copy of the bar widget) to the debug sentence; add `OMADDONS_WIDGET_OUT` and `COVERAGE_HOME` to the harness sentence; and end the section with "A test fails when the binary reads a variable this section does not list." Nothing else in README changes.

Decided while writing this bead (confirm or adjust in the close reason):
- **The scan recognises lookup closures, constants and clap attributes**, not only `env::var("…")` literals, because 14 of the 23 production names are read through a lookup (Facts above); a literal-only scan, as the plan's wording has it, would pass with most variables unregistered.
- **Harness rows are the variables a developer, the checkpoint or a pipeline script sets** to steer the test harness. Variables one test sets only for its own child process (`OMADDONS_LOCK_TEST_HOLD_MS`, `OMADDONS_LOCK_TEST_HOME`, `OMADDONS_LOCK_TEST_MODE`, `OMADDONS_RESTORE_*`, `OMADDONS_RECLAIM_*`, `OMADDONS_READER_*`, `OMADDONS_PRUNE_TEST_*`, `OMADDONS_LUA_WORKLOAD`, `OMADDONS_FSX_TEST_PATH`) are that test's private plumbing and get no row.
- **The harness check applies to production code**, not to the `src/` directory, so `src/net/tests.rs` reading `OMADDONS_LIVE` passes: it is test code, never the binary. (The plan's "every harness name appears only under `tests/`" would fail on that file.)
- **A variable the binary reads, even only in debug builds and only ever set by tests, is `debug`, never `harness`.** E6's `OMADDONS_TEST_FIXERS` (debug builds only) is a `debug` row when E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`, `doctor fix`) adds it; B1's `OMADDONS_UPDATE_SKILL` and H2's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.2`) `OMADDONS_UPDATE_WIRE_NAMES` and `OMADDONS_ADVANCE_RELEASED_BASELINE`, read only by tests, are `harness` rows, each added by its own leaf.
- **Build-time values are not rows.** `build.rs` reads Cargo's own variables; D1's `OMADDONS_BUILD_ID` and B1's `OMADDONS_GUIDE_SHA256` are compiled in with `env!`, never read at run time, and the scan ignores `env!`/`option_env!` arguments.
- **Variables read inside dependencies are not rows** (jiff reads `TZ` for local times): the registry lists what omaddons' own code reads, which the scan can hold complete.
- **README's section is held equal to the registry by a test**, because the reason for the registry (M4-D6) is that README's list was the only one and nothing noticed when it went stale; H4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`, the README final pass) later reconciles README with the generated guide.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `src/contract/env.rs` defines `EnvKind`, `EnvVar`, `ENV_VARS` with the rows of the table (plus `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG` if T1 had landed), `release()` and `get()`; both types derive `Serialize + JsonSchema`; `src/contract/mod.rs` declares `pub mod env;`.
- [ ] Over the tree at this commit, every check passes: complete, harness never in the binary, seams declared, no stale rows, debug rows debug-gated, rows well formed, README agrees.
- [ ] `planted_reads_are_found_or_ignored` passes all 15 cases below; in particular a planted `std::env::var("OMADDONS_X")` is reported as unregistered with its line.
- [ ] README's Environment variables section lists `PATH`, `OMADDONS_WIDGET_ID`, `OMADDONS_WIDGET_OUT` and `COVERAGE_HOME`, and ends with the sentence about the test, in this part's commit.
- [ ] No behaviour or output changes: no snapshot is re-accepted, and the gate's existing tests pass.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes and `ubs` is clean on the changed files; the close reason lists every row by kind, says whether `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG` was registered, and confirms or adjusts the seven decided items.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

In `src/contract/env.rs` (`#[cfg(test)] mod tests`):

- `the_tree_reads_only_registered_variables`: the complete check over the tree.
- `planted_reads_are_found_or_ignored`: a table of named cases, each a path, a source text and the expected findings, run through `scan` and the same checks against the real `ENV_VARS` and `LOOKUP_SEAMS`:

  | Case | Text | Expected |
  |---|---|---|
  | `direct_var_literal` | `fn f() { let _ = std::env::var("OMADDONS_X"); }` | unregistered `OMADDONS_X`, line 1 |
  | `direct_var_os_literal` | `std::env::var_os("OMADDONS_X")` | unregistered `OMADDONS_X` |
  | `lookup_closure_env` | `fn f(env: &dyn Fn(&str) -> Option<String>) { env("SOME_VAR"); }` | unregistered `SOME_VAR` |
  | `lookup_closures_var_lookup_xdg` | `var("A_VAR"); lookup("B_VAR"); xdg("C_VAR", ".x");` | unregistered `A_VAR`, `B_VAR`, `C_VAR` |
  | `name_in_a_constant` | `pub const V: &str = "OMADDONS_X";` | unregistered `OMADDONS_X` |
  | `clap_env_attribute` | `#[arg(long, env = "OMADDONS_X")] x: bool,` | unregistered `OMADDONS_X` |
  | `after_a_non_ascii_literal` | `let _ = "…"; let _ = std::env::var("OMADDONS_X");` on line 3 | unregistered `OMADDONS_X`, line 3 (char indices aligned) |
  | `registered_name` | `std::env::var_os("OMADDONS_NOW")` | nothing |
  | `setting_a_child_variable` | `cmd.env("GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT", "0");` | nothing |
  | `in_a_comment` | `// std::env::var("OMADDONS_X")` | nothing |
  | `in_a_message` | `Suggestion::text("unset OMADDONS_X, or set it")` | nothing (the literal is not a bare name) |
  | `in_test_code` | `#[cfg(test)] mod tests { fn t() { let _ = std::env::var("OMADDONS_X"); } }` | nothing |
  | `compile_time_value` | `const B: &str = env!("OMADDONS_BUILD_ID");` | nothing |
  | `harness_name_in_the_binary` | `let _ = std::env::var("OMADDONS_LIVE");` | harness in the binary: `OMADDONS_LIVE` |
  | `non_literal_read_outside_a_seam` | path `src/new.rs`: `fn f(name: &str) { let _ = std::env::var(name); }` | undeclared seam `src/new.rs` |

- `harness_names_never_appear_in_production_code`, `lookup_seams_are_declared`, `no_row_is_stale`, `debug_rows_are_read_behind_debug_assertions`, `rows_are_well_formed`, `readme_lists_exactly_the_registered_variables`: the checks of step 5 over the tree, one test each, so a failure names the rule.
- `release_rows_are_what_capabilities_publishes`: `release()` yields exactly the 14 release rows, in table order, and `get("OMADDONS_OFFLINE")` returns the row with `mirrors: Some("--offline")`; `get("NOPE")` is `None`.
- `rows_serialize_as_capabilities_shows_them`: `serde_json::to_value(get("OMADDONS_OFFLINE"))` has `name`, `kind: "release"`, `description` and `mirrors: "--offline"`.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

None in this part. Subtask 5 proves the mirrored flags against the real binary (`each_mirrored_variable_acts_like_its_flag`).

### Logging

Unit tests only: every planted case is named, and every failure prints the case, the file and line, the name found and the fix sentence; the README check prints the two difference sets.

## Considerations

- **Keep the scan small and honest.** It is text matching over the production view, not a parser. Each read shape it knows is a planted case; a shape found later becomes a new case and a new rule, not an exemption. Never add an allowlist of unregistered names.
- **What a later leaf does.** A leaf that reads a new variable adds its row (and, once B1 has landed, regenerates `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` with `OMADDONS_UPDATE_SKILL=1 cargo test --test skill`, common rule 17); a new lookup closure adds its `LOOKUP_SEAMS` entry; a new harness knob adds its row and its README mention. The failure messages say so.
- **Hot spots:** `README.md` (edit only the Environment variables section); `src/contract/mod.rs` (one line). T1 adds its one row to `ENV_VARS` if it lands second; coordinate through `SendMessage`/`ListAgents` if both are in flight.
- **Privacy:** rows hold names and descriptions, never values. The README test reads the repository's README, never a user file.
- **Performance:** the scans read about 200 source files once per `cargo test`; they are plain string work.

## Dependencies

- Parent: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.2 (Registries for actions, events, env vars, features and per-source facts).
- Before it: none. It does not depend on subtasks 1, 2 or 4 and can run in parallel with them; whichever lands first creates `src/contract/mod.rs`.
- After it: subtask 5 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.2.5, Tests: the registries agree with live output) proves each mirrored variable against its flag on the real binary.
- Related: T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`) registers or asks for `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG` (see step 3).

title: Feature words, per-source credentials and hosts, and the target-id forms
description:
Part 4 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.2 (Registries for actions, events, env vars, features and per-source facts). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

A2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.2`) is the M4 leaf that turns the facts omaddons' self-descriptions need into enumerable registries in a new module, `src/contract/`, without changing any output. M4's `capabilities` (A4, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`) is generated from those registries, never kept by hand (M4-D2: one contract registry feeds every description of the CLI; a fact clap cannot provide is declared once, beside what it describes, and a test cross-checks it against behaviour).

This part does the four small registries `capabilities` lists beside the commands:
- **`features`**, one of the six keys the vision requires in capabilities (checkpoint criterion 1): stable feature words, never removed, that an agent can test for (`"stored_plans" in features`).
- **`sources[].requires_credential`** and **`sources[].hosts`**: capabilities' source rows are `{id, enabled, requires_credential, credential_configured, hosts[]}`. Today no source records whether it needs a credential, and the HTTP allowlist is one flat list with no record of which source each host serves. The plan's capabilities rules: `requires_credential` is "a new field on each source's registration (`sources/mod.rs`): `false` for every keyless source, and `true` only for CurseForge and Wago, which are parsed and disabled until M5"; "the allowlist is re-keyed by source (`net::allowlist::hosts_for(SourceId)`, the flat `ALWAYS` list becoming the union)", with "the existing allowlist tests unchanged".
- **`target_id_forms`**: the forms a `-t` selector may take, today implicit in the order of seven closures in `discover::registry::resolve`. The plan: `contract::target_id_forms()`, "read from `discover::registry::resolve`'s step order, so the list cannot drift".

They share a subtask because each is small and none touches another's files; together they are one commit of registry facts with their unit tests.

**Facts this part relies on** (verified at `c0ab5e9`):
- No feature list exists anywhere. The vision and the plan fix fourteen words, in this order: `json_envelope`, `ndjson_stderr`, `dry_run_everywhere`, `preconditions`, `stored_plans`, `doctor`, `offline`, `progress_ndjson`, `undo`, `backups`, `lua_errors`, `omarchy_widget`, `completions`, `agent_skill`. Four of them name surfaces that do not exist yet: `stored_plans` (`apply`, D5 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`), `doctor` (E3 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`), `completions` (A7 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.7`) and `agent_skill` (`robot-docs install-skill`, B3 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3`).
- `app::COMMANDS` (`src/app/mod.rs:121-165`): 42 rows `{name, group, mutates}`, including `undo`, `backup create`, `errors` and `omarchy install`. The global flags (`src/cli.rs:44-119`) include `--json`, `--dry-run`, `--if-match`, `--offline` and `--progress`. Stderr is NDJSON whenever it is not a terminal, or under `CI` or `TERM=dumb` (`src/output/term.rs:126-130`).
- `SourceId` (`src/sources/mod.rs:81-171`): `Github, Git, Url, Local, Wowi, Tukui, Curseforge, Wago, Wowace`; `ALL: [Self; 9]` (`:99-109`), `wire()` (`:126-138`, so CurseForge's wire name is `curseforge`, which the plan abbreviates `cf`), `name()` (`:145-157`), `later()` (`:160-171`, `Some("M5")` for CurseForge and Wago).
- `src/net/allowlist.rs`: `ALWAYS` (`:8-18`) = `api.github.com`, `github.com`, `codeload.github.com`, `objects.githubusercontent.com`, `release-assets.githubusercontent.com`, `api.mmoui.com`, `cdn.wowinterface.com`, `api.tukui.org`, `repos.wowace.com`; `CURSEFORGE` (`:21-25`) = `api.curseforge.com`, `edge.forgecdn.net`, `mediafilez.forgecdn.net`; `WAGO` (`:28`) = `addons.wago.io`. `Allowlist::new(curseforge, wago)` (`:39-53`) chains `ALWAYS` with the enabled optional lists into a lowercase `BTreeSet`; `is_http_host` (`:98-100`) is `Allowlist::new(true, true).permits(host)`. The tests (`:102-167`): `exact_case_insensitive_hosts_only`, `optional_sources`, `git_hosts_and_http_hosts_are_disjoint`, plus their helpers, iterate `ALWAYS`, `CURSEFORGE` and `WAGO` as slices.
- The `url:` source's allowlist is `Allowlist::new(false, false)` (`src/sources/url.rs:25-28`): a `url:` ref may download from any `ALWAYS` host. `git:` refs on github.com are read without the git binary, from `github.com` (the commits feed) and `codeload.github.com` (the archive) (`src/sources/git_github.rs:1-4`); other git hosts are reached by the git binary, only as the user's configured `git_hosts` (`GitHosts`, `src/net/allowlist.rs:58-95`), which never include an HTTP host.
- `discover::registry::resolve` (`src/discover/registry.rs:638-708`): doc "Precedence, first match wins: key, id, product code, flavor folder, game mode (`table`'s mode ids and aliases: `sod` selects the Classic Era client), family, then a path (install root, client dir or AddOns path)"; `let steps: [&dyn Fn(&DiscoveredTarget) -> bool; 7] = [ … ]` (`:660-679`), then the first non-empty match (`:680-683`), else `target_not_found`. Tests: `selector_precedence` (`:989-1031`), `a_missing_client_is_never_resolved_to_another` (`:1036`), `game_modes_select_the_client_that_runs_them` (`:1075`), with a `discovered(id, family, product, flavor, root)` helper.
- `src/contract/` does not exist at `c0ab5e9`; whichever of A2's subtasks 1–4 lands first creates it.

## Technical Approach

1. **The module.** If `src/contract/mod.rs` does not exist, create it with its module doc ("The contract registry (M4-D2): every description of the CLI is generated from the tables here and from the registries they join, never kept by hand.") and add `pub mod contract;` to `src/lib.rs`. Add `pub mod features;` and the function of step 4.

2. **`src/contract/features.rs`:**

   ```rust
   /// The stable feature words `capabilities.features` lists. Each names a surface this
   /// build has; a word is added by the leaf that builds its surface, at its place in
   /// the canonical order, and is never removed.
   pub const FEATURES: &[&str] = &[
       "json_envelope", "ndjson_stderr", "dry_run_everywhere", "preconditions",
       "offline", "progress_ndjson", "undo", "backups", "lua_errors", "omarchy_widget",
   ];
   ```

   Test-side, `CANONICAL: [&str; 14]` (the order above) and `EVIDENCE`, one row per canonical word, saying what proves the surface exists:

   | Word | Evidence |
   |---|---|
   | `json_envelope` | global flag `--json` |
   | `ndjson_stderr` | built in: stderr is NDJSON whenever it is not a terminal (`StderrMode::Ndjson`, `src/output/term.rs:126-130`); the row is `Evidence::Builtin` with that reason, and always holds |
   | `dry_run_everywhere` | global flag `--dry-run` |
   | `preconditions` | global flag `--if-match` |
   | `stored_plans` | command `apply` |
   | `doctor` | command `doctor` |
   | `offline` | global flag `--offline` |
   | `progress_ndjson` | global flag `--progress` |
   | `undo` | command `undo` |
   | `backups` | command `backup create` |
   | `lua_errors` | command `errors` |
   | `omarchy_widget` | command `omarchy install` |
   | `completions` | command `completions` |
   | `agent_skill` | command `robot-docs install-skill` |

   `Evidence` is a test-side enum: `Flag(long)` is checked on `Cli::command().build()`'s root arguments by long name, `Command(path)` by `app::COMMANDS`' `name`, and `Builtin(reason)` always holds (it documents why the word is true of every build).

3. **Per-source facts.**
   - In `src/sources/mod.rs`, beside `wire()`, `name()` and `later()`:

     ```rust
     /// Whether this source needs a credential to work at all (`capabilities.sources[]`):
     /// CurseForge and Wago (M5). GitHub's token is optional, so it does not.
     pub const fn requires_credential(self) -> bool {
         match self {
             Self::Curseforge | Self::Wago => true,
             Self::Github | Self::Git | Self::Url | Self::Local | Self::Wowi | Self::Tukui | Self::Wowace => false,
         }
     }
     ```

     (an exhaustive `match`, so a new source must decide).
   - In `src/net/allowlist.rs`, each host is written once, in a per-source constant, and `ALWAYS` is built from them at compile time:

     ```rust
     /// GitHub's hosts: REST, web (feeds, releases), archives and release assets.
     pub const GITHUB_HOSTS: &[&str] = &["api.github.com", "github.com", "codeload.github.com",
         "objects.githubusercontent.com", "release-assets.githubusercontent.com"];
     pub const WOWI_HOSTS: &[&str] = &["api.mmoui.com", "cdn.wowinterface.com"];
     pub const TUKUI_HOSTS: &[&str] = &["api.tukui.org"];
     pub const WOWACE_HOSTS: &[&str] = &["repos.wowace.com"];
     /// The HTTPS hosts `git:` refs on github.com are read from (`sources::git_github`).
     pub const GIT_GITHUB_HOSTS: &[&str] = &["github.com", "codeload.github.com"];

     /// `parts` end to end, as an array of exactly `N` hosts (checked at compile time).
     const fn joined<const N: usize>(parts: &[&[&'static str]]) -> [&'static str; N] { … }
     const ALWAYS_HOSTS: [&str; 9] = joined(&[GITHUB_HOSTS, WOWI_HOSTS, TUKUI_HOSTS, WOWACE_HOSTS]);
     /// Always allowed: the union of the keyless sources' hosts.
     pub const ALWAYS: &[&str] = &ALWAYS_HOSTS;

     /// The hosts built into `source`. A `url:` ref may use any always-allowed host; the
     /// git binary's hosts are the configured `git_hosts`, which are config, not built in.
     pub fn hosts_for(source: SourceId) -> &'static [&'static str] {
         match source {
             SourceId::Github => GITHUB_HOSTS,
             SourceId::Git => GIT_GITHUB_HOSTS,
             SourceId::Url => ALWAYS,
             SourceId::Local => &[],
             SourceId::Wowi => WOWI_HOSTS,
             SourceId::Tukui => TUKUI_HOSTS,
             SourceId::Wowace => WOWACE_HOSTS,
             SourceId::Curseforge => CURSEFORGE,
             SourceId::Wago => WAGO,
         }
     }
     ```

     `joined` copies with two nested `while` loops and ends with `assert!(k == N, "…")`, so a wrong `N` is a compile error. `ALWAYS` keeps its type, its nine hosts and their order; `CURSEFORGE`, `WAGO`, `Allowlist`, `GitHosts` and `is_http_host` do not change, nor does any existing test.

4. **The target-id forms.** In `src/discover/registry.rs`:

   ```rust
   /// A form a `-t` selector may take.
   #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
   pub enum SelectorForm { Key, Id, ProductCode, FlavorFolder, GameMode, Family, Path }

   impl SelectorForm {
       /// In `resolve`'s precedence: the first form that matches any target wins.
       pub const ALL: [Self; 7] = [Self::Key, Self::Id, Self::ProductCode, Self::FlavorFolder,
           Self::GameMode, Self::Family, Self::Path];
       /// `key`, `id`, `product_code`, `flavor_folder`, `game_mode`, `family`, `path`.
       pub const fn wire(self) -> &'static str { … }
   }
   ```

   `resolve` replaces its array of seven closures with one closure `matches(form, d)` holding an exhaustive `match form { SelectorForm::Key => key.is_some() && d.target.key == key, SelectorForm::Id => …, … }`, whose arms are today's seven predicates verbatim, and iterates `SelectorForm::ALL` (`.iter().map(|form| pick(&|d| matches(*form, d))).find(|found| !found.is_empty())`). Its doc names `SelectorForm::ALL` as the precedence. Behaviour is identical.

   In `src/contract/mod.rs`:

   ```rust
   /// The forms `-t` accepts, in `resolve`'s precedence (`capabilities.target_id_forms`).
   pub fn target_id_forms() -> Vec<&'static str> {
       crate::discover::registry::SelectorForm::ALL.iter().map(|f| f.wire()).collect()
   }
   ```

   C2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.2`, a client named as an addon, and `-t all`) adds `all` to this list when `-t all` exists (M4-D13); capabilities' example list ends with it.

Decided while writing this bead (confirm or adjust in the close reason):
- **`FEATURES` holds only the ten words whose surface exists**, and the four others are added by D5, E3, A7 and B3 when they build `apply`, `doctor`, `completions` and `robot-docs install-skill`. A word for a command that does not exist would be a false capability, against G-M4-1 ("every fact in those outputs is generated from the code, so it cannot drift from what the code does"). The evidence test makes forgetting impossible: the commit that adds the `doctor` row to `COMMANDS` fails it until `doctor` is in `FEATURES`.
- **`ALWAYS` is built by a `const fn`**, rather than turned into a `LazyLock` or kept as a hand list beside the per-source ones: it stays a `&[&str]` constant, so the existing tests and callers stay unchanged as the plan requires, and each host is written exactly once.
- **`git`'s built-in hosts are `github.com` and `codeload.github.com`**, the two the `git:https://github.com/…` path requests; confirm against `src/sources/git_github.rs`'s request URLs while implementing and add any other host it requests (none at `c0ab5e9`, as far as its module doc says). The configured `git_hosts` are reported by A4 as the git source's effective hosts with `source: "config"` (M4-D4: capabilities reports effective values); `hosts_for` never reads config.
- **`url`'s hosts are `ALWAYS`**, because the `url:` source permits exactly `Allowlist::new(false, false)`.
- **`SelectorForm` drives `resolve`** rather than a separate list kept equal to it by a test, so the published order is the executed order by construction.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `src/contract/features.rs` defines `FEATURES` with the ten words, in canonical order; `features_are_unique_snake_case_and_canonically_ordered` and `each_feature_word_is_listed_exactly_when_its_surface_exists` pass.
- [ ] `SourceId::requires_credential` is `true` for `curseforge` and `wago` only.
- [ ] `net::allowlist::hosts_for` returns the hosts of the table for each source; `ALWAYS` is the same nine hosts in the same order, built from the per-source constants; `exact_case_insensitive_hosts_only`, `optional_sources` and `git_hosts_and_http_hosts_are_disjoint` pass unchanged, and the new allowlist tests pass.
- [ ] `SelectorForm::ALL` drives `resolve`; `selector_precedence`, `a_missing_client_is_never_resolved_to_another` and `game_modes_select_the_client_that_runs_them` pass unchanged; `contract::target_id_forms()` returns `["key", "id", "product_code", "flavor_folder", "game_mode", "family", "path"]`.
- [ ] No behaviour or output changes: no snapshot is re-accepted; the whole gate passes.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes and `ubs` is clean on the changed files; the close reason lists the ten feature words, the per-source hosts and `requires_credential` values and the seven forms, and confirms or adjusts the five decided items.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

- `src/contract/features.rs`:
  - `features_are_unique_snake_case_and_canonically_ordered`: every word matches `[a-z][a-z0-9_]*`; no duplicates; `FEATURES` is a subsequence of `CANONICAL` (each word's canonical index is greater than the previous word's), so a word added out of place fails, naming it and its expected neighbours.
  - `each_feature_word_is_listed_exactly_when_its_surface_exists`: `EVIDENCE` has one row per `CANONICAL` word; for each row, "the evidence holds" equals "the word is in `FEATURES`". The two failure messages: "the doctor command exists: add the feature word doctor to src/contract/features.rs at its place in the canonical order" and "FEATURES lists stored_plans, but the apply command does not exist: a feature word names a surface this build has".
- `src/sources/mod.rs`: `only_curseforge_and_wago_require_a_credential`: a table over all nine `SourceId::ALL` values with the expected bool; the table covers `ALL` exactly.
- `src/net/allowlist.rs` (beside the unchanged tests):
  - `hosts_for_each_source`: a table of all nine sources with their exact host slices (the table of step 3).
  - `always_is_the_union_of_the_keyless_sources_hosts`: `ALWAYS` equals the literal nine hosts in today's order; it has no duplicate; as sets, `ALWAYS` equals the union of `hosts_for(s)` over every `s` with `!s.requires_credential()`.
  - `every_source_host_is_allowlisted`: every keyless source's host is permitted by `Allowlist::new(false, false)`; every CurseForge and Wago host is refused by it and permitted by `Allowlist::new(true, true)`; `GitHosts::new(&hosts)` permits none of them (HTTP and git never share a host).
- `src/discover/registry.rs`:
  - `selector_forms_follow_resolve_precedence`: `SelectorForm::ALL`'s wires are the seven names in order.
  - `each_selector_form_selects_on_its_own`: one case per form, built by an exhaustive `match` over `SelectorForm::ALL` (a new form without a case does not compile): `key` (a target given a `TargetKey`, selected by the key's lowercase string), `id` (`"wotlk"` → `[wotlk]`), `product_code` (`"wowf"` → `[forever]`), `flavor_folder` (`"_classic_beta_"` → `[classic-beta]`), `game_mode` (`"sod"` on a `wow_classic_era` target → that target), `family` (`"wrath-legacy"` → `[wotlk, wotlk@b]`), `path` (a tempdir made one target's client dir, selected by its path); each assertion names the form, the selector and the ids returned.
- `src/contract/mod.rs`: `target_id_forms_are_the_selector_forms`: the seven names, in order.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

None in this part. Subtask 5 proves every form against the real binary (`every_target_id_form_selects_its_client`) and every source's requests against `hosts_for` (`each_source_reaches_only_its_hosts`).

### Logging

Unit tests only: table-driven, every case named, every message naming the case, its input and the value seen.

## Considerations

- **The `resolve` change must be behaviour-neutral.** Move the seven predicates into the `match` verbatim; the existing resolve tests are the proof, and they must not be edited. `resolve` is on every `-t` path, so a regression here would misroute commands; review the diff line by line.
- **Hot spots:** `src/discover/registry.rs` is also touched by C2 (the reserved id `all` and its warning); this part changes only `resolve`'s step mechanism and adds `SelectorForm`; rebase on whichever lands first. `src/net/allowlist.rs` and `src/sources/mod.rs` have no other M4 writer (F7, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.7`, reads `hosts_for` for its online probes).
- **Forward duties of later leaves**, enforced by the tests here: D5, E3, A7 and B3 each add their feature word; C2 adds `all` to `target_id_forms()`; a new source must decide `requires_credential` (exhaustive `match`) and its hosts (`hosts_for`'s `match`).
- **Privacy and performance:** constants and `const fn`s only; nothing is read at run time.

## Dependencies

- Parent: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.2 (Registries for actions, events, env vars, features and per-source facts).
- Before it: none. It does not depend on subtasks 1, 2 or 3 and can run in parallel with them; whichever lands first creates `src/contract/mod.rs`.
- After it: subtask 5 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.2.5, Tests: the registries agree with live output) proves the forms and the hosts against the real binary.
