title: Tests: the registries agree with live output
description:
Part 5 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.2 (Registries for actions, events, env vars, features and per-source facts). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

A2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.2`) is the M4 leaf that turns the facts omaddons' self-descriptions need into enumerable registries in `src/contract/`, without changing any output: recommendation actions (`Action`, subtask 1), the stderr event vocabulary (`EventName`, `Phase`, `LogLevel` and the event structs, subtask 2), environment variables (`ENV_VARS`, subtask 3), and feature words, per-source credentials and hosts, and the `-t` forms (subtask 4). M4's `capabilities` (A4, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`), schemas (A3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`) and guide (B1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`) publish them, so every published fact must be true of the real binary (G-M4-1: "every fact in those outputs is generated from the code, so it cannot drift from what the code does"; M4-D2: a declared fact is cross-checked against behaviour by a test).

This part is that cross-check against live output. Unit tests in subtasks 1–4 prove each registry against the source; this part proves them against what the binary actually prints and does:
- the contract suite stops keeping its own hand lists of event names and actions, and checks every matrix envelope and every stderr line against the registries (M4-D11: these names are contract, and "today they are scattered literals that only test hand-lists cover");
- `tests/contract/recommendations.rs` switches its hand lists to `Action` (the plan's test plan for A2);
- a new end-to-end suite shows, in the other direction, that nothing registered is dead: every event, phase and level appears in live stderr with the fields its schema declares, every target-id form selects its client, every source's requests stay on that source's hosts, and every mirrored environment variable acts like its flag.

It is its own step because it needs all four registries, and because it is the only part of A2 that writes integration and end-to-end tests.

**Facts this part relies on** (verified at `c0ab5e9`; the registries are as subtasks 1–4 build them):
- `tests/contract/main.rs`: the suite includes `tests/common/` (`#[path = "../common/mod.rs"] mod common;`) and declares its modules `exit_sites`, `matrix`, `recommendations`, `special`, `usage_fixes` (`:8-15`). `support::check(run, code)` (`:114-225`) asserts the envelope; for `commands[]` it requires `action` to be a string and `destructive` a boolean (`:194-197`) and, for the verbs `install` and `search`, that the action names `argv[1]` (`:198-203`); for stderr it requires each line to be JSON with `event` in the hand list `"progress" | "log" | "warning" | "error"` (`:208-216`) and exactly one `error` event per failure (`:217-223`). Failures print `Run::context()` (argv, exit, stdout, stderr; `tests/common/home.rs:327-332`).
- `support::Scene::new()` (`tests/contract/main.rs:366-…`): a `Home` with the `wow` (retail) and `wow_classic` (Mists of Pandaria Classic) clients, local zips, and a WeakAuras GitHub release fixture (`WeakAuras/WeakAuras2` 5.19.2, an asset for `mainline` 120105 and `mists` 50504), with `s.json(args, code)` running `--json` through `check()`.
- `tests/contract/recommendations.rs`: the scenario table `[(&str, Builder, &str); 10]` (`:214-225`), the destructive hand list `matches!(action.as_str(), "remove_orphans" | "forget_target")` (`:249-253`), the expected coverage list repeating the ten action names (`:338-354`), and literal `"reinstall_widget"` (`:448`, `:476`) and `"check_errors"` (`:495`) lookups.
- The default ids and codes: retail is product `wow`, folder `_retail_`, id `retail`, family `mainline`, game mode `retail`; Mists Classic is product `wow_classic`, folder `_classic_`, id `classic`, game mode `mists-classic` with aliases `mop` and `mop-classic` (`src/rules.rs:1050-1079`).
- Phases are emitted as: `fetch` by release resolution (`src/resolve/cache.rs:281-284`), `download` and `verify` by the engine's plan (`src/engine/plan.rs:4509`, `:4905`), `stage` and `commit` by the transaction (`src/engine/tx.rs:840`, `:455`), `copy` by backups (`src/backup/tree.rs:323-329`); the `info` log event by `history` when `history.jsonl` ends with an incomplete line (`src/app/mod.rs:545-551`); `debug` log events with `-v` (for example "lock released: tx …", `src/app/mod.rs:306-313`). Warnings are mirrored to stderr (`src/output/mod.rs:126-128`), and stderr is NDJSON whenever it is not a terminal (`src/output/term.rs:126-130`), as in every test.
- `history --json` entries carry `actor` (`src/app/history.rs:66`); a non-terminal stdin makes the actor `agent` by default (`src/model.rs:330-356`).
- Fixture helpers: `common::tukui::{tukui_list, elvui}` and `info tukui:elvui` (as `tests/changelog.rs:399-410` uses them); `common::wowi::{wowi_file, wowi_details, details}` and `install wowi:5995 -t retail` (`tests/changelog.rs:336-355`); `common::netlog::net_log(&home)` returns the `net.log` entries with `host`, `method`, `path`, `purpose` (`tests/common/netlog.rs:15-56`).
- T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs) provides `tests/common/tlog.rs`: `tlog!()`, `log.step(label)`, `log.note`, `log.json(label, &value)`, `log.assert_eq`, `log.run(&runner, &argv) -> Ran` (argv without `omaddons`, used verbatim: `log.run` adds no `--json`), `log.cmd(&runner, &argv).env(key, value).run()`, and `Ran::{ok, exit, fails, envelope, data, events, commands, stdout, stderr}`; `Home` implements its `Runner`. A failing `Ran` assertion or panic prints `test log: <path>` and the last 20 records.

## Technical Approach

1. **`check()` uses the registries** (`tests/contract/main.rs`, inside `support`, importing `omaddons::contract::actions::Action` and `omaddons::contract::events::{EventName, LogLevel, Phase}`):
   - For every `commands[]` entry: `let action = Action::from_wire(command["action"].as_str().unwrap_or_default())`, asserting it is `Some` ("unregistered action {name}\n{ctx}"); then `command["destructive"] == action.destructive()` unless `VARIES.contains(&action)`, where `const VARIES: &[Action] = &[];` holds the actions whose instances may differ from their default (D4, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`, adds `Action::Apply`, whose hint is destructive exactly when the stored command is). The verb rule becomes `for verb in [Action::Install, Action::Search]`, comparing `verb.wire()` with the action and with `argv[1]`.
   - For every stderr line: `event` is one of `EventName::ALL`'s wires; for `progress`, `phase` is one of `Phase::ALL`'s wires; for `log`, `level` is one of `LogLevel::ALL`'s wires. The error-count rule stays.
   - The rules apply to every envelope `check()` sees: the whole contract matrix, the special and usage-fix runs, and `recommendations.rs`.

2. **`tests/contract/recommendations.rs`:**
   - The scenario table becomes `[(&str, Builder, Action); 10]` with `Action::Reinstall`, `Action::Update`, `Action::Adopt`, `Action::CheckUpdates`, `Action::RemoveOrphans`, `Action::ForgetTarget`, `Action::Inspect`, `Action::ListUnmanaged`, `Action::BackupCreate`, `Action::RefreshBackups`; the `expected` check compares `a == expected.wire()`.
   - The destructive assertion becomes `Action::from_wire(action)` (asserted `Some`, "{name}: unregistered action {action}") and `*destructive == registered.destructive()`.
   - The `match action.as_str()` arms compare with `Action::…wire()` constants or match on `Action::from_wire(…)`; the promises they check do not change.
   - The coverage list at `:338-354` is derived from the scenario table (`scenarios.iter().map(|(_, _, a)| a.wire())`) instead of repeating ten names.
   - `"reinstall_widget"` and `"check_errors"` become `Action::ReinstallWidget.wire()` and `Action::CheckErrors.wire()`.

3. **`tests/contract/registries.rs`**, a new module of the contract suite (`mod registries;` in `tests/contract/main.rs`), with a module doc stating what it proves; each test a `TestLog` scenario on its own `Scene::new()` unless it says otherwise:

   1. **`live_stderr_events_are_the_registered_events`**
      - step "install with progress": `install weakauras -t retail --json --progress json -v` → `ok()`; collect `events()`.
      - step "back up a played WTF": `common::wtf::Wtf::at(s.home.client("_retail_")).saved_variables("Foo", 100).build()`, then `backup create -t retail --json --progress json` → `ok()`; collect.
      - step "a warning": `pin WeakAuras -t retail --json` → `ok()`; `install weakauras -t retail --json` → `ok()`, its envelope's `warnings[]` contains `addon_pinned`; collect.
      - step "an info log": append `{"tx":` (no newline) to `history.jsonl` in `s.home.state()`; `history --json` → `ok()`; collect.
      - step "an error": `status -t nosuch --json` → `fails(3, "target_not_found")`; collect.
      - step "compare": `log.json` the observed sets of `event`, `phase` and `level` values and the registry sets, then `log.assert_eq` each pair: observed events = `EventName::ALL`, observed phases = `Phase::ALL`, observed levels = `LogLevel::ALL` (as sets of wires). For every collected event, with a fresh `schemars::generate::SchemaSettings::draft2020_12().for_serialize().into_generator()`, its keys are a subset of its `EventName::schema`'s `properties` and a superset of its `required`; a failure names the event line, the extra or missing keys and the step.
   2. **`every_target_id_form_selects_its_client`**
      - step "register": `status --json` → `ok()`; `targets --json` → read retail's `key`.
      - one step per form of `omaddons::contract::target_id_forms()`: the selector comes from an exhaustive `match form { "key" => retail's key, "id" => "retail", "product_code" => "wow", "flavor_folder" => "_retail_", "game_mode" => "mop", "family" => "mainline", "path" => s.home.client("_retail_") as a string, other => panic!("no probe for the target-id form {other}: add one to every_target_id_form_selects_its_client") }` and the expected id (`classic` for `mop`, `retail` otherwise); `status -t <selector> --json` → `ok()`, and `data.targets[].id` is exactly `[expected]`; `log.json("selected", ids)`.
   3. **`each_source_reaches_only_its_hosts`**
      - step "github": `let before = net_log(&s.home).len();` `install weakauras -t retail --json` → `ok()`; the entries after `before` are not empty, and every `host` is in `hosts_for(SourceId::Github)`; `log.json("hosts", hosts)`.
      - step "tukui": `tukui_list(&s.home.http, &[elvui()])`; `info tukui:elvui --json` → `ok()`; every added host is in `hosts_for(SourceId::Tukui)`.
      - step "wowinterface": a BugSack zip through `wowi_file(&s.home.http, 5995, &zip)` and `wowi_details(&s.home.http, &[5995], &[details(5995, "BugSack", "1.0", &md5)])`; `install wowi:5995 -t retail --json` → `ok()`; every added host is in `hosts_for(SourceId::Wowi)`.
      - Each failure lists the offending `net.log` lines (`method host path (purpose)`).
   4. **`each_mirrored_variable_acts_like_its_flag`**
      - For every `omaddons::contract::env::release()` row with `mirrors`, a probe chosen by an exhaustive `match` on the name (an unknown name panics "no probe for the mirrored variable {name}: add one"):
        - `OMADDONS_OFFLINE`: `status --json` → `meta.offline` false (the baseline); `log.cmd(&s.home, &["status", "--json"]).env("OMADDONS_OFFLINE", "1").run()` → true; `status --json --offline` → true.
        - `OMADDONS_FORMAT`: `status` (no flag) → stdout is not a JSON envelope (the baseline); `log.cmd(&s.home, &["status"]).env("OMADDONS_FORMAT", "json").run()` → `envelope()` parses with `command: "status"`; `status --json` → the same.
        - `OMADDONS_ACTOR`: `install weakauras -t retail --json` → `ok()`; `log.cmd(&s.home, &["pin", "WeakAuras", "-t", "retail", "--json"]).env("OMADDONS_ACTOR", "widget").run()` → `ok()`; `unpin WeakAuras -t retail --json --actor widget` → `ok()`; `history --json --limit 2` → both entries' `actor` is `widget` (not the non-terminal default `agent`).
      - One `log.step` per probe; `log.json` the values compared.

4. Every new test runs in the gate (`cargo test --test contract`), offline, on synthetic homes with recorded HTTP fixtures; none needs a real client, the network or a clone-capable filesystem.

Decided while writing this bead (confirm or adjust in the close reason):
- **The live suite is a module of the contract suite**, not a new top-level test file, so it reuses `Scene`, `check()`'s helpers and the fixture builders, and runs under `cargo test --test contract`.
- **`VARIES` starts empty** and D4 adds `apply` to it, rather than `check()` skipping the destructive comparison, so every other action's published default is verified on every matrix row.
- **The hosts check uses a GitHub install, a Tukui `info` and a WoWInterface install**, the three keyless sources with cheap fixtures; WowAce, `git:` and `url:` are covered by the unit tests' host tables (`hosts_for_each_source`, `every_source_host_is_allowlisted`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `check()` asserts, on every envelope it sees, that each `commands[].action` is a registered `Action` whose `destructive` equals its default (no `VARIES` entry yet), and that each stderr line's `event`, `phase` and `level` are registered; the hand lists at `tests/contract/main.rs:199-203` and `:213-216` are gone.
- [ ] `tests/contract/recommendations.rs` names typed actions in its scenario table, takes destructiveness from `Action::destructive()`, derives its coverage list from the table, and passes.
- [ ] `tests/contract/registries.rs` passes its four scenarios: every `EventName`, `Phase` and `LogLevel` value is observed live and every event's keys fit its schema; every target-id form selects its client; every request of the GitHub, Tukui and WoWInterface runs goes to that source's `hosts_for`; every mirrored variable acts like its flag.
- [ ] Each scenario writes its `TestLog` (`steps.jsonl` and `transcript.md` under `<CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR>/test-logs/`), with one step per phase and the compared sets recorded.
- [ ] The whole contract suite passes; no snapshot is re-accepted.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes and `ubs` is clean on the changed files; the close reason quotes the four test names, the log root, and confirms or adjusts the three decided items.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

None new: this part changes test code only. The unit tests of subtasks 1–4 must still pass.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

- `tests/contract/main.rs` (`check()`): the registry assertions above, run on every contract matrix row (success and failure), every `special.rs` and `usage_fixes.rs` run, and every run of `recommendations.rs`.
- `tests/contract/recommendations.rs`: `every_status_recommendation_runs_on_a_fresh_home`, `reinstall_widget_runs_and_clears_the_widget_issue` and `check_errors_runs_and_settles_the_cached_view`, with typed actions.
- `tests/contract/registries.rs`: the four scenarios of Technical Approach step 3, each with its steps, commands, exit codes and assertions as listed there.

### Logging

- Every scenario of `tests/contract/registries.rs` starts with `let log = tlog!();` and names each phase with `log.step` ("install with progress", "back up a played WTF", "a warning", "an info log", "an error", "compare"; "register" and one step per form; "github", "tukui", "wowinterface"; one step per mirrored variable). Every command runs through `log.run` or `log.cmd(…).env(…).run()`, so the log records each argv, environment override, exit code, envelope, stderr event and the `net.log` lines it added. Every comparison first records both sides with `log.json` and then uses `log.assert_eq` (or a `Ran` assertion), so a failure prints the step, both values and `test log: <path>` with the last 20 records. `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG=verbose cargo test --test contract registries -- --nocapture` echoes every step live (the contract suite is not one of the suites `argc e2e` runs).
- `check()` failures keep the contract suite's context: every new assertion message ends with `Run::context()` (argv, exit, stdout, stderr) and names the action, event, phase or level that failed.

## Considerations

- **Hot spot: `check()`.** A1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1`, per-command facts) adds the exit observation there, and A3 adds schema validation of `data`, `error`, `warnings[]`, `commands[]` and every stderr line. Each adds its own block; rebase on whichever lands first and keep the blocks separate. Once A3 validates stderr lines against `EventName::schema`, this part's key-set check stays as the cheap, readable first failure.
- **What can make these tests flaky:** none of them depends on time, order of parallel work or the network (recorded fixtures, `TestEnv`'s fixed environment). The torn history line is written after the state exists and is read by `history` only. If `install` ever stops emitting a phase in this scenario, the failure names the missing phase; add the command that emits it, never remove the phase from the comparison.
- **Forward duties:** a leaf that adds an action whose instances vary adds it to `VARIES`; a leaf that adds an event, a phase (A8 adds no phase; it adds `LogLevel::Trace`) or a level makes this scenario emit it, so the observed set stays equal to the registry (A8 extends step "install with progress" with `-vv` to emit `trace`); C2 adds the `all` probe when it adds the form; a new mirrored variable adds its probe.
- **Privacy:** synthetic homes only; the played `WTF/` uses the fixture builder's fake names; no real `HOME` is read.

## Dependencies

- Parent: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.2 (Registries for actions, events, env vars, features and per-source facts).
- Before it: subtasks 1 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.2.1, `Action`), 2 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.2.2, the event types), 3 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.2.3, `ENV_VARS`) and 4 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.2.4, `target_id_forms` and `hosts_for`): it tests all four against the real binary. It also needs T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs; a `blocks` edge added at filing) for `TestLog`.
- After it: this bead closes when this part does (if it is the last open subtask); A3, A4, B1 and T2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.2`, slice 1 end to end) then become unblocked.

title: Schemas with the serialize contract, declared `details`, and live validation
description:
## How to work this bead

This bead is worked through its 6 subtasks, listed below in work order. Claim a subtask, not this bead (`br ready --parent omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3` lists the ready ones). The agent that closes the last open subtask then verifies every acceptance criterion of this bead (they are the leaf's, not any one subtask's), and closes this bead with `br close omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3 --reason "done: <evidence> · found: <ids>"`. Until this bead is closed, every bead it blocks stays blocked.

1. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3.1 The published schemas: every command's data, the envelope, the events and the files, with the serialize contract: `src/contract/schema.rs`, `Envelope`/`Meta` schemas, `store::KINDS` rows that carry their schema, and `DesiredStateSchema` held equal to the parser's keys.
2. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3.2 Typed `details` in the error schema, the schema walk, and `contract::OPAQUE`: the code-discriminated union as `ErrorBody`'s schema, one path walker over every published schema, and the registry of deliberately open values with its two completeness tests.
3. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3.3 The `jsonschema` dev-dependency and the strict test-side transform, with its composition tests: the validator behind one wrapper, `cargo tree`/`cargo deny` evidence, and `unevaluatedProperties: false` at every instance position, proven on every composition case.
4. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3.4 Live validation in `support::check`, and every mismatch it finds fixed: data, error, frame and stderr validated strictly on every contract envelope; planted violations fail with readable paths; README's Stability paragraph.
5. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3.5 The rule test of M4-D55's rules 1–4 and 6, with `tests/contract/rules_allowlist.txt`: one checker per rule, the allowlist that may only shrink, and the byte-preserving fixes made here.
6. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3.6 Tests: every envelope snapshot, the `-v`-only fields, the files a session writes, and the declared-`details` report: the snapshot walker, two `TestLog` scenarios, and the report H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, the pre-freeze audit) later turns into an assertion.

Subtasks 1 and 3 touch different files and start at once. Subtask 2 needs subtask 1's schemas. Subtask 4 needs 1, 2 and 3. Subtasks 5 and 6 need subtask 4 (the rule test is generated once, from the schemas as live validation leaves them; the walker reuses subtask 4's validators) and run in parallel.

**Size L, kept as one leaf.** The parts (schemas, typed details, validation, the rule test) are one invariant: half of it would leave either unvalidated schemas or a validator with nothing to check. The subtasks split the work into commits that each pass `argc gate`; they do not split the closure. This bead closes only when all six are done, so A4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`, `capabilities`), A5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5`, `robot-docs schema`), A10 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.10`, the semantic manifest) and T2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.2`, the slice-1 demo) never see half of it.

## Background

**What this bead is.** omaddons prints one JSON envelope per command, and agents read it. Every command's `data` type already derives `schemars::JsonSchema` (the `Outcome` trait requires it, `src/output/mod.rs:35`), but no schema is ever generated, published or checked against real output, and the defaults schemars would use describe the wrong contract. This bead makes the schemas real and true:

- it generates a draft 2020-12 JSON Schema for every command's `data`, the envelope, every stderr NDJSON event and every persisted file, each with the **serialize** contract and its own fresh generator (M4-D9);
- it makes the error envelope's schema a **union discriminated by `code`**, whose variants carry each code's typed `details` specification from A9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9`, a meaning and a typed `DetailSpec` for every code) (M4-D10);
- it **validates live output** against those schemas in the contract suite, strictly (an emitted key the schema lacks fails), and every JSON envelope snapshot in the repository too;
- it adds the **rule test** that holds every schema to the contract's naming and nullability rules (M4-D55) from slice 1 on, with the pre-existing violations on an allowlist that may only shrink.

A5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5`, `robot-docs schema` and `robot-docs errors`) publishes what this bead generates; A4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`, `omaddons capabilities`) points at it; A10 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.10`, the semantic contract manifest) records it; H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, the pre-freeze contract audit) empties the allowlist this bead creates.

**What is true today** (verified at `c0ab5e9`; the full list is under "Facts this bead relies on"):

- There is no JSON Schema validator among the dev-dependencies (`Cargo.toml:43-53`), no `src/contract/` module, and no generated schema anywhere.
- schemars derives the *deserialize* contract by default. There are 96 `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = …)]` sites in `src/`, mostly for `-v`-only fields, so default schemas would mark them `required` and every real output that omits them would fail. schemars 1.2.3 has `SchemaSettings::for_serialize()` (crate source, `src/generate.rs:183`), under which a field is optional exactly when it has `skip_serializing_if`.
- schemars disambiguates duplicate type names by generation order (`Summary`, `Summary2`, …; crate source `src/generate.rs:337-346`), and `root_schema_for` copies every definition the generator has seen so far into the root (`src/generate.rs:466`). One shared generator would make a command's `$defs` names depend on what was generated before it. `Summary` alone names 4 types and `TargetRef` 3.
- schemars emits `additionalProperties: false` only for types with `deny_unknown_fields` (schemars_derive 1.2.3, `src/schema_exprs.rs:85, 264`); only 2 sites in `src/` use it. A plain validation would never notice an emitted key the schema lacks.
- `Envelope` and `Meta` (`src/output/envelope.rs:13-38`) derive only `Serialize`. `error.details` is an untyped `serde_json::Value` (`src/error.rs:512`, `:625`).
- Contract snapshots are redacted: `support::stable` (`tests/contract/main.rs:307-362`) removes `meta`, sets `tool_version` to `<version>`, and replaces ULIDs, RFC 3339 times and precondition tokens with `<ulid>`, `<time>` and `<precondition>`. ULID ids carry a `pattern` in their schema (`src/model.rs:265-276`), so `<ulid>` does not validate as it stands. That is why validation runs on live envelopes inside `check()`, and why the snapshot walker must substitute typed samples for placeholders.

**What it serves.**

- **G-M4-1, self-describing:** "every command's output has a published JSON Schema, and the contract suite validates real output against it". This bead is that sentence.
- **G-M4-5, frozen and enforced:** "at the first tag the contract is consistent (audited) … and enforced". The rule test enforces the naming rules from slice 1; the allowlist's length is the audit's remaining work, visible all milestone long.
- **Vision G4, agent ergonomics** ("the first command an agent guesses works"): an agent can validate what it receives, and branch on `details.reason` knowing the closed set of values.

**Checkpoint criteria it is responsible for** (§3.2 of the plan; H6, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the checkpoint, records the evidence):

- **Criterion 2, schemas** (with A5 for publication): "`omaddons robot-docs schema` gives a JSON Schema for every command path in `app::COMMANDS`, for the envelope and for every NDJSON event. The contract suite validates the `data` of every live envelope it produces (every matrix row, success and failure) against its command's schema, and every stderr event against its event schema. Every JSON envelope snapshot in the repository validates too. Validation in tests is strict: an emitted key that the schema lacks fails it, except under the declared `OPAQUE` paths. The strict transform is itself tested on `$ref`, maps, tagged unions and composition: it admits no unknown field and rejects no valid variant field. … Every observed `details` object validates against its code's specification, so a `details.changed` that turned into a string fails the suite. `apply`'s data validates as the wrapper variant of its own `applied.command`." (The last sentence is D5's, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`, `omaddons apply`, built on this bead's transform.)
- **Criterion 14, the contract is frozen** (through H1 and H2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.2`, the golden): the audit H1 records is this bead's rule test with an empty allowlist.
- **Criterion 17, gate and checkpoint runs:** `argc gate --all` passes from a clean checkout with the new dev-dependency.

**The decisions that shape it** (the full decision log is filed as comments on the milestone epic omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm):

- **M4-D9: schemas use the serialize contract, one generator per command, validated against live output.** Each command and each event gets a fresh `SchemaGenerator` built from `SchemaSettings::draft2020_12().for_serialize()`, so its `$defs` names depend only on that one type. New `JsonSchema` derives: `Envelope`, `Meta`, and the four NDJSON event structs (A2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.2`, moved them to module scope in `src/contract/events.rs`). `addons.toml` gets a documentation-only schema type, `DesiredStateSchema`, held equal by a test to the parser's known keys, the ones that drive `desired_unknown_key`. The contract suite's `check()` validates every live envelope's `data` against its command's schema, every stderr NDJSON line against its event schema, and `error` against `ErrorBody`. The validator is the `jsonschema` crate as a dev-dependency with `default-features = false`, pinned to an exact version, so it pulls no `reqwest` or TLS backend, which `deny.toml` bans; this is unverified until this bead runs `cargo tree` and `cargo deny`, and if either fails the fallback is `boon`, which has no network features. *Why:* the deserialize contract would mark every `-v`-only field required and every real output would fail; per-command generators avoid order-dependent `Summary2` names; validation must run on live envelopes because snapshots are redacted. *Rejected:* one generator for everything (unstable `$defs` names that change when an unrelated type is added); validating snapshots instead of live output (they are redacted); a hand-written validator for schemars' subset (correctness risk in test infrastructure); enabling `serde_json/preserve_order` for declaration-order properties (it changes every `Value` in the crate, dozens of snapshots, for a cosmetic gain: property order inside a schema carries no meaning).
- **M4-D10: `error.details` are typed per code by a recursive specification, and are part of the contract.** A9 wrote a `DetailSpec` per `error_codes!` row (allowed keys, each key's type, nesting, required or optional, nullable or not, and the closed set of every stable enum such as `reason` and `changed`). Emitters keep building `details` as `serde_json::Value`: the specification, not the emitter, is the contract. The error envelope's schema is a union discriminated by `code` whose variants carry those fragments, and the contract suite validates every observed `details` object against its code's spec. Writing the specs is A9's; validating them is this bead's. *Why:* agents branch on `details` (`reason`, `changed`, `holder`); a key list would freeze names only, not types (`changed` could turn from an array into a string unnoticed). *Rejected:* free-form `details` after the freeze; a struct per code now (churn across every error site for the same guarantee); a key list.
- **M4-D55: the contract's rules hold from slice 1; the pre-freeze audit is their final pass.** Six rules govern every command's data shape, every error's `details`, every warning, action, event and file kind:
  1. **Timestamps.** Every instant is RFC 3339 UTC with an `_at` suffix; every duration is an integer with a unit suffix (`_ms`, `_s`).
  2. **Null versus omitted.** A key in a command's schema is always present, `null` when it has no value. Omission is reserved for `-v`/`--raw-details` additions and fields documented as optional, and each must be optional in the serialize schema.
  3. **Names.** Snake case. Plurals for arrays. `id` for the user-facing identifier and `key` for ULID keys. Counts are bare nouns (`files`, `bytes`). Booleans are adjectives or `is_`-free states (`restorable`, `busy`).
  4. **Enumerations.** Snake case values. Every one has a closed set in its schema.
  5. **Command names** (A1's, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1`, done): the envelope `command` equals the canonical clap path.
  6. **`details`.** Every observed `details` object validates against its code's `DetailSpec`, and every declared key appears in at least one test.

  This bead's rule test checks rules 1–4 and 6 over every schema from slice 1 on and fails any shape that breaks them, except the pre-existing violations it lists in `tests/contract/rules_allowlist.txt`, which may only shrink. A known pre-release inconsistency is fixed in the leaf that owns the surface, with a compatibility note in its close comment and the widget, guide and snapshot changes in the same commit; cheap fixes of listed violations on surfaces no M4 leaf rewrites are made here. H1 fixes every remaining line, empties the allowlist, and walks the six rules once more. *Why:* after the tag each fix costs a major bump (M4-D56); before it, a commit and a widget update, and less the earlier it lands. *Rejected:* freezing as is (it would freeze known warts); one late window in H1 only (it propagates known mistakes through every consumer). H1's list of known items records "`-v`-only fields optional" as corrected by this bead.
- **M4-D2 (context): one contract registry feeds every description of the CLI.** A fact clap cannot provide is declared once, beside what it describes, and a test cross-checks it against behaviour. A1 declared each command's schema function (`CommandEntry.data`); this bead is the test that cross-checks it, by validating every live envelope's `data` against it.
- **M4-D18 and DEC-3 (context):** maps are `BTreeMap`, no `HashMap` in a serialized type, so schema generation is deterministic; field order is rendering order, not contract (M4-D56), which is why property order in a schema does not matter.
- **M4-D3 (context):** persisted files keep their own versions (`store::KINDS`, the journal, `addons.toml`); the contract lists them but does not tie them to `schema_version`. This bead publishes their schemas; it does not hold their field names to the wire rules (a persisted field changes only by its kind's version).

**Facts this bead relies on** (as of `c0ab5e9`):

- `trait Outcome { type Data: Serialize + schemars::JsonSchema; … }` at `src/output/mod.rs:34-35`: every command's data can produce a schema. There are about 403 `JsonSchema` derives in `src/` and 33 `Outcome` impls. `schemars = "1.2.3"` (`Cargo.toml:24`), default features (no `jiff` impls: timestamps use `#[schemars(with = "String")]`, for example `src/state/history.rs:34-35`).
- No custom `impl Serialize` exists outside tests, and no `serialize_with`. Two hand-written `JsonSchema` impls: `Error` delegates to `ErrorBody` (`src/error.rs:643-653`), and the ULID ids (`TargetKey`, `TxId`, `PlanId`, `RunId`, `BackupId`, …) give `{"type":"string","pattern":"^[0-9A-HJKMNP-TV-Z]{26}$"}` (`src/model.rs:265-276`).
- `ErrorBody` (`src/error.rs:617-626`) derives `Serialize, JsonSchema` with `code: ErrorCode, message, fix, fix_argv: Option<Vec<String>>, alternatives: Vec<Suggestion>, retryable: bool, details: serde_json::Value`. `TargetResult.error: Option<ErrorBody>` (`src/app/outcome.rs:274`) embeds it inside the `data` of every multi-target command.
- `Warning` serializes through `WarningBody` (`#[serde(into, from)]`, `src/error.rs:659-701`), whose `code` is `WarningCode` with an untagged `Item(ErrorCode)` variant. `CommandHint` (`src/error.rs:441-447`) is `{action, command, argv, destructive}`; A2 typed `action` as `contract::actions::Action`.
- The four NDJSON event structs, `EventName::ALL`, `Phase::ALL`, `LogLevel::ALL` and `EventName::schema(g)` are A2's, in `src/contract/events.rs`.
- `app::COMMANDS` rows carry `data: fn(&mut SchemaGenerator) -> Schema` (A1's `data_schema::<O>()`, which calls `g.root_schema_for::<O::Data>()`), and A1's `ENVELOPE_ONLY` lists the two envelope `command` names that are no clap path (`omaddons`, `version`), each with its `data` function. A1 also added `observe_exit` to `support::check`.
- `ErrorCode::details_schema()`, `check_details()`, `declared_detail_paths()`, `DetailSpec::opaque_paths()` and the shared `COMMON` keys (`items`, `required_by`, `journal_pending`, `recovery_error`) are A9's (`src/error.rs`, `src/error/detail_spec.rs`, `src/error/specs.rs`). A9 renders `DetailSpec::Opaque` as `{"type":"object","description":why}` and lists `items[].error.details` (an `ItemError`'s kept details) as its one opaque path.
- `store::KINDS` (`src/state/store.rs:107-185`) is `&[(&str, SchemaVersion)]`: 19 `Versioned` rows plus `("history", history::CURRENT)`. Only `store.rs` reads it (its test `every_persisted_format_has_a_kinds_row`, `:435-452`, scans the row text). `trait Versioned: Serialize + DeserializeOwned + JsonSchema` (`:89-102`). `encode` (`:320-334`) writes `{"schema_version": …, ..value}` through a function-local `Document` struct with `#[serde(flatten)]`.
- The folder journal's line type `JournalLine` (`src/engine/journal.rs:49-60`) derives `Serialize, JsonSchema` with `#[serde(tag = "type")]`; history lines are `HistoryEntry` (`src/state/history.rs:30-68`), which carries its own `schema_version` field.
- `addons.toml` is parsed with `toml::de::DeTable` (`src/state/desired.rs:37`), and its known keys exist only as match-arm literals: the file's `schema_version`, `family`, `target` (`:189-195`), a section's `addons`, `addon` (`:392-397`), an entry's `name`, `ref`, `version`, `channel`, `pinned`, `dependency`, `sha256`, `revision`, `any_flavor` (`:467-498`). Every other key reaches `unknown_key` (`:283-298`), which emits `desired_unknown_key`.
- Deliberately unconstrained `Value` fields in serialized types: `Setting.value` (`src/app/config.rs:65`), `GetData.value` and `default` (`:83`, `:85`), `SetData.value` and `previous` (`:92-93`), `ItemError.details` (`src/app/outcome.rs:180`), and the flattened `LeftOutFolder.details: serde_json::Map<String, Value>` (`src/model.rs:624-630`), which reaches `list` and `info` data and the `target_record` file.
- `support::check` (`tests/contract/main.rs:114-225`) checks one stdout document, key order, `ok`/`exit_code`/registered exit, fixes, `commands[]` argv and one stderr `error` event per failure. Every contract test goes through it (`Scene::json`, `:426-428`). The contract suite runs its tests on parallel threads, so no test can run "after" the others.
- The repository holds 159 `.snap` files (140 under `tests/`, 19 under `src/`). 123 of them are JSON envelopes: the 105 contract matrix snapshots (`tests/contract/snapshots/`, `meta` removed), 14 under `tests/snapshots/`, and 4 under `src/output/snapshots/`. Three of the last four (`omaddons__output__tests__envelope_success.snap`, `…_partial_success.snap`, `…_check_failed.snap`) are renderer fixtures whose `data` is a synthetic struct (`{zeta, alpha, map}`) under a real command name. Placeholders seen in envelope snapshots: `<ulid>`, `<version>`, `<time>`, `<root>`, `<tx>`, `<meta>`, `<key>`, `<precondition>`, `<run>`, `<checked_at>`, `<binary>`, `<addon>`, `<ref>`, `<path>`, and `"<bytes>"`, which replaces an integer (`tests/contract/matrix.rs:979`).
- `src/source_scan.rs` (`production_code`, `sources`) is `#[cfg(test)]` in the library (`src/lib.rs:37-38`), usable by unit tests in `src/` only.
- `deny.toml` bans tokio, reqwest, native-tls, openssl-sys, aws-lc-rs and aws-lc-sys, allows seven licenses, and checks dev-dependencies too (its `[graph]` has no `exclude-dev`). The gate runs `cargo clippy --locked` and `cargo test --locked`, so `Cargo.lock` changes with the dependency.

**Where the plan and the code disagree** (each handled by a "Decided while writing this bead" note below, and listed in the close comment):

1. §6.4 of the plan says "the schemas carry no `pattern` or `format` on ids, so redacted snapshots validate". At `c0ab5e9` every ULID id's schema has a `pattern` (`src/model.rs:265-276`), and M4-D9 itself says "`<ulid>` fails the ULID pattern". The contract snapshots also drop `meta` (`tests/contract/main.rs:310-313`), which the envelope requires, and one replaces an integer with the string `"<bytes>"` (`tests/contract/matrix.rs:979`). The walker therefore substitutes typed samples for placeholders; the patterns stay (they are contract information A10 records).
2. Three envelope snapshots under `src/output/snapshots/` carry synthetic `data` under real command names; they cannot validate against those commands' schemas. The walker validates their frame only, by an explicit three-line list with the reason.
3. M4-D9 speaks of "the parser's known-key lists"; there are none, only match arms (`src/state/desired.rs:189-195`, `:392-397`, `:467-498`), and the parser is `toml::de`, not `toml_edit` as §2.1 says. This bead adds the three lists and a source scan that holds the match arms equal to them.
4. The plan cites "config values (`config.rs:65-93`)"; the file is `src/app/config.rs`, not `src/state/config.rs`.
5. The plan's `OPAQUE` source scan covers `src/app`, `src/output`, `src/contract` and `src/doctor`, which misses `LeftOutFolder.details` in `src/model.rs:624-630`; it reaches `data` all the same. A schema-walk completeness test is added beside the scan.
6. `store::KINDS` rows are tuples with no room for the schema function the plan asks for (`src/state/store.rs:107`); the rows become a small struct.
7. The plan's list of instance positions for the strict transform (the root, `properties` values, `items`, `prefixItems`, `additionalProperties`) omits `patternProperties`, which schemars emits for maps keyed by a patterned type (`BTreeMap<TargetKey, _>`; schemars 1.2.3 `src/json_schema_impls/maps.rs`). The transform treats `patternProperties` values as instance positions too.

## Technical Approach

### 1. Files and module layout

| File | What | Subtask |

### 2. The published schemas (subtask 1)

#### 2.1 Settings and generators

```rust
/// The settings every published schema is generated with (M4-D9).
pub fn settings() -> schemars::generate::SchemaSettings {
    schemars::generate::SchemaSettings::draft2020_12().for_serialize()
}
/// A fresh generator: one per command, event, file or error variant, so `$defs` names
/// depend only on the one type being described.
pub fn generator() -> schemars::SchemaGenerator { settings().into_generator() }
```

No generator is ever reused across two roots (`root_schema_for` copies every definition the generator has seen into its root). The published schemas are open: no `additionalProperties: false` is added (M4-D9: a newer minor's additions must not break an older consumer's validator); strictness is a test-side transform (§5 below). Serialized with `serde_json` without `preserve_order`, every schema's object keys are sorted, so the bytes are deterministic.

#### 2.2 Command data

- `pub fn command_schema(entry: &CommandEntry) -> Schema`: `(entry.data)(&mut generator())`, with `title` set to the command path (`"backup restore"`).
- `pub fn command_schemas() -> BTreeMap<&'static str, Schema>`: one per `app::COMMANDS` row (criterion 2: "every command path in `app::COMMANDS`"). A5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5`, `robot-docs schema`) publishes this map as `commands`.

### 3. Typed `details`: the error union (subtask 2)

`ErrorBody` drops its `JsonSchema` derive and gets a hand-written impl in `src/error.rs`:

```rust
/// The error object's schema: one variant per code, discriminated by `code` (M4-D10).
impl JsonSchema for ErrorBody {
    fn schema_name() -> Cow<'static, str> { "ErrorBody".into() }
    fn json_schema(g: &mut SchemaGenerator) -> Schema {
        let alternatives = g.subschema_for::<Vec<Suggestion>>();
        let variants: Vec<serde_json::Value> = ErrorCode::ALL.iter().map(|c| error_variant_value(*c, &alternatives)).collect();
        json_schema!({ "oneOf": variants })
    }
}
/// One code's variant: `code` const, the common fields, and the code's own `details` schema.
pub(crate) fn error_variant_value(code: ErrorCode, alternatives: &Schema) -> serde_json::Value {
    json!({
        "type": "object",
        "description": code.meaning(),
        "properties": {
            "code": {"type": "string", "const": code.wire()},
            "message": {"type": "string"},
            "fix": {"type": "string"},
            "fix_argv": {"type": ["array", "null"], "items": {"type": "string"}},
            "alternatives": alternatives,
            "retryable": {"type": "boolean"},
            "details": code.details_schema(),
        },
        "required": ["code", "message", "fix", "fix_argv", "alternatives", "retryable", "details"],
    })
}
```

- Because `ErrorBody`'s own schema is the union, every place an `ErrorBody` appears carries typed `details`: the envelope's `error`, `TargetResult.error` inside multi-target `data` (`src/app/outcome.rs:274`), and any `Error` field (whose impl delegates to `ErrorBody`, `src/error.rs:645-653`). Decided while writing this bead: the hand-written impl, rather than a union only in `envelope_schema()`, because `TargetResult.error` carries the same per-code `details` (A9's consumers table says so) and rule 6 covers every observed `details` object.
- `pub fn error_schema() -> Schema` in `src/contract/schema.rs`: `generator().root_schema_for::<ErrorBody>()`. `pub fn error_variant(code: ErrorCode) -> Schema`: one variant as a root (fresh generator, `$defs` for `Suggestion`, `title` "`<wire>` error"), for the contract suite's precise diagnostics and for A10's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.10`, the semantic manifest) error nodes.
- `oneOf` is right: the `const` discriminator makes the variants mutually exclusive. It is also the shape schemars emits for internally tagged enums, so A10 walks it like any tagged union.

Semantically it changes nothing (an absent `additionalProperties` already allows extra keys), but it makes the opaque position structurally open, so the strict transform leaves it open without any lookup (§5.2 below). ### 4. The schema walk and `contract::OPAQUE` (subtask 2)

#### 4.1 The walk

`pub fn walk(root: &serde_json::Value, visit: &mut dyn FnMut(&Visit<'_>))` in `src/contract/schema.rs`: a traversal of one published schema with `$ref`s resolved, used by the `OPAQUE` tests here, the rule test (§7 below) and A10's manifest.

- **Paths** use A9's syntax: `a` for a top-level key, `a.b` for key `b` of the object at `a`, `a[]` for an array's items, plus `a{}` for a map's values (`additionalProperties` or `patternProperties` values). The root is the empty path, printed `.`.
- **References**: `#/$defs/<name>` and `#` are resolved inline; a definition already on the current path is not entered again (recursion), and is visited once.
- **In-place applicators** (`allOf`, `anyOf`, `oneOf`) contribute their positions at the same path: a field present in two variants is visited once per variant, at one path.
- It reports two kinds of visit: `Visit::Position { path, node }` for every schema position (the root, each property value, items, map values), and `Visit::Property { path, name, node, required, parent }` for every property of every object node reached (with `required` read from that object node's own `required`).
- Unit tests: a table of synthetic schemas (a `$ref` used twice, a self-recursive definition, an `anyOf` with `null`, a `oneOf` of two variants sharing a field, a map with `additionalProperties`, a map with `patternProperties`, `prefixItems`), each with its expected sorted list of visited paths.

#### 4.2 `contract::OPAQUE`

```rust
/// A schema position that admits any value on purpose (M4-D9): the strict transform leaves it
/// open (it is structurally open), and A10's manifest records it as `opaque`.
pub struct Opaque {
    pub scope: &'static str,   // "envelope", "error", "event <name>", "command <path>", "command *", "file <kind>"
    pub path: &'static str,    // walk syntax; a leading "**." matches at any depth
    pub source: &'static str,  // the Rust type and field it comes from: "Setting.value"
    pub reason: &'static str,  // one sentence: why the value is unconstrained
}
pub const OPAQUE: &[Opaque] = &[ … ];
```

A position is **open** when its resolved node, or any in-place branch at it, is the boolean `true`, the empty schema `{}`, or an object schema with `additionalProperties: true` or `unevaluatedProperties: true`.

The starting inventory (verified by reading the code at `c0ab5e9`; the walk is the authority, and each row's reason is one sentence):

| scope | path | source | reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| `envelope` | `data` | `Envelope.data` | a command's data is described by its own schema (`robot-docs schema <command>`) and validated against it |
| `error` | `details.items[].error.details` | `ItemError.details` (A9's `COMMON.items`) | an item error keeps the subset of its own code's details that the item needs |
| `command *` | `**.items[].error.details` | `ItemError.details` | the same, inside a multi-target command's data |
| `command config` | `settings[].value` | `Setting.value` | a config value is whatever TOML value its key admits; each key's type is published with the config keys |
| `command config get` | `value`, `default` | `GetData.value`, `GetData.default` | as above |
| `command config set` | `value`, `previous` | `SetData.value`, `SetData.previous` | as above |
| `command list`, `command info` | `**.left_out[]` | `LeftOutFolder.details` | a left-out folder's reason carries that reason's own fields, kept as written so a reason a newer build wrote still reads |
| `file target_record` | `**.left_out[]` | `LeftOutFolder.details` | as above |

#### 5.2 The strict transform

`pub fn strict(schema: &serde_json::Value) -> Result<serde_json::Value, StrictError>` in `tests/contract/validate.rs`, test-side only (the published schemas stay open). It returns a new value and never mutates its input.

- It adds `"unevaluatedProperties": false` at every **instance position**: the root, each `properties` value, each `patternProperties` value, `items` (and each `prefixItems` entry) and `additionalProperties` when it is a schema, wherever those positions occur, inside `$defs` entries included. The keyword goes beside that position's in-place applicators (`allOf`, `anyOf`, `oneOf`, `$ref`), which in draft 2020-12 contribute their evaluated properties to it, so every valid variant field still passes.
- It **never** adds it at the root of a branch applied in place (an `allOf`/`anyOf`/`oneOf` entry) or at the root of a `$defs` entry (reached only through a `$ref`): in draft 2020-12 a branch's `unevaluatedProperties` sees only its own annotations, and would reject a sibling branch's valid fields. It recurses into those roots' own instance positions.
- It leaves **open positions** untouched: the boolean `true`, the empty schema `{}`, and any object schema that already has `additionalProperties: true` or any `unevaluatedProperties`. Every `contract::OPAQUE` position is open in this sense (§3 and §4.2 above), so the transform needs no lookup of `OPAQUE`, and the `OPAQUE` completeness tests guarantee the two agree.
- It **refuses**, with `StrictError { keyword, path }`, any keyword it does not model: `not`, `if`, `then`, `else`, `contains`, `dependentSchemas`, `dependencies`, `propertyNames`, `unevaluatedItems`, `additionalItems`, a `$defs` that is not at the root, and any unknown keyword. Known non-applicator keywords (`type`, `enum`, `const`, `required`, `$ref`, `$schema`, `$id`, `$comment`, `$anchor`, `title`, `description`, `default`, `examples`, `deprecated`, `readOnly`, `writeOnly`, `format`, `pattern`, `minimum`, `maximum`, `exclusiveMinimum`, `exclusiveMaximum`, `multipleOf`, `minLength`, `maxLength`, `minItems`, `maxItems`, `uniqueItems`, `minProperties`, `maxProperties`) pass through. Decided while writing this bead: refusing is safer than guessing, since `unevaluatedProperties: false` inside a `not` would invert its meaning; schemars emits none of the refused keywords for omaddons' types, so a refusal means a new shape needs a decision.
- It is idempotent: `strict(strict(s)) == strict(s)`.

### 6. Live validation in `support::check` (subtask 4)

- `tests/contract/validate.rs` gains `Schemas`, built once per process (`std::sync::OnceLock`): a strict `Validator` per `data_schema_for` name (every `COMMANDS` path and the two `ENVELOPE_ONLY` names), per `error_variant(code)` for every `ErrorCode::ALL`, per event in `event_schemas()`, and one for the envelope frame (`envelope_schema()`). A schema the transform refuses, or that does not compile, fails with its name and the reason.
- `pub fn validate_envelope(envelope: &Value, stderr: &str) -> Result<(), String>` validates four parts and collects every failure (at most 20 per part, then "… and N more"):
  1. `data`, when present, against its `command`'s schema; an unknown `command` is itself a failure;
  2. `error`, when present, against `error_variant(<its code>)`, so `details` is checked against its `DetailSpec`;
  3. the envelope with `data` and `error` removed, against the envelope schema: the top-level keys, `partial`, `warnings[]`, `commands[]` and `meta`;
  4. each stderr line against the schema of its `event`.

  The message names the part, each failure's instance path, message and schema path, then the run's context: `schema validation failed for <command>: data /targets/0/items/1: … (schema /properties/targets/items/…/unevaluatedProperties)`.
- **Re-explaining a union failure.** When a failure inside `data` reports a `oneOf` at an instance whose value is an object with a registered `code` (an embedded `ErrorBody`), the message re-validates that object against `error_variant(code)` and reports those failures instead, because "not valid under any of the given schemas" names no field. Decided while writing this bead.
- `support::check` calls `validate_envelope(&envelope, &run.stderr)` after its existing structural checks (so a broken envelope still fails with today's message first) and panics with its message. Every envelope of `matrix.rs`, `special.rs`, `recommendations.rs`, `usage_fixes.rs` and the new suites goes through it. ### 7. The rule test and the allowlist (subtask 5)

`tests/contract/rules.rs`, a module of the contract test binary. It walks the published (open) schemas with `contract::schema::walk` and runs one pure checker per rule. Scopes and paths are those of the walk (§4.1 above): `command <path>` (the command's data; paths relative to `data`), `envelope` (the frame), `error <code>` (one variant; paths relative to the error object, so details keys read `details.reason`), `event <name>`, and `file` (kind names only).

| id | Rule | Violation |
|---|---|---|
| `r1-at-type` | 1 | a property named `*_at` whose schema admits anything but a string (or a string and `null`) |
| `r1-instant-name` | 1 | a property named `at`, `time`, `date`, `timestamp` or `when`, or ending in `_time`, `_date`, `_timestamp` or `_on`: an instant not named `*_at` |
| `r1-duration-type` | 1 | a property ending in `_ms` or `_s` whose schema is not an integer (or an integer and `null`) |
| `r1-duration-name` | 1 | an integer or number property named `duration`, `elapsed`, `timeout`, `ttl`, `age` or `interval`, or ending in `_duration`, `_secs`, `_seconds`, `_millis`, `_age`, `_timeout`, `_ttl` or `_interval`: a duration without `_ms` or `_s` |
| `r2-omittable-undocumented` | 2 | a property its object does not require whose `description` does not say when it is omitted (none of, ignoring case: `omitted`, `absent`, `present when`, `present iff`, `present only`, `only with`, `only when`, `only under`, `` `-v` ``, `--raw-details`) |
| `r2-verbose-required` | 2 | a property whose description says it is `-v`-only (contains `` `-v` only``) but which its object requires: a `-v`-only field that is not optional in the serialize schema |
| `r3-name-case` | 3 | a property name, or a `file` kind name, that is not `^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(_[a-z0-9]+)*$` |
| `r3-array-plural` | 3 | an array property whose name ends neither in `s` nor in `argv` |
| `r3-bool-is` | 3 | a boolean property whose name starts with `is_` |
| `r3-count-name` | 3 | an integer property ending in `_count` or starting with `num_`, `n_` or `count_` |
| `r3-key-ulid` | 3 | a property named exactly `key` whose schema is not the ULID string (`^[0-9A-HJKMNP-TV-Z]{26}$`) |
| `r4-value-case` | 4 | an `enum` or `const` string value that is not `^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(_[a-z0-9]+)*$` |
| `r4-open-enum` | 4 | a property named `kind`, `status`, `state`, `reason`, `mode`, `action`, `op`, `class`, `level`, `phase`, `event`, `severity`, `confidence`, `verdict`, `channel`, `type` or `result` whose schema is a plain string with no `enum` or `const`: an enumeration without a closed set |
| `r6-details-object` | 6 | an error variant whose `details` is not an object schema (A9 guarantees one; this keeps it so) |

- **Scope of the rules.** Rules 1, 3 and 4 apply to command data, the envelope frame, every error variant (its `details` included) and every event. Rule 2 applies to command data, the frame and events, not to `details`: whether a details key appears depends on the construction site, which rule 6 governs. File schemas are checked for their kind names only. Decided while writing this bead, because a persisted field changes only through its kind's version (M4-D3), not through a wire audit. Rule 6's live half (every observed `details` validates) is subtask 4's validation, which admits no allowlist; its "every declared key appears in a test" half is subtask 6's report.
- **What counts.** Each checker is a pure function from a visited property or value to an optional violation. A violation's identity is the line `<rule> | <scope> | <path>` (for `r4-value-case`, the path of the property or position holding the value). Identical lines (a field in two variants) count once.
- **`tests/contract/rules_allowlist.txt`**: one violation per line in that exact form, sorted, unique; `#` starts a comment line, and the file opens with a comment saying what it is, that it may only shrink, and that H1 empties it. Decided while writing this bead: no regeneration variable. On the first write, the failing test prints every current violation in file form, and the implementer copies them in by hand; after that, a new violation fails with "a new shape breaks rule <n> (`<rule id>`): fix the shape; never add to `tests/contract/rules_allowlist.txt` (M4-D55)", and a line no violation matches fails with "the allowlist line no longer matches a violation: remove it (the list may only shrink)".
- **`EXCEPTIONS`**, a coded list in `rules.rs` (`(rule, scope pattern, path pattern, reason)`), empty here: permanent, reasoned exceptions for vocabularies omaddons does not own, such as the external doctor contract's state names and severities (E3 decided to add theirs there, never to the allowlist; whichever of this bead and E3 lands second adds them). H1 audits every exception. A checker that flags something H1 judges compliant is a defect in the checker, narrowed with the reason recorded.
- **Expected entries** at `c0ab5e9` (examples, not a list to copy): `history`'s `entries[].at` (`r1-instant-name`); `config`'s `settings[].key` and `config get`/`set`'s `key`, `desired_state_invalid`'s and `state_corrupt`'s `details.key` (`r3-key-ulid`); every family name with a hyphen (`vanilla-legacy`; `Family` is `kebab-case`, `src/rules.rs:148`) under `r4-value-case`; `Setting.source` (`r4-open-enum`; a `&'static str`, "file" or "default"); `left_out` (`r3-array-plural`); `tried[].reason` in three error variants (A9 noted it as free text, `r4-open-enum`).
- **Cheap fixes made here** (decided while writing this bead: byte-preserving only, so no snapshot, widget or guide changes): doc comments that say when an omittable key is omitted (most `r2-omittable-undocumented` lines), and closed enums for string fields whose values are already a fixed literal set and serialize to the same bytes (`Setting.source` as an enum of `file` and `default`). Renames, and anything that changes a byte, wait for H1 or the owning leaf. Each fix removes its allowlist line in the same commit and is listed in the close comment.

- `tests/contract/details_report.rs`, `declared_details_keys_no_contract_test_observes` (subtask 6, ignored), as Technical Approach §8 above.

### Logging

- `TestLog` (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, `tests/common/tlog.rs`) in every scenario that runs commands: `the_harness_rejects_schema_violations` records one `log.step` per case, the planted envelope with `log.json("planted", …)`, and the caught message with `log.note`; `verbose_only_fields_are_optional_and_validate` one step per command and flag set, every run through `log.run`, and `log.json("field", …)` of the value compared; `every_file_a_session_writes_validates_against_its_kind` one step per command, `log.tree` of `<state>` and `<cache>` after each, and `log.json("validated", {kind: count})` plus the unreached kinds.
- The walker is not a command scenario: it logs, on failure, the snapshot file, the substituted envelope (pretty), and every failure; on success it prints one summary line (`validated 123 envelope snapshots (3 frame-only) in 159 .snap files`).
- Pure tests (strict, rules, unit tests): every case has a name; every assertion message names the case and prints the input schema and instance, the expected and the actual result.
- `validate_envelope`'s own failure message is the diagnostic for every contract test: the part, each instance path, message and schema path, then the run's argv, exit, stdout and stderr (`Run::context`).

No checkpoint-only test belongs to this bead.

## Considerations

- **Risk #2 (likelihood medium, impact medium; owner this bead): live validation finds many schema/output mismatches and the bead balloons.** Mitigations: A9's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9`, meanings and `DetailSpec`s) starting inventory and its "Required only when every site emits it" rule shrink the details mismatches; the bytes are the default truth, so most fixes are one attribute or one spec line; the trigger at 40 distinct mismatches files the rest as bugs that block H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, the pre-freeze audit), so the leaf closes without hiding them.
- **Risk #15 (likelihood low, impact low; owner this bead): `jsonschema` violates `deny.toml`** (pulls `reqwest` or a TLS backend). Default features off, version pinned, the `cargo tree` results recorded, `boon` as the fallback; `deny.toml` is never widened for it.
- **The validator's 2020-12 support is itself under test.** `unevaluatedProperties` must see annotations through `$ref` and `oneOf`; the composition tests are where a validator bug would show, and they decide the crate.
- **Hot spots (§10.5 of the plan):**
  - `src/error.rs` (A9, A3, D4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`, the plan store), D5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`, `omaddons apply`), E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, `doctor diagnose`), E10 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.10`, the old fixes point at the doctor), F*, H1): **A9, then A3**; later leaves append rows with their specs. This bead touches `ErrorBody`'s schema impl and, for mismatches, A9's spec consts; never reflow a row a peer added.
  - `src/output/stderr.rs`, `envelope.rs`, `mod.rs` (A2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.2`, the action and event registries), A3, A8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.8`, verbosity levels), E3): no ordering rule; this bead adds derives and doc comments to `envelope.rs` only.
  - `tests/contract/main.rs`: A1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1`, per-command facts) added exit observation, A2 action and event checks, E3 adds a doctor mode; keep `validate_envelope` one call in `check`, in its own block.
  - `tests/contract/rules_allowlist.txt`: this bead creates it; only H1 and owning leaves that fix a listed violation touch it after, and only to remove lines.
  - `src/state/store.rs` `KINDS`: D4, E3 and E5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`, the repair transaction) add rows in the `KindRow` form.
  - `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock`: A7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.7`, completions) adds `clap_complete`; rebase, and rerun `argc gate --all`.
- **Later leaves rely on this bead's tests staying in the gate:** every new shape passes the rule test (common rule 6), every new `Value` field gets an `OPAQUE` row, every new persisted file a `KINDS` row (the files scenario fails otherwise), and every new placeholder a walker table row.
- **What could go wrong, and how it shows.**
  - A `#[serde(flatten)]` of a map makes the whole object open (`additionalProperties: true`): the `OPAQUE` walk reports it, and it needs a row with a reason or a typed field.
  - An untagged enum whose branches overlap lets `anyOf` admit an object mixing both branches' fields; the strict transform cannot catch a field valid in either branch. Review the untagged types (`src/app/help.rs:31`, `src/app/adopt.rs:79`, `src/app/list.rs:122`, `src/backup/mod.rs:147`, `src/state/config.rs:142`, `:168`) once, and record in the close comment that their branches are disjoint or why not.
  - The union makes every multi-target command's published schema carry one variant per error code: the schemas grow, which is expected.
  - A validator that silently ignores `unevaluatedProperties` would make every strict test pass vacuously; the planted cases of subtask 4 and the composition tests of subtask 3 fail if it does.
- **Gate time.** Validators compile once per test process; validating one envelope is fast compared with running the binary. Record the contract suite's wall time before and after subtask 4 in its close comment. The details report is `#[ignore]`d because it reruns the whole suite.
- **Privacy.** Failure messages print instance values; every test home is synthetic (`FAKEACCT`/`FakeRealm`/`FakeChar` where a `WTF/` exists), and the files scenario runs `assert_private_all(stdout, stderr)` over each step with `--progress json`.
- **Compatibility with older builds:** nothing persisted changes; schemas are generated, never stored.
- **Defaults applied (§8.1 of the plan):** no new error or warning code (1); stable sorted order everywhere (3); fail closed on anything that cannot be fully read, here a schema the transform cannot model (6).
- **Decided defaults, collected:** every "Decided while writing this bead" above. The implementer confirms or adjusts each in the close comment.

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M4 plan, 2026-10-24).**

**Why this bead.** Every omaddons command already declares a typed `data` that derives `JsonSchema`, but nothing generates a schema, nothing checks one against what the binary prints, and the defaults would describe the wrong contract: schemars derives the deserialize contract, under which the 96 `skip_serializing_if` fields (mostly `-v`-only) would be required, and it never closes an object, so a validator would not notice a key the schema lacks. `error.details`, the object agents branch on, is an untyped `Value`. After this bead, every command's data, the envelope, every stderr event and every persisted file has a draft 2020-12 schema generated with the serialize contract; the error schema is a union of one variant per code carrying its typed `details`; and the contract suite validates every envelope it produces, every stderr event and every envelope snapshot in the repository against them, strictly. The rule test holds every shape to the contract's naming rules from slice 1, so H1's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, the pre-freeze audit) remaining work is visible all milestone as the length of one allowlist. It is what makes G-M4-1's "every command's output has a published JSON Schema, and the contract suite validates real output against it" true, and what A4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`, `capabilities`), A5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5`, `robot-docs schema`), A10 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.10`, the semantic manifest) and the slice-1 demo stand on.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M4-D9:** the serialize contract (`SchemaSettings::draft2020_12().for_serialize()`), a fresh generator per command, event and file so `$defs` names depend only on one type; `Envelope`, `Meta` (and A2's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.2`, the action and event registries) event structs) derive `JsonSchema`; `DesiredStateSchema` for `addons.toml`, held equal to the parser's keys; validation of live envelopes in `check()`; `jsonschema` with default features off, pinned, proven by `cargo tree` and `cargo deny`, `boon` as the fallback.
- **M4-D10:** the error schema is a union discriminated by `code`, each variant carrying A9's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9`, meanings and `DetailSpec`s) `DetailSpec` as its `details` schema; every observed `details` is validated against it; emitters keep building `Value`.
- **M4-D55:** rules 1–4 and 6 are a test from slice 1, with an allowlist of the violations that predate it which may only shrink; cheap fixes here, renames left to H1 or the owning leaf; "`-v`-only fields optional" is this bead's correction, made by the serialize contract and checked by the rule test.
- **M4-D2 (context):** the schema function A1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1`, per-command facts) declared beside each command is cross-checked against behaviour by validating every live envelope's `data` against it.
- **M4-D3 (context):** persisted files publish their schemas but keep their own versions, so the rule test checks only their kind names.

**Alternatives rejected that matter here.**
- One generator for every schema: `$defs` names (`Summary2`) would change whenever an unrelated type is added.
- Validating snapshots as they are, instead of live output: they are redacted (`<ulid>` fails the ULID pattern, `meta` is stripped); the walker substitutes typed samples so it can validate them too.
- A hand-written validator for schemars' subset: correctness risk in the very code that is meant to catch errors.
- `serde_json/preserve_order` for declaration-order properties: dozens of snapshots change for a cosmetic gain.
- Strict schemas published (`additionalProperties: false`): a newer minor's additions would break an older consumer's validator; strictness stays a test-side transform.
- A union of error variants only in the envelope schema: `TargetResult.error` inside multi-target `data` carries the same per-code `details` and would stay untyped; the union is `ErrorBody`'s own schema instead.
- A regeneration variable for the allowlist: it would make "may only shrink" one environment variable away from meaningless.

**Risks and how they are watched.**
- Risk #2, live validation finds many mismatches and the bead balloons: each mismatch is a real bug fixed here, with the emitted bytes as the default truth; past 40 distinct mismatches the rest become bugs discovered from subtask 4 that block H1, listed in a file that may only shrink.
- Risk #15, `jsonschema` violates `deny.toml`: default features off, pinned, the `cargo tree` results recorded, `boon` as the fallback, `deny.toml` never widened for it.
- A validator that mishandles `unevaluatedProperties` through `$ref` or `oneOf` would make strictness vacuous: the composition tests (subtask 3) and the planted violations (subtask 4) fail if it does, and decide the crate.

**What it unblocks, and why they wait.** A5 publishes these schemas as `robot-docs schema` and the specs as `robot-docs errors`, so it needs them generated and proven. A4's `capabilities` points at `robot-docs schema <path>` and publishes `details_schema`, which must be proven against live output first. A10's semantic manifest normalizes these schemas and error variants and records `OPAQUE` as `opaque`; without them it has nothing to pin. T2's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.2`) slice-1 demo ("`robot-docs schema` validates the whole matrix and every envelope snapshot, `details` included") runs on this bead's validators and walker.

**How it serves the milestone.** G-M4-1 (self-describing): every output has a published schema that the suite proves. G-M4-5 (frozen and enforced): the rule test is the continuous half of the audit, and the allowlist is H1's work list. Slice 1, "Self-describing", demos it.

**Confidence.** High for generation and the transform, which build on schemars' existing derives and a well-defined draft 2020-12 rule; medium for the size, because the number of mismatches live validation will find is unknown until it runs, which is why the trigger and its follow-up path are part of the bead.

comments.text:
**The M4 plan's entry for A3, verbatim (M4 plan, 2026-10-24).** This is the M4 plan's entry, lines 3709–3742 of the plan, kept as provenance. The description above is the authoritative, elaborated version; where they differ, the description was decided while filing and says why.

#### A3 Schemas with the serialize contract, declared `details`, and live validation
- **Type** feature · **P1** · **size-L** · **slice-1**
- **Blocked by:** A1 (`entry.data`), A2 (event types), A9 (the code table and its `DetailSpec`s).
- **Unblocks:** A4, A5, A10.
- **Background.** §2.1's schema hazards and M4-D9 and M4-D10. The vision's checkpoint: "`robot-docs schema` validates every snapshot-tested JSON response". The naming and nullability rules (M4-D55) are established here, as a test every later shape must pass.
- **Technical approach.**
  1. `src/contract/schema.rs`:
     - `fn command_schema(entry) -> Schema`, using `SchemaSettings::draft2020_12().for_serialize()`, a fresh generator per call;
     - `fn envelope_schema()`;
     - `fn error_schema()`: a union discriminated by `code`, one variant per code with `code` as `const` and its `DetailSpec` rendered as the `details` schema;
     - `fn event_schemas()`;
     - `fn file_schemas()`, which needs a schema function on each `store::KINDS` row (extend `Versioned` with `fn schema(g)`) plus the journal line types.
  2. `Envelope` and `Meta` derive `JsonSchema`.
  3. `DesiredStateSchema` (a documentation-only type in `src/state/desired.rs`), and a test that its property names equal the parser's known-key lists.
  4. **The dev-dependency.** `jsonschema` with `default-features = false`, pinned to an exact version. Record in the close comment that `cargo tree -e normal,dev -i reqwest` and `cargo tree -e normal,dev -i aws-lc-rs` are both empty, and run `argc gate --all` (cargo deny checks dev-dependencies). If either fails, switch to `boon` and record `decided:`.
  5. **`tests/contract/support::check`** validates `data`, `error` (against its code's variant, so `details` is checked against its `DetailSpec`), `warnings[]`, `commands[]` and every stderr line against their schemas, failing with the instance and schema paths.
  6. **Strict validation in tests** (§6.4): the transform adding `unevaluatedProperties: false` at every instance position, never at the root of an in-place branch or a `$defs` entry, test-side only; its own tests over `$ref` used two ways, a map, an internally tagged enum, a flattened struct and `oneOf` with shared fields; and `contract::OPAQUE` with its test that every serialized `Value` field is listed.
  7. **The snapshot walker**: every `.snap` file in the repository (`tests/` and `src/`) whose body is a JSON envelope validates against its command's schema.
  8. A test listing declared `details` keys that no test observes, printed as a report. H1 makes it empty and turns it into an assertion.
  9. **The rule test, enforcing from here on.** A test that checks M4-D55's rules 1–4 and 6 over every schema. Every violation that exists when this leaf lands is written to `tests/contract/rules_allowlist.txt`, one per line with the rule broken. The test fails on any violation not on the allowlist, and on any allowlist line that no longer matches a violation, so the list can only shrink. From slice 1, every new shape is held to the rules, and H1's remaining work is visible as the list's length. Cheap fixes of listed violations on surfaces no M4 leaf rewrites are made here, with the widget and snapshot changes in the same commit.
  10. `-v`-only fields optional in every schema (the serialize contract makes them so; the rule test checks it).
- **Acceptance criteria.**
  - Every matrix envelope, every stderr event and every envelope snapshot validates, under the strict transform.
  - A `details` value of the wrong type, an undeclared key and an undeclared `reason` value each fail the suite (unit tests plant them). An emitted key missing from a schema fails validation (a unit test plants one).
  - The strict transform's own tests pass: unknown fields fail and valid variant fields pass, in every composition case.
  - `-v`-only fields are optional in their schemas.
  - The rule test passes with the allowlist, fails on a planted new violation, and fails on a stale allowlist line.
  - `jsonschema` (or `boon`) passes `cargo deny`, with the two `cargo tree` results recorded.
- **Test plan.** Unit tests for the generator settings (a type with a `skip_serializing_if` field is optional) and for the transform. Contract: every row now validates. A deliberate schema mismatch in a unit test fails with a readable path.
- **Considerations.**
  - **Size L, kept as one leaf.** The parts (schemas, typed details, validation, the rule test) are one invariant: half of it would leave either unvalidated schemas or a validator with nothing to check.
  - **Risk:** live validation finds real mismatches between schemas and output. Each is fixed in this leaf (they are bugs) and listed in the close comment.
  - **Hot spot:** `src/error.rs`. A9 first, then A3.
