title: Typed `details` in the error schema, the schema walk, and `contract::OPAQUE`
description:
Part 2 of 6 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3 (Schemas with the serialize contract, declared `details`, and live validation). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

The parent leaf makes omaddons' JSON output describe itself truthfully: draft 2020-12 schemas for every command's `data`, the envelope, every stderr event and every persisted file, generated with the serialize contract (M4-D9); strict validation of live output in the contract suite; and a rule test over every shape (M4-D55). Subtask 1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3.1`) generated the schemas in `src/contract/schema.rs`.

This part adds what M4-D10 asks of the schemas: **the error object's schema becomes a union discriminated by `code`**, one variant per error code, each carrying that code's typed `details` specification. A9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9`, a meaning and a typed `DetailSpec` for every code) wrote the specs; this part puts them into the schema every error is validated against. M4-D10, restated: each code's `details` is described by a recursive `DetailSpec` (allowed keys, each key's type, nesting, required or optional, nullable or not, and the closed set of every stable enum such as `reason` and `changed`); emitters keep building `serde_json::Value`, and the specification, not the emitter, is the contract; the error envelope's schema is a union discriminated by `code` whose variants carry those fragments. *Why:* agents branch on `details`, and a key list would freeze names but not types (`details.changed` could turn from an array into a string unnoticed). *Rejected:* free-form `details`, a struct per code now, a key list.

It also adds two things every later part reads: **one walker** over a published schema (refs resolved, paths in one syntax), and **`contract::OPAQUE`**, the registry of the few values that are deliberately unconstrained (config values, an item error's kept details), each with its reason. The strict transform of subtask 3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3.3`) must leave those open and close everything else; the manifest of A10 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.10`) records them as `opaque`. It is its own step because the union changes `src/error.rs` (the hot spot "A9, then A3") and the registry needs the full set of schemas to be proven complete.

**Facts it relies on** (`c0ab5e9`, plus the blocking leaves):
- `ErrorBody` (`src/error.rs:617-626`) derives `Serialize, JsonSchema`: `code: ErrorCode, message: String, fix: String, fix_argv: Option<Vec<String>>, alternatives: Vec<Suggestion>, retryable: bool, details: serde_json::Value`. `Error`'s hand-written `JsonSchema` delegates to `ErrorBody::json_schema` (`:643-653`). `Suggestion` (`:384-388`) derives `JsonSchema` (`{display, argv}`).
- `TargetResult.error: Option<ErrorBody>` (`src/app/outcome.rs:274`) embeds an error inside the `data` of every multi-target command (`TargetsData`); A9's consumers table records that it carries the same per-code `details`.
- A9's `ErrorCode::details_schema() -> serde_json::Value` (the code's own keys merged with `COMMON`'s: `items`, `required_by`, `journal_pending`, `recovery_error`), `ErrorCode::meaning()`, `ErrorCode::declared_detail_paths()` and `DetailSpec::opaque_paths()`. A9 renders `DetailSpec::Opaque(why)` as `{"type":"object","description":why}` (nullable: `"type":["object","null"]`), and its one opaque path is `items[].error.details` (an `ItemError`'s kept details, `ITEM_ERROR` in `src/error/specs.rs`). A9's test-only `check_rendered` accepts only the keywords `type`, `enum`, `items`, `properties`, `required`, `oneOf`, `description`; A9 snapshots every rendered spec in `src/snapshots/omaddons__error__specs__tests__error_details_schemas.snap`.
- Unconstrained `Value` fields in serialized types at `c0ab5e9`: `Setting.value` (`src/app/config.rs:65`), `GetData.value`, `GetData.default` (`:83`, `:85`), `SetData.value`, `SetData.previous` (`:92-93`), `ItemError.details: Option<serde_json::Value>` (`src/app/outcome.rs:180`), and `LeftOutFolder.details: serde_json::Map<String, Value>` with `#[serde(flatten)]` (`src/model.rs:624-630`), which reaches `list`'s and `info`'s data (`src/app/list.rs:109`, `src/app/info.rs:124`) and the `target_record` file (`src/model.rs:611`). `Precondition`'s `Value` fields (`src/app/precondition.rs:73-74`) are not serialized.
- schemars renders `serde_json::Value` as the boolean schema `true` (crate source `src/json_schema_impls/serdejson.rs`), a `BTreeMap<String, Value>` as `{"type":"object","additionalProperties":true}`, and a map keyed by a patterned type (`TargetKey`) through `patternProperties` (`src/json_schema_impls/maps.rs`).
- `src/source_scan.rs` (`production_code`, `sources`) is `#[cfg(test)]` and usable here; `src/doctor/` does not exist yet.

## Technical Approach

### 1. The error union as `ErrorBody`'s schema

In `src/error.rs`, `ErrorBody` drops `JsonSchema` from its derive and gets:

```rust
/// An error's schema: one variant per code, discriminated by `code`, each with that code's typed
/// `details` (M4-D10). Every `ErrorBody` (the envelope's `error`, `TargetResult.error`) and every
/// `Error` (through its impl above) carries it.
impl JsonSchema for ErrorBody {
    fn schema_name() -> Cow<'static, str> { "ErrorBody".into() }
    fn json_schema(g: &mut SchemaGenerator) -> Schema {
        let alternatives = g.subschema_for::<Vec<Suggestion>>();
        let variants: Vec<serde_json::Value> =
            ErrorCode::ALL.iter().map(|code| error_variant_value(*code, &alternatives)).collect();
        json_schema!({ "oneOf": variants })
    }
}

/// One code's variant.
pub fn error_variant_value(code: ErrorCode, alternatives: &Schema) -> serde_json::Value {
    json!({
        "type": "object",
        "description": code.meaning(),
        "properties": {
            "code": {"type": "string", "const": code.wire()},
            "message": {"type": "string"},
            "fix": {"type": "string"},
            "fix_argv": {"type": ["array", "null"], "items": {"type": "string"}},
            "alternatives": alternatives,
            "retryable": {"type": "boolean"},
            "details": code.details_schema(),
        },
        "required": ["code", "message", "fix", "fix_argv", "alternatives", "retryable", "details"],
    })
}
```

- Decided while writing this bead: the union is `ErrorBody`'s own schema, not only the envelope's `error` property, because `TargetResult.error` inside multi-target `data` carries the same per-code `details`, and M4-D55 rule 6 covers every observed `details` object. A published command schema that embeds `ErrorBody` therefore carries one variant per code; that growth is expected.
- `oneOf` is correct: the `const` discriminator makes variants mutually exclusive. It is the shape schemars emits for internally tagged enums, so A10 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.10`, the semantic manifest) walks it like any tagged union (`<code=plan_stale>`).
- `ErrorBody`'s serialized keys and the variant's properties must not drift: a unit test serializes an `ErrorBody` and compares (§5).
- In `src/contract/schema.rs`: `pub fn error_schema() -> Schema` (`generator().root_schema_for::<ErrorBody>()`, `title` "ErrorBody") and `pub fn error_variant(code: ErrorCode) -> Schema` (a fresh generator; the variant as a root with `$schema`, `title` "`<wire>` error" and `$defs` holding `Suggestion`). The contract suite validates an envelope's `error` against its own code's variant for precise messages (subtask 4); A10 records each variant.
- `envelope_schema()` (subtask 1) now embeds the union with no change of its own.

### 2. A9's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9`, meanings and `DetailSpec`s) `Opaque` rendering

In `src/error/detail_spec.rs`, `DetailSpec::Opaque(why)` renders `{"type":"object","description":why,"additionalProperties":true}` (nullable: `{"type":["object","null"],"description":why,"additionalProperties":true}`). Add `additionalProperties` (boolean `true` only) to `check_rendered`'s accepted keywords, update A9's `Opaque` rendering test, and re-accept A9's rendered-spec snapshot (review the diff: only the opaque fragments change).

Decided while writing this bead: an absent `additionalProperties` already admits extra keys, so this changes no meaning, but it makes the opaque position **structurally open**, which is what the strict transform (subtask 3) leaves untouched. One rendering means `capabilities.error_codes[].details_schema` (A4, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`), `robot-docs errors` (A5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5`, `robot-docs schema`)), the union and A10 all publish the same fragment. Nothing has published it yet.

### 3. The schema walk

In `src/contract/schema.rs`:

```rust
/// What `walk` reports.
pub enum Visit<'a> {
    /// A schema position: the root, a property value, array items, a map's values.
    Position { path: &'a str, node: &'a Value },
    /// A property of an object node.
    Property { path: &'a str, name: &'a str, node: &'a Value, required: bool, parent: &'a Value },
}
/// Walks one published schema with every local `$ref` resolved.
pub fn walk(root: &Value, visit: &mut dyn FnMut(&Visit<'_>));
```

- **Paths.** A9's syntax: `a`, `a.b` (key `b` of the object at `a`), `a[]` (the items of the array at `a`), plus `a{}` for a map's values (`additionalProperties` or `patternProperties` value schemas). The root's path is the empty string, printed `.` in messages. `prefixItems` entries share the array's `[]`.
- **References.** `#/$defs/<name>` and `#` are resolved inline. A definition already on the current path is not entered again (recursion), so every walk terminates.
- **In-place applicators** (`allOf`, `anyOf`, `oneOf`): their branches are walked at the same path, so a field present in two variants is reported once per variant at one path. Each `Property` carries `required` as its own object node says.
- It ignores keywords it does not need; it does not validate.
- Used by the `OPAQUE` tests below, the rule test (subtask 5, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3.5`) and A10's manifest normalization.

### 4. `contract::OPAQUE`

`src/contract/opaque.rs` (declared `pub mod opaque;` with `pub use opaque::{Opaque, OPAQUE};` in `src/contract/mod.rs`):

```rust
/// A schema position that admits any value on purpose. The strict transform leaves it open (it is
/// structurally open); A10's manifest records it as `opaque`.
pub struct Opaque {
    /// `envelope`, `error`, `event <name>`, `command <path>`, `command *` (every command) or `file <kind>`.
    pub scope: &'static str,
    /// A `walk` path; a leading `**.` matches at any depth.
    pub path: &'static str,
    /// The Rust type and field it comes from, `Setting.value`.
    pub source: &'static str,
    /// One sentence: why it is unconstrained.
    pub reason: &'static str,
}
pub const OPAQUE: &[Opaque] = &[ /* sorted by scope, then path */ ];
```

A position is **open** when its resolved node, or any in-place branch at it, is the boolean `true`, the empty schema `{}`, or an object schema with `additionalProperties: true` or `unevaluatedProperties: true`.

The starting inventory (from reading the code; the walk is the authority, and its failure message lists what to add):

| scope | path | source | reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| `command *` | `**.items[].error.details` | `ItemError.details` | An item error keeps the subset of its own code's details that the item needs. |
| `command config` | `settings[].value` | `Setting.value` | A config value is whatever TOML value its key admits, and each key's type is published with the config keys. |
| `command config get` | `default` | `GetData.default` | As for `value`. |
| `command config get` | `value` | `GetData.value` | As above. |
| `command config set` | `previous` | `SetData.previous` | As above. |
| `command config set` | `value` | `SetData.value` | As above. |
| `command info` | `**.left_out[]` | `LeftOutFolder.details` | A left-out folder carries its reason's own fields, kept as written so a reason a newer build wrote still reads. |
| `command list` | `**.left_out[]` | `LeftOutFolder.details` | As above. |
| `envelope` | `data` | `Envelope.data` | A command's data is described by its own schema, `robot-docs schema <command>`, and validated against it. |
| `error` | `details.items[].error.details` | `ItemError.details` | An item error keeps the subset of its own code's details that the item needs. |
| `file target_record` | `**.left_out[]` | `LeftOutFolder.details` | As for `list`. |

(Write each reason out in full in the code: "As above" is shorthand here only.)

### 5. Tests that hold the registry complete

In `src/contract/opaque.rs`, unit tests:

- `every_open_position_is_declared_opaque`: walk every published schema (`command_schemas()`, `envelope_schema()`, `error_schema()`, `event_schemas()`, `file_schemas()`), with its scope; every open position must match exactly one row (scope `command *` matches every command; `**.` matches at any depth). The failure lists each unmatched `(scope, path)` with "add a `contract::OPAQUE` row with its reason, or give the value a type".
- `every_opaque_row_matches_an_open_position`: a row that matches no open position fails as stale.
- `every_serialized_value_field_has_an_opaque_row`: over `production_code` of every `.rs` file under `src/app`, `src/output`, `src/contract` and `src/doctor` (skipping a directory that does not exist), each field of a `struct` (or struct-like enum variant) whose derive list contains `Serialize` and whose type mentions `serde_json::Value`, `Map<String, Value>`, or `Value` in a file that imports `serde_json::Value`, must be the `source` of some row (`<Type>.<field>`). This is the plan's scan. Decided while writing this bead: the schema walk is added beside it because the scan's directories miss `LeftOutFolder.details` (`src/model.rs`), which reaches `data` all the same.
- `opaque_rows_are_sorted_unique_and_reasoned`: sorted by (scope, path), no duplicate pair, every `reason` one sentence ending with a period, every `source` of the form `Type.field`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `ErrorBody`'s `JsonSchema` is the hand-written union: one variant per `ErrorCode::ALL` entry, `code` as `const`, `details` equal to `code.details_schema()`, `description` equal to `code.meaning()`, and the common fields required.
- [ ] `error_schema()` and `error_variant(code)` exist in `src/contract/schema.rs`; `envelope_schema()`'s `error` and the `install` schema's `targets[].error` both reach the union.
- [ ] A test holds each variant's `properties` and `required` equal to the keys a serialized `ErrorBody` has.
- [ ] `DetailSpec::Opaque` renders with `"additionalProperties": true`; A9's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9`, meanings and `DetailSpec`s) rendering test and rendered-spec snapshot are updated, and no other fragment changes.
- [ ] `contract::schema::walk` exists with the path syntax above, resolves local `$ref`s with a recursion guard, and walks in-place branches at one path; its table test passes.
- [ ] `contract::OPAQUE` exists, and `every_open_position_is_declared_opaque`, `every_opaque_row_matches_an_open_position`, `every_serialized_value_field_has_an_opaque_row` and `opaque_rows_are_sorted_unique_and_reasoned` pass.
- [ ] No serialized byte changes (every existing snapshot passes unchanged); `argc gate` passes; `br lint` is clean for this subtask.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

- `src/error.rs`:
  - `error_union_has_one_variant_per_code`: `oneOf` length equals `ErrorCode::ALL.len()`; variant `i`'s `properties.code.const` equals `ErrorCode::ALL[i].wire()`; its `details` equals `details_schema()`; its `description` equals `meaning()`.
  - `error_variant_properties_equal_the_serialized_body`: for one `Error` per code (built with `Error::new(code, "m", Suggestion::text("f"))`), `serde_json::to_value(ErrorBody::from(e))`'s keys equal the variant's `properties` keys and its `required`.
  - `target_result_error_uses_the_union`: in `command_schema` of `install`, walking `targets[].error` resolves to a node whose branches include a `$ref` to `ErrorBody`, whose `oneOf` has `ErrorCode::ALL.len()` entries.
- `src/error/detail_spec.rs`: A9's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9`, meanings and `DetailSpec`s) `Opaque` rendering cases (plain and nullable) expect `additionalProperties: true`; `check_rendered` accepts it and still refuses `additionalProperties: false` and any other new keyword.
- `src/contract/schema.rs`: `walk_visits_every_position`, one table case per shape, each with its expected sorted list of `(Position|Property, path)`: `ref_used_twice` (two properties naming one definition), `self_recursive_definition` (terminates; the recursive property reported once), `any_of_with_null` (an `Option` of a `$ref`), `one_of_sharing_a_field` (the shared field reported once per variant at one path; `required` per variant), `map_additional_properties` (`m{}`), `map_pattern_properties` (`m{}`), `prefix_items` (`t[]`).
- `src/contract/opaque.rs`: the four tests of Technical Approach §5 above. `every_open_position_is_declared_opaque`'s message lists the unmatched scope and path pairs, one per line.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

None in this part. Subtask 4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3.4`) validates live errors against the union, including a bad `details` value inside `data`'s `TargetResult.error`.

### Logging

Unit tests only: each table case has a name; every assertion message names the case and prints the schema walked, the expected and the actual visits (or the unmatched positions), pretty-printed.

## Considerations

title: The `jsonschema` dev-dependency and the strict test-side transform, with its composition tests
description:
Part 3 of 6 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3 (Schemas with the serialize contract, declared `details`, and live validation). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

The parent leaf makes omaddons' JSON output describe itself truthfully: draft 2020-12 schemas generated with the serialize contract (M4-D9), a typed error union (M4-D10), and the contract suite validating every live envelope against them, strictly, so that an emitted key the schema lacks fails. The schemas themselves stay open when published (M4-D9: a newer minor's additions must not break an older consumer's validator), so strictness is a transform the test side applies.

This part adds the two test-side tools the validation needs, and proves them before anything relies on them:

- **the validator**, the `jsonschema` crate as a dev-dependency with `default-features = false`, pinned to an exact version, with evidence that it pulls nothing `deny.toml` bans (M4-D9: "unverified until A3 runs it"; risk #15), and `boon` as the fallback;
- **the strict transform**, which adds `unevaluatedProperties: false` at every instance position of a schema, never at the root of an in-place branch or a `$defs` entry, with its own tests over every composition case: a `$ref` used two ways, maps, an internally tagged enum, a flattened struct, and `oneOf` with shared fields.

Why the transform is needed: schemars emits `additionalProperties: false` only for types with `deny_unknown_fields` (schemars_derive 1.2.3 `src/schema_exprs.rs:85, 264`; 2 uses in `src/`), so a plain validation never notices a key the schema lacks. Why not `additionalProperties: false`: it sees only its own object's `properties`, so it would reject the valid fields of a flattened struct or of a sibling `allOf` branch. In draft 2020-12, `unevaluatedProperties` sees the properties evaluated by the in-place applicators beside it (`allOf`, `anyOf`, `oneOf`, `$ref`), so it closes an object without rejecting a valid variant field; but a branch's own `unevaluatedProperties` sees only that branch's annotations, which is why it must never sit at a branch's root.

It is its own step because it needs none of subtask 1's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3.1`) or subtask 2's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3.2`) code: its tests run on synthetic schemas and schemars-derived test types, so it starts at once, in parallel with subtask 1, and it is where the validator choice is decided.

Rejected (M4-D9): a hand-written validator for schemars' subset (a correctness risk in the very code meant to catch errors).

**Facts it relies on** (`c0ab5e9`):
- `Cargo.toml:43-53` (`[dev-dependencies]`: `assert_cmd`, `etcetera`, `insta`, `predicates`, `proptest`, `rustix` with `pty`), each with a comment line in the file's style when its reason is not obvious. No JSON Schema validator. `Cargo.lock` is committed and the gate runs `cargo clippy --locked` and `cargo test --locked`.
- `deny.toml`: `[graph]` has only `targets` (no `exclude-dev`, so dev-dependencies are checked); `[bans] deny` lists tokio, reqwest, native-tls, openssl-sys, aws-lc-rs, aws-lc-sys; seven licenses are allowed (Apache-2.0, BSD-3-Clause, CDLA-Permissive-2.0, ISC, MIT, Unicode-3.0, Zlib), with the comment "Widen only in response to a concrete `cargo deny check licenses` rejection"; `multiple-versions = "warn"`.
- The gate runs `cargo deny check` when `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` or `deny.toml` changed, and always under `argc gate --all`.
- The contract test binary is `tests/contract/main.rs` with modules `exit_sites`, `matrix`, `recommendations`, `special`, `usage_fixes` (`:11-15`) and `#[path = "../common/mod.rs"] mod common;`. Integration tests may use the package's normal dependencies (`schemars`, `serde`, `serde_json`) and its dev-dependencies.
- schemars 1.2.3 renders: `serde_json::Value` as `true`; a `BTreeMap<String, T>` through `additionalProperties`; a map keyed by a patterned type (`BTreeMap<TargetKey, T>`, ULID pattern from `src/model.rs:265-276`) through `patternProperties` with `additionalProperties: false`; an internally tagged enum as a `oneOf` whose branches carry `{"type":"string","const":<tag>}`; a `#[serde(flatten)]` field merged into its parent's `properties` (or an `allOf` for flattened enums); an `Option<T>` of a referenced type as an `anyOf` with `{"type":"null"}`; a recursive type through `$ref` (`#` or `#/$defs/<name>`); integers with `format` annotations (`uint64`, `uint8`).

## Technical Approach

### 1. The dev-dependency

- Add to `Cargo.toml` `[dev-dependencies]`, with a comment line:

  ```toml
  # The contract suite's JSON Schema validator (M4-D9): default features off, so no
  # reqwest or TLS backend (deny.toml); pinned so a release cannot change what passes.
  jsonschema = { version = "=<the newest release at implementation time>", default-features = false }
  ```

  Commit `Cargo.lock` with it.
- Record in the close comment the output of:
  - `cargo tree -e normal,dev -i reqwest`
  - `cargo tree -e normal,dev -i aws-lc-rs`
  - and, decided while writing this bead, the same for `tokio`, `native-tls` and `openssl-sys` (the rest of `deny.toml`'s bans).

  For a package absent from the graph, `cargo tree -i` prints an error saying the package ID specification "did not match any packages" and exits non-zero: that is the expected, empty result. Quote the message.
- Run `argc gate --all` (cargo deny: bans, licenses, advisories, sources, dev-dependencies included) and record that it passed.
- **Fallback to `boon`** (pinned the same way; it has no network features) if any of these holds: a `cargo tree` result is non-empty; `cargo deny` refuses `jsonschema` or anything it pulls, for any reason; or the composition tests below show that `jsonschema` mishandles `unevaluatedProperties` through `$ref` or `oneOf`. Record the switch as a `decided: boon because …` comment on this subtask and in the leaf's close comment. Decided while writing this bead: `deny.toml` is never widened for the validator (its own comment allows widening only for a concrete rejection, and the plan names a fallback instead).
- **Options**, whichever crate: draft 2020-12 selected explicitly (not inferred), `format` assertions off (schemars' integer `format`s are annotations), no remote reference resolution (every `$ref` is local).

### 2. `tests/contract/validate.rs`

A module of the contract test binary (`mod validate;` in `tests/contract/main.rs`). It depends only on the library, `serde_json` and the validator, so another test binary can include it with `#[path = "contract/validate.rs"] mod validate;` (T2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.2`, the slice-1 demo, does). The validator crate is used only inside this file.

```rust
/// A schema construct the strict transform does not model.
#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct StrictError { pub keyword: String, pub path: String }   // Display: "strict: unsupported `<keyword>` at <path>"

/// The test-side strict form of a published schema (M4-D9): `unevaluatedProperties: false`
/// at every instance position. Returns a new value; the input is not changed.
pub fn strict(schema: &serde_json::Value) -> Result<serde_json::Value, StrictError>;

/// One validation failure.
pub struct Failure { pub instance_path: String, pub schema_path: String, pub message: String }
// Display: "<instance path or `/`>: <message> (schema <schema path>)", JSON pointers.

/// A compiled schema.
pub struct Validator { /* the crate's compiled form */ }
impl Validator {
    /// Compiles `schema`, after `strict` when `strict` is true.
    pub fn new(schema: &serde_json::Value, strict: bool) -> Result<Validator, String>;
    /// Every failure, in the validator's order, at most `MAX_FAILURES` (20), then one
    /// "… and N more" failure.
    pub fn validate(&self, instance: &serde_json::Value) -> Vec<Failure>;
}
```

### 3. The strict transform's rules

Walk the schema, tracking whether the current node is at an **instance position** and its JSON pointer path:

1. **Instance positions** are: the root; each value of `properties`; each value of `patternProperties`; `additionalProperties` when it is a schema (not a boolean); `items` (a schema, or each entry of an array form); each entry of `prefixItems`. These positions occur inside `$defs` entries too, and are treated the same there.
2. At an instance position whose node is an object schema, insert `"unevaluatedProperties": false`, unless the node is **open**: the boolean `true`, the empty schema `{}`, or an object that already has `additionalProperties: true` or any `unevaluatedProperties`. An open node is left exactly as it is (every `contract::OPAQUE` position is open in this sense, which subtask 2's tests guarantee). A boolean `false` stays `false`.
3. **In-place positions** are each entry of `allOf`, `anyOf` and `oneOf`, and the root of each `$defs` entry (which is only ever reached through a `$ref`). Never insert at an in-place position's root; recurse into its own instance positions (its `properties` values, its `items`, …) and its own in-place branches.
4. `$defs` (or `definitions`) is handled only at the root; a nested one is refused.
5. **Refused**, with `StrictError`: `not`, `if`, `then`, `else`, `contains`, `dependentSchemas`, `dependencies`, `propertyNames`, `unevaluatedItems`, `additionalItems`, a nested `$defs`, and any keyword not in the pass-through list. Decided while writing this bead: refusing beats guessing, because `unevaluatedProperties: false` inside a `not` would invert its meaning, and schemars emits none of these for omaddons' types; a refusal means a new shape needs a decision here.
6. **Passed through unchanged**: `type`, `enum`, `const`, `required`, `$ref`, `$schema`, `$id`, `$comment`, `$anchor`, `title`, `description`, `default`, `examples`, `deprecated`, `readOnly`, `writeOnly`, `format`, `pattern`, `minimum`, `maximum`, `exclusiveMinimum`, `exclusiveMaximum`, `multipleOf`, `minLength`, `maxLength`, `minItems`, `maxItems`, `uniqueItems`, `minProperties`, `maxProperties`, and `unevaluatedProperties`/`additionalProperties` already present.
7. The transform is idempotent (an inserted `unevaluatedProperties` makes the node count as already decided) and deterministic.

Decided while writing this bead: `patternProperties` values are instance positions (the plan's list omits them; schemars emits them for maps keyed by a ULID type, so without this the values of such maps would stay open).

### 4. The composition tests

`tests/contract/strict.rs` (`mod strict;` in `tests/contract/main.rs`). Pure, table-driven tests of test-side code: no command is run. Each case builds a published-form schema (from a schemars-derived test type with `SchemaSettings::draft2020_12().for_serialize()`, or hand-written JSON where schemars would not emit the shape), applies `strict`, compiles it with `Validator::new(…, false)`, and checks lists of valid and invalid instances. Each invalid instance names the instance path its failure must report.

| Case | Shape | Valid (all pass) | Invalid (each fails at) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ref_as_property_and_in_all_of` | hand-written: `$defs.Inner {a: integer, required a}`; `properties.p = {$ref Inner}`, `properties.q = {allOf: [{$ref Inner}]}` | `{p:{a:1}, q:{a:2}}` | `p.x` → `/p`; `q.x` → `/q`; top-level `x` → `/` |
| `map_through_additional_properties` | `struct M { m: BTreeMap<String, Inner> }` | `{m:{}}`, `{m:{k1:{a:1}, k2:{a:2}}}` | `m.k1.x` → `/m/k1`; top-level `x` → `/` |
| `map_through_pattern_properties` | `struct P { m: BTreeMap<TargetKey, Inner> }` (any ULID-patterned key type; a test-local newtype with the same hand-written schema is fine) | `{m:{"00000000000000000000000000":{a:1}}}` | value `x` → `/m/0000…`; key `"nope"` → `/m` |
| `internally_tagged_enum` | `#[serde(tag = "type", rename_all = "snake_case")] enum E { A { x: u8 }, B { y: String }, C }` as a field `e` | `{e:{type:"a",x:1}}`, `{e:{type:"b",y:"s"}}`, `{e:{type:"c"}}` | `{type:"a",y:"s"}` → `/e`; `{type:"a",x:1,z:1}` → `/e` |
| `flattened_struct` | `struct O { o: u8, #[serde(flatten)] f: F }` with `F { f: u8, #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")] g: Option<u8> }` | `{o:1,f:2}`, `{o:1,f:2,g:3}` | `{o:1,f:2,h:4}` → `/` |
| `one_of_with_shared_fields` | hand-written, `apply`-like: `properties.plan_id` (string) at the root, `oneOf` of two variants each with `applied.command` `const` (`install`/`update`) and `result` a `$ref` to its own result definition | each variant with a matching result, `plan_id` present | an `install` command with `update`'s result → `/`; an unknown field inside `result` → `/result`; an unknown top-level field → `/` |
| `option_of_a_ref` | `struct N { n: Option<Inner> }` | `{n:null}`, `{n:{a:1}}` | `{n:{a:1,x:1}}` → `/n` |
| `recursive_ref` | `struct Node { v: u8, children: Vec<Node> }` | three levels deep | an unknown field at depth 3 → `/children/0/children/0` |
| `items_and_prefix_items` | `struct V { v: Vec<Inner>, t: (Inner, u8) }` | `{v:[{a:1}], t:[{a:1},2]}` | `v[0].x` → `/v/0`; `t[0].x` → `/t/0` |

Further tests:

- `open_positions_stay_open`: a struct with a `serde_json::Value` field, a `BTreeMap<String, serde_json::Value>` field, a hand-written `{}` property and an opaque fragment as A9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9`, meanings and `DetailSpec`s) renders it, `{"type":"object","description":"…","additionalProperties":true}`, beside a closed sibling field: arbitrary nested content passes in each open field; an unknown key in the closed sibling still fails.
- `defs_and_branch_roots_are_untouched`: after `strict`, no `$defs` entry's root and no `allOf`/`anyOf`/`oneOf` entry's root has `unevaluatedProperties`; every `properties` value that is an object schema has it.
- `unmodelled_keywords_are_refused`: one case per refused keyword (`not`, `if`, `then`, `else`, `contains`, `dependentSchemas`, `dependencies`, `propertyNames`, `unevaluatedItems`, `additionalItems`, nested `$defs`, `x-unknown`), each asserting the error's `keyword` and `path`.
- `strict_is_idempotent` and `strict_does_not_mutate_its_input` (over every case's schema).
- `failures_name_instance_and_schema_paths`: an unknown field's `Failure` has `instance_path` `/p` and a `schema_path` ending in `unevaluatedProperties`; its `Display` contains both.
- `failures_are_capped`: an instance with 30 unknown keys gives 21 failures, the last "… and 10 more".

The validator decision rides on these: if any composition case fails because the validator, not the transform, gets draft 2020-12 wrong (check by reading the failure and the schema), switch to `boon` (§1 above) and rerun.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `jsonschema` (or, after a recorded `decided:`, `boon`) is in `[dev-dependencies]`, pinned with `=` and `default-features = false`, with its comment line; `Cargo.lock` is committed.
- [ ] The close comment quotes `cargo tree -e normal,dev -i reqwest` and `cargo tree -e normal,dev -i aws-lc-rs` (and the same for tokio, native-tls and openssl-sys) each reporting that no such package is in the graph, and records that `argc gate --all` (cargo deny) passed; `deny.toml` is unchanged.
- [ ] `tests/contract/validate.rs` provides `strict`, `StrictError`, `Validator` and `Failure` as above, with the validator crate used nowhere else.
- [ ] Every composition case of the table passes (every valid instance passes, every invalid one fails at its named instance path), and `open_positions_stay_open`, `defs_and_branch_roots_are_untouched`, `unmodelled_keywords_are_refused`, `strict_is_idempotent`, `strict_does_not_mutate_its_input`, `failures_name_instance_and_schema_paths` and `failures_are_capped` pass.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `br lint` is clean for this subtask.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

The tests of `tests/contract/strict.rs` above. They live in the contract integration crate because the validator is a dev-dependency and the transform is test code, but they are pure: table-driven, one name per case, no command run.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

None in this part: nothing here runs the binary. Subtask 4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3.4`) wires the transform and the validator into `support::check` for every contract envelope.

### Logging

Every case has a name; every assertion message names the case and prints the published schema, the strict schema, the instance, and the failures it got (or "passed" when a failure was expected), pretty-printed. `unmodelled_keywords_are_refused` prints the keyword and path expected and the error got.

## Considerations

- **Risk #15 (likelihood low, impact low): `jsonschema` violates `deny.toml`** (pulls `reqwest` or a TLS backend). Mitigated by default features off, the exact pin, the recorded `cargo tree` results and the `boon` fallback.
- **A validator that ignores `unevaluatedProperties`** (or ignores it through `$ref`) would make every strict test in the milestone pass vacuously. The composition table is the guard: its invalid instances can only fail if the keyword works through `$ref`, `allOf`, `anyOf` and `oneOf`.
- **Licenses.** A license `cargo deny` rejects is a reason to fall back to `boon`, not to widen `deny.toml`.
- **Hot spot `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock`:** A7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.7`, completions) adds `clap_complete`; whichever lands second rebases and reruns `argc gate --all`.
- **Gate time.** The transform's tests are fast; no binary runs.
- **Why the transform is test code, not in `src/`:** the published schemas must stay open, and nothing in the binary needs a strict form. Keeping it beside the validator keeps the validator dependency out of the library.

## Dependencies

- Parent: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3 (Schemas with the serialize contract, declared `details`, and live validation).
- Before it: none inside the leaf (it starts at once, in parallel with subtask 1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3.1`).
- After it: subtask 4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3.4`) compiles every published schema in strict form with this wrapper and validates every contract envelope.

From omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3.2: the strict transform's open rule (Technical Approach §3, rule 2) must match `omaddons::contract::schema::is_open`, which is public so this file can call it.

title: Live validation in `support::check`, and every mismatch it finds fixed
description:
Part 4 of 6 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3 (Schemas with the serialize contract, declared `details`, and live validation). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

The parent leaf makes omaddons' JSON output describe itself truthfully: schemas generated with the serialize contract (subtask 1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3.1`), an error schema that types every code's `details` (subtask 2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3.2`), and a strict validator with its transform (subtask 3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3.3`). M4-D9 requires the contract suite's `check()` to validate every live envelope's `data` against its command's schema, every stderr NDJSON line against its event schema, and `error` against `ErrorBody`; M4-D10 requires every observed `details` to validate against its code's `DetailSpec`, so that, in criterion 2's words, "a `details.changed` that turned into a string fails the suite". Validation runs on live envelopes because snapshots are redacted (subtask 6, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3.6`, handles those separately).

This part wires the validation into `support::check`, so every envelope every contract test produces is validated strictly, and fixes every mismatch it finds: each one is a real bug, either in a schema, in a `DetailSpec`, or (rarely) in an emitter. It is its own step because it is where the unknown amount of work lies (risk #2), and because the rule test and the snapshot walker that follow are generated from the schemas as this part leaves them.

It is also the plan's dispatch-table test (§6.2.1 of the plan): A1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1`) declared each command's schema function in its `COMMANDS` row (`data: fn(&mut SchemaGenerator) -> Schema`) without being able to prove it names the type the dispatch arm returns; validating every live `data` against it proves it (M4-D2: a declared fact is cross-checked against behaviour).

**Facts it relies on** (`c0ab5e9`, plus earlier parts and leaves):
- `support::check(run: Run, code: i32) -> Checked` (`tests/contract/main.rs:114-225`): one stdout document, key order, `schema_version`, `ok`/`exit_code`/registered exit, `meta`, the error's `retryable`, `details` object, message and fixes, warnings' fixes, `commands[]` argv, and one stderr `error` event per failure. A1 added the canonical-name and `observe_exit` checks; A2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.2`, the action and event registries) added that `commands[].action` is a registered `Action` with its `destructive` default and that every stderr `event`, `phase` and `level` is registered. Every contract test calls `check` (through `Scene::json`, `json_env`, `json_input`, `:426-492`).
- A1's self-test `the_harness_rejects_broken_envelopes` (`tests/contract/main.rs:546-581`) has a helper that runs `check` under `catch_unwind` and asserts the panic message contains a given phrase.
- The contract tests run on parallel threads in one process.
- From subtask 1: `contract::schema::{data_schema_for, envelope_schema, event_schemas}`; from subtask 2: `error_variant(code)` and the union as `ErrorBody`'s schema; from subtask 3: `tests/contract/validate.rs` with `strict`, `Validator`, `Failure`.
- `Scene::new()` (`tests/contract/main.rs:371-413`) is a retail and a Mists Classic client with fixture zips and replayed GitHub releases; `Scene::install_foo()` installs `gh:o/foo` into retail.
- README "Stability" (`README.md:1959-1963`) describes what the contract suite checks; the Tests table's `tests/contract/` row (`README.md:2625`) summarizes it.

## Technical Approach

### 1. The compiled schemas

In `tests/contract/validate.rs`:

```rust
/// Every published schema in strict form, compiled once per process.
pub struct Schemas {
    data: BTreeMap<String, Validator>,          // every `data_schema_for` name: COMMANDS paths and ENVELOPE_ONLY names
    errors: BTreeMap<ErrorCode, Validator>,     // `error_variant(code)` for every ErrorCode::ALL
    events: BTreeMap<String, Validator>,        // `event_schemas()`
    envelope: Validator,                        // `envelope_schema()`
}
pub fn schemas() -> &'static Schemas;           // std::sync::OnceLock
```

Building it applies `strict` to each schema and compiles it; a schema the transform refuses or the validator cannot compile panics with its name and the reason, so the problem is reported once, clearly.

### 2. `validate_envelope`

```rust
/// Validates one envelope and its stderr in four parts; `Err` holds every failure, formatted.
pub fn validate_envelope(envelope: &Value, stderr: &str) -> Result<(), String>;
```

1. **`data`**, when present, against `schemas().data[<command>]`. An envelope `command` with no schema is itself a failure ("no schema for command `<command>`: add its COMMANDS row").
2. **`error`**, when present, against `schemas().errors[<code>]`, so `details` is checked against that code's `DetailSpec` with precise paths.
3. **The frame**: a copy of the envelope with `data` and `error` removed, against `schemas().envelope`: the top-level keys, `partial`, every `warnings[]` entry, every `commands[]` entry and `meta`.
4. **Each stderr line** (every line is NDJSON under `--json`; `check` already parsed it) against `schemas().events[<event>]`.

The message:

```text
schema validation failed for `<command>` (exit <code>):
  data /targets/0/items/1: unexpected property `bogus` (schema /properties/targets/items/…/unevaluatedProperties)
  error /details/changed: "selection" is not of type "array" (schema /properties/details/properties/changed/type)
  stderr line 3 /: unexpected property `x` (schema /unevaluatedProperties)
```

at most 20 failures per part, then "… and N more".

**Re-explaining a union failure.** A failure inside `data` whose schema path ends in `oneOf`, at an instance that is an object with a string `code` naming a registered `ErrorCode` (an embedded `ErrorBody`, such as `TargetResult.error`), is replaced by that object's failures against `schemas().errors[<code>]`, prefixed with its instance path. Decided while writing this bead: without it, the message would say only "not valid under any of the given schemas".

### 3. `support::check`

After every existing assertion (so a structurally broken envelope still fails with today's message first), `check` calls `validate::validate_envelope(&envelope, &run.stderr)` and, on `Err`, panics with the message followed by `run.context()` (argv, exit, stdout, stderr). Keep it one call in its own block: E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`) adds a doctor mode to `check` and H2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.2`) an observed-keys check; each adds its own block.

### 4. Fixing what it finds

Run the whole contract suite (`cargo test --test contract`), collect every failure, and fix each one in this subtask. Every mismatch is a real bug: the schema, the spec or the emitter is wrong. Decided while writing this bead, the policy:

- **The emitted bytes are the default truth.** Fix the description: a `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = …)]` that the field's doc already promises, a `#[schemars(with = …)]` for a field whose serialized form differs from its Rust type, an `into`/`from` the derive missed, or a `DetailSpec` (in `src/error/specs.rs`, A9's file, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9`) that marks a key `Required` that one site omits, misses a key, types one wrongly, or misses a `reason` value.
- **Change an emitter only when its output contradicts README or its own doc comment.** That is a pre-release correction (M4-D55): record it in the close comment with a compatibility note (before → after → why, who reads it), and update any widget reader (`omarchy/Model.js`, run the widget pipeline) and any snapshot in the same commit.
- **Never loosen a schema to make a failure pass** (no `Value`, no removed pattern, no added `OPAQUE` row for a field that has a real type).
- **List every fix** in the close comment: part (`data`, `error`, frame, event), command or code, schema path, the fix, and whether it changed a byte.
- **The trigger (risk #2).** If the first full run reports more than 40 distinct mismatches (distinct pairs of command or code and schema path, about twice what one size-M part can absorb), fix them in order of how many envelopes each fails; for each one left, file a bug with `br create "…" --type bug --deps discovered-from:omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3.4`, block H1 on it (`br dep add omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1 <bug id>`), and list it in `tests/contract/schema_mismatches.txt`, one line `<part> | <command or code> | <schema path> | <bug id>`, sorted. `validate_envelope` drops failures matching a line; a line that matches no failure fails the suite (the file may only shrink). Create the file only if the trigger fires.

Where to look first (from reading the code): `details` specs of codes with several construction sites (A9's inventory), untagged enums (`src/app/help.rs:31`, `src/app/adopt.rs:79`, `src/app/list.rs:122`, `src/backup/mod.rs:147`, `src/state/config.rs:142`, `:168`), flattened fields (`src/app/outcome.rs:299`, `src/app/outdated.rs:125`, `src/engine/inspect.rs:948`, `src/resolve/updates.rs:468`, `src/engine/undo.rs:125`, `src/backup/export.rs:67`), and internally tagged enums (`src/toc.rs:229`, `src/discover/target.rs:24`, `src/resolve/updates.rs:35`, `src/toc/loaded.rs:266`, `:284`).

### 5. README

- "Stability" (`README.md:1961`), after the sentence about the matrix: "Every envelope the suite produces is validated against its command's JSON Schema (draft 2020-12, generated with the serialize contract), strictly: a key the schema does not declare fails. Every error's `details` is validated against its code's typed specification, and every stderr event against its event's schema." (Subtask 6, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3.6`, adds the envelope snapshots to this sentence when its walker lands: README describes what exists.)
- The Tests table's `tests/contract/` row: add "schema validation of every envelope, `details` and stderr event".

### 6. Time

Record the contract suite's wall time (`cargo test --test contract`, warm build, three runs, median) before and after this subtask in the close comment.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `tests/contract/validate.rs` has `Schemas` (built once per process) and `validate_envelope` validating `data`, `error`, the frame and every stderr line, each strictly, with the message format above and the union re-explanation.
- [ ] `support::check` calls `validate_envelope` after its existing checks, and every contract test passes with it: every matrix row (success and failure), `special.rs`, `recommendations.rs` and `usage_fixes.rs`.
- [ ] `the_harness_rejects_schema_violations` passes: each planted case fails `check` with its expected instance path and keyword in the message, and the unmutated bases pass.
- [ ] Every mismatch found is fixed and listed in the close comment (part, command or code, schema path, fix, whether a byte changed, compatibility note for any byte change); or, past 40, the remainder is filed as bugs discovered from omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3.4, each blocking omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1, and listed in `tests/contract/schema_mismatches.txt`, whose stale-line check passes.
- [ ] README's "Stability" paragraph and the Tests table's `tests/contract/` row describe the validation, in this subtask's commit.
- [ ] The close comment records the contract suite's wall time before and after.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes (the widget pipeline too if an emitter changed); `br lint` is clean for this subtask.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

None in `src/` beyond the fixes' own (a fixed `DetailSpec` keeps A9's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9`, meanings and `DetailSpec`s) tests passing; a new `skip_serializing_if` keeps its type's tests passing).

### Integration and end-to-end tests

- **Every existing contract test**: unchanged in what it asserts; each now also validates its envelope, its `error` and its stderr. This is the bulk of the coverage: the 40 matrix tests' success and failure rows, the special cases (a held lock, a panic, offline, `HOME` unset, dry runs, read-only commands, NDJSON stderr, JSON spellings, repeated runs), the recommendations and the usage-fix corpus.
- **`tests/contract/main.rs`, `the_harness_rejects_schema_violations`**, a `TestLog` scenario on one `Scene::new()`:
  1. Step `bases`: through `log.run` and `support::check`: `status --json` (exit 0); `install gh:o/foo --file <foo.zip> -t retail --json` (exit 0); `pin` of the installed addon on retail as `tests/contract/matrix.rs` does (a `TargetsData` envelope, exit 0); `status -t nosuch --json` (exit 3, `target_not_found`). Each passes.
  2. One step per planted case. Each takes one base envelope (or builds a failure envelope by hand: `ok: false`, the code's registered exit, `command` a row that declares that exit, an `error` whose base `details` first passes `ErrorCode::check_details` (A9) and `check`, and a stderr line `{"event":"error",…}` valid for that error), applies one mutation, and runs `check` under A1's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1`, per-command facts) message-checking helper, which asserts the panic message contains the expected instance path and keyword:

     | Case | Base and mutation | Expected in the message |
     |---|---|---|
     | `data_key_missing_from_schema` | `status`: `data.bogus = 1` | `data /`, `unevaluatedProperties` (or the validator's "unexpected property" wording) and `bogus` |
     | `nested_data_key` | `pin`: `data.targets[0].bogus = 1` | `data /targets/0` |
     | `details_wrong_type` | hand-built `plan_stale` on `install` (exit 1), base `details {"changed": ["selection"]}`, mutated to `"changed": "selection"` | `error /details/changed`, `type` |
     | `details_undeclared_key` | `status -t nosuch`: `error.details.extra = 1` | `error /details`, `extra` |
     | `details_undeclared_reason` | hand-built `filesystem_unsupported` on `backup restore` (exit 4), base `details {"reason": "no_rename_exchange", "backup_dir": "<root>/b"}` (plus any key A9's spec requires), mutated to `"reason": "bogus_reason"` | `error /details/reason`, `enum` |
     | `warning_unknown_key` | `status`: `warnings = [{"code":"reload_required","message":"m","fix":null,"fix_argv":null,"extra":true}]` | `frame /warnings/0`, `extra` |
     | `command_hint_unknown_key` | `status`: `commands = [{"action":"undo","command":"omaddons undo","argv":["omaddons","undo"],"destructive":false,"extra":1}]` | `frame /commands/0`, `extra` |
     | `stderr_event_unknown_field` | `status`'s run with stderr `{"event":"log","level":"info","message":"m","x":1}` | `stderr line 1`, `x` |
     | `target_result_error_bad_details` | `pin`: `data.targets[0].error = {"code":"plan_stale","message":"m","fix":"rerun the dry run","fix_argv":null,"alternatives":[],"retryable":false,"details":{"changed":"selection"}}` | `data /targets/0/error/details/changed` (re-explained against `plan_stale`'s variant) |

     Decided while writing this bead: the hint case plants an extra key, not an unknown action, because A2's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.2`, the action and event registries) registry check in `check` already rejects an unknown action before validation runs; the stderr case plants an extra field for the same reason.
  3. Step `bases_still_pass`: `check` on each unmutated base again.

### Logging

`the_harness_rejects_schema_violations` uses `TestLog` (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, `tests/common/tlog.rs`): `log.step` per case (named as in the table), every base run through `log.run`, `log.json("planted", &envelope)` for each mutated envelope, and `log.note` of the panic message caught (or "no panic" when a case unexpectedly passes). A failing case therefore shows the exact envelope that was checked and what `check` said. For every other contract test, `validate_envelope`'s message (part, instance path, message, schema path, then `run.context()`) is the diagnostic.

## Considerations

- **Risk #2 (likelihood medium, impact medium; owner this leaf).** This is the part where it bites. A9's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9`, meanings and `DetailSpec`s) starting inventory and its "Required only when every site emits it" rule were written to shrink the `details` mismatches; most other fixes are one attribute. The trigger bounds the work without hiding anything.
- **Hot spots.** `tests/contract/main.rs` (A1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1`, per-command facts), A2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.2`, the action and event registries) and E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, `doctor diagnose`) each add a block to `check`; keep this one call in its own block); `src/error/specs.rs` and `src/error.rs` (A9, then A3; later leaves append rows with specs: never reflow a row); any `src/app/*.rs` file a fix touches may be a peer's hot spot (§10.5 of the plan: D2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2`, `--if-match` on install, update, sync and copy), D3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.3`, `--if-match` on pin, unpin and adopt), D4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`, the plan store), C2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.2`, misplaced clients as addons and `-t all`) touch `update`, `sync`, `copy`, `pin`, `install`, `remove`): keep fixes to attributes and doc comments, rebase before the gate.

1. **The union re-explanation covers `anyOf` as well as `oneOf`.** An embedded `ErrorBody` is an `Option` field (`TargetResult.error`), which schemars renders as `anyOf: [{$ref ErrorBody}, {type: null}]`. So at a value whose `code` names a registered code and that fails a `oneOf` or an `anyOf`, every failure gives way to that value's failures against `schemas().errors[code]`. title: The rule test of M4-D55's rules 1–4 and 6, with `tests/contract/rules_allowlist.txt`
description:
Part 5 of 6 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3 (Schemas with the serialize contract, declared `details`, and live validation). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

The parent leaf makes omaddons' JSON output describe itself truthfully: generated schemas (subtask 1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3.1`), a typed error union (subtask 2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3.2`), a strict validator (subtask 3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3.3`) and live validation of every contract envelope (subtask 4, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3.4`).

This part adds the other half of M4-D55: a test that holds every schema to the contract's rules from slice 1 on, so mistakes are fixed while they cost a commit rather than a major version bump after the tag. M4-D55, restated: six rules govern every command's data shape, every error's `details`, every warning, action, event and file kind.

1. **Timestamps.** Every instant is RFC 3339 UTC with an `_at` suffix; every duration is an integer with a unit suffix (`_ms`, `_s`).
2. **Null versus omitted.** A key in a command's schema is always present, `null` when it has no value. Omission is reserved for `-v`/`--raw-details` additions and fields documented as optional, and each must be optional in the serialize schema.
3. **Names.** Snake case. Plurals for arrays. `id` for the user-facing identifier and `key` for ULID keys. Counts are bare nouns (`files`, `bytes`). Booleans are adjectives or `is_`-free states (`restorable`, `busy`).
4. **Enumerations.** Snake case values. Every one has a closed set in its schema.
5. **Command names**: A1's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1`), already enforced.
6. **`details`.** Every observed `details` object validates against its code's `DetailSpec`, and every declared key appears in at least one test.

This part's test checks rules 1–4 and 6 over every schema. Every violation that exists when it lands goes, one per line with the rule broken, into `tests/contract/rules_allowlist.txt`. The test fails on any violation not on the allowlist, and on any allowlist line that no longer matches a violation, so the list can only shrink; H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, the pre-freeze contract audit) fixes every remaining line and empties it, and its size is visible all milestone. Cheap fixes of listed violations on surfaces no M4 leaf rewrites are made here. *Why:* after the tag each fix costs a major bump (M4-D56); before it, a commit and a widget update. *Rejected:* freezing as is; one late window in H1 only, which propagates known mistakes through every consumer.

It is its own step, after subtask 4, because its allowlist is written once from the schemas as live validation leaves them (subtask 4 may change a schema while fixing a mismatch), and because it touches different files from subtask 6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3.6`), with which it runs in parallel.

**Facts it relies on** (`c0ab5e9`, plus earlier parts):
- `contract::schema::walk` (subtask 2) visits every position and every property of a published schema with `$ref`s resolved, in paths `a`, `a.b`, `a[]`, `a{}`; `command_schemas()`, `envelope_schema()`, `error_variant(code)`, `event_schemas()` and `file_schemas()` (subtasks 1, 2) give every schema.
- schemars puts a field's doc comment in its property schema's `description`, beside any `$ref`; under the serialize contract a field is optional exactly when it has `skip_serializing_if`.
- `Family` serializes `kebab-case` (`src/rules.rs:148`), so `vanilla-legacy` and similar values are enum values with hyphens. `Setting.source` is a `&'static str`, `"file"` or `"default"` (`src/app/config.rs:62-67`). `HistoryLine.at` (`src/app/history.rs`, the `history` command's `entries[]`) is an instant named `at`. `Setting.key`, `GetData.key`, `SetData.key` (`src/app/config.rs`) and the `key` in `desired_state_invalid`'s and `state_corrupt`'s `details` are config or TOML keys, not ULIDs. `LeftOutFolder` arrays are named `left_out` (`src/app/list.rs:109`, `src/app/info.rs:124`). A9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9`) recorded `tried[].reason` (in `no_compatible_release`, `wrong_flavor`, `hash_mismatch`) as free text under a key named `reason`.
- E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, `doctor diagnose`) decided that the doctor report's `state` values (`DONE_OK`, …) and severities (`P0`–`P3`) keep the external doctor contract's spelling, through an exception in this test keyed by those two types, never through the allowlist; whichever of this bead and E3 lands second adds it.

## Technical Approach

### 1. The test module

`tests/contract/rules.rs` (`mod rules;` in `tests/contract/main.rs`). Pure: it reads published schemas and the allowlist file, and runs no command.

**Roots, each with a scope:**

| Scope | Schema | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `command <path>` | `command_schemas()` | paths relative to `data` |
| `envelope` | `envelope_schema()` | the frame: the walk does not enter `data` (open) or `error` (checked per code) |
| `error <code>` | `error_variant(code)` for every `ErrorCode::ALL` | paths relative to the error object (`details.reason`) |
| `event <name>` | `event_schemas()` | |
| `file` | `file_schemas()`'s keys | kind names only (rule 3's case check) |

From a command or envelope root, the walk does not enter a position that resolves to `ErrorBody`'s union (a `$ref` to `…/ErrorBody`): every error variant is checked once, under its own `error <code>` scope, rather than again inside each multi-target command's `targets[].error`.

**Facts of a node.** A helper `facts(root, node) -> Facts { types, enum_values, pattern, description }` merges a node through `$ref` and its in-place branches: `types` is the set of JSON types it admits (`integer` and `number` kept distinct; `const` and `enum` values contribute their JSON types), `enum_values` the union of its `enum` and `const` values, `pattern` the pattern if one applies. `description` is the property schema's **own** (the field's doc comment, beside any `$ref`), never its type's.

### 2. The rules

Each checker is a pure function from a visited property (or a node with enum values) to an optional violation. Names are tested as written. Snake case means `^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(_[a-z0-9]+)*$`.

| id | Rule | Violation |
|---|---|---|
| `r1-at-type` | 1 | a property named `*_at` whose types are not string, or string and null |
| `r1-instant-name` | 1 | a property named `at`, `time`, `date`, `timestamp` or `when`, or ending in `_time`, `_date`, `_timestamp` or `_on` |
| `r1-duration-type` | 1 | a property ending in `_ms` or `_s` whose types are not integer, or integer and null |
| `r1-duration-name` | 1 | a property whose types include integer or number, named `duration`, `elapsed`, `timeout`, `ttl`, `age` or `interval`, or ending in `_duration`, `_secs`, `_seconds`, `_millis`, `_age`, `_timeout`, `_ttl` or `_interval` |
| `r2-omittable-undocumented` | 2 | a property its object does not require whose own `description` contains none of (ignoring case) `omitted`, `absent`, `present when`, `present iff`, `present only`, `only with`, `only when`, `only under`, `` `-v` ``, `--raw-details` |
| `r2-verbose-required` | 2 | a property whose own `description` contains `` `-v` only`` but which its object requires |
| `r3-name-case` | 3 | a property name, or a file kind name, that is not snake case |
| `r3-array-plural` | 3 | a property whose types include array and whose name ends neither in `s` nor in `argv` |
| `r3-bool-is` | 3 | a property whose types include boolean and whose name starts with `is_` |
| `r3-count-name` | 3 | a property whose types include integer and whose name ends in `_count` or starts with `num_`, `n_` or `count_` |
| `r3-key-ulid` | 3 | a property named exactly `key` whose pattern is not `^[0-9A-HJKMNP-TV-Z]{26}$` |
| `r4-value-case` | 4 | a string in any node's `enum` or `const` that is not snake case |
| `r4-open-enum` | 4 | a property named `kind`, `status`, `state`, `reason`, `mode`, `action`, `op`, `class`, `level`, `phase`, `event`, `severity`, `confidence`, `verdict`, `channel`, `type` or `result` whose types are string (or string and null) with no enum or const values |
| `r6-details-object` | 6 | an error variant whose `details` property does not admit exactly an object |

**Which roots each rule covers.** Rules 1, 3 and 4 apply to every command, the envelope frame, every error variant (its `details` included) and every event. Rule 2 applies to commands, the frame and events, not inside `details`: whether a details key appears depends on its construction site, which A9's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9`, meanings and `DetailSpec`s) `DetailSpec` and rule 6 govern. `r3-name-case` also applies to file kind names; no other rule applies to file schemas. Decided while writing this bead: persisted formats change only through their own kind versions (M4-D3), not through a wire audit, so their field names are not held to these rules; their kind names are contract, so they are.

**Rule 6** has a static checker here (`r6-details-object`). Its live half (every observed `details` validates against its spec) is subtask 4's validation, which admits no allowlist: a mismatch there is fixed, never listed. Its "every declared key appears in a test" half is subtask 6's report.

**Decided while writing this bead:** the exact checks above. They are the parts of rules 1–4 a schema can show mechanically; anything they cannot judge (a name that is snake case but misleading) is H1's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, the pre-freeze audit) manual walk. A checker that flags something H1 judges compliant is a defect in the checker: H1 narrows it and records why.

### 3. A violation's identity

A violation is the line `<rule> | <scope> | <path>`, for example:

```text
r1-instant-name | command history | entries[].at
r3-key-ulid | command config get | key
r3-key-ulid | error desired_state_invalid | details.key
r4-open-enum | command config | settings[].source
r4-value-case | command list | targets[].family
```

(These are expected at `c0ab5e9`; they are examples, not a list to copy.) For `r4-value-case` the path is the position holding the value (a property's path, or `x[]` for array items). Identical lines (a field present in two variants) count once. `violations(&roots) -> BTreeSet<String>` computes the set.

### 4. `tests/contract/rules_allowlist.txt`

- One violation per line, exactly in the form above; sorted; no duplicate; `#` starts a comment line; blank lines are ignored. The file opens with:

  ```text
  # Contract rule violations that predate the rule test (M4-D55). This list may only shrink:
  # a new shape that breaks a rule is fixed, never added here. H1 empties it before the freeze.
  # Format: <rule> | <scope> | <path>
  ```
- **No regeneration variable.** Decided while writing this bead: one would make "may only shrink" a matter of one environment variable. On the first write, the test fails and prints every current violation in file form; copy them in by hand (CLAUDE.md "No Script-Based Changes" concerns code; this is a reviewed data file, written once).
- **The test**, `every_schema_follows_the_contract_rules`: compute `violations`, read the allowlist, then:
  - a violation not on the allowlist (and not covered by `EXCEPTIONS`) fails: "a new shape breaks rule <n> (`<rule id>`): `<line>`. Fix the shape; never add to `tests/contract/rules_allowlist.txt` (M4-D55)";
  - a line that matches no violation fails: "`<line>` no longer matches a violation: remove it (the allowlist may only shrink)";
  - a malformed, unsorted or duplicate line fails with its line number;
  - all failures are reported together, then the count of allowlisted lines per rule.
- **`EXCEPTIONS`**, a coded list in `rules.rs`, `struct Exception { rule: &'static str, scope: &'static str, path: &'static str, reason: &'static str }` (`scope` exact or `command *`; `path` a walk path, `**.` for any depth): permanent, reasoned exceptions for vocabularies omaddons does not own, such as E3's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, `doctor diagnose`) doctor states and severities. Empty when this part lands, unless E3 landed first. An exception that matches nothing fails as stale. H1 audits each.

### 5. The cheap fixes made here

Decided while writing this bead: only fixes that change no serialized byte, so no snapshot, widget or guide changes:

- **Doc comments** that say when an omittable key is omitted ("Omitted when …", "`-v` only."), for `r2-omittable-undocumented` lines: one line per field in `src/app/*.rs`, `src/output/envelope.rs` (`data`, done in subtask 1), `src/contract/events.rs` (`current`, `total`: "Omitted when unknown." or as the code says).
- **Closed enums** for string fields whose values are already a fixed literal set and that serialize to the same bytes: `Setting.source` (`"file"`, `"default"`) as a `#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]` enum, and any other `r4-open-enum` field of that kind.

Each fix removes its allowlist line in the same commit and goes in the close comment. Renames, retypes and anything that changes a byte wait for H1 or the leaf that owns the surface (M4-D55), even when cheap: the widget and the snapshots read today's names.

### 6. README

"Stability" (`README.md:1961`), after subtask 4's sentences: "A rule test holds every schema to the contract's naming rules (timestamps, null versus omitted, names, closed enumerations); the violations that predate it are listed in `tests/contract/rules_allowlist.txt`, which may only shrink and is empty at the first tag."

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `tests/contract/rules.rs` computes violations of the fourteen checks over every command, the envelope frame, every error variant, every event and every file kind name, without entering the error union from command roots.
- [ ] `tests/contract/rules_allowlist.txt` exists with its header, holds exactly the violations left after this part's fixes, sorted and unique, every line naming its rule; its line count per rule is in the close comment.
- [ ] `every_schema_follows_the_contract_rules` passes; `a_new_violation_fails_with_the_rule_message` (one planted violation per rule id) and `a_stale_line_fails` pass.
- [ ] `r2-verbose-required` reports no violation (every `-v`-only field is optional in its serialize schema), so it has no allowlist line.
- [ ] `EXCEPTIONS` exists (empty unless E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, `doctor diagnose`) landed first), and a stale exception fails.
- [ ] The byte-preserving fixes made here are listed in the close comment, each with the allowlist line it removed; every existing snapshot passes unchanged.
- [ ] README's "Stability" section has the rule-test sentence, in this subtask's commit.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `br lint` is clean for this subtask.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

Pure tests in `tests/contract/rules.rs` (no command is run; they live in the contract crate beside the test they check):

- One table per rule id, `r1_at_type`, `r1_instant_name`, `r1_duration_type`, `r1_duration_name`, `r2_omittable_undocumented`, `r2_verbose_required`, `r3_name_case`, `r3_array_plural`, `r3_bool_is`, `r3_count_name`, `r3_key_ulid`, `r4_value_case`, `r4_open_enum`, `r6_details_object`: each case a synthetic root schema (hand-written JSON) and the exact set of violation lines expected; at least one passing and one violating case per rule (for example `r1_at_type`: `started_at` string passes, `started_at` integer violates; `r3_array_plural`: `entries` and `fix_argv` pass, `left_out` violates).
- `facts_merge_refs_and_branches`: a property whose schema is `anyOf [$ref string-enum, null]` gives types `{string, null}` and the enum's values; a `$ref` with a sibling `description` gives that description.
- `allowlist_parses_sorted_and_unique`: cases `well_formed`, `unsorted` (fails with the line number), `duplicate`, `unknown_rule_id`, `missing_field`, `comment_and_blank_lines_ignored`.
- `a_new_violation_fails_with_the_rule_message`: for each rule id, the real roots plus one planted synthetic root violating exactly that rule, compared with the real allowlist, fails with a message naming that rule id, the planted line and "never add to".
- `a_stale_line_fails`: the real violations minus one allowlisted line, compared with the real allowlist, fails naming that line and "may only shrink".
- `a_stale_exception_fails`: an exception matching nothing fails.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

`every_schema_follows_the_contract_rules` over the real published schemas and the committed allowlist. It runs no command, so it does not use `TestLog`.

### Logging

Every table case has a name; every assertion message names the case and prints the synthetic schema and the expected and actual violation sets. The main test prints, on failure, every new violation and every stale line, and, always (with `--nocapture`), the allowlist's count per rule.

## Considerations

- **The allowlist's size is H1's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, the pre-freeze audit) work, made visible.** It may hold hundreds of lines: a violation in a type shared by several commands (for example `TargetsData`) appears once per command. That is the honest count of places a fix touches. When H1 fixes a shared type, all its lines go at once.
- **Hot spots.** `tests/contract/rules_allowlist.txt` is created here; after this only H1 and owning leaves that fix a listed violation touch it, and only to remove lines (common rule 6: "never add"). The doc-comment fixes touch many `src/app/*.rs` files that other leaves edit (D2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2`, `--if-match` on install, update, sync and copy), D3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.3`, `--if-match` on pin, unpin and adopt), D4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`, the plan store) and C2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.2`, misplaced clients as addons and `-t all`) in `update`, `sync`, `copy`, `pin`, `install`, `remove`): keep each fix to its one doc line and rebase before the gate run.
- **Later leaves:** every new shape must pass this test; a leaf whose shape breaks a rule fixes the shape (E12 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.12`, target-less history lines) decided to file a bug rather than allowlist if its `born_ns` spelling is refused).
- **What could go wrong.** A heuristic name list (`r1-instant-name`, `r4-open-enum`) misses a case or flags a compliant one. Missing a case only weakens the check (H1's walk is the backstop); a false flag is fixed by narrowing the checker with a recorded reason, never by allowlisting a non-violation.
- **Privacy, performance:** nothing here runs the binary; the walk over every schema takes well under a second.
