title: Tests: every envelope snapshot, the `-v`-only fields, the files a session writes, and the declared-`details` report
description:
Part 6 of 6 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3 (Schemas with the serialize contract, declared `details`, and live validation). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

The parent leaf makes omaddons' JSON output describe itself truthfully: generated schemas (subtask 1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3.1`), a typed error union (subtask 2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3.2`), a strict validator (subtask 3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3.3`), and live validation of every contract envelope in `support::check` (subtask 4, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3.4`).

This part adds the integration and end-to-end suites that prove the rest of the leaf's promises, which the contract matrix alone does not reach:

- **every JSON envelope snapshot in the repository validates** (the vision's checkpoint: "`robot-docs schema` validates every snapshot-tested JSON response"; criterion 2: "Every JSON envelope snapshot in the repository validates too"). Snapshots are redacted, which is why M4-D9 validates live envelopes; this walker validates them anyway, by substituting typed samples for the placeholders;
- **`-v`-only fields are optional in their schemas** (the plan's step 10, and H1's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, the pre-freeze audit) list of corrections made by this leaf): a command validates with and without `-v`, and the field is absent without it;
- **the published file schemas describe what the binary writes**: every state file, history line, journal line and exported `addons.toml` a session leaves validates against its kind's schema (decided while writing this bead: `file_schemas()` is published by A5, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5`, and nothing else checks it);
- **the declared-but-unobserved `details` report**: M4-D55 rule 6 says every declared `details` key appears in at least one test; this report lists those no contract test observes, and H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`) makes it empty and an assertion.

It is the leaf's test subtask: last, after the validation it reuses, and in parallel with subtask 5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3.5`, the rule test).

**Facts it relies on** (`c0ab5e9`, plus earlier parts):
- 159 `.snap` files: 140 under `tests/`, 19 under `src/`. 123 have a JSON envelope body: 105 in `tests/contract/snapshots/` (the matrix; `meta` removed by `support::stable`, `tests/contract/main.rs:307-316`), 14 in `tests/snapshots/`, 4 in `src/output/snapshots/`. insta's format: a header between two `---` lines, then the body.
- Three of the four `src/output/snapshots/` envelopes (`omaddons__output__tests__envelope_success.snap`, `omaddons__output__tests__envelope_partial_success.snap`, `omaddons__output__tests__envelope_check_failed.snap`) are renderer fixtures with synthetic `data` (`{"zeta":1,"alpha":"a","map":{…}}`) under the real command names `update` and `outdated`; the fourth (`…_envelope_failure.snap`, `install`, `target_ambiguous`) is a real shape.
- Placeholders in envelope snapshots: whole-value `<ulid>`, `<tx>`, `<key>`, `<run>`, `<time>`, `<checked_at>`, `<precondition>`, `<version>`, and `"<bytes>"` replacing an integer (`compressed_bytes`, `tests/contract/matrix.rs:979`); and `<root>`, `<meta>`, `<binary>`, `<addon>`, `<ref>`, `<path>` inside longer strings. ULID ids' schemas carry the pattern `^[0-9A-HJKMNP-TV-Z]{26}$` (`src/model.rs:265-276`), so `<ulid>` as such does not validate.
- `-v`-only fields with `skip_serializing_if` at `c0ab5e9` include `status`'s per-target `client_dir`, `install_root`, `exe_name` (`src/app/status.rs:245-253`), `list`'s per-target `client_dir` (`src/app/list.rs:60-62`), `history`'s `ops` (`-v`) and `changes` (without it) (`src/app/history.rs:69-74`), `targets`' `details` (`src/app/targets.rs:112-114`), `info`'s `record_path` (`src/app/info.rs:130-132`) and `install`'s `client_dir` (`src/app/install.rs:109-111`).
- `Paths::with_roots(home, config, state, cache)` builds the binary's paths for a test home (`tests/common/http.rs:285` does); its accessors (`src/state/paths.rs:271-441`) name every state and cache file (`registry_file`, `target_record`, `files_index`, `history_file`, `status_file`, `journal_dir`, `state_snapshots_dir`, `state_trash`, `blobs_dir`, `http_cache_dir`, `wowi_index`, `discovery_cache`, `release_memo`, `export_memo`, `backup_inventory`, `history_tail`, `errors_ack`, `errors_memo`, `doorbell_file`, `cache_trash`); `ClientPaths::new(client_dir)` gives `meta_dir`, `marker`, `backups`, `stage`, `snapshots` (`:484-566`). A backup is `<meta>/backups/<id>/` with `backup.json`, `manifest.json` and `addons.json` (`src/backup/mod.rs:1-3`).
- From subtask 4: `validate::validate_envelope(&envelope, stderr)`, `validate::schemas()`, and `support::check`. From A9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9`): `ErrorCode::declared_detail_paths()` (own and shared keys), `ErrorCode::detail_spec().declared_paths()` (own only), in the path syntax `a`, `a.b`, `a[].b`.
- `TestLog` (T1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, `tests/common/tlog.rs`): `tlog!()`, `log.step`, `log.note`, `log.json`, `log.run` (whose result exposes the `common::home::Run` that `support::check` takes), `log.tree`, `log.assert_unchanged`.

## Technical Approach

### 1. `tests/contract/snapshot_walk.rs`

`every_envelope_snapshot_validates`:

1. Collect every `*.snap` file under `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR/tests` and `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR/src` (not `*.snap.new`), sorted.
2. Body: the text after the second line that is exactly `---`. Keep the file when the body parses as a JSON object with the keys `ok`, `schema_version` and `command`.
3. **Substitute typed samples** for whole-value placeholders, in string values and in object keys, recursively:

   | Placeholder | Sample |
   |---|---|
   | `<ulid>`, `<tx>`, `<key>`, `<run>` | `"00000000000000000000000000"` (26 Crockford zeros: it matches the ULID pattern) |
   | `<time>`, `<checked_at>` | `"2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"` |
   | `<bytes>` | the integer `0` |

   `<version>`, `<precondition>` and placeholders inside longer strings stay as they are (their schemas are plain strings). Any other whole-value string of the form `<[a-z_]+>` fails the test with its file and JSON path: a new redaction must be added to this table.
4. If `meta` is absent, insert `{"elapsed_ms": 0, "offline": false}` (the contract snapshots strip it).
5. Validate with `validate_envelope(&envelope, "")`. For the three renderer fixtures listed in `FRAME_ONLY` (exact paths, with the reason "a renderer fixture: its data is a synthetic struct that proves declaration-order rendering"), remove `data` first, so only the frame, the error and the warnings are checked.
6. Collect every failing file's message; at the end, fail with all of them, or pass and print one line: `validated <n> envelope snapshots (<f> frame-only) of <m> .snap files`.
7. Assert `n >= 100` (123 at `c0ab5e9`), so a wrong root fails rather than passing on nothing.

Decided while writing this bead: substitution keeps the ULID pattern in the schemas (A10 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.10`, the semantic manifest) records it as a bound) while still validating every snapshot; the plan's §6.4 assumed ids had no pattern, which is not so.

`placeholder_table_cases` (a table test of the substitution function): `ulid_value`, `tx_value`, `key_value`, `run_value`, `time_value`, `checked_at_value`, `bytes_value_becomes_integer`, `ulid_as_map_key`, `placeholder_inside_a_string_stays`, `version_stays`, `unknown_placeholder_fails`.

### 2. `tests/contract/verbose_fields.rs`

`verbose_only_fields_are_optional_and_validate`, a `TestLog` scenario on one `Scene::new()`:

1. Step `install`: `Scene::install_foo()` through `log.run`, checked.
2. For each command below, step `<command> without -v` then `<command> with -v`: run it with `--json`, and the second time also `-v --progress json`, each through `log.run` and `support::check` (which validates data, frame and every stderr event); then `log.json("field", …)` the value at the field path and assert it is absent without `-v` and present with it:

   | Command | Field |
   |---|---|
   | `status` | `targets[].client_dir` (each target) |
   | `list` | `targets[].client_dir` |
   | `history` | `entries[].ops` present only with `-v`; `entries[].changes` present only without |
   | `targets` | `targets[].details` |
   | `info foo -t retail` (the name `install_foo` installed) | `record_path` |
   | `install gh:o/foo --file <foo2.zip> -t retail --dry-run` | `client_dir` |

   (Confirm each path against the data type before writing the assertion; the field names and their `-v`-only doc comments are at the locations above.)
3. Step `events`: assert that, across the `-v --progress json` runs, at least one `progress` event and one `log` event at level `debug` were validated (counted from the parsed stderr), so event validation is exercised under `-v`.

### 3. `tests/contract/state_files.rs`

`every_file_a_session_writes_validates_against_its_kind`, a `TestLog` scenario on one `Scene::new()` whose retail client has a played `WTF/` (`common::wtf`, with the `FAKEACCT`/`FakeRealm`/`FakeChar` names):

1. Steps, each through `log.run` and `support::check`, with `--progress json`, and `assert_private_all(stdout, stderr)` (common rule 9) on each: `install gh:o/foo -t retail` (the replayed GitHub release, not a local file: `export` leaves locally installed addons out, with `export_local_source`); `export --write` (writes `addons.toml` and the export memo; its `data.content` is the same TOML); `backup create -t retail`; `install gh:o/foo --file <foo2.zip> -t retail` with `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS=engine.journal.prepared=abort` (a crash: exit -1, not checked, leaves a journal); `status` (recovers it).
2. After each step, step `files after <step>`: `log.tree` of `<state>` and `<cache>`, then validate strictly (subtask 3's `Validator::new(…, true)` over `file_schemas()`):
   - every `.json` document under `<state>`, `<cache>` and each client's `<meta>`, by kind, from a table built with `Paths::with_roots(env.home(), env.config(), env.state(), env.cache())` and `ClientPaths::new(<client dir>)`: `registry_file` → `registry`; `targets_dir()/*.json` → `target_record`; the files-index accessor's directory → `files_index`; `status_file` → `status`; `discovery_cache` → `discovery_cache`; `http_cache_dir()/**.json` → `http_validators`; `release_memo` → `release_memo`; `wowi_index` → `wowi_index`; `export_memo` → `export_memo`; `backup_inventory` → `backup_inventory`; `history_tail` → `history_tail`; `errors_memo`, `errors_ack`; `doorbell_file` → `doorbell`; `ClientPaths::marker` → `target_marker`; `<meta>/backups/<id>/backup.json`, `manifest.json`, `addons.json` → `backup`, `backup_manifest`, `backup_addons`;
   - every line of `history_file()` against `history`, every line of every `journal_dir()/*.jsonl` against `journal`;
   - the exported `addons.toml` (`Paths::addons_toml`), read with the `toml` crate into a `serde_json::Value`, against `desired_state`.

   Skipped, each with its reason in a `SKIPPED` table: the state and client snapshot directories and the trash directories (copies kept for undo, which may be an older version), the stage directories, `blobs_dir()` (archives), `<meta>`'s client folders (`Interface/AddOns`, `WTF/`: not omaddons' files), `net.log`, and `*.lock` files. Any other `.json` document matching no row fails with its path relative to the home: a new persisted file cannot ship without a kind.
3. Step `coverage`: assert that the kinds validated include `registry`, `target_record`, `files_index`, `target_marker`, `history`, `history_tail`, `journal`, `backup`, `backup_manifest`, `export_memo` and `desired_state`; `log.json("validated", {kind: count})` and `log.note` of the kinds no step wrote.

### 4. The declared-`details` report

**Observation.** In `tests/contract/validate.rs`, `pub fn observed_details(envelope: &Value) -> BTreeSet<(String, String)>`: the `(code, path)` pairs of the envelope's `error.details` and of every object anywhere in `data` that has a string `code` naming a registered `ErrorCode` and an object `details` (`TargetResult.error`). Paths are A9's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9`, meanings and `DetailSpec`s) syntax: each key `k` of a details object gives `k`; a nested object gives `k.j`; an array of objects gives `k[]` and `k[].j`; an array of scalars gives `k`. In `support::check`, when the environment variable `CONTRACT_DETAILS_OBSERVED` is set, append each pair not yet seen in this process (a process-wide `Mutex<BTreeSet>`) to that file as one JSON line `{"code":…,"path":…}`, with one `write_all` on a file opened in append mode. Decided while writing this bead: the variable is a private parent-to-child handshake of the contract test binary, not an `OMADDONS_` variable, so it needs no `contract::env` registry row (T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs) decided the same for its own child handshake).

**The report.** `tests/contract/details_report.rs`, `declared_details_keys_no_contract_test_observes`, `#[ignore = "a report: run with --ignored --nocapture; H1 makes it empty and an assertion"]` (H1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, the pre-freeze audit, later turns it into an assertion):

1. The contract tests run on parallel threads with no "after all" hook, so the report runs the suite again as a child: `std::process::Command::new(std::env::current_exe())` with `--skip declared_details_keys_no_contract_test_observes` and `CONTRACT_DETAILS_OBSERVED=<a file in a fresh tempdir>`; wait for it.
2. Read the observed pairs. The declared pairs: for every `ErrorCode::ALL`, its own paths `code.detail_spec().declared_paths()`, and the shared paths (`declared_detail_paths()` minus the own ones) once, under `*` (observed when any code observed them).
3. Print, sorted: the totals (`declared <d>, observed <o>, unobserved <u>`), then each code with its unobserved paths, then the shared ones, then the child's exit status (a failing child is reported, not hidden).
4. The test passes unless the child could not be started or the file could not be read.

Decided while writing this bead: it counts only what `support::check` sees, because a key observed in another suite is never validated against its spec; H1 empties the list by adding contract rows, which also validates those keys.

### 5. README

When the walker lands, in the same commit: README's "Stability" sentence that subtask 4 added ("Every envelope the suite produces is validated against its command's JSON Schema …") becomes "Every envelope the suite produces, and every JSON envelope snapshot in the repository, is validated against its command's JSON Schema …", and the Tests table's `tests/contract/` row (`README.md:2625`) adds "and every envelope snapshot".

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `every_envelope_snapshot_validates` passes: at least 100 envelope snapshots validated (123 at `c0ab5e9`), the three renderer fixtures frame-only, and the summary line printed; `placeholder_table_cases` passes, including an unknown placeholder failing.
- [ ] `verbose_only_fields_are_optional_and_validate` passes: each command of its table validates with and without `-v`, the named field absent without `-v` and present with it, and `progress` and debug `log` events validated.
- [ ] `every_file_a_session_writes_validates_against_its_kind` passes: every `.json` document, history line and journal line after each step, and the exported `addons.toml`, validate strictly against their kinds' schemas; the eleven named kinds were validated; an unmatched `.json` document fails it; `assert_private_all` holds on every step.
- [ ] `declared_details_keys_no_contract_test_observes` runs (with `--ignored`) and prints the totals and the unobserved paths; the leaf's close comment quotes its output.
- [ ] `support::check` records observed `details` pairs only when `CONTRACT_DETAILS_OBSERVED` is set, and otherwise behaves exactly as before.
- [ ] README's "Stability" sentence and the Tests table's `tests/contract/` row name the envelope snapshots, in the walker's commit.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `br lint` is clean for this subtask.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

- `placeholder_table_cases` (in `snapshot_walk.rs`), the cases of §1.
- `observed_details_paths` (in `validate.rs` or beside it): cases `flat_keys`, `nested_object`, `array_of_objects`, `array_of_scalars`, `embedded_target_result_error`, `no_error`, each with its expected set of `(code, path)` pairs.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

The four tests of the Technical Approach: `every_envelope_snapshot_validates`, `verbose_only_fields_are_optional_and_validate`, `every_file_a_session_writes_validates_against_its_kind`, and the ignored `declared_details_keys_no_contract_test_observes`. They are modules of the contract test binary (`mod snapshot_walk; mod verbose_fields; mod state_files; mod details_report;` in `tests/contract/main.rs`).

Run them alone with `cargo test --test contract snapshot_walk verbose_fields state_files`, and the report with `cargo test --test contract -- --ignored --nocapture declared_details_keys_no_contract_test_observes`. Once T1's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs) `argc e2e` exists, mark `verbose_fields` and `state_files` as end-to-end suites the way T1 documents.

### Logging

- `verbose_only_fields_are_optional_and_validate` and `every_file_a_session_writes_validates_against_its_kind` use `TestLog` (`tlog!()`): one `log.step` per command and flag set, every command through `log.run` (argv, environment overrides, exit, envelope, stderr events, `net.log` lines, failpoints armed), `log.json("field", …)` for each value compared, `log.tree` of `<state>` and `<cache>` after each step, `log.json("validated", …)` per step with the kinds and counts, and, on a validation failure, `log.note` with the file (relative to the home), its kind, and every `Failure`. A failing scenario prints the transcript path and its last steps (T1's guard).
- The walker logs, on failure, each failing snapshot's path, the substituted envelope (pretty) and every failure; on success, its summary line.
- The report prints its whole result to stdout (`--nocapture`).
- Unit tests: every case named; messages print the input and the expected and actual output.

## Considerations

- **Placeholders are contract test conventions.** A leaf that adds a redaction to a snapshot helper (E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, `doctor diagnose`) adds `<run>` for doctor run ids, already in the table as a ULID sample; check the sample still fits that leaf's schema) adds its row to the walker's table in the same commit, or the walker fails naming it.
- **Later leaves and the files scenario.** D4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`, plan files under `<cache>/plans/`), E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, `<state>/doctor/runs/<run>/report.json`) and E5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`, repair journals) add `KINDS` rows; whichever session of this scenario reaches their files then needs their rows in its table. A new `.json` file with no kind fails here, which is the point.
- **Privacy.** The backup's `manifest.json` names `WTF/` paths; the scenario uses only the synthetic `FAKEACCT`/`FakeRealm`/`FakeChar` names, never prints file contents on success, and runs `assert_private_all` over every step's stdout and stderr with `--progress json`.
- **Gate time.** The walker reads about 160 small files; the two scenarios run about 25 commands between them. The report reruns the whole contract suite, so it is ignored by default.
- **Hot spot `tests/contract/main.rs`:** this part adds four `mod` lines and the observation hook inside `check`, in its own block beside subtask 4's.

## Dependencies

- Parent: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3 (Schemas with the serialize contract, declared `details`, and live validation).
- Before it: subtask 4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3.4`): `validate_envelope`, the compiled schemas and `support::check`'s validation, which every test here reuses (and, through it, subtasks 1–3). Also T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs), whose `TestLog` the two scenarios use.
- After it: nothing inside the leaf; subtask 5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3.5`) runs in parallel. T2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.2`, the slice-1 demo) calls this part's walker for "every envelope snapshot, `details` included".

title: `omaddons capabilities`
description:
## How to work this bead

This bead is worked through its 4 subtasks, listed below in work order. Claim a subtask, not this bead (`br ready --parent omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4` lists the ready ones). The agent that closes the last open subtask then verifies every acceptance criterion of this bead (they are the leaf's, not any one subtask's), and closes this bead with `br close omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4 --reason "done: <evidence> · found: <ids>"`. Until this bead is closed, every bead it blocks stays blocked.

1. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4.1 `CommandInfo` from the live clap tree, value sets for the app-validated flags, and declared requirements: `src/contract/commands.rs` and `src/contract/values.rs`, the per-command facts every description of the CLI reads (this bead, and A10's manifest).
2. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4.2 Effective configuration values with their source, a tolerant `config.toml` load, and per-code retryability: `src/contract/effective.rs`, `Config::load_tolerant`, `ConfigProblem`, `LIMIT_CONFIG_KEYS`, credential presence without reading a secret, and `ErrorCode::retryability()`.
3. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4.3 The `capabilities` command: `Registry::build()`, its data and human form, wired in under DEC-1: `src/contract/mod.rs`'s `Registry`, `src/app/capabilities.rs`, and every registry touch point in one commit.
4. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4.4 Tests: `tests/capabilities.rs` (round trip, completeness, purity, broken config, credentials, the human form) and the 20 ms budget in `tests/perf.rs`.

Subtasks 1 and 2 touch different files and do not depend on each other's code: work them in parallel. Subtask 3 joins them and adds the command; subtask 4 proves it end to end.

**Size M, one closure.** The registry walk, the effective values and the command are one promise: what `capabilities` says is what the binary does. Subtasks split the work into commits that each pass `argc gate`; they do not split the closure. This bead closes only when all four are done, so A6, H1 and T2 never see half of it.

## Background

### Why this bead exists

An agent meeting omaddons for the first time has, at `c0ab5e9`, no machine-readable description of the tool. It can read `omaddons help --json` (`HelpData`, `src/app/help.rs:29-97`), which lists command names, about lines and four facts per flag (`name`, `short`, `takes_value`, `about`, `src/app/help.rs:128-140`), and nothing else: no flag values, no defaults, no conflicts, no exit codes per command, no error catalog, no limits, no sources. Everything else it must learn from a 2,800-line README or by trial and error.

This bead adds `omaddons capabilities [--json]`: one call, offline, in a few milliseconds, that lists every command with every flag (its allowed values, default, conflicts and requirements), every alias, each command's exit codes and exit dictionary, whether it mutates, binds a preview or stores a plan, whether it uses the network, the error and warning codes with their exits, retryability, meaning and typed `details` shape, the recommendation actions, the failure-mode summary, the release environment variables, every limit, source, game family, client-rules row and `-t` form, and pointers to the schemas and the guide. Every value is generated from the live clap tree and the binary's registries, never kept by hand, and the values `config.toml` can change are reported as they are in effect, each saying whether it is built in or comes from the config.

It is the first of the three calls M4 promises an agent needs (`capabilities --json`, `robot-docs guide`, `status --json`), and the contract a later MCP adapter or Claude Code mod would read (`omad-claude-mod-explore-0va5`, deferred outside M4).

Leaves named in this section: A1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1`, per-command facts in `COMMANDS` and canonical names), A2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.2`, the action, event, env-var, feature and per-source registries), A3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`, schemas, declared `details` and live validation), A5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5`, `robot-docs schema` and `robot-docs errors`), A6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.6`, bare help's discovery line), A9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9`, a meaning and a typed `DetailSpec` for every code), A10 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.10`, the semantic contract manifest), B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`, the guide renderer and `robot-docs guide`), C1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.1`, misplaced clients), C4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4`, the run-the-fix corpus), D1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1`, the approval witness and the build id), E1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`, the failure-mode registry), E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, `doctor diagnose` and the doctor exit dictionary), E4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4`, `doctor capabilities` and the other doctor verbs), H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, the pre-freeze audit), T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs), T2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.2`, the slice-1 end-to-end suite).

### The milestone goals and checkpoint criteria it serves

- **G-M4-1 Self-describing.** "An agent with no prior knowledge learns everything it needs from the binary itself, in at most three calls: `omaddons capabilities --json`, `omaddons robot-docs guide`, `omaddons status --json`. Every fact in those outputs is generated from the code, so it cannot drift from what the code does." This bead is the first of the three calls.
- **G-M4-2 The first guess works**, in part: every alias, flag alias and allowed value is listed, so an agent can build a correct argv before it guesses.
- **G-M4-5 Frozen and enforced**, in part: `capabilities` is one of the shapes the freeze pins, and the per-command facts it builds (`CommandInfo`) are the CLI inputs A10's semantic manifest records.
- **Checkpoint criterion 1, Capabilities** (this bead owns it):
  - `omaddons capabilities --json` carries the six keys the vision requires (`version`, `contract_version`, `features`, `commands`, `exit_codes`, `env_vars`) and the extra keys of the capabilities shape;
  - it round-trips: every command entry, every flag of it and every alias parses (`Cli::try_parse_from` with `--help`); every error, warning and action it lists is registered, and every registered one is listed; failure modes are summarized (`count`, `subsystems`) with a pointer to `doctor capabilities`, which lists every id, and the count equals the registry's;
  - it makes no request and writes nothing: `net.log`, `<state>` and `<cache>` are hash-identical before and after;
  - it takes under 20 ms (median of 21, release build).
  - (Amended from vision §7, which asked only for the six keys.)
- **Checkpoint criterion 14, The contract is frozen**, in part: the golden records the CLI's paths, flags, positionals, defaults, value grammars, arity, conflicts and requirements; A10 reads them from this bead's `CommandInfo`.
- **Checkpoint criterion 17**, in part: the perf budgets in `tests/perf.rs` pass, this bead's among them.

The slice-1 demo ("`capabilities --json` round-trips; …") is run and recorded by T2 as a test, reusing this bead's round-trip helper.

### The decisions that shape it

- **M4-D4: `capabilities` is offline, scan-free and write-free, and reports effective values.** It reads the binary's registries and `config.toml`, and nothing else: no discovery, no target registry, no network, no writes. Values `config.toml` can change (limits, source enablement, rules rows, `git_hosts`) are reported as their effective values, each with `source: "builtin" | "config"`. A broken `config.toml` does not fail the command: it reports built-in values and a `config_error` object (path, line, column, message), because an agent asking "what can this tool do?" must get an answer even when the config is broken. The human form is a compact summary, at most 40 lines, ending with "`--json` for the full description". It runs in under 20 ms. *Why:* capabilities is the first call of an agent's session and is cached by agents, so it must be cheap and must not depend on the machine's clients; effective values matter because a user who raised `limits.download_max_bytes` changed what the tool does. *Rejected:* including the discovered clients (that is `status`, and it costs a scan); failing on a broken config (it hides the description exactly when an agent needs it to diagnose).
- **M4-D2: one contract registry feeds every description of the CLI.** A new module, `src/contract/`, assembles a `Registry` from the live clap tree (`Cli::command()`), `app::COMMANDS` with its per-command facts, the error, warning and exit registries, the action, event, env-var and feature registries, the limits and politeness registries, the rules table and the sources registry, and the doctor's failure-mode registry. `capabilities`, `robot-docs` (guide, schema, errors), the wire-name golden, bare help's discovery line and `doctor capabilities` all read this registry. A fact clap cannot provide is declared exactly once, beside the command or code it describes, and a test cross-checks it against behaviour. *Why:* the vision's rule for capabilities ("generated from the live clap tree and the registries, never maintained by hand") only works if the registries exist, and one registry means the guide, capabilities and the golden cannot disagree. *Rejected:* a hand-written `capabilities.json` asset (it drifts, which is the exact failure capabilities exists to prevent); deriving every fact from runtime behaviour (a command's exits are a promise and need a declaration that tests verify); proc-macro attributes on clap structs (a dependency and compile time for no gain over a table).
- **M4-D3: the envelope's `schema_version` is the contract version.** The contract has one version, `output::SCHEMA_VERSION` ("1.0"); `capabilities.contract_version` repeats it. Persisted files keep their own versions; the crate version (`version`, `tool_version`) is independent. *Rejected:* a separate `contract_version` that moves on its own (two numbers for one contract invite them to disagree).
- **M4-D5: per-command exit codes are declared beside the command and verified.** A1 gave every `CommandEntry` `dictionary` (`General` | `Doctor`), `exits: &'static [u8]`, `data` (its schema function), `stores_plan` and `network` (`None` | `Optional` | `Required`), with static rules (a `--check`/`--strict` command lists 6, a mutating command lists 5, every general command lists 0, 1 and 2) and the contract suite's check that every observed exit is declared. This bead publishes them as `commands[].exit_codes`, `dictionary`, `stores_plan` and `network`. *Rejected:* deriving exits from the codes a command can raise (not statically knowable); every command declaring 0–6 (true but useless).
- **M4-D6: environment variables get a registry.** `contract::env::ENV_VARS` (A2) lists every variable the binary reads with a kind (`release`, `debug`, `harness`); `capabilities.env_vars` publishes the `release` ones only. *Rejected:* publishing debug variables (release builds ignore them, so listing them would mislead).
- **M4-D10 and A.1's tri-state.** Every error code has a typed `DetailSpec` (A9), published as `error_codes[].details_schema`, a JSON Schema fragment. Per code, `retryable` is `true`, `false` or `"conditional"` for codes whose instances decide; every error *instance* keeps its boolean `error.retryable`. *Why:* a boolean would lie for those codes.
- **M4-D11:** recommendation actions are an enumerable `Action` registry (A2); `actions[]` lists `Action::ALL` with each action's description and destructive default.
- **M4-D29 and M4-D30:** one failure-mode registry (`FAILURE_MODES`, E1) serves the doctor, `status` and capabilities; capabilities carries only a summary (`count`, `subsystems`) and points at `doctor capabilities`, which lists every id (E4).
- **M4-D19 and M4-D22:** `binds` is not a field of `CommandEntry`; it is derived from `precondition::BINDING_COMMANDS`, which stays the single list. `stores_plan` is D4's to set.
- **M4-D55 and A3's rule test:** six naming and shape rules hold for every new shape from slice 1 (timestamps; null versus omitted, where a key in a command's schema is always present and `null` when it has no value; snake case and plural array names; closed enumerations; canonical command paths; typed `details`). A new shape may not be added to `tests/contract/rules_allowlist.txt`; reasoned permanent exceptions go in the rule test's coded `EXCEPTIONS` list, which H1 audits.

- **M4-D18 and DEC-3:** every data struct derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`; maps are `BTreeMap`; no `HashMap` or `HashSet` in a serialized type. `capabilities` adds no volatile key: two runs of one binary on one home print identical bytes.

### How it serves the vision

The vision's G4 is "the first command an agent guesses works", with discovery through `capabilities`, `doctor` and `robot-docs`. Vision §5.10 lists capabilities' required keys (`version`, `contract_version`, `features`, `commands`, `exit_codes`, `env_vars`), its extra keys (`limits`, `sources` with `enabled`, `requires_credential` and `hosts`, `families`, `client_rules`, `target_id_forms`, `error_codes` with meaning, exit and retryable, `schemas_uri`, `robot_docs_uri`), each command's `description`, `mutates`, `json`, `args`, `flags`, `exit_codes` and `aliases`, and the rule that every alias is listed and everything is "generated from the live clap tree and the registries, never maintained by hand". The project's thesis is that omaddons stays the sole, safe, undoable authority over what it manages; a description generated from the code, which tests hold equal to behaviour, is what lets an agent trust that authority without reading the source.

### 1. `CommandInfo`: the per-command facts from the live clap tree (subtask 1)

`src/contract/commands.rs` walks `Cli::command()` after `.build()` (so every subcommand carries the propagated global flags) and joins each `app::COMMANDS` row with the clap command at its path. A10's manifest reads the same `CommandInfo`; it is the one place the CLI's inputs are extracted.

```rust
/// One command path this build has, with every fact the descriptions of the CLI publish:
/// clap's (arguments, aliases, about) joined with its `COMMANDS` row's (M4-D2, M4-D5).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct CommandInfo {
    pub path: &'static str,            // the COMMANDS row's name, = envelope `command`
    pub about: String,                 // clap's about (the variant's doc comment), trimmed
    pub group: Group,
    pub mutates: bool,
    pub dictionary: Dictionary,
    pub exits: &'static [u8],
    pub args: Vec<ArgInfo>,            // positionals, in index order
    pub flags: Vec<FlagInfo>,          // the command's own flags in declaration order, then the propagated globals
    pub aliases: Vec<String>,          // clap's visible aliases of the command
    pub stores_plan: bool,
    pub binds: bool,                   // precondition::BINDING_COMMANDS.contains(path)
    pub network: Network,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ArgInfo {
    pub id: String,                    // clap's argument id (`refs`), as `help --json` names it
    pub value_name: String,            // the first value name, else the id upper-cased (clap's display)
    pub required: bool,
    pub multiple: bool,                // the arity's maximum exceeds 1
    pub default: Option<String>,       // clap's recorded default
    pub values: Values,
    pub help: String,
    pub conflicts_with: Vec<String>,   // names (flag long names, positional ids), symmetric
    pub requires: Vec<String>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct FlagInfo {
    pub long: String,                  // without dashes
    pub short: Option<char>,
    pub aliases: Vec<String>,          // visible long aliases, without dashes (`flavor`)
    pub value_name: Option<String>,    // `None` for a flag that takes no value
    pub takes_value: bool,
    pub multiple: bool,                // ArgAction::Append or Count, or an arity above 1
    pub default: Option<String>,       // `None` for a flag that takes no value
    pub values: Values,
    pub conflicts_with: Vec<String>,
    pub requires: Vec<String>,
    pub global: bool,
    pub help: String,                  // clap's short help, trimmed
}

/// What a value may be.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Values {
    /// Any text clap accepts (a path, a number, an id).
    Any,
    /// Exactly these words: clap's possible values (hidden ones left out), or an
    /// app-validated flag's declared set.
    Words(Vec<&'static str>),          // decided: `String` if clap's `PossibleValue` names are not 'static
    /// A duration (a whole number and one of these units) or an RFC 3339 time.
    DurationOrTime(&'static [DurationUnit]),
}

/// Every `COMMANDS` row's facts, in `COMMANDS` order.
pub fn commands() -> Vec<CommandInfo>;
/// One row's facts; `None` for a path that is no row.
pub fn command(path: &str) -> Option<CommandInfo>;
/// The facts of `entry` from the built clap command `cmd` at its path (pure, so unit tests
/// can pass synthetic clap commands).
pub fn command_info(entry: &CommandEntry, cmd: &clap::Command) -> CommandInfo;
```

Rules of the walk, each a unit-tested case:

- **Joining.** The clap command of a row is found by walking `get_subcommands()` word by word along the row's path (`backup restore` → `backup`, then `restore`). A1's bijection test guarantees every row has one; a row whose path does not resolve is left out of `commands()` and fails `every_commands_row_has_command_info` (no `unwrap`, no panic in production).
- **Flags** are the arguments with a long or short name; **args** are the positionals, ordered by `get_index()`. Hidden arguments (`is_hide_set()`) and hidden possible values are left out, as clap's help leaves them out (none exist at `c0ab5e9`). The root-only `-V/--version` is not a subcommand's argument and is not published.
- **Own flags first,** in declaration order, then the propagated globals in `GlobalArgs` order, each `global: true`. Decided while writing this bead (confirm or adjust in the close comment): **`--if-match` is listed only on paths where `binds` is true.** clap propagates it everywhere, but `cli::check_if_match` (`src/cli.rs:309-339`) refuses it with `usage` on every other path, so listing it there would describe a flag the command does not accept. The rule is applied in `command_info` from `BINDING_COMMANDS`, so D2, D3, E6 and E8 extending the list extend capabilities with no edit here.
- **`value_name`:** the first of `get_value_names()`; otherwise, for a positional or a value-taking flag, the id upper-cased (what clap's usage shows); `None` for a flag that takes no value.
- **`takes_value`** is `get_action().takes_values()`. **`multiple`**: `ArgAction::Append` or `ArgAction::Count`, or `get_num_args()`'s maximum above 1.
- **`default`:** decided while writing this bead: clap's `get_default_values()` for a value-taking argument (`omarchy install --section` → `"right"`); `None` for an argument that takes no value, whose recorded default is clap's implicit `"false"` or `"0"`, which nobody types. An argument with more than one default value fails the unit test `no_argument_has_several_defaults` (none exist), so the leaf that adds one decides how to publish it.
- **`values`:** an `APP_VALIDATED` row's set when the flag has one (section 2); else clap's possible values when there are any; else `Any`.
- **`conflicts_with`:** decided while writing this bead: the **symmetric closure** of what clap records, because clap enforces a conflict in both directions while recording it on one side. For each argument `a`, `cmd.get_arg_conflicts_with(a)` gives the arguments `a` names; the published list of `a` is those plus every `b` whose list names `a`, deduplicated, in the command's argument order, each named by its long name (flags) or its id (positionals). So `install --any-flavor` lists `no-any-flavor` and `--no-any-flavor` lists `any-flavor`; `undo`'s positional `tx` lists `last-by` and `run`. Group conflicts are unrolled by clap's getter. `errors`' `args_conflicts_with_subcommands` is a command setting, expressed by the path structure (`errors` and `errors dismiss` are two paths), and lists nothing.
- **`requires`:** from the declared `REQUIRES` table (section 3), because clap gives no public getter.
- **`aliases`** of a command: `get_visible_aliases()` (`install` → `add`; nested commands have none). Of a flag: `get_visible_aliases()` without dashes (`target` → `flavor`). Decided while writing this bead: a visible *short* alias fails the unit test `no_flag_has_a_visible_short_alias` (none exist), so the leaf that adds one decides how to publish it; the vision requires every alias to be listed.
- **`about` and `help`:** `get_about()` and `get_help()` rendered with `to_string()` and trimmed (no colour: the tree is built with `ColorChoice::Never`).
- **The row's facts:** `group`, `mutates`, `dictionary`, `exits`, `stores_plan` and `network` are copied from the `CommandEntry`; `binds` is `BINDING_COMMANDS.contains(&path)`.

A unit test `the_clap_tree_passes_clap_debug_asserts` runs `Cli::command().debug_assert()`, which rules out the one panic of `get_arg_conflicts_with` (a conflict naming an unknown argument) for every tree the gate accepts.

### 2. Value sets: one list for the parser and for capabilities (subtask 1)

The plan's rule: `possible_values` comes from clap where clap validates; for the flags validated in app code (`--actor`, `--by`, `--last-by`, the `--since` forms) it comes from a declared value set beside the flag's parser, one list used by both the parser and capabilities.

`src/contract/values.rs` (a leaf module with no dependencies, so `model.rs` and `app/history.rs` can use it):

```rust
/// What an app-validated flag accepts, declared once beside its parser (M4-D2): the parser
/// reads it, and so do capabilities and the manifest.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum ValueSet {
    /// Exactly these words.
    Words(&'static [&'static str]),
    /// A whole number followed by one of these units (`30m`), or an RFC 3339 time.
    DurationOrTime(&'static [DurationUnit]),
```

### 3. Requirements: declared, because clap hides them (subtask 1)

```rust
/// Flags clap requires another argument with (`#[arg(requires = …)]`), declared here because
/// clap gives no public getter (M4-D2: a fact clap cannot provide is declared once and
/// cross-checked). Empty at `c0ab5e9`; E6 adds `doctor fix --force` → `yes`.
pub struct Requirement { pub path: &'static str, pub long: &'static str, pub requires: &'static [&'static str] }
pub const REQUIRES: &[Requirement] = &[];

/// Every way `REQUIRES` disagrees with `cmd`'s behaviour (pure; unit-tested on synthetic commands).
pub fn requirement_violations(path: &str, cmd: &clap::Command, table: &[Requirement]) -> Vec<String>;
```

`requirement_violations` probes the built command: for each flag, it parses `[<path words>, <sample of every required positional>, --<flag> <sample>]` with `cmd.clone().try_get_matches_from(…)`. A `MissingRequiredArgument` error whose missing argument is not declared for that flag is a violation ("`doctor fix --force` needs `--yes` to parse: declare it in contract::commands::REQUIRES"); a declared requirement under which the flag parses alone is a violation too ("REQUIRES says `--force` requires `--yes`, but it parses without it"). The sample of a value is its first possible value, else `"1"` (which every text, path and number parser accepts; a parser that refuses it fails the test with its flag named, and the implementer adds a sample case). The unit test `requirements_are_declared_and_true` runs it over every `COMMANDS` path.

### 4. The tolerant `config.toml` load (subtask 2)

In `src/state/config.rs`:

```rust
/// Why config.toml could not be used: what `capabilities` reports as `config_error` instead of
/// failing (M4-D4).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ConfigProblem {
    /// The file; `None` when HOME gives no config path at all.
    pub path: Option<PathBuf>,
    /// 1-based line and column; `None` when the file could not be read at all.
    pub line: Option<u64>,
    pub column: Option<u64>,
    /// What is wrong, without the location: the TOML parser's message, or "<key> <rule>",
    /// or the OS error.
    pub message: String,
}

/// config.toml as `capabilities` reads it: never an error.
pub struct TolerantConfig { pub loaded: LoadedConfig, pub problem: Option<ConfigProblem> }

impl Config {
    /// `parse`'s checks, with the problem typed: `corrupt` and `invalid` build a `ConfigProblem`,
    /// and `parse` maps it into today's `state_corrupt` error byte for byte.
    pub fn parse_checked(text: &str, path: &Path) -> std::result::Result<(Self, Vec<Warning>), ConfigProblem>;
    /// `load`, never failing: a missing file is the default config with no problem; an unreadable
    /// one (permission, a directory, invalid UTF-8) is a problem with no line; a broken one is a
    /// problem with its line and column. Then `loaded` holds the default config, no warnings.
    pub fn load_tolerant(paths: &Paths) -> TolerantConfig;
}
```

- `corrupt` and `invalid` (`src/state/config.rs:772-811`) are split: a function building the `ConfigProblem` (`message` is the part after the location: the trimmed TOML message for `corrupt`; `"<key> <message>"` for `invalid`, with `column: 1`), and `ConfigProblem::into_error(self, text)` rebuilding today's error (`"<path> line L, column C: <message>"` or `"<path> line L: <message>"`, the same `details` and fix). `parse` becomes `parse_checked(..).map_err(into_error)`; every existing test of `parse` and `load` passes unchanged, and `parse_errors_are_unchanged_through_the_problem` pins each message and `details` object.
- `load` itself is unchanged (its `io` error and its missing-file case).
- Decided while writing this bead: **no size bound is added.** Every command reads `config.toml` whole through `Config::load` today; capabilities adds no new reader, and a bound would change every command and is not in the plan's constant table. ### 6. Per-code retryability (subtask 2)

A5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5`, `robot-docs errors`) publishes the same tri-state, so there is one declaration, read by both commands; **whichever of A4 and A5 lands first adds it, in exactly this form** (A5's bead specifies the same), and the other reuses it. In `src/error.rs`, beside `default_retryable` (outside the code rows):

```rust
/// Whether an error of a code is worth retrying, as the code registry publishes it
/// (`robot-docs errors`, `capabilities`, the manifest). Each error instance keeps its own
/// boolean `error.retryable`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, JsonSchema)]
#[serde(untagged)]
pub enum Retryability {
    /// Every instance of the code has this retryability.
    Fixed(bool),
    /// Instances differ; each error's `retryable` decides, and the code's meaning says when.
    Conditional(Conditional),
}

/// The one word of [`Retryability::Conditional`].
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, JsonSchema)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum Conditional { Conditional }

impl ErrorCode {
    pub const fn retryability(self) -> Retryability {
        match self {
            Self::PlanStale | Self::HttpStatus | Self::HashMismatch | Self::Network | Self::Io => {
                Retryability::Conditional(Conditional::Conditional)
            }
            _ => Retryability::Fixed(self.default_retryable()),
        }
    }
}
```

- It serializes as `true`, `false` or `"conditional"`; its schema is a union of a boolean and the one string, so the value set is closed; no custom `Serialize` (none exists outside tests, and none is added).
- **Decided while writing this bead (the plan names three):** the conditional set is the plan's `http_status`, `hash_mismatch` and `plan_stale`, plus `network` and `io`, because the code shows instances of those two that differ from their registered default (facts above), and publishing them as fixed booleans would be the lie A.1's decision exists to prevent. `recovery_failed` (`src/engine/tx.rs:572-578`) assigns `error.retryable = false` to any error whose in-process recovery failed: a property of the run, not of a code, and not a `.retryable(…)` call, so it is outside the scan below.
- **The guard that keeps it honest** (unit test `retryable_overrides_are_on_conditional_codes`): scan the production code of `src/` (`source_scan::production_code`) for every `.retryable(<arg>)` call with an argument; find the code it applies to (the nearest `ErrorCode::<Variant>` on the same line or in the 12 lines before it, inside the same function; a call where none is found fails with its location, so the scan never passes by not looking); fail unless `<arg>` is the literal of that code's registered default or the code is conditional. The message names the site and says "an instance of `<code>` changes its retryability: make the code conditional in `ErrorCode::retryability`, and say when in its meaning". Calls with no argument (`Exit::retryable()`) are not error constructions and are skipped.
- **Meanings say when.** A9's `conditional_retryability_is_stated` test is generalized to every code whose `retryability()` is `Conditional`. If A9's meanings of `network` and `io` do not yet say when an instance is retryable, rewrite them under A9's style rules (one sentence, at most 200 characters, naming no command), as A5's bead words them: `network`: "A connection failed or a response could not be read; an instance is retryable unless it followed too many redirects or met an encoding omaddons does not decode." `io`: "A filesystem operation failed; an instance is retryable only when `WTF/` changed while a backup copied it."

| `failure_modes` | `{count, subsystems, command}`: `count` = `FAILURE_MODES.len()`; decided while writing this bead: `subsystems` = the distinct subsystems of the registered rows, in `Subsystem::ALL` order (a summary of what is registered; listing every applicable subsystem before the F leaves fill them would claim coverage that does not exist); `command` per section 9 |
| `schemas_uri`, `robot_docs_uri` | section 9 |
| `config_error` | `null`, or `{path, line, column, message}` from `ConfigProblem` (`path` `null` when HOME gives none; `line` and `column` `null` for a file that could not be read) |

Types: `CapabilitiesData` and every part derive `Debug, Serialize, JsonSchema`; fields are in the order above; lists are `Vec`; nothing is a map, so no `BTreeMap` is needed. `group`, `dictionary`, `network`, `install_kind`, `source`, `action` and `families[].name` use their enums (`Group`, `Dictionary`, `Network`, `InstallKind`, `ValueSource`, `Action`, `Family`), so their schemas are closed. `details_schema` is a `SchemaDoc` (a JSON Schema document, structurally open) and gets an `OPAQUE` row (section 12).

The envelope: `warnings` carries the config's `config_unknown_key` warnings when the config loaded; `commands` is empty (decided while writing this bead: no action exists for "read the guide", and the data already points at it); `meta.offline` reflects the flag and variable as for every command.

- `every_command_entry_carries_its_registry_facts`, `json_is_always_true`.
- `pointers_are_null_exactly_when_their_command_is_missing`: each pointer is `Some` iff its path is a row; a `Some` pointer's argv (`shell_words::split`) parses.
- `limit_values_publish_bare_values`, table: one limit per unit → integer, string, array, retention object.
- `error_codes_publish_meaning_spec_and_tri_state`, `failure_modes_summarize_the_registry` (count, distinct subsystems in `Subsystem::ALL` order, each applicable).
- `config_error_is_reported_with_builtin_values`, table: a parse problem, an unreadable file, no HOME.
- `human_form_fits`, table: the built-in registry; with a config error; a synthetic registry of 70 commands, every late key and an eleven-code doctor dictionary → ≤ 40 lines, each < 80 columns, first and last lines as specified. Message: the case and the rendered text.
- `human_form_names_every_general_exit_and_source`.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

**Contract suite** (subtask 3), each new test function logging its phases with `TestLog` (`log.step` per row, `log.json("envelope", …)` of each checked envelope):

- `tests/contract/matrix.rs::capabilities`: on a fresh `Scene`: `capabilities` → 0, `support::check` (schema-validated), snapshot `capabilities_ok_digest`; `capabilities --bogus` → 2, `usage`, snapshot `capabilities_usage`; `capabilities --if-match pc1:<64 zeros>` → 2, `usage`, `fix_argv ["omaddons", "capabilities"]`.
- `tests/contract/special.rs`: the read-only invocation (identical envelope with `--dry-run --reason x`, `<state>` unchanged); `HOME` unset → 0 with `config_error.path` null; byte-identical repeats.
- `tests/omarchy_widget.rs` passes with the new `CLI_PATHS` row; `tests/cli_skeleton.rs` and the two bare-help snapshots; `tests/contract/usage_fixes.rs`'s typo sweep covers `capabilities` with no edit.

**`tests/capabilities.rs`** (subtask 4), every scenario a `TestLog` scenario (`let log = tlog!();`), with the checks shared through `tests/common/capabilities.rs` (`fetch(&log, &runner) -> Value`, `round_trip(&Value) -> Vec<String>`, `completeness(&Value) -> Vec<String>`, `digest(&Value) -> Value`) so T2 reuses them:

1. `capabilities_round_trips`: on `common::home::Home::new(&["wow", "wow_classic"])`: step "fetch" `capabilities --json` (`Ran::ok`); step "help per command": for each path, the library parse with samples and `--help`, and the binary `omaddons <path> --help --json` → 0, `command: "help"`; step "flags": each flag with a sample (and its requirements), each possible value, each declared conflict pair refused (`ArgumentConflict`), each declared requirement enforced (`MissingRequiredArgument`); step "aliases": each command alias's parse has the same `canonical_path`, each flag alias's `Cli` debug form equals its long form's; step "pointers": each non-null pointer parses and runs to exit 0 with `--json`. A failure lists every broken item at once (command, flag, argv, clap's message), via `log.json("failures", …)`.
2. `capabilities_lists_every_registered_name_exactly_once`: step "fetch", then one step per registry comparing the published list with the library's (names, order, per-entry facts, meanings, `details_schema`, tri-state, `binds`, `exit_codes`), each comparison logged with `log.assert_eq`.
3. `capabilities_reads_only_config_and_writes_nothing`: a home with clients, a `status` run first (so `<state>` and `<cache>` exist), a `config.toml` with overrides and a stored token file; step "hash": `log.tree` of `<state>`, `<cache>`, `<config>` and each client dir; step "run": `capabilities --json`, then `capabilities` (human); step "unchanged": `log.assert_unchanged` for every tree and `Ran`'s `net_log.added` empty for both runs. A second case on a fresh `TestEnv` with no `<state>/omaddons`: after the run, neither `<state>/omaddons` nor `<cache>/omaddons` exists.
4. `a_broken_config_still_answers`, one step per case: malformed TOML, out of range, bad `git_hosts`, unreadable (skipped as root, with the reason in `log.note`), a directory, invalid UTF-8, `HOME=relative/home` → exit 0, `config_error` exactly, every `source` `builtin`, `limits` equal to the registry; an unknown key → no `config_error`, the warning, the other overrides applied.
5. `effective_values_carry_their_source`: one config with every override of the unit table → each value and `source`, everything else `builtin`; then `check_interval_hours = 0` → builtin.
6. `credentials_are_detected_but_never_read_or_run`, one step per case: none; `OMADDONS_GITHUB_TOKEN=<planted>` (registered with `log.secret`; the value appears in neither stream); a stored file of mode 000 (true, no warning); `[sources.github] credential = { command = [<a script writing a marker>] }` (true, no marker afterwards); `{ env = "OMADDONS_A4_UNSET" }` (false); `{ file = "<missing>" }` (false).
7. `the_human_form_is_a_summary`: `capabilities` → 0; ≤ 40 lines, each < 80 columns; first and last lines; every general exit name and source id; stderr empty; then with a broken config → the `config.toml` line; then with `NO_COLOR` unset and `TERM` unset, no escape byte.
8. `flags_that_do_not_apply_change_nothing`: `-t nosuch`, `--offline`, `--dry-run`, `--actor agent --reason x` → each 0 with `data` equal to the plain run's; `--if-match pc1:<64 zeros>` → 2 `usage`.

### Logging

- Unit tests are table-driven with a name per case; every assertion message names the case and shows the input (the argv, the config text, the planted source) and the output (the parsed facts, the problem, the violations).
- Every integration scenario uses T1's `TestLog`: `log.step` per phase, `log.run` for every binary run (argv, environment overrides with secrets redacted, exit, the parsed envelope, stderr events, `net.log` lines added), `log.tree`/`log.assert_unchanged` for every tree the purity case hashes, `log.json` for the fetched data's digest (never the whole 300 KB data in the transcript: `digest()` keeps it readable), `log.assert_eq` for each registry comparison. A failing assertion names the step and the transcript path; the drop guard prints `test log: <path>` and the last 20 steps. `argc e2e capabilities` runs the suite with verbose logs.

### Checkpoint-only tests

- `tests/perf.rs::capabilities_answers_in_under_20_ms` (`#[ignore = "a release-build budget: cargo test --release --test perf -- --ignored"]`): a `Home` with two clients and a `config.toml` of overrides; one warm-up run; `median_of_21` of `home.run(&["capabilities"])` (JSON, process spawn included); `measured` prints the median, p95 and stdout size; asserts the median < 20 ms. Run at the checkpoint with `cargo test --release --test perf capabilities_answers_in_under_20_ms -- --ignored --test-threads=1`. No `SKIP` applies: a budget either passes or the criterion is unmet.

## Considerations

- **Size M, four subtasks, one closure** (above). Not a design-gate leaf: it adds no journal, recovery, binding, deletion or durability rule, so common rule 14 does not apply. Common rule 16 does not apply: `capabilities` is not a mutating path (M4-D22 lists only mutating commands).
- **Risks** (no risk of the plan's table is owned by this bead; its own):
  - *A fact drifts from behaviour:* every list is read from its registry; the round trip proves each flag, value, alias, conflict and requirement against clap, and the completeness test against the library; `REQUIRES`, `APP_VALIDATED` and the retryability set each have a test against the code.
  - *Capabilities becomes slow or large:* about 45 commands × about 20 flags (globals repeated per command, as the plan requires) make roughly 300 KB of JSON; the release budget (20 ms with process spawn) is measured at the checkpoint and the size recorded in the close comment; agents select with `jq`. If the budget fails, profile the clap build (`Cli::command()` + `.build()` once per run) before touching the shape.
  - *A later leaf forgets capabilities:* nothing to forget for commands, codes, actions, env vars, limits and failure modes (generated); the snapshot digest shows each new path; the four late keys are named in D1's, B1's and E3's beads and in section 9.
  - *Purity regresses* (someone calls `World::load` or `GithubToken::resolve`): the purity scenario hashes every tree and the credential scenario uses an unreadable token file that a read would trip.
  - *A3's rule test or strict validation rejects the shape:* the exceptions of section 12 are reasoned and audited by H1; a real mismatch is a bug fixed here.
- **Hot spots (§10.5 rules):** `src/app/mod.rs` (A1 first, then each command leaf adds its own row and rebases: add the row and arms only); `src/cli.rs` (one variant; keep each hook in its own function); `src/error.rs` (A9 then A3 own the code rows: add `Retryability` and its test beside `default_retryable`, edit at most the two meanings, rebase on whoever is in flight); `tests/contract/matrix.rs` and its snapshots (append one function, one snapshot file per row); `omarchy/Model.js` (one `CLI_PATHS` row); `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` (regenerate after rebasing, never merge by hand); `README.md` (only the sections named); `src/contract/mod.rs` (one line per module plus `Registry`). Coordinate through `SendMessage` and `ListAgents`; treat unrecognized working-tree changes as a peer's work.
- **A10 and `CommandInfo`.** A10 (the manifest) reads `CommandInfo` but is not blocked by this bead. If A10 starts first, whichever of A10 and subtask 1 lands first creates `src/contract/commands.rs` exactly as section 1 specifies, and the other builds on it.
- **Compatibility:** nothing persisted changes; older builds have no `capabilities` (a usage error). The refactors (`config.rs`, `parse_since`, `Actor`, `--last-by`) keep every byte of existing output.
- **Privacy:** no output names an account, realm or character; no token or credential value is ever printed (tested); `config_error.path` is the user's own config path, like every other config error.
- **Performance:** one clap build, one config read, at most two metadata calls, one serialization.
- **`-t` and other globals** are accepted and ignored; `OMADDONS_ACTOR` with a bad value still fails with `usage`, as for every command including `help`, because `Context::new` validates it before dispatch (not changed here).

Decided while writing this bead (confirm or adjust each in the close comment):

1. `Registry::builtin()` (no I/O) and `Registry::build()` (config) are separate; the golden, the guide and `robot-docs` read `builtin()`.
2. `build_id` and `guide_digest` are published by whichever of this bead and their producer (D1, B1) lands second, absent until then; `exit_codes.doctor` and `error_codes[].doctor_exit` are always present, `[]` and `null` until E3's dictionary exists, as A5 does for `robot-docs errors`.
3. The pointers are computed from `COMMANDS` and are `null` when the command they name is missing.
4. `failure_modes.subsystems` lists the registered rows' distinct subsystems in `Subsystem::ALL` order.
5. `retryable` is conditional for `network`, `http_status`, `hash_mismatch`, `plan_stale` and `io`, declared once as `ErrorCode::retryability()` in the form A5's bead also specifies (whichever lands first adds it), held by a source scan; `recovery_failed` is a run-level assignment outside it.
6. `requires` comes from a declared `REQUIRES` table probed against clap.
7. `conflicts_with` is the symmetric closure of clap's declared conflicts.
8. `default` is published for value-taking arguments only.
9. Globals are listed per command after the own flags; `--if-match` only where it binds; hidden arguments and values and the root-only `-V` are left out.
10. `args[].name` is clap's argument id.
11. Value sets live in `src/contract/values.rs`; `ACTORS` beside `Actor`, `SINCE` beside `parse_since`; `--last-by` keeps clap's validation built from the same list; `--since` publishes `possible_values: null`.
12. `limits[].value` is a bare value by unit; `config_key` is the `config.toml` key from `LIMIT_CONFIG_KEYS`, `TX_RETENTION` publishing its first.
13. `source` is `config` when `config.toml` sets a key that applies to the value; `sources` and `families` gain `source` (M4-D4).
14. CurseForge and Wago are never `enabled`; git's hosts are its built-in hosts followed by the configured ones.
15. `credential_configured` means present, found without reading or running anything, at the cost of at most two metadata calls.
16. A broken config or an unusable `HOME` gives exit 0, built-in values and `config_error` with nullable `path`, `line` and `column`.
17. Config warnings pass through as envelope warnings; `commands[]` is empty.
18. `-t` and the other globals are ignored; `capabilities` is client-free in C1's vocabulary.
19. The human form's layout and wording (section 10).
20. The success contract snapshot is a digest of the data.
21. The rule test's `EXCEPTIONS` rows and the `OPAQUE` row of section 12; `details_schema` typed as A5's `SchemaDoc`.
22. No size bound is added on `config.toml`.
23. The round-trip and completeness checks live in `tests/common/capabilities.rs` for T2 to reuse.
24. The row and variant sit after `omarchy` and before `help`.
25. `families` includes `unknown`; `client_rules` ends with both fallback rows.

## Dependencies

Parent: the area epic omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1 (the contract registry and the discovery surfaces).

**Blocked by:**

- A1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1`, per-command facts in `COMMANDS`, and canonical names): the five facts on every row (`dictionary`, `exits`, `data`, `stores_plan`, `network`), `Dictionary` and `Network` with their wire names, `canonical_path` for the aliases' round trip, the `auth github` path, and the `entry` constructor the new row uses.
- A2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.2`, registries for actions, events, env vars, features and per-source facts): `Action::ALL`, `contract::env::release()`, `FEATURES`, `SourceId::requires_credential`, `hosts_for` and `target_id_forms()`, and `src/contract/mod.rs` itself.
- A3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`, schemas with the serialize contract, declared `details`, and live validation): the strict validation of capabilities' data in every contract run, `contract::OPAQUE` and the rule test's `EXCEPTIONS`, and the schema each `data_schema` pointer names.
- A9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9`, a meaning and a typed `DetailSpec` for every code): `meaning()` on every error and warning code and `details_schema()` on every error code.
- E1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`, the failure-mode registry, the finding model and the repair action model): `FAILURE_MODES`, `Subsystem::ALL` and `applicable()` for the `failure_modes` summary.

Subtasks 3 and 4 are also blocked by T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs and the `argc e2e` runner), because their tests use `TestLog` (an edge added at filing).

**Unblocks:**

- A6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.6`, bare help's discovery line and `help --json` `discovery`): the line names `omaddons capabilities --json`, which must exist.
- H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, the pre-freeze contract audit): the capabilities shape is part of the contract it audits, including the pointers' nullability and the rule-test exceptions recorded here.
- T2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.2`, the slice-1 end-to-end suite; edge added at filing): the slice-1 demo's "`capabilities --json` round-trips", run through this bead's `tests/common/capabilities.rs`.

**Slice:** `slice-1`, "Self-describing". Exit demo (run by T2 as a test): `capabilities --json` round-trips; `robot-docs schema` validates the whole matrix and every envelope snapshot, `details` included; the manifest's report prints; `robot-docs guide` equals `SKILL.md`, frontmatter first; `install-skill` into a throwaway `HOME`; `omaddons retail update` suggests `update -t retail`, `remove dbm retail` changes nothing, and the corpus runs; `completions bash` passes `bash -n`. It pre-checks criteria 1, 2, 3 (part), 5 and 15. This bead records no demo itself.

**Related, not edges:** D1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1`), B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`) and E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`) publish `build_id`, `guide_digest` and the doctor dictionary if they land after this bead; A5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5`), B1 and E4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4`) switch the pointers on by adding their rows; A10 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.10`) reads `CommandInfo`; C1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.1`) owns `CLIENT_FREE` and C4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4`) the corpus.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `omaddons capabilities --json` exits 0 with `data` keys in this order: `version`, `contract_version`, (`build_id` once D1 has landed), (`guide_digest` once B1 has landed), `features`, `commands`, `exit_codes`, `env_vars`, `limits`, `sources`, `families`, `client_rules`, `target_id_forms`, `error_codes`, `warning_codes`, `actions`, `failure_modes`, `schemas_uri`, `robot_docs_uri`, `config_error`; the six required keys are present; `build_id` and `guide_digest` are present exactly when D1 and B1 have landed; `exit_codes.doctor` and `error_codes[].doctor_exit` carry E3's dictionary when E3 has landed, else `[]` and `null` (with the comment on E3); the close comment says which this bead published.
- [ ] Round trip: for every `commands[]` entry, `omaddons <path> --help` parses (with sample values for required positionals) and the binary answers it with a help envelope; every flag parses with a sample value (and its declared requirements); every listed possible value parses; every declared conflict is refused by clap and every declared requirement is enforced; every command alias resolves to the same canonical path, and every flag alias parses as its flag; every non-null pointer parses.
- [ ] Completeness: `commands[].path` equals `app::COMMANDS`' names in order; `error_codes` equals `ErrorCode::ALL`, `warning_codes` `WarningCode::ALL`, `actions` `Action::ALL`, `env_vars` the `release` rows of `ENV_VARS`, `exit_codes.general` `Exit::ALL`, `limits` the politeness and limits registries, `sources` `SourceId::ALL`, `families` `Family::ALL`, `client_rules` the effective table's rows plus both fallbacks, `target_id_forms` `contract::target_id_forms()`, `features` `FEATURES`, each exactly once; every per-entry fact equals its registry's; `failure_modes.count` equals `FAILURE_MODES.len()`.
- [ ] `failure_modes.command` is `"omaddons doctor capabilities --json"` exactly when `doctor capabilities` is a `COMMANDS` path (else `null`), and likewise `schemas_uri`, `robot_docs_uri` and `commands[].data_schema` for `robot-docs schema` and `robot-docs guide`.
- [ ] Purity: one `capabilities --json` run and one human run on a synthetic home leave the tree hashes of `<state>`, `<cache>`, `<config>` and every client dir unchanged, add no `net.log` line, and create no `<state>/omaddons` or `<cache>/omaddons` directory on a home that had none.
- [ ] A broken `config.toml` (malformed TOML, a value out of range, an unreadable file, a directory in its place, invalid UTF-8) and an unusable `HOME` each give exit 0 with built-in values (`source: "builtin"` everywhere) and `config_error {path, line, column, message}` (line and column for a parse problem, `null` for an unreadable file, `path` `null` without HOME); a config with an unknown key gives no `config_error` and a `config_unknown_key` warning.
- [ ] Effective values: every value `config.toml` overrides (a limit, `check_interval_hours`, the two retention keys, a disabled source, `git_hosts`, a family range, a client-rules patch and a new row) is reported with its effective value and `source: "config"`, everything else `builtin`; `check_interval_hours = 0` stays `builtin`; CurseForge and Wago stay `enabled: false` whatever the config says.
- [ ] `credential_configured` is true for an `OMADDONS_GITHUB_TOKEN`, a configured reference or a stored token file, without reading a secret or running a command: a stored file of mode 000 still counts, no `credential_file_mode` warning appears, a `command` reference's marker file is never created, and no token value appears on stdout or stderr.
- [ ] `--if-match` appears in `commands[].flags` exactly on the paths whose `binds` is true; every other propagated global flag appears on every command with `global: true`, after the command's own flags.
- [ ] `error_codes[].retryable` is `"conditional"` exactly for the five codes `ErrorCode::retryability()` marks conditional (`network`, `http_status`, `hash_mismatch`, `plan_stale`, `io`) and the registry's boolean otherwise, declared once for both `capabilities` and `robot-docs errors`; the source scan holds every production `.retryable(<arg>)` override to that set, and every conditional code's meaning says when an instance is retryable.
- [ ] The human form is at most 40 lines, each under 80 columns, starts with `omaddons <version> · contract 1.0`, names every general exit code and every source, shows a `config.toml` line only with a `config_error`, and ends with `--json for the full description`; stderr is empty.
- [ ] `capabilities` takes under 20 ms, median of 21, release build (`tests/perf.rs`, ignored; run at the checkpoint).
- [ ] Every DEC-1 touch point is in subtask 3's commit: the clap variant, the `COMMANDS` row with every M4 field, the `canonical_path` and dispatch arms, the help-layout test and both bare-help snapshots, the contract rows (`capabilities_ok_digest`, `capabilities_usage`) and the `--if-match` assertion, the read-only invocation in `special.rs`, the `cli_skeleton` literal, the `CLI_PATHS` row, README's `### capabilities` section; plus `CLIENT_FREE`, the `OPAQUE` row, the rule-test `EXCEPTIONS`, and (when their leaves have landed) the corpus row and the regenerated `SKILL.md`.
- [ ] `support::check` (A3's strict validation) passes on every capabilities envelope the suite produces, and A3's rule test passes with no new allowlist line.
- [ ] Every behaviour change outside the new command is byte-neutral: the existing `config.rs` error messages and `details`, `parse_since`, `Actor` parsing and `undo --last-by` behave as before (their tests pass unchanged), and no snapshot other than the bare-help pair, the two new contract snapshots and those of later producers changes.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes for every subtask's commit, `ubs` is clean on the changed files, and README's `### capabilities` section, "What works today" row and Tests row land with the code they describe.
- [ ] The close comment lists every new or changed wire name (the `capabilities` path and every data key and value set, `ValueSource`'s values, the `Retryability` tri-state, the changed meanings of `network` and `io` if any), every "Decided while writing this bead" item confirmed or adjusted, and the measured human-form line count and JSON size.
- [ ] `br lint` is clean for this bead and its subtasks.
