comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M4 plan, 2026-10-24).**

**Why this bead.** At `c0ab5e9` an agent cannot learn omaddons from omaddons: `help --json` gives command names and four facts per flag, and everything else (allowed values, defaults, conflicts, per-command exits, the error catalog with retryability and `details` shapes, limits, sources, families, client rules, `-t` forms) lives in a 2,800-line README or in the code. M4's first goal (G-M4-1) is that an agent learns everything it needs in at most three calls, and `omaddons capabilities --json` is the first of them: one offline call, a few milliseconds, generated from the live clap tree and the binary's registries, so it cannot drift from what the code does. It is also the contract a later MCP adapter or Claude Code mod would read. This bead builds the per-command facts every description of the CLI shares (`CommandInfo`, which A10's manifest also reads), the effective configuration values with their source, the tolerant config load, the per-code retryability, and the command itself, and proves checkpoint criterion 1 end to end.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M4-D4:** offline, scan-free, write-free; effective values with `source: builtin | config`; a broken config answers with built-in values and `config_error`; a human summary of at most 40 lines; under 20 ms.
- **M4-D2:** one registry (`contract::Registry`) joins the clap tree and every registry; facts clap cannot give (app-validated value sets, `requires`, retryability) are declared once and cross-checked by tests.
- **M4-D3:** `contract_version` is `schema_version`.
- **M4-D5:** each command's declared exits, dictionary, plan storage and network use are published as A1 declared them.
- **M4-D6:** only `release` environment variables are published.
- **M4-D10 / A.1:** each code's `details_schema` and the tri-state `retryable`.
- **M4-D11, M4-D29:** the `Action` registry; the failure-mode summary with a pointer to `doctor capabilities`.
- **M4-D19:** `binds` derived from `BINDING_COMMANDS`.
- **M4-D55, M4-D56, M4-D18, DEC-3, DEC-1, M4-D7:** the shape passes A3's rule test with reasoned exceptions only; key order deterministic but not contract; no volatile key; every touch point in one commit; `SKILL.md` regenerated once B1 has landed.

**Alternatives rejected that matter here.**
- A hand-written `capabilities.json` (M4-D2): it drifts, the failure capabilities exists to prevent.
- Including the discovered clients (M4-D4): that is `status`, and it costs a scan.
- Failing on a broken config (M4-D4): it hides the description when an agent needs it most.
- Publishing debug environment variables (M4-D6): release builds ignore them.
- A boolean `retryable` per code (A.1): it would lie for the codes whose instances decide.
- A placeholder `build_id` or `guide_digest` before D1 or B1 lands, and pointers to commands the build lacks (decided while writing the bead): each would publish a fact the build does not have. The doctor dictionary is the one exception, published as `[]` and `null` until E3 lands, because `robot-docs errors` (A5) publishes the same `doctor_exit` that way and an agent reading both must see one type.
- Snapshotting the whole 300 KB data in the contract matrix (decided): every later leaf would re-accept it and parallel leaves would collide; a digest shows each new path in one line, and the full data is validated live.
- Resolving the GitHub token to say whether one is configured (decided): it reads a secret; presence is found by environment and metadata only.

**Facts verified during planning, and corrections.** As of `c0ab5e9`: clap 4.6.7 has no public getter for `requires` (`Arg.requires` is `pub(crate)`, `clap_builder-4.6.7/src/builder/arg.rs:70`), so requirements are declared and probed; conflicts come from `Command::get_arg_conflicts_with` (`command.rs:4036`) and are recorded one-sided, so the published lists are their symmetric closure. `undo --last-by` is already clap-validated (`src/app/undo.rs:42-48`), so its value set is shared with clap rather than replacing it. `LimitInfo.config_key` is the internal override key (`src/limits.rs:235-239`), not the `config.toml` key the capabilities example shows, and `LimitValue` is externally tagged (`src/limits.rs:244-258`) where the example shows a bare number; a `config.toml` key table and a bare-value projection fix both, with `TX_RETENTION`'s two keys published by the first. `network` (`src/net/guard.rs:334-343`, `src/net/decode.rs:61-68`) and `io` (`src/backup/tree.rs:152-165`) instances override their default retryability, so the conditional set is five codes, not the plan's three; `recovery_failed` (`src/engine/tx.rs:572-578`) is a run-level override. `credential_configured` for GitHub depends on the stored token file (`src/sources/github_token.rs:1-12`), so the bead makes at most two metadata calls beyond `config.toml`, never a read. `Paths::from_env` fails with `usage` when `HOME` is unset or relative (`src/state/paths.rs:72-90`), so capabilities turns that into `config_error` too. M4-D4 requires a `source` on every config-changeable value, so `sources[]` and `families[]` gain one. A3's rule test flags four names the plan itself fixes (`conflicts_with`, `exit_codes.general`, `limits[].value`, the kebab-case family values); they get reasoned `EXCEPTIONS` rows for H1 to audit, never allowlist lines.

**Risks and how they are watched.** No risk of the plan's table is owned here. Drift between capabilities and behaviour: every list is read from its registry, the round trip proves each flag, value, alias, conflict and requirement against clap, and completeness compares every list with the library. Purity regressions (a call to `World::load` or `GithubToken::resolve`): the purity scenario hashes every tree and the credential scenario plants an unreadable token file and a command whose marker must never appear. Output size (about 300 KB, globals repeated per command as the plan requires) and the 20 ms budget: measured in `tests/perf.rs` at the checkpoint, the size recorded in the close comment. A later leaf forgetting capabilities: nothing to forget for generated lists, and the late keys (`build_id`, `guide_digest`, the doctor dictionary) follow D1's, B1's and E3's beads' "whichever lands second" rule, with a comment left on E3 when the dictionary is still missing. The per-code tri-state and the `SchemaDoc` wrapper are declared once, in the form A5's bead also specifies, so `capabilities` and `robot-docs errors` cannot disagree.

**What it unblocks and why they wait.** A6's discovery line names `omaddons capabilities --json`, which must exist before bare help may mention it. H1 audits the whole contract, so every shape (this one, with its nullable pointers and rule-test exceptions) must exist first. T2 runs the slice-1 demo, whose first item is "`capabilities --json` round-trips", through this bead's shared checks.

**How it serves the milestone.** G-M4-1 (the first of the three calls, every fact generated from code), G-M4-2 in part (every alias and allowed value listed before an agent guesses), G-M4-5 in part (`CommandInfo` is the CLI-input half of the semantic manifest), and checkpoint criteria 1 (owned), 14 and 17 in part. It serves the vision's G4, "the first command an agent guesses works", and the thesis that omaddons stays the sole, safe, undoable authority over what it manages: an agent can trust what the tool says about itself because tests hold it equal to what the tool does.

**Confidence.** High. The command is a projection of registries that exist or that the blockers add, and clap's tree is already walked at run time by help; the two facts clap hides are declared and probed. The work that needs care is the tolerant config refactor (held byte-identical by tests) and the retryability scan, both specified case by case.

title: `CommandInfo` from the live clap tree, value sets for the app-validated flags, and declared requirements
description:
Part 1 of 4 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4 (`omaddons capabilities`). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

A4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`) adds `omaddons capabilities [--json]`, the machine-readable description of this build that an agent calls first: every command with every flag (its allowed values, default, conflicts and requirements), every alias, each command's exit codes and facts, the error, warning and action registries, limits, sources, families, client-rules rows and `-t` forms, generated from the live clap tree and the binary's registries, never kept by hand (M4-D2: one contract registry feeds every description of the CLI; a fact clap cannot provide is declared exactly once, beside what it describes, and a test cross-checks it against behaviour; M4-D4: capabilities is offline, scan-free and write-free).

**This part builds the per-command facts:** `CommandInfo`, extracted from `Cli::command()` after `.build()` and joined with each `app::COMMANDS` row, plus the two facts clap cannot give: the allowed values of the flags validated in app code (`--actor`, `history --by`, `undo --last-by`, the `--since` grammar), declared once beside their parsers, and the requirements between flags (`#[arg(requires = …)]`), which clap records privately. It is its own step because it is pure extraction with no output change, it is what A10's semantic manifest (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.10`) also reads, and it can land in parallel with subtask 2 (the effective configuration values), which touches different files.

**Facts this part relies on** (verified at `c0ab5e9`):
- `Cli` (`src/cli.rs:25-41`), `GlobalArgs` (`src/cli.rs:44-119`: every flag `global = true` except `-V/--version`; `-t` has `visible_alias = "flavor"`), the `Command` enum (`src/cli.rs:137-213`). Help already walks the built tree (`src/app/help.rs:199-349`); `.build()` propagates the globals to every subcommand. clap `4.6.7`.
- clap's getters: `Command::get_subcommands`, `get_arguments`, `get_positionals`, `get_visible_aliases`, `get_about`; `Arg::get_id`, `get_long`, `get_short`, `get_visible_aliases`, `get_value_names`, `get_num_args`, `get_action`, `get_possible_values` (`clap_builder-4.6.7/src/builder/arg.rs:4320`, empty for an argument that takes no value; each `PossibleValue` has `is_hide_set`), `get_default_values` (`:4414`; after `.build()` a `SetTrue` flag records `"false"` and a `Count` flag `"0"`, `Arg::_build`, `:4578-4608`), `is_required_set`, `is_global_set`, `is_hide_set`, `get_help`. Conflicts: `Command::get_arg_conflicts_with(&arg)` (`command.rs:4036`), which unrolls groups and panics on a conflict naming an unknown argument. **`requires` has no public getter**: `Arg.requires` is `pub(crate)` (`arg.rs:70`).
- Conflicts declared at `c0ab5e9`: `install --any-flavor` ↔ `no_any_flavor` (`src/app/install.rs:86`); `status --deep` ↔ `cached` (`src/app/status.rs:75`); `backup create --auto` ↔ `verify` (`src/app/backup.rs:214`); `backup prune --keep`, `--older-than` ↔ positional `ids` (`src/app/backup.rs:250`, `:254`); `undo --last-by` ↔ `tx`, `undo --run` ↔ `tx`, `last_by` (`src/app/undo.rs:42-50`). `omarchy install --section` has `default_value_t = Section::Right` (`src/app/omarchy.rs:40`). No argument is hidden and no production argument uses `requires` (E6 adds `doctor fix --force` requiring `--yes`).
- `Actor` (`src/model.rs:315-375`): `as_str()` (`human`, `agent`, `widget`), `resolve` (`:334-356`), `FromStr` ignoring ASCII case over a literal array (`:359-369`). `--actor` (global) and `history --by` (`src/app/history.rs:43`) are parsed with it (`src/app/history.rs:253-276`). **Corrected:** `undo --last-by` is already validated by clap, `value_parser = ["human", "agent", "widget"]` (`src/app/undo.rs:42-48`), and parsed again in `undo::run` (`:336-349`).
- `parse_since` (`src/app/history.rs:428-445`): an RFC 3339 time, or a whole number with `m` (60 s), `h` (3,600), `d` (86,400) or `w` (604,800); used by `history --since` (`:37`, parsed at `:290-305`), `net-log --since` (`src/app/net_log.rs:32`, `:154`) and `errors --since` (`src/app/errors.rs:62`, `:829`). Its test is `since_takes_durations_and_rfc3339` (`src/app/history.rs:534`).
- After A1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1`): `app::COMMANDS` rows `CommandEntry {name, group, mutates, dictionary, exits, data, stores_plan, network}`, `Dictionary`, `Network`, `app::command_entry(path)`, `app::canonical_path`. `precondition::BINDING_COMMANDS` (`src/app/precondition.rs:25-31`) is the list `binds` is derived from (M4-D19: `binds` is not a `CommandEntry` field). `src/contract/mod.rs` exists (A2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.2`).
- `cli::check_if_match` (`src/cli.rs:309-339`) refuses `--if-match` with `usage` on every path not in `BINDING_COMMANDS`.

## Technical Approach

1. **`src/contract/values.rs`** (new, declared `pub mod values;` in `src/contract/mod.rs`; no dependency on the rest of the crate, so low-level modules can use it):

   ```rust
   //! The values an app-validated flag accepts, declared once beside its parser (M4-D2):
   //! the parser reads the set, and so do capabilities and the semantic manifest.

   #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
   pub enum ValueSet {
       /// Exactly these words.
       Words(&'static [&'static str]),
       /// A whole number followed by one of these units (`30m`), or an RFC 3339 time.
       DurationOrTime(&'static [DurationUnit]),
   }

   #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
   pub struct DurationUnit { pub suffix: &'static str, pub seconds: i64 }
   ```

2. **Actors** (`src/model.rs`, beside `Actor`):

   ```rust
   impl Actor {
       pub const ALL: [Self; 3] = [Self::Human, Self::Agent, Self::Widget];
       /// The wire names, in `ALL` order: the one list `--actor`, `history --by` and
       /// `undo --last-by` accept.
       pub const WORDS: [&'static str; 3] = [Self::Human.as_str(), Self::Agent.as_str(), Self::Widget.as_str()];
   }
   /// The value set of the actor flags.
   pub const ACTORS: ValueSet = ValueSet::Words(&Actor::WORDS);
   ```

   `FromStr` iterates `Self::ALL` (same behaviour: ASCII case ignored; `Err(())` otherwise).

3. **`--last-by`** (`src/app/undo.rs`): replace `value_parser = ["human", "agent", "widget"]` by a parser built from `Actor::WORDS` (`clap::builder::PossibleValuesParser::new(Actor::WORDS)`; adapt the expression to what the derive accepts). Same values, same order: help, the usage fixes (clap's `InvalidValue` corrected in place) and `undo::run` are unchanged.

4. **`--since`** (`src/app/history.rs`, beside `parse_since`):

   ```rust
   /// The `--since` grammar of `history`, `net-log` and `errors`.
   pub const SINCE: ValueSet = ValueSet::DurationOrTime(&[
       DurationUnit { suffix: "m", seconds: 60 },
       DurationUnit { suffix: "h", seconds: 3_600 },
       DurationUnit { suffix: "d", seconds: 86_400 },
       DurationUnit { suffix: "w", seconds: 604_800 },
   ]);
   ```

   `parse_since` finds the unit by looking the suffix up in `SINCE` instead of its `match` (same results for every input; the `checked_mul`/`checked_sub` overflow handling stays).

5. **`src/contract/commands.rs`** (new, `pub mod commands;`): the types and functions of the leaf's section 1, verbatim:

   ```rust
   pub struct CommandInfo { pub path: &'static str, pub about: String, pub group: Group, pub mutates: bool,
       pub dictionary: Dictionary, pub exits: &'static [u8], pub args: Vec<ArgInfo>, pub flags: Vec<FlagInfo>,
       pub aliases: Vec<String>, pub stores_plan: bool, pub binds: bool, pub network: Network }
   pub struct ArgInfo { pub id: String, pub value_name: String, pub required: bool, pub multiple: bool,
       pub default: Option<String>, pub values: Values, pub help: String,
       pub conflicts_with: Vec<String>, pub requires: Vec<String> }
   pub struct FlagInfo { pub long: String, pub short: Option<char>, pub aliases: Vec<String>,
       pub value_name: Option<String>, pub takes_value: bool, pub multiple: bool, pub default: Option<String>,
       pub values: Values, pub conflicts_with: Vec<String>, pub requires: Vec<String>, pub global: bool, pub help: String }
   pub enum Values { Any, Words(Vec<&'static str>), DurationOrTime(&'static [DurationUnit]) }
   pub fn commands() -> Vec<CommandInfo>;
   pub fn command(path: &str) -> Option<CommandInfo>;
   pub fn command_info(entry: &CommandEntry, cmd: &clap::Command) -> CommandInfo;
   ```

   All derive `Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq`; none is serialized (A4's subtask 3 projects them into wire types; A10 into manifest nodes). If clap's `PossibleValue` names are not `'static` through the getter, `Words` holds `String`s (decided while writing this bead; either is fine, the tests compare values).

   The rules, each a unit-tested case:
   - **Joining:** walk `get_subcommands()` word by word along the row's path in the tree built once (`let mut root = Cli::command(); root.build();`). A row that does not resolve is left out (no panic); a unit test fails on it.
   - **Flags** (a long or short name) in declaration order: the command's own first, then the propagated globals in `GlobalArgs` order with `global: true`. **Args** are the positionals by `get_index()`.
   - **Left out:** hidden arguments and hidden possible values; `--if-match` on a path whose `binds` is false (decided while writing this bead: `check_if_match` refuses it there, so it is not accepted input; D2, D3, E6 and E8 extend `BINDING_COMMANDS` and so the listing with no edit here). The root-only `-V/--version` is not a subcommand argument.
   - **`value_name`:** the first of `get_value_names()`, else the id upper-cased for a positional or a value-taking flag; `None` for a flag that takes no value.
   - **`takes_value`:** `get_action().takes_values()`. **`multiple`:** `Append` or `Count`, or the arity's maximum above 1. **`required`:** `is_required_set()`.
   - **`default`** (decided while writing this bead): `get_default_values()`' one value for a value-taking argument; `None` for a flag that takes no value (clap's implicit `"false"`/`"0"`).
   - **`values`:** the `APP_VALIDATED` row's set when there is one (step 6); else `Words` of clap's visible possible values when there are any; else `Any`.
   - **`conflicts_with`** (decided while writing this bead): the symmetric closure of `cmd.get_arg_conflicts_with(arg)` over the command's arguments, deduplicated, in the command's argument order, each named by its long name (flags) or id (positionals). So `any-flavor` lists `no-any-flavor` and `no-any-flavor` lists `any-flavor`.
   - **`requires`:** from `REQUIRES` (step 7).
   - **`aliases`:** the command's `get_visible_aliases()`; a flag's `get_visible_aliases()` (long, without dashes).
   - **`about`, `help`:** `to_string()` of `get_about()`/`get_help()`, trimmed; empty when absent.
   - **Row facts:** `group`, `mutates`, `dictionary`, `exits`, `stores_plan`, `network` from the `CommandEntry`; `binds = BINDING_COMMANDS.contains(&path)`.

6. **The app-validated flags** (`src/contract/commands.rs`):

   ```rust
   /// The flags clap does not validate (or validates from the same list), each with the
   /// value set its parser reads (M4-D2).
   pub struct AppValidated { pub path: Option<&'static str>, pub long: &'static str, pub set: &'static ValueSet }
   pub const APP_VALIDATED: &[AppValidated] = &[
       AppValidated { path: None, long: "actor", set: &crate::model::ACTORS },
       AppValidated { path: Some("history"), long: "by", set: &crate::model::ACTORS },
       AppValidated { path: Some("undo"), long: "last-by", set: &crate::model::ACTORS },
       AppValidated { path: Some("history"), long: "since", set: &crate::app::history::SINCE },
       AppValidated { path: Some("net-log"), long: "since", set: &crate::app::history::SINCE },
       AppValidated { path: Some("errors"), long: "since", set: &crate::app::history::SINCE },
   ];
   ```

   `path: None` is a global flag (every command). A `Words` set becomes `Values::Words`; `DurationOrTime` becomes `Values::DurationOrTime` (capabilities publishes `possible_values: null` for it, an open grammar; A10 records the grammar).

7. **Requirements** (`src/contract/commands.rs`):

   ```rust
   /// Flags clap requires another argument with (`#[arg(requires = …)]`), declared here
   /// because clap gives no public getter (M4-D2). Empty at `c0ab5e9`; E6 adds
   /// `doctor fix --force` → `yes`.
   pub struct Requirement { pub path: &'static str, pub long: &'static str, pub requires: &'static [&'static str] }
   pub const REQUIRES: &[Requirement] = &[];

   /// Every way `table` disagrees with `cmd`'s behaviour at `path` (pure).
   pub fn requirement_violations(path: &str, cmd: &clap::Command, table: &[Requirement]) -> Vec<String>;
   ```

   `requirement_violations` probes: for each flag of `cmd`, parse `[bin, <path words>, <a sample for each required positional>, --<long>, <sample if it takes a value>]` with `cmd.clone().try_get_matches_from(…)` (on the root command, so the path words select the subcommand). The sample of a value is its first possible value, else `"1"`. A `MissingRequiredArgument` naming an argument the table does not declare for that flag is a violation: "`<path> --<long>` needs `<arg>` to parse: declare it in contract::commands::REQUIRES"; a declared requirement under which the flag parses alone is a violation: "REQUIRES says `<path> --<long>` requires `<arg>`, but it parses without it"; a table row naming a path or flag that does not exist is a violation. When a row declares a requirement, the probe adds the required flags (with samples) and the parse must then succeed.

8. **Module doc** of `commands.rs`: what `CommandInfo` is, that it is read by capabilities and the manifest, the two declared facts (value sets, requirements) and why each is declared, and the `--if-match` and default rules.

9. **A10's `CommandInfo`.** A10 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.10`, the manifest) reads this type but is not blocked by A4. If A10 has already created `src/contract/commands.rs`, extend it to this specification instead of creating a second one (and coordinate through `SendMessage`); if this part lands first, A10 builds on it.

No output changes in this part: nothing serializes these types yet, and `--last-by`, `parse_since` and `Actor` behave exactly as before.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `src/contract/values.rs` defines `ValueSet` and `DurationUnit`; `src/contract/commands.rs` defines `CommandInfo`, `ArgInfo`, `FlagInfo`, `Values`, `commands()`, `command()`, `command_info()`, `APP_VALIDATED`, `Requirement`, `REQUIRES` and `requirement_violations()`; both are declared in `src/contract/mod.rs`.
- [ ] `commands()` returns one `CommandInfo` per `app::COMMANDS` row, in `COMMANDS` order, with every rule of the Technical Approach (own flags then globals with `global: true`, `--if-match` only where `binds`, hidden arguments and values left out, value names, `multiple`, defaults for value-taking arguments only, symmetric conflicts named by long name or id, aliases, row facts and `binds` from `BINDING_COMMANDS`).
- [ ] `Actor::ALL`, `Actor::WORDS` and `model::ACTORS` exist and `Actor::from_str` iterates `ALL`; `undo --last-by`'s clap parser is built from `Actor::WORDS`; `history::SINCE` exists and `parse_since` reads its units; every existing test of `Actor`, `parse_since`, `undo` and the usage fixes passes unchanged.
- [ ] `APP_VALIDATED` lists `--actor` (global), `history --by`, `undo --last-by` and the three `--since` flags, each flag exists where its row says, and the `Words` sets equal their parsers' lists.
- [ ] `requirement_violations` is empty over every `COMMANDS` path with the (empty) `REQUIRES`, and reports each planted fault on synthetic commands.
- [ ] `Cli::command().debug_assert()` passes in a unit test.
- [ ] No output, snapshot or help text changes (`cargo test` passes with no snapshot re-accepted).
- [ ] `argc gate` passes and `ubs` is clean on the changed files.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

`src/contract/commands.rs`:

- `the_clap_tree_passes_clap_debug_asserts`: `Cli::command().debug_assert()`.
- `every_commands_row_has_command_info`: `commands().len() == COMMANDS.len()`, paths equal and in order; message "row `<path>` resolves to no clap command".
- `command_info_reads_clap_facts`, table-driven, one name per case (`install_refs_and_channel`, `install_any_flavor_conflicts_both_ways`, `install_alias_add`, `status_deep_conflicts_cached`, `backup_create_auto_conflicts_verify`, `backup_prune_keep_and_older_than_conflict_ids`, `undo_tx_conflicts_last_by_and_run`, `undo_last_by_words`, `undo_saved_variables_words`, `omarchy_install_section_default_right`, `history_by_words_and_since_grammar`, `help_command_positional`, `global_target_short_alias_global`, `global_verbose_multiple_no_value_no_default`, `global_format_words`): each asserts the named fields; message "case <name>: <field> expected <x>, got <y>".

- `requirements_are_declared_and_true`: `requirement_violations` over every `COMMANDS` path is empty.
- `requirement_violations_finds_each_fault`, synthetic: a flag with `.requires("yes")` and no row (one violation); a row for a flag that parses alone (one violation); a row naming an unknown flag (one violation); a correct row (none).

`src/model.rs`:

- `actor_words_are_the_parser_list`: `Actor::ALL.map(Actor::as_str) == Actor::WORDS`; `human`, `AGENT`, `Widget` parse; `robot` and `` do not.

`src/app/history.rs`:

- `since_units_drive_the_parser`, table: for each unit, `parse_since("2<suffix>", now) == now - 2 × seconds`; `2y`, `m`, `-1d`, `` → `None`; an RFC 3339 time parses to itself; `since_takes_durations_and_rfc3339` passes unchanged.
- `every_since_help_names_its_units`: for each `--since` flag of `APP_VALIDATED`, its help text contains, per unit of `SINCE`, a token of digits followed by the suffix.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

None in this part: it changes no output. The existing suites (`tests/contract/usage_fixes.rs`'s typo sweep, which covers `undo --last-by`'s value fix, `tests/history.rs`-style tests of `--since`, `tests/cli_skeleton.rs`) must pass unchanged, which proves the refactors byte-neutral.

### Logging

Table-driven unit tests with a name per case; each assertion message names the case and shows the input (the path, the flag, the argv or the synthetic command) and the output (the extracted field, the violations list). `requirement_violations` returns its messages, and the test prints all of them at once rather than stopping at the first.

## Considerations

- **Why the declarations.** M4-D2 requires a fact clap cannot provide to be declared once and cross-checked. clap validates `--actor` and `--by` nowhere (they are free strings validated by `Actor::from_str`, whose errors carry the commands' own fixes), and records `requires` privately; the value sets and `REQUIRES` are those declarations, and the tests are the cross-checks.
- **Not breaking `--last-by`:** the plan lists it among the app-validated flags, but clap already validates it; keeping clap's validation (built from the same list) keeps its usage-fix behaviour, which the typo sweep tests.
- **The panic of `get_arg_conflicts_with`** cannot fire on a tree that passes `debug_assert`, which the gate runs.
- **Performance:** one tree build per `commands()` call; `capabilities` calls it once per run.
- **Hot spots:** `src/model.rs` and `src/app/history.rs` are not on §10.5's list; `src/app/undo.rs` is E7's later (rebase); `src/contract/mod.rs` gets one line per module.
- **Privacy:** nothing here prints.

Decided while writing this bead (confirm or adjust in the close comment): the `--if-match` listing rule; defaults for value-taking arguments only; symmetric conflicts; `requires` from a probed table; `--last-by` keeps clap's validation from `Actor::WORDS`; `--since` is a `DurationOrTime` set whose capabilities form is `possible_values: null`; `Words` holds `&'static str` or `String` as clap allows; hidden arguments and values left out; a visible short alias or several defaults fail a test until a leaf decides how to publish them.

- Parent: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4 (`omaddons capabilities`), under the area epic omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.
- Before it: none among the siblings; the leaf's blockers (A1 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1` for the `COMMANDS` facts and `canonical_path`, A2 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.2` for `src/contract/mod.rs`) have landed by the time this bead is ready. It runs in parallel with omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4.2 (different files).
- After it: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4.3 builds `Registry` and the command on `commands()`; omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4.4 round-trips what it extracts against the binary. A10 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.10`) reads `CommandInfo` for the manifest's inputs.

title: The `capabilities` command: `Registry::build()`, its data and human form, wired in under DEC-1
description:
Part 3 of 4 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4 (`omaddons capabilities`). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

A4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`) adds `omaddons capabilities [--json]`: one call, offline, in a few milliseconds, that describes this build for an agent, generated from the live clap tree and the binary's registries, never kept by hand (M4-D2), and reporting the values `config.toml` changes as they are in effect (M4-D4). Subtask 1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4.1`) extracted the per-command facts (`CommandInfo`); subtask 2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4.2`) built the tolerant config load, the effective values with their source, credential presence and per-code retryability.

**This part is the command.** It joins those into `contract::Registry`, projects the registry into `capabilities`' data (in the plan's key order) and its human summary, and wires the command in under DEC-1 (no stubs): the clap variant, the `COMMANDS` row with every M4 field, the `canonical_path` and dispatch arms, the help-layout update, contract matrix rows with snapshots, the read-only invocation, the `cli_skeleton` literals, the widget's `CLI_PATHS` row and README's section, all in this one commit. It is its own step because it is the first user-visible change and every touch point must land together.

The decisions it implements, restated:

- **M4-D4:** reads the binary's registries and `config.toml`, nothing else (no discovery, no target registry, no network, no writes); effective values each with `source: "builtin" | "config"`; a broken config gives built-in values and `config_error {path, line, column, message}`, never a failure; the human form is at most 40 lines ending with "`--json` for the full description"; under 20 ms. *Rejected:* the discovered clients (that is `status`, and it costs a scan); failing on a broken config.
- **M4-D3:** `contract_version` = `output::SCHEMA_VERSION` ("1.0"), the one contract version; `version` is the crate's.
- **M4-D5:** each command's declared `exits`, `dictionary`, `stores_plan` and `network` (A1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1`) are published as they are declared.
- **M4-D6:** `env_vars` publishes `ENV_VARS`' `release` rows only (A2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.2`); debug variables would mislead, because release builds ignore them.
- **M4-D10, M4-D11, M4-D29:** each error code's typed `details` specification (A9, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9`) as `details_schema`; the `Action` registry (A2); the failure-mode summary from `FAILURE_MODES` (E1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`).
- **M4-D19:** `binds` derives from `precondition::BINDING_COMMANDS`, the single list.
- **M4-D55:** the new shape passes A3's rule test (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`) with no allowlist line; reasoned exceptions go in the rule test's `EXCEPTIONS`, which H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`) audits.
- **M4-D56, M4-D18:** key order deterministic (the order below), not contract; no volatile key.
- **DEC-1, M4-D7 (common rule 17), common rule 18:** every touch point here; `SKILL.md` regenerated if B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`) has landed; the corpus row if C4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4`) has landed.

**Facts this part relies on** (verified at `c0ab5e9`, after the leaf's blockers):
- `src/app/mod.rs`: `COMMANDS` (`:121-165` at `c0ab5e9`; after A1 each row is `entry(name, group, mutates, exits, data, network)` with `data_schema::<O>`); `command_name` (`:195-237`, after A1 delegating to `canonical_path`); `dispatch` (`:331-371`) and `run_command` (`:374-587`); `Out::emit` (`:256-258`) takes a `Result<O>`.
- `src/cli.rs`: the `Command` enum (`:137-213`; `Omarchy` is last at `:211-212`); `Context::new` (`:247-302`) validates `OMADDONS_ACTOR`/`--actor`, `--reason` and `--if-match` before dispatch; `check_if_match` (`:309-339`) refuses `--if-match` on a non-binding path with `usage` and, for a command that does not mutate, the fix argv without the flag.
- `src/output/mod.rs:34-55`: `Outcome { type Data: Serialize + JsonSchema; command(); data(); warnings(); commands(); partial(); assertion_failure(); render_human(w, style) }`. `HelpOutcome` writes pre-rendered text (`src/app/help.rs:22-113`); `short_meaning` is private (`:116-126`).
- Bare help: Setup line pinned at `tests/cli_skeleton.rs:125-127` (`Setup     targets  config  auth  omarchy  help`), snapshots `tests/snapshots/cli_skeleton__bare_help_human.snap` and `…__bare_help_json.snap`, layout test `src/app/help.rs:433-477`.
- `tests/contract/matrix.rs` (rows as `fn <command>()` over `Scene`, `s.json(args, code)`, `insta::assert_json_snapshot!(name, s.stable(&c.envelope))`); `tests/contract/main.rs` (`support::check`, `Scene`, `stable`); `tests/contract/special.rs:135-172` (HOME), `:313-386` (read-only invocations), `:456-476` (repeats).
- `omarchy/Model.js:134-177` (`CLI_PATHS`), held by `tests/omarchy_widget.rs:29-49`.
- After A3: `contract::opaque::OPAQUE` (`{scope, path, source, reason}` rows, sorted by scope then path, with a test that every serialized `serde_json::Value` field has one); `tests/contract/rules.rs` with `EXCEPTIONS: (rule, scope pattern, path pattern, reason)`; `support::check` validates every envelope's `data` strictly against the row's `data` schema; the snapshot walker validates every `.snap` body that is a JSON object with `ok`, `schema_version` and `command`.
- After C1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.1`): `src/vocabulary.rs` `CLIENT_FREE` (`help`, `config`, `targets`, `net-log`, `auth`, `omarchy`, `copy`) and the test `every_command_says_whether_it_selects_a_client`.
- After E1: `crate::doctor::registry::FAILURE_MODES` (7 rows) and `Subsystem::ALL` (13, `applicable()` false for `sockets` and `hooks`), `as_str()`.
- README: `### help [COMMAND]` at `README.md:1748`; "What works today" table at `:126-163` with the milestone-4 planned row "`capabilities`, `doctor`, `robot-docs`, stored plans, the agent skill, the first tag | 🗓️ Milestone 4".

## Technical Approach

1. **`Registry`** (`src/contract/mod.rs`), as the leaf's section 7 specifies:

   ```rust
   pub struct Registry {
       pub commands: Vec<commands::CommandInfo>,
       pub effective: effective::Effective,
       pub config_error: Option<crate::state::config::ConfigProblem>,
       pub warnings: Vec<crate::error::Warning>,
   }
   impl Registry {
       pub fn builtin() -> Self;    // no I/O, no environment: for A10, B1 and robot-docs
       pub fn build() -> Self;      // builtin + config.toml through the process environment; never fails
       pub fn from_parts(config: TolerantConfig, credential: &dyn Fn(SourceId) -> bool) -> Self;
   }
   ```

   - `build()`: `Paths::from_env()`; on `Err(e)` → `config_error = Some(ConfigProblem { path: None, line: None, column: None, message: e.message })`, built-in values; on `Ok(paths)` → `from_parts(Config::load_tolerant(&paths), &credential)` where `credential` is subtask 2's (GitHub: `github_credential_present(&paths, &config.sources)`; CurseForge, Wago: `credential_present` of their configured reference; else `false`).
   - `from_parts`: `commands::commands()`; with a problem, `Effective::builtin()`, `config_error = problem`, no warnings; else `Effective::of(&config, credential)` and the config's warnings.
   - Module doc: M4-D2's registry and the builtin/build split (decided while writing this bead: the golden, the guide and `robot-docs` read `builtin()`, so they never vary with a user's config).

2. **`src/app/capabilities.rs`** (new; `pub mod capabilities;` in `src/app/mod.rs`):

   ```rust
   //! `omaddons capabilities`: this build, described for agents (vision §5.10, M4-D4).
   //! Offline, scan-free and write-free: the live clap tree, the registries and config.toml.

   #[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, clap::Args)]
   pub struct CapabilitiesArgs {}

   #[derive(Debug)]
   pub struct CapabilitiesOutcome { data: CapabilitiesData, warnings: Vec<Warning>, text: String }

   /// Runs `capabilities` (it reads nothing the context holds).
   pub fn run() -> Result<CapabilitiesOutcome>;  // Registry::build(), data_of, render
   /// The data of `registry` (pure; unit-tested).
   pub fn data_of(registry: &Registry) -> Result<CapabilitiesData>;   // Err only `internal`: a details spec that is no schema
   fn render(data: &CapabilitiesData, registry: &Registry) -> String;   // the human form
   ```

   `impl Outcome`: `command()` = `"capabilities"`; `data()`; `warnings()` = the config's `config_unknown_key` warnings; `commands()` empty (decided while writing this bead: no action exists for "read the guide", and the data already points at it); `render_human` writes `text`.

3. **The data**, keys in this order (`CapabilitiesData`, every part deriving `Debug, Serialize, JsonSchema`, field order = this order):

   | Key | Type and source |
   |---|---|
   | `version` | `&'static str`, `env!("CARGO_PKG_VERSION")` |
   | `contract_version` | `&'static str`, `output::SCHEMA_VERSION` |
   | `build_id` | only if D1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1`) has landed: `build_info::BUILD_ID` (step 4) |
   | `guide_digest` | only if B1 has landed: `"sha256:" + contract::guide::EXPECTED_DIGEST` (or the constant as is, if it already carries the prefix), as the guide's stamp line writes it (step 4) |
   | `features` | `Vec<&'static str>`, `contract::features::FEATURES` |
   | `commands` | `Vec<CommandDescription>`, one per `registry.commands` |
   | `exit_codes` | `ExitDictionaries { general: Vec<GeneralExit>, doctor: Vec<DoctorExit> /* [] until E3's dictionary exists */ }` |
   | `env_vars` | `Vec<EnvVarDescription {name, description, mirrors: Option<&str>}>` from `contract::env::release()` |
   | `limits` | `Vec<LimitDescription {name, value: PublishedValue, unit, config_key: Option<&str>, source: ValueSource}>` |
   | `sources` | `Vec<SourceDescription {id: SourceId, enabled, requires_credential, credential_configured, hosts: Vec<String>, source: ValueSource}>` |
   | `families` | `Vec<FamilyDescription {name: Family, interface_min: Option<u32>, interface_max: Option<u32>, legacy, source}>` |
   | `client_rules` | `Vec<ClientRulesDescription {row, family: Family, install_kind: Option<InstallKind>, version_min: ClientVersion, version_max: Option<ClientVersion>, game_types, multi_toc, comma_interface, game_suffixes, family_suffixes, legacy_suffixes, directive_conditionals, interface_includes_patch, legacy, reload_rereads_toc, interface_floor: Option<u32>, source}>` |
   | `target_id_forms` | `Vec<&'static str>`, `contract::target_id_forms()` |
   | `error_codes` | `Vec<ErrorCodeDescription {code: ErrorCode, exit: u8, doctor_exit: Option<u8> /* u8 once E3 has landed */, retryable: Retryability, meaning: &'static str, details_schema: SchemaDoc}>` |
   | `warning_codes` | `Vec<WarningCodeDescription {code: WarningCode, meaning}>` over `WarningCode::ALL` |
   | `actions` | `Vec<ActionDescription {action: Action, description, destructive}>` over `Action::ALL` |
   | `failure_modes` | `FailureModeSummary {count: usize, subsystems: Vec<Subsystem>, command: Option<String>}` |
   | `schemas_uri` | `Option<String>` |
   | `robot_docs_uri` | `Option<String>` |
   | `config_error` | `Option<ConfigErrorDescription {path: Option<String>, line: Option<u64>, column: Option<u64>, message}>` |

   - **`CommandDescription`:** `{path, description, group: Group, mutates, json: bool /* always true */, dictionary: Dictionary, exit_codes: &'static [u8], stores_plan, binds, network: Network, aliases, args: Vec<ArgDescription>, flags: Vec<FlagDescription>, data_schema: Option<String>}`. `ArgDescription {name, value_name, required, multiple, default: Option<String>, possible_values: Option<Vec<&str>>}`; `FlagDescription {long, short: Option<String>, aliases, value_name: Option<String>, takes_value, multiple, default: Option<String>, possible_values: Option<Vec<&str>>, conflicts_with, requires, global, description}`. `possible_values` is `Some` only for `Values::Words`.
   - **`GeneralExit {code, name, meaning, retryable: Option<bool>}`** from `Exit::ALL` (`meaning()`, the full meaning, as `help --json` gives it). **`DoctorExit {code, name, meaning}`** from E3's `doctor::Exit::ALL`.
   - **`PublishedValue`** (decided while writing this bead: a bare value by unit, as the capabilities example shows, not `LimitValue`'s tagged form): `#[serde(untagged)] enum PublishedValue { Integer(u64), Text(&'static str), List(&'static [&'static str]), Retention { min_age_ms: u64, keep_last: u64, window_ms: u64 } }`, mapped from `LimitValue` (`Count`, `Bytes`, `Millis`, `Ratio` → `Integer`).
   - **`failure_modes`:** `count` = `FAILURE_MODES.len()`; `subsystems` = the distinct `subsystem` of the rows, in `Subsystem::ALL` order (decided while writing this bead: a summary of what is registered); `command` per step 4.
   - Every list is a `Vec`; no map. Every enum field uses its enum so its schema is closed.

4. **Keys and pointers whose producer may land later** (the leaf's section 9). Decided while writing this bead:
   - `build_id` and `guide_digest`: present only when their producer (D1, B1) has landed; whichever of this bead and the producer lands second adds the field at its place, with the snapshot, schema, README and (after A10, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.10`) manifest updates in its commit (D1's bead and B1's plan entry say the same). Check for `crate::build_info::BUILD_ID` and `crate::contract::guide::EXPECTED_DIGEST` now.
   - The doctor dictionary, consistently with A5's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5`) `robot-docs errors`: if E3's `crate::doctor::Exit` and `doctor::exit_for` are on `main`, `exit_codes.doctor` = `doctor::Exit::ALL` → `{code, name, meaning}` and `doctor_exit` = `exit_for(code).code()` as a non-null `u8`; if not, `exit_codes.doctor` = `[]`, `doctor_exit: Option<u8>` = `null` (doc "`null` while this build has no doctor exit dictionary"), and add a comment on E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`): "capabilities publishes `exit_codes.doctor` as `[]` and `error_codes[].doctor_exit` as `null` until your dictionary lands: in your commit, fill both from `doctor::Exit::ALL` and `exit_for`, make `doctor_exit` a non-null integer, re-accept the capabilities snapshot and update README's `### capabilities`" (extend A5's comment for `robot-docs errors` if one exists). Never compute a doctor exit here.
   - Record in the close comment which of the four this bead published.
   - The pointers are computed from `COMMANDS`: `schemas_uri` = `Some("omaddons robot-docs schema")` iff `robot-docs schema` is a row; `commands[].data_schema` = `Some(<shell_words::join of ["omaddons", "robot-docs", "schema", path words]>)` under the same condition (read A5's clap definition: if its positional takes the path as one argument, pass it as one argument); `robot_docs_uri` = `Some("omaddons robot-docs guide")` iff `robot-docs guide` is a row; `failure_modes.command` = `Some("omaddons doctor capabilities --json")` iff `doctor capabilities` is a row. Each is `null` otherwise, so capabilities never names a command the build lacks.

5. **The human form**, the leaf's section 10 exactly: line 1 `omaddons <version> · contract <contract_version>` (plus ` · build <build_id>` when published); line 2 `<n> commands: look <a> · change <b> · setup <c> (omaddons help <command> for one)`; `Exit codes:` and the seven general rows (`  <code>  <name padded>  <help::short_meaning>`; make `short_meaning` `pub(crate)`); the doctor dictionary as one `Doctor exit codes:` line of `<code> <name>` items joined by ` · `, wrapped under the first item to stay under 80 columns, only when `exit_codes.doctor` is not empty; `Sources:` and one line per source (`  <id padded>  on|off`, then `token configured` for a configured credential, `needs a key (M5)` for a source that requires one and this build lacks, `+ <host>, …` for configured git hosts, `(config)` when its source is `config`); one counts line `<e> error codes · <w> warning codes · <a> actions · <f> failure modes · <l> limits (<c> from config)`; the `config.toml line L, column C: <message>; built-in values shown` line only with a `config_error` (`config.toml: <message>; built-in values shown` without a line; `HOME is not an absolute path; built-in values shown` without a path); last line `--json for the full description`. Never the full config path, never a credential. At most 40 lines; each under 80 columns.

6. **DEC-1 touch points, all in this commit:**
   1. `src/cli.rs`: after `Omarchy`, `/// Describe this build for agents: commands, flags, exit codes, errors, limits and sources (offline; writes nothing)` and `#[command(after_long_help = CAPABILITIES_HELP)] Capabilities(crate::app::capabilities::CapabilitiesArgs)`, with `CAPABILITIES_HELP` beside the other help constants: three examples (`omaddons capabilities` the summary; `omaddons capabilities --json` everything as data; `omaddons capabilities --json | jq '.data.commands[] | select(.mutates) | .path'`) and one sentence: "It reads only the binary and config.toml, and changes nothing."
   2. `src/app/mod.rs`: `pub mod capabilities;`; the row `entry("capabilities", Group::Setup, false, &[0, 1, 2], data_schema::<capabilities::CapabilitiesOutcome>, Network::None)` after `omarchy remove`, before `help`; `canonical_path` arm `Command::Capabilities(_) => "capabilities"`; `run_command` arm `Some(Command::Capabilities(_)) => out.emit(capabilities::run())`.
   3. Help layout: `bare_help_stays_one_screen_with_every_planned_command` (`src/app/help.rs:433-477`) gains `("capabilities", Setup)`; the bare Setup line becomes `Setup     targets  config  auth  omarchy  capabilities  help`.
   4. Contract matrix rows (`tests/contract/matrix.rs`, `fn capabilities()`): see the Test Plan.
   5. `tests/contract/special.rs`: `"capabilities" => &["capabilities"]` in `read_only_commands_ignore_dry_run_and_reason`; in `a_home_that_is_unset_or_relative_is_a_usage_error`, `check(run(None, &["capabilities"]), 0)` with `data.config_error.path` null and a message starting "HOME"; `(&["capabilities"][..], 0)` in `repeated_runs_are_byte_identical`.
   6. `tests/cli_skeleton.rs:125-127`: the Setup literal; re-accept both bare-help snapshots after reviewing the diff (one name in the human form, one `commands[]` entry `{"name":"capabilities","about":…,"aliases":[],"group":"setup"}` in the JSON form; nothing else).
   7. `omarchy/Model.js`: `"capabilities":    { "mutates": false, "destructive": false, "binds": false },` before `"help"` (aligned like its neighbours).
   8. README (step 9).
   9. Also: `"capabilities"` in `vocabulary::CLIENT_FREE` (decided while writing this bead: it reads no `-t`; resolving one would need discovery, which M4-D4 forbids); if C4 has landed, the row `omaddons capabilites` → `usage` → fix `omaddons capabilities` → exit 0 in `tests/contract/intent_corpus.rs`; if B1 has landed, `OMADDONS_UPDATE_SKILL=1 cargo test --test skill` and commit `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` (never a shell redirect).

7. **Contract-suite registrations** (the leaf's section 12):
   - `details_schema` is A5's `SchemaDoc` (`src/contract/schema.rs`: `#[serde(transparent)] pub struct SchemaDoc(pub schemars::Schema)` whose hand-written `JsonSchema` is `{"type": "object", "additionalProperties": true, "description": "A JSON Schema (draft 2020-12): JSON Schema's own vocabulary, not omaddons' wire names"}`); whichever of A4 and A5 lands first adds it exactly so. Why: a `schemars::Schema` field publishes `{"type": ["object", "boolean"]}`, which A3's strict transform would close, so every key of a schema document would fail validation; a `serde_json::Value` would be open but would not say what it holds. Wrap A9's `details_schema()` with `schemars::Schema::try_from(value)`; its failure (neither an object nor a boolean) cannot happen for a rendered spec and becomes `Error::internal` naming the code (`data_of` returns `Result`; no `unwrap`).
   - `contract::OPAQUE` row `{scope: "command capabilities", path: "error_codes[].details_schema", source: "ErrorCodeDescription.details_schema", reason: "A code's `details` schema is a JSON Schema fragment, written in JSON Schema's own vocabulary."}` (A5's wording for its own row), sorted into place.
   - The rule test's `EXCEPTIONS` (never the allowlist): `r3-array-plural` for `commands[].flags[].conflicts_with` (clap's own name for the relation), `exit_codes.general` and `exit_codes.doctor` (each array named for the exit dictionary it lists), `limits[].value` (one value whose type follows `unit`; for a `list` unit the value is the list); `r4-value-case` for `families[].name` and `client_rules[].family` (game-family names are an input vocabulary users type in `-t` and `config.toml`; the same values are allowlisted wherever `Family` appears, and H1 judges them against their own grammar). If the checkers report different paths for this scope, add exactly what they report for `command capabilities` with these reasons, and list each in the close comment.

8. **Volatile keys:** none (`build_id` is constant per binary; no time, id or path that changes between runs).

9. **README:**
   - `### capabilities`, before `### help [COMMAND]`: purpose (the agent's first call: "one call, offline, in a few milliseconds"); `omaddons capabilities` (the summary) and `omaddons capabilities --json`; what it reads (the binary, `config.toml`, and whether a stored GitHub token file exists, never its content) and never does (no discovery, no network, no writes, no credential command); the data keys in order, one line each, with `commands[]`' and the flags' fields; effective values and `source`; `config_error`, and that a broken config or an unset `HOME` still answers with built-in values; `credential_configured` means present, not valid (`auth github status` checks it); a pointer is `null` in a build without the command it names; `-t` and the other globals are ignored, `--if-match` is refused; no volatile key, so two runs print the same bytes. Write only what this commit's binary does: a key whose producer has not landed is not mentioned.
   - "What works today": a row "`capabilities`: every command, flag, value, alias, exit code, error and warning code, action, limit, source, family, client-rules row and `-t` form, generated from the code, offline, in milliseconds | ✅ Done (milestone 4)"; `capabilities` removed from the milestone-4 planned row.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `contract::Registry` exists with `builtin()`, `build()` and `from_parts()`; `builtin()` touches no file and no environment variable; `build()` never fails.
- [ ] `omaddons capabilities --json` exits 0 with `data` keys in the order of step 3 (`build_id` and `guide_digest` exactly when D1 and B1 have landed; `exit_codes.doctor` and `doctor_exit` from E3's dictionary when it has landed, else `[]` and `null` with the comment on E3; the close comment names which), every value from its registry or the effective configuration, `details_schema` as A5's `SchemaDoc`, `retryable` from `ErrorCode::retryability()`, and passes `support::check`'s strict schema validation.
- [ ] Each pointer is a runnable command string exactly when the command it names is a `COMMANDS` row, else `null`.
- [ ] `omaddons capabilities` (human) prints at most 40 lines, each under 80 columns, in the layout of step 5, ending with `--json for the full description`.
- [ ] Every DEC-1 touch point of step 6 is in this commit: the variant and its help, the row with every M4 field, both arms, the layout test, both bare-help snapshots and the `cli_skeleton` literal, the matrix rows and their two snapshots, the three `special.rs` additions, the `CLI_PATHS` row, README's section and "What works today" row; plus `CLIENT_FREE`, the `OPAQUE` row, the `EXCEPTIONS` rows, and the corpus row and `SKILL.md` when C4 and B1 have landed.
- [ ] A3's rule test and `OPAQUE` tests pass with no allowlist line added; `tests/omarchy_widget.rs` and the widget pipeline pass; A1's exit observation sees only declared exits (0 and 2).
- [ ] No snapshot changes except the two bare-help snapshots and the two new contract snapshots (and `SKILL.md` when B1 has landed).
- [ ] `argc gate` passes and `ubs` is clean on the changed files.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

`src/contract/mod.rs`:

- `registry_builtin_needs_no_environment`: `Registry::builtin()` equals `Registry::from_parts(TolerantConfig::default_for_tests(), &|_| false)` (a test helper building the default tolerant config with a fixed path), and `config_error` is `None`.
- `from_parts_uses_builtin_values_with_a_problem`: a `TolerantConfig` with a problem and a config that would override a limit → every `source` `builtin`, `config_error` set, no warnings.

`src/app/capabilities.rs` (all on `Registry::builtin()` or `from_parts` with synthetic configs; table-driven where there are cases):

- `data_keys_are_in_the_published_order`: the serialized top-level keys equal `EXPECTED_KEYS` (a test constant; each later producer adds its key in its own commit).
- `every_command_entry_carries_its_registry_facts`: for each `COMMANDS` row, the entry's `path`, `group`, `mutates`, `dictionary`, `exit_codes`, `stores_plan`, `network` equal the row's, `binds` equals `BINDING_COMMANDS.contains`, `json` is true.
- `pointers_are_null_exactly_when_their_command_is_missing`: each pointer is `Some` iff its path is a row; each `Some` pointer's `shell_words::split` parses with `Cli::try_parse_from`.
- `limit_values_publish_bare_values`, table: a `count` limit → JSON integer; `bytes` → integer; `ms` → integer; `text` (`USER_AGENT`) → string; `list` (`DISCOVERY_SKIP_DIRS`) → array of strings; `retention` (`TX_RETENTION`) → object with exactly `min_age_ms`, `keep_last`, `window_ms`.
- `limits_carry_config_keys_and_sources`: `DOWNLOAD_MAX_BYTES`'s `config_key` is `limits.download_max_bytes`, `TX_RETENTION`'s `limits.tx_retention_count`, `DEFAULT_CHECK_INTERVAL`'s `check_interval_hours`, a non-overridable limit's `null`; with a config overriding `DOWNLOAD_MAX_BYTES`, that one reports `config` and its effective value.
- `error_codes_publish_meaning_spec_and_tri_state`: for every code, `exit`, `meaning`, `details_schema` (its JSON value) equal the registry's; `plan_stale`, `network`, `io` → `"conditional"`, `locked` → `true`, `usage` → `false`; `doctor_exit` is E3's `exit_for` when E3 has landed, else `null` for every code, and `exit_codes.doctor` is E3's dictionary or `[]`.
- `failure_modes_summarize_the_registry`: `count == FAILURE_MODES.len()`; `subsystems` distinct, in `Subsystem::ALL` order, each `applicable()`.
- `config_error_is_reported_with_builtin_values`, table: a parse problem (path, line, column, message), an unreadable file (line and column `null`), no `HOME` (`path` `null`).
- `human_form_fits`, table: `builtin` registry; with a config error; with configured overrides; a synthetic registry of 70 commands across the three groups (and a synthetic eleven-code doctor dictionary, so the wrapped doctor line is measured before E3 lands) → at most 40 lines, every line under 80 columns, line 1 starts `omaddons <version> · contract 1.0`, last line `--json for the full description`. Message: the case and the rendered text.
- `human_form_names_every_general_exit_and_source`.
- `human_form_never_prints_a_path_or_credential`: with a config error carrying an absolute path and a configured token reference, the text contains `config.toml` but not the path, and not the reference.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

Each new test function records its phases with T1's `TestLog` (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`): `let log = tlog!();`, `log.step` per row, `log.json("envelope", &c.envelope)` (for the success row, `log.json("digest", …)` instead of the 300 KB envelope).

- **`tests/contract/matrix.rs::capabilities`**, on a fresh `Scene`:
  1. step "success": `s.json(&["capabilities"], 0)` (contract checks, strict schema validation, exit observation); `insta::assert_json_snapshot!("capabilities_ok_digest", digest(&c.envelope))`, where `digest` (a helper in the matrix module; subtask 4 moves it into `tests/common/capabilities.rs`, keeping its output byte-identical so this snapshot does not move) builds `{envelope_keys, data_keys, counts: {commands, error_codes, warning_codes, actions, env_vars, limits, sources, families, client_rules, target_id_forms, features}, paths, capabilities_entry, pointers: {schemas_uri, robot_docs_uri, failure_modes_command}, config_error}` with `build_id` and `guide_digest` redacted to `<build_id>` and `<guide_digest>` when present. Decided while writing this bead: a digest, so later leaves change one line (`paths`) or a count, not a 300 KB snapshot, and A3's snapshot walker (which validates bodies holding `ok`, `schema_version` and `command`) skips it; the full data is validated live in step 1.
  2. step "usage": `s.json(&["capabilities", "--bogus"], 2)` → `error.code` `usage`, `command` `capabilities`; snapshot `capabilities_usage` (`s.stable`).
  3. step "if-match refused": `s.json(&["capabilities", "--if-match", "pc1:<64 zeros>"], 2)` → `usage`, `fix_argv` `["omaddons", "capabilities"]` (asserted, no snapshot).
- **`tests/contract/special.rs`:** the read-only invocation (identical envelope and unchanged `<state>` with `--dry-run --reason x`); `HOME` unset → exit 0, `config_error.path` null, message starting "HOME"; byte-identical repeats of `capabilities`.
- **Existing suites that must pass:** `tests/cli_skeleton.rs` (new literal and snapshots), `tests/omarchy_widget.rs` (the new row), `tests/contract/usage_fixes.rs` (its one-edit typo sweep now covers `capabilities` with no edit: `capabilites` → `omaddons capabilities`), C1's `every_command_says_whether_it_selects_a_client`, C4's corpus when present, `tests/skill.rs` when B1 has landed.

### Logging

- Unit tests: a name per case; messages name the case and show the registry input and the rendered output (for the human form, the whole text).
- Contract tests: as above; a failure prints the step, the run's context (argv, exit, stdout, stderr) through `support::check`, and the transcript path through the `TestLog` guard.

## Considerations

- **Hot spots (§10.5):** `src/app/mod.rs` (add the row and the two arms only, after rebasing on whoever is in flight; A1's fields are already on every row); `src/cli.rs` (one variant and one help constant); `tests/contract/matrix.rs` (one function, two snapshot files); `omarchy/Model.js` (one `CLI_PATHS` row); `README.md` (only `### capabilities` and the one table row); `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` (regenerate after rebasing, never merge by hand); `src/vocabulary.rs` (one word).
- **Size of the output:** about 300 KB of JSON at this point (globals repeated per command, as the plan's walk "globals propagated" requires); record the measured size in the close comment.
- **The pointers' and late keys' nullability** is an intermediate state H1 reviews; the pointers become strings automatically when A5, B1 and E4 land, and the late keys are added by D1, B1 and E3 if they land after this part.
- **`OMADDONS_ACTOR=robot`** still fails `capabilities` with `usage` (validated by `Context::new` before dispatch, as for `help`); not changed here.
- **Common rule 16** does not apply (not a mutating path); **rule 14** does not apply (no protocol).

Decided while writing this bead (confirm or adjust in the close comment): the builtin/build split; `run()` without context, returning `Result` only for the impossible `SchemaDoc` failure; `SchemaDoc` and the doctor dictionary's `[]`/`null` until E3, aligned with A5's `robot-docs errors`; no `commands[]` hints; config warnings in `warnings`; the late keys and pointers rule; `subsystems` as registered; `PublishedValue`; the human layout and wording; the digest snapshot; client-free in C1's vocabulary; the `OPAQUE` and `EXCEPTIONS` rows; the row's place before `help`.

## Dependencies

- Parent: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4 (`omaddons capabilities`), under the area epic omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.
- Before it: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4.1 (`CommandInfo`, `commands()`, the value sets) and omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4.2 (`TolerantConfig`, `Effective`, credential presence, `retryability()`), which `Registry` joins; and T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, an edge added at filing), whose `TestLog` the contract tests use. The leaf's blockers (A1, A2, A3, A9, E1) supply everything else.
- After it: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4.4 tests the command end to end and measures its budget.

- [ ] The eight scenarios of `tests/capabilities.rs` pass in the gate, each a `TestLog` scenario with its steps, runs, trees and comparisons in its transcript.
- [ ] The round trip finds no failure: every command's help parses and the binary answers it, every flag, short form, alias and listed value parses, every declared conflict is refused and every declared requirement enforced, every command alias resolves to its path, every non-null pointer parses and runs.
- [ ] Completeness finds no failure against `COMMANDS`, `ErrorCode::ALL`, `WarningCode::ALL`, `Action::ALL`, `ENV_VARS`' release rows, `Exit::ALL`, the two limit registries, `SourceId::ALL`, `Family::ALL`, the built-in client rules, `target_id_forms()`, `FEATURES` and `FAILURE_MODES`.
- [ ] Purity: every hashed tree is unchanged, no `net.log` line is added, no state or cache directory is created on a fresh home, and the planted token never appears.
- [ ] Every broken-configuration case and the relative `HOME` exit 0 with the exact `config_error` and built-in values; the unknown key warns and still applies the other overrides.
- [ ] Every override reports `source: "config"` with its effective value, everything else `builtin`; `check_interval_hours = 0` stays `builtin`; CurseForge stays disabled.
- [ ] Credentials are detected in every present case and never read or run.
- [ ] The human form passes its checks; the ignored flags change nothing and `--if-match` is `usage`.
- [ ] `capabilities_answers_in_under_20_ms` exists, is ignored in the gate, and passes on a release build (`cargo test --release --test perf capabilities_answers_in_under_20_ms -- --ignored --test-threads=1`), its printed median quoted in the leaf's close comment.
- [ ] README's Tests table names the suite and the budget.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes and `ubs` is clean on the changed files.
