title: `robot-docs schema` and `robot-docs errors`
description:
## How to work this bead

This bead is worked through its 3 subtasks, listed below in work order. Claim a subtask, not this bead (`br ready --parent omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5` lists the ready ones). The agent that closes the last open subtask then verifies every acceptance criterion of this bead (they are the leaf's, not any one subtask's), and closes this bead with `br close omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5 --reason "done: <evidence> · found: <ids>"`. Until this bead is closed, every bead it blocks stays blocked.

1. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5.1 A fix pattern for every code, and the code registry's three-valued retryability: `ErrorCode::fix_pattern`, `WarningCode::fix_pattern` and `ErrorCode::retryability` in `src/error/`, with their style and honesty tests. No command yet, no wire change.
2. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5.2 The `robot-docs` tree: `robot-docs schema [<command>]` and `robot-docs errors`, with every registry touch point: the command, its outcomes, its unit tests, its contract rows and snapshots, the widget's `CLI_PATHS` rows and README, in one commit (DEC-1).
3. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5.3 E2E: `tests/robot_docs.rs`, the published schemas and the catalog end to end: ten `TestLog` scenarios that prove the acceptance criteria against the real binary, plus README's Tests row.

The three run in that order: subtask 2 publishes what subtask 1 declares, and subtask 3 tests what subtask 2 ships.

**Size S, with three subtasks.** The plan sizes this leaf S: one new command module over registries that A3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`, schemas and live validation) and A9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9`, meanings and `DetailSpec`s) have already built. It is split anyway, for two reasons. Subtask 1 is the only part that touches `src/error.rs`, a collision hot spot of A9, A3, D4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`, the plan store), D5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`, `omaddons apply`), E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, `doctor diagnose`), E10 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.10`, the old fixes point at the doctor), the F leaves and H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, the pre-freeze audit), so it lands as its own small commit. Subtask 3 is new integration code on T1's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs) `TestLog`. The split is for the work only: this bead closes only when all three are done, so B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`, the guide renderer and `robot-docs guide`), A6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.6`, bare help's discovery line), H1 and T2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.2`, the slice-1 demo) never see half of it.

## Background

**What this bead is.** `omaddons robot-docs` is the binary's machine-readable documentation, the third of vision §5.10's discovery trio (`omaddons capabilities --json`, `omaddons doctor --json`, `omaddons robot-docs guide`). Vision §5.10 defines its subcommands: `guide` (the Markdown handbook, B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`, the guide renderer and `robot-docs guide`)), `schema [<command>]` ("JSON Schema of each command's `data`, via `schemars`"), `errors` ("the error-code catalog") and `install-skill` (B3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3`, `robot-docs install-skill`)). This bead creates the `robot-docs` clap tree with its first two subcommands:

- `omaddons robot-docs schema [<command>]`: the JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) of every command's `data`, of the envelope, of every stderr NDJSON event and of every file omaddons writes; or, with a command path, of that one command's `data`.
- `omaddons robot-docs errors`: every registered error code with its exit, its doctor exit, its retryability, its one-sentence meaning, its typed `details` schema and its fix pattern, and every warning code with its meaning and fix pattern.

Both are pure: they read no file (not even `config.toml`), need no `HOME`, send no request and write nothing. Everything they print is generated from the code, so it cannot drift from what the code does. The schemas and the catalog exist before this bead (A3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`, schemas and live validation) generates the schemas, A9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9`, meanings and `DetailSpec`s) wrote the meanings and the `details` specifications); this bead publishes them, adds the two facts nobody else declares (each code's fix pattern, and the honest three-valued retryability), and makes an unknown command path a usage error whose fix is the closest real path.

**What is true today** (verified at `c0ab5e9`):

- There is no `robot-docs` command (§2.1 of the plan: "The discovery trio (`capabilities`, `doctor`, `robot-docs`) that vision §5.9 asks bare help to list does not exist"). The `Command` enum is `src/cli.rs:137-213`; `app::COMMANDS` is `src/app/mod.rs:121-165` (42 rows of `{name, group, mutates}`), `command_name` is `src/app/mod.rs:195-237` and `run_command` is `src/app/mod.rs:374-587`.
- No schema is generated anywhere, and no error or warning code has a meaning text or a fix description. Agents learn the error catalog from README's tables (`README.md:1822-1869` and `:1871-1929`), which can drift.
- The registry's retryability is one boolean per code (`ErrorCode::default_retryable`, `src/error.rs:138-144`), but five codes have instances that differ from it (listed under "Facts this bead relies on"), so a boolean published per code would be wrong for them.

**What it serves.**

- **G-M4-1, self-describing:** "An agent with no prior knowledge learns everything it needs from the binary itself … Every fact in those outputs is generated from the code, so it cannot drift from what the code does. Every command's output has a published JSON Schema, and the contract suite validates real output against it." This bead is the publication half of the last sentence, and `capabilities` (A4, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`) points every command's `data_schema` at it (`"omaddons robot-docs schema install"`).
- **G-M4-2, the first guess works:** "A plausible wrong invocation yields a usage error whose fix is the command the user meant … Each such fix is proven to run, not only to parse." `robot-docs schema instal` answers `usage` with the fix `omaddons robot-docs schema install`, and the tests run that fix.
- **G-M4-5, frozen and enforced:** "Repeated runs print identical bytes." Both commands are deterministic, and they publish the schemas and the code catalog that the semantic manifest (A10, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.10`) and the golden (H2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.2`) pin.
- **Vision G4, agent ergonomics** ("the first command an agent guesses works"; "discovery via `capabilities`, `doctor` and `robot-docs`"): an agent can validate what it receives and look up any code it meets, from the tool itself.

**Checkpoint criteria it is responsible for** (§3.2 of the plan; H6, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the checkpoint, records the evidence):

- **Criterion 2, schemas:** "`omaddons robot-docs schema` gives a JSON Schema for every command path in `app::COMMANDS`, for the envelope and for every NDJSON event." And: "`robot-docs errors` lists every error code with its exit, retryability, meaning and its typed `details` specification (keys, value types, nested objects, nullability and reason enums)." (The live validation half of criterion 2 is A3's, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`.)
- **Criterion 14, the contract is frozen** (its last line, for this bead's paths): "Repeated runs of every command path print identical bytes, after stripping only the keys the volatile registry declares."
- In support of **criterion 1** (capabilities): every `commands[].data_schema` pointer that A4 publishes (`omaddons robot-docs schema <path>`) runs and returns that path's schema; this bead's suite runs one for every `COMMANDS` path. In support of **criterion 5** (intent inference): a mistyped `robot-docs` invocation gets a fix that runs (corpus rows, common rule 18).

**The decisions that shape it** (the full decision log is filed as comments on the milestone epic omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm):

- **M4-D2: one contract registry feeds every description of the CLI.** `src/contract/` assembles a registry from the live clap tree, `app::COMMANDS` and its per-command facts, the error, warning and exit registries, the action, event, env-var and feature registries, the limits, the rules and the sources; `capabilities`, `robot-docs` (guide, schema, errors), the wire-name golden, bare help's discovery line and `doctor capabilities` all read it. A fact clap cannot provide is declared exactly once, beside the command or code it describes, and a test cross-checks it against behaviour. *Why:* the vision's rule for `capabilities` ("generated from the live clap tree and the registries, never maintained by hand") works only if the registries exist, and one registry means the guide, `capabilities` and the golden cannot disagree. *Rejected:* a hand-written JSON asset (it drifts, the exact failure these surfaces exist to prevent); deriving every fact from runtime behaviour (a declaration is a promise tests verify); proc-macro attributes (a dependency and compile time for no gain over a table). For this bead: the fix pattern is such a fact, so it is declared once beside the code (`src/error/fix_pattern.rs`, an exhaustive match a new code cannot skip), not in `robot_docs.rs`, and B1's guide (`{{errors_common}}`, "with exit, retryability and the fix pattern") reads the same function.
- **M4-D9: schemas use the serialize contract, one generator per command, validated against live output.** Each schema is built with `SchemaSettings::draft2020_12().for_serialize()`, and each command, event and file gets a fresh `SchemaGenerator`, so its `$defs` names depend only on that one type. `robot-docs schema`'s output is `{envelope, events: {progress, warning, error, log}, commands: {<path>: schema}, files: {<kind>: schema}}`, map keys sorted, and `robot-docs schema <command>` gives one entry. *Why:* the deserialize contract would mark every `-v`-only field required, so every real output would fail; one shared generator would give unstable `Summary2` names. *Rejected:* one generator for everything; validating snapshots instead of live output; a hand-written validator; `serde_json/preserve_order` for declaration-order properties (property order inside a schema carries no meaning). The generation itself is A3's (`contract::schema`); this bead calls it and never builds a schema of its own.
- **M4-D10 (context): `error.details` are typed per code by a recursive specification, and are part of the contract.** A9 wrote one `DetailSpec` per error code (keys, value types, nesting, required or optional, nullable or not, and the closed value set of every stable enum such as `reason` and `changed`), rendered as a JSON Schema fragment by `ErrorCode::details_schema()`. "`robot-docs errors` and `capabilities.error_codes[].details_schema` publish each spec as a JSON Schema fragment." This bead publishes exactly that fragment, the same one A3's error union carries, so the three can never disagree.
- **§6.4 of the plan, published schemas stay open.** schemars emits `additionalProperties: false` only for `deny_unknown_fields` types; A3's contract suite applies a strict transform (`unevaluatedProperties: false` at every instance position) on the test side only. "The published schemas (`robot-docs schema`) stay open, so a newer minor's additions do not break an older consumer's validator." This bead must never apply the strict transform to what it prints.
- **Appendix A.1 of the plan, three-valued retryability.** In the code registry, `retryable` per code is `true`, `false` or `"conditional"`, the last where an instance decides; every error instance keeps its boolean `error.retryable`. "The tri-state appears only in the code registry (`capabilities`, `robot-docs errors`, the manifest's `error` nodes)." *Why (as the plan decided it):* a boolean would lie for the codes whose instances differ. The plan names `plan_stale`, `http_status` and `hash_mismatch`; the code has two more (see "Facts", and the decision in Technical Approach §3, which A4's bead shares).
- **M4-D40 (context): the doctor exit dictionary**, `0 healthy, 1 findings_present, 2 fix_partial, 3 fix_failed_rolled_back, 4 refused_unsafe, 5 concurrency_lost, 6 online_required, 64 usage_error, 66 no_input, 73 cannot_create, 74 io_error`, and every error code maps to it through E3's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, `doctor diagnose`) total `doctor::exit_for(ErrorCode)`. `robot-docs errors` publishes each code's `doctor_exit` from that function, declared once.
- **M4-D15 (context): a usage fix must run, not just parse.** The fix of an unknown command path is a real `robot-docs schema <path>` command line, and the tests run it.
- **M4-D18 and M4-D56 (context): determinism, and member order is not contract.** Every path's output is byte-identical across runs once the declared volatile keys are stripped (only `meta.*` here: this bead declares no new volatile key). JSON member order is deterministic (struct declaration order, sorted maps) but is not compared as contract.
- **M4-D55 (context): the contract rules hold from slice 1.** Every new shape passes A3's rule test (timestamps, null versus omitted, snake_case names, plural arrays, closed enumerations); this bead's data keys are chosen to pass it, and nothing is ever added to `tests/contract/rules_allowlist.txt`.
- **DEC-1, no stubs (common rule 4).** The command adds every registry touch point in the commit that adds its clap variant, and adds no stub for the subcommands that later leaves own (`guide` is B1's, `install-skill` B3's).

**Facts this bead relies on** (as of `c0ab5e9`, plus what its blockers deliver):

- `trait Outcome { type Data: Serialize + schemars::JsonSchema; fn command(&self) -> &'static str; … fn render_human(&self, w: &mut dyn Write, style: &Style) -> io::Result<()>; }` (`src/output/mod.rs:34-56`): a command returns an outcome that `src/output/` renders; on success the envelope's `command` is `outcome.command()`.
- `HelpOutcome` (`src/app/help.rs:22-113`) holds `data` plus pre-rendered `text`, and its human form writes the text raw: the pattern this bead's outcomes follow. `help::for_command(Some(path), argv)` (`src/app/help.rs:249-349`) renders the long help of a nested path and gives `usage` with the closest name for an unknown one; its envelope `command` is `help`.
- Usage fixes: `cli::usage_error` (`src/cli.rs:604-773`) turns clap errors into `usage`, keeps only fixes that parse, and corrects an unknown subcommand in place when the guessed path changes nothing (`subcommand_fix`, `src/cli.rs:849-890`); `cli::levenshtein` is `src/cli.rs:1202`.
- The error registry: `error_codes!` rows at `src/error.rs:149-204` (41 codes), `ErrorCode::ALL`, `wire()`, `exit()`, `default_retryable()` (`:122-145`); `warning_codes!` rows at `src/error.rs:245-349` (52 codes) with an extra untagged `WarningCode::Item(ErrorCode)` for a mirrored item failure, excluded from `WarningCode::ALL` (`:224-232`). A `Warning`'s `fix` is optional (`src/error.rs:661-665`), and `WarningBody` serializes it as `fix: null` (`:696-701`).
- Per-instance retryability: `Error::http_status` is retryable for 5xx only (`src/error.rs:580-584`), `Error::plan_stale` only for `PlanStaleSource::Replan` (`:587-593`), `Error::hash_mismatch` on its first attempt only (`:597-599`). Instances that override their code's registered default: `network` (registered `true`) is made `false` for more than 5 redirects (`src/net/guard.rs:343`) and for an undecodable `Content-Encoding` (`src/net/decode.rs:68`); `io` (registered `false`) is made `true` for a `WTF/` that changed or failed while a backup copied it (`src/backup/tree.rs:158`, `:165`); `hash_mismatch` is made `false` for a cached blob (`src/engine/blobs.rs:296`). README's table already says so for `network` and `io` (`README.md:1853`, `:1866`). One run-level override applies to any code: `recovery_failed` (`src/engine/tx.rs:573-578`) sets `error.retryable = false` on a commit's error whose in-process recovery failed too.
- The read-only contract test `read_only_commands_ignore_dry_run_and_reason` (`tests/contract/special.rs:313-386`) needs an invocation for every `mutates: false` row in its table (`:317-338`), and fails "add a read-only invocation of {name} here" otherwise.
- Bare help's Setup line is pinned by `tests/cli_skeleton.rs:123-128` (`"\nSetup     targets  config  auth  omarchy  help\n"`) and by `tests/snapshots/cli_skeleton__bare_help_human.snap` and `…_json.snap`; the planned-layout test is `bare_help_stays_one_screen_with_every_planned_command` (`src/app/help.rs:433-477`, 22 planned entries).
- The widget's `CLI_PATHS` table is `omarchy/Model.js:134-177`, held equal to `app::COMMANDS` by `cli_paths_mirror_the_registry` (`tests/omarchy_widget.rs:30`).
- The contract suite: `Scene` (`tests/contract/main.rs:366-505`), `support::check` (`:114-225`), `support::without_meta` (`:508`), `PROSE_COMMANDS` and `names_a_command` (`:51-81`); the matrix (`tests/contract/matrix.rs`) snapshots envelopes as `tests/contract/snapshots/contract__matrix__<name>.snap` (105 today).
- schemars 1.2.3 (crate source): `impl JsonSchema for schemars::Schema` gives `{"type": ["object", "boolean"]}` (`src/schema.rs:470-485`), and `serde_json::Value`'s schema is `true` (`src/json_schema_impls/serdejson.rs:8-18`).
- From A1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1`, per-command facts): `CommandEntry { name, group, mutates, dictionary, exits, data, stores_plan, network }`, rows built by `const fn entry(name, group, mutates, exits, data, network)`, `data_schema::<O: Outcome>`, `app::canonical_path(&Command)` (the one mapping from a parsed command to its envelope name, which `command_name` delegates to), `app::command_entry(path)`, and the rule "`COMMANDS` has one row per runnable path: every clap leaf, plus every parent whose bare form runs". `auth`'s row is `auth github`.
- From A2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.2`, the registries): `contract::events::EventName::ALL` and `wire()` (`progress`, `warning`, `error`, `log`).
- From A3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`, schemas and live validation): in `src/contract/schema.rs`, `command_schema(entry)`, `command_schemas() -> BTreeMap<&'static str, Schema>` (one per `COMMANDS` row, `title` = the path), `envelope_schema()`, `error_schema()`, `error_variant(code)`, `event_schemas()` (keyed by event wire name, `event` pinned by `const`) and `file_schemas()` (every `store::KINDS` kind, plus `journal` and `desired_state`); `contract::OPAQUE` (`src/contract/opaque.rs`, rows `{scope, path, source, reason}`) with tests that fail an open schema position without a row and a row matching no open position; an open position is the boolean `true`, the empty schema, or an object schema with `additionalProperties: true` or `unevaluatedProperties: true`; the strict transform and the `Validator` wrapper in `tests/contract/validate.rs`, includable by another suite with `#[path = "contract/validate.rs"] mod validate;`; and `support::check` validating every envelope's `data` strictly against its command's schema.
- From A9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9`, meanings and `DetailSpec`s): `ErrorCode::meaning()`, `ErrorCode::details_schema() -> serde_json::Value`, `WarningCode::meaning()` (an `Item` takes its error's), the meaning style rules (one sentence, at most 200 characters, names no command or milestone), and its decision that `fix_pattern` is this bead's to declare. A9's `conditional_retryability_is_stated` test checks that the meanings of `http_status`, `hash_mismatch` and `plan_stale` say when an instance is retryable.
- Not an edge: E3's `doctor::exit_for` and `doctor::Exit` may or may not be on `main` when this bead lands (E3's earliest start is before this bead's, but neither blocks the other). Technical Approach §6 says what to do in each case.

## Technical Approach

### 1. Files

| File | What | Subtask |
|---|---|---|
| `src/error/fix_pattern.rs` (new) | `ErrorCode::fix_pattern`, `WarningCode::fix_pattern` (exhaustive matches), the style check and their unit tests | 1 |
| `src/error.rs` | `mod fix_pattern;`; `Retryability`, `ConditionalTag`, `ErrorCode::CONDITIONALLY_RETRYABLE` and `ErrorCode::retryability` (unless A4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`, `omaddons capabilities`) added them first); the `network` and `io` meanings where they do not yet say when an instance is retryable; unit tests | 1 |
| `src/contract/schema.rs` (A3's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`, schemas and live validation) file) | `pub struct SchemaDoc` | 2 |
| `src/contract/opaque.rs` (A3's file) | five `OPAQUE` rows | 2 |
| `src/app/robot_docs.rs` (new) | `RobotDocsArgs`, `RobotDocsAction`, `SchemaArgs`, the data types, the two outcomes, path resolution, the human renderers, unit tests | 2 |
| `src/app/mod.rs` | `pub mod robot_docs;`, three `COMMANDS` rows, the `canonical_path` arm, the dispatch arm | 2 |
| `src/cli.rs` | `Command::RobotDocs` | 2 |
| `src/app/help.rs` | the planned-layout test | 2 |
| `omarchy/Model.js` | three `CLI_PATHS` rows | 2 |
| `tests/contract/matrix.rs`, `tests/contract/snapshots/contract__matrix__robot_docs_*.snap` (new) | the contract rows | 2 |
| `tests/contract/special.rs` | three read-only invocations | 2 |
| `tests/cli_skeleton.rs`, `tests/snapshots/cli_skeleton__bare_help_human.snap`, `…_json.snap` | the Setup line literal; snapshots re-accepted | 2 |
| `tests/contract/intent_corpus.rs` | three corpus rows, if C4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4`, the run-the-fix corpus) is on `main` | 2 |
| `README.md` | `### robot-docs` (command reference), a pointer in "Exit codes" (subtask 2); the Tests table row (subtask 3) | 2, 3 |
| `tests/robot_docs.rs` (new) | the end-to-end suite | 3 |

### 2. Fix patterns (subtask 1)

§6.4 of the plan: "`fix_pattern` is a short prose description of what the fix is, for example 'the same command with `-t <candidate>`'". It tells an agent, before it meets an error, what kind of remedy the code's `fix` carries: a command it can run (`fix_argv` set), the same command with a change, or prose it must act on itself.

**Where it is declared.** `src/error/fix_pattern.rs`, declared from `src/error.rs` with `mod fix_pattern;` (A9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9`, meanings and `DetailSpec`s) created the `src/error/` directory beside `src/error.rs`; do not confuse it with `src/errors/`, the Lua error capture):

```rust
impl ErrorCode {
    /// What form this code's fix takes, for every instance (`robot-docs errors`, the guide).
    pub const fn fix_pattern(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Usage => "the corrected command line when a correction is close, else `omaddons help <command>`",
            // … one arm per code, no wildcard …
        }
    }
}
impl WarningCode {
    pub const fn fix_pattern(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::ReloadRequired => "prose: `/reload` in game, or restart the game client",
            // … one arm per code …
            Self::Item(code) => code.fix_pattern(),
        }
    }
}
```

Decided while writing this bead: an exhaustive `match` in its own file, not a column in the `error_codes!` rows, because A9 decided the pattern is not a row column, adding a column would rewrite every row of the `src/error.rs` hot spot a third time (after A9 and A3), and an exhaustive match still makes the fact impossible to forget: a leaf that adds a code gets a compile error until it writes its pattern. It is declared beside the codes (M4-D2), in the error module, so the guide (B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`, the guide renderer and `robot-docs guide`)) reads the same text.

**The style rules** (decided while writing this bead; the plan fixes only the example). A test-only checker `fn check_fix_pattern(text: &str) -> Result<(), &'static str>` enforces 1–6:

1. One line of at most 120 characters (`FIX_PATTERN_MAX_CHARS`, a constant of the test module: a style rule, not a runtime limit, so no `src/limits.rs` row), no tab or newline, no leading, trailing or doubled space.
2. It starts with a lowercase ASCII letter or a backtick and has no final period (it is a phrase, as the plan's example is).
3. It describes the form of every instance's fix, not one instance: values are `<placeholders>` (`<candidate>`, `<id>`, `<tx>`, `<command>`), and "the same command" means the command that failed.
4. #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Serialize)]

pub struct SchemaDoc(pub schemars::Schema);

impl JsonSchema for SchemaDoc {
    fn schema_name() -> Cow<'static, str> { "SchemaDoc".into() }

### 6. `robot-docs errors` (subtask 2)

**Data.**

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Serialize, JsonSchema)]
pub struct ErrorsData {
    /// Every error code, in registry order.
    pub error_codes: Vec<ErrorCodeDoc>,
    /// Every warning code, in registry order (a mirrored item failure carries its error's code, listed above).
    pub warning_codes: Vec<WarningCodeDoc>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Serialize, JsonSchema)]
pub struct ErrorCodeDoc {
    pub code: ErrorCode,
    /// The general exit code of every command but the doctor tree.
    pub exit: u8,
    /// The doctor tree's exit for this code.
    pub doctor_exit: u8,            // present only once E3's doctor dictionary is on `main` (below)
    /// `true`, `false`, or `"conditional"` when each error's own `retryable` decides.
    pub retryable: Retryability,
    /// What the code reports, in one sentence.
    pub meaning: &'static str,
    /// The code's typed `details`, as a JSON Schema fragment.
    pub details_schema: SchemaDoc,
    /// What form the fix takes.
    pub fix_pattern: &'static str,
}

#[derive(Debug, Serialize, JsonSchema)]
pub struct WarningCodeDoc {
    pub code: WarningCode,
    pub meaning: &'static str,
    pub fix_pattern: &'static str,
}
```

- `error_codes` is `ErrorCode::ALL` in order, each row from the code's own accessors: `code.exit().code()`, `code.retryability()`, `code.meaning()`, `code.details_schema()` (wrapped in `SchemaDoc`), `code.fix_pattern()`. `warning_codes` is `WarningCode::ALL` in order (the `Item` variant is no registered code). Decided while writing this bead: registry order rather than sorted by code, because it groups the codes by exit as README's tables do and is what every registry iteration yields; it is deterministic.
- **`doctor_exit`** is `crate::doctor::exit_for(code).code()` (M4-D40, E3's). Decided while writing this bead, as A4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`) decided for `capabilities.error_codes[].doctor_exit`: the key is published by whichever of this bead and E3 lands second. If E3's `doctor::exit_for` is on `main` when subtask 2 lands, the field exists as shown. If it is not, the field is left out of `ErrorCodeDoc` (so out of the data and its schema: a placeholder would publish a fact the build does not have), and subtask 2 adds a comment on E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`) saying that E3's commit adds `doctor_exit` to `robot-docs errors` between `exit` and `retryable`, re-accepts `contract__matrix__robot_docs_errors.snap`, adds the `DOCTOR` column to the human table and updates README's `robot-docs` section. Never compute a doctor exit here: the mapping is declared once, in E3's `exit_for`.
- Every field is always present when it exists (rule 2). The names pass A3's rule test (snake case; plural arrays; `code` is a closed enum through `ErrorCode`'s and `WarningCode`'s schemas).

### 9. What not to do

- Do not generate, edit or post-process a schema here, and never apply the strict transform to output: publish `contract::schema`'s results as they are.
- Do not compute a doctor exit, a meaning or a details schema here: each is declared once elsewhere (E3, A9).
- Do not read `config.toml`, `HOME` or any path; do not resolve a target; do not take a lock.
- Do not snapshot the full listing or the full catalog: every leaf that changes any data type or code would have to re-accept them (Test Plan explains the projections).
- Do not add `Guide` or `InstallSkill` variants, or rows for them.
- Do not add a `details` key, an error or warning code, an action, an event or a volatile key.

| the full listing | `robot-docs schema` | 0 | no snapshot (it changes with every data type); `data` keys, `commands` keys equal to `COMMANDS`, `events` and `files` keys as above |
| unknown path | `robot-docs schema nosuch` | 2 | snapshot `robot_docs_schema_unknown` |
| the catalog | `robot-docs errors` | 0 | snapshot `robot_docs_errors` of a projection: the envelope with `data.error_codes` reduced to the `network` row and `data.warning_codes` to the `reload_required` row (codes no M4 leaf changes), and `log.json("counts", …)` of both list lengths, asserted equal to `ErrorCode::ALL.len()` and `WarningCode::ALL.len()` |
| catalog usage | `robot-docs errors extra` | 2 | snapshot `robot_docs_errors_usage` |
| bare | `robot-docs` | 0 | `command: "help"`, `data.command: "robot-docs"` |
| usage at the parent | `robot-docs --bogus` | 2 | `command: "robot-docs"`, `error.code: "usage"` |

Decided while writing this bead: snapshots of a stable entry and of a projection, never of the full listing or the full catalog, so a leaf that changes an unrelated data type or adds a code does not have to re-accept this bead's snapshots (the full outputs are asserted structurally here and in `tests/robot_docs.rs`).

**`tests/contract/special.rs`**, `read_only_commands_ignore_dry_run_and_reason`: the three new invocations; the flagged runs print the same envelopes and write nothing.

**`tests/robot_docs.rs`** (new, subtask 3; first line `//! e2e suite: robot-docs`, T1's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs) marker, so `argc e2e robot_docs` runs it). Every scenario uses `let log = tlog!();` on a fresh `TestEnv` (or `Home`, where noted), runs every command through `log.run`, and asserts through `Ran`:

1. `schema_lists_every_path_the_envelope_every_event_and_every_file`: step "full listing": `robot-docs schema --json` → `ok()`; `data` keys exactly the four; `commands` keys equal `omaddons::app::COMMANDS` names; `events` keys equal `EventName::ALL` wires; `files` keys equal `contract::schema::file_schemas()` keys and include every `store::KINDS` kind, `journal` and `desired_state`; every entry is an object whose `$schema` is the draft 2020-12 URI; each entry equals the library's schema for it (`omaddons::contract::schema`, serialized), so nothing was added to it, the strict transform's keywords included. `log.json("counts", {commands, events, files, bytes})`; the stdout is under 8 MiB (a test constant, `LISTING_MAX_BYTES`, so an accidental explosion of `$defs` fails here).
2. `schema_of_one_command_gives_exactly_one_entry`: a table of argv forms (`install`; `add`; `backup restore`; `"backup restore"`; `robot-docs schema`; `backup`), one step each: exactly one `commands` key (the expected path), the other three `null`, the entry equal to step 1's listing for that path (fetched once at the start).
3. `every_command_path_has_a_runnable_schema_command`: for every `COMMANDS` row, `robot-docs schema <path words> --json` (the line `capabilities` publishes as `data_schema`) → `ok()`, one entry, the right key; one step per path, so a failure names the path.
4. `an_unknown_path_is_usage_with_the_closest_path_and_the_fix_runs`: a table (`instal`, `backup restor`, `install extra`, `auth` while it has no row, `nosuch`), each a step: `log.tree("home", <TestEnv root>)`; the wrong argv → `fails(2, "usage")`, `retryable: false`, `details` `{}`, `fix_argv` as expected; `log.assert_unchanged("home", …)`; then `log.run` of the `fix_argv` (without its `omaddons`) → `ok()`.
5. `errors_lists_every_code_with_its_facts`: `robot-docs errors --json` → `ok()`; codes in order equal `ErrorCode::ALL` and `WarningCode::ALL` wires; per row, every field equals the library accessor; the set of `"conditional"` codes is exactly the five; each `details_schema` equals the `details` property of `contract::schema::error_variant(code)` (one source, three publications); `log.json("conditional", …)`, `log.json("counts", …)`.
6. `published_schemas_validate_live_output`: fetch `robot-docs schema --json` once; with A3's `Validator` (`#[path = "contract/validate.rs"] mod validate;`), both as published and with `strict = true`, validate the `data` of `status --json`, `list --json`, `help --json`, `robot-docs errors --json`, `robot-docs schema --json` (itself) and `robot-docs schema install --json` against `commands[<envelope command>]`, each envelope with `data` and `error` removed against `envelope`, and every stderr line of `status -v --progress json --json` against `events[<event>]`; a usage failure (`robot-docs schema nosuch --json`) validates its `error` against the envelope schema's error union. Each validation is a step, and a failure logs the instance path, the schema path and the document.
7. `outputs_are_byte_identical_across_runs_and_environments`: `robot-docs schema --json`, `robot-docs schema install --json`, `robot-docs errors --json`, and the human `robot-docs schema install` and `robot-docs errors`, each run twice: JSON stdout equal after `support`-style `meta` removal (or a local helper in the suite), human stdout byte-identical; then once more with `TZ=Asia/Tokyo`, `LANG=C` and another working directory (`Cmd::env`, `Cmd::cwd`): identical again.
8. `human_forms_are_pretty_json_and_a_table`: human `robot-docs schema install` parses as JSON equal to the JSON envelope's `data`; human `robot-docs errors` starts with "Error codes (<ErrorCode::ALL.len()>)", has one line per code, a "Warning codes (<n>)" heading, no ANSI; with `-v`, a `fix:` line after each code line; stderr empty in all of them.
9. `robot_docs_reads_nothing_writes_nothing_and_needs_no_home`: on a `Home` with a client tree: `log.tree` of `<state>`, `<cache>`, `<config>` and the client dirs; `robot-docs schema --json` and `robot-docs errors --json` → `ok()`; `assert_unchanged` for each tree; no `net.log` line added (the `Ran`'s record); then with `HOME=relative/home` (`Cmd::env`): `status --json` fails `usage` (the control) while both `robot-docs` commands succeed with the same stdout as before (`meta` removed); then with a broken `config.toml` planted: both still exit 0 with the same stdout; no stdout contains the `TestEnv` root's path.
10. `bare_robot_docs_is_its_help_until_the_guide_exists`: while `app::command_entry("robot-docs guide")` is `None`: `robot-docs --json` → `ok()`, `command: "help"`, `data.command: "robot-docs"`; human `robot-docs`, `help robot-docs` and `robot-docs --help` print identical stdout, which lists `schema` and `errors`. When B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`, the guide renderer and `robot-docs guide`) has added `robot-docs guide`, the scenario instead asserts `command: "robot-docs guide"` (B1 owns that behaviour; the branch keeps this suite true on both sides of it).

No crash, concurrency or performance matrix belongs to this bead: it adds no protocol, takes no lock and writes nothing.

### Logging

- Every scenario of `tests/robot_docs.rs` and the matrix row use T1's `TestLog`: one `log.step` per phase (named as in the tables above), every command through `log.run` (argv, env overrides, cwd, timing, exit, the parsed envelope, stderr events, `net.log` lines added), `log.json` for every value compared (counts, the conditional set, the resolved key, the fix argv), and `log.tree` / `log.assert_unchanged` for every "changes nothing" claim. On a panic the guard prints `test log: <path>` and the last 20 steps; `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG=verbose` (or `argc e2e robot_docs`) echoes each step live.
- The full listing can exceed T1's 1 MiB per-stream capture: the transcript then records it truncated, with the truncation noted, while assertions read the full stdout from `Ran`.
- Unit tests are table-driven: every case has a name, and every assertion message names the case and shows the input, the expected and the actual value (for a schema, the path inside it and both values).

No checkpoint-only test (real machine, perf budget, compat, live probe) belongs to this bead.

## Considerations

- **Hot spots (§10.5 of the plan) and their rules:**
  - `src/app/mod.rs` (`COMMANDS`, dispatch; A1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1`, per-command facts in `COMMANDS`), A4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`, `omaddons capabilities`), this bead, A7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.7`, `omaddons completions`), B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`, the guide renderer and `robot-docs guide`), B3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3`, `robot-docs install-skill`), D5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`, `omaddons apply`), D9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.9`, `omaddons plans show`), E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, `doctor diagnose`), E4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4`, `doctor health`, `ls`, `capabilities` and `robot-docs`), E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`, `doctor fix`), E7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7`, undo of repairs), E8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.8`, `doctor gc`)): A1 first; each command leaf adds its own rows and rebases. This bead adds three rows before `help`, one `canonical_path` arm and one dispatch arm.
  - `src/cli.rs` (A1, A8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.8`, verbosity levels), C1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.1`, misplaced clients), C2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.2`, a client named as an addon, and `-t all`), D5, E3): one `Command` variant and one help constant; no hook, no `Context` field.
  - `src/error.rs` (A9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9`, meanings and `DetailSpec`s), then A3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`, schemas and live validation); later leaves append rows): subtask 1 adds `mod fix_pattern;` and, unless A4 did first, `Retryability`, `ConditionalTag`, `CONDITIONALLY_RETRYABLE` and `retryability()`, all outside the rows, and at most rewrites the meaning strings of `network` and `io`. Rebase onto peers' new rows and give them fix patterns; never reflow a row.
  - `src/contract/` (A1–A5, A9, A10 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.10`, the semantic manifest), H2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.2`, the golden), H3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3`, the determinism audit)): `SchemaDoc` in A3's `schema.rs`, five rows in A3's `opaque.rs`, inserted in sort order.
  - `omarchy/Model.js` (G1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1`, the widget previews plans) → G2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.2`, the Issues view runs repairs); command leaves add only `CLI_PATHS` rows): three rows.
  - `tests/contract/matrix.rs` and snapshots (append rows; one snapshot file per row), `tests/contract/special.rs` (one table line per path), `tests/cli_skeleton.rs` and the bare-help snapshots (each command leaf re-accepts them; rebase and re-accept, never merge snapshot text by hand), `README.md` (own section only).
- **Why size S holds.** The schemas, the meanings and the specs exist; this bead adds one module, two small functions per code family and the registry touch points. The largest piece of judgement is the 93 fix patterns, which are short and checked by a style test; the starting tables above leave verification, not invention.
- **What could go wrong, and how it shows.**
  - A schema-valued field typed `schemars::Schema` or `serde_json::Value`: the first is closed by A3's strict transform and makes every live `robot-docs schema` envelope fail validation in `support::check`; the second hides its meaning. `SchemaDoc` avoids both, and A3's `OPAQUE` tests fail if a row is missing.
  - The full listing is large (every multi-target command embeds the error union of one variant per code): expect hundreds of KiB to a few MiB on one line. It is generated in memory with no I/O; the suite bounds it at 8 MiB and logs the size, and the close comment records the size and time. An agent that needs one schema asks for one path.
  - A fix pattern that is true of most sites but not all: the starting tables are a draft; the implementer re-reads each code's sites. H1's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, the pre-freeze audit) final walk reviews the texts again.
  - Later leaves change a code's fix: C3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.3`, closest client id) gives `target_not_found` the same command with the closest `-t`, E10 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.10`, the old fixes point at the doctor) points `internal` and `state_corrupt` at the doctor, D5 starts raising `plan_not_found`. The reserved-code guard forces D5; for C3 and E10, add a comment on each of their beads at close saying that their commit updates that code's `fix_pattern` (and its README row), since nothing else would notice.
  - E3 not yet on `main`: `doctor_exit` is left out and E3 is told by a comment to add it (Technical Approach §6).
  - B1 rewires bare `robot-docs` to the guide: only the `None` arm, its `canonical_path` arm and the `robot-docs` row's `data` change, and scenario 10 already branches on it.
- **Compatibility.** Additive: three new command paths and their data keys, plus the published value `"conditional"`. No persisted format, no existing envelope and no existing wire byte changes (the meanings of `network` and `io`, if rewritten, are A9's new texts, not yet frozen or snapshot-pinned outside A9's own snapshot). Older builds are unaffected: nothing is written.
- **Privacy.** The outputs hold only generated schemas and code texts: no path, no account, realm or character, no environment value. Scenario 9 asserts that no output contains the test home's path.
- **Performance.** No I/O, no lock, no discovery: the cost is schema generation (one generator per schema) and serialization. No budget is set by the plan; the suite logs each run's `elapsed_ms`.
- **Previews bind (common rule 16):** not applicable; no path mutates. **Bounded work (rule 15):** not applicable; no input is read. **The guide (rule 17):** not yet; B1 lands after this bead. **The corpus (rule 18):** the three rows, when C4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4`, the run-the-fix corpus) is on `main`.
- **Defaults applied (§8.1 of the plan):** no new code, key or action (1); additive JSON, detail behind `-v` in the table (2); stable order: registry order for codes, sorted maps for schemas (3); no network (4); no write at all (5).
- **Decided while writing this bead** (collected; confirm or adjust each in the close comment): three subtasks for an S leaf, to isolate the `src/error.rs` hot spot; the fix pattern as an exhaustive match in `src/error/fix_pattern.rs`; its seven style rules and the 120-character limit as a test constant; the starting tables; the reserved-code guard; five conditional codes instead of the plan's three, with a source-scan guard, `RUN_LEVEL_OVERRIDES` for `recovery_failed`, and the `network` and `io` meanings saying when; `Retryability`, `ConditionalTag` and `CONDITIONALLY_RETRYABLE` as derive-only types, named as A4's bead names them; reusing A4's declaration if it came first; bare `robot-docs` as `help robot-docs` through an optional subcommand, named `help` in its envelope; one data shape for both `schema` forms with `null`s; top-level keys in declaration order, maps sorted; aliases naming their command; the path resolution rules and fallbacks, with `details` `{}` and `user_verb` when available; `SchemaDoc` in `contract::schema`, reused by A4; the five `OPAQUE` rows; the human forms (exactly the data, pretty; a table with headings, `-` and `-v` fix lines); registry order for codes; `doctor_exit` published by whichever of this bead and E3 lands second (left out until then, as A4 decided for `capabilities`), with a comment on E3; the rows placed before `help`; snapshots of a stable entry and a projection only; the 8 MiB listing bound in the suite; comments on C3 and E10 about their fix patterns.

acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `omaddons robot-docs schema --json` exits 0 with `data` holding exactly `envelope`, `events`, `commands` and `files`: `commands` has one entry for every `app::COMMANDS` path and no other key, `events` one for every `EventName::ALL` name (`progress`, `warning`, `error`, `log`), `files` one for every key of `contract::schema::file_schemas()` (every `store::KINDS` kind, `journal` and `desired_state`), and every entry equals the schema `contract::schema` generates for it (`command_schema`, `envelope_schema`, `event_schemas`, `file_schemas`), with no strict-transform keyword added.
- [ ] `omaddons robot-docs schema install --json` gives one schema: `commands` holds exactly the key `install`, equal to the full listing's entry, and `envelope`, `events` and `files` are `null`; `backup restore` as two words, as one quoted word, and an alias (`add` → `install`) resolve the same way; every `COMMANDS` path's own `omaddons robot-docs schema <path>` command runs and returns that path's entry.
- [ ] An unknown path is `usage` (exit 2, not retryable, `details` `{}`), with the closest path as `fix_argv` (`instal` → `["omaddons","robot-docs","schema","install"]`, `backup restor` → `… backup restore`), the walked row for trailing words (`install extra` → `… install`), the first row under a rowless parent (`auth` → `… auth github`), else `omaddons help robot-docs schema`; each fix runs to exit 0, and the failing run changes nothing.
- [ ] `omaddons robot-docs errors --json` lists every registered error code (`ErrorCode::ALL`, in order) with `code`, `exit`, `doctor_exit` (when E3's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, `doctor diagnose`) doctor dictionary is on `main`; otherwise the key is left out and a comment on omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3 hands it over), `retryable`, `meaning`, `details_schema` and `fix_pattern`, and every warning code (`WarningCode::ALL`, in order) with `code`, `meaning` and `fix_pattern`; a test holds the lists equal to `ErrorCode::ALL` and `WarningCode::ALL` and every value equal to the code's own accessor (`exit().code()`, `doctor::exit_for(code).code()`, `retryability()`, `meaning()`, `details_schema()`, `fix_pattern()`).
- [ ] `retryable` is `true`, `false` or `"conditional"`, and `"conditional"` exactly for `ErrorCode::CONDITIONALLY_RETRYABLE` (`plan_stale`, `http_status`, `hash_mismatch`, `network`, `io`); the source scan `retryable_overrides_are_on_conditional_codes` fails any `.retryable(…)` on a fixed code other than its default, and any unattributed override not in `RUN_LEVEL_OVERRIDES`; every conditional code's meaning says when an instance is retryable.
- [ ] Every error and warning code has a fix pattern that passes the style test (one line of at most 120 characters, lowercase or backtick first, no final period, placeholders in angle brackets, `prose: ` exactly when no site gives a command, `none: ` when there is no fix, no milestone), every backticked `omaddons …` in a pattern names a `COMMANDS` path, and a code whose pattern says it is reserved has no construction site.
- [ ] Both commands' JSON is deterministic: two runs print byte-identical stdout once `meta` is removed, the human forms are byte-identical, and changing `TZ`, `LANG` or the working directory changes nothing.
- [ ] The human form of `robot-docs schema` is the `data` object as pretty JSON; the human form of `robot-docs errors` is a table with one line per code under the headings "Error codes (<n>)" and "Warning codes (<n>)", `-v` adds each code's fix pattern, and neither carries ANSI without a terminal.
- [ ] Both commands read no file and need no `HOME`: with `HOME` relative or unset, and with a broken `config.toml`, they exit 0 with the same output; one run of each on a synthetic home leaves `<state>`, `<cache>`, `<config>` and every client tree hash-identical and adds no `net.log` line; no output contains the test home's path.
- [ ] Bare `omaddons robot-docs` is `help robot-docs` (exit 0, envelope `command: "help"`, the same text as `omaddons help robot-docs` and `omaddons robot-docs --help`) until B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`, the guide renderer and `robot-docs guide`) adds `robot-docs guide`.

**Planning rationale (M4 plan, 2026-10-24).**

**Why this bead.** Today an agent can learn omaddons' output shapes and error codes only from README, which can drift, or by trial and error: no schema is published, and no code has a machine-readable meaning or fix description. After this bead, `omaddons robot-docs schema` prints the JSON Schema of every command's `data`, the envelope, every stderr event and every file omaddons writes, all generated from the code with the serialize contract; `omaddons robot-docs schema <command>` prints one; and `omaddons robot-docs errors` prints every error and warning code with its exit, doctor exit, honest retryability, one-sentence meaning, typed `details` schema and fix pattern. Both read nothing, write nothing and need no `HOME`. It is the publication half of G-M4-1 ("every command's output has a published JSON Schema"), the target every `capabilities` `data_schema` pointer names, and the `robot-docs` tree that B1's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`, the guide renderer and `robot-docs guide`) guide and B3's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3`, `robot-docs install-skill`) `install-skill` join.

**Decisions applied.**

- **M4-D2:** one registry; a fact clap cannot give is declared once beside what it describes. This bead publishes A3's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`, schemas and live validation) schemas, A9's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9`, meanings and `DetailSpec`s) meanings and specs and E3's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, `doctor diagnose`) doctor exits without recomputing any of them, and declares the one new fact, the fix pattern, beside the codes (an exhaustive match a new code cannot skip), where the guide reads it too.
- **M4-D9:** draft 2020-12, the serialize contract, one generator per schema, `{envelope, events, commands, files}` with sorted maps, one entry for one path; published schemas stay open (strictness is a test-side transform). Rejected there: one shared generator, the deserialize contract, `preserve_order`.
- **M4-D10 (context):** `details_schema` is A9's `DetailSpec` fragment, the same one A3's error union carries.
- **Appendix A.1:** retryability per code is `true`, `false` or `"conditional"`; every error instance keeps its boolean.
- **M4-D40 (context):** `doctor_exit` from E3's total `exit_for`, declared once there.
- **M4-D15, M4-D18, M4-D55, M4-D56 (context):** the unknown-path fix runs; repeated runs are byte-identical; the new shapes pass A3's rule test; member order is not contract.
- **DEC-1:** every registry touch point in the commit that adds the command; no stub for `guide` or `install-skill`.

**Decided while writing this bead** (each confirmed or adjusted in the close comment): three subtasks for an S leaf (the `src/error.rs` hot spot isolated; the end-to-end suite separate); the fix pattern as an exhaustive match in `src/error/fix_pattern.rs` with seven style rules and starting tables for all 93 codes; a reserved-code guard; five conditional codes instead of the plan's three, because `network` and `io` instances also differ from their default at `c0ab5e9`, held by a source scan and named as A4's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`, `omaddons capabilities`) bead names them (`Retryability`, `ConditionalTag`, `CONDITIONALLY_RETRYABLE`, `RUN_LEVEL_OVERRIDES`); bare `robot-docs` as `help robot-docs` through an optional subcommand; one data shape with `null`s for one path; aliases naming their command; the path-resolution fallbacks; `SchemaDoc`, a structurally open newtype, so A3's strict validation of this command's own envelopes passes; five `OPAQUE` rows; pretty JSON and a table as the human forms; registry order; `doctor_exit` left out until E3 is on `main` (as A4 decided for `capabilities`); snapshots of a stable entry and a projection only.

**Alternatives rejected here.**

- A fix-pattern column in the code rows: a third rewrite of every row of a hot spot, for no gain over an exhaustive match.
- Publishing `network` and `io` as plain booleans: the lie Appendix A.1 exists to prevent.
- A required subcommand for `robot-docs`: bare `robot-docs` would be a usage error, not `help robot-docs` as the plan says, and the corpus fix `omaddons robot-docs` would exit 2.
- Typing the schema fields `schemars::Schema` (closed by A3's strict transform, so every live envelope would fail validation) or `serde_json::Value` (open, but it hides what it holds).
- A different shape for one path (`{command, schema}`): two shapes on one command path, and a different jq path per form.
- Snapshotting the full listing or catalog: every leaf that changes any data type or adds a code would re-accept them.
- A `null` placeholder for `doctor_exit` before E3: a value for a fact the build does not have, and a nullable field to narrow later.

**Risks and how they are watched.** No §11.4 risk is this bead's. The concrete risks are a fix pattern that is not true of every site (watched by the style and command-path tests, the reserved-code guard, a re-read of each code's sites against the starting tables, and H1's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, the pre-freeze audit) final walk), the published schemas failing their own strict validation (watched by `SchemaDoc`, the `OPAQUE` rows and A3's tests), and the listing's size (bounded at 8 MiB in the suite and recorded at close). Later fix changes (C3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.3`, the closest client id), E10 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.10`, the old fixes point at the doctor), D5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`, `omaddons apply`)) are handed over by comments and by the reserved-code guard.

**What it unblocks, and why they wait.** B1 adds `robot-docs guide` to the tree this bead creates (DEC-1: the tree's first leaf creates it) and quotes its fix patterns. A6's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.6`, bare help's discovery line) discovery line may name only commands that exist. H1 audits every wire shape and walks these two outputs. T2's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.2`, the slice-1 demo) slice-1 demo runs `robot-docs schema` over the whole matrix and every envelope snapshot.

**How it serves the milestone.** G-M4-1: the schemas and the catalog come from the binary, generated, so an agent needs no README. G-M4-2: a mistyped path's fix runs. G-M4-5: deterministic outputs that the manifest and the golden pin. Checkpoint criterion 2 ("`robot-docs schema` gives a JSON Schema for every command path …, for the envelope and for every NDJSON event"; "`robot-docs errors` lists every error code with its exit, retryability, meaning and its typed `details` specification") is this bead's to show.

**Confidence.** High. The command is a thin, pure layer over registries that A3 and A9 build and test; the only judgement is in the fix-pattern texts and the honest retryability, both pinned by tests.

title: A fix pattern for every code, and the code registry's three-valued retryability
description:
Part 1 of 3 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5 (`robot-docs schema` and `robot-docs errors`). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

**The leaf.** A5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5`) adds `omaddons robot-docs schema [<command>]` (the JSON Schema of every command's `data`, the envelope, the stderr events and the files) and `omaddons robot-docs errors` (the error and warning catalog), the machine-readable half of vision §5.10's `robot-docs`. It serves G-M4-1 ("an agent with no prior knowledge learns everything it needs from the binary itself … every fact in those outputs is generated from the code") and checkpoint criterion 2 ("`robot-docs errors` lists every error code with its exit, retryability, meaning and its typed `details` specification").

**This part.** `robot-docs errors` publishes, per code, two facts that no registry holds yet:

- a **fix pattern**: §6.4 of the plan, "`fix_pattern` is a short prose description of what the fix is, for example 'the same command with `-t <candidate>`'", for every error and warning code. A9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9`, a meaning and a typed `DetailSpec` for every code) decided it is A5's to declare and is not a column of the code rows;
- an honest **retryability per code**: Appendix A.1 of the plan, "`retryable`, per code, is `true`, `false` or `"conditional"`. The last is for `plan_stale`, `http_status` and `hash_mismatch`, whose instances decide … a boolean would lie for those three. Every error instance keeps a boolean `error.retryable`, as today. The tri-state appears only in the code registry (`capabilities`, `robot-docs errors`, the manifest's `error` nodes)."

M4-D2 requires each such fact to be declared exactly once, beside the code it describes, with a test that cross-checks it, so `capabilities` (A4, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`), `robot-docs errors` (this leaf's next part) and the guide (B1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`, whose `{{errors_common}}` block shows "exit, retryability and the fix pattern") read one source. This part declares both in the error module and tests them, and changes no output: nothing serializes them until subtask 2 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5.2).

It is its own step because it is the only part of the leaf that touches `src/error.rs`, a collision hot spot (A9 and A3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`, schemas and live validation) rewrote every row; D4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`, the plan store), D5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`, `omaddons apply`), E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, `doctor diagnose`), E10 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.10`, the old fixes point at the doctor), the F leaves and H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, the pre-freeze audit) append rows or edit fixes). Landing it alone keeps that window short, and the command can then be built without touching the file.

**Facts this part relies on** (as of `c0ab5e9`, plus A9 and A3, both landed before this leaf can start):

- `error_codes!` rows (`src/error.rs:149-204`, 41 codes) generate `ErrorCode::ALL`, `wire()`, `exit()` and `default_retryable()` (`:122-145`); `warning_codes!` rows (`src/error.rs:245-349`, 52 codes) generate `WarningCode` with an extra untagged `Item(ErrorCode)` (a mirrored item failure, whose wire name is its error's), excluded from `WarningCode::ALL` (`:224-232`). After A9, each row also carries a meaning (`meaning()`) and, for errors, a `DetailSpec`; A9 created `src/error/` (`detail_spec.rs`, `specs.rs`, a `#[cfg(test)]` `sentence.rs`) declared from `src/error.rs`. Do not confuse `src/error/` with `src/errors/` (the Lua error capture).
- A `Warning`'s fix is optional (`Warning.fix: Option<Suggestion>`, `src/error.rs:661-665`), serialized as `fix: null` when absent (`WarningBody`, `:696-701`). An `Error` always has a fix: `Suggestion::command(argv)` (with `fix_argv`) or `Suggestion::text(display)` (prose, `fix_argv: null`) (`src/error.rs:385-420`).
- Retryability decided per instance: `Error::http_status` (5xx only, `src/error.rs:580-584`), `Error::plan_stale` (`PlanStaleSource::Replan` only, `:587-593`), `Error::hash_mismatch` (first attempt only, `:597-599`). Instances that override their code's registered default: `network` (registered `true`) set `false` for more than 5 redirects (`src/net/guard.rs:343`) and for an undecodable `Content-Encoding` (`src/net/decode.rs:68`); `io` (registered `false`) set `true` when `WTF/` changed or failed while a backup copied it (`src/backup/tree.rs:158`, `:165`); `hash_mismatch` set `false` for a cached blob (`src/engine/blobs.rs:296`). README's error table already says so for `network` and `io` (`README.md:1853`, `:1866`). One run-level override applies to any code: `recovery_failed` (`src/engine/tx.rs:573-578`) sets `error.retryable = false` (`:578`) on a commit's error whose in-process recovery failed too.
- `src/source_scan.rs` (`production_code`, `sources`) is `#[cfg(test)]` in the library (`src/lib.rs:37-38`) and usable by unit tests in `src/` only.
- A9's `conditional_retryability_is_stated` test checks that the meanings of `http_status`, `hash_mismatch` and `plan_stale` say when an instance is retryable; A9's meaning rules: one sentence, uppercase or backtick first, one closing period, at most 200 characters, names no command or milestone.
- A3 provides `contract::schema::generator()` (draft 2020-12, serialize contract), used here to test the new type's schema.

## Technical Approach

### 1. `src/error/fix_pattern.rs` (new)

Declared from `src/error.rs` with `mod fix_pattern;` beside A9's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9`, meanings and `DetailSpec`s) module declarations. It holds two inherent impls (Rust allows them in any module of the crate):

```rust
//! What form each code's fix takes (`robot-docs errors`, the guide): one phrase per code,
//! declared once beside the codes (M4-D2). An exhaustive match: a new code does not
//! compile until its pattern is written.

impl super::ErrorCode {
    pub const fn fix_pattern(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Usage => "the corrected command line when a correction is close, else `omaddons help <command>`, or prose for `HOME`",
            // … one arm per code, no wildcard …
        }
    }
}

impl super::WarningCode {
    pub const fn fix_pattern(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::ReloadRequired => "prose: `/reload` in game, or restart the game client",
            // … one arm per code, no wildcard …
            Self::Item(code) => code.fix_pattern(),
        }
    }
}
```

Decided while writing this bead: an exhaustive `match` in its own file, not a column in the `error_codes!` and `warning_codes!` rows, because A9 decided the pattern is no row column, a column would rewrite every row of the hot spot a third time, and the exhaustive match still makes the fact impossible to forget (a new code is a compile error until its arm exists).

**The style rules** (decided while writing this bead; the plan fixes only its example). A test-only `fn check_fix_pattern(text: &str) -> Result<(), &'static str>` in the file's test module enforces 1–6:

1. One line of at most 120 characters (`FIX_PATTERN_MAX_CHARS`, a constant of the test module: a style rule, not a runtime limit, so no `src/limits.rs` row), no tab or newline, no leading, trailing or doubled space.
2. It starts with a lowercase ASCII letter or a backtick and has no final period (a phrase, as the plan's example is).
3. It describes the form every instance's fix takes, not one instance: values are `<placeholders>` (`<candidate>`, `<id>`, `<tx>`, `<command>`), and "the same command" means the command that failed.
4. It starts with `prose: ` exactly when no construction site of the code gives a command (every instance's `fix_argv` is `null`); a code with both kinds names the command form first and the prose after it. It starts with `none: ` when there is no fix: a warning whose sites pass no fix (`none: this warning carries no fix`) or a code no site raises yet (`none: no command raises it yet`).

### 2. Three-valued retryability (`src/error.rs`, outside the rows)

```rust
/// Whether a code's errors can be retried, as the registry publishes it (capabilities,
/// robot-docs errors, the manifest): `true`, `false`, or "conditional" where each instance decides.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, JsonSchema)]
#[serde(untagged)]
pub enum Retryability { Fixed(bool), Conditional(ConditionalTag) }

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, JsonSchema)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum ConditionalTag { Conditional }

impl ErrorCode {
    /// The codes whose construction sites decide retryability per instance.
    pub const CONDITIONALLY_RETRYABLE: &[ErrorCode] = &[ErrorCode::Network, ErrorCode::HttpStatus,
        ErrorCode::HashMismatch, ErrorCode::PlanStale, ErrorCode::Io];
    /// `Conditional` for the list above, else `Fixed(default_retryable())`.
    pub const fn retryability(self) -> Retryability;
}
```
