title: E2E: `tests/robot_docs.rs`, the published schemas and the catalog end to end
description:
Part 3 of 3 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5 (`robot-docs schema` and `robot-docs errors`). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

**The leaf.** A5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5`) adds `omaddons robot-docs schema [<command>]` and `omaddons robot-docs errors`, the binary's machine-readable documentation (vision §5.10): every command's data schema, the envelope's, every stderr event's and every file's, and the full error and warning catalog with meanings, exits, retryability, typed `details` schemas and fix patterns. It serves G-M4-1 ("an agent with no prior knowledge learns everything it needs from the binary itself"), G-M4-2 (a mistyped path's fix runs) and G-M4-5 (byte-identical repeats), and checkpoint criteria 2 and 14 (last line, for its paths).

**This part** proves the leaf's acceptance criteria against the real binary, in ten logged scenarios a developer can read step by step when one regresses: the listing is complete and equal to the library's schemas; one path gives one entry; every path's own schema command (the line `capabilities` publishes as `data_schema`) runs; an unknown path's fix runs; the catalog equals the registries; the published schemas, fetched from the binary, validate live output; repeats and other environments give the same bytes; the human forms; the commands read, write and request nothing and need no `HOME`; and bare `robot-docs` is its help until the guide exists. It is its own step because it is new integration code on T1's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`) `TestLog`, over the command subtask 2 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5.2) ships.

**What the scenarios rely on** (from subtasks 1 and 2, and the leaf's blockers):

- The commands: `robot-docs schema [<COMMAND>...]` gives `data: {envelope, events, commands, files}` (the full listing) or, for one path, `commands` with that one entry and the other three `null`; an alias names its command (`add` → `install`); an unknown path is `usage` (exit 2, not retryable, `details` `{}`) with the fix `omaddons robot-docs schema <closest path>` (Levenshtein ≤ 2 over `COMMANDS` paths and top-level aliases), else the walked row (`install extra` → `install`), else the first row under a rowless parent (`auth` → `auth github`), else `omaddons help robot-docs schema`. `robot-docs errors` gives `data: {error_codes: [{code, exit, doctor_exit, retryable, meaning, details_schema, fix_pattern}], warning_codes: [{code, meaning, fix_pattern}]}` in registry order, `retryable` being `true`, `false` or `"conditional"` (conditional exactly for `plan_stale`, `http_status`, `hash_mismatch`, `network`, `io`), `doctor_exit` from E3's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, `doctor diagnose`) `doctor::exit_for`, present only once E3 is on `main` (until then the key is absent). Human forms: `schema` prints its data as pretty JSON; `errors` prints a table headed "Error codes (<n>)" and "Warning codes (<n>)", `-v` adding a `      fix: <pattern>` line per code. Bare `robot-docs` is `help robot-docs` (envelope `command: "help"`) until B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`) adds `robot-docs guide`.
- The library (the test crate links `omaddons`): `omaddons::app::COMMANDS`, `app::command_entry`; `omaddons::contract::schema::{command_schema, command_schemas, envelope_schema, error_variant, event_schemas, file_schemas}` (A3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`); `omaddons::contract::events::EventName::ALL` (A2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.2`); `omaddons::state::store::KINDS` rows with their `kind`; `omaddons::error::{ErrorCode, WarningCode}` with `meaning()`, `details_schema()`, `fix_pattern()`, `retryability()`.
- A3's validator: `tests/contract/validate.rs` (`Validator::new(&schema, strict) -> Result<Validator, String>`, `validate(&instance) -> Vec<Failure>` with instance and schema paths, and `strict(&schema)`), includable from another suite with `#[path = "contract/validate.rs"] mod validate;`.
- T1's `TestLog` (`tests/common/tlog.rs`): `tlog!()`, `log.step(label)`, `log.note(text)`, `log.json(label, &value)`, `log.assert_eq(label, &actual, &expected)`, `log.run(&runner, argv) -> Ran` (argv without the binary name, used verbatim: add `--json` yourself), `log.cmd(&runner, argv).env(k, v).cwd(dir).run()`, `log.tree(label, root)`, `log.assert_unchanged(label, root)`, `log.env(&runner)`; `Ran::{ok(), exit(n), fails(exit, code), envelope(), data(), error_code(), events(), stdout(), stderr()}` and `Ran.run` (a `common::home::Run`); the record of every run includes the `net.log` lines it added; the drop guard prints `test log: <path>` and the last 20 steps on a panic; `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG=verbose` echoes steps live; `argc e2e [FILTER]` runs every suite whose first line is `//! e2e suite: <name>`. Each stream is captured into the log up to 1 MiB (truncation noted); `Ran` holds the full output.
- The homes: `TestEnv` (a synthetic home under `CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR`, `TZ=UTC`, its own `HOME` and XDG dirs; `config()`, `state()`, `cache()`, `root()`), and `common::home::Home` (a `TestEnv` with clients and replayed HTTP fixtures) for scenario 9.

## Technical Approach

`tests/robot_docs.rs` (new), first line `//! e2e suite: robot-docs`, with `mod common;` and `#[path = "contract/validate.rs"] mod validate;`. Shared helpers in the file: `fn listing(log, env) -> Value` (runs `robot-docs schema --json` once, `ok()`, returns `data`), `fn without_meta(stdout) -> String` (the envelope with `meta` removed, re-serialized; or reuse the contract suite's if it is shared), `fn words(path: &str) -> Vec<&str>`, and `const LISTING_MAX_BYTES: usize = 8 << 20` (a test bound, not a `src/limits.rs` constant). B3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3`, `robot-docs install-skill`) later adds its `install_skill_*` tests to this file.

Every scenario: `let log = tlog!();` on a fresh `TestEnv::new()` (scenario 9 on a `Home`), every command through `log.run` or `log.cmd`, every compared value through `log.json` or `log.assert_eq`.

1. **`schema_lists_every_path_the_envelope_every_event_and_every_file`.** Step "full listing": `robot-docs schema --json` → `ok()`. Assert: `data` keys are exactly `envelope`, `events`, `commands`, `files`; `commands` keys equal `COMMANDS` names; `events` keys equal `EventName::ALL` wire names; `files` keys equal `file_schemas()` keys and contain every `store::KINDS` kind, `journal` and `desired_state`; every entry is an object with `"$schema": "https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/schema"`; every entry equals the library's (`command_schema(entry)`, `envelope_schema()`, `event_schemas()`, `file_schemas()`, serialized to `Value`), so nothing was added to it, the strict transform included. `log.json("counts", {commands, events, files, bytes: stdout.len()})`; `stdout.len() < LISTING_MAX_BYTES`.
2. **`schema_of_one_command_gives_exactly_one_entry`.** Step "listing" (helper). Then one step per form: `["robot-docs","schema","install"]` → key `install`; `["robot-docs","schema","add"]` → `install`; `["robot-docs","schema","backup","restore"]` and `["robot-docs","schema","backup restore"]` → `backup restore`; `["robot-docs","schema","robot-docs","schema"]` → `robot-docs schema`; `["robot-docs","schema","backup"]` → `backup`; each with `--json`, `ok()`, exactly one `commands` key, `envelope`, `events` and `files` `null`, the entry equal to the listing's.
3. **`every_command_path_has_a_runnable_schema_command`.** One step per `COMMANDS` row (labelled with the path): `robot-docs schema <path words> --json` → `ok()`, exactly the key of that path. This is the line `capabilities` (A4, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`) publishes as each command's `data_schema`, so it must run for every path.
4. **`an_unknown_path_is_usage_with_the_closest_path_and_the_fix_runs`.** A table of cases, one step each, on one home: `log.tree("home", env.root())` first; then per case the wrong argv with `--json` → `fails(2, "usage")`, `error.retryable == false`, `error.details == {}`, `error.fix_argv` as expected; `log.assert_unchanged("home", env.root())`; then `log.run` of the fix (its `fix_argv` without the leading `omaddons`, plus `--json`) → `ok()`. Cases: `instal` → `["omaddons","robot-docs","schema","install"]`; `backup restor` → `[…,"backup","restore"]`; `install extra` → `[…,"install"]`; `auth` → `[…,"auth","github"]` (only while `app::command_entry("auth")` is `None`); `nosuch` → `["omaddons","help","robot-docs","schema"]`.
5. **`errors_lists_every_code_with_its_facts`.** `robot-docs errors --json` → `ok()`. Assert: `error_codes[].code` equals `ErrorCode::ALL` wire names in order and `warning_codes[].code` `WarningCode::ALL`'s; for every error row, `exit == code.exit().code()`, `retryable == serde_json::to_value(code.retryability())` (`Retryability`: `Fixed(bool)` or `Conditional(ConditionalTag)`), `meaning == code.meaning()`, `details_schema == code.details_schema()`, `fix_pattern == code.fix_pattern()`, `doctor_exit` equal to `doctor::exit_for(code).code()` when E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, `doctor diagnose`) is on `main`, else absent from every row; for every warning row, `meaning` and `fix_pattern` likewise; the codes whose `retryable` is `"conditional"` are exactly `ErrorCode::CONDITIONALLY_RETRYABLE` (`plan_stale`, `http_status`, `hash_mismatch`, `network`, `io`); each `details_schema` equals the `details` property of `error_variant(code)` (the error union of the envelope schema), so the three publications share one source. `log.json("conditional", …)`, `log.json("counts", …)`.
6. **`published_schemas_validate_live_output`.** Step "listing" (helper; keep the published schemas). Then for each of `status --json`, `list --json`, `help --json`, `robot-docs errors --json`, `robot-docs schema --json` and `robot-docs schema install --json`: one step that builds `Validator::new(&published.commands[<envelope command>], false)` and `…, true)` and validates the envelope's `data` with both, and validates the envelope with `data` and `error` removed against `published.envelope` with both. Then `status -v --progress json --json`: every stderr line (`Ran::events()`) against `published.events[<line.event>]`, both ways. Then `robot-docs schema nosuch --json` (exit 2): its envelope against `published.envelope` (which holds the error union). Each failure is logged with its instance path, schema path and the document (`log.json`), and the step fails with the first ten. A schema the strict transform refuses fails the step with A3's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`, schemas and live validation) message (that would be a defect in A3's transform, filed `discovered-from` this bead).
7. **`outputs_are_byte_identical_across_runs_and_environments`.** For `robot-docs schema --json`, `robot-docs schema install --json`, `robot-docs errors --json`, and the human `robot-docs schema install` and `robot-docs errors`: run twice (JSON compared with `meta` removed, human byte for byte); then a third time through `log.cmd(…).env("TZ", "Asia/Tokyo").env("LANG", "C").cwd(<another directory under the TestEnv root>)`: equal again. `log.json` of each pair's lengths and equality.
8. **`human_forms_are_pretty_json_and_a_table`.** Human `robot-docs schema install` → `ok()`; stdout parses as JSON equal to the `--json` envelope's `data`; it has more than one line. Human `robot-docs errors` → `ok()`; the first line is `Error codes (<ErrorCode::ALL.len()>)`; one line per error code and per warning code; a `Warning codes (<WarningCode::ALL.len()>)` heading; no `\u{1b}`; with `-v`, a line starting `      fix: ` after each code line, the code lines otherwise identical. stderr is empty in every run.
9. **`robot_docs_reads_nothing_writes_nothing_and_needs_no_home`.** On a `Home` with clients (`common::home::Home` and its usual builder): `log.tree` of `<state>`, `<cache>`, `<config>` and each client dir; `robot-docs schema --json` and `robot-docs errors --json` → `ok()`, each run's record showing no `net.log` line added; `log.assert_unchanged` on every tree. Then with `HOME=relative/home` (`log.cmd(…).env("HOME", "relative/home")`): `status --json` → `fails(2, "usage")` (the control: a command that needs `HOME`), while both `robot-docs` commands → `ok()` with stdout equal (meta removed) to the earlier runs. Then plant a `config.toml` that does not parse (`<config>/omaddons/config.toml` with `[[[`): both still `ok()` and equal. No stdout of any run contains the `TestEnv` root's absolute path.
10. **`bare_robot_docs_is_its_help_until_the_guide_exists`.** If `app::command_entry("robot-docs guide")` is `None`: `robot-docs --json` → `ok()`, `envelope.command == "help"`, `data.command == "robot-docs"`; the human `robot-docs`, `help robot-docs` and `robot-docs --help` print identical stdout, which names `schema` and `errors`. Otherwise (B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`, the guide renderer and `robot-docs guide`) on `main`): `robot-docs --json`'s `command` is `robot-docs guide` (B1 owns that behaviour and its own tests); log which branch ran.

**README** (`README.md:2619-2640`, the Tests table): add the row `| tests/robot_docs.rs | robot-docs schema and robot-docs errors end to end: every path, the envelope, the events and the files listed and equal to the library's schemas; one path's entry and every path's own schema command; unknown paths' fixes run; the catalog equal to the registries; the published schemas validating live output, strictly too; byte-identical repeats in other environments; no reads, writes or requests, and no HOME needed |` (in the file's backtick style).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `tests/robot_docs.rs` exists, starts with `//! e2e suite: robot-docs`, and its ten scenarios pass in the gate, each through T1's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs) `TestLog` with a transcript: `schema_lists_every_path_the_envelope_every_event_and_every_file`, `schema_of_one_command_gives_exactly_one_entry`, `every_command_path_has_a_runnable_schema_command`, `an_unknown_path_is_usage_with_the_closest_path_and_the_fix_runs`, `errors_lists_every_code_with_its_facts`, `published_schemas_validate_live_output`, `outputs_are_byte_identical_across_runs_and_environments`, `human_forms_are_pretty_json_and_a_table`, `robot_docs_reads_nothing_writes_nothing_and_needs_no_home`, `bare_robot_docs_is_its_help_until_the_guide_exists`.
- [ ] The listing's entries equal the library's schemas, its keys cover every `COMMANDS` path, `EventName::ALL` and `file_schemas()`, and its size is under 8 MiB and logged.
- [ ] Every `COMMANDS` path's `robot-docs schema <path>` runs and returns one entry; every unknown-path case fails with the expected `fix_argv`, changes nothing, and its fix exits 0.
- [ ] The catalog's rows equal the registries' accessors, the conditional set is exactly the five codes, and each `details_schema` equals the `details` of its code's variant in the error union.
- [ ] The published schemas validate the live `data`, frames and stderr events listed in scenario 6, as published and under the strict transform.
- [ ] Repeats, and runs with another `TZ`, `LANG` and working directory, are byte-identical (`meta` aside for JSON); the human forms are pretty JSON and the table; neither command reads `HOME`, a broken `config.toml`, or the network, or changes any tree.
- [ ] `argc e2e robot_docs` runs the suite with verbose logs and prints the log root.
- [ ] README's Tests table has the `tests/robot_docs.rs` row, in this commit.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes and `ubs` is clean on the changed files; the close comment quotes the test names, the commit, the listing's size and the log root.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

None new: this part adds an integration suite. The unit tests of the command are subtask 2's (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5.2), and those of the fix patterns and retryability subtask 1's (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5.1).

### Integration and end-to-end tests

`tests/robot_docs.rs`, the ten scenarios of Technical Approach, each on its own fresh home (a `TestEnv`, or a `Home` for scenario 9), with the steps, commands and assertions listed there. Summary of what each asserts after each command:

| Scenario | Commands | Asserted |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `robot-docs schema --json` | exit 0; the four keys; key sets equal to `COMMANDS`, `EventName::ALL`, `file_schemas()`; entries equal to the library's; `$schema` draft 2020-12; size < 8 MiB |
| 2 | six one-path forms | exit 0; one `commands` key, the expected path; three `null`s; entry equal to the listing's |
| 3 | one per `COMMANDS` row | exit 0; one key, that path |
| 4 | five unknown paths, then each fix | exit 2, `usage`, not retryable, `details` `{}`, the expected `fix_argv`; home tree unchanged; the fix exits 0 |
| 5 | `robot-docs errors --json` | codes and order equal `ALL`; every field equal to its accessor; conditional set; `details_schema` equal to the error union's |
| 6 | six commands, one `-v --progress json` run, one usage failure | `data` valid against `commands[<command>]`, frames against `envelope`, events against `events[<event>]`, published and strict |
| 7 | five commands ×3 (two plain, one with `TZ`, `LANG`, cwd changed) | identical stdout (`meta` aside for JSON) |
| 8 | human `schema install`, human `errors`, `errors -v` | pretty JSON equal to `data`; the table's headings and lines; `fix:` lines; no ANSI; empty stderr |
| 9 | `schema`, `errors`, `status` (control), with `HOME` relative and a broken `config.toml` | trees unchanged; no `net.log` line; `status` fails `usage` while both succeed with unchanged output; no absolute test path in any output |
| 10 | bare `robot-docs` (JSON and human), `help robot-docs`, `robot-docs --help` | `command: "help"` and identical texts while there is no `robot-docs guide`; `robot-docs guide` otherwise |

No crash, concurrency or performance matrix belongs here: the commands take no lock and write nothing.

### Logging

- Every scenario uses T1's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs) `TestLog`: one `log.step` per phase (the labels name the case or the path), every command through `log.run` or `log.cmd` (argv, environment overrides such as `HOME`, `TZ`, `LANG`, the working directory, timing, exit, the parsed envelope, stderr events, the `net.log` lines added), `log.json` or `log.assert_eq` for every value compared (key sets, counts, the conditional set, the resolved key, each `fix_argv`, each validation failure with its instance path, schema path and document), and `log.tree` / `log.assert_unchanged` for every "changes nothing" claim, which on a difference logs the first differing paths.
- The full listing may pass T1's 1 MiB capture per stream: the transcript records it truncated, with the truncation noted; assertions read the full stdout from `Ran`.
- On a panic the guard prints `test log: <path>` and the last 20 steps; `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG=verbose` or `argc e2e robot_docs` echoes every step live.

No checkpoint-only test belongs to this part.

## Considerations

- **Keep the suite fast.** Scenario 3 runs the binary once per `COMMANDS` path (about 45 today, more as M4 adds commands); each run generates one schema in memory, so the scenario stays around a second. Scenario 1 and the listing helper run the full listing; fetch it once per scenario.
- **Independence from later leaves.** The suite reads every expected set from the library (`COMMANDS`, `EventName::ALL`, `file_schemas()`, `ErrorCode::ALL`, `WarningCode::ALL`), never a literal list, so a leaf that adds a command, an event, a file kind or a code changes nothing here. Scenario 4's `auth` case and scenario 10 branch on the registry (`command_entry`) for the same reason, and scenario 5 follows whether E3's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, `doctor diagnose`) doctor dictionary is on `main`.
- **What a failure means.** A key-set or equality failure in scenarios 1, 2, 3 or 5 is a defect of subtask 2; a validation failure in scenario 6 is a mismatch between a command's output and its schema, which A3's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`, schemas and live validation) live validation should have caught first: fix it where it lives (the schema or the emitter, by A3's mismatch policy) and say so in the close comment.
- **Privacy:** synthetic homes only (`TestEnv`, `Home`); scenario 9 checks that no output carries the home's path.
- **Hot spot:** `README.md`'s Tests table (each suite adds its own row). `tests/robot_docs.rs` is new; B3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3`, `robot-docs install-skill`) later appends to it.

## Dependencies

Parent: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5 (`robot-docs schema` and `robot-docs errors`). It starts when the parent's blockers are closed: A3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`, whose generators and `tests/contract/validate.rs` it uses) and A9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9`). Also blocked by T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs), whose `TestLog` every scenario uses.

- **Before it:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5.2, the command it tests (and through it omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5.1).
- **After it:** nothing inside omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5; the agent closing this part, if it is the last open one, verifies the leaf's acceptance criteria and closes omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5, which unblocks B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`), A6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.6`), H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`) and T2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.2`).

title: Bare help's discovery line and `help --json` `discovery`
description:
## Background

**What this is.** Bare `omaddons` is the first command an agent guesses. The vision's CLI contract (vision §5.9) says what it must answer: "Bare `omaddons` prints concise help to stdout and exits 0. The help lists the most common verbs, the discovery trio (§5.10) and the exit-code table. It never runs an action, never opens a pager or TUI, and never prompts. Bare `omaddons --json` prints the same information as JSON." The discovery trio (vision §5.10) is `omaddons capabilities --json`, `omaddons doctor --json` and `omaddons robot-docs guide`: the three commands from which an agent with no prior knowledge learns what the tool can do, how to use it safely, and what is broken.

At `c0ab5e9` none of the three commands exists, so bare help lists the verbs, a "Start with" sentence and the exit codes, and nothing else. This bead adds the trio once its three commands exist:

- one line in the human form, after the "Start with" sentence, naming the three commands;
- `discovery: [{command, argv, purpose}]` in bare `help --json`, an additive key;
- the "Start with" sentence, 116 columns today, wrapped to `MAX_WIDTH` like the group lines.

The tail of bare help after this bead (the group lines above it depend on which command leaves have landed and are not this bead's):

```text
Start with `omaddons status`. Run `omaddons help <command>` for details; add
--json for one JSON envelope on stdout.
Agents: omaddons capabilities --json · omaddons robot-docs guide
        omaddons doctor --json

Exit codes:
  0  ok            Success, including partial success (partial: true)
  …
```

**It lands late by design.** Bare help must never name a command this build does not have, so this bead waits for the four leaves that add the line's commands:
- A4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`, `omaddons capabilities`) adds `capabilities`;
- A5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5`, `robot-docs schema` and `robot-docs errors`) creates the `robot-docs` tree;
- B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`, the guide renderer and `robot-docs guide`) adds `robot-docs guide` to that tree;
- E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, `doctor diagnose` and `explain`: runtime, run directories, the doctor envelope and its exit dictionary) adds `doctor`.

**The milestone goals it serves.**
- **G-M4-1, self-describing:** an agent with no prior knowledge learns everything it needs from the binary itself, in at most three calls (`omaddons capabilities --json`, `omaddons robot-docs guide`, `omaddons status --json`), and every fact in those outputs is generated from the code. Bare help is where an agent that knows nothing lands; this line hands it the first two of those calls, and `status` is already the "Start with" sentence.
- **G-M4-2, the first guess works:** the most likely first guess, bare `omaddons`, answers with where to go next.
- **G-M4-5, frozen and enforced:** at the first tag the contract is audited and pinned. `discovery[]` is a new wire shape, so it must exist before H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, the pre-freeze contract audit) walks the contract and H2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.2`, the golden and the released baseline) pins it.

**The checkpoint criteria it serves.**
- **14, the contract is frozen:** the pre-freeze audit is recorded; the golden passes (the semantic manifest of every input and output); repeated runs of every command path print identical bytes. This bead adds a key the audit and the golden must see, and its content is static, so repeats are byte-identical.
- **17, gate and checkpoint runs:** `argc gate --all` passes from a clean checkout.
- **18, README and vision:** README describes exactly what exists. This bead updates README's `help` section in the same commit.

**How it serves the vision.** Vision goal G4, agent ergonomics: "the first command an agent guesses works", with "discovery via `capabilities`, `doctor` and `robot-docs`". The vision's fix for the old tool's agent support (an `AGENTS.md` key-setup walkthrough, "no machine contract") is the full agent contract of §5.9–5.10; bare help is its front door.

**The decisions that shape it** (none of the plan's numbered decisions is this bead's alone; these are the ones it obeys, restated):
- **Vision §5.9 and §5.10:** bare help lists the most common verbs, the discovery trio and the exit table, and `--json` prints the same information as JSON. Hence a human line and a JSON key, both from one table.
- **M4-D2, one contract registry feeds every description of the CLI.** `capabilities`, `robot-docs`, the wire-name golden, bare help's discovery line and `doctor capabilities` all read the registries; a fact clap cannot provide is declared exactly once, beside what it describes, and a test cross-checks it against behaviour. *Rejected there:* a hand-written description (it drifts, the exact failure these surfaces exist to prevent). For this bead: which commands bare help recommends to agents is a fact of help, declared once as `help::DISCOVERY` in `src/app/help.rs`, and tests hold every entry to the clap tree and to `app::COMMANDS` (it parses, and it names a row that does not mutate). Bare help does not build `contract::Registry` (whose `build()` reads `config.toml`, M4-D4), so it still reads no file and stays as fast and side-effect free as today. Decided while writing this bead: declared in `help.rs`, cross-checked by tests, because help must stay write-free and file-free and the table is help's own fact.
- **M4-D55, the contract's rules hold from slice 1.** Six rules govern every data shape; A3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`, schemas, declared `details` and live validation) checks rules 1–4 and 6 over every schema with a rule test; a new shape is never added to `tests/contract/rules_allowlist.txt`; reasoned permanent exceptions go in the rule test's coded `EXCEPTIONS` list, which H1 audits. ### 2. One wrapping rule for all of bare help (`src/app/help.rs`)

The plan wraps the "Start with" sentence "to `MAX_WIDTH` like the group lines". The discovery line needs the same, because the plan's literal line is 89 characters. One helper does all three:

```rust
/// `items` after `lead`, joined by `separator`, wrapped so every line is narrower than
/// `MAX_WIDTH` characters: an item that would make the line reach `MAX_WIDTH` starts the
/// next line, after `indent` spaces, and the separator before it is dropped. An item is
/// never split, so one wider than a line stands on a line of its own. Widths are
/// characters, not bytes (`·` is two bytes); help text carries no color sequences.
/// No items, no text. Every line ends with `\n`.
fn wrap<S: AsRef<str>>(lead: &str, items: &[S], separator: &str, indent: usize) -> String
```

- The break rule is `render_groups`' rule in characters: before appending `separator + item`, break when `width(line) + width(separator) + width(item) >= MAX_WIDTH`. The first item always follows `lead`, so the first line is never empty.
- Width is `str::chars().count()`. Decided while writing this bead: not `visible_width` (`src/output/human.rs:81`), which is private to `output` and exists to skip color sequences that help text never contains (clap is built with `color = Never`, `src/cli.rs:30`, and the text is written raw). Do not use `len()`: the separator ` · ` is 3 columns and 4 bytes, and a byte count would break the discovery line one item early on a near-full line.
- **`render_groups` moves onto `wrap`,** decided while writing this bead so bare help has one wrapping rule: `wrap(&format!("{:<GROUP_COLUMN$}", group.label()), &names, "  ", GROUP_COLUMN)` per group (an empty group gives no text, as its `continue` did). The output is byte-identical: the existing unit test `groups_render_one_line_each_and_wrap_under_the_first_name` passes unchanged and proves it, and the group lines in both snapshots do not change.
- **Prose is wrapped by words, never inside a backtick span:**

  ```rust
  /// The words of a sentence for [`wrap`]: split at whitespace, except inside a
  /// backtick span, so a quoted command never breaks across lines. A run of
  /// whitespace counts as one space; an unclosed span runs to the end.
  fn prose_words(text: &str) -> Vec<String>
  ```

  The live sentence gives the words `Start`, `with`, `` `omaddons status`. ``, `Run`, `` `omaddons help <command>` ``, `for`, `details;`, `add`, `--json`, `for`, `one`, `JSON`, `envelope`, `on`, `stdout.`, laid out by `wrap("", &words, " ", 0)`.

  ```rust

      rule: "r3-array-plural",
      scope: "command help",
      path: "discovery",
      reason: "the vision's \"discovery trio\" (§5.10): a collective noun for the list of the commands an agent starts with, the name the plan's contract additions fix for `help --json`",
  ```

**Files:** `src/app/help.rs`; `tests/cli_skeleton.rs`, `tests/snapshots/cli_skeleton__bare_help_human.snap`, `tests/snapshots/cli_skeleton__bare_help_json.snap`; `tests/contract/matrix.rs` (`bare_and_help`); `tests/contract/rules.rs` (`EXCEPTIONS`); `README.md` (`### help [COMMAND]`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Bare help (`omaddons`, `omaddons -h`, `omaddons help`) prints, directly after the wrapped "Start with" sentence and before the blank line and `Exit codes:`, exactly two lines rendered from `help::DISCOVERY`: `Agents: omaddons capabilities --json · omaddons robot-docs guide`, then 8 spaces and `omaddons doctor --json`.
- [ ] The line names `omaddons capabilities --json`, `omaddons robot-docs guide` and `omaddons doctor --json`, each whole on one line.
- [ ] The "Start with" sentence is wrapped to `MAX_WIDTH`: ``Start with `omaddons status`. Run `omaddons help <command>` for details; add`` then `--json for one JSON envelope on stdout.`; no backtick span is split.
- [ ] Every line of bare help above `Exit codes:` is narrower than `MAX_WIDTH` (80) characters, counted in characters, in the live help and in the planned-layout test; bare help stays under 30 lines in both.
- [ ] The group lines are byte-identical to before (`render_groups` on the shared `wrap`; `groups_render_one_line_each_and_wrap_under_the_first_name` passes unchanged).
- [ ] Bare `help --json`, under every JSON spelling, carries `data.discovery`: three entries in the line's order, each `{command, argv, purpose}` with `argv[0] == "omaddons"`, `command == shell_words::join(argv)` and a non-empty `purpose`; `help <command> --json` and `--version --json` carry no `discovery`.
- [ ] Every argv in `discovery` parses (`Cli::try_parse_from` in the unit test, `support::parses` in the contract suite) and names a `COMMANDS` row that does not mutate: `capabilities`, `robot-docs guide`, `doctor diagnose`.
- [ ] Every argv in `discovery` runs on a fresh one-client home: `capabilities --json` exits 0 with envelope `command` `capabilities`; `robot-docs guide` exits 0 and prints the guide, frontmatter first; `doctor --json` exits 0 or 1 with a doctor envelope (`command` `doctor diagnose`, `state` `DONE_OK` or `DONE_FINDINGS`).
- [ ] Bare help is byte-identical across two renders, text and JSON.
- [ ] `cli_skeleton__bare_help_human.snap` and `cli_skeleton__bare_help_json.snap` are re-accepted after review: the human diff is only the sentence's wrap and the two discovery lines, the JSON diff only `data.discovery`.
- [ ] The live validation of A3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`, schemas and live validation) passes on the bare help envelope and its snapshot, and its rule test passes with the `EXCEPTIONS` row `r3-array-plural | command help | discovery` and its reason; `tests/contract/rules_allowlist.txt` is untouched.
- [ ] No other wire name is added or changed: no code, `details` key, action, event, volatile key or limit; `schema_version` stays "1.0".
- [ ] README's `### help [COMMAND]` describes bare help's layout, the discovery line and its three commands, and `help --json`'s keys including `discovery[]`, in the commit that ships them.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files; `tests/skill.rs` passes (or `SKILL.md` is regenerated if it reports a difference).
- [ ] The close comment lists the new wire names (`help` data key `discovery`, its item keys `command`, `argv` and `purpose`), the `EXCEPTIONS` row, the report of A10 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.10`, the semantic manifest and its classifier) for `help`, that common rule 16 does not apply (no mutating path), and each "Decided while writing this bead" item as confirmed or adjusted.
- [ ] `br lint` is clean for this bead.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

In `src/app/help.rs`'s `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`. Table-driven, one named case per row; every assertion message names the case and shows the input and the actual and expected text (`"{case}: wrap({lead:?}, {items:?}) = {got:?}, expected {want:?}"`).

- **`wrap_lays_items_out_narrower_than_max_width`**, rows `(case, lead, items, separator, indent, expected)`:
  - `fits_on_one_line`: `"Agents: "`, `["a", "b"]`, `" · "`, 8 → `"Agents: a · b\n"`;
  - `fits_at_79`: `""`, `["x" × 40, "y" × 38]`, `" "`, 0 → one line of 79 characters;
  - `breaks_at_80`: `""`, `["x" × 40, "y" × 39]`, `" "`, 0 → `"x…\ny…\n"` (the second line starts with the item, no indent);
  - `counts_characters_not_bytes`: `""`, `["a" × 38, "b" × 38]`, `" · "`, 0 → one line, 79 characters and 80 bytes (a byte count would break it);
  - `continuation_is_indented_and_drops_the_separator`: `"Agents: "`, `["a" × 30, "b" × 30, "c" × 10]`, `" · "`, 8 → `"Agents: aaa… · bbb…\n        cccccccccc\n"` (84 characters would not fit);
  - `an_item_wider_than_a_line_stands_alone`: `""`, `["a", "z" × 100, "b"]`, `" "`, 0 → `"a\n" + "z" × 100 + "\nb\n"` (nothing split, nothing lost);
  - `the_first_item_follows_the_lead`: `"Agents: "`, `["q" × 90]`, `" · "`, 8 → `"Agents: " + "q" × 90 + "\n"` (no empty first line);
  - `no_items_no_text`: `"Look      "`, `[]`, `"  "`, 10 → `""`.
  Each row also asserts that joining the output's words back gives every item exactly once.
- **`prose_words_keep_backtick_spans_whole`**, rows `(case, text, expected)`:
  - `the_start_sentence`: the live sentence → the 15 words listed in Technical Approach section 2;
  - `span_with_trailing_punctuation`: ``"see `omaddons status`."`` → ``["see", "`omaddons status`."]``;
  - `whitespace_runs_collapse`: `"a  b\tc"` → `["a", "b", "c"]`;
  - `unclosed_span_runs_to_the_end`: ``"a `b c"`` → ``["a", "`b c"]``;
  - `empty`: `""` → `[]`.
- **`the_start_sentence_wraps_at_add`**: `bare_text("omaddons [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>", &[("status", Look), ("help", Setup)], &[])` contains these two lines, then a blank line and `Exit codes:`:

  ```text
  Start with `omaddons status`. Run `omaddons help <command>` for details; add
  --json for one JSON envelope on stdout.
  ```

  The same call without `("status", Look)` contains these, then a blank line and `Exit codes:`:

  ```text
  Run `omaddons help <command>` for details; add --json for one JSON envelope on
  stdout.
  ```

  With an empty discovery table there is no `Agents:` line.
- **`bare_help_names_the_discovery_trio`** (the live `bare()`):
  - the text contains `"stdout.\nAgents: omaddons capabilities --json · omaddons robot-docs guide\n        omaddons doctor --json\n\nExit codes:\n"`;
  - each `shell_words::join(entry.argv)` of `DISCOVERY` appears whole within a single line of the text;
  - `data["discovery"]` equals, in order, `[{command, argv, purpose}]` built from `DISCOVERY`, with `command == shell_words::join(argv)`, `argv[0] == "omaddons"` and a non-empty `purpose` for each;
  - the three argv are exactly `["omaddons","capabilities","--json"]`, `["omaddons","robot-docs","guide"]`, `["omaddons","doctor","--json"]`, in that order.
- **`every_discovery_argv_parses_to_a_read_only_command`**, rows `(argv, envelope name)`: `capabilities --json` → `capabilities`; `robot-docs guide` → `robot-docs guide`; `doctor --json` → `doctor diagnose`. For each entry of `DISCOVERY`: `crate::cli::Cli::try_parse_from(entry.argv)` is `Ok` (on failure the message shows the argv and clap's error); `super::command_name(cli.command.as_ref())` equals the row's name; `super::COMMANDS` has exactly one row of that name and its `mutates` is `false`; no argv word is empty. The table has exactly these three rows, so a fourth entry fails until the test is extended.
- **`command_help_and_version_have_no_discovery`**: `serde_json::to_value(&for_command(Some("help"), &[]).unwrap().data)` and `version()`'s have no `discovery` key.
- **`bare_help_is_the_same_every_time`**: two `bare()` calls give identical `text` and identical `serde_json::to_string(&data)`.
- **`bare_help_stays_one_screen_with_every_planned_command`** (existing, extended): call `bare_text("omaddons [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>", &planned, DISCOVERY)`; keep the fewer-than-30-lines assertion and the group-line assertions; add that every line before `Exit codes:` has fewer than `MAX_WIDTH` characters (`chars().count()`), printing the text on failure, and that the text contains `"\nAgents: omaddons capabilities --json · omaddons robot-docs guide\n        omaddons doctor --json\n"`. Keep the planned rows the command leaves added; add none.
- **Unchanged, and must pass:** `bare_help_lists_commands_and_every_exit_code` (its ``Start with `omaddons status` `` clause stays on the sentence's first line), `groups_render_one_line_each_and_wrap_under_the_first_name` (proves `render_groups` on `wrap` is byte-identical), `every_subcommand_has_exactly_one_registry_entry`, `command_help_and_unknown_commands`, `positional_values_resolve_to_their_command`.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

**`tests/cli_skeleton.rs`** (the suite of "the first commands an agent guesses"):
- `bare_omaddons_prints_help_and_exits_0` (existing, extended): also assert that stdout contains, as one literal, the four lines of Technical Approach section 3 (the two sentence lines and the two discovery lines) followed by a blank line and `Exit codes:`, and that every stdout line before `Exit codes:` has fewer than 80 characters (message: the line, its width and `r.context()`). Re-accept `bare_help_human` after review.
- `every_json_spelling_gives_one_help_envelope` (existing, extended): for each of the five spellings, `envelope["data"]["discovery"]`'s `argv` arrays equal the three expected argv in order, and each `command` equals the argv joined with spaces. Re-accept `bare_help_json` after review (the diff is `data.discovery` only).
- `help_for_a_command` (existing, extended): `help help --json`'s `data` has no `discovery` key.
- **`discovery_commands_run_on_a_fresh_home`** (new; a `TestLog` scenario, `let log = tlog!();`, on `common::home::Home::new(&["wow"])`, one retail client):
  1. step `bare help (json)`: `let ran = log.run(&home, &["--json"]); ran.ok();` then `log.json("discovery", &ran.data()["discovery"])`; assert three entries whose `argv` are the expected three and whose `command` is `shell_words::join(argv)`.
  2. step `bare help (human)`: `log.run(&home, &[] as &[&str]).ok()`; for each entry, some stdout line contains its `command` whole.
  3. step `discovery: omaddons capabilities --json`: `log.run(&home, &["capabilities", "--json"]).ok()`; `envelope()["command"] == "capabilities"`.
  4. step `discovery: omaddons robot-docs guide`: `log.run(&home, &["robot-docs", "guide"]).ok()`; stdout starts with `"---\n"` and contains `"\nname: omaddons\n"` (the frontmatter that B1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`, the guide renderer and `robot-docs guide`, puts first).
  5. step `discovery: omaddons doctor --json`: `let ran = log.run(&home, &["doctor", "--json"]);` exit 0 or 1 (`healthy` or `findings_present`; decided while writing this bead: a one-client home may hold findings, and this test proves the argv runs to a finished diagnosis, not that the home is healthy); `common::doctor::check_envelope(ran.stdout(), ran.stderr(), code)` passes; its `command` is `doctor diagnose` and its `state` is `DONE_OK` or `DONE_FINDINGS`.
  Steps 3 to 5 run the argv that step 1 read from the binary's `discovery` (without the leading `omaddons`; written out above for clarity), not `DISCOVERY`, so the test proves what the binary prints; step 1 compares that list with the three argv written out in the test, so a changed table fails it.
- No crash, concurrency or performance case: the change adds no write, lock or protocol. No `WTF/` is created, so common rule 9's privacy check does not apply.

**`tests/contract/matrix.rs`**, `bare_and_help` (existing, extended): after `let c = s.json(&[], 0);`, for each element of `c.envelope["data"]["discovery"]` (exactly 3), `let argv = support::strings(&entry["argv"]);` then `assert_eq!(entry["command"], shell_words::join(&argv), "{}", c.run.context())` and `support::parses(&argv, &c.run.context())`. `support::check` already validates the envelope against `help`'s schema (A3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`, schemas and live validation). No new snapshot.

**`tests/contract/rules.rs`**: the `EXCEPTIONS` row of Technical Approach section 5; `every_schema_follows_the_contract_rules` passes and its stale-exception check holds.

### Logging

- Unit tests: every case is named; assertion messages carry the case name, the input (lead, items, separator, indent, or the text) and the expected and actual output, with newlines shown (`{:?}`).
- `discovery_commands_run_on_a_fresh_home`: its steps are named as above; `log.run` records each argv, the environment overrides, the exit, the envelope (or the raw Markdown for `robot-docs guide`), the stderr events and any `net.log` lines; `log.json("discovery", …)` records the list the binary printed. A failing `Ran` assertion names the step and the transcript path. On panic the guard prints `test log: <path>` and the last 20 steps; `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG=verbose cargo test --test cli_skeleton discovery -- --nocapture` echoes every step live.
- The existing `cli_skeleton` and `matrix` tests keep their style: every assertion message carries `r.context()` or `c.run.context()` (argv, exit, stdout, stderr).

No checkpoint-only test: everything runs in the gate.

## Considerations

- **Size S, no subtasks.** One module (a table, a wrapper, a word splitter, one data struct and one field), its tests, two snapshots, one contract assertion, one exception row and one README section: one commit.
- **Lands late by design.** Bare help must never name a command that does not exist, so this bead waits for A4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`, `omaddons capabilities`), A5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5`, the `robot-docs` tree), B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`, `robot-docs guide`) and E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, `doctor diagnose`). Its earliest start is t = 8 with 6 units of slack; the computed schedule puts it in lane 6 at t = 14–15, before H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, the pre-freeze contract audit).
- **The wrapper must not change the group lines.** `render_groups` moves onto `wrap`. Notice: `groups_render_one_line_each_and_wrap_under_the_first_name` and the group lines of both snapshots must not change; a snapshot diff that touches a group line is a bug in `wrap`.
- **Bytes versus characters.** A byte count would break the discovery line early (the ` · ` separator is 3 columns and 4 bytes). Notice: `counts_characters_not_bytes`.
- **A discovery entry that stops running.** If a later leaf renames `capabilities`, the `robot-docs guide` path or bare `doctor`, `every_discovery_argv_parses_to_a_read_only_command` and `discovery_commands_run_on_a_fresh_home` fail in the gate; there is no runtime filter to hide it.
- **The exception row.** `discovery` breaks rule 3's plural check by name only. H1 audits every exception; if it judges the name wrong, it renames it before the last regeneration of the golden by H2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.2`, the golden and the released baseline), as M4-D55 allows, with the snapshots and README in the same commit (the widget does not read it).
- **M4-D8's sentence** (bare help's discovery line names `install-skill`) is not applied, as also recorded by B3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3`, `robot-docs install-skill`); nothing in the product recommends installing the skill unasked.
- **Risk 14 (the milestone is large)** applies to every late leaf; this one has 6 units of slack and touches no engine code. No other risk of §11.4 concerns it.
- **Hot spots and collisions:**
  - `src/app/help.rs`: every leaf that adds a top-level command (A4, A5, E3, and A7, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.7`, `omaddons completions`; D5, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`, `omaddons apply`; D9, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.9`, `omaddons plans show`) adds a row to the planned-layout test. This bead changes that test's `bare_text` call and adds assertions; rebase and keep every row they added.
  - `tests/cli_skeleton.rs` and its two snapshots: every leaf that adds a top-level command re-accepts them. Rebase first, then re-accept, and review that the diff is only this bead's lines and `data.discovery`.
  - `tests/contract/rules.rs` `EXCEPTIONS`: A4, E3 and E4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4`, `doctor health`, `ls`, `--robot-triage`, `capabilities` and `robot-docs`) add rows; insert this one in sorted place.
  - `tests/contract/matrix.rs`: one assertion inside `bare_and_help`; no snapshot file.
  - `README.md`: edit only ``### `help [COMMAND]` ``; H4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`, the README final pass) reconciles the rest.
- **Compatibility.** `discovery` is an additive key; consumers that ignore unknown keys (the guide tells agents to) are unaffected. The human text changes by a line break and two lines; nothing in the repository parses it. Nothing persisted changes, so there is nothing for E9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9`, the M3 build against M4 state) to characterize.
- **Privacy.** Static text only; no path, client or account.
- **Performance.** Bare help still builds no registry and reads no file; the wrapper is a few dozen string operations.
- **Bounded work (common rule 15).** No untrusted or user-sized input is read.
- **Previews bind (common rule 16).** No mutating path is added; say so in the close comment.
- **Decided while writing this bead** (confirm or adjust each in the close comment): the line's wrap (between entries, continuation indented 8, separator dropped) and its place (directly after the sentence); one `wrap` helper for groups, the sentence and the line, with `render_groups` moved onto it; widths in characters; prose never broken inside a backtick span, whitespace runs collapsed; the width assertion covering the lines above `Exit codes:` and the exit table left as is, with `MAX_WIDTH`'s doc comment narrowed; `DISCOVERY` declared in `help.rs` and checked by tests, bare help building no registry; no runtime filter; `command` as the display of `argv`; `argv` keeping `--json` where the line shows it; the three purposes' wording; `discovery` after `commands`; the `r3-array-plural` exception rather than a rename; `install-skill` left off the line (M4-D8 versus §6.6); the doctor step accepting exit 0 or 1 on a one-client home; README's `help` section only; the contract matrix's `bare_and_help` checking each argv with `support::parses`.

## Dependencies

Parent: the A area epic, AREA-A (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1`, the contract registry and the discovery surfaces), under the milestone epic (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`).

**Blocked by:**
- A4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`, `omaddons capabilities`): the line's first command must exist, with its `COMMANDS` row (`mutates: false`) and its envelope.
- A5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5`, `robot-docs schema` and `robot-docs errors`): the `robot-docs` tree that `robot-docs guide` lives in.
- B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`, the guide renderer and `robot-docs guide`): the line's second command, its `COMMANDS` row and its Markdown output, frontmatter first.
- E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, `doctor diagnose` and `explain`): the line's third command, bare `doctor` named `doctor diagnose`, the doctor envelope and `common::doctor::check_envelope`.
- T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs and the `argc e2e` runner; edge added at filing because this bead writes an integration scenario): `tlog!()`, `log.run` and `Ran` for `discovery_commands_run_on_a_fresh_home`.

**Unblocks:**
- H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, the pre-freeze contract audit): every leaf that adds a wire shape lands before the audit, so it sees `discovery[]` and audits this bead's `EXCEPTIONS` row.
- H4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`, the README final pass): it reconciles README against `main`, including this bead's `help` section and the "For coding agents" block it replaces with the skill pointer.

**Slice:** `slice-4`, "Freeze and close". Exit demo (recorded by H6, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the M4 checkpoint and the first tag): the recipes pass; the audit's change list and the empty allowlist; the golden and the updater tests; README; the tag and the released baseline. It pre-checks criteria 3, 4, 14, 17 and 18. This bead records no demo.

**Related, not edges:** A1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1`, `command_name` and `canonical_path`); A3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`, the rule test, `EXCEPTIONS` and live validation); A10 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.10`, whose report shows the additive change); H2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.2`, the golden that pins `discovery`); H3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3`, the determinism audit that repeats every matrix row); B3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3`, `install-skill`, and M4-D8's sentence about this line); B2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.2`, the guide's content, whose prose also names the discovery trio); A7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.7`, `omaddons completions`), D5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`, `omaddons apply`) and D9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.9`, `omaddons plans show`), which add top-level commands to the group lines and the planned-layout test.

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M4 plan, 2026-10-24).**

**Why this bead.** Bare `omaddons` is the first thing an agent that knows nothing about the tool runs. Vision §5.9 says its help lists the most common verbs, the discovery trio and the exit table, and that bare `--json` prints the same as JSON; vision §5.10 names the trio: `omaddons capabilities --json`, `omaddons doctor --json`, `omaddons robot-docs guide`. At `c0ab5e9` none of the three commands exists, so bare help cannot list them. Once A4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`, `omaddons capabilities`), A5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5`, the `robot-docs` tree), B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`, `robot-docs guide`) and E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, `doctor diagnose`) have landed, this bead adds one human line naming them, the same three as `discovery[{command, argv, purpose}]` in bare `help --json`, and wraps the 116-column "Start with" sentence to bare help's 80-column width. It is the front door of G-M4-1 ("an agent learns everything it needs from the binary itself, in at most three calls") and of vision goal G4 ("the first command an agent guesses works", with discovery through `capabilities`, `doctor` and `robot-docs`).

**Decisions applied.**
- **Vision §5.9 and §5.10:** the trio in bare help, human and JSON alike; one table renders both, so they cannot disagree.
- **M4-D2, one registry, a fact declared once and cross-checked by a test:** `help::DISCOVERY` is declared once in `src/app/help.rs`; tests hold each entry to the clap tree (it parses) and to `app::COMMANDS` (its row does not mutate), and an end-to-end scenario runs each argv. Bare help still builds no registry, so it reads no file.
- **M4-D55, the contract's rules from slice 1:** `discovery` breaks A3's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`, schemas and live validation) `r3-array-plural` check by name; it gets a reasoned `EXCEPTIONS` row that H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, the pre-freeze contract audit) audits, never an allowlist line.
- **M4-D56, member order is not contract:** where `discovery` sits in `BareHelp` is a rendering choice; H2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.2`, the golden) pins the key and its types.
- **M4-D18, determinism:** the table is static, so no volatile key.
- **DEC-4:** an additive key on an existing shape; `schema_version` stays "1.0".
- **M4-D8 (context):** its sentence that bare help's discovery line names `robot-docs install-skill` is not applied. §6.6 and this bead's own acceptance criteria give exactly three commands, this bead is not blocked by B3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3`, `robot-docs install-skill`), and B3's bead records the same reading.
- **§8.1 defaults:** the `{command, argv}` pair keeps its contract-wide meaning (display and argv); token-frugal (purposes in JSON only); the table's order is the line's.

**Alternatives rejected that matter here.**
- **The plan's line as one 89-column line:** wider than `MAX_WIDTH` (80), contradicting the plan's own "wrapped to `MAX_WIDTH` like the group lines". It wraps between entries, its continuation under the first entry, like a group line.
- **Measuring width in bytes,** as `render_groups` does today: the ` · ` separator is 3 columns and 4 bytes, so a byte count breaks the line one entry early.
- **A runtime filter** that hides an entry whose command is missing (as the "Start with" clause is guarded by `status`): it would hide a renamed command instead of failing the gate.
- **`discovery[].command` as a `COMMANDS` path:** every `{command, argv}` pair in the contract is "display and argv"; the path of `doctor --json` is `doctor diagnose`, which an agent does not type.
- **Dropping `--json` from the argv** to match the no-presentation-flag rule of fixes and `commands[]`: that rule exists because those rerun under the caller's flags; a discovery entry recommends how to read the tool, and `capabilities`' own pointer to `doctor capabilities` keeps `--json` too.
- **Renaming the key to a plural** (`discovery_commands`): the plan fixes the name and the vision's word is "discovery trio"; H1, which owns pre-freeze renames of audited exceptions, can still change it.
- **Building `contract::Registry` in bare help:** its `build()` reads `config.toml`; bare help reads no file today, and must stay fast and side-effect free.
- **Fixing the exit table's 82-column `not_found` row here:** outside this bead's lines; the width assertion covers the lines above `Exit codes:`, and `MAX_WIDTH`'s doc comment says so.

**Risks and how they are watched.**
- The shared wrapper changing the group lines: `groups_render_one_line_each_and_wrap_under_the_first_name` passes unchanged, and the snapshot diff may touch only the sentence and the discovery lines.
- A discovery entry that stops running after a later rename: the parse-and-`COMMANDS` unit test and the end-to-end scenario fail in the gate.
- The exception being judged wrong at the audit: H1 renames before H2's last regeneration (M4-D55); nothing but README and the snapshots reads the key.
- Collisions: `src/app/help.rs`'s planned-layout test and `tests/cli_skeleton.rs`'s snapshots are touched by every leaf adding a top-level command; this bead rebases, keeps their rows and re-accepts after review.
- Risk 14 (the milestone is large): 6 units of slack, no engine code.

**What it unblocks, and why they wait.**
- H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`): every leaf that adds a wire shape lands before the audit, so the audit sees `discovery[]` and this bead's `EXCEPTIONS` row.
- H4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`, the README final pass): it reconciles README against `main`, including this bead's `help` section, and replaces "For coding agents" with the skill pointer.

**How it serves the milestone.** G-M4-1 (self-describing): the first screen an agent sees names the two "learn the tool" calls and the health check. G-M4-2 (the first guess works): the likeliest first guess answers with where to go next. G-M4-5 (frozen and enforced): the shape exists, validated and rule-checked, before the audit and the golden. Checkpoint criteria 14 (the frozen contract and byte-identical repeats), 17 (the gate) and 18 (README describes what exists).

**Facts verified during planning** (as of `c0ab5e9`). Bare help is 19 lines, built by `bare_text` (`src/app/help.rs:173-196`) and `bare()` (`:198-245`), with `MAX_WIDTH = 80` (`:19`) and `render_groups`' byte-measured wrap (`:142-171`). The "Start with" sentence is one 116-character line (`:180-183`; snapshot line 14). The exit table's `not_found` row is 82 characters (snapshot line 20). `BareHelp` is `{name, version, usage, commands, global_flags, exit_codes}` (`:38-47`) inside the untagged `HelpData` (`:29-36`). The planned-layout test is `help.rs:433-477`; the bare-help tests and snapshots are `tests/cli_skeleton.rs:118-177`. Every `{command, argv}` pair is display and argv (`CommandHint`, `src/error.rs:440-467`). No widget code reads `help --json`. README's `help` section is `README.md:1748-1754`.

**Where the plan and the code differ.** The plan calls the "Start with" line 117 columns (§2.1, §6.6); it is 116. The plan's literal discovery line is 89 columns, so it cannot stay one line under `MAX_WIDTH`; it wraps between entries. `MAX_WIDTH`'s doc comment ("Bare help's lines stay narrower than this") is already untrue for the exit table, and only the group lines are asserted; the new assertion covers every line above `Exit codes:`. The plan's array name `discovery` fails rule 3's plural check as A3's rule test implements it; an `EXCEPTIONS` row keeps the plan's name. Within the plan, M4-D8 says the line names `install-skill` while §6.6 gives three commands without it; §6.6 wins, as B3 decided.

**Confidence.** High. The change is a static table, a text wrapper and one additive field in one module, with no write, lock, I/O or protocol; every argv it publishes is parsed by a unit test and run by an end-to-end scenario, and the shared wrapper is held to the group lines' existing output by an unchanged test.

comments.text: **Common rules.** The rules every M4 leaf and subtask follows, cited in this bead as "common rule N", are in the pinned docs bead `omad-bxb1` (`br show omad-bxb1`). Read them once per session, not once per bead.

title: `omaddons completions <SHELL>`
description:
## How to work this bead

This bead is worked through its 2 subtasks, listed below in work order. Claim a subtask, not this bead (`br ready --parent omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.7` lists the ready ones). The agent that closes the last open subtask then verifies every acceptance criterion of this bead (they are the leaf's, not any one subtask's), and closes this bead with `br close omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.7 --reason "done: <evidence> · found: <ids>"`. Until this bead is closed, every bead it blocks stays blocked.

1. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.7.1 The `completions` command: the `clap_complete` dependency, the in-memory generator, every DEC-1 registry touch point, its contract and usage-fix rows, and its README sections, in one commit.
2. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.7.2 Tests: every shell's script snapshot-tested, checked by its own shell, and proven static, deterministic and pure (`tests/completions.rs`, the shared `tests/common/shells.rs`, the zsh and fish checkpoint checks).

Order: subtask 2 after subtask 1, because it tests the command subtask 1 adds; subtask 2 also needs T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs), because its scenarios use `TestLog`. This is a size-S leaf: the command is one small module plus its registry rows, and most of the work is its tests, which is why they are their own step.

## Background

Leaves named in this section: A3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`, schemas, live validation and the rule test), A4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`, `omaddons capabilities`), B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`, the guide renderer and `SKILL.md`), C4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4`, the run-the-fix corpus), H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, the pre-freeze contract audit).

### What this is for

`omaddons completions <SHELL>` prints a shell completion script for `bash`, `zsh`, `fish`, `elvish` or `powershell`. After a user saves it where the shell looks, pressing Tab after `omaddons` offers the commands, subcommands, aliases, flags and fixed values of this build: `omaddons st<Tab>` becomes `status`, `omaddons backup re<Tab>` becomes `restore`, `omaddons --format <Tab>` offers `json human`.

The vision lists `omaddons completions <shell>` among M4's deliverables, and its CLI contract (vision §5.9) says "every command offers `--json`. This includes `help`, `completions` (`{"shell","script"}`), `robot-docs` … and every doctor verb". The vision's crate table already names `clap_complete` for the CLI. Nothing of it exists at `c0ab5e9`: `clap_complete` is not a dependency, and README says "Shell completions are planned for milestone 4" (`README.md:252`) and lists "Shell completions ❌ M4" under "What omaddons does not do (yet)" (`README.md:2538`).

The command is part of milestone 4's first slice, "Self-describing": the binary describes itself to agents (`capabilities`, `robot-docs`) and, through this command, to the shell a human types in. Like every other description of the CLI in M4, the script is generated from the live clap tree, never kept by hand, so it cannot drift from the commands the binary has.

### Goals served

- **G-M4-1 Self-describing:** an agent with no prior knowledge learns everything it needs from the binary itself, and every fact in those outputs is generated from the code, so it cannot drift from what the code does. The completion script is one more generated view of the clap tree: a command, flag or value the binary has is in the script, and nothing else is.
- **G-M4-2 The first guess works:** a plausible wrong invocation yields a usage error whose fix is the command the user meant, and the fix is proven to run. `omaddons completions bsh` gets `omaddons completions bash`, which runs.
- **G-M4-5 Frozen and enforced:** at the first tag the contract is complete and enforced, and repeated runs print identical bytes. The `completions` path, its `{shell, script}` data and the five shell names land before the pre-freeze audit (H1), so they are frozen with the rest of the contract; the script itself is the same bytes on every run and every terminal.
- Vision goal G4, agent ergonomics ("the first command an agent guesses works"): completion makes the right spelling the easy one for a human at a terminal, and the JSON form gives an agent the script as data.

### Checkpoint criteria this bead is responsible for

- **15, Completions** (this bead owns it): "`omaddons completions <shell>` prints a script for bash, zsh, fish, elvish and powershell, each snapshot-tested. The bash script passes `bash -n`, and the zsh and fish scripts pass `zsh -n` and `fish --no-execute` (pre-accepted `SKIP` where those shells are missing). `--json` gives `{shell, script}`." The checkpoint's pre-accepted skips are exactly "the `zsh -n` and `fish --no-execute` syntax checks of generated completions, where those shells are not installed (bash's check is never skipped)". Any other `SKIP` means the criterion is not met.
- **14, The contract is frozen** (its determinism part, for this path): "repeated runs of every command path print identical bytes, after stripping only the keys the volatile registry declares". `completions` declares no volatile key.
- **18, README** describes exactly what exists: the Installation, command reference, "What works today", limitations and Development sections this bead edits.
- Fed through other leaves, with nothing extra from this bead: criterion 1 (A4's `capabilities` lists the `completions` path with its positional and possible values, generated from the row this bead adds), criterion 2 (A3 validates `completions`' live `data` against the schema the row declares), criterion 5 (the intent corpus row `omaddons completions bsh` → `usage` → `omaddons completions bash` → exit 0).

### The decisions that shape it

- **M4-D16: completions are static, generated by `clap_complete`, for five shells.**
  - `omaddons completions <bash|zsh|fish|elvish|powershell>` prints the script to stdout (data). `--json` gives `{shell, script}`.
  - The script is generated in memory from `Cli::command()` with the bin name `omaddons`, so commands still never print.
  - README says where each shell looks. Packaging the scripts is M5.
  - `clap_complete` is pinned to the version matching `clap` 4.6.x.
  - **Why:** the vision lists `completions <shell>` in M4 with the `--json` shape. Static completion covers commands, subcommands, flags and fixed values, which is what users press Tab for most.
  - **Rejected:** clap's dynamic completion (client ids and addon names): unstable in `clap_complete` (it sits behind the `unstable-dynamic` feature), and it would make every Tab press run discovery. Do not be tempted to add a hidden `complete` subcommand or an environment-variable protocol that calls back into the binary: a Tab press must never run omaddons.
  - The milestone's non-goals (§3.4) restate both halves: dynamic completion of client ids and addon names is not M4's, and release engineering beyond the tag (packaged completions, a man page with `clap_mangen`, a PKGBUILD) is M5's.
- **M4-D2: one contract registry feeds every description of the CLI.** A fact clap cannot provide is declared exactly once, beside the command, and a test cross-checks it. `completions` is a view of the live clap tree, like help, `capabilities` and the manifest; its own facts (group, mutates, exits, data schema, network) are declared once, on its `COMMANDS` row.
- **M4-D5: per-command exit codes are declared beside the command and verified.** Every general command lists 0, 1 and 2; a mutating command lists 5; one with `--check` or `--strict` lists 6. The contract suite records every exit each path produced and fails on an undeclared one. `completions` declares exactly `[0, 1, 2]`: success, a runtime failure (only `internal`, which a write into memory cannot cause but the panic path and the static rule cover), and usage. Declaring more "to be safe" is what M4-D5 rejects.
- **M4-D18: determinism is enforced per command path, and volatile keys are declared.** Every path has a success and a failure row in the contract matrix, every row runs twice with identical stdout bytes, and only keys declared in `contract::VOLATILE` may differ. `completions` has no volatile key: its bytes depend only on the binary, never on the terminal, the environment, the home or the time. That is why generation uses a fixed terminal width.
- **M4-D55: the contract's rules hold from slice 1.** Rule 2: every key of a command's data is always present. Rule 3: snake-case names. Rule 4: every enumeration is snake case with a closed set in its schema. Rule 5: the envelope `command` equals the canonical clap path. `{shell, script}` obeys all four: both keys always present, `shell` a closed enum of five snake-case values, and the path is `completions`. A3's rule test checks it once A3 has landed; this bead never adds a line to `tests/contract/rules_allowlist.txt`.
- **M4-D15: a usage fix must run, not just parse.** The intent corpus runs each wrong argv, then its `fix_argv`, and asserts the fix's exit; an erroring row must change nothing. `completions bsh` → `completions bash` (exit 0) is one of the corpus's starting rows. This bead also proves its own wrong invocations' fixes run, in its end-to-end suite, so the guarantee holds before C4 lands.
- **M4-D7: the guide and `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` are one artifact.** Once B1 has landed, the guide's generated command table includes every command, so adding `completions` changes `SKILL.md`, which is regenerated with `OMADDONS_UPDATE_SKILL=1 cargo test --test skill` and committed in the same commit.
- **DEC-1, no stubs:** every registry touch point of the command lands in the commit that adds its clap variant (common rule 4), never split.
- **§8.1 defaults applied:** prefer existing codes (only `usage` and `internal` can occur, no new code); additive JSON; no network on a read path; no write at all.

### Facts this bead relies on (verified at `c0ab5e9`)

- **No completion exists.** `clap_complete` is not in `Cargo.toml` (dependencies at `Cargo.toml:16-36`; `clap = { version = "4.6.7", features = ["derive", "env", "wrap_help"] }` at `:17`); `Cargo.lock` holds `clap`, `clap_builder` and `clap_derive` 4.6.7 and `clap_lex` 1.1.1, and no `clap_complete`.
- **The tree a generator walks.** `Cli` (`src/cli.rs:24-41`) has `name` and `bin_name` `"omaddons"`, `color = Never`, `disable_help_flag`, `disable_version_flag`, `disable_help_subcommand` and `args_override_self`. `-h/--help` and `-V/--version` are the CLI's own flags (`GlobalArgs`, `src/cli.rs:113-118`; `-V` is not global), and `help` is its own subcommand (`Command::Help`, `src/cli.rs:139-144`), so clap adds no flag or subcommand of its own to the tree. No argument, value or subcommand is hidden (`hide` appears nowhere in `src/`).
- **The `Command` enum** is `src/cli.rs:137-213`; its last variant is `Omarchy` (`:211-212`). Long helps are `const <NAME>_HELP: &str` blocks in the same file (`src/cli.rs:469-587`), each starting `Examples:`.
- **The fixed values clap validates,** which a static script can complete: `--format` (`json`, `human`; `src/cli.rs:53-61`), `--progress` (`json`, `human`, `none`; `:98-106`), `search --source` (a value enum, `src/app/search.rs:54`), `omarchy install --section` (`src/app/omarchy.rs:40`), and `auth`'s value enums (`src/app/auth.rs:39-42`; A1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1`, turns `github` into a real subcommand of `auth`, and its ACTION stays a value enum: `status`, `set`, `clear`). The value enums of the CLI are case-sensitive; only `--format` and `--progress` set `ignore_case`.
- **The raw human form has a precedent.** `HelpOutcome` (`src/app/help.rs:22-27`) holds `data` and pre-rendered text, and its `render_human` writes the text raw (`:110-112`). Every outcome implements `trait Outcome { type Data: Serialize + schemars::JsonSchema; fn command(&self) -> &'static str; fn data(&self) -> &Self::Data; … fn render_human(…) }` (`src/output/mod.rs:34-56`).
- **The registry and dispatch.** `app::COMMANDS` is `src/app/mod.rs:121-165`, with `help` last (`:164`); `command_name` is `:195-237`; `run_command`'s match is `:374-587`. After A1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1`), every row is built by `const fn entry(name, group, mutates, exits, data, network)` with `data: data_schema::<TheOutcome>` (dictionary `General` and `stores_plan: false` by default), and the parsed-command → name mapping is `app::canonical_path(&Command)`, which `command_name` calls.
- **Usage fixes the command will get, from existing code.**
  - An invalid value goes to `value_fix` (`src/cli.rs:896-938`): every valid value within Levenshtein distance 2, sorted by distance then name, the first applied in place, the rest alternatives. For `completions bsh`: `bash` (distance 1), then `zsh` (1) and `fish` (2). `PowerShell` is distance 2 from `powershell`, `BASH` distance 4 from `bash` (no value fix).
  - An unknown subcommand goes to `subcommand_fix` (`src/cli.rs:849-890`), which applies a read-only guess in place (`completion bash` → `completions bash`) and turns a mutating guess into its help.
  - A missing argument takes the default arm, `help_fix()` (`src/cli.rs:754`): `omaddons help completions`.
  - Every suggestion must parse and must not be the failing argv, else it falls back to help (`src/cli.rs:756-761`). So `omaddons completons` (no shell) gets `omaddons help`, because `omaddons completions` alone does not parse.
  - `-h` on a command whose required argument is missing shows that command's help (`src/cli.rs:374`), so `omaddons completions --help` works.
  - `--if-match` on a command outside `precondition::BINDING_COMMANDS` is `usage` from `Context::new`, and for a read-only command the fix is the same argv without the flag (`check_if_match`, `src/cli.rs:309-337`).
- **Help.** Bare help lists commands one line per group in `COMMANDS` order (`src/app/help.rs:145-245`). At `c0ab5e9` the Setup line is `Setup     targets  config  auth  omarchy  help`, asserted literally at `tests/cli_skeleton.rs:127` and snapshotted in `tests/snapshots/cli_skeleton__bare_help_human.snap`; `help --json`'s `commands` list is snapshotted in `cli_skeleton__bare_help_json.snap`. The planned-layout test `bare_help_stays_one_screen_with_every_planned_command` (`src/app/help.rs:433-477`) holds 22 entries (`:462`). `help <cmd> <value>` stays on the command when the word is a possible value of its positional (`src/app/help.rs:270-285`), so `help completions bash` is `completions`' help.
- **The contract suite.** `tests/contract/matrix.rs` ends with `fn omarchy()` (`:1161-1200`); `s.json(argv, code)` runs `omaddons <argv> --json` through `support::check`, and `s.stable(&envelope)` removes `meta` and redacts for snapshots (`tests/contract/main.rs:307-330`, `:426-428`). `tests/contract/special.rs:313-387` runs every `mutates: false` path with and without `--dry-run --reason x` from an invocation map (`:317-338`) that fails with "add a read-only invocation of <name> here" for a path it lacks; `repeated_runs_are_byte_identical` is `:456-476`. `tests/contract/usage_fixes.rs` holds the `CORPUS` (`:47`), `VALUE_TYPOS` (`:102`) and `DECIDED` (`:126`) tables, and the one-edit typo sweep over every `COMMANDS` row (`:257-311`).
- **The widget.** `CLI_PATHS` (`omarchy/Model.js:133-178`, `help` row at `:176`) is held equal to `COMMANDS` by `tests/omarchy_widget.rs:30-51`. The widget never runs `completions`.
- **Subprocesses.** `tests/single_writer.rs` scans `src/` only for process spawns (`:811`), so test code may run `bash`; `completions` itself spawns nothing.
- **The checkpoint skip helper** (`tests/common/checkpoint.rs`): `skip(test, reason)` prints `SKIP <test>: <reason>` on stderr and fails unless `OMADDONS_ALLOW_SKIP` names the test; `require(test, vars)` skips unless each variable is `1`.
- **The test environment.** `TestEnv` clears `CI`, `NO_COLOR`, `TERM`, `XDG_DATA_DIRS` and `XDG_CONFIG_DIRS` and sets `TZ=UTC` (`tests/common/env.rs:9-22`); it leaves `COLUMNS` alone. On the development machine bash 5.3 is installed and zsh, fish, elvish and pwsh are not (checked while planning).
- **`clap_complete` 4.6.11** (the newest 4.6.x in the local cargo registry while planning): requires `clap` `^4.6.6` with only its `std` feature; its default feature set is empty (the dynamic engine is behind `unstable-dynamic`); licensed `MIT OR Apache-2.0`, both allowed by `deny.toml`. Its `Shell` enum is `#[non_exhaustive]`, with `Bash`, `Elvish`, `Fish`, `PowerShell` and `Zsh`, whose clap values are `bash`, `elvish`, `fish`, `powershell` and `zsh`. `clap_complete::generate(shell, &mut cmd, name, &mut buf)` is exactly `cmd.set_bin_name(name); cmd.build(); shell.generate(&cmd, buf)`, and each shell's `generate` calls `try_generate(…).expect("failed to write completion file")`; `Generator::try_generate` returns the `io::Error` instead. No generator reads the terminal width.
- **Measured while planning** (a scratch build of the `c0ab5e9` tree with `clap_complete` 4.6.11, outside the repository): bash 85,357 bytes (2,284 lines), zsh 115,696 (1,837), fish 164,241 (1,263), elvish 108,354 (1,397), powershell 202,993 (1,457), about 676 KB in all. `bash -n` accepts the bash script. `COLUMNS=40` gives identical bytes. No script contains a path of the machine, an ANSI escape, or any call back into the binary.
