### 2. `DetailSpec` (subtask 1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9.1`)

```rust
/// A typed description of one error code's `details` object, or of a value inside it (M4-D10).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum DetailSpec {
    Str,
    Int,
    Num,
    Bool,
    /// A string from a closed set of snake_case values, in declared order.
    Enum(&'static [&'static str]),
    Array(&'static DetailSpec),
    /// An object with exactly these keys, sorted by key.
    Object(&'static [Field]),
    /// A value matching exactly one of these specs (two or more).
    OneOf(&'static [&'static DetailSpec]),
    /// An object whose keys this spec does not constrain; the text says why.
    Opaque(&'static str),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Field {
    pub key: &'static str,
    pub spec: &'static DetailSpec,
    pub presence: Presence,      // Required | Optional
    pub null: Nullability,       // NotNull | Nullable
}

impl Field {
    pub const fn req(key: &'static str, spec: &'static DetailSpec) -> Self;  // Required, NotNull
    pub const fn opt(key: &'static str, spec: &'static DetailSpec) -> Self;  // Optional, NotNull
    pub const fn nullable(self) -> Self;
}

impl DetailSpec {
    pub const EMPTY: DetailSpec = DetailSpec::Object(&[]);
    pub fn to_json_schema(&self) -> serde_json::Value;
    pub fn admits(&self, value: &serde_json::Value) -> Result<(), Mismatch>;
    pub fn declared_paths(&self) -> Vec<String>;
    pub fn opaque_paths(&self) -> Vec<String>;
    pub fn field(&self, key: &str) -> Option<&'static Field>;    // an Object's field
    pub fn enum_values(&self) -> Option<&'static [&'static str]>;
    pub fn well_formed(&self) -> Result<(), String>;
}

pub struct Mismatch { pub path: String, pub expected: String, pub found: String }
// Display: "details.<path>: expected <expected>, found <found>"
```

- **Two variants beyond the plan's list.** Decided while writing this bead: `OneOf` and `Opaque` are added, because the code at `c0ab5e9` emits keys in two shapes and embeds `ItemError.details`, which neither the plan's seven variants nor a retype of M2-era emitters can honestly describe (the plan's intent, a precise type for every key, is kept; see "Where the plan and the code disagree", items 2 and 5). `OneOf` is used only where an emitter really produces two shapes; a unit test pins the list (§5.4).
- **`Field` is a named struct.** Decided while writing this bead: the plan writes the object member as a tuple `(key, &DetailSpec, Required | Optional, Nullable | NotNull)`; a struct with the same four members, built by `const fn` constructors, reads better in 41 consts and changes nothing else.
- **Rendering** (`to_json_schema`), deterministic, matching Appendix A.1's example:

  | Spec | Rendered | Rendered for a `Nullable` field |
  |---|---|---|
  | `Str`, `Int`, `Num`, `Bool` | `{"type":"string"}`, `"integer"`, `"number"`, `"boolean"` | `{"type":["string","null"]}` (and so on) |
  | `Enum(vs)` | `{"enum":[…vs]}` (no `type`, as A.1 writes it) | `{"enum":[…vs, null]}` |
  | `Array(s)` | `{"type":"array","items":<s>}` | `{"type":["array","null"],"items":<s>}` |
  | `Object(fs)` | `{"type":"object","properties":{…},"required":[…]}`; `required` lists the `Required` keys in declaration order and is omitted when empty; `properties` is omitted when there are no fields | `{"type":["object","null"],…}` |
  | `OneOf(bs)` | `{"oneOf":[…]}` | `{"oneOf":[…, {"type":"null"}]}` |
  | `Opaque(why)` | `{"type":"object","description":why}` | `{"type":["object","null"],"description":why}` |

  Objects are rendered open (no `additionalProperties`), as M4-D9 requires of published schemas. Decided while writing this bead: these conventions (nullability as a type array, `null` in the enum list or a null branch; `required` omitted when empty), because they are what schemars' serialize contract emits for `Option<T>` of inline types, so the error fragments read like every other published schema.
- **`admits`** is the spec's reference semantics, used by this bead's tests: `Str` admits a string; `Int` an integer JSON number (`is_i64() || is_u64()`), never a float; `Num` any number; `Bool` a boolean; `Enum` a string in the set; `Array` an array whose every item is admitted; `Object` an object holding every `Required` key, holding no key it does not declare, with each present value admitted (`null` only where the field is `Nullable`); `OneOf` a value exactly one branch admits; `Opaque` any object. The `Mismatch` names the first failing path in `declared_paths` syntax (`folders[1].owner`, with the array index). Unknown keys are rejected on purpose: that is how the strict test-side validation of A3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`, schemas and live validation) behaves, so a test passing here does not surprise A3. Decided while writing this bead: `admits` is public, because the integration tests of subtask 5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9.5`) use it; A3 still validates with its JSON Schema validator, which is the contract's proof.
- **Paths** (`declared_paths`, `opaque_paths`): keys only, `a` for a top-level key, `a.b` for key `b` of the object at `a`, `a[].b` for key `b` of the objects in array `a`; `OneOf` branches contribute the union of their paths at the same position; sorted, deduplicated. Example: `items`, `items[].code`, `items[].error`, `items[].error.details`, … A3's report of declared keys no test observes, and A10's manifest (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.10`, the semantic manifest), read these.
- **`well_formed`**: an `Object`'s keys are snake_case, unique and sorted (so declaration order is canonical order); an `Enum` is non-empty, its values unique and snake_case (`[a-z][a-z0-9_]*`); a `OneOf` has at least two branches and no two branches are equal; an `Opaque` reason is non-empty. It recurses.
- **No JSON Schema validator is a dependency yet** (A3 adds `jsonschema`, or `boon`, as a dev-dependency after its `cargo deny` check). "Every spec renders to a valid JSON Schema" is therefore checked structurally: a test-only `check_rendered(&Value)` accepts only the keywords above (`type`, `enum`, `items`, `properties`, `required`, `oneOf`, `description`), each with a value of the right JSON type, `type` from the seven JSON type names, `required` a subset of `properties`' keys without duplicates, and recurses. Decided while writing this bead: the structural check, because adding a validator here would pre-empt A3's dependency decision and its `cargo deny` record; A3 adds meta-schema validation of the same fragments.

### 3. The meanings (subtask 2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9.2`)

- **The row format.** `error_codes!` rows become `Variant = "wire", Exit, retryable, "meaning";` and `warning_codes!` rows `Variant = "wire", "meaning";` (subtask 4, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9.4`, later appends the spec). The macros generate `pub const fn meaning(self) -> &'static str` on both enums; `WarningCode::Item(code).meaning()` returns `code.meaning()`.
- **Writing rules** (decided while writing this bead, because the plan fixes only "one sentence" and "no empty meaning or one without a period"; the style test enforces 1–7 and 9):
  1. One sentence of plain English that says what the code reports: the condition, never the remedy (remedies are each instance's `fix` and the `fix_pattern` of A5, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5`, `robot-docs errors`).
  2. It starts with an ASCII uppercase letter or a backtick and ends with exactly one period; no `?` or `!`, no newline or tab, no leading, trailing or doubled space.
  3. No second sentence: no `. ` followed by an uppercase letter or a backtick ("for example", not "e.g.").
  4. At most 200 characters (`MEANING_MAX_CHARS`, a constant of the test module: a style rule of the registry, not a runtime limit, so it gets no `src/limits.rs` row).
  5. Backticks only around literal names (codes, keys, flags, paths, `/reload`); no other Markdown.
  6. It names no omaddons command: "omaddons" followed by the first word of any `app::COMMANDS` path is refused ("another omaddons process" and "a newer omaddons" are fine). This is not the prose-fix rule of common rule 8, which covers fixes; it keeps meanings from becoming unverified fixes.
  7. It names no milestone. A code no construction site raises says "reserved: no command raises it yet"; the leaf that starts raising it rewrites its meaning in that commit.
  8. `http_status`, `hash_mismatch` and `plan_stale` say when an instance is retryable (Appendix A.1: "`meaning` says when").
  9. All meanings are distinct, errors and warnings together.
  10. Each is the one-sentence gist of README's row (errors `README.md:1825-1867`, column "When"; warnings `README.md:1874-1927`, column "Meaning"). README keeps its longer text until H4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`, the README final pass) makes the tables quote `robot-docs errors`.
- **Examples** (the implementer may refine the wording within the rules):

  | Code | Meaning |
  |---|---|
  | `usage` | The command line was not accepted: an unknown command or flag, a bad value or id, or a missing or relative `HOME`. |
  | `locked` | Another omaddons process held the lock past the acquire timeout. |
  | `http_status` | A host answered with an unexpected HTTP status; an instance is retryable for a 5xx status only. |
  | `hash_mismatch` | Bytes did not match the hash they were expected or recorded with; an instance is retryable on a download's first attempt only, never for a backup. |
  | `plan_stale` | What a command planned or previewed no longer matches the state it would change; an instance is retryable when re-planning raised it, never under `--if-match`. |
  | `plan_not_found` | No stored plan answers to the given id; reserved: no command raises it yet. |
  | `reload_required` (warning) | The change takes effect in game only after a `/reload`. |
  | `journal_pending` (warning) | An interrupted transaction waits for the next change command, or cannot be recovered by this omaddons and is left as it is. |

- **Every row present when the subtask lands**, including any a peer leaf added in between (the warning `target_id_reserved` of C2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.2`, a client named as an addon and `-t all`; `plan_not_stored` of D4, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`, the plan store; the two codes of E3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, `doctor diagnose`): whichever of this bead and that leaf lands second writes the meaning.

### 5. The 41 specs (subtask 4)

#### 5.1 The row column and the accessors

`error_codes!` rows become `Variant = "wire", Exit, retryable, "meaning", specs::CONST;`, with one `pub(crate) const` per code in `src/error/specs.rs`, named after the wire name in upper case (`specs::PLAN_STALE`), in registry order, each with a doc comment naming its construction sites. Decided while writing this bead: named consts rather than inline specs, because some specs run to fifteen lines and the table must stay readable; the row still names its spec, so the fact is declared once, beside the code (M4-D2). The macro generates:

```rust
impl ErrorCode {
    /// What the code means, in one sentence.
    pub const fn meaning(self) -> &'static str;
    /// The code's own `details` specification (M4-D10), without the shared keys.
    pub const fn detail_spec(self) -> &'static DetailSpec;   // match self { $(Self::$variant => &$spec,)+ }
    /// The JSON Schema fragment of this code's `details`: its own keys and `COMMON`'s.
    pub fn details_schema(self) -> serde_json::Value;
    /// Whether `details` matches this code's own keys and `COMMON`'s.
    pub fn check_details(self, details: &serde_json::Value) -> Result<(), Mismatch>;
    /// Every declared key path, own and shared.
    pub fn declared_detail_paths(self) -> Vec<String>;
}
```

If the compiler refuses to promote `&$spec` to `'static` in the `const fn`, declare the consts as `&'static DetailSpec` and return them directly. The 9 doc comments that list `details` keys (for example `DesiredStateInvalid`'s at `src/error.rs:153`) drop the key list, which the spec now holds.

#### 5.2 Keys any code may carry: `COMMON`

Four wrappers add keys to an error whatever its code. Decided while writing this bead: they are declared once, in `specs::COMMON` (all `Optional`), and `details_schema`, `check_details` and `declared_detail_paths` merge them into every code's own fields (own fields win on a name clash, and a unit test asserts that no clash differs in spec), because declaring them on 41 rows would make A3's declared-but-unobserved report demand an `items` test for `usage`.

| Key | Spec | Added by |
|---|---|---|
| `items` | `Array(OneOf[{code: Str, message: Str, request: Str}, {error: ITEM_ERROR nullable, request: Str, target: Str}])`, all keys required | `src/app/install.rs:1366-1378` (`install`, `remove`: every item failed) and `src/app/outcome.rs:595-622` (`pin`, `update`, `sync`, `copy`, `adopt`: every item failed) |
| `required_by` | `Array(Str)` | `src/engine/plan.rs:2409-2425` (a dependency that could not be planned) |
| `journal_pending` | `Str` (a transaction id) | `src/engine/tx.rs:573-590` (a failed commit whose recovery failed too) |
| `recovery_error` | `Object{code: Str, message: Str}` | the same |

`ITEM_ERROR` is the wire form of `ItemError` (`src/app/outcome.rs:165-181`): `{code: Str, details?: Opaque("an item error's kept details: the subset of its own code's details the item keeps"), fix: Str, fix_argv: Array(Str) nullable, message: Str}`, `details` optional because it is skipped when empty.

#### 5.3 How each key is typed

Decided while writing this bead, because the plan states only "record each key's type, nesting, presence and nullability, and every stable enum's closed value set":

- **Required** only when every construction site of the code, pass-through and wrappers included, emits the key. Otherwise `Optional`. So `plan_stale.changed` is optional (re-plan instances carry none; "Where the plan and the code disagree", item 1), and the leaf that makes every instance carry it may tighten it, as a breaking change only before H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, the pre-freeze audit).
- **Nullable** only where a site can emit `null`: `locked.holder` (`HolderInfo` unreadable, `src/fsx/lock.rs:149-159`), `state_too_new.target` and `state_corrupt.target` from an unreadable journal (`parsed.target: Option<TargetKey>`, `src/engine/journal.rs:1131-1157`), `not_found.target` from a backup id prefix without `-t` (`src/backup/mod.rs:424`), `path` in `backup import`'s refusals (`shown()` returns `Option<String>`, `src/backup/import.rs:818-821`, so `unsafe_archive.path`, `bad_archive.path`, `io.path`), `items[].error`.
- **`Enum`** for every top-level `details.reason`, for `changed`, and for every other key whose values are a closed vocabulary of literals or of a Rust enum at the emitting site: `ops[].op` and `running` (`game_running`), `class` (`not_managed`, `unmanaged_folder`), the refused folders' `reason`.
- **`Str`** for names of things defined elsewhere: ids, keys, paths, refs, folder and addon names, families, transaction kinds, and error-code names nested in `details` (`cause`, `items[].code`, `folders[].code`, `recovery_error.code`). Their value sets are owned and published by other registries (`capabilities.families`, the history kinds, `error_codes`), and an enum here would turn every new family or code into a `details` change. M4-D10's own example writes `cause?: string`.
- **`tried[].reason` is `Str`.** In `no_compatible_release`, `wrong_flavor` and `hash_mismatch`, `tried` lists the candidates passed over, and its `reason` mixes refusal codes with prose that interpolates error messages (`src/engine/plan.rs:3689-3696`, `:3756-3765`). It is free text under a key named `reason`; the close comment lists it for H1's naming walk (renaming it is H1's to decide, since it breaks the key).
- **Integers are `Int`** (`line`, `column`, `limit`, `measured`, `status`, `lines`, `hop`, `files`, `first_line`, `other_line`, `pid`, `compressed`, `distinct`); no `details` value is a float at `c0ab5e9`.
- **Declare only what a construction site emits when the subtask lands.** Keys that later leaves add (§7.4 of the plan: `plan_stale.reason`, `path` and `txs` from D5, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`, `omaddons apply`; `locked.lease`; `undo_conflict.paths` and `changed` from E7, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7`, undo of repairs; `usage.target`, `command` and `flag` from C1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.1`, misplaced clients, and C2; `plan_not_found.reason` and `path`; `hash_mismatch.blob` from F6, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.6`, verified blob reads; `scope_denied` reasons `skill_dir` and `symlink` and `not_found.path` from B3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3`, `robot-docs install-skill`; a fence's `tx` and `resource`) are declared by those leaves in the commit that emits them (common rule 6). Pre-declaring them would put unobservable keys on A3's report.

#### 5.4 Two-shape keys

Declared with `OneOf`, not retyped: their emitters belong to no M4 leaf, and a retype is a breaking rename only H1 may make (M4-D55). A unit test, `two_shape_keys_are_the_known_ones`, asserts that the `(code, path)` pairs whose spec contains a `OneOf` are exactly:

- `case_collision`, `ownership_conflict`, `protected_folder`, `unmanaged_folder` `folders[].existing`: `OneOf[Str, Array(Str)]` (one shared `REFUSED_FOLDER` sub-spec);
- `COMMON` `items[]`: the two branches of §5.2.

Its failure message says that a new two-shape key needs a reason in this bead's close comment or its own leaf's, and that one shape is preferred. The close comment lists the three for H1.

Subtasks 2 and 4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9.2`, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9.4`) rewrite every row, so land them early and in one commit each, rebase before each gate run, and do not reflow rows a peer added (the `target_id_reserved` of C2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.2`, D4's `plan_not_stored` and E3's two codes may appear meanwhile; give them their column, or leave the column to them when they land second). A `OneOf` with overlapping branches makes `admits` report "matches 2 branches": give the branches a distinguishing required key. A meaning that paraphrases README badly: H4's comparison catches it. - **Performance.** `details_schema()` renders 41 small trees; the 20 ms budget of A4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`, `omaddons capabilities`) is unaffected.

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M4 plan, 2026-10-24).**

**Why this bead.** omaddons' error catalog is half a contract. The codes, their exits and their default retryability are registered, but nothing says what a code means, and the `details` object every failure carries is an untyped `serde_json::Value` that agents nonetheless branch on (`details.reason`, `details.changed`, `details.holder`, `details.candidates`). After this bead, every error and warning code carries a one-sentence `meaning` beside its wire name, and every error code carries a `DetailSpec`: its keys, their types, nesting, presence, nullability and the closed set of every `reason`. That is the data `capabilities` and `robot-docs errors` publish, the variants of the error schema built by A3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`, schemas and live validation), and what the freeze pins. Without it, M4 would freeze the names of `details` and none of their shapes.

**Decisions applied.**

- **M4-D10:** `details` are typed per code by a recursive specification that is the contract; emitters keep building `Value`; this bead writes the specs (and the meanings), A3 validates them. Rejected: free-form `details` after the freeze, a struct per code now, a key list.
- **M4-D2:** one registry; a fact clap cannot give (the meaning of a code) is declared once, beside the code, and cross-checked against behaviour. README's code tables become the derived copy, which H4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`, the README final pass) holds equal.
- **M4-D55:** rule 4 (closed snake_case enumerations) and rule 6 (every `details` validates against its spec; every declared key observed) hold from slice 1; the leaf that owns a surface corrects a known pre-release inconsistency, here the prose `reason` of archive inspection's `unsafe_archive`.
- **M4-D9 (context):** published fragments stay open; A3 applies strictness in tests.
- **Appendix A.1 (context):** `http_status`, `hash_mismatch` and `plan_stale` are "conditional" in the registry, and their meanings say when an instance is retryable.

**Decided while writing this bead** (each confirmed or adjusted in the close comment): two variants beyond the plan's seven (`OneOf` for the three keys the code emits in two shapes, `Opaque` for the item error's kept details already in `contract::OPAQUE`); a named `Field` struct; named spec consts in `src/error/specs.rs`; a shared `COMMON` fragment for the four keys wrappers add to any code; "Required only when every site emits it", which makes `plan_stale.changed` optional against the plan's example; `Enum` for every `reason`, `changed` and closed literal vocabulary, `Str` for names owned by other registries; `tried[].reason` left as prose for H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, the pre-freeze audit); a closed `HostileReason` for archive inspection; the meaning style rules; a structural schema check instead of a validator dependency; `Action` descriptions left to A2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.2`, the action registry) with a shared check; `fix_pattern` left to A5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5`, `robot-docs errors`); no edit to the hot-spot `journal.rs`.

**Alternatives rejected here.**

- Retyping the two-shape keys to one shape now: a breaking rename on M2-era surfaces that no M4 leaf owns, which M4-D55 reserves for H1. They are declared precisely with `OneOf` and pinned by a test.
- Declaring `reason` as `Str` where an emitter writes prose: it would satisfy the type and defeat the guarantee (an undeclared reason could never fail), contrary to this bead's own acceptance criterion.
- Pre-declaring keys later leaves will emit (`plan_stale.reason`, `locked.lease`, …): unobservable until those leaves land, so they would sit on A3's declared-but-unobserved report; each leaf declares its own.
- Adding `jsonschema` here to prove the fragments valid: it would pre-empt A3's dependency decision and its `cargo deny` record.
- A `debug_assert!` that checks every error's `details` at serialization: it would turn one wrong spec into panics across the whole suite and duplicate A3's validation.

**Risks and how they are watched.** Risk #2 (A3 balloons because live validation finds mismatches) is fed directly by this bead's accuracy. It is watched by the starting inventory of every construction site at `c0ab5e9`, the "Required only when every site emits it" rule, cross-checks against the emitting enums, a source scan for undeclared `reason` literals, and end-to-end tests of the subtle shapes. The hot spot `src/error.rs` (this bead, A9 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9`, then A3; C2 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.2`, D4 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4` and E3 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3` may add rows meanwhile) is handled by landing each row rewrite as one commit and giving peers' rows their columns.

**What it unblocks, and why they wait.** A3 builds its error union from these specs and validates against them, and both rewrite every row, so A3 must come second. A4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`, `omaddons capabilities`) and A5 publish the meanings and specs; the guide of B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`, the guide renderer) quotes the meanings; the slice demo of T2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.2`, slice 1 end to end) validates `details` through them.

**How it serves the milestone.** G-M4-1: the error catalog becomes generated, published and validated fact, so an agent learns what a code means and which `details` to read from the binary. G-M4-5: the freeze covers the shapes agents branch on, not just their names. Checkpoint criterion 2 ("a `details.changed` that turned into a string fails the suite") is only possible because this bead says what `details.changed` is.

**Confidence.** High for the type and the meanings; medium-high for the specs, whose accuracy depends on reading about 120 construction sites once. Any error shows up in A3 as a precise mismatch path, and is fixed where it is found.

title: `DetailSpec`: the typed details description, its JSON Schema rendering and its matcher
description:
Part 1 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9 (A meaning and a typed `DetailSpec` for every code). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

The parent leaf gives every omaddons error and warning code a one-sentence `meaning`, and every error code a typed description of its `details` object, so that `capabilities` and `robot-docs errors` can publish them and the contract suite can validate every real `details` against them (M4-D10: "`error.details` are typed per code by a recursive specification, and are part of the contract"; the specification, not the emitter, is the contract, and emitters keep building `serde_json::Value`). Today `details` is an untyped `Value` (`src/error.rs:512`, `:625`) that agents branch on, so nothing can freeze its shapes.

This part adds the type that description is made of, `DetailSpec`, with its JSON Schema rendering, a reference matcher, path walkers and a well-formedness check, in a new file, and touches no registry row. It is its own step because the type must exist before subtask 4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9.4`, the 41 specs) can write any spec, and because it can be built and fully tested in parallel with the meanings (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9.2`) and the emitter correction (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9.3`).

Facts it relies on (`c0ab5e9`): `src/error.rs` is a single file; the repository already pairs files with same-named directories for submodules (`src/toc.rs` with `src/toc/loaded.rs`, `src/app/adopt.rs` with `src/app/adopt/`), so `src/error/detail_spec.rs` is declared from `src/error.rs`. `src/errors/` is the unrelated Lua error capture. No JSON Schema validator is a dependency (`Cargo.toml:43-53` has none; A3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`, adds `jsonschema` or `boon` after its `cargo deny` check).

## Technical Approach

1. **The module.** Create `src/error/detail_spec.rs`. In `src/error.rs`, add `mod detail_spec;` and `pub use detail_spec::{DetailSpec, Field, Mismatch, Nullability, Presence};` next to the existing `use` lines, and nothing else.
2. **The types.**

   ```rust
   /// A typed description of one error code's `details` object, or of a value inside it (M4-D10).
   #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
   pub enum DetailSpec {
       Str,
       Int,
       Num,
       Bool,
       /// A string from a closed set of snake_case values, in declared order.
       Enum(&'static [&'static str]),
       Array(&'static DetailSpec),
       /// An object with exactly these keys, sorted by key.
       Object(&'static [Field]),
       /// A value matching exactly one of these specs (two or more).
       OneOf(&'static [&'static DetailSpec]),
       /// An object whose keys this spec does not constrain; the text says why.
       Opaque(&'static str),
   }

   #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
   pub enum Presence { Required, Optional }
   #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
   pub enum Nullability { NotNull, Nullable }

   #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
   pub struct Field {
       pub key: &'static str,
       pub spec: &'static DetailSpec,
       pub presence: Presence,
       pub null: Nullability,
   }

   impl Field {
       pub const fn req(key: &'static str, spec: &'static DetailSpec) -> Self;  // Required, NotNull
       pub const fn opt(key: &'static str, spec: &'static DetailSpec) -> Self;  // Optional, NotNull
       pub const fn nullable(self) -> Self;                                     // Nullable, same presence
   }

   #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
   pub struct Mismatch { pub path: String, pub expected: String, pub found: String }
   // Display: "details.<path>: expected <expected>, found <found>" ("details: …" at the root)
   ```

   - Decided while writing this bead: two variants beyond the plan's seven (`Str`, `Int`, `Num`, `Bool`, `Enum`, `Array`, `Object`). `OneOf` exists because the code at `c0ab5e9` emits three keys in two shapes (`ref_ambiguous.details.candidates` as strings or `{ref, from}` objects; the refused folders' `existing` as one name or a pair; the aggregated `items` in two element shapes), and `Opaque` because an aggregated error embeds `ItemError.details` (`src/app/outcome.rs:180`), which the plan already lists as deliberately unconstrained (`contract::OPAQUE`, added by A3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`, schemas and live validation). The plan's intent, a precise type for every key, is kept.
   - Decided while writing this bead: `Field` is a named struct with the four members the plan writes as a tuple (`(key, &DetailSpec, Required | Optional, Nullable | NotNull)`), because subtask 4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9.4`) writes 41 consts with it and `Field::opt("cause", &DetailSpec::Str)` reads better than a four-tuple.
   - Every constructor is a `const fn`, so a spec is a `const` item: `const X: DetailSpec = DetailSpec::Object(&[Field::req("holder", &HOLDER).nullable()]);`. Rust promotes the borrowed temporaries of a `const` initializer to `'static` because the types have no `Drop` and no interior mutability.
3. **`pub const EMPTY: DetailSpec = DetailSpec::Object(&[])`**, the spec of a code whose details are always `{}`.
4. **Rendering: `pub fn to_json_schema(&self) -> serde_json::Value`**, deterministic:

   | Spec | Rendered | Rendered for a `Nullable` field |
   |---|---|---|
   | `Str`, `Int`, `Num`, `Bool` | `{"type":"string"}`, `{"type":"integer"}`, `{"type":"number"}`, `{"type":"boolean"}` | `{"type":["string","null"]}` and so on |
   | `Enum(vs)` | `{"enum":[…vs]}` (no `type`, as the plan's Appendix A.1 example writes it) | `{"enum":[…vs, null]}` |
   | `Array(s)` | `{"type":"array","items":<s>}` | `{"type":["array","null"],"items":<s>}` |
   | `Object(fs)` | `{"type":"object","properties":{<key>: <field spec, nullability applied>},"required":[…]}`; `required` lists the `Required` keys in declaration order and is omitted when there are none; `properties` is omitted when there are no fields | `{"type":["object","null"],…}` |
   | `OneOf(bs)` | `{"oneOf":[…]}` | `{"oneOf":[…, {"type":"null"}]}` |
   | `Opaque(why)` | `{"type":"object","description":why}` | `{"type":["object","null"],"description":why}` |

   Nullability is a property of a field, so it is applied where an `Object` renders its fields; `to_json_schema` on a bare spec renders it not-null. Objects are open: no `additionalProperties`, because M4-D9 keeps published schemas open so a newer minor's additions never break an older consumer's validator (A3's test-side transform adds strictness). Decided while writing this bead: these conventions, because they are what schemars' serialize contract emits for `Option<T>` of inline types, so the error fragments read like every other published schema. `serde_json::Value` (no `preserve_order` feature) sorts object keys, and arrays keep declaration order, so the output is byte-stable.
5. **Matching: `pub fn admits(&self, value: &serde_json::Value) -> Result<(), Mismatch>`**, the spec's reference semantics:
   - `Str` a string; `Int` a number with `is_i64() || is_u64()` (a float such as `1.0` is rejected); `Num` any number; `Bool` a boolean; `Enum` a string in the set;
   - `Array` an array whose every item is admitted (the mismatch path carries the index, `folders[1].owner`);
   - `Object` an object that holds every `Required` key, holds no key it does not declare, and whose present values are each admitted; `null` is admitted only where the field is `Nullable`;
   - `OneOf` a value that exactly one branch admits ("matches no branch" and "matches 2 branches" are both mismatches);
   - `Opaque` any object.

   Unknown keys are rejected on purpose: A3 validates strictly in tests, so a value this matcher admits is one A3 admits too. It is public because the integration tests of subtask 5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9.5`) use it. Decided while writing this bead: `admits` is a small matcher for this bead's own type, not a JSON Schema validator; the plan's rejection of "a hand-written validator for schemars' subset" (M4-D9) is about validating full schemas, which stays A3's job with its validator.
6. **Walkers.**
   - `pub fn declared_paths(&self) -> Vec<String>`: key positions only, `a`, `a.b` (key `b` of the object at `a`), `a[].b` (key `b` of the objects in array `a`); `OneOf` branches contribute the union of their paths at the same position; sorted and deduplicated. A3's report of declared keys no test observes and A10's manifest (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.10`) read it.
   - `pub fn opaque_paths(&self) -> Vec<String>`: the paths, in the same syntax, of every `Opaque` node, for A3's strict transform to leave open.
   - `pub fn field(&self, key: &str) -> Option<&'static Field>` (an `Object`'s field) and `pub fn enum_values(&self) -> Option<&'static [&'static str]>` (an `Enum`'s values, looking through an `Array`), for cross-check tests and for A5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5`, `robot-docs errors`).
7. **`pub fn well_formed(&self) -> Result<(), String>`**, recursive: an `Object`'s keys are snake_case (`[a-z][a-z0-9_]*`), unique and sorted, so declaration order is canonical order; an `Enum` is non-empty and its values unique and snake_case; a `OneOf` has at least two branches, none equal to another; an `Opaque` reason is non-empty. The error names the path and the fault.
8. **A structural check of the rendering**, `#[cfg(test)] pub(crate) fn check_rendered(schema: &Value) -> Result<(), String>` in the same file: an object using only the keywords `type`, `enum`, `items`, `properties`, `required`, `oneOf` and `description`; `type` a JSON type name (`string`, `integer`, `number`, `boolean`, `array`, `object`, `null`) or an array of them; `enum` a non-empty array of distinct strings, with at most one `null`; `items` and every `properties` value and `oneOf` element themselves passing the check; `required` an array of distinct strings, each a key of `properties`; `description` a non-empty string. Decided while writing this bead: a structural check stands in for "renders to a valid JSON Schema", because no validator is a dependency until A3, and adding one here would pre-empt A3's dependency decision and its `cargo deny` record; A3 adds meta-schema validation of the same fragments.
9. **Nothing else.** No registry row, no other file, no output change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `src/error/detail_spec.rs` defines `DetailSpec` (nine variants), `Field` with `req`, `opt` and `nullable` as `const fn`, `Presence`, `Nullability`, `Mismatch`, `DetailSpec::EMPTY`, and the methods `to_json_schema`, `admits`, `declared_paths`, `opaque_paths`, `field`, `enum_values` and `well_formed`; `src/error.rs` re-exports the types.
- [ ] A spec can be written as a `const` item (a unit test declares a nested one).
- [ ] Every rendering of the table above is produced exactly (unit test), and the output is byte-identical across two calls.
- [ ] `admits` accepts and rejects each case of its table, rejects unknown keys, and names the failing path with array indexes.
- [ ] `well_formed` rejects each fault of its table and accepts a correct nested spec.
- [ ] Every rendered case passes `check_rendered`, and `check_rendered` rejects each malformed fragment of its table.
- [ ] No other output changes; `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

All in `src/error/detail_spec.rs`'s `tests` module, table-driven, each case named.

- `renders_each_variant`: cases `str`, `int`, `num`, `bool`, `enum`, `array_of_str`, `object_required_and_optional` (`{a: req Str, b: opt Int}` → `"required":["a"]`), `object_without_required` (no `required` key), `empty_object` (`{"type":"object"}`), `nullable_str_field`, `nullable_enum_field` (`{"enum":["x","y",null]}`), `nullable_object_field`, `nullable_array_field`, `one_of`, `nullable_one_of`, `opaque`, `nullable_opaque`, `nested_array_of_objects`. Each compares `to_json_schema()` with an expected `serde_json::json!` value, and a second call with the first (byte-identical through `serde_json::to_string`).
- `specs_are_const_items`: a `const NESTED: DetailSpec` three levels deep compiles and renders.
- `admits_and_rejects`: cases `str_ok`, `str_given_int`, `int_ok`, `int_given_float` (`1.0` rejected), `num_given_int` (accepted), `bool_given_string`, `enum_member`, `enum_outsider` (expected names the set), `missing_required`, `missing_optional` (accepted), `unknown_key` (rejected, path `extra`), `null_for_not_null`, `null_for_nullable` (accepted), `nested_failure` (path `folders[1].owner`), `one_of_no_branch`, `one_of_two_branches` (two identical-shaped open branches), `one_of_one_branch` (accepted), `opaque_any_object` (accepted with nested objects), `opaque_given_string`, `object_given_array`.
- `mismatch_names_the_path_and_both_sides`: the `Display` of three mismatches (root, nested key, array index).
- `well_formed_rejects_each_fault`: cases `unsorted_keys`, `duplicate_key`, `camel_case_key`, `empty_enum`, `duplicate_enum_value`, `enum_value_with_dash`, `one_branch_one_of`, `equal_one_of_branches`, `empty_opaque_reason`, `fault_deep_inside` (the message names the nested path); and `well_formed_accepts_a_correct_nested_spec`.
- `declared_paths_walk_every_level`: `{a: Array(Object{b: Str}), c: OneOf[Str, Array(Str)], d: Object{e: Opaque}}` gives `a`, `a[].b`, `c`, `d`, `d.e`; a `OneOf` of two objects gives the union of their keys.
- `opaque_paths_find_each_opaque_node`: the same spec gives `d.e`; an `items[].error.details` shaped spec gives that path.
- `field_and_enum_values_reach_inside`: `field("changed")` of a `plan_stale`-shaped spec and `enum_values()` through its `Array`.
- `rendered_schemas_pass_the_structural_check`: every case of `renders_each_variant` passes `check_rendered`.
- `the_structural_check_rejects_each_fault`: cases `unknown_keyword` (`additionalProperties`), `bad_type_name`, `empty_enum`, `required_not_in_properties`, `duplicate_required`, `items_not_a_schema`, `empty_description`.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

None in this part: subtask 5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9.5`) holds the integration tests.

### Logging

Every assertion message names the case and shows the input and the output, for example `assert_eq!(got, want, "case {name}: spec {spec:?} rendered {got}")` and, for `admits`, the value, the expected result and the `Mismatch` actually returned.

## Considerations

- **Keep it small and dependency-free.** The module uses `serde_json` only. It derives no `Serialize` or `JsonSchema`: specs are rendered by `to_json_schema`, so no serialized type gains a field (DEC-3) and the `OPAQUE` scan of serialized `Value` fields that A3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`) adds is unaffected.
- **Hot spot `src/error.rs`** (§10.5: A9, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9`, this bead, then A3; later leaves append rows). This part touches only the module declarations at its top, so it does not conflict with the row rewrite of subtask 2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9.2`); rebase before the gate run.
- **What could go wrong.** A `const` promotion error when a spec borrows a non-promotable expression: keep every nested spec a literal or a named `const`. Recursion depth is tiny (three or four levels), so the recursive walkers need no bound.
- Decisions taken here and listed for the leaf's close comment: the two added variants, the named `Field`, the rendering conventions, the public `admits`, the structural check.

## Dependencies

- Parent: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9 (A meaning and a typed `DetailSpec` for every code).
- Before it: nothing; it can start at once, in parallel with subtasks 2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9.2`) and 3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9.3`).
- After it: subtask 4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9.4`, the 41 specs) writes every spec with this type, and subtask 5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9.5`) checks real envelopes with `admits` through `ErrorCode::check_details`.

title: A one-sentence `meaning` for every error and warning code
description:
Part 2 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9 (A meaning and a typed `DetailSpec` for every code). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

The parent leaf gives every omaddons error and warning code a one-sentence `meaning`, and every error code a typed `details` specification, so that `capabilities` and `robot-docs errors` publish them (vision §5.10 lists `error_codes (meaning, exit code, retryable)` among `capabilities`' keys) and the freeze pins them. M4-D2 requires such a fact, which clap cannot provide, to be declared exactly once, beside the code it describes; "the meaning of an error code" is one of the plan's own examples. Today the registries hold only the wire name, the exit and the default retryability, and just 9 of 41 error rows have a doc comment (`src/error.rs:153`, `:172-173`, `:175`, `:177-178`, `:180-181`, `:186`, `:189`, `:191`, `:193`).

This part adds the `meaning` column to every row of both registries, the accessors that read it, and the style test. It is its own step because it rewrites every row of `error_codes!` and `warning_codes!` (the hot spot of §10.5, where this bead, A9 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9`, lands before A3 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`, schemas and live validation, under the rule "A9, then A3"), independent of the spec type, and because its 93 sentences are careful writing work of their own. Subtask 4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9.4`) appends the spec column to the same error rows afterwards, so it waits for this part.

Facts it relies on (`c0ab5e9`):

- `error_codes!` is defined at `src/error.rs:111-147` (row pattern `$(#[$doc:meta])* $variant:ident = $wire:literal, $exit:ident, $retryable:literal;`) and invoked under `#[rustfmt::skip]` at `:149-204` (41 rows). It generates `ErrorCode::ALL`, `wire()`, `exit()` and `default_retryable()`.
- `warning_codes!` is defined at `src/error.rs:215-243` (row pattern `$(#[$doc:meta])* $variant:ident = $wire:literal;`) and invoked at `:245-349` (52 rows). It generates `WarningCode`, whose extra untagged variant `Item(ErrorCode)` (`:224-227`) is a per-item failure mirrored into `warnings` with the error's wire name; `WarningCode::ALL` (`:232`) excludes `Item`.
- Count tests: `src/error.rs:803` (41) and `:847` (52).
- README's tables: errors `README.md:1822-1869` (columns Code, Exit, Retryable, When), warnings `README.md:1871-1929` (columns Code, Meaning). The warning summary at `README.md:1872` says "Every warning code (51)", but the table has 52 rows, one per code: the count is wrong at `c0ab5e9`.
- `app::COMMANDS` (`src/app/mod.rs:121-165`) lists the 42 command paths.
- Appendix A.1 of the plan: `retryable` per code is `"conditional"` for `plan_stale`, `http_status` and `hash_mismatch`, whose instances decide (`Error::plan_stale` retryable only for re-planning, `src/error.rs:587-593`; `Error::http_status` for 5xx only, `:580-584`; `Error::hash_mismatch` on attempt 1 only, `:597-599`), and for those three "`meaning` says when".

## Technical Approach

1. **The macros.**
   - `error_codes!` rows become `Variant = "wire", Exit, retryable, "meaning";`. The pattern gains `, $meaning:literal` after `$retryable:literal`, and the macro generates:

     ```rust
     /// What the code reports, in one sentence (published by `capabilities` and `robot-docs errors`).
     pub const fn meaning(self) -> &'static str { match self { $(Self::$variant => $meaning,)+ } }
     ```
   - `warning_codes!` rows become `Variant = "wire", "meaning";`, generating `WarningCode::meaning()` with `Self::Item(code) => code.meaning()`.
   - Keep `#[rustfmt::skip]` and the column alignment style of the existing rows; a long meaning may continue on the next line, indented under the wire name.
2. **The writing rules.** Decided while writing this bead, because the plan fixes only "one sentence" and "no meaning empty or ending without a period". The style test enforces 1–7 and 9:
   1. One sentence of plain English that says what the code reports: the condition, never the remedy. Remedies are each instance's `fix` and the `fix_pattern` of A5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5`, `robot-docs errors`).
   2. It starts with an ASCII uppercase letter or a backtick and ends with exactly one period: no `?` or `!`, no newline or tab, no leading, trailing or doubled space.
   3. No second sentence: no `. ` followed by an uppercase letter or a backtick (write "for example", not "e.g.").
   4. At most 200 characters (`MEANING_MAX_CHARS`, a constant of the test module: a style rule of the registry, not a runtime limit, so it gets no `src/limits.rs` row).
   5. Backticks only around literal names (codes, keys, flags, paths, `/reload`); no other Markdown.
   6. It names no omaddons command: "omaddons" followed by the first word of any `app::COMMANDS` path is refused, while "another omaddons process" and "a newer omaddons" are fine. This keeps meanings from becoming unverified fixes; it is separate from common rule 8's prose-fix rule.
   7. It names no milestone. A code no construction site raises says "reserved: no command raises it yet" (`plan_not_found`, `distribution_disabled`); the leaf that starts raising it rewrites the meaning in that commit.
   8. `http_status`, `hash_mismatch` and `plan_stale` say when an instance is retryable.
   9. All 93 meanings are distinct.
   10. Each is the one-sentence gist of its README row (the "When" column for errors, "Meaning" for warnings). README keeps its longer text; H4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`, the README final pass) later makes the tables quote `robot-docs errors` and checks they agree.
3. **Examples** (refine the wording within the rules if needed):

   | Code | Meaning |
   |---|---|
   | `usage` | The command line was not accepted: an unknown command or flag, a bad value or id, or a missing or relative `HOME`. |
   | `locked` | Another omaddons process held the lock past the acquire timeout. |
   | `http_status` | A host answered with an unexpected HTTP status; an instance is retryable for a 5xx status only. |
   | `hash_mismatch` | Bytes did not match the hash they were expected or recorded with; an instance is retryable on a download's first attempt only, never for a backup. |
   | `plan_stale` | What a command planned or previewed no longer matches the state it would change; an instance is retryable when re-planning raised it, never under `--if-match`. |
   | `plan_not_found` | No stored plan answers to the given id; reserved: no command raises it yet. |
   | `distribution_disabled` | A source declined to distribute a file to third-party clients; reserved: no command raises it yet. |
   | `reload_required` (warning) | The change takes effect in game only after a `/reload`. |
   | `journal_pending` (warning) | An interrupted transaction waits for the next change command, or cannot be recovered by this omaddons and is left as it is. |
4. **Every row present when this part lands.** If a peer leaf added a row meanwhile (C2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.2`: the warning `target_id_reserved`; D4, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`: `plan_not_stored`; E3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`: `online_required`, `doctor_refused`), write its meaning too; if it lands after, it writes its own (common rule 6: "whichever lands second"). Take the counts from the registry, never from literals.
5. **The sentence check**, `src/error/sentence.rs`, declared from `src/error.rs` as `#[cfg(test)] pub(crate) mod sentence;`:

   ```rust
   #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
   pub(crate) enum SentenceFault { Empty, Start, NoClosingPeriod, Whitespace, SecondSentence, TooLong(usize), NamesCommand(String), NamesMilestone }
   pub(crate) const MEANING_MAX_CHARS: usize = 200;
   pub(crate) fn check(text: &str) -> Result<(), SentenceFault>;
   ```

   `NamesCommand` takes the first words of `crate::app::COMMANDS` paths; `NamesMilestone` refuses `M1`…`M9` as whole words.
6. **`Action` descriptions are A2's** (A2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.2`, the action, event, env and feature registries). The plan's step also says "`Action` (A2) gets its description". A2 creates `contract::actions::Action` with `wire()`, `description()` and `destructive()` (M4-D11), and is not an edge of this bead. Decided while writing this bead: this part does not touch `Action`. If `Action::ALL` exists when this part lands, add `action_descriptions_are_one_sentence` running `sentence::check` over every description; if not, A2 adds it when it lands (whichever lands second), and the leaf's close comment says which happened.
7. **README.** `README.md:1872`: "Every warning code (51)" becomes "Every warning code (52)" (or the count at the time). Nothing else in README changes in this part.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every row of `error_codes!` and `warning_codes!` present when this part lands carries a meaning; `ErrorCode::meaning()` and `WarningCode::meaning()` exist as `const fn`, and `WarningCode::Item(code).meaning() == code.meaning()`.
- [ ] `every_code_has_a_one_sentence_meaning` passes over `ErrorCode::ALL` and `WarningCode::ALL`, enforcing writing rules 1–7 and 9.
- [ ] The meanings of `http_status`, `hash_mismatch` and `plan_stale` say when an instance is retryable (`conditional_retryability_is_stated`).
- [ ] The sentence check rejects each fault of its table and accepts each allowed form.
- [ ] If `Action::ALL` exists, its descriptions pass the same check.
- [ ] README says "Every warning code (52)".
- [ ] No output changes (meanings are not on the wire until A4, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`, and A5, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5`, publish them); the count tests and `EXPECTED` stay as they are; `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

- **`src/error.rs`** `tests`:
  - `every_code_has_a_one_sentence_meaning`: for every `ErrorCode::ALL` and `WarningCode::ALL` entry, `sentence::check(meaning)` is `Ok`; a failure names the wire name, quotes the meaning and the `SentenceFault`.
  - `meanings_are_distinct`: the 93 meanings (errors and warnings together) are pairwise different; a failure names both codes.
  - `item_warnings_take_their_error_meaning`: for every `ErrorCode::ALL` entry `c`, `WarningCode::Item(c).meaning() == c.meaning()`.
  - `conditional_retryability_is_stated`: the meanings of `http_status`, `hash_mismatch` and `plan_stale` contain "retryable".
  - `action_descriptions_are_one_sentence` (only if `Action::ALL` exists, see step 6).
- **`src/error/sentence.rs`** `tests`:
  - `sentence_check_rejects_each_fault`: cases `empty` (`""`), `lowercase_start` (`"a thing failed."`), `no_period` (`"A thing failed"`), `question` (`"A thing failed?"`), `two_periods` (`"A thing failed.."`), `trailing_space` (`"A thing failed. "`), `double_space`, `newline`, `second_sentence` (`"A failed. Then B."`), `second_sentence_after_backtick` (``"A failed. `x` too."``), `too_long` (201 characters), `names_a_command` (`"Run omaddons undo first."` → `NamesCommand("undo")`), `names_a_milestone` (`"Arrives in M5."`).
  - `sentence_check_accepts_the_allowed_forms`: cases `backtick_start` (``"`--offline` blocked a request."``), `the_word_omaddons` (`"A newer omaddons wrote this file."`), `semicolon_and_colon` (`"A failed: the cause; retryable once."`), `exactly_200_characters`.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

None in this part.

### Logging

Each assertion message names the code (or the case), quotes the text and shows the fault, for example `"{wire}: {meaning:?} breaks the meaning style: {fault:?}"`.

## Considerations

- **Hot spot `src/error.rs`** (§10.5: A9, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9`, this bead, then A3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`, because both touch every row; later leaves append rows with their specs). Land this part as one commit; rebase right before the gate run; never reflow or reorder a row a peer added. Subtask 4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9.4`) rewrites the same error rows again, after this part, so the two never run in parallel.
- **README is the source, not the target.** Do not edit README's tables to match the new sentences; only the count. H4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`, the README final pass) reconciles.
- **What could go wrong.** A paraphrase that changes meaning: compare each sentence with its README row once more before committing. A meaning that sneaks in a remedy ("…; run …"): rule 1 and the `NamesCommand` check catch the obvious cases; review the rest. A meaning that is true only today (a reserved code): rule 7's wording makes the later rewrite explicit.
- Decisions taken here and listed for the leaf's close comment: the writing rules and `MEANING_MAX_CHARS`, `Action` left to A2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.2`), the README count fix.

## Dependencies

- Parent: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9 (A meaning and a typed `DetailSpec` for every code).
- Before it: nothing; it can start at once, in parallel with subtasks 1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9.1`) and 3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9.3`).
- After it: subtask 4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9.4`) appends the spec column to the same rows, so it waits for this part to avoid two rewrites of one table at once.

- [ ] `every_code_has_a_one_sentence_meaning` passes over `ErrorCode::ALL` and `WarningCode::ALL`, enforcing writing rules 1–7 and 9.
- [ ] The meanings of `http_status`, `hash_mismatch` and `plan_stale` say when an instance is retryable (`conditional_retryability_is_stated`).
- [ ] The sentence check rejects each fault of its table and accepts each allowed form.

title: Closed snake_case `reason` codes for archive inspection's `unsafe_archive`
description:
Part 3 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9 (A meaning and a typed `DetailSpec` for every code). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

The parent leaf types every error code's `details` with a `DetailSpec` (M4-D10), whose stable enums (`details.reason`, `details.changed`) carry a closed set of values, and its acceptance criteria require that "every `reason` and `changed` value any construction site emits is in its enum". M4-D55's rule 4 says the same for every enumeration of the contract: snake_case values, a closed set in its schema.

One emitter makes that impossible today. Archive inspection builds every hostile-entry refusal (`unsafe_archive`, exit 4) as `json!({"entry": entry, "reason": why})` (`src/engine/inspect.rs:192-198`), where `why` is the prose of the message: "contains a control character", "climbs out of its folder with '..'", and, from `:332`, `format!("collides with {other:?} once case is ignored")`, which interpolates another archive entry's name. No closed enum can hold that. This part gives those refusals closed snake_case reason codes, leaving every message byte-identical. It is its own step because it is the leaf's only behaviour change on the wire, in a file no other part touches, and subtask 4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9.4`) must declare the final values.

Why this is this leaf's to change: M4-D10 makes the specification, not the emitter, the contract, and gives the writing of the specs to this leaf; M4-D55 lets the leaf that owns a surface fix a known pre-release inconsistency, recording it with a compatibility note, while any other rename waits for H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, the pre-freeze audit). Decided while writing this bead: this leaf owns the typing of `error.details`, so it corrects an emitter only where no closed spec can describe it (this one); every other inconsistency is described as it is and listed for H1.

Facts it relies on (`c0ab5e9`):

- `fn hostile(entry: &str, why: &str) -> Error` at `src/engine/inspect.rs:192-198` calls `archive_error(ArchiveFault::Hostile, format!("the archive entry {entry:?} {why}"), json!({"entry": entry, "reason": why}))`; `archive_error` (`:165-189`) maps `ArchiveFault::Hostile` to `ErrorCode::UnsafeArchive` with a prose fix and passes `details` through.
- Its callers: `:244`, `:247`, `:251`, `:258`, `:272`, `:273` (entry-name and entry-type checks), `:332` (the case-folded tree, three messages), `:541-544`, `:548`, `:554`, `:589` (directory inspection), `:708` (a read past the declared size), `:742` (an addon root whose name is not a valid folder name).
- Two sibling refusals already emit codes: `ratio_exceeded` (`:216-224`, `"reason": "ratio"`) and the duplicate-name count (`:390-394`, `"reason": "duplicate_entry"`).
- `backup import`'s `unsafe_archive` reasons are already snake_case (`src/backup/import.rs:840-871`: `unsupported_entry`, `bad_name`, `duplicate_name`, …); this part does not touch them.
- Nothing reads these values: the only `details["reason"]` readers in `src/` concern other codes, the widget (`omarchy/`) never reads `unsafe_archive`'s details, and the one `unsafe_archive` contract snapshot is `backup import`'s (`tests/contract/snapshots/contract__matrix__backup_import_unsafe_archive.snap`). The tests assert only the code and the message (`tests/inspect.rs:72-188`, `tests/engine_fallbacks.rs:140-200`).

## Technical Approach

1. **`HostileReason`** in `src/engine/inspect.rs`, public, so the cross-check of subtask 4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9.4`) and the integration tests of subtask 5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9.5`) can read it:

   ```rust
   /// Why archive inspection refused an entry: `details.reason` of its `unsafe_archive`.
   #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
   pub enum HostileReason { ControlCharacter, AbsolutePath, DriveLetter, ParentDir, Symlink, SpecialFile,
       FileAndDirectory, DuplicateEntry, CaseCollision, NotUtf8, SizeOverrun, InvalidFolderName, Ratio }
   impl HostileReason {
       pub const ALL: [HostileReason; 13] = [ /* every variant */ ];
       pub const fn wire(self) -> &'static str; // "control_character", "absolute_path", …
   }
   ```
2. **`fn hostile(entry: &str, reason: HostileReason, why: &str) -> Error`**: the message stays `format!("the archive entry {entry:?} {why}")`; `details` become `{"entry": entry, "reason": reason.wire()}`. `ratio_exceeded` uses `HostileReason::Ratio.wire()` and the duplicate count `HostileReason::DuplicateEntry.wire()`, so every `unsafe_archive` archive inspection raises draws its reason from one type.
3. **The mapping.** Decided while writing this bead (the names; re-read every `hostile(` call and give each its value):

   | Call site | Prose kept in the message | `details.reason` |
   |---|---|---|
   | `:244` | contains a control character | `control_character` |
   | `:247` | is an absolute path | `absolute_path` |
   | `:251` | starts with a drive letter | `drive_letter` |
   | `:258` | climbs out of its folder with '..' | `parent_dir` |
   | `:272`, `:554` | is a symlink | `symlink` |
   | `:273`, `:589` | is a device, FIFO or socket | `special_file` |
   | `:332`, first branch | is both a file and a directory (with …) | `file_and_directory` |
   | `:332`, second branch | appears twice | `duplicate_entry` |
   | `:332`, third branch | collides with … once case is ignored | `case_collision` |
   | `:541-544` | has a name that is not UTF-8 | `not_utf8` |
   | `:548` | contains a control character or backslash | `control_character` |
   | `:708` | expands past the size its header declares | `size_overrun` |
   | `:742` | cannot be an addon folder: … | `invalid_folder_name` |
   | `:216-224` | the compression ratio | `ratio` |
   | `:390-394` | entries sharing one name | `duplicate_entry` |

   At `:332` the three messages come from one `match`; return the reason beside each message (`(HostileReason, String)`).
4. **README.** In the `unsafe_archive` row of the error table (`README.md:1843`), after "the compression-ratio limit", add: "an installed archive's `details.reason` names the rule it broke (`parent_dir`, `absolute_path`, `drive_letter`, `control_character`, `not_utf8`, `symlink`, `special_file`, `file_and_directory`, `duplicate_entry`, `case_collision`, `size_overrun`, `invalid_folder_name`, `ratio`) and `details.entry` the entry". Keep the rest of the row.
5. **The close comment** (for the leaf) records the pre-release correction: "`unsafe_archive.details.reason` from archive inspection: prose → the closed `HostileReason` codes above; message, exit, fix and `details.entry` unchanged; no reader in the widget, the guide or the snapshots."
6. **Do not** change `backup import`'s refusals, `bad_archive`'s `malformed()` reasons (already codes) or any message.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `HostileReason` exists with `ALL` (13 values) and `wire()`; its wires are unique snake_case.
- [ ] Every `hostile(` call passes a `HostileReason`; `ratio_exceeded` and the duplicate count use `HostileReason::Ratio` and `HostileReason::DuplicateEntry`; no `unsafe_archive` raised by `src/engine/inspect.rs` carries a `details.reason` outside `HostileReason::ALL`.
- [ ] Every message is byte-identical to before (unit test over each case's message).
- [ ] README's `unsafe_archive` row lists the codes.
- [ ] Every existing test passes unchanged (`tests/inspect.rs`, `tests/engine_fallbacks.rs`, the contract suite); no snapshot is re-accepted; `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

In `src/engine/inspect.rs`'s `tests` module, table-driven:

- `hostile_reasons_are_closed_codes`: one case per reachable value, each driving the smallest input that reaches the check (an entry name through the name check, a mode through the type check, two names through the case-folded tree, a directory entry through directory inspection where a unit-level entry point exists). Cases: `control_character` (`Foo/a\x07.lua`), `absolute_path` (`/etc/x`), `drive_letter` (`C:/x`), `parent_dir` (`Foo/../../x`), `symlink` (mode `0o120777`), `special_file` (mode `0o020644`), `file_and_directory` (`Foo/x`, `Foo/X/y`), `duplicate_entry` (`Foo/a.lua` twice), `case_collision` (`Foo/a.lua`, `Foo/A.lua`), `size_overrun` (a read error whose text says the header's size was passed), `invalid_folder_name` (an addon root `.hidden`). Each asserts `err.code == ErrorCode::UnsafeArchive`, `err.details["reason"] == <expected wire>` and that `err.message` equals the message the old code produced for that input (written out literally in the case).
- `hostile_reason_wires_are_unique_snake_case`: over `HostileReason::ALL`, each wire matches `[a-z][a-z0-9_]*` and none repeats; `ALL` holds every variant (an exhaustive `match` in the test fails to compile when a variant is added without listing it).

### Integration and end-to-end tests

None in this part: subtask 5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9.5`) asserts each reason through `tests/inspect.rs`'s hostile tables and through the binary.

### Logging

Each assertion names the case and shows the input, the expected reason and the error actually returned (`code`, `message`, `details`).

## Considerations

- **Privacy and bounds.** The prose that moves out of `details.reason` interpolated archive entry names; `details.entry` still carries the refused entry, as before. Archive entries are addon file names, never paths below `WTF/`, so common rule 9's redaction does not apply.
- **No collision rule.** `src/engine/inspect.rs` is not a §10.5 hot spot; README is edited only in its own row.
- **What could go wrong.** A case reaching a different check than expected (for example a backslash name normalized before the `..` check): the unit test fails with the reason actually given; adjust the case or the mapping and record the change in the leaf's close comment.
- Decisions taken here and listed for the leaf's close comment: that this leaf corrects the emitter, the reason names, the README row.

## Dependencies

- Parent: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9 (A meaning and a typed `DetailSpec` for every code).
- Before it: nothing; it can start at once, in parallel with subtasks 1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9.1`) and 2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9.2`).
- After it: subtask 4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9.4`) declares `unsafe_archive`'s reason enum from `HostileReason::ALL` and `backup import`'s values, and subtask 5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9.5`) proves the codes end to end.

title: A `DetailSpec` in every `error_codes!` row, with the keys every code may carry
description:
Part 4 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9 (A meaning and a typed `DetailSpec` for every code). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

The parent leaf types every omaddons error code's `details` object (M4-D10). Each `error_codes!` row gains a `DetailSpec`: the allowed keys, each key's type (string, integer, number, boolean, array of a spec, object of a spec), nesting, whether each key is required and whether it may be null, and the closed set of every stable enum (`reason`, `changed`). Emitters keep building `details` as `serde_json::Value`; the specification is the contract. A3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`, schemas and live validation) builds the error envelope's schema as a union discriminated by `code`, one variant per code carrying its spec, and validates every observed `details` against it; A4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`, `capabilities`) and A5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5`, `robot-docs errors`) publish each spec as `details_schema`. *Why:* agents branch on `details` (`details.reason`, `details.changed`, `details.holder`), and a list of keys would freeze names only, letting `details.changed` turn into a string or a `reason` gain values unnoticed. *Rejected:* free-form `details` after the freeze, a struct per code now, a key list.

This part writes the 41 specs and the keys any code may carry, adds the spec column to every `error_codes!` row and the accessors the consumers read, and cross-checks the specs against the emitting code. It is the leaf's main reading work: about 120 `.details(` construction sites in 44 files outside `src/error.rs`, plus wrappers and pass-through. It needs the type (subtask 1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9.1`), the rows as subtask 2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9.2`) leaves them (the same rows, rewritten once more), and the closed archive-inspection reasons of subtask 3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9.3`).

The type it uses (from subtask 1, in `src/error/detail_spec.rs`, re-exported from `crate::error`): `DetailSpec::{Str, Int, Num, Bool, Enum(&[&str]), Array(&DetailSpec), Object(&[Field]), OneOf(&[&DetailSpec]), Opaque(&str)}`, `Field::{req, opt}(key, &spec)` and `.nullable()`, `DetailSpec::EMPTY`, and the methods `to_json_schema`, `admits`, `declared_paths`, `opaque_paths`, `field`, `enum_values`, `well_formed`. Rendering: scalars `{"type":"string"}` and so on, `Enum` as `{"enum":[…]}`, objects open with `required` in declaration order (omitted when empty), nullability as a type array, `null` in the enum or a null branch; object keys must be sorted, unique and snake_case.

## Technical Approach

### 1. The row column and the accessors

- `error_codes!` rows become `Variant = "wire", Exit, retryable, "meaning", specs::CONST;` (the pattern gains `, $spec:path` after `$meaning:literal`).
- `src/error/specs.rs` (new, declared from `src/error.rs` with `mod specs;`) holds one `pub(crate) const` per code, named after the wire name in upper case (`PLAN_STALE`), in registry order, each with a doc comment naming its construction sites, plus the shared sub-specs (`REFUSED_FOLDER`, `ITEM_ERROR`, `HOLDER`, `TRIED`) and `COMMON`. Decided while writing this bead: named consts rather than inline specs, because some run to fifteen lines and the table must stay readable; the row still names its spec, so the fact is declared once, beside the code (M4-D2).
- The macro generates, beside `meaning()`:

  ```rust
  /// The code's own `details` specification (M4-D10), without the shared keys.
  pub const fn detail_spec(self) -> &'static DetailSpec { match self { $(Self::$variant => &$spec,)+ } }
  ```

  If the compiler refuses to promote `&$spec`, declare the consts as `&'static DetailSpec` and return them directly.
- And, outside the macro, in `src/error.rs`:

  ```rust
  impl ErrorCode {
      /// The JSON Schema fragment of this code's `details`: its own keys and `COMMON`'s.
      pub fn details_schema(self) -> serde_json::Value;
      /// Whether `details` match this code's own keys and `COMMON`'s.
      pub fn check_details(self, details: &serde_json::Value) -> Result<(), Mismatch>;
      /// Every declared key path, own and shared (`DetailSpec::declared_paths` syntax).
      pub fn declared_detail_paths(self) -> Vec<String>;
  }
  ```

  The merge takes the code's own fields and `COMMON`'s, sorted by key, an own field winning on a name clash. `details_schema()` is what A3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`) puts in each variant of its error union, what A4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`, `capabilities`) and A5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5`, `robot-docs errors`) publish, and what A10 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.10`, the semantic manifest) records.
- The doc comments on rows that list `details` keys (`DesiredStateInvalid` `:153`, `FilesystemUnsupported` `:177-178`, `RateLimited` `:186`) drop the key list, which the spec now holds.

### 2. `COMMON`: keys any code may carry

Four wrappers add keys to an error whatever its code. Decided while writing this bead: they are declared once, all `Optional`, and merged into every code, because declaring them on 41 rows would put an `items` key on `usage` that no test could ever observe (A3 reports declared-but-unobserved keys, and H1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, makes that report an assertion).

| Key | Spec | Added by |
|---|---|---|
| `items` | `Array(OneOf[{code: Str, message: Str, request: Str}, {error: ITEM_ERROR, nullable; request: Str; target: Str}])`, every key of each branch required | `src/app/install.rs:1366-1378` (`install`, `remove`: every item failed) and `src/app/outcome.rs:595-622` (`pin`, `update`, `sync`, `copy`, `adopt`: every item failed) |
| `required_by` | `Array(Str)` | `src/engine/plan.rs:2409-2425` (a dependency that could not be planned) |
| `journal_pending` | `Str` (a transaction id) | `src/engine/tx.rs:573-590` (a failed commit whose recovery failed too) |
| `recovery_error` | `Object{code: Str, message: Str}` | the same |

`ITEM_ERROR` is the wire form of `ItemError` (`src/app/outcome.rs:165-181`): `{code: Str, details: opt Opaque("an item error's kept details: the subset of its own code's details an item keeps"), fix: Str, fix_argv: req Array(Str) nullable, message: Str}`. `details` is optional because `ItemError` skips it when empty; it is `Opaque` because the plan already lists `ItemError.details` (`src/app/outcome.rs:180`) in `contract::OPAQUE` (A3), and `opaque_paths()` reports it as `items[].error.details` for A3's strict transform.

### 3. How each key is typed

Decided while writing this bead, because the plan states only "record each key's type, nesting, presence and nullability, and every stable enum's closed value set":

- **`Required`** only when every construction site of the code, pass-through and wrappers included, emits the key; otherwise `Optional`. `plan_stale.changed` is therefore optional, although M4-D10's example and Appendix A.1 mark it required: at `c0ab5e9` only `src/app/precondition.rs:214-225` sets it, and the re-plan instances carry `{}` (`src/engine/swap.rs:914-920`, `src/engine/restore_addons.rs:713-719`, `:783-791`, `src/engine/restore.rs:778-786`, `src/sources/git_hosts.rs:488-492`) or `{cause, cause_message}` (`src/engine/tx.rs:1376-1386`).
- **`Nullable`** only where a site can emit `null`: `locked.holder` (`src/fsx/lock.rs:149-159`), `state_too_new.target` and `state_corrupt.target` from an unreadable journal (`parsed.target: Option<TargetKey>`, `src/engine/journal.rs:1131-1157`), `not_found.target` for a backup prefix without `-t` (`src/backup/mod.rs:424`), the `path` of `backup import`'s refusals (`shown()` returns `Option<String>`, `src/backup/import.rs:818-821`: `unsafe_archive.path`, `bad_archive.path`, `io.path`), `items[].error`, `ITEM_ERROR.fix_argv`.
- **`Enum`** for every top-level `details.reason`, for `changed`, and for every key whose values are a closed vocabulary of literals or a Rust enum at the emitting site: `ops[].op` and `running` (`game_running`), `class` (`not_managed`, `unmanaged_folder`, `REFUSED_FOLDER`), `REFUSED_FOLDER.reason`.
- **`Str`** for names of things defined elsewhere: ids, keys, paths, refs, folder and addon names, families, transaction kinds, and error-code names nested in `details` (`cause`, `items[].code`, `ITEM_ERROR.code`, `REFUSED_FOLDER.code`, `recovery_error.code`); their value sets belong to other registries (`capabilities.families`, the history kinds, `error_codes`), and M4-D10's own example writes `cause?: string`.
- **`tried[].reason` is `Str`.** In `no_compatible_release`, `wrong_flavor` and `hash_mismatch`, `tried` (`TRIED = Array(Object{asset: Str, reason: Str})`) lists the candidates passed over; its `reason` mixes refusal codes with prose that interpolates error messages (`src/engine/plan.rs:3689-3696`, `:3756-3765`). The close comment lists it for H1's naming walk.
- **Integers are `Int`**: `line`, `column`, `first_line`, `other_line`, `limit`, `measured`, `compressed`, `distinct`, `status`, `lines`, `hop`, `files`, `pid`. No `details` value is a float at `c0ab5e9`.
- **Declare only what a construction site emits when this part lands.** Keys later leaves add are theirs to declare in the commit that emits them (common rule 6): `plan_stale.reason`, `path`, `txs` (D5, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`); `locked.lease`; `undo_conflict.paths` and `changed` (E7, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7`, undo of repairs); `usage.target`, `command`, `flag` (C1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.1`, misplaced clients, and C2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.2`, `-t all`); `plan_not_found.reason`, `path`; `hash_mismatch.blob` (F6, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.6`, verified blob reads); `scope_denied` reasons `skill_dir`, `symlink` and `not_found.path` (B3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3`, `robot-docs install-skill`); a fence's `tx` and `resource`; the new codes `online_required` and `doctor_refused` (E3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`). The plan's "43 specs" counts E3's two; this part writes 41.
- **Every row present when this part lands**, including any a peer added meanwhile (E3's codes): whichever lands second writes the spec.

### 4. Two-shape keys

Declared with `OneOf`, not retyped: their emitters belong to no M4 leaf, and a retype breaks a key, which M4-D55 reserves for H1.

- `ref_ambiguous` `candidates[]`: `OneOf[Str, Object{from: Str, ref: Str}]` (objects at `src/sources/refs.rs:645-648`; strings at `src/app/remove.rs:338`, `src/app/restore_addons.rs:369`, `:414`, `src/backup/mod.rs:447`).
- `REFUSED_FOLDER.existing` (in `case_collision`, `ownership_conflict`, `protected_folder`, `unmanaged_folder`): `OneOf[Str, Array(Str)]` (a pair for `case_duplicates`, `src/engine/ownership.rs:278`; one name at `:305`, `:352`, `:370`, `:384`).
- `COMMON` `items[]`: the two branches of §2.

### 5. The starting inventory (`c0ab5e9`)

What each code's construction sites emit, read from the code while planning. It is a starting point: the construction sites are the authority. Re-read each one (`grep -rn "ErrorCode::<Variant>\|\.details(" src`, and each helper constructor and pass-through), and record in each spec's doc comment where its keys come from. "Always" means every construction site found; `{}` a site with no details. Line numbers are those of the `.details(` call.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every `error_codes!` row present when this part lands names its spec; `ErrorCode::detail_spec()` (`const fn`), `details_schema()`, `check_details()` and `declared_detail_paths()` exist.
