title: The guide's content
description:
## How to work this bead

This bead is worked through its 3 subtasks, listed below in work order. Claim a subtask, not this bead (`br ready --parent omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.2` lists the ready ones). The agent that closes the last open subtask then verifies every acceptance criterion of this bead (they are the leaf's, not any one subtask's), and closes this bead with `br close omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.2 --reason "done: <evidence> · found: <ids>"`. Until this bead is closed, every bead it blocks stays blocked.

1. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.2.1 The guide's content checks: the size budget, the recipe grammar, registered names and command fragments: `tests/skill.rs` and `tests/common/guide.rs` gain the checks the final prose must pass (the 500-line and 32 KiB budget, the `sh recipe=` grammar and its fill rules, every backticked name registered, every command and command fragment parsing, plain Markdown the extractors can read). They pass on the skeleton of B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`, the guide renderer), so they land first and the prose is written against them.
2. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.2.2 The guide's prose and its eight recipes, with `SKILL.md` regenerated: `src/contract/guide/guide.md` rewritten to the outline below (the core loop with its reconcile step, the per-client wording of the preview guarantee, the advice to ignore unknown names, the safety model, the eight recipes, the doctor loop), `ERRORS_COMMON` updated, the outline test, the truth audit, the de-slopify and `rumdl` passes, README's sentence, and the regenerated `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md`.
3. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.2.3 E2E: the guide's core loop and doctor loop run as written: `tests/skill_loops.rs` runs the core loop (preview, apply, a lost output reconciled with `plans show`, a second apply refused, the escape hatch) and the doctor loop (triage, the recommended repair, the two kinds of run told apart, the repair undone) exactly as the guide writes them, and runs every read-only command the guide names on a synthetic home.

The subtasks form one chain (1 → 2 → 3): the prose is written against the checks of subtask 1, and the end-to-end suite extracts its commands from the prose of subtask 2. The size stays M: one Markdown template of about 10 KiB of prose, a few test helpers, and three scenario tests; no command, no wire shape and no product code beyond one list in `render.rs`. The leaf closes only when all three parts are done, so B4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.4`, the recipes run end to end) never sees half of it.

## Background

### Why this work exists

M4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`, the agent surface, the doctor and the first tag) makes omaddons describe itself to a coding agent that has never seen it. One of the three calls such an agent needs is `omaddons robot-docs guide`, the agent handbook, which is also the committed `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` and the skill `omaddons robot-docs install-skill` installs, byte for byte (M4-D7). B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`, the guide renderer and `robot-docs guide`) built the mechanism: the template `src/contract/guide/guide.md`, a renderer that splices registry-generated blocks into it, the stamp, the command and the byte-identity test. B1 shipped a **skeleton**: every section heading, every placeholder, and short holding prose that names only M1–M3 commands, because the commands the guide must teach (`apply`, `plans show`, the doctor verbs, undo of repairs) did not exist yet.

This bead writes the guide's real content: the prose of every section of the outline, the eight canonical recipes an agent copies verbatim, and the tests that keep that prose true. **An agent copies the guide verbatim, so every claim in it must be true of the code**: every command parses and runs, every name it uses is registered, and the two loops it teaches (the core loop and the doctor loop) work as written on a real binary. The bead lands late by design (slice 4), after `apply` (D5, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`), `plans show` (D9, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.9`) and the doctor's triage, fix and undo of repairs (E4, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4`; E6, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`; E7, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7`), so the guide describes M4's final behaviour rather than a moving target.

At `c0ab5e9` there is no guide at all: an agent learns omaddons from README's hand-written "For coding agents" block (`README.md:2743-2798`), which drifts with every change and already teaches flows M4 replaces (`update --all --dry-run --json # then without --dry-run`). H4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`, the README final pass) later turns that block into a pointer to the skill plus a short excerpt of this bead's core loop.

### Goals and checkpoint criteria it serves

- **G-M4-1, self-describing:** "An agent with no prior knowledge learns everything it needs from the binary itself, in at most three calls: `omaddons capabilities --json`, `omaddons robot-docs guide`, `omaddons status --json`. Every fact in those outputs is generated from the code, so it cannot drift from what the code does." The guide's tables are generated (B1); this bead makes its prose checkable against the code, so it cannot drift silently either.
- **G-M4-2, the first guess works,** in spirit: the guide's commands are the ones an agent will guess from; each parses, and each read-only one runs.
- **G-M4-3, what was previewed is what runs, target by target:** the guide states the guarantee exactly as the code keeps it: per client, never invocation-wide, with `outcomes[]` saying what happened where, and `plans show` answering a lost output.
- **G-M4-4, diagnosable and repairable:** the doctor loop (triage, then the recommended repair or explanation, then undo) is taught once, correctly, and tested end to end.
- **Vision G4, agent ergonomics:** "the first command an agent guesses works". The guide is where an agent with the skill installed starts.

Checkpoint criteria (run by H6, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`):
- **Criterion 3 (the guide and the skill), its last bullet, which this bead owns:** "The guide is under 500 lines and 32 KiB." The other bullets are B1's (byte identity, the stamp, the fixed point), those of B3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3`, install-skill writes the same bytes) and of F10 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.10`, skill drift).
- **Criterion 4 (canonical intents):** "Each of the eight canonical intents (vision §5.10, listed in §6.3.4) takes at most two omaddons commands with JSON output, and each is a recipe in `SKILL.md` that `tests/skill_recipes.rs` runs end to end on a synthetic home with recorded HTTP fixtures." This bead writes the eight recipes and enforces the two-command limit; B4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.4`, the recipes run end to end) runs them.
- **Criterion 18 (README and vision), in part:** README describes what exists; this bead updates the guide's README section.

### The decisions that shape it

(The full decision log is also filed as comments on the milestone epic `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`.)

- **M4-D7: the guide, `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` and the installed skill are one artifact.** `robot-docs guide` renders hand-written prose from the embedded template `src/contract/guide/guide.md` with generated blocks spliced in by a small renderer (`{{name}}` placeholders, no template-engine crate). The generated blocks are the command table, both exit dictionaries, the error catalog summary, the "will never do" list, the env-var table, the action table and the stamp. The document opens with YAML frontmatter (`name: omaddons`, `description: …`, the text Claude Code uses to decide when to load the skill), and the stamp `<!-- omaddons guide sha256:<hex> -->` is the line right after it. **Size budget: at most 500 lines and 32 KiB (test).** Detail lives in `capabilities`, `robot-docs errors` and `robot-docs schema`, which the guide points to. *Why:* splicing generated tables into hand prose keeps the prose readable and the tables true, and a skill is loaded into an agent's context window, so it must be small; 500 lines is a generous ceiling for the core loop, the safety rules and the recipes. *Rejected, and do not be tempted:* a fully generated guide (unreadable prose); a fully hand-written guide (its tables drift). For this bead: write prose, never type a table the renderer generates, and keep the stamp on the line after the frontmatter even though a Markdown linter would like a blank line there.
- **M4-D63: `plans show` inspects an approval and reconciles it with history.** `omaddons plans show <PLAN_ID> [--json]` is read-only, offline and write-free; it returns the stored approval, history's evidence keyed by the plan id (every line carrying `plan: <id>`, as `{target, tx, result, at}`), a `state` (`pending`, `completed`, `partial`, `expired` or `unknown`) and `evidence.complete`. Success is never inferred from current addon versions. **The guide's core loop says: when an `apply`'s result is unknown (a broken pipe, an agent restart), run `plans show` before previewing again or changing anything.** *Why:* an agent can lose stdout after a successful commit; a retry then reports `plan_stale` (or `already_applied`), which does not say whether the first attempt succeeded. *Rejected:* a `plans list` (an agent keeps its own plan ids); making `apply` silently idempotent (it would hide a partial application). This bead is listed in M4-D63's tasks for exactly that core-loop step.
- **M4-D61: one applier per plan, and the guarantee is per target.** On each target a bound run commits exactly the approved operations or none of them; a multi-target run is one transaction per target and can end partial; `apply`'s `outcomes[]` reports each target as `committed`, `unchanged`, `stale` or `failed` with its transaction id or error code; nothing calls such a run atomic. A preview that would change nothing stores no plan (`plan_id: null`, no `apply` hint). The guide states the guarantee in these per-client words, never as "exactly that or nothing" for a whole invocation.
- **M4-D23, M4-D24, M4-D20: `apply` and the plan lifecycle.** `omaddons apply <PLAN_ID>` executes the stored typed intent bound to its stored token. Its refusals are `plan_stale`, never retryable, with `details.reason` `expired` (past the 24-hour `PLAN_TTL`), `binary_changed` (another build), `input_missing` (a local archive or `sync` file gone) or `already_applied` (history records it, with `details.txs`), and `details.changed` naming the token part when the world moved; a missing, unknown or unreadable plan is `plan_not_found`. `apply` revalidates every source, so a release landing since the preview stales the plan rather than installing something the user did not see. The guide's "previews bind" bullet restates exactly this.
- **M4-D22: which commands store plans.** `install`, `update`, `pin`, `unpin`, `adopt`, `sync`, `copy`, `remove`, `undo`, `backup restore` and `backup prune` store a plan on `--dry-run`; `capabilities.commands[].stores_plan` and the guide's command list say which. `doctor fix` and `doctor gc` bind with `--if-match` but store nothing.
- **M4-D34 and M4-D40: the doctor's JSON and exits.** Every doctor verb puts its report at the top level (`state`, `summary`, `findings`, …) with the general envelope keys around it and **no `data` key**; `ok` is `exit_code == 0`; findings (exit 1), a partial fix (2) and a rolled-back fix (3) are reports, not errors. The doctor tree uses its own exit dictionary (`0 healthy`, `1 findings_present`, `2 fix_partial`, `3 fix_failed_rolled_back`, `4 refused_unsafe`, `5 concurrency_lost`, `6 online_required`, `64 usage_error`, `66 no_input`, `73 cannot_create`, `74 io_error`). An agent that reads doctor output like any other envelope would look for `data` and treat exit 1 as a failure, so the guide says both.
- **M4-D46 and M4-D38: undo of repairs, and the force gate.** `omaddons undo` (bare, `<tx>`, `--run`, `--last-by`) reverts a repair like any change, strictly: it refuses with `undo_conflict` before moving anything once something the repair touched has changed. `doctor undo [<run>]` resolves a doctor run to the same code. A set-aside of a stuck journal needs `--force --yes` and is never part of a default fix; the widget never runs one, because a forced repair needs someone who has read what it does. The guide tells an agent never to add `--force --yes` itself.
- **M4-D8 (one line of it):** "Bare help's discovery line and the guide name `robot-docs install-skill`." Nothing recommends installing the skill unasked; the guide names the command in "Where to look next".
- **M4-D3 and M4-D56: the contract version.** The envelope's `schema_version` is the contract version; after the tag an additive change needs `1.1` and a breaking one `2.0`. Hence the guide's advice: within `1.x`, ignore keys, enum values, codes and actions you do not know.
- **M4-D55 (the leaves that may land after the audit):** B2 is among the leaves that may land after H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, the pre-freeze audit) closes; none of them adds a wire shape. This bead adds no wire name at all. A rename H1 makes on a surface it owns updates the guide in the same commit, and this bead's name check points at the line.
- **M4-D2: one contract registry feeds every description of the CLI.** The command table, the exits, the common errors, the actions, the env vars, the `-t` forms and the NEVER list are generated by B1's blocks; the hand-written prose may not restate a table.

### Facts this bead relies on (as of `c0ab5e9`, verified)

- There is no `src/contract/` and no `skills/` directory; B1 creates `src/contract/guide/{mod.rs,render.rs,stamp.rs,guide.md}`, `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md`, `tests/skill.rs` and `tests/common/guide.rs`, and E4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4`) adds `doctor.md` and one placeholder row (`{{doctor_commands}}`) without editing `guide.md`. B1's interface, which this bead builds on: `contract::guide::TEMPLATE` (the template text), `render_guide()`, `render::{render, GuideInputs, PLACEHOLDERS, NEVER, ERRORS_COMMON}`; the twelve placeholders of `guide.md` (`{{stamp}}`, `{{commands}}`, `{{actions}}`, `{{exit_general}}`, `{{exit_doctor}}`, `{{errors_common}}`, `{{never}}`, `{{env}}`, `{{targets}}` as whole lines in their own paragraphs, and the inline `{{command_count}}`, `{{error_code_count}}`, `{{warning_code_count}}`); the test helpers `SKILL_FILE`, `REGENERATE`, `skill_path()`, `committed()`, `rendered(log, on)`, `layout(text)`, `first_difference(a, b)`, `sha256_hex(text)` and `unparsable(text)` with its `SAMPLES` table; the tests `skill_md_is_the_guide`, `every_command_the_guide_names_parses`, `a_planted_unparsable_span_is_reported` and `guide_size_is_reported` (a report only; B1 left the assertion to this bead).
- The global flag `--actor` records who acts (`src/cli.rs:75-77`); `history`'s filter by actor is `--by` (`src/app/history.rs:41-43`), and `--since` takes `30m`, `12h`, `1d`, `2w` or an RFC 3339 time (`:35-37`). **`history --actor agent` therefore lists every actor's changes**, which is why the `undo-agent-today` recipe uses `--by agent` (see plan versus code below).
- `undo` takes `[TX]` (default: the most recent run, `src/app/undo.rs:37-40`), `--last-by <actor>` (`:41-48`) and `--run <RUN>` (`:49-51`, which conflicts with both). `TxKind::is_undoable` excludes only backup and settings lines (`src/model.rs:451-453`), so an undo is itself undoable, and `history::newest_run` selects the newest undoable line of that actor (`src/state/history.rs:609-633`): **a second `undo --last-by agent` reverts the agent's own undo** (a redo), not the run before. README states "An undo is itself undoable" (`README.md:88`). The guide says so and names `undo --run <run>` for an earlier run.
- `update` with no names updates every managed addon on every client (`src/app/update.rs:41-46`, the help's examples at `src/cli.rs:478-483`); `outdated --changelog` adds release notes (`src/app/outdated.rs:64-66`); `sync [FILE] --locked` installs the versions the file records (`src/app/sync.rs:45-47`, `:54-56`).
- Refs (`src/sources/refs.rs:1-5`, `src/app/install.rs:52-56`): canonical refs (`gh:`, `git:`, `url:`, `file:`, `wowi:`, `tukui:`, `wowace:`), pasted URLs, local zip or folder paths, `owner/repo` shorthand, installed names and catalog names.
- The envelope (`src/output/envelope.rs:20-38`): `ok, schema_version, tool_version, command, exit_code, partial?, data?, error?, warnings, commands, meta`; `partial` is present whenever the command produced data (`:27-29`), `error` exactly when `ok` is false (`:32-34`). `ErrorBody` is `{code, message, fix, fix_argv, alternatives, retryable, details}` (`src/error.rs:618-625`), each alternative a `Suggestion {display, argv}` (`:383-388`), each `commands[]` entry a `CommandHint {action, command, argv, destructive}` (`:441-447`).
- Items live in `data.items` only for single-target commands (`InstallData`, `src/app/install.rs:95-102`); multi-target commands put them in `data.targets[].items` (`TargetsData`, `src/app/outcome.rs:248-275`). The typed `data.approval` that D4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`, the plan store) adds to every storable dry run is the one place a preview's changes have the same shape for every command.
- 41 error codes (`src/error.rs:150-204`), among them `plan_not_found` (`:160`, raised by no code at `c0ab5e9`; the meaning A9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9`, a meaning for every code) gives it calls it reserved until D5 raises it), `locked` (`:183`, retryable) and `plan_stale` (`:194`, registered retryable, each instance deciding); 52 warning codes with `WarningCode::ALL` and `wire()` (`src/error.rs:232-240`); `Exit::ALL` with `name()` (`src/error.rs:20-60`). E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, `doctor diagnose` and the doctor exit dictionary) adds two codes (43).
- `app::COMMANDS` (`src/app/mod.rs:121-165`, 42 rows of `{name, group, mutates}`, `:100-108`) and `command_name(Option<&Command>)` (`:195`); A1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1`) adds `dictionary`, `exits`, `data`, `stores_plan` and `network` to each row. `Cli` disables clap's own help flag (`src/cli.rs:25-41`), so `--help` is a global flag and `Cli::try_parse_from` returns `Ok` for `… --help`.
- `PLAN_TTL` is one day (`src/limits.rs:49`); the guide's "24 hours" is checked against it.
- `shell-words` is a dependency (`Cargo.toml:28`); there is no regex or Markdown crate, so the test extractors are hand-written over a deliberately simple Markdown subset.
- `TestEnv` points every XDG directory into a tempdir, strips the developer's `OMADDONS_*` variables and sets `TZ=UTC` (`tests/common/env.rs:9-21`); `Home::new(&["wow"])` builds a synthetic retail client in a Wine prefix (`tests/common/home.rs:27-52`), `home.state()` is `<state>` (`:63-66`) and `home.addons("_retail_")` its `Interface/AddOns` (`:59-61`). A local zip whose TOC says `## Interface: 120105` installs on it by path (`tests/install.rs:736-757`). The first change on a client writes a `target.json` marker into the client dir that stays after undo, by design (`README.md:2658`), so a round trip compares `Interface/AddOns`, never the whole client dir.
- `rumdl` 0.2.78 is on the development machine, and the repository has no rumdl configuration, so a plain `rumdl check` reads the user's own configuration (machine-local line length and disabled rules). With `--no-config`, its defaults report MD013 (lines over 80 characters) and MD071 (no blank line after frontmatter) on the guide's required layout and nothing else (checked while writing this bead on a draft rendered with stand-in blocks).

### Plan versus code (found while writing this bead)

- The plan's `undo-agent-today` recipe is `omaddons history --actor agent --since 1d --json`. At `c0ab5e9` `--actor` is the global attribution flag (`src/cli.rs:75-77`) and the filter is `--by` (`src/app/history.rs:41-43`); with `--actor` the recipe would list every actor's changes while parsing cleanly. Decided while writing this bead: the recipe is `omaddons history --by agent --since 1d --json`, which keeps the plan's intent.
- The plan's core loop (§4.1's transcript, step 3) says "Show the user `data.items`". At `c0ab5e9` `items` is top-level only for single-target commands (`src/app/install.rs:95-102`) and per target for `update`, `sync` and `copy` (`src/app/outcome.rs:248-275`). Decided while writing this bead: the guide points at `data.approval.selection` and `data.approval.reasons`, the typed approval summary D4 adds to every storable dry run (M4-D24, M4-D28), which has one shape for every command.
- The plan's intent "undo what the agent did today" in two commands meets the code's undo rule: `undo --last-by agent` reverts the agent's newest run only, and running it again reverts that undo (facts above). Decided while writing this bead: the recipe keeps the plan's commands, and its lead line says that an earlier run is reverted with `undo --run <run>` from the history listing, so the recipe never promises more than one run.
- The plan's outline (Appendix C.1) says of the two kinds of run that "each command refuses the other's with the right fix". The specification of E7 has `undo --run <doctor run id>` refused with the fix `omaddons doctor undo <id>`, but `doctor undo <history run>` refused as "not a doctor run id" with the fix `omaddons help doctor undo`. Decided while writing this bead: the guide states only the first.
- The plan asks for `rumdl check` on the rendered file with "no new findings". rumdl 0.2.78's defaults flag the guide's required layout (MD071, the stamp on the line after the frontmatter) and its unwrapped prose (MD013), and the repository has no rumdl configuration, so the result of a plain run depends on the user's own. Decided while writing this bead: a fixed invocation with `--no-config` and those two rules disabled, and zero findings (section 7).

## Technical Approach

### 1. Files

| File | Subtask | Change |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/common/guide.rs` | 1 | `GUIDE_MAX_LINES`, `GUIDE_MAX_BYTES`, the extended `SAMPLES`, `commands()` (full commands, recipe lines and fragments), `fill()`, `argv()`, `inline_spans()`, `recipes()`, `Vocabulary`, `classify()`, `unregistered()`, `sections()`, `simple_markdown()` |
| `tests/skill.rs` | 1, 2 | the size assertion (replacing `guide_size_is_reported`), the extended parse check, the recipe grammar, the name check, the Markdown check; then the outline test |
| `src/contract/guide/guide.md` | 2 | the final prose (the template; generated blocks stay placeholders) |
| `src/contract/guide/render.rs` | 2 | `ERRORS_COMMON`: `locked` out, `plan_not_found` in; the unit test `errors_common_holds_no_reserved_code` |
| `src/error.rs` | 2, only if needed | `plan_not_found`'s meaning, if D5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`, `apply`) left it "reserved" |
| `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` | 2 | regenerated with `OMADDONS_UPDATE_SKILL=1 cargo test --test skill` |
| `README.md` | 2, 3 | one sentence in the `robot-docs guide` section; the tests-table row gains `tests/skill_loops.rs` |
| `tests/skill_loops.rs` (new) | 3 | the three end-to-end scenarios |

No command, flag, data key, error, warning, action, event, kind, file kind or constant is added or changed. `src/limits.rs` is not touched: the guide's budget is a test budget, not a product limit (the plan's constants table lists "the guide under 500 lines and 32 KiB" among the budgets that are not constants).

### 2. The outline (Appendix C.1 of the plan, restated) and what each section must say

The document, in this order. Every `##` heading below is exact; there is one `#` heading and no `###` heading.

1. **Frontmatter**, unchanged from B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`, the guide renderer): `name: omaddons` and the trigger sentence below, verbatim. Then `{{stamp}}` on the next line, then B1's generated-by comment line.

   ```yaml
   ---
   name: omaddons
   description: Manage World of Warcraft addons on Linux with the omaddons CLI — install, update, preview and apply exactly, undo, back up WTF/, read Lua errors, and run `omaddons doctor`. Use whenever the user mentions WoW addons, a WoW client (retail, Classic Era, Anniversary, Mists Classic, Forever, a private server), BugGrabber/Lua errors, or addon backups.
   ---
   ```

   Decided while writing this bead: **the description stays verbatim, em dash included.** It is the plan's fixed trigger text; every capability it names exists once this bead's blockers have landed (preview and apply exactly: D5; `omaddons doctor`: E3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, and E4, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4`), which subtask 2 rechecks. Replacing the em dash with a colon, as the de-slopify pass would, would put `: ` inside the value and make it an unsafe YAML plain scalar, which B1's `layout()` check rejects.
2. **`# omaddons for agents`**: what it is in one short paragraph (one binary for every client on this Linux machine with `{{command_count}}` commands; every change a journaled, undoable transaction; previews applied exactly; one JSON envelope per command with fixes as argv), plus the discovery trio `omaddons capabilities --json`, `omaddons robot-docs schema <command>`, `omaddons robot-docs errors`.
3. **`## The core loop`**: six numbered steps (§4.1 of the plan): status; preview with `--dry-run --json` (returns `data.plan_id`) unless the user asked for exactly that change; show `data.approval.selection` and `data.approval.reasons`, then `omaddons apply <plan_id> --json --actor agent --reason "<why>"`; **step 4, the reconcile step: a lost `apply` output → `omaddons plans show <plan_id> --json` before previewing or changing anything again**; something broken → the doctor loop; the escape hatch `omaddons undo --last-by agent --json`. Then one line: pass `--actor agent` and a `--reason` on every change.

````markdown
# omaddons for agents

omaddons manages World of Warcraft addons for every client on this Linux machine, with one binary of {{command_count}} commands. Every change is a journaled transaction that `omaddons undo` reverts, a preview can be applied exactly as it was shown, and with `--json` every command prints one envelope whose errors carry their fix as an argv. Ask the binary for the rest: `omaddons capabilities --json`, `omaddons robot-docs schema <command>` and `omaddons robot-docs errors`.

## The core loop

1. `omaddons status --json`: every client, what needs attention, and the next commands in `commands[]`.
2. Preview a change before you make it, unless the user asked for exactly that change: add `--dry-run --json`, as in `omaddons update --dry-run --json`. The preview changes nothing and returns `data.plan_id`.
3. Show the user `data.approval.selection` (each change) and `data.approval.reasons` (anything beyond a routine update). When they approve, run `omaddons apply <plan_id> --json --actor agent --reason "<why>"`.
4. Lost an `apply`'s output? Run `omaddons plans show <plan_id> --json` before you preview or change anything again: it says whether the plan committed.
5. Something broken? Follow the doctor loop below.
6. The escape hatch: `omaddons undo --last-by agent --json` reverts the newest run an agent made.

Pass `--actor agent` and a `--reason` on every change: history records both.

## Reading the envelope

With `--json`, stdout is one JSON object: `ok`, `schema_version`, `tool_version`, `command`, `exit_code`, `partial`, `data`, `error`, `warnings`, `commands` and `meta`.

- `error` is present exactly when `ok` is `false`. It carries `code`, `message`, `fix`, `fix_argv`, `alternatives`, `retryable` and `details`. `fix_argv` is `null` when the fix is prose or needs a value only you can supply.
- `partial: true` with exit 0 means some items failed; `data` says which and why.
- `warnings` never change the exit code. `commands` are the suggested next steps, each with `action`, `command`, `argv` and `destructive`; ask the user before running one marked `destructive: true`.
- Run `fix_argv`, `alternatives[].argv` and `commands[].argv` as argv arrays, never through a shell. Never parse `message`, `fix`, `command` or human output: branch on `exit_code`, `error.code` and `data`.
- Doctor commands put their report at the top level instead of in `data` (`state`, `summary`, `findings`). There `ok` means exit 0, and findings (exit 1) are a report, not an error.
- `schema_version` is the contract version. A `1.x` release only adds keys, enum values, codes and actions, so ignore the ones you do not know.

Each `commands[]` entry names its `action`:

## Targets and refs

`-t` names a client in any of these forms, tried in this order:

{{targets}}

The client always goes in `-t`, as in `omaddons update -t retail`. A command that acts on one client needs `-t` when several match (`target_ambiguous` lists them), and `-t all` selects every client where a command takes several. `omaddons targets --json` lists the clients.

Refs: a catalog name, `gh:Owner/Repo` or `Owner/Repo`, `wowi:<id>`, `tukui:<slug>`, `wowace:<slug>`, `git:https://…#<rev>`, `url:https://…`, a pasted addon page link, or a local zip or folder. `omaddons search <words> --json` finds one.

## The safety model

- **Transactions.** Every change is one journaled transaction per client, and a crash leaves each client wholly old or wholly new. Bare `omaddons undo` reverts the newest run, `--last-by agent` the newest run by an agent, `undo <tx>` one transaction and `undo --run <run>` one run. An undo is itself a change: running the same undo again puts the change back.
- **Running clients.** A folder change while a client runs needs `--while-running`, and the user then types `/reload` in game (`data.reload_required`). SavedVariables are never written while the client runs, whatever the flags.
- **Previews bind.** `omaddons apply <plan_id>` runs exactly what the preview showed, or refuses with `plan_stale` and changes nothing; `--if-match <data.precondition>` binds a typed run the same way. `plan_stale` from a bound run is never retryable: `details.changed` or `details.reason` (`expired`, `binary_changed`, `input_missing`, `already_applied`) says why, and its `fix_argv` previews again. A plan lives 24 hours; after that, or once the cache is cleared, `apply` answers `plan_not_found`. A preview that would change nothing stores no plan (`plan_id` is `null`).
- **Per client.** On each client a bound run commits exactly the approved operations or none of them. A run over several clients is one transaction per client, so it can end partial: `data.outcomes[]` gives each client's `status` (`committed`, `unchanged`, `stale` or `failed`) with its `tx` or `error_code`. No run over several clients is atomic.
- **Lost output.** `plans show` reads history: its `state` is `pending`, `completed`, `partial`, `expired` or `unknown`, and `evidence` lists each committed client with its `tx`. A second `apply` of an applied plan refuses with `already_applied`; it never applies twice.
- **The doctor.** `omaddons doctor` only reads. `doctor fix` changes things only when run, backs up what it replaces and deletes nothing. `undo` reverts a repair as long as nothing it touched has changed since; after such a change it refuses with `undo_conflict` before moving anything.
- **Two kinds of run.** History's `run` is one omaddons invocation, a ULID, reverted with `undo --run <run>`. A doctor run is a directory of reports and backups named by its UTC time and a ULID, reverted with `doctor undo <doctor_run>`. `undo --run` given a doctor run refuses, and its fix is the matching `doctor undo`.

## Recipes

Each recipe is at most two commands; run them in order. `expect=` lists each command's exit code (`|` separates alternatives), and a `# <name> is …` line says which field of the first command's JSON fills a placeholder. Use them for requests the user made explicitly, and preview anything else first, as the core loop says.

```

```sh recipe=whats-broken expect=0,0|1

```

Install an addon on one client:

```sh recipe=install-for-target expect=0

```

Add a legacy addon from a git repository:

# <plan_id> is data.plan_id of the command above

```

Undo what the agent did today. `undo --last-by agent` reverts the newest agent run; revert an earlier one with `undo --run <run>` from the list:

## Errors you will meet

omaddons has {{error_code_count}} error codes and {{warning_code_count}} warning codes. Branch on `error.code`, never on `message`. `retryable: true` means the same command may succeed if run again: `locked` (another omaddons is committing), `network`, and `rate_limited` after `details.reset_at`. `game_running` means the user must quit the game; never work around it. **The grammar** (decided while writing this bead; the plan fixes the info string `sh recipe=<id> expect=<exit>[,<exit>]` and "a declared rule (`plan_id ← data.plan_id`)" but not their exact syntax, and B4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.4`) runs what this grammar describes):
````

- A recipe is a fenced block whose info string is exactly `sh recipe=<id> expect=<item>[,<item>…]`, single spaces, no other attribute.
  - `<id>` is kebab-case: `[a-z][a-z0-9]*(-[a-z0-9]+)*`. Ids are unique in the guide.

| a command or a fragment (starts with `omaddons `, or with a `COMMANDS` path's first word and has two or more words) | `plans show`, `undo --run <run>` | skipped here: the parse check above owns it |
| anything else | `-t all`, `/reload`, `1.x`, `gh:Owner/Repo`, `addons.toml` | not checked (logged as such, so a reviewer sees the list) |

`Vocabulary::load(log, on)` takes error and warning codes from `ErrorCode::ALL` and `WarningCode::ALL` (`wire()`), exit names from `Exit::ALL` and E3's `doctor::Exit::ALL` (`name()`), actions from `contract::actions::Action::ALL` (`wire()`) of A2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.2`, the registries), path words from `app::COMMANDS`, long flags from a walk of `Cli::command()` after `.build()` (every argument's `get_long()` and visible long aliases), property names and `enum`/`const` strings from a recursive walk of `omaddons robot-docs schema --json`'s `data` and `omaddons robot-docs errors --json`'s `data` (every key of every `properties` object, every string in every `enum` array and every string `const`), and failure-mode ids from `omaddons doctor capabilities --json` (`detectors[].id` and `fixers[].id`, read at the top level, since doctor reports have no `data`). Adapt the import paths to what landed; the sources are the published registries, never a copy. A failure reads "src/contract/guide/guide.md:<line>: `<span>` is not a registered <kind>: <reason>. Fix the guide, or register the name where it belongs." `a_planted_unregistered_name_is_reported` runs the classifier over synthetic prose holding `` `no_such_code` ``, `` `data.no_such_key` ``, `` `--no-such-flag` `` and `` `fm-no-such-mode` `` (each reported with its kind) and `` `plan_stale` ``, `` `data.plan_id` `` and `` `--dry-run` `` (none reported).

**`the_guide_uses_simple_markdown`**: the extractors above rely on a subset: inline code only in single backticks (no double-backtick span), an even number of backticks on every line outside fences, fences opened and closed by a line that starts with exactly three backticks at column 0 (no `~~~`, no indented fence), no tab, no HTML other than the two comment lines after the frontmatter. Failures name the template line.

**`the_guide_follows_its_outline`** (subtask 2), over the rendered guide, using `guide::sections(text)`:
- the `##` headings are exactly the twelve titles of section 2, items 3 to 14, in order, after one `# omaddons for agents`, with no `###`;

## Considerations

- **Risk 13 of the plan, "the guide drifts from behaviour"** (likelihood low, impact medium; owners this bead and B4, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.4`): mitigated by the generated tables and byte identity of B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`), and here by the parse check over commands and fragments, the name check against the published registries, the outline test, the two loops run as written, every read-only command run, and B4's recipes. What remains unchecked is the meaning of a sentence; the truth audit (section 6) covers it once, and later changes are caught when they rename or remove a name the prose uses.
- **Lands late by design,** after its blockers (`apply`, `plans show`, triage, fix and undo of repairs; see Dependencies), so it describes M4's final behaviour. Leaves that are not its ancestors may still land after it: for example H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, the pre-freeze audit), C4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4`, the run-the-fix corpus), D7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.7`, release drift and apply races), G3 (`omad-7ccp`, durability), and B4 by construction. They change generated blocks (and regenerate `SKILL.md`, common rule 17) or nothing the guide states; one that changes a behaviour the prose states (H1's renames above all) updates `guide.md` in the same commit (M4-D55), and this bead's tests point at the line.
- **The size budget is tight.** Rendered with stand-in blocks sized from the plan, the draft measured about 31.8 KiB and 323 lines; the real blocks are expected smaller (about 28–30 KiB), but the margin is a few KiB. Measure the generated part first (B1's report, or the new test's log, on `main` at claim time); the prose gets what remains less 2 KiB. Trim, in this order: the recipe lead lines, the "Where to look next" descriptions, the envelope bullets. Never cut a required element of section 5; if the required content alone leaves less than 2 KiB of headroom, record it and file a task `discovered-from` this bead to shorten B1's generated formats (the actions table's descriptions, for example). A leaf that later breaks the budget gets the test's message, which names the prose to trim.
- **Hot spots (§10.5 rules):** `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` (every leaf after B1: regenerate after rebasing, never merge by hand); `src/contract/guide/` (B1 created it; E4, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4`, adds `doctor.md` and one placeholder row and never edits `guide.md`; this bead owns `guide.md`'s prose and `ERRORS_COMMON`); `tests/skill.rs` and `tests/common/guide.rs` (B1's; B4 adds `tests/skill_recipes.rs` and reuses the helpers: append, rebase); `README.md` (edit only the guide's section and the tests-table row).
- **What could go wrong in implementation, and how to notice:**
  - The prose names a key or value the schemas do not publish (a `details` key a leaf never declared, say): the name check fails and names the line; declare it where it belongs (the `DetailSpec` of A9, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9`) if the code emits it, else fix the prose.
  - A fragment such as `plans show` is parsed strictly and fails on its missing id: fragments accept the missing-argument error kinds only.
  - The read-only run test hits a network command: `OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1` makes it answer offline, which is a declared exit; a request in `net.log` would mean the variable was not honoured, which is a bug in that command.
  - The doctor scenario finds other auto-fixable findings on the synthetic home: the assertions require only that `fm-test-write` is among them, and the undo reverts the whole repair.
  - Two tests read the committed `SKILL.md` while the regeneration writes it: none of this bead's tests reads the file; they render through the binary (B1's rule).
  - Markdown the extractors cannot read (a double-backtick span, an indented fence): `the_guide_uses_simple_markdown` fails first.
- **No crate is added.** The extractors are hand-written over the simple Markdown subset; do not add `regex` or a Markdown parser for them (CLAUDE.md: add a crate only when the bead needs it).
- **Compatibility.** Nothing persisted changes; an older binary prints its own guide. An installed skill from B1's skeleton becomes an older guide than this build's, which the drift check of F10 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.10`) reports and `doctor fix` brings current; that is the intended behaviour, not a defect. The capabilities snapshot redacts `guide_digest` (B1), so the regeneration causes no snapshot churn.
- **Privacy.** The guide holds no machine data. The end-to-end scenarios run on synthetic `TestEnv` homes and create no `WTF/`; the doctor scenario's planted file is test content under `<state>`.
- **Performance.** The checks render once and run three commands; the end-to-end suite runs about 25 commands on small homes, a few seconds in the gate.
- **Bounded work (common rule 15)** does not apply: no product code reads new input. **Previews bind (common rule 16)** does not apply: no mutating path changes.
- **Why size M.** About 10 KiB of prose, a handful of hand-written extractors, and three scenarios; the work is in writing and verifying, not in code.

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M4 plan, 2026-10-24).**

**Why this bead.** B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`, the guide renderer and `robot-docs guide`) built the agent guide as a mechanism: a template with generated tables, a stamp, the `robot-docs guide` command and a committed `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` held byte-identical to it. It shipped a skeleton, because the commands the guide has to teach did not exist yet. This bead writes the content an agent actually copies: the core loop with its reconcile step, how to read the envelope (the doctor's top-level report included), the safety model stated as the code keeps it (per client, never atomic across clients), the eight canonical recipes, the doctor loop, and pointers to the rest. Because an agent copies the guide verbatim, the bead's other half is the tests that keep the prose true: every command and command fragment parses, every name in backticks is registered, the outline's required elements are present, the two loops run as written on a real binary, and every read-only command the guide names runs. It lands late on purpose, after `apply`, `plans show`, the doctor's triage, fix and undo of repairs, so it describes M4's final behaviour.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M4-D7:** the guide is one artifact with the skill; hand-written prose around generated blocks; frontmatter first and the stamp on the next line; at most 500 lines and 32 KiB (this bead's test, strict).
- **M4-D63:** the core loop's reconcile step: an `apply` whose result is unknown → `omaddons plans show <plan_id>` before anything else (this bead is named in the decision's tasks).
- **M4-D61:** the guarantee is per target; the guide says "on each client … or none of them", names `outcomes[]` and its four statuses, and never calls a multi-client run atomic.
- **M4-D23, M4-D24, M4-D20, M4-D22:** what `apply` does and refuses (`plan_stale` reasons, `plan_not_found`), which commands store plans, and that a no-op preview stores none.
- **M4-D34, M4-D40:** doctor reports at the top level with no `data`; the doctor's own exit dictionary, in which exit 1 means findings.
- **M4-D46, M4-D38:** `undo` reverts a repair strictly (`undo_conflict` once something changed); never add `--force --yes` on an agent's own initiative.
- **M4-D8:** the guide names `robot-docs install-skill`.
- **M4-D3, M4-D56:** `schema_version` `1.x` only adds, so the guide tells agents to ignore unknown keys, values, codes and actions.
- **M4-D55:** the bead may land after H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, the pre-freeze audit) and adds no wire name.
- **M4-D2:** the prose never restates a generated table.

**Alternatives rejected that matter here.**
- A fully generated guide (unreadable) and a fully hand-written one (its tables drift), both rejected by M4-D7: this bead writes prose only.
- Pinning the prose with a snapshot of whole paragraphs: every wording polish would need a re-accept; the outline test pins required tokens and a few short phrases instead.
- Checking only "error codes" in the prose: the plan's criterion, generalized to every backticked name (codes, actions, exit names, schema keys and values, flags, failure-mode ids) against what the binary publishes, because a renamed key drifts the guide as surely as a renamed code.
- A gate test that runs `rumdl`: `rumdl` is not a project dependency, and a missing tool would mean a failure or an unaccepted `SKIP`; it is a recorded manual step with a fixed invocation.
- Repeating `undo --last-by agent` to undo earlier agent runs: at `c0ab5e9` the second undo reverts the first (an undo is undoable), so the recipe's lead line names `undo --run <run>` instead.

**Risks and how they are watched.**
- Risk 13, the guide drifts from behaviour (L, M; owners this bead and B4, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.4`, the recipes run end to end): generated tables and byte identity (B1); here the parse check over commands and fragments, the name check against the published registries, the outline test, the loops run as written, every read-only command run; B4 runs the recipes. Later renames (H1) update the guide in their own commit, and these tests point at the line.
- The 32 KiB budget is tight (a draft rendered with stand-in blocks measured about 31.8 KiB): the bead measures the generated part first, keeps 2 KiB of headroom, trims prose in a fixed order, and files a task against the generated formats if required content alone cannot fit.

**Plan versus code, found while writing.** The plan's `undo-agent-today` recipe used `history --actor agent`, but `--actor` is the global attribution flag and the filter is `--by` (`src/cli.rs:75-77`, `src/app/history.rs:41-43`); the recipe uses `--by agent`. The plan's core loop showed `data.items`, which is per target for multi-target commands (`src/app/outcome.rs:248-275`); the guide points at `data.approval`, which every storable dry run returns in one shape.

**What it unblocks, and why it waits.** B4 runs the eight recipes this bead writes, with the `recipes()` grammar it defines; B4 cannot start until the recipes exist. This bead waits for B1 (the template and helpers), D5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`) and D9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.9`) (`apply` and `plans show`, which the core loop and the safety model describe), and E4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4`), E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`) and E7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7`) (triage, fix and undo of repairs, which the doctor loop runs), so that nothing it teaches is still moving.

**How it serves the milestone.** G-M4-1: the guide is the second of the three calls that teach an agent omaddons, and now its prose is checked against the code like its tables. G-M4-3 and G-M4-4: the preview guarantee and the doctor loop are taught exactly as built and proven by running them. Criteria 3 (the size bullet) and 4 (the recipes, run by B4) are this bead's.

title: The guide's content checks: the size budget, the recipe grammar, registered names and command fragments
description:
Part 1 of 3 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.2 (The guide's content). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

B2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.2`) writes the content of omaddons' agent guide: the hand-written prose of `src/contract/guide/guide.md` around the tables B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`, the guide renderer and `robot-docs guide`) generates, rendered by `omaddons robot-docs guide`, committed byte-identical as `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` and installed as a coding agent's skill (M4-D7). An agent copies the guide verbatim, so every claim in it must be true of the code. B1 shipped a skeleton (every heading, every placeholder, short holding prose) and a first parse check over the commands it names; B2 replaces the prose late in the milestone, once `apply`, `plans show` and the doctor's triage, fix and undo exist.

This part adds the checks the final prose must pass, before the prose: the size budget (M4-D7: at most 500 lines and 32 KiB; criterion 3: "under"), a grammar for the eight recipe blocks and their fill rules (which B4, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.4`, runs end to end), a parse check that also covers command fragments and refuses shell syntax, a check that every name the prose puts in backticks is registered (the plan's "every error code it names is registered", generalized), and a check that the Markdown stays simple enough for these hand-written extractors. Every check passes on B1's skeleton, so this part lands on its own and passes the gate; subtask 2 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.2.2) then writes the prose against them. It is its own step because the checks are test code with their own table-driven cases, and because writing the prose against finished checks keeps each commit honest.

The decisions it applies, restated:
- **M4-D7.** The guide is hand-written prose with generated blocks (the command table, both exit dictionaries, the common errors, the NEVER list, the env vars, the actions, the stamp); the YAML frontmatter is first and the stamp `<!-- omaddons guide sha256:<hex> -->` is the line right after it; the guide stays within 500 lines and 32 KiB (test), because a skill is loaded into an agent's context window, and detail lives in `capabilities`, `robot-docs errors` and `robot-docs schema`.
- **Criterion 4 (canonical intents):** each of the eight intents takes at most two omaddons commands with JSON output and is a recipe in `SKILL.md`; a recipe that needs a third command means the recipe or the CLI is wrong, and the CLI is what gets fixed (vision §5.10).
- **M4-D2:** the published registries are the source of every name; the name check reads them, never a copy.
- **Risk 13 of the plan, "the guide drifts from behaviour":** these checks are its mitigation for the prose.

## Technical Approach

### Files

- `tests/common/guide.rs` (the helper module of B1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`): new constants and helpers below. B1's names and signatures (`SKILL_FILE`, `REGENERATE`, `skill_path()`, `committed()`, `rendered(log, on)`, `layout(text)`, `first_difference(a, b)`, `sha256_hex(text)`, `unparsable(text) -> Vec<(String, String)>`, `SAMPLES`) are kept: T2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.2`, slice 1 end to end) and B4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.4`, the recipes run end to end) call them.
- `tests/skill.rs` (B1's suite): B1's `guide_size_is_reported` becomes `guide_meets_its_size_budget`; `every_command_the_guide_names_parses` and `a_planted_unparsable_span_is_reported` are extended; four tests are added.
- If B1's skeleton prose fails a new check (a double-backtick span, a name no registry has), fix that holding sentence in `src/contract/guide/guide.md` in this commit and regenerate `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` with `OMADDONS_UPDATE_SKILL=1 cargo test --test skill` (common rule 17). Otherwise no product file changes.

No crate is added (`shell-words` is already a dependency, `Cargo.toml:28`; there is no regex or Markdown crate, and none is needed for a deliberately simple subset of Markdown).

### 1. The size budget

```rust
pub const GUIDE_MAX_LINES: usize = 500;     // lines < 500
pub const GUIDE_MAX_BYTES: usize = 32 * 1024; // bytes < 32,768
pub const HEADROOM_LINES: usize = 30;       // reported; B2 lands with at least this much
pub const HEADROOM_BYTES: usize = 2048;
```

**`guide_meets_its_size_budget`** replaces `guide_size_is_reported` and keeps its log line: render with `guide::rendered(&log, &env)` on a fresh `TestEnv`; `lines = text.lines().count()`, `bytes = text.len()`; `log.json("size", {lines, bytes, max_lines, max_bytes, headroom_lines, headroom_bytes})`; assert `lines < GUIDE_MAX_LINES` and `bytes < GUIDE_MAX_BYTES`. Failure: "the guide is <n> lines / <b> bytes; the budget is under 500 lines and 32 KiB (M4-D7). Trim the hand-written prose in src/contract/guide/guide.md, or move detail to capabilities or robot-docs, which the guide points to."

Decided while writing this bead: **both bounds strict**, so the plan's "at most" (M4-D7) and "under" (criterion 3) both hold; **the constants live in `tests/common/guide.rs`, not `src/limits.rs`**: the plan's constants table lists "the guide under 500 lines and 32 KiB" among test budgets that are not constants, and no product code reads it. Unlike the timing budgets of `tests/perf.rs`, this one does not depend on the build profile, so it runs in the gate. The headroom constants are reported only: later leaves may legitimately use the headroom.

### 2. Commands, fragments and their parse

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum SpanKind { Full, Fragment, RecipeLine { recipe: String } }
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct NamedCommand { pub line: usize, pub section: String, pub span: String, pub kind: SpanKind }

/// Every command the body names (after the stamp line): inline code spans and fenced lines that
/// start with `omaddons ` (Full, or RecipeLine inside a `sh recipe=` block), and inline code
/// spans of two or more words whose first word is the first word of an `app::COMMANDS` path
/// (Fragment: `undo --run <run>`, `plans show`, `doctor undo <doctor_run>`).
pub fn commands(text: &str) -> Vec<NamedCommand>;
/// Replaces each `<name>` with `value(name)`; an unknown name and a `…` are errors.
pub fn fill(span: &str, value: &dyn Fn(&str) -> Option<String>) -> Result<String, String>;
/// Refuses shell syntax outside quotes, then `shell_words::split`.
pub fn argv(filled: &str) -> Result<Vec<String>, String>;
/// B1's helper, same name and signature, now built on the three above.
pub fn unparsable(text: &str) -> Vec<(String, String)>;
pub fn inline_spans(line: &str) -> Vec<String>; // single-backtick spans of one line
```

- **The extraction.** The body is everything after the stamp line (the frontmatter `description` is a loading trigger, not an instruction an agent runs). A fence opens and closes on a line starting with three backticks at column 0; a fence whose info string starts `sh recipe=` is a recipe block, and its lines starting `omaddons ` are `RecipeLine`s; other fenced lines starting `omaddons ` are `Full`. Outside fences, each inline code span is `Full` when it starts with `omaddons `, `Fragment` when it has two or more words and its first word is the first word of a `COMMANDS` path (`omaddons::app::COMMANDS`, names split on spaces), and ignored otherwise. `section` is the title of the nearest `##` heading above.
- **The fill.** `SAMPLES` (decided while writing this bead; B1 defined the first six):

  | Placeholder | Sample | Why this name |
  |---|---|---|
  | `<command>` | `update` (was `install`) | `omaddons <command> --dry-run --json` must parse; `install` requires a ref |
  | `<target>` | `retail` | B1 |
  | `<key>`, `<id>` | `01J00000000000000000000000` | B1 |
  | `<plan_id>` | `01J00000000000000000000000` | B1 |
  | `<ref>` | `dbm` | B1 |
  | `<why>` | `the user approved the preview` | `--reason "<why>"`, never `"…"` |
  | `<finding_id>` | `fm-schemas-state-corrupt` | failure-mode ids, distinct from transaction ids |
  | `<tx>` | `01J00000000000000000000000` | `undo <tx>` |
  | `<run>` | `01J00000000000000000000000` | `undo --run <run>` (history's run) |
  | `<doctor_run>` | `2026-10-30T18-02-11Z__01J00000000000000000000000` | `doctor undo <doctor_run>` (a doctor run directory) |
  | `<words>` | `deadly boss mods` | `search <words>` |

  An unknown `<name>` fails "add a sample for <name> in SAMPLES"; a span containing `…` fails "write the command out in full" (both B1's messages). Distinct names for the kinds of id were decided because one `<id>` cannot have one sample valid as a transaction, a run, a doctor run and a failure mode.
- **Shell syntax.** After filling, `argv` scans the text outside single and double quotes and refuses `|`, `&`, `;`, `>`, `<`, a backtick, `$(`, and a `#` at the start of a word, with "write the command as plain argv: omaddons never runs a shell" (the guide's NEVER list says "argv only", and B4 runs recipe lines without a shell). A `#` inside a word (`git:https://…#main`) is allowed.
- **The parse.** `omaddons::cli::Cli::try_parse_from(argv)` with `omaddons` first (a fragment is prefixed with it). `Full` and `RecipeLine` spans must parse; clap's `DisplayHelp` and `DisplayVersion` count as parsing (B1's rule; `Cli` disables clap's own help flag, `src/cli.rs:25-41`, so `--help` parses as a global flag anyway). A `Fragment` names a command path, not a whole command, so `ErrorKind::MissingRequiredArgument`, `MissingSubcommand` and `DisplayHelpOnMissingArgumentOrSubcommand` are accepted too (`plans show` lacks its id); any other kind (`InvalidSubcommand`, `UnknownArgument`, `InvalidValue`, `ArgumentConflict`, …) fails with clap's message.

**`every_command_the_guide_names_parses`** (B1's name): step "extract" logs every `NamedCommand` (line, section, kind, span); step "fill and split" logs each filled argv or its reason; step "parse" logs each verdict; then asserts `unparsable(&rendered)` is empty, listing every failure with its line and reason.

**`a_planted_unparsable_span_is_reported`** keeps B1's cases (`omaddons nosuch`, `omaddons status <nope>`, `omaddons install …` reported; `omaddons status --json` not) and adds, each asserted with its reason: `omaddons status --json | jq .data` (shell), `omaddons apply <plan_id> --json; echo done` (shell), `` `undo --no-such-flag` `` (a fragment, unknown flag), `` `plans shwo` `` (a fragment, unknown subcommand); and `` `plans show` ``, `` `doctor undo <doctor_run>` `` and `` `undo --run <run>` `` are not reported. (The synthetic text has a frontmatter and a stamp line, so the body rule applies.)

### 3. The recipe grammar

Decided while writing this bead (the plan fixes the info string `sh recipe=<id> expect=<exit>[,<exit>]` and a declared fill rule, `plan_id ← data.plan_id`, but not their exact syntax; B4 runs exactly what this grammar describes):

- A recipe is a fenced block whose info string is exactly `sh recipe=<id> expect=<item>[,<item>…]`, single spaces, no other attribute. Any other fence whose info string contains `recipe=` is an error ("a recipe fence is `sh recipe=<id> expect=…`").
  - `<id>` is kebab-case, `[a-z][a-z0-9]*(-[a-z0-9]+)*`, unique in the text.
  - One `<item>` per command, in order; an item is an exit code 0–255, or several joined by `|`, any of which is acceptable (`0|1` for the doctor, whose exit 1 means findings).
- The block's lines are command lines and fill lines, nothing else (no blank line, no other comment):
  - a **command line** starts with `omaddons `, contains no `…`, and passes `argv` (no shell syntax);
  - a **fill line** is exactly `# <name> is <path> of the command above`, `<name>` matching `[a-z_]+`, `<path>` being `data` followed by one or more `.<key>` (`[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`) or `[<n>]` segments.
- One or two commands. The first contains no placeholder. Every `<name>` in the second command has a fill line between the two commands; every fill line's `<name>` appears in the second command.
- Three or more commands: "recipe <id> has <n> commands; a canonical intent takes at most two (fix the CLI, not the recipe)".

```rust
pub struct Recipe { pub id: String, pub line: usize, pub steps: Vec<RecipeStep> }
pub struct RecipeStep { pub line: usize, pub command: String, pub expect: Vec<u8>, pub fills: Vec<Fill> }
pub struct Fill { pub name: String, pub path: String } // from the previous step's stdout envelope
/// Every recipe block of `text`, or every problem found, each naming the recipe id (or the fence
/// line) and the line.
pub fn recipes(text: &str) -> Result<Vec<Recipe>, Vec<String>>;
```

How B4 runs a recipe (stated so the two leaves agree): split each command line with `shell_words`, drop the leading `omaddons`, replace each `<name>` with the JSON value at `path` in the previous step's stdout envelope (a string as is, a number in decimal; a missing value fails the recipe), and compare the exit with the step's `expect`.

**`recipe_blocks_are_well_formed`**: `guide::recipes(&rendered)` is `Ok`; log every recipe as parsed. On B1's skeleton it holds zero recipes; subtask 2 adds eight, and its outline test asserts their ids.

**`recipe_grammar_cases`**, table-driven, one name per case, each a synthetic Markdown text and either the expected recipes (id, then each step's command, expect and fills) or a substring of the expected error:

| Case | Input (the block) | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| `valid_one_command` | `sh recipe=a expect=0` / `omaddons status --json` | one step, `[0]`, no fill |
| `valid_two_with_fill` | `sh recipe=b expect=0,0` / `omaddons install x -t retail --dry-run --json` / `# <plan_id> is data.plan_id of the command above` / `omaddons apply <plan_id> --json` | two steps; the second's fill `plan_id ← data.plan_id` |
| `alternatives_in_expect` | `expect=0,0\|1` with two commands | second step `[0, 1]` |
| `missing_expect` | `sh recipe=c` | "expect=" |
| `expect_count_mismatch` | `expect=0` with two commands | "one expect item per command" |
| `three_commands` | three command lines | "at most two" |
| `unknown_attribute` | `sh recipe=d expect=0 shell=bash` | "no other attribute" |
| `bad_id` | `sh recipe=Update_all expect=0` | "kebab-case" |
| `duplicate_id` | two blocks `recipe=e` | "duplicate recipe id e" |
| `unfilled_placeholder` | second command uses `<plan_id>`, no fill line | "<plan_id> has no fill rule" |
| `placeholder_in_first_command` | first command uses `<tx>` | "the first command has nothing to fill from" |
| `fill_without_use` | fill line for `<x>`, second command does not use it | "<x> is filled but not used" |
| `fill_before_first_command` | fill line first | "follows no command" |
| `bad_fill_path` | `# <plan_id> is plan_id of the command above` | "data." |
| `blank_line_in_block` | an empty line between commands | "blank line" |
| `other_comment_in_block` | `# run this first` | "fill line" |
| `elided_command` | `omaddons install …` | "write the command out in full" |
| `shell_operator` | `omaddons status --json \| jq .` | "plain argv" |
| `not_sh` | `bash recipe=f expect=0` | "a recipe fence is" |
| `exit_out_of_range` | `expect=256` | "0–255" |

### 4. Every name the prose uses is registered

**Which spans.** The prose is `omaddons::contract::guide::TEMPLATE` (the template, so messages give `src/contract/guide/guide.md:<line>`) without the frontmatter, without fenced blocks (recipes are the parse check's and the grammar's), and with every `{{…}}` placeholder removed (generated blocks are registry-true by construction). Every inline code span left is classified, first match wins:

| Class | Shape | Must be |
|---|---|---|
| command | starts with `omaddons ` | skipped: the parse check's |
| fragment | two or more words, the first a `COMMANDS` path's first word | skipped: the parse check's |
| flags | first word starts with `--` | every `--word` (before any `=`) a long flag or visible long alias of some command, or a global flag |
| failure mode | `fm-[a-z0-9_-]+` | a detector or fixer id |
| key path | first segment `data`, `error`, `warnings`, `commands`, `meta`, `details` or `alternatives` (each optionally `[]`), then zero or more `.<key>` segments (each optionally `[]`) | every segment after the first a property name of a published schema or `details` specification |
| bare name | `[a-z][a-z0-9_]*` | an error code, a warning code, an action, a general or doctor exit name, a word of a `COMMANDS` path, a property name or `enum`/`const` string of a published schema or `details` specification, or `true`, `false`, `null` |
| unchecked | anything else (`-t all`, `/reload`, `1.x`, `gh:Owner/Repo`, `addons.toml`, `partial: true`) | nothing; logged, so a reviewer sees the list |

```rust
pub struct Vocabulary {
    pub codes: BTreeSet<String>, pub warnings: BTreeSet<String>, pub actions: BTreeSet<String>,
    pub exits: BTreeSet<String>, pub command_words: BTreeSet<String>, pub first_words: BTreeSet<String>,
    pub flags: BTreeSet<String>, pub keys: BTreeSet<String>, pub values: BTreeSet<String>,
    pub failure_modes: BTreeSet<String>,
}
impl Vocabulary { pub fn load(log: &TestLog, on: &impl Runner) -> Self; }
pub enum SpanClass { Command, Fragment, Flags, FailureMode, KeyPath, Bare, Unchecked }
pub fn classify(span: &str, vocab: &Vocabulary) -> SpanClass;
/// (template line, span, reason) for every span whose class requires a registered name it lacks.
pub fn unregistered(template: &str, vocab: &Vocabulary) -> Vec<(usize, String, String)>;
```

**Where `Vocabulary::load` reads each set** (the published registries; adapt the import paths to what landed):
- `codes`: `omaddons::error::ErrorCode::ALL`, `wire()` (`src/error.rs:150-204` at `c0ab5e9`, 41 codes; E3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, adds two);
- `warnings`: `WarningCode::ALL`, `wire()` (`src/error.rs:232-240`);
- `exits`: `omaddons::error::Exit::ALL`, `name()` (`src/error.rs:20-60`) and E3's `omaddons::doctor::Exit::ALL`, `name()`;
- `actions`: `omaddons::contract::actions::Action::ALL`, `wire()`, of A2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.2`, the registries);
- `command_words`, `first_words`: `omaddons::app::COMMANDS` names, split on spaces;
- `flags`: a walk of `omaddons::cli::Cli::command()` after `.build()` (which propagates globals) over every subcommand, each argument's `get_long_and_visible_aliases()`;
- `keys` and `values`: a recursive walk of the `data` of `log.run(&env, ["robot-docs", "schema", "--json"])` (the shape `{envelope, events, commands, files}` of A5, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5`, `robot-docs schema` and `errors`) and of `log.run(&env, ["robot-docs", "errors", "--json"])` (every code's `details` specification): every key of every object named `properties`, every string in every `enum` array, every string `const`;
- `failure_modes`: `log.run(&env, ["doctor", "capabilities", "--json"])`, `detectors[].id` and `fixers[].id`, read at the envelope's top level (doctor reports have no `data`, M4-D34).

The three runs use a fresh `TestEnv`; each must exit 0.

**`every_name_the_guide_uses_is_registered`**: step "vocabulary" (load; `log.json` of each set's size); step "classify" (`log.json` of every span with its line, class and verdict, and of the unchecked list); step "verdict": assert `unregistered(TEMPLATE, &vocab)` is empty; each failure reads "src/contract/guide/guide.md:<line>: `<span>` is not a registered <kind>: <reason>. Fix the guide, or register the name where it belongs."

**`a_planted_unregistered_name_is_reported`**: the same vocabulary over a synthetic template (`---`, `name: omaddons`, `description: x`, `---`, `{{stamp}}`, a blank line, then one line) naming `` `no_such_code` ``, `` `data.no_such_key` ``, `` `--no-such-flag` ``, `` `fm-no-such-mode` ``, `` `plan_stale` ``, `` `data.plan_id` ``, `` `--dry-run` ``, `` `undo --run <run>` `` and `` `-t all` ``: exactly the first four are reported, with the kinds bare name, key path, flag and failure mode.

### 5. Simple Markdown

```rust
/// (line, problem) for every construct the extractors above cannot read.
pub fn simple_markdown(text: &str) -> Vec<(usize, String)>;
```

Rules: inline code only in single backticks (no two consecutive backticks outside a fence delimiter line); an even number of backticks on every line outside fences; fences open and close only on lines that start with exactly three backticks at column 0 (an indented fence, a `~~~` fence or a four-backtick fence is a problem); no tab; no line outside a fence that starts with `<`, except B1's two comment lines after the frontmatter (the stamp and the generated-by line).

**`the_guide_uses_simple_markdown`**: `simple_markdown(TEMPLATE)` and `simple_markdown(&rendered)` are empty; failures name the line.

### 6. The sections helper (used by subtasks 2 and 3)

```rust
pub struct Section { pub level: u8, pub title: String, pub line: usize, pub body: String }
/// The `#` and `##`/`###` headings outside fences, each with the text up to the next heading of
/// its level or higher.
pub fn sections(text: &str) -> Vec<Section>;
```

It lands here because `commands()` reports each span's section through it; its own cases are in `recipe_grammar_cases`' sibling `sections_cases` (a heading inside a fence is not a section; a `###` belongs to its `##`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `tests/skill.rs::guide_meets_its_size_budget` replaces `guide_size_is_reported`, asserts lines < 500 and bytes < 32,768 on the rendered guide, and logs the size and headroom.
- [ ] `every_command_the_guide_names_parses` covers full commands, recipe lines and command fragments, fills placeholders from the extended `SAMPLES`, refuses shell syntax and elisions, and accepts only missing-argument errors for fragments; `a_planted_unparsable_span_is_reported` shows each new case with its reason.
- [ ] `guide::recipes` implements the grammar of section 3; `recipe_grammar_cases` passes all twenty cases and `recipe_blocks_are_well_formed` passes on the rendered guide.
- [ ] `every_name_the_guide_uses_is_registered` classifies every prose span and finds every bare name, key path, flag and failure-mode id in the published registries; `a_planted_unregistered_name_is_reported` reports exactly the four planted names.
- [ ] `the_guide_uses_simple_markdown` passes on the template and the rendered guide, and `sections_cases` passes.
- [ ] The helper names and signatures of B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`) are unchanged, and B1's other skill tests still pass; any skeleton sentence a new check rejected is fixed and `SKILL.md` regenerated in this commit.
- [ ] No crate is added; no product behaviour or wire name changes.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

The helpers are test code in `tests/common/guide.rs`; their cases run as the table-driven tests of `tests/skill.rs` listed below, each case with its name, input, expected and actual result in the assertion message:
- `recipe_grammar_cases` (twenty cases, section 3);
- `sections_cases`: `two_sections`, `heading_inside_fence_ignored`, `subsection_belongs_to_section`, `text_before_first_heading`;
- `a_planted_unparsable_span_is_reported` (the three cases of B1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`, and seven new ones, section 2);
- `a_planted_unregistered_name_is_reported` (nine spans, four reported, section 4);
- inside `the_guide_uses_simple_markdown`, a synthetic-text table `simple_markdown_cases`: `double_backtick`, `odd_backticks`, `indented_fence`, `tilde_fence`, `four_backtick_fence`, `tab`, `raw_html_line`, `allowed_comment_lines` (no problem).

### Integration and end-to-end tests

`tests/skill.rs`, each on a fresh `TestEnv`, each rendering the guide through the real binary with B1's `guide::rendered(&log, &env)`:
- `guide_meets_its_size_budget`: render → size and headroom logged → the strict budget asserted.
- `every_command_the_guide_names_parses`: render → extract → fill and split → parse → no failure.
- `recipe_blocks_are_well_formed`: render → `recipes()` is `Ok` (zero recipes on the skeleton).
- `every_name_the_guide_uses_is_registered`: three runs (`robot-docs schema --json`, `robot-docs errors --json`, `doctor capabilities --json`, each exit 0) plus the library registries → classify the template's prose → nothing unregistered.
- `the_guide_uses_simple_markdown`: render → the template and the rendered text both clean.

### Logging

Every test that renders or runs the binary uses the `TestLog` of T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`) (`let log = tlog!();`, `log.step`, `log.run`, `log.json`, `log.note`): each run records its argv, environment overrides, exit code, the parsed envelope or the raw Markdown, stderr and `net.log` lines added, and each rendered guide is logged as `{sha256, lines, bytes}`, never whole. The checks log what they extracted and decided: every command span with its kind, filled argv and verdict; every recipe as parsed; the vocabulary's set sizes, every prose span with its class and verdict, and the unchecked spans; the size and headroom. A failing assertion names the line, the span and the reason; T1's guard prints `test log: <path>` and the last 20 steps on a panic, and `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG=verbose` echoes every step live.

## Considerations

- **These checks must pass on the skeleton of B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`).** If one fails there, the skeleton's holding prose is what changes (with a regeneration), never the check; the failure is the check working.
- **Keep B1's interface.** `unparsable` keeps its name and return type; the slice-1 suite of T2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.2`) and B4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.4`) call the helpers. New helpers are additive.
- **Fragments are deliberately lenient** about missing arguments and strict about everything else: a fragment like `plans show` names a path, and an unknown flag in a fragment is exactly the drift these checks exist to catch.
- **The vocabulary comes from what the binary publishes.** A name the code emits but no schema or `details` specification declares fails here; the fix is to declare it where it belongs (the `DetailSpec` of A9, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9`, or the schemas of A3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`), not to add it to a list in the test.
- **The unchecked bucket is visible, not silent:** it is logged, so a reviewer of subtask 2's prose can see which spans no rule covers.
- **Hot spots:** `tests/skill.rs` and `tests/common/guide.rs` (B1's; B4 adds its own suite and reuses the helpers: append, rebase); `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` (regenerate after rebasing, never merge by hand) if a skeleton sentence changes.
- **No `regex`, no Markdown crate:** the subset is enforced by `the_guide_uses_simple_markdown`, so hand-written extractors stay correct.

## Dependencies

- Parent: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.2 (The guide's content).
- Before it: nothing inside the leaf. The leaf's blockers must have landed: B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`: the template, `TEMPLATE`, the renderer, the helpers and `tests/skill.rs`), D5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`), D9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.9`), E4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4`: `doctor capabilities --json`, which the vocabulary reads), E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`) and E7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7`). It also needs T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs and the `argc e2e` runner; a `blocks` edge added at filing) for `TestLog`.
- After it: subtask 2 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.2.2) writes the prose against these checks and adds the outline test with `sections()` and `recipes()`; subtask 3 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.2.3) extracts its commands with `commands()` and `sections()`.
