comments.text: **Common rules.** The rules every M4 leaf and subtask follows, cited in this bead as "common rule N", are in the pinned docs bead `omad-bxb1` (`br show omad-bxb1`). Read them once per session, not once per bead.

title: The guide's prose and its eight recipes, with `SKILL.md` regenerated
description:
Part 2 of 3 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.2 (The guide's content). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

B2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.2`) writes the content of omaddons' agent guide: the hand-written prose of `src/contract/guide/guide.md` around the tables B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`, the guide renderer and `robot-docs guide`) generates. `omaddons robot-docs guide` renders it, the repository commits it byte-identical as `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md`, and `robot-docs install-skill` (B3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3`) installs it as a coding agent's skill (M4-D7). An agent copies the guide verbatim, so every claim in it must be true of the code. B1 shipped a skeleton with holding prose naming only M1–M3 commands; subtask 1 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.2.1) added the checks the final prose must pass.

This part writes the prose: every section of the outline, the core loop with its reconcile step (M4-D63), the per-client wording of the preview guarantee (M4-D61), the advice to ignore unknown names (M4-D3, M4-D56), the safety model, the eight canonical recipes (criterion 4; B4, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.4`, runs them), the doctor loop and the pointers. It also changes the common-errors list, audits every sentence against the code on `main`, runs the de-slopify and `rumdl` passes, adds the outline test, updates README's guide section, and regenerates `SKILL.md`. It is one step because the prose, its outline test and the regenerated file must land in one commit for the gate to pass (`skill_md_is_the_guide` compares the committed file with what the binary renders).

The decisions it applies, restated:
- **M4-D7:** hand-written prose around generated blocks (never restate a table the renderer generates); YAML frontmatter first, then the stamp on the next line; at most 500 lines and 32 KiB, detail left to `capabilities`, `robot-docs errors` and `robot-docs schema`. *Rejected:* a fully generated guide (unreadable) and a fully hand-written one (its tables drift).
- **M4-D63:** `omaddons plans show <PLAN_ID>` is read-only and offline; it reports the stored approval, history's evidence keyed by the plan id, a `state` (`pending`, `completed`, `partial`, `expired`, `unknown`) and `evidence.complete`, and never infers success from current versions. The guide's core loop says: when an `apply`'s result is unknown (a broken pipe, an agent restart), run `plans show` before previewing again or changing anything.
- **M4-D61:** on each target a bound run commits exactly the approved operations or none of them; a multi-target run is one transaction per target and can end partial; `apply`'s `outcomes[]` says `committed`, `unchanged`, `stale` or `failed` per target with its transaction or error code; nothing calls such a run atomic; a no-op preview stores no plan (`plan_id: null`).
- **M4-D23, M4-D24, M4-D20:** `apply` runs the stored typed intent bound to its token and revalidates every source; its refusals are `plan_stale` (never retryable from a bound run) with `details.reason` `expired`, `binary_changed`, `input_missing` or `already_applied`, or `details.changed` naming the part that moved; an unknown, oversized or unreadable plan is `plan_not_found`; a plan lives `PLAN_TTL`, 24 hours.
- **M4-D22:** the storable commands (`install`, `update`, `pin`, `unpin`, `adopt`, `sync`, `copy`, `remove`, `undo`, `backup restore`, `backup prune`) store a plan on `--dry-run`; the generated command list marks them `stores plan`.
- **M4-D34, M4-D40:** doctor reports sit at the top level with no `data`; `ok` is `exit_code == 0`; findings (1) are a report, not an error; the doctor has its own exit dictionary.
- **M4-D46, M4-D38:** `undo` reverts a repair strictly and refuses with `undo_conflict` before moving anything once something the repair touched has changed; a forced set-aside (`--force --yes`) is never part of a default fix and is for someone who has read `doctor explain`.
- **M4-D8:** the guide names `robot-docs install-skill`.
- **M4-D3, M4-D56:** `schema_version` is the contract version; `1.x` only adds keys, values, codes and actions; `2.0` would be the first break.

Facts it relies on (as of `c0ab5e9`, verified while writing the leaf): the global `--actor` (`src/cli.rs:75-77`) versus `history --by` (`src/app/history.rs:41-43`); an undo is itself undoable (`src/model.rs:451-453`, `src/state/history.rs:609-633`, `README.md:88`), so a second `undo --last-by agent` is a redo; `data.items` is top-level only for single-target commands (`src/app/install.rs:95-102`) and per target in `TargetsData` (`src/app/outcome.rs:248-275`); the envelope keys and `ErrorBody`, `Suggestion` and `CommandHint` fields (`src/output/envelope.rs:20-38`, `src/error.rs:383-388`, `:441-447`, `:618-625`); `PLAN_TTL` is one day (`src/limits.rs:49`); `plan_not_found` has no construction site at `c0ab5e9` (`src/error.rs:160`) and A9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9`, a meaning for every code) gave it a "reserved" meaning that D5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`) rewrites when it starts raising it.

## Technical Approach

### 1. The outline

The document, in this order; the `##` headings are exact, there is one `#` heading and no `###`:

1. The frontmatter of B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`, the guide renderer), unchanged (`name: omaddons` and the trigger sentence below, verbatim), `{{stamp}}` on the next line, then B1's generated-by comment line.
2. `# omaddons for agents`: what it is, with `{{command_count}}`, and the discovery trio.
3. `## The core loop`: six numbered steps (status; preview unless the user asked for exactly that change; show `data.approval` and apply with `--actor agent --reason "<why>"`; **lost output → `plans show` before anything else**; the doctor loop; the escape hatch), and one line on `--actor` and `--reason`.
4. `## Reading the envelope`: keys, `error`, `partial`, `warnings`, `commands[]` and `destructive`, argv only, never parse display text, the doctor's top-level report, ignore unknown names within `1.x`; then `{{actions}}`.
5. `## Exit codes`: `{{exit_general}}`, `{{exit_doctor}}`.
6. `## Targets and refs`: `{{targets}}`, `-t` always, `target_ambiguous`, `-t all`, `targets --json`, refs, `search`.
7. `## The safety model`: transactions and undo (and the redo), running clients, previews bind, per client, lost output, the doctor, two kinds of run.
8. `## Things omaddons will NEVER do`: `{{never}}`.
9. `## Recipes`: how to read them, then the eight blocks.
10. `## Errors you will meet`: counts, `error.code`, `retryable: true`, `game_running`, then `{{errors_common}}`.
11. `## The doctor loop`: four numbered steps (triage; run `recommended_argv`; a P0 not auto-fixable is the user's call, never add `--force --yes`; undo).
12. `## Commands`: one lead line, `{{commands}}`.
13. `## Environment`: `{{env}}`.
14. `## Where to look next`: capabilities, robot-docs schema and errors, doctor robot-docs and capabilities, help, `robot-docs install-skill`, README.

### 2. The draft to commit

# omaddons for agents

omaddons manages World of Warcraft addons for every client on this Linux machine, with one binary of {{command_count}} commands. Every change is a journaled transaction that `omaddons undo` reverts, a preview can be applied exactly as it was shown, and with `--json` every command prints one envelope whose errors carry their fix as an argv. Ask the binary for the rest: `omaddons capabilities --json`, `omaddons robot-docs schema <command>` and `omaddons robot-docs errors`.

## The core loop

1. `omaddons status --json`: every client, what needs attention, and the next commands in `commands[]`.
2. Preview a change before you make it, unless the user asked for exactly that change: add `--dry-run --json`, as in `omaddons update --dry-run --json`. The preview changes nothing and returns `data.plan_id`.
3. Show the user `data.approval.selection` (each change) and `data.approval.reasons` (anything beyond a routine update). When they approve, run `omaddons apply <plan_id> --json --actor agent --reason "<why>"`.
4. Lost an `apply`'s output? Run `omaddons plans show <plan_id> --json` before you preview or change anything again: it says whether the plan committed.
5. Something broken? Follow the doctor loop below.
6. The escape hatch: `omaddons undo --last-by agent --json` reverts the newest run an agent made.

Pass `--actor agent` and a `--reason` on every change: history records both.

## Reading the envelope

With `--json`, stdout is one JSON object: `ok`, `schema_version`, `tool_version`, `command`, `exit_code`, `partial`, `data`, `error`, `warnings`, `commands` and `meta`.

- `error` is present exactly when `ok` is `false`. It carries `code`, `message`, `fix`, `fix_argv`, `alternatives`, `retryable` and `details`. `fix_argv` is `null` when the fix is prose or needs a value only you can supply.
- `partial: true` with exit 0 means some items failed; `data` says which and why.
- `warnings` never change the exit code. `commands` are the suggested next steps, each with `action`, `command`, `argv` and `destructive`; ask the user before running one marked `destructive: true`.
- Run `fix_argv`, `alternatives[].argv` and `commands[].argv` as argv arrays, never through a shell. Never parse `message`, `fix`, `command` or human output: branch on `exit_code`, `error.code` and `data`.
- Doctor commands put their report at the top level instead of in `data` (`state`, `summary`, `findings`). There `ok` means exit 0, and findings (exit 1) are a report, not an error.
- `schema_version` is the contract version. A `1.x` release only adds keys, enum values, codes and actions, so ignore the ones you do not know.

`-t` names a client in any of these forms, tried in this order:

{{targets}}

The client always goes in `-t`, as in `omaddons update -t retail`. A command that acts on one client needs `-t` when several match (`target_ambiguous` lists them), and `-t all` selects every client where a command takes several. `omaddons targets --json` lists the clients.

Refs: a catalog name, `gh:Owner/Repo` or `Owner/Repo`, `wowi:<id>`, `tukui:<slug>`, `wowace:<slug>`, `git:https://…#<rev>`, `url:https://…`, a pasted addon page link, or a local zip or folder. `omaddons search <words> --json` finds one.

## The safety model

- **Transactions.** Every change is one journaled transaction per client, and a crash leaves each client wholly old or wholly new. Bare `omaddons undo` reverts the newest run, `--last-by agent` the newest run by an agent, `undo <tx>` one transaction and `undo --run <run>` one run. An undo is itself a change: running the same undo again puts the change back.
- **Running clients.** A folder change while a client runs needs `--while-running`, and the user then types `/reload` in game (`data.reload_required`). SavedVariables are never written while the client runs, whatever the flags.
- **Previews bind.** `omaddons apply <plan_id>` runs exactly what the preview showed, or refuses with `plan_stale` and changes nothing; `--if-match <data.precondition>` binds a typed run the same way. `plan_stale` from a bound run is never retryable: `details.changed` or `details.reason` (`expired`, `binary_changed`, `input_missing`, `already_applied`) says why, and its `fix_argv` previews again. A plan lives 24 hours; after that, or once the cache is cleared, `apply` answers `plan_not_found`. A preview that would change nothing stores no plan (`plan_id` is `null`).
- **Per client.** On each client a bound run commits exactly the approved operations or none of them. A run over several clients is one transaction per client, so it can end partial: `data.outcomes[]` gives each client's `status` (`committed`, `unchanged`, `stale` or `failed`) with its `tx` or `error_code`. No run over several clients is atomic.
- **Lost output.** `plans show` reads history: its `state` is `pending`, `completed`, `partial`, `expired` or `unknown`, and `evidence` lists each committed client with its `tx`. A second `apply` of an applied plan refuses with `already_applied`; it never applies twice.
- **The doctor.** `omaddons doctor` only reads. `doctor fix` changes things only when run, backs up what it replaces and deletes nothing. `undo` reverts a repair as long as nothing it touched has changed since; after such a change it refuses with `undo_conflict` before moving anything.
- **Two kinds of run.** History's `run` is one omaddons invocation, a ULID, reverted with `undo --run <run>`. A doctor run is a directory of reports and backups named by its UTC time and a ULID, reverted with `doctor undo <doctor_run>`. `undo --run` given a doctor run refuses, and its fix is the matching `doctor undo`.

## Recipes

Each recipe is at most two commands; run them in order. `expect=` lists each command's exit code (`|` separates alternatives), and a `# <name> is …` line says which field of the first command's JSON fills a placeholder. Use them for requests the user made explicitly, and preview anything else first, as the core loop says.

Update every addon on every client; one `omaddons undo` reverts it all:

```sh recipe=update-everything expect=0
omaddons update --json --actor agent --reason "the user asked to update every addon"
```

What is broken (the doctor exits 1 when it has findings):

```sh recipe=whats-broken expect=0,0|1
omaddons status --json
omaddons doctor --robot-triage --json
```

Install an addon on one client:

```sh recipe=install-for-target expect=0
omaddons install weakauras -t era --json --actor agent
```

Add a legacy addon from a git repository:

```sh recipe=legacy-from-git expect=0
omaddons install git:https://github.com/fondlez/GroupBulletinBoard#main -t wotlk --json
```

Preview, then apply exactly what was shown:

```sh recipe=preview-then-apply expect=0,0
omaddons install dbm -t retail --dry-run --json
# <plan_id> is data.plan_id of the command above
omaddons apply <plan_id> --json
```

Undo what the agent did today. `undo --last-by agent` reverts the newest agent run; revert an earlier one with `undo --run <run>` from the list:

```sh recipe=undo-agent-today expect=0,0
omaddons history --by agent --since 1d --json
omaddons undo --last-by agent --json
```

Explain pending updates with their release notes:

```sh recipe=explain-updates expect=0
omaddons outdated --changelog --json
```

Set up a fresh machine from the `addons.toml` that `omaddons export` wrote on the old one, at the recorded versions:

```sh recipe=fresh-machine expect=0
omaddons sync addons.toml --locked --json
```

## Errors you will meet

omaddons has {{error_code_count}} error codes and {{warning_code_count}} warning codes. Branch on `error.code`, never on `message`. `retryable: true` means the same command may succeed if run again: `locked` (another omaddons is committing), `network`, and `rate_limited` after `details.reset_at`. `game_running` means the user must quit the game; never work around it. The ones agents meet most:

## The doctor loop

1. `omaddons doctor --robot-triage --json`: the findings, `actions_planned` (what `doctor fix` would do) and `recommended_argv`, the one command to run next.
2. Run `recommended_argv` with `--json --actor agent --reason "<why>"`. When something is auto-fixable it is `omaddons doctor fix --only <finding_id>`, which backs up what it changes; otherwise it is `omaddons doctor explain <finding_id>`, which only reads.
3. A P0 finding that is not auto-fixable is the user's decision: tell them before anything else. Never add `--force --yes` yourself; a forced repair is for someone who has read `doctor explain`.
4. `omaddons undo --last-by agent --json` reverts a repair like any other change.

A failure names the section and the missing token or the out-of-order heading; T1's guard prints `test log: <path>` and the last 20 steps on a panic. The truth audit is the step that catches it; the name check and the parse check catch renamed names and flags mechanically.

title: E2E: the guide's core loop and doctor loop run as written
description:
Part 3 of 3 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.2 (The guide's content). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

B2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.2`) writes the content of omaddons' agent guide, the Markdown that `omaddons robot-docs guide` prints, that the repository commits as `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` and that an agent loads as its skill (M4-D7). An agent copies the guide verbatim, so every claim must be true of the code. Subtask 1 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.2.1) made every command parse and every name registered; subtask 2 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.2.2) wrote the prose: a core loop (status, preview, apply, reconcile a lost output with `plans show`, the doctor, the escape hatch) and a doctor loop (triage, run `recommended_argv`, undo a repair).

Parsing proves syntax, not behaviour. This part proves the two loops work **as written**: it extracts the commands from the rendered guide's sections and runs them, in order, on synthetic homes, asserting what the prose promises after each step. It also runs every read-only command the guide names, because a command can parse and still refuse its values at run time (`history --since yesterday` parses and is a usage error). The eight recipes are B4's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.4`, the recipes run end to end) to run; the two loops are not recipes, so nothing else runs them. It is its own step because these are cross-cutting end-to-end scenarios over the finished prose, and they need subtask 2's text to extract from.

The behaviour these scenarios hold the guide to, restated from the decisions:
- **M4-D63:** `omaddons plans show <PLAN_ID>` reconciles an approval with history, offline and writing nothing: `state` `completed` when every approved target has a committed transaction carrying the plan id, with `evidence.targets[]` of `{target, key, tx, result, at}` and `evidence.complete`.
- **M4-D23, M4-D25, M4-D61:** `apply` runs the stored plan; `outcomes[]` names each target's `status` and `tx`; a second `apply` of an applied plan is `plan_stale` with `details.reason: "already_applied"` and `details.txs`, never retryable, and changes nothing. A plan whose only source is a local archive applies offline.
- **M4-D34, M4-D40:** doctor reports are at the envelope's top level (no `data`); `--robot-triage` gives `view: "triage"`, `summary`, `actions_planned[]` and `recommended_argv`; the doctor's exit 1 means findings, 0 healthy.
- **M4-D46 (E7, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7`):** `undo --last-by agent` selects and reverts a repair like any change, byte for byte; `undo --run <a doctor run id>` is `usage` with the fix `omaddons doctor undo <id>`.
- **E6's test fixers** (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`, `doctor fix`): in debug builds, with `OMADDONS_TEST_FIXERS=1`, `fm-test-write` (enabled, auto-fixable, needs no force) finds any `*.write` file under `<state>/doctor-test/` whose bytes are not `repaired\n` and repairs it by writing `repaired\n` with a verbatim backup.
- **A1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1`):** every `COMMANDS` row declares its `exits` (in its row's dictionary) and `mutates`.

## Technical Approach

### The suite

`tests/skill_loops.rs` (new). Its crate doc starts with the marker of T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs and the `argc e2e` runner), so `argc e2e` runs it:

```rust
//! e2e suite: the guide's core loop and doctor loop run as written, and every read-only command it names runs
```

It uses `common::guide` (`rendered` of B1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`; subtask 1's `commands`, `sections`, `inline_spans`, `fill`, `argv`), `common::home::Home`, `common::archives::zip_text`, `common::addons::toc` and T1's `tlog`. Each scenario renders the guide through the binary on its own home and takes the commands it runs from the named section. A span it needs and cannot find fails with "the <section> section no longer holds `<prefix>`; update tests/skill_loops.rs with the guide", so a prose change that alters a loop is a reviewed change of this test too.

How a span becomes an argv: `guide::fill(span, &values)` with the scenario's values, then `guide::argv`, then drop the leading `omaddons`. Values used here: `<plan_id>` the plan the scenario stored; `<why>` `the user approved the preview` (core loop) or `the doctor recommended this repair` (doctor loop); `<finding_id>`, `<command>` and `<words>` as listed in scenario 3. A span with any other placeholder fails, naming it.

### Scenario 1: `core_loop_runs_as_written`

Setup: `Home::new(&["wow"])` (one synthetic retail client); create `home.addons("_retail_")` empty (so the round trip compares a directory that exists before and after); write `<root>/dl/Foo-1.0.0.zip` holding `Foo/Foo.toc` = `toc("120105", &["## Version: 1.0.0"])` (the pattern of `tests/install.rs:736-757`). The first change writes a `target.json` marker into the client dir that stays after undo by design, so the scenario hashes `Interface/AddOns`, never the client dir. From the rendered guide's "The core loop" section: the spans starting `omaddons status`, `omaddons apply`, `omaddons plans show` and `omaddons undo --last-by agent`.

1. `log.step("status")`: run the status span → `ok()`; `data` present.
2. `log.tree("addons", addons)`.
3. `log.step("preview")`: `["install", <zip>, "-t", "retail", "--dry-run", "--json"]` (the concrete instance of the loop's step 2) → `ok()`; `data.plan_id` is a 26-character string (`plan_id`); `data.approval.selection` has one item naming the addon `Foo` (compared case-insensitively) with `op` `install`; `commands()` holds an entry with `action` `apply` and `argv` `["omaddons", "apply", plan_id]`; `log.assert_unchanged("addons", addons)`.
4. `log.step("apply as the guide writes it")`: the apply span with `<plan_id>` and `<why>` filled → `ok()`; `data.outcomes` is one element with `target` `retail`, `status` `committed` and a `tx` string (`tx`); `Interface/AddOns/Foo/Foo.toc` is a file; `log.tree("installed", addons)`.
5. `log.step("lost output: plans show")`: the plans-show span with `<plan_id>` filled → `ok()`; `data.state` `completed`, `data.stored` `true`, `data.evidence.complete` `true`, and `data.evidence.targets` holds `{target: "retail", tx: tx, result: "committed"}`; the run added no `net.log` line (offline, M4-D63).
6. `log.step("a second apply refuses")`: the same apply argv → `fails(1, "plan_stale")`; `error.retryable` `false`; `error.details.reason` `already_applied`; `error.details.txs` contains `tx`; `log.assert_unchanged("installed", addons)`.
7. `log.step("escape hatch")`: the undo span → `ok()`; `log.assert_unchanged("addons", addons)`: `Interface/AddOns` is back to its first hash.

### Scenario 2: `doctor_loop_runs_as_written`

`#[cfg_attr(not(debug_assertions), ignore = "needs the debug build's test fixers")]`: the test fixers are compiled into debug builds only (E6, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`), which is what `cargo test` and the gate build. Every run of this scenario is `log.cmd(&home, &argv).env("OMADDONS_TEST_FIXERS", "1").run()`.

Setup: `Home::new(&["wow"])`; `let subject = home.state().join("doctor-test")`; create it and write `a.write` = `broken\n`; `log.tree("subject", &subject)`. From the rendered guide's "The doctor loop" section: the spans starting `omaddons doctor --robot-triage` and `omaddons undo --last-by agent`, and the inline span of step 2 that starts with `--json` (the flags it says to add, `--json --actor agent --reason "<why>"`).

1. `log.step("triage")`: the triage span → `exit(1)` (findings present, the doctor dictionary); at the top level, `view` `triage`, `summary.auto_fixable >= 1`, `actions_planned[]` has an entry with `fixer_id` `fm-test-write`; `recommended_argv` starts `["omaddons", "doctor", "fix", "--only", <ids>]` where `<ids>` split on `,` contains `fm-test-write`, and it holds neither `--force` nor `--yes`; `log.assert_unchanged("subject", &subject)`.
2. `log.step("fix by the recommendation")`: `recommended_argv` without its leading `omaddons`, followed by the step-2 flags span with `<why>` filled → `exit(0)`; at the top level, `state` `DONE_OK`, a `tx` string and a `run_id` string (`run_id`); `a.write` now holds `repaired\n`; `log.tree("repaired", &subject)`.
3. `log.step("the two kinds of run")`: `["undo", "--run", run_id, "--json"]` → `fails(2, "usage")`; `error.fix_argv` is `["omaddons", "doctor", "undo", run_id]`; `log.assert_unchanged("repaired", &subject)`.
4. `log.step("escape hatch")`: the undo span → `ok()`; `log.assert_unchanged("subject", &subject)`: the planted bytes and mode are back; `a.write` holds `broken\n`.
5. `log.step("triage again")`: the triage span → `exit(1)`, and `actions_planned[]` again names `fm-test-write`.

### Scenario 3: `every_read_only_command_the_guide_names_runs`

Setup: `Home::new(&["wow"])` with an empty `Interface/AddOns`; install `<root>/dl/Foo-1.0.0.zip` (`["install", <zip>, "-t", "retail", "--json"]` → `ok()`), so history has a transaction; preview `<root>/dl/Bar-1.0.0.zip` (`--dry-run --json` → `ok()`), whose `data.plan_id` is the stored plan; `["doctor", "capabilities", "--json"]` → `exit(0)`, whose first `detectors[].id` (top level) is a real failure-mode id.

1. `log.step("extract")`: `guide::commands(&rendered)`, keeping `Full` and `RecipeLine` spans (fragments are not whole commands).
2. `log.step("classify")`: for each, fill with B1's and subtask 1's `SAMPLES`, parse with `omaddons::cli::Cli::try_parse_from`, take its path with `omaddons::app::command_name(cli.command.as_ref())`, and find its `COMMANDS` row; a row with `mutates: true` is skipped and logged ("mutating: run by the loops above or by the recipes of B4, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.4`"); the rest are deduplicated by their filled argv.
3. `log.step("run")`: for each read-only command, `log.case(<span>)`: fill with the run values (`<plan_id>` the stored preview's id, `<finding_id>` the detector id from setup, `<command>` `update`, `<words>` `foo`; any other placeholder fails "add a run value for <name> in tests/skill_loops.rs"), append `--json` when absent, run with `OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1`; assert the exit is one of the row's declared `exits` and, when the envelope has an `error`, that its `code` is not `usage`.
4. `log.json("ran", {ran, skipped_mutating})`; assert `ran >= 8`, so an extractor bug cannot make the test vacuous.

`OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1` (the variable that mirrors `--offline`) keeps the network commands (`outdated --changelog`, `search`) from making requests; an offline answer, success or `offline`, is a declared exit. A `net.log` line added by any of these runs is a failure: the variable was not honoured.

### README

Development, the tests table: the row that names `tests/skill.rs` (B1's) gains `tests/skill_loops.rs`: "the guide's core loop and doctor loop run as written, and every read-only command it names runs".

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `tests/skill_loops.rs` exists, carries the `//! e2e suite:` marker of T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`), and its three scenarios take every command they run from the rendered guide's sections, failing with a named message when a needed span is gone.
- [ ] `core_loop_runs_as_written` passes: the preview stores a plan and offers `apply`; the guide's apply commits on `retail` (`outcomes[]`: `committed`, with a `tx`); the guide's `plans show` reports `completed` with that `tx` and adds no `net.log` line; a second apply is `plan_stale` with `already_applied`, `details.txs` and `retryable: false`, changing nothing; the guide's undo returns `Interface/AddOns` to its first hash.
- [ ] `doctor_loop_runs_as_written` passes in debug builds: triage exits 1 and recommends `doctor fix --only` naming `fm-test-write` without `--force` or `--yes`; the recommendation with the guide's flags repairs the file (`DONE_OK`, exit 0); `undo --run <run_id>` is `usage` with the fix `omaddons doctor undo <run_id>` and changes nothing; the guide's undo restores the planted bytes and mode; triage finds the finding again.
- [ ] `every_read_only_command_the_guide_names_runs` runs at least eight read-only commands, each to an exit its `COMMANDS` row declares and never to `usage`, with no `net.log` line added.
- [ ] README's tests table names `tests/skill_loops.rs`.
- [ ] Every scenario logs through `TestLog`, and a failure prints its log path; `argc e2e skill` runs the suite with verbose logs.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

None new: the helpers' cases are subtask 1's.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

The three scenarios above, in `tests/skill_loops.rs`, each on its own `Home` (a synthetic Battle.net root with one retail client in a Wine prefix, under a `TestEnv` tempdir), with the steps, commands and assertions listed. No HTTP fixture is needed: the installs and the plan use local archives, and the read-only scenario runs offline.

### Logging

Every scenario starts with `let log = tlog!();` and names its phases with `log.step` as listed; every command goes through `log.run` or `log.cmd(…).env(…).run()`, so the log records each argv, the overrides (`OMADDONS_TEST_FIXERS`, `OMADDONS_OFFLINE`), the working directory, the exit code, the parsed envelope (doctor reports included), stderr and the `net.log` lines added. The rendered guide is logged as `{sha256, lines, bytes}`, and each span the scenario took from it is logged with its section and line before it runs (`log.note`). Trees go through `log.tree` and `log.assert_unchanged` (`addons` and `installed` in scenario 1; `subject` and `repaired` in scenario 2), which log the first differing paths. Scenario 3 runs each command as `log.case(<span>)`, so a failure points at one command, and ends with the `ran` summary. On a panic, the guard of T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`) prints `test log: <path>` and the last 20 steps; `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG=verbose` (as `argc e2e skill` sets it) echoes each step live.

## Considerations

- **Extraction by prefix is intended to be strict.** If subtask 2's prose (or a later edit) rewords a loop so that a span is gone, this test fails and says which; updating the test with the guide is the review that keeps the loops runnable.
- **Other findings on the synthetic home.** The doctor scenario asserts only that `fm-test-write` is among the planned fixes; if another auto-fixable finding is planned too, the recommendation includes it, the repair fixes it, and the undo reverts the whole repair, which the tree assertions still check for the subject.
- **Debug only.** A release build has no test fixers, so scenario 2 is ignored there with its reason; the gate builds debug, so it always runs in the gate.
- **The target marker.** The first change on a client writes `target.json` into the client dir, and it stays after undo (README: "Target registrations and target.json markers written on the first change stay"); compare `Interface/AddOns` only.
- **No network.** A plan whose only source is a local archive applies offline; `plans show` is offline by design; the read-only scenario sets `OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1`. A request would show in `net.log` and fail the scenario.
- **Privacy.** No `WTF/` is created; the planted file is test content under `<state>`.
- **Hot spots:** `tests/skill_loops.rs` is new and this subtask's alone; `README.md` (only the tests-table row).

## Dependencies

- Parent: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.2 (The guide's content).
- Before it: subtask 2 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.2.2), whose prose it extracts from, and through it subtask 1 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.2.1), whose helpers it uses. Through the leaf: D5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`, `apply`), D9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.9`, `plans show`), E4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4`, `--robot-triage` and `doctor capabilities`), E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`, `doctor fix` and the test fixers) and E7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7`, undo of repairs and the doctor-run refusal). It also needs T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs and the `argc e2e` runner; a `blocks` edge added at filing) for `TestLog` and the e2e marker.
- After it: when this is the last open subtask, the leaf closes and unblocks B4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.4`, the recipes run end to end).

description:
## How to work this bead

This bead is worked through its 5 subtasks, listed below in work order. Claim a subtask, not this bead (`br ready --parent omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3` lists the ready ones). The agent that closes the last open subtask then verifies every acceptance criterion of this bead (they are the leaf's, not any one subtask's), and closes this bead with `br close omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3 --reason "done: <evidence> · found: <ids>"`. Until this bead is closed, every bead it blocks stays blocked.

1. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3.1 The `skill` settings kind, its `dir`, and `history_tail.skill_dirs[]`: `TxKind::Skill`, `SettingEntry.dir`, `history`'s `entries[].dir`, the projection field and the constant `SKILL_DIRS_MAX`, with their unit tests. Starts at once.

## Background

**What this is.** M4 makes omaddons describe itself to coding agents. B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`, the guide renderer and `robot-docs guide`) renders one Markdown handbook, the guide, and commits it as `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md`; B2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.2`, the guide's content) writes its prose. This bead puts that guide where agents load skills, with one command:

```text
$ omaddons robot-docs install-skill
installed the omaddons skill: $HOME/.claude/skills/omaddons/SKILL.md (18,432 bytes)
```

Claude Code loads every `SKILL.md` under `$HOME/.claude/skills/<name>/` and decides from its frontmatter `description` when to read it, so after this command a Claude Code session on the machine knows omaddons' core loop, safety model and recipes as soon as a conversation mentions WoW addons, without reading README. The command writes exactly the guide's bytes (byte identity is what lets the doctor detect drift later), never writes anywhere it was not asked to, records who installed it in history, and leaves the folder name the doctor needs in the history projection. Today none of this exists: there is no command that writes a skill.

**The milestone goals it serves.**
- **G-M4-1, self-describing:** an agent with no prior knowledge learns everything it needs from the binary itself (`capabilities --json`, `robot-docs guide`, `status --json`). The installed skill is the shortcut for the agent that runs on this machine: it starts with the guide already loaded.
- **G-M4-6, no new risk to the engine's guarantees:** every new write goes through fsx, dry runs leave `<state>` untouched, and the global lock is held only for the write. This bead's one write is an atomic fsx `WriteFile` under the global lock, plus a settings history line.

**The checkpoint criteria it serves** (§3.2, H6 records the evidence):
- **Criterion 3, the guide and the skill:** "`omaddons robot-docs install-skill` writes the same bytes to `<skills>/SKILL.md`, and a second run writes nothing." The same criterion's drift bullet ("`doctor` reports an installed skill whose guide digest differs from this binary's … `doctor fix` brings it current, undoably; a skill whose bytes no longer match its own stamp was edited by hand and is left to the user") is F10's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.10`, skill drift), built on the `history_tail.skill_dirs[]` field and the stamp inspector this bead adds.
- **Criterion 17, gate and checkpoint runs:** "the real-machine tests pass with every `SKIP` quoted". This bead owns `tests/real_machine.rs::install_skill_round_trip`, one of the three real-machine tests M4 adds (with D7's and E6's); H6 only runs it.
- **§3.3, owner involvement, decided:** nothing in M4 installs the skill into the real `$HOME/.claude/skills/`. A skill there is loaded by every Claude Code session on the machine, which is the owner's choice, made with one command whenever they like. The checkpoint proves that the default path resolves (a dry run against the real home) and that the install works (a real install into a scratch folder), which is the whole of what an install into the real directory would prove.
- **Slice 1's exit demo** ("`install-skill` into a throwaway `HOME`") is recorded by T2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.2`, slice 1 end to end), which calls this bead's test helpers.

**How it serves the vision.** The vision says "the skill is installed where agents look" and names `$HOME/.claude/skills/omaddons/` (vision G4, agent ergonomics: "the first command an agent guesses works"). The history line keeps G4's "every change is attributed". The thesis that omaddons stays the sole, safe, undoable authority over what it manages holds here in its smallest form: the skill is one derived file, written only where the user pointed, never through a symlink, never over a hand-edited copy without keeping that copy.

**The decisions that shape it** (full text in the decision log comments on the milestone epic `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`):

- **M4-D8: `install-skill` writes `<skills>/SKILL.md` by default, `--dir` anywhere sensible, and records a history line.** Restated in full, because every rule below comes from it:
  - `omaddons robot-docs install-skill [--dir <DIR>]` writes `<DIR>/SKILL.md` (default `<skills>` = `$HOME/.claude/skills/omaddons`) through fsx (`Writer::Skill`).
  - **Creating directories.** The default creates `skills/` and `skills/omaddons/` when `$HOME/.claude` exists: a machine that has used Claude Code but never installed a skill has no `skills/` yet, and refusing there would fail the one obvious command. Without `$HOME/.claude` it is `not_found` naming the path, with the alternatives `--dir <d>` for each other skill root that exists. A custom `--dir` is created if its parent exists; a missing parent is `not_found` (exit 3) with the path, never `scope_denied`: nothing was refused, something is missing.
  - A custom `--dir` gets a runtime single-directory scope, like M3's `ExportFile`. It refuses with `scope_denied`: a directory inside a client dir or a Wine prefix; a directory inside `<config>`, `<state>` or `<cache>`.
  - **A symlinked `SKILL.md`** (common in dotfiles setups) is never written through: fsx refuses a symlink as an operation's final component. The result is `scope_denied` with `details.reason: "symlink"`, the link's target, and prose advice to install with `--dir` into the real directory or to replace the link.
  - **The stamp** is M4-D7's guide digest, on the line after the frontmatter. It lets the doctor detect drift (another guide) and local edits (bytes that no longer match their own stamp) without rendering anything.
  - Unchanged bytes (the whole file compared) write nothing (`written: "unchanged"`). Otherwise `written: "fresh" | "replaced"`.
  - The write takes the global lock, as `config set` and `auth` do, so it serializes with repairs that rewrite a skill.
  - Each write appends a settings history line of a new kind, `skill`, which undo never reverts (like `widget`, M3-D38). It is not a transaction: the previous file is recoverable by re-running an older build. The History scope row admits `Writer::Skill` for that line. `history_tail` gains `skill_dirs[]`, the directories those lines name, newest first, bounded to `SKILL_DIRS_MAX` (this bead owns the constant).
  - `commands[]` offers `install-skill --dir <d>/omaddons` for each other agent skill root that exists on the machine (`$HOME/.codex/skills`, `$HOME/.agents/skills`), never writing there unasked.
  - Nothing recommends installing the skill unasked. `status` stays about the clients: a recommendation the user cannot dismiss would nag forever, and suppressing it after a removal would need state.
  - There is no remove command. Deleting the folder is the removal, and README says so.
  - **Why:** the vision names the location; the machine has three skill roots, and offering the others as commands respects "never write without being asked" while making the second install one command; the history line keeps attribution.
  - **Rejected:** (i) writing every known root by default (surprising writes outside the vision's one location); (ii) a transaction with undo (the skill is a derived file anyone can regenerate, so undo would be machinery for nothing); (iii) a symlink to a repository file (it breaks when the binary is installed without the repository, and Omarchy's plugin rules forbid symlinks in a similar situation).
  - **Departure from the vision:** additions only, the `skill` history kind and the other-roots hints.
- **M4-D7: the guide, `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` and the installed skill are one artifact.** The guide opens with YAML frontmatter (`name: omaddons`, `description: …`), because a skill file must start with it; the line right after the frontmatter is the stamp `<!-- omaddons guide sha256:<hex> -->`, the SHA-256 of the canonical document with that one line omitted. The guide never embeds a build id, crate version or contract version, so its identity is its own content. `build.rs` computes the stamp-omitted digest of the committed `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` into `OMADDONS_GUIDE_SHA256` (`contract::guide::EXPECTED_DIGEST`, published as `capabilities.guide_digest`). **`install-skill` writes the same bytes**, so the guide, the repository file and an installed skill from the same guide are byte-identical, and drift is a digest comparison. Rejected there, and tempting here: stamping the version only at install time (the installed skill would then differ from the guide, breaking byte identity, which the vision requires and drift detection uses). This bead never edits, re-stamps or post-processes the rendered bytes.
- **M4-D50: drift of the widget is reported; drift of the skill is repaired.** F10's detector `fm-plugins-skill-version-drift` (`cached` tier) looks at `Paths::skill_dir()` and at every directory in `history_tail.skill_dirs[]`, "a projection field B3 adds (every directory a `skill` history line names, newest first, bounded to `SKILL_DIRS_MAX`). The projection keeps them however old the install is, which a scan of the history tail's runs would not." A locally edited skill is never rewritten by the doctor; its finding's remediation is manual, "`omaddons robot-docs install-skill --dir <dir>`, which keeps a backup". A symlinked `SKILL.md` is reported with advice and never written through. A skill directory that no longer exists is not a finding.
- **M4-D22 (context): `robot-docs install-skill` neither stores a plan nor binds** (`--if-match`). A plan would describe nothing the command line does not already say. Common rule 16 is met by recording that in the close comment, citing M4-D22.
- **M4-D11 (context): recommendation actions are an enumerable registry.** `contract::actions::Action` (A2) gains `InstallSkill`, wire name `install_skill`, one of M4's five new actions. A2 decided to add only the actions that exist when it lands, so the variant lands here, in the commit that first constructs it.
- **M4-D55 (context): the contract's naming and nullability rules hold from slice 1** (A3's rule test). Rule 2 (a key is always present, `null` when it has no value; omission is reserved for `-v` additions and fields documented as optional) shapes `entries[].dir` below; rule 4 (closed enumerations) shapes `written`.
- **M4-D18 (context):** no `HashMap` or `HashSet` in a serialized type; this bead declares no volatile key (its data holds no time, id or duration).

## Technical Approach

### 1. The command surface

`omaddons robot-docs install-skill [--dir <DIR>]`, group Setup (a nested command takes its parent's group), plus the global flags as everywhere. `--dry-run`, `--json`, `--actor`, `--reason` and `--progress` behave as on every command; `-t`, `--offline` and `--while-running` have no effect (there is no client and no request); `--if-match` is refused by the existing check (`usage`, fix `omaddons help robot-docs install-skill`).

- The clap variant `InstallSkill(InstallSkillArgs)` joins A5's `robot-docs` action enum in `src/app/robot_docs.rs`; the command lives in a new module `src/app/install_skill.rs` (`pub mod install_skill` in `src/app/mod.rs`). Decided while writing this bead: a module of its own keeps the hot spot `robot_docs.rs` (A5, B1) to a one-line change.
- `InstallSkillArgs { dir: Option<PathBuf> }`, `#[arg(long, value_name = "DIR")]`, doc: "The skill folder to write SKILL.md into (default: $HOME/.claude/skills/omaddons; created if its parent exists)".
- About (the variant's doc comment): "Install the agent guide as a skill (SKILL.md) where coding agents load skills". `after_long_help`: three examples (the default, `--dry-run`, `--dir $HOME/.codex/skills/omaddons`) and one line: "Remove it by deleting the folder." The help never promises what a later leaf adds: the sentence that `omaddons doctor` reports an outdated skill lands with F10.

### 2. Resolving the directory (part 4, `install_skill::resolve`)

Everything in §2–§4 runs before the lock and writes nothing, so a wrong invocation changes nothing (common rule 8).

- **Default (no `--dir`):** `dir = Paths::skill_dir()` (`$HOME/.claude/skills/omaddons`), and the folder that must already exist is `Paths::claude_dir()` (`$HOME/.claude`, a new one-line accessor beside `skill_dir` in `src/state/paths.rs`). If `$HOME/.claude` is not a directory: `not_found` (exit 3), `details.path` = `$HOME/.claude`, the message "Claude Code's folder $HOME/.claude does not exist, so there is no default place to install the skill" (with the real path), the prose fix "set up Claude Code first, or choose a skills folder with --dir <dir>", `fix_argv` null, and one `alternatives` entry per other existing skill root (§8).
- **Custom (`--dir D`):** a relative `D` is joined to the working directory (as `backup export` does). Before anything else:
  - `D` that names no folder (empty, `/`, or ending in `..`) is `usage`: "--dir names the folder that holds SKILL.md".
  - `D` that exists and is not a directory (a file, a FIFO) is `usage`: "--dir <D> is not a folder".
  - `D` whose path is not valid UTF-8 is `usage`: the folder is recorded in history and JSON, both text. Decided while writing this bead: refuse before writing rather than record a lossy path.
  - The folder that must exist is `D`'s parent. A missing parent is `not_found` (exit 3) with `details.path` = the parent, message "the folder <parent> that would hold <D> does not exist; install-skill creates only the skill folder itself", prose fix "create the parent folder first, or choose a --dir whose parent exists" (raised by part 2's `with_skill_dir`).
- `--dir $HOME/.claude/skills/omaddons` given explicitly follows the custom rules (its parent `skills/` must exist); only the default creates `skills/`. That is M4-D8's wording, and the README says it.
- **Paths are canonical.** The directory reported in `data.dir`, recorded in the history line's `dir` and kept in `skill_dirs[]` is the canonical absolute path (symlinked ancestors resolved, through the deepest existing ancestor). Decided while writing this bead: one spelling per folder, so `skill_dirs[]` deduplicates `--dir` spellings and symlinked homes, and F10 compares like with like.

### 3. The scope (part 2, `src/fsx/scope.rs`)

- **The History row admits `Writer::Skill`** (`:114-117`), so the history line goes through the command's own session, as `config set`'s and the widget's do. No other row changes: `Writer::Skill` stays refused everywhere but the Skill, History, NetLog and Cache rows.
- **`ScopeTable::with_skill_dir(mut self, dir: &Path, create_from: &Path) -> Result<Self>`**, the install-skill run's single skill folder (M4-D8's "uses that slot for this run"):
  1. `create_from` (the default's `$HOME/.claude`, or a `--dir`'s parent) must exist as a directory: else `not_found`, `details.path` = `create_from` as given (§2's message).
  2. `dir` is canonicalized with the table's `canonical` helper (deepest existing ancestor; an existing `dir` that is a symlink resolves to where it points).
  3. The refusals, on the canonical `dir`, each `scope_denied` (exit 4, not retryable) with `details: {"reason": "skill_dir", "path": <canonical dir>}`, the prose fix "install the skill into a folder of your own, outside game clients, Wine prefixes and omaddons' own folders: --dir <dir>", and a message naming what it is inside:
     - inside a registered client dir ("<dir> is inside the game client <client dir>"), for every client dir the table holds;
     - inside a Wine prefix ("<dir> is inside the Wine prefix <prefix>"): any ancestor of `dir` that holds both `drive_c` and `dosdevices`;
     - inside `<config>`, `<state>` or `<cache>` ("<dir> is inside omaddons' own state folder", and so on).
     The checks are `with_export_file`'s, applied to a folder; share the helper rather than copy it.
  4. On success the table's skill slot is the canonical `dir` (it replaces the default; if E5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`, the repair transaction) has already turned the slot into a list, the list becomes `[dir]`), and `skill_anchor` is the canonical `create_from`.
- **Creatable ancestors.** `candidates()` gains, for the Skill row only: a path strictly between `skill_anchor` and the skill folder (below the anchor, above the folder) is `Position::Ancestor`, which accepts only `CreateDir`. With the default that is exactly `$HOME/.claude/skills`; with a `--dir` there is none (its parent must exist). The anchor itself and its other children are never creatable or writable by the Skill row.
- Decided while writing this bead: the same refusals apply to the default folder too (it can only fail them in a pathological home), and the registered client dirs are read only for a custom `--dir`: the default is a fixed path under `$HOME/.claude`, and reading `registry.json` for it would let an unrelated broken registry block the one obvious command. For a custom `--dir`, a `registry.json` that cannot be read fails the run with the loader's own error (`state_corrupt` or `state_too_new`), because a refusal check that cannot see the clients must not pass (§8.1 default 6, fail closed).

### 4. Reading what is there (part 3, beside B1's renderer)

- **`contract::guide::stamp::read_skill_file(path) -> io::Result<SkillFile>`**: one `symlink_metadata`, then
  - `Missing`;
  - `Symlink { link_target: PathBuf }` (from `read_link`, unresolved; a dangling link counts);
  - `NotAFile` (a directory, a FIFO, a socket: never opened);
  - `TooLarge { len }` when the file is longer than `DISCOVERY_FILE_MAX_BYTES` (1 MiB): never read past the bound;
  - `Bytes(Vec<u8>)` otherwise, read with a `take(DISCOVERY_FILE_MAX_BYTES + 1)` guard so a file that grows between `stat` and read is still bounded.
  Decided while writing this bead: the bound reuses `DISCOVERY_FILE_MAX_BYTES` (as C1 does for `registry.json`) rather than a new constant, because a generated guide is under 32 KiB (B2's size test) and a new limit would change `capabilities.limits`; a file past the bound is treated as locally edited (common rule 15: exhaustion is reported, never a clean result).
- **`contract::guide::stamp::inspect(bytes: &[u8]) -> Stamp`**: `Stamped { claimed: [u8; 32], actual: [u8; 32] }` or `Unstamped`.
  - The file must start with the line `---`; the frontmatter ends at the next line that is exactly `---`; the line after it must be exactly `<!-- omaddons guide sha256:<64 lowercase hex> -->`. Anything else (no frontmatter, no closing fence, a stamp on another line, upper-case or short hex, CRLF line ends) is `Unstamped`.
  - `actual` is computed with **the same function B1's renderer uses to fill the stamp** (the document with the stamp line omitted, exactly as B1 defines it). Never re-implement it: a unit test holds `inspect(rendered guide)` to `Stamped { claimed == actual == EXPECTED_DIGEST }`.
  - `Stamp::is_pristine()` is `claimed == actual` (bytes some guide produced); `Stamp::digest()` is `claimed` when pristine. If B1 already exposes a stamp parser, reuse it and add only what is missing.
- F10 uses both functions for its detector (`symlink`, `edited`, current, drifted), so the two beads cannot classify a file differently.

### 5. The flow (part 4, `install_skill::run(ctx, args) -> Result<InstallSkillOutcome>`)

1. `Paths::from_env()`; render the guide with B1's renderer (the bytes `robot-docs guide` prints). The renderer reads no `config.toml` value that changes its output (B1's design: the generated blocks come from the registry and the built-in rules); a test here proves it (§Test Plan).
2. Resolve the directory (§2) and build the scope: `ScopeTable::new(&paths, &clients, None)?.with_skill_dir(&dir, &create_from)?`, where `clients` is the registry's client dirs for a custom `--dir` and empty for the default (§3).
3. `file = <canonical dir>/SKILL.md`; `existing = read_skill_file(&file)`.
   - `Symlink { link_target }` → `scope_denied`, `details: {"reason": "symlink", "path": <file>, "link_target": <link target>}`, message "<file> is a symlink to <link target>; omaddons never writes through a symlink", prose fix "install into the link's real folder with --dir <dir>, or replace the link with a regular file". The link and what it points to stay untouched. This holds even when the link's target already holds these exact bytes (decided while writing this bead, true to M4-D8's unconditional rule; F10 reports such a link the same way).
   - `NotAFile` → `io` (exit 1): "<file> exists and is not a regular file; move it away, then rerun".
4. **Decide** (`install_skill::decide(&existing, &guide) -> Decision`, pure):
   - `Bytes(b)` with `b == guide` → `Unchanged`.
   - `Missing` → `Fresh`.
   - otherwise → `Replaced { keep_edited }`, where `keep_edited` is true when the file is `TooLarge`, `Unstamped`, or `Stamped` but not pristine (its bytes no longer match its own stamp).
5. Build the `commands[]` hints (§8).
6. **`Unchanged`, or `--dry-run`: return now.** No lock, no recovery, no write, no history line. The dry run reports what the run would do (`written` is `fresh`, `replaced` or `unchanged`). Dry runs never take the global lock (§6.18's invariant), and an unchanged run is not a change.
7. **The lock.** `GlobalLock::acquire(&paths, ctx.command)` (waits up to `LOCK_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT`, 5 s; `locked`, exit 5, retryable, whose fix reruns the same argv through the existing boundary fix), then `recover_under(&guard, &paths, &no_saved_variables, ctx.command, ctx.actor)` with its warnings reported through `ctx.notes`, exactly as `config set` does.
8. **Re-read under the lock**: steps 3 and 4 again. Another process may have installed the same bytes meanwhile (→ `Unchanged`: release the lock, no line), replaced the file with a symlink (→ `scope_denied`), or edited it. The decision made under the lock is the one reported.
9. **Write**, in `WriteSession::untracked(Writer::Skill, &scopes, "SKILL.md")`:
   1. `ensure_dir_all(&mut s, &dir)`: creates `skills/` and `skills/omaddons/` for the default, or the `--dir` folder, one scope-checked `CreateDir` each (umask-default permissions, `0755` under the usual `022`).
   2. If `keep_edited`: `Op::Rename { to: <dir>/SKILL.md.bak, mode: Replace }` of the old file. The rename reads nothing (any size works) and replaces an older `.bak`, as `export --write` replaces `addons.toml.bak`.
   3. `Op::WriteFile { content: Content::Bytes(&guide), mode: Some(0o644) }` on `<dir>/SKILL.md`: atomic (temporary file and rename), readable as any skill is.
   4. The history line (§7).
   5. `crate::state::doorbell::ring(&paths, ctx.command, ctx.actor)`: once F10 lands, an install changes what `status` reports.
10. Release the lock and return. `dispatch` then rebuilds the projection if it is stale.

What a failure leaves (the write is one atomic file replacement): a failure before step 9.3 leaves the old file (or, after a `keep_edited` rename, no `SKILL.md` and the edited copy as `SKILL.md.bak`: nothing is lost, and the next run installs fresh); a crash inside step 9.3 may leave fsx's temporary `.omaddons-*` file beside `SKILL.md`, which no agent loads and nothing sweeps (§2.3's known gap, reported in the close comment); a history line that cannot be written leaves the installed file and the warning `history_not_recorded`, exit 0.

**Why the edited copy is kept** (decided while writing this bead). M4-D8 says the skill is a derived file, so the replaced file needs no undo: that is true of a file some guide produced, which any build can write again. M4-D50 sends the user who edited their skill to `install-skill --dir <dir>`, "which keeps a backup", and the doctor refuses to overwrite an edited skill for exactly that reason. fsx's own verbatim backup exists only in transaction sessions, which M4-D8 rejects here. So the command keeps a copy only when the file is not pristine, as `SKILL.md.bak` in the same folder: Claude Code loads only `SKILL.md`, F10 reads only `SKILL.md`, and `export --write`'s `addons.toml.bak` is the house precedent. The fact is shown in the human output and documented in README; it is not added to `data`, to keep §7.3's shape exact (if review prefers machine-readable evidence, `data.backup` as in `export --write` is the additive way, recorded in the close comment).

### 7. The history line and the projection (part 1)

- **`TxKind::Skill`** (wire `"skill"`), a settings kind: `is_setting()` includes it, so `is_undoable()` is false. `undo` never reverts a skill line and steps over it, `undo <its tx>` is `not_found` (as for every settings line), and the projection never counts it as a run to undo.
- **`SettingEntry.dir: Option<PathBuf>`**, `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`, last in the struct, with a doc comment "The skill folder a `skill` line installed into; absent on every other kind." Existing lines serialize byte-identically.
- The line, as `history.jsonl` holds it:

  ```json
  {"schema_version":"1.0","tx":"01M9…","kind":"skill","at":"2026-10-24T18:02:11.123Z","target":null,"actor":"agent","reason":"user asked for the skill","argv":["omaddons","robot-docs","install-skill","--reason","user asked for the skill"],"ops":[],"result":"committed","run":"01M9…","dir":"$HOME/.claude/skills/omaddons"}
  ```

  Built as `SettingEntry { dir: Some(dir), ..SettingEntry::now(TxKind::Skill, None, ctx.actor, ctx.reason.clone(), ctx.argv.clone()) }` and written with `history::record_setting(&mut s, &paths, &entry)` in the install's session, under the lock; a returned `history_not_recorded` warning goes to `ctx.notes.warn`, as `app::record_setting` does. One line per write (`fresh` or `replaced`); none for `unchanged` or `--dry-run`.
- **`history --json`**: `HistoryLine` gains `dir: Option<PathBuf>`, `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`, filled by `setting_line` from the entry, with the doc comment "The skill folder, on `skill` lines only" (A3's rule-2 check reads a property's own description to accept an omittable key). Decided while writing this bead: `dir` follows the kind-specific pattern of `backup` and `dismissed` (omitted on other kinds), because `"dir": null` on every history entry would change every history envelope and cost tokens on every line (§8.1 default 2). If A3's rule test does not accept the documented omission, make the key always present and `null`, never an allowlist line. `target` is `null` (a skill line is about no client), so `history -t <id>` never shows it. The human table shows what was run, as for every settings line.
- **`history_tail.skill_dirs`** (M4-D50), on `HistoryTail`: `skill_dirs: Option<Vec<PathBuf>>`, `#[serde(default)]`, the folders `skill` lines name, newest first, each once, at most `SKILL_DIRS_MAX`.
  - **Following an append** (`follow`): a `skill` line with a `dir` moves that folder to the front (removing an earlier occurrence) and truncates the list to `SKILL_DIRS_MAX`. `trim` never touches it, so a folder stays listed however many runs later its line is dropped from `lines`.
  - **A rebuild** (`from_text`): one backward pass over every complete line of the whole history, before trimming, keeping the first `SKILL_DIRS_MAX` distinct folders. A line is a skill line when a substring check finds `"kind":"skill"` and it then deserializes `{kind, dir}` (salvaged like `line_facts`: the part from the last line start, for a line an older build merged). The follow rule and the rebuild agree by construction: both compute "the `SKILL_DIRS_MAX` most recently installed distinct folders" (a unit test holds them equal).
  - **`None` means "written by a build that does not track skill folders"**: an M3 build that rewrites the projection drops the unknown key. `rebuild_if_stale` treats `skill_dirs: None` as stale and rebuilds, so the next mutating command restores the list; `follow` leaves `None` as it is. This build always writes `Some` (an empty array when there are none). Readers (F10, E5's recovery) treat `None` as "only `Paths::skill_dir()` is known". Decided while writing this bead: the kind stays `history_tail` 1.0 (a minor bump would make the M3 build treat the projection as missing and lose its `status --cached` answer), and `Option` makes the older writer's loss visible instead of silent.
- **`SKILL_DIRS_MAX` = 8** in `src/limits.rs` (§7.9), "skill directories `history_tail.skill_dirs[]` keeps and the drift check follows", with its `REGISTRY` row (`LimitValue::Count(8)`, unit `count`, not configurable) and `LIMIT_NAMES` entry; the `limit_registries` snapshot is re-accepted after reviewing its diff. E5 uses the same constant for `ScopeTable::with_skill_dirs`; whichever of this bead and E5 lands first adds it, and the second reuses it.

- `src/fsx/scope.rs` (part 2): `the_history_row_admits_the_skill_writer`, `a_chosen_skill_dir_replaces_the_slot_for_skill_and_doctor_only`, `skill_dirs_inside_clients_prefixes_or_own_dirs_are_refused` (table), `a_missing_create_from_is_not_found`, `only_folders_between_the_anchor_and_the_skill_dir_are_creatable`, `a_symlinked_skill_dir_is_judged_where_it_points`.
- `src/contract/guide/stamp.rs` (part 3): `the_rendered_guide_is_stamped_and_current`, `an_edited_guide_is_not_pristine`, `another_guide_with_its_own_stamp_is_pristine`, `malformed_stamps_are_unstamped` (table), `read_skill_file_classifies_every_kind` (table), `read_skill_file_never_reads_past_the_bound`.
- `src/app/install_skill.rs` (part 4): `decide_covers_every_existing_state` (table), `resolve_covers_default_and_custom_dirs` (table), `hints_cover_every_root_state` (table), `data_serializes_in_order_with_closed_written_values`, `human_output_for_each_outcome` (table).

### Integration and end-to-end tests

- **Contract matrix** (part 4): `tests/contract/matrix.rs::robot_docs_install_skill`, the five rows of §10 item 5, each through `support::check` (A3's live validation of `data`, `error`, `details`, `commands[]` and stderr events) and an insta snapshot with the tempdir redacted.
- **End to end** (part 5), `tests/robot_docs.rs`, every scenario a `TestLog` scenario on a fresh `TestEnv` (or `common::home::Home` where a client or a Wine prefix is needed), with the helpers of `tests/common/skill.rs`:
  1. `install_skill_default_writes_the_guide_and_a_second_run_writes_nothing`
  2. `install_skill_creates_skills_under_an_existing_claude_dir`
  3. `install_skill_without_claude_dir_is_not_found_and_offers_other_roots`
  4. `install_skill_refuses_dirs_inside_clients_prefixes_and_its_own_dirs`
  5. `install_skill_refuses_a_symlinked_skill_md_and_leaves_it_untouched`
  6. `install_skill_records_a_skill_line_that_undo_steps_over`
  7. `install_skill_keeps_skill_dirs_newest_first_and_bounded`
  8. `install_skill_dry_run_writes_nothing_and_takes_no_lock`
  9. `install_skill_replaces_an_outdated_guide_and_keeps_an_edited_copy`
  10. `install_skill_offers_other_agent_roots_without_writing_there`
  11. `install_skill_waits_for_the_global_lock_and_times_out_as_locked`
  12. `install_skill_failures_leave_a_consistent_skill` (failpoints `fsx.write_atomic.before@1=error`, `fsx.append_durable.before=error`, `fsx.write_atomic.before@1=abort`)
  13. `install_skill_refuses_if_match`
  14. `install_skill_bytes_do_not_depend_on_config`
  15. `status_never_recommends_install_skill`
  16. `install_skill_human_output` (insta snapshots)
  Part 5's body gives each scenario's steps and assertions.

### Logging

- Every end-to-end scenario uses T1's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs) `TestLog` (`let log = tlog!();`): one `log.step(…)` per phase (seed, run, check), every command through `log.run(&env, &argv)` (argv, env overrides, exit, envelope, stderr events, `net.log` lines, failpoints), `log.tree(…)`/`log.assert_unchanged(…)` over `HOME`, the skill folder, `<config>`, `<state>` and `<cache>`, and `log.json(…)` for the history lines and `skill_dirs` it compares. A failure prints `test log: <path>` and the last 20 steps. `tests/robot_docs.rs` carries T1's end-to-end marker (`//! e2e suite: …`) so `argc e2e robot_docs` runs it with verbose logs.
- Unit tests are table-driven, one name per case; every assertion message names the case and shows the input and the output.
- The real-machine test logs evidence with `real_machine.rs`'s `note(label, &value)` (the home path printed as `<home>`), since `TestLog` refuses roots outside test directories by design.

### Checkpoint-only test

`tests/real_machine.rs::install_skill_round_trip` (part 5), `#[ignore = "real machine: OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE=1"]`, run by H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the M4 checkpoint) with `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE=1 OMADDONS_LIVE=1 OMADDONS_ALLOW_SKIP=keyless_installs_forever cargo test --test real_machine -- --ignored --test-threads=1`, and alone with `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE=1 cargo test --test real_machine install_skill_round_trip -- --ignored --test-threads=1`. Without `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE=1` it prints `SKIP install_skill_round_trip: OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE is not 1` and fails unless `OMADDONS_ALLOW_SKIP` names it; its skip is not pre-accepted at the checkpoint (§3.2), so H6 must see it run.

## Considerations

- **Not a design-gate leaf** (common rule 14 lists D1, D2, D5, D8, E5, E7, E8, E11, E14 and G3): it adds no journal shape, recovery rule, binding rule or durability rule. Its write is one atomic fsx `WriteFile`, preceded at most by one rename of an edited copy, and part 5 still crashes and fails it at each of those operations.
- **Size M, five parts.** The command itself is small; the parts that make it safe (a scope that refuses, a reader that never follows a symlink or reads unboundedly, a projection that never loses a folder) are each testable alone and touch three different hot spots, so they land first and in parallel.
- **No §11.4 risk names this leaf.** The nearest: #13 (the guide drifts from behaviour; B2 and B4 own it: this bead only writes the bytes and proves they are the guide's) and #21 (fences scoped wrong; E14's cases include a skill file: once E14 lands, a stuck repair of a skill fences `install-skill` into that folder through the scope table, which is why this bead builds its table with `ScopeTable::new` and E14's fences apply centrally). Risks this bead carries itself, and their watch:
  - writing into another agent's folder unasked: only hints and `alternatives`, never a default, never a `fix_argv`; scenario 10 hashes those roots;
  - losing a hand-edited skill: `SKILL.md.bak` (scenario 9);
  - writing through a dotfiles symlink: refused before the lock and again by fsx (scenario 5);
  - losing a custom folder from `skill_dirs[]`: kept beside `lines`, `None` triggers a rebuild (scenario 7, part 1's unit tests);
  - a `skill_dirs[]` filled by throwaway folders: the real-machine test reuses one fixed scratch path, so checkpoint runs occupy one slot.
- **Hot spots** (§10.5) and their rules: `src/app/mod.rs` (A1 first; each command leaf adds its rows and rebases); `src/fsx/scope.rs` ("E13 first, G3 last"; E3, D4 and B3 touch separate functions; E5 turns the skill slot into a list, so keep the slot and the anchor in one place); `src/state/history.rs` and `history_tail.rs` ("E12 → E5 → E7"; D5, D9 and B3 are additive and rebase); `src/limits.rs` (append rows, re-accept the snapshot in the same commit); `src/error/specs.rs` (A9, A3 first; later leaves append their keys); `omarchy/Model.js` (command leaves add only `CLI_PATHS` rows); `tests/contract/matrix.rs` (append rows, one snapshot file per row); `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` (regenerate after rebasing, never merge by hand); `README.md` (own sections only).
- **Discovery, decided while writing this bead.** M4-D8 says bare help's discovery line and the guide name `robot-docs install-skill`, while §6.6 (A6, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.6`) gives that line as `capabilities --json · robot-docs guide · doctor --json`. This bead adds no recommendation anywhere and does not touch bare help; `help robot-docs` lists the subcommand once it exists, B2 names it in the guide, and README names it in Installation. A6's line stays A6's.
- **Compatibility with older builds.** The M3 build does not know `TxKind` `skill`: it reads a skill line as an unreadable history line (`history_lines_skipped`, and its undo conflict analysis treats an unreadable line as possibly touching anything, M3-D28 rule 5), exactly as it reads M4's other new lines. It drops `skill_dirs` when it rewrites the projection, which this build detects (`None`) and repairs. E9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9`, the M3 build against M4 state) characterizes both; README's Limitations quote its result.
- **What could go wrong in implementation, and how to notice:** re-implementing B1's stamp digest (part 3's unit test against `EXPECTED_DIGEST` fails); a `skill_dirs` follow rule that disagrees with the rebuild (part 1's equality tests); reading a symlinked `SKILL.md`'s target to compare bytes (scenario 5's identical-copy case must still refuse); forgetting that `--dir`'s parent must exist (scenario 4); taking the lock on a dry run (scenario 8 runs it while the lock is held).
- **Privacy.** The command reads and writes nothing under any `WTF/`. Paths of the user's home appear in output and history, as `config path` and `backup export` already show them. Scenarios built on `Home` (whose clients hold `WTF/`) run with `--progress json` and `assert_private_all(stdout, stderr)`.
- **Performance.** One render of the guide, a few `stat`s and at most `1 + OTHER_SKILL_ROOTS.len()` bounded reads of small files; the lock is held for one file write and one history append.
- **A possible follow-up, not this bead:** agents may guess `omaddons install-skill` at the top level; today's sweep gives `omaddons help`. If the corpus shows it matters, file a bead `discovered-from` this one for a usage synonym (C's area).

## Dependencies

Parent: the B area epic `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2` (the guide and the skill).

**Blocked by:**
- B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`, the guide renderer and `robot-docs guide`): `install-skill` writes exactly what B1's renderer produces, uses B1's stamp function and `EXPECTED_DIGEST`, extends the `robot-docs` tree B1 completes, and must regenerate the `SKILL.md` B1 committed. Through B1's blockers this bead also builds on A1, A2, A3, A5 and A9 (§Background), none of them a direct edge.

Parts 4 and 5 also wait for T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs and `argc e2e`), by edges on those subtasks added at filing: part 4 writes the contract matrix rows, and part 5's end-to-end scenarios use `TestLog`.

**Unblocks:**
- B4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.4`, the recipes run end to end): the recipes are proven against the guide an agent actually reads; B4 waits until the installed skill exists and is shown to be that guide byte for byte, and reuses `tests/common/skill.rs`.
- F10 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.10`, skill drift): its `cached`-tier detector reads `history_tail.skill_dirs[]` (at most `SKILL_DIRS_MAX` folders), classifies each file with `read_skill_file` and `inspect`, and names `omaddons robot-docs install-skill --dir <dir>` as the manual remediation for an edited skill, which keeps the edited copy.
- T2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.2`, slice 1 end to end, an edge added at filing): its demo item "`install-skill` into a throwaway `HOME`" calls this bead's helpers and command.

**Delivery slice:** `slice-1`, "Self-describing" (A1–A5, A7–A10, B1, B3, C1–C4). Its exit demo, recorded by T2: `capabilities --json` round-trips; `robot-docs schema` validates the whole matrix and every envelope snapshot; the manifest's report prints; `robot-docs guide` equals `SKILL.md`, frontmatter first; `install-skill` into a throwaway `HOME`; `omaddons retail update` suggests `update -t retail`; `remove dbm retail` changes nothing; the corpus runs; `completions bash` passes `bash -n`. It pre-checks criteria 1, 2, 3 (part), 5 and 15.

**Related, not edges:** E5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`, the repair transaction: `ScopeTable::with_skill_dirs`, the shared `SKILL_DIRS_MAX` and `skill_dir` reason, recovery admitting only folders `skill_dirs[]` names); E14 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14`, fences: its skill-file case includes `install-skill` once both are on `main`); C4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4`, the corpus rows, common rule 18); A6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.6`, bare help's discovery line); B2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.2`, the guide's prose names this command); E9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9`, older builds against skill lines); H4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`, the README final pass checks Installation and Files and state); H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, runs the real-machine test).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] With `$HOME/.claude` present, `omaddons robot-docs install-skill --json` exits 0 with `written: "fresh"`, and `<skills>/SKILL.md` is byte-identical to `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` and to `robot-docs guide --json`'s `data.content`, mode `0644`; a second run exits 0 with `written: "unchanged"`, leaves the file's bytes, inode and mtime unchanged, and appends no history line.
- [ ] A home with `$HOME/.claude` but no `$HOME/.claude/skills` installs, creating `skills/` and `skills/omaddons/`; a home without `$HOME/.claude` gives `not_found` (exit 3) with `details.path` = `$HOME/.claude`, an `alternatives` entry for each existing other skill root, and nothing written anywhere.
- [ ] A `--dir` inside a registered client dir, inside a Wine prefix, or inside `<config>`, `<state>` or `<cache>` is `scope_denied` (exit 4) with `details.reason: "skill_dir"` and `details.path`, and creates nothing; a `--dir` whose parent is missing is `not_found` with `details.path`; a `--dir` that is a file, names no folder, or is not UTF-8 is `usage`.
- [ ] A symlinked `SKILL.md` (to a file with other bytes, to an identical copy, or dangling) is `scope_denied` with `details.reason: "symlink"`, `details.path` and `details.link_target`, and the link and its target are untouched.
- [ ] Each write records one `history.jsonl` line of kind `skill` with `dir`, `target: null`, the actor, reason and argv; `history --json` shows it with `entries[].dir`; bare `undo` steps over it (it reverts the transaction before it), and `undo <its tx>` is `not_found`.
- [ ] `history_tail.skill_dirs[]` names the installed folder, newest first, each once, at most `SKILL_DIRS_MAX` (8) entries; a reinstall moves a folder to the front; it survives its line being trimmed from the projection's `lines`; a rebuild from the whole history gives the same list; a projection without the key is rebuilt by the next mutating command.
- [ ] `--dry-run` writes nothing (the trees of `HOME`, `<config>`, `<state>` and `<cache>` hash identical before and after), appends no history line, takes no global lock, and reports the `written` the run would produce.
- [ ] Replacing a file whose bytes do not match its own stamp (edited, unstamped or larger than 1 MiB) keeps it as `SKILL.md.bak` with its exact bytes; replacing a pristine guide of another digest keeps no `.bak`.
- [ ] `commands[]` offers `install-skill --dir <root>/omaddons` (action `install_skill`, not destructive) for each existing `$HOME/.codex/skills` and `$HOME/.agents/skills`, omits a root that already holds these bytes or was just written, and nothing under those roots changes; `status` never offers `install_skill`.
- [ ] `SKILL_DIRS_MAX` (8) has its `limits::REGISTRY` row and `LIMIT_NAMES` entry, and the `limit_registries` snapshot was re-accepted after review.
- [ ] Every DEC-1 touch point is in part 4's commit: the clap variant, the `COMMANDS` row (`exits` 0–5, `stores_plan: false`, `network: None`), the `command_name` and dispatch arms, `help robot-docs`, the five contract matrix rows with snapshots (which A3's live validation passes), the `CLI_PATHS` row, README; `Action::InstallSkill` and the feature word `agent_skill` are registered.
- [ ] `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` was regenerated with `OMADDONS_UPDATE_SKILL=1 cargo test --test skill` and `tests/skill.rs` passes.
- [ ] `tests/real_machine.rs::install_skill_round_trip` exists (ignored, gated by `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE`), and passes on the development machine: the dry run against the real `HOME` resolves `<skills>` (or is `not_found` when `$HOME/.claude` is absent) and writes nothing; the install into a scratch folder outside every real skill root is byte-identical to the guide; the second run is `unchanged`.
- [ ] README's `robot-docs install-skill`, `history`, Files and state, Uninstall and Installation sections, and the `commands` row of Fields, describe exactly what shipped, in the commit that shipped it.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes for every subtask's commit, `ubs` is clean on the changed files, and `br lint` is clean for this bead and its subtasks.
- [ ] The close comment lists every new or changed wire name (the command path, `data` keys, `written` values, `entries[].dir`, `TxKind` `skill`, the action `install_skill`, the feature word `agent_skill`, the `details` keys and reason values, `history_tail.skill_dirs`, the constant, the files `<skills>/SKILL.md` and `SKILL.md.bak`), states that the command neither stores a plan nor binds (common rule 16, citing M4-D22), and confirms or adjusts each "Decided while writing this bead" item.
