title: The `robot-docs install-skill` command
description:
Part 4 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3 (`robot-docs install-skill`). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

B3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3`) puts the agent guide where coding agents load skills. B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`, the guide renderer and `robot-docs guide`) renders the guide, a Markdown document that opens with YAML frontmatter (`name: omaddons`, `description: …`, the text Claude Code uses to decide when to load it) and whose next line is the stamp `<!-- omaddons guide sha256:<hex> -->` (M4-D7). Claude Code loads every `SKILL.md` under `$HOME/.claude/skills/<name>/`, so after `omaddons robot-docs install-skill` a Claude Code session on the machine starts with omaddons' core loop, safety model and recipes. It serves G-M4-1 (self-describing), G-M4-6 (every write through fsx, dry runs write nothing, the lock held only for the write), checkpoint criterion 3 ("`install-skill` writes the same bytes to `<skills>/SKILL.md`, and a second run writes nothing") and vision G4 ("the skill is installed where agents look").

**This part** is the command itself: the argument handling, the ordered flow (everything that can refuse runs before the lock and writes nothing), the write, the history line, the hints for other agents, the data and human output, the errors, and, in the same commit, every DEC-1 registry touch point, the contract matrix rows, README and the regenerated `SKILL.md`. DEC-1 ("no stubs") requires those to land with the command, so they are not split. It builds on part 1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3.1`: `TxKind::Skill`, `SettingEntry.dir`, `skill_dirs[]`, `SKILL_DIRS_MAX`), part 2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3.2`: `ScopeTable::with_skill_dir` and the History row) and part 3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3.3`: `read_skill_file` and `inspect`).

**The decisions this part implements**, restated:
- **M4-D8:** `omaddons robot-docs install-skill [--dir <DIR>]` writes `<DIR>/SKILL.md` (default `<skills>` = `$HOME/.claude/skills/omaddons`) through fsx as `Writer::Skill`. The default creates `skills/` and `skills/omaddons/` when `$HOME/.claude` exists, and is `not_found` naming the path without it, with the alternatives `--dir <d>` for each other skill root that exists. A custom `--dir` is created if its parent exists; a missing parent is `not_found` with the path. A custom `--dir` inside a client dir, a Wine prefix, `<config>`, `<state>` or `<cache>` is `scope_denied` (`details.reason: "skill_dir"`). A symlinked `SKILL.md` is never written through: `scope_denied`, `details.reason: "symlink"`, the link's target, and prose advice to install with `--dir` into the real directory or to replace the link. Unchanged bytes (the whole file compared) write nothing (`written: "unchanged"`); otherwise `written: "fresh" | "replaced"`. The write takes the global lock, as `config set` and `auth` do. Each write appends a settings history line of kind `skill` with `dir`, which undo never reverts; it is not a transaction. `commands[]` offers `install-skill --dir <d>/omaddons` for each other agent skill root that exists (`$HOME/.codex/skills`, `$HOME/.agents/skills`), never writing there unasked. Nothing recommends installing the skill unasked; `status` stays about the clients. There is no remove command: deleting the folder is the removal, and README says so. Rejected: writing every known root by default; a transaction with undo (the skill is derived); a symlink to a repository file.
- **M4-D7:** `install-skill` writes the same bytes as the guide and the committed `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md`; it never re-stamps or post-processes them (stamping at install time was rejected: it breaks byte identity, which drift detection uses).
- **M4-D50:** an edited skill's manual remediation is "`omaddons robot-docs install-skill --dir <dir>`, which keeps a backup".
- **M4-D22:** `robot-docs install-skill` neither stores a plan nor binds (`--if-match` is refused by the existing check).
- **M4-D11:** `Action::InstallSkill` (`install_skill`) is one of M4's five new recommendation actions.
- **§6.3.3:** data `{dry_run, dir, file, written: fresh|replaced|unchanged, bytes, tool_version}`; the file is `0644`; `--dry-run` reports what it would write.

**Facts this part relies on** (as of `c0ab5e9`, plus what the blockers add):
- The settings-write pattern, `config set` (`src/app/config.rs:286-361`): no lock under `--dry-run` (`:291-295`); `recover_under` under the lock with its warnings to `ctx.notes` (`:296-305`); an untracked session, `ensure_dir_all`, `WriteFile` with mode `0o644`, then the history line (`:330-340`); `drop(guard)`.
- Building a kind-specific settings entry and recording it: `src/app/errors.rs:310-339` (struct update over `SettingEntry::now`, `history::record_setting`, the warning, `doorbell::ring`); `app::record_setting` (`src/app/mod.rs:53-71`) reports the warning through `ctx.notes.warn` and rings the doorbell.
- `GlobalLock::acquire(paths, command)` waits up to `LOCK_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT` (5 s) and then fails `locked` (exit 5, retryable); `Out::boundary_fix` makes a `locked` error's fix rerun the same argv (`src/app/mod.rs:284-300`).
- `--if-match` on a path outside `BINDING_COMMANDS` is `usage` with the fix `omaddons help <path>` for a mutating one (`src/cli.rs:309-327`).
- `registry::load_registry` gives an empty registry when the file is missing and fails on an unreadable or newer one (`src/state/registry.rs:79-89`, `src/state/store.rs:238-273`).
- `backup export` resolves a relative path against `std::env::current_dir()` (`src/app/backup.rs:2561-2562`).
- `dispatch` (`src/app/mod.rs:331-371`) runs the command and, for a mutating non-dry-run path, `history_tail::rebuild_if_stale` after it; `command_name` (`:195-237`); `COMMANDS` (`:121-165`); the dispatch arms emit through `out.emit` (`:374-587`).
- `CLI_PATHS` (`omarchy/Model.js:130-177`) must list every `COMMANDS` path with its `mutates`, `destructive` and `binds` (`tests/omarchy_widget.rs:25-53`).
- The contract matrix (`tests/contract/matrix.rs`) uses `Scene::new()`, `s.json(args, code)` (checked against the whole contract by `support::check`, which A3 extended with live schema validation) and `insta::assert_json_snapshot!(name, s.stable(&c.envelope))`, which removes `meta` and redacts the tempdir (`tests/contract/main.rs:307-316`, `:366-505`).
- From the blockers: A5's `robot-docs` clap tree and `src/app/robot_docs.rs`; A1's `CommandEntry` fields and row builder (A1 decided rows are built by `entry(name, group, mutates, exits, data, network)` with `data_schema::<O: Outcome>`, every mutating row declares exit 4, and exits are verified by the matrix's exit observation); A2's `contract::actions::Action` (`CommandHint::new(Action, argv)`, destructiveness from `Action::destructive()`; A2 decided M4's five actions land with the leaves that first emit them, a usage scan failing on a variant no production code constructs, and every action documented in README's `commands` row) and `contract::features::FEATURES` (A2 left `agent_skill` to this bead, tied to a `COMMANDS` path by a test); A9's `src/error/specs.rs`; B1's renderer, `EXPECTED_DIGEST` and `tests/skill.rs`.

## Technical Approach

### 1. Arguments and the clap variant

In A5's `src/app/robot_docs.rs`, the action enum gains:

```rust
/// Install the agent guide as a skill (SKILL.md) where coding agents load skills
#[command(after_long_help = INSTALL_SKILL_HELP)]
InstallSkill(crate::app::install_skill::InstallSkillArgs),
```

with `command()` → `"robot-docs install-skill"`. In the new `src/app/install_skill.rs` (`pub mod install_skill` in `src/app/mod.rs`):

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, clap::Args)]
pub struct InstallSkillArgs {
    /// The skill folder to write SKILL.md into (default: $HOME/.claude/skills/omaddons;
    /// created if its parent exists)
    #[arg(long, value_name = "DIR")]
    pub dir: Option<PathBuf>,
}
```

`INSTALL_SKILL_HELP` (examples, then one line):

```text
omaddons robot-docs install-skill                     # for Claude Code
omaddons robot-docs install-skill --dry-run           # what it would write
omaddons robot-docs install-skill --dir $HOME/.codex/skills/omaddons
Remove it by deleting the folder.
```

The help says nothing about the doctor; F10 adds that sentence when its detector exists.

### 2. Resolving the directory

```rust
struct Target { dir: PathBuf, create_from: PathBuf, default: bool }
fn resolve(paths: &Paths, dir: Option<&Path>, cwd: &Path) -> Result<Target>
```

- **No `--dir`:** `dir = paths.skill_dir()`, `create_from = paths.claude_dir()` (add `Paths::claude_dir()` = `<home>/.claude` beside `skill_dir` in `src/state/paths.rs:263-266`, with a unit row in its path test, `paths.rs:640-650`). If `create_from` is not a directory:

  ```rust
  Error::new(
      ErrorCode::NotFound,
      format!("Claude Code's folder {} does not exist, so there is no default place to install the skill", claude.display()),
      Suggestion::text("set up Claude Code first, or choose a skills folder with --dir <dir>"),
  )
  .details(json!({ "path": claude.display().to_string() }))
  ```

  plus one `.alternative(Suggestion::command([...]))` per other existing skill root (§5), in `OTHER_SKILL_ROOTS` order. `fix_argv` is `null`: choosing another agent's folder is the user's decision.
- **`--dir D`:** `D` relative → `cwd.join(D)` (`std::env::current_dir()`, as `backup export` does; an unreadable working directory is `io`). Then, in order, each a `usage` error with a prose fix and no `details`:
  - no file name (empty, `/`, a path ending in `..` or `.`): "--dir names the folder that holds SKILL.md, not <D>";
  - exists and is not a directory: "--dir <D> is not a folder";
  - not valid UTF-8: "--dir <lossy D> is not valid UTF-8; omaddons records the folder in history and JSON".
  `create_from = D.parent()`. Its existence is checked by `with_skill_dir` (part 2): missing → `not_found`, `details.path` = the parent.
- An explicit `--dir $HOME/.claude/skills/omaddons` follows the custom rules (its parent `skills/` must exist).

### 3. The flow (`pub fn run(ctx: &Context, args: &InstallSkillArgs) -> Result<InstallSkillOutcome>`)

1. `let paths = Paths::from_env()?;` `let guide = <B1's renderer>()` (the bytes `robot-docs guide` prints; `bytes = guide.len() as u64`).
2. `let target = resolve(&paths, args.dir.as_deref(), &cwd)?;`
3. **The scope.** `clients` = for a custom `--dir`, every `client_dir` of `registry::load_registry(&paths)?` (an unreadable or newer registry fails the run with the loader's own error: a refusal check that cannot see the clients must not pass, §8.1 default 6); for the default, none (decided while writing this bead: the default is a fixed path under `$HOME/.claude`, and an unrelated broken registry must not block the one obvious command). `let scopes = ScopeTable::new(&paths, &clients, None)?.with_skill_dir(&target.dir, &target.create_from)?;` `let dir = scopes.skill_dir().to_path_buf();` (canonical) `let file = dir.join("SKILL.md");`
4. **What is there.** `let existing = read_skill_file(&file).map_err(|e| Error::io(&file, &e, retry_fix))?;`
   - `Symlink { link_target }`:

     ```rust
     Error::new(
         ErrorCode::ScopeDenied,
         format!("{} is a symlink to {}; omaddons never writes through a symlink", file.display(), link_target.display()),
         Suggestion::text("install into the link's real folder with --dir <dir>, or replace the link with a regular file"),
     )
     .details(json!({ "reason": "symlink", "path": file.display().to_string(), "link_target": link_target.display().to_string() }))
     ```

     Even when the link's target holds exactly these bytes (decided while writing this bead: M4-D8's rule has no exception, and F10 reports such a link the same way).
   - `NotAFile` → `Error::new(ErrorCode::Io, "<file> exists and is not a regular file; move it away, then rerun", …)`.
5. **Decide** (pure, unit-tested):

   ```rust
   #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
   enum Decision { Unchanged, Fresh, Replaced { keep_edited: bool } }
   fn decide(existing: &SkillFile, guide: &[u8]) -> Decision
   ```

   `Bytes(b)` with `b == guide` → `Unchanged`; `Missing` → `Fresh`; `TooLarge` → `Replaced { keep_edited: true }`; `Bytes(b)` otherwise → `Replaced { keep_edited: !inspect(&b).is_pristine() }`. (`Symlink` and `NotAFile` never reach it.)
6. `let commands = hints(&paths, &dir, &guide);` (§5).
7. **`Unchanged`, or `ctx.dry_run`: return the outcome now.** No lock, no recovery, no write, no history line, no doorbell. A dry run's `written` is the decision's (`fresh`, `replaced` or `unchanged`); its human output says "would …" and, for `keep_edited`, "would keep your edited copy as …".
8. **The lock and recovery**, exactly as `config set`:

   ```rust
   let guard = GlobalLock::acquire(&paths, ctx.command)?;
   ctx.notes.warn_all(&recover_under(&guard, &paths, &no_saved_variables, ctx.command, ctx.actor));
   ```

9. **Again under the lock**: steps 4 and 5 on a fresh `read_skill_file`. Another process may have installed the same bytes (→ `Unchanged`: drop the lock, return, no line), put a symlink there (→ `scope_denied`), or edited the file (→ a new `keep_edited`). The decision made under the lock is the one reported.
10. **Write**, `let mut s = WriteSession::untracked(Writer::Skill, &scopes, "SKILL.md");`
    1. `ensure_dir_all(&mut s, &dir)?;` (the default's `skills/` and `skills/omaddons/`, or the `--dir` folder; umask-default permissions).
    2. If `keep_edited`: `mutate(&mut s, &file, Op::Rename { to: &dir.join("SKILL.md.bak"), mode: RenameMode::Replace })?;` (reads nothing, so any size works; replaces an older `.bak`, as `export --write` replaces `addons.toml.bak`).
    3. `mutate(&mut s, &file, Op::WriteFile { content: Content::Bytes(&guide), mode: Some(0o644) })?;` (atomic: temporary file and rename).
    4. The history line:

       ```rust
       let entry = SettingEntry {
           dir: Some(dir.clone()),
           ..SettingEntry::now(TxKind::Skill, None, ctx.actor, ctx.reason.clone(), ctx.argv.clone())
       };
       if let Some(warning) = history::record_setting(&mut s, &paths, &entry) {
           ctx.notes.warn(warning);
       }
       crate::state::doorbell::ring(&paths, ctx.command, ctx.actor);
       ```

11. `drop(s); drop(guard);` and return `written: fresh | replaced`. `dispatch` then rebuilds the projection if it is stale (it is fresh after a followed append).

**Why `keep_edited` keeps a copy** (decided while writing this bead): M4-D8's "the previous file is recoverable by re-running an older build" holds for a pristine file (some guide produced it), so it is replaced without a copy. An edited or unstamped file is the user's work, M4-D50 promises the manual reinstall "keeps a backup", and fsx's own backups exist only in transaction sessions, which M4-D8 rejects for the skill. `SKILL.md.bak` in the same folder is not loaded by Claude Code and not read by F10. It is not added to `data` (§7.3's shape is kept exact); the human output and README say it. If review prefers machine-readable evidence, `data.backup` as `export --write` has it is the additive form; record the choice in the close comment.

### 4. Data and human output

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, JsonSchema)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum Written { Fresh, Replaced, Unchanged }

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, JsonSchema)]
pub struct InstallSkillData {
    pub dry_run: bool,
    /// The skill folder, canonical.
    pub dir: PathBuf,
    /// `<dir>/SKILL.md`.
    pub file: PathBuf,
    /// What the run wrote, or under `--dry-run` would write.
    pub written: Written,
    /// The guide's length.
    pub bytes: u64,
    pub tool_version: &'static str,
}

pub struct InstallSkillOutcome { data: InstallSkillData, commands: Vec<CommandHint>, kept_edited: bool }
```

`impl Outcome for InstallSkillOutcome` (`command()` = `"robot-docs install-skill"`, `data()`, `commands()`, `render_human`). Field order is rendering order (DEC-3; not contract, M4-D56).

```json
{"ok":true,"schema_version":"1.0","tool_version":"0.1.0","command":"robot-docs install-skill","exit_code":0,
 "data":{"dry_run":false,"dir":"$HOME/.claude/skills/omaddons","file":"$HOME/.claude/skills/omaddons/SKILL.md",
         "written":"fresh","bytes":18432,"tool_version":"0.1.0"},
 "warnings":[],
 "commands":[{"action":"install_skill","command":"omaddons robot-docs install-skill --dir $HOME/.codex/skills/omaddons",
              "argv":["omaddons","robot-docs","install-skill","--dir","$HOME/.codex/skills/omaddons"],"destructive":false}],
 "meta":{"elapsed_ms":4,"offline":false}}
```

(`$HOME` is the real absolute path in actual output.) Human output, one line per outcome (byte counts with the house thousands separator, `crate::output` helpers):

```text
installed the omaddons skill: <file> (18,432 bytes)
updated the omaddons skill: <file> (18,432 bytes)
  your edited copy is kept as <file>.bak
the omaddons skill is up to date: <file>
would install the omaddons skill: <file> (18,432 bytes)
would update the omaddons skill: <file> (18,432 bytes)
  would keep your edited copy as <file>.bak
other agents: omaddons robot-docs install-skill --dir <root>/omaddons
```

The wording was decided while writing this bead; the `other agents:` line appears once per hint.

### 5. `commands[]` hints

- `pub const OTHER_SKILL_ROOTS: &[&str] = &[".codex/skills", ".agents/skills"];` in `src/contract/guide/render.rs` (M4-D8's fixed list, relative to `$HOME`).
- `fn hints(paths: &Paths, written: &Path, guide: &[u8]) -> Vec<CommandHint>`: for each root in order, when `home/<root>` is a directory, and `home/<root>/omaddons` is not the folder this run wrote or checked (canonical comparison), and `read_skill_file(home/<root>/omaddons/SKILL.md)` is not `Bytes(guide)`: `CommandHint::new(Action::InstallSkill, ["omaddons", "robot-docs", "install-skill", "--dir", "<home>/<root>/omaddons"])`. Decided while writing this bead: a root that already holds these bytes gets no hint (it would change nothing).
- The same argv are the default `not_found`'s `alternatives` (as `Suggestion::command`).
- `Action::InstallSkill` in A2's `src/contract/actions.rs`: wire `install_skill`, description "Install the omaddons skill into another agent's skill folder", `destructive()` false; README's `commands` row in "Fields" lists it.
- `status` is untouched: it never offers `install_skill`.

### 6. Errors, details and their specs

| Code | Exit | Raised by | `details` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `not_found` | 3 | §2 (no `$HOME/.claude`), part 2 (missing `--dir` parent) | `path` |
| `scope_denied` | 4 | part 2 (`skill_dir`), §3 step 4 (`symlink`), fsx's backstop | `reason`, `path`, `link_target` (`symlink` only) |
| `usage` | 2 | §2's `--dir` checks; `--if-match`; clap | none new |
| `locked` | 5 | `GlobalLock::acquire` | as today |
| `io` | 1 | `NotAFile`; a failed read or write | as today |
| `state_corrupt`, `state_too_new` | as registered | `load_registry` (custom `--dir` only) | as the loader gives |

- In `src/error/specs.rs` (A9's): `scope_denied`'s `reason` enum gains `symlink`, and the optional key `link_target` (string). Part 2 added `skill_dir`, `path` and `not_found`'s `path`.
- No new error or warning code. `history_not_recorded` (existing) when the line cannot be written; recovery's warnings from `recover_under`.

### 7. Registry touch points (DEC-1, this commit)

1. The clap variant (§1) and its `command()` arm.
2. `COMMANDS` row: `entry("robot-docs install-skill", Group::Setup, true, &[0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5], data_schema::<InstallSkillOutcome>, Network::None)` with `dictionary: General` and `stores_plan: false` (A1's builder), placed after A5's and B1's `robot-docs` rows. Exits: 0 success; 1 `io`, `internal`; 2 `usage`; 3 `not_found`; 4 `scope_denied` (and `state_too_new`); 5 `locked`. Never 6.
3. `canonical_path` / `command_name` arm and the `dispatch` arm: `out.emit(install_skill::run(ctx, args))`.
4. Help: `help robot-docs` lists `install-skill`; `help robot-docs install-skill` and `robot-docs install-skill --help` work. Re-accept any `help robot-docs` snapshot A5 or B1 added. Bare help is unchanged (nested commands are not on the group lines); `tests/cli_skeleton.rs` passes unchanged unless A5 or B1 added a literal listing `robot-docs`'s subcommands, which is then extended.
5. Contract matrix rows, `tests/contract/matrix.rs::robot_docs_install_skill`, each `s.json(…)` then a snapshot:
   - `robot_docs_install_skill_ok`: `fs::create_dir_all(home/.claude)`, then `robot-docs install-skill` (0);
   - `robot_docs_install_skill_dry_run`: a fresh scene with `home/.claude`, `robot-docs install-skill --dry-run` (0, `written: "fresh"`);
   - `robot_docs_install_skill_not_found`: no `home/.claude` (3);
   - `robot_docs_install_skill_scope_denied`: `--dir <state>/omaddons/skill` (4, `reason: "skill_dir"`);
   - `robot_docs_install_skill_symlink`: `home/.claude/skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` a symlink to a file in `home/dotfiles/` (4, `reason: "symlink"`).
   Each envelope passes `support::check`, which validates `data` against the row's schema, `error` and its `details` against the code's variant, and `commands[]` against `CommandHint`.
6. `special.rs`: no row (the path mutates).
7. `cli_skeleton` literals: item 4.
8. `CLI_PATHS` row: `"robot-docs install-skill": { "mutates": true, "destructive": false, "binds": false }` in `omarchy/Model.js` (the widget pipeline then runs in the gate).
9. README (§8).

Also in this commit:
- the feature word `agent_skill` in `contract::features::FEATURES`, tied by A2's test to the path `robot-docs install-skill`;
- `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` regenerated with `OMADDONS_UPDATE_SKILL=1 cargo test --test skill` (the `{{commands}}` block gains the row), never by hand or by a shell redirect (common rule 17);
- if C4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4`, the run-the-fix corpus) has landed, two rows in `tests/contract/intent_corpus.rs` (common rule 18): `omaddons robot-docs install-skil` → `usage` → `omaddons help robot-docs install-skill` (fix exit 0; a guessed mutating verb becomes `help`), and `omaddons robot-docs install-skill --dry-rn` → `usage` → `omaddons robot-docs install-skill --dry-run` (fix exit 3 on `intent_home()`, which has no `$HOME/.claude`; if the typo sweep demotes the fix to `help`, the row records the fix it gives and the close comment says so). If C4 has not landed, C4 adds them.
- If the current golden `tests/contract/manifest.json` exists (H2 commits it later), regenerate it with `OMADDONS_UPDATE_WIRE_NAMES=1` and review the diff.

### 8. README (this commit)

- `#### robot-docs install-skill` under A5's `### robot-docs`: what it writes and where (the default, `--dir`, and that only the default creates `skills/`); byte identity with `omaddons robot-docs guide` and the stamp line; `written` (`fresh`, `replaced`, `unchanged`) and `bytes`; `--dry-run`; the refusals (client dirs, Wine prefixes, omaddons' own folders; a symlinked `SKILL.md`, with the advice); `SKILL.md.bak` for an edited copy; the other-agents hints and that it never writes there unasked; the history line; no remove command (delete the folder); a new Claude Code session picks it up.
- `### history`: the `skill` kind with `dir` in JSON; `undo` steps over it; `undo <tx>` of one is `not_found`.
- `## Files and state`: a row for `<skills>/SKILL.md` (written as README writes the other home paths) and other `--dir` folders, with `SKILL.md.bak`, safe to delete; the `history.jsonl` row's settings kinds gain `skill`; the `history_tail.json` row mentions `skill_dirs`.
- `### Uninstall`: delete the skill folder.
- `## Installation`: one line, "For Claude Code: `omaddons robot-docs install-skill`".
- "Fields", the `commands` row: `install_skill`.

### What not to do

- Never write under `OTHER_SKILL_ROOTS` unless the user runs that argv; never put an other-root argv in `fix_argv`.
- Never read through a symlinked `SKILL.md` to compare bytes; never re-stamp the guide.
- Never take the lock, recover, or write under `--dry-run` or for `unchanged`.
- No `print!`/`eprint!` (the outcome renders); no `unwrap`/`expect` outside tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `omaddons robot-docs install-skill` installs the guide's exact bytes into `<skills>/SKILL.md` (mode `0644`) when `$HOME/.claude` exists, creating `skills/` and `skills/omaddons/`, and returns `written: "fresh"` with `bytes` equal to the guide's length; a second run returns `written: "unchanged"` and writes nothing.
- [ ] Without `$HOME/.claude` it is `not_found` (exit 3) with `details.path`, a prose fix, `fix_argv: null`, and one `alternatives` entry per existing `$HOME/.codex/skills` or `$HOME/.agents/skills`.
- [ ] `--dir` resolves relative paths against the working directory; refuses with `usage` a `--dir` that names no folder, is not a folder, or is not UTF-8; and passes the rest to part 2's refusals.
- [ ] A symlinked `SKILL.md` is `scope_denied` with `details {reason: "symlink", path, link_target}` before the lock, and again under it; nothing is written.
- [ ] `--dry-run` and an unchanged run take no lock, run no recovery, write nothing and append no line; a real `fresh` or `replaced` run takes the lock, runs `recover_under`, re-reads and re-decides under it, writes, and appends one `skill` line with `dir`, then rings the doorbell.
- [ ] A replaced file that is not pristine (edited, unstamped, or larger than 1 MiB) is first renamed to `SKILL.md.bak`; a pristine one is replaced without a copy.
- [ ] `commands[]` holds one `install_skill` hint per existing other root that was not just written and does not already hold these bytes; `Action::InstallSkill` is registered and documented in README's `commands` row; `status` never offers it.
- [ ] All DEC-1 touch points are in this commit: the clap variant, the `COMMANDS` row (`exits` `[0,1,2,3,4,5]`, `stores_plan: false`, `network: None`), the `command_name` and dispatch arms, `help robot-docs`, the five contract matrix rows with snapshots (each passing `support::check`'s live validation), the `CLI_PATHS` row, and README; A1's exit observation sees only declared exits.
- [ ] `agent_skill` is in `FEATURES`; `scope_denied`'s `DetailSpec` has `symlink` and `link_target`.
- [ ] `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` was regenerated with `OMADDONS_UPDATE_SKILL=1 cargo test --test skill` and `tests/skill.rs` passes; the corpus rows exist if C4 has landed.
- [ ] README's `robot-docs install-skill`, `history`, Files and state, Uninstall and Installation sections, and the `commands` row of Fields, describe exactly this behaviour.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes (the widget pipeline included, since `omarchy/Model.js` changed); `ubs` is clean on every changed file; `br lint` is clean for this subtask.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

In `src/app/install_skill.rs`:
- `decide_covers_every_existing_state`: table, one name per case: `missing` → `Fresh`; `same_bytes` → `Unchanged`; `pristine_other_guide` (B1's guide with a prose line changed and re-stamped) → `Replaced { keep_edited: false }`; `edited_guide` (one byte changed) → `Replaced { keep_edited: true }`; `unstamped_file` → `Replaced { keep_edited: true }`; `too_large` → `Replaced { keep_edited: true }`; `empty_file` → `Replaced { keep_edited: true }`. Messages print the case and the decision.
- `resolve_covers_default_and_custom_dirs` (tempdir home): `default_with_claude` → `dir` = `skill_dir()`, `create_from` = `claude_dir()`, `default: true`; `default_without_claude` → `not_found` with `details.path` and no alternatives; `default_without_claude_with_codex` → one alternative whose argv parses with `Cli::try_parse_from`; `relative_dir` (`cwd` = `home/work`, `--dir skills/omaddons`) → `home/work/skills/omaddons`; `empty_dir`, `root_dir`, `dotdot_dir` → `usage`; `dir_is_a_file` → `usage`; `non_utf8_dir` (an `OsString` from raw bytes) → `usage`.
- `hints_cover_every_root_state`: table over `.codex/skills` × {absent, present, present with these bytes in `omaddons/SKILL.md`, present with other bytes, the folder just written} and `.agents/skills` present: the expected argv list, in order; every hint's action is `install_skill`, `destructive` false, and its argv parses.
- `data_serializes_in_order_with_closed_written_values`: `InstallSkillData` serializes with keys `dry_run, dir, file, written, bytes, tool_version` in that order; `Written` serializes as `fresh`, `replaced`, `unchanged` and its schema is a closed enum of those three.
- `human_output_for_each_outcome`: table: fresh, replaced without a copy, replaced keeping a copy, unchanged, dry-run fresh, dry-run replaced keeping a copy, with zero and two hints: the exact lines of §4.

In `src/state/paths.rs`: the path table gains `(p.claude_dir(), "/h/.claude")`.

In `src/contract/actions.rs` and `features.rs`: A2's existing completeness tests (every variant constructed by production code, documented in README, every feature word tied to a path) pass with the new entries.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

- **Contract matrix** `tests/contract/matrix.rs::robot_docs_install_skill`: the five rows of §7 item 5, each through `support::check` and an insta snapshot (`s.stable`, tempdir redacted). After the success row, the test also asserts that the installed file equals `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` (read from `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`). Each row runs one command; the second-run (`unchanged`) behaviour and every multi-command scenario are part 5's.
- **Corpus** (if C4 landed): the two rows of §7, run by C4's harness on `intent_home()` copies.
- The full end-to-end suite is part 5's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3.5`).

### Logging

- Unit tests are table-driven; every assertion message names the case and prints the input (paths relative to the tempdir, byte lengths and first lines for file contents) and the output.
- The contract matrix rows use the contract suite's own harness (`Scene`, `support::check`, which prints the envelope and the instance and schema paths of a validation failure). Each row runs one command, so T1's `TestLog` (required for tests that run more than one command) is not needed there; because this part writes integration tests, it is ordered after T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs) by an edge added at filing, like part 5.

## Considerations

- **Hot spots:** `src/app/mod.rs` (A1 first; add the module, the row, the two arms; rebase); `src/app/robot_docs.rs` (A5's and B1's: one variant and one arm); `src/contract/actions.rs`, `features.rs` (A2's: append); `src/contract/guide/render.rs` (B1's: one constant); `src/error/specs.rs` (append keys); `omarchy/Model.js` (one `CLI_PATHS` row); `tests/contract/matrix.rs` (append; one snapshot file per row); `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` (regenerate after rebasing, never merge by hand); `README.md` (own sections).
- **Common rule 16:** the close comment records that the command neither stores a plan nor binds, citing M4-D22: the bytes come from the binary, the destination is the argument, and the one outside input (the existing file) is re-read and re-decided under the lock, with an edited copy kept.
- **Common rule 6:** the close comment lists the wire names: the path `robot-docs install-skill`; `data.{dry_run, dir, file, written, bytes, tool_version}`; `written` values; the action `install_skill`; the feature `agent_skill`; `scope_denied` `details.reason` `symlink` and `details.link_target` (with part 2's `skill_dir`, `path` and `not_found.path`); the files `<skills>/SKILL.md` and `SKILL.md.bak`.
- **What could go wrong:** taking the lock before the checks (a refused run would then wait on another command's lock); reading the link's target to compare (the symlink case must refuse before any read); forgetting the re-check under the lock (two concurrent installs would both append a line); a hint argv carrying a presentation flag (the contract check rejects it).
- **Fences (later):** once E14 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14`, fences) lands, a stuck repair of a skill fences writes to that folder through the scope table, and `install-skill` into it fails with the fencing journal's own stop error; E14's skill-file case covers it.
- **Size M:** a thin command over parts 1–3, but with the full DEC-1 set and README.

## Dependencies

- Parent: B3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3`, `robot-docs install-skill`).
- Before it: part 1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3.1`: the kind, `dir` and the projection field it writes through), part 2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3.2`: the scope it builds and the History row its line needs), part 3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3.3`: the reader and inspector its decision uses). T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`) blocks it too (an edge added at filing, because it writes the contract matrix rows).
- After it: part 5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3.5`, the end-to-end suite and the real-machine test), which drives this command through every scenario.
- Related: A5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5`, the `robot-docs` tree), A1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1`, the row fields), A2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.2`, actions and features), A9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9`, the specs), A3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`, live validation), C4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4`, corpus rows), F10 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.10`, names this command as the edited skill's remediation).

- [ ] `tests/common/skill.rs` provides `committed_guide`, `claude_ready`, `skill_root`, `assert_is_guide`, `restamped_guide`, `skill_dirs` and `skill_lines`, with their self-tests in `tests/common_selftest.rs`.
- [ ] `tests/robot_docs.rs` carries T1's end-to-end marker and the sixteen scenarios of §2 (fifteen `install_skill_*` and `status_never_recommends_install_skill`), each a `TestLog` scenario, all passing in the gate.
- [ ] The scenarios prove: the default install's bytes equal the committed guide and `robot-docs guide`; a second run writes nothing; `skills/` is created under an existing `$HOME/.claude`; no `$HOME/.claude` is `not_found` with runnable alternatives; every refusal of §2.4 and §2.5 changes nothing; the skill line is recorded and stepped over by `undo`; `skill_dirs[]` is newest first, bounded, rebuilt and repaired; `--dry-run` writes nothing and takes no lock; edited copies are kept; hints never write; the lock times out as `locked`; each injected failure leaves a consistent skill; `--if-match` is refused; the bytes do not depend on `config.toml`; `status` never recommends the skill.
- [ ] Scenarios built on `Home` run with `--progress json` and assert privacy over stdout and stderr.

- [ ] `argc e2e robot_docs` runs the suite with verbose logs and prints the log root.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed test files; `br lint` is clean for this subtask.

title: The recipes run end to end
description:
## How to work this bead

This bead is worked through its 4 subtasks, listed below in work order. Claim a subtask, not this bead (`br ready --parent omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.4` lists the ready ones). The agent that closes the last open subtask then verifies every acceptance criterion of this bead (they are the leaf's, not any one subtask's), and closes this bead with `br close omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.4 --reason "done: <evidence> · found: <ids>"`. Until this bead is closed, every bead it blocks stays blocked.

1. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.4.1 The recipe grammar: extraction, fill rules and the eight intents, read from the installed skill: the parser and filler in `tests/common/guide.rs`, their self-tests, and the first gate test of `tests/skill_recipes.rs`.
2. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.4.2 The recorded scenario: recipe homes, the record plan, trimmed fixtures and the recorder: `tests/common/recipes.rs`, `archives::skeleton`, `record_skill_recipes` (ignored), the committed `tests/fixtures/http/skill_recipes/` and the gate's hygiene test.
3. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.4.3 E2E: the eight recipes run end to end: one gate test per recipe, each with its setup, its assertion and a `--progress json` privacy pass, and README's Tests row.
4. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.4.4 Tests: the checkpoint's live re-recording of the recipe fixtures: `tests/live_probes.rs::skill_recipes_record_live_and_match_the_fixtures` and the scenario comparison.

Order: 1, then 2, then 3 and 4 (each after 2; they do not depend on each other).

## Background

M4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`, the agent surface, the doctor and the first tag) makes omaddons describe itself so that an agent that has never seen it works correctly. Its centrepiece for coding agents is the **guide**: one Markdown document printed by `omaddons robot-docs guide`, committed as `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md`, and installed by `omaddons robot-docs install-skill` as the skill a Claude Code session loads. B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`, the guide renderer and `robot-docs guide`) built the renderer and the committed file, B3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3`, `robot-docs install-skill`) the install, and B2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.2`, the guide's content) wrote its prose, including the section **Recipes**: eight fenced command blocks, one per canonical intent of vision §5.10, each with the exit codes it expects and the rule that fills its placeholders.

An agent copies those lines verbatim. Today nothing runs them: B2's test only checks that every command the guide names parses. A recipe can parse and still fail (a flag that does nothing, a placeholder filled from the wrong key, a target the command refuses, a third command an agent must guess), and a wrong recipe in a skill is worse than none, because an agent trusts it. This bead runs every recipe end to end, in the gate, on a synthetic home with recorded HTTP fixtures, and asserts that each one does what its intent says, in at most two commands.

**Why it exists.** The vision's M4 checkpoint says "Canonical intents (§5.10) each complete in ≤ 2 commands; the `SKILL.md` recipes run as e2e tests". The plan's risk 13, "the guide drifts from behaviour" (likelihood low, impact medium), names this bead as an owner beside B2: generated tables, the parse check, byte identity with `SKILL.md`, and the recipes run.

**Milestone goals it serves:**
- **G-M4-1, self-describing:** "an agent with no prior knowledge learns everything it needs from the binary itself … Every fact in those outputs is generated from the code, so it cannot drift from what the code does." The recipes are the one part of the guide that is prose, not generated; running them is how they are held to the code.
- **G-M4-3, what was previewed is what runs:** the `preview-then-apply` recipe is the guide's own statement of the guarantee ("`--dry-run` → `plan_id` → `apply`"); this bead proves that the lines the guide prints commit exactly the previewed items.
- **G-M4-6, no new risk to the engine's guarantees:** "Dry runs still leave `<state>` untouched": asserted here on the recipe's own dry run.
- **Vision G4, agent ergonomics:** "the first command an agent guesses works". An agent that reads the skill does not need to guess: what it copies works.

**Checkpoint criteria it is responsible for** (§3.2; H6, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the checkpoint, records the evidence):
- **4, canonical intents:** "Each of the eight canonical intents (vision §5.10, listed in §6.3.4) takes at most two omaddons commands with JSON output, and each is a recipe in `SKILL.md` that `tests/skill_recipes.rs` runs end to end on a synthetic home with recorded HTTP fixtures." This bead owns it.
- **3, the guide and the skill** (part): "`omaddons robot-docs guide` and `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` are byte-identical … `install-skill` writes the same bytes to `<skills>/SKILL.md`." The recipes are read from a skill installed by `install-skill`, checked byte-identical to the rendered guide first.
- **17, gate and checkpoint runs** (part): "the live probes and the real-machine tests pass with every `SKIP` quoted." This bead adds one live probe, the re-recording of its fixtures (§11.1: "Live probes … the skill-recipes fixtures re-recorded and compared").
- **Slice 4's exit demo** ("the recipes pass") is recorded by H6 after the tag (§10.6, §11.3). This bead never records a slice demo.

**The decisions that shape it** (the full decision log is filed as comments on the milestone epic `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`):
- **M4-D7: the guide, `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` and the installed skill are one artifact.** `robot-docs guide` renders hand-written prose from `src/contract/guide/guide.md` with generated blocks spliced in; the committed file and an installed skill are the same bytes; the guide stays under 500 lines and 32 KiB. *For this bead:* the recipes are extracted from the guide an agent actually reads (an installed skill, checked byte-identical to the rendered guide), never from a copy kept in the test. A recipe corrected by this bead is corrected in `guide.md` and the committed file is regenerated (`OMADDONS_UPDATE_SKILL=1 cargo test --test skill`), never edited by hand. *Rejected there and not to be revived here:* a fully generated guide (unreadable prose) and a fully hand-written one (its tables drift).
- **M4-D8: `install-skill` writes `<skills>/SKILL.md`** (`$HOME/.claude/skills/omaddons`), creating `skills/omaddons/` when `$HOME/.claude` exists. *For this bead:* the structural test installs the skill into a synthetic `HOME` that has `.claude/`, then reads the installed file.
- **M4-D21, M4-D22, M4-D23, M4-D25, M4-D63 (the stored plan, as `preview-then-apply` uses it):** a storable command's `--dry-run` that would change something stores a plan under `<cache>/plans/<plan_id>.json` and returns `data.plan_id`, with `apply` in `commands[]`; `omaddons apply <plan_id>` executes the stored typed intent bound to its token and reports `{plan_id, applied{command, display_argv}, approved, result, outcomes[]}`; every history line `apply` commits carries `plan: <plan_id>` and the plan's `display_argv` as its `argv`; `omaddons plans show <plan_id>` reports the plan `completed` once history records it. The recipe's assertion is stated in those terms.
- **M4-D34 and M4-D40 (the doctor, as `whats-broken` uses it):** doctor JSON puts the report at the top level of the envelope, not under `data`, and the doctor dictionary's exit 1 is `findings_present`, a normal outcome. So a fill rule or an assertion on a doctor envelope addresses `findings…`, not `data.findings…`, and the recipe expects exit 1 from `doctor --robot-triage` on a home with a problem.
- **M4-D47 (context): fixtures are Rust, never shell scripts.** The recipes are shell-looking lines, but the test never runs a shell: it splits each line with `shell_words` and runs the argv, which is also what the guide's own "will never do" list promises (item 6: "Run a shell, or interpret a string as a command: argv only").
- **M4-D55's after-H1 rule:** this bead may land after H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, the pre-freeze contract audit) closes, because it adds no wire shape: only tests, fixtures, and possibly a corrected recipe in the guide's prose. A recipe that needs a new flag is a contract change, which is not this bead's to make (Technical Approach, section 9).
- **Vision §5.10, the canonical intents**, each at most two commands with JSON output: update everything; what is broken (`status`, then `doctor` or `errors`); install X for target Y; add a legacy addon from a git repo; preview, then apply exactly (`--dry-run`, `apply`); undo what the agent did today (`history --actor agent --since 1d`, `undo --last-by agent`); explain pending updates with changelogs; restore a fresh machine (`sync`). The plan's §6.3.4 fixes their ids and commands (section 1 below).

**Facts this bead relies on** (verified at `c0ab5e9`; the leaves that land before it add the rest, listed after):
- Recorded HTTP fixtures live in `tests/fixtures/http/<scenario>/<host>/<method>-<slug>-<hash>.{json,body}`; `common::http::scenario(name)` returns that directory (`tests/common/http.rs:400-405`). Debug builds replay a scenario with `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES=<dir>` and record one with `OMADDONS_RECORD=1` as well (`choose_transport`, `src/net/mod.rs:326-345`); release builds always use the real transport.
- Replay holds one fixture per request key (`METHOD` plus the URL with secret query parameters dropped and the rest sorted); a second fixture for one key, or a file that does not parse, fails the load; a request with no fixture fails with `internal` ("replay: no fixture for <key>") and no socket is opened; a fixture's responses are served in order, the last repeating (`src/net/replay.rs:1-8, 108-195`).
- Record mode forwards each request to the real transport and writes the response through fsx under the debug-only record-fixtures scope (`src/net/record.rs:1-40`, `ScopeTable::add_record_fixtures` at `src/fsx/scope.rs:273`). It stores no request header, drops `set-cookie`, and strips secret query parameters from the URL and from `location` headers. The transport is the innermost layer of `Limited<Retrying<Validating<Redirecting<Guarded<Decoding<transport>>>>>>` (`src/net/mod.rs:316-321`), so it records the wire body, and conditional requests that `Validating` sends from its validator cache (`<cache>/http/`, `src/net/validators.rs:1-6`, `src/state/paths.rs:391-393`) reach it too.
- The house recorders are `#[ignore = "records live fixtures: OMADDONS_RECORD=1"]` tests that return early unless `OMADDONS_RECORD=1`, with a doc comment saying to delete the directory first and review the diff (`tests/catalog.rs:69-90`, `tests/git_github.rs:53-90`). Their Atom feeds are trimmed to the newest entry with the author `contributor` (for example `tests/fixtures/http/git-github/github.com/get-fondlez-GroupBulletinBoard-commits-main.atom-118b95f0.body`).
- The committed fixtures total 2.6 MB. The only release archive among them is GroupBulletinBoard's 280 KB codeload zip (`tests/fixtures/http/git-github/codeload.github.com/`); the catalog scenario records release metadata, not archives.
- GitHub releases found through `releases/latest` and `git:` refs to GitHub carry no expected hash (`src/sources/github.rs:784`, `src/sources/git_github.rs:276`; only the REST path, used for beta and alpha look-backs, carries one, `src/sources/github_rest.rs:503`), and a response's `content-length` is read only to refuse one that is too large (`src/net/guard.rs:149-156`). So a recorded archive reduced to its skeleton (section 3) replays and installs.
- `Home` (`tests/common/home.rs`): `serve_recorded(name)` copies a committed scenario into the home's fixture directory (`:146-149`); `std_command` sets `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES` to that directory and `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT` (`:254-266`); `run` appends `--json` (`:196-200`), so the recipe runner never uses it (a recipe runs verbatim); `seed_memo` and `installed_behind` age the release memo (`:75-80, 95-125`).
- `TestEnv` clears every `OMADDONS_*` variable of the test process from the child and sets `TZ=UTC`, `OMADDONS_FS_CLONE=no` and `OMADDONS_FS_FREE_MB=65536` (`tests/common/env.rs:10-21, 132-146`).
- **The default actor is `agent` when stdin is not a terminal** (`Actor::resolve`, `src/model.rs:330-356`). Test children have no terminal, so every setup command that stands for a person passes `--actor human`.
- `history`'s global `--actor` is read as its actor filter, the same as `--by` (`src/app/history.rs:5-6, 243-290`). `--since 1d` is measured from the wall clock (`:295`), and a commit's history `at` is the wall clock too (`src/engine/tx.rs:1166, 1187`), not `OMADDONS_NOW`; so a test cannot plant an "older" run by freezing time, and this bead does not try.
- `undo --last-by <actor>` reverts that actor's most recent run: every transaction of that one command invocation, one per target, newest first (`src/app/undo.rs:7-13, 452-510`). `data.transactions[]` lists each `{target, reverted, tx, status}` and `data.reverted_run` names the run (`:58-143`).
- `update` without addons or `-t` updates every managed addon on every client, one transaction per target under one run, from the release memo when it is under 15 minutes old (`src/app/update.rs:1-11`).
- `outdated --changelog` attaches each update's notes since the installed release; for GitHub they come from `releases.atom`, one request, never REST (`src/app/outdated.rs:64-66, 121-133`; `src/sources/changelog.rs:1-9`).
- `export` builds `addons.toml` from the records alone, with `version` where known and `sha256` while the archive is in the blob cache; `--json` returns the document in `data.content` (`src/app/export.rs:1-18, 57-69`), rendered deterministically (`src/state/desired.rs:663-700`). `sync <file> --locked` installs the versions the file records (`src/app/sync.rs:54-56`).
- The catalog maps `weakauras` to `WeakAuras`, `gh:WeakAuras/WeakAuras2` (no mainline build), `dbm` to `DBM`, `gh:DeadlyBossMods/DeadlyBossMods`, and `gbb` to `GroupBulletinBoard`, `git:https://github.com/fondlez/GroupBulletinBoard#main` (`catalog/catalog.toml:37-50, 472-477`). A `git:` ref to GitHub resolves through the commits Atom feed and downloads from codeload, never REST, and a 3.3.5a custom root is registered with `targets add <dir> --name wotlk` (`tests/git_github.rs:1-4, 271-285`).
- The synthetic retail and Classic Era clients are 12.1.5 and 1.15.9 (`tests/common/trees.rs:25-39`), loading interfaces 120105 and 11509.
- Synthetic fixture builders: `gh_release`, `gh_release_v`, `gh_latest` (which replaces an earlier `releases/latest` of the same repository) and `gh_feed` (`tests/common/http.rs:139-262`); `common::wtf::Wtf::at(client)` with the fake names `FAKEACCT`, `FakeRealm`, `FakeChar` (`tests/common/wtf.rs:21-30`); `common::netlog::{read_net_log, assert_no_github_rest}`; `common::checkpoint::require` (`tests/common/checkpoint.rs`, the `SKIP` rule); `common::archives::zip_of` over the `zip` crate, already a dependency (`Cargo.toml`).
- `omaddons::app::COMMANDS` is public (`src/lib.rs:11`, `src/app/mod.rs:121-165`); `omaddons::net::replay::{Fixture, FixtureResponse, normalize_url, request_key}` are public (`src/net/mod.rs:17-18`, `src/net/replay.rs:41-90`). Net-log purposes are `asset` for a download, `release-latest` and `release-json` for GitHub metadata (`src/engine/blobs.rs:275`, `src/sources/github.rs:601, 673`).

**From the leaves this bead waits for, directly or through B2:** T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs: `tests/common/tlog.rs`, `tlog!()`, `log.run`, `log.cmd(…).cwd(…).env(…)`, `Ran`, `log.tree`, `log.diff`, `log.assert_unchanged`, `log.case`; a `blocks` edge to each subtask, added at filing); B1 (`tests/common/guide.rs`: `rendered(log, on)`, `unparsable(text)`, `sha256_hex`); B3 (`tests/common/skill.rs`: `claude_ready(env)`, `assert_is_guide(file)`); A1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1`, each `COMMANDS` row's `exits`); D4, D5 and D9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.9`: `plan_id`, `apply`, `plans show`); E1, E3 and E4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4`: the registry that holds `fm-state_files-record-folder-missing`, `doctor diagnose`, `--robot-triage`). If a helper's name or signature differs from what is written here when this bead starts, use the one that landed and say so in the close comment.

## Technical Approach

### 1. What the suite proves, and what it does not

For each of the eight recipes, on its own fresh synthetic home: the commands the installed skill prints, run exactly as written (split into argv, never through a shell), exit with the codes the block declares; each declared code is one the command's `COMMANDS` row declares; and the recipe's intent is met, as a per-recipe assertion. The commands run against `tests/fixtures/http/skill_recipes/`, recorded from the live hosts, so a recipe that names a real addon (`weakauras`, `dbm`, GroupBulletinBoard) is proven against what those hosts really answered, not against a fixture written to pass.

It does not test the commands themselves; their own suites do. A recipe test that fails because a command misbehaves points at that command's leaf (file a bug `discovered-from` this bead), never at the recipe.

The eight recipes, as the plan fixes them (§6.3.4; B2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.2`, the guide's content, wrote the blocks):

| Id | Intent | Commands |
|---|---|---|
| `update-everything` | update everything | `omaddons update --json --actor agent --reason "…"` |
| `whats-broken` | what is broken | `omaddons status --json`; then `omaddons doctor --robot-triage --json` |
| `install-for-target` | install X for target Y | `omaddons install weakauras -t era --json --actor agent` |
| `legacy-from-git` | add a legacy addon from a git repo | `omaddons install git:https://github.com/fondlez/GroupBulletinBoard#main -t wotlk --json` |
| `preview-then-apply` | preview, then apply exactly | `omaddons install dbm -t retail --dry-run --json`; then `omaddons apply <plan_id> --json` |
| `undo-agent-today` | undo what the agent did today | `omaddons history --actor agent --since 1d --json`; then `omaddons undo --last-by agent --json` |
| `explain-updates` | explain pending updates with changelogs | `omaddons outdated --changelog --json` |
| `fresh-machine` | restore a fresh machine | `omaddons sync addons.toml --locked --json` |

The `"…"` is the plan's elision: the parse check of B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`, the guide renderer) rejects `…` in the guide, so B2's block carries a concrete reason, and the test reads whatever reason the block has.

### 2. The recipe grammar (subtask 1)

A recipe is a fenced code block whose info string is `sh recipe=<id> expect=<exit>[,<exit>]` (§6.3.4). As B2 writes it:

````markdown
```sh recipe=preview-then-apply expect=0,0
# Preview, then apply exactly what was previewed.
# fill: plan_id ← data.plan_id
omaddons install dbm -t retail --dry-run --json
omaddons apply <plan_id> --json
```
````

The rules, made exact (decided while writing this bead; §6.3.4 gives the info string and the example rule `plan_id ← data.plan_id`, and leaves the rest open):
- **Fences.** A fence opens with three or more backticks or tildes followed by the info string, and closes with a line of at least as many of the same character. An unclosed fence is a problem.
- **The info string.** First word `sh`; then space-separated `key=value` attributes: `recipe`, an id matching `[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*`, and `expect`, one exit code per command, comma-separated, each 0 to 255. A missing, duplicated or unknown attribute is a problem; so is an id used twice.
- **Where.** Every recipe block sits in the guide's `## Recipes` section (from that heading to the next `## ` heading). A recipe block outside it is a problem, and so is an `sh` block inside it without `recipe=`: a command block in Recipes that no test runs.
- **Lines inside a block.** Blank lines are ignored. `# fill: <name> ← <path>` declares a fill rule. Any other line starting with `#` is a comment, kept for the log. Every other line is a command and must start with `omaddons `. A line ending in `\` (a continuation), or any other line, is a problem.
- **Commands.** One or two per recipe (criterion 4: "at most two omaddons commands"); the `expect` list has exactly one value per command; every command has the token `--json` (criterion 4: "with JSON output"). A line is split with `shell_words::split` (so `--reason "weekly check"` is one argument), the leading `omaddons` dropped, and nothing appended.
- **Shell syntax is refused.** After filling, no argument may contain any of `|`, `;`, `&`, `<`, `>`, `$`, a backtick or `#`, and no argument may contain `…`. A recipe is argv, never a shell pipeline; an agent that pipes output loses the envelope.
- **Placeholders** are `<name>` with `name` matching `[a-z][a-z0-9_]*`, inside one argument (the argument is filled after splitting, so a filled value never splits into two). A placeholder needs a fill rule declared in the same block; a placeholder in the first command is a problem (nothing precedes it); a fill rule no command uses is a problem.
- **Fill rules** fill command k's placeholders from command k−1's envelope, the whole stdout JSON object. `<path>` is a dotted path from the envelope's root: segments `[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*` name object keys and all-digit segments index arrays (`data.plan_id`, `data.targets.0.tx`, `findings.0.id`). The root is the envelope, not `data`, because the doctor's report sits at the top level (M4-D34). The value must be a string (used as is) or a number (its decimal form); missing, `null`, a boolean, an array or an object fails, naming the recipe, the rule, the path and the command whose envelope lacked it.

`tests/common/guide.rs` (B1's helper module, extended here):

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
pub struct Fill { pub name: String, pub path: String }
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
pub struct Recipe {
    pub id: String,
    pub expect: Vec<i32>,
    pub fills: Vec<Fill>,
    pub commands: Vec<String>,   // the command lines exactly as the guide writes them
    pub comments: Vec<String>,   // the other `#` lines, for the log
    pub line: usize,             // the opening fence's line in the guide, 1-based
}
pub const RECIPES_HEADING: &str = "## Recipes";
pub const RECIPE_MAX_COMMANDS: usize = 2;
/// Every recipe block of `guide`, or every problem found, each naming its guide line.
pub fn recipes(guide: &str) -> Result<Vec<Recipe>, Vec<String>>;
/// Command `k` (0-based) as argv without the leading `omaddons`, its placeholders filled
/// from `previous` (command k−1's envelope).
pub fn recipe_argv(recipe: &Recipe, k: usize, previous: Option<&serde_json::Value>) -> Result<Vec<String>, String>;
/// The string at `path` in `envelope` (a number in decimal); an error names the path.
pub fn resolve_fill(envelope: &serde_json::Value, path: &str) -> Result<String, String>;
```

If B2 already added a recipe parser to `tests/common/guide.rs` for its parse check, extend that one rather than adding a second, and make B2's parse check and this bead's runner share it. If B2's blocks use another notation for the same information (an id, one exit per command, a declared fill rule per placeholder), the parser follows the guide and the close comment records the notation. If a block lacks information the runner needs, this bead corrects the block in `src/contract/guide/guide.md` and regenerates `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` in the same commit (common rule 17).

**The intents table** (decided while writing this bead), `CANONICAL` in `tests/skill_recipes.rs`: the eight ids of section 1 with their intent sentences, and each id's shape, checked on the block's argv so that a recipe edited into something else cannot keep passing under its old name:

| Id | Commands | Shape |
|---|---|---|
| `update-everything` | 1 | first word `update`; no addon positional; no `-t` |
| `whats-broken` | 2 | `status`; then `doctor` with `--robot-triage` |
| `install-for-target` | 1 | `install`, one positional, `-t <id>` |
| `legacy-from-git` | 1 | `install`, one positional starting `git:`, `-t <id>` |
| `preview-then-apply` | 2 | a storable command with `--dry-run`; then `apply <plan_id>` with a fill rule for `plan_id` |

### 3. The recorded scenario `tests/fixtures/http/skill_recipes/` (subtask 2)

**What it holds:** exactly the requests the recipes and their setups make to real hosts (github.com, codeload.github.com, release-assets.githubusercontent.com): WeakAuras for Classic Era, GroupBulletinBoard's `main` for the 3.3.5a client, DBM for retail (its dry run, its `apply`, its pin-time probe), the locked reinstall of all three on a fresh home, and a re-check of each with an aged memo.

**How it is recorded:** once, by `tests/skill_recipes.rs::record_skill_recipes` (ignored), with `OMADDONS_RECORD=1`, running the **record plan** (`common::recipes::record_plan`) against the live hosts. The record plan runs the recipes' own commands, extracted from the guide, never copies of them:

1. Recording home 1, a recipe home (section 4) whose fixture directory is the scenario directory:
   1. `install-for-target`'s command, verbatim;
   2. `legacy-from-git`'s command;
   3. `preview-then-apply`'s two commands, the second filled from the first;
   4. `pin <install-for-target's addon> -t <its target> --json` (`pin` revalidates its source, so its probe is recorded for `fresh-machine`'s setup);
   5. `export --json`, keeping `data.content`.
2. Recording home 2, a fresh recipe home: `data.content` written to `<work>/<fresh-machine's file argument>`, then `fresh-machine`'s command.
3. Recording home 1 again, with the release memo aged by 24 hours: `update --json --actor human` and `outdated --changelog --json`, so every real ref's re-check is recorded however its source probes.

Each recipe command must exit with its block's `expect`, and every other command with 0; a failure stops the recording and names the step, the argv, the exit and the error.

**The validator-cache hazard** (found while writing this bead): `Validating` sends `If-None-Match` from `<cache>/http/` when a feed was fetched earlier in the same home; a live `304` would then be recorded over the `200`, and replay in a fresh home, which has no validator cache, would get a bare `304` and fail. So the record plan deletes the home's `<cache>/http/` before every command, and the hygiene check refuses any committed `304`.

**Trimming** (decided while writing this bead), `common::recipes::trim_scenario(dir)`, run by the recorder after recording:
- **Archives become skeletons.** A body whose bytes start with the zip signature `PK\x03\x04` is rewritten by `common::archives::skeleton`: the same entries, in the same order, with the same names, kinds and Unix modes and the archive comment; every file whose name ends in `.toc` (any case) byte for byte; every other file empty. omaddons reads only TOCs to decide what installs where (folder names, interfaces per flavor suffix, dependencies), so the replayed installs make the same decisions.
- **Atom feeds keep their newest entry.** A body whose `content-type` contains `atom` (decoded first when `content-encoding: gzip`, re-encoded after) keeps the feed header and its first `<entry>` only; each `<author>` becomes `<author><name>contributor</name></author>`, and `<media:thumbnail>` elements are removed: the house's existing trimming, done by code instead of by hand.
- **`content-length`**, when present, is set to the trimmed body's length.

*Why trim:* whole release archives would add several megabytes of third-party addon code per recording to a repository whose fixtures total 2.6 MB and which has so far committed one small archive; the skeleton keeps everything omaddons reads. *Rejected:* (i) whole bodies (size, and redistributing third-party code in this repository); (ii) synthetic fixtures for the recipes that name real addons, as C4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4`, the run-the-fix corpus) chose for its corpus home: they would prove only that the CLI runs, not that `weakauras` on Classic Era resolves to a release that loads there, which is what an agent copying the recipe needs; (iii) trimming by hand, as the older recorders' doc comments ask: a skeleton cannot be made by hand, and a check (below) is more reliable than a review.

**The hygiene check** (in the gate), `the_recorded_scenario_is_trimmed_public_and_small`, over `common::recipes::scenario_problems(dir)`:
- the whole directory is at most `SCENARIO_MAX_BYTES` (2 MiB, a test constant in `tests/common/recipes.rs`, like the harness constants of T1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs; not a `src/limits.rs` row, which is for the binary), listing the five largest files when it is not;
- every fixture parses as `omaddons::net::replay::Fixture`, has exactly one response, no `304`, no `set-cookie` or `authorization` header, and a URL equal to its own `normalize_url`;
- every zip body is a skeleton (`archives::is_skeleton`: every non-`.toc` file entry is empty);
- every Atom body has at most one `<entry>`, no `<email>`, and every `<name>` is `contributor`;
- every `content-length` equals its body's length.

- `malformed_recipe_blocks_are_reported` (subtask 1), each case with the expected problem text and guide line: `three_commands`, `expect_count_mismatch`, `expect_not_a_number`, `expect_out_of_range`, `missing_expect`, `unknown_attribute`, `duplicate_id`, `bad_id`, `not_an_omaddons_line`, `continuation_line`, `pipe`, `redirect`, `command_substitution`, `ellipsis`, `no_json`, `placeholder_without_rule`, `placeholder_in_first_command`, `unused_rule`, `recipe_outside_the_section`, `untested_sh_block_in_the_section`, `unclosed_fence`.
- `fill_rules_resolve_from_the_previous_envelope` (subtask 1): `string`, `number`, `array_index`, `top_level_key`, `missing_key`, `null_value`, `boolean_value`, `object_value`, `value_with_a_space_stays_one_argument`.
- `an_archive_skeleton_keeps_every_entry_and_the_tocs`, `an_archive_skeleton_is_idempotent`, `an_atom_feed_keeps_its_newest_entry_without_authors` (plain and gzip, a feed with no entry), `trimming_sets_content_length`, `the_scenario_check_reports_each_kind_of_problem` (subtask 2).
- `scenario_comparison_names_moved_releases_and_changed_statuses` (subtask 4).

### Integration and end-to-end tests

`tests/skill_recipes.rs` (gate):
- `the_installed_skill_holds_exactly_the_eight_canonical_recipes` (subtask 1).
- `the_recorded_scenario_is_trimmed_public_and_small` (subtask 2).
- `recipe_update_everything`, `recipe_whats_broken`, `recipe_install_for_target`, `recipe_legacy_from_git`, `recipe_preview_then_apply`, `recipe_undo_agent_today`, `recipe_explain_updates`, `recipe_fresh_machine` (subtask 3): each builds a recipe home over the recorded scenario, runs its setup, extracts its recipe from `robot-docs guide`, runs it verbatim with the runner of section 5 (exit per command, declared exits, privacy), asserts section 6, ends with `left_healthy`, then runs the `--progress json` pass of section 7 as a case.

`argc e2e skill_recipes` runs them with verbose logs.

### Logging

Every scenario starts with `let log = tlog!();` and names its phases with `log.step`: `home`, `setup`, `recipe <id>`, `assert`, `healthy`, and the case `progress json`. Every command goes through `log.run` or `log.cmd(…).cwd(…).run()`, so the log records each argv as run, the working directory, the exit, the parsed envelope, the stderr events and the `net.log` lines added. The recipe as extracted is logged with `log.json("recipe", …)`; each filled placeholder with `log.note("fill <name> = <value> from <path>")`. Client and state trees are recorded with `log.tree` and checked with `log.assert_unchanged` or `log.diff` (which logs the first differing paths); compared values (dry-run items against applied items, the exported documents, the transaction sets) go through `log.assert_eq`. On a panic, the guard of T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs) prints `test log: <path>` and the last 20 steps; `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG=verbose` echoes every step live. The recorder logs each record-plan step and the trimming totals; the live probe prints its steps and its comparison report to stderr.

### Checkpoint-only tests

- **The recorder**, run by hand when the fixtures must change (never by the gate): delete `tests/fixtures/http/skill_recipes/`, then `OMADDONS_RECORD=1 cargo test --test skill_recipes -- --ignored record_skill_recipes`, then review the diff and run `cargo test --test skill_recipes`. Without `OMADDONS_RECORD=1` it returns at once (a recorder, not a checkpoint check).
- **The live probe**, run by H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the checkpoint; §11.3 step 8): `OMADDONS_LIVE=1 cargo test --test live_probes -- --ignored skill_recipes_record_live_and_match_the_fixtures`. Without `OMADDONS_LIVE=1` it prints `SKIP skill_recipes_record_live_and_match_the_fixtures: OMADDONS_LIVE is not 1` and fails unless `OMADDONS_ALLOW_SKIP` names it; that skip is not pre-accepted by §3.2, so at the checkpoint it must run.

## Considerations

- **Risk 13, "the guide drifts from behaviour"** (L, M; owners B2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.2`, the guide's content, and this bead): mitigated by generated tables, the parse check of every command the guide names, byte identity with `SKILL.md`, and here the recipes run and their declared exits held to `COMMANDS`. A later leaf that changes a command a recipe uses breaks this suite in the gate, which is the point.
- **Recorded data is pinned.** The committed scenario answers as the hosts did on the recording day; a newer upstream release is invisible to the gate. The checkpoint's live probe reports what moved; re-record when a recipe's real addon changes its layout or a host its answers.
- **A missing fixture** shows as a command exiting 1 with `internal` "replay: no fixture for GET …": the record plan did not make that request. Extend the record plan (never add a hand-written fixture to the recorded scenario) and re-record.
- **Skeleton archives** prove what installs where, not that the addon's Lua is intact; the recipes never needed more. Folder trees compared in `fresh-machine` are skeleton trees on both homes.
- **Runtime.** Eighteen recipe homes (two passes per recipe, and two homes in each pass of `fresh-machine`) with small skeleton archives; the tests run in parallel across the binary's threads. If the suite adds more than about 30 s to a gate run, report it in the close comment.
- **`apply` downloads nothing** is the plan's own claim (§11.4 risk 7: "the blobs are then cached, so `apply` downloads nothing"). If that assertion fails, the recipe is right and the cache reuse is not: file a bug `discovered-from` this bead against D5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`, `omaddons apply`) rather than dropping the check.
- **Privacy.** Synthetic homes only; the fake account, realm and character names in `WTF/` and `assert_private` on both streams of every run. The recorded fixtures carry no request header, cookie or secret query parameter, and feed authors are anonymized; the hygiene test holds that.
- **The default actor in tests is `agent`** (no terminal on stdin). A setup command that forgets `--actor human` turns a person's change into the agent's, and `undo-agent-today` would then revert it: the test fails, which is the right outcome, but the cause is the setup.
- **Time.** `history --since 1d` and history's `at` use the wall clock, not `OMADDONS_NOW`; nothing here depends on a frozen clock. `TZ=UTC` comes from `TestEnv`.
- **Hot spots (§10.5):** `tests/common/guide.rs` is the helper module of B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`, the guide renderer) and B2 too (append functions, rebase); `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` is regenerated after rebasing, never merged by hand; `README.md`: edit only the Tests row, the recorded-fixtures sentence and the live-probes bullet; `tests/live_probes.rs`: append one probe.
- **Why size M, four subtasks.** The work is tests and fixtures in one area, but four commits of different kinds: a pure parser with its self-tests; a recording that needs the network once and commits fixtures; eight scenarios; a checkpoint-only probe. Each lands green on its own.
- **After H1.** This bead may land after H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, the pre-freeze contract audit) closes and adds no wire shape; the rule test and the golden see nothing new from it.
- **Defaults decided while writing this bead** (confirm or adjust in the close comment): the grammar details of section 2 (fences, attributes, the `# fill:` notation, envelope-rooted paths, refused shell characters); the intents table; extraction from an installed skill; the record plan and its order; deleting `<cache>/http/` before each recorded command; skeleton archives and code-trimmed feeds; `SCENARIO_MAX_BYTES` 2 MiB; the recipe home's three clients, `WTF/` and work directory; the synthetic `R`, `S`, `T` setups; each recipe's assertion beyond the plan's three; the declared-exits check; `left_healthy`; the `--progress json` second pass; `whats-broken` expecting `0,1`; the live probe's place and its fail-or-report rule; one agent run for `undo-agent-today`.

## Dependencies

Parent: the B area epic `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2` (the guide and the skill).

**Blocked by:**
- B2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.2`, the guide's content): the eight recipe blocks with their `expect=` and fill rules are what this bead runs. Through B2's own blockers this bead can also rely on the stored plan and `apply` (D4, D5), `plans show` (D9) and `doctor --robot-triage` (E3, E4), which the recipes and their assertions use.
- B3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3`, `robot-docs install-skill`): the recipes are read from a skill installed by it, and its `tests/common/skill.rs` helpers (`claude_ready`, `assert_is_guide`) prove the installed bytes are the guide's.

Each subtask is also blocked by T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs), an edge added at filing, for `TestLog`.

**Unblocks:**
- H4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`, the README final pass): README's "For coding agents" block becomes a pointer to the skill with an excerpt; that excerpt quotes recipes this bead has proven, and the test counts H4 matches include this suite.

**Slice:** `slice-4`, "Freeze and close" (the discovery line, the guide's content, this bead, and the freeze: the audit, the golden, the determinism audit, README, the vision comments and the checkpoint). Its exit demo starts with "the recipes pass"; H6 runs this suite at the checkpoint and records the demo after the tag. It pre-checks criteria 3, 4, 14, 17 and 18; this bead owns 4.

**Related, not edges:** B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`, whose `tests/common/guide.rs` this bead extends); C4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4`, whose corpus home is synthetic by design; this suite's homes are its own, because the recipes name real addons); A1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1`, the `exits` the runner checks); D4, D5 and D9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.9`: the stored plan, `apply`, `plans show`); E1, E3 and E4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4`: the failure mode and the triage report `whats-broken` reads); H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, after which this bead may land); H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, which runs the live probe and records slice 4's demo).
