title: Misplaced-client fixes before and after the verb in usage_error
description:
Part 2 of 4 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.1 (Misplaced clients before and after the verb). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

C1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.1`) makes a client named where a command or an argument belongs a `usage` error whose fix is the user's own command with the client moved into `-t`. Agents guess the client-first shape (`omaddons retail update`) before reading anything, and today it gets `omaddons help`. That serves G-M4-2 ("the first guess works") and checkpoint criterion 5 (the intent corpus's misplaced-client rows before and after the verb). Vision §5.10 names the case ("`omaddons retail update` gives `fix: omaddons update -t retail`"), and vision goal G4 is "the first command an agent guesses works".

This part is the behaviour. It adds the `UsageFix` marker, hook 1 and hook 2 of M4-D12 in `cli::usage_error`, the lazy vocabulary in `run_with`, and the README text, all in one commit (common rule 11). It builds on part 1's `TargetVocabulary` (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.1.1`). Parts 3 and 4 test it through the binary.

**M4-D12, as it applies here.**
- **Hook 1, before the verb:** clap's `InvalidSubcommand(w)` where `w` names a client and the next word is a subcommand. The fix is the argv minus `w`, plus `-t w` at the end. `omaddons retail update` → `omaddons update -t retail`; `omaddons sod install questie` → `omaddons install questie -t sod`. The message is "'<w>' is a client, not a command; the client goes in -t", with `details {target, command}`.
- **Hook 2, after the verb:** clap's `UnknownArgument(tok)` where `tok` has no leading dash and names a client. The fix replaces `tok` with `-t tok`. It covers a command with no positional (`omaddons status retail` → `omaddons status -t retail`) and one whose single positional is filled (`omaddons info dbm era` → `omaddons info dbm -t era`, `omaddons pin dbm retail` → `omaddons pin dbm -t retail`).
- **Hook 3** (a client named among `install`/`update`/`remove`'s names) is C2's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.2`), at app level.
- **The verb exemption:** these fixes keep the user's verb, so they are exempt from "never guess a mutating command" (vision comment 660, which exists so a typo never turns into another verb). They are marked `UsageFix::UserVerb` so the mutating-guess rule never demotes them to `help`, and they must still parse.
- **The addon wins:** a word that is both a client and an addon or catalog entry is never moved (risk 12).
- **Rejected:** running discovery in the usage path (a scan for a usage error; usage errors must be fast and side-effect free), and accepting the misplaced form silently (commands must have one shape, or agents learn two).

**Facts this part relies on** (as of `c0ab5e9`):
- `usage_error` (`src/cli.rs:604-773`): the presentation-flag case (`:627-634`) and `update --version` (`:645-674`) handle dash tokens only. Then comes the `match err.kind()` at `:675`, whose `InvalidSubcommand` arm (`:676-688`) tries `reinstall` and then `subcommand_fix`, and whose `UnknownArgument` arm (`:689-743`) corrects flags. The final filter (`:756-763`) replaces a fix with `help` only when it does not parse or equals the failing argv.
- `subcommand_fix` (`:849-890`) offers a guessed mutating command as `help <it>` (`:879`). That is the mutating-guess rule. `omaddons era status` today gets "…; the closest command is remove" and `omaddons help remove`, because the alias `rm` is within distance 2 of `era`.
- `run_with` calls `usage_error(&err, &argv)` at `:389-392`, with the environment as `env` (`:353`).
- Helpers: `command_path` (`:1010-1037`), `takes_value` (`:993-1006`), `command_at` (`:799`), `help_for` (`:805-809`), `parses` (`:788-796`), `fix_argv` (`:1055`), `fix_argv_keeping` (`:1091`), and `without_target` (`:1148-1173`, the target flag's spellings: `-t`, `--target`, `--flavor`, their `=` forms, `-tX`, a short cluster with `t`).
- `Error` (`src/error.rs:501`) wraps `ErrorData` (`:505-513`), built only by `Error::new` (`:539`). It serializes through `ErrorBody` (`:618-641`), which copies only the wire fields. `PlanStaleSource` (`:529-536`) is the precedent for a per-instance marker. No `UsageFix` exists.
- `Catalog::builtin()` (`src/resolve/catalog.rs:136`) parses the embedded catalog only. `Entry::answers_to` (`:52`) matches a name or alias ignoring case. No built-in entry is named like a client word today.
- `app::COMMANDS` (`src/app/mod.rs:121-165`) includes parents that run bare (`backup`, `errors`). `app::canonical` is at `:177`.
- `info` takes one positional (`src/app/info.rs:50-51`), as do `pin` and `unpin` (`src/app/pin.rs:33-47`). clap rejects their extra word as `UnknownArgument` ("unexpected argument 'era' found").

## Technical Approach

### 1. `UsageFix` (`src/error.rs`)

```rust
/// How a usage fix relates to the command the user typed (M4-D12). Not on the wire:
/// `cli::usage_error` and the tests read it.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default)]
pub enum UsageFix {
    /// May name another command (the closest name, a synonym, `help`); a guessed command
    /// that changes something is offered as its help (`subcommand_fix`).
    #[default]
    Guess,
    /// The user's own command, kept: only a client word moved into -t (M4-D12) or a
    /// selector corrected (M4-D14). Never demoted to help; it must still parse.
    UserVerb,
}
```

- `ErrorData` gains `pub usage_fix: UsageFix` (doc: "Not serialized"). `Error::new` sets `UsageFix::Guess`. `#[must_use] pub fn user_verb(mut self) -> Self` sets `UserVerb`. `ErrorBody`, its `From<Error>` and `impl JsonSchema for Error` are unchanged.
- **Decided while writing this bead:** the marker lives on `ErrorData` beside `PlanStaleSource`, so that C2's hook 3 (in `app`) and C3's selector fix (in `discover::registry`) can mark their errors and in-process tests can read it.
- **Where the plan and the code differ:** M4-D12 says the marker keeps "the final filter" from demoting these fixes, but the demotion of mutating guesses is in `subcommand_fix`, not in the final filter. The intent is kept. The hooks run before `subcommand_fix`. Each hook applies the final filter's own two checks to its candidate (it parses; it is not the failing argv). A failing candidate makes the hook return `None`, so `usage_error` continues exactly as today, and a user-verb fix is never replaced by `help`.

### 2. Shared pieces (`src/cli.rs`)

- `struct UsageWords<'a> { vocabulary: std::cell::OnceCell<TargetVocabulary>, load: &'a dyn Fn() -> TargetVocabulary, names_an_addon: &'a dyn Fn(&str) -> bool }` with `fn vocabulary(&self) -> &TargetVocabulary` (`get_or_init(self.load)`). The loader runs at most once per usage error, and only after a hook's argv checks passed.
- `fn has_target_flag(argv: &[String]) -> bool`: before any `--`, a token `-t`, `--target`, `--flavor`, `--target=…`, `--flavor=…`, `-tX` (attached value), or a short cluster (one dash, not `--`) containing `t`, such as `-vt`. It uses the same spellings as `without_target`. `--to` (copy's flag) is not one.
- `fn rejected_subcommand_at(argv: &[String]) -> Option<usize>`: walk `argv[1..]` exactly as `command_path` does (stop at `--`; skip a flag and, when `takes_value` at the level reached, its value; descend on a subcommand name or alias). Return the index of the first positional that names no subcommand of the level reached.
- `fn last_positional_at(argv: &[String], word: &str) -> Option<usize>`: the index of the last token equal to `word` that is positional-looking. It is not a flag, not the value of a flag that takes one (`takes_value` at the command `command_path(argv)` reaches, globals included), and not after `--`.
- `pub(crate) fn with_target_appended(argv: &[String], at: usize) -> Vec<String>`: `argv` without the token at `at`, with `-t` and that token inserted at the end, or just before the first `--` when there is one, then `fix_argv` (presentation flags dropped). **Decided while writing this bead:** before `--`, because after it `-t` and the word would be positionals.
- `pub(crate) fn with_target_in_place(argv: &[String], at: usize) -> Vec<String>`: the token at `at` replaced by `-t` and the token, every other argument where it was, then `fix_argv`. C2's hook 3 reuses it.
- `fn misplaced_client_error(message: String, fix: Vec<String>, path: &[String], word: &str) -> Error`: `Error::new(ErrorCode::Usage, message, Suggestion::command(fix)).alternative(help_for(path)).details(json!({"target": word, "command": path.join(" ")})).user_verb()`. **Decided while writing this bead:** `details.target` is the word as typed (the value placed after `-t`), and `details.command` the canonical command path the fix runs (`update` for `omaddons retail upgrade`). Both hooks offer one alternative, `omaddons help <command>`: the milestone's target transcript for `omaddons retail update` carries exactly `{"display":"omaddons help update","argv":["omaddons","help","update"]}` (§4.1), and hook 2 does the same for symmetry.
- `fn names_a_builtin_catalog_entry(word: &str) -> bool`: `Catalog::builtin().is_ok_and(|c| c.entries().iter().any(|e| e.answers_to(word)))`. **Decided while writing this bead:** on the usage path the addon-wins test reads only the embedded catalog's names and aliases. It reads no `catalog.d` file and no installed record, because those need the config dir and a target. C2's preflight, which has the world loaded, checks installed addons.

### 3. Hook 1: `fn misplaced_before_verb(err: &clap::Error, argv: &[String], words: &UsageWords<'_>) -> Option<Error>`

In order, `None` at the first failing step:
1. `err.kind() == ErrorKind::InvalidSubcommand`, and `w` is its `ContextKind::InvalidSubcommand` string.
2. `at = rejected_subcommand_at(argv)?` and `argv[at] == w`; `parent = command_path(argv)`.
3. `!has_target_flag(argv)`. **Decided while writing this bead:** with a target already given (`omaddons retail update -t era`), keep today's fix: moving a second client would silently override the first (`args_override_self`) or be overridden.
4. `words.vocabulary().classify(w).is_some()` (the vocabulary is loaded here, at most once).
5. `!(words.names_an_addon)(w)`: the addon wins.
6. `candidate = with_target_appended(argv, at)`; `path = command_path(&candidate)`.
7. `path` is non-empty, `crate::app::COMMANDS` has a row named `path.join(" ")`, and `vocabulary::selects_client(&path)`. Then either `path.len() > parent.len()` (a subcommand followed `w`, at any depth: `omaddons retail update`, `omaddons retail backup list`, `omaddons backup retail list`), or `path == parent` and `parent` is itself a `COMMANDS` row (a parent that runs bare: `omaddons backup retail` → `omaddons backup -t retail`, `omaddons errors retail` → `omaddons errors -t retail`). **Decided while writing this bead:** the hook works at every level and on parents that run bare, because `backup` and `errors` are commands of their own and the corrected argv has exactly hook 1's shape. `omaddons retail` alone gives an empty path and keeps today's fix: there is no verb to keep.
8. `parses(&Suggestion::command(candidate.clone()))` and `candidate != fix_argv(argv)`.
9. `Some(misplaced_client_error(format!("'{w}' is a client, not a command; the client goes in -t"), candidate, &path, w))`.

### 4. Hook 2: `fn misplaced_after_verb(err: &clap::Error, argv: &[String], words: &UsageWords<'_>) -> Option<Error>`

1. `err.kind() == ErrorKind::UnknownArgument`, `tok` is its `ContextKind::InvalidArg` string, and `!tok.starts_with('-')`.
2. `path = command_path(argv)`: non-empty, a `COMMANDS` row, and `selects_client(&path)`.
3. `!has_target_flag(argv)`.
4. `at = last_positional_at(argv, tok)?`. **Decided while writing this bead:** the last occurrence, because clap rejects the word after the filled positionals (`omaddons pin retail retail` → `omaddons pin retail -t retail`), and a word after `--` is never moved.
5. `classify(tok).is_some()` and `!(words.names_an_addon)(tok)`.
6. `candidate = with_target_in_place(argv, at)`. It must parse and differ from `fix_argv(argv)`.
7. `Some(misplaced_client_error(format!("'{tok}' is a client, not an argument of {}; the client goes in -t", path.join(" ")), candidate, &path, tok))`. **Decided while writing this bead:** this message wording (the plan fixes only hook 1's).

### 5. Wiring

- `pub fn usage_error_with(err: &clap::Error, argv: &[String], vocabulary: &dyn Fn() -> TargetVocabulary, names_an_addon: &dyn Fn(&str) -> bool) -> Error` takes today's body. Right before `let (fix, alternatives) = match err.kind()` (`:675`) it runs:

  ```rust
  let words = UsageWords::new(vocabulary, names_an_addon);
  if let Some(error) = misplaced_before_verb(err, argv, &words)
      .or_else(|| misplaced_after_verb(err, argv, &words)) {
      return error;
  }
  ```

  Neither match arm changes (hot-spot rule: each hook in its own function).
- `pub fn usage_error(err: &clap::Error, argv: &[String]) -> Error` keeps its signature for the in-process callers (the cli unit tests and `tests/contract/usage_fixes.rs`'s typo sweep): `usage_error_with(err, argv, &TargetVocabulary::builtin, &names_a_builtin_catalog_entry)`, the built-in words, no file read.
- `run_with` (`:389-392`): `usage_error_with(&err, &argv, &|| TargetVocabulary::from_env(env), &names_a_builtin_catalog_entry)`. `from_env` reads `<state>/registry.json` bounded and read-only, or falls back to the built-in words.
- Nothing else in the run changes. The error renders through `render_error` with `command_of(&argv)` (`omaddons` for `omaddons retail update`, `status` for `omaddons status retail`), before `Context`, discovery, recovery or any lock exist (common rule 8: a usage error found from the arguments changes nothing).

### 6. `details` declarations

The new wire names are `usage`'s `details.target` (string) and `details.command` (string). If A9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9`) has landed (a `DetailSpec` per code row, `src/error/detail_spec.rs`), add both to `usage`'s spec as optional, non-null strings in this commit. If A3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`) has landed, the contract suite then validates them on every envelope. If neither has landed, A9 records them from these construction sites. List both in the close comment.

### 7. README (same commit)

- **"Choosing a target with `-t`"** (`README.md:467`), a new paragraph:

  > **A client in the wrong place.** A client named where a command or an argument belongs is a usage error whose fix moves it into `-t` and keeps your command: `omaddons retail update` → `omaddons update -t retail`, `omaddons sod install questie` → `omaddons install questie -t sod`, `omaddons status era` → `omaddons status -t era`, `omaddons info dbm era` → `omaddons info dbm -t era`. A client word is a built-in id, product code, flavor folder, game mode or family, or the id of a registered target. A catalog addon of the same name is never moved, and nothing is moved when `-t` is already given. `error.details` is `{target, command}`. `config`, `targets`, `net-log`, `auth`, `omarchy`, `copy` and `help` do not take `-t` this way and keep their usual fix.
- **Command reference intro** (`README.md:689`), after the typo sentences: "A client named before or after the command is moved into `-t`; that fix keeps your command even when it changes something, because only the client moved."
- **"Every error code", the `usage` row** (`README.md:1827`): append "a client named where a command or argument belongs (`details: {target, command}`)".

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `UsageFix { Guess, UserVerb }` exists in `src/error.rs`; `ErrorData.usage_fix` defaults to `Guess`; `Error::user_verb()` sets `UserVerb`; the serialized error is byte-identical with and without the mark.
- [ ] `omaddons retail update` gives `usage`, the message `'retail' is a client, not a command; the client goes in -t`, `fix_argv` `["omaddons","update","-t","retail"]`, the alternative `omaddons help update`, `details {"target":"retail","command":"update"}`, marked `UserVerb`.
- [ ] Hook 1 covers `era status`, `sod install questie`, `wotlk list`, `Retail update`, `retail upgrade` (`details.command` `update`), `--dry-run retail update`, `retail remove -- dbm` (`-t retail` before `--`), `backup retail list`, `retail backup list`, `backup retail` and `errors retail`.
- [ ] Hook 2 covers `status retail`, `list era`, `outdated retail`, `history retail`, `export retail`, `info dbm era`, `pin dbm retail`, `unpin dbm retail` and `pin dbm retail --version 12.1.14`, each with the word replaced in place, with the message `'<w>' is a client, not an argument of <command>; the client goes in -t`.
- [ ] Today's fix is unchanged (equal to `usage_error_with` with `TargetVocabulary::empty()`) for a non-client word, a client word on a `CLIENT_FREE` command, an argv that already names a target, a client word that a planted addon predicate claims, a word after `--`, and `omaddons retail` alone.
- [ ] The vocabulary loader runs at most once per usage error, and never for a usage error that no hook could apply to.
- [ ] `run_with` passes `TargetVocabulary::from_env(env)`; `usage_error(err, argv)` keeps its signature and uses the built-in words.
- [ ] README's three places describe the fixes, in this commit.
- [ ] If A9 has landed, `usage`'s `DetailSpec` declares `target` and `command`.
- [ ] The existing cli unit tests and `tests/contract/usage_fixes.rs` pass unchanged.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs src/cli.rs src/error.rs README.md` is clean.
- [ ] `br lint` is clean for this subtask.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests (`src/cli.rs` `mod tests`, and `src/error.rs`)

Each table row is a named case. Each assertion message prints the case, the argv, the expected and actual `fix_argv`, `details` and `usage_fix`. Every case calls `usage_error_with(&Cli::try_parse_from(&raw).unwrap_err(), &raw, &vocab, &no_addon)`, where `vocab` is `TargetVocabulary::builtin` unless the row says otherwise and `no_addon` is `|_| false`.

- `a_client_before_the_verb_moves_to_the_end_as_dash_t` (argv → fix argv, `details.target`, `details.command`; message `'<target>' is a client, not a command; the client goes in -t`; one alternative `omaddons help <command>`; `UserVerb`; `retryable` false):
  - `retail update` → `omaddons update -t retail`, `retail`, `update`
  - `era status` → `omaddons status -t era`, `era`, `status`
  - `sod install questie` → `omaddons install questie -t sod`, `sod`, `install`
  - `wotlk list` → `omaddons list -t wotlk`
  - `Retail update` → `omaddons update -t Retail`, `Retail`, `update`
  - `retail upgrade` → `omaddons upgrade -t retail`, `retail`, `update`
  - `--json retail update` → `omaddons update -t retail` (presentation flag dropped)
  - `--dry-run retail update` → `omaddons --dry-run update -t retail`
  - `--actor agent retail update` → `omaddons --actor agent update -t retail`
  - `retail remove -- dbm` → `omaddons remove -t retail -- dbm`, `remove`
  - `backup retail list` → `omaddons backup list -t retail`, `backup list`
  - `retail backup list` → `omaddons backup list -t retail`, `backup list`
  - `backup retail` → `omaddons backup -t retail`, `backup`
  - `errors retail` → `omaddons errors -t retail`, `errors`
  - `wow_classic_era list`, `_retail_ outdated`, `mainline status`, `hc list` → each `omaddons <verb> -t <word>`
  - `turtle list` with `vocab = || TargetVocabulary::new(&RulesTable::builtin(), ["turtle"])` → `omaddons list -t turtle`
- `a_client_after_the_verb_is_replaced_by_dash_t` (message `'<w>' is a client, not an argument of <command>; the client goes in -t`):
  - `status retail` → `omaddons status -t retail`, `status`
  - `list era` → `omaddons list -t era`; `outdated retail`; `history retail`; `export retail`
  - `info dbm era` → `omaddons info dbm -t era`, `info`
  - `pin dbm retail` → `omaddons pin dbm -t retail`; `unpin dbm retail` → `omaddons unpin dbm -t retail`
  - `pin dbm retail --version 12.1.14` → `omaddons pin dbm -t retail --version 12.1.14`
  - `status retail --json` → `omaddons status -t retail`
  - `pin retail retail` → `omaddons pin retail -t retail` (the last occurrence moves)
- `words_that_are_not_misplaced_clients_keep_todays_fix`: for each argv, the error equals `usage_error_with(…, &TargetVocabulary::empty, &no_addon)` (same message, fix, alternatives, `details`, and `usage_fix == Guess`). Cases: `frobnicate update`, `retail` (alone), `retail dbm`, `status dbm`, `info dbm questie`, `retail update -t era`, `retail update --target=era`, `status retail --flavor era`, `-vt era retail update`, `retail config`, `retail targets`, `retail net-log`, `retail auth github`, `retail help`, `retail copy --from era --to classic`, `config retail`, `targets retail`, `omarchy retail`, `01JZ0000000000000000000000 update`.
- `the_addon_wins_over_a_client_word`: with `names_an_addon = |w| w.eq_ignore_ascii_case("sod")`, `sod install questie`, `SOD update` and `pin dbm sod` each equal the empty-vocabulary oracle, while `era status` with the same predicate is still moved.
- `has_target_flag_knows_every_spelling`: `-t x`, `--target x`, `--target=x`, `--flavor x`, `--flavor=x`, `-tx`, `-vt x` → true; `-v`, `--json`, `--to x`, `-- -t x` (after `--`) → false.
- `the_vocabulary_loads_once_and_only_when_a_hook_could_apply`: a loader that counts its calls in a `Cell<usize>`: `retail update` → 1; `frobnicate` → 1 (it classifies the word, finds nothing); `status --bogus` → 0; `install` (a missing argument) → 0; `retail update -t era` → 0; `install x --channel betaa` → 0.
- `hook_fixes_are_user_verb_and_guesses_are_not`: `retail update` → `UserVerb`; `statsu`, `instal dbm`, `reinstall x -t retail` → `Guess`.
- `src/error.rs`: `user_verb_marks_the_error_and_never_reaches_the_wire`: `serde_json::to_string` of an error with and without `.user_verb()` is byte-identical, and `usage_fix` reads back `UserVerb` and `Guess`.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

In parts 3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.1.3`, contract rows and sweeps) and 4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.1.4`, end to end with `TestLog`).

### Logging

Unit tests only: table-driven, each assertion message names the case and shows the argv, the expected and actual fix, `details` and `usage_fix`.

## Considerations

- **Hot spot `src/cli.rs`** (A1 `auth github`, A8, C1, C2, D5, E3): each hook and helper is its own function, and the only edits inside `usage_error`'s body are the early-return block and the signature split. If A1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1`) is in flight, let its `auth github` change land first and rebase. These hooks land before D5's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`) `Context` fields.
- **Hot spot `src/error.rs`** (A9 then A3 edit every code row): this part adds the `UsageFix` type, one field and one builder, outside the rows. Rebase onto A9 or A3 if either is in flight.
- **Risk 12, misplaced-client fixes misfire** (L, M): the addon-wins test, no fix when a target is given, the `CLIENT_FREE` list, and the parse check. One residual case remains. A hand-installed addon named like a client, typed before the verb, is moved (`omaddons classic update` meant as "update the addon Classic"). The verb is still the user's, `--dry-run` shows the scope, and one `undo` reverts it.
- **clap error kinds.** The hooks depend on clap reporting a misplaced word as `InvalidSubcommand` (subcommand slot) or `UnknownArgument` (an extra positional). A clap upgrade that changes either fails the unit tables first.
- **Performance.** The extra work happens only on the error path: one vocabulary build (microseconds, plus at most 1 MiB of `registry.json`), one catalog parse for a word that classifies, and a few `command_path`/`parses` calls, which already rebuild the clap tree.
- **Privacy.** The error echoes only the user's own word.
- **Previews bind (common rule 16):** no mutating path is added.

## Dependencies

- Parent: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.1 (Misplaced clients before and after the verb).
- Before it: part 1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.1.1`), for `TargetVocabulary`, `classify`, `from_env`, `builtin`, `empty` and `selects_client`.
- After it: part 3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.1.3`), the contract rows and in-process sweeps, and part 4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.1.4`), the end-to-end suite. Both test this part's behaviour through the binary and run in parallel.

title: Tests: contract rows and sweeps for misplaced-client fixes
description:
Part 3 of 4 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.1 (Misplaced clients before and after the verb). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

C1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.1`) makes a client named where a command or an argument belongs (`omaddons retail update`, `omaddons status era`, `omaddons info dbm era`) a `usage` error whose fix is the user's own command with the client moved into `-t` (M4-D12 hooks 1 and 2; goal G-M4-2; checkpoint criterion 5). Part 2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.1.2`) built the hooks. This part extends the contract suite's usage-fix tests (`tests/contract/usage_fixes.rs`) to them, as C1's plan entry asks ("extend `usage_fixes.rs`'s existing parse checks to the new fixes"; "Contract `usage_fixes` rows").

It adds four things. A table of misplaced-client rows, each run through the real binary and the contract's `check()`. A table of words that must keep today's fix. An in-process sweep over every built-in client word and every command path. Two envelope snapshots. It is its own step because these suites test the behaviour across every word and command at once (cross-cutting property tests), separately from part 2's unit tables. It touches only `tests/contract/`, so it runs in parallel with part 4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.1.4`).

**What the hooks promise, restated (the properties tested here):**
- **Hook 1** (clap's `InvalidSubcommand(w)`, `w` a client word): the fix is the argv minus `w`, with `-t w` at the end (before `--` when there is one), and the message is `'<w>' is a client, not a command; the client goes in -t`. It also applies at nested levels (`backup retail list` → `backup list -t retail`) and on parents that run bare (`backup retail` → `backup -t retail`).
- **Hook 2** (clap's `UnknownArgument(tok)`, `tok` a non-dash client word): the fix replaces `tok` with `-t tok` in place. The message is `'<w>' is a client, not an argument of <command>; the client goes in -t`.
- Both give `details {target: <word as typed>, command: <canonical command path>}`, one alternative `omaddons help <command>`, `retryable: false`, exit 2, and the in-process marker `UsageFix::UserVerb`. Each fix parses, and keeps the user's command path (exempt from "never guess a mutating command", vision comment 660, because the verb is the user's).
- No fix is given when the word is not a client, when the command's first word is in `vocabulary::CLIENT_FREE` (`help`, `config`, `targets`, `net-log`, `auth`, `omarchy`, `copy`: they never read `-t`, or refuse it), when the argv already names a target, when the word is also a catalog name or alias (the addon wins, risk 12), or when the corrected argv would not parse. In each case the error is exactly what it was before C1. That equals `usage_error_with` called with `TargetVocabulary::empty()`, the oracle used below.

**Facts this part relies on** (as of `c0ab5e9`, plus part 2's API):
- `tests/contract/usage_fixes.rs`: `never_another_mutating_command(argv, typed, ctx)` (`:13-23`), `suggestions(envelope)` (`:26-39`), `owned` (`:41-43`), the `CORPUS`, `VALUE_TYPOS`, `DECIDED` and `DECIDED_ACTORS` tables (`:47-189`), and the in-process one-edit sweep (`:257-311`). All stay as they are.
- `tests/contract/main.rs`: `support::check(run, code)` (`:114-218`) asserts one envelope, the key order, the registered exit, and that every fix and alternative parses and round-trips through shell words. It also asserts exactly one stderr `error` event. `Scene::new()` (`:366`) is a retail and a Mists Classic client. `Scene::json(args, code)` (`:426`) runs `omaddons <args> --json` and checks it. `s.stable(&envelope)` gives the redacted envelope for `insta::assert_json_snapshot!`. Snapshots live in `tests/contract/snapshots/contract__<module>__<name>.snap`.
- Part 2's API: `omaddons::cli::{usage_error, usage_error_with, command_path, Cli}`, `omaddons::vocabulary::{TargetVocabulary, SELECTS_CLIENT, CLIENT_FREE, selects_client}`, `omaddons::error::UsageFix`, and `Error.usage_fix` and `Error.details` through `Deref`.
- `omaddons::app::COMMANDS` (`src/app/mod.rs:121-165`); `omaddons::resolve::catalog::Catalog::builtin()` and `Entry::{name, aliases}`.
- T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`) provides `tests/common/tlog.rs` (`tlog!()`, `step`, `note`, `json`); the contract suite reaches it through its `#[path = "../common/mod.rs"] mod common;`.

## Technical Approach

All in `tests/contract/usage_fixes.rs`, after the existing tests, with new imports `omaddons::cli::usage_error_with`, `omaddons::vocabulary::{TargetVocabulary, CLIENT_FREE, selects_client}` and `omaddons::error::UsageFix`.

1. **`const MISPLACED: &[(&[&str], &[&str], &str, &str)]`**, rows of (argv after `omaddons`, expected `fix_argv`, `details.target`, `details.command`):
   - `["retail", "update"]` → `["omaddons", "update", "-t", "retail"]`, `retail`, `update`
   - `["era", "status"]` → `["omaddons", "status", "-t", "era"]`, `era`, `status`
   - `["wotlk", "list"]` → `["omaddons", "list", "-t", "wotlk"]`, `wotlk`, `list`
   - `["sod", "install", "questie"]` → `["omaddons", "install", "questie", "-t", "sod"]`, `sod`, `install`
   - `["Retail", "upgrade"]` → `["omaddons", "upgrade", "-t", "Retail"]`, `Retail`, `update`
   - `["--dry-run", "retail", "update"]` → `["omaddons", "--dry-run", "update", "-t", "retail"]`, `retail`, `update`
   - `["retail", "remove", "--", "dbm"]` → `["omaddons", "remove", "-t", "retail", "--", "dbm"]`, `retail`, `remove`
   - `["backup", "retail", "list"]` → `["omaddons", "backup", "list", "-t", "retail"]`, `retail`, `backup list`
   - `["errors", "retail"]` → `["omaddons", "errors", "-t", "retail"]`, `retail`, `errors`
   - `["status", "retail"]` → `["omaddons", "status", "-t", "retail"]`, `retail`, `status`
   - `["list", "era"]` → `["omaddons", "list", "-t", "era"]`, `era`, `list`
   - `["outdated", "retail"]` → `["omaddons", "outdated", "-t", "retail"]`, `retail`, `outdated`
   - `["info", "dbm", "era"]` → `["omaddons", "info", "dbm", "-t", "era"]`, `era`, `info`
   - `["pin", "dbm", "retail"]` → `["omaddons", "pin", "dbm", "-t", "retail"]`, `retail`, `pin`
   - `["unpin", "dbm", "retail"]` → `["omaddons", "unpin", "dbm", "-t", "retail"]`, `retail`, `unpin`
   - `["pin", "dbm", "hc", "--version", "12.1.14"]` → `["omaddons", "pin", "dbm", "-t", "hc", "--version", "12.1.14"]`, `hc`, `pin`
2. **`#[test] fn a_misplaced_client_moves_into_dash_t_and_keeps_the_verb()`:** `let s = Scene::new(); let log = tlog!();`. For each row: `log.step(&format!("{argv:?}"))`, then `let c = s.json(argv, 2)` (the full contract check), then `log.json("envelope", &c.envelope)`. Assert, with `c.run.context()` in each message:
   - `error.code == "usage"` and `error.fix_argv == expected`;
   - `error.details == {"target": target, "command": command}`;
   - `error.alternatives` is exactly `[{"display": "omaddons help <command>", "argv": ["omaddons", "help", <command words>…]}]`;
   - `error.message` is `'<target>' is a client, not a command; the client goes in -t` for the rows where the word came before the verb (the first nine), and `'<target>' is a client, not an argument of <command>; the client goes in -t` for the others;
   - `never_another_mutating_command(&fix, Some(command), &ctx)` and `command_path(&fix).join(" ") == command`.

   The envelope's `command` is `"omaddons"` for `retail update` and `"status"` for `status retail` (asserted on those two rows). Two rows are snapshotted with `insta::assert_json_snapshot!`: `"misplaced_client_before_the_verb"` (`retail update`) and `"misplaced_client_after_the_verb"` (`info dbm era`), each of `s.stable(&c.envelope)`. Accept them with `cargo insta review` and read the diff.
3. **`const NOT_MISPLACED: &[&[&str]]`:** `["frobnicate", "update"]`, `["retail"]`, `["retail", "dbm"]`, `["status", "dbm"]`, `["info", "dbm", "questie"]`, `["retail", "update", "-t", "era"]`, `["status", "retail", "--flavor", "era"]`, `["retail", "config"]`, `["retail", "targets"]`, `["retail", "net-log"]`, `["retail", "help"]`, `["retail", "copy", "--from", "era", "--to", "classic"]`, `["config", "retail"]`, `["targets", "retail"]`, `["omarchy", "retail"]`.
4. **`#[test] fn a_word_that_names_no_client_keeps_todays_fix()`:** `Scene` and `tlog!()` as above. For each row:
   - run `s.json(argv, 2)`;
   - compute the oracle in process: `usage_error_with(&err, &full, &TargetVocabulary::empty, &|_| false)`, where `full` is `["omaddons", argv…, "--json"]` and `err = Cli::try_parse_from(&full).unwrap_err()`;
   - assert that the envelope's `fix_argv`, `alternatives` and `message` equal the oracle's, that `details` is `{}`, and that the in-process `usage_error(&err, &full)` has `usage_fix == UsageFix::Guess`.
5. **`#[test] fn every_client_word_before_or_after_a_command_gets_a_fix_that_keeps_the_verb()`**, in process (no binary, so fast; it uses the built-in vocabulary, as `usage_error` does). The helper `fn hook(argv) -> (Error, Error)` returns `(usage_error(&e, argv), usage_error_with(&e, argv, &TargetVocabulary::empty, &|_| false))`.
   - **Every word:** for each `(spelling, _)` in `TargetVocabulary::builtin().words()`, `[omaddons, spelling, update]` must give `UserVerb` with fix `[omaddons, update, -t, spelling]`, and `[omaddons, status, spelling]` must give `UserVerb` with fix `[omaddons, status, -t, spelling]`. Each must have `details.target == spelling` and parse (`support::parses`).
   - **Every command:** for each `entry` of `app::COMMANDS`, with `path = entry.name.split(' ')`, build `[omaddons, retail, path…]` (hook 1's shape) and `[omaddons, path…, retail]` (hook 2's shape). Skip an argv that parses, because those positionals belong to the command (C2's preflight covers `install`, `update` and `remove`). For the others, let `(e, o) = hook(argv)`:
     - if `e.usage_fix == UserVerb`: `selects_client(&path)` holds, the fix parses, `command_path(fix).join(" ") == e.details["command"]`, the fix holds `-t` followed by `retail`, `never_another_mutating_command(fix, Some(&e.details["command"]))` holds, and every token of the failing argv except `retail` appears in the fix in the same order;
     - otherwise `e == o` (today's error, exactly);
     - when `path[0]` is in `CLIENT_FREE`, `e.usage_fix` is `Guess`;
     - when `path[0]` is in `SELECTS_CLIENT`, the argv has hook 1's shape, and `[omaddons, path…, -t, retail]` parses, `e.usage_fix` is `UserVerb` (no silent miss).
   - Assertion messages name the argv, both errors' fix argv, `details` and `usage_fix`. The test also asserts that it produced at least one `UserVerb` per runnable `SELECTS_CLIENT` path that parses with `-t retail` alone (`status`, `list`, `outdated`, `update`, `export`, `history`, `errors`, `backup`, `backup list`, and so on), so the sweep cannot pass vacuously.
6. **`#[test] fn a_catalog_name_that_is_a_client_word_is_never_moved()`**, in process: for each name and alias of `Catalog::builtin()`'s entries that `TargetVocabulary::builtin().classify` recognises, `usage_error` of `[omaddons, <it>, update]` and of `[omaddons, status, <it>]` equals the empty-vocabulary oracle. It prints the number of such words to stderr as a `note` line (0 at `c0ab5e9`). It guards the addon-wins rule for the day a catalog entry is named like a mode (an addon called `Hardcore` exists). Part 2's unit test proves the rule with a planted predicate.
7. **Once A3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`) has landed**, `check()` also validates each envelope's `details` against `usage`'s `DetailSpec` (which part 2 extended if A9 had landed). Nothing extra is needed here.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `MISPLACED` (16 rows) passes through `Scene::json` and `check()`, with the exact `fix_argv`, `details`, message and alternative per row.
- [ ] `NOT_MISPLACED` (15 rows) passes: each envelope's fix, alternatives and message equal the empty-vocabulary oracle, and `details` is `{}`.
- [ ] The in-process sweep passes for every built-in word (hooks 1 and 2) and every `app::COMMANDS` path, with no silent miss on a client-selecting path, never a `UserVerb` fix on a `CLIENT_FREE` path, and never a different mutating command.
- [ ] The catalog guard passes and reports its count.
- [ ] Snapshots `contract__usage_fixes__misplaced_client_before_the_verb.snap` and `contract__usage_fixes__misplaced_client_after_the_verb.snap` exist and were reviewed.
- [ ] The existing usage-fix tests pass unchanged.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs tests/contract/usage_fixes.rs` is clean.
- [ ] `br lint` is clean for this subtask.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

None: this part is the contract suite's integration tests.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

`tests/contract/usage_fixes.rs` (run with `cargo test --test contract usage_fixes`): the four tests and two snapshots above. The two `Scene` tests run the real binary once per row on a retail and Mists Classic home. The sweep and the catalog guard run in process, as the existing one-edit sweep does.

### Logging

- The two `Scene` tests open `let log = tlog!();`, call `log.step(&format!("{argv:?}"))` before each row and `log.json("envelope", &c.envelope)` after it, and put `c.run.context()` (argv, exit, stdout, stderr) in every assertion message. On failure, T1's guard prints `test log: <path>` and the last 20 steps.
- The in-process tests run no binary. Each assertion message names the argv and shows the expected and actual `fix_argv`, `details` and `usage_fix` of both the hooked error and the oracle.

## Considerations

- **Hot spot:** `tests/contract/usage_fixes.rs` is shared with C2 and C3, which add their own rows after this part. Append, and keep the existing tables untouched.
- **Snapshots:** two new files, one per row, so conflicts are rare. Review each with `cargo insta review` before accepting.
- **Speed:** the sweep calls `usage_error` about 300 times, each building the clap tree a few times. That is comparable to the existing one-edit sweep, which checks more than 100 typos, and well within the gate.
- **The oracle.** "Keeps today's fix" is defined as "equals the error computed with no vocabulary". That holds by construction, because the hooks are the only code that reads the vocabulary. Hand-written expected values would drift with later typo-fix work.
- **No corpus rows here.** C4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4`) lands after C1 and adds the misplaced-client rows to `tests/contract/intent_corpus.rs`, where each fix is also run (M4-D15).

## Dependencies

- Parent: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.1 (Misplaced clients before and after the verb).
- Before it: part 2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.1.2`), which provides the hooks, `usage_error_with` and `UsageFix`. T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs) through an edge added at filing.
- Beside it: part 4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.1.4`), the end-to-end suite, in another file, with no order between them.

**Done (part 3 of C1).** Commit `fb36e91`: `tests/contract/usage_fixes.rs` (appended; existing tables untouched), two new snapshots, and the crate doc marker in `tests/contract/main.rs`.

**What was added.**
- **`MISPLACED`** (16 rows, as specified) and `a_misplaced_client_moves_into_dash_t_and_keeps_the_verb`. Each row goes through the binary and `support::check`, and is asserted for: `usage`, `retryable: false`, the exact `fix_argv`, `details {target, command}`, exactly one alternative `omaddons help <command>`, the slot's message, `never_another_mutating_command`, and `command_path(fix) == command`. The envelope `command` is checked on `retail update` (`omaddons`) and `status retail` (`status`). Snapshots: `contract__usage_fixes__misplaced_client_before_the_verb.snap` (`retail update`) and `…_after_the_verb.snap` (`info dbm era`), both read before accepting; they match the milestone transcript's alternative exactly.
- **`NOT_MISPLACED`** (15 rows) and `a_word_that_names_no_client_keeps_todays_fix`. The envelope's `fix_argv`, `alternatives` and `message` equal the serialized `usage_error_with(.., TargetVocabulary::empty, ..)` oracle, `details` is `{}`, and in process `usage_fix` is `Guess`.
- **`every_client_word_before_or_after_a_command_gets_a_fix_that_keeps_the_verb`** (in process).
  - Every built-in word is moved, both as `<w> update` and as `status <w>`, with the exact fix, `details.target` and a parse check; more than 50 words are asserted.
  - Every `app::COMMANDS` path with `retail` before and after it is either `UserVerb` or exactly equal to the oracle. A `UserVerb` fix must be on a selecting path, must parse, has `command_path == details.command`, contains `-t retail`, never names another mutating command, and keeps every other token in order.
  - A `CLIENT_FREE` path is always `Guess`, and there is no silent miss on a selecting path that runs with `-t retail` alone.
  - The set moved before the verb equals the set runnable with `-t retail`, and contains status, list, outdated, update, export, history, errors, backup and backup list.
- **`a_catalog_name_that_is_a_client_word_is_never_moved`**: the count goes to the test log as a `note` (0 today), and each such word must equal the oracle.

**Decided while implementing.**
- **The `--` row:** `Scene::json` appends `--json`, which after `--` would be a positional. `run_json` inserts it before the `--` instead and calls `support::check` itself.
- **The message:** a `Slot { Command, Argument }` field on each row chooses it, rather than "the first nine rows", so C2 and C3 can append rows in any order. The row type is the `Misplaced` alias, because clippy's `type_complexity` rejects the inline tuple.
- **The word sweep** skips a word that a catalog entry answers to (the addon wins). None does today, and the catalog guard covers those words.
- **The count** is logged with `log.note`, not printed: `print_stderr` is denied.
- **The e2e marker:** `tlog!` in the contract crate requires `//! e2e suite:` on `tests/contract/main.rs` (`tlog_selftest`'s convention), so `argc e2e` now also runs the contract suite.

title: E2E: registered ids, registry fallbacks, and a usage path that scans and writes nothing
description:
Part 4 of 4 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.1 (Misplaced clients before and after the verb). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

C1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.1`) makes a client named where a command or an argument belongs a `usage` error whose fix is the user's own command with the client moved into `-t` (M4-D12 hooks 1 and 2; goal G-M4-2, "the first guess works"; checkpoint criterion 5). Part 1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.1.1`) built the vocabulary from the built-in rules and `registry.json`'s ids. Part 2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.1.2`) built the hooks. This part proves, end to end through the real binary, the promises that only show across several commands and on real state:
- the wrong invocation changes nothing (common rule 8: a usage error found from the arguments is raised before planning, recovery or any commit);
- the corrected command runs;
- a registered custom id is a client word, and becomes one only once registered;
- every unusable `registry.json` falls back to the built-in words without blocking or changing the file (C1's acceptance: "a missing or unreadable `registry.json` falls back to the built-in vocabulary");
- the usage path makes no scan and reads no discovery state (C1's acceptance: "the usage path makes no scan (test: `HOME` without `Games/` and with a poisoned discovery cache)"; M4-D12 rejected "running discovery in the usage path: a scan for a usage error, and usage errors must be fast and side-effect free").

It is its own step because these scenarios run five to fifteen commands each against one home and compare tree hashes, which is T1's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`) logged end-to-end form. It touches only a new test file, so it runs in parallel with part 3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.1.3`).

**What is asserted, restated from parts 1 and 2:**
- Hook 1 (a client before the verb): `omaddons retail update` → `usage`, exit 2, message `'retail' is a client, not a command; the client goes in -t`, `fix_argv` `["omaddons","update","-t","retail"]`, alternative `omaddons help update`, `details {"target":"retail","command":"update"}`.
- Hook 2 (a client after the verb): `omaddons status retail` → `fix_argv` `["omaddons","status","-t","retail"]`, message `'retail' is a client, not an argument of status; the client goes in -t`, the same `details` shape.
- The vocabulary: built-in default ids (`retail`, `era`, `wotlk` …), product codes, flavor folders, game modes and aliases, and family names, plus `<state>/registry.json`'s ids. The registry is read through `crate::discover::read_bytes`: at most `DISCOVERY_FILE_MAX_BYTES` (1 MiB), regular files only, so a FIFO never blocks. It is decoded with `store::load_bytes`. A missing, unparsable, non-regular, unreadable, oversized or newer-version registry contributes no ids, and nothing reports it.
- Today's fixes (observed at `c0ab5e9`) that must stay: `omaddons frobnicate update` → `omaddons help`; `omaddons retail` → `omaddons help`; `omaddons status dbm` → `omaddons help status`; `omaddons info dbm questie` → `omaddons help info`; `omaddons retail update -t era` → `omaddons help`; `omaddons retail config` → `omaddons help`; `omaddons retail copy --from era --to classic` → `omaddons help`; `omaddons config retail` → `omaddons help config`; `omaddons targets retail` → `omaddons help targets`. In each, `details` is `{}`.

**Facts this part relies on** (as of `c0ab5e9`):
- `common::home::Home::new(products)` (`tests/common/home.rs:27-50`) builds a Battle.net root with the named products in a Wine prefix under `<home>/Games/battlenet` (`Prefix::new`, `tests/common/trees.rs:90-92`). `Home::new(&["wow", "wow_classic_era", "wow_classic"])` gives the clients `retail`, `era` and `classic`.
- `common::env::TestEnv::new()` (`tests/common/env.rs:31-54`) lays out `home/.local/share`, `config`, `state`, `cache` and `no-proc` under one tempdir, with no `Games/`. `home.state()` is `<state>`. `<cache>` is `env.cache().join("omaddons")`. `env.command()` (`:97-108`) is an `assert_cmd::Command` with the environment applied, so `.timeout(…)` works on it.
- `common::trees::CustomRoot::at(path).build()` (`tests/common/trees.rs:346-433`) writes a custom (3.3.5a) client. `omaddons targets add <path> --name <id>` registers it.
- `common::trees::tree_hash(dir)` (`:439`) reads every entry that is neither a directory nor a symlink with `fs::read`, so it blocks on a FIFO. `tree_stat(dir)` (`:480`) only stats.
- `common::privacy::assert_private_all(stdout, stderr)` (`tests/common/privacy.rs:40`); `common::procfs::running_as_root()` (`tests/common/procfs.rs:10`).
- `mkfifo` is how the suite makes a FIFO (`tests/toc_loaded.rs:60`, `std::process::Command::new("mkfifo")`); test code may spawn processes.
- `omaddons::limits::DISCOVERY_FILE_MAX_BYTES` is `1 << 20` (`src/limits.rs:65`).
- T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`): `tlog!()`; `log.step`, `log.note`, `log.json`; `log.run(&env, &argv) -> Ran` with `ok()`, `exit(n)`, `envelope()`, `data()`, `error_code()`, `warnings()` and `commands()`; `log.tree(label, root)` and `log.assert_unchanged(label, root)`. `argc e2e [FILTER]` runs `tests/e2e_*.rs` with `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG=verbose`.

## Technical Approach

A new suite, **`tests/e2e_misplaced_clients.rs`** (`mod common;`). **Decided while writing this bead:** the name starts with `e2e_`, so T1's `argc e2e` runner picks it up (`argc e2e misplaced`). Every command runs with `--json --progress json`, and every run's stdout and stderr go through `assert_private_all`. Two helpers keep the scenarios short:
- `fn wrong(log, env, args, fix, target, command, before_verb: bool)`: `log.run` the argv. Then assert exit 2, `error_code() == "usage"`, the exact `fix_argv`, `details == {target, command}`, one alternative `["omaddons", "help", <command words>]`, the hook 1 or hook 2 message, and exactly one stderr `error` event whose `fix_argv` equals the envelope's.
- `fn baseline(log, env)` / `fn unchanged(log, env)`: `log.tree` / `log.assert_unchanged` for `<state>` (`env.state()`), `<config>` (`env.config()`), `<cache>` (`env.cache()`) and `HOME` (`env.home()`, which holds the clients).

### Scenario 1: `misplaced_clients_before_the_verb_change_nothing_and_their_fixes_run`

1. `step("home")`: `Home::new(&["wow", "wow_classic_era", "wow_classic"])`; `baseline`.
2. `step("wrong invocations")`: `wrong` for:
   - `retail update` → `omaddons update -t retail` (`update`);
   - `era status` → `omaddons status -t era` (`status`);
   - `retail list` → `omaddons list -t retail` (`list`);
   - `sod install questie` → `omaddons install questie -t sod` (`install`);
   - `wotlk list` → `omaddons list -t wotlk` (`list`; the vocabulary knows `wotlk` though this home has no such client);
   - `backup retail list` → `omaddons backup list -t retail` (`backup list`);
   - `errors era` → `omaddons errors -t era` (`errors`).
3. `step("nothing changed")`: `unchanged`.
4. `step("the fixes run")`: `log.run` `status -t era` → `exit(0)`; `log.run` `list -t retail` → `exit(0)`. These are read-only fixes. C4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4`) runs every corpus fix on its own home.

### Scenario 2: `misplaced_clients_after_the_verb_change_nothing_and_their_fixes_run`

The same home and steps, with `wrong` (hook 2 messages) for: `status retail` → `omaddons status -t retail`; `list era` → `omaddons list -t era`; `outdated retail` → `omaddons outdated -t retail`; `history retail` → `omaddons history -t retail`; `export retail` → `omaddons export -t retail`; `info dbm era` → `omaddons info dbm -t era`; `pin dbm retail` → `omaddons pin dbm -t retail`; `unpin dbm retail` → `omaddons unpin dbm -t retail`. Then `unchanged`, then `log.run` `status -t retail` → `exit(0)` and `list -t era` → `exit(0)`.

### Scenario 3: `words_that_name_no_client_keep_todays_fix`

The same home. For each argv in the table of today's fixes above: `log.run`, then assert exit 2, `usage`, the exact `fix_argv` listed, `details == {}`, and a message starting with `unrecognized subcommand` (subcommand slot) or `unexpected argument` (argument slot). Then `unchanged`.

### Scenario 4: `a_registered_custom_id_is_a_client_word`

1. `step("home")`: `Home::new(&["wow"])`, and a custom client built with `CustomRoot::at(env.root().join("clients/turtle")).build()` (outside `Games/`).
2. `step("before registration")`: `turtle list` → exit 2, `fix_argv` `["omaddons","help"]`, `details == {}`. The word is no client yet: the usage path reads only `registry.json`, which does not exist.
3. `step("register")`: `log.run` `targets add <client path> --name turtle` → `exit(0)`; `baseline`.
4. `step("registered")`: `wrong` for `turtle list` → `omaddons list -t turtle` (`list`), `status turtle` → `omaddons status -t turtle` (`status`, hook 2), and `TURTLE update` → `omaddons update -t TURTLE` (`update`, `details.target` `TURTLE`); then `unchanged`.
5. `step("the fix runs")`: `log.run` `list -t turtle` → `exit(0)`.

### Scenario 5: `an_unusable_registry_falls_back_to_the_builtin_words`

1. Steps 1–3 of scenario 4. Then `let good = fs::read(<state>/registry.json)`.
2. For each variant, `step(<variant>)`. Put the variant in place (test code writes it), `log.note` what it is, and run `turtle list` (expect today's fix, `["omaddons","help"]`, `details == {}`) and `retail update` (expect `["omaddons","update","-t","retail"]`). Then assert that the variant is still there, unchanged, and restore `good`. The variants:
   - `missing`: the file removed;
   - `unparsable`: `{ not json`;
   - `directory`: a directory at the path;
   - `unreadable`: `good` with mode `0o000`. When `running_as_root()`, this variant is skipped with `log.note("unreadable: skipped, root reads mode 000 files")`;
   - `oversized`: `good` followed by spaces up to `DISCOVERY_FILE_MAX_BYTES + 1` bytes in all. It would still decode, so only the bound rejects it;
   - `fifo`: `mkfifo <path>`. A failed `mkfifo` fails the test with "mkfifo is required (coreutils)". Both runs use `env.command().args(…).timeout(Duration::from_secs(10))` directly, recorded with `log.json`, because a run that opened the FIFO would block;
   - `newer`: `good` with `"schema_version"` set to `"9.0"`. It decodes, and is ignored by decision (part 1).

   "Unchanged" means: the same bytes for a file, still a directory or FIFO for those, still mode `0o000` for `unreadable`, still absent for `missing`.
3. `step("restored")`: with `good` back, `turtle list` → `omaddons list -t turtle` again.

### Scenario 6: `the_usage_path_reads_no_discovery_and_writes_nothing`

1. `step("home")`: `TestEnv::new()` alone: `HOME` has no `Games/`, no client and no registry. `mkfifo <cache>/discovery.json` (after creating `<cache>`). Any reader that opens it blocks, so a run that touched discovery state would hang. `log.tree` for `<state>`, `<config>` and `HOME`. For `<cache>`: `log.json("cache before", &tree_stat(<cache>))` (not `log.tree`, which would read the FIFO).
2. `step("wrong invocations")`: each with `env.command().args([…, "--json", "--progress", "json"]).timeout(Duration::from_secs(10))`, recorded with `log.json("run", {argv, exit, stdout, stderr})`:
   - `retail update` → exit 2, `fix_argv` `["omaddons","update","-t","retail"]`;
   - `status era` → exit 2, `["omaddons","status","-t","era"]`;
   - `sod install questie` → exit 2, `["omaddons","install","questie","-t","sod"]`.

   A timeout fails with "the usage path opened <cache>/discovery.json (a FIFO): it must read no discovery state". The built-in words work with nothing discoverable on the machine.
3. `step("nothing changed")`: `log.assert_unchanged` for `<state>`, `<config>` and `HOME` (no `Games/` created, no registry written). `tree_stat(<cache>)` equals the "cache before" listing: the FIFO is still a FIFO, and nothing was added. `log.note` each run's `meta.elapsed_ms`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `tests/e2e_misplaced_clients.rs` holds the six scenarios, each a `TestLog` scenario, all passing in the gate.
- [ ] Every wrong invocation exits 2 with the exact `fix_argv`, `details`, message and alternative, and one stderr `error` event, and leaves `<state>`, `<config>`, `<cache>` and `HOME` hash-identical.
- [ ] The read-only fixes (`status -t era`, `list -t retail`, `status -t retail`, `list -t era`, `list -t turtle`) run with exit 0.
- [ ] `turtle` is a client word after `targets add … --name turtle` and not before.
- [ ] Every registry variant (missing, unparsable, directory, unreadable, oversized, FIFO, newer) falls back to the built-in words, never blocks, and is left as it was.
- [ ] With no `Games/` and a FIFO at `<cache>/discovery.json`, the fixes arrive within 10 seconds, and nothing under `<state>`, `<config>`, `<cache>` or `HOME` changes.
- [ ] `assert_private_all` passes on every run.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs tests/e2e_misplaced_clients.rs` is clean; `argc e2e misplaced` runs the suite with verbose logs.
- [ ] `br lint` is clean for this subtask.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

None: this part is an end-to-end suite.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

`tests/e2e_misplaced_clients.rs`, the six scenarios above (run with `cargo test --test e2e_misplaced_clients`, or `argc e2e misplaced`). Homes: `Home::new` with three, then one, Battle.net client; a `CustomRoot` registered as `turtle`; a bare `TestEnv` for the no-scan scenario. No HTTP fixture is needed: no fix that is run here makes a request.

### Logging

- Each scenario opens `let log = tlog!();`. Each phase is a `log.step`: `home`, `wrong invocations`, `nothing changed`, `the fixes run`, `before registration`, `register`, `registered`, one step per registry variant, `restored`.
- Every command goes through `log.run`, which records the argv, env overrides, exit, envelope, stderr events and elapsed time. The exceptions are the runs with a timeout (the FIFO cases), recorded with `log.json` with the same fields.
- Trees: `log.tree` / `log.assert_unchanged` for `<state>`, `<config>`, `<cache>` and `HOME`. In scenario 6, `<cache>` is recorded with `tree_stat` through `log.json`, and a difference logs both listings.
- On failure, the guard prints `test log: <path>` and the last 20 steps. `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG=verbose cargo test --test e2e_misplaced_clients -- --nocapture` echoes every step live.

## Considerations

- **Why the FIFO.** A test cannot observe a read that did not happen. A FIFO turns any open of the discovery cache into a hang that the 10-second timeout reports by name, so "reads no discovery state" becomes checkable. The registry FIFO variant checks the opposite: the one file the usage path does read is opened only after its type is checked (`read_bytes` uses `open_regular`).
- **Why no `Games/`.** With nothing discoverable, a fix proves the built-in words do the work, and an absent `Games/` afterwards proves nothing was created.
- **Exit codes of the fixes.** Only read-only fixes on clients this home has are run here. The others (`install questie -t sod`, `update -t retail`) need HTTP fixtures or managed addons, so C4's corpus runs them on `intent_home()` with its documented exits.
- **Root.** The mode-000 variant cannot fail a read as root. It is skipped with a logged note, and the other six variants still run.
- **Cost.** About 60 short runs of the debug binary in all. A usage error does no I/O beyond one bounded read, so the suite takes seconds.

## Dependencies

- Parent: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.1 (Misplaced clients before and after the verb).
- Before it: part 2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.1.2`), which provides the behaviour under test, and T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, `tests/common/tlog.rs` and `argc e2e`), through an edge added at filing.
- Beside it: part 3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.1.3`), the contract rows, in another file, with no order between them.

title: A client named as an addon, and `-t all`
description:
## How to work this bead

This bead is worked through its 5 subtasks, listed below in work order. Claim a subtask, not this bead (`br ready --parent omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.2` lists the ready ones). The agent that closes the last open subtask then verifies every acceptance criterion of this bead (they are the leaf's, not any one subtask's), and closes this bead with `br close omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.2 --reason "done: <evidence> · found: <ids>"`. Until this bead is closed, every bead it blocks stays blocked.

1. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.2.1 The misplaced-client preflight in `install`, `update` and `remove`: hook 3 (`resolve_args::misplaced_clients`), its two `cli` helpers, the three call sites, README, and their unit tests.
2. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.2.2 `-t all`, the reserved id `all` and the `target_id_reserved` warning: the keyword in `discover::registry::resolve`, `World::select_many` and `World::selects_all`, `id_problem`, the warning row, `update -t all`'s human line, the `-t` help text, README, and their unit tests. Independent of part 1.
3. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.2.3 Tests: contract rows for the misplaced-client preflight and `-t all`: `tests/contract/usage_fixes.rs` and `tests/contract/matrix.rs` rows with snapshots. Needs parts 1 and 2.
4. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.2.4 E2E: a misplaced client among the addons changes nothing: scenarios appended to `tests/e2e_misplaced_clients.rs`. Needs part 1.
5. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.2.5 E2E: `-t all` across commands, the reserved id and the warning: `tests/target_selection.rs` extended. Needs part 2.

The leaf is size M and closes as one unit: no bead it blocks starts on half of it. The subtasks split the work into commits that each pass `argc gate` on their own.

## Background

**What this is.** Two pieces of M4's intent inference (area C), both about where a client name goes:

1. **A client named as an addon** (M4-D12, hook 3). `install`, `update` and `remove` take several names, so clap accepts `omaddons update retail` and `omaddons remove dbm retail`, and the word `retail` reaches the command as an addon name. This bead makes each such invocation a `usage` error (exit 2) whose fix is the user's own command with the client moved into `-t` (`omaddons remove dbm -t retail`), raised **before planning, recovery or any commit**, so the wrong invocation changes nothing.
2. **`-t all`** (M4-D13). Agents guess `-t all`. Today it is `target_not_found`. This bead makes it select every target on commands that take several, and `target_ambiguous` (one fix per client) on commands that must land on one. `all` becomes an id that `targets add --name` and `targets rename` refuse, and a target already named `all` keeps working by id, wins over the keyword, and draws the new warning `target_id_reserved` naming `targets rename`.

C1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.1`, misplaced clients before and after the verb) built the vocabulary and hooks 1 and 2 (`omaddons retail update`, `omaddons status era`). This bead is the third hook and the keyword. C4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4`, the run-the-fix corpus) then runs every misplaced-client fix on a synthetic home.

**Why hook 3 must be a preflight.** `remove` resolves every positional, commits the names it recognized on the one target they agree on, and only then turns the others into warnings (`src/app/remove.rs:163-321`: the engine runs at `:254-258`, the unknown names become warnings at `:273-280`). Without `-t` it searches every managed target (`:167-180`). So today `omaddons remove dbm retail`, on a home where DBM is managed only on `era`, removes DBM from `era` and then warns that `retail` is not managed. Running the "corrected" `omaddons remove dbm -t retail` afterwards would not undo that. The check therefore runs before anything else in the command, and a recognized misplaced client invalidates the whole invocation. `update` is the same shape: `omaddons update dbm retail` updates DBM on every client and reports `retail` as a failed item; `omaddons update retail` alone even reaches `recover_waiting` (a write, `src/app/update.rs:312-314`) before failing `not_managed`. `install questie era` (no `-t`) installs Questie on whichever client `install` chooses and fails `era` as a name.

**The milestone goals it serves.**
- **G-M4-2, "the first guess works":** a plausible wrong invocation yields a usage error whose fix is the command the user meant. That covers a misplaced client name, a typo of a command, flag, value or client id, `-t all`, and `apply` vs `adopt --apply`. Each fix is proven to run, not only to parse (C4). A fix never turns the user's verb into a different command that changes something.
- **G-M4-6, "no new risk to the engine's guarantees":** a wrong invocation must not commit anything; this bead closes the one path where today it does (a misplaced client among several names).

**The checkpoint criterion it serves.** Criterion 5, "Intent inference": a corpus of at least 60 wrong invocations covers misplaced client names before and after the verb, **a client name given as an addon**, **`-t all`**, client-id typos, command, flag and value typos, `apply` for `adopt --apply`, and doctor verb typos. Each yields its documented error with a `fix_argv` that parses and runs on the corpus home to its documented exit code. No fix turns the user's verb into a different command that changes something. **A misplaced-client invocation changes nothing at all: records and client trees hash identical before and after it, including `remove dbm retail` and `update dbm retail` with DBM also installed on a client other than the misplaced one,** and the corrected argv runs on an independent copy of the original home. This bead delivers the bold parts; C4 runs the corpus. Slice 1's exit demo includes "`remove dbm retail` changes nothing" (T2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.2`, records it as a test).

**How it serves the vision.** Vision goal G4, agent ergonomics: "the first command an agent guesses works". Vision §5.10 promises that "misplaced target names are recognized" (its example: `omaddons retail update` gives `fix: omaddons update -t retail`), and M4 extends that promise to a client named among the addons. The vision's thesis that omaddons stays the sole, safe, undoable authority over what it manages is why hook 3 is a refusal before anything runs, not a best effort after a commit.

**The decisions that shape it.**
- **M4-D12, misplaced client names are recognised before the verb, after it, and as an addon.** Three hooks over one `TargetVocabulary` (C1 built it: the built-in rules table's product default ids, product codes, flavor folders, game modes and aliases, family names, plus `registry.json`'s ids). Hook 3, this bead's: `install`, `update` and `remove` take several names. Before planning, recovery or any commit, each classifies every positional. A word that names a client and matches no installed addon, catalog entry, alias, ref form or path rejects the whole invocation with `usage`, `details {target, command}` and `fix_argv` moving it into `-t`, exactly as hooks 1 and 2 do (`omaddons update retail` → `omaddons update -t retail`; `omaddons remove dbm retail` → `omaddons remove dbm -t retail`). `pin`, `unpin` and `info` take one name, so their extra word is hook 2's (C1).
  - It must be a preflight: see "Why hook 3 must be a preflight" above.
  - Ordinary partial success is unchanged: a name that is simply not found (`remove dbm nosuch -t retail`) still fails alone while the others proceed. Only a recognized misplaced client invalidates the whole invocation.
  - The addon wins: a word that is both a client and an addon or catalog entry is never moved (risk 12).
  - **The verb exemption.** These fixes keep the user's own verb, so they are exempt from "never guess a mutating command" (vision comment 660). That rule stops a typo turning into another verb; here the verb is the user's and only the client moves. The fixes are marked `UsageFix::UserVerb` (C1's marker). They must still parse.
  - Rejected: (i) running discovery in the usage path (a scan for a usage error); (ii) accepting the misplaced form silently (commands must have one shape, or agents learn two). Hook 3 runs inside the command, after the world is loaded, because only there are the installed addons and the catalog known; it adds no scan of its own.
- **M4-D13, `-t all` selects every client where a command takes several, and `all` becomes a reserved id.**
  - `-t all` (any case) selects every registered target for the commands that accept several (`status`, `list`, `info`, `outdated`, `update`, `export`, `sync`, `adopt`, `pin`, `unpin`, `search`, `backup`, `errors`, `doctor`). For most of them that equals omitting `-t`. "All" means all: test clients are included, and `update`'s human output says how many of the clients are test clients ("6 clients, including 2 test clients"); the dry run lists them, so the wider selection is never silent.
  - On a command that must land on one client, `-t all` is `target_ambiguous` with one alternative per client.
  - `all` joins the ids `targets add --name` and `targets rename` refuse.
  - An existing registered target already named `all` keeps working by id, wins over the keyword, and gets a one-time `target_id_reserved` warning naming `targets rename`.
  - Why: agents guess `-t all`, and making it mean the obvious thing costs one match arm. Including test clients gives the explicit form a meaning beyond the default, and matches how `-t <family>` already selects that family's test clients.
  - Rejected: (i) making `-t all` a usage error (a needless failure for the obvious guess); (ii) excluding test clients (then `-t all` would mean nothing omitting `-t` does not).
  - Departure from the vision: additions only: one selector keyword, one reserved id, one warning code.
- **Decisions it obeys, restated.**
  - **M4-D10 (typed `details`):** every error code's `details` has a declared, recursive `DetailSpec` (A9, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9`), validated by the contract suite (A3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`). Hook 3 reuses `usage`'s `details.target` and `details.command`, which C1 declares; it adds no key.
  - **M4-D15 (context):** a usage fix must run, not just parse. C4's corpus runs each wrong argv on one copy of `intent_home()` (which must hash unchanged when the row is an error) and its `fix_argv` on an independent copy, asserting the documented exit.
  - **M4-D18 (determinism):** stable order. The keyword's targets are sorted by id, as `World::select_many` already sorts.
  - **M4-D55 (contract rules from slice 1):** the new warning code passes A3's naming rules; nothing is added to `tests/contract/rules_allowlist.txt`.
  - **M4-D22 (context, for common rule 16):** `targets add|rm|rename|default` edit one value whose preview is the command itself, so they neither store nor bind; this bead only adds a refusal to two of them.

**Facts this bead relies on** (as of `c0ab5e9`, each verified in the source):
- C1's surface (it lands first; C2 is blocked by it): `crate::vocabulary::TargetVocabulary` with `new(table, registered_ids)`, `classify(word) -> Option<TargetWord>` (case-insensitive) and `words()`; `UsageFix { Guess, UserVerb }` on `ErrorData` with the builder `Error::user_verb()`; in `src/cli.rs`, `pub(crate) fn with_target_in_place(argv, at) -> Vec<String>` (the token at `at` replaced by `-t <token>`, then `fix_argv`), and the private `misplaced_client_error(message, fix, path, word)` (`usage`, the fix, one alternative `omaddons help <command>`, `details {target: word, command: path.join(" ")}`, `.user_verb()`). C1 decided that `all` is not a client word and left `omaddons all update` to this bead; that `details.target` is the word as typed and `details.command` the canonical command path; and that with a target already given (any spelling of `-t`) the hooks keep today's fix.
- `remove`'s flow: `World::load`, records, then the targets (`-t` → `resolve_one_in`, else every registered target, `src/app/remove.rs:167-180`), then `find` per positional (`:181-188`), the one-target agreement (`:191-211`, several → `target_ambiguous` via `spans`), the engine (`:254-258`), and the unknown names as warnings (`:273-280`). `matches(record, request)` (`:374-386`) matches a record name (any case), a canonical ref or an owned folder's key.
- `update`'s flow: `check_args` (`src/app/update.rs:128`, usage errors from flags alone), `World::load` (`:129`), the catalog (`:133`), `world.select_many(ctx)` (`:135`), records (`:137`), `in_scope` (`:138`, `:493-545`; a name matches a record name or a catalog name or alias whose variants include the record's ref, `world::names_addon`, `src/app/world.rs:312-318`), `Engine::new` (`:151`), `recover_waiting` when nothing changes (`:312-314`), unknown names as failed `not_managed` items (`:365-397`), every selected target listed with or without work (`:401-410`).

- The plan's helper is `resolve_args::misplaced_clients(ctx, world, command, &positionals)`. It also needs the catalog the command loaded and the command's own reading of a name (installed addons on the selected targets for `update` and `remove`, `parse_ref`'s answer for `install`), so the signature gains those two and takes the command from `ctx`.
- The plan speaks of "a registered target" named `all`. A provisional (discovered, never registered) target can be named `all` too (an unknown flavor folder `_all_`), and a registered `all` can be missing (its directory gone). Each of them wins over the keyword, with the warning.
