title: E2E: a misplaced client among the addons changes nothing
description:
Part 4 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.2 (A client named as an addon, and `-t all`). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

C2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.2`) makes a client named among the addons of `install`, `update` or `remove` a `usage` error raised before planning, recovery or any commit (M4-D12 hook 3, built in part 1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.2.1`). The reason it exists: at `c0ab5e9`, `remove` commits the names it recognized on the one target they agree on and only then reports the others (`src/app/remove.rs:254-258`, `:273-280`), and without `-t` it searches every registered target, so `remove dbm retail` with DBM managed only on `era` removes DBM from `era`; `update dbm retail` updates DBM everywhere; `install questie era` installs Questie on a client `install` picks. Checkpoint criterion 5 requires that "a misplaced-client invocation changes nothing at all: records and client trees hash identical before and after it, including `remove dbm retail` and `update dbm retail` with DBM also installed on a client other than the misplaced one", and slice 1's exit demo includes "`remove dbm retail` changes nothing" (T2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.2`). This part proves those promises end to end through the real binary, on real state, with T1's logged scenarios: the wrong invocation changes nothing (trees hashed before and after, `net.log` included), the corrected command does exactly what was meant and touches only the client it names, ordinary partial success is unchanged, and an addon named like a client is never moved. It is its own step because these scenarios run many commands per home with HTTP fixtures, and it touches only a test file, so it runs in parallel with parts 3 and 5.

**What is asserted, restated from part 1:**
- The error: `usage`, exit 2, not retryable, message `'<w>' is a client, not an addon; the client goes in -t` (two words: `'<w1>' and '<w2>' are clients, not addons; the client goes in -t, one per command`), `fix_argv` the argv with the first misplaced word replaced in place by `-t <w>` and any other misplaced word dropped (presentation flags dropped, the alias and every other argument kept), alternatives `omaddons help <command>` then each other word's own move, `details {"target": <word as typed>, "command": <canonical path>}`.
- When the hook stays out: a target is given (`-t`, any spelling): the word fails alone as an unknown name; the word is an installed addon of the selected targets (by name, ref or owned folder for `remove`; by name or catalog variant for `update`), a catalog name or alias (built-in or `<config>/catalog.d`), or (for `install`) anything `parse_ref` resolves; the word comes after `--`; the fix would not parse.

**Facts this part relies on** (as of `c0ab5e9`):
- `tests/e2e_misplaced_clients.rs` is C1's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.1`) suite (`mod common;`, marked for `argc e2e`), with helpers that run `--json --progress json` and check privacy. This part appends a section to it.
- `common::home::Home::new(&["wow", "wow_classic_era"])` (`tests/common/home.rs:27-50`) gives `retail` (12.1.5, interface 120105) and `era` (1.15.9, interface 11509) in one Battle.net root; `home.client("_retail_")`, `home.client("_classic_era_")` are their client dirs, `home.state()` is `<state>`, `home.env.config()` and `home.env.cache()` the config and cache roots.
- `Home::installed_behind(base, (old_tag, old_assets), (new_tag, new_assets), targets)` (`:95-121`) installs `old` of `gh:<owner>/<repo>` on each target id through recorded GitHub fixtures, then serves a scenario where `new` is the latest and ages the release memo a day, so the next `update` asks the source and finds `new`. Assets are `common::http::Asset` = `(file, &[(flavor, interface)], entries)` (`tests/common/http.rs:140`); `gh_release(scenario, base, tag, assets)` (`:144`) serves one release as the latest. Example: `tests/install_multi_flavor.rs:1130-1142`.
- `gh:DeadlyBossMods/DeadlyBossMods` is the built-in catalog's DBM ref (aliases `deadlybossmods`, `dbm-core`), so an install of it is recorded as `DBM`. `gh:Questie/Questie` is the catalog's Questie (folders `Questie`, `QuestieDB`).
- `common::state::record(home, id)` (`tests/common/state.rs:27`) reads a target's committed record; `common::netlog::net_log(home)` (`tests/common/netlog.rs:15`) reads `<state>/net.log` (`len()`, `context()`).
- `<config>/catalog.d/*.toml`: `schema_version = "1.0"` and `[[addon]]` tables with `name`, `aliases`, `ref`, `families`, `folders` (README "The built-in catalog"); tests write it at `home.env.config().join("omaddons/catalog.d")`.
- T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`): `tlog!()`; `log.step`, `log.note`, `log.json`; `log.run(&home, &argv) -> Ran` (argv without the binary and used verbatim: pass `--json` yourself) with `Ran::{ok(), exit(n), fails(exit, code), envelope(), data(), warnings(), assert_private()}`; `log.tree(label, root)` and `log.assert_unchanged(label, root)` (tree hashes with modes and symlink targets; the first differing paths logged); `argc e2e [FILTER]`.

## Technical Approach

Append a section `// ---- A client named among the addons (C2, M4-D12 hook 3) ----` to `tests/e2e_misplaced_clients.rs`. Every command runs with `--json --progress json` and goes through `ran.assert_private()`.

Helpers (in this section):
- `fn dbm_home(log, on: &[&str]) -> Home`: `Home::new(&["wow", "wow_classic_era"])`, then `installed_behind("https://github.com/DeadlyBossMods/DeadlyBossMods", ("v1", &old), ("v2", &new), on)`, the release a `DBM-Core/DBM-Core.toc` with `## Interface: 120105, 11509` and `## Version: v1` (`v2`), so it loads on both clients. `log.json("installed", …)` the version of DBM on each client from `record(&home, id)`.
- `fn baseline(log, home)` / `fn unchanged(log, home)`: `log.tree` / `log.assert_unchanged` of `<state>` (which holds the records, the files indexes, `history.jsonl`, the journal directory and `net.log`), `<config>`, `home.client("_retail_")` and `home.client("_classic_era_")`. `<cache>` is not asserted: `World::load` may refresh the derived discovery cache; its listing is recorded with `log.json("cache", …)` for the reader.
- `fn misplaced(log, home, args, fix, target, command, extra_alternatives)`: `log.run` the argv with `--json --progress json`, then `fails(2, "usage")`, the exact `fix_argv`, `details == {target, command}`, alternatives `["omaddons","help",<command words>]` then `extra_alternatives`, the message, `retryable == false`, and exactly one stderr `error` event whose `fix_argv` equals the envelope's.

### Scenario 1: `remove_and_update_with_a_misplaced_client_change_nothing`

1. `step("home")`: `dbm_home(log, &["retail", "era"])`; `baseline`.
2. `step("wrong invocations")`: `misplaced` for:
   - `remove dbm retail` → `omaddons remove dbm -t retail` (`remove`);
   - `rm dbm retail` → `omaddons rm dbm -t retail` (`remove`);
   - `update dbm retail` → `omaddons update dbm -t retail` (`update`);
   - `upgrade dbm retail --dry-run` → `omaddons upgrade dbm -t retail --dry-run` (`update`);
   - `update retail` → `omaddons update -t retail` (`update`);
   - `remove dbm retail --dry-run` → `omaddons remove dbm -t retail --dry-run` (`remove`).
3. `step("nothing changed")`: `unchanged`; `log.json("net.log", …)` and assert `net_log(&home).len()` equals its count at step 1 (no request was sent).
4. `step("the update fix runs")`: `log.run` `update dbm -t retail --json` → `ok()`; `record(&home, "retail")`'s DBM is `v2`, `record(&home, "era")`'s DBM is still `v1`.
5. `step("the remove fix runs")`: `log.run` `remove dbm -t retail --json` → `ok()`; `retail`'s record has no DBM; `era`'s still has DBM `v1`, and `home.client("_classic_era_")/Interface/AddOns/DBM-Core` exists.

### Scenario 2: `a_misplaced_client_never_removes_from_another_client`

The case that commits at `c0ab5e9`.
1. `step("home")`: `dbm_home(log, &["era"])` (DBM only on `era`); `install gh:o/foo --file <zip> -t retail --json` → `ok()` (a zip `Foo/Foo.toc` with `## Interface: 120105`, so `retail` is registered and has an addon of its own); `baseline`.
2. `step("wrong invocation")`: `misplaced` for `remove dbm retail` → `omaddons remove dbm -t retail`.
3. `step("nothing changed")`: `unchanged`; `era`'s record still holds DBM. `log.note("before C2 this removed DBM from era (remove.rs:254-258), then warned that retail is not managed")`.
4. `step("the fix says where DBM is")`: `log.run` `remove dbm -t retail --json` → `fails(3, "not_managed")`; `unchanged` again. The corrected command is honest about the user's mistake, and still changes nothing.

### Scenario 3: `install_with_a_misplaced_client_installs_nothing`

1. `step("home")`: `Home::new(&["wow", "wow_classic_era"])`; serve `gh_release(&home.http, "https://github.com/Questie/Questie", "v1", …)` with `Questie/Questie.toc` (`## Interface: 11509`); `install gh:o/foo --file <zip> -t retail --json` → `ok()`; `baseline`.
2. `step("wrong invocations")`: `misplaced` for `install questie era` → `omaddons install questie -t era` (`install`), and `install questie sod` → `omaddons install questie -t sod` (a mode alias).
3. `step("nothing changed")`: `unchanged`; `net_log(&home).len()` unchanged (the preflight runs before any download).
4. `step("the fix runs")`: `log.run` `install questie -t era --json` → `ok()`; `era`'s record holds Questie; `retail`'s does not.

### Scenario 4: `ordinary_partial_success_is_unchanged`

1. `step("home")`: `dbm_home(log, &["retail", "era"])`; `baseline`.
2. `step("an unknown name fails alone")`: `log.run` `remove dbm nosuch -t retail --json` → `ok()`; `envelope()["partial"] == true`; a warning with code `not_managed` naming `nosuch`; `retail`'s record has no DBM; `era`'s still has it.
3. `step("a target given: the client word fails alone")`: `log.run` `update dbm retail -t era --json` → `ok()` (exit 0, `partial: true`); `era`'s DBM is `v2`; `data.targets` has a failed `not_managed` item whose `request` is `retail`; `retail` (whose DBM was removed in step 2) is untouched.
4. `step("an unknown name with no client word")`: `log.run` `remove nosuch --json` → `fails(3, "not_managed")`; the trees of step 3 unchanged.

### Scenario 5: `an_addon_named_like_a_client_is_never_moved`

1. `step("home")`: `Home::new(&["wow", "wow_classic_era"])`; a catalog file `<config>/omaddons/catalog.d/50-hardcore.toml` with one entry `name = "Hardcore"`, `ref = "gh:o/hardcore"`, `families = ["vanilla"]`, `folders = ["Hardcore"]` (`hardcore` is also a game mode of `era`); `gh_release` for `https://github.com/o/hardcore` (`Hardcore/Hardcore.toc`, `## Interface: 11509`); and `install gh:o/sod --file <zip> -t era --json` → `ok()` for a zip whose folder is `SoD/SoD.toc` (`## Interface: 11509`), an addon owning a folder named like the mode `sod`. `log.json` the records.
2. `step("a catalog name is read as the addon")`: `log.run` `install hardcore -t era --json` → `ok()`; then `log.run` `update hardcore --json` → `ok()` (no `usage`: `hardcore` is the installed catalog addon); `log.run` `update hardcore era --json` → `misplaced` with fix `omaddons update hardcore -t era` (only `era` is moved).
3. `step("an owned folder is read as the addon")`: `log.run` `remove sod --json` → `ok()`, the addon owning `SoD` removed from `era` (no `usage`).
4. `step("a client word after -- is never moved")`: `log.run` `remove hardcore -- era --json`: the hook stays out, `remove` resolves `hardcore` on `era` and reports `era` as unknown (exit 0, `partial: true`), as at `c0ab5e9`.

### Scenario 6: `several_misplaced_clients_move_the_first`

1. `step("home")`: `dbm_home(log, &["retail", "era"])`; `baseline`.
2. `step("wrong invocation")`: `misplaced` for `update dbm retail era` → `omaddons update dbm -t retail`, extra alternative `["omaddons","update","dbm","-t","era"]`, the plural message.
3. `step("a lone client word")`: `log.run` `remove retail --json` → `fails(3, "not_managed")` (the fix `remove -t retail` would not parse, so the command fails as before).
4. `step("nothing changed")`: `unchanged`.

### What this part does not do

No product code changes. C4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4`) builds `common::intent_home()` and the corpus later; these scenarios use their own homes so they can stand before it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The six scenarios pass in the gate (`cargo test --test e2e_misplaced_clients`) and under `argc e2e misplaced`.
- [ ] Scenario 1 shows `<state>` (with `net.log`), `<config>` and both client trees unchanged by six wrong invocations, then `update dbm -t retail` and `remove dbm -t retail` changing `retail` only.
- [ ] Scenario 2 shows DBM still on `era` after `remove dbm retail`.
- [ ] Scenario 3 shows no install and no request from `install questie era`, then the fix installing on `era` only.
- [ ] Scenarios 4–6 show partial success, the addon-wins cases, `--`, several words and a lone client word behaving as specified.
- [ ] Every run's stdout and stderr pass `assert_private_all`.
- [ ] Every scenario logs through `TestLog`, with `log.tree`/`log.assert_unchanged` around each wrong invocation.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs tests/e2e_misplaced_clients.rs` is clean.
- [ ] `br lint` is clean for this subtask.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

None: this part is end-to-end tests only.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

The six scenarios of the Technical Approach in `tests/e2e_misplaced_clients.rs`, each a `#[test]` of its own name, on its own `Home`, with recorded HTTP fixtures (never the network) and no fake `/proc` (nothing runs).

### Logging

- `let log = tlog!();` in each test. Each numbered step is a `log.step`. Every command goes through `log.run` (argv, environment overrides, cwd, `elapsed_ms`, exit, the parsed envelope, the stderr events, the `net.log` lines it added).
- Trees: `log.tree` of `<state>`, `<config>`, `_retail_` and `_classic_era_` before the wrong invocations and `log.assert_unchanged` after; a difference logs the first differing paths, so a write by a wrong invocation is named, not just detected.
- `log.json` records the DBM version on each client before and after each fix, the `net.log` count, and the `<cache>` listing.
- On a failure the guard prints `test log: <path>` and the last 20 steps. `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG=verbose cargo test --test e2e_misplaced_clients -- --nocapture` or `argc e2e misplaced` echoes every step.

## Considerations

- **Why `<cache>` is not asserted:** `World::load` refreshes the derived discovery cache on any command; the promise is about records, client trees and `<state>`, and C4's harness hashes the same set.
- **Fixtures:** `installed_behind` switches scenarios and ages the memo, so the `update` fix finds `v2` without the network; keep both releases loadable on both clients.
- **Scenario 5's `remove hardcore -- era`** documents today's behaviour after `--` (a partial remove); it is deliberate, by C1's and this bead's decision that nothing after `--` is moved.
- **Hot spot:** `tests/e2e_misplaced_clients.rs` is C1's file; this part appends its own section and leaves C1's scenarios as they are.
- **Runtime:** six homes, about 50 commands in all, offline; well within the gate.

## Dependencies

Parent: C2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.2`, a client named as an addon, and `-t all`).

- **Before it:** part 1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.2.1`, hook 3), whose behaviour this tests. T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs), through an edge added at filing.
- **After it:** nothing among the siblings; it runs in parallel with parts 3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.2.3`) and 5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.2.5`).

description:
Part 5 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.2 (A client named as an addon, and `-t all`). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

C2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.2`) makes `-t all` select every client (M4-D13, built in part 2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.2.2`), for goal G-M4-2 ("the first guess works": agents guess `-t all`) and checkpoint criterion 5, whose corpus includes `-t all`. This part proves the behaviour end to end through the real binary, across the commands that read `-t`: every client is selected, test clients included; for most commands that equals omitting `-t`; `update -t all` says how many of the clients are test clients; a command that must land on one client refuses with one runnable fix per client; a target already named `all` wins with one `target_id_reserved` warning; `all` cannot become a new id; a registered client whose directory is gone is listed as without `-t`. The plan's test plan for C2 names exactly this file: "`tests/target_selection.rs` extended". It is its own step because the scenarios run many commands per home, and it touches only that file, so it runs in parallel with parts 3 and 4.

**What is asserted, restated from part 2:**
- `-t all`, in any case and any spelling of the flag (`-t ALL`, `--target=all`, `--flavor all`), selects every target in id order; with no target, the commands that take several select nothing (as without `-t`) and the ones that take one fail `target_not_found` ("-t all selects every client, and none was found on this machine", fix `omaddons targets`, `details {selector}`).
- On `install`, `remove`, `adopt --ref`, `history`, `undo`, `backup restore` and `backup import`, two or more clients give `target_ambiguous`: `details.candidates` every id in id order, the first as `fix_argv`, each other as an alternative; one client is taken.
- `update -t all`'s human output begins `-t all selects N clients, including K test clients (<ids>)` or `…, none of them a test client`; `--json` has no new key and lists every selected target.
- A target whose id is `all` (registered, provisional, or registered with its directory gone) wins over the keyword; the run gets exactly one `target_id_reserved` warning (message `a client has the id "all", so -t all selected that client, not every client`; prose fix `rename it, and -t all selects every client again: omaddons targets rename all <new id>`; no `fix_argv`); without `-t all`, no such warning.
- `targets add <path> --name all` (and `--dry-run`) and `targets rename <id> all` are `usage` (exit 2, "\"all\" is reserved: -t all selects every client") and write nothing.
- `status -t all` and `export -t all` list a registered client whose directory is gone, as `status` and `export` do.

**Facts this part relies on** (as of `c0ab5e9`):
- `tests/target_selection.rs` (150 lines): `support::two_vanilla()` (a Battle.net Classic Era client plus a 1.15 custom client renamed `custom`), `support::ids(values, field)`, and three tests (`read_commands_cover_every_client_a_family_names`, `info_covers_every_client_a_family_names`, `install_still_refuses_to_guess_among_a_familys_clients`). They use `Home::run` (appends `--json`) and `Run::expect(code)`, and stay as they are.
- `Home::new(&["wow", "wowt", "wow_classic_era"])` gives `retail` (live), `ptr` (test, 12.1.0, interface 120100) and `era` (live, 11509) (`tests/common/home.rs:27-50`, `tests/common/trees.rs:24-37`). `common::trees::CustomRoot::at(path).build()` writes a custom client; `BattlenetRoot::at(root).product(code).unknown_folder(folder, product, version).build()` (`tests/common/trees.rs:163-200`) writes a flavor folder the rules do not know, whose provisional id is the folder name without its underscores; `Prefix::new(&env, name)` makes a Wine prefix for it.
- A zip built with `common::archives::zip_text(&[("Foo/Foo.toc", "## Interface: 120105, 120100, 11509\n")])` loads on all three clients; `install gh:o/foo --file <zip> -t <id>` installs it offline (a `static` addon: `update` skips it).
- `<state>/registry.json` holds `targets[].id`; `targets default <id>` registers an unregistered target first.
- `status`'s `data.targets[].id`; `export`'s stdout (the `addons.toml` text) and its `export_missing_target` warning for a registered client whose directory is gone.
- T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`): `tlog!()`; `log.step`, `log.note`, `log.json`, `log.assert_eq`; `log.run(&home, &argv) -> Ran` (argv verbatim: pass `--json` yourself) with `Ran::{ok(), exit(n), fails(exit, code), envelope(), data(), warnings(), commands(), stdout()}`; `log.tree`/`log.assert_unchanged`; `TestEnv` and `Home` are both runners. Its marker test requires a crate that logs to carry `//! e2e suite:` in its root crate doc.

## Technical Approach

Extend `tests/target_selection.rs`. Add to its crate doc the line `//! e2e suite: target selection: family and mode fan-out, -t all, the reserved id all.` (T1's marker). The existing tests stay unchanged. New helpers in `support`:
- `fn three_clients(log) -> Home`: `Home::new(&["wow", "wowt", "wow_classic_era"])`, then `install gh:o/foo --file <zip> -t <id> --json` → `ok()` for `retail`, `ptr` and `era` (so all three are registered and managed); `log.json("targets", …)` from `targets --json`.
- `fn selected(ran, command) -> Vec<String>`: the ids a command covered, read where each command puts them: `data.targets[].id` (`status`, `list`), `data.targets[].target.id` (`outdated`, `update`), `data.installed[].target.id` (`info`), `data.targets` (`export`, a list of ids), `data.targets[].target.id` or `.id` (`backup list`: read the field the envelope has).

### Scenario 1: `all_selects_every_client_test_clients_included`

1. `step("home")`: `three_clients`.
2. `step("every command that takes several")`: for each of `status`, `list`, `outdated --offline`, `info gh:o/foo --offline`: `log.run` it with `-t all --json` and without `-t`, both `ok()`; `log.assert_eq("<command> ids", selected(-t all), ["era", "ptr", "retail"])` and equal to the no-`-t` ids. For `export`: `export -t all --json` and `export --json` give the same `data.targets` and `data.entries` (`log.assert_eq`; `content` is not compared, in case it carries a time).
3. `step("every spelling")`: `status -t ALL`, `status --target=All`, `status --flavor all` → the same three ids.
4. `step("a default that leaves clients out")`: `backup list --json` (no client has backups) lists none; `backup list -t all --json` lists all three, each with no backups.

### Scenario 2: `update_all_says_how_many_are_test_clients`

1. `step("home")`: `three_clients`.
2. `step("dry run, human")`: `log.run` `update -t all --dry-run` (no `--json`) → `exit(0)`; the first stdout line is exactly `-t all selects 3 clients, including 1 test client (ptr)`; every client id appears in a later header line.
3. `step("dry run, json")`: `update -t all --dry-run --json` → `ok()`; `data.targets[].target.id` is `["era", "ptr", "retail"]`; the data has the same keys as `update --dry-run --json`'s, which selects the same three (`log.note("bare update already covers every client at c0ab5e9; -t all selects the same ones and says how many are test clients")`).
4. `step("real run")`: `update -t all` (human) → `exit(0)`, the same first line; nothing changes (the addons are `static`).
5. `step("no line without the keyword")`: `update -t era` (human) → its first line is not a `-t all` line.

### Scenario 3: `single_target_commands_refuse_all_with_one_fix_per_client`

1. `step("home")`: `three_clients`; `baseline` (`log.tree` of `<state>`, `<config>` and the three client dirs).
2. `step("install")`: `install gh:o/foo --file <zip> -t all --json` → `fails(3, "target_ambiguous")`; `details.candidates == ["era","ptr","retail"]`; `fix_argv` ends `-t era`, the alternatives end `-t ptr` and `-t retail`; `unchanged`.
3. `step("every fix runs")`: each of the fix and the two alternatives, run with `--json` → `ok()` (the addon is already installed there: nothing new).
4. `step("other single-target commands")`: `remove foo -t all --json`, `history -t all --json`, `undo -t all --dry-run --json` → each `fails(3, "target_ambiguous")` with the three candidates; `unchanged` after them.
5. `step("one client")`: a fresh `Home::new(&["wow"])`; `install gh:o/foo --file <zip> -t all --json` → `ok()`, installed on `retail`.
6. `step("no client")`: a fresh `TestEnv::new()` (no `Games/`): `status -t all --json` → `ok()` with no targets, as `status --json`; `install gh:o/foo --file <zip> -t all --json` → `fails(3, "target_not_found")`, `details.selector == "all"`, fix `["omaddons","targets"]`.

### Scenario 4: `a_target_named_all_wins_with_a_warning`

1. `step("home")`: `Home::new(&["wow", "wow_classic_era"])`; `targets default retail --json` and `targets default era --json` → `ok()` (both registered). Then the test rewrites `era`'s `id` in `<state>/registry.json` to `all` (`serde_json` read, modify, write), as a build before C2 that accepted `targets rename era all` would have left it; `log.json("registry", …)` before and after.
2. `step("the id wins")`: `status -t all --json` → `ok()`; `selected == ["all"]`; `warnings()` contains `target_id_reserved` exactly once; that warning's `fix` contains `omaddons targets rename all <new id>` and its `fix_argv` is `null`.
3. `step("quiet without the keyword")`: `status --json` → `ok()`, both clients, no `target_id_reserved`; `status -t retail --json` → no `target_id_reserved`.
4. `step("a single-target command takes it")`: `install gh:o/foo --file <zip> -t ALL --json` → `ok()`, installed on the target `all` (the `era` client dir), with the warning once.
5. `step("rename restores the keyword")`: `targets rename all era2 --json` → `ok()`; `status -t all --json` → `selected == ["era2", "retail"]`, no `target_id_reserved`.
6. `step("a flavor folder named _all_")`: a fresh `TestEnv::new()` with `Prefix::new(&env, "battlenet")` and `BattlenetRoot::at(prefix.wow_root()).product("wow").unknown_folder("_all_", None, None).build()`; `targets --json` lists a target with id `all` (assert it; if the builder's folder became no target, fail with that message rather than skip); `status -t all --json` → `selected == ["all"]`, one `target_id_reserved`.
7. `step("a registered all whose directory is gone")`: back on step 1's home with `era2` renamed back by registry rewrite to `all`, move `_classic_era_` aside (`fs::rename`, test code); `status -t all --json` → `fails(3, "target_not_found")` (the registered `all` is gone, never another client), with `target_id_reserved` in `warnings`.

### Scenario 5: `all_is_a_reserved_id`

1. `step("home")`: `Home::new(&["wow", "wow_classic_era"])`; `targets default retail --json` → `ok()`; a custom client built with `CustomRoot::at(home.env.root().join("clients/custom")).build()`; `baseline` of `<state>` and the three client dirs (the custom one included: its marker must not appear).
2. `step("refusals")`: `targets rename retail all --json`, `targets add <custom path> --name all --json`, `targets add <custom path> --name all --dry-run --json` → each `fails(2, "usage")`, message containing `reserved`.
3. `step("nothing written")`: `unchanged`; `registry.json`'s bytes equal step 1's.
4. `step("near names are fine")`: `targets rename retail all-1 --json` → `ok()`; `targets rename all-1 retail --json` → `ok()`.

### Scenario 6: `all_lists_registered_clients_whose_directory_is_gone`

1. `step("home")`: `three_clients`; move `_ptr_` aside (`fs::rename`).
2. `step("status")`: `status --json` and `status -t all --json` → both `ok()` and list `ptr` as missing (`log.assert_eq` of the missing ids and the found ids).
3. `step("export")`: `export --json` and `export -t all --json` → the same `data.targets` and `data.entries`, and the same `export_missing_target` warning.

### What this part does not do

No product code changes. C4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4`) later adds the corpus rows `omaddons update -t all` (succeeds) and `omaddons install dbm -t all` (`target_ambiguous`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `tests/target_selection.rs` carries the `//! e2e suite:` marker; its three existing tests pass unchanged.
- [ ] The six scenarios pass in the gate (`cargo test --test target_selection`) and under `argc e2e target_selection`.
- [ ] Scenario 1 shows `-t all` equal to no `-t` on `status`, `list`, `outdated`, `info` and `export`, in every spelling, and wider on `backup list`.
- [ ] Scenario 2 shows the `update -t all` line in the dry run and the real run, the same targets as bare `update` in JSON, and no line for `-t era`.
- [ ] Scenario 3 shows `target_ambiguous` with id-ordered candidates on `install`, `remove`, `history` and `undo`, every fix running, nothing changed by the refusals, one client taken, and the no-client cases.
- [ ] Scenario 4 shows a target named `all` (registered, provisional, missing) winning with exactly one `target_id_reserved`, no warning without the keyword, and the keyword restored by a rename.
- [ ] Scenario 5 shows `all` refused as a new id with nothing written, and `all-1` accepted.
- [ ] Scenario 6 shows missing registered clients listed under `-t all` as without `-t`.
- [ ] Every scenario logs through `TestLog`.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs tests/target_selection.rs` is clean.
- [ ] `br lint` is clean for this subtask.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

None: this part is end-to-end tests only.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

The six scenarios of the Technical Approach in `tests/target_selection.rs`, each a `#[test]` of its own name, offline (`--file` installs, `--offline` reads), with no fake `/proc`.

### Logging

- `let log = tlog!();` in each new test; each numbered step is a `log.step`; every command goes through `log.run` (argv, environment overrides, exit, the parsed envelope or the human stdout, stderr events, `net.log` lines added).
- `log.assert_eq` for every id list compared (labelled by command and selector), so a mismatch prints both lists and the step.
- `log.tree`/`log.assert_unchanged` around every refusal (scenarios 3 and 5); a difference logs the first differing paths.
- `log.json` for `registry.json` before and after each rewrite, and for `targets --json` in every home.
- On a failure the guard prints `test log: <path>` and the last 20 steps. `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG=verbose cargo test --test target_selection -- --nocapture` or `argc e2e target_selection` echoes every step.

## Considerations

- **Registry rewrites** simulate an older build's state; they are test code writing fixtures, the only way to get a registered `all` once part 2 refuses it.
- **Scenario 4 step 6** depends on the tree builder making `_all_` a target. The scenario asserts that precondition first and fails with a clear message, rather than passing vacuously.
- **Determinism:** every id list is compared in id order, never in discovery order.
- **Hot spot:** `tests/target_selection.rs` has no other M4 writer; the new tests append after the existing ones.
- **Runtime:** six scenarios, about 60 commands, offline; well within the gate.

## Dependencies

Parent: C2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.2`, a client named as an addon, and `-t all`).

- **Before it:** part 2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.2.2`, `-t all`), whose behaviour this tests. T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs), through an edge added at filing.
- **After it:** nothing among the siblings; it runs in parallel with parts 3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.2.3`) and 4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.2.4`).

title: Closest client id on `target_not_found`
description:
## Background

**What this is.** A client selector that matches nothing is `target_not_found` (exit 3). At `c0ab5e9` the fix of that error is always `omaddons targets`, a listing. An agent that typed `-t retial` must read the listing, guess which id it meant, and rebuild its own command: a detour for the most ordinary slip there is. After this bead the fix is the user's own command with the closest client selector in place of the typo, the other close words follow as alternatives, and the listing stays reachable as the last alternative:

```text
$ omaddons status -t retial --json
{"ok":false,"schema_version":"1.0","tool_version":"0.1.0","command":"status","exit_code":3,
 "error":{"code":"target_not_found","message":"no target matches \"retial\"; the closest selector is \"retail\"",
   "fix":"omaddons status -t retail","fix_argv":["omaddons","status","-t","retail"],
   "alternatives":[{"display":"omaddons targets","argv":["omaddons","targets"]}],
   "retryable":false,"details":{"selector":"retial"}},
 "warnings":[],"commands":[],"meta":{"elapsed_ms":9,"offline":false}}
```

The same error in human mode, on stderr:

```text
error[target_not_found]: no target matches "retial"; the closest selector is "retail"
fix: omaddons status -t retail
  or: omaddons targets
```

Nothing is corrected silently. The command the user typed did nothing; the fix is a suggestion that the user or the agent runs. That is the whole difference between this bead and an auto-correct, which M4-D14 rejects.

**The milestone goal it serves.** G-M4-2, "the first guess works": a plausible wrong invocation yields an error whose fix is the command the user meant. That covers a misplaced client name, a typo of a command, flag, value **or client id**, `-t all`, and `apply` vs `adopt --apply`. Each such fix is proven to run, not only to parse, and a fix never turns the user's verb into a different command that changes something. This bead delivers the client-id typo part.

**The checkpoint criterion it serves.** Criterion 5, "Intent inference": a corpus of at least 60 wrong invocations covers misplaced client names before and after the verb, a client name given as an addon, `-t all`, **client-id typos**, command, flag and value typos, `apply` for `adopt --apply`, and doctor verb typos. Each yields its documented error with a `fix_argv` that parses and runs on the corpus home to its documented exit code (`tests/contract/intent_corpus.rs`), and no fix turns the user's verb into a different command that changes something. The corpus rows this bead makes pass are added by C4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4`, the run-the-fix corpus), which lands after it:

| Wrong | Code | Fix | Fix exit |
|---|---|---|---|
| `omaddons status -t retial` | `target_not_found` | `omaddons status -t retail` | 0 |
| `omaddons list -t wtolk` | `target_not_found` | `omaddons list -t wotlk` | 0 |
| `omaddons undo -t retial` | `target_not_found` | `omaddons undo -t retail` | 3 (nothing to undo on the corpus home, declared) |
| `omaddons pin dbm -t retial` | `target_not_found` | `omaddons pin dbm -t retail` | 0 |

The corpus home (`common::intent_home()`, C4's) holds two Battle.net clients, `retail` and `era`, one legacy 3.3.5a client, `wotlk`, DBM managed on `retail` and `era`, and Questie.

**How it serves the vision.** Vision goal G4, agent ergonomics: "the first command an agent guesses works". The vision promises a "flexible `-t`" (key, id, product code, flavor folder, game mode, family, path); that flexibility exists at `c0ab5e9`, but its errors do not help an agent recover. It also keeps the project's thesis: omaddons acts only on what the user asked for. A guess is offered, never executed.

**The decision that shapes it: M4-D14, a mistyped client id gets the closest one.**
- `target_not_found`'s fix becomes the same argv with the closest selector: Levenshtein distance at most 2 over every id, mode and family the vocabulary holds, ties broken by registered ids first, then alphabetically.
- Further candidates go in `alternatives`. With no close candidate the fix stays `omaddons targets`.
- The fix keeps the user's verb. That is M4-D12's exemption from the rule "never guess a mutating command" (vision comment 660): that rule exists so a typo of a verb (`omaddons unpn x`) is never handed a different command that changes something (`omaddons undo`). Here the verb is the user's own and only the client word changed, so `omaddons remove dbm -t retial` may be offered `omaddons remove dbm -t retail`.
- **Why:** `-t retial` gets `omaddons targets` today, a detour. The vision's flexible `-t` exists; its fixes do not.
- **Rejected:** auto-correcting the selector (running `retail` when `retial` was typed). Never act on a guess: a guess that is wrong on a command that changes addons changes the wrong client.

**Decisions it obeys, restated.**

## Technical Approach

The work is four small pieces in four files, plus README and tests. `resolve` ranks the close words and records them on the error, in process. The command boundary, which knows the argv, puts the best one into the user's command.

### 1. The ranking: `TargetVocabulary::closest` (`src/vocabulary.rs`)

```rust
/// The words that may be what `typed` meant, a selector that matched nothing (M4-D14),
/// best first: within Levenshtein distance 2 of `typed` (ASCII case ignored) and closer
/// than its length, never equal to it, of kind Registered, DefaultId, Mode or Family,
/// and accepted by `admit`. Ordered by distance, then registered ids before built-in
/// words, then alphabetically. A registered id is returned as stored, any other word as
/// the vocabulary spells it (`hc`, not `hardcore`). Pure: no I/O.
pub fn closest(&self, typed: &str, admit: &dyn Fn(&str) -> bool) -> Vec<String>
```

- `let typed = typed.to_ascii_lowercase();` and `let len = typed.chars().count();`.
- For each `(spelling, word)` of `self.words`: skip kinds `ProductCode` and `FlavorFolder` (M4-D14 names ids, modes and families; product codes and flavor folders are machine spellings copied from output, and a near miss of one is usually also near an id or mode that selects the same client: `_retail` is distance 1 from `retail`, `_classic_era` distance 2 from `classic-era`). Skip a word whose length in chars differs from `len` by more than 2 before computing anything (the edit distance is at least the length difference, so this changes no result). Otherwise compute `d = crate::cli::levenshtein(&typed, spelling)` and keep the word when `1 <= d && d <= 2 && d < len`.
- **Bounded work (common rule 15). Decided while writing this bead:** the length-difference skip above. The typed value is user-sized (a `-t` value can be as long as the command line allows). Thanks to the length-difference skip, a distance is only ever computed between two strings at most two characters apart in length, each no longer than a vocabulary word plus 2, so the cost is bounded by the vocabulary whatever is typed (a 100,000-character `-t` value costs no more than `retial`). No named constant is needed: the bound is the vocabulary itself.
- **Decided while writing this bead:** the bound `d < len` (a candidate must keep at least one character of what was typed) is added to M4-D14's `d <= 2`, so a one-letter selector never gets a guess that replaces all of it (`-t x` would otherwise be offered `-t hc`, the Hardcore mode, which selects the Classic Era client), and a two-letter one only a one-edit neighbour (`-t er` → `era`). `d >= 1` is implied by the not-found branch (a word equal to the selector that selected a client would have matched), and is kept explicit so the fix never repeats the failing argv.
- Then call `admit(word)` only for the words that passed the distance test (the call is the expensive part in the caller), and keep those it accepts.
- Sort by the key `(d, word.kind != TargetWordKind::Registered, returned_word)` and return the words. Each spelling is in the vocabulary once, so the list has no duplicates.
- **The distance 2 stays a literal**, documented in this function's doc comment as M4-D14's bound, as at the five existing typo sites in `src/cli.rs`. **Decided while writing this bead:** no `src/limits.rs` row. It is a matching threshold, not a bound on work, and a `REGISTRY` row would add a published name to `capabilities`' `limits` list (A4, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`, `omaddons capabilities`), which a leaf that may land after H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, the pre-freeze contract audit) must not add (M4-D55).
- **Decided while writing this bead:** no cap on the number of candidates. They are vocabulary words that select a client on this machine, so the list is bounded by the vocabulary (about 70 built-in words plus one id per client), and in practice it holds one or two words.

### 2. The not-found branch of `resolve` (`src/discover/registry.rs`)

1. **Extract the step list** into a private helper, so the same matching serves `resolve` and the candidate filter:

   ```rust
   /// The targets the first matching step selects (key, id, product code, flavor folder,
   /// game mode, family, then `path` when given), `None` when no step matches.
   fn first_match<'a>(
       selector: &str,
       targets: &'a [DiscoveredTarget],
       table: &RulesTable,
       path: Option<&Path>,
   ) -> Option<Vec<&'a DiscoveredTarget>>
   ```

   It holds `resolve`'s seven closures unchanged (`src/discover/registry.rs:647-683`), with the path step reading the `path` argument. `resolve` becomes `let path = std::fs::canonicalize(selector).ok(); first_match(selector, targets, table, path.as_deref()).ok_or_else(|| no_match(selector, targets, table))`. Behaviour is identical: the existing tests `selector_precedence`, `game_modes_select_the_client_that_runs_them`, `a_missing_client_is_never_resolved_to_another` and `ambiguity_fixes_rewrite_argv` must pass unchanged.
2. **`fn no_match(selector, targets, table) -> Error`** holds both arms of today's `ok_or_else`. The mode arm (`Some((product, mode))`) is moved as it is: its selector is spelled right, its client is missing, and `targets --rescan` is the right fix. **Decided while writing this bead:** only the `None` arm changes, because M4-D14 is about a selector that names nothing, and a known mode whose client is missing is spelled right.
3. **The `None` arm:**

   ```rust
   let closest = closest_selectors(selector, targets, table);
   let message = match closest.first() {
       Some(best) => format!("no target matches {selector:?}; the closest selector is {best:?}"),
       None => format!("no target matches {selector:?}"),
   };
   Error::new(ErrorCode::TargetNotFound, message, Suggestion::command(["omaddons", "targets"]))
       .details(serde_json::json!({ "selector": selector }))
       .closest_selectors(selector, closest)
   ```

   **Decided while writing this bead:** the message names the best candidate, as `subcommand_fix` already appends "; the closest command is …" (`src/cli.rs:682-685`), so a human reading the error sees the suggestion even where the fix cannot carry it (config's `default_target`, below). The fix stays `omaddons targets` here because `resolve` has no argv; the boundary rewrites it (section 4).
4. **The candidates:**

   ```rust
   /// The words close to `selector` that select at least one client here (M4-D14).
   fn closest_selectors(selector: &str, targets: &[DiscoveredTarget], table: &RulesTable) -> Vec<String> {
       TargetVocabulary::new(table, targets.iter().map(|d| d.target.id.as_str()))
           .closest(selector, &|word| first_match(word, targets, table, None).is_some())
   }
   ```

   - **Decided while writing this bead: a candidate must select at least one client on this machine** (the key, id, product, folder, mode or family step matches; never the path step, so a word that happens to name a directory in the working directory is not read as a path). M4-D14 says "every id, mode and family the vocabulary holds", and the vocabulary holds every built-in word whether or not its client is here. Offering `-t retail` on a machine without a retail client would give a fix that fails with `target_not_found` again, a worse detour than the listing, and M4-D15 requires a fix to run. With the filter, `-t sodd` on a machine without a Classic Era client gets no guess.
   - **Decided while writing this bead: "registered ids first" means the ids of the clients on this machine.** At `resolve` time the ids at hand are `DiscoveredTarget.target.id`, registered or provisional (an unregistered client answers to its provisional id, such as `retail@steam`, exactly as a registered one does at the id step). They are passed as the vocabulary's `Registered` words, so they rank before built-in words at equal distance. The usage path of C1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.1`, misplaced clients before and after the verb) reads `registry.json`'s ids instead, because it has no world; here the world is loaded and its ids are the better source (they include every provisional id).
   - The table is the world's (`World.table`, config.toml's rules overrides applied), as every caller passes it today.
   - `all` is never a candidate: it is not a vocabulary word (C1 decided so), and it is the `-t all` keyword of C2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.2`, a client named as an addon, and `-t all`). **Decided while writing this bead:** if C2 makes `all` a vocabulary word, `closest` must still skip it, because a typo fix must never silently widen a selection from one client to every client (for `update`, test clients included).
   - Keys and paths are not candidates (they are not vocabulary words).

### 3. The in-process record: `ClosestSelectors` (`src/error.rs`)

```rust
/// The words closest to a selector that named no client (M4-D14), best first, for the
/// command boundary to put into the user's argv (`discover::registry::fix_with_closest_selector`).
/// In process only: `ErrorBody` does not copy it, so it never reaches the wire.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct ClosestSelectors {
    /// The selector exactly as given (the raw `-t`, `--from` or `--to` value).
    pub typed: String,
    /// Never empty.
    pub closest: Vec<String>,
}
```

- `ErrorData` gains `pub closest_selectors: Option<ClosestSelectors>`, `None` from `Error::new`.
- `#[must_use] pub fn closest_selectors(mut self, typed: &str, closest: Vec<String>) -> Self` sets it to `Some` when `closest` is not empty and leaves it `None` otherwise.
- `ErrorBody` and its `From<Error>` are unchanged, so nothing new reaches the JSON, the schema or a snapshot.
- **Decided while writing this bead:** the record lives on `ErrorData`, beside C1's `usage_fix` and in the pattern of `PlanStaleSource`, because the code that knows the candidates (`resolve`, which has the targets and the table) and the code that knows the argv (the command boundary) are different layers, and the error is what travels between them.

### 4. The fix in the user's argv (`src/discover/registry.rs`, called from `src/app/mod.rs`)

1. **`pub(crate) fn with_selector(argv: &[String], typed: &str, with: &str) -> Option<Vec<String>>`**, beside `with_target`. It copies `argv`, replacing `typed` with `with` wherever `typed` is the value of a selector flag, and returns `Some(crate::cli::fix_argv(&out))` when it replaced at least one, else `None`. The selector flags, in every spelling clap accepts:
   - `-t V`, `--target V`, `--flavor V` (the value is the next token);
   - `--target=V`, `--flavor=V`, `-t=V`, and `-tV` (the value attached);
   - a short cluster of value-less flags ending in `t`, `-vt V` (next token), or with the value attached, `-vtV` (the short flags that take no value are `-v` and `-h`);
   - `copy`'s `--from V`, `--to V`, `--from=V`, `--to=V`.

   Rules:
   - The comparison is exact (`V == typed`): `typed` is the raw value the command received, so it is spelled exactly as in the argv.
   - Every such occurrence is replaced (`-t retial -t retial`, `copy --from retial --to retial`). Nothing after `--` is read or changed. A positional or another flag's value that equals the typo (`remove retial -t retial`, `--reason retial`) is left alone.
   - The flag keeps the user's spelling: `--target=retial` becomes `--target=retail` and `-tretial` becomes `-tretail`. **Decided while writing this bead:** keep the spelling rather than normalize to `-t <id>` as `with_target` does, because M4-D14 says "the same argv", and only the value was wrong.
   - Presentation flags (`--json`, `--robot`, `--format`, `--progress`, `--no-color`, `--no-progress`) are dropped by `fix_argv`, as in every fix.
2. **`pub(crate) fn fix_with_closest_selector(error: &mut Error, argv: &[String])`**, its doc comment saying what follows:
   - Returns at once unless `error.code == ErrorCode::TargetNotFound` and `error.closest_selectors` is `Some`.
   - Builds one argv per candidate with `with_selector(argv, &typed, candidate)`.
   - When the first candidate gives `None` (the selector is not on the command line: config's `default_target`), the error is left exactly as it is. **Decided while writing this bead:** the fix then stays `omaddons targets`; the message already names the closest word, and a fix that added `-t retail` would hide the typo in config.toml rather than correct it. (Every candidate shares one `typed`, so either all give `Some` or all give `None`.)
   - Otherwise: the old fix (`omaddons targets`) is set aside, `error.fix` becomes the first candidate's argv, `error.alternatives` gets the other candidates' argvs in rank order, then the old fix last, and `error.usage_fix = UsageFix::UserVerb`.
   - **Decided while writing this bead:** `omaddons targets` stays as the last alternative, so an agent whose typo was not the guessed word still has the listing without a second error; it costs one array entry.
   - Code, exit, `retryable` (false), message and `details` are unchanged.
   - No parse check at run time. Replacing a flag's value with a vocabulary word (lowercase, never starting with `-`) cannot make a parsing argv stop parsing. The property is held by the `with_selector` unit table (every result parses) and by the contract suite's `check()`, which parses every fix and alternative of every envelope.
3. **`Out::boundary_fix`** (`src/app/mod.rs:284-300`) gains one arm, `ErrorCode::TargetNotFound => crate::discover::registry::fix_with_closest_selector(e, self.argv),`, and its doc comment gains "a `target_not_found` whose selector was a near miss names the closest one in the user's own command (M4-D14)". This covers every command, because every dispatch arm emits through `Out::emit_as`.

**Where the plan and the code differ.** The plan says "in `resolve`'s not-found branch, compute the closest vocabulary word …, make it the fix with the argv otherwise unchanged". At `c0ab5e9`, `resolve` has no argv (`src/discover/registry.rs:642-646`), and neither does `World::select_many`'s free function (`src/app/world.rs:254-262`), its most common caller. The intent is kept as follows: `resolve`'s not-found branch computes the closest words (as planned) and records them in process; the fix is assembled at the command boundary, the one place that already rewrites fixes from the argv and that sees every command's errors. The plan also speaks of `-t` alone; the same selector can come from `copy`'s `--from`/`--to` and from config's `default_target`, which section 4 handles.

### 6. What does not change

- No new error code, warning code, `details` key, data key, action, event, env var, limit, constant or file; `schema_version` stays "1.0". `src/limits.rs` and the `limit_registries` snapshot are unchanged.
- Nothing runs for the mistyped invocation that did not run before: the error is raised where it always was (after the world is loaded, before any planning, recovery or commit), so a mistyped selector on a command that changes addons still changes nothing under `<state>`, `<config>` or any client dir. Only `<cache>`'s derived discovery cache may be rewritten, as by any command that loads the world.
- A selector with no close word that selects a client here keeps today's error byte for byte (message, fix, no alternatives, `details`).
- The other `target_not_found` sites listed under Facts keep their fixes. **Decided while writing this bead:** `unknown_id` (`targets rename`, `targets rm`, `targets default` and the like, whose positional is an id) is out of scope, because M4-D14 is about `-t`'s resolution and those commands take an id, not a selector.

## Considerations

- **A guess can be wrong.** The closest word is not always the meant one (a user with `era` and `era-ptr` who typed `-t er-ptr` gets `era-ptr`, probably right; one who typed `-t ptrr` meaning the Classic Era PTR gets `ptr`, the retail PTR, if that client is here). Mitigations: nothing runs on a guess (M4-D14 rejected auto-correction); the message names the word; the other close words and the listing are alternatives; only words that select a client here are offered; the distance and length bounds keep wild guesses out; and a fix that changes addons is previewable (`--dry-run`) and undoable like any command the user types.
- **A family or mode can select several clients.** `install x -t vanila` gets `install x -t vanilla`, which on a home with two vanilla clients gives `target_ambiguous` (exit 3) with one fix per client. Each step's fix runs; the typo alone cannot say which client was meant. At equal distance an id still wins over a family or mode.
- **Risk 14 (the milestone is large):** the intent area absorbs slips. This bead has 15 units of slack; the computed schedule puts it in lane 3 at t = 15–16. It may land after H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, the pre-freeze contract audit), because it adds no wire shape (M4-D55).
- **Risk 12 (misplaced-client fixes misfire), related:** owned by C1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.1`) and C2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.2`). This bead adds no misplaced-client hook and changes no `usage` error.
- **Hot spots and collisions:**
  - `src/app/mod.rs` (A1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1`, per-command facts in `COMMANDS`, first; each command leaf adds its `COMMANDS` rows and dispatch arms): this bead adds one arm to `boundary_fix` and nothing else. Rebase if A1 or a command leaf is in flight.
  - `src/error.rs` (A9, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9`, then A3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`, edit every code row; later leaves append rows): this bead adds no row, only `ClosestSelectors`, one `ErrorData` field and one builder, outside the rows, next to C1's `UsageFix`.
  - `src/discover/registry.rs` and `src/vocabulary.rs`: C2 also edits `resolve` (the `-t all` keyword before the id step) and may extend the vocabulary. Whichever of C2 and this bead lands second rebases and keeps both. The `all` keyword stays outside `first_match`, so it is never a candidate.
  - `tests/contract/matrix.rs`: append the new test; one new snapshot file.
  - `README.md`: edit only this bead's paragraph and the two single lines.
- **Size S, no subtasks.** One function in the vocabulary, one branch and two helpers in the registry, one in-process field, one boundary arm, README and tests: one commit.
- **What could go wrong, and how to notice.**
  - The `resolve` refactor changes a selection: the existing selection tests fail (listed in the acceptance criteria), and `first_match_is_resolve_without_its_path_step` compares both over every built-in word.
  - An error path that bypasses `boundary_fix`: the contract rows and the end-to-end scenarios check the fix on `status`, `list`, `install`, `copy`, `remove`, `update`, `pin`, `history`, `backup list` and `undo`.
  - A candidate that does not run: scenario 1 runs each fix, and the corpus of C4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4`) runs them again on its own home.
  - A flag spelling missed by `with_selector`: the fix falls back to `omaddons targets` (fails safe), and the unit table lists every spelling.
- **Performance.** Only the not-found path pays: at most about 70 edit distances between short words (the length-difference skip removes most of them), plus one in-memory `first_match` per close word. No perf budget applies; `status --cached`'s budget is untouched (a successful selection never computes candidates).
- **Bounded work (common rule 15).** No file or network input is read: the vocabulary is the built-in table plus the ids of the clients the world already loaded. The one user-sized input, the typed selector, is bounded by the length-difference skip (section 1), not by a constant.
- **Privacy.** The message and fix carry only the typed selector and a client id, mode or family, all of which `targets` already shows. No `WTF/` is read.
- **Compatibility.** Nothing persisted changes, so there is nothing for E9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9`, the M3 build against M4 state) to characterize. An older build given the same typo still offers `omaddons targets`.
- **Previews bind (common rule 16).** No mutating path is added; the rule does not apply. Say so in the close comment. A fix carries `--if-match` along when the user gave it (the argv is otherwise unchanged).
- **The guide (common rule 17) and the corpus (rule 18).** No command, code, action or env var changes, so `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` needs regenerating only if `target_not_found`'s `meaning` (A9) is edited or `tests/skill.rs` reports a difference. C4 lands after this bead and adds the four corpus rows.
- **Decided while writing this bead** (confirm or adjust each in the close comment): the boundary assembles the fix; candidates must select a client here; "registered" means the ids of the clients here; the `d < len` bound; the length-difference skip; no limits row and no cap; only the no-match arm changes; the message names the best word; the flag keeps its spelling and every occurrence is replaced; no rewrite when the selector came from config; `omaddons targets` stays as the last alternative; `all` is never offered; `unknown_id` is out of scope; the record lives on `ErrorData`; the tests live in `tests/contract/matrix.rs` (`target_typos`) and `tests/e2e_target_typos.rs`.

## Dependencies

Parent: the C area epic, AREA-C (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3`, intent inference), under the milestone epic (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`).

**Blocked by:**

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M4 plan, 2026-10-24).**

**Why this bead.** A mistyped client selector is the most ordinary slip an agent makes with a multi-client tool, and at `c0ab5e9` it is answered with a detour: `target_not_found`'s fix is always `omaddons targets`, so the agent must read a listing, guess which id it meant and rebuild its command. After this bead `omaddons status -t retial` is answered with `omaddons status -t retail`: the user's own command, with the closest client id, game mode or family that selects a client on this machine, the other close words as alternatives, and the listing last. Nothing is corrected on its own; the typed command did nothing. It completes the "client-id typos" part of G-M4-2 ("the first guess works") and of checkpoint criterion 5, whose corpus rows C4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4`) adds and runs. It serves vision goal G4, "the first command an agent guesses works", and keeps the thesis that omaddons acts only on what it was asked: a guess is offered, never executed.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M4-D14:** the fix is the same argv with the closest selector, Levenshtein distance at most 2 over every id, mode and family the vocabulary holds, ties broken by registered ids first, then alphabetically; further candidates in `alternatives`; `omaddons targets` when nothing is close; the user's verb kept.
- **M4-D12 (context, built by C1 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.1`):** the `TargetVocabulary` this bead ranks, and the exemption that lets a fix keep a verb that changes something (`remove dbm -t retail`), marked `UsageFix::UserVerb` in process.
- **M4-D15 (context):** a fix must run, not just parse; this is why only words that select a client on this machine are offered.
- **M4-D55:** this bead may land after H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`) because it adds no wire shape; it changes only the message text, the `fix` and the entries of the existing `alternatives`, and `details` stays `{selector}`.
- **M4-D10 (context):** `target_not_found`'s `details` keys are unchanged, so A9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9`) and A3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`) need nothing from it.
- **§8.1 defaults:** an existing code and key over new ones; token-frugal (one alternative per further candidate plus the listing); no network on a read path.

**Alternatives rejected that matter here.**
- Auto-correcting the selector (M4-D14): a wrong guess on a command that changes addons would change the wrong client.
- Offering every vocabulary word within distance 2, whether or not its client is here: `-t retial` on a machine without retail would get a fix that fails with `target_not_found` again, worse than the listing.
- Building the fix inside `resolve`: it has no argv, and neither does its most common caller (`World::select_many`). Threading the argv through every caller would touch a dozen commands; the command boundary already rewrites fixes from the argv for every command.
- Normalizing the flag to `-t <id>` as `with_target` does: M4-D14 says "the same argv", and only the value was wrong.
- A `src/limits.rs` row for the distance: it is a matching threshold like the five existing typo sites, and a row would add a published name to `capabilities`, which a leaf that may land after H1 must not add (M4-D55).
- Rewriting the fix when the selector came from config's `default_target`: a `-t retail` fix would hide the typo in config.toml rather than correct it; the message names the closest word instead.
- Offering `all` (the `-t all` keyword of C2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.2`): a typo fix must never widen a selection from one client to every client.

**Risks and how they are watched.**
- A wrong guess: nothing runs on it; the message names the word; alternatives and the listing are there; only clients present are offered; the distance and length bounds keep wild guesses out (`-t x` gets none). The end-to-end suite runs every offered fix.
- The `resolve` refactor changing a selection (the step list moves into `first_match`): the existing selection tests are acceptance criteria, and a unit test compares `first_match` with `resolve` over every built-in word.
- An error path that bypasses the boundary: contract rows and end-to-end scenarios cover ten commands, including `copy`'s `--from`.
- A user-sized selector (common rule 15): a word whose length differs from the typed value by more than 2 is skipped before any distance is computed, so the cost is bounded by the vocabulary.
- Risk 14 (the milestone is large): this bead has 15 units of slack, the most of any leaf.
- Collisions: C2 also edits `resolve` and the vocabulary; whichever lands second rebases and keeps both.

**What it unblocks, and why they wait.**
- C4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4`): its corpus rows `status -t retial`, `list -t wtolk`, `undo -t retial` and `pin dbm -t retial` expect these fixes, and its harness runs them; without this bead those rows would assert `omaddons targets`.
- T2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.2`): slice 1's demo includes "the corpus runs".

**How it serves the milestone.** G-M4-2 names "a typo of a … client id" among the first guesses that must work; criterion 5 lists "client-id typos" in the corpus. This is the leaf that makes them work, and it does so without a new wire name, so it can land late without reopening the contract audit.

**Facts verified during planning** (as of `c0ab5e9`). `resolve` (`src/discover/registry.rs:638-708`) has no argv; its not-found branch has a mode arm (`targets --rescan`) and a no-match arm (`omaddons targets`, `details {selector}`). `resolve_one` rewrites `target_ambiguous`'s fixes from the argv with `with_target` (`:788-856`). `Out::boundary_fix` (`src/app/mod.rs:281-300`) runs on every emitted error and already rewrites fixes from the argv. `ErrorBody` copies only the wire fields of `ErrorData` (`src/error.rs:504-513`, `:616-641`). `copy` resolves `--from`/`--to` through `resolve_one_in` and passes non-ambiguity errors through (`src/app/copy.rs:388-425`). Config's `default_target` reaches `resolve_one_in` without being on the command line (`src/app/world.rs:177-184`). Every existing test that pins `omaddons targets` uses a selector with no close word (`nosuch`, `nowhere`, `nothing-here`).

**Where the plan and the code differ.** The plan computes the closest word in `resolve` and makes it the fix "with the argv otherwise unchanged", but `resolve` has no argv: the words are computed there and recorded in process (`ErrorData.closest_selectors`), and the fix is assembled at the command boundary. The plan speaks of `-t`; the selector also comes from `copy`'s `--from`/`--to` and from config's `default_target`, and both are handled. The not-found branch has two arms; only the no-match arm changes. "Registered ids first" is read as "the ids of the clients on this machine", the ids `resolve` has.

**Confidence.** High. The change is a pure ranking over an in-memory vocabulary, one error branch, one in-process field and one boundary arm; it adds no write, no lock and no protocol, and every offered fix is run by its own tests and again by C4's corpus.

title: The run-the-fix corpus
description:
## How to work this bead

This bead is worked through its 4 subtasks, listed below in work order. Claim a subtask, not this bead (`br ready --parent omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4` lists the ready ones). The agent that closes the last open subtask then verifies every acceptance criterion of this bead (they are the leaf's, not any one subtask's), and closes this bead with `br close omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4 --reason "done: <evidence> · found: <ids>"`. Until this bead is closed, every bead it blocks stays blocked.

1. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4.1 The corpus home `common::intent_home()` and its exact same-path restore: `tests/common/intent.rs`, `trees::copy_tree_exact`, and their self-tests in `tests/common_selftest.rs`.
2. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4.2 Tests: the run-the-fix harness and the misplaced-client, `-t all` and client-id rows: `tests/contract/intent_corpus.rs` (row model, harness, failure report, structural tests, 21 starting rows and 2 collision rows), README. Needs part 1.
3. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4.3 Tests: the command, flag, value and argument rows of the starting set: 28 more starting rows, each with the fix the binary gives pinned. Needs part 2.
4. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4.4 Tests: the rows of surfaces other leaves own, the pending table and the criterion-5 checks: `PENDING`, promotion of every row whose surface has landed, the plan-row and pending tests, the checkpoint test. Needs part 3.

The leaf is size M and closes as one unit: no bead it blocks starts on half of it. The subtasks split the work into commits that each pass `argc gate` on their own. They form one chain because parts 2 to 4 all write `tests/contract/intent_corpus.rs`, and each part's tests count the rows the part before it added.

## Background

Leaves named in this section: A1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1`, per-command facts in `COMMANDS`, and `auth github`), C4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4`, this bead), D9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.9`, `omaddons plans show`), E1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`, the failure-mode registry), E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`, `doctor fix`), F3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.3`, the doctor's state-file detectors), H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the M4 checkpoint and the first tag).

**What this is.** A corpus of common wrong invocations, each run for real. For every row, `tests/contract/intent_corpus.rs` runs the wrong argv on a copy of a synthetic home, checks the error it gets, takes the error's `fix_argv`, runs that fix on an independent copy of the same original home, and asserts the exit the row declares. A wrong invocation that is an error must leave every record and every client tree of its copy byte for byte unchanged. The home, `common::intent_home()`, holds two Battle.net clients (`retail` and `era`), one legacy 3.3.5a client (`wotlk`), DBM managed on `retail` and on `era`, Questie on `era`, and HTTP fixtures for their sources.

**Why it exists.** At `c0ab5e9` no test checks that a suggested fix runs; the contract suite checks only that every fix parses (`tests/contract/usage_fixes.rs`, and `support::parses`, `tests/contract/main.rs:257`). The one exception runs `status`'s recommendations (`every_status_recommendation_runs_on_a_fresh_home`, `tests/contract/recommendations.rs:213`). A fix that parses but fails is worse than `omaddons help`: an agent that follows it gets a second error and has learned nothing. The vision's M4 checkpoint asks that "an intent-inference corpus of common wrong invocations yields usage errors whose `fix_argv` runs successfully", and that is unmet today. Area C's other leaves, C1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.1`), C2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.2`) and C3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.3`), build the fixes; this leaf proves they run, and proves that the wrong invocation changed nothing before the user ran the fix.

**The milestone goals it serves.**
- **G-M4-2, "the first guess works":** a plausible wrong invocation yields a usage error whose fix is the command the user meant (a misplaced client name, a typo of a command, flag, value or client id, `-t all`, `apply` vs `adopt --apply`). "Each such fix is proven to run, not only to parse. A fix never turns the user's verb into a different command that changes something." This bead is the proof.
- **G-M4-6, "no new risk to the engine's guarantees":** a wrong invocation must not commit anything. The corpus hashes every record and client tree around every erroring row.

**The checkpoint criterion it serves: criterion 5, "Intent inference".** "A corpus of at least 60 wrong invocations covers: misplaced client names before and after the verb, a client name given as an addon, `-t all`, client-id typos, command, flag and value typos, `apply` for `adopt --apply`, and doctor verb typos. Each yields its documented error with a `fix_argv` that parses and runs on the corpus home to its documented exit code (`tests/contract/intent_corpus.rs`). No fix turns the user's verb into a different command that changes something. A misplaced-client invocation changes nothing at all: records and client trees hash identical before and after it, including `remove dbm retail` and `update dbm retail` with DBM also installed on a client other than the misplaced one, and the corrected argv runs on an independent copy of the original home." (Amended from the vision, which asked only that fixes run successfully.) This bead owns the corpus and its harness; H4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`, the README final pass) checks the count of at least 60, which this bead's checkpoint test reports; H6 records the criterion.

**Slice 1's exit demo** includes "`omaddons retail update` suggests `update -t retail`, `remove dbm retail` changes nothing, and the corpus runs". T2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.2`, slice 1 end to end) records it as a test; this bead does not record a demo itself.

**How it serves the vision.** Vision goal G4, agent ergonomics: "the first command an agent guesses works". The thesis that omaddons stays the sole, safe, undoable authority over what it manages is why an erroring row must hash unchanged: an error that has already changed something is not a usage error, and the corrected command run afterwards would not undo it.

**The decisions that shape it** (full text in the decision log comments on the milestone epic `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`):
- **M4-D15, a usage fix must run, not just parse.** `tests/contract/intent_corpus.rs` holds a corpus of at least 60 entries, each `(wrong argv, expected error code, expected exit of the fix)`. For each entry the harness runs the wrong argv on a synthetic home (two Battle.net clients, one legacy client, two managed addons, recorded HTTP fixtures), takes `fix_argv`, runs it, and asserts the fix's exit. The existing parse-only sweeps stay. An erroring row must change nothing: the wrong argv runs on its own copy of the home, which must hash unchanged. Each later leaf that adds a command or a hook adds corpus rows (D5 for `apply`, D9 for `plans show`, E3 and E6 for `doctor`). Why: the vision checkpoint is unmet, and a fix that parses but fails is worse than `help`. **Rejected:** requiring every fix to exit 0, because some correct fixes legitimately fail on the corpus home (an `--offline` rerun, `plans show` of a plan the home does not hold). The corpus states each expected exit instead.
- **M4-D12, misplaced client names are recognised before the verb, after it, and as an addon** (C1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.1`, and C2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.2`, implement it). Hook 1: `omaddons retail update` → `omaddons update -t retail` (the client word removed, `-t <word>` appended). Hook 2: a non-dash word after a verb whose positionals are filled (`omaddons status retail` → `omaddons status -t retail`; `omaddons info dbm era` → `omaddons info dbm -t era`). Hook 3, a preflight in `install`, `update` and `remove` before planning, recovery or any commit: a positional that names a client and no installed addon, catalog entry, alias, ref form or path makes the whole invocation `usage`, `details {target, command}`, with the client moved into `-t` (`omaddons remove dbm retail` → `omaddons remove dbm -t retail`). The addon wins: a word that is both a client and an addon is never moved. These fixes keep the user's own verb, so they are exempt from vision comment 660's rule "never guess a mutating command", which exists to stop a typo turning into another verb; they are marked `UsageFix::UserVerb`.
- **M4-D13, `-t all`** (C2): selects every registered target, test clients included, where a command takes several; on a command that must land on one client it is `target_ambiguous` with one alternative per client.
- **M4-D14, a mistyped client id gets the closest one** (C3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.3`): `target_not_found`'s fix is the same argv with the closest selector within Levenshtein distance 2 (`-t retial` → `-t retail`); with none, the fix stays `omaddons targets`. The fix keeps the user's verb.
- **M4-D27, `apply` keeps its name; intent inference separates it from `adopt --apply`** (D5, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`, implements the hints; this bead's corpus holds their rows). `omaddons apply` with no argument is `usage` with the fix `omaddons help apply` and the alternative `omaddons adopt --apply` (read-only help first, because `adopt --apply` mutates); `omaddons adopt apply` is `usage` with the fix `omaddons adopt --apply`. Rejected: renaming the command, which breaks the vision's canonical intent "preview, then apply exactly".
- **M4-D40, the doctor's exit dictionary** (E3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`): inside the `doctor` tree a usage error exits 64 (`usage_error`), not 2; a lookup error exits 66. The corpus therefore states each row's wrong-run exit explicitly.

### 1. The corpus home: `common::intent_home()` (part 1)

**`tests/common/intent.rs`** (new; declared in `tests/common/mod.rs`, which re-exports `intent::{IntentHome, intent_home}` so `common::intent_home()` works in every test crate):

```rust
/// The synthetic home of the run-the-fix corpus (M4-D15), kept at one directory for
/// its whole life and restored there byte for byte before every run that needs an
/// untouched home: state holds absolute paths, so a copy elsewhere is not independent.
pub struct IntentHome {
    slot: tempfile::TempDir,   // <slot>/: env/, pristine/, row/
    pub home: Home,            // Home::at(<slot>/env, &["wow", "wow_classic_era"])
    pristine: PathBuf,         // <slot>/pristine: the home as built
    row: PathBuf,              // <slot>/row: the home after a row's setup
}

pub fn intent_home() -> IntentHome;

impl IntentHome {
    pub const CLIENTS: [&'static str; 3] = ["era", "retail", "wotlk"]; // id order
    pub fn env_root(&self) -> &Path;                   // self.home.env.root()
    pub fn work_dir(&self) -> PathBuf;                 // <env root>/work, empty
    pub fn client_dir(&self, id: &str) -> PathBuf;     // era, retail or wotlk
    pub fn reset(&self);                               // the pristine home again
    pub fn save_row(&self);                            // snapshot the current home as <slot>/row
    pub fn reset_row(&self);                           // <slot>/row again
    pub fn records(&self) -> BTreeMap<String, String>; // see below
    pub fn cmd<'l>(&self, log: &'l TestLog, argv: &[&str]) -> Cmd<'l>; // log.cmd(&self.home, argv).cwd(self.work_dir())
}

/// Files a command may write even when it fails, never part of `records()`.
pub const VOLATILE_STATE: &[&str] = &["net.log", "net.log.1"];
```

**What the home holds** (decided while writing this bead, filling in the plan's description "two Battle.net clients, `retail` and `era`; one legacy client, `wotlk`; managed DBM on `retail` and `era`, and Questie; HTTP fixtures for their sources"):
1. A Battle.net root with `wow` and `wow_classic_era` (ids `retail` and `era`).
2. A `WTF/` on each Battle.net client under the fake names (`Wtf::at(client).saved_variables("DBM-Core", 512)`, and `Questie` on `era`), so every run's privacy check has names to miss.
3. HTTP fixtures, synthetic (written by `common::http` into the home's fixture scenario and replayed through `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES` exactly as recorded ones are), not the recorded catalog scenario: the recorded zips are large and pinned to live data, while the corpus needs a few small, deterministic releases.
   - DBM (`https://github.com/DeadlyBossMods/DeadlyBossMods`): tag `12.1.14` (asset `DBM-12.1.14.zip`, flavors `[("mainline", 120_105), ("classic", 11_509)]`, folders `DBM-Core/` and `DBM-GUI/`, each with one TOC `## Interface: 11509, 120105`).

4. Through the binary, in this order, each exiting 0: `install dbm -t retail`, `install dbm -t era`, `install questie -t era` (by catalog name, so the records carry the catalog names `DBM` and `Questie`); `home.with_custom(CustomRoot::at(<env root>/pserver/wotlk))` (`targets add`, a 3.3.5a root, id `wotlk`, asserted); `targets default retail`.
5. After the installs, in the same scenario: DBM tag `12.1.20` served as latest (`gh_release`, which replaces `releases/latest`), and the release memo aged by 24 hours as `Home::installed_behind` does, so the next online check asks the source and sees `12.1.20`. DBM is behind on both clients on purpose: a hook that let `update dbm retail` through would update DBM and change the hashes, so the corpus catches it.
6. `gh:o/r` tag `v1` (`R/R.toc`, `## Interface: 120105`, flavor `mainline`), for the fix `install https://github.com/o/r`; and `search`'s sources: a WoWInterface file list with one entry (`wowi_filelist`), Tukui's list (`tukui_list(&[elvui()])`) and GitHub's search for `unknownthing` with no repository (`github_search`).
