title: Tests: the command, flag, value and argument rows of the starting set
description:
Part 3 of 4 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4 (The run-the-fix corpus). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

Leaves named in this section: A1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1`, per-command facts in `COMMANDS`, and `auth github`).

C4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4`) builds the run-the-fix corpus of M4-D15 for checkpoint criterion 5 ("a corpus of at least 60 wrong invocations covers … command, flag and value typos …; each yields its documented error with a `fix_argv` that parses and runs on the corpus home to its documented exit code; no fix turns the user's verb into a different command that changes something") and goal G-M4-2 ("the first guess works"). Part 1 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4.1) built the corpus home `common::intent_home()` (clients `era`, `retail`, `wotlk`; default target `retail`; DBM on `retail` and `era` at 12.1.14 with 12.1.20 served; Questie on `era`; fixtures for `gh:o/r` and for `search`'s sources). Part 2 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4.2) built the harness in `tests/contract/intent_corpus.rs`: each `CORPUS` row's wrong argv runs on a restore of the home with `--json --progress json` appended; its code and exit, its pinned fix (`Fix::Argv`, or `Fix::FirstAlternative` when `fix_argv` is `null`), the contract (`support::check`), privacy and the verb rule (each fix and alternative is `help …`, a command that only reads, or one of the row's `verbs`) are checked; an erroring row must leave the client trees and `records()` unchanged and make no request; then the fix runs on an independent restore and must reach one of the row's fix exits. Part 2 added the 21 starting rows of area C's hooks and two collision rows.

**This part adds the 28 starting rows of Appendix C.2 whose surfaces exist at `c0ab5e9`**: mistyped commands, flags and values, argument mistakes and one warning whose fix is a rerun. These fixes come from the usage-fix machinery that M2 and M3 built (`cli::usage_error`, `src/cli.rs:604-773`) and from the commands' own errors; until now only their parsing was tested. It is its own step because each row must be checked against the binary (several of the binary's fixes differ from the plan's Fix column, below), and because a row that fails here points at a different code path than part 2's hooks.

**The rule each row follows** (M4-D15, restated): the row states its wrong argv, the code and exit of its error (or success with a warning), the exact fix the binary gives, and the fix's exit on the corpus home. Rejected by the plan: requiring every fix to exit 0. Decided while writing this bead: the fix is pinned (a fix that silently degrades to `omaddons help` still exits 0), and the binary's fix is pinned where it differs from Appendix C.2's Fix column, as long as it parses, reaches the row's exit and obeys the verb rule; no product fix is changed only to match the column.

**Facts this part relies on** (as of `c0ab5e9`):
- The fixes the binary gives, observed by running each wrong argv with `--json` through the debug binary on an empty synthetic home: see the table of section 1 (the "Pinned fix" column is that observation). Differences from Appendix C.2's Fix column: `history --since yesterday` → `omaddons history --since 1d` (a corrected value; the plan wrote `help history`); `backup list 01M6` → `omaddons backup list` (the message says the id is too short; the plan wrote `help backup list`); `errors --limit 0` → `omaddons errors --limit 10` (the plan wrote `help errors`); `copy --from era --to era` → `omaddons targets` (`src/app/copy.rs:186-194`; the plan wrote `help copy`); `status --cached --deep` → `omaddons help status` (the plan wrote `status --deep`); `export --overwrite` → `omaddons export --overwrite --write` (the plan wrote `help export`); `update --version 12.1.14 dbm` → `omaddons install --version 12.1.14 dbm`, with the alternative `omaddons pin --version 12.1.14 dbm` (the plan wrote the same tokens in another order); `auth github shwo` → `omaddons help auth` (the plan wrote `auth github status`, which A1's `auth github` subcommand may give).
- `sync <missing file>` is `not_found` (exit 3) with the prose fix "pass the file: `omaddons sync <path>`", `fix_argv: null`, and the one alternative `omaddons help sync` (`src/app/sync.rs:402-418`).
- `install http://github.com/o/r` is `ref_invalid`, exit 2 ("is not https; omaddons fetches over https only").
- `install unknownthing -t retail` is `not_found` (exit 3) from the name lookup (`src/sources/refs.rs:501-589`: installed addons, the catalog, a path in the working directory), fix `omaddons search <word>`.
- `--offline` answers from the release memo with `stale_check` (`src/resolve/cache.rs:483-505`), whose fix becomes the same command online (`src/output/notes.rs:104-116`).
- `install` without `-t` uses the configured default target (`choose_target`, `src/app/install.rs:825-850`); the corpus home's default is `retail`.
- `targets rm <id>` removes a registered target even when it manages addons (`src/app/targets.rs:469-505`); `config` with no subcommand lists the settings; `export` is a mutating path (`src/app/mod.rs:129`) and `--write` writes `<config>/omaddons/addons.toml`.

## Technical Approach

Leaves named in this section: C1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.1`, misplaced clients before and after the verb), C2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.2`, a client named as an addon, and `-t all`), C3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.3`, closest client id on `target_not_found`).

### 1. The rows

Append to `CORPUS` in `tests/contract/intent_corpus.rs`, grouped by kind in this order, all `Origin::Plan`, no setup:

| # | Kind | Wrong argv | Code (exit) | Pinned fix | Fix exit | `verbs` | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | CommandTypo | `instal dbm -t retail` | `usage` (2) | `omaddons help install` | 0 | — | a mutating guess becomes help |
| 2 | CommandTypo | `statsu` | `usage` (2) | `omaddons status` | 0 | — | a read-only guess runs |
| 3 | CommandTypo | `lsit` | `usage` (2) | `omaddons list` | 0 | — | |
| 4 | CommandTypo | `reinstall dbm -t retail` | `usage` (2) | `omaddons install dbm -t retail --reinstall` | 0 | `install` | a synonym keeps the user's intent |
| 5 | CommandTypo | `targets remove era` | `usage` (2) | `omaddons targets rm era` | 0 | `targets rm` | a synonym (user verb); the fix unregisters `era` on its copy |
| 6 | CommandTypo | `config ls` | `usage` (2) | `omaddons config` | 0 | `config` | |
| 7 | CommandTypo | `backup restor 01M6Q2VA` | `usage` (2) | `omaddons help backup restore` | 0 | — | a nested mutating guess becomes help |
| 8 | CommandTypo | `omarchy instal` | `usage` (2) | `omaddons help omarchy install` | 0 | — | |
| 9 | FlagTypo | `upgrade --al` | `usage` (2) | `omaddons upgrade --all` | 0 | `update` | the alias is kept; the fix updates DBM on both clients |
| 10 | FlagTypo | `install dbm --chanel beta -t retail` | `usage` (2) | `omaddons install dbm --channel beta -t retail` | 0 | `install` | |
| 11 | FlagTypo | `status --json=1` | `usage` (2) | `omaddons status` | 0 | `status` | a refused presentation flag is dropped |
| 12 | FlagTypo | `status --jsno` | `usage` (2) | `omaddons status` | 0 | `status` | |
| 13 | FlagTypo | `status --cached --deep` | `usage` (2) | `omaddons help status` | 0 | `status` | conflicting flags |
| 14 | FlagTypo | `list --protectd -t wotlk` | `usage` (2) | `omaddons list --protected -t wotlk` | 0 | `list` | |
| 15 | FlagTypo | `export --overwrite` | `usage` (2) | `omaddons export --overwrite --write` | 0 | `export` | the fix writes `addons.toml` on its copy |
| 16 | ValueTypo | `install dbm --channel betaa -t retail` | `usage` (2) | `omaddons install dbm --channel beta -t retail` | 0 | `install` | |
| 17 | ValueTypo | `history --since yesterday` | `usage` (2) | `omaddons history --since 1d` | 0 | `history` | |
| 18 | ValueTypo | `undo --last-by robot` | `usage` (2) | `omaddons help undo` | 0 | `undo` | nothing is close to `robot`: help, never a guessed actor |
| 19 | ValueTypo | `backup list 01M6` | `usage` (2) | `omaddons backup list` | 0 | `backup list` | |
| 20 | ValueTypo | `errors --limit 0` | `usage` (2) | `omaddons errors --limit 10` | 0 | `errors` | |
| 21 | ValueTypo | `install http://github.com/o/r` | `ref_invalid` (2) | `omaddons install https://github.com/o/r` | 0 | `install` | installs `gh:o/r` on `retail` (the default target) |
| 22 | ValueTypo | `auth github shwo` | `usage` (2) | `omaddons help auth` | 0 | `auth` | changes when A1 lands (section 3) |
| 23 | Argument | `update --version 12.1.14 dbm` | `usage` (2) | `omaddons install --version 12.1.14 dbm` | 0 | `install`, `pin` | a given version is an install; pins DBM at 12.1.14 on `retail` |
| 24 | Argument | `install unknownthing -t retail` | `not_found` (3) | `omaddons search unknownthing` | 0 | `install` | the fix only reads |
| 25 | Argument | `search` | `usage` (2) | `omaddons help search` | 0 | `search` | a required argument missing |
| 26 | Argument | `copy --from era --to era` | `usage` (2) | `omaddons targets` | 0 | `copy` | |
| 27 | Argument | `sync missing.toml` | `not_found` (3) | `Fix::FirstAlternative`: `omaddons help sync` | 0 | `sync` | the fix is prose with `<path>`; the first alternative runs; resolved in the work directory |
| 28 | WarningFix | `--offline outdated` | `Warning stale_check` (exit 0) | `omaddons outdated` | 0 | `outdated` | the warning's fix reruns online |

Row 24's pinned fix is whatever the binary gives for `-t retail` (the lookup's fix is `omaddons search <word>`; if it keeps `-t retail`, pin that). Row 28's fix is `RunNotes::rerun_stale`'s argv (the same command without `--offline` and presentation flags).

**`verbs` notes** (the verb rule admits a fix or alternative that runs one of `verbs`): row 23 names `install` and `pin`, because the user's intent, this version held, is an install that pins (the fix) or a pin with `--version` (the alternative the binary offers); `update` installs only the newest, and both keep the user's arguments; the contract suite's corpus treats `reinstall` (row 4) the same way. Row 9's `upgrade` is an alias of `update`, whose canonical path the rule compares.

Decided while writing this bead (confirm or adjust in the close comment):
- **The binary's fix is pinned** where it differs from Appendix C.2's Fix column (the eight rows listed in Background), because each reaches the row's exit and obeys the verb rule; changing working fixes to match the column is not this bead's work. The close comment lists each with both fixes.
- **`sync missing.toml` runs its first alternative.** Its fix is prose with a `<path>` only the user can fill (common rule 8: a fix that needs a value only the user has carries no argv), and the plan's "fix" `omaddons help sync` is that alternative.
- **`export --overwrite`'s fix writes** (`--write`): it keeps the user's verb and adds the flag the user's `--overwrite` presupposes; the verb rule admits it (`verbs` `export`), and it runs on the fix's own copy.

### 2. Rows that change when another leaf lands

- `auth github shwo` pins `omaddons help auth` while `auth` takes positional values (`src/app/auth.rs:37-46`). A1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1`) makes `github` a real subcommand of `auth`; the typo's fix may then become `omaddons auth github status`. If A1 has landed when this part does, pin what the binary gives then; if A1 lands later, A1's commit updates the row (it changes the surface; common rule 6 lists the changed fix).
- A row whose fix C1, C2 or C3 changed (a hook that now also fires here) is a finding: check the new fix against the verb rule and the exit, pin it, and list it.

### 3. When a row fails

A row that fails because the home lacks a fixture (a fix's request to an unserved URL, visible in `net.log`): add the fixture to `intent_home()` (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4.1's module), never to one row. A row that fails because a landed leaf misbehaves: fix it here when it is a one-line change to an error's fix; otherwise file a bug `--deps discovered-from:omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4` carrying the row, make this subtask wait on it (`br dep add`), and leave it open until the bug closes. Never commit a failing row or a weakened expectation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `CORPUS` holds the 28 rows of section 1 (with the binary's fix pinned where it differs from the table after the checks of section 1), each passing the harness: the wrong run's exit and code (or success with `stale_check`), the pinned fix (`fix_argv`, or the first alternative for `sync missing.toml`), the fix's exit on an independent restore, `support::check` and `assert_private_all` on every envelope, and the verb rule over the fix and every alternative.
- [ ] No erroring row of section 1 changes a client tree or `records()`, and none adds a `net.log` line.
- [ ] `corpus_command_typos`, `corpus_flag_typos`, `corpus_value_typos`, `corpus_argument_mistakes` and `corpus_warning_fixes` each run their rows; the structural tests of part 2 (`corpus_rows_are_unique`, `corpus_fixes_parse_and_name_commands_that_exist`, `corpus_fixes_follow_the_verb_rule`) still pass over the larger table.
- [ ] The close comment lists every row whose pinned fix differs from Appendix C.2's Fix column, with both fixes, and any fixture or product change a row required.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files.

## Test Plan

Leaves named in this section: T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs).

### Unit tests

None new: the rows are data, and the structural tests of part 2 (`corpus_rows_are_unique`, `corpus_fixes_parse_and_name_commands_that_exist`, `corpus_fixes_follow_the_verb_rule`, `case_names_are_safe_file_names`) cover them; each assertion names the row's case and shows its argv.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

- `corpus_command_typos` (8 rows), `corpus_flag_typos` (7), `corpus_value_typos` (7), `corpus_argument_mistakes` (5), `corpus_warning_fixes` (1), each on its own `intent_home()`, every row through `run_row`: steps `restore`, `before`, `wrong`, `after` (erroring rows), `restore for the fix`, `fix`, with the assertions of part 2's harness after each.
- Specific expectations to assert inside the rows' runs: row 27's wrong envelope has `error.fix_argv: null` and `error.details.path` under the work directory; row 28's wrong envelope has `meta.offline: true` and its run adds no `net.log` line, while its fix run adds at least one; row 21's fix envelope names the target `retail`.

### Logging

Each row runs in its own case log under its kind's `tlog!()` log, with part 2's steps (`restore`, `before`, `wrong`, `after`, `restore for the fix`, `fix`) and records (three `log.tree`, the records digest, the `net.log` lines of each run). A failure prints the `RowFailure` report with both envelopes and the transcript path, and T1's guard prints `test log: <path>` and the last 20 steps. `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG=verbose cargo test --test contract intent_corpus` echoes every step live.

## Considerations

- **These fixes are M2's and M3's.** A failing row here is more likely a gap in `cli::usage_error` or a command's own error than in area C's hooks; the report's two envelopes show which.
- **Rows whose fix changes state** (rows 5, 9, 10, 15, 16, 21, 23) run their fix on an independent restore, so nothing they write reaches another row.
- **Gate time:** about 56 more binary runs, spread over five parallel kinds. Record the new wall-clock time in the close comment.
- **Hot spot:** `tests/contract/intent_corpus.rs` only; keep the rows grouped by kind and in this order. The category and count tests (`every_landed_category_has_a_row`, `plan_rows_are_never_dropped`) land in part 4, which needs these rows.

## Background

Leaves named in this section: F3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.3`, the doctor's state-file detectors).

C4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4`) builds the run-the-fix corpus of M4-D15 for checkpoint criterion 5: "a corpus of at least 60 wrong invocations covers: misplaced client names before and after the verb, a client name given as an addon, `-t all`, client-id typos, command, flag and value typos, `apply` for `adopt --apply`, and doctor verb typos", each fix run on the corpus home to its documented exit. Parts 1 to 3 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4.1, omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4.2, omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4.3) built the corpus home `common::intent_home()`, the harness in `tests/contract/intent_corpus.rs` (each `CORPUS` row's wrong argv on a byte-exact restore of the home, its code, exit, pinned fix, contract, privacy and verb rule checked, the home hashed unchanged around an erroring row, the fix run on an independent restore to the row's exit), and 51 rows: 49 of Appendix C.2's 56 starting rows and two collision rows.

**This part handles the rows whose surfaces other leaves own.** Seven starting rows name commands that do not exist at `c0ab5e9` (`capabilities`, `robot-docs`, `robot-docs guide`, `completions`, and three doctor verbs), and the plan gives D5, D9, E3 and E6 eleven more (`apply`, `plans show`, the doctor verbs). Common rule 18: "Once C4 has landed, a leaf that adds a command or an intent hook adds its corpus rows. Whichever of C4 and the command leaf lands second adds them." Some of those leaves land before this one (the computed schedule puts C4 at t = 18–20, after most of them), some after. This part writes every such row, runs the ones whose surfaces exist, and keeps the others in a pending table that a test forces into the corpus the moment their surfaces land. It also adds the count, category and checkpoint tests. It is the last part because those tests count the rows parts 2 and 3 added.

**The decisions it applies** (restated):
- **M4-D15:** at least 60 entries; "C4 lands 56, the surface leaves add 11"; each later leaf that adds a command or a hook adds corpus rows (D5 for `apply`, D9 for `plans show`, E3 and E6 for `doctor`). H4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`) checks the count of at least 60.
- **M4-D27:** `omaddons apply` alone is `usage` with the fix `omaddons help apply` (alternative `omaddons adopt --apply`; read-only help first, because `adopt --apply` mutates); `omaddons adopt apply` is `usage` with the fix `omaddons adopt --apply` (the user's own verb); `omaddons apply <word>` naming an unmanaged folder is `not_found` with the alternative `omaddons adopt <word>`. Rejected: renaming `apply`.
- **M4-D40:** inside the `doctor` tree a usage error exits 64 (`usage_error`), a lookup error 66; a root-level typo (`doctr`) uses the general dictionary (exit 2).
- **Common rule 18**, made mechanical here (decided while writing this bead): a pending table plus a test that fails as soon as a pending row's surfaces exist.

**Facts this part relies on:**
- `app::COMMANDS` (`src/app/mod.rs:121-165`) lists every command path; at `c0ab5e9` it has none of `capabilities`, `robot-docs`, `completions`, `apply`, `plans show` or `doctor`. Each command leaf adds its rows in the commit that adds its clap variant (DEC-1).
- The surface leaves' beads decided these rows (restated in the table of section 2): A5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5`) makes bare `robot-docs` run `help robot-docs` (exit 0) and adds `robot-docs schema instal` and `robot-docs erors`; A7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.7`) adds `completion bash`; B3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3`) adds `robot-docs install-skil` (fix `help robot-docs install-skill`) and `robot-docs install-skill --dry-rn` (fix exit 3 on a home with no `$HOME/.claude`); D5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`) writes `aply 01M8Q2VA` and declares `apply nosuchid0`'s fix `help apply`; D9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.9`) declares fix exit 3 for `plans show` of a plan the home does not hold; E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`) moves the `--explain` row to `fm-schemas-state-version-newer` (F3's `fm-schemas-state-corrupt` does not exist when E3 lands), gives `doctor --fix` the fix `omaddons help doctor` until E6, and declares "0 or 1" for diagnose fixes (a finding is a successful run with exit 1); E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`) changes that fix to `omaddons doctor fix --dry-run` and adds `doctor fxi`; E7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7`) needs one committed repair (made by E6's test fixer `fm-test-write` with `OMADDONS_TEST_FIXERS=1`, debug build) as a row setup, and adds `undo --run <a doctor run id>`.
- The harness of part 2 supports a row `setup` (binary commands, then a snapshot so both runs see identical ids) and `{name}` captures, for E7's rows.

## Technical Approach

Leaves named in this section: A4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`, `omaddons capabilities`), A5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5`, `robot-docs schema` and `robot-docs errors`), A7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.7`, `omaddons completions`), B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`, the guide renderer and `robot-docs guide`), B3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3`, `robot-docs install-skill`), C4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4`, this bead), D5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`, `omaddons apply`), D9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.9`, `omaddons plans show`), E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, `doctor diagnose` and `explain`, with the doctor's exit dictionary), E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`, `doctor fix`), E7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7`, undo of repairs and `doctor undo`), H4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`, the README final pass), H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the M4 checkpoint and the first tag).

### 1. The pending table

    pub row: Row,
    /// `app::COMMANDS` paths the row needs: its wrong argv's and its fix's.
    pub needs: &'static [&'static str],
    /// The leaf that owns the surface, and promotes the row if it lands after this bead.
    pub leaf: &'static str,
}

pub const PENDING: &[Pending] = &[ /* the rows of section 2 not promoted */ ];

`fn landed(path: &str) -> bool { omaddons::app::COMMANDS.iter().any(|c| c.name == path) }`.

### 3. The tests this part adds

- **`pending_rows_wait_for_a_surface_that_has_not_landed`** (gate): for each `PENDING` entry, at least one of `needs` is not in `app::COMMANDS`; otherwise it fails with `pending row <argv> (surface of <leaf>): its surfaces <needs> exist; move it from PENDING to CORPUS and make it pass (common rule 18)`. It also asserts every `needs` path is spelled as a `COMMANDS` path would be (lowercase words separated by single spaces).
- **`pending_rows_are_unique_and_not_in_the_corpus`** (gate): no argv appears twice across `CORPUS` and `PENDING`.
- **`plan_rows_are_never_dropped`** (gate): the `Origin::Plan` rows of `CORPUS` and `PENDING` together number exactly 67 (Appendix C.2's 56 plus D5's 4, D9's 2, E3's 4 and E6's 1). The message lists the plan rows per kind. A leaf that adapts a plan row keeps it `Plan`; one that adds a row of its own marks it `Leaf(<key>)`.
- **`every_landed_category_has_a_row`** (gate): `CORPUS` holds at least one row of each of `MisplacedBeforeVerb`, `MisplacedAfterVerb`, `ClientAsAddon`, `TargetAll`, `TargetTypo`, `CommandTypo`, `FlagTypo` and `ValueTypo` (the categories whose surfaces exist without any other M4 leaf).
- **`the_corpus_meets_checkpoint_criterion_5`** (checkpoint only, `#[ignore = "checkpoint: H4 and H6 run it once every M4 surface has landed"]`): `CORPUS.len() >= 60`; `PENDING` is empty; every criterion-5 category has a row (the eight above plus `ApplyForAdopt` and `DoctorVerb`). It prints `intent corpus: <n> rows` and the count per kind and per origin, and on failure names each pending row with its leaf and each missing category. Command: `cargo test --test contract intent_corpus::the_corpus_meets_checkpoint_criterion_5 -- --ignored --exact`. It reads nothing outside the repository, so the `SKIP` rule never applies.

### 4. The close comment of the leaf

The agent closing this part (the last) closes C4 too, with a close comment that lists: the rows promoted here and the rows still pending, each with its surface's leaf; every row (all parts) whose pinned fix differs from Appendix C.2's Fix column, with both fixes; any fixture or product change a row required; the wall-clock time of `cargo test --test contract intent_corpus`; that no wire name was added (common rule 6); and each "Decided while writing this bead" item of the leaf as confirmed or adjusted. Then comment on the bead of each leaf that owns a pending row (`br comments add <leaf id> "C4 has landed: your corpus rows are in PENDING in tests/contract/intent_corpus.rs; promote them in the commit that adds the surface (pending_rows_wait_for_a_surface_that_has_not_landed fails until you do)"`), so the agent working that leaf learns of it before its gate tells it.

## Acceptance Criteria

Leaves named in this section: E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, `doctor diagnose` and `explain`, with the doctor's exit dictionary).

- [ ] `Pending` and `PENDING` exist; every row of section 2 is in exactly one of `CORPUS` (all its `needs` landed, run and passing, the binary's fix pinned) and `PENDING` (some need missing, written as in section 2, with its surface's leaf).
- [ ] Each promoted row passes the harness: its exit and code, its pinned fix, the fix's exit on an independent restore, `support::check` (doctor mode for a doctor-tree argv once E3 has landed), `assert_private_all` and the verb rule; an erroring promoted row changes no client tree or record and makes no request.
- [ ] `pending_rows_wait_for_a_surface_that_has_not_landed`, `pending_rows_are_unique_and_not_in_the_corpus`, `plan_rows_are_never_dropped` (exactly 67) and `every_landed_category_has_a_row` pass in the gate.
- [ ] `the_corpus_meets_checkpoint_criterion_5` exists, is `#[ignore]`d with its reason, prints the counts, and asserts at least 60 rows, an empty `PENDING` and every criterion-5 category.
- [ ] The close comment of section 4 is written, and the bead of each leaf that owns a pending row has the comment of section 4.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files.

## Test Plan

Leaves named in this section: E7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7`, undo of repairs and `doctor undo`), H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the M4 checkpoint and the first tag).

### Unit tests

In `tests/contract/intent_corpus.rs`:
- `pending_rows_wait_for_a_surface_that_has_not_landed` and `pending_rows_are_unique_and_not_in_the_corpus` (section 3), plus a table over the readiness helper itself, `fn ready(needs: &[&str], commands: &[&str]) -> bool`, one name per case: `all_present` (`["status"]` in `["status", "list"]` → true); `one_missing` (`["doctor undo", "doctor fix"]` with only `doctor fix` → false); `none_present` → false; `empty_needs` → true (a pending row must name at least one need: a separate assertion that every `PENDING` entry's `needs` is not empty).
- `plan_rows_are_never_dropped`, `every_landed_category_has_a_row` (section 3).

Each assertion message names the row (its case name and argv) and shows the needs and the paths found.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

- The `corpus_<kind>` tests of part 2 run every promoted row with the rest of its kind (`corpus_command_typos`, `corpus_value_typos`, `corpus_flag_typos`, `corpus_apply_for_adopt`, `corpus_doctor_verbs`), steps `restore`, `setup` (E7's rows), `before`, `wrong`, `after`, `restore for the fix`, `fix`, with the harness's assertions after each. A kind with no active row logs "no active row; K pending" with the pending argvs and their owners.

### Logging

As part 2: each row in its own case log with its steps and tree records; the kind's log notes each pending row of that kind with its leaf (so a run shows what is not yet proven); the checkpoint test prints its counts per kind and origin to stdout and names every pending row and missing category on failure.

### Checkpoint-only

`cargo test --test contract intent_corpus::the_corpus_meets_checkpoint_criterion_5 -- --ignored --exact`, run by H4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`) for its "at least 60" check and by H6 for criterion 5. No `SKIP` exists for it; a failure means the criterion is unmet.

## Considerations

Leaves named in this section: E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`, `doctor fix`).

- **Why a forcing test.** Common rule 18 relies on each surface leaf remembering the corpus. The test turns the memory into a gate failure in the very commit that adds the last needed surface, with a message saying what to do, so no surface can land with its rows unproven. The cost to the surface leaf is moving rows already written and making them pass.
- **What could go wrong.** A surface whose canonical path differs from a row's `needs` (a leaf named its command differently) would leave the row pending forever without failing the gate; the checkpoint test catches it (`PENDING` must be empty), and section 4's comment tells each surface leaf which rows are its. A leaf that changes a fix on purpose (E6's `doctor --fix`) updates the promoted row in its own commit.
- **Rows that are not 0.** `plans show` of an absent plan (3), `install-skill --dry-run` with no `$HOME/.claude` (3) and the diagnose fixes (0 or 1) are correct fixes that do not exit 0 on the corpus home; M4-D15 rejected requiring 0 for exactly this reason.
- **Hot spot:** `tests/contract/intent_corpus.rs` only; after this part, other leaves edit it (promotions, new rows), so keep `PENDING` grouped by leaf.
- **No wire name** is added; common rules 16 and 17 do not apply.

## Dependencies

- Parent: C4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4`, the run-the-fix corpus).
- Before it: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4.3 (its count and category tests count part 3's rows; parts 1 and 2 before that). Its edge from T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs) is added at filing.
- After it: none among its siblings. Closing it closes C4, which unblocks H4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`, the count check and README reconciliation) and T2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.2`, slice 1's demo item "the corpus runs").
- Related: the leaves that own section 2's surfaces, A4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`), A5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5`), A7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.7`), B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`), B3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3`), D5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`), D9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.9`), E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`), E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`), E7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7`): each promotes its pending rows when it lands after this bead.

- `the_corpus_meets_checkpoint_criterion_5`, `#[ignore = "checkpoint: H4 and H6 run it once every M4 surface has landed"]`. Run today, it fails as it should: "intent corpus: 51 rows", the 25 pending rows, and the missing categories `apply_for_adopt` and `doctor_verb`.

title: Epic: M4 previews and stored plans
description:
## Background

Area D is the previews-and-stored-plans area of M4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`, the milestone epic: the agent surface, the doctor and the first tag). It makes every command that changes addons previewable and bindable to that preview. It stores each preview as a typed plan that `omaddons apply <plan_id>` executes exactly, target by target. And it lets an agent that lost an `apply`'s output find out what committed. It has nine leaves, all in slice 2 ("Preview, then apply exactly"):

- D1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1`, `precondition::of_plan` and the approval witness for engine commands): the token of an engine command, computed from the engine's own plan, with a per-target witness of everything the plan reads, replaces or removes;
- D2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2`, `--if-match` on `install`, `update`, `sync` and `copy`): the release-bearing commands bind, on every path, dry runs and no-op runs included;
- D3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.3`, `--if-match` on `pin`, `unpin` and `adopt`): the records-only commands bind;
- D8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8`, the approval checked again under the commit lock): the witness and the re-judged operations are compared again inside the commit window, and each swap rename checks the identity of what it moves;
- D4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`, the plan store): the typed intent, the typed approval summary, and `<cache>/plans/` with hard quotas;
- D5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`, `omaddons apply`): the command, its plan lease, its forced revalidation and its typed execution;
- D9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.9`, `omaddons plans show`): read-only inspection of an approval, reconciled with history;
- D6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.6`, plan retention: blob pins and sweeps): unexpired plans pin their archives, and expired plans are swept after commits;
- D7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.7`, release drift and apply races, end to end): the area's verification leaf.

The leaves weigh 21 units: four size-L (D1, D2, D4, D5), four size-M (D3, D7, D8, D9) and one size-S (D6). The plan's second review round added D8 and D9 and resized D1 and D4 from M to L. Four leaves are design gates: D1, D2, D5 and D8.

**What the area adds to the contract** (each leaf lists the names it actually added in its close comment, common rule 6):

- two commands: `apply <PLAN_ID> [--dry-run]` (group Change, mutating, general dictionary, `binds: false`, stores no plan) and `plans show <PLAN_ID>` (group Look, read-only, offline);
- `--if-match` on seven more paths (`install`, `update`, `pin`, `unpin`, `adopt`, `sync`, `copy`), so `BINDING_COMMANDS` grows from five to twelve; E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`, `doctor fix`) and E8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.8`, `doctor gc`) add their two doctor paths later;
- data keys: `precondition` on those seven commands' data (a token under `--dry-run`, `null` on real runs); `plan_id`, `plan_expires_at` and `approval` on every storable command's data (`null` on real runs); `history`'s `entries[].plan`; `capabilities.build_id`;
- shapes: `apply`'s data (one wrapper variant per storable command), `plans show`'s data, and `approval {routine, reasons[], selection[], scope}`;
- closed sets: `outcomes[].status` (`committed`, `unchanged`, `stale`, `failed`), the `plans show` states (`pending`, `completed`, `partial`, `expired`, `unknown`) and the approval reasons;
- errors and warnings: the warning `plan_not_stored`; the first use of `plan_not_found` (exit 3, reserved since M1), which also covers an unreadable plan file (`details.reason: "unreadable"`, `details.path`); `plan_stale` gains `details.reason` (`expired`, `binary_changed`, `input_missing`, `already_applied`), `details.path` and `details.txs`; `locked` gains `details.lease` and the lease holder;
- the recommendation action `apply`;
- files: `<cache>/plans/<plan_id>.json` (kind `plan` 1.0), `<cache>/plans/<plan_id>.lease` and `<cache>/plans/.lock`;
- six constants in `src/limits.rs`: `PLANS_MAX_FILES` (512), `PLANS_MAX_BYTES` (32 MiB), `PLAN_MAX_BYTES` (256 KiB), `PLANS_SWEEP_MAX` (64), `PLAN_LEASE_TIMEOUT` (30 s) and `PLAN_EVIDENCE_LINES_MAX` (20,000);
- the build-time variable `OMADDONS_BUILD_ID`, stamped by `build.rs` and never read from the environment at run time;
- fsx internals that are not wire names: `lock::Lease`, `LockUse::Expired` and the prune kind `PlanLease`.

Once the area has landed, the preview-then-apply loop looks like this:

```text
$ omaddons install weakauras dbm -t era --dry-run
era: would install WeakAuras 5.22.1 (5 folders)
era: would install DBM 12.1.15 (4 folders, 4 skipped this client does not load)
Plan 01M8Q2… stored for 24 hours. Run exactly this: omaddons apply 01M8Q2…

$ omaddons apply 01M8Q2
era: installed WeakAuras 5.22.1 (5 folders)
era: installed DBM 12.1.15 (4 folders)
tx 01M8Q3… · undo: omaddons undo 01M8Q3…
```

Under `--json` the dry run's data carries `"precondition":"pc1:…"`, `"plan_id":"01M8Q2…"`, `"plan_expires_at":"…"` and `"approval":{"routine":false,"reasons":["dependency_added"],"selection":[…],"scope":{…}}`, and `commands[]` holds `{"action":"apply","argv":["omaddons","apply","01M8Q2…"],…}`. `apply`'s data is `{plan_id, applied: {command, display_argv}, approved, result, outcomes[]}`, with one `{target, key, status, tx, error_code}` per target.

### Why it matters to the milestone

This area is the milestone goal **G-M4-3, what was previewed is what runs, target by target**:

- Every command that changes addons can be previewed with `--dry-run` and then run bound to that preview, by token (`--if-match`) or by stored plan (`apply <plan_id>`).
- The guarantee is per target. On each target the bound run commits exactly the operations the preview approved, or none of them. A run over several targets commits one transaction per target, as it always has, so it can end partial after a late conflict or an I/O failure. It then reports each target as committed, unchanged, stale or failed, with its transaction id, and never calls the whole run atomic.
- The approval covers what the preview saw, not only the record generations: every file of every folder the plan replaces or removes, clean or edited; every name it creates; its local inputs; a copy's source folders; the rules that judged it. The commit checks all of it again under the lock, and the operations it re-judges there must equal the approved ones.
- What the guarantee is against: other omaddons processes are serialized by the global lock and by one applier per plan. Other writers (an editor, a file-sync tool) are caught up to the moment before the first change, and each move then re-checks only the identity of what it moves. omaddons promises no compare-and-swap against arbitrary writers, because the filesystem offers none.
- "Anything else" is named precisely: a new release, a change on an affected client, another binary, an expired plan, a missing input, a plan already applied.
- An approval can be inspected and reconciled: `plans show <plan_id>` says, offline and without writing, what was approved and what history records of it.
- The bar widget applies a plan directly only when it matches the row the user pressed and needs no further approval. That last part is G1's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1`, the widget previews and applies plans); this area gives it the typed approval summary it decides on.

It also carries promises of the vision bead `omad-vision-8qa`:

- its D31, "what a human approved is exactly what runs", which M3 met only for destructive commands;
- its §7 M4 checkpoint item "a release landing in between yields `plan_stale`, never a different install", unmet at `c0ab5e9`;
- its §5.11, "mutating buttons first fetch a plan and then call `apply <plan_id>` for the plan shown" (M3-D9 deferred it);
- its canonical intent "preview, then apply exactly (`--dry-run`, `apply`)" (vision §5.10), one of the eight intents the guide's recipes run in at most two commands.

And it must keep **G-M4-6, no new risk to the engine's guarantees**: every new write goes through fsx, dry runs still leave `<state>` untouched (a plan is cache), and the global lock is still held only for commit windows (the plan lease is a separate lock, and `apply --dry-run` takes no lock at all).

### What is true today (verified at `c0ab5e9`)

- **Five paths bind.** M3's tokens (M3-D46) are `pc1:` plus four 16-hex fields, the first 64 bits of the SHA-256 of `command`, `targets`, `selection` and `observed`. `BINDING_COMMANDS` lists `remove`, `undo`, `backup restore`, `backup prune` and `errors dismiss` (`src/app/precondition.rs:25-31`), and the CLI refuses `--if-match` on every other path (`check_if_match`, `src/cli.rs:309-338`). A mismatch is a non-retryable `plan_stale` with `details.changed` and the dry run as `fix_argv`.
- **`remove`'s token skips unregistered targets** (`of_remove`, `src/app/precondition.rs:249-251`), and `Precondition.targets` is keyed by `TargetKey` (`src/app/precondition.rs:72`), so it cannot hold a provisional id.
- **Bound dry runs never compare.** `engine::tx::run` checks a binding only outside dry runs: `Some(binding) if !req.dry_run` (`src/engine/tx.rs:404`).
- **No-op paths never reach the engine.** `update` (`src/app/update.rs:312-314`), `sync` (`src/app/sync.rs:673-675`), `copy` (`src/app/copy.rs:288-289`), `pin` (`src/app/pin.rs:245, 306`) and `adopt` (`src/app/adopt/apply.rs:753-777`) return without calling the engine when they have nothing to change, so a bound run there would never check its token.
- **Under the lock, only generations are compared.** `commit_target` compares each record's generation (`src/engine/tx.rs:1050-1056`), then re-judges offline (`src/engine/tx.rs:1105-1141`). Nothing compares the re-judged operations with the approved ones, and nothing re-reads a clean file the preview saw. A hand edit or a hand-installed folder never moves a generation.
- **Hand edits reach planning only as a warning.** `LocalChanges` holds at most `LOCAL_CHANGES_SHOWN` (10) paths, a count and the changed folders, and no digest (`src/engine/plan.rs:749-760`): a display sample, not evidence.
- **Two inputs differ between identical previews.** A deferred asset's `PlannedRelease.url` is the resolved address after a fresh download and `None` after a blob-cache hit (`src/engine/plan.rs:3862-3870, 4833-4861`); Tukui assets are always deferred. `--file <dir>` gets a fresh `dir:<ULID>` release id on every plan (`src/engine/plan.rs:5444`).
- **Builds cannot be told apart.** `tool_version` is `CARGO_PKG_VERSION`, which stays `0.1.0` until M5, and `build.rs` stamps only the widget digest.
- **`update` and `sync` answer from the 15-minute release memo** (`Freshness::Window(SOURCE_RECHECK_MIN_INTERVAL)`, `src/app/update.rs:153-160`), so a release landing between a preview and a re-run within 15 minutes is invisible to them. `Freshness::Revalidate` exists (`src/resolve/cache.rs:36`) and `install`, `copy` and `pin` use it.
- **The commit lock is per target.** `commit_target` takes the global lock itself (`src/engine/tx.rs:1015`), and the target loop records a failed target and moves on (`src/engine/tx.rs:429-468`). Two processes holding one token can each commit a different target of the same plan.
- **The plan plumbing is reserved and unused.** `Paths::plans_dir()` is `<state>/plans` (`src/state/paths.rs:338-340`); prune has `Kind::Plan` under `<state>` with `PruneReason::PlanExpiry` and writer `Mutating` (`src/fsx/prune.rs:368-374`); `PlanId` exists; `plan_not_found` is registered with exit 3 and never raised (`src/error.rs:160`); `PLAN_TTL` is one day (`src/limits.rs:49`). `plan::Plan` derives no `Deserialize` and never reaches the wire, and its working parts (`TargetPlan.work`, `Inspected`) are not serializable.
- **No lease type exists.** `InflightLock::create_scratch` takes a transaction id and opens with `create_new(true)` (`src/fsx/lock.rs:213-231`), so it cannot serve as a per-plan lock.
- **The widget updates without a preview.** Update, Update all and per-addon updates run directly, by design (M3-D9; `omarchy/Model.js:1602-1607`). Only destructive actions preview and confirm with `--if-match`.
- **Dry runs stay out of `<state>`.** The rule "every dry run leaves the state directory untouched (bar `net.log`)" is pinned by `tests/contract/special.rs:251` and `tests/sync.rs:721`.

### The decisions that shape the area

The full decision log is in the decision-log comments on the milestone epic. These are the decisions this area implements, restated:

- **M4-D19: every command that changes addons binds with `--if-match`, using a token computed from the engine's plan** (D1, D2, D3, D8). `precondition::of_plan(command, &Plan, witnesses, extras)` generalizes `of_remove` to `install`, `update`, `pin`, `unpin`, `adopt` (`--apply`, folder names, `--ref`), `sync` and `copy`. The token's four parts: `targets` (each target's key, or its provisional id while unregistered, with its generation); `selection` (per target, canonically ordered: the folder ops, each change, each release, keyed for a deferred asset by `{source, key, release_id, expected_hash, blob_sha256}` without its URL, and `creates_addons_dir`); `observed` (each target's judge digest and approval witness, the `build_id`, a copy's source key and generation, a sync file's SHA-256, update's skip decisions); and `command`. Human text is excluded. Dry runs carry the token in `data.precondition`; real runs carry `null`. The token is checked before staging and again under the lock; bound dry runs compare too, and each no-op path checks it itself. `--file <dir>` gets a stable release id from its listing hash. Why: "what a human approved is exactly what runs" held only for destructive commands, and the `Binding` seam already runs after planning and before staging. Rejected: binding by generation alone (misses release drift, copy's source and every hand edit), and hashing the whole dry-run `data` (human text and volatile fields would change tokens for no reason).
- **M4-D60: every engine-command token carries an approval witness, validated again under the commit lock** (D1, D8; E13, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.13`, resource sets and fsx endpoint predicates, supplies the predicates). The witness is evidence, not a warning. It records every live folder a replace or remove will move (managed or not, edited or clean) as an entry digest over each file's path, size and SHA-256, each symlink's target and each directory, so an added symlink or empty directory counts; every name the plan creates (absent); the client marker's digest; the local inputs; for `copy`, the source folders; for `adopt`, the recorded folders; the dependency choices and the judge digest. A file that is racy-clean against the files index takes its digest from the index, so a clean file costs a `stat`. Under the lock, before the first managed mutation: the generations, then the witness again (an unchanged, settled `TreeStamp` proves unchanged bytes; anything else is re-hashed), then the re-judged operations compared with the approved ones. Each swap rename then carries fsx endpoint predicates (the moved folder's identity, the destination's absence), so a folder replaced at the last moment fails its operation and the target rolls back. Rejected: generations only (misses every writer that is not omaddons); re-hashing every file under the lock (costly, and unnecessary behind a settled stamp); promising an absolute compare-and-swap (Linux offers none).
- **M4-D20: both races bind; stored plans revalidate their sources** (D2, D5, D7). A typed `--if-match` run uses its command's normal freshness, so `update` and `sync` inside the memo window still do exactly what the preview showed. `apply` always revalidates every source it touches, so a release that landed since the preview changes `selection` and the plan is stale. Every probe writes the release memo, stale or not, so the re-preview after a stale `apply` shows the new release instead of looping. Rejected: revalidating on every `--if-match` run (costly for no gain), and installing the pinned old release at `apply` (silently installs what the user would no longer choose).
- **M4-D21: stored plans live in `<cache>/plans/`, not `<state>/plans/` (owner-visible)** (D4). A plan is derived, reproducible and expires within a day, which is the cache's contract; it shares fate with the blobs it pins; and dry runs keep leaving `<state>` untouched. Rejected: `<state>/plans/` with a scope row admitting `Derived`, which breaks a pinned rule for no safety gain. Departure from vision §5.6.
- **M4-D22: which commands store plans** (D4). Eleven store one: `install`, `update`, `pin`, `unpin`, `adopt` (when it adopts), `sync`, `copy`, `remove`, `undo`, `backup restore` and `backup prune`. `errors dismiss`, `doctor fix` and `doctor gc` bind but store nothing. `plans show`, `apply`, `doctor undo`, `backup create|verify|export|import`, `targets`, `config set`, `export --write`, `auth`, `omarchy install|remove` and `robot-docs install-skill` neither store nor bind, each for a stated reason (a plan would hold a secret, be stale by construction, or describe nothing the command line does not say). `capabilities.commands[].stores_plan` and `binds` say which is which.
- **M4-D23: `apply` executes the stored, typed intent bound to its stored token** (D4, D5). A plan holds a `StoredIntent`, an enum with one variant per storable command, normalized at preview: absolute paths, selectors resolved to keys or provisional ids, safety options typed. `display_argv` is derived from it for people and history, and is never parsed. `apply` finds the plan (a prefix of at least 8 characters), fails closed on a bad file (`plan_not_found`, `reason: "unreadable"`), takes the plan's lease, checks freshness (`plan_stale` with `reason` `expired`, `binary_changed`, `input_missing` or `already_applied`), then calls the command's own `run` with the stored token, `force_revalidate` and `applying` in its `Context`, and wraps the typed outcome in `ApplyData`. The envelope's `command` is `apply` and its exit is the executed command's. Plan files are immutable. Rejected: serializing and executing `TargetPlan.work`; re-dispatching a stored argv through the parser and a capturing output adapter (the parser became a storage format); deleting the plan on success.
- **M4-D61: one applier per plan, and the guarantee is per target** (D4, D5, D7). A real `apply` holds `<cache>/plans/<plan_id>.lease` (an fsx `Lease`, a `flock`, never created exclusively) from before its checks until every target's outcome is known. A second applier waits up to `PLAN_LEASE_TIMEOUT`, then exits `locked` (5, retryable) with `details.lease`; when it gets the lease it reloads the plan and finds `already_applied`, or proceeds if the first committed nothing. `outcomes[]` reports each target. A preview that would change nothing stores no plan (`plan_id: null`, its token kept, no `apply` hint). Rejected: no plan lock (two appliers split one approval); holding the global lock across `apply` (blocks every command for a download); one transaction across targets.
- **M4-D24: the plan lifecycle and its quotas** (D4, D6). A plan lives `PLAN_TTL` (24 h). Its file holds `{schema_version, plan_id, created_at, expires_at, tool_version, build_id, intent, display_argv, actor, reason, precondition: {token, parts}, releases[], approval, summary[]}`; on load the token must equal its parts' digest and `display_argv` must equal the intent's. Hard quotas: at most `PLANS_MAX_FILES` plans and `PLANS_MAX_BYTES` bytes, no file over `PLAN_MAX_BYTES`. A storing dry run takes `<cache>/plans/.lock` (a `Lease`, never the global lock), deletes at most `PLANS_SWEEP_MAX` expired plans with their leases under `LockUse::Expired`, reuses an identical unexpired plan (dedupe), and writes only within both quotas, else returns the preview and token with `plan_id: null` and `plan_not_stored`. Nothing unexpired is ever evicted. Retention sweeps after each commit too. Rejected: sweeping only in retention, evicting the oldest live plan, and a soft cap.
- **M4-D25: history lines from `apply` carry the plan id** (D5). The line's `argv` is the plan's `display_argv`, plus an optional `plan` field; `actor` and `reason` are the applier's. History stays 1.0 (additive optional field, M2-D36).
- **M4-D63: `plans show` inspects an approval and reconciles it with history** (D9). Read-only, offline, write-free; it never re-plans. It returns the stored approval, history's evidence keyed by the plan id, a `state` and `evidence.complete`, from a bounded backward scan. Success is never inferred from current addon versions. Rejected: a `plans list`, and making `apply` idempotent (it would hide a partial application).
- **M4-D26: an unexpired plan pins its blobs; local inputs are re-hashed** (D6). A performance pin, not a correctness one: `apply` re-plans and a re-download is verified against the same expected hash.
- **M4-D27: `apply` keeps its name; intent inference separates it from `adopt --apply`** (D5's hints, proved by the harness of C4, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4`, the run-the-fix corpus). Bare `apply` is `usage` with the fix `omaddons help apply` and the alternative `omaddons adopt --apply`; `apply <folder>` is `not_found` with the alternative `omaddons adopt <folder>`; `adopt apply` is `usage` with the fix `omaddons adopt --apply`.
- **M4-D28: the widget previews updates, and applies directly only a routine plan that matches the row** (D4's `approval`, then G1). Every storable dry run returns a typed summary: the canonical selection (per target: client key, addon identity, source and channel, release id and asset, from and to versions), the scope (dependencies added, folders removed, local edits replaced, source changed, the running-client policy), `reasons[]` from a closed set, and `routine`, true only when `reasons[]` is empty. The policy lives in the CLI, so the widget, an agent and a future mod apply one rule and none parses human messages.
- **M4-D55: the contract's rules hold from slice 1** (D2). The known pre-release correction assigned here, `errors dismiss`'s `precondition` presence (always present, `null` on real runs), was already made by the closed M3 bead `omad-q585`; D2 guards it with a presence-rule test over every binding path.
- **M4-D18: volatile keys are declared** (D4). `plan_id` and `plan_expires_at` join `contract::VOLATILE`; the repeat test strips only declared keys.
- **Common rules 14, 15 and 16.** A leaf that adds a binding or deletion rule closes only when its own adversarial matrix passes (D1, D2, D5, D8). Every untrusted or user-sized read is bounded by a named constant, and a full store declines rather than evicts (the plan store, the history scan, pin discovery). Every mutating path binds or says why not (`apply` carries its plan's token and refuses `--if-match`).

### How the area connects to the others

- **Area A** (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1`, the contract registry and the discovery surfaces).
  - A1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1`, per-command facts in `COMMANDS`) blocks D4: D4 sets `stores_plan: true` on the eleven storable rows. A1 also gives every command leaf its row fields and the rowless-parent rule `plans` relies on.
  - A4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`, `capabilities`) publishes `build_id`, `stores_plan` and `binds`; whichever of D1 and A4 lands second adds `capabilities.build_id`.
  - A2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.2`, the registries) holds the `apply` action, which D5 adds. A9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9`, meanings and `DetailSpec`s) declares the new `details` keys, and A3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`, schemas and live validation) validates `apply`'s wrapper union strictly.
- **Area B** (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2`, the guide and the skill). B2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.2`, the guide's content) waits for D5 and D9: the guide's plans section, the `preview-then-apply` recipe and the core loop's reconcile step ("when an `apply`'s result is unknown, run `plans show` before previewing again"). D1's input-manifest test keeps `skills/` outside the build id, so regenerating the guide never changes the build id. After B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`, the guide renderer) lands, D-leaves that add a command, code or action regenerate `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md`.
- **Area C** (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3`, intent inference). The preflight of C2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.2`, a client named as an addon) shares `src/app/{install,update,remove}.rs` with D2, D3 and D4, ordered by the hot-spot rule, with no edge. C4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4`, the run-the-fix corpus) runs D5's four rows (M4-D27's hints) and D9's two (`plans shwo`, `plan show`).
- **Area E** (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5`, the doctor core).
  - E13 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.13`, resource sets and fsx endpoint predicates) blocks D8: the swap renames' predicates are E13's.
  - E9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9`, the M3 build against M4 state) waits for D5: its compatibility homes hold stored plans and their leases.
  - E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`, `doctor fix`) and E8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.8`, `doctor gc`) bind with `--if-match` through `src/app/precondition.rs` after D1, and store no plan (M4-D22). E7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7`, undo of repairs) can run D7's public lifecycle scenario for a repair undo; `doctor undo`'s bound form is `undo <tx> --dry-run` then `apply`.

## Goals

Every leaf but D6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.6`) is worked through its subtasks (claim a subtask, never the leaf; whoever closes a leaf's last subtask verifies the leaf's acceptance criteria and closes it); D6 is one size-S commit.

- **D1** `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1` (`precondition::of_plan` and the approval witness for engine commands, size-L, slice-2): defines the one canonical token every engine command binds to: `of_plan` over the engine's plan, `TargetRef` so a token can name an unregistered target, deferred releases keyed without their URL, a stable `--file <dir>` release id, `build_id` from an explicit build-input manifest, and `src/engine/witness.rs`'s `ApprovalWitness` with index digests reused behind a racy-clean stamp check. Its pinned token is the guard against a canonical form that drifts, and `remove`'s M3 token stays byte-identical.
- **D2** `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2` (`--if-match` on `install`, `update`, `sync` and `copy`, size-L, slice-2): binds the four release-bearing commands on every path: `PlanBinding`, bound dry runs that compare, `check_noop` on the no-op paths, and the app-level extras (update's skips, copy's source, sync's file digest). It also rewrites README's "Previews and --if-match" for what exists when it lands.
- **D3** `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.3` (`--if-match` on `pin`, `unpin` and `adopt`, size-M, slice-2): binds the records-only commands, `pin --version` included, with their no-op checks; `adopt`'s report stays unbound because it changes nothing. After D2 and D3, `BINDING_COMMANDS` holds twelve paths.
- **D4** `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4` (The plan store, size-L, slice-2): `StoredIntent` (`src/app/intent.rs`), the typed `Approval` (`src/app/approval.rs`) and the store (`src/state/plans.rs`), moved to `<cache>/plans/`, with `fsx::lock::Lease`, `LockUse::Expired`, bounded fail-closed loads, dedupe and hard quotas. Every storable dry run that would change something writes a plan whose token equals `data.precondition`, without touching `<state>` or taking the global lock.
- **D5** `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5` (`omaddons apply`, size-L, slice-2): the command (DEC-1, every registry touch point in one commit), the plan lease and the reload after acquiring it, the lifecycle checks, `force_revalidate` with the memo refresh, the typed execution through each command's own `run`, `ApplyData` as a union of complete wrapper variants, `app::emit_side_events`, the history `plan` field, `apply --dry-run`, and M4-D27's hints. It is the protocol the slice is named for, and none of its parts is usable alone.
- **D6** `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.6` (Plan retention: blob pins and sweeps, size-S, slice-2): retention's pin closure gains every unexpired plan's blobs (bounded by the store's quotas; an unreadable plan pins nothing and fails nothing), retention runs the bounded expired-plan sweep after each commit, and a local zip is re-hashed when a bound run re-plans. An approval made an hour ago does not re-download a large archive.
- **D7** `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.7` (Release drift and apply races, end to end, size-M, slice-2): the verification leaf. Release landings for every source (GitHub, git, WoWInterface, Tukui, WowAce) and every release-bearing command, concurrent changes and no-ops for every storable command, the lifecycle, the two-applier split race, the lease timeout and the interference race, plus the real-machine `apply_one_update_and_undo`. It owns no feature code and files the fixes its tests force `discovered-from` itself.
- **D8** `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8` (The approval checked again under the commit lock, size-M, slice-2): `Binding::witness` and `Binding::operations` in `locked()`, after the generation check and before the first managed mutation, the swap renames' identity predicates from E13 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.13`, resource sets and fsx endpoint predicates), and the measured cost of the check on the realistic home. It closes the window between a bound run's first check and its lock, which M3's generations never covered.
- **D9** `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.9` (`omaddons plans show`, size-M, slice-2): the `plans` noun with `show <PLAN_ID>`, which reads the plan fail-closed, scans history backwards within `PLAN_EVIDENCE_LINES_MAX`, and judges `pending`, `completed`, `partial`, `expired` or `unknown`, writing nothing and making no request. An agent that lost an `apply`'s output learns whether it committed before it changes anything.

## Non-Goals

- **Executing a deserialized engine plan.** `apply` executes the stored typed intent, re-planning bound to its token (M4-D23). `TargetPlan.work` and `Inspected` stay unserialized.
- **An invocation-wide atomic transaction across clients.** The guarantee is per target, as the engine's one transaction per target has always been; partial outcomes are reported, never hidden (M4-D61).
- **A compare-and-swap against arbitrary writers.** omaddons checks everything it approved under its lock, and each operation's identity, but no filesystem primitive renames a directory only if nobody wrote into it a moment earlier (M4-D60). Content is not re-hashed per operation.
- **`plans list`.** `plans show` inspects one approval by id; listing every preview (the widget's too) is noise (M4-D63).
- **An idempotent or resuming `apply`.** A second `apply` is `already_applied`, and a partial first application is never resumed on its own; `plans show` tells the agent what happened.
- **Revalidating on every typed `--if-match` run**, and **installing an old release at `apply`** when a newer one has landed (M4-D20).
- **Storing plans for every mutating command.** Only the eleven of M4-D22. `errors dismiss`, `doctor fix` and `doctor gc` bind without a plan; `config set`, `auth`, `targets`, `omarchy`, `backup create|verify|export|import` and `install-skill` neither store nor bind.
- **Plans in `<state>`** (M4-D21), **evicting a live plan or a soft cap** (M4-D24), **editing or deleting a plan file on success** (M4-D23), and **a correctness pin for blobs** (M4-D26).
- **Inferring success from current addon versions.** Only history lines carrying the plan id are evidence (M4-D63).
- **Changing M3's tokens.** `remove`, `undo`, `backup restore`, `backup prune` and `errors dismiss` keep their tokens byte for byte; the under-lock operation comparison applies to `remove` without changing its token.
- **Holding the global lock across `apply`.** The lease is separate, so network work under it blocks nothing else (M4-D61).
- **`--if-match` on `apply`.** `apply` carries its plan's own token and refuses the flag.
- **Renaming `apply`** (M4-D27).
- **The widget's consumption of plans** (G1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1`), **the plan-store doctor row** (F3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.3`) and **the doctor's own bindings** (E6, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`; E8, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.8`). They build on this area; their code is not this area's.
- **New configuration.** No `config.toml` key and no configurable limit: the plan bounds are safety limits, not preferences.

### How the leaves are worked

D1, D2, D4 and D5 have seven subtasks each, D7, D8 and D9 five each, and D3 four: 47 in all. Claim a subtask, never the leaf (`br ready --parent <leaf id>` lists the ready ones); the agent that closes a leaf's last subtask verifies the leaf's acceptance criteria and closes it. D6 has no subtasks: one commit holds its code, unit tests, end-to-end suite and README. The size-L leaves (D1, D2, D4, D5) stay one bead for closure, so no dependent ever sees half of a token format, a binding, a store or `apply`; their subtasks split only the work.

### Order of work, and why the edges are where they are

- **D1 first.** It is a root. The token's canonical form and the witness it digests are one format: every binding, every stored token and every test compares against it, so a token without the witness would be redefined a leaf later.
- **D1 → D2 and D3, in parallel.** Binding the commands needs the token. D2 and D3 touch different command files and share one set of pieces: `PlanBinding`, `precondition::check_noop`, `TargetsData.precondition` and the `TargetsData::all_failed` fix. **Whichever of D2 and D3 lands first adds those pieces; the second reuses them.** `PlanBinding` holds `command`, `expected`, `extras` and `preview` in both beads; D2 adds a constructor for runs given `--if-match` (dry or not) and D3 one for real runs only, and both may exist. D2's four commands compare a bound dry run in the engine (`tx.rs:404`'s `!req.dry_run` dropped; `remove` then hands the engine its binding only on real runs, so its M3 dry run is unchanged). D3's three compare in the app and never touch `src/engine/tx.rs`. Neither compares a token twice.
- **D2 + D3 + A1 → D4.** Every storable command needs a token to store, and A1's `stores_plan` field marks the eleven rows. D2 and D3 land before D4 in the shared command files (hot spots below).
- **D2 + D3 + E13 → D8.** The under-lock checks cover every engine binding at once, and the swap predicates are E13's. E13 is a root so the plan area and the doctor area can both start on it at once.
- **D4 + D8 → D5.** `apply` executes stored intents bound to stored tokens, and a stored token is only as good as its check under the lock.
- **D4 → D6, F3.** Pin discovery reads the store under its quotas; `plan-store-crowded` reads the store and its quotas.
- **D5 → D9.** `plans show` reads the history `plan` field, the stored plan and `already_applied`'s scan, which `apply` writes and uses.
- **D5 + D6 + D9 → D7.** D7 tests `apply`, retention and, in the interference race, `plans show`'s verdict.
- **Out of the area.** D5 → G1, B2, E9, H1, H3 (the widget's runner, the guide's plan recipe, the compat homes holding plans, the audit and the determinism audit all need `apply`); D9 → B2, H1 (the reconcile step, and its shape audited); D8 → G3 (durability optimized against the settled under-lock check); D7 → H4 (README's tests and counts after the verification lands).
- **After H1.** D6 and D7 add no wire shape (M4-D55), so they may land after the audit. D6 adds no warning; its sweep counters are internal fields of `RetentionReport`. D7 adds only tests and the fixes they force.
- **Area T's edges, added at filing.** All nine leaves block T3. T1 blocks D6 and every subtask that writes integration or end-to-end tests: 22 of the 47.
- **Inside the leaves.** D1's build-id and `--file <dir>` subtasks are independent of its witness chain. D2's three command subtasks run in parallel after its `PlanBinding` subtask. D4's plumbing, intent and approval subtasks are independent; the store waits for all three, then the seven engine-backed dry runs, then the four M3 commands. D5's history subtask and its typed-execution subtask start at once. D7's scenario subtasks are mostly independent; only its lifecycle subtask waits for the concurrent-change one.
- **Waves.** By earliest start: D1 at t = 0; D2 and D3 at t = 3; D4 and D8 at t = 6; D5 and D6 at t = 9; D9 at t = 12; D7 at t = 14.

### Design gates

Four of the area's leaves are design gates (common rule 14): each adds or changes a binding rule, and D5 also writes a new lock file and a new field inside the engine's journaled commit. Each closes only when its own adversarial matrix passes: every failpoint it adds, every journaled step, repeated recovery, and injected I/O failure where it writes.

- **D1:** its subtask "Tests: the approval witness's adversarial matrix (the design gate)", in `tests/witness.rs`. A canonical form that drifts breaks every confirmation; the pinned token is the guard.
- **D2:** its subtask "E2E: the binding's adversarial matrix (design gate)", in `tests/preconditions_matrix.rs`.
- **D8:** its subtask "Tests: the design gate's adversarial matrix: refused renames at every journaled step, bound crash matrices and repeated recovery", in `tests/engine_witness.rs`, so `tests/engine_crash.rs` reruns literally unchanged. It changes what the commit window checks.
- **D5:** its subtask "Tests: the adversarial matrix of `apply` (the design gate)", in `tests/apply_crash.rs`: crashes at every engine failpoint under `apply`, recovery crashed and repeated, a killed lease holder, the reload proven, and injected I/O failures.

Expect them to take longer than their size label. A gate that changes a leaf's size or edges is recorded in a comment on the milestone epic, and the agent closing it reruns the graph computation (edges, critical path, slack, lanes) and posts the result there. D4 is not a design gate, but its deletion rule (`LockUse::Expired`) gets an adversarial unit table and crash scenarios anyway.

### Slice share and demos

The area holds 9 of slice 2's 12 leaves (D1–D9, E13, G1 and T3). It feeds every slice-2 demo item except the widget's (Success Criteria above), and T3 records them as tests. A demo item that fails is a defect in the owning leaf: reopen it, or file a bug `discovered-from` T3 and block T3 on it. No leaf of the area records a slice demo itself.

### Risks

- **Risk 6, tokens too sensitive** (likelihood medium, impact low; owner D1). A rules edit, a binary upgrade or a judge-digest change stales every preview. Intended: a verdict is only as good as its rules and code. The fix is one re-preview, and `details.changed` names the part.
- **Risk 19, a token stales for no reason** (medium, medium; owners D1, E6). A field that differs between two runs of an unchanged world (as the deferred URL did), or a stamp that moved without a content change. Mitigations: the "cache hit equals download" rows per source, equal tokens for two dry runs of an unchanged home, a witness that hashes content and keeps stamps only as private proof of "unchanged since", and a token that holds only stable digests.
- **Risk 20, the under-lock check lengthens the commit window** (medium, low; owner D8). A `stat` per witnessed entry and a hash only for what changed, measured on the realistic home (5,040 files) and recorded; G3's counts include it.
- **Risk 7, widget update previews feel slow** (medium, low; owner G1). The dry run does the work the real run did before, the blobs are then cached, so `apply` downloads nothing, and D6's pins keep them for the plan's lifetime.
- **Risk 9, the M3 build destroys M4 artifacts** (low, high; owner E9). Stored plans and their leases are among the artifacts E9 characterizes. They live in `<cache>/plans/`, and no production path at `c0ab5e9` lists the cache root (blob eviction lists only its own directories, and the reserved plan directory is under `<state>`). E9's test is what proves the M3 build leaves them alone.
- **Risk 14, the milestone is large** (medium, medium; all leaves). The plans chain has slack 1 and is claimed early.
- **The residual window under the lock** (D8). Between a swap step's journal line and fsx's own check, a replaced folder leaves that step in neither state: recovery stops for manual repair with nothing lost. It is pinned by a test and named in README, beside the guarantee's stated scope.
- **The quota arithmetic** (D4). The reviewed draft wrote a plan when nothing expired could go, so its own test (600 expired plans less 64 deleted, plus one, leaves 537, not at most 512) contradicted its bound. D4's admission declines instead, and its convergence scenario repeats bounded batches until no expired plan remains.
- **Two clocks** (D6, D9). Plans are dated by `crate::clock::now()`, which `OMADDONS_NOW` freezes in debug builds, while commit lines in history take the system clock under the lock. D6 passes the plan clock to retention explicitly, and D9's history horizon also uses the time the plan id encodes.
- **Performance of dry runs** (D4). Agents and the widget preview everything, so a storing dry run writes one small file and its admission reads one bounded listing.
- **Compatibility.** An older build ignores the optional `plan` field on history lines (history stays 1.0). Records that older builds wrote for a `--file <dir>` install (an `@dir:` release id) reinstall once, because D1's stable id differs; D1's close comment carries that note. A plan from another build is `binary_changed`, never executed.
- **Privacy.** Plan files are 0600 and hold no secret (`auth` is not storable); evidence and outputs name no account, realm or character.

### What the leaf beads found against the plan

Each leaf records these under "Facts this bead relies on", with its adaptation. The ones that cross leaf boundaries:

- **D1:** `Precondition.targets` becomes `Vec<(TargetRef, Option<u64>)>`, keeping the `Option` because `errors dismiss` and `backup prune` bind keys only; `TargetRef` lives in `src/model.rs`, since the engine never imports `app`. The stable `--file <dir>` id is spelled `listing:<hash>` (the code's form), not M4-D19's `@dir:<hash>`, and `resolve::updates::is_static` learns it, so such an install is never updated from upstream. The plan's "`PlanExtras` through `Engine` into `tx::run`" becomes an engine-level `TxRequest.witness`, while `PlanExtras` reach `of_plan` through the command and `PlanBinding`. `capabilities.build_id` is added by whichever of D1 and A4 lands second.
- **D1 and D8:** `copy` never reads `--from`'s folders; it installs each addon from its ref. So D8 re-checks the witnessed source folders under the lock instead of comparing a staged tree with the source digest.
- **D2:** `errors dismiss`'s presence correction was already made (`omad-q585`), so D2 adds a guard test, not a wire change. `remove` hands the engine its binding only on real runs, so dropping `tx.rs:404`'s condition does not change M3's `remove` dry run. `install`'s target-choosing probe stays unbound; only its final run binds.
- **D2 and D3:** `TargetsData::all_failed` rebuilds a target-level refusal from an item error, losing `retryable: false` and `details.changed`. Both fix it. *Decided while writing this bead:* the fix takes D3's narrower form. The command's error becomes the target-level error only when that error is a `plan_stale`; every other case stays as it is. Widening the fix to every target-level error would add `details` keys to existing failures that have nothing to do with binding. D2's tests assert only the `plan_stale` case, so they hold under the narrow rule.
- **D3:** `AdoptData` is an untagged enum, so the adopting token is `TargetsData.precondition` inside `Adopted`. `adopt`'s existing under-lock guard stays a retryable `plan_stale` until D8. A `touch` alone does not stale an adopt preview, because the witness is content.
- **D4:** the `apply` hint in `commands[]`, the `apply` action, the human words "Run exactly this: omaddons apply <id>" and the move of each dry run's `--if-match` line behind `-v` land with D5's command commit, because every `commands[].argv` must parse and `apply` does not exist before D5. `StoredIntent::from_args` takes the run's own resolution, because selectors cannot be resolved from arguments alone. Single-target intents store `target_id` beside the key so `display_argv` shows `-t era`. Releases are stored as a new `StoredRelease`. The approval adds the reason `destructive`, the item fields `fields`, `tx` and `backup`, and the ops `undo`, `restore` and `prune`, so no destructive plan is routine. Lease files carry a holder line, which D5's `locked` details need.
- **D5:** `PLAN_EVIDENCE_LINES_MAX` and `history::plan_evidence` are D5's, because `already_applied` needs them before D9 can start; D9 reuses and generalizes them. The `adopt apply` hint lives in `adopt`'s own argument handling, because that argv parses. `ApplyData`'s schema is a hand-written `oneOf`. `adopt` also uses the memo window, so `force_revalidate` covers it. For M3's four commands, whose dry runs never compare a token, `apply --dry-run` compares the fresh token with the stored one itself. The backward scan never stops on a backup line, whose time is a capture time.
- **D6:** there is no separate eviction lock: `BlobCache::evict` takes the global lock itself after a lock-free first pass. A stored local zip's digest names no cached blob, so its pin keeps nothing.
- **D7:** fixture sequences restart in every process, so a release landing is a second fixture scenario directory. A stale bound no-op `remove` is `not_found`, not `plan_stale`, and M3's binding stays as it is. A WowAce landing is a re-tag at a higher revision. The real-machine test makes its own update rather than skip.
- **D8:** `tests/apply.rs`'s witness scenarios drive typed `--if-match` runs, because `apply` arrives after D8. D8 lifts `common::realistic_home()`. A forget whose folder reappeared re-judges to nothing and is now refused with `selection`. The folders a dependency choice records as unmanaged are re-checked under the lock too.
- **D9:** `plans` is a parent without a `COMMANDS` row of its own (A1's rule). Bare `omaddons plan`'s pinned fix changes from `omaddons help pin` to `omaddons help plans`. A `backup prune` plan is always `unknown`, because a prune writes no history line. An unfinished journal on an approved target makes the state `unknown`. `plans show` reads the registry and journals directly, because the usual `World` load writes the discovery cache.
