title: `precondition::of_plan` and the approval witness for engine commands
description:
## How to work this bead

This bead is worked through its 7 subtasks, listed below in work order. Claim a subtask, not this bead (`br ready --parent omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1` lists the ready ones). The agent that closes the last open subtask then verifies every acceptance criterion of this bead (they are the leaf's, not any one subtask's), and closes this bead with `br close omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1 --reason "done: <evidence> · found: <ids>"`. Until this bead is closed, every bead it blocks stays blocked.

1. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.1 `build_id` from an explicit build-input manifest: `OMADDONS_BUILD_ID`, the input and exclusion lists, and the test that classifies every top-level path.
2. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.2 A stable release id for `install --file <dir>`: the listing hash instead of a fresh ULID, `is_static` taught the new id, README.
3. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.3 `EntryDigest` and the folder witness, with index digests reused behind a racy-clean stamp check: content digests that count symlinks and empty directories, never opening or following what they must not.
4. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.4 `witness::collect` at the end of planning, and the witness plumbing from `TxRequest`: `TargetRef`, `WitnessScope`, `Plan.witnesses`, inputs, dependency choices, absent names, the marker, the judge.
5. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.5 `of_plan`, `PlanExtras` and deferred-release keys, with `Precondition.targets` over `TargetRef`: the canonical parts, the pinned tokens, and `of_remove` covering unregistered targets.
6. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.6 Tests: equal tokens across dry runs and per source, and the `--file <dir>` id end to end: library-level token suites over replayed fixtures, and the binary rows for `--file <dir>`.
7. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.7 Tests: the approval witness's adversarial matrix (the design gate): edits that must stale, changes that must not, entries never opened or followed, inputs that fail closed.

Subtasks 1, 2 and 3 can start at once; 4 waits for 3; 5 waits for 1 and 4; 6 waits for 2 and 5; 7 waits for 6.

**Size L, kept as one leaf for closure.** The token's form and the witness it digests are one canonical format: a token without the witness would be redefined a leaf later, and every binding test with it. The subtasks split the work into commits that each pass `argc gate`; the leaf closes only when all of them are done, so D2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2`, `--if-match` on `install`, `update`, `sync` and `copy`) and D3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.3`, `--if-match` on `pin`, `unpin` and `adopt`) never see half of the format.

**Design gate (common rule 14).** This leaf adds a binding rule: what an engine-command token covers, and the evidence it digests. Its design gate is passed only when omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.7 (the adversarial matrix) is closed. This leaf adds no journal shape, no recovery rule, no write and no failpoint, so its matrix is about collection under change and failure: edits racing the collection, stamps that lie, entries that must never be opened or followed, and inputs that must fail closed.

## Background

omaddons' previews bind today only for destructive commands. M3 (M3-D46) gave `remove`, `undo`, `backup restore`, `backup prune` and `errors dismiss` a precondition token: `--dry-run` returns `data.precondition`, and the real run with `--if-match <token>` recomputes the token from its own plan before it stages anything, refusing with `plan_stale` (not retryable, `details.changed`, `fix_argv` the dry run again) when a part differs. The engine commands that change addons (`install`, `update`, `pin`, `unpin`, `adopt`, `sync`, `copy`) have no token at all, and the token machinery cannot simply be pointed at them: it covers only what M3's five commands needed.

This leaf builds the token every engine-backed command will carry, and the evidence that makes it honest. It binds no command itself. D2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2`, `--if-match` on `install`, `update`, `sync` and `copy`) and D3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.3`, `--if-match` on `pin`, `unpin` and `adopt`) bind the commands on top of it, D8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8`, the approval checked again under the commit lock) re-checks its witness under the lock, and D4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`, the plan store) stores its token and `build_id`.

**What this leaf delivers:**

- `precondition::of_plan(command, &Plan, &[ApprovalWitness], &PlanExtras) -> Precondition`: the token of an engine command, computed from the plan that command will execute, in M3's canonical form.
- The **approval witness** (`src/engine/witness.rs`): per target, the complete content, identity and absence evidence of everything the plan reads, replaces or removes, collected cheaply at the end of planning.
- `OMADDONS_BUILD_ID`: an identity of the binary that changes whenever anything that affects the build changes, from an explicit input manifest that excludes `skills/`.
- A stable release id for `install --file <dir>`, so two previews of an unchanged directory agree.
- `Precondition.targets` able to hold an unregistered target's provisional id, and `remove`'s token covering unregistered targets.

**It serves these milestone goals:**

- **G-M4-3, what was previewed is what runs, target by target.** Every command that changes addons can be previewed and then run bound to that preview; the approval covers what the preview saw, not only the record generations: every file of every folder the plan replaces or removes, clean or edited; every name it creates; its local inputs; a copy's source folders; the rules that judged it. This leaf defines that coverage.
- **G-M4-6, no new risk to the engine's guarantees.** Dry runs still leave `<state>` untouched: the witness is read-only, and collecting it writes nothing anywhere.
- **G-M4-1, self-describing**, in one key: `capabilities.build_id` tells an agent which build it is talking to, where `tool_version` cannot.

**Checkpoint criteria it serves** (the M4 checkpoint list, criteria by number):

- **Criterion 6, previews bind on every addon-changing command, target by target:** "Two dry runs of an unchanged home give equal tokens for every source, including when the second one is served from the blob cache" is this leaf's to prove. The rest of criterion 6 (a change in between gives `plan_stale`: a hand edit in any file of a replaced folder, including a file that was clean at preview, the eleventh changed file, a same-size edit, a file that disappeared or was replaced, a name the plan creates appearing, an edited `sync` file, a copy source whose folders changed while its record did not) is proven by D2, D3 and D8 on top of the evidence this leaf collects; each of those inputs gets its unit row here.
- **Criterion 7, stored plans:** "a plan from another build (`build_id`) gives `plan_stale` with `details.reason: "binary_changed"`" rests on the build id this leaf stamps.
- **Criterion 3, the guide and the skill:** "regenerating, rebuilding and regenerating again leaves the bytes and the digest unchanged" needs the build id to exclude `skills/`; B1's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`, the guide renderer and `robot-docs guide`) `tests/skill.rs::regeneration_is_a_fixed_point` relies on this leaf's input-manifest test asserting it.

**How it serves the vision.** Vision G4 (agent ergonomics) and D31 ("what a human approved is exactly what runs") are met today only for destructive commands. An agent that previews `update dbm` and then runs it bound to the token must get exactly that update or a refusal, never something else because a release landed, a file was edited by hand, or the rules changed. The thesis is that omaddons stays the sole, safe, undoable authority over what it manages; a confirmation that silently covers less than the preview showed would break it.

**The decisions that shape it** (the full decision log is also filed as comments on the milestone epic `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`):

- **M4-D19: every command that changes addons binds with `--if-match`, using a token computed from the engine's plan.** `of_plan` generalizes `of_remove`: it computes the token of `install`, `update`, `pin`, `unpin`, `adopt` (`--apply`, folder names, `--ref`), `sync` and `copy` from the plan the command will execute. `remove` keeps its M3 token. The token's four parts are `command`; `targets` (each target's key, or its provisional id while unregistered, with its record generation, which fixes `of_remove`'s skip of unregistered targets); `selection` (per target: the folder ops, each change, each release, and `creates_addons_dir`; a deferred asset keyed by `{source, key, release_id}` without the URL it resolves only on a fresh download); and `observed` (each target's judge digest, each target's approval witness, the binary's `build_id`, and the command's extras: `copy`'s source key and generation, `sync`'s desired-file SHA-256, `update`'s skip decisions). `--file <dir>` installs get a stable release id from the directory's listing hash. *Why:* `Binding` already runs after planning and before staging, so binding the engine commands needs no engine refactor; a verdict is only as good as the rules and code that made it, so the judge digest and the build belong in `observed`. *Rejected:* (i) binding by target generation alone, which misses release drift, copy's source and every hand edit that leaves the record alone; (ii) hashing the whole dry-run `data`, which includes human-facing text and volatile fields, so tokens would change for no reason. It extends M3-D46 from five commands to twelve (D2 and D3 do the binding).
- **M4-D60: every engine-command token carries an approval witness, validated again under the commit lock.** The witness is evidence, not a warning: a dedicated per-target structure, separate from every human-facing field, recording every live folder a replace or remove will move (managed or not, edited or clean) as an entry digest over each regular file's path, size and SHA-256, each symlink's target and each directory, so an added symlink or empty directory counts; every name the plan creates, as absent; the target's identity (its key and the client marker's digest); the local inputs; for `copy`, the source's key and generation and the entry digests of every source folder it copies; for `adopt`, the entry digests of the folders it records; the dependency selections and the judge digest. It is complete and cheap: a file whose stamp proves it racy-clean against the files index takes its digest from the index, every other file is hashed, so a clean file costs a `stat` and a file that was clean at preview and edited afterwards is caught because its stamp moved. Its canonical digest is `observed`'s witness part, so the bound run's own planning compares it before anything is staged; D8 checks it again under the lock (stamps re-read against the private ones, anything else re-hashed). *Why:* generations prove only that no omaddons transaction committed; a person editing a file, a sync tool restoring one, or a hand-installed folder appearing never moves a generation. `LocalChanges` is a sample of at most ten paths with no digest, so it cannot be evidence. *Rejected:* (i) generations only, which misses every writer that is not omaddons; (ii) re-hashing every file under the lock, correct but costly when a settled stamp proves the bytes unchanged; (iii) promising an absolute compare-and-swap, which Linux cannot provide. This leaf owns the witness and its digest; D8 owns the under-lock checks; E13 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.13`, resource sets and fsx endpoint predicates) owns the per-operation predicates.
- **M4-D7: the guide, `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` and the installed skill are one artifact.** For this leaf: the execution build id hashes an explicit input manifest that excludes `skills/`, and the guide embeds no build id, so regenerating, rebuilding and regenerating again gives the same bytes and the same digest. *Rejected there:* a stamp carrying the build id, which had no fixed point because the build id hashed `skills/`.
- **M4-D20 (context, D2's):** a typed `--if-match` run uses its command's normal freshness rules, so `update` and `sync` inside the 15-minute memo window do exactly what the preview showed even if a release landed; `apply` always revalidates. This leaf's token must therefore be computed from the plan as executed, never from a fresh lookup.
- **M4-D22, M4-D23 (context, D4's and D5's; D5 is `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`, `omaddons apply`):** stored plans embed the same `Precondition`, and `apply` re-plans bound to the stored token; `binary_changed` compares the stored `build_id` with this binary's.

**Facts this bead relies on** (verified at `c0ab5e9`; corrections are marked):

- `engine::tx::run` calls `plan::plan` once and then `binding.plan(&plan)`, but skips the binding in a dry run: `Some(binding) if !req.dry_run` (`src/engine/tx.rs:401-407`, the condition at `:404`). D2 drops that condition; this leaf does not touch it.
- The token format is `pc1:` plus four 16-hex fields, each the first 64 bits of the SHA-256 of a part's canonical JSON (`src/app/precondition.rs:93-138`); the canonical encoder sorts every object's keys whatever map built it, and callers sort arrays and use integers only (`:140-170`). `check` and `stale` give `plan_stale` with `PlanStaleSource::Apply` (not retryable), `details.changed` and the dry run as `fix_argv` (`:187-225`). The pinned fixture token is `a_fixture_token_never_drifts` (`:634-646`).
- `Precondition.targets` is `Vec<(TargetKey, Option<u64>)>` (`src/app/precondition.rs:72`; the plan cites `:73`). **Correction:** the plan writes the new type as `Vec<(TargetRef, u64)>`, but the generation is optional today because `errors dismiss` and `backup prune` bind keys only (`of_dismiss`, `of_prune`, `:419-448`, `:582-607`). The new type keeps the `Option`: `Vec<(TargetRef, Option<u64>)>`.
- `of_remove` skips unregistered targets: `let Some(key) = tp.key else { continue; }` (`src/app/precondition.rs:248-251`).
- `BINDING_COMMANDS` holds M3's five paths (`src/app/precondition.rs:25-31`); this leaf leaves it unchanged (D2 and D3 grow it).
- `plan::Plan` (`src/engine/plan.rs:481-502`) is `Serialize + JsonSchema` but never reaches the CLI wire; `TargetPlan` (`:513-548`) carries `key: Option<TargetKey>`, `target` (the id, provisional while unregistered), and `#[serde(skip)]` `generation`, `work` and `dependencies`. `Plan.generations` is keyed by "target key (or provisional id)" (`:494-495`, filled at `:1201-1205`).
- Provisional ids come from `discover::registry::reconcile`, deterministic in discovery's route order (`src/discover/registry.rs:123-136`), and are always lowercase (`id_safe`, `:203-221`), while a `TargetKey` displays as an uppercase ULID, so the two never spell the same string.
- `PlannedRelease` is `{release_id, url, expected_hash, blob_sha256}` (`src/engine/plan.rs:672-680`). A deferred asset's `url` is the canonical URL after a fresh download and `None` after a blob-cache hit: the release is built at `:3862-3881` from `winner.canonical_url`, which `fetch_blob` leaves `None` on every cached path (`:4834-4852`) and sets only when it resolves the deferred location (`:4855-4861`). Tukui assets are always deferred (`src/sources/tukui.rs:129`).
- `--file <dir>` gets a fresh `dir:<ULID>` release id on every plan (`local_identity`, `src/engine/plan.rs:5429-5446`, the ULID at `:5444`; the doc comment at `:5388-5389` says "a directory has no cheap identity and always reinstalls"). A `file:` directory ref already uses `listing:<hash>` (`src/sources/local.rs:48-52`), from the private `listing_hash` (`:119-150`, `fn` at `:120`), a SHA-256 of every regular file's `(path, size, mtime)`, `.git` skipped. **Correction:** M4-D19 spells the new id `@dir:<hash>`; the code's form, and §6.9.1's, is `listing:<hash>`. This leaf follows the code: `<ref>@listing:<hash>`.
- **Found while writing this bead, not in the plan:** `resolve::updates::is_static` treats a record as having nothing upstream when its release id contains `@sha256:` or `@dir:` (`src/resolve/updates.rs:168-176`), and `update` (`src/app/update.rs:174`), `outdated` (`src/app/outdated.rs:418`) and the only-copy warning (`src/engine/plan.rs:800`) read it. A `--file <dir>` install under a `gh:` ref with an `@listing:` id would stop being static, and `update` would replace the user's local folder with the upstream release. `is_static` must learn `@listing:` in the same commit as the id change (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.2).
- **Found while writing this bead:** with a stable id, an unchanged `--file <dir>` plans as already current (the same-release check at `src/engine/plan.rs:3608-3619`), as a `file:` directory already does; `--reinstall` installs it again. README's "A browser download" paragraph documents only `--file ZIP` (README.md, install section) and gains the directory case.
- `LocalChanges` holds at most `LOCAL_CHANGES_SHOWN` (10) paths, a count and the changed folders, and no digest (`src/engine/plan.rs:748-760`); it feeds only the `local_changes_replaced` warning (`:768`). It stays exactly as it is and never enters a token.
- `predigest` hashes each unindexed live folder a replace or remove will move before the lock, keeps the digest only when the folder's `TreeStamp` was settled and unchanged across the hash, and `with_predigests` re-reads the stamp under the lock (`src/engine/swap.rs:574-634`). The witness follows the same pattern.
- `TreeStamp` is every entry's `lstat` stamp (device, inode, type, mode, size, mtime, ctime), in byte order, symlinks stamped and never followed, directories counted (`src/fsx/stamp.rs:108-146`); `FileStamp::settled` trusts a stamp only once its ctime is a racy slack older than the read (`:89-105`; `RACY_SLACK_NS` 20 ms, `RACY_SLACK_COARSE_NS` 2 s for whole-second timestamps, `src/limits.rs:118`, `:127`). Its fields and entries are private today, and `TreeStamp::read` is unbounded and lists a symlinked root's target through `read_dir` (`:115-131`).
- `TreeDigest` covers regular files only; symlinks and empty directories do not contribute (`src/fsx/mutate.rs:118-122`). The witness needs its own digest.
- The files index (`src/state/files_index.rs:27-75`) records each managed folder's files as `{path, size, mtime_ns, sha256}` with the moment they were trusted from (`recorded_at_ns`, falling back to the index's `written_at_ns`). `drift::check`'s stat mode trusts a file when its size and mtime equal the index's and the mtime is older than `recorded_at_ns` minus the folder's racy slack (`src/drift.rs:306-318`, `:343-346`). It does not look at ctime.
- `hash_file_streaming` opens with `File::open`, which follows a symlink and blocks on a FIFO (`src/state/files_index.rs:139-143`); `hash_reader` (`:116-137`) is private. `index_live_folder` (`:145-261`) already builds the two error shapes a witnessed folder needs: `io` with `details.reason: "unindexable"` (`:160-168`) and `archive_too_large` with `details.reason: "limit_exceeded"` and `folder`, `measured`, `limit`, `config_key` (`:169-184`).
- The judge digest is `Target.judge: String` (`src/model.rs:546-550`), the hex SHA-256 from `toc::judge_digest` over the judging revision, the client's rules row and every family's range (`src/toc/loaded.rs:387-412`). There is no `JudgeDigest`, `AddonName` or `Sha256` type in the code: the plan's sketch uses them as names for `String` values (lowercase hex for digests).
- **Correction:** the plan sketches `TargetRef` in `src/app/precondition.rs`, but `app::outcome::TargetRef` already exists, a wire struct `{id, key, mode}` used in 69 places (`src/app/outcome.rs:33-41`), and the engine never imports `app` outside tests (the one `crate::app` import under `src/engine/` is in `restore.rs`'s test module). `ApprovalWitness.target` lives in the engine, so the enum is defined in `src/model.rs` and re-exported as `precondition::TargetRef`.
- The client marker is `<client dir>/Interface/.omaddons/target.json` (`discover::registry::marker_path`, `src/discover/registry.rs:33-39`), a `TargetMarker {key}` (`src/state/registry.rs:70-72`): stable bytes, rewritten only when a target registers.
- **Correction (affects D8, recorded here because this leaf builds the evidence):** `copy` never reads `--from`'s folders. It installs each of `--from`'s addons on `--to` from its ref, downloading like any install (`src/app/copy.rs:1-11`, the request at `:238-247`). The witness still records the source folders (criterion 6 requires a copy-source edit to stale the preview, and M4-D60 names them), but the plan's D8 step "a copy's staged tree digest must equal its witnessed source digest" cannot hold for a download from the ref; D8 should re-check the source folders' stamps under the lock like any other witnessed folder.
- `build.rs` stamps only the widget digest, with `rerun-if-changed=omarchy` (`build.rs:1-69`); `tool_version` is `CARGO_PKG_VERSION`, `0.1.0` (`Cargo.toml:3`), and stays so until M5. `capabilities` does not exist at `c0ab5e9` (A4, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`, adds it), and neither do `skills/` nor `src/contract/`.
- The tracked top-level paths at `c0ab5e9` are `.beads`, `.gitignore`, `AGENTS.md`, `Argcfile.sh`, `CLAUDE.md`, `Cargo.lock`, `Cargo.toml`, `README.md`, `build.rs`, `catalog`, `clippy.toml`, `deny.toml`, `fuzz`, `omarchy`, `proptest-regressions`, `rust-toolchain.toml`, `rustfmt.toml`, `scripts`, `src`, `tests`; the development machine's checkout also holds the untracked `.rumdl_cache` (a Markdown linter's cache) and `target`. Every `include_str!`/`include_bytes!` of a path under `tests/` or `fuzz/` sits in a `#[cfg(test)]` module (`src/toc.rs`, `src/discover/product_db.rs`), so neither affects the shipped binary.
- `Cargo.toml`'s `bench-fixtures` profile inherits `release` with debug assertions on, so Cargo's `PROFILE` reads `release` for it although its binary behaves differently (failpoints and fixtures are read in debug-assertion builds).
- The engine's failpoint list `engine::tx::FAILPOINTS` (`src/engine/tx.rs:77-113`) is held equal to the source by a scan, and `an_error_at_any_failpoint_leaves_folders_wholly_old_or_wholly_new` (`:1940-2014`) expects every listed point to fire on an update. This leaf adds no failpoint (the plan keeps the list unchanged).
- `tests/single_writer.rs` scans only `src/` (`:811`); outside `src/fsx/` it bans `OpenOptions` and write-mode `OFlags`, not read-only opens (`:17-58`). `rustix` (feature `fs`) is a dependency.
- `TxRequest` (`src/engine/tx.rs:116-130`) is built as a literal at 13 sites (the commands in `src/app/`, `src/engine/testing.rs`, `tests/undo_history.rs`, `tests/engine_multi_target.rs`, `tests/deps.rs`), `PlanRequest` (`src/engine/plan.rs:75-85`) at 4. `Engine::run_bound` already hands a command's `Binding` to `tx::run` (`src/app/engine.rs:201-209`).

## Technical Approach

The work is described here as one design; each subtask restates the part it builds.

### 1. `TargetRef`: a target's key, or its provisional id (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.4)

In `src/model.rs`, beside `TargetKey`:

```rust
/// A target as a token or a stored plan names it: its key once registered, its
/// provisional id before (deterministic, `discover::registry::reconcile`).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash)]
pub enum TargetRef { Key(TargetKey), Provisional(String) }
```

- `TargetRef::of(key: Option<TargetKey>, id: &str)`; `Display` gives the plain string (the key's canonical ULID display, or the id). Derived `Ord` puts every `Key` before every `Provisional` and orders keys by `TargetKey`'s order, so a list of registered targets sorts exactly as `Vec<(TargetKey, _)>` did.
- `Serialize` as the plain string; `Deserialize` reads a string that is exactly a `TargetKey`'s canonical display as `Key`, anything else as `Provisional`; `JsonSchema` is `string`. D4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`, the plan store) decodes stored plans with it. Provisional ids are lowercase and keys uppercase, so the two never collide.
- `src/app/precondition.rs` re-exports it (`pub use crate::model::TargetRef;`). A file that also uses `app::outcome::TargetRef` imports one of them by path.

### 2. The approval witness (`src/engine/witness.rs`, new; omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.3 and omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.4)

```rust
pub struct ApprovalWitness {
    pub target: TargetRef,
    pub marker: Option<String>,               // the client marker: "sha256:<hex>" of its bytes, "link:<target>" for a symlink,
                                              // "kind:<type>" for anything else; None when there is no marker
    pub folders: Vec<FolderWitness>,          // sorted by (key, role)
    pub absent: Vec<String>,                  // every name the plan creates: folder keys, and "Interface/AddOns" itself; sorted
    pub inputs: Vec<InputWitness>,            // sorted by (kind, source)
    pub dependencies: Vec<DependencyChoice>,  // sorted by (requester ASCII-lowercase, requester, folder, by)
    pub judge: String,                        // Target.judge, hex
    stamps: Vec<(PathBuf, TreeStamp)>,        // in memory only: settled stamps per witnessed folder dir; never hashed
    cost: WitnessCost,                        // files hashed, files reused from the index, bytes hashed
}
pub struct FolderWitness { pub role: WitnessRole, pub key: String, pub digest: EntryDigest }
pub enum WitnessRole { Replaced, Removed, CopySource, Adopted }    // wire(): "replaced" | "removed" | "copy_source" | "adopted"
pub struct EntryDigest([u8; 32]);                                    // Display: "entry:sha256:<hex>"
pub struct InputWitness { pub kind: InputKind, pub source: String, pub digest: String }
pub enum InputKind { Zip, Dir, Git }                                 // wire(): "zip" | "dir" | "git"
pub struct DependencyChoice { pub requester: String, pub folder: String, pub by: DependencyBy }
pub enum DependencyBy { Installs(String), Unmanaged, Unresolved(UnresolvedReason), Failed(String) }
pub struct WitnessCost { pub files_hashed: u64, pub files_reused: u64, pub bytes_hashed: u64 }
```

`ApprovalWitness::new(...)` builds one from its public parts with no stamps (unit tests and the no-op path of D2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2`, use it); `stamp(&self, dir) -> Option<&TreeStamp>` (`pub(crate)`) and `cost()` are for D8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8`, the approval checked again under the commit lock: its under-lock check and its `lock_held_ms` report). The witness derives `Debug` and `Clone`, never `Serialize`: it is not a wire shape, and only its digest leaves the engine (section 3 below).

**`EntryDigest`: what a folder's content is.** A SHA-256 over the folder's entries in bytewise path order (raw path bytes, never a lossy conversion, relative to the folder with `/` separators, the folder itself as the empty path). Every value is framed as a length-prefixed field (a big-endian `u64` length, then the bytes), as `build.rs`'s `field()` frames the widget digest, so no file name can forge a boundary. The digest starts with the field `omaddons entry digest 1`; then, per entry, a kind field, the path field, and the kind's payload:

| Kind | When | Payload |
|---|---|---|
| `d` | a real directory (the root included) | none |
| `f` | a regular file | the size in decimal, then the lowercase hex SHA-256 |
| `l` | a symlink (never followed) | the raw target bytes (`read_link`) |
| `o:fifo`, `o:socket`, `o:char`, `o:block`, `o:unknown` | anything else (never opened) | none |
| `x` | an entry that changed while it was read (2.1 below, step 3) | none |
| `a` | the witnessed folder itself is absent | none (the only entry) |

Unlike `TreeDigest`, an added symlink, an added empty directory or an added empty file changes it; unlike `StampDigest`, it is content, so a `touch` or a `chmod` does not. Modes are not part of it (M4-D60 lists content, identity and absence). A root that is a symlink or a regular file is digested as that one entry, with the empty path, never walked. `EntryDigest::of_dir(dir, limits)` hashes everything (no index), for D8's re-hash and for tests.

#### 2.1 Witnessing one folder, cheaply (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.3)

`witness::folder(dir, index: Option<(&FilesIndex, &FolderIndex)>, limits: &ArchiveLimits, now_ns: i128, between: &mut dyn FnMut()) -> Result<Folder>` (`pub(crate)`; `Folder` is the digest, the optional settled stamp and the cost). `now_ns` is taken by the caller before the first read (`Timestamp::now()`) and is injectable so tests decide settledness exactly; `between` runs after hashing and before the second stamp read, a no-op in production and the moving-folder seam in tests.

1. `lstat` the folder. Absent: digest `a`, no stamp. A symlink, a regular file or anything else: that one entry, no stamp. A directory: go on.
2. Read its `TreeStamp` with a bound: `TreeStamp::read_at_most(dir, limits.max_entries)` stops after `max_entries + 1` entries and says so; past the bound the folder fails (`archive_too_large`, below).
3. For each entry in stamp order:
   - a directory, symlink or other: encoded from the stamp (a symlink's target read with `read_link`);
   - a regular file **reused from the index** when the index has its path and the file is racy-clean: its size and mtime equal the index entry's, and both its mtime and its **ctime** are older than the folder's racy-clean moment, `index.recorded_at_ns(folder) - slack(folder)` (the same slack `drift` uses: `RACY_SLACK_NS` when any indexed mtime has a sub-second part, else `RACY_SLACK_COARSE_NS`). Its `(size, sha256)` then come from the index and the file is not opened;
   - every other regular file is **hashed**: opened with `rustix::fs::open(path, OFlags::RDONLY | OFlags::NOFOLLOW | OFlags::NONBLOCK | OFlags::CLOEXEC, Mode::empty())`, checked with `fstat` to be a regular file with the stamp's device and inode, and streamed through `files_index::hash_reader` (made `pub(crate)`). Its recorded size is the number of bytes hashed. A file that is gone, is no longer a regular file, or has another inode when opened is encoded `x` (changed while read). The bytes hashed count against `limits.max_uncompressed` per folder; reused files do not count.
4. Run `between`, then read the `TreeStamp` again. If it equals the first and the first is settled at `now_ns` (`TreeStamp::settled`), keep it as the folder's private stamp; otherwise keep the digest without a stamp (as `predigest` does), so D8 re-hashes that folder under the lock. A digest taken while the folder moved, or one holding an `x` entry, matches no later steady-state collection: comparing against it is always stale, which is the safe direction.

*Decided while writing this bead:* the index-reuse test adds the ctime condition to `drift`'s stat-mode test, because user space can set an mtime back (`touch -r`, `rsync -t`, editors that preserve times) but never a ctime, so an mtime-preserving same-size edit made between the preview and the bound run would otherwise be trusted from the index at the bound run's own planning, and D8's under-lock check (which compares against the bound run's own stamps) would not see it either. Staging writes every file fresh and waits out the racy slack before the lock (`Staged::wait_out_racy_slack`), so freshly committed files pass the ctime test like the mtime test, and the condition costs a hash only where an inode changed after it was indexed. The implementer may confirm or adjust this in the close comment; dropping it would leave criterion 6's "same-size edit" true only for edits that move the mtime.

*Decided while writing this bead:* entries are never opened unless the stamp says regular file, and then without following links and without blocking, because a FIFO swapped in (or present) would hang a dry run and a symlink swapped in would read outside the folder.

**Failures, each failing that target's changes, never the whole plan:**
- an unreadable directory or file: `io`, `details {reason: "unindexable", folder, path}`, message "`<folder>/<path>` cannot be read (`<error>`), so the folder cannot be witnessed for this preview", prose fix "make it readable, or move the folder out of AddOns, then preview again";
- more than `limits.max_entries` entries (`ARCHIVE_MAX_ENTRIES`, 20,000, config `limits.archive_max_entries`) or more than `limits.max_uncompressed` bytes hashed (`ARCHIVE_MAX_UNCOMPRESSED`, 1 GiB, config `limits.archive_max_uncompressed`): `archive_too_large`, `details {reason: "limit_exceeded", folder, measured, limit, config_key}`.

Both shapes (code and `details`) are `index_live_folder`'s, factored into `pub(crate)` constructors in `src/state/files_index.rs` and used by both, so adoption and the witness report the same codes and keys; `index_live_folder`'s own messages and fixes stay byte-identical. *Decided while writing this bead:* incomplete evidence fails closed (§8.1 rule 6, common rule 15); recording an unreadable file as "unreadable" in the digest was rejected because it would approve bytes nobody observed. These refusals can appear only where witnesses are collected (dry runs and bound runs of the commands D2 and D3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.3`, bind), never on an unbound real run.

#### 2.2 Collecting a target's witness at the end of planning (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.4)

`witness::collect(tp: &TargetPlan, ctx: &WitnessCtx<'_>) -> Result<ApprovalWitness>`, with `WitnessCtx {paths, target, index: Option<&FilesIndex>, scope: &WitnessScope, limits: ArchiveLimits}`, called at the end of each target's iteration in `plan::plan` (after `tp.notes.extend(..)`, before `targets.push(tp)`, `src/engine/plan.rs:1508-1523`), where that target's record, files index and live inventory are still in scope. It witnesses:

- **Replaced and removed folders:** every `SwapOp::Replace { live, .. }` (role `Replaced`) and `SwapOp::Remove { live, .. }` (role `Removed`) of every work (`tp.work[].swap()`), the folder at `target.addons_dir().join(live.as_str())`, with the target's index entry for `live.key()` when there is one (managed, so clean files are reused) and none otherwise (unmanaged, so hashed).
- **Adopted folders:** each folder in `folders.recorded` of every change of kind `ChangeKind::Adopt`, role `Adopted`, without index reuse (an adopted folder is unmanaged until the commit indexes it). Pins, unpins and other edits record folders without witnessing them: they change a record field, not what the folder holds.
- **Copy's source folders:** when `ctx.scope.copy_from` is set, each of its folders under the source target's `addons_dir()`, role `CopySource`, with the source target's files index (loaded with `store::load::<FilesIndex>` when the source has a key) for reuse. A source folder that is gone is digested `a`.
- **Absent names:** each `SwapOp::Add { name }` as `name.key()`, plus `"Interface/AddOns"` when `tp.creates_addons_dir`. *Decided while writing this bead:* the live inventory planning just read is the evidence of absence, so collection does not `lstat` them again; D8 re-checks them under the lock, and a name that appears before the bound run starts changes the bound run's own planning (an `Add` becomes a takeover or a failure, which moves `selection`).
- **The marker:** `marker_path(&target.client_dir)`, read with the same no-follow, non-blocking open, as `sha256:<hex>`, `link:<target>` or `kind:<type>`; `None` when absent. An unreadable marker fails the target (`io`, as above).
- **Inputs:** `FolderWork` gains `input: Option<InputWitness>` (not serialized: `FolderWork` derives no serde), set where the winning candidate is turned into a work (carried on `PendingBuild` from `prepare_install`, where `winner.candidate.asset.location` is known, `src/engine/plan.rs:3862-3881`, and written in `build` beside `f.deps = b.deps`, `:3908-3910`): `AssetLocation::LocalZip(path)` outside the blob cache directory gives `Zip` with the zip's SHA-256 (`inspected.blob_sha256`); `LocalDir(path)` gives `Dir` with `local::listing_hash(path)`; `GitCheckout { url, sha, .. }` gives `Git` with the commit. A cached blob (a reinstall from the cache, `local_blob_candidate`) is not an input: its identity is already `releases[].blob_sha256`. `source` is the path's display or the URL.
- **Dependency choices:** from `tp.dependencies` (requester → `DepReport`): each `installs (folder, addon)` as `Installs(addon)`, each `unmanaged` folder as `Unmanaged`, each `unresolved` as `Unresolved(reason)` (candidates are hints for people and are left out), each `failed (folder, ref)` as `Failed(ref)`. Bridge dependencies and `first_install` are reports, not choices.
- **The judge:** `target.judge`.

*Decided while writing this bead:* the sync file's SHA-256 enters `observed` through `PlanExtras::desired_sha256` only, not as a witness input, because the engine never reads `addons.toml`; the witness's `inputs` hold what the engine itself reads.

**Every target gets exactly one witness when collection is on.** A target pushed before its folder plan because `live_inventory` failed (`:1344-1368`) gets `witness::bare(target)` (marker and judge only); a target whose record did not read plans on with every change failed and is collected normally (it has no work). When `collect` fails, the target's works, ops, changes and releases are cleared, each change becomes a `PlanFailure` under its ref and addon with the error (as a `live_inventory` failure does), and the target gets the bare witness, so nothing of it can commit and the token still describes it. `witness::bare` is public: D2's no-op check (`check_noop`) witnesses in-scope targets with nothing to do through it.

The witnesses go into `Plan`: `#[serde(skip)] pub witnesses: Vec<ApprovalWitness>`, in `plan.targets` order, empty when collection was off. `TxOutcomes.plan` carries them back to the command.

### 3. `of_plan`: the token of an engine command (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.5)

```rust
// src/app/precondition.rs
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct PlanExtras<'a> {
    pub copy_source: Option<(TargetKey, u64)>,                        // copy: --from's key and generation
    pub desired_sha256: Option<String>,                               // sync: lowercase hex of the addons.toml bytes
    pub update_skips: &'a [(TargetRef, String, outcome::SkipReason)], // update: what it chose not to touch (target, addon name, why)
}
pub fn of_plan(command: &'static str, plan: &Plan, witnesses: &[ApprovalWitness], extras: &PlanExtras<'_>) -> Precondition
fn of_plan_at(build_id: &str, command: &'static str, plan: &Plan, witnesses: &[ApprovalWitness], extras: &PlanExtras<'_>) -> Precondition
```

`of_plan` calls `of_plan_at(crate::build_info::BUILD_ID, ..)`; unit tests call `of_plan_at` with a fixed build id. Canonicalization is M3's: the same encoder, sorted keys, sorted id arrays, integers only, strings for every digest. Text a human reads (messages, warnings, notes) is never included.

- **`command`:** the command path, as in M3.
- **`targets`:** one `(TargetRef::of(tp.key, &tp.target), Some(tp.generation))` per `TargetPlan`, rendered as M3 renders keys: `[{"generation":7,"key":"01JB8Q2V9W0000000000000000"},{"generation":0,"key":"retail@steam"}]`. A target that registers between preview and run moves from provisional id to key: stale in `targets` (and in `selection` and `observed`, which are keyed by it), which is correct, since registration writes a marker the preview did not see.
- **`selection`:** an object keyed by each target's ref string:

  ```json
  {"01JB8Q2V9W0000000000000000":{
     "ops":[{"addon":"Foo","folder":"Foo","op":"replace"}],
     "changes":[{"addon":"Foo","ref":"gh:o/foo","kind":"update","fields":[],"from_version":"1.0","to_version":"2.0",
                 "folders":{"added":[],"replaced":["Foo"],"removed":[],"skipped":[],"recorded":[]}}],
     "releases":[{"release_id":"gh:o/foo@v2","url":"https://github.com/o/foo/releases/download/v2/Foo.zip",
                  "expected_hash":null,"blob_sha256":"<hex>"},
                 {"release_id":"tukui:elvui@13.80","source":"tukui","key":"elvui",
                  "expected_hash":{"md5":"<hex>"},"blob_sha256":"<hex>"}],
     "creates_addons_dir":false}}
  ```

  - `ops`: `PlannedOp` as `{op, folder, addon}` (`folder` as spelled), sorted by folder key, then op, then addon;
  - `changes`: `{addon, ref, kind, fields, from_version, to_version, folders{added, replaced, removed, skipped, recorded}}`, sorted by addon (ASCII lowercase, then as spelled), each folder list sorted by key, `fields` the `EditField` wire names sorted (always present, `[]` when empty), each skipped folder in its own wire form (`name` and the flattened reason);
  - `releases`: sorted by `release_id`; a direct release is `{release_id, url, expected_hash, blob_sha256}`, a **deferred** one `{release_id, source, key, expected_hash, blob_sha256}` with no URL;
  - `creates_addons_dir`.
- **`observed`:**

  ```json
  {"build_id":"9c41e0b7a2d35f18","copy_source":null,"desired_sha256":null,"update_skips":[],
   "witnesses":{"01JB8Q2V9W0000000000000000":"<64 hex>"}}
  ```

  - `witnesses`: per target ref, the witness's canonical digest: the SHA-256 (64 hex digits) of the canonical JSON array `[marker, folders, absent, inputs, dependencies, judge]` (positional, so the order M4-D60 gives is fixed; each folder `{role, key, digest}`, each input `{kind, source, digest}`, each dependency `{requester, folder, by, detail}` with `detail` the addon, the reason, the ref or `null`). The private stamps and the cost are never part of it: they are proof of "unchanged since", not content. A target with no matching witness (collection was off) is `null`; witnesses are paired with targets by `TargetRef`, not by position;
  - `build_id`: `crate::build_info::BUILD_ID` (never `tool_version`);
  - `copy_source`: `{key, generation}` or `null`; `desired_sha256`: hex or `null`; `update_skips`: `[{target, addon, reason}]` sorted by target, then addon, then reason, `reason` the `SkipReason` wire name. All three are always present, so every engine command's `observed` has one shape.

  `local_changes` (the reviewed draft's choice) is not in the token: `LocalChanges` is a display sample, and `local_changes_replaced` stays a warning for people.

**Deferred releases keyed without their URL.** `PlannedRelease` gains `#[serde(skip)] pub deferred: Option<DeferredAsset>` with `DeferredAsset { source: SourceId, key: String }`, set where the release is built (`src/engine/plan.rs:3862-3881`) when `winner.candidate.asset.location` is `AssetLocation::Deferred { source, key }`. `of_plan` renders such a release without `url`, so a Tukui plan whose first preview downloads and whose second hits the blob cache keeps its token. *Decided while writing this bead:* the field is not serialized, because `Plan` is not a wire shape and this leaf owns no stored-plan format; D4 may expose it when it serializes releases.

**Files:** `build.rs`; `src/build_info/mod.rs`, `src/build_info/inputs.rs` (new); `src/lib.rs`; `src/model.rs`; `src/engine/witness.rs` (new), `src/engine/mod.rs`, `src/engine/plan.rs`, `src/engine/tx.rs`, `src/engine/testing.rs`; `src/fsx/stamp.rs` (read-only accessors and `read_at_most`); `src/state/files_index.rs` (`hash_reader` and the two error constructors `pub(crate)`); `src/drift.rs` (`slack` `pub(crate)`); `src/sources/local.rs`; `src/resolve/updates.rs`; `src/app/precondition.rs`; the `TxRequest` sites in `src/app/{install,update,sync,copy,pin,remove,outdated}.rs` and `src/app/adopt/apply.rs`; `tests/plan.rs`, `tests/install.rs`, `tests/witness.rs` (new), `tests/common/planning.rs` (new), the `TxRequest` sites in `tests/undo_history.rs`, `tests/engine_multi_target.rs`, `tests/deps.rs`; README.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Two dry runs of an unchanged home give equal tokens (`of_plan` over each run's plan and witnesses), for an install and an update on a home with a managed folder and an unmanaged folder replaced with `--force`, and a third run agrees too.
- [ ] Per source, a cache hit equals a download: for GitHub, git (a GitHub-hosted `git:` ref), WoWInterface, Tukui and WowAce, the first dry run downloads (a `net.log` asset or file line), the second is served from the blob cache (no such line), and the two tokens are equal; for Tukui the first plan's release has a URL and the second's none.
- [ ] Every covered input moves its own part, one unit row each: a generation (`targets`); an op, a release id, an expected hash, a blob digest, a direct URL, a deferred source key, a change's versions or folders, `creates_addons_dir` (`selection`); the judge digest, the marker, a replaced or removed folder's digest (standing for a hand edit in any file, including a clean file, the eleventh changed file and a same-size edit, an added symlink or empty directory), an absent name, an input digest, a dependency choice, the build id, copy's source generation, a copy-source folder's digest, sync's file bytes, an adopted folder's digest and update's skips (`observed`); the command (`command`). A target registering moves `targets`, `selection` and `observed`.
- [ ] A `touch` that changes a file's stamp but not its bytes does not move the token, and neither do a `chmod`, the warnings' text, the plan's creation time, the planning transaction id, the order of targets, ops, changes, releases or skips, or a deferred release's URL being present or absent.
- [ ] A pinned `of_plan` fixture token's bytes never change; M3's pinned token and `remove`'s M3 token (`of_remove_keeps_its_m3_token`) are byte-identical after the change, and every existing M3 binding test passes unchanged.
- [ ] `remove`'s token now covers an unregistered target, keyed by its provisional id.
- [ ] `--file <dir>` twice gives one release id, `<ref>@listing:<hash>`; an edited file in the directory gives another; installing an unchanged directory again reports it unchanged, `--reinstall` reinstalls it, and `update --dry-run` skips it as `static` with no request.
- [ ] The input-manifest test fails on a planted untracked-and-unlisted top-level path, passes on the repository as it is, and asserts that `skills` is excluded and that `BUILD_ID` is 16 lowercase hex digits.
- [ ] The witness's adversarial matrix (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.7) passes; the design gate is not passed until it does.
- [ ] With witnesses collected, planning writes nothing outside the cache: `<state>` and every client dir hash identical before and after.
- [ ] If A4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`, `omaddons capabilities`) has landed, `capabilities --json` carries `build_id` equal to `build_info::BUILD_ID`, with its contract rows, schema and README updated.
- [ ] README's install section documents `--file <dir>`, in the same commit as the id change.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes for every subtask's commit; `ubs` is clean on the changed files.
- [ ] The close comment lists every new or changed wire name (the Technical Approach's wire-name list), each "decided" item with its outcome, and the facts corrected against the plan.
- [ ] `br lint omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1 --json` is clean, and so is each subtask's.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

- **`src/build_info/mod.rs`** (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.1): `build_id_is_sixteen_lowercase_hex_digits`; `every_top_level_path_is_an_input_or_excluded` (reads the repository root's entries from `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`; the failure lists each unclassified name with the fix "add it to BUILD_ID_INPUTS or BUILD_ID_EXCLUDED with its reason"); `a_planted_unlisted_path_is_reported` (the pure `unclassified(&[names])` over a listing with `new-build-input.txt` returns exactly it); `skills_never_feeds_the_build_id`; `the_input_digest_is_content_and_order_free` (over a temp tree: equal for two calls and for files created in another order; a byte change in `src/x.rs` moves it; a `touch` does not; a change under `skills/` or `tests/` does not; a new file under `catalog/` does).
- **`src/engine/plan.rs`** (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.2): `a_directory_input_is_identified_by_its_listing` (two calls equal and prefixed `listing:`; an edited file changes it; `.git` content does not; a zip keeps `sha256:`).
- **`src/resolve/updates.rs`** (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.2): `static_unchecked_and_failed` gains the `gh:o/foo@listing:<hex>` row (static), keeping `@sha256:` and `@dir:`.
- **`src/engine/witness.rs`** (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.3): the entry digest per kind; index reuse and its racy-clean edge (the ctime condition, the coarse slack); the moving folder (`between` edits a file: no stamp, digest of what was read); unsettled stamps (`now_ns` within the slack: no stamp); a FIFO never opened; a symlinked directory never followed; a non-UTF-8 name hashed by its bytes; an unreadable file and the two limits failing with their codes and `details`; cost counters.
- **`src/engine/witness.rs`** (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.4): `collect` over `engine::testing::TxScene` plans: roles, absent names (`Interface/AddOns` on a first install), the marker, inputs per kind, dependency choices, a failing target cleared into failures while another plans on, `bare`, the copy source; `TargetRef` ordering, display and serde in `src/model.rs`.
- **`src/app/precondition.rs`** (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.5): `of_plan_fixture_token_never_drifts` (pinned); `of_remove_keeps_its_m3_token` (pinned before the change); `every_covered_input_moves_its_own_part` (the table of the acceptance criteria, one named row per input, each asserting `details.changed` exactly); `benign_differences_leave_the_token_equal`; `a_deferred_release_is_keyed_without_its_url`; `a_registering_target_moves_targets_selection_and_observed`; `remove_covers_an_unregistered_target`; `a_missing_witness_is_null`; `the_binding_commands_are_the_five_of_m3_d46` unchanged.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

- **`tests/plan.rs`** (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.6), library-level over replayed HTTP fixtures, through a new shared builder `tests/common/planning.rs` modeled on its `support::Env` (which stays as it is), with a persistent `ReleaseCache` and `remember(&plan.facts)` as `install` does at `src/app/install.rs:613-618`: `two_dry_runs_of_an_unchanged_home_give_equal_tokens`; `a_cache_hit_equals_a_download_github`, `_git`, `_wowi`, `_tukui`, `_wowace`; `a_file_directory_plans_with_one_release_id`.
- **`tests/install.rs`** (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.6), through the binary: `an_unchanged_file_directory_installs_once` (install, install again → `unchanged`, `--reinstall` → reinstalled, `update --dry-run` → `skip_reason: "static"`, no `net.log` line).
- **`tests/witness.rs`** (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.7, new): the adversarial matrix, table-driven through `plan::plan` with witnesses on: content edits that must move `observed` only, benign changes that must not, identity changes, fail-closed inputs, repeated collection, and nothing written.

### Logging

Every integration scenario uses the `TestLog` of T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs and the `argc e2e` runner), `tlog!()`: `log.step` per phase ("seed home", "first dry run", "second dry run", "compare"), `log.json("token parts", ..)` with the four canonical parts of each token (`Precondition::parts()` gives them), `log.json("witness", ..)` with each target's folders, digests and `cost()`, `log.json("net.log added", ..)` per plan, `log.tree("state", <state>)`, `log.tree("client", <client dir>)` and `log.assert_unchanged` around every collection, and `log.run` for every binary invocation. A failing token comparison prints both tokens' parts side by side and the first differing part. Unit tests are table-driven with one name per case; each assertion message names the case and shows the input and both values.

### Checkpoint-only tests

None. The cost of the under-lock check is the report of D8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8`, the approval checked again under the commit lock); this leaf's suites all run in the gate.

## Considerations

- **Risk #6, tokens too sensitive** (a rules edit, a binary upgrade or a judge digest stales every preview; likelihood M, impact L; owner: this leaf): intentional (M4-D19: a verdict is as good as its rules), and the fix is one re-preview; `details.changed` names the part.
- **Risk #19, a token stales for no reason** (a field that differs between two runs of an unchanged world, as the deferred URL did, or a stamp that moved without a content change; M, M; owners: this leaf and E6, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`, `doctor fix`): the per-source "cache hit equals download" rows; two dry runs of an unchanged home give equal tokens; the witness hashes content and keeps stamps only as private proof of "unchanged since"; the token holds only stable digests (no planning transaction id, no timestamp, no path a stamp moved). The benign-differences row is the guard.
- **Risk #14, the milestone is large:** this leaf heads the plans chain (D1 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1` → D2 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2` → D4 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4` → D5 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5` → D9 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.9` → H1 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`), one unit behind the critical path (slack 1). Start it at once; subtasks 1–3 run in parallel.
- **Why size L, kept as one leaf:** one canonical format; see "How to work this bead". Design gate with D2: a canonical form that drifts breaks every confirmation, and the pinned tokens are the guard. Expect the gate to take longer than the label.
- **Hot spots (§10.5 collision rules):** `src/app/precondition.rs` (D1, D2, D3 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.3`, D8 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8`, E6, E7 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7`): **D1 first**. `build.rs` (D1, B1 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`): **D1 first**; B1 adds one block for `OMADDONS_GUIDE_SHA256`. `src/engine/plan.rs` and `src/engine/tx.rs` (D1, then D2 → D8; G3 `omad-7ccp` last): this leaf adds a field and the collection call, nothing in the commit window. `src/fsx/stamp.rs` is in the fsx hot spot (E13 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.13` first, G3 last): this leaf adds only read-only accessors and `read_at_most`, separate from E13's `mutate.rs` and `journal.rs` work; rebase. The `TxRequest` literals in `src/app/{update,sync,copy,pin,install,remove}.rs` and `adopt/apply.rs` (C2 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.2`, D2, D3, D4): one added line each. `README.md`: the install section only.
- **What could go wrong, and how to notice:** a canonical-form change that slips into an M3 token (the two pinned M3 tests fail); index reuse trusting too much (the ctime and racy rows of the adversarial matrix); a collection that hangs or escapes the folder (the FIFO and symlink rows, each under a timeout); a token that moves between identical runs (the equality and per-source rows, three runs each); `is_static` forgetting `@listing:` (`update --dry-run` would try GitHub: the E2E row asserts no request).
- **Compatibility:** tokens are not stable across builds by design (`build_id`), so a preview from an older binary never confirms a run of a newer one; M3 tokens of `remove`, `undo`, `backup restore`, `backup prune` and `errors dismiss` are byte-identical within a build. Records with `@dir:<ULID>` ids from older builds stay static and reinstall once. The M3 build ignores everything this leaf adds (nothing is persisted).
- **Privacy:** the witness never reads `WTF/` or SavedVariables; `observed` holds digests only, so the paths of local inputs leave the process only hashed; nothing is logged or rendered from the witness.
- **Performance:** a clean managed file costs a `stat` (two stamp walks per witnessed folder), an unmanaged or edited file one streamed hash; collection runs only for dry runs and bound runs. D8 measures the under-lock cost on the realistic home; `WitnessCost` gives it the counts.
- **Rejected while writing this bead:** collecting witnesses on every run (it would slow unbound real runs for evidence nobody compares); a new failpoint for the moving-folder case (the plan keeps `engine::tx::FAILPOINTS` unchanged; an injected `now_ns` and a `between` seam make the cases deterministic in unit tests); putting `PlanExtras` in `EngineCtx` (the engine would import `app`).
- **Decided defaults (confirm or adjust in the close comment):** keep `Option<u64>` generations; `TargetRef` in `model.rs`; the ctime condition; no-follow, non-blocking opens; failing a target on unreadable or oversized folders with the existing codes; `x` for entries that changed while read; absent names from planning's inventory; the sync file through extras only; `TxRequest.witness` as the plumbing; `PlannedRelease.deferred` not serialized; the lists in `src/build_info/inputs.rs`; the profile fields and rustflags in the build id; the exclusion list; `capabilities.build_id` by whichever of this leaf and A4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`) lands second; the `dir:` fallback for unreadable files; README's `--file` paragraph.

## Dependencies

Parent: the area D epic (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4`, previews and stored plans).

**Blocked by:** none. This leaf is a root. Its two test subtasks wait for T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs and the `argc e2e` runner), whose `TestLog` they use; that edge is the subtasks', not the leaf's.

**Unblocks:**
- D2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2`, `--if-match` on `install`, `update`, `sync` and `copy`): its `PlanBinding` computes `of_plan` with witnesses and extras, its no-op check uses `witness::bare`, and its commands set `TxRequest.witness` (`copy` with `CopyFrom`).
- D3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.3`, `--if-match` on `pin`, `unpin` and `adopt`): `adopt`'s recorded folders are witnessed (role `Adopted`); `pin` and `unpin` bind through the same `of_plan`.
- T3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.3`, slice 2 end to end): it records slice 2's demo, which needs every slice-2 leaf closed.

Through D2 and D3 it also feeds D8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8`: the private stamps, `EntryDigest::of_dir`, absent names and the marker for the under-lock checks; see the copy correction above), D4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`: the token parts, `TargetRef`, `BUILD_ID`) and D5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`: `binary_changed`). B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`) relies on the input-manifest test excluding `skills/`; A4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`) publishes `capabilities.build_id` if it lands after this leaf. None of these is a direct edge.

**Delivery slice `slice-2`, "Preview, then apply exactly"** (D1 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1` to D9 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.9`, E13 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.13`, and G1 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1`, the widget previews and applies plans). Its demo (install, then `update --dry-run` then `apply`; a release landing in between gives `plan_stale`; a late hand edit is caught under the lock; a Tukui plan applies from the cache; the widget's Update) is recorded by T3, not by this leaf. It pre-checks checkpoint criteria 6, 7 and 8 (updates).

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M4 plan, 2026-10-24).**

**Why this bead.** Today only omaddons' destructive commands can be previewed and then confirmed exactly: `remove`, `undo`, `backup restore`, `backup prune` and `errors dismiss` carry M3's precondition token. The commands that change addons, which agents and the bar widget run most, have none. An agent that previews `update dbm` and then runs `update dbm` may get a different release, may overwrite a file someone edited by hand in between, and nothing would say so. This bead builds the token every engine-backed command will carry and the evidence that makes it honest: `of_plan` over the plan the command will execute, and a per-target approval witness of everything that plan reads, replaces, removes or creates. It binds no command itself; D2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2`, `--if-match` on `install`, `update`, `sync` and `copy`) and D3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.3`, `--if-match` on `pin`, `unpin` and `adopt`) do, D8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8`, the approval checked again under the commit lock) re-checks the witness under the lock, and D4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`, the plan store) stores the token. It keeps the thesis true where agents act most: omaddons stays the sole, safe, undoable authority, and what a person or an agent approved is exactly what runs.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M4-D19: every command that changes addons binds with a token computed from the engine's plan.** `of_plan` generalizes `of_remove` to twelve paths: `targets` (key or provisional id, with the generation), `selection` (ops, changes, releases, `creates_addons_dir`; a deferred asset keyed without its URL), `observed` (judge digest, witness, `build_id`, the command's extras). `--file <dir>` gets a stable id from its listing hash. Rejected: generations alone (miss release drift, copy's source and hand edits); hashing the whole dry-run `data` (human text and volatile fields would stale tokens for no reason).
- **M4-D60: the token carries an approval witness, checked again under the lock.** Every live folder a replace or remove moves (managed or not, edited or clean) as an entry digest that counts symlinks and empty directories; every created name as absent; the marker; local inputs; copy's source folders; adopt's recorded folders; dependency choices; the judge. Clean files reuse index digests behind a racy-clean stamp check, so the witness is complete at the cost of a `stat`. Rejected: generations only; re-hashing everything under the lock; promising a compare-and-swap no filesystem offers. This bead owns the witness and its digest; D8 the under-lock checks; E13 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.13`, resource sets and fsx endpoint predicates) the per-operation predicates.
- **M4-D7: the build id excludes `skills/`,** so regenerating the guide, rebuilding and regenerating again is a fixed point; B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`, the guide renderer) relies on this bead's input-manifest test.
- **M4-D20, M4-D22, M4-D23 (context):** typed bound runs keep their command's freshness, so the token is computed from the plan as executed; stored plans embed the same `Precondition`, and `binary_changed` compares `build_id`.

**Alternatives rejected while writing the bead.**
- Collecting witnesses on every run: it would slow unbound real runs for evidence nothing compares. Witnesses are collected only when a command asks (`TxRequest.witness`), which D2 and D3 do for dry runs and bound runs.
- Trusting index digests on size and mtime alone, as `drift` does: an mtime-preserving same-size edit between the preview and the bound run would be trusted at the bound run's own planning and missed under the lock too. The witness also requires the ctime to predate the index's racy-clean moment, which costs a hash only where an inode changed after indexing.
- Recording an unreadable or oversized folder in the digest as "unreadable": it would approve bytes nobody observed. Such a target fails closed with the codes adoption already uses.
- A new failpoint for the moving-folder case: the plan keeps `engine::tx::FAILPOINTS` unchanged; an injected clock and a test seam make the cases deterministic.
- Putting `PlanExtras` into the engine context: the engine never imports `app`; the engine-facing part is the witness scope.

**Facts the plan got wrong against the code, and how the bead adapts.**
- `Precondition.targets` keeps an optional generation (`errors dismiss` and `backup prune` bind keys only), so the new type is `Vec<(TargetRef, Option<u64>)>`, not `Vec<(TargetRef, u64)>`.
- `app::outcome::TargetRef` already exists, and the witness lives in the engine, so the enum goes in `src/model.rs` and is re-exported as `precondition::TargetRef`.
- M4-D19's `@dir:<hash>` is `listing:<hash>` in the code and in §6.9.1; the bead follows the code.
- `resolve::updates::is_static` recognizes `--file` installs by `@sha256:` or `@dir:`; without learning `@listing:`, `update` would replace a user's local folder from upstream. The bead changes both in one commit, and README documents that an unchanged folder now installs once.
- `copy` installs from refs and never reads `--from`'s folders, so D8's "staged tree equals the witnessed source digest" cannot hold; the witness still records the source folders, and D8 should re-check them like any witnessed folder.
- `capabilities` does not exist until A4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`, `omaddons capabilities`); whichever of the two lands second publishes `build_id`.

**Risks and how they are watched.**
- Risk #6, tokens too sensitive: intended; one re-preview fixes it, and `details.changed` names the part.
- Risk #19, a token stales for no reason: the per-source cache-hit rows, two and three dry runs of an unchanged home, the benign-differences unit row, and a token that holds only content digests and stable ids.
- A canonical form that drifts breaks every confirmation: the pinned `of_plan` token and M3's pinned tokens (`a_fixture_token_never_drifts`, `of_remove_keeps_its_m3_token`).
- Collection that hangs or escapes a folder (a FIFO, a symlink): no-follow, non-blocking opens, and adversarial rows under a timeout.

**What it unblocks, and why they wait.** D2 and D3 cannot bind a command without the token's form and the witness; binding first would redefine every binding test a leaf later. T3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.3`, slice 2 end to end) records slice 2's demo once every slice-2 leaf is closed. D8, D4 and D5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`, `omaddons apply`) build on it through D2 and D3.

**The M4 plan's entry for D1, verbatim (M4 plan, 2026-10-24).** This is the M4 plan's entry, lines 3997–4023 of the plan, kept as provenance. The description above is the authoritative, elaborated version; where they differ, the description was decided while filing and says why.

#### D1 `precondition::of_plan` and the approval witness for engine commands
- **Type** feature · **P1** · **size-L** · **slice-2**
- **Blocked by:** none (a root).
- **Unblocks:** D2, D3.
- **Background.** §2.2: M3's tokens cover five commands. `of_remove` skips unregistered targets, and `--file <dir>` release ids differ on every plan. Generations alone miss every writer that is not omaddons, and `LocalChanges` is a ten-path sample with no digest (§2.7). M4-D19, M4-D60, §6.9.1.
- **Technical approach.**
  1. Write `of_plan(command, &Plan, &[ApprovalWitness], &PlanExtras)`, with canonicalization per §6.9.1 (sorted keys, sorted id arrays, integers only, as M3's canonical form).
  2. `Precondition.targets` becomes `Vec<(TargetRef, u64)>` so it can hold provisional ids (`precondition.rs:73`), serializing registered targets exactly as before. Fix `of_remove` the same way.
  3. **Deferred releases.** Key a deferred asset by `{source, key, release_id, expected_hash, blob_sha256}` without its resolved URL, which is `None` on a cache hit (`plan.rs:3862-3870, 4833-4861`).
  4. **The approval witness** (`src/engine/witness.rs`): `ApprovalWitness`, `FolderWitness` and `EntryDigest` (§6.9.1), and `witness::collect` at the end of `plan::plan`: every replaced or removed live folder (managed or not, edited or clean), copy sources, adopt's recorded folders, absent names, the marker, local inputs, dependency choices and the judge digest. Clean files take their digests from the files index behind a racy-clean stamp check; everything else is hashed; a folder that moved while hashed keeps no stamp. Its canonical digest is `observed`'s witness part; `local_changes` leaves the token.
  5. **`build_id` from an explicit input manifest.** `build.rs` (which already stamps the widget digest) stamps `OMADDONS_BUILD_ID` over `BUILD_ID_INPUTS` (§6.9.1: the manifests and configuration that affect the build, `src/`, `catalog/`, `omarchy/`, the compiler version, target, profile and features; never `skills/`), with `rerun-if-changed` on each, and a test that every tracked top-level path is either an input or explicitly excluded. `capabilities.build_id` publishes it (an additive key this leaf adds).
  6. Make `--file <dir>` derive its release id from the listing hash: `plan.rs:5444` calls `local::listing_hash` (`sources/local.rs:120`, made `pub(crate)`), giving `listing:<hash>` as `file:` directories do.
  7. Add the `PlanExtras` plumbing (including `update_skips`) through `app::engine::Engine` into `tx::run`.
- **Acceptance criteria.**
  - Two dry runs of an unchanged home give equal tokens.
  - **Per source, a cache hit equals a download.** For GitHub, git, WoWInterface, Tukui and WowAce: the first dry run downloads, the second hits the blob cache, and the tokens are equal.
  - Every covered input moves its part: a generation, an op, a release id, an expected hash, the judge digest, a hand edit in any file of a replaced folder (including a file that was clean, the eleventh changed file and a same-size edit), an added symlink or empty directory, a created name appearing, the marker, the build id, copy's source generation and source folder contents, sync's file bytes, adopt's folder digest, update's skips (one unit row each).
  - A `touch` that changes a file's stamp but not its bytes does not move the token (the digest is content).
  - A pinned fixture token's bytes never change; `remove`'s M3 token is byte-identical.
  - `remove`'s token now covers an unregistered target.
  - `--file <dir>` twice gives one release id.
  - The input-manifest test fails on a planted untracked-and-unlisted top-level path.
- **Test plan.** Unit tests in `src/app/precondition.rs` (the covered-input table, the pinned token) and `src/engine/witness.rs` (collection, index reuse, the moving-folder case). `tests/plan.rs` for the dir id and the per-source cache-hit rows.
- **Considerations.**
  - **Size L, kept as one leaf.** The token's form and the witness it digests are one canonical format; a token without the witness would be redefined a leaf later, and every binding test with it.
  - Design gate with D2 (common rule 14). A canonical form that drifts breaks every confirmation. The pinned token is the guard.
