title: `build_id` from an explicit build-input manifest
description:
Part 1 of 7 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1 (`precondition::of_plan` and the approval witness for engine commands). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

D1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1`) builds the precondition token that every engine-backed command (`install`, `update`, `pin`, `unpin`, `adopt`, `sync`, `copy`) will carry in M4, so that a run confirmed with `--if-match <token>` (or later `apply <plan_id>`) does exactly what its preview showed or nothing. One part of that token's `observed` is the identity of the binary that made the preview: a verdict is only as good as the rules and the code that made it (M4-D19), so a preview made by one build must not confirm a run of another. `tool_version` cannot say which build it is: it is `CARGO_PKG_VERSION`, `0.1.0` (`Cargo.toml:3`), and stays so for every build until M5 (M4-D57).

This subtask adds `OMADDONS_BUILD_ID`: the first 16 hex digits of a SHA-256 over an **explicit input manifest** of everything that affects the build, stamped by `build.rs` and compiled in as `build_info::BUILD_ID`. It is its own step because it touches only `build.rs` and a new module, nothing else in D1 depends on its internals (only on the constant), and it can land first, in parallel with subtasks 2 and 3. Later users: `of_plan`'s `observed.build_id` (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.5), D4's stored plan (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`, the plan store, `StoredPlan.build_id`), D5's `binary_changed` refusal (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`, `omaddons apply`), D9's `plans show` (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.9`, `build_matches`), and `capabilities.build_id` (A4, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`, `omaddons capabilities`).

**M4-D7 sets the one hard rule:** the build id never hashes `skills/`. The committed guide `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` (B1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`, the guide renderer) is generated output with its own content digest; if the build id hashed it, rendering the skill would change the next build id and rebuilding would change the next skill, with no fixed point (the reviewed draft's rejected stamp failed exactly so). B1's `tests/skill.rs::regeneration_is_a_fixed_point` relies on this subtask's input-manifest test asserting that `skills/` is outside the inputs.

**Facts this subtask relies on** (verified at `c0ab5e9`):
- `build.rs` (`build.rs:1-69`) computes only the widget assets' digest into `OUT_DIR/assets_digest.rs` (included by `src/omarchy/render.rs:192`), with `cargo::rerun-if-changed=omarchy` and a length-prefixed `field()` framing (`build.rs:65-69`). It allows `clippy::print_stdout` for its Cargo directives. `sha2` is its only build-dependency.
- `tests/single_writer.rs` scans only `src/` (`:811`) for writes and process spawns; `build.rs` is outside it, but a new file under `src/` is inside it: the shared input module must not spawn a process (the `rustc -V` call stays in `build.rs`).
- The library denies `unwrap`, `expect`, `print!` and `eprint!` (`Cargo.toml` `[lints.clippy]`), so the shared module must too.
- Tracked top-level paths: `.beads`, `.gitignore`, `AGENTS.md`, `Argcfile.sh`, `CLAUDE.md`, `Cargo.lock`, `Cargo.toml`, `README.md`, `build.rs`, `catalog`, `clippy.toml`, `deny.toml`, `fuzz`, `omarchy`, `proptest-regressions`, `rust-toolchain.toml`, `rustfmt.toml`, `scripts`, `src`, `tests`. The development machine's checkout also has `target` and the untracked `.rumdl_cache`. `.gitignore` ignores `lcov.info`, `*.profraw` and `*.profdata`, which coverage runs may leave at the top level. There is no `.cargo/`, `skills/` or `docs/` yet.
- Every `include_str!`/`include_bytes!` of a path under `tests/` or `fuzz/` is inside a `#[cfg(test)]` module (`src/toc.rs`, `src/discover/product_db.rs`), so neither tree affects the shipped binary; `catalog/catalog.toml` and the `omarchy/` runtime files are embedded.
- The `bench-fixtures` profile inherits `release` with `debug-assertions = true` (`Cargo.toml`), so Cargo's `PROFILE` reads `release` for it while its binary reads failpoints and fixtures.
- `capabilities` does not exist at `c0ab5e9`; A4 adds it with `build_id` third in its key order (after `version` and `contract_version`).

## Technical Approach

1. **`src/build_info/inputs.rs` (new), shared by the build script and the library.** It imports only `std` and `sha2` (both available to `build.rs`), spawns nothing, writes nothing, and has no `unwrap`/`expect`. `build.rs` compiles it with `#[path = "src/build_info/inputs.rs"] mod inputs;`; the library exposes it as `build_info::inputs`. *Decided while writing this bead:* the plan puts the list in `build.rs` itself; a test cannot import from a build script, so the shared file lets the classification test read the very list the build hashes. It holds:

   ```rust
   pub enum Input { File(&'static str), OptionalFile(&'static str), Tree(&'static str) }
   pub const BUILD_ID_INPUTS: &[Input] = &[
       Input::File("Cargo.toml"), Input::File("Cargo.lock"), Input::File("build.rs"),
       Input::File("rust-toolchain.toml"), Input::OptionalFile(".cargo/config.toml"),
       Input::Tree("src"), Input::Tree("catalog"), Input::Tree("omarchy"),
   ];
   /// Top-level names that never feed the build id, each with why; `*.<ext>` matches a suffix.
   pub const BUILD_ID_EXCLUDED: &[(&str, &str)] = &[ /* below */ ];
   pub struct Toolchain { pub rustc_version: String, pub target: String,
                          pub profile: Vec<(String, String)>, pub features: Vec<String>, pub rustflags: String }
   pub fn input_digest(root: &Path, toolchain: &Toolchain) -> std::io::Result<String>;   // 16 lowercase hex
   pub fn rerun_paths(root: &Path) -> Vec<&'static str>;  // every File and Tree, and each OptionalFile that exists
   pub fn unclassified<'a>(names: impl IntoIterator<Item = &'a str>) -> Vec<&'a str>;
   ```

   - **The exclusions**, each with its reason in the table: `.git` (the repository), `target` (build output), `.beads` (the tracker), `tests` (integration tests and fixtures; unit tests' `include_*!` of fixtures are test-only), `skills` (generated guide output, M4-D7), `docs` (prose), `fuzz` (its own crate), `scripts` (gate and widget scripts), `proptest-regressions` (test seeds), `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` (prose), `Argcfile.sh` (task runner), `clippy.toml`, `rustfmt.toml`, `deny.toml` (lint, format and licence policy: they decide whether the gate passes, never the binary's bytes), `.gitignore`, `.claude` (agent settings, when present), `.rumdl_cache` (a Markdown linter's cache on the development machine), `lcov.info`, `*.profraw`, `*.profdata` (coverage outputs `.gitignore` already ignores). A top-level name is an input when it is the first component of an `Input` path (`.cargo` for `.cargo/config.toml`).
   - **`input_digest`:** a SHA-256 over length-prefixed fields (a big-endian `u64` length, then the bytes, as `build.rs`'s `field()`): the domain field `omaddons build id 1`; then each `File` and existing `OptionalFile` in list order as its path field and its bytes field; then, for each `Tree` in list order, every entry under it in bytewise order of its repository-relative path (raw bytes, `/`-separated): a regular file as its path and its bytes, a symlink as its path and `symlink:` plus its target (never followed), any other kind as its path and its kind name; directories are walked, not hashed; then the toolchain: `rustc_version`, `target`, each `KEY=VALUE` of `profile` in order, each feature (sorted), and `rustflags`. The result is the first 16 lowercase hex digits. A missing `File` or `Tree` is an error (the build would fail anyway); a missing `OptionalFile` is skipped, and its appearing changes the digest.
   - **The profile and flags.** *Decided while writing this bead:* `profile` is `PROFILE`, `OPT_LEVEL`, `DEBUG` and `debug_assertions=1|0` (from whether `CARGO_CFG_DEBUG_ASSERTIONS` is set), and `rustflags` is `CARGO_ENCODED_RUSTFLAGS`, because `PROFILE` alone reads `release` for `bench-fixtures`, whose binary reads failpoints, and flags can add `--cfg`s. Features are every `CARGO_FEATURE_*` variable's name, sorted.
2. **`build.rs`:** keep the widget digest exactly as it is. Add:
   - a `Toolchain` from the environment Cargo gives build scripts: `rustc_version` from running `$RUSTC -V` (`std::process::Command`, its stdout trimmed; `RUSTC` falls back to `rustc`), `TARGET`, the profile variables above, the features and `CARGO_ENCODED_RUSTFLAGS` (empty when unset);
   - `println!("cargo::rerun-if-changed={path}")` for each of `inputs::rerun_paths(".")` (it already prints `omarchy`; keep one line per path). `.cargo/config.toml` is watched only when it exists, because Cargo reruns a build script on every build for a watched path that does not exist; creating it later is picked up the next time any other input changes (say so in a comment);
   - `println!("cargo::rustc-env=OMADDONS_BUILD_ID={id}")`.
3. **`src/build_info/mod.rs` (new):** `pub mod inputs;` and `pub const BUILD_ID: &str = env!("OMADDONS_BUILD_ID");` with a doc comment: compiled in by `build.rs` from the explicit input manifest, never read from the environment at run time, and never including `skills/`. `src/lib.rs` gains `pub mod build_info;`. A2's env-var scan (A2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.2`, the registries) matches `env::var`/`var_os` calls only, so `env!` needs no `ENV_VARS` row.
4. **`capabilities.build_id`.** *Decided while writing this bead:* whichever of D1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1`) and A4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`, `omaddons capabilities`) lands second publishes it. If `src/app/capabilities.rs` exists when this subtask lands, add `build_id` to its data (third, after `contract_version`, reading `build_info::BUILD_ID`), and in the same commit its contract snapshot, its schema, the semantic manifest golden if A10 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.10`, the semantic manifest) has landed, README's capabilities section, and the wire-name note. Otherwise do nothing here, and A4 publishes it. Mark which happened in the close comment.

**What not to do:** never hash `skills/`; never spawn a process or write a file from `src/build_info/inputs.rs`; never read `OMADDONS_BUILD_ID` with `env::var` at run time; never fold the widget digest into the build id's computation path (they are separate outputs of one script).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `build_info::BUILD_ID` is 16 lowercase hex digits, set by `build.rs` from `BUILD_ID_INPUTS`.
- [ ] `every_top_level_path_is_an_input_or_excluded` passes on the repository as it is, and fails, naming the path, on a planted untracked-and-unlisted top-level name (the pure `unclassified` reports it).
- [ ] `skills` is in `BUILD_ID_EXCLUDED`, no input starts with it, and a change under `skills/` leaves `input_digest` unchanged.
- [ ] `input_digest` changes with any byte of an input file, a new file under an input tree, the compiler version, the target, any profile field, a feature or the flags; it does not change with a `touch`, with file creation order, or with anything under an excluded path.
- [ ] `build.rs` emits `rerun-if-changed` for every input path, `.cargo/config.toml` only when it exists, and the widget digest is unchanged (the existing `src/omarchy/render.rs` digest test passes).
- [ ] If A4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`, `omaddons capabilities`) has landed: `capabilities --json` has `build_id` equal to `BUILD_ID`, with contract snapshot, schema, README and manifest updated in the same commit; otherwise nothing in `capabilities` is touched.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on `build.rs` and `src/build_info/`.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

In `src/build_info/mod.rs` (`#[cfg(test)]`), each table case named, each assertion message naming the case and showing the input and the result:

- `build_id_is_sixteen_lowercase_hex_digits`: `BUILD_ID.len() == 16` and every byte in `0-9a-f`.
- `every_top_level_path_is_an_input_or_excluded`: reads the names in `env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")`; `unclassified(names)` must be empty; the failure lists each name with "add it to BUILD_ID_INPUTS or BUILD_ID_EXCLUDED with its reason".
- `a_planted_unlisted_path_is_reported`: `unclassified(["src", "README.md", "new-build-input.txt", "lcov.info", "default.profraw", ".cargo"])` is exactly `["new-build-input.txt"]`.
- `no_name_is_both_an_input_and_excluded`, and `skills_never_feeds_the_build_id` (the list check).
- `the_input_digest_is_content_and_order_free`, over a temp tree with every input present (small files) and a fixed `Toolchain`, table rows: `unchanged` (two calls equal); `same files created in another order` (equal); `touch src/x.rs` (equal); `one byte of src/x.rs` (moves); `new file under catalog/` (moves); `a symlink under omarchy/ retargeted` (moves); `edit under skills/` (equal); `edit under tests/` (equal); `edit README.md` (equal); `.cargo/config.toml created` (moves); `Cargo.lock edited` (moves).
- `toolchain_fields_move_the_digest`: rows for `rustc_version`, `target`, `PROFILE`, `OPT_LEVEL`, `DEBUG`, `debug_assertions`, a feature added, `rustflags`, each moving the digest; feature order not moving it.
- `rerun_paths_watch_every_input`: equals every `File` and `Tree`, plus `.cargo/config.toml` only in the tree where it exists.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

title: A stable release id for `install --file <dir>`
description:
Part 2 of 7 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1 (`precondition::of_plan` and the approval witness for engine commands). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

D1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1`) builds the precondition token of every engine-backed command, so that `--if-match <token>` (D2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2`) and `apply <plan_id>` (D5, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`) run exactly what a preview showed. The token's `selection` holds each release the plan installs, by release id (M4-D19). A token is useless if two previews of an unchanged world disagree (risk #19, "a token stales for no reason"): an agent would preview, confirm, and get `plan_stale` every time.

`install <ref> --file <dir>` (a folder the user unpacked or develops in, installed as the release of one ref) breaks that today: its release id is `<ref>@dir:<ULID>`, a fresh ULID on every plan (`src/engine/plan.rs:5444`). This subtask gives it a stable id from the directory's listing hash, the identity a `file:<dir>` ref already uses, and fixes the two things that depend on the id's spelling. It is its own step because it touches the local-input identity, the "nothing upstream" rule and README, none of which the token code needs to know about; it can land in parallel with subtasks 1 and 3.

M4-D19 states the rule: "`--file <dir>` installs get a stable release id from the directory's listing hash, as `file:` directories already have, instead of a fresh `dir:<ULID>`, so two previews of an unchanged directory agree."

**Facts this subtask relies on** (verified at `c0ab5e9`):
- `local_identity(file)` (`src/engine/plan.rs:5429-5446`) gives `sha256:<hex>` for a readable regular file and `dir:<ULID>` for a directory or an unreadable file; `file_candidate` (`:5378-5408`) builds the `--file` candidate with `release_id: format!("{}@{}", wanted.r#ref, local_identity(file))`, and its comment says "a directory has no cheap identity and always reinstalls" (`:5388-5389`).
- A `file:` directory ref's release id is `<ref>@listing:<hash>` (`src/sources/local.rs:48-52`), from the private `listing_hash` (`:119-150`): a SHA-256 over the sorted `<path>\0<size>\0<mtime_ns>\n` lines of every non-directory entry, `.git` skipped. **Correction:** M4-D19 spells the new form `@dir:<hash>`; the code (and §6.9.1 of the plan) spells it `listing:<hash>`. Follow the code.
- **Found while writing this bead:** `resolve::updates::is_static` (`src/resolve/updates.rs:168-176`) decides that a record has nothing upstream (`static`) when its ref is `file:` or `url:`, or its release id contains `@sha256:` or `@dir:`. `update` (`src/app/update.rs:174`), `outdated` (`src/app/outdated.rs:418`) and the only-copy rule (`src/engine/plan.rs:800`) read it. A `--file <dir>` install under a `gh:` ref with an `@listing:` id would stop being static, and `update` would replace the user's local folder with the upstream release. `is_static` must learn `@listing:` in this same commit.
- **Found while writing this bead:** with a stable id, installing an unchanged `--file <dir>` again plans as already current (the same-release check, `src/engine/plan.rs:3608-3619`), as a `file:` directory already does; `--reinstall` still installs it again. README's install section ("A browser download") documents only `--file ZIP`.
- `same_release` (`src/resolve/updates.rs:369-382`) compares the part after the last `@`; a record an older build wrote with `@dir:<ULID>` therefore differs from the new `@listing:<hash>` once, so the first install after the upgrade reinstalls, and every later one is stable.

## Technical Approach

1. **`src/sources/local.rs`:** make `listing_hash` `pub(crate)` (no behaviour change; its doc comment already describes the hash).
2. **`src/engine/plan.rs`, `local_identity`:** a directory gives `listing:<hash>` from `crate::sources::local::listing_hash`; a readable regular file keeps `sha256:<hex>`; anything else keeps today's fresh `dir:<ULID>`. *Decided while writing this bead:* the fallback stays, because such an input fails inspection before it can become a change, so its id never reaches a record or a token's selection. Update the doc comments at `:5388-5389` ("a directory is identified by its listing, so an unchanged one is current and a changed one an update") and `:5429-5430`.
3. **`src/resolve/updates.rs`, `is_static`:** a release id containing `@listing:` is static too, beside `@sha256:` and `@dir:` (kept for records older builds wrote). Extend the doc comment.
4. **README, install section, "A browser download":** add that `--file` also takes an unpacked folder; its identity is a hash of its listing (every file's path, size and modification time, `.git` aside), as for a `file:` folder, so installing an unchanged folder again changes nothing (the item is `unchanged`), an edited one updates, `--reinstall` installs it again, and `update` and `outdated` never replace it from upstream (`static`). Edit only that paragraph. *Decided while writing this bead:* the flag's clap `value_name` (`ZIP`, `src/app/install.rs:64-66`) and README's flag-table row stay as they are, because changing the help text would ripple into the help snapshots and `cli_skeleton` literals for no behaviour change; the paragraph is where the directory case is documented.

**Wire note for the close comment (common rule 6, M4-D55):** a `--file <dir>` record's `release_id` changes form from `<ref>@dir:<ULID>` to `<ref>@listing:<hash>`. It is a value, not a key, on install's own surface. Compatibility: records older builds wrote keep `@dir:` and stay static; the next `install --file <dir>` of such an addon reinstalls once.

**What not to do:** do not change `file:` refs (already stable), the zip identity, `listing_hash`'s algorithm, or `same_release`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `local_identity` of a directory is `listing:<hash>`, equal for two calls on an unchanged directory, different after a file in it is edited, unchanged by content under `.git`; a zip still gives `sha256:<hex>`.
- [ ] `is_static` is true for a `gh:` record whose release id ends `@listing:<hex>`, and still for `@sha256:` and `@dir:` ids.
- [ ] README's install section documents `--file <dir>` (identity, unchanged when unchanged, `--reinstall`, never updated from upstream), in this commit.
- [ ] The close comment carries the release-id wire note and its compatibility note.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

- `src/engine/plan.rs`, `a_directory_input_is_identified_by_its_listing`: table over a temp directory, rows `unchanged` (two calls equal, prefix `listing:`), `file edited` (differs), `file added` (differs), `.git/HEAD written` (equal), `a zip` (prefix `sha256:`), `a missing path` (prefix `dir:`). Messages name the row and show both identities.
- `src/engine/plan.rs`, the existing `only_copies_are_what_no_source_gives_again` gains the row `("a local directory by listing", owned("gh:o/foo", Some("gh:o/foo@listing:ab"), None), true)`.
- `src/resolve/updates.rs`, `static_unchecked_and_failed` gains `"gh:o/foo@listing:ab12"` among its given-archive ids (static).

### Integration and end-to-end tests

The end-to-end rows (`install --file <dir>` twice through the binary, `--reinstall`, `update --dry-run` skipping it with no request, and the library-level `a_file_directory_plans_with_one_release_id`) are in omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.6, which waits for the test log of T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs and the `argc e2e` runner).

### Logging

Unit tests only: one name per row, messages `"<row>: <first id> vs <second id>"`.

## Considerations

- **Behaviour change, intended:** a repeated `install --file <dir>` of an unchanged folder used to reinstall it every time; now it is `unchanged`, like a `file:` folder. A developer who edits files in place gets an update (the listing moves with size or mtime); one who wants a reinstall regardless uses `--reinstall`. README says so.
- **What the listing cannot see:** an edit that keeps a file's size and restores its mtime. That is the existing `file:` rule; the approval witness (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.4) records the same listing for the token, and the folders the plan replaces are witnessed by content.
- **Risk #19:** this subtask removes one known source of tokens that stale for no reason.
- **Hot spot:** `src/engine/plan.rs` is shared with omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.4 and omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.5 (different functions: `local_identity` here) and with D2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2`, `--if-match` on `install`, `update`, `sync` and `copy`) and D8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8`, the approval checked again under the commit lock) later; rebase before the gate.

## Dependencies

Parent: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1 (`precondition::of_plan` and the approval witness for engine commands).

- **Before it:** none; it can start at once.
- **After it:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.6 (Tests: equal tokens across dry runs and per source, and the `--file <dir>` id end to end) tests the id through planning and the binary.

title: `EntryDigest` and the folder witness, with index digests reused behind a racy-clean stamp check
description:
Part 3 of 7 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1 (`precondition::of_plan` and the approval witness for engine commands). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

D1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1`) builds the token every engine-backed command carries in M4, and the **approval witness** that makes it honest (M4-D60): per target, the complete content, identity and absence evidence of everything the plan reads, replaces or removes, so that any edit between a preview and its bound run stales the token. Generations prove only that no omaddons transaction committed: a person editing a file, a sync tool restoring one, or a hand-installed folder appearing never moves a generation. And the existing `LocalChanges` (`src/engine/plan.rs:748-760`) is a warning sample of at most ten paths with no digest, so it cannot be evidence.

This subtask builds the witness's foundation: **`EntryDigest`**, a content digest of one folder that counts every entry kind, and **`witness::folder`**, which computes it cheaply by reusing the files index's digests for racy-clean files and hashing everything else, and keeps the folder's stat stamp as private proof of "unchanged since" when the folder was settled. It is its own step because it is pure filesystem reading with no dependency on planning, and its correctness (what to trust, what never to open or follow, when to fail closed) is the heart of the design gate; the next subtask, omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.4, decides which folders to witness and puts the result into the plan.

M4-D60's rule for this part: "A file whose stamp proves it racy-clean against the files index takes its digest from the index, exactly as `drift::check`'s quick mode trusts it; every other file is hashed. So a clean file costs a `stat`, and a file that was clean at preview and edited afterwards is caught, because its stamp moved." And: read the `TreeStamp`, reuse or hash, read the stamp again; "if it is unchanged and settled, keep it in the witness's private `stamps` for the under-lock check; if it moved while hashing, or is within the racy slack, keep the digest without a stamp, as `predigest` does" (so D8, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8`, re-hashes that folder under the lock).

**Facts this subtask relies on** (verified at `c0ab5e9`):
- `TreeDigest` covers regular files only; symlinks and empty directories do not contribute (`src/fsx/mutate.rs:118-122`), so it cannot be the witness's digest.
- `TreeStamp` (`src/fsx/stamp.rs:108-146`) is every entry's `lstat` stamp (device, inode, type, permission bits, size, mtime, ctime) by relative path, in byte order, the root as the empty path; symlinks are stamped, never followed; directories count. Its entries, and `FileStamp`'s device, inode, type and ctime, are private (`:21-31`). `TreeStamp::read` has no bound and lists the root with `read_dir`, which follows a symlinked root (`:115-131`). `FileStamp::settled(read_at_ns)` is true once the ctime is a racy slack older than the read (`:89-105`): `RACY_SLACK_NS` (20 ms), or `RACY_SLACK_COARSE_NS` (2 s) for whole-second ctimes (`src/limits.rs:118`, `:127`).
- `predigest`/`with_predigests` (`src/engine/swap.rs:574-634`) already follow the pattern: read the stamp, skip if unsettled, hash, keep the digest only when the stamp read again is unchanged.
- The files index (`src/state/files_index.rs:27-75`): per folder key, `{name, tree, files[{path, size, mtime_ns, sha256}], recorded_at_ns?}`; `FilesIndex::recorded_at_ns(folder)` falls back to `written_at_ns`. `drift`'s stat mode trusts a file when size and mtime equal the index's and `mtime < recorded_at_ns - slack(entry)` (`src/drift.rs:306-318`, `:343-346`), `slack` being `RACY_SLACK_NS` when any indexed mtime has a sub-second part, else `RACY_SLACK_COARSE_NS`. It never looks at ctime.
- `hash_file_streaming` opens with `File::open` (follows symlinks, blocks on a FIFO; `src/state/files_index.rs:139-143`); `hash_reader` (`:116-137`) streams 64 KiB chunks and is private. `index_live_folder` (`:145-261`) builds two errors this subtask reuses: `io` with `details {reason: "unindexable", folder, path}` (`:160-168`) and `archive_too_large` with `details {reason: "limit_exceeded", folder, measured, limit, config_key}` (`:169-184`).
- `ArchiveLimits` (`src/engine/inspect.rs:42-59`) carries `max_entries` (`ARCHIVE_MAX_ENTRIES`, 20,000, config `limits.archive_max_entries`) and `max_uncompressed` (`ARCHIVE_MAX_UNCOMPRESSED`, 1 GiB, config `limits.archive_max_uncompressed`); `src/limits.rs:21`, `:23`.
- Outside `src/fsx/`, `tests/single_writer.rs` bans `OpenOptions` and write-mode `OFlags` but allows read-only opens (`:17-58`); `rustix` with `fs` is a dependency.
- Staging writes every file fresh and waits until the newest staged mtime is a racy slack in the past before the lock (`Staged::wait_out_racy_slack`, `src/engine/stage.rs:48-74`), so the files a commit indexes have mtime and ctime both older than the index's `recorded_at_ns` minus the slack.

## Technical Approach

### 1. `src/fsx/stamp.rs`: read-only accessors and a bounded read

- `FileStamp::{dev(), ino(), ctime_ns(), file_type()}` (plain getters beside the existing `size()`, `mtime_ns()`, `is_file()`).
- `TreeStamp::entries(&self) -> &[(PathBuf, FileStamp)]`.
- `TreeStamp::read_at_most(dir: &Path, max_entries: u64) -> io::Result<Option<Self>>`: `read`'s walk, stopping with `Ok(None)` as soon as it has seen more than `max_entries` entries (the root included). `read` keeps its behaviour (it is `read_at_most(dir, u64::MAX)` or stays as is).
- Nothing else in `src/fsx/` changes: no write path, no new primitive.

### 2. `src/state/files_index.rs` and `src/drift.rs`

- `hash_reader` becomes `pub(crate)`.
- The two error shapes of `index_live_folder` become `pub(crate) fn unindexable(folder: &str, rel: &str, message: String, fix: Suggestion) -> Error` (code `io`, `details {reason: "unindexable", folder, path}`) and `pub(crate) fn limit_exceeded(folder: &str, what: &str, measured: u64, limit: u64, config_key: &str) -> Error` (code `archive_too_large`, `details {reason: "limit_exceeded", folder, measured, limit, config_key}`, message "`<folder>` has `<measured>` `<what>`, over the limit of `<limit>`", its existing prose fix); `index_live_folder` calls them with its existing messages and fixes, byte-identical (its tests pass unchanged).
- `drift::slack` becomes `pub(crate)`, so the witness uses exactly drift's slack.

### 3. `src/engine/witness.rs` (new; `pub mod witness;` in `src/engine/mod.rs`)

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash)]
pub struct EntryDigest([u8; 32]);          // Display: "entry:sha256:<64 hex>"
impl EntryDigest {
    pub fn of_dir(dir: &Path, limits: &ArchiveLimits) -> Result<Self>;   // no index: everything hashed (the re-hash under the lock, and tests)
}
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash)]
pub enum WitnessRole { Replaced, Removed, CopySource, Adopted }   // wire(): "replaced" | "removed" | "copy_source" | "adopted"
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct FolderWitness { pub role: WitnessRole, pub key: String, pub digest: EntryDigest }
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct WitnessCost { pub files_hashed: u64, pub files_reused: u64, pub bytes_hashed: u64 }
pub(crate) struct Folder { pub digest: EntryDigest, pub stamp: Option<TreeStamp>, pub cost: WitnessCost }
pub(crate) fn folder(dir: &Path, index: Option<(&FilesIndex, &FolderIndex)>, limits: &ArchiveLimits,
                     now_ns: i128, between: &mut dyn FnMut()) -> Result<Folder>;
```

**The digest's encoding.** A SHA-256 over length-prefixed fields (a big-endian `u64` length, then the bytes, as `build.rs`'s `field()` frames the widget digest, so no file name, which may contain a newline, can forge a boundary): first the field `omaddons entry digest 1`; then each entry in bytewise order of its raw relative path (`OsStr::as_bytes`, `/`-separated, the folder itself as the empty path; never a lossy conversion, so two names that differ only in invalid UTF-8 differ), as a kind field, a path field and the kind's payload fields:

| Kind | Entry | Payload |
|---|---|---|
| `d` | a real directory, the root included | none |
| `f` | a regular file | its size in decimal; its lowercase hex SHA-256 |
| `l` | a symlink, never followed | its raw target bytes (`std::fs::read_link`) |
| `o:fifo`, `o:socket`, `o:char`, `o:block`, `o:unknown` | anything else, never opened | none |
| `x` | an entry that changed while it was read (step 3) | none |
| `a` | the folder itself is absent (the only entry) | none |

So an added symlink, an added empty directory or an added empty file changes the digest (unlike `TreeDigest`), while a `touch` or a `chmod` does not (it is content, unlike `StampDigest`). Modes are not part of it: M4-D60 lists content, identity and absence, and the under-lock stamp comparison of D8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8`, the approval checked again under the commit lock) sees a mode change and simply re-hashes.

**`folder(..)`, step by step.** `now_ns` is the wall clock (`Timestamp::now().as_nanosecond()`) taken by the caller before the first read; tests inject it to decide settledness exactly. `between` runs after the entries are digested and before the second stamp read: `&mut || {}` in production, a closure that edits the folder in the moving-folder tests.

1. `lstat` the folder (`FileStamp::read`). Absent: the digest is the single `a` entry, no stamp. A symlink, regular file or other kind: the digest is that one entry with the empty path (a root file hashed as in step 3), no stamp, never walked. A directory: go on.
2. `TreeStamp::read_at_most(dir, limits.max_entries)`. `None` fails the folder with `limit_exceeded(folder, "entries", limits.max_entries + 1, limits.max_entries, "limits.archive_max_entries")`. If the root entry of the stamp is not a directory (it was replaced between the two reads), start again from step 1 once, then treat it as that kind.
3. For each entry of the stamp, in order:
   - a directory, symlink or other kind: encoded from its stamp (a symlink's target via `read_link`; a `read_link` failure because it is gone encodes `x`);
   - a regular file whose relative path (`/`-separated, UTF-8) the index lists is **reused** when it is racy-clean: the stamp's size equals the index entry's size, the stamp's mtime equals the entry's `mtime_ns`, and both the stamp's mtime and its **ctime** are strictly older than `racy_from = index.recorded_at_ns(folder) - drift::slack(folder)`. Its `(size, sha256)` come from the index; the file is not opened; `files_reused += 1`;
   - every other regular file is **hashed**: `rustix::fs::open(path, OFlags::RDONLY | OFlags::NOFOLLOW | OFlags::NONBLOCK | OFlags::CLOEXEC, Mode::empty())`, then `rustix::fs::fstat` must show a regular file with the stamp's device and inode; the handle (as a `std::fs::File`) is streamed through `files_index::hash_reader`; the recorded size is the number of bytes read. `files_hashed += 1`, `bytes_hashed += size`. When `bytes_hashed` passes `limits.max_uncompressed` the folder fails with `limit_exceeded(folder, "bytes", bytes_hashed, limits.max_uncompressed, "limits.archive_max_uncompressed")`. An open that finds the file gone (`ENOENT`), a symlink (`ELOOP`), a non-regular file or another inode encodes `x`. Any other open, read or `read_dir` error (`EACCES`, `EIO`) fails the folder with `unindexable(..)`, message "`<folder>/<rel>` cannot be read (`<error>`), so the folder cannot be witnessed for this preview", prose fix "make it readable, or move the folder out of AddOns, then preview again" (a prose fix names no runnable command, common rule 8).
4. Call `between`, then read the `TreeStamp` again (bounded the same way). If it equals the first and the first is settled at `now_ns` (`TreeStamp::settled`), return it as the folder's stamp; otherwise return no stamp. A digest computed while the folder moved, or holding an `x`, matches no later steady-state digest, so any comparison against it is stale: the safe direction.

`EntryDigest::of_dir(dir, limits)` is `folder(dir, None, limits, i128::MAX, &mut || {})`'s digest, the stamp discarded.

*Decided while writing this bead:* the reuse test adds the ctime condition to drift's. User space can set an mtime back (`touch -r`, `rsync -t`, editors that keep times) but never a ctime, so with drift's rule alone an mtime-preserving same-size edit made between a preview and its bound run would be trusted from the index at the bound run's own planning, and D8's under-lock check (which compares with the bound run's own stamps) would not see it either. Freshly committed files pass the ctime test as they pass the mtime test (staging writes them fresh and waits out the slack), so the condition costs a hash only where an inode changed after it was indexed. Confirm or adjust in the close comment.

*Decided while writing this bead:* only entries the stamp calls regular files are ever opened, always without following links and without blocking, and checked by inode after opening; a FIFO present (or swapped in) would otherwise hang a dry run, and a symlink swapped in would read outside the folder.

*Decided while writing this bead:* incomplete evidence fails closed (common rule 15, §8.1 rule 6), with the codes adoption already uses for a live folder it cannot read; recording an unreadable file as "unreadable" inside the digest was rejected, because the token would then approve bytes nobody observed. The bounds are per folder, as for adoption; reused files do not count against the byte bound.

**What not to do:** never call `TreeStamp::read` on a path that is not a real directory; never use `File::open`, `hash_file_streaming` or anything that follows links on a witnessed entry; never read `WTF/` (the witness is given AddOns folders only); never write.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `EntryDigest` changes with an added empty directory, empty file or symlink, a retargeted symlink, a renamed, deleted, grown or same-size-edited file, and the eleventh edited file of eleven; it does not change with a `touch`, a `chmod`, or a file recreated with identical bytes.
- [ ] A clean indexed file is reused without being opened (`files_reused` counts it, `files_hashed` does not), and the reused digest equals `EntryDigest::of_dir`'s; a file whose size, mtime or ctime fails the racy-clean test is hashed; an mtime-preserving same-size edit is hashed and moves the digest (while drift's stat mode reports no change for it).
- [ ] A folder edited by `between` keeps no stamp; an unsettled folder (`now_ns` within the slack of its newest ctime) keeps none; a settled, unchanged one keeps a stamp equal to `TreeStamp::read`.
- [ ] A FIFO inside a folder is recorded `o:fifo` and never opened (the call returns within 5 s); a symlink to `/` and a symlink loop are recorded by target and never followed; a root that is a symlink is one `l` entry.
- [ ] An unreadable file or directory fails with `io`, `details.reason: "unindexable"`, `folder` and `path`; more entries than `max_entries` or more hashed bytes than `max_uncompressed` fails with `archive_too_large`, `details.reason: "limit_exceeded"`, `measured`, `limit` and `config_key`; reused bytes never count.
- [ ] `index_live_folder`'s errors are byte-identical after the refactor (its tests pass unchanged), and drift's behaviour is unchanged.
- [ ] Nothing outside `src/fsx/` writes (`tests/single_writer.rs` passes); `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

In `src/engine/witness.rs` (`#[cfg(test)]`), over temp directories, with helpers `folder_with(&[(path, bytes)])`, `indexed(dir, recorded_at_ns)` (from `index_live_folder(..).stamped(at)`, wrapped in a one-folder `FilesIndex`) and `tick()` (sleep 30 ms, longer than the kernel's timestamp tick, as `src/fsx/stamp.rs`'s tests do). Every table row is named; messages show the row, both digests and the cost.

- `the_entry_digest_counts_every_kind`: base `Foo/Foo.toc`, `Foo/libs/lib.lua`; rows that move it: `added empty dir`, `added empty file`, `added symlink`, `symlink retargeted`, `file renamed`, `file deleted`, `same size, one byte changed`, `file grew`; rows that do not: `touch`, `chmod 600`, `recreated identical (new inode)`.
- `the_eleventh_changed_file_moves_the_digest`: 11 files; ten edited versus the same ten plus the eleventh: the digests differ.
- `a_root_that_is_not_a_directory_is_one_entry`: a root symlink to an identical copy (differs from the real folder's digest), a root regular file, an absent root (`a`).
- `clean_indexed_files_are_reused_and_others_hashed`: index recorded well after every ctime: `files_reused == n`, `files_hashed == 0`, digest equal to `of_dir`; one file edited: `files_hashed == 1`.
- `the_racy_clean_edge`: rows `recorded at ctime + slack + 1` (reused), `recorded at ctime + slack` (hashed: not strictly older), `index mtime differs` (hashed), `index size differs` (hashed), `whole-second index mtimes` (the coarse slack applies).
- `an_mtime_preserving_same_size_edit_is_hashed`: index, `tick()`, rewrite with other bytes of the same size and `set_modified` back to the old mtime: hashed, digest moved; the control asserts `drift::check_folder(.., DriftMode::Stat)` reports `changed == 0` for the same state, which is why the ctime condition exists.
- `a_trusted_index_digest_is_used_as_recorded`: an index entry with matching stamps and a deliberately wrong SHA-256 is used as recorded (the digest differs from `of_dir`): the economy drift already relies on, documented by a test.
- `a_folder_that_moves_while_hashed_keeps_no_stamp`: `between` writes a new file: `stamp == None`, digest is the pre-edit content's.
- `an_unsettled_folder_keeps_no_stamp`: `now_ns = newest ctime + RACY_SLACK_NS` gives no stamp; `+ 1` gives one equal to `TreeStamp::read(dir)`.
- `a_fifo_is_recorded_and_never_opened`: a FIFO created with `rustix::fs::mknodat` (test code); the call runs on a thread joined with a 5 s timeout; the digest has an `o:fifo` entry.
- `a_symlink_is_never_followed`: `escape -> /` and `loop -> .` inside; returns, `files_hashed` counts only the folder's own files.
- `open_regular_refuses_another_inode_and_never_blocks`: the open helper given a FIFO, a symlink, a gone path and a wrong inode returns "changed" each time without blocking.
- `a_non_utf8_name_is_hashed_by_its_bytes`: names `b"\xff"` and `b"\xfe"` give different digests.
- `an_unreadable_file_fails_with_unindexable` and `an_unreadable_directory_fails_with_unindexable` (mode `0o000`, as `tests/remove.rs` does): `ErrorCode::Io`, `details == {reason: "unindexable", folder, path}`.
- `past_the_entry_limit_fails_with_limit_exceeded` (`max_entries: 3`, five entries: `measured 4`, `limit 3`, `config_key "limits.archive_max_entries"`) and `past_the_byte_limit_fails_but_reused_bytes_do_not_count` (`max_uncompressed: 10`, a 20-byte unindexed file fails; the same file indexed and clean passes).
- `entry_digest_displays_as_entry_sha256`.

In `src/fsx/stamp.rs`: `read_at_most_stops_past_the_bound` (four entries: `max 3` gives `None`, `max 4` gives the same stamp as `read`) and `the_accessors_report_the_stamp` (ino, dev, ctime, type of a file, a dir and a symlink).

### Integration and end-to-end tests

None here; the adversarial matrix through planning is omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.7.

### Logging

Unit tests only, table-driven, one name per row, messages `"<row>: digest <a> vs <b>, cost <cost>"`.

## Considerations

- **Hot spot `src/fsx/` (E13 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.13` first, G3 `omad-7ccp`, group commit and deferred directory fsyncs, last).** This subtask adds only read-only accessors and `read_at_most` to `stamp.rs`, a file E13 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.13`, resource sets and fsx endpoint predicates) does not edit (it works in `mutate.rs` and `journal.rs`); rebase if E13 lands first.
- **Cost:** two `lstat` walks per witnessed folder, plus one streamed hash per file that is unindexed or no longer racy-clean. D8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8`, the approval checked again under the commit lock) reports what the under-lock re-read adds; `WitnessCost` gives it the counts.
- **The index is trusted as drift trusts it:** a corrupted index entry with matching stamps is believed (the documented test). Whoever can rewrite `<state>` can rewrite anything omaddons trusts; this is not a new exposure.
- **Timing tests:** settledness is decided by the injected `now_ns`, never by sleeping against the slack, so no row is flaky; `tick()` is used only where a ctime must move.
- **Risk #19 (a token stales for no reason):** the digest is content, so stamps that move without a content change (a `touch`, a backup tool's `chmod`) never move it.

## Dependencies

Parent: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1 (`precondition::of_plan` and the approval witness for engine commands).

- **Before it:** none; it can start at once.
- **After it:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.4 (`witness::collect` at the end of planning) calls `folder` for every witnessed folder and builds the per-target witness around it.
- Related, not an edge: D8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8`, the approval checked again under the commit lock) uses `EntryDigest::of_dir`, `TreeStamp::entries` and the private stamps for its under-lock check.

comments.text:
**Done (part 3 of D1).** Commit `ec70995`.

**What changed.**
- **`src/fsx/stamp.rs`:**
  - `FileStamp::{dev, ino, ctime_ns, file_type}` and `TreeStamp::entries` (read-only accessors).
  - `TreeStamp::read_at_most(dir, max_entries)` returns `None` past the bound. A root that is not a real directory is its one entry and is never listed, so a symlinked root is not followed.
  - A walk that cannot list or stamp a directory returns an `io::Error` carrying a new `WalkError { rel, source }`, which `WalkError::rel_of` reads back. That gives the witness the failing directory for `details.path`. `read` keeps its code and behaviour.
  - `WalkError` is re-exported from `fsx`. Nothing writes.
- **`src/state/files_index.rs`:** `hash_reader` becomes `pub(crate)`. The two error shapes become `pub(crate) fn unindexable(folder, rel, message, fix)` and `pub(crate) fn limit_exceeded(folder, what, measured, limit, config_key)`. `index_live_folder` calls them with its existing messages and fixes, so its errors are byte-identical (its tests pass unchanged).
- **`src/drift.rs`:** `slack` becomes `pub(crate)`; drift is otherwise unchanged.
- **`src/engine/witness.rs`** (new):
  - The types: `EntryDigest` (`entry:sha256:<hex>`, with `of_dir`), `WitnessRole` (with `wire()`), `FolderWitness`, `WitnessCost`, and `Folder` with `folder(dir, index, limits, now_ns, between)`.
  - The digest is a SHA-256 over u64-big-endian length-prefixed fields: `omaddons entry digest 1`, then each entry's kind (`d`, `f`, `l`, `o:fifo|socket|char|block|unknown`, `x`, `a`), raw path bytes and payload, in byte order.
  - Reuse, opening and `x` follow section 3. Only regular files are opened, with `RDONLY | NOFOLLOW | NONBLOCK | CLOEXEC`, and `fstat` must show the stamp's device and inode. ENOENT, ELOOP, ENXIO, ENOTDIR, a non-regular file or another inode encodes `x`.
  - Failures: an unreadable entry gives `unindexable` with the bead's message and prose fix; too many entries or hashed bytes gives `limit_exceeded`.
  - The stamp is kept only when the second bounded read equals the first and the first is settled at `now_ns`.

**Decided while implementing.**
- **The byte bound is checked before reading:** the stamp's size against what is left of the budget, so a huge file is never read. The read is also capped at `remaining + 1` bytes, so a file growing while read cannot run past the bound.
- **A `NotFound` during the stamp walk** (something moved while listed) retries the folder once, as a root kind change does.
- **`Folder` and `folder()` are `pub`,** not `pub(crate)`: the lib exports `engine::witness`, and in-crate-only items would be dead code until part 4 calls them.
- **`std::fs::File` is named in full,** not imported: the single-writer scanner forbids importing `File` outside fsx, as the rest of `src/` follows.

**Decided while writing the bead, confirmed:**
- The ctime condition on reuse. The control test shows drift's stat mode reports `changed == 0` for an mtime-preserving same-size edit, while the witness hashes it and the digest moves.
- Only stamped regular files are opened, never following links and never blocking, and checked by inode.
- Incomplete evidence fails closed, with adoption's codes; reused bytes never count against the byte bound.

**Tests** (24 in `engine::witness` and `fsx::stamp`):
- **Digest content:**
  - `the_entry_digest_counts_every_kind`: 11 rows. These move the digest: an added empty dir, empty file or symlink, a retargeted symlink, a rename, a delete, a same-size edit, a growth. These do not: `touch`, `chmod`, an identical recreation.
  - `the_eleventh_changed_file_moves_the_digest`.
  - `a_root_that_is_not_a_directory_is_one_entry`: a symlinked root (never walked), a root file, an absent root.
  - `a_non_utf8_name_is_hashed_by_its_bytes`.
  - `entry_digest_displays_as_entry_sha256`.
- **Reuse:**
  - `clean_indexed_files_are_reused_and_others_hashed`.
  - `the_racy_clean_edge`: `+slack+1` is reused and `+slack` is hashed; a differing index mtime or size is hashed; whole-second mtimes use the coarse slack.
  - `an_mtime_preserving_same_size_edit_is_hashed`, with the drift control.
  - `a_trusted_index_digest_is_used_as_recorded`.
- **Stamps:** `a_folder_that_moves_while_hashed_keeps_no_stamp`, and `an_unsettled_folder_keeps_no_stamp` (`now = ctime + slack` gives none; `+1` gives a stamp equal to `TreeStamp::read`).
- **Opening:**
  - `a_fifo_is_recorded_and_never_opened`: run on a thread with a 5 s timeout; `o:fifo` is present.
  - `a_symlink_is_never_followed`: `escape -> /` and `loop -> .`.
  - `open_regular_refuses_another_inode_and_never_blocks`: a FIFO, a symlink, a gone path and another inode.
- **Failures:**
  - `an_unreadable_file_fails_with_unindexable` and `an_unreadable_directory_fails_with_unindexable` (both skipped as root).

title: `witness::collect` at the end of planning, and the witness plumbing from `TxRequest`
description:
Part 4 of 7 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1 (`precondition::of_plan` and the approval witness for engine commands). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

D1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1`) builds the token every engine-backed command carries in M4 and the per-target **approval witness** its `observed` part digests (M4-D60). The witness records, for the plan it binds: every live folder a replace or remove will move, managed or not, edited or clean (as an entry digest); every name the plan creates, as absent; the target's identity (its key and the client marker's digest); the local inputs (a `--file` zip's SHA-256, a `--file <dir>`'s listing hash, a git checkout's commit); for `copy`, the entry digests of every source folder; for `adopt`, the entry digests of the folders it records; the dependency selections (which addon satisfies which requirement) and the judge digest. Its canonical digest is `observed`'s witness part, so a bound run's own planning, before anything is staged, already compares it; D8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8`, the approval checked again under the commit lock) checks it again under the lock.

omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.3 built `EntryDigest` and `witness::folder` (one folder, cheaply, with its private settled stamp). This subtask decides **which** folders and facts each target's witness holds, collects it at the end of planning, and plumbs it: `TargetRef` (a target's key, or its provisional id), the `ApprovalWitness` type, `witness::collect` and `witness::bare`, `Plan.witnesses`, and `TxRequest.witness`, the switch a command flips to have witnesses collected. It is its own step because it is the only part that touches planning (`src/engine/plan.rs`, `src/engine/tx.rs`) and every `TxRequest` site; it changes no command's behaviour (every site passes `witness: None`), and omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.5 turns the witnesses into the token.

**Facts this subtask relies on** (verified at `c0ab5e9`):
- `plan::plan` (`src/engine/plan.rs:1186-1542`) plans each target in a loop where its record, files index (`target_state`, `:2563-2569`) and live inventory are in scope; the iteration ends with `tp.creates_addons_dir`, `tp.notes` and `targets.push(tp)` (`:1508-1523`). A target whose live inventory cannot be read fails every change under its own ref and addon and is pushed with no work (`:1344-1368`).
- `TargetPlan` (`:513-548`): `target` (the id, provisional while unregistered), `key: Option<TargetKey>`, `changes`, `ops`, `releases`, `creates_addons_dir`, and `#[serde(skip)]` `generation`, `work: Vec<AddonWork>` and `dependencies: BTreeMap<String, DepReport>`. A work's folder renames are `SwapOp::{Add {name}, Replace {name, live, ..}, Remove {live, ..}}` (`src/engine/swap.rs:46-60`), read through `AddonWork::swap()` (`plan.rs:1120-1126`). `DepReport` (`:550-566`) lists `installs (folder, addon)`, `unmanaged` folders, `unresolved {folder, reason, candidates}` and `failed (folder, ref)`. `ChangeKind::Adopt` marks "unmanaged folders brought under management, unchanged", whose folders are in `folders.recorded` (`:631-654`).
- `FolderWork` (`:713-746`) derives no serde; the winning candidate's `AssetLocation` is known in `prepare_install` where the release is built (`:3862-3881`) and the work is finished in `build` (`:3895-3924`, `f.deps = b.deps` at `:3909`). Asset locations (`src/model.rs:1169-1197`): `LocalZip(path)`, `LocalDir(path)`, `GitCheckout {url, rev, sha}`, `Url`, `Deferred`, `WowAceTree`; a reinstall from the blob cache is a `LocalZip` under the blob cache directory (`local_blob_candidate`, `plan.rs:5346-5376`).
- `Target.judge` is the hex judge digest (`src/model.rs:546-550`); the client marker is `discover::registry::marker_path(client_dir)` (`src/discover/registry.rs:33-39`), a `{schema_version, key}` file written only at registration.
- Provisional ids are deterministic (`src/discover/registry.rs:123-136`) and lowercase (`id_safe`, `:203-221`); a `TargetKey` displays as an uppercase ULID. `app::outcome::TargetRef` already exists as a wire struct `{id, key, mode}` (`src/app/outcome.rs:33-41`), and the engine never imports `app` outside tests.
- `TxRequest` (`src/engine/tx.rs:116-130`) derives `Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq` and is built as a literal at 13 sites: `src/app/{remove,pin,install (2),outdated,update,copy,sync}.rs`, `src/app/adopt/apply.rs`, `src/engine/testing.rs:504`, `tests/undo_history.rs:971`, `tests/engine_multi_target.rs:146`, `tests/deps.rs:1743`. `tx::run` builds the `PlanRequest` from it (`:351-367`); `PlanRequest` (`plan.rs:75-85`) is built at 4 sites (`src/engine/tx.rs:351`, `src/engine/plan.rs:2624` and `:6357`, `tests/plan.rs:141`). `engine::testing::TxScene` (`src/engine/testing.rs:324-590`) runs requests for unit tests.

## Technical Approach

### 1. `TargetRef` (`src/model.rs`)

```rust
/// A target as a token or a stored plan names it: its key once registered, else its
/// provisional id (deterministic, discover::registry::reconcile).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Hash)]
pub enum TargetRef { Key(TargetKey), Provisional(String) }
```

- `TargetRef::of(key: Option<TargetKey>, id: &str) -> Self`; `Display` is the plain string (the key's canonical display, or the id).
- Derived `Ord`: every `Key` before every `Provisional`, keys by `TargetKey`'s own order, so a sorted list of registered targets is ordered exactly as a sorted `Vec<TargetKey>` (M3's tokens depend on it, omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.5).
- `Serialize` as the plain string; `Deserialize`: a string equal to a parsed `TargetKey`'s canonical display is `Key`, anything else `Provisional`; `JsonSchema`: a string. Lowercase provisional ids and uppercase keys never collide. D4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`, the plan store) decodes stored intents with it.
- *Decided while writing this bead:* the plan sketches it in `src/app/precondition.rs`; it lives in `src/model.rs` because the engine's witness holds one and the engine never imports `app`, and because `app::outcome::TargetRef` (a different, wire struct) already owns that name in `app`. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.5 re-exports it as `precondition::TargetRef`; a file that uses both imports one by path.

### 2. The witness types (`src/engine/witness.rs`, beside omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.3's)

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct ApprovalWitness {
    pub target: TargetRef,
    pub marker: Option<String>,               // "sha256:<hex>" of the marker's bytes, "link:<target>", "kind:<type>"; None if absent
    pub folders: Vec<FolderWitness>,          // sorted by (key, role)
    pub absent: Vec<String>,                  // folder keys the plan creates, and "Interface/AddOns" itself; sorted bytewise
    pub inputs: Vec<InputWitness>,            // sorted by (kind, source)
    pub dependencies: Vec<DependencyChoice>,  // sorted by (requester ASCII-lowercase, requester, folder, by)
    pub judge: String,                        // Target.judge
    stamps: Vec<(PathBuf, TreeStamp)>,        // each witnessed folder's settled stamp, by its directory; never hashed
    cost: WitnessCost,                        // summed over the folders
}
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct InputWitness { pub kind: InputKind, pub source: String, pub digest: String }
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)]
pub enum InputKind { Zip, Dir, Git }                     // wire(): "zip" | "dir" | "git"
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct DependencyChoice { pub requester: String, pub folder: String, pub by: DependencyBy }
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum DependencyBy { Installs(String), Unmanaged, Unresolved(UnresolvedReason), Failed(String) }
                                                          // wire(): "install" | "unmanaged" | "unresolved" | "failed";
                                                          // detail(): the addon, the reason's wire name, the ref, or None
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct WitnessScope { pub copy_from: Option<CopyFrom> }
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct CopyFrom { pub target: Target, pub folders: Vec<FolderName> }
pub struct WitnessCtx<'a> { pub paths: &'a Paths, pub target: &'a Target, pub index: Option<&'a FilesIndex>,
                            pub scope: &'a WitnessScope, pub limits: ArchiveLimits }
```

- `ApprovalWitness::new(target, marker, folders, absent, inputs, dependencies, judge)` sorts its lists and has no stamps (unit tests, and the no-op check of D2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2`, build witnesses with it); `pub(crate) fn stamp(&self, dir: &Path) -> Option<&TreeStamp>` and `pub fn cost(&self) -> WitnessCost` are for D8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8`, the approval checked again under the commit lock).
- The witness is not a wire shape: no `Serialize`. Only its digest (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.5) leaves the engine.

### 3. `witness::collect(tp: &TargetPlan, ctx: &WitnessCtx<'_>) -> Result<ApprovalWitness>`

`now_ns` is read once at its start (`Timestamp::now().as_nanosecond()`), and every folder is witnessed with omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.3's `folder(dir, index, &ctx.limits, now_ns, &mut || {})`.

- **Replaced and removed folders.** For every `SwapOp::Replace { live, .. }` (role `Replaced`) and `SwapOp::Remove { live, .. }` (role `Removed`) of every `tp.work[]`: the folder `ctx.target.addons_dir().join(live.as_str())`, with `ctx.index` and its entry for `live.key()` when there is one (managed: clean files reused) and no index otherwise (unmanaged: hashed). One witness per `(key, role)`.
- **Adopted folders.** For every change of kind `ChangeKind::Adopt`, each folder of `folders.recorded`, role `Adopted`, without index reuse. Pins, unpins and other `Edit` changes record folders without witnessing them: they change a record field, not what the folder holds.
- **Copy's source folders.** When `ctx.scope.copy_from` is `Some(CopyFrom { target, folders })`: each folder under `target.addons_dir()`, role `CopySource`, with the source's files index (`store::load::<FilesIndex>(&paths.files_index(&key))` when the source has a key) for reuse. A missing source folder is digested `a`.
- **Absent names.** Each `SwapOp::Add { name }` as `name.key()`, and `"Interface/AddOns"` when `tp.creates_addons_dir` (a folder key never contains `/`, so this entry is unambiguous). *Decided while writing this bead:* the live inventory planning just read is the evidence of absence, so they are not `lstat`ed again here; D8 re-checks them under the lock, and a name that appears before the bound run starts changes that run's own planning (an `Add` becomes a takeover or a failure, which moves `selection`).
- **The marker.** `marker_path(&ctx.target.client_dir)`: `None` when absent; a regular file hashed through omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.3's no-follow, non-blocking open (`sha256:<hex>`); a symlink as `link:<target>`; anything else as `kind:<type>`. An unreadable marker fails the target (`io`, `unindexable`, folder `Interface/.omaddons`, path `target.json`).
- **Inputs.** `FolderWork` gains `pub input: Option<InputWitness>`, carried on `PendingBuild` from `prepare_install` (where the winning candidate's location is known) and set in `build` beside `f.deps`: `LocalZip(path)` outside `paths.blobs_dir()` gives `Zip` with `inspected.blob_sha256`; `LocalDir(path)` gives `Dir` with `crate::sources::local::listing_hash(path)` (made `pub(crate)` by omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.2; if that subtask has not landed, make it so here); `GitCheckout { url, sha, .. }` gives `Git` with `sha`. `source` is the path's `display()` or the URL. Everything else (a download, a cached blob, a WowAce tree) is no input: its identity is already in `releases[]`. `collect` gathers every work's `input`.
- **Dependency choices.** From `tp.dependencies` (requester name → `DepReport`): `installs (folder, addon)` → `Installs(addon)`, `unmanaged` → `Unmanaged`, `unresolved` → `Unresolved(reason)` (candidates are hints for people, left out), `failed (folder, ref)` → `Failed(ref.to_string())`; `folder` is the folder's key. Bridge dependencies and `first_install` are reports, not choices.
- **The judge:** `ctx.target.judge.clone()`.

*Decided while writing this bead:* the `sync` file's SHA-256 is not a witness input: the engine never reads `addons.toml`; it enters `observed` through `PlanExtras::desired_sha256` (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.5).

`witness::bare(target: &Target) -> Result<ApprovalWitness>`: the marker and the judge, nothing else. Used for a target with no folder plan, and by D2's no-op check (`check_noop`) for in-scope targets that have nothing to do.

### 4. Where it runs: `PlanRequest.witness` and `Plan.witnesses` (`src/engine/plan.rs`)

- `PlanRequest` gains `pub witness: Option<WitnessScope>`; `Plan` gains `#[serde(skip)] pub witnesses: Vec<ApprovalWitness>` (empty when the request's `witness` is `None`; `schemars` skips it with serde). `rejudge` ignores the field.
- When `req.witness` is `Some(scope)`, every `TargetPlan` gets exactly one witness, pushed in `targets` order:
  - at the end of each target's iteration (after `tp.notes.extend(..)`, before `targets.push(tp)`): `witness::collect(&tp, &WitnessCtx { paths: ctx.paths, target, index: index.as_ref(), scope, limits: ctx.limits })`;
  - a target pushed early because `live_inventory` failed (`:1344-1368`): `witness::bare(target)`, or if even that fails, a witness with `marker: None` from `ApprovalWitness::new` (its changes have already failed). A target whose record or files index did not read plans on with every change failed (`unreadable_want`, `:1193-1213`) and reaches the end of the iteration, where `collect` runs normally and finds no work;
  - **when `collect` fails:** clear `tp.work`, `tp.ops`, `tp.releases` and `tp.changes`, turn each removed change into a `PlanFailure` under its `ref` and `addon` with the error (as a `live_inventory` failure does), set `tp.kind = None` and `tp.creates_addons_dir = false`, and push the bare witness. Nothing of that target can commit, and the other targets plan on.
- Only `plan::plan` collects; `check_releases`, `rejudge` and the commit window never do.

### 5. `TxRequest.witness` (`src/engine/tx.rs`) and every request site

- `TxRequest` gains `pub witness: Option<WitnessScope>` (doc: "collect an approval witness per target while planning: a dry run that returns a token, or a run bound to one"). `tx::run` copies it into the `PlanRequest`. `TxOutcomes.plan.witnesses` carries the witnesses back to the command.
- Every existing literal gets `witness: None`: the 13 `TxRequest` sites and the 4 `PlanRequest` sites listed above (grep `TxRequest {` and `PlanRequest {` again before the commit: peers may have added one). No production command collects a witness after this subtask; D2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2`) and D3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.3`) set `Some(..)` for the commands they bind (`copy` with its `CopyFrom`). No unbound real run ever pays for one.
- `engine::testing::TxScene` gains `run_witnessed(changes, scope) -> Result<TxOutcomes>`, a dry run with `witness: Some(scope)`, for this subtask's and later unit tests.
- *Decided while writing this bead:* this field is how the plan's "`PlanExtras` plumbing through `app::engine::Engine` into `tx::run`" is realized. `PlanExtras` itself is app-level (it holds `app::outcome::SkipReason`) and reaches `of_plan` through the command and through D2's `PlanBinding`, which `Engine::run_bound` (`src/app/engine.rs:201-209`) already hands to `tx::run`; what the engine needs from the command is only whether to witness and which source folders a `copy` reads.

**What not to do:** never collect witnesses in the commit window or in `rejudge`; never read `WTF/` or SavedVariables; never write; never make a collection failure fail the whole plan (it fails its target only).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `TargetRef` orders keys before provisional ids and keys as `TargetKey` does, displays and serializes as the plain string, and deserializes a key's canonical display as `Key` and anything else as `Provisional`.
- [ ] With `witness: Some(..)`, `plan.witnesses` has one witness per target, in target order, each with the right `target`; with `None` it is empty and planning behaves exactly as before (every existing engine and plan test passes unchanged).
- [ ] A replaced managed folder is witnessed `Replaced` with clean files reused; a replaced unmanaged folder (`--force`) is hashed; a removed folder is `Removed`; an adopt's recorded folders are `Adopted`; a pin's recorded folders are not witnessed; a `CopyFrom` source's folders are `CopySource`.
- [ ] A first install lists its new folders' keys and `Interface/AddOns` in `absent`; an update lists only folders it adds.
- [ ] The marker is `None` for an unregistered target and `sha256:<hex>` after registration; `judge` is the target's.
- [ ] A `--file` zip, a `--file <dir>` and a `git:` checkout each give their input (`zip`, `dir`, `git`) with the right digest; a download and a reinstall from the blob cache give none.
- [ ] A dependency installed with its requester, one satisfied by an unmanaged folder, and an unresolved one appear as `install`, `unmanaged` and `unresolved` choices.
- [ ] A target whose witness cannot be collected (an unreadable file in a replaced folder) has no work and one failure per change with the error, gets a bare witness, and another target in the same plan plans and witnesses normally.
- [ ] Collection writes nothing: `<state>` and the client dir hash identical before and after a witnessed dry run.
- [ ] Every `TxRequest` and `PlanRequest` literal passes `witness: None`; `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

In `src/model.rs`: `target_refs_order_keys_first_and_as_keys_do` (a shuffled mix sorts keys by ULID, then ids by string), `a_target_ref_is_its_plain_string` (`Display` and `serde_json` round trip for both variants; a lowercase ULID-like id stays `Provisional`).

In `src/engine/witness.rs`, over `engine::testing::TxScene` (local zips from `scene.zip`, `scene.install`, `scene.adopt`, `scene.remove`, `run_witnessed`), each case named, messages showing the case and the witness's folders, absent names, inputs and dependencies:
- `an_update_witnesses_its_replaced_folder_and_reuses_the_index`: install Foo, then a witnessed update: one `Replaced` folder `foo`, `cost().files_reused > 0`, `files_hashed == 0`.
- `a_forced_replace_of_an_unmanaged_folder_is_hashed`: `hand_made` folder, `install --force` witnessed: `Replaced`, `files_hashed > 0`.
- `a_remove_witnesses_the_removed_folder`; `an_adopt_witnesses_its_recorded_folders`; `a_pin_witnesses_no_folder`.
- `a_copy_witnesses_its_source_folders`: a second client dir as `CopyFrom`; its folder is `CopySource`; a missing source folder digests as absent.
- `a_first_install_lists_its_absent_names`: a client without `Interface/AddOns`: `absent` holds the folder key and `"Interface/AddOns"`.
- `the_marker_and_the_judge_identify_the_target`: unregistered: `marker == None`; after `testing::mark(..)`: `Some("sha256:…")`; `judge == target.judge`.
- `local_inputs_are_witnessed`: a `--file` zip (`zip`, its SHA-256), a `--file` directory (`dir`, its listing hash), and a cached reinstall (no input). The `git` kind is covered by a unit test of the location-to-input mapping with a `GitCheckout` location.
- `dependency_choices_are_witnessed`: a zip whose TOC requires a library present unmanaged (`unmanaged`), and one that requires a folder nothing provides (`unresolved`).
- `a_target_that_cannot_be_witnessed_fails_alone`: two targets, one with a `0o000` file inside a folder it replaces: that target has no work, one `PlanFailure` per change with `io`/`unindexable`, and a bare witness; the other is witnessed normally.
- `a_dry_run_without_a_scope_collects_nothing`: `witness: None`: `plan.witnesses` is empty.
- `collection_writes_nothing`: tree snapshots (`testing::tree_snapshot`) of `<state>` and the client dir equal before and after.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

None here: the token-level and adversarial suites through `plan::plan` are omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.6 and omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.7.

### Logging

Unit tests only: one name per case, assertion messages naming the case and printing the witness's public parts (`{:?}` of folders, absent, inputs, dependencies) and its cost.

## Considerations

- **Hot spots:** `src/engine/plan.rs` and `src/engine/tx.rs` (D1 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1` here, then D2 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2` and D8 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8`; G3, `omad-7ccp`, last): this subtask adds fields and one call at the end of each target's planning, nothing in the commit window. The `TxRequest` literals in `src/app/{update,sync,copy,pin,install,remove}.rs` and `adopt/apply.rs` are also C2's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.2`, the misplaced-client preflight) and D4's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`, the plan store): one added line each; rebase.
- **Cost:** none for any existing command (every site passes `None`). For the commands D2 and D3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.3`, `--if-match` on `pin`, `unpin` and `adopt`) bind, a dry run pays two stat walks per witnessed folder and a hash for each unindexed or changed file.
- **Why one witness per target, even a bare one:** the token pairs witnesses with targets; a missing one would make `observed` `null` for that target and weaken the binding silently.
- **Risk #19:** nothing collected here depends on time, process or path stamps; the private stamps never enter the token.

## Dependencies

Parent: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1 (`precondition::of_plan` and the approval witness for engine commands).

- **Before it:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.3 (`EntryDigest` and the folder witness): `collect` calls `witness::folder` for every folder.

comments.text:
**Done (part 4 of D1).** Commit `688a5cf`.

**What changed.**
- **`model::TargetRef`** `{Key(TargetKey), Provisional(String)}`.
  - The derived `Ord` puts keys first, ordered as `TargetKey` orders them.
  - `of(key, id)`, plus `parse(s)` (`Key` only when `s` is the key's canonical display).
  - `Display`, and `Serialize`/`Deserialize` as the plain string; `JsonSchema` is a string.
- **`engine::witness`:**
  - Types: `ApprovalWitness` (public parts, plus private `stamps` and `cost`), `InputWitness`, `InputKind` (`wire()`), `DependencyChoice`, `DependencyBy` (`wire()`, `detail()`), `WitnessScope`, `CopyFrom` and `WitnessCtx`.
  - `ApprovalWitness::new` sorts its lists. `stamp(dir)` is `pub(crate)` and `cost()` is public.
  - `collect(tp, ctx)`, `bare(target)`, and `pub(crate) input_of(location, blob_sha256, blobs_dir)`.
  - The module doc now covers the target witness.
- **`engine::plan`:**
  - `PlanRequest.witness: Option<WitnessScope>`, and `Plan.witnesses` (`#[serde(skip)]`).
  - `FolderWork.input`, set from `PendingBuild.input`, which `prepare_install` computes from the winning location. `AddonWork::input()` reads it.
  - Collection runs at the end of each target's iteration, after `tp.notes`. A target pushed early by a `live_inventory` failure gets `bare_witness`.
  - On a collection failure, `unwitnessed` empties that target and the target gets the bare witness.
  - Only `plan::plan` collects; `check_releases`, `rejudge` and the commit window never do.
- **`engine::tx`:** `TxRequest.witness`, copied into the `PlanRequest`.
- **`sources::local::listing_hash`** is now `pub(crate)`, because `…4.1.2` has not landed.
- **Request literals:** every one passes `witness: None`. That is 13 `TxRequest` literals (9 in `src/app`, the scene's, and 3 in `tests/`) and 4 `PlanRequest` literals (`tx::run` copies the request's own value). The compiler holds the count: a literal without the field does not build.
- **`engine::testing`:** `TxScene::request` (public, `run_as` uses it) and `TxScene::run_witnessed`.

**Decided while writing the bead, confirmed:**
- `TargetRef` lives in `src/model.rs`.
- Absent names are not `lstat`ed again.
- The `sync` file is not a witness input.
- `TxRequest.witness` is how the engine receives `PlanExtras`' plumbing.
- One witness per target, bare when nothing else can be collected.

**Decided while implementing:**
- **A collection failure clears more than the bead listed.** Besides work, ops, releases and changes (each change becomes a `PlanFailure` under its ref and addon with the error), it clears `dependencies`, resets `warnings` to `unchanged_warnings`, and sets `reload_required` to `None`, `kind` to `None` and `creates_addons_dir` to `false`. Otherwise a target that can commit nothing would still report its dependency installs and its `local_changes_replaced` warning.
- **The copy source's files index is only an optimisation.** If it is missing or unreadable, every source file is hashed; that is never a failure.
- **Marker kinds:** a symlink is `link:<target>`; a directory `kind:dir`; a FIFO, socket or device `kind:fifo`, `kind:socket` and so on; a file replaced while it was read `kind:changed`. An unreadable marker is `io`/`unindexable` for folder `Interface/.omaddons`, path `target.json`, as the bead says.
- **`bare(target)`** keeps the bead's signature and bounds the marker read by the default archive limits.
- **Duplicates:** identical inputs and repeated absent names are listed once.
- **`stamp()`** carries `#[expect(dead_code, reason = …)]` until D8 (`…4.8`) reads it under the commit lock. The `expect` makes the build fail once D8 uses it, so the attribute comes off then.

**Tests.**
- **`src/model.rs`:**
  - `target_refs_order_keys_first_and_as_keys_do`
  - `a_target_ref_is_its_plain_string`, including a lowercase ULID-like id that stays `Provisional`.
- **`src/engine/witness.rs`, 15 new tests over `TxScene`:**
  - `an_update_witnesses_its_replaced_folder_and_reuses_the_index`: the folder is adopted more than 20 ms after it was written, so its files are racy-clean (an install right before an update could be racy). It shows `Replaced foo`, files reused > 0, files hashed = 0, and `absent == ["fooextra"]`, so an update lists only the folders it adds.
  - `a_forced_replace_of_an_unmanaged_folder_is_hashed`: the digest equals `EntryDigest::of_dir`.
  - `a_remove_witnesses_the_removed_folder`, `an_adopt_witnesses_its_recorded_folders` and `a_pin_witnesses_no_folder`.
  - `a_copy_witnesses_its_source_folders`: a missing source folder digests as absent.
  - `a_first_install_lists_its_absent_names`: `["Interface/AddOns", "foo"]`.
  - `the_marker_and_the_judge_identify_the_target`: an unregistered target has `marker` `None` and a `Provisional` ref. After registration it is `sha256:` of the marker's bytes, the ref is `Key`, and `judge` is the target's.
  - `local_inputs_are_witnessed`: a `--file` zip (its SHA-256) and a `--file` directory (its listing hash).
  - `locations_map_to_their_inputs`: 8 location cases.
  - `dependency_choices_are_witnessed`: a scene run, a TOC requiring an unmanaged `LibFoo` and a missing `NoSuchLib`.
  - `dependency_choices_cover_every_kind`: all four kinds, the detail strings, and the sort order.
  - `a_target_that_cannot_be_witnessed_fails_alone`
  - `a_dry_run_without_a_scope_collects_nothing`
  - `collection_writes_nothing`: `tree_snapshot` of `<state>` and the client dir are equal before and after.

**Acceptance cases proven by mapping tests instead of scene runs:**
- **A cached reinstall, a download and a `git` checkout giving no input or a `git` input** are proven by `locations_map_to_their_inputs`. `TxScene`'s `--file` zips never enter the blob cache, and the scene has neither network nor git.
- **The `install` dependency choice** is proven by `dependency_choices_cover_every_kind`. The scene has no catalog or network to install a dependency through; the unmanaged and unresolved choices come from a real scene run.

**The bead's fail-alone case** (two targets): the retail target's update must replace `Foo`, which holds a mode-000 file the index does not know. The result:
- that target keeps no work or changes, and has one failure (`addon: Foo`, `io`, `details.reason: unindexable`);
- its witness is bare, with the marker present;
- the second target (`other`, provisional) is witnessed with `absent == ["bar"]` and has no failures.

**Mutation check** (tried locally, not committed): dropping `tp.work.clear()` from `unwitnessed` fails `a_target_that_cannot_be_witnessed_fails_alone`.

**Behaviour unchanged with `None`:** `cargo test --lib` passes (1,383, 4 ignored), as do `tests/plan.rs` (51), `engine_multi_target` (4), `deps` (13) and `undo_history` (22), all unmodified apart from the one added field line.

**Evidence.**

- `ubs` on the 18 changed Rust files: 0 critical. Its first pass flagged three test comparisons (`w.cost()…`, `f.target == "retail"`, `f.target != "other"`) as secret comparisons. They were restructured with a `let` binding and `matches!`, as elsewhere in the codebase.
