title: `of_plan`, `PlanExtras` and deferred-release keys, with `Precondition.targets` over `TargetRef`
description:
Part 5 of 7 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1 (`precondition::of_plan` and the approval witness for engine commands). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

D1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1`) builds the precondition token every engine-backed command carries in M4 (M4-D19): `--dry-run` will return it as `data.precondition` (D2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2`, and D3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.3`, thread it), `--if-match <token>` will refuse with `plan_stale` when the bound run's own token differs, and stored plans (D4, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`) embed it. M3 (M3-D46) gave tokens to five commands; `of_remove` is the one computed from an engine `Plan`, and it skips unregistered targets. This subtask writes **`of_plan`**, the generalization for `install`, `update`, `pin`, `unpin`, `adopt`, `sync` and `copy`: the token's four parts from the plan the command will execute, its per-target approval witnesses (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.4), the build id (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.1) and the command's app-level extras. It also lets `Precondition.targets` hold an unregistered target's provisional id, fixes `of_remove` the same way, and keys deferred releases (Tukui) without the URL they resolve only on a fresh download. It is its own step because the canonical form is one coherent, pinned format in one file (`src/app/precondition.rs`, D1 first among its six leaves), built on the witness types the previous subtasks made.

**The token's parts** (M4-D19, M4-D60): `command` (the path); `targets` (each target's key, or its provisional id while unregistered, with its record generation); `selection` (per target, canonically ordered: the folder ops; each change `{addon, ref, kind, fields, from_version, to_version, folders{added, replaced, removed, skipped, recorded}}`; each release `{release_id, url, expected_hash, blob_sha256}`, a deferred one keyed `{source, key, release_id, expected_hash, blob_sha256}` without its URL; `creates_addons_dir`); `observed` (per target, the witness's canonical digest: marker, folders, absent names, inputs, dependency choices, judge, in that order, the private stamps excluded; globally `build_id`, not `tool_version`; `copy`'s source key and generation, `sync`'s desired-file SHA-256 and `update`'s skip decisions from the extras). Text a human reads is excluded. *Rejected:* binding by generations alone (misses release drift, copy's source and hand edits), and hashing the whole dry-run `data` (human text and volatile fields would stale tokens for no reason).

**Facts this subtask relies on** (verified at `c0ab5e9`):
- `Precondition` (`src/app/precondition.rs:66-75`) holds `command`, `targets: Vec<(TargetKey, Option<u64>)>` (`:72`; the plan cites `:73`), `selection` and `observed` as `serde_json::Value`s; `canonical()` sorts and dedups targets and renders each as `{"key", "generation"}` or `{"key"}` (`:105-129`); `field()` is the first 64 bits of the SHA-256 in hex (`:131-138`); the encoder sorts object keys (`:140-170`). **Correction:** the plan writes the new type `Vec<(TargetRef, u64)>`, but `of_dismiss` and `of_prune` bind keys only (`None` generations, `:419-448`, `:582-607`), so the `Option` stays.
- `of_remove` (`:245-276`) skips a target with no key (`:248-251`), sorts ops and changes by `Value::to_string`, and has `observed: null`. The pinned M3 fixture is `a_fixture_token_never_drifts` (`:634-646`), and `every_covered_input_moves_its_own_field` (`:679-737`) is M3's covered-input table, the pattern this subtask's table follows.
- `PlannedRelease` (`src/engine/plan.rs:672-680`) has no notion of deferral; it is built at `:3876-3881`, where `winner.candidate.asset.location` is known (`AssetLocation::Deferred { source, key }` at `:3868-3871`). Its `url` for a deferred asset is `winner.canonical_url`: the canonical URL after a fresh download, `None` after a blob-cache hit (`:4834-4852` versus `:4855-4861`).
- `Change` (`:616-629`), `FolderSummary` (`:643-654`), `PlannedOp` (`:656-670`), `SkippedFolder` (serialized as `name` plus its flattened reason, `src/engine/inspect.rs:946-950`), `EditField::wire` (`src/engine/edit.rs:85-97`), `ExpectedHash` (`{"sha256": …}` or `{"md5": …}`, `src/model.rs:1253-1262`) and `SourceId` (snake_case, `src/sources/mod.rs:82-96`) all have stable serialized forms.
- `app::outcome::SkipReason` (`src/app/outcome.rs:131`) is the wire enum of update's skips. There is no `AddonName` or `Sha256` type: the plan's sketch means `String`s (an addon's record name; lowercase hex).
- `BINDING_COMMANDS` (`:25-31`) and its test `the_binding_commands_are_the_five_of_m3_d46` (`:848-864`) stay unchanged here.

## Technical Approach

### 1. `PlanExtras`, the re-export, and the build id

```rust
pub use crate::model::TargetRef;                     // as the plan names it: precondition::TargetRef

/// What a command decided above the engine, which its token covers too.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct PlanExtras<'a> {
    /// `copy`: --from's key and record generation.
    pub copy_source: Option<(TargetKey, u64)>,
    /// `sync`: lowercase hex SHA-256 of the desired-state file's bytes.
    pub desired_sha256: Option<String>,
    /// `update`: what it chose not to touch, as (target, addon name, why).
    pub update_skips: &'a [(TargetRef, String, SkipReason)],
}
```

`of_plan` reads `crate::build_info::BUILD_ID` (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.1).

### 2. `of_plan`

```rust
pub fn of_plan(command: &'static str, plan: &Plan, witnesses: &[ApprovalWitness], extras: &PlanExtras<'_>) -> Precondition {
    of_plan_at(crate::build_info::BUILD_ID, command, plan, witnesses, extras)
}
fn of_plan_at(build_id: &str, command: &'static str, plan: &Plan, witnesses: &[ApprovalWitness],
              extras: &PlanExtras<'_>) -> Precondition
```

For each `tp` in `plan.targets`, `let r = TargetRef::of(tp.key, &tp.target)`:

- **`targets`:** `(r, Some(tp.generation))`.
- **`selection`:** `selection[r.to_string()] = {"ops", "changes", "releases", "creates_addons_dir"}`:
  - `ops`: each `PlannedOp` as `{"op": <wire>, "folder": <as spelled>, "addon": <name>}`, sorted by (folder key, op wire, addon);
  - `changes`: each `Change` as `{"addon", "ref": <ref string>, "kind": <wire>, "fields": [<EditField wire>, sorted; [] when none], "from_version", "to_version", "folders": {"added", "replaced", "removed", "recorded": [<as spelled>, sorted by key], "skipped": [<SkippedFolder as serialized>, sorted by name key]}}`, sorted by (addon ASCII-lowercase, addon, ref);
  - `releases`: each `PlannedRelease` sorted by `release_id` (ties by canonical text): `{"release_id", "url", "expected_hash", "blob_sha256"}`, or, when `deferred` is `Some(DeferredAsset { source, key })`, `{"release_id", "source": <SourceId wire>, "key", "expected_hash", "blob_sha256"}` with no `url`;
  - `creates_addons_dir`: the bool.
- **`observed`:** one object for the whole token:

  ```json
  {"build_id":"<16 hex>","copy_source":{"key":"01JB…","generation":4},"desired_sha256":"<64 hex>",
   "update_skips":[{"target":"01JB…","addon":"DBM-Core","reason":"pinned"}],
   "witnesses":{"01JB8Q2V9W0000000000000000":"<64 hex>","retail@steam":null}}
  ```

  `copy_source` is `null` without one, `desired_sha256` `null`, `update_skips` `[]` (sorted by target string, addon, reason wire); every key is always present, so every engine command's `observed` has one shape. `witnesses[r]` is `witness_digest(w)` of the witness whose `target == r` (paired by ref, not by position), or `null` when none matches (collection was off; only commands that bind turn it on: D2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2`, and D3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.3`).
- **`witness_digest(w) -> String`:** the lowercase hex SHA-256 (64 digits, untruncated) of the canonical JSON of the positional array

  ```json
  [<marker or null>,
   [{"role":"replaced","key":"foo","digest":"entry:sha256:<hex>"}, …],
   ["foo","Interface/AddOns"],
   [{"kind":"zip","source":"<path>","digest":"<hex>"}, …],
   [{"requester":"Foo","folder":"libstub","by":"install","detail":"LibStub"}, …],
   "<judge hex>"]
  ```

  in M4-D60's order (marker, folders, absent, inputs, dependency choices, judge), each list already sorted by the witness. Its private stamps and cost never enter it.

`local_changes` (the reviewed draft's choice) is not in the token; `LocalChanges` stays a display sample for the `local_changes_replaced` warning.

### 3. `Precondition.targets` over `TargetRef`

- `targets: Vec<(TargetRef, Option<u64>)>`; `Precondition::new` takes that; `canonical()` sorts with `TargetRef`'s order and renders `{"key": r.to_string(), "generation": g}` or `{"key": r.to_string()}` exactly as before.
- `of_undo`, `of_dismiss`, `of_restore`, `of_restore_addons` and `of_prune` wrap their keys as `TargetRef::Key(k)`; nothing else in them changes, and their tokens are byte-identical.
- `pub fn parts(&self) -> [String; 4]`: the four canonical JSON texts in token order (what `canonical()` gives), for test logs now and the stored `precondition.parts` of D4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`, the plan store) later.

### 4. `of_remove` covers unregistered targets

**Order of work:** first add `of_remove_keeps_its_m3_token` against the unchanged code (a `Plan` with one registered target, one remove op and one change), run it, and pin the token it gives; then change `of_remove`. The test must pass before and after.

- A target with no key is included as `(TargetRef::Provisional(tp.target.clone()), Some(tp.generation))`, its selection entry keyed by the provisional id; registered targets are rendered exactly as before (ops and changes sorted by `Value::to_string`, `observed: null`).
- `remove`'s binding (`RemoveBinding`) is otherwise unchanged.

### 5. Deferred releases (`src/engine/plan.rs`)

- `PlannedRelease` gains `#[serde(skip)] pub deferred: Option<DeferredAsset>`; `#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)] pub struct DeferredAsset { pub source: SourceId, pub key: String }`.
- Set at `:3876-3881`: `deferred: match &winner.candidate.asset.location { AssetLocation::Deferred { source, key } => Some(DeferredAsset { source: *source, key: key.clone() }), _ => None }`.
- *Decided while writing this bead:* not serialized, because `Plan` is not a wire shape and this leaf owns no stored-plan format; D4 may expose it when it stores releases.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `of_plan_fixture_token_never_drifts` pins the token of a fixed plan (two targets, one registered and one provisional; ops, changes with every folder list, a direct and a deferred release, `creates_addons_dir`), fixed witnesses, fixed extras and build id `0123456789abcdef`; its failure message prints the four canonical parts.
- [ ] `a_fixture_token_never_drifts` (M3) passes unchanged, and `of_remove_keeps_its_m3_token`, pinned against the unchanged code, passes after the change; every M3 binding test in `tests/` passes unchanged.
- [ ] `every_covered_input_moves_its_own_part` has one named row per input of the leaf's list and each gives `plan_stale` with exactly the expected `details.changed`, `retryable: false` and the dry run as `fix_argv`.
- [ ] `benign_differences_leave_the_token_equal` holds for every row (warnings, notes, `created_at`, `plan_id`, argv, actor, the planning tx, any reordering, a witness's stamps and cost, a deferred release's URL present or absent).
- [ ] `remove`'s token covers an unregistered target; a registering target moves `targets`, `selection` and `observed`; a missing witness is `null` in `observed.witnesses`.
- [ ] `BINDING_COMMANDS` and `the_binding_commands_are_the_five_of_m3_d46` are unchanged.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

In `src/app/precondition.rs` (`#[cfg(test)]`), with builders `plan_with(targets)`, `tp(key_or_id, generation)`, `op(..)`, `change(..)`, `release(..)`, `deferred(..)`, `witness(..)` (through `ApprovalWitness::new`) and `extras(..)`; every row named; messages print the row, both tokens and `parts()` of each.

- `of_plan_fixture_token_never_drifts` (pinned at the first green run; record how to recompute it: the four `parts()` texts piped through `sha256sum`, first 16 hex digits each, as M3's fixture comment explains).
- `of_remove_keeps_its_m3_token` (pinned before the change).
- `every_covered_input_moves_its_own_part`, rows and expected `changed`:

  | Row | Changed |
  |---|---|
  | `generation 7 -> 8` | `targets` |
  | `an op added` / `an op's kind` | `selection` |
  | `a release id` / `an expected hash` / `a blob digest` / `a direct release's url` | `selection` |
  | `a deferred release's source key` | `selection` |
  | `a change's to_version` / `a change's replaced folders` / `a change's fields` | `selection` |
  | `creates_addons_dir` | `selection` |
  | `the judge digest` / `the marker` | `observed` |
  | `a replaced folder's digest` (stands for a hand edit in any file: a clean one, the eleventh, a same-size edit; an added symlink or empty directory) / `a removed folder's digest` | `observed` |
  | `an absent name added` / `an input digest` (zip, dir, git rows) / `a dependency choice` | `observed` |
  | `the build id` | `observed` |
  | `copy's source generation` / `a copy-source folder's digest` | `observed` |
  | `sync's file bytes` (`desired_sha256`) / `an adopted folder's digest` / `update's skips` (a reason changed; an entry added) | `observed` |
  | `the command` | `command` |
  | `a target registering` (provisional id to key, marker appearing) | `targets`, `selection`, `observed` |
- `benign_differences_leave_the_token_equal`, rows: `warnings text`, `notes`, `created_at`, `plan_id`, `argv`, `actor`, `generations map`, `targets reordered`, `ops, changes, releases and skips shuffled`, `witness stamps and cost`, `a deferred release with and without its url`.
- `a_deferred_release_is_keyed_without_its_url`: the parts text of a deferred release has `source` and `key` and no `url`.
- `remove_covers_an_unregistered_target`: a plan whose only target is provisional gives a `targets` entry keyed by the id.
- `a_missing_witness_is_null`: no witness for a target gives `"witnesses":{"<ref>":null}`.
- `observed_always_has_one_shape`: with default extras, the observed text has all five keys.
- In `src/engine/plan.rs`: `a_deferred_location_marks_its_release` (a `Deferred` winner sets `deferred`, a `Url` one does not).

### Integration and end-to-end tests

None here; omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.6 proves equal tokens across real plans and sources, and omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.7 the adversarial matrix.

### Logging

Unit tests only. Every token comparison's failure message prints both tokens and the four `parts()` texts of each, so a drifting part is visible without a debugger.

## Considerations

- **Hot spot `src/app/precondition.rs` (D1 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1`, D2 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2`, D3 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.3`, D8 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8`, E6 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`, E7 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7`): D1 first.** D2 adds `PlanBinding` and `check_noop` here next; keep `of_plan` free of binding logic.
- **Risk #6, tokens too sensitive** (a rules edit or a new build stales previews): intended; `details.changed` says `observed`.
- **Risk #19, a token stales for no reason:** the benign-differences table is the guard; any new field added to `selection` or `observed` later must earn a row there.
- **A canonical form that drifts breaks every confirmation:** the two pinned M3 tests and the new pinned fixture must never be re-pinned to make a change pass; a change that moves them is a contract change for H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, the pre-freeze audit) to see.
- **Compatibility:** M3 tokens are byte-identical within a build; tokens never survive builds (`build_id`).

## Dependencies

Parent: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1 (`precondition::of_plan` and the approval witness for engine commands).

- **Before it:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.1 (`build_info::BUILD_ID`) and omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.4 (`TargetRef`, `ApprovalWitness`, `Plan.witnesses`).

**Done (part 5 of D1).** Commit `dfdcef3`. Files: `src/app/precondition.rs`, `src/engine/plan.rs` and `src/engine/witness.rs`.

**What changed.**
- **`precondition::TargetRef`** re-exports `model::TargetRef`.
- **`PlanExtras<'a>`** (`copy_source`, `desired_sha256`, `update_skips`; `Default`).
- **`of_plan(command, plan, witnesses, extras)`** reads `build_info::BUILD_ID` and delegates to `of_plan_at(build_id, …)`. The token's parts are as the bead specifies:
  - `targets`: each target's `TargetRef` with `Some(generation)`.
  - `selection`, keyed by the target's string:
    - `ops`, sorted by (folder key, op wire, addon);
    - `changes`, sorted by (addon lowercase, addon, ref), each with `fields` as sorted wires, and the folder lists as spelled, sorted by key; `skipped` as serialized, sorted by name key;

    - `creates_addons_dir`.
  - `observed`: `{build_id, copy_source, desired_sha256, update_skips, witnesses}`, every key always present. `update_skips` is sorted by (target, addon, reason wire). `witnesses` maps each target to its digest, paired by target, or `null`.
- **`witness_digest(w)`**: the full 64-hex SHA-256 of the canonical positional array `[marker, folders{role,key,digest}, absent, inputs{kind,source,digest}, dependencies{requester,folder,by,detail}, judge]`. Stamps and cost never enter it.
- **`Precondition.targets: Vec<(TargetRef, Option<u64>)>`**, keeping the `Option` per the bead's correction, and `new` takes that. `canonical()` sorts with `TargetRef`'s order and renders as before.

- **`of_undo`, `of_dismiss`, `of_restore`, `of_restore_addons` and `of_prune`** wrap their keys as `TargetRef::Key`; nothing else in them changed.

title: Tests: equal tokens across dry runs and per source, and the `--file <dir>` id end to end
description:
Part 6 of 7 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1 (`precondition::of_plan` and the approval witness for engine commands). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

D1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1`) builds the token of every engine-backed command: `of_plan` over the plan the command will execute, with a per-target approval witness, the build id and the command's extras (M4-D19, M4-D60). A token that differs between two previews of an unchanged world is worse than none: every bound run would be `plan_stale`, and an agent would loop between preview and refusal (risk #19, "a token stales for no reason", which the review found twice: Tukui's deferred URL, present after a download and absent after a cache hit, and `--file <dir>`'s fresh ULID). Checkpoint criterion 6 states the requirement this subtask proves: "Two dry runs of an unchanged home give equal tokens for every source, including when the second one is served from the blob cache."

This subtask adds the integration suites that prove it through real planning over replayed HTTP fixtures, plus the end-to-end rows for `install --file <dir>` through the binary. It is its own step because it needs every implementation subtask (the id from omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.2, the token from omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.5) and the test log of T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs and the `argc e2e` runner), and it adds the shared planning builder that omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.7 reuses. No command emits an `of_plan` token yet (D2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2`, threads `data.precondition`), so the token rows run at library level, calling `omaddons::engine::plan::plan` and `omaddons::app::precondition::of_plan` directly, exactly as `tests/plan.rs` already drives planning.

**Facts this subtask relies on** (verified at `c0ab5e9`):
- `tests/plan.rs`'s `support::Env` (`tests/plan.rs:43-150`) builds a retail and a Forever target, a replay scenario and a `PlanCtx`, but with `ReleaseCache::transient` (`:115`), which keeps no memo, so a second plan cannot hit the blob cache through remembered facts. A command does: `install` runs the engine with a `ReleaseCache::new(..)` and then `cache.remember(&facts)` (`src/app/install.rs:613-618`). A blob is found on the second run by its expected SHA-256, or by the hash a remembered fact gives (`src/engine/plan.rs:4839-4852`).
- Fixture builders exist per source: GitHub (`tests/common/http.rs`: `gh_release`, `gh_latest`, `gh_feed`, `fixture_seq`), WoWInterface (`tests/common/wowi.rs`: `wowi_filelist`, `wowi_details`, `wowi_file`), Tukui (`tests/common/tukui.rs`: `tukui_list`, `tukui_addon`, `tukui_download`), the recorded `git:` scenario for a GitHub-hosted repository on a 3.3.5a custom root (`tests/git_github.rs`, `tests/fixtures/http/git-github/`), and the recorded WowAce scenario (`tests/sources_wowace.rs`). `common::netlog::read_net_log` reads `net.log` lines with their `purpose` (`asset` for every download, `wowace-file` for a WowAce tree's files).
- `tests/install.rs` and `common::home::Home` drive the real binary on a synthetic home; `TestEnv` sets every `HOME`/`XDG_*`, `TZ=UTC` and `OMADDONS_FS_CLONE=no` (`tests/common/env.rs`).

## Technical Approach

### 1. `tests/common/planning.rs` (new shared builder)

Modeled on `tests/plan.rs`'s `support::Env`, which stays as it is:

```rust
pub struct PlanningHome { pub env: TestEnv, pub retail: Target, pub other: Target, pub paths: Paths, pub scenario: PathBuf, /* scopes, running */ }
impl PlanningHome {
    pub fn new() -> Self;
    /// Registers `target` (record at generation 3) with `addons`, writes their live folders and a files
    /// index from `index_live_folder`, stamped `recorded_at_ns` (default: well after every file's ctime).
    pub fn manage(&self, target: &mut Target, addons: &[ManagedAddon<'_>]);
    /// A hand-made (unmanaged) folder in `target`'s AddOns.
    pub fn hand_made(&self, target: &Target, folder: &str, files: &[(&str, &str)]);
    /// `plan::plan` as a command runs it: a persistent `ReleaseCache::new(.., freshness, "install", Actor::Agent)`,
    /// a fresh `TxId` per call, `witness: Some(scope)`, then `cache.remember(&plan.facts)`.
    pub fn plan(&self, requests: Vec<TargetRequest>, opts: &PlanOpts) -> Plan;
    pub fn token(&self, command: &'static str, plan: &Plan, extras: &PlanExtras<'_>) -> Precondition;  // of_plan
    pub fn net_log(&self) -> Vec<NetLine>;                                                               // read_net_log
}
pub struct PlanOpts { pub force: bool, pub freshness: Freshness, pub registry: SourceRegistry, pub scope: WitnessScope, pub limits: ArchiveLimits }
```

### 2. `tests/plan.rs`: equal tokens, per source, and the directory id

Each test is a `TestLog` scenario (`let log = tlog!();`, from `tests/common/tlog.rs` of T1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`).

- **`two_dry_runs_of_an_unchanged_home_give_equal_tokens`.** Retail managed with `Foo` at v1 (live and indexed) and a hand-made `Bar` folder; fixtures: `Foo` v2 and `gh:o/bar` (whose archive ships `Bar`). Requests: update `Foo`, and install `gh:o/bar` with `force` (replacing the unmanaged `Bar`). Steps: `log.tree("state", ..)` and `log.tree("client", ..)`; plan three times (each with a fresh planning tx and clock); after each, `log.json("parts", token.parts())` and `log.json("witness", ..)` (folders with roles and digests, absent, inputs, cost). Assert: the three tokens are equal; each witness has `Replaced` folders `foo` (reused from the index: `files_reused > 0`) and `bar` (hashed); `log.assert_unchanged` for `state` and `client` after the plans (planning wrote only cache).
- **`a_cache_hit_equals_a_download_github`, `_git`, `_wowi`, `_tukui`, `_wowace`.** One test per source, the same steps: a fresh home and that source's fixtures; plan an install dry run (`Freshness::Revalidate`, as `install` uses); `log.json("net.log added", ..)`: at least one download line (`purpose: "asset"`, or `wowace-file` for WowAce); plan again with a new `ReleaseCache` over the same paths (the memo and blob cache from disk); `log.json("net.log added", ..)`: no download line; the two tokens are equal (print both `parts()` on failure). For Tukui also assert that the first plan's release has `url: Some(..)` and the second's `url: None`, the very case the deferred keying fixes. The `git` row uses the recorded GitHub-hosted repository on its 3.3.5a custom root; the WowAce row the recorded tree.
  - If a source cannot serve its second plan from the blob cache at all, that is a defect in the source, not in this suite: file it `discovered-from` this bead and block this subtask on it.
- **`a_file_directory_plans_with_one_release_id`.** A folder `Mine/` (with `Mine.toc`) outside AddOns; plan `install gh:o/mine --file <dir>` twice: the release ids are equal and start `gh:o/mine@listing:`, the tokens are equal, and the witness's `inputs` holds one `dir` input with the same digest; edit `Mine.toc` and plan again: the id differs and the token differs in `selection` and `observed` (`precondition::check(Some(&t0), &p1, ..)`'s `details.changed == ["selection", "observed"]`).

### 3. `tests/install.rs`: `--file <dir>` through the binary

**`an_unchanged_file_directory_installs_once`**, a `TestLog` scenario on a `common::home::Home` with a registered retail target and a folder `Mine/` outside AddOns:

1. `log.run(&env, ["omaddons", "install", "gh:o/mine", "--file", <dir>, "-t", "retail", "--json"])`: exit 0, the item `installed`; the record's `release_id` starts `gh:o/mine@listing:` (`log.json("record", ..)`).
2. `log.tree("addons", <client dir>/Interface/AddOns)`, then the same install again: exit 0, the item `unchanged`; `log.assert_unchanged("addons", ..)`.
3. Edit `Mine/Mine.toc` (size changes) and install again: the item `updated`.
4. The same with `--reinstall`: the item reinstalled (its status as `install --reinstall` reports a reinstall today).
5. `log.run(.., ["omaddons", "update", "-t", "retail", "--dry-run", "--json"])`: the addon is `skipped` with `skip_reason: "static"`, and the `net.log` lines the step recorded are none (nothing upstream was asked; `common::netlog::read_net_log` agrees).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `tests/common/planning.rs` exists and `tests/plan.rs`'s existing tests pass unchanged.
- [ ] `two_dry_runs_of_an_unchanged_home_give_equal_tokens` passes: three equal tokens, a reused managed folder and a hashed unmanaged one, `<state>` and the client dir unchanged.
- [ ] The five `a_cache_hit_equals_a_download_*` rows pass: a download on the first plan, none on the second, equal tokens; Tukui's URL is present then absent.
- [ ] `a_file_directory_plans_with_one_release_id` passes: one `@listing:` id for an unchanged folder, a different one after an edit, with `details.changed == ["selection", "observed"]`.
- [ ] `an_unchanged_file_directory_installs_once` passes through the binary: installed, unchanged, updated after an edit, reinstalled with `--reinstall`, and skipped as `static` by `update --dry-run` with no `net.log` line.
- [ ] Every scenario writes its `TestLog` (`steps.jsonl`, `transcript.md`); a failing comparison prints both tokens' `parts()`.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

None new (this subtask is the integration suites).

### Integration and end-to-end tests

As in the Technical Approach: `tests/plan.rs` (`two_dry_runs_of_an_unchanged_home_give_equal_tokens`, `a_cache_hit_equals_a_download_github`, `a_cache_hit_equals_a_download_git`, `a_cache_hit_equals_a_download_wowi`, `a_cache_hit_equals_a_download_tukui`, `a_cache_hit_equals_a_download_wowace`, `a_file_directory_plans_with_one_release_id`) and `tests/install.rs` (`an_unchanged_file_directory_installs_once`). Run them with `argc e2e plan` and `argc e2e install` for verbose logs.

### Logging

Every scenario uses `tlog!()`:
- `log.step` per phase: `seed home`, `first plan`, `second plan`, (`third plan`), `compare`;
- `log.json("parts", token.parts())` per plan, and `log.json("witness", ..)` with each target's folders (role, key, digest), absent names, inputs, dependency choices and `cost()`;
- `log.json("net.log added", ..)` with the lines each plan added (`purpose`, host, path, status);
- `log.tree("state", ..)`, `log.tree("client", ..)` and `log.assert_unchanged` around the plans;
- `log.run` for each binary invocation in `tests/install.rs` (argv, exit, envelope, stderr events, `net.log` lines).

A failing token comparison names the step, prints both tokens and the first differing part, and points at the transcript.

## Considerations

- **Fixtures are replayed, never live:** no row makes a real request; `net.log` assertions read the replayed requests.
- **A cache hit depends on remembered facts** for sources without a published SHA-256 (GitHub without `release.json` digests, WoWInterface's MD5, Tukui, WowAce): the builder must remember facts after each plan, as `install` does, or the second plan downloads again and the row proves nothing.
- **Unsettled folders right after seeding** (within the 20 ms racy slack) are simply hashed instead of reused; tokens are content, so equality holds either way; the reuse assertion in the first scenario seeds the index with a `recorded_at_ns` well after the files' ctimes.
- **Hot spots:** `tests/plan.rs` and `tests/install.rs` are shared with D2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2`) and D7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.7`, release drift end to end) later; add new tests at the end of each file.

- **After it:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.7 (the adversarial matrix) reuses `tests/common/planning.rs`.

title: Tests: the approval witness's adversarial matrix (the design gate)
description:
Part 7 of 7 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1 (`precondition::of_plan` and the approval witness for engine commands). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

D1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1`) adds a binding rule: what an engine-command token covers, and the approval witness it digests (M4-D19, M4-D60). Common rule 14 makes D1 a design-gate leaf: a protocol change lands with its own adversarial matrix, and **D1's design gate is passed only when this subtask is closed.** D1 adds no journal shape, no recovery rule, no write and no failpoint, so its matrix is not a crash matrix; it is the evidence under attack: edits that try to slip past the witness (same-size edits, restored mtimes, the eleventh file the warning never names, symlinks and empty directories that a file-only digest would miss), changes that must not stale a preview (a `touch`, a `chmod`, another process's clock and transaction id), entries the witness must never open or follow (a FIFO, a symlink to `/`, a loop), inputs that must fail closed (unreadable files, folders past the bounds), and repeated collection.

M4-D60's guarantee, which this matrix holds the evidence to: "every change to a witnessed resource that happens before the under-lock check is caught", whoever made it. This subtask proves the half D1 owns: that each such change moves the token a bound run's own planning computes. D8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8`, the approval checked again under the commit lock) proves the under-lock half with the same witness, and D2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2`) and D3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.3`) the command-level `plan_stale` refusals with tree hashes. The moving-folder case (a folder edited while it is being hashed) is covered deterministically by omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.3's unit test, through its `between` seam; no failpoint is added for it (the plan keeps `engine::tx::FAILPOINTS` unchanged).

**Facts this subtask relies on:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.6's `tests/common/planning.rs` (`PlanningHome`, `manage`, `hand_made`, `plan` with a `WitnessScope` and `ArchiveLimits`, `token`, `net_log`); `precondition::check(Some(&token), &actual, &preview)` returns `plan_stale` whose `details.changed` names the differing parts in token order (`src/app/precondition.rs:187-225`); `Precondition::parts()` gives the canonical texts (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.5); `ApprovalWitness::cost()` and its public parts (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.4); existing tests create unreadable files with mode `0o000` without a root check (`tests/remove.rs:373`, `tests/copy.rs:527`).

## Technical Approach

`tests/witness.rs` (new), one table-driven matrix. Each row is `{name, home: fn(&PlanningHome) -> Requests, mutate: fn(&PlanningHome), expect}` with `expect` one of `Moves(&[parts])`, `Equal`, or `Fails { code, reason }`. For each row, on a fresh home: plan (witnesses on) and keep the token `t0` and the witnesses; apply `mutate`; plan again; then compare `check(Some(&t0), &p1, &preview)` with `expect` (for `Fails`, the second plan's target has no work and a `PlanFailure` per change with that code and `details.reason`, while every other target plans and witnesses normally). Rows that touch a FIFO or a symlink run each plan on a thread joined with a 10 s timeout, failing the row on a hang.

**The base homes:** `managed` (retail manages `Foo` at v1, eleven files, live and indexed with `recorded_at_ns` well after their ctimes; the request updates it to v2, so `Foo` is `Replaced` and reused from the index), `unmanaged` (a hand-made `Bar`, replaced by `install gh:o/bar` with `force`), `fresh` (a first install into a client without `Interface/AddOns`), `copy` (a `CopyFrom` of the other client's `Foo`), `adopt` (an adoption of a hand-made folder).

|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `clean_file_edited` | managed | `Foo/Foo.lua` rewritten with other bytes | `Moves([observed])` |
| 2 | `same_size_edit` | managed | one byte flipped, size kept | `Moves([observed])` |
| 3 | `same_size_edit_with_mtime_restored` | managed | one byte flipped, `set_modified` back to the indexed mtime | `Moves([observed])` (the ctime rule) |
| 4 | `the_eleventh_changed_file` | managed with ten files already edited before the first plan | the eleventh edited | `Moves([observed])` (the warning still names ten) |
| 5 | `file_deleted` | managed | `Foo/libs/lib.lua` removed | `Moves([observed])` |
| 6 | `file_replaced_by_other_bytes` | managed | another file renamed over it | `Moves([observed])` |
| 7 | `file_replaced_by_identical_bytes` | managed | an identical copy renamed over it (new inode) | `Equal` (content, not identity) |
| 8 | `symlink_added` | managed | `Foo/link -> Foo.toc` | `Moves([observed])` |
| 9 | `empty_directory_added` | managed | `Foo/empty/` | `Moves([observed])` |
| 10 | `empty_file_added` | managed | `Foo/empty.lua` | `Moves([observed])` |
| 11 | `touch_only` | managed | every file's mtime moved, no byte changed | `Equal` |
| 12 | `chmod_only` | managed | `Foo/Foo.toc` to `0600` | `Equal` |
| 13 | `unmanaged_file_edited` | unmanaged | `Bar/Bar.lua` edited | `Moves([observed])` |
| 14 | `unmanaged_touch_only` | unmanaged | `touch` | `Equal` |
| 15 | `a_created_name_appears` | managed, plus `install gh:o/baz` (a new folder `Baz`) | a hand-made `Baz/` created | `Moves([selection, observed])` (the add becomes a refusal; `baz` leaves `absent`) |
| 16 | `the_addons_directory_appears` | fresh | `Interface/AddOns` created empty | `Moves([selection, observed])` (`creates_addons_dir` and `absent`) |
| 17 | `copy_source_edited_record_unchanged` | copy | the source client's `Foo/Foo.lua` edited, its record untouched | `Moves([observed])` |

| 20 | `target_registered_between_plans` | an unregistered target with a hand-made folder replaced by `--force` | the target registered (record, registry entry, marker) | `Moves([targets, selection, observed])` |
| 21 | `another_process_and_clock` | managed | none (the second plan draws its own tx id and time) | `Equal` |
| 22 | `unrelated_folder_edited` | managed | an unmanaged `Other/` the plan does not touch edited | `Equal` |
| 23 | `saved_variables_edited` | managed | `WTF/Account/FAKEACCT/SavedVariables/Foo.lua` written | `Equal` (the witness never reads `WTF/`) |
| 24 | `unreadable_file_fails_closed` | unmanaged plus a second target with an update | `Bar/secret.lua` set to `0o000` | `Fails { io, "unindexable" }` for that target; the other target's witness digest and selection entry unchanged |
| 25 | `entry_limit_fails_closed` | unmanaged, `limits.max_entries: 4` | `Bar/` given 8 entries | `Fails { archive_too_large, "limit_exceeded" }` |
| 26 | `byte_limit_fails_closed_reused_bytes_free` | managed and unmanaged on retail, `limits.max_uncompressed: 64`, `Bar`'s files 32 bytes in all and `Foo`'s reused files over 64 | `Bar/big.lua` of 128 bytes added | first plan succeeds (reused bytes do not count); second `Fails { archive_too_large, "limit_exceeded" }` on retail |
| 27 | `fifo_is_never_opened` | unmanaged with a FIFO `Bar/pipe` before the first plan | none | `Equal`, both plans finish within the timeout |
| 28 | `fifo_replaced_by_a_file` | as 27 | the FIFO replaced by a regular file | `Moves([observed])` |
| 29 | `symlink_to_root_is_never_followed` | unmanaged with `Bar/escape -> /` | none | `Equal`, finishes, `cost().files_hashed` counts only `Bar`'s own files |

| 31 | `non_utf8_name_renamed` | unmanaged with a file named `b"\xff.lua"` | renamed to `b"\xfe.lua"` | `Moves([observed])` |

Two more scenarios outside the table:
- **`repeated_collection_agrees`:** on the `managed` and `unmanaged` homes, after waiting 50 ms (past `RACY_SLACK_NS`) so every folder is settled, three plans give equal tokens, every witnessed folder of the third keeps a private stamp (`ApprovalWitness::stamp(dir)` is `Some`), and `cost().files_reused` is the same each time.
- **`collection_writes_nothing`:** for rows 1, 13, 24, 25 and 27, `log.tree` of `<state>` and of each client dir before the second plan and `log.assert_unchanged` after it: the witness and every fail-closed path write nothing outside the cache.

Privacy: row 23 plants `FAKEACCT`/`FakeRealm`/`FakeChar` names (the house's synthetic names); nothing in this suite renders output, so `assert_private_all` is not needed, but the row asserts that no witnessed path contains `WTF`.

**Closing this subtask passes the design gate of D1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1`).** The closing agent records in D1's close comment that the gate passed, with the matrix's row count and the log root (`<CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR>/test-logs/witness/`). A row that cannot be made to pass is a design defect: fix it in the subtask that owns the code (reopen it), never by changing a row's expectation without recording why in the close comment.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every row of the matrix passes with its stated expectation, each a named case in `tests/witness.rs`.
- [ ] `repeated_collection_agrees` passes: three equal tokens, private stamps on every settled witnessed folder, the same reuse counts.
- [ ] `collection_writes_nothing` passes for its rows: `<state>` and every client dir unchanged.
- [ ] No row hangs: the FIFO and symlink rows finish within their timeout.
- [ ] Every row writes its `TestLog`; a failing row prints both tokens' `parts()`, the witness's folders and cost, and the transcript path.
- [ ] The close comment of D1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1`) records that the design gate passed, with the row count and the log root.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

None new; the moving-folder, unsettled-stamp, racy-edge and open-helper cases are omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.3's unit tests, and this suite does not repeat them.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

`tests/witness.rs` as above: the 31-row matrix, `repeated_collection_agrees` and `collection_writes_nothing`. `argc e2e witness` runs it with verbose logs.

### Logging

One test per row (a small `macro_rules!` turns each table row into its own `#[test] fn <row>()`), each with its own `tlog!()`, so a failure names its row in `cargo test`'s output and has its own transcript. Per row: `log.step("first plan")`, `log.json("parts", t0.parts())`, `log.json("witness", ..)` (each target's folders with role, key and digest, absent names, inputs, dependency choices, `cost()`), `log.step("mutate")` with `log.note` describing the change and `log.json("stamp", ..)` of the mutated entry before and after (`lstat`'s size, mtime, ctime, inode), `log.step("second plan")` with the same records, then `log.step("compare")` with `log.json("changed", ..)`. Fail-closed rows log the failure's code, message and `details`. Rows that touch the filesystem outside the mutation take `log.tree` before and `log.assert_unchanged` after.

## Considerations

- **Why a table:** every adversarial idea is one row, so a new one (found in review or in the work of D8, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8`) is one line, and a regression names the exact kind of edit that slipped through.
- **Timing:** settledness never decides an expectation here (tokens are content), except in `repeated_collection_agrees`, which waits out the slack explicitly before planning.
- **Running as root:** `0o000` does not stop root; like the existing `0o000` tests, this suite assumes a normal user (the gate runs as one).
- **What this matrix does not cover, and who does:** the bound run's refusal and its unchanged tree (D2 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2`, D3 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.3`); edits after the bound run's first check and before its lock, and a folder replaced at the last moment (D8, with E13's predicates, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.13`); crash safety (D1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1`, writes nothing; the engine's crash matrices are unchanged).

## Dependencies

Parent: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1 (`precondition::of_plan` and the approval witness for engine commands).

- **Before it:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1.6 (its `tests/common/planning.rs` builder, and through it every implementation subtask); and T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs), whose `TestLog` it uses (an edge added at filing).
- **After it:** none inside D1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1`); closing it passes D1's design gate. The agent that closes the last open subtask of D1 verifies D1's acceptance criteria and closes D1.

title: E2E: the apply forms of plan retention scenarios
description:
## Background

Plan retention (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.6, M4-D26) pins the archives referenced by unexpired saved plans and sweeps expired plans after commits. Its first seven scenarios exercise real typed commands bound with --if-match. The apply command is not implemented when that work starts, so this task records the three apply-specific proofs required by scenario 8. Implement them after omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5 lands. Read the M4 common rules in omad-bxb1.

## Technical Approach

Extend tests/e2e_plan_retention.rs and reuse its Home, release, blob and saved-plan helpers. Every binary invocation, including setup and fresh previews, goes through TestLog with explicit --json and --progress json. Keep every scenario in a fresh synthetic home and check privacy on both channels after commit steps.

1. apply_uses_a_pinned_archive_after_an_eviction: install GitHub fixture A v1 on retail, publish fixture A v2, and preview its update with a one-byte blob cap. Record the saved plan id, token and v2 blob hash. Plant an unpinned blob, commit fixture B on era, and prove eviction removed the planted blob while keeping A v1, A v2 and B archives. Run apply with the saved id; expect success with the update committed and no additional asset-purpose net.log entry. Release revalidation probes may occur. Assert the old A v1 archive can subsequently be evicted.
2. apply_hashes_a_local_zip_again: preview a local Foo archive with stored core.lua bytes -- a. Replace its archive with equal-length stored bytes -- b and restore the original modification time. Prove length and mtime match and SHA-256 differs. Apply the original plan; expect exit 1, plan_stale, selection among details.changed, and unchanged AddOns tree and history. Re-preview the edited archive, apply the new plan successfully, and assert the installed core.lua contains -- b. An mtime-only touch with identical bytes must still apply.
3. A deleted local input: preview a valid local archive, remove it, and apply its new plan id. Expect exit 1, plan_stale, details.reason input_missing, details.path identifying the synthetic archive, and unchanged AddOns and history. Restore the archive, preview again, and apply successfully.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] All three apply scenarios above pass through the real binary, without live network.
- [ ] Pinned application adds no asset download; edited or missing input changes no client or history; restored inputs apply after a fresh preview.
- [ ] Every command and phase is recorded by TestLog; logs include blob hashes/sizes, plan ids, input hashes/mtimes, network asset counts and tree checks.
- [ ] argc e2e plan_retention passes with complete verbose logs; argc gate and changed-file UBS pass; br lint is clean.
- [ ] Record any changed wire names in the close reason, or state that tests add none; commit code and synced beads together on main.

## Test Plan

No new unit test or production feature is required. Add the three named real-binary scenarios to tests/e2e_plan_retention.rs, using recorded HTTP fixtures and synthetic retail/era clients. Verify the same-size and restored-mtime preconditions explicitly before asserting staleness. Count only asset-purpose network entries when proving cache reuse. Compare history length and AddOns trees around every refusal.

## Considerations

The pin saves a download; losing a cached blob remains recoverable through verified re-download. Do not weaken apply's source revalidation or token binding to make the scenarios pass. Use the apply output shape that D5 actually ships, and record any difference from the older scenario text. No scenario needs WTF fixtures; privacy assertions still cover commit output. All repo edits remain manual, with filesystem mutations in production routed through fsx.
acceptance_criteria: All three real-binary apply scenarios pass; pinned application adds no asset download; edited and missing local inputs leave AddOns and history unchanged; restored inputs succeed after re-preview; TestLog captures every run; verbose E2E, gate, UBS and bead lint pass.

title: `--if-match` on `install`, `update`, `sync` and `copy`
description:
## How to work this bead

This bead is worked through its 7 subtasks, listed below in work order. Claim a subtask, not this bead (`br ready --parent omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2` lists the ready ones). The agent that closes the last open subtask then verifies every acceptance criterion of this bead (they are the leaf's, not any one subtask's), and closes this bead with `br close omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2 --reason "done: <evidence> · found: <ids>"`. Until this bead is closed, every bead it blocks stays blocked.

1. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2.1 `PlanBinding`, the bound dry-run check and the no-op token check: the engine-side binding every bound command uses, `tx.rs:404`'s dry-run skip dropped, `check_noop`, and `remove`'s dry run kept exactly as M3 shipped it.
2. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2.2 `install` binds to its preview: `InstallData.precondition`, witnesses on for dry and bound runs, the probe left unbound, the registry rows and contract rows.
3. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2.3 `update` and `sync` bind, with update's skip decisions and sync's file digest: `TargetsData.precondition`, both no-op paths checked, and the per-target refusal that keeps `plan_stale`'s contract.
4. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2.4 `copy` binds, with its source's generation and folders: `copy_source`, the `CopyFrom` witness scope, its no-op path checked.
5. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2.5 Tests: the four commands' binding scenarios, end to end (`tests/preconditions.rs`).

## Background

`omaddons install`, `update`, `sync` and `copy` are the release-bearing commands: they fetch releases, download archives and replace folders. At `c0ab5e9` their `--dry-run` returns no token and `--if-match` on them is a usage error, so an agent or a confirm dialog that previews one of them has no way to say "do exactly what I just saw, or nothing". Between the preview and the run, three things can make the preview untrue: another omaddons command commits on the same client, a person or another program edits a folder the run will replace, and a newer release appears upstream. Today each run simply plans again and commits whatever it now finds. M3 built the binding mechanism (`--if-match`, `pc1:` tokens, `plan_stale`) for five destructive commands; D1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1`, `precondition::of_plan` and the approval witness) builds the token of an engine command from its plan and an approval witness of everything the plan reads, replaces or removes. This leaf puts that token behind the four release-bearing commands, on every path they can take: the engine path, the bound dry run, and the paths that find nothing to do and never reach the engine. D3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.3`, `--if-match` on `pin`, `unpin` and `adopt`) does the same for the records-only commands on top of this leaf's `PlanBinding` and `check_noop`.

It serves:
- **G-M4-3, what was previewed is what runs, target by target:** "every command that changes addons can be previewed with `--dry-run` and then run bound to that preview, by token (`--if-match`) or by stored plan; the guarantee is per target: on each target the bound run commits exactly the operations the preview approved, or none of them; the approval covers what the preview saw, not only the record generations." This leaf delivers the token half for four of the seven commands; D4 and D5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`, `omaddons apply`) build the stored-plan half on it.
- **G-M4-6, no new risk to the engine's guarantees:** "dry runs still leave `<state>` untouched, and the global lock is still held only for commit windows." A bound dry run compares its token and writes nothing under `<state>`, and the binding adds no work under the lock beyond M3's generation check (D8 adds the under-lock witness check).
- **G-M4-1, self-describing:** the token is in every dry run's JSON (`data.precondition`), so an agent needs no extra call to bind.
- **Vision G4, agent ergonomics ("the first command an agent guesses works"):** `--dry-run` then `--if-match <data.precondition>` now works on every command that changes addons, not only the destructive ones, and the thesis that omaddons stays the sole, safe, undoable authority over what it manages extends to "and it never commits something you did not approve".

**Checkpoint criterion 6** ("previews bind on every addon-changing command, target by target"), for `install`, `update`, `sync` and `copy`:
- `--dry-run` returns a `precondition` token, and `--if-match <token>` commits, on each target, exactly that preview's operations or none of them;
- a change in between gives `plan_stale` and changes nothing on that target: another install on an affected client; a hand edit in a file of a folder the plan replaces (the full witness matrix of clean files, the eleventh file, same-size edits and replaced files is D1's unit rows plus D8's scenarios; this leaf proves the pre-lock case end to end); a name the plan creates appearing; an edited `sync` file; a copy source whose folders changed while its record did not;
- it holds on every path: a bound run that finds nothing left to do, and a bound dry run, also check the token;
- the M3 binding of `remove`, `undo`, `backup restore`, `backup prune` and `errors dismiss` is unchanged.
The under-lock half ("an edit made after the bound run's first check, before its lock, is `plan_stale` too; the re-judged operations must equal the approved ones") is D8's, and "two dry runs of an unchanged home give equal tokens for every source" is D1's; this leaf re-asserts the latter per command as a regression row.

**The decisions that shape it** (the full decision log is also on the milestone epic `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`):
- **M4-D19: every command that changes addons binds with `--if-match`, using a token computed from the engine's plan.** The token has four parts, each the first 64 bits of a SHA-256 of canonical JSON: `command`; `targets` (each target's key, or its provisional id while unregistered, with its record generation); `selection` (per target: the folder ops, each change, each release keyed by `{release_id, url, expected_hash, blob_sha256}` or, for a deferred asset such as Tukui, by `{source, key, release_id, expected_hash, blob_sha256}` without the URL it resolves only on a fresh download, and `creates_addons_dir`); `observed` (each target's judge digest and approval witness, the binary's `build_id`, and the command's extras: `copy`'s source key and generation, `sync`'s desired-file SHA-256, `update`'s skip decisions). Every such command's `--dry-run` data gains `precondition`; real runs carry `null`. The token is checked through the existing `Binding::plan` seam before anything is staged, and again under the lock (generations here; the witness and the operations in D8). The engine stops skipping the check in dry runs (`tx.rs:404`), and each command's no-op path, which never reaches the engine, checks the token itself. `BINDING_COMMANDS` grows. *Why:* "what a human approved is exactly what runs" was true only for destructive commands; `Binding` already runs after planning and before staging, so binding the engine commands needs no engine refactor. *Rejected:* (i) binding by target generation alone, which misses release drift, copy's source and every hand edit that leaves the record alone; (ii) hashing the whole dry-run `data`, which holds human text and volatile fields, so tokens would change for no reason. It extends M3-D46 from five commands to twelve (this leaf adds four, D3 three).
- **M4-D20: both races bind; a typed bound run keeps its command's freshness.** A concurrent change (another command, the game, a hand edit) and release drift (a newer release between preview and run) both make a preview untrue. A typed `--if-match` run uses its command's normal freshness rules: `install` and `copy` already revalidate their sources (`Freshness::Revalidate`), so a newer release changes `selection` and the run is `plan_stale`; `update` and `sync` answer from the 15-minute release memo, so inside that window a typed bound run does exactly what the preview showed even if a newer release exists. `apply` (D5) always revalidates. *Why:* a typed `--if-match` is an agent asserting "do what I just saw", and doing exactly that is correct; `apply` is the moment of approval, where a user should see a newer release before it installs. *Rejected:* (i) revalidating on every `--if-match` run (as costly as an unbound install for no gain); (ii) installing the old release at `apply` though a newer one exists. Do not add revalidation to bound `update`/`sync` runs: the acceptance tests pin the memo behaviour.
- **M4-D60: every engine-command token carries an approval witness.** The witness is evidence, not a warning: per target, the entry digest of every live folder a replace or remove will move (managed or not, edited or clean: each regular file's path, size and SHA-256, each symlink's target, each directory), every name the plan creates (absent), the client marker's digest, the local inputs, the dependency choices and the judge digest. Clean files take their digests from the files index behind a racy-clean stamp check, so a clean file costs a `stat`. D1 collects it; this leaf turns collection on for the runs that need it and compares it before staging; D8 compares it again under the lock. *Rejected:* generations only (misses every non-omaddons writer); `LocalChanges` as evidence (a ten-path warning sample with no digest).
- **M4-D61: the guarantee is per target.** Multi-target runs keep one transaction per target (M1, comment 269), so a late conflict on one target can leave a partial run. A typed `--if-match` run reports each target through `TargetsData`'s per-target results (committed, unchanged, stale or failed, with its transaction id or error code), and nothing calls such a run atomic. (The plan lease and `apply`'s `outcomes[]` are D5's.)
- **M4-D55: known pre-release inconsistencies are fixed by the leaf that owns the surface.** The plan names one for this leaf: `errors dismiss`'s `precondition` presence (null versus omitted). At `c0ab5e9` it is already fixed (see the facts below); this leaf confirms it with a presence-rule test over every binding path and records the confirmation, with no wire change.
- **M3-D46 (context):** a mismatch is `plan_stale` from `PlanStaleSource::Apply`: not retryable (the same token can only fail again), `details.changed` naming the parts that differ, and `fix_argv` the same command with `--dry-run` in place of `--if-match <token>`. Without `--if-match` nothing changes: binding is opt-in.
- **M4-D22 (context):** all four commands are storable; D4 stores their plans and reuses this leaf's token unchanged.

## Technical Approach

The work is described here as one design; each subtask restates the part it builds.

### 1. `PlanBinding`: the binding of an engine command (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2.1)

In `src/app/precondition.rs`, beside `RemoveBinding`:

```rust
/// An engine command's run bound to its preview's token (M4-D19): its own plan's token,
/// witnesses and extras included, must be the preview's before anything is staged, and
/// its targets' generations must not have moved under the lock. D8 adds the under-lock
/// witness and operation checks to this type.
pub struct PlanBinding<'a> {
    command: &'static str,
    expected: Option<String>,      // --if-match; None computes nothing and checks nothing
    extras: PlanExtras<'a>,
    preview: Vec<String>,          // preview_argv(ctx.argv): the fix of every refusal
}
impl<'a> PlanBinding<'a> {
    pub fn new(command: &'static str, expected: Option<String>, extras: PlanExtras<'a>,
               preview: Vec<String>) -> Self;
    /// This run's binding: `Some` exactly when `--if-match` was given, dry run or not.
    pub fn of_run(ctx: &Context, command: &'static str, extras: PlanExtras<'a>) -> Option<Self>;
}
impl Binding for PlanBinding<'_> {
    fn plan(&self, plan: &Plan) -> Result<()>;   // None: Ok; else check(expected, of_plan(command, plan, &plan.witnesses, extras), preview)
    fn undo(&self, _: &EngineUndo) -> Result<()>; // Ok(()): engine commands never undo
    fn moved(&self, _target: &str) -> Error;      // stale(command, &[Part::Targets], preview)
}
/// A dry run's token: `of_plan` over the plan it ran, its witnesses and the extras.
pub fn plan_token(command: &'static str, plan: &Plan, extras: &PlanExtras<'_>) -> String;
/// Whether this run collects witnesses: a dry run, or a bound run.
pub fn witnessing(ctx: &Context) -> Option<WitnessScope>;
```

- `plan()` returns `Ok(())` without computing anything when `expected` is `None`, so the type is usable by D5 (`apply`, which sets the stored token) and by any caller that wants the binding without a token.
- `moved()` is M3's refusal for a commit that landed between planning and the lock: `plan_stale`, `PlanStaleSource::Apply` (not retryable), `details.changed: ["targets"]`, fix the preview argv.
- *Decided while writing this bead:* a command passes a `PlanBinding` only when `--if-match` is given. An unbound dry run computes its token afterwards from `TxOutcomes.plan` with `plan_token`, which equals what the binding would have computed (same plan, same witnesses, same extras). This keeps unbound runs on today's code path and matches D1's statement that "a dry run computes its token from `TxOutcomes.plan`".
- *Decided while writing this bead:* witnesses are collected on dry runs and on bound real runs, never on unbound real runs (`witnessing(ctx)` is `Some(WitnessScope::default())` exactly when `ctx.dry_run || ctx.if_match.is_some()`). An unbound real run would compute evidence nobody compares, and D1 states the same rule. Forgetting to turn it on for a bound real run would make every bound run stale (its `observed.witnesses` would be `null` where the preview's held digests), which the end-to-end tests catch.

### 2. Bound dry runs check, and `remove` keeps M3's dry run (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2.1)

- `src/engine/tx.rs:403-406` becomes `Some(binding) => binding.plan(&plan).map(|()| plan)`, with the comment "a bound run, dry or not, stages nothing and reports nothing unless it planned what the preview showed". So `install … --dry-run --if-match <token>` compares: a matching token returns the same preview and the same token (exit 0); a different one is `plan_stale` (exit 1). Either way the dry run writes nothing under `<state>` and takes no global lock, as every dry run.
- **`remove` keeps its M3 behaviour.** It builds its `RemoveBinding` only on a real run: `ctx.if_match.clone().filter(|_| !ctx.dry_run)` at `src/app/remove.rs:247-253`. *Decided while writing this bead:* the plan says to drop the condition in the engine, which is right for the commands this leaf binds, but `remove` passes its binding on dry runs too, so dropping it alone would turn `remove --dry-run --if-match <stale>` from "previews afresh" (M3's tested behaviour, README's documented rule) into `plan_stale`, against criterion 6's "the M3 binding of `remove` … is unchanged". `undo`, `backup restore`, `backup prune` and `errors dismiss` do not go through `tx::run`'s plan seam and are not affected. D5 decides how `apply --dry-run` reports a stale stored plan of an M3 command; this leaf changes nothing there.
- The rule after this leaf, as README states it (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2.7): on `install`, `update`, `sync` and `copy` (and, after D3, `pin`, `unpin`, `adopt`) a bound dry run compares; on M3's five it previews afresh and returns the current token.

### 3. The no-op paths: `check_noop` (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2.1, called by omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2.3 and omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2.4)

A bound run that finds nothing left to do must still compare its token, so that the loser of two concurrent typed runs that planned after the winner committed is `plan_stale` rather than a quiet "unchanged" (the loser that planned before is stopped under the lock by `moved()`).

```rust
// src/app/precondition.rs
/// One in-scope target of a run that found nothing to change.
pub struct Idle<'a> { pub target: &'a Target, pub generation: u64 }
/// The token of a run that changes nothing on `targets`: `of_plan` over an idle plan of
/// those targets, each with its bare witness (marker and judge), plus the extras.
pub fn of_noop(command: &'static str, targets: &[Idle<'_>], extras: &PlanExtras<'_>) -> Result<Precondition>;
/// The no-op path's check, one line at each call site: `Ok(None)` for an unbound real run
/// (nothing computed, nothing read); otherwise the token is computed, checked against
/// `--if-match` when given (`plan_stale` as `check` makes it), and returned for a dry
/// run's `data.precondition`.
pub fn check_noop(ctx: &Context, command: &'static str, targets: &[Idle<'_>], extras: &PlanExtras<'_>) -> Result<Option<String>>;

// src/engine/plan.rs, beside `Plan::has_ops`
/// The plan of a run that changes nothing on `targets` (each with the generation it was
/// judged at): one empty `TargetPlan` per target, no ops, changes, releases or failures.
pub fn idle(targets: &[(&Target, u64)], argv: &[String], actor: Actor) -> Plan;
```

- `of_noop` builds `Plan::idle`, witnesses each target with D1's `witness::bare(target)` (an unreadable marker fails closed with D1's `io` error), and calls `of_plan`. Using `of_plan` itself guarantees the no-op token has exactly the canonical form of an engine token, so a preview that had work and a bound run that has none differ in `selection` (and the reverse).
- The call sites, placed **before** `recover_waiting` so that a stale bound no-op run changes nothing at all, not even a recovery (a matching one then recovers as an unbound run does):
  - `update` (`update.rs:312-314`): every selected target (`world.select_many`, sorted by id), each with its record's generation (0 without a record), extras `{update_skips}`.
  - `sync` (`sync.rs:673-675`): every selected target the file has a section for (`has_section`, the targets `target_work` ran for), extras `{desired_sha256}`. The no-op path still builds no `Engine` and makes no request.
  - `copy` (`copy.rs:288-289`): `--to`, with its record's generation, extras `{copy_source}`.
  - `install` needs none: its no-op ("already installed") goes through the engine, whose binding check runs before its own no-op branch.
- *Decided while writing this bead:* "its in-scope targets" (the plan's phrase) is every selected target for `update`, the selected targets with a section for `sync`, and `--to` for `copy`, because each of these is a client the preview said "nothing to do" about; a change on any of them may make that untrue. This is more sensitive than the engine path's token (which covers only targets with work), which errs on the safe side.

### 4. Each command's run, with witnesses and the binding (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2.2, omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2.3, omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2.4)

```text
install weakauras -t retail --if-match pc1:…
  CLI: install is in BINDING_COMMANDS; the token is well formed (else usage, before anything)
  plan (no lock; witnesses on; install revalidates): fetch · download · witness::collect per target
  PlanBinding::plan: of_plan(install, plan, plan.witnesses, extras) == token?
        no → plan_stale (not retryable, details.changed, fix: the same command with --dry-run)
        (a --dry-run --if-match stops after this check: the same preview and token; writes nothing in <state>)
  stage (no lock)
  lock (per target): recover · register · generation == plan's?  no → PlanBinding::moved → plan_stale (targets)
        re-judge as today (D8 adds the witness and operation checks here)
        journal · swap · record · history · committed
update -t retail --if-match pc1:…        (nothing has an update)
  statuses from the memo · skip decisions → update_skips
  no changes: check_noop(update, [retail @ gen], {update_skips}) == token?  no → plan_stale
  then recover_waiting, exactly as an unbound run
```

- `TxRequest.witness = precondition::witnessing(ctx)` on the run the token describes (copy: with its `CopyFrom`, §6).
- **`install`'s probe stays unbound and unwitnessed** (`witness: None`, plain `engine.run`): it is a planning aid that chooses the client, its plan is not the one the token describes, and binding it would compare the wrong plan. Only the final run (`install.rs:613`) uses `engine.run_bound(&req, Some(&cache), binding)`. *Decided while writing this bead* (the plan does not mention the probe). If the world changed so that the probe now chooses another client, the bound run's `targets` differ and it is stale, which is correct.
- The dry run's token: `ctx.dry_run.then(|| plan_token(command, &done.plan, &extras))` on the engine path, `check_noop`'s return on the no-op path.
- A multi-target bound run (`update` or `sync` over several clients) keeps one transaction per target (M4-D61). The before-staging check covers the whole plan, so a mismatch anywhere refuses the whole run before anything is staged. Under the lock, a target whose generation moved is refused by `moved()`; the engine records that target's failure and goes on (`tx.rs:429-468`), so the run can end `partial`: `targets[].tx` set for the committed ones, `targets[].error.code: "plan_stale"` for the stale one, no tx and no error for an unchanged one. *Decided while writing this bead:* these existing keys express M4-D61's "committed, unchanged, stale or failed" for typed runs, so no new key is added (§8.1 rule 1); `apply`'s `outcomes[]` is D5's.

### 5. `data.precondition` (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2.2, omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2.3)

- `InstallData.precondition: Option<String>`, after `creates_addons_dir` and before the `-v`-only `client_dir`; `TargetsData.precondition: Option<String>`, last. Both always present (A3's rule 2: `null`, never omitted), a token under `--dry-run`, `null` on real runs. Doc comment: "`--dry-run`: the token `--if-match` takes to bind the real run to this preview (M4-D19); `null` on a real run."
- `TargetsData::build` and `TargetsData::assemble` set `None`; `TargetsData::with_precondition(self, Option<String>) -> Self` sets it. `pin`, `unpin` and `adopt` therefore carry `"precondition": null` on every run until D3 fills their dry runs (an additive key; D3 owns their tokens).

```json
{"dry_run":true,"target":{"id":"retail","key":"01JB8Q2V…"},"tx":null,"kind":"install",
 "items":[{"request":"weakauras","status":"installed","to_version":"5.22.1","…":"…"}],
 "reload_required":"reload","atomic_swap":null,"creates_addons_dir":false,
 "precondition":"pc1:3f9a0c1e5b7d2a46…"}
{"dry_run":true,"run":null,"targets":[{"target":{"id":"retail","key":"01JB8Q2V…"},"tx":null,"…":"…"}],
 "summary":{"…":"…"},"precondition":"pc1:9b1c…"}
```

A stale bound run:

```json
{"ok":false,"command":"update","exit_code":1,"error":{"code":"plan_stale",
 "message":"this update is no longer what its preview showed (targets changed); nothing was changed: preview it again",
 "fix":"omaddons update -t retail --dry-run","fix_argv":["omaddons","update","-t","retail","--dry-run"],
 "alternatives":[],"retryable":false,"details":{"changed":["targets"]}}}
```

(The message and fix are `precondition::stale`'s, unchanged from M3. On the all-failed path of the `TargetsData` commands, `details` also carries the existing `items` list.)

### 6. The app-level extras (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2.3, omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2.4)

- **`update`: `update_skips`.** Every addon `update` decided to skip before the engine (each `skipped(s, reason)` push: `pinned`, `ahead`, `blocked`, `static`, `unchecked`), as `(TargetRef::of(key, id), addon name, reason)`; `of_plan` sorts them. So a skip that changes stales the token even when the engine's selection does not move (an addon `unchecked` at preview and known `current` at the run). Failed and unchanged items are not skips; failures turned into `blocked` skips after the engine (`settle_failures`) are not app-level decisions and are not included.
- **`sync`: `desired_sha256`.** Lowercase hex SHA-256 of the exact bytes `read` returned (`sync.rs:620`), computed once, before parsing. A comment added to the file changes only `observed`; an added entry changes `selection` and `observed`. The engine never reads `addons.toml`, so this is an extra, not a witness input (D1's decision).
- **`copy`: `copy_source` and `CopyFrom`.** `copy_source = from.target.key.map(|k| (k, source.map_or(0, |r| r.generation)))`: `--from`'s key and its record's generation; `None` when `--from` is unregistered (it then manages nothing, so copy plans nothing from it, and a registration in between changes `selection`). `TxRequest.witness = Some(WitnessScope { copy_from: Some(CopyFrom { target: from.target.clone(), folders }) })` on dry and bound runs, `folders` the union of `AddonRecord.folders` of every addon whose install `copy` requests (not the skipped ones), sorted by key and deduplicated. D1's `witness::collect` digests them with role `copy_source`, so a source edit that leaves the source's record alone stales the token (`observed`).

### 7. A per-target refusal keeps `plan_stale`'s contract (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2.3)

`TargetsData::all_failed` (`src/app/outcome.rs:595-622`) builds the command's error from the first failed item. When that item's target has a target-level `error` (the full `ErrorBody` the engine recorded for a whole-target failure) with the same code, the returned error takes that body's `retryable`, `message`, `fix` and `details`, and adds `details.items` as today; only item-level failures keep today's reconstruction. So a single-target bound `update`, `sync` or `copy` refused under the lock reports `plan_stale` with `retryable: false` and `details.changed: ["targets"]`, like the before-staging refusal. *Decided while writing this bead* (the plan does not see this path): without it, a bound refusal would read as retryable, and README's rule that a retryable `plan_stale` may be rerun would invite an agent to rerun the stale token's command. The item-level `ItemError` shape is not changed. Unbound target-level failures keep their own retryability (they were reconstructed with the code's default, which equals the engine's for `plan_stale` from re-planning); any snapshot whose `details` gains the target error's keys is reviewed and re-accepted, and the close comment lists it as a correction (M4-D55: a known inconsistency on a surface this leaf's binding owns).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `install`, `update`, `sync` and `copy` bind: each `--dry-run --json` returns `data.precondition` as a `pc1:` token, each real run carries `"precondition": null`, and `--if-match <token>` over an unchanged world commits exactly the previewed operations (the real run's items and versions equal the dry run's, and the AddOns tree equals the expected result).
- [ ] `BINDING_COMMANDS` is `remove, undo, backup restore, backup prune, errors dismiss, install, update, sync, copy`; `--if-match` on `backup create` is still `usage` with `fix_argv` `["omaddons","help","backup","create"]`; `CLI_PATHS[].binds` is true for the four and `tests/omarchy_widget.rs::cli_paths_mirror_the_registry` passes.
- [ ] Another omaddons command's commit on an affected client between the preview and the bound run gives `plan_stale`, `retryable: false`, `details.changed: ["targets"]` and `fix_argv` the `--dry-run` form, for each of the four; the same holds when the commit lands between the bound run's planning and its lock (pause at `engine.snapshot.prestaged`), through `PlanBinding::moved`.
- [ ] For `update` and `sync`, a newer release published after the preview, inside the 15-minute memo window, gives success with the previewed version and no new request to the release host; for `install` and `copy`, `plan_stale` with `details.changed: ["selection"]`; a bound `update --refresh` behaves like `install` (`selection`).
- [ ] A same-size edit of a file that was clean at preview, in a folder the plan replaces, made before the bound run starts, gives `plan_stale` with `details.changed: ["observed"]` for `install`, `update` and `sync`.
- [ ] A folder created by hand at a name a bound `install` would create gives `plan_stale` with `selection` among the changed parts, and the hand-made folder is untouched.
- [ ] A `copy` whose source changed gives `plan_stale` with `details.changed: ["observed"]`: a file edited in a copied source folder (the source's record unchanged), and separately a commit on `--from` of an addon the copy does not name.
- [ ] An edited `sync` file (a comment line added) gives `plan_stale` with `details.changed: ["observed"]`.
- [ ] A bound run with nothing left to do and a stale token gives `plan_stale`, never an unchanged success: `update`, `sync` and `copy` through `check_noop`, `install` through the engine; the second of two sequential bound runs holding one token is `plan_stale` and changes nothing.
- [ ] A bound dry run of each of the four compares: a matching token returns the same token and preview (exit 0), a stale one gives `plan_stale` (exit 1); both leave `<state>` byte-identical (`tests/contract/special.rs` extended) and take no global lock.
- [ ] Nothing changes on any stale run: the AddOns trees of every client, the target records, files indexes and `history.jsonl` hash identical before and after.
- [ ] A two-client bound `update` whose second client receives a commit while the run is paused before that client's lock ends `partial`: the first client committed (`targets[].tx` set), the second refused with `targets[].error.code: "plan_stale"`, `retryable: false`, `details.changed: ["targets"]`, its tree as the concurrent commit left it. A single-client bound `update`, `sync` or `copy` refused under the lock returns `plan_stale` with `retryable: false` and `details.changed: ["targets"]`.
