title: E2E: the binding's adversarial matrix (design gate)
description:
Part 6 of 7 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2 (`--if-match` on `install`, `update`, `sync` and `copy`). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

D2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2`) makes `install`, `update`, `sync` and `copy` bind to their previews: `--dry-run` returns `data.precondition`, a `pc1:` token over the executed plan, D1's approval witness (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1`) and the command's extras, and `--if-match <token>` makes the real run do exactly that on each client or nothing (`plan_stale`, not retryable, `details.changed`, fix the `--dry-run` form). The token is checked before anything is staged (`PlanBinding::plan`), again under the commit lock for a moved generation (`PlanBinding::moved`), in bound dry runs, and on every no-op path (`check_noop`, before any recovery).

D2 is a **design-gate leaf** (common rule 14): it changes a binding rule, so it closes only when its own adversarial matrix passes, and this subtask is that matrix. The leaf's design gate is passed only when this subtask is closed. The question the matrix answers is whether a bound run can ever commit something other than its preview, or leave a client half-changed, when the world moves at the worst moment: a concurrent commit at every pause point before the lock, a crash at every engine step after the check, an injected I/O error at the swap, two runs holding one token, a folder the run cannot read. D2 adds no failpoint and no journal shape of its own; its writes are the engine's, so the matrix runs the bound commands through the engine's existing failpoints (`engine::tx::FAILPOINTS`) and checks the binding's promises at each.

**The promises under test** (the decisions, restated):
- **M3-D46 / M4-D19:** a bound run commits exactly the previewed operations or nothing; a refusal is `plan_stale`, never retryable, with `details.changed`; nothing changes on a stale run; a bound run that finds nothing to do still compares.
- **M4-D61:** per client: a client is either wholly as before or wholly as previewed.
- **The engine's crash guarantee (M1, unchanged):** after a crash, the next lock-taking command recovers the journal, and every folder is wholly old or wholly new; recovery is idempotent.
- **This leaf's ordering rule:** a bound no-op run checks its token before it recovers anything, so a stale one changes nothing at all.
- **G-M4-6:** a bound dry run takes no global lock and writes nothing under `<state>` (bar `net.log`).

**Facts this subtask relies on** (verified at `c0ab5e9`):
- Failpoints are debug-only (`#![cfg(debug_assertions)]` suites, DEC-7). `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS=<name>[=abort|=error|=pause|=sleep:<ms>|=panic][@N]` (`src/fsx/failpoint.rs:1-130`): `abort` is `std::process::abort()` (a child killed by a signal reports exit code `-1` through `common::home::wait`, `tests/common/home.rs:208`); `error` makes `hit` return an I/O error; `pause` waits for `common::pause::Pause::resume`; `@N` fires on the Nth hit.
- `engine::tx::FAILPOINTS` (`src/engine/tx.rs:78-113`) lists 34 names. On a bound run, before the lock: `engine.plan.fetched` (`src/engine/plan.rs:1311`, after the records were read), `engine.plan.downloaded` (`:4902`, only when something downloads), `engine.plan.done` (`:1528`, after witness collection, before `PlanBinding::plan`), `engine.stage.begin`, `engine.stage.file`, `engine.stage.synced`, `engine.snapshot.prestaged` (`src/engine/tx.rs:1014`, once per client commit); under the lock: `engine.lock.acquired`, `engine.recovered`, `engine.registered`, `engine.revalidated`, `engine.journal.prepared`, `engine.addons_dir.created` (first install only), `engine.snapshot.sv`, `engine.snapshot.state`, `engine.swap.before_rename`, `engine.swap.after_exchange`, `engine.swapped`, `engine.record.written`, `engine.history.appended`, `engine.committed`; after: `engine.unlocked`, `engine.cleanup.done`, `engine.retention`.
- `tests/engine_crash.rs` is the engine's own crash matrix (every failpoint as a real abort; wholly old or wholly new afterwards; recovery by the next lock-taking command). Every lock acquisition for a mutation recovers all journals first (`recover_all`), whatever client the command changes.
- `common::engine::Scene` (V1: `Foo`, `FooOld`; V2: `Foo` grown, `FooOld` dropped: an update that replaces one folder and removes another), `Scene::journals()`, `Scene::folders()`, `Scene::generation()`, `Scene::lock_inode()`; `Home::new(&["wow", "wow_classic"])`; `Home::spawn`, `common::home::wait`; `common::pause::Pause`.
- T1's `TestLog` (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`): `tlog!()`, `log.step`, `log.note`, `log.json`, `log.run -> Ran`, `log.tree`, `log.assert_unchanged`.
- From D1: a replaced folder that cannot be read fails that client's witness collection with `io`, `details.reason: "unindexable"`, clearing the client's works (so a bound run's `selection` differs).

## Technical Approach

A new suite, `tests/preconditions_matrix.rs`, `#![cfg(debug_assertions)]`, marked end to end as T1's convention says (so `argc e2e` runs it verbosely), using `tests/common/binding.rs` (whichever of this subtask and omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2.5 lands first adds it: `preview`, `bound`, `preview_argv`, `assert_stale`, `assert_stale_with`, `guard`/`unchanged`, `state_without_net_log`, `two_clients_with_foo`). Every row runs on a fresh home. The commands and their shapes:
- `install`: Foo v2 over v1 from `--file` archives (replace one folder, remove one);
- `update`: Foo v1 installed from `gh:o/foo`, v2 published, the memo aged with `age_release_memo` so the preview sees v2 (`update Foo -t retail`);
- `sync`: an `addons.toml` that installs Foo;
- `copy`: Foo from classic to retail on a two-client home.

### M1. A concurrent commit at every pause point before the lock

`a_commit_at_each_pre_lock_pause_stales_the_bound_run`: for each command × each point in `[engine.plan.fetched, engine.plan.done, engine.stage.begin, engine.stage.synced, engine.snapshot.prestaged]` (plus `engine.plan.downloaded` for the runs that download):
1. preview T; `log.tree` of the client the run changes;
2. spawn the bound run with `<point>=pause`; `Pause::reached(<point>)` (a point the run never reaches fails the row with "<point> not reached");
3. commit on the same client from another process (`install` Bar, a ref outside the run's scope); `log.tree` of the client as `after-concurrent`;
4. resume and wait: exit 1, `plan_stale`, `retryable == false`, `details.changed == ["targets"]` (the records were read before every listed point, so the token check passes and `PlanBinding::moved` refuses under the lock; assert at least `targets` at `engine.plan.fetched` in case planning order changes);
5. the client equals `after-concurrent` (the bound run added nothing); `history.jsonl` gained exactly Bar's line; no journal remains.

### M2. A crash at every engine step after the check, recovery, and the re-run rule

`a_bound_run_crashed_after_its_check_recovers_whole`, for `install` and `update` (the add-and-remove shape and the replace-and-remove shape) at every failpoint from `engine.stage.begin` to `engine.committed` that the run reaches (and `engine.swap.before_rename=abort@N` for each N up to the number of journaled renames, as `tests/engine_crash.rs` does), plus one row each for `sync` and `copy` at `engine.swapped`, on a two-client home (the run on retail):
1. preview T; record `before` (retail's AddOns tree hash, its record view without `tx_id` and `installed_at` (`Scene::view`'s form), and its generation); compute `after` once per command on a second, identical home, by previewing and running the same command there without failpoints (a token never crosses homes: their target keys differ), and keep its AddOns tree hash and record view;
2. run the bound command with `<point>=abort` → exit `-1` (a row whose child exits normally fails with "<point> not reached");
3. recover with three lock-taking commands on **classic** in turn (`install` Bar, `pin` Bar, `unpin` Bar), each through `log.run`; after each: retail equals `before` or `after` exactly (tree hash and record), never a mix; after the first, no journal remains under `<state>/journal/`; the second and third change nothing on retail (repeated recovery is idempotent);
4. the re-run rule: the bound command again with T:
   - retail at `before` (rolled back; its generation unchanged) → exit 0, and retail equals `after`;
   - retail at `after` (rolled forward; generation + 1) → exit 1, `plan_stale`, `["targets"]`, retail unchanged.
   Never any third state.

### M3. An injected I/O error at the swap

`an_injected_io_error_at_the_swap_leaves_the_client_whole`, for `update` (and `install`) at `engine.swap.before_rename=error`, `engine.swap.after_exchange=error`, `engine.swapped=error` and `engine.record.written=error`: the bound run fails with the injected I/O error (exit 1, not `plan_stale`), retail is `before` or `after` exactly; if a journal remains, recover as in M2; then the re-run rule of M2 holds.

### M4. Two bound runs holding one token

- `two_concurrent_bound_runs_never_both_commit` (`update`): preview T; spawn A and B with the same bound argv, each with `engine.snapshot.prestaged=pause` and its own `Pause` directory; both reached; resume A → exit 0; resume B → exit 1, `plan_stale`, `["targets"]`; retail equals the single expected `after`; `history.jsonl` has exactly one update line.
- `a_bound_run_that_plans_after_the_winner_is_stale_not_unchanged` (`update`, `copy`): A runs to completion with T; B then runs with T → nothing left to do → exit 1, `plan_stale` with `targets` and `selection` among the parts (through `check_noop`), not exit 0.

### M5. A stale bound no-op run recovers nothing

`a_stale_bound_noop_run_recovers_nothing` (`update`): Foo current, Bar installed; preview `update Foo -t retail` (no-op token T); `pin` Bar (the generation moves: T is stale); crash an unbound `install Baz --file … -t retail` at `engine.swapped=abort` (a journal is left); `guard` and list the journals; bound `update Foo -t retail --if-match T` → exit 1, `plan_stale`; the journal is still there and every tree is unchanged (the check ran before `recover_waiting`); then an unbound lock-taking command recovers it as usual.

### M6. A folder the run cannot read

`an_unreadable_replaced_folder_stales_the_bound_run` (`update`): preview T; `chmod 000` on `Foo/core.lua`; bound run → exit 1, `plan_stale` with `selection` among the parts (D1's collection failure cleared the client's works); Foo unchanged; a fresh dry run reports the item failure `io` with `details.reason: "unindexable"`; restore the mode; the bound run with T now succeeds (the world is again as previewed). The row first checks it is not running as root (`rustix::process::geteuid().is_root()`); as root (where `chmod 000` does not deny reads) it prints `SKIP an_unreadable_replaced_folder_stales_the_bound_run: running as root` and fails unless `OMADDONS_ALLOW_SKIP` names it, per `tests/common/checkpoint.rs`.

### M7. A bound dry run holds no lock

`a_paused_bound_dry_run_holds_no_lock` (`install`): spawn `install … --dry-run --if-match T` with `engine.plan.done=pause`; while it is paused, an unbound `install Bar` on the same client completes within 10 seconds (it would wait for the global lock if the dry run held it, and time out with `locked`); resume; `<state>` (without `net.log`) is as the concurrent install left it: the dry run wrote nothing. Its own verdict is not asserted (it planned before the commit).

### README

The Development section's test-suite table gains `tests/preconditions_matrix.rs`: "the `--if-match` binding's adversarial matrix: concurrent commits at every pause before the lock, crashes at every engine step with repeated recovery, injected I/O errors, two runs holding one token".

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `tests/preconditions_matrix.rs` exists (debug builds only) and is run by `argc e2e`.
- [ ] M1 passes for all four commands at every listed pause point: `plan_stale` (`["targets"]`), not retryable, the client exactly as the concurrent commit left it.
- [ ] M2 passes for `install` and `update` at every reached engine failpoint (every journaled rename included) and for `sync` and `copy` at `engine.swapped`: after recovery, wholly before or wholly after; recovery repeated three times changes nothing more; the re-run with the original token commits exactly the preview from `before` and is `plan_stale` (`["targets"]`) from `after`.
- [ ] M3 passes: an injected I/O error at each swap failpoint leaves the client whole, and the re-run rule holds.
- [ ] M4 passes: two concurrent bound runs holding one token never both commit; the later sequential one is `plan_stale`, never "nothing to do".
- [ ] M5 passes: a stale bound no-op run leaves a pending journal and every tree untouched.
- [ ] M6 passes (or prints its quoted `SKIP` only where allowed): an unreadable replaced folder stales the bound run, and the token is valid again once the folder is readable.
- [ ] M7 passes: another command takes the lock and commits while a bound dry run is paused.
- [ ] Every row names any failpoint it never reached as a failure (no row passes vacuously).
- [ ] The Development table names the suite; the close comment of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2 records "design gate passed" with this suite's row count and runtime.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files; `br lint` is clean for this subtask.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

None: the matrix is end to end. The helpers it shares with omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2.5 are exercised by both suites.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

`tests/preconditions_matrix.rs`, rows M1–M7 as specified, each generated from a table (command × failpoint) so that adding an engine failpoint later only extends the table; the expected `after` state of each command is computed once per test by an unfailing preview and bound run on a second, identical home (tree hashes and record views compared, keys aside), never hard-coded.

### Logging

One `tlog!()` log per test; each table row is a `log.step("<command> × <failpoint>")`. Per row: `log.run` for the preview and every recovering or re-running command; the child (paused or crashed) spawned with `Home::spawn` and logged with `log.json("child", {argv, failpoints})`, a `log.note` for `reached <point>` and `resumed`, and `log.json("child envelope", …)` with its exit (`-1` for an abort); `log.tree` of retail's and classic's AddOns, `<state>/targets`, `<state>/journal` and `history.jsonl` before the run, after the crash, after each recovery and after the re-run; `log.assert_unchanged` wherever a tree must not move; `log.json("verdict", {state: "before"|"after", generation})` after recovery. A failure prints `test log: <path>` and the last 20 steps, so the row, the failpoint and the exact tree that differed are in the transcript.

## Considerations

- **Runtime:** about 20 rows in M1 and 40 in M2, each a handful of process runs; keep the homes small (the Scene fixtures). If the suite passes 60 seconds in a debug build, split it into two files rather than sampling rows away (no boundary is skipped to save time).
- **What the matrix does not cover:** an edit by another program after the bound run's own check and before its lock is committed over until D8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8`) adds the under-lock witness check; this matrix's concurrent changes are omaddons commits (caught by the generation). D8 extends this suite or adds its own witness scenarios.
- **Expect the gate to take longer than its size label** (design gates do); a row that fails is a defect in the leaf's protocol or in the engine: fix the binding, or file a bug `discovered-from` omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2 for an engine defect and block the leaf on it.
- **Hot spots:** a new file; `tests/common/binding.rs` shared with omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2.5; README's Development table (one row).

## Dependencies

- Parent: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2 (`--if-match` on `install`, `update`, `sync` and `copy`).
- Before it: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2.2, omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2.3 and omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2.4 (all four commands bind). It runs in parallel with omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2.5.
- After it: nothing inside the leaf; the leaf's design gate, and so its closure, wait for it, and through the leaf D4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`) and D8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8`).

`tests/preconditions_matrix.rs` (new, `#![cfg(debug_assertions)]`, `//! e2e suite:` so `argc e2e` runs it): **8 tests, 72 rows, 7.3 s** in a debug build. Every row runs on a fresh two-client home (retail, which the run changes, and classic) built by `Shape`: `install` (Foo v2 over v1 from `--file`, replacing `Foo` and removing `FooOld`), `update` (the same two folders from `gh:o/foo`, the memo aged), `sync` (an `addons.toml` installing Foo, retail registered by Baz) and `copy` (Foo from classic to retail). Retail is compared as a `View`: its AddOns tree hash, its records without `tx_id`/`installed_at`, its generation. The expected "after" is computed once per command by an unfailing preview and bound run on an identical home, never hard-coded. It reuses `tests/common/binding.rs` from `…4.2.5`.

- **M1** `a_commit_at_each_pre_lock_pause_stales_the_bound_run`: 4 commands × `engine.plan.fetched`, `plan.done`, `stage.begin`, `stage.synced`, `snapshot.prestaged` (20 rows): an install of Bar on retail while paused → exactly `["targets"]`, not retryable, the `--dry-run` fix; retail exactly as the concurrent commit left it; history gained Bar's line alone; no journal.
- **M2** `a_bound_run_crashed_after_its_check_recovers_whole` (38 rows): install and update at each of 16 failpoints from `engine.stage.begin` to `engine.committed` plus `engine.swap.before_rename@1` and `@2` (the preview's journaled renames, counted from its items), and sync and copy at `engine.swapped`; each a real `abort` (SIGABRT asserted, so no row passes unreached); then `install Bar`, `pin Bar`, `unpin Bar` on classic, retail wholly before or after after each, no journal after the first, the later two changing nothing; then the re-run rule. 112 before-verdicts and 40 after-verdicts were recorded.
- **M3** `an_injected_io_error_at_the_swap_leaves_the_client_whole` (8 rows): install and update × `swap.before_rename@1`, `swap.after_exchange`, `swapped`, `record.written` with `=error`, then recovery three times and the re-run rule.
- **M4** `two_concurrent_bound_runs_never_both_commit` (both paused at `prestaged` with their own `Pause`: the first commits, the second is `["targets"]`, retail is the one expected result, history holds one update) and `a_bound_run_that_plans_after_the_winner_is_stale_not_unchanged` (update, copy: `targets` and `selection`, never "nothing to do").
- **M5** `a_stale_bound_noop_run_recovers_nothing`: a no-op `update` token staled by `pin Bar`, an `install Baz --file` crashed at `engine.swapped`; the bound run is `plan_stale`, the journal still waits and every tree is unchanged (the check runs before `recover_waiting`); an unbound `unpin` then recovers it.
- **M6** `an_unreadable_replaced_folder_stales_the_bound_run`: `Foo/core.lua` at mode 000 → `selection` among the parts; a fresh preview fails `io`; the mode restored → retail unchanged and the same token binds and commits the expected result. - **M7** `a_paused_bound_dry_run_holds_no_lock`: a bound `install --dry-run` paused at `engine.plan.done`; an unbound install commits within the 10 s bound (a held lock would make it `locked` after 5 s); `<state>` without `net.log` is as that install left it.

**Where the bead's expectation met the engine's actual rule (decided, each recorded in the suite's comments):**
- **M2's re-run from `after` is `targets` among the parts, not exactly `["targets"]`.** Rolled forward, retail already holds the result, so the re-run plans nothing: `selection` and `observed` differ too. This is the second-runner case of M4 and `…4.2.5`'s scenario 11.
- **M3: an error at or after `engine.swapped` does not fail the run.** The engine rolls the transaction forward in process and reports it as committed (its own rule, pinned by `tx::tests::an_error_at_any_failpoint_leaves_the_pin_iff_its_history_line`). So `swapped` and `record.written` rows exit 0 with retail wholly after, and `before_rename`/`after_exchange` rows exit 1 with the injected error (not `plan_stale`) and retail wholly before. title: README: previews bind on every addon-changing command, and what the guarantee covers
description:
Part 7 of 7 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2 (`--if-match` on `install`, `update`, `sync` and `copy`). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

D2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2`) makes `install`, `update`, `sync` and `copy` bind to their previews: every `--dry-run` returns `data.precondition`, and `--if-match <token>` makes the real run do exactly that on each client or nothing (`plan_stale`). Subtasks 2, 3 and 4 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2.2, omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2.3, omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2.4) each updated their own command's README section, the global flag table's `--if-match` row and the list of binding commands, so README stayed true at every commit. README is the product contract (common rule 11), and the plan names three promises this leaf must write down (step 8 of its approach): the list of binding commands, M4-D20's wording about release drift, and the per-target guarantee and its scope (M4-D60, M4-D61). This subtask rewrites the section "Previews and `--if-match`" around them, once all four commands bind, so the section is written once, as one argument, rather than patched four times.

**What the section must promise, and why** (the decisions, restated):
- **M4-D19:** the token of an engine command covers what the run will do and everything it saw: the client and its record generation; the folder operations, each change and each release; the content of every folder the run replaces or removes, every file of it, edited or clean; every name it creates; the client marker; local inputs; dependency choices; the rules that judged it; the omaddons build; plus `update`'s skip decisions, `sync`'s file bytes, `copy`'s source client and source folders. Hashing human text was rejected, so a token never moves because a message changed.
- **M4-D20:** a typed bound run keeps its command's freshness. `install` and `copy` ask their sources again (a newer release stales them); `update` and `sync` answer from the 15-minute release memo (inside that window a bound run installs the previewed version even if a newer one appeared: it does what you saw).
- **M4-D61:** the guarantee is per client: on each client a bound run commits exactly the previewed operations or none; a run over several clients commits one transaction per client and can end partial; it says which client committed and which was refused; nothing calls it atomic.
- **M4-D60 (as far as it is built when this lands):** everything the token covers is compared before anything is staged, whoever changed it; under the commit lock, another omaddons commit is caught by the record generation; there is no compare-and-swap against other programs writing into `AddOns`. (D8, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8`, later adds the under-lock witness and operation checks and extends this paragraph; this subtask must not describe them.)
- **M3-D46, unchanged:** the refusal's shape, opt-in binding, no stored state, the token is no credential.
- **Bound dry runs and no-op runs** (this leaf's rules): on the four commands a dry run given `--if-match` compares; on M3's five it previews afresh, as shipped; a bound run with nothing left to do still compares.

**Facts this subtask relies on** (verified at `c0ab5e9`, before this leaf): the section is `README.md:1931-1945`; its "previews afresh" rule is `:1944`; "Real runs carry `precondition: null`" is `:1945`; the "What works today" row on previews is `:159`; the error table's `plan_stale` row (`:1858`) already says "no under `--if-match`"; the agent block says "A locked or retryable plan_stale error's fix_argv reruns the same command" (`:2777`), which is why every bound refusal must be non-retryable.

## Technical Approach

Rewrite `### Previews and \`--if-match\`` (keep its anchor `#previews-and---if-match`, which the command sections link to) to this content, in the README's plain declarative style; the wording below is the target, adjust only for flow:

1. Opening paragraph: "A confirm dialog, or an agent that previews before it acts, must not run something other than what it showed. A `--dry-run` of a command that changes addons, or of a destructive command, returns `data.precondition`, a token describing exactly what the run would do and what it saw, and the real run with `--if-match <token>` does that, client by client, or nothing. `install`, `update`, `sync`, `copy`, `remove`, `undo`, `backup restore`, `backup prune` and `errors dismiss` bind. An `errors` read carries its own token for each client (`dismiss.precondition`), so a dismissal can be bound to the read the user saw."
2. The example block: keep `remove`'s two lines and add `omaddons update -t retail --dry-run --json  # data.precondition: "pc1:…"` and `omaddons update -t retail --if-match pc1:…  # exactly that update, or plan_stale`.
3. "The real run plans again and computes the token from its own plan before it stages anything. Under the commit lock, a commit by another omaddons process on that client since then is caught too."
4. The refusal bullet (`plan_stale`, not retryable, `details.changed` with `command`, `targets`, `selection`, `observed`, `fix_argv` the `--dry-run` form): keep, and add what moves each part for the four engine commands: `targets` (another change committed on the client, or the client registered since), `selection` (the run would now do something else: a new release for `install` or `copy`, a different set of changes), `observed` (what it saw changed: a file in a folder it replaces or removes, the client marker, a local archive or folder, the rules, the omaddons build, `update`'s skip decisions, the `sync` file, `copy`'s source client or source folders).
5. What each token covers: keep `remove`'s, `undo`'s, `backup prune`'s and `backup restore`'s sentences; add one for the four: "`install`'s, `update`'s, `sync`'s and `copy`'s cover, per client, its record generation; the folder operations, each change and each release (by release id, download address, expected hash and archive digest; a Tukui download by source, key and release id, because its address is resolved fresh); the content of every folder the run replaces or removes, managed or not: every file, edited or clean, every symlink and empty directory; every name it would create, that it is still absent; the client's marker; local inputs (a `--file` archive's hash, a folder's listing, a git checkout's commit); which addon satisfies which dependency; the rules that judged the releases; and the omaddons build (a preview made by another build is stale). `update`'s also covers what it chose to skip and why; `sync`'s the exact bytes of its file (even a comment); `copy`'s the source client's generation and the content of every source folder it copies."
6. **Releases between preview and run:** "A bound run keeps its command's freshness. `install` and `copy` always ask their sources again, so a release published since the preview makes the bound run `plan_stale` (`selection`). `update` and `sync` answer from releases remembered in the last 15 minutes, as they do without `--if-match` (unless `--refresh`), so inside that window a bound run installs exactly the previewed version even when a newer one appeared: it does what you saw."
7. **Per client:** "The guarantee is per client. On each client a bound run commits exactly the previewed operations or none of them. A run over several clients commits one transaction per client, as every run does: when a client changes after the run's own check (another omaddons command committed there first), that client is refused and the others still commit. The run is then `partial`: `targets[].tx` names each committed transaction, `targets[].error` (`plan_stale`) each refused client, and a client with neither changed nothing. Nothing calls such a run atomic."
8. **Scope:** "What is checked, and when: everything the token covers is compared before anything is staged, whoever changed it. Between that check and the commit lock, another omaddons commit on the client is caught by its record generation. omaddons does not promise a compare-and-swap against another program writing into `AddOns` at the same moment: no filesystem primitive offers one."
9. **Nothing left to do:** "A bound run that finds nothing left to do still compares its token. If the world moved since the preview it is `plan_stale`, not 'nothing to do', so the second of two runs holding one token learns that the first one won."
10. **Dry runs:** "On `install`, `update`, `sync` and `copy`, a `--dry-run` given `--if-match` checks the token as the real run would and writes nothing: the same preview and token while it holds, `plan_stale` once it does not. On `remove`, `undo`, `backup restore`, `backup prune` and `errors dismiss`, a `--dry-run` given one previews afresh and returns the current token." (Replaces `:1944`'s last sentence; keep its "opt-in" and "usage error" sentences.)
11. "The token is `pc1:` and 64 hex digits. Nothing is stored: it holds as long as what it describes is unchanged, and it is no credential." (unchanged) "Real runs of every binding command carry `precondition: null`." "With `-v`, a dry run of `install`, `update`, `sync` or `copy` ends with the line `Run it bound to this preview: --if-match <token>`."
12. "What works today" (`:159`): the previews row lists the nine binding commands; keep it "✅ Done (milestone 3)" for M3's five and add "(milestone 4: `install`, `update`, `sync`, `copy`)", or split it into an M4 row in the table's style. H4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`, the README final pass) reconciles the table at the end.

Do not mention `apply`, stored plans, `plans show` or the under-lock witness check: they do not exist when this lands (D4, D5, D8 and D9 each add their own paragraph).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] "Previews and `--if-match`" lists all nine binding commands and states, in README's words, what the four engine tokens cover (§5), the freshness rule of M4-D20 (§6), the per-client guarantee and how to read a partial bound run (§7), the scope of the checks (§8), nothing-left-to-do runs (§9), the bound dry-run rule for both groups (§10), `null` on real runs and the `-v` line (§11).
- [ ] The section's anchor is unchanged, and every command section's link to it still resolves.
- [ ] No sentence describes `apply`, stored plans, `plans show` or an under-lock witness check.
- [ ] "What works today" lists the four commands among those whose previews bind.
- [ ] Every statement is true of the code at this commit: each is backed by a test of subtasks 2–4 or a scenario of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2.5 (name the test beside each promise in the close comment).
- [ ] The change touches only `README.md` (no gate needed for a README-only commit, CLAUDE.md D16); `br lint` is clean for this subtask.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

None: this subtask changes only `README.md`.

title: `--if-match` on `pin`, `unpin` and `adopt`
description:
## How to work this bead

This bead is worked through its 4 subtasks, listed below in work order. Claim a subtask, not this bead (`br ready --parent omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.3` lists the ready ones). The agent that closes the last open subtask then verifies every acceptance criterion of this bead (they are the leaf's, not any one subtask's), and closes this bead with `br close omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.3 --reason "done: <evidence> · found: <ids>"`. Until this bead is closed, every bead it blocks stays blocked.

1. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.3.1 The shared binding of engine commands: `PlanBinding`, `check_noop`, the app-level dry-run check, `witness_scope`, `TargetsData.precondition`, and a refusal under the lock that keeps its form (added here unless D2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2`, landed them first).
2. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.3.2 `pin` and `unpin` bind to their preview on every path: witnesses, the bound real run, the bound dry run, the no-op check, the registry rows and README.
3. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.3.3 `adopt` binds to its preview when it adopts (`--apply`, folder names, `--ref`), and its report refuses `--if-match`.
4. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.3.4 Tests: `pin`, `unpin` and `adopt` bound end to end (`tests/preconditions.rs`), with contract rows and the dry-run `<state>` rule.

Subtask 1 comes first. Subtasks 2 and 3 can then run in parallel: they touch different command files and share only list lines (`BINDING_COMMANDS` and its unit test, three adjacent `CLI_PATHS` rows, one README sentence and one snapshot message), which the second to land rebases. Subtask 4 waits for 2 and 3 (and for T1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, whose `TestLog` it uses).

**Not a design gate.** Common rule 14 lists D1, D2, D5, D8, E5, E7, E8, E11, E14 and G3. This leaf adds no journal shape, recovery rule, binding *rule*, deletion rule, durability rule or failpoint: it applies the token and witness D1 defines, through the binding seam M3 built, to three more commands. Size M.

## Background

omaddons binds a preview to the run it confirms. M3 (M3-D46) gave five destructive commands a precondition token: `remove`, `undo`, `backup restore`, `backup prune` and `errors dismiss`. Their `--dry-run` returns `data.precondition` (`pc1:` and four 16-hex fields: `command`, `targets`, `selection`, `observed`), and the real run given `--if-match <token>` recomputes the token from its own plan before it stages anything, refusing with `plan_stale` (exit 1, not retryable, `details.changed` naming the parts that differ, `fix_argv` the same command with `--dry-run` in place of `--if-match <token>`). Every other command refuses `--if-match` as a usage error.

M4 extends the binding to every command that changes addons (M4-D19). D1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1`, `precondition::of_plan` and the approval witness for engine commands) builds the token of an engine command and the evidence it digests. D2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2`, `--if-match` on `install`, `update`, `sync` and `copy`) binds the four release-bearing commands. **This leaf binds the other three:** `pin` and `unpin`, which change only a record (except `pin --version`, which installs a release first), and `adopt`, which brings folders installed by hand under management and changes only records. After it, an agent or a person can preview `pin dbm`, `unpin dbm` or `adopt --apply` and then run exactly that preview, or nothing.

**Why these three matter.** They are cheap and frequent, and agents run them unattended. A bound `adopt --apply` must record exactly the folders the preview showed, with the bytes the preview hashed: adopting a folder someone edited after the preview would record content nobody approved, and the files index would then trust it. A bound `pin` must not report a quiet "unchanged" when another process pinned the addon in between: the agent asserted "do what I just saw", and what it saw is no longer the world.

**It serves these milestone goals:**

- **G-M4-3, what was previewed is what runs, target by target.** "Every command that changes addons can be previewed with `--dry-run` and then run bound to that preview, by token (`--if-match`) or by stored plan (`apply <plan_id>`)." The guarantee is per target: on each target the bound run commits exactly the approved operations or none. The approval covers what the preview saw, not only record generations: for `adopt`, every file of every folder it records; for `pin --version`, every file of every folder it replaces.
- **G-M4-6, no new risk to the engine's guarantees.** Dry runs still leave `<state>` untouched; unbound runs behave exactly as before; nothing new is written.

**Checkpoint criteria it serves** (the M4 checkpoint list, by number):

- **Criterion 6, previews bind on every addon-changing command, target by target.** "For `install`, `update`, `pin`, `unpin`, `adopt` (`--apply`, folder names, `--ref`), `sync` and `copy`, `--dry-run` returns a `precondition` token, and `--if-match <token>` commits, on each target, exactly that preview's operations or none of them." "A change in between gives `plan_stale` and changes nothing on that target." "That holds on every path: a bound run that finds nothing left to do, and a bound dry run, also check the token." "Two dry runs of an unchanged home give equal tokens for every source." This leaf proves all of it for `pin`, `unpin` and `adopt`. The under-lock re-check of the witness ("an edit made after the bound run's first check, before its lock, is `plan_stale` too") is D8's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8`) and applies to these commands through the type this leaf uses.
- **Criterion 7, stored plans** (context): D4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`, the plan store) stores the token every storable dry run returns, so `pin`, `unpin` and `adopt` must return one, also when they would change nothing.

**How it serves the vision.** Vision G4 (agent ergonomics: "the first command an agent guesses works") and D31 ("what a human approved is exactly what runs") are met today only for destructive commands. The thesis is that omaddons stays the sole, safe, undoable authority over what it manages; a confirmation that covers less than its preview showed would quietly break it.

**The decisions that shape it** (the full decision log is also filed as comments on the milestone epic `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`):

- **M4-D19: every command that changes addons binds with `--if-match`, using a token computed from the engine's plan.** `precondition::of_plan(command, &Plan, &[ApprovalWitness], &PlanExtras) -> Precondition` generalizes `of_remove`: the token of `install`, `update`, `pin`, `unpin`, `adopt` (`--apply`, folder names, `--ref`), `sync` and `copy` is computed from the plan the command will execute. Its parts: `command`; `targets` (each target's key, or its provisional id while unregistered, with its record generation); `selection` (per target: the folder ops, each change `{addon, ref, kind, fields, from_version, to_version, folders{added, replaced, removed, skipped, recorded}}`, each release, `creates_addons_dir`); `observed` (each target's judge digest and approval witness, the binary's `build_id`, and the command's extras). Further rules this leaf implements for its three commands: every such command's `--dry-run` data gains `precondition`, and real runs carry `precondition: null`; the token is checked through the existing `Binding::plan` seam before anything is staged, and again under the lock (the generations through `Binding::moved` today; the witness and the re-judged operations once D8 lands); each command's no-op path, which never reaches the engine, checks the token itself; `BINDING_COMMANDS` grows. *Why:* G4 and D31 are met today only for destructive commands, and `Binding` already runs after planning and before staging, so binding the engine commands needs no engine refactor. *Rejected:* (i) binding by target generation alone, which misses every hand edit that leaves the record alone (an edited folder `adopt` is about to record is exactly that); (ii) hashing the whole dry-run `data`, whose human-facing text and volatile fields would change the token for no reason.
- **M4-D60: every engine-command token carries an approval witness.** The witness is evidence, not a warning: for `adopt`, the entry digests of the folders it records (each regular file's path, size and SHA-256, each symlink's target, each directory, so an added empty directory counts too); for `pin --version`, every live folder the install replaces; for every target, the client marker's digest and the judge digest; the local inputs and dependency choices. Its canonical digest is `observed`'s witness part, so the bound run's own planning compares it before anything is staged. *Why:* generations prove only that no omaddons transaction committed; a person editing a file never moves one. *Rejected:* generations only. D1 owns the witness, D8 its re-check under the lock.
- **M4-D20 (context): a typed `--if-match` run uses its command's normal freshness rules.** `pin` revalidates its sources (`Freshness::Revalidate`); `adopt` answers from the 15-minute release memo window unless `--refresh`; neither changes here. A typed bound run does exactly what the preview showed, which is the guarantee; only `apply` (D5, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`) forces revalidation.
- **M4-D61 (context): the guarantee is per target.** Multi-target runs keep one transaction per target. A bound `pin` over two clients whose second client changed between the bound run's first commit and its second can commit the first and refuse the second; `TargetsData` reports each target, and nothing calls the run atomic. **A preview that would change nothing** still returns its token, so `--if-match` can assert "nothing changed".
- **M4-D22 (context): `pin`, `unpin` and `adopt` (when it adopts) store plans** once D4 lands; the token this leaf returns is what D4 stores. `adopt`'s report changes nothing, and stays unbound.
- **M3-D46 (kept):** a mismatch is `plan_stale` with `PlanStaleSource::Apply` (not retryable, because the same token can only fail again), `details.changed`, and the preview as `fix_argv`; without `--if-match` nothing changes: binding is opt-in.

**Facts this bead relies on** (verified at `c0ab5e9`; corrections are marked):

- `pin` and `unpin` share `run` (`src/app/pin.rs:128-346`). They find the targets where the addon is installed (`found`, `:139-150`), build one `RequestedChange` per target that needs one (`RecordEdit::SetPinned(true|false)`, or `RequestedChange::Install` with the version for `pin --version`, `:178-208`), and collect the others as `unchanged` items (`:220-237`). With changes they build an `Engine` with `Freshness::Revalidate` (`:246-251`), one `TxTarget` per target with changes (`:253-276`; kind `pin` when records-only, `:242`, `:273`), and call `engine.run` (`:277`). **The no-op path** is `if !changes.is_empty() { … } else { recover_waiting(ctx, &world, command); }` (`:245`, `:305-307`): with nothing to change, the engine is never called, so a token would never be checked. `not_managed` (no target has the addon, `:151-160`) and the `--version` usage error on `url:`/local refs (`:161-176`) refuse before anything.
- `adopt`'s modes are decided in `Mode::of` (`src/app/adopt/apply.rs:51-81`), which already raises its usage errors (`--apply` with folders, `--ref` without exactly one folder) before `World::load` (`src/app/adopt.rs:467-469`). The report mode (`Mode::Report`, no folders, no `--apply`) returns `AdoptData::Report` and commits nothing (`adopt.rs:651-707`). The adopting modes go through `apply::commit` (`adopt/apply.rs:589-792`): one `RecordEdit::Adopt(AdoptSpec)` per adopted group (`:682-685`), `RecordEdit::Repoint` for `--ref` on a managed folder (`:701-704`), one `TxTarget` per target with changes (`:743-750`), a `TxRequest` with `kind: Some(TxKind::Adopt)` and `no_deps: true` (`:755-764`), and `engine.run` (`:765`). **The no-op path** is `else { engine.recover_waiting(ctx); }` (`:776-778`; the plan cites `:753-777`, the whole `if`). `adopt` uses `Freshness::Window(SOURCE_RECHECK_MIN_INTERVAL)` unless `--refresh` or `--offline` (`adopt.rs:490-496`).
- **Correction:** the plan's architecture names `AdoptData.precondition`, but `AdoptData` is an untagged enum, `Report(AdoptReport)` or `Adopted(TargetsData)` (`src/app/adopt.rs:77-85`). The adopting token lives in `TargetsData.precondition`, inside `Adopted`; the report carries none.
- `TargetsData` (`src/app/outcome.rs:246-256`) is `{dry_run, run, targets, summary}` and has no `precondition`; `pin`, `unpin` and `adopt` (adopting) all return it, as do `update`, `sync` and `copy`. It is built by `TargetsData::build` and `assemble` (`:484-535`).
- **Found while writing this bead, not in the plan: a refusal under the lock loses its binding form when every item failed.** When a target's commit fails (`binding.moved` under the lock, or adopt's guard), `tx::run` records a target-level `PlanFailure` whose `ErrorBody` keeps the error whole (`tx.rs:460-466`), and `TargetResult.error` carries it (`outcome.rs:750-770`). But each of that target's items gets an `ItemError` (`outcome.rs:165-243`), which has no `retryable` field and keeps only a few `details` keys (`item_details`, `:183-204`, drops `changed`), and when every item failed, `TargetsData::all_failed` rebuilds the command's error from the first item's `ItemError` (`:595-622`) through `Error::new`, so it takes `plan_stale`'s registry default, **retryable** (`src/error.rs:193-194`), and its `details` are only `{items}`. A single-target bound `pin` refused under the lock would therefore exit with a retryable `plan_stale` without `details.changed`, contradicting M3-D46. `remove` is not affected: it keeps its own `Error` per item (`src/app/remove.rs:262-270`). See §2.6.
- **Adopt's existing under-lock guard.** `AdoptSpec` carries each adopted folder's index taken at planning (`src/engine/edit.rs:70-78`), and `check_adopt` re-lists the folder under the lock and compares every file's `(path, size, mtime_ns)` (`edit.rs:343-402`), failing with `hash_mismatch`. `rejudge` turns an adoption's guard failure into `plan_stale` "whatever the generation" (`src/engine/plan.rs:2715-2721`), and `locked()` returns it as it is (`src/engine/tx.rs:1134-1137`): it is `tx::stale`'s form, `PlanStaleSource::Replan`, **retryable**, with `details {cause, cause_message}` (`tx.rs:1375-1386`). README's adopt section says so ("one that changed in between makes its client's transaction `plan_stale` (retryable)", `README.md:1472`), and README's error table says `plan_stale` is retryable "(no under `--if-match`)" (`README.md:1858`). The guard compares stamps, not content, and does not see an added empty directory. **Not covered by the plan;** see "Decided" item 8.
- The `Binding` trait (`src/engine/tx.rs:187-206`): `plan(&Plan)` runs after planning and before staging, but only outside dry runs (`Some(binding) if !req.dry_run`, `tx.rs:401-407`, the condition at `:404`); `moved(target)` is returned under the lock when the target's record generation changed (`tx.rs:1049-1056`); `observed(target)` defaults to `moved`. `Engine::run_bound(req, cache, binding)` already hands a binding to `tx::run` (`src/app/engine.rs:201-209`). `Engine::recover_waiting` never recovers in a dry run (`engine.rs:248-254`), and neither does the free `recover_waiting` (`:259-267`).
- `src/app/precondition.rs` at `c0ab5e9`: `BINDING_COMMANDS` holds M3's five paths (`:25-31`); `check(expected, &actual, preview)` (`:187-209`) and `stale(command, changed, preview)` (`:211-225`) give the M3 refusal; `preview_argv(argv)` (`:227-237`) is the fix; `RemoveBinding` (`:278-296`) is the pattern this leaf follows; the unit test `the_binding_commands_are_the_five_of_m3_d46` pins the list (`:848-864`).
- `check_if_match` (`src/cli.rs:305-339`) refuses `--if-match` on any path outside `BINDING_COMMANDS`, with a message that lists every binding path ("only remove, undo, backup restore, backup prune and errors dismiss take it"); the contract snapshot `contract__matrix__if_match_unbound_command.snap` holds that message (`tests/contract/matrix.rs:801-817`), and `tests/preconditions.rs:251-278` asserts each listed name.
- `omarchy/Model.js` `CLI_PATHS` (`:133-178`) has `pin`, `unpin` and `adopt` with `binds: false` (`:147-149`). `tests/omarchy_widget.rs::cli_paths_mirror_the_registry` (`:29-51`; the `binds` assertion at `:42-46`, which the plan cites as `:44-48`) holds `binds` equal to `BINDING_COMMANDS` membership. In the widget, `binds` alone forces nothing: `ifMatchFor` (`Model.js:309-324`) requires a token only for a `destructive` path, so flipping `binds` lets the widget pass a token to `pin`/`unpin` and changes no button (they run without a preview, by design, M3-D9).
- Contract snapshots redact every token to `<precondition>` (`tests/contract/main.rs:335-344`), so token-bearing envelopes snapshot stably across builds.
- `tests/contract/special.rs::a_dry_run_leaves_the_state_directory_as_it_was` (`:250-305`) already includes `pin Foo -t retail --dry-run` (`:304`); `unpin` and `adopt` are not in it.
- `tests/adopt.rs::a_file_changed_between_planning_and_the_lock_is_plan_stale` (`:1185-1220`) pauses an unbound `adopt --apply` at `engine.plan.done` (`src/engine/plan.rs:1528`, inside `plan::plan`, before the bound check at `tx.rs:404`), edits a file, and expects the guard's retryable `plan_stale` and nothing recorded. `engine.snapshot.prestaged` (`tx.rs:1014`) is hit in each target's commit just before the global lock is taken (`:1015`); a `pause` failpoint stops at its first hit only (`tests/common/pause.rs`).

## Technical Approach

The work is described here as one design; each subtask restates the part it builds.

### 1. What binds, and where each path checks the token

| Command and mode | Engine path (what it plans) | `selection` holds | The witness (`observed`) holds | No-op path (never calls the engine) | No-op scope |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `pin <addon>` | per target needing it, `RecordEdit::SetPinned(true)`, kind `pin`, `Freshness::Revalidate` | the `edit` change (`fields: ["pinned"]`, `recorded` = the record's folders) | the marker and the judge only | every target holding the addon is already pinned (`pin.rs:305-307`) | every target where the addon is installed (`found`) |
| `pin <addon> --version V` | per target, `RequestedChange::Install` at `V` (kind `install` or `update`), dependencies included | ops, the change, the release (`{release_id, url, expected_hash, blob_sha256}`; a deferred asset without its URL) | every replaced folder's entry digest (role `Replaced`), absent names, a `git:` checkout's commit, dependency choices, marker, judge | none: `--version` always plans through the engine, which reports an unchanged release itself | — |
| `unpin <addon>` | `RecordEdit::SetPinned(false)`, kind `pin` | the `edit` change | marker and judge | every target holding it is already unpinned | `found` |
| `adopt --apply` | one `RecordEdit::Adopt` per `exact` or `identified` group, kind `adopt`, no dependencies, `Freshness::Window` | the `adopt` change `{addon, ref, kind: "adopt", from_version: null, to_version, folders{recorded}}` | each adopted folder's entry digest (role `Adopted`), marker, judge | no group to adopt on any examined target (`adopt/apply.rs:776-778`) | every target the run examined |
| `adopt <folder>…` | the groups holding the named folders, from `guess` up | as above | as above | every named folder is already managed (`unchanged`) or fails | every examined target |
| `adopt --ref R <folder>` | unmanaged: `Adopt` with the override; managed: `RecordEdit::Repoint(R)` | the `adopt` change, or an `edit` change with `fields: ["ref"]` | the adopted folder's digest; none for a re-point | `R` is the folder's own ref (`unchanged`) | the one `--ref` target |
| `adopt` (the report) | — | **unbound**: no token, and `--if-match` is a usage error (§5) | — | — | — |

A bound command reaches a token check on every path that can report success:

1. **A bound real run through the engine:** `PlanBinding::plan` before anything is staged (`tx.rs:404`), and `PlanBinding::moved` under the lock when a generation moved (`tx.rs:1054-1055`). D8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8`, the approval checked again under the commit lock) later adds the witness and operations checks under the lock to the same type.
2. **A bound dry run:** the command computes its token from the dry run's plan, as it must anyway for `data.precondition`, and compares it with `--if-match` in the app (§2.3).
3. **A bound run with nothing to change** (dry or real): `precondition::check_noop` (§2.4).

**Paths that refuse the whole run keep their own errors.** `not_managed`, `usage`, `target_not_found`, `target_ambiguous` and the other errors raised before the engine change nothing and carry more useful fixes than "preview again"; a bound run that ends in one of them is not checked against its token. *Decided while writing this bead:* only paths that can report success (committed, unchanged) need the token check, because a refusal already changes nothing and says why; `plan_stale` there would hide the real cause.

### 2. The shared pieces (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.3.1)

*Decided while writing this bead:* the plan assigns `PlanBinding` and `check_noop` to D2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2`, `--if-match` on `install`, `update`, `sync` and `copy`) but does not make D2 a blocker of this leaf, and its lane schedule finishes this leaf first. **Whichever of D2 and D3 lands first adds `PlanBinding`, `check_noop`, `TargetsData.precondition` and §2.6's change to `TargetsData::all_failed`, in the shape below (which follows the plan's §6.9.1 names); the second reuses them.** Before writing any of it, look on `main` (`grep -n "struct PlanBinding\|fn check_noop" src/app/precondition.rs`, `grep -n "precondition\|fn all_failed" src/app/outcome.rs`). If D2 has landed them, omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.3.1 checks that they provide what §2.1–§2.6 need (adding only what is missing, such as `dry_run_token`, `witness_scope` or the `all_failed` change), and closes with the commit that added them.

#### 2.1 `PlanBinding` (`src/app/precondition.rs`)

```rust
/// An engine command's run bound to its preview's token (M4-D19): install, update,
/// pin, unpin, adopt, sync and copy. The engine asks it before staging and, when a
/// target's record moved, under the lock (D8 adds the witness and operations checks).
pub struct PlanBinding<'a> {
    pub command: &'static str,
    /// `--if-match`; `None` binds nothing (the run only computes its token).
    pub expected: Option<String>,
    /// The preview (`preview_argv(&ctx.argv)`): the fix of every refusal.
    pub preview: Vec<String>,
    pub extras: PlanExtras<'a>,
}

impl<'a> PlanBinding<'a> {
    /// The binding of a real run given `--if-match`, else `None` (dry runs compare in
    /// the app, `dry_run_token`; unbound runs bind nothing).
    pub fn for_real_run(ctx: &Context, command: &'static str, extras: PlanExtras<'a>) -> Option<Self>;
}

impl Binding for PlanBinding<'_> {
    fn plan(&self, plan: &Plan) -> Result<()> {
        check(self.expected.as_deref(), &of_plan(self.command, plan, &plan.witnesses, &self.extras), &self.preview)
    }
    fn undo(&self, _planned: &EngineUndo) -> Result<()> { Ok(()) }
    fn moved(&self, _target: &str) -> Error { stale(self.command, &[Part::Targets], &self.preview) }
}
```

The plan's sketch is `PlanBinding { expected: Option<String>, extras }`; `command` and `preview` are added because `of_plan` and every refusal need them (`RemoveBinding` carries its preview the same way).

#### 2.2 `witness_scope` (`src/app/precondition.rs`)

`pub fn witness_scope(ctx: &Context) -> Option<WitnessScope>`: `Some(WitnessScope::default())` for a dry run or a run given `--if-match`, `None` otherwise, through a pure `fn collects_witnesses(dry_run: bool, bound: bool) -> bool`. So an unbound real run never pays for a witness (D1's rule), and every token that can be compared was computed with one. `copy`'s `CopyFrom` scope is D2's.

#### 2.3 `dry_run_token`: the bound dry run compares, in the app

`pub fn dry_run_token(ctx: &Context, command: &'static str, plan: &Plan, extras: &PlanExtras<'_>) -> Result<Option<String>>`: for a dry run, `actual = of_plan(command, plan, &plan.witnesses, extras)`, then `check(ctx.if_match.as_deref(), &actual, &preview_argv(&ctx.argv))?`, then `Some(actual.token())`; for a real run, `None` (real runs carry `precondition: null`). Its pure core, `fn dry_run_token_of(dry_run: bool, expected: Option<&str>, actual: &Precondition, preview: &[String]) -> Result<Option<String>>`, is what the unit tests call.

*Decided while writing this bead:* **this leaf does not touch `src/engine/tx.rs`.** The plan has the engine stop skipping the binding in dry runs (drop `!req.dry_run` at `tx.rs:404`), and lists that step under D2, whose hot-spot order there is D2 → D8. `pin`, `unpin` and `adopt` compute their dry-run token in the app anyway, so comparing it there gives the same result (a `plan_stale` before anything could be staged; a dry run stages nothing) without depending on D2's engine change. These three commands therefore pass a `PlanBinding` to the engine only on real runs (`PlanBinding::for_real_run`), and no comparison is ever made twice. When D2 drops the dry-run skip, nothing changes for them.

This differs from M3's rule for its own commands until D2 lands: today "a `--dry-run` that is given one previews afresh and returns the current token" (`README.md:1944`, `tests/preconditions.rs:280-293`, and `undo`'s `Some(token) if !ctx.dry_run`, `src/app/undo.rs:387-388`). M4's rule (M4-D19, criterion 6) is that a bound dry run compares; this leaf applies it to its three commands and leaves the M3 commands to D2. README states both until they agree (§6).

#### 2.4 `check_noop` (`src/app/precondition.rs`)

```rust
/// A target in scope of a run that sends nothing to the engine.
pub struct NoopTarget<'a> {
    pub target: &'a Target,   // crate::model::Target
    /// The record generation now (0 for an unregistered target, or one with no record).
    pub generation: u64,
}

/// The token of a run with nothing to change (it never calls the engine): `of_plan` over
/// a plan of `targets` with no change, their bare witnesses and `extras`. A bound run (dry
/// or real) compares it with `--if-match` and is `plan_stale` when it differs; a dry run
/// returns its token for `data.precondition`; an unbound real run computes nothing.
pub fn check_noop(ctx: &Context, command: &'static str, targets: &[NoopTarget<'_>], extras: &PlanExtras<'_>)
    -> Result<Option<String>>
```

- **Nothing is computed for an unbound real run** (`!ctx.dry_run && ctx.if_match.is_none()` returns `Ok(None)` at once): no marker is read, so the M3 behaviour and cost of a no-op are unchanged.
- Otherwise each target's witness is `witness::bare(target)?` (an unreadable marker fails the command with D1's `io` error: fail closed, §8.1 rule 6), and the plan is a `plan::Plan` whose `targets` are one `TargetPlan` per `NoopTarget`: `target` its id, `key` its key, `generation` as given, every list empty, `kind: None`, `creates_addons_dir: false`. The other `Plan` fields are never read by `of_plan` and take neutral values (`schema_version: "1.0"`, `plan_id` and `expires_at` `None`, `created_at` now, `argv` the run's, `dry_run`, `generations` from the targets, empty `failures` and `facts`; `witnesses` the bare ones). Its pure core, `fn noop_precondition(command, targets: &[(TargetRef, u64, ApprovalWitness)], extras) -> Precondition`, is what the unit tests call.
- Then `check(ctx.if_match.as_deref(), &actual, &preview_argv(&ctx.argv))?`, then `Ok(ctx.dry_run.then(|| actual.token()))`.
- **Why it works.** A preview and a bound run over the same world take the same path: both reach the engine with the same targets, or both find nothing to do over the same scope, so their tokens agree. When the world changed so that the bound run takes the other path, the tokens differ in `selection` at least (a change versus none) and in `targets` when a generation moved, so the run is `plan_stale`, never a quiet "unchanged": "the loser of two concurrent typed runs that planned after the winner committed is `plan_stale` rather than a quiet 'unchanged'". A no-op bound to a no-op preview of the same world succeeds as `unchanged`.
- **Order.** `check_noop` runs **before** `recover_waiting` on the no-op path. *Decided while writing this bead:* a stale bound run changes nothing at all, not even a recovery a crashed earlier command left waiting; a matching run then recovers exactly as today.

#### 2.5 `TargetsData.precondition` (`src/app/outcome.rs`)

`pub precondition: Option<String>`, the last field, documented "`--dry-run`: the token `--if-match` takes to bind the real run to this preview (one token for the whole run); `null` for a real run". `assemble` sets `None`; each binding command sets it after `build`, before `listing`. Always serialized (never `skip_serializing_if`), as `RemoveData.precondition` is: real runs carry `precondition: null`. `listing()` keeps it.

*Decided while writing this bead:* if this leaf lands before D2, `update`, `sync` and `copy` also gain the key, as `null`, until D2 fills it in their dry runs; the key is additive and `null` says "no token", which is true until D2 binds them. Every `TargetsData` envelope snapshot gains `"precondition": null` (dry runs of the binding commands: `"<precondition>"`) and is re-accepted in that commit, its list in the commit message.

#### 2.6 A refusal under the lock keeps its form (`src/app/outcome.rs`)

`TargetsData::all_failed` (`:595-622`): when the first failed item belongs to a target whose `error` is a `plan_stale`, the command's error is **that target error**, converted back from its `ErrorBody` with its own `retryable`, `details`, `fix`, `fix_argv` and `alternatives`, and with `details.items` added exactly as today. Every other case is unchanged. So a single-target bound run refused under the lock exits with the non-retryable `plan_stale`, `details.changed: ["targets"]` and the preview as `fix_argv`, as M3-D46 requires, and D8's under-lock refusals (`observed`, `selection`) keep their form through the same path. A small `fn error_of(body: &ErrorBody) -> Error` does the conversion.

*Decided while writing this bead:* narrow to `plan_stale`, because that is the binding's code and the only one whose retryability depends on how it was raised; widening it to every target-level error would add `details` keys to many existing failures for no binding reason. Its one visible effect on an unbound run: adopt's guard refusal (`tx::stale`, retryable) gains its `details.cause` and `details.cause_message` beside `items`, an additive change. Whichever of D2 and D3 lands first makes this change with the other shared pieces.

In `src/app/pin.rs`'s `run`:

2. `let binding = PlanBinding::for_real_run(ctx, command, PlanExtras::default());` and `engine.run_bound(&req, Some(&cache), binding.as_ref().map(|b| b as &dyn Binding))` in place of `engine.run` (`:277`). `cache.remember(..)` keeps running on the result whatever it is, as today.

5. `fn noop_targets(found: &[(&DiscoveredTarget, &AddonRecord)], records: &BTreeMap<String, TargetRecord>) -> Vec<NoopTarget<'_>>`: one per found target, `generation` its record's (`world.records()` holds every registered target's; `found` targets are always registered, and a missing record gives 0).

The plan's acceptance scenario, traced: `pin dbm -t retail --dry-run` with DBM unpinned plans an edit on retail and returns `TOK` = {targets `[retail, g7]`, selection: the edit, observed: marker and judge}. Another process pins DBM (g8). The bound `pin dbm -t retail --if-match TOK` finds DBM pinned, so `changes` is empty and the no-op branch runs: `check_noop` over `[retail, g8]` with an empty selection gives `targets` and `selection` different from `TOK` (and `observed` equal, because a records-only pin's witness is the bare witness), so the run is `plan_stale`, `details.changed: ["targets", "selection"]`, and nothing is written.

### 5. `adopt`'s report refuses `--if-match`

The report changes nothing and returns no token, so there is nothing to bind. Accepting `--if-match` there silently would let an agent believe it ran a bound adoption. In `Mode::of` (`src/app/adopt/apply.rs:54-80`), after the mode is decided and before `World::load`, a pure helper `fn report_takes_no_token(report: bool, if_match: Option<&str>, argv: &[String]) -> Result<()>` refuses:

```json
{"ok":false,"command":"adopt","exit_code":2,"error":{"code":"usage","retryable":false,
 "message":"--if-match binds a run that adopts (--apply, folder names or --ref); the report adopts nothing, so it takes no token",
 "details":{},"fix":"omaddons adopt -t retail","fix_argv":["omaddons","adopt","-t","retail"]}}
```

The fix is the same argv without `--if-match <token>` (`cli::fix_argv(&cli::without_flag(argv, "--if-match"))`, which removes both the spaced and the `=` form): the report, which only reads. *Decided while writing this bead:* an existing code (`usage`, §8.1 rule 1), raised from the arguments before anything is read (common rule 8), and a fix that reads rather than one that adds `--apply` (a fix never turns the user's command into one that changes something it did not ask to change). A malformed token is refused earlier by `check_if_match`, as for every binding command.

```json
   "precondition":"pc1:3f0c9a1b7d2e4c55a8e1f3b6c0d2e7f1b4a9c8d7e6f5a4b3c2d1e0f9a8b7c6d5"}}
```

The real run's `data.precondition` is `null`. The refusal of a stale bound run:

```json
{"ok":false,"command":"pin","exit_code":1,
 "error":{"code":"plan_stale","retryable":false,
   "message":"this pin is no longer what its preview showed (targets, selection changed); nothing was changed: preview it again",
   "details":{"changed":["targets","selection"]},
   "fix":"omaddons pin dbm -t retail --dry-run","fix_argv":["omaddons","pin","dbm","-t","retail","--dry-run"]}}
```

`details.changed` by scenario (single target unless said; the client registered before the preview, since a client that registers in between moves from provisional id to key and is stale in `targets`, `selection` and `observed` alike):

| Between the preview and the bound run | Path the bound run takes | `details.changed` |
|---|---|---|
| another process pins the addon (`pin`), or unpins it (`unpin`) | no-op | `["targets", "selection"]` |
| another process commits anything else on the target | engine (before staging) | `["targets"]` |
| a commit on the target while the bound run waits before its lock (`engine.snapshot.prestaged`) | engine (under the lock, `moved`) | `["targets"]` |
| a file in a folder `adopt` records is edited (same size, or longer), or an empty directory is added in it | engine (before staging) | `["observed"]` |
| the folders `adopt --apply` would record were adopted meanwhile | no-op | `["targets", "selection", "observed"]` (the preview's witness held the folders; the no-op's is bare) |
| a file in a folder `pin --version` replaces is edited | engine | `["observed"]` |
| the build of omaddons changed | either | `["observed"]` at least (`build_id`) |

- Unbound runs: without `--if-match`, every command behaves exactly as before, collects no witness on a real run, and keeps its output but for the added `precondition` key.
- `src/engine/tx.rs`, `src/engine/plan.rs`, the `Binding` trait, the M3 tokens and bindings, adopt's guard, `engine::tx::FAILPOINTS`, `src/limits.rs` (no new constant), the human output (the token is JSON-only here; D4, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`, adds the human `--if-match` line, under `-v`), and the rule that every dry run leaves `<state>` untouched.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `pin`, `unpin` and `adopt` (`--apply`, folder names, `--ref` on an unmanaged and on a managed folder) each bind: `--dry-run` returns `data.precondition` (a `pc1:` token), `--if-match <token>` on an unchanged home commits exactly the preview's changes (the records; for `pin --version`, the release and its folders), and real runs carry `precondition: null`.
- [ ] Two dry runs of an unchanged home give equal tokens for `pin`, `unpin`, `pin --version` (the second served from the blob cache, with no asset request in `net.log`), `adopt --apply --no-verify` and `adopt --apply` with verification (the second from the cache).
- [ ] A file whose content is edited (a same-size edit; a longer write) inside a folder `adopt` records, or an empty directory added in one, between `adopt --apply --dry-run` and the bound run gives `plan_stale` with `details.changed: ["observed"]`, `retryable: false`, `fix_argv` the `--dry-run` form, and nothing is recorded: the target's records and the `AddOns` tree hash as they did just before the bound run, and no history line is added. A `touch` alone does not stale the preview: the bound run adopts.
- [ ] A concurrent pin of the same addon between the preview and a bound `pin` gives `plan_stale` with `details.changed: ["targets", "selection"]`: the bound run finds nothing to change, and the no-op check sees the moved generation. The same holds for `unpin` after a concurrent unpin, and for `adopt --apply` after the same folders were adopted meanwhile (`["targets", "selection", "observed"]`). A no-op bound to a no-op preview of the same home succeeds as `unchanged`.
- [ ] Every path checks: a bound dry run of `pin`, `unpin` and `adopt` given a stale token is `plan_stale` and given a matching one returns it; a bound real run is refused before staging after a commit on its target (`["targets"]`), and under the lock after a commit made while it waits at `engine.snapshot.prestaged` (`["targets"]`, `retryable: false`, the preview as `fix_argv`, with `details.items` beside); a hand edit in a folder `pin --version` replaces is `plan_stale` (`["observed"]`); a no-op preview whose target moved is `plan_stale` (`["targets"]`) for each of the three commands. Every stale run leaves records and folders hash-identical.
- [ ] A bound `pin` over two clients whose second client changed while the run waited before its first commit commits the first client and reports the second with `error.code: "plan_stale"` (`details.changed: ["targets"]`), `partial: true`.
- [ ] A bound `adopt` whose folder changes after its own check and before its lock records nothing (the guard's retryable `plan_stale`), and running the same bound command again is the non-retryable `plan_stale` (`["observed"]`).
- [ ] `adopt`'s report given `--if-match` is `usage` (exit 2) before anything is read, its `fix_argv` the same command without `--if-match <token>`, and that fix runs to exit 0.
- [ ] Without `--if-match`, every existing `pin`, `unpin` and `adopt` test passes unchanged except for the added `precondition` key, and an unbound real run collects no witness.
- [ ] `BINDING_COMMANDS` holds `pin`, `unpin` and `adopt` after M3's five; `CLI_PATHS` has `binds: true` for them and `tests/omarchy_widget.rs` passes; `--if-match` on a non-binding command lists the new names.
- [ ] Dry runs of `pin`, `unpin` and `adopt --apply` leave `<state>` untouched (`tests/contract/special.rs` covers `unpin` and `adopt`, beside `pin`).

## Considerations

- **Risk #6, tokens too sensitive** (a rules edit, a binary upgrade or a judge digest stales every preview; likelihood M, impact L; owner D1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1`): intentional, since a verdict is as good as the rules that made it; the fix is one re-preview, and `details.changed` names the part.
- **Risk #19, a token stales for no reason** (M, M; owners D1 and E6): the equal-token scenarios here (pin, unpin, `pin --version` from download and cache, adopt verified and not) are this leaf's guard for its commands; the witness is content, so a `touch` changes nothing.
- **Risk #14, the milestone is large:** D3 has 2 units of slack (lane 3, t = 3–5, before D8, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8`, at t = 6–8). D8 and D4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`) wait for it.
- **The D2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2`) overlap is the likeliest collision.** Both leaves can start at t = 3, and both need `PlanBinding`, `check_noop` and `TargetsData.precondition`. Look on `main` before omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.3.1, claim with the file list, and coordinate through `SendMessage` if D2 is in progress. Whoever lands second rebases and reuses; never two `PlanBinding`s.
- **Hot spots (collision rules):** `src/app/precondition.rs` (D1, D2, D3, D8, E6, E7): **D1 first**; this leaf appends. `src/app/{update,sync,copy,pin,install,remove}.rs` and `adopt/apply.rs` (C2, D2, D3, D4): C2 touches argument handling only; **D2 and D3 before D4** (D4's `StoredIntent::from_args` comes after). `src/engine/tx.rs` (**D2 → D8**): not touched here. `omarchy/Model.js` (G1 → G2): command leaves change only `CLI_PATHS` rows. `tests/contract/matrix.rs` and snapshots: append rows. `README.md`: own sections only.
- **Cost.** A dry run or bound run of `adopt` hashes each adopted folder twice: once to index it for the `AdoptSpec` (`index_group`) and once for the witness (D1 hashes adopted folders fully). That doubles the read of folders adoption reads anyway, and only where a token is computed; unbound real runs pay nothing new. Reusing the index for the witness is a later optimization, not M4's. A records-only `pin` reads one marker per target.
- **What could go wrong, and how to notice:** a witness collected on an unbound real run (the `witness_scope` table and the unchanged unbound tests); a no-op path that skips its check (the no-op scenarios, one per command, and `a_noop_preview_goes_stale_when_its_target_moves`); a refusal under the lock that comes out retryable or without `details.changed` (§2.6's unit test and the paused-commit scenarios); a preview and a bound run taking different scopes for the same world (the equal-token scenarios); a `plan_stale` that is retryable under `--if-match` before staging (each refusal asserts `retryable: false`); a check placed after `recover_waiting` (the no-op scenarios hash the state they assert unchanged).
- **After D8:** D8 adds `witness()` and `operations()` to `PlanBinding`, so these three commands get the under-lock witness check, the operations comparison and the swap predicates without further change here; D8 updates `a_bound_adopt_edited_before_its_lock_records_nothing_and_converges` to its non-retryable `observed`.
- **For D4 and D5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`, `omaddons apply`):** D4's `StoredIntent` gets `pin`, `unpin` and `adopt` variants and stores the token these dry runs return, `plan_id: null` with the token for a no-op preview. D5's `apply` calls these commands' `run` with `ctx.if_match` set to the stored token and `ctx.dry_run` for `apply --dry-run`; the binding reads only `Context`, so `apply` needs nothing more from this leaf.
- **Compatibility:** tokens are not stable across builds (`build_id`), by design. The `precondition` key is additive. The M3 build ignores everything here (nothing is persisted).
- **Privacy:** tokens hold digests only; nothing reads `WTF/` or SavedVariables; no test creates `WTF/`.
- **Decided defaults (confirm or adjust in the close comment):** (1) whichever of D2 and D3 lands first adds the shared pieces; (2) no change to `tx.rs`, dry runs compare in the app, the engine gets a binding only on real runs; (3) the no-op scopes (`found` for `pin`/`unpin`, every examined target for `adopt`); (4) `check_noop` before `recover_waiting`; (5) refusals before the engine keep their codes; (6) `adopt`'s report refuses `--if-match` with a reading fix; (7) witnesses only for dry and bound runs; (8) adopt's retryable guard kept until D8; (9) `BINDING_COMMANDS`' order; (10) no human token line; (11) `TargetsData.precondition` last and always serialized, `null` on commands not yet bound; (12) a stale target of a multi-target run reported through its existing `error`, no new status; (13) the corpus row only if C4 has landed; (14) "a folder touched" read as a content change; (15) `all_failed` keeps a target-level `plan_stale` whole, and only that code.
