title: The cache-side plumbing: plans in `<cache>/plans/`, prune's plan and lease kinds, `fsx::lock::Lease` and `LockUse::Expired`
description:
Part 1 of 7 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4 (The plan store). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

D4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`, the plan store) makes every storable `--dry-run` (`install`, `update`, `pin`, `unpin`, `adopt`, `sync`, `copy`, `remove`, `undo`, `backup restore`, `backup prune`) store what it showed as a small, typed plan file, so that `omaddons apply <plan_id>` (D5, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`) can execute exactly that later. Two decisions fix where and how: **M4-D21** puts stored plans in `<cache>/plans/<plan_id>.json`, written by `Writer::Derived`, because every dry run must leave `<state>` untouched (a rule two tests pin) and a plan is derived, reproducible by previewing again, and expires within 24 hours, which is the cache's contract (rejected: `<state>/plans/` with a scope row admitting `Derived`, which breaks the pinned rule for no safety gain); **M4-D24** bounds the store with hard quotas and cleans it, at each storing dry run, under a cache-local lock and never the global commit lock, deleting at most 64 expired plans with their leases per batch through `fsx::prune(PruneReason::PlanExpiry)` "under `LockUse::Expired`, which admits only expired plan files and their leases", and never evicting an unexpired plan. M4-D61 adds that `apply` holds a per-plan lease (`<cache>/plans/<plan_id>.lease`, an `fsx::lock::Lease`), which "the plan sweep deletes … only together with its expired plan and only while it can take that lease itself, so a held lease is never unlinked"; the lease type is this leaf's because it uses one first, for its admission lock.

This subtask builds the filesystem layer under all of that and nothing above it: the path move, prune's two plan kinds, the `Lease` type and the `LockUse::Expired` mode. It is its own step because it touches only `src/fsx/` and `src/state/paths.rs` (a hot spot whose rule is "touch separate functions, rebase before the gate"), it changes no command's behaviour, and the store (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4.4) and D5 build on it. It is also where D4's one deletion rule lives, so its adversarial cases (every victim it must refuse) are unit tests here.

**Facts this subtask relies on** (verified at `c0ab5e9`):

- `Paths::plans_dir()` is `self.state.join("plans")` (`src/state/paths.rs:338-340`), `Paths::plan(&PlanId)` is `<plans_dir>/<id>.json` (`:342-345`), and nothing outside the path test calls either. `every_documented_path` (`:612`) pins them at `/s/omaddons/plans` and `/s/omaddons/plans/<id>.json` (`:677-678`); the test's cache root is `/k/omaddons`. `Paths::cache_trash()` is `<cache>/trash` (`:468-470`).
- `src/fsx/prune.rs`: `PruneReason::PlanExpiry`'s writer is `Mutating` (`:43-50`, the arm at `:45`); `LockUse` is `Acquire | Held(&GlobalLockGuard) | Own(&InflightLock)` (`:53-63`); under `Own` every victim must be named for the caller's transaction (`:105-120`) and an unfinished journal is refused (`:121-134`); `Acquire` takes the global lock (`:136-139`); victims are renamed into their side's `trash/` and then deleted (`:140-199`); the trash left by crashed prunes is swept only when the call is not `Own` (`:200-205`). `classify` (`:247-298`) refuses a non-normalized path, a symlink and a location that is not prunable, and checks the kind's reason. `location` (`:336-406`): the state branch's `["plans", "<PlanId>.json"]` arm gives `Kind::Plan` (`:368-374`); the cache branch knows `blobs`, `tmp` and `inflight` (`:380-391`). `held(path)` probes a lock file with `try_lock` (`:451-461`). The test `every_reason_reaches_only_its_locations` (`:649-732`) has the row `state/plans/<TX>.json → PlanExpiry` (`:688-691`).
- `src/fsx/lock.rs`: `GlobalLock::acquire_with_timeout` opens its file `read`, `write`, `create(true)`, `truncate(false)`, mode 0644 (`:91-98`), polls `try_lock` with a pause doubling from 5 ms to 50 ms (`:99-113`), then writes `HolderInfo {pid, command, started_at}` through the locked handle (`write_holder`, `:125-137`); `InflightLock::create_at` opens with `create_new(true)` (`:221-239`), which is why a plan lock cannot reuse it; `DirLock`'s `open_dir` uses rustix with `NOFOLLOW` (`:320-325`). The test `no_code_path_truncates_renames_or_unlinks_the_lock_file` (`:414-453`) forbids `.truncate(true)`, `remove_file`, `rename(`, `rename_with` and `prune(` anywhere in `lock.rs`, and allows only `lock.rs`, `scope.rs` and `paths.rs` to name `lock_file`. `a_holder_that_dies_frees_the_dir_lock` (`:507-544`) is the child-process pattern for a death test.
- The `Cache` scope row admits every writer (`src/fsx/scope.rs:113`); `ScopeTable::check(writer, owned, path, access)` checks one normalized absolute path (`:416`); `ScopeTable::cache_dir()` (`:352`).
- `crate::clock::now()` gives the debug build's `OMADDONS_NOW` or the real time (`src/clock.rs:8-11`); `PLAN_TTL = DAY` (`src/limits.rs:49`). `PLAN_MAX_BYTES` does not exist yet: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4.4 adds it to `src/limits.rs`. **Decided while writing this bead:** this subtask adds it (with its `REGISTRY` row, its `LIMIT_NAMES` entry and the re-accepted `limit_registries` snapshot), because fsx's expiry read is the first code that needs it; omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4.4 adds the other three.

## Technical Approach

### 1. The paths (`src/state/paths.rs`)

- `plans_dir()` → `self.cache.join("plans")`, with the doc comment "Stored plans (M4-D21): derived, so in the cache; a dry run never writes `<state>`."
- `plan(&id)` unchanged (`<plans_dir>/<id>.json`).
- New: `plan_lease(&id) -> <plans_dir>/<id>.lease` ("A plan's apply lease (M4-D61): an flock, swept only with its expired plan") and `plans_lock() -> <plans_dir>/.lock` ("The plan store's admission lock: an flock, never deleted").
- `every_documented_path`: the rows become `(p.plans_dir(), "/k/omaddons/plans")`, `(p.plan(&plan), "/k/omaddons/plans/<TX>.json")`, `(p.plan_lease(&plan), "/k/omaddons/plans/<TX>.lease")`, `(p.plans_lock(), "/k/omaddons/plans/.lock")`. No migration: no build ever wrote `<state>/plans/`.

### 2. prune's plan kinds (`src/fsx/prune.rs`)

- `PruneReason::PlanExpiry.writer()` → `Writer::Derived`; its doc: "Stored plans and their leases (M4-D24), only as expired, under `LockUse::Expired`."
- `location`: delete the state branch's `["plans", …]` arm (a `<state>/plans/` victim is then "not a prunable location", `scope_denied`, for every reason). Add to the cache branch:
  - `["plans", name]` where `name.strip_suffix(".json")` parses as a `PlanId` → `Kind::Plan`;
  - `["plans", name]` where `name.strip_suffix(".lease")` parses as a `PlanId` → `Kind::PlanLease` (new kind);
  - anything else under `plans/` (`.lock`, temp files) → `None`.
  Trash for both: `scopes.cache_dir().join("trash")`.
- `Kind::PlanLease.reason()` is `PlanExpiry`, like `Kind::Plan`.

### 3. `fsx::lock::Lease` (`src/fsx/lock.rs`, exported from `src/fsx/mod.rs`)

```rust
/// A named advisory lock on a cache file: the plan store's admission lock
/// (`<cache>/plans/.lock`) and an applier's plan lease (`<cache>/plans/<id>.lease`, D5).
/// Never the global lock: work under it blocks no other command. The file is opened, or
/// created when missing, never created exclusively and never truncated away, so a crashed
/// holder leaves nothing that blocks: the kernel releases its flock. The holder writes
/// `{pid, command, started_at}` through the locked handle, for diagnosis only; nothing
/// trusts it unless the lock is held.
pub struct Lease;

#[derive(Debug)]
pub struct LeaseGuard { file: File, path: PathBuf, acquired_at: Instant }

#[derive(Debug)]
pub enum LeaseError {
    /// Held by another process for the whole wait.
    Busy { holder: Option<HolderInfo>, waited: Duration },
    /// Not a lease this writer may take: outside the cache scope, or a symlink.
    Refused(String),
    Io(std::io::Error),
}

impl Lease {
    pub fn acquire(scopes: &ScopeTable, path: &Path, command: &str, timeout: Duration) -> Result<LeaseGuard, LeaseError>;
    pub fn try_acquire(scopes: &ScopeTable, path: &Path, command: &str) -> Result<Option<LeaseGuard>, LeaseError>;
    pub fn holder(path: &Path) -> Option<HolderInfo>;
}
impl LeaseGuard {
    pub fn held_for(&self) -> Duration;
    pub fn path(&self) -> &Path;
    /// Releases it now (dropping does the same).
    pub fn release(self) {}
}
```

- **Scope:** `path` must be absolute and normalized, lie under `scopes.cache_dir()`, and pass `scopes.check(Writer::Derived, &OwnedFolders::default(), path, Access::Write)`; anything else is `LeaseError::Refused` before any file is opened or directory created. The parent is created with `ensure_dir_all` in `WriteSession::untracked(Writer::Derived, scopes, "lease")`.
- **Open:** `OpenOptions::new().read(true).write(true).create(true).truncate(false).mode(0o600).custom_flags(O_NOFOLLOW | O_CLOEXEC)` (through `std::os::unix::fs::OpenOptionsExt`); `ELOOP` (a symlink) is `Refused`.
- **Wait:** `try_lock` in a loop, the pause doubling from 5 ms to 50 ms, never past `timeout`; then `Busy { holder: Lease::holder(path), waited }`. `try_acquire` is one `try_lock`.
- **Hold:** after locking, rewrite the holder line through the handle (`set_len(0)`, seek to 0, `serde_json::to_vec(&HolderInfo)` + `\n`), reusing `write_holder`. **Decided while writing this bead:** the line is written although M4's file table calls these "empty lock files", because D5's `locked` error reports the holder's `{pid, command, age_s}` when a second applier times out; it is diagnostic, rewritten by each holder, and never trusted unless the lock is held.
- **Decided while writing this bead:** `LeaseError` is fsx's own type, not a crate `Error`, because its two callers map a timeout differently: the store (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4.4) turns it into the warning `plan_not_stored`, D5 into `locked` (exit 5) with `details.lease`.
- `lock.rs` still never uses `.truncate(true)`, `remove_file`, `rename(`, `rename_with` or `prune(`; the existing test proves it.

### 4. `LockUse::Expired` (`src/fsx/prune.rs`)

```rust
pub enum LockUse<'a> {
    Acquire,
    Held(&'a GlobalLockGuard),
    Own(&'a InflightLock),
    /// No global lock, for the plan store's sweeps (M4-D24): only `<cache>/plans/<id>.json`
    /// files whose `expires_at` (read here, bounded by `PLAN_MAX_BYTES`) is not after
    /// `now`, and `<id>.lease` files of such plans, or of plans already gone, that fsx takes
    /// itself. Any other victim refuses the whole call with `scope_denied` before anything
    /// moves.
    Expired { now: Timestamp },
}
```

- **Pairing, both ways:** `PlanExpiry` with a lock mode other than `Expired`, or `Expired` with a reason other than `PlanExpiry`, is `scope_denied` ("plan victims are pruned only as expired, without the global lock"). **Decided while writing this bead:** this makes "nothing unexpired is ever evicted" structural: no caller can delete a plan file under the global lock without the expiry check.
- **Validation, after `classify` and before any rename:**
  - `Kind::Plan`: a bounded read (`std::fs::File::open`; `metadata().len() > PLAN_MAX_BYTES` → refuse; `take(PLAN_MAX_BYTES + 1)`), then decode only `expires_at` with a private `#[derive(Deserialize)] struct Expiry { expires_at: jiff::Timestamp }` (other keys ignored). Unreadable, oversized, without a valid `expires_at`, or `expires_at > now` → `scope_denied` "refusing to prune <path>: not an expired plan".
  - `Kind::PlanLease` `<id>.lease`: its sibling `<id>.json` must be a `Kind::Plan` victim of this call that passed the check, or not exist. **Decided while writing this bead:** an orphan lease (no plan of that id) is admitted, because a crash between a sweep's two renames, or a lease an applier creates just after its plan was swept, would otherwise stay forever; it guards nothing, since no plan of that id exists or will ever be created again (ids are fresh ULIDs). Then fsx takes it with `Lease::try_acquire`; held → `scope_denied` "refusing to prune <path>: a held lease is never unlinked". The guards live until every victim of the call is in trash.
  - any other kind → `scope_denied`.
- **No global lock, and no foreign trash:** `Expired` takes no lock. As under `Own`, it never sweeps trash it did not fill (that sweep needs the global lock): the condition at `:200-205` becomes "the call is `Acquire` or `Held`". It deletes its own trash entries as every prune does.
- **Why this is safe without the global lock:** `apply` reads its plan once under its lease and refuses an expired plan itself, so deleting an expired plan races with nothing that matters; a lease is taken by fsx before it moves, so an applier is never left holding a lock on a deleted path.

**What not to do:** do not make `Expired` skip a held lease instead of refusing (the refusal is the tested contract; the store's sweep makes one call per plan so a refusal costs only that pair); do not read more than `PLAN_MAX_BYTES + 1` bytes; do not follow a symlink; do not take the global lock.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `Paths::plans_dir()` is `<cache>/plans`, with `plan`, `plan_lease` and `plans_lock` under it, and `every_documented_path` pins all four.
- [ ] prune deletes `<cache>/plans/<id>.json` and `<cache>/plans/<id>.lease` only for `PlanExpiry` under `LockUse::Expired`, with writer `Derived`, through `<cache>/trash/`; a `<state>/plans/` victim and `.lock` are refused for every reason.
- [ ] `LockUse::Expired` deletes an expired plan, an expired plan with its free lease, and an orphan free lease, without taking the global lock (it completes while another holder has it), and refuses with `scope_denied`, before anything moves, an unexpired plan, an unreadable, truncated or oversized plan, a plan without `expires_at`, a held lease (of an expired plan or orphaned), `.lock`, a blob, a record file, a journal and an in-flight lock.
- [ ] `PlanExpiry` under `Acquire`, `Held` or `Own`, and `Expired` with another reason, are `scope_denied`; an `Expired` call leaves trash it did not fill in place.
- [ ] `Lease::acquire` creates a missing lease file (0600) and reuses an existing one, writes its holder line, waits at most its timeout and then returns `Busy` with the holder; `try_acquire` returns `None` while it is held; a killed holder frees it; a path outside the cache or a symlinked lease file is `Refused` with nothing created.
- [ ] `PLAN_MAX_BYTES` (256 KiB) is in `limits::REGISTRY` and `LIMIT_NAMES`, and the `limit_registries` snapshot is re-accepted.
- [ ] `no_code_path_truncates_renames_or_unlinks_the_lock_file` still passes; no behaviour of any command changes (every existing test passes).
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

- **`src/state/paths.rs`**, `every_documented_path`: the four rows above (and no `/s/omaddons/plans` row).
- **`src/fsx/prune.rs`** (the module's `fixture()`, with a file helper that writes plan JSON `{"schema_version":"1.0","plan_id":"<id>","expires_at":"<t>"}`):
  - `every_reason_reaches_only_its_locations`: replace the state plans row with `(cache.join("plans").join(format!("{TX}.json")), PruneReason::PlanExpiry)` and add `(cache.join("plans").join(format!("{TX}.lease")), PruneReason::PlanExpiry)`; the test calls `classify` only, so the pairing rule does not apply to it.
  - `the_state_plans_dir_is_not_prunable`: `<state>/plans/<TX>.json` for every reason and every lock mode → `scope_denied`, the file kept.
  - `expired_admits_only_expired_plans_and_free_leases`, table, `now = 2026-10-24T12:00:00Z`, each row a fresh store and one prune call: `expired plan` (expires 11:00) → removed; `expired plan with its free lease` → both removed; `plan expiring exactly now` → removed; `unexpired plan` (13:00) → refused; `plan without expires_at` → refused; `truncated plan` (`{"plan_id":`) → refused; `oversized plan` (`PLAN_MAX_BYTES + 1` bytes) → refused; `expired plan with a held lease` (the test holds it with `Lease::acquire`) → refused, both kept; `orphan free lease` → removed; `orphan held lease` → refused; `.lock` → refused; `a blob`, `a target record`, `a journal`, `a cache in-flight lock` → refused; `an expired plan beside an unexpired one in one call` → refused, both kept. Each refusal asserts `ErrorCode::ScopeDenied`, the message, and that every victim of the call still exists. Messages show the row name and the report.
  - `plan_expiry_pairs_only_with_expired`: an expired plan under `Acquire`, `Held(&guard)` and `Own(&lock)` → `scope_denied`; a blob under `Expired` with `Retention` → `scope_denied`.
  - `expired_takes_no_global_lock`: another guard holds the global lock; an `Expired` call on an expired plan returns within 1 s and removes it.
  - `expired_leaves_foreign_trash_alone`: a planted `<cache>/trash/01OLDPRUNE-0-crashed` survives an `Expired` call, and the next `Acquire` call sweeps it (as `leftovers_in_trash_are_swept` does).
- **`src/fsx/lock.rs`**:
  - `a_lease_is_created_and_reused`: `acquire` on a missing file creates it with mode 0600 and a holder line naming this pid and the command; after `release`, a second `acquire` reuses the same inode (`std::os::unix::fs::MetadataExt::ino`).
  - `a_held_lease_times_out_with_its_holder`: hold it, `acquire` with a 50 ms timeout from a second open (another thread) → `Busy { holder: Some(h), waited ≥ 50 ms }` with `h.pid == std::process::id()`.
  - `try_acquire_returns_none_while_held`.
  - `a_lease_holder_that_dies_frees_it`: an `#[ignore]`d child test holds a lease and touches a ready file; the parent sees `try_acquire` → `None`, kills the child, then `Some` (`freed()` polling, as the existing death test).
  - `a_lease_outside_the_cache_is_refused`: rows `<state>/x.lock`, the global lock file path, a relative path, a path with `..`, a symlink at the lease path → `Refused`, and nothing created (the symlink's target untouched).
  - the existing `no_code_path_truncates_renames_or_unlinks_the_lock_file` unchanged.
- **`src/limits.rs`**: `LIMIT_NAMES` gains `PLAN_MAX_BYTES`; the snapshot re-accepted after reviewing that the diff is that one row.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

None in this subtask: no command uses the new code yet. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4.7 crashes a real sweep at `fsx.prune.renamed` and runs concurrent dry runs against the admission lease.

### Logging

Unit tests only: one name per row; each assertion message is `"<row>: expected <outcome>, got <result>; victims now <listing>"`.

## Considerations

- **Hot spot `src/fsx/`** (E13 first, G3 last; E3, D4 and B3 touch separate functions): this subtask touches `prune.rs`'s `LockUse`, `classify`/`location`/`Kind` and the trash-sweep condition, and `lock.rs`'s new type only. Rebase before the gate.
- **A lease is not the global lock:** the global lock's file is immutable and never pruned; a lease file may be pruned, but only by fsx while fsx itself holds it, which is what "a held lease is never unlinked" needs.
- **What could go wrong:** taking the lease in validation and then dropping it before the rename would reopen the race; keep the guards until every rename of the call is done. Reading `expires_at` with the full `StoredPlan` type here would make fsx depend on `app`; the private `Expiry` struct keeps fsx independent.
- **Compatibility:** nothing older reads `<cache>/plans/`; the M3 build's prune points at `<state>/plans/`, which never holds anything.

## Dependencies

Parent: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4 (The plan store).

- **Before it:** none; it starts at once, in parallel with omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4.2 and omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4.3 (different files).
- **After it:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4.4 (the plan store) uses `Paths::plans_dir`, `Lease` and `LockUse::Expired`; D5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`, `omaddons apply`) uses `Lease` for its plan lease.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `Paths::plans_dir()` is `<cache>/plans`, with `plan`, `plan_lease` and `plans_lock` under it, and `every_documented_path` pins all four.
- [ ] prune deletes `<cache>/plans/<id>.json` and `<cache>/plans/<id>.lease` only for `PlanExpiry` under `LockUse::Expired`, with writer `Derived`, through `<cache>/trash/`; a `<state>/plans/` victim and `.lock` are refused for every reason.
- [ ] `LockUse::Expired` deletes an expired plan, an expired plan with its free lease, and an orphan free lease, without taking the global lock (it completes while another holder has it), and refuses with `scope_denied`, before anything moves, an unexpired plan, an unreadable, truncated or oversized plan, a plan without `expires_at`, a held lease (of an expired plan or orphaned), `.lock`, a blob, a record file, a journal and an in-flight lock.
- [ ] `PlanExpiry` under `Acquire`, `Held` or `Own`, and `Expired` with another reason, are `scope_denied`; an `Expired` call leaves trash it did not fill in place.
- [ ] `Lease::acquire` creates a missing lease file (0600) and reuses an existing one, writes its holder line, waits at most its timeout and then returns `Busy` with the holder; `try_acquire` returns `None` while it is held; a killed holder frees it; a path outside the cache or a symlinked lease file is `Refused` with nothing created.
- [ ] `PLAN_MAX_BYTES` (256 KiB) is in `limits::REGISTRY` and `LIMIT_NAMES`, and the `limit_registries` snapshot is re-accepted.
- [ ] `no_code_path_truncates_renames_or_unlinks_the_lock_file` still passes; no behaviour of any command changes (every existing test passes).
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files.

**Done (part 1 of D4): the plan store's filesystem layer.** No command uses it yet, so no command's behaviour changes.

**What landed.**
- **Paths.** `src/state/paths.rs`:
  - `plans_dir()` is now `<cache>/plans`, documented as derived data that a dry run never writes to `<state>`.
  - `plan(&id)` is unchanged under it.
  - New: `plan_lease(&id)` (`<id>.lease`) and `plans_lock()` (`.lock`).
  - `every_documented_path` pins all four under `/k/omaddons/plans`, and the `/s/omaddons/plans` rows are gone.
- **prune** (`src/fsx/prune.rs`):
  - `PruneReason::PlanExpiry`'s writer is `Derived`.
  - The state branch's `plans` arm is deleted. The cache branch knows `plans/<PlanId>.json` (`Kind::Plan`) and `plans/<PlanId>.lease` (new `Kind::PlanLease`), both through `<cache>/trash`; anything else under `plans/`, `.lock` included, is no prunable location.
  - **`LockUse::Expired { now }`:** `PlanExpiry` pairs only with `Expired`, and `Expired` only with `PlanExpiry`; any other pairing is `scope_denied` before anything is read.
  - **Before anything moves**, every victim must pass:
    - a plan: a regular file, read without following a symlink and at most `PLAN_MAX_BYTES`, of which only `expires_at` is decoded (a private `Expiry` struct), and that is not after `now`;
    - a lease: its plan is a victim of the same call or does not exist; fsx then takes it with `Lease::try_acquire`, and a held lease refuses the call.
  - The lease guards live until the call returns.
  - `Expired` takes no global lock, and it sweeps no trash it did not fill (the sweep condition is now "`Acquire` or `Held`").
- **`fsx::lock::Lease`, `LeaseGuard` and `LeaseError`** (exported from `fsx`):
  - `acquire` (polling, the pause doubling from 5 to 50 ms, then `Busy {holder, waited}`), `try_acquire` and `holder`.
  - The location check runs before any directory is created or file opened: an absolute normalized path, its parent canonicalized through its deepest existing ancestor and under the canonical cache dir, and the `Derived` scope check.
  - The parent is created by `ensure_dir_all` in an untracked `Derived` session.
  - The file is opened `RDWR | CREATE | NOFOLLOW | CLOEXEC` with mode 0600 and never truncated away; `ELOOP` is `Refused`. After locking, the holder line is rewritten through the handle (`write_holder`).
  - `lock.rs` still uses no `.truncate(true)`, `remove_file`, `rename(`, `rename_with` or `prune(`.
- **`PLAN_MAX_BYTES`** (256 KiB) in `src/limits.rs`, with its `REGISTRY` row and its `LIMIT_NAMES` entry. The `limit_registries` snapshot was re-accepted; the diff is that one row.

**Tests (unit).**
- `src/fsx/prune.rs`:
  - `every_reason_reaches_only_its_locations` (the two cache plan rows);
  - `the_state_plans_dir_is_not_prunable` (6 reasons × 4 lock modes);
  - `expired_admits_only_expired_plans_and_free_leases` (17 rows, the bead's 16 plus "the lease of a plan not pruned with it");
  - `plan_expiry_pairs_only_with_expired`, `expired_takes_no_global_lock` and `expired_leaves_foreign_trash_alone`.
- `src/fsx/lock.rs`:
  - `a_lease_is_created_and_reused` (0600, holder line, same inode);
  - `a_held_lease_times_out_with_its_holder` (from another thread, `waited ≥ 50 ms`);
  - `try_acquire_returns_none_while_held`;
  - `a_lease_holder_that_dies_frees_it` (child `child_holds_a_lease`);
  - `a_lease_outside_the_cache_is_refused` (6 rows; nothing created, and a link's target is untouched);
  - `no_code_path_truncates_renames_or_unlinks_the_lock_file`, unchanged and passing.
- `src/state/paths.rs`: `every_documented_path`.

**Decided:**
- **`Lease::holder` reads at most `PLAN_MAX_BYTES`, without following a symlink** (common rule 15). A lease is a plan-store file, so no new constant was added; the constant's note says reads stop past it.
- **The lease's parent is canonicalized leniently, as `prune`'s `classify` does.** A symlinked `~/.cache` works; a `plans/` linked out of the cache is refused.
- **A lease path that is not a regular file** (a FIFO, a device) is `Refused`.
- **`LeaseError` implements `Display`**, because prune's refusal embeds it.
- **A lease whose plan exists but is not a victim of the call is refused** ("its plan is not pruned with it"). This is the bead's rule ("must be a victim of this call, or not exist"), now with a row of its own.
- **The pairing check runs first.** A mismatched reason and lock mode is refused before any victim is classified.
- **Test assertions compare `Option`s instead of calling `panic!`.** `ubs` counts `panic!` in `src/` as critical, tests included.

**Corrected facts:** none. Every line the bead cites matched at `3d7d9be`.

**Wire names:**
- `capabilities.limits` (A4, once it lands) gains `PLAN_MAX_BYTES`, `{bytes: 262144}`.
- New files `<cache>/plans/<id>.json`, `<id>.lease` and `.lock`, which no command writes yet.
- No code, key or action changed.

**Evidence:** `argc gate` passed: 2,758 Rust tests passed, 0 failed, 81 ignored; the widget bun and argv steps passed (QML skipped, nothing under `omarchy/` changed); `ubs` 0 critical on the changed files; cargo deny skipped (no dependency change).

title: `StoredIntent`: the typed, normalized intent of the eleven storable commands, its validation and its `display_argv`
description:
Part 2 of 7 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4 (The plan store). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

D4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`, the plan store) makes every storable `--dry-run` store what it showed, so that `omaddons apply <plan_id>` (D5, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`) can execute exactly that later. What a stored plan executes is decided by **M4-D23**: a plan holds a **`StoredIntent`**, "a versioned enum with exactly one variant per storable command (`install`, `update`, `pin`, `unpin`, `adopt`, `sync`, `copy`, `remove`, `undo`, `backup restore`, `backup prune`), each holding that command's normalized arguments. The preview normalizes once: every path is made absolute, every target selector is resolved to its key (or its provisional id while unregistered), and every effective safety option (`--while-running`, `--force`, `--no-deps`, the channel) is recorded as a typed field. A `display_argv` is derived from the intent for people and history; it is documentation and is never parsed or dispatched." *Why:* the commit runs offline from an in-memory plan whose working parts are not serializable, so `apply` re-plans bound to the stored token; a typed intent makes the cache format independent of the CLI parser, and an edited plan file can no longer name an unsupported or recursive command, because the enum has no such variant; normalizing at preview makes the plan independent of where it was made (deleting an unrelated working directory should not invalidate an approval). *Rejected:* storing an argv and re-dispatching it through `Cli::try_parse_from` (the parser becomes a storage format, and decoding proves nothing about whether command, argv, token and parts agree); serializing `TargetPlan.work`.

This subtask writes the intent: its types, its decoding rules (it decodes only what agrees with itself), its validation, `display_argv`, and `from_args`. It is its own step because it is pure data (`src/app/intent.rs`, plus `Deserialize` on D1's `TargetRef` if missing), has no caller until omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4.5 and omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4.6, and can be written and unit-tested in parallel with omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4.1 and omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4.3. The whole enum lands at once: a plan format whose enum grows later would be rewritten under its readers.

**Facts this subtask relies on** (verified at `c0ab5e9`; D1 adds the noted items before this leaf starts):

- The storable commands' clap arguments: `InstallArgs` (`src/app/install.rs:51-91`: `refs`, `channel` ∈ {stable, beta, alpha}, `version`, `file: Option<PathBuf>`, `reinstall`, `no_deps`, `force`, `strict`, `refresh`, `any_flavor`, `no_any_flavor`); `UpdateArgs` (`src/app/update.rs:40-60`: `addons`, `all`, `channel`, `refresh`, `strict`, `no_deps`); `PinArgs { addon, version }` and `UnpinArgs { addon }` (`src/app/pin.rs:33-48`); `AdoptArgs` (`src/app/adopt.rs:58-75`: `folders`, `apply`, `ref`, `no_verify`, `refresh`); `SyncArgs` (`src/app/sync.rs:44-61`: `file`, `strict`, `no_deps`, `locked`, `prune`); `CopyArgs` (`src/app/copy.rs:37-55`: `from`, `to`, `addons`, `strict`, `no_deps`); `RemoveArgs { addons }` (`src/app/remove.rs:36-40`); `UndoArgs` (`src/app/undo.rs:36-56`: `tx`, `last_by`, `run`, `saved_variables` ∈ {auto, restore, keep}); `BackupRestoreArgs { id, addon }` and `BackupPruneArgs { ids, keep, older_than }` (`src/app/backup.rs:181-189`, `:245-256`). The global `--while-running` and `-t` are `Context.while_running` and `Context.target` (`src/cli.rs`).
- `update --all` together with addon names is a usage error, and bare `update` is `update --all` (`tests/update.rs:251-260` asserts their dry runs' `data` are equal).
- The process working directory is read for `install`'s refs and `--file` (`src/app/install.rs:408-409`), `adopt --ref` (`src/app/adopt/apply.rs:125`) and `sync <FILE>` (`src/app/sync.rs:386-394`, which falls back to `world.paths.addons_toml()`). A path selector of `-t` is canonicalized by `discover::registry::resolve` (`src/discover/registry.rs:652`).
- `sources::refs::ParsedRef { ref, version_hint, asset_hint, matched_by, catalog_variants }` with `MatchKind` ∈ {canonical, url, path, installed, catalog, shorthand} (`src/sources/refs.rs:18-42`); a bare name is an installed addon, a catalog name or alias, or a local entry of the working directory (`:501-561`); a catalog name with variants is resolved per client (M3-D16, `catalog_variants`).
- `Channel` (`src/model.rs:397-402`), `SvPolicy` (`src/engine/undo.rs:80-83`), `TxId`, `RunId`, `BackupId` (`src/model.rs:280-303`) derive `Serialize` and `Deserialize`; `TargetKey` too.
- D1 adds `model::TargetRef { Key(TargetKey), Provisional(String) }`, displayed and serialized as the plain string, ordered keys first, with `TargetRef::of(key, id)`; D1 specifies that it deserializes a key's canonical display as `Key` and anything else as `Provisional`. If it shipped without `Deserialize` or `JsonSchema`, this subtask adds them.
- `std::path::absolute` keeps `..` components on Unix; `Path::components()` drops `.` components and trailing slashes.

## Technical Approach

`src/app/intent.rs` (new; `pub mod intent;` in `src/app/mod.rs`). Every struct derives `Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema` and carries `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]`; an internally tagged enum's own attribute does not reach a variant's fields, so each variant struct must carry it.

### 1. The enum

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
#[serde(tag = "command", rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum StoredIntent {
    Install(InstallIntent), Update(UpdateIntent), Pin(PinIntent), Unpin(PinIntent),
    Adopt(AdoptIntent), Sync(SyncIntent), Copy(CopyIntent), Remove(RemoveIntent),
    Undo(UndoIntent), BackupRestore(RestoreIntent), BackupPrune(PruneIntent),
}
impl StoredIntent {
    /// The eleven storable command paths with their widget `destructive` flag.
    pub const PATHS: [(&'static str, bool); 11] = [("install", false), ("update", false), ("pin", false),
        ("unpin", false), ("adopt", false), ("sync", false), ("copy", false), ("remove", true),
        ("undo", true), ("backup restore", true), ("backup prune", true)];
    pub fn command_path(&self) -> &'static str;
    pub fn destructive(&self) -> bool;
    pub fn display_argv(&self) -> Vec<String>;
    pub fn validate(&self) -> Result<(), String>;
    pub fn approval_flags(&self) -> crate::app::approval::ApprovalFlags;   // once omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4.3 landed
    pub fn inputs(&self) -> Vec<&AbsPath>;
    pub fn from_args(ctx: &Context, args: &StorableArgs<'_>) -> Result<StoredIntent>;
}
```

- The tags are the plan's (`rename_all = "snake_case"`): `install`, `update`, `pin`, `unpin`, `adopt`, `sync`, `copy`, `remove`, `undo`, `backup_restore`, `backup_prune`. `command_path()` gives the canonical path (`"backup restore"`) for everything that needs it; nothing ever uses the tag as a path. A tag this build does not know (`"command":"auth"`, `"apply"`, `"doctor"`) fails to decode, which is the point.
- `inputs()`: the absolute inputs D5's `input_missing` check looks for (install's `file`, a `file:` ref's path, sync's `file`).
- `approval_flags()`: `{reinstall, force, while_running, destructive}` from the variant (false where the variant has no such field). If omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4.3 has not landed when this subtask lands, add it there instead (whichever lands second wires it).

### 2. Building blocks

- **`AbsPath`** (`#[serde(try_from = "String", into = "String")]`, `JsonSchema` as a string): decodes only a UTF-8 path that is absolute, contains no `..`, no `.` and no trailing slash, and equals `components().collect::<PathBuf>()` of itself. `AbsPath::resolve(cwd: &Path, input: &Path) -> Result<AbsPath, String>`: `std::path::absolute(cwd.join(input))`; if a `..` remains, `std::fs::canonicalize` of it (the input exists at preview; a missing one already failed the dry run); then the lexical form; a non-UTF-8 result is an error "this path cannot be stored in a plan".
- **`NormalizedRef`** (`#[serde(try_from = "String", into = "String")]`): one ref-like argument stored as the plain string a person would type. It decodes only as one of: a canonical ref whose prefix is a known `RefKind` (`gh:`, `git:`, `url:`, `wowi:`, `tukui:`, `wowace:`, `cf:`, `wago:`) and which `Ref::from_str` accepts; `file:<AbsPath>`; an `https://` URL; a bare name (non-empty, no `/`, not starting with `.`, `~` or `-`, no ASCII control character). `NormalizedRef::from_parsed(request: &str, parsed: &ParsedRef) -> NormalizedRef`, by `matched_by`:
  - `Path` → `file:<absolute path of parsed.ref>`;
  - `Canonical` with a `Ref::File` → `file:<absolute>`; any other `Canonical` → `request.trim()`;
  - `Shorthand` (`owner/repo`) → `parsed.ref.to_string()` (`gh:owner/repo`);
  - `Url` → `request.trim()` (keeps a pasted release link's version and asset hints);
  - `Catalog`, `Installed` → `request.trim()`.
  **Decided while writing this bead:** a catalog name or alias stays the name the user typed, rather than becoming the ref of the preview's default variant, because each client resolves its own variant at plan time (M3-D16): a replaced name would install something else on a client whose variant differs. A catalog edit between preview and `apply` changes the token's `selection` (stale, never different). This is this leaf's reading of the plan's "catalog names as resolved names".
- **`IntentTarget { target: TargetRef, target_id: String }`**: the key (or provisional id) the preview resolved, and the id it had then. **Decided while writing this bead:** `target_id` is stored for `display_argv` only (A.3's own example shows `-t era`, which the key cannot give, and `display_argv` is derived from the intent alone); execution uses `target`.
- **`TargetScope { all: bool, selector: Option<String>, targets: Vec<IntentTarget> }`**, for `update`, `pin`, `unpin`, `adopt`, `sync` and `backup prune`: `all` when `-t` was absent (or `-t all` once C2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.2`, has landed); `selector` is `-t` as typed, a path selector (one containing `/`, or `.` or `..`) canonicalized, `None` exactly when `all`; `targets` is every target the preview selected (`World::select_many`), sorted by `target_id`, unique by `target`. **Decided while writing this bead, as the contract D5 executes:** `apply` selects exactly `targets` (one as `-t <key>`, several through a key-set restriction of the selection), never re-resolving `selector`; `all` and `selector` only shape `display_argv`. A client discovered after the preview is never touched by `apply` of a plan that did not show it.
- **`UndoSelection`** (`#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]` enum, externally tagged): `{"tx": "<TxId>"}` or `{"run": "<RunId>"}`.

### 3. The variants

| Struct | Fields, in `display_argv` order | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `InstallIntent` | `refs: Vec<NormalizedRef>`, `target: TargetRef`, `target_id: String`, `channel: Option<Channel>`, `version: Option<String>`, `file: Option<AbsPath>`, `reinstall`, `no_deps`, `force`, `strict`, `refresh`, `any_flavor`, `no_any_flavor`, `while_running` | `target` is the client `install` chose (`-t`, the default, or its probe's one client) |
| `UpdateIntent` | `addons: Vec<String>`, `scope: TargetScope`, `channel: Option<Channel>`, `refresh`, `strict`, `no_deps`, `while_running` | no `all`: bare `update` and `update --all` are one intent |
| `PinIntent` | `addon: String`, `scope`, `version: Option<String>`, `while_running` | shared by `pin` and `unpin`; an `unpin` with a `version` fails `validate` |
| `AdoptIntent` | `folders: Vec<String>`, `apply: bool`, `ref: Option<NormalizedRef>` (`#[serde(rename = "ref")] pub r#ref`), `scope`, `no_verify`, `refresh`, `while_running` | must adopt: `apply`, a folder or a ref |
| `SyncIntent` | `file: AbsPath`, `default_file: bool`, `scope`, `strict`, `no_deps`, `locked`, `prune`, `while_running` | the file the dry run read |
| `CopyIntent` | `from: TargetRef`, `from_id: String`, `to: TargetRef`, `to_id: String`, `addons: Vec<String>`, `strict`, `no_deps`, `while_running` | sides differ |
| `RemoveIntent` | `addons: Vec<String>`, `target`, `target_id`, `while_running` | the one target `remove` settled on |
| `UndoIntent` | `selection: UndoSelection`, `saved_variables: Option<SvPolicy>`, `while_running` | the transaction or run the dry run reverted |
| `RestoreIntent` | `backup: BackupId`, `target`, `target_id`, `addons: Vec<String>` | the full id and its owning target |
| `PruneIntent` | `ids: Vec<BackupId>`, `keep: Option<u64>`, `older_than: Option<Timestamp>`, `scope` | full ids; the absolute cutoff |

- **Decided while writing this bead:** every option the command's `Args` has is recorded, beyond the plan's `InstallIntent` example (which lacks `strict`, `refresh`, `any_flavor` and `no_any_flavor`): `strict` changes the exit code, `any_flavor`/`no_any_flavor` change what is installed and recorded, and `refresh` is part of what was asked.
- **Decided while writing this bead:** `while_running` is recorded where the command reads it, so not on `RestoreIntent` (a restore refuses while the client runs whatever the flag) or `PruneIntent` (prune never asks).
- **Decided while writing this bead:** relative inputs are resolved to what the preview used: bare `undo`, `undo -t <id>` and `undo --last-by <actor>` to `{"run": …}` when the dry run reverted a run (`UndoData.reverted_run`) else to the one `{"tx": …}`; id prefixes to full ids; `--older-than 30d` to the absolute cutoff the dry run computed (`backup.rs:2289-2293`). "Most recent", a prefix or an age would mean something else when `apply` runs.
- Never in an intent: `--dry-run`, `--if-match`, `--actor`, `--reason` (top-level plan fields), `--offline` (`apply`'s own), presentation flags.

### 4. `validate()`

Rules decoding cannot express, each failure a `String` naming the rule (the store maps it to `plan_not_found` `unreadable`):

- install: `file` set ⇒ exactly one ref; `refs` non-empty;
- update: no rule beyond the scope's;
- pin/unpin: `addon` non-empty; `unpin` ⇒ `version` is `None`;
- adopt: `apply || !folders.is_empty() || ref.is_some()`; `apply` ⇒ `folders` empty (clap's rule);
- copy: `from != to`;
- remove: `addons` non-empty;
- prune: `ids` non-empty ⇒ `keep` and `older_than` are `None`;
- every `TargetScope`: `all == selector.is_none()`, `targets` non-empty, sorted by `target_id`, unique by `target`;
- every `Vec<String>` of names: no empty element.

### 5. `display_argv()`

`["omaddons", <path words>, <positionals>, <targets>, <the command's own flags in clap declaration order>, "--while-running"?]`:

- install: `install <refs…> -t <target_id> [--channel C] [--version V] [--file F] [--reinstall] [--no-deps] [--force] [--strict] [--refresh] [--any-flavor] [--no-any-flavor]` (A.3: `["omaddons","install","weakauras","dbm","-t","era"]`);
- update: `update [<addons…>] [-t T] [--channel C] [--refresh] [--strict] [--no-deps]`;
- pin: `pin <addon> [-t T] [--version V]`; unpin: `unpin <addon> [-t T]`;
- adopt: `adopt [<folders…>] [--apply] [--ref R] [-t T] [--no-verify] [--refresh]`;
- sync: `sync [<file>] [-t T] [--strict] [--no-deps] [--locked] [--prune]` (no file when `default_file`);
- copy: `copy [<addons…>] --from <from_id> --to <to_id> [--strict] [--no-deps]`;
- remove: `remove <addons…> -t <target_id>`;
- undo: `undo <tx>` or `undo --run <run>`, `[--saved-variables P]`;
- backup restore: `backup restore <backup> -t <target_id> [--addon A]…`;
- backup prune: `backup prune [<ids…>] [--keep N] [--older-than <RFC 3339>] [-t T]`.

`-t T` for a scope: none when `all`; `-t <target_id>` when it has one target; `-t <selector>` when several. If any positional starts with `-`, the positionals move to the end, after `--`. It never contains `--dry-run`, `--if-match` or a presentation flag. It must parse back (§Test Plan).

### 6. `from_args`

```rust
pub enum StorableArgs<'a> {
    Install { args: &'a InstallArgs, target: IntentTarget, refs: Vec<NormalizedRef>, file: Option<AbsPath> },
    Update { args: &'a UpdateArgs, scope: TargetScope },
    Pin { args: &'a PinArgs, scope: TargetScope },
    Unpin { args: &'a UnpinArgs, scope: TargetScope },
    Adopt { args: &'a AdoptArgs, scope: TargetScope, r#ref: Option<NormalizedRef> },
    Sync { args: &'a SyncArgs, scope: TargetScope, file: AbsPath, default_file: bool },
    Copy { args: &'a CopyArgs, from: IntentTarget, to: IntentTarget },
    Remove { args: &'a RemoveArgs, target: IntentTarget },
    Undo { args: &'a UndoArgs, selection: UndoSelection },
    BackupRestore { args: &'a BackupRestoreArgs, backup: BackupId, target: IntentTarget },
    BackupPrune { args: &'a BackupPruneArgs, ids: Vec<BackupId>, older_than: Option<Timestamp>, scope: TargetScope },
}
```

`from_args(&ctx, &args)` keeps the plan's signature: the clap options come from `args`, `while_running` from `ctx.while_running`, the channel and saved-variables strings are parsed into their enums, and the rest from the resolution each variant carries. The result must pass `validate()`, else `Error::internal("the preview's intent does not validate: <rule>")` (a bug, never a user error). Helpers for the runs: `IntentTarget::of(&Target)`, `TargetScope::of(ctx.target.as_deref(), &selected)` (sorts, normalizes the selector).

**Decided while writing this bead:** the run hands over its own resolution because target keys, provisional ids, parsed refs and backup and undo ids are known only after it resolved them; resolving again in `from_args` could disagree with what the run planned, and the intent must describe the plan its token describes.

**What not to do:** never store `-t` as typed for a single-target command; never parse `display_argv`; never add a variant for a command that is not storable (M4-D22).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `StoredIntent` has exactly the eleven variants, with the tags above, `command_path()`, `destructive()` (true exactly for `remove`, `undo`, `backup restore`, `backup prune`) and `PATHS`.
- [ ] Every variant round-trips through JSON unchanged, and decoding rejects an unknown variant tag, an unknown field in every variant, a relative, non-normalized or `..` path, a bare `a/b` ref, `./x` and tilde-relative refs, and every `validate()` rule's violation.
- [ ] `from_args` builds each variant from its arguments and resolution: paths absolute, single-target commands keyed by `TargetRef` with their `target_id`, multi-target commands with a sorted `TargetScope`, `update --all` equal to bare `update`, undo resolved to a transaction or a run, prune's prefixes and relative age resolved.
- [ ] `display_argv()` gives A.3's install example and the canonical form of every variant, and `Cli::try_parse_from(display_argv())` parses to the same command path; converted back through `from_args` with the same resolution it gives an equal intent.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

In `src/app/intent.rs` (`#[cfg(test)] mod tests`), with a synthetic `Context` (the test helper the app tests use) and fixed ids (`01JB8Q2VA0…`):

- `from_args_builds_each_variant`: one row per command (eleven), each `StorableArgs` value and the expected intent literal; message `"<command>: from_args gave <intent>"`.
- `intents_round_trip_through_json`: every row's intent → `serde_json::to_string` → back, equal; and the JSON of the install row equals A.3's intent shape (`{"command":"install","refs":["weakauras","dbm"],"target":"01M5…","target_id":"era","channel":null,…}`).

Message: `"<row>: decoded <value> but must be rejected"`.
- `normalized_refs_from_each_match_kind`: rows `path ./Foo.zip` (cwd `/w`) → `file:/w/Foo.zip`; `canonical file:./Foo` → `file:/w/Foo`; `shorthand o/r` → `gh:o/r`; `url https://github.com/o/r/releases/tag/v1` → as typed; `canonical gh:o/r` → as typed; `catalog wa` → `wa`; `installed DBM` → `DBM`.

- `display_argv_examples`, table: A.3's install row; update with one target (`-t retail`) and with several (`-t classic`, the selector); pin with `--version`; unpin; `adopt --apply`; `adopt Foo --ref gh:o/foo -t retail`; sync with the default file (no path) and with `/w/addons.toml`; copy; remove; `undo 01JB…`; `undo --run 01JB…` with `--saved-variables keep`; `backup restore <id> -t retail --addon WeakAuras`; `backup prune --older-than 2026-10-01T00:00:00Z -t retail`; a remove of `-weird` (positionals after `--`); every row with and without `--while-running` where the variant has it.

Message shows the argv and both intents.
- `destructive_flags` and `paths_are_the_eleven` (`PATHS` order and flags; every variant's `command_path()` is in `PATHS` once).

### Integration and end-to-end tests

None here: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4.5, omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4.6 and omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4.7 build intents from real runs and read them back from real plan files.

### Logging

Unit tests only: one name per row; messages show the input (args or JSON), the expected value and the actual one.

## Considerations

- **The intent is a stored format** (kind `plan` 1.0, through omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4.4): from the tag `v0.1.0` on, its shape is contract (A10, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.10`, records it once landed). Get names right now; a field added later is a minor version.
- **Bare names re-parse at `apply` with the applier's working directory:** a local entry of the same name there makes the parse ambiguous (`ref_ambiguous`) or different (the token's `selection` differs, `plan_stale`), never a different install. Stated in the leaf's considerations for D5.
- **Hot spot:** none; `src/app/intent.rs` is new. `src/model.rs` changes only if D1's `TargetRef` lacks `Deserialize`/`JsonSchema`.
- **What could go wrong:** forgetting `deny_unknown_fields` on one variant struct would let an edited option through; the per-variant rows of `decoding_rejects_hand_edits` catch it.

## Dependencies

Parent: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4 (The plan store).

- **Before it:** none; it starts at once, in parallel with omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4.1 and omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4.3.
- **After it:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4.4 stores `StoredIntent` in `StoredPlan` and validates it on load; omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4.5 and omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4.6 build intents in the eleven runs; D5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`) executes them.

comments.text:
**Done (part 2 of D4): `StoredIntent`, the typed intent of a stored plan**, in `src/app/intent.rs` (new; `pub mod intent` in `src/app/mod.rs`). It has no caller yet; `…4.4.4`, `…4.4.5` and `…4.4.6` add them.

**What landed.**
- **The enum.** `StoredIntent` has eleven variants, internally tagged by `command` (`install`, `update`, `pin`, `unpin`, `adopt`, `sync`, `copy`, `remove`, `undo`, `backup_restore`, `backup_prune`). Each variant struct carries its own `deny_unknown_fields`.
  - `PATHS` lists the eleven canonical paths with their widget `destructive` flag.
  - `command_path()` gives the canonical path; `destructive()` is true exactly for `remove`, `undo`, `backup restore` and `backup prune`.
  - `inputs()` gives install's `--file`, a `file:` ref's path and the `sync` file.
- **The variant structs**, fields in `display_argv` order, as the bead's table gives them: `InstallIntent`, `UpdateIntent`, `PinIntent` (shared by `pin` and `unpin`), `AdoptIntent` (`ref` on the wire), `SyncIntent`, `CopyIntent`, `RemoveIntent`, `UndoIntent`, `RestoreIntent` and `PruneIntent`.
- **Building blocks.**
  - **`AbsPath`** decodes only an absolute, normalized UTF-8 path (no `..`, no `.`, no trailing or doubled slash, no NUL). `resolve(cwd, input)` canonicalizes only when a `..` remains.
  - **`NormalizedRef`** is one of four forms, serialized as the string:
    - `File(AbsPath)`, written `file:<path>`;
    - a canonical ref, which must parse as a `Ref`;
    - an `https://` link;
    - a bare name: no `/`, and not starting with `.`, `~` or `-`.

    None of them may be padded or hold a control character. `from_parsed` maps each `MatchKind` as the bead says.
  - **`IntentTarget`, `TargetScope`** (`of`, sorted by id and unique by target) and **`UndoSelection`** (`{"tx": …}` or `{"run": …}`).
  - **`StorableArgs`**, the run's resolution, handed to `from_args`.
- **`validate()`** implements the bead's rules plus the few listed under "Decided".
- **`display_argv()`** gives each command's canonical form, and parses back.
- **`from_args(&ctx, &StorableArgs)`** returns `Error::internal` when the result does not validate.

**Tests (unit, `src/app/intent.rs`).** The shared `rows()` holds 18 runs covering all eleven commands, each with its clap args, the intent and the display argv. Over them:
- `from_args_builds_each_variant`, `from_args_refuses_a_resolution_that_does_not_validate` and `intents_round_trip_through_json` (A.3's install shape, tag first);
- `decoding_rejects_hand_edits`: 31 edits, plus an unknown field in every row, asserted rejected for that field itself;
- `normalized_refs_from_each_match_kind`, `abs_path_resolves_and_rejects` and `update_all_and_bare_update_are_one_intent`;
- `display_argv_examples`, every row also with `--while-running` flipped;
- `display_argv_parses_back_to_the_same_intent`: `Cli::try_parse_from`, then `command_name`, then `from_args` gives an equal intent;
- `destructive_flags_and_the_eleven_paths`, `inputs_are_the_local_files` and `a_scope_is_sorted_unique_and_shows_its_selector`.

**Decided:**
- **`NormalizedRef::from_parsed` returns `Result`.** A path holding `..` canonicalizes, and a non-UTF-8 path cannot be stored, so either can fail. A run maps the failure to its own error.
- **`NormalizedRef` is an enum of the four forms**, so `inputs()` reads a `file:` ref's path without parsing strings again.
- **A canonical-prefix string must parse as a `Ref`.** `gh:owner` is rejected, never read as a name.
- **Rules beyond the bead's list:**
  - install takes `--any-flavor` or `--no-any-flavor`, not both (clap's own rule);
  - every single-target id is non-empty, and so are copy's two;
  - a scope's selector is non-empty.

  An undo selection holding both `tx` and `run` fails to decode; that is the externally tagged enum, not `validate()`.
- **`TargetScope::of`:** `-t all` in any case is the keyword unless a selected client is named `all` (`target_id_reserved`). A path selector that cannot be canonicalized keeps its typed form; it is used for display only.
- **`display_argv` writes `--flag=value` for a value that starts with `-`** (an addon named `-x` under `--addon`), so the argv parses back. Positionals that start with `-` go after `--`, as the bead says.
- **`keep` is converted `usize` → `u64`, saturating.**
- **`approval_flags()` is left to `…4.4.3`.** This part landed first, and the bead says the second lander wires it; noted on that bead.

**Corrected facts (HEAD `8906292`):**
- `model::TargetRef` already has `Deserialize` and `JsonSchema`, from D1, so `src/model.rs` is unchanged.
- `BackupRestoreArgs` derives no `Default` (it has a required id).
- The arguments' line numbers moved by one or two since `c0ab5e9`.

**Wire names:**
- A new stored format: the intent's tag values and field names above. It becomes contract when `…4.4.4` writes it inside plan files (kind `plan` 1.0).
- No envelope, code, action or `details` key changed.

**Evidence:** `argc gate` passed: 2,770 Rust tests passed (12 new), 0 failed, 81 ignored; the widget bun and argv steps passed (QML skipped, nothing under `omarchy/` changed); `ubs` 0 critical on the changed files.

title: The typed approval summary: `Approval` from an engine plan, an undo, a restore and a prune
description:
Part 3 of 7 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4 (The plan store). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

D4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`, the plan store) makes every storable `--dry-run` store what it showed, so that `omaddons apply <plan_id>` (D5, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`) can execute exactly that. Every storable dry run also returns, and every stored plan keeps, a **typed approval summary** (**M4-D28**, M4-D24): "the canonical selection (per target: the client's key, the addon's identity, its source and channel, the release id and asset, the from and to versions), the scope (`dependencies_added`, `folders_removed`, `local_changes_replaced`, `source_changed`, the running-client policy), `reasons[]` from a closed set naming each effect that needs a person's eyes, and `routine`, true only when `reasons[]` is empty." The bar widget's Update buttons (G1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1`) apply a plan with no dialog only when its selection equals the row the user pressed and it is routine; an agent applies the same rule; `apply --dry-run` (D5) shows it as `approved`; `plans show` (D9, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.9`) reports it. *Why:* a version match alone does not establish that the row described what the user is about to approve (another source or asset, an added dependency, a removed folder, replaced local edits), and the policy must live in the CLI's typed summary so no client parses human messages. *Rejected:* a version-only match (it auto-applied plans that did more than the row showed); an opaque copy of the dry run's `data` in the plan (no runtime code could validate it: the data types derive `Serialize` and not `Deserialize`).

This subtask writes `src/app/approval.rs`: the types and the functions that compute an approval from an engine plan (seven engine commands and `remove`), an undo, a restore and a prune, plus the one engine change it needs (the asset's file name on `PlannedRelease`). It is its own step because it is pure computation over existing plan types, with its own unit tests per reason, and can be written in parallel with omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4.1 and omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4.2.

**Facts this subtask relies on** (verified at `c0ab5e9`):

- `engine::plan::Plan.targets[TargetPlan]` (`src/engine/plan.rs:481-502`, `TargetPlan` at `:515-543`): `target` (id), `key: Option<TargetKey>`, `changes: Vec<Change>`, `releases: Vec<PlannedRelease>`, `work: Vec<AddonWork>` (`#[serde(skip)]`, pushed together with `changes`, so `changes[i]` and `work[i]` describe one addon: `PlannedAddon::push`, `:3242-3249`), `dependencies: BTreeMap<String, DepReport>` (requester name → what its dependencies came to; `DepReport.installs: Vec<(FolderName, String)>` = (folder required, dependency addon installed), `:552-564`).
- `Change { addon, ref, kind, fields: Vec<EditField>, from_version, to_version, folders: FolderSummary }` (`:618-629`), `ChangeKind` ∈ {install, update, remove, adopt, edit} (`:631-641`), `FolderSummary { added, replaced, removed, skipped, recorded }` (`:645-654`). `EditField` ∈ {channel, pinned, reason, ref, required_by, any_flavor} with `wire()` (`src/engine/edit.rs:85-104`).
- `AddonWork::record()` is the record after the change, `None` when the addon goes (`src/engine/plan.rs:1095-1101`); `FolderWork.local_changes: Option<LocalChanges { paths, count, folders }>` (`:741`, `:750-757`); `RecordsWork.before` (`:1080-1093`).
- `PlannedRelease { release_id, url, expected_hash, blob_sha256 }` (`:672-680`) has no asset name; it is built at `:3862-3881`, where `winner.candidate.asset.filename` (`model::Asset.filename`, `src/model.rs:1158`) is at hand. `tests/plan.rs`'s snapshot serializes `Plan`.
- `AddonRecord { ref, name, version, release_id, channel, … }` (`src/model.rs:575-618`); `Ref::identity()` compares refs (`:785-799`); `SourceId::of(&Ref)` (`src/sources/mod.rs:111`) with lowercase wire names (`github`, `git`, `url`, `local`, `wowi`, `tukui`, `curseforge`, `wago`, `wowace`).
- `resolve::updates::compare_versions(a, b) -> Option<Ordering>` compares dotted numbers and is `None` when either does not parse (`src/resolve/updates.rs:434-444`); "unknown is never older" (`:449`).

## Technical Approach

### 1. Types (`src/app/approval.rs`, new; `pub mod approval;` in `src/app/mod.rs`)

All derive `Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema` with `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` (the approval is stored in the plan file and must decode or fail). Field order is rendering order.

```rust
pub struct Approval {
    pub routine: bool,
    pub reasons: Vec<ApprovalReason>,
    pub selection: Vec<ApprovedItem>,
    pub scope: ApprovalScope,
}
pub struct ApprovedItem {
    pub target_key: Option<TargetKey>,   // null while the target is unregistered
    pub target_id: String,
    pub addon: Option<String>,
    pub source: Option<SourceId>,        // wire name ("github", "tukui", …)
    pub channel: Option<Channel>,
    pub release_id: Option<String>,
    pub asset: Option<String>,           // the downloaded asset's file name
    pub from_version: Option<String>,
    pub to_version: Option<String>,
    pub op: ApprovedOp,
    pub fields: Vec<String>,             // an edit's record fields (EditField::wire), sorted; else []
    pub tx: Option<TxId>,                // undo: the transaction reverted
    pub backup: Option<BackupId>,        // restore, prune: the backup
}
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum ApprovedOp { Install, Update, Remove, Adopt, Edit, Undo, Restore, Prune }
pub struct ApprovalScope {
    pub dependencies_added: Vec<String>,
    pub folders_removed: Vec<String>,
    pub local_changes_replaced: LocalChangesScope,
    pub source_changed: Vec<String>,
    pub while_running: bool,
}
pub struct LocalChangesScope { pub count: u64, pub folders: Vec<String> }
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum ApprovalReason { DependencyAdded, FoldersRemoved, LocalChangesReplaced, SourceChanged,
    ChannelChanged, WhileRunning, Reinstall, Force, Downgrade, Destructive }
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]   // not serialized
pub struct ApprovalFlags { pub reinstall: bool, pub force: bool, pub while_running: bool, pub destructive: bool }
```

`SourceId` already derives `Deserialize` and `JsonSchema` with snake_case wire names (`src/sources/mod.rs:82-96`). **Decided while writing this bead:** the plan's closed sets gain `ApprovedOp`'s `undo`, `restore` and `prune`, the item fields `fields`, `tx` and `backup`, and the reason `destructive`. Without them a `backup prune` or a whole restore would be `routine: true` (no listed reason fits deleting backups or replacing `WTF/`), and a pin, an unpin, an undo, a restore and a prune would have selections that do not say what they change. The widget keeps its dialog for destructive commands anyway (M4-D28); the reason makes the rule hold for agents and future clients too.

### 2. Functions

```rust
impl Approval {
    /// An engine plan's approval: `install`, `update`, `pin`, `unpin`, `adopt`, `sync`, `copy`, `remove`.
    pub fn of_plan(plan: &Plan, before: &BTreeMap<String, TargetRecord>, flags: &ApprovalFlags) -> Approval;
    /// An undo's: one item per transaction reverted; `folders_removed` the folders the undo removes.
    pub fn of_undo(reverted: &[(Option<TargetKey>, String, TxId)], folders_removed: &[FolderName], flags: &ApprovalFlags) -> Approval;
    /// A restore's: one item for a whole restore, one per `--addon` name otherwise.
    pub fn of_restore(target_key: Option<TargetKey>, target_id: &str, backup: BackupId, addons: &[String]) -> Approval;
    /// A prune's: one item per backup it would delete.
    pub fn of_prune(victims: &[(Option<TargetKey>, String, BackupId)]) -> Approval;
    /// A dry run with nothing to do: an empty selection, the flags' reasons.
    pub fn nothing(flags: &ApprovalFlags) -> Approval;
}
```

`before` maps target id → the `TargetRecord` the run loaded (`World::records()`).

**`of_plan`**, for each target plan (sorted by id) and each `(change, work)` pair:

- `target_key = tp.key`, `target_id = tp.target`, `op` from `change.kind`, `addon = Some(change.addon)`, `from_version`, `to_version` from the change, `fields` = `change.fields` wire names, sorted;
- `source = Some(SourceId::of(&change.ref))`;
- `channel`, `release_id` from `work.record()` (the record after); `None` for a remove;
- `asset` = the `PlannedRelease.asset` of `tp.releases` whose `release_id` equals the record's, else `None` (a local directory, an adoption, a records-only change);
- `tx: None`, `backup: None`.

`selection` sorted by `(target_id, addon, op)`.

**Scope** of `of_plan`: `dependencies_added` = every `tp.dependencies[*].installs[*].1`; `folders_removed` = every `change.folders.removed` name; `local_changes_replaced` = `count` summed over `WorkMode::Folders` works' `local_changes`, `folders` their union; `source_changed` = each change on an addon present in `before[tp.target]` whose recorded ref's identity differs from `change.ref`'s; `while_running = flags.while_running`. Every list is sorted and de-duplicated across targets. **Decided while writing this bead:** plain names, as A.2's example shows; the per-target detail is in `selection`.

**Reasons**, each exactly when its effect is present (sorted in declaration order, unique):

| Reason | When |
|---|---|
| `dependency_added` | `scope.dependencies_added` non-empty |
| `folders_removed` | `scope.folders_removed` non-empty |
| `local_changes_replaced` | `scope.local_changes_replaced.count > 0` |
| `source_changed` | `scope.source_changed` non-empty |
| `channel_changed` | an addon present in `before` whose recorded channel differs from its record after |
| `while_running` | `flags.while_running` |
| `reinstall` | `flags.reinstall` |
| `force` | `flags.force` |
| `downgrade` | an item with `compare_versions(to_version, from_version) == Some(Ordering::Less)` |
| `destructive` | `flags.destructive` (`remove`, `undo`, `backup restore`, `backup prune`) |

`routine = reasons.is_empty()`. **Decided while writing this bead:** a version that does not parse as dotted numbers never counts as a downgrade (the existing "unknown is never older" rule), so a git commit hash or a date version never makes an update non-routine by itself.

**`of_undo`:** one item per reverted transaction (`op: undo`, `tx: Some(tx)`, every other field `None`/empty), `folders_removed` from the given folders, reasons from the flags (`destructive` always, for undo) plus `folders_removed`. **`of_restore`:** `addons` empty → one item `{op: restore, backup, addon: None}`; else one per name; reason `destructive`. **`of_prune`:** one item per victim `{op: prune, backup}`; reason `destructive`. **`nothing`:** empty selection and scope, reasons from the flags (so a no-op bound `--while-running` still says so).

### 3. The asset name on `PlannedRelease` (`src/engine/plan.rs`)

`PlannedRelease` gains `#[serde(skip)] pub asset: Option<String>`, set at its build site (`:3876-3881`) to `Some(winner.candidate.asset.filename.clone())`; every other construction sets `None`. **Decided while writing this bead:** `#[serde(skip)]` keeps `tests/plan.rs`'s `plan_dry_run` snapshot unchanged; D1's token `selection` does not use it (it is not part of what binds), so tokens do not change.

### 4. Example (A.2)

```json
{"routine":false,"reasons":["dependency_added"],
 "selection":[{"target_key":"01M5…","target_id":"era","addon":"weakauras","source":"github","channel":"stable",
               "release_id":"gh:…@v5.22.1","asset":"WeakAuras-5.22.1.zip","from_version":null,"to_version":"5.22.1",
               "op":"install","fields":[],"tx":null,"backup":null}],
 "scope":{"dependencies_added":["libdeflate"],"folders_removed":[],"local_changes_replaced":{"count":0,"folders":[]},
          "source_changed":[],"while_running":false}}
```

**What not to do:** never read warning text to decide a reason; never include human messages in an approval; never mark an approval routine when a reason applies.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `Approval`, `ApprovedItem`, `ApprovedOp`, `ApprovalScope`, `LocalChangesScope` and `ApprovalReason` exist with the fields and wire names above, decode with `deny_unknown_fields`, and round-trip.
- [ ] `of_plan` gives each change one item with its target, addon, source, channel, release id, asset, versions, op and edit fields, sorted, and the scope's lists sorted and de-duplicated.
- [ ] Each reason is raised exactly when its effect is present, and `routine` is true exactly when no reason applies; a version that does not parse is never a downgrade.
- [ ] `of_undo`, `of_restore`, `of_prune` and `nothing` give the items and reasons above; every destructive command's approval carries `destructive`.
- [ ] `PlannedRelease.asset` is set at the build site and not serialized (`tests/plan.rs`'s snapshot unchanged).
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

In `src/app/approval.rs`, with a small builder for synthetic `Plan`s (a `TargetPlan` with given changes, works, releases and dependency reports; the engine's test helpers where they exist):

### Integration and end-to-end tests

None here: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4.5, omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4.6 and omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4.7 compare `data.approval` with the stored plan's on real dry runs, including one that adds a dependency.

- **The approval is contract** from the tag on: G1 compares `selection` with its rows and reads `reasons`; D9 shows it; D5 shows it as `approved`. Its names are this leaf's to get right now; additions later are minor-version changes.

A debug assertion `tp.changes.len() == tp.work.len()` in `of_plan` (returning an internal error in release, never panicking) guards it.
