### Checkpoint-only tests

None. Nothing here needs a real machine, a release build or a live probe.

## Considerations

- **Why a performance pin is enough** (M4-D26): `apply` re-plans and `fetch_blob` verifies whatever it downloads against the release's expected hash, so an evicted archive costs time and network, never correctness. That is why every failure in pin discovery may safely pin nothing, and why no warning is needed.
- **The cache can exceed its cap for at most a day per plan.** Pinned archives stay even over `blob_cache_max_bytes`, as installed releases' do today (README already says the cache can exceed the cap). The store's quotas bound how many plans pin (512, 32 MiB of plan files), the `now + PLAN_TTL` rule bounds how long, and a plan dated ahead pins nothing.
- **A hand-edited `releases[]` still pins.** D4's `load` checks the token against its stored parts but does not compare `releases[]` with `parts.selection`, so a plan whose `releases[]` was edited, token untouched, still loads and pins what it names. That can only keep archives, never delete one, and is bounded by the quotas and the 24-hour rule; it is not worth a second consistency check on a read path.
- **Time under the global lock.** Pin discovery runs inside the lock eviction already takes, and only when eviction must delete something. A typical store holds a handful of small plans (well under a millisecond each to load); the worst case is bounded by the quotas (512 files, 32 MiB). The plan accepted this placement ("read under the eviction lock"); if a measurement ever shows it matters, moving the read before the lock is safe, because plan pins exclude no writer.
- **Races, all benign.** A preview that downloads an archive and stores its plan just after pin discovery ran may lose that archive to the same eviction: `apply` downloads it again. A plan deleted by a concurrent sweep while pin discovery reads it fails to load and pins nothing; it was expired. Two sweeps (a commit's and a preview's) serialize on `.lock`, and the loser skips.
- **Multi-target runs** run retention once per committed target, so one command may run several bounded sweeps; the later ones usually find nothing.
- **Compatibility.** The M3 build (`c0ab5e9`) ignores `<cache>/plans/`: its eviction may take a plan's archive (`apply` then downloads it again), and its retention cannot delete plans (its prune knows plans only under `<state>/plans/`). E9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9`, the M3 build against M4 state) characterizes that build against stored plans and leases; nothing here changes the outcome.
- **Privacy.** Plans hold the previewer's argv-derived intent and `--reason`. Pin discovery and the sweep read them and print nothing; the E2E plants no `WTF/`, and its commit steps still check stdout and stderr with `assert_private()`.
- **Hot spots** (§10.5 and the plan's file map):
  - `src/engine/retention.rs` is also changed by E5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`, the repair transaction: retention skips `*.repair` directories in snapshot retention and the orphan sweep) and named for F6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.6`, verified blob reads). This bead changes `run`'s head and tail, adds `RetentionClock` and appends tests; E5 changes the snapshot and orphan filters. Rebase before the gate; keep the edits apart.
  - `src/engine/tx.rs`: one line in `retain` (rule: D2 → D8; E5 touches recovery calls only; G3 last).
  - `src/state/plans.rs` (D4's file; D9 and F3 add readers): append the new items after `sweep`; rebase.
  - `README.md`: only the lines of section 8.
- **What could go wrong in implementation, and how to notice.**
  - *The clock change moves snapshot retention:* the existing retention, undo and restore suites pass unchanged, and `plans_follow_the_plan_clock_and_snapshots_the_system_clock` pins the split.
  - *A sweep or pin error leaks into the commit:* `bad_plans_pin_nothing_and_fail_nothing`, the unlistable-store cases and scenario 5 assert `Ok` and no `retention_failed`.
  - *Pins read outside the lock, or eagerly:* `plan_pins_are_read_inside_eviction_under_the_global_lock` and `no_eviction_reads_no_plan`.
  - *Retention creates the plan store on homes that never previewed:* `a_home_without_a_plan_store_gets_none` and scenario 4's last step.
  - *The E2E's cap affects other assertions:* a 1-byte cap evicts every unpinned archive after every commit, which is what scenarios 1, 2 and 5 rely on; the other scenarios run with the default cap.
- **Why size S, with no subtasks.** One small read path (pin discovery), one call (the sweep D4 already wrote), one clock split, one README edit, and their tests: one commit that passes the gate. The E2E suite belongs in the same commit because it is the proof of the leaf's three acceptance criteria.
- **Decided while writing this bead, collected** (confirm or adjust each in the close comment): the plan clock and `RetentionClock` with `impl Into`; the `now + PLAN_TTL` ceiling; the two read bounds and newest-first order; full `load`; no early stop; hex-only pins; the sweep first, skipped when the store is absent; no warning and the four internal report fields; the suite's own file; the `--if-match` form of the local-zip proof with the `apply` forms here or in a follow-up; the expected `["selection", "observed"]`; the README wording.

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M4 plan, 2026-10-24).**

**Why this bead.** D4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`, the plan store) stores every storable preview as a plan for 24 hours, and the plan's `releases[]` name the archives the dry run downloaded and verified. Today blob eviction, which runs after every commit, spares only the archives of installed releases, so any commit between a preview and its `apply` can evict the archive the approval is waiting for, and the approval then downloads it again. On a cache near its 1 GiB cap that happens to every approval, and the widget's "preview, then apply with no dialog" (G1) turns into a second download. Separately, only previews sweep expired plans; a store whose previews stop keeps them until the next one. This bead makes eviction spare every unexpired plan's archives (read under the lock eviction already takes, bounded by the store's own quotas) and makes retention run D4's bounded sweep after every commit. It also proves, with a test, that a local zip named by a plan is hashed again when the plan is carried out, so an edited archive can never be installed under the old approval. It keeps the thesis true in a small but visible place: the cache omaddons owns stays bounded without a daemon, and an approval the user may still act on is never deleted to make room.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M4-D26:** unexpired plans pin `releases[].blob_sha256`, read under the eviction lock, bounded by the quotas; an unreadable or oversized plan pins nothing; the pin is a performance pin (an evicted archive is downloaded and verified again), and local zips are re-hashed at `apply`.
- **M4-D24:** "retention sweeps too, after each commit, with the same bound"; nothing unexpired is ever deleted to make room; readers are bounded.
- **M4-D61 (context):** a lease is deleted only with its expired plan and only while the sweeper can take it, so a held lease is never unlinked (D4's sweep enforces it; this bead's tests assert it through retention).
- **M4-D21, M4-D23 (context):** plans share the cache's fate with their blobs; an unreadable plan is a missing one, so it has nothing worth pinning.
- **M4-D20, M4-D60 (context):** `apply` revalidates but reuses archives by hash, which is what the pin keeps cheap; the witness records a `--file` zip's SHA-256, so an edited zip moves `observed` as well as `selection`.
- **M4-D55 (context):** this bead adds no wire shape and may land after H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, the pre-freeze contract audit).

**Alternatives rejected that matter here.**
- *A correctness pin* that refuses `apply` when an archive is gone (M4-D26's rejected option): needless, the re-download is verified against the same expected hash.
- *A sweep only in retention* (M4-D24's rejected option): a machine whose previews never lead to commits would grow without bound; admission sweeps, and this is the second sweeper.
- *Evicting the oldest unexpired plan, or a soft cap:* both silently lose approvals or are no bound.
- *Judging plan expiry by retention's system clock* (decided while writing the bead): plans are dated by `crate::clock::now()`, which a debug build's `OMADDONS_NOW` freezes; one clock for both would make a plan expired for retention and live for `apply` in tests that freeze time. Moving snapshot retention to the frozen clock instead would change M3 behaviour for no reason. Hence `RetentionClock { system, plans }`, accepted by `run` as `impl Into`, so existing calls compile unchanged.
- *A partial decode of plan files for speed:* only a plan `apply` could use deserves a pin, and D4's full `load` is exactly that test.
- *A warning when the post-commit sweep fails:* noise on a successful commit, a new wire name the leaf must not add, and the condition it would report (a full store) is the doctor's row 45.
- *Pinning a plan dated ahead of now + 24 hours:* a hand edit or a stepped-back clock could then hold the cache over its cap until a far date.
- *Appending the scenarios to `tests/apply.rs`:* four other leaves append there; a suite of its own avoids the collision.

**Facts verified during planning** (at `c0ab5e9`). Retention's eviction pins come from a caller closure (`src/engine/retention.rs:135-228`, `:142`, `:225`) that today returns only installed releases' blobs (`:230-238`). `BlobCache::evict` takes the global lock itself after a lock-free first pass and reads the pins under it (`src/engine/blobs.rs:344-386`). `tx::retain` runs retention after every committed transaction with `Timestamp::now()` and turns any failure into `retention_failed` (`src/engine/tx.rs:910-947`), and commit, undo, whole restore and addon restore all call it. History is dated by the system clock (`tx.rs:1166`), M3's time rules by `crate::clock::now()` (`src/clock.rs:8-11`). Re-planning reuses a cached archive by expected hash or remembered hash and downloads otherwise (`src/engine/plan.rs:4818-4855`). A local zip's release id is its SHA-256, recomputed on every plan (`plan.rs:5390`, `:5429-5446`; `src/sources/local.rs:37-117`); it is never cached, but the plan's release still names its digest (`plan.rs:3876-3881`). `RetentionReport` is emitted by no command. The plan's file map names `src/engine/blobs.rs` for this bead; no change is needed there.

**Risks and how they are watched.**
- Milestone risk #7 (widget update previews feel slow; mitigated by "the blobs are then cached, so `apply` downloads nothing"): this bead keeps that mitigation true across evictions; E2E scenario 1 counts the asset downloads.
- A pin or sweep failure leaking into a commit: unit tables and E2E scenario 5 assert `Ok` and no `retention_failed`.
- The clock split moving snapshot retention: the existing suites unchanged, plus a unit test that runs both clocks apart.
- Time under the global lock: bounded by the quotas, and only when eviction must delete; noted for measurement if it ever matters.

**What it unblocks, and why they wait.**
- **D7** (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.7`, release drift and apply races, end to end): its Tukui cache-hit row and its lifecycle rows assume an approval downloads nothing within its lifetime and that expired plans are swept.
- **T3** (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.3`, slice 2 end to end): it waits for every slice-2 leaf; its demo item "a Tukui plan applies from the cache" rests on the pin (edge added at filing).
It is blocked by **D4** (the store it pins and sweeps) and, at filing, **T1** (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs and the `argc e2e` runner), because its end-to-end suite uses `TestLog`.

**How it serves the milestone.** G-M4-3: an approval stays cheap to carry out for its whole life, and a local archive edited after the preview can never be installed under it. G-M4-6: every deletion is D4's `fsx::prune` under `LockUse::Expired`, retention never fails a commit, and nothing new takes the global lock. Checkpoint criterion 7: the store converges through commits as well as previews, and the missing-or-changed local input half is proven.

**Confidence.** High. The code is a bounded read path and one call into D4's sweep, both best effort and unable to delete anything D4's rules would keep; the only subtle choice, the clock split, is explicit, tested, and invisible in release builds.

#### D6 Plan retention: blob pins and sweeps
- **Type** task · **P1** · **size-S** · **slice-2**
- **Blocked by:** D4.
- **Unblocks:** D7.
- **Background.** M4-D24, M4-D26, §6.9.4.
- **Technical approach.**
  1. `retention::run`'s pin closure gains `plans::unexpired_blob_pins`, read under the eviction lock and bounded by the store's quotas.
  2. Retention runs the bounded expired-plan sweep after each commit (`LockUse::Expired`, D4).
  3. A local zip in a plan is re-hashed at apply (asserted here).
- **Acceptance criteria.**
  - An unexpired plan's blobs survive an eviction that would otherwise take them.
  - An expired plan's blobs do not.
  - An unreadable or oversized plan pins nothing and fails nothing.
- **Test plan.** Unit tests in `src/engine/retention.rs`, and an E2E eviction test.
- **Considerations.** None.

done: blob eviction spares unexpired plans' archives, retention runs D4's bounded sweep after every commit, and the local-zip re-hash is proven end to end.

**What landed.** `plans::unexpired_blob_pins(paths, now) -> PlanPins` (private `pins_within` with the two bounds; `src/state/plans.rs`); `retention::RetentionClock { system, plans }` with `current()` and `From<Timestamp>`; `retention::run(.., now: impl Into<RetentionClock>, ..)` sweeps first and unions the plan pins inside the closure `BlobCache::evict` calls under the global lock; four internal `RetentionReport` fields (`plans_swept`, `plan_leases_swept`, `plan_sweep_failed`, `#[serde(skip)] plan_pins`); `tx::retain` passes `RetentionClock::current()` (one line). Unit tests in `src/state/plans/pins_tests.rs` (helpers in `src/state/plans/test_support.rs`; D4's `plan_at` made `pub(super)`) and `src/engine/retention/tests/plan_tests.rs`; E2E `tests/e2e_plan_retention.rs` (scenarios 1–7). README: the Retention bullets and the `limits.blob_cache_max_bytes` row.

**Evidence.** `argc gate` passes; `argc e2e plan_retention` 7/7 with complete logs; 54 plan-store and retention unit tests pass, every pre-existing retention, undo and restore test unchanged.

**No new or changed wire name.** No error/warning code, `details` key, data key, action, event, kind or file. No constant, config key, prune caller, failpoint or doctor failure mode; `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` unchanged. No command path added or changed, so common rule 16 is not engaged.

**Decided while writing this bead, confirmed or adjusted:**
- Plan clock and `RetentionClock` with `impl Into`: confirmed; `undo.rs` untouched.
- `now < expires_at <= now + PLAN_TTL` ceiling: confirmed (`pins_follow_expiry`).
- Two read bounds, newest first: confirmed. The file and byte bound cases are one table test, `the_file_and_byte_bounds_keep_the_newest_plans`, instead of two named tests.
- Full `load`, no early stop, hex-only pins: confirmed.
- Sweep first, skipped when `<cache>/plans/` is absent: confirmed (`the_sweep_runs_even_when_history_cannot_be_read`, `a_home_without_a_plan_store_gets_none`, scenario 4).
- No warning, four internal report fields: confirmed. `an_unlistable_plan_store_pins_nothing_and_retention_completes` also asserts `plan_sweep_failed == true`.
- Own suite file: confirmed.
- `--if-match` form of the local-zip proof, `details.changed == ["selection", "observed"]`: confirmed (scenarios 6 and 7).
- `apply` forms: D5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`) is still open, so scenario 8 is filed as `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.10` (discovered-from this bead, blocked by D5).
- README wording: adjusted. D4's `LockUse::Expired` prune creates a guard lease for a plan that has none (`only_expired` in `src/fsx/prune.rs`, so no applier enters mid-prune) and leaves it behind as an orphan, which the next pass collects. README therefore says "Free leases are collected with their plans or on the following pass" instead of "each with its lease". It is bounded (at most `PLANS_SWEEP_MAX` per pass, well inside `list`'s entry cap) and converges, so it is not filed as a defect.
- Scenario 3 numbers: adjusted to that rule. 63 plans per commit (`e5` refused with its held lease), 87 then 24 expired left; leases 55, 64, then 23 after commit 3, so a fourth commit (`pin B -t era`) is needed before no lease is left. The invariants hold: at most 64 per commit, the held pair intact while held, `p` byte-identical, none expired after enough commits.
- E2E commands: the previews and bound updates pass `--refresh` (A v2 is published after the install), and every command runs under a fixed `OMADDONS_NOW`, so the plan clock is deterministic.

title: Release drift and apply races, end to end
description:
## How to work this bead

This bead is worked through its 5 subtasks, listed below in work order. Claim a subtask, not this bead (`br ready --parent omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.7` lists the ready ones). The agent that closes the last open subtask then verifies every acceptance criterion of this bead (they are the leaf's, not any one subtask's), and closes this bead with `br close omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.7 --reason "done: <evidence> · found: <ids>"`. Until this bead is closed, every bead it blocks stays blocked.

1. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.7.1 E2E: a release landing between preview and `apply`, for every source and every release-bearing command, with the memo refresh. The release-landing builders (`tests/common/landing.rs`), their self-tests, the per-source and per-command matrices, the typed `--if-match` contrasts and the Tukui cache-hit row.
2. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.7.2 E2E: a concurrent change and a stale bound no-op, for every storable command. One test per storable command for each: another process commits (or a file changes) between the dry run and `apply`; and a bound run whose work another run already did is refused, never told "unchanged".
3. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.7.3 E2E: the plan lifecycle for every storable command, as a scenario other suites reuse. `common::plans::lifecycle` (the dry run under held locks, expiry, another build, hand edits, the real run, the second run), one test per storable command, the missing inputs and the vanished working directory.
4. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.7.4 E2E: two appliers of one plan, the lease timeout, interference between targets, and a held lease against the sweeps. The split race (and its "the first committed nothing" variant), the 30-second lease timeout, the interference race with `plans show`'s `partial`, and a lease a running `apply` holds that neither sweep may delete.
5. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.7.5 Tests: the real-machine `apply_one_update_and_undo`. One update previewed, applied through its stored plan and undone on a non-Forever client of the development machine (checkpoint only).

Subtasks 1, 2, 4 and 5 can start at once; 3 waits for 2, because it reuses 2's per-command home builders. Subtasks 1 to 4 each append their own test families to `tests/apply.rs`: rebase before each gate run.

**Size M, one bead for closure.** The five parts are one claim: "what a stored plan approved is what `apply` runs, whatever lands, changes or races in between". H4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`, the README final pass) and T3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.3`, slice 2 end to end) must see all of it proven, so the bead closes only when all five subtasks are closed; the subtasks split the work into commits that each pass `argc gate`.

**What kind of leaf this is.** The verification leaf of area D, in the style of M2's H2: it owns no feature code. It adds tests, test builders and the fixes the tests force. A scenario that fails because the product is wrong is a finding: file it as a bug with `--deps discovered-from:<the subtask's id>`, block the subtask on it (`br dep add <subtask> <bug>`), and let the bug's own commit carry the fix while this bead's scenario stays as its regression test. A scenario that fails because a builder or fixture is wrong is fixed in place. No scenario is weakened to pass.

## Background

### What this bead is, and why it exists

M4 makes every addon-changing command previewable and bindable. A `--dry-run` returns a precondition token and, for the eleven storable commands, stores a plan at `<cache>/plans/<plan_id>.json`. `omaddons apply <plan_id>` then executes exactly that plan's typed intent, re-planning bound to its stored token, target by target, with one applier per plan at a time. The leaves before this one built and unit-tested each piece:

- D1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1`, `precondition::of_plan` and the approval witness) defined the token; D2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2`, `--if-match` on `install`, `update`, `sync` and `copy`) and D3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.3`, `--if-match` on `pin`, `unpin` and `adopt`) bound the commands to it, no-op paths included; D8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8`, the approval checked again under the commit lock) checks it again under the lock;
- D4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`, the plan store) stores the plans; D5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`, `omaddons apply`) executes them under a lease; D6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.6`, plan retention) pins their blobs and sweeps expired ones; D9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.9`, `omaddons plans show`) reconciles an approval with history.

What none of them proves is the behaviour across processes and time that the vision's M4 checkpoint names: "a release landing in between yields `plan_stale`, never a different install". Nor do they run the races M4-D61 was written for: two appliers of one plan, and another command committing between an `apply`'s targets. This bead runs those scenarios end to end through the real binary, on synthetic homes with HTTP fixtures and `pause` failpoints, for every source and every storable command, and adds the one real-machine test the checkpoint runs for stored plans.

It must also prove that each refusal is honest: after a stale `apply`, the client's AddOns, its records and history hash exactly as before; after a fresh one, exactly the new release is installed.

### Goals it serves

- **G-M4-3, what was previewed is what runs, target by target.** "Every command that changes addons can be previewed with `--dry-run` and then run bound to that preview, by token (`--if-match`) or by stored plan (`apply <plan_id>`)." "The guarantee is per target. On each target the bound run commits exactly the operations the preview approved, or none of them … It then reports each target as committed, unchanged, stale or failed, with its transaction id, and never calls the whole run atomic." "Other omaddons processes are serialized by the global lock and by one applier per plan." "'Anything else' is named precisely: a new release, a change on an affected client, another binary, an expired plan, a missing input, a plan already applied." "An approval can be inspected and reconciled." This bead is where each sentence is run, not assumed.
- **G-M4-6, no new risk to the engine's guarantees.** "Dry runs still leave `<state>` untouched, and the global lock is still held only for commit windows." Every stale run here is checked to change nothing, and every `apply --dry-run` of the lifecycle runs while the test itself holds the global lock and the plan's lease.
- **The vision.** Vision §7's M4 checkpoint (above); vision D31, "what a human approved is exactly what runs"; and the thesis that omaddons stays the sole, safe, undoable authority over what it manages. An approval that silently installs a newer release, or that two processes split between them, would break it.

### Checkpoint criteria it serves (by number; H6, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, records the evidence)

- **Criterion 7, stored plans**, the rows that are this bead's (D5 owns the others):
  - "A release landing between the preview and `apply` gives `plan_stale` (`details.changed: ["selection"]`), never a different install. This is tested for `install`, `update`, `sync` and `copy` with fixture sequences in which the newest release changes."
  - "The re-preview that follows a stale `apply` shows the new release (the probe refreshed the memo)."
  - "An expired plan, a plan from another build (`build_id`), a missing input (a local archive, a `sync` file) and a plan history already records as applied each give `plan_stale` with their `details.reason`. An unknown, oversized or unreadable plan gives `plan_not_found`. A vanished working directory alone stales nothing, because the stored intent's paths are absolute. `apply --dry-run` re-validates and shows without changing anything." D5 proves these on representative commands; this bead runs the lifecycle for every storable command.
  - "Two `apply`s of one multi-target plan, both paused between target commits, never split its targets: one holds the plan's lease and runs, the other waits and then reports the first one's work."
  - The plan adds: "one test per storable command for a concurrent change".
- **Criterion 6, previews bind**, its every-path bullet, through the no-op scenarios: "That holds on every path: a bound run that finds nothing left to do, and a bound dry run, also check the token." D2 and D3 test their own commands' no-op paths through `--if-match`; this bead runs one per storable command, through `apply` too.
- **Criterion 17, gate and checkpoint runs:** "the live probes and the real-machine tests pass with every `SKIP` quoted". This bead owns `apply_one_update_and_undo`, one of the three real-machine tests M4 adds. The owner's approval of the plan is the go-ahead for it: "one update previewed and applied on a non-Forever client, then undone".
- **The invariants table** names this bead in two rows: "A bound run checks its token on every path: the no-op scenarios (D2, D3, D7)", and "Two applications of one plan never split its targets: the two-applier scenarios (D7): one lease holder, `already_applied` for the other".
- **Slice 2's exit demo** ("a release landing in between gives `plan_stale`, and the re-preview shows it; … a second `apply` is `already_applied`; two appliers never split a plan; … a Tukui plan applies from the cache") is recorded by T3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.3`), which reuses this bead's builders. This leaf never records a slice demo itself.

### The decisions that shape it

The full decision log is also filed as comments on the milestone epic `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`; each decision this bead relies on is restated here.

- **M4-D20: both races bind; stored plans revalidate their sources.** Two kinds of change make a preview untrue, and both stale it: a concurrent change (another command, the game, a hand edit) and release drift (a newer release appearing between preview and run). A typed `--if-match` run uses its command's normal freshness: `install`, `copy` and `pin` revalidate (`Freshness::Revalidate`); `update` and `sync` (and `adopt`) answer from the 15-minute release memo, so release drift inside that window does not stale them, and a typed bound run does exactly what the preview showed. `apply` always revalidates every source it touches, whatever the command's window, so a release that landed since the preview changes `selection` and the plan is stale. The revalidation refreshes the memo: `apply`'s probes write the release memo, stale or not, so the re-preview after a stale `apply` shows the new release instead of the memo's old one (which would loop: preview, stale, the same preview). *Why:* a typed `--if-match` is an agent asserting "do what I just saw", while `apply` is the moment of approval, and approving "update DBM" means approving the version shown. *Rejected:* (i) revalidating on every `--if-match` run (as costly as an unbound install, for no gain); (ii) installing the old release at `apply` though a newer one exists (it silently installs something the user would no longer choose). This bead's release matrix tests both halves in the same scenarios.
- **M4-D61: one applier per plan, and the guarantee is per target.** A real `apply` holds an advisory lease (`fsx::lock::Lease`, a `flock`) on `<cache>/plans/<plan_id>.lease` from before its freshness checks until every target's outcome is known, independent of the global commit lock. A second applier of the same plan waits up to `PLAN_LEASE_TIMEOUT` (30 s); on timeout it exits `locked` (5, retryable) with `details.lease` and the holder's `{pid, command, age_s}`. When it gets the lease it reloads the plan and finds `already_applied` or, if the first applier committed nothing, proceeds. Process death releases the lease; `apply --dry-run` takes none. The plan sweep deletes a lease only together with its expired plan, and only while it can take that lease itself, so a held lease is never unlinked. Multi-target runs keep one transaction per target, so a late conflict or an I/O failure can leave a partial run, which `outcomes[]` reports per target as `committed`, `unchanged`, `stale` or `failed`. *Why:* without the lease, two processes holding one plan split it (A commits retail; B finds retail stale but commits era; A then finds era stale), and both callers see a partial result for one approval. *Rejected:* (i) no plan lock; (ii) holding the global lock across the whole `apply` (it would block every other command for the length of a download); (iii) one transaction across targets. M4-D61's task list gives this bead "the split race and the interference race".
- **M4-D23: `apply` executes the stored, typed intent bound to its stored token** (context). It refuses, each as `plan_stale` (not retryable) with `details.reason`: `expired`, `binary_changed` (the plan's `build_id` differs from this binary's), `input_missing` (an absolute input the intent names is gone, with `details.path`) and `already_applied` (history holds a committed transaction carrying this plan id, with `details.txs`). A file larger than `PLAN_MAX_BYTES`, undecodable, of a newer major, with an unknown intent variant or option, a relative path, a `display_argv` that is not the intent's own, or a token that is not its parts' digest is `plan_not_found` with `details.reason: "unreadable"`. A vanished working directory stales nothing: the intent holds no relative path. Plan files are immutable.
- **M4-D25: history lines from `apply` carry the plan id** (context). A transaction `apply` commits records the plan's `display_argv` as its `argv` and `plan: <plan_id>`. That field is the evidence `already_applied` and `plans show` read. A line committed by a direct command carries no `plan`.
- **M4-D63: `plans show` reconciles an approval with history** (context). Its `state` is `pending`, `completed` (a committed transaction for every approved target), `partial` (some, not all), `expired` or `unknown`; it never infers success from current addon versions. The interference race asserts its `partial`, which is why D9 blocks this bead.
- **M4-D19 and M4-D60: the token's four parts** (context). `command`; `targets` (each target's key, or provisional id, with its record generation); `selection` (the folder ops, the changes, the releases sorted by id, with a deferred asset such as Tukui's keyed without its URL; `creates_addons_dir`); `observed` (the approval witness: the content of every folder the plan replaces or removes, every name it creates, the local inputs, a copy's source folders and source generation, the sync file's digest, update's skips, the judge digest and the build id). `details.changed` names the parts that differ. Each row's expected `changed` set below comes from these definitions.
- **M4-D22: which commands store plans** (context). The eleven storable commands are `install`, `update`, `pin`, `unpin`, `adopt` (when it adopts), `sync`, `copy`, `remove`, `undo`, `backup restore` and `backup prune`. "One per storable command" in this bead always means these eleven.
- **M4-D24 and M4-D26: the lifecycle and the pins** (context, D4's and D6's). A plan lives `PLAN_TTL` (24 h). The store sweeps at most `PLANS_SWEEP_MAX` (64) expired plans with their leases at each admission and after each commit, under `LockUse::Expired`, which admits only expired plans and leases fsx can take at that moment. An unexpired plan pins its blobs.
- **M4-D55, the "after H1" rule.** This bead may land after the pre-freeze audit H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`) closes, because it adds no wire shape. Any fix a scenario forces must be additive; a needed change that is not additive is a defect against H1, fixed before H2 regenerates the golden for the last time and recorded on H1's change list.
- **M4-D47 (context): end-to-end tests are Rust.** "End-to-end test scripts" in this repository are Rust integration tests that drive the real binary on a synthetic home. M4-D47 rejected shell fixture scripts ("a second test language, and shell scripts that must clean up after themselves"). `argc e2e` (T1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`) runs the suites with verbose logs.

### Facts this bead relies on (verified at `c0ab5e9`, plus what the leaves before it add)

- **A fixture sequence never spans two runs of the binary.** `common::http::fixture_seq` serves its responses in order with the last repeating, but "replay restarts every sequence in each process, so a sequence never spans two CLI runs; scenarios spanning commands switch fixture sets with `Home::scenario`" (`tests/common/http.rs:94-97`). A dry run and the `apply` that follows are two processes. `Home::scenario(name)` makes a fresh, empty scenario directory (`tests/common/home.rs:81-86`); the private `Home::next_scenario` makes one that starts as a copy of the current one (`:150-160`); `Home::installed_behind` uses it to install an old GitHub tag and then serve a newer one with the memo aged a day (`:95-118`). Every run reads the current directory through `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES` (`Home::std_command`, `:254-266`).
- **Per-source fixture builders**, some private to their suites: GitHub `gh_release`, `gh_release_v`, `gh_latest` (which replaces any earlier `releases/latest` fixture of that repository by URL) and `gh_feed` (`tests/common/http.rs:142-257`); WoWInterface `wowi_details`, `wowi_file` and `details` (`tests/common/wowi.rs:85-160`), while the per-version builder `bugsack` is private to `tests/sources_wowi.rs:86-102`; Tukui `entry`, `elvui`, `tukui_list`, `tukui_addon` (one download token per call), `tukui_download` and `etag` (`tests/common/tukui.rs`), while `elvui_zip(version)` is private to `tests/sources_tukui.rs:68-82`; WowAce only privately, in the `support` module of `tests/sources_wowace.rs` (`serve_recorded` `:42-51` over the recording `tests/fixtures/http/wowace-bug-grabber/`, `serve` for any method including `PROPFIND` `:53-75`, `moved` to re-tag a tag at another revision `:76-95`, `retagged_tree` `:96-113`, `index` `:149-161`, and the tags URL `TAGS` at `:719`); git only privately, as `synthetic` in `tests/git_github.rs:160-205` (a `commits/<branch>.atom` feed and a `codeload.github.com/<o>/<r>/zip/<sha>` archive).
- **Only GitHub has a cheap probe.** `Source::probe` defaults to `None` (`src/sources/mod.rs:258-261`); only GitHub implements it, with one `releases/latest` request (`src/sources/github.rs:160-176`). Under `Revalidate` a memo entry with a probe is probed, and anything else is fetched (`decide`, `src/resolve/cache.rs:84-102`). So "the probe" of each source is: GitHub `release-latest` (`src/sources/github.rs:601`), plus `release-json` (`:673`) only when the tag moved; git one `commits-atom` request (`src/sources/git_github.rs:135`); WoWInterface one `wowi-details` (`src/sources/wowi.rs:102`); Tukui one `tukui-list` (`src/sources/tukui.rs:100`), plus `tukui-addon` (`:248`) when a download needs a token; WowAce one `PROPFIND` named `wowace-tags` (`src/sources/wowace.rs:106`). Downloads are `asset` (`src/engine/blobs.rs:275`). `common::netlog::{net_log, read_net_log, NetLogView::count_purpose}` read them (`tests/common/netlog.rs:10-60`).
- **Freshness per command:** `install` (`src/app/install.rs:541-547`), `copy` (`src/app/copy.rs:282-286`) and `pin` (`src/app/pin.rs:247-251`) revalidate; `update` (`src/app/update.rs:154-160`), `sync` (`src/app/sync.rs:678-682`) and `adopt` (`src/app/adopt.rs:490-496`) use `Window(SOURCE_RECHECK_MIN_INTERVAL)`, 15 minutes (`src/politeness.rs:35`). D5 adds `Context.force_revalidate`, which turns every window into `Revalidate` under `apply` (`Freshness::Revalidate` is `src/resolve/cache.rs:36`).
- **The memo's window timestamps** are `entries[].fetched_at`, `tukui_list.fetched_at` and `look_backs[].at` (`src/state/memo.rs:29-54, 165-173`). `Home::installed_behind` ages only `entries[].fetched_at` (`tests/common/home.rs:112-116`).
- **A WowAce release keeps its id across a re-tag.** A re-tag of the installed tag is an update whose release id stays `wowace:bug-grabber@v12.1.1` while the record's `revision` moves (`tests/sources_wowace.rs:739-806`). Its planned release's URL is the pinned tree `!svn/bc/<rev>/tags/<tag>/` (`src/engine/plan.rs:3872-3873`), so a re-tag still changes `selection`.
- **Planning does every download before the token check.** `engine::tx::run` calls `plan::plan` once for all targets, then `Binding::plan` before anything is staged (`src/engine/tx.rs:401-407`; D2 removes the `!req.dry_run` condition at `:404`). A stale `apply` has therefore already downloaded the newer archive when it refuses, and a later run finds it in the blob cache, by expected hash or by the candidate fact the download recorded (`fetch_blob`, `src/engine/plan.rs:4815-4855`).
- **A deferred asset's planned URL** is its canonical URL after a fresh download and `None` after a blob-cache hit (`src/engine/plan.rs:3862-3871`, `:4833-4840`); its token URL is never stored. The existing Tukui suite shows a real run after its dry run "took the blob the dry run cached, so it resolved nothing: no URL", with only the list requested (`tests/sources_tukui.rs:262-321`). D1 keys deferred releases without the URL.
- **Targets commit one at a time, in key order.** The commit loop sorts targets by key (`src/engine/tx.rs:430-437`) and runs one commit window per target. `engine.cleanup.done` is hit after each target's window has unlocked and cleaned up, before the next target starts (`src/engine/tx.rs:885`). Under the lock, a moved record generation is refused through `Binding::moved` (`src/engine/tx.rs:1050-1056`). Which target commits first therefore depends on the keys, and a test finds it from history, never from target ids.
- **Partial runs:** `TargetsData::partial()` is true when any item failed or any target has an error (`src/app/outcome.rs:587-590`); such an outcome renders `ok: true`, `partial: true` and exit 0 (`src/output/mod.rs:130-176`).
- **Failpoints:** `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS=<name>[=abort|=error|=sleep:<ms>|=panic|=pause][@N][,…]` (`src/fsx/failpoint.rs:3-12`); a `pause` waits at most 60 s (`PAUSE_MAX`, `:25`) and writes `<name>.reached` holding the pid (`:140-158`). `common::pause::Pause` gives each child its own marker directory; `reached` waits up to 30 s; after `resume`, "later hits of `name` pass straight through" (`tests/common/pause.rs:13-48`). `engine.plan.done`, `engine.lock.acquired` and `engine.cleanup.done` are in `engine::tx::FAILPOINTS` (`src/engine/tx.rs:78-113`); `engine.plan.done` is hit at the end of planning (`src/engine/plan.rs:1528`), `engine.lock.acquired` right after the global lock is taken (`src/engine/tx.rs:1016`).
- **M3's binding scenarios** run through `--if-match` in `tests/preconditions.rs`: `remove` after a concurrent install gives `["targets"]` (`:91-106`); `undo <tx>` after a later commit `["targets"]` (`:174-195`); an undo whose SavedVariables a play session rewrote `["observed"]` (`:197-210`); `backup prune -t retail --keep 2` after a new automatic backup `["selection","observed"]` (`:382-405`) and with its victim's `backup.json` rewritten `["observed"]` (`:407-424`); `backup restore` after a play session or with its `backup.json` rewritten `["observed"]` (`:468-508`), and after a commit on its target `["targets"]` (`:510-523`). Their builders (`restorable` `:431-441`, `three_days` `:336-346`, `at_noon` `:314-320`) are private to that file.

### Where the plan and the code disagree (each also in "Decided while writing this bead")

1. The plan builds "fixture sequences (`common::http::fixture_seq`) in which `releases/latest` … answer newer releases on the second call". A sequence restarts in every process (`tests/common/http.rs:94-97`), and the second call is `apply`, a second process. The landing is a second scenario directory instead; `fixture_seq` stays the per-file mechanism.
2. The plan's no-op scenarios "expect `plan_stale`" for every storable command. `remove` resolves its names before its binding runs (`src/app/remove.rs:181-209`), so a stale bound `remove` of an addon another run already removed is `not_found` (exit 3). That is a refusal that changes nothing, and M3's `remove` binding must stay unchanged (criterion 6), so `remove`'s row expects `not_found`.
3. The plan says `apply_one_update_and_undo` prints `SKIP` "when nothing has an update", while criterion 17 pre-accepts only three skips (`keyless_installs_forever`, the sandbox tests, the `zsh`/`fish` checks) and calls any other `SKIP` an unmet criterion. The test makes its own update when none exists (as `m2_pin_unpin_update_on_era` does) and skips only when even that is impossible.
4. The WowAce, git, WoWInterface-per-version and Tukui-zip builders are private to their suites, and `Home::next_scenario` is private (locations above): the landing builders need them in `tests/common/`.
5. `Home::installed_behind` ages only the memo's `entries`, not `tukui_list` or `look_backs`; a Tukui landing needs all three aged.
6. The plan speaks of each source's "probe"; only GitHub has one (`src/sources/github.rs:160`). For the other four, `Revalidate` fetches, at the cost §6.9.5 states (one commits feed, `filedetails`, list or `PROPFIND` request), so the assertions count those purposes.
7. The plan's WowAce row "answers newer releases"; WowAce's identity of a release is its tag plus the tag's revision, and its release id does not change on a re-tag. The WowAce landing is a re-tag of the installed tag at a higher revision, which M3 already proves is an update.
8. The plan's split race has "both appliers paused between target commits". With the lease, the second applier never reaches the commit loop. Both are armed; the test asserts the second never reached either of its failpoints.

## Technical Approach

### 1. Ground rules for every scenario

- **Real binary, synthetic homes.** Every scenario drives `omaddons` through T1's `TestLog` on a `Home` or `Scene` (one or two Battle.net clients: `Home::new(&["wow"])` gives target `retail` (`_retail_`); `Home::new(&["wow", "wow_classic"])` adds `classic` (`_classic_`, Mists, interface 50504)), with HTTP fixtures and `pause` failpoints. Nothing reads the developer's real home except omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.7.5's real-machine test.
- **Every run passes `--json` explicitly** (T1's `log.run` appends nothing). Runs on a home with a `WTF/` built from `common::wtf::Wtf` add `--progress json` and call `ran.assert_private()`.
- **What a stale run must leave unchanged:** each client's `Interface/AddOns`, the records directory `<state>/targets/`, the client's `WTF/` where the row has one, and the history line count. `<cache>/plans/*.json` must be unchanged by any `apply` (plan files are immutable), but a real `apply` may create `<cache>/plans/<plan_id>.lease`, so the plan store is compared through D4's `plan_files()` (names and bytes of the `.json` files), never by a tree hash. The release memo and the blob cache may change: that is M4-D20's memo refresh.
- **"Exactly the new release":** after a fresh apply, the addon's marker file (a file whose content only that release has) holds that release's content, its record names that version (and revision, for WowAce), and history's newest line on the target carries the applied plan's id.
- **The expected `fix_argv` of a `plan_stale`:** `omaddons::app::precondition::preview_argv(&plan.display_argv)`, from the plan file read with D4's `read_plan`, never hard-coded.
- **Test names** (the plan's `tests/apply.rs::drift_*`, `race_*` and `lease_*`): `drift_` for release landings, concurrent changes, no-ops and the lifecycle; `race_` for two appliers and interference; `lease_` for the timeout and the sweeps. D4's `store_*`/`quota_*`, D5's `apply_*` and D8's `witness_*` share the file; the prefixes keep the families apart. The crate doc gains one `//!` line after the e2e marker naming D7's three families.
- **One `#[test]` per storable command** wherever the plan says "one per storable command": a declarative macro over a table of rows, so the eleven names exist and fail independently.

- `drift_install_lands_between_preview_and_apply`, `drift_update_inside_the_window`, `drift_sync_inside_the_window`, `drift_copy_revalidates_typed_and_applied` (the per-command matrix, on GitHub): the same stale-then-fresh sequence for `install`, `update`, `sync` and `copy`, plus the typed contrast: a typed `--if-match` run of the old token succeeds with the previewed release for `update` and `sync` (their memo window) and is `plan_stale` (`["selection"]`) for `install` and `copy` (which revalidate).
- `drift_tukui_cache_hit_applies`: a Tukui install whose dry run downloaded applies from the blob cache with no release change: one `tukui-list` request, no `tukui-addon` or `asset` request, `asset_url: null`, and no download token in the plan file or any output.

`tests/apply.rs` gains a private `drift_support` module of per-command home builders (`fn built(log, command) -> Built { on, preview, roots, env, privacy }`), reused by omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.7.3. Each row's interfering commit is a local-zip install of `Bar` (`install gh:o/bar --file <bar.zip> -t <target> --offline --json`: no fixture, and it moves only that target's generation), unless the row names another change.

| `update` | `Home::installed_behind` (v1 installed, v2 newest) | `update foo -t retail` | Bar on retail | contains `targets` |
| `pin` | foo v1 installed | `pin foo -t retail` | Bar on retail | contains `targets` |
| `unpin` | foo installed with `--version v1` (pinned) | `unpin foo -t retail` | Bar on retail | contains `targets` |
| `adopt` | an unmanaged `Foo` byte-equal to v1's, v1's fixtures | `adopt Foo --ref gh:o/foo -t retail` | (a) Bar on retail; (b) one line appended to `Foo/core.lua` | (a) contains `targets`; (b) contains `observed` |
| `sync` | desired `[family.mainline] addons = ["gh:o/foo"]` | `sync` | (a) Bar on retail; (b) `# edited` appended to the desired file | (a) contains `targets`; (b) contains `observed` |
| `copy` | retail and classic; foo v1 on retail | `copy --from retail --to classic` | (a) Bar on classic; (b) `pin foo -t retail` (the source's record) | (a) contains `targets`; (b) contains `observed` |
| `remove` | `Scene`, Foo v1 | `remove Foo -t retail` | `Scene::install("gh:o/bar", "bar")` | exactly `["targets"]` |
| `undo` | (a) `Scene`, Foo v1 (tx T); (b) `Scene::new().with_saved_variables(&["Foo"])`, Foo v1 then v2, played | (a) `undo T`; (b) `undo` | (a) Bar installed; (b) `Scene::play(&["Foo"])` | (a) exactly `["targets"]`; (b) exactly `["observed"]` |
| `backup restore` | a `WTF/` with fake account names and a manual backup (as M3's `restorable`), Foo v1 | `backup restore <id> -t retail` | (a) Bar installed; (b) the account's `Foo.lua` rewritten; (c) the backup's `backup.json` rewritten | (a) exactly `["targets"]`; (b), (c) exactly `["observed"]` |
| `backup prune` | three automatic backups on three old days and a newer manual one (as M3's `three_days`); every run with `OMADDONS_NOW=2026-10-10T12:00:00Z` | `backup prune -t retail --keep 2` | (a) a new automatic backup seeded; (b) the victim's `backup.json` rewritten | (a) exactly `["selection","observed"]`; (b) exactly `["observed"]` |

Each `drift_concurrent_<command>`: seed, preview (plan P), change, record the trees, `apply P` (`plan_stale`, not retryable, the expected `changed`, the plan's preview as `fix_argv`, every tree unchanged, no new history line), then run the fix (P2) and `apply P2` (exit 0, every target `committed`, history `plan == P2`). The engine rows assert `contains` (D2, D3 and D8 may name further parts); the M3 rows assert the exact sets M3 established, because `apply` must not change M3's bindings.

Each `drift_noop_<command>`: preview P (token T); make the same change directly (the same argv without `--dry-run`); then:

- the typed bound run `<argv> --if-match T --json` is refused (`plan_stale`, exit 1), never an "unchanged" success, and changes nothing;
- `apply P` is refused the same way, never with `reason: "already_applied"` (the direct run's history line carries no `plan`), and changes nothing;
- for the eight rows whose second preview is a no-op (`install`, `update`, `pin`, `unpin`, `adopt`, `sync`, `copy`, `backup prune`): that preview returns `plan_id: null`, no `apply` action in `commands[]`, and a token T0; `<argv> --if-match T0` exits 0 and changes nothing;
- `remove`: the bound run and `apply P` are `not_found` (exit 3), not `plan_stale` (see the disagreement above), and change nothing.

### 4. The plan lifecycle for every storable command (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.7.3)

`common::plans::lifecycle(log, on, &case) -> Lifecycle` in `tests/common/plans.rs` (D4's module; public, because E7, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7`, undo of repairs, "runs the D7 lifecycle scenarios once for a repair undo"):

```rust
pub struct LifecycleCase<'a> {
    pub label: &'a str,                    // the command path, for step labels
    pub preview: Vec<String>,              // the storable argv, without --dry-run and --json
    pub roots: Vec<(String, PathBuf)>,     // labelled trees every refusal leaves unchanged
    pub env: Vec<(String, String)>,        // set on every run (OMADDONS_NOW for backup prune)
    pub progress_json: bool,               // the home has a WTF/: --progress json and assert_private
    pub second: Second,                    // AlreadyApplied, or StaleSelection (backup prune)
}
pub enum Second { AlreadyApplied, StaleSelection }
pub struct Lifecycle { pub plan_id: String, pub txs: Vec<String> }
pub fn lifecycle(log: &TestLog, on: &impl Runner, case: &LifecycleCase<'_>) -> Lifecycle;
```

Its steps, each a `log.step`, each refusal followed by `log.assert_unchanged` of every root, a check that `plan_files()` is unchanged and that history gained no line:

1. **Preview:** `<preview> --dry-run --json` → a plan id P.
2. **The dry run under held locks:** the test process takes the global lock (`GlobalLock::acquire`) and the plan's lease (D4's `Lease::acquire` on `Paths::plan_lease(P)`); `apply P --dry-run --json` exits 0 in under 4 s (a dry run that waited for the global lock would exit 5 after its 5 s timeout, one that waited for the lease after 30 s); `data.approved` equals the stored approval, `data.result.dry_run` is true, every outcome is `unchanged` with `tx: null`, `commands[]` holds the `apply` hint; nothing changed; the locks are released.
3. **Expired:** `apply P` with `OMADDONS_NOW` = `expires_at` + 60 s → `plan_stale`, `reason: "expired"`, `changed: []`, not retryable.
4. **Another build:** the file's bytes saved, top-level `build_id` set to `"0000000000000000"` → `reason: "binary_changed"`; the bytes restored and re-hashed equal.
5. **An unknown option in this command's intent:** `"bogus": true` added inside `intent` → `plan_not_found`, `reason: "unreadable"`, `details.path`; restored.
6. **A `display_argv` that disagrees:** its last element replaced → `plan_not_found`, `unreadable`; restored.
7. **The real run:** `apply P --json` exits 0; every outcome `committed`; history's lines carrying `plan == P` are exactly the outcomes' transactions.
8. **The second run:** `apply P` → `plan_stale`, `reason: "already_applied"`, `details.txs` those transactions oldest first; with `OMADDONS_NOW` past `expires_at`, still `already_applied`. For `backup prune` (`Second::StaleSelection`: a prune writes no history line, so it can never be `already_applied`): `plan_stale` whose `changed` contains `selection`, and after expiry `expired`.

Then `drift_lifecycle_<command>` for the eleven rows (with omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.7.2's builders); `drift_lifecycle_input_missing` (a deleted `--file <dir>` and a deleted `file:` zip, each `input_missing` with `details.path`; D5 covers the `--file` zip and the `sync` file); `drift_lifecycle_cwd_gone` (`sync ./addons.toml`, `install gh:o/foo --file ./Foo -t retail`, and `install … -t <the client dir relative to the cwd>`, each previewed from a working directory that is then deleted and applied from another: exit 0). Unknown ids, short and ambiguous prefixes and the other unreadable files are command-independent and stay D5's.

### 5. Two appliers, the lease timeout, interference and the sweeps (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.7.4)

The race home: `Home::new(&["wow", "wow_classic"])`, `Home::installed_behind("https://github.com/o/foo", v1, v2, &["retail", "classic"])` (both clients at v1, v2 newest, memo aged), and a `bar.zip`; the plan is `update foo --dry-run --json` (two targets). New helpers: `Pause::was_reached(name) -> bool` in `tests/common/pause.rs`; `common::plans::{holds_open(pid, path) -> bool, wait_until_open(log, pid, path, limit)}` (reads `/proc/<pid>/fd`; reuse D5's helper if it shipped one).

- `race_split_two_appliers_never_split_a_plan`: A (`apply P`, armed `engine.cleanup.done=pause`) reaches the pause after its first target; B (armed `engine.plan.done=pause,engine.cleanup.done=pause` with its own `Pause`) is started and waits on the lease (it holds `<cache>/plans/<P>.lease` open, and has reached neither failpoint); A resumed commits the second target (exit 0, both `committed`, transactions T1 then T2); B then reports `plan_stale`, `reason: "already_applied"`, `details.txs == [T1, T2]`, without ever reaching either failpoint; history holds exactly two lines with `plan == P`; `plans show P` is `completed`.

## Considerations

- **Risks (the plan's register; none is owned by this leaf).**
  - **#19, a token stales for no reason** (M, M; owners D1 and E6): every fresh apply after a re-preview, every concurrent row's fix and the Tukui cache-hit row apply a plan in an unchanged world; a spurious `plan_stale` there is a D1 defect, filed `discovered-from` the subtask.
  - **#6, tokens too sensitive** (M, L; owner D1): `binary_changed` makes every plan stale after an upgrade, by design; the lifecycle rows check that the refusal says why.
  - **#14, the milestone is large** (M, M): this leaf has 4 units of slack (wave t = 14–15; the computed lane 6 runs it at t = 16–18) and is not on the critical path, but H4 waits for it. Its subtasks run in parallel lanes.
- **Flakiness.** Every interleaving is made by `pause` markers, never by sleeps: a child stops at a named failpoint and the test acts only after `log.reached`. The two waits that are not markers are bounded and observable: the waiter's open lease file (`/proc/<pid>/fd`, up to 10 s) and the lease timeout (30 s, asserted as a range). A `pause` gives up after 60 s, so a broken test never hangs the gate, and T1's run timeout kills a hung child.
- **Test time.** About 45 end-to-end scenarios of 5 to 15 runs each, plus one 31-second timeout. Keep homes minimal (one client unless the row needs two), use local zips for interfering commits, and `log.case` for sub-cases of one test; cargo runs the tests of `tests/apply.rs` on parallel threads. Record the suite's added wall time in the close comment.
- **Clock.** `OMADDONS_NOW` moves only `clock::now()` (expiry, the sweeps, backup ages); commit lines use real time, and the evidence scan compares them with `created_at`. Set it only on the runs that must see the future, and never on a preview or an apply that must commit, except `backup prune`'s rows, which freeze it on every run as M3's do (a prune writes no history line).
- **Hot spots (the plan's collision rules).** `tests/apply.rs` is shared by D4, D5, D8 and this bead: append, keep the prefixes, rebase. `tests/common/` is shared by every suite: additions and pure moves only (moved helpers keep their names and behaviour, and the suites that used them are edited only in their `use` lines). `tests/real_machine.rs` gains one test each from D7, E6 and B3: append. README: only the two places of section 7. `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md`, the contract matrix and `src/limits.rs` are not touched.
- **After H1.** This bead may land after the pre-freeze audit; every fix it forces must be additive (M4-D55), or it is a defect against H1.
- **Privacy.** Rows with a `WTF/` built from `common::wtf::Wtf` (`backup restore`) use fake account, realm and character names and assert `assert_private_all` over stdout and stderr with `--progress json`. The engine `Scene`'s SavedVariables (`undo`'s played row) use its own fake names (`ACCT`, `Realm`, `Char`), which no output may name either; that row asserts it directly. Tukui download tokens must never reach a plan file or an output. The real-machine test never lists a `WTF/` path, and its notes replace the home directory with `<home>`.
- **Compatibility.** Nothing here changes a stored format. The real-machine test leaves one plan file in the real `<cache>/plans/`, which an M3 build never lists (its `Kind::Plan` is under `<state>/plans/`) and M4 sweeps after 24 hours.
- **What could go wrong, and how to notice.** A landing that does not change what the source answers (the `drift_landing_*` self-tests fail first); a memo window that is not really open (the typed `update`/`sync` rows would make a request: their `net.log` assertion fails); a stale apply that installed something (the AddOns and records trees); a waiter that slipped past the lease (its sentinel marker, and a third history line); a sweep that unlinked a held lease (the lease scenario); a fix argv that does not run (every concurrent row runs it).

**Planning rationale (M4 plan, 2026-10-24).**

**Why this bead.** M4 promises that what a person or an agent approved in a preview is what runs, target by target, and the vision's M4 checkpoint names the hardest case: "a release landing in between yields `plan_stale`, never a different install". D1–D9 build and unit-test the pieces (the token and its witness, the typed bindings, the under-lock checks, the plan store, `apply` and its lease, retention, `plans show`), but each leaf proves its own piece, mostly on one command and one source. None of them runs, across processes and time, what can actually happen between a preview and its `apply`: a newer release appearing at any of the five sources, another command committing on an affected client, a plan expiring, a binary upgrade, a hand-edited plan file, a deleted working directory, two appliers of one plan, or a different command committing between an `apply`'s targets. This bead is the verification leaf of area D, in the style of M2's H2: it owns no feature code, runs those scenarios end to end through the real binary on synthetic homes, for every source and every storable command, adds the one real-machine test the checkpoint runs for stored plans, and files whatever it finds as bugs `discovered-from` the subtask that found them. Without it, criterion 7's release-landing, two-applier and lifecycle rows would rest on unit tests of parts that were never composed.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M4-D20 (both races bind; stored plans revalidate):** a typed `--if-match` keeps its command's freshness (so `update`/`sync` inside the 15-minute window do exactly what was previewed), while `apply` revalidates every source and refreshes the memo, so a landing is `plan_stale` (`selection`) and the re-preview shows the new release. The release matrix tests both halves on the same scenarios.
- **M4-D61 (one applier per plan; the guarantee is per target):** the lease makes a second applier wait and report `already_applied`, or proceed if the first committed nothing; a timeout is `locked` with the holder; a held lease is never swept; interference is reported per target (`committed`, `stale`) and never called atomic. Its task list gives this bead the split and interference races.
- **M4-D23 (the typed intent and its refusals):** `expired`, `binary_changed`, `input_missing`, `already_applied`, and `plan_not_found` `unreadable` for a hand-edited file; a vanished working directory stales nothing. The lifecycle runs them for all eleven intent variants.
- **M4-D25 and M4-D63 (history's `plan`, and `plans show`):** a direct command's line carries no `plan`, so a plan whose work another run did is `plan_stale`, never `already_applied`; `plans show` says `completed` or `partial` from history alone.
- **M4-D19 and M4-D60 (the token's parts):** each row's expected `details.changed` comes from what `targets`, `selection` and `observed` cover, a deferred Tukui asset keyed without its URL included.
- **M4-D22 (the eleven storable commands):** "one per storable command" always means `install`, `update`, `pin`, `unpin`, `adopt`, `sync`, `copy`, `remove`, `undo`, `backup restore` and `backup prune`.
- **M4-D24 and M4-D26 (lifecycle, sweeps, pins)** as context for the lease-and-sweep scenario.
- **M4-D55 (after H1):** this bead may land after the pre-freeze audit because it adds no wire shape; any fix it forces must be additive.
- **M4-D47:** end-to-end tests are Rust suites driving the real binary, logged through T1's `TestLog`, not shell scripts.

**Alternatives rejected that matter here.**
- Fixture sequences that "answer a newer release on the second call": replay restarts every sequence in each process, so the second call (`apply`, another process) would see the first answer again. A landing is a second scenario directory (`Home::next_scenario`, made public).
- A test-only override of `PLAN_LEASE_TIMEOUT`: it would be a new environment variable (a wire name this bead may not add); the lease-timeout test waits the real 30 s in the gate instead.
- Timing the races with sleeps: every interleaving is made by `pause` markers and the waiter is detected by its open lease file, so the scenarios cannot flake on a loaded machine.
- Skipping the real-machine test when nothing has an update: criterion 17 pre-accepts three skips and no other, so the test makes its own update, as M2's Dominos test does.
- Forcing `plan_stale` on `remove`'s no-op row: `remove` resolves names before its M3 binding, and criterion 6 keeps M3's bindings unchanged; its row expects `not_found`, a refusal that changes nothing.
- Copying private builders (WowAce, Tukui's zip) into a new module: they move into `tests/common/` as pure moves, so one copy exists.

**Plan against code, found while writing.** `fixture_seq` restarts per process (`tests/common/http.rs:94-97`); `Home::next_scenario` is private (`tests/common/home.rs:150-151`); the WowAce, git, WoWInterface-per-version and Tukui-zip builders are private to their suites; `Home::installed_behind` ages only the memo's `entries`; only GitHub has a cheap probe (`src/sources/github.rs:160`), so the other four sources are counted by their one revalidating fetch; a WowAce re-tag keeps its release id and changes `selection` through the pinned tree URL; `remove`'s no-op is `not_found` (`src/app/remove.rs:181-209`); and the split race's second applier never reaches the failpoints the plan pauses it at, which the test turns into its assertion.

**Risks and how they are watched.**
- #19, a token that stales for no reason (owners D1, E6): every fresh apply after a re-preview, every concurrent row's fix and the Tukui cache-hit row apply a plan in an unchanged world; a spurious `plan_stale` there is filed against D1.
- #6, tokens too sensitive (owner D1): `binary_changed` is intended; the lifecycle checks the refusal says why.
- #14, the milestone's size: 4 units of slack, off the critical path, but H4 and T3 wait for it; the five subtasks run in parallel lanes (only the lifecycle waits for the per-command homes).
- Flakiness and test time: markers instead of sleeps, bounded waits, a 60 s pause ceiling, T1's run timeout; about 45 scenarios plus one 31 s timeout, recorded in the close comment.

**What it unblocks, and why they wait.** H4 (the README final pass) reconciles the tests table and the real-machine bullet this bead writes, and matches test counts against the code. T3 (slice 2 end to end, an edge added at filing) runs its demo items ("a release landing in between gives `plan_stale`, and the re-preview shows it", "two appliers never split a plan", "a Tukui plan applies from the cache") on this bead's builders and patterns, and needs every slice-2 leaf closed.

**How it serves the milestone.** G-M4-3 (what was previewed is what runs, target by target, against new releases, concurrent changes, other binaries, expiry, missing inputs and a second applier, with `plans show` reconciling) and G-M4-6 (stale runs change nothing; dry runs take no lock even while the test holds the global lock and the lease). Checkpoint criteria 7 (its release-landing, two-applier and lifecycle rows, and one concurrent-change test per storable command), 6 (the every-path bullet, through the no-op rows) and 17 (it owns `apply_one_update_and_undo`). Vision D31: what a human approved is exactly what runs.

description:
Part 1 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.7 (Release drift and apply races, end to end). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

D7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.7`) is the verification leaf of M4's stored plans: it owns no feature code, and runs end to end, through the real binary on synthetic homes, the scenarios that the vision's M4 checkpoint and the decisions M4-D20 and M4-D61 promise: "a release landing in between yields `plan_stale`, never a different install"; two appliers of one plan never split it; another command's interference is reported per target. Product defects its scenarios find are filed as bugs `discovered-from` the subtask that found them; builder defects are fixed in place; no scenario is weakened to pass.

This part builds the release landings and proves the release-drift half of M4-D20 for every source and every release-bearing command:

- **M4-D20, restated.** A typed `--if-match` run uses its command's normal freshness: `install`, `copy` and `pin` revalidate their sources; `update`, `sync` and `adopt` answer from the 15-minute release memo (`SOURCE_RECHECK_MIN_INTERVAL`), so a release landing inside that window does not stale a typed run, which does exactly what the preview showed. `apply` always revalidates every source it touches (D5's `Context.force_revalidate`), so a release that landed since the preview changes the token's `selection` and the plan is `plan_stale`, never a different install. `apply`'s probes write the release memo, stale or not, so the re-preview after a stale `apply` shows the new release (otherwise preview, stale, the same preview would loop). *Why:* a typed `--if-match` is an agent asserting "do what I just saw"; `apply` is the moment of approval, and approving "update DBM" means approving the version shown. *Rejected:* revalidating on every `--if-match` run (as costly as an unbound install, for nothing); installing the old release at `apply` though a newer one exists (it installs what the user would no longer choose).
- **Checkpoint criterion 7, the rows this part proves:** "A release landing between the preview and `apply` gives `plan_stale` (`details.changed: ["selection"]`), never a different install. This is tested for `install`, `update`, `sync` and `copy` with fixture sequences in which the newest release changes." "The re-preview that follows a stale `apply` shows the new release (the probe refreshed the memo)." And the plan's Tukui row: "a Tukui `install` whose first dry run downloads and whose `apply` hits the cache, with no release change, **succeeds** (deferred releases are keyed without their URL)".
- **The token's `selection` part** (M4-D19): per target, the folder ops, each change `{addon, ref, kind, fields, from_version, to_version, folders{…}}`, each release `{release_id, url, expected_hash, blob_sha256}` (a deferred asset such as Tukui's keyed `{source, key, release_id, expected_hash, blob_sha256}` without its URL, which is `None` on a cache hit), and `creates_addons_dir`. A newer release changes it; nothing else in these scenarios changes `targets` or `observed`, which is why the expected set is exactly `["selection"]`.
- **Why it is its own step:** the landing builders are the infrastructure slice 2's end-to-end suite reuses (T3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.3`, runs its "a release landing in between gives `plan_stale`, and the re-preview shows it" and "a Tukui plan applies from the cache" items on them), and the release matrix is independent of D7's state-drift and race parts.

**Facts this part relies on** (verified at `c0ab5e9`, plus the leaves before D7):

- `common::http::fixture_seq` serves its responses in order with the last repeating, but "replay restarts every sequence in each process, so a sequence never spans two CLI runs" (`tests/common/http.rs:94-97`). A preview and its `apply` are two processes, so a landing is a second scenario directory. `Home::scenario(name)` makes a fresh, empty one (`tests/common/home.rs:81-86`); `Home::next_scenario` (private, `:150-160`) makes one that starts as a copy of the current one; each run reads the current one through `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES` (`:254-266`). `Home::installed_behind` (`:95-118`) installs an old GitHub tag, then serves a newer one and ages the memo's `entries` a day.
- Builders: GitHub `gh_release_v`, `gh_latest` (replaces an earlier `releases/latest` fixture of that repository by its URL) in `tests/common/http.rs:142-213`; WoWInterface `wowi_file`, `wowi_details`, `details` in `tests/common/wowi.rs:85-160` (the per-version builder `bugsack`, private to `tests/sources_wowi.rs:86-102`, is the pattern: a zip whose TOC carries `## X-WoWI-ID` and whose `core.lua` differs per version, with its `filedetails` entry); Tukui `entry`, `elvui`, `tukui_list`, `tukui_addon` (one download token per call, the last repeating), `tukui_download`, `etag` in `tests/common/tukui.rs`, while `elvui_zip(version)` is private to `tests/sources_tukui.rs:68-82`; WowAce `serve_recorded` (`:42-51`), `serve(dir, method, url, status, body)` (`:53-75`), `moved(tag, rev)` (`:76-95`), `retagged_tree(dir, rev)` (`:96-113`) and `index(entries)` (`:149-161`, which `retagged_tree` calls) are private to the `support` module of `tests/sources_wowace.rs`, over the recording `tests/fixtures/http/wowace-bug-grabber/` (BugGrabber's tag list, `v12.1.1` at revision 403), with the tags URL `TAGS = "https://repos.wowace.com/wow/bug-grabber/tags/"` at `:719`. A re-tag of the installed tag is an update, installed at its new revision while the release id stays `wowace:bug-grabber@v12.1.1` (`only_a_re_tag_of_the_installed_tag_is_an_update`, `:739-806`). git's synthetic repository (`commits/<branch>.atom` plus `codeload.github.com/<o>/<r>/zip/<sha>`) is private to `tests/git_github.rs:160-205`; a git head's release version is its sha's first 7 characters and its archive name `<repo>-<version>.zip` (`src/sources/git_github.rs:257-276`).
- The memo's window timestamps are `entries[].fetched_at`, `tukui_list.fetched_at` and `look_backs[].at` (`src/state/memo.rs:29-54, 165-173`); `omaddons::state::memo::load(&paths)` and `Home::seed_memo` read and write it.
- **What a revalidation costs per source.** Only GitHub implements `Source::probe` (`src/sources/github.rs:160-176`; the default is `None`, `src/sources/mod.rs:258-261`). Under `Revalidate` a memo entry with a probe is probed, anything else is fetched (`decide`, `src/resolve/cache.rs:84-102`). The `net.log` purposes: GitHub `release-latest` (`src/sources/github.rs:601`), plus `release-json` (`:673`) when the tag moved; git `commits-atom` (`src/sources/git_github.rs:135`); WoWInterface `wowi-details` (`src/sources/wowi.rs:102`); Tukui `tukui-list` (`src/sources/tukui.rs:100`), plus `tukui-addon` (`:248`) when a download needs a token; WowAce `wowace-tags`, a `PROPFIND` (`src/sources/wowace.rs:106`). Downloads are `asset` (`src/engine/blobs.rs:275`). `common::netlog::net_log(&home)` returns a `NetLogView` with `count_purpose` (`tests/common/netlog.rs:15-60`).
- Freshness: `install` (`src/app/install.rs:541-547`) and `copy` (`src/app/copy.rs:282-286`) revalidate; `update` (`src/app/update.rs:154-160`) and `sync` (`src/app/sync.rs:678-682`) use the window, 15 minutes (`src/politeness.rs:35`). `update -t retail` updates every managed addon on retail (an empty `UpdateArgs.addons` means all, `src/app/update.rs:39-44`); `sync` installs what the desired file lists and does not update (it computes its changes before any engine run, `src/app/sync.rs:670-676`); `copy` installs each addon of `--from` on `--to` from its ref, unpinned (`src/app/copy.rs:1-11`).
- Planning does every download before the token check (`src/engine/tx.rs:401-407`): a stale `apply` has already cached the newer archive when it refuses, and a later run finds it by expected hash or by the candidate fact its download recorded (`fetch_blob`, `src/engine/plan.rs:4815-4855`).
- A deferred asset's planned URL is its canonical URL after a fresh download and `None` after a blob-cache hit (`src/engine/plan.rs:3862-3871`, `:4833-4840`). The existing Tukui test shows a real run after its dry run "took the blob the dry run cached, so it resolved nothing: no URL" and made only the list request (`tests/sources_tukui.rs:262-321`).
- From D5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`, `omaddons apply`): `apply <id> --json` data `{plan_id, applied{command, display_argv}, approved, result, outcomes[{target, key, status, tx, error_code}]}`; a token mismatch is `plan_stale` (not retryable) with `details.changed` and `fix_argv` = `preview_argv(display_argv)`; history lines it commits carry `plan`. `precondition::preview_argv` is public (`src/app/precondition.rs:229-237`). From D4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`, the plan store): `tests/common/plans.rs` (`read_plan`, `plan_files`). From D9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.9`): `tests/common/plans.rs::plan_id`. From T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`): `TestLog` (`tlog!()`, `log.step`, `log.run`, `log.case`, `log.tree`, `log.assert_unchanged`, `log.diff`, `log.json`, `log.note`, `log.assert_eq`; `Ran::{ok, fails, data, envelope}`; `Runner` for `Home`). `tests/apply.rs` exists (D4, D5 and D8 write to it).

## Technical Approach

### 1. `tests/common/landing.rs` (new; `pub mod landing;` in `tests/common/mod.rs`)

```rust
//! Release landings (D7): one addon per source whose newest release a test moves forward
//! between two runs of the binary. Replay restarts every fixture sequence in each process
//! (`http::fixture_seq`), so "the next probe answers a newer release" is a second scenario:
//! `land` copies the home's current scenario (`Home::next_scenario`) and serves release
//! n + 1 there as the newest; the next run of the binary replays it.

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Source { GitHub, Git, Wowi, Tukui, WowAce }
impl Source {
    pub const ALL: [Source; 5] = [Source::GitHub, Source::Git, Source::Wowi, Source::Tukui, Source::WowAce];
    pub fn label(self) -> &'static str;      // "github", "git", "wowi", "tukui", "wowace"
}
pub struct Landing { source: Source, newest: u32 }
impl Landing {
    /// Serves release 1 as the newest, in a fresh copy of the home's scenario.
    pub fn start(home: &mut Home, source: Source) -> Self;
    /// Serves release `newest + 1` as the newest, in a fresh copy; returns its version.
    pub fn land(&mut self, home: &mut Home) -> String;
    pub fn source(&self) -> Source;
    pub fn newest(&self) -> u32;
    pub fn r#ref(&self) -> &'static str;
    pub fn version(&self, n: u32) -> String;
    /// A file under `Interface/AddOns` that only release `n` has, with its content.
    pub fn marker(&self, n: u32) -> Option<(String, String)>;
    /// The `net.log` purpose of this source's revalidation request.
    pub fn probe(&self) -> &'static str;
}
```

| Source | `ref` | Release n's fixtures (n ≤ 9) | `version(n)` | `marker(n)` | `probe()` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GitHub | `gh:o/foo` | for every k ≤ n, `gh_release_v(dir, "https://github.com/o/foo", "v{k}", [("Foo.zip", [("mainline", 120105), ("mists", 50504)], [("Foo/Foo.toc", "## Interface: 120105, 50504\n## Version: v{k}\n"), ("Foo/core.lua", "-- foo release {k}\n")])])`; then `gh_latest(dir, base, "v{n}")` | `v{n}` | `Foo/core.lua`, `-- foo release {n}\n` | `release-latest` |
