title: The approval witness and the re-judged operations checked under the commit lock
description:
Part 1 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8 (The approval checked again under the commit lock). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

D8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8`) makes a run bound to its preview (`--if-match <token>`) check its approval a second time inside the commit window, under the global lock, before the first managed mutation. Today a bound run is checked once against its token, by its own planning before anything is staged (`Binding::plan`), and under the lock the engine compares only the target record's generation (`Binding::moved`, `src/engine/tx.rs:1050-1056`), then re-judges the work offline (`:1095-1142`) without comparing the outcome with what the preview approved. An edit made after the first check by anything that is not omaddons (a person, an editor, a sync tool, a hand-installed folder) moves no generation, so the run commits over bytes its preview never observed. Between the first check and the lock the run stages archives, waits out the racy slack and copies SavedVariables, which can take seconds.

This part adds the two under-lock checks of M4-D60: the approval witness checked again (M4-D60 check 2.2) and the re-judged operations compared with the approved ones (check 2.4), with their refusals, the `-v` note that reports what the check cost, and README's statement of the guarantee. It is its own step because it is the content half of the guarantee and lands as one commit; part 2 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8.2) adds the identity predicates on each rename on top of it.

**M4-D60, as this part needs it.** The witness (the `ApprovalWitness` of D1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1`, `precondition::of_plan` and the approval witness; one per target) records every live folder a replace or remove will move as a content digest (`EntryDigest`: each regular file's path, size and SHA-256, each symlink's target, each directory), every name the plan creates as absent, the client marker's digest, the local inputs, a copy's source folders, an adopt's folders, the dependency choices and the judge digest. Clean files take their digests from the files index behind a racy-clean stamp check, so a clean file costs a `stat`, and D1 keeps, privately, each folder's settled `TreeStamp` from the moment it computed the digest. Under the lock: re-read each witnessed folder's `TreeStamp`; equal to the private stamp, it is unchanged (a settled stamp proves an unchanged digest); otherwise re-hash it and compare the digest. Every created name must still be absent and the marker unchanged. Then the re-judged operations, in the token's selection terms, must equal the run's own pre-lock operations for that target (which the first check proved equal to the token). Any mismatch is `plan_stale` with `details.changed` naming the part (`observed` for the witness, `selection` for the operations). *Rejected there:* generations only (misses every writer that is not omaddons); re-hashing every file under the lock (correct but costly, and unnecessary behind a settled stamp); an absolute compare-and-swap promise (Linux offers none). M3-D46's refusal shape holds: `plan_stale` not retryable, `details.changed`, `fix_argv` the same command with `--dry-run` in place of `--if-match <token>`.

**What this part relies on** (D1 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1`, D2 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2` and D3 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.3`, all landed before it; locations verified at `c0ab5e9` for the existing code):

- `Plan.witnesses: Vec<ApprovalWitness>` (`#[serde(skip)]`), one per target in `plan.targets` order, collected only when `TxRequest.witness` is `Some` (D2 and D3 set it for dry runs and bound runs). `ApprovalWitness { target: TargetRef, marker: Option<String>, folders: Vec<FolderWitness>, absent: Vec<String>, inputs, dependencies: Vec<DependencyChoice>, judge, stamps (private), cost (private) }`; `FolderWitness { role: Replaced | Removed | CopySource | Adopted, key, digest }`; `absent` holds folder keys and `"Interface/AddOns"`; `marker` is `"sha256:<hex>"`, `"link:<target>"`, `"kind:<type>"` or `None`; `DependencyChoice { requester, folder, by: Installs(addon) | Unmanaged | Unresolved(reason) | Failed(ref) }`. `pub(crate) fn stamp(&self, dir) -> Option<&TreeStamp>`; `witness::folder(dir, index, limits, now_ns, between) -> Result<Folder>` (digest, optional settled stamp, cost); `TreeStamp::read_at_most`.
- `PlanBinding` (D2, `src/app/precondition.rs`): `expected: Option<String>` (`None` when a dry run only computes its token), extras, its command path and preview argv; `plan()` checks the token; `moved()` refuses with `targets`.
- `Binding` (`src/engine/tx.rs:187-206`): `plan`, `undo`, `moved`, `observed` (defaults to `moved`). M3's `RemoveBinding` (`src/app/precondition.rs:279-296`) reaches `tx.rs`'s commit window; `UndoBinding` and `RestoreBinding` never do.
- The commit window `locked()` (`src/engine/tx.rs:976-1369`): `refuse_newer_state` again (`:1047`), the generation check (`:1050-1056`), `TargetState::now` (`:1095`), the re-judge loop over `tp.work` (`:1105-1141`), `settle_handovers` (`:1142`), `engine.revalidated` (`:1143`), "everything became unnecessary" (`:1144-1164`), `Journal::create` (`:1226`). A new target is registered at `:1034-1044` (`ensure_registered` writes the client marker) before the checks.
- A records-only forget whose guard fails while the generation is unchanged re-judges to `Planned::nothing()` (`src/engine/plan.rs:4045-4048`, the guard at `src/engine/edit.rs:318-338`), so a bound run whose forget no longer applies ends today as "unchanged".
- `copy` installs each addon on `--to` from its ref and never reads `--from`'s folders (`src/app/copy.rs:1-11`, `:238-260`). **Correction:** the plan's D8 step 3 ("a copy's staged tree digest must equal its witnessed source digest") cannot hold; the copy-source folders are re-checked under the lock instead (Technical Approach 5).
- Staging checks every extracted file's size and SHA-256 against the inspection (`src/engine/stage.rs:132-165`).
- Commands log their outcome's `notes` as `-v` debug events (`src/app/mod.rs:392-420`), and `install`, `update` and `copy` carry `TxOutcome.notes` into them.

## Technical Approach

### 1. The trait (`src/engine/tx.rs`)

Add beside `Binding`:

```rust
pub struct UnderLock<'a> {
    pub id: &'a str,                           // the target's id, for messages
    pub planned: &'a TargetRef,                // as the plan named it
    pub key: TargetKey,                        // its key now
    pub registered_here: bool,                 // this window registered it (its marker is new)
    pub client: &'a ClientPaths,
    pub witness: Option<&'a ApprovalWitness>,  // the run's own pre-lock witness, if collected
    pub limits: &'a ArchiveLimits,             // EngineCtx.limits
}
```

and to the trait two methods with defaults that accept, so M3's bindings keep their behaviour:

```rust
fn witness(&self, _at: &UnderLock<'_>) -> Result<Option<RecheckCost>> { Ok(None) }
fn operations(&self, _at: &UnderLock<'_>, _approved: &Operations, _rejudged: &Operations) -> Result<()> { Ok(()) }
```

*Decided while writing this bead:* the engine owns the mechanics (the plan, the witness with its private stamps, the paths, the lock) and passes them in; the binding owns the policy and the refusal (its command path and preview argv). `witness` returns the check's cost so the engine can log it.

### 2. Wiring in `locked()`

- `run`'s loop (`:429-468`) finds each target's witness in `plan.witnesses` by `TargetRef::of(tp.key, &tp.target)` (never by position) and passes `Option<&ApprovalWitness>` to `commit_target` and on to `locked()` (both already carry `#[allow]`/`#[expect]` for their argument count).
- After the generation check (`:1050-1056`), build `UnderLock` (`registered_here` is `discovered.target.key.is_none()`; `key` the key the window has now) and call `let checked = ctx.binding.map(|b| b.witness(&at)).transpose()?.flatten();`. The refusal returns before the re-judge; nothing has moved.
- Extract the re-judge (`:1095-1142`, from `TargetState::now` to `settle_handovers`) unchanged into `fn rejudge_target(..) -> Result<Rejudged>` returning `works`, `changes`, `warnings`, `notes` and `reload_required`, so the unchanged-world property can be unit tested.
- After it, when `ctx.binding` is `Some`: `binding.operations(&at, &Operations::of(&tp.work, &tp.changes), &Operations::of(&works, &changes))?`, before `engine.revalidated` and before the "everything became unnecessary" return. *Decided while writing this bead:* a bound run whose re-judge leaves nothing to do while its approved operations were not empty is therefore refused (`selection`) rather than reported unchanged: "exactly the approved operations, or none" reports the none as stale.
- *Decided while writing this bead:* an error from the re-judge keeps today's handling (the command fails with that error, nothing moved); it is more precise than `plan_stale`, and adding its cause would add `details` keys.
- Leave one slot for part 2: the identity capture goes between the generation check and the witness check. This part adds a comment there naming it.

### 3. `witness::recheck` (`src/engine/witness.rs`)

```rust
pub struct RecheckAt<'a> { pub client: &'a ClientPaths, pub registered_key: Option<TargetKey>, pub limits: &'a ArchiveLimits }
pub struct Rechecked { pub drift: Option<Drift>, pub cost: RecheckCost }
pub enum Drift { Marker, Appeared { name: String }, DependencyGone { requester: String, folder: String },
                 Folder { role: WitnessRole, key: String, why: FolderDrift } }
pub enum FolderDrift { Changed, Unreadable, TooLarge }
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct RecheckCost { pub folders: u64, pub entries_stamped: u64, pub folders_rehashed: u64,
                         pub files_hashed: u64, pub bytes_hashed: u64, pub elapsed_us: u64 }
pub fn recheck(witness: &ApprovalWitness, at: &RecheckAt<'_>) -> Rechecked
```

Reads only. Cheapest first; stops at the first drift:

1. **Marker.** `registered_key: Some(k)` (this window registered the target): the marker must name `k`. Otherwise the marker reader of D1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1`, the approval witness) must return exactly `witness.marker`. *Decided while writing this bead:* registration by the run itself writes a marker the preview could not see, so for a target the run registers, the check is that the marker is the one it wrote; registration by another process between the first check and the lock changes no addon, and a commit it made moves the generation.
2. **Created names and unmanaged dependencies.** One `read_dir` of `client.addons()` (absent `AddOns`: no names), names ASCII case-folded like `FolderName::key()`. Each `absent` folder key must not be listed (`Appeared`); `"Interface/AddOns"` must have no case variant (`client.addons_case_variants()` empty). Each `DependencyChoice` with `by: Unmanaged` must still have its folder listed (`DependencyGone`). *Decided while writing this bead:* this presence check is added to the plan's list because the re-judge does not resolve dependencies again (`rejudge` copies the planned `deps`, `src/engine/plan.rs:2812-2813`), so a deleted unmanaged dependency would otherwise be committed past.
3. **Folders.** D1's `ApprovalWitness` gains a private `dir: PathBuf` per folder, set by `witness::collect` where it already joins the path (the target's `addons_dir()` with the live spelling, or the copy source's `addons_dir()`), never serialized and never hashed, so no token moves; `pub(crate) fn folder_dirs()` iterates `(&FolderWitness, &Path)`. For each, in witness order: `TreeStamp::read_at_most(dir, limits.max_entries)` (over the bound: `TooLarge`; missing: treated as absent); equal to `witness.stamp(dir)`: unchanged; otherwise `witness::folder(dir, None, limits, Timestamp::now().as_nanosecond(), &mut || {})` (every file hashed, no index) and compare with `FolderWitness.digest`: equal passes (a `touch` or `chmod` lands here), different is `Changed`. An absent folder digests as `a`, so a copy source already gone at the preview stays unchanged. An unreadable entry is `Unreadable`; past `max_entries` or `max_uncompressed` is `TooLarge`. *Decided while writing this bead:* both fail closed as drifts, because the preview read the folder within its limits; the fix (preview again) then reports D1's precise `io` or `archive_too_large`.
4. `elapsed_us` from `std::time::Instant` around the whole check.

*Decided while writing this bead:* local inputs are not re-read (staging verified every file against the inspection, and the commit installs the staged copy), nor is the judge digest (the re-judge uses the rules this process loaded, which the first check compared).

`Drift::describe()`: "the client's marker changed"; "a folder named <key> appeared in AddOns"; "Interface/AddOns now exists"; "<folder>, which <requester> requires, is no longer in AddOns"; "<key> changed after the preview"; "<key> cannot be read now"; "<key> grew past the archive limits". Folder keys only: never file content, digests or paths below `WTF/`.

### 4. `Operations` (`src/engine/witness.rs`)

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Operations { pub ops: Vec<PlannedOp>, pub changes: Vec<Change> }
impl Operations { pub fn of(works: &[AddonWork], changes: &[Change]) -> Self; pub fn describe_difference(&self, other: &Self) -> String }
```

- `ops` from each work's swap ops by planning's `PlannedOp` rule (`src/engine/plan.rs:4392-4422`): `Add { name }` → `(add, name, addon)`, `Replace { live, .. }` → `(replace, live, addon)`, `Remove { live }` → `(remove, live, addon)`; sorted by folder key, op, addon. `changes`: the `Change` values, sorted by addon ASCII lowercase, addon, ref.
- *Decided while writing this bead:* both sides come from the one renderer over the engine's own works and changes, so an unchanged world agrees by construction; `releases` and `creates_addons_dir` are not re-derived (the re-judge is offline and stages only planned blobs, and a dropped work drops its change; a created `AddOns` is the witness's `"Interface/AddOns"` absent name).
- `describe_difference`: the first addon whose entry differs, as "<addon>: <kind> no longer planned", "<addon>: <kind> now planned", or "<addon>: its folders differ".

### 5. `copy`

No staged-digest check. *Decided while writing this bead:* the `CopySource` folders are re-checked by `recheck` like every other witnessed folder (section 3), because `copy` never reads them; a source edit between the first check and the lock is caught, which covers the plan's "between check 1 and staging" and more. The global lock is one lock for every client.

### 6. The refusals (`src/app/precondition.rs`)

- `pub fn stale_because(command: &str, changed: &[Part], preview: &[String], why: &str) -> Error`: `stale`'s error with the message "this <command> is no longer what its preview showed (<parts> changed: <why>); nothing was changed: preview it again". Same `details` (`{"changed": [...]}`), `retryable` false, `fix_argv` the preview. No new `details` key (§8.1 rule 1).
- `PlanBinding::witness`: `expected: None` → `Ok(None)`; no witness → `internal` ("the bound run collected no approval witness for <target>"), failing closed; otherwise `recheck`, and a drift → `stale_because(command, &[Part::Observed], preview, &drift.describe())`, else `Ok(Some(cost))`.
- `PlanBinding::operations`: `expected: None` → `Ok(())`; equal → `Ok(())`; else `stale_because(command, &[Part::Selection], preview, &approved.describe_difference(rejudged))`.
- `RemoveBinding::operations`: the same with `"remove"` (its token is unchanged, M4-D60); it keeps the default `witness`.

### 7. The cost note

When `checked` is `Some(cost)`, `locked()` pushes onto the outcome's `notes`: `"<target>: approval checked under the lock in <elapsed_us> us: folders <folders>, entries <entries_stamped>, rehashed <folders_rehashed>, files <files_hashed>, bytes <bytes_hashed>"`. A `-v` debug line, not a data key. Part 5 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8.5) parses it.

### 8. README

- "Previews and `--if-match`": replace "The real run plans again and computes the token from its own plan before it stages anything, and compares it again under the lock (a commit that slips in between counts too)" with the bullet **Checked again under the lock** (the text in the parent bead's Technical Approach 9, without its identity sentence), and the scope sentence that D2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2`, `--if-match` on `install`, `update`, `sync` and `copy`) wrote with **What the guarantee covers**, ending at "omaddons does not promise a compare-and-swap against another program writing into `AddOns` in the last instant before a rename … `omaddons undo <tx>` brings it back." Part 2 adds the identity and repair sentences.
- Safety model, "Transactions" diagram: after "re-check the target's generation", add "bound runs: check the approval again (witnessed folders, created names, marker, dependencies), then the re-judged operations".

**Files:** `src/engine/tx.rs`, `src/engine/witness.rs`, `src/app/precondition.rs`, README.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `Binding` has `witness` and `operations` with defaults that accept; `PlanBinding` implements both and `RemoveBinding` implements `operations`; `UndoBinding` and `RestoreBinding` are unchanged.
- [ ] In `locked()`, a bound run calls `witness` after the generation check and before the re-judge, and `operations` after `settle_handovers` and before `engine.revalidated`; an unbound run calls neither; a moved generation still refuses with `targets` and calls neither.
- [ ] `witness::recheck` finds each drift of its unit table and passes a touched, chmodded or byte-identical folder; an unchanged settled folder costs stamps only (`rehashed 0`).
- [ ] An unchanged world re-judges to the approved `Operations` for every plan shape of the unit property, and a bound run whose re-judge leaves nothing to do is refused with `selection`.
- [ ] Refusals are `plan_stale`, not retryable, `details` exactly `{"changed": ["observed"]}` or `{"changed": ["selection"]}`, `fix_argv` the preview, and a message naming what changed by folder key.
- [ ] A bound engine-command window logs the `-v` cost note; `remove`'s logs none.
- [ ] The pinned tokens (`a_fixture_token_never_drifts`, `of_plan_fixture_token_never_drifts`, `of_remove_keeps_its_m3_token`) and every existing test pass unchanged.
- [ ] README's "Previews and `--if-match`" and the transaction diagram say what this commit makes true, and nothing more.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

- **`src/engine/witness.rs`**, over temp folders and witnesses collected with an injected `now_ns`:
  - `recheck_passes_an_unchanged_settled_folder_by_stamps_alone`: one folder of 13 entries, settled → no drift; cost `{folders: 1, entries_stamped: 13, folders_rehashed: 0, files_hashed: 0}`.
  - `recheck_rehashes_a_folder_without_a_private_stamp_and_passes_equal_bytes`: collected with `now_ns` inside the racy slack (no private stamp) → no drift, `folders_rehashed: 1`.
  - `recheck_passes_a_touched_or_chmodded_folder_after_rehashing_it`: cases `touch_one_file`, `chmod_one_file` → no drift, `rehashed 1`.
  - `recheck_finds_each_drift`: cases `clean_file_edited`, `same_size_edit_with_mtime_restored` (`File::set_times` puts the mtime back), `file_deleted`, `file_replaced` (written beside and renamed over), `symlink_added`, `empty_dir_added`, `empty_file_added`, `folder_deleted`, `folder_replaced_by_a_file` → `Folder { why: Changed }` with the folder's key and role; `folder_replaced_by_identical_copy` → no drift.
  - `recheck_finds_a_created_name_appearing`: cases `exact_case`, `other_case` (`foo_extra` vs `Foo_Extra`) → `Appeared`. `recheck_finds_addons_appearing_when_the_plan_creates_it`: cases `Interface/AddOns`, `interface/addons`.
  - `recheck_finds_a_changed_marker`: cases `bytes_changed`, `replaced_by_a_symlink`, `deleted` → `Marker`. `recheck_accepts_the_marker_this_window_registered`: names `registered_key` → pass; names another key → `Marker`.
  - `recheck_finds_an_unmanaged_dependency_gone` → `DependencyGone { requester, folder }`.
  - `recheck_fails_closed_on_an_unreadable_entry` (mode 000, no private stamp) → `Unreadable`; when the test runs as root, where mode bits do not stop reads, it asserts a pass and its message says why. `recheck_fails_closed_past_the_limits`: `max_entries` 5 and, separately, `max_uncompressed` 10 bytes → `TooLarge`.
  - `recheck_reads_copy_sources_where_the_witness_read_them` (a `CopySource` folder under a second client dir).
  - `recheck_stops_at_the_first_drift`: two drifted folders → the first's drift, and the cost counts one folder.
  - `recheck_writes_nothing`: the tree hash of the temp root before and after every case above.
  - `operations_of_sorts_ops_and_changes` (shuffled inputs, equal results), `operations_render_swap_ops_as_planning_renders_planned_ops` (Add → name, Replace → live spelling, Remove → live), `describe_difference_names_the_first_difference` (cases `dropped`, `added`, `folders_differ`).
- **`src/engine/tx.rs`**, through `engine::testing::TxScene::with_ctx` with a recording test `Binding` (it pushes `"plan"`, `"moved"`, `"witness"`, `"operations"` into a `RefCell<Vec<&str>>` and returns what the case says):
  - `an_unchanged_world_rejudges_to_the_approved_operations`: cases `install_new`, `update`, `update_with_a_handover`, `install_with_a_dependency`, `remove`, `forget`, `adopt`, `pin`, `unpin`, `first_install_creating_addons`, `force_over_an_unmanaged_folder`, `sync_prune`; each plans, then `rejudge_target` over the same scene, and asserts `Operations::of(tp.work, tp.changes) == Operations::of(works, changes)`, printing both on failure.
  - `the_bound_checks_run_after_the_generation_and_around_the_rejudge`: calls `["plan", "witness", "operations"]`; with the record's generation moved before the lock: `["plan", "moved"]`.
  - `a_witness_refusal_moves_nothing` and `an_operations_refusal_moves_nothing`: the error is the binding's; folders (tree hash), the record, the files index and history unchanged; no journal; the stage and in-flight lock cleaned up.
  - `a_bound_run_left_with_nothing_to_do_is_refused_not_unchanged`: a forget whose folder reappears between planning and the commit → the binding's `operations` sees approved one change, re-judged none.
  - `an_unbound_commit_calls_no_check`; `m3_bindings_accept_by_default` (a binding implementing only `plan`, `undo`, `moved`); `a_checked_window_notes_its_cost` (the note's format, parsed back into its six numbers).
- **`src/app/precondition.rs`**: `plan_binding_refuses_a_drift_as_observed`, `plan_binding_refuses_other_operations_as_selection`, `plan_binding_without_a_token_checks_nothing`, `plan_binding_without_a_witness_fails_closed`, `remove_binding_compares_operations_and_binds_no_witness`, `stale_because_keeps_details_retryability_and_fix` (equal to `stale`'s error but for the message, which contains the reason); the pinned token tests unchanged.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

None in this part: the end-to-end witness scenarios are omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8.3's, the adversarial matrix omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8.4's. Every existing suite (`tests/preconditions.rs`, `tests/engine_crash.rs`, `tests/engine_concurrency.rs`, the binding scenarios of D2 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2` and D3 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.3`) must pass unchanged in this commit.

### Logging

## Considerations

title: Endpoint predicates on every swap rename, with the identities the under-lock check saw
description:
Part 2 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8 (The approval checked again under the commit lock). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

D8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8`) makes a run bound to its preview check its approval again inside the commit window. Part 1 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8.1) added the content half: under the global lock, before the first managed mutation, the witnessed folders, the created names, the marker and the re-judged operations are checked again. Between that check and each rename, M4-D60 re-checks only identity: "the swap's renames carry fsx endpoint predicates, the moved folder's identity and the destination's absence (or recorded identity, for an exchange), so a folder replaced in the last moment fails its operation and the transaction rolls back. Content is not re-hashed per operation." And it states the scope: "Between that check and an individual operation, only the identity of what moves is re-checked. omaddons does not promise a compare-and-swap against arbitrary writers … because no filesystem protocol it can use provides one."

Today no swap rename checks anything about its endpoints beyond the rename mode itself, so a folder replaced after the checks is swapped out as if it were the approved one. This part attaches the predicates, in a way that keeps the in-process rollback clean, and turns a refused rename of a bound run into the bound refusal. It is its own step because it changes the swap (`src/engine/swap.rs`), a different module from part 1's checks, and its correctness argument is about the journal, not the witness.

**Facts this part relies on** (verified at `c0ab5e9`; E13 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.13`, resource sets and fsx endpoint predicates, has landed):

- The swap (`src/engine/swap.rs:671-771`) renames in three phases: new and replacing folders go live (`Noreplace` for a new one, `Exchange` for a replaced one, or two plain renames where the filesystem lacks the flags), old versions move from the stage path to the snapshot, removals move to the snapshot. Each rename is journaled first by `Run::step` (`:871-880`, which discards the `StepRecord`), then run by `mutate_with` with `tree_before`/`tree_after` only (`:808-814`, `:836-869`).
- `Journal::step` records `from_id` and `to_id`, the identities at both paths **when it appends the step line**, before the rename (`src/engine/journal.rs:406-418`). Recovery's `ran` (`:1654-1675`) compares the identities now at the paths with the recorded ones: the before state means "did not run" (skip), the after state means "ran" (undo), neither stops the journal for manual repair with `internal`.
- `try_flagged` maps `FsxError::Precondition` to `plan_stale` only for `StepPurpose::SwapIn` (`:850-852`); otherwise, and in `plain` (`:858-869`), the error becomes `io` (`src/fsx/mutate.rs:58-73`). The swap's `stale()` is `PlanStaleSource::Replan` (`:913-919`), which `Error::plan_stale` makes retryable (`src/error.rs:587-593`), with a prose fix. README's error table says `plan_stale` is not retryable under `--if-match`.
- In `locked()` (`src/engine/tx.rs`) the planned swap ops are `planned_ops` (`:1010`); the swap is called at `:1240`; a failure inside the commit closure runs `recover_tx` and returns the original error when the transaction rolled back, or `recovery_failed(..)` (`:573-591`) when recovery itself failed (`:1273-1300`).
- `src/engine/undo.rs:514` also calls `swap()`; `undo.rs` is the one-leaf hot spot of E7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7`, undo of repairs), §10.5.
- From E13: `fsx::FileId` and `FileId::same` (inode and birth time, device ignored); `Expect::Absent | Expect::Present(Predicate)` with `Predicate { file_type, identity, sha256, mode, stamp, link_target }` (every given part checked together); `MutateOpts::expect_to`, the predicate on a rename's destination; checked in step 1 of `mutate_with`, before `fsx.mutate.checked`; a mismatch is `FsxError::Precondition` with a message naming the part.

## Technical Approach

### 1. `Seen`: the identities the checks are about

In `src/engine/swap.rs`:

```rust
/// The identities the commit window's checks saw of everything the swap moves (M4-D60
/// check 3), by folder key: every live folder a replace or remove moves, every staged folder.
#[derive(Debug, Default, Clone)]
pub struct Seen { live: BTreeMap<String, Option<FileId>>, staged: BTreeMap<String, Option<FileId>> }
impl Seen { pub fn capture(addons: &Path, ops: &[SwapOp], staged: &Staged) -> Self }
```

`capture` takes `FileId::of(addons.join(live))` for each `Replace { live, .. }` and `Remove { live, .. }`, and `FileId::of(path)` for each staged folder. In `locked()`, for every run (bound or not): `let seen = Seen::capture(&client.addons(), &planned_ops, staged);` immediately after the generation check and **before** part 1's witness check. *Decided while writing this bead:* capturing before the content check means the content check validates the very inodes the renames will require: a folder replaced after the capture fails at its rename (even with identical bytes), one replaced before it is what the witness check reads. Unbound runs get the same protection from this point on.

### 2. `swap_checked`, and `swap` kept for undo

```rust
pub fn swap_checked(s: &mut WriteSession<'_>, journal: &mut Journal, ops: &[SwapOp], staged: &Staged,
                    client: &ClientPaths, snapshot: &Path, seen: &Seen) -> Result<SwapReport>
pub fn swap(s, journal, ops, staged, client, snapshot) -> Result<SwapReport>  // swap_checked(.., &Seen::capture(..))
```

`locked()` calls `swap_checked(.., &seen)`. *Decided while writing this bead:* `swap()` keeps its signature and captures at its start, so `src/engine/undo.rs` gets the predicates without being edited (it is the one-leaf hot spot of E7, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7`, undo of repairs). An op whose folder `seen` lacks (an unbound run whose re-judge added it) is captured when the swap reaches it.

### 3. What each rename requires

`Move` gains the expected endpoints. Folders are directories; identities compare with `FileId::same`.

| Rename (purpose, mode) | `from` must be | `to` must be |
|---|---|---|
| new folder goes live (`SwapIn`, `Noreplace`) | the staged folder | absent |
| replaced folder (`SwapIn`, `Exchange`) | the staged folder | the live folder |
| fallback live to snapshot (`FallbackLiveToSnapshot`, plain) | the live folder | absent |
| fallback stage to live (`FallbackStageToLive`, plain) | the staged folder | absent |
| old version to snapshot (`OldToSnapshot`, `Noreplace`) | the live folder's identity (now at the stage path) | absent |
| removal (`RemoveToSnapshot`, `Noreplace`) | the live folder | absent |

### 4. Checked twice per rename

1. **Against the journal, before the rename.** `Run::step` returns the `StepRecord`. If `record.from_id` is not the expected `from` (by `FileId::same`), or `record.to_id` is not the expected `to` (`None` for absent, or the identity for an exchange), refuse before renaming: `stale(format!("{} changed after the approval was checked", path.display()))`. The record holds the identities of that moment, so recovery finds the step in its before state, skips it and undoes the earlier steps: a clean rollback. *Decided while writing this bead:* this is what makes "a folder replaced in the last moment fails its operation, and the engine's existing in-process rollback restores the target" true; a predicate that failed only after the step line would leave the step in neither state.
2. **On the rename.** `mutate_with(s, from, Op::Rename { to, mode }, MutateOpts { expect: Some(Expect::Present(Predicate { file_type: Some(FileKind::Directory), identity: Some(from_id), ..Default::default() })), expect_to: Some(Expect::Absent or Expect::Present(Predicate { file_type: Some(FileKind::Directory), identity: Some(to_id), .. })), ..m.opts() })`. This narrows the remaining interval to fsx's own check, immediately before the operation.

**The residual window.** A replacement after the step line and before fsx's check (in tests only reachable by pausing at `engine.swap.before_rename`) fails the predicate before that rename runs, and leaves that step in neither state: recovery stops it for manual repair (`internal`, wrapped by `recovery_failed` with `details.journal_pending`), which the doctor's stuck-journal findings and repairs handle (F1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1`, F2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.2`). A replacement between fsx's check and the `renameat2` call is outside every check. Neither loses data. *Decided while writing this bead:* keep the predicate on the rename anyway, because the alternative in that interval is committing an unapproved folder; omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8.4 pins this behaviour and README names it.

### 5. Every predicate failure is `plan_stale`

- `try_flagged`: `Err(FsxError::Precondition(why)) => Err(stale(format!("{} changed after planning: {why}", to.display())))` for **every** purpose (today only a swap-in; others become `io`). `plain`: the same mapping on its `mutate_with`. Op-rule failures ("does not exist", "the rename target exists") map the same way; in practice they arise only from races.
- For an unbound run this stays the retryable `Replan` form with its prose fix ("run the command again; it re-plans against the current folders").

### 6. A bound run's refusal

- `Binding` gains `fn operation_refused(&self, target: &str, _why: &str) -> Error { self.observed(target) }` (defaulted: undo's and the restores' bindings never reach `tx.rs`'s swap).
- `PlanBinding` and `RemoveBinding` implement it: `stale_because(<command>, &[Part::Observed], &self.preview, why)` (part 1's helper): `plan_stale`, not retryable, `details.changed: ["observed"]`, `fix_argv` the preview.
- In `locked()`'s error branch (`:1273-1300`): when recovery rolled back (`Ok(_)`), the error is `plan_stale` and `ctx.binding` is `Some`, return `binding.operation_refused(&target.id, &error.message)`; otherwise unchanged (a failed recovery stays `recovery_failed`). *Decided while writing this bead:* this aligns the code with README's error table ("not retryable under `--if-match`"); undo's bound refusals stay as they are (its binding and engine are not this bead's).

### 7. README

- "Previews and `--if-match`", **What the guarantee covers**: add after "caught up to that second check": "After it, each rename re-checks only the identity of the folder it moves and that its destination is still free, so a folder replaced in that interval rolls the transaction back." and at the end: "A folder swapped in the instant between a rename's journal line and the rename stops the transaction for repair (`omaddons doctor`), with nothing lost."
- Safety model, "Transactions" diagram, under "swap each folder (journal step per rename)": add "each rename: the folder it moves is the one checked, the destination still free".

**Files:** `src/engine/swap.rs`, `src/engine/tx.rs`, `src/app/precondition.rs`, README. Not `src/engine/undo.rs`, not `src/engine/journal.rs`, not `src/fsx/`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every swap rename of every purpose carries `expect` and `expect_to` built from `Seen`, and compares its journaled identities with them before it renames; `Seen` is captured in `locked()` after the generation check and before the witness check, for bound and unbound runs.
- [ ] A rename refused because its endpoint changed before its step line leaves that step reading as not run, and the in-process rollback restores every earlier step (unit tests per purpose).
- [ ] A predicate failure is `plan_stale` for every purpose; unbound it is the retryable `Replan` form; bound, after a clean rollback, it is `plan_stale`, not retryable, `details.changed: ["observed"]`, `fix_argv` the preview; after a failed rollback it stays `recovery_failed`.
- [ ] `src/engine/undo.rs` is unchanged and its swaps capture at the swap's start; every existing swap, undo and crash test passes unchanged.
- [ ] README states the per-operation identity check and the residual window, and the transaction diagram shows the rename check.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

- **`src/engine/swap.rs`** (its test module, with the engine's test journal and stage helpers):
  - `seen_captures_every_moving_and_staged_folder` (a replace, a remove and an add: two live identities, three staged).
  - `each_rename_refuses_an_endpoint_that_is_not_what_was_seen`: one named case per table row (`add_destination_taken`, `exchange_live_replaced`, `exchange_staged_replaced`, `fallback_live_replaced`, `fallback_stage_replaced`, `old_to_snapshot_source_replaced`, `remove_live_replaced`); each replaces the endpoint before the swap reaches it, then asserts `plan_stale`, that nothing was renamed at that step, and that `journal::ran` on the written record is `Ok(false)`. The `old_to_snapshot_source_replaced` case asserts only that: replacing the old version at the stage path also breaks the earlier exchange's after state, which no supported writer can do (Considerations), so its rollback is not asserted.
  - `a_refused_rename_after_earlier_steps_rolls_back_cleanly`: three exchanges, the third's live folder replaced; `recover_tx` restores the first two; every folder is wholly old.
  - `a_predicate_failure_is_plan_stale_for_every_purpose` (was `io` outside swap-in).
  - `swap_without_seen_captures_at_its_start` (the undo path).
  - Every existing test in the module unchanged.
- **`src/engine/tx.rs`**: `identities_are_captured_before_the_witness_check` (a test binding's `witness` replaces a live folder with an identical copy: the witness passes, the rename refuses); `a_bound_runs_refused_rename_becomes_the_bindings_refusal`; `an_unbound_runs_refused_rename_stays_retryable`; `a_refused_rename_whose_rollback_failed_stays_a_recovery_failure` (`engine.recover.step=error` in process).
- **`src/app/precondition.rs`**: `operation_refused_is_observed_and_not_retryable` for `PlanBinding` and `RemoveBinding`.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

None in this part (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8.3 runs the last-moment replacement through the binary, omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8.4 every journaled step). `tests/engine_crash.rs`, `tests/engine_concurrency.rs` and `tests/engine_undo.rs` must pass unchanged in this commit: their unbound swaps now carry the predicates.

### Logging

Table-driven unit tests, one name per case; each assertion message names the case, the purpose, the expected and the found identity (`FileId` debug form) and the error.

## Considerations

- **Correctness argument.** The rollback is clean exactly when the step record matches the world at refusal time. Comparing the record (taken at journaling) with `Seen` guarantees that for every refusal the swap makes itself; only fsx's own check, after the record, can refuse with a stale record, and that is the residual window.
- **Do not tamper-test omaddons' private directories.** `<meta>/stage/<tx>/` and `<meta>/snapshots/<tx>/` belong to the transaction. Replacing an entity there after an earlier step moved it violates that earlier step's after state, so recovery cannot decide it; that is not a supported scenario, and the matrices do not do it.
- **Hot spots:** `src/engine/swap.rs` and `src/engine/tx.rs` (D2 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2` → D8; E5 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`, the repair transaction, touches recovery calls only; G3 `omad-7ccp` last, which later routes these renames' directory fsyncs through `CommitWindow`); `src/app/precondition.rs` (D1 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1` first). `undo.rs` is not touched.
- **Cost:** one `statx` per moving or staged folder at capture, and two `lstat`s per rename for the predicates.
- **No new failpoint, constant, error code, `details` key or wire name;** the behaviour changes (`io` → `plan_stale`, and the bound form) go in the leaf's close comment.

## Dependencies

title: E2E: the witness scenarios, the operations check and the guarantee's scope
description:
Part 3 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8 (The approval checked again under the commit lock). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

D8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8`) makes a run bound to its preview (`--if-match <token>`) check its approval again inside the commit window: part 1 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8.1) checks the approval witness (every witnessed folder's content, the names the plan creates, the client marker, unmanaged dependencies) and the re-judged operations under the global lock; part 2 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8.2) makes each swap rename re-check the identity of what it moves. This part proves both through the real binary, end to end: every kind of hand edit, made at every moment that matters, refuses the bound run and leaves the target exactly as the edit left it; operations that re-judge differently refuse with `selection`; an unchanged world still commits exactly the preview; and the guarantee's stated scope (only identity after the under-lock check) is pinned by tests, so README's wording is checked rather than hoped.

It is its own step because it is a large, table-driven suite in new files, which can run in parallel with the adversarial matrix (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8.4) and the cost report (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8.5).

**What the suite relies on** (all landed before it):

- Bound runs of `install`, `update`, `sync`, `copy` (D2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2`), `pin`, `unpin`, `adopt` (D3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.3`) and `remove` (M3): `--dry-run` returns `data.precondition`, and `--if-match <token>` binds. A refusal is `plan_stale`, not retryable, with `details.changed` and `fix_argv` the same command with `--dry-run` in place of `--if-match <token>`; for the multi-target `TargetsData` commands whose every item failed, `details` also carries `items` (`src/app/outcome.rs:592-620`).
- The check moments, as failpoints in `locked()` (`src/engine/tx.rs`): `engine.snapshot.prestaged` (`:1014`, after the bound run's own first check and staging, before the lock: a "late" edit), `engine.registered` (`:1045`, holding the lock, before the under-lock check), `engine.revalidated` (`:1143`, after both under-lock checks, before the swap). A `pause` failpoint stops the child at that point until the test resumes it (`tests/common/pause.rs`; a pause waits at most 60 s).
- The refusal messages name the drifted folder by key ("<key> changed after the preview", "a folder named <key> appeared in AddOns"); the `-v` note "<target>: approval checked under the lock in <us> us: folders …, entries …, rehashed …, files …, bytes …" appears once per checked window.
- T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs and the `argc e2e` runner): `TestLog` (`tlog!()`, `step`, `note`, `json`, `run`, `cmd(..).failpoints(..).pause(..).spawn()`, `reached`, `resume`, `tree`, `assert_unchanged`, `diff`), `Ran::{ok, fails, envelope, data, error_code, warnings, assert_private}`, and the e2e marker: a suite whose root file's crate doc starts `//! e2e suite:` runs under `argc e2e`.
- Builders that exist at `c0ab5e9`: `common::engine::Scene` (one retail client with SavedVariables under `WTF/`; `release(repo, tag, folders)`, `install`, `install_args`, `ok`, `folders_of`, `generation`, `history`, `catalog`), `common::http::{gh_release_v, gh_latest}` (a release with arbitrary files, as `tests/perf.rs`'s `addon_release` builds them), `common::archives::zip_text`, `common::home::Home` (several clients; `write_desired`), `common::trees::tree_hash`, `common::privacy::assert_private_all`.

## Technical Approach

### 1. `tests/apply.rs` (new)

Crate doc: `//! e2e suite: bound runs commit exactly what their preview approved, or nothing (M4-D60): the approval witness and the re-judged operations checked again under the commit lock, and each rename's identity.` *Decided while writing this bead:* the plan names `tests/apply.rs::witness_*`; the file does not exist yet and `apply` arrives with D5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`, `omaddons apply`), which this bead blocks, so the scenarios drive typed `--if-match` runs, the same bound path `apply` uses. D5 and D7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.7`) append their `apply` scenarios to this file.

`mod support` holds:

- `const FILES: usize = 12;` A witnessed folder `Foo` is `Foo/Foo.toc` (`## Interface: 120105, 50504, 11509`, `## Version: <tag>`) plus `Foo/f00.lua` … `Foo/f11.lua` (`-- <tag> <i>\n`).
- `fn foo_release(http: &Path, tag: &str, extra: &[&str])`: release `tag` of `gh:o/foo` with `Foo` and each extra folder (a TOC only), served as latest (`gh_release_v` and `gh_latest`).
- `fn foo_zip(dl: &Path, name: &str, tag: &str, extra: &[&str]) -> PathBuf`: the same archive as a local zip.
- `enum Cmd { Install, Update, Copy }`, each building its world and naming its preview argv, the folder its edits touch (`edit_root`), the client dir whose tree must not change (`target_root`) and the folder the plan creates (`appear`):

  | Cmd | World | Preview argv (each run adds `--json --progress json`) | `edit_root` | `appear` |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | `Install` | `Scene`; `install gh:o/foo --file foo-v1.zip -t retail --offline` | `install gh:o/foo --file foo-v2.zip -t retail --offline --dry-run` (v2 adds `Foo_Extra`) | retail `AddOns/Foo` (witnessed `Replaced`) | retail `AddOns/Foo_Extra/Foo_Extra.toc` |
  | `Update` | `Scene`; `foo_release(v1)`, `install gh:o/foo -t retail`, then `foo_release(v2, ["Foo_Extra"])` | `update Foo -t retail --refresh --dry-run` | retail `AddOns/Foo` (`Replaced`) | retail `AddOns/Foo_Extra/Foo_Extra.toc` |
  | `Copy` | `Home::new(&["wow", "wow_classic"])` (retail and classic); `foo_release(v1)`, `install gh:o/foo -t retail` | `copy --from retail --to classic Foo --dry-run` | retail `AddOns/Foo` (`CopySource`; its record stays unchanged) | classic `AddOns/Foo/Foo.toc` |

- `enum Edit` (applied by `Edit::apply(&self, root: &Path)`, each logged with `log.note`):

  | Edit | Before the preview | The edit |
  |---|---|---|
  | `CleanFileEdited` | nothing | `f05.lua` rewritten with `-- edited by hand, a longer line\n` |
  | `EleventhChangedFile` | `f00.lua` … `f09.lua` each appended `-- local\n` (for `Install` and `Update` the preview's `local_changes_replaced` warning names exactly those ten paths, asserted) | `f10.lua` appended `-- local\n` |
  | `SameSizeEdit` | nothing | `f06.lua`'s bytes replaced by as many different bytes, then its mtime put back with `std::fs::File::set_times` (only the ctime moves) |
  | `FileDeleted` | nothing | `f07.lua` removed |
  | `FileReplaced` | nothing | a new `f08.lua.new` with other content, renamed over `f08.lua` (a new inode) |
  | `SymlinkAdded` | nothing | `link.lua` → `f00.lua` |
  | `EmptyDirAdded` | nothing | `empty/` created |
  | `CreatedNameAppeared` | nothing | `appear` created with a one-line TOC |

- `enum When { Early, Late, UnderLock }`: `Early` applies the edit after the preview and before the bound run starts (caught by the first check of D2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2`, and D3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.3`); `Late` applies it while the bound run is paused at `engine.snapshot.prestaged` (after its first check: caught by the under-lock check of D8, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8`); `UnderLock` while it is paused at `engine.registered` (holding the lock, before the check).
- `fn assert_stale(ran: &Ran, changed: &[&str], preview: &[String])`: `ran.fails(1, "plan_stale")`, `error.retryable == false`, `error.details.changed == changed`, `error.fix_argv == ["omaddons", preview…]`.

### 2. The witness matrix

A macro generates one test per row, named `witness_<when>_<cmd>_<edit>`:

- `witness_late_<cmd>_<edit>` for every `Cmd` and every `Edit`: 24 tests.
- `witness_early_<cmd>_clean_file_edited` for every `Cmd`: 3 tests.
- `witness_under_lock_update_clean_file_edited`: 1 test.

Each test, as `TestLog` steps:

1. **seed**: build the `Cmd`'s world; apply the edit's "before the preview" part.
2. **preview**: `log.run` the preview; `ok()`; the token `T` from `data.precondition`; for `EleventhChangedFile` with `Install`/`Update`, the warning `local_changes_replaced` lists exactly the ten paths.
3. **edit, at the moment**: `Early`: apply the edit, then run the bound argv (the preview's argv with `--if-match T` in place of `--dry-run`). `Late`/`UnderLock`: `let run = log.cmd(&world, &bound).failpoints("<point>=pause").pause(&pause).spawn(); log.reached(&pause, point);` apply the edit; record `log.tree("target", target_root)`, `log.tree("source", retail client dir)` for `Copy`, and `log.tree("records", <state>/targets)` and the history line count; `log.resume(&pause, point); let ran = run.wait();`.
4. **refusal**: `assert_stale(&ran, &["observed"], &preview)`; the message names the edited folder's key (`foo`, or `foo_extra`/`foo` for `CreatedNameAppeared`); `log.json("refusal", &ran.envelope()["error"])`.
5. **nothing moved**: `log.assert_unchanged("target", ..)` (and `"source"`, `"records"`); history has no new line; `<state>/journal/` is empty; no `<meta>/stage/<tx>` directory is left; `ran.assert_private()`.
6. **the fix**: run `fix_argv` with `--json --progress json`; for every edit but `CreatedNameAppeared` it succeeds with a new token, and the bound run with that token succeeds (the hand edit is replaced and kept in the transaction's snapshot for `Install`/`Update`; copied around for `Copy`); for `CreatedNameAppeared` the new preview reports the hand-made folder as its own planning decides, and the test asserts only that it changes nothing (`log.assert_unchanged("target", ..)`).

### 3. The operations rows (`selection`) and the dependency rows

- `witness_rejudged_sync_prune_forget_is_selection`: `Scene` with `Foo` and `Bar` installed; both of `Foo`'s folders deleted by hand; `write_desired` naming only `Bar`; preview `sync --prune -t retail --dry-run` plans `Foo`'s forget (a records-only change, no folder op); the bound run paused at `engine.snapshot.prestaged`; `AddOns/Foo/Foo.toc` recreated by hand; resume → `assert_stale(&ran, &["selection"], ..)`; `list -t retail --json` still shows `Foo`; the generation and history unchanged; `AddOns/Foo` as the test left it.
- `witness_rejudged_dependency_satisfied_by_hand_is_observed`: `Little` v2 requires `Big` (catalog entries through `Scene::catalog`); the preview of `update Little -t retail --refresh` plans `Big`'s install (`Big` absent); at the pause `AddOns/Big/Big.toc` created by hand → `["observed"]`. *Decided while writing this bead:* the plan lists this case under "re-judged operations that differ … `selection`", but the witness check runs before the re-judge and `big` is one of the names the plan creates, so the absent-name check refuses it first, with `observed`; the `selection` rows are the forgets above and in `tests/preconditions.rs`.
- `witness_unmanaged_dependency_gone_is_observed`: `Little` v2 requires `Lib`, present as an unmanaged folder at the preview (the preview reports it unmanaged and installs nothing for it); at the pause `AddOns/Lib` is moved out of `AddOns` → `["observed"]`, message "lib, which Little requires, is no longer in AddOns".

### 4. The unchanged-world rows

- `witness_unchanged_world_commits_exactly_the_preview_<cmd>` for `install` (the `Install` world), `update`, `copy`, `sync` (a desired file naming `Foo` at a newer version), `pin` (`pin Foo -t retail`), `unpin`, `adopt` (`adopt --apply -t retail Bar` over an unmanaged `Bar`): preview, then the bound run with nothing changed in between → `ok()`. The oracle: a twin world built by the same seed runs the same command unbound, and the bound run's target `AddOns` tree hash and record equal the twin's (`log.json` both); the new history line's ops name exactly the folders of the preview's `changes[].folders` (`added`, `replaced`, `removed`, `recorded`). The `-v` stderr has exactly one "approval checked under the lock" debug line per committed target.
- `witness_late_touch_still_commits`: `Update`; at the `Late` pause, `f03.lua`'s mtime set to now (`File::set_times`, bytes unchanged) → `ok()`; the cost note shows `rehashed 1`.

### 5. The scope rows

- `witness_scope_an_edit_after_the_check_is_committed_and_undoable`: `Update`; the bound run paused at `engine.revalidated` (after both under-lock checks); `f04.lua` edited in place (the folder keeps its inode) → `ok()`: the edit is outside the guarantee by design (M4-D60); `<meta>/snapshots/<tx>/AddOns/Foo/f04.lua` holds the edited bytes; `undo <tx> --json` → `ok()`, and `AddOns/Foo` hashes as it did right after the edit.
- `predicate_a_folder_replaced_at_the_last_moment_rolls_back`: `Scene` with `Alpha` and `Beta` at v1 and v2 released (`common::engine::shapes`-style, 12 files each); preview `update -t retail --refresh --dry-run`; the bound run paused at `engine.revalidated`; `AddOns/Beta` moved out of `AddOns` and replaced by a byte-identical copy (a new inode) → `assert_stale(&ran, &["observed"], ..)`; `AddOns` hashes as right after the replacement (`Alpha`'s exchange, which ran first, rolled back); journal directory empty; generation and history unchanged.
- `predicate_unbound_folder_replaced_at_the_last_moment_rolls_back_retryable`: the same without `--if-match` → `plan_stale` with `retryable: true` and the prose fix; the same tree assertions.

### 6. `tests/preconditions.rs` (append; M3's `remove` binding)

- `a_bound_remove_whose_forget_no_longer_applies_changes_nothing`: `Foo` installed, its folder deleted; `remove Foo -t retail --dry-run` (a forget) → token; the bound run paused at `engine.snapshot.prestaged`; `AddOns/Foo/Foo.toc` recreated → `plan_stale`, `["selection"]`, not retryable, `fix_argv` `REMOVE_PREVIEW`; `Foo` still recorded, generation unchanged. Then the same race without `--if-match` ends as before: exit 0, `Foo` reported unchanged.
- `a_bound_remove_whose_folder_was_replaced_at_the_last_moment_changes_nothing`: `Foo` and `Bar` installed; `remove Foo Bar -t retail --dry-run`; paused at `engine.revalidated`; `AddOns/Bar` replaced by a byte-identical copy → `plan_stale`, `["observed"]`, not retryable; both folders in place (tree hash as after the replacement); record and history unchanged.
- `a_bound_remove_logs_no_approval_check`: `-v` on a bound remove of an unchanged world: success, and no "approval checked under the lock" line (its token has no witness; only the operations are compared).
- Every M3 scenario of the file passes unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `tests/apply.rs` exists with the `//! e2e suite:` crate doc, and `argc e2e apply` runs it.
- [ ] All 24 `witness_late_*` rows, the 3 `witness_early_*` rows and `witness_under_lock_update_clean_file_edited` pass: `plan_stale`, not retryable, `["observed"]`, the preview as `fix_argv`, the folder named in the message, and the target (and for `copy` the source) hash-identical to the tree right after the edit, with no journal, stage or history line left.
- [ ] The forget rows give `["selection"]` for `sync --prune` and for `remove`, and the unbound `remove` race still ends unchanged.
- [ ] The dependency rows give `["observed"]`, with the decided reason recorded in the close comment.
- [ ] Every unchanged-world row commits exactly what its twin's unbound run commits and what its preview listed; a touch between preview and run still commits.
- [ ] The scope rows pass: an edit after the check commits and undoes byte for byte; a folder replaced at `engine.revalidated` rolls the target back, bound (not retryable) and unbound (retryable).
- [ ] Every scenario that creates `WTF/` asserts privacy over stdout and stderr with `--progress json`.
- [ ] Every existing `tests/preconditions.rs` scenario passes unchanged.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

None: this part adds test code only. Its `support` helpers are exercised by the rows themselves; `Edit::apply` logs what it did, and a row whose edit did not change the folder (its tree hash equal before and after the edit) fails at once with "the edit changed nothing", so a broken helper cannot pass as a refused run.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

The rows of Technical Approach 2 to 6, in `tests/apply.rs` and `tests/preconditions.rs`. Every child that pauses is waited for with `Running::wait`, whose timeout (`RUN_TIMEOUT` of T1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`) is far above the 60 s pause limit, so a missed resume fails the test instead of hanging the gate.

### Logging

Every row uses `TestLog` (`tlog!()`): the steps `seed`, `preview`, `bound run, paused`, `edit`, `resume`, `refusal`, `nothing moved`, `the fix`; `log.run` and `log.cmd(..).spawn()` for every command (argv, exit, envelope, stderr events, failpoints armed); `log.reached`/`log.resume` around each pause; `log.tree` of the target, the source and the records right after the edit, then `log.assert_unchanged` (which lists the first differing paths if any); `log.json("refusal", ..)`, `log.json("cost note", ..)` where read, and `log.note` naming the edit applied. On a failure the guard prints the transcript path and the last 20 steps, so the interleaving and every envelope are on record. `argc e2e apply` and `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG=verbose` echo the steps live.

## Considerations

- **Runtime.** About 40 rows, each a few short commands and at most one paused child on a small home; the debug build of the gate runs them in well under a minute in parallel. Each row builds its own home, so rows never share state.
- **Determinism.** Every interleaving is forced by `pause` failpoints, never by sleeps. The "late" edits happen after the child's staging, which waits out the racy slack, so the child's stamps are settled when it reads them.
- **The fix step** proves the refusal's `fix_argv` is useful, not just well formed, in the spirit of M4-D15 ("a usage fix must run, not just parse").
- **Hot spots:** `tests/apply.rs` is new here (D5 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`, D7 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.7` and D9 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.9`, `plans show`, append later); `tests/preconditions.rs` is appended by D2 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2`, D3 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.3` and D7 too: append at the end and rebase.
- **Privacy:** `Scene` homes hold SavedVariables under `WTF/`; each row runs `ran.assert_private()` (stdout and stderr) with `--progress json`.

## Dependencies

title: Tests: the design gate's adversarial matrix: refused renames at every journaled step, bound crash matrices and repeated recovery
description:
Part 4 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8 (The approval checked again under the commit lock). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

D8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8`) changes what the commit window checks and how every swap rename is guarded: part 1 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8.1) checks the approval witness and the re-judged operations under the global lock; part 2 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8.2) makes each rename compare its journaled identities with the ones the under-lock check saw and carry the endpoint predicates of E13 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.13`, resource sets and fsx endpoint predicates), so a refused rename rolls back in process. Common rule 14 makes D8 a design-gate leaf: "A leaf that adds or changes … a binding rule … closes only when its own adversarial matrix passes: every failpoint it adds, every journaled step, repeated recovery, and injected I/O failure where it writes." This part is that matrix, and **D8's design gate is passed only when this subtask is closed.**

D8 adds no failpoint and no write of its own, so its matrix is about the journaled steps it now guards and the crashes around them: a refused rename at every journaled step of every swap shape, the residual window after a step line, the existing crash points armed in bound runs, a refused rename whose rollback is itself crashed and then finished by later commands, injected I/O failures at the predicated renames, and the under-lock re-check's failure and bound modes. It is its own suite because it crashes and pauses children at engine failpoints (debug builds only), apart from the user-level scenarios of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8.3.

**Facts the matrix relies on** (verified at `c0ab5e9`, with parts 1 and 2 landed):

- The swap (`src/engine/swap.rs:671-771`) renames, in key order, every new or replacing folder (`Noreplace` or `Exchange`), then each old version from the stage path to the snapshot (`Noreplace`), then each removal (`Noreplace`); where flagged renames are unsupported (the failpoint `fsx.renameat2.einval`, `src/fsx/sys.rs:246`) it uses two plain renames per replaced folder. Each rename is preceded by its journal step line and the failpoint `engine.swap.before_rename` (`:871-880`), which `@N` targets at the Nth step.
- Recovery decides each step by the identities now at its paths against those the step line recorded (`ran`, `src/engine/journal.rs:1654-1675`): before state, not run; after state, ran; neither, it stops for manual repair (`internal`). The in-process rollback after a failed commit is `recover_tx`; a failed rollback becomes `recovery_failed` (`src/engine/tx.rs:573-591`) with `details.journal_pending` and `details.recovery_error`, and the next lock-taking command recovers (`recover_all`). `engine.recover.step` crashes recovery at a step.
- `engine::FAILPOINTS` (`src/engine/tx.rs:78-113`) lists the 34 engine failpoints; `tests/engine_crash.rs` arms each as a real `abort` in a child (the process dies by `SIGABRT`, the kernel frees the locks) for unbound runs, with an oracle that every folder is wholly old or wholly new and the next lock-taking command recovers (`journal_recovered`). `fsx.mutate.checked` (`src/fsx/mutate.rs:373`) fires right after the predicate check of each `mutate`, and `@N` targets the Nth.
- `common::engine::{Scene, shapes}` (`tests/common/engine.rs`): `Scene` is one retail client with SavedVariables; `shapes::update_many` installs `Alpha`, `Beta` and `Gamma` at v1 and releases v2 (`:441-458`); `Scene::folders_of`, `generation`, `history`. `common::pause::Pause` forces interleavings.
- T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`): `TestLog`, `log.cmd(..).failpoints(..).pause(..).spawn()`, `Ran::{fails, aborted, envelope}`, the `//! e2e suite:` marker.

## Technical Approach

`tests/engine_witness.rs` (new): crate doc `//! e2e suite: the adversarial matrix of the approval under the commit lock: every guarded rename refused and rolled back, the residual window, bound crash matrices, repeated recovery and injected failures.`, then `#![cfg(debug_assertions)]` (failpoints exist only in debug builds, DEC-7). *Decided while writing this bead:* a suite of its own, not new cells in `tests/engine_crash.rs`, so that file is rerun **unchanged** (the plan's "every existing crash matrix passes unchanged" is then literally true) and so the new cells use `TestLog`.

### 1. A refused rename at every journaled step

Shapes, each bound (its preview first, the run with `--if-match`), and the first one also unbound:

| Shape | Steps the matrix tampers with | The tamper |
|---|---|---|
| `update_of_three` (`shapes::update_many`, preview `update -t retail --refresh --dry-run`) | steps 1–3: the exchanges of `Alpha`, `Beta`, `Gamma` | the live folder moved out of `AddOns` and replaced by a byte-identical copy (new inode) |
| `remove_of_two` (`Foo`, `Bar` installed; `remove Foo Bar -t retail`) | steps 1–2: the removals | the same |
| `install_of_two_new` (`gh:o/alpha` and `gh:o/beta` released, not installed; `install gh:o/alpha gh:o/beta -t retail`) | steps 1–2: the new folders going live | a folder created by hand at the destination |
| `update_in_the_fallback` (`Alpha` and `Beta` at v1, v2 released; the child armed with `fsx.renameat2.einval`) | steps 1 and 3: each folder's live-to-snapshot rename | the live folder replaced by a byte-identical copy |

For step `n`, the child pauses just before step `n`'s line is written: at `engine.journal.prepared` for `n = 1`, at `engine.swap.before_rename@(n-1)` for `n ≥ 2` (step `n-1`'s line is written, its rename not yet run). The test tampers, records `log.tree("addons", AddOns)`, and resumes. Expected, for every cell:

- bound: `plan_stale`, not retryable, `details.changed: ["observed"]`, `fix_argv` the preview; unbound: `plan_stale`, retryable, the prose fix;
- `AddOns` hashes as it did right after the tamper (every earlier step undone; the byte-identical copies make that the pre-run content);
- `<state>/journal/` is empty, no stage or in-flight lock is left, the generation and history are unchanged, and `status --json` reports no unfinished transaction.

*Decided while writing this bead:* the old-version-to-snapshot steps and the fallback's stage-to-live steps are not tampered with: their source lives in the transaction's private `<meta>/stage/<tx>/`, and replacing it there would also break the earlier step's after state, which no supported writer can do. Their predicates are covered by omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8.2's unit cases.

### 2. The residual window, pinned

`residual_after_the_step_line_<shape>` for `update_of_three` (step 2) and `remove_of_two` (step 2): the child pauses at `engine.swap.before_rename@2` (step 2's line is written), the test replaces step 2's live folder with a byte-identical copy, and resumes. Expected: the rename's predicate fails and nothing is renamed at that step; the in-process rollback finds step 2 in neither state and stops; the command fails with `details.journal_pending` set to its transaction and `details.recovery_error.code == "internal"`; the journal file remains; every folder is wholly one version (step 1's folder at its new version or its removal done, step 2's folder the copy); the test's moved-out original and the staged new version are intact; `status --json` reports the transaction as waiting; the next lock-taking command (`pin Gamma -t retail --json` after the update, `pin Bar -t retail --json` after the remove) fails with the same stop and changes nothing. This is M4-D60's stated scope ("between that check and an individual operation, only the identity of what moves is re-checked") at its narrowest point: no data is lost, and the doctor (F1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1`, F2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.2`) names and repairs the stuck journal.

### 3. Bound crash matrices

- `crash_matrix_bound_update`: for **every** name in `omaddons::engine::FAILPOINTS`, a fresh `Scene` with `Foo` (and `FooOld`) at v1 as `tests/engine_crash.rs`'s update cell builds it, a preview of `install gh:o/foo --file v2.zip -t retail --offline --dry-run`, then the bound run with `<name>=abort`. A name the run never reaches lets it complete. The oracle, as `tests/engine_crash.rs`'s: after the crash (`Ran::aborted`) every folder is wholly v1 or wholly v2 (`folders_of`); a reader (`status --json`) changes nothing (tree hash) and reports an unfinished transaction exactly when a journal exists; the next lock-taking command (`pin Foo -t retail --json`) recovers it (`journal_recovered` when there was a journal), after which every folder sits on one side, consistent with the generation (v2 exactly when it moved by one) and history (an `update` line exactly when v2). One test per name, generated by a macro (`crash_bound_update_<name with dots as underscores>`).
- `a_crash_at_every_rename_of_a_bound_update_of_three`: `engine.swap.before_rename=abort@N` for `N` in 1..=6 on a bound `update_of_three`; the same oracle over `Alpha`, `Beta`, `Gamma`.

### 4. Repeated recovery after a refused rename

`a_refused_renames_crashed_rollback_is_finished_by_later_commands`: bound `update_of_three`; `Beta` replaced by a byte-identical copy at `engine.swap.before_rename@1`; the child also armed with `engine.recover.step=abort`, so its in-process rollback dies; then `pin Gamma -t retail --json` armed with `engine.recover.step=abort` dies in recovery too; then `pin Gamma -t retail --json` unarmed recovers (`journal_recovered`) and commits its pin; a fourth command finds nothing to recover. After the third: `AddOns` hashes as right after the tamper, plus nothing else; the journal is gone; the record differs from before only by `Gamma`'s pin; history holds the pin's line and no update line. Three recoveries in a row, two of them crashed: recovery stays idempotent with the predicates in place.

### 5. Injected failures

- `an_injected_io_error_after_a_predicated_check_rolls_back`: bound `update_of_three` with `fsx.mutate.checked=error@N`, where `N` is the second exchange's `mutate` in the run's session (found by a reference run of the same shape whose `actions.jsonl` numbers each action; the test asserts that action is `Beta`'s exchange before arming it). Expected: the command fails with `io`; the rollback restores `Alpha`; every folder is wholly v1; no journal is left.
- `an_unreadable_witnessed_file_under_the_lock_is_stale`: `Scene` with `Foo` at v1; preview of `update Foo -t retail --refresh`; at the `engine.snapshot.prestaged` pause, `AddOns/Foo/f03.lua` set to mode 000 and its mtime moved (so the stamp moves and the re-check must read it) → `plan_stale`, `["observed"]`, message "foo cannot be read now"; nothing moved; the mode restored afterwards so the temp dir can be cleaned. Run as an unprivileged user (the gate's normal case); when the test runs as root, where mode bits do not stop reads, it asserts the run commits instead and logs why.
- `a_witnessed_folder_grown_past_the_limits_under_the_lock_is_stale`: the config's `limits.archive_max_entries` set to 40 before the preview (the preview's 13-entry folder fits); at the pause, 40 files added to `AddOns/Foo` → `plan_stale`, `["observed"]`, message "foo grew past the archive limits"; nothing moved.

### 6. The existing matrices, rerun

`cargo test --test engine_crash` and `cargo test --test engine_concurrency` pass with those files unchanged: their unbound swaps now carry the predicates, and every crash point, rename crash and recovery crash they already exercise must give the same results.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `tests/engine_witness.rs` exists (debug builds, `//! e2e suite:` crate doc) and runs under `argc e2e engine_witness`.
- [ ] Every cell of the per-step matrix (4 shapes, every tampered step, bound and, for `update_of_three`, unbound) refuses before the rename, rolls back cleanly (AddOns as after the tamper, no journal, generation and history unchanged) and gives the bound or unbound `plan_stale` form.
- [ ] Both residual cells stop for manual repair with `details.journal_pending` and `recovery_error.code: "internal"`, lose nothing, and keep every folder wholly one version.
- [ ] `crash_matrix_bound_update` passes for every name of `engine::FAILPOINTS`, and the rename crash matrix of a bound update of three for every step.
- [ ] A refused rename whose rollback is crashed twice is finished by the third lock-taking command, and a fourth finds nothing.
- [ ] The injected `io` at a predicated rename rolls back; an unreadable or oversized witnessed folder under the lock is `plan_stale` (`observed`) with nothing moved.
- [ ] `tests/engine_crash.rs` and `tests/engine_concurrency.rs` pass unchanged (`git diff --exit-code tests/engine_crash.rs tests/engine_concurrency.rs`).
- [ ] The design gate of D8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8`) is recorded as passed in this subtask's close comment, with the cell counts and the test names.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

None: test code only. A helper that tampers checks that it changed what it meant to (the tampered path's `FileId` differs and its tree hash does not, for a byte-identical copy) and fails the cell otherwise, so a no-op tamper cannot pass as a refused rename.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

The cells of Technical Approach 1 to 6. Every crash is a real `abort` in a child process; every interleaving is a `pause` failpoint; nothing sleeps to wait for a race.

### Logging

Every cell uses `TestLog`: steps `seed`, `preview`, `bound run, paused at <point>`, `tamper`, `resume`, `outcome`, `recover` (for each later command), `oracle`; `log.cmd(..).failpoints(spec).pause(&pause).spawn()` records the failpoint spec of each child; `log.tree("addons", ..)` after the tamper and `log.assert_unchanged("addons", ..)` after recovery; `log.json("journal", ..)` lists the journal directory and, for the residual cells, the step records (identities included) so a classification can be checked by eye; `log.json("folders", folders_of(..))` at each oracle. A failing cell prints its transcript path and last 20 steps, which name the failpoint, the step and the identities involved.

## Considerations

- **Runtime.** The bound crash matrix is about 34 children and recoveries; the per-step matrix about 12 cells; the rest a handful. Debug builds run them in a few minutes, in parallel with the rest of the gate (each cell owns its home).
- **What a failure here means.** A refused rename that does not roll back cleanly is a bug in part 2's ordering (the journal comparison must precede the rename) or in recovery's assumptions; fix the code, never the oracle. A residual cell that rolls back cleanly would mean the window is closed: update README's scope paragraph and this cell together.
- **No tampering with omaddons' private directories** (`<meta>/stage/<tx>/`, `<meta>/snapshots/<tx>/`): no supported writer touches them, and tampering there breaks earlier steps' after states by construction.
- **Hot spots:** none; the suite is new, and `tests/engine_crash.rs` is deliberately not edited.

## Dependencies

- Parent: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8 (The approval checked again under the commit lock).
- Before it: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8.1 and omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8.2, the behaviour under test; T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`) for `TestLog`.

  - The next `pin` stops the same way and changes nothing, and so does an `install`, which also carries `details.reason: "step_unrecognized"` and `journal_pending`.
- **The bound crash matrix**: 34 `crash_bound_update_engine_*` tests, one per `engine::FAILPOINTS` name, plus `the_bound_crash_matrix_covers_every_engine_failpoint`, which holds the rows equal to the list.
  - Each row asserts whether a bound update reaches its failpoint: 22 crash, and 12 run to the end (recovery, restore, preservation, `engine.autobackup` with cloning off, `engine.plan.downloaded` with `--file`, `engine.addons_dir.created` with AddOns present).
  - The oracle is `tests/engine_crash.rs`'s, with SavedVariables under the fake account, realm and character, and privacy asserted on every run with `--progress json`.
- **The rename crash matrix**: `a_crash_at_every_rename_of_a_bound_update_of_three`, `engine.swap.before_rename=abort@1..6`, every rename reached and recovered.
- **Repeated recovery**: `a_refused_renames_crashed_rollback_is_finished_by_later_commands`. The rollback dies, then the next command's recovery dies, then the third recovers (`journal_recovered`) and commits its pin. AddOns are as before the run, the record differs only by Gamma's pin, and history holds the pin's line. A fourth command recovers nothing.
- **Injected failures**: `an_injected_io_error_after_a_predicated_check_rolls_back`, `an_unreadable_witnessed_file_under_the_lock_is_stale` ("foo cannot be read now"; when run as root, it asserts a commit instead) and `a_witnessed_folder_grown_past_the_limits_under_the_lock_is_stale` ("foo grew past the archive limits").
- README: the Tests table row; the Known issues entry for omad-alz5.

**Evidence**
- `cargo test --test engine_witness`: 46 passed, three runs in a row.
- `argc e2e engine_witness`: 46 passed, 104 test logs written, 0 panicked.
- `argc gate`: passed, 3353 passed, 0 failed, 83 ignored (46 new). Commit `bba5c14`.
- `git diff --exit-code tests/engine_crash.rs tests/engine_concurrency.rs`: clean. Both pass unchanged in the gate.
- `ubs` on the changed files: 0 critical.

**Decided while doing it, and facts corrected**
- The per-step oracle compares with the tree before the run, not "right after the tamper". For step n ≥ 3, the pause at `before_rename@(n-1)` comes after steps 1 to n-2 ran, so that tree is mid-swap. The exact copies make the content before the run the clean rollback's result.
  - The made-by-hand shape compares with the tree right after the tamper: both of its steps pause before any of its renames.
- The fallback's step numbers. Alpha's exchange attempt is journaled as step 1 and refused by the filesystem, which switches the swap to plain renames. Alpha's live-to-snapshot rename is step 2, its stage-to-live step 3, and Beta's live-to-snapshot step 4.
  - The matrix tampers at step 1 (Alpha, refused by its journal comparison before the attempt) and step 4 (Beta's live-to-snapshot, after Alpha's two plain renames ran and are rolled back).
  - Alpha's step 2 cannot be tampered with cleanly: the only pause before its line comes after step 1's line, the residual window.
- An unbound refusal's fix is the rerun of the same command, not prose: `app::Out::boundary_fix` rewrites every retryable `plan_stale`.
- The residual's next lock-taking `pin` gives the right code and message, but its `details` hold only `items`: per-client commands drop the target error's details (filed as omad-alz5, P2, with a Known issues entry). The cell asserts code and message on `pin`, and the full details on `install`, a single-target command that keeps them.
- The crash oracle's recovering command is an install of Bar, as in `tests/engine_crash.rs`, not `pin Foo`. A pin plans against v1, so when recovery rolls the update forward under its lock, the pin is correctly a retryable `plan_stale` ("Foo is no longer at the release this change was planned against").
- The fourth command of repeated recovery is `unpin Gamma`. A second `pin Gamma` would be a no-op, which takes no lock.
- The injected I/O error uses `fsx.rename_with.before=error@2`, the second rename's syscall after its predicates passed: Beta's exchange, asserted from the error message, which names its staged folder. It does not use `fsx.mutate.checked=error@N` numbered from `actions.jsonl`, because failpoint hit counts are process-wide and other sessions mutate, so `actions.jsonl` cannot number them.
- Not tampered with, as the bead decided: old-version-to-snapshot steps and the fallback's stage-to-live steps, whose sources live in omaddons' private stage.

**Contract**: no wire name added or changed. Test code, README's Tests table and Known issues.
