title: Tests: the under-lock check's cost on the realistic home
description:
Part 5 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8 (The approval checked again under the commit lock). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

D8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8`) adds work inside the commit window, where the global lock is held and every other omaddons process waits (vision D24: the lock is held only for commit windows). M4-D60 accepted that cost on one condition: "Cost is measured, not avoided. The under-lock re-read is one `stat` per witnessed entry. D8 reports what it adds to `lock_held_ms` on the realistic home (5,040 files), and G3's pinned counts include it." (G3 is `omad-7ccp`, group commit, derived writes and deferred directory fsyncs.) Risk #20 of the plan ("the under-lock witness check lengthens the commit window on large folders", likelihood M, impact L, owner D8) is watched by exactly this report. Part 1 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8.1) logs each checked window's cost as a `-v` note; this part measures it on a home of realistic size and prints the report the close comment quotes. It is a report, not a budget: nothing fails on a number.

It is its own step because it needs a shared builder the plan names but nobody has written yet, `common::realistic_home()`, and because the perf suite runs only in release builds at the checkpoint.

**Facts this part relies on** (verified at `c0ab5e9`):

- `tests/perf.rs` holds every speed budget, each `#[ignore]` and run in release by `cargo test --release --test perf -- --ignored --skip bench_home --skip live_home --test-threads=1` (its crate doc); its `support::measured` prints a report line (`:57-60`). `common::engine::lock_held_ms` reads `lock released: tx <tx>, lock_held_ms <ms>` from `-v` stderr (`tests/common/engine.rs:517-527`; the line is written at `src/app/mod.rs:306-313`).
- `bench_home` (`tests/perf.rs:228-262`) builds the realistic shape (retail, classic, era; the same 10 addons on each, installed one release behind; two folders of 84 files per addon; 30 records; 5,040 managed files) from GitHub fixtures, in a debug build, for `argc bench`.
- Release builds ignore `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES` (`choose_transport`, `src/net/mod.rs:336-344`), so a release test cannot install or update from fixtures; and `update` never updates a `file:` ref or a `--file` install (`is_static`, `src/resolve/updates.rs:168-176`). An `install <ref> --file <newer zip>` over an installed addon is an update of it (the crash matrix's update cell does exactly this, `tests/engine_crash.rs:83-86`).
- The cost note of part 1: `"<target>: approval checked under the lock in <us> us: folders <n>, entries <n>, rehashed <n>, files <n>, bytes <n>"`, a `-v` debug line, once per checked window.
- §6.19 lists `realistic_home()` among M4's new builders in `tests/common/` ("lifted from `tests/perf.rs`'s bench home"); the F leaves use it for "no false positive on the realistic home". It does not exist at `c0ab5e9`, and no leaf before this one needs it.

## Technical Approach

### 1. `tests/common/realistic.rs` (new; `pub mod realistic;` in `tests/common/mod.rs`)

```rust
/// The realistic home: retail, classic and era (`wow`, `wow_classic`, `wow_classic_era`),
/// each with the same 10 addons `gh:bench/addon00` … `addon09` installed at release `v1`
/// from local archives: two folders per addon (`AddonNN` and `AddonNN_Options`), each a TOC
/// for all three interfaces and 83 Lua files, so 30 records and 5,040 managed files.
/// Built offline, so it works in release builds.
pub struct Realistic { pub home: Home, archives: PathBuf }
pub const REALISTIC_TARGETS: [&str; 3] = ["retail", "classic", "era"];
pub fn realistic_home(dir: &Path) -> Realistic
impl Realistic {
    /// `<dir>/archives/addonNN-<tag>.zip`, written once (`common::archives::zip_text`).
    pub fn archive(&self, n: usize, tag: &str) -> PathBuf;
    /// `install gh:bench/addonNN --file <archive> -t <target> --offline`.
    pub fn install_args(&self, n: usize, tag: &str, target: &str) -> Vec<String>;
}
```

`realistic_home` builds the home with `Home::at(dir, ..)` and 30 `install` runs, then asserts 30 records and 5,040 files under the three `AddOns` directories. *Decided while writing this bead:* the shared builder installs from local archives under `gh:` refs (release ids `@sha256:`), not from the bench home's GitHub fixtures, because release builds replay no fixture and the perf suite runs in release; `bench_home` stays exactly as it is for `argc bench`. The shape (clients, addons, folders, files) is the bench home's, so the F leaves' "no false positive on the realistic home" reads the same sizes. If another leaf has already added `common::realistic_home()` by the time this part starts, reuse it and add only what is missing (the local archives), rather than adding a second builder.

### 2. `tests/perf.rs::the_approval_check_under_the_lock_costs` (release, `#[ignore = "a release-build report: cargo test --release --test perf -- --ignored"]`)

1. Build `realistic_home` in a fresh directory under `CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR`.
2. Three rounds. In round `r`, for each target and each addon `n`:
   - **bound:** `install … --file <addonNN-v(2r+2)> --dry-run --json` → its token; `install … --file <addonNN-v(2r+2)> --if-match <token> -v --json` → exit 0; record the window's `lock_held_ms` (`lock_held_ms(&r)`) and the cost note's six numbers;
   - **unbound:** `install … --file <addonNN-v(2r+3)> -v --json` → exit 0; record its `lock_held_ms`.

   Each run updates both folders of that addon (168 files), so each target's ten bound runs together witness all of its 1,680 files and a round covers the 5,040. *Decided while writing this bead:* "an update of every addon" is measured as these 30 single-addon updates per round, because release builds cannot run `update` over fixtures and local-archive installs are static to `update`; the check is per witnessed folder, so its cost per entry is the same as inside one `update` of ten addons.
3. Report with `measured(format_args!(..))`, one line per target and one total:
   - the summed `check_us` of the target's ten bound windows (median over the three rounds), and the median per window;
   - the median `lock_held_ms` per window, bound and unbound, and their difference;
   - the summed `entries`, `rehashed`, `files` and `bytes` of the note (an unchanged settled home should show `rehashed 0`; any other value is reported, not hidden);
   - the total over the three targets: the under-lock check's cost for all 5,040 files.
4. Assert only what makes the report trustworthy: every run exits 0; every bound run logged exactly one cost note and one `lock released` line; every note's `folders` is 2 and its `entries` the two folders' entry count (170: 84 files and the folder itself, each); no unbound run logged a cost note.

The close comment of D8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8`) quotes the printed lines with the commit and the machine's filesystem. G3 (`omad-7ccp`) later measures the same windows' fsyncs; the checks add none.

**Files:** `tests/common/realistic.rs` (new), `tests/common/mod.rs`, `tests/perf.rs`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `common::realistic_home(dir)` builds three clients with 30 records and 5,040 managed files from local archives, in debug and release builds alike, and asserts that shape.
- [ ] `tests/perf.rs::the_approval_check_under_the_lock_costs` runs in release, prints the per-target and total report (summed and per-window `check_us`, bound and unbound `lock_held_ms` medians and their difference, the note's counts), and asserts only the trustworthiness conditions.
- [ ] It needs no network, no fixture and no special filesystem, so it never prints a `SKIP` line.
- [ ] `realistic_home_builds_and_one_bound_update_logs_its_cost` runs in the gate (not ignored) and passes, asserting the home's shape and the note's numbers, never a duration.
- [ ] The report's lines are quoted in the close comment of D8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8`).
- [ ] `bench_home` and every other perf test are unchanged.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

None: test code only. `realistic_home` asserts the shape it built (30 records, 5,040 files, every folder present), so a broken builder fails loudly before any measurement.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

- `the_approval_check_under_the_lock_costs` itself (release, ignored).
- `realistic_home_builds_and_one_bound_update_logs_its_cost` (in `tests/perf.rs`, not ignored, like the suite's request-economy tests): it builds the full realistic home and runs one bound update on one target, asserting the shape, exit 0 and the note's numbers (`folders 2`, `entries 170`), never a duration. *Decided while writing this bead:* this smoke test runs in the gate so the builder the F leaves rely on, and the note's parsing, are proven on every run, while the timing stays a checkpoint report.

### Logging

Both tests use `TestLog` (`tlog!()`): steps `build the realistic home`, `round <r> <target>`, `report`; `log.run` for every command (about 270 in the release run, each a small record); `log.json("note", ..)` for each parsed cost note and `log.json("report", ..)` with the final numbers, so the checkpoint can quote them from `steps.jsonl` as well as from the printed lines. A failed assertion names the run (target, addon, round) and prints the transcript path.

### Checkpoint-only tests

`cargo test --release --test perf -- --ignored the_approval_check_under_the_lock_costs --nocapture --test-threads=1`, also run by the checkpoint's whole perf run (H6, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, step 2.2). No `SKIP` applies.

## Considerations

- **Risk #20:** the report is the risk's watch. If the per-window cost is a large share of an unbound window's `lock_held_ms`, or `rehashed` is above zero on the settled home, file a bead `discovered-from` D8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8`) with the numbers (for example, stamps that never settle on this filesystem), rather than changing the check here.
- **Noise.** `lock_held_ms` is milliseconds and noisy; `check_us` from the note is the precise number, measured inside the window around the checks themselves. The report gives both.
- **Runtime.** Building the home is 30 installs; the release run is about 270 short commands, well under a minute. It is ignored, so the gate never pays for it; the debug smoke test is one round on one target.
- **Hot spots:** `tests/perf.rs` (G3, `omad-7ccp`, adds `commit_windows_on_a_real_disk`) and `tests/common/mod.rs` (several M4 leaves add modules): append and rebase.

## Dependencies

title: `omaddons plans show`
description:
## How to work this bead

This bead is worked through its 5 subtasks, listed below in work order. Claim a subtask, not this bead (`br ready --parent omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.9` lists the ready ones). The agent that closes the last open subtask then verifies every acceptance criterion of this bead (they are the leaf's, not any one subtask's), and closes this bead with `br close omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.9 --reason "done: <evidence> · found: <ids>"`. Until this bead is closed, every bead it blocks stays blocked.

1. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.9.1 The bounded backward history scan for a plan's evidence, shared with `apply`'s `already_applied`: `state::history::plan_evidence`, its horizon, and `PLAN_EVIDENCE_LINES_MAX`.
2. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.9.2 The `plans show` command: the `plans` noun with its one subcommand, every DEC-1 touch point, the read-only reconciliation in `src/app/plans.rs`, its data, human output and README.
3. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.9.3 Typos of the `plans` noun get fixes that run, and the corpus rows: `plan show <id>` and `plans shwo <id>` both fix to `plans show <id>`.
4. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.9.4 E2E: the reconciliation scenarios: a lost output, a partial run, pending and expired, a deleted cache, an interrupted apply, a cut scan, and every run proven read-only.
5. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.9.5 E2E: every storable command's applied plan reconciles from history (`backup prune` as the one `unknown`).

Subtasks 3, 4 and 5 each need subtask 2 and nothing else, so three agents can work them at once.

## Background

**What this leaf is.** `omaddons plans show <PLAN_ID>` inspects one stored plan and reconciles it with history. It answers the question an agent must ask after losing an `apply`'s output (a broken pipe, a killed terminal, an agent restart): did that approval commit, on which clients, as which transactions? It reads the plan file and `history.jsonl`, takes no lock, makes no request and writes nothing, and it reports one of five states: `pending`, `completed`, `partial`, `expired` or `unknown`.

**Why it is needed.** M4 gives every addon-changing command a stored plan: a `--dry-run` stores the typed intent it previewed under a plan id for 24 hours, and `omaddons apply <plan_id>` executes exactly that intent, target by target (D4, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`, the plan store; D5, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`, `omaddons apply`). Without this leaf a plan has two verbs only, create (a dry run) and execute (`apply`), and neither answers "did it happen?":

- `apply --dry-run` revalidates the plan's sources (it may need the network) and refuses a stale plan with `plan_stale`, which is exactly the moment the user wants to see what they approved.
- A second `apply` reports `plan_stale` (`already_applied`, or `targets` when something else changed the client), which does not say whether the first attempt succeeded on every client or whether something else interfered.
- `apply` must never retry partial work on its own (that would hide the interference that caused it), so the agent needs a read that tells it what history holds.

History already holds the answer: every transaction an `apply` commits records the plan id in its history line (the field `plan`, M4-D25, written by D5). This leaf reads it back, bounded, and judges.

**It serves:**
- **G-M4-3, what was previewed is what runs, target by target:** "An approval can be inspected and reconciled. `omaddons plans show <plan_id>` says, offline and without writing, what was approved and what history records of it, so an agent that lost an `apply`'s output learns whether it committed before it does anything else." The guarantee is per target, and a multi-target run can end partial; this command is how a caller learns which part happened.
- **G-M4-2, the first guess works:** `omaddons plan show <id>` and `omaddons plans shwo <id>` get a usage fix that runs (`omaddons plans show <id>`), proven by the intent corpus.
- **G-M4-1, self-describing:** the command's data has a published JSON Schema (from its `COMMANDS` row), validated strictly against live output by the contract suite.
- **G-M4-6, no new risk to the engine:** the command is read-only by construction: no global lock, no plan lease, no fsx write, no network, no history projection rebuild.

**Checkpoint criteria this leaf is responsible for** (§3.2 of the M4 plan; H6, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, records the evidence):
- **7, stored plans,** its `plans show` bullet: "`omaddons plans show <plan_id>` reports, offline and writing nothing, the approved selection and history's evidence: pending, completed, partial, expired or unknown. An `apply` whose output was lost after it committed is reported completed; one with a deleted plan file still shows its transactions." Criterion 7's other bullets are D4's, D5's and D7's.
- **5, intent inference,** for its two corpus rows (`plans shwo <id>`, `plan show <id>`), each a `usage` error whose fix parses and runs to its declared exit.
- **2, schemas,** for its own path: `robot-docs schema plans show` exists, and every live envelope of the path validates strictly.
- **14, the contract is frozen,** for its own path: repeated runs print identical bytes after stripping only the declared volatile keys (H3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3`, audits it; this leaf adds no volatile key).

**The decisions that shape it** (the full decision log is filed as comments on the milestone epic `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`; each is restated here because this bead must stand alone):

- **M4-D63, `plans show` inspects an approval and reconciles it with history (added in review).** This leaf implements it.
  - `omaddons plans show <PLAN_ID> [--json]` is a read-only command (`mutates: false`, group Look), offline and write-free. It never re-plans and makes no request.
  - It returns the stored approval when the plan file exists (the intent's command and `display_argv`, the typed approval summary, the absolute inputs, `created_at`, `expires_at`, `build_id` and whether it matches this binary); history's evidence keyed by the plan id (every line carrying `plan: <id>`, as `{target, tx, result, at}`); a `state`; and `evidence.complete`, false when the scan stopped at `PLAN_EVIDENCE_LINES_MAX` lines before reaching the plan's `created_at`.
  - States: `pending` (stored, unexpired, no commit recorded), `completed` (a committed transaction for every target of the approved selection), `partial` (some but not all), `expired` (past expiry, nothing recorded), `unknown` (the file is gone or the history scan was cut short, so completeness cannot be judged).
  - A missing plan file with recorded commits still answers, with `stored: false`, the evidence and `state: unknown`. A missing file with no evidence is `plan_not_found`.
  - **Success is never inferred from current addon versions happening to match the plan:** only history lines with the plan id count.
  - The history scan reads backwards from the end and stops at the first line older than the plan's `created_at` (or `PLAN_TTL` before now when the file is gone), bounded by `PLAN_EVIDENCE_LINES_MAX`.
  - The guide's core loop says: when an `apply`'s result is unknown, run `plans show` before previewing again or changing anything (B2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.2`, writes that prose; this leaf updates README's agent block).
  - *Why:* `apply --dry-run` is no substitute (it revalidates, may need the network, refuses a stale plan); a lost stdout after a successful commit makes a retry report `plan_stale` or `already_applied`, which does not say whether the first attempt succeeded; the history `plan` field already holds the answer; reconciliation makes automation robust to broken pipes and restarts without making `apply` retry partial work.
  - *Rejected:* (i) a `plans list`: an agent keeps its own plan ids, and listing every preview ever made (the widget previews every update) is noise; it can come later as an addition. **Do not add one.** (ii) Making `apply` idempotent (silently succeeding the second time): it would hide a partial application and the interference that caused it.
- **M4-D25, history lines from `apply` carry the plan id.** A transaction committed by `apply` records the plan's `display_argv` as its `argv` plus the optional field `plan: <plan_id>`; the history `schema_version` stays 1.0 (an additive optional field never bumps it, M2-D36). The field is the evidence both `apply`'s `already_applied` check and `plans show` read, and it outlives the plan file. D5 writes it; this leaf reads it.
- **M4-D23, `apply` executes the stored, typed intent.** Step 1, "find the plan": an id prefix of at least 8 characters, matched ignoring case. Step 2, "fail closed on a bad file": a file larger than `PLAN_MAX_BYTES`, one that does not decode, a newer major, an unknown intent variant or option, a relative path, a `display_argv` that is not the intent's own, or a token that is not its parts' digest is `plan_not_found` with `details: {plan_id, path, reason: "unreadable"}` (a plan is cache: to its user an unreadable plan is a missing one; `state_corrupt` stays for `<state>`). Step 4's `already_applied`: history holds a committed transaction carrying this plan id. `plans show` resolves ids exactly as `apply` does and reads plans with the same fail-closed load, but **reports** an unreadable file (`stored: true, readable: false`) instead of failing, and never acts on it.
- **M4-D24, the plan lifecycle.** A plan lives `PLAN_TTL` (24 h). Its file (kind `plan` 1.0) is `{schema_version, plan_id, created_at, expires_at, tool_version, build_id, intent, display_argv, actor, reason, precondition: {token, parts}, releases[], approval, summary[]}`; `approval` is the typed summary (selection per target, scope, reasons, `routine`) and is "what `apply --dry-run` shows as `approved` and what `plans show` reports"; `summary[]` holds the human lines the dry run printed. "Readers are bounded: `plans show` reads one plan and a bounded history tail."
- **M4-D61, one applier per plan, and the guarantee is per target.** Multi-target runs keep one transaction per target, so a late conflict or an I/O failure on one target can leave a partial run; `apply`'s `outcomes[]` reports each target `committed`, `unchanged`, `stale` or `failed`. A preview that would change nothing stores no plan, so every stored plan has at least one change, on at least one target.
- **M4-D22, which commands store plans.** `plans show` neither stores nor binds: it reads and changes nothing. (Common rule 16 is satisfied by this: the leaf adds no mutating path.)
- **M4-D21, stored plans live in `<cache>/plans/`.** A cache wipe removes plans; history lives in `<state>` and outlives them. That is why the "file gone, evidence kept" answer exists.
- **M4-D15, a usage fix must run, not just parse.** The intent corpus (`tests/contract/intent_corpus.rs`, C4, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4`) holds rows of `(wrong argv, expected code, expected exit of the fix)`; each wrong argv runs on its own copy of the corpus home, which must hash unchanged when the row is an error, and its fix runs on an independent copy. "Each later leaf that adds a command or a hook adds corpus rows: … D9 for `plans show`." Rejected there: requiring every fix to exit 0 (a correct fix may legitimately fail on the corpus home); each row states its exit instead.
- **M4-D12 (context), the verb exemption.** A usage fix never turns the user's verb into a different command that changes something; a guessed mutating command becomes `omaddons help <it>`. `plans show` only reads, so a corrected argv may be the fix itself.
- **M4-D7, the guide is the skill.** Once B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`, the guide renderer) has landed, a leaf that adds a command regenerates `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` (its generated command table changes).
- **M4-D5, M4-D10, M4-D18, M4-D55, M4-D56 (contract rules this leaf obeys).** Each command row declares its exits (verified by the matrix); every error's `details` has a typed specification; serialized types use `BTreeMap`, never `HashMap`; the naming and nullability rules hold from slice 1 (A3's rule test, no allowlist line); field order is rendering order, deterministic but not contract.

**How it serves the vision.** The thesis is that omaddons stays the sole, safe, undoable authority over what it manages. An agent that cannot tell whether its last change landed either retries blindly (and may stack a second change on a first it did not see) or gives up. This command makes the safe path the obvious one: it tells the agent exactly what committed, with each transaction's undo command, and never guesses. It also serves vision G4 (agent ergonomics, "the first command an agent guesses works"): `plans show`, `plan show` and `plans shwo` all lead to the answer.

## Technical Approach

### 1. The command surface (subtask 2)

```text
omaddons plans show <PLAN_ID> [--json] [-v]     (Look; mutates false; no lock, no network, no write)
```

- `Command::Plans(crate::app::plans::PlansArgs)` in `src/cli.rs`, doc comment (bare help's about): "Inspect a stored plan and what history records of it (changes nothing)". `PlansArgs { #[command(subcommand)] action: PlansAction }`, with `#[command(subcommand_required = true, arg_required_else_help = false)]` on the variant, as A1 decided for `auth`: clap derive would otherwise set `arg_required_else_help`, which turns bare `plans` into a help-text error instead of a usage error with a fix.
- `PlansAction::Show(ShowArgs)`: about "What a stored plan approved, and whether history records it as applied (offline; changes nothing)"; `ShowArgs { #[arg(value_name = "PLAN_ID")] plan_id: String }` with help "The plan id a --dry-run returned (data.plan_id), or its first 8 or more characters". `PlansAction::command(&self) -> &'static str` returns `"plans show"`.
- `after_long_help` (a `PLANS_SHOW_HELP` constant beside the others in `src/cli.rs` or in `src/app/plans.rs`):

  ```text
  Examples:
    omaddons plans show 01M8Q2VA          what plan 01M8Q2VA… approved, and whether it was applied
    omaddons plans show 01M8Q2VA --json   the same as one JSON envelope, for an agent

  A plan is what a --dry-run stored (data.plan_id). plans show reads it and history.jsonl
  and changes nothing: no lock, no network. Its state is pending, completed, partial,
  expired or unknown; only history lines that carry the plan id count as applied, never
  addon versions that happen to match. -t does not apply: a plan names its own clients.
  ```

- **Bare `omaddons plans`** is clap's missing-subcommand error, mapped by `usage_error` to `usage` (exit 2) with the fix `omaddons help plans` (its `help_fix`, `src/cli.rs:638-642`). Its envelope `command` is `plans show`: `canonical("plans")` is the only row beneath it (A1's rule). `omaddons help plans` lists `show`.
- **Flags.** `--json`/`--robot`/`--format` as everywhere; `-v` adds detail (section 9). `--dry-run` and `--reason` are accepted and ignored, as for every read (the existing `read_only_commands_ignore_dry_run_and_reason` test proves the envelope is unchanged). `--if-match` is `usage` (not a binding command; its fix drops the flag). `--offline` changes nothing (there is no network to refuse). `-t` is ignored. *Decided while writing this bead:* `-t` is ignored rather than refused or used as a filter, because a plan names its own clients, the evidence of the other clients is part of the answer, and an agent that habitually passes `-t` should still get the whole truth.
- **Exits:** 0 for every answered state (a report, never a failure), 1 when `history.jsonl` exists but cannot be read (`io`, fix `omaddons status`, as `history::text` does), 2 for usage errors, 3 for `plan_not_found` and `ref_ambiguous`. `exits: &[0, 1, 2, 3]`, `network: Network::None`.

### 2. Resolving the id (subtask 2)

`plans show` resolves exactly as `apply` does, plus one step `apply` does not need:

1. The given text is uppercased (ULIDs are Crockford base32, case-insensitive). Fewer than `MIN_PREFIX` (8) characters is `usage`, raised before any read: message "a plan id or prefix has at least 8 characters, not \"<given>\"", fix `omaddons help plans show`. *Decided while writing this bead:* the 8-character rule and the reuse of `app::history::MIN_PREFIX`, because `apply` (M4-D23), `undo`, `history --run` and backups all use it; if D5's `apply` treats a short prefix differently, match `apply` and record it in the close comment.
2. **Stored plans first.** The same resolver `apply` uses lists `<cache>/plans/` (D4's bounded listing) and matches `<id>.json` names by prefix. If D5's resolver builds `apply`'s own errors (alternatives `omaddons apply <id>`), split it in subtask 2 into a shared `state::plans::matching(paths, prefix) -> Result<Vec<PlanId>>` and each command's error, so `apply`'s messages stay byte-identical and `plans show`'s alternatives are `omaddons plans show <id>`.
   - Exactly one match: that is the plan id, `stored: true`. Evidence is then matched by the **full** id.
   - Two or more: `ref_ambiguous` (exit 3), message "<n> stored plans have ids starting with <prefix>: <id>, <id>", fix `omaddons plans show <first>`, one alternative `omaddons plans show <id>` per other candidate, `details {prefix, candidates}` (the shape `backup::ambiguous` uses), candidates sorted by id (creation order).
3. **History second, only when no stored plan matched** (the file was swept or the cache wiped). The scan of section 4 runs with a prefix matcher. The distinct plan ids found: one → that id, `stored: false`; two or more → `ref_ambiguous` as above, message "<n> plans in history have ids starting with <prefix>: …"; none → `plan_not_found` (section 8).

A text longer than 26 characters, or with characters outside Crockford base32, can match nothing and ends in `plan_not_found` (the same answer `apply nosuchid0` gives, D5's corpus row). A prefix that names exactly one stored plan never consults history for other ids sharing that prefix: the answer is about the stored plan.

### 3. Reading the plan (subtask 2)

- `state::plans::load(paths, id)` (D4's bounded, fail-closed load, at most `PLAN_MAX_BYTES`, every self-consistency check of M4-D23 step 2). Any failure for a file that exists, an `io` error on it included, gives `stored: true, readable: false`; the failure's message is kept for the human output and a debug note, and nothing from the file is used: `created_at`, `expires_at`, `build_id`, `build_matches`, `intent` and `approval` are all `null`, `inputs` is `[]`. The file is never acted on.
- Readable: `created_at`, `expires_at`, `build_id` (the plan's), `build_matches` (`plan.build_id == build_info::BUILD_ID`), `intent: {command, display_argv}`, `approval` (the stored typed summary, the same `Approval` type the dry runs return), `inputs`.
  - `intent.command` is the intent's **command path** (`install`, `backup restore`, the envelope's spelling), from `StoredIntent::command()`; never the serde tag (`backup_restore`). If D4 named the accessor differently, use it; if it has none, add `pub fn command(&self) -> &'static str` with an exhaustive match. It must equal what `apply`'s `applied.command` says for the same plan.
  - `intent.display_argv` is the stored `display_argv` (D4's load has already checked it is the intent's own).
  - `inputs[]` is one `{path, present}` per absolute input the intent names (a `--file` zip or directory, a `file:` ref's path, `sync`'s desired-state file), in the intent's order. `present` is the same existence test `apply`'s `input_missing` check uses (one helper; if D5 inlined it, subtask 2 factors it out and points `apply` at it), so `present: false` means `apply` would refuse with `input_missing`. *Decided while writing this bead:* the element shape `{path, present}`, because the plan names only "the absolute inputs", a bare path list would hide the one fact a caller needs (would `apply` still run?), and inventing a `kind` vocabulary would add wire names for no decision a caller makes.
- `plans show` takes neither `<cache>/plans/.lock` nor the plan's lease, and never opens a plan file for writing.

### 4. The history scan (subtask 1)

One function serves `plans show` and `apply`'s `already_applied` check, so the two can never disagree about what history records.

```rust
// src/state/history.rs
/// Which plan a scan looks for.
pub enum PlanMatch<'a> {
    /// Lines whose `plan` is exactly this id.
    Exact(PlanId),
    /// Lines whose `plan`, uppercased, starts with this (already uppercased, 8+ characters).
    Prefix(&'a str),
}

/// One history line that carries a matching plan id, read far enough to attribute it.
pub struct PlanLine {
    pub plan: PlanId,
    pub tx: TxId,
    pub target: TargetKey,
    pub run: Option<RunId>,
    pub result: TxResult,
    pub at: Timestamp,
}

/// Why a scan stopped.
pub enum ScanStop {
    /// It read back to the first line of the file.
    Start,
    /// It met a line older than its horizon.
    Horizon,
    /// It read `max_lines` lines first: what lies before them is unknown.
    Bound,
}

pub struct PlanEvidence {
    /// The matching lines, oldest first (commit order).
    pub lines: Vec<PlanLine>,
    /// Lines whose `plan` matched but whose `tx`, `target`, `result` or `at` did not read.
    pub unattributed: usize,
    /// Complete lines in the window that did not read as a history line at all.
    pub unreadable: usize,
    /// Lines examined, the one that stopped the scan included.
    pub lines_read: usize,
    pub stop: ScanStop,
}
impl PlanEvidence {
    /// The scan covered its whole window: it was not cut by its bound.
    pub fn complete(&self) -> bool { !matches!(self.stop, ScanStop::Bound) }
}

/// Reads `history.jsonl` backwards in bounded blocks for the lines of `wanted`, stopping at
/// the first line older than `horizon` and after `max_lines` lines. Never loads the file
/// whole; writes nothing. A missing history is an empty one.
pub fn plan_evidence(paths: &Paths, wanted: &PlanMatch<'_>, horizon: Timestamp, max_lines: usize)
    -> Result<PlanEvidence>;
```

**How it reads.** Open `paths.history_file()` read-only (`std::fs::File`; reads never go through fsx) and take its length once: an append made after that is not seen, and a later call sees it. Read blocks of `SCAN_BLOCK_BYTES` (64 KiB, a private `const` in `history.rs`: a buffer size, not a limit, it changes no answer, only how many reads a scan makes, like `LINE_START`) from the end towards the start with `seek` and `read_exact`, carrying the partial line at each block's start into the next block. The real work is in an inner function generic over `Read + Seek`, the length and the block size, so unit tests drive it with tiny blocks.

**Line by line, newest first:**
1. The bytes after the last newline are a torn tail (a write in progress or cut by a crash): skipped and not counted, as `parse` skips them (`torn_tail`).
2. Empty lines are skipped and not counted (as `parse` filters them).
3. Before examining a line, if `lines_read == max_lines` and a line remains, stop with `Bound`.
4. A line longer than `DISCOVERY_FILE_MAX_BYTES` (1 MiB) is counted `unreadable` without being held whole: once the carry passes the cap, its bytes are dropped until the line's start is found. Memory stays at one block plus one capped line.
5. Decode lossily (UTF-8) and deserialize a minimal private struct: `{at: Option<Timestamp>, tx: Option<String>, target: Option<String>, run: Option<String>, plan: Option<String>, result: Option<String>}`, unknown fields ignored (so lines from newer builds, E12's target-less repair lines, settings lines and backup lines all read). On failure, retry from the last `LINE_START` (the merged-line salvage `line_facts` does). A line that still fails: a JSON end-of-input error is a torn line a later write closed off (counted as read, never as unreadable: recovery appends the whole line again); anything else is `unreadable`.
6. A line whose `at` is older than `horizon` (`at < horizon`) stops the scan with `Horizon`. A line at exactly the horizon does not stop it. A line with no readable `at` never stops it.
7. A line whose `plan` matches: parse `plan` as `PlanId`, `tx` as `TxId`, `target` as `TargetKey`, `run` as `RunId` (optional), `result` as `TxResult` (`"committed"`); any failure (a `null` target, an unknown result value from a newer build) counts `unattributed`. Never unwrap a target (E12's grep test `no_reader_unwraps_or_expects_a_history_target` forbids `.target.unwrap()`).
8. Reaching the first byte of the file stops with `Start`.

The matches are returned oldest first. An `io` error opening or reading an existing file is `Error::io(path, err, Suggestion::command(["omaddons", "status"]))`, as `history::text` reports it.

**The horizon** (`src/state/plans.rs`, subtask 1):

```rust
/// Where a plan's evidence scan stops: no line older than this can be one of its commits.
pub fn evidence_horizon(created_at: Option<Timestamp>, given: &str, now: Timestamp) -> Timestamp
```

It is the earliest of: the plan's `created_at` when the file was readable; the creation time the id encodes (a ULID's first 10 characters are its 48-bit millisecond timestamp; a shorter prefix is padded with `0`, which gives the earliest time it can encode; text that is not Crockford base32 encodes none); and, only when the file is missing or unreadable, `PLAN_TTL` before `now` (`now = crate::clock::now()`).

*Decided while writing this bead:* M4-D63's rule is the first and the third. Adding the id's own time only ever moves the horizon **earlier**, so the scan reads at least what the plan's rule reads (still bounded by `PLAN_EVIDENCE_LINES_MAX`) and can never miss what it would find. It closes a hole the plan's rule leaves: with the file gone and the plan older than 24 hours, `PLAN_TTL` before now falls after the plan's first commits, the scan would stop before them, and it would still report `complete: true`, a clean result for an incomplete search (common rule 15). It also makes the stop robust in tests that freeze `clock::now()` while plan ids are minted from the real clock.

### 5. Unfinished journals (subtask 2)

A crashed or running `apply` may have swapped a client's folders without its history line yet: the line is appended at commit, or by recovery's roll-forward from the journal's payload. `plans show` never recovers (it takes no lock), so it reads `engine::journal::pending(&paths)` (read-only) and treats an unfinished journal on an approved target, or one whose target cannot be read, as a reason the state cannot be judged (rule 9 below). It also adds `engine::journal::pending_warnings(&paths)` to its warnings exactly as every read command does through `World::load` (`src/app/world.rs:132-139`): `journal_pending` while the lock is free (the next change on that client finishes or rolls it back), `tx_in_progress` while it is held. *Decided while writing this bead:* the journal rule, keyed on the journal's target rather than on the plan id inside its payload, because `journal::read` is private and `src/engine/journal.rs` is another chain's hot spot (E11 → E13 → E5 → E14 → F1), and because any unfinished transaction on an approved client means that client's state is in flux; the price is an occasional `unknown` caused by an unrelated stuck journal, which its warning names.

*Rejected while writing this bead:* probing the plan's lease (`<cache>/plans/<id>.lease`) to report a running `apply`. While an `apply` works before its first commit, `pending` is literally true; a second `apply` waits on the lease and then reports `already_applied`; and once the running transaction journals, rule 9 reports `unknown`. A probe would add an fsx entry point for no change in what a caller should do.

### 6. Judging the state (subtask 2)

A pure function, `judge(&Judgement) -> (PlanState, Why)`, over: `stored`, `readable`, the intent (when readable), the approved target keys (the distinct `target_key`s of `approval.selection`), the evidence, the unfinished journals, `now` and `expires_at`. The rules, **first match wins**:

| # | Condition | State | `Why` (human output only) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | no file | `unknown` | `FileGone` |
| 2 | file unreadable | `unknown` | `Unreadable(message)` |
| 3 | the intent's command records no history line (`backup prune`) | `unknown` | `NoHistoryLine` |
| 4 | the approval names no target | `unknown` | `NoApprovedClients` |
| 5 | a matching line names a target the approval does not | `unknown` | `Disagrees` |
| 6 | every approved target has a committed line | `completed` | — |
| 7 | the scan was cut by its bound | `unknown` | `ScanCut` |
| 8 | the window held unreadable or unattributed lines | `unknown` | `UnreadableLines(n)` |
| 9 | an unfinished journal is on an approved target, or on a target it cannot name | `unknown` | `Unfinished(tx)` |
| 10 | some approved targets have a committed line | `partial` | — |
| 11 | the plan has expired | `expired` | — |
| 12 | otherwise | `pending` | — |

- **Rule 3, `backup prune`.** README promises `backup prune` "appends no history line" (`README.md:1242`), so history can never show whether a prune plan ran, and `pending` or `expired` would claim more than history proves. The test is an **exhaustive `match` on `StoredIntent` with no wildcard arm** (`fn records_history(intent: &StoredIntent) -> bool`): `BackupPrune` → `false`, every other variant → `true`, so a new storable command forces this decision. *Decided while writing this bead* (the plan's state table does not cover it); changing `backup prune` to write a line would change a README promise and is not this leaf's.
- **Rule 6 before rules 7–9.** A commit cannot be undone by lines the scan did not read, so "every approved target committed" is certain even when the scan was cut, a line was unreadable or a journal is open. *Decided while writing this bead:* M4-D63 lists both "completed: a committed transaction for every target" and "unknown: … the scan was cut short"; when both hold, the certain one wins. `evidence.complete` still reports the cut.
- **Rule 5.** A well-formed plan cannot produce it (`apply` commits only approved targets, under the plan's token); when history and the plan disagree, nothing is claimed.
- **Rule 8.** An unreadable line inside the window could be this plan's commit (written by a newer build, or damaged), so `partial`, `expired` and `pending` would be guesses. *Decided while writing this bead*, applying the plan's default "fail closed on anything persisted that cannot be fully read" (§8.1 default 6). Torn lines a later write closed off do not count (recovery appends the whole line again). The warning `history_lines_skipped` (existing, `src/state/history.rs:425-438`) is added with the count.
- **Rule 11, expiry.** The same predicate `apply`'s `expired` refusal uses, one helper (`StoredPlan::is_expired(now)`; if D4 or D5 compare inline, factor the comparison into that method and point `apply` at it), with `now = crate::clock::now()`. So `plans show` says `expired` exactly when `apply` would refuse it as expired.
- **Never consulted:** the records, the installed versions, the release memo, the client trees. Matching versions are not evidence (M4-D63).
- "Committed" means a matching history line with `result: committed`; it is the only result a history line has today.

- **Header:** `plan <full id> (<intent.command>): <state>` and, per state: `pending, stored until <expires_at>, nothing applied yet`; `completed, <n> of <n> clients committed`; `partial, <k> of <n> clients committed`; `expired at <expires_at>, nothing applied`; `unknown: <why>`. - **`approved:`** the shell-joined `display_argv`, then the stored `summary[]` lines indented two spaces (the lines the person saw when approving); when `summary[]` is empty, one line per approval item (`<target_id>: <op> <addon> <from> → <to>`). *Decided while writing this bead:* the stored `summary[]` lines are "the approval summary's lines" the plan names, because they are exactly what the user read before saying yes.
- **`committed:`** one line per evidence line: `<target>: tx <short tx> at <local time> · undo: omaddons undo <full tx>` (`short_id`, `src/app/history.rs:453-455`, for the display; the undo command always carries the full id). For `partial`: `not recorded: <ids of approved targets without a line>`.
- **Advice, one line:** `pending` → `apply it with: omaddons apply <id>` (or, when `build_matches` is false, `made by another build of omaddons, so apply will refuse it: preview again with <display_argv> --dry-run`; when an input is missing, `<path> is gone, so apply will refuse it: preview again …`); `partial` → the line shown above; `expired` → `preview again: <display_argv> --dry-run`; `unknown` from `NoHistoryLine` → `see what is left: <display_argv> --dry-run`. Everywhere, `<display_argv> --dry-run` means the plan's `display_argv` with `--dry-run` inserted before its first `--` when it has one (`backup prune -t retail -- <id>`), else appended, so the suggested preview parses and keeps every positional; a unit case pins it.
- **`-v` (`Style::detail()`, A8's name for today's `paths_visible()`, `src/output/human.rs:26-28`)** adds: `reasons: <approval.reasons>` and the scope; `build: <build_id> (this build | another build)`; `inputs: <path> (present | missing)` per input; `history: read <n> lines back to <horizon> (<stopped at the start | at the horizon | at its bound>)`.
- Debug notes (stderr `log` events at debug level, as other commands emit theirs): the scan's lines read, its stop and horizon, and a registry or plan-file read failure.
- Human text names no account, realm or character (it shows ids, addon names, versions and the user's own argv).

## Considerations

- **Risks (§11.4 of the M4 plan).**
  - #14, the milestone is large and the critical path long: this leaf is on the plans chain (D1 → D2 → D4 → D5 → D9 → H1), one unit of slack behind the critical path. Claim it as soon as D5 closes; subtasks 3–5 run in parallel.
  - #13, the guide drifts from behaviour: the guide's reconcile step (B2) names `plans show`; B2's test parses every command the guide names, and this leaf's README text is what B2 copies.
  - No risk is owned by this leaf; the reading is bounded and read-only, so the failure modes are wrong answers, which the judge table and the two suites pin.
- **What could go wrong, and how to notice.**
  - *D5 writes `plan` on some history lines but not all* (a roll-forward path, `undo`, the `--addon` restore): subtask 5's per-command table and subtask 4's interrupted-apply scenario fail for that command. File the defect `discovered-from` the failing subtask against D5's code and block this bead on it; do not paper over it in `plans show`.
  - *Two clocks:* the commit's history `at` uses the real clock, `clock::now()` honours `OMADDONS_NOW`. A test that freezes time for the preview or the `apply` could put lines before a frozen `created_at`. Freeze time only on the `plans show` invocation; the id-time term of the horizon also protects the scan.
  - *A wall clock stepped backwards* after a plan was made could put a later commit's `at` before `created_at`, and the scan would stop before it. omaddons' other time rules (retention, `PLAN_TTL`) share this assumption; the consequence is a `pending` or `partial` that `apply` (bound to its token) would still refuse to repeat.
  - *A huge history* (tens of thousands of lines within a day, which nothing in omaddons produces) cuts the scan: the answer is `unknown` with `complete: false`, never a false `pending`.
  - *Concurrent appends* during a scan are not seen (the length is taken once); the next call sees them.
- **Hot spots (§10.5 of the M4 plan) and their rules.**
  - `src/app/mod.rs` (`COMMANDS`, dispatch): A1 first; each command leaf adds its own rows afterwards and rebases.
  - `src/cli.rs`: not listed for this leaf in §10.5; its edits are one `Command` variant (subtask 2) and the guess judgement inside `subcommand_fix` (subtask 3), each in its own function; keep A1's subcommand and C1's hooks as they are, and rebase.
  - `src/state/history.rs`: E12 → E5 → E7; D5's `plan` field and this leaf's scan are additive and rebase.
  - `src/limits.rs` and its snapshot: append the row; re-accept the snapshot in the same commit.
  - `omarchy/Model.js`: command leaves add only their `CLI_PATHS` row.
  - `tests/contract/matrix.rs` and snapshots: append rows; one snapshot file per row.
  - `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md`: regenerate after rebasing, never merge by hand.
  - `README.md`: edit only this leaf's sections.
  - `src/app/apply.rs` and `src/state/plans.rs` are D5's and D4's files; this leaf's edits there are one call site and small helpers.
- **Why size M, 5 subtasks.** The command itself is a read over two files; the scan, the judge and the registry touch points are each a separate commit that passes the gate on its own, and the two E2E suites are mechanical but long (twenty-odd homes). Nothing here is a protocol: no journal, no recovery rule, no deletion, so this is not a design-gate leaf (common rule 14 does not apply).
- **Compatibility.** `plans show` is new. The history `plan` field is optional and additive (history stays 1.0); the M3 build ignores it, and `plans show` reads lines from any build with a minimal tolerant parse. A plan from another build is shown with `build_matches: false` and its state judged normally; the human line says `apply` will refuse it.
- **Privacy.** Outputs show plan and transaction ids, client ids, addon names, versions, the user's own argv and input paths; never anything below `WTF/`. A `backup restore --addon` plan's intent names addons, not accounts or characters. Subtask 5 asserts it on homes with `FAKEACCT`/`FakeRealm`/`FakeChar` planted.
- **Performance.** One small plan file and a backward scan that stops at the plan's creation: typically a few dozen lines and a few milliseconds. The worst case is bounded by `PLAN_EVIDENCE_LINES_MAX` lines of at most `DISCOVERY_FILE_MAX_BYTES` each, held one block and one line at a time. No perf budget is set (the plan sets none); the bound is the guarantee.
- **Decided defaults** are each marked "Decided while writing this bead" above; the implementer confirms or adjusts each in the close comment.

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M4 plan, 2026-10-24).**

**Why this bead.** M4 lets every addon-changing command store its preview as a plan, and `omaddons apply <plan_id>` executes exactly that plan, one transaction per client. An agent whose `apply` output is lost (a broken pipe, a killed terminal, its own restart) cannot tell what happened: `apply --dry-run` revalidates and refuses a stale plan, and a second `apply` says `plan_stale` (`already_applied`, or `targets`) without saying whether the first one committed everywhere or something else interfered. Without an answer, an agent either retries blindly, stacking a second change on a first it never saw, or gives up. History already records the plan id on every transaction `apply` commits. This bead adds the read that turns that into an answer, `omaddons plans show <plan_id>`: offline, with no lock and no write, it reports what was approved, what history records of it, and one of `pending`, `completed`, `partial`, `expired` or `unknown`, with an undo command for each committed transaction. It keeps the thesis true for agents: omaddons stays the sole, safe, undoable authority, and the safe next step is always the obvious one.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M4-D63:** `plans show` inspects one approval and reconciles it with history; read-only, offline, write-free; five states; `evidence.complete`; a missing file with evidence still answers (`stored: false`, `unknown`), with no evidence it is `plan_not_found`; never infer success from matching versions; a backward scan bounded by `PLAN_EVIDENCE_LINES_MAX` that stops at the plan's creation.
- **M4-D25:** the history `plan` field (written by D5) is the only evidence, shared with `apply`'s `already_applied`.
- **M4-D23:** ids are 8+ characters matched ignoring case, resolved as `apply` resolves them; a plan file that does not load is reported (`stored: true, readable: false`) and never acted on.
- **M4-D24:** the plan file's fields (`approval`, `summary[]`, `created_at`, `expires_at`, `build_id`); readers are bounded.
- **M4-D61:** one transaction per target, so a run can be partial and the answer is per target; a no-op preview stores no plan, so every stored plan approves at least one change.
- **M4-D22 / M4-D21:** `plans show` neither stores nor binds; plans live in `<cache>`, history in `<state>`, so history outlives a wiped plan.
- **M4-D15 / M4-D12:** `plans shwo <id>` and `plan show <id>` are corpus rows whose fix runs; a guessed command is a corrected argv only when it reads.
- **M4-D7:** the guide's generated command table gains `plans show`; `SKILL.md` is regenerated.
- **M4-D5, M4-D10, M4-D18, M4-D55, M4-D56:** declared exits `[0, 1, 2, 3]`, typed `details`, no `HashMap`, the contract rules from slice 1, field order as rendering order.

**Alternatives rejected that matter here.**
- A `plans list` (M4-D63): agents keep their own ids, and listing every preview (the widget previews every update) is noise.
- Making `apply` idempotent (M4-D63): it would hide a partial application and the interference that caused it.
- Judging from records or installed versions: matching versions are not evidence; a typed command can install the same versions without the plan.
- Reading `history.jsonl` whole, as every reader does today: cost proportional to the machine's whole history on every reconciliation.
- A second reverse reader for `apply`: two readers could disagree; one function serves both (decided while writing this bead, since the plan gives the scan to D9 but has D5 need it first).
- `PLAN_TTL` before now as the only horizon when the file is gone (the plan's rule): adding the time the plan id itself encodes only moves the horizon earlier, and stops a plan older than 24 hours from reporting `complete: true` for a search that ended before its commits.
- Calling a `backup prune` plan `pending` or `expired`: `backup prune` appends no history line by README's promise, so history cannot show whether it ran; it is `unknown`.
- Probing the plan's lease to report a running `apply`: `pending` is literally true until the first commit, a second `apply` waits on the lease and then reports `already_applied`, and once the running transaction journals the journal rule says `unknown`.
- A one-word synonym `plan` → `plans` for the typo: judging a rowless parent's guess by the command the corrected argv reaches is `subcommand_fix`'s own documented rule, covers near-misses too, and changes nothing for paths with a row.

**Risks and how they are watched.**
- Risk #14 (a large milestone, a long critical path): this leaf is on the plans chain (D1 → D2 → D4 → D5 → D9 → H1), one unit behind the critical path; its subtasks 3–5 run in parallel once subtask 2 lands.
- Risk #13 (the guide drifts): B2 copies this leaf's reconcile wording, and B2's test parses every command the guide names.
- Evidence gaps in D5 (a command path or a roll-forward without `plan`): subtask 5 checks every storable command and subtask 4 the roll-forward; a gap is filed against D5 and blocks this bead.
- Two clocks (history `at` is the real clock; `OMADDONS_NOW` freezes only `clock::now()`): tests freeze time only on `plans show`; the id-time horizon protects the scan.
- Unreadable lines, a cut scan, an open journal: each makes the answer `unknown` unless every approved client is already proven committed, so nothing is ever guessed.

**What it unblocks, and why they wait.**
- B2 (the guide's content): its core loop's reconcile step names `plans show`.
- D7 (release drift and apply races): its interference race asserts `plans show`'s `partial`.
- H1 (the pre-freeze audit): it must see this command's data shape, like every other new shape.
- T3 (slice 2 end to end): its demo item "`plans show` reconciles a lost output" runs this command with subtask 4's helpers.

**How it serves the milestone's goals.** G-M4-3 ("an approval can be inspected and reconciled", per target), G-M4-2 (the two typos get fixes that run), G-M4-1 (a published, strictly validated schema from the command's row), G-M4-6 (read-only by construction: no lock, no write, no request, asserted by a whole-home tree hash on every run in the suites). Checkpoint criteria: 7 (its `plans show` bullet), 5 (its two corpus rows), 2 and 14 (for its own path).

**Facts verified while writing this bead** (at `c0ab5e9`): no `plans` command, no `plan` history field and no reverse history reader exist; every history reader loads the whole file (`src/state/history.rs:442-503`), with `line_facts` (`:579-594`) as the minimal-field precedent. A commit's history `at` is `Timestamp::now()` under the lock (`src/engine/tx.rs:1166`). `World::load` writes the discovery cache (`src/app/world.rs:1-4`), so the command must not build one; `journal::pending` and `probe_global` are read-only. `backup prune` appends no history line (`README.md:1242`). `tests/contract/usage_fixes.rs:127` pins bare `omaddons plan` to `omaddons help pin`, which changes once `plans` exists (distance 1). `subcommand_fix` judges a guess by the guessed path (`src/cli.rs:876-885`), and `mutates()` counts a rowless path as mutating (`src/app/mod.rs:169-174`), so `plan show <id>` would get only `omaddons help plans` without subtask 3's rule. The contract snapshots redact ULIDs, times and tokens but not build ids (`tests/contract/main.rs:307-360`).

**Confidence.** High. The command is a bounded read over two files and existing read-only helpers, with a pure judgment function that is unit-tested rule by rule; nothing here is a protocol, so there is no crash matrix to design. The residual risk lives in D5's evidence, which subtask 5 checks for every storable command.

title: The `plans show` command: the `plans` noun, its registry touch points, the read-only reconciliation and its README
description:
Part 2 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.9 (`omaddons plans show`). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

D9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.9`) adds `omaddons plans show <PLAN_ID>`, the read that tells an agent what it approved and what history records of it, after an `apply`'s output was lost to a broken pipe or a restart (M4-D63). A stored plan otherwise has two verbs, create (`--dry-run`) and execute (`apply`), and neither answers "did it happen?": `apply --dry-run` revalidates and refuses a stale plan, and a second `apply` reports `plan_stale` (`already_applied`, or `targets`), which does not say whether the first one committed on every client. History holds the answer: every transaction `apply` commits records `plan: <plan_id>` (M4-D25, D5, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`).

This subtask is the command itself: the `plans` noun with its one subcommand, every DEC-1 registry touch point in one commit (common rule 4), the read-only reconciliation in `src/app/plans.rs` (resolve, read, scan, judge), its typed data, its human output, its errors, and its README sections. It builds on subtask 1's `history::plan_evidence` and `plans::evidence_horizon`. It is one step because DEC-1 forbids splitting a command's registry touch points, and the command is not useful without its judgment.

**The decision it implements (M4-D63), restated.** `omaddons plans show <PLAN_ID> [--json]` is read-only (`mutates: false`, group Look), offline and write-free; it never re-plans and makes no request. It returns the stored approval when the file exists (the intent's command and `display_argv`, the typed approval summary, the absolute inputs, `created_at`, `expires_at`, `build_id` and whether it matches this binary), history's evidence keyed by the plan id (`{target, tx, result, at}` per line carrying `plan: <id>`), a `state` (`pending`: stored, unexpired, no commit recorded; `completed`: a committed transaction for every target of the approved selection; `partial`: some, not all; `expired`: past expiry, nothing recorded; `unknown`: the file is gone or unreadable, or the scan was cut short), and `evidence.complete` (false when the scan stopped at its bound before the plan's creation). A missing file with recorded commits still answers, with `stored: false`, the evidence and `state: unknown`; a missing file with no evidence is `plan_not_found`. **Success is never inferred from addon versions that happen to match.** Rejected: a `plans list` (an agent keeps its own ids; listing every preview, the widget's included, is noise; do not add one), and an idempotent `apply` (it would hide a partial application).

Other decisions it obeys: M4-D23 (ids are 8+ characters matched ignoring case; a plan file that does not load is `plan_not_found` for `apply`, and here it is **reported**, `stored: true, readable: false`, never acted on); M4-D24 (the plan file's fields; "`plans show` reads one plan and a bounded history tail"); M4-D61 (one transaction per target; a no-op preview stores no plan, so every stored plan approves at least one change); M4-D22 (`plans show` neither stores nor binds); M4-D21 (plans live in `<cache>`, history in `<state>`); DEC-3 and M4-D18 (`Serialize + JsonSchema`, no `HashMap`); M4-D5 (declared exits); M4-D7 (regenerate `SKILL.md`).

**Facts this subtask relies on** (verified at `c0ab5e9`, except D4's and D5's, which their beads deliver):
- `app::COMMANDS` (`src/app/mod.rs:121-165`), `canonical`/`group_of` (`:176-192`), `command_name` (`:195-237`; A1 turns its body into `canonical_path`), `dispatch`/`run_command` (`:331-587`). A1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1`) adds the M4 row fields, builds rows with `entry(name, group, mutates, exits, data, network)`, and gives a parent that requires a subcommand no row: `group_of` places it at its first subcommand's row, `canonical` maps it to the only row beneath it.
- `Command` (`src/cli.rs:137-213`); A1 made `auth` `subcommand_required = true, arg_required_else_help = false`. `usage_error`'s `help_fix` (`src/cli.rs:638-642`) gives `omaddons help <path>` for a missing subcommand. `cli::command_of` names a usage error's envelope (`:461-467`). `check_if_match` (`:309-339`) refuses `--if-match` on a non-binding command and, for a read, fixes it by dropping the flag.
- `World::load` writes the discovery cache (`src/app/world.rs:1-4`, `:116-117`): do not build a `World`. Read-only pieces: `Paths::from_env()`, `state::registry::load_registry` (`src/state/registry.rs:80-88`), `engine::journal::pending` and `pending_warnings` (`src/engine/journal.rs:679-744`), `World::target_id`'s fallback chain (`src/app/world.rs:196-212`) as the model for naming a key.

- Registry tests: `bare_help_stays_one_screen_with_every_planned_command` (`src/app/help.rs:433-477`); `help_walks_a_nested_path` (`tests/cli_skeleton.rs:208-260`) and the bare-help snapshot (`tests/snapshots/cli_skeleton__bare_help_human.snap`); `read_only_commands_ignore_dry_run_and_reason` (`tests/contract/special.rs:312-386`, the invocation table `:317-338`); `cli_paths_mirror_the_registry` (`tests/omarchy_widget.rs:28-50`) over `CLI_PATHS` (`omarchy/Model.js:133-178`); the contract matrix (`tests/contract/matrix.rs`) and `support::stable`/`scrub`/`redact` (`tests/contract/main.rs:307-360`, no build-id rule); `usage_fixes.rs`'s `DECIDED` row `(&["plan"], &["omaddons", "help", "pin"])` (`tests/contract/usage_fixes.rs:127`).

## Technical Approach

### 1. clap (`src/cli.rs`) and the module (`src/app/plans.rs`)

```rust
// src/cli.rs, in Command, after History
/// Inspect a stored plan and what history records of it (changes nothing)
#[command(subcommand_required = true, arg_required_else_help = false)]
Plans(crate::app::plans::PlansArgs),

// src/app/plans.rs
#[derive(Debug, Clone, clap::Args)]
pub struct PlansArgs {
    #[command(subcommand)]
    pub action: PlansAction,
}
#[derive(Debug, Clone, clap::Subcommand)]
pub enum PlansAction {
    /// What a stored plan approved, and whether history records it as applied (offline;
    /// changes nothing)
    #[command(after_long_help = PLANS_SHOW_HELP)]
    Show(ShowArgs),
}
impl PlansAction {
    pub fn command(&self) -> &'static str { match self { Self::Show(_) => "plans show" } }

```

`PLANS_SHOW_HELP`:

```text
Examples:
  omaddons plans show 01M8Q2VA          what plan 01M8Q2VA… approved, and whether it was applied
  omaddons plans show 01M8Q2VA --json   the same as one JSON envelope, for an agent

A plan is what a --dry-run stored (data.plan_id). plans show reads it and history.jsonl
and changes nothing: no lock, no network. Its state is pending, completed, partial,
expired or unknown; only history lines that carry the plan id count as applied, never
addon versions that happen to match. -t does not apply: a plan names its own clients.
```

Bare `plans` is clap's missing-subcommand error → `usage`, fix `omaddons help plans`, envelope `command` `plans show` (A1's `canonical`). `-t`, `--dry-run`, `--reason`, `--offline`, `--while-running` change nothing; `--if-match` is `usage` from `check_if_match`. *Decided while writing this bead:* `-t` is ignored (a plan names its own clients; the other clients' evidence is part of the answer).

### 2. `pub fn show(ctx: &Context, args: &ShowArgs) -> Result<PlansShowOutcome>`

In order; nothing in it takes a lock, writes, or makes a request.

1. **Prefix check.** Uppercase `args.plan_id`. Fewer than `app::history::MIN_PREFIX` (8) characters → `usage` before any read: "a plan id or prefix has at least 8 characters, not \"<given>\"", fix `omaddons help plans show`.
2. `let paths = Paths::from_env()?; let now = crate::clock::now();`
3. **Stored plans first.** `state::plans::matching(&paths, &given)` lists `<cache>/plans/` (D4's bounded listing) and returns the matching ids, sorted. If D5's resolver builds `apply`'s errors itself, split it here into this shared function plus each command's error, keeping `apply`'s messages byte-identical. Two or more → `ref_ambiguous` (section 6). One → `id`, `stored = true`. None → go to step 5 with `stored = false`.
4. **Read the plan** (`stored`): `state::plans::load(&paths, id)`. `Ok(plan)` → `readable = true`. `Err(e)` (any error for a file that exists) → `readable = false`, keep `e.message` for the human line and a debug note, use nothing from the file.
5. **Scan.** `let horizon = state::plans::evidence_horizon(readable.then(|| plan.created_at), &given_or_id, now);` then `history::plan_evidence(&paths, &matcher, horizon, PLAN_EVIDENCE_LINES_MAX)?` with `PlanMatch::Exact(id)` when stored, else `PlanMatch::Prefix(&given)`.
   - Not stored: the distinct `plan` ids in `evidence.lines`: one → `id` (keep only its lines); two or more → `ref_ambiguous` (section 6, the history message); none → `plan_not_found` (section 6).
6. **Journals.** `engine::journal::pending(&paths)?` for rule 9, and `engine::journal::pending_warnings(&paths)?` into the outcome's warnings, as every read command adds them through `World::load` (`src/app/world.rs:132-139`). *Decided while writing this bead:* keyed on each journal's target (an unfinished journal on an approved target, or one whose target cannot be read, makes the state unknown), because `journal::read` is private and `src/engine/journal.rs` is another chain's hot spot.
7. **Registry** for names: `state::registry::load_registry(&paths).ok()` (a failure is a debug note, never an error).
8. **Judge** (section 3), **build the data** (section 4), the warnings, the `commands[]` and the human view (section 5).

`plans show` never builds a `World`, never takes `<cache>/plans/.lock` or a lease, never calls `history::read` (it reads the file whole), and never touches the doorbell, the history projection, the discovery cache or the release memo.

### 3. The judgment: `fn judge(j: &Judgement) -> (PlanState, Why)`

Pure, unit-tested on its own. `Judgement` holds `stored`, `readable`, `records_history` (from the intent), the approved target keys (distinct `approval.selection[].target_key`, a `BTreeSet`), the committed target keys of the evidence, the evidence's `complete()`, `unreadable + unattributed`, the unfinished journals' targets (`Option<TargetKey>` each), `expired` (the plan's expiry predicate at `now`). First match wins:

| # | Condition | State | `Why` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | not stored | `unknown` | `FileGone` |
| 2 | not readable | `unknown` | `Unreadable(message)` |
| 3 | `!records_history` (`backup prune`) | `unknown` | `NoHistoryLine` |
| 4 | no approved target | `unknown` | `NoApprovedClients` |
| 5 | a committed line names a target not approved | `unknown` | `Disagrees` |
| 6 | approved ⊆ committed | `completed` | — |
| 7 | `!complete` | `unknown` | `ScanCut` |
| 8 | `unreadable + unattributed > 0` | `unknown` | `UnreadableLines(n)` |
| 9 | an unfinished journal on an approved target, or with no target | `unknown` | `Unfinished(tx)` |
| 10 | approved ∩ committed ≠ ∅ | `partial` | — |
| 11 | expired | `expired` | — |
| 12 | otherwise | `pending` | — |

- `fn records_history(intent: &StoredIntent) -> bool`: an **exhaustive `match` with no wildcard arm**: `BackupPrune(_) => false`, every other variant `true`. *Decided while writing this bead:* README promises `backup prune` "appends no history line", so history cannot show whether a prune plan ran; `pending` or `expired` would claim more than history proves.
- *Decided while writing this bead:* rule 6 precedes 7–9 (a commit cannot be undone by lines the scan did not read, so "every approved target committed" is certain even when the scan was cut, a line was unreadable or a journal is open); rule 5 (history and the plan disagree, which a well-formed plan cannot produce); rule 8 (an unreadable line in the window could be this plan's commit, §8.1 default 6; the warning `history_lines_skipped` is added, worded as `HistoryRead::skipped_warning` words it, with the count).
- Expiry: the same predicate `apply`'s `expired` refusal uses, as one helper `StoredPlan::is_expired(&self, now: Timestamp) -> bool` in `src/state/plans.rs`; if D4 or D5 compare inline, factor that comparison into it and point `apply` at it, so the two agree at the exact instant.
- Nothing else is consulted: no records, no installed versions, no release memo, no client tree.

- Every key is always present (no `skip_serializing_if`); `null` when unknown. With the file gone or unreadable: `created_at`, `expires_at`, `build_id`, `build_matches`, `intent`, `approval` are `null` and `inputs` is `[]`. `readable` is `false` whenever nothing was read. *Decided while writing this bead*, so the key set is stable (A3's nullability rule) and the plan's own example (`"intent":null`) holds.

- **Warnings:** `journal_pending`/`tx_in_progress` from `pending_warnings`; `history_lines_skipped` when `unreadable + unattributed > 0`. No new code.
- **`commands[]`:** undo hints only, like `TargetsData::undo_commands`: `undo_run` (`omaddons undo --run <run>`) first when the evidence holds more than one transaction and all share one `run`; then `undo` (`omaddons undo <tx>`) per evidence line, by target id; all `destructive: false`. *Decided while writing this bead:* no `apply` hint and no re-preview hint (M4-D28 admits an `apply` argv only from a preview's own `commands[]`; a re-preview hint would need a new action name).
- **Human output** (`render_in(&self, w, style, tz)`; times through `app::history::local_time`'s format in `tz`, so tests pass `TimeZone::UTC`):

  ```text
  plan 01M8Q2VA7K3N5P8R1T4W6X9Y0Z (update): partial, 1 of 2 clients committed
  approved: omaddons update
    classic: would update DBM 12.1.14 → 12.1.15
    retail: would update DBM 12.1.14 → 12.1.15
  committed:
    classic: tx 01M8T4… at 2026-10-30 18:05 · undo: omaddons undo 01M8T4…
  not recorded: retail
  apply never resumes a partial plan; preview again for the rest: omaddons update --dry-run
  ```

  - Header `plan <id> (<intent.command>): <state>` (the command omitted when unknown), then per state: `pending, stored until <expires_at>, nothing applied yet`; `completed, <n> of <n> clients committed`; `partial, <k> of <n> clients committed`; `expired at <expires_at>, nothing applied`; `unknown: <why>`.
  - `Why` texts: `FileGone` "its file is no longer in the cache, so what it approved is not known; history shows:"; `Unreadable` "its file cannot be read (<message>), so nothing in it is trusted"; `NoHistoryLine` "backup prune records no history line, so history cannot show whether it ran"; `NoApprovedClients` "its approval names no client"; `Disagrees` "history names a client the plan did not approve"; `ScanCut` "history holds more than 20000 lines since the plan was made; the search stopped there"; `UnreadableLines(n)` "<n> lines of history.jsonl in that time could not be read"; `Unfinished(tx)` "an interrupted transaction (<tx>) on <client> may hold its commit; the next change on that client finishes or rolls it back".
  - `approved:` the shell-joined `display_argv`, then the stored `summary[]` lines indented two spaces; if `summary[]` is empty, one line per approval item, `<target_id>: <op> <addon> <from_version> → <to_version>`. *Decided while writing this bead:* `summary[]` is "the approval summary's lines" (what the person saw).
  - `committed:` one line per evidence line, `<target>: tx <short_id(tx)> at <time> · undo: omaddons undo <full tx>`; for `partial`, `not recorded: <ids>`.
  - One advice line: `pending` → `apply it with: omaddons apply <id>`, or `made by another build of omaddons, so apply will refuse it: preview again with <display_argv> --dry-run` when `build_matches` is false, or `<path> is gone, so apply will refuse it: preview again with <display_argv> --dry-run` when an input is missing; `partial` → as shown; `expired` → `preview again: <display_argv> --dry-run`; `NoHistoryLine` → `see what is left: <display_argv> --dry-run`. Everywhere, `<display_argv> --dry-run` means the plan's `display_argv` with `--dry-run` inserted before its first `--` when it has one (`backup prune -t retail -- <id>`), else appended, so the suggested preview parses and keeps every positional; a unit case pins it.
  - `-v` (`style.paths_visible()`, `detail()` after A8): `reasons:` and the scope; `build: <id> (this build | another build)`; `inputs: <path> (present | missing)` each; `history: read <n> lines back to <horizon> (stopped at the start | at the horizon | at its bound)`.
- **Notes** (debug `log` events the dispatch arm emits): the scan's lines read, stop and horizon; a plan-file or registry read failure.
