title: The finding model: subsystems, severity, confidence, evidence, remediation and instance keys
description:
Part 2 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1 (The failure-mode registry, the finding model and the repair action model). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says. ## Background E1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`) creates the doctor's data model: one registry of failure modes that `status`, `doctor` and `doctor health` all read (M4-D29), the finding model every report carries, and the pure data model of a repair. It is the first leaf of M4's critical path, and every later doctor leaf codes against its types: E2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.2`, the tolerant view), E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, the runtime and its report), E5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`, the repair transaction), the catalog leaves of area F (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6`) and A4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`, `capabilities`). This part is the finding model, `src/doctor/finding.rs`: what one finding is, how it names what is broken (a stable, resource-specific `instance` key and a human `label`, built together so no detector can spell them differently), how sure it is (`confidence`), what it shows (`evidence`, typed, never file content) and how to address it (`remediation`). It is its own step because it has no dependency on the repair model (part 3) and is needed by the registry (part 4); it adds types and pure functions only, with no caller yet. The decisions it implements: - **M4-D30.** Failure-mode ids keep the published `fm--` form, the subsystem in snake_case (`concurrency_primitives`, `state_files`), because README calls the seven published ids "stable across releases" (`README.md:750`); the doctor contract's hyphen-only pattern was rejected for that reason. A finding's `instance` is `@[:]`: the scope is the target's **key** (a ULID, never the renameable id) or `machine`; the discriminator is a canonical key of the broken resource (`tx=`, `path=`, `folder=`, `blob=`), so two stuck journals on one client are two instances. The `label` is the human form (`retail · tx 01M7…`, `retail/DBM`), may change on a rename, and is never compared. Rejected: the reviewed draft's `@[/]`, which merged every journal of a client into one instance and changed on a rename, and labels as identities. - **M4-D41.** `confidence` is `high` (the state observed directly: a hash, a mode, a missing file), `medium` (inferred from consistent evidence) or `low` (a heuristic): the same enum as `errors`' attribution confidence. Rejected: a float (false precision). - **M4-D42.** Evidence is a typed object of paths, digests, modes, counts and line numbers, never file content (credentials, a config line, a TOC alike) and never a path below `WTF/`. Rejected: free-form strings (unparseable, and they leak). - **M4-D29 (the parts used here):** severity is fixed per failure mode (one instance is as bad as another, and the widget and `--severity` filter without reading evidence); `app::issues`' `Severity` is the doctor's. Facts (verified at `c0ab5e9`): `Severity` is at `src/app/issues.rs:44-51` (`P0`–`P3`, `Ord`, serialized `"P0"`…); `errors::attribute::Confidence {High, Medium, Low}` (snake_case) at `src/errors/attribute.rs:38-45`; `TargetKey` and `TxId` are ULID newtypes with `Display`, `FromStr` and a ULID-pattern schema (`src/model.rs:222-300`); `FolderName::key()` is the ASCII case-folded name (`src/model.rs:76-79`); `CommandHint` is at `src/error.rs:440-467`; there is no regex crate in `Cargo.toml`; `insta` (with `json`) is a dev-dependency (`Cargo.toml:48`). ## Technical Approach ### 1. Module - `src/lib.rs`: `pub mod doctor;` (alphabetical, after `discover`). - `src/doctor/mod.rs`: a module doc ("The doctor (M4): the failure-mode registry every `status` issue and doctor finding comes from, and the finding model. Pure: nothing here writes."), and `pub mod finding;`. Part 4 adds the other modules. ### 2. Types in `src/doctor/finding.rs` Every serialized type derives `Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, JsonSchema`; field order is rendering order (M4-D56: deterministic, not contract); no `HashMap` or `HashSet`. - **`Subsystem`** (`Copy`, `Ord`, `#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]`): `StateFiles, Configs, Schemas, Caches, Sockets, Hooks, Plugins, Secrets, Permissions, ExternalArtifacts, ConcurrencyPrimitives, Network, UserlandState`, the doctor contract's thirteen. `pub const ALL: [Subsystem; 13]` in that order; `const fn as_str(self) -> &'static str` (equal to the serde name); `FromStr` (exact names only); `const fn applicable(self) -> bool` (false for `Sockets` and `Hooks`, which have no failure modes in omaddons). - **`Severity`**: moved here from `src/app/issues.rs:44-51` unchanged (variants, derives including `Hash`, `PartialOrd`, `Ord`, doc comment). `src/app/issues.rs` replaces the definition with `pub use crate::doctor::finding::Severity;`, so `crate::app::issues::Severity` keeps resolving everywhere (`src/app/status.rs:1695` uses it). Decided while writing this bead: the doctor owns the type and `app` re-exports it, because the doctor is the lower layer that both `app::status` and later `app::doctor` depend on. - **`Confidence`**: `pub use crate::errors::attribute::Confidence;` (no new enum). - **`Evidence`**, `#[derive(Default)]`, every field `Option` with `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]` (documented optional, M4-D55 rule 2), in this order: | Key | Type | Holds | |---|---|---| | `path` | `PathBuf` | the one path concerned | | `paths` | `Vec` | several paths | | `hash` | `String` | a digest in fsx's text form (`sha256:…`, `stamp:sha256:…`, `tree:sha256:…`) | | `observed` | `String` | what was found (a version, a mode, a digest) | | `expected` | `String` | what was expected | | `mode` | `u32` | written as four octal digits (`"0600"`) by a `serialize_with` helper; schema `string`, pattern `^[0-7]{4}$` | | `pid` | `u32` | a process id | | `age_s` | `u64` | an age in seconds | | `line`, `column` | `u32` | 1-based position in a file | | `tx` | `TxId` | a transaction | | `count` | `u64` | a count | | `reason` | `&'static str` | a snake_case code, never formatted text | Decided while writing this bead: one struct with typed optional keys, not one type per failure mode, so the report has one evidence schema; catalog leaves add keys as further optional fields (never a map). `reason` is added beside M4-D42's list for the journal rows. `pub fn is_private_safe(&self) -> bool`: `false` when `path`, or any entry of `paths`, has a component equal to `WTF` (ASCII case-insensitive) that is followed by at least one more component, or when `observed` or `expected` contains `/wtf/` (ASCII case-insensitive); `/WTF` itself is allowed. No field can hold file content. - **`Remediation`** (A.4's shape), `#[derive(Default)]`, `#[schemars(rename = "DoctorRemediation")]` so its schema definition never collides with `status`'s `Remediation` in one generator: `command: String` (the display form, or prose), `argv: Option>` (`null` for prose; never skipped), `explain_command: String`, `explain_argv: Vec`, `auto_fixable: bool`, `needs_force: bool`, `estimated_actions: u32`, `destructive: bool`. - **`FindingTarget { id: String, key: TargetKey }`**. - **`Subject`**, the one way to say what a finding is about: ```rust pub enum InstanceScope { Target { id: String, key: TargetKey }, Machine } pub enum Discriminator { Tx(TxId), Path(PathBuf), Folder(FolderName), Addon(String), Blob([u8; 32]) } pub struct Subject { scope: InstanceScope, discriminator: Option } impl Subject { pub fn target(id: &str, key: TargetKey) -> Self; pub fn machine() -> Self; pub fn tx(self, tx: TxId) -> Self; pub fn path(self, path: &Path) -> Self; // stored lexically normalized pub fn folder(self, folder: &FolderName) -> Self; pub fn addon(self, name: &str) -> Self; pub fn blob(self, sha256: [u8; 32]) -> Self; } ``` A second discriminator replaces the first (`debug_assert!` that none was set). - **`InstanceKey(String)`**: no public constructor from a string; built only by `fn key_and_label(fm_id: &'static str, subject: &Subject) -> (InstanceKey, String)`, which returns both: | Discriminator | Appended to `@` | Appended to the scope label (`` or `machine`) | |---|---|---| | none | nothing | nothing | | `Tx(tx)` | `:tx=` | ` · tx ` | | `Path(p)` | `:path=

` | ` ·

` | | `Folder(f)` | `:folder=` | `/` | | `Addon(n)` | `:addon=` | `/` | | `Blob(b)` | `:blob=<64 lowercase hex>` | ` · blob ` | (` · ` is a space, U+00B7, a space.) Path normalization is lexical, by `Path::components()`: `.`, repeated and trailing separators dropped, `..` pops the previous component; `debug_assert!(path.is_absolute())`; non-UTF-8 bytes become U+FFFD. Decided while writing this bead: the `addon=` discriminator is added to the plan's four, because two of the seven moved rows (record-folder-missing, managed-files-modified) report one finding per addon and no other discriminator names one; it is an additive instance-key form. `InstanceKey` implements `Display` and `Serialize` (as the string), `JsonSchema` (a string), `Ord`. `pub fn parse(s: &str) -> Result` for E3's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`) `explain ` and `--since`: `ParsedInstance { fm: String, scope: ParsedScope, discriminator: Option<(DiscriminatorKind, String)> }`, `ParsedScope::{Target(TargetKey), Machine}`. Rules: split at the first `@` (missing → `MissingScope`); the fm part must pass `is_fm_id` (`BadFmId`); the scope is up to the first `:` and must be `machine` or a ULID (`BadScope`); the rest, when present, is `=` with kind `tx`, `path`, `folder`, `addon` or `blob` (`UnknownDiscriminator`) and a valid value (`BadValue`: `tx` a ULID; `path` starts with `/`; `folder` and `addon` non-empty and equal to their ASCII lowercase; `blob` 64 lowercase hex). `InstanceParseError` implements `Display` naming the part. - **`pub fn is_fm_id(s: &str) -> bool`**: the plan's pattern `^fm-[a-z0-9_]+-[a-z0-9-]+$`, by hand: starts with `fm-`; then one or more of `[a-z0-9_]` (the subsystem part, up to the next `-`); then `-`; then one or more of `[a-z0-9-]` to the end. `pub fn subsystem_part(id: &str) -> Option<&str>` returns the part between `fm-` and the next `-`. Part 4's invariant test uses both. - **`Finding`**, serialized in A.4's order: ```rust pub struct Finding { pub id: &'static str, pub instance: InstanceKey, pub label: String, pub severity: Severity, pub subsystem: Subsystem, pub title: String, // this instance's title pub confidence: Confidence, pub target: Option, // null for the machine pub addon: Option, // always present, null when none pub folder: Option, // always present, null when none pub evidence: Evidence, pub remediation: Remediation, } ``` Serialize only (`id` is `&'static str`; E3 reads a past run's instance keys as plain JSON). - **`Observation`**, what a detector reports, one per instance: `subject: Subject`, `title: String`, `confidence: Confidence`, `addon: Option`, `folder: Option`, `evidence: Evidence`. - **`Detected { found: Vec, incomplete: Option }`** (`Default`), a detector's return; **`Incomplete { limit: IncompleteLimit }`**, `IncompleteLimit::{Deadline, Entries, OnlineRequests}` (snake_case). M4-D43: a detector stopped by its deadline, `DOCTOR_SCAN_MAX_ENTRIES` or an online request limit returns what it found plus this record; E3 turns each into a `fm-state_files-check-incomplete` finding and may add fields. - **`pub(crate) fn Finding::build(id: &'static str, subsystem: Subsystem, severity: Severity, obs: Observation, remediation: impl FnOnce(&Finding) -> Remediation) -> Finding`**: computes `(instance, label)` with `key_and_label`, `target` from the scope, copies the observation's fields, sets `remediation` to `Remediation::default()`, then replaces it with `remediation(&finding)`. Only the registry (part 4) calls it. Decided while writing this bead: detectors return `Observation`s and the registry row turns them into `Finding`s, because the row owns the id, severity, subsystem and remediation; the plan's `Detected` "holds findings", and this is the same contract one step earlier. - `debug_assert!(obs.evidence.is_private_safe())` in `Finding::build`, so a detector that put a path below `WTF/` into evidence fails every debug test that exercises it. ### 3. What not to do - No I/O, no `std::fs`, no clock. - No `Deserialize` on `Finding` or `Evidence` (nothing reads them back in M4 except as JSON values). - Do not move or change `status`'s `Remediation` or `Issue`: `status`'s wire shape stays its own. ## Acceptance Criteria - [ ] `src/doctor/finding.rs` defines `Subsystem`, `Severity` (moved), `Confidence` (re-export), `Evidence`, `Remediation`, `FindingTarget`, `Subject`, `InstanceScope`, `Discriminator`, `InstanceKey` (with `parse`), `Finding`, `Observation`, `Detected`, `Incomplete`, `is_fm_id` and `subsystem_part`; `src/lib.rs` declares `pub mod doctor`; `app::issues` re-exports `Severity` and every existing use compiles unchanged. - [ ] Instance keys: two subjects of one failure mode on one target with different resources give different keys; the same key with a different target id gives the same `instance` and a different `label`; every built key parses back to its parts; each malformed key is refused with its own error. - [ ] `is_fm_id` accepts the seven published ids and rejects every invalid case of `fm_ids_by_case`. - [ ] `Evidence::default()` serializes as `{}`; set keys appear in the declared order; `is_private_safe` is false exactly for paths below `WTF/`. - [ ] A finding's JSON matches the reviewed `finding_report_shape` snapshot (A.4's key order, `target`/`addon`/`folder` present as `null`), and the doctor `Remediation`'s schema is named `DoctorRemediation`. - [ ] No production code outside `src/lib.rs`, `src/doctor/` and the `Severity` re-export changes; every existing test and snapshot passes unchanged. - [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files. ## Test Plan ### Unit tests (`src/doctor/finding.rs`, `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`) All table-driven, each case named; assertion messages name the case and show the input and the actual value. - `subsystems_are_the_doctor_contracts_thirteen`: `ALL.len() == 13`; `as_str` in order equals the thirteen names; `serde_json::to_value(s) == as_str` for each; `FromStr` round-trips each and rejects `"state-files"`, `"StateFiles"`, `""`; `applicable()` is false exactly for `sockets` and `hooks`. - `severity_keeps_its_wire_form_and_order`: `P0`…`P3` serialize as `"P0"`…`"P3"`; `P0 < P1 < P2 < P3`; a function taking `crate::app::issues::Severity` accepts `crate::doctor::finding::Severity::P2` (same type). - `confidence_is_the_errors_enum`: `high`, `medium`, `low` serialize so; the type is `crate::errors::attribute::Confidence`. - `instance_keys_and_labels_by_case`, with `K = 01M5ZQ7Y3KJ8V9W2X4C6B0N1RT`, `T = 01M7A1B2C3D4E5F6G7H8J9K0MN`, fm `fm-state_files-example-mode`: | Case | Subject | `instance` | `label` | |---|---|---|---| | `target_only` | target(`retail`, K) | `fm-state_files-example-mode@K` | `retail` | | `target_tx` | + tx T | `…@K:tx=T` | `retail · tx T` | | `machine_only` | machine | `…@machine` | `machine` | | `machine_tx` | machine + tx T | `…@machine:tx=T` | `machine · tx T` | | `path_normalized` | target + path `/fixture/a/./b//c/` | `…@K:path=/fixture/a/b/c` | `retail · /fixture/a/b/c` | | `path_parent_resolved` | target + path `/fixture/a/b/../c` | `…@K:path=/fixture/a/c` | `retail · /fixture/a/c` | | `folder_key` | target + folder `DBM-Core` | `…@K:folder=dbm-core` | `retail/DBM-Core` | | `addon_lowercased` | target + addon `DBM` | `…@K:addon=dbm` | `retail/DBM` | | `blob_hex` | machine + blob `[0xab; 32]` | `…@machine:blob=abab…ab` (64) | `machine · blob abababababab` | - `resources_on_one_target_are_distinct_instances`: two `tx` subjects on one target give two keys; two `path` subjects; two `addon` subjects; the same resource twice gives equal keys. - `a_rename_changes_the_label_not_the_instance`: `target("retail", K).tx(T)` and `target("main", K).tx(T)` give equal `instance` and labels `retail · tx T` and `main · tx T`. - `instance_keys_parse_back`: every key of the table parses to its fm, scope and discriminator, and re-serializes equal. - `malformed_instance_keys_are_refused_by_part`: `fm-a-b` (`MissingScope`), `fm-A-b@machine` (`BadFmId`), `fm-a-b@retail` (`BadScope`: an id is not a key), `fm-a-b@machine:color=red` (`UnknownDiscriminator`), `fm-a-b@machine:tx=nope` (`BadValue`), `fm-a-b@machine:path=relative` (`BadValue`), `fm-a-b@machine:addon=DBM` (`BadValue`: not lowercase), `fm-a-b@machine:blob=abc` (`BadValue`). - `fm_ids_by_case`: accepted: the seven published ids, `fm-state_files-check-incomplete`, `fm-a-b-`; rejected: `fm-a` (no slug), `fm--b`, `fm-a-` (empty slug), `fm-a-b_c` (underscore in the slug), `fm-State-b`, `xm-a-b`, `fm-a-b c`, `""`; `subsystem_part("fm-state_files-record-folder-missing") == Some("state_files")`. - `evidence_serializes_only_what_it_holds`: `Evidence::default()` gives `{}`; `{tx, reason: "journal_too_new"}` gives exactly those two keys in that order; `mode: 0o600` gives `"0600"` and `0o4755` gives `"4755"`; `paths` of two entries keeps their order. - `evidence_below_wtf_is_not_private_safe`: safe: `/fixture/state/omaddons/targets/K.json`, `/fixture/client/WTF`, `/fixture/client/Interface/AddOns/WTFHelper`; not safe: `/fixture/client/WTF/Account/A/SavedVariables/x.lua`, `/fixture/client/wtf/Config.wtf`, `paths` holding one bad entry among good ones, `observed` containing `/WTF/Account`. - `a_finding_serializes_in_report_order`: a target finding (the journal-pending example of the parent bead, built with `Finding::build` and a fixed remediation) and a machine finding (`target`, `addon`, `folder` all `null`); `insta::assert_json_snapshot!("finding_report_shape", [target_finding, machine_finding])`; a second assertion lists the keys in order: `id, instance, label, severity, subsystem, title, confidence, target, addon, folder, evidence, remediation`, and the remediation's `command, argv, explain_command, explain_argv, auto_fixable, needs_force, estimated_actions, destructive`. - `the_doctor_remediation_schema_has_its_own_name`: `::schema_name()` is `DoctorRemediation`, and `status`'s is `Remediation`. - `build_runs_the_remediation_on_the_finished_finding`: the closure sees the computed `instance` and `target`. ### Integration and end-to-end tests None: nothing calls these types yet. Part 4 uses them, and part 5 checks `status` end to end. ### Logging Case names in every table; assertion messages show `case`, the subject or input, and the actual key, label or JSON. The snapshot is named `finding_report_shape`. ## Considerations - **These shapes are first emitted by E3** (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, `doctor diagnose`). Get them right now: after E3 they are the doctor report's contract, and after H2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.2`, the golden) they are frozen. Every name follows M4-D55's rules 1–4 (snake_case keys, closed snake_case enums, `age_s` with its unit, optional keys documented as optional). - `label` is display only. Nothing may compare it (E3's `--since` compares `instance`). - **Hot spot:** `src/app/issues.rs` (this leaf, then F1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1`, then F8, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.8`) changes by one line here (the re-export); part 4 changes it further. - `Subsystem` order is the doctor contract's; A4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`) decides what its `failure_modes.subsystems` lists from `ALL` and `applicable()`. ## Dependencies - **Parent:** E1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`). - **Before it:** nothing; it starts at once, beside parts 1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1.1`) and 3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1.3`), which touch other files. - **After it:** part 4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1.4`) builds the registry, the runner and the seven rows on these types.

comments.author: RadiantNebula
comments.text:
decided: Finding::build stays pub(crate), as specified. Until the registry (part 4) calls it, the non-test build has no caller, so it carries #[cfg_attr(not(test), expect(dead_code, reason = ...))]. That expectation goes unfulfilled, and so fails clippy, the moment part 4 adds the call, which makes part 4 remove it.

decided: an instance key reads back only in its canonical form. The scope must be the target key's uppercase text (a lowercase ULID is BadScope), and a tx value must be its canonical ULID. So every key that parses re-serializes byte for byte (ParsedInstance's Display), which E3's --since comparison relies on. A discriminator without '=' is UnknownDiscriminator naming the whole text. Values may hold ':' and '=' (a path), because the split takes the first ':' after the scope and the first '=' after the kind.

decided: Subject's fields stay private, as the bead's sketch has them. Finding::build reads them in-module, and part 4 can add accessors if a row needs one.

decided: README's code map gains a src/doctor/ row saying the doctor is in progress and naming finding.rs. That is no product promise, so it is not the command reference section E3 writes.

decided: the r4-open-enum issue for evidence.mode and evidence.reason (A3's rule test) is E3's to settle when it publishes the report schema. I left a note on c6cm.5.3.5 rather than retyping the keys against this bead's spec.

title: The repair action model: fixes, primitives, steps, endpoint predicates and guards
description:
Part 3 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1 (The failure-mode registry, the finding model and the repair action model). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

E1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`) creates the doctor's data model. Beside the failure-mode registry and the finding model, the plan gives it the **repair action model**: the pure data types that describe a doctor repair, which E5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`, the repair transaction) lowers, journals, executes and recovers, E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`, `doctor fix`) previews and binds, E7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7`) inverts for undo, and E12's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.12`) history lines record. This part is `src/engine/repair_action.rs`: no lowering, no I/O, no execution. It is its own step because it shares nothing with the finding model (part 2) and is needed by the registry's fixer spec (part 4); its acceptance includes the plan's "The `Primitive` and `Step` types serialize to the repair journal's `primitives[]` wire form (unit snapshot)".

What a repair is, and why this shape (the decisions it follows):
- **M4-D31: a doctor fix run is one engine transaction of kind `repair`.** A fixer returns presentation-level **fixes** (a write, a chmod, a quarantine, a flatten, a suspension, a delegation). Before anything commits, E5 lowers them into one immutable, ordered list of **primitives**, each exactly one filesystem operation: `WriteFile`, `Chmod` or `RenameNoReplace`. A flatten becomes two or three separately journaled renames; no step hides more than one rename. Each primitive has its own sequence number, its own write-ahead `step` line, complete **endpoint predicates** (what must be at its path, and at a rename's destination, before and after it, including required absence), a reserved backup path when it overwrites, and an inverse. A chmod's predicate is compound (a regular file of the recorded identity with the old mode), so a same-mode replacement file is never taken for the credential that was inspected. Identity is compared the reboot-safe way: inode and birth time, device ignored. The journal's `prepared` line holds `fixes[]` (`{fix, fm, kind}`) and `primitives[]` (`{seq, fix, fm, op, path, to?, mode?, pre, post, backup?, activation?, guards?}`). Rejected: one write-ahead step per presentation-level action (a crash between a flatten's two renames would match neither its before nor its after); a doctor-only undo from `actions.jsonl` (written after the fact, so not crash-safe).
- **M4-D35: quarantine never crosses a filesystem.** A victim under `<state>` or `<config>` goes to `<run>/quarantine/{state,config}/<relative path>`, one under `<cache>` to `<cache>/quarantine/<run id>/<relative path>`, one in a client (`<meta>` or `Interface/AddOns`) to `<meta>/snapshots/<repair tx>.repair/quarantine/<relative path>`. Rejected: copy plus delete across filesystems (a deletion, and not atomic).
- **M4-D37: a recoverable journal is fixed by the engine's own recovery, as a declared delegation** `{tx, family, phase, direction}`, predicted by `journal::diagnose` and disclosed in the preview.
- **M4-D38: the stuck journal states get a guarded set-aside**: one `RenameNoReplace` per artifact of the journal set, carrying a **suspension manifest** (`guards`: the target's record generation, the client marker's digest, and the epochs of the resources the suspended journal would touch; for a `WTF` journal one digest of the tree's stamps, never a path below it); its undo reactivates through an **activation** rename (`activation: true`) that comes last.
- **M4-D44:** a preview's token holds nothing run-specific; the primitive's fields here are what E6 canonicalizes.
- **M4-D55, M4-D56:** every wire name follows the contract rules (snake_case keys, closed snake_case enums, optional keys documented as optional); field order is deterministic but not contract.

Facts (verified at `c0ab5e9`): fsx's digest text forms are `sha256:<hex>` (content), `stamp:sha256:<hex>` (a stamp digest), `mode:<octal>` (`src/fsx/mutate.rs:256-287`), and `StampDigest` has `Display` but no public bytes (`mutate.rs:188-261`); `Expect` is `Absent | Hash` (`mutate.rs:85-90`), which E13 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.13`) generalizes to `Present(Predicate)` (internal, not wire); `FileId {dev, ino, born_ns: Option<i64>}` skips `born_ns` when `None` and is compared without the device (`src/engine/journal.rs:297-337`); `TxId` and `TargetKey` are ULID newtypes (`src/model.rs:222-300`); the folder journal's line tag is `"type"` (`journal.rs:48-60`); `insta` (`json`) is a dev-dependency.

## Technical Approach

### 1. Module

`src/engine/mod.rs`: `pub mod repair_action;` with a one-line doc. `src/engine/repair_action.rs` opens with a module doc that states: what a fix, a primitive and a step are; that this module holds data only (E5, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`, lowers, journals and runs; E7, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7`, inverts); that every path is absolute; and that the wire form is the repair journal's `primitives[]` and history's `repairs[]`. Every wire type derives `Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema`; no `deny_unknown_fields` (a newer minor's additive keys must keep reading); no `HashMap`; no `serde_json::Value`.

### 2. Scalars

- **`Mode(u32)`**: `pub const fn new(bits: u32) -> Option<Mode>` (`None` above `0o7777`), `bits()`; `Display` and `Serialize` as exactly four octal digits (`format!("{:04o}")`: `"0600"`, `"0644"`, `"4755"`); `FromStr` and `Deserialize` accept only `^[0-7]{4}$`; schema `string` with that pattern.
- **`Identity { ino: u64, born_ns: Option<i64> }`**: a path's identity without its device. Written `{"ino":"<decimal>","born_ns":"<decimal>"}` (decimal **strings**), `born_ns` omitted when the filesystem records no birth time (as `FileId` does), read back exactly. Decided while writing this bead: strings, because a nanosecond birth time (about 1.8 × 10^18) exceeds the 2^53 integers that `jq` or the widget's JavaScript hold exactly, and the plan's examples quote them. A `From<&FileId>` is not added here (E13, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.13`, moves `FileId` into fsx; E5 converts).
- **`Sha256([u8; 32])`**: written `sha256:<64 lowercase hex>`. **`Stamp([u8; 32])`**: written `stamp:sha256:<64 lowercase hex>` (M3-D25's stat digest of a directory). Each `FromStr` accepts only its own prefix and exactly 64 lowercase hex digits, so a stamp is never read as a content digest. Because the text equals fsx's `Display`, E5 converts an fsx `StampDigest` with `Stamp::from_str(&digest.to_string())` and touches no fsx code.

### 3. Predicates

```rust
/// One path's predicate: what must be there (or that nothing is). A part that is absent
/// is not checked.
#[serde(tag = "kind", rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum Endpoint {
    Absent,
    File    { identity: Option<Identity>, sha256: Option<Sha256>, mode: Option<Mode> },
    Dir     { identity: Option<Identity>, stamp: Option<Stamp> },
    Symlink { identity: Option<Identity>, link_target: Option<PathBuf> },
}

/// A step's `pre` or `post`.
#[serde(untagged)]
pub enum Endpoints {
    /// A write's or a chmod's: the predicate of its one path.
    One(Endpoint),
    /// A rename's: its source (`path`) and its destination (`to`).
    Pair { path: Endpoint, to: Endpoint },
}
```

Every optional part has `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`. Decided while writing this bead: one variant per kind (§7.6's predicate kinds `absent`, `file`, `dir`, `symlink`), so a content digest on a directory or a stamp on a file cannot be expressed; the JSON equals a flat optional-parts predicate for every valid combination (E12's, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.12`, history type is one). Which part is recorded where (§6.14.1): the file type for every present endpoint; `identity` for a rename's source and its destination afterwards, and a chmod's file before and after; `sha256` for a write's `pre` when it overwrites and its `post`; `mode` for a chmod's `pre` and `post` and a write's `post`; `stamp` for a directory that is renamed; `link_target` for a symlink that is renamed.

### 4. Primitives and steps

```rust
#[serde(tag = "op")]
pub enum Primitive {
    #[serde(rename = "write_file")]
    WriteFile { path: PathBuf, mode: Mode, backup: Option<PathBuf> },   // backup omitted when the write creates a file
    #[serde(rename = "chmod")]
    Chmod { path: PathBuf, mode: Mode },
    #[serde(rename = "rename_noreplace")]                                 // snake_case would give rename_no_replace
    RenameNoReplace { #[serde(rename = "path")] from: PathBuf, to: PathBuf,
                      #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "std::ops::Not::not")] activation: bool },
}

pub struct Step {
    pub seq: u32,                      // 1-based, contiguous
    pub fix: u32,                      // 1-based index into the journal's fixes[]
    pub fm: Cow<'static, str>,
    #[serde(flatten)]
    pub op: Primitive,
    pub pre: Endpoints,
    pub post: Endpoints,
    #[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]
    pub guards: Vec<Guard>,
}
```

- `backup` has `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`: the reserved backup path of an overwriting write, omitted when the write creates a file (the plan's `backup?`).
- Decided while writing this bead: **a write's content digest lives in its `post`** (`{"kind":"file","sha256":…,"mode":…}`) and nowhere else, because the plan's journal key list has no `content_sha256` key and one digest in two places could disagree; `Step::write_digest(&self) -> Option<&Sha256>` reads it. **`fm` is a `Cow<'static, str>`**, because a journal written by a newer build may name a failure mode this build does not know and recovery must still read it (fixers construct `Cow::Borrowed`). **`Step` has no `resources` field yet**: the plan's `ResourceSet` is E13's type and E13 is not a blocker of this leaf; E5 adds it (not part of a primitive's wire form: the journal records the union as its top-level `resources`).
- Wire order produced: `seq, fix, fm, op, path, to | mode [, backup] [, activation], pre, post [, guards]`.
- If schemars cannot render the flattened, internally tagged `Primitive` faithfully under `SchemaSettings::for_serialize()` (each op's keys required in its variant), implement `JsonSchema` for `Step` by hand as a `oneOf` over the three ops; `the_step_schema_is_pinned` snapshots whichever is used.
- `Step::touched(&self) -> Vec<&Path>`: its path, and a rename's destination (for E13's resource sets in E5).

### 5. Guards, fixes and their companions

- **`Guard`**, `#[serde(tag = "kind", rename_all = "snake_case")]`: `Generation { target: TargetKey, generation: u64 }`; `Marker { target: TargetKey, sha256: Sha256 }` (the digest of `<meta>/target.json`); `Epoch { path: PathBuf, stamp: Stamp }` (the live stamp of a folder the suspended journal would touch on recovery); `WtfEpoch { target: TargetKey, stamp: Stamp }` (one stamp digest over a client's whole `WTF/`, never a path below it). F2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.2`) fills them; E7 checks them and refuses with `undo_conflict` (`changed_since_suspension`).
- **`FixKind`** (`Copy`, snake_case): `Write, Chmod, Quarantine, Flatten, Suspend, Delegate` (`prepared.fixes[].kind`, capabilities' `ops`).
- **`FixEntry { fix: u32, fm: Cow<'static, str>, kind: FixKind }`** (`prepared.fixes[]`).
- **`Fix`** (Rust only, no serde: what a fixer returns): `Write { path, content: Vec<u8>, mode: Mode }`, `Chmod { path, mode: Mode }`, `Quarantine { path, root: QuarantineRoot }`, `Flatten { inner, outer }` (`inner` = `AddOns/X/Y`, `outer` = `AddOns/X`: `AddOns/X/Y` → `AddOns/Y`, then `AddOns/X` → quarantine; when the inner name equals the wrapper's, E5 lowers three renames through `AddOns/.omaddons-flatten-<tx>`), `Suspend { journal: JournalSet }`, `Delegate { what: Delegation }`. `pub fn kind(&self) -> FixKind`.
- **`QuarantineRoot`** (Rust only): `State`, `Config`, `Cache`, `Client { client_dir: PathBuf }`, each doc comment giving its layout from M4-D35 (for `Client`, the path is relative to the client dir). E5 resolves them to absolute destinations.
- **`JournalSet`** (Rust only, M4-D38): `{tx: TxId, family: JournalFamily, target: Option<TargetKey>, artifacts: Vec<SuspendedArtifact>, guards: Vec<Guard>, attribution: Attribution, unattributed: Vec<PathBuf>}`; `SuspendedArtifact { path: PathBuf, root: QuarantineRoot }`; `Attribution::{Complete, Partial}` (`Serialize`, `complete`, `partial`: A.4's evidence uses it).
- **`Delegation`** (wire: A.5's `delegated_planned`): `{tx: TxId, family: JournalFamily, phase: JournalPhase, direction: Direction}` with `JournalFamily::{Folder, Repair}` (`folder`, `repair`), `JournalPhase::{Prepared, Step, Swapped, Preserve, Preserved, Done}` (the phases a pending journal can be in, across both families), `Direction::{RollBack, RollForward}` (`roll_back`, `roll_forward`). E11 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.11`, `journal::diagnose`) may reuse these three enums; whichever of this leaf and E11 lands second reuses the first's.

### 6. Validation (pure)

`pub fn validate(&self) -> Result<(), StepError>` on `Step`, and `pub fn validate_steps(fixes: &[FixEntry], steps: &[Step]) -> Result<(), StepError>`. `StepError` is an enum whose every variant carries the `seq`; `Display` names the rule. The rules:
1. every path the step acts on or reserves (`path`, `to`, `backup`, and an `Epoch` guard's `path`) is absolute, valid UTF-8 and has no `..` component; a `link_target` is recorded as the link holds it and may be relative;
2. `write_file`: `Endpoints::One`; `post` is `File` with `sha256` and with `mode` equal to the primitive's; `pre` is `Absent` (then `backup` is `None`) or `File` with `sha256` (then `backup` is `Some`);
3. `chmod`: `Endpoints::One`; `pre` and `post` are `File` with equal, present `identity`; `post.mode` equals the primitive's; `pre.mode` is present and differs from it;
4. `rename_noreplace`: `Endpoints::Pair`; `pre.path` is present (not `Absent`) with an `identity`; `pre.to` is `Absent`; `post.path` is `Absent`; `post.to` has `pre.path`'s kind and identity; a renamed `Dir` has a `stamp` in `pre.path`; a renamed `Symlink` has a `link_target` in `pre.path`;
5. `guards` appear only on `rename_noreplace`;
6. (`validate_steps`) `seq` runs 1, 2, 3 … without a gap; each `fix` is between 1 and `fixes.len()`; each step's `fm` equals `fixes[fix - 1].fm`; each step passes `validate`.

A non-UTF-8 path also makes serialization fail (serde's `PathBuf` refuses it): it is never written lossily, unlike `actions.jsonl`'s audit paths.

### 7. Wire form, as the snapshot pins it

```json
[{"seq":1,"fix":1,"fm":"fm-plugins-skill-version-drift","op":"write_file","path":"/fixture/skills/omaddons/SKILL.md","mode":"0644",
  "backup":"/fixture/state/omaddons/doctor/runs/R/backups/1",
  "pre":{"kind":"file","sha256":"sha256:<64 hex>"},"post":{"kind":"file","sha256":"sha256:<64 hex>","mode":"0644"}},
 {"seq":2,"fix":2,"fm":"fm-secrets-credential-file-mode","op":"chmod","path":"/fixture/config/omaddons/credentials/github","mode":"0600",
  "pre":{"kind":"file","identity":{"ino":"4242","born_ns":"1767225600000000000"},"mode":"0644"},
  "post":{"kind":"file","identity":{"ino":"4242","born_ns":"1767225600000000000"},"mode":"0600"}},
 {"seq":3,"fix":3,"fm":"fm-external_artifacts-nested-addon-folder","op":"rename_noreplace",
  "path":"/fixture/client/Interface/AddOns/X/Y","to":"/fixture/client/Interface/AddOns/Y",
  "pre":{"path":{"kind":"dir","identity":{"ino":"77","born_ns":"1767225600000000000"},"stamp":"stamp:sha256:<64 hex>"},"to":{"kind":"absent"}},
  "post":{"path":{"kind":"absent"},"to":{"kind":"dir","identity":{"ino":"77","born_ns":"1767225600000000000"}}}}]
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `src/engine/repair_action.rs` defines `Mode`, `Identity`, `Sha256`, `Stamp`, `Endpoint`, `Endpoints`, `Primitive`, `Step`, `Guard`, `FixKind`, `FixEntry`, `Fix`, `QuarantineRoot`, `JournalSet`, `SuspendedArtifact`, `Attribution`, `Delegation`, `JournalFamily`, `JournalPhase`, `Direction`, `StepError`, `Step::validate`, `validate_steps`, `Step::write_digest` and `Step::touched`, with no I/O.
- [ ] The wire-form snapshot of the eight steps (`repair_primitives_wire_form`) and of `fixes[]` (`repair_fixes_wire_form`) is reviewed and committed: op names `write_file`/`chmod`/`rename_noreplace`, `"path"`/`"to"` for renames, `pre`/`post` pairs for renames, decimal-string identities with `born_ns` omitted when unknown, `backup` omitted on a creating write, `activation` only when true, `guards` only when non-empty.
- [ ] Every snapshot case deserializes back equal; a newer minor's extra key is ignored on read; an unknown `op` or predicate `kind` fails to read.
- [ ] `validate`/`validate_steps` accept the eight valid cases and refuse each invalid case with its own `StepError`; a non-UTF-8 path fails serialization.
- [ ] `Step`'s JSON Schema (`repair_step_schema`) is snapshotted and lists, per op, the keys it requires.
- [ ] README's code map row for `src/engine/` names `repair_action.rs`.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests (`src/engine/repair_action.rs`, `#[cfg(test)] mod tests`)

All table-driven, each case named, each assertion message naming the case and showing input and output. Fixture paths are under `/fixture/…`; digests are built from fixed bytes (`[0x11; 32]`, `[0x22; 32]`, …).
- `primitives_serialize_to_the_journal_wire_form`: `insta::assert_json_snapshot!("repair_primitives_wire_form", steps)` over eight named cases, in order: `write_over_a_file` (pre `File{sha256}`, post `File{sha256, mode}`, `backup`), `write_creating_a_file` (pre `Absent`, no `backup`), `chmod_a_credential` (identity and modes 0644 → 0600), `rename_a_dir_into_quarantine` (dir with identity and stamp; destination absent), `rename_a_state_file_into_quarantine` (a regular file, identity only), `rename_a_temp_symlink` (symlink with identity and `link_target`), `activation_rename` (`activation: true`), `set_aside_rename_with_guards` (all four guard kinds; one identity without `born_ns`); and `insta::assert_json_snapshot!("repair_fixes_wire_form", fixes)` over one `FixEntry` per `FixKind`.
- `the_wire_form_reads_back_equal`: each of the eight serializes and deserializes to an equal `Step`.
- `ops_kinds_and_guards_use_the_published_names`: the `op` values are `write_file`, `chmod`, `rename_noreplace`; `Endpoint` kinds `absent`, `file`, `dir`, `symlink`; `FixKind` values `write`, `chmod`, `quarantine`, `flatten`, `suspend`, `delegate`; guard kinds `generation`, `marker`, `epoch`, `wtf_epoch`; `Attribution` `complete`, `partial`.
- `modes_are_four_octal_digits`: `0o600` → `"0600"`, `0o644` → `"0644"`, `0o4755` → `"4755"`, `0o7777` → `"7777"`; `Mode::new(0o10000)` is `None`; parse `"0600"` ok; `"600"`, `"0800"`, `"07777"`, `"06o0"`, `""` refused.
- `identities_are_decimal_strings`: `{ino: 12345, born_ns: Some(1_767_225_600_123_456_789)}` writes those exact digits and reads back exactly (no float rounding); `born_ns: Some(-5)` round-trips; `born_ns: None` omits the key and reads back `None`; `{"ino":"x"}` and `{"ino":12}` (a number) are refused.
- `digests_keep_their_prefixes`: `Sha256` writes `sha256:` plus 64 lowercase hex and `Stamp` `stamp:sha256:` plus 64; `Sha256::from_str` refuses a `stamp:sha256:` string, uppercase hex and 63 digits; `Stamp::from_str` refuses `sha256:…`.
- `an_fsx_stamp_reads_as_a_stamp`: `fsx::StampDigest::from_entries([("a", "file", 1, 0o644, 1)])`'s `to_string()` parses with `Stamp::from_str` and displays back identical.
- `steps_validate_by_case`: the eight valid cases pass; each invalid case returns its own error: `relative_path`, `parent_component`, `write_with_pair_endpoints`, `rename_with_one_endpoint`, `write_post_without_sha256`, `write_post_mode_differs`, `overwrite_without_backup`, `create_with_backup`, `chmod_identity_changed`, `chmod_to_the_same_mode`, `chmod_pre_without_mode`, `rename_destination_not_absent_before`, `rename_source_not_absent_after`, `rename_identity_changed`, `rename_kind_changed`, `dir_rename_without_stamp`, `symlink_rename_without_link_target`, `guards_on_a_chmod`.
- `step_lists_validate_by_case`: valid three-step list ok; `seq_starts_at_two`, `seq_gap`, `fix_zero`, `fix_past_the_end`, `fm_differs_from_its_fix` refused.
- `a_non_utf8_path_never_serializes`: a step whose `path` is `OsStr::from_bytes(b"/fixture/\xff")` fails `validate` and makes `serde_json::to_string` return an error.
- `newer_minor_keys_are_ignored_and_unknown_ops_refused`: a step with an extra `"note":"x"` key reads; `"op":"symlink_atomic"` and `"kind":"socket"` fail.
- `fix_kinds_match_fixes`: each `Fix` variant's `kind()`.
- `delegations_serialize_as_previewed`: `{tx, family: "folder", phase: "step", direction: "roll_back"}` and a `repair`/`done`/`roll_forward` one, read back equal.
- `write_digest_reads_the_post`: a write's `write_digest()` is its post's `sha256`; a chmod's is `None`.
- `the_step_schema_is_pinned`: `insta::assert_json_snapshot!("repair_step_schema", schema)` with `SchemaSettings::for_serialize()`; assert that each op's variant requires its keys (`write_file`: `path`, `mode`; `chmod`: `path`, `mode`; `rename_noreplace`: `path`, `to`) and that `backup`, `activation` and `guards` are optional.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

None: nothing writes a repair journal before E5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`). E5's crash matrix and E12's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.12`) history tests exercise the wire form end to end.

### Logging

Case names in every table and in every assertion message (`"{case}: {step:?} -> {err}"`); snapshots named `repair_primitives_wire_form`, `repair_fixes_wire_form` and `repair_step_schema`.

## Considerations

- **These shapes are first written by E5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`) and E12 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.12`), and first shown by E6** (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`, `doctor fix --dry-run`'s `actions_planned`). After H2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.2`, the golden) they are frozen. E12 defines the history line's `repairs[]` type independently (no edge between the leaves); E5 joins the two and asserts their JSON is equal. Where this part decides (identity strings, `born_ns` omitted when unknown, `backup` omitted on a creating write, `activation` only when true), E12's draft agrees except that it types `born_ns` as a required string: E5 must make that optional when it joins them, because a filesystem without birth times yields an identity without one.
- **Why the device is not in `Identity`:** btrfs subvolumes, FUSE and device-mapper volumes get a new device number on every mount, so a reboot would make every step look like neither state.
- **No run-specific value belongs in a canonical form** (M4-D44): E6's token takes `{fm, fix, op, path, to_rel, mode?}` from these fields and leaves out `backup` and absolute quarantine paths; keep the fields separable for that.
- **Hot spot:** `src/engine/` gains a new file only; `src/engine/mod.rs` gains one line.

## Dependencies

- **Parent:** E1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`).
- **Before it:** nothing; it starts at once, beside parts 1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1.1`) and 2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1.2`).
- **After it:** part 4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1.4`): the registry's `FixerSpec` returns `Vec<Fix>` and declares `FixKind`s.

title: `FAILURE_MODES`, and `status`'s seven failure modes moved onto it
description:
Part 4 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1 (The failure-mode registry, the finding model and the repair action model). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

E1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`) creates the doctor's data model and moves `status`'s seven published failure modes onto it without changing a byte of `status`'s output. Parts 2 and 3 defined the finding model (`src/doctor/finding.rs`) and the repair action model (`src/engine/repair_action.rs`); part 1 pinned `status`'s issues in snapshots before anything moved.

This part is the registry and the move: the `FailureMode` row type of M4-D29, `FAILURE_MODES` with the seven moved rows, the minimal view, selection and budget the row's detector signature names, the runner `doctor::detect`, the invariant test, and `status` wired to the registry. It is one step because the row type, its first rows and its first caller are one change: a registry with no rows or no caller proves nothing, and the move's proof (part 1's snapshots unchanged) needs all of it in one commit.

The decisions it implements:
- **M4-D29: one detector registry serves `doctor`, `doctor health` and `status`, by tier.** Each failure mode is declared once with an id, a subsystem, a severity, a title, a description and a "why it matters"; a tier (`cached`, `quick`, `default`, `deep`); `online_required` and `estimated_cost_ms`; `requires` (the layers it needs); a pure detector; an optional fixer; a manual remediation builder. `status --cached` runs `cached`; `status`, `doctor --quick` and `doctor health` run `cached` and `quick`; `doctor` runs all but `deep`; `doctor --include-deep` runs all. `app::issues` keeps its wire shape; its 7 ids move in unchanged, and `status`'s issues become the registry's findings mapped to `Issue`. Why: two implementations of "is this broken?" would drift, and tiers are how `status --cached` keeps its 5 ms budget (a `cached` detector reads only what `status --cached` reads today, plus single-file stats). Rejected: `status` calling `doctor` as a subprocess; separate code synced by test.
- **M4-D30** (instance keys `<fm-id>@<target key | machine>[:<discriminator>]`, labels separate), **M4-D41** (`confidence`), **M4-D42** (evidence never holds content) are implemented by part 2's types, which this part uses.
- **M4-D39** (a fixer that changes user content ships `enabled: false`), **M4-D38** (set-asides are `needs_force`, never default), **M4-D40** (`doctor_refused`'s closed reasons) shape the fixer spec and its invariants.
- **M4-D2:** the failure-mode registry is one of the registries `src/contract/` assembles; `capabilities` (A4, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`) and `doctor capabilities` (E4, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4`) read it.
- **M4-D48:** F1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1`, the journal detectors) later narrows `journal-pending` to recoverable journals; this part keeps today's meaning exactly.

Facts (verified at `c0ab5e9`): the seven ids are at `src/app/issues.rs:18-33`; `issues_for` at `:122-208` (sorted by `(severity, id, addon)` at `:206`) and `machine_issues` at `:92-120`; `status` builds attention at `src/app/status.rs:704-733` (selected targets) and `:839-883` (registered targets whose directory is gone), computes each target's journal reason and calls `issues_for` at `:884-892`, reads the widget at `:894-905`, calls `machine_issues` at `:906-909`; a pending journal counts only when the lock is free (`:705`, `:842`, `:908`); `--cached` keeps only `missing` drift (`:720-727`). `journal::Pending {tx, target, unrecoverable}` (`src/engine/journal.rs:681-687`); `Unrecoverable` has two values, `journal_too_new` and `journal_unreadable` (`:489-503`). Hints: `reinstall_hint` (`src/app/drift.rs:88-94`), `forget_target_hint` and `inspect_hint` (`src/app/status.rs:1202-1209`, `pub(super)`), `omarchy::status::reinstall_hint` (`src/omarchy/status.rs:134-140`); `WidgetInfo::needs_reinstall` (`:56-58`). `TargetRecord::CURRENT` is 1.0 (`src/state/records.rs:24-27`); `store::Loaded.version` holds the version read (`src/state/store.rs:199-204`); `Paths::target_record` (`src/state/paths.rs:280-282`); `ClientPaths::addons()` (`paths.rs:504`). `fsx::scope::Scope::admits` (`src/fsx/scope.rs:105-125`). `QUICK_DETECTOR_BUDGET` (5 ms, `src/limits.rs:61-62`). `crate::source_scan::{sources, production_code, Literals}` (`src/source_scan.rs:26-80`). `proptest` is a dev-dependency.

## Technical Approach

### 1. `src/doctor/registry.rs`

```rust
pub type DetectFn = fn(&DoctorView, &Selection, &mut Budget) -> Detected;

pub struct FailureMode {
    pub id: &'static str,
    pub subsystem: Subsystem,
    pub severity: Severity,
    pub title: &'static str,
    pub description: &'static str,
    pub why: &'static str,
    pub tier: Tier,
    pub online: bool,
    pub cost_ms: u32,
    pub requires: &'static [Layer],
    pub detect: Option<DetectFn>,
    pub fix: Option<FixerSpec>,
    pub manual: Option<fn(&Finding) -> Remediation>,
}
pub struct FixerSpec {
    pub plan: fn(&DoctorView, &Finding) -> Result<Vec<Fix>, Refusal>,
    pub writes_to: &'static [ScopeName],
    pub ops: &'static [FixKind],
    pub enabled: bool,
    pub needs_force: bool,
    pub cardinality: Cardinality,
    pub preconditions: &'static [FixerPrecondition],
}
pub static FAILURE_MODES: &[FailureMode] = &[ /* the seven rows, sorted by id */ ];
```

- `Tier` (`Copy`, `Ord`, in this order): `Cached, Quick, Default, Deep`, serialized `cached`, `quick`, `default`, `deep`.
- `Layer`: `Config, Registry, Discovery, Records, Inventory` (snake_case). E2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.2`, the tolerant view) decides when each is unavailable.
- `ScopeName`: `State, Config, Cache, ClientMeta, AddOns, Skill`, serialized `state`, `config`, `cache`, `client_meta`, `addons` (explicit rename), `skill`; `pub const fn scope(self) -> crate::fsx::scope::Scope` maps each to its fsx row (`Scope::State`, `Config`, `Cache`, `ClientMeta`, `AddOns`, `Skill`).
- `Cardinality`: `Low` (at most 10 paths), `High`; `FixerPrecondition`: `LockHeld, InflightFree, ClientNotRunning, Online, SameFs` (§6.10's `Precondition`, renamed because `app::precondition::Precondition` exists); `RefusalReason`: `ForceRequired, FixerConflict, TooManyActions, OverBudget, FilesystemMismatch, ClientRunning, NotEnabled, EditedLocally` with `ALL` and `as_str` (M4-D40's closed set, which E3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, uses for `doctor_refused`'s `details.reason` spec); `Refusal { reason: RefusalReason, message: String }`. All `Serialize` (snake_case) and `JsonSchema`.
- `detect` is an `Option`. Decided while writing this bead: two Appendix B modes (`fm-state_files-detector-crashed`, row 18; `fm-state_files-check-incomplete`, row 46) are raised by E3's runtime, need rows for `explain` and `capabilities`, and have no detector.
- `pub mod ids`: the seven constants moved from `src/app/issues.rs:18-33` with the same names, values and doc comments (the widget one's doc comment says "(E4 raises it)" and may stay: it names an M3 leaf, not M4's E4). `src/app/issues.rs` gets `pub use crate::doctor::registry::ids;`.
- `impl FailureMode`:
  - `pub fn finding(&'static self, obs: Observation) -> Finding` = `Finding::build(self.id, self.subsystem, self.severity, obs, |f| self.remediation(f))`;
  - `pub fn remediation(&self, f: &Finding) -> Remediation`: `command`/`argv`/`destructive` from `(self.manual)(f)` when set; otherwise from the fixer: argv `["omaddons","doctor","fix","--only",<id>]`, plus `["-t", <target id>]` when `f.target` is set, plus `["--force","--yes"]` when `needs_force`, with `command = shell_words::join(&argv)` (through `CommandHint::new`), `destructive: false`; `explain_argv` = `["omaddons","doctor","explain",<id>]` plus `["-t", <target id>]` when set, `explain_command` its join; `auto_fixable` = a fixer that is `enabled && !needs_force`; `needs_force` from the fixer; `estimated_actions: 0`. Decided while writing this bead: this is the per-row default; E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`, `doctor fix`) and F8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.8`) refine it per instance (M4-D53). No row has a fixer before E6, and no `Finding` is emitted on any channel before E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`), so no argv naming a command that does not exist yet becomes visible.
- `pub fn row(id: &str) -> Option<&'static FailureMode>` (lookup by id).
- **`pub fn invariant_violations(rows: &[FailureMode]) -> Vec<RowViolation>`** (pure and public, for A4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`), E4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4`) and F9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`) too), `RowViolation { id: String, rule: Rule }`, one per broken rule:
  1. `DuplicateId`; `NotSorted` (rows sorted by id: decided while writing this bead, checkable without an external numbering, and each catalog leaf inserts its rows where they sort);
  2. `BadId` (`!finding::is_fm_id(id)`), `SubsystemMismatch` (`subsystem_part(id) != subsystem.as_str()`), `InapplicableSubsystem` (`sockets`, `hooks`);
  3. `EmptyText` (`title`, `description` or `why` empty, untrimmed or containing a newline);
  4. `NoRemediation` (`fix.is_none() && manual.is_none()`);
  5. `ForcedFixerEnabled` (`needs_force && enabled`);
  6. `OnlineInFastTier` (`online && tier <= Quick`), so `status` and `doctor health` never run an online row;
  7. `TooCostlyForTier` (`tier <= Quick && cost_ms > QUICK_DETECTOR_BUDGET.as_millis()`), §6.13's tier contracts;
  8. `FixerWithoutDetector` (`detect.is_none() && fix.is_some()`);
  9. `FixerWithoutOps`, `FixerWithoutScope` (no `writes_to` unless `ops == [Delegate]`), `ScopeRefusesDoctor` (a `writes_to` whose `scope()` does not admit `Writer::Doctor`);
  10. (over `FAILURE_MODES` only) `IdWithoutRow`: every constant in `ids` has a row.

### 2. The minimal view, facts, selection and budget

Decided while writing this bead: this leaf defines `DoctorView`, `Selection` and `Budget` in their smallest true form, so that every row has §6.10's final detector signature from the first commit; later leaves extend these types and never change the signature every catalog leaf codes against.

- **`src/doctor/facts.rs`** (the bridge from what `status` already computes):
  ```rust
  pub struct StatusFacts { pub targets: Vec<TargetFacts>, pub machine: MachineFacts }
  pub struct TargetFacts {
      pub id: String, pub key: TargetKey,
      pub journals: Vec<PendingJournal>,      // pending journals naming it, lock free; else empty
      pub newer_record: Option<NewerFile>,    // attention: state_version_newer
      pub vanished: Option<PathBuf>,          // registered, its client dir gone: that dir
      pub degraded: usize,                    // attention: addon_degraded, else 0
      pub drift: Vec<AddonDriftFact>,         // missing or modified addons, as status filtered them
  }
  pub struct PendingJournal { pub tx: TxId, pub unrecoverable: Option<journal::Unrecoverable> }
  pub struct NewerFile { pub path: PathBuf, pub on_disk: SchemaVersion, pub writes: SchemaVersion }
  pub struct AddonDriftFact { pub addon: String, pub state: DriftState, pub files: u64, pub missing_folders: Vec<PathBuf> }
  pub struct MachineFacts { pub unattributed: Vec<PendingJournal>, pub widget: Option<WidgetDrift> }
  pub struct WidgetDrift { pub version: Option<String> }
  ```
  All `Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Default` where applicable; no serde (internal).
- **`src/doctor/view.rs`**: `pub struct DoctorView { status_facts: StatusFacts }`, `pub fn from_status_facts(facts: StatusFacts) -> Self`, `pub fn status_facts(&self) -> &StatusFacts`. The module doc says: E2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.2`) adds the tolerant layers and `DoctorView::load`, and its `load` must also fill `status_facts` (from its layers, as `status` computes them) so that `doctor` reports these seven; each F leaf that moves one of the seven onto the layers drops that row's use of the facts; F8 removes the layer.
- **`src/doctor/selection.rs`**: `pub struct Selection { only: Option<BTreeSet<&'static str>> }`, `all()`, `only(ids: &[&'static str])`, `includes(&self, row: &FailureMode) -> bool`. The doc says E2 adds `-t`, `--skip`, subsystem names and `--only` validation (closest id on a miss).
- **`src/doctor/budget.rs`**: `pub struct Budget { _private: () }` with `pub fn unlimited() -> Self`. The doc says the seven moved detectors read computed facts and walk nothing, so they never charge it; E3 adds the deadline, the entry counter and the bounded walker (M4-D43).

### 3. The runner (`src/doctor/mod.rs`)

```rust
pub struct Detection { pub findings: Vec<Finding>, pub incomplete: Vec<(&'static str, Incomplete)> }

/// Runs every selected row up to `max_tier`, in registry order, and turns what each detector
/// found into findings. Pure: reads only the view. (No budgets, no catch_unwind: E3's.)
pub fn detect(view: &DoctorView, selection: &Selection, max_tier: Tier) -> Detection
```

For each `row` of `FAILURE_MODES`: skip unless `selection.includes(row) && row.tier <= max_tier`, and skip a row whose `detect` is `None`; call `detect(view, selection, &mut Budget::unlimited())`; push `row.finding(obs)` for each observation, and `(row.id, inc)` when `incomplete` is set. §6.13 names this call for `status` (`doctor::detect(view, Tier::Cached)`, or `Cached | Quick` without `--cached`); tiers are ordered, so a maximum tier expresses both.

### 4. The seven rows and their detectors

Each detector lives in its subsystem's file, so the catalog leaf that later owns the row (F1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1`; F3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.3`; F4, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.4`; F5, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.5`; F7, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.7`) rewrites it in place: `src/doctor/detectors/{concurrency,schemas,state_files,external,userland,plugins}.rs`, with `detectors/mod.rs` declaring them. Every detector reads only `view.status_facts()`, sets `confidence: Confidence::High` and `folder: None`.

| Id (subsystem file) | Sev | Tier | `requires` | `cost_ms` | Observation per | Subject | Finding title | Evidence | `manual` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fm-concurrency_primitives-journal-pending` (`concurrency.rs`) | P0 | cached | `[]` | 1 | pending journal of a target; unattributed journal | `target(id, key).tx(tx)`; `machine().tx(tx)` | target: "An interrupted change needs manual repair" when `unrecoverable` is set, else "An interrupted change waits to be finished"; machine: always "…needs manual repair" | `tx`, `reason: Some(u.reason())` when unrecoverable | prose (argv `None`): for a target finding whose evidence has no `reason`, "quit the game if it is running, then run any change command; it finishes or rolls back the change first"; otherwise "see \"journal_pending that does not clear\" under Troubleshooting in the README" |
| `fm-schemas-state-version-newer` (`schemas.rs`) | P0 | cached | `[Records]` | 1 | `newer_record` | `.path(record file)` | "State was written by a newer omaddons" | `path`, `observed: on_disk`, `expected: writes` | prose "upgrade omaddons" |
| `fm-state_files-record-folder-missing` (`state_files.rs`) | P1 | cached | `[Records, Discovery]` | 1 | drift entry `Missing` | `.addon(name)` | "`<name>`'s folder is gone" | `paths: missing_folders` (omitted when empty) | `reinstall_hint(addon, id)` |
| `fm-external_artifacts-managed-files-modified` (`external.rs`) | P2 | quick | `[Records, Discovery]` | 5 | drift entry `Modified` | `.addon(name)` | "`<name>`'s files changed on disk (`<n>` file)" or "(`<n>` files)" | `count: files` | `reinstall_hint(addon, id)` |
| `fm-external_artifacts-ownership-transferred` (`external.rs`) | P2 | cached | `[Records]` | 1 | `degraded > 0` | `target(id, key)` | "`<n>` addon lost a folder to another addon" or "`<n>` addons …" | `count: degraded` | `inspect_hint(id)` |
| `fm-userland_state-target-vanished` (`userland.rs`) | P2 | cached | `[Registry, Discovery]` | 1 | `vanished` | `target(id, key)` | "The client's directory is gone" | `path: the client dir` | `forget_target_hint(id)` (destructive) |
| `fm-plugins-widget-version-drift` (`plugins.rs`) | P3 | cached | `[]` | 1 | `machine.widget` | `machine()` | "The bar widget is from another omaddons build" | `observed: version` when known | `omarchy::status::reinstall_hint()` |

Every row: `online: false`, `fix: None`, `addon: Some(name)` on the two per-addon rows. The manual builders take the target id from `f.target` (always set on target rows) and the addon from `f.addon`; build hints with the existing functions (`forget_target_hint` and `inspect_hint` become `pub(crate)`; decided while writing this bead: reusing `status`'s own builders keeps a finding's remediation equal to `status`'s `commands`, and moving them would touch `status`'s recommendation code, F8's hot spot). The `Remediation` they return: `command` = the hint's `command()` (or the prose), `argv` = `Some(hint.argv())` (or `None`), `destructive` = the hint's.

The static texts (first shown by `doctor explain`, E3, and `doctor capabilities`, E4); none names a runnable command:

| Row | `title` | `description` | `why` |
|---|---|---|---|
| journal-pending | an interrupted change waits to be finished | A change's journal is still in the state directory and no omaddons process holds the lock, so the change was interrupted between its first step and its commit. | Every change on that client recovers it first; one that recovery cannot read blocks the client's changes until it is repaired. |
| state-version-newer | state was written by a newer omaddons | A client's record carries a newer schema version than this build writes. | This build reads it but never writes it, so every change on that client is refused until omaddons is upgraded. |
| record-folder-missing | a managed addon's folder is gone | A folder the client's record says omaddons installed is missing from Interface/AddOns, or a symlink stands in its place. | The addon no longer loads as recorded, and an update or a removal would act on a folder that is not there. |
| managed-files-modified | a managed addon's files changed on disk | Files of a folder omaddons installed differ from what its commit recorded: modified, deleted or added since. | A reinstall or an update replaces them, so a hand edit would be lost, and an unintended change can break the addon. |
| ownership-transferred | addons lost a folder to another addon | An install with --force gave a folder one addon owned to another, so the first addon is recorded as degraded. | A degraded addon may not load, and updating it can take the folder back. |
| target-vanished | a registered client's directory is gone | A client in the target registry no longer has its directory on disk. | Nothing can be installed there; its record and history are kept until the client is forgotten. |
| widget-version-drift | the bar widget is from another omaddons build | The installed bar widget's code is not what this binary renders for the directories it was installed under. | An outdated widget stays read-only and may misread this build's output. |

### 5. `status` on the registry (`src/app/status.rs`)

Keep the edit to building facts and assigning issues; everything else (`attention`, `needs_attention`, `first_fix`, `summary`, recommendations, `--check`, rendering) is untouched.
1. In the selected-targets loop (`:675-838`), for a target with a key, build its `TargetFacts` beside the `StatusTarget`, **mirroring `attention` exactly**: `journals` = `pending` entries with `p.target == Some(key)` when `!held` (so it is non-empty exactly when `attention` has `journal_pending`); `newer_record` when the record's status is `Newer` (`path: world.paths.target_record(&key)`, `on_disk: loaded.version`, `writes: <TargetRecord as Versioned>::CURRENT`); `degraded` = `addons.degraded` when it is above 0 (the `addon_degraded` condition); `drift` = the `drifted` addons (already filtered for `--cached`) whose state is `Missing` or `Modified`, with `files` from `DriftItem::of`'s count and `missing_folders` = `ClientPaths::new(&t.client_dir).addons().join(folder)` for each `FolderDrift` with `present == false`.
2. In the missing-targets loop (`:839-883`): `TargetFacts { journals: as above, vanished: Some(e.client_dir.clone()), degraded: 0, newer_record: None, drift: [] }` (a vanished target never raised `addon_degraded` or `state_version_newer`, even when its record holds degraded addons).
3. Move the widget read (`:894-905`) above the issue assignment, then build `MachineFacts { unattributed: pending entries with no target when !held, widget: the widget when needs_reinstall, as WidgetDrift { version } }`.
4. Replace `:884-892` and `:909` with:
   ```rust
   let max = if args.cached { Tier::Cached } else { Tier::Quick };
   let found = doctor::detect(&DoctorView::from_status_facts(facts), &Selection::only(issues::STATUS_FAILURE_MODES), max);
   for t in &mut targets { t.issues = t.key.map(|k| issues::for_target(&found.findings, k)).unwrap_or_default(); }
   let issues = issues::for_machine(&found.findings);
   ```
   `found.incomplete` is always empty for these rows (they walk nothing); a `debug_assert!` says so.

### 6. `app::issues`

- `pub const STATUS_FAILURE_MODES: &[&str]` = the seven `ids`. Decided while writing this bead: `status` runs exactly these rows until F8 moves it onto every `cached` and `quick` row, because E2, E3 and the F leaves add rows before F8 and `status`'s output must not change in between; F1 extends the list when it retitles the journal states.
- `fn issue_of(f: &Finding) -> Issue { id: f.id, severity: f.severity, title: f.title.clone(), addon: f.addon.clone(), remediation: Remediation { command: Some(f.remediation.command.clone()), argv: f.remediation.argv.clone(), destructive: f.remediation.destructive } }`.
- `pub fn for_target(findings: &[Finding], key: TargetKey) -> Vec<Issue>`: the findings whose `target.key == key`, mapped, with **one rule**: the `journal-pending` findings of that target become one issue, the first whose evidence has a `reason` when any does, else the first; then sorted by `(severity, id, addon)` as at `:206`. `pub fn for_machine(findings) -> Vec<Issue>`: the findings without a target, with the journal ones collapsed to the first, mapped and sorted the same way. Decided while writing this bead: findings are one per journal (M4-D30; E3's `--since` acceptance needs two stuck journals on one client to be two instances), while `status` shows one row per target, so the collapse is a `status` presentation rule; F1 revisits it.
- Delete `issues_for`, `machine_issues` and `MANUAL_REPAIR` from production; keep a verbatim copy under `#[cfg(test)] mod legacy` as the oracle of the property test. Port the four existing tests (`every_attention_maps_to_its_failure_mode`, `a_journal_that_needs_manual_repair_says_so`, `one_file_and_one_addon_read_singular`, `severities_serialize_as_p0_to_p3_and_count`) to build facts and call `for_target`, with the same assertions (the `a_journal_that_needs_manual_repair_says_so` cases become `TooNew`, `Unreadable` and recoverable, since the other two reason strings are never produced). Rewire part 1's adapters `issues_of_case` and `machine_issues_of_case` to facts → `doctor::detect` → `for_target`/`for_machine`, leaving their snapshot files untouched.
- `SeverityCounts`, `Issue` and `Remediation` keep their shapes.

### 7. README

The code map (`README.md:2363-2394`) gains, after the `src/app/` row: "| `src/doctor/` | The doctor: the failure-mode registry `status`'s issues come from (`registry.rs`) and the finding model with stable instance keys (`finding.rs`); the view, runtime, detectors and fixers follow |". No other README change: `status`'s output and its issue table (`:752-760`) are unchanged.
