title: E2E: `status` reports the seven failure modes from the registry, unchanged
description:
Part 5 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1 (The failure-mode registry, the finding model and the repair action model). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

E1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`) moved the seven failure-mode ids `status` publishes onto the doctor's registry (`FAILURE_MODES` in `src/doctor/registry.rs`), with the promise that `status`'s output stays byte-identical: README calls the ids "stable across releases" (`README.md:750`), and the bar widget and agents read `status`'s `issues[]` constantly. Parts 1 and 4 proved it at unit level (snapshots taken before the move, and a property test against the old code). This part proves it through the real binary, on synthetic homes with each state actually planted, in JSON and human output, with and without `--cached`, and it becomes the regression net that protects the seven published ids for the rest of M4, while the catalog leaves F1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1`), F3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.3`), F4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.4`), F5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.5`) and F7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.7`) rewrite their detectors and F8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.8`) moves `status` onto the whole registry.

It is an end-to-end suite, and every scenario runs several commands, so it uses T1's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`) structured test log: a failure at any step can be diagnosed from the log alone.

What `status` must keep showing, per failure mode (today's code, `src/app/issues.rs:92-208`; README's table at `README.md:752-760`):

| Id | Severity | `title` | `remediation` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fm-concurrency_primitives-journal-pending` | P0 | "An interrupted change waits to be finished"; "An interrupted change needs manual repair" when its journal is too new or unreadable, and always for a journal with no readable target (in the machine's `data.issues`) | prose, `argv: null`: "quit the game if it is running, then run any change command; it finishes or rolls back the change first", or "see \"journal_pending that does not clear\" under Troubleshooting in the README" |
| `fm-schemas-state-version-newer` | P0 | "State was written by a newer omaddons" | prose "upgrade omaddons" |
| `fm-state_files-record-folder-missing` | P1 | "`<addon>`'s folder is gone" | `omaddons install <addon> -t <id> --reinstall` |
| `fm-external_artifacts-managed-files-modified` | P2 | "`<addon>`'s files changed on disk (`<n>` file[s])"; plain `status` only, never `--cached` | `omaddons install <addon> -t <id> --reinstall` |
| `fm-external_artifacts-ownership-transferred` | P2 | "`<n>` addon[s] lost a folder to another addon" | `omaddons list -t <id> -v` |
| `fm-userland_state-target-vanished` | P2 | "The client's directory is gone" | `omaddons targets rm <id>`, `destructive: true` |
| `fm-plugins-widget-version-drift` | P3 | "The bar widget is from another omaddons build" (machine) | `omaddons omarchy install` |

One `journal-pending` issue per client however many journals name it; none while another process holds the lock. Issues are ranked by severity, then id, then addon. Human output prints each under its client's row as `  <severity> <title> → <command>`.

## Technical Approach

### 1. The suite

`tests/e2e_status_issues.rs`, named `e2e_*` so T1's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`) `argc e2e` runner picks it up (decided while writing this bead). `mod common;`, and `use common::tlog::*` (T1's `TestLog`, `tlog!()`, `Ran`). Builders, all existing in `tests/common/` or in the library:
- the home: `common::home::Home::new(&["wow"])` (a Battle.net retail client, `_retail_`, target id `retail`); for the vanished scenario also a 3.3.5a custom client, `common::trees::CustomRoot::at(home.env.home().join("Games/wow-335")).version(3, 3, 5, 12_340).blizzard_folders(23).build()` (as `tests/status.rs:36-44`);
- addons: a one-folder zip per addon written with `common::archives::zip_text(&[("Foo/Foo.toc", &common::addons::toc("120105", &[]))])` and installed with `install gh:o/foo --file <zip> -t retail` (as `tests/status.rs:54-64`); the recorded addon name is read back from `common::state::record(&home, "retail")`, never assumed;
- journals: a `Prepared` line built as `tests/status.rs:304-349` does (`omaddons::engine::journal::{Prepared, JournalLine, CommitPayload, IndexChanges, CURRENT}`), written to `paths.journal(&tx)` with `std::fs::write` in the test (test code may write directly); a **too-new** journal is that line with `schema_version` `"2.0"`; an **unreadable** journal on a known target is a valid `prepared` line followed by `{"type":"bogus"}\n` (a complete line that does not decode); an **unattributed** journal is a file holding only `{"type":"bogus"}\n` (no `prepared`, so no target);
- a held lock: `omaddons::fsx::GlobalLock::acquire(&paths, "another process")`, held across the run;
- a newer record: read `<state>/omaddons/targets/<key>.json`, set `schema_version` to `"9.0"`, write it back;
- modified files: `common::drift::edit_managed(&toc_path, b"## Interface: 120105\n## Title: edited\n")`;
- a forced takeover: install `Foo`, then install `gh:o/bar` from a zip holding `Bar/` and `Foo/` with `--force` (as `tests/contract/recommendations.rs:92-112`);
- a vanished client: rename the 3.3.5a client's directory away inside the test root (as `recommendations.rs:81-90`);
- an outdated widget: a fake Omarchy (`OMARCHY_PATH=<root>/omarchy` with a `shell/` dir, an empty `<root>/no-tools` as `PATH`, and `<config>/omarchy` created), `omarchy install`, then the installed `Build.js`'s `var CONTENT_SHA256 = …` line replaced by 64 zeros, exactly as `tests/contract/recommendations.rs:364-420` builds it, with the same two variables on every run of that scenario.

### 2. The scenarios

Each is a `#[test]` with `let log = tlog!();`, phases as `log.step(…)`, every command through `log.run(&home.env, &argv)` (the scenario's extra variables passed on the run so the log records them). After the state is planted: `log.tree(…)` for `<state>/omaddons`, `<cache>/omaddons`, `<config>/omaddons` and each client dir; then each `status` run; then `log.assert_unchanged(…)` for each tree (`status` never writes). For each run, `log.json("expected issues", &expected)` before comparing, and the comparison is exact (`assert_eq!` on the `issues` arrays as JSON values).

1. **`journal_pending_is_one_issue_per_client_and_titled_by_its_journals`**: install `Foo`; plant a recoverable journal on retail. `status --json` (exit 0): retail's `issues` is exactly `[{"id":"fm-concurrency_primitives-journal-pending","severity":"P0","title":"An interrupted change waits to be finished","addon":null,"remediation":{"command":"quit the game if it is running, then run any change command; it finishes or rolls back the change first","argv":null,"destructive":false}}]`; `summary.issues.p0 == 1`; `summary.state == "attention"`. Plant a second, unreadable journal on retail. `status --json`: still one journal issue, now titled "An interrupted change needs manual repair" with the README prose; `data.journal.pending == 2`. `status --cached --json`: the same issue. Human `status`: stdout contains `  P0 An interrupted change needs manual repair → see "journal_pending that does not clear" under Troubleshooting in the README`. `status --check --json`: exit 6, `error.code == "check_failed"`. Then hold the lock: `status --json` shows no journal issue and `data.journal.in_progress == true`; release it.
2. **`an_unattributed_journal_is_the_machines_issue`**: plant the unattributed journal. `status --json`: `data.issues == [{"id":"fm-concurrency_primitives-journal-pending","severity":"P0","title":"An interrupted change needs manual repair","addon":null,"remediation":{"command":"see \"journal_pending that does not clear\" under Troubleshooting in the README","argv":null,"destructive":false}}]`; no client carries it; `needs_attention == true`. `status --check --json`: exit 6.
3. **`a_newer_record_is_state_version_newer`**: install `Foo`; set the record's `schema_version` to `"9.0"`. `status --json` and `status --cached --json`: retail's issues include `{"id":"fm-schemas-state-version-newer","severity":"P0","title":"State was written by a newer omaddons","addon":null,"remediation":{"command":"upgrade omaddons","argv":null,"destructive":false}}`. `status --check`: exit 6.
4. **`a_missing_folder_is_record_folder_missing_in_both_modes`**: install `Foo`; remove its folder. `status --json` and `status --cached --json`: `{"id":"fm-state_files-record-folder-missing","severity":"P1","title":"Foo's folder is gone","addon":"Foo","remediation":{"command":"omaddons install Foo -t retail --reinstall","argv":["omaddons","install","Foo","-t","retail","--reinstall"],"destructive":false}}` (the addon name as the record holds it). Human: `  P1 Foo's folder is gone → omaddons install Foo -t retail --reinstall`. `status --check`: exit 6.
5. **`modified_files_show_in_plain_status_only`**: install `Foo`; edit its TOC. `status --json`: `{"id":"fm-external_artifacts-managed-files-modified","severity":"P2","title":"Foo's files changed on disk (1 file)","addon":"Foo","remediation":{…reinstall…}}`. `status --cached --json`: no such issue (the `quick` tier, and the presence check). Human `status`: the line `  P2 Foo's files changed on disk (1 file) → omaddons install Foo -t retail --reinstall`.
6. **`a_forced_takeover_is_ownership_transferred`**: the forced takeover. `status --json` and `--cached`: `{"id":"fm-external_artifacts-ownership-transferred","severity":"P2","title":"1 addon lost a folder to another addon","addon":null,"remediation":{"command":"omaddons list -t retail -v","argv":["omaddons","list","-t","retail","-v"],"destructive":false}}`.
7. **`a_vanished_client_is_target_vanished`**: install `Foo` on the 3.3.5a client (id read from `status --json`); rename its directory away. `status --json` and `--cached`: that client's issues are exactly `[{"id":"fm-userland_state-target-vanished","severity":"P2","title":"The client's directory is gone","addon":null,"remediation":{"command":"omaddons targets rm <id>","argv":["omaddons","targets","rm","<id>"],"destructive":true}}]`. Human: `  P2 The client's directory is gone → omaddons targets rm <id>`.
8. **`an_outdated_widget_is_widget_version_drift`**: the outdated widget. `status --json` and `--cached`: `data.issues == [{"id":"fm-plugins-widget-version-drift","severity":"P3","title":"The bar widget is from another omaddons build","addon":null,"remediation":{"command":"omaddons omarchy install","argv":["omaddons","omarchy","install"],"destructive":false}}]`; `summary.issues.p3 == 1`; `summary.widget_outdated == true`.
9. **`several_states_rank_by_severity_id_and_addon`**: on retail, first every install (`Aaa`, `Foo`, `Baz`, then `gh:o/bar` from a zip holding `Bar/` and `Baz/` with `--force`, which leaves `Baz` degraded), then remove `Aaa`'s folder, edit `Foo`'s TOC, and plant a too-new journal last (a too-new journal blocks later changes on the client, so nothing installs after it). `status --json`: retail's issues in this order: `journal-pending` (P0, "needs manual repair"), `record-folder-missing` for `Aaa` (P1), `managed-files-modified` for `Foo` (P2), `ownership-transferred` (P2, "1 addon lost a folder to another addon"); `summary.issues` is `{"p0":1,"p1":1,"p2":2,"p3":0}` and `summary.state == "attention"`; the human lines appear in that order under retail's row; no `net.log` line was added by any run (from `Ran`'s recorded `net.log` lines).

In every scenario, also assert for each issue seen: `omaddons::doctor::registry::row(issue.id)` exists and its severity serializes to the issue's `severity` (the ids come from the registry).

### 3. Helpers (local to the suite)

- `fn issues(env: &Value, target: &str) -> Value` and `fn machine_issues(env: &Value) -> Value`;
- `fn reinstall(addon: &str, target: &str) -> Value` building the expected remediation object;
- `fn assert_registry_ids(log: &TestLog, env: &Value)` (the registry cross-check, logging each id it checked).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `tests/e2e_status_issues.rs` holds the nine scenarios (`journal_pending_is_one_issue_per_client_and_titled_by_its_journals`, `an_unattributed_journal_is_the_machines_issue`, `a_newer_record_is_state_version_newer`, `a_missing_folder_is_record_folder_missing_in_both_modes`, `modified_files_show_in_plain_status_only`, `a_forced_takeover_is_ownership_transferred`, `a_vanished_client_is_target_vanished`, `an_outdated_widget_is_widget_version_drift`, `several_states_rank_by_severity_id_and_addon`), each a `TestLog` scenario, passing in `cargo test` and under `argc e2e status_issues`.
- [ ] Every scenario compares the exact `issues` JSON (ids, severities, titles, addons, remediation command, argv and `destructive`) and, where listed, the human line and the `--check` exit.
- [ ] `managed-files-modified` appears in plain `status` and never under `--cached`; every other state appears in both.
- [ ] Two journals on one client give one issue, titled by the worse; a held lock hides it; an unattributed journal is the machine's.
- [ ] Every issue's id is a registry row whose severity equals the issue's.
- [ ] The trees of `<state>/omaddons`, `<cache>/omaddons`, `<config>/omaddons` and every client dir are unchanged by every `status` run (`log.assert_unchanged`).
- [ ] A deliberately broken expectation (tried locally, not committed) prints `test log: <path>` and the last steps, and the transcript shows each argv, envelope and tree hash.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

None: this part adds an integration suite only.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

The nine scenarios of `tests/e2e_status_issues.rs` above. Fixture builders: `Home::new(&["wow"])`, `CustomRoot` for the 3.3.5a client, local `--file` zips, planted journal files, `GlobalLock::acquire`, the record edit, `edit_managed`, the forced install, the renamed client dir, and the fake Omarchy. No network: every install is from a local file (`net.log` gains nothing; assert it in scenario 9 through `Ran`'s recorded `net.log` lines).

### Logging

T1's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`) `TestLog` in every scenario:
- `log.step` phases: `build the home`, `install <addon>`, `plant <state>`, `status --json`, `status --cached --json`, `status (human)`, `status --check`, `hold the lock`, `release the lock`;
- every command through `log.run`, which records the argv, the scenario's overrides (`OMARCHY_PATH`, `PATH`), the cwd, `elapsed_ms`, the exit code, the parsed envelope, the stderr events and the `net.log` lines added;
- `log.json("expected issues", …)` before every comparison, and `log.note` naming which state is planted;
- `log.tree(label, root)` after planting and `log.assert_unchanged(label, root)` after the `status` runs, for each of the four tree kinds;
- on a failure the guard prints `test log: <path>` and the last 20 steps; `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG=verbose argc e2e status_issues` echoes each step live.

## Considerations

- **This suite outlives the move.** F1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1`) retitles the stuck journal states and narrows `journal-pending` (M4-D48), F8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.8`) adds `auto_fixable` and `explain` to each issue and moves `status` onto the whole registry: each of those leaves updates the scenarios it changes, in its own commit, and the rest must keep passing. A scenario that fails after another leaf's change is that leaf's defect.
- **No real home, no real Omarchy.** Every run has `TestEnv`'s isolated `HOME` and XDG directories, the fake `OMARCHY_PATH` and an empty `PATH` for the widget scenario, so the desktop's shell and bar are never touched.
- **Privacy:** these homes create no `WTF/`, and `status` reads none here; no `assert_private_all` is needed (common rule 9 applies to tests that create `WTF/`).
- **Speed:** nine homes with one or two local installs each; the suite should take a few seconds.

## Dependencies

- **Parent:** E1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`).
- **Before it:** part 4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1.4`, the registry and the move), the behaviour this suite checks; and T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs and `argc e2e`), whose `TestLog` it uses (an edge added at filing).
- **After it:** nothing inside E1; closing it (if it is the last open part) closes E1, which unblocks E2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.2`), E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`), E5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`), A4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`) and T4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4`).

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M4 plan, 2026-10-24).**

**Why this bead.** Before M4 there was no doctor, so three kinds of error said the only thing they could. An `internal` error said `omaddons status` (vision DEC-5: "until `doctor` exists (M4), the `fix` for `internal` errors is `omaddons status`"). A state file omaddons could not read said `omaddons status`. A journal that recovery leaves for manual repair said to read a README section, or `omaddons status`, which shows the same journal and offers no way out. Once the doctor and its journal and state-file failure modes exist, those fixes are wrong in the most visible place: the error a user or an agent meets first. This bead points each one at the doctor and proves each new fix runs: an internal error at `omaddons doctor` (never at the command that failed), an unreadable state file at `omaddons doctor explain fm-schemas-state-corrupt`, and each stuck journal at `omaddons doctor explain <its failure mode> -t <client>`. It adds no code, no `details` key and no command, and changes no recovery decision.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M4-D53:** `internal_fix_for` returns `omaddons doctor` for every command but `status` (→ `status --cached`, as today) and `doctor` (→ `doctor health`); this retires DEC-5; `store::status_fix` points at `doctor explain fm-schemas-state-corrupt`. F8 owns the decision's other half (`auto_fixable`, `explain` and the `doctor fix --only` remediations on `status`).
- **M4-D1:** the "`internal` and `state_corrupt` fixes pointing at the doctor" handoff is in M4's scope.
- **M4-D40 (context):** a doctor-tree internal error exits 74; `doctor health` (cached and quick tiers, no run directory) is the next step there, not a rerun of the doctor.
- **M4-D29 and M4-D30 (context):** `doctor` isolates detector panics, so it is the right look after a bug elsewhere; `explain` takes a failure-mode id and `-t` narrows by target id.
- **DEC-4 and M4-D55 (context):** no wire name changes; the changed fix values are listed before → after in the close comment because agents run them.
- **§8.1 default 1:** no new code, action or key.

**Alternatives rejected that matter here.**
- *`doctor` → `doctor health` applied to `doctor health` itself:* it would rerun the failing command; `doctor health` gets the same bug-report prose `status --cached` has.
- *Pointing a stuck journal at `doctor fix`:* the set-aside of the stuck states is forced (`--force --yes`, M4-D38) and needs someone who has read the explanation, which is why the fix is `explain`.
- *`-t <target key>`:* it would parse, but F1's remediations name the id, and a target the registry does not name may not be selected by the doctor's `-t`; without an entry there is no `-t`, and `explain` lists every instance.
- *Building the fix inside each stop constructor:* several have no `Paths` and E11's refactor moves them; one function applied at recovery's entry points, keyed on the stop's `details.reason`, covers them all.
- *Leaving the stop warnings on the old prose:* a stop reported on another client's command is the same state, and the code already says a reader and another target's recovery report "the same warning both ways".
- *Changing every `omaddons status` fix in the tree:* the other sites are `io` errors and a recoverable journal's warning, for which `omaddons status` runs and is true.

**Facts verified during planning** (at `c0ab5e9`). `internal_fix()` is `omaddons status` (`src/error.rs:360-363`) and `internal_fix_for` (`:365-379`) maps only `status`; the boundary (`src/app/mod.rs:288-290`), the `cli.panic` seam (`src/cli.rs:398-402`) and `render_panic` (`src/cli.rs:1336`) apply it. `src/net/replay.rs:166-170` builds an internal error with an explicit `omaddons status`. `store::status_fix` (`src/state/store.rs:404-407`) serves both `corrupt` (`:381-388`) and `load`'s `io` read error (`:243`). The stops and their current fixes are in `src/engine/journal.rs` (`Unrecoverable::fix` `:505-515`, `unrecoverable` `:1131-1158`, the marker mismatch `:1013-1023`, `ran` `:1654-1675`, `stopped` `:1201-1221`, `recover_all` `:811-849`, `unrecoverable_warning` `:748-760`, `recover_under`'s `left` `:865-877`), and `recovery_failed` is `src/engine/tx.rs:573-591`. The tests that pin the old fixes are `src/error.rs:926, 940`, `tests/contract/special.rs:45-69`, `tests/cli_skeleton.rs:404-418`, `tests/fail_closed.rs:227` and `src/engine/journal.rs:2868`. The contract suite parses fixes but never runs them (`tests/contract/main.rs:229-269`).

**Risks and how they are watched.** No §11.4 risk is this bead's. Risk 18's guard (recovery's tests and E11's differential test unchanged) also covers this bead's edits in `src/engine/journal.rs`. The concrete risks are a stop that keeps an old fix (each state's fix argv is asserted end to end), a fix that names something `-t` cannot select or a command that fails (every new fix is run on the home that produced it and must exit as its command documents, with the instance present), and a fix chain that loops (a unit test over every command path and an end-to-end chain with the panic armed at every hop). One gap in the plan's graph: the `doctor …` arm names `doctor health`, which is E4's, and E4 is not an edge; the bead's Dependencies section tells the claiming agent to add `E4 → E10` if E4 is still open.

**What it unblocks, and why they wait.** H1 (the pre-freeze audit) walks every error's fix and fix pattern, so the changed fixes must land first and the golden H2 commits records them. T4 (the slice-3 demo, an edge added at filing) waits for every slice-3 leaf, so its "`doctor` on a home with each stuck state" scene runs where the failing commands already point at the doctor.

**How it serves the milestone's goals.** G-M4-4: a user who meets a stuck journal or a broken state file is one command from the doctor's explanation and evidence, instead of advice that cannot work. G-M4-2, in spirit: every fix this bead changes is proven to run, not only to parse. G-M4-6: recovery is untouched; only what its errors say changes. Vision G4 ("the first command an agent guesses works") holds for the fix an agent follows, and G7 ("`doctor` follows the world-class doctor contract") holds for the errors a broken home produces.

**Confidence.** High. The change is small and local (two functions, one choke point, one rename), every new fix is exercised end to end on the state that produces it, and the only open question in the plan (E4's missing edge) has a concrete rule.

title: `journal::diagnose`: a read-only simulation of recovery
description:
## How to work this bead

This bead is worked through its 5 subtasks, listed below in work order. Claim a subtask, not this bead (`br ready --parent omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.11` lists the ready ones). The agent that closes the last open subtask then verifies every acceptance criterion of this bead (they are the leaf's, not any one subtask's), and closes this bead with `br close omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.11 --reason "done: <evidence> · found: <ids>"`. Until this bead is closed, every bead it blocks stays blocked.

1. `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.11.1` Recovery's stop errors name their reason: `marker_mismatch`, `step_unrecognized` and `unattributed`. Small, wire-visible, in `src/engine/journal.rs` and README. First, so its unit tests pin the new `details` before the refactor runs over the same functions.
2. `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.11.2` Recovery's decision procedure behind a `LiveView`, with no change in behaviour. The refactor of `ran`, `ran_after`, `roll_back`, `roll_back_wtf`, `classify`, `candidates`, `source_gone` and preservation's checks, in `journal.rs` and `preserve.rs`. After s1 (same functions).
3. `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.11.3` `journal::diagnose`: the simulated tree, the verdicts and their unit tests. New `src/engine/simulate.rs`. After s2 (it calls the shared procedure).
4. `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.11.4` Tests: the `journal` fuzz target with its `parse` and `diagnose` arms, its seeds, and the seed property in the gate. After s3.
5. `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.11.5` E2E: the differential test over every crash matrix, and E11's adversarial matrix. `tests/common/differential.rs`, hooks in `tests/engine_crash.rs`, new cases in `tests/journal.rs`, assertions in the in-crate WTF recovery tests. After s3.

s4 and s5 touch different files and can be worked at the same time.

**Size L, kept as one leaf for closure.** The refactor, the simulation and the differential test are one guarantee: a classifier that has not been held to recovery by the differential test is a guess, and a refactor of recovery without the differential test is unguarded. The subtasks split the work; the leaf closes only when all five are closed, so E5, E14 and F1 never see half of it.

**Design gate (common rule 14).** E11 is one of the ten design-gate leaves: it changes recovery's code (the `LiveView` refactor) and adds a protocol that must agree with recovery (the simulation). The design gate is passed only when `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.11.5`, the adversarial matrix, is closed.

## Background

**What this leaf is.** Recovery (`src/engine/journal.rs`) is the code that finishes or undoes an interrupted transaction. M4's doctor must say, before anything moves, what recovery would do with each interrupted journal: settle it (roll forward, roll back, or just delete it), wait for the game, or stop for manual repair, and at which step and why. `status` must title each of those states correctly, the delegated recovery in `doctor fix` must disclose and bind each recovery it will run, `doctor gc` must keep what an unfinished journal needs, and E14's fences must know what a stuck journal protects. All of them read one classifier: `journal::diagnose`. This leaf builds it, as a read-only simulation of recovery that shares recovery's own decision code, and holds the two together with a differential test over every crash-matrix state.

**Why a simulation, not a classifier written beside recovery.** Recovery decides whether step k of a rollback ran by looking at the live files after it has already undone steps k+1…n (`ran_after`, `src/engine/journal.rs:1643-1651`, calling `ran`, `:1654-1675`; the WTF walk `roll_back_wtf`, `:1359-1388`). Its verdicts are interleaved with its own renames: a step that "matches neither state" before the later steps are undone may match its after state once they are. A read-only function cannot ask the disk those questions, and a second, hand-written classifier would drift from recovery with the first edit to either. So `diagnose` replays recovery's own decision functions against a virtual tree, applying each inverse rename to the tree instead of the disk, in recovery's order, and its verdict is the state recovery would end in.

**What is wrong today** (verified at `c0ab5e9`):

1. **`status` mislabels the stuck states** (the plan's "§2.4 mislabelling"). `status` passes only the `journal_too_new` and `journal_unreadable` reasons to `issues_for` (`src/app/status.rs:884-891`), so a journal stopped at a marker mismatch, at a step in neither state, at `unexpected_state` or at `preservation_incomplete` is titled "An interrupted change waits to be finished" with the advice "run any change command" (`src/app/issues.rs:130-140`), which will keep failing. Fixing the titles is F1's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1`, journal and lock detectors); this leaf provides the classification F1 maps from.
2. **Three of recovery's stops carry no `details.reason`.** A marker mismatch is a bare `scope_denied` (`journal.rs:1013-1023`); a non-WTF rollback that meets a step in neither state fails with `internal` and no details (the error `ran` builds, `:1669-1674`, propagated by `roll_back`, `:1626-1635`); and a journal recovery cannot attribute to one target fails every committing command with whatever error it had (`recover_all`'s `(None, _)` arm, `:843`). An agent cannot branch on any of them.
3. **Nothing predicts recovery.** No function answers "what will recovery do with this journal" without doing it.

**Milestone goals it serves:**

- **G-M4-4 (diagnosable and repairable):** `omaddons doctor` names every broken state omaddons can detect, with concrete evidence and an exact remediation; the states README calls "manual repair" each get a name, an explanation and a guarded repair; `status` and `doctor` never disagree about what is wrong. Every journal finding of F1, both `status` and `doctor`, reads this one classifier, so they cannot disagree about journals.
- **G-M4-6 (no new risk to the engine's guarantees):** every repair is a journaled transaction that recovers like any other. This leaf refactors recovery's most-tested code; the differential test and the unchanged crash matrices are the proof that recovery's behaviour did not change.

**Checkpoint criteria it serves** (H6, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, runs them):

- **11 (stuck states are named and repairable):** every manual-repair state (`journal_too_new`, `journal_unreadable`, marker mismatch, a step in neither state, `unexpected_state`, `preservation_incomplete`, a journal with no readable target, and a restore journal waiting for the game) has a finding with a correct title in both `status` and `doctor`. Each of these is one `JournalVerdict` of this leaf, which F1 maps to its failure-mode id.
- **12 (`status` and `doctor` agree):** for every fixture, the issue ids `status` reports equal the doctor's cached and quick findings. Both read `journal::diagnose`.
- **13 (durability), its last bullet:** every crash matrix in `tests/engine_crash.rs` passes unchanged. This leaf is the first M4 leaf to change recovery's code, and must leave every matrix green.
- **17 (gate and checkpoint runs):** every fuzz target runs 10 minutes, and the new `journal` target 30 minutes (`argc fuzz journal --time 1800`). This leaf creates that target for the folder family.
- It also underlies criterion **10**'s "a bound fix whose preview did not disclose a pending journal it would recover is stale before any recovery or repair moves anything": the preview lists recoveries from `diagnose`'s prediction (E6).

**The decisions that shape it** (full text in the decision-log comments on the milestone epic `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`):

- **M4-D37, recoverable journals are fixed by the engine's own recovery, as a declared delegation.** The fixer of `fm-concurrency_primitives-journal-pending` runs `journal::recover_under` with the doctor's lock. Its effects are planned and disclosed first: planning predicts each pending journal's outcome with `journal::diagnose`, so the preview lists every recovery it will run as `{tx, family, phase, direction, protected resources}`, and the token covers them (M4-D44). Under the lock the doctor re-plans (diagnose again) and compares the token before the first recovery. Rejected: making recovery a repair action (a second recovery implementation). For this leaf: `diagnose` must predict the direction exactly and must be cheap and repeatable, because it runs twice per `doctor fix`.
- **M4-D44, the token's canonical form.** Each delegated recovery enters `selection` as `{tx, family, phase, direction}` with the direction "`journal::diagnose`'s prediction", and `observed` holds each delegated journal's protected resources as stable digests. So the prediction and the protected paths must be deterministic: two diagnoses of an unchanged home give equal results, and nothing volatile (a pid, an age) enters them.
- **M4-D45, concurrent fixers serialize and re-plan.** Under the lock: load a fresh view, re-run detectors and re-plan the effect plan "the selected recoveries (predicted by `journal::diagnose`) included", compare `--if-match`, and only then run the recoveries. `diagnose` therefore runs both without and under the global lock; it never takes the lock itself.
- **M4-D38, the stuck journal states get a guarded set-aside.** The states `journal-too-new`, `journal-unreadable`, `journal-unexpected-state`, `journal-step-unrecognized`, `journal-marker-mismatch` and `journal-unattributed` get F2's set-aside. For unreadable and newer journals "attribute independently, never follow the payload": the set moved is what can be attributed by the transaction id in known locations (`<state>/journal/`, `<state>/inflight/`, `<state>/snapshots/`, and each client's `<meta>/stage/` and `<meta>/snapshots/`), on clients whose markers check out. For this leaf: the verdict of an untrusted journal carries only artifacts found by transaction id in those known locations, never a path its payload names. Rejected (for F2, and so for this leaf's evidence): guessing a direction for a journal recovery cannot read (M3-D45's rule).
- **M4-D48, the published `journal-pending` is narrowed.** From F1 it means only "a journal recovery can settle"; the six stuck states have their own ids, and a restore waiting for the game is `journal-waits-for-game` (P2). This leaf's verdicts are exactly that split: `Recoverable` versus the stuck verdicts versus `WaitsForGame`.
- **M4-D62, one canonical resource model.** Repairs, fences, undo and gc reason about `ResourceSet`s (E13). gc's reachability pins walk "every unfinished journal of both families (`journal::diagnose`'s protected resources)". This leaf reports each journal's protected paths; they become E13's `ResourceSet` once E13 has landed (until then a path list, which E5 converts).
- **M4-D31, a repair is a second journal family.** Repair journals (`<tx>.repair.jsonl`) come with E5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`, the repair transaction), which extends `diagnose` to that family; E14 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14`, fences and activation barriers) changes recovery's order to three passes and adds the `BehindBarrier` verdict. This leaf covers the folder family (folder and WTF journals) and is built so both extensions are local.
- **M3-D45, what this build cannot read, it never acts on.** A journal of a newer major format, or with a complete line it cannot decode, is left whole for manual repair (`Parsed::unrecoverable`, `journal.rs:522-530`). The simulation obeys the same rule: such a journal's verdict is `TooNew` or `Unreadable`, and nothing in it is trusted.
- **M3-D24 (c), the WTF rollback's rules 2 and 3, and M3-D29.** A WTF rollback leaves a step it cannot reverse but can place as it is, collects what it displaced, and preserves every version no other copy holds as a `recovered` backup through a journaled intent before it prunes; it never runs while the game runs or may run. The simulation reproduces rule 2 (`classify`), rule 3's candidates, the intent's resumption checks, and the wait.

**Facts this bead relies on** (as of `c0ab5e9`; each verified, drift noted):

- `JournalLine` is `prepared | step | swapped | committed | preserve | preserved`, tagged by `"type"` (`src/engine/journal.rs:49-60`). The format is 1.1 (`CURRENT`, `:46`). `Phase` is `Unprepared | Prepared | Swapped | Committed` (`:454-461`).
- `FileId` is `{dev, ino, born_ns}` (`:296-319`), and `same` (`:324-337`, `pub(super)`) compares inode and birth time, ignoring the device. E13 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.13`, resource sets and fsx endpoint predicates) moves both into fsx (`FileId::same`) after this leaf by the hot-spot order; if E13's move is already on `main`, every `same` below is `FileId::same`.
- `parse` never fails and counts what it cannot read (`:538-607`); `Parsed::unrecoverable` is `TooNew` when the `prepared` line's major is newer, `Unreadable` when a complete line does not decode or no `prepared` decodes while there are lines (`:522-530`); `parsed.target` is read from the raw `prepared` line even when it does not decode (`:572-580`).
- The listing is the private `journals()` (`:610-635`): it lists `<state>/journal/`, names each file through `paths::tx_named` (`:629`, which strips only `.wtf`), and returns `(TxId, PathBuf)` sorted. A `.repair.jsonl` name does not parse and is not listed. There is no `journal::list`, which §6.13 and E2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.2`, the tolerant view) name.
- `recover_all` (`:811-848`): for each listed journal, it skips one whose in-flight lock is live (`InflightLock::is_live`, `:814`; a read-only `flock` probe, `src/fsx/lock.rs:247-276`), reads its target from the raw line, calls `recover_one`, and on an error turns it into a `journal_pending` warning when the journal belongs to another target, else returns it (`:822-844`). The `(None, _)` arm (`:843`) is reached both when the journal's target cannot be read and when it is one of the caller's own (`target.filter(|t| !env.own.contains(t))`, `:824`). The listing error (`:813`) and the liveness error (`:814`) also fail every caller.
- `recover_parsed` (`:998-1126`) decides in this order: an unrecoverable journal fails with `state_too_new` or `state_corrupt` and `{journal_pending, reason, target}` (`unrecoverable`, `:1131-1158`); an unfinished journal (`Prepared` or `Swapped`) whose client dir's marker does not name its target, or whose dir the scopes cannot add, fails with a bare `scope_denied` (`:1013-1023`, `journal_scopes` `:936-945`); a `writes_wtf` unfinished journal with at least one step, whose client SavedVariables may not be written now (`env.sv_writable`), fails with `game_running` and `{reason: "saved_variables", journal_pending, target}` (`:1039-1046`, `:1162-1176`); then by phase: unprepared or committed → nothing but pruning (`:1052-1054`), swapped → `roll_forward` (`:1486-1558`), prepared with `writes_wtf` → `roll_back_preserving` (`:1231-1285`), prepared → `roll_back` (`:1626-1635`).
- `roll_back` walks steps last first, undoing each that `ran_after` says ran, and hits `engine.recover.step` after each (`:1626-1635`); a step in neither state propagates `ran`'s `internal` error, whose message is "journal step {n} ({from} → {to}) matches neither its before nor its after state; leaving it for manual repair" (`:1669-1674`).
- `roll_back_wtf` (`:1359-1388`) does the same, but a step in neither state goes to `classify` (`:1320-1353`): `Replaced` (our restored copy was replaced; go on), `Displaced(item)` (keep the displaced side as an item to preserve; go on) or `Unrecognized` (stop: `internal`, `details.reason: "unexpected_state"`, `stopped`, `:1201-1221`).
- `roll_back_preserving` (`:1231-1285`): with no `preserve` intent yet, it walks (`roll_back_wtf`), computes rule 3's `candidates` (`:1403-1432`; a partial restore's `staged_file_candidates`, `:1438-1464`; `source_gone`, `:1469-1481`), writes one intent when there are items, and runs `preserve::run`; with intents already written, it skips the walk and resumes each one not yet `preserved`. Any failure is `state_corrupt` with `details.reason: "preservation_incomplete"`. `candidates` reads `StampDigest::compute` of the staged `WTF/` (a stat walk) and `file_stamp` of staged files (`:202-220`).
- `preserve::run` (`src/engine/preserve.rs:40-79`) checks: when the backup `backups/<id>` is already published, every item must be in it with its identity (`:49-61`); otherwise each item must be in the assembly or at the path recovery found it (`move_items`, `:90-125`; "in neither place" is a surprise, `:96-98`); then `describe` walks the assembly within `BACKUP_TREE_MAX_ENTRIES`/`BACKUP_TREE_MAX_DEPTH` (`:137-142`) and needs `described_client` (`:200-226`: `prepared.client`, else the source backup's `backup.json`). The module is private to `engine` (`src/engine/mod.rs:10`).
- **A partial restore names a directory and the files below it.** Its journal has one step per file (`stage/<tx>.wtf/WTF/<rel>` ⇄ `<client dir>/WTF/<rel>`), then one step moving the whole staged `WTF/` directory into `<meta>/snapshots/<tx>.wtf/WTF` (`src/engine/restore_addons.rs:917-966`). Undoing that last step brings every file back below the stage. A flat map from path to identity cannot simulate it: the virtual tree must move subtrees.
- `recover_under` builds `ScopeTable::new(paths, &[], None)` at `journal.rs:877` (the plan said `:875`), and `ScopeTable::add_client_dir` canonicalizes through the deepest existing ancestor, failing only on a relative path or an I/O error other than not-found (`src/fsx/scope.rs:263-269`, `:657-683`).
- Whether recovery may write a client's SavedVariables is the caller's predicate: a discovered client that is not running (`src/engine/tx.rs:598-603`); commands without discovery pass `no_saved_variables` (`journal.rs:899-901`). `status` already scans running clients (`src/app/status.rs:625`).
- **Correction to the plan's location of the mislabel:** the plan cites `status.rs:1319-1326`. At `c0ab5e9` the title is chosen in `src/app/issues.rs:130-140` (with `MANUAL_REPAIR` at `:37-42`), and `status`'s attention text "an interrupted transaction for … awaits recovery" is at `src/app/status.rs:1314-1320`.
- **No `journal` fuzz target exists.** `fuzz/Cargo.toml` has 20 targets, held by `TARGETS` in `tests/fuzz_seeds.rs:18-39` and README's Development section (`README.md:2659`). E5's plan entry creates "the repair-journal fuzz target `journal` (both families)", but E5 lands after this leaf, whose own test plan gives the target a `diagnose` arm. This leaf creates it for the folder family, and E5 extends it.
- The tests this leaf must keep green and extend: `tests/journal.rs` (504 lines; an in-process six-step scene, `:36-285`, and its prefix, swapped, committed, torn, unprepared and live cases, `:288-504`); `tests/engine_crash.rs` (4,588 lines; cross-process crashes of the binary at every failpoint, with shared helpers `crash` `:235-375`, `crash_shape` `:587-696`, `record_matrix` `:784-899`, the restore helpers `crash_op` `:2440-2635` and `preserve_crash` `:2350-2437`, the partial-restore helpers from `:3409`, and the undo-of-restore helper `undo_preserve_crash` from `:4278`); and the in-crate tests of `journal.rs` (from `:1708`) and `preserve.rs` (from `:303`).

**How it serves the vision.** Vision G7 asks that `doctor` follow the world-class doctor contract: every finding has evidence and an exact remediation, and a fix's effects are disclosed before they happen. Both need a truthful prediction of recovery. And the thesis that omaddons stays the sole, safe, undoable authority over what it manages holds only if the doctor's view of an interrupted change is the engine's own: a doctor that guessed differently from recovery would advise the wrong repair at the worst moment.

## Technical Approach

### 1. The shape of the work

Three layers, in this order:

1. **One decision procedure** (s2). Recovery's reads move behind a trait, `LiveView`, and its rollback walks behind `Replay` (a `LiveView` that can reverse a step). Recovery implements them with the disk. Nothing else changes: the same functions, the same order, the same failpoints, the same errors.
2. **One simulation** (s3). `src/engine/simulate.rs` implements `LiveView` and `Replay` with a virtual tree (disk reads cached once per path, plus the ordered list of simulated inverse renames), runs the same decision procedure against it, and maps the end state to a `JournalVerdict`.
3. **One differential guard** (s5). For every crash-matrix state, `diagnose` runs on the home (and is proven to write nothing), then real recovery runs, and the two must agree on the outcome: rolled forward, rolled back, pruned, skipped, or stopped with the same code, `details.reason` and step.

Before the refactor, s1 gives the three silent stops their `details.reason`, so the differential test can compare reasons for every stop, and s1's tests pin those details through the refactor. s4 adds the fuzz target.

### 2. Recovery's stop errors gain `details.reason` (s1)

A single vocabulary, `pub enum StopReason` in `src/engine/journal.rs`, with `as_str()` and `ALL`: `JournalTooNew` (`journal_too_new`), `JournalUnreadable` (`journal_unreadable`), `MarkerMismatch` (`marker_mismatch`), `StepUnrecognized` (`step_unrecognized`), `UnexpectedState` (`unexpected_state`), `PreservationIncomplete` (`preservation_incomplete`), `SavedVariables` (`saved_variables`) and `Unattributed` (`unattributed`). `Unrecoverable::reason` (`:497-503`) and `Stop::reason` (`:1190-1197`) return through it, and `waits_for_the_game` uses `SavedVariables`. The simulation's expected outcomes (s3) use the same enum, so the strings exist once.

| Stop | Today | After s1 |
|---|---|---|
| Marker mismatch (`:1013-1023`) | `scope_denied`, no details | `scope_denied`, `details: {reason: "marker_mismatch", journal_pending: <tx>, target: <key>}`; message, fix (`omaddons status`) unchanged |

**`unattributed` defined.** A failure recovery cannot attribute to one target, so it fails every committing command on every target. Three sources, all in `recover_all`: the journal directory cannot be listed (`:813`, an `io` error, no `journal_pending`); a journal's in-flight lock cannot be probed (`:814`, an `io` error); and a journal whose own target cannot be read fails (`:843` with `target.is_none()`: a read failure gives `io`, a newer major gives `state_too_new`, an undecodable one gives `state_corrupt`). The `(None, _)` arm is also reached for the caller's own targets; those errors are returned unchanged (a marker mismatch of the caller's own target keeps `marker_mismatch`). ### 3. The decision procedure behind `LiveView` (s2)

**The traits** (in `src/engine/journal.rs`, `pub(crate)`):

```rust
/// What is at a path as recovery's decisions see it, never following a final symlink.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
pub struct LiveEntry { pub kind: LiveKind, pub id: FileId }
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum LiveKind { File, Dir, Symlink, Other }

/// Every read recovery's decision procedure makes (E11). Recovery reads the disk
/// (`Disk`); `diagnose` reads a simulation of it (`simulate::Simulated`).
pub(crate) trait LiveView {
    fn entry(&mut self, path: &Path) -> Option<LiveEntry>;
    fn id(&mut self, path: &Path) -> Option<FileId> { self.entry(path).map(|e| e.id) }
    fn is_dir(&mut self, path: &Path) -> bool { matches!(self.entry(path), Some(LiveEntry { kind: LiveKind::Dir, .. })) }
    /// `file_stamp` of the one entry at `path`.
    fn file_stamp(&mut self, path: &Path) -> Option<String>;
    /// `StampDigest::compute(path)` as text; an error is what recovery stops on.
    fn tree_stamp(&mut self, path: &Path) -> std::io::Result<String>;
}

/// A rollback walk's two effects: reversing a step that ran, and the point after each step.
pub(crate) trait Replay: LiveView {
    fn reverse(&mut self, step: &StepRecord) -> Result<()>;
    fn stepped(&mut self, step: &StepRecord) -> Result<()>;
}
```

`Disk` (a unit struct) implements `LiveView` with exactly today's reads: `FileId::of` (`symlink_metadata`, `:308-318`), `file_stamp` and `StampDigest::compute`. `Recovering<'s, 'a> { s: &'s mut WriteSession<'a> }` implements `LiveView` through `Disk` and `Replay` with today's effects: `reverse` is today's `undo(s, step)` (`:1677-1706`, the `NoReplace` rename with its `Replace` fallback on `Unsupported`), and `stepped` is `failpoint::hit("engine.recover.step")` mapped to `Error::io(&step.from, …)` as today.

**The API:**

```rust

pub struct Diagnoses {

}

pub struct JournalDiagnosis {
    pub tx: TxId,

    pub client_dir: Option<PathBuf>,        // prepared.client_dir, when `prepared` decodes

impl JournalDiagnosis {
    pub fn expected(&self) -> Expected;     // what recovery then does (the differential's oracle)

```

- **`client_dirs`** are the clients the caller knows (the doctor's Discovery layer, `status`'s discovered targets, a test's home). They are where an untrusted journal's artifacts are searched by transaction id (below).
- **`sv_writable`** is the predicate the caller's recovery would pass as `RecoveryEnv::sv_writable`: a discovered client that is not running. Decided while writing this bead: the plan's signature has no such parameter, but recovery's outcome for a `writes_wtf` journal depends on it (`journal.rs:1039-1046`), so `diagnose` takes it rather than guessing.
- Decided while writing this bead: the plan writes `-> Vec<JournalDiagnosis>`; `Diagnoses` adds `unlisted`, because a journal directory that cannot be listed must not read as "no journals" (common rule 15). Consumers iterate `.journals`.
- `diagnose` never fails and never takes the global lock. It runs without the lock (status, doctor planning) and under it (doctor re-planning, M4-D45); it is a snapshot either way.

**The virtual tree.** Decided while writing this bead (the plan's "virtual map `path → {exists, kind, FileId, digest}`", made able to move subtrees):

- `Base` (trait, `pub`): what the simulation reads besides recovery's own reads: `entry`, `file_stamp`, `tree_stamp`, `owns_client_dir(prepared) -> bool`, `writer_alive(tx) -> Result<bool, String>`, `describable(prepared) -> bool`, `backup_meta_loads(dir) -> bool`, `marker(client_dir) -> Option<TargetKey>`.
  - `DiskBase` reads the disk, read-only: `symlink_metadata`, `file_stamp`, `StampDigest::compute`; `owns_client_dir` is today's `journal_scopes` test (`read_marker(client_dir) == Some(target_key)` and `add_client_dir` succeeding on a scratch clone of one `ScopeTable::new(paths, &[], None)` built once per call; if that table cannot be built, the marker test plus `is_absolute`); `writer_alive` is `InflightLock::is_live`; `describable` is `preserve::described_client(prepared).is_ok()`; `backup_meta_loads` is `store::load::<BackupMeta>(&meta_file(dir))` returning `Some`. Decided while writing this bead: the scratch `ScopeTable` keeps the check identical to recovery's without touching `src/fsx/` (whose hot-spot order starts with E13).
  - `MapBase` (pub) holds all of these in `BTreeMap`s, for unit tests and the fuzz target.
- `Cached<B>` reads each path at most once per call (a `BTreeMap` per read kind) and counts its reads, so the plan's "read the live identity of every path it names, once" is testable.
- `Simulated<B>` = a `Cached<B>` plus `moves: Vec<Move>`, where `Move` is `Rename { from, to }` (what was at `from` is now at `to`, and `from` is empty) or `Exchange { a, b }`. A query for path `p` walks the moves latest first: under a `Rename`'s `to`, `p` becomes `from` plus the rest; under its `from`, the answer is "absent"; under an `Exchange` side, `p` becomes the other side plus the rest; an ancestor of a moved path keeps its own identity. The translated path is then read from the base. So a directory's subtree moves with it, which a partial restore needs.
- `Replay for Simulated`: `reverse` pushes the inverse move (`Exchange` for an exchange; `Rename { from: step.to, to: step.from }` for `Noreplace` and `Rename`); `stepped` does nothing. A `checkpoint()`/`restore(cp)` pair truncates `moves`.
- `tree_stamp(p)` is read on `p`'s translated origin. That is exact when no move lies strictly inside `p`'s subtree, which holds for every journal shape the engine writes (a whole restore's `WTF` renames are of whole trees; a partial restore's staged files are judged by `file_stamp`). When a move does lie inside, the origin's stamp is returned and the approximation `CompositeTreeStamp` is recorded.

**Per journal, in recovery's order on one shared simulated tree.** Decided while writing this bead: journals are simulated in `journal::list`'s order on one `Simulated` (as recovery would leave the disk for the next journal), which is also where E14's three-pass order plugs in. A live journal's moves are discarded (recovery skips it). Prunes are not simulated: every prune victim is named by the journal's own transaction id, which no other journal reads.

```text
for (tx, path) in list:
    live    = base.writer_alive(tx)        Err → verdict Unattributed{LivenessUnknown}
    text    = read(path)                   Err → verdict Unattributed{ReadFailed}
    parsed  = parse(text)
    cp      = sim.checkpoint()
    match route(&parsed, base.owns_client_dir(prepared), sv_writable):
      Unrecoverable(why)  → target none ? Unattributed{why as cause} : TooNew | Unreadable
      MarkerMismatch      → MarkerMismatch
      WaitsForGame        → WaitsForGame
      Prune               → Recoverable{phase: parsed.phase, direction: Prune}
      Forward             → Recoverable{phase: Swapped, direction: Forward}
      Back                → walk_back(sim): Done → Recoverable{Prepared, Back}; StoppedAt(k) → StepUnrecognized{k}
      BackPreserving      → an intent without `preserved`? → resume(sim): PreservationIncomplete{stops}
                            intents all preserved?           → Recoverable{Prepared, Back}
                            else walk_back_wtf(sim): Unplaced{k} → UnexpectedState{k}
                                 Done(displaced) → candidates(sim): Err → PreservationIncomplete{stops: true}
                                     [] → Recoverable{Prepared, Back}
                                     items → describable ? Recoverable{Prepared, Back} (+ evidence.preservation, approx PreservationWalk)
                                                         : PreservationIncomplete{stops: true}
    if live: sim.restore(cp)
```

`resume` mirrors `preserve::run` for each intent not `preserved`: when `backups/<id>` exists in the simulated tree, `published_matches` must be true and `backup_meta_loads` must hold; otherwise each item must be `InAssembly` (skipped) or `AtFound` (its move into the assembly is applied to the simulated tree), never `Neither`; then `describable`. Any failure gives `stops: true`. Resumption records the approximation `PreservationWalk`.

**The verdicts and what recovery then does** (`JournalVerdict`, and `expected()`; the differential test compares `expected()` with what recovery did):

| Verdict | When (recovery's order) | `expected()` |
|---|---|---|
| `Unattributed { cause: LivenessUnknown }` | the in-flight lock cannot be probed | `Stops { code: io, reason: unattributed }` |
| `Unattributed { cause: ReadFailed }` | the journal file cannot be read | `Stops { code: io, reason: unattributed }` |
| `Unattributed { cause: TooNew }` | newer major format, target unreadable | `Stops { code: state_too_new, reason: unattributed }` |
| `Unattributed { cause: Unreadable }` | an undecodable complete line, target unreadable | `Stops { code: state_corrupt, reason: unattributed }` |
| `TooNew` | newer major format (`Parsed::unrecoverable`) | `Stops { code: state_too_new, reason: journal_too_new }` |
| `Unreadable` | an undecodable complete line, or no `prepared` among complete lines | `Stops { code: state_corrupt, reason: journal_unreadable }` |
| `MarkerMismatch` | unfinished, and the client dir is not the target's | `Stops { code: scope_denied, reason: marker_mismatch }` |
| `WaitsForGame` | `writes_wtf`, unfinished, at least one step, `sv_writable` false | `Stops { code: game_running, reason: saved_variables }` |
| `Recoverable { phase: Unprepared or Committed, direction: Prune }` | no complete line, or committed | `Pruned` |
| `Recoverable { phase: Swapped, direction: Forward }` | swapped | `RolledForward` |
| `Recoverable { phase: Prepared, direction: Back }` | prepared, and the walk completes | `RolledBack` |
| `StepUnrecognized { step }` | non-WTF walk meets step `k` in neither state | `Stops { code: internal, reason: step_unrecognized, step: Some(k) }` |
| `UnexpectedState { step }` | WTF walk meets step `k` that `classify` cannot place | `Stops { code: internal, reason: unexpected_state, step: Some(k) }` |
| `PreservationIncomplete { stops: false }` | an intent without `preserved`, whose resumption's checks pass | `RolledBack` |
| `PreservationIncomplete { stops: true }` | a resumption or a new intent that will fail its checks, or a staged tree whose stamp cannot be computed | `Stops { code: state_corrupt, reason: preservation_incomplete }` |
| any verdict with `live: true` | the in-flight lock is held | `Skipped` |

- Decided while writing this bead: the plan's verdicts are kept, with fields where `expected()` needs them: `PreservationIncomplete { stops }` (an intent can be pending and resumable, or bound to stop) and `Unattributed { cause }`. `Unattributed` takes precedence over `TooNew` and `Unreadable` when the target cannot be read, matching recovery's `(None, _)` arm.
- Decided while writing this bead: a held in-flight lock is the field `live`, not a verdict: recovery skips the journal now, and the verdict says what it will do once the writer is gone.
- Decided while writing this bead: committed and never-prepared journals are `Recoverable` with `direction: Prune` (recovery deletes them silently, `:1052-1054`). F1 should not report committed ones: `journal::pending` never does (`:691-710`).
- `direction()` is `Some` for `Recoverable` and for `PreservationIncomplete { stops: false }` (`Back`), else `None`; E6 puts it into the token's `selection` (M4-D44).
- `Expected::{RolledForward, RolledBack, Pruned, Skipped, Stops { code: ErrorCode, reason: StopReason, step: Option<u32> }}`.

**Evidence** (`JournalEvidence`; what F1 builds finding evidence from, and what a failing differential case logs): `version: Option<SchemaVersion>`, `kind: Option<TxKind>`, `writes_wtf`, `steps` (recorded), `ran: Vec<u32>` (steps the walk reversed, ascending), `torn_tail`, `unknown_lines`, `marker: Option<TargetKey>` (what the client dir's marker names now), `displaced: usize` (WTF steps left as found with their displaced side kept), `preservation: Option<Preservation { intent: Option<BackupId>, items: usize, pending: bool }>`, `artifacts: Vec<Artifact>`, `approximations: Vec<Approximation>`.

- **`artifacts`**: everything found by the transaction id in its known locations, whatever the verdict: `<state>/journal/<tx>.jsonl` and `<tx>.wtf.jsonl`, `<state>/inflight/<tx>.lock`, `<state>/snapshots/<tx>` and `<tx>.wtf`, and for each entry of `client_dirs`, `<meta>/stage/<tx>`, `<tx>.wtf`, `<meta>/snapshots/<tx>` and `<tx>.wtf`; only those that exist. Each `Artifact { path, kind: Journal | Inflight | StateSnapshot | ClientStage | ClientSnapshot, client: Option<PathBuf>, marker_matches: Option<bool> }` (whether that client's marker names `parsed.target`; `None` when the target is unknown). F1 sizes them; F2 decides attribution from them.
- **`approximations`**: `PreservationWalk` (preservation would run: its describe walk's bounds `BACKUP_TREE_MAX_ENTRIES` and `BACKUP_TREE_MAX_DEPTH` are not simulated), `CompositeTreeStamp` (above), `WtfPathWithoutFlag` (a step of a journal without `writes_wtf` names a path below its client's `WTF/`, which recovery's `Mutating` writer may not rename; fsx's scope check is not simulated). Decided while writing this bead: these are flagged, not guessed around; F1 lowers a finding's `confidence` when `exact()` is false.
- **Not predicted, by design:** I/O failures (a full disk, an `EIO`, an injected failpoint), fsx refusals other than the flagged one, and a roll-forward's own state-file failures (a damaged or newer record or files index, which F3's detectors report). These are not approximations of a deterministic outcome; they are outside any prediction, and the differential test compares only with the command that finishes recovery.

**Protected paths.** `ProtectedPaths { reads: Vec<PathBuf>, writes: Vec<PathBuf> }`, sorted by path and deduplicated (the milestone's default: stable order).

- **A trusted journal** (its `prepared` decodes and its client dir is the target's: `Recoverable`, `WaitsForGame`, `StepUnrecognized`, `UnexpectedState`, `PreservationIncomplete`): `writes` = the journal file, its in-flight lock, every step's `from` and `to`, the stage dir (`prepared.commit.stage_dir`), both snapshot halves (`ClientPaths::snapshots(tx)` or `snapshots_wtf(tx)`, `Paths::state_snapshot(tx)` or `state_snapshot_wtf(tx)`, by `puts_settings_back`), for `Swapped` the target record, files index and `history.jsonl`, and for a preserving rollback each intent's assembly and `backups/<id>`; `reads` = the source backup dir and the reverted transaction's `WTF.previous` (`writes_wtf`), and the client marker.
- **An untrusted journal** (`TooNew`, `Unreadable`, `Unattributed`, `MarkerMismatch`): `writes` = the artifacts' paths only, `reads` empty. Never a path the payload names (M4-D38).
- **Privacy** (common rule 9): every path with a `WTF` or `WTF.previous` component is cut after that component, so no protected path or artifact names a file below `WTF/` (account, realm and character names). Decided while writing this bead, following M4-D38's "one digest of the `WTF/` tree's stamps, never a path below it".
- Decided while writing this bead: a path list until E13's `ResourceSet` exists; if E13 has landed when this is implemented, build the `ResourceSet` directly (`writes` as written resources, directories as `Subtree`). Otherwise E5 converts it (E5 is blocked by both E11 and E13).

**Serialization.** `JournalDiagnosis` and every type in it derive `Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize` (snake_case; `Phase` gains `Serialize`), for test logs and assertion messages. It is not a wire shape: F1 builds its finding evidence, and E6 its token's selection, in their own spellings. Maps are `BTreeMap`.

**Cost.** With no journal, `diagnose` costs one directory listing, exactly what `journal::pending` costs today (F8 holds `status --cached` under 5 ms). Per journal: one read, one `flock` probe, at most a few `stat`s per step (each path read once), and, only for a prepared whole-restore journal with no intent, the stamp walk of its staged `WTF/` that recovery itself would make. Decided while writing this bead: no byte bound on reading a journal, and no new constant: `diagnose` reads exactly what recovery reads, whole, so the two cannot disagree; a journal is omaddons-written, one line per step of one transaction.

**Concurrency.** `diagnose` takes no lock. Its `flock` probe of an in-flight lock is the same probe `recover_waiting` already makes before taking the global lock (`journal::recoverable`, `:923-930`): two concurrent probes can make a recovering command see a dead writer as alive once, which leaves the journal for the next command and harms nothing. Decided while writing this bead: accepted, as it already exists.

**What not to do.**

- Do not let any `simulate.rs` production code hold a `WriteSession`, call `mutate`, `prune` or any `std::fs` write: a unit test scans for them (the same rule the doctor's detectors get: a source scan that must find no `fsx::` write and no `WriteSession`), and `tests/single_writer.rs` scans all of `src/`.
- Do not re-implement a decision in `simulate.rs` that recovery makes in `journal.rs` or `preserve.rs`: call the shared function. A decision written twice is the drift this leaf exists to prevent.
- Do not trust an untrusted journal's payload for anything but its transaction id and raw target.
- Do not change `paths::tx_named` (E5 relies on `.repair` names staying invisible to it).

Seeds under `fuzz/seeds/journal/` (at least three, one `malformed…`), written by the ignored generator `write_fuzz_seeds` (`OMADDONS_WRITE_SEEDS=1 cargo test --test fuzz_seeds -- --ignored write`) from real journals: the six-step folder journal at several prefixes, a swapped and a committed one, a whole restore, a partial restore with a `preserve` intent, a newer major, an undecodable middle line and a torn tail.

- **The property**, a `#[doc(hidden)] pub fn fuzz_property(data: &[u8])` in `simulate.rs`, which panics on a violation, so the target and a gate test share it:
  - the `parse` arm: `parse` never panics; `lines`, `unknown_lines` and `torn_tail` are consistent; parsing twice gives equal results;
  - the `diagnose` arm: from the parsed journal and the input's bytes, a `MapBase` that puts each named path absent, at its recorded before identity, at its after identity or at another identity (chosen deterministically from the input), plus a marker and a liveness answer; `diagnose_journals` over it never panics, gives equal results twice, `expected()` is total, and the verdict agrees with `parse` (an unrecoverable journal is `TooNew`, `Unreadable` or `Unattributed`; a committed or unprepared one is `Prune`);
  - the disk arm: the input written as `<state>/journal/<tx>.jsonl` in one scratch home created at the first input, `diagnose` on disk, and the home's listing (paths, kinds, sizes, modes, modification times) unchanged by it.
- A gate test, `tests/fuzz_seeds.rs::journal_seeds_satisfy_the_fuzz_property`, runs `fuzz_property` over every committed `journal` seed.
- Run `argc fuzz journal --time 600` (10 minutes, the leaf's run; H6 runs 30) and quote its summary in the close comment. A crash input becomes a regression unit test in `simulate.rs` or `journal.rs` before the fix (README's rule).
- E5 extends the target to the repair family (its item 11); the count stays 21.
- Decided while writing this bead: this leaf creates the target E5's plan entry names, because the plan's E11 test plan gives it a `diagnose` arm and E11 lands first.

### 6. The differential test and the adversarial matrix (s5)

**The helper**, `tests/common/differential.rs` (new), using T1's `TestLog` (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs):

- `predict(log, label, paths, clients, running) -> Prediction`: hashes `<state>`, `<cache>` and every client dir (`common::trees::tree_hash`), calls `journal::diagnose(paths, clients, &|d| clients.contains(d) && !running.contains(d))` in process, hashes again and asserts equality ("diagnose wrote nothing"), and logs the diagnoses with `log.json`.
- `observe_envelope(envelope, prediction, journals_after, caller) -> BTreeMap<TxId, Observed>` (the recovering command was the binary) and `observe_result(result, …)` (recovery ran in process, `recover_all`): `journal_recovered` naming the tx → `RolledForward` or `RolledBack` by its text; an error envelope whose `details.journal_pending` is the tx (or whose `details.reason` is `unattributed`) → `Stopped { code, reason, step }` with the step parsed from `journal step <n>` in the message; a `journal_pending` warning naming the tx → `Stopped { reason }` from its `(<reason>)` text; else the journal file gone → `Pruned`, present → `Untouched`.
- `Caller::{Commit { own: Vec<TargetKey> }, Under}` encodes who recovered: an engine commit fails on a stop of its own target or an unattributed one and warns for other targets; `recover_under` (`config set`, `targets`, `auth`) only warns. The first journal in recovery's order whose outcome fails the caller ends the run: every later journal is expected `Untouched`.
- `assert_agrees(log, label, prediction, observed)`: each diagnosis's `expected()` against `Observed`, the reason always, the code when observed, the step when expected. A mismatch panics with the label, the diagnosis, the observation and the transcript path.

**Where it runs:**

- **`tests/engine_crash.rs`**: every helper that crashes a run and then recovers it calls `predict` after the existing reader check and before the recovering command, and `assert_agrees` after it. That is `crash`, `crash_shape`, `record_matrix`, the restore helpers `crash_op` and `preserve_crash`, the partial-restore helpers, `undo_preserve_crash`, and every other test in the file that leaves a journal and recovers it (including `another_clients_journal_is_recovered_or_reported_never_blocking` and `a_journal_recovery_cannot_finish_only_warns_outside_the_engine`, whose planted step in neither state is now compared through the binary). Each `#[test]` creates `tlog!()` and passes it down. Each matrix logs how many states it compared and asserts it compared at least one. Decided while writing this bead: hooking the helpers covers every state of the matrices without duplicating 4,588 lines or doubling the suite's run time.
- **Repeated recovery**: where a recovering command crashed or failed (`engine.recover.*=abort@K`, injected `=error` failpoints), `predict` runs again before the next command, and its `expected()` must equal the final observation; after the finishing command, `diagnose` has no entry for the tx; two `predict`s of one state give equal diagnoses.
- **`tests/journal.rs`** (in process): every interrupted prefix of the six-step scene, with and without the device renumbering; swapped; committed; torn; unprepared; live; and every planted stuck state: marker rewritten to another key, a step's `from_id.ino` changed, `schema_version` `9.0`, an undecodable middle line, no readable target with a newer major and with an undecodable `prepared`, the journal file at mode `0o000`, the in-flight lock at `0o000`, and the journal directory at `0o000` (`Diagnoses.unlisted`).
- **The in-crate WTF recovery tests** of `journal.rs` (the `WtfScene` and preservation tests from `:3000`): a `crate::engine::testing` helper predicts before their recovery and compares after. Two of them are the known approximations and assert the flag: `a_tree_too_deep_to_describe_stops_preservation_and_keeps_it` (`PreservationWalk`) and the flagless case of `a_wtf_journal_is_recovered_as_backup_restore_whatever_its_kind` (`WtfPathWithoutFlag`).
- **Privacy**: every scene with a `WTF/` tree asserts that no serialized diagnosis contains a planted account, realm or character name (`common::privacy::assert_private`).

The plan says "`diagnose` on a copy of the home predicts what real recovery then does on the original". Decided while writing this bead: run it on the original and prove with tree hashes that it wrote nothing, because a copy has new inode numbers and birth times, and recovery and `diagnose` decide by identity (`FileId`): on a copy every recorded step would be in neither state.

### 7. Files

- `src/engine/journal.rs`: `StopReason` and the three reasons (s1); `LiveView`, `Replay`, `Disk`, `Recovering`, the shared functions, `route`, the wrappers, `journal::list`, the census test (s2); the re-export (s3); the in-crate differential assertions (s5).

- `fuzz/fuzz_targets/journal.rs`, `fuzz/Cargo.toml`, `fuzz/seeds/journal/*`, `tests/fuzz_seeds.rs` (s4).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **The differential test.** For every state of `tests/engine_crash.rs`'s folder and WTF matrices (every failpoint crash, every journaled-rename crash with and without the two-rename fallback, every crashed or failed recovery, every preservation crash and injected failure), `journal::diagnose` run on the home before the recovering command predicts exactly what recovery then does: rolled forward, rolled back, pruned, skipped, or stopped with the same code, `details.reason` and step. Each matrix logs and asserts the number of states it compared.
- [ ] The same agreement holds for `tests/journal.rs`'s prefixes (with and without device renumbering), swapped, committed, torn, unprepared and live cases, every planted stuck state (marker mismatch, step in neither state, newer major, undecodable line, no readable target, unreadable journal file, unreadable in-flight lock, unlistable journal directory), and the in-crate WTF recovery tests; the two known approximations are flagged (`exact()` false) rather than silently wrong.
- [ ] **`diagnose` writes nothing:** the tree hashes of `<state>`, `<cache>` and every client dir are equal before and after every `diagnose` call in those suites; no production code in `src/engine/simulate.rs` holds a `WriteSession` or calls `mutate`, `prune` or a `std::fs` write (unit scan), and `tests/single_writer.rs` passes.
- [ ] **Repeated recovery:** after a recovering command that crashed or failed, a fresh `diagnose` predicts what the next command then does; after recovery, `diagnose` has no entry for that transaction; two `diagnose` calls on one state are equal.

- [ ] **Stop reasons:** a marker mismatch is `scope_denied` with `details {reason: "marker_mismatch", journal_pending, target}`; a non-WTF step in neither state is `internal` with `details {reason: "step_unrecognized", journal_pending, target}` and its message still names `journal step <n>`; a listing failure, an unprobeable in-flight lock and a journal whose target cannot be read fail with their own code and `details.reason: "unattributed"`; a stop of the caller's own target keeps its own reason.
- [ ] Every verdict of the table has unit tests, table-driven, one name per case, on a `MapBase` with no disk; `expected()` is total over the verdicts; each path is read at most once per call.
- [ ] Protected paths and artifacts never name a path below `WTF/`, and an untrusted journal's protected paths are only artifacts found by its transaction id.
- [ ] **The `journal` fuzz target** exists with its `parse`, `diagnose` and disk arms, at least three seeds (one malformed), registered in `fuzz/Cargo.toml` and `TARGETS`; `journal_seeds_satisfy_the_fuzz_property` passes in the gate; `argc fuzz journal --time 600` ran clean and its summary is in the close comment.

- **Risk 18, the classifier's `LiveView` refactor changes recovery** (likelihood L, impact H). Mitigation: recovery's tests unchanged (s2's rule); the differential test over every crash-matrix state (s5); the census test; and this leaf lands before E5 touches `journal.rs`. Watch for: a failpoint hit moving by one step (the recovery matrices fail), a redaction lost on a WTF error (the privacy assertions in `preserve_crash` fail), an error code changing (contract and crash assertions fail).
- **Hot spot `src/engine/journal.rs`** (§10.5 order: E11 → E13 → E5 → E14 → F1). This leaf lands first. Keep s1 and s2 to the functions named, and land the simulation in its own file. E13 moves `FileId` and `same` into fsx: if that lands first, use `FileId::same`; if after, its rename of the call sites is mechanical. E5 adds the repair family's entry points, E14 the three passes, F1 only reads.

- **What could go wrong in implementation, and how to notice.** Sharing a function but calling it with a stale view (the simulation must apply each move before the next decision): the six-step prefix cases catch it. A subtree translation bug: the partial-restore matrix catches it. Treating a journal of the caller's own target as unattributed: `an_own_targets_stop_keeps_its_reason`.

- **Privacy.** Diagnoses carry no file content and no path below `WTF/`; the error texts are today's, redacted as today.
- **Performance.** A clean home costs one directory listing. F8 measures `status --cached` with the cached tier; a journal home is rare and its cost is what recovery itself spends.
- **Why size L.** The refactor touches recovery's most-tested code, the simulation is a new protocol, and the differential test spans the largest test suite. E5 extends both the simulation and the differential to the repair family, and E14 to the barrier order.
