title: Tests: the predicate matrix through real fsx sessions, resource and fsx agreement, and the unchanged suites
description:
Part 4 of 4 of `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.13` (Resource sets and fsx endpoint predicates). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

E13 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.13`, resource sets and fsx endpoint predicates) builds two primitives for M4's protocols: the canonical resource model with its overlap relation (`src/engine/resource.rs`, s1) and fsx endpoint predicates (`Expect::Absent | Expect::Present(Predicate)` plus a rename destination's `expect_to`, s3), with `FileId`'s reboot-safe comparison moved into fsx (s2). The approval check under the commit lock (D8, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8`), the repair transaction (E5, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`) and fences (E14, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14`) build on them.

**This part is the leaf's integration suite.** s1 and s3 test their types in isolation; this part proves, through the public `omaddons::fsx` and `omaddons::engine::resource` API on a synthetic home, the three things the consumers will rely on together:

1. **every predicate part refuses its own kind of change through a real `mutate_with` on every operation it applies to, and a refused operation writes nothing** (no action line, no backup, an unchanged tree);
2. **`Resource::canonical` resolves a path exactly as `mutate()` normalizes it**, so a fence E14 builds from a resource matches the operation `mutate()` is about to run, even through a symlinked home;
3. **nothing that existed changed behaviour**: the `Expect` tests and every crash matrix pass unchanged.

It is its own step because it is a matrix across both halves (it needs s1 and s3), and because it uses T1's `TestLog` (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs) so a failing cell can be diagnosed from its log alone.

**What the matrix stands for.** The plan's acceptance criteria for E13: "Each predicate part refuses a path changed in that respect between planning and the operation: another file of the same mode (identity), a same-size edit (`sha256`), a mode change, a directory content change (`stamp`), a retargeted symlink. Identity survives a remount that changes the device number (a test that rewrites `dev`). Every existing `Expect` test and crash matrix passes unchanged." M4-D60's per-operation check (D8: "a folder replaced in the last moment fails its operation and the transaction rolls back") and M4-D31's compound predicates (E5: "a chmod's predicate is a regular file of the recorded identity with the old mode, so a same-mode replacement file is never taken for the credential that was inspected") are both cells of it. M4-D62's overlap rule ("two path resources overlap when one is the other or an ancestor of it") is only safe for fences if resources and `mutate()` spell paths the same way, which the agreement scene checks.

It supports checkpoint criteria 6 (the approval checked again at each operation), 9 (overlapping fixes refused together; recovery classifying by predicates) and 13 ("every crash matrix in `tests/engine_crash.rs` passes unchanged").

**Facts this part relies on** (as of `c0ab5e9`, plus s1–s3):

- `tests/fsx_scope.rs` builds a synthetic home against the public API (`Paths::with_roots` over a canonicalized temp root; a client dir with `Interface/AddOns`, `Interface/.omaddons/stage`, `WTF/…`; `ScopeTable::new(&paths, &[client], None)`; `WriteSession::tx(tx, writer, &scopes, SnapshotRoots::for_tx(&paths, &tx), actions_log)`), and fingerprints trees with paths, kinds, modes, content and link targets. This suite follows the same pattern.
- `tests/common/trees.rs:439` `tree_hash(dir)` covers sorted relative paths, kinds, permission bits, file bytes and symlink targets, never inodes; T1's `log.tree` reuses it. A refused identity cell therefore also asserts the subject's `FileId::of` is unchanged.
- `ActionRecord.path` is the normalized target (`fs::canonicalize(parent)` joined with the final name, `mutate.rs:590-617`), written lossily as a `String` (`mutate.rs:289-310`).
- `tests/backup_export.rs::refused_destinations_are_untouched` (`:326`) and `::what_happens_meanwhile_is_never_clobbered_or_pruned` (`:445`, a destination created while the export is paused at `fsx.write_atomic.after` gives `file_exists`) are the end-to-end tests of `Expect::Absent` and its no-clobber publish.
- The gate runs `cargo test --locked` (`scripts/gate.sh:32-33`), so every crash matrix in `tests/engine_crash.rs` already runs in each gate.
- T1's API, as T1's bead defines it: `TestLog::new(suite, test)` (or `tlog!()`) creates `<CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR>/test-logs/<suite>/<test>/steps.jsonl` and `transcript.md`; `log.step(label)`, `log.note(text)`, `log.json(label, &value)`, `log.tree(label, root)`, `log.assert_unchanged(label, root)` (logging the first differing paths); on panic it prints `test log: <path>` and the last 20 steps; `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG=verbose` echoes every step.

## Technical Approach

Beads this section names: D8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8`, the approval checked again under the commit lock), E5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`, the repair transaction), E8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.8`, `doctor gc`) and T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs and the `argc e2e` runner). Only T1's `TestLog` is used; the others are named for the shapes their later code will take.

1. **New `tests/fsx_predicates.rs`** with `mod common;` (for `common::tlog` and `common::trees::tree_hash`) and a module doc saying what the suite proves and where each half is built (s1, s3).
2. **The home builder** `fn home() -> Home` (local to the suite): a canonicalized temp root with `home/`, `<state>` and `<config>` from `Paths::with_roots`, a client dir with `Interface/AddOns/{X,Y}` (each with a `.toc` and a `.lua`), and the `ScopeTable` and a tracked `WriteSession` as `tests/fsx_scope.rs` builds them (`Writer::Mutating`; `Writer::Doctor` where a cell writes under `<config>`). A variant `linked_home()` reaches the same tree through `<root>/link-home`, a symlink to `<root>/real-home`, as `mutate.rs`'s `Fixture::through_a_linked_home` does.
3. **`every_predicate_part_refuses_its_own_change`**: a table of 17 cells `(name, op, endpoint, predicate, change)`, each run as one `TestLog` step group. `preconditions()` runs the op's own rules before the predicates (a rename of a missing path is "does not exist", a no-replace rename onto an existing path is "the rename target exists", a `SymlinkAtomic` over a non-link is refused, `mutate.rs:634-670`), and `normalize` refuses a rename of a final symlink (`mutate.rs:610-615`; E5 adds the one exception later). So each cell is chosen so that the op's own rules pass and the predicate is what refuses:

   | Cell | Op | Endpoint | Predicate | Change between capture and operate |
   |---|---|---|---|---|
   | `write_identity` | `WriteFile` | path | identity | the file replaced by a copy with the same bytes and mode |
   | `write_sha256` | `WriteFile` | path | `Expect::hash` | `aaaa` → `aaab`, mtime put back |
   | `write_mode` | `WriteFile` | path | mode 0644 | chmod to 0600 |
   | `write_absent` | `WriteFile` | path | `Absent` | the file created by another writer |
   | `write_present` | `WriteFile` | path | `Present(default)` | the file removed |
   | `chmod_identity` | `Chmod 0600` | path | identity + mode 0644 | a same-mode replacement file (M4-D31's credential case) |
   | `chmod_mode` | `Chmod 0600` | path | identity + mode 0644 | the mode already changed to 0640 |
   | `noreplace_from_identity` | `Rename NoReplace` | from | identity (directory) | the folder replaced by a same-named copy (D8's "a folder replaced in the last moment") |
   | `noreplace_from_stamp` | `Rename NoReplace` | from | stamp | a file added inside the folder |
   | `noreplace_from_type` | `Rename NoReplace` | from | file type `Directory` | the folder replaced by a regular file |
   | `replace_to_absent` | `Rename Replace` | to | `Absent` (`expect_to`) | the destination created (the shape of the swap's plain-rename fallback, `swap.rs:857-869`) |
   | `exchange_to_identity` | `Rename Exchange` | to | identity (`expect_to`) | the destination folder replaced by a same-named copy |
   | `exchange_from_identity` | `Rename Exchange` | from | identity | the source folder replaced |
   | `replace_to_sha256` | `Rename Replace` | to | `Expect::hash` (`expect_to`) | the destination file edited, same size |
   | `symlink_link_target` | `SymlinkAtomic` on a link under `<state>` | path | file type `Symlink` + link target | the link retargeted (the shape of E8's `latest` retarget) |
   | `write_identity_renumbered_device_still_refuses_another_file` | `WriteFile` | path | identity with `dev` rewritten | the file replaced (a device rewrite never excuses another inode) |
   | `destination_predicate_on_a_write` | `WriteFile` | path | `expect_to: Absent` | none (refused: a destination predicate needs a rename) |

   Each cell: build the subject; `Expect::capture(path, parts)` (or the literal predicate); `log.tree("subject", root)` and record `FileId::of` of every endpoint; apply the change; `log.tree("changed", root)`; run `mutate_with` with the predicate as `expect` or `expect_to`; assert `Err(FsxError::Precondition(msg))` with `msg` naming the endpoint path and containing that part's message (s3's table); assert `log.assert_unchanged("changed", root)` (the refused operation changed nothing after the change), no new line in the session's actions log, nothing new under its snapshot roots, and each endpoint's `FileId` as recorded after the change. Subjects live under the client's `Interface/AddOns` (folders) and under `<state>` (files and the symlink), written as `Writer::Mutating`, which both scope rows admit (`src/fsx/scope.rs:104-130`).
4. **`an_unchanged_path_passes_every_part`**: the same cells without the change (all but `destination_predicate_on_a_write`, 16 cells); each operation succeeds and the actions log gains exactly one line whose `op` is the cell's.
5. **`identity_survives_a_renumbered_device`**: capture folder `X` with identity, set `dev ^= 0x5a5a` in the captured `FileId`, rename `X` to a sibling with `expect` = that predicate and `expect_to: Absent`: it succeeds. (The plan's "a test that rewrites `dev`": bind mounts keep the device number, `tests/common/mounts.rs`, so a real remount cannot be staged without privileges.)
6. **`a_rename_checks_both_endpoints`**: an exchange of folders `X` and `Y` with both identities captured, `Y` then replaced by a same-named copy: refused, the message naming `Y`'s path; afterwards `X` and the replacement `Y` are where they were (`FileId`s and tree hash). Then the same exchange with fresh captures succeeds and the two trees have swapped.
7. **`resources_canonicalize_as_fsx_normalizes`** on `linked_home()`: for each spelling of a path under the client's `AddOns` (through the link; with `..` through an existing directory; with `.`; with a trailing slash), `Resource::canonical(p, PathKind::File)` is computed first, then a `WriteFile` on the same spelling (spelled without `..`, which `mutate()` refuses) runs in a tracked session; assert `resource.path().to_str() == Some(record.path.as_str())` and `resource.overlaps_path(Path::new(&record.path))`. For a final symlink (`<state>/latest-like → somewhere`), a `SymlinkAtomic` on it logs the link's own path, and the resource equals it (the final component never followed).
8. **`conflicts_hold_across_spellings`** on `linked_home()`: a set that writes `Subtree` `<real home>/x` (a quarantine spelled through the real path) conflicts with a set that writes `File` `<linked home>/x/y`, and does not conflict with one that writes `<linked home>/xy`; the `Conflict` names both canonical resources.
9. **The regression run, recorded** (no new code): run and record in the close comment, with pass counts:
   - `cargo test --locked --test engine_crash --test journal --test fsx_scope --test fsx_prune --test backup_export --test restore --test restore_addon --test restore_undo --test engine_undo --test engine_concurrency`;
   - `cargo test --locked --lib -- fsx:: engine::`;
   - `argc e2e fsx_predicates` (T1's runner, verbose logs), quoting the log root it prints; where the runner does not pick this suite up (it lists the suites marked end to end), `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG=verbose cargo test --locked --test fsx_predicates -- --nocapture` instead.
   Every crash matrix passes unchanged and no snapshot is re-accepted (`git status` shows no `.snap` change).

**Files:** `tests/fsx_predicates.rs` (new). Nothing under `src/` changes in this part; if a cell finds a defect in s1 or s3, fix it in this commit when it is small, or reopen that subtask (or file a bug `discovered-from` this one) and block on it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `tests/fsx_predicates.rs` exists and passes in the gate, with the scenes `every_predicate_part_refuses_its_own_change`, `an_unchanged_path_passes_every_part`, `identity_survives_a_renumbered_device`, `a_rename_checks_both_endpoints`, `resources_canonicalize_as_fsx_normalizes` and `conflicts_hold_across_spellings`.
- [ ] Every cell of the matrix is refused with `FsxError::Precondition` naming its endpoint and part, and a refused cell leaves the tree, the actions log, the snapshot roots and every endpoint's identity as they were after the change.
- [ ] Every cell passes when nothing changed, logging exactly one action.
- [ ] A rewritten device number never refuses the same file and never excuses another one.
- [ ] For every spelling, `Resource::canonical`'s path equals the `ActionRecord.path` `mutate()` logs, and a quarantine spelled through the real home conflicts with a write into its child spelled through the symlinked home.
- [ ] The regression run passes unchanged (the listed suites and the `fsx::` and `engine::` unit tests), with its pass counts and `argc e2e`'s log root in the close comment; no snapshot changes.
- [ ] Each scene writes `steps.jsonl` and `transcript.md` under `<CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR>/test-logs/fsx_predicates/<test>/`, with the steps listed under Logging.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the new file; `br lint` is clean for this subtask.
- [ ] If this is the last open subtask: every acceptance criterion of `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.13` is verified and the leaf is closed with its evidence.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

None new in this part: s1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.13.1`) and s3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.13.3`) carry the unit and property tests of their code.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

`tests/fsx_predicates.rs`, as in the Technical Approach (steps 3–8): six scenes on a synthetic home built from `tempfile` and `Paths::with_roots` (never the developer's real `HOME`), using only the public API. No binary is run: the leaf has no command surface, and no command uses `Present` predicates until D8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8`, the approval checked again under the commit lock) and E5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`, the repair transaction) land. No contract matrix row, snapshot, crash failpoint or concurrency case is added: the leaf has no protocol of its own, and its consumers' matrices (D8's witness scenarios, E5's repair crash matrix, the fence cases of E14, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14`, fences and activation barriers) exercise these predicates under crashes and races.

The regression run (step 9) is this part's evidence for "every existing `Expect` test and crash matrix passes unchanged".

### Logging

Every scene uses the `TestLog` of T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs and the `argc e2e` runner), as `TestLog::new("fsx_predicates", "<test name>")`:

- per matrix cell: `log.step("<cell>: build")`; `log.note` of the predicate (`{:?}`; the types are not `Serialize`) and of each endpoint's `FileId`; `log.tree("subject", root)`; `log.step("<cell>: change")` with a note saying what changed; `log.tree("changed", root)`; `log.step("<cell>: operate")` with `log.json("result", json!({"ok": false, "error": "<FsxError Display>", "part": "<expected part>"}))`; `log.assert_unchanged("changed", root)`, which logs the first differing paths on failure; `log.json("actions_lines", json!({"before": n, "after": m}))`;
- the canonicalization scene: one step per spelling with `log.json("spelling", json!({"input": …, "resource": resource.text(), "action_path": record.path}))`;
- the conflict scene: `log.json("conflicts", …)` with each `Conflict`'s two resources as text.

Paths are logged relative to the temp root. A failing scene prints `test log: <path>` and its last 20 steps; `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG=verbose` (with `--nocapture`, or through `argc e2e`) echoes every step live.

## Considerations

- **Library-level, not binary-level.** M4's end-to-end suites run the binary; this one cannot, because nothing user-visible uses the new predicates yet. It uses `TestLog` anyway, because a 33-cell matrix (17 refused, 16 passing) is exactly where a failure needs its steps. Decided while writing this bead: this suite sets `uses_test_log`, so T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs) blocks it.
- **Birth times.** On a filesystem without birth times (the system temp dir, where `tempfile` puts test homes, is often a tmpfs), identity is decided by inode alone; the replacement cells still differ by inode, so they hold everywhere. Cells that depend on birth time are s3's unit cases, which branch as the journal's test does.
- **Kernel tick.** A mode change or a rewrite in the same kernel timestamp tick as the capture still changes the predicate's parts that do not depend on time (mode, content, identity). The `stamp` cell adds a file, which changes the entry list regardless of the clock.
- **Privacy.** Synthetic homes only; no `WTF/` content is written by the matrix (the client's `WTF/` exists only so the scope table is realistic), so `assert_private_all` is not needed; logs hold paths relative to the temp root.
- **Hot spots.** None: a new test file.

## Dependencies

- **Parent:** `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.13` (Resource sets and fsx endpoint predicates).
- **Before it:** s1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.13.1`, the resource model) for the canonicalization and conflict scenes; s3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.13.3`, the endpoint predicates) for the matrix. s2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.13.2`) comes in through s3.
- **Also blocked by** T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs and the `argc e2e` runner), an edge added at filing because this part writes an integration suite that uses `TestLog`.
- **After it:** nothing inside the leaf; closing this part (if last) closes `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.13`, which unblocks D8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8`, the approval checked again under the commit lock), E5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`, the repair transaction), E14 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14`, fences and activation barriers) and T3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.3`, slice 2 end to end).

title: Fences and activation barriers
description:
## How to work this bead

This bead is worked through its 5 subtasks, listed below in work order. Claim a subtask, not this bead (`br ready --parent omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14` lists the ready ones). The agent that closes the last open subtask then verifies every acceptance criterion of this bead (they are the leaf's, not any one subtask's), and closes this bead with `br close omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14 --reason "done: <evidence> · found: <ids>"`. ## Background

Beads this section names: E14 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14`, this leaf), E1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`, the repair action model), E5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`, the repair transaction), E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`, `doctor fix`), E9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9`, the M3 build against M4 state), E7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7`, undo of repairs), E8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.8`, `doctor gc`), E11 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.11`, `journal::diagnose`), E13 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.13`, resource sets and fsx endpoint predicates), F2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.2`, journal fixers: the delegation and the set-aside), H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the M4 checkpoint) and the milestone epic (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`).

**What this leaf is.** M4 adds a second journal family: a doctor repair is one engine transaction of kind `repair`, journaled in `<state>/journal/<tx>.repair.jsonl` as an ordered list of primitive steps (`WriteFile`, `Chmod`, `RenameNoReplace`), each with endpoint predicates, and recovered by every lock-taking command (E5). Two things are still missing before that family is safe to live beside the folder journals, and this leaf adds both:

1. **Fences.** A repair journal that recovery cannot settle (a recorded primitive whose live paths match neither its `pre` nor its `post` predicate) stays on disk. A repair has no target, so the per-target isolation that protects folder journals (a stuck journal fails only commands on its own target, `src/engine/journal.rs:822-844`) does not apply. Without a fence, `auth github set` could rewrite the very credential a stuck chmod repair would put back on rollback, or a skill install could overwrite the file a stuck rewrite backed up. With a fence on everything, one stuck chmod would block every client. A fence refuses exactly the writes that overlap what the stuck journal protects, at the one writer (`mutate()`), and lets everything else proceed. A repair journal whose `prepared` line cannot be read has unknowable resources, and fails every committing command closed until a set-aside moves it.
2. **Activation barriers and recovery's order.** F2's set-aside suspends a stuck journal set by moving its artifacts into quarantine, and E7's undo of that set-aside reactivates it by moving them back. A reactivation that crashes after the journal file is back but before the undo's durable `done` must be rolled back as a whole, provisional name included, before ordinary recovery may touch the journal it exposed. Today recovery runs folder journals first (and, after E5, repair journals after them), which is exactly the wrong order for a reactivation: the next lock-taking command would recover the restored folder journal ahead of the undo that exposed it, and the undo's own rollback would then fail on a journal file that recovery had already pruned, leaving a mixture of before and after. This leaf restores the journal under a provisional name that recovery does not list (`<tx>.reactivating.jsonl`), makes the activation the undo's last primitive, and makes recovery run three passes: repairs that own a suspension or an activation first, then folder journals (skipping any whose transaction an unsettled pass-1 repair names), then the remaining repairs.

It was added by the plan's second review round, split out of E5 so that E5's leaf stays one protocol (the repair journal, its commit and its per-journal recovery), and so that E7 (the activation-aware inverse) and F2 (the set-aside) build on settled fences and barriers.

The guarded repair of the stuck states is F2's set-aside, and its undo is E7's reactivation; both are safe only with this leaf's barrier. A stuck repair that fences only what it protects keeps every other client usable while the user reads `doctor explain`.

**The decisions that shape it** (full text in the decision-log comments on the milestone epic `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`):

- **M4-D62, one canonical resource model; fences are enforced at the one writer.** `engine::resource` (E13) defines `Resource` (a canonical path that stands for a file or a whole subtree, or a named resource: a journal by tx, a target record by key, a backup input by run and sequence) and `ResourceSet` (reads and writes; two sets conflict when one's writes overlap the other's reads or writes; two paths overlap when one is the other or an ancestor of it). The same sets drive fixer conflicts (E6), **fences (this leaf)**, undo's conflicts (E7) and gc's pins (E8). For fences: "a stuck, readable repair journal refuses only the mutations whose write sets overlap its protected resources, which are its primitives' writes, the backups its rollback reads, and, for a suspension, the suspended journal's target and the resources that journal would recover. Every other command, client and path keeps working." "Each command loads the fences once, from `journal::diagnose`'s repair-family verdicts, into its `ScopeTable` (`with_fences`). `mutate()` refuses an operation whose path overlaps a fenced resource. The command fails with the fencing journal's own stop error (the code and `details.reason` its state has, plus `details.tx` and `details.resource`) and the fix `omaddons doctor explain <fm>`." "When the set cannot be read, fail closed": a repair journal with no complete first line protects nothing (by write-ahead no primitive ran, and recovery prunes it as unstarted); a complete `prepared` line that does not decode, or declares a newer major format, "fails every committing command, exactly as a folder journal with no readable target does (`journal.rs:843`), until its set-aside (whose own resources are known) moves it. `targets: []` is never evidence that home-side writes are safe." *Why:* an unresolved target-less repair can collide with `auth github set` or a skill install, and the reviewed draft, which warned every command and blocked only named targets, left exactly those home-side resources unprotected. *Rejected:* (i) exact-path comparison (it misses ancestors, descendants and rename destinations); (ii) blocking the whole machine for any stuck repair (one stuck chmod would block every client); (iii) trusting `targets: []` from an unreadable journal.
- **M4-D38, the set-aside is suspension, and its undo reactivates only behind an activation barrier.** F2's fixer moves the journal set (the journal file, its in-flight lock file, its state snapshot half, its client stage and snapshot halves) into quarantine, one `RenameNoReplace` primitive per artifact, and records a suspension manifest as the primitives' `guards` (each artifact's identity and stamp, the target's key, the client marker's digest, the target's record generation, the stamps of the folders the suspended journal would touch, and for a WTF journal one digest of the `WTF/` tree's stamps, never a path below it). E7's `doctor undo` of a set-aside checks every guard under the lock and refuses with `undo_conflict` (`changed_since_suspension`) if anything moved. **The barrier (this leaf's part):** "The undo restores every artifact but the journal file first, and restores the journal under a provisional name ordinary recovery does not list (`<tx>.reactivating.jsonl`, which `tx_named` cannot parse). Its last primitive, the activation, renames it to its own name. Recovery resolves the repair that owns a barrier before it considers ordinary journals, and never recovers a journal behind an unresolved barrier. So a crash anywhere in a reactivation, including after the activation and before the undo's durable `done`, can never let the folder pass run the restored journal ahead of the undo that exposed it: before `done` the undo rolls back, provisional name included, and from `done` on the journal is an ordinary pending journal again." *Why:* restoring the journal last does not close the crash window by itself, because folder recovery ran before repair recovery. *Rejected:* (iv) unconditional restore (the reviewed draft): it activates stale instructions after later work, and had this crash window. Within the undo, this leaf orders the journal's provisional rename first, as M4-D46 writes it ("provisional name first, activation last"), for the orphan-sweep reason given in §6 of the Technical Approach.
- **M4-D31, a repair is one engine transaction of a second journal family.** Its `prepared` line records `targets[]`, `client_dirs[]`, `resources{reads[], writes[]}` (the union of the steps' sets, "what a fence protects if this journal is ever stuck"), `fixes[]` and `primitives[]` (`{seq, fix, fm, op, path, to?, mode?, pre, post, backup?, activation?, guards?}`), then one write-ahead `step {seq}` line before each primitive, `done` after the last primitive and the commit window's barrier, the history line, then `committed` (`rolled_back` replaces `done` and `committed` on an in-process rollback). Recovery before `done` rolls back by inverses in reverse, from `done` on rolls forward. **"Ordering. Recovery first resolves the repairs that own a suspension or an activation barrier (M4-D38), then folder journals, then the remaining repair journals, and never recovers a journal behind an unresolved barrier."** Only `engine/repair.rs` parses repair journal names; `paths::tx_named` stays unchanged, so builds before M4 never see `.repair` names.
- **M4-D46, a repair is undone strictly, as a new repair transaction.** "An activation-sensitive rename (a suspended journal file) is inverted through the activation barrier: provisional name first, activation last." E7 builds that inverse; this leaf defines the activation primitive, its validation and recovery's handling of it.
- **M3-D45, what this build cannot read, it never acts on.** A journal of a newer major format, or with a complete line that does not decode, is left whole. For the repair family this leaf adds the consequence for everyone else: since its resources are unknowable, nothing may write anything (the closed fence), and recovery may run no other journal behind it (it might be a barrier).
- **M4-D36 (context), gc deletes only through a dependency-aware plan.** E8's reachability pins include "barriers and fences": this leaf's protected sets and barrier ownership are what E8 reads.

### 2. Fences at the one writer (s1)

**Types**, in a new `src/fsx/fence.rs` (`mod fence;` and `pub use fence::{Fence, FenceSet, FenceStop, Fenced};` in `src/fsx/mod.rs`). Decided while writing this bead: fsx holds only canonical paths and the refusal to report, because fsx must not depend on `engine` (see Facts); the engine translates resources into fence paths (s2).

```rust
/// What a write refused by a fence reports: the fencing journal's own stop (M4-D62).
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct FenceStop {
    pub tx: Option<TxId>,            // the fencing journal; None only for an unlistable journal directory
    pub target: Option<TargetKey>,   // that journal's target; None for a repair
    pub code: ErrorCode,             // its stop code
    pub reason: Option<&'static str>, // its stop reason (StopReason::as_str()); None for a recovery that failed on I/O, which has none
    pub summary: String,             // e.g. "repair transaction 01M9… did not finish, and recovery could not settle it (step_unrecognized)"
    pub fix: Suggestion,             // omaddons doctor explain <fm> (s2)
}

/// One protected canonical path. It stands for itself and, when a directory, everything below it.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Fence { pub path: PathBuf, pub resource: String, pub stop: FenceStop }

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct FenceSet { fences: Vec<Fence>, closed: Option<(String, FenceStop)> }

pub enum FencedOp<'a> { CreateDir(&'a Path), Write(&'a Path), Rename { from: &'a Path, to: &'a Path } }

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct Fenced { pub resource: String, pub stop: FenceStop, pub closed: bool }

impl FenceSet {
    pub fn new() -> Self;
    pub fn fence(&mut self, path: PathBuf, resource: String, stop: FenceStop); // path canonical and absolute (debug_assert)
    pub fn close(&mut self, resource: String, stop: FenceStop);                // the lowest tx wins, so the result is deterministic
    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool;
    pub fn is_closed(&self) -> bool;
    pub fn txs(&self) -> BTreeSet<TxId>;                                       // every fencing journal, the closed one included
    pub fn covering(&self, path: &Path) -> Option<&Fence>;                     // the first fence that overlaps `path`
    pub fn check(&self, op: FencedOp<'_>) -> Result<(), Fenced>;
    pub fn excusing(&self, txs: &BTreeSet<TxId>) -> Self;                      // without the fences (and the close) of these journals
}
```

- `fences` is kept sorted by `(path, tx)` and deduplicated, so the fence a refusal names is the same on every run (§8.1 default 3). No `HashMap` or `HashSet` (M4-D18).
- **Overlap**, by whole path components (`Path::starts_with`): a path overlaps a fence when it is the fence's path, an ancestor of it, or a descendant of it. `<root>/a/b` and `<root>/a/bc` do not overlap. This is E13's `Resource::overlaps` rule, re-stated in fsx on canonical paths (a unit test cross-checks the two on the same table of cases).
- **`check`**:

  | Operation (from `Op`) | Refused when |
  |---|---|
  | `CreateDir(p)` | the set is closed; or `p` is a fence's path or below one. A missing `p` that is a strict ancestor of a fence's path is allowed: creating an empty directory above a protected path changes nothing at or below it, and `ensure_dir_all` issues `CreateDir` only for missing directories |
  | `Write(p)` (`WriteFile`, `AppendFile`, `CloneFile`'s target, `Chmod`, `SymlinkAtomic`) | the set is closed; or `p` overlaps a fence's path (equal, ancestor or descendant): a `Chmod` of `credentials/` is a write over the credential below it |
  | `Rename { from, to }` | the set is closed; or `from` or `to` overlaps a fence's path |

  A `CloneFile`'s source is read, never written, and is not checked. Decided while writing this bead: the `CreateDir` exception, because without it a fence on a path under a missing parent would refuse unrelated commands that create the parent, which risk 21 ("too wide blocks unrelated work") warns against, and it can never change the protected path.
- **`ScopeTable`** (`src/fsx/scope.rs`) gains a `fences: FenceSet` field (empty from `ScopeTable::new`, so every existing caller is unchanged), `pub fn with_fences(mut self, fences: FenceSet) -> Self`, `pub fn fences(&self) -> &FenceSet` and `pub fn without_fences(&self) -> Self` (a clone with an empty set, for recovery, s3). The derives stay.
- **`mutate_with`** (`src/fsx/mutate.rs`): in step 1, after the target's and the destination's scope checks and before the durability check, `preconditions` and `fsx.mutate.checked`, call `s.scopes.fences().check(op)` and return `FsxError::Fenced(Box<Fenced>)` on refusal. So a fenced write touches nothing: no before-digest, no backup, no execution, no actions line, and `fsx.mutate.checked` is not hit. Decided while writing this bead: the check sits after the scope check (an out-of-scope path is a programming error and should surface as `scope_denied`) and before the preconditions (a fenced path's state is not this command's business). No failpoint moves.
- **`prune`** (`src/fsx/prune.rs`): `classify` gains a third outcome. A victim the table's fences cover (or every victim, when the set is closed) is not planned and is reported in `PruneReport.skipped` with the reason `"fenced by transaction <tx>"` (or `"every change is refused: <reason>"`). Never an error: retention, cleanup and gc prune best effort, and a protected victim must simply stay. A prune that skipped a victim this way still prunes the others.
- **The error** (`From<FsxError> for Error`): `Error::new(stop.code, message, stop.fix).details(json!({"journal_pending": stop.tx, "reason": stop.reason, "target": stop.target, "tx": stop.tx, "resource": resource}))` (`reason` omitted when the stop has none: a recovery that failed on I/O; every text then shows the code in its parentheses), retryable as its code is (every stop code is non-retryable). The message is `"<summary>; it protects <resource>, so omaddons does not write it"`, or for a closed set `"<summary>; every change is refused until it is set aside"`. It never names the path the command tried to write, only the fenced resource, which is never below a `WTF/` (s2 guarantees it), so no account, realm or character name can appear (common rule 9).
- Decided while writing this bead: the details are the fencing journal's own stop details as E11 gives every recovery stop (`journal_pending`, `reason`, `target`) plus the plan's `tx` and `resource`; `journal_pending` equals `tx` here and is kept so consumers that already branch on it see the journal.

### 3. What a stuck repair protects (s2)

`engine::fence::protected(prepared: &RepairPrepared, paths: &Paths) -> ResourceSet` returns the write set nothing else may touch while that repair is unsettled. Its reads stay empty. It is the one rule; E5's repair arm of `journal::diagnose` uses it for `JournalDiagnosis.protected` (s2 replaces whatever E5 computed there, so fences and E8's pins cannot disagree):

1. **Its primitives' writes:** every resource in `prepared.resources.writes()` (E5 records the union: a write's or a chmod's path; a rename's `from` and `to`).
2. **The backups its rollback reads:** for every overwriting `WriteFile`, its reserved backup path (`primitive.backup`: `<run>/backups/<seq>` home side, `<meta>/snapshots/<tx>.repair/files/<seq>` client side) as a file path resource, plus `Resource::Backup { run_dir: prepared.doctor_run_id, seq }` (named; E8 reads it as a pin, the fence translation ignores it).
3. **For a repair that owns a barrier** (`barrier::of(prepared).is_some()`, below): every key in `prepared.targets` as `Resource::Record(key)` ("the suspended journal's target"); and from every primitive's `guards`: `Epoch { path, .. }` → the path as a subtree (a folder the suspended journal would recover), `WtfEpoch { target, .. }` → `<client dir of that target in prepared.client_dirs>/WTF` as a subtree, `Generation { target, .. }` and `Marker { target, .. }` → `Resource::Record(target)`.

**Barrier classification** (`src/engine/barrier.rs`, new; s2 adds `of`, s3 the rest):

```rust
pub enum BarrierKind { Suspension, Activation }
pub struct Barrier { pub kind: BarrierKind, pub names: BTreeSet<TxId> }
pub fn of(prepared: &RepairPrepared, paths: &Paths) -> Option<Barrier>;
```

- **Activation:** any primitive with `activation: true`.
- **Suspension:** otherwise, any `RenameNoReplace` whose `from` is a journal file in `<state>/journal/` under its own name (`<tx>.jsonl`, `<tx>.wtf.jsonl` or `<tx>.repair.jsonl`). Decided while writing this bead: the plan's wording is "guards on a rename of a journal file out of `<state>/journal/`"; the rule here is the rename alone, because a suspension of a journal with no readable target (F2's `journal-unattributed` row, "state side only") may carry no guard at all, and a suspension that recovery failed to put first would be exactly the crash window M4-D38 closes. Guards remain what E7 checks.
- **`names`:** the transaction of every journal file a primitive moves (`from` or `to` under `<state>/journal/`, any of the four names), and of every artifact it moves in the known locations (`<state>/inflight/<tx>.lock`, `<state>/snapshots/<tx>` and `<tx>.wtf`, `<meta>/stage/<tx>` and `<tx>.wtf`, `<meta>/snapshots/<tx>` and `<tx>.wtf` for the prepared's `client_dirs`), never the repair's own. These are the journals behind the barrier.
- Journal file names are parsed only in `engine/repair.rs` (M4-D31): s2 adds `repair::journal_file(path) -> Option<(TxId, JournalName)>` with `JournalName::{Folder, Wtf, Repair, Reactivating}`, and `repair::provisional_journal(paths, tx) -> PathBuf` (`<state>/journal/<tx>.reactivating.jsonl`). Folder artifact names (`<tx>`, `<tx>.wtf`, `<tx>.lock`) are read with the existing `paths::tx_named`.

**Translating a protected set into fence paths** (`fence::paths_of`), each with its E13 text for `details.resource`:

| Resource | Fence paths |
|---|---|
| `Path { path, kind }` | the path itself (recorded canonical: `Resource::from_canonical`/`parse`, never re-resolved, because a symlink may have changed since) |
| `Record(key)` | `paths.target_record(key)` and `paths.files_index(key)`, canonicalized with `fsx::canonical_lenient` |
| `Journal(tx)` | `<state>/journal/<tx>.jsonl`, `<tx>.wtf.jsonl`, `<tx>.repair.jsonl`, `<tx>.reactivating.jsonl` and `<state>/inflight/<tx>.lock` |
| `Backup { .. }` | none (rule 2 adds its path form) |

- **Never a fence path:** `<state>/history.jsonl` (and `net.log`). History is append-only and shared; a pending roll-forward appends its own line once (`append_once`, which looks for its tx in the raw text), whatever others appended meanwhile. A fence on it would refuse every commit on every client, the "too wide" half of risk 21. A swapped folder journal's protected set (E11) names it; the translation drops it, with a unit test.
- **Privacy:** a path with a `WTF` (or `WTF.previous`) component below a client dir is cut after that component (as E11 does for protected paths), so no fence path, resource text or message names anything below `WTF/`. A unit test asserts it over every translation case.

### 4. Loading the fences, and who carries them (s2)

**`engine::fence::load(paths: &Paths, client_dirs: &[PathBuf]) -> FenceSet`** calls `journal::diagnose(paths, client_dirs, &journal::no_saved_variables)` (conservative: a WTF journal then counts as waiting, which can only add fences) and maps each diagnosis:

| Diagnosis | Fences |
|---|---|
| `live` (its writer holds its in-flight lock) | none: a live transaction is in progress, and its commit window holds the global lock |
| repair, `Recoverable { .. }` | none: the next lock-taking command settles it |
| repair, a stop (`expected()` is `Stops`), whose `prepared` line decodes (`repair::read_prepared(&d.path)` is `Decoded`: `StepUnrecognized`, a `MarkerMismatch` of its `client_dirs`, or an undecodable *later* line) | `paths_of(protected(prepared))`, each with this journal's own stop |
| repair, a stop whose `prepared` line is complete but does not decode, or declares a newer major format | `close(journal:<tx>, its own stop)` |
| repair, no complete first line | none (it protects nothing; recovery prunes it as unstarted) |
| any family, `BehindBarrier { owner }` whose owner has a stop (s3) | `paths_of(d.protected)`, each with the owner's stop ("fenced with that repair"); behind a live, unfinished owner, none |
| a folder journal otherwise | none: the per-target rule (a stuck journal fails its own target's commits) already protects it, as today |
| `Diagnoses.unlisted` (the journal directory exists and cannot be listed) | `close(<state>/journal, {tx: None, code: io, reason: "unattributed"})` |

Decided while writing this bead: `repair::read_prepared` (E5's decoder for the first line, returning `Decoded(RepairPrepared) | Undecodable | TooNew | Absent`) decides between a path fence and a closed set, rather than a new field on `JournalDiagnosis`, because only stuck repair journals are read a second time and E11's type stays as E11 and E5 left it. A decodable `prepared` whose later line does not decode is left whole by recovery (M3-D45), yet its resources are known, so it gets path fences, not a closed set (the plan's "unknowable" is about the `prepared` line).

**`FenceStop` of a diagnosis** (`fence::stop_of(&JournalDiagnosis) -> Option<FenceStop>`): `code` and `reason` from `expected()`'s `Stops`, `tx`, `target` (none for a repair), the `summary` (the texts of §5 below without their `; …` tail) and `fix: fence::explain_fix(reason)`.

**`fence::explain_fix(reason)`** is `Suggestion::command(["omaddons", "doctor", "explain", fm])` with the failure mode of the state:

| `reason` | `fm` |
|---|---|
| `step_unrecognized` | `fm-concurrency_primitives-journal-step-unrecognized` |
| `unexpected_state` | `fm-concurrency_primitives-journal-unexpected-state` |
| `journal_too_new` | `fm-concurrency_primitives-journal-too-new` |
| `journal_unreadable` | `fm-concurrency_primitives-journal-unreadable` |
| `marker_mismatch` | `fm-concurrency_primitives-journal-marker-mismatch` |
| `unattributed` | `fm-concurrency_primitives-journal-unattributed` |
| `preservation_incomplete` | `fm-concurrency_primitives-journal-preservation-incomplete` |
| `saved_variables` | `fm-concurrency_primitives-journal-waits-for-game` |
| none (recovery itself failed on I/O; the next lock-taking command retries) | `fm-concurrency_primitives-journal-pending` |

No `-t`: a repair has no target, and `doctor explain <fm>` lists every instance. Decided while writing this bead: if E3's `doctor explain` is not in `app::COMMANDS` when s2 lands, `explain_fix` returns `omaddons status` (the fix every recovery stop has today), and the agent files a bead `discovered-from` this one, blocked by E3, that switches the one function and makes s4's `doctor` assertion unconditional; the unit test `explain_fix_parses` pins whichever is in force. The `fm` ids are the catalog's journal rows (Appendix B rows 1–9: row 1, `journal-pending`, is published since M3; rows 2–9 are F1's); until F1 registers rows 2–9, `doctor explain` answers `not_found` with the closest id, which is acceptable for a state this rare and is fixed by F1 in the same slice.

**Who carries the fences.** `engine::fence::table(paths, client_dirs, skill_dir) -> Result<ScopeTable>` is `ScopeTable::new(..)?.with_fences(load(paths, client_dirs))`. Every production table that a mutating command writes its subject with is built through it (s2 changes each call site by hand):

**Dry runs and read commands.** A dry run of an engine command plans with the run's table, so a fence refuses its writes too: with path fences only a dry run that would write a protected path (a fenced cache blob) fails, and with a closed set every engine dry run fails at its first cache write, saying why and naming the fix. Read commands (`status`, `list`, `history`, `info`, `outdated`, `doctor`) use unfenced tables for their derived data and always run. Decided while writing this bead: a dry run is not exempted, because an exemption would need a second table for the same run, and a preview of a change that cannot be applied is better refused with the reason.

The line numbers are as of `c0ab5e9` and drift; the scan test keys on files, not lines. **The scan test**, `engine::fence::tests::every_mutating_scope_table_carries_fences`, reads every production source with `crate::source_scan::{sources, production_code}` and counts `ScopeTable::new(` per file. Every occurrence must be `fence::table`'s own, or listed in a `const UNFENCED: &[(&str /*file*/, usize /*count*/, &str /*reason*/)]` beside the test. A new unlisted occurrence fails with: "a new write-scope table in <file>: build it with `engine::fence::table` (a mutating command's subject writes), or add it to UNFENCED with its reason (derived data, recovery, own-transaction cleanup, the doctor runtime)". So a leaf landing after this one (B3, D4, E3, F*) that adds a table must classify it.

**Why a command that built its table before its lock still refuses correctly: the under-lock gate.** The engine builds its table at the start of a run (before staging, outside the lock). A repair that becomes stuck after that (a crash in another process, then this command's own recovery failing on it) is not in the table. **`engine::fence::under_lock(scopes: &ScopeTable, paths: &Paths, target: Option<&Target>, writes: &[PathBuf]) -> Result<()>`**, called right after recovery and `refuse_newer_state` under the lock, before the first write:

1. `let now = load(paths, scopes.client_dirs())`. Any fencing journal in `now.txs()` that `scopes.fences().txs()` lacks, or `now` closed while the table is not, refuses with that journal's stop (`resource` `journal:<tx>`, the summary plus "it could not be settled after this command started, so the command changes nothing"), the lowest tx first. Fences the table holds that `now` lacks (a repair this command's recovery just settled) only over-protect this one command, which fails closed.
2. If `target` has a key: when the table's fences cover its record or files index (`Record(key)`, a barrier owner's target, s2 rule 3), refuse with that fence. A commit on a suspended or reactivating journal's target is refused before its journal is written, not at the record save after its swap.
3. Each path in `writes` that a fence covers refuses with that fence. The callers pass what they will write first-hand: the commit window the live folders of its planned swap (`<client dir>/Interface/AddOns/<folder>` for each of `planned_folders`, `src/engine/tx.rs:1011`); undo the folders it puts back and `<client dir>/WTF` when it restores SavedVariables; whole and `--addon` restores `<client dir>/WTF`; `register_early` the registry file and the client's marker (`<meta>/target.json`).
4. A closed table refuses.

Call sites (each right after `refuse_newer_state` or recovery under the lock): `src/engine/tx.rs:1047` and `:770`, `src/engine/undo.rs:417`, `src/engine/restore.rs:773`, `src/engine/restore_addons.rs:777`. Decided while writing this bead: a refreshed check at the one gate, not a table that recovery mutates (an interior-mutable fence set inside `ScopeTable` would make every borrowed table change under its sessions), and not a failure inside `recover_all` (whose `recover_under` callers turn errors into warnings and build their tables after recovery, so they always load fresh). Commands that take the lock and then build their table (`auth`, `config`, `targets`, E5's repair commit) need no gate: their `fence::table` runs after their recovery. The checks 2 and 3 make a refusal happen before the journal, where the mutate-level refusal (the backstop) would come only after a swap had to be rolled back. Decided while writing this bead: no pre-lock gate; a closed set refuses the first staging write anyway, and the authoritative check is under the lock.

### 5. The `journal_pending` warnings, and every command's view (s2, s3)

"Every command also gets one `journal_pending` warning per stuck repair." One function per text, used by the reader (`journal::pending_warnings`, which every `World::load` calls) and by recovery (`recover_all`), so the two are equal and `Notes::warn_all` keeps one:

| State | Text (`WarningCode::JournalPending`, fix `explain_fix(reason)`) | Subtask |
|---|---|---|
| a readable repair that recovery cannot settle | `repair transaction <tx> did not finish, and recovery could not settle it (<reason>); writes to what it protects are refused, and everything else proceeds` | s2 |
| a repair whose `prepared` cannot be read | `repair transaction <tx> did not finish, and this omaddons cannot read what it changed (<reason>); every change is refused until it is set aside` | s2 |
| a folder journal behind an unsettled repair | `transaction <tx> on target <t> waits behind repair <owner>, which recovery could not settle (<reason>); it is left as it is` (no ` on target <t>` when the journal has none; for an unreadable owner, `which this omaddons cannot read (<reason>)`) | s3 |
| a repair journal behind an unsettled repair | `repair transaction <tx> waits behind repair <owner>, which recovery could not settle (<reason>); writes to what it protects are refused` | s3 |
| a repair waiting behind a journal pass 2 left unresolved | `repair transaction <tx> waits behind transaction <owner>, which recovery could not settle (<reason>); writes to what it protects are refused` | s3 |

- Each text carries exactly one parenthesized reason, which is how E11's differential reads a warning's outcome ("Stopped { reason } from its `(<reason>)` text").
- `pending_warnings` calls `journal::diagnose(paths, &[], &no_saved_variables)` only when `repair::list` is non-empty (a crashed reactivation always leaves its own repair journal), so `status --cached` (5 ms budget, F8) pays one directory listing as today. If E5 has not already listed repair journals in `journal::pending`, s2 adds them there (readers must see a pending repair: F9's harness asserts that `status` reports `journal_pending` after a crashed repair).
- A recoverable repair keeps E5's text ("did not finish; the next omaddons command that changes … recovers it").

### 6. The activation barrier (s3)

**The provisional name** is `<state>/journal/<tx>.reactivating.jsonl` for every family: the activation's `to` names the journal's own file (`<tx>.jsonl`, `<tx>.wtf.jsonl` or `<tx>.repair.jsonl`), so one spelling suffices. Decided while writing this bead: one spelling, exactly the plan's file name (§7.7), because a second (`<tx>.wtf.reactivating.jsonl`) would be one more name for E9, gc and the attribution to know, for no information the journal does not already carry. It is invisible to everything that lists journals by `tx_named` (see Facts), and `prune()` refuses it, so only renames move it.

**The activation rules**, `barrier::validate(prepared, paths) -> Result<(), String>`:

1. At most one primitive has `activation: true`, and it is the repair's last primitive.
2. It is a `RenameNoReplace` from `repair::provisional_journal(paths, tx)` to `<state>/journal/<tx>.jsonl`, `<tx>.wtf.jsonl` or `<tx>.repair.jsonl` of the same `tx`.
3. Exactly one earlier primitive renames into that provisional name, and it is the **first** primitive of the repair that names `tx`. So the provisional journal exists from the reactivation's first move on.
4. No other primitive renames onto the activation's `to` or out of the provisional name, and no primitive without `activation: true` moves a journal file into `<state>/journal/` under its own name (only an activation exposes a journal). In-process rollback and recovery's inverses are not primitives and are not bound by this rule.

Where it is enforced: E5's `repair::commit` validates before writing `prepared` and refuses a violation with `internal` (`"a repair that reactivates a journal must …"`, naming the rule), and E5's decoder (`read_prepared`, used by recovery and `diagnose`) treats a `prepared` that decodes but violates the rules as undecodable, so it fails closed (M3-D45). E7 builds its activation-aware inverses to satisfy the rules and calls `validate` in its own tests.

Decided while writing this bead: rule 3 (provisional first, activation last) follows M4-D46's "provisional name first, activation last", and closes a race M4-D38's "restores every artifact but the journal file first" would leave open: retention's orphan sweep computes victims without the lock and judges a transaction dead when neither `<tx>.wtf.jsonl` nor `<tx>.jsonl` exists (Facts), and a restored in-flight lock, stage or state snapshot keeps its old modification time, so a sweep that looked between the artifact restores and the journal's restore would later prune what the reactivation had just put back. **With rule 3 and one more line in retention's `dead` test** (`!repair::provisional_journal(paths, tx)` exists, `src/engine/retention.rs:358-360`), a reactivating transaction is never dead to the sweep. F2's set-aside order is F2's; E7 must order the undo by rule 3 rather than simply reversing the set-aside.

`journal::diagnose`'s artifact search (E11's `evidence.artifacts`, found by tx in known locations) also lists `<state>/journal/<tx>.reactivating.jsonl`, kind `Journal`, so F2's attribution and E8's gc see a provisional journal.

### 7. Recovery's three passes (s3)

**The pass planner**, `barrier::Passes`, is the one decision procedure for order, used by `recover_all` with the disk and by `journal::diagnose` with the simulated tree (E11's rule: a decision written twice drifts):

```rust
pub enum Outcome { Settled, Unsettled(FenceStop), Live { finished: bool } }
pub struct ListedRepair { pub tx: TxId, pub prepared: Option<RepairPrepared>, pub live: bool }   // prepared None: unknowable
pub struct Passes { /* owners, the rest, the unknowable, the outcomes so far */ }
impl Passes {
    pub fn new(repairs: Vec<ListedRepair>, paths: &Paths) -> Self;
    pub fn next_owner(&mut self) -> Option<TxId>;                  // pass 1, in naming order
    pub fn record(&mut self, tx: TxId, outcome: Outcome);
    pub fn behind(&self, tx: &TxId) -> Option<TxId>;               // the unsettled repair that names tx (an unknowable one names everything)
    pub fn rest(&self) -> Vec<TxId>;                               // pass 3, in transaction order
    pub fn waits_for(&self, resources: &ResourceSet, unresolved: &[(TxId, ResourceSet)]) -> Option<TxId>; // pass 3's overlap rule
    pub fn stop(&self, owner: &TxId) -> Option<&FenceStop>;        // an unsettled owner's stop, for errors and warnings
}
```

- **Pass 1, repairs that own a barrier** (`barrier::of(prepared).is_some()`). Order: an owner named by another listed owner comes after the one naming it; otherwise in transaction order. A repair can name only journals that existed when it was planned, so this order exists; if a cycle is ever found (it cannot be built by M4 code), every owner in it counts as unsettled, which fails closed. An owner named by an unsettled owner is not recovered: it is behind it. Each owner is recovered by E5's `repair::recover`: `Ok` is settled (rolled back, rolled forward or pruned), `Err` is unsettled with its stop. A live owner is skipped; it counts as settled when its journal is finished (last complete line `committed` or `rolled_back`, which is the only live state visible under the global lock: a writer holds the lock for its whole commit window) and as unsettled otherwise (visible only to a lock-free `diagnose`).
- **An unknowable repair** (a `prepared` that is complete and does not decode, or declares a newer major, and whose writer is gone) might be a barrier owner, so it is treated as owning everything: it is "recovered" first (E5 leaves it with its stop), and every other journal of both families is behind it. Decided while writing this bead: this follows M3-D45 and §8.1 default 6 (fail closed on what cannot be read); nothing else commits while it exists anyway (the closed fence), and its set-aside is how the user gets out.
- **Pass 2, folder journals**, listed **after** pass 1 with `journal::list` (pass 1 may have moved a journal back to its own name, by rolling back an interrupted suspension, or away, by rolling back a reactivation). Each one behind an unsettled owner is skipped:
  - on one of the caller's own targets, or with no readable target: `recover_all` returns `Err` with the owner's code and `details {journal_pending: <this tx>, reason: <owner's reason>, target: <this journal's target>, tx: <owner>, resource: "journal:<this tx>"}`, the message `transaction <tx> on target <t> waits behind repair <owner>, which recovery could not settle (<reason>); it is left as it is`, and the owner's `explain_fix`. Decided while writing this bead: no new `reason` value; the journal is "fenced with that repair" (§6.14.3), and a fenced refusal is the fencing journal's own stop plus `tx` and `resource` (M4-D62), which tells an agent both what to fix (the owner) and what is held back (`journal:<tx>`);
  - otherwise: the behind-barrier warning (§5), and the journal is left untouched.
  Every other folder journal is recovered exactly as today (`recover_one`; own-target errors fail the caller, others warn).
- **Pass 3, the remaining repair journals**, listed after pass 2, in transaction order, excluding those pass 1 processed. One that an unsettled owner names is behind it (warning). One whose `prepared.resources` conflict (`ResourceSet::conflicts_with`) with the protected set of a journal pass 2 left unresolved (stopped, or behind a barrier; not live) waits behind that journal: not recovered, the pass-3 warning (§5), and fenced with that journal's stop (s3 extends the loader). The rest are recovered by `repair::recover`; a stop leaves them stuck (the s2 warning).
- **Repair stops never fail the caller** in `recover_all`: they are target-less and fence-scoped; the closed fence, the fences and the under-lock gate refuse exactly the writes that must not happen. Decided while writing this bead: this keeps `recover_under`'s callers recovering every other journal (an error there would end its loop), and keeps the own-target failure rule for folder journals unchanged.
- **Recovery writes unfenced.** Every recovery session and prune uses `env.scopes.without_fences()` (in `journal_scopes`, in `recover_parsed`, and in E5's repair recovery). Why that is safe: a stuck repair's resources are written by no later commit (its table is fenced, or its gate refuses); a folder journal that predates the repair is recovered in pass 2, before pass 3 re-attempts the repair; pass 1 owners are settled before pass 2; and pass 3's overlap rule keeps a pending repair from running over a journal pass 2 could not settle. The order, not the fence, governs recovery.
- `recover_under` and `recover_waiting` call `recover_all` and get the passes. `recoverable` (`journal.rs:923-930`) counts pending repair journals too (E5's, if already there). `recover_tx` (a writer recovering its own new transaction in process) is unchanged: no other repair names a transaction that is still being written.
- **Repeated recovery.** Each pass decides from the disk as it finds it, so a recovery killed anywhere (`doctor.recover.step=abort`, `engine.recover.step=abort`) is finished by the next lock-taking command in the same order.

### 8. `journal::diagnose` simulates the three passes (s3)

In `src/engine/simulate.rs` (E11), the per-journal loop becomes the three passes on the one simulated tree, driven by `barrier::Passes`:

- Pass 1 simulates each owner (E5's repair arm) and records `Settled` or `Unsettled(stop)` from its simulated verdict; a settled owner's simulated moves stay in the tree.
- Pass 2's listing is the disk listing of `<state>/journal/` adjusted by pass 1's simulated moves: a listed journal that a simulated move took away is gone, and a journal that a simulated move brought into `<state>/journal/` under a listed name is added, its text read from its origin through the simulated tree's path translation (E11's `Simulated`).
- **`JournalVerdict::BehindBarrier { owner: TxId }`** for every journal behind an unsettled owner, and for every pass-3 repair that waits behind an unresolved pass-2 journal (`owner` is then that journal). Its `expected()` is `Stops { code: <owner's code>, reason: <owner's reason>, step: None }`, or `Skipped` when the owner is live and unfinished; its `direction()` is `None`. Its `protected` is the journal's own protected set, which the loader fences with the owner's stop.
- An unknowable repair makes every later journal `BehindBarrier { owner: <it> }`.
- E11's differential then compares these predictions with what recovery does, case by case (s5).

### 9. The set-aside's excusing rule (s3)

A repair that sets a journal aside must be able to move it even while that journal's own fence or closed set stands (that is the point of the set-aside: "until its set-aside, whose own resources are known, moves it"). E5's repair commit builds its table as `fence::table(..)?` and then `with_fences(fences.excusing(&names))`, where `names` is `barrier::of(prepared)`'s names when it is a `Suspension`. Only the fences and the closed set whose stop's `tx` is one of those journals are lifted; every other journal's fences still apply. Decided while writing this bead: excuse by the journals the suspension moves, not by fix kind, because a set-aside of a stuck repair must cross that repair's own fence (its quarantine roots lie under it), and nothing else may.

### 13. What not to do

- Do not let `tx_named`, `journals()` or the orphan sweep parse `.repair` or `.reactivating` names.
- Do not fence recovery's own writes, and do not make `recover_all` fail its caller for a repair stop.
- Do not put a fence on `history.jsonl`, and never let a fence path, resource text or message name a path below `WTF/`.
- Do not add an error code, a warning code, a failpoint or a constant.
- Do not write: the loader, the gate, the planner and the simulation read only (common rule 2; `tests/single_writer.rs` scans `src/`).

### 14. Decided while writing this bead (confirm or adjust each in the close comment)

1. fsx holds fences as canonical paths plus the stop to report (`FenceSet`), because fsx cannot depend on `engine`; the engine translates resources.
2. A missing directory created strictly above a fence's path is allowed; every other overlapping operation is refused.
3. The fence check sits in `mutate()`'s step 1 after the scope checks and before the preconditions and `fsx.mutate.checked`.
4. `prune()` skips a fenced victim with a reason instead of failing.
5. Fence refusal details are the stop's `{journal_pending, reason, target}` plus `tx` and `resource`; the message names only the fenced resource.
6. The protected set adds, for a barrier owner, every `prepared.targets` record and the guards' paths; `history.jsonl` is never a fence path; paths are cut at `WTF/`.
7. A suspension is recognized by the rename of a journal file out of `<state>/journal/`, guards or not.
8. The loader decides between path fences and a closed set by decoding the stuck repair's `prepared` line (`repair::read_prepared`), and a decodable `prepared` with a bad later line gets path fences.
9. An unlistable journal directory closes the set.
10. `explain_fix` uses `omaddons status` until E3's `doctor explain` is on `main` (a follow-up bead switches it).
11. Fences are loaded at each mutating table's construction (`fence::table`), and a scan test keeps every production table classified.
12. Commands that build their table before the lock are protected by one under-lock gate that reloads the fences, checks the target's record and the caller's first-hand writes; there is no pre-lock gate.
13. One provisional spelling, `<tx>.reactivating.jsonl`, for every family.
14. The activation rules, including provisional first, activation last, and retention's `dead` test treating a provisional journal as present.
15. A malformed activation is refused by `commit` (`internal`) and read as undecodable by recovery.
16. Pass 1 runs in naming order, an unknowable repair puts every other journal behind it, and a live owner is settled only when finished.
17. A journal behind an unsettled owner reports the owner's stop with `tx` and `resource: "journal:<tx>"`, no new reason value.
18. Repair stops never fail `recover_all`'s caller; recovery writes unfenced.
19. The set-aside's commit excuses exactly the fences of the journals it moves.
20. `pending_warnings` runs `diagnose` only when a repair journal exists.
21. A dry run is fenced like its real run (it plans with the same table); read commands are never fenced.
22. A stop without a reason (recovery itself failed on I/O) omits `details.reason`, shows its code in the texts' parentheses, and its fix explains `fm-concurrency_primitives-journal-pending`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A quarantine of a directory and a write into its child, lowered together by `repair::lower` of E5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`, the repair transaction), give step resource sets that conflict (`ResourceSet::conflicts`, both resources named): the unit case of the `fixer_conflict` refusal of E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`, `doctor fix`).
- [ ] A stuck chmod repair on the stored GitHub token: `auth github set` is refused with the stuck journal's own error (its code and `details.reason`, plus `details.tx` and `details.resource` naming the token, fix `omaddons doctor explain fm-concurrency_primitives-journal-step-unrecognized`, or the interim fix of decision 10), and `<config>` hashes as before; an install whose cache blob is unrelated proceeds; an update on another client proceeds; each command reports exactly one `journal_pending` warning for the stuck repair.
- [ ] A stuck quarantine of `<client dir>/Interface/AddOns/X` refuses any write to `AddOns/X` or below it, and an install of addon `X` on that client is refused under the lock before its journal is written (the client tree hashes as before), while an install of another addon on the same client proceeds.
- [ ] A stuck skill rewrite fences only that skill file: a write to `<skills>/SKILL.md` is refused, a write beside it in the skill directory and every other command proceed.
- [ ] A stuck quarantine of one cache blob refuses a write of that blob and nothing else: an install that uses another blob proceeds.
- [ ] A repair journal whose complete `prepared` line does not decode (and, separately, one with a newer major `format`) fails every committing command closed: `install`, `update`, `remove`, `config set`, `auth github set`, `targets rename`, `errors dismiss`, `backup create`, `omarchy install` each fail with that journal's stop (`state_corrupt`/`journal_unreadable` or `state_too_new`/`journal_too_new`) and `details.tx`, every tree hashing as before; `status`, `list` and `history` still run (and `doctor`, once E3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, `doctor diagnose`, is on `main`); recovery runs no other journal behind it.
- [ ] A repair journal with no complete first line protects nothing: it is pruned as unstarted and no command is refused.
- [ ] A repair that becomes stuck after an engine command built its table (the command paused at `engine.snapshot.prestaged`) is caught by the under-lock gate: the command fails with that journal's stop and changes nothing; the next command loads the fence and proceeds when it does not overlap.
- [ ] Retention's prune skips a victim a fence covers, with the reason, and prunes the others.
- [ ] Every production `ScopeTable::new` is either built through `engine::fence::table` or listed with its reason (the scan test passes, and fails on a planted unlisted table).
- [ ] Recovery runs three passes: repairs owning a suspension or an activation first (in naming order), then folder journals listed after pass 1, then the remaining repairs in transaction order; a journal behind an unsettled barrier is never recovered, on the caller's own target fails the caller with the owner's stop and `details.resource: "journal:<tx>"`, elsewhere warns; a pass-3 repair overlapping a journal pass 2 left unresolved waits behind it, fenced; an unknowable repair puts every other journal behind it.
- [ ] A reactivation crashed after each artifact restore, immediately before the activation, and between the activation and `done`, and a suspension crashed at each of its primitives: the next lock-taking command (`config set`, an `install` on that client, an `update` on another) never recovers the folder journal before the reactivating or suspending repair has settled, and the end state is the whole before (crash before the durable `done`) or the whole after (from `done` on), never a mixture; every primitive boundary actually fired.
- [ ] Recovery itself crashed at every inverse of a reactivation's rollback, then repeated three times, ends in the same whole state; an injected I/O failure in that rollback leaves the repair unsettled and the folder journal behind it, and a clean recovery afterwards settles both in order.
- [ ] The provisional journal `<tx>.reactivating.jsonl` is listed by neither `journal::list`, the orphan sweep nor `prune()`; while it exists, the orphan sweep keeps that transaction's in-flight lock, stage and snapshots however old they are.
- [ ] `barrier::validate` refuses each malformed activation (not last, not from the provisional name, provisional not first, two activations, a journal moved in without activation), `repair::commit` refuses it with `internal` before `prepared`, and recovery reads such a `prepared` as undecodable.
- [ ] `journal::diagnose` simulates the three passes and gives `BehindBarrier { owner }`; the differential test of E11 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.11`, `journal::diagnose`) agrees with real recovery over every case above (fence cases, barrier crash cases, repeated recovery, the unknowable and pass-3 cases).
- [ ] Every existing crash matrix in `tests/engine_crash.rs` and every case of `tests/journal.rs` passes unchanged.
- [ ] No output on any channel names an account, realm or character (`assert_private_all` over stdout and stderr with `--progress json` in every scenario that has a `WTF/`), and no fence path or `details.resource` lies below a `WTF/`.
- [ ] The design gate: s5's adversarial matrix passes.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; README's Safety model (stuck repairs fence what they protect; Interrupted runs' order), Files and state (`<tx>.reactivating.jsonl`), the error table and Troubleshooting are updated in the commits that ship them.
- [ ] The close comment lists every new or changed wire name (`details.tx` and `details.resource` on the stop codes, the file `<state>/journal/<tx>.reactivating.jsonl`) and every "Decided while writing this bead" item with its outcome; `br lint` is clean for this bead and its subtasks.
