title: The activation barrier and recovery's three passes, in recovery and in `journal::diagnose`
description:
Part 3 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14 (Fences and activation barriers). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

Beads this section names: E14 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14`, fences and activation barriers, the parent), E5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`, the repair transaction), E7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7`, undo of repairs), E11 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.11`, `journal::diagnose`), F2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.2`, the set-aside) and the parent's parts omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14.2 and omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14.5.

**The leaf.** M4's repairs are transactions of a second journal family (E5). Two of them move other journals: F2's set-aside **suspends** a stuck journal set by renaming its artifacts (the journal file, its in-flight lock, its state snapshot half, its client stage and snapshot halves) into quarantine, one `RenameNoReplace` per artifact; E7's `doctor undo` of a set-aside **reactivates** it by renaming them back. M4-D38 decides how a reactivation stays crash-safe: "The undo restores the journal under a provisional name ordinary recovery does not list (`<tx>.reactivating.jsonl`, which `tx_named` cannot parse). Its last primitive, the activation, renames it to its own name. Recovery resolves the repair that owns a barrier before it considers ordinary journals, and never recovers a journal behind an unresolved barrier. So a crash anywhere in a reactivation, including after the activation and before the undo's durable `done`, can never let the folder pass run the restored journal ahead of the undo that exposed it: before `done` the undo rolls back, provisional name included, and from `done` on the journal is an ordinary pending journal again." M4-D31 fixes the order: "Recovery first resolves the repairs that own a suspension or an activation barrier, then folder journals, then the remaining repair journals." M4-D46: an activation-sensitive rename is inverted "provisional name first, activation last". *Why:* restoring the journal last does not close the crash window, because folder recovery ran before repair recovery; the next command would recover the exposed journal first, and the undo's rollback would then fail on a journal file recovery had already pruned, leaving a mixture. *Rejected:* the reviewed draft's unconditional restore with folder recovery first.

**This part** builds that barrier: the activation primitive's rules and their validation, the pass planner that orders recovery (one decision procedure shared by recovery and the simulation), `recover_all` in three passes, the `BehindBarrier` verdict in `journal::diagnose` and its fences, the set-aside's right to move a journal its own fence protects, and retention's orphan test. It is its own step because it changes recovery's order, the leaf's design-gate protocol, and omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14.5's adversarial matrix tests exactly this part. It comes after omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14.2 because the barrier's fences reuse s2's loader, protected rule and warnings.

## Technical Approach

Beads this section names: E14 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14`, the parent), E5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`), E7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7`), E8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.8`, `doctor gc`), E9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9`, the M3 build against M4 state), E11 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.11`), E13 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.13`, resource sets), F1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1`, journal and lock detectors), F2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.2`) and the parent's parts omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14.1, omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14.2 and omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14.5.

**Facts this part relies on** (as of `c0ab5e9`, or as the blockers and s2 leave them):

- `recover_all` (`src/engine/journal.rs:811-848`, E5 adds a repair pass after the folder pass) is called by every commit (`src/engine/tx.rs:770, 1025`, `src/engine/undo.rs`, `src/engine/restore.rs:750`, `src/engine/restore_addons.rs:764`) and by `recover_under` (`journal.rs:858-896`), itself called by `recover_waiting` (`:907-920`) and by `config set`, `targets`, `auth github` and `backup` (`src/app/config.rs:297`, `src/app/targets.rs:352`, `src/app/auth.rs:307`, `src/app/backup.rs:1443, 1500`). `recover_tx` (`:950-956`) recovers a writer's own journal in process.
- Recovery writes through the caller's table: `journal_scopes` clones `env.scopes` (`:936-945`), `recover_parsed` opens `WriteSession::untracked(writer, scopes, "recovery")` (`:1047`) and prunes with it (`:1097-1102`).
- `paths::tx_named` (`src/state/paths.rs:33-35`) strips only `.wtf`; `<tx>.reactivating.jsonl` is listed by neither `journals()` (`journal.rs:629`), the orphan sweep (`src/engine/retention.rs:365, 393`) nor builds before M4, and `prune()` refuses it (`src/fsx/prune.rs:364-366`).
- Retention's orphan sweep computes victims without the lock (`src/engine/retention.rs:207`, `orphans` `:347-407`) and prunes them later with `LockUse::Acquire` (`:209-222`); a transaction is dead when its in-flight lock is not live and `journal::existing` (`journal.rs:669-674`) finds neither `<tx>.wtf.jsonl` nor `<tx>.jsonl` (`retention.rs:358-360`). A rename keeps the moved entry's modification time.
- From E11: the simulation in `src/engine/simulate.rs` runs journals "in `journal::list`'s order on one `Simulated` …, which is also where E14's three-pass order plugs in"; `Simulated` translates path queries through its recorded moves; `JournalVerdict`, `expected()` (`Stops { code, reason, step }`, `Skipped`, …), `direction()`, `evidence.artifacts`.
- From E5: `repair::{list, recover, commit, read_prepared}` and `RepairPrepared`; from s2: `repair::{journal_file, provisional_journal}`, `barrier::of`, `fence::{protected, load, stop_of, stuck_warning, explain_fix, table}`; from s1: `FenceSet::excusing`, `ScopeTable::without_fences`.

**1. The activation rules** (`barrier::validate(prepared: &RepairPrepared, paths: &Paths) -> Result<(), String>`, in `src/engine/barrier.rs`):

1. At most one primitive has `activation: true`, and it is the repair's last primitive.
2. It is a `RenameNoReplace` from `repair::provisional_journal(paths, tx)` to `<state>/journal/<tx>.jsonl`, `<tx>.wtf.jsonl` or `<tx>.repair.jsonl` of the same `tx` (`repair::journal_file` gives `Reactivating` and then `Folder`, `Wtf` or `Repair`).
3. Exactly one earlier primitive renames into that provisional name, and it is the **first** primitive of the repair that names `tx` (per `barrier::of`'s naming).
4. No other primitive renames onto the activation's `to` or out of the provisional name, and no primitive without `activation: true` moves a journal file into `<state>/journal/` under its own name.

Each violation returns a message naming the rule and the primitive's `seq`. Where it is enforced:

- `repair::commit` (E5) calls it before writing `prepared` and refuses with `Error::new(ErrorCode::Internal, "a repair that reactivates a journal must …: <rule>", internal_fix)`; nothing is written.
- `repair::read_prepared` returns `Undecodable` for a `prepared` that decodes but violates the rules, so recovery leaves it and s2's loader closes the set (fail closed, M3-D45). In-process rollback and recovery's inverses are not primitives and are not bound by rule 4.

**The provisional name** is one spelling for every family, `<state>/journal/<tx>.reactivating.jsonl`: the activation's `to` names the real file. Decided while writing this bead: one spelling, the plan's own file name (§7.7 of the plan), so E9, gc and the attribution know one more name, not two.

**Why rule 3, and retention's change.** Decided while writing this bead: M4-D38's prose ("restores every artifact but the journal file first, and restores the journal under a provisional name") would leave a race open, and M4-D46's "provisional name first, activation last" closes it. The orphan sweep judges a transaction dead when neither normal journal name exists, computes its victims without the lock, and sees a restored artifact as old at once. A sweep that looked between a reactivation's artifact restores and its journal's restore would prune, once the lock is free, the in-flight lock and state snapshot the reactivation had just put back. So: the journal goes to its provisional name first; and in `retention.rs`'s `dead` closure (`:358-360`), a transaction whose `repair::provisional_journal(paths, tx)` exists (`symlink_metadata(..).is_ok()`) is not dead. F2's set-aside order is F2's choice; E7 must order the undo by these rules rather than simply reversing the set-aside's primitives.

**`journal::diagnose`'s artifacts** (E11's `evidence.artifacts`, found by tx id in known locations) also list `<state>/journal/<tx>.reactivating.jsonl` (kind `Journal`), so F2's attribution and E8's gc see a provisional journal.

**2. The pass planner** (`barrier::Passes`), the one decision procedure for order, driven by recovery with the disk and by the simulation with the simulated tree (E11's principle: a decision written twice drifts):

```rust
pub enum Outcome { Settled, Unsettled(FenceStop), Live { finished: bool } }
pub struct ListedRepair { pub tx: TxId, pub prepared: Option<RepairPrepared>, pub live: bool }
pub struct Passes { /* owners, rest, unknowable, outcomes so far */ }

impl Passes {
    pub fn new(repairs: Vec<ListedRepair>, paths: &Paths) -> Self;
    /// Pass 1: the next barrier owner to recover, or None when pass 1 is over.
    pub fn next_owner(&mut self) -> Option<TxId>;
    pub fn record(&mut self, tx: TxId, outcome: Outcome);
    /// The unsettled repair that names `tx` (any family), if any: `tx` is behind it.
    pub fn behind(&self, tx: &TxId) -> Option<TxId>;
    /// Pass 3: the repairs not yet processed, in transaction order.
    pub fn rest(&self) -> Vec<TxId>;
    /// Pass 3's overlap rule: the first journal in `unresolved` whose protected set conflicts with `resources`.
    pub fn waits_for(&self, resources: &ResourceSet, unresolved: &[(TxId, ResourceSet)]) -> Option<TxId>;
    /// The stop of an unsettled owner (for errors and warnings), and whether it is unknowable.
    pub fn stop(&self, owner: &TxId) -> Option<&FenceStop>;
}
```

Rules:

- **Owners** are the listed repairs with `barrier::of(prepared).is_some()`. **Unknowable** repairs (`prepared: None`: a complete first line that does not decode, a newer major, or a malformed activation; writer gone) are treated as owners of everything: processed first, and every other journal of both families is behind them. Decided while writing this bead: an unreadable repair might be a reactivation that has already exposed a journal, so nothing may be recovered behind it (M3-D45, default 6 of the plan's §8.1: fail closed on what cannot be read); nothing else can commit meanwhile anyway (s2's closed fence), and its set-aside is the way out.
- **Pass 1 order:** an owner named by another listed owner comes after the one naming it; ties in transaction order. A repair names only journals that existed when it was planned, so the order exists; if a cycle is ever found (M4 code cannot build one), every owner in it is unsettled (fail closed). An owner named by an unsettled owner is not recovered: `behind` answers for it.
- **Settled:** recovery's `Ok` (rolled back, rolled forward or pruned). **Unsettled:** recovery's stop. **Live** owners are skipped; one counts as settled when its journal is finished (last complete line `committed` or `rolled_back`: the only live state visible under the global lock, because a writer holds the lock for its whole commit window) and as unsettled otherwise (seen only by a lock-free `diagnose`).
- **Pass 3** takes the repairs pass 1 did not process, re-listed after pass 2, in transaction order.

**3. `recover_all` in three passes** (`src/engine/journal.rs`):

```text
repairs  = repair::list(paths)            → ListedRepair (read_prepared, InflightLock::is_live)
passes   = Passes::new(repairs)
pass 1:  while let Some(owner) = passes.next_owner():
             live → record(Live{finished}); behind(owner) → skip (warning, below)
             else repair::recover(owner) → Ok: record(Settled) + its warnings
                                         → Err(stop): record(Unsettled(stop)); stuck_warning (s2)
pass 2:  for (tx, path) in journal::list(paths)  (listed now, after pass 1)
             live → skip as today
             passes.behind(tx) = Some(owner):
                 own target, or no readable target → return Err(behind error)
                 else → behind warning; left untouched; remember (tx, protected) as unresolved
             else recover_one as today (own-target stop → Err; other → warning, remember as unresolved)
pass 3:  for tx in passes.rest() re-listed with repair::list:
             live → skip; behind(tx) → behind warning (repair form)
             waits_for(prepared.resources, unresolved) = Some(f) → "waits behind" warning
             else repair::recover → Ok: warnings; Err: stuck_warning
```

- **The behind error** (a journal behind an unsettled owner, on the caller's own target or with no readable target): code = the owner's stop code; `details: {journal_pending: <this tx>, reason: <owner's reason>, target: <this journal's target>, tx: <owner>, resource: "journal:<this tx>"}`; message `transaction <tx> on target <t> waits behind repair <owner>, which recovery could not settle (<reason>); it is left as it is` (for an unknowable owner, `which this omaddons cannot read (<reason>)`); fix `fence::explain_fix(<owner's reason>)`. Decided while writing this bead: no new `reason` value: the journal is "fenced with that repair", and a fenced refusal is the fencing journal's own stop plus `tx` and `resource` (M4-D62), which tells an agent what to fix (the owner) and what is held back.
- **The behind warnings** (`fence::behind_warning`, `WarningCode::JournalPending`, the owner's `explain_fix`), one parenthesized reason each: a folder journal `transaction <tx> on target <t> waits behind repair <owner>, which recovery could not settle (<reason>); it is left as it is`; a pass-3 repair named by an owner `repair transaction <tx> waits behind repair <owner>, which recovery could not settle (<reason>); writes to what it protects are refused`; a pass-3 repair waiting on an unresolved journal `repair transaction <tx> waits behind transaction <f>, which recovery could not settle (<reason>); writes to what it protects are refused`. `journal::pending_warnings` (readers) gives the same texts from `diagnose`'s `BehindBarrier` verdicts.
- **"Unresolved by pass 2"** means stopped (error or warning) or behind; a live folder journal is not. Its protected set is E11's (the function that fills `JournalDiagnosis.protected`; call it, do not recompute).
- **Recovery writes unfenced:** `journal_scopes`, `recover_parsed` and E5's repair recovery use `env.scopes.without_fences()`. Why safe: a stuck repair's resources are written by no later commit (its table is fenced, or s2's gate refuses); a folder journal that predates a repair is recovered in pass 2, before pass 3 retries the repair; pass 1 is settled before pass 2; pass 3's overlap rule keeps a pending repair off a journal pass 2 could not settle. Order, not the fence, governs recovery.
- **Repair stops never fail the caller** (s2 already made them warnings); folder journals keep today's own-target rule.
- `recover_under` and `recover_waiting` call `recover_all` and get the passes; `recoverable` counts pending repair journals (E5's, if already there); `recover_tx` is unchanged (no repair names a transaction still being written).
- **Repeated recovery:** every pass decides from the disk as it finds it, so a recovery killed anywhere is finished by the next lock-taking command in the same order.

**4. `journal::diagnose` simulates the passes** (`src/engine/simulate.rs`), on the one simulated tree, driven by `Passes`:

- Pass 1 simulates each owner with E5's repair arm and records `Settled` (keeping its simulated moves in the tree) or `Unsettled(stop_of(d))`.
- Pass 2's listing is `journal::list`'s disk listing adjusted by pass 1's simulated moves: a listed journal moved away is dropped; a journal moved into `<state>/journal/` under a listed name (a rolled-back suspension puts it back) is added, its text read from its origin through `Simulated`'s path translation. Pass 3's listing is adjusted likewise.
- **`JournalVerdict::BehindBarrier { owner: TxId }`** (new) for every journal `behind` gives, and for a pass-3 repair that `waits_for` gives (`owner` is then that journal). `expected()`: `Stops { code: <owner's code>, reason: <owner's reason>, step: None }`, or `Skipped` when the owner is live and unfinished. `direction()`: `None`. `protected`: the journal's own.
- An unknowable repair makes every other journal `BehindBarrier { owner: <it> }`.

**5. The barrier's fences** (`fence::load`, s2's table gains its row): every diagnosis with `BehindBarrier { owner }` whose owner has a stop adds `paths_of(d.protected)` with the **owner's** stop (`stop_of` of the owner's diagnosis), "fenced with that repair"; behind a live, unfinished owner (seen only without the lock: a reactivation in progress elsewhere, whose commit window holds the lock) nothing is fenced, as for any live transaction. A folder journal behind an owner therefore protects its stage, snapshots and step paths from every command, not only its own target's.

**6. The set-aside may move what its own fence protects.** E5's repair commit builds its table with `fence::table(..)?`, then, when `barrier::of(prepared)` is a `Suspension`, replaces its fences with `fences.excusing(&barrier.names)`. Only the fences and the close whose stop's `tx` is a journal the suspension moves are lifted; every other journal's fences still apply. Decided while writing this bead: excuse by the journals moved, not by fix kind, because a set-aside of a stuck repair must cross that repair's own fence (its quarantine lies under it), and a set-aside of an unreadable repair must pass its closed set ("until its set-aside, whose own resources are known, moves it").

**7. README** (same commit, common rule 11):

- **Safety model, "Interrupted runs"** (`README.md:1995`): add "Recovery runs in three passes: first the repairs that suspend or reactivate a journal (a doctor set-aside and its undo), then folder journals, then the other repairs. A journal behind a repair that recovery could not settle is left as it is and reported (`journal_pending`); on the client a command changes, the command fails with that repair's error. An undo of a set-aside puts the journal back under the provisional name `<tx>.reactivating.jsonl` first and renames it to its own name last, so a crash in between is rolled back whole before anything recovers the journal."
- **Files and state** (`README.md:2269-2281`): a row for `<state>/journal/<tx>.reactivating.jsonl`: "a suspended journal while an undo of its set-aside is unfinished; recovery settles that undo first; never deleted by retention".

**What not to do:** do not let `tx_named`, `journals()` or the orphan sweep parse `.reactivating`; do not recover anything behind an unknowable repair; do not fence recovery's own writes; do not add a failpoint (s5 crashes the repair through E5's eleven `doctor::FAILPOINTS` and fsx's `fsx.mutate.*@N`), an error code, a warning code or a constant.

**Files:** `src/engine/barrier.rs` (`validate`, `Passes`), `src/engine/journal.rs` (`recover_all`'s passes, `without_fences` in `journal_scopes` and `recover_parsed`, `pending_warnings`' behind texts), `src/engine/repair.rs` (validation in `commit` and `read_prepared`, the excusing rule, `without_fences` in repair recovery), `src/engine/simulate.rs` (the passes, `BehindBarrier`, provisional artifacts), `src/engine/fence.rs` (the `BehindBarrier` row, `behind_warning`), `src/engine/retention.rs` (`dead`), `src/error/specs.rs` (if the behind error's `tx` and `resource` reach a code s2 did not cover), `README.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `barrier::validate` refuses each malformed activation (two activations; activation not last; not from the provisional name; `to` another transaction's name; provisional not the first primitive naming the tx; a journal moved in under its own name without activation) and accepts a well-formed reactivation; `repair::commit` refuses a violation with `internal` before writing `prepared`; `read_prepared` reads one as undecodable.
- [ ] The provisional journal is listed by neither `journal::list`, `repair::list`, the orphan sweep nor `prune()`; while it exists, the orphan sweep keeps its transaction's in-flight lock, stage and snapshots however old.
- [ ] `recover_all` runs three passes: owners in naming order; folder journals listed after pass 1 (a rolled-back suspension's journal is recovered in the same call; a rolled-back reactivation's is not seen); remaining repairs in transaction order. A journal behind an unsettled owner is never recovered: on the caller's own target (or with no readable target) the caller fails with the owner's code and reason, `details.tx` (the owner) and `details.resource` (`journal:<tx>`); elsewhere one `journal_pending` warning. A pass-3 repair whose resources overlap a journal pass 2 left unresolved waits behind it. An unknowable repair puts every other journal behind it.
- [ ] A repair stop never fails `recover_all`'s caller, and every recovery session and prune is unfenced.
- [ ] `journal::diagnose` simulates the three passes on the simulated tree (including a journal pass 1 moves back into the listing) and gives `BehindBarrier { owner }` with the owner's stop as `expected()`.
- [ ] The loader fences a journal behind a barrier with its owner's stop; a set-aside's commit excuses exactly the fences of the journals it moves.
- [ ] Every existing test of `tests/engine_crash.rs`, `tests/journal.rs` and the in-crate recovery tests passes unchanged.

- **Confirmed as the bead decided:** one provisional spelling (`<tx>.reactivating.jsonl`); rule 3 (provisional first) and retention's `dead` change; a malformed activation read as undecodable; naming order in pass 1, ties in tx order, and the cycle rule; unknowable repairs put everything behind them; a live owner is settled only when finished; no new reason value for the behind error; recovery writes unfenced; excusing by the journals a suspension moves.
- **`ListedRepair.prepared` is a `PreparedRead`, not `Option<RepairPrepared>`.** `None` would make a journal with no complete line (nothing ran, `Absent`) an unknowable owner of everything. Unknowable = `Undecodable | TooNew` (a malformed activation reads as `Undecodable`); a journal that cannot be read at all counts as `Undecodable`.
- **Where the rules are enforced:** `ParsedRepair::checked(paths)` demotes a `prepared` line that breaks them (prepared dropped, one unknown line), and `repair::journal::read` and `read_prepared` now take `paths` so every reader that acts on a repair journal goes through it (recovery, `pending_repairs`, the fence loader, the simulation, the fuzz property's verdict check). `repair::commit` refuses with `internal` after building `prepared` and before the roots or any journal line.
- **Rule details:** with no activation only rule 4's second half applies (no non-activation rename into `<state>/journal/` under a journal's own name). No rule beyond the bead's four: a rename into or out of a provisional name in a repair without activation stays F2's/E7's business.
- **An unknowable repair is never behind anything:** recovering it only stops and writes nothing, so each of two unknowable repairs gets its own stuck warning rather than a behind text.
- **Outcome has a fourth variant, `Behind(owner)`**, and `Passes::stop` follows a chain of them to the repair that could not be settled (a journal named by a held owner reports the root's reason). `Unsettled` carries `Stuck { stop: FenceStop, closed }`. A cycle's owners start `Unsettled` with `state_corrupt` / `journal_unreadable` (no new reason) and stay so whatever is recorded later, so what they name keeps a stop.
- **`JournalVerdict::BehindBarrier { owner, stop: Option<OwnerStop> }`:** `expected()` needs the owner's code and reason, and the verdict stays `Copy`. `stop: None` is a live, unfinished owner (`Skipped`). The journal's own verdict is kept in `JournalEvidence.held` ("protected: the journal's own" is computed from it, then its simulated moves are undone).
- **F1** (closed) now reports a held journal under its own state (`evidence.held`); the `behind_barrier` evidence key is a doctor wire change, filed as omad-c1fu.
- **Behind a live, unfinished owner** (under the lock, only a newer build's unreadable repair in its cleanup), recovery skips the journal silently and fences nothing, as for any live transaction.
- **Pass 3's overlap rule:** an unresolved folder journal's protected set is `journal::diagnose`'s own `protected` (diagnosed once, only when a decodable pass-3 repair might wait), as a resource set by `fence::resources_of` (a directory on disk a subtree, else a file; unresolvable: everything). A repair whose recorded resources do not parse waits behind the first unresolved journal.
- **The behind error:** the owner's code; `details` `{journal_pending, reason, resource: "journal:<tx>", target, tx: <owner>}`, `reason` omitted when the owner failed on I/O without one; fix `fence::explain_fix` of the owner's reason.
- **`recover_repairs` is gone** (the passes replace it); `settle_all` is test-only; `fence::recovery_warning` folded into the pass (stop and warning from one `closes` read).
- **The simulation keeps the listing's order** and inserts a journal a simulated move brought back at its sorted place (two in-crate tests hand their listing out of tx order).
- **`fence::stop_of`** names a folder owner (pass 3 waits on folder journals) as a folder journal in its summary.
- **`doctor fix`** never delegates a held journal: `recoveries()` plans only journals with a `direction()`, which `BehindBarrier` has none of.

title: Tests: a stuck repair fences only what it protects, and an unreadable one fails closed
description:
Part 4 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14 (Fences and activation barriers). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

Beads this section names: E14 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14`, fences and activation barriers, the parent), E5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`, the repair transaction), E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`, `doctor fix`), E11 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.11`, `journal::diagnose`), T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs) and the parent's parts omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14.1 and omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14.2.

**The leaf.** A doctor repair is a transaction of a second journal family (E5); one that recovery cannot settle stays on disk, and has no target that would isolate it. M4-D62 decides: **a stuck, readable repair journal refuses only the mutations whose write sets overlap its protected resources (its primitives' writes, the backups its rollback reads, and for a suspension the suspended journal's target and the resources that journal would recover); every other command, client and path keeps working**. The refusal is the fencing journal's own stop error plus `details.tx` and `details.resource`, fix `omaddons doctor explain <fm>`. A repair journal whose complete `prepared` line does not decode, or declares a newer major, fails every committing command closed until its set-aside moves it, while read commands still run. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14.1 built the fence at `mutate()` and `prune()`; omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14.2 decided what a stuck repair protects, loaded it into every mutating command's table, and added the under-lock gate.

**This part** proves it end to end, through the real binary, on the cases the plan names: a stuck chmod on the GitHub token against `auth github set`, an unrelated cache blob, another client's update; a directory and its child; a stuck skill rewrite; an undecodable (and a newer-major) `prepared` line against every committing command, with read commands still running; plus three cases this bead adds because they are the edges of s2's design: a repair with no complete line, a repair that becomes stuck after a command built its table, and retention's prune skipping a fenced orphan. It is the leaf's integration suite (a test subtask after the code it tests), and it can run beside omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14.3. "Via E6's planner when it lands": E6's test fixers do not exist yet, so the stuck repairs are produced by E5's own commit, crashed, with the live path then changed so it matches neither `pre` nor `post`: real journals written by real code, not hand-written lines.

## Technical Approach

Beads this section names: A3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`, schemas and live validation), B3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3`, `robot-docs install-skill`), E1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`, the repair action model), E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, `doctor diagnose` and `explain`), E5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`), E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`, `doctor fix`), E11 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.11`), T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`) and the parent's parts omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14.1, omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14.2 and omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14.5.

**Facts this part relies on:**

- The test-side builders (`tests/common/`): `common::home::Home::new(&["wow", "wow_classic_era"])` gives `_retail_` and `_classic_era_` clients in a synthetic Battle.net home (`tests/common/home.rs:27`), with `home.serve_recorded(name)` for recorded HTTP fixtures (`:146`) and `home.installed_behind(..)` (`:95`); `TestEnv` sets every `HOME`/`XDG_*`, `TZ=UTC` and `OMADDONS_FS_CLONE=no`; `common::trees::tree_hash(dir)` covers modes and symlink targets (`tests/common/trees.rs:439`); `common::pause::Pause` drives `<name>=pause` failpoints (`tests/common/pause.rs`); the `auth` suite's canary token pattern (`tests/auth.rs:20-21`).
- T1's `TestLog`: `tlog!()`, `log.step`, `log.note`, `log.json`, `log.secret`, `log.run(&env, argv) -> Ran`, `log.cmd(&env, argv).stdin(..).failpoints(..).pause(&p).spawn()/run()`, `log.reached`/`log.resume`, `log.tree`/`log.assert_unchanged`/`log.diff`, `log.case(name)`; `Ran::{ok, exit, fails(exit, code), envelope, data, error_code, warnings, assert_private}`.
- E11's differential helper (`tests/common/differential.rs`): `predict(log, label, paths, clients, running)` and `assert_agrees(log, label, prediction, observed)`, with `observe_envelope`.
- The repo's child-process pattern: an `#[ignore]` test that the suite re-runs as `current_exe() <name> --exact --ignored --nocapture --test-threads=1` with environment variables naming the home and the outcome file (`child_restore`, `tests/engine_crash.rs:2814-2828`, driven by `tests/engine_crash.rs:2141-2181`). E5's repair crash matrix drives `repair::commit` in a child that way; reuse its driver if it lives in `tests/common/`, else this part adds one.
- The fence error's shape and the warning texts are omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14.2's: code and `details.reason` of the fencing journal's stop, `details.{journal_pending, target, tx, resource}`, the fix from `fence::explain_fix`, and one `journal_pending` per stuck repair whose message contains its tx and one parenthesized reason.

**1. Builders** (`tests/common/repairs.rs`, new; extend E5's if it already exists):

- `child_repair` (an `#[ignore]` test in `tests/doctor_repair.rs`, run as a child): reads `OMADDONS_REPAIR_ROOT` (the home), `OMADDONS_REPAIR_FIXES` (a JSON list of E1's `Fix`, built by the parent), `OMADDONS_REPAIR_OUT`; takes the global lock, lowers the fixes with `repair::lower`, commits with `repair::commit` (no recovery first, so the child can build states a doctor fix never would), and writes its outcome; `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS` arms it. Run on its own it does nothing.
- `pub fn stuck(home, log, fix: Fix, disturb: impl FnOnce(&Path)) -> StuckRepair { tx, protected: Vec<PathBuf> }`: runs `child_repair` with `fsx.mutate.executed@1=abort` (the first primitive ran and its `step` line is durable, no `done`), asserts the child aborted, then calls `disturb` to change the live path so that it matches neither the primitive's `pre` nor its `post`; logs the journal's lines (`log.json`). The next recovery stops at it (`step_unrecognized`).
- `pub fn plant_undecodable_prepared(home) -> TxId`: writes `<state>/journal/<tx>.repair.jsonl` = `{"type":"prepared","format":"1.0","tx":"<tx>","primitives":"not a list"}` plus a newline (a complete line that does not decode) and an in-flight lock file nobody holds.
- `pub fn plant_newer_major(home) -> TxId`: the same with `"format":"9.0"` and an otherwise valid line.
- `pub fn plant_torn_first_line(home) -> TxId`: `{"type":"prep` without a newline.
- `pub fn subject_hashes(home) -> BTreeMap<&str, String>`: `tree_hash` of `<config>/omaddons`, each client dir, `<state>/omaddons/{targets,snapshots,inflight}`, `<state>/omaddons/history.jsonl`, `<state>/omaddons/registry.json`, `<cache>/omaddons/blobs` and `<state>/omaddons/journal` (derived files such as `net.log`, the discovery cache, `history_tail` and the doorbell are left out: read commands and dry runs write them legitimately).

**2. The scenarios** (`tests/doctor_repair.rs`, created by this part if E6 has not created it, with a module doc naming its sections; every scenario `let log = tlog!();`, one `log.step` per phase):

1. **`fence_a_stuck_chmod_guards_the_token_only`.**
   - Setup: `Home::new(&["wow","wow_classic_era"])`; `auth github set` with a canary token on stdin (`log.secret`); `foo` installed on both clients from recorded fixtures (so `update` has work).
   - Stuck: `stuck(Fix::Chmod { path: <config>/omaddons/credentials/github, mode: 0o600 }, |p| replace the token file with a new file of the old mode)`.
   - `status --json`: exit as on a clean home with one pending journal; exactly one `journal_pending` warning whose message contains the repair's tx and `(step_unrecognized)`; `log.tree` of every subject before.
   - `auth github set --json` (another canary on stdin): `Ran::fails(1, "internal")`; `details.reason` `step_unrecognized`, `details.tx` and `details.journal_pending` the repair's tx, `details.target` null, `details.resource` the token's path; `error.fix_argv` equals `explain_fix`'s argv (or `["omaddons","status"]` under s2's interim rule); `log.assert_unchanged` of `<config>/omaddons`.
   - `install gh:o/bar -t retail --json`: ok (its blob is unrelated); one `journal_pending` for the repair.
   - `update -t classic_era --json`: ok.
   - `config set check_interval_hours 6 --json`: ok (`config.toml` is a sibling of `credentials/`).
   - Around each lock-taking command: `predict` then `assert_agrees` (the repair stays `Stops { internal, step_unrecognized }`).
   - Neither canary appears in any step's record (T1's redaction) or in any output.
2. **`fence_a_stuck_quarantine_guards_a_directory_and_its_child`.**
   - Setup: an unmanaged folder `AddOns/X` (with a child file) on `_retail_`; `bar` installable.
   - Stuck: `stuck(Fix::Quarantine { path: <retail>/Interface/AddOns/X, root: client }, |p| create a new, empty AddOns/X)`.
   - `install gh:o/x -t retail --json` (an addon whose folder is `X`): fails with the repair's stop; `details.resource` is `<retail>/Interface/AddOns/X/`; the journal directory holds only the repair's journal afterwards (the commit was refused by the under-lock gate before its journal), and the retail client hashes as before.
   - `install gh:o/bar -t retail --json`: ok.
   - In process: `fence::table(&paths, &[retail], None)` then a `Writer::Mutating` session `mutate(WriteFile)` of `AddOns/X/child.lua`: `FsxError::Fenced`; of `AddOns/Y/a.lua` (with `AddOns/Y` created first): ok.
3. **`fence_a_stuck_skill_rewrite_guards_only_that_file`.**
   - Setup: `<skills>/SKILL.md` with some bytes (the `TestEnv` skill dir).
   - Stuck: `stuck(Fix::Write { path: <skills>/SKILL.md, content: new bytes, mode: 0o644 }, |p| edit SKILL.md)`.
   - In process: a `Writer::Skill` session over `fence::table(&paths, &[], Some(skills))`: writing `SKILL.md` is refused (`Fenced`, resource the file); writing `<skills>/notes.md` succeeds.
   - If `robot-docs install-skill` is in `app::COMMANDS` (B3 on `main`): `robot-docs install-skill --json` fails with the repair's stop and the skill dir hashes as before.
   - `config set check_interval_hours 6 --json` and `install gh:o/bar -t retail --json`: ok.
4. **`fence_a_stuck_blob_quarantine_guards_that_blob_only`.**
   - Setup: two releases whose blobs `A` and `B` are in the blob cache (installed once on `_classic_era_` from recorded fixtures), `foo` (blob `A`) removed again from retail.
   - Stuck: `stuck(Fix::Quarantine { path: <cache>/omaddons/blobs/<A>, root: cache }, |p| write a different file at the blob's path)`.
   - `install` of the release with blob `B` on retail: ok.
   - `install` of the release with blob `A` on retail (the cache entry is now unusable, so the engine writes blob `A` again): fails with the repair's stop, `details.resource` the blob's path; the retail client hashes as before.
5. **`fence_an_unreadable_prepared_fails_every_committing_command_closed`**, two cases with `log.case`: `undecodable` (`plant_undecodable_prepared`, expected `state_corrupt`/`journal_unreadable`) and `newer_major` (`plant_newer_major`, expected `state_too_new`/`journal_too_new`).
   - `subject_hashes` before.
   - Each committing command fails with that code, `details.reason`, `details.tx` the planted tx and `details.resource` `journal:<tx>`, and `subject_hashes` is unchanged after each: `install gh:o/bar -t retail`, `install gh:o/bar -t retail --dry-run` (its first write is the blob cache through the run's fenced table: refused too), `update -t retail`, `remove foo -t retail`, `config set check_interval_hours 6`, `auth github set` (stdin), `targets rename retail main`, `backup create -t retail`, `omarchy install`.
   - Read commands still run, each with its usual exit and one `journal_pending` (the closed text): `status --json`, `list --json`, `history --json`; and `doctor --json` when `doctor` is in `app::COMMANDS` (E3 on `main`; s2's follow-up bead makes this unconditional otherwise).
   - Recovery runs no other journal: a pending folder journal planted beside it (an `update` on `_classic_era_` killed at `engine.swap.after_exchange`) is still there after each command (s3 makes it "behind"; before s3 lands, recovery's folder pass may still recover it, so this assertion is added by omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14.5's unknowable case, not here).
6. **`fence_a_repair_with_no_complete_line_protects_nothing`.** `plant_torn_first_line`; `config set check_interval_hours 6 --json` ok; the journal is gone afterwards (pruned as unstarted); the next `status --json` has no `journal_pending`.
7. **`fence_a_repair_stuck_after_the_table_was_built_is_caught_under_the_lock`.**
   - `install gh:o/bar -t retail --json` spawned with `engine.snapshot.prestaged=pause` (`log.cmd(..).pause(&p).spawn()`), `log.reached`: its table is built, its lock not yet taken.
   - Meanwhile `stuck(Fix::Chmod { token }, replace)` (the child repair takes the lock; the paused install does not hold it).
   - `log.resume`, `wait`: the install fails with the repair's stop, `details.resource` `journal:<tx>`, the message containing "could not be settled after this command started"; the retail client hashes as before and no folder journal remains.
   - `install gh:o/bar -t retail --json` again: ok (the fence is now loaded and does not overlap).
8. **`fence_retention_keeps_a_fenced_orphan`.**
   - Two orphan stages on `_retail_`, `<meta>/stage/<t1>` and `<meta>/stage/<t2>`, both aged past `ORPHAN_MIN_AGE` (1 h) by the test's fsx-free mtime helper (as `tests/compat_m2.rs` does).
   - Stuck: `stuck(Fix::Quarantine { path: <meta>/stage/<t1> }, |p| recreate <meta>/stage/<t1> and age it)`.
   - `install gh:o/bar -t retail --json` (a commit on that client runs retention): ok; afterwards `<meta>/stage/<t1>` exists, `<meta>/stage/<t2>` is gone.

**3. Contract.** Add two failure rows to `tests/contract/matrix.rs` with snapshots, when its row builder can plant state (it runs setup closures for other failure rows): `auth github set` refused by a fence, and `install` refused by a closed set. If it cannot, pin the two envelopes with `insta` snapshots in `tests/doctor_repair.rs` and run them through the contract suite's validator (`tests/contract/support::check`, with A3's live `DetailSpec` validation), so `tx` and `resource` are checked against their specs.

**4. Privacy.** Every scenario whose home has a `WTF/` runs its commands with `--progress json` and `Ran::assert_private` (`assert_private_all` over stdout and stderr), with `FAKEACCT`/`FakeRealm`/`FakeChar` planted in the client's `WTF/`.

**Files:** `tests/doctor_repair.rs`, `tests/common/repairs.rs` (and `tests/common/mod.rs`), `tests/contract/matrix.rs` and its snapshots (or the fallback snapshots).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `fence_a_stuck_chmod_guards_the_token_only` passes: `auth github set` refused with the stuck journal's stop, `details.tx`, `details.resource` (the token) and the documented fix, `<config>` unchanged; the unrelated install, the other client's update and `config set` succeed; one `journal_pending` per command; the differential of E11 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.11`, `journal::diagnose`) agrees around each command.
- [ ] `fence_a_stuck_quarantine_guards_a_directory_and_its_child` passes: the install of `X` refused before its journal, the client unchanged; a write into `AddOns/X/child.lua` refused; the install of another addon succeeds.
- [ ] `fence_a_stuck_skill_rewrite_guards_only_that_file` passes (and the `install-skill` case when B3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3`, `robot-docs install-skill`, is on `main`).
- [ ] `fence_a_stuck_blob_quarantine_guards_that_blob_only` passes.
- [ ] `fence_an_unreadable_prepared_fails_every_committing_command_closed` passes for both cases: every listed committing command (and the dry run) refused with the planted journal's stop and nothing changed; `status`, `list` and `history` run (and `doctor` when registered).

title: E2E: reactivations and suspensions crashed at every primitive, recovered in barrier order, with the differential
description:
Part 5 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14 (Fences and activation barriers). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

Beads this section names: E14 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14`, fences and activation barriers, the parent), E5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`, the repair transaction), E7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7`, undo of repairs), E11 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.11`, `journal::diagnose`), F2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.2`, the set-aside), T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs) and the parent's parts omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14.3 and omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14.4.

**The leaf.** M4's set-aside (F2) suspends a stuck journal set by renaming its artifacts into quarantine, and its undo (E7) reactivates it. M4-D38 makes the reactivation crash-safe with an activation barrier: the undo restores the journal under a provisional name that recovery does not list (`<tx>.reactivating.jsonl`), its last primitive (the activation) renames it to its own name, and recovery settles the repair that owns a barrier before it considers ordinary journals and never recovers a journal behind an unsettled barrier, "so a crash anywhere in a reactivation, including after the activation and before the undo's durable `done`, can never let the folder pass run the restored journal ahead of the undo that exposed it: before `done` the undo rolls back, provisional name included, and from `done` on the journal is an ordinary pending journal again". M4-D31 orders recovery in three passes: barrier owners, folder journals, the remaining repairs. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14.3 built the activation rules, the pass planner, `recover_all`'s passes and `journal::diagnose`'s `BehindBarrier` verdict.

**This part is the leaf's design gate** (common rule 14: a leaf that adds or changes a recovery rule closes only when its own adversarial matrix passes: every failpoint it adds, every journaled step, repeated recovery, and injected I/O failure where it writes; this leaf adds no failpoint, so its matrix is every primitive boundary of the protocols it orders). It crashes a real reactivation and a real suspension at every primitive boundary and at every repair failpoint, recovers with three different lock-taking commands, crashes recovery itself and repeats it, injects an I/O failure into recovery, covers the unknowable owner and pass 3's wait, and holds `journal::diagnose` to real recovery with E11's differential test over every one of these states. The plan's checkpoint criterion 11, "a crash at any point of a reactivation never lets ordinary recovery run the restored journal before the reactivating repair has settled", is proven here. The design gate is passed only when this subtask is closed.

## Technical Approach

Beads this section names: E5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`), E7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7`), E9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9`, the M3 build against M4 state), E11 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.11`), F2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.2`), F9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`, the safety harness), G3 (`omad-7ccp`, group commit), H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the checkpoint), T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`) and the parent's parts.

**Facts this part relies on:**

- `tests/engine_crash.rs` crashes the real binary at every failpoint and recovers with a lock-taking command (shared helpers `crash` `:235-375`, `crash_shape` `:587-696`, the restore helpers from `:2065`); its restore matrix drives the engine in a child process that the test binary re-runs as an `#[ignore]` test (`child_restore`, `:2814-2828`, driven by `:2141-2181`) and asserts that every on-path failpoint actually crashed (`crash_matrix_restore`, `:2832-2876`). E5's repair crash matrix adds a child driver for `repair::commit` in the same file; reuse it.
- `engine::tx::FAILPOINTS` (`src/engine/tx.rs:78-112`) includes `engine.swap.after_exchange`, `engine.swapped`, `engine.snapshot.prestaged` and `engine.recover.step`; E5's `doctor::FAILPOINTS` includes the abort points `doctor.repair.prepared`, `.step`, `.done`, `.history`, `.committed` and `doctor.recover.step`; fsx's `fsx.mutate.{checked,backed_up,executed,logged}` take `@N` for the Nth action of a session (`src/fsx/failpoint.rs`). Any failpoint can be armed `=abort`, `=error` or `=pause`.
- E11's differential helper (`tests/common/differential.rs`): `predict(log, label, paths, clients, running)` (hashes the trees, runs `journal::diagnose` in process, asserts nothing changed), `observe_envelope`, `assert_agrees`, and `Caller::{Commit { own }, Under}`; it attributes an error to a journal by `details.journal_pending` and a warning by the tx in its text with its one parenthesized reason. The first journal in recovery's order whose outcome fails the caller ends the run.
- From omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14.3: the activation rules (`barrier::validate`: at most one activation, last; from `<tx>.reactivating.jsonl` to the journal's own name; the provisional rename is the first primitive naming the tx); `recover_all`'s three passes; a journal behind an unsettled owner, on the caller's own target, fails the caller with the owner's code and reason and `details {journal_pending: <it>, target, tx: <owner>, resource: "journal:<it>"}`, elsewhere one `journal_pending` warning; `BehindBarrier { owner }` with the owner's stop as `expected()`.
- A copied home has new inodes and birth times, which journals record, so every case builds its own home (E11 found the same).

**1. The scene** (`tests/common/barrier.rs`, new):

```rust
pub enum FolderCrash { MidSwap, Swapped }       // the folder journal F: prepared with one step run, or swapped
pub enum SuspendOrder { JournalFirst, JournalLast }

pub struct BarrierScene { pub home: Home, pub f: TxId, pub artifacts: Vec<Artifact>, pub trees: Trees }
impl BarrierScene {
    /// A home with `_retail_` and `_classic_era_`, `foo` (two folders) at v1 on retail and `bar` installable,
    /// then `update foo -t retail` to v2 killed at `engine.swap.after_exchange` (MidSwap) or `engine.swapped`
    /// (Swapped): F, a real folder journal with its in-flight lock, state snapshot, stage and client snapshot.
    pub fn new(log: &TestLog, crash: FolderCrash) -> Self;
    /// F2's suspension of F as a repair (E5's `lower` of `Fix::Suspend` with F's artifacts and guards),
    /// committed in the child driver, with `failpoints` armed. Returns whether the child aborted.
    pub fn set_aside(&self, log: &TestLog, order: SuspendOrder, failpoints: &str) -> bool;
    /// E7's reactivation as a repair: [journal quarantine → provisional, every other artifact
    /// quarantine → its place, provisional → own name with `activation: true`], `barrier::validate`d first,
    /// committed in the child driver with `failpoints` armed. Returns whether the child aborted.
    pub fn reactivate(&self, log: &TestLog, failpoints: &str) -> bool;
    pub fn before(&self) -> Trees;   // the state a crash before `done` must return to
    pub fn after(&self) -> Trees;    // the state from `done` on (after the same command's pass 2)
}
```

- `Trees` holds `tree_hash`es of the retail client dir, `<state>/omaddons/{journal,inflight,snapshots,targets}`, `<state>/omaddons/history.jsonl` (its line count and the transactions it names), every quarantine root and `<meta>/snapshots`, recorded with `log.tree`.
- The reactivation's primitive count `N` is F's artifact count plus one (the activation); with `MidSwap` F has a journal, an in-flight lock, a state snapshot half, a stage and a client snapshot half, so `N = 6`.
- Decided while writing this bead: the scene builds the suspension and the reactivation from E5's primitives directly, because F2 and E7 land after this leaf; F2 and E7 then run the same properties on their own fixers (F9's harness integrates).

**2. The reactivation matrix** (`barrier_reactivation_crashed_at_every_boundary`, `FolderCrash::MidSwap`):

For every boundary `b` in `doctor.repair.prepared`, `doctor.repair.step@k`, `fsx.mutate.checked@k`, `fsx.mutate.backed_up@k`, `fsx.mutate.executed@k`, `fsx.mutate.logged@k` (for every `k` in `1..=N`), `doctor.repair.done`, `doctor.repair.history`, `doctor.repair.committed`, in a `log.case(b)`:

1. A fresh `BarrierScene`, `set_aside(.., JournalLast, "")` committed, then `reactivate(.., "<b>=abort")`; record whether the child aborted (`crashed_at`).
2. **A reader changes nothing:** `status --json` hashes nothing differently (`log.assert_unchanged`), and reports `journal_pending` for the reactivating repair when its journal exists.
3. **The recovering command,** `config set check_interval_hours 6 --json` (`Caller::Under`), between E11's `predict` and `assert_agrees`.
4. **Whole before or whole after, never a mixture.** Let `done` be whether the repair's journal held a durable `done` line at the crash (read before the recovering command and logged):
   - without `done`: the trees equal `before()`: F's artifacts back in quarantine with the identities and stamps the set-aside recorded, no `<F>.jsonl` and no `<F>.reactivating.jsonl`, the retail client as after the set-aside, the repair's journal gone (`rolled_back`, pruned), and no `journal_recovered` warning naming F;
   - with `done`: the trees equal `after()`: the repair's history line present exactly once, F recovered in the same command's pass 2 (a `journal_recovered` naming F, after any warning naming the repair), F's journal, in-flight lock, stage and state snapshot pruned, its client snapshot kept only if it still holds a folder, and the retail client's `foo` folders back at v1 (F, a mid-swap update, rolled back);
   - a state matching neither fails with `log.diff` of both comparisons.
5. **F never ahead of its repair:** when the repair rolled back, F's journal is untouched in quarantine; when it rolled forward, the warning naming the repair (if any) precedes F's `journal_recovered`.

Then the same boundaries recovered by **`install gh:o/bar -t retail --json`** (`Caller::Commit { own: [retail] }`: F's own target) and by **`update -t classic_era --json`** (`Caller::Commit { own: [classic_era] }`), each for the three key boundaries in fresh scenes: after every artifact restore (`fsx.mutate.logged@N-1`), immediately before the activation (`fsx.mutate.checked@N`), and between the activation and `done` (`fsx.mutate.logged@N`, `doctor.repair.done`). Both commands succeed, with the same whole-state assertions. After the loop: every `fsx.mutate.*@k` for `k` in `1..=N` and every `doctor.repair.*` point on the path is in `crashed_at`, or the test fails naming the boundary that never fired (F9's rule: no boundary is sampled away).

**3. The swapped variant** (`barrier_reactivation_behind_a_swapped_journal`, `FolderCrash::Swapped`): the three key boundaries and `doctor.repair.{done, history, committed}`; F rolls forward in pass 2 from `done` on (its history line appended once, after the repair's), so history is never fenced and the target's record reaches v2.

**4. The suspension matrix** (`barrier_suspension_crashed_at_every_boundary`, two `log.case`s, `JournalLast` and `JournalFirst`): `set_aside(.., order, "<b>=abort")` at every boundary as in item 2 (`N` = F's artifact count), then `config set`. Without `done`: the set-aside rolled back, F's artifacts back in place, and F recovered in the same command (pass 2 lists after pass 1): `journal_recovered` naming F after the warning naming the set-aside, retail's `foo` back at v1. With `done`: the set-aside rolled forward (its history line), F's artifacts in quarantine, F not recovered, retail's AddOns as F's crash left them. Every boundary fired.

**5. Recovery crashed, then repeated** (`barrier_recovery_crashed_at_every_inverse_then_repeated`): for the reactivation crashed at `fsx.mutate.logged@N-1` and at `fsx.mutate.logged@N` (before `done`), for every inverse `j` of its rollback: `config set` with `doctor.recover.step=abort@j` (aborts), then `config set` unarmed, then three more `config set`s; after each, `predict`/`assert_agrees`, and the end state is `before()` every time, with no journal left and no warning after the first settled run.

**6. Injected I/O failure** (`barrier_io_failure_in_recovery_leaves_the_journal_behind`): the reactivation crashed at `fsx.mutate.logged@N` (activated, no `done`; `<F>.jsonl` in place). Then:

- `install gh:o/bar -t retail --json` with `doctor.recover.step=error@1`: the repair's rollback fails on its first inverse, so it is unsettled; F is behind it on the caller's own target, so the install fails with the repair's code (the code E5's recovery gives an injected failure: `io`, as folder recovery's `engine.recover.step` does, with no `details.reason`), `details.journal_pending` F, `details.tx` the repair, `details.resource` `journal:<F>`; the retail client hashes as before; F's journal is untouched.
- `update -t classic_era --json` (unarmed): the repair is settled by its pass 1 now (rolled back), F leaves the listing with it, the update succeeds; end state `before()`.
- A second case arms `doctor.recover.step=error@1` on `config set` instead: the warning for F's `journal_pending` behind the repair carries `(io)`, `config set` itself succeeds (its write does not overlap the repair's resources), and the next command settles both.
- The differential compares only with the commands that finish recovery (E11's rule: an injected failure is not predicted).

**7. The unknowable owner** (`barrier_an_unknowable_repair_holds_every_journal`): a `MidSwap` F pending at its own name, plus a planted repair journal whose complete `prepared` line does not decode (`tests/common/repairs.rs`'s `plant_undecodable_prepared`, from omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14.4):

- `install gh:o/bar -t retail --json`: fails with the planted journal's stop (`state_corrupt`, `journal_unreadable`), `details.journal_pending` F, `details.tx` the planted journal, `details.resource` `journal:<F>`; F untouched.
- `update -t classic_era --json`: recovery leaves F (a `journal_pending` warning naming F and `(journal_unreadable)`), and the run is refused by the closed set.
- `config set check_interval_hours 6 --json`: the same warning, then refused by the closed set.
- `status --json`: runs.
- The test then moves the planted journal out of `<state>/journal/` by hand (standing in for its set-aside); `config set` recovers F (`journal_recovered` naming F) and succeeds.
- Differential: F is predicted `BehindBarrier { owner: <planted> }` with `expected()` `Stops { state_corrupt, journal_unreadable }`, and agrees with each command.

**8. Pass 3's wait** (`barrier_a_repair_waits_behind_an_unresolved_folder_journal`):

- F2: a folder journal on `_retail_` (an update of `foo` killed at `engine.swap.after_exchange`) made unrecoverable by rewriting one step's `from_id.ino` (E11's planted step-in-neither-state).
- R3: a quarantine of `<retail>/Interface/AddOns/Foo` committed by the child driver without recovering first, killed at `fsx.mutate.executed@1` (pending, overlapping F2's protected set).
- R4: a chmod repair of a test file under `<state>/omaddons/` killed the same way (pending, disjoint).
- `config set check_interval_hours 6 --json`: F2 is reported (`step_unrecognized`) and left; R3 is not recovered (its rename stays, a `journal_pending` warning `repair transaction <R3> waits behind transaction <F2>, … (step_unrecognized)`); R4 is rolled back. Differential: R3 `BehindBarrier { owner: F2 }`.
- `fence::load(&paths, &[retail])` (in process) holds a fence on `<retail>/Interface/AddOns/Foo/` whose stop is F2's (`tx` F2, `step_unrecognized`): R3 waits fenced with the journal it waits behind.

**9. In-process differential states** (`tests/journal.rs`): an owner stuck (its inverse's live path changed), an owner unknowable, and a suspension rolled back by pass 1 so that F reappears in pass 2's listing; for each, `journal::diagnose` then `recover_all` in process (`Caller::Under`), compared with `assert_agrees`.

**10. Privacy:** every scene has a `WTF/` with `FAKEACCT`/`FakeRealm`/`FakeChar`; every command runs with `--progress json` and `Ran::assert_private`; the serialized diagnoses contain none of the names.

**11. Existing matrices:** every existing test in `tests/engine_crash.rs` and `tests/journal.rs` passes without edits (common rule 14 and checkpoint criterion 13: "every crash matrix passes unchanged"). If E11's differential helper assumed listing order rather than the diagnoses' order for "the first journal whose outcome fails the caller", update it to the diagnoses' order (the three passes).

**Files:** `tests/engine_crash.rs` (a `barrier` section with items 2–8 and the child driver if E5's is not reusable), `tests/common/barrier.rs` (new), `tests/common/mod.rs`, `tests/journal.rs` (item 9), `tests/common/differential.rs` (only if item 11 requires it).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The reactivation matrix passes for every boundary with `config set`, and at the three key boundaries with an `install` on the journal's own client and an `update` on the other client: whole before without `done`, whole after from `done` on, never a mixture, F never recovered ahead of its repair; every primitive boundary and every on-path repair failpoint fired.
- [ ] The swapped variant passes: F rolls forward after its repair settles, its history line appended once.
- [ ] The suspension matrix passes for both orders: rolled back and F recovered in the same command without `done`; rolled forward and F left in quarantine from `done` on; every boundary fired.
- [ ] Recovery crashed at every inverse of a reactivation's rollback, then recovered, then recovered three more times, ends in the same whole before state each time.
- [ ] An injected I/O failure in recovery leaves the repair unsettled and F behind it: the own-target command fails with the repair's stop and `details.resource` `journal:<F>`, changing nothing; the next command settles both in order.
- [ ] An unknowable repair holds every journal: F is never recovered while it exists, every committing command is refused, `status` runs; once it is moved away, F is recovered.
- [ ] Pass 3 makes an overlapping pending repair wait behind an unresolved folder journal and recovers a disjoint one.
- [ ] The differential of E11 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.11`, `journal::diagnose`) agrees with real recovery in every case above and in `tests/journal.rs`'s planted barrier states.
- [ ] No output names an account, realm or character, and no serialized diagnosis does.
- [ ] Every existing crash matrix and `tests/journal.rs` case passes unchanged.
- [ ] The design gate: this matrix is green in `argc gate`; its counts (cases, boundaries fired) are quoted in the close comment, and `argc e2e engine_crash` runs it with verbose logs.

## Test Plan

Beads this section names: E5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`, the repair transaction), E11 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.11`), H6 and G3 (named where used), and T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`).

### Unit tests

`tests/common/barrier.rs` carries one self-check in the gate: `the_scene_builds_a_valid_reactivation` (`barrier::validate` accepts the reactivation's primitives, its count is `N`, and the set-aside it reverts committed).

### Integration and end-to-end tests

Items 2–9: each a `#[test]` in `tests/engine_crash.rs` (or `tests/journal.rs` for item 9), each case a fresh home, the real binary for every recovering command and E5's child driver for every repair, with E11's `predict` before and `assert_agrees` after every recovering command. The matrices iterate boundaries inside one test each and record `crashed_at`; the cases of different tests run in parallel.

### Logging

- `let log = tlog!();` per test, `log.case(<boundary>)` per crash case, with `log.note` of the boundary, whether the child aborted and whether the repair's journal held `done`.
- `log.step` for "build F", "set aside", "reactivate (crash at <b>)", "status changes nothing", "recover with <command>", "assert whole state".
- Every command through `log.run`/`log.cmd(..).failpoints(..)`; the child driver's outcome through `log.json`.
- `log.tree` of every `Trees` member before and after; on a mixture, `log.diff` against both `before()` and `after()`, printing the first differing paths.
- `log.json("diagnoses", …)` from `predict`; the journal lines of the repair and of F before each recovery.
- At the end of each matrix, `log.json("crashed_at", …)` and the count of cases, quoted in the close comment.
- `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG=verbose argc e2e engine_crash` runs the section with every step echoed.

There are no checkpoint-only tests here: H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the checkpoint) reruns every crash matrix, these barrier cases included, after G3 (`omad-7ccp`, group commit) as a regression check.

## Considerations

Beads this section names: D8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8`, the approval checked again under the commit lock), E5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`, the repair transaction), E9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9`, the M3 build against M4 state), E11 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.11`, `journal::diagnose`), F9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`, the safety harness), G3 (`omad-7ccp`, group commit), E7 and F2 (named where used) and the parent's parts.

- **Run time.** About 30 boundaries per matrix, three matrices plus the variants: on the order of 150 cases, each a fresh home and two or three commands (about 0.5 to 1 s each on tmpfs). Run the matrices as separate tests so they parallelize; never drop a boundary to save time (F9's rule for the harness, applied here). If the section runs past a minute in the gate, make fixture setup cheaper (a shared recorded-fixture server, fewer folders), not the matrix smaller.
- **Hot spot `tests/engine_crash.rs`** (shared with E5, E11, D8 and G3): add a `barrier` section and its helpers; touch no existing helper except as item 11 requires; rebase before each gate run.
- **What a failure means.** A mixture, or F recovered ahead of its repair, is a defect in omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14.3 (the order) or in E5's per-journal recovery; reopen the part, or file a bug `discovered-from` omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14 and block this part on it. A boundary that never fires means the scene does not exercise the path it claims: fix the scene.
- **Older builds** are E9's: E9 characterizes an M3 build recovering a journal an M4 undo has just activated (it ignores the barrier) and its orphan sweep around a crashed reactivation.
- **For the dependents:** E7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7`) and F2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.2`) reuse `BarrierScene` for their own fixers' crash cases, instead of building a second scene.

## Dependencies

- **Parent:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14 (Fences and activation barriers). This subtask is the leaf's design gate: the leaf closes only after it.
- **Before it:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14.3: the barrier, the passes and the `BehindBarrier` verdict this matrix crashes and checks. It reuses omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14.4's `tests/common/repairs.rs` planting helpers when that part is on `main` (otherwise it adds the one it needs, `plant_undecodable_prepared`, to the same file).
- **Test infrastructure:** T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs and the `argc e2e` runner) blocks this part.
- **Uses, from the leaf's blockers:** E5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`: `lower`, `commit`, its failpoints and its child driver) and E11 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.11`: the differential helper).

comments.text:
decided (where the tree made me deviate from the plan):

- **Its own test crate, `tests/barrier_crash.rs`, not a section of `tests/engine_crash.rs`.** Appended to that 6,000-line file, the section tripped a whole-file heuristic of ubs ("secret compared with ==", 25 criticals on pre-existing lines such as `r.code == -1`; the committed file and the section alone each scan clean), which fails the gate. A crate of its own also runs the matrices in parallel with the engine's, as the bead's run-time note asks. It has its own `child_repair` entry point and the `e2e suite:` line (`argc e2e barrier` runs it). `tests/engine_crash.rs` is unchanged.
- **The reactivation is built by the scene**, as the bead decided: `common::repairs::reactivation` inverts the committed set-aside's own lowered steps (each inverse's `pre` is what the set-aside found, a directory's stamp included; its `post` what the set-aside left), the journal first under its provisional name, the activation last; `barrier::validate` accepts it (`the_scene_builds_a_valid_reactivation`). The child driver gained a `Suspend` fix spec, a reactivation mode (`OMADDONS_REPAIR_REACTIVATE`), its lowered steps in its outcome, and the error's message.
- **Item 6, the injected I/O failure:** `doctor.recover.step` fires after an inverse has run, so the rollback's first inverse (the activation's) has already put F back under its provisional name when the failure comes: no pass lists F while its repair is unsettled, and every command (install on F's client, install on the other, `config set`) succeeds with the repair's `(io)` stuck warning; the next command settles it, whole before. The bead's own-target failure with an `io` stop cannot be produced this way; it is proved in process (`engine::journal`'s `a_behind_journal_of_the_callers_target_fails_it_with_the_owners_stop`), and through the binary with a stuck owner instead (next item).
- **Added: `barrier_a_journal_behind_a_stuck_set_aside`** (a set-aside killed after its first step line, F's journal then replaced by another inode): F stays at its own name behind an owner recovery cannot settle. An install on F's client fails with the owner's stop (`internal`, `step_unrecognized`, `journal_pending` F, `tx` the set-aside, `resource` `journal:<F>`), changing nothing; an install on the other client commits; `config set` warns and goes on.
- **Item 7, the unknowable owner:** a committing command stages before it takes the lock, so the closed set refuses it at that first write, before its recovery runs: its error is the planted journal's own (`journal_pending`/`tx` the planted repair, `resource` `journal:<it>`), not F's behind error. `config set` recovers first, so F's `journal_pending` warning with `(journal_unreadable)` appears, then its write is refused. F is never recovered until the planted journal is moved away.
- **Item 9 in process** (`tests/journal.rs`): the stuck owner and the suspension rolled back by pass 1 are held to the differential in process. The unknowable owner is held to it through the binary (item 7) only: in-process `recover_all` has no first write for the closed fences to refuse, which the differential's callers model.
- **E11's differential (`tests/common/differential.rs`), item 11:** it already compared in the diagnoses' order (the three passes). Three changes for barriers: `reason_in` reads the behind texts; `warned` prefers the warning whose subject is the transaction (a behind text names its owner too); and `assert_agrees` models a closed repair by the caller (a committing command is refused before its recovery: only that repair's stop is seen, other journals untouched or reported as a reader reports them; under the lock alone it warns in pass 1 and fails at the write after every pass) and the warnings recovery loses when a later journal fails the command (omad-ef89), a reader's identical report accepted in their place.
- **A repair killed before its `prepared` line** leaves only its in-flight lock (the orphan sweep's, once old): whole before allows exactly that lock.
