title: The view's layer model, bounded reads, and the config, registry and records layers
description:
Part 1 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.2 (`DoctorView`: the tolerant view). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

The leaf builds `doctor::view::DoctorView`, the doctor's picture of the machine. Today every command loads the machine through `World::load` (`src/app/world.rs:60-154`), which returns `state_corrupt` as soon as `config.toml` (`:72`) or `registry.json` (`:78`) cannot be read: right for a change, wrong for a diagnosis. The view instead loads each layer separately, lazily and at most once; a layer that fails becomes one content-free finding plus an unavailable layer, and the checks that need it are later listed as skipped (M4-D43: "a skipped check must not read as a pass"). Nothing in the view writes.

This part lays the skeleton the other four parts hang on: the view type and its once-only lazy cells, the record of failures and the findings they become, the bounded file read, and the three layers every later layer leans on, config, registry and records. It also registers the two failure modes whose findings only the view produces (`fm-configs-config-parse-error`, `fm-schemas-state-corrupt`) and the listing bound `DOCTOR_SCAN_MAX_ENTRIES`. It is its own step because discovery (part 2) and the machine layers (part 3) both build on exactly these types, and they can then proceed in parallel.

**What the registry leaf provides** (E1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`, the failure-mode registry and finding model) is closed before this leaf starts): `src/doctor/registry.rs` with `FailureMode`, `Tier`, `Layer` (`Config`, `Registry`, `Discovery`, `Records`, `Inventory`), `Subsystem` and `FAILURE_MODES` with the seven moved ids; `src/doctor/finding.rs` with `Finding` (`instance`, `label`), `Evidence`, `Remediation`, `Confidence`, `Severity` and the helper that builds `instance` and `label` together. If E1 declared a placeholder `DoctorView` so its `detect` signature compiles, this part replaces it at the same path.

**Decisions this part implements:** M4-D43 (above); M4-D42 (evidence holds paths, line numbers, sizes and reasons, never file content, and never a path below `WTF/`); M4-D41 (directly observed, so `confidence: high`); M4-D30 (instance keys `<fm-id>@<target key | machine>[:<discriminator>]` with `path=<normalized absolute path>` as the discriminator here); DEC-3 (every serialized type derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`, maps are `BTreeMap`).

**Facts it relies on** (at `c0ab5e9`):

- `Config::parse(text, path)` (`src/state/config.rs:466-542`) returns `state_corrupt` with `details {path, line, column}` for a TOML or type error (`corrupt`, `:772-783`) or `{path, line, column: 1, key}` for a value out of range (`invalid`, `:799-811`). Its message quotes the TOML parser, which can quote file content. `Config::load` (`:442-463`) reads without a bound; a missing file is the default config (`LoadedConfig`, `:427-437`).
- `store::load_bytes::<T>(path, bytes)` (`src/state/store.rs:250-273`): a decode failure is `state_corrupt` with `details {path}` (`:381-388`); a newer version that does not decode is `state_too_new` with `details {path, schema_version}` (`:390-402`); a newer one that decodes returns `VersionStatus::Newer`. `load_registry` (`src/state/registry.rs:80-89`) and `load_record` (`src/state/records.rs:59-67`) wrap the unbounded `store::load`; a missing registry is empty, a missing record is empty at generation 0.
- `DISCOVERY_FILE_MAX_BYTES` = 1 MiB (`src/limits.rs:65`, `REGISTRY` row `:408-414`); the plan bounds `registry.json` reads by it (§6.5). `discover::read_bytes` (`src/discover/mod.rs:661-668`) cannot tell missing from unreadable from oversized; `discover::open_regular` (`:672-678`) shows the FIFO-safe open.
- `Paths::config_file()` (`src/state/paths.rs:166-168`), `registry_file()` (`:271-273`), `targets_dir()` (`:275-277`), `target_record(key)` (`:280-282`), `files_index(key)` = `<key>.files.json` (`:285-287`).
- `tests/single_writer.rs` forbids `OpenOptions` and every write outside `src/fsx/` (`:37`, `:97-109`); `crate::source_scan::production_code` (`src/source_scan.rs`) gives a file's production code for source-scan unit tests.

## Technical Approach

### Files

`src/doctor/view.rs` (new), `src/doctor/mod.rs` (`pub mod view;`), `src/doctor/registry.rs` (`Layer::ALL`, `Layer::depends_on`, two rows), `src/doctor/finding.rs` (optional `Evidence` fields if absent), `src/limits.rs` and `src/snapshots/omaddons__limits__tests__limit_registries.snap`.

### The view (this part's shape; parts 2–4 add to it)

```rust
pub struct DoctorView {
    paths: Paths,
    config: OnceCell<LayerState<LoadedConfig>>,
    registry: OnceCell<LayerState<Loaded<Registry>>>,
    records: OnceCell<LayerState<Records>>,
    failures: RefCell<Vec<LayerFailure>>,
    warnings: RefCell<Vec<Warning>>,
    loaded: RefCell<BTreeSet<Layer>>,
}
impl DoctorView {
    pub fn load(ctx: &Context) -> Result<DoctorView>;  // Paths::from_env()?, then load_at (part 2 adds ViewOptions)
    pub fn load_at(paths: Paths) -> DoctorView;        // never fails
    pub fn paths(&self) -> &Paths;
    pub fn config(&self) -> Option<&LoadedConfig>;
    pub fn registry(&self) -> Option<&Loaded<Registry>>;
    pub fn records(&self) -> Option<&Records>;
    pub fn target_ref(&self, key: TargetKey) -> TargetRef;   // registry id, else the key's string
    pub fn failures(&self) -> Vec<LayerFailure>;            // sorted
    pub fn failure_findings(&self) -> Vec<Finding>;         // sorted
    pub fn warnings(&self) -> Vec<Warning>;
    pub fn loaded_layers(&self) -> BTreeSet<Layer>;
}
pub enum LayerState<T> { Available(T), Unavailable(Unavailable) }
pub struct Unavailable { pub layer: Layer, pub cause: Layer }
pub struct Records { by_key: BTreeMap<TargetKey, LayerState<Loaded<TargetRecord>>> }
impl Records {
    pub fn get(&self, key: &TargetKey) -> Option<&Loaded<TargetRecord>>;
    pub fn available(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = (&TargetKey, &Loaded<TargetRecord>)>;
    pub fn unavailable(&self) -> impl Iterator<Item = &TargetKey>;
}
pub struct LayerFailure { pub layer: Layer, pub fm: &'static str, pub target: Option<TargetKey>,
                          pub path: PathBuf, pub evidence: Evidence, pub title: String }
```

- Each accessor initializes its `std::cell::OnceCell` on first use and inserts its layer into `loaded`; a second call reads nothing. No `&mut self` method and no write method exist. Failures and warnings are pushed to their `RefCell`s as layers load, and `failures()`, `failure_findings()` and `warnings()` sort what they return (by severity, then failure-mode id, then target id, then path), so output never depends on access order.
- The type's doc comment says: not `Sync`, not `RefUnwindSafe` (E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, `doctor diagnose`) wraps detector calls in `AssertUnwindSafe`), and a panic during a layer load leaves that cell empty so the next access retries.
- `target_ref(key)`: `TargetRef { id, key }` (the finding's `target` type, from E1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`, the registry and finding model)), `id` the registry entry's id when the Registry layer is available and has the key, else the key's string. Never from discovery, so a label never depends on which layers loaded.
- A `#[cfg(test)] DoctorView::preloaded(paths, Preloaded { config, registry, records, … })` fills cells directly for unit tests of later parts (part 4 extends it).

### `read_bounded`

```rust
pub enum BoundedRead { Missing, Bytes(Vec<u8>), TooLarge { bytes: u64 }, NotAFile, Unreadable { kind: std::io::ErrorKind } }
pub(crate) fn read_bounded(path: &Path, max: u64) -> BoundedRead;
```

`symlink_metadata` NotFound → `Missing`; `metadata` error (a dangling symlink included) → `Unreadable`; not a regular file → `NotAFile` (never opened, so a FIFO cannot block); `File::open` (never `OpenOptions`), re-check the handle's metadata is a regular file, `take(max + 1).read_to_end`; more than `max` → `TooLarge { bytes: <metadata len> }`. The view always passes `DISCOVERY_FILE_MAX_BYTES`.

Decided while writing this bead: a dangling symlink is `Unreadable`, not `Missing`, so a `config.toml` symlink whose target vanished never reads as the defaults; and one bound, `DISCOVERY_FILE_MAX_BYTES`, for every file the view decodes (a record is about 1 KB per addon). Extend that constant's doc comment and its `REGISTRY` description to "…or from one state or config file the doctor's view reads" (keep any wording C1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.1`, misplaced clients) or C2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.2`, a client named as an addon, and `-t all`) added for the target vocabulary) and re-accept `limit_registries`.

### Config layer

`read_bounded(paths.config_file())`: `Missing` → `Available(LoadedConfig { path, exists: false, ..Default })`; `Bytes` → `String::from_utf8` (failure → `not_utf8` with the line and column of the first invalid byte, computed from `Utf8Error::valid_up_to()`), then `Config::parse(&text, &path)`: `Ok((config, warnings))` → `Available(LoadedConfig { config, warnings, path, exists: true, text: Some(text) })` and the warnings into the view's warnings; `Err(e)` → `Unavailable` plus a failure. Reason: `invalid_value` when `e.details` has `key`, else `parse`; `line`, `column` (and `key`) copied from `details`; `TooLarge` → `too_large` (`bytes`, `limit: "DISCOVERY_FILE_MAX_BYTES"`); `NotAFile` → `not_a_file`; `Unreadable` → `unreadable`. Every config failure is `fm-configs-config-parse-error`, machine-scoped, `path` the config file. The parser's message is never copied.

### Registry layer

`read_bounded(paths.registry_file())`: `Missing` → `Available(Loaded { Registry::default(), CURRENT, Current })`; `Bytes` → `store::load_bytes::<Registry>`: `Ok` (a `Newer` that decodes included) → `Available` and its version warning (`Loaded::warning`) into the view's warnings; `Err` with code `state_too_new` → `fm-schemas-state-version-newer`, `reason: "newer"`, `observed` from `details.schema_version`; any other `Err` → `fm-schemas-state-corrupt`, `reason: "decode"`; `TooLarge`, `NotAFile`, `Unreadable` → `state-corrupt` with that reason. Machine-scoped.

### Records layer

Keys: the Registry layer's entry keys when it is available (loading it), united with the names in `<state>/targets/` that are exactly `<TargetKey>.json` (the stem parses as a `TargetKey`; `<key>.files.json`, `.omaddons-*` and anything else ignored), from one `read_dir` that stops after `DOCTOR_SCAN_MAX_ENTRIES` entries. Per key: `read_bounded(paths.target_record(&key))`: `Missing` → an empty record at generation 0 (`TargetRecord::empty(key)`, `Current`), exactly as `load_record`; `Bytes` → `load_bytes::<TargetRecord>` mapped as for the registry, the failure scoped to that key. A missing `targets/` dir → `Available` and empty. A listing error → `Unavailable` and `state-corrupt` (`unreadable`, the dir's path); more than `DOCTOR_SCAN_MAX_ENTRIES` entries → `Unavailable` and `state-corrupt` (`too_many_entries`, `count`, `limit: "DOCTOR_SCAN_MAX_ENTRIES"`). The listing function takes its bound as a parameter so the unit test can use 2.

Decided while writing this bead: records never require the registry (a corrupt `registry.json` must not stop the records-only checks), and an overflowing listing fails the whole layer closed (a record past the cut might be the broken one; `<state>/targets/` holding 20,000 entries is damage, since omaddons writes two files per client there).

### `DOCTOR_SCAN_MAX_ENTRIES`

`pub const DOCTOR_SCAN_MAX_ENTRIES: u64 = 20_000;` in `src/limits.rs`, `REGISTRY` row `limit("DOCTOR_SCAN_MAX_ENTRIES", LimitValue::Count(DOCTOR_SCAN_MAX_ENTRIES), "count", None, "Most entries one doctor walk or listing visits per run")`, its `LIMIT_NAMES` entry, the `limit_registries` snapshot re-accepted (review the diff: one row added, one description extended). The plan's §7.9 lists it under E3 with the same value and meaning; decided while writing this bead: it lands here because this part's listing is the doctor's first, and E3 (which this leaf blocks) uses it for its `Budget`'s entry counter.

### Failure findings

`failure_findings()` maps each `LayerFailure` through E1's helper to a `Finding`: the row's id, severity, subsystem; `instance` `<fm>@machine:path=<normalized absolute path>` or `<fm>@<key>:path=<…>`; `label` `config.toml`, `registry.json`, `targets/`, or `<target_ref(key).id> · targets/<key>.json`; `target` `null` or `target_ref(key)`; `addon` and `folder` `null`; `confidence: high`; `evidence` (§ below); the failure's `title`; a prose `remediation` with no argv.

Evidence keys: `path` (always), `line`, `column`, `key` (a config key name from `details.key` only), `reason` (`parse`, `invalid_value`, `not_utf8`, `too_large`, `not_a_file`, `unreadable`, `decode`, `newer`, `too_many_entries`), `observed` (`newer`: the on-disk version), `bytes` and `limit` (`too_large`), `count` and `limit` (`too_many_entries`). If E1's `Evidence` lacks `key`, `reason`, `bytes` or `limit`, add them as optional fields following E1's presence rule.

Titles and remediations (decided while writing this bead; H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, the pre-freeze contract audit) may polish):

| Reason | Title | Remediation (prose, no argv) |
|---|---|---|
| config `parse` | `config.toml does not parse (line L, column C)` | `fix line L, column C of <path>; omaddons never rewrites config.toml` |
| config `invalid_value` | `config.toml has an invalid value for <key> (line L)` | `fix the value of <key> on line L of <path>` |
| config `not_utf8` | `config.toml is not UTF-8 (line L, column C)` | `save <path> as UTF-8` |
| config `too_large` | `config.toml is larger than omaddons reads` | `shorten <path>: omaddons reads at most 1 MiB of it` |
| state `too_large` | `<file> is larger than omaddons reads` | `<path> is over 1 MiB, which omaddons never writes; restore it from a backup` |
| `not_a_file` | `<file> is not a regular file` | `replace <path> with a regular file` |
| `unreadable` | `<file> cannot be read` | `make <path> readable by your user` |
| `decode` | `<file> is corrupt` | `omaddons cannot decode <path> and never rewrites it; restore it from a backup of the state directory` |
| `newer` | `<file> was written by a newer omaddons (version V)` | `upgrade omaddons` |
| `too_many_entries` | `targets/ holds more entries than omaddons ever writes` | `inspect <path>: it holds over 20000 entries` |

None of these texts names a runnable omaddons command (common rule 8's prose rule).

### `Layer` and the two rows (`src/doctor/registry.rs`)

- `Layer::ALL` (Config, Registry, Discovery, Records, Inventory) and `Layer::depends_on(self) -> &'static [Layer]` (Discovery → Config, Registry; Inventory → Discovery, Records; others none). Part 3 appends seven variants.
- Two rows with Appendix B's metadata, as E1 registered the seven published ids:
  - `fm-configs-config-parse-error`: `configs`, P1, `cached`, `online: false`, `cost_ms: 1`, `requires: []`, title `config.toml cannot be read`, a description (config.toml does not parse, holds an out-of-range value, or cannot be read) and a `why` (every change command fails closed with `state_corrupt` until it is fixed, and the doctor skips every check that depends on the configuration), no fixer, the manual remediation returning the finding's prose; `detect` = the view's failures with this id (it calls `view.config()`).
  - `fm-schemas-state-corrupt`: `schemas`, P0, `default`, `cost_ms: 2`, `requires: []`, title `a state file cannot be read`, description and `why` alike; `detect` = the view's failures with this id (it calls `registry()` and `records()`; part 3 adds the journals, lock and history layers).
  - The moved `fm-schemas-state-version-newer` row's `detect` also returns the view's failures with its id (calling `registry()` and `records()`), beside its own rule (part 4 moves that rule onto the view).
  - A row that reports a layer's failure never `requires` that layer. Each detector returns the failures as findings through the same mapping as `failure_findings()`, so the instances are equal and part 4's merge keeps one.

Decided while writing this bead: registering these two rows in this leaf. Appendix B lists row 19 under F4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.4`, configs, userland state and permissions) and row 12 under F3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.3`, state files and schemas); those leaves keep the fixture, the README doctor-table row and the true and false positive tests (common rule 19), and F3 adds its decode of every `KINDS` file.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `DoctorView::load_at(paths)` never fails, and `config()`, `registry()`, `records()` each read their files at most once per view and only when called (`loaded_layers()` shows exactly the layers asked for).
- [ ] `read_bounded` distinguishes missing, regular (up to and including `max` bytes), oversized, non-regular (never opened: a FIFO does not block) and unreadable (a dangling symlink included).
- [ ] Config: a TOML error gives `config() == None` and one `fm-configs-config-parse-error` failure with `path`, `line`, `column`, `reason: "parse"`; an out-of-range value gives `invalid_value` with `key` and `line`; non-UTF-8 gives `not_utf8` with the first bad byte's line and column; oversized, directory, mode 000 and dangling symlink give their reasons; a missing file is the default config; no failure's JSON contains any planted text of the file.
- [ ] Registry: a missing file is an empty registry; a newer file that decodes is available with `Newer` and records no failure; a newer one that does not decode is `fm-schemas-state-version-newer` with `observed`; invalid JSON, no `schema_version`, an empty file, oversized and mode 000 are `fm-schemas-state-corrupt` with their reasons.
- [ ] Records: keys are the registry's (when readable) plus every `<TargetKey>.json` in `<state>/targets/` and nothing else; a registry key without a file is an empty record at generation 0; one corrupt record makes only that key unavailable, with a failure scoped to it; a corrupt registry leaves the listed records available; a listing over the bound makes the layer unavailable with `too_many_entries`.
- [ ] `failure_findings()` gives `Finding`s with the instance and label forms above, `confidence: high`, prose remediations without argv, sorted.
- [ ] The rows `fm-configs-config-parse-error` and `fm-schemas-state-corrupt` are registered with the metadata above and pass the registry's invariant test; their detectors return exactly the view's failures of their id.
- [ ] `DOCTOR_SCAN_MAX_ENTRIES` (20,000) has its `REGISTRY` row and `LIMIT_NAMES` entry, `DISCOVERY_FILE_MAX_BYTES`'s description names the view, and `limit_registries` is re-accepted.
- [ ] `view_source_never_writes` passes over `src/doctor/view.rs`.
- [ ] `status`'s output is unchanged (its snapshots pass untouched).

title: Discovery without writes: `FullNoWrite`, `World::assemble`, and the discovery and inventory layers
description:
Part 2 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.2 (`DoctorView`: the tolerant view). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

The leaf builds the doctor's tolerant view of the machine (`doctor::view::DoctorView`): each layer loaded separately, lazily and once; a failing layer becomes one content-free finding plus an unavailable layer; checks that need it are listed as skipped, never reported clean (M4-D43); and the view writes nothing. Part 1 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.2.1) built the view type, the bounded read and the config, registry and records layers.

This part adds the two layers that need the discovered clients: **Discovery** (every client on the machine, reconciled with the registry) and **Inventory** (one client's `AddOns/`, built on demand). The plan says the discovery layer is "`World::load_with` with the doctor's tolerant config and registry". At `c0ab5e9` that call cannot be given a config or a registry (it loads and fails on them itself), and in its normal mode it writes `<cache>/discovery.json`, which would break the leaf's rule that loading the view writes nothing (checkpoint criterion 9 hashes `<cache>`). So this part splits `World::load_with` into its loads and a reusable `World::assemble`, and adds a discovery mode that scans without writing. It is its own step because it is the only part that changes code every command runs (`World::load_with`), and that change must land with every existing test passing untouched.

**Decisions this part implements:** M4-D43 and its rejected alternative (i): the view never runs discovery with a default config in place of a broken one (an `extra_roots` entry or a `[targets.*]` override the broken file holds would vanish, and clients would look gone), so Discovery requires Config and Registry. M4-D33: a diagnosis writes only its own run directory, so the view it reads from writes nothing, the discovery cache included.

**Facts it relies on** (at `c0ab5e9`):

- `World::load_with(ctx, mode)` (`src/app/world.rs:65-154`): `Paths::from_env()?` (`:66`); `Config::load(&paths)?` (`:72`) and its warnings (`:73`); the rules table (`:75-77`); `load_registry(&paths)?` (`:78`) and its version warning (`:79`); the extra and registered roots (`:81-101`); the running clients' prefixes for `Full` and `Rescan` (`:103-106`); `discover_cached` (`:116-118`); `reconcile` (`:119-120`); `apply_target_overrides` (`:121`); unknown-flavor warnings (`:122-128`); `journal::pending_warnings` and `ctx.notes.journal_found` (`:132-139`); `GithubToken::resolve` and its warnings (`:141-142`). Every batch of warnings goes to `ctx.notes` and into `World::warnings` in that order.
- `DiscoveryMode` (`src/discover/cache.rs:28-38`) is `NoScan`, `Full`, `Rescan`. `discover_cached` (`cache.rs:146-289`) scans unless `NoScan` (`:187-213`) and writes the cache when it changed unless `NoScan` (`:278-287`, `write_cache` at `:300-311`, an untracked `Writer::Derived` session). Its other users: `status` (`src/app/status.rs:610-614`) and `targets` (`src/app/targets.rs:212-214`).
- `GithubToken::resolve` reads the stored token file's bytes (`src/sources/github_token.rs:78-123`); `GithubToken::none()` (`:61`) is public; `GithubToken::source()` (`:142`) reports where a token came from.
- `World::select_many(ctx)` (`world.rs:245-250`) calls `missing_named` (`src/discover/registry.rs:736-761`, which refuses a registered client whose directory is gone) and then the private `select_many` (`world.rs:254-278`).
- `inventory::inventory_shared(target, record, shared, table, depth)` (`src/inventory.rs:160`); `World::sibling_records` (`world.rs:188-194`) and `inventory::sibling_records` (`inventory.rs:296-311`) load siblings with the unbounded `load_record`; `discover::shared::siblings(target, all)` (`src/discover/shared.rs:26`); `discover::registry::read_marker(client_dir)` (`registry.rs:43`, a read). An `AddOns/` that cannot be listed is an `io` error (`inventory.rs:148-175`).
- `discover::running::process_prefixes` (`src/discover/running.rs:174-199`) reads `/proc` (or `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT` in debug builds) and keeps only prefixes under the given home.

## Technical Approach

### `DiscoveryMode::FullNoWrite` (`src/discover/cache.rs`)

- New variant with the doc comment "Scan for roots, reusing each unchanged root's cached parse; never write the cache (the doctor's view: a diagnosis writes nothing outside its run directory)."
- `impl DiscoveryMode { pub fn scans(self) -> bool /* all but NoScan */; pub fn writes_cache(self) -> bool /* Full, Rescan */ }`.
- The scan branch (`cache.rs:187-213`) keys on `scans()`; the cache reuse (`reusable`, `:158-160`) treats `FullNoWrite` as `Full`; the write (`:282`) becomes `if changed && mode.writes_cache()`. `stats.written` stays `false` for `FullNoWrite`.
- `World::assemble`'s prefix match gives `FullNoWrite` the running prefixes, as `Full`.

### `World::assemble`, `World::load_with`, `World::select_in` (`src/app/world.rs`)

```rust
pub(crate) fn assemble(
    paths: Paths,
    config: LoadedConfig,
    registry: Loaded<Registry>,
    mode: DiscoveryMode,
    found: &mut dyn FnMut(&[Warning]),
) -> Result<World>;
pub(crate) fn select_in(&self, selector: Option<&str>) -> Result<Vec<&DiscoveredTarget>>;
```

- `assemble` is today's body from `:73` to `:128`: config warnings, rules table, registry warning, roots, prefixes (by `mode`), `discover_cached`, `reconcile`, overrides, unknown-flavor warnings; each batch passed to `found` and appended to `World::warnings`. It sets `github_token: GithubToken::none()` and computes no journal warnings. Doc comment: "builds a world from a config and a registry that already loaded: fail-closed for commands (`load_with`), tolerantly for the doctor's view; resolves no credential."
- `load_with` keeps its signature and does: `Paths::from_env()?`, `Config::load(&paths)?`, `load_registry(&paths)?`, `assemble(paths, config, registry, mode, &mut |b| ctx.notes.warn_all(b))?`, then the journal warnings and `journal_found` (`:132-139`) and the token with its warnings (`:141-142`), each appended to the returned world's `warnings` in today's order. Its result, warnings and notes are unchanged.
- `select_in` is the private `select_many` (`:254-278`) over this world's targets and table, without `missing_named`; `select_many(ctx)` keeps calling `missing_named` first.

Decided while writing this bead: this split and the new mode (rather than a `write: bool` flag), because the mode already is what decides what discovery may do with its cache; and `assemble` resolves no token, because the view's credentials are stat-only and online checks (F7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.7`, plugins, secrets and the network)) resolve the token themselves.

### View options and the Discovery layer (`src/doctor/view.rs`)

```rust
pub struct ViewOptions { pub discovery: ViewDiscovery }
pub enum ViewDiscovery { Scan /* FullNoWrite, the default */, Cached /* NoScan: status --cached */ }
impl DoctorView {
    pub fn load(ctx: &Context, opts: ViewOptions) -> Result<DoctorView>;
    pub fn load_at(paths: Paths, opts: ViewOptions) -> DoctorView;
    pub fn world(&self) -> Option<&World>;
    pub fn inventory(&self, target: &DiscoveredTarget) -> Option<&Inventory>;
}
struct Discovered { world: World, inventories: Vec<OnceCell<LayerState<Inventory>>> } // parallel to world.resolved.targets
```

- `load` and `load_at` gain `opts` (part 1 had none). Decided while writing this bead: the view admits only the two non-writing modes, so "loading the view writes nothing" holds by construction.
- `world()` loads Config and Registry (part 1's accessors). Either unavailable → `Unavailable { layer: Discovery, cause: <its cause> }` and no failure of its own (the cause's finding already stands). Both available → `World::assemble(paths.clone(), config.clone(), registry.clone(), mode, &mut |b| <append to the view's warnings>)`. An `Err` from `assemble` (not expected after `Config::parse` validated the rules) → `Unavailable { cause: Discovery }`, mapped by its code: `state_too_new` → `fm-schemas-state-version-newer`, `state_corrupt` or `io` → `fm-schemas-state-corrupt` (path from `details.path`, `reason: "unreadable"` for `io`, `decode` otherwise); any other code records no finding and its message goes to the view's warnings as a debug note.
- The view's world carries no GitHub token; `world()`'s doc comment says so.

### The Inventory layer

- `inventory(target)` finds `target`'s index in `world.resolved.targets` by `client_dir` and initializes that cell once:
  - its own record: none for an unregistered target (`key: None`, as `status` passes none); else `records().get(key)`, and an unavailable record (or an unavailable Records layer) → `Unavailable { cause: Records }`;
  - its siblings: `discover::shared::siblings(&target.target, all discovered targets)`, each keyed by `target.key` or `read_marker(&client_dir)`; a keyed sibling whose record is unavailable → `Unavailable { cause: Records }` (shared ownership would be misclassified); unkeyed siblings contribute nothing, as today;
  - `inventory_shared(&target.target, record, &siblings, &world.table, Depth::Full)`: `Ok` → `Available`; `Err` (an unlistable `AddOns/`) → `Unavailable { cause: Inventory }` with no finding.
- `inventory()` returns `None` for a target not in the world, for an unavailable world, and for an unavailable inventory. Part 4's `unavailable_targets(Inventory)` reads which cells hold `Unavailable`.

Decided while writing this bead: no finding for an unlistable `AddOns/`, because no failure mode of the catalog describes it (the `addons-dir-not-writable` row of F4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.4`, configs, userland state and permissions) is about writability); part 4's per-target skips are its report.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `DiscoveryMode::FullNoWrite` scans, reuses unchanged cached parses, takes the running prefixes, and never writes `<cache>/discovery.json` (absent before → still absent; present → bytes unchanged even when roots changed); `scans()` and `writes_cache()` are right for all four modes.
- [ ] `World::load_with` is `assemble` plus its loads, journal warnings and token: every existing test (`tests/status.rs`, `tests/targets.rs`, `tests/discover_cache.rs`, the contract suite and the rest) passes without modification.
- [ ] `World::assemble` builds the world from the given config and registry, reports warnings in today's order through `found`, resolves no GitHub token (a planted token file stays unread) and computes no journal warnings.
- [ ] `World::select_in` resolves like `select_many` without refusing a vanished client.
- [ ] The view's `world()` is `None` with `cause: Config` when `config.toml` is broken and `cause: Registry` when `registry.json` is, recording no extra failure; otherwise it is the assembled world in the chosen mode.
- [ ] `inventory(target)` is built once per target on first request; it is unavailable with `cause: Records` when the target's own record or a keyed sibling's is unavailable, and with `cause: Inventory` when `AddOns/` cannot be listed.
- [ ] `view_source_never_writes` still passes.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

One name per case; assertion messages name the case and show input and output.

- **`src/discover/cache.rs`**:
  - `discovery_mode_predicates`: a table of `(mode, scans, writes_cache)` for `NoScan` `(false, false)`, `Full` `(true, true)`, `Rescan` `(true, true)`, `FullNoWrite` `(true, false)`.
  - `full_no_write_scans_but_never_writes_the_cache`: two tempdir homes with no clients (`Paths::with_roots`, `DiscoveryInput { home, ..Default::default() }`, `RulesTable::builtin()`, `ScanLimits::default()`). Case `full_writes`: `Full` → `stats.scanned`, `stats.written`, file present. Case `full_no_write_never_writes`: `FullNoWrite` → `stats.scanned`, `!stats.written`, file absent. Case `full_no_write_keeps_an_existing_cache`: copy the first home's cache bytes into the second's `<cache>`, add an empty `Games/` dir (a changed listing), run `FullNoWrite`: the file's bytes equal the copied ones.
- **`src/app/world.rs`**:
  - `assemble_builds_a_world_from_given_layers`: a tempdir home with no clients; a `Registry` holding one `Origin::Manual` entry whose `install_root` does not exist; `assemble(paths, LoadedConfig::default(), Loaded { value: registry, … }, FullNoWrite, &mut collect)` → `resolved.targets` empty, `resolved.missing` holds the entry, `collect` saw the batches in order, no `discovery.json`.
  - `assemble_never_resolves_the_github_token`: write `<config>/credentials/github` with a token; `assemble` → `world.github_token.source()` is the "no token" source.
  - `select_in_does_not_refuse_a_missing_client`: a world (via `found()`, the module's existing test helper) with `resolved.missing` naming `gone` → `select_in(Some("gone"))` gives `resolve`'s `target_not_found`, not `missing_named`'s "is registered, but … is gone" message; `select_in(Some("retail"))` selects retail.
- **`src/doctor/view.rs`**:
  - `discovery_layer_requires_config_and_registry`: cases `config_broken` (`cause: Config`, one failure total), `registry_broken` (`cause: Registry`), `both_fine` (available, empty home), `cached_mode` (`ViewDiscovery::Cached` with no discovery cache: available, nothing written).
  - `inventory_layer_outcomes`: built on `DoctorView::preloaded` with a world from `found()`-style targets whose `client_dir` is a tempdir holding `Interface/AddOns/Foo/Foo.toc`: `available`; `own_record_unavailable` (`cause: Records`); `keyed_sibling_record_unavailable` (two targets sharing one AddOns dir, the sibling's record unavailable: `cause: Records`); `addons_mode_000` (`cause: Inventory`, no failure); `built_once` (a second call returns the same reference and lists nothing again: remove the TOC between calls and see the first result).

### Integration and end-to-end tests

None in this part; subtask 5 runs discovery on real synthetic clients (`loading_every_layer_writes_nothing`, `scanning_discovery_reuses_the_cache_and_never_writes_it`).

### Logging

Unit tests only, with case names and descriptive assertion messages.

## Considerations

- **Every command goes through `World::load_with`.** Move code, do not rewrite it: keep the statements in their order, so the warnings, notes and their order stay byte-identical. The gate's full suite is the guard; do not edit an existing test to make it pass.
- `status` and `targets` keep `Full`/`Rescan`/`NoScan`; nothing but the view uses `FullNoWrite`.
- `process_prefixes` in `FullNoWrite` reads `/proc`. In an in-process test it reads the real one (an in-process test cannot set `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT`), and it keeps only prefixes under the test's home, so no real client enters. Decided while writing this bead: accepted.
- Inventories are the costliest layer (`Depth::Full` opens every TOC): build one only when a detector asks for that target.
- `src/app/world.rs` and `src/discover/cache.rs` are not hot spots in §10.5, but C2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.2`, `-t all`) and C3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.3`, closest client id) change `resolve` in `src/discover/registry.rs`, which `select_in` calls: rebase onto them if they landed.

title: The machine layers: journals, lock, history, caches, widget, skill and credentials
description:
Part 3 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.2 (`DoctorView`: the tolerant view). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

The leaf builds the doctor's tolerant view of the machine (`doctor::view::DoctorView`): each layer loaded separately, lazily and once; a failing layer becomes one content-free finding plus an unavailable layer; checks that need it are listed as skipped, never reported clean (M4-D43); and the view writes nothing. Part 1 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.2.1) built the view type, the bounded read (`read_bounded`, bounded by `DISCOVERY_FILE_MAX_BYTES`) and the config, registry and records layers.

This part adds the seven machine layers of the plan's §6.13 table that do not need discovery: **Journals**, **Lock**, **History**, **Caches**, **Widget**, **Skill** and **Credentials**, and makes each of them a `Layer` a detector can require. The `Layer` of E1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`, the registry leaf) has only `Config`, `Registry`, `Discovery`, `Records` and `Inventory`; without the seven, a detector reading the journals or the lock would run on an unavailable layer and report nothing, which reads as a pass, the exact failure M4-D43 forbids. Each layer wraps a reader that exists today. It is its own step because it touches only `view.rs` and `registry.rs` and is independent of part 2's discovery work.

**Decisions this part implements:** M4-D43 (above); M4-D42 (no content in evidence: history's damaged lines and credentials' bytes never leave the layer); M4-D33 (the view writes nothing); common rule 15 (bounded listings; exhaustion is reported, never clean).

**Facts it relies on** (at `c0ab5e9`):

- There is no `journal::list` (the plan's name). `journal::pending(paths)` (`src/engine/journal.rs:691-710`) returns every unfinished journal as `Pending { tx, target: Option<TargetKey>, unrecoverable: Option<Unrecoverable> }` (`:681-687`; `Unrecoverable::{TooNew, Unreadable}` with `reason()` `journal_too_new`/`journal_unreadable`, `:489-503`); a journal whose `prepared` line does not decode is attributed through its raw `target_key` (`journal::parse`, `:572-580`). Its only error is a failed listing of `<state>/journal/` (`journals()`, `:610-635`). It writes nothing. `src/engine/journal.rs` is a hot spot, changed in order by E11 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.11`, `journal::diagnose`), E13 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.13`, resource sets and endpoint predicates), E5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`, the repair transaction), E14 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14`, fences and activation barriers) and F1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1`, journal and lock detectors); this part does not edit it.
- `fsx::lock::probe_global(paths)` (`src/fsx/lock.rs:163`) → `LockState::{Free, Held { holder }, Missing}` (`:37-45`), creating nothing; its error is `Error::io` with `details.path` (`src/error.rs:574-577`). Only `src/fsx/lock.rs`, `src/fsx/scope.rs` and `src/state/paths.rs` may contain `lock_file` (`fsx/lock.rs:415-440`).
- `history::read(paths, &HistoryFilter::default())` (`src/state/history.rs:442-445`, `HistoryFilter` `:346-357`) reads the whole file; missing is empty; `HistoryRead` (`:380-397`) has `skipped_lines` and `unreadable[].raw`, the text of damaged lines.
- `Paths::blobs_dir()` = `<cache>/blobs` (`src/state/paths.rs:374-376`). There is no `Paths` entry for `<cache>/plans/` (`Paths::plans_dir()` is `<state>/plans`, `:338-340`, which D4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`, the plan store) moves) or `<cache>/quarantine/`.
- `omarchy::status::widget(paths)` (`src/omarchy/status.rs:63-76`) reads files only and returns `None` without Omarchy's config dir.
- `Paths::skill_dir()` = `$HOME/.claude/skills/omaddons` (`paths.rs:264-266`); the skill file is `SKILL.md` in it (`<skills>/SKILL.md`, §7.7).
- `Paths::credentials_dir()` = `<config>/credentials` (`paths.rs:171-173`); `[sources.<name>] credential` is a `CredentialRef::{Env, File { file }, Command}` (`src/state/config.rs:161-179`), used as configured (`resolve_credential`, `config.rs:958-993`, does no `~` expansion).

## Technical Approach

### `Layer` (`src/doctor/registry.rs`)

Append `Journals`, `Lock`, `History`, `Caches`, `Widget`, `Skill`, `Credentials` (serde snake_case, like the first five). `Layer::ALL` becomes Config, Registry, Discovery, Records, Inventory, Journals, Lock, History, Caches, Widget, Skill, Credentials; `depends_on(Credentials) == [Config]`, the six others none. Decided while writing this bead: every layer of the §6.13 table is requirable, so a check that reads it is skipped, never silently clean, when it fails. E4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4`, `doctor capabilities`) publishes these names in each detector's `requires`.

### The layers (`src/doctor/view.rs`)

Each is a `OnceCell<LayerState<T>>` with an accessor returning `Option<&T>`, recorded in `loaded_layers()`:

| Accessor | Type | Loads | On failure |
|---|---|---|---|
| `journals()` | `Journals { pending: Vec<journal::Pending> }` | `journal::pending(&paths)` | `Err` → `Unavailable` + `fm-schemas-state-corrupt` (machine, `reason: "unreadable"`, `path` from `details.path`, label `journal/`) |
| `lock()` | `LockState` | `probe_global(&paths)` | `Err` → `Unavailable` + `state-corrupt` (machine, `unreadable`, `path` from `details.path`, label `lock`) |
| `history()` | `HistoryRead` | `history::read(&paths, &HistoryFilter::default())` | `Err` → `Unavailable` + `state-corrupt` (machine, `unreadable`, label `history.jsonl`) |
| `caches()` | `Caches { blobs: Listing }` | one-level listing of `paths.blobs_dir()` | listing error → `Unavailable`, no failure |
| `widget()` | `WidgetLayer { info: Option<WidgetInfo> }` | `omarchy::status::widget(&paths)` | never fails |
| `skill()` | `[SkillFile]` | `read_bounded(skill_dir().join("SKILL.md"), DISCOVERY_FILE_MAX_BYTES)` | never fails: the outcome is the entry's `read` |
| `credentials()` | `[CredentialStat]` | stat of each entry of `credentials_dir()` and each configured `{ file }` | unavailable only through Config |

- **Journals.** F1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1`, journal and lock detectors) adds `journal::diagnose`'s classifications (from E11 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.11`)) to `Journals` later. Decided while writing this bead: `journal::pending`, not the plan's nonexistent `journal::list`, and no edit to `journal.rs`.
- **Lock.** Detectors treat `Missing` as `Free`. The failure's path comes from the error; the view's code never names the lock file.
- **History.** Doc comment on the accessor: "`unreadable[].raw` holds damaged lines' text: count them, never put them in evidence (M4-D42)." The read stays today's unbounded `history::read`, the same read `history` and `undo` make; the `default` tier, which reads the full history, is bounded by the detector budgets of E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, `doctor diagnose`).
- **Caches.** `Listing { dir: PathBuf, entries: Vec<ListedEntry>, truncated: bool }`, `ListedEntry { name: String /* lossy */, kind: EntryKind /* File | Dir | Symlink | Other */, bytes: u64 }`, from one `read_dir` and one `symlink_metadata` per entry, sorted by name, at most `DOCTOR_SCAN_MAX_ENTRIES` entries (more → `truncated: true`, and the doc comment says a detector reading a truncated listing must report itself incomplete through E3's `incomplete` record). A missing dir is an empty listing. Directory sizes are not summed (that is a walk: E3's bounded walker). Decided while writing this bead: only `<cache>/blobs/` exists today; D4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`, the plan store) adds a `plans` listing and E5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`) or F6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.6`) a `quarantine` listing, each in its own leaf; a cache listing error records no finding (derived data; no catalog row).
- **Widget.** `WidgetLayer { info }` as returned.
- **Skill.** `SkillFile { dir: PathBuf, file: PathBuf, read: BoundedRead }`, one entry today. Decided while writing this bead: B3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3`, `install-skill`) or F10 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.10`, skill drift), whichever lands after this leaf, adds the `history_tail.skill_dirs[]` directories (at most `SKILL_DIRS_MAX`) to this list.
- **Credentials.** `CredentialStat { path: PathBuf, origin: CredentialOrigin /* Stored | Configured { source: String } */, stat: FileStat }`, `FileStat::{ Missing, Regular { mode: u32, uid: u32, bytes: u64, symlink: bool }, NotRegular { symlink: bool }, Unreadable { kind } }`, from `symlink_metadata` (for `symlink`) and `metadata` (following it). Stored: each entry of `<config>/credentials/` (missing dir → none; at most `DOCTOR_SCAN_MAX_ENTRIES`). Configured: each source in `config().sources` whose `credential` is `CredentialRef::File { file }`, sorted by source name, with `file` as configured. `Env` and `Command` credentials are not files and are not listed. The type has no field that could hold a credential's bytes, and no file is opened. Config unavailable → `Unavailable { layer: Credentials, cause: Config }`.

### `state-corrupt`'s detector

Part 1's `fm-schemas-state-corrupt` row reports the view's failures of its id after calling `registry()` and `records()`; it now also calls `journals()`, `lock()` and `history()`, the other layers that can record that id.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `Layer` has the twelve variants in the order above with snake_case names, `Credentials` depends on `Config`, and the registry's invariant test passes.
- [ ] Journals: no journal dir → empty; an unreadable journal naming a key → `Pending { target: Some(key), unrecoverable: Some(Unreadable) }`; a committed journal → absent; an unlistable `<state>/journal/` → `Unavailable` and one `state-corrupt` failure with the dir's path.
- [ ] Lock: no lock file → `Missing`; free → `Free`; held by another lock holder → `Held` with the holder; an unopenable lock file → `Unavailable` and a `state-corrupt` failure whose path came from the error; the source scan finds no `lock_file` in the view.
- [ ] History: missing → empty; good and bad lines → entries and `skipped_lines`; unreadable → `Unavailable` and a `state-corrupt` failure.
- [ ] Caches: entries sorted by name with kind and size; over the bound → `truncated: true`; unlistable → `Unavailable` with no failure.
- [ ] Widget: no Omarchy config dir → available with `info: None`.
- [ ] Skill: missing, present, oversized and directory `SKILL.md` give `Missing`, `Bytes`, `TooLarge` and `NotAFile` in the one entry.
- [ ] Credentials: stored and configured file credentials are stat'ed (mode, owner, size, symlink), never opened; a missing configured file is `Missing`; with a broken `config.toml` the layer is unavailable with `cause: Config`.
- [ ] `fm-schemas-state-corrupt`'s detector returns the failures of all five layers that can record it.
- [ ] `view_source_never_writes` still passes.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files; the commit lists the seven new `Layer` names for the leaf's close comment.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests (`src/doctor/view.rs`, `src/doctor/registry.rs`)

Tempdir homes with `Paths::with_roots`; one name per case; messages `case <name>: input <…> → got <…>`.

- `journals_layer_outcomes`: `no_journal_dir`; `unreadable_journal_naming_a_key` (the file `<state>/journal/<tx>.jsonl` holding the raw line `{"type":"prepared","schema_version":"1.1","target_key":"<key>"}` and a newline); `committed_journal` (absent from `pending`, built with the module's own journal types in a test); `journal_dir_mode_000` (unavailable, one failure, `path` the dir; mode restored at the end of the case).
- `lock_layer_outcomes`: `no_lock_file` (`Missing`); `free` (a lock file created by acquiring and dropping `GlobalLock::acquire(&paths, "test")`); `held` (a `GlobalLock` held by the test while the view probes in the same process; `probe_global` reports it `Held`, as `tests/status.rs`'s held-lock case observes from a child); `unopenable` (lock file mode 000: unavailable, failure with the error's path).
- `history_layer_outcomes`: `missing`; `two_good_one_bad` (two lines written with the module's own `HistoryEntry` serialization and one garbage line with a newline: `entries.len() == 2`, `skipped_lines == 1`); `mode_000` (unavailable, failure).
- `caches_layer_outcomes`: `no_blobs_dir` (empty, not truncated); `three_blobs_and_a_subdir` (sorted names, kinds `File`/`Dir`, sizes); `over_the_bound` (the listing helper called with a bound of 2: `truncated: true`, two entries); `blobs_dir_mode_000` (unavailable, `failures()` empty).
- `widget_layer_without_omarchy`: `info: None`.
- `skill_layer_outcomes`: `missing`, `present` (bytes equal), `oversized` (`DISCOVERY_FILE_MAX_BYTES + 1`), `directory`.
- `credentials_layer_outcomes`: `stored_0600` (`<config>/credentials/github`, mode 0o600: `Regular { mode: 0o600, symlink: false }`); `configured_0644` (`[sources.github] credential = { file = "<tmp>/token" }` with mode 0o644); `configured_symlink` (a symlink to a 0600 file: `symlink: true`, mode of the target); `configured_missing` (`Missing`); `env_and_command_not_listed`; `config_broken` (unavailable, `cause: Config`). Each case asserts the planted token text appears nowhere in `format!("{:?}", stats)`.
- `state_corrupt_detector_covers_every_state_layer`: failures planted in the registry, one record, the journal dir, the lock and the history; the row's `detect` returns five findings.
- `layer_order_and_dependencies` (part 1's test, extended to the twelve layers).

### Integration and end-to-end tests

None in this part; subtask 5 loads these layers on real synthetic homes (`loading_every_layer_writes_nothing`, `target_selection_scopes_findings_and_keeps_machine_ones`).

### Logging

Unit tests only, with case names and descriptive assertion messages.

## Considerations

- **Mode-000 cases** restore the mode before the tempdir drops (a mode-000 directory cannot be removed by its cleanup otherwise). The tests run as the developer's user in the gate, as the repository's other mode-000 tests do (`tests/inventory.rs:349`, `src/engine/preserve.rs:321`).
- **The in-process held lock**: `GlobalLock` is not re-entrant (`lock.rs:69-71`), but `probe_global` only probes; holding a guard while probing in one process is fine. `probe_global` opens the lock file anew and calls `try_lock_shared` (`lock.rs:176-191`), and an `flock` held through another open file description of the same process blocks it, so the in-process case works; if it ever does not, hold the lock from a child process, as `tests/status.rs` does.
- No layer here can make the view write: each reader is a read (`probe_global` creates nothing, `tests/fsx_lock.rs:196`).
- Hot spot avoided: `src/engine/journal.rs` is untouched.

- Parent: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.2 (`DoctorView`: the tolerant view).
- Before it: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.2.1, whose view type, `LayerState`, `LayerFailure`, `read_bounded` and failure-to-finding mapping this part uses.

title: `Selection`, `--only`/`--skip` validation, the `skipped` bookkeeping, and the moved detectors on the view
description:
Part 4 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.2 (`DoctorView`: the tolerant view). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

The leaf builds the doctor's tolerant view of the machine (`doctor::view::DoctorView`). Parts 1–3 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.2.1, omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.2.2, omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.2.3) built its twelve layers (config, registry, discovery, records, inventory, journals, lock, history, caches, widget, skill, credentials), each loaded lazily and once, each failure recorded as a content-free finding plus an unavailable layer.

This part turns those layers into what the doctor's runtime consumes: the **selection** (`-t`, `--only`, `--skip`, with the closest id as the fix for a typo), the **`skipped` bookkeeping** (a detector whose `requires` names an unavailable layer is listed with the layer that caused it, never run, never reported clean: M4-D43), the rules for which view failures a report shows, the merge that keeps one finding per instance, and the **seven moved detectors** reading the view instead of `status`'s computed data. It is its own step because it is pure logic over the layers, testable with synthetic views, and it is the interface E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, `doctor diagnose` and its runtime) builds on.

**Decisions this part implements:**

- **M4-D43:** detectors whose `requires` names an unavailable layer are reported in `skipped: [{id, reason}]` and counted in `summary.skipped`, never silently dropped, never reported clean. Rejected: running them with defaults in place of the broken layer (findings about a config the user does not have).
- **M4-D30:** `--only` and `--skip` take comma lists whose items match `^fm-[a-z0-9_-]+$` (a registered failure-mode id) or name a subsystem; per §6.11, an unknown id is `usage` with the closest id as the fix. Instance keys `<fm-id>@<target key | machine>[:<discriminator>]` identify findings; labels are never compared.

## Technical Approach

### `Selection` (`src/doctor/selection.rs`, new; `pub mod selection;` in `src/doctor/mod.rs`)

```rust
pub struct Selection { pub target: Option<String>, pub only: Vec<Pick>, pub skip: Vec<Pick> }
pub enum Pick { Mode(&'static str), Subsystem(Subsystem) }
impl Selection {
    pub fn all() -> Self;
    pub fn parse(target: Option<&str>, only: &[String], skip: &[String], argv: &[String]) -> Result<Self>;
    pub fn includes(&self, fm: &FailureMode) -> bool;  // only empty = every row; then minus skip
    pub fn skips(&self, id: &str) -> bool;              // --skip names it, by id or subsystem
    pub fn scope(&self, view: &DoctorView) -> Result<Scope>;
}
pub enum Scope { All, Targets(BTreeSet<TargetSel>), Unresolved { cause: Layer } }
pub enum TargetSel { Key(TargetKey), Unregistered { id: String } }
impl Scope { pub fn includes(&self, target: Option<&TargetRef>) -> bool; } // None (machine) → always true
```

If E1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`, the registry leaf) declared a placeholder `Selection` so its `detect` signature compiles, replace it here at the path E1 used (re-export it from there if E1 placed it elsewhere).

**`parse`.** `only` and `skip` are the raw values of every occurrence of the flags (E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, `doctor diagnose`) declares them as repeatable `String` options, without clap's `value_delimiter`, so the fix can rebuild the token as typed). Each value splits on `,`. Each item:

1. a registered id (exact, in `FAILURE_MODES`) → `Pick::Mode`;
2. one of the 13 `Subsystem` names (exact) → `Pick::Subsystem` (`sockets` and `hooks` are valid and select nothing);
3. empty → `usage`, message `empty item in --only` (or `--skip`), fix: that token without its empty items, or the prose below when nothing is left;
4. anything else → `usage`, message `unknown failure mode or subsystem '<item>' in --only` (or `--skip`), no `details`. The fix is the candidate with the least `cli::levenshtein` distance, at most 2, comparing the item lowercased against every registered id, every subsystem name and, when the item does not start with `fm-`, every id's slug (the part after `fm-<subsystem>-`, so `journal-pending` suggests `fm-concurrency_primitives-journal-pending`). Ties go to the first in `FAILURE_MODES` order, then subsystem order. Its `fix_argv`: `argv` with exactly that item replaced inside the token that holds it (`--only X` or `--only=X`; a comma list keeps its other items and order), then `cli::fix_argv`. With no candidate within 2: the prose fix `use a failure-mode id such as fm-configs-config-parse-error, or a subsystem name such as schemas` and no argv.

Duplicates are dropped silently; `--skip` wins over `--only`. Decided while writing this bead: the slug and lowercase matches, and that a fix never drops the item or the flag (for `doctor fix --only <typo>` that would broaden a mutating command); the fix keeps the user's verb, so once the `UsageFix::UserVerb` marker of C1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.1`, misplaced clients) exists, mark it. Decided too: `Selection` parses `--skip` as well as `--only`, with one parser, because both take the same list.

**`scope`.** Machine-level findings are never narrowed. For `-t <selector>`:

1. none → `Scope::All`;
2. Discovery available: a registry entry in `world.resolved.missing` named by its key or (ASCII case-insensitive) its id → that key; else a Records key equal to the selector → that key; else `world.select_in(Some(selector))` → its targets (`Key` when registered, `Unregistered { id }` otherwise), its `target_not_found` or `target_ambiguous` returned as is;
3. Discovery unavailable: a registry entry by id or key (when the Registry layer is available), then a Records key → that key; no match → `Scope::Unresolved { cause: <Discovery's cause> }` (not an error: the client may exist behind the broken layer).

Decided while writing this bead: a vanished registered client is selectable (`World::select_many`'s `missing_named` refusal suits a command that would act on it; the doctor exists to report it).

### The bookkeeping (`src/doctor/selection.rs`)

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, JsonSchema)]
pub struct Skipped { pub id: &'static str, pub reason: SkipReason, pub target: Option<TargetRef> }
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Serialize, JsonSchema)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum SkipReason { ConfigUnavailable, RegistryUnavailable, DiscoveryUnavailable, RecordsUnavailable,
    InventoryUnavailable, JournalsUnavailable, LockUnavailable, HistoryUnavailable, CachesUnavailable,
    WidgetUnavailable, SkillUnavailable, CredentialsUnavailable }
impl SkipReason { pub fn for_layer(layer: Layer) -> Self; }
pub struct Partition<'r> { pub scope: Scope, pub run: Vec<&'r FailureMode>, pub skipped: Vec<Skipped> }
pub fn partition<'r>(view: &DoctorView, sel: &Selection, rows: &'r [FailureMode], tiers: &[Tier]) -> Result<Partition<'r>>;
pub fn target_skips(view: &DoctorView, part: &Partition<'_>) -> Vec<Skipped>;
pub fn visible_failures(view: &DoctorView, sel: &Selection, part: &Partition<'_>, skipped: &[Skipped]) -> Vec<Finding>;
```

and in `src/doctor/view.rs`:

```rust
pub fn availability(&self, layer: Layer) -> Availability;   // loads it; Available | Unavailable { cause }
pub fn unavailable_targets(&self, layer: Layer) -> Vec<(TargetRef, Layer)>; // Records and Inventory: (target, cause)
pub fn merge_findings(view: Vec<Finding>, detected: Vec<Finding>) -> Vec<Finding>;
```

- **`partition`**: resolve `sel.scope(view)` first and return its error before anything else loads. Then, for each row with `sel.includes(row)` whose tier is in `tiers` (a row outside `tiers` is neither run nor skipped; E3 chooses the tiers per caller): if every layer in `row.requires` is available (`view.availability`), and the scope is not `Unresolved` or the row requires no per-target layer (`Discovery`, `Records`, `Inventory`), it runs; otherwise one `Skipped { id, reason, target: None }`. The reason names the root cause: among the unavailable required layers, the first in `Layer::ALL` order, then its `cause` (a row requiring `Discovery` skipped because `config.toml` is broken says `config_unavailable`); under `Unresolved { cause }` it is that cause.
- **`target_skips`**, after the detectors ran: for each ran row and each of `Records` and `Inventory` in its `requires`, every target in scope listed by `view.unavailable_targets(layer)` (inventories that failed during detection included) gives `Skipped { id, reason: for_layer(cause), target: Some(target) }`. Detectors read only available per-target data (`Records::available()`, `inventory()` returning `None`), so they never report on those targets.
- **`visible_failures`**: `view.failure_findings()`, kept when `sel.includes` its row or its layer is the cause of one of `skipped` (unless `sel.skips` its id), then narrowed by `part.scope` (machine findings always kept). Decided while writing this bead: the second condition, because a skip saying `config_unavailable` without the finding that explains it is worse than a finding `--only` did not ask for; and view failures are shown at every tier, since detection already happened when the layer loaded.
- **`merge_findings`**: one finding per `instance` (the first: pass the view's failures first, so a row that re-reports a view failure, like the two view-reported rows and later the full decode of F3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.3`, state files and schemas), never doubles it), then sorted by severity, id, target id and instance. E3 applies `part.scope` to the merged list as a backstop (`Scope::includes`).
- `skipped` lists sort by id, then target id; serialized, an entry is `{"id": "<fm id>", "reason": "<layer>_unavailable", "target": null | {"id", "key"}}` (`target` always present). E3 adds an `OnlineRequired` variant (A.4's `online_required`), puts the entries in its report's `skipped[]` and counts them in `summary.skipped`.

Decided while writing this bead: the entry carries `target` (the plan's A.4 shows `{id, reason}`), because a per-target layer failure skips a detector for one client while it runs for the others, and the reasons are `<layer>_unavailable` over the twelve layers.

### The seven moved detectors

Each moved row gets `requires` and a `detect` that reads only those layers (and `Scope::includes` to skip out-of-scope targets early), calling the same per-instance rule E1 moved out of `src/app/issues.rs` with facts from the view:

| Row | Tier | `requires` | Facts from the view |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fm-concurrency_primitives-journal-pending` | cached | Journals, Lock | none when `lock()` is `Held`; per `journals().pending` entry with a target: that key, the "needs manual repair" title only for `journal_too_new`/`journal_unreadable` (as `status` passes them), else "waits to be finished"; an entry with no target: the machine finding |
| `fm-schemas-state-version-newer` | cached | Records | `records().available()` with `VersionStatus::Newer`, plus the view's failures with this id (part 1) |
| `fm-state_files-record-folder-missing` | cached | Discovery, Records | per registered discovered target in scope: `app::drift::report(paths, target, record, DriftMode::Presence)`, `Missing` items |
| `fm-external_artifacts-managed-files-modified` | quick | Discovery, Records | the same with `DriftMode::Stat`, `Modified` items (F5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.5`, external artifacts) adds `Deep` under `--include-deep`) |
| `fm-external_artifacts-ownership-transferred` | cached | Records | records with degraded addons (the count `status` titles) |
| `fm-userland_state-target-vanished` | cached | Discovery | `world().resolved.missing` |
| `fm-plugins-widget-version-drift` | cached | Widget | `widget().info` needing reinstall |

Each finding's `target` is `view.target_ref(key)` (the registry id, else the key's string). Decided while writing this bead: the `requires` column, the least each rule reads, so that `state-version-newer` and `ownership-transferred` are the records-only detectors that still run with a corrupt registry.

`status` stays byte-identical: it keeps computing its issues through E1's path until F8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.8`, `status` on the registry). If E1 routed `status` through these `detect` functions over a placeholder view, point `status`'s call at the pure rules with today's inputs instead, so `status` builds no `DoctorView` before F8; keep that edit to the call site (`src/app/status.rs` and `src/app/issues.rs` are a hot spot changed in order by E1, F1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1`, journal and lock detectors) and F8). Known difference, accepted: the view's `journal-pending` also reports a journal naming a key that no discovered or registered client has, which `status` omits; F1 rewrites journal detection on the classifier of E11 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.11`, `journal::diagnose`).

The source scan `view_source_never_writes` extends to `src/doctor/selection.rs`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `Selection::parse` accepts ids, subsystem names (`sockets` and `hooks` included), comma lists, repeated flags and the `--flag=value` form, drops duplicates, and lets `--skip` win.
- [ ] An unknown item is `usage` with the closest id (distance ≤ 2; also from a bare slug or an uppercase spelling) in a `fix_argv` that differs from the invocation in exactly that item; an item with nothing close, or an empty list, gets a prose fix naming no command and no argv; no fix ever drops a non-empty item or a flag.
- [ ] `scope`: no `-t` is `All`; a discovered id, a vanished registered id and a record key each select their client; a selector nothing knows is `target_not_found` while Discovery is available; with Discovery unavailable the registry, then the records resolve it, and no match is `Unresolved` (no error).
- [ ] `partition` runs exactly the selected rows of the given tiers whose required layers are available, and skips the others once each with the root cause's reason (`config_unavailable` for a Discovery-requiring row when `config.toml` is broken); under `Unresolved` the per-target rows are skipped with the cause.
- [ ] `target_skips` names each in-scope target whose record or inventory was unavailable, once per ran row that requires that layer.
- [ ] `visible_failures` shows a view failure when its row is selected or it caused a skip, never when `--skip` names it, and narrows per-target failures by scope.
- [ ] `merge_findings` keeps one finding per instance, view failures first, sorted.
- [ ] Each moved row has the `requires` above and reads only those layers; `ownership-transferred` and `state-version-newer` produce their findings from a view whose config, registry and discovery are all unavailable.
- [ ] For synthetic facts equal to `status`'s inputs, the moved rows give the ids, severities, titles, addons and remediations `issues_for` and `machine_issues` give (the held-lock and manual-repair cases included).
- [ ] `status`'s snapshots and `tests/status.rs` pass unchanged.
- [ ] `view_source_never_writes` covers `selection.rs` and passes.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files; the commit lists for the leaf's close comment the `skipped[]` entry shape and its twelve `reason` values.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

None in this part; subtask 5 checks these rules on real synthetic homes, including the agreement with `status --json` (`the_moved_detectors_agree_with_status`, `target_selection_scopes_findings_and_keeps_machine_ones`).

### Logging

Unit tests only, with case names and descriptive assertion messages.

## Considerations

- **The fixes cannot be run yet.** No `doctor` command parses until E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, `doctor diagnose`); these tests compare `fix_argv` token by token. E3's contract rows and its intent-corpus rows run them (common rules 8 and 18).
- **Laziness meets determinism here.** Which failures exist depends on which layers loaded, which depends on the selection and the tiers. For one selection and one tier set the output is fixed; keep every list sorted on the way out.
- **Hot spots:** `src/app/status.rs` and `src/app/issues.rs` only if E1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`, the registry leaf) routed `status` through a placeholder view, and then the call site only. `src/doctor/registry.rs`: edit the seven moved rows in place, append nothing out of order.
- What could go wrong: a moved detector reading a layer it does not declare (it would then run, and report nothing, when that layer failed). `moved_detectors_run_from_their_layers_alone` and a review of each `detect` against its `requires` guard it.
