title: Tests: the tolerant view against synthetic homes
description:
Part 5 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.2 (`DoctorView`: the tolerant view). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

The leaf builds the doctor's tolerant view of the machine (`doctor::view::DoctorView`): twelve layers (config, registry, discovery, records, inventory, journals, lock, history, caches, widget, skill, credentials), each loaded lazily and once; a failing layer becomes one content-free finding plus an unavailable layer; every detector whose `requires` names an unavailable layer is listed in `skipped` with the layer that caused it, never run and never reported clean (M4-D43); and loading the view writes nothing. Parts 1–4 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.2.1 … omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.2.4) built it and unit-tested each piece on synthetic layers.

This part proves the whole on real synthetic homes: clients built by the repository's test builders, addons installed by the real binary, faults planted on disk, the view loaded in-process, and `status --json` run beside it. It is the leaf's integration suite: the leaf's acceptance criteria about broken configs and registries, writes, determinism, agreement with `status`, `-t` and privacy are checked here, end to end. It comes last because it needs every layer and the bookkeeping.

**What the suite checks, and why it matters:** checkpoint criterion 9 ("bare `doctor` changes nothing outside `<state>/doctor/`", checked by tree hashes of `<state>`, `<cache>`, `<config>` and every client dir, and "two diagnoses of one state give identical findings") and criterion 12 ("`status` and `doctor` agree") start here; M4-D42 (findings never hold file content, never a path below `WTF/`) and common rule 9 (no output names an account, realm or character) are checked over real trees.

**Facts it relies on** (at `c0ab5e9`, plus the earlier parts):

- No command exposes the view until E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, `doctor diagnose`), so the suite loads it in-process: `DoctorView::load_at(Paths::with_roots(env.home(), env.config(), env.state(), env.cache()), ViewOptions::default())` (`Paths::with_roots`, `src/state/paths.rs:105-121`). The library is public (`src/lib.rs`), as other suites use it (`tests/discover_cache.rs:11-14`).
- `common::home::Home::new(&["wow", "wow_classic_era"])` (`tests/common/home.rs:17-53`) builds a Wine prefix with Battle.net clients `_retail_` and `_classic_era_`; `common::trees::CustomRoot` builds a private-server client; `common::trees::tree_hash` covers modes and symlink targets (`tests/common/trees.rs:439`). `tests/status.rs:53-63` installs an addon offline from a local zip (`install gh:o/foo --file <zip> -t <target>`), and `:433` deletes a registered client; local zips are never cached, so no blob appears unless planted.
- `journal::parse` attributes a journal whose `prepared` line does not decode through the line's raw `target_key` (`src/engine/journal.rs:572-580`), and `journal::pending` reports it with `Unrecoverable::Unreadable` (`:522-530`): a raw `{"type":"prepared","schema_version":"1.1","target_key":"<key>"}` line plants an attributed, unreadable journal without depending on `Prepared`'s fields.
- `common::wtf::Wtf::at(client_dir)` builds `WTF/` under `FAKEACCT`/`FakeRealm`/`FakeChar` (`tests/common/wtf.rs:22-33`); `common::privacy::assert_private` checks text (`tests/common/privacy.rs`).
- T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`)'s `TestLog` (`tests/common/tlog.rs`): `tlog!()`, `log.step`, `log.note`, `log.json`, `log.assert_eq`, `log.run(&home, &argv)` (argv without the binary name, used verbatim) returning `Ran` with `ok()`, `envelope()`, `data()`, `assert_private()`, `log.tree(label, root)`, `log.assert_unchanged(label, root)`, `log.case(name)`.
- `tree_hash` panics on a directory it cannot read (`fs::read_dir(..).unwrap()`), so a mode-000 fault is planted after the first hash and undone before the second.

## Technical Approach

### `tests/doctor_view.rs`

`mod common;` and a small `support` module:

- `fn view(home: &Home) -> DoctorView` (the default `Scan` options) and `fn view_with(home, ViewDiscovery)`.
- `fn diagnose(log: &TestLog, view: &DoctorView, sel: &Selection) -> Report` with `Report { findings: Vec<Finding>, skipped: Vec<Skipped>, ran: Vec<&'static str> }`: the steps the runtime of E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, `doctor diagnose`) will take, so the suite tests the leaf's interface as E3 will use it: `partition(view, sel, FAILURE_MODES, &[Tier::Cached, Tier::Quick, Tier::Default])`; each run row's `detect` (with the unbounded `Budget` that E1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`, the registry leaf) or E3 provides); `target_skips`; `visible_failures`; `merge_findings`; then `Scope::includes` over the merged list. It logs `loaded layers`, `availability` (layer → available or cause), `failures`, `skipped`, `ran` and `findings` with `log.json`. Its doc comment says E3's runtime replaces it, and E3's tests cover the real one.
- `fn install(log, home, target, name)` writes a one-folder zip (`common::archives::zip_text`, `common::addons::toc`) and runs `log.run(home, &["install", "gh:o/<name>", "--file", <zip>, "-t", target, "--json"]).ok()`.
- `fn key_of(home, target_id) -> TargetKey` (`common::state::key_of`).
- `fn edit_record(home, target_id, f: impl FnOnce(&mut serde_json::Value))`: read, change and write `<state>/omaddons/targets/<key>.json` as JSON (test code writes files directly, as other suites do).
- `fn agreement_home(log: &TestLog) -> Home`: builds scenario 8's home (three clients, the six planted states below), so scenarios 9–11 and each of scenario 9's cases start from a fresh copy of it.

### Scenarios

Every scenario: `let log = tlog!();`, then `log.step` per phase, `log.tree("home", env.root())` after building and planting (or before planting a mode change), and `log.assert_unchanged("home", env.root())` after the view was used. Each fault's scenario also checks its clean twin: before planting, `diagnose` on the same home gives no view failure and no skip (no false positive).

1. **`a_broken_config_is_a_finding_and_its_dependents_are_skipped`.** Two clients; `install` on retail and on era. Plant `<config>/omaddons/config.toml` = `check_interval_hours = 6\n[limits\ndefault_target = "PLANTED-CONTENT-7f3a"\n`. Diagnose with `Selection::all()`. Assert: `view.config()` is `None`; exactly one finding with id `fm-configs-config-parse-error`, `evidence.reason == "parse"`, `evidence.line == 2`, `evidence.path` the config file, `target: null`; every row whose `requires` contains Config, Discovery, Inventory or Credentials is in `skipped` with `reason: "config_unavailable"`, `target: null`, and not in `ran`; `fm-schemas-state-version-newer` and `fm-external_artifacts-ownership-transferred` are in `ran`; `serde_json::to_string(&report)` contains no `PLANTED-CONTENT-7f3a`. `assert_unchanged`.
2. **`a_corrupt_registry_is_a_finding_and_records_only_detectors_still_run`.** Two clients with addons; `edit_record(retail)`: `schema_version` → `"1.9"` and the addon's `state` → `"degraded"`; truncate `<state>/omaddons/registry.json` to its first 20 bytes. Assert: `registry()` is `None`; one `fm-schemas-state-corrupt` with `evidence.reason == "decode"` and `path` the registry; rows requiring Discovery skipped with `registry_unavailable`; findings `fm-schemas-state-version-newer` and `fm-external_artifacts-ownership-transferred` for retail's key, with `target.id` equal to the key's string (the registry cannot name it).
3. **`one_corrupt_record_skips_only_its_target`.** Two clients with addons; append bytes to era's installed `Foo/Foo.toc`; replace retail's record with `{`. Assert: a `state-corrupt` finding with `target.key` retail's; for each ran row requiring Records, one `skipped` entry `{reason: "records_unavailable", target: {key: retail's}}`; era's `fm-external_artifacts-managed-files-modified` finding present; no finding of a records-requiring row names retail.
4. **`newer_state_that_does_not_decode_is_a_finding`.** Era's record replaced by `{"schema_version":"9.0","addons":"x"}`. Assert: `fm-schemas-state-version-newer` for era with `evidence.observed == "9.0"` and `reason == "newer"`; era's record unavailable (a records skip names era).
5. **`oversized_unreadable_and_odd_state_files_are_never_clean`.** One `log.case` per fault, each on a fresh one-client home with an addon: `registry_over_the_bound` (the registry padded with spaces to `DISCOVERY_FILE_MAX_BYTES + 1` bytes: `too_large`, `bytes`, `limit: "DISCOVERY_FILE_MAX_BYTES"`); `registry_mode_000` (`unreadable`; mode restored before the second hash); `registry_is_a_directory` (`not_a_file`); `registry_dangling_symlink` (`unreadable`, never the empty registry); `config_is_a_fifo` (`not_a_file`, returned without blocking; the case is skipped with a `log.note` when `mkfifo` is absent); `history_mode_000` (a machine `state-corrupt`, `reason: "unreadable"`, label `history.jsonl`). In each case the Discovery-requiring rows are skipped (where the fault is the registry) and no layer reads as empty.
6. **`loading_every_layer_writes_nothing`.** Two clients with addons; plant: the raw unreadable journal naming retail's key in `<state>/omaddons/journal/<tx>.jsonl`; `$HOME/.claude/skills/omaddons/SKILL.md`; `<config>/omaddons/credentials/github` (mode 0600, a fake token, registered with `log.secret`); two files in `<cache>/omaddons/blobs/`; and no `<cache>/omaddons/discovery.json`. Hash. Load a `Scan` view and touch every accessor and every discovered target's `inventory`; load a `Cached` view and do the same. Assert unchanged, and `discovery.json` absent.
7. **`scanning_discovery_reuses_the_cache_and_never_writes_it`.** Two clients with addons; `log.run(&home, &["status", "--json"]).ok()` (it writes the cache); record the cache's bytes; build a third client with `CustomRoot::at(env.home().join("Games/wow-335"))`; hash; load a `Scan` view. Assert: `world().resolved.targets` holds the new client; the cache's bytes are unchanged; `assert_unchanged`.
8. **`the_moved_detectors_agree_with_status`.** `agreement_home` builds: three clients (the two Battle.net ones and the `CustomRoot` one). Install `Foo` and `Bar` on retail, `Foo` on era, `Foo` on the custom client. Plant: retail's `Bar` folder deleted (`record-folder-missing`); retail's `Foo` marked degraded in its record (`ownership-transferred`); the raw unreadable journal naming retail's key (`journal-pending`, "needs manual repair"); a byte appended to era's `Foo/Foo.toc` (`managed-files-modified`); era's record `schema_version` → `"1.9"` (`state-version-newer`); the custom client's directory removed (`target-vanished`). Run `log.run(&home, &["status", "--json"]).ok()` and collect `(id, target id or null, addon, severity, title)` from `data.targets[].issues[]` (target id from the enclosing target) and `data.issues[]` (null), sorted. Hash. Diagnose with an `only` selection of the seven moved ids. Collect the same tuples from the findings. `log.assert_eq("findings equal status's issues", &findings, &issues)`. `assert_unchanged`. (`widget-version-drift` is covered by part 4's unit test.)
9. **`target_selection_scopes_findings_and_keeps_machine_ones`.** Each case on a fresh `agreement_home`, with `history.jsonl` at mode 000 (a machine failure; restored before the final hash). Cases: `t_era` (`Selection::parse(Some("era"), …)`: era's findings and the machine history finding, none of retail's); `t_vanished` (the custom client's id: its `target-vanished` finding); `t_unknown` (`nosuch`: `partition` returns `target_not_found`); `t_era_config_broken` (a broken `config.toml`: scope resolved through the registry to era's key; records-only findings for era only); `t_era_both_broken` (registry truncated too: `Unresolved`, the records-only rows skipped with `config_unavailable`, no error).
10. **`two_loads_of_one_home_give_identical_findings_and_skips`.** An `agreement_home` plus a broken `config.toml`; two fresh views diagnosed with the same selection; `serde_json::to_string` of both reports equal, byte for byte.
11. **`no_view_output_names_an_account_realm_or_character`.** An `agreement_home` plus `Wtf::at(home.client("_retail_"))` and `Wtf::at(home.client("_classic_era_"))` with SavedVariables (`saved_variables`, `config_wtf`); diagnose; `common::privacy::assert_private` over the serialized findings, skips and `view.warnings()`; then `log.run(&home, &["status", "--json", "--progress", "json"]).ok().assert_private()`.

### What this suite does not cover

No contract rows or snapshots (no command yet: E3's), no crash or concurrency cases (the view writes nothing and takes no lock), no performance budget (F8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.8`, `status` on the registry) holds `status --cached` under 5 ms; E4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4`, `doctor health` and the other doctor views) holds `doctor health` under 200 ms).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `tests/doctor_view.rs` holds the eleven scenarios above, each logging through `TestLog`, and all pass in `argc gate`.
- [ ] Every fault scenario also asserts its clean twin: the same home before the fault gives no view failure and no skip.
- [ ] Every scenario that loads a view asserts the test home's tree hash unchanged across the load.
- [ ] Scenario 8 shows the moved detectors' findings equal to `status --json`'s issues, tuple for tuple.
- [ ] Scenario 10's two reports are byte-identical.
- [ ] Scenario 11 passes `assert_private` on the view's output and `assert_private_all` on `status`'s stdout and stderr.
- [ ] A deliberately broken assertion (tried locally, not committed) prints `test log: <path>` and the last steps, and the transcript shows the loaded layers, the failures and the skips.
- [ ] `ubs` is clean on the new file.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

None in this part (parts 1–4 carry them).

### Integration and end-to-end tests

The suite above, `tests/doctor_view.rs`. Run alone with `cargo test --test doctor_view`; with live step logs: `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG=verbose cargo test --test doctor_view -- --nocapture`.

### Logging

- One `log.step` per phase: `build the home`, `install`, `clean twin`, `plant <fault>`, `hash`, `load the view`, `diagnose`, `assert`, `unchanged`.
- Every binary run through `log.run`, so argv, exit code, envelope and stderr events are in the transcript.
- `diagnose` logs `loaded layers`, `availability`, `failures`, `skipped`, `ran` and `findings` (`log.json`), so a failure reads from the transcript alone.
- Trees: `log.tree("home", env.root())` and `log.assert_unchanged("home", env.root())`, which logs the first differing paths.
- Comparisons that matter (scenario 8's tuples, scenario 10's reports) go through `log.assert_eq`, which records both sides.
- The planted credential is registered with `log.secret`, so it never appears in `steps.jsonl` or `transcript.md`.
- On failure, the guard of T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs) prints `test log: <path>` and the last 20 steps.

## Considerations

- **In-process loads read `/proc`.** The `Scan` view's discovery calls `process_prefixes`, which an in-process test cannot point at the fake `/proc` (no `set_var` without `unsafe`); it keeps only prefixes under the test's home, so no real client enters. Decided while writing this bead: accepted. A scenario needing a running client waits for the command of E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, `doctor diagnose`).
- **Mode-000 cases** hash before planting and after restoring, because `tree_hash` cannot read a mode-000 directory; restoring the mode is the test's own change and leaves the hash equal when the view wrote nothing.
- **Coupling to the finding types of E1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`, the registry leaf):** the suite reads findings through their serialized JSON where it can (`id`, `instance`, `target`, `evidence`), so a field E1 named differently changes one helper, not eleven scenarios.
- **Time:** each scenario installs a few addons with the debug binary; keep homes minimal (one addon per client unless the scenario needs two).
- The local `diagnose` driver must not grow product logic: it calls the leaf's functions in E3's order and nothing else.

## Dependencies

- Parent: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.2 (`DoctorView`: the tolerant view).
- Before it: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.2.4 (and through it parts 1–3): the full view, the selection and the bookkeeping this suite drives.
- Also waits for T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs and the `argc e2e` runner), whose `TestLog` every scenario uses.
- After it: nothing in this leaf. Closing it, if it is the last open subtask, closes the leaf, which unblocks E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`) and counts toward T4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4`, slice 3's demo as a test).

- [ ] Every fault scenario also asserts its clean twin: the same home before the fault gives no view failure and no skip.
- [ ] Every scenario that loads a view asserts the test home's tree hash unchanged across the load.
- [ ] Scenario 8 shows the moved detectors' findings equal to `status --json`'s issues, tuple for tuple.
- [ ] Scenario 10's two reports are byte-identical.
- [ ] Scenario 11 passes `assert_private` on the view's output and `assert_private_all` on `status`'s stdout and stderr.

title: `doctor diagnose` and `explain`: runtime, run directories, the doctor envelope and its exit dictionary
description:
## How to work this bead

This bead is worked through its 7 subtasks, listed below in work order. Claim a subtask, not this bead (`br ready --parent omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3` lists the ready ones). The agent that closes the last open subtask then verifies every acceptance criterion of this bead (they are the leaf's, not any one subtask's), and closes this bead with `br close omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3 --reason "done: <evidence> · found: <ids>"`. Until this bead is closed, every bead it blocks stays blocked.

1. `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3.1` The doctor exit dictionary, the doctor envelope and the contract harness's doctor mode: `doctor::Exit`, the total `exit_for`, a process exit that can carry either dictionary, `DoctorEnvelope` and `emit_doctor`, and `support::check`'s doctor mode. No command yet.
2. `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3.2` `WriteSession::untracked_logged`: an untracked fsx session that logs its writes: one line per `mutate()` to its own log, with its own sequence. fsx only.
3. `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3.3` Detector budgets: the `Budget` handle, the bounded walker and the detector signature: plus `DOCTOR_SCAN_MAX_ENTRIES` and `DOCTOR_DETECTOR_DEADLINE`. `src/doctor/budget.rs`, the registry, `status`'s call.
4. `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3.4` The diagnose runtime: run ids, run directories, isolated detectors, `report.json`, `latest` and hardening: staged and published runs, budgeted detectors, the two runtime failure modes. Library code with in-crate tests. After s1, s2 and s3.
5. `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3.5` `omaddons doctor` and `doctor diagnose`: the command, its flags and selection, `--since` and the human output: with the two new error codes and every DEC-1 touch point of the two paths. After s4.
6. `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3.6` `omaddons doctor explain`, and the `--fix` and `--explain` intent hints: with every DEC-1 touch point of `doctor explain` and the corpus rows. After s5.
7. `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3.7` E2E: the doctor runtime end to end, every doctor exit site, and the two runtime fixtures. `tests/doctor.rs` with the `TestLog` of T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs). After s6.

s1, s2 and s3 touch different files and do not depend on each other: they can be worked at the same time.

**Size L, kept as one leaf for closure.** The runtime, the envelope and the exit dictionary are one contract surface: a run directory nobody can render, an envelope no exit code agrees with, or a dictionary no command uses would each emit output no consumer can parse. The subtasks split the work into commits that each pass the gate; the closure stays whole, so the nine beads it blocks (listed under Dependencies) never see half of it.

## Background

**What this leaf is.** `omaddons doctor` is M4's answer to "what is broken in what omaddons manages, and what exactly do I do about it". This leaf builds the read side of the doctor: the command tree (`doctor`, `doctor diagnose`, `doctor explain`), the runtime that runs every selected detector under a budget and records the run in its own directory, the doctor's JSON envelope (the report's keys at the top level, as the external doctor contract wants), and the doctor's own exit dictionary, to which every error code maps. Everything the doctor later repairs (E6 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`, `doctor fix`; E7 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7`, undo of repairs; E8 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.8`, `doctor gc`) and every detector the catalog leaves add (F1 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1` to F10 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.10`) runs inside what this leaf builds.

`explain` lands here and not in E4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4`, the other read verbs of the doctor) because this leaf's own reports put `doctor explain` argv in `commands[]` and in each finding's remediation, and the contract suite runs every argv it sees: shipping a report that names a command that does not exist would fail the gate.

**What is true today** (verified at `c0ab5e9`):

- There is no doctor at all. `src/doctor/` does not exist yet (E1 creates it, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`), and no `doctor` subcommand exists in `src/cli.rs` (`Command` enum, `cli.rs:137-213`).
- **The process exit is the general dictionary, end to end.** `cli::run` converts an `Exit` (`cli.rs:343-358`, the conversion at `cli.rs:357`); `run_with`, `render_error` (`cli.rs:432-449`) and `render_panic` (`cli.rs:1307-1352`) return `Exit`; `output::emit` and `emit_panic` return `Exit` (`src/output/mod.rs:78-217`); `output::emitted_exit` maps the stored code back only through `Exit::ALL` (`output/mod.rs:70-73`); and the panic path falls back to `Exit::Failed` (`cli.rs:1341`). A doctor exit of 64 or 74 cannot be expressed anywhere today.
- **The envelope** is `{ok, schema_version, tool_version, command, exit_code, partial?, data?, error?, warnings, commands, meta}` (`src/output/envelope.rs:20-38`), and `exit_code` always comes from `error.exit().code()`.
- **The contract harness** (`support::check`, inside `tests/contract/main.rs`'s `mod support`, `main.rs:29-225`) checks the key order against a fixed list (`main.rs:35-47`), that a failure's `exit_code` equals its code's registered general exit (`main.rs:155-159`), and that each failure prints exactly one stderr `error` event (`main.rs:219-223`). A check that ran out of budget or entries says so: incomplete coverage is never reported as healthy." This leaf is the runtime that makes that sentence true for every detector anyone adds.
- **G-M4-5 (frozen and enforced):** "Every exit site maps to a published code in the right dictionary. Repeated runs print identical bytes." The doctor dictionary, its total mapping and the volatile-key declarations are this leaf's.

**The decisions that shape it** (full text in the decision log comments on the milestone epic `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`):

- **M4-D32: the run directory holds the report, the audit log, the backups, the quarantine and `undo.sh`.** `<run>` = `<state>/doctor/runs/<YYYY-MM-DDTHH-MM-SSZ>__<ULID>/`. A diagnose run holds `report.json` (the command's report, with `kind: diagnose`) and `runtime.jsonl` (one line per write the runtime itself made: the run directory, `report.json`, `latest`, hardening), so the audit trail is complete without mixing two sessions' sequences in one file. `actions.jsonl`, `backups/`, `quarantine/` and `undo.sh` belong to fix and undo runs (E5 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`, the repair transaction; E6). `<state>/doctor/latest` is a symlink to the newest run whose state was `DONE_OK`, `DONE_FINDINGS` or `DONE_PARTIAL`, updated with `SymlinkAtomic`; it is for reading the last report, and `doctor undo` never resolves it. Run files are 0600 and the directory 0700 while the run is open; at the terminal state the record files (`report.json`, `actions.jsonl`, `runtime.jsonl`) become 0400 and `undo.sh` 0500. Directories, `backups/` and `quarantine/` are never hardened. *Why:* these are the doctor contract's artifacts, minus the ones that serve the doctor-building workflow; hardening more than the record would break undo (a backup turned 0400 restores the wrong mode, a 0500 directory forbids the rename out of `quarantine/`). *Rejected:* `report.md` (the human output is the CLI's, a second rendering drifts); scorecards (they belong to the skill that builds doctors); `stderr.log` and `stdout.json` (`report.json` is the stdout payload).
- **M4-D33: every diagnose, fix and undo of a repair makes a run directory; the other verbs do not.** `doctor`, `doctor diagnose`, `doctor --quick` and `doctor --robot-triage` each create one; `health`, `ls`, `explain`, `diff`, `gc`, `capabilities` and `robot-docs` do not. **The run id** is the readable UTC start time, `__`, then a fresh ULID: `2026-10-30T18-03-40Z__01M8S…`. Every invocation gets its own. The directory is published with `RENAME_NOREPLACE` from a staged name; on the vanishingly rare collision the runtime draws a new ULID and retries, at most `RUN_ID_RETRY` (2) times. Nothing waits for the wall clock to advance. `doctor diagnose` is `mutates: false` in `app::COMMANDS` because it never changes project state, and it accepts no mutating flag; its run directory is doctor-owned. `special.rs`'s read-only test exempts exactly `<state>/doctor/`, and its "ignores `--dry-run` and `--reason`" comparison strips the doctor's volatile keys (`run_id`, `run_dir`, `started_at`, `finished_at`, `duration_ms`). *Rejected:* a run directory for `health` (it would grow without bound under a widget or a cron job); the doctor contract's deterministic run id (a hash of the state directory and the second: several agents plus a widget preview in one second exhaust two retries, and a frozen test clock never progresses).
- **M4-D34: doctor JSON puts the report at the top level, with the general envelope keys around it.** Every verb of the doctor tree emits `{ok, schema_version, tool_version, command, exit_code, <report keys>, error?, warnings, commands, meta}`. `ok` is `exit_code == 0`. `error` is present only for exits 4, 5, 6, 64, 66, 73 and 74: findings (1), a partial fix (2) and a rolled-back fix (3) are reports, not errors. There is no `data` key. `next_steps` (display strings) mirrors `commands[]` (argv). The schema registry's `data` schema for a doctor path is its report schema. *Why:* vision §5.8; generic doctor consumers read `.state`, `.summary` and `.findings` at the top level. *Rejected:* nesting the report under `data`.
- **M4-D40: the doctor dictionary uses the vision's names, and every error code maps to it.** `doctor::Exit` is `0 healthy`, `1 findings_present`, `2 fix_partial`, `3 fix_failed_rolled_back`, `4 refused_unsafe`, `5 concurrency_lost`, `6 online_required`, `64 usage_error`, `66 no_input`, `73 cannot_create`, `74 io_error`. `doctor::exit_for(ErrorCode) -> Exit` is total: three explicit rows first (`plan_stale` → 4, `online_required` → 6, `check_failed` → 1), then by the code's general exit class: exit 2 → 64, exit 3 → 66, exit 4 → 4, `locked` → 5, an `io` error creating the run directory → 73, every other exit-1 code → 74. A unit test iterates `ErrorCode::ALL`, and a new code added without a class cannot compile. `capabilities` publishes the mapping; `exit_sites.rs`, `output::emitted_exit` and the panic path learn it (a panic in the doctor tree exits 74, never 101 and never 1). Two new codes: `online_required` (general exit 1, doctor exit 6), raised when `--only` selects only online failure modes and `--online` is absent (a mixed selection runs the offline ones and lists the rest in `skipped`); `doctor_refused` (general exit 4, doctor exit 4), the error of every `REFUSING` run, `details.reason` from the closed set `force_required`, `fixer_conflict`, `too_many_actions`, `over_budget`, `filesystem_mismatch`, `client_running`, `not_enabled`, `edited_locally`, with `details.fm` when one failure mode is concerned. *Why:* vision D18 spells the names; a doctor command can hit every general error. *Rejected:* the general dictionary in the doctor tree ("findings present" is a normal outcome there).

### 2. The doctor exit dictionary (s1)

`src/doctor/exit.rs`:

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Serialize, JsonSchema)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum Exit { Healthy, FindingsPresent, FixPartial, FixFailedRolledBack, RefusedUnsafe,
                ConcurrencyLost, OnlineRequired, UsageError, NoInput, CannotCreate, IoError }
impl Exit {
    pub const ALL: &[Exit] = &[/* in code order */];
    pub const fn code(self) -> u8;      // 0 1 2 3 4 5 6 64 66 73 74
    pub const fn name(self) -> &'static str; // "healthy" … "io_error"
    pub const fn meaning(self) -> &'static str;
}
pub const fn exit_for(code: ErrorCode) -> Exit;
```

- **Meanings** (one sentence each; capabilities and `help doctor` publish them): healthy "every selected check ran to completion and found nothing"; findings_present "the run completed and reports findings, a check that could not finish among them"; fix_partial "a fix ran and some findings remain"; fix_failed_rolled_back "a fix failed and was rolled back; nothing changed"; refused_unsafe "refused before changing anything: a safety precondition, a missing --force, a conflict, a stale preview or an over-budget selection"; concurrency_lost "another omaddons process held the lock past the acquire timeout"; online_required "the selection needs the network: add --online"; usage_error "unknown command or flag, or a bad argument"; no_input "a target, run, failure mode or other input was not found, or is ambiguous"; cannot_create "the run directory could not be created"; io_error "a runtime failure: I/O, state, network or internal".
- **`exit_for`**: `match code { PlanStale => RefusedUnsafe, OnlineRequired => OnlineRequired, CheckFailed => FindingsPresent, _ => match code.exit() { Usage => UsageError, NotFound => NoInput, Refused => RefusedUnsafe, Locked => ConcurrencyLost, Failed => IoError, CheckFailed => FindingsPresent, Ok => IoError } }`. The inner match is exhaustive over the general `Exit` with no wildcard, so a new general class does not compile until it is mapped. `Exit::Ok` has no code (`exit_sites.rs:133` asserts no code exits 0) and maps to `IoError` as the conservative failure; `Exit::CheckFailed` holds only `check_failed`. The `online_required` row lands with that code in s5; s1 ships the other two explicit rows and the classes.
- **73 is a context, not a code.** "An `io` error creating the run directory → 73" cannot come from `ErrorCode` alone: `exit_for(Io)` is 74, and the runtime's STARTING failure carries an explicit override (decided while writing this bead): `output::DoctorFailure { error: Error, exit: doctor::Exit }`, built by `DoctorFailure::from(error)` (exit = `exit_for(error.code)`) or `DoctorFailure::cannot_create(error)` (exit 73). capabilities' per-code `doctor_exit` publishes `exit_for`, and the 73 case is documented beside the dictionary.
- **capabilities** (A4, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`) publishes `exit_codes.doctor` from `doctor::Exit::ALL` and each code's `doctor_exit` from `exit_for`; whichever of A4 and this leaf lands second wires them.
- **The process exit.** `src/error.rs` gains `pub enum ProcessExit { General(Exit), Doctor(crate::doctor::Exit) }` with `code() -> u8`, `From<Exit>`, `From<doctor::Exit>` and `From<ProcessExit> for ExitCode` (in `error.rs`, where the exit-site test allows the conversion). `cli::run`, `run_with`, `render_error`, `render_panic` and `app::dispatch` return `ProcessExit`. `app::dictionary_of(command: &str) -> Dictionary` reads A1's field (an unknown name is `General`). `render_error` and the panic path choose the dictionary from the command they render: a usage error or `Context::new` failure on a doctor path exits 64; a panic or the `cli.panic` failpoint in the doctor tree exits 74 with a doctor-shaped `internal` envelope. `output::emitted_exit()` returns `Option<ProcessExit>` (the stored code plus its dictionary), so a panic after a doctor document keeps that document's doctor exit.
- **`tests/contract/exit_sites.rs`** learns the dictionary: `doctor_exit_dictionary_is_the_visions` (exactly `{0,1,2,3,4,5,6,64,66,73,74}` with the vision's names, unique, snake_case); `every_error_code_has_a_doctor_exit` (over `ErrorCode::ALL`, the class rule restated as an independent table, never `healthy`); `the_doctor_tree_exits_only_through_its_dictionary` (a production-code scan of `src/app/doctor.rs` and `src/doctor/**`: no general `Exit::` variant outside `src/doctor/exit.rs`'s match); and `the_process_exits_only_through_exit` updated to say `ProcessExit`.

      pub command: &'a str,
      #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")] pub kind: Option<RunKind>, // report.json only
      pub exit_code: u8,
      #[serde(flatten, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")] pub report: Option<&'a R>,

- **`support::check`'s doctor mode** (`tests/contract/main.rs`), selected when the envelope's `command` is a Doctor-dictionary path (`omaddons::app::dictionary_of`). The doctor-specific checks live in a new `tests/common/doctor.rs` (`common::doctor::check_envelope(stdout, stderr, code) -> Value`) so the contract suite and `tests/doctor.rs` share one implementation; `support::check` calls it, then runs its usual fix and `commands[]` argv checks. ### 5. The runtime (s4)

`src/doctor/runtime.rs`, `src/doctor/report.rs` (the report types; decided while writing this bead), `src/doctor/mod.rs` (`pub fn diagnose(…)`), `src/state/paths.rs`.

**Paths.** `Paths::doctor_dir() = <state>/doctor`, `doctor_latest() = <state>/doctor/latest`, `doctor_run(&DoctorRunId) = <state>/doctor/runs/<id>`, `doctor_run_stage(&DoctorRunId) = <state>/doctor/runs/.<id>.tmp`, beside `doctor_runs_dir()`.

**The run id.** `pub struct DoctorRunId(String)` (decided while writing this bead, distinct from `model::RunId`): `DoctorRunId::new(at: Timestamp, ulid: Ulid)` formats `at` in UTC as `%Y-%m-%dT%H-%M-%SZ`, then `__`, then the ULID; `parse(&str) -> Option<Self>` accepts exactly that shape; `Display`, `Serialize` as a string; its JSON schema is a plain string with no pattern, so redacted snapshots (`<run>`) validate. Ordering is string order, which is start time then ULID.

**The states** (§6.12, the doctor contract's lifecycle), for a diagnose:

| State | What happens |
|---|---|
| `STARTING` | `at = clock::now()` (frozen by `OMADDONS_NOW` in debug builds); `id = DoctorRunId::new(at, Ulid::generate())`. One `Writer::Doctor` session, `untracked_logged(…, "doctor runtime", <stage>/runtime.jsonl)` over `ScopeTable::new(paths, &[], None)`. `ensure_dir_all(<state>/doctor/runs)`; `CreateDir <stage>`; `Chmod <stage> 0700` (`Op::CreateDir` takes no mode). Failpoint `doctor.run.staged` (abort). `Rename { to: <run>, mode: NoReplace }`; a `Precondition` error whose destination exists is a collision: draw a fresh ULID for the final name and retry, at most `RUN_ID_RETRY` (2) more times; then `cannot_create`. Failpoint `doctor.run.published` (abort). Any failure here is `DoctorFailure::cannot_create(io error with details.path)`, exit 73. Nothing sleeps or waits for the clock. |
| `DIAGNOSING` | `DoctorView::load` (E2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.2`), then every selected detector in `FAILURE_MODES` order. Per detector: force the view layers its `requires` names; start its `Budget` (§6); failpoint `doctor.detector.panic` (inside the isolation below); if the budget has already expired, the detector is incomplete with no work done; otherwise call it inside `std::panic::catch_unwind(AssertUnwindSafe(…))`. A panic becomes a `fm-state_files-detector-crashed` finding; a returned `incomplete` becomes a `fm-state_files-check-incomplete` finding. The run goes on. |
| `DONE_OK` / `DONE_FINDINGS` | `DONE_OK` requires no finding at all (so a crashed or incomplete detector, which is a finding, makes the run `DONE_FINDINGS`); exit 0 or 1. Then the terminal writes, in this order: `WriteFile <run>/report.json` (mode 0600, fsx's atomic write); `SymlinkAtomic <state>/doctor/latest → runs/<id>`; `Chmod <run>/report.json 0400`; `Chmod <run>/runtime.jsonl 0400` (last; its own line goes out through the already-open descriptor). |

- **`latest`** (decided while writing this bead): a relative target `runs/<id>` (it survives a moved state directory and names no home path). It is retargeted only when `latest` is missing, dangling, not pointing at a run, or pointing at a run id that sorts before this one, so a slow run that finishes after a newer quick one does not move it back. A `latest` that exists and is not a symlink is left alone (a debug log line). Two runs finishing in the same instant may race; `latest` is a reading convenience, never an input to undo (M4-D46), so the race is accepted.
- **Hardening failure** (decided while writing this bead): an I/O error while writing `report.json`, `latest` or a chmod is `io` (exit 74), with the report keys kept in the envelope; the run directory then has an unhardened or missing record, which E4's `ls` reports.
- **Isolation.** `const _: () = assert!(cfg!(panic = "unwind"));` in `runtime.rs`: a profile change to `panic = "abort"` fails the build instead of silently breaking isolation. After a caught panic the runtime calls `cli::take_caught_panic()` (new, `pub(crate)`, beside `first_panic` in its own function), which clears the hook's first-panic slot (so a later real panic is reported with its own cause) and returns the panic's `file:line`. The view is still usable: it has no write methods, and a panic inside a lazy layer's load leaves that layer unloaded for the next detector (if E2 guards a layer with a `Mutex`, recover a poisoned one with `into_inner`).
- **The two runtime failure modes** (Appendix B rows 18 and 46), added to `FAILURE_MODES` with `tier: Tier::Runtime` and `detect: None`:

  | Id | P | Evidence | Instance | Remediation |
  |---|---|---|---|---|
  | `fm-state_files-detector-crashed` | P1 | `{detector: "<fm id>", location: "<file>:<line>"}` | `…@machine:detector=<fm id>` | prose: "a bug in omaddons: report the detector and location above" (no argv) |
  | `fm-state_files-check-incomplete` | P3 | `{detector, limit: "deadline" \| "entries", deadline_ms: u64 \| null, max_entries: u64 \| null}` | `…@machine:detector=<fm id>` | `limit: deadline`: argv `omaddons doctor --only <fm> --budget <10 × deadline_ms>ms` (a read); `limit: entries`: prose "this check visits at most 20,000 entries; narrow it with -t <client>" |

  Titles: "a check stopped with an internal error" and "a check could not finish within its limit". `confidence: high`, `auto_fixable: false`, `needs_force: false`. Decided while writing this bead: the panic payload is never reported on any channel (it may format data, and the privacy rule covers every channel); the evidence holds only values the limit fixes (no elapsed time or visited count), so two diagnoses of one state stay byte-identical; `detector=` joins the canonical discriminator keys of E1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`).
- **`doctor::FAILPOINTS`** in `src/doctor/mod.rs`: `doctor.run.staged`, `doctor.run.published`, `doctor.detector.panic`, with a scan test like `tx.rs:2240-2255` over `src/doctor/**` (and `src/engine/repair.rs` once it exists). ### 6. Budgets (s3)

`src/doctor/budget.rs`:

```rust
pub struct Budget { /* deadline: Instant, deadline_ms: u64, max_entries: u64, used: u64, exhausted: Option<Limit> */ }
pub enum Limit { Deadline, Entries }                      // wire "deadline" | "entries"
pub struct Incomplete { pub limit: Limit, pub deadline_ms: Option<u64>, pub max_entries: Option<u64> }
pub struct Detected { pub findings: Vec<Finding>, pub incomplete: Option<Incomplete> }
pub struct Exhausted(pub Limit);
impl Budget {
    pub fn new(deadline: Duration, max_entries: u64) -> Self;
    pub fn for_tier(tier: Tier) -> Self;     // the tier's default deadline, DOCTOR_SCAN_MAX_ENTRIES
    pub fn charge(&mut self, entries: u64) -> Result<(), Exhausted>;  // entries first, then the deadline
    pub fn check(&mut self) -> Result<(), Exhausted>;                 // the deadline only
    pub fn expired(&self) -> bool;
    pub fn incomplete(&self) -> Option<Incomplete>;
}
pub fn walk(root: &Path, max_depth: usize, budget: &mut Budget, visit: impl FnMut(&WalkEntry) -> WalkStep) -> WalkResult;
pub fn list_dir(dir: &Path, budget: &mut Budget) -> io::Result<Listing>;
pub fn parse_budget(s: &str) -> Result<Duration, String>;
```

- **The bounded walker** reads with `std::fs::read_dir` and `symlink_metadata` (reads are allowed outside fsx), never follows a symlink (a symlink is an entry of kind `symlink`), visits names in sorted order (deterministic), charges one entry per visited entry, and on the first `Exhausted` stops and returns what it saw with `complete: false`. `WalkResult { complete, unreadable: Vec<PathBuf> }` (an unreadable directory is recorded, never fatal, and bounded by the same budget). `list_dir` is the one-level form.
- **Tier defaults:** `cached` and `quick` → `QUICK_DETECTOR_BUDGET` (5 ms); `default` and `deep` → `DOCTOR_DETECTOR_DEADLINE` (2 s); `runtime` never runs. **Debug builds** (decided while writing this bead): the implicit tier deadlines are multiplied by `DEBUG_DEADLINE_SCALE` (20), a test seam beside the code like `failpoint::PAUSE_MAX` (`src/fsx/failpoint.rs:22-25`), not a safety limit, because a debug build is 10–50 times slower than the release build the 5 ms contract is measured on (§3.2 criterion 10), and without the scale every gate run on a realistic home would report `check-incomplete`. Explicit `--budget` deadlines are never scaled, and the entries cap never is.
- **`--budget`:** before STARTING, the selected detectors' declared `cost_ms` are summed; a sum above the budget is `doctor_refused` (§7). Otherwise each detector's share is `budget × cost_ms / Σcost_ms`, at least 1 ms, or the whole budget when Σcost_ms is 0; its deadline is the earlier of `now + share` and `diagnosing_start + budget` (decided while writing this bead).
- **The constants** (`src/limits.rs`, each with a `REGISTRY` row and a `LIMIT_NAMES` entry; re-accept the `limit_registries` snapshot and review the diff): `DOCTOR_SCAN_MAX_ENTRIES: u64 = 20_000` ("entries one detector's walks visit per run; past it the detector stops and reports check-incomplete"), `DOCTOR_DETECTOR_DEADLINE: Duration = 2 s` ("a default or deep detector's run-time deadline without --budget; past it, check-incomplete"), and, in s4, `RUN_ID_RETRY: u32 = 2` ("fresh ULIDs drawn after a run-directory name collision").
- **The detector signature** becomes `pub detect: Option<fn(&DoctorView, &Selection, &mut Budget) -> Detected>` (`None` exactly for `Tier::Runtime` rows; E1's invariant test gains that rule), whatever E1 shipped. Every existing detector and caller is updated by hand. `status` passes `Budget::for_tier(tier)`; no cached or quick detector walks before F3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.3`), so `incomplete` never arises there, and F8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.8`) decides how `status` shows one when it moves `status` onto the registry. `Tier::Runtime` (wire `runtime`) is added and never selected by a tier filter.

### 7. `doctor diagnose`: selection, refusals, `--since`, output (s5)

`src/app/doctor.rs` (the CLI wiring and outcomes) and `src/doctor/mod.rs` (`pub fn plan_diagnose(registry, args) -> Result<DiagnosePlan, Error>`, pure).

**Order of a run.** Arguments (clap) → `Context::new` → selection and refusals (no write) → `-t` resolved by E2's `Selection` (a read of the registry, tolerant) → `--since` resolved → STARTING → DIAGNOSING → terminal writes → emit. Every refusal before STARTING creates no run directory (decided while writing this bead): usage errors, `online_required`, `doctor_refused`/`over_budget`, `--since` errors and `-t` errors.

**Selection** (decided while writing this bead where the plan is silent):

- The candidate set is `--only`'s entries (failure-mode ids or subsystem names, validated by E2 with the closest id on a miss) or every row. `--skip` removes entries. Runtime rows are never candidates: `--only` or `--skip` naming one is `usage` ("fm-state_files-check-incomplete is reported by the run, not a check"), fix = the argv without it.
- **Tier filter:** with `--quick`, `cached` and `quick`; with `--include-deep`, every tier; with neither, every tier but `deep`, except that `--only` without a tier flag runs exactly what it names, whatever the tier. A selection that ends empty is `usage` naming why (`--quick excludes fm-x (tier default)`), fix = the argv without the excluding flag.
- **`--severity Pn`** keeps rows of severity ≤ Pn. It never hides the runtime rows: a `check-incomplete` (P3) under `--severity P2` is still reported, because hiding it would make incomplete coverage read as healthy (M4-D43).
- **Online:** a selection holding only `online: true` rows without `--online` is `online_required` (`details {fms}`), fix = the argv with `--online`. A mixed selection runs the offline rows and lists the online ones in `skipped` with reason `online_required`. `--online` together with `--offline` or `OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1` is `usage` whose fix drops `--online` (the offline guard wins).
- **`skipped[]`** holds only selected rows that did not run (online-only without `--online`; E2's unavailable-layer reasons), sorted by id; rows excluded by `--only`, `--skip`, `--severity` or the tier filter are not listed.
- **`-t`** narrows target-scoped detectors; machine-level findings stay unless `--only` excludes them (E2's `Selection`). An unknown target is `target_not_found`, exit 66 (with the closest id of C3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.3`, once it has landed).

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `online_required` | 1 (`failed`) | 6 | no | `{fms: [string]}` | `--only` selects only online failure modes without `--online` | the argv plus `--online` |
| `doctor_refused` | 4 (`refused`) | 4 | no | `{reason: enum of 8, fm?: string, resources?: [string], budget_ms?: integer, estimated_ms?: integer}` | `reason: "over_budget"`: Σcost_ms > `--budget` | the argv with `--budget <Σcost rounded up to 100>ms`; alternative: the argv without `--budget` |

### 8. `doctor explain` (s6)

- `omaddons doctor explain <ID> [-t <target>]`: `<ID>` is a failure-mode id (all its live instances) or an instance key (exactly that instance). An unknown id, or a key whose failure-mode part is unknown or whose scope is neither a ULID nor `machine`, is `usage` (64) with the closest id within distance 2 in place, else `omaddons help doctor explain` (decided while writing this bead).
- **Re-detected purely:** `DoctorView::load` with a selection of that one row and `-t`, then the runtime's per-detector helper with a `Budget` of `DOCTOR_DETECTOR_DEADLINE` whatever the row's tier (an explain is a deliberate look). No run directory, no request, no write of any kind. A caught panic is `internal` (exit 74): explain has no run to continue and its answer would be wrong (decided while writing this bead).
- **Data** (`ExplainReport`, A.8 plus one additive key):

  ```json
  {"failure_mode":{"id":"…","subsystem":"…","severity":"P2","title":"…","description":"…","why":"…","tier":"cached",
                   "fixer":null,"manual":{"instruction":"omaddons targets rm <id> forgets it","reason":"only you know whether the client is gone for good"}},
   "instances":["…findings, the diagnose shape…"],
   "incomplete":null}
  ```

  `fixer` is `{ops, writes_to, enabled, needs_force, reversible}` or `null` (every row is `null` until the F leaves add fixers). `manual` is `{instruction, reason}` or `null` (decided while writing this bead, the same pair E4's `doctor capabilities` lists as `manual_remediations`); if E1's row has no static manual text, add it to the row and fill it for the 9 rows that exist. `incomplete` (additive, decided while writing this bead) is `null`, or `{limit: "deadline" | "entries" | "online_required", deadline_ms, max_entries}` when the detector was cut short or the row is online-only (explain never requests). A key whose instance no longer exists gives exit 0 with `instances: []`; `-t` and a key on another target give `instances: []`. A runtime row gives its registry entry and `instances: []` (its instances live in a run's report). `commands: []`.
- **Human output:** the title, `P2 · subsystem · tier`, the description, why it matters, the repair (`no automatic repair` or the fixer), the manual remediation, then each instance's label, evidence (`key: value` lines, never file content) and remediation.

- [ ] A detector given a one-entry budget, or a 1 ms deadline, yields `fm-state_files-check-incomplete` (P3, naming the detector and the limit), exit 1 and `DONE_FINDINGS` (never `DONE_OK`), with `summary.incomplete` 1; `--severity P2` does not hide it.

  - `src/limits.rs` and its snapshot (B3, D4, D5, D9, E3, E6, E8, F1, G3): append rows; re-accept the snapshot in the same commit.
  - `tests/contract/matrix.rs` and snapshots: append rows; one snapshot file per row.
  - `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md`: regenerate after rebasing, never merge by hand.
- **Risk 3 (doctor false positives erode trust)** and **risk 14 (the milestone is large)**: the runtime's own rows are conservative (P1 only for a crash, P3 for incomplete coverage), and its tests run a clean home to `DONE_OK`.
- **Deadline flakiness.** A 5 ms deadline in a loaded debug build could cut a quick detector short and report `check-incomplete` on a clean home; the ×20 debug scale exists for that. If a gate test still flakes on a deadline, the fix is in the detector's charging or the scale, never a `--budget` added to the test to hide it. Tests of the deadline itself use an explicit `--budget` and the sleep failpoint, so they are exact.
- **What could go wrong in implementation, and how to notice:**
  - a flattened report key colliding with an envelope key (`command`, `warnings`): the envelope key-order test fails;
  - `runtime.jsonl` lines lost before the stage exists, or written to the stage path after the rename: `runtime_jsonl_names_every_write` and the e2e line check;
  - a caught panic shadowing a later real one: `take_caught_panic_clears_the_slot`;
  - a general `Exit` sneaking into the doctor tree: `the_doctor_tree_exits_only_through_its_dictionary`;
  - `latest` moving backwards: `latest_moves_only_forward` pins the rule, and the hundred-run test asserts `latest` resolves to one of the hundred runs (never dangling; the same-instant race is accepted, so it does not assert which one).
- **Compatibility with older builds.** The M3 build never lists or sweeps `<state>/doctor/` (its orphan sweep matches only transaction names, `src/state/paths.rs:33-35`), and E9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9`) characterizes it against doctor run directories. Retention never touches `<state>/doctor/` (M4-D36). A staged `.<id>.tmp` left by a crash is not a run (it does not parse as `DoctorRunId`), is never listed, and is deletable by E8's gc (`Kind::DoctorRun` matches any plain name).
- **Privacy.** Evidence never holds file content (M4-D42); the runtime's evidence holds detector ids and source locations only; labels name targets and addons. The run directory is the user's own state, owner-only.
- **Performance.** The runtime adds one directory creation, one rename, one small file write, one symlink swap and two chmods to a diagnose: well under a millisecond on a local filesystem. `explain` writes nothing.
- **The doctor never configures anything** (§7.8): no new `config.toml` key; the budgets are constants, not preferences.
- **Previews bind (common rule 16).** No mutating path is added here; `doctor diagnose` and `doctor explain` are `mutates: false`, and the close comment says so.

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M4 plan, 2026-10-24).**

**Why this bead.** Today omaddons has no doctor. A user whose client is stuck gets an error whose fix points at README prose, an agent has no single call that says what is broken, and the states README calls "left for manual repair" have no name. After this bead, `omaddons doctor` runs every selected detector under a budget, names each finding with evidence and an exact remediation, records the run in its own directory, prints the report at the top level of the envelope as the external doctor contract wants, and exits with the doctor's own dictionary; `omaddons doctor explain` says what a failure mode is and shows its live instances. It is the runtime every later doctor bead runs inside: the fixes of E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`, `doctor fix`), the undo of E7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7`, undo of repairs), the gc of E8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.8`, `doctor gc`) and the catalog leaves' forty-odd detectors (F1 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1` to F10 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.10`) all extend the state machine, the run directory, the envelope and the dictionary built here. It keeps the thesis true where it begins: the doctor diagnoses without changing anything but its own record, and says when it could not look.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M4-D32:** a run directory `<state>/doctor/runs/<UTC time>__<ULID>/` holding `report.json` and `runtime.jsonl` (the runtime's own writes), `latest` as an `SymlinkAtomic` link for reading the last report, files 0600 in a 0700 directory, record files 0400 at the end, directories never hardened.
- **M4-D33:** every diagnose makes a run directory; `explain` does not. Run ids are a readable timestamp plus a fresh ULID, published with `RENAME_NOREPLACE`, retried with a new ULID at most `RUN_ID_RETRY` times, never waiting for the clock. `doctor diagnose` is `mutates: false`; `special.rs` exempts exactly `<state>/doctor/` and strips the doctor's volatile keys.
- **M4-D34:** the report's keys at the top level, `error` only for exits 4, 5, 6, 64, 66, 73 and 74, no `data`, `next_steps` mirroring `commands[]`, the report schema as the path's `data` schema.
- **M4-D40:** `doctor::Exit` with the vision's eleven names, the total `exit_for` (three explicit rows, then the general class), `online_required` and `doctor_refused`, and a panic in the doctor tree exiting 74.
- **M4-D43:** budgets enforced at run time through a `Budget` and the bounded walker; a cut-short detector becomes `check-incomplete`, so incomplete coverage is never `DONE_OK`.
- **M4-D18:** the doctor's volatile keys declared (`run_id`, `run_dir`, `started_at`, `finished_at`, `summary.duration_ms`).
- **M4-D30:** `--since` and `explain` work on resource-specific instance keys, never labels.
- **M4-D47, M4-D48:** the two runtime failure modes (`detector-crashed`, `check-incomplete`) with Rust fixtures in `tests/doctor/`.
- **M4-D15:** the doctor's corpus rows, whose fixes must run.

**Alternatives rejected that matter here.**
- The doctor contract's deterministic run id (a hash of the state directory and the second): collisions under ordinary parallel use, and no progress at all under a frozen test clock.
- A run directory for `health`: unbounded growth under a widget or a cron job.
- Nesting the report under `data`: it breaks every generic doctor consumer.
- The general exit dictionary in the doctor tree: "findings present" is a normal outcome there, not a failure.
- Estimated budgets only: a walk over a huge `AddOns` would run past any budget, and a walk cut short would look like a clean one.
- `doctor --fix` and `doctor --explain` as flags: one path, one meaning; typed anyway they are intent hints, and `doctor --fix` points at a preview, never a mutation.
- `report.md`, scorecards and captured streams in the run directory: drift, or the doctor-builder's artifacts, not the user's.

**Risks and how they are watched.**
- A deadline that cuts a detector short on a clean home in a slow debug build would make the gate report `check-incomplete` spuriously: implicit tier deadlines are scaled in debug builds, explicit `--budget` deadlines are exact, and the deadline tests use an explicit budget and a sleep failpoint.
- A caught detector panic must not crash the run or shadow a later real panic: `catch_unwind` per detector, a compile-time check that the build unwinds, and the first-panic slot cleared after each caught panic.
- The process exit was typed as the general dictionary everywhere: a `ProcessExit` carries either dictionary, and exit-site tests (a source scan plus a behavioural table) hold the doctor tree to its own.
- Risk 3 (false positives erode trust): the runtime's own rows are conservative, and a clean home must reach `DONE_OK`.

**Facts verified while writing this bead** (at `c0ab5e9`): no `src/doctor/` and no `doctor` subcommand exist; `cli::run` converts an `Exit` (`cli.rs:357`), `render_error` and `render_panic` return `Exit` (`cli.rs:432-449`, `cli.rs:1307-1352`), and `emitted_exit` maps only `Exit::ALL` (`output/mod.rs:70-73`); the envelope is `envelope.rs:20-38`; `support::check` is inside `tests/contract/main.rs` (`main.rs:29-225`); the read-only test is `special.rs:312-386`; untracked sessions log nothing (`mutate.rs:375-396`); `Paths::doctor_runs_dir()` exists (`paths.rs:347-350`); prune's `Kind::DoctorRun` exists (`prune.rs:375`); `Op::CreateDir` takes no mode (`op.rs:19-20`); `QUICK_DETECTOR_BUDGET` exists unused (`limits.rs:62`); `model::RunId` already names M2's invocation id (`model.rs:295-300`); the panic hook keeps the first panic even when caught (`cli.rs:1278-1301`); `status` reports one journal issue per target (`issues.rs:126-150`).

**What it unblocks, and why they wait.** E4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4`, `doctor health`, `ls`, `--robot-triage`, `capabilities` and `robot-docs`) adds `health`, `ls`, `--robot-triage`, `capabilities` and `robot-docs` to this clap tree and reads its run directories; E6 extends this state machine with planning, the lock, mutation and verification; E8's gc needs the run layout and the terminal-record rule; F1 (journal and lock detectors), F3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.3`, state files and schemas), F4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.4`, configs, userland state and permissions) and F5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.5`, external artifacts) add detectors that run under these budgets and walk with this walker; the discovery line of A6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.6`, bare help's discovery line) names `omaddons doctor --json`, which must exist first; the slice-3 demo of T4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4`, slice 3 end to end) runs `doctor` on stuck homes. Each would otherwise invent its own run handling, envelope or exit mapping, and the three would drift.

**How it serves the milestone.** G-M4-4 (a check that ran out of budget says so; findings carry evidence and remediation), G-M4-5 (every exit site maps to its dictionary; repeated runs print identical bytes after declared volatile keys), G-M4-6 (every write through one logged fsx session; nothing outside `<state>/doctor/`), and checkpoint criteria 10 (in part), 9 (the runtime's part), 5 (the doctor rows) and 14 (the doctor's volatile keys). It is on the critical path (slack 0, plan keys resolved by the key table on the milestone epic `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`): E1 → E2 → **E3** → E6 → E7 → F2 → H1 → H2 → H4 → H5 → H6.

**Confidence.** Medium-high. The runtime is plumbing over fsx primitives that exist; the risks are interface ones (the process exit type, the envelope's flattened keys, the detector signature that E1 and E2 shape), each pinned by a unit test before any command uses it, and the seven subtasks land in commits that each pass the gate.

**The M4 plan's entry for E3, verbatim (M4 plan, 2026-10-24).** This is the M4 plan's entry, lines 4283–4313 of the plan, kept as provenance. The description above is the authoritative, elaborated version; where they differ, the description was decided while filing and says why.

#### E3 `doctor diagnose` and `explain`: runtime, run directories, the doctor envelope and its exit dictionary
- **Type** feature · **P1** · **size-L** · **slice-3**
- **Blocked by:** A1 (the doctor's `COMMANDS` rows carry the new fields), E1, E2.
- **Unblocks:** E4, E6, E8, F1, F3, F4, F5, A6.
- **Background.** M4-D32, M4-D33, M4-D34, M4-D40, M4-D43, §6.11, §6.12. `explain` lands here, not in E4, because E3's own reports emit `doctor explain` argv in `commands[]` and `remediation`, and the contract suite runs every argv it sees.
- **Technical approach.**
  1. The `doctor` clap tree with bare `doctor`, `doctor diagnose` and `doctor explain`, with every diagnose flag of §6.11. DEC-1 (no stubs) applies: E4, E6, E7 and E8 each add their own subcommands (`health`, `ls`, `capabilities`, `robot-docs`; `fix` and `diff`; `undo`; `gc`) with their `COMMANDS` rows and `CLI_PATHS` rows, in their own commits.
  2. **No mutating flag on a read-only path.** `doctor --fix` and `doctor --explain <id>` are intent hints in `usage_error`: the fix is `omaddons doctor fix` or `omaddons doctor explain <id>` (C.2 rows). `--dry-run` is global and changes nothing on `diagnose`.
  3. `doctor::Exit` and the total `exit_for` (M4-D40), with its test over `ErrorCode::ALL`. The error codes `online_required` and `doctor_refused`. `output::emitted_exit` and the panic path learn the doctor dictionary, and `exit_sites.rs` learns it too.
  4. The doctor envelope (`output::envelope::DoctorEnvelope`, report keys at the top level). The `diagnose` report is a serde enum tagged by `view` (`full`; E4 adds `triage`). `tests/contract/support::check` gains a doctor mode.
  5. `runtime.rs`: `STARTING` (the run id as UTC timestamp plus a fresh ULID, a staged run directory, publication with `RENAME_NOREPLACE` and a fresh ULID on collision, at most `RUN_ID_RETRY` times), `DIAGNOSING` (detectors under `catch_unwind`, `detector-crashed` findings), the terminal states, `report.json`, `latest`, and hardening of the record files only (§6.12).
  6. **Budgets** (M4-D43): `src/doctor/budget.rs` with `Budget` (a deadline and an entry counter) and the bounded walker; each detector gets its `Budget` (`QUICK_DETECTOR_BUDGET`, `DOCTOR_DETECTOR_DEADLINE`, `--budget`'s share, `DOCTOR_SCAN_MAX_ENTRIES`); an `incomplete` return becomes a `fm-state_files-check-incomplete` finding (Appendix B row 46, this leaf's row), so the run is not `DONE_OK`.
  7. fsx: `WriteSession::untracked_logged(path)`, an untracked session that appends one line per `mutate()` to `<run>/runtime.jsonl` with its own sequence.
  8. `explain` (§6.11): a failure-mode id or an instance key; the registry entry plus live instances, re-detected purely.
  9. The human output (§6.11). Flags: `--only`, `--skip`, `--severity`, `--quick`, `--include-deep`, `--online`, `--budget`, `--since` (comparing instance keys), `-t`. An online-only `--only` without `--online` is `online_required`.
  10. Declare the volatile keys (M4-D18). Exempt `<state>/doctor/` in `special.rs`'s read-only rule, and strip the doctor's volatile keys in its "ignores `--dry-run` and `--reason`" comparison (`special.rs:313`); H3 generalizes this later.
- **Acceptance criteria.**
  - `doctor` on a clean synthetic home exits 0, `state: DONE_OK`, and creates exactly one run directory with `report.json`, `runtime.jsonl` and `latest`.
  - With the 7 moved findings planted, it exits 1, `DONE_FINDINGS`, and every `commands[]` argv in the report (each a `doctor explain`) runs and exits 0.
  - Every exit site of the doctor tree maps to the doctor dictionary, and `exit_for` maps every `ErrorCode`.
  - A panicking detector (the debug failpoint `doctor.detector.panic`) yields a `detector-crashed` finding, and the run completes.
  - **Unique run ids.** A hundred concurrent `doctor` runs under a frozen clock (`OMADDONS_NOW`) create a hundred distinct run directories, and none waits.
  - A detector given a one-entry budget, or a 1 ms deadline, yields `check-incomplete`, exit 1, and `health` is not `ok`.
  - `--since` with two stuck journals on one client, one of them resolved, reports one resolved and one unchanged; two skill roots give two instances.
  - At the end, the record files are 0400 and the run directory is 0700.
  - `omaddons doctor --fix` and `omaddons doctr --fix --force --yes` never yield a runnable mutating fix.
- **Test plan.** `tests/doctor.rs`. Contract doctor-mode rows. Exit-site test. The intent rows above.
- **Considerations.**
  - **Size L, kept as one leaf.** Runtime, envelope and exit dictionary are one contract surface. Each half alone emits output no consumer can parse.
  - Hot spots `src/output/` and `src/cli.rs`.
