title: `omaddons doctor` and `doctor diagnose`: the command, its flags and selection, `--since` and the human output
description:
Part 5 of 7 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3 (`doctor diagnose` and `explain`: runtime, run directories, the doctor envelope and its exit dictionary). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, the leaf this subtask belongs to) builds the read side of `omaddons doctor`. s1 built the doctor exit dictionary and envelope, s2 the logged fsx session, s3 the budgets, s4 the runtime as library code. **This part** ships the user-visible command: `omaddons doctor` (bare) and `omaddons doctor diagnose`, with every diagnose flag of §6.11 but `--robot-triage` (E4's, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4`), the selection rules, the two new error codes (`online_required`, `doctor_refused`), `--since`, the human output, the volatile-key declarations, and every DEC-1 registry touch point of the two paths in this one commit. It is its own step because DEC-1 requires a command's touch points to land together, and `doctor explain` (s6) is a separate path with its own.

It serves G-M4-4 ("`omaddons doctor` names every broken state omaddons can detect … A check that ran out of budget or entries says so"), G-M4-5 ("every exit site maps to a published code in the right dictionary; repeated runs print identical bytes"), and checkpoint criteria 10 (the surface of `doctor diagnose`, every exit site in the doctor dictionary), 9 (bare `doctor` changes nothing outside `<state>/doctor/`) and 14 (the doctor's volatile keys declared). Vision G4: "the first command an agent guesses works": `omaddons doctor --json` is the third call of the discovery line of A6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.6`).

**What is true today** (verified at `c0ab5e9`, plus s1–s4):

- `Command` (`src/cli.rs:137-213`) has no `Doctor` variant. `errors` shows the pattern for a command with both its own flags and a subcommand: `#[command(…, args_conflicts_with_subcommands = true)]` (`cli.rs:194`) and `ErrorsArgs { #[command(subcommand)] action: Option<ErrorsAction>, … }` (`src/app/errors.rs:56-90`).
- `app::COMMANDS` (`src/app/mod.rs:121-165`; A1 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1` added `dictionary`, `exits`, `data`, `stores_plan`, `network` to each row and `canonical_path`), `command_name` (`mod.rs:195-237`) and `dispatch`/`run_command` (`mod.rs:331-371`, `374-…`). The bare-help layout test `bare_help_stays_one_screen_with_every_planned_command` (`src/app/help.rs:434-477`) and `every_subcommand_has_exactly_one_registry_entry` (`help.rs:480-516`, or A1's bijection test that replaces it).
- `tests/cli_skeleton.rs:118-142` asserts bare help's group lines and snapshots it (`cli_skeleton__bare_help_human.snap`). `omarchy/Model.js:134-177` holds `CLI_PATHS`, equal to the registry (`tests/omarchy_widget.rs:30-48`).
- The read-only test `read_only_commands_ignore_dry_run_and_reason` (`tests/contract/special.rs:312-386`) has an invocation table (`special.rs:317-338`), compares envelopes with `support::without_meta` (`tests/contract/main.rs:508-514`) and the whole state tree with `state_tree` (`special.rs:226-248`).
- `error_codes!` (`src/error.rs:149-204`) has 41 codes; README's table says "Every error code (41)" (`README.md:1823`).
- README's `status` section has the only failure-mode table (`README.md:752-760`); there is no doctor section. "The JSON contract" (`README.md:1758-1964`) documents the general envelope and exit codes; its panic sentence says exit 1 (`README.md:1820`). "Files and state" is `README.md:2269-2301`.

**The decisions it implements** (full text in the decision log comments on the milestone epic `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`):

- **M4-D40** (the two codes): `online_required` (general exit 1, doctor exit 6), raised when `--only` selects only online failure modes and `--online` is absent; a mixed selection runs the offline ones and lists the rest in `skipped`. `doctor_refused` (general exit 4, doctor exit 4), the error of every `REFUSING` run, `details.reason` from the closed set `force_required`, `fixer_conflict`, `too_many_actions`, `over_budget`, `filesystem_mismatch`, `client_running`, `not_enabled`, `edited_locally`, `details.fm` when one failure mode is concerned, `details.resources` for `fixer_conflict`. This part raises `over_budget`; E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`) raises the others.
- **§6.11 (the surface):** `doctor` and `doctor diagnose` never mutate and accept no mutating flag; `--dry-run`, `--reason` and `--actor` are global and change nothing here. `--only`/`--skip` take comma lists of failure-mode ids or subsystem names; an unknown id is `usage` (64) with the closest id as the fix. `--severity P2` reports P0–P2 and hides P3. `--budget 500ms` refuses to start (exit 4, `doctor_refused`, `over_budget`) when the selected detectors' declared `cost_ms` sum exceeds it, and otherwise is the run's deadline, each detector getting its share. `--since <run>` adds `since: {run, new[], resolved[], unchanged}`, comparing instance keys with that run's `report.json`. `-t` narrows target-scoped detectors; machine-level findings stay unless `--only` excludes them. Tiers (M4-D29): `doctor` runs every tier but `deep`, `--quick` runs `cached` and `quick`, `--include-deep` every tier.
- **M4-D33:** `doctor diagnose` is `mutates: false`; `special.rs` exempts exactly `<state>/doctor/` and strips the doctor's volatile keys (`run_id`, `run_dir`, `started_at`, `finished_at`, `duration_ms`).
- **M4-D34:** the report at the top level; the registry's `data` schema for a doctor path is its report schema.
- **M4-D18:** the doctor's volatile keys are declared in `contract::VOLATILE`, each with a reason.
- **M4-D43:** detectors that need an unavailable layer, or the network without `--online`, go to `skipped`, never reported clean.

## Technical Approach

1. **clap** (`src/cli.rs`, `src/app/doctor.rs` new): `Command::Doctor(app::doctor::DoctorArgs)` with about "Diagnose what omaddons manages (bare: diagnose; changes nothing outside its run record)", `args_conflicts_with_subcommands = true`, and `after_long_help` listing the doctor dictionary (code, name, meaning), held equal to `doctor::Exit::ALL` by a test (decided while writing this bead: `omaddons help doctor` documents the exits).

   ```rust
   #[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, clap::Args)]
   pub struct DoctorArgs { #[command(subcommand)] pub action: Option<DoctorAction>, #[command(flatten)] pub diagnose: DiagnoseArgs }
   #[derive(Debug, Clone, clap::Subcommand)]
   pub enum DoctorAction { /// Find what is broken, with evidence and the exact fix (changes nothing)
                           Diagnose(DiagnoseArgs) }        // s6 adds Explain; the later doctor verbs add theirs
   #[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, clap::Args)]
   pub struct DiagnoseArgs {
       #[arg(long, value_delimiter = ',', value_name = "IDS")] pub only: Vec<String>,
       #[arg(long, value_delimiter = ',', value_name = "IDS")] pub skip: Vec<String>,
       #[arg(long, value_parser = ["P0", "P1", "P2", "P3"])] pub severity: Option<String>,
       #[arg(long, conflicts_with = "include_deep")] pub quick: bool,
       #[arg(long)] pub include_deep: bool,
       #[arg(long)] pub online: bool,
       #[arg(long, value_name = "DURATION", value_parser = crate::doctor::budget::parse_budget)] pub budget: Option<Duration>,
       #[arg(long, value_name = "RUN")] pub since: Option<String>,
   }
   ```

   `-t` is the global flag. No `--fix`, `--force`, `--yes`, `--explain` or `--robot-triage` (E4, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4`, adds `--robot-triage` with its view, decided while writing this bead: a flag with no view behind it would be a stub).
2. **Registry rows** (`src/app/mod.rs`), at the end of the Look group (decided while writing this bead: the least churn in bare help's Look line):

   | Path | Group | Mutates | Dictionary | Exits | Data | Stores plan | Network |
   |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
   | `doctor` | Look | false | Doctor | 0, 1, 4, 6, 64, 66, 73, 74 | `DiagnoseReport` | false | Optional |
   | `doctor diagnose` | Look | false | Doctor | 0, 1, 4, 6, 64, 66, 73, 74 | `DiagnoseReport` | false | Optional |

   `Optional` because `--online` lets F7's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.7`) online detectors request; nothing here does. `command_name`: bare `doctor` and `doctor diagnose` → `"doctor diagnose"` (the `canonical_path` of A1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1`, as bare `backup` → `backup list`). A1's static-rules test gains the doctor rule (decided while writing this bead): every Doctor-dictionary row declares 0, 64 and 74, and only codes of `doctor::Exit::ALL`.
3. **Dispatch** (`src/app/mod.rs`): the `Doctor` arm calls `doctor::run_diagnose(ctx, &args)` and renders through `Out::emit_doctor` (a new method beside `emit`, applying `boundary_fix` to a failure, then `output::emit_doctor`), returning `ProcessExit::Doctor`.
4. **The order of a run** (`app::doctor::run_diagnose`):
   1. clap and `Context::new` (their errors render with the doctor dictionary, s1);
   2. `--online` with `--offline` or `OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1` → `usage` whose fix drops `--online` (decided while writing this bead: the offline guard wins);
   3. `doctor::plan_diagnose(FAILURE_MODES, &args)` (pure, `src/doctor/mod.rs`): the selection and its refusals (item 5);
   4. `Selection` from `-t` and `--only` (E2 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.2`; `target_not_found`/`target_ambiguous`, exit 66);
   5. `--since` resolved and its report read (item 7);
   6. `Runtime::start` (s4), `DoctorView::load`, `Runtime::diagnose`, the report built (s4's `report.rs`, with `since`), the record built and `Runtime::finish`;
   7. emit.
   Every refusal in steps 1–5 happens before `STARTING` and creates no run directory (decided while writing this bead: nothing ran, so there is nothing to record).
5. **Selection** (`plan_diagnose`; decided while writing this bead where §6.11 is silent):
   - Candidates: `--only`'s entries (ids or subsystem names; E2 validates and gives the closest id on a miss, turned here into `usage` with `fix_argv` replacing the token in place, `UsageFix::UserVerb` if C1 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.1` has added it) or every row; `--skip` removes entries. A runtime row (`Tier::Runtime`) in `--only` or `--skip` is `usage` ("fm-state_files-check-incomplete is reported by the run, not a check"), fix = the argv without it.
   - Tier filter: `--quick` → `cached`, `quick`; `--include-deep` → every tier; neither → every tier but `deep`, except that `--only` without a tier flag runs exactly what it names whatever the tier. An empty result is `usage` naming why (`--quick excludes fm-x (tier default)`), fix = the argv without the excluding flag.
   - `--severity Pn` keeps rows with severity ≤ Pn. It never hides the runtime rows' findings (a P3 `check-incomplete` under `--severity P2` is still reported), because hiding it would make incomplete coverage read as healthy (M4-D43).
   - Online: only `online: true` rows without `--online` → `online_required` (`details {fms}`), fix = the argv plus `--online`; mixed → the online rows go to `skipped` with reason `online_required`.
   - `--budget`: Σ`cost_ms` of the selected rows > the budget → `doctor_refused` with `details {reason: "over_budget", budget_ms, estimated_ms}`, fix = the argv with `--budget <Σcost rounded up to the next 100>ms`, alternative = the argv without `--budget` (decided while writing this bead: the refusal says what it compared, and the fix runs). Otherwise s3's `shares` gives each row its deadline, and the run deadline is DIAGNOSING's start plus the budget.
   - `skipped[]` holds only selected rows that did not run (online-only, E2's unavailable-layer reasons), sorted by id; rows excluded by `--only`, `--skip`, `--severity` or the tier filter are not listed.
6. **The two error codes** (`src/error.rs`, appended to `error_codes!`; 41 → 43):

   ```text
   OnlineRequired = "online_required", Failed,  false;
   DoctorRefused  = "doctor_refused",  Refused, false;
   ```

   With their `meaning` and `DetailSpec` if A9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9`) has landed, otherwise A9 adds them (whichever lands second): `online_required` "a doctor selection needs the network and --online was not given", `details {fms: [string]}`; `doctor_refused` "the doctor refused before changing anything", `details {reason: enum(force_required, fixer_conflict, too_many_actions, over_budget, filesystem_mismatch, client_running, not_enabled, edited_locally), fm?: string, resources?: [string], budget_ms?: integer, estimated_ms?: integer}`. `exit_for` gains `ErrorCode::OnlineRequired => Exit::OnlineRequired` and its unit case. Add both to the hand-written table `EXPECTED` in `error.rs`'s tests (`error.rs:744-762`: `("online_required", 1, false)`, `("doctor_refused", 4, false)`), bump its two counts from 41 to 43 (`error.rs:803-804`), and update README's table.
7. **`--since <run>`:**
   - `<run>` is an exact `DoctorRunId`, or `latest` (resolved through `<state>/doctor/latest`; decided while writing this bead: reading the last report is what `latest` is for). A run directory that does not exist, or has no `report.json` (an interrupted run), is `not_found` (exit 66) with the message naming which, fix = the argv with the newest run id, alternatives = the next two (newest first; listed with `budget::list_dir` under a `DOCTOR_SCAN_MAX_ENTRIES` budget, keeping names that parse as `DoctorRunId`). With no run at all, the fix is the argv without `--since`.
   - The report is read with a bound of `API_RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES` (64 MiB, `src/limits.rs:85`; decided while writing this bead: the largest JSON document omaddons reads anywhere, rather than a new constant), decoded into `{schema_version, findings: [{instance}]}` ignoring other keys. A newer major `schema_version` is `state_too_new` (exit 4); an oversized or undecodable file is `state_corrupt` (exit 74) with `details.path`.
   - `report.since = report::since(old, &findings)` (s4): `{run, new, resolved, unchanged}`.
8. **`DiagnoseOutcome`** (`impl DoctorOutcome`): `command()` = `"doctor diagnose"`; `report()` = `DiagnoseReport::Full(…)`; `exit()` = `Healthy` for `DONE_OK`, `FindingsPresent` for `DONE_FINDINGS`; `commands()` = s4's explain hints; `render_human`:

   ```text
   omaddons doctor · 3 clients · 9 checks · 2 findings (1 P0, 1 P3)
     P0 fm-concurrency_primitives-journal-pending  retail
        An interrupted change waits to be finished
        → quit the game if it is running, then run any change command; it finishes or rolls back the change first
     P3 fm-state_files-check-incomplete  fm-external_artifacts-managed-files-modified (incomplete)
        a check could not finish within its limit (its 100 ms deadline)
        → omaddons doctor --only fm-external_artifacts-managed-files-modified --budget 1000ms
   run 2026-10-30T18-02-11Z__01M8R… · omaddons doctor explain <id> for the evidence
   ```

   "N clients" is the view's target count; "N checks" the detectors that ran. A clean run says `· no findings`. Skipped checks: `(3 online checks skipped)` in the summary, and under `-v` one line each with its reason. `--since` adds `since <run>: 1 new · 1 resolved · 1 unchanged` (the keys under `-v`). Labels name targets and addons only.
9. **Volatile keys** (`src/contract/volatile.rs`; create `src/contract/` and this file with `VOLATILE: &[(&str, &str)]` and the existing rows `meta.*`, `data.**.duration_ms` and `data.**.lock_held_ms` if no earlier leaf created them, decided while writing this bead): add `run_id`, `run_dir`, `started_at`, `finished_at` ("a new doctor run per invocation") and `summary.duration_ms` ("timing").
10. **The read-only test** (`tests/contract/special.rs`): invocations `"doctor" => &["doctor"]` and `"doctor diagnose" => &["doctor", "diagnose"]`; for a Doctor-dictionary path, `state_tree` skips exactly `<state>/doctor/` and the envelope comparison strips `run_id`, `run_dir`, `started_at`, `finished_at` and `summary.duration_ms` besides `meta` (a local helper `without_volatile`; H3 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3` generalizes it to `VOLATILE`). Every other path is compared exactly as before.
11. **Contract matrix rows** (`tests/contract/matrix.rs`, a new `fn doctor()`; snapshots through `stable()`, which redacts run ids to `<run>`): `doctor` on `Scene::new()` → 0 or 1 as the Scene is (assert the code it is and snapshot it, `doctor_ok`); `doctor --only fm-nope` → 64 (`doctor_unknown_only`); `doctor diagnose` → `doctor_diagnose_ok`; `doctor diagnose --since 2026-01-01T00-00-00Z__01M8R000000000000000000000` → 66 (`doctor_diagnose_since_unknown`). Each row goes through `support::check`'s doctor mode and A1's exit observation.
12. **Help and skeleton:** `help.rs`'s planned-layout test gains `("doctor", Look)` (23 rows; still under 30 lines; the Look line still fits `MAX_WIDTH`); `tests/cli_skeleton.rs`'s literals and the bare-help snapshot are updated (bare help's Look line ends with `doctor`); `doctor_help_lists_the_doctor_dictionary` (unit, `help.rs`).
13. **`CLI_PATHS`** (`omarchy/Model.js`): `"doctor": { "mutates": false, "destructive": false, "binds": false }` and `"doctor diagnose"` the same.
14. **The rule test** (M4-D55, A3 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`): the report's `state` values (`DONE_OK`, `DONE_FINDINGS`) and `Severity` (`P0`–`P3`, values and `by_severity` keys) are the external doctor contract's vocabulary (A.4) and are not snake case. Decided while writing this bead: keep A.4's spelling and add an exception keyed by those two types to A3's rule test, with the reason "the doctor contract's names (M4-D34)", never a line on `tests/contract/rules_allowlist.txt`; whichever of A3 and this leaf lands second adds it, and H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`) audits it.
15. **README** (this commit): a `### doctor` section in the command reference (synopsis; what it reads; "changes nothing outside `<state>/doctor/`"; the flags and selection rules; `--budget`, `--since`, `--online`; the human output; the run directory); "The JSON contract" gains "The doctor envelope" and "Doctor exit codes" (the dictionary, `exit_for`'s rule, 73 for the run directory), and its panic sentence says 74 in the doctor tree; the error table gains `online_required` and `doctor_refused` and its title "Every error code (43)"; "Files and state" gains `<state>/doctor/runs/<run>/` (`report.json`, `runtime.jsonl`; 0700 directory, 0400 records; owner-only, kept until `doctor gc`) and `<state>/doctor/latest`; the doctor's failure-mode table is created (decided while writing this bead: README has none) with the 7 published rows and `detector-crashed` and `check-incomplete`; the volatile keys under the JSON contract's determinism note.
16. **`skills/omaddons/SKILL.md`:** once B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`) has landed, regenerate with `OMADDONS_UPDATE_SKILL=1 cargo test --test skill` and commit it.

## Acceptance Criteria

From s4 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3.4, landed): the runtime is library code on main. Here is how this part drives it, and two items s4 left for the commit that adds the command.

**The calls, in order** (`src/doctor/runtime.rs`, `src/doctor/report.rs`):
1. `let scopes = ScopeTable::new(&paths, &[], None)?; let run = Runtime::start(&paths, &scopes, clock::now())?;`. Its `Err` is a `DoctorFailure` with exit 73: emit it through `emit_doctor`.
2. `let diagnosis = run.diagnose(FAILURE_MODES, &view, &selection, tiers, budgets)?;`. `budgets` is `Budgets::TierDefaults`, or `Budgets::Run(d)` for `--budget` (`budget::parse_budget` is the clap value parser). `tiers` is what `--quick` and `--include-deep` select. Its error (an unresolvable `-t`) is a `DoctorFailure::from(error)`.
3. `let full = FullReport::new(run.id().clone(), run.dir().display().to_string(), diagnosis, since);`, where `since = report::since(old_run, &old_instance_keys, &findings)` when `--since` is given. Reading the old `report.json` is this part's.
4. Build the envelope from `DiagnoseReport::Full(full)`, serialize its `DoctorEnvelope::report(…).record(RunKind::Diagnose)` form, and pass the bytes to `run.finish(&bytes)`. Then emit the stdout form with `emit_doctor`. Exit: `Healthy` iff `RunState::of(&findings) == DoneOk`, else `FindingsPresent`.

title: `omaddons doctor explain`, and the `--fix` and `--explain` intent hints
description:
Part 6 of 7 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3 (`doctor diagnose` and `explain`: runtime, run directories, the doctor envelope and its exit dictionary). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, the leaf this subtask belongs to) builds the read side of `omaddons doctor`; s5 shipped `doctor` and `doctor diagnose`. Every report s5 prints names `omaddons doctor explain <fm> [-t <id>]` in `commands[]` (`doctor_explain`), in `next_steps` and in each finding's `remediation.explain_argv`, and the contract suite runs every argv it sees. **This part** ships that command: `omaddons doctor explain <fm-id | instance key> [-t <target>]`, with its DEC-1 touch points in one commit; plus the two intent hints for the doctor contract's flags that omaddons does not have (`doctor --fix`, `doctor --explain <id>`), which point at real commands, and the doctor's rows of the run-the-fix corpus. `explain` lands in this leaf and not in E4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4`, the doctor's other read verbs) precisely because this leaf's own reports emit its argv.

It serves G-M4-4 (each finding's evidence and remediation are inspectable on demand), G-M4-2 ("a plausible wrong invocation yields a usage error whose fix is the command the user meant … each such fix is proven to run … a fix never turns the user's verb into a different command that changes something"), and checkpoint criterion 5 (the doctor verb typos in the corpus). Vision G4: "the first command an agent guesses works".

**What is true today** (verified at `c0ab5e9`, plus s1–s5):

- `cli::usage_error` (`src/cli.rs:604-773`) handles an `UnknownArgument` by correcting the flag in place (Levenshtein ≤ 2 over the root's globals and the reached command's flags) or falling back to help (`cli.rs:689-743`); a final filter drops any suggestion that does not parse or is the failing command itself and falls back to `omaddons help <path>` (`cli.rs:756-763`). `subcommand_fix` turns a guessed *mutating* path into its help and corrects a read-only one in place (`cli.rs:849-890`, the decision at `cli.rs:879`).
- `tests/contract/usage_fixes.rs` holds a corpus of mistyped invocations and the rule `never_another_mutating_command`: a suggestion is `help …`, the command the user typed, or one that only reads (`usage_fixes.rs:12-22`).
- `tests/contract/intent_corpus.rs` is C4's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4`, the run-the-fix corpus); it may or may not exist when this part lands.
- From s5: the `doctor` clap tree with `DoctorAction::Diagnose`, the registry rows, `run_diagnose`, `Out::emit_doctor`. From s4: the per-detector helper with isolation and budgets, `DoctorRunId`, the `Finding` shape of the reports. From E2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.2`): `DoctorView::load(ctx, selection)` and `Selection`; from E1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`): the registry, the instance-key format.

**The decisions it implements** (full text in the decision log comments on the milestone epic `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`):

- **M4-D30:** `explain` accepts a failure-mode id (all its instances) or an instance key (`<fm-id>@<target key | machine>[:<discriminator>]`); `-t` narrows. Instance keys are compared, labels never.
- **M4-D33:** `explain` creates no run directory.
- **M4-D34 and §6.11:** `explain`'s report keys are `failure_mode{id, subsystem, severity, title, description, why, tier, fixer{…}|null, manual}, instances[]` (A.8), at the top level of the doctor envelope.
- **§6.11, one path one meaning:** the doctor contract's `doctor --fix` and `doctor --explain <id>` are not flags here; typed anyway, they are intent hints: a usage error whose fix is `omaddons doctor fix …` or `omaddons doctor explain <id>`. So a typo such as `omaddons doctr --fix --force --yes` can never get a runnable fix: `subcommand_fix` turns a guessed mutating path into help, and no read-only path accepts a mutating flag. E3's acceptance: "`omaddons doctor --fix` and `omaddons doctr --fix --force --yes` never yield a runnable mutating fix".
- **M4-D15:** each corpus row's wrong argv runs on its own copy of `intent_home()` and must change nothing; its `fix_argv` runs on an independent copy and must reach the declared exit.
- **M4-D12:** a fix that keeps the user's verb is `UsageFix::UserVerb` (once C1 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.1` adds the marker).
- **M4-D42:** evidence is typed and never holds file content.

## Technical Approach

1. **clap** (`src/app/doctor.rs`): `DoctorAction::Explain(ExplainArgs)`, about "One failure mode in full: what it is, why it matters, and its live instances (changes nothing)", with `ExplainArgs { #[arg(value_name = "ID")] pub id: String }` (`-t` is global).
2. **Registry row** (`src/app/mod.rs`): `doctor explain`, Look, `mutates: false`, Doctor, exits `[0, 64, 66, 74]`, data `ExplainReport`, `stores_plan: false`, network `None` (explain never requests). `command_name` → `"doctor explain"`; a dispatch arm through `Out::emit_doctor`.
3. **Resolving `<ID>`** (`src/doctor/explain.rs`, new):
   - A string with `@` is an instance key: split at the first `@`; the failure-mode part must be a registry id; the scope runs to the first `:` and must be a ULID (a target key) or `machine`; the rest (possibly containing `:`, `=` or `/`) is the discriminator, matched exactly.
   - Otherwise it is a failure-mode id.
   - An unknown failure-mode id, or a malformed key, is `usage` (exit 64): the fix replaces the id in place with the closest registry id within Levenshtein distance 2, else `omaddons help doctor explain` (decided while writing this bead: an id is an argument value, like `--only`'s, §6.11).
4. **Re-detecting** (pure, no write):
   - `DoctorView::load` with a `Selection` of that one row and `-t` (E2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.2`). An unknown `-t` is `target_not_found` (66).
   - The runtime's per-detector helper (s4) with `Budget::new(DOCTOR_DETECTOR_DEADLINE, DOCTOR_SCAN_MAX_ENTRIES)`, whatever the row's tier (decided while writing this bead: an explain is a deliberate look at one failure mode, and a 5 ms tier budget would cut it short). It is not scaled in debug builds (an explicit budget).
   - A caught panic is `internal` (exit 74) with the message "the detector of <fm> panicked at <location>; this is a bug in omaddons" (decided while writing this bead: explain has no run to continue, and an answer without its detector would be wrong).
   - Instances: the detector's findings filtered by the instance key (when one was given) and by `-t`. A key with no live instance, or a key on another target than `-t`, gives exit 0 with `instances: []` (decided while writing this bead: explain always describes the failure mode, and an empty list says the instance is gone).
   - A runtime row (`detector-crashed`, `check-incomplete`) has no detector: its registry entry and `instances: []` (its instances live in a run's report).
   - An online-only row is never re-detected (explain makes no request): `instances: []` and `incomplete.limit: "online_required"`.
5. **Data** (`ExplainReport`, `Serialize + JsonSchema`, `BTreeMap` for any map):

   ```json
   {"failure_mode":{"id":"fm-userland_state-target-vanished","subsystem":"userland_state","severity":"P2",
                    "title":"The client's directory is gone","description":"…","why":"…","tier":"cached",
                    "fixer":null,
                    "manual":{"instruction":"omaddons targets rm <id> forgets the client","reason":"only you know whether the client is gone for good"}},
    "instances":[ …findings, the same shape as `doctor diagnose`'s… ],
    "incomplete":null}
   ```

   - `fixer` is `{ops, writes_to, enabled, needs_force, reversible}` from the row's `FixerSpec`, or `null` (every row is `null` until the F leaves add fixers).
   - `manual` is `{instruction, reason}` or `null` (decided while writing this bead: the same pair E4's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4`) `doctor capabilities` lists as `manual_remediations[{id, instruction, reason}]`). If the row of E1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`) carries no static manual text, add `manual: Option<Manual { instruction: &'static str, reason: &'static str }>` to `FailureMode` and fill it for the 9 rows that exist (the 7 published and the 2 runtime rows). `instruction` uses `<placeholders>` for values only the user has, so it never names a runnable command (`names_a_command`).
   - `incomplete` (an additive key, decided while writing this bead: a cut-short explain must not read as a complete list, common rule 15) is `null` or `{limit: "deadline" | "entries" | "online_required", deadline_ms: u64 | null, max_entries: u64 | null}`.
   - `commands: []`, no `next_steps` (explain's own report does not suggest; each instance carries its remediation).
6. **Human output:**

   ```text
   fm-userland_state-target-vanished · P2 · userland_state · cached
   The client's directory is gone
     what: a registered client's directory no longer exists
     why:  its records stay, and every command that selects it fails
     repair: no automatic repair; omaddons targets rm <id> forgets the client (only you know whether it is gone for good)
   1 instance:
     retail  (01M5…)
       path: <client dir>
       → omaddons targets rm retail
   ```

   Evidence prints as `key: value` lines, never file content; `incomplete` prints "this list may be partial: the check stopped at its <limit>".
7. **The intent hints** (`src/cli.rs`, a new function `doctor_intent_hint(argv, path, bad_flag) -> Option<(Suggestion, Vec<Suggestion>)>` called first in the `UnknownArgument` arm when `path` is `["doctor"]` or `["doctor", "diagnose"]`; its own function, as the hot-spot rule for `src/cli.rs` asks):
   - `--fix`: once `doctor fix` is a `COMMANDS` path (E6 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6` adds it), the fix is `omaddons doctor fix --dry-run` keeping the selection flags the user typed (`--only`, `--skip`, `--severity`, `--quick`, `--include-deep`, `--online`, `-t` and their values) and dropping `--fix`, `--force` and `--yes`; until then, `omaddons help doctor`. Decided while writing this bead: the leaf's acceptance requires that `doctor --fix` never yields a runnable mutating fix, and a preview shows exactly what `doctor fix` would do (Appendix C.2's "fix `omaddons doctor fix`, exit 0 or 1" holds for the preview). The message: "doctor has no --fix flag; fixing is its own command".
   - `--explain <id>` (or `--explain=<id>`): the fix is `omaddons doctor explain <id>`, keeping `-t`; with no value, `omaddons help doctor explain`. The message: "doctor has no --explain flag; explaining is its own command".
   - Mark both `UsageFix::UserVerb` if C1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.1`) has added it.
   - `tests/contract/usage_fixes.rs`'s rule `never_another_mutating_command` gains: a suggestion holding `--dry-run` counts as one that only reads (decided while writing this bead: every dry run leaves `<state>` untouched, `special.rs:251`, so a preview never changes something), so the `--fix` hint passes it after E6 too.
   - `omaddons doctr --fix --force --yes` needs no new code: `doctr` → `subcommand_fix` guesses the read-only `doctor`, the corrected argv `omaddons doctor --fix --force --yes` does not parse, and the final filter gives `omaddons help`. A test pins it.
8. **Corpus rows** (`tests/contract/intent_corpus.rs`; if C4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4`) has not landed, C4 adds them when it does, whichever lands second):

   | Wrong | Code | Fix | Fix exit |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | `omaddons doctor --fix` | `usage` | `omaddons help doctor` (from E6 on, `omaddons doctor fix --dry-run`) | 0 or 1 |
   | `omaddons doctor --explain fm-schemas-state-version-newer` | `usage` | `omaddons doctor explain fm-schemas-state-version-newer` | 0 |
   | `omaddons doctor diagnoze` | `usage` | `omaddons doctor diagnose` | 0 or 1 |
   | `omaddons doctor --only fm-nope` | `usage` | `omaddons doctor` | 0 or 1 |
   | `omaddons doctr` | `usage` | `omaddons doctor` | 0 or 1 |
   | `omaddons doctor explain fm-concurrency_primitives-journal-pendng` | `usage` | `omaddons doctor explain fm-concurrency_primitives-journal-pending` | 0 |

   Decided while writing this bead: the `--explain` row uses the published `fm-schemas-state-version-newer` instead of Appendix C.2's `fm-schemas-state-corrupt`, which is F3's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.3`) row and does not exist when this lands, so the C.2 argv's fix would exit 64; diagnose fixes declare "0 or 1", because a finding on the corpus home is a successful run. Each erroring row changes nothing on its copy of the home (the corpus harness's tree hashes), which also proves a diagnose that never started wrote no run directory.
   - `doctor --only fm-nope`'s fix is the argv without the unknown entry (`omaddons doctor`), since no id is within distance 2 (s5's `--only` rule).
9. **The other DEC-1 touch points** (this commit): the help layout (nothing in bare help: `explain` is a subcommand); a contract matrix row pair in `tests/contract/matrix.rs::doctor` (`doctor explain fm-userland_state-target-vanished` → 0, snapshot `doctor_explain_ok`; `doctor explain fm-nope` → 64, snapshot `doctor_explain_unknown`); the `special.rs` invocation `"doctor explain" => &["doctor", "explain", "fm-userland_state-target-vanished"]` (its state comparison exempts `<state>/doctor/` like every doctor path, though explain writes nothing there either); `cli_skeleton` literals if any list doctor's subcommands; the `CLI_PATHS` row `"doctor explain": { "mutates": false, "destructive": false, "binds": false }`; README `### doctor explain` (what it shows, the id and key forms, `-t`, `incomplete`) and the two hints in the usage-fix examples; `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` regenerated if B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`) has landed.

**What not to do:** create a run directory or write anything in `explain`; make a request; fall back to a fuzzy match beyond distance 2 (a wrong failure mode explained confidently is worse than help); add a `--fix` or `--explain` flag to clap (they must stay unknown so the hint fires).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `omaddons doctor explain <fm-id>` prints the doctor envelope with `failure_mode`, every live instance and `incomplete: null`; `<instance key>` gives exactly that instance; `-t` narrows; a vanished instance gives `instances: []` and exit 0.
- [ ] An unknown id or a malformed key is `usage` (64) with the closest id within distance 2 in place, else `omaddons help doctor explain`.
- [ ] `explain` writes nothing (the whole `<state>`, `doctor/` included, hash-identical), creates no run directory and makes no request; a runtime row and an online-only row answer with `instances: []` (the latter with `incomplete.limit: online_required`).
- [ ] Every `doctor explain` argv in a `doctor diagnose` report runs and exits 0.
- [ ] `omaddons doctor --fix` gives `omaddons help doctor` (from E6, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`, on, `omaddons doctor fix --dry-run` with the selection flags kept and never `--force` or `--yes`); `omaddons doctr --fix --force --yes` gives `omaddons help`; `omaddons doctor --explain <id> -t retail` gives `omaddons doctor explain <id> -t retail`.
- [ ] The DEC-1 touch points of `doctor explain` all land in this commit (clap variant, `COMMANDS` row, `command_name` and dispatch, the matrix rows with snapshots, the `special.rs` invocation, the `CLI_PATHS` row, README).
- [ ] The six corpus rows pass when C4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4`) has landed (each wrong argv changes nothing; each fix reaches its declared exit).
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files; `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` is regenerated where B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`) has landed; `br lint` is clean.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

- `src/doctor/explain.rs`:
  - `instance_key_parsing`, cases: `fm-x-y@machine` (machine, no discriminator); `fm-x-y@01M5…:tx=01M7…`; `fm-x-y@01M5…:path=/a/b:c` (a discriminator with `:` and `/`); unknown fm part → usage; scope `retail` (an id, not a key) → usage; empty discriminator after `:` → kept as empty and matched exactly.
  - `closest_id_within_two`: `fm-concurrency_primitives-journal-pendng` → `…-journal-pending`; `fm-nope` → none.
  - `filtering_by_key_and_target`.
  - `explain_report_shape` (key order `failure_mode, instances, incomplete`; `manual` object; `fixer: null`).
- `src/cli.rs`: `doctor_intent_hint_cases`, one name each: `doctor --fix` (before `doctor fix` exists → `help doctor`); `doctor --fix --only fm-x -t retail --force --yes` (same); a synthetic registry with `doctor fix` present (the function takes the registry predicate as a parameter for this test) → `doctor fix --dry-run --only fm-x -t retail`, never `--force` or `--yes`; `doctor --explain fm-x -t retail` → `doctor explain fm-x -t retail`; `doctor --explain=fm-x`; `doctor --explain` with no value → `help doctor explain`; `doctor diagnose --fix` → the same as `doctor --fix`.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

- `tests/contract/matrix.rs::doctor`: the two explain rows with snapshots, in doctor mode.
- `tests/contract/special.rs`: the explain invocation.
- `tests/contract/usage_fixes.rs`: `doctor --fix`, `doctor --explain fm-schemas-state-version-newer`, `doctr --fix --force --yes` (fix exactly `["omaddons", "help"]`), each through the rule `never_another_mutating_command` (with its `--dry-run` extension and a unit case of the extension: `["omaddons", "doctor", "fix", "--dry-run"]` reads; `["omaddons", "doctor", "fix"]` does not, once `doctor fix` exists).
- `tests/contract/intent_corpus.rs`: the six rows (item 8).

The multi-command explain scenarios (explaining each planted finding by id, by instance and by target, and the write-nothing check across a diagnose) are s7's, logged through `TestLog`.

### Logging

The contract rows report through `support::check`'s failure context and the corpus harness's (both runs' envelopes on a failed row). Unit tests name their cases and show input and output.

## Considerations

- **Hot spots:** `src/cli.rs` (the hint is one new function and one call at the top of the `UnknownArgument` arm; C1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.1`) and C2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.2`, a client named as an addon) also hook `usage_error`, keep each hook separate); `src/app/mod.rs` and `tests/contract/matrix.rs` (append); `README.md` (your sections).
- **After E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`):** the `--fix` hint changes from help to the preview by itself (it asks the registry); E6's own corpus row (`doctor fix --force` without `--yes`) is E6's. If E6 lands first in some reordering, this part writes the preview form directly.
- **Why `-t` with a key on another target is not an error:** two filters that select nothing answer "nothing", consistently with a vanished instance; a usage error would need a rule about which filter wins.
- **Privacy:** instances carry the typed evidence of E1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`) (no file content, no `WTF/` path); explain adds nothing of its own beyond the registry's texts.
- Wire names added here (list in the leaf's close comment): the path `doctor explain`, `ExplainReport`'s keys (`failure_mode` and its fields, `instances`, `incomplete` with its `limit` values), the `manual` object.

- Parent: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3.

title: E2E: the doctor runtime end to end, every doctor exit site, and the two runtime fixtures
description:
Part 7 of 7 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3 (`doctor diagnose` and `explain`: runtime, run directories, the doctor envelope and its exit dictionary). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, the leaf this subtask belongs to) builds the read side of `omaddons doctor`. s1–s6 built the exit dictionary and envelope, the logged fsx session, the budgets, the runtime, `doctor`/`doctor diagnose` and `doctor explain`, each with unit tests and contract rows that run one command at a time. **This part** proves the leaf's acceptance end to end through the real binary: multi-command scenarios on synthetic homes (clean and planted states, crashes at the runtime's failpoints, a hundred concurrent runs under a frozen clock, `--since` across runs, purity and privacy), a table of every doctor exit site, and the fixtures of the leaf's two runtime failure modes, which F9's harness (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`) later runs with every other fixture. It is its own step because these scenarios need the whole command surface, and because they are the evidence the leaf's closing agent quotes. It is the last subtask: its closing agent verifies the leaf's acceptance criteria and closes omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3.

It serves checkpoint criteria 10 (every exit site in the doctor dictionary; a hundred concurrent runs, none waiting; a check out of budget is never `ok`), 9 (bare `doctor` changes nothing outside `<state>/doctor/`; repeatable detectors) and 14 (identical bytes after the declared volatile keys), and G-M4-4, G-M4-5 and G-M4-6.

**What exists to build on:**

- T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs) provides `tests/common/tlog.rs`: `let log = tlog!();`, `log.step(label)`, `log.note(text)`, `log.json(label, &value)`, `log.run(&home, &argv) -> Ran` (the argv without `omaddons`, used verbatim: pass `--json` yourself), `log.cmd(&home, &argv).env(k, v).failpoints(spec).spawn()` and `Running::wait()`, `log.tree(label, root)`, `log.assert_unchanged(label, root)`, `log.case(name)`, and `Ran::{ok, exit, fails, aborted, envelope, error_code, warnings, commands, events, assert_private, stdout, stderr}` (`Ran::data()` requires a `data` key, which a doctor envelope does not have: use `envelope()`). A suite that uses the log carries the crate-doc marker `//! e2e suite: <purpose>`, which `argc e2e` and T1's convention test read.
- s1's `tests/common/doctor.rs::check_envelope(stdout, stderr, code)`: the doctor envelope's shape rules, shared with the contract harness.
- `tests/common/`: `Home` (`home.rs`, with its HTTP fixtures and `client`/`addons` paths), `TestEnv` (`env.rs`: `TZ=UTC`, every `OMADDONS_*` of the test process removed), `wtf::Wtf` (`WTF/` trees for `FAKEACCT` on `FakeRealm` as `FakeChar`), `privacy::assert_private`/`assert_private_all`, `trees::tree_hash` (modes and symlink targets included), `procfs::running_as_root`.
- Planting patterns for the 7 published failure modes exist in today's tests: a crashed install leaving a journal (`tests/contract/matrix.rs::status`, `engine.journal.prepared=abort`); a deleted client (`tests/status.rs:433-470`); a hand-edited addon (`tests/contract/recommendations.rs`'s `edited`); a degraded addon (`recommendations.rs`'s `degraded`, `:93`); a newer state file (`tests/fail_closed.rs`); a missing folder (`tests/drift_surfaces.rs`); an outdated widget (`tests/omarchy.rs`).
- M4-D47 (fixtures): each failure mode has a `Fixture` in `tests/doctor/fixtures/` with `corrupt`, `assert_healthy`, `subject` and a doc comment that is its README; `tests/doctor_harness.rs` (F9) runs every fixture through the safety-harness properties; a coverage test asserts every failure mode has a fixture. *Rejected:* shell `corrupt.sh`/`assert.sh`.

## Technical Approach

1. **`tests/common/doctor.rs`** gains `pub mod plant` (deterministic, on the common builders; each a doc comment saying what it breaks and what the finding's id, severity and evidence are):
   - `managed_files_modified(home, target, addon)`, `record_folder_missing(home, target, addon)`, `ownership_transferred(home, target)`, `target_vanished(home) -> String` (the vanished target's id), `state_version_newer(home, target)`, `widget_version_drift(home)`, `journal_pending(home, target)`;
   - each documents its order constraint: `journal_pending` last (any later change command would recover its journal first), `state_version_newer` after every change on that target (a newer record refuses changes);
   - `restore_file(home, target, addon, rel)` puts back a planted edit's original bytes (for `--since`);
   - `pub fn runs(home) -> Vec<String>` (the published run directory names, sorted) and `pub fn latest(home) -> Option<String>` (the `latest` link's target name).
   F1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1`), F3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.3`), F4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.4`), F5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.5`) and F9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`) reuse these helpers in their fixtures.
2. **`tests/doctor/mod.rs`** (new; included by test crates as `#[path = "doctor/mod.rs"] mod fixtures;`, decided while writing this bead: a plain `mod doctor;` inside `tests/doctor.rs` would match both `tests/doctor.rs` and `tests/doctor/mod.rs`, which Rust refuses):

   ```rust
   /// One failure mode, broken on purpose (M4-D47). The doc comment of each implementation is its README.
   pub trait Fixture {
       fn id(&self) -> &'static str;
       fn corrupt(&self, home: &Home);
       fn assert_healthy(&self, home: &Home);
       fn subject(&self, home: &Home) -> Vec<PathBuf>;
       fn fixer(&self) -> bool { false }
       /// Environment the diagnosing run needs (a failpoint, for a runtime row).
       fn run_env(&self) -> Vec<(String, String)> { Vec::new() }
       /// Arguments the diagnosing run needs (`--only`, `--budget`, for a runtime row).
       fn run_args(&self) -> Vec<String> { Vec::new() }
   }
   pub mod fixtures;   // tests/doctor/fixtures/mod.rs: one `pub mod` per fixture and `pub fn all() -> Vec<Box<dyn Fixture>>`
   ```

   Decided while writing this bead: the methods take `&Home` (whose `env` is the plan's `TestEnv`), because fixtures that install an addon need the HTTP fixtures `Home` serves; `run_env` and `run_args` (defaulted) exist for the two runtime rows, which no file on disk can trigger. Module files use the id in snake case (`fm_state_files_detector_crashed.rs`), since a module name cannot hold a hyphen.
3. **The two runtime fixtures:**
   - `fm_state_files_detector_crashed.rs`: `corrupt` registers one clean client and installs nothing; `run_env` = `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS=doctor.detector.panic=panic@1`; the finding: `fm-state_files-detector-crashed`, P1, evidence keys `detector` and `location`; `assert_healthy`: a run without the failpoint reports no such finding; `subject`: empty (no fixer).
   - `fm_state_files_check_incomplete.rs`: `corrupt` likewise; `run_args` = `--only <the cached row with the smallest declared cost_ms, read from omaddons::doctor::registry::FAILURE_MODES> --budget <max(1, its cost_ms)>ms`; `run_env` = `doctor.detector.panic=sleep:50`; the finding: `fm-state_files-check-incomplete`, P3, evidence `{detector, limit: "deadline", deadline_ms, max_entries: null}`; `assert_healthy`: the same run without the failpoint reports none.
4. **`tests/doctor.rs`** (new), first line `//! e2e suite: the doctor runtime: run directories, the doctor envelope and exit dictionary, budgets, isolation, --since and explain`. Every scenario below is a `TestLog` scenario (`let log = tlog!();`), runs commands only through `log.run`/`log.cmd` with `--json` passed explicitly, checks each doctor envelope with `common::doctor::check_envelope`, and works on its own `Home` (`Home::new(&["wow", "wow_classic"])` unless it says otherwise). `<state>` below is `home.env.state().join("omaddons")`.

   1. **`a_clean_home_is_healthy_and_leaves_one_run`** — steps: "home" (install one addon on retail through the HTTP fixtures; `log.tree` of `<state>` without `doctor/`, `<config>`, `<cache>`, each client dir); "diagnose" (`doctor --json --progress json`). Asserts: exit 0; `state: DONE_OK`, `view: full`, `doctor_contract_version: "1.0"`, `summary.total_findings: 0`, `findings: []`, `commands: []`, `next_steps: []`; exactly one directory in `<state>/doctor/runs/`, named `run_id`, holding exactly `report.json` and `runtime.jsonl`; `run_dir` is that absolute path; `latest` is a symlink to `runs/<run_id>`; modes 0700, 0400, 0400; `report.json` parses as the stdout envelope without `meta`, with `kind: "diagnose"` after `command`; `runtime.jsonl`'s ops in order (`create_dir`… `chmod` `rename_noreplace` `write_file` `symlink_atomic` `chmod` `chmod`), `seq` 1… consecutive, every `path` under `<state>/doctor/`; `log.assert_unchanged` on every tree recorded in "home"; no `net.log` line added.
   2. **`bare_doctor_is_doctor_diagnose`** — `doctor --json` and `doctor diagnose --json` both report `command: "doctor diagnose"`, and their envelopes are equal after stripping `meta`, `run_id`, `run_dir`, `started_at`, `finished_at` and `summary.duration_ms`.
   3. **`the_seven_published_findings_and_their_explain_commands`** — one case per published id (`log.case(<id>)`, each on a fresh home): plant it; `doctor --json` → exit 1, `DONE_FINDINGS`, the id present at its severity (P0 journal-pending, P0 state-version-newer, P1 record-folder-missing, P2 managed-files-modified, P2 ownership-transferred, P2 target-vanished, P3 widget-version-drift), its `instance` starting with the id; `next_steps == commands[].command`; every `commands[]` argv (each `doctor explain …`) run → exit 0 and its `instances` holds that finding's instance. Then one combined case with all seven planted on a home with enough clients (retail for the addon states, a second for the newer record, a third deleted for target-vanished, the widget, and the journal planted last): exit 1 with all seven ids, and every explain argv exits 0.
   4. **`a_panicking_detector_becomes_a_finding_and_the_run_completes`** — plant `managed_files_modified`; select two rows A and B with `--only` (the test reads their order from `FAILURE_MODES`); case `@2` (`doctor.detector.panic=panic@2`): B is a `detector-crashed` finding (P1, `evidence.detector == B`, `evidence.location` under `src/doctor/`), A's findings are present, exit 1, `report.json` written, `latest` updated; case `@1`: the mirror. In both, the payload text `failpoint doctor.detector.panic` appears in neither stdout, stderr, `report.json` nor `runtime.jsonl`.
   5. **`a_detector_past_its_deadline_is_incomplete_never_healthy`** — on a clean home, `doctor --json --only <cheapest cached row> --budget <its cost>ms` with `doctor.detector.panic=sleep:50`: exit 1, `DONE_FINDINGS` (never `DONE_OK`), `summary.incomplete: 1`, one `fm-state_files-check-incomplete` with `{detector: <row>, limit: deadline, deadline_ms: <budget>, max_entries: null}`, its remediation argv `doctor --only <row> --budget <10 × budget>ms`, which run (without the failpoint) exits 0; with `--severity P2` added, the finding is still there.
   6. **`an_over_budget_selection_refuses_before_starting`** — Σcost_ms of the default selection, read from `FAILURE_MODES` (asserted ≥ 2, so the case is meaningful); `doctor --json --budget <Σ − 1>ms` → exit 4, `doctor_refused`, `details {reason: over_budget, budget_ms, estimated_ms: Σ}`; no run directory and no `latest` created; its `fix_argv` run → exit 0 or 1.
   7. **`a_hundred_concurrent_runs_get_a_hundred_run_ids_under_a_frozen_clock`** — 100 `log.cmd(&home, ["doctor", "--json"]).env("OMADDONS_NOW", "2026-10-30T18:02:11Z").spawn()`, then wait for all. Asserts: 100 exits 0; 100 distinct `run_id`s, each `2026-10-30T18-02-11Z__<ULID>`; 100 directories in `runs/`, each with `report.json`; every `started_at` equal to the frozen time; the batch's wall time under 60 s (a design that waited for the clock to advance could not finish under a frozen clock, and one that waited a second per collision would need about 100 s); `latest` resolves to one of the 100 (which one is not asserted: two runs finishing in the same instant may race, by design). Each run is logged as a case (`run-<n>`) with its `run_id` and `elapsed_ms`.
   8. **`since_reports_new_resolved_and_unchanged_instances`** — plant `managed_files_modified` for two addons on retail; `doctor --json` (run A, two instances); `plant::restore_file` for one; `doctor --json --since <A>` → `since: {run: A, new: [], resolved: [<restored instance>], unchanged: 1}`; `doctor --json --since latest` → `since.run` is the run `latest` named before this run; `doctor --json --since 2026-01-01T00-00-00Z__01M8R000000000000000000000` → exit 66, `not_found`, `fix_argv` naming the newest run and alternatives the next ones; crash a run at `doctor.run.published=abort` and `--since <that id>` → exit 66 with "interrupted" in the message.
   9. **`a_crash_while_staging_or_after_publishing_leaves_no_report`** — case `staged`: `doctor --json` with `doctor.run.staged=abort` → `Ran::aborted()`; `runs/` holds one `.<id>.tmp` directory (0700, its `runtime.jsonl` naming the stage's creation) and no run; `latest` absent; `status --json` exits 0 and `log.assert_unchanged` on `<state>` without `doctor/`; a following `doctor --json` → exit 0, exactly one published run, the leftover stage still present and never listed by `plant::runs` or offered by `--since`'s alternatives. Case `published`: with `doctor.run.published=abort`, a published run with `runtime.jsonl` and no `report.json`; `latest` unchanged; the next `doctor` works.
   10. **`an_unwritable_runs_directory_exits_73`** — skipped as root (`procfs::running_as_root()`, saying so in the log). Create `<state>/doctor/runs/` and chmod it 0500; `doctor --json` → exit 73, `error.code: io`, `details.path` under `<state>/doctor/`; no report keys in the envelope; `<state>` otherwise unchanged; restore the mode afterwards.
   11. **`a_panic_in_the_doctor_tree_exits_74`** — `doctor --json` with `cli.panic=error` → exit 74, `error.code: internal`, `exit_code: 74`, one stderr `error` event; with `cli.panic=panic` → exit 74, one envelope, `internal`; and the control: `status --json` with `cli.panic=panic` still exits 1 (the general dictionary is unchanged).
   12. **`every_doctor_exit_site_uses_the_doctor_dictionary`** — a table, one `log.case` per row, each row `(name, argv, setup, exit, code)`, each checked with `check_envelope` and `Ran::fails(exit, code)`:

       | Row | Argv | Setup | Exit | Code |
       |---|---|---|---|---|
       | clean | `doctor` | — | 0 | — |
       | findings | `doctor` | `managed_files_modified` | 1 | — |
       | over budget | `doctor --budget <Σ − 1>ms` | — | 4 | `doctor_refused` |
       | newer report | `doctor --since <run>` | that run's `report.json` made writable, then rewritten with `schema_version: "2.0"` | 4 | `state_too_new` |
       | clap flag | `doctor --bogus` | — | 64 | `usage` |
       | the `--fix` hint | `doctor --fix` | — | 64 | `usage` |
       | unknown id | `doctor --only fm-nope` | — | 64 | `usage` |
       | bad actor | `doctor --actor robot` | — | 64 | `usage` |
       | `--if-match` | `doctor --if-match pc1:<64 hex>` | — | 64 | `usage` |
       | online and offline | `doctor --online --offline` | — | 64 | `usage` |
       | explain unknown | `doctor explain fm-nope` | — | 64 | `usage` |
       | unknown target | `doctor -t nosuch` | — | 66 | `target_not_found` |
       | unknown run | `doctor --since <unknown id>` | — | 66 | `not_found` |
       | explain unknown target | `doctor explain fm-userland_state-target-vanished -t nosuch` | — | 66 | `target_not_found` |
       | cannot create | `doctor` | runs dir 0500 (not as root) | 73 | `io` |
       | failpoint error | `doctor` | `cli.panic=error` | 74 | `internal` |
       | panic | `doctor` | `cli.panic=panic` | 74 | `internal` |
       | explain panic | `doctor explain <cached row>` | `doctor.detector.panic=panic` | 74 | `internal` |
       | corrupt report | `doctor --since <run>` | that run's `report.json` made writable, then replaced by `{` | 74 | `state_corrupt` |

       Exit 6 (`online_required`) has no end-to-end row until F7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.7`) adds an online failure mode (s5's unit case covers it); the row is added then. Every exit seen is declared in the path's `COMMANDS.exits`.
   13. **`explain_answers_by_id_by_instance_and_by_target_and_writes_nothing`** — plant `managed_files_modified` for two addons on retail and one on the second client; `log.tree` of the whole `<state>` (`doctor/` included) and of `net.log`; `doctor explain fm-external_artifacts-managed-files-modified --json` → three instances; `-t retail` → two; by the instance key of one → exactly it; a vanished instance (restore it, then explain its key) → `instances: []`, exit 0; `doctor explain fm-external_artifacts-managed-files-modifed` → 64, `fix_argv` with the corrected id; `doctor explain fm-state_files-check-incomplete` → `tier: runtime`, `instances: []`. After all of them, `log.assert_unchanged` on `<state>` and `net.log` (explain wrote nothing and created no run directory).
   14. **`a_diagnose_changes_nothing_outside_its_run_directory`** — a home with retail holding an installed addon and a `Wtf::at(retail).saved_variables("Foo", 64).build()` tree (`FAKEACCT`/`FakeRealm`/`FakeChar`), plus `managed_files_modified`; trees of `<state>` without `doctor/`, `<config>`, `<cache>` and both client dirs; `doctor --json --progress json` and `doctor -v --progress json` (human): `log.assert_unchanged` on every tree; `Ran::assert_private()` for both runs; `common::privacy::assert_private` over `report.json` and `runtime.jsonl`.
   15. **`two_diagnoses_of_one_state_give_identical_findings`** — plant `managed_files_modified` and `target_vanished`; run `doctor --json` twice; the two `findings` arrays are equal, and the two envelopes are byte-equal after stripping `meta` and the five declared volatile keys (and nothing else).
   16. **`runtime_fixtures_produce_their_findings`** — for each fixture of `fixtures::all()` that is a runtime row: `corrupt`, then `doctor --json` with its `run_args` and `run_env` → exit 1 and the fixture's id present with its severity and evidence keys; then `assert_healthy`.

**What not to do:** add a `--budget` or a failpoint to a scenario that asserts a clean result, to hide a slow detector (fix the detector or the scale instead); share one home between scenarios; read a doctor envelope with `Ran::data()`; write under a real `HOME`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every scenario of item 4 passes in the gate, and `argc e2e doctor` runs the suite with verbose logs.
- [ ] The exit-site table covers 0, 1, 4, 64, 66, 73 and 74 through the real binary (73 skipped as root, saying so), each with the doctor envelope's shape and the code shown; every exit seen is declared.
- [ ] A hundred concurrent runs under a frozen clock give a hundred distinct run ids within 60 s.
- [ ] Crashes at `doctor.run.staged` and `doctor.run.published` leave no report, never move `latest`, and never block the next run.
- [ ] A diagnose changes nothing outside `<state>/doctor/`, adds no `net.log` line, and names no account, realm or character on any channel or in its record files; `explain` writes nothing at all.
- [ ] `tests/doctor/mod.rs` defines `Fixture`, `tests/doctor/fixtures/` holds the two runtime fixtures, and each produces its finding.
- [ ] `tests/common/doctor.rs::plant` covers the 7 published failure modes, each documented.
- [ ] The closing agent of this subtask verifies every acceptance criterion of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3 with evidence (test names, the commit, `argc e2e doctor`'s summary and log root), and closes omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3 with the close comment its body asks for.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files; `br lint` is clean.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

None new in `src/`; the scenarios above are the tests. `tests/common/doctor.rs`'s planting helpers get one self-check each inside `tests/doctor.rs`'s per-state cases (the planted state is the one the finding names).

### Integration and end-to-end tests

The sixteen scenarios of item 4, in `tests/doctor.rs`, with the shared fixtures in `tests/doctor/`. Failpoints used: `doctor.run.staged=abort`, `doctor.run.published=abort`, `doctor.detector.panic=panic[@N]`, `doctor.detector.panic=sleep:50`, `cli.panic=error`, `cli.panic=panic`, and the planting helpers' `engine.journal.prepared=abort`.

### Logging

- Every scenario opens `let log = tlog!();` and names its phases with `log.step`: "home", "plant", "diagnose", "explain each command", "restore one", "since", "crash", "recover", "check trees".
- Every command goes through `log.run`/`log.cmd`, so its argv, environment overrides (failpoints, `OMADDONS_NOW`), exit, envelope, stderr events and `net.log` lines are in `steps.jsonl` and `transcript.md`. Envelopes the test inspects beyond `Ran`'s helpers are recorded with `log.json("report", …)`; the run directory's listing (names and modes) and `runtime.jsonl`'s lines are recorded with `log.json` before they are asserted.
- Trees: `state-outside-doctor` (`<state>` with `doctor/` excluded), `config`, `cache`, each client dir by its folder name, and `state-all` where explain's write-nothing is asserted; purity is `log.assert_unchanged`, which logs the first differing paths.
- Table-driven scenarios (the seven findings, the exit sites, the hundred runs) log one `log.case(<name>)` per row, so a failing row's transcript stands alone.
- On a failure, the guard of T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`) prints `test log: <path>` and the last 20 steps; `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG=verbose argc e2e doctor` echoes every step live.

## Considerations

- **Runtime and flakiness:** the suite runs about a hundred and fifty commands; the concurrency scenario dominates. Keep homes small (one or two clients) except where a scenario needs more. A scenario that flakes on a deadline is a defect in the detector's charging or in s3's debug scale, never fixed by loosening the scenario.
- **Root:** chmod-based cases (73, unreadable directories) skip as root with a logged reason, as `tests/contract/matrix.rs::status_running_unknown` does.
- **What later leaves reuse:** `plant::*` and the `Fixture` trait are the start of M4-D47's `tests/doctor/`; F1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1`), F3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.3`), F4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.4`), F5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.5`) and F9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`) add their fixtures beside these two and extend the trait only additively. F1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1`) adds the end-to-end case of `--since` with two stuck journals on one client once its detectors emit one finding per journal; F10 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.10`) the two-skill-roots case.
- **T4** (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4`, slice 3 end to end) calls these scenarios' helpers rather than re-implementing them.
- **Privacy:** the only `WTF/` trees here use the fake names; the scenario asserts them absent everywhere.

## Dependencies

- Parent: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3.
- Before it: s6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3.6`: `doctor explain`, whose argv every report carries), and through it s1–s5.
- T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs and the `argc e2e` runner) blocks this part (filed edge).
- After it: nothing in this leaf; its closure unblocks E4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4`), E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`), E8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.8`), F1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1`), F3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.3`), F4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.4`), F5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.5`), A6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.6`) and T4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4`).

title: `doctor health`, `ls`, `--robot-triage`, `capabilities` and `robot-docs`
description:
## How to work this bead

This bead is worked through its 5 subtasks, listed below in work order. Claim a subtask, not this bead (`br ready --parent omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4` lists the ready ones). The agent that closes the last open subtask then verifies every acceptance criterion of this bead (they are the leaf's, not any one subtask's), and closes this bead with `br close omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4 --reason "done: <evidence> · found: <ids>"`. Until this bead is closed, every bead it blocks stays blocked.

1. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4.1 `omaddons doctor health`: the one-line summary of the cheap checks, with no run directory. The status word and its precedence, the last run, the one-line human form, and every DEC-1 touch point of the path.
2. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4.2 `omaddons doctor ls`: the run directories newest first, with kinds, states and aborted runs. Bounded listing, `ABORTED` runs, `truncated`, and every DEC-1 touch point of the path.
3. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4.3 `omaddons doctor capabilities` and `omaddons doctor robot-docs`: the doctor's generated description and its handbook. Generated from the registry and the scope table, rendered by the guide renderer, with every DEC-1 touch point of both paths. After s1 and s2.
4. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4.4 `omaddons doctor --robot-triage`: the triage view, with the planner's actions and the command to run next. The `triage` view of `doctor diagnose` and the handbook's agent loop. After s3.
5. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4.5 E2E: the doctor's read surface end to end, its perf budgets and its intent-corpus rows. `tests/doctor.rs` with T1's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`) `TestLog`, the two perf budgets in `tests/perf.rs`, and the corpus rows. After s4.

s1 and s2 touch different modules and do not depend on each other's code, so they can be worked at the same time; both add rows to the same registry tables (`COMMANDS`, `CLI_PATHS`, the matrix, `special.rs`, `cli_skeleton`), so the second to land rebases. s3 waits for both because the handbook's examples run `doctor health` and `doctor ls`, and a test parses every command the handbook shows. s4 waits for s3 because the triage view names `omaddons doctor capabilities --json` and `omaddons doctor robot-docs`, which must be real commands, and adds its section to the handbook s3 creates. s5 tests all four.

**Size M, five subtasks, one closure.** The five surfaces are each small, but each is a command path (or, for `--robot-triage`, a report view) with its own registry touch points and contract rows, so each lands in its own commit that passes the gate. The leaf closes once, when all five are done, so no bead it blocks ever sees half of the surface.

## Background

**What this leaf is.** E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, `doctor diagnose` and `explain`) builds the doctor's read side: the `doctor` command tree, the run directories, the doctor envelope and its exit dictionary. E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`, `doctor fix`) builds its repair side and the fix planner. This leaf adds the rest of the doctor contract's read-only surface, the verbs that make the doctor usable by scripts and agents without reading a full diagnosis:

- `omaddons doctor health`: one line whose first word a script dispatches on (`ok`, `findings`, `unsafe`, `concurrency`), from the cheap checks run live, writing nothing and creating no run directory;
- `omaddons doctor ls`: the run directories, newest first, with each run's kind (`diagnose`, `fix`, `undo`) and state;
- `omaddons doctor --robot-triage`: one call that returns the findings, the repairs `doctor fix` would make, and the exact command to run next;
- `omaddons doctor capabilities`: the doctor's machine-readable description, generated from the failure-mode registry and the write-scope table, never hand-kept;
- `omaddons doctor robot-docs`: the doctor's handbook for agents, rendered by the guide's renderer, with its exit codes, examples and the list of things it will never do.

**Milestone goals it serves:**

- **G-M4-1 (self-describing):** "An agent with no prior knowledge learns everything it needs from the binary itself … Every fact in those outputs is generated from the code, so it cannot drift from what the code does." `doctor capabilities` and `doctor robot-docs` are the doctor's part of that promise.
- **G-M4-4 (diagnosable and repairable):** "A check that ran out of budget or entries says so: incomplete coverage is never reported as healthy." `health` is never `ok` with a `check-incomplete` finding, and `--robot-triage` tells an agent which repair is safe to run.
- **G-M4-5 (frozen and enforced):** "Every exit site maps to a published code in the right dictionary. Repeated runs print identical bytes." Every path here uses the doctor dictionary and is deterministic.
- **G-M4-6 (no new risk to the engine's guarantees):** none of these verbs writes, except `--robot-triage`'s own run directory (it is a diagnose, M4-D33); none takes the global lock.

**Checkpoint criteria it is responsible for** (§3.2; H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the checkpoint) records them):

- **10, the surface items of these verbs:** "Every verb and flag of §6.11 exists and is listed by `doctor capabilities --json`. That output is generated from the registry and carries all eleven doctor exit codes by name, the write scopes, the allowed ops, every detector, every fixer and every manual remediation." "`doctor robot-docs` contains the literal strings `EXIT CODES`, `capabilities` and `NEVER do`." "`doctor health` prints one line whose first token is `ok`, `findings`, `unsafe` or `concurrency`, in under 200 ms; each `quick` detector takes under 5 ms (release build, on the bench home)." "Every exit site in the doctor tree maps to the doctor dictionary." "A check that runs out of its budget or its entry limit yields a `check-incomplete` finding, so the run is never `ok`" (here: `health`'s first token is never `ok` for it).
- **5 (intent inference), the doctor-verb rows of these verbs:** typos of `health`, `capabilities`, `robot-docs`, `--robot-triage` and a bad `--limit` yield usage errors whose `fix_argv` runs to its declared exit.
- **14 (frozen), in part:** each path has a success and a failure row in the contract matrix (H3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3`) audits the coverage) and prints identical bytes on a repeat.
- **9 (the safety harness), in part:** these verbs change nothing (tree hashes), and `--robot-triage` changes nothing outside `<state>/doctor/`.

**The decisions that shape it** (full text in the decision log comments on the milestone epic `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`):

- **M4-D2: one contract registry feeds every description of the CLI.** `capabilities`, `robot-docs`, the wire-name golden, bare help's discovery line and `doctor capabilities` all read the registries: the live clap tree, `app::COMMANDS`, the error, warning and exit registries, the action, event and env-var registries, the limits, and the doctor's failure-mode registry. A fact clap cannot provide is declared once, beside what it describes, and a test cross-checks it. *Why:* the rule "generated from the live clap tree and the registries, never maintained by hand" works only if the registries exist, and one registry means the descriptions cannot disagree. *Rejected:* a hand-written capabilities file (it drifts, the exact failure capabilities exists to prevent); deriving every fact from observed behaviour (a command's exits are a promise and need a declaration); proc-macro attributes (a dependency and compile time for no gain). Here: `doctor capabilities` is computed from the effective failure-mode registry, `doctor::Exit::ALL`, A2's env-var registry, `app::COMMANDS` with the clap tree, and the fsx scope table; the handbook's tables come from the guide renderer's generated blocks. The one hand list is `ALLOWED_OPS`, tied to the primitive types by a test.
- **M4-D3: the envelope's `schema_version` is the contract version.** The doctor surface also carries `doctor_contract_version` ("1.0"), the revision of the external doctor contract whose shapes it implements, which changes only when omaddons adopts a new revision of that contract; omaddons' own wire names follow `schema_version`'s bump rule; the crate version (`tool_version`) is independent of both. *Rejected:* a separate `contract_version` that moves on its own (confusing); a `doctor_version` (there is none). `health`'s line prints it as `doctor=1.0`; `doctor capabilities` carries it as a key.
- **M4-D34: doctor JSON puts the report at the top level, with the general envelope keys around it.** Every verb of the doctor tree emits `{ok, schema_version, tool_version, command, exit_code, <report keys>, error?, warnings, commands, meta}`. `ok` is `exit_code == 0`; `error` is present only for exits 4, 5, 6, 64, 66, 73 and 74; findings (1), a partial fix (2) and a rolled-back fix (3) are reports, not errors; there is no `data` key; the schema registry's `data` schema of a doctor path is its report schema. *Why:* vision §5.8, and generic doctor consumers read `.state`, `.summary` and `.findings` at the top level. *Rejected:* nesting the report under `data` (it breaks the doctor contract's consumers). Consequence here: a report key may not reuse an envelope key name (`tool_version`, `command`, `commands`, `warnings`).
- **Decisions it obeys:**
  - **M4-D29:** one detector registry serves `doctor`, `doctor health` and `status`, by tier: `status --cached` runs `cached`; `status`, `doctor --quick` and `doctor health` run `cached` and `quick`; bare `doctor` every tier but `deep`; `doctor --include-deep` every tier. *Rejected:* `status` calling `doctor` as a subprocess; two implementations of each check.
  - **M4-D33:** `doctor`, `doctor diagnose`, `doctor --quick`, `doctor --robot-triage` and `doctor fix` each create a run directory, and so does every undo of a repair; `health`, `ls`, `explain`, `diff`, `gc`, `capabilities` and `robot-docs` do not, and `health` reports the last run it finds. *Why:* `health` exists to be cheap and frequent. *Rejected:* a run directory for `health` (it would grow without bound under a widget or a cron job). The run id is the UTC start time, `__`, and a fresh ULID.
  - **M4-D40:** the doctor dictionary is `0 healthy`, `1 findings_present`, `2 fix_partial`, `3 fix_failed_rolled_back`, `4 refused_unsafe`, `5 concurrency_lost`, `6 online_required`, `64 usage_error`, `66 no_input`, `73 cannot_create`, `74 io_error`, with the total `exit_for(ErrorCode)`; `capabilities` publishes the mapping. *Rejected:* reusing the general dictionary in the doctor tree ("findings present" is a normal outcome there).
  - **M4-D43:** the doctor loads the world tolerantly; a failed layer is a finding and an unavailable layer; a detector cut short by its deadline or `DOCTOR_SCAN_MAX_ENTRIES` returns an `incomplete` record that becomes a `fm-state_files-check-incomplete` finding (P3), "so a run with incomplete coverage is never `DONE_OK`, and `health`'s first token is never `ok` for it". *Rejected:* treating truncation as a warning on a healthy run.
  - **M4-D30:** a finding's `instance` is `<fm-id>@<target key | machine>[:<discriminator>]`; findings are compared by instance, never by `label`.
  - **M4-D31, M4-D46:** a repair is one transaction of kind `repair`, undone by `omaddons undo` or `doctor undo` as a new repair transaction whose run directory is of kind `undo`; `doctor ls` reports `undo_complete` and `reverted_run`.
  - **M4-D44, M4-D38:** `doctor fix` binds with `--if-match`; a set-aside repair needs `--force --yes` and is never part of a default fix; the widget never runs a forced repair. The triage therefore never recommends one.
  - **M4-D11:** recommendation actions are a closed registry (`apply`, `install_skill`, `doctor_fix`, `doctor_explain`, `doctor_gc`, and the earlier ones).
  - **M4-D18:** keys that change between identical runs are declared in `contract::VOLATILE`; maps are `BTreeMap`; no `HashMap`/`HashSet` in a serialized type.
  - **M4-D55:** the six naming rules (an instant ends `_at` and a duration `_ms`/`_s`; null rather than omitted; snake case, plural arrays, counts as bare nouns; closed snake-case enums; the envelope `command` equals the clap path; typed `details`) hold from slice 1 and are checked by A3's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`) rule test; a new shape never goes on `tests/contract/rules_allowlist.txt`.
  - **M4-D7:** the guide's renderer splices generated, fixed-width blocks into a hand-written template; it holds the shared `NEVER` table, which `doctor robot-docs` uses too.
  - **M4-D5:** each path declares its exits beside the command in `COMMANDS`, and the contract suite verifies every observed exit against them.

**How it serves the vision.** G7: "`doctor` follows the world-class doctor contract": `health`, `ls`, `--robot-triage`, `capabilities` and `robot-docs` are that contract's verbs, with its shapes. G4: "the first command an agent guesses works": an agent's whole doctor loop is `omaddons doctor --robot-triage --json`, then the `recommended_argv` it returns; `doctor capabilities` and `doctor robot-docs` answer "what can this doctor do?" without README. The thesis that omaddons stays the sole, safe, undoable authority over what it manages: every verb here only reads, and the triage never recommends a forced repair.
