## Technical Approach

### 1. The surface and its registry rows

```text
omaddons doctor health
omaddons doctor ls [--limit N]
omaddons doctor capabilities
omaddons doctor robot-docs
omaddons doctor [diagnose] --robot-triage   [diagnose's selection flags; not with --since]
```

- **clap** (`src/app/doctor.rs`, beside E3's and E6's variants): `DoctorAction::Health`, `DoctorAction::Ls(LsArgs)`, `DoctorAction::Capabilities` and `DoctorAction::RobotDocs` (clap names `health`, `ls`, `capabilities`, `robot-docs`). `LsArgs { #[arg(long, value_name = "N")] limit: Option<usize> }`. Their `about` lines (the variants' doc comments, shown by `help doctor`, the guide's command list, the handbook's surface and `verbs`): "One line for scripts: ok, findings, unsafe or concurrency (the quick checks; no run record)", "List the doctor's runs, newest first", "What this doctor checks and repairs, as JSON for agents", "The doctor's handbook for agents, as Markdown". `--robot-triage` is a flag of E3's `DiagnoseArgs`: `#[arg(long, conflicts_with = "since")] robot_triage: bool`, about "One call for agents: the findings, the repairs doctor fix would make, and the command to run next". `doctor fix` takes no `--robot-triage`.
- **Global flags** work as everywhere: `--json`, `--robot`, `-v`, `--quiet`, `--no-color`, `--no-progress`, `--progress`. `--dry-run`, `--reason` and `--actor` are accepted and change nothing (the read-only test checks it). `--if-match` is refused by `check_if_match` (none of these paths binds), exit 64. `-t` narrows `health`'s target-scoped checks exactly as it narrows a diagnose (E2's `Selection`); `ls`, `capabilities` and `robot-docs` belong to no client and do not resolve `-t` (decided while writing this bead: a run, the doctor's description and its handbook are machine-wide, and other target-less commands ignore `-t` the same way).
- **Registry rows** (A1's fields, through `entry(…).doctor()`; each path's own subtask adds its row, after the doctor rows E3 and E6 placed at the end of the Look group):

  | Path | Group | Mutates | Dictionary | Exits | Data (report) | Stores plan | Network |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | `doctor health` | Look | no | Doctor | 0, 1, 64, 66, 74 | `HealthReport` | no | None |
  | `doctor ls` | Look | no | Doctor | 0, 64, 74 | `LsReport` | no | None |
  | `doctor capabilities` | Look | no | Doctor | 0, 64, 74 | `DoctorCapabilities` | no | None |
  | `doctor robot-docs` | Look | no | Doctor | 0, 64, 74 | B1's `GuideData` | no | None |

  66 is `health -t <unknown>` (`target_not_found`, through `exit_for`). The rows `doctor` and `doctor diagnose` keep E3's exits and data; `--robot-triage` adds neither (its report is the `triage` variant of the same `DiagnoseReport`).
- **`command_name` and dispatch arms:** `Some(DoctorAction::Health) => "doctor health"`, `Ls(_) => "doctor ls"`, `Capabilities => "doctor capabilities"`, `RobotDocs => "doctor robot-docs"`; each dispatch arm calls its `run` and emits through E3's `emit_doctor`.
- **The help layout:** no change to bare help (the paths are nested under `doctor`, which E3 placed in the Look line); `omaddons help doctor` lists them through clap; `help_walks_a_nested_path` gains each path's literal.
- **`CLI_PATHS`** rows in `omarchy/Model.js`: `"doctor health"`, `"doctor ls"`, `"doctor capabilities"`, `"doctor robot-docs"`, each `{ "mutates": false, "destructive": false, "binds": false }`.
- Every report derives `Serialize + JsonSchema`, uses `BTreeMap` for maps, is its `COMMANDS` row's `data`, and is validated live by A3's strict validation through E3's doctor mode (whichever of A3 and this leaf lands second wires the check).

### 2. `doctor health` (s1)

`src/doctor/health.rs` (new), `src/doctor/runtime.rs` (the shared detection loop) and the wiring in `src/app/doctor.rs`.

1. **Selection.** Exactly `doctor --quick`'s: build `DiagnoseArgs { quick: true, ..Default::default() }` and call E3's `plan_diagnose(failure_modes(), &args)` with the global `-t`, so the rows (`cached` and `quick` tiers, never a runtime row, never an online row by E1's invariant) and the `-t` narrowing cannot differ from `doctor --quick`'s by construction (M4-D29). An unknown `-t` is E3's `target_not_found` (66), raised before anything is read.
2. **Detection, with no run directory.** `DoctorView::load(ctx, &selection)` (E2), then the same detection loop E3's DIAGNOSING runs: every selected row in registry order, its view layers forced first, its `Budget::for_tier(tier)`, the failpoint `doctor.detector.panic`, the call inside `catch_unwind`, a panic turned into `fm-state_files-detector-crashed`, a cut-short turned into `fm-state_files-check-incomplete`, then E2's `target_skips` and `visible_failures` and the merge, exactly as diagnose does. Decided while writing this bead: if E3's loop lives only inside `Runtime::diagnose(&mut self, …)`, move it into `pub(crate) fn detect(registry: &[FailureMode], view: &DoctorView, selection: &Selection, budgets: &Budgets) -> Detection` in `src/doctor/runtime.rs` and make `Runtime::diagnose` call it, with no change to diagnose's behaviour (its tests pass unchanged); `health` calls `detect` and never `Runtime::start`. `Detection` also holds each detector's elapsed time (`Vec<(&'static str, Duration)>`, in run order), which `health` logs at debug level, one line each, `check <fm id>: <n> us` (shown under `-v`; decided while writing this bead: the per-detector perf budget needs a measurement of the release binary, and a debug log line is no wire name).
3. **The lock.** `view.lock()` (E2's Lock layer over `fsx::lock::probe_global`): `Some(LockState::Held { .. })` means another process holds the global lock right now (`health` never acquires it, so a held lock is never its own); `Some(Free)` and `Some(Missing)` are free; `None` (the probe failed) is not `concurrency`, and E2 turns that failure into a machine `fm-schemas-state-corrupt` finding (P0), which `visible_failures` reports because the failure makes `journal-pending` (which requires the Lock layer) skip. So an unreadable lock file reads `unsafe`, never `ok` (§8.1 rule 6, fail closed). The holder's identity is not printed (decided while writing this bead: `status` and `doctor` show it; the one-liner stays one line).
4. **The status word** (the plan fixes the four meanings; the precedence was decided while writing this bead):
   1. `unsafe`: at least one P0 finding;
   2. `concurrency`: no P0, and the lock is held by another process;
   3. `findings`: at least one finding of any severity, `check-incomplete` and `detector-crashed` included (M4-D43: incomplete coverage is never `ok`);
   4. `ok`: no finding at all and the lock free.

   *Why this order:* a P0 state (a stuck journal, newer state, a corrupt state file, an unwritable state directory) is persistent and the most urgent thing to tell a script, and the journal detectors already ignore a transaction whose writer is alive (E2: `journal-pending` reports none while the lock is held), so a P0 seen during another process's commit is real; a held lock lasts milliseconds (vision D24) and only tells a script to look again; any finding, a cut-short check included, means "look". A check skipped because a layer failed never makes `health` `ok`, because E2 reports the failure that caused the skip.
5. **The last run.** Read `paths.doctor_latest()` with `std::fs::read_link`: it is accepted only when the target is exactly `runs/<name>` with `<name>` parsing as a `DoctorRunId` and `paths.doctor_run(&id)` a directory (`symlink_metadata`, never followed elsewhere). Then `run_id` is that id and `last_run` its start time, taken from the id's timestamp prefix (whole seconds, UTC; `DoctorRunId::started_at() -> Timestamp`, added here if E3 has none). Anything else (missing, dangling, a regular file, a target outside `runs/`, a name that is not a run id) gives `null` for both. No `report.json` is read: one `readlink` and one `stat` keep `health` cheap.
6. **The report** (`HealthReport`, A.7, in this key order):

   ```json
   {"ok":false,"schema_version":"1.0","tool_version":"0.1.0","command":"doctor health","exit_code":1,
    "status":"findings","findings":2,"by_severity":{"P0":0,"P1":0,"P2":1,"P3":1},
    "last_run":"2026-10-30T18:02:11Z","run_id":"2026-10-30T18-02-11Z__01M8R…",
    "warnings":[],"commands":[],"meta":{"elapsed_ms":38,"offline":false}}
   ```

   `status` is the closed enum `HealthStatus { Ok, Findings, Unsafe, Concurrency }` (snake case); `findings` is the total count (runtime rows included); `by_severity` is E3's `BySeverity`; `last_run` RFC 3339 UTC or `null`; `run_id` or `null`. `warnings` carries what the view reported (E2's warnings), as diagnose does. `commands` is `[]` (decided while writing this bead: the next step after a non-`ok` line is a diagnose, for which M4-D11's closed action set has no action).
7. **Exit codes** (decided while writing this bead; the plan is silent): `ok` → 0 (`healthy`); `findings`, `unsafe` and `concurrency` → 1 (`findings_present`), a report with no `error`. *Why:* `ok` is the only state in which a script may go on without looking, and the first token is the contract's dispatch mechanism. *Rejected:* the doctor contract's 4 for `unsafe` and 5 for `concurrency`: M4-D34 reserves 4 and 5 for runs that carry an `error` (`refused_unsafe` is a refusal, `concurrency_lost` a lock timeout), and `health` neither refuses nor waits for the lock; an `error`-less exit 4 would break the envelope rule E3's doctor mode checks. The close comment records this as a departure from the doctor contract for H5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.5`, the vision comments).
8. **The human form**, exactly one line and a newline:

   ```text
   findings  omaddons=0.1.0 doctor=1.0 findings=2 P2=1 P3=1 last_run=2026-10-30T18:02:11Z run_id=2026-10-30T18-02-11Z__01M8R…
   ok  omaddons=0.1.0 doctor=1.0 findings=0 last_run=none run_id=none
   ```

   The status word, two spaces, then `omaddons=<tool_version> doctor=<doctor_contract_version> findings=<n>`, then each non-zero severity as ` P<k>=<n>` in P0–P3 order, then ` last_run=<time | none> run_id=<id | none>`. No colour, no tab. Under `--json` the envelope replaces the line.
9. **What it never does:** create a run directory (or `<state>` itself on a fresh home), write any file, take the lock, recover a journal, make a request, read `WTF/`, or read a report.

### 3. `doctor ls` (s2)

`src/doctor/runs.rs` (shared with E8, see below) and the wiring in `src/app/doctor.rs`.

1. **`--limit`:** default `DEFAULT_LIMIT = 20`, a module constant beside the command as in `history.rs:26-27` (decided while writing this bead: a presentation default, not a safety limit, so not a `limits.rs` row; §7.9 adds none). `--limit 0` is `usage` "--limit must be at least 1", `fix_argv` `["omaddons", "doctor", "ls", "--limit", "20"]`, exit 64. A non-number is clap's usage error.
2. **The listing, newest first and bounded.** `<state>/doctor/runs/` is listed through E3's bounded walker with an entries-only budget of `DOCTOR_SCAN_MAX_ENTRIES` (20,000; `Budget::entries_only(max)`, added by whichever of E4 and E8 needs it first) in **descending** name order: add an order parameter to E3's one-level lister (`list_dir_in(dir, budget, Order::Descending)`; `list_dir` stays ascending for every other caller). Run names sort by start time, so a bound keeps the newest. Decided while writing this bead: with ascending order a home past the bound would list its oldest runs. A missing runs directory is an empty listing (exit 0); an unreadable one is `io` (exit 74, `details.path`). Only directories whose names parse as `DoctorRunId` are runs: staged `.<id>.tmp` names, `latest`, other names, and symlinks or files named like a run are skipped, never followed.
3. **`src/doctor/runs.rs` with E8.** E8's bead plans the same module (`RunEntry`, `RunListing { runs, complete }`, `list_runs(paths, budget)` ascending, `read_summary(dir) -> Option<RunSummary>`, `has_actions_log(dir)`). Decided while writing this bead: whichever of E4 and E8 lands first creates the module with E8's names and semantics; this leaf adds `list_runs_in(paths, budget, Order)` (with `list_runs` the ascending form) and extends `RunSummary` with the fields `ls` needs (`exit_code`, `view`, `summary_ok`, `actions_taken`, `reverted_run`), keeping every field E8 defined.
4. **`truncated`** (additive; decided while writing this bead: common rule 15 requires a cut listing to say so, and `history` has the same key): true when more runs exist than `--limit` shows, or when the listing stopped at its bound.
5. **Each listed run** (at most `--limit` of them) is read in this order:
   1. `<run>/report.json`, read with at most `API_RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES` bytes (64 MiB, E3's bound for reading a report) and decoded into a tolerant record that ignores unknown keys: `{schema_version, kind, exit_code, view?, state?, summary?: {ok?, actions_taken?}, tx?, undo_tx?, reverted_run?, actions_taken?}`. A missing file, an unreadable or oversized one, one that does not decode, a newer major `schema_version`, or a `state` value this build does not know all count as **no readable terminal report** (decided while writing this bead, matching E8's reading of the same directories, and failing closed: `ls` never vouches that a run finished when it cannot read the record).
   2. **With a readable terminal report:** `kind` from it; `state` from its `state`, or, for a triage report (`view: "triage"`, which has no `state`, A.6), `DONE_OK` when `summary.ok` is true and `DONE_FINDINGS` otherwise; `exit_code` from it; `action_count` from `summary.actions_taken` (fix), `actions_taken` (undo) or 0 (diagnose); `tx` = the transaction the run itself committed: a fix report's `tx` (`null` for a dry run), an undo report's `undo_tx`, else `null`; `reverted_run` from an undo report, else `null`.
   3. **Without one:** `state: "ABORTED"`; `exit_code: null` (decided while writing this bead: a killed run has no exit code); `kind` and `tx` from history: the history line whose `doctor_run_id` equals the run (E12's field) gives `kind` (`repair` → `fix`, `undo` → `undo`) and its `tx`; with no such line, `fix` when `<run>/actions.jsonl` exists (only a repair session writes it), else `diagnose` (decided while writing this bead: an undo killed before its commit also has an `actions.jsonl` and then reads as `fix`, which is acceptable for a listing and never an input to `doctor undo`); `action_count` = the complete lines of `actions.jsonl` (read with the same bound), 0 without it; `reverted_run: null`.
   4. **`started_at`** is always the run id's timestamp (whole seconds, UTC; decided while writing this bead: the run id is defined as the UTC start time, it exists for every run, killed ones included, and one source keeps the column uniform).
   5. **`undo_complete`:** for a fix run with a `tx`, `true` when E7's `undo_state(entries, at)` says the repair is no longer in effect (`UndoneBy`); `false` otherwise and for every other kind. Until E7 has landed, `false` for every run; whichever of E4 and E7 lands second wires it and `reverted_run` (E7's bead says the same).
   6. **History** is read once with `history::read(paths, &HistoryFilter::default())`, only when a listed run lacks a readable terminal report or `undo_state` is needed. Its skipped-line warning (`history_lines_skipped`) is passed on, as `history` does (`history.rs:360`). A history that cannot be read at all is treated as empty for these two uses, with that error's warning when the reader gives one (decided while writing this bead: the listing must still answer, and nothing here acts on the answer).
6. **The state's type.** `ListedState`, a closed enum of every `RunState` value plus `ABORTED` (wire names as written, the doctor contract's), with `From<RunState>` and a unit test that every `RunState` maps to the variant of the same wire name. Decided while writing this bead: `ABORTED` is not added to `RunState`, because `RunState` is `doctor diagnose`'s and `doctor fix`'s `state` schema and the runtime never writes `ABORTED` (E6's bead says so); a separate type keeps both schemas exact.
7. **The report** (`LsReport`, A.8 plus `truncated`):

   ```json
   {"runs":[{"run_id":"2026-10-30T18-03-40Z__01M8S…","kind":"fix","started_at":"2026-10-30T18:03:40Z","state":"DONE_OK",
             "exit_code":0,"action_count":1,"tx":"01M9…","reverted_run":null,"undo_complete":false}],
    "truncated":false}
   ```

   Runs are ordered newest first (run id descending). `commands` is `[]` (decided while writing this bead: token-frugal; the undo commands are in each fix report). Nothing here is volatile: two `ls` of one home print the same bytes.
8. **The human form:** a table through `output::table`, columns `RUN`, `KIND`, `STATE`, `EXIT` (`-` for `null`), `ACTIONS`, `TX` (`-` for `null`), `NOTE` (`undone` when `undo_complete`, `reverts <run>` for an undo run); then `(older runs: --limit N)` when `truncated`; `no doctor runs yet` for an empty listing.
9. **What it never does:** write anything, take the lock, follow a symlink in the runs directory, or act on a run.

### 4. `doctor capabilities` (s3)

`src/doctor/capabilities.rs` (new), `src/doctor/scopes.rs` (new, the scope resolver) and the wiring. It reads the binary's registries plus, through E2's tolerant view, `registry.json` (the Registry layer: the registered clients) and the skill directories the Skill layer knows (`Paths::skill_dir()` and B3's `history_tail.skill_dirs[]`), and nothing else: no discovery scan, no request, no write (decided while writing this bead, by analogy with M4-D4 for `capabilities`: offline, scan-free, write-free).

The report (`DoctorCapabilities`, §6.11.1, in this key order):

| Key | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `tool` | `"omaddons"` | constant |
| `build_id` | the execution build id, the value `capabilities.build_id` carries | D1's `crate::build_info::BUILD_ID`; if D1 has not landed, the key is absent and whichever of D1 and this leaf lands second adds it |
| `doctor_contract_version` | `"1.0"` | E3's constant (M4-D3) |
| `platform` | `{os, arch}` | `std::env::consts::{OS, ARCH}` |
| `lock_timeout_seconds` | 5 | `LOCK_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT.as_secs()` |
| `subsystems` | `[{name, applicable}]`, all thirteen | `Subsystem::ALL`, `applicable()` |
| `allowed_ops` | `["write_file", "rename_noreplace", "chmod", "symlink_atomic", "create_dir"]` | `ALLOWED_OPS`: the primitive ops a repair may run, then the runtime's own (`symlink_atomic` for `latest`, `create_dir` for its roots); a unit test ties it to E1's primitive op enum, so a new primitive fails until it is listed |
| `verbs` | `[{path, about, mutates, binds, args, flags}]`, one per `doctor` path | below |
| `detectors` | `[{id, subsystem, severity, description, tier, estimated_cost_ms, online_required, requires, depends_on: []}]` | every row of `failure_modes()`, in registry order; `estimated_cost_ms` = `cost_ms`, `online_required` = `online`; `depends_on` is always `[]` (omaddons' checks depend on view layers, listed in `requires`, never on each other) |
| `fixers` | `[{id, preconditions, writes_to, ops, reversible: true, idempotent: true, cardinality, enabled, needs_force, estimated_cost_ms}]` | every row with `fix: Some(spec)`; `estimated_cost_ms` = the row's `cost_ms` (decided while writing this bead: `FixerSpec` declares no cost of its own); `reversible` and `idempotent` are true for every fixer M4 admits, proven per fixer by F9's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`) harness |
| `manual_remediations` | `[{id, instruction, reason}]` | every row with E3's static manual pair (what `doctor explain` prints) |
| `exit_codes` | `{"0": "healthy", "1": "findings_present", …, "74": "io_error"}` | `doctor::Exit::ALL` into a `BTreeMap<String, String>` (string order equals code order for these eleven) |
| `env_vars` | `{"<NAME>": "<description>", …}` | A2's `contract::env::release()`, the release kind only |
| `write_scopes` | `[{scope, path}]` | below |
| `cost_summary` | `{quick_total_ms, default_total_ms, deep_total_ms, online_total_ms_estimate}` | sums of `cost_ms` over rows with a detector, cumulative (decided while writing this bead): offline `cached`+`quick` (what `--quick` and `health` run); plus `default` (bare `doctor`); plus `deep` (`--include-deep`); and every online row |

- **`tool_version`** is not a report key: the envelope's `tool_version` says it (decided while writing this bead; a second key of that name would be a duplicate in the flattened JSON).
- **`verbs`** (additive, decided while writing this bead, so criterion 10's "every verb and flag … is listed" is checkable): one entry per `COMMANDS` row whose path is `doctor` or starts with `doctor `, in `COMMANDS` order: `path`, `about` (clap's), `mutates` (the row's), `binds` (`BINDING_COMMANDS` membership, so `--if-match` applies), `args` (the positionals' value names, in index order), `flags` (the path's own long flag names without dashes, in declaration order; global flags are left out because every path has them). Built from A4's `contract::commands::command(path)` (its `ArgInfo` and its non-global `FlagInfo`) when A4 has landed, else from help's builders (`help::flags`, `help.rs:128-140`, and the positional loop, `help.rs:329-337`, made `pub(crate)`). E7's and E8's paths appear as their rows land, with no change here.
- **`detectors` lists every failure-mode id exactly once**, the two runtime rows included with `tier: "runtime"` (§6.2.3: "`doctor capabilities` lists every id exactly once"). In a release build, and in a debug build without `OMADDONS_TEST_FIXERS=1`, no `fm-test-` id appears.
- **`write_scopes`**, generated (§6.11.1: "from `FAILURE_MODES` and the fsx scope table"). The scope set is the union of: `state` always (the runtime's run directories and `latest`, and every repair's home-side backups and quarantine under `<run>/`); every `writes_to` of every fixer in `failure_modes()`; and the scopes a repair's own roots imply: `client_meta` whenever `addons` or `client_meta` is declared (client-side backups and quarantine live in `<meta>/snapshots/<tx>.repair/`), `cache` whenever `cache` is declared (`<cache>/quarantine/<run id>/`). Each scope is resolved to paths by `doctor::scopes::roots(scope, &ScopeInputs) -> Vec<PathBuf>`, through `ScopeName::scope()` and the scope table's roots: `state` → `<state>`; `config` → `<config>` (the Config row's root; decided while writing this bead, see Background); `cache` → `<cache>`; `client_meta` → each registered client's `<meta>` (`<client dir>/Interface/.omaddons`); `addons` → each registered client's `<client dir>/Interface/AddOns`; `skill` → `<skills>` and every skill directory the Skill layer knows. E6's `FixPlan::triage()` resolves `writes_to` through the same function: if E6 resolved scopes inline, extract that code into `scopes::roots` so both call one function. Clients come from the Registry layer; an unreadable registry lists no client paths and the command still exits 0 (the doctor reports the registry itself). Entries are sorted by scope (enum order), then path, without duplicates. Paths are absolute: they are this machine's.

### 6. `--robot-triage` (s4)

`src/doctor/triage.rs` (new), `src/doctor/report.rs` (the variant), the diagnose wiring in `src/app/doctor.rs`, and the handbook's agent loop.

1. **It is a diagnose** (M4-D33): E3's runtime runs STARTING (a run directory), DIAGNOSING over the selection the flags give, and the terminal writes; only the report differs. `--robot-triage` with `--since` is a clap conflict, exit 64 (decided while writing this bead: the triage view has no `since` key, and a silently ignored flag would mislead).
2. **Planning, read-only.** After DIAGNOSING and before the terminal writes: `plan_fix(&view, &diagnosis.findings, &FixOptions { only: <the run's --only entries>, force: false, roots: <the placeholder roots doctor diff uses> })`. It takes no lock, allocates no transaction, writes nothing and is never journaled. With `force: false` a forced repair is never planned. A `PlanRefusal` is reported through the recommendation (below); any other planning error (E6's unlisted journal directory, an `io`) leaves `actions_planned` empty and the recommendation to the findings, and does not fail the run (decided while writing this bead: the triage only reports, and the same directory failure is itself a finding of the journal detectors).
3. **The report** (`TriageReport`, A.6), added to E3's enum as `#[serde(rename = "triage")] Triage(TriageReport)`, so `doctor diagnose`'s one schema is a `oneOf` tagged by `view`:

   ```json
   {"ok":false,"schema_version":"1.0","tool_version":"0.1.0","command":"doctor diagnose","exit_code":1,
    "view":"triage","summary":{"ok":false,"total_findings":2,"auto_fixable":1},
    "quick_ref":["P0: 1 finding (1 needs --force --yes)","P3: 1 finding (1 auto-fixable)"],
    "findings":["…the full view's finding objects…"],
    "actions_planned":[{"fixer_id":"fm-plugins-skill-version-drift","writes_to":["<skills>"],"estimated_bytes":24576}],
    "recommended_command":"omaddons doctor fix --only fm-plugins-skill-version-drift",
    "recommended_argv":["omaddons","doctor","fix","--only","fm-plugins-skill-version-drift"],
    "capabilities_command":"omaddons doctor capabilities --json","robot_docs_command":"omaddons doctor robot-docs",
    "warnings":[],"commands":[{"action":"doctor_fix","command":"omaddons doctor fix --only fm-plugins-skill-version-drift","argv":["…"],"destructive":false}],
    "meta":{"elapsed_ms":61,"offline":false}}
   ```

   - `summary.ok` is "no finding at all" (the run's `DONE_OK`); `total_findings` and `auto_fixable` as in the full view.
   - **`quick_ref`** (display strings; the format was decided while writing this bead): one entry per severity that has findings, P0 to P3: `P<k>: <n> finding` or `findings`, then ` (`, the non-zero parts of `<a> auto-fixable`, `<f> needs --force --yes` (`need` when f ≠ 1) and `<m> manual`, comma-separated, then `)`. A finding is auto-fixable when its remediation's `auto_fixable` is true, else needs force when `needs_force` is true, else manual (E3's summary split). No findings: `[]`.
   - `findings`: the same objects, in the same order, as the full view of the same state.
   - **`actions_planned`**: `FixPlan::triage()` (E6); `[]` when nothing is planned or the plan was refused.
   - **`recommended_command` / `recommended_argv`** (the plan names their source; the fallbacks were decided while writing this bead): with planned fixes, `FixPlan::recommended_argv` (passing the run's `-t` when E6's signature takes it); with no planned fix but findings, the first finding's `remediation.explain_argv` (findings are severity-ordered, so a P0 that needs force is explained, never forced); with a `PlanRefusal`, its `doctor_refused` fix argv when the fix is a command, else the first finding's explain argv; with no finding, `null` for both. `recommended_command` is the argv's display string (`shell_words::join`, as `CommandHint` builds it). It never holds `--force` or `--yes`.
   - `capabilities_command` and `robot_docs_command` are the two constant strings (A.6: the doctor contract's `capabilities_url` becomes `capabilities_command`, since omaddons has no URL to give).
   - **`commands[]`:** one hint for the recommendation (action `doctor_fix` for a fix, `doctor_explain` for an explain, with their registered `destructive`), or `[]`. The triage view has no `next_steps` (§6.11's key list), so E3's `next_steps == commands` check does not apply to it.
4. **`report.json`** of a triage run is this envelope without `meta`, plus `kind: "diagnose"` (E3's rule: one value for the file and stdout). `latest` moves to it as for any diagnose; `ls` lists it as a `diagnose` run whose state comes from `summary.ok`; `--since <a triage run>` reads its `findings[].instance` like any report.
5. **The human form:**

   ```text
   omaddons doctor --robot-triage · 2 findings (1 auto-fixable)
     P0: 1 finding (1 needs --force --yes)
     P3: 1 finding (1 auto-fixable)
   next: omaddons doctor fix --only fm-plugins-skill-version-drift
   also: omaddons doctor capabilities --json · omaddons doctor robot-docs
   ```

   A clean run prints `omaddons doctor --robot-triage · no findings` and the `also:` line.
6. **The handbook's agent loop** (`## The agent loop` in `doctor.md`, after `## Surface`): `omaddons doctor --robot-triage --json`; if `actions_planned` is not empty, run `recommended_argv` (an auto-fixable repair, backed up and undoable); otherwise run it too (an explain); a P0 that is not auto-fixable is the user's decision, to be told before anything else; `omaddons undo --last-by agent --json` reverts a repair. It is the same loop B2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.2`, the guide's content) writes into the guide.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `omaddons doctor health` prints exactly one line whose first token is `ok`, `findings`, `unsafe` or `concurrency`, with the precedence unsafe (a P0 finding) > concurrency (the lock held by another process) > findings (any finding, `check-incomplete` and `detector-crashed` included) > ok; it exits 0 only for `ok` and 1 otherwise, with no `error`; its JSON report holds `status`, `findings`, `by_severity`, `last_run` and `run_id`.
- [ ] `doctor health` runs exactly `doctor --quick`'s checks (its `findings` and `by_severity` equal `doctor --quick --json`'s on the same state), creates no run directory, writes nothing (`<state>` including `doctor/`, `<config>`, `<cache>` and every client dir hash-identical; no `<state>` on a fresh home), takes no lock, adds no `net.log` line, and names the run `latest` points at (or `null`).
- [ ] A check cut short (`doctor.detector.panic=sleep:<ms>`) or crashed (`=panic`) makes `health` report `findings`, never `ok`; a corrupt `registry.json` or an unreadable lock file makes it `unsafe`, never `ok`.
- [ ] `doctor health` takes under 200 ms (median of 21, release build, on `common::realistic::realistic_home()`), and each `cached` and `quick` detector under 5 ms (median of 21 of its debug timing line); on that clean home at least 11 of the 21 runs are `ok` and no run reports any finding but a cut-short check, so the detectors fit their 5 ms deadline and report no false positive.
- [ ] `omaddons doctor ls` lists run directories newest first, at most `--limit` (default 20), each with `run_id`, `kind`, `started_at`, `state`, `exit_code`, `action_count`, `tx`, `reverted_run` and `undo_complete`, plus `truncated`; `--limit 0` is `usage` (64) with the fix `omaddons doctor ls --limit 20`; a run without a readable terminal report is `ABORTED` with `exit_code: null`; staged and foreign names are skipped; the listing is bounded by `DOCTOR_SCAN_MAX_ENTRIES` newest first and each report by `API_RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES`; it writes nothing.

Every unit test is table-driven where it has cases, with a name per case and assertion messages that name the case and show the input and the output.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

- **`tests/doctor.rs` (s5),** every scenario a `TestLog` scenario on its own `Home`: `health_on_a_clean_home_is_ok_and_writes_nothing`, `health_on_a_fresh_home_creates_no_state`, `health_reports_findings_unsafe_and_concurrency`, `health_is_never_ok_when_a_check_is_cut_short_or_crashed`, `health_fails_closed_on_corrupt_state`, `health_agrees_with_doctor_quick`, `health_names_the_latest_run`; `ls_on_a_home_with_no_runs`, `ls_lists_runs_newest_first_with_their_kinds`, `ls_limit_and_truncated`, `ls_reports_killed_runs_as_aborted`, `ls_writes_nothing`; `triage_on_a_clean_home`, `triage_recommends_a_fix_that_runs`, `triage_explains_what_needs_force`, `triage_findings_equal_the_full_view`, `triage_changes_nothing_outside_its_run_directory`; `capabilities_lists_every_failure_mode_once`, `capabilities_round_trips_with_only`, `capabilities_verbs_cover_the_doctor_tree`, `capabilities_write_scopes_resolve_this_home`, `capabilities_is_pure`; `robot_docs_has_the_three_literals`, `robot_docs_json_and_human_agree`, `robot_docs_commands_run`; `the_read_surface_names_no_account_realm_or_character`; and the rows added to `every_doctor_exit_site_uses_the_doctor_dictionary`. Each scenario's steps and assertions are listed in s5.
- **`tests/perf.rs` (s5):** `doctor_health_stays_under_200_ms`, `each_quick_detector_stays_under_5_ms`.

### Logging

- Every `tests/doctor.rs` scenario opens `let log = tlog!();`, names each phase with `log.step(…)`, runs every command through `log.run(&env, &argv)` with `--json` (and `--progress json` where it reads stderr), records each envelope it inspects with `log.json(label, &envelope)`, and records `log.tree` of `<state>` (with `doctor/`), `<config>`, `<cache>` and each client dir before every command whose purity it asserts, then `log.assert_unchanged` after it, which logs the first differing paths. Doctor envelopes are read with `Ran::envelope()` (they have no `data`) and checked with `common::doctor::check_envelope`.
- A failing scenario prints `test log: <path>` and the last 20 steps (T1's guard); `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG=verbose argc e2e doctor` echoes every step live.
- The perf tests print one `measured` line each (median, p95, first run, home shape; per detector its id, median and p95), which H6 quotes.
- Unit tests log nothing; their assertion messages name the case and show the input and the output.

### Checkpoint-only tests

- `cargo test --release --test perf -- --ignored --skip bench_home --skip live_home --test-threads=1` runs `doctor_health_stays_under_200_ms` and `each_quick_detector_stays_under_5_ms` (owned here; F8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.8`, `status` on the registry) owns `status --cached`'s). They need no external resource and never print `SKIP`; a debug build proves nothing about them and they are not run there (they are `#[ignore]`d like every budget in the file).

## Considerations

- **Size M, five subtasks; slack 4.** Five small surfaces, each a command path or view with its own registry touch points and contract rows, each in its own commit. The leaf has four units of slack (§10.3) and sits in lane 5 at t = 11–13 of the six-lane schedule; it is not on the critical path, but B2, H1, H3 and T4 wait for it.
- **Hot spots and their rules (§10.5; plan keys resolve through the key table in the first comment on the milestone epic):**
  - `src/app/mod.rs` (`COMMANDS`, dispatch; A1, A4, A5, A7, B1, B3, D5, D9, E3, E4, E6, E7, E8): A1 first; each command leaf adds its own rows and rebases. s1 and s2 both add rows: the second to land rebases.
  - `src/contract/guide/` (B1, B2, E4): this leaf adds `doctor.md`, `DOCTOR_TEMPLATE`, `render_doctor()` and the `{{doctor_commands}}` row, and never edits `guide.md`.
  - `tests/contract/matrix.rs` and snapshots: append rows, one snapshot file per row.
  - `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md`: regenerate after rebasing, never merge by hand.
  - `omarchy/Model.js`: command leaves add only `CLI_PATHS` rows.
  - `README.md`: edit only this leaf's sections.
  - `src/doctor/budget.rs`, `runtime.rs` and `report.rs` are E3's (E6, E7 and E8 extend them too): this leaf adds an order parameter, possibly `Budget::entries_only`, the free `detect`, the `Triage` variant and `ListedState`, each without changing an existing caller's behaviour. `src/doctor/runs.rs` is shared with E8 (section 3).
- **Risks (§11.4):**
  - #3, doctor false positives erode trust (M, M): `health` and the triage only relay what the detectors find; a scenario asserts a clean home reads `ok`, and the perf test fails on any finding but a rare cut-short check on the realistic home, so a new detector's false positive fails at the checkpoint.
  - #4, `status --cached` slows past 5 ms (M, M): `health` shares the tiers, and its own budgets (200 ms, 5 ms per quick detector) are measured here, so a slow detector is caught even before F8's `status` test.
  - #13, the guide drifts from behaviour (L, M): the handbook's surface and exit tables are generated, every command in it parses, and a test requires the example of every present flow.
  - #14, the milestone is large (M, M): five subtasks, two of which can run in parallel.
- **Departures and settled conflicts** (each "Decided while writing this bead" above; confirm or adjust in the close comment): `health`'s exits 0/1 instead of the doctor contract's 4 and 5 (H5 records it); the status precedence; the lock read through the view; `tool_version` left to the envelope; `verbs`; `config` resolved to `<config>`; the implied repair-root scopes; `truncated`; the newest-first listing; `started_at` from the run id; `ABORTED` with `exit_code: null`, in its own `ListedState`; the aborted runs' kind inference; triage state from `summary.ok`; the shared `runs.rs`; the naming-rule exceptions; `{{doctor_commands}}`; the two NEVER lists; the undo flow gated on `doctor undo`; `--robot-triage` conflicting with `--since`; the recommendation fallbacks; `quick_ref`'s format; `-t` ignored by `ls`, `capabilities` and `robot-docs`; `commands: []` for `health` and `ls`; `fixers[].estimated_cost_ms` = the row's cost; cumulative `cost_summary`; the digest snapshot; the realistic home for perf; the per-detector debug timing lines.
- **What could go wrong in implementation, and how to notice:**
  - `health` and `doctor --quick` drifting apart: the shared `plan_diagnose` call and `detect` function, and `health_agrees_with_doctor_quick` (s5).
  - `health` writing something (a discovery cache, a `<state>` directory on a fresh home): the purity scenario hashes `<state>`, `<config>`, `<cache>` and every client, and asserts no `<state>` on a fresh home.
  - a deadline flake: in debug builds the quick deadline is 100 ms (×20); a gate scenario on a small home has that margin. Tests of the cut-short case use the sleep failpoint, so they are exact.
  - `ls` reporting a live run as `ABORTED`: a run still in DIAGNOSING has no report yet; README says so, and `ls` never acts on it.
  - the triage recommending something that does not run: `triage_recommends_a_fix_that_runs` runs it, and the contract suite runs every `commands[]` argv.
  - a flattened report key colliding with an envelope key (`commands`, `tool_version`): E3's key-order check, this leaf's `no_tool_version_key` test, and the name `verbs` for the verb list.
  - `write_scopes` understating what a repair writes: `write_scopes_cases` include the implied roots, and F9's harness asserts every write lands inside a declared scope.
- **Compatibility with older builds.** Nothing here writes, so nothing changes what an M3 build sees; a triage run directory is a diagnose's, which E9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9`) characterizes.
- **Privacy.** None of these verbs reads `WTF/`. Findings carry no file content and no path below `WTF/` (M4-D42). `write_scopes` and `ls` print absolute paths of this machine (state, cache, client dirs), never an account, realm or character name.
- **Performance.** `health` is a view load, the cheap checks, one `readlink` and one `stat`. `ls` reads at most `--limit` reports. `capabilities` reads compiled-in data, `registry.json` and the history projection; `robot-docs` reads compiled-in data only.
- **The doctor has no configuration** (§7.8): nothing here reads a `config.toml` key.
- **`health` is a fallback fix.** E10 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.10`) points the doctor tree's `internal` fix at `omaddons doctor health`, so `health` must answer on a damaged home: every layer it reads is tolerant, and a failure there is a finding, not an error. For an internal error in `health` itself, E10's rule keeps the fix from rerunning it.

Its demo (recorded by T4): `doctor` on a home with each stuck state planted; a set-aside with `--force --yes`, then `doctor undo`; a set-aside, a later install, and the refused undo; a stuck repair that fences only its own resources; a bound gc; the credential fix from the Issues view and Undo last; the harness green at every primitive boundary; the fsync counts table. It pre-checks criteria 8 (doctor), 9, 10, 11, 12, 13 and 16.

**Related, not edges:** E7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7`, `undo_state` and undo runs for `ls`; the handbook's undo flow), E8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.8`, the shared `runs.rs`), A3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`, schema validation and the rule test), A4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`, `capabilities`' failure-mode summary and `CommandInfo`), A5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5`, `robot-docs schema`), C3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.3`), C4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4`, the corpus), D1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1`, the build id), D8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8`, `common::realistic_home()`), F7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.7`), F8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.8`, `status` on the same tiers), F9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`, which asserts every fixer has a fixture and proves `reversible` and `idempotent`), E9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9`), E10 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.10`), H5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.5`, which records the `health` exit departure), H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, which runs the perf budgets).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `omaddons doctor health` prints exactly one line whose first token is `ok`, `findings`, `unsafe` or `concurrency`, with the precedence unsafe (a P0 finding) > concurrency (the lock held by another process) > findings (any finding, `check-incomplete` and `detector-crashed` included) > ok; it exits 0 only for `ok` and 1 otherwise, with no `error`; its JSON report holds `status`, `findings`, `by_severity`, `last_run` and `run_id`.
- [ ] `doctor health` runs exactly `doctor --quick`'s checks (its `findings` and `by_severity` equal `doctor --quick --json`'s on the same state), creates no run directory, writes nothing (`<state>` including `doctor/`, `<config>`, `<cache>` and every client dir hash-identical; no `<state>` on a fresh home), takes no lock, adds no `net.log` line, and names the run `latest` points at (or `null`).
- [ ] A check cut short (`doctor.detector.panic=sleep:<ms>`) or crashed (`=panic`) makes `health` report `findings`, never `ok`; a corrupt `registry.json` or an unreadable lock file makes it `unsafe`, never `ok`.
- [ ] `doctor health` takes under 200 ms (median of 21, release build, on `common::realistic::realistic_home()`), and each `cached` and `quick` detector under 5 ms (median of 21 of its debug timing line); on that clean home at least 11 of the 21 runs are `ok` and no run reports any finding but a cut-short check, so the detectors fit their 5 ms deadline and report no false positive.
- [ ] `omaddons doctor ls` lists run directories newest first, at most `--limit` (default 20), each with `run_id`, `kind`, `started_at`, `state`, `exit_code`, `action_count`, `tx`, `reverted_run` and `undo_complete`, plus `truncated`; `--limit 0` is `usage` (64) with the fix `omaddons doctor ls --limit 20`; a run without a readable terminal report is `ABORTED` with `exit_code: null`; staged and foreign names are skipped; the listing is bounded by `DOCTOR_SCAN_MAX_ENTRIES` newest first and each report by `API_RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES`; it writes nothing.
- [ ] `--robot-triage` returns the `triage` view (`summary{ok, total_findings, auto_fixable}`, `quick_ref`, `findings`, `actions_planned`, `recommended_command`, `recommended_argv`, `capabilities_command`, `robot_docs_command`) in one leaf: `actions_planned` and the fix recommendation come from E6's planner; its `recommended_argv` runs (a planned fix exits 0 and clears its finding; an explain exits 0); it is `null` on a clean home; it never holds `--force` or `--yes`; with `--since` it is `usage` (64); a triage run creates one run directory whose `report.json` is its envelope without `meta` plus `kind: "diagnose"`, and changes nothing outside `<state>/doctor/`.
- [ ] `doctor diagnose`'s schema is one `oneOf` tagged by `view` (`full`, `triage`), and both views validate against it (once A3 has landed).
- [ ] `omaddons doctor capabilities --json` is generated from the registry and the scope table: it carries all eleven doctor exit codes by name, `write_scopes`, `allowed_ops`, every detector (each failure-mode id exactly once), every fixer, every manual remediation, `cost_summary`, and `verbs` listing every `doctor` path with its own flags; every detector id with a detector works with `--only` (exit 0 or 1, or 6 for an online-only row without `--online`) and the two runtime ids give E3's `usage`; no `fm-test-` id appears without `OMADDONS_TEST_FIXERS=1`; it makes no request and writes nothing; its detector count equals `capabilities`' `failure_modes.count` (once A4 has landed).
- [ ] `omaddons doctor robot-docs` renders `src/contract/guide/doctor.md` with the guide renderer: the doctor surface (`{{doctor_commands}}`), the doctor exit dictionary, schema pointers, the examples of every present flow, the capabilities endpoint, the ten doctor NEVER items and B1's shared `NEVER` table; it contains the literal strings `EXIT CODES`, `capabilities` and `NEVER do`; every command in its code fences parses; its JSON is `{format: "markdown", content}`, its human form is `content` byte for byte, and two runs print the same bytes.
- [ ] Every exit site of the four paths and of `--robot-triage` maps to the doctor dictionary (rows in E3's `every_doctor_exit_site_uses_the_doctor_dictionary`), and every observed exit is a declared one (A1's exit observation).
- [ ] DEC-1 for each of the four paths, in the subtask that adds it: the clap variant, the `COMMANDS` row with every M4 field, `command_name` and dispatch, the help layout (no bare-help change; `help_walks_a_nested_path`'s literal), matrix rows (one success and one failure, snapshotted, checked in doctor mode), the `special.rs` read-only invocation, the `CLI_PATHS` row and the README section; `--robot-triage` gets its matrix rows and README paragraph.
- [ ] `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` is regenerated in each subtask that adds a path, and `tests/skill.rs` passes.
- [ ] The intent-corpus rows of section 9 pass (when C4 has landed; otherwise the close comment lists them for C4).
- [ ] No output of any of these verbs, on any channel, names an account, realm or character (`assert_private_all` with `--progress json` on a home with `FAKEACCT`/`FakeRealm`/`FakeChar` trees).
- [ ] `argc gate` passes for every subtask's commit, and `ubs` is clean on the changed files.

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M4 plan, 2026-10-24).**

**Why this bead.** After E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`) and E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`) the doctor can diagnose and repair, but only through a full report a script has to parse and an agent has to reason about. The doctor contract that vision G7 adopts has five more read-only verbs, and this bead adds them: `doctor health` (one line a script dispatches on by its first word, from the cheap checks, writing nothing), `doctor ls` (the run history, so a postmortem or an undo can find its run), `doctor --robot-triage` (one call that tells an agent what is wrong, what `doctor fix` would do, and exactly what to run next), `doctor capabilities` (the doctor's own machine description, generated, never hand-kept) and `doctor robot-docs` (its handbook). They are what makes the doctor usable without README, which is the whole point of M4's agent surface, and they keep the thesis true: every verb only reads, and the triage never recommends a forced repair.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M4-D2:** one registry feeds every description of the CLI; `doctor capabilities` is computed from the failure-mode registry, the doctor exit dictionary, the env-var registry, `COMMANDS` and the fsx scope table, and the handbook's tables are the guide renderer's generated blocks. The only hand list is `ALLOWED_OPS`, tied to the primitive types by a test.
- **M4-D3:** `doctor_contract_version` ("1.0") names the external contract's revision, apart from `schema_version` and `tool_version`; `health` prints it as `doctor=1.0`.
- **M4-D34:** every verb emits the report at the top level with the envelope keys around it; `error` only for 4, 5, 6, 64, 66, 73, 74. This is why `health` exits 1, not the doctor contract's 4 or 5, for `unsafe` and `concurrency`, and why `doctor capabilities` carries no `tool_version` report key.
- **M4-D29 (context):** `health` runs exactly the `cached` and `quick` tiers that `doctor --quick` and `status` run, through the same selection and the same detection loop.
- **M4-D33 (context):** `health`, `ls`, `capabilities` and `robot-docs` create no run directory; `--robot-triage` is a diagnose and does.
- **M4-D43 (context):** a check cut short is a `check-incomplete` finding, so `health` is never `ok` for it; a layer failure that causes a skip is itself reported (E2's rule), so a skipped check never reads as healthy either.
- **M4-D40, M4-D30, M4-D46, M4-D38, M4-D11, M4-D18, M4-D55, M4-D7, M4-D5 (context):** the doctor dictionary on every exit; instance keys; undo runs and `undo_complete`; no forced repair in any recommendation; the closed action set; determinism; the naming rules, with the doctor contract's names as a type- and field-keyed exception; the shared renderer and `NEVER` table; declared, verified exits.

**Alternatives rejected that matter here.**
- A run directory for `health` (M4-D33): it would grow without bound under a widget or a cron job.
- The doctor contract's `health` exits 4 and 5: they would be `error`-less refusals and lock timeouts, which M4-D34 forbids; a script dispatches on the first token instead.
- A hand-written capabilities description (M4-D2): it drifts.
- Nesting doctor reports under `data` (M4-D34): it breaks the doctor contract's consumers.
- Adding `ABORTED` to the runtime's `RunState`: it would publish a state `doctor diagnose` and `doctor fix` never report; `ls` gets its own `ListedState`.
- A full snapshot of `doctor capabilities` and of the handbook in the matrix: every later catalog leaf would re-accept them; a digest and a sample-rendered snapshot pin what matters.
- Recommending `doctor fix --force --yes` for a stuck journal: a forced repair needs someone who has read what it does (M4-D38), so the triage recommends its `explain`.

**Risks and how they are watched.**
- #3, doctor false positives (M, M): a clean home must read `ok`, and the release perf test fails on any finding but a rare cut-short check on the realistic home, so a new detector's false positive fails the checkpoint.
- #4, `status --cached` slowing (M, M): `health`'s 200 ms and 5 ms-per-quick-detector budgets are measured here on the same tiers, before F8's `status` test.
- #13, the guide drifting (L, M): the handbook's surface and exit tables are generated, every command in it parses, and the examples follow the commands that exist.
- Plan-versus-code: the bench home cannot be built in a release build, so the budgets use D8's realistic home; `support::stable()` redacts no build id, so the capabilities snapshot is a digest.

**What it unblocks and why they wait.** B2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.2`) writes the guide's doctor loop, which runs `--robot-triage` and points at `doctor robot-docs`; the loop must describe the final surface. H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`) audits the whole contract and must see these shapes and their naming exceptions. H3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3`) needs a success and a failure matrix row for every path. T4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4`) records slice 3's demo once every slice-3 leaf is closed.

**How it serves the milestone.** G-M4-1 (self-describing: the doctor describes itself from code), G-M4-4 (incomplete coverage never reads as healthy, and the agent loop names the safe next step), G-M4-5 (one dictionary per tree, deterministic bytes) and G-M4-6 (no new writes, no lock). It owns the surface items of checkpoint criterion 10, including `health`'s 200 ms and the 5 ms per quick detector, and its doctor-verb rows of criterion 5.

**Confidence.** High. Every verb is a thin, read-only layer over E2's view, E3's runtime and envelope, E6's planner and B1's renderer, all of which land first with their own tests; the risk is in getting the many small shape decisions consistent, which the unit tables, the contract rows and the end-to-end scenarios pin.

title: `omaddons doctor health`: the one-line summary of the cheap checks, with no run directory
description:
Part 1 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4 (`doctor health`, `ls`, `--robot-triage`, `capabilities` and `robot-docs`). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

The leaf E4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4`) adds the doctor contract's read-only verbs on top of the doctor that E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, `doctor diagnose` and `explain`) and E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`, `doctor fix`) built: `health`, `ls`, `--robot-triage`, `capabilities` and `robot-docs`. It exists so scripts and agents can use the doctor without parsing a full report or reading README (vision G7, "`doctor` follows the world-class doctor contract"; G4, "the first command an agent guesses works").

**This part ships `omaddons doctor health`**: one line whose first word a script dispatches on (`ok`, `findings`, `unsafe`, `concurrency`), computed from the cheap checks run live, with no run directory and no write of any kind, plus every DEC-1 registry touch point of the path in one commit. It is its own step because a command's touch points must land together (DEC-1, no stubs), and because it needs one refactor of E3's runtime (the detection loop as a free function) that nothing else in the leaf needs. It touches different modules from s2 (`doctor ls`), so the two can be worked at the same time.

**What is true when this part starts** (verified at `c0ab5e9`, plus what the blockers land):

- E3 has landed: `Command::Doctor(app::doctor::DoctorArgs)` with `#[command(subcommand)] action: Option<DoctorAction>` and the diagnose flags flattened on `DoctorArgs`; `DoctorAction::{Diagnose, Explain}` (E6 adds `Fix`, `Diff`); `doctor::Exit` (`0 healthy`, `1 findings_present`, …, `64 usage_error`, `66 no_input`, `74 io_error`) and the total `exit_for(ErrorCode)`; `output::envelope::DoctorEnvelope` (report keys flattened between `exit_code` and `error`), the `DoctorOutcome` trait (`type Report: Serialize + JsonSchema; command(); report(); exit(); error(); warnings(); commands(); render_human()`) and `emit_doctor`; `plan_diagnose(registry, &DiagnoseArgs) -> Result<DiagnosePlan, Error>` (pure); `Runtime::{start, diagnose, finish}` with `Runtime::diagnose(&mut self, registry, view, selection, budgets) -> Diagnosis`; `BySeverity` (P0–P3, always all four); `DoctorRunId` (`new`, `parse`, `Display`; `<YYYY-MM-DDTHH-MM-SSZ>__<ULID>`); `Paths::{doctor_latest, doctor_run}`; `<state>/doctor/latest`, a relative symlink `runs/<id>`; `Budget::for_tier` (the `cached`/`quick` deadline is `QUICK_DETECTOR_BUDGET`, 5 ms, ×20 in debug builds by `DEBUG_DEADLINE_SCALE`); the runtime rows `fm-state_files-detector-crashed` (P1) and `fm-state_files-check-incomplete` (P3); the failpoint `doctor.detector.panic` (`=panic`, `=sleep:<ms>`, `@N`); `common::doctor::check_envelope` and the contract harness's doctor mode; the static rule that every Doctor row declares 0, 64 and 74.
- E2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.2`, the tolerant view) has landed: `DoctorView::load(ctx, &selection)` with lazy, load-once, write-free layers; `view.lock() -> Option<&LockState>` (a failed probe is a machine `fm-schemas-state-corrupt` failure, P0); `visible_failures`: a layer failure is reported when its row is selected or when it caused a skip, so a skipped check always comes with the finding that explains it; `journal-pending` reports none while the lock is held.
- E6 has landed: `doctor::registry::failure_modes()`, the effective registry (test-only rows are tier `default`, so `health` never runs them). E1's invariant holds that online rows are `default` or `deep`, so `health` never selects one.
- `fsx::lock::probe_global` (`src/fsx/lock.rs:161-191`) returns `LockState::{Free, Held { holder }, Missing}` (`lock.rs:36-45`) and creates nothing. Only `src/fsx/lock.rs`, `src/fsx/scope.rs` and `src/state/paths.rs` may name the lock file.
- `app::COMMANDS` rows are built by A1's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1`) `entry(name, group, mutates, exits, data, network)` with the `doctor()` modifier (`src/app/mod.rs:121-165` at `c0ab5e9`, before A1); `command_name` is `mod.rs:195-237`, `run_command` `mod.rs:374-587`; `dispatch` writes nothing after a read-only command (`mod.rs:360-370`).
- The registry tables: `tests/contract/special.rs:317-338` (read-only invocations, test at `:313-386`; E3 exempts `<state>/doctor/` for Doctor paths); `tests/cli_skeleton.rs:216-224` (`help_walks_a_nested_path`); `omarchy/Model.js:133-178` (`CLI_PATHS`, held equal by `tests/omarchy_widget.rs:28-51`); `tests/contract/matrix.rs` (`s.json(args, code)` then `insta::assert_json_snapshot!(name, s.stable(&c.envelope))`, as `matrix.rs:27-56`).

**The decisions that shape it:**
- **M4-D29:** one detector registry serves `doctor`, `doctor health` and `status`, by tier; `doctor --quick` and `doctor health` run `cached` and `quick`. Rejected: two implementations of each check.
- **M4-D33:** `health` creates no run directory and "reports the last run it finds". Why: `health` exists to be cheap and frequent. Rejected: a run directory for `health` (it would grow without bound under a widget or a cron job).
- **M4-D43:** a check cut short by its deadline or entry cap becomes a `fm-state_files-check-incomplete` finding, "and `health`'s first token is never `ok` for it". A failed layer is a finding and an unavailable layer, never silently a pass.
- **M4-D34:** every doctor verb puts its report at the top level with `{ok, schema_version, tool_version, command, exit_code, …, error?, warnings, commands, meta}` around it; `error` only for exits 4, 5, 6, 64, 66, 73, 74; findings (1) are a report. Rejected: nesting under `data`.
- **M4-D3:** `doctor_contract_version` ("1.0") is printed as `doctor=1.0`; the crate version is independent.
- **M4-D40:** the doctor dictionary; `exit_for` maps every code.

## Technical Approach

### 1. The command and its registry touch points (DEC-1, all in this commit)

1. **clap:** `DoctorAction::Health` in `src/app/doctor.rs`, doc comment (its `about`) "One line for scripts: ok, findings, unsafe or concurrency (the quick checks; no run record)", with an `after_long_help` listing the four tokens, their precedence and the exits 0 and 1. No flags of its own; the global `-t` narrows it.
2. **`COMMANDS` row:** `entry("doctor health", Group::Look, false, &[0, 1, 64, 66, 74], data_schema::<HealthReport>, Network::None).doctor()`, after the doctor rows E3 and E6 placed at the end of the Look group (`stores_plan: false`). 66 is `-t <unknown>` (`target_not_found`).
3. **`command_name`:** `Some(Command::Doctor(a))` with `Some(DoctorAction::Health)` → `"doctor health"`. **Dispatch:** the arm calls `doctor::health::run(ctx)` and emits through E3's `emit_doctor`.
4. **Help layout:** no bare-help change (the path is nested under `doctor`, which E3 placed); `omaddons help doctor` lists it through clap.
5. **Contract matrix** (`tests/contract/matrix.rs`, a new `#[test] fn doctor_health()`): `doctor health` → 0, snapshot `doctor_health_ok`; `doctor health -t nosuch` → 66, `target_not_found`, snapshot `doctor_health_unknown_target`. Both checked in E3's doctor mode by `support::check`.
6. **`special.rs`:** `"doctor health" => &["doctor", "health"]` in the read-only invocation table.
7. **`cli_skeleton`:** `&["doctor", "health"]` in `help_walks_a_nested_path`'s path list.
8. **`CLI_PATHS`:** `"doctor health": { "mutates": false, "destructive": false, "binds": false }` in `omarchy/Model.js`.
9. **README:** a `### \`doctor health\`` section (section 6 below).

### 2. The shared detection loop (`src/doctor/runtime.rs`)

`health` must run the same checks a diagnose runs, without `Runtime::start` (which creates a run directory). Decided while writing this bead: if E3's loop lives only inside `Runtime::diagnose(&mut self, …)`, move it into

```rust
pub(crate) struct Detection {
    pub findings: Vec<Finding>,          // merged and ordered exactly as diagnose orders them
    pub skipped: Vec<Skipped>,
    pub timings: Vec<(&'static str, Duration)>, // each detector that ran, in run order
}
pub(crate) fn detect(registry: &[FailureMode], view: &DoctorView, selection: &Selection, budgets: &Budgets) -> Detection;
```

and make `Runtime::diagnose` call it, with no change to diagnose's behaviour (E3's unit and end-to-end tests pass unchanged). `detect` does exactly what DIAGNOSING does per selected row, in registry order: force the view layers its `requires` names; start its `Budget`; fire `doctor.detector.panic`; if the budget has already expired, record it incomplete with no work done; otherwise call the detector inside `catch_unwind(AssertUnwindSafe(…))`; a panic becomes `fm-state_files-detector-crashed`, an `incomplete` return `fm-state_files-check-incomplete`; then E2's `target_skips`, `visible_failures` and the merge. It writes nothing and takes no lock. `timings` is measured with `Instant` around each call. If E3 already exposes such a function, use it and add only `timings`.

`DoctorRunId::started_at(&self) -> Timestamp` (the id's timestamp prefix parsed as UTC, whole seconds) is added beside `DoctorRunId` if E3 has none (by whichever of this part and s2, which needs it too, lands first).

### 3. `src/doctor/health.rs`

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, JsonSchema)]
#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum HealthStatus { Ok, Findings, Unsafe, Concurrency }

#[derive(Debug, Serialize, JsonSchema)]
pub struct HealthReport {
    pub status: HealthStatus,
    pub findings: u64,                 // every finding, runtime rows included
    pub by_severity: BySeverity,       // E3's, P0–P3 always present
    pub last_run: Option<Timestamp>,   // RFC 3339 UTC; the doctor contract's name (no _at)
    pub run_id: Option<DoctorRunId>,
}
pub fn run(ctx: &Context) -> Result<HealthOutcome, DoctorFailure>;
pub(crate) fn status_of(findings: &[Finding], lock: Option<&LockState>) -> HealthStatus; // pure
pub(crate) fn last_run(paths: &Paths) -> Option<(DoctorRunId, Timestamp)>;          // readlink + stat
pub(crate) fn line(report: &HealthReport, tool_version: &str) -> String;            // pure
```

**`run`, in order:**

1. **Selection:** `DiagnoseArgs { quick: true, ..Default::default() }` (add `Default` to E3's `DiagnoseArgs` if missing) through `plan_diagnose(failure_modes(), &args)` with the global `-t`. So the rows (`cached` and `quick`, never a runtime row, never an online row) and the `-t` narrowing equal `doctor --quick`'s by construction (M4-D29). An unknown `-t` is E3's `target_not_found` (exit 66) before anything is read.
2. **Detection:** `DoctorView::load(ctx, &selection)`, then `detect(…)` with the tier budgets. Each `(id, elapsed)` of `timings` is logged at debug level as `check <fm id>: <n> us` (µs, integer), visible under `-v` (decided while writing this bead: s5's per-detector perf budget needs a measurement of the release binary, and a debug log line is no wire name).
3. **The lock:** `view.lock()`. `Some(LockState::Held { .. })` → held by another process (`health` never acquires the lock, so a held lock is never its own). `Some(Free)` and `Some(Missing)` → free (`Missing` means nothing ever mutated). `None` (the probe failed) → not `concurrency`; E2 already turned the failure into a P0 `fm-schemas-state-corrupt` finding, which `visible_failures` reports because the failure makes `journal-pending` skip, so the status is `unsafe` (fail closed, §8.1 rule 6). Never name the lock file here. The holder's identity is not printed (decided while writing this bead: `status` and `doctor` show it; the one-liner stays one line).
4. **The status word** (`status_of`; the plan fixes the meanings, the precedence was decided while writing this bead):
   1. `unsafe`: at least one P0 finding;
   2. `concurrency`: no P0, and the lock is held by another process;
   3. `findings`: at least one finding of any severity, `check-incomplete` and `detector-crashed` included;
   4. `ok`: no finding at all and the lock free.

   *Why:* a P0 state is persistent and the most urgent thing to tell a script, and the journal checks ignore a transaction whose writer is alive, so a P0 seen during another commit is real; a held lock lasts milliseconds and only tells a script to look again; any finding, a cut-short check included, means "look" (M4-D43).
5. **The last run** (`last_run`): `std::fs::read_link(paths.doctor_latest())`; accepted only when the target is exactly the two components `runs/<name>`, `<name>` parses as a `DoctorRunId`, and `std::fs::symlink_metadata(paths.doctor_run(&id))` is a directory. Then `run_id` = that id and `last_run` = `id.started_at()`. Anything else (missing, dangling, a regular file, an absolute target, `../…`, a name that is not a run id, a file in place of the run) gives `None`. No `report.json` is read.
6. **The outcome:** `HealthOutcome { report, warnings }` implementing `DoctorOutcome`: `command()` = `"doctor health"`; `exit()` = `Healthy` for `ok`, `FindingsPresent` for the other three; `error()` = `None` always; `warnings()` = the view's warnings; `commands()` = `[]` (decided while writing this bead: the next step after a non-`ok` line is a diagnose, for which M4-D11's closed action set has no action).

**Exit codes** (decided while writing this bead; the plan is silent): `ok` → 0, `findings`/`unsafe`/`concurrency` → 1, a report with no `error`. *Rejected:* the doctor contract's 4 for `unsafe` and 5 for `concurrency`: M4-D34 reserves 4 and 5 for runs that carry an `error`, and `health` neither refuses nor waits for the lock; an `error`-less exit 4 would fail E3's envelope check. The close comment records it as a departure from the doctor contract for H5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.5`).

**What it never does:** create a run directory or `<state>` itself on a fresh home, write any file, take the lock, recover a journal, make a request, read `WTF/`, or read a report.

### 4. Output

JSON (A.7):

```json
{"ok":false,"schema_version":"1.0","tool_version":"0.1.0","command":"doctor health","exit_code":1,
 "status":"findings","findings":2,"by_severity":{"P0":0,"P1":0,"P2":1,"P3":1},
 "last_run":"2026-10-30T18:02:11Z","run_id":"2026-10-30T18-02-11Z__01M8R…",
 "warnings":[],"commands":[],"meta":{"elapsed_ms":38,"offline":false}}
```

Human (`line`), exactly one line and a newline, no colour, no tab:

```text
findings  omaddons=0.1.0 doctor=1.0 findings=2 P2=1 P3=1 last_run=2026-10-30T18:02:11Z run_id=2026-10-30T18-02-11Z__01M8R…
ok  omaddons=0.1.0 doctor=1.0 findings=0 last_run=none run_id=none
```

The status word, two spaces, `omaddons=<tool_version> doctor=<doctor_contract_version> findings=<n>`, each non-zero severity as ` P<k>=<n>` in P0–P3 order, then ` last_run=<RFC 3339 | none> run_id=<id | none>`. (A.7's example line shows `findings` with `P0=1`; by the rule above that line reads `unsafe`. The rule wins; the example's values were illustrative.)

### 5. The contract

- New wire names (close comment): the path `doctor health`; the keys `status`, `findings`, `by_severity`, `last_run`, `run_id`; the values `ok`, `findings`, `unsafe`, `concurrency`.
- Naming rules (M4-D55): `last_run` is an instant without `_at`, the doctor contract's name. Decided while writing this bead: it keeps that spelling and joins E3's doctor-contract exception in A3's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`) rule test, keyed by type and field (`HealthReport.last_run`), with the reason "the doctor contract's names (M4-D34)"; never a line on `tests/contract/rules_allowlist.txt`. Whichever of A3 and this part lands second adds it.
- No volatile key: `last_run` and `run_id` come from the run directories, identical on a repeat from a copy of the home.
- No new error code, warning, action, env var, failpoint or constant.
- Previews bind (common rule 16): not a mutating path; say so in the close comment.

### 6. README and the skill

- `### \`doctor health\``: the line and its tokens with their precedence; exits 0 (`ok`) and 1 (the other three), never an `error`; `-t`; "runs the quick checks live, creates no run directory and writes nothing"; `last_run`/`run_id` name the run `latest` points at; the JSON keys; that a check cut short or a state file the doctor cannot read is never `ok`.
- Regenerate `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` (`OMADDONS_UPDATE_SKILL=1 cargo test --test skill`): the guide's `{{commands}}` block lists the new path (common rule 17). If A4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`) has landed, re-accept its `capabilities_ok_digest` snapshot (one more path line).

**Files:** `src/doctor/health.rs` (new), `src/doctor/runtime.rs`, `src/doctor/mod.rs` (`pub mod health`), `src/app/doctor.rs`, `src/app/mod.rs`, `tests/contract/matrix.rs` and two snapshots, `tests/contract/special.rs`, `tests/cli_skeleton.rs`, `omarchy/Model.js`, `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md`, `README.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `omaddons doctor health` prints exactly one line whose first token is `ok`, `findings`, `unsafe` or `concurrency`, in the precedence unsafe > concurrency > findings > ok, and exits 0 only for `ok`, 1 otherwise, with no `error` key.
- [ ] Its JSON report holds `status`, `findings`, `by_severity` (all four severities), `last_run` and `run_id` in that order, with `commands: []`.
- [ ] Its selection is built by E3's `plan_diagnose` with `quick: true`, and its detection by the shared `detect`, which `Runtime::diagnose` also calls; E3's tests pass unchanged.
- [ ] It creates no run directory and writes nothing: the purity unit test and the read-only contract test pass, and `detect_writes_nothing` holds.
- [ ] An unavailable lock layer gives `unsafe` (E2's P0 failure), never `ok` and never `concurrency`; a `Missing` lock counts as free.
- [ ] `last_run`/`run_id` are taken from `latest` only when it is exactly `runs/<valid id>` naming a directory; every other case gives `null`.
- [ ] Each detector's time is logged under `-v` as `check <fm id>: <n> us`.
- [ ] DEC-1 in this commit: the clap variant, the `COMMANDS` row with every M4 field, `command_name` and dispatch, no bare-help change, the matrix rows `doctor_health_ok` and `doctor_health_unknown_target` (snapshotted, doctor mode), the `special.rs` invocation, the `cli_skeleton` literal, the `CLI_PATHS` row and README's section.
- [ ] `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` is regenerated and `tests/skill.rs` passes.
- [ ] `last_run`'s naming exception is keyed by type and field with its reason, with no allowlist line (once A3 has landed).
- [ ] `argc gate` passes and `ubs` is clean on the changed files; the close comment lists the wire names, the exit departure for H5 and each "Decided while writing this bead" item.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

- **`src/doctor/health.rs`:**
  - `status_precedence_cases` (table, one name per case; input findings by severity and a `LockState`): `none_free` → `ok`; `p3_free` → `findings`; `p0_free` → `unsafe`; `none_held` → `concurrency`; `p2_held` → `concurrency`; `p0_held` → `unsafe`; `incomplete_only` (a `check-incomplete`, P3) → `findings`; `crashed_only` (P1) → `findings`; `none_missing` → `ok`; `lock_unavailable_with_its_p0` (`None` plus the P0 `state-corrupt` finding) → `unsafe`; `lock_unavailable_alone` (`None`, no finding: the defensive case) → `findings`, never `ok`.
  - `health_line_cases` (exact strings): `ok_no_last_run`; `findings_two_severities` (only non-zero severities, P0–P3 order); `unsafe_with_p0_and_p3`; `with_last_run` (the RFC 3339 time and the id); the line ends with exactly one `\n` and contains no tab.
  - `latest_resolution_cases` on a tempdir: `missing`; `valid` (`runs/<id>` to a directory) → that id and its time; `dangling`; `parent_escape` (`../x`); `absolute_target`; `regular_file_latest`; `not_a_run_id` (`runs/junk`); `run_is_a_file` → `None` except `valid`.
  - `exit_cases`: `ok` → `Exit::Healthy`; each of the other three → `Exit::FindingsPresent`; `error()` is `None` in all four.
  - `health_report_key_order`: the serialized keys are exactly `status, findings, by_severity, last_run, run_id`.
- **`src/doctor/runtime.rs`:** `detect_matches_runtime_diagnose` (a synthetic registry slice of a cached, a quick and a default row and one panicking row: identical findings and skips through `detect` and through `Runtime::diagnose` on a tempdir home); `detect_writes_nothing` (the tempdir's `tree_hash` before and after); `timings_name_every_detector_in_run_order`; `run_id_started_at_cases` (`2026-10-30T18-02-11Z__<ulid>` → `2026-10-30T18:02:11Z`).

### Integration and end-to-end tests

- `tests/contract/matrix.rs::doctor_health`: on a fresh `Scene`, `doctor health` → 0, `support::check` in doctor mode, snapshot `doctor_health_ok`; `doctor health -t nosuch` → 66, `error.code: target_not_found`, snapshot `doctor_health_unknown_target`.
- `tests/contract/special.rs::read_only_commands_ignore_dry_run_and_reason`: the new invocation; `--dry-run --reason x` changes neither the envelope nor `<state>`.
- `tests/cli_skeleton.rs::help_walks_a_nested_path`: `help doctor health` equals `doctor health --help`.
- The end-to-end scenarios (`health_*` in `tests/doctor.rs`) and the perf budget are s5's.

### Logging

- Unit tests are table-driven; each assertion message names the case and shows the input (findings by severity, the lock state, the link target) and the output.
- The contract rows log through the contract harness; a failing snapshot shows its diff. The `TestLog` scenarios of this surface are s5's.

## Considerations

- **Hot spots:** `src/app/mod.rs` (A1 first; each command leaf adds its own rows and rebases; s2 adds rows too, so the second to land rebases); `src/doctor/runtime.rs` (E3's; E6, E7 and E8 extend it: keep the extraction behaviour-neutral and rebase); `tests/contract/matrix.rs` (append a function, one snapshot file per row); `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` (regenerate after rebasing, never merge by hand); `omarchy/Model.js` (one `CLI_PATHS` row; the widget's asset digest changes, which is expected); `README.md` (this section only).
- **A deadline flake:** in debug builds the quick deadline is 100 ms (×20), so the gate's small homes have a wide margin; tests of the cut-short case use the sleep failpoint and are exact.
- **`health` is a fallback fix:** E10 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.10`) points the doctor tree's `internal` fix at `omaddons doctor health`, so it must answer on a damaged home; every layer it reads is tolerant and a failure is a finding.
- **Risk #3** (false positives) and **#4** (`status` speed): `health` relays the same detectors on the same tiers; its budgets are measured in s5.
- **Privacy:** no `WTF/` read; findings carry no file content; the line names no account, realm or character.

## Dependencies

- Parent: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4. No sibling before it; s2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4.2`, `doctor ls`) can be worked at the same time.
- After it: s3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4.3`, `doctor capabilities` and `robot-docs`), whose handbook runs `doctor health` in its "Healthy" example; s5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4.5`), which tests it end to end and measures it.
- Built on E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, the runtime, envelope and dictionary), E2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.2`, the view), E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`, `failure_modes()`), A1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1`, the `COMMANDS` fields) and B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`, the skill regeneration), all on `main` before E4 starts.
