comments.text: **Common rules.** The rules every M4 leaf and subtask follows, cited in this bead as "common rule N", are in the pinned docs bead `omad-bxb1` (`br show omad-bxb1`). Read them once per session, not once per bead.

title: `omaddons doctor ls`: the run directories newest first, with kinds, states and aborted runs
description:
Part 2 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4 (`doctor health`, `ls`, `--robot-triage`, `capabilities` and `robot-docs`). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

The leaf E4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4`) adds the doctor contract's read-only verbs on top of the doctor that E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, `doctor diagnose` and `explain`) and E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`, `doctor fix`) built, so scripts and agents can use the doctor without parsing a full report or reading README (vision G7, the doctor contract; G4, agent ergonomics).

**This part ships `omaddons doctor ls [--limit N]`**: the run directories under `<state>/doctor/runs/`, newest first, each with its kind (`diagnose`, `fix`, `undo`), state, exit code, action count and transaction, including runs that were killed before they wrote a report, plus every DEC-1 registry touch point of the path in one commit. A postmortem, an undo and `doctor gc` all start by finding a run, and M4-D33 gives every diagnose, fix and undo its own directory. It is its own step because a command's touch points must land together (DEC-1), and it touches different modules from s1 (`doctor health`), so the two can be worked at the same time.

**What is true when this part starts** (verified at `c0ab5e9`, plus what the blockers land):

- E3 has landed: the run directory `<state>/doctor/runs/<YYYY-MM-DDTHH-MM-SSZ>__<ULID>/` (`DoctorRunId`, whose string order is start time then ULID), published by renaming a staged `.<id>.tmp`; `report.json` = the stdout envelope without `meta`, with `kind` (`diagnose`, `fix`, `undo`) after `command`, hardened 0400 at the terminal state; `runtime.jsonl`; a run killed after publication has no `report.json`; `RunState` (`DONE_OK`, `DONE_FINDINGS`; E6 adds `DONE_PARTIAL`, `DONE_FAILED`, `REFUSING`, `LOCK_LOST`; E6's bead says `ABORTED` is what `ls` reports and the runtime never writes); `RunKind`; `doctor::budget::{Budget, Listing, list_dir, walk}` (the walker visits names in sorted **ascending** order, charges one entry per name, stops at its bound with `complete: false`, never follows a symlink); `DOCTOR_SCAN_MAX_ENTRIES` (20,000); E3's bound for reading a report, `API_RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES` (64 MiB, `src/limits.rs:85`); `support::stable()` redacting run ids to `<run>`; the rule-test exception for the doctor contract's names keyed by type (`RunState`, `Severity`).
- E6 has landed: a fix run's `report.json` has `tx` (the repair's transaction, `null` for a dry run) and `summary.actions_taken`; only a repair session writes `<run>/actions.jsonl` (one line per primitive).
- E12 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.12`, target-less history lines) has landed: `HistoryEntry.doctor_run_id` names the run directory of a `repair` line and of an `undo` line that reverts a repair.
- `history::read(paths, &HistoryFilter)` (`src/state/history.rs:442`) returns the entries and a skipped-line count whose warning `history` passes on (`src/app/history.rs:360`).
- **The precedent:** `history`'s `DEFAULT_LIMIT = 20` (`src/app/history.rs:26-27`, a module constant, not a `limits.rs` row), `--limit 0` → `usage` "--limit must be at least 1" with the fix `omaddons history --limit 20` (`history.rs:245-252`), and `data.truncated` (`history.rs:50-52`).
- **Not edges:** E7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7`, undo of repairs) provides `undo_state(entries, at) -> UndoState { InEffect, UndoneBy(TxId) }` and undo runs whose `report.json` holds `reverted_run`, `tx` (the reverted repair), `undo_tx` (the undo's own transaction), `actions_taken` and `state`; its bead says whichever of E4 and E7 lands second wires `undo_complete` and `reverted_run`. E8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.8`, `doctor gc`) plans a module `src/doctor/runs.rs` over the same directories: `RunEntry { id, dir, staged }`, `RunListing { runs, complete }` (sorted by id), `list_runs(paths, budget)`, `RunSummary { kind, state, tx, undo_tx }`, `read_summary(dir) -> Option<RunSummary>` (bounded, tolerant; `None` for an absent, oversized, undecodable or newer-major report), `has_actions_log(dir)`, and `Budget::entries_only(max)` if E3 has none.
- The registry tables: `tests/contract/special.rs:317-338`; `tests/cli_skeleton.rs:216-224`; `omarchy/Model.js:133-178` (`CLI_PATHS`); `tests/contract/matrix.rs`; `app::COMMANDS` through A1's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1`) `entry(…).doctor()`.

**The decisions that shape it:**
- **M4-D33:** every diagnose, fix and undo of a repair makes a run directory; `ls` does not. The run id is the UTC start time, `__`, a fresh ULID, so names sort by start time.
- **M4-D32:** the run directory holds `report.json` (`kind: diagnose | fix | undo`), `actions.jsonl` (the repair's primitives only), `runtime.jsonl`, `backups/`, `quarantine/` and `undo.sh`.
- **M4-D46:** a repair is undone by `omaddons undo` or `doctor undo` as a new repair transaction whose run is of kind `undo` and names `reverted_run`; `ls` reports `undo_complete`.
- **M4-D34:** the report sits at the top level of the doctor envelope; a findings-free listing is exit 0 with no `error`.
- **Common rule 15 (bounded work):** a listing of a user-sized directory is bounded by a named constant and reports truncation, never a clean result.
- **§8.1:** prefer existing codes and keys; fail closed on anything persisted that cannot be fully read.

## Technical Approach

### 1. The command and its registry touch points (DEC-1, all in this commit)

1. **clap:** `DoctorAction::Ls(LsArgs)` with `LsArgs { #[arg(long, value_name = "N")] limit: Option<usize> }`, doc comment "List the doctor's runs, newest first".
2. **`COMMANDS` row:** `entry("doctor ls", Group::Look, false, &[0, 64, 74], data_schema::<LsReport>, Network::None).doctor()`, after the other doctor rows.
3. **`command_name`:** `Some(DoctorAction::Ls(_))` → `"doctor ls"`; the dispatch arm calls `doctor::runs::ls(ctx, args)` and emits through `emit_doctor`.
4. **Help layout:** no bare-help change; `help doctor` lists it.
5. **Contract matrix** (`#[test] fn doctor_ls()`): after one `doctor` run on a fresh `Scene`, `doctor ls` → 0, snapshot `doctor_ls_ok` (run ids redacted to `<run>` by `stable()`); `doctor ls --limit 0` → 64, `usage`, snapshot `doctor_ls_limit_zero`.
6. **`special.rs`:** `"doctor ls" => &["doctor", "ls"]`.
7. **`cli_skeleton`:** `&["doctor", "ls"]` in `help_walks_a_nested_path`.
8. **`CLI_PATHS`:** `"doctor ls": { "mutates": false, "destructive": false, "binds": false }`.
9. **README:** a `### \`doctor ls\`` section.

`-t` is accepted and ignored (decided while writing this bead: a run belongs to no single client, and other target-less commands ignore `-t` the same way).

### 2. `src/doctor/runs.rs`, shared with E8

Decided while writing this bead: whichever of E4 and E8 lands first creates the module with E8's names and semantics above; the second extends it without changing a caller's behaviour. This part needs, in addition:

```rust
pub enum Order { Ascending, Descending }
pub fn list_runs_in(paths: &Paths, budget: &mut Budget, order: Order) -> io::Result<RunListing>; // list_runs = Ascending
pub struct RunSummary {            // E8's four fields, plus:
    pub kind: Option<RunKind>, pub state: String, pub tx: Option<TxId>, pub undo_tx: Option<TxId>,
    pub exit_code: Option<u8>, pub view: Option<String>, pub summary_ok: Option<bool>,
    pub actions_taken: Option<u64>, pub reverted_run: Option<DoctorRunId>,
}
pub fn count_action_lines(dir: &Path) -> u64;  // complete lines of <dir>/actions.jsonl; reads at most
                                               // API_RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES (a repair plans at most
                                               // DOCTOR_FIX_MAX_ACTIONS = 1,000 primitives)
```

- **The bounded, newest-first listing.** `list_runs_in` lists `<state>/doctor/runs/` with one level of E3's walker in the given order. Add the order to E3's one-level lister (`budget::list_dir_in(dir, budget, Order)`; `list_dir` stays ascending for every other caller), so the walker visits names in descending order when asked and stops at the budget with `complete: false`. The budget is entries-only, `DOCTOR_SCAN_MAX_ENTRIES` (`Budget::entries_only(max)`, added by whichever of E4 and E8 needs it first): a listing must not depend on timing. Decided while writing this bead: with ascending order a home past the bound would list its oldest runs, the wrong ones for `ls`. A name that parses as `DoctorRunId` and is a directory (`symlink_metadata`, never followed) is a run; `.<id>.tmp` is a staged run (listed by E8, skipped by `ls`); `latest`, other names, and symlinks or regular files named like a run are skipped and never followed. A missing runs directory is an empty, complete listing; an unreadable one is the `io` error with `details.path`.
- **`read_summary`** reads `<dir>/report.json` with at most `API_RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES` bytes (E3's bound for reading a report) and decodes it tolerantly into `{schema_version, kind, exit_code, view?, state?, summary?: {ok?, actions_taken?}, tx?, undo_tx?, reverted_run?, actions_taken?}`, ignoring unknown keys. It returns `None` for an absent, unreadable or oversized file, one that does not decode, a newer major `schema_version`, or (for `ls`'s use) a `state` value this build does not know.

### 3. `ls` (in `src/doctor/runs.rs` or `src/app/doctor.rs`)

1. **`--limit`:** `DEFAULT_LIMIT = 20`, a module constant beside the command (decided while writing this bead: a presentation default, as `history`'s; not a safety limit, so no `limits.rs` row). `--limit 0` is `usage` "--limit must be at least 1" with `Suggestion::command(["omaddons", "doctor", "ls", "--limit", "20"])`, exit 64, raised before anything is read. A non-number is clap's usage error (64).
2. **List** with `Order::Descending`; keep the first `limit` runs (staged entries skipped). `truncated` = more runs were listed than `limit`, or the listing stopped at its bound (decided while writing this bead: an additive key, as `history` has, because a cut listing must say so).
3. **Each kept run:**
   1. `read_summary(dir)`.
   2. **With a readable terminal report:** `kind` from it; `state` = its `state`, or for a triage report (`view: "triage"`, which has no `state`) `DONE_OK` when `summary.ok` is true, else `DONE_FINDINGS`; `exit_code` from it; `action_count` = `summary.actions_taken` (fix), `actions_taken` (undo), else 0; `tx` = the transaction the run committed: a fix report's `tx` (`null` for a dry run), an undo report's `undo_tx`, else `null`; `reverted_run` from an undo report, else `null`.
   3. **Without one:** `state: "ABORTED"`, `exit_code: null` (decided while writing this bead: a killed run has no exit code); `kind` and `tx` from the history line whose `doctor_run_id` equals the run (`repair` → `fix`, `undo` → `undo`, its `tx`); with no such line, `fix` when `has_actions_log(dir)`, else `diagnose` (decided while writing this bead: only a repair session writes `actions.jsonl`; an undo killed before its commit also has one and reads as `fix`, acceptable for a listing and never an input to `doctor undo`); `action_count` = `count_action_lines(dir)` (0 without the file; a torn last line is not counted); `reverted_run: null`.
   4. **`started_at`** = the run id's timestamp (whole seconds, UTC; `DoctorRunId::started_at() -> Timestamp`, the id's prefix parsed as UTC, added by whichever of s1 and this part lands first if E3 has none; decided while writing this bead: it exists for every run, killed ones included, and one source keeps the column uniform).
   5. **`undo_complete`:** for a fix run with a `tx`, `true` when E7's `undo_state(entries, tx's at)` is `UndoneBy(_)`; `false` otherwise and for every other kind. If E7 is not on `main` yet, `false` for every run, and E7's commit wires it (whichever lands second).
4. **History** is read once, `history::read(paths, &HistoryFilter::default())`, only when a kept run lacks a readable report or `undo_state` is needed (a fix run with a `tx`, once E7 has landed). Its skipped-line warning (`history_lines_skipped`) is passed on in `warnings`. A history that cannot be read at all is treated as empty for these two uses, its error turned into the reader's warning where one exists (decided while writing this bead: the listing must still answer, and nothing acts on it).
5. **The state type.** `ListedState` in `src/doctor/report.rs`: every `RunState` value plus `Aborted`, `#[serde(rename_all = "SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE")]` (wire `ABORTED`, the doctor contract's spelling), `From<RunState>`. Decided while writing this bead: `ABORTED` is not added to `RunState`, which is `doctor diagnose`'s and `doctor fix`'s `state` schema and is never `ABORTED`; a unit test holds every `RunState` mapped to the `ListedState` of the same wire name.

### 4. Output

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Serialize, JsonSchema)]
pub struct LsReport { pub runs: Vec<ListedRun>, pub truncated: bool }
#[derive(Debug, Serialize, JsonSchema)]
pub struct ListedRun {
    pub run_id: DoctorRunId, pub kind: RunKind, pub started_at: Timestamp, pub state: ListedState,
    pub exit_code: Option<u8>, pub action_count: u64, pub tx: Option<TxId>,
    pub reverted_run: Option<DoctorRunId>, pub undo_complete: bool,
}
```

```json
{"ok":true,"schema_version":"1.0","tool_version":"0.1.0","command":"doctor ls","exit_code":0,
 "runs":[{"run_id":"2026-10-30T18-03-40Z__01M8S…","kind":"fix","started_at":"2026-10-30T18:03:40Z","state":"DONE_OK",
          "exit_code":0,"action_count":1,"tx":"01M9…","reverted_run":null,"undo_complete":false}],
 "truncated":false,"warnings":[],"commands":[],"meta":{"elapsed_ms":4,"offline":false}}
```

Runs newest first; `commands: []` (decided while writing this bead: token-frugal; each fix report carries its own undo command). Nothing is volatile. Human form: an `output::table` with columns `RUN`, `KIND`, `STATE`, `EXIT` (`-` for `null`), `ACTIONS`, `TX` (`-`), `NOTE` (`undone` when `undo_complete`; `reverts <run>` for an undo run), then `(older runs: --limit N)` when `truncated`; `no doctor runs yet` for an empty listing. Exit 0 whatever the runs' states (a listing is not a diagnosis).

**What it never does:** write anything, take the lock, follow a symlink in the runs directory, or act on a run.

### 5. The contract

- New wire names (close comment): the path `doctor ls`; the flag `--limit` on it; `runs[]` with `run_id`, `kind`, `started_at`, `state`, `exit_code`, `action_count`, `tx`, `reverted_run`, `undo_complete`; `truncated`; the state value `ABORTED`.
- Naming rules (M4-D55): `action_count` is a count that is not a bare noun, the doctor contract's name; `ListedState`'s values are the doctor contract's uppercase names. Decided while writing this bead: both join E3's doctor-contract exception in A3's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`) rule test (`ListedRun.action_count` by field, `ListedState` by type, beside `RunState`), with the reason "the doctor contract's names (M4-D34)"; never an allowlist line. Whichever of A3 and this part lands second adds them.
- No volatile key, no new code, warning, action, env var, failpoint or constant. Not a mutating path (common rule 16; say so in the close comment).
- README `### \`doctor ls\``: `--limit` (default 20), the columns and keys, newest first, what `ABORTED` means (no terminal report this build can read: killed, still running, damaged, or written by a newer omaddons), `truncated`, and that it writes nothing. Regenerate `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` (`OMADDONS_UPDATE_SKILL=1 cargo test --test skill`); re-accept A4's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`) `capabilities_ok_digest` if A4 has landed.

**Files:** `src/doctor/runs.rs` (new or extended), `src/doctor/budget.rs` (the order parameter, `entries_only` if missing), `src/doctor/report.rs` (`ListedState`), `src/doctor/mod.rs`, `src/app/doctor.rs`, `src/app/mod.rs`, `tests/contract/matrix.rs` and two snapshots, `tests/contract/special.rs`, `tests/cli_skeleton.rs`, `omarchy/Model.js`, `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md`, `README.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `omaddons doctor ls` lists the run directories newest first, at most `--limit` (default 20), each with `run_id`, `kind`, `started_at`, `state`, `exit_code`, `action_count`, `tx`, `reverted_run` and `undo_complete`, plus `truncated`; it exits 0.
- [ ] `--limit 0` is `usage` (exit 64) with `fix_argv` `["omaddons", "doctor", "ls", "--limit", "20"]`.
- [ ] The listing goes newest first through E3's walker with an entries-only `DOCTOR_SCAN_MAX_ENTRIES` budget, so a cut listing keeps the newest runs and sets `truncated`; every other caller of the walker keeps ascending order.
- [ ] A run without a readable terminal report (missing, oversized, undecodable, newer major, unknown state) is `ABORTED` with `exit_code: null`, its kind and transaction from history or from `actions.jsonl`; a triage report's state comes from `summary.ok`; `started_at` always comes from the run id.
- [ ] Staged `.<id>.tmp` directories, `latest`, foreign names and symlinks or files named like a run are never listed or followed.
- [ ] `undo_complete` and `reverted_run` are wired to E7's `undo_state` and undo reports if E7 is on `main`; otherwise they are `false`/`null` and the close comment names E7 as the one to wire them.
- [ ] `ListedState` covers every `RunState` plus `ABORTED`, and `RunState` is unchanged.
- [ ] `src/doctor/runs.rs` keeps every name and semantic E8's bead defines, whichever lands first.
- [ ] DEC-1 in this commit: the clap variant, the `COMMANDS` row with every M4 field, `command_name` and dispatch, no bare-help change, the matrix rows `doctor_ls_ok` and `doctor_ls_limit_zero` (snapshotted, doctor mode), the `special.rs` invocation, the `cli_skeleton` literal, the `CLI_PATHS` row and README's section.
- [ ] `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` is regenerated and `tests/skill.rs` passes; the naming exceptions are keyed with their reason (once A3 has landed), with no allowlist line.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes and `ubs` is clean; the close comment lists the wire names and each "Decided while writing this bead" item.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

- **`src/doctor/budget.rs`:** `descending_one_level_listing` (names `a`…`e`, descending → `e`…`a`); `descending_listing_keeps_the_newest_under_a_bound` (five run directories with ascending ids, `entries_only(3)` → the three newest, `complete: false`); `ascending_listing_is_unchanged` (the existing order and bound behaviour of `list_dir`).
- **`src/doctor/runs.rs`** (tempdir runs directories; table-driven, one name per case):
  - `entry_from_report_cases`: `full_diagnose` (state `DONE_FINDINGS`, exit 1, count 0, tx `null`); `triage_ok` (`view: triage`, `summary.ok: true` → `DONE_OK`); `triage_findings` (→ `DONE_FINDINGS`); `fix_committed` (tx, `summary.actions_taken: 3` → count 3); `fix_dry_run` (`tx: null`); `undo_run` (`undo_tx` as `tx`, `reverted_run`, `actions_taken`); `newer_major` (`schema_version: "2.0"`) → `ABORTED`; `truncated_json` → `ABORTED`; `oversized` (under an injected 1 KiB bound) → `ABORTED`; `unknown_state` (`"DONE_LATER"`) → `ABORTED`; `missing_report` → `ABORTED`.
  - `aborted_kind_cases`: `history_repair_line` (a `repair` history line with the run's `doctor_run_id` → `fix`, its tx); `history_undo_line` → `undo`; `actions_log_only` (2 complete lines and a torn third → `fix`, count 2); `nothing` → `diagnose`, count 0.
  - `names_that_are_not_runs_are_skipped`: `.<id>.tmp`, `latest`, `junk`, a symlink named like a run, a regular file named like a run → none listed, none followed.
  - `limit_and_truncated_cases`: `one_of_three` → truncated; `three_of_three` → not; `five_limit_of_three` → not; `cut_listing` (bound 2, three runs, limit 20) → truncated.
  - `started_at_comes_from_the_run_id` (a report whose `started_at` differs: the id's time wins).
  - `undo_complete_cases` (when E7's `undo_state` is present: a repair undone → `true`; undone then redone → `false`; a diagnose → `false`; otherwise every run `false`).
  - `missing_runs_directory_is_empty`; `unreadable_runs_directory_is_io` (skipped as root, saying so).
- **`src/doctor/report.rs`:** `listed_state_covers_every_run_state` (each `RunState` maps to the `ListedState` of the same wire name; `ABORTED` is only in `ListedState`).
- **`src/app/doctor.rs`:** `ls_limit_zero_is_usage` (code `usage`, message "--limit must be at least 1", the `fix_argv`); `ls_report_key_order` (`runs, truncated`; each run's keys in the documented order).

### Integration and end-to-end tests

- `tests/contract/matrix.rs::doctor_ls`: `doctor` then `doctor ls` → 0, one run, snapshot `doctor_ls_ok`; `doctor ls --limit 0` → 64, snapshot `doctor_ls_limit_zero`.
- `tests/contract/special.rs`: the read-only invocation (two consecutive `ls` print the same envelope).
- `tests/cli_skeleton.rs::help_walks_a_nested_path`: `help doctor ls` equals `doctor ls --help`.
- The end-to-end scenarios (`ls_*` in `tests/doctor.rs`) are s5's.

### Logging

- Unit tests are table-driven; each assertion message names the case and shows the planted directory listing or report and the listed run.
- Contract rows log through the harness; a failing snapshot shows its diff. The `TestLog` scenarios are s5's.

## Considerations

- **Hot spots:** `src/app/mod.rs` (A1 first; rebase on s1's rows); `src/doctor/budget.rs` and `report.rs` (E3's; add the order parameter and `ListedState` without changing existing behaviour); `src/doctor/runs.rs` (shared with E8: keep its names; if E8 is in flight, coordinate through `SendMessage` before creating the file); matrix, `SKILL.md`, `Model.js`, README as in s1.
- **What could surprise:** a run still in DIAGNOSING has no report yet and lists as `ABORTED`; README says so, and `ls` never acts on it.
- **Bounds:** at most `--limit` reports are read, each at most 64 MiB, and the listing at most 20,000 names; history is read whole, as `history` reads it (its reader is the existing bounded-by-file one).
- **Privacy:** `ls` prints run ids and transaction ids only; no path, no account, realm or character.
- **Compatibility:** nothing is written, so an M3 build sees nothing new.

## Dependencies

- Parent: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4. No sibling before it; s1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4.1`, `doctor health`) can be worked at the same time.
- After it: s3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4.3`), whose handbook's undo flow runs `doctor ls`; s5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4.5`), which tests it end to end.
- Built on E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, run directories, `report.json`, the walker), E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`, fix reports), E12 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.12`, `doctor_run_id`), A1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1`) and B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`, the skill regeneration). Coordinates with E7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7`, `undo_state`) and E8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.8`, `runs.rs`), which are not edges.

title: `omaddons doctor capabilities` and `omaddons doctor robot-docs`: the doctor's generated description and its handbook
description:
Part 3 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4 (`doctor health`, `ls`, `--robot-triage`, `capabilities` and `robot-docs`). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says. ## Background The leaf E4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4`) adds the doctor contract's read-only verbs on top of the doctor that E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, `doctor diagnose` and `explain`) and E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`, `doctor fix`) built, so scripts and agents can use the doctor without parsing a full report or reading README (vision G7, the doctor contract; G4, agent ergonomics; G-M4-1, "every fact in those outputs is generated from the code, so it cannot drift"). **This part ships the doctor's self-description:** - `omaddons doctor capabilities`: the doctor contract's machine description (its detectors, fixers, manual remediations, exit codes, write scopes, allowed operations and costs), generated from the failure-mode registry and the fsx scope table, never hand-kept; - `omaddons doctor robot-docs`: the doctor's handbook for agents, rendered from a new template `src/contract/guide/doctor.md` by B1's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`) guide renderer, with the doctor's exit dictionary, examples of every flow, and the list of things it will never do. Both are one step because they describe the same surface from the same registries, the handbook points at `doctor capabilities --json`, and each path's DEC-1 touch points land in this commit. It comes after s1 (`doctor health`) and s2 (`doctor ls`) because the handbook's examples run those commands and a unit test parses every command the handbook shows. **What is true when this part starts** (verified at `c0ab5e9`, plus what the blockers land): - **E1/E3/E6's registry:** `doctor::registry::failure_modes()` (E6), the effective registry: in release builds exactly `FAILURE_MODES`; in debug builds with `OMADDONS_TEST_FIXERS=1` it appends `fm-test-write` (enabled, `writes_to: [state]`), `fm-test-quarantine` (`needs_force`, not enabled, writes to `state`, `config`, `cache`, `client_meta`) and `fm-test-flatten` (not enabled, `addons`), all tier `default`, P3; `failure_modes_with(test_fixers: bool)` for unit tests. Each `FailureMode` has `id, subsystem, severity, title, description, why, tier, online, cost_ms, requires, detect, fix, manual`; `FixerSpec` has `plan, writes_to, ops, enabled, needs_force, cardinality, preconditions`. Wire names: `Subsystem` (the thirteen; `applicable()` false only for `sockets` and `hooks`), `Tier` (`cached, quick, default, deep`, plus E3's `runtime`), `Layer`, `ScopeName` (`state, config, cache, client_meta, addons, skill`, with `ScopeName::scope()` giving the fsx `Scope` row), `Cardinality` (`low, high`), `FixerPrecondition` (`lock_held, inflight_free, client_not_running, online, same_fs`), `FixKind` (`write, chmod, quarantine, flatten, suspend, delegate`), the primitive ops (`write_file, chmod, rename_noreplace`). E3 added each row's static manual pair `{instruction, reason}` (what `doctor explain` prints) and the two runtime rows (tier `runtime`, no detector, `--only` refuses them as `usage`). - **E3's doctor:** `doctor::Exit::ALL` with `code()`, `name()`, `meaning()`; the doctor envelope and `DoctorOutcome`; `emit_doctor`; the contract harness's doctor mode; `DOCTOR_CONTRACT_VERSION` ("1.0"). - **E2's view:** the Registry layer (the registered targets and their client directories, tolerant) and the Skill layer (`Paths::skill_dir()` and B3's `history_tail.skill_dirs[]`); both read single files and write nothing. - **E6's planner:** `FixPlan::triage()` resolves each planned failure mode's `writes_to` scopes to paths (s4 renders it). - **B1's renderer** (`src/contract/guide/render.rs`): `render(template, &GuideInputs) -> Result`; `GuideInputs::live()` (from `app::COMMANDS` and clap, `Exit::ALL`, `doctor::Exit::ALL`, A2's env registry, `NEVER`, …) and the test helper `GuideInputs::sample()`; `PLACEHOLDERS` (twelve; each `Placeholder { name, kind: Block | Inline, render: fn(&GuideInputs) -> String }`); `{{commands}}` renders one list line per command path, `` - `path` — about `` plus ` (mutates)`, ` (stores plan)` or ` (mutates · stores plan)`; `{{exit_doctor}}` renders "Every `doctor` command uses its own exit dictionary:", a blank line and a `Code | Name | Meaning` table; `{{never}}` renders the eight `NEVER` items as a numbered list; a template without `{{stamp}}` renders without one; a tab or carriage return in a template is refused; the output ends with exactly one `\n`. `contract::guide::{TEMPLATE, render_guide}` in `src/contract/guide/mod.rs`. `robot_docs::{GuideData { format: DocFormat, content: String }, DocFormat::Markdown}`. B1's tests: a placeholder count of twelve, and "the skeleton holds every placeholder in place". - **Not edges:** A4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`, `capabilities`) provides `contract::commands::command(path) -> Option` with `args: Vec` and `flags: Vec`, and publishes `failure_modes.command` = `"omaddons doctor capabilities --json"` exactly when `doctor capabilities` is a `COMMANDS` row; its success snapshot `capabilities_ok_digest` lists every path. D1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1`) provides `crate::build_info::BUILD_ID`. A5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5`) owns `robot-docs schema […]` (a path as words or one argument, `num_args = 0..`). E7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7`) adds `doctor undo`; E8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.8`) `doctor gc`. - **Code at `c0ab5e9`:** the fsx scope table (`src/fsx/scope.rs:66-101`; the Config row is ``, the State row `` except the lock file, the Cache row ``, ClientMeta `/Interface/.omaddons/`, AddOns `/Interface/AddOns/`, Skill the skill dir); `Paths::skill_dir()` (`src/state/paths.rs:264-266`); `LOCK_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT` 5 s (`src/limits.rs:36`); help's builders `help::flags` (`src/app/help.rs:128-140`) and the positional `ArgInfo` loop (`help.rs:329-337`); `support::stable()` (`tests/contract/main.rs:306-316`) redacts no build id and no platform name. **The decisions that shape it:** - **M4-D2:** one contract registry feeds every description of the CLI, `doctor capabilities` included; a fact clap cannot give is declared once beside what it describes. *Rejected:* a hand-written capabilities file (it drifts); proc-macro attributes. - **M4-D3:** `doctor_contract_version` ("1.0") is the external doctor contract's revision; `tool_version` is the crate's; `schema_version` the wire contract's. - **M4-D34:** the report sits at the top level of the doctor envelope; no `data` key; so no report key may repeat an envelope key. - **M4-D7:** the guide is hand-written prose with generated, fixed-width blocks spliced in by a small renderer, no template engine; the `NEVER` table is shared with `doctor robot-docs`. *Rejected:* a fully generated or fully hand-written document. - **M4-D40:** the doctor dictionary of eleven codes, published by `capabilities`. - **M4-D4 (by analogy):** a capabilities endpoint is offline, scan-free and write-free. - **M4-D35, M4-D32:** a repair quarantines on the victim's own side: home-side victims under `/quarantine/`, client-side under `/snapshots/.repair/`, cache-side under `/quarantine//`; backups likewise. ## Technical Approach ### 1. `doctor capabilities`: the command (DEC-1, in this commit) 1. **clap:** `DoctorAction::Capabilities`, doc comment "What this doctor checks and repairs, as JSON for agents". 2. **`COMMANDS` row:** `entry("doctor capabilities", Group::Look, false, &[0, 64, 74], data_schema::, Network::None).doctor()`. 3. **`command_name`** `"doctor capabilities"`; the dispatch arm calls `doctor::capabilities::run(ctx)` and emits through `emit_doctor`. 4. **Help layout:** no bare-help change. 5. **Contract matrix** (`#[test] fn doctor_capabilities()`): `doctor capabilities` → 0, snapshot `doctor_capabilities_ok_digest` (section 3); `doctor capabilities --bogus` → 64, `usage`, snapshot `doctor_capabilities_unknown_flag`. 6. **`special.rs`:** `"doctor capabilities" => &["doctor", "capabilities"]`. 7. **`cli_skeleton`:** `&["doctor", "capabilities"]`. 8. **`CLI_PATHS`:** `"doctor capabilities": { "mutates": false, "destructive": false, "binds": false }`. 9. **README:** `### \`doctor capabilities\``. It reads the binary's registries plus, through E2's tolerant view, the Registry layer (registered clients) and the Skill layer (skill directories), and nothing else: no discovery scan, no request, no write (decided while writing this bead, by analogy with M4-D4). `-t` is accepted and ignored (the description is machine-wide). ### 2. The report (`src/doctor/capabilities.rs`, `DoctorCapabilities`, §6.11.1 in this key order) | Key | Value | Source | |---|---|---| | `tool` | `"omaddons"` | constant | | `build_id` | the execution build id, equal to `capabilities.build_id` | D1's `BUILD_ID`; absent while D1 has not landed, added by whichever of D1 and this part lands second | | `doctor_contract_version` | `"1.0"` | E3's constant | | `platform` | `{os, arch}` | `std::env::consts::{OS, ARCH}` | | `lock_timeout_seconds` | 5 | `LOCK_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT.as_secs()` | | `subsystems` | `[{name, applicable}]`, all thirteen, in `Subsystem::ALL` order | `Subsystem::ALL`, `applicable()` | | `allowed_ops` | `["write_file", "rename_noreplace", "chmod", "symlink_atomic", "create_dir"]` | `ALLOWED_OPS`: the primitive ops a repair may run, then the runtime's own (`symlink_atomic` for `latest`, `create_dir` for its roots) | | `verbs` | `[{path, about, mutates, binds, args, flags}]` | section 2.1 | | `detectors` | `[{id, subsystem, severity, description, tier, estimated_cost_ms, online_required, requires, depends_on}]` | every row of `failure_modes()`, in registry order; `estimated_cost_ms` = `cost_ms`; `online_required` = `online`; `requires` = the row's layers; `depends_on` always `[]` (checks depend on view layers, never on each other) | | `fixers` | `[{id, preconditions, writes_to, ops, reversible, idempotent, cardinality, enabled, needs_force, estimated_cost_ms}]` | every row with `fix: Some(spec)`, in registry order; `reversible` and `idempotent` `true` (every fixer M4 admits is both, proven per fixer by F9's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`) harness); `estimated_cost_ms` = the row's `cost_ms` (decided while writing this bead: `FixerSpec` declares no cost of its own) | | `manual_remediations` | `[{id, instruction, reason}]` | every row with E3's static manual pair, in registry order | | `exit_codes` | `{"0": "healthy", …, "74": "io_error"}` | `doctor::Exit::ALL` into `BTreeMap` (string order equals code order for these eleven) | | `env_vars` | `{"": ""}` | A2's `contract::env::release()`, release kind only, `BTreeMap` | | `write_scopes` | `[{scope, path}]` | section 2.2 | | `cost_summary` | `{quick_total_ms, default_total_ms, deep_total_ms, online_total_ms_estimate}` | section 2.3 | - **`tool_version` is not a report key** (decided while writing this bead): §6.11.1 lists it, but the envelope already carries `tool_version` at the top level (M4-D34), so a report key would be a duplicate JSON key. The envelope's value is the same `CARGO_PKG_VERSION`. - **`detectors` lists every failure-mode id exactly once**, the two runtime rows included with `tier: "runtime"`. In a release build, and in a debug build without `OMADDONS_TEST_FIXERS=1`, no `fm-test-` id appears. - **`ALLOWED_OPS`** is the one hand list; a unit test serializes one primitive of each kind of E1's primitive op enum and requires its `op` to be listed, so a new primitive fails until listed. #### 2.1 `verbs` (additive) Decided while writing this bead: §3.2 criterion 10 says every verb and flag of the doctor is "listed by `doctor capabilities --json`", and §6.11.1's shape has no such list, so `verbs` is added. One entry per `COMMANDS` row whose path is `doctor` or starts with `doctor `, in `COMMANDS` order: `path`; `about` (clap's); `mutates` (the row's); `binds` (`BINDING_COMMANDS` membership, so `--if-match` applies); `args` (each positional's value name, in index order); `flags` (the path's own long flag names without dashes, in declaration order; global flags left out, since every path has them). Built from A4's `contract::commands::command(path)` (`ArgInfo.value_name`, the `FlagInfo.long` of entries with `global: false`) when A4 is on `main`; otherwise from help's builders (`help::flags` and the positional loop, made `pub(crate)`), with the same output. E7's and E8's paths appear as their rows land. #### 2.2 `write_scopes` (`src/doctor/scopes.rs`) Generated (§6.11.1: "from `FAILURE_MODES` and the fsx scope table"): ```rust pub struct ScopeInputs<'a> { pub paths: &'a Paths, pub clients: &'a [PathBuf], pub skill_dirs: &'a [PathBuf] } pub fn roots(scope: ScopeName, inputs: &ScopeInputs) -> Vec; pub fn write_scopes(registry: &[FailureMode], inputs: &ScopeInputs) -> Vec; // {scope, path} ``` - **The scope set** is the union of: `state` always (the runtime's run directories and `latest`, and every repair's home-side backups and quarantine under `/`); every `writes_to` of every fixer in the registry; and the scopes a repair's own roots imply: `client_meta` whenever `addons` or `client_meta` is declared (client-side backups and quarantine live in `/snapshots/.repair/`), `cache` whenever `cache` is declared (`/quarantine//`). Decided while writing this bead: the doctor's NEVER list promises it "writes only inside `write_scopes`", so the list must include where its backups and quarantines go. - **`roots`**, through `ScopeName::scope()` and the scope table's roots: `state` → ``; `config` → ``; `cache` → ``; `client_meta` → each client's `/Interface/.omaddons`; `addons` → each client's `/Interface/AddOns`; `skill` → `` and every skill directory the Skill layer knows. Decided while writing this bead: `config` resolves to `` (the Config row's root), not §6.11.1's `/credentials`, because the list is generated from the scope table and F7's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.7`) credential-mode fixer chmods any configured credential file inside ``; the doctor still never writes `config.toml` (the NEVER list says so). - **Clients** come from the Registry layer's entries (their `client_dir`); an unreadable registry lists no client paths and the command still exits 0 (the doctor reports the registry itself). - E6's `FixPlan::triage()` must resolve `writes_to` through `roots`: if E6 resolved scopes inline, extract that code into `scopes::roots` so both call one function (common rule: one implementation). - Entries are sorted by scope (enum order), then path, without duplicates. Paths are absolute: this machine's. #### 2.3 `cost_summary` Sums of `cost_ms` over rows that have a detector (runtime rows count 0), cumulative (decided while writing this bead, so each figure is what one invocation runs): `quick_total_ms` = offline `cached` + `quick` (`--quick`, `health`); `default_total_ms` = that plus offline `default` (bare `doctor`); `deep_total_ms` = that plus offline `deep` (`--include-deep`); `online_total_ms_estimate` = every online row. #### 2.4 Human form About a dozen lines (decided while writing this bead): `omaddons doctor capabilities · contract 1.0 · linux/x86_64`; `lock timeout 5 s · ops write_file rename_noreplace chmod symlink_atomic create_dir`; `subsystems: 11 applicable; sockets, hooks not applicable`; `verbs: doctor, doctor diagnose, …`; `detectors: (cached , quick , default , deep , runtime 2)`; `fixers: ( enabled, need --force --yes, disabled)`; `manual remediations: `; the exit dictionary on one line (`0 healthy · 1 findings_present · …`); `write scopes: , , , clients` (each path under `-v`); `cost: quick ms · default ms · deep

ms · online ~ ms`; and `--json for the full description`. Placeholders here are for this text only; the output prints real paths. ### 3. The digest snapshot Decided while writing this bead (as A4 did for `capabilities`): the success matrix snapshot is a **digest**, because every F leaf that adds a failure mode would otherwise re-accept a large snapshot, and `build_id` and `platform.arch` vary by build and machine (`support::stable()` redacts neither): `{report_keys, tool, doctor_contract_version, lock_timeout_seconds, platform: {os, arch: ""}, build_id: "" (when present), subsystems, allowed_ops, exit_codes, verbs: [paths], counts: {detectors, fixers, manual_remediations, env_vars, write_scopes}, cost_summary_keys}`. The full report is validated live on every run by A3's strict validation through E3's doctor mode (whichever of A3 and this part lands second wires it). ### 4. `doctor robot-docs`: the command (DEC-1, in this commit) 1. **clap:** `DoctorAction::RobotDocs` (clap name `robot-docs`), doc comment "The doctor's handbook for agents, as Markdown". 2. **`COMMANDS` row:** `entry("doctor robot-docs", Group::Look, false, &[0, 64, 74], data_schema::, Network::None).doctor()`. 3. **`command_name`** `"doctor robot-docs"`; dispatch calls `contract::guide::render_doctor()`; a `RenderError` becomes `Error::internal` (exit 74 through `exit_for`; a bug, never expected). 4. **Help layout:** no bare-help change. 5. **Contract matrix** (`#[test] fn doctor_robot_docs()`): `doctor robot-docs` → 0, snapshot `doctor_robot_docs_ok` with `content` replaced by `""` before snapshotting (decided while writing this bead, as B1 did for the guide: the content is pinned by the unit snapshot below, and a later leaf adding a command would otherwise re-accept a contract snapshot); `doctor robot-docs extra` → 64, `usage`, snapshot `doctor_robot_docs_extra_argument`. 6. **`special.rs`:** `"doctor robot-docs" => &["doctor", "robot-docs"]`. 7. **`cli_skeleton`:** `&["doctor", "robot-docs"]`. 8. **`CLI_PATHS`:** `"doctor robot-docs": { "mutates": false, "destructive": false, "binds": false }`. 9. **README:** `### \`doctor robot-docs\``. The outcome's report is B1's `GuideData { format: Markdown, content }` at the top level of the doctor envelope; the human form writes `content` byte for byte. ### 5. The handbook (`src/contract/guide/doctor.md`, `render.rs`, `mod.rs`) - `pub const DOCTOR_TEMPLATE: &str = include_str!("doctor.md");` and `pub fn render_doctor() -> Result { render(DOCTOR_TEMPLATE, &GuideInputs::live()) }` in `src/contract/guide/mod.rs`. The template has no frontmatter and no `{{stamp}}` (it is not a skill file and is never installed). Its output depends only on compiled-in data, so it is the same bytes on every machine and run. `doctor.md` is an embedded asset under the gate (common rule 1). - **One new block placeholder, `{{doctor_commands}}`** (decided while writing this bead: the surface must grow when E7 and E8 add verbs, without anyone editing the handbook): `{{commands}}`'s lines restricted to paths that are `doctor` or start with `doctor `, in `COMMANDS` order, in the same line format; one `Placeholder` row in `PLACEHOLDERS`. B1's count test becomes thirteen, and its "every placeholder in place" test accepts a placeholder that appears in either template (`guide.md` does not use this one). `guide.md` is not edited, so `SKILL.md` does not change because of this row. - **The sections, in order** (§6.11.2): 1. `# The omaddons doctor: a handbook for agents`, then four lines: what it checks (omaddons' own state, managed folders, caches, the widget, the skill, credentials); bare `doctor` changes nothing but its own run record; `doctor fix` repairs with consent, backs up verbatim, never deletes, and is undoable; `omaddons doctor capabilities --json` is the machine description. 2. `## Surface`: `{{doctor_commands}}`, then a short paragraph on diagnose's and fix's selection flags (`--only`, `--skip`, `--severity`, `--quick`, `--include-deep`, `--online`, `--budget`, `-t`) and `--since`. 3. `## EXIT CODES`: `{{exit_doctor}}`. 4. `## Schemas`: a fenced `omaddons robot-docs schema "doctor diagnose"`, and the sentence that any path of the surface above can replace the quoted one. 5. `## Examples`, five subsections, each a fenced `sh` block whose lines starting `omaddons ` are commands and whose `# ` lines show abbreviated output: `### Healthy` (`omaddons doctor health` → `ok …`, exit 0; `omaddons doctor --json` → `DONE_OK`); `### Findings present` (`omaddons doctor --json` → exit 1, `DONE_FINDINGS`, a finding's id, instance, severity, evidence and remediation argv); `### The fix flow` (`omaddons doctor fix --only --dry-run --json` → `actions_planned`, `precondition`; then `omaddons doctor fix --only --if-match --json` → `DONE_OK`, `tx`, `undo_argv`); `### The undo flow` (`omaddons doctor ls --json`, `omaddons doctor undo --dry-run --json`, `omaddons doctor undo --json`, or `omaddons undo --last-by agent --json`); `### The explain flow` (`omaddons doctor explain --json`, `omaddons doctor explain -t --json`). 6. `## capabilities`: `omaddons doctor capabilities --json` and what it lists (every detector, fixer and manual remediation, the eleven exit codes, `write_scopes`, `allowed_ops`, `cost_summary`, `verbs`). 7. `## Things this doctor will NEVER do` (the doctor contract's negative space, adapted; ten numbered items): never deletes during diagnose, fix or undo (it moves what it removes into a quarantine on the same filesystem; only `omaddons doctor gc --before --yes` deletes, and never what an unfinished transaction needs); runs no shell command, destructive or not; writes only inside `write_scopes`; never writes `WTF/`, `config.toml`, `addons.toml` or a SavedVariables file; makes no request without `--online`; never changes anything while another omaddons holds the lock past 5 s (it waits that long, then exits 5); never overwrites a file without a verbatim backup checked byte for byte; never rewrites `history.jsonl`; never reports a check it did not finish as passed (a cut-short check is a `check-incomplete` finding); emits no prompt and no ANSI under `--json`. 8. `## Things omaddons will NEVER do`: `{{never}}` (B1's shared eight). Decided while writing this bead: the plan's E4 entry says "with the shared `NEVER` table" and §6.11.2 lists ten doctor-specific items; the handbook renders both, the doctor's first. 9. s4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4.4`) adds `## The agent loop` after `## Surface`. - **The undo flow exists only with `doctor undo`.** `every_present_doctor_flow_has_its_example` requires `### The fix flow`, `### The undo flow` and `### The explain flow` exactly for the paths `doctor fix`, `doctor undo` and `doctor explain` present in `COMMANDS`, so if E7 lands after this part, its commit adds the undo flow, told by the test's message ("add the undo flow to src/contract/guide/doctor.md"). The gc clause of item 7 is an upper bound on what deletes, true before and after E8 lands. - **Size budget** (decided while writing this bead; a test budget, not a constant): under 300 lines and 20 KiB. - **Placeholders in commands:** fenced commands use ``, ``, ``, ``, `` for values; the parse test substitutes sample values (a registered id, a run id, `retail`, a `pc1:` token) before parsing. ### 6. The contract - New wire names (close comment): the paths `doctor capabilities` and `doctor robot-docs`; every key of section 2 (`tool`, `build_id`, `doctor_contract_version`, `platform.{os, arch}`, `lock_timeout_seconds`, `subsystems[].{name, applicable}`, `allowed_ops`, `verbs[].{path, about, mutates, binds, args, flags}`, `detectors[].{id, subsystem, severity, description, tier, estimated_cost_ms, online_required, requires, depends_on}`, `fixers[].{id, preconditions, writes_to, ops, reversible, idempotent, cardinality, enabled, needs_force, estimated_cost_ms}`, `manual_remediations[].{id, instruction, reason}`, `exit_codes`, `env_vars`, `write_scopes[].{scope, path}`, `cost_summary.{quick_total_ms, default_total_ms, deep_total_ms, online_total_ms_estimate}`); `format` and `content` on `doctor robot-docs`; the placeholder `{{doctor_commands}}` (internal). - Naming rules (M4-D55): `lock_timeout_seconds` and `online_total_ms_estimate` (durations without a `_ms`/`_s` suffix), `writes_to` and `depends_on` (arrays without a plural noun) are the doctor contract's names. comments.text: **Common rules.** The rules every M4 leaf and subtask follows, cited in this bead as "common rule N", are in the pinned docs bead `omad-bxb1` (`br show omad-bxb1`). Read them once per session, not once per bead.

title: `omaddons doctor --robot-triage`: the triage view, with the planner's actions and the command to run next
description:
Part 4 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4 (`doctor health`, `ls`, `--robot-triage`, `capabilities` and `robot-docs`). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

The leaf E4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4`) adds the doctor contract's read-only verbs on top of the doctor that E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, `doctor diagnose` and `explain`) and E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`, `doctor fix`) built, so scripts and agents can use the doctor without parsing a full report or reading README (vision G7, the doctor contract; G4, "the first command an agent guesses works").

**This part ships `omaddons doctor --robot-triage`** (also `doctor diagnose --robot-triage`): the doctor contract's `triage` view of a diagnose, for agents. One call returns the findings, the repairs `doctor fix` would make (`actions_planned`, from E6's planner), and the exact command to run next (`recommended_command`/`recommended_argv`), plus pointers to `doctor capabilities` and `doctor robot-docs`. With it, an agent's whole doctor loop is "triage, then run what it recommends". It also adds that loop to the doctor's handbook. It is its own step because it is a report variant of an existing path, not a new path, with its own matrix rows; it comes after s3 because its report names `omaddons doctor capabilities --json` and `omaddons doctor robot-docs`, which must be real commands, and it edits the handbook s3 creates. The plan keeps the flag and its view in one leaf: E3 added every other diagnose flag but not this one, because a flag with no view behind it would be a stub (DEC-1), and the view needs E6's planner (the edge E6 → E4: "`--robot-triage` reports `actions_planned`, which is fix planning").

**What is true when this part starts** (the blockers' interfaces, plus s3):

- **E3:** `DiagnoseArgs` (flattened on `DoctorArgs`, so the flag works on bare `doctor`) with `--only`, `--skip`, `--severity`, `--quick`, `--include-deep`, `--online`, `--budget`, `--since`; the runtime: STARTING (a run directory), DIAGNOSING (`detect` over the selection, or `Runtime::diagnose`), the terminal writes (`report.json` = the stdout envelope without `meta`, with `kind: "diagnose"`; `latest`; hardening); `DiagnoseReport`, `#[serde(tag = "view")]`, with the one variant `full` (`FullReport`: `doctor_contract_version, run_id, run_dir, started_at, finished_at, state, summary, findings, skipped, since?, next_steps`); `Summary` with `total_findings`, `auto_fixable`, `needs_force`, `manual` (= total − auto_fixable − needs_force); findings ordered by (severity, id, instance key), each with `remediation {command, argv, explain_command, explain_argv, auto_fixable, needs_force, estimated_actions, destructive}`; the doctor envelope and `emit_doctor`; the contract harness's doctor mode (which checks `next_steps == commands[].command` only when a report has `next_steps`).
- **E6:** `doctor::plan_fix(view: &DoctorView, findings: &[Finding], opts: &FixOptions) -> Result<FixPlan, PlanRefusal>`, pure (no write, no lock, no request, no transaction); `FixOptions { only: &[OnlyEntry], force: bool, roots: &RepairRoots }`; `doctor diff`'s `<run>` placeholder `RepairRoots` (no run directory); without `--only`, the plan holds every finding whose fixer is enabled, needs no force and whose instance is fixable; `--only` naming a `needs_force` mode with a finding and no `--force` is `PlanRefusal` with `doctor_refused`/`force_required` and the fix `omaddons doctor explain <fm> [-t <id>]`; other refusals (`fixer_conflict`, `too_many_actions`, `filesystem_mismatch`, `client_running`, `not_enabled`, `edited_locally`) carry their own fixes; an unlistable journal directory ends planning with an `io` error; `FixPlan::triage() -> Vec<TriageAction { fixer_id, writes_to: Vec<String>, estimated_bytes: u64 }>` (one per failure mode with planned fixes, `writes_to` resolved through s3's `doctor::scopes::roots`); `FixPlan::recommended_argv(…) -> Option<Vec<String>>` (`omaddons doctor fix --only <every planned fm, comma-joined> [-t …]`, `None` for an empty plan); the test fixers behind `OMADDONS_TEST_FIXERS=1` in debug builds (`fm-test-write`: enabled, auto-fixable, plants `<state>/doctor-test/*.write`; `fm-test-quarantine`: `needs_force`, not enabled, plants `*.quarantine`; `fm-test-flatten`: not enabled).
- **A2's actions** `doctor_fix` and `doctor_explain` (`destructive: false`), and `CommandHint::new(action, argv, destructive)` (`src/error.rs:442-466`; its `command` is `shell_words::join(argv)`).
- **s3:** `doctor capabilities` and `doctor robot-docs` exist; `src/contract/guide/doctor.md` exists with its sections.

**The decisions that shape it:**
- **M4-D33:** `doctor --robot-triage` creates a run directory like every diagnose; only the report differs.
- **M4-D34:** the report sits at the top level of the doctor envelope; findings (exit 1) are a report, not an error.
- **M4-D38, M4-D44:** a set-aside (forced) repair needs `--force --yes`, is never part of a default fix and needs someone who has read what it does; `doctor fix` binds with `--if-match`. So the triage never recommends `--force` or `--yes`.
- **M4-D11:** recommendation actions are a closed registry; a recommendation is `doctor_fix` or `doctor_explain`.
- **§6.11's one-schema rule:** `doctor diagnose` has two report shapes, so its schema is one `oneOf` tagged by `view` (`full`, `triage`), generated from the serde enum.
- **A.6:** the doctor contract's `capabilities_url` becomes `capabilities_command`, since omaddons has no URL to give.

## Technical Approach

### 1. The flag

`#[arg(long, conflicts_with = "since")] pub robot_triage: bool` on E3's `DiagnoseArgs`, doc "One call for agents: the findings, the repairs doctor fix would make, and the command to run next". `--robot-triage --since <run>` is a clap conflict, exit 64 (decided while writing this bead: the triage view has no `since` key, and a silently ignored flag would mislead). Every other selection flag combines with it. `doctor fix` takes no `--robot-triage`. No new `COMMANDS` row: the path is `doctor diagnose` (and bare `doctor`), whose `data` is `DiagnoseReport`, now with two variants.

### 2. The run

1. **It is a diagnose** (M4-D33): selection and refusals as E3 does them; STARTING; DIAGNOSING over the selection.
2. **Planning, read-only** (`src/doctor/triage.rs`), after DIAGNOSING and before the terminal writes: `plan_fix(&view, &diagnosis.findings, &FixOptions { only: <the run's --only entries>, force: false, roots: <doctor diff's placeholder roots> })`. It takes no lock, allocates no transaction, writes nothing, and is never journaled. With `force: false` a forced repair is never planned.
   - `Ok(plan)` → `actions_planned = plan.triage()`, the recommendation from `plan.recommended_argv(…)` (passing the run's `-t` when E6's signature takes it).
   - `Err(refusal)` (a `PlanRefusal`) → `actions_planned = []`; the recommendation is the refusal's `doctor_refused` fix argv when that fix is a command, else the first finding's explain argv.
   - Any other planning error (E6's unlisted journal directory, an `io`) → `actions_planned = []`, the recommendation from the findings, and the run is **not** failed (decided while writing this bead: the triage only reports, and the same directory failure is itself a finding of the journal detectors).
3. **The report** is built as `DiagnoseReport::Triage(TriageReport)`; the terminal writes are E3's, unchanged: `report.json` = this envelope without `meta`, with `kind: "diagnose"`; `latest` moves to it; the record files are hardened.

### 3. The report (`src/doctor/report.rs` and `triage.rs`)

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Serialize, JsonSchema)]
#[serde(tag = "view")]
pub enum DiagnoseReport {
    #[serde(rename = "full")] Full(FullReport),     // E3's
    #[serde(rename = "triage")] Triage(TriageReport),
}
#[derive(Debug, Serialize, JsonSchema)]
pub struct TriageReport {
    pub summary: TriageSummary,                // {ok, total_findings, auto_fixable}
    pub quick_ref: Vec<String>,                // display strings
    pub findings: Vec<Finding>,                // the full view's objects, same order
    pub actions_planned: Vec<TriageAction>,    // E6's
    pub recommended_command: Option<String>,
    pub recommended_argv: Option<Vec<String>>,
    pub capabilities_command: &'static str,    // "omaddons doctor capabilities --json"
    pub robot_docs_command: &'static str,      // "omaddons doctor robot-docs"
}
```

```json
{"ok":false,"schema_version":"1.0","tool_version":"0.1.0","command":"doctor diagnose","exit_code":1,
 "view":"triage","summary":{"ok":false,"total_findings":2,"auto_fixable":1},
 "quick_ref":["P0: 1 finding (1 needs --force --yes)","P3: 1 finding (1 auto-fixable)"],
 "findings":["…the full view's finding objects…"],
 "actions_planned":[{"fixer_id":"fm-plugins-skill-version-drift","writes_to":["<skills>"],"estimated_bytes":24576}],
 "recommended_command":"omaddons doctor fix --only fm-plugins-skill-version-drift",
 "recommended_argv":["omaddons","doctor","fix","--only","fm-plugins-skill-version-drift"],
 "capabilities_command":"omaddons doctor capabilities --json","robot_docs_command":"omaddons doctor robot-docs",
 "warnings":[],"commands":[{"action":"doctor_fix","command":"omaddons doctor fix --only fm-plugins-skill-version-drift","argv":["…"],"destructive":false}],
 "meta":{"elapsed_ms":61,"offline":false}}
```

(Placeholders such as `<skills>` are for this text; the output prints real paths.)

- **`summary`:** `ok` = no finding at all (the run's `DONE_OK`); `total_findings` and `auto_fixable` exactly as the full view's `summary` of the same run.
- **`quick_ref`** (display strings; format decided while writing this bead): one entry per severity that has findings, P0 to P3: `P<k>: <n> finding` (or `findings` when n ≠ 1), then ` (`, the non-zero parts among `<a> auto-fixable`, `<f> needs --force --yes` (`need` when f ≠ 1) and `<m> manual`, joined by `, `, then `)`. A finding counts as auto-fixable when its remediation's `auto_fixable` is true, else as needing force when `needs_force` is true, else as manual (E3's summary split). No findings: `[]`.
- **`findings`:** the same objects, in the same order, as the full view of the same state.
- **`actions_planned`:** section 2.
- **`recommended_command` / `recommended_argv`** (the plan names their source, E6's planner; the fallbacks were decided while writing this bead), first match wins:
  1. planned fixes → `FixPlan::recommended_argv`;
  2. a `PlanRefusal` whose fix is a command → that fix's argv;
  3. any finding → the first finding's `remediation.explain_argv` (findings are severity-ordered, so a P0 that needs force is explained, never forced);
  4. no finding → `null` for both.

  `recommended_command` is `shell_words::join` of the argv. The recommendation never holds `--force` or `--yes`.
- **`capabilities_command`, `robot_docs_command`:** the two constant strings.
- **`commands[]`:** one `CommandHint` for the recommendation, action `doctor_fix` for a fix argv (`argv[1..3] == ["doctor", "fix"]`) or `doctor_explain` for an explain argv, with the action's registered `destructive`; `[]` with no recommendation. There is no `next_steps` key in this view (§6.11's key list), so E3's `next_steps == commands` check does not apply to it.
- **Exit codes:** E3's: 0 when `summary.ok`, else 1; the refusals and errors E3 raises before STARTING unchanged.
- **Determinism:** the view holds no run id, path of the run, or time, so two triages of one state print the same bytes once `meta` is stripped.

### 4. The human form

```text
omaddons doctor --robot-triage · 2 findings (1 auto-fixable)
  P0: 1 finding (1 needs --force --yes)
  P3: 1 finding (1 auto-fixable)
next: omaddons doctor fix --only fm-plugins-skill-version-drift
also: omaddons doctor capabilities --json · omaddons doctor robot-docs
```

A clean run prints `omaddons doctor --robot-triage · no findings` and the `also:` line. Labels name targets and addons, never a path below `WTF/`.

### 5. The handbook's agent loop

`## The agent loop` in `src/contract/guide/doctor.md`, after `## Surface`, a fenced `sh` block and four sentences: run `omaddons doctor --robot-triage --json`; if `actions_planned` is not empty, run `recommended_argv` (an auto-fixable repair, backed up and undoable); otherwise run it too (an explain, which changes nothing); a P0 that is not auto-fixable is the user's decision, to be told before anything else; `omaddons undo --last-by agent --json` reverts a repair. This is the same loop B2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.2`, the guide's content) writes into the guide. The handbook's size budget and parse test (s3) still pass. Update the s3 unit snapshot `doctor_handbook_sample`.

### 6. The contract and README

- New wire names (close comment): the flag `--robot-triage`; the view value `triage`; `summary.ok`; `quick_ref`; `actions_planned[].{fixer_id, writes_to, estimated_bytes}`; `recommended_command`; `recommended_argv`; `capabilities_command`; `robot_docs_command`.
- Naming rules (M4-D55): `quick_ref` (an array without a plural noun) and `writes_to` are the doctor contract's names. Decided while writing this bead: each one A3's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`) rule test flags joins E3's doctor-contract exception, keyed by type and field, with the reason "the doctor contract's names (M4-D34)"; never an allowlist line.
- Schema: `DiagnoseReport`'s schema becomes a `oneOf` of `full` and `triage` tagged by `view` (`for_serialize` settings); A3's live validation checks both (whichever of A3 and this part lands second wires it).
- No volatile key (the view holds no run identity). No new code, warning, action, env var, failpoint or constant. Not a mutating path (common rule 16).
- **Contract matrix** (`#[test] fn doctor_triage()`): `doctor --robot-triage` on a fresh `Scene` → 0, snapshot `doctor_triage_clean`; `doctor --robot-triage --since latest` → 64, `usage`, snapshot `doctor_triage_since_conflict`.
- **README:** `### \`doctor\`` gains a `--robot-triage` paragraph (what the view holds, that it recommends a fix only when one is auto-fixable and otherwise an explain, never `--force`, that it is a diagnose and leaves a run directory); "The JSON contract"'s doctor-envelope paragraph names the `triage` view and the `oneOf` schema.
- **Skill:** if the guide's generated blocks show the flag (they list paths, not flags), regenerate `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md`; otherwise nothing changes there (say which in the close comment).

**Files:** `src/doctor/triage.rs` (new), `src/doctor/report.rs`, `src/doctor/mod.rs`, `src/app/doctor.rs`, `src/contract/guide/doctor.md` and the s3 unit snapshot, `tests/contract/matrix.rs` and two snapshots, `README.md`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `omaddons doctor --robot-triage --json` (and `doctor diagnose --robot-triage`) returns the `triage` view: `summary{ok, total_findings, auto_fixable}`, `quick_ref`, `findings`, `actions_planned`, `recommended_command`, `recommended_argv`, `capabilities_command`, `robot_docs_command`, with `commands[]` holding one hint matching the recommendation or none.
- [ ] `actions_planned` and the fix recommendation come from E6's `plan_fix` with `force: false` and doctor diff's placeholder roots; the planning writes nothing, takes no lock and allocates no transaction.
- [ ] The recommendation follows the four-step rule; it never holds `--force` or `--yes`; it is `null` on a clean home.
- [ ] A `PlanRefusal` and a non-refusal planning error both leave `actions_planned: []` and never fail the run.
- [ ] `findings` equal the full view's for the same state, in the same order; `summary` equals its counts.
- [ ] `--robot-triage --since <run>` is `usage` (exit 64).
- [ ] A triage run creates one run directory whose `report.json` is the envelope without `meta` plus `kind: "diagnose"`, and `latest` moves to it.
- [ ] `doctor diagnose`'s schema is one `oneOf` tagged by `view` (`full`, `triage`), and both validate (once A3 has landed).
- [ ] The handbook gains `## The agent loop`; its parse test and size budget pass.
- [ ] Matrix rows `doctor_triage_clean` and `doctor_triage_since_conflict` are snapshotted and checked in doctor mode; README's paragraphs are updated.
- [ ] The naming exceptions are keyed with their reason (once A3 has landed), with no allowlist line.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes and `ubs` is clean; the close comment lists the wire names and each "Decided while writing this bead" item.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

- **`src/doctor/triage.rs`** (synthetic findings and plans; one name per case):
  - `quick_ref_cases`: `no_findings` → `[]`; `one_p0_needs_force` → `["P0: 1 finding (1 needs --force --yes)"]`; `one_p3_auto` → `["P3: 1 finding (1 auto-fixable)"]`; `p2_two_manual_one_auto` → `["P2: 3 findings (1 auto-fixable, 2 manual)"]`; `two_need_force` → `… (2 need --force --yes)`; `mixed_severities` (P0 and P3 → two entries, P0 first).
  - `recommended_cases`: `planned_fixes` → E6's argv; `refusal_with_command_fix` → the refusal's argv; `refusal_with_prose_fix` → the first finding's explain argv; `planning_io_error` → the first finding's explain argv; `findings_without_plan` → the first finding's explain argv; `no_findings` → `None`.
  - `never_recommends_force`: over every case above, the argv contains neither `--force` nor `--yes`.
  - `summary_cases` (`ok`, `total_findings`, `auto_fixable` against the full summary of the same findings).
  - `commands_hint_matches_the_recommendation` (`doctor_fix` for a fix argv, `doctor_explain` for an explain argv, `[]` for none; the hint's argv equals `recommended_argv`).
  - `triage_report_serializes_with_view_triage` (the tag value, the key order of section 3, no `next_steps`, no `run_id`).
- **`src/app/doctor.rs`:** `robot_triage_conflicts_with_since` (clap rejects the pair; each alone parses); `diagnose_report_schema_is_one_of_full_and_triage` (the generated schema has a `oneOf` of two objects whose `view` is `const` `full` and `triage`).

### Integration and end-to-end tests

- `tests/contract/matrix.rs::doctor_triage`: `doctor --robot-triage` → 0, doctor mode, snapshot `doctor_triage_clean`; `doctor --robot-triage --since latest` → 64, snapshot `doctor_triage_since_conflict`.
- The end-to-end scenarios (`triage_*` in `tests/doctor.rs`: a recommendation that runs, the force case, equality with the full view, purity outside the run directory) are s5's.

### Logging

- Unit tests are table-driven; each assertion message names the case and shows the findings (id, severity, remediation flags), the plan or refusal, and the produced `quick_ref` and argv.
- Contract rows log through the harness; a failing snapshot shows its diff.

## Considerations

- **Hot spots:** `src/doctor/report.rs` and `src/app/doctor.rs` (E3's, extended by E6, E7, E8 and s1–s3: add the variant and the branch, rebase); `src/contract/guide/doctor.md` (s3's; add one section); matrix and README as in s1.
- **What could go wrong:** the triage recommending something that does not run (s5's `triage_recommends_a_fix_that_runs` runs it, and the contract suite runs every `commands[]` argv); the triage silently recommending a forced repair (`never_recommends_force`, and `force: false` at the call); the two views drifting apart (`findings` built by the same code; s5 compares them).
- **Why a refusal does not fail the triage:** `doctor fix` refuses before anything moves, and the triage only reports what that refusal would be, through its fix.
- **Privacy:** the view reuses E3's findings (no file content, no path below `WTF/`); `writes_to` holds this machine's scope roots.

## Dependencies

- Parent: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4.
- Before it: s3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4.3`), because the report names `doctor capabilities --json` and `doctor robot-docs`, which must exist, and the agent loop is added to the handbook s3 creates. (s1 and s2 come before s3.)
- After it: s5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4.5`), which runs the recommendations end to end.
- Built on E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, the diagnose runtime and the `DiagnoseReport` enum), E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`, `plan_fix`, `FixPlan::triage`, `recommended_argv`, the test fixers) and A2's actions. B2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.2`) writes the same loop into the guide after this leaf closes.

comments.text: **Common rules.** The rules every M4 leaf and subtask follows, cited in this bead as "common rule N", are in the pinned docs bead `omad-bxb1` (`br show omad-bxb1`). Read them once per session, not once per bead.

title: E2E: the doctor's read surface end to end, its perf budgets and its intent-corpus rows
description:
Part 5 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4 (`doctor health`, `ls`, `--robot-triage`, `capabilities` and `robot-docs`). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

The leaf E4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4`) adds the doctor contract's read-only verbs on top of the doctor that E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`) and E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`) built: `doctor health` (s1), `doctor ls` (s2), `doctor capabilities` and `doctor robot-docs` (s3), and `doctor --robot-triage` (s4). Each of those parts shipped its unit tests and its contract rows.

**This part proves the surface end to end, on the real binary:** one `TestLog` scenario per behaviour in `tests/doctor.rs` (the suite E3 created), the rows added to E3's exit-site table, the privacy sweep, the two release-build perf budgets of checkpoint criterion 10 in `tests/perf.rs` ("`doctor health` … in under 200 ms; each `quick` detector takes under 5 ms"), and the intent-corpus rows of criterion 5. It is its own step because these scenarios run several commands against one home, plant states, crash children at failpoints and compare tree hashes, which the parts' unit tests cannot; and because the perf budgets run only at the checkpoint, in release builds.

**What this part relies on** (all on `main` before it starts):

- **The surface** (s1–s4): `doctor health` (`status` ∈ `ok | findings | unsafe | concurrency`, precedence unsafe > concurrency > findings > ok, exit 0 only for `ok`, 1 otherwise; `findings`, `by_severity`, `last_run`, `run_id`; no run directory, no write; per-detector debug lines `check <fm id>: <n> us` under `-v`); `doctor ls` (newest first, `--limit` default 20, `--limit 0` → 64 with the fix `omaddons doctor ls --limit 20`, `truncated`, `ABORTED` with `exit_code: null`, kinds from reports, history or `actions.jsonl`, `started_at` from the run id); `doctor capabilities` (every failure-mode id once, the eleven exit codes, `write_scopes`, `verbs`, `cost_summary`; no request, no write); `doctor robot-docs` (the handbook with `EXIT CODES`, `capabilities` and `NEVER do`; JSON `{format, content}`; human = `content`); `--robot-triage` (the `triage` view; `recommended_argv` from E6's planner, else an explain, never `--force`/`--yes`; conflicts with `--since`).
- **T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs):** `tests/common/tlog.rs`: `let log = tlog!();`; `log.step(label)`, `log.note(text)`, `log.json(label, &value)`, `log.case(name)`; `log.run(&env, &argv) -> Ran` (argv, env overrides with secrets redacted, cwd, start time, `elapsed_ms`, exit, stdout envelope, stderr NDJSON, `net.log` lines added, failpoints armed); `Ran::{ok(), exit(n), envelope(), data(), error_code(), warnings(), commands(), aborted()}`; `log.tree(label, root)` and `log.assert_unchanged(label, root)` (tree hashes with modes and symlink targets; the first differing paths on a mismatch); on panic, `test log: <path>` and the last 20 steps; `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG=verbose` and `argc e2e [FILTER]`.
- **E3's test kit:** `tests/doctor.rs` (first line `//! e2e suite: …`), `common::doctor::check_envelope(stdout, stderr, code)` (the doctor envelope's rules: key order, `ok == (code == 0)`, no `data`, `error` iff code ∈ {4, 5, 6, 64, 66, 73, 74}), `Ran::fails(exit, code)`, `common::doctor::plant::{record_folder_missing, managed_files_modified, state_version_newer, journal_pending, runs, latest}` (each documenting its order constraint: `journal_pending` last, `state_version_newer` after every change on that target), `Home::new(&["wow", "wow_classic"])` (retail and classic) with HTTP fixtures, `<state>` = `home.env.state().join("omaddons")`; the table test `every_doctor_exit_site_uses_the_doctor_dictionary` with rows `(name, argv, setup, exit, code)`; the failpoints `doctor.run.staged`, `doctor.run.published`, `doctor.detector.panic` (`=panic`, `=sleep:<ms>`, `@N`); `OMADDONS_NOW` (frozen clock, debug builds).
- **E6's test fixers** (debug builds, `OMADDONS_TEST_FIXERS=1`): `fm-test-write` (enabled; detects a regular file `*.write` at depth ≤ 3 under `<state>/doctor-test/` whose bytes are not exactly `repaired\n`; fixes it by writing `repaired\n`); `fm-test-quarantine` (`needs_force`, not enabled; a `*.quarantine` under `<state>/doctor-test/`, `<config>/doctor-test/`, `<cache>/doctor-test/` or a client's `<meta>/doctor-test/`); `fm-test-flatten` (not enabled; `Interface/AddOns/TestWrap*`); all P3, tier `default`. `doctor fix --dry-run --json` lists `actions_planned[]` with each primitive's `bytes`. E5's failpoint `doctor.repair.committed`.
- **Other helpers:** `common::privacy::assert_private_all(stdout, stderr)` and `common::wtf::Wtf` (`FAKEACCT`/`FakeRealm`/`FakeChar` trees); `omaddons::fsx::GlobalLock::acquire(&paths, "test")` from the test process (as `tests/backup_verify.rs:371` does); `common::procfs::running_as_root()` for mode-based cases; `tests/perf.rs`'s `measured` and `median_of_21` (`tests/perf.rs:56-73`); D8's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8`) `common::realistic::realistic_home(dir) -> Realistic` (retail, classic and era, 10 addons each from local archives, 30 records and 5,040 managed files, works in release builds; `REALISTIC_TARGETS`).
- **Not edges:** C4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4`) owns `tests/contract/intent_corpus.rs` and its harness (each row on its own copy of `common::intent_home()`, an erroring row must change nothing, the fix runs on an independent copy to its declared exit); E7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7`) adds `doctor undo` and `undo_state`; A4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`) adds `capabilities` with `failure_modes.{count, command}`.

**The decisions that shape it:**
- **M4-D33, M4-D43, M4-D29:** `health` creates no run directory and is never `ok` with incomplete coverage; it runs exactly the `cached` and `quick` tiers that `doctor --quick` runs.
- **M4-D34, M4-D40:** every verb's envelope follows the doctor rules; every exit is in the doctor dictionary.
- **M4-D2:** `doctor capabilities` is generated, so its ids equal the registry's.
- **M4-D38:** the triage never recommends a forced repair.
- **M4-D47 (context):** doctor tests are Rust, driving the real binary on synthetic homes; no shell fixture scripts.
- **§3.2 criterion 10's perf budgets** run on a release build; "the bench home" is replaced by the realistic home, because `bench_home` (`tests/perf.rs:227-262`) replays GitHub fixtures and release builds never replay them (`choose_transport`, `src/net/mod.rs:336-344`) (decided while writing this bead).

## Technical Approach

### 1. `tests/doctor.rs`: the scenarios

Append to E3's suite, each function prefixed by its surface (`health_`, `ls_`, `triage_`, `capabilities_`, `robot_docs_`) so `cargo test --test doctor health_` selects one surface. Every scenario opens `let log = tlog!();`, runs every command through `log.run` with `--json` passed explicitly where it reads the envelope, checks every doctor envelope with `common::doctor::check_envelope`, and works on its own `Home::new(&["wow", "wow_classic"])` unless it says otherwise. "Trees" means `log.tree` of `<state>` (with `doctor/`), `<config>`, `<cache>` and each client dir, followed later by `log.assert_unchanged` of the same labels. Scenarios that need the test fixers set `OMADDONS_TEST_FIXERS=1` on every run (the gate runs debug builds, where they exist).

**`doctor health`**

1. **`health_on_a_clean_home_is_ok_and_writes_nothing`**
   - step "home": install one addon on retail through the HTTP fixtures; trees.
   - step "json": `doctor health --json --progress json` → exit 0; `status: "ok"`, `findings: 0`, `by_severity` `{P0: 0, P1: 0, P2: 0, P3: 0}`, `last_run: null`, `run_id: null`, `commands: []`, no `error` key; no stderr `error` event.
   - step "human": `doctor health` → exit 0; stdout is exactly one line, matching `^ok  omaddons=\S+ doctor=1\.0 findings=0 last_run=none run_id=none\n$`.

### Logging

- Every `tests/doctor.rs` scenario uses `let log = tlog!();`; each phase is a `log.step("…")` named as in section 1; each table row is a `log.case("…")`; every command goes through `log.run(&home.env, &argv)`, so its argv, environment overrides (with `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS`, `OMADDONS_NOW` and `OMADDONS_TEST_FIXERS` visible), exit, envelope, stderr events and added `net.log` lines are in `steps.jsonl` and `transcript.md`.

- A failing scenario prints `test log: <path>` and its last 20 steps; `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG=verbose argc e2e doctor` echoes every step live.
- The perf tests print their `measured` lines on stderr (median, p95, first run, home shape; per detector its id, median and p95), which H6 quotes; they do not use `TestLog`, as no budget in `tests/perf.rs` does.

## Considerations

- **Hot spots:** `tests/doctor.rs` is E3's suite and also grows from E6, E7, E8 and the F leaves: append functions, never reorder, rebase; `tests/perf.rs` (append two functions); `tests/contract/intent_corpus.rs` (C4's; append rows); `tests/common/mod.rs` (append `pub mod realistic;` only if this part adds it).
- **Flake risks:** the debug-scaled 100 ms deadline gives the gate's small homes a wide margin; the cut-short case uses the sleep failpoint, so it is exact; frozen clocks (`OMADDONS_NOW`) make run ids sort as intended; `GlobalLock` held from the test process is released by dropping its guard before the next case.
- **Mode-based cases** (an unreadable lock file or runs directory) are skipped as root, saying so in the log, and restore modes afterwards.
- **The undo step** of `ls_lists_runs_newest_first_with_their_kinds` depends on E7, which is not an edge; it is written by whichever lands second, never as a runtime switch that could hide a missing path.
- **Risks (§11.4):** #3 (false positives): the perf home must read `ok`; #4 (speed): the two budgets; #13 (the guide drifts): `robot_docs_commands_run`.
- **Privacy:** the logs hold only synthetic `TestEnv` homes; tokens are redacted by T1.
