title: fsx groundwork for repairs: repair paths, the temp-symlink rename, several skill directories, the repair journal's prune kind and durable chmods
description:
Part 1 of 7 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5 (The repair transaction). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

E5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`) builds M4's second journal family, the **repair transaction** (`<state>/journal/<tx>.repair.jsonl`): the doctor's fixes lowered to primitive filesystem operations (`WriteFile`, `Chmod`, `RenameNoReplace`), each written ahead in its own journal line before it runs, committed under the global lock, rolled back by inverse primitives on failure, and recovered by every command that takes the lock (M4-D31). It exists so that every doctor repair is exactly as safe as an install: journaled, crash-safe, undoable, and never deleting anything (M4-D35, M4-D36), which is what G-M4-4 ("every auto-fixable state is repaired by one consented command that backs up verbatim, never deletes") and G-M4-6 ("every repair is a journaled transaction that recovers like any other") promise.

This part adds the small fsx and path pieces every later part needs, and nothing that writes a repair yet: the names (`.repair`), client-side backups under the repair's snapshot half, several skill directories in one scope table, prune's knowledge of the repair journal, a narrow exception that lets a repair quarantine a temporary symlink a crash left, and a durable chmod. It is its own step because these touch `src/fsx/`, the busiest hot spot, whose collision rule is "E13 first, G3 last; E5 before E14, E7 and E8": landing them first and alone keeps that rule and gives lowering (s2) and the journal format (s3) a stable base to work beside each other.

## Technical Approach

**Facts this part relies on** (as of `c0ab5e9`):

- `paths::tx_named` strips only `.wtf` and parses a ULID (`src/state/paths.rs:33-35`); the folder journal listing (`src/engine/journal.rs:629`) and the orphan sweep (`src/engine/retention.rs:365`, `:393`) name transactions only through it, so `<tx>.repair…` names are invisible to them. **Do not change `tx_named`.**
- `SnapshotRoots` puts client-side backups under `<meta>/snapshots/<tx>/files/` or, for a settings transaction, `<tx>.wtf/files/` (`src/fsx/session.rs:13-54`); the home side is any root the caller gives.
- `ScopeTable` holds one skill directory, `skill: PathBuf` (`src/fsx/scope.rs:227`, set from `skill_dir` or `Paths::skill_dir()` at `:251`), and the Skill row admits `Writer::Skill` and `Writer::Doctor` (`:126`).
- `normalize` refuses an operation whose final component is an existing symlink unless the op is `SymlinkAtomic` (`src/fsx/mutate.rs:593-617`, the check at `:610-615`); `symlink_atomic` makes a temporary link named `TEMP_PREFIX` + random (`.omaddons-…`, `src/fsx/sys.rs:20-22`, `:338-349`) and renames it over the link, so a crash between the two leaves that temporary link.
- prune's location table matches journals as `["journal", name] if name.strip_suffix(".jsonl").is_some_and(is_tx_named)` (`src/fsx/prune.rs:364`), which a `<tx>.repair.jsonl` fails; `unfinished()` reads the `"type"` tag of the first and last complete lines and calls a journal finished only at `committed` (`prune.rs:408-427`); under `LockUse::Own` an unfinished journal is refused (`prune.rs:122-136`).
- `sys::chmod` calls `set_permissions` and does not fsync (`src/fsx/sys.rs:410-419`). Chmod is used today only in untracked sessions (staging `src/engine/stage.rs:314,324`, `src/engine/restore_addons.rs:620`, preservation `src/engine/preserve.rs:100,238-239`, `src/app/auth.rs:332,341`).
- `ScopeTable::is_internal` admits backups and action logs under `<state>` and a client's `<meta>` (`scope.rs:397-402`).
- E13 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.13`, a blocker of the leaf) has already changed `mutate.rs`: `Expect` moved to `src/fsx/expect.rs` with `Expect::Present(Predicate)`, `MutateOpts` gained `expect_to`, and `FileId` moved to `src/fsx/identity.rs`. Add this part's `MutateOpts` field beside `expect_to` and keep E13's check position unchanged.

**1. Repair names and paths** (`src/state/paths.rs`):

- `pub const REPAIR_SUFFIX: &str = ".repair";` with a doc comment saying what it marks (the repair family's journal, its client-side snapshot half), that older builds cannot parse it (the reason it exists, M4-D31), and that only `engine::repair::list` parses such names while retention only matches the suffix to skip it.
- Constructors that build names and parse nothing:
  - `Paths::journal_repair(tx) -> PathBuf`: `<state>/journal/<tx>.repair.jsonl`;
  - `Paths::doctor_run(id: &str) -> PathBuf`: `<state>/doctor/runs/<id>` (beside the existing `doctor_runs_dir()`, `paths.rs:348`; skip if E3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, already added it);
  - `Paths::cache_quarantine(run_id: &str) -> PathBuf`: `<cache>/quarantine/<run_id>`;
  - `ClientPaths::snapshots_repair(tx) -> PathBuf`: `<meta>/snapshots/<tx>.repair` (beside `snapshots_wtf`, `paths.rs:554`).
- `tx_named` keeps its body; its doc comment gains one sentence: "Names with `.repair` are not parsed here, on purpose: they belong to the repair family, which older builds must not see (M4-D31)."

**2. Client-side backups of a repair** (`src/fsx/session.rs`):

- `SnapshotRoots` gains a suffix choice: replace `wtf: bool` with a private `enum ClientHalf { Plain, Wtf, Repair }` (or add a second flag; keep `for_tx` and `for_wtf_tx` unchanged in behaviour), and add `pub fn for_repair(home_side: impl Into<PathBuf>, tx: &TxId) -> Self` whose `dir_for(Side::Client(c), tx)` is `ClientPaths::new(c).snapshots_repair(tx).join("files")` and whose home side is the given root (the repair passes `<run>/backups/`).
- `WriteSession::tx` is unchanged: it already takes `<run>/actions.jsonl` and any home-side backup root (`session.rs:85-94`).

**3. Several skill directories, and the quarantine roots** (`src/fsx/scope.rs`):

- `ScopeTable.skill: PathBuf` becomes `skills: Vec<PathBuf>` (the first is the default one `new` sets, as today), and `candidates()` matches each (`Position::Root` or `Below`, `Side::Home`) exactly as the one does now.
- `pub fn with_skill_dirs(mut self, dirs: &[PathBuf]) -> Result<Self>`: canonicalizes each through its deepest existing ancestor (the same `canonical` helper `new` uses), skips duplicates, and refuses when the total would exceed `SKILL_DIRS_MAX` with `Error::new(ErrorCode::ScopeDenied, "a repair names <n> skill directories; at most <SKILL_DIRS_MAX> are admitted", Suggestion::command(["omaddons", "status"]))`. Writer rules stay the Skill row's (`Writer::Skill`, `Writer::Doctor`).
- `pub fn is_quarantine(&self, path: &Path) -> bool`: true exactly for paths strictly below one of `<state>/doctor/runs/<name>/quarantine/`, `<cache>/quarantine/<name>/`, or `<client dir>/Interface/.omaddons/snapshots/<name>.repair/quarantine/` of a registered client dir (`<name>` one plain component). It touches no file (the table's roots are canonical already).
- **`SKILL_DIRS_MAX`** (8, "skill directories `history_tail.skill_dirs[]` keeps and the drift check follows", §7.9) is B3's constant (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3`, `robot-docs install-skill`). If B3 has not landed, add it here to `src/limits.rs` with its `REGISTRY` row (`LimitValue::Count(8)`, unit `count`, not configurable, purpose "skill directories a scope table, `history_tail.skill_dirs[]` and the skill-drift check admit at most") and its `LIMIT_NAMES` entry, and re-accept the `limit_registries` snapshot after reviewing its diff (common rule 7). Whichever of B3 and this part lands second reuses it.

**4. The temp-symlink rename exception** (`src/fsx/mutate.rs`):

- `MutateOpts` gains `pub temp_symlink: bool` (default `false`). When it is `true`, `mutate_with` admits a source whose final component is a symlink if, and only if, all of these hold; otherwise it refuses exactly as today (`FsxError::ScopeDenied("<path> is a symlink, which fsx never writes through")`), so nothing else loosens:
  1. the op is `Op::Rename { mode: RenameMode::NoReplace, .. }`;
  2. the session's writer is `Writer::Doctor`;
  3. the source is a symlink (`symlink_metadata`), and the final components of both the source and the destination start with `sys::TEMP_PREFIX`;
  4. one end is inside an omaddons-owned directory (below `<state>`, `<config>`, `<cache>` or a registered client's `<meta>`) and the other satisfies `scopes.is_quarantine(..)`.
- Both directions are admitted (into quarantine for a fix; back out for its rollback or its undo, E7 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7`). Decided while writing this bead: the flag is explicit (a caller asks for the exception) and the conditions are checked in fsx, so a caller cannot widen it; `rename` moves the link, never its target (the before-digest is `link:<target>`, as `digest_after` already records for a symlink).
- The scope check of both ends, the predicates (E13's `expect`/`expect_to`: a symlink's `pre` is `Symlink { identity, link_target }`), the actions line and the failpoints run as for any rename.

**5. prune's `Kind::RepairJournal`** (`src/fsx/prune.rs`):

- In `location()`, under `<state>`: `["journal", name] if name.strip_suffix(".repair.jsonl").is_some_and(is_tx) => Kind::RepairJournal` (exactly a ULID followed by `.repair.jsonl`; `<tx>.wtf.repair.jsonl`, `<tx>.repair.json` and `<tx>.repair.jsonl.tmp` are not prunable). Decided while writing this bead: this is a location check that recognizes one exact shape, not a lister; `engine::repair::list` (s3) stays the only function that turns repair names into transactions.
- `Kind::RepairJournal.reason()` is `PruneReason::PostCommitCleanup` (the folder `Journal` kind's), and `Planned.journal` is set for it.
- The `LockUse::Own` refusal of an unfinished journal uses a repair rule for this kind: finished when the last complete line's tag is `committed` or `rolled_back`; unstarted (prunable) when the first complete line is not `prepared` or there is none; anything else unfinished. Factor the tag reading out of `unfinished()` into a helper both rules use.

**6. A durable chmod in tracked sessions** (`src/fsx/mutate.rs`, `src/fsx/sys.rs`):

- In a **tracked** session, `Op::Chmod` fsyncs the file after `set_permissions` (one counted `fsync`, `SyncCounts`), so that a repair's `done` line can never become durable before a mode change that a power loss could undo. Untracked sessions keep today's behaviour exactly (staging's one-`syncfs`, no-`fsync` contract is untouched). Decided while writing this bead: the plan's durability barrier (M4-D54, G3 `omad-7ccp`) syncs directories, not file inodes, and nothing else makes a chmod durable; no tracked session chmods today, so no existing fsync count changes.

**Not in this part:** no repair module, no journal, no lowering, no `PRUNE_CALLERS` change (a caller is added in s4), no retention change (s3).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `Paths::journal_repair`, `Paths::doctor_run` (unless E3 added it), `Paths::cache_quarantine` and `ClientPaths::snapshots_repair` return the documented paths, and `tx_named("<tx>.repair")` is `None` while `tx_named("<tx>.wtf")` and `tx_named("<tx>")` still parse.
- [ ] `SnapshotRoots::for_repair(<run>/backups, tx)` puts a client-side backup under `<meta>/snapshots/<tx>.repair/files/` and a home-side one under `<run>/backups/`; `for_tx` and `for_wtf_tx` are unchanged.
- [ ] `ScopeTable::with_skill_dirs` admits each given directory for `Writer::Skill` and `Writer::Doctor` only, and refuses more than `SKILL_DIRS_MAX` with `scope_denied`; `ScopeTable::new` behaves as before.
- [ ] `ScopeTable::is_quarantine` is true for exactly the three quarantine root shapes and false for everything around them (a run's `backups/`, a non-`.repair` snapshot, the roots themselves).
- [ ] A `Writer::Doctor` rename of a `.omaddons-*` symlink between an omaddons-owned directory and a quarantine root, with `temp_symlink: true`, moves the link (not its target) in both directions; every other combination is refused exactly as before and changes nothing.
- [ ] prune deletes a finished (`committed` or `rolled_back`) or unstarted `<tx>.repair.jsonl` under `LockUse::Own` and refuses an unfinished one; it refuses any other `.repair` name shape and any reason but `PostCommitCleanup` for this kind.
- [ ] A tracked chmod adds exactly one fsync; an untracked chmod adds none.
- [ ] If `SKILL_DIRS_MAX` was added here: its `REGISTRY` row and `LIMIT_NAMES` entry exist and the `limit_registries` snapshot was re-accepted after review.
- [ ] Every existing test passes unchanged (`tests/fsx_scope.rs`, `tests/fsx_prune.rs`, the fsx unit tests, `tests/engine_crash.rs`), and `argc gate` passes for this commit.
- [ ] The close comment lists the internal names added (`REPAIR_SUFFIX`, the four constructors, `SnapshotRoots::for_repair`, `ScopeTable::with_skill_dirs`, `ScopeTable::is_quarantine`, `MutateOpts::temp_symlink`, prune's `Kind::RepairJournal`) and `SKILL_DIRS_MAX` if added; no wire name changes.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

- `src/state/paths.rs`:
  - `repair_names_are_invisible_to_tx_named`: cases `bare` (`<tx>` → `Some`), `wtf` (`<tx>.wtf` → `Some`), `repair` (`<tx>.repair` → `None`), `repair_after_wtf` (`<tx>.wtf.repair` → `None`), `wtf_after_repair` (`<tx>.repair.wtf` → `None`).
  - `repair_paths_are_where_the_layout_says`: each constructor against a `Paths::with_roots` fixture, the expected path spelled out per case.
- `src/fsx/session.rs`:
  - `repair_snapshot_roots_put_client_backups_under_the_repair_half`: `dir_for(Side::Home, tx)` is the given root; `dir_for(Side::Client(c), tx)` is `c/Interface/.omaddons/snapshots/<tx>.repair/files`; `for_tx` and `for_wtf_tx` give their old paths (regression cases).
- `src/fsx/scope.rs`:
  - `with_skill_dirs_admits_each_dir_for_skill_and_doctor_only`: table over the `ALL` writers × {default dir, second dir, third dir, a sibling of a skill dir}: `Skill` and `Doctor` allowed below each skill dir, every other writer refused, the sibling refused for all.

### Logging

Unit tests only: table-driven, one case name per row, each assertion message naming the case and printing the input path and the result (`"{case}: {path} → {result:?}"`). No `TestLog`.

## Considerations

- **Hot spot `src/fsx/`** (`session.rs`, `mutate.rs`, `sys.rs`, `scope.rs`, `prune.rs`): rule **E13 first, G3 last**; E5 before E14 (`with_fences`), E7 and E8 (prune kinds `ClientRepair`, `CacheQuarantine`, `DoctorLatest`); E3 (`untracked_logged`), D4 (`Lease`, `LockUse::Expired`) and B3 (the History row, its own skill-dir scope) touch separate functions and rebase. Every condition above is checked in fsx, so no caller can widen it.
- **Compatibility:** none of this is wire; the M3 build sees no new name it can parse.
- **What could go wrong:** turning `skill` into a list changes every `candidates()` call; the `allowed()` row tests in `scope.rs` (`:700-735`) catch a writer that gains or loses a row. A chmod fsync placed in the untracked path would break staging's no-fsync test (`tests/engine_*` staging counts): keep it tracked-only.

title: Lowering fixes to primitive steps with endpoint predicates, resources, quarantine roots and the mount check
description:
Part 2 of 7 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5 (The repair transaction). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

E5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`) builds M4's repair transaction: the doctor's fixes lowered to primitive filesystem operations, each written ahead in its own journal line, committed under the global lock, rolled back by inverses, and recovered by every lock-taking command (M4-D31), so every repair is as safe and as undoable as an install (G-M4-4, G-M4-6).

This part is **lowering**: `engine::repair::lower`, which turns the presentation-level fixes a fixer returns (E1's `Fix`: a write, a chmod, a quarantine, a flatten, a suspension, a delegation) into one immutable, ordered list of primitive steps, each with its endpoint predicates, its resources, its reserved backup path and its quarantine destination, and refuses everything a repair may never do before anything is written. It is its own step because it is pure planning (it reads the filesystem and writes nothing), it is what E6's preview shows and its token covers, and getting each step's predicates right is what makes recovery decidable: M4-D31 rejected the reviewed draft's "one write-ahead step per presentation-level action", because a flatten is two renames and a crash between them leaves a state matching neither its before nor its after.

## Technical Approach

**Facts this part relies on** (as of `c0ab5e9`, after the leaf's blockers):

- E1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`) defines the pure types in `src/engine/repair_action.rs`: `Fix::{Write { path, content, mode: Mode }, Chmod { path, mode }, Quarantine { path, root: QuarantineRoot }, Flatten { inner, outer }, Suspend { journal: JournalSet }, Delegate { what: Delegation }}`; `QuarantineRoot::{State, Config, Cache, Client { client_dir }}`; `Endpoint::{Absent, File { identity?, sha256?, mode? }, Dir { identity?, stamp? }, Symlink { identity?, link_target? }}`; `Endpoints::{One(Endpoint), Pair { path, to }}`; `Primitive::{WriteFile { path, mode, backup }, Chmod { path, mode }, RenameNoReplace { from, to, activation }}`; `Step { seq, fix, fm, op, pre, post, guards }`; `FixEntry { fix, fm, kind }`; `JournalSet { …, artifacts: Vec<SuspendedArtifact { path, root }>, guards }`; and the pure validation `Step::validate`, `validate_steps(fixes, steps)`. A write's content digest lives in its `post` only.
- E13 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.13`) defines `engine::resource::{Resource, PathKind, ResourceSet}` (`rename(from, to)` makes both ends writes; `extend` unions; a lossless text form), and fsx's `Expect::capture(path, Parts) -> io::Result<Expect>` (records the file type always and the requested parts: identity, sha256, mode, stamp, link target).
- `fsx::mount_id(path)` is the `statx` mount id, the final component not followed (`src/fsx/sys.rs:219-234`); two paths a rename can join share it, and a device number cannot tell (two bind mounts of one filesystem share a device and `EXDEV` between them).
- `StampDigest::compute(dir)` is a stat walk with no content read (`src/fsx/mutate.rs:217-253`); it covers entries below the root, not the root itself, so a directory's stamp survives its own rename.
- `ScopeTable::check(writer, owned, path, access)` is read-only (`src/fsx/scope.rs:413-480`); the Wtf and SavedVariables rows refuse `Writer::Doctor`, and `check_protected` refuses `Blizzard_*` AddOns folders as `protected_folder`.
- s1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5.1`) added `Paths::doctor_run`, `Paths::cache_quarantine`, `ClientPaths::snapshots_repair`, `ScopeTable::with_skill_dirs`, `ScopeTable::is_quarantine`, `MutateOpts::temp_symlink` and `SKILL_DIRS_MAX`.

**The module.** Create `src/engine/repair.rs` (the module root: a module doc that summarizes the protocol, the public re-exports) and `src/engine/repair/lower.rs`, and `pub mod repair;` in `src/engine/mod.rs`. Decided while writing this bead: a root file with submodules (`lower.rs`, `journal.rs`, `commit.rs`, `recover.rs`), following the crate's `src/app/adopt.rs` + `src/app/adopt/` pattern, so this part and s3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5.3`) edit different files; every rule the plan states for `src/engine/repair.rs` applies to the root and its directory.

**The API:**

```rust
pub struct RepairTx { tx: TxId, inflight: InflightLock }
impl RepairTx {
    /// A fresh transaction id and its in-flight lock `<state>/inflight/<tx>.lock`, held from
    /// planning to cleanup (§6.14.2 step 1). Lowering needs the id for quarantine paths.
    pub fn begin(paths: &Paths) -> Result<RepairTx>;
    pub fn tx(&self) -> TxId;
}
/// A published run directory `<state>/doctor/runs/<id>` (E3's runtime makes it).
pub struct RepairRun { pub dir: PathBuf, pub id: String }
pub struct LowerCtx<'a> {
    pub paths: &'a Paths,
    pub tx: TxId,
    pub run: &'a RepairRun,
    /// The registered clients a step may touch, each with its key (markers checked by the caller).
    pub clients: &'a [(PathBuf, TargetKey)],
    /// The skill directories a write may touch: `Paths::skill_dir()` and `history_tail.skill_dirs[]`.
    pub skill_dirs: &'a [PathBuf],
    /// The scope table the commit will use (`with_skill_dirs` applied).
    pub scopes: &'a ScopeTable,
    /// `fsx::mount_id` in production; a seam in unit tests.
    pub mount_id: &'a dyn Fn(&Path) -> io::Result<u64>,
}
pub struct PlannedFix { pub fm: Cow<'static, str>, pub fix: Fix }
pub struct LoweredStep { pub step: Step, pub resources: ResourceSet, pub backup_bytes: u64 }
pub struct Lowered {
    pub fixes: Vec<FixEntry>, pub steps: Vec<LoweredStep>, pub resources: ResourceSet,
    pub targets: Vec<TargetKey>, pub client_dirs: Vec<(PathBuf, TargetKey)>,
    /// Every root directory the commit must create before `prepared` (sorted, deduplicated).
    pub roots: Vec<PathBuf>,
}
pub enum RefusedReason { FilesystemMismatch }   // maps to E6's doctor_refused details.reason "filesystem_mismatch"
pub enum LowerError {
    Refused { reason: RefusedReason, path: PathBuf, to: Option<PathBuf>, message: String },
    Error(Error),
}
pub fn lower(ctx: &LowerCtx<'_>, fixes: &[PlannedFix]) -> Result<Lowered, LowerError>;
```

Decided while writing this bead: the plan writes `lower(&[Fix]) -> Vec<Step>`; lowering needs the transaction id, the run directory and the live filesystem to compute predicates and destinations, and each fix needs its failure-mode id, hence `LowerCtx` and `PlannedFix`. `RepairRun` is a plain value because E3's run-directory type is not a blocker of this leaf; E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`) builds it from E3's runtime. `RefusedReason` is a closed enum with one variant now; E6 maps it to `doctor_refused` (M4-D40's `filesystem_mismatch`), and this part adds no error code.

**The lowering table** (`seq` 1-based and contiguous across the whole repair; `fix` the 1-based index of its `PlannedFix`; `fm` copied):

| Fix | Primitives, in order |
|---|---|
| `Write { path, content, mode }` | one `WriteFile { path, mode, backup }`; `backup` = the reserved path when a regular file is there now |
| `Chmod { path, mode }` | one `Chmod { path, mode }` (a regular file only) |
| `Quarantine { path, root }` | one `RenameNoReplace { from: path, to: <root dest> }` |
| `Flatten { inner: <A>/X/Y, outer: <A>/X }` (`<A>` = `Interface/AddOns`), `Y ≠ X` | `RenameNoReplace <A>/X/Y → <A>/Y`; `RenameNoReplace <A>/X → <client quarantine>/Interface/AddOns/X` |
| `Flatten { inner: <A>/X/X, outer: <A>/X }` | `RenameNoReplace <A>/X → <A>/.omaddons-flatten-<tx>`; `RenameNoReplace <A>/.omaddons-flatten-<tx>/X → <A>/X`; `RenameNoReplace <A>/.omaddons-flatten-<tx> → <client quarantine>/Interface/AddOns/X` |
| `Suspend { journal }` | one `RenameNoReplace` per `journal.artifacts` entry, in that order, into its `root`; `journal.guards` copied onto the primitive that moves the journal file out of `<state>/journal/` only |
| `Delegate { what }` | none (E6 runs the disclosed recovery before the primitives) |

- **Reserved backups:** an overwriting `WriteFile` at `seq = k` reserves `<run>/backups/<k>` for a home-side path, or `<meta>/snapshots/<tx>.repair/files/<k>` for a path inside a client dir (the commit's tracked session numbers its actions 1, 2, … in primitive order, so fsx's backup lands exactly there; s4 asserts it). `backup_bytes` is the overwritten file's size (E6's preview reports `bytes`).
- **Quarantine destinations** (M4-D35), `<rel>` the victim's path relative to the root's base:
  - `State` → `<run>/quarantine/state/<path relative to <state>>`; `Config` → `<run>/quarantine/config/<path relative to <config>>`;
  - `Cache` → `<cache>/quarantine/<run id>/<path relative to <cache>>`;
  - `Client { client_dir }` → `<meta>/snapshots/<tx>.repair/quarantine/<path relative to the client dir>`;
  - **`Skill`** (new variant of E1's Rust-only `QuarantineRoot`, decided while writing this bead) → `<run>/quarantine/skill/<path relative to the home directory>`, for a victim in a skill directory: M4-D35's table has no row for a home-side victim outside `<state>`, `<config>` and `<cache>`, and s4's rollback of a created skill file must quarantine it (never delete it).
  - A root that does not match the victim's side (a client path with `State`, a `<state>` path with `Cache`, …) is `LowerError::Error(scope_denied)` "the quarantine root of <path> must be on its own side".
  - The emptied wrapper of a three-rename flatten goes under its original relative path (`…/Interface/AddOns/X`), not the provisional name, so a person inspecting quarantine sees the folder's own name (decided while writing this bead).
  - Every destination's missing parent directories are listed in `Lowered.roots` (the commit creates them before `prepared`; they are doctor-owned, never primitives).
  - For each creating `WriteFile`, the root of its own side is also checked and the parent of `<root>/rolled_back/<seq>/` listed, because s4's rollback quarantines a created file there.
- **Endpoint predicates** (captured with `Expect::capture`, recorded as E1 `Endpoint`s; identity as `{ino, born_ns}` without the device):
  - `WriteFile` over a file: `pre` = `File { sha256, mode }` (decided while writing this bead: the old `mode` is recorded too, because the rollback restores bytes **and** mode, and a reflinked backup's own mode is not a reliable record); `post` = `File { sha256: sha256(content), mode }`. Creating: `pre` = `Absent`, `post` as above.
  - `Chmod`: `pre` = `File { identity, mode: old }`, `post` = `File { identity, mode: new }` (a same-mode replacement fails `pre` by identity). Decided while writing this bead: a chmod whose old mode already equals the new one is dropped (E1's validation forbids an unchanged mode, and there is nothing to do); its fix stays in `fixes[]`.
  - `RenameNoReplace`: `pre` = `Pair { path: <kind> { identity, stamp (Dir) | link_target (Symlink) }, to: Absent }`; `post` = `Pair { path: Absent, to: <same kind> { identity } }`.
  - **Later steps see earlier steps' effects.** Lowering keeps a small virtual view of the steps already lowered (renamed subtrees move with their parent) and captures each step's `pre` against it: the three-rename flatten's step 2 has `pre.path` = `<A>/.omaddons-flatten-<tx>/X` (which does not exist yet) with the inner folder's identity and stamp, and step 3's `pre.path` stamp is the wrapper's stamp with the moved child's entries removed (computed from step 1's single stat walk). Two fixes that touch one path in one repair are E6's conflict check (M4-D62); lowering still records what each sees in order.
- **Resources** (E13's `ResourceSet`): a `WriteFile` writes `Resource::canonical(path, File)` and its reserved backup (`Resource::backup(run id, seq)` for a home-side one, the path for a client-side one); a `Chmod` writes its path; a `RenameNoReplace` is `rename(from, to)`, a directory as `Subtree`. `Lowered.resources` is the union (`extend`), which s3 serializes in E13's text form as `prepared.resources`.
- **`targets` and `client_dirs`:** every `ctx.clients` entry whose client dir contains a step's path or destination, sorted by key; a path under a client dir that `ctx.clients` does not name is refused (`scope_denied`, "… is in a client this repair was not planned for").
- **The mount check** (M4-D35), for every rename and every creating write's rollback destination: `mount_id(parent of from)` must equal `mount_id(deepest existing ancestor of to's parent)`, and the victim must not be a mount point (`mount_id(from) == mount_id(parent of from)`); a `<config>` victim's mount must equal `<state>`'s (its root is under `<run>`). Otherwise `LowerError::Refused { reason: FilesystemMismatch, path, to }` with a message naming both paths and "they are on different mounts, and a quarantine never crosses one; nothing was moved". An `Unsupported` mount id (a kernel before 5.8) is refused the same way (fail closed).
- **Refusals** (all before anything is written; `LowerError::Error` with an existing code and a prose fix that names no command):
  - a path or destination under a client's `WTF/` (any case): `scope_denied`, "the doctor never writes WTF/" (`a_repair_never_writes_wtf`);
  - `ScopeTable::check(Writer::Doctor, …)` refusing a path or destination (`scope_denied`, or `protected_folder` for `Blizzard_*`), with `Access::Rename` for both ends of a rename and `Access::Write` otherwise;
  - a `Chmod` of anything but a regular file (`scope_denied`, "… is not a regular file; the doctor changes modes of files only");
  - a symlink source without a `.omaddons-` name (only the temp-symlink exception moves links), or a temp symlink whose destination is not a quarantine root;
  - a flatten whose destination exists, or whose inner folder is not a direct child of its outer one (`file_exists` for the first: "… already exists; it is never replaced");
  - more skill directories named than `SKILL_DIRS_MAX`;
  - a relative or non-UTF-8 path, or one with `..` (`validate_steps` over the result; a `StepError` becomes `internal` with the `seq`);
  - an I/O error while capturing (`io`, the path).
- **Determinism:** the same fixes over an unchanged home give equal `Lowered` values (E6's preview token, M4-D44, depends on it); sort nothing that the fix order defines, sort everything else by path.

**What not to do:** never write (no `WriteSession` in `lower.rs`; a unit test scans for `mutate`, `WriteSession` and `std::fs` writes, as §6.12 does for detectors); never content-hash a directory (stamps only); never read below `WTF/`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `lower` produces, for every fix kind, exactly the primitives of the table, with contiguous `seq`, correct `fix` and `fm`, and every step passing E1's `validate_steps`.
- [ ] Every primitive's `pre` and `post` hold the parts the table names, captured from the live paths, and the three-rename flatten's later steps carry the predicates of the state earlier steps leave.
- [ ] Each overwriting write reserves `<run>/backups/<seq>` (home side) or `<meta>/snapshots/<tx>.repair/files/<seq>` (client side); each quarantine destination is on its victim's own side, and a skill-directory victim uses `<run>/quarantine/skill/…`.
- [ ] `Lowered.resources` is the union of the steps' sets (a rename's both ends, a write's path and backup), and `targets`/`client_dirs` name exactly the clients the steps touch.
- [ ] A victim on another mount than its root, a victim that is a mount point, and a `<config>` victim on another mount than `<state>` are refused with `FilesystemMismatch` before anything is written.
- [ ] Every refusal of the list above is raised, with its code and message, and nothing is written (tree hash); a `WTF/` path is always refused.
- [ ] Lowering is deterministic and writes nothing (tree hash over the whole fixture home).
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files.
- [ ] The close comment lists the internal API added (`RepairTx`, `RepairRun`, `LowerCtx`, `PlannedFix`, `Lowered`, `LoweredStep`, `LowerError`, `RefusedReason`, `QuarantineRoot::Skill`) and confirms or adjusts each "Decided while writing this bead" item of this part.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

In `src/engine/repair/lower.rs`'s `tests` module, on a tempdir home built by a helper `repair_home()` in `src/engine/testing.rs` (the crate's in-crate engine test helpers, `#[cfg(test)]`): a `Paths::with_roots` home with `<state>`, `<config>/credentials/github` (0644), `<cache>`, a skill directory `$HOME/.claude/skills/omaddons/SKILL.md`, and a registered client dir with a marker and `Interface/AddOns/{Stray/…, Wrap/Inner/Inner.toc, Same/Same/Same.toc}`; a published `<run>`.

- `each_fix_kind_lowers_to_its_primitives`: table, one case per kind: `write_over`, `write_create`, `chmod`, `quarantine_state_file`, `quarantine_config_file`, `quarantine_cache_file`, `quarantine_client_dir`, `quarantine_temp_symlink`, `flatten_two`, `flatten_three`, `suspend_three_artifacts`, `delegate`; each asserts the ops, `path`/`to`, `seq`, `fix`, `fm`, `backup`, and `validate_steps` passing. The message prints the case and the lowered steps as JSON.
- `predicates_are_captured_from_the_live_paths`: per case, the exact `pre`/`post` endpoints (kinds and parts present), and that the identity equals `FileId::of` of the live path (device ignored).
- `a_three_rename_flatten_predicts_each_steps_endpoints`: step 1 `pre.path` = `Dir { identity(Same), stamp(Same) }`, step 2 `pre.path` path `<A>/.omaddons-flatten-<tx>/Same` with the inner folder's identity and stamp, step 3 `pre.path` stamp equals `StampDigest::from_entries` of the wrapper without its child; destinations as in the table.
- `the_reserved_backup_is_the_primitives_seq`: a write as the third primitive reserves `<run>/backups/3`; a client-side write reserves `<meta>/snapshots/<tx>.repair/files/3`; a creating write reserves none.
- `quarantine_roots_follow_the_victims_side`: table `state`, `config`, `cache`, `client`, `skill_dir` → the destination spelled out; `a_root_on_the_wrong_side_is_refused`: table of mismatched roots → `scope_denied`.
- `resources_are_the_union_of_the_steps`: for `flatten_two`, the writes are exactly `{<A>/Wrap/Inner/, <A>/Inner/, <A>/Wrap/, <quarantine>/…/Wrap/}` in E13's text form; for `write_over`, the file and `backup:<run id>/1`.
- `a_victim_on_another_mount_is_refused_before_anything`: the `mount_id` seam returns different ids for the victim's parent and the root (`cases: client_dir_vs_meta, config_vs_state, state_vs_run, cache_vs_cache_quarantine`), a victim that is a mount point, and an `Unsupported` mount id → `Refused { FilesystemMismatch }`; tree hash unchanged.
- `lowering_refuses_what_a_repair_may_never_do`: table `wtf_path` (`<client>/WTF/Config.wtf`), `wtf_destination`, `saved_variables_path`, `blizzard_folder` (`protected_folder`), `chmod_directory`, `unknown_client`, `flatten_destination_exists` (`file_exists`), `flatten_inner_not_a_child`, `plain_symlink_source`, `temp_symlink_outside_quarantine`, `too_many_skill_dirs`, `relative_path`, `dotdot_path`; each asserts the code (or `Refused`), a message naming the path, and an unchanged tree hash.
- `a_repair_never_writes_wtf`: every fix kind aimed at a `WTF/` path (or with a `WTF/` destination) is refused at lowering, before any root, journal or backup exists.
- `lowering_is_deterministic`: lowering each case twice gives equal `Lowered` values (`PartialEq` on the steps, resources and roots).
- `lowering_writes_nothing`: the home's `tree_hash` before and after lowering every case is equal.
- `lower_rs_never_writes`: a source scan of `src/engine/repair/lower.rs`'s production code finds no `mutate`, `WriteSession`, `prune(` or `std::fs` write call.

### Logging

Unit tests only. Each table case is named; each assertion message names the case and prints the input fixes and the lowered result as JSON (`serde_json::to_string_pretty` of the steps), so a failure shows the whole plan. No `TestLog`.

## Considerations

- **Why lowering is where safety is decided.** Recovery can only classify a step whose `pre` and `post` were known before it ran. A predicate captured against the wrong state (the virtual view) would make a crash between two flatten renames unrecognizable: that is exactly the failure M4-D31 exists to prevent. The three-rename unit test is the guard.
- **E6 and the token.** E6's preview reports these steps and puts each in its token's `selection` as `{fm, fix, op, path, to_rel, mode?}` with `to_rel` relative to the quarantine root, and their `pre` predicates in `observed` (M4-D44): lowering must expose the root of every destination (keep it in `LoweredStep` or derivable from the path) and must be deterministic.
- **Hot spots:** `src/engine/repair.rs` and `src/engine/repair/` (E5 → E14 → E7); `src/engine/mod.rs` (one `pub mod` line); `src/engine/testing.rs` (append helpers).
- **Performance:** lowering stats each named path, hashes overwritten files (small: a skill file, a credential is never hashed), and stat-walks each renamed directory once.
- **Privacy:** lowering refuses `WTF/`, so no path below it can enter a journal or history line.

## Dependencies

- Parent: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5 (The repair transaction). Like its leaf, it starts only once E1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`), E11 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.11`), E12 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.12`) and E13 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.13`) are closed: it lowers E1's types into E13's predicates and resources.
- Before it: `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5.1` (the repair paths, `with_skill_dirs`, `is_quarantine`, the symlink flag, `SKILL_DIRS_MAX`).
- Beside it: `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5.3` (the journal format) touches other files and may land in either order.
- After it: `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5.4` (the commit runs what this part lowers).

decided: the questions this part's body left open, and the "Decided while writing this bead" items, as built.

Confirmed as the body states them: the module layout (`src/engine/repair.rs` root plus `src/engine/repair/lower.rs`); `LowerCtx` and `PlannedFix`; `RepairRun` as a plain value; `RefusedReason` as a closed enum with one variant (`wire()` gives `filesystem_mismatch` for E6); `QuarantineRoot::Skill` (`<run>/quarantine/skill/<path relative to the home directory>`); the emptied wrapper of a three-rename flatten parked under its own relative path (`…/Interface/AddOns/X`); an overwriting write's `pre` recording the old mode; a chmod to the mode a file already has dropped, its fix kept in `fixes[]`.

Adjusted or added:
1. **The flatten's provisional folder needed an fsx exception.** fsx's deny-list requires the first component under any `Interface/AddOns` to be a valid folder name, and a leading dot is not one, so `<A>/.omaddons-flatten-<tx>` was refused by the scope table: the three-rename flatten could never have committed, and this bead's own rule ("`ScopeTable::check(Writer::Doctor, …)` refusing a path") refused it at lowering. Because six downstream beads (fences, the crash matrix, undo, the flatten fixer, the M3 compat runs, orphan-temp) are built on the three-rename shape, the shape stays and fsx admits exactly that name: `check_protected` skips the folder-name rule for `Writer::Doctor` when the component is `FLATTEN_PREFIX` plus a transaction id as written (`state::paths::flatten_provisional_tx`; a lowercase id, another suffix or another `.omaddons-` name is still refused, and so is every other writer). `ClientPaths::flatten_provisional(tx)` names it. Rejected: two renames through the client's quarantine (wrapper first, then the inner folder back out), which needs no exception but would have changed every bead listed above.
2. **Same name means the same ignoring ASCII case.** A wrapper whose inner folder has its name in another case (`Foo/foo`) lowers to the three renames, and the lifted folder keeps the inner folder's own spelling (`<A>/foo`): two renames would put `foo` beside `Foo` for a moment, a case collision the game folds.
3. **A flatten destination is checked ignoring case.** Any entry of `<A>` named like the lifted folder in any case (other than the wrapper itself) refuses with `file_exists` naming that entry, as the engine refuses case collisions; the view counts entries earlier steps moved in or out.
4. **`LoweredStep` gained two fields.** `quarantine`: the root a rename moves into (its destination is below it), `None` for writes, chmods and a flatten's renames within AddOns, so E6 can show `to_rel`. `rollback_to`: where s4's rollback moves a file a write creates.
5. **A created file's rollback destination is `<root>/rolled_back/<seq>`** (the file renamed to its step's number, not into a per-step folder), `<root>` the quarantine root of the file's own side; `Lowered.roots` lists `<root>/rolled_back` and its missing ancestors, and the mount check covers that rename. A creating write on a side with no quarantine (the bar widget's folder, which the Doctor writer may write) is refused (`scope_denied`, "has no quarantine on its side").
6. **Further refusals:** a write over anything but a regular file (`scope_denied`); a creating write whose folder does not exist (`io`, nothing created); a rename source or chmod target that is not there (`io`, "nothing is there"); a special file as a rename source (`scope_denied`); a temporary link outside omaddons' own folders (fsx's exception needs `is_app_owned`), `scope_denied`; a flatten whose inner folder is not a direct child of its outer one (`internal`: the fixer built it wrong); a flatten outside a planned client's `Interface/AddOns` (`scope_denied`); a suspension with guards that moves no journal file out of `<state>/journal/` (`internal`: the guards would be lost).
7. **Paths are canonical** in every step, resolved as `mutate()` resolves its targets, and `client_dirs` are canonical too, matching fsx's `Side::Client` and the backup layout. A fix's own path is checked (absolute, UTF-8, no `..`) before it is resolved, since resolving hides a `..`; a failure is `internal` with the step's `seq`.
8. **Privacy:** the `WTF/` refusal names the client's directory, never the path below `WTF/`, and runs before any other check that would print the path.
9. **The view's stamps** come from one stat walk per renamed folder, with the same entries as `StampDigest::compute`, forwarded through the moves lowered so far (moved-out entries dropped, moved-in ones added). They are exact when entries move straight out of or into the stamped folder (every flatten); a move deeper inside would change a folder's mtime the view cannot know, which only two fixes over one path cause, and E6 refuses those (M4-D62). The replay tests run every lowered rename on disk and compare each `pre` and `post` with the real result.
10. **Test names:** the plan's `temp_symlink_outside_quarantine` is `temp_symlink_outside_own_folders`, since every lowered destination is a quarantine and only the source side of fsx's rule can fail; the plan's `wtf_destination` has no fix kind that can name a `WTF/` destination without its source there, so `a_repair_never_writes_wtf` covers every kind with a `WTF/` path, a lowercase `wtf/` and a symlink into `WTF/` instead.

title: The repair journal's format, names and history line, and retention that never touches what a repair keeps
description:
Part 3 of 7 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5 (The repair transaction). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

E5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`) builds M4's repair transaction: the doctor's fixes lowered to primitive filesystem operations, each written ahead in its own journal line, committed under the global lock, rolled back by inverses, and recovered by every lock-taking command (M4-D31), so every repair is as safe and as undoable as an install (G-M4-4, G-M4-6).

This part defines what is persisted: the repair journal's line types and their grammar (`<state>/journal/<tx>.repair.jsonl`, format `1.0`), the never-failing parser recovery and `diagnose` share, the one function that lists repair journals, the history line a repair writes (built from the journal alone, so the commit and recovery's roll-forward write the same bytes), the `store::KINDS` row, and retention's promise never to touch what a repair keeps (M4-D36). It is its own step because the format is the contract between the commit (s4), recovery (s5), `diagnose` (s6), E7's undo and E9's compat test, and it can be built and pinned beside lowering (s2) without touching its files.

## Technical Approach

**Facts this part relies on** (as of `c0ab5e9`, after the leaf's blockers):

- Folder journal lines are tagged by `"type"` (`#[serde(tag = "type")]`, `src/engine/journal.rs:49-60`), and fsx's prune safeguard reads exactly that tag (`src/fsx/prune.rs:408-427`); s1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5.1`) taught prune the repair rule (finished at `committed` or `rolled_back`).
- The folder parser never fails, counts what it cannot read, ignores a torn last line, reads `schema_version` and `target_key` from the raw JSON even when `prepared` does not decode, and treats a newer major as too new (`journal.rs:533-607`, `Parsed::unrecoverable` at `:518-531`). Serde ignores unknown fields inside a known line (no `deny_unknown_fields`).
- The folder listing (`journals()`, `journal.rs:610-635`; E11 made it `journal::list`) keeps only names that `tx_named` parses after stripping `.jsonl` (`:629`), so `<tx>.repair.jsonl` is invisible to it. **Do not change `paths::tx_named`.**
- E1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`) defines `Step` (wire form `{seq, fix, fm, op, path, to?, mode?, pre, post, backup?, activation?, guards?}`), `FixEntry {fix, fm, kind}`, `Mode` (four octal digits), `Identity {ino, born_ns}` (decimal strings), `Sha256` (`sha256:…`), `Stamp` (`stamp:sha256:…`), all `Serialize + Deserialize + JsonSchema`, and a unit snapshot of the `primitives[]` wire form.
- E12 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.12`) made `HistoryEntry.target` an `Option<TargetKey>` and added `targets`, `doctor_run_id` and `repairs: Vec<RepairEntry>` (`src/state/history.rs`), with the repair wire types `RepairEntry { seq, fix, fm, op: RepairOp, path, to?, mode?, pre: RepairEndpoints, post: RepairEndpoints, backup?, activation, target?, folder? }`, `RepairOp`, `RepairEndpoints`, `RepairPredicate`, `RepairIdentity`, `PredicateKind`, the read rule `HistoryEntry::well_formed()` and the touch rule `reach()`. E12 left two things to this leaf: join `RepairEntry` to E1's types through one conversion (with a JSON-equality test), and add `guards` to `RepairEntry` (skipped when empty). E12 also made retention's "most recent transaction" skip target-less lines (`src/engine/retention.rs:151-155`).
- E13 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.13`) defines `ResourceSet` and its lossless text form (a path as is; a subtree with a trailing `/`; `journal:<tx>`; `record:<key>`; `backup:<run_dir>/<seq>`), with `Resource::parse` validating through `from_canonical` (no filesystem access).
- `store::KINDS` (`src/state/store.rs:107-185`) lists every persisted format; the test `every_persisted_format_has_a_kinds_row` (`:435-451`) asserts `found.len() + 1 == KINDS.len()`, the `+ 1` being history's literal row (`("history", super::history::CURRENT)`, `:184`).
- Retention's orphan sweep names transactions through `tx_named` (`retention.rs:365`, `:393`) and keeps a client snapshot whose `AddOns/` or `WTF.previous` is non-empty (`:313-323`); transaction retention names only `<tx>` and `<tx>.wtf` halves (`snapshot_dirs`, `:262-269`); blob eviction lists only `<cache>/blobs/`.

**1. The line types** (`src/engine/repair/journal.rs`, re-exported from `src/engine/repair.rs`):

```rust
pub const FORMAT: SchemaVersion = SchemaVersion::new(1, 0);

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
#[serde(tag = "type", rename_all = "snake_case")]
pub enum RepairLine {
    Prepared(Box<RepairPrepared>),
    Step { seq: u32 },
    Done,
    RolledBack,
    Committed,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize, JsonSchema)]
pub struct RepairPrepared {
    pub format: SchemaVersion,              // "1.0"
    pub tx: TxId,
    pub run: RunId,                         // the invocation's id (history's `run`)
    pub doctor_run_id: String,              // the run directory's name, `<UTC time>Z__<ULID>`
    pub actor: Actor,
    pub reason: Option<String>,             // written as null when absent, as A.9 shows
    pub argv: Vec<String>,
    pub at: Timestamp,
    pub targets: Vec<TargetKey>,
    pub client_dirs: Vec<ClientDirEntry>,   // {dir, target}
    pub resources: ResourcesWire,           // {reads: [text], writes: [text]} in E13's text form
    pub fixes: Vec<FixEntry>,
    pub primitives: Vec<Step>,
}
```

The JSON, as M4-D31 and the milestone's Appendix A.9 fix it (paths here use the plan's placeholders; on disk they are absolute):

```text
{"type":"prepared","format":"1.0","tx":"01M9…","run":"01M9…","doctor_run_id":"2026-10-30T18-03-40Z__01M8S…",
 "actor":"human","reason":null,"argv":["…"],"at":"…","targets":["01M5…"],
 "client_dirs":[{"dir":"<client dir>","target":"01M5…"}],
 "resources":{"reads":[],"writes":["<client dir>/Interface/AddOns/X/","<meta>/snapshots/01M9….repair/quarantine/Interface/AddOns/X/"]},
 "fixes":[{"fix":1,"fm":"fm-external_artifacts-nested-addon-folder","kind":"flatten"}],
 "primitives":[{"seq":1,"fix":1,"fm":"fm-external_artifacts-nested-addon-folder","op":"rename_noreplace",
   "path":"<client dir>/Interface/AddOns/X/Y","to":"<client dir>/Interface/AddOns/Y",
   "pre":{"path":{"kind":"dir","identity":{"ino":"…","born_ns":"…"},"stamp":"stamp:sha256:…"},"to":{"kind":"absent"}},
   "post":{"path":{"kind":"absent"},"to":{"kind":"dir","identity":{"ino":"…","born_ns":"…"}}}}, …]}
{"type":"step","seq":1}
{"type":"step","seq":2}
{"type":"done"}
{"type":"committed"}
```

`rolled_back` replaces `done` and `committed` after an in-process rollback. A set-aside's primitives carry `guards`; an undo's activation primitive carries `"activation":true` (E14, E7). s4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5.4`) builds it from s2's `Lowered`; this part defines only the type, its serialization and its parser, so it does not depend on s2.

**2. The parser** (never fails; one function for recovery, `diagnose`, the fuzz target and E9's compat homes):

```rust
pub struct ParsedRepair {
    pub prepared: Option<RepairPrepared>,
    pub phase: RepairPhase,           // Unprepared | Prepared | Stepped(k) | Done | Committed | RolledBack
    pub steps: u32,                   // step lines recorded, in order 1..=steps
    pub unknown_lines: usize,
    pub torn_tail: bool,
    pub lines: usize,                 // complete lines
    pub format: Option<SchemaVersion>,// read from the raw `prepared` JSON even when it does not decode
}
impl ParsedRepair { pub fn unrecoverable(&self) -> Option<Unrecoverable>; }  // the folder family's TooNew | Unreadable
pub fn parse(text: &str) -> ParsedRepair;
```

The grammar (decided while writing this bead; the plan gives the lines, not their order rules): the first complete line must be `prepared` (else `Unprepared` with no complete line, or unreadable when a complete first line is something else); `step` lines must run `1, 2, …` without gaps and never beyond the primitive count; `done` only after exactly as many step lines as primitives (zero included); `committed` only after `done`; `rolled_back` only after `prepared` or a step line, never after `done`; nothing after `committed` or `rolled_back`. Any other order, a second `prepared`, an unknown line type, or a complete line that does not decode counts as an unknown line, which makes the journal unreadable (M3-D45: never act on a journal this build cannot fully read). A `format` whose major is above `FORMAT`'s is too new (checked first, as `Parsed::unrecoverable` does). A last line cut short (no newline), or a last line that is not JSON, is a torn tail and is ignored: a line is fsynced before what it announces runs, so a torn `step` never ran and a torn `prepared` means nothing ran. Unknown fields inside a known line are ignored (serde's default), so a later minor can add optional fields (E7 will add an undo's `kind` and `reverts`).

**3. The listing** (the only parser of repair journal names):

```rust
/// Every `<state>/journal/<ULID>.repair.jsonl`, by transaction. Nothing else lists them.
pub fn list(paths: &Paths) -> Result<Vec<(TxId, PathBuf)>>;
pub fn read(path: &Path) -> Result<ParsedRepair>;
```

`list` strips exactly `.repair.jsonl` and parses the rest as a `TxId`; `<tx>.jsonl`, `<tx>.wtf.jsonl`, `<tx>.reactivating.jsonl` (E14's) and malformed names are not repair journals. A journal directory that is missing lists as empty; one that cannot be listed is an `io` error (the caller fails closed). Module doc: `paths::tx_named` must never learn `.repair`, because the folder listing would then read repair journals as folder journals and the orphan sweep would judge `.repair` snapshot directories by `AddOns/` and `WTF.previous` alone and could delete a quarantine.

**4. The history line** (built from `prepared` alone):

```rust
pub fn history_line(prepared: &RepairPrepared) -> HistoryEntry;
```

`{schema_version: history::CURRENT (1.0), tx, kind: TxKind::Repair, at: prepared.at, target: None, targets, actor, reason, argv, ops: [], result: Committed, reverts: None, sv_deferred: false, sv_restored: None, created_addons_dir: false, run: Some(prepared.run), backup: None, doctor_run_id: Some(..), repairs}`. Each `repairs[]` entry is the primitive converted to E12's `RepairEntry` with no field renamed, plus `target` (the key of the client dir containing `path` or `to`, from `client_dirs`) and `folder` (the `Interface/AddOns` folder it is or is in, when a valid `FolderName`), plus `guards`. The result must satisfy `HistoryEntry::well_formed()` (`debug_assert!` and a unit test).

- **Joining E12's and E1's types** (E12's request): one conversion `impl From<&Step> for RepairEntry` (or `RepairEntry::from_step(step, client_dirs)`), and the unit test `repairs_entries_equal_the_journal_primitives` asserting that, per op, the conversion's JSON equals the journal primitive's JSON plus `target` and `folder`. Add `guards: Vec<Guard>` to `RepairEntry` (`#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]`). Decided while writing this bead: keep E12's predicate types and convert, unless E1's `Endpoints` serialize identically (then E12's may be replaced by E1's, with E12's golden JSON tests still passing); record which in the close comment.
- The commit (s4) and recovery's roll-forward (s5) both call `history_line(prepared)`, so the line is byte-identical either way (asserted).
- No path below `WTF/` can appear: lowering refuses it (s2); `history_line` also `debug_assert!`s it.

**5. `store::KINDS`** (§7.7): add `("repair_journal", crate::engine::repair::FORMAT)` after the history row, documented "for documentation and schema listing; the repair journal reader, not `store`, reads it". Update `every_persisted_format_has_a_kinds_row` to count two literal rows (`found.len() + 2`, message "every row but history's and repair_journal's"), and add `repair_journal` to the kinds it checks by name.

**6. Retention never touches what a repair keeps** (`src/engine/retention.rs`, M4-D36):

- In `orphans()`, before `tx_named(&name)` in both the stage and the snapshot loops, `if name.ends_with(REPAIR_SUFFIX) { continue; }` with the comment "the repair family's halves are deleted only by `doctor gc` (M4-D36); the suffix is matched to skip, never parsed". (At `c0ab5e9` `tx_named` already returns `None` for these names; the explicit skip keeps the promise if `tx_named` ever changes.)
- `snapshot_dirs` and `dead_snapshots` keep naming only `<tx>` and `<tx>.wtf` halves (a regression test pins it); retention never lists `<cache>/quarantine/` (blob eviction stays in `<cache>/blobs/`).
- README "Retention" (`README.md:2070-2082`) gains one bullet: "A repair's client-side half (`<meta>/snapshots/<tx>.repair/`) and the cache quarantine (`<cache>/quarantine/`) are never pruned by retention or the orphan sweep, however old: only `doctor gc` deletes them." (Decided while writing this bead: the promise is written where it becomes true, though `doctor gc` lands with E8, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.8`; H4 reconciles the wording.)

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every `RepairLine` round-trips through JSON, and a lowered flatten repair's `prepared` line serializes to the documented wire form (snapshot, paths redacted to placeholders).
- [ ] `parse` reads each phase (`Unprepared`, `Prepared`, `Stepped(k)`, `Done`, `Committed`, `RolledBack`), counts every out-of-grammar line as unknown, reports a newer major as too new and an undecodable complete line as unreadable, ignores a torn last line and unknown fields, and never panics.
- [ ] `list` returns exactly the `<ULID>.repair.jsonl` files, sorted; the folder listing over the same directory never returns one; `tx_named` is unchanged.
- [ ] `history_line(prepared)` is `well_formed()`, has `target: null`, `targets`, `ops: []`, `doctor_run_id`, and `repairs[]` equal to the journal primitives (JSON) plus `target`, `folder` and `guards`.
- [ ] `store::KINDS` has the `repair_journal` row and its test passes with two literal rows.
- [ ] Retention never touches a `<meta>/snapshots/<tx>.repair/` half or `<cache>/quarantine/`: aged past every bound, unnamed by history, with an empty `AddOns/`, both survive `retention::run` byte for byte, including blob eviction at a zero cap; a later repair line never takes the most-recent protection from the last folder transaction.
- [ ] README's "Retention" section has the repair bullet, in the same commit.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean.
- [ ] The close comment lists the wire names this part fixes (the file and `repair_journal` 1.0; the five line types; the `prepared` keys; `step.seq`; the `guards` key on history `repairs[]`) and whether E12's predicate types were kept or replaced.

## Background

E5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`) builds M4's repair transaction: the doctor's fixes lowered to primitive filesystem operations, each written ahead in its own journal line, committed under the global lock, rolled back by inverses, and recovered by every lock-taking command (M4-D31), so every repair is as safe and as undoable as an install (G-M4-4, G-M4-6).

This part is the commit: `engine::repair::commit`, which runs a lowered repair (s2) under the caller's global lock, writing the journal format (s3) ahead of every primitive, and rolls back by inverse primitives when a step fails, and the cleanup after the lock is released. It also adds the repair failpoints the crash matrix arms. It is its own step because it is the write side of the protocol, testable in process on its own, while recovery by other processes (s5) builds on the same inverse routine.

## Technical Approach

**Facts this part relies on** (as of `c0ab5e9`, after the leaf's blockers and s1–s3):

- `mutate_with` (`src/fsx/mutate.rs:334-486`): checks (E13's `expect`/`expect_to` predicates among them), `fsx.mutate.checked` (`:373`); an untracked session executes and returns (`:375-396`) without hitting `fsx.mutate.backed_up` (`:436`), `fsx.mutate.executed` (`:452`) or `fsx.mutate.logged` (`:484`); a tracked one takes the before-digest (a directory's `stamp_before` when given), backs an overwritten regular file up to `<backup dir>/<seq>` (`:756-791`), executes, logs one `ActionRecord` (also on failure, `ok: false`), and `seq` comes from the session's own counter starting at 1 (`src/fsx/session.rs:63-68`). A rename fsyncs both parents (`:843-845`); s1 made a tracked chmod fsync its file.
- `history::append(s, paths, entry)` appends one line with one fsync and closes a torn tail in the same write (`src/state/history.rs:252-258`); the History row admits `Writer::Doctor` (`src/fsx/scope.rs:115-116`).
- `doorbell::ring(paths, command, actor)` (`src/state/doorbell.rs:40`); `history_tail::rebuild_if_stale(paths, command, actor)` (`src/state/history_tail.rs:316`), run after the lock is released.
- prune under `LockUse::Own(&inflight)` deletes only victims named for the caller's transaction and refuses an unfinished journal (`src/fsx/prune.rs:104-136`); s1 taught it `Kind::RepairJournal` (finished at `committed` or `rolled_back`). `PRUNE_CALLERS` (`tests/single_writer.rs:830-863`) must list every file that calls `prune()`, and no listed file name may contain "doctor" (`:868`).
- `engine::tx::FAILPOINTS` is checked against a scan of `failpoint::hit("engine.` in `src/engine` and `src/backup` (`src/engine/tx.rs:2240-2254`); the `doctor.*` names are outside it. `src/doctor/mod.rs` exists (E1).
- s2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5.2`) gives `RepairTx`, `RepairRun`, `Lowered` (steps with `pre`/`post`, reserved backups, roots, resources, targets, client dirs); s3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5.3`) gives `RepairLine`, `RepairPrepared`, `history_line`, `parse`, `Paths::journal_repair`.

**The API** (`src/engine/repair/commit.rs`):

```rust
pub struct RepairMeta { pub run: RunId, pub actor: Actor, pub reason: Option<String>, pub argv: Vec<String>, pub command: &'static str }
pub enum RepairOutcome {
    Committed { tx: TxId, primitives: u32, bytes_backed_up: u64, backups: Vec<(u32, PathBuf)> },
    RolledBack { tx: TxId, failed_seq: Option<u32>, cause: Error, backups_restored: u32 },
}
pub struct RepairCleanup { /* the RepairTx (journal path, in-flight lock), command, actor */ }
pub fn commit(lock: &GlobalLockGuard, run: &RepairRun, rtx: RepairTx, lowered: &Lowered, meta: &RepairMeta)
    -> Result<(RepairOutcome, RepairCleanup)>;
impl RepairCleanup { pub fn finish(self, paths: &Paths) -> Vec<Warning>; }
```

`commit` takes `&GlobalLockGuard`: the type proves the lock is held, and it is the only path by which repair primitives reach `mutate()` (§6.12: "the forbidden transitions are absent by construction"). `Err` means the rollback itself could not finish, or a failure after a durable `done` could not be rolled forward in process: the journal stays for the next lock-taking command, and `details.journal_pending` names the transaction.

**Two sessions** (decided while writing this bead): a **tracked** `WriteSession::tx(tx, Writer::Doctor, &scopes, SnapshotRoots::for_repair(run.dir.join("backups"), &tx), run.dir.join("actions.jsonl"))` runs the primitives and nothing else; an **untracked** `WriteSession::untracked(Writer::Doctor, &scopes, "repair journal")` writes the roots, the journal lines and the history line. So `actions.jsonl` holds exactly the repair's primitives (§6.12: "exactly what undo reverts"), its `seq` equals the primitive's `seq`, each overwriting write's backup lands at the path lowering reserved (asserted: `record.backup == step.backup`, else the step fails as `internal`), and `fsx.mutate.{backed_up,executed,logged}@k` address primitive `k` exactly. `scopes` = `ScopeTable::new(paths, &client dirs, None)?.with_skill_dirs(&skill dirs)`.

**The commit, in order** (the global lock is held by the caller throughout):

1. **Revalidate, writing nothing:** `run.dir` exists; every `lowered.client_dirs` entry's marker still names its target (`discover::registry::read_marker`), else `scope_denied` "… whose marker is not target …'s"; the mount checks of s2 again (`fsx::mount_id`); E1's `validate_steps`. Any failure returns `Err` with nothing written (the in-flight lock is released when `rtx` drops).
2. **Roots** (untracked): `ensure_dir_all` for every `lowered.roots` entry (`<run>/backups/`, the quarantine destinations' parents, `<meta>/snapshots/<tx>.repair/{files,quarantine/…}`, `<cache>/quarantine/<run id>/…`, the `rolled_back/` parents). They are doctor-owned, never primitives, and only `doctor gc` (E8, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.8`) removes them.
3. **`prepared`** (untracked): `ensure_dir_all(<state>/journal/)`, then `AppendFile` of the serialized `RepairLine::Prepared` and a newline to `Paths::journal_repair(tx)` (the file is created by the append). `RepairPrepared` is built here from `lowered`, `rtx.tx()`, `run` and `meta`, with `at = Timestamp::now()`. Failpoint **`doctor.repair.prepared`**.
4. **For each step `k`** (in `seq` order):
   1. append `{"type":"step","seq":k}` (untracked; fsynced by the append); failpoint **`doctor.repair.step`**;
   2. `mutate_with` in the tracked session, with `MutateOpts { expect: Some(pre of path), expect_to: Some(pre.to) for a rename, stamp_before/stamp_after: the recorded stamp for a directory rename, temp_symlink: true for a `.omaddons-` link rename, ..Default }` and `Op::WriteFile { content, mode }` (`Expect::Absent` for a creating write publishes without clobbering), `Op::Chmod { mode }`, or `Op::Rename { to, mode: RenameMode::NoReplace }`. The content of a write comes from the `PlannedFix` (`Lowered` keeps it beside its step; it is never journaled).
   3. on `Err` (a predicate failed, an I/O error, `Unsupported`, `EXDEV`): roll back (below), with `failed_seq = k`.
5. **`done`** (untracked); failpoint **`doctor.repair.done`**. An error appending `done` rolls back all primitives (`failed_seq: None`). G3 (`omad-7ccp`) later inserts `session.finish()` and the commit window's barrier immediately before this line; until then every fsx operation above is durable when it returns (renames fsync both parents, writes fsync file and directory, a tracked chmod fsyncs its file, every append fsyncs).
6. **History:** `history::append(&mut untracked, paths, &history_line(&prepared))`; failpoint **`doctor.repair.history`**. Then append `committed`; failpoint **`doctor.repair.committed`**. A failure in this step runs `inverse::roll_forward` (below) for this journal in process; when that succeeds the outcome is `Committed`, else `Err` with `details.journal_pending`.
7. Return `(Committed { tx, primitives: n, bytes_backed_up, backups }, RepairCleanup)`.

**`RepairCleanup::finish`** (called by E6 after it releases the lock, §6.14.2 step 3): ring the doorbell with `meta.command` and `meta.actor` (E6 passes `"doctor fix"`); `fsx::prune(scopes, PruneReason::PostCommitCleanup, &[journal, inflight lock], LockUse::Own(&inflight))` from `commit.rs`; then `history_tail::rebuild_if_stale`. A cleanup failure is a warning, never a failure (the transaction stands); the next recovery prunes a committed journal. `src/engine/repair/commit.rs` joins `PRUNE_CALLERS` with the reason "a repair's own journal and in-flight lock, after commit or rollback, under its own lock".

**Rollback in process** (decided while writing this bead: one routine for in-process rollback and for recovery, in a new `src/engine/repair/inverse.rs` this part adds: `roll_back(s: &mut WriteSession, view: &mut impl LiveView, prepared: &RepairPrepared, recorded: u32) -> Result<u32>` (the steps inverted) and `roll_forward(s, paths, journal: &Path, prepared, torn_tail: bool) -> Result<()>` (close the torn history tail, append `history_line(prepared)` only if the **parsed** history holds no entry with this transaction, then `committed` unless the journal's tail was torn). Both run in an untracked `Writer::Doctor` session; s5's recovery calls them, so the crash matrix exercises the same code that rolls back and forward in process. `LiveView` is E11's trait (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.11`); the disk implementation reads through E13's `Expect::check`. For each step whose `step` line was written, `k` down to 1, classify it against the live paths, comparing each endpoint's kind and identity plus the one part the primitive changes (a write's `sha256`, a chmod's `mode`; a rename's directory `stamp` is not compared, since it says nothing about whether the rename ran): `post` holds → invert; `pre` holds → skip; neither → stop. Inverses, each run through `mutate_with` with the step's `post` as its `expect`:

| Primitive | Inverse |
|---|---|
| `WriteFile` over a file | check that the reserved backup is a regular file whose `sha256` equals `pre.sha256` (else stop), then `WriteFile` of the backup's bytes with `pre.mode` |
| `WriteFile` that created a file | `RenameNoReplace` into `<its side's quarantine root>/rolled_back/<seq>/<relative path>` (never a delete) |
| `Chmod` | `Chmod(pre.mode)`, expecting `post` (same identity, new mode) |
| `RenameNoReplace` | rename `to` back to `path` with `RENAME_NOREPLACE` (`temp_symlink` for a link), expecting `post.to` at `to` and absence at `path` |

After the walk, append `rolled_back` (untracked), write no history line, and return `RolledBack { tx, failed_seq, cause, backups_restored }` (`backups_restored` = the number of inverted steps; E6 reports `DONE_FAILED`, exit 3, M4-D34). A step in neither state stops the walk: nothing more is inverted, no `rolled_back` is appended, and `commit` returns `Err(internal)` with `details {journal_pending: tx, reason: "step_unrecognized", target: null}` and the message naming `journal step <k>` (E11's convention), leaving the journal for recovery and for F1/F2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1`, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.2`); E6 maps it to its `corrupt_rollback` state. The tracked session's `actions.jsonl` keeps the forward attempt (the failed line with `ok: false`); the rollback is recorded by `rolled_back` and `backups_restored`.

**Other journals** (decided while writing this bead): `commit` neither recovers nor refuses because of other journals. E6 runs the disclosed recoveries under the same lock hold before it commits (M4-D37, M4-D45); E14's fences (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14`) refuse writes that overlap a stuck repair's resources; and F2's set-aside must be able to commit while a stuck journal exists. Each primitive's predicates are the last line of defense.

**The repair failpoints** (debug only, `src/fsx/failpoint.rs` semantics, `@N` = the Nth hit): `doctor.repair.prepared` (after `prepared` is durable, before the first step line), `doctor.repair.step` (after step line `k` is durable, before primitive `k` is checked), `doctor.repair.done` (after `done`, before the history line), `doctor.repair.history` (after the history line, before `committed`), `doctor.repair.committed` (after `committed`, before returning), and `doctor.recover.step`, hit by `inverse::roll_back` after each inverse (recovery's crash point, which s5 and s7 arm in the recovering command). Decided while writing this bead: whichever of E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, the doctor runtime) and this part lands first creates `pub const FAILPOINTS: &[&str]` in `src/doctor/mod.rs` (eleven names in all, each added by its owner as it lands: this part's five plus `doctor.recover.step`; E3's `doctor.run.staged`, `doctor.run.published` and `doctor.detector.panic`; E6's pause point `doctor.fix.planned`; E8's pause point `doctor.gc.planned`) and its test `doctor_failpoints_match_the_source`, which collects every `failpoint::hit("doctor.` in the production code of `src/doctor/**` and `src/engine/repair.rs` + `src/engine/repair/**` (using the crate's `source_scan` helpers, as the engine scan does) and asserts equality. `engine::tx::FAILPOINTS` is unchanged.

**What not to do:** never append a journal or history line through the tracked session; never delete (a created file's rollback is a quarantine); never call `commit` without the lock (the signature prevents it); never let `commit` write before step 1's checks pass.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Each of the eight fix kinds (write over, write create, chmod, quarantine of a state file, of a client directory and of a temp symlink, two-rename flatten, three-rename flatten) commits in process: the live paths reach the after state, the journal holds `prepared`, one `step` per primitive, `done` and `committed`, history has exactly one `well_formed()` repair line equal to `history_line(prepared)`, and cleanup prunes the journal and the in-flight lock.
- [ ] `actions.jsonl` holds exactly one line per primitive, `seq` 1..n equal to the primitives' `seq`, and every overwriting write's backup is at its reserved path and byte-identical to the file it replaced.
- [ ] A chmod over a same-mode replacement file (replaced between lowering and commit) fails its identity predicate: the outcome is `RolledBack { failed_seq: Some(1) }`, the replacement keeps its mode and bytes, no history line is written, and the journal ends `rolled_back` and is pruned.
- [ ] A failed step rolls back every step that ran, in reverse: a write's bytes and mode restored from its backup, a created file moved under `rolled_back/<seq>/` (never deleted), a chmod's old mode restored, a rename moved back; `backups_restored` counts them; the subject is the whole before state.
- [ ] A rollback that meets a step in neither state stops, appends nothing, and returns `internal` with `details.reason: "step_unrecognized"` and `details.journal_pending`, the journal kept.
- [ ] A failure after `done` (the history append failing once) still ends `Committed` with exactly one history line.
- [ ] Revalidation failures (missing run directory, changed marker, a mount that changed, an invalid step) write nothing at all.
- [ ] `doctor::FAILPOINTS` lists the five `doctor.repair.*` names and `doctor.recover.step`, and the source scan agrees; `src/engine/repair/commit.rs` is in `PRUNE_CALLERS` with its reason.
- [ ] The doorbell rings with the command given, and `history_tail` is rebuilt after cleanup.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean.
- [ ] The close comment lists the failpoint names and the internal API (`RepairMeta`, `RepairOutcome`, `RepairCleanup`, `commit`).

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

In `src/engine/repair/commit.rs`'s `tests` module, on `src/engine/testing.rs`'s `repair_home()` (s2), each test lowering its fixes, taking `GlobalLock::acquire`, committing, dropping the lock and calling `finish`:

- `each_fix_kind_commits`: table over the eight kinds; per case: outcome `Committed`, the after state of every subject path (compared as `kind + sha256 + mode` for files, `tree_hash` for directories, the link target for links), journal lines before cleanup equal to `[prepared, step 1..n, done, committed]`, the journal and in-flight lock gone after `finish`, one history line equal to `history_line(prepared)`.
- `the_actions_log_holds_only_the_primitives`: for `flatten_three` and `write_over`, `actions.jsonl` has n lines, `seq` 1..n, each `ok: true`, paths equal to the primitives', and no line for the journal, the roots or history.
- `the_reserved_backup_holds_the_replaced_bytes`: `write_over`: `<run>/backups/1` equals the old `SKILL.md` bytes.
- `a_chmod_over_a_same_mode_replacement_fails_its_identity_predicate`: lower a chmod of the credential (0644 → 0600), replace the file with a new inode of mode 0644 (write a temp file, rename it over), commit: `RolledBack { failed_seq: Some(1) }`, the replacement is 0644 with its bytes, no history line, journal `[prepared, step 1, rolled_back]` before cleanup.
- `a_changed_path_rolls_back_every_step_that_ran`: `flatten_two`; between lowering and commit add a file inside `Wrap/` so step 2's stamp predicate fails: step 1 is inverted, `Inner` is back inside `Wrap`, `backups_restored: 1`.
- `a_failed_step_after_a_write_restores_the_backup_and_mode`: two fixes, a write over `SKILL.md` (old mode 0640, new 0644) and a quarantine whose victim vanished after lowering: the write is inverted, `SKILL.md` has its old bytes and mode 0640.
- `a_created_file_is_rolled_back_into_quarantine_never_deleted`: a creating write of `SKILL.md` followed by a failing step: `SKILL.md` is absent, `<run>/quarantine/skill/…/rolled_back/1/…/SKILL.md` holds the written bytes.
- `an_error_after_execute_is_rolled_back_by_its_predicates`: `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS`-style in-process override (`failpoint::with_spec("fsx.mutate.executed=error@1", …)`) on a chmod: the chmod ran, the step returned an error, rollback classifies it as ran (`post` holds) and restores the old mode.
- `roll_back_stops_at_a_step_in_neither_state` (`inverse.rs`): lower `flatten_two`, run both primitives through a tracked session as `commit` does, move `<A>/Inner` elsewhere (step 1 is now in neither state), call `roll_back`: step 2 is inverted (`Wrap` back), then `Err(internal)` with `details.reason == "step_unrecognized"` and `journal step 1` in the message.
- `a_rollback_that_meets_an_unrecognized_step_stops_and_keeps_the_journal`: `flatten_two` committed with `fsx.mutate.executed=error@2` and a `#[cfg(test)]` thread-local hook in `commit.rs`, run just before the rollback walk, that moves `<A>/Inner` away: `commit` returns that `Err`, and the journal is kept as `[prepared, step 1, step 2]` with no `rolled_back`.
- `a_failure_after_done_rolls_forward_in_process`: `failpoint::with_spec("doctor.repair.history=error", …)` (the history line appended, then an error) and, separately, an `fsx.append_durable.before=error@N` aimed at the history append: outcome `Committed`, exactly one history line, journal ends `committed`.
- `revalidation_writes_nothing`: cases `run_dir_missing`, `marker_changed`, `mount_changed` (the seam), `invalid_step` (a hand-built step with a gap in `seq`): `Err`, tree hash of the home unchanged, no journal, no roots.
- `the_roots_exist_before_prepared`: with `doctor.repair.prepared=error`, the roots exist, the journal holds `prepared` then `rolled_back`, nothing else changed.
- `cleanup_rings_the_doorbell_and_prunes_under_its_own_lock`: after `finish`, the doorbell file names the command and actor, the journal and in-flight lock are gone, `history_tail` covers the new line.
- `doctor_failpoints_match_the_source` (`src/doctor/mod.rs`): the scan described above.
- `commit_rs_writes_only_through_fsx`: covered by `tests/single_writer.rs` (no new pattern needed); its `PRUNE_CALLERS` entry is the change.

### Logging

Unit tests only: one name per case; assertion messages print the case, the journal's lines, the `actions.jsonl` lines and the subject's state before and after (as JSON), so a failing rollback shows which step was classified how. No `TestLog`.

## Considerations

- **Risk 1** (the repair journal has a recovery bug that loses a repaired file): this part's half is the write side. The predicates are checked by fsx immediately before each operation (E13), every step is written ahead, and the rollback is one routine with recovery's. The crash matrix (s7) proves it across processes.
- **Why two sessions:** one session would interleave journal appends with primitives in `actions.jsonl`, shift `seq`, put backups where lowering did not reserve them, and make `fsx.mutate.*@k` count journal lines. The assertion on the backup path catches any regression.
- **Durability before `done`:** today every operation is durable when it returns; G3 will group-commit `actions.jsonl` and defer directory fsyncs to barriers before `prepared`, `done`, `committed`, `rolled_back`, the history line and every step line that follows a rename (M4-D54). Keep those points as separate, commented lines in `commit.rs` so G3 has one place to insert each barrier.
- **Hot spots:** `src/engine/repair/` (E5 → E14 → E7), `src/doctor/mod.rs` (E1, E3: append rows), `tests/single_writer.rs` (one `PRUNE_CALLERS` row).
- **Privacy:** no path below `WTF/` reaches here (s2 refuses it); messages name paths under `<state>`, `<config>`, `<cache>`, skill dirs and `Interface/` only.
