title: `omaddons doctor undo [<run>]`, and `undo`'s refusal of a doctor run id
description:
Part 4 of 7 of `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7` (Undo of repairs). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

E7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7`, undo of repairs) makes every doctor repair undoable through `omaddons undo` (s1–s3: `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7.1`, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7.2`, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7.3`). The doctor contract also wants an undo addressed by the doctor's own run: the run id is what `doctor fix` prints, what `undo.sh` in a fix run's directory runs, and what an agent following the doctor loop holds.

**This part adds the command `omaddons doctor undo [<run>] [--dry-run]`**, which resolves a run to its transaction and calls the same engine code; with no run it selects the newest fix run whose repair is still in effect; `latest` is refused with a runnable fix; undoing a run already undone is a no-op with exit 0. It also adds `undo`'s refusal of a doctor run id (its fix names this command). It is its own step because DEC-1 requires every registry touch point of a new command path in one commit, and none of them belongs to the engine work before it.

**The rules it implements** (restated):

- **M4-D46:** "`omaddons doctor undo [<run>]` resolves the run to its transaction and calls the same code. Without a run, it selects the newest run of kind `fix` whose repair is committed and not yet undone. 'The newest run' would usually be a diagnose, since every triage and preview makes one, and a diagnose has nothing to undo. `latest` is not accepted as a run (usage error, fix `omaddons doctor undo`). Undoing a run already undone is a no-op with exit 0 (the doctor contract's undo idempotence). `doctor ls` reports `undo_complete`. The undo writes its own run directory of kind `undo` (M4-D33). There is no `--no-strict`." Rejected: the doctor contract's `doctor undo latest` (the `latest` symlink is for reading reports and may point at a diagnose) and `--no-strict`.
- **§6.11:** "`undo`. Without a run, it selects the newest run of kind `fix` whose committed repair is not yet undone. It never selects a diagnose, which has no transaction." The JSON report keys of `undo`: "`run_id` (the undo's own run), `reverted_run, tx, undo_tx, state, actions_taken, already_undone`; under `--dry-run`, `actions_planned[]`, with `commands[]` offering `omaddons undo <tx> --dry-run` for a preview that stores a bindable plan".
- **M4-D22:** `doctor undo` neither stores nor binds: "its bound form is `omaddons undo <tx> --dry-run` then `apply`, which stores the plan, and `doctor undo --dry-run` offers exactly that in `commands[]`".
- **M4-D34:** doctor JSON puts the report at the top level, with the general envelope keys around it (`{ok, schema_version, tool_version, command, exit_code, <report keys>, error?, warnings, commands, meta}`).
- **M4-D40:** the doctor exit dictionary (`0 healthy, 1 findings_present, 2 fix_partial, 3 fix_failed_rolled_back, 4 refused_unsafe, 5 concurrency_lost, 6 online_required, 64 usage_error, 66 no_input, 73 cannot_create, 74 io_error`) and the total `exit_for(ErrorCode)`.
- **§6.14.4, two kinds of run:** history's `run` (and `undo --run`) is the invocation's ULID; `doctor_run_id` is the run-directory name with its `…Z__<ULID>` shape, "so `omaddons undo --run <a doctor run id>` is recognized and refused with the fix `omaddons doctor undo <id>`".
- **M4-D37:** `doctor undo` does not revert a delegated action; a rolled-forward transaction is undone with `omaddons undo <tx>`.
- **M4-D12 / M4-D15:** a fix that keeps the user's verb is marked `UsageFix::UserVerb`; a usage fix must run, not just parse.

**Facts this part relies on** (as of `c0ab5e9`, plus blockers):

- `app::COMMANDS` (`src/app/mod.rs:121-165`) lists every path with `{name, group, mutates}` (A1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1`, adds `dictionary`, `exits`, `data`, `stores_plan`, `network`); `command_name` and dispatch arms are in the same file; `CLI_PATHS` (`omarchy/Model.js:134-177`) must equal it (`tests/omarchy_widget.rs:30`), with `binds` equal to membership in `BINDING_COMMANDS` (`tests/omarchy_widget.rs:44-48`).
- The CLI refuses `--if-match` on any path outside `BINDING_COMMANDS` (`src/cli.rs:309-338`), so `doctor undo --if-match …` is already a usage error once the path exists.
- E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`) delivers the `doctor` clap tree in `src/cli.rs` / `src/app/doctor.rs`, `DoctorRunId` (`parse` accepts exactly `<YYYY-MM-DDTHH-MM-SSZ>__<ULID>`), `DoctorEnvelope`, `DoctorOutcome`, `DoctorFailure`, `emit_doctor`, `doctor::Exit`, `exit_for`, the contract harness's doctor mode (`common::doctor::check_envelope`), and `support::stable()`'s `<run>` redaction. E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`) adds `doctor fix` beside it and the fix report (`tx`, `delegated[]`).
- s2 delivers `UndoReport` in `src/doctor/report.rs` and `undo_repair`; s1 `undo_state`.
- `resolve_run` (`src/app/history.rs:459-496`) and `by_prefix` (`src/app/undo.rs:562-597`) match only ULIDs; `MIN_PREFIX` is 8 (`src/app/history.rs:499`).
- The existing tests that hold the registry: `tests/cli_skeleton.rs` (literals and bare-help snapshots), `src/app/help.rs`'s planned-layout test, `tests/omarchy_widget.rs`.

## Technical Approach

### 1. The command (DEC-1, one commit)

1. **clap** (`src/cli.rs`, E3's `DoctorCommand`): `Undo(DoctorUndoArgs)` with

   ```rust
   #[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, clap::Args)]
   pub struct DoctorUndoArgs {
       /// The doctor run to undo: its run id, as `doctor fix` printed it
       /// (default: the newest fix run whose repair is still in effect)
       #[arg(value_name = "RUN")]
       pub run: Option<String>,
   }
   ```

   About: "Undo a doctor repair: revert a fix run (or the newest one), strictly". `after_long_help` examples: `omaddons doctor undo`, `omaddons doctor undo 2026-10-30T18-03-40Z__01M8S…`, `omaddons doctor undo --dry-run`, and the bound form `omaddons undo <tx> --dry-run` then `omaddons apply <plan>`. `--dry-run` is the global flag.
2. **`COMMANDS` row** `doctor undo`: group Change, beside `doctor fix`; `mutates: true`; `dictionary: Doctor`; `exits: [0, 3, 4, 5, 64, 66, 73, 74]`; `data`: the `UndoReport` schema; `stores_plan: false`; `network: None`.
3. **`command_name`** `"doctor undo"` and the dispatch arm through `emit_doctor`.
4. **Help layout:** the planned-layout test and the doctor help list `undo` after `fix`.
5. **Contract matrix rows** (doctor mode), with snapshots: success (`doctor undo` on a home with one committed repair), dry run (`doctor undo --dry-run`), failure (`doctor undo latest`, `usage`, exit 64), and `undo --run <doctor run id>` (`usage`, general exit 2).
6. **`special.rs`:** no read-only row (the path mutates); `a_dry_run_leaves_the_state_directory_as_it_was` (`tests/contract/special.rs:251`) gains `doctor undo --dry-run` and `doctor undo <run> --dry-run` on a home with a committed repair (the whole state directory unchanged, `<state>/doctor/` included).
7. **`cli_skeleton` literals** for the new path.
8. **`CLI_PATHS` row** in `omarchy/Model.js`: `"doctor undo": { "mutates": true, "destructive": true, "binds": false }` (destructive like `undo`; not in `BINDING_COMMANDS`; the widget has no template for it: Undo last runs `undo`).
9. **README** `### doctor undo` (below).

### 2. Arguments (raised before anything is read beyond the arguments and history)

| Argument | Result |
|---|---|
| none | bare selection (section 4) |
| a `DoctorRunId` | resolve (section 3) |
| `latest` (any case) | `usage` "`latest` names the newest report, which may be a diagnose; `doctor undo` takes a run", fix `omaddons doctor undo` (bare), marked `UsageFix::UserVerb` |
| a `TxId` that is a repair-family line's tx | `usage` "<tx> is a transaction; `doctor undo` takes the doctor run that made it", fix `omaddons doctor undo <that line's doctor_run_id>` (same verb) |
| anything else | `usage` "<v> is not a doctor run id", fix `omaddons help doctor undo` |

The doctor dictionary maps `usage` to 64.

### 3. Resolving a run to its transaction

- `<state>/doctor/runs/<run>/report.json` (read bounded as E3's `--since` reads a report): its `kind` and `tx`. A `fix` or `undo` run with a `tx` resolves to that tx.
- **Fallback:** no directory, or no terminal `report.json` (an aborted run, or a run gc deleted): the history line whose `doctor_run_id` equals `<run>`. Decided while writing this bead: history is the authority on what committed, so a run whose report is missing but whose repair committed (a fix killed after `done`, rolled forward by recovery) is still undoable.
- Neither → `not_found` "there is no doctor run <run>" (66), fix `omaddons doctor ls` once E4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4`) has landed, `omaddons history` before (whichever of E4 and this leaf lands second switches it).
- **Nothing to undo** (exit 0, `DONE_OK`, nothing written, `run_id: null`, `undo_tx: null`, `actions_taken: 0`): a `diagnose` run (`tx: null`); a fix run whose repair rolled back or never committed (no history line; `tx` the fix's tx); a repair line with no primitives. Human: "run <id> changed nothing; nothing to undo".
- **Already undone** (exit 0, `DONE_OK`, `already_undone: true`, nothing written, `run_id: null`): s1's `undo_state` is `UndoneBy(U)`; `undo_tx: U`. Human: "run <id> was already undone by <U>; nothing to do".
- Otherwise: `undo_repair` (s2) with `UndoRequest { selector: Tx(tx), command: "doctor undo", run: RunId::new(), .. }`. An in-effect race (another process undid it between selection and the lock) surfaces from the engine as s1's "already undone" `undo_conflict`; `doctor undo` maps that one case to the idempotent no-op above (exit 0), so two concurrent `doctor undo <run>` both exit 0.

### 4. Bare selection

From history (already read by the command): the newest line with `kind: repair` (a fix run's line; undo runs write `undo` lines), `result: committed`, `undo_state == InEffect`. Diagnose runs write no history, so an intervening diagnose never changes the selection. Decided while writing this bead: selecting from history rather than listing run directories, because history alone says what committed and what is undone, and its reader is already bounded. Nothing in effect → exit 0, `reverted_run: null`, `tx: null`, human "nothing to undo: no fix run has a committed repair still in effect". So bare `doctor undo` twice reverts the newest repair, then reports nothing (the first undo's line is `kind: undo`, which bare selection skips; the repair is no longer in effect).

### 5. The report and the output

`UndoReport` (s2), rendered through E3's `DoctorEnvelope` with the report keys at the top level:

```json
{"ok":true,"schema_version":"1.0","tool_version":"0.1.0","command":"doctor undo","exit_code":0,
 "run_id":"2026-10-30T18-05-12Z__01MA…","reverted_run":"2026-10-30T18-03-40Z__01M8S…",
 "tx":"01M9…","undo_tx":"01MA…","state":"DONE_OK","actions_taken":2,"already_undone":false,
 "warnings":[],
 "commands":[{"action":"undo","command":"omaddons undo 01MA…","argv":["omaddons","undo","01MA…"],"destructive":false}],
 "meta":{"elapsed_ms":41,"offline":false}}
```

- **`--dry-run`:** `run_id: null`, `undo_tx: null`, `actions_taken: 0`, `state: "DONE_OK"`, plus `actions_planned[]` (A.5's primitive shape `{seq, fix, fm, op, path, to?, mode?, pre, post, backup, bytes}`, one per inverse in execution order; `backup: null`, because the undo's own reservations need its run directory, which a dry run does not create; `bytes` the size an inverse write would back up), and `commands[]` = `undo` → `omaddons undo <tx> --dry-run` (the bindable preview that stores a plan). The dry run runs s1's checks and refuses as the real run would.
- **Delegated recoveries** (M4-D37). Decided while writing this bead: when the reverted fix run's `report.json` lists `delegated[]` entries with `outcome: rolled_forward`, the human output adds "this run also completed tx <T> (an interrupted change); `doctor undo` does not revert it: omaddons undo <T>", and `commands[]` adds `undo` → `omaddons undo <T>` for each.
- **States and exits:** `DONE_OK` (0) for an undo, a no-op or a dry run; `DONE_FAILED` (3) when the undo's commit rolled back (the step's error in `error`); `REFUSING` (4) with `error` for a refusal found after the run directory exists; `LOCK_LOST` (5) with `locked` when the global lock is not acquired within 5 s; a refusal before STARTING is the envelope plus `error` and no report keys (E3's rule). Codes through `exit_for`: `undo_conflict`, `game_running`, `scope_denied` → 4; `locked` → 5; `usage` → 64; `not_found`, `target_not_found` → 66; the run directory → 73; `io`, `internal`, `state_corrupt` → 74.
- **Human output:**

  ```text
  $ omaddons doctor undo
  undid repair 01M9… from run 2026-10-30T18-03-40Z__01M8S… (2 renames)
  run 2026-10-30T18-05-12Z__01MA… · tx 01MA… · redo: omaddons undo 01MA…
  ```

  The dry run: "would undo repair 01M9… from run …: 2 renames", then one line per primitive (at most 10), then "bind it: omaddons undo 01M9… --dry-run, then apply its plan".
- `undo_tx` is declared volatile in `contract::VOLATILE` (E3 declared `run_id`).

### 6. `undo`'s refusal of a doctor run id (`src/app/undo.rs`)

From the arguments, before `World::load` or any history read: when `args.run` or `args.tx` parses as a `DoctorRunId`, `usage` "<v> is a doctor run directory; `undo` takes a transaction or a run of the history", fix `omaddons doctor undo <v>` marked `UsageFix::UserVerb` (C1's mark, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.1`: the same undo of the same run through its doctor form; if the mark is not on `main` yet, the plain suggestion, and whichever of C1 and this leaf lands second marks it).

### 7. `doctor ls`

`runs[].undo_complete` (a fix run whose repair `undo_state` is `UndoneBy`) and `runs[].reverted_run` (an undo run's `report.json`): if E4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4`) is on `main`, wire them to s1's `undo_state` and the undo report here; otherwise E4 does when it lands (whichever lands second).

### 8. README `### doctor undo` (same commit)

Usage and arguments; that it is the same undo as `omaddons undo <tx>` (the strict checks, the refusal reasons, the run directory of kind `undo`); bare selection ("the newest fix run whose repair is still in effect, whatever diagnoses ran since"); `latest` refused and why; idempotence (exit 0, `already_undone`); `--dry-run` and the bound form (`omaddons undo <tx> --dry-run`, then `apply`); that it never reverts a delegated recovery (`omaddons undo <tx>` does); its exit codes in the doctor dictionary; the JSON report. `### undo [TX]` gains one sentence: `undo --run` takes history runs; given a doctor run id it answers `usage` with the fix `omaddons doctor undo <id>`.

### 9. The guide and the corpus

- Once B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`) has landed: regenerate `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` (the command list shows `doctor undo`).
- Once C4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4`) has landed (whichever lands second adds them), rows in `tests/contract/intent_corpus.rs`: `omaddons doctor undo latest` → `usage` → `omaddons doctor undo` → 0, and `omaddons undo --run <a doctor run id>` → `usage` → `omaddons doctor undo <id>` → 0, each on `intent_home()` with one committed repair made by E6's `fm-test-write` (debug build, `OMADDONS_TEST_FIXERS=1`) through the corpus's per-row setup (add a setup hook to the corpus harness if it has none). An erroring row's home hashes unchanged; the fix runs on an independent copy.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `omaddons doctor undo [<run>]` exists with every DEC-1 touch point in one commit: the clap variant, the `COMMANDS` row with every M4 field (`dictionary: Doctor`, `exits: [0, 3, 4, 5, 64, 66, 73, 74]`, `data`, `stores_plan: false`, `network: None`), `command_name` and dispatch, the help layout, contract matrix rows (success, dry run, `latest` usage) with snapshots, `cli_skeleton` literals, the `CLI_PATHS` row `{mutates: true, destructive: true, binds: false}`, and README `### doctor undo`.
- [ ] `doctor undo <run>` resolves a fix run (from its report, or from history when the report is missing) and reverts it through the same code as `omaddons undo <tx>`, with its own run directory of kind `undo`; the report has `run_id, reverted_run, tx, undo_tx, state, actions_taken, already_undone` at the top level.
- [ ] Bare `doctor undo` selects the newest committed repair still in effect, also after an intervening `doctor` diagnose; a second bare `doctor undo` selects nothing and exits 0 saying so; `doctor undo <run>` twice gives exit 0 with `already_undone: true` the second time, and nothing written.
- [ ] `doctor undo latest` is `usage` (64) with fix `omaddons doctor undo`; a repair's tx is `usage` with fix `omaddons doctor undo <its run>`; an unknown run id is `not_found` (66); `doctor undo --if-match <token>` is `usage`.
- [ ] `doctor undo --dry-run` returns `actions_planned[]` and `commands[]` with `omaddons undo <tx> --dry-run`, creates no run directory and writes nothing (`special.rs:251` rows).
- [ ] `undo --run <a doctor run id>` and `undo <a doctor run id>` are `usage` with fix argv `omaddons doctor undo <id>`, raised before anything is read beyond the arguments; the fix runs to exit 0.
- [ ] Each exit of the doctor dictionary the path declares is reached by a test or a contract row (0, 3, 4, 5, 64, 66; 73 and 74 by unit tests of the mapping), and `exit_sites.rs` accepts the path.
- [ ] Corpus rows exist if C4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4`, the intent corpus) has landed; `SKILL.md` is regenerated if B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`) has landed; `doctor ls`' `undo_complete` and `reverted_run` are wired if E4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4`, `doctor ls`) has landed.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean; `br lint` is clean; the close comment lists the new wire names (`doctor undo`, its `CLI_PATHS` row, the report keys, `actions_planned[]`, volatile `undo_tx`) and records why `doctor undo` does not bind (M4-D22).

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

- `src/app/doctor.rs`:
  - `doctor_undo_argument_cases`: a table: `none`, `run_id`, `latest`, `LATEST`, `a_repair_tx`, `a_folder_tx` (→ help), `garbage`, `a_ulid_prefix` (→ help); expected code, fix argv and whether anything beyond history was read.
  - `doctor_undo_selects_the_newest_repair_in_effect`: synthetic histories: one repair; two repairs (newest selected); newest repair undone (the older selected); newest repair undone and redone (the newest selected again); only undo lines (nothing); a folder line after a repair (the repair still selected).
  - `doctor_undo_resolves_a_run_without_its_report`: a fix run directory without `report.json` and a history line naming its run id resolves; neither is `not_found`.
  - `doctor_undo_maps_its_outcomes_to_the_doctor_dictionary`: `undo_conflict` → 4, `game_running` → 4, `locked` → 5, `usage` → 64, `not_found` → 66, run directory failure → 73, `state_corrupt` → 74, a rolled-back undo → 3.
- `src/app/undo.rs`:
  - `a_doctor_run_id_is_refused_before_anything_is_read`: `--run` and positional forms, upper- and lower-case ULIDs; `usage` with argv `["omaddons","doctor","undo",<id>]`; the check is a function of the arguments alone.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

- **Contract rows** (doctor mode through `common::doctor::check_envelope`, plus the `usage` row of `undo` in general mode): homes with one committed repair made in setup by E6's `fm-test-write`; snapshots redact run ids (`<run>`), ULIDs and identity values; every `commands[]` argv runs (the suite runs each, so `omaddons undo <tx> --dry-run` and `omaddons undo <undo tx>` must succeed).
- **`tests/doctor_repair.rs::doctor_undo_smoke`** (with T1's `TestLog`): step `home`; step `repair` (`doctor fix --only fm-test-write --json`, keep `run_id`); step `diagnose` (`doctor --json`, a diagnose run made after the fix); step `bare_undo` (`doctor undo --json`: `reverted_run` is the fix run, `state: DONE_OK`); step `again` (`doctor undo --json`: exit 0, `reverted_run: null`); step `by_run` (`doctor undo <fix run> --json`: exit 0, `already_undone: true`, `run_id: null`); step `trees` (`log.assert_unchanged` of the subject against the tree before the repair). The full scenario set is s6's.

### Logging

The smoke scenario uses `TestLog` (one `step` per phase, `log.run` for every command, `log.tree`/`log.assert_unchanged` for the subject and `<state>/doctor/runs/`); a failure prints the transcript path and the last steps. Unit tests name each case and print the input and the produced error or selection.

## Considerations

- **Hot spots.** `src/app/mod.rs` (A1 first; each command leaf adds its rows and rebases); `src/cli.rs` (keep the doctor subcommand in E3's tree, one variant); `omarchy/Model.js` (only the `CLI_PATHS` row); `tests/contract/matrix.rs` (append rows); `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` (regenerate after rebasing).
- **Previews bind (common rule 16).** `doctor undo` does not bind, by M4-D22: it is a convenience that resolves a run to its transaction, its bound form is `omaddons undo <tx> --dry-run` then `apply`, and its dry run offers exactly that. Record this in the close comment.
- **Idempotence vs. `omaddons undo`.** `omaddons undo <tx>` of an already undone repair stays `undo_conflict` (M3's behaviour for every undo); only `doctor undo` turns it into exit 0, as the doctor contract requires. Both are documented.
- **What could go wrong.** Selecting a diagnose run (impossible by construction: selection reads history, which diagnoses never write). A run id prefix accepted by mistake (only exact `DoctorRunId`s resolve; prefixes go to help). A race where two agents undo the same run: both exit 0, one undid it.
- **Compatibility.** A run directory written by an older E3/E6 build without some report key still resolves through history.

## Dependencies

Parent: `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7` (Undo of repairs).

- **Before it:** s3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7.3`): the contract suite runs every `commands[]` argv, and this command's dry run offers `omaddons undo <tx> --dry-run`, which works for a repair only once s3 has landed.
- **After it:** s6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7.6`) drives `doctor undo` through every scenario.

- [ ] Bare `doctor undo` selects the newest committed repair still in effect, also after an intervening `doctor` diagnose; a second bare `doctor undo` selects nothing and exits 0 saying so; `doctor undo <run>` twice gives exit 0 with `already_undone: true` the second time, and nothing written.
- [ ] `doctor undo latest` is `usage` (64) with fix `omaddons doctor undo`; a repair's tx is `usage` with fix `omaddons doctor undo <its run>`; an unknown run id is `not_found` (66); `doctor undo --if-match <token>` is `usage`.

- [ ] Each exit of the doctor dictionary the path declares is reached by a test or a contract row (0, 3, 4, 5, 64, 66; 73 and 74 by unit tests of the mapping), and `exit_sites.rs` accepts the path.
- [ ] Corpus rows exist if C4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4`, the intent corpus) has landed; `SKILL.md` is regenerated if B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`) has landed; `doctor ls`' `undo_complete` and `reverted_run` are wired if E4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4`, `doctor ls`) has landed.

comments.text:
decided: where this body left a choice, or where the tree differed from it.

1. **`UndoReport` takes §6.11's keys.** s2 had named them `reverts`/`tx`, which this surface corrects:
   - `tx` is the transaction reverted, `undo_tx` the undo's own;
   - `run_id` and `run_dir` are nullable;
   - `already_undone` and `actions_planned` (omitted unless a dry run planned) are added.
   
   The record an undo run writes and `doctor undo`'s stdout are one value. No released build reads a `report.json` of kind `undo`.
2. **A run resolves through history, not its report.** The repair-family line whose `doctor_run_id` is the run is selected: a fix run's `repair` line, or an undo run's `undo` line, whose undo is a redo. History is the authority on what committed, and that answers every case the report would:
   - a fix killed after `done` has no terminal report but a line;
   - a diagnose, a dry run or a rolled-back fix has a directory but no line, which reports "changed nothing" (exit 0);
   - neither is `not_found` (66), fix `omaddons history` (`doctor ls` has not landed; E4 switches it).
   
   The report is read only for `delegated[]`, as advice.
3. **`actions_planned[]` reuses `doctor fix`'s.** The engine's dry run lowers the verified inverses against `doctor diff`'s placeholder run (`<state>/doctor/runs/<run>`), and `doctor::fix::planned_actions` (factored out of `FixPlan::actions_planned`) writes them with the neutral `<run>`/`<tx>` and `bytes`. So `backup` is the neutral path, as in `doctor fix --dry-run`, not `null`. `RepairUndone.planned` carries them; it is empty for a real run.
4. **The engine says what it recorded.** `undo_repair_reported` returns `Recorded::{Nothing, CannotCreate, Report}`, so `doctor undo` exits as below. `undo_repair` keeps its signature for `omaddons undo`.
   - **`CannotCreate`**: a run directory that cannot be made exits 73 (`DoctorFailure::cannot_create`), not 74.
   - **`Report`**: a run that refused or rolled back prints its recorded report (`REFUSING` 4, `DONE_FAILED` 3, `LOCK_LOST` 5) with `error`.
   - **`Nothing`**: a refusal before the run is the envelope and `error` alone (E3's rule).
5. **The race to undo.** s1's already-undone refusal is recognized by `already_undone_by` (`undo_conflict`, no `reason`, one conflicting `undo`) and becomes the idempotent no-op. A run directory the losing process already made is named in `run_id`/`run_dir` rather than hidden.
6. **The `COMMANDS` row** is in group `Look`, beside `doctor fix` and `doctor diff`, which are there too, not `Change`. The doctor's subcommands list together. clap lists `undo` last, after `fix` and `diff`.
7. **`undo`'s refusal** recognizes a doctor run id with its ULID in any case (`to_ascii_uppercase` before `DoctorRunId::parse`), as `undo`'s own prefixes are case-insensitive. The fix names the canonical id. C1's `UsageFix::UserVerb` mark is on `main`, so the fix carries it.
8. **The corpus harness gains a plant hook** (`Row.plant`, set with `.on(plant, setup)`). Before the setup commands it writes what no command can make, here `fm-test-write`'s subject. The two E7 rows moved from `PENDING` to `CORPUS`:
   - `doctor undo latest` → 64 → bare `doctor undo` → 0;
   - `undo --run {run}` → 2 → `doctor undo {run}` → 0.
9. **The human output** follows this body's lines:
   - "undid repair <tx> from run <run> (<counts>)", then `run … · tx … · redo: omaddons undo <U>`;
   - the dry run's "would undo …", with at most 10 primitive lines and a "bind it: …" line;
   - "nothing to undo: …", "run <id> changed nothing; nothing to undo", "run <id> was already undone by <U>; nothing to do";
   - a delegated recovery's line.
10. **`undo_tx` is volatile** (`contract::VOLATILE`).

title: Tests: the undo's adversarial matrix, with the chmod and suspension test fixers
description:
Part 5 of 7 of `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7` (Undo of repairs). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

E7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7`, undo of repairs) undoes a doctor repair by committing its inverse primitives as a new repair-family transaction of kind `undo` (s1 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7.1` plans and verifies, s2 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7.2` commits, s3 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7.3` puts it behind `omaddons undo`). E7 is a **design-gate leaf** (common rule 14): it adds a journal shape (`prepared.kind`, `prepared.reverts`), a recovery rule (an undo journal rolls forward into an `undo` history line), a binding rule (the repair-undo token) and a new use of the activation barrier (a reactivation). It closes only when its own adversarial matrix passes.

**This part is that matrix**, plus the two debug-only test fixers it needs: `fm-test-chmod` (so the chmod kind can be repaired and undone before F7's credential fixer exists) and `fm-test-suspend` (a guarded set-aside of a planted journal, so guards and reactivation can be exercised before F2's set-aside fixer exists). It is its own subtask because the design gate is passed only when this matrix is green, and because F9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`, the safety harness) must never be the place where this leaf's protocol is first found to work.

**What must hold** (restated from the decisions and criteria):

- **Checkpoint criterion 9:** "A crash (a real `abort`) at every repair-journal failpoint and at every primitive boundary of every fixer (each lowered write, chmod and rename) is recovered by the next lock-taking command. Afterwards the whole subject set equals the before state when the crash preceded the durable `done`, and the after state from `done` on; a mixture fails. Recovery itself is crashed at every primitive inverse and repeated three times, every preserved original is accounted for, and the harness asserts that every primitive boundary of every action kind actually fired. No boundary is sampled away to save time." For an undo, "before" is the repaired state and "after" the original state.
- **Checkpoint criterion 11 / M4-D38:** "A crash at any point of a reactivation never lets ordinary recovery run the restored journal before the reactivating repair has settled": before the undo's durable `done` it rolls back (the provisional `<tx>.reactivating.jsonl` goes back to quarantine with the rest); from `done` on it rolls forward, and the folder pass then recovers the activated journal like any pending one.
- **M4-D31's recovery rule:** a repair-family journal before `done` rolls back by the primitives' inverses in reverse (each classified by its endpoint predicates: `post` → it ran, invert; `pre` → it did not, skip; neither → stop and leave the journal); from `done` it rolls forward (append the history line if the parsed history does not name the tx, then `committed`); then prune.
- **E14's order** (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14`): recovery runs repairs that own a suspension or an activation first, then folder journals (skipping any behind an unresolved barrier), then the remaining repairs.
- **The differential test** (E11, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.11`): `journal::diagnose` predicts what recovery then does, for every crash state; extended by E5 and E14, and here by the undo's states.

**Facts this part relies on** (as of `c0ab5e9`, plus blockers):

- `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS=<name>[=abort|=error|=sleep:<ms>|=panic|=pause][@N]` (`src/fsx/failpoint.rs:1-12`); an entry without an action aborts; `@N` fires on the Nth hit. In `mutate_with`, `fsx.mutate.checked` is hit by every session (`src/fsx/mutate.rs:373`), `fsx.mutate.backed_up`, `.executed` and `.logged` only by tracked sessions (`:436`, `:452`, `:484`); E5's commit keeps the primitives alone in its tracked session, so `@k` of those three addresses primitive `k` (as E5's matrix established).
- The doctor failpoints (`doctor::FAILPOINTS`, eleven): `doctor.run.staged`, `doctor.run.published` (E3), `doctor.repair.prepared`, `.step`, `.done`, `.history`, `.committed`, `doctor.recover.step` (E5), `doctor.fix.planned`, `doctor.gc.planned`, `doctor.detector.panic`. The undo path also hits the engine failpoints `engine.snapshot.prestaged`, `engine.lock.acquired` and `engine.revalidated` (s2).
- `tests/engine_crash.rs` holds the crash matrices (`crash_matrix_undo` at `:927`), shared with E11, E14, D8 and G3 ("add your section at the end and rebase"); E5 adds the repair-family section with `child_repair` and the scene builder `tests/common/repair.rs` (synthetic committed repairs of each kind); E11 adds `tests/common/differential.rs` and runs `journal::diagnose` on the crashed home itself before the recovering command (a copy would change every inode and birth time, so identity predicates would match neither state).
- E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`) delivers the test fixers `fm-test-write`, `fm-test-quarantine` and `fm-test-flatten`, compiled in debug builds only and registered only with `OMADDONS_TEST_FIXERS=1`, and their module under `src/doctor/fixers/`.
- `tests/common/trees.rs::tree_hash` (`:439`) covers paths, kinds, modes, file bytes and symlink targets; `tests/common/privacy.rs::assert_private_all` (`:40`).

## Technical Approach

### 1. The two test fixers (debug builds only, `OMADDONS_TEST_FIXERS=1`)

Added to E6's test-fixer module and registered the way E6 registers its own (never listed by a release build's `capabilities`, which E6 asserts):

- **`fm-test-chmod`**: detects a planted regular file named by the harness's request for this fixer (E6's convention for its test fixers' subjects; for example `<config>/test-fixers/chmod-me` with mode 0644) and fixes it with `Fix::Chmod { path, mode: 0o600 }`. `needs_force: false`, `enabled: true`, `writes_to: [Config]`.
- **`fm-test-suspend`**: detects each journal named in its planted request (one line per journal: `<tx> <target key> [<folder> …]`, the folders whose epochs to guard, or `WTF` for a WTF journal's epoch), and fixes it with E1's `Fix::Suspend { journal: JournalSet }`: the set found by the transaction id in known locations (`<state>/journal/<tx>.jsonl` or `<tx>.wtf.jsonl`, `<state>/inflight/<tx>.lock`, `<state>/snapshots/<tx>/`, the client's `<meta>/stage/<tx>/` and `<meta>/snapshots/<tx>/`, each when present), with guards built by s1's constructors (`observe_generation`, `observe_marker`, and one `observe_folder_epoch` per folder named, or `observe_wtf_epoch`). `needs_force: true`, `enabled: false` (run with `--only fm-test-suspend --force --yes`, as F2's set-aside will be), preconditions: the in-flight lock free, the client not running. Decided while writing this bead: the request names the target and folders, so the fixer works for a readable, an unreadable and a newer journal alike, without depending on F2's attribution.
- Unit tests of their `plan` functions (E6's `FixerSpec.plan`): `fm_test_chmod_plans_one_chmod`, `fm_test_suspend_plans_one_rename_per_present_artifact_with_its_guards`.

### 2. The scenes

Each scene builds a fresh `TestEnv` home, makes the original state `O`, commits a repair through the binary (`doctor fix --only <fm>` with `OMADDONS_TEST_FIXERS=1`, plus `--force --yes` for `fm-test-suspend`), giving the repaired state `R`, and records the repair's tx `T` and run. Where a test fixer does not produce a kind, the repair is made with E5's synthetic builder (`tests/common/repair.rs`), which commits a real repair transaction with its history line; the undo reads only the history line. The nine kinds:

| Kind | Repair | Subject trees |
|---|---|---|
| `write_over` | `fm-test-write` over an existing file (or E5's builder) | the file's directory |
| `write_create` | `fm-test-write` creating a file | its directory |
| `chmod` | `fm-test-chmod` | its directory |
| `quarantine_state_file` | `fm-test-quarantine` of a `<state>` file | `<state>` minus bookkeeping, the fix run's `quarantine/` |
| `quarantine_client_dir` | `fm-test-quarantine` of a `<meta>` directory | `<meta>` minus the `.repair` halves of the undo, the fix's client quarantine |
| `quarantine_temp_symlink` | `fm-test-quarantine` of a `.omaddons-*` symlink | its directory and the quarantine |
| `flatten_two` | `fm-test-flatten` of `AddOns/X/Y` | `AddOns`, the fix's client quarantine |
| `flatten_three` | `fm-test-flatten` of `AddOns/X/X` | as above |
| `suspend` | `fm-test-suspend` of a planted stuck folder journal (a complete `prepared` line that does not decode, `journal_unreadable`) on retail | `<state>/journal`, `<state>/inflight`, `<state>/snapshots`, retail's `<meta>/stage` and `<meta>/snapshots` (minus the undo's `.repair` half), and the fix run's `quarantine/` |

**Bookkeeping excluded from every comparison** (and only it, §6.15's rule): the undo's own repair journal and in-flight lock (which must be gone after recovery), its run directory, its quarantine roots (`<meta>/snapshots/<undo tx>.repair`, `<cache>/quarantine/<undo run>`), the history lines, the doorbell, `net.log` and the projections. A fixer's subject is never excluded.

### 3. The matrix (`tests/engine_crash.rs`, a "repair undo" section at the end)

For each kind, `repair_undo_crash_matrix_<kind>`:

1. **Boundaries.** For each failpoint, run `omaddons undo <T> --json` in a child with it armed (`abort`): `doctor.run.staged`, `doctor.run.published`, `engine.snapshot.prestaged`, `engine.lock.acquired`, `engine.revalidated`, `doctor.repair.prepared`, `doctor.repair.step@k`, `fsx.mutate.backed_up@k`, `fsx.mutate.executed@k`, `fsx.mutate.logged@k` for every inverse `k` (1…n), `fsx.mutate.checked@N` swept from 1 until a run completes without firing (each fired `N` attributed to the operation it hit), `doctor.repair.done`, `doctor.repair.history`, `doctor.repair.committed`.
2. **Read.** `omaddons status --json` reports the undo's journal as `journal_pending` (when one exists) and changes nothing (`log.assert_unchanged` over every tree).
3. **Recover.** `omaddons config set check_interval_hours 6` (a lock-taking command that recovers both families).
4. **Oracle.** The whole subject set equals `R` when the crash preceded the undo's durable `done` (every boundary up to and including `doctor.repair.done`), and `O` from `done` on; a mixture fails, even when each path alone is wholly `R` or `O`. No repair journal and no in-flight lock remain. Every preserved original is accounted for: in `O`, each `write_over` undo's backup `<undo run>/backups/<k>` equals `R`'s bytes, and each `write_create` undo's file sits in the undo's quarantine with `R`'s bytes; in `R`, the fix run's backups and quarantine are as the repair left them. History holds the undo line exactly once from `done` on, and none before.
5. **Recovery crashed.** For each crash before `done`, repeat with recovery itself crashed: `config set` with `doctor.recover.step@j` (abort) for every inverse `j` recovery runs, then `config set` again; then three more times. The end state is `R`, the same each time, and no journal remains.
6. **Witnessed.** `crashes_exercised` records every `(kind, failpoint, k)` that fired; the test fails, naming the boundary, if any primitive boundary of any kind never fired ("crash point never hit").

Also in this section:

- **`repair_undo_of_an_undo_crash_matrix`** (kinds `chmod`, `flatten_two` and `suspend`): after the undo `U` committed (state `O`), `omaddons undo <U>` crashed at every boundary as above; the oracle swaps: `O` before `done`, `R` from `done` on.
- **`a_reactivation_crashed_anywhere_settles_before_the_folder_pass`**: the planted journal is a **recoverable** folder journal (an install crashed mid-swap with the existing helpers of `tests/engine_crash.rs`, so folder recovery visibly changes `AddOns`), set aside by `fm-test-suspend`, giving `S1` (journal suspended, `AddOns` in its interrupted state). Expected end states: `E_before` = `S1` (the undo rolled back: every artifact back in quarantine, the provisional name gone, `AddOns` untouched, no `journal_recovered` warning for the folder tx); `E_after` = the state a clean reactivation followed by `config set` produces on a fresh replica of the scene (the folder journal recovered by the folder pass after the undo committed). Crashes: after each artifact restore (`fsx.mutate.logged@k` for the non-journal artifacts), after the provisional restore, immediately before the activation (`doctor.repair.step@n`), after the activation and before `done` (`fsx.mutate.logged@n`, `doctor.repair.done`), and after `done` (`doctor.repair.history`, `doctor.repair.committed`). Oracle: before `done` → `E_before`; from `done` → `E_after`; anything else (the folder journal recovered while the undo rolled back, or a provisional journal left behind) fails.
- **`io_failures_in_a_repair_undo_roll_it_back`**: for every kind and every `k`, `fsx.mutate.executed=error@k` (and `fsx.mutate.backed_up=error@k` for `write_over`), `doctor.repair.step=error@k` and `doctor.repair.done=error`: the undo rolls back in process: subject `R`, no undo history line, `<undo run>/report.json` `state: "DONE_FAILED"`, `omaddons undo` exits with the error's general code, and `doctor undo <fix run>` (one case per kind) exits 3. A failure after `done` (`doctor.repair.history=error`): E5's in-process roll-forward completes the undo (subject `O`, the line once).
- **`a_repair_undo_that_cannot_create_its_run_moves_nothing`**: `doctor.run.staged=error`: `omaddons undo` fails with `io`, `doctor undo` exits 73; subject `R`; no journal, no in-flight lock, no run directory.
- **`config_set_install_and_undo_recover_a_repair_undo_identically`**: the `flatten_two` undo crashed at `doctor.repair.step@2`, built three times (the scene is deterministic; a copied home would change every identity); recovered by `config set check_interval_hours 6`, by an `install` on another client, and by an `undo` of that install; the three end states' subject trees are equal (and equal `R`).

### 4. The differential test (`tests/journal.rs`)

For every crash state of section 3 (every kind's boundaries, the undo-of-undo matrix, the reactivation cases, recovery crashed at every inverse), E11's differential helper runs `journal::diagnose` on the crashed home itself before the recovering command (tree hashes prove it wrote nothing), then the recovering command; the diagnosis's verdict for the undo's journal (`Recoverable { direction: Back | Forward | Prune }`, `StepUnrecognized`, …, and `BehindBarrier` for the folder journal in the reactivation cases) equals what recovery did. Decided while writing this bead: the differential runs over this matrix too (the plan names it for E5's and E14's states; an undo journal is a repair journal, so the same guarantee must hold for it).

### 5. Speed

Reuse the scene setup per kind (one repair per kind, then one fresh replica per crash case built by the same deterministic steps), and run kinds in parallel test functions. Never drop a crash position. If the section runs longer than the gate tolerates, file a bug `discovered-from` this subtask for faster scenes; F9's 60 s harness budget is not this matrix's.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `fm-test-chmod` and `fm-test-suspend` exist in debug builds behind `OMADDONS_TEST_FIXERS=1` only (a release build's `capabilities` lists neither), with their unit tests.
- [ ] `repair_undo_crash_matrix_<kind>` passes for all nine kinds: every listed failpoint and every primitive boundary fired (`crashes_exercised`), the subject set is wholly `R` before the undo's durable `done` and wholly `O` from `done` on, no journal or in-flight lock remains, every preserved original is accounted for, and the undo line appears exactly once from `done` on.
- [ ] Recovery crashed at every inverse, then repeated three more times, ends in the same state.
- [ ] `repair_undo_of_an_undo_crash_matrix` passes with the swapped oracle.
- [ ] `a_reactivation_crashed_anywhere_settles_before_the_folder_pass` passes: before `done` the end state is `E_before` with no folder recovery; from `done` on it is `E_after`; never a mixture, never a provisional journal left.
- [ ] Injected I/O failures at every inverse roll the undo back in process (`DONE_FAILED`, `doctor undo` exit 3); a failure after `done` completes it; a run directory failure moves nothing (`doctor undo` exit 73).
- [ ] Recovery by `config set`, `install` and `undo` gives identical end states.
- [ ] The differential test passes over every crash state of this matrix.
- [ ] Every scenario uses `TestLog`; each case's `crash` record names its kind, failpoint, `k`, phase, expected and observed end state, so a failing case is diagnosable from its transcript alone.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean; `br lint` is clean; the close comment records that the design gate of `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7` is passed, with the boundary counts per kind.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

- `src/doctor/fixers/` (E6's test-fixer module): `fm_test_chmod_plans_one_chmod` (one `Fix::Chmod` with mode 0600 for the planted file; nothing for a file already 0600); `fm_test_suspend_plans_one_rename_per_present_artifact_with_its_guards` (cases: all five artifacts; journal and in-flight lock only; a WTF journal with a WTF epoch guard; the guards hold the target's generation, the marker digest and one epoch per named folder).

### Integration and end-to-end tests

As sections 3 and 4: the section of `tests/engine_crash.rs` and the extension of `tests/journal.rs`, each test named as listed.

### Logging

Every scene uses T1's `TestLog` (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`): `let log = tlog!();`; steps `home`, `repair`, `crash <failpoint>`, `read`, `recover`, `oracle`; every command through `log.run(&env, &argv)` (which records the failpoints armed); `log.tree("subject:<tree>", root)` for `O` and `R` at their moments and after recovery, compared with `log.assert_unchanged` against the expected one (logging the first differing paths); `log.json("crash", {kind, failpoint, k, phase: before_done|from_done, expected: R|O, got: R|O|mixture})` per case; `log.json("crashes_exercised", …)` at the end of each kind. On a failure the guard prints `test log: <path>` and the last 20 steps; `argc e2e repair_undo` runs the section with `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG=verbose`.

## Considerations

- **Design gate.** E7's design gate is passed only when this subtask is closed; record it in the close comment so the leaf's closing agent sees it.
- **Hot spot `tests/engine_crash.rs`:** shared with E11, E14, D8 and G3: add this section at the end and rebase before each gate run. G3 (`omad-7ccp`) reruns it later under group commit.
- **What could go wrong.** A failpoint numbering that counts the runtime's own writes (attribute each `fsx.mutate.checked@N` to its operation; for the three tracked-only points, `k` is the primitive); a scene that is not deterministic (build replicas by the same steps, never by copying); an oracle that compares per path instead of the whole set (the "mixture" rule must be on the whole subject).
- **Privacy.** The `suspend` scene on a WTF journal plants `WTF/Account/FAKEACCT/FakeRealm/FakeChar/` and runs `assert_private_all` over every command's stdout and stderr with `--progress json`.
- **Time.** Tests set `TZ=UTC` (TestEnv does).

## Dependencies

Parent: `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7` (Undo of repairs).

- **Before it:** s3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7.3`): the matrix drives `omaddons undo <tx>` through the binary, which reverts a repair only from s3 on (and s2's commit and s1's checks beneath it). It also needs T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, the test log), whose edge the filing adds.
- **After it:** s6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7.6`) uses this part's two test fixers. Independent of s4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7.4`, which touches other files): the two can be worked at the same time.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `fm-test-chmod` and `fm-test-suspend` exist in debug builds behind `OMADDONS_TEST_FIXERS=1` only (a release build's `capabilities` lists neither), with their unit tests.
- [ ] `repair_undo_crash_matrix_<kind>` passes for all nine kinds: every listed failpoint and every primitive boundary fired (`crashes_exercised`), the subject set is wholly `R` before the undo's durable `done` and wholly `O` from `done` on, no journal or in-flight lock remains, every preserved original is accounted for, and the undo line appears exactly once from `done` on.

title: E2E: every fix kind round-trips, the strict refusals, guards, conflicts and `doctor undo`
description:
Part 6 of 7 of `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7` (Undo of repairs). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

E7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7`, undo of repairs) makes every doctor repair undoable: `omaddons undo` and `omaddons doctor undo` invert a repair's primitives, strictly checked, guarded where a set-aside recorded a suspension manifest, through the activation barrier where a journal comes back, as a new repair-family transaction (s1–s4: `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7.1`, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7.2`, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7.3`, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7.4`). s5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7.5`) proved the protocol under crashes.

**This part proves the behaviour end to end, through the binary, scenario by scenario**: every fix kind round-trips (repair → undo → byte-identical; undo of the undo → repaired again); the strict refusals happen before anything moves; guards refuse a reactivation after later work; a set-aside reactivates byte-identical when nothing changed; conflicts by resource overlap; `doctor undo`'s selection and idempotence; the usage refusals and their fixes; dry runs that write nothing; the running refusal; concurrency and the lock timeout; the bound preview; `status.last_change`; privacy. It is its own subtask because these are the leaf's acceptance criteria as a user and an agent meet them, after every part has landed.

**What must hold** (restated):

- **G-M4-4:** "A repair can be undone byte for byte as long as no later change overlaps what it touched; once one does, undo refuses before moving anything, and the kept bytes stay inspectable."
- **Checkpoint criterion 9's round trip:** "`doctor undo` → the subject tree is byte-identical to the corrupted state, modes and symlinks included … A second case runs bare `doctor undo` after an intervening `doctor` diagnose and asserts it selects the same run."
- **Checkpoint criterion 11:** "While nothing that overlaps the suspended set has changed, `doctor undo` reactivates it byte-identical, after which recovery behaves exactly as before the repair. After an overlapping change (a later install on that client, say), `doctor undo` refuses with `undo_conflict` before moving anything, and the set stays inspectable in quarantine."
- **M4-D46:** strict checks (`changed_since_repair` with `paths`, `changed_since_suspension` with `changed`); conflicts are resource overlaps ("an older install's undo whose folder a later repair touched is `undo_conflict`"); `doctor undo` selects the newest committed, not-undone fix run; `latest` is a usage error with fix `omaddons doctor undo`; undoing a run already undone is a no-op with exit 0; bare `undo`, `status.last_change` and Undo last may select a repair.
- **§4.6 (an agent repairs and undoes):** `doctor fix --only fm-state_files-orphan-temp-file --json --actor agent …` then `omaddons undo --last-by agent --json`: "the same repair, undone through the general undo … The agent never has to know that `doctor undo <run>` and `omaddons undo <tx>` are the same thing. Both work, and `history` shows the repair (`kind: repair`) and its undo like any other change."
- **M3-D46:** a bound run whose preview no longer holds is `plan_stale` and changes nothing.

**Facts this part relies on:**

- T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`) delivers `tests/common/tlog.rs` (`tlog!()`, `step`, `note`, `json`, `run -> Ran`, `tree`, `assert_unchanged`, the panic guard, `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG=verbose`, `argc e2e`).
- E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`) delivers `tests/doctor_repair.rs` with its test fixers (`fm-test-write`, `fm-test-quarantine`, `fm-test-flatten`, `OMADDONS_TEST_FIXERS=1`, debug builds); s5 adds `fm-test-chmod` and `fm-test-suspend`.
- `tests/engine_undo.rs` (cross-process undo checkpoints, `common::engine::Scene`), `tests/common/procfs.rs` (a fake `/proc` for running clients through `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT`), `tests/common/pause.rs` (pause failpoints across processes), `tests/common/trees.rs::tree_hash` (`:439`), `tests/common/privacy.rs::assert_private_all` (`:40`).

## Technical Approach

All scenarios live in `tests/doctor_repair.rs` (E6's suite) inside one `mod undo { … }` block, so their paths are `undo::<name>` and `cargo test --test doctor_repair undo` (or `argc e2e undo`) selects exactly them, except the two cross-process checkpoints added to `tests/engine_undo.rs`. Each builds a fresh `TestEnv` home with two clients (retail and era), uses T1's `TestLog`, sets `OMADDONS_TEST_FIXERS=1`, and plants `WTF/Account/FAKEACCT/FakeRealm/FakeChar/` with a SavedVariables file in each client so the privacy assertion has something to catch. Every command runs with `--json --progress json` through `log.run`, and every output pair goes through `assert_private_all`.

### 1. Round trips

- **`undo_round_trips_every_fix_kind`**, for the nine kinds (`write_over`, `write_create`, `chmod`, `quarantine_state_file`, `quarantine_client_dir`, `quarantine_temp_symlink`, `flatten_two`, `flatten_three`, `suspend`): plant `O` → `log.tree` of the subject trees (as s5's table names them) → `doctor fix --only <fm>` (with `--force --yes` for `fm-test-suspend`), exit 0 → `log.tree` `R` → `doctor undo <fix run>`: exit 0, `state: "DONE_OK"`, `actions_taken` = the primitive count (plus one activation for `suspend`), `reverted_run` = the fix run, `run_id` a new directory with `report.json` `kind: "undo"` → the subject trees equal `O` (`log.assert_unchanged`) → `omaddons undo <undo_tx>` (the undo of the undo): exit 0 → equal `R` → `doctor undo <the second undo's run>`: equal `O` again.
- **`undo_through_omaddons_undo_and_doctor_undo_are_the_same`**: two identical homes; one repaired then undone with `omaddons undo <tx>`, the other with `doctor undo <run>`; both subject trees equal `O`; both history tails end with an `undo` line with `reverts`, `target: null`, the same `targets`, and `repairs` equal after redacting identities; the human output of each names the repair.
- **`an_agent_repairs_and_undoes_with_last_by`** (§4.6): `doctor fix --only fm-test-write --actor agent --reason "cleanup the doctor recommended"` → `undo --last-by agent --json`: `data.kind: "repair"`, `data.reverted.tx` = the fix's tx, `data.doctor_run_id` set, the subject equals `O`; `history --json` shows `kind: repair` then `kind: undo`.
- **`bare_undo_and_undo_run_select_a_repair`**: after a fix, bare `undo --json` reverts it (it is the newest change); on another home, `undo --run <the fix invocation's history run>` reverts it; `undo -t retail` reverts a repair whose `targets` names retail and not one on era.

### 2. Strict refusals (nothing moves)

- **`undo_refuses_a_path_changed_after_the_repair`**: per case, after the fix, change one thing, then `omaddons undo <tx>` and `doctor undo <run>`: `undo_conflict` (general exit 4; doctor exit 4), `details.reason: "changed_since_repair"`, `details.paths` exactly the changed path(s); every tree hash unchanged (`log.assert_unchanged` over `<state>`, `<config>`, `<cache>` and both client dirs), no new run directory. Cases: `identity_replaced` (the chmodded file replaced by a same-mode copy), `same_size_content_edit` (the written file), `mode_changed` (chmod back by hand), `destination_appeared` (a file created where a quarantined path would return), `source_vanished` (the quarantined entry deleted by hand), `backup_edited` (one byte of the fix run's backup flipped), `backup_missing`.
- **`undo_refuses_a_changed_guard`** (`fm-test-suspend` on a planted unreadable folder journal on retail, guarding folder `DBM-Core`): after the set-aside, `install` on retail succeeds (the client is unblocked); then `doctor undo <run>`: `undo_conflict`, `reason: "changed_since_suspension"`, `changed: ["generation"]`, `target` = retail's key, fix `omaddons doctor explain fm-test-suspend -t retail` (and that fix runs to exit 0); the suspended set is intact in the fix run's quarantine (tree hash). Second case: a hand edit in `AddOns/DBM-Core` → `changed: ["epochs"]`. Third: the marker rewritten with the same key and different bytes → `changed: ["marker"]`. A WTF case (a `.wtf.jsonl` journal guarded by the WTF epoch, a SavedVariables file touched) → `changed: ["epochs"]`, and neither the message nor `details` names `FAKEACCT`, `FakeRealm` or `FakeChar`.
- **`undo_reactivates_a_set_aside_byte_identical`**: before the set-aside, `install -t retail` fails with the unreadable journal's error (record the code and `details.reason`); after it, `install` would succeed (not run); `doctor undo <run>` with nothing changed: exit 0; the subject trees (journal, in-flight lock, snapshot halves, stage) equal `O`; the next `install -t retail` fails with exactly the recorded code and `details.reason`; `status --json` reports the same journal issue as before the set-aside.
- **`undo_of_a_repair_refuses_while_its_client_runs`**: a `flatten_two` repair on retail; retail running per the fake `/proc` → `undo <tx>` and `undo <tx> --while-running` both `game_running` with `details.reason: "repair"`, nothing moved; with running unknown (an unreadable fake `/proc` entry) the same; a home-side `chmod` repair's undo proceeds while retail runs.

### 3. Conflicts by overlap

- **`an_older_install_undo_conflicts_with_a_later_flatten`**: install `X` on retail (folder `AddOns/X`); plant a folder `AddOns/X/Y` by hand, so `AddOns/X` looks like a wrapper to `fm-test-flatten`; flatten (`AddOns/X/Y` → `AddOns/Y`, then `AddOns/X` → quarantine); `undo <install tx>`: `undo_conflict` naming the repair (`details.conflicting[0].tx` = the fix's tx, `kind: "repair"`, `folders` containing `X`), nothing moved; after `undo <repair tx>`, the install's undo proceeds (the repair and its undo cancel out).
- **`undoing_a_repair_after_later_work_on_its_resources_conflicts`**: flatten `AddOns/X/Y` to `AddOns/Y`, then `adopt Y` (records it, folders untouched) → `undo <repair tx>`: `undo_conflict`, `reason: "changed_since_repair"`, `conflicting[0].kind: "adopt"`, fix `omaddons undo <adopt tx>`; after undoing the adopt, the repair's undo proceeds.

### 4. `doctor undo` selection, idempotence and usage

- **`bare_doctor_undo_twice`**: fix → `doctor undo` (reverts it) → `doctor undo` again: exit 0, `reverted_run: null`, human "nothing to undo …", nothing written (tree hashes).
- **`doctor_undo_run_twice`**: `doctor undo <run>` → `doctor undo <run>`: exit 0, `already_undone: true`, `undo_tx` = the first undo's tx, `run_id: null`, no new run directory.
- **`doctor_undo_after_a_diagnose_selects_the_fix_run`**: fix → `doctor` (a diagnose run newer than the fix) → bare `doctor undo`: `reverted_run` = the fix run.
- **`doctor_undo_latest_is_usage`**: `doctor undo latest`: exit 64, `usage`, `fix_argv` `["omaddons","doctor","undo"]`; running the fix exits 0 and reverts the repair.
- **`undo_run_with_a_doctor_run_id_is_usage`**: `undo --run <fix run id>`: `usage`, fix argv `["omaddons","doctor","undo","<fix run id>"]`, nothing read beyond the arguments (records and trees unchanged); running the fix exits 0.
- **`doctor_undo_of_a_failed_or_diagnose_run_changes_nothing`**: a diagnose run id → exit 0, "changed nothing"; a fix run that rolled back (`fsx.mutate.executed=error@1` during the fix) → exit 0, nothing to undo.
- **`doctor_undo_names_a_delegated_roll_forward`** (only if F2's delegation has landed; otherwise this case is F2's to add): a fix run that also completed an interrupted transaction `T2` → `doctor undo <run>` reverts only the repair, and `commands[]` offers `omaddons undo <T2>`.

### 5. Dry runs, previews and binding

- **`undo_dry_runs_write_nothing`**: after a fix: `undo <tx> --dry-run`, `doctor undo --dry-run`, `doctor undo <run> --dry-run`: exit 0; `<state>` (with `<state>/doctor/`), `<config>`, `<cache>` and both client trees unchanged; no new run directory; `doctor undo --dry-run` has `actions_planned[]` (one per inverse) and `commands[]` with `omaddons undo <tx> --dry-run`, and running that argv exits 0.
- **`a_bound_undo_of_a_repair_is_stale_after_a_change`**: `undo <tx> --dry-run` → token `P`; (a) nothing changed → `undo <tx> --if-match P`: exit 0, subject `O`; (b) on a replica, edit the repaired file → `--if-match P`: `plan_stale`, `details.changed: ["observed"]`, `retryable: false`, `fix_argv` the `--dry-run` form, nothing moved; (c) on a replica of a client-side repair, a commit on retail (an install) → `plan_stale` with `targets`; (d) a preview made in one process and the bound run in another agree (the token holds nothing run-specific).

### 6. Concurrency and the lock

- **`two_concurrent_doctor_undos_serialize`**: two `doctor undo <run>` paused at `engine.snapshot.prestaged` (both planned), resumed together: exactly one has `already_undone: false` with `actions_taken > 0`; the other exits 0 with `already_undone: true`; the subject equals `O`; the two `actions.jsonl` never both hold lines.
- **`two_concurrent_omaddons_undos`**: the same with `omaddons undo <tx>`: one exit 0, the other `undo_conflict` "already undone by …" (exit 4), nothing moved by the second.
- **`an_undo_waits_for_the_lock_and_then_gives_up`**: another process holds the global lock (an `install` paused at `engine.lock.acquired`) past 5 s: `doctor undo <run>` exits 5 (`locked`, the holder's `{pid, command, age_s}`), its run directory's report says `LOCK_LOST`, the subject is `R`, no journal remains; after the holder resumes, `doctor undo <run>` succeeds.

### 7. `status.last_change` and Undo last

- **`status_last_change_offers_the_repair_undo`**: after a fix, `status --json`'s `last_change.kind` is `repair` and `last_change.undo.argv` is `["omaddons","undo","--run","<run>"]`; running it (and its `--dry-run` form first, as the widget's Undo last does) reverts the repair; afterwards `last_change.kind` is `undo`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every fix kind round-trips through `doctor undo` (byte-identical, modes and symlinks included), and the undo of the undo restores the repaired state; `omaddons undo` and `doctor undo` give the same end state and the same history.
- [ ] `undo --last-by agent`, bare `undo`, `undo --run` and `undo -t` select and revert a repair.
- [ ] Each changed-path case refuses with `changed_since_repair` and its exact `paths`, and each guard case with `changed_since_suspension` and its `changed` value, before anything moves (every tree hash unchanged, no run directory).
- [ ] An unchanged set-aside reactivates byte-identical, and the next lock-taking command then fails exactly as before the set-aside.
- [ ] An older install's undo after a later flatten, and a repair's undo after a later adopt, are `undo_conflict` naming the later transaction; after that transaction is undone, the undo proceeds.
- [ ] Bare `doctor undo` twice, `doctor undo <run>` twice, `doctor undo` after a diagnose, `doctor undo latest` and `undo --run <doctor run id>` behave as specified, and both usage fixes run to exit 0.
- [ ] Every dry run writes nothing; the bound undo of a repair succeeds unchanged and is `plan_stale` after a change (`observed`, `targets`), across processes.
- [ ] Two concurrent `doctor undo`s serialize (one undoes, the other exits 0 already undone); a held lock gives exit 5 with nothing moved.
- [ ] A client-side repair's undo refuses while its client runs (or may), whatever `--while-running` says; a home-side one does not.
- [ ] `status.last_change`'s undo argv reverts a repair.
- [ ] `assert_private_all` passes over every command of every scenario; no guard, message or `details` names a path below `WTF/`.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean; `br lint` is clean; the close comment lists the scenarios and their test names.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

None new (the scenarios are integration tests; units shipped with s1–s4).

### Integration and end-to-end tests

As listed in the Technical Approach, by file and test name: `tests/doctor_repair.rs::undo_*` (the scenarios of sections 1 to 7, each a test function of the name given) and `tests/engine_undo.rs`'s two checkpoints.

### Logging

Every scenario: `let log = tlog!();`; one `log.step` per phase (`home`, `plant`, `repair`, `change`, `undo`, `again`, `assert`); every command through `log.run(&env, &argv)` (argv, env overrides with any token redacted, exit code, envelope, stderr events, `net.log` lines, failpoints armed); `log.tree(label, root)` for `O`, `R` and each end state, and `log.assert_unchanged(label, root)` for every "nothing moved" claim (the first differing paths are logged); `log.json("refusal", {code, reason, paths|changed, fix_argv})` for each refusal; `log.json("report", …)` for each `doctor undo` report. A failure prints `test log: <path>` and the last 20 steps; `argc e2e undo` runs the suite verbosely.

## Considerations

- **Hot spots.** `tests/doctor_repair.rs` is E6's suite and E14's and F2's add theirs: append the `undo_*` scenarios in their own block and rebase before each gate run. `tests/engine_undo.rs`: append.
- **What could go wrong.** A scenario that copies a home and then expects identity predicates to hold (never copy; build replicas by the same steps). A fake `/proc` left armed into the next step (scope it per step). A pause failpoint without its resume (the pause helper's timeout is 60 s; resume explicitly).
- **Runtime.** These scenarios run in `cargo test` (the gate). Keep each to the commands it needs; share nothing mutable between scenarios.
- **F9 relation.** F9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`) repeats the round trip for every real fixer through its harness; these scenarios cover the test fixers and the cases F9 does not (guards, conflicts, selection, concurrency, binding).

## Dependencies

Parent: `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7` (Undo of repairs).

- **Before it:** s4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7.4`, `doctor undo` and the doctor-run refusal) and s5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7.5`, whose `fm-test-chmod` and `fm-test-suspend` these scenarios use). T1's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`) edge is added at filing.
- **After it:** none inside the leaf; the leaf closes when s6 and s7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7.7`) are closed.

done: the undo of repairs end to end, through the binary. All scenarios are in `tests/doctor_repair.rs` as `mod undo` (`tests/doctor_repair/undo.rs`), selected by `cargo test --test doctor_repair undo::`. Each uses `TestLog` and two clients where a scenario needs them. Private `WTF/` names are planted, every JSON run goes through `checked` (`assert_private_all` plus the doctor envelope check), and every human run through `assert_private`.

**The scenarios, by test name:**
1. Round trips:
   - `undo_round_trips_every_fix_kind`: nine kinds: `doctor undo` to `O`, `undo <U>` to `R`, `doctor undo <the redo's run>` to `O` again, `actions_taken` the inverse count.
   - `undo_through_omaddons_undo_and_doctor_undo_are_the_same`.
   - `an_agent_repairs_and_undoes_with_last_by`.
   - `bare_undo_and_undo_run_select_a_repair` (bare, `--run`, `-t retail` versus `-t era`).
2. Strict refusals:
   - `undo_refuses_a_path_changed_after_the_repair`: seven cases, each with its exact `paths`, through both undos.
   - `undo_refuses_a_changed_guard`: `generation`, `epochs` for a folder, `marker`, and `epochs` for `WTF/` with no private name in the error. The fix `doctor explain` runs.
   - `undo_reactivates_a_set_aside_byte_identical`.
   - `undo_of_a_repair_refuses_while_its_client_runs`: running, may run, a home-side repair proceeds.
3. Conflicts:
   - `an_older_install_undo_conflicts_with_a_later_flatten`.
   - `undoing_a_repair_after_later_work_on_its_resources_conflicts`: an adopt.
4. `doctor undo`:
   - `bare_doctor_undo_twice`, `doctor_undo_run_twice`, `doctor_undo_after_a_diagnose_selects_the_fix_run`;
   - `doctor_undo_latest_is_usage` and `undo_run_with_a_doctor_run_id_is_usage`, both fixes run to 0;
   - `doctor_undo_of_a_failed_or_diagnose_run_changes_nothing`.
5. Dry runs and binding: `undo_dry_runs_write_nothing`, `a_bound_undo_of_a_repair_is_stale_after_a_change` (unchanged, `observed`, `targets`).
6. Concurrency: `two_concurrent_doctor_undos_serialize`, `two_concurrent_omaddons_undos`, `an_undo_waits_for_the_lock_and_then_gives_up` (exit 5 and `LOCK_LOST`, then succeeds).
7. `status_last_change_offers_the_repair_undo`.

**Found and fixed: undoing the redo of a set-aside was refused.** That is the third leg of a set-aside's round trip, reactivating a journal that a redo had set aside again. s1's `invert` read the redo's deactivation (own name to provisional) as a set-aside of the journal file. It planned a restore renaming the provisional name onto itself, which a check then refused as "changed since the repair". The redo's set-aside of the provisional journal it inverted as a plain rename instead of the provisional restore. The fix:
- a journal file moved to its own provisional name inverts to the activation alone;
- a journal moved out of its provisional name inverts to the provisional restore.

Test: `engine::repair::undo::a_set_aside_round_trips_three_deep`. s5's matrices (`repair_undo_*`, `barrier_crash`) all still pass.

**decided** (where this body's letter and the tree differ):
- The round trip uses E5's synthetic repairs (`RepairScene`) for all nine kinds. The test fixers cannot make `quarantine_temp_symlink` (fsx never moves a final-component symlink), and the scene's oracle knows each subject exactly, modes and symlinks included. This crate gains E5's `child_repair` for it.
- The install-undo conflict uses E5's synthetic quarantine of the installed folder in place of a flatten. `fm-test-flatten` takes only unmanaged `TestWrap*` folders; what the rule checks is the overlap on the install's folder.
- The bound-undo case asserts `observed` among `details.changed`. A refused re-plan's token part is its verdict and its transaction alone, as a folder undo's is, so `selection` moves with it.
- `undo <tx> --dry-run` stores its plan in `<cache>/omaddons/plans`: that dry run leaves every tree but `<cache>` unchanged, and the doctor's dry runs every tree.
- Trees are recorded after a `status`, which writes the derived discovery cache that every first look at the machine writes.
- `doctor_undo_names_a_delegated_roll_forward` is F2's to add, since its delegation has not landed. A note went on F2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.2`).
- `tests/engine_undo.rs`'s two checkpoints are covered here: the round trip, and the install-undo conflict, through the same binary. They were not duplicated.

**Also fixed: a flaky test.** `tests/journal.rs::readers_report_without_writing` read the global lock free right after its in-process run dropped it. Under s5's heavier differential, which runs in the same test binary, a child forked in that instant still held the inherited descriptor until its `exec` closed it, so the reader saw `tx_in_progress`. Descriptors are close-on-exec, so this is no product issue. The test now takes the lock once before reading, which waits any such copy out.

**Evidence:** `argc gate` passes (4184 tests); `ubs` is clean; `br lint` is clean.
