title: The growth row `fm-state_files-doctor-runs-accumulated`: its `quick` detector, its fixture, its README row and the `doctor_gc` hint
description:
Part 4 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.8 (`doctor gc`: the retention plan). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.8 builds `omaddons doctor gc`, the one deletion surface for what the doctor keeps (M4-D36). Because nothing else ever deletes run directories, backups and quarantines, they grow until the user runs gc; M4's risk 10 is exactly that ("the retention exemption grows disk use"). The mitigation is a finding: `fm-state_files-doctor-runs-accumulated` (Appendix B row 17, moved from F3 to this leaf in review), which reports when the kept fix and undo runs or the quarantined bytes pass a soft bound, and whose remediation is a gc **preview** (`omaddons doctor gc --before 30d --dry-run`), never the real gc, because the real gc ends undos and is the user's choice.

This part adds that failure mode: its `FAILURE_MODES` row, its `quick`-tier detector, its fixture, its README doctor-table row, and the `doctor_gc` recommendation hint in `doctor`'s output. It is its own step because it is catalog work (a detector and a fixture, M4-D47) on top of a finished command: its remediation must run, which needs s3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.8.3`).

## Technical Approach

### 1. The row (`src/doctor/registry.rs`, E1's `FAILURE_MODES`)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `id` | `fm-state_files-doctor-runs-accumulated` |
| `subsystem` | `state_files` |
| `severity` | P3 |
| `title` | "the doctor's kept runs and quarantines have grown large" |
| `description` | "more fix and undo runs, or more quarantined bytes, are kept than the soft bound; nothing deletes them but `doctor gc`" |
| `why` | "each kept run keeps the backups and quarantined files its undo needs, so they only grow until you choose to end those undos" |
| `tier` | `Quick` |
| `online` | false |
| `cost_ms` | 3 (decided while writing this bead: a listing and stats, inside `QUICK_DETECTOR_BUDGET`) |
| `requires` | `[Registry]` (the registered clients, for their `.repair` halves) |
| `fix` | `None` (M4-D48: no automatic fix where the right action is a choice) |
| `manual` | the remediation below |

The id keeps the `fm-<subsystem>-<name>` spelling with the subsystem's underscore (M4-D30), and passes E1's invariant test.

### 2. The detector (`src/doctor/detectors/state_files.rs`)

`fn doctor_runs_accumulated(view: &DoctorView, sel: &Selection, budget: &mut Budget) -> Detected` (E3's signature):

1. **Runs.** `doctor::runs::list_runs(paths, budget)` (s2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.8.2`): `runs` = the run directories (staged ones not counted). For each, `runs::has_actions_log(dir)` (one `stat` of `<run>/actions.jsonl`, charged to the budget): `fix_undo_runs` counts the runs that hold one.
   - Decided while writing this bead: a run counts when it holds `actions.jsonl`, which only a repair's tracked session writes, so fix and undo runs whose repair started (committed, rolled back or interrupted) count, and diagnose runs, dry-run fixes and refused fixes do not. That is one `stat` per run instead of a `report.json` read, and it applies the plan's own reason for leaving diagnose runs out ("agents and the widget make one per triage, and they hold only a small report") to the other report-only runs, which the widget's Issues view previews make just as often. If E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`) writes `actions.jsonl` for runs that changed nothing, count by `report.json`'s `kind` and `summary.actions_taken` instead and say so in the close comment.
2. **Quarantine bytes:** the apparent sizes of regular files under every `<run>/quarantine/`, `<cache>/quarantine/` and, for each registered client in the view's Registry layer, every `<meta>/snapshots/<name>/quarantine/` where `engine::repair::half_tx(name)` recognizes a repair half (only `engine::repair` parses `.repair` names, E5's rule). Every listing and walk goes through E3's bounded walker with the detector's `Budget`.
3. **Order and early stop:** names, then the `stat`s, then the quarantine walks; the detector stops as soon as both thresholds are passed.
4. **Thresholds** (strictly greater): `fix_undo_runs > DOCTOR_RUNS_SOFT_MAX` (200) or `quarantine_bytes > DOCTOR_QUARANTINE_SOFT_MAX` (1 GiB).
5. **Cut short** (M4-D43): a budget or entry limit reached returns `incomplete` (E3 turns it into `check-incomplete`, so the run is never `DONE_OK`), **and** if what was counted already passes a threshold, the finding too, since more entries can only add.

The detector reads only (E3's purity scan: no `fsx::`, no `WriteSession` under `src/doctor/detectors/`) and never reads below `WTF/`.

### 3. The finding

- `instance`: `fm-state_files-doctor-runs-accumulated@machine` (E1's helper), `label` "machine", `target: null`, `confidence: high`.
- `evidence` (M4-D42, counts only): `{"runs": 1243, "fix_undo_runs": 212, "runs_soft_max": 200, "quarantine_bytes": 1310720, "quarantine_soft_max": 1073741824, "over": ["fix_undo_runs"]}`; `over` lists `fix_undo_runs` and/or `quarantine_bytes`. When cut short, the counts are what was counted.
- `remediation`: `{command: "omaddons doctor gc --before 30d --dry-run", argv: ["omaddons","doctor","gc","--before","30d","--dry-run"], destructive: false, auto_fixable: false, needs_force: false}` with the explanation "preview what gc would delete; the real run is yours to choose, because it ends the undo of every repair it deletes". `30d` is `DOCTOR_GC_SUGGESTED_AGE` through s3's `suggested_age_arg()`.
- **The `doctor_gc` hint.** When this finding is present, `doctor`'s `commands[]` gains `{action: "doctor_gc", command: "omaddons doctor gc --before 30d --dry-run", argv: […], destructive: false}` after its `doctor_explain` hints, and `next_steps` mirrors it (M4-D34). It is the first output that emits A2's `doctor_gc` action (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.2`), offered only as a preview (M4-D11).
- `status`: the row's Appendix B status column is `Q (machine)`: plain `status` reports it as a machine-level issue, `status --cached` does not (it is not `cached`). That mapping is F8's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.8`, `status` on the registry); this part adds nothing to `src/app/status.rs`.

### 4. The fixture (`tests/doctor/fixtures/fm_state_files_doctor_runs_accumulated.rs`, E3's `Fixture` trait)

```rust
/// fm-state_files-doctor-runs-accumulated: 201 fix runs older than 30 days, each keeping
/// its record and an actions log. Nothing deletes them but `doctor gc`, so the doctor
/// reports them (P3, quick tier, evidence: the counts) and suggests the gc preview.
pub struct DoctorRunsAccumulated;
impl Fixture for DoctorRunsAccumulated {
    fn corrupt(&self, home: &Home) { /* seed_run(…, Fix, real now, actions log, empty backups/) × 201 */ }
    fn assert_healthy(&self, home: &Home) { /* doctor --json --only <id> → exit 0 */ }
    fn subject(&self, home: &Home) -> Vec<PathBuf> { vec![home.env.state().join("doctor/runs")] }
}
```

- The runs are seeded at the real time with s3's `tests/common/doctor.rs::seed_run` (E3's modes: 0700 directories, 0400 records), and `run_env()` (E3's defaulted hook) sets `OMADDONS_NOW` 40 days ahead, so `--before 30d` makes them eligible.
- Register it where E3's fixture list lives (`tests/doctor/mod.rs`). F9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`) runs it through the per-detector properties (repeatability, true positive, no false positive on `common::realistic_home()`, purity, status agreement).

### 5. README (this commit)

The doctor's failure-mode table gains row 17: id, P3, `quick`, "fix and undo runs past 200, or quarantines past 1 GiB", remediation `omaddons doctor gc --before 30d --dry-run` (a preview), status column "plain `status` (machine)". Troubleshooting gains "the doctor reports `doctor-runs-accumulated`": what it counts, why diagnose runs do not count, that the remediation previews, and how to bind and run the real gc.

### 6. What not to do

- Never put the real gc (`--yes`) in the remediation, the hint or anything a button could run.
- Never read `report.json` per run in this detector (the `quick` budget), and never report a cut-short count as clean.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `FAILURE_MODES` holds the row with the fields above, passing E1's invariant test; `doctor explain fm-state_files-doctor-runs-accumulated` describes it, and `doctor capabilities` lists it once E4 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4) has landed.
- [ ] On the fixture, `doctor --json --only fm-state_files-doctor-runs-accumulated` exits 1 with one finding (instance `…@machine`, the evidence keys, `over: ["fix_undo_runs"]`), and its remediation argv parses and runs on the fixture, exits 0, lists 201 deletions and deletes nothing (`<state>` hashes identical).
- [ ] 200 fix runs and 1,000 diagnose runs give no finding; 1 GiB + 1 byte of quarantine (a sparse file) with no fix runs gives one with `over: ["quarantine_bytes"]`; exactly 1 GiB gives none.
- [ ] A detector cut short by a one-entry budget reports `check-incomplete`, and also the finding when the counted runs already pass the bound.
- [ ] After a real `doctor gc --before 30d --yes` on the fixture, the finding is gone.
- [ ] `doctor`'s `commands[]` holds the `doctor_gc` hint (the preview argv, `destructive: false`) when the finding is present, and its argv runs and exits 0.
- [ ] `status --json` (not `--cached`) reports `fm-state_files-doctor-runs-accumulated` as a machine-level issue with the same id `doctor` reports, and `status --cached` does not (the test is enabled by whichever of this leaf and F8 lands second).
- [ ] README's doctor table has row 17 and Troubleshooting its entry.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes and `ubs` is clean on the changed files.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

In `src/doctor/detectors/state_files.rs`, on tempdir homes (`Paths::with_roots`) with synthetic run directories and E3's view built over them:

- `counts_only_runs_with_an_actions_log` (5 diagnose runs, 3 fix runs with `actions.jsonl`, 2 dry-run fix runs without, 1 undo run with, 1 staged run → `runs: 11` (the staged run is not counted) and `fix_undo_runs: 4`; the message prints both counts and the listing).
- `thresholds` (table: 200 → none; 201 → finding `over: [fix_undo_runs]`; `GIB` bytes → none; `GIB + 1` → `over: [quarantine_bytes]`; both → both, in that order).
- `quarantine_bytes_sum_every_root` (a file in a run's quarantine, one in `<cache>/quarantine/<run>/`, one in a client half's `quarantine/`, one in a half's `files/` which does not count, one under an unregistered client's half which is not seen).
- `a_cut_short_walk_is_incomplete` (a one-entry `Budget` → `incomplete` and no finding with 0 counted fix runs) and `a_cut_short_walk_that_already_passed_reports_both` (a bound past 201 runs but before the quarantine walk → finding and `incomplete`).
- `evidence_holds_counts_only` (serialize the evidence; its keys are exactly the six; no path, no name).
- `the_remediation_is_the_gc_preview` (argv equal to `["omaddons","doctor","gc","--before","30d","--dry-run"]`, `destructive: false`).
- `instance_is_machine`.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

`tests/doctor.rs`, each a `TestLog` scenario:

- `gc_growth_row_finds_the_fixture`: `corrupt()`; `doctor --json --only fm-state_files-doctor-runs-accumulated` → 1, the finding as above; `log.tree(<state>)`; run the finding's `remediation.argv` → 0, `deletions` holds 201 `run` entries; `log.assert_unchanged(<state>)`.
- `gc_growth_row_ignores_diagnose_runs`: 1,000 seeded diagnose runs and 200 fix runs → `doctor --only …` → 0, no finding.
- `gc_growth_row_reports_quarantine_bytes`: one fix run whose `quarantine/state/blob` is a sparse file of `GIB + 1` bytes (`File::set_len`) → finding, `over: ["quarantine_bytes"]`; no disk space is used.
- `gc_growth_row_clears_after_gc`: on the fixture, `doctor gc --before 30d --dry-run` → token → `doctor gc --before 30d --yes --if-match <token>` → 0 → `doctor --only …` → 0.
- `gc_diagnose_offers_the_doctor_gc_hint`: on the fixture, bare `doctor --json` → `commands[]` holds the `doctor_gc` entry, `next_steps` its command; its argv run → 0.
- `gc_growth_row_agrees_with_status`: on the fixture, `status --json` issue ids include the row's id at machine level; `status --cached --json` do not. Decided while writing this bead: if F8 has not landed when this subtask is worked, the test is committed with `#[ignore = "enabled by F8: status takes its issues from the registry"]`, and whichever of this leaf and F8 lands second removes the ignore and makes it pass; the close comment says which.

The fixture also runs in F9's harness (after this leaf).

### Logging

`TestLog` throughout: steps "corrupt", "diagnose", "remediation", "gc", "status"; every run through `log.run` (argv, `OMADDONS_NOW`, exit, envelope); `log.json("finding", …)` of the finding; `log.tree`/`log.assert_unchanged` over `<state>/doctor`. Unit tests: one name per case; every message names the case, the seeded layout (counts per kind) and the actual counts and evidence.

## Considerations

- **Shared file.** `src/doctor/detectors/state_files.rs` is also F3's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.3`, rows 11–16): whichever lands first creates it, the other appends a function and its registry row.
- **The quick budget.** On a large store (thousands of diagnose runs) the listing alone can exhaust 5 ms in a release build; the row then reports `check-incomplete`, whose remediation reruns it with a larger `--budget` (E3's rule). That is honest, and `doctor gc` (which deletes diagnose runs by the same rules) shrinks the store.
- **Status timing.** The plan's lanes put this leaf before F8, while F8's text assumes the row exists; the whichever-second rule above keeps both beads' acceptance true without a new edge.
- **Privacy.** The evidence is counts; no path is reported.

## Dependencies

- **Parent:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.8 (`doctor gc`: the retention plan).
- **Before it:** s3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.8.3`, the command its remediation runs; through it s1's constants and s2's `runs.rs` and `half_tx`). T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs) blocks this subtask (filed edge).
- **After it:** nothing in this leaf; s5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.8.5`) may run beside it. Outside the leaf, F9 runs its fixture and F8 its status half.

title: E2E: gc's races, reachability pins, `latest`, interruption and injected failures (the design gate's adversarial matrix)
description:
Part 5 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.8 (`doctor gc`: the retention plan). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.8 builds `omaddons doctor gc`, the one command that deletes what the doctor keeps, through a retention plan that never deletes what an unfinished transaction, an interrupted undo or a still-reactivatable set-aside needs, bound to its preview and computed again under the global lock (M4-D36). It adds a **deletion rule**, so it is a design-gate leaf (common rule 14): it closes only when its own adversarial matrix passes, and F9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`, the safety harness) never discovers whether gc's protocol works.

This part is that matrix, as end-to-end scenarios through the real binary: the races at the `doctor.gc.planned` pause, the reachability pins on real crashed repairs and undos, `latest` under every outcome, a gc killed and failed at every fsx boundary it crosses followed by recovery and repeated gc runs, the fail-closed case, the cap and two gc runs at once. It is its own step because it is the leaf's proof, written after the command (s3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.8.3`) exists, and because the leaf's design gate is passed only when it is closed.

## Technical Approach

### 1. What each scenario stands on (restated)

- **The plan** (s2): a group of artifacts (a run directory, its `.repair` client halves, its cache quarantine) is eligible when its run started strictly before `--before`; kept with `active_run` when one of its transactions has a live in-flight lock, or it has no `report.json` and is younger than an hour; kept with `unfinished_journal` when a repair journal of one of its transactions exists; a candidate is kept with `active_undo` when it overlaps what an unfinished undo of a repair reads, `unfinished_journal` when it overlaps what another unfinished journal protects, `recovery_dependency` when it holds a live set-aside's quarantined set whose guards still hold, or when an unreadable history line names it. Everything else eligible is deleted, at most 1,000 victims per run, whole groups only, oldest first, inside a group the cache quarantine, then the halves, then the run directory.
- **The command** (s3): plan without the lock; `doctor.gc.planned` (pause); the global lock; a fresh plan; an unknowable repair journal refuses; `--if-match` compared; `latest` retargeted (or removed as the first victim); `prune(…, LockUse::HandOff(guard))` renames into trash under the lock, releases it, deletes. **No recovery** runs. A dry run never takes the lock.
- **Why races are safe:** `--before` is resolved once at the start and never in the future, so a fix committing while gc waits is never eligible; an undo that starts while gc waits either finishes under the lock before gc gets it, or crashes and leaves a journal that pins its inputs; with `--if-match`, any change to the set, the identities, the `latest` decision or `undo_lost` is `plan_stale`.

### 2. Scenes and helpers (`tests/doctor.rs`, `tests/common/doctor.rs`)

- **Time.** Scenes are built at the real time. Every gc runs with `OMADDONS_NOW` = the scene's build time + 40 days (debug builds), with `--before 30d`, so run ids (from `clock::now()`) and transaction ULIDs (from the real clock) are both about 40 days old, and runs made during a scenario under the same frozen time are young.
- **Repairs and undos** come from E6's test fixers (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`; `OMADDONS_TEST_FIXERS=1`, debug builds): `fm-test-write` (an overwriting write, so a backup), `fm-test-quarantine` (a quarantine, so a client-side `.repair` half when its victim is under a client), with the planting helpers E6's tests use, and `doctor undo <run>` (E7, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7`).
- **Crashes** run the command in a child with `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS=<name>=abort[@N]`; **pauses** use `tests/common/pause.rs` (`Pause::new`, `.env()`, `.reached(name)`, `.resume(name)`).
- **A synthetic set-aside**, `seed_set_aside(env, target)` (new in `tests/common/doctor.rs`): an old run directory holding `quarantine/state/journal/<tx>.jsonl` (a copy of a small folder journal) and a committed history line of kind `repair` (built with the library's `HistoryEntry` from E12 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.12` and appended as one JSON line) whose single `rename_noreplace` primitive moves that file into the quarantine and carries a guard on the target's current record generation, the shape F2's set-aside writes (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.2`). When F2 has landed, the scenario also runs once with a real set-aside (`doctor fix --only fm-concurrency_primitives-journal-unreadable --force --yes` on a planted unreadable journal).
- **`GcScene::standard()`** (built fresh for every case, deterministic): a registered client `retail` with `WTF/` holding `FAKEACCT`/`FakeRealm`/`FakeChar`; old runs:
  - `D1`, `D2`: diagnose runs (`doctor --json`);
  - `F`: a committed `fm-test-write` repair (backup in `F/backups/1`) and a committed `fm-test-quarantine` of a file under `retail`'s `<meta>` (a `.repair` half);
  - `R1`: a `fm-test-write` repair crashed at `doctor.repair.step=abort` (journal unfinished, nobody recovered it);
  - `R2`: a committed `fm-test-write` repair, then `doctor undo R2` crashed at its first step (`U`'s journal unfinished, its reads are `R2/backups/1`);
  - `latest` naming `D2`.
  Expected plan: deletions `D1`, `D2`, `F` (its half, then its run dir); excluded `R1` (`unfinished_journal`, its run and half), `R2` (`kind: backup`, `R2/backups/1`, `active_undo`); `undo_lost` = `F`'s transactions; `latest` retargeted to the newest retained terminal run, or removed when none.

### 3. The scenarios

**A. Races, paused at `doctor.gc.planned`.**

1. `gc_race_a_fix_that_commits_meanwhile_is_never_deleted_from`: start `doctor gc --before 30d --yes` paused; run `doctor fix --only fm-test-write` (it commits a run `N` and a backup); resume. Assert gc exits 0; `N`'s directory, backup and half hash as before the resume; `doctor undo N` → 0 and its subject is byte-identical to before `N`'s repair; the old victims are gone.
2. `gc_race_an_undo_that_crashes_meanwhile_keeps_its_inputs`: a scene with only `R2` committed (no crashed undo yet); start the gc (unbound) paused; run `doctor undo R2` crashed at `doctor.repair.step=abort@1`; resume. Assert `R2/backups/1` exists and `excluded` (from `--json`) holds it with `active_undo`; then `config set check_interval_hours 6` → 0 (recovers the undo); then `doctor undo R2` → 0 and the subject is byte-identical to before `R2`'s repair.
3. `gc_race_an_undo_that_finishes_meanwhile`: as 2, but the undo succeeds during the pause. Assert gc exits 0; `R2` (eligible and unpinned once the undo committed) is deleted and is not in `undo_lost` (its repair is reverted); the undo's own young run and its backups are untouched; undoing that undo (`doctor undo <the undo's run>`) → 0, because it reads only the undo run's own backups.
4. `gc_race_a_bound_gc_whose_set_changed_is_stale`: a dry run gives the token; then start `doctor gc --before 30d --yes --if-match <token>` paused, and change one thing; resume. Variants, each a fresh scene: (a) **grown**: `config set check_interval_hours 6` recovers `R1`'s journal, unpinning `R1`; (b) **shrunk**: an undo of `F` crashes, pinning `F`; (c) **`latest`**: a `doctor` diagnose finishes and moves `latest`; (d) **identity**: a listed run directory is replaced by an identical copy at the same path (`std::fs` in the test); (e) **`undo_lost`**: an undo of `F` commits, so `F`'s repair is no longer live and leaves `undo_lost` while the deletion set stays the same. Assert exit 4, `error.code` `plan_stale`, `details.changed` (grown/shrunk/identity: `selection` and/or `observed`; `latest`: `selection`; `undo_lost`: `observed`), `retryable: false`, `fix_argv` the `--dry-run` form; `<state>/doctor`, `<state>/journal`, the client's `<meta>/snapshots` and `<cache>/quarantine` hash identical to just before the resume (nothing deleted, nothing recovered).
5. `gc_race_the_unbound_run_uses_the_fresh_plan`: the pre-lock plan includes `F`; pause; crash an undo of `F`; resume an unbound real run. Assert `F` is kept (`active_undo`).
6. `gc_two_at_once_serialize`: two real gc runs, both paused at `doctor.gc.planned`, then both resumed. Assert both exit 0, no error, the union of their `deletions` equals the standard plan's, no path appears in both, and the end state equals one gc's.

**B. Reachability.**

7. `gc_pin_an_old_backup_needed_by_a_newer_crashed_undo_is_active_undo`: the standard scene; `doctor gc --before 30d --dry-run --json` lists `R2/backups/1` as `{kind: backup, pin: active_undo}`; the real run keeps it; `config set` recovers `U`; `doctor undo R2` → 0, byte-identical subject.
8. `gc_pin_a_run_whose_repair_journal_is_unfinished_is_kept`: `R1` and its half are excluded with `unfinished_journal`; after the real gc, `R1`'s journal bytes are unchanged (**gc did not recover**), then `config set` recovers it (rolled back), and the next `doctor gc --before 30d --yes` deletes `R1` (no report, old, no journal).
9. `gc_pin_a_reactivatable_set_aside_is_recovery_dependency`: `seed_set_aside` on `retail`; the dry run excludes its quarantined file with `recovery_dependency`; then a committed install on `retail` (a local `--file` zip built with `tests/common/archives.rs`), which moves its record generation; the next dry run lists the set-aside's run as a deletion with `may_hold_only_copy: true` and its transaction in `undo_lost`.
10. `gc_pin_an_unreadable_history_line_keeps_the_run_it_names`: append a line `{"tx":"<F's tx>","kind":` (cut, not JSON) followed by a newline and another valid append; the dry run keeps `F` with `recovery_dependency`.
11. `gc_pin_no_deletion_overlaps_a_protected_resource`: in every scenario of A and B, before the gc, call the library's `journal::diagnose` (E11 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.11`, read-only) on the `TestEnv`'s paths, and assert that no `deletions[].path` overlaps (E13's `overlaps`) any protected resource of an unfinished journal.

**C. `latest`.**

12. `gc_latest_is_retargeted_to_the_newest_retained_terminal_run`: `latest` names `D2` (a victim); a young `DONE_FINDINGS` diagnose exists; after gc, `readlink latest` is `runs/<young id>` and the report says `{from: D2, to: <young id>}`.
13. `gc_latest_is_removed_when_no_run_remains`: every run old and unpinned; after gc, `latest` does not exist and the report says `{from: D2, to: null}`.
14. `gc_latest_dangling_is_repaired_and_a_regular_file_left_alone`: (a) `latest` names a run removed by hand → retargeted; (b) `latest` is a regular file → untouched, `latest: null`.
15. `gc_latest_never_dangles_when_killed`: kill the gc at `fsx.symlink_atomic.after=abort`, at `fsx.rename_with.before=abort@1` (the first trash rename) and at `fsx.prune.renamed=abort`; after each, `latest` is absent or resolves to an existing run directory.

**D. Interruption and injected failure** (each `N` on a freshly built standard scene).

16. `gc_killed_at_every_boundary_strands_nothing`: for each family `fsx.mutate.checked` and `fsx.rename_with.before`, for `N` = 1, 2, …: run `doctor gc --before 30d --yes` in a child with `<family>=abort@N`; stop when the child exits 0 (the failpoint never fired). After each kill assert: (i) `latest` absent or resolving; (ii) `R1`'s run, half and journal, and `R2/backups/1`, hash as before the gc; (iii) every victim path either exists with its pre-gc tree hash or does not exist (no half-deleted victim: prune moves whole trees); (iv) `<state>/journal/` is byte-identical (gc never touches journals). Then `config set check_interval_hours 6` → 0 with a `journal_recovered` warning for `R1` and for `U`, and no journal left; then `doctor gc --before 30d --yes` → 0 and every eligible victim is gone and every trash directory empty; then a third gc → `deletions: []`. Also the single points `fsx.prune.renamed=abort` and `fsx.prune.deleting=abort` (the second leaves only trash, which the next gc's prune sweeps). Assert that the number of boundaries fired (`N − 1` at the stop) is at least the number of victims, so every rename was witnessed, and log it.
17. `gc_io_error_at_every_boundary_reports_and_the_next_gc_finishes`: the same sweep with `=error@N`: exit 74 (`io`, with `details.path`); the same invariants (i)–(iv); the next gc finishes; a third deletes nothing.
18. `gc_injected_failure_before_any_deletion_deletes_nothing`: `fsx.symlink_atomic.before=error` with a retarget planned → exit 74, every victim still present, `latest` unchanged.

**E. Fail closed, the cap and recovery.**

19. `gc_fail_closed_on_an_unknowable_repair_journal`: plant `<state>/journal/<ULID>.repair.jsonl` whose first line is complete but does not decode (`{"type":"prepared","format":"1.0","tx":7}\n`); the dry run → 0, every eligible candidate `unfinished_journal`, `deletions: []`, a `journal_pending` warning; the real run → 74, `state_corrupt`, `details.reason` `journal_unreadable`, `details.tx`; every tree unchanged. Variant: `"format":"2.0"` → 4, `state_too_new`, `journal_too_new`.
20. `gc_cap_deletes_at_most_the_maximum_and_the_next_gc_finishes`: 1,005 old diagnose runs (`seed_run`); a dry run lists 1,000, the oldest, `remaining: 5`; the real run deletes those 1,000; a second deletes 5, `remaining: 0`.
21. `gc_does_not_recover`: the standard scene; after the real gc, `R1`'s and `U`'s journals are byte-identical to before it, and no `journal_recovered` warning was emitted by the gc.
22. `gc_scenarios_are_private`: every gc run in this file passes `--progress json`, and `assert_private_all(stdout, stderr)` holds (the scene's `WTF/` holds the planted names).

### 4. Gate time

The matrix builds a fresh scene per case (an absolute-path home cannot be copied without changing every identity, as E11 found for its differential test). Keep each scene small, run cases as separate `#[test]` functions so `cargo test` runs them in parallel, and never drop a boundary to save time. If the suite exceeds about 30 s in a debug build on the development machine, file the speed-up `discovered-from` this bead rather than sampling.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every scenario of §3 passes in `cargo test` (the gate), each a `TestLog` scenario.
- [ ] Races: a fix committing and an undo starting while gc waits are never deleted from; a bound gc whose set, identities, `latest` decision or `undo_lost` changed is `plan_stale` with the matching `details.changed` and deletes and recovers nothing; an unbound gc uses the fresh plan; two gc runs at once serialize without error.
- [ ] Reachability: an old run's backup that a newer crashed undo needs is kept with `active_undo`; a run whose repair journal is unfinished is kept with `unfinished_journal`; a reactivatable set-aside is kept with `recovery_dependency` and becomes a deletion with `may_hold_only_copy: true` and an `undo_lost` entry once its guard changed; an unreadable history line keeps the run it names; no deletion overlaps any resource `journal::diagnose` reports as protected.
- [ ] `latest` is retargeted, removed when no run remains, repaired when dangling, left alone when a regular file, and never dangling after a kill.
- [ ] A gc killed or failed at every `fsx.mutate.checked` and `fsx.rename_with.before` boundary, and at `fsx.prune.renamed`, `fsx.prune.deleting` and the `latest` write, leaves `<state>/journal/` and every pinned input intact; the next lock-taking command recovers every planted crashed journal; the next gc finishes; a third deletes nothing; the boundary count witnessed covers every victim.
- [ ] An unknowable repair journal pins everything in the dry run and fails the real run with its stop error, deleting nothing.
- [ ] The cap holds (1,000, `remaining: 5`, the next gc finishes), gc never recovers, and every gc output is private.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes and `ubs` is clean on the changed files.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

None new: this part is the end-to-end matrix. (`tests/common/doctor.rs`'s new helpers carry doc comments and are exercised by every scenario.)

### Integration and end-to-end tests

`tests/doctor.rs`, functions `gc_race_*`, `gc_pin_*`, `gc_latest_*`, `gc_killed_*`, `gc_io_*`, `gc_injected_*`, `gc_fail_closed_*`, `gc_cap_*`, `gc_does_not_recover`, `gc_scenarios_are_private` and `gc_two_at_once_serialize`, exactly as §3 lists them, with their scene, steps and assertions. `argc e2e doctor` runs them with verbose logs.

### Logging

Every scenario uses T1's `TestLog` (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`): `let log = tlog!();`; one `log.step` per phase ("build scene", "preview", "pause reached", "change during the pause", "resume", "kill N", "after the kill", "recover", "gc again", "third gc"); every binary run through `log.run(&env, &argv)` (argv, `OMADDONS_NOW`, `OMADDONS_TEST_FIXERS`, the armed failpoints and their `@N`, exit, envelope, stderr events); `log.json("plan", …)` of each dry run's report; `log.json("diagnose", …)` of the protected resources used by the overlap property; `log.note` of each kill's failpoint and child status and of the boundary count; `log.tree` before the gc and `log.assert_unchanged` after it over `<state>/journal`, `R1`'s and `R2`'s directories, the client's `<meta>/snapshots`, `<cache>/quarantine` and the trash directories, which logs the first differing paths. A failure prints the log path and the last 20 steps, so a failing `N` of a sweep is diagnosable from its log alone.

## Considerations

- **The point of this subtask.** It proves the deletion rule; a failing case is fixed in s2's plan or s3's flow (in this leaf), never by weakening an assertion.
- **Dependence on other leaves' test tools.** E6's test fixers and their planting helpers, E7's undo, E11's `journal::diagnose` and E13's `overlaps` are library or binary surfaces of landed blockers; if a name differs, use the landed one.
- **Hot spot `tests/doctor.rs`** (E3–E7 and s3, s4 append functions; rebase before each gate run) and `tests/common/doctor.rs` (E3's; append helpers).
- **The set-aside case** is synthetic until F2 lands, because F2 is not a blocker of this leaf; F9's harness then round-trips the real one, and this scenario's F2 variant runs whenever F2 exists.
- **Flakiness.** Pauses are marker files, so the interleaving is the one the test names; kills are `abort`s in children; nothing sleeps for timing.

## Dependencies

- **Parent:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.8 (`doctor gc`: the retention plan).
- **Before it:** s3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.8.3`, the command, and through it s1's prune changes and s2's plan). T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs) blocks this subtask (filed edge). It can be worked beside s4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.8.4`, the growth row).
- **After it:** the leaf's design gate is passed when this closes; T4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4`, the slice 3 demo) records "a bound gc" from these scenarios.

title: The M3 build against M4 state
description:
## How to work this bead

This bead is worked through its 5 subtasks, listed below in work order. Claim a subtask, not this bead (`br ready --parent omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9` lists the ready ones). The agent that closes the last open subtask then verifies every acceptance criterion of this bead (they are the leaf's, not any one subtask's), and closes this bead with `br close omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9 --reason "done: <evidence> · found: <ids>"`. Until this bead is closed, every bead it blocks stays blocked.

1. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9.1 Tests: the M3 build, its runner, the M4 inventory and the control rows. `tests/common/compat.rs` builds `c0ab5e9` with the toolchain that commit records, keeps a provenance record, runs that binary in a test home, ages what it judges by age, and checks what it must not touch; `tests/compat_m3.rs` starts with two control tests; the harness's unit tests run in the gate.
2. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9.2 E2E: the M3 build against committed M4 state. Every artifact class at rest (run directories, committed repairs of every fix kind, a repair undo, a committed set-aside, stored plans with their lease and lock files, quarantines on every side, temp symlinks, M4's history lines), under every M3 command, at once and two hours on.
3. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9.3 E2E: the M3 build against interrupted repairs, interrupted repair undos and an interrupted `apply`. Every fix kind crashed before and after each of its primitives and at each phase point.
4. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9.4 E2E: the M3 build against set-asides and reactivations interrupted at every primitive, the provisional `<tx>.reactivating.jsonl` included.
5. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9.5 README's limitation for pre-M4 builds, written from the recorded tables, and the leaf's own checkpoint run.

Subtasks 2, 3 and 4 each add one file under `tests/compat_m3/` and one `mod` line to `tests/compat_m3.rs`, so they can be worked at the same time once subtask 1 has landed. Subtask 5 comes last, because it needs every table.

**Size M, closed as one leaf.** H4 quotes the whole characterization and T4 quotes its last run; a partial table would let README promise something no test showed. The subtasks split the work, not the closure.

## Background

**What this leaf is.** M4 writes state that no earlier build has seen: repair journals and their client halves, doctor run directories with backups and quarantines, cache quarantines, suspended journal sets, the provisional journal of an unfinished reactivation, stored plans with their lease and lock files, target-less history lines, and the fsx temp names a crash can leave. An older `omaddons` binary can meet all of it. A binary installed with `cargo install` may be older than the one the bar widget stamped, and an agent or a person can run either on the same home.

M3 learned what that costs. The last M2 build deleted M3's journals unread until their names changed (M3's comment 1242). M3 fixed it by naming the journal, stage and snapshot halves of a settings transaction `<tx>.wtf` (comment 1250), and `tests/compat_m2.rs` proved it by running the M2 build against M3 state.

This leaf does the same for M4. It builds the last M3 commit, `c0ab5e9`, with the toolchain that commit records, and runs it against homes holding every kind of M4 state, at rest and interrupted at every primitive. It asserts that the M3 build never deletes or overwrites what M4 still needs. It records everything else that build does, and turns the record into README's limitation for pre-M4 builds. Where the M3 build would delete an M4 artifact, the artifact's naming changes until it does not.

It is a verification leaf. It adds test code, one README entry and, only if the M3 build touches something, the renames that stop it. It adds no command, no error or warning code, no constant in `src/limits.rs` and no wire name of its own.

**Goals it serves.**

- **G-M4-6, no new risk to the engine's guarantees:** "A build from before M4 never destroys what M4 wrote: the M3 build is characterized against M4 state, and README states the result." This leaf is that characterization.
- **G-M4-4, diagnosable and repairable:** every auto-fixable state is repaired by one consented command that "backs up verbatim, never deletes", and what a repair keeps is deleted only by `doctor gc`. An older build that swept a quarantine or a run directory would break that promise from outside; this leaf shows it does not.
- **The vision's thesis:** omaddons stays the sole, safe, undoable authority over what it manages, also when an older copy of itself runs on the same home.

**The checkpoint criterion it owns: 16, older builds against M4 state.** "`tests/compat_m3.rs` builds `c0ab5e9` with its recorded toolchain (`1.97.1`; never a pre-accepted `SKIP`) and runs it against homes holding: committed and interrupted repair transactions, and undo runs; target-less repair history lines; suspended journal sets and provisional `<tx>.reactivating.jsonl` journals; stored plans and their leases; doctor run directories, quarantines and temp symlinks. It records what that build does. It must never delete or overwrite anything M4 wrote that M4 would still need: repair journals and their halves, quarantines, run directories. README's Limitations quote the result." (§3.2 of the plan, added by M4-D58.)

The checkpoint's rule for this criterion: **the compatibility characterizations are never skipped.** An older commit that needs an older compiler is built with the toolchain it records; both `af10e34` and `c0ab5e9` pin `1.97.1` in `rust-toolchain.toml`, which rustup installs on demand. Otherwise a provenance-verified binary of that commit is used. If neither can be had, criterion 16 is unmet and the checkpoint says so: "compiler inconvenience is not evidence that storage is safe." The checkpoint's pre-accepted `SKIP`s (`keyless_installs_forever`, the bind-mount and size-limited-tmpfs sandbox tests, the `zsh -n` and `fish --no-execute` checks) do not include this test. Any other `SKIP` is an unmet criterion.

The slice-3 demo (T4, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4`, slice 3 end to end) pre-checks criterion 16 by quoting this test's last run, because the test is checkpoint-only. H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the checkpoint) runs it again with `cargo test --test compat_m3 -- --ignored --nocapture` (a debug build of the test, no `--release`: M3's plan got that wrong).

**The decisions that shape it.** The full decision log is also filed as comments on the milestone epic `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`.

- **M4-D58, the M3 build is characterized against M4 state** (this leaf's own decision).
  - `tests/compat_m3.rs` (debug, ignored, checkpoint only) mirrors `tests/compat_m2.rs`. It builds `c0ab5e9` into `target/compat/` with the toolchain that commit records (`1.97.1`, from its `rust-toolchain.toml`, installed by rustup on demand), and runs it against homes holding committed and interrupted repairs, repair history lines, `.repair` snapshot halves, cache quarantines, suspended journal sets and provisional `<tx>.reactivating.jsonl` journals, stored plans and their leases, and doctor run directories.
  - **No pre-accepted skip.** If the recorded toolchain cannot build the commit, a provenance-verified binary of it is used; if neither is available, criterion 16 is unmet.
  - It asserts that the M3 build never deletes or overwrites any of them. It records everything else that build does (skipping lines with `history_lines_skipped`, a conservative `undo_conflict`) for README's Known limitations.
  - If the M3 build would delete an M4 artifact (its orphan sweep matching a name, say), the artifact's naming changes until it does not, as M3 did with `.wtf`.
  - *Why:* the expected behaviour and the observed behaviour differed in M3. *Rejected:* documenting without testing.
- **M4-D31, a repair is a second journal family the older build cannot see.** The journal is `<state>/journal/<tx>.repair.jsonl`, its lines tagged by `"type"` (`prepared`, `step`, `done`, `rolled_back`, `committed`). "Builds before M4 list only `<tx>.jsonl` and `<tx>.wtf.jsonl` (`paths::tx_named` strips only `.wtf`), so they never see it. M4 keeps it that way: only `engine/repair.rs` parses repair names, and `tx_named` is unchanged." The history line has kind `repair`, `target: null`, `targets`, `ops: []`, `repairs[]` and `doctor_run_id`. "Builds before M4 cannot decode a target-less line, so they skip it with `history_lines_skipped`, and their undo's rule 5 treats it as touching everything. That fails closed." This leaf tests that reliance against the real older binary.
- **M4-D35 and M4-D36, what a repair keeps.** A quarantined path is renamed (`RENAME_NOREPLACE`) into the root on its own side: `<state>` and `<config>` victims into `<run>/quarantine/{state,config}/…`, `<cache>` victims into `<cache>/quarantine/<run id>/…`, client victims into `<meta>/snapshots/<repair tx>.repair/quarantine/…`. "Transaction retention and the orphan sweep never touch `<meta>/snapshots/<tx>.repair/` or `<cache>/quarantine/`, and nothing touches `<state>/doctor/`." Only `doctor gc` deletes, through a bound, dependency-aware retention plan. M4's own retention was taught that rule; the M3 build's was not, so only its name parsing protects these.
- **M4-D38, set-aside is suspension; reactivation is guarded behind a barrier.**
  - The set-aside moves a stuck journal's set (the journal file, `.jsonl` or `.wtf.jsonl`; its in-flight lock; its state snapshot half; its client stage and snapshot half) into quarantine, one `RenameNoReplace` per artifact, with a suspension manifest as the primitives' `guards`.
  - Its undo (a reactivation) restores every artifact but the journal first, restores the journal under the provisional name `<tx>.reactivating.jsonl`, "which `tx_named` cannot parse", and its last primitive, the activation, renames it to its own name. Recovery resolves a repair that owns a barrier before it considers folder journals.
  - F2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.2`, the journal fixers) orders the set-aside journal-last, "so that until the final primitive the journal stays where every listing, recovery and orphan sweep (of this build and of older ones) sees it". E7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7`, undo of repairs) orders the reactivation: every other inverse first, then the provisional restore, then the activation.
- **M4-D21, M4-D24 and M4-D61, stored plans.** A plan is `<cache>/plans/<plan_id>.json` (mode 0600), admitted under `<cache>/plans/.lock`, applied under the lease `<cache>/plans/<plan_id>.lease`, and swept after `PLAN_TTL` (24 h) by M4's own bounded sweep.
- **M4-D32 and M4-D33, run directories.** `<run>` (`<state>/doctor/runs/<YYYY-MM-DDTHH-MM-SSZ>__<ULID>/`) holds `report.json`, `runtime.jsonl` and `actions.jsonl` (0400 once the run is terminal), `backups/<seq>`, `quarantine/` and `undo.sh` (0500); the directory stays 0700. `<state>/doctor/latest` is a symlink to the newest terminal run. Diagnose, fix and undo runs each make one. A run is staged as `<state>/doctor/runs/.<id>.tmp/` and published by `RENAME_NOREPLACE`.
- **M4-D25:** a history line committed by `apply` carries the additive field `plan`.
- **M4-D55, after H1:** this leaf may land after H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, the pre-freeze contract audit) has closed, because it adds no wire shape. A rename it needs is not additive: "a change they need that is not additive is a defect against H1: it is fixed before H2 regenerates the golden for the last time, and recorded on H1's change list."
- **§8.1 defaults** applied here: 6, "fail closed on anything persisted that cannot be fully read" (what the M3 build is expected to do with M4's lines and journals), and 7, "never ask the owner": every open question below is decided and marked.

**What M4 writes, and where** (the artifact classes this leaf plants; each comes from the leaf named):

| Artifact | Location and shape | Written by |
|---|---|---|
| repair journal | `<state>/journal/<tx>.repair.jsonl` | E5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`, the repair transaction) |
| provisional journal | `<state>/journal/<tx>.reactivating.jsonl` (one spelling for every family) | E14 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14`, fences and activation barriers), E7 |
| a repair's in-flight lock | `<state>/inflight/<repair tx>.lock` | E5 |
| client half | `<meta>/snapshots/<tx>.repair/{files,quarantine}/` | E5 |
| cache quarantine | `<cache>/quarantine/<run id>/…` | E5 |
| run directory | `<run>/` as above; `<state>/doctor/latest`; a staged `.<id>.tmp/` after a crash | E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, `doctor diagnose`), E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`, `doctor fix`), E7 |
| suspended journal set | inside `<run>/quarantine/state/…` and `<meta>/snapshots/<repair tx>.repair/quarantine/…` | F2, or E7's test fixer `fm-test-suspend` |
| history lines | kind `repair` and kind `undo` with `target: null`, `targets`, `repairs[]`, `doctor_run_id`; `plan` on lines `apply` committed; kind `skill` | E5, E7, E12 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.12`, target-less history lines), D5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`, `omaddons apply`), B3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3`, `robot-docs install-skill`) |
| stored plans | `<cache>/plans/<plan_id>.json`, `<plan_id>.lease` (a `flock` file with a holder line), `.lock` | D4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`, the plan store), D5 |
| history projection | `<cache>/history_tail.json`, with B3's `skill_dirs[]` | derived (B3) |
| fsx temp names | `.omaddons-*` entries in omaddons-owned directories, left by a crash | crash debris (F3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.3`, reports them) |

**Facts this bead relies on** (each verified at `c0ab5e9`, which is both the commit under test and the commit the plan was verified against):

- **Toolchains.** `rust-toolchain.toml` at `c0ab5e9` (and at `af10e34`) is `channel = "1.97.1"`, `components = ["rustfmt", "clippy"]`, `profile = "minimal"`.
- **The M2 precedent.** `tests/compat_m2.rs` is debug-only (`#![cfg(debug_assertions)]`, `:14`). It builds `af10e34` in a detached worktree under `target/compat/<commit>` with `cargo build --release` (`:37-62`), runs it with the test home's environment (`:162-181`), ages entries with `File::set_modified` (`:245-265`), prints its table through `std::io::Write` on stderr (`:592`), and calls `common::checkpoint::skip` when the build fails (`:367-373`). It does not name the toolchain: it relies on rustup reading the worktree's `rust-toolchain.toml`. Its helpers live in a `#[cfg(test)] mod support` (`:30-31`) so clippy's test exemptions cover them.
- **The skip helper** (`tests/common/checkpoint.rs:18-25`) prints `SKIP <test>: <reason>` and fails unless `OMADDONS_ALLOW_SKIP` names the test. This leaf must never call it: no allowance may turn criterion 16 into a pass.

1. The M3 build never lists, recovers, sweeps or prunes a repair journal, a provisional journal, a `.repair` half, a run directory or `latest`, a cache quarantine, a stored plan, a lease or `.lock` file, or a `.omaddons-*` entry. 4. It rewrites `<cache>/history_tail.json` without `skill_dirs[]`; the next M4 command rebuilds it.
5. When the cache is over its cap, its post-commit eviction may take a blob that only a stored plan pins; M4's `apply` then downloads it again.
6. **Touch A, expected harmless:** an interrupted repair's own in-flight lock (`<state>/inflight/<repair tx>.lock`, whose writer died) is a `<ULID>.lock` with no folder journal, so once it is an hour old the M3 build's sweep deletes it after any commit. A missing lock reads as free (`src/fsx/lock.rs:251-255`), so M4's recovery should behave as if it were there.
7. **Touch B, expected to lose data:** between a reactivation's first restore and its activation, the suspended folder transaction's stage (`<meta>/stage/<tx>/` or `<tx>.wtf/`) and in-flight lock are back at their own names while its journal is in quarantine or at `<tx>.reactivating.jsonl`, where `journal::existing` cannot see it. To the M3 build's sweep they are dead orphans; their mtimes are the original transaction's (a rename keeps them), so on a real home they are old at once. The stage may hold the only copy of an addon version or of a `WTF/` tree. The snapshot halves are spared: the set-aside's own history line names the transaction id in its raw text (`in_history`), and a client half that holds a folder is kept anyway.
8. **The plan's characterized limitation:** after the activation and before the undo's durable `done`, the M3 build sees `<tx>.jsonl` (or `<tx>.wtf.jsonl`) and treats it as an ordinary journal: it recovers it when it can read and finish it, or stops on it when it is stuck. The plan calls this "a characterized limitation, not data loss".
9. An interrupted set-aside (journal last) keeps the folder journal visible to the M3 build until its final primitive, so that build's sweep spares the set, and its recovery stops on the stuck journal as it did before the set-aside.

### 2. The M3 build (`tests/common/compat.rs`, subtask 1)

```rust
pub const M3_COMMIT: &str = "c0ab5e904db26e95cade7fe1ef5129c27bb16ead"; // c0ab5e9, the last M3 commit
pub const M3_SHORT: &str = "c0ab5e9";
pub const AGE: Duration = Duration::from_secs(2 * 3600);              // past either build's ORPHAN_MIN_AGE (1 h)

pub struct OldBuild { pub short: String, pub bin: PathBuf, pub provenance: Provenance, pub reused: bool }
#[derive(Serialize, Deserialize, PartialEq)]
pub struct Provenance {
    pub commit: String,        // the full hash
    pub toolchain: String,     // the channel read from the commit's rust-toolchain.toml
    pub rustc: String,         // `rustup run <channel> rustc -vV`, verbatim
    pub profile: String,       // "release"
    pub locked: bool,          // built with --locked
    pub binary_sha256: String,
    pub built_at: String,      // RFC 3339 UTC
}
pub fn toolchain_channel(rust_toolchain_toml: &str) -> Option<String>;
pub fn old_build(short: &str, full: &str) -> Result<OldBuild, String>;  // never skips
pub fn m3() -> &'static OldBuild;                                       // OnceLock over old_build(M3_SHORT, M3_COMMIT)
```

`old_build` does, in order (all paths relative to the repository root, `env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")`):

1. Takes an exclusive `std::fs::File::lock` on `target/compat/.<short>.lock`, so two test processes never build at once; inside one process `m3()` builds once (`OnceLock`).
2. **The worktree** `target/compat/<short>/`. If it is missing, `git worktree prune` (which only forgets worktrees whose directory is gone) and `git worktree add --detach target/compat/<short> <full>`. If it exists, `git -C target/compat/<short> rev-parse HEAD` must equal `<full>`; otherwise return an error naming the directory. Never delete it: the house rules ban `rm -rf`, and it may hold someone's build.
3. **The toolchain.** Read `target/compat/<short>/rust-toolchain.toml` and take its `[toolchain] channel` (`toolchain_channel`). If `rustup run <channel> rustc -vV` fails, run `rustup toolchain install <channel> --profile minimal` once and try again. Decided while writing this bead: install explicitly rather than rely on the proxy's implicit installation, because whether rustup installs a `rust-toolchain.toml` channel on demand depends on its version and settings.
4. **The build.** `cargo build --release --locked` in the worktree, with `RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=<channel>` and `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=<worktree>/target` set and `RUSTFLAGS`, `CARGO_ENCODED_RUSTFLAGS` and `CARGO_BUILD_TARGET` removed, its output written to `target/compat/<short>-build.log`. Decided while writing this bead: the toolchain and target dir are set explicitly because the outer `cargo test` may run under a `RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN` or `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` that would override the worktree's own (`tests/compat_m2.rs` relies on neither being set); release, as `compat_m2` builds its commit, because that is what `cargo install` leaves on the `PATH`, and the paths under test (listing, recovery, the sweep, history) do not differ between profiles. The build always runs; when nothing changed it is a no-op.
5. **The provenance record** `target/compat/<short>.provenance.json`, rewritten after every successful build: the fields above, the sha256 of `target/compat/<short>/target/release/omaddons`.
6. **The verified fallback.** When the toolchain cannot be installed or the build fails, the binary already there is used only if the record exists and parses, its `commit` equals `<full>`, the worktree's `HEAD` equals `<full>`, and the binary's sha256 equals `binary_sha256`. `reused: true` and the record are logged and quoted.
7. **Otherwise** return `Err` with the last 40 lines of the build log. `m3()` then panics with: "criterion 16 is unmet: <short> could not be built with its recorded toolchain (<channel>) and no provenance-verified binary of it exists; this is a failure, never a SKIP. <log tail>". It never calls `common::checkpoint::skip` and never reads `OMADDONS_ALLOW_SKIP`.

Decided while writing this bead: "provenance-verified" means a record this helper wrote right after building the binary from that commit with that toolchain, checked by digest, because the `c0ab5e9` binary carries no commit stamp of its own (its `build.rs` stamps only the widget digest) and no other evidence ties a binary to a commit without rebuilding it. No environment variable names an outside binary: a new harness variable would need an `ENV_VARS` row (M4-D6), and the leaf adds no wire name.

The disk cost: the worktree's release target directory (about a gigabyte), on the repository's disk, never on tmpfs. A clean checkout for the checkpoint must be a full clone, so `c0ab5e9` is reachable.

### 4. Scenes, replicas and probes

- **A scene** is a deterministic builder, `fn(&TestLog) -> Scene`, that makes a fresh `Home` (`Home::new(&["wow", "wow_classic_era"])`: retail and classic era), plants what it needs, and runs the M4 build (`log.cmd(&home, argv).env("OMADDONS_TEST_FIXERS", "1")`, with `.failpoints("<point>=abort[@k]")` for a crash and `Ran::aborted()` asserted). `Scene` holds the home plus what the rows need (transaction ids, run ids, the expected class).
- **A replica** is one fresh run of the scene's builder. Each probe gets its own replica, never a copy: identities (inode and birth time) are part of every repair predicate, and a copied home would have none of the originals.
- **The probes** (M3 commands, each on its own replica):

  | Probe | Age | M3 argv |
  |---|---|---|
  | readers, then install | at once | `status --json --progress json`, `list --json`, `history --json`, then `install <probe folder> -t retail --json --progress json` |
  | install | two hours | `install <probe folder> -t retail --json --progress json` |
  | undo | at once, two hours | `undo --json --progress json` (bare: what an agent guesses first) |
  | config set | at once, two hours | `config set check_interval_hours 6 --json --progress json` |

  The probe folder is a local addon folder `M3Probe` under `<TestEnv root>/src/` (`common::addons::addon_folder` with a retail TOC, as `tests/compat_m2.rs` builds its locals). Families add probes where a row needs one (named in their subtasks).
- **Aging** (`age(home, spare)`): set the mtime two hours back (`AGE`) on every top-level entry of the directories the M3 build judges by age, `<meta>/stage/`, `<meta>/snapshots/`, `<state>/snapshots/`, `<state>/inflight/`, `<cache>/inflight/`, `<cache>/tmp/` and `<cache>/blobs/`, and of M4's own, `<state>/journal/`, `<state>/doctor/runs/`, `<cache>/quarantine/` and `<cache>/plans/`, plus `<state>/doctor/latest`, for every client of the home. Files and directories through `File::set_modified` (as `compat_m2` does), symlinks by their own mtime through `rustix::fs::utimensat` with `AtFlags::SYMLINK_NOFOLLOW` (the crate's `fs` feature is already a dependency). Never below those entries, and never `Interface/AddOns/` or `WTF/`.
  - **`spare`:** every path an unfinished repair journal's `pre` predicate names with a `stamp`, read from the journal's `prepared` line (`primitives[].pre.path.stamp` or `.to.stamp`, as JSON). Such a path is a directory that has not been renamed yet, and setting its mtime moves its ctime and so its stamp, which would make M4's next recovery stop on it for a reason no real wait produces. None of them is a sweep candidate the M3 build could delete in that state (a not-yet-moved suspension artifact still has its journal visible; a not-yet-restored reactivation artifact is inside a quarantine root).
  - Decided while writing this bead: the plan says "everything aged two hours (`touch` through the test's own fsx-free helper, as `compat_m2` does)". Aging exactly the entries the M3 build reads an age from (and M4's own top-level entries, to show it ignores them even when old) reproduces two hours passing for that build, without changing anything a real wait leaves alone. The aged paths are logged.

### 5. What is asserted (the same in every row)

Before the M3 command (after aging, if the probe ages), the test collects; after it, collects again and compares:

1. **The protected inventory** (`M4Inventory::collect(home)`), each entry with its hash (a regular file's sha256 and mode, a directory's `tree_hash`, a symlink's target):
   - every file in `<state>/journal/` named `*.repair.jsonl` or `*.reactivating.jsonl`;
   - every entry under `<state>/doctor/` (runs, staged runs, `latest`, temp names);
   - every entry of each client's `<meta>/snapshots/` named `*.repair`;
   - every entry under `<cache>/quarantine/` and `<cache>/plans/`;
   - every path an unfinished repair or undo journal's primitives name (`path` and `to`) that exists, which covers a suspension's and a reactivation's artifacts wherever they are, except the journal's own in-flight lock `<state>/inflight/<repair tx>.lock`, which no primitive names;
   - each committed, not undone repair's subject (the files the test fixers wrote, chmodded or created), because M4's undo of that repair needs them as the repair left them.

   Every entry must still exist with the same hash. A missing entry is **deleted**, a changed one **overwritten**.
2. **History** (`history_prefix_kept`): the bytes of `<state>/history.jsonl` before are a byte prefix of the bytes after. The M3 build may append; it may never rewrite.
3. **Bytes accounted for** (`FolderBytes`): every addon folder (a directory directly holding a file whose name ends in `.toc`, any case) and every `WTF` or `WTF.previous` tree found, before the M3 command, inside a protected entry or inside an unfinished repair's subject paths, is still present after it, by `tree_hash` (which is independent of location), somewhere under the TestEnv root (the client dirs, `<state>`, `<cache>`, and the `src/` folders the scenes install from, so an install's new version is found at its source). The same check runs again after the M4 build's next commands.

**The classes.** Each row ends in one class:

- `untouched`: checks 1 to 3 hold.
- `recovered_by_m3`: the M3 build recovered a folder journal it can read (one `journal_recovered` warning of that build names the folder transaction). The folder transaction's own artifacts (its journal, in-flight lock, stage and snapshot halves) are then exempt from check 1, because recovering and cleaning them up is that build's own, legitimate behaviour on its own format. Instead the folder transaction must have ended whole (the `Interface/AddOns` tree hashes as the scene says it must after a rollback, or after a roll-forward), and checks 2 and 3 must hold, check 3 leaving out only the folders found nowhere but in that transaction's own stage (after a whole rollback or roll-forward the stage holds only what the transaction staged, which that build's cleanup prunes as it always has). This class is allowed only in the rows the family tables mark with it; anywhere else it is a failure ("unexpected recovery").
- `fail`: anything else. The row names what was deleted or overwritten (relative paths, cut at a `WTF` component), which bytes are gone and from where, and the transcript path.

Decided while writing this bead: the classes and the bytes check. The plan's criterion lists what must survive ("repair journals and their halves, quarantines, run directories"); the inventory takes every artifact M4 wrote that M4 reads again (plans and leases included, since `apply` and `plans show` read them), and the bytes check catches a loss that moves through a legitimate step, such as a stage the sweep deletes after a reactivation put it back.

**Touch A** (an interrupted repair's own in-flight lock, swept once it is an hour old) is recorded, not a failure. Decided while writing this bead, because that lock means only "the writer is alive": its flock dies with the writer, a missing file reads as free (`src/fsx/lock.rs:251-255`), E5's recovery prunes it "if present", and `tests/compat_m2.rs` never protected M3's equivalent. The row asserts the consequence instead: the M4 build's next lock-taking command settles the repair exactly as E5's oracle says. An in-flight lock that is a primitive's subject (a suspension or a reactivation moves the folder transaction's lock) is protected like any other subject.

### 6. What is recorded: the row and the table

```rust
#[derive(Serialize)]
pub struct Row {
    pub family: &'static str,     // committed | interrupted | undo | apply | set-aside | reactivation | control
    pub scene: String,            // e.g. "flatten_three", "reactivation of a stuck WTF journal"
    pub position: String,         // "at rest", "prepared", "before 2", "after 2", "done", "history", "committed"
    pub age: &'static str,        // "at once" | "2 h"
    pub m3: String,               // the M3 command, as a person would type it
    pub exit: i32,
    pub code: String,             // error.code, or "ok"
    pub warnings: Vec<String>,    // warning codes of the M3 run, in order
    pub protected: String,        // "unchanged" | "<n> deleted, <m> overwritten: <paths>"
    pub bytes: String,            // "accounted" | "<n> lost: <digests and former paths>"
    pub other: Vec<String>,       // everything else that changed: AddOns entries, history lines appended, history_tail rewritten, blobs evicted, Touch A
    pub m4_next: String,          // what the M4 build's next commands did
    pub class: &'static str,      // untouched | recovered_by_m3 | fail
}
pub fn table(title: &str, rows: &[Row]) -> String;   // Markdown; `|` escaped; paths relative to the TestEnv root, cut at WTF
pub fn print_table(title: &str, rows: &[Row]);       // through std::io::Write on stderr, as compat_m2 prints
```

Each test function prints its table, logs it (`log.json("observations", &rows)`, and `table.md` written into the test's log directory), and only then asserts that no row is `fail`, so the table is printed whether the test passes or not. "Everything else" is recorded by T1's `log.diff` over `<state>`, `<cache>`, `<config>` and each client dir before and after the M3 command, summarized into `other`.

### 7. The M4 build's next commands

After the M3 command, every row runs the M4 build: `status --json --progress json` (its warnings and issues recorded), `doctor --json --progress json` (its finding ids recorded), then the family's own checks, and the bytes check again. For interrupted repairs and undos the lock-taking command is `config set check_interval_hours 6 --json --progress json`, and in every `untouched` row the repair must then be settled as E5's oracle says (E7's for an undo): the whole subject set equals the before state when the crash preceded the durable `done`, and the after state from `done` on, never a mixture; no repair journal is left. A mismatch is a failure. To tell whose it is, a row that fails at this step rebuilds its scene once more and runs the same M4 commands with no M3 command at all (the baseline replica), and records the result in `m4_next` ("… also without the M3 build" or "… only after the M3 build"). Only after the M3 build: a criterion-16 failure, handled as section 9 says. Also without it: a bug in the owning leaf (E5, E7, E14), filed `discovered-from` this bead, which blocks omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9.5.

### 9. When the M3 build touches something

A `fail` row is handled before this bead closes, in the subtask that found it:

1. **Find the name that let the M3 build in.** The row's diff and the facts above say which code path (`tx_named`, the `<ULID>.lock` rule, the `<cache>/tmp` rule, a prune location).
2. **If a rename removes it,** rename the family in the M4 module that builds and parses that name, so the M3 build cannot parse it and M4 parses it explicitly (as `.repair` and `.wtf` before it): the owning module's unit tests, the owning leaf's suites (`tests/engine_crash.rs`, `tests/doctor_repair.rs`, …) and this whole suite re-run green. Record the rename in the close comment with a compatibility note (DEC-4, M4-D55); if H1 has closed, add it to H1's change list before H2's last regeneration of the golden; update README's file table in the same commit.
3. **If no rename can remove it,** file a P1 bug `discovered-from` the subtask, with the rows, the code path and the analysis below, and make it a blocker of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9.5, so this bead cannot close while the loss stands. Criterion 16 is not met until the bug lands and the rows are green.

**Touch B is expected to need step 3.** No name hides a restored stage from the M3 build's sweep without also hiding it from the folder journal that needs it there, and the sweep spares a stage only while `<tx>.jsonl` or `<tx>.wtf.jsonl` is visible. A suspended set is safe from that build in exactly two states, every artifact hidden or every artifact at its own name, and any reactivation of more than one artifact passes through states in between: either the journal is hidden while the stage is back (the sweep's window, a loss), or the journal is back while an artifact is still hidden (that build may then recover an incomplete set). The bug compares the candidate orders against E14's barrier (which already keeps the M4 build's own folder pass from running a journal behind an unsettled undo): restoring the stage and lock under names that build cannot parse and activating them just before the journal, which shrinks the window to single boundaries; or activating the journal before the stage, which turns the window into the plan's accepted limitation and changes M4-D38's "the activation is the last primitive". Whoever takes the bug decides, records the decision, and re-runs E7's, E14's and this suite's matrices. Decided while writing this bead: this bead does not weaken the criterion to "characterized" for a row that loses bytes, because criterion 16 says the M3 build "must never delete … anything M4 wrote that M4 would still need", and the undo's own rollback needs that stage.

### 12. Run time

Each family is several `#[test]` functions (one per fix kind, per variant, per probe group), so libtest runs them in parallel; scenes are built from scratch per replica. Each test logs its wall time and row count; the close comment quotes the total. Decided while writing this bead: if the whole suite takes more than 20 minutes on the development machine, make scene building faster (E5's technique: build a scene's static parts once into a template directory and copy it before anything is given an identity to preserve), never drop a position.

### 13. What not to do

- Never `SKIP`, never call `common::checkpoint::skip`, never read `OMADDONS_ALLOW_SKIP`.
- Never copy a crashed home to make a replica.
- Never delete `target/compat/<short>/` or any worktree.
- Never write under a real home: every command runs in a `TestEnv` home; only the build writes outside it, under `target/compat/` and the repository's worktree metadata.
- Never assert on an M3-build behaviour the M4 code cannot change (a warning text, an exit code of a refusal) beyond recording it; assert only what criterion 16 requires and what M4 owns.
- Never mark a row that loses bytes as anything but `fail`.

- `tests/compat_m3/interrupted.rs` (subtask 3): `interrupted_repair_<kind>_under_the_m3_build` and `interrupted_repair_undo_<kind>_under_the_m3_build` for the eight kinds; `an_m3_install_over_a_folder_an_interrupted_flatten_moved`; `an_interrupted_apply_under_the_m3_build`.
- `tests/compat_m3/reactivation.rs` (subtask 4): `an_interrupted_set_aside_of_a_stuck_folder_journal_under_the_m3_build` (V1), `an_interrupted_set_aside_of_a_stuck_wtf_journal_under_the_m3_build` (V3), `an_interrupted_reactivation_of_a_stuck_folder_journal_under_the_m3_build` (V1), `…_of_a_recoverable_folder_journal_…` (V2), `…_of_a_stuck_wtf_journal_…` (V3), `the_m3_build_meets_a_journal_an_m4_undo_has_just_activated`.

Each scene's steps, assertions and classes are in Technical Approach sections 4 to 8 and in the subtasks. Every M4 run asserts `assert_private_all(stdout, stderr)` (T1's `Ran::assert_private`) with `--progress json`; every M3 run is checked the same way and a leak is recorded as a row observation (the M3 build cannot be changed), and named in README if one occurs.

### Logging

As Technical Approach section 11: one sub-log per replica with the steps `build`, `crash`, `age`, `inventory before`, `m3 <command>`, `inventory after`, `bytes`, `m4 next`, `row`; trees of `<state>`, `<cache>`, `<config>` and each client dir recorded before and diffed after the M3 command; the table printed and written to `table.md`; failures naming the case, the class, the entries and the transcript path. `argc e2e compat_m3 --ignored --nocapture` runs the suite with verbose logs (T1's runner takes a suite filter and passes the remaining arguments to the test binary; the suite is ignored, so `--ignored` is needed).

### Checkpoint-only

The whole suite: `cargo test --test compat_m3 -- --ignored --nocapture` (a debug test build; no `--release`). Run by subtask 5 on the development machine for this bead's close, quoted by T4, run again by H6. **No `SKIP` is ever accepted:** a build failure without a verified binary is a failure of criterion 16, and a bug is filed `discovered-from` this bead.

## Considerations

Beads this section names: E5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`), E7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7`), E12 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.12`), E14 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14`), F2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.2`), G3 (`omad-7ccp`, group commit and deferred directory fsyncs), T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`).

- **Risk 9, the M3 build destroys M4 artifacts** (likelihood low, impact high; owner E9). Mitigation: `.repair` and `.reactivating` names the M3 build cannot parse, the compat test before the tag, renames where it touches something. Watch Touch B: if it shows as predicted, this bead stays open behind its bug.
- **Risk 11, target-less repair lines confuse readers** (medium, medium; owners E12, E7). Its mitigation includes "older builds skip them (fail closed)"; this leaf shows the older build does, and that its undo refuses rather than guessing.
- **The bytes check is what makes the criterion honest.** The inventory alone would miss Touch B in rows where the stage the sweep deletes was the undo's subject and not one of M4's named artifacts; the content search through the whole test root finds a loss wherever it happens, and finds a legitimately moved folder wherever it went.
- **What could go wrong in implementation, and how to notice.**
  - A replica made by copying: identities break and M4's next recovery stops everywhere. Every replica is rebuilt; the baseline replica of section 7 shows such a failure "also without the M3 build", which points at the scene, not at that build.
  - Aging too much (a stamped subject): M4's next recovery stops in aged rows only. `spare` is logged; a stop that appears only in aged rows points here.
  - A toolchain inherited from the outer `cargo test`: the provenance's `rustc` line says which compiler built the binary; it must be `1.97.1`'s.
  - An expected class that is wrong: `recovered_by_m3` outside the allowed rows fails as "unexpected recovery", so the class cannot hide a loss.
- **Hot spots** (§10.5 of the plan): `README.md` (everyone; edit only the Known limitations entry, the suite table row and the checkpoint command); `tests/common/mod.rs` (one line); `tests/common_selftest.rs` (append). A rename remedy touches the hot spots of its owner: `src/engine/repair.rs` (E5 → E14 → E7; F2 adds fixers, not engine code), `src/engine/journal.rs` (E11 → E13 → E5 → E14 → F1), `src/fsx/` (E13 first, G3 last), `src/state/paths.rs`; rebase on each and re-run their suites.
- **Size M.** One harness and three families of scenes over shared code; no product code unless a rename is needed.
- **Compatibility.** Nothing here changes a persisted format. A rename remedy changes a file name M4 writes: record it as a pre-release correction (M4-D55) with a compatibility note; no released build ever wrote the old name.
- **Privacy.** The scenes use the synthetic `FAKEACCT`, `FakeRealm` and `FakeChar` names. The table and README never print a path below `WTF/`. The test logs hold only `TestEnv` homes.
- **Performance.** Hundreds of replicas; parallel test functions; a 20-minute target for the whole suite on the development machine, met by faster scene building, never by fewer positions.
- **Environment.** The build needs `git`, `rustup` and network access for crates and the toolchain on a first run; afterwards the worktree's target directory caches it. The test writes outside its `TestEnv` homes only under `target/compat/` and in git's worktree metadata, as `compat_m2` does.
- **Defaults decided while writing this bead** (confirm or adjust in the close comment): one binary with three submodules; the explicit toolchain and target dir; a release build of `c0ab5e9`; the explicit `rustup toolchain install`; the provenance record as the only fallback evidence, with no environment variable; no `SKIP` path at all; the T1 runner; the replica-per-probe rule; aging the age-judged top-level entries and sparing stamped subjects; the protected inventory, the bytes check and the classes; Touch A recorded, not failed; the layout-distinct crash positions; V2 only for reactivations; journal-last for `fm-test-suspend`; Touch B handled by a blocking bug rather than a weaker criterion; this leaf writing its README entries; the 20-minute run-time target.

## Dependencies

Parent: the E epic omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5 (the doctor core).

**Blocked by:**

- D5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`, `omaddons apply`): the homes hold stored plans that were applied (a history line with `plan`, a lease file) and an `apply` interrupted inside its commit; without `apply` none of them exists.
- E7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7`, undo of repairs): repair-undo runs and lines, the reactivation (the undo of a set-aside) with its provisional journal and activation, and the test fixers `fm-test-chmod` and `fm-test-suspend`. Through E7 this bead also builds on E5 (the repair transaction and its crash positions), E6 (`doctor fix` and its test fixers), E14 (the provisional name and recovery's passes), E12 (target-less lines), E3 (run directories) and D4 (the plan store), none of them a direct edge.
Subtasks 1 to 4 are also blocked by T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs), because they write integration tests with its `TestLog`; those edges are added at filing, on the subtasks, not on this leaf.

**Unblocks:**

- H4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`, the README final pass): its checklist (Appendix D, items 12 and 14) verifies the Known limitations entry and the checkpoint command this bead writes, and matches the test counts.
- T4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4`, slice 3 end to end): its demo pre-checks criterion 16 by quoting this suite's last run (the suite is checkpoint-only).

**Slice:** `slice-3`, "Diagnose and repair". Its exit demo (recorded by T4) pre-checks criteria 8 (doctor), 9, 10, 11, 12, 13 and 16.

**Schedule:** earliest start 12, earliest finish 14 (in units of the plan's critical-path arithmetic), slack 6; the computed six-lane schedule places it in lane 5 at t = 18–20. It may land after H1 (M4-D55).

**Related, not edges:** H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`) runs the suite at the checkpoint. F2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.2`) provides the real set-aside when on `main`. B3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3`) provides the `skill` line when on `main`. E8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.8`, `doctor gc`) deletes what this suite proves the M3 build leaves alone. `tests/compat_m2.rs` is this suite's model and stays as it is.
