title: E2E: the M3 build against set-asides and reactivations interrupted at every primitive
description:
Part 4 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9 (The M3 build against M4 state). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

E9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9`) characterizes the last M3 build, commit `c0ab5e9`, against state M4 writes (checkpoint criterion 16, M4-D58): the M3 build must never delete or overwrite anything M4 still needs, and everything else it does is recorded for README. Subtask 1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9.1`) built the harness in `tests/common/compat.rs` and the probes in `tests/compat_m3.rs`.

This part covers **set-asides and reactivations**: a stuck folder journal set aside into quarantine, interrupted at each primitive, and the undo of a committed set-aside (a reactivation, with its provisional `<tx>.reactivating.jsonl`) interrupted at each primitive, for a stuck folder journal, a recoverable one and a stuck `WTF` journal. Criterion 16 names "suspended journal sets and provisional `<tx>.reactivating.jsonl` journals"; the plan's entry adds that "an M3 build that recovers a journal an M4 undo has just activated, before that undo's `done`, is a characterized limitation, not data loss." It is its own step because it is where the leaf's one predicted loss (Touch B) lives, and its rows may send work back to the reactivation's owners.

**Restated from M4-D38 and its leaves:**

- **The set-aside** (F2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.2`, when on `main`; otherwise E7's test fixer `fm-test-suspend`): one `RenameNoReplace` per artifact of the stuck journal's set, into quarantine: `<state>` artifacts (the journal file `<tx>.jsonl` or `<tx>.wtf.jsonl`, its in-flight lock `<state>/inflight/<tx>.lock`, its state snapshot half `<state>/snapshots/<tx>[.wtf]/`) into `<run>/quarantine/state/…`, client artifacts (`<meta>/stage/<tx>[.wtf]/`, `<meta>/snapshots/<tx>[.wtf]/`) into `<meta>/snapshots/<repair tx>.repair/quarantine/…`. F2 orders the set "client stages, client snapshot halves, state snapshot halves, the in-flight lock, then the journal file(s) last", so the journal stays visible to every listing until the final primitive. The primitives carry the suspension manifest as `guards` (each artifact's identity and stamp, the target's key, the marker's digest, the target's record generation, the epochs of what the journal would touch).
- **The reactivation** (E7, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7`; E14, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14`): `doctor undo <set-aside run>` checks every guard under the lock (any change is `undo_conflict` with `changed_since_suspension`), then runs, in order: every other inverse (each non-journal artifact back to its own name), the journal file's restore to `<state>/journal/<tx>.reactivating.jsonl`, and last the activation (`rename_noreplace` from the provisional name to `<tx>.jsonl` or `<tx>.wtf.jsonl`, `activation: true`). The M4 build's recovery resolves a repair that owns a barrier before folder journals, so its own folder pass never runs a journal behind an unsettled undo.

**What the M3 build is expected to do** (from reading `c0ab5e9`; the rows decide):

- It cannot parse `<tx>.reactivating` (`paths::tx_named`, `src/state/paths.rs:33-35`), so it never lists the provisional journal (`src/engine/journal.rs:629`) and `journal::existing` (`:670-674`) does not see it either.
- **Interrupted set-aside:** until the last primitive the journal is at its own name, so the orphan sweep's `dead` (`src/engine/retention.rs:358-360`) is false for every artifact still in place, and nothing is swept; the M3 build's recovery stops on the stuck journal as it did before.
- **Touch B, an interrupted reactivation from its first restore to its activation:** the restored stage and in-flight lock are at their own names while the journal is not visible, so they are dead orphans to the sweep (`:364-384`), deleted after a commit of that build on that client once they are an hour old. Their mtimes are the original transaction's (a rename keeps them), so on a real home that is at once. The snapshot halves survive: the set-aside's history line names the transaction id in its raw text (`in_history`, `:331-333`), and a client half holding a folder or `WTF.previous` is kept anyway (`:313-323`). A stage may hold the only copy of an addon version or of a `WTF/` tree: a loss.
- **After the activation, before `done`:** the M3 build sees `<tx>.jsonl` and treats it as any journal: it recovers a journal it can read and finish, and stops on a stuck one. The plan calls that "a characterized limitation, not data loss".

## Technical Approach

Beads this section names: E7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7`, the reactivation and `fm-test-suspend`), E14 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14`, the provisional name, the barrier and its planting helpers), F2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.2`, the set-aside fixer), E5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`, the repair oracle), and omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9.5.

### 1. `tests/compat_m3/reactivation.rs` (new) and `mod reactivation;` in `tests/compat_m3.rs`

### 2. The three planted journals (on retail, after `install <local Foo> -t retail` by the M4 build)

- **V1, a stuck folder journal:** `<state>/journal/<tx>.jsonl` whose complete `prepared` line does not decode (`journal_unreadable` to both builds; E14's `tests/common/repairs.rs` has a planting helper for undecodable lines, or write it by hand), naming retail's target; `<state>/inflight/<tx>.lock` (no holder); `<state>/snapshots/<tx>/` (a copy of retail's record); `<meta>/stage/<tx>/StageOnly/` (an addon folder with a `.toc`, found nowhere else in the home); `<meta>/snapshots/<tx>/AddOns/OldCopy/` (another).
- **V2, a recoverable folder journal:** the M4 build's `install <local Foo2> -t retail` crashed mid-swap before `swapped` (as E7's reactivation matrix builds it with `tests/engine_crash.rs`'s helpers, for example `engine.swap.before_rename=abort@2`), leaving a real folder journal, its stage, snapshots and in-flight lock, which the M3 build can read and roll back. Record `Interface/AddOns`'s `tree_hash` before the crashed install (`addons_before`).
- **V3, a stuck `WTF` journal:** `<state>/journal/<tx>.wtf.jsonl` with an undecodable `prepared` line; `<meta>/stage/<tx>.wtf/WTF/` holding a `WTF/` tree with the synthetic `FAKEACCT`, `FakeRealm` and `FakeChar` names and one SavedVariables file found nowhere else; `<state>/snapshots/<tx>.wtf/` and `<meta>/snapshots/<tx>.wtf/`.

### 3. The set-aside rows (V1 and V3)

The set-aside: F2's fixer for `journal-unreadable` (`doctor fix --only <its fm id> --force --yes`) when F2 is on `main`; else `doctor fix --only fm-test-suspend --force --yes` with its request `<tx> <retail key>` (V1) or `<tx> <retail key> WTF` (V3), `OMADDONS_TEST_FIXERS=1`. Read the journal's `prepared` line: the journal file's rename must be the last primitive. If `fm-test-suspend` orders it otherwise, change that test fixer to order its set as F2 does (client stages, client snapshot halves, state snapshot halves, the in-flight lock, the journal last), in its own commit with its unit test (`fm_test_suspend_moves_the_journal_last`): it is debug-only test code, and these rows must characterize the order the real set-aside uses. Decided while writing this bead: V2 has no set-aside rows, because no real set-aside moves a recoverable journal (F2's rows are the six stuck states); V2 appears only where the plan's limitation needs a journal the M3 build can recover.

Positions: `doctor.repair.prepared`; before and after each primitive (`doctor.repair.step=abort@k`, `fsx.mutate.logged=abort@k`); `doctor.repair.done`, `doctor.repair.history`, `doctor.repair.committed`. Every probe of `PROBES` per position.

Expected class: `untouched`. M4 next: `status` (a `journal_pending` warning naming the set-aside's repair, beside whatever it reports for the stuck folder journal while that is still at its own name), `config set check_interval_hours 6` (recovery: before `done`, the set-aside rolls back and every artifact is at its own name again; from `done`, it completes and the set is in quarantine), E5's oracle over the set's artifacts, and the bytes check (`StageOnly`, `OldCopy`, V3's `WTF/` tree).

### 4. The reactivation rows (V1, V2 and V3)

Commit the set-aside first (V1 and V3 as in section 3; V2 with `fm-test-suspend --force --yes` and request `<tx> <retail key> Foo2`). Then `doctor undo <the set-aside's run>` crashed at:

- `doctor.repair.prepared`;
- before and after each non-journal restore (`doctor.repair.step=abort@k`, `fsx.mutate.logged=abort@k`, for `k` in `1..=n-2`);
- before and after the provisional restore (`k = n-1`);
- immediately before the activation (`doctor.repair.step=abort@n`);
- after the activation, before `done` (`fsx.mutate.logged=abort@n`, `doctor.repair.done`);
- after `done` (`doctor.repair.history`, `doctor.repair.committed`).

Every probe per position. Expected classes:

| Position | At once | Two hours on, under an M3 command that commits on retail (the install; an undo only if it commits, since one refused by rule 5 runs no sweep) | `config set`, either age |
|---|---|---|---|
| `prepared`, before the first restore | `untouched` | `untouched` | `untouched` |
| from the first restore to just before the activation | `untouched` (nothing is old yet) | **Touch B predicts `fail`**: the restored stage (`StageOnly`, Foo2's staged folders, V3's `WTF/`) and in-flight lock swept | `untouched` (no sweep) |
| after the activation, before `done` | V1, V3 `untouched` (the M3 build stops on the stuck journal); V2 `recovered_by_m3` | same | V2 `recovered_by_m3` (`config set` recovers too) |
| after `done` | V1, V3 `untouched`; V2 `recovered_by_m3` | same | same |

For a `recovered_by_m3` row: one `journal_recovered` warning of the M3 build names V2's transaction; `Interface/AddOns` hashes as `addons_before` plus the probe folder when the probe installed it (the rollback of an install crashed before `swapped`); nothing in a quarantine root is lost; the inventory holds for everything but V2's own artifacts. M4 next records what the M4 build does with the undo's journal afterwards (rolled back, rolled forward, or stopped as `fm-concurrency_primitives-journal-step-unrecognized`, reported by `doctor --json`); none of these is a failure, because the M3 build already finished the folder transaction it exposed. That is the plan's characterized limitation, and `the_m3_build_meets_a_journal_an_m4_undo_has_just_activated` asserts it on its own for README.

For every other row, M4 next: `status`, `config set check_interval_hours 6`, E7's oracle for the undo (the suspended state before its durable `done`, the reactivated state from `done` on), and the bytes check.

### 5. If Touch B shows

Each `fail` row names the swept paths and the lost folder or `WTF/` digests. No rename can remove this touch: the stage must be at its own name for the folder journal that needs it, and the M3 build's sweep spares it only while that journal is visible at `<tx>.jsonl` or `<tx>.wtf.jsonl`. So, as the leaf's section 9 says, file one P1 bug `discovered-from` this subtask, titled "A crashed reactivation's restored stage is an orphan to the M3 build's sweep", holding: the rows; the code path (`src/engine/retention.rs:358-384` with `src/engine/journal.rs:670-674`); the analysis (a suspended set is safe from the M3 build in only two states, every artifact hidden or every artifact at its own name; between them, either the journal is hidden while the stage is back, which is the sweep's window and a loss, or the journal is back while an artifact is hidden, which lets that build recover an incomplete set); and the two candidate orders to compare against E14's barrier (restore the stage and lock under names the M3 build cannot parse and activate them just before the journal, which shrinks the window to single boundaries; or activate the journal before restoring the stage, which turns the window into the plan's accepted limitation and changes M4-D38's "the activation is the last primitive"). Make the bug a blocker of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9.5. Close this subtask with its table showing those rows as `fail (<bug id>)`; the test keeps failing until the bug lands and its rows turn green. Decided while writing this bead: the rows stay failing rather than being reclassified, because criterion 16 says the M3 build "must never delete … anything M4 wrote that M4 would still need", and the undo's own rollback needs that stage.

### 6. Tables

One test function per variant and family, plus the limitation test; each prints its table (title "set-aside of V1 under the M3 build", "reactivation of V3 under the M3 build", …), logs `observations`, writes `table.md`, and fails on any `fail` row after printing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] V1, V2 and V3 are planted as specified, each asserted present (journal, in-flight lock, stage holding a folder or `WTF/` tree found nowhere else, snapshot halves) before the set-aside.
- [ ] Set-asides of V1 and V3, by F2's fixer when on `main` or by `fm-test-suspend` ordered journal-last, are interrupted at every position and end `untouched` under every probe; the M4 build then settles each per E5's oracle.
- [ ] Reactivations of V1, V2 and V3 are interrupted at every position under every probe, with the classes of the table in section 4; every `recovered_by_m3` row has the folder transaction whole and nothing lost from a quarantine root.
- [ ] `the_m3_build_meets_a_journal_an_m4_undo_has_just_activated` passes and records, for each variant, what the M3 build did and what the M4 build did with the undo afterwards.
- [ ] Every Touch B row that fails is covered by one P1 bug `discovered-from` this subtask, blocking omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9.5, with the rows, the code path and the analysis; or every such row is green.
- [ ] No row prints a path below `WTF/` (paths cut at the `WTF` component); every M4 run passes `assert_private_all` with `--progress json`.
- [ ] Each test prints its table and logs `observations`; the close comment quotes every non-`untouched` row and the wall time.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files.
- [ ] If this is the last open subtask: every acceptance criterion of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9 is verified and the leaf is closed with the evidence.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

- `fm_test_suspend_moves_the_journal_last` (in the test fixer's module, only if this part reorders it): a planted set with every artifact kind; the planned `Fix::Suspend`'s artifacts end with the journal file, the rest ordered client stages, client snapshots, state snapshots, in-flight lock, each group by path.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

`tests/compat_m3/reactivation.rs`, every test `#[ignore = "builds the M3 commit: cargo test --test compat_m3 -- --ignored --nocapture"]`, each with `tlog!()`:

- `an_interrupted_set_aside_of_a_stuck_folder_journal_under_the_m3_build` (V1) and `…_of_a_stuck_wtf_journal_…` (V3).
- `an_interrupted_reactivation_of_a_stuck_folder_journal_under_the_m3_build` (V1), `…_of_a_recoverable_folder_journal_…` (V2), `…_of_a_stuck_wtf_journal_…` (V3).
- `the_m3_build_meets_a_journal_an_m4_undo_has_just_activated`: the three variants at `fsx.mutate.logged=abort@n` and at `doctor.repair.done`, with the readers then install at once and `config set` at once: V1 and V3, the M3 build's install fails or warns on the stuck journal (recorded), nothing deleted; V2, `recovered_by_m3` with `Interface/AddOns` as `addons_before` plus the probe; then M4's `doctor --json` and `config set`, recorded.

Each row (`log.case("<variant> · <set-aside|reactivation> · <position> · <probe> · <age>")`): steps `plant`, `set-aside` (and `reactivation` with its crash, `aborted()`, `log.note` of the undo journal's last complete line and of `<state>/journal/`, `<state>/inflight/`, retail's `<meta>/stage/` and `<meta>/snapshots/` listings), `age` (aged and spared paths), `inventory before`, `m3 <command>`, `inventory after` (`log.diff` of the trees), `bytes`, `m4 status`, `m4 config set`, `oracle`, `row`.

### Logging

As above. A Touch B failure's message lists the swept paths (relative, cut at `WTF`), the lost digests with their former paths, the M3 run's warnings, and the transcript path; the transcript shows the restored stage present before the M3 command and absent after.

## Considerations

- **Risk 9** (the M3 build destroys M4 artifacts; low likelihood, high impact; owner E9) lives here. A real loss needs a crash inside a reactivation, then an older build committing on that client; low, but the bytes may be the only copy, and the leaf does not ship it as "characterized".
- **E14's bead already flagged this window** for this leaf to characterize ("the M3 build's orphan sweep does not know the provisional name, so restored artifacts of a crashed reactivation could look dead to it after an hour"); this part measures it.
- **Interrupted set-asides are expected to pass** because F2 moves the journal last; the rows are what proves that order matters.
- **Privacy:** V3's `WTF/` uses the synthetic names; tables and README never print below `WTF/`.
- **Hot spots:** the new file and one `mod` line; `src/doctor/fixers/` only if `fm-test-suspend` must be reordered (debug-only test code).
- **Decided while writing this bead** (confirm or adjust in the close comment): V2 only for reactivations; journal-last for `fm-test-suspend`; the class table; the Touch B bug and its contents; failing rows kept failing until the bug lands.

## Dependencies

- Parent: E9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9`, The M3 build against M4 state).
- Before it: subtask 1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9.1`), for the harness. T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`) blocks it (added at filing).
- Beside it: subtasks 2 and 3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9.2`, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9.3`), in other files.
- After it: subtask 5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9.5`) writes README from this table and waits for any Touch B bug.

description:
Part 5 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9 (The M3 build against M4 state). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

E9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9`) characterizes the last M3 build, commit `c0ab5e9`, against state M4 writes (checkpoint criterion 16, M4-D58). Subtasks 1 to 4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9.1` to `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9.4`) built `tests/compat_m3.rs`: the build with its recorded toolchain and provenance, and the committed, interrupted, set-aside and reactivation families, each printing a table of what the M3 build did. G-M4-6 asks that "a build from before M4 never destroys what M4 wrote: the M3 build is characterized against M4 state, and README states the result", and criterion 16 ends "README's Limitations quote the result."

This part runs the whole suite from one commit, makes sure every row is green (or waits for the bugs that make them so), writes README's limitation for pre-M4 builds from the tables, adds the suite to README's Development section, and records the run for T4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4`, the slice-3 demo, which quotes it) and H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the checkpoint, which runs it again). It is its own step because README may only say what every family showed, and because any bug a family filed (a Touch B loss, an owning leaf's defect) must land first.

**What README already says about the M2 build** (`README.md:2550-2555`, under "Known limitations"), the model for this entry: "Do not run a pre-M3 omaddons build to change state that M3 has written. Reading with it (`status`, `list`, `history`) is safe, also while an M3 restore waits to be recovered. This is what the last M2 build (`af10e34`) does, as `tests/compat_m2.rs` observes it:" followed by bullets of observed behaviour, each tied to what the test ran, and the closing line "From M3 on, every build refuses what it cannot read". The Development section lists `tests/compat_m2.rs` in its suite table (`:2628`) and its command in the checkpoint block (`:2642-2652`: `cargo test --test compat_m2 -- --ignored --nocapture       # the M2 build against M3 state (prints its table)`).

## Technical Approach

Beads this section names: E9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9`, the parent), H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, the pre-freeze audit), H4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`, the README final pass), T4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4`, slice 3 end to end), and the sibling parts omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9.2 to omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9.4.

### 1. Blocking bugs first

Every bug filed `discovered-from` subtasks 2 to 4 that blocks this subtask (a Touch B loss, an owning leaf's defect, a rename that could not be made there) must be closed before this subtask starts; `br ready` will not offer it until then. A touch that a rename removes was fixed in the subtask that found it (the leaf's section 9); check the close comments of subtasks 2 to 4 for each rename and its compatibility note.

### 2. The run

From the commit that will close the leaf, on the development machine (on disk, not tmpfs):

```bash
cargo test --test compat_m3 -- --ignored --nocapture
```

(a debug build of the test; no `--release`). Record: the commit hash; the provenance record `target/compat/c0ab5e9.provenance.json` (toolchain, `rustc -vV`, binary digest, whether the binary was reused); the wall time; every table printed; the number of rows per family and class; and T1's log root (`target/tmp/test-logs/compat_m3/`). Every row must be `untouched` or, where its family allows it, `recovered_by_m3`. A `fail` row stops this subtask. Handle it as the leaf's remedy says: if a rename removes the touch, rename the family in the M4 module that builds and parses the name, so the M3 build cannot parse it and M4 parses it explicitly; run that module's unit tests, the owning leaf's suites and this suite again; record the rename in the close comment with a compatibility note (DEC-4, M4-D55), on H1's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`) change list if H1 has closed, with README's file table updated in the same commit. If no rename removes it, file a P1 bug `discovered-from` this subtask with the rows, the code path and what was lost, block this subtask on it, and run again once it lands.

### 3. README: Known limitations

Add one entry directly after the M2 entry, in its style, every sentence backed by a row of the run (quote the scene names in the close comment beside each sentence):

> - Do not run a pre-M4 omaddons build to change state that M4 has written. Reading with it (`status`, `list`, `history`) is safe. This is what the last M3 build (`c0ab5e9`) does, as `tests/compat_m3.rs` observes it:
>   - It skips every M4 history line it cannot read (repairs, undos of repairs, skill installs) with `history_lines_skipped`, and its `undo` of a change older than a repair, or a bare `undo` that would reach one, is refused (`undo_conflict`, `history_unreadable`). [Fill in exactly what the committed rows showed, including `undo <repair tx>`.]
>   - It never lists or deletes a repair's journal, its `<meta>/snapshots/<tx>.repair/` half, a doctor run directory, `latest`, a quarantine in `<cache>/quarantine/`, a stored plan or its lease, at once or two hours on. [N scenes, M rows.]
>   - It does not see an interrupted repair: `status` does not report it, and its own changes do not respect what a stuck repair protects. The next M4 command that changes something recovers the repair, or reports it stuck when the older build changed what it protected. [The flatten-collision row; Touch A, if it showed: the older build may delete an interrupted repair's in-flight lock file, which the M4 build does not need.]
>   - [The set-aside and reactivation rows: what the older build does with a journal an M4 `doctor undo` had just reactivated, and that nothing was lost; and, if Touch B's bug changed the reactivation, what the rows show now.]
>   - It may evict a stored plan's download from the cache; `apply` downloads it again. It rewrites the history projection (`history_tail.json`) without M4's fields; the next M4 command rebuilds it. [Only what the rows showed.]

Write only what the rows showed; remove a bracketed bullet that no row supports, and add one for any other behaviour the tables show. Never print a path below `WTF/`, a host name or an absolute path.

### 4. README: Development

- The suite table, after the `tests/compat_m2.rs` row: "| `tests/compat_m3.rs` | The last M3 build (`c0ab5e9`, built once into `target/compat/` with the toolchain it records, `1.97.1`) against state M4 wrote: committed repairs of every kind and their undos, run directories, quarantines, stored plans and leases, M4's history lines; every repair and undo interrupted before and after each primitive; set-asides and reactivations interrupted at each primitive; each at once and two hours on, under its `status`, `list`, `history`, `install`, `undo` and `config set`. Checkpoint only, with a debug build of the current binary; never skipped: a build failure is a failed checkpoint |".
- The checkpoint block, after the `compat_m2` line: `cargo test --test compat_m3 -- --ignored --nocapture       # the M3 build against M4 state (prints its tables)`.
- The sentence listing the `#[ignore]`d kinds ("the M2 build against M3 state (`tests/compat_m2.rs`)") gains "and the M3 build against M4 state (`tests/compat_m3.rs`)". The test counts are H4's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`), not this subtask's.

Decided while writing this bead: this leaf writes these entries, because README is the product contract and each leaf updates its own section in the commit that ships what it describes (common rule 11); H4 verifies them against Appendix D's items 12 and 14 and reconciles the counts. The plan's acceptance says H4 quotes the table; it quotes this entry.

### 5. The close comment (this subtask closes the leaf)

As the last subtask, after verifying every acceptance criterion of E9, close the leaf with: the commit; the provenance record; the run command and its wall time; every table (or, if they are long, each family's row counts by class and every row that is not `untouched`, with the full tables in a comment on the leaf); the README lines added; every rename made (with its compatibility note, and whether it went on H1's change list); every bug filed and closed; "no new wire names" (or the renamed file names); and the slice-3 note for T4 ("criterion 16: compat_m3 run at <commit>, <rows> rows, all green").

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every bug that blocked this subtask is closed, and every rename made by subtasks 2 to 4 is listed with its compatibility note.
- [ ] `cargo test --test compat_m3 -- --ignored --nocapture` passes from the closing commit on the development machine, every row `untouched` or an allowed `recovered_by_m3`; its tables, provenance record and wall time are recorded.
- [ ] README's Known limitations has the pre-M4 entry after the M2 one, every sentence backed by a named row, no path below `WTF/`, no absolute path.
- [ ] README's Development section has the `tests/compat_m3.rs` suite row, the checkpoint command, and the ignored-tests sentence updated.
- [ ] The leaf's close comment holds what section 5 lists, including the note T4 quotes.
- [ ] `rumdl check README.md` reports no new finding (the project's Markdown lint), and the commit passes `argc gate` if it also changes code.
- [ ] If this is the last open subtask: every acceptance criterion of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9 is verified and the leaf is closed with the evidence.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

None (no code, unless a rename lands here, which then carries its own unit tests in its owning module).

### Integration and end-to-end tests

The whole suite, as section 2. If a rename lands in this subtask, also the owning leaf's suites (`cargo test --test engine_crash`, `cargo test --test doctor_repair`, and the others its close comment names), green.

### Logging

The suite's own (T1's logs under `target/tmp/test-logs/compat_m3/`, one transcript per row); the close comment quotes the log root, repo-relative.

### Checkpoint-only

This is the leaf's checkpoint run. No `SKIP` is ever accepted: a build failure with no provenance-verified binary is an unmet criterion 16, and a bug is filed `discovered-from` this subtask.

## Considerations

- **README is a hot spot** (everyone edits their own sections; H4 reconciles): edit only the Known limitations entry, the suite table row, the checkpoint line and the one sentence.
- **Never generalize past the rows.** If a family ran with `fm-test-suspend` instead of F2's fixer, or with a planted `skill` line instead of B3's, say what was tested ("a set-aside", not "every set-aside fixer").
- **A long close comment:** the tables can run to hundreds of rows; summarize by class in the close reason and post the full tables as a comment on the leaf.
- **Decided while writing this bead** (confirm or adjust in the close comment): this leaf writes its README entries; the entry's bullets and their order; full tables as a comment when the close reason would be too long.

## Dependencies

- Parent: E9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9`, The M3 build against M4 state).
- Before it: subtasks 2, 3 and 4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9.2`, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9.3`, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9.4`), for every table, and any bug they filed against this subtask.

title: Epic: M4 the doctor's catalog
description:
## Background

Area F is the doctor's catalog of M4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`, the milestone epic: the agent surface, the doctor and the first tag). Area E (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5`, the doctor core) builds a doctor that can load a damaged world, run detectors, plan, bind and commit repairs, undo them and collect what they keep. Without this area that doctor knows almost nothing that can go wrong. Area F fills it in three steps:

1. **The catalog.** Every failure mode of the catalog (the plan's Appendix B, restated below) becomes code: a registry row, a detector, a Rust fixture and, where a safe automatic repair exists, a fixer.
2. **`status` on the same registry.** `status` stops computing issues on its own and reads the doctor's cheap tiers, so the two can never disagree.
3. **The safety harness.** Every real fixer is driven through undo, crashes at every primitive boundary and concurrency, in every gate.

Ten leaves, all in slice 3 ("Diagnose and repair"):

- F1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1`, journal and lock detectors, and `status`'s journal titles): the ten `concurrency_primitives` rows (every state a journal can be left in, and a lock held too long), and correct titles in `status`;
- F2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.2`, journal fixers: the delegation and the set-aside as suspension): the repairs of those rows;
- F3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.3`, state files and schemas): the `schemas` and `state_files` rows, with the orphan-temp quarantine;
- F4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.4`, configs, userland state and permissions, detection only): nine report-only rows;
- F5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.5`, external artifacts): the managed and unmanaged addon folder rows, with the disabled flatten fixer;
- F6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.6`, caches: verified blob reads and the blob detector): blob verification on every use, plus a deep detector and its quarantine;
- F7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.7`, plugins, secrets and the network): the widget, credential-mode and online rows, with the chmod fixer;
- F8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.8`, `status` on the registry): `status` takes its issues from the registry by tier;
- F9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`, the safety harness): the fourteen properties over every fixture;
- F10 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.10`, skill drift): the installed agent skill's drift row and its rewrite fixer.

The leaves weigh 21 units (one size-S, seven size-M, two size-L) and hold 48 subtasks. The area adds no command, no error code and no config key. It adds:

- 34 failure-mode rows to the registry, and it completes the other 9 rows it owns. E1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`, the failure-mode registry and finding model) and E2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.2`, the tolerant view) register those 9 first: E1 the 7 ids published in M3, E2 the two rows its tolerant layers report (`config-parse-error` and `state-corrupt`). This area adds their detectors, fixtures and README rows;
- the warning `delegated_recovery`, and the delegation's `delegated[]` and the suspension's evidence on `doctor fix`'s report;
- `details.blob` on `hash_mismatch`;
- `auto_fixable` and `explain` on `status` issues;
- the `net.log` purpose `doctor-probe`;
- the constant `LOCK_HELD_LONG` (10 min), and `DOCTOR_STATE_FILE_MAX_BYTES` (64 MiB), which F3's bead decided;
- four values of the limit a `check-incomplete` finding names: `bytes`, `unanswered`, `skill_dirs` and `history_projection`, added by the leaf beads;
- typed evidence keys per row.

### Why it matters to the milestone

This area delivers most of milestone goal **G-M4-4, diagnosable and repairable**:

- "`omaddons doctor` names every broken state omaddons can detect in what it owns or manages. Each finding carries concrete evidence and an exact remediation. A check that ran out of budget or entries says so: incomplete coverage is never reported as healthy."
- "Every auto-fixable state is repaired by one consented command that backs up verbatim, never deletes, and is proven by a fixture that round-trips. A repair can be undone byte for byte as long as no later change overlaps what it touched; once one does, undo refuses before moving anything, and the kept bytes stay inspectable."
- "The states README calls 'manual repair' today each get a name, an explanation and a guarded repair."
- "`status` and `doctor` never disagree about what is wrong."

It also holds the area's share of **G-M4-6, no new risk to the engine's guarantees**: every repair is a journaled transaction that recovers like any other, and the doctor never writes `WTF/`.

It carries promises of the vision bead `omad-vision-8qa`:

- its goal G7, "`doctor` follows the world-class doctor contract": evidence, exact remediations, consented and undoable repairs, no silent passes;
- its §5.8 catalog, which this area builds as amended by M4-D48 (below);
- its "five-property safety harness in the local gate", which F9 builds as fourteen properties.

The deepest reason is README's dead end. Today a journal that recovery cannot settle blocks every change on that client, and README can only say "`doctor`, which will automate this repair, is planned for milestone 4" (`README.md:2523`). F1 and F2 turn that dead end into a named finding and a guarded, undoable repair. omaddons then stays the sole, safe, undoable authority over what it manages, even after a crash or a newer build left it stuck.

### What is true today (verified at `c0ab5e9`)

- **There is no doctor.** Neither `src/doctor/` nor `tests/doctor/` exists. Area E creates both. Every file of this area lands on top of E1–E3, E5–E7, E11 and E14.
- **`status`'s issues are computed in `src/app/issues.rs`.** The seven ids published in M3 are constants at `src/app/issues.rs:20-32`:
  - `fm-concurrency_primitives-journal-pending` (P0);
  - `fm-schemas-state-version-newer` (P0);
  - `fm-state_files-record-folder-missing` (P1);
  - `fm-external_artifacts-managed-files-modified` (P2);
  - `fm-external_artifacts-ownership-transferred` (P2);
  - `fm-userland_state-target-vanished` (P2);
  - `fm-plugins-widget-version-drift` (P3).

  README calls them "stable across releases" (`README.md:750`). The issue shape is `{id, severity, title, addon, remediation{command, argv, destructive}}`.
- **Stuck journals are mislabelled.** Recovery stops for manual repair in these states:

  | State | Where recovery stops | Error on the client's own commands |
  |---|---|---|
  | `journal_too_new` | `Parsed::unrecoverable` | `state_too_new` with `details.reason` |
  | `journal_unreadable` | same | `state_corrupt` with `details.reason` |
  | marker mismatch (`target.json` names another key) | folder recovery | `scope_denied`, no `details.reason` |
  | a step in neither state (non-WTF rollback) | `ran()` | `internal`, no `details.reason` |
  | `unexpected_state` (WTF rollback) | `roll_back_wtf` | `internal` with `details.reason` |
  | `preservation_incomplete` | `roll_back_preserving` | `state_corrupt` with `details.reason` |
  | a journal with no readable target | `recover_all` | every committing command on every target fails |

  `status` passes a reason to `issues_for` only from `journal::Unrecoverable` (`src/app/status.rs:884-892`). That enum has only `TooNew` and `Unreadable` (`src/engine/journal.rs:489-494`), so of the four reasons `MANUAL_REPAIR` lists (`src/app/issues.rs:37-42`) only two can ever arrive. Every other stuck state is titled "An interrupted change waits to be finished", with the advice "run any change command" (`src/app/issues.rs:129-148`), which keeps failing.
- **Detection exists, the finding does not.** Existing code already computes these facts, and nothing turns them into findings:
  - the lock holder (`fsx::lock::probe_global`, `src/fsx/lock.rs:161-191`);
  - newer state (`store::refuse_newer`) and torn or skipped history lines;
  - drift (`drift::check`);
  - ownership conflicts and case duplicates (`inventory`);
  - wrong-flavor and out-of-date TOC verdicts for folders on disk;
  - dependency satisfaction (plan time only);
  - widget drift and plugin validation (`omarchy::status`, `omarchy::validate`);
  - shared AddOns (`discover::shared::shared_addons`) and copied markers (`registry::reconcile`).

  README promises that "M4's doctor will report" records doubled across a shared AddOns directory (`README.md:2565`).
- **Nothing detects these at all:**
  - fsx's own temp files `.omaddons-*`, whose definition says "A crash can orphan one; the doctor (M4) collects them" (`src/fsx/sys.rs:20-22`), and which nothing sweeps;
  - missing dependencies of installed addons at rest;
  - a record file missing behind a registered target;
  - a missing extra root;
  - non-writable AddOns, state or cache directories;
  - nested addon folders on disk;
  - skill drift (no skill install exists before B3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3`, `robot-docs install-skill`).
- **Cached blobs are trusted by name.** `BlobCache::get` returns a cached archive without hashing it (`src/engine/blobs.rs:307-326`). F6's bead found that a reinstall's first step, `local_blob_candidate` (`src/engine/plan.rs:5341-5376`), already re-hashes. The unchecked uses are `fetch_blob`'s cache hits (`src/engine/plan.rs:4839-4852`) and the per-command download memo, which every install, update and copy uses.
- **Credential file modes** are checked only as a `credential_file_mode` warning, raised when a command resolves that credential (`src/state/config.rs:980-991`).
- **History is never rewritten.** This is a README promise (the `history_lines_skipped` row at `README.md:1917`, "omaddons never rewrites the file") and a code comment (`src/state/history.rs:435`).

### The decisions that shape the area

The full decision log is in the decision-log comments on the milestone epic. These are the decisions that shape this area, restated.

- **M4-D29: one detector registry serves `doctor`, `doctor health` and `status`, by tier.**
  - `src/doctor/registry.rs` declares every failure mode once: an id, a subsystem, a fixed severity, a title, a description, a "why it matters", a tier (`cached`, `quick`, `default` or `deep`), `online`, a declared `cost_ms`, the layers it `requires`, a pure detector, an optional fixer and a manual remediation builder.
  - What runs where:

    | Caller | Tiers it runs |
    |---|---|
    | `status --cached` | `cached` |
    | `status` | `cached` and `quick` |
    | `doctor --quick`, `doctor health` | `cached` and `quick` |
    | `doctor` | every tier but `deep` |
    | `doctor --include-deep` | every tier |

  - **The tier contracts.**
    - A `cached` detector may read exactly what `status --cached` reads today (records, the cached discovery, journals, the lock probe, the projections, the widget's files), plus single-file `stat`s and at most `SKILL_DIRS_MAX` skill files. It never walks a directory, reads history beyond its projection or renders the guide.
    - A `quick` detector adds bounded listings and stat-mode drift, each under 5 ms (`QUICK_DETECTOR_BUDGET`).
    - A `default` detector adds full inventories, the full history read and decoding every state file, under `DOCTOR_DETECTOR_DEADLINE`.
    - A `deep` detector adds content hashing.
  - Why: two implementations of "is this broken?" would drift. Tiers are how `status --cached` keeps its 5 ms budget.
  - Rejected: `status` calling `doctor` as a subprocess (costly, and recursive for the widget), and keeping `status`'s code separate with ids synced by a test.
- **M4-D30: failure-mode ids keep the vision's subsystem spelling, and instance keys are resource-specific.**
  - Ids are `fm-<subsystem>-<slug>`, with the subsystem in snake_case, as M3 published them.
  - A finding's `instance` is `<fm-id>@<target key | machine>[:<discriminator>]`, for example `tx=<ULID>`, `path=<absolute path>`, `folder=<key>` or `blob=<sha256>`. Two stuck journals on one client are therefore two instances.
  - `label` is the human form. It may change when a target is renamed, and nothing compares it.
  - Rejected: renaming the published ids to hyphens, which would break README's "stable across releases".
- **M4-D41 and M4-D42: evidence is typed and never holds file content.**
  - Evidence is a typed object per failure mode: paths, digests, modes, counts, line numbers, pids and ages, never file content (credentials, config lines and TOCs alike).
  - No path below `WTF/` ever appears.
  - `confidence` is `high` (observed directly), `medium` (inferred from consistent evidence) or `low` (a heuristic).
  - Rejected: free-form evidence strings, which cannot be parsed and which leak.
- **M4-D43: the doctor loads the world tolerantly and says what it skipped.**
  - A layer that fails to load becomes a finding and an unavailable layer. Detectors that require it are listed in `skipped`, never reported clean.
  - Every walk and listing goes through the bounded walker of E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, the diagnose runtime) and charges a `Budget` (a deadline and `DOCTOR_SCAN_MAX_ENTRIES`, 20,000).
  - A detector cut short returns what it found plus an `incomplete` record. The runtime reports that as `fm-state_files-check-incomplete`, so such a run is never healthy.
  - Rejected: running detectors on defaults in place of a broken config, and treating truncation as a warning on a healthy run.
- **M4-D47: fixtures are Rust, in `tests/doctor/`, and coverage is bidirectional.**
  - Each failure mode has a `Fixture` in `tests/doctor/fixtures/<fm_id>.rs`. It has a deterministic `corrupt(&TestEnv)` built on `tests/common/`, an `assert_healthy(&TestEnv)`, a `subject(&TestEnv)` naming the trees a round trip compares, and a doc comment that is its README (what breaks, why, the evidence).
  - A coverage test asserts that `set(fixers in the registry) == set(fixtures that declare a fixer)`, and that every detector has a fixture.
  - Rejected: `corrupt.sh` and `assert.sh` per failure mode. That would be a second test language, and shell scripts that must clean up after themselves (the house rules ban `rm -rf` even in tests).
- **M4-D48: the catalog is pruned to what can actually go wrong.**
  - **Dropped** from vision §5.8's list, each for a reason given in Non-Goals below: `status-stale`, `validator-orphan`, `client-version-changed`, `lock-orphaned`, `duplicate-addon`, `orphan-inflight`, `orphan-snapshot-dir` and the `state-version-older` fixer.
  - **Report-only:** every finding whose fix is an omaddons command the user should choose (`install --reinstall`, `targets rm`, `config set`, `omarchy install`), and every finding with no safe automatic fix (a config parse error, ownership conflicts, case collisions, wrong-flavor folders, missing dependencies).
  - **Added:** the six stuck-journal states, `orphan-temp-file`, `target-addons-shared`, `shared-record-doubled`, `plan-store-crowded` and the network checks. Area E adds `doctor-runs-accumulated`, `detector-crashed` and `check-incomplete`.
  - **Narrowed:** the published `journal-pending`. From F1 on it means only "a journal recovery can settle". The six stuck states get their own ids, and a restore waiting for the game is `journal-waits-for-game` (P2). The id keeps its spelling and its most common meaning. It is a narrowing of a published id before the freeze, recorded on the change list of H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, the pre-freeze audit) (M4-D55). The widget matches no issue id by name.
  - Rejected: shipping the vision's list verbatim, with dead detectors and fixers that pre-empt the user's choices.
- **M4-D37: recoverable journals are fixed by the engine's own recovery, as a declared delegation** (F2).
  - The fixer of `journal-pending` (and of a resumable `journal-preservation-incomplete`) runs the engine's recovery under the doctor's held lock, with discovery, so SavedVariables follow M2's rules.
  - Planning predicts each recovery with `journal::diagnose` (E11, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.11`, the read-only simulation of recovery). The preview lists `{tx, family, phase, direction, protected resources}`, and the token covers them.
  - Under the lock the doctor re-plans and compares the token before the first recovery, then runs only the disclosed recoveries. A pending journal that appeared since the preview stales a bound run.
  - The report lists `delegated: [{fm, tx, outcome: rolled_back|rolled_forward|waiting|failed}]`, with a `delegated_recovery` warning.
  - `doctor undo` does not revert a delegation. A roll-forward is undone with `omaddons undo <tx>`, and a rollback needs no undo.
  - Rejected: a second recovery implementation inside the repair transaction, and leaving `journal-pending` out of the doctor.
- **M4-D38: the stuck journal states get a guarded "set aside" repair** (F2, on the barrier of E14, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14`, fences and activation barriers, and the guards of E7, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7`, undo of repairs).
  - The six states are `journal-too-new`, `journal-unreadable`, `journal-unexpected-state`, `journal-step-unrecognized`, `journal-marker-mismatch` and `journal-unattributed`.
  - One shared fixer moves the journal set into quarantine, one `RenameNoReplace` per artifact: the journal file, its in-flight lock, its state snapshot half, and its client stage and snapshot halves.
  - It records a **suspension manifest** as guards: each artifact's identity and stamp, the target's key, the marker's digest, the target's generation, and the epochs of the resources the journal would recover (for a `WTF/` journal, one digest of the tree's stamps, never a path below it).
  - **Undo is a guarded reactivation.** If anything guarded changed (a later install on that client, a new marker, a changed folder), the undo is `undo_conflict` with `details.reason: "changed_since_suspension"` and moves nothing. The bytes stay in quarantine, inspectable.
  - The journal comes back under a provisional name that recovery does not list (`<tx>.reactivating.jsonl`), and an activation barrier makes recovery settle the reactivating repair before it considers ordinary journals.
  - **For unreadable and newer journals, the fixer never follows the payload.** It moves only what it can attribute by the transaction id in known locations, on clients whose markers check out. It reports `attribution: complete | partial` and `unattributed[]`.
  - Preconditions: the in-flight lock is free (the writer is dead), the global lock is held, and the client is not running (unknown counts as running).
  - It is `auto_fixable: false` and `needs_force: true`, run only with `--only <fm> --force --yes`, never by a default `doctor fix`, and never by the widget.
  - Rejected: guessing a direction and finishing the transaction (never act on what you cannot read, M3-D45); deleting the journal; a default fix; and an unconditional restore, which would activate stale instructions over newer work.
- **M4-D39: a fixer that changes user content ships disabled** (F5).
  - The nested-addon-folder flatten has `enabled: false`. It runs only with `--only fm-external_artifacts-nested-addon-folder`, refuses while the client runs, and never overwrites a destination.
  - Rejected: no fixer at all, which would leave the common `Foo-main/Foo/` mistake with a finding and no help.
- **M4-D44 and M4-D45: `doctor fix` binds, and concurrent fixers serialize** (the protocol of E6, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`, `doctor fix`, which every fixer here plugs into).
  - `doctor fix --dry-run` discloses every primitive, every delegated recovery and the bytes to back up, with a token that holds nothing run-specific. `--if-match` runs exactly that or nothing.
  - Under the lock the order is fixed: a fresh view, the detectors and the complete plan re-run (predicted recoveries included), the token compared, and only then the recoveries and the primitives. Verification re-runs the fixed failure modes' detectors after the lock is released.
  - A second fixer waits for the lock (up to 5 s) and re-plans: it takes 0 actions for what the first fixed, or exits 5 `concurrency_lost`.
- **M4-D31, M4-D35 and M4-D46: what a fixer returns, where quarantine goes, and how undo works** (the protocols of E5, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`, the repair transaction, and of E7).
  - A fixer returns presentation-level fixes (`write`, `chmod`, `quarantine`, `flatten`, `suspend`, `delegate`). E5 lowers them into primitives, each one filesystem operation with its write-ahead step and endpoint predicates.
  - A quarantine never crosses a filesystem:

    | Victim under | Quarantine root |
    |---|---|
    | `<state>` or `<config>` | `<run>/quarantine/{state,config}/…` |
    | `<cache>` | `<cache>/quarantine/<run id>/…` |
    | a client | `<meta>/snapshots/<repair tx>.repair/quarantine/…` |

  - Undo is E7's generic inverse of the history line's `repairs[]`, checked strictly by predicates and guards. **No fixer writes undo code.**
- **M4-D49: `history.jsonl` is never rewritten; history findings are reports** (F3).
  - `history-unreadable-lines` reports the count of complete lines the reader cannot decode. The vision's `history-torn-line*` fixer is not built.
  - Why: README's promise, undo's rule 5, and retention's raw-text check all rely on keeping those lines.
- **M4-D50 and M4-D7: drift of the widget is reported; drift of the skill is repaired** (F7, F10).
  - `widget-version-drift` stays manual (`omaddons omarchy install`), because reinstalling the widget runs Omarchy's tools in the desktop session and is never undone.
  - `skill-version-drift` compares the stamp on the line after `SKILL.md`'s frontmatter (`<!-- omaddons guide sha256:<hex> -->`, a digest of the file without that line) with this binary's `OMADDONS_GUIDE_SHA256`, without rendering the guide.
    - A file whose bytes match its own stamp but carry another digest is outdated, and the fixer rewrites it with a verbatim backup.
    - A file whose bytes no longer match its own stamp was edited by hand. It is reported `edited: true` and refused by the fixer (`edited_locally`).
    - A symlinked `SKILL.md` is never written through.
    - A deleted skill directory is not a finding.
- **M4-D51: the doctor checks credentials and sources that exist today** (F7).
  - `fm-secrets-credential-file-mode` covers the stored token and every `{ file = … }` credential readable by group or others. It is fixed by `chmod 0600` inside `<config>` (undo restores the exposure, and `explain` says so), and gets prose advice outside it.
  - The `--online` checks make one allowlisted, logged request each (`net.log` purpose `doctor-probe`): `github-rate-limited` (`GET /rate_limit`), `credential-rejected` (a 401) and `source-unreachable` (one cheap request per enabled source in use).
  - Without `--online` they are `skipped: online_required`. A selection of only them is `online_required` (doctor exit 6).
  - Rejected: waiting for M5, which would grow the `secrets` and `network` subsystems' first shapes after the freeze.
- **M4-D52: cache blobs are verified when used, and corrupt ones are quarantined** (F6).
  - `BlobCache::get` checks the SHA-256 against the name. A mismatch is a cache miss: online, the archive is fetched again and the cache heals in place; offline, the result is `hash_mismatch` (`retryable: true`, `details.blob`, fix `omaddons doctor --include-deep`).
  - `fm-caches-blob-hash-mismatch` (`deep`) hashes every blob and quarantines mismatches, pinned ones too.
  - Rejected: detection only (a bad blob would still install), and deleting on the read path (reads never prune).
- **M4-D53: `status` issues gain two keys** (F8; E10 owns the rest of this decision).
  - `targets[].issues[]` and `data.issues[]` gain `auto_fixable` and `explain {command, argv}`, both additive.
  - An auto-fixable finding's remediation becomes `omaddons doctor fix --only <fm> [-t <id>]`. A manual one keeps its command or prose.
  - The manual journal states stop promising "any change command".
  - `status --check` also fails on any P0 or P1 issue.
  - Rejected: a new `status` field per finding kind.
- **M4-D40, the doctor dictionary, as this area uses it.**
  - Refusals are `doctor_refused` (exit 4) with `details.reason` from a closed set. This area raises `force_required`, `fixer_conflict`, `client_running`, `not_enabled` and `edited_locally`.
  - A selection of only online rows without `--online` is `online_required` (exit 6). No new error code comes from this area.
- **M4-D55: the contract's rules hold from slice 1.**
  - F1's narrowing of `journal-pending` is the kind of known pre-release correction that the owning leaf makes. It is recorded with a compatibility note in F1's close comment and on H1's change list, rather than carried to the end.
  - Every new shape here passes the rule test of A3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`, schemas and live validation). The leaves that add shapes (F2, F6 and F8 directly, the others through F8) land before H1. F9 adds none and may land after it.
- **"Fix and verify here; round-trip in F9."** A catalog leaf's acceptance is "detect, fix, verify": the finding appears, the fixer's run clears it, and its actions are exactly those planned. Undo is E7's generic inverse, so F9, which waits for E7 and every fixer, owns every undo round trip. That keeps the fixer leaves (all but F2) off E7, and the critical path at its length.
- **Common rule 19: the catalog is code.** A leaf that adds a failure mode adds its `FAILURE_MODES` row, its fixture, its row in README's doctor table, and its Appendix B line in its close comment.

### The catalog this area builds

The set-aside suspends the six stuck states' journal sets into quarantine, behind `--only <id> --force --yes`, with a suspension manifest. `doctor undo` reactivates the set only while nothing it depends on has changed. For unreadable and newer journals it moves only what it can attribute without the payload.
