description:
Part 2 of 4 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1 (Journal and lock detectors, and `status`'s journal titles). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

**The leaf.** F1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1`) gives every state in which recovery leaves an interrupted change "for manual repair" its own failure mode, title and evidence, in `doctor` and in `status`. All of them are read from one classifier, E11's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.11`) `journal::diagnose`, which predicts exactly what recovery will do with each journal. The leaf adds `lock-held-long`, and narrows the published `fm-concurrency_primitives-journal-pending` to "an interrupted change recovery can settle" (M4-D48). Part 1 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1.1) registered the ten rows, the mapping and the Journals layer, so `doctor` reports them.

**This part** puts `status` on the same detectors. Today `status` lists one `journal-pending` issue per client for any unfinished journal. It titles it "An interrupted change needs manual repair" only for a newer or unreadable journal (the only reasons that reach `issues_for`, `src/app/status.rs:884-892`, because `journal::Pending` carries only `Unrecoverable::{TooNew, Unreadable}`, `src/engine/journal.rs:487-494`, `:681-710`). Every other stuck state gets "An interrupted change waits to be finished" with "quit the game if it is running, then run any change command; it finishes or rolls back the change first" (`src/app/issues.rs:129-148`). Its `--check` fix says "run any omaddons command that changes addons (install, remove, undo); it recovers the transaction first" (`status.rs:1314-1320`). Both are wrong for every stuck state (M4-D53: "`status`'s journal remediation stops promising 'any change command' for the manual states"). After this part, `status` and `doctor` report the same id, severity and title for every journal state (checkpoint criteria 11 and 12), which is F1's half of G-M4-4's "`status` and `doctor` never disagree". It is its own step because `src/app/status.rs` and `src/app/issues.rs` are a hot spot ordered E1 → F1 → F8 (F8, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.8`, later moves every `status` issue onto `doctor::detect`), and this edit must stay small and separate.

**Decisions it obeys:** M4-D29 (one registry; `status` reads its `cached` and `quick` rows, never a second implementation; rejected: `status` calling `doctor` as a subprocess, two implementations synced by tests), M4-D48 (the narrowing; the stuck states and the game-waiting restore leave `journal-pending`), M4-D53 (as quoted; `auto_fixable` and `explain` on issues are F8's), M4-D55 (the narrowing is this leaf's recorded pre-release correction), and M4-D30 (the doctor reports one finding per journal; `status`, whose `Issue` has no instance key, groups them).

**What exists to build on:** part 1's `concurrency::journal_observations(&JournalInput)`, `lock_observation(&LockState, caller_holds_lock, now)`, `Journals::read(paths, client_dirs, sv_writable)` and the ten registry rows. E1's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`) `issues::STATUS_FAILURE_MODES`, `issue_of`, `for_target`/`for_machine` (with E1's rule "one `journal-pending` issue per target", left for this leaf to revisit), the facts bridge (`TargetFacts.journals`, `MachineFacts.unattributed`) or E2's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.2`) direct rule calls, whichever is on `main`. E1's characterization snapshots of `status`'s issues (its s1). Today's `status` reads (`status.rs:609-952`): `journal::pending` (`:627`), `probe_global` (`:628`), running for the selected targets (`detect_running(&found)`, `:625`), journal attention only when the lock is free (`:705-707`, `:842-844`), the machine's unattributed journal (`:906-919`), `needs_attention` (`:926`), `summary_state` (`:1114-1125`: `attention` on any P0 or P1 issue).

## Technical Approach

### 1. The rows `status` now reports

| # | Id (`fm-concurrency_primitives-…`) | P | Scope in `status` | Remediation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `journal-pending` | P0 | per client, or `data.issues` for a target-less repair journal | prose, today's text verbatim: `quit the game if it is running, then run any change command; it finishes or rolls back the change first` |
| 2 | `journal-waits-for-game` | P2 | per client | prose `quit the game; the next change finishes or undoes it` |
| 3 | `journal-too-new` | P0 | per client | `omaddons doctor explain fm-concurrency_primitives-journal-too-new -t <id>` |
| 4 | `journal-unreadable` | P0 | per client | `… doctor explain …-journal-unreadable -t <id>` |
| 5 | `journal-unexpected-state` | P0 | per client | `… doctor explain …-journal-unexpected-state -t <id>` |
| 6 | `journal-step-unrecognized` | P0 | per client, or `data.issues` for a target-less repair journal | `… doctor explain …-journal-step-unrecognized [-t <id>]` |
| 7 | `journal-marker-mismatch` | P0 | per client | `… doctor explain …-journal-marker-mismatch -t <id>` |
| 8 | `journal-unattributed` | P0 | `data.issues` | `omaddons doctor explain fm-concurrency_primitives-journal-unattributed` |
| 9 | `journal-preservation-incomplete` | P1 | per client | `… doctor explain …-journal-preservation-incomplete -t <id>` |
| 10 | `lock-held-long` | P2 | `data.issues` | prose `if the process holding the lock (pid <pid>) is stuck, end it (kill <pid>); the lock is released when it exits, and omaddons never touches the lock file` |

`-t` is omitted for a target that is neither in the registry nor has a record file. Every `doctor explain` remediation has `argv` and `destructive: false`; the prose ones have `argv: null`.

**Titles.** One instance: the finding's own title. More than one of a row on one client: the plural.

| # | Instance title | Plural (`n > 1`) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | folder: `An interrupted change waits to be finished` (today's text); repair: `An interrupted doctor repair waits to be finished` | `<n> interrupted changes wait to be finished` |
| 2 | `An interrupted change to WTF/ waits for the game to exit` | `<n> interrupted changes to WTF/ wait for the game to exit` |
| 3 | `An interrupted change (<kind>) was started by a newer omaddons; this build cannot read its journal (format <format>)` | `<n> interrupted changes were started by a newer omaddons` |
| 4 | `An interrupted change's journal holds lines this omaddons cannot read` | `<n> interrupted changes' journals hold lines this omaddons cannot read` |
| 5 | `An interrupted change to WTF/ stopped at step <k>, which it does not recognize` | `<n> interrupted changes to WTF/ stopped at steps they do not recognize` |
| 6 | folder: `An interrupted change stopped at step <k>, which matches neither its before nor its after state`; repair: `An interrupted doctor repair stopped at step <k>, …` | `<n> interrupted changes stopped at steps that match neither their before nor their after state` |
| 7 | `An interrupted change names a client directory that is no longer this client's` | `<n> interrupted changes name a client directory that is no longer this client's` |
| 8 | `An interrupted change cannot be attributed to any client, so every change is refused` | `<n> interrupted changes cannot be attributed to any client, so every change is refused` |
| 9 | resumable: `An interrupted change to WTF/ is still keeping the settings it displaced`; stops: `An interrupted change to WTF/ could not finish keeping the settings it displaced` | `<n> interrupted changes to WTF/ have not finished keeping the settings they displaced` |
| 10 | `An omaddons process (pid <pid>, <command>) has held the lock for more than 10 minutes` | never plural |

The plural titles are part 1's `concurrency::plural_title(id, n)`; if part 1 did not add it, add it here in `src/doctor/detectors/concurrency.rs`, beside the instance titles.

### 2. `status`'s reads and findings (`src/app/status.rs`)

1. Keep `let pending = journal::pending(&world.paths)?;`, so an unlistable journal directory fails `status` exactly as today, and `data.journal.pending` keeps its source and meaning (E5 decided not to list repair journals there).
2. Keep the lock's value: `let lock = probe_global(&world.paths)?; let held = matches!(lock, LockState::Held { .. });`.
3. Add `let journals = Journals::read(&world.paths, &client_dirs, &sv_writable)?;`. `client_dirs` is every discovered target's client dir plus every missing registry entry's (`world.resolved.targets`, `world.resolved.missing`), sorted and deduplicated. `sv_writable(dir)` holds when `dir` is a selected target whose `running` is `Some(false)`. Decided while writing this bead: `status` computes running only for its selected targets (`:625`); an unselected client's journal is out of scope under `-t` anyway, and `false` (possibly running) is the fail-closed value.
4. Run the journal rows: `journal_observations(&JournalInput { journals: &journals, lock: Some(&lock), caller_holds_lock: false, target_id, registered })` and `lock_observation(&lock, false, crate::clock::now())`. Turn each into a finding through its registry row (`FailureMode::finding`), along the path `status` uses for its other moved rows. Decided while writing this bead, for either path on `main`: if `status` runs rows through `doctor::detect` over E1's facts view, add `journals: Journals` and `lock: LockState` to `StatusFacts` and make the view's `journals()` and `lock()` accessors return them for a facts view, so the ten rows' own `detect` functions run unchanged. If `status` calls rule functions directly (E2's form), call `journal_observations` and `lock_observation` directly. `issues::STATUS_FAILURE_MODES` gains the nine new ids. Remove the journal fields from E1's facts bridge (`TargetFacts.journals`, `MachineFacts.unattributed`), if they are still there, and the facts-view branch part 1 kept in the `journal-pending` row's `detect` (or E2's direct journal rule function): the journal rows now read `Journals`.
5. **Attention.** A target's `Attention::JournalPending` is set exactly when that target has at least one finding of rows 1–9: both loops ask the findings (today `:705-707` and `:842-844`). The machine's `unattributed` flag (`:908`), which drives `needs_attention` and the machine's `--check` fix, is true exactly when a machine-scoped finding of rows 1–9 exists. `lock-held-long` is never attention. Decided while writing this bead: this gives today's results for folder journals (the findings already apply the "another process holds the lock" rule `status` applied, and skip live and committed journals), and it makes a stuck repair-family journal attention too, which `journal::pending` cannot see.
6. **A journal on a client `status` does not list.** Without `-t`, a finding scoped to a key that is neither a listed target nor a missing one goes into `data.issues`, so a P0 is never invisible. With `-t`, it is out of scope like every other client's. Decided while writing this bead.

### 3. Grouping (`src/app/issues.rs`)

`for_target(findings, key)` and `for_machine(findings)` group the scope's findings of the ten rows by id: one `Issue` per group, its title the instance's when the group holds one finding, the row's plural otherwise. Its remediation is the row's for that scope (§1), and its `addon` is `null`. Other rows keep E1's one-issue-per-finding mapping. Sorting is unchanged: severity, then id, then addon. This replaces E1's journal-pending rule. Decided while writing this bead: `status` is triage and its `Issue` has no instance key, while the doctor reports each journal as its own instance (M4-D30).

### 4. The `--check` fix (`attention_fixes`, `status.rs:1308-1369`)

For a target's `JournalPending`, take the target's most blocking journal issue: by severity, with `journal-pending` last within a severity.

- `journal-pending`: today's message (`an interrupted transaction for <id> awaits recovery`) and fix, byte for byte.
- `journal-waits-for-game`: message `<id>: <title>`, fix the row's prose.
- Rows 3–9: message `<id>: <title>`, fix `Suggestion::command(<the issue's doctor explain argv>)`.
- The machine's (today `status.rs:912-919`, "an interrupted change needs manual repair: its journal cannot be read" with a README pointer): message row 8's title, fix `Suggestion::command(["omaddons", "doctor", "explain", "fm-concurrency_primitives-journal-unattributed"])`.

No recommendation (`commands[]`) is added: decided while writing this bead, because the issue's remediation carries the argv, and `status`'s recommendations are F8's.

### 5. What stays exactly as it is

`data.journal` (`pending`, `in_progress`); the `journal_pending` and `tx_in_progress` warnings, which `World::load_with` computes; every non-journal issue; `summary` and its rule. The P0 rows keep `summary.state` at `attention`, as `journal-pending` did. A game-waiting journal is now P2, so it no longer makes the state `attention` by itself, while `status --check` still fails on it, through attention. `status` writes nothing and takes no lock.

### 6. E1's characterization snapshots

E1's s1 snapshotted every issue `status` produced for a named case table through one adapter. The adapter's journal cases now build `Journals` values (synthetic `JournalDiagnosis` values) instead of `Pending` lists. Re-accept the snapshots and review the diff:

- byte-identical: the recoverable cases;
- changed, to their new ids, titles and remediations: the `journal_too_new`, `journal_unreadable` and machine-unattributed cases;
- added: one case per new row.

Record the diff summary in the close comment.

### 7. README (common rule 11)

- **`status`'s issue table** (`README.md:752-760`): the `journal-pending` row becomes "`journal_pending` that recovery can settle | advice: quit the game and run any changing command". Add one row per new id `status` reports, with its severity, what raises it and its remediation (`omaddons doctor explain <id> -t <client>` for rows 3–9, advice for rows 2 and 10). Say that `lock-held-long` and a journal no client can carry are in the machine's `issues`. F8 later repoints the table at the doctor's.
- **Troubleshooting "`journal_pending` that does not clear"** (`README.md:2521-2525`):
  - replace "and `status` titles the issue 'needs manual repair'" with "`status` and `omaddons doctor` name the state (for example `fm-concurrency_primitives-journal-too-new`), and `omaddons doctor explain <id> -t <client>` shows its evidence";
  - replace the closing sentence ("`doctor`, which will automate this repair, is planned for milestone 4") with "The doctor names each of these states; a guarded repair for them is not part of this build yet."

  Edit only these sentences: E11 and E5 also edit this entry, and F2 rewrites it when its set-aside ships.

### 8. Files

`src/app/status.rs`, `src/app/issues.rs`, `src/doctor/detectors/concurrency.rs` (only if part 1 did not add `plural_title`), E1's characterization snapshot files, README.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `status` (plain and `--cached`) reports each journal state under its row's id, at its severity, with the instance or plural title and the remediation of Technical Approach §1; a recoverable folder journal's issue is byte-identical to today's (id, severity, title, remediation).
- [ ] Journal attention, the machine's `needs_attention` and `--check` follow the findings of rows 1–9; `lock-held-long` appears in `data.issues` and is never attention.
- [ ] The `--check` fix follows Technical Approach §4: today's text for a recoverable journal, the `doctor explain` argv for rows 3–9, the row-8 command for the machine.
- [ ] Without `-t`, a journal on an unlisted key is in `data.issues`; with `-t`, out of scope.
- [ ] Every `doctor explain` remediation argv parses (`Cli::try_parse_from`) in the unit tests; no prose remediation names a runnable omaddons command.
- [ ] E1's characterization snapshots are re-accepted with only the documented cases changed or added.
- [ ] `tests/status.rs` passes unchanged, including `a_leftover_journal_needs_attention_and_a_held_lock_does_not`.
- [ ] README's `status` issue table and the Troubleshooting sentences are updated in this commit.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files; the close comment lists `status`'s new ids, titles and remediations and the changed `--check` fix texts (wire names, common rule 6).

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

In `src/app/issues.rs` and `src/app/status.rs` (in-crate, synthetic findings and `Journals` values; one name per case; every assertion message names the case and shows the findings in and the issues out):

- `journal_issues_group_per_client_and_row`: two too-new journals and one recoverable on retail → two issues, the plural title for too-new, the singular for pending.
- `stuck_rows_remediate_with_doctor_explain`: exact argv with `-t retail`; machine-scoped and unregistered-key findings → no `-t`; each argv parses with `Cli::try_parse_from`.
- `recoverable_and_waiting_rows_keep_prose`: argv `null`, the exact texts.
- `lock_held_long_is_a_machine_issue_and_never_attention`.
- `attention_follows_the_journal_findings`: each row 1–9 → `journal_pending`; row 10 → none; a live journal → none.
- `check_fix_prefers_the_blocking_state`: pending + too-new → too-new's message and argv; pending alone → today's text byte for byte; waits-for-game → its prose.
- `unattributed_sets_needs_attention_and_its_check_fix`.
- `an_unlisted_clients_journal_is_a_machine_issue_without_t`, and out of scope with `-t`.
- E1's characterization snapshots, re-accepted.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

None new in this part: part 4 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1.4) runs `status` through the binary for every fixture. `tests/status.rs` must pass unchanged here.

### Logging

Unit tests only, as above: case names, and messages that show the findings and the issues compared.

## Considerations

- **Hot spot `src/app/status.rs`, `src/app/issues.rs` (E1 → F1 → F8, then E10 and G1 rebase).** Keep the edit to the journal reads, the two attention conditions, the machine flag, `attention_fixes`' journal arm and `issues`' grouping. Do not touch recommendations, drift, backups or errors.
- **Cost:** one more directory listing for `status --cached` on a home without journals (`journal::pending` and `Journals::read` each list `<state>/journal/`). F8 measures the 5 ms budget.
- **Compatibility:** consumers see new ids in `issues[]` (the widget lists them generically), new titles, the `doctor explain` remediations, and P2 for a game-waiting journal. The compatibility note of the narrowing goes in the leaf's close comment.
- **What could go wrong:** a byte change in the recoverable case (watch E1's snapshots and `tests/status.rs`); attention and issues disagreeing (watch `attention_follows_the_journal_findings`); a remediation that does not run (part 4 runs every one).

## Dependencies

- **Parent:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1.
- **Before it:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1.1, whose rows, texts and functions this part calls.
- **Beside it:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1.3 (fixtures; different files, may land in either order).
- **After it:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1.4, which runs `status` and `doctor` side by side on every fixture.

**`status`'s new ids, titles and remediations (wire names):**

**`--check` fix:**
- A client's message and fix come from its most blocking journal issue (by severity, `journal-pending` last within one). A settleable journal keeps today's "an interrupted transaction for <id> awaits recovery" and advice, byte for byte. A stuck state gives `<id>: <title>` with its `doctor explain` argv (or its advice).
- The machine's "an interrupted change needs manual repair: its journal cannot be read" + README pointer becomes the machine issue's title with its `doctor explain` argv.

**Characterization snapshots (re-accepted):**

- Changed: the too-new and unreadable cases move to their rows, titles and `doctor explain` argvs. Mixed cases (recoverable plus stuck) now list the pending issue and the stuck row's. The machine cases show "An interrupted doctor repair waits to be finished" plus `journal-unattributed`. `status_issue_lines` gains one line (14 issues).

**Tests:**

decided:
- **`status` calls the mapping directly** (E2's form), and the facts bridge loses its journal fields (`TargetFacts.journals`, `MachineFacts.unattributed`, `PendingJournal`, the facts `RULES` row and `concurrency::journal_pending_in`). `status::pending_journals` is gone. `status::journal_findings` is the shared entry point, used by `status` and E1's adapter.

title: Tests: the ten fixtures, their planting helpers and their detection checks
description:
Part 3 of 4 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1 (Journal and lock detectors, and `status`'s journal titles). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

**The leaf.** F1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1`) gives every state in which recovery leaves an interrupted change "for manual repair" its own failure mode, title and evidence, in `doctor` and in `status`. They are all read from E11's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.11`) `journal::diagnose`, the classifier that predicts exactly what recovery will do. It also adds `lock-held-long`. Part 1 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1.1) registered the ten rows (Appendix B rows 1–10, `fm-concurrency_primitives-…`: `journal-pending`, `journal-waits-for-game`, `journal-too-new`, `journal-unreadable`, `journal-unexpected-state`, `journal-step-unrecognized`, `journal-marker-mismatch`, `journal-unattributed`, `journal-preservation-incomplete`, `lock-held-long`).

**This part** builds the fixture of each row (M4-D47: "each failure mode has a fixture: a Rust type implementing `Fixture` in `tests/doctor/fixtures/<fm_id>.rs`, with `corrupt` deterministic and built on the `tests/common/` builders, `assert_healthy`, `subject`, and a doc comment that is the fixture's README"). It also builds the planting helpers they share, and the first suite that proves each fixture plants exactly its state. The fixtures are reused by part 4 (cross-surface scenarios), by F2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.2`, the journal fixers: it flips `fixer()` and round-trips `subject()`), by F9 (the safety harness: true positive, no false positive, repeatability, purity for every row) and by T4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4`, the slice-3 demo: "`doctor` on a home with each §2.3 stuck state planted"). Common rule 19: a leaf that adds a failure mode adds its fixture. It is its own step because the planting recipes are delicate (each must produce exactly one verdict of E11's classifier) and are shared infrastructure, separate from `status`'s wiring (part 2), which it does not touch.

M4-D47's rejected alternative, kept rejected: `corrupt.sh`/`assert.sh` scripts per failure mode (a second test language, and scripts that must clean up after themselves; the house rules ban `rm -rf` even in test scripts).

**What exists to build on:**

- E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`): `tests/doctor/mod.rs` with the `Fixture` trait (`id()`, `corrupt(&Home)`, `assert_healthy(&Home)`, `subject(&Home) -> Vec<PathBuf>`, `fixer() -> bool` default `false`, `run_env() -> Vec<(String, String)>`, `run_args() -> Vec<String>`; included by test crates as `#[path = "doctor/mod.rs"] mod fixtures;`; extended only additively), `tests/doctor/fixtures/mod.rs` with `pub fn all() -> Vec<Box<dyn Fixture>>`, and `tests/common/doctor.rs::plant` with `plant::journal_pending(home, target)` (an install crashed at `engine.journal.prepared=abort`), `plant::runs`, `plant::latest`, and `check_envelope`.
- T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`): `tests/common/tlog.rs` (`tlog!()`, `log.step`, `log.case`, `log.run(&home, argv)` through `Home::std_command`, which sets `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT` when `home.proc` is set, `log.cmd(&home, argv).env(k, v)`, `log.tree`, `log.assert_unchanged`, `log.json`, `Ran::{ok, exit, envelope, …}`; a suite carries the crate-doc marker `//! e2e suite: <purpose>`).
- `tests/common/`: `Home` (`home.rs`), `common::engine::Scene::install_args` (an `install <ref> --file <local zip> -t retail --offline` argv, `tests/common/engine.rs:117-127`), `common::wtf::Wtf` (`WTF/` trees for the fake `FAKEACCT`/`FakeRealm`/`FakeChar`), `common::procfs::FakeProc` (a fake `/proc` with a running client, as `tests/adopt.rs:759-766` builds one), `common::trees::tree_hash`, `common::privacy::assert_private_all`.
- The engine facts the recipes rely on (`c0ab5e9`): a swap journals each step and then hits `engine.swap.before_rename` before the rename (`src/engine/swap.rs:871-879`); `engine.journal.prepared`, `engine.restore.exchanged` and `engine.preserve.intent` are engine failpoints (`src/engine/tx.rs:78-113`); `Parsed::unrecoverable` is `TooNew` for a newer major `schema_version` and `Unreadable` for any complete line that does not decode (`src/engine/journal.rs:522-530`, `parse` `:538-607`); a `writes_wtf` journal with a step is left alone while its client runs or may run (`:1039-1046`), and a command without discovery treats every client as possibly running.

## Technical Approach

### 1. The trait gains one defaulted method (`tests/doctor/mod.rs`)

```rust
/// The manual remedy this finding's remediation advises, applied by hand (quit the game,
/// finish the journal with a build that can read it, release the lock), after which
/// `assert_healthy` holds. A fixer's fixture leaves it empty.
fn remedy(&self, home: &Home) {}
```

Additive (E3 allows only that). Decided while writing this bead: report-only rows need a way back to healthy for `assert_healthy` to be meaningful, and the remedy is the row's own advice, applied.

### 2. The planting helpers (`tests/common/doctor.rs::plant`)

Each is deterministic, documented (what it breaks, the verdict, the finding's id, severity and evidence), and works through the real binary or through plain edits of the files the binary wrote. Each journal edit parses the line as JSON, changes one key and writes the line back with its newline. Test code may use `std::fs`; only `src/` must go through fsx. "Recover" below means:

- for a folder journal, `config set check_interval_hours 6` (a lock-taking command that runs `recover_under`);
- for a `WTF/` journal, `install <ref> --file <local archive> -t <target> --offline`, as `Scene::install_args` builds it. This is a change command that runs discovery: a command without discovery never moves `WTF/` (`journal.rs:1039-1046`).

`<root>/aside/` is a directory under the `Home`'s root, outside every scanned or state directory.

| # | Helper | Recipe | Expected verdict and evidence | `remedy` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `journal_pending(home, target)` (E3's) | an `install` on `target` crashed at `engine.journal.prepared=abort`: a `prepared` line, no step | `Recoverable { Prepared, Back }`; `phase: prepared`, `kind: install` | recover |
| 2 | `journal_waits_for_game(home, target) -> FakeProc` | a `Wtf::at(<client dir>).saved_variables("Foo", 64).build()` tree; `backup create -t <target>`; `backup restore <id> -t <target>` crashed at `engine.restore.exchanged=abort` (a `writes_wtf` journal with its exchange step); a `FakeProc` running the client's executable (`/usr/bin/wine <client dir>/Wow.exe`) | with `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT` set to the fake: `WaitsForGame`; `reason: saved_variables`, `kind: restore` | recover, without the fake process (the game exited) |
| 3 | `journal_too_new(home, target)` | row 1's crash, then the `prepared` line's top-level `schema_version` set to `"9.0"` | `TooNew`; `reason: journal_too_new`, `format: "9.0"` | set it back to the build's version, then recover |
| 4 | `journal_unreadable(home, target)` | row 1's crash, then the complete line `{"type":"from_a_later_build"}` appended | `Unreadable`; `reason: journal_unreadable` | remove that line, then recover |
| 5 | `journal_unexpected_state(home, target)` | row 2's crashed restore with no fake process; then both sides of its step 1 replaced: the staged `WTF` (under `<meta>/stage/<tx>.wtf/`) and the live `WTF` moved into `<root>/aside/`, and an empty `WTF/` created at the live path | `UnexpectedState { step: 1 }`; `reason: unexpected_state`, `step: 1` | remove the empty `WTF/`, move both back, then recover |
| 6 | `journal_step_unrecognized(home, target)` | an `install` of an addon not installed yet, crashed at `engine.swap.before_rename=abort` (step 1 journaled, its rename not run); then that `step` line's `from_id.ino` increased by 1,000,000 | `StepUnrecognized { step: 1 }`; `reason: step_unrecognized`, `step: 1` | restore the recorded `ino`, then recover |
| 7 | `journal_marker_mismatch(home, target, other)` | row 1's crash on `target`, then the `prepared` line's `client_dir` set to `other`'s client dir (whose marker names `other`) | `MarkerMismatch`; `reason: marker_mismatch`, `path` = `other`'s client dir, `expected` = `target`'s key, `observed` = `other`'s key | set it back, then recover |
| 8 | `journal_unattributed(home) -> String` | `<state>/journal/<a fresh ULID>.jsonl` holding the one complete line `{"type":"prepared","schema_version":"1.1"}` (no target; it does not decode); returns the tx | `Unattributed { cause: Unreadable }`, machine; `cause: unreadable` | move the file into `<root>/aside/` |
| 9 | `journal_preservation_incomplete(home, target)` | row 2's crashed restore with no fake process; the restored `WTF/` played on (one SavedVariables file rewritten); then recover with `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS=engine.preserve.intent=abort` (the intent is journaled, `preserved` is not) | `PreservationIncomplete { stops: false }`; `resumable: true`, `count` ≥ 1 | recover again (it resumes and completes; a `recovered` backup then exists) |
| 10 | (inside the fixture) | `omaddons::fsx::GlobalLock::acquire(&paths, "update")` from the test process, the guard kept in the fixture's state, the acquisition time recorded; `run_env` sets `OMADDONS_NOW` to that time plus `LOCK_HELD_LONG` plus 60 s | `lock-held-long`, machine; `pid` = the test process, `command: update`, `age_s` ≈ 660 | drop the guard |

Also add `plant::journals(home) -> Vec<(String, PathBuf)>` (the transaction ids and files in `<state>/journal/`, sorted), so fixtures and scenarios name the planted tx without parsing output, and `plant::copy_journal(home, tx) -> String`: a copy of `tx`'s journal file under a fresh ULID, with every `tx` field of its `prepared` line (the top-level one and `commit.history.tx`) set to the new id, returning it. A client holds at most one journal planted by a crash: the next change on that client recovers a recoverable journal first, and an unrecoverable one refuses the change. So a scenario that needs several journals on one client plants one by a crash and derives the others by copying and editing; their verdicts (`TooNew`, `Unreadable`, `MarkerMismatch`) do not depend on the copy's artifacts. The lock fixture never names the lock file; it acquires through the library, as `tests/status.rs:412` does.

Ordering constraints, documented on each helper as E3's helpers do: plant a journal last on its client, because any later change on that client would recover it first; a too-new or unreadable journal blocks further changes on its client.

### 3. The ten fixtures (`tests/doctor/fixtures/fm_concurrency_primitives_<slug>.rs`)

- One file per row, named after the id in snake case (a module name cannot hold a hyphen), each a `pub struct` implementing `Fixture`, added to `fixtures/mod.rs`'s `all()`.
- `corrupt`: the row's helper. The fixture keeps what it needs for `remedy` (the tx, the original values it edited, the fake process, the lock guard) in interior state (`RefCell`), since the trait takes `&self`.
- `run_env`: row 2 `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT=<fake root>`; row 10 `OMADDONS_NOW=<time>`; others none. `run_args`: none.
- `assert_healthy`: `doctor --json --only <id>` (with `run_env`) reports no finding of the id, and `<state>/journal/` holds no journal of the planted tx.
- `subject`: for rows 1–9, the transaction's journal set: the journal file, `<state>/inflight/<tx>.lock`, `<state>/snapshots/<tx>[.wtf]`, `<meta>/stage/<tx>[.wtf]` and `<meta>/snapshots/<tx>[.wtf]`, those that exist after `corrupt`; for row 10, nothing. Decided while writing this bead: defined now, because F2's round trip compares exactly these (the safety harness's subject rule: "a set-aside's subject is the original journal, its in-flight lock file, its stage and both snapshot halves").
- `fixer()`: `false` for all ten; F2 flips rows 1 and 3–9 when it adds their fixers.
- The doc comment of each is its README: what breaks, how `corrupt` builds it, the verdict E11 gives it, the finding's id, severity, scope and evidence keys, and the remedy.
- Each fixture's `corrupt` targets `retail` on a `Home::new(&["wow", "wow_classic"])` (classic is `other` for row 7), so the fixtures compose in one home when a scenario needs several.

### 4. The detection suite (`tests/doctor_concurrency.rs`, new)

First line `//! e2e suite: the journal and lock detectors, and status's journal titles`. It includes the fixtures with `#[path = "doctor/mod.rs"] mod fixtures;`. Decided while writing this bead: a suite of its own rather than more scenarios in E3's `tests/doctor.rs`, which F3, F4 and F5 also extend. Part 4 adds its scenarios to this file. This part's scenarios:

1. **`every_concurrency_fixture_is_found_and_cleared`**: one `log.case(<id>)` per fixture of the ten, each on a fresh `Home`. Steps:
   - "plant": `corrupt`; `log.json("journals", plant::journals(&home))`.
   - "doctor --only": `doctor --json --only <id>` with `run_env`. Exit 1; exactly one finding, of that id, at its severity, its `instance` ending `:tx=<the planted tx>` (rows 1–9) or equal to `<id>@machine` (row 10), and its evidence holding the keys and values of §2's table.
   - "doctor": `doctor --json`. The id is present.
   - "remedy": `remedy`.
   - "healthy": `assert_healthy`.
2. **`no_concurrency_detector_fires_on_a_clean_home`**: the clean home is `common::realistic_home()` if it exists on `main`; otherwise a three-client home with five addons installed from local archives, one update, one undo, one `backup create` and one completed whole `backup restore` (decided while writing this bead). Then `doctor --json --only <the ten ids, comma-separated>` → exit 0 and no finding; and the same while a young lock is held (a guard acquired in process, no `OMADDONS_NOW`).
3. **`the_concurrency_fixtures_are_registered`**: `fixtures::all()` holds exactly one fixture per row of `FAILURE_MODES` whose id starts `fm-concurrency_primitives-`, each row `Tier::Cached`, each fixture `fixer() == false`.

### 5. Files

`tests/doctor/mod.rs` (`remedy`), `tests/doctor/fixtures/mod.rs` and the ten fixture files, `tests/common/doctor.rs` (`plant::*`), `tests/doctor_concurrency.rs` (new).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The ten fixture files exist, each registered in `fixtures::all()`, each with a doc comment that is its README, `fixer() == false`, and `subject` as Technical Approach §3 says.
- [ ] `every_concurrency_fixture_is_found_and_cleared` passes: each `corrupt` yields exactly its row's finding with Technical Approach §2's evidence, and its `remedy` makes `assert_healthy` hold.
- [ ] `no_concurrency_detector_fires_on_a_clean_home` passes, with and without a young held lock.
- [ ] `the_concurrency_fixtures_are_registered` passes.
- [ ] The `Fixture` trait gained only the defaulted `remedy`; E3's runtime fixtures and `tests/doctor.rs` pass unchanged.
- [ ] `argc e2e doctor_concurrency` runs the suite with verbose logs.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files; the close comment lists the fixture files and the `plant` helpers (for F2, F9 and T4).

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

None in `src/`. Each planting helper is checked by its fixture's case in scenario 1: the planted state is the one the finding names, with the expected `reason` and `step`.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

The three scenarios of §4, in `tests/doctor_concurrency.rs`, through the real binary. Failpoints used by the helpers: `engine.journal.prepared=abort`, `engine.swap.before_rename=abort`, `engine.restore.exchanged=abort`, `engine.preserve.intent=abort`. Environment: `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT` (row 2), `OMADDONS_NOW` (row 10).

### Logging

- Every scenario opens `let log = tlog!();` and names its phases with `log.step` ("home", "plant", "doctor --only", "doctor", "remedy", "healthy"). The planting commands also go through `log.run`/`log.cmd`, so each crashed child (its argv, the failpoint armed, its abort) is in `steps.jsonl` and `transcript.md`.
- Per fixture: `log.case(<id>)`; `log.json("journals", …)` after planting; `log.json("finding", …)` before asserting it; the journal lines the helper edited are logged before and after the edit (`log.note`, with any `WTF/` path cut at `WTF`).
- A failing case prints the fixture id, the expected and actual finding, and the transcript path; T1's guard prints the last 20 steps.

## Considerations

- **Fragility of the recipes.** Each depends on where an engine failpoint sits and on recovery's rules, which E11's differential test pins. A recipe that yields another verdict fails its own case with the diagnosis logged, never silently.
- **Row 10 runs in process:** the guard is held by the test process, so the holder's `pid` is the test's. Use one `Home` per case, so a guard never outlives its case (drop it in `remedy` and on panic, through the fixture's `Drop`).
- **Privacy:** rows 2, 5 and 9 create `WTF/` trees with the fake names only. Part 4 asserts no output names them.
- **Root:** no step here depends on file modes, so nothing is skipped as root.
- **Hot spots:** `tests/common/doctor.rs` and `tests/doctor/fixtures/mod.rs` are shared with F3, F4, F5 and F9. Append, then rebase.

## Dependencies

- **Parent:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1.
- **Before it:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1.1 (the rows and the detectors these fixtures trigger). It is blocked by T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`) at filing, because it writes a `TestLog` suite.
- **Beside it:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1.2 (`status`'s wiring; different files).
- **After it:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1.4, which runs `status` and `doctor` on every fixture.

title: E2E: `status` and `doctor` name every stuck state alike
description:
Part 4 of 4 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1 (Journal and lock detectors, and `status`'s journal titles). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

**The leaf.** F1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1`) gives every state in which recovery leaves an interrupted change "for manual repair" its own failure mode, title and evidence, in `doctor` and in `status`. They are read from E11's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.11`) `journal::diagnose`, the classifier that predicts exactly what recovery will do. It adds `lock-held-long`, and narrows the published `fm-concurrency_primitives-journal-pending` to "an interrupted change recovery can settle" (M4-D48).

The earlier parts:

- Part 1 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1.1) registered the ten rows (Appendix B rows 1–10), the mapping and the Journals layer.
- Part 2 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1.2) put `status`'s journal issues, attention and `--check` fix on them.
- Part 3 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1.3) built the ten fixtures and their planting helpers, and proved each plants exactly its state.

**This part** proves the leaf's promises end to end, through the real binary, across both surfaces:

- each state is reported under the same id, severity and title by `status` and by `doctor` (checkpoint criteria 11 and 12: "a finding with a correct title in both `status` and `doctor`"; "the issue ids `status` reports equal the doctor findings of those tiers");
- the published id keeps its spelling and its most common meaning;
- two stuck journals are two instances, and `--since` tells them apart (the end-to-end case E3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, left to this leaf);
- a young lock is no finding and an old one is;
- a lock held by another process hides journals until it is released;
- the detectors are repeatable and write nothing (criterion 9's properties for these rows);
- no output names an account, realm or character (common rule 9);
- the widget matches no id by name (M4-D48: "The widget matches no issue id by name (it lists `issues[]` generically)");
- the contract pins the new shapes.

It is the leaf's last part. Its closing agent verifies every acceptance criterion of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1, writes the close comment (the wire names, the compatibility note of the narrowing, the ten Appendix B lines, every "decided" item), adds the narrowing to H1's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`) change list with a comment, and closes the leaf.

**What exists to build on:**

- Part 3's fixtures (`fixtures::all()`, the ten `fm_concurrency_primitives_*` types with `corrupt`, `run_env`, `remedy`, `assert_healthy`, `subject`) and `plant::*` helpers, in `tests/doctor_concurrency.rs`'s crate.
- T1's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`) `TestLog` (`tlog!()`, `log.step`, `log.case`, `log.run`, `log.cmd(...).env(...)`, `log.tree`, `log.assert_unchanged`, `log.json`, `Ran`).
- E3's `common::doctor::check_envelope`, the doctor envelope (report keys at the top level), `doctor --since <run>` (`since: {run, new[], resolved[], unchanged}` by instance key), and `contract::VOLATILE`.
- `common::privacy::assert_private_all`.
- `tests/status.rs`'s `Machine` helpers and its existing `a_leftover_journal_needs_attention_and_a_held_lock_does_not` (`tests/status.rs:296-430`).
- `tests/omarchy_widget.rs`'s file walk (`the_plugin_id_is_a_literal_in_the_manifest_only`, `:166-219`).
- `tests/contract/recommendations.rs`, whose scenarios run every issue remediation and require it to clear its issue unless it is a look (`:304-326`).

**What the surfaces must show** (the rows of part 1, the `status` mapping of part 2):

- **Severities:** rows 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8 are P0; row 9 is P1; rows 2 (`journal-waits-for-game`) and 10 (`lock-held-long`) are P2.
- **Scope:** rows 8 and 10 are machine-scoped (`data.issues` in `status`); the others are per client.
- **Remediation:** rows 1, 2 and 10 are prose; rows 3–9 are `omaddons doctor explain <id> -t <client>` (without `-t` for a machine-scoped finding).
- **Titles:** `status` uses the finding's instance title when a client has one instance of a row, and the row's plural title for more.
- **Attention:** rows 1–7 and 9 make their client's attention `journal_pending`; row 8, and any machine-scoped journal finding, makes `data.needs_attention` true; row 10 is never attention.
- **The held-lock rule:** while another process holds the global lock, no journal row reports anything.
- **Row 1's issue for a recoverable folder journal** is byte-identical to today's: title `An interrupted change waits to be finished`, remediation `quit the game if it is running, then run any change command; it finishes or rolls back the change first`.

## Technical Approach

### 1. Scenarios in `tests/doctor_concurrency.rs` (appended to part 3's suite)

Every scenario is a `TestLog` scenario on its own `Home::new(&["wow", "wow_classic"])`, runs every command through `log.run`/`log.cmd` with `--json` passed explicitly (and the fixture's `run_env`), checks every doctor envelope with `check_envelope`, and records the trees `state-outside-doctor` (`<state>` without `doctor/`), `config`, `cache` and each client dir with `log.tree` before the first reader, then asserts them with `log.assert_unchanged` after the last.

1. **`status_and_doctor_name_each_state_alike`**: one `log.case(<id>)` per fixture of the ten.
   - "plant": `corrupt`.
   - "trees".
   - "doctor": `doctor --json` → exit 1. Collect `(id, scope, severity, title)` of every finding of the ten rows, where scope is `target.key` or `machine`.
   - "status", then "status --cached": `status --json` and `status --cached --json`, both exit 0. Collect `(id, scope, severity, title)` from `data.targets[].issues[]` (scope: that target's key) and `data.issues[]` (scope: machine). The three sets are equal for the ten rows; `log.json` each before comparing.
   - "attention": for rows 1–7 and 9 the client's `attention` contains `journal_pending`; for row 8 (machine-scoped) `data.needs_attention` is true and no client's `attention` changes. For rows 1–9, `status --check --json` → exit 6, `error.code: check_failed`. The fix is the issue's `doctor explain` argv for rows 3–9, row 2's prose, and for a recoverable journal today's text; for row 8, the machine fix `omaddons doctor explain fm-concurrency_primitives-journal-unattributed`. For row 10, `attention` holds no `journal_pending`, and `status --check` → exit 0.
   - "summary": `summary.state` is `attention` for the P0 and P1 rows, and not `attention` for rows 2 and 10 alone.
   - "explain each remediation": every `remediation.argv` in `status` and every `remediation.argv`/`explain_argv` in `doctor` → exit 0; the explain output's `instances` holds the finding.
   - "check trees": `assert_unchanged` on every tree.
2. **`a_recoverable_journal_keeps_its_published_id_and_meaning`**: fixture 1. `status --json`: the issue's id is exactly `fm-concurrency_primitives-journal-pending`, its severity P0, its title `An interrupted change waits to be finished`, its remediation `{command: <today's prose>, argv: null, destructive: false}`. `doctor --json`: the finding has `evidence.family: "folder"`, `evidence.phase: "prepared"`, and no `reason`. Then "recover" (`config set check_interval_hours 6`): `status` and `doctor` report nothing of the ten rows.
3. **`two_stuck_journals_on_one_client_are_two_instances_and_since_tells_them_apart`**:
   - Plant two too-new journals on retail: `plant::journal_too_new(home, "retail")`, then `plant::copy_journal` of it (a client holds at most one crash-planted journal: a second install would refuse to commit behind the first). Assert two journals in `plant::journals`.
   - "run A": `doctor --json`. Two instances `…journal-too-new@<key>:tx=<A>` and `…:tx=<B>`, two labels.
   - `status --json`: one issue with the plural title `2 interrupted changes were started by a newer omaddons`.
   - "settle one": move journal A's set (its journal file, in-flight lock file, stage and snapshots) into `<root>/aside/`, as if the newer build had finished it.
   - "since": `doctor --json --since <run A>` → `since.resolved` is `[<A's instance>]`, `since.unchanged` is 1, `since.new` is `[]`. `status`'s issue now has the singular instance title.
4. **`another_holder_hides_journals_until_it_releases`**:
   - Plant fixture 3 (too-new).
   - "hold": `GlobalLock::acquire(&paths, "update")` in the test process. `status --json`: no journal issue, `data.journal.in_progress: true`, a `tx_in_progress` warning. `doctor --json`: no finding of rows 1–9, exit 0 (or 1 only for unrelated rows, of which there are none here).
   - "hold long": the same two reads with `OMADDONS_NOW` set to the acquisition time plus 11 minutes. `lock-held-long` is present in both (`data.issues` and the doctor's findings), and the journal still is not.
   - "release": drop the guard. The too-new finding and issue are back; `lock-held-long` is gone.
5. **`a_young_lock_is_no_finding_and_an_old_one_is`**: fixture 10, case by case (`log.case`):
   - `OMADDONS_NOW` unset: no finding.
   - acquisition time + 9 min 59 s: no finding.
   - + 10 min 1 s: the finding, with evidence `{pid: <this process>, command: "update", age_s: 601}`, `confidence: medium`, and title `An omaddons process (pid <pid>, update) has held the lock for more than 10 minutes`. Its remediation prose names `kill <pid>` and no omaddons command.
   - Run `doctor --json` twice at the same frozen time: the findings are equal; with two different frozen times, they differ only in `evidence.age_s`, which `contract::VOLATILE` declares.
   - The lock file is never touched: `log.tree` of `<state>` holds its digest, unchanged by the reads.
6. **`the_detectors_are_repeatable_and_change_nothing`**: for each fixture, `doctor --json` twice → equal `findings` after stripping only the declared volatile keys, and envelope bytes equal after stripping them; `status --json` twice → byte-equal stdout. Every tree is unchanged except `<state>/doctor/` (new run directories only).
7. **`journal_findings_name_no_account_realm_or_character`**: fixtures 2, 5 and 9 (their `WTF/` trees hold `FAKEACCT`, `FakeRealm`, `FakeChar`). Check `status --json --progress json`, `status --progress json` (human), `doctor --json --progress json` and `doctor -v --progress json`, each with `Ran::assert_private()` (`assert_private_all` over stdout and stderr), and `common::privacy::assert_private` over the run's `report.json`. Every `evidence` path is under `<state>` or is a client directory.
8. **`status_prints_each_stuck_title_and_its_command`**: a too-new journal on retail (`plant::journal_too_new(home, "retail")`), then a stuck step on classic (`plant::journal_step_unrecognized(home, "classic")`, whose install proceeds because retail's journal only warns another client). Human `status` prints, under each client's row, `  P0 <the instance title> → omaddons doctor explain <id> -t <client>`.
9. **Conditional cases, added by whichever of this leaf and E5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`) or E14 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14`) lands second:**
   - `a_crashed_repair_is_journal_pending_with_family_repair`: E5's crashed-repair scene builder; `doctor` reports `journal-pending` with `evidence.family: "repair"`, and `status` lists it at the scope E5's diagnosis gives it.
   - `a_journal_behind_a_barrier_reports_its_own_state`: E14's barrier scene; `evidence.behind_barrier` names the owning repair's tx.

### 2. `tests/status.rs`

- New: **`a_stuck_journal_has_its_own_issue_title_and_remediation`**, using the file's `Machine` helpers with the `plant` helpers.
  - Plant a step-unrecognized journal on retail (`plant::journal_step_unrecognized`), then two copies of it (`plant::copy_journal`), one edited into a too-new journal (`schema_version` `"9.0"`) and one into a marker mismatch (`client_dir` set to classic's), and then a recoverable journal on classic (`plant::journal_pending(home, "classic")`: its install proceeds, because retail's journals only warn another client).
  - Assert retail's `issues` hold exactly the three ids with their titles and `doctor explain` argvs, and classic's the recoverable `journal-pending` with today's title.
  - Assert both clients' `attention` is `["journal_pending"]`, `summary.issues.p0` is 4, and `status` changed nothing (`m.hashes()`).
- Unchanged and passing: `a_leftover_journal_needs_attention_and_a_held_lock_does_not`.

### 3. `tests/omarchy_widget.rs`

**`the_widget_matches_no_issue_id_by_name`** (always on, no `TestLog`: one read-only scan):

- Walk every `.js` and `.qml` file under `omarchy/` except `omarchy/tests/`, as `the_plugin_id_is_a_literal_in_the_manifest_only` walks them.
- Assert none contains `fm-` followed by an ASCII lowercase letter, and none contains any id of `omaddons::doctor::registry::FAILURE_MODES` (through the file's `id_literals`).
- Check itself: plant `"fm-concurrency_primitives-journal-pending"` into a copy of `Model.js`'s text and assert the scan finds it at `Model.js:<line>`.

Decided while writing this bead: a test rather than the one-time grep the plan names, so a later widget change cannot start matching ids silently.

### 4. Contract

- **`tests/contract/matrix.rs`**: two rows, each with its snapshot.
  - `status_with_a_journal_too_new` (exit 0; retail's issue in full);
  - `doctor_diagnose_with_a_journal_too_new` (doctor mode, exit 1; the finding in full, with the volatile keys stripped by the harness).
  - Every argv in either envelope runs (the contract suite's existing rule).
- **`tests/contract/recommendations.rs`**: a scenario `stuck` (a too-new journal on retail). Its issue's remediation runs (`doctor explain …`, exit 0) and is a look: extend the `look` rule (`:323`) to any remediation whose argv starts `["omaddons", "doctor", "explain"]`. Decided while writing this bead, so the "every remediation runs" audit covers the new remediations now, and F8 inherits a correct rule.
- A3's live validation, if A3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`) has landed, validates both new rows' envelopes against their schemas, the new evidence keys included.

### 5. Files

`tests/doctor_concurrency.rs`, `tests/status.rs`, `tests/omarchy_widget.rs`, `tests/contract/matrix.rs` and its two new snapshots, `tests/contract/recommendations.rs`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `status_and_doctor_name_each_state_alike` passes for all ten fixtures: equal `(id, scope, severity, title)` sets in `doctor`, `status` and `status --cached`; attention, `--check` and `summary.state` as specified; every remediation and explain argv exits 0; trees unchanged.
- [ ] `a_recoverable_journal_keeps_its_published_id_and_meaning` passes: the published id, title and remediation are today's.
- [ ] `two_stuck_journals_on_one_client_are_two_instances_and_since_tells_them_apart` passes: two instances, one plural `status` issue, and `--since` reports one resolved and one unchanged.
- [ ] `another_holder_hides_journals_until_it_releases` and `a_young_lock_is_no_finding_and_an_old_one_is` pass, including the 9 min 59 s / 10 min 1 s boundary, and the lock file is never touched.
- [ ] `the_detectors_are_repeatable_and_change_nothing` and `journal_findings_name_no_account_realm_or_character` pass.
- [ ] `status_prints_each_stuck_title_and_its_command` passes.
- [ ] `tests/status.rs::a_stuck_journal_has_its_own_issue_title_and_remediation` passes, and the existing journal case passes unchanged.
- [ ] `tests/omarchy_widget.rs::the_widget_matches_no_issue_id_by_name` passes and finds the planted id.
- [ ] The two contract rows and their snapshots exist; the `stuck` recommendations scenario passes.
- [ ] The conditional E5/E14 cases exist if those leaves had landed (otherwise the close comment says which of them adds them).
- [ ] `argc e2e doctor_concurrency` passes with verbose logs; its log root is quoted in the close comment.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean; the closing agent verifies every acceptance criterion of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1 and closes it as its body says (close comment with the wire names, the compatibility note and the ten Appendix B lines; the comment on omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1).

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

None in `src/` (parts 1 and 2 hold them). The contract rows' snapshots are reviewed by hand once.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

The scenarios of §1–§4 above, through the real binary. The environment each needs:

- failpoints, through the `plant` helpers: `engine.journal.prepared=abort`, `engine.swap.before_rename=abort`, `engine.restore.exchanged=abort`, `engine.preserve.intent=abort`;
- `OMADDONS_NOW` for the lock cases, `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT` for the game-waiting case, and `--progress json` for privacy.

There are no crash or concurrency matrices of this leaf's own: it adds no protocol. The held-lock cases use an in-process guard, not a race.

### Logging

- Every scenario opens `let log = tlog!();` and names its phases: "home", "plant", "trees", "doctor", "status", "status --cached", "attention", "summary", "explain each remediation", "hold", "hold long", "release", "settle one", "since", "check trees".
- Each fixture or boundary is a `log.case(<id or boundary>)`, so a failing case's transcript stands alone.
- The three collected `(id, scope, severity, title)` sets are recorded with `log.json` before they are compared. A mismatch prints the case, the three sets, the first differing element and the transcript path.
- Trees are recorded with `log.tree` and compared with `log.assert_unchanged`, which logs the first differing paths.
- On panic, T1's guard prints `test log: <path>` and the last 20 steps; `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG=verbose argc e2e doctor_concurrency` echoes every step live.

## Considerations

- **Run time.** The suite runs roughly 150 commands, each fixture on a fresh home, several with a crashed child. Keep homes to two clients, and build the clean home of part 3 once per scenario, not per case.
- **The in-process lock guard** must be dropped at the end of its case (and on panic, through the fixture's `Drop`), or every later case in the same thread would see a held lock. Each case has its own `Home`, so the guard never crosses homes.
- **Flakiness.** No scenario sleeps. Ages come from `OMADDONS_NOW`, and "running" from the fake `/proc`.
- **Hot spots:**
  - `tests/contract/matrix.rs` and its snapshots: append rows, one snapshot file per row.
  - `tests/status.rs` and `tests/omarchy_widget.rs`: append tests.
  - `tests/contract/recommendations.rs`: one scenario, and the one-line `look` rule.
- **What could go wrong:**
  - The marker-mismatch fixture also leaves the journal unrecovered on retail while classic's marker is correct: assert only the rows each case planted.
  - A plural title shown where a case expects a singular one: plant one journal per row unless the case says otherwise.

## Dependencies

- **Parent:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1.
- **Before it:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1.2 (`status` on the detectors) and omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1.3 (the fixtures and the suite file). It is blocked by T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`) at filing, because it writes `TestLog` scenarios.
- **After it:** nothing inside the leaf; closing it closes omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1, which unblocks F2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.2`), F8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.8`), E10 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.10`) and T4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4`).

title: Skill drift
description:
## How to work this bead

This bead is worked through its 3 subtasks, listed below in work order. Claim a subtask, not this bead (`br ready --parent omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.10` lists the ready ones). The agent that closes the last open subtask then verifies every acceptance criterion of this bead (they are the leaf's, not any one subtask's), and closes this bead with `br close omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.10 --reason "done: <evidence> · found: <ids>"`. Until this bead is closed, every bead it blocks stays blocked.

1. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.10.1 The skill layer follows every installed skill, and the drift detector: the doctor's view reads each installed `SKILL.md` (the default folder and the folders `history_tail.skill_dirs[]` names), classifies it by its stamp without rendering the guide, and `fm-plugins-skill-version-drift` reports what is outdated, edited, linked or unreadable. Starts at once.
2. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.10.2 The rewrite fixer brings an outdated skill current: `doctor fix` rewrites it with a verbatim backup, and refuses every skill it must leave to the user. Needs part 1.
3. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.10.3 Tests: the skill-drift fixture, the drift and repair scenarios end to end, and the detector's cached-tier budget: the fixture, twelve scenarios through the real binary, two contract rows and a release-build measurement. Needs parts 1 and 2.

The plan sized this leaf S (one sitting). The three parts split the work into three commits that each pass the gate; the leaf still closes as one unit, so F8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.8`, `status` on the registry) and F9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`, the safety harness) never see half of it.

## Background

**What this work is.** M4 makes the agent guide (`omaddons robot-docs guide`) the skill coding agents load: B3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3`, `robot-docs install-skill`) writes it as `SKILL.md` into `<skills>` (`$HOME/.claude/skills/omaddons`) or any folder given with `--dir`, byte-identical to the guide this build renders. An installed skill is a copy, so it goes out of date the moment a newer omaddons ships a different guide, and an agent that loads the old copy is taught commands, error codes and rules this build may not have. This leaf adds the doctor's check for that state, `fm-plugins-skill-version-drift` (Appendix B row 40, P3, `cached` tier), and its repair: `doctor fix` rewrites an outdated skill with this build's guide, keeping the replaced file as a verbatim backup, and leaves every skill a person edited, linked or broke to that person.

**Why it is a leaf of its own.** The check needs two things from the guide chain (A3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`, schemas) → A5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5`, the `robot-docs` tree) → B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`, the guide renderer) → B3): the guide's content stamp and expected digest (B1's) and the list of folders the skill was installed into (B3). It needs one thing from the doctor chain: the fix runtime (E6, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`, `doctor fix`). Folding it into B3 would put the doctor on the guide chain's path, and folding it into F7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.7`, plugins, secrets and the network) would make F7 wait for B3. As its own leaf it starts when both chains are ready, and neither waits for it.

**What is true today** (verified at `c0ab5e9`): no skill is installed by anything. `Paths::skill_dir()` exists (`src/state/paths.rs:263-266`) and fsx already has a `Skill` writer and a `Skill` scope row that admits the `Doctor` writer (`src/fsx/scope.rs:38-41`, `:126`), but no command writes a skill, the repository has no `skills/` folder, and nothing detects drift ("skill drift (no skill install exists)", the plan's §2.5). B3 and B1 add the install and the stamp; this leaf adds the check and the fix.

**The milestone goals it serves:**
- **G-M4-4, diagnosable and repairable:** "`omaddons doctor` names every broken state omaddons can detect in what it owns or manages. Each finding carries concrete evidence and an exact remediation. A check that ran out of budget or entries says so: incomplete coverage is never reported as healthy. Every auto-fixable state is repaired by one consented command that backs up verbatim, never deletes, and is proven by a fixture that round-trips."
- **G-M4-1, self-describing:** an agent learns omaddons from the binary itself, and a Claude Code session learns it from the installed skill, which is the guide. A stale skill breaks that promise silently; this check makes it visible and repairable.
- **G-M4-6, no new risk to the engine:** the rewrite is an ordinary repair transaction (E5, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`, the repair transaction): every write through fsx, journaled per primitive, recovered by any lock-taking command.

**The checkpoint criteria it is responsible for:**
- **Criterion 3 (the guide and the skill), its doctor bullet:** "`doctor` reports an installed skill whose guide digest differs from this binary's (`fm-plugins-skill-version-drift`), never one that differs only by build, and `doctor fix` brings it current, undoably. A skill whose bytes no longer match its own stamp was edited by hand and is left to the user."
- **Criterion 9 (the safety harness), its share:** every detector has a fixture that triggers it and a clean home that does not; detectors are repeatable; bare `doctor` changes nothing outside `<state>/doctor/`; every auto-fixer round-trips byte for byte. This leaf ships the fixture and its own detect-fix-verify proof; F9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`, the safety harness) runs the round trip through `doctor undo`, every crash boundary and the declared pair "credential-file-mode + skill-version-drift".
- **Criterion 12 (`status` and `doctor` agree, and `status` stays fast):** the row is `cached` and `status` reports it once F8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.8`, `status` on the registry) lands ("C (machine)" in Appendix B), so it must fit `status --cached`'s 5 ms budget.

**The decisions that shape it** (the full log is in the decision-log comments on the milestone epic `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`):
- **M4-D50: drift of the widget is reported; drift of the skill is repaired.** `fm-plugins-skill-version-drift` (P3, `cached`) has a fixer that rewrites each drifted skill.
  - *Where it looks:* `Paths::skill_dir()` and each directory in `history_tail.skill_dirs[]`, the projection field B3 adds (every directory a `skill` history line names, newest first, bounded to `SKILL_DIRS_MAX`). The projection keeps them however old the install is, which a scan of the history tail's runs would not.
  - *How it compares, without rendering:* the line after the frontmatter is the guide's stamp, `<!-- omaddons guide sha256:<hex> -->` (M4-D7). The detector reads each file (a few kilobytes) and hashes it with that line omitted. If the hash equals the stamp and the stamp differs from this binary's `OMADDONS_GUIDE_SHA256`, the skill is outdated: that is drift. A skill whose stamp equals the binary's is current, whatever build wrote it, so unrelated code changes never make a skill look stale. The `cached` tier never renders the guide.
  - *A locally edited skill* (its bytes no longer match its own stamp) is never rewritten by the doctor. If its stamp also differs from the binary's, the finding is reported with `evidence.edited: true`, and the fixer refuses that instance (`doctor_refused`, reason `edited_locally`), so it is manual: `omaddons robot-docs install-skill --dir <dir>`, which keeps a backup.
  - *A symlinked `SKILL.md`* is never written through (fsx refuses a symlink's final component, `src/fsx/mutate.rs:610-615`). It is reported with prose advice.
  - The fixer writes the current guide through `mutate()` with a verbatim backup, and is undoable. A skill directory that no longer exists is not a finding: the user deleted it.
  - *Why:* the skill is one file in a scope the doctor may write, whereas reinstalling the widget runs Omarchy's own tools with the user's environment, is never undone (M3-D38) and must run from the desktop session. *Rejected:* doctor-driven widget reinstalls (subprocesses outside the doctor's safety envelope); that row (`fm-plugins-widget-version-drift`) stays F7's, manual.
- **M4-D7: the guide, `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` and the installed skill are one artifact.** The guide opens with YAML frontmatter; the stamp is the line right after it; the digest covers the document with that one line omitted; the guide embeds no build id, crate version or contract version. `build.rs` computes the stamp-omitted SHA-256 of the committed `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` into `OMADDONS_GUIDE_SHA256`, so the binary knows its expected digest without rendering, and the gate holds it equal to the rendered guide's. *Rejected, and the reason this leaf can be cheap and correct:* the reviewed draft's stamp `<!-- omaddons <version> build <build_id> body sha256:<hex> -->` as the first line had no fixed point, broke the skill's frontmatter, and "every unrelated code change made an installed skill look outdated". The plan's review also found that the draft's skill-drift check rendered the guide and "could not meet its tier's budget" (§12.3); comparing a stamp is the fix.
- **M4-D8 (context): how a skill gets installed.** `install-skill` writes `<DIR>/SKILL.md` through fsx under the global lock, records a `skill` settings history line with `dir`, never writes through a symlinked `SKILL.md`, and keeps no undo (the file is derived). Nothing recommends installing the skill unasked, and there is no remove command: deleting the folder is the removal. "The doctor checks an installed skill for drift only, never a missing one."
- **M4-D47: fixtures are Rust, in `tests/doctor/`, and coverage is bidirectional.** Each failure mode has a fixture: a type implementing `Fixture` in `tests/doctor/fixtures/<fm_id>.rs` with a deterministic `corrupt`, `assert_healthy`, `subject` and a doc comment that is its README; a coverage test asserts `set(fixers) == set(fixtures that declare a fixer)` and that every detector has a fixture. *Rejected:* `corrupt.sh`/`assert.sh` per failure mode (a second test language, and scripts that must clean up after themselves).
- **M4-D29 and the tier contract (§6.13):** one detector registry serves `doctor`, `doctor health` and `status`, by tier. The `cached` tier may read "exactly what `status --cached` reads today (records, the cached discovery, journals, the lock probe, the projections, the widget's files), plus single-file `stat`s and reads of at most `SKILL_DIRS_MAX` skill files. No directory walk, no BugGrabber read, no history read beyond the projection, no render of the guide." Its budget is its share of `status --cached`'s 5 ms.
- **M4-D43: incomplete coverage is never healthy.** A detector that cannot finish returns what it found plus an `incomplete` record, which E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, the doctor runtime) turns into `fm-state_files-check-incomplete`, so the run is never `DONE_OK`.
- **M4-D42: evidence never holds file content.** Paths, digests, modes, counts and reasons only.
- **M4-D30: instance keys.** `instance = <fm-id>@<target key | machine>[:<discriminator>]`, the discriminator a canonical resource key; a skill finding is `fm-plugins-skill-version-drift@machine:path=<file>`, so two skill roots are two instances (E3's `--since` relies on it).
- **M4-D40 (context): `doctor_refused`.** Exit 4, not retryable, `details.reason` from the closed set `force_required`, `fixer_conflict`, `too_many_actions`, `over_budget`, `filesystem_mismatch`, `client_running`, `not_enabled`, `edited_locally`. `edited_locally` exists for this leaf.

A skill changed between the preview and the run therefore stales the run, and a skill that became edited is no longer planned.

**How it serves the vision.** G4, agent ergonomics ("the first command an agent guesses works"): an agent's first guesses come from the skill it loaded, so an outdated skill makes the agent's first guess wrong; keeping it current keeps the guide's promise. G7, "`doctor` follows the world-class doctor contract": a precise detector with evidence, a consented, backed-up, undoable fixer, a fixture, and a manual path where a repair would overwrite a person's work. The thesis, that omaddons stays the sole, safe, undoable authority over what it manages: the doctor rewrites only the file omaddons itself installed and can prove unedited, and never writes through a link or over a person's edit.

## Technical Approach

### 1. The folders the check follows (part 1, `src/doctor/view.rs`)

E2's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.2`, the tolerant view) Skill layer holds one entry. It becomes the list of every skill omaddons installed, bounded:

```rust
pub struct SkillLayer {
    /// `Paths::skill_dir()` first, then `history_tail.skill_dirs[]` newest first; each folder
    /// once (compared by canonical path); at most `SKILL_DIRS_MAX` folders in all.
    pub files: Vec<SkillFile>,
    pub coverage: SkillCoverage,
}
pub struct SkillFile {
    pub dir: PathBuf,   // canonical when the folder exists, else as given
    pub file: PathBuf,  // dir.join("SKILL.md")
    pub read: SkillRead,
}
pub enum SkillRead {
    Missing,
    Bytes(Vec<u8>),
    TooLarge { len: u64 },
    NotAFile,
    /// `SKILL.md` is a symlink (never written through): its text as `read_link` gives it,
    /// and what reading through it found.
    Symlink { link_target: PathBuf, through: BoundedRead },
    Unreadable { kind: std::io::ErrorKind },
}
pub enum SkillCoverage {
    Complete,
    /// A further installed folder exists beyond the bound (the first one not read).
    Overflow { first_unread: PathBuf },
    /// `history.jsonl` exists, but the projection that lists the folders is missing, stale,
    /// newer than this build, or lacks `skill_dirs` (an older build rewrote it).
    ProjectionUnavailable,
}
impl DoctorView { pub fn skill(&self) -> Option<&SkillLayer>; } // always Some: the layer never fails
```

How it loads (once, lazily, like every layer; no write):

1. **The projection.** `history_tail::fresh(&paths)`. If it is `Some` and `skill_dirs()` is `Some(list)`, the installed folders are `list`. Otherwise, if `paths.history_file()` does not exist (one `stat`), no skill line was ever written and the list is empty (`Complete`). Otherwise the list is unknown: `ProjectionUnavailable`, and only the default folder is read.
2. **The candidates.** `Paths::skill_dir()` first (it always takes a slot, as E5's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`, the repair transaction) `with_skill_dirs` counts it), then the projection's folders in order. Canonicalize each existing folder (`std::fs::canonicalize`; a missing one keeps its spelling: it holds no file, so its spelling decides nothing) and drop duplicates, so a symlinked home or two `--dir` spellings of one folder count once.
3. **The bound.** Keep the first `SKILL_DIRS_MAX` candidates. If a further candidate exists and its `SKILL.md` exists (one `symlink_metadata`), the coverage is `Overflow { first_unread }`. With the projection bounded to `SKILL_DIRS_MAX`, only one candidate can be left over, so at most one extra `stat` happens.
4. **The reads.** For each kept folder, B3's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3`, `robot-docs install-skill`) `read_skill_file(<dir>/SKILL.md)`, which never follows a symlink, never opens a FIFO and never reads more than `DISCOVERY_FILE_MAX_BYTES` bytes; an I/O error becomes `Unreadable { kind }`. For a `Symlink { link_target }`, also E2's `read_bounded(<dir>/SKILL.md, DISCOVERY_FILE_MAX_BYTES)`, which reads through the link with the same bound and FIFO safety, into `through`.

So the layer reads at most `SKILL_DIRS_MAX` skill files, plus the projection `status --cached` already reads: exactly the `cached` tier's allowance. The accessor's type changes from E2's `Option<&[SkillFile]>` to `Option<&SkillLayer>`; update E2's `skill_layer_outcomes` test and every caller in the same commit.

Decided while writing this bead: **the default folder always counts, and at most `SKILL_DIRS_MAX` folders are followed in all**, because the plan says the detector reads "at most `SKILL_DIRS_MAX` files", because E5's `ScopeTable::with_skill_dirs` admits that many counting the default (so every finding is repairable in one run), and because the extra folder is only possible when someone installed into eight other folders that all still exist; then the check says it is incomplete rather than skipping one silently (common rule 15).

Decided while writing this bead: **an unknown folder list is incomplete coverage**, not "only the default is known" (the reading B3's bead gives its readers), because G-M4-4 and M4-D43 forbid reporting incomplete coverage as healthy and the cached tier may not read the history itself. It happens only after the projection was deleted with the cache, or rewritten by an older build, and the next change command rebuilds it (`rebuild_if_stale`). A home with no `history.jsonl` has no skill lines, so its coverage is complete. Test homes built through the binary always have a fresh projection; a test that writes `history.jsonl` by hand and then expects a clean `doctor` must run a mutating command (or `history_tail::rebuild_if_stale`) first.

### 2. The classification (part 1, `src/doctor/detectors/plugins.rs`)

One pure function implements this leaf's column of B3's table, so `install-skill` and the doctor can never disagree about a file:

```rust
pub(crate) enum SkillState {
    Absent,                                         // no finding
    Current,                                        // no finding
    Outdated { digest: [u8; 32] },                  // drift: auto-fixable
    Edited { claimed: Option<[u8; 32]>, cause: EditedCause }, // Changed | Unstamped | TooLarge
    Symlink { link_target: PathBuf, through: Box<SkillState> }, // through is never Absent or Current
    NotAFile,
    Unreadable { kind: std::io::ErrorKind },
}
pub(crate) fn classify(read: &SkillRead, expected_hex: &str) -> SkillState;
```

| `SkillRead` | `inspect` (B3) | State |
|---|---|---|
| `Missing` | | `Absent` (a deleted skill, or a folder that never held one) |
| `Bytes` | `Stamped`, pristine, `hex(digest) == expected` | `Current`, whatever build wrote it |
| `Bytes` | `Stamped`, pristine, another digest | `Outdated` |
| `Bytes` | `Stamped`, not pristine, `hex(claimed) == expected` | `Current` (an edited copy of this build's guide) |
| `Bytes` | `Stamped`, not pristine, another claim | `Edited { claimed: Some, Changed }` |
| `Bytes` | `Unstamped` | `Edited { claimed: None, Unstamped }` |
| `TooLarge` | | `Edited { claimed: None, TooLarge }` (never a guide; never read past the bound) |
| `NotAFile` | | `NotAFile` |
| `Unreadable { kind }` | | `Unreadable { kind }` |
| `Symlink { through }` | the same rules on `through` | `Current` or `Absent` (a dangling link: `Unreadable { NotFound }`) when the target is; otherwise `Symlink { link_target, through: <the target's state> }` |

`expected_hex` is `contract::guide::EXPECTED_DIGEST` in production; tests pass others. The function never renders the guide.

Decided while writing this bead: **an edited copy of this build's guide is not a finding**, because M4-D50 reports an edited skill only "if its stamp also differs from the binary's": there is no newer guide to offer, and a finding the user cannot clear without undoing their own edit would make `doctor` and `health` permanently unhealthy. Once omaddons ships another guide, the same file's claim differs from the binary's and it is reported as edited.

Decided while writing this bead: **a symlinked `SKILL.md` is read through (bounded, FIFO-safe) and reported only when what it points to is not this build's guide**; a dangling link is not a finding (as a deleted folder is not). The link is never written through, and its finding is always manual, with prose advice. Reason: M4-D8 calls a symlinked `SKILL.md` common in dotfiles setups, `install-skill` refuses it, so its owner keeps the target current by hand; reporting a link to the current guide would be a finding its owner can never clear, the nag M4-D8 refuses for a missing skill. The cached tier's allowance ("reads of at most `SKILL_DIRS_MAX` skill files") covers one read through a link. B3's bead says in passing that this leaf reports such a link unconditionally; the doctor's column of that table is this leaf's to define, and the close comment records the choice.

Decided while writing this bead: **a `SKILL.md` that is a directory, FIFO, socket or device, or that cannot be read, is a manual finding** (`not_a_file`, `unreadable`), never silence, because no agent can load such a skill and the check cannot prove it current; and never a rewrite, because the doctor cannot know what it would replace.
