**One observation per finding state** (`Absent` and `Current` give none). Every observation: `subject = Subject::machine().path(&file)`, so `instance = fm-plugins-skill-version-drift@machine:path=<file>` and `label = machine · <file>`; `confidence: high` (a stamp comparison is exact); `addon` and `folder` `null`. The digest strings use `capabilities.guide_digest`'s form, `sha256:<64 hex>`.

| State | Title | Evidence | Fixable (part 2) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Outdated` | "The installed agent skill carries another guide than this binary's" | `{path, observed: sha256:<its digest>, expected: sha256:<EXPECTED_DIGEST>, reason: "outdated", edited: false}` | yes |
| `Edited { Changed }` | "The installed agent skill was edited by hand, and its guide is not this binary's" | `{path, observed: sha256:<the stamp's claim>, expected, reason: "edited", edited: true}` | no |
| `Edited { Unstamped }` | "The installed agent skill has no guide stamp, so it was changed by hand" | `{path, expected, reason: "unstamped", edited: true}` | no |
| `Edited { TooLarge }` | "The installed agent skill is larger than any guide, so it was changed by hand" | `{path, expected, reason: "too_large", edited: true}` | no |
| `Symlink` | "The installed agent skill is a symbolic link to a file that is not this binary's guide" | `{path, link_target?, observed?: the target's digest or claim, expected, reason: "symlink", edited?: false for an outdated target, true for an edited one, absent otherwise}` | no |
| `NotAFile` | "The installed agent skill's SKILL.md is not a regular file" | `{path, expected, reason: "not_a_file"}` | no |
| `Unreadable` | "The installed agent skill cannot be read" | `{path, expected, reason: "unreadable"}` | no |

- **Two new optional `Evidence` keys** (E1's struct, appended at its end, omitted when `None`, each with a doc comment for A3's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`, schemas and the rule test) rule test): `edited: Option<bool>` (the plan's `evidence.edited`) and `link_target: Option<PathBuf>` (the link's text as `read_link` gives it, relative or absolute). `link_target` is left out when recording it would fail `Evidence::is_private_safe` (a target below a `WTF/`), so the finding stays private on every channel. No evidence key holds a byte of the file (M4-D42).
- **`reason`** uses E1's existing `reason` key with the closed values `outdated`, `edited`, `unstamped`, `too_large`, `symlink`, `not_a_file`, `unreadable`.

Decided while writing this bead: the instance titles above. The plan's example (§4.3) says "carries an older guide than this binary's"; a digest cannot tell older from newer (a newer build may have written the skill before a downgrade), so the title says "another".

**The manual remediation** (`skill_manual(finding) -> Remediation`, the row's `manual` builder):

| `evidence.reason` | `command` / `argv` |
|---|---|
| `outdated`, `edited`, `unstamped`, `too_large` | `omaddons robot-docs install-skill --dir <dir>` (argv; `destructive: false`): B3's command replaces a pristine file and keeps any other as `SKILL.md.bak` |
| `symlink` | prose, `argv: null`: "SKILL.md is a symbolic link, and omaddons never writes through one: update the file it points to with this build's guide (the robot-docs guide command prints it), or replace the link with a regular file and run the fix again" |
| `not_a_file` | prose: "SKILL.md is not a regular file, so no agent can load it: move it out of the folder, then install the skill there again with robot-docs install-skill" |
| `unreadable` | prose: "omaddons cannot read SKILL.md: give your user read access to it, then run the doctor again" |

`explain_command`/`explain_argv` are E1's (`omaddons doctor explain fm-plugins-skill-version-drift`, no `-t`: the finding is machine-level, and `-t` never hides it, §6.11). Decided while writing this bead: `--dir <dir>` even for the default folder, so one argv shape serves every instance, and `install-skill --dir <the default folder>` writes exactly what the bare command writes.

**The detector** (`detectors::plugins::skill_version_drift(view, selection, budget) -> Detected`): one observation per finding state, in the layer's order; `incomplete` from the coverage (section 4). It walks nothing and makes no request, so it never charges its `Budget`. It sits beside F7's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.7`, plugins, secrets and the network) widget detectors in `plugins.rs` (create the file if F7 has not): add functions, never edit F7's.

### 5. The fixer (part 2, `src/doctor/fixers/rewrite.rs`)

```rust
pub(crate) fn plan(view: &DoctorView, finding: &Finding) -> Result<Vec<Fix>, Refusal>;
```

Called by the planner of E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`, `doctor fix`) for each planned finding, both in the preview and again under the lock from a fresh view (M4-D45):

1. Find the layer entry whose `file` equals `finding.evidence.path`. None (the folder is no longer followed), or a state that is now `Absent` or `Current`: `Ok(vec![])`, nothing to do for this instance (E6's verify then finds it gone).
2. `Outdated`: render `contract::guide::render_guide()`. A render error, or a rendered guide whose `hex(digest_without_stamp(..))` differs from `EXPECTED_DIGEST`, is `Refusal { reason: NotEnabled, .. }` with prose "this omaddons build cannot produce the guide it was built with; rebuild it after regenerating skills/omaddons/SKILL.md" (a build whose committed guide is stale, which the gate rejects; writing it would leave a file the detector still calls outdated). Otherwise `Ok(vec![Fix::Write { path: <file>, content: <rendered bytes>, mode: <0644 as E1's Mode> }])` (`Mode::new` returns an `Option`; use a constant built once).
3. Every other state: `Refusal { reason: EditedLocally, message, path: <file>, fix }`: the message names the file and why ("<file> was edited by hand", "… is a symbolic link", "… is not a regular file", "… cannot be read"), and `fix` is the instance's manual remediation (section 3: the `install-skill --dir` argv, or the prose).

**Its `FixerSpec`:** `writes_to: [Skill]`, `ops: [Write]`, `enabled: true`, `needs_force: false`, `cardinality: Low` (at most `SKILL_DIRS_MAX` files, within Low's ten paths), `preconditions: [LockHeld]`. No `ClientNotRunning`: no client is involved.

- **Mode 0644**, `install-skill`'s mode (§6.3.3: "The file is 0644, readable as any skill is"); E5 records the old mode in `pre`, so the undo restores bytes and mode. Decided while writing this bead.
- **The write path** is the canonical `<dir>/SKILL.md`. A symlinked skill **folder** (not file) is followed to where it points, as `install-skill` does; only a symlinked final component is refused (by the classification first, and by fsx as the backstop).
- **The repair, through E5 and E6, unchanged:** one `WriteFile` primitive per skill, a reserved backup `<run>/backups/<seq>` holding the replaced bytes verbatim, `pre` = `File { sha256, mode }` of the outdated file, `post` = `File { sha256, mode: 0644 }` of the guide, a journaled step, a `kind: repair` history line (`target: null`, `targets: []`) with the primitives in `repairs[]`. A file changed between the plan and its write fails its `pre` predicate, and the repair rolls back: the doctor never writes over a change it did not plan.
- **The skill folders the commit may write:** E6's planner passes the view's followed folders (`view.skill()`'s `dir`s) as E5's `LowerCtx.skill_dirs`, and the commit's scope table applies `ScopeTable::with_skill_dirs` with the same list. If E6 passes only `Paths::skill_dir()`, change it here. Recovery and undo admit exactly these folders (the rule of E5 and of E7, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7`, the undo of repairs: the default, or listed in `history_tail.skill_dirs[]`), so a crashed rewrite of a `--dir` skill recovers.
- **`Refusal`'s fix and keys.** E6's `PlanRefusal::Fixer` reports "`fm` and the refusal's keys" and "the refusal's own fix". If E1's `Refusal` still has only `reason` and `message` on `main`, add `path: Option<PathBuf>` (written as `details.path`) and `fix: Option<Suggestion>` (the error's `fix` and, for an argv, `fix_argv`), make `PlanRefusal::Fixer`'s `into_error` use them (keeping E6's default when absent), and declare `path` in `doctor_refused`'s `DetailSpec` (A9, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9`; declared additively).

So `doctor fix --only fm-plugins-skill-version-drift` on a home with an edited skill fails as:

```json
{"ok":false,"command":"doctor fix","exit_code":4,"state":"REFUSING",
 "error":{"code":"doctor_refused","message":"<skills>/SKILL.md was edited by hand; the doctor never overwrites it",
          "details":{"reason":"edited_locally","fm":"fm-plugins-skill-version-drift","path":"<skills>/SKILL.md"},
          "fix":"omaddons robot-docs install-skill --dir <skills>",
          "fix_argv":["omaddons","robot-docs","install-skill","--dir","<skills>"],"retryable":false}}
```

(paths shown with the plan's placeholder; real output prints them absolute), and a plain `doctor fix` never plans that instance: it lists it as manual.

E6 computes `auto_fixable` from "the detector's own verdict for the instance", and neither E1 nor E6 defines how a detector states it. If E6 or F2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.2`, the journal fixers) has already added the mechanism on `main`, use it. Otherwise add it here:

### 9. What not to do

- Never render the guide in the detector or the layer (the `cached` tier forbids it; a test scans for it).
- Never read the whole history from the detector; never derive the folder list from the projection's `lines` (they are trimmed; B3).
- Never write through a symlinked `SKILL.md`, never rewrite an edited, unstamped, oversized, non-regular or unreadable file, and never delete anything (a repair only writes, with a backup).
- Never report a missing skill or a deleted folder, and never recommend installing the skill.
- Never put a byte of the file into evidence, a message or a log line.
- Never classify a file with code other than B3's `inspect` and this leaf's `classify`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A skill with another guide digest (pristine, stamp ≠ `EXPECTED_DIGEST`) is reported as `fm-plugins-skill-version-drift` (P3, `reason: outdated`, `edited: false`, `auto_fixable: true`), and `doctor fix` rewrites it with this build's guide: the run ends `DONE_OK` (its verify step finds nothing), the file equals `robot-docs guide`'s bytes with mode 0644, and `<run>/backups/<seq>` holds the replaced bytes verbatim, so F9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`, the safety harness) can round-trip it byte for byte.
- [ ] A skill with this binary's guide digest, whatever build wrote it (different metadata, copied by hand, rendered with another build id and crate version), is not a finding; neither is an edited copy of this build's guide.
- [ ] An edited skill (bytes that no longer match their own stamp, with a stamp that differs from the binary's; or no stamp; or larger than any guide) is reported with `edited: true`, `auto_fixable: false` and the remediation `omaddons robot-docs install-skill --dir <dir>`; a plain `doctor fix` leaves it untouched, and `doctor fix --only fm-plugins-skill-version-drift` refuses with `doctor_refused`, `details.reason: edited_locally`, `details.path`, and that remediation as its fix.
- [ ] A deleted skill folder (the default or a `--dir` one) is not a finding.
- [ ] A symlinked `SKILL.md` is never written through: one whose target is not this build's guide is reported (`reason: symlink`) with prose advice and is refused by the fixer; one pointing at this build's guide, or dangling, is not a finding.
- [ ] A `SKILL.md` that is not a regular file, or cannot be read, is a manual finding with prose advice, never rewritten.
- [ ] The check follows `<skills>` and every folder `history_tail.skill_dirs[]` names, at most `SKILL_DIRS_MAX` in all counting the default; a further installed folder, or a folder list that cannot be known while history exists, yields `fm-state_files-check-incomplete` (`limit: skill_dirs` or `history_projection`), never a clean result.
- [ ] The detector never renders the guide, reads at most `SKILL_DIRS_MAX` skill files, and its evidence never holds file content.
- [ ] The `cached`-tier detector stays inside `status --cached`'s budget with `SKILL_DIRS_MAX` skills installed: the skill layer plus the detector run under 1 ms (median of 21, release build).
- [ ] A skill changed between `doctor fix --dry-run` and `doctor fix --if-match <token>` makes the bound run `plan_stale` with nothing written; a skill edited while the repair runs fails its step's `pre` predicate and the repair rolls back, leaving the edit.
- [ ] `--since` compares two skill roots as two instances; `doctor explain` answers by the id and by an instance key.
- [ ] The fixture `tests/doctor/fixtures/fm_plugins_skill_version_drift.rs` exists (`fixer() == true`, doc comment as README), is in `fixtures::all()`, and its `corrupt`, `assert_healthy` and `subject` hold.
- [ ] Rule 19: the `FAILURE_MODES` row, the fixture, README's doctor-table row, and the Appendix B line in the close comment; the invariant test of E1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`, the registry) passes.
- [ ] README's doctor table and `robot-docs install-skill` section, and the `install-skill` help, are updated in the commits that ship the behaviour; the snapshots that list failure modes are re-accepted after review.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes for each commit; `ubs` is clean on the changed files.
- [ ] The close comment lists every new or changed wire name (section 8), the Appendix B line, states that this leaf adds no command path (common rule 16: the rewrite runs inside `doctor fix`, which binds), and confirms or adjusts every "Decided while writing this bead" item; `br lint` is clean for this bead and its subtasks.

- **Risk #3, doctor false positives** (likelihood M, impact M): the stamp comparison is exact; a current skill is never stale whatever build wrote it; an edited copy of the current guide, a symlink to the current guide and a deleted folder are not findings; the fixture's clean counterpart and the no-false-positive property of F9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`) on `common::realistic_home()` (which installs no skill) hold it; H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the checkpoint) reviews every real-home finding. The checkpoint's real-machine install goes to a scratch folder that is deleted afterwards (the decision of B3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3`), which this check never reports.
- **Risk #4, `status --cached` slows past 5 ms** (M, M): the tier contract; no render; at most `SKILL_DIRS_MAX` bounded reads of guide-sized files (about 30 KiB each) and one projection `status --cached` already loads; the 1 ms share measured here, the whole budget measured by the test of F8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.8`), whose perf home should install `SKILL_DIRS_MAX` skills.
- **Risk #21, fences scoped wrong** (context): a stuck skill rewrite fences only that skill file (E14, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14`, fences and barriers, tests it); the rewrite's resources are exactly the file and its backup.
- **The committed guide must be current.** The detector compares with `EXPECTED_DIGEST` (the committed file's digest at build time) and the fixer writes `render_guide()`. They agree whenever the gate passes; in a development build with a stale `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` the fixer refuses (`not_enabled`) rather than write a file the detector would still call outdated.
- **A symlinked skill folder is followed** (a folder, not the file): the rewrite then lands in the folder it points to, as `install-skill` writes there, with a backup and undo. Only a symlinked `SKILL.md` is refused.
- **What could go wrong in implementation, and how to notice:** a second copy of the stamp rules (the unit tests compare with the renderer of B1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`, and B3's inspector, so a re-implementation that disagrees fails); a folder list compared by spelling (the two-spellings case); a fixer that writes a folder recovery would not admit (the crash scenario on a `--dir` folder); evidence that leaks file text (the marker test); collateral `check-incomplete` findings in other suites whose homes write `history.jsonl` by hand (fix those homes, not this check).
- **Hot spots:** `src/doctor/view.rs` (E2's, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.2`; F3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.3`), F5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.5`), F6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.6`) and F7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.7`) also extend layers: change only the Skill layer), `src/doctor/registry.rs` (every F leaf inserts rows: insert where the id sorts, rebase), `src/doctor/detectors/plugins.rs` (shared with F7: add functions only), `src/doctor/finding.rs` (append evidence keys), `src/doctor/fix.rs` (E6's, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`; F2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.2`, the journal fixers) may also extend `remediation_for`: whichever lands second merges), `src/error.rs` (append the `DetailSpec` key), `tests/common/doctor.rs` and `tests/doctor/fixtures/mod.rs` (append), `tests/contract/matrix.rs` (append rows, one snapshot file each), `README.md` (own rows and sentence only), `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` (regenerate after rebasing if the skill test asks, never merge by hand).
- **Compatibility.** An older build ignores the new row and evidence keys. The rewrite's journal and history line are the formats of E5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`), which the M3 build does not list (E9, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9`, the M3 build against M4 state, characterizes it). An M3 build that rewrites the projection drops `skill_dirs`, which this check reports as incomplete until the next change command.
- **Privacy.** Skill files live under the home, never under a `WTF/`; evidence holds paths, digests and reasons only; a link target below a `WTF/` is not recorded.
- **Why size S.** One detector over one layer, one single-primitive fixer, one fixture, on machinery the doctor core (E1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`) to E6) and the guide chain (B1 to B3) already built.
- **Critical path.** Slack 2; the computed lanes place it at t = 12–13, before F8 (13–15).

## Dependencies

Parent: the F area epic `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6` (the doctor's catalog).

**Blocked by:**

**Unblocks:**

acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] A skill with another guide digest (pristine, stamp ≠ `EXPECTED_DIGEST`) is reported as `fm-plugins-skill-version-drift` (P3, `reason: outdated`, `edited: false`, `auto_fixable: true`), and `doctor fix` rewrites it with this build's guide: the run ends `DONE_OK` (its verify step finds nothing), the file equals `robot-docs guide`'s bytes with mode 0644, and `<run>/backups/<seq>` holds the replaced bytes verbatim, so F9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`, the safety harness) can round-trip it byte for byte.
- [ ] A skill with this binary's guide digest, whatever build wrote it (different metadata, copied by hand, rendered with another build id and crate version), is not a finding; neither is an edited copy of this build's guide.
- [ ] An edited skill (bytes that no longer match their own stamp, with a stamp that differs from the binary's; or no stamp; or larger than any guide) is reported with `edited: true`, `auto_fixable: false` and the remediation `omaddons robot-docs install-skill --dir <dir>`; a plain `doctor fix` leaves it untouched, and `doctor fix --only fm-plugins-skill-version-drift` refuses with `doctor_refused`, `details.reason: edited_locally`, `details.path`, and that remediation as its fix.
- [ ] A deleted skill folder (the default or a `--dir` one) is not a finding.
- [ ] A symlinked `SKILL.md` is never written through: one whose target is not this build's guide is reported (`reason: symlink`) with prose advice and is refused by the fixer; one pointing at this build's guide, or dangling, is not a finding.
- [ ] A `SKILL.md` that is not a regular file, or cannot be read, is a manual finding with prose advice, never rewritten.
- [ ] The check follows `<skills>` and every folder `history_tail.skill_dirs[]` names, at most `SKILL_DIRS_MAX` in all counting the default; a further installed folder, or a folder list that cannot be known while history exists, yields `fm-state_files-check-incomplete` (`limit: skill_dirs` or `history_projection`), never a clean result.
- [ ] The detector never renders the guide, reads at most `SKILL_DIRS_MAX` skill files, and its evidence never holds file content.
- [ ] The `cached`-tier detector stays inside `status --cached`'s budget with `SKILL_DIRS_MAX` skills installed: the skill layer plus the detector run under 1 ms (median of 21, release build).

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M4 plan, 2026-10-24).**

**Why this bead.** M4 turns the agent guide into a skill that coding agents load (B3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3`, `robot-docs install-skill`). An installed skill is a copy: the day a newer omaddons ships a different guide, every installed copy starts teaching agents commands, codes and rules the binary may no longer have, and nothing says so. After this bead, `omaddons doctor` reports such a skill as `fm-plugins-skill-version-drift` (P3, `cached`, Appendix B row 40), and `omaddons doctor fix` rewrites it with this build's guide inside an ordinary repair transaction, keeping the replaced file as a verbatim backup so the repair can be undone. A skill someone edited, linked or broke is reported with the command or advice to fix it by hand and is never overwritten. It is the vision's own `skill-version-drift` failure mode, and the one plugin-subsystem drift the doctor repairs itself.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M4-D50:** drift of the skill is repaired, drift of the widget only reported. The check follows `Paths::skill_dir()` and every folder in `history_tail.skill_dirs[]`, compares the stamp on the line after the frontmatter with `OMADDONS_GUIDE_SHA256` without rendering, treats a stamp equal to the binary's as current whatever build wrote it, leaves an edited skill to the user (`edited: true`, `edited_locally`), never writes through a symlink, and ignores a deleted folder.
- **M4-D7:** the guide's identity is its content digest after the frontmatter, independent of the build id, and the binary knows its expected digest without rendering; that is what makes the check exact and cheap.
- **M4-D8 (context):** how a skill is installed and recorded; nothing recommends installing one, and the doctor never reports a missing one.
- **M4-D47:** one Rust fixture per failure mode, with a fixer, so F9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`, the safety harness) can round-trip it.
- **M4-D29 and the `cached` tier contract:** at most `SKILL_DIRS_MAX` skill-file reads, no render, no history read beyond the projection, within `status --cached`'s 5 ms.
- **M4-D43:** a folder list that is cut short or unknown is reported as incomplete, never as clean. **M4-D42:** evidence holds paths, digests and reasons, never file text. **M4-D30:** one instance per `SKILL.md`. **M4-D40:** `doctor_refused`'s `edited_locally` and `not_enabled`.

**Alternatives rejected that matter here.**
- A stamp holding the version and build id (the reviewed draft's): every unrelated code change would make every skill look outdated, it had no regeneration fixed point, and as the first line it broke the skill's frontmatter (M4-D7).
- Rendering the guide in the detector (the reviewed draft's check): it could not meet the `cached` budget (§12.3).
- Finding the installed folders by scanning the history tail's runs: old installs fall out of the tail; the projection keeps them (M4-D50).
- Rewriting an edited skill with a backup: the doctor would overwrite a person's work without asking; `install-skill --dir <dir>` is the consented path and keeps the edited copy as `SKILL.md.bak`.
- Writing through a symlinked `SKILL.md`: fsx forbids it, and the target may be a dotfiles repository.
- Reporting a missing skill or suggesting an install: a finding nobody can dismiss (M4-D8).
- Doctor-driven widget reinstalls (the contrast in M4-D50): subprocesses outside the doctor's safety envelope.

**Choices made while writing the bead** (each marked in the body, to confirm or adjust in the close comment): three subtasks for this size-S feature leaf (detector, fixer, tests); an edited copy of the current guide, a symlink to the current guide and a dangling link are not findings; a non-regular or unreadable `SKILL.md` is a manual finding; at most `SKILL_DIRS_MAX` folders followed counting the default, with `check-incomplete` (`skill_dirs`, `history_projection`) for an overflow or an unknown list; evidence keys `edited` and `link_target`; the instance titles ("another guide", not "older"); the fixer's mode 0644 and its `not_enabled` refusal when the build's guide does not match its expected digest; `Refusal` carrying a file and a fix; the per-instance `fixable` verdict if E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`, `doctor fix`) or F2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.2`, the journal fixers) has not added one; the 1 ms share of `status --cached`'s budget.

**Risks and how they are watched.**
- Risk #3, doctor false positives: exact stamp comparison; the current-skill cases (other metadata, copied by hand, rendered with another build id, edited copy of the current guide, link to the current guide, deleted folder) are tests; F9's no-false-positive home; H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the checkpoint) reviews every real-home finding.
- Risk #4, `status --cached` slows past 5 ms: no render, no walk, bounded reads; the release-build measurement here (under 1 ms with `SKILL_DIRS_MAX` skills) and the whole-budget test of F8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.8`, `status` on the registry).
- Risk #21, fences scoped wrong (context): a stuck rewrite fences only its skill file and backup (a case of E14, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14`, fences and barriers).
- A fixer that writes a guide the detector still calls outdated (a stale committed `SKILL.md` in a development build): the fixer checks the rendered digest against `EXPECTED_DIGEST` and refuses.
- A crashed rewrite in a `--dir` folder that recovery would not admit: the crash scenario on such a folder.

**What it unblocks, and why they wait.** F8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.8`, `status` on the registry) moves `status` onto every `cached` and `quick` row, and this row is `cached` ("C (machine)"), so `status` and `doctor` agree on skills only once it exists. F9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`, the safety harness) needs this fixer and its fixture for the undo round trip, the crash boundaries, concurrency and the declared pair with the credential mode. T4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4`, slice 3 end to end) records slice 3's demo once every slice-3 leaf has closed.

**How it serves the milestone.** G-M4-4: one more failure mode named with evidence, repaired by a consented, backed-up, undoable command, proven by a fixture, never reported clean when its coverage is incomplete. G-M4-1: the installed skill stays the guide, so an agent's first guesses stay right. G-M4-6: the rewrite is an ordinary repair transaction through fsx. Checkpoint criteria 3 (the doctor bullet), 9 (the fixture and its properties) and 12 (`status` agreement and the 5 ms budget).

**The M4 plan's entry for F10, verbatim (M4 plan, 2026-10-24).** This is the M4 plan's entry, lines 4666–4684 of the plan, kept as provenance. The description above is the authoritative, elaborated version; where they differ, the description was decided while filing and says why.

#### F10 Skill drift
- **Type** feature · **P2** · **size-S** · **slice-3**
- **Blocked by:** B3, E6.
- **Unblocks:** F8, F9.
- **Background.** M4-D50, Appendix B row 40. A separate leaf, so that the guide chain (A3 → A5 → B1 → B3) stays off the doctor's critical path.
- **Technical approach.**
  1. `fm-plugins-skill-version-drift` (`cached`) reads the `SKILL.md` at `Paths::skill_dir()` and at each `history_tail.skill_dirs[]` entry (B3), at most `SKILL_DIRS_MAX` files.
  2. It finds the stamp on the line after each file's frontmatter (`<!-- omaddons guide sha256:<hex> -->`, M4-D7) and hashes the file with that line omitted. If the hash equals the stamp and the stamp differs from `OMADDONS_GUIDE_SHA256` (B1), the skill is outdated: drift. A stamp equal to the binary's is current, whatever build wrote it. It never renders the guide, so it fits the `cached` budget.
  3. A file whose bytes no longer match its own stamp was edited locally: the finding carries `evidence.edited: true`, and the fixer refuses that instance (`edited_locally`), making it manual (`robot-docs install-skill --dir <dir>`, which keeps a backup). A file with no stamp line is treated the same way. A symlinked `SKILL.md` is reported with prose advice and never written through.
  4. Its fixer, `fixers/rewrite.rs`, does a `Write` of the current guide with a verbatim backup through the Skill row, which admits `Writer::Doctor`. The scope table holds every skill directory involved (`with_skill_dirs`, E5). It adds fixtures: drifted, edited, symlinked, and current-but-from-another-build.
- **Acceptance criteria.**
  - A skill with another guide digest is reported and rewritten; the verify step passes (F9 round-trips it byte for byte).
  - A skill with this binary's guide digest, written by another build, is not a finding.
  - An edited skill is reported as edited and is not rewritten by `doctor fix`.
  - A deleted skill directory is not a finding.
  - The `cached`-tier detector stays inside `status --cached`'s budget with `SKILL_DIRS_MAX` skills installed.
- **Test plan.** Fixture. F9.
- **Considerations.** None.

title: The skill layer follows every installed skill, and the drift detector
description:
Part 1 of 3 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.10 (Skill drift). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

**The leaf.** F10 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.10`, skill drift) adds the doctor's check and repair for an installed agent skill that has gone out of date. B3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3`, `robot-docs install-skill`) installs the agent guide as `SKILL.md` into `<skills>` (`$HOME/.claude/skills/omaddons`) or any folder given with `--dir`, byte-identical to the guide this build renders. When a newer omaddons ships a different guide, every installed copy teaches agents commands, codes and rules this build may not have. The failure mode is `fm-plugins-skill-version-drift` (Appendix B row 40, P3, `cached` tier); its fixer (part 2) rewrites an outdated skill with a verbatim backup and leaves every skill a person edited, linked or broke to that person. It serves G-M4-4 ("`omaddons doctor` names every broken state omaddons can detect in what it owns or manages … incomplete coverage is never reported as healthy") and checkpoint criterion 3 ("`doctor` reports an installed skill whose guide digest differs from this binary's, never one that differs only by build").

**This part** is the read side: the doctor's view learns every folder the skill was installed into, reads each `SKILL.md` within the `cached` tier's allowance, classifies it by its stamp without rendering the guide, and the registry row reports what it finds, each finding with a manual remediation. It is its own step because it is complete and useful alone (the findings and their reinstall command work before any fixer exists), and because the fixer (part 2) is planned from exactly this layer and this classification.

**The decisions it obeys** (restated; the full log is in the decision-log comments on the milestone epic `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`):
- **M4-D50.** The detector looks at `Paths::skill_dir()` and each folder in `history_tail.skill_dirs[]` (B3's projection field: every folder a `skill` history line names, newest first, bounded to `SKILL_DIRS_MAX`; "the projection keeps them however old the install is, which a scan of the history tail's runs would not"). It reads each file and hashes it with the stamp line omitted; if the hash equals the stamp and the stamp differs from this binary's `OMADDONS_GUIDE_SHA256`, the skill is outdated. "A skill whose stamp equals the binary's is current, whatever build wrote it, so unrelated code changes never make a skill look stale. The `cached` tier never renders the guide." A locally edited skill (bytes that no longer match their own stamp) is never rewritten: "if its stamp also differs from the binary's, the finding is reported with `evidence.edited: true`", and its remediation is `omaddons robot-docs install-skill --dir <dir>`. A symlinked `SKILL.md` is never written through and is reported with prose advice. "A skill directory that no longer exists is not a finding: the user deleted it."
- **M4-D7.** The stamp is the line right after the YAML frontmatter, `<!-- omaddons guide sha256:<hex> -->`; the digest covers the document with that one line omitted; the guide embeds no build id or version. `build.rs` computes the committed guide's stamp-omitted digest into `OMADDONS_GUIDE_SHA256` (exposed as `contract::guide::EXPECTED_DIGEST`), so the binary knows its expected digest without rendering. *Rejected:* a build-id stamp ("every unrelated code change made an installed skill look outdated") and a check that renders the guide ("could not meet its tier's budget", the plan's review).
- **The `cached` tier (§6.13):** it may read what `status --cached` reads today (records, the cached discovery, journals, the lock probe, the projections, the widget's files) "plus single-file `stat`s and reads of at most `SKILL_DIRS_MAX` skill files. No directory walk, … no history read beyond the projection, no render of the guide."
- **M4-D43:** incomplete coverage is never healthy; a detector that cannot finish returns `incomplete`, which E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, the doctor runtime) turns into `fm-state_files-check-incomplete`. **M4-D42:** evidence never holds file content. **M4-D30:** `instance = <fm-id>@machine:path=<file>` here.
- **M4-D8 (context):** nothing recommends installing the skill unasked; the doctor never reports a missing skill.

**Facts this part relies on** (as of `c0ab5e9`, plus the blockers' beads; record any name that differs on `main` in the close comment):
- `Paths::skill_dir()` = `<home>/.claude/skills/omaddons` (`src/state/paths.rs:263-266`).
- `history_tail::fresh(paths)` (`src/state/history_tail.rs:126-133`) returns the projection only when it matches `history.jsonl`; `load` treats a missing, corrupt or newer file as none (`:331-336`); `rebuild_if_stale` runs after every mutating, non-dry-run command (`src/app/mod.rs:358-369`). B3 adds `skill_dirs: Option<Vec<PathBuf>>` (canonical folders, newest first, at most `SKILL_DIRS_MAX` = 8; `None` when an older build rewrote the file) and `HistoryTail::skill_dirs()`.
- B3's `read_skill_file(path) -> io::Result<SkillFile>` (`Missing`, `Symlink { link_target }`, `NotAFile`, `TooLarge { len }`, `Bytes`; never follows a symlink, never opens a FIFO, reads at most `DISCOVERY_FILE_MAX_BYTES` (1 MiB, `src/limits.rs:65`)) and `inspect(bytes) -> Stamp` (`Stamped { claimed, actual }` with `is_pristine()` and `digest()`, or `Unstamped`), in `contract::guide::stamp` or a sibling module. B3's table: "`Missing` → no finding (a deleted skill is not a finding); `Symlink` → reported with advice, never written; `NotAFile` → per F10; `TooLarge` → edited; `Bytes`, `Stamped`, pristine → drift if `digest() != EXPECTED_DIGEST`, else current; `Stamped`, not pristine, or `Unstamped` → edited." From B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`, the guide renderer): `stamp::hex(&[u8; 32]) -> String` and `EXPECTED_DIGEST: &str` (64 lowercase hex).
- E2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.2`, the tolerant view): `DoctorView::load_at(paths, opts)`, lazily loaded layers, `Layer::Skill`, the `skill()` accessor (today one entry, `SkillFile { dir, file, read: BoundedRead }`), and `read_bounded(path, max) -> BoundedRead` (`Missing`, `Bytes`, `TooLarge`, `NotAFile`, `Unreadable { kind }`; follows a symlink, a dangling one is `Unreadable { NotFound }`). E2 left the `skill_dirs[]` folders to "B3 or F10, whichever lands after"; B3 does not add them, so this part does.
- E1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`, the registry): `FailureMode` (`id, subsystem, severity, title, description, why, tier, online, cost_ms, requires, detect, fix, manual`), `Observation { subject, title, confidence, addon, folder, evidence }`, `Detected { found, incomplete }`, `Incomplete { limit: IncompleteLimit }` (`Deadline`, `Entries`, `OnlineRequests`), `Evidence` (one struct of optional keys, including `path`, `observed`, `expected`, `reason`; catalog leaves append keys; `is_private_safe`), `Subject::machine().path(..)`, `doctor::registry::ids`, `invariant_violations` (rule 7: a `cached` row's `cost_ms` is at most `QUICK_DETECTOR_BUDGET`, 5 ms). `status` runs only `STATUS_FAILURE_MODES` until F8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.8`).
- E3: the check-incomplete finding is `{detector, limit, deadline_ms, max_entries}` with a remediation per limit, instance `fm-state_files-check-incomplete@machine:detector=<fm id>`.
- The prose guard (`tests/contract/main.rs:66-80`): prose may not name `omaddons <subcommand>` unless it holds a `<placeholder>`.

## Technical Approach

### 1. The Skill layer (`src/doctor/view.rs`)

Replace the one-entry list of E2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.2`, the tolerant view) with:

```rust
pub struct SkillLayer { pub files: Vec<SkillFile>, pub coverage: SkillCoverage }
pub struct SkillFile { pub dir: PathBuf, pub file: PathBuf, pub read: SkillRead }
pub enum SkillRead {
    Missing, Bytes(Vec<u8>), TooLarge { len: u64 }, NotAFile,
    Symlink { link_target: PathBuf, through: BoundedRead },
    Unreadable { kind: std::io::ErrorKind },
}
pub enum SkillCoverage { Complete, Overflow { first_unread: PathBuf }, ProjectionUnavailable }
impl DoctorView { pub fn skill(&self) -> Option<&SkillLayer>; } // always Some
```

Loading, once and lazily, writing nothing:

1. `history_tail::fresh(&paths)` and its `skill_dirs()`: `Some(list)` → the installed folders. Otherwise, when `paths.history_file()` does not exist, the list is empty and coverage `Complete`; when it exists, the list is unknown and coverage `ProjectionUnavailable` (only the default is read).
2. Candidates: `Paths::skill_dir()` first, then the list in order; each existing folder canonicalized (`std::fs::canonicalize`), a missing one kept as given; duplicates dropped.
3. Keep the first `SKILL_DIRS_MAX` candidates (the default always counts, as `ScopeTable::with_skill_dirs` of E5, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`, the repair transaction, counts it). If one more candidate remains and `symlink_metadata(<it>/SKILL.md)` succeeds, coverage `Overflow { first_unread }`.
4. Read each kept `<dir>/SKILL.md` with the `read_skill_file` of B3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3`), mapping `Err(e)` to `Unreadable { kind: e.kind() }`; for a symlink, also `read_bounded(<file>, DISCOVERY_FILE_MAX_BYTES)` into `through`.

Write the loader as `fn load_skill_layer(paths: &Paths, projection: Option<&HistoryTail>, read: &dyn Fn(&Path) -> SkillRead) -> SkillLayer` so the unit tests can count reads; the accessor passes the real reader. Change E2's accessor type and its `skill_layer_outcomes` test in this commit.

Decided while writing this bead: at most `SKILL_DIRS_MAX` folders in all, counting the default, and `Overflow` when a further installed folder exists, because the plan says "at most `SKILL_DIRS_MAX` files", E5 admits that many skill folders in one repair, and common rule 15 forbids a silent cut. Decided too: an unknown folder list while history exists is incomplete coverage, not "only the default" (the reading B3's bead gives its readers), because M4-D43 forbids reporting incomplete coverage as healthy; the next change command rebuilds the projection.

### 2. The classification (`src/doctor/detectors/plugins.rs`)

```rust
pub(crate) enum EditedCause { Changed, Unstamped, TooLarge }
pub(crate) enum SkillState {
    Absent, Current, Outdated { digest: [u8; 32] },
    Edited { claimed: Option<[u8; 32]>, cause: EditedCause },
    Symlink { link_target: PathBuf, through: Box<SkillState> },
    NotAFile, Unreadable { kind: std::io::ErrorKind },
}
pub(crate) fn classify(read: &SkillRead, expected_hex: &str) -> SkillState;
```

- `Missing` → `Absent`.
- `Bytes(b)` → `inspect(b)`: pristine with `hex(digest) == expected_hex` → `Current`; pristine otherwise → `Outdated`; not pristine with `hex(claimed) == expected_hex` → `Current`; not pristine otherwise → `Edited { Some(claimed), Changed }`; `Unstamped` → `Edited { None, Unstamped }`.
- `TooLarge` → `Edited { None, TooLarge }`; `NotAFile` → `NotAFile`; `Unreadable` → `Unreadable`.
- `Symlink { link_target, through }`: classify `through` by the same rules (its `Bytes`, `TooLarge`, `NotAFile`, `Unreadable`; `Unreadable { NotFound }`, a dangling link, and `Missing` are `Absent`); `Absent` or `Current` → that state; anything else → `Symlink { link_target, through: Box::new(state) }`.

Decided while writing this bead: an edited copy of this build's guide is `Current` (M4-D50 reports an edited skill only "if its stamp also differs from the binary's"); a symlinked `SKILL.md` is read through and is a finding only when its target is not this build's guide, and a dangling link is not a finding (a dotfiles owner keeps the target current by hand, since `install-skill` refuses the link, and a link to the current guide would be a finding they can never clear); a non-regular or unreadable `SKILL.md` is a manual finding.

### 3. The row and its observations (`src/doctor/registry.rs`, `src/doctor/detectors/plugins.rs`, `src/doctor/finding.rs`)

- `ids::SKILL_VERSION_DRIFT = "fm-plugins-skill-version-drift"`; the `FAILURE_MODES` row inserted where its id sorts: subsystem `plugins`, `P3`, `Tier::Cached`, `online: false`, `cost_ms: 1`, `requires: &[Layer::Skill]`, `detect: Some(detectors::plugins::skill_version_drift)`, `fix: None` (part 2 sets it), `manual: Some(skill_manual)`. Texts:
  - title: "an installed agent skill holds another version of the guide";
  - description: "A SKILL.md omaddons installed for coding agents (in the default skill folder, or in a folder robot-docs install-skill wrote) carries a guide stamp other than this build's guide, or no longer matches its own stamp.";
  - why: "Coding agents load SKILL.md to learn omaddons, so an outdated guide teaches commands, codes and rules this build may not have. The check compares the stamp on the line after the file's frontmatter with this build's guide digest and never renders the guide. A skill edited by hand, a symbolic link, or a file that cannot be read is never rewritten by the doctor: reinstall it yourself, and install-skill keeps your edited copy as SKILL.md.bak."
  Part 2 inserts, before the last sentence, "The fix rewrites an outdated skill with this build's guide and keeps the replaced file as a verbatim backup in the run directory.", so the text never promises a fixer that does not exist yet.
- `STATUS_FAILURE_MODES` is not changed (F8, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.8`, moves `status` onto every cached row).
- **Evidence:** append to the `Evidence` of E1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`, the registry), at its end, omitted when `None`, each with a doc comment: `edited: Option<bool>` and `link_target: Option<PathBuf>`. `reason` takes the closed values below.
- **The detector** `skill_version_drift(view, _selection, _budget) -> Detected`: for each `view.skill()` file, `classify(&f.read, EXPECTED_DIGEST)`, and for each finding state one `Observation` with `subject: Subject::machine().path(&f.file)`, `confidence: High`, `addon: None`, `folder: None`:

| State | Title | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `Outdated` | "The installed agent skill carries another guide than this binary's" | `path`, `observed: "sha256:<hex digest>"`, `expected: "sha256:<EXPECTED_DIGEST>"`, `reason: "outdated"`, `edited: false` |
| `Edited { Changed }` | "The installed agent skill was edited by hand, and its guide is not this binary's" | `path`, `observed: "sha256:<hex claimed>"`, `expected`, `reason: "edited"`, `edited: true` |
| `Edited { Unstamped }` | "The installed agent skill has no guide stamp, so it was changed by hand" | `path`, `expected`, `reason: "unstamped"`, `edited: true` |
| `Edited { TooLarge }` | "The installed agent skill is larger than any guide, so it was changed by hand" | `path`, `expected`, `reason: "too_large"`, `edited: true` |
| `Symlink` | "The installed agent skill is a symbolic link to a file that is not this binary's guide" | `path`, `link_target` (unless it fails `is_private_safe`), `observed` (the target's digest or claim, when it has one), `expected`, `reason: "symlink"`, `edited` (false for an outdated target, true for an edited one, absent otherwise) |
| `NotAFile` | "The installed agent skill's SKILL.md is not a regular file" | `path`, `expected`, `reason: "not_a_file"` |
| `Unreadable` | "The installed agent skill cannot be read" | `path`, `expected`, `reason: "unreadable"` |

  `incomplete`: `Overflow` → `Some(Incomplete { limit: SkillDirs })`, `ProjectionUnavailable` → `Some(Incomplete { limit: HistoryProjection })`, `Complete` → `None`. The detector never charges its `Budget` (it walks nothing).
- **`skill_manual(finding) -> Remediation`:** by `evidence.reason`: `outdated`, `edited`, `unstamped`, `too_large` → argv `["omaddons", "robot-docs", "install-skill", "--dir", <the file's folder>]`, `destructive: false`; `symlink` → prose "SKILL.md is a symbolic link, and omaddons never writes through one: update the file it points to with this build's guide (the robot-docs guide command prints it), or replace the link with a regular file and run the fix again"; `not_a_file` → prose "SKILL.md is not a regular file, so no agent can load it: move it out of the folder, then install the skill there again with robot-docs install-skill"; `unreadable` → prose "omaddons cannot read SKILL.md: give your user read access to it, then run the doctor again" (the builder sees only the finding, whose evidence holds no error text). Without a fixer, E1's mapping gives every instance this remediation.

Decided while writing this bead: the titles above ("another guide", since a digest cannot tell older from newer); `--dir <dir>` for the default folder too; `confidence: high`.

### 4. Two new incomplete limits (E1's `IncompleteLimit`, and the check-incomplete mapping of E3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`)

| Limit (wire) | `max_entries` | Remediation (prose) |
|---|---|---|
| `skill_dirs` | 8 (`SKILL_DIRS_MAX`) | "omaddons checks at most 8 skill folders, and more than that hold a SKILL.md it installed: delete the skill folders you no longer use" |
| `history_projection` | `null` | "the list of folders omaddons installed the skill into lives in its history projection, which is missing or was rewritten by an older build: the next change command rebuilds it" |

`deadline_ms: null` for both. Write the 8 from the constant, never a literal.

### 5. README

README's doctor section's failure-mode table (rule 19) gains the row: `fm-plugins-skill-version-drift`, P3, `cached`, "an installed agent skill (`SKILL.md` in `<skills>` or a folder `install-skill --dir` wrote) whose guide stamp differs from this build's; the stamp is compared, the guide never rendered", repair "reported; reinstall it with `install-skill --dir <folder>`; a symbolic link or unreadable file gets advice" (part 2 changes it to the rewrite), status column as the table writes rows `status` does not report yet (F8 adds "C (machine)"). Re-accept the snapshots that count or list failure modes (`capabilities`' summary if A4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`) has landed, `doctor capabilities` if E4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4`) has, any registry snapshot), after reviewing that the diff is exactly this row. Whichever of E4 and this part lands second makes `doctor capabilities.write_scopes` list each followed skill folder. Run `cargo test --test skill`; regenerate `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` only if it asks.

**Files:** `src/doctor/view.rs`, `src/doctor/detectors/plugins.rs` (create it if F7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.7`) has not; add functions only) and `src/doctor/detectors/mod.rs`, `src/doctor/registry.rs`, `src/doctor/finding.rs`, E3's check-incomplete mapping, snapshots, `README.md`.

**What not to do:** render the guide; read the history beyond the projection; derive folders from the projection's `lines`; report a missing skill or a deleted folder; put a byte of a file into evidence or a log; classify with anything but B3's `inspect` and `classify`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `view.skill()` lists `<skills>` first and then the projection's folders, each once by canonical path, at most `SKILL_DIRS_MAX` in all; reads each with the no-follow bounded read of B3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3`) (and through a symlink with the bounded read of E2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.2`); reports `Overflow` and `ProjectionUnavailable` exactly as specified; and writes nothing.
- [ ] `classify` gives every row of section 2's table, with B3's `inspect` and the `hex` of B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`); a guide rendered with another build id and crate version is `Current`.
- [ ] The row `fm-plugins-skill-version-drift` is registered (P3, `cached`, `plugins`, `cost_ms` 1, `requires [skill]`, a manual builder) and the invariant test of E1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`) passes; `STATUS_FAILURE_MODES` is unchanged.
- [ ] One finding per outdated, edited, unstamped, oversized, symlinked (to a non-current target), non-regular or unreadable `SKILL.md`, with section 3's instance key, title and evidence; none for a missing, current, current-but-edited or dangling-linked one.
- [ ] Overflow and an unknown folder list yield `fm-state_files-check-incomplete` with `limit: skill_dirs` (`max_entries: 8`) and `limit: history_projection`, with their remediations, while the findings made are kept.
- [ ] No evidence, title or remediation holds file content; a link target below a `WTF/` is not recorded; no prose remediation names a runnable omaddons command.
- [ ] The detector never renders the guide (source scan) and reads at most `SKILL_DIRS_MAX` skill files (counting seam).
- [ ] README's doctor table has the row; the failure-mode snapshots are re-accepted after review.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files; `br lint` is clean for this subtask.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

In `src/doctor/view.rs` (tempdir homes built with `Paths::with_roots`; a projection written with the `HistoryTail` of B3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3`) and the module's own writer, or a raw JSON file for the malformed cases):
- `skill_layer_follows_the_default_then_the_projection_newest_first`: projection `[c, b, a]` (three existing folders) → `files` dirs `[<skills>, c, b, a]` (canonical), coverage `Complete`.
- `skill_layer_counts_the_default_and_stops_at_skill_dirs_max`, cases: `seven_installed_plus_default` → 8 files, `Complete`; `eight_installed_ninth_exists` (projection of 8 folders, none the default, all holding a `SKILL.md`) → 8 files (`<skills>` and the newest 7), `Overflow { first_unread: <the oldest> }`; `eight_installed_ninth_deleted` (the oldest folder removed) → 8 files, `Complete`; `default_also_in_projection` → `<skills>` once; `two_spellings_of_one_folder` (`<skills>` reached through a symlinked home and its canonical form in the projection) → one entry.
- `skill_layer_reports_an_unknown_folder_list`, cases: `no_history_file` (no `history.jsonl`, no projection) → default only, `Complete`; `projection_missing` (history present) → `ProjectionUnavailable`; `projection_without_skill_dirs` (the key removed from the JSON) → `ProjectionUnavailable`; `projection_newer` (`schema_version` "9.0") → `ProjectionUnavailable`; `projection_stale` (a line appended to `history.jsonl` after the projection) → `ProjectionUnavailable`.
- `skill_layer_reads_each_kind`: `missing` → `Missing`; `regular` → `Bytes` (exact bytes); `too_large` (`DISCOVERY_FILE_MAX_BYTES + 1`) → `TooLarge`; `directory` → `NotAFile`; `fifo` (made with `mkfifo` when available, else the case logs that it was skipped) → `NotAFile`, returning at once; `mode_000` (skipped as root) → `Unreadable { PermissionDenied }`; `symlink_to_file` → `Symlink { link_target, through: Bytes }`; `dangling_symlink` → `Symlink { through: Unreadable { NotFound } }`; `symlink_to_fifo` → `Symlink { through: NotAFile }`.
- `skill_layer_reads_at_most_skill_dirs_max_files`: with nine installed folders, the counting reader is called exactly `SKILL_DIRS_MAX` times.
- `loading_the_skill_layer_writes_nothing`: the tempdir's tree hash before and after loading every case.

In `src/doctor/detectors/plugins.rs`:
- `classify_skill_cases` (table, one name per case, built from the rendered guide of B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`) and B3's `restamped_guide`-style edits done in-crate): `missing`, `current_guide`, `rendered_with_another_build_id_and_version` (B1's renderer with other `GuideInputs` build id and crate version), `outdated_guide`, `edited_copy_of_current_guide`, `edited_other_guide`, `unstamped`, `malformed_stamp_is_unstamped` (upper-case hex), `too_large`, `not_a_file`, `unreadable`, `symlink_to_current`, `symlink_to_outdated`, `symlink_to_edited`, `dangling_symlink`, `symlink_to_directory`, `symlink_to_unreadable` → section 2's states.
- `observation_per_state`: for each finding state, the instance key string `fm-plugins-skill-version-drift@machine:path=<file>`, the label, the title, `confidence: high`, and the evidence JSON compared literally.
- `evidence_never_holds_skill_content`: every state's file carries the marker `PLANTED-SKILL-TEXT-7f3a`; no serialized observation contains it.
- `a_link_target_below_wtf_is_not_recorded`: a link to `<root>/client/WTF/Account/X/SKILL.md` → no `link_target`, `is_private_safe()`.
- `coverage_becomes_incomplete`: `Complete` → `None`; `Overflow` → `SkillDirs`; `ProjectionUnavailable` → `HistoryProjection`; the observations are kept in each.
- `the_skill_row_is_registered_as_planned`: the row's fields; `invariant_violations(FAILURE_MODES)` empty; the id is not in `STATUS_FAILURE_MODES`.
- `manual_remediation_per_state`: each argv parses with `Cli::try_parse_from`; each prose text contains no `omaddons ` followed by a command name.
- `detectors_never_render_the_guide`: a source scan of `src/doctor/detectors/` finds no `render_guide` and no call into `contract::guide::render` (beside the existing scan of E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`) for `fsx::` and `WriteSession`).

In E3's check-incomplete mapping: `check_incomplete_for_the_skill_limits`: both limits' evidence (`max_entries` 8 and `null`, `deadline_ms` `null`) and remediation texts.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

None in this part: part 3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.10.3`) drives every state through the real binary.

### Logging

Unit tests only: one name per case; assertion messages name the case and show the input's length, first three lines (lossy UTF-8) and SHA-256, the layer's folder list and coverage, and the state, observation or evidence returned. File contents are never printed.

## Considerations

- **Collateral `check-incomplete`.** A test elsewhere that writes `history.jsonl` by hand and then expects a clean `doctor` now sees `history_projection`. Fix such a home (run a mutating command or `history_tail::rebuild_if_stale` before asserting), never this rule; record each in the close comment.
- **Risk #3 (false positives)** is answered here: exact stamps; current skills, edited copies of the current guide, links to the current guide and deleted folders are never findings. **Risk #4 (`status --cached` slows):** no render, no walk, at most `SKILL_DIRS_MAX` bounded reads of guide-sized files.
- **Hot spots:** `src/doctor/view.rs` (E2's, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.2`; F3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.3`), F5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.5`), F6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.6`) and F7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.7`) extend other layers: change only the Skill layer); `src/doctor/registry.rs` (insert where the id sorts; rebase); `src/doctor/detectors/plugins.rs` (shared with F7: add functions only); `src/doctor/finding.rs` (append keys); `README.md` (own row only).
- **Privacy:** paths under the home, digests and reasons; no file text; no path below a `WTF/`.

## Dependencies

- Parent: F10 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.10`, skill drift).
- Before it: nothing inside F10; it starts once the leaf's blockers B3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3`) and E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`) have closed (E6 brings E1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`), E2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.2`), E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`) and E5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`) with it).
- After it: part 2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.10.2`, the rewrite fixer) plans from this layer and classification; part 3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.10.3`) tests both end to end.

title: The rewrite fixer brings an outdated skill current
description:
Part 2 of 3 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.10 (Skill drift). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

**The leaf.** F10 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.10`, skill drift) adds the doctor's check and repair for an installed agent skill that has gone out of date. B3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3`, `robot-docs install-skill`) installs the agent guide as `SKILL.md` into `<skills>` (`$HOME/.claude/skills/omaddons`) or any `--dir` folder; when a newer omaddons ships a different guide, an installed copy teaches agents what this build may no longer do. Part 1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.10.1`) built the read side: the view's Skill layer follows `<skills>` and every folder `history_tail.skill_dirs[]` names (at most `SKILL_DIRS_MAX` = 8 in all, the default counted), `classify` sorts each `SKILL.md` into `Absent`, `Current`, `Outdated`, `Edited`, `Symlink`, `NotAFile` or `Unreadable` by its stamp without rendering the guide, and `fm-plugins-skill-version-drift` (P3, `cached`) reports each finding state with a manual remediation.

**This part** is the repair: the fixer `fixers/rewrite.rs`, which `doctor fix` runs to rewrite an outdated skill with this build's guide, through one journaled `WriteFile` with a verbatim backup, and which refuses every skill it must leave to the user. It also makes the remediation of each instance say whether it is auto-fixable. It is its own step because it depends on E6's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`, `doctor fix`) planner and runtime and on E5's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`, the repair transaction) lowering, while part 1 depends on neither; it serves checkpoint criterion 3 ("`doctor fix` brings it current, undoably. A skill whose bytes no longer match its own stamp was edited by hand and is left to the user") and G-M4-4 ("every auto-fixable state is repaired by one consented command that backs up verbatim, never deletes").

**The decisions it obeys:**
- **M4-D50:** "The fixer writes the current guide through `mutate()` with a verbatim backup, and is undoable." A locally edited skill "is never rewritten by the doctor … the fixer refuses that instance (`doctor_refused`, reason `edited_locally`), so it is manual: `omaddons robot-docs install-skill --dir <dir>`, which keeps a backup." A symlinked `SKILL.md` is never written through (fsx refuses a symlink's final component, `src/fsx/mutate.rs:610-615`) and is reported with prose advice.
- **M4-D31 and §6.14 (context, E5's):** a fix run is one engine transaction of kind `repair`; a `Fix::Write` lowers to one `WriteFile` primitive with a reserved backup when it overwrites, `pre` and `post` endpoint predicates checked immediately before the operation, write-ahead per step, recovery by any lock-taking command, and a `kind: repair` history line with the primitives.
- **M4-D44 and M4-D45 (context, E6's):** the dry run's token binds the planned primitives' `pre` predicates; a bound run re-plans under the lock from a fresh view (findings resolved meanwhile drop out, new instances join) and compares the token before anything moves.
- **M4-D40:** `doctor_refused` (exit 4, not retryable) with `details.reason` from a closed set that includes `edited_locally` (this fixer's) and `not_enabled` (a fixer that cannot run in this build).
- **M4-D7:** the guide's identity is its content digest; `contract::guide::EXPECTED_DIGEST` is the committed guide's digest; `render_guide()` renders the guide.

**Facts this part relies on** (from the blockers' beads and part 1; record any name that differs on `main`):
- E1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`): `FixerSpec { plan: fn(&DoctorView, &Finding) -> Result<Vec<Fix>, Refusal>, writes_to, ops, enabled, needs_force, cardinality, preconditions }`; `Fix::Write { path, content: Vec<u8>, mode: Mode }`; `Mode::new(bits)`; `RefusalReason::{EditedLocally, NotEnabled, …}`; `Refusal { reason, message }`; `ScopeName::Skill` (whose fsx row admits `Writer::Doctor`, `src/fsx/scope.rs:126`); `FixKind::Write`; `Cardinality::Low` (at most 10 paths); `FixerPrecondition::LockHeld`; invariant 9 (a fixer has an op, a `writes_to`, and each scope admits the doctor writer).
- E5: `lower` turns `Fix::Write` over an existing file into one `WriteFile` with `pre = File { sha256, mode }`, `post = File { sha256(content), mode }` and a reserved backup `<run>/backups/<seq>`; `LowerCtx.skill_dirs` ("the skill directories a write may touch") and `ScopeTable::with_skill_dirs` (at most `SKILL_DIRS_MAX`, the default counted) decide which skill folders a repair may write; recovery and undo admit a skill folder only when it is `Paths::skill_dir()` or listed in `history_tail.skill_dirs[]`.
- E6: `plan_fix` groups findings (planned: `auto_fixable` ones by default, and every finding of a mode `--only` names by id, "so its fixer can refuse it by name (`edited_locally`)"; manual: the rest); a fixer's `Err(Refusal)` is run-level (`PlanRefusal::Fixer { fm, refusal }`, reported with "`fm` and the refusal's keys" and "the refusal's own fix"); `remediation_for(finding, spec, target_id)` gives `omaddons doctor fix --only <fm>` with `auto_fixable` = "enabled, no force, and the detector's own verdict for the instance"; VERIFYING re-runs the fixed modes' detectors after the lock; a run with nothing planned ends `DONE_OK` or `DONE_FINDINGS`.
- B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`): `render_guide() -> Result<String, RenderError>`, `stamp::digest_without_stamp(doc) -> Result<[u8; 32], StampError>`, `stamp::hex`.
- `Suggestion::command(argv)` and `Suggestion::text(display)` (`src/error.rs:385-420`).
- B3: `install-skill` replaces a pristine `SKILL.md` and keeps any other as `SKILL.md.bak`; its help's `after_long_help` was written without the doctor sentence, which B3's bead leaves to F10.

## Technical Approach

### 1. The fixer (`src/doctor/fixers/rewrite.rs`, `pub mod rewrite;` in `src/doctor/fixers/mod.rs`)

```rust
pub(crate) fn plan(view: &DoctorView, finding: &Finding) -> Result<Vec<Fix>, Refusal> {
    plan_with(view, finding, &render_guide, EXPECTED_DIGEST)
}
fn plan_with(view: &DoctorView, finding: &Finding,
             render: &dyn Fn() -> Result<String, RenderError>, expected_hex: &str)
    -> Result<Vec<Fix>, Refusal>;
```

1. Find the Skill layer entry whose `file` equals `finding.evidence.path`. None, or `classify` now `Absent` or `Current`: `Ok(vec![])` (nothing to do; VERIFYING finds the instance gone).
2. `Outdated`: `render()`; an error, or `hex(digest_without_stamp(&rendered)) != expected_hex`, is `Refusal { reason: NotEnabled, message: "this omaddons build cannot produce the guide it was built with", fix: prose "rebuild omaddons after regenerating skills/omaddons/SKILL.md" }`. Otherwise `Ok(vec![Fix::Write { path: file, content: rendered.into_bytes(), mode: SKILL_MODE }])`, where `SKILL_MODE` is 0644 as the `Mode` of E1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`, the registry and action model) (`Mode::new` returns an `Option`, so build the constant once, in a `const` or a tested helper).
3. Any other state: `Refusal { reason: EditedLocally, message, path: Some(file), fix }`, with the message `"<file> was edited by hand; the doctor never overwrites it"`, `"<file> is a symbolic link; omaddons never writes through one"`, `"<file> is not a regular file"` or `"<file> cannot be read"`, and `fix` part 1's manual remediation for the instance (`Suggestion::command(["omaddons", "robot-docs", "install-skill", "--dir", <dir>])` for `edited`, `unstamped`, `too_large`; `Suggestion::text(<the prose>)` for `symlink`, `not_a_file`, `unreadable`).

Decided while writing this bead: a render failure or a digest mismatch is `not_enabled` (the closed set's "this fixer cannot run in this build"; E6, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`, keeps the reason for a fixer's own refusal), because writing a guide the detector would still call outdated would make the run end partial on every retry; the gate rejects such a build (`tests/skill.rs`), so this guards development builds only. Decided too: mode 0644, `install-skill`'s mode (§6.3.3); E5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`) records the old mode in `pre`, so the undo restores it.

### 2. The row's fixer (`src/doctor/registry.rs`)

The row's `fix` becomes `Some(FixerSpec { plan: fixers::rewrite::plan, writes_to: &[ScopeName::Skill], ops: &[FixKind::Write], enabled: true, needs_force: false, cardinality: Cardinality::Low, preconditions: &[FixerPrecondition::LockHeld] })`. Insert into the row's `why`, before its last sentence: "The fix rewrites an outdated skill with this build's guide and keeps the replaced file as a verbatim backup in the run directory." No `ClientNotRunning`: no client is involved.

### 3. `Refusal` carries its file and its fix (the `Refusal` of E1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`, and E6's `PlanRefusal::Fixer`)

If `Refusal` on `main` has only `reason` and `message`, add `path: Option<PathBuf>` and `fix: Option<Suggestion>`. `PlanRefusal::Fixer`'s `into_error` writes `details.path` when set and uses `fix` as the error's `fix` (and `fix_argv` for a command) when set, keeping E6's default otherwise. Declare `path` (an optional string) in `doctor_refused`'s `DetailSpec` (`src/error.rs` or `src/error/specs.rs`, A9's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9`) registry), additively. The resulting error, for an edited default skill (absolute paths in real output):

```json
{"code":"doctor_refused","message":"<skills>/SKILL.md was edited by hand; the doctor never overwrites it",
 "details":{"reason":"edited_locally","fm":"fm-plugins-skill-version-drift","path":"<skills>/SKILL.md"},
 "fix":"omaddons robot-docs install-skill --dir <skills>",
 "fix_argv":["omaddons","robot-docs","install-skill","--dir","<skills>"],"retryable":false}
```

### 4. The instance's own verdict (E1's `Observation`/`Finding`, E6's `remediation_for`)

If E6 or F2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.2`, the journal fixers) has already added a per-instance verdict on `main`, use it. Otherwise add:
- `Observation.fixable: bool` (default `true`; a builder method such as `.manual_only()` sets it `false`) and `Finding.fixable: bool` (`#[serde(skip)]`, `#[schemars(skip)]`), copied by `Finding::build`.
- `remediation_for` takes the `FailureMode` (or the row's `manual` builder as an extra parameter): `auto_fixable = spec.enabled && !spec.needs_force && finding.fixable`; for `!finding.fixable`, `command`, `argv` and `destructive` come from the row's `manual` builder when it has one, otherwise the `doctor explain` argv; `estimated_actions` as E6 computes it (0 when not fixable).
- The skill detector (part 1's `skill_version_drift`) marks every observation but `Outdated` as `manual_only()`.

So an outdated skill's remediation is `omaddons doctor fix --only fm-plugins-skill-version-drift` (`auto_fixable: true`, `needs_force: false`, `estimated_actions: 1`), and every other skill instance keeps part 1's manual remediation (`auto_fixable: false`). A default `doctor fix` plans only outdated skills and lists the others as manual; `--only fm-plugins-skill-version-drift` plans every instance, so a manual one makes the run refuse by name (E6's rule).

### 5. The skill folders the repair may write (E6's planner)

E6's planner passes the view's followed folders (each `view.skill()` file's `dir`) as `LowerCtx.skill_dirs`, and the commit's scope table applies `ScopeTable::with_skill_dirs` with the same list. If E6 passes only `Paths::skill_dir()`, change it here. The rewrite's path is the canonical `<dir>/SKILL.md`; a symlinked skill folder is followed to where it points (as `install-skill` writes there), and only a symlinked `SKILL.md` is refused (by `classify`, with fsx's own refusal as the backstop).

### 6. Help and README

- `install-skill`'s `after_long_help` (`src/app/install_skill.rs`, the file of B3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3`) gains: "`omaddons doctor` reports an installed skill whose guide differs from this build's, and `omaddons doctor fix` rewrites it with a backup; a skill you edited, or a symlinked SKILL.md, is left to you." Re-accept any help snapshot that quotes it.
- README `robot-docs install-skill` section: the same sentence. README's doctor table row: the repair column becomes "rewritten by `doctor fix` with a verbatim backup in the run directory; a skill edited by hand, a symbolic link, a non-regular or unreadable file is left to you, with the reinstall command or advice". Say "undone with `omaddons doctor undo`" only if E7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7`, the undo of repairs) has landed; otherwise E7's README pass covers the undo of every repair.
- Re-accept the `doctor capabilities` snapshot (E4, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4`) if it has landed: the fixer entry `{id: fm-plugins-skill-version-drift, preconditions: [lock_held], writes_to: [skill], ops: [write], reversible: true, idempotent: true, cardinality: low, enabled: true, needs_force: false}`.
- Run `cargo test --test skill`; regenerate `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` only if it asks (this part adds no command, code, action or env var).

**Files:** `src/doctor/fixers/rewrite.rs` (new), `src/doctor/fixers/mod.rs`, `src/doctor/registry.rs`, `src/doctor/finding.rs`, `src/doctor/fix.rs` (E6's: `remediation_for`, `PlanRefusal::Fixer`, `LowerCtx.skill_dirs`), `src/doctor/detectors/plugins.rs` (the `manual_only()` marks), `src/error.rs` or `src/error/specs.rs`, `src/app/install_skill.rs`, snapshots, `README.md`.

**What not to do:** write anything but the one `SKILL.md` of a planned instance; delete anything; write through a symlink; plan an instance part 1 did not classify `Outdated`; render the guide in the detector (only `plan` renders); add a refusal reason outside M4-D40's set.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `plan` returns one `Fix::Write` of this build's rendered guide (mode 0644) for an outdated skill, nothing for an instance that is now absent or current, `edited_locally` with the file and the manual fix for every other state, and `not_enabled` for a render error or a digest mismatch.
- [ ] The row's `FixerSpec` is `writes_to [skill]`, `ops [write]`, enabled, not forced, `low`, `[lock_held]`; the invariant test of E1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`) passes.
- [ ] An outdated instance's remediation is the `doctor fix --only fm-plugins-skill-version-drift` argv with `auto_fixable: true`; every other skill instance keeps its manual remediation with `auto_fixable: false`; a default plan lists them as manual, and `--only` makes the planner of E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`) refuse with `doctor_refused`, `details {reason: edited_locally, fm, path}` and the manual fix.
- [ ] The lowering of a skill rewrite is one `WriteFile` with `pre` and `post` predicates and a reserved backup, for the default folder and for a followed `--dir` folder; a folder outside the followed list is refused.
- [ ] The `install-skill` help and README carry the doctor sentence; README's doctor-table row names the rewrite; the snapshots are re-accepted after review.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files; `br lint` is clean for this subtask.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

In `src/doctor/fixers/rewrite.rs` (a tempdir view built with `DoctorView::load_at` over `Paths::with_roots`, skill files planted from the rendered guide of B1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`):
- `plan_rewrites_an_outdated_skill_with_this_builds_guide`: an outdated `<skills>/SKILL.md` → exactly `[Fix::Write { path: <canonical>/SKILL.md, content == render_guide() bytes, mode 0o644 }]`; the same for a followed `--dir` folder.
- `plan_refuses_every_state_it_must_leave_alone`, cases `edited`, `unstamped`, `too_large`, `symlink`, `not_a_file`, `unreadable`: each `Err(Refusal { reason: EditedLocally, path: Some(<file>), .. })`, the message naming the file and the cause, and the fix the `install-skill --dir` argv (the first three) or prose without a runnable command (the last three).
- `plan_is_empty_when_the_instance_is_gone`, cases `now_current` (the file reinstalled), `now_missing` (the folder deleted), `no_longer_followed` (a finding whose path is in no layer entry): each `Ok(vec![])`.
- `plan_refuses_a_guide_that_is_not_the_expected_one`, cases `render_error` (a `render` stand-in returning an error) and `digest_mismatch` (`expected_hex` of 64 zeros): each `NotEnabled`, nothing planned.
- `the_fixer_spec_is_as_declared`: the spec's fields; `Fix::primitive_count` of the fix is 1.

In `src/doctor/fix.rs` (the module of E6, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`):
- `remediation_follows_the_instance_verdict`: `outdated` → argv `["omaddons","doctor","fix","--only","fm-plugins-skill-version-drift"]`, `auto_fixable: true`, `estimated_actions: 1`; `edited` → the `install-skill --dir` argv, `auto_fixable: false`; `symlink` → prose, `argv: null`, `auto_fixable: false`; and, if this part added the verdict, a row with no `manual` and a non-fixable instance → the `doctor explain` argv.
- `a_skill_refusal_becomes_doctor_refused_with_its_path_and_fix`: `PlanRefusal::Fixer` with an `edited_locally` refusal → `doctor_refused`, `details == {reason, fm, path}`, `fix_argv` the `install-skill --dir` argv; a prose refusal → `fix` text, no `fix_argv`.
- `planner_lists_manual_skill_instances_and_refuses_them_by_name`: one outdated and one edited skill; the default plan → planned `[outdated]`, unplanned `[(edited, manual)]`; `--only fm-plugins-skill-version-drift` → `PlanRefusal::Fixer` with `edited_locally`.
- `lowering_a_skill_rewrite`: the `lower` of E5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`) on a tempdir home with an outdated `<skills>/SKILL.md` and an outdated followed `--dir` folder → two `WriteFile` steps, each `pre = File { sha256 of the old bytes, mode 0o644 }`, `post = File { sha256 of the guide, mode 0o644 }`, backups `<run>/backups/1` and `/2`, resources the file and its backup; with the `--dir` folder left out of `LowerCtx.skill_dirs` → E5's `scope_denied`.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

None in this part: part 3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.10.3`) runs the fixer through the real binary (preview, bound run, verify, refusals, the last-moment edit and crashes).

### Logging

Unit tests only: each case is named; assertion messages show the case, the planted file's length and SHA-256, the state `classify` gave, and the fixes, refusal (reason, message, path, fix) or remediation returned. File contents are never printed.

## Considerations

- **The committed guide must be current.** The detector compares with `EXPECTED_DIGEST` (the committed file's digest at build time); the fixer writes `render_guide()`. They agree whenever the gate passes; the `not_enabled` refusal covers a development build with a stale `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md`.
- **Run-level refusals.** With an outdated and an edited skill, `doctor fix --only fm-plugins-skill-version-drift` refuses as a whole (the rule of E6, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`: a preview never silently drops a selected fix); plain `doctor fix` rewrites the outdated one and lists the edited one. README and the refusal's message make this clear.
- **The last-moment edit.** A change to a planned `SKILL.md` after the under-lock re-plan fails the step's `pre` predicate and rolls the repair back (E5, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`); an edit in the instant between fsx's check and its write is caught only by the verbatim backup, which the undo restores (the plan's stated limit: no compare-and-swap against arbitrary writers).
- **Hot spots:** `src/doctor/fix.rs` (E6's; F2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.2`) may extend `remediation_for` too: whichever lands second merges the verdict once); `src/doctor/finding.rs` (append); `src/error.rs` (append the `DetailSpec` key); `src/app/install_skill.rs` (the file of B3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3`; one help line); `README.md` (own row and sentence).
- **Concurrency.** `install-skill` and `doctor fix` both take the global lock, so they serialize; the fix's re-plan under the lock sees whatever `install-skill` wrote first.

## Dependencies

- Parent: F10 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.10`, skill drift).
- Before it: part 1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.10.1`): the Skill layer, `classify`, the row and its manual remediations, which this fixer plans from and returns as its refusals' fixes.
- After it: part 3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.10.3`) tests the detector and the fixer end to end.
