title: Tests: the skill-drift fixture, the drift and repair scenarios end to end, and the detector's cached-tier budget
description:
Part 3 of 3 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.10 (Skill drift). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

**The leaf.** F10 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.10`, skill drift) adds the doctor's check and repair for an installed agent skill that has gone out of date. B3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3`, `robot-docs install-skill`) installs the agent guide as `SKILL.md` into `<skills>` (`$HOME/.claude/skills/omaddons`) or any `--dir` folder, and records each folder in `history_tail.skill_dirs[]`. Part 1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.10.1`) made the doctor's view follow `<skills>` and those folders (at most `SKILL_DIRS_MAX` = 8 in all, the default counted), classify each `SKILL.md` by its stamp without rendering the guide, and report `fm-plugins-skill-version-drift` (P3, `cached`) for an outdated, edited, unstamped, oversized, symlinked (to a non-current target), non-regular or unreadable file, with `check-incomplete` when the folder list is cut short or unknown. Part 2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.10.2`) added the fixer: `doctor fix` rewrites an outdated skill with this build's guide through one journaled `WriteFile` with a verbatim backup, and refuses every other state (`doctor_refused`, `edited_locally`).

**This part** proves the leaf through the real binary: the fixture M4-D47 requires (common rule 19), the planting helpers, an end-to-end suite of every state, the repair and its binding, a crash recovered on a `--dir` folder, two contract rows, and the release-build measurement that the check fits the `cached` tier. It is its own step because the scenarios need both the detector and the fixer, and because its closing agent verifies the leaf's acceptance criteria and closes omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.10.

**What the tests must show** (the leaf's acceptance, from the plan and M4-D50): a skill with another guide digest is reported and rewritten, and the verify step passes; a skill with this binary's guide digest, written by another build, is not a finding; an edited skill is reported as edited and is not rewritten by `doctor fix`; a deleted skill directory is not a finding; the `cached`-tier detector stays inside `status --cached`'s budget with `SKILL_DIRS_MAX` skills installed. F9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`, the safety harness) later runs the same fixture through the undo round trip, every crash boundary, concurrency and the declared pair with `fm-secrets-credential-file-mode`; this part does not test `doctor undo`, because E7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7`, the undo of repairs) is not one of this leaf's blockers.

**What exists to build on:**
- T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs): `tests/common/tlog.rs` (`let log = tlog!();`, `log.step`, `log.note`, `log.json`, `log.case`, `log.run(&home, &argv) -> Ran` with the argv after `omaddons`, `log.cmd(&home, &argv).env(k, v).failpoints(spec).spawn()` and `Running::wait()`, `log.tree`, `log.assert_unchanged`; `Ran::{ok, exit, fails, aborted, envelope, error_code, warnings, commands, events}`; a doctor envelope has no `data`, so use `envelope()`), and the crate-doc marker `//! e2e suite: <purpose>` that `argc e2e` reads.
- E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`): `tests/doctor/mod.rs` with the `Fixture` trait (`id`, `corrupt(&Home)`, `assert_healthy(&Home)`, `subject(&Home) -> Vec<PathBuf>`, `fixer() -> bool`, `run_env`, `run_args`, and the defaulted `remedy` of F1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1`), included as `#[path = "doctor/mod.rs"] mod fixtures;`; `tests/doctor/fixtures/mod.rs::all()`; `tests/common/doctor.rs` (`plant`, `plant::runs`, `plant::latest`, `check_envelope(stdout, stderr, code)`); the contract harness's doctor mode in `tests/contract/matrix.rs`.
- B3: `tests/common/skill.rs`: `committed_guide()`, `claude_ready(&env) -> PathBuf` (creates `$HOME/.claude`), `skill_root(&env, rel)`, `assert_is_guide(&file)`, `restamped_guide(edit) -> Vec<u8>` (a pristine guide with another digest), `skill_dirs(&env) -> Option<Vec<String>>`, `skill_lines(&env)`.
- `tests/common/`: `Home` and `TestEnv` (every `HOME`/`XDG_*` inside one tempdir, `TZ=UTC`), `trees::tree_hash` (modes and symlink targets), `pause::Pause` (`new(root)`, `env()`, `reached(name)`, `resume(name)`), `procfs::running_as_root()`.
- E5's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`, the repair transaction) repair failpoints: `doctor.repair.step` (after step line k is durable, before primitive k is checked) and `doctor.repair.done` (after `done`, before the history line); recovery runs in every lock-taking command (`config set check_interval_hours 6` is the suites' usual one).
- `tests/perf.rs`: `median_of_21` (`:63`), `measured`, `Paths::with_roots(env.home(), env.config(), env.state(), env.cache())` (`:835`); its budgets are ignored release-build tests.

## Technical Approach

### 1. The planting helpers (`tests/common/doctor.rs`, `plant::skill_*`)

Each documented (what it plants, the state `classify` gives, the finding's `reason`), deterministic, using the real binary for installs and plain file edits for the damage (test code may use `std::fs`; only `src/` must go through fsx):

| Helper | Plants | State / `reason` |
|---|---|---|
| `skill_install(home, dir: Option<&Path>) -> PathBuf` | `robot-docs install-skill [--dir <dir>] --json` (creating `<dir>`'s parent first), returns the canonical folder | current (no finding) |
| `skill_outdated(dir) -> Vec<u8>` | `restamped_guide(\|t\| t.push_str("\nA paragraph from another version of the guide.\n"))`, mode 0644 | `outdated` |
| `skill_edited(dir) -> Vec<u8>` | the outdated bytes plus the line `PLANTED-SKILL-TEXT-7f3a` appended after stamping | `edited`, `edited: true` |
| `skill_unstamped(dir)` | `committed_guide()` with its stamp line removed, plus the marker line | `unstamped` |
| `skill_too_large(dir)` | the outdated bytes padded with marker lines to `DISCOVERY_FILE_MAX_BYTES + 1` | `too_large` |
| `skill_link(dir, target: &Path, bytes: Option<&[u8]>)` | `SKILL.md` a relative symlink to `target` (written with `bytes` when given, left absent when `None`) | `symlink`, or no finding |
| `skill_not_a_file(dir)` | a directory named `SKILL.md` | `not_a_file` |
| `skill_unreadable(dir)` | an outdated file chmodded 000 (callers skip it as root) | `unreadable` |

Order constraint, documented on each: plant after the installs, since `install-skill` replaces what it finds (and keeps an edited copy as `SKILL.md.bak`).

### 2. The fixture (`tests/doctor/fixtures/fm_plugins_skill_version_drift.rs`, registered in `fixtures/mod.rs::all()`)

```rust
/// `fm-plugins-skill-version-drift`: two installed agent skills carry another version of the guide.
///
/// What breaks: a newer or older omaddons shipped a different guide, so the SKILL.md files agents
/// load no longer describe this build. `corrupt` installs the skill into `<skills>` and into
/// `<root>/agents/second/omaddons` (so `history_tail.skill_dirs[]` names it), then replaces both with
/// a pristine guide stamped with another digest. The finding: P3, machine, one instance per file
/// (`…@machine:path=<file>`), evidence `{path, observed, expected, reason: "outdated", edited: false}`.
/// The fixer rewrites both with this build's guide, keeping each replaced file in `<run>/backups/<seq>`.
pub struct SkillVersionDrift;
```

- `corrupt`: `claude_ready`; `plant::skill_install(home, None)`; `plant::skill_install(home, Some(<root>/agents/second/omaddons))`; `plant::skill_outdated` on both folders.
- `assert_healthy`: `assert_is_guide` on both files, both 0644, and `doctor --json --only fm-plugins-skill-version-drift` reports no finding (exit 0).
- `subject`: the two skill folders (F9, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`, compares them with modes after the undo).
- `fixer()`: `true`. `run_env`, `run_args`, `remedy`: the defaults.

The other states are scenario cases (section 3), not `Fixture`s: a `Fixture` must yield its finding and, with a fixer, round-trip, which an edited or current skill by design does not. Decided while writing this bead.

### 3. The suite (`tests/doctor_skill.rs`, new)

First line `//! e2e suite: skill drift: the detector, its fixer and the folders it follows`; `#[path = "doctor/mod.rs"] mod fixtures;`. Each scenario, and each case of a table-driven scenario, on its own `Home` (no client is needed: `Home::new(&["wow"])` or the smallest `Home` the module offers), every command through `log.run`/`log.cmd` with `--json` passed explicitly, every doctor envelope checked with `common::doctor::check_envelope`. `<skills>` below is `home.env.home().join(".claude/skills/omaddons")`, `<second>` is `<root>/agents/second/omaddons`.

1. **`the_fixture_is_found_rewritten_and_verified`**
   - "plant": the fixture's `corrupt`; `log.tree` of both folders; `log.json("planted", {len, sha256} per file)`.
   - "diagnose": `doctor --only fm-plugins-skill-version-drift --json` → exit 1, `DONE_FINDINGS`, exactly two findings, sorted by instance key; each `instance == "fm-plugins-skill-version-drift@machine:path=<file>"`, `severity: P3`, `subsystem: plugins`, `target: null`, evidence `{path, observed: "sha256:<the planted digest>", expected: "sha256:" + omaddons::contract::guide::EXPECTED_DIGEST, reason: "outdated", edited: false}` (and `expected` equal to `capabilities --json`'s `guide_digest` once A4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`, `omaddons capabilities`) has wired it), `remediation.argv == ["omaddons","doctor","fix","--only","fm-plugins-skill-version-drift"]`, `auto_fixable: true`, `estimated_actions: 1`.
   - "explain": `doctor explain <the second instance key> --json` → exit 0, `instances` holds exactly that finding.
   - "preview": `doctor fix --only fm-plugins-skill-version-drift --dry-run --json` → exit 1, two `actions_planned` `write_file` entries, `path` the two files, `mode: "0644"`, `backup` under `<run>/backups/`, `bytes` the planted lengths; a `precondition` token; `log.assert_unchanged` on both folders.
   - "fix": `doctor fix --only fm-plugins-skill-version-drift --if-match <token> --json` → exit 0, `DONE_OK`, `summary {findings_before: 2, findings_after: 0, actions_taken: 2, actions_failed: 0, bytes_backed_up: <sum of the planted lengths>}`, two `actions` with `ok: true`; both files pass `assert_is_guide`, mode 0644; each `<run>/backups/<seq>` byte-equals the bytes planted at its action's `path` (F9's backup property); `history --json` holds one `kind: repair` entry with `target: null`, two `repairs[]` `write_file` primitives on the two files.
   - "verify": `doctor --only fm-plugins-skill-version-drift --json` → exit 0, no finding; the fixture's `assert_healthy`.
   - "again": the same `doctor fix --only …` → exit 0, `actions_taken: 0` (idempotence).
2. **`a_current_skill_is_never_a_finding_whatever_wrote_it`** — `log.case` per case: `installed_by_this_build` (`skill_install(None)`); `same_bytes_other_metadata` (the installed file chmodded 0600 and its mtime set to 2020-01-01); `copied_by_hand` (`committed_guide()` written into `<second>` with no history line, and `<second>` reached through `skill_install` first so it is followed); `edited_copy_of_the_current_guide` (`committed_guide()` plus one appended line). Each: `doctor --only fm-plugins-skill-version-drift --json` → exit 0, no finding; `doctor fix --only … --json` → exit 0, `actions_taken: 0`; the folders unchanged (`log.assert_unchanged`).
3. **`an_edited_skill_is_reported_and_left_to_the_user`** — cases `changed` (`skill_edited`), `unstamped`, `too_large`, each in `<skills>` after `skill_install(None)`, with an outdated `<second>` beside it:
   - `doctor --json` → the edited instance with its `reason`, `edited: true`, `auto_fixable: false`, `remediation.argv == ["omaddons","robot-docs","install-skill","--dir","<skills>"]`, and `observed` only for `changed`; the outdated `<second>` instance as in scenario 1. The marker `PLANTED-SKILL-TEXT-7f3a` appears in no stdout, stderr or `<run>/report.json`.
   - `doctor fix --json` (no `--only`) → exit 0 (`DONE_OK`: every planned instance is gone), `<second>` rewritten, `<skills>` byte-identical to its planted bytes (`log.assert_unchanged`), the edited instance still reported among the unplanned.
   - `doctor fix --only fm-plugins-skill-version-drift --json` → exit 4, `state: REFUSING`, `error.code: doctor_refused`, `details == {reason: "edited_locally", fm: "fm-plugins-skill-version-drift", path: "<skills>/SKILL.md"}`, `fix_argv` the same `install-skill --dir` argv, `retryable: false`; `<skills>` unchanged.
   - "manual fix": run that `fix_argv` → exit 0, `written: "replaced"`; `assert_is_guide(<skills>/SKILL.md)`; `<skills>/SKILL.md.bak` byte-equals the planted bytes (the rule of B3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3`); `doctor --json` → no skill finding.
4. **`a_symlinked_skill_is_reported_only_when_its_target_is_not_current`** — `skill_install(None)`, then `skill_link(<skills>, <root>/dotfiles/omaddons/SKILL.md, …)`; cases: `to_outdated` (outdated bytes) → one finding `reason: symlink`, `link_target` the link's text, `observed` the target's digest, `edited: false`, `remediation.argv: null`, prose `command`, `auto_fixable: false`; `doctor fix --only …` → exit 4, `edited_locally`, `details.path`; `doctor fix` → exit 1 (`DONE_FINDINGS`, nothing planned); `log.assert_unchanged` on `<skills>` (the link) and on `<root>/dotfiles` (the target). `to_edited` → `reason: symlink`, `edited: true`. `to_current` (`committed_guide()`) → no finding. `dangling` (`bytes: None`) → no finding. `to_directory` (the target a directory) → `reason: symlink`, no `edited`.
5. **`deleted_skill_folders_are_not_findings`** — `claude_ready`; `skill_install(Some(<root>/agents/a/omaddons))` and `skill_install(Some(<root>/agents/b/omaddons))`; remove folder `a` (and never install `<skills>`); `skill_dirs(&env)` still names both; `doctor --only fm-plugins-skill-version-drift --json` → exit 0, `DONE_OK`, no finding, no `check-incomplete`; `doctor fix --only fm-plugins-skill-version-drift --json` → exit 0, `actions_taken: 0`.
6. **`odd_skill_files_are_reported_with_advice`** — cases `not_a_file` (`skill_not_a_file(<skills>)`) → `reason: not_a_file`, prose remediation, no `edited`; `unreadable` (`skill_unreadable(<skills>)`; skipped as root, saying so in the log) → `reason: unreadable`, prose. Each: `doctor fix --only …` → exit 4, `edited_locally`, nothing changed; restore mode 0644 after the `unreadable` case.
7. **`the_check_follows_at_most_skill_dirs_max_folders`** — `skill_install(None)`, then `skill_install(Some(<root>/agents/c<i>/omaddons))` for i = 1…8 (so `skill_dirs` = c8…c1 and `<skills>` was pushed out of the projection); `skill_outdated` in all nine folders.
   - `doctor --json --only fm-plugins-skill-version-drift` → exit 1, eight skill findings (`<skills>` and c8…c2), plus one `fm-state_files-check-incomplete` with `evidence {detector: "fm-plugins-skill-version-drift", limit: "skill_dirs", deadline_ms: null, max_entries: 8}` and its prose remediation; `state` never `DONE_OK`.
   - Remove c1's folder; `doctor --json --only …` → eight findings and no `check-incomplete`.
   - `doctor fix --only fm-plugins-skill-version-drift --json` → exit 0, `actions_taken: 8` (the scope table of E5, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`, admits eight skill folders counting the default), all eight pass `assert_is_guide`.
8. **`an_unknown_folder_list_is_incomplete_never_clean`** — case `projection_deleted`: `skill_install(Some(<second>))`, `skill_outdated(<second>)`; remove `<cache>/omaddons/history_tail.json`; `doctor --json --only …` → no `<second>` finding, one `check-incomplete` with `limit: "history_projection"`, `max_entries: null`, exit 1; `config set check_interval_hours 6 --json` → exit 0 (it rebuilds the projection); `doctor --json --only …` → the `<second>` finding, no `check-incomplete`. Case `no_history_at_all`: on a home where no command has run, `claude_ready`, create `<skills>` and write `skill_outdated` by hand; `doctor --json --only …` → one finding, no `check-incomplete`.
9. **`since_compares_skill_findings_by_instance`** (the two-skill-roots case E3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, left to this leaf) — the fixture's `corrupt`; `doctor --json` → run A (two instances); `robot-docs install-skill --dir <second> --json` (the manual fix of one); `doctor --json --since <A>` → `since == {run: A, new: [], resolved: [<second's instance>], unchanged: 1}`.
10. **`the_doctor_never_overwrites_a_change_it_did_not_plan`** — case `after_the_preview`: the fixture's `corrupt`; `doctor fix --only … --dry-run --json` → token; append a line to `<second>/SKILL.md` (it becomes edited); `log.tree` of both folders; `doctor fix --only … --if-match <token> --json` → exit 4, `plan_stale`, `retryable: false`, `details.changed` non-empty, `fix_argv` the `--dry-run` form; both folders unchanged since the edit. Case `while_the_repair_runs`: the fixture's `corrupt`; the dry run names the file of `seq` 2 (`<file2>`); `log.cmd(&home, ["doctor","fix","--only","fm-plugins-skill-version-drift","--json"]).failpoints("doctor.repair.step@2=pause")` with a `Pause` dir, spawned; `reached("doctor.repair.step")`; append a line to `<file2>`; `resume`; → exit 3, `DONE_FAILED`, `backups_restored: 1`; the file of `seq` 1 byte-equals its planted bytes again (restored from its backup), `<file2>` holds the hand edit; no `<state>/omaddons/journal/*.repair.jsonl` left; no `kind: repair` history line; `doctor --json` → two findings again (`outdated` and `edited`).
11. **`a_crashed_rewrite_recovers_whole`** — the fixture's `corrupt`; cases:
    - `before_done`: `doctor fix --only … --json` with `doctor.repair.step@2=abort` → `Ran::aborted()`; "reader": `status --json` → exit 0 and both folders unchanged since the crash (`log.assert_unchanged`); "recover": `config set check_interval_hours 6 --json` → exit 0; both files byte-equal their planted bytes (the whole subject set before: a crash before the durable `done`), no repair journal left, no `kind: repair` history line; recover again (the same command) → nothing changes.
    - `after_done`: with `doctor.repair.done=abort` → aborted; recover as above → both files pass `assert_is_guide` (the whole set after), exactly one `kind: repair` history line; recover again → still one line.
    This proves recovery admits a `--dir` skill folder that `history_tail.skill_dirs[]` lists (E5's rule); F9 crashes every boundary.
12. **`a_diagnose_with_skills_changes_nothing_and_repeats`** — plant one of each finding state into eight folders (`skill_install` for each, then the helper); `log.tree` of every skill folder, `<root>/dotfiles`, `<state>` without `doctor/`, `<config>` and `<cache>`; `doctor --json` twice; every tree unchanged; the two `findings` arrays equal after stripping the declared volatile keys.

### 4. Contract rows (`tests/contract/matrix.rs`, E3's doctor rows; one snapshot file each)

- `doctor_skill_drift`: setup `claude_ready`, `skill_install(None)`, `skill_edited(<skills>)`, `skill_install(Some(<second>))`, `skill_outdated(<second>)`; `doctor --only fm-plugins-skill-version-drift --json` → exit 1; snapshot.
- `doctor_fix_skill_edited_refused`: the same setup; `doctor fix --only fm-plugins-skill-version-drift --json` → exit 4, `doctor_refused`; snapshot.

The harness's doctor mode validates both envelopes against the published schemas (the new evidence keys, `details.path`) and parses every argv they hold. Both rows are machine-level and create no `WTF/`.

### 5. The cached-tier measurement (`tests/perf.rs`)

`skill_drift_detector_stays_within_its_cached_share`, `#[ignore = "a release-build budget: cargo test --release --test perf -- --ignored"]`:
- A `TestEnv` home: `claude_ready`; `robot-docs install-skill` into `<skills>` and into seven `--dir` folders under the env root (through the binary, so the projection is real); each `SKILL.md` then replaced by `restamped_guide(…)` (outdated: every file is hashed in full).
- In process: `let paths = Paths::with_roots(env.home(), env.config(), env.state(), env.cache());` then `median_of_21(|| { let view = DoctorView::load_at(paths.clone(), ViewOptions { discovery: ViewDiscovery::Cached }); let d = doctor::detect(&view, &Selection::only(&[ids::SKILL_VERSION_DRIFT]), Tier::Cached); assert_eq!(d.findings.len(), 8); })`.
- Budget: median under 1 ms. `measured(...)` prints `skill drift detector: median …, p95 …, 8 skills of <n> bytes` for H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`).

Decided while writing this bead: the detector's share is 1 ms of `status --cached`'s 5 ms (eight reads and SHA-256s of about 30 KiB each plus nine `stat`s), measured in process because `status` does not run this row until F8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.8`), whose `status --cached` test then holds the whole budget.

**Files:** `tests/common/doctor.rs` (`plant::skill_*`), `tests/doctor/fixtures/fm_plugins_skill_version_drift.rs` (new), `tests/doctor/fixtures/mod.rs`, `tests/doctor_skill.rs` (new), `tests/contract/matrix.rs` and two snapshots, `tests/perf.rs`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The fixture `fm_plugins_skill_version_drift.rs` exists with its README doc comment, `fixer() == true`, is in `fixtures::all()`, and its `corrupt`, `assert_healthy` and `subject` behave as section 2 says.
- [ ] Every scenario of section 3 passes in the gate, and `argc e2e doctor_skill` runs the suite with verbose logs.
- [ ] Scenario 1 shows detect, a bound fix, verify (`DONE_OK`), byte-identical backups, one repair history line and idempotence; scenarios 2–6 show that current skills, edited copies of the current guide, links to the current guide, dangling links and deleted folders are never findings, and that edited, linked, non-regular and unreadable skills are reported with their remediations and never rewritten.
- [ ] Scenarios 7 and 8 show `check-incomplete` (`skill_dirs`, `history_projection`) exactly when the folder list is cut short or unknown, and never otherwise.
- [ ] Scenarios 10 and 11 show that a change after the preview stales a bound run, a change during the repair rolls it back, and a crash before or after `done` on a `--dir` folder recovers to the whole before or after state, repeatably.
- [ ] The two contract rows pass with their snapshots in the doctor mode.
- [ ] `skill_drift_detector_stays_within_its_cached_share` passes in a release build (median under 1 ms), and its measured line is recorded in the close comment.
- [ ] The closing agent of this subtask verifies every acceptance criterion of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.10 with evidence (test names, the commit, `argc e2e doctor_skill`'s summary and log root, the perf line), and closes omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.10 with the close comment its body asks for (the wire names, the Appendix B line, each "Decided while writing this bead" item confirmed or adjusted).
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files; `br lint` is clean.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

None in `src/` (parts 1 and 2 carry them). The planting helpers are checked by the scenarios that use them: each helper's state is asserted through the finding's `reason` (or its absence) the first time it is used.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

The twelve scenarios of section 3 in `tests/doctor_skill.rs`, the fixture of section 2 (also run by the harness of F9, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`), and the two contract rows of section 4. Failpoints used: `doctor.repair.step@2=pause`, `doctor.repair.step@2=abort`, `doctor.repair.done=abort`. Recovery is driven by `config set check_interval_hours 6`. No scenario creates `WTF/`, so `assert_private_all` is not required; scenario 12 still checks that no output holds the planted marker.

### Logging

- Every scenario opens `let log = tlog!();` and names its phases with `log.step`: "home", "install", "plant", "diagnose", "explain", "preview", "fix", "verify", "again", "manual fix", "edit", "crash", "reader", "recover".
- Every command goes through `log.run`/`log.cmd`, so its argv, environment overrides (failpoints, the pause dir), exit, envelope, stderr events and `net.log` lines are in `steps.jsonl` and `transcript.md`.
- Trees: `log.tree` of each skill folder (labelled `skill default`, `skill second`, `skill c<i>`), of `<root>/dotfiles`, of `<state>` without `doctor/`, of `<config>` and of `<cache>`; every "unchanged" claim is `log.assert_unchanged`, which logs the first differing paths.
- Before asserting, `log.json` records the findings, `actions_planned`, `actions`, the `since` block, `skill_dirs(&env)`, the repair history line, each skill file's `{len, sha256, mode}` and each backup's `{len, sha256}`. File contents are never logged.
- Table-driven scenarios log one `log.case(<name>)` per case, so a failing case's transcript stands alone; a skipped root-only case logs why.
- On a failure, the guard of T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`) prints `test log: <path>` and the last 20 steps; `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG=verbose argc e2e doctor_skill` echoes every step live.

### Checkpoint-only test

`cargo test --release --test perf -- --ignored skill_drift_detector_stays_within_its_cached_share` (section 5), run by this subtask and again by the perf pass of H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`). No `SKIP` applies.

## Considerations

- **Runtime.** About ninety commands; scenario 7 installs nine skills. Keep homes small and never share one between scenarios. A slow scenario is fixed by smaller setups, never by loosening an assertion.
- **Root.** `unreadable` and any chmod-based case skip as root with a logged reason, as the existing suites do.
- **Collateral.** If another suite's clean-home assertion now meets `check-incomplete` (`history_projection`) because its home writes `history.jsonl` by hand, fix that home in this commit and list it in the close comment.
- **Hot spots:** `tests/common/doctor.rs` and `tests/doctor/fixtures/mod.rs` (shared with E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`), the other catalog leaves from F1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1`) to F7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.7`), and F9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`): append, rebase); `tests/contract/matrix.rs` (append rows, one snapshot file each); `tests/perf.rs` (append one test).
- **What F9 adds on top:** the undo round trip (`doctor undo` → the subject byte-identical, modes included), every crash boundary with recovery crashed at every inverse, two concurrent fixers, the no-false-positive home, and the pair with the credential mode. Keep the fixture's `subject` exact for it.

## Dependencies

- Parent: F10 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.10`, skill drift).
- Before it: part 1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.10.1`, the Skill layer and the detector) and part 2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.10.2`, the rewrite fixer), whose behaviour this part drives end to end; T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs), through the edge the filing adds for every bead that writes integration tests.
- After it: nothing inside F10; closing this part (the last) means verifying the leaf's acceptance criteria and closing F10, which unblocks F8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.8`), F9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`) and T4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4`, slice 3 end to end).

title: Journal fixers: the delegation and the set-aside as suspension
description:
## How to work this bead

This bead is worked through its 6 subtasks, listed below in work order. Claim a subtask, not this bead (`br ready --parent omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.2` lists the ready ones). The agent that closes the last open subtask then verifies every acceptance criterion of this bead (they are the leaf's, not any one subtask's), and closes this bead with `br close omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.2 --reason "done: <evidence> · found: <ids>"`. Until this bead is closed, every bead it blocks stays blocked.

**Size L, kept as one leaf.** The fixer, its manifest and its attribution are one consent: a set-aside without guarded reactivation, or with payload-derived paths, would be the unsafe version this leaf exists to avoid. The subtasks split the work, not the closure: this bead closes only when all six are done, so no dependent ever sees a set-aside whose guards or attribution are missing.

## Background

**What this leaf is.** Before M4, a journal that recovery cannot settle is a dead end. Recovery stops and leaves the journal, its in-flight lock, its stage and both snapshot halves for "manual repair", every later change on that client fails (on every client, when the journal's target cannot be read), and README's only advice is prose (`README.md:2521-2525`, "`doctor`, which will automate this repair, is planned for milestone 4"). A journal recovery *can* settle is finished only as a side effect of some unrelated change command. This leaf gives the doctor (built by E3, E5, E6, E7 and E14) its two journal repairs:

- **The delegation** (Appendix B rows 1 and 9: `fm-concurrency_primitives-journal-pending` and `fm-concurrency_primitives-journal-preservation-incomplete`): `doctor fix` runs the engine's own recovery for exactly the pending journals its preview disclosed, and reports each outcome.
- **The set-aside as suspension** (rows 3–8: `journal-too-new`, `journal-unreadable`, `journal-unexpected-state`, `journal-step-unrecognized`, `journal-marker-mismatch`, `journal-unattributed`): a forced repair that moves the stuck journal's whole set into quarantine, which unblocks the client, records a suspension manifest, and can be undone (the journal reactivated) only while nothing it depends on has changed.

Keeping the bytes of a stuck journal is necessary but not sufficient: putting the journal back after later work would replay stale instructions over newer folders, and an unreadable journal's paths cannot be trusted to say what it owns. Those two facts are why the set-aside is a guarded suspension with independent attribution, not a move.

**Goals served.**

- **G-M4-4 Diagnosable and repairable:** "the states README calls 'manual repair' today each get a name, an explanation and a guarded repair"; "a repair can be undone byte for byte as long as no later change overlaps what it touched; once one does, undo refuses before moving anything, and the kept bytes stay inspectable"; "`status` and `doctor` never disagree about what is wrong".
- **G-M4-6 No new risk to the engine's guarantees:** every repair is a journaled transaction that recovers like any other; the doctor never writes `WTF/` (finishing an interrupted restore stays the engine's recovery, as `BackupRestore`, only while the game is closed).
- **G-M4-3 What was previewed is what runs:** a bound `doctor fix` runs exactly the disclosed recoveries and primitives, or nothing.

**Checkpoint criteria this leaf is responsible for** (§3.2):

- **11, stuck states are named and repairable:** the guarded repairs of the force-gated states suspend the journal set and unblock the client; while nothing that overlaps the suspended set has changed, `doctor undo` reactivates it byte-identical, after which recovery behaves exactly as before the repair; after an overlapping change (a later install on that client), `doctor undo` refuses with `undo_conflict` before moving anything, and the set stays inspectable in quarantine; a crash at any point of a reactivation never lets ordinary recovery run the restored journal before the reactivating repair has settled; for an unreadable or newer journal, the set-aside moves only what it can attribute independently (by transaction id, in known locations, on clients whose markers check out), never a path the payload names, and reports any remainder as unattributed. (F1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1`, owns the naming half of criterion 11.)
- **10, the doctor's surface (part):** "a bound fix whose preview did not disclose a pending journal it would recover is stale before any recovery or repair moves anything", now with the real delegation fixer.
- **9, the safety harness (part):** these fixers are the ones the harness (F9, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`) round-trips with guards; this leaf makes them round-trip-ready (fix and verify here, every undo round trip there).
- **12 (part):** `status` and `doctor` show the same remediation for every journal row, because both read the same detector output.

**The decisions that shape it** (full text in the decision log comments on the milestone epic `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`):

- **M4-D37: recoverable journals are fixed by the engine's own recovery, as a declared delegation.** The fixer of `journal-pending` runs `journal::recover_under` with the doctor's held lock, for every target, with discovery, so SavedVariables follow M2's rules (only a discovered client that is not running gets its SavedVariables written; otherwise `saved_variables_deferred`). Its effects are planned and disclosed before they happen: planning predicts each pending journal's outcome with `journal::diagnose` (E11, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.11`), so the preview lists every recovery it will run, `{tx, family, phase, direction, protected resources}`, and the token covers them (M4-D44). Under the lock the doctor re-plans and compares the token **before** the first recovery (M4-D45), then executes only the recoveries its plan disclosed. A pending journal that appeared since the preview stales a bound run; an unbound run includes it in its own plan. Effects are recorded where every recovery records them (the recovered transaction's journal and history), and the report lists them under `delegated: [{fm, tx, outcome: rolled_back|rolled_forward|waiting|failed}]`. `doctor undo` does not revert a delegated action: a rolled-forward transaction is undone with `omaddons undo <tx>`, and a rollback needs no undo; `explain` says so. *Why:* every change command already runs this recovery; re-implementing it inside a repair would duplicate the engine's most-tested code; the inverse of a roll-forward is the transaction's own undo. *Rejected:* (i) making recovery a repair action (a second recovery implementation); (ii) excluding journal-pending from the doctor (users would have to learn that "run any change" is the fix).
- **M4-D38: the stuck journal states get a guarded "set aside" repair, which suspends the journal and reactivates it only while that is safe.**
  - *Set-aside is suspension:* one `RenameNoReplace` primitive per artifact of the journal set (the journal file `.jsonl` or `.wtf.jsonl`, its in-flight lock file, its state snapshot half, its client stage and snapshot half), each into its own filesystem's quarantine root.
  - *A suspension manifest,* recorded in the repair's `prepared` line and in the history line's primitives as `guards`: each artifact's independently validated identity and stamp (the primitives' `pre` predicates), the target's key, the client marker's digest, the target's record generation, and the epochs of the resources the suspended journal would touch on recovery (the live stamps of the folders its steps name; for a `WTF/` journal one digest of the `WTF/` tree's stamps, never a path below it, so no account or character name enters history).
  - *Reactivation is guarded:* `doctor undo` of a set-aside checks every guard under the lock before moving anything; a moved generation (a later install or update), a changed marker or a changed epoch is `undo_conflict` with `details.reason: "changed_since_suspension"` and `details.changed`, and nothing moves. The bytes stay in quarantine, readable.
  - *An activation barrier* (E14, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14`, and E7, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7`): the undo restores the journal under the provisional name `<tx>.reactivating.jsonl` (which no listing parses), every other artifact, and activates the journal last by renaming it to its own name; recovery resolves repairs that own a barrier before folder journals, so a crash anywhere in a reactivation never lets the folder pass run the restored journal ahead of the undo that exposed it.
  - *Unreadable and newer journals: attribute independently, never follow the payload.* The set is what can be attributed by the transaction id in known locations (`<state>/journal/`, `<state>/inflight/`, `<state>/snapshots/`, each client's `<meta>/stage/` and `<meta>/snapshots/`), on clients whose markers check out. The finding and the report state `attribution: complete | partial` and list what may remain unaccounted for. Nothing claims the whole set was repaired when that cannot be known.
  - *Preconditions:* the in-flight lock is free (the writer is dead); the global lock is held; the client is not running (running unknown counts as running, M2's fail-closed rule).
  - *Consent:* `auto_fixable: false`; it runs only with `--only <fm> --force --yes` and is never part of a default `doctor fix`.
  - *`explain`* states what the set holds (counts of folders and files, whether a folder may be the only copy), the attribution, that undo is possible only while nothing on that client has changed, and the safer alternative if any: for `journal_too_new`, finishing with the newer build.
  - *Not covered:* `journal-preservation-incomplete` resumes by itself once its cause (usually disk space) is gone, so its remediation is that advice plus the delegation; a restore journal waiting for the game is the delegation's job once the game exits.
  - *Why:* README's dead end is the doctor's main reason to exist (G7); setting aside keeps every byte, unblocks the client and is reversible; keeping bytes is not the same as being safe to put them back; a binary that cannot read a journal has no business deriving client-side write authority from the paths inside it. *Rejected:* (i) guessing a direction and finishing the transaction (M3-D45: never act on what you cannot read); (ii) deleting the journal (forbidden); (iii) a default fix (it changes how an interrupted change ends, which needs explicit consent); (iv) an unconditional restore on undo (it activates stale instructions after later work).
  - *Departure from the vision:* undo of a set-aside is conditional ("undoable while nothing it depends on has changed, and inspectable until gc").
- **Obeyed, implemented elsewhere:** M4-D31 (a repair is lowered to primitives, each one filesystem operation with its own write-ahead step; E5, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`, lowers, journals, commits and recovers); M4-D35 (quarantine never crosses a filesystem: `<state>` victims go to `<run>/quarantine/state/…`, client victims to `<meta>/snapshots/<repair tx>.repair/quarantine/…`); M4-D36 (nothing but `doctor gc` deletes what a repair keeps, and gc pins suspended sets while their manifests are reachable; E8, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.8`); M4-D39 (`enabled: false` fixers run only with an explicit `--only`); M4-D40 (`doctor_refused` and its closed reason set, `plan_stale` exits 4); M4-D44 (the token's canonical form: delegations enter `selection` as `{tx, family, phase, direction}`, their protected resources enter `observed`; nothing run-specific); M4-D45 (the fixed order under the lock: fresh view, re-plan, token check, only then the delegation, then the primitives); M4-D46 (a repair is undone by `omaddons undo`, strictly, with guards and the activation-aware inverse; E7); M4-D48 (the published `journal-pending` is narrowed to journals recovery can settle; F1); M4-D53 (`status` issues carry `auto_fixable` and `explain`; an auto-fixable finding's remediation is `omaddons doctor fix --only <fm> [-t <id>]`; F8, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.8`); M4-D62 (resources, fences, undo conflicts and gc pins share one resource model; E13, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.13`, E14); M3-D29 (`WTF/` is never written while the game runs, or may run); M3-D45 (never act on what this build cannot read).

**Plan statements adapted to the code** (each is handled in Technical Approach and listed in the planning record):

- The plan says the delegation "runs `journal::recover_under`". At `c0ab5e9` that function returns only warnings and recovers every journal whose writer is gone. M4-D37 needs per-transaction outcomes and "only the recoveries its plan disclosed", so this leaf runs recover_under's code path restricted to the disclosed transactions, with outcomes (Technical Approach §1.3).
- Appendix B row 8 says the set-aside of `journal-unattributed` is "state side only". Attribution by transaction id can find that transaction's client halves on clients whose markers check out, and leaving them would expose them to the orphan sweep once the journal is gone. This leaf moves them too, by the same rule as every other row (Technical Approach §2).
- M4-D38 names "its in-flight lock file"; `is_live` also probes the cache scratch lock. The cache scratch (`<cache>/tmp/<tx>`, `<cache>/inflight/<tx>.lock`) holds downloads and clones that recovery never reads; it is not part of the set, and the blob cache's sweep reclaims it as for every dead transaction (decided while writing this bead).

**How it serves the vision.** G7, "`doctor` follows the world-class doctor contract": every fix has a recorded inverse (a roll-forward's is the transaction's undo; a set-aside's is its guarded reactivation), and the doctor never deletes. The thesis that omaddons stays the sole, safe, undoable authority over what it manages: the one state where omaddons used to give up ("left for manual repair") becomes a consented, journaled, undoable repair that never trusts what it cannot read.

### 1. The delegation (rows 1 and 9; s1)

**1.1 The fixer row.** Rows 1 and 9 get `fix: Some(FixerSpec { plan: recover::plan, writes_to: &[State, ClientMeta, AddOns], ops: &[FixKind::Delegate], enabled: true, needs_force: false, cardinality: Low, preconditions: &[LockHeld] })`. It is part of a default `doctor fix`. `writes_to` lists what the engine's recovery writes through scopes the doctor declares; a delegated recovery of a restore or of an undo may also write `WTF/` or SavedVariables, as `BackupRestore` or `Undo`, under the engine's own rules, and the row's `why` text says so (capabilities' scope names have no `WTF` row, and the doctor's own writes never touch it).

**1.2 Planning.** `pub fn plan(view: &DoctorView, finding: &Finding) -> Result<Vec<Fix>, Refusal>` looks the finding's transaction up in the view's Journals layer (`journal::diagnose`'s `JournalDiagnosis`, as E11, E5 and E14 left it) and returns `vec![Fix::Delegate { what }]` with `what = delegation_for(&diagnosis)`, or `Ok(vec![])` when there is none to run. `delegation_for` maps the prediction to E1's `Delegation { tx, family, phase, direction }`:

| Prediction (`JournalDiagnosis`) | `family` | `phase` | `direction` |
|---|---|---|---|
| folder, recoverable, phase prepared, rolls back | `folder` | `prepared` | `roll_back` |
| folder, recoverable, phase swapped, rolls forward | `folder` | `swapped` | `roll_forward` |
| folder or repair, no complete `prepared` line (recovery only removes it) | as found | `unprepared` | `roll_back` |
| folder, preservation pending and resumable (`PreservationIncomplete { stops: false }`) | `folder` | `preserve` | `roll_back` |
| repair, recoverable, before `done` | `repair` | `prepared` or `step` | `roll_back` |
| repair, recoverable, `done` | `repair` | `done` | `roll_forward` |
| a held in-flight lock (`live: true`), a predicted stop, waits for the game, behind a barrier, committed | none | | |

- Decided while writing this bead: a journal with no complete `prepared` line ran nothing, and recovery only removes it; it is disclosed as `{phase: "unprepared", direction: "roll_back"}` (F1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1`, added `JournalPhase::unprepared`) and its outcome is `rolled_back` (the rollback of zero steps, which needs no undo). E11's `Prune` direction maps to `roll_back`.
- E6 builds each `PlannedRecovery { fm, tx, family, phase, direction, protected }` from the transaction's own diagnosis and drops a delegated transaction that has no direction any more; `delegation_for` returns the same values, so the fix and E6's expansion can never disagree.
- Decided while writing this bead: a row-9 instance is delegated exactly while `journal::diagnose` predicts its resumption succeeds (F1's `evidence.resumable`, which is `!stops`). One predicted to stop (a published backup that does not match, an item in neither place) gets no delegation now: its plan is empty and the detector marks the instance not fixable, so its remediation is `doctor explain` only (`auto_fixable: false`); as soon as the cause is gone the prediction becomes resumable and the delegation is offered again, which is M4-D38's "retries once the cause is gone" (and F1's mapping of every `PreservationIncomplete` to row 9). A full disk is not predicted by `diagnose` (an I/O failure is outside any prediction), so it stays delegated and ends `failed` until space is freed. E6 drops a delegation without a direction anyway.
- An empty plan is how a fixer says "nothing to do for this instance": E6 reports the instance among the unfixable ones (exit 1 when only such instances remain, never 2), which is also what F9's idempotence property requires.
- E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`, `doctor fix`) puts each `Delegation` into `delegated_planned` and the token's `selection`, and the diagnosis's protected resources into `observed` (M4-D44). This leaf adds nothing to the token.

**1.3 Execution: exactly the disclosed recoveries.** E6 built the seam (`src/doctor/delegate.rs`): `trait RecoveryDelegate { fn recover(&self, lock: &GlobalLockGuard, disclosed: &[PlannedRecovery]) -> Result<Vec<DelegatedOutcome>>; }`, called exactly once, under the global lock, after the fresh re-plan and the `--if-match` comparison, with exactly the disclosed recoveries; production passes `&NoDelegate` until this leaf. This leaf adds `JournalDelegate { paths, targets /* the view's Discovery layer */, actor }` in `src/doctor/fixers/recover.rs`, implements the trait, and makes the `doctor fix` dispatch arm pass it instead of `NoDelegate`. Decided while writing this bead: the trait's return gains the warnings the recovery produced (`Result<DelegationReport { delegated: Vec<DelegatedOutcome>, warnings: Vec<Warning> }>`), because E6's signature has no channel for them; update `NoDelegate`, E6's recording fake and the runtime (which adds the warnings to the report) in the same commit.

1. **The running scan, last before recovery.** One fresh `discover::running::detect_running(self.targets)`. `sv_writable(dir)` is true only when `scan.unavailable` is `None`, some target in `self.targets` has `same_dir(&t.client_dir, dir)`, and that target's dir is not in `scan.clients`: the rule of `engine::tx::sv_writable` (`src/engine/tx.rs:598-603`), built from the doctor's view. With no Discovery layer (a broken config), no client is writable: a `writes_wtf` journal then waits and an undo's SavedVariables restore is deferred, which is the safe side.
2. **Recovery, restricted.** Call the engine's recovery for the disclosed transaction ids only, with per-transaction outcomes:
   - If E6 or E14 already exposes such an entry point, use it.
   - Otherwise add it in `src/engine/journal.rs`, beside `recover_under` and sharing its code path: `pub fn recover_disclosed(lock: &GlobalLockGuard, paths: &Paths, sv_writable: &dyn Fn(&Path) -> bool, command: &str, actor: Actor, only: &BTreeSet<TxId>) -> Disclosed { outcomes: Vec<TxOutcome>, warnings: Vec<Warning> }`. `RecoveryEnv` gains `only: Option<&'a BTreeSet<TxId>>` (`None` everywhere else, so every existing caller behaves exactly as before) and an outcome sink. In every pass of the loop (E14's three passes: repairs owning a barrier, folder journals, the other repairs), a journal whose transaction is not in `only` is skipped exactly as a journal with a live in-flight lock is skipped: left as it is, with no warning and no error. `TxOutcome { tx, family, result: RolledBack | RolledForward | Pruned | Stopped { code: ErrorCode, reason: Option<String> } }` records what recovery did to each transaction it reached, and the warnings recovering it produced. `recover_under` becomes `recover_disclosed`'s body with `only: None` and the outcomes dropped. The filter lives in the pass loop, never inside `engine::repair::recover`.
   - Decided while writing this bead, why a filter and not a plain `recover_under` call: under the lock held since the re-plan, the recoverable set can still change if a writer that held its in-flight lock (one whose own in-process rollback failed) exits between the re-plan and recovery; `recover_under` would then recover a journal nobody approved, breaking M4-D44's "exactly that or nothing". Skipping an undisclosed journal, an unattributed one included, adds no hazard: today's `recover_all` already recovers every journal that sorts before an unattributed one, and a disclosed journal's own client dir was verified by its marker.
   - Hot spot: `src/engine/journal.rs` (E11 → E13 → E5 → E14 → F1). This leaf lands after all five; rebase, touch only the pass loop, `RecoveryEnv` and the new wrapper, and keep `tests/journal.rs`, `tests/engine_crash.rs` and the in-crate recovery tests green unchanged.
3. **Outcomes.** One `DelegatedOutcome` per disclosed transaction, in disclosure order:

   | Recovery's result for that transaction | `outcome` | `reason` |
   |---|---|---|
   | rolled back | `rolled_back` | absent |
   | rolled forward | `rolled_forward` | absent |
   | removed with nothing run (`Pruned`) | `rolled_back` | absent |
   | stopped with `game_running` (`details.reason: "saved_variables"`) | `waiting` | `saved_variables` |
   | stopped with any other error | `failed` | the error's `details.reason`, else its code's wire name (`io`, `internal`, …) |
   | not reached (the call failed before it, say an unlistable journal directory) | `failed` | the call's error reason, else its code |

   A `waiting` or `failed` outcome leaves the journal; VERIFYING then finds the finding still present and the run is `DONE_PARTIAL` (exit 2, §6.12: "a delegated recovery that did not settle a journal also makes the run partial").
4. **Warnings.** For each transaction that rolled back or forward, its `journal_recovered` warning becomes one `delegated_recovery` warning with the same message text (which already says whether a snapshot was kept, and how many folders are in it), prefixed `doctor fix: `, and the fix `omaddons undo <tx>` (argv `["omaddons","undo","<tx>"]`) when it rolled forward, or `omaddons history --limit 5` when it rolled back. Every other warning recovery produced (`saved_variables_deferred`, `restore_rolled_back`, `journal_pending` for a journal it left) passes through unchanged. Decided while writing this bead: replace rather than duplicate, because the two would describe one event twice (§8.1.2, token-frugal), and the delegated one carries strictly more (the undo argv).
5. **The doorbell** rings once (`command: "doctor fix"`) when anything was recovered, as `recover_under` does.

`why` texts (registry rows; H1 reviews every one for clarity; no runnable command in prose):

- Row 1: "An interrupted change is waiting to be finished. `doctor fix` finishes it with omaddons' own recovery, the same one every change command runs first: it rolls the change back, or forward when its renames had all completed. The preview lists every recovery before it runs. This is not a doctor repair, so the doctor's undo does not revert it: a change that recovery completed is undone like any other change, by its transaction id; one it rolled back needs no undo. An interrupted settings restore is finished only while its game is closed."
- Row 9: "Recovering an interrupted `WTF/` restore could not finish giving the settings it displaced a home as a `recovered` backup, usually because the disk was full or an I/O error occurred. Everything is still in place under the transaction's stage. Recovery resumes with the same backup id once the cause is gone: free space or fix the error, then run the fix. When the evidence says resumption would stop for another reason, no fix is offered and the evidence names what blocks it."

### 2. Attribution without the payload (rows 3–8; s2)

`src/doctor/attribution.rs` (read-only: no `fsx::` write, no `WriteSession`; the detectors' source scan is extended to this file). Decided while writing this bead: a module of its own, beside the detectors, because both the detectors (for evidence) and the fixer (for its plan) call it.

```rust
pub struct JournalAttribution {
    pub artifacts: Vec<Artifact>,          // existing, attributed, ordered as Technical Approach §4 moves them
    pub clients: Vec<(PathBuf, TargetKey)>,// the checked-out clients that hold an artifact
    pub attribution: Attribution,          // Complete | Partial (E1)
    pub unattributed: Vec<PathBuf>,        // sorted, deduplicated directories
    pub incomplete: bool,                  // the payload scan hit its bound
}
pub struct Artifact { pub path: PathBuf, pub kind: ArtifactKind, pub client: Option<PathBuf> }
pub enum ArtifactKind { ClientStage, ClientSnapshot, StateSnapshot, Inflight, Journal }
pub fn attribute(view: &DoctorView, d: &JournalDiagnosis, budget: &mut Budget) -> JournalAttribution;
```

1. **Checked-out clients.** Every registry entry (the view's Registry layer) whose `discover::registry::read_marker(client_dir)` equals that entry's key. A registered client whose marker is missing, malformed or another key, or whose `<meta>` cannot be stat'ed (an error other than not-found), is **unverified**.
2. **Artifacts, by name only.** For the transaction id `tx` (the one thing taken from the journal, with its raw target):
   - state side: `Paths::journal(tx)`, `journal_wtf(tx)`, `journal_repair(tx)` (E5), E14's provisional `<state>/journal/<tx>.reactivating.jsonl` (`repair::provisional_journal`, which E11's artifact search also lists), `inflight_lock(tx)`, `state_snapshot(tx)`, `state_snapshot_wtf(tx)`;
   - each checked-out client: `ClientPaths::stage(tx)`, `stage_wtf(tx)`, `snapshots(tx)`, `snapshots_wtf(tx)`, `snapshots_repair(tx)` (E5);
   - each probed with `symlink_metadata`; an existing regular file (journal, lock) or directory (stage, snapshot) is an artifact. A symlink or another kind at one of these names is not moved (fsx never renames through a symlink): its directory goes to `unattributed[]` (decided while writing this bead).
   - E11's `JournalEvidence.artifacts` already holds these for the clients `diagnose` was given; reuse its stats when they cover the same paths, but decide "checked out" here (E11's `marker_matches` compares with the journal's raw target, which is a different question).
   - Never `<state>/doctor/`: nothing but `doctor gc` touches it (M4-D36), so a stuck repair's own run directory stays in place.
3. **The payload is read, never followed.** To judge completeness, the journal's complete lines are parsed as JSON where they parse (lines that do not are skipped), and every string value that is an absolute path is collected, each charged one entry against the `Budget` (E3's handle; the fixer's plan uses a budget of `DOCTOR_SCAN_MAX_ENTRIES`, 20,000). Nothing is ever moved, written or stat'ed because the payload names it.
4. **`unattributed[]`**, sorted and deduplicated, holds directories, never a file below `Interface/` or `WTF/`:
   - each unverified registered client: its `<client dir>`;
   - each client directory the payload names that is not the checked-out client of the journal's own target (the registered target its raw `target_key` names): for a path under a registered client, that client's dir; otherwise the path cut before its first `Interface` or `WTF` component, or its parent directory when it has neither;
   - for a repair-family journal whose payload cannot be trusted (rows 3, 4 and 8 of family `repair`): `<state>/doctor/runs`, because its run directory, which holds the backups its rollback reads, cannot be identified without the payload and stays where it is.
5. **`attribution`** is `complete` when `unattributed[]` is empty and the scan was not cut short, else `partial`. So a newer journal whose payload names only its own, checked-out client is `complete` (§4.3, Appendix A.4); an unreadable journal naming another client's paths, or a marker-mismatched journal, is `partial`.
6. **Evidence.** F1's findings of rows 3–8 gain `attribution` (`"complete" | "partial"`) and `unattributed` (absolute paths) beside F1's keys (`tx`, `family`, `kind`, `phase`, `target`, `journal`, `format`, `reason`, the folder counts `stage_folders` and `snapshot_folders`, `may_hold_only_copy`), as Appendix A.4 shows:

```json
"evidence":{"tx":"01M7…","kind":"update","journal":"<state>/journal/01M7….jsonl","format":"2.0",
            "stage_folders":3,"may_hold_only_copy":true,"attribution":"complete","unattributed":[]}
```

   A cut-short scan also returns the detector's `incomplete` record, so the run reports `check-incomplete` (M4-D43). The cost fits the `cached` tier: stats of fixed names, one marker read per registered client, and one read of a journal that exists only in this rare state.

### 3. The suspension manifest (s2)

`pub fn manifest(view: &DoctorView, d: &JournalDiagnosis, a: &JournalAttribution) -> Result<Vec<Guard>>`. Every guard is built with E7's constructors (`engine::repair::guard::observe_generation(paths, key)`, `observe_marker(client_dir, key)`, `observe_folder_epoch(client_dir, key, folder)`, `observe_wtf_epoch(client_dir, key)`), and E7's `guard::current(&Guard, ctx)` re-reads exactly the same thing under the lock, so a recorded value and a checked value can never be computed two ways. Wire form (E7's, in the repair journal's `prepared` and the history line's `repairs[]`):

```json
"guards":[{"kind":"generation","target":"01M5…","value":"7"},
          {"kind":"marker","target":"01M5…","value":"sha256:…"},
          {"kind":"epoch","target":"01M5…","folder":"DBM-Core","value":"stamp:sha256:…"},
          {"kind":"epoch","target":"01M5…","folder":"WTF","value":"stamp:sha256:…"}]
```

Sorted by (kind, target, folder) for determinism:

| Guard | Recorded for |
|---|---|
| `generation` | every target whose client holds an artifact, and the journal's own target when it is registered; for a journal with no readable target (row 8), every registered target, since what it would recover could be on any client (decided while writing this bead) |
| `marker` | every target whose client holds an artifact, and the journal's own target when it is registered (its registered client dir's `<meta>/target.json`; `absent` when missing). For row 7 whose `prepared.client_dir` is the target's registered dir, this records the foreign marker, so the next change on that client (which re-marks it) makes the reactivation refuse |
| `epoch` with a folder | for a journal whose `prepared` decodes (rows 5–8): each distinct `Interface/AddOns/<folder>` its steps name on a registered client (absent ones included, value `absent`) |
| `epoch` with `folder: "WTF"` | for a journal that puts settings back (named `<tx>.wtf.jsonl`, or whose decoded `prepared` puts settings back): one stamp of that client's whole `WTF/`, never a path below it |

- E7's `details.changed` names the changed kinds from its closed set `generation`, `marker`, `epochs`, with `details.target`.
- **No path below `WTF/` ever appears:** a step path with a `WTF` component contributes the client's `WTF` epoch, never a folder epoch.
- Decided while writing this bead: **an untrusted journal (rows 3, 4 and 8) gets no folder epochs**, because the folders it would recover cannot be known without trusting its payload. Its guards are the generation and marker of every client it touches (every registered target's generation for row 8), which catch every change omaddons makes there, and, for a settings journal, the `WTF` epoch. A change made by hand inside an addon folder is not detected for these rows, and the `why` text says reactivation is refused "after any change omaddons makes on that client". Rejected: a stamp of the whole `Interface/AddOns` tree, which walks a user-sized tree under the commit lock at every undo check.
- A repair-family journal's own run directory (`<state>/doctor/runs/<doctor_run_id>/`, the backups its rollback reads) stays in place and is not guarded: E7's guards have no kind for it. E8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.8`, `doctor gc`) keeps it while the set-aside's manifest is reachable (M4-D36's pins for suspended sets); if E8's pins do not cover it when this leaf lands, file that `discovered-from` this bead.
- No new constant: epochs walk only the folders a journal names and at most one `WTF/` tree, which the engine already stamps unbounded for whole restores (M3-D25).

### 4. The set-aside fixer (rows 3–8; s3)

**4.1 The fixer row**, shared by rows 3–8: `fix: Some(FixerSpec { plan: set_aside::plan, writes_to: &[State, ClientMeta], ops: &[FixKind::Suspend], enabled: false, needs_force: true, cardinality: Low, preconditions: &[LockHeld, InflightFree, ClientNotRunning, SameFs] })`. E1's invariant ("a `needs_force` fixer is never `enabled` by default") holds.

**4.2 `plan(view, finding) -> Result<Vec<Fix>, Refusal>`**, run by E6 in PLANNING and again under the lock (so every check below is repeated immediately before any mutation):

1. Find the finding's `JournalDiagnosis`. A held in-flight lock (`live: true`) plans nothing (`Ok(vec![])`): the writer is alive and the journal is not stuck yet. E6's `InflightFree` precondition drops such a fix too ("not a refusal, because there is nothing to refuse"); a free in-flight file can never be taken again (`create_new`, `src/fsx/lock.rs:207-237`), so this is a defensive case.
2. `attribution::attribute` (Technical Approach §2), with a budget of `DOCTOR_SCAN_MAX_ENTRIES`.
3. **Running check.** The clients involved are those holding an artifact, plus those a `marker` or `epoch` guard reads (E6's `ClientNotRunning` check covers only clients a step touches; this covers the guarded ones too). One `discover::running::detect_running` scan over their discovered targets; any involved client running, or the process table unreadable while any client is involved, is `Refusal { reason: client_running, … }`, message "<client id>'s game is running, or may be; quit it before setting aside transaction <tx>". A set with no client (a state-only row 8) needs no scan.
4. `attribution::manifest` (Technical Approach §3).
5. `Ok(vec![Fix::Suspend { journal: JournalSet { tx, family, target, artifacts, guards, attribution, unattributed } }])`, where each `SuspendedArtifact { path, root }` has `root: QuarantineRoot::State` for state-side artifacts and `QuarantineRoot::Client { client_dir }` for client-side ones.

**4.3 Order of the set.** `JournalSet.artifacts` (which E5 lowers in order, one `RenameNoReplace` each) is ordered client stages, client snapshot halves, state snapshot halves, the in-flight lock, then the journal file(s) last, each group by path. Decided while writing this bead: the journal moves last so that until the final primitive the journal stays where every listing, recovery and orphan sweep (of this build and of older ones) sees it, and keeps protecting what it owns; and the order is deterministic, which E6's token needs (M4-D44). E7 reorders the inverse for activation regardless.

**4.4 Lowering and commit are E5's.** E5 resolves each root: `State` → `<run>/quarantine/state/<path relative to <state>>`; `Client { client_dir }` → `<meta>/snapshots/<repair tx>.repair/quarantine/<path relative to the client dir>` (E5's rule; the §4.3 transcript's `…/quarantine/stage/01M7…/` is illustrative). E5 refuses a cross-mount move (`filesystem_mismatch`), records each rename's `pre` (identity, and a stamp for a directory) and `post`, and puts the `JournalSet`'s guards on the primitive that moves the journal file out of `<state>/journal/` (E5's decision: the one E14's barrier order recognizes as owning a suspension). E14's excusing rule lets this set-aside commit while the stuck journal it moves fences or fails committing commands closed (only the fences of the journals a suspension moves are lifted). The repair's `prepared.client_dirs` are the checked-out clients holding an artifact, each re-validated by its marker at commit (E5).

**4.4a E6's conflict rule and the set-aside's own journal.** E6's PLANNING refuses (`fixer_conflict`) every planned fix whose resources conflict with an observed journal the plan does not delegate. A `Fix::Suspend` necessarily conflicts with the journal it suspends (its renames move exactly that journal's artifacts). Exempt exactly that pair in `src/doctor/fix.rs` (the suspend fix against the observed journal whose `tx` it names); every other observed journal still conflicts as E6 defined. Decided while writing this bead; if E6 already exempts it, keep E6's rule. A journal held behind an unsettled barrier (its evidence has `behind_barrier`, Appendix B) is therefore still refused, naming the owning repair, because the owner's protected resources are the same artifacts: the owner is set aside or recovered first.

**4.5 Consent.** E6's gate applies, unchanged: `--only <fm>` (by id) without `--force`, with a finding present, is `doctor_refused` (`force_required`, exit 4, `fix_argv` the `doctor explain` argv, never one with `--force` or `--yes`); `--force` without `--yes` is a usage error (exit 64, `details.flag: "--force"`); `--force --yes` without `--only` is a usage error too (exit 64: a forced repair is never part of a default fix); a bare `doctor fix` lists the finding under "needs force" with its remediation and does not run it; a subsystem name in `--only` (`concurrency_primitives`) never enables an `enabled: false` fixer. This leaf asserts the gate end to end with its real fixer (s5).

- Shared ending of rows 3–8: "Setting it aside is a forced repair: it moves the journal, its in-flight lock, its stage and both snapshot halves into quarantine, each on its own filesystem, and deletes nothing. The client is unblocked. Undo puts the whole set back exactly, but only while nothing it depends on has changed: after any install, update or other change omaddons makes on that client, a change to its marker, or (where the journal can be read) a change to a folder it names or to its `WTF/` folder, undo refuses with `undo_conflict` and the set stays in quarantine, readable. - Row 5 (`journal-unexpected-state`): "Recovering an interrupted `WTF/` restore found something it did not record where a step left it, and stopped with everything exactly as found. Every change on this client fails until it is resolved. The set-aside, and its undo, need the game closed."
- Row 6 (`journal-step-unrecognized`): "Rolling back an interrupted change met a step whose paths match neither its before nor its after state, so recovery stopped; the steps after it were already reversed. Every change on this client fails (for a repair transaction, every change that touches what it protects)."
- Row 7 (`journal-marker-mismatch`): "The journal names a client directory whose identity marker belongs to another client, so recovery never writes there, and every change on this client fails. A set-aside moves only what it finds by the transaction id on clients whose markers check out; whatever is in the mismatched directory stays where it is and is listed."
- Row 8 (`journal-unattributed`): "A journal whose client cannot be read blocks every change on every client. A set-aside moves the journal and everything its transaction id names in omaddons' own directories on clients whose markers check out."

### 5. Reactivation (E7's and E14's machinery; what this leaf proves)

`doctor undo <run>` (and `omaddons undo <repair tx>`, bare `doctor undo`, `undo --last-by`) of a set-aside is E7's generic inverse of the history line's `repairs[]`: strict predicates, every guard checked under the lock before anything moves, `undo_conflict` (`details.reason: "changed_since_suspension"`, `details.changed` naming the changed guard kinds from E7's closed set `generation`, `marker`, `epochs`, and `details.target`), the journal restored first under the provisional `<tx>.reactivating.jsonl` (E14's rule 3: provisional first, so the orphan sweep never sees a reactivating transaction as dead), every other artifact after it, and the activation rename last, in its own run directory of kind `undo`. ## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **Delegation:** a recoverable journal is recovered by `doctor fix` (default and `--only fm-concurrency_primitives-journal-pending`), and `delegated[]` records `{fm, tx, family, outcome}`: an interrupted install rolled back (client tree equals its pre-install hash) and a swapped update rolled forward (equals its post-update hash), each with a `delegated_recovery` warning naming the transaction and its outcome, whose fix is `omaddons undo <tx>` when rolled forward; a crashed repair-family journal is delegated the same way (`family: "repair"`).
- [ ] **A bound fix whose preview did not include a pending journal is stale before any recovery runs:** `doctor fix --dry-run`, then a second interrupted transaction, then `doctor fix --if-match <token>` exits 4 with `plan_stale` (`details.changed` includes `selection`), both journals and every subject tree hash unchanged, apart from the run's own run directory.
- [ ] The delegation runs only the disclosed recoveries: with two recoverable journals and a recovery restricted to one, the other is left byte-identical; every existing recovery suite passes unchanged.
- [ ] A delegated recovery that fails (`engine.recover.step=error`) is `outcome: "failed"` with its `reason`, the run is `DONE_PARTIAL` (exit 2), the journal stays, and the next `doctor fix` recovers it.
- [ ] An interrupted restore journal is never delegated while its game runs or may run (it is `journal-waits-for-game`, no action), and is delegated once the game is closed; no output on any channel names an account, realm or character.
- [ ] A resumable `journal-preservation-incomplete` is delegated and resumes once its cause is gone; one whose resumption `diagnose` predicts will stop plans nothing and offers only `doctor explain`.
- [ ] `doctor undo` never reverts a delegation: a run with only delegations commits no repair transaction (`tx: null`), bare `doctor undo` does not select it, and the recovered transaction's tree is unchanged by any `doctor undo`.
- [ ] **Set-aside gate:** each of rows 3–8 is set aside only with `--only <id> --force --yes`; `--only <id>` without `--force` exits 4 (`doctor_refused`, `force_required`); `--force` without `--yes`, and `--force --yes` without `--only`, exit 64; a bare `doctor fix` and `--only concurrency_primitives --force --yes` do not run it and list it as needing `--only <id> --force --yes`; nothing in the set moves in any of these.
- [ ] After a set-aside, a change on that client succeeds (for row 8, a change on every client).
- [ ] The set-aside moves exactly the attributed set, one rename per artifact, the journal file last, each into the quarantine root on its own filesystem; nothing is copied or deleted (each quarantined artifact hashes as the original did); its dry run writes nothing outside its run directory, and a bound run after a change to any artifact is `plan_stale` with nothing moved.
- [ ] A set-aside is refused (`doctor_refused`, `client_running`) while a client the set touches or guards runs, or while running cannot be determined.
- [ ] The quarantined set survives retention and the orphan sweep after later changes on that client (aged past `ORPHAN_MIN_AGE`).
- [ ] **Reactivation:** with nothing changed since, `doctor undo` reactivates the set byte-identical (bytes, modes, kinds), and the next lock-taking command then reports the same state as before (the same error code and `details.reason` on that client's commands, the same `journal_pending` warning elsewhere, the same `status` issue ids and instance keys).
- [ ] **Set-aside → a later install on that client → `doctor undo`:** `undo_conflict` with `details.reason: "changed_since_suspension"` and `details.changed` naming the generation, nothing moved, the set intact in quarantine; a changed marker (`marker`), a changed folder named by a readable journal and a changed `WTF/` of a settings journal (`epochs`) each refuse the same way.
- [ ] **Crash cases of a reactivation:** a crash after every artifact restore, immediately before the activation, and between the activation and `done`: the next lock-taking command never recovers the folder journal before the reactivating repair settles, and the end state is the whole before (the set in quarantine, no provisional journal) or the whole after (the set back, the journal under its own name); recovery crashed at each inverse and repeated three times gives the same end state.
- [ ] A crash at every primitive boundary of the set-aside itself leaves the whole set before (crash before the durable `done`) or after (from `done` on), with no repair journal left after recovery; an injected I/O failure at each primitive rolls it back in process (`DONE_FAILED`, exit 3).
- [ ] **Misleading payloads:** an unreadable journal whose bytes name paths in another client, and a marker-mismatched journal naming paths outside its client: only the independently attributed artifacts move, the other client's tree hashes unchanged, and the finding and the report say `attribution: "partial"` with `unattributed` naming those client directories.
- [ ] A newer journal whose payload names only its own, checked-out client reports `attribution: "complete"` and `unattributed: []`.
- [ ] An unreadable repair-family journal fails committing commands closed until its set-aside, which succeeds (with `<state>/doctor/runs` in `unattributed`), after which an install succeeds.
- [ ] Rows 3–8 carry the forced remediation (`--only <id> [-t <id>] --force --yes`, `auto_fixable: false`, `needs_force: true`, `estimated_actions` = the artifact count); rows 1 and 9 carry `doctor fix --only <id> [-t <id>]`; `status` and `doctor` show the same remediation for every journal row (made equal here or by F8, whichever lands second); `explain` names what the set holds, the attribution, that undo is possible only while nothing on that client has changed, and, for `journal-too-new`, finishing with the newer build.
- [ ] No output on any channel names an account, realm or character (`assert_private_all` over stdout and stderr with `--progress json`, for `doctor`, `doctor fix`, `doctor explain`, `doctor undo`, `status` and `history` on a `WTF/` journal's set-aside), and no evidence, history line or `unattributed` entry holds a path below `WTF/`.
- [ ] The fixtures of rows 1 and 3–9 declare their fixer, so F9's coverage test (`set(fixers) == set(fixtures with a fixer)`) holds for this leaf's rows.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; README's doctor table, status issues table, warning table, Troubleshooting and Safety model describe the delegation and the set-aside in the commits that ship them; `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` is regenerated; the close comment lists every new or changed wire name and the Appendix B lines of rows 1 and 3–9; `br lint` is clean on this bead and its subtasks.

## Considerations

- **Risk #23, guarded reactivation refuses more often than users expect** (any later install on that client blocks undo of a set-aside; likelihood medium, impact low): intended (M4-D38). The refusal names what changed, the set stays inspectable in quarantine, and `explain` says so before the user consents. Owners: this leaf and E7.
- **Risk #1, a recovery bug in the repair journal** (likelihood medium, impact high): this leaf adds no protocol. The set-aside is lowered, journaled and recovered by E5's machinery and reactivated through E7's and E14's, each landed with its own crash matrix; s6 repeats the crash property on the real fixer, and anything it finds is fixed in the owning leaf and filed `discovered-from` this bead.
- **Risk #21, fences scoped wrong** (likelihood medium, impact medium): the suspended set's resources (its target and what its journal would recover) are E14's fence when the set-aside's own repair is ever stuck; this leaf supplies them through the `JournalSet` and its guards.
- **Partial attribution leaves leftovers exposed.** A stage left in an unverified client (a missing or foreign marker) is not moved and is listed; once the journal is in quarantine, that client's next change heals its marker (`registry.rs:300-313`) and its orphan sweep may then remove the leftover. The plan accepts partial attribution and moves only what is independently attributed; this leaf makes the risk visible before consent (`unattributed[]`, the `explain` text, `may_hold_only_copy`) rather than writing into a client whose identity it cannot verify. Decided while writing this bead.
- **The delegation's restriction touches `src/engine/journal.rs`,** a hot spot whose order is E11 → E13 → E5 → E14 → F1. This leaf lands after all five; it changes only the pass loop, `RecoveryEnv` and one wrapper, and every recovery suite must pass unchanged.
- **Other hot spots:** `src/error.rs` (append the warning row with its meaning; get the count right), `src/doctor/detectors/concurrency.rs` (F1's; this leaf changes rows 1 and 3–9's remediations and evidence only), `src/doctor/registry.rs` (rows' `fix` and `why` only), `src/output/` (the doctor renderers: additive lines), `tests/doctor_repair.rs` (shared with E6, E7, E14: append, rebase before each gate run), `README.md` (own sections), `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` (regenerate, never merge by hand).
- **Older builds.** The M3 build cannot read `.repair` names or `<tx>.reactivating.jsonl` (`tx_named`), so a crash mid-set-aside or mid-reactivation is characterized by E9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9`); the journal-last order keeps the journal visible to it until the final primitive of a set-aside.
