title: The permissions rows: AddOns, state and cache writability
description:
Part 3 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.4 (Configs, userland state and permissions (detection only)). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

**The leaf.** F4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.4`) fills three subsystems of the doctor's catalog, `configs`, `userland_state` and `permissions`, with nine failure modes (the plan's Appendix B rows 19–27), each a pure detector over E2's tolerant `DoctorView`, registered in `src/doctor/registry.rs`'s `FAILURE_MODES` and reported by `omaddons doctor` (E3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`). It is **detection only**: no row has a fixer (M4-D48: rows with no safe automatic fix are report-only; the doctor never changes a permission, a mode or an owner of the user's directories).

**This part** delivers the subsystem's first two rows, `permissions`:

- row 26, `fm-permissions-addons-dir-not-writable` (P1, `quick`): a managed client's `Interface/AddOns` that omaddons cannot write;
- row 27, `fm-permissions-state-dir-not-writable` (P0, `quick`): `<state>` (`$XDG_STATE_HOME/omaddons`) or `<cache>` (`$XDG_CACHE_HOME/omaddons`), or one of their top-level directories, that omaddons cannot write.

Both rest on one read-only probe over `access(2)` (the plan: "`access(W_OK)` through `rustix::fs::access`, a read"). It is its own step because the probe is a self-contained piece with its own failure taxonomy and its own testing problem (root bypasses mode bits, and `EROFS` cannot be produced in a tempdir), and nothing else in the leaf touches `src/doctor/detectors/permissions.rs`.

**Why it matters.** Today nothing detects a non-writable AddOns or state directory (the plan's ground truth: "Nothing detects: … non-writable AddOns or state directories"). The first change command fails in the middle of its plan with an `io` error, often after a download. A command once run with `sudo` is the classic cause: it leaves `<state>/journal/` or `<cache>/blobs/` owned by root while the user's own directories look fine. This serves G-M4-4 ("`omaddons doctor` names every broken state omaddons can detect in what it owns or manages"), G-M4-6 (the check itself writes nothing), and, through F8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.8`), checkpoint criterion 12 (both rows are `quick`, so plain `status` will report them; row 27 is P0, so `status --check` will fail on it).

**The decisions that shape this part:**

- **M4-D29:** a `quick` detector may add "bounded listings (`<state>`, `<cache>`, `<meta>` top levels …)" and single stats to what `status --cached` reads, under 5 ms (`QUICK_DETECTOR_BUDGET`); it declares `requires`, a pure detector and a manual remediation builder.
- **M4-D30:** `instance` is `<fm-id>@<target key | machine>[:<discriminator>]`, here `path=` of the directory.
- **M4-D41:** `confidence` `high` for an answer of `access(2)` (observed directly), `medium` when the check itself failed.
- **M4-D42:** evidence holds paths and reasons, never content.
- **M4-D43:** walks are charged to the detector's `Budget`; exhaustion is `incomplete`, never clean.
- **M4-D33 (context, E3):** every diagnosis creates its run directory under `<state>/doctor/runs/` before any detector runs and exits 73 (`io`) when it cannot. That shapes how row 27 can be seen (§4).
- **Common rule 8:** a prose remediation may not name a runnable omaddons command.

**Facts this part relies on** (verified at `c0ab5e9`):

- `rustix` is a dependency with the `fs` feature (`Cargo.toml:23`). `rustix::fs::access(path, Access)` is `access(2)` (rustix 1.1.5, `fs/abs.rs:244`), with `Access::WRITE_OK` and `Access::EXEC_OK`. `tests/single_writer.rs` flags only rustix's write calls (`RUSTIX_WRITES`, `:59-93`: `rename`, `mkdir`, `chmod`, …), never `access`, and its `std::fs` patterns are write calls only; `metadata`, `symlink_metadata` and `read_dir` are reads.
- `access(2)` checks the real user id (omaddons is never set-user-id, so it is the effective one), honours ACLs, and fails with `EROFS` on a read-only filesystem for `W_OK`. Root passes mode checks, so a `chmod 0555` denies nothing as root; `common::procfs::running_as_root()` (`tests/common/procfs.rs:10-12`) is how tests detect it (`tests/discover_scan.rs:235`).
- `Target::addons_dir()` (`src/model.rs:553-558`) returns `<client dir>/Interface/AddOns`, each part spelled as on disk, even when absent ("a client creates it on its first launch", `src/state/paths.rs:502-508`); a transaction creates a missing AddOns directory (`src/engine/tx.rs:1173-1181`, `created_addons_dir`). So for a missing AddOns the directory that must be writable is its nearest existing ancestor inside the client directory.
- `Paths::state_dir()` is `<state>` and `Paths::cache_dir()` is `<cache>` (`src/state/paths.rs:153-161`); omaddons creates both on its first write. Their top-level directories are omaddons' own (`journal/`, `inflight/`, `snapshots/`, `targets/`, `trash/`, `doctor/` in `<state>`; `blobs/`, `http/`, `tmp/`, `inflight/`, `trash/`, `git-home/`, `wowi/` in `<cache>`; README "Files and state", `README.md:2269-2302`), created 0700 or 0755 (`git-home/` 0700 through fsx, `src/sources/git_hosts.rs:90-116`; the doctor's run directories stay 0700, M4-D32).
- From E1 and E2 (through E3): `Subject::{target, machine}` with `.path`, `Evidence` with `path, paths, reason`, `Remediation`, `DoctorView::world()` (`resolved.targets`, each `DiscoveredTarget { target, … }` with `target.key`), `view.paths()`, `Selection::scope` and `Scope::includes`. From E3: `Budget::{new, charge, incomplete}`, `budget::list_dir(dir, &mut Budget) -> io::Result<Listing>` (one level, sorted, charging one entry per entry, never following a symlink), the detector signature on `main`.

## Technical Approach

### 1. The writability probe (`src/doctor/detectors/permissions.rs`, new; `pub mod permissions;` in `detectors/mod.rs`)

```rust
pub(crate) enum Writability {
    Writable,
    NotWritable { reason: Denial, checked: PathBuf },  // `checked`: the directory access(2) refused
    Missing,                                           // nothing exists at or below `floor`
}
#[derive(Clone, Copy)] pub(crate) enum Denial {
    PermissionDenied, ReadOnlyFilesystem, NotADirectory, CannotCreate, Unreadable,
}
impl Denial { pub(crate) const fn as_str(self) -> &'static str; } // "permission_denied", "read_only_filesystem",
                                                                  // "not_a_directory", "cannot_create", "unreadable"
pub(crate) enum Kind { Dir, NotDir, Dangling, Missing }
pub(crate) trait Probe {
    /// `std::fs::metadata` (symlinks followed); on `NotFound`, `symlink_metadata` tells a
    /// dangling symlink (`Dangling`) from nothing (`Missing`); `ENOTDIR` on a component is `NotDir`.
    fn kind(&self, path: &Path) -> io::Result<Kind>;
    /// `rustix::fs::access(path, Access::WRITE_OK | Access::EXEC_OK)`.
    fn access_wx(&self, path: &Path) -> rustix::io::Result<()>;
}
pub(crate) struct RealProbe;  // the only production implementation
/// Whether omaddons can create and rename entries in `dir`, or create `dir` itself. Never writes.
pub(crate) fn writable_dir(dir: &Path, floor: &Path, probe: &dyn Probe) -> Writability;
```

1. `kind(dir)`:
   - `Dir` → `access_wx(dir)`: `Ok` → `Writable`; `EACCES` or `EPERM` → `PermissionDenied`; `EROFS` → `ReadOnlyFilesystem`; any other error → `Unreadable`;
   - `NotDir` or `Dangling` → `NotADirectory`;
   - an error from `kind` → `Unreadable`.
2. `Missing`: omaddons would create `dir`, so walk up `dir`'s ancestors, never above `floor`, to the nearest one that exists, and judge it as in step 1: `Writable` → `Writable`; `NotWritable { reason, .. }` of the ancestor → `NotWritable { reason: CannotCreate, checked: <ancestor> }` when the ancestor is a directory that refused, or the ancestor's own reason when it is not a directory. Nothing exists at or below `floor` → `Missing`.

Decided while writing this bead:

- **`W_OK | X_OK`, not `W_OK` alone** (the plan says `access(W_OK)`): creating or renaming an entry needs write and search permission on the directory; `chmod 0600` on a directory denies it while passing `W_OK`.
- **`access(2)`, never a mode check:** a mode check misses ACLs and read-only mounts and is wrong as root.
- **A `Probe` trait** so unit tests can answer `EPERM`, `EROFS` or `EIO`, which no tempdir produces; `RealProbe` is the only production implementation, and a unit test runs it on real tempdirs.

Titles and prose remediations by reason (`<path>` the finding's directory, `<checked>` the refused ancestor):

| `reason` | Title suffix | Remediation (prose) | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| `permission_denied` | `(permission denied)` | `give <path> back to your user, or make it writable by you (chmod u+wx); another user, such as root after a sudo run, may own it` | high |
| `read_only_filesystem` | `(read-only filesystem)` | `<path> is on a filesystem mounted read-only: remount it read-write` | high |
| `not_a_directory` | `(not a directory)` | `<path> is not a directory: move what is there aside so omaddons can create the directory` | high |
| `cannot_create` | `(it does not exist, and <checked> is not writable)` | `make <checked> writable by your user, or create <path> yourself` | high |
| `unreadable` | `(it cannot be checked)` | `check that <path> and its parent directories are reachable by your user` | medium |

Evidence `{path, reason, paths: [<checked>]}`, `paths` present only when `checked` differs from `path` (`cannot_create`). Every remediation: `argv: None`, `destructive: false`. None names an omaddons command (`chmod` and `sudo` are not omaddons commands).

### 2. Row 26, `fm-permissions-addons-dir-not-writable`

- **Row:** `permissions`, P1, `quick`, `requires: [Discovery]`, `online: false`, `cost_ms` 1, `fix: None`, `manual: Some(denial_remediation)`.
- **Detector:** for each discovered target with `key: Some` (registered: "each managed client's AddOns", Appendix B) and in scope (`Scope::includes`), `budget.charge(1)` (on `Exhausted`, return what was found with `incomplete`), then `writable_dir(&target.addons_dir(), &target.client_dir, &RealProbe)`:
  - `Writable` → nothing;
  - `Missing` (the client directory vanished since discovery) → nothing: row 22, `target-vanished`, reports a vanished client;
  - `NotWritable` → `Subject::target(&id, key).path(&addons)`, title `<id>'s AddOns directory is not writable <suffix>`, evidence and remediation as §1.
- An AddOns directory two clients share gives one finding per client, each true for that client. Unregistered clients are not checked (omaddons writes nothing there until a change registers the client, and that change reports its own `io` error).

### 3. Row 27, `fm-permissions-state-dir-not-writable`

- **Row:** `permissions`, P0, `quick`, `requires: []` (it reads only `view.paths()`, so it runs even when every layer is broken), `online: false`, `cost_ms` 1, `fix: None`, `manual: Some(denial_remediation)`.
- **Detector:** in this order, `paths.state_dir()`, `paths.cache_dir()`, then the top-level entries of each that are directories (`budget::list_dir`, sorted, charging the `Budget` per entry; a listing error, a missing root included, lists nothing; a symlink entry is judged by `access(2)`, which follows it): `writable_dir(dir, Path::new("/"), &RealProbe)`, charging one entry per directory judged. Each `NotWritable` → `Subject::machine().path(&dir)`, title `omaddons' state directory is not writable <suffix>`, `omaddons' cache directory …`, or `<name>/ in omaddons' state directory is not writable <suffix>` (or cache), evidence and remediation as §1. `Missing` cannot occur with `/` as the floor.
- Decided while writing this bead: **the top-level directories too**, not only the two roots, because a command once run with `sudo` leaves exactly those root-owned while the roots stay the user's, and two top-level listings are what the `quick` tier allows. Every directory omaddons creates there is 0700 or 0755, so a non-writable one is damage, never a design. Deeper levels are not checked.

### 4. Row 27 and the run directory

E3's runtime publishes `<state>/doctor/runs/<run>/` before any detector runs and exits 73 (`io`, `details.path`) when it cannot (M4-D33). So:

- with `<state>` not writable but `<state>/doctor/` writable (a diagnosis ran before), `doctor` runs and reports the P0 finding;
- with no writable `<state>/doctor/runs/`, `doctor` exits 73 naming the path, and the finding is seen through `doctor explain fm-permissions-state-dir-not-writable` (which creates no run directory, E3), and, once they exist, `doctor health` (E4, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4`) and `status` (F8).

The row's `why` and README row say so. Part 5 tests both paths.

### 5. Registry rows, `ids`, texts

- Insert rows 26 and 27 into `FAILURE_MODES` by id; add `ids::ADDONS_DIR_NOT_WRITABLE` and `ids::STATE_DIR_NOT_WRITABLE`. Each detector returns `Detected` as the row signature on `main` defines it.
- Texts (none names a runnable omaddons command; H1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, may polish):

  | Id | `title` | `description` | `why` |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | addons-dir-not-writable | a client's AddOns directory is not writable | omaddons cannot create or rename entries in this client's Interface/AddOns (or, before the client's first launch, in the directory that will hold it): its permissions, owner or filesystem do not allow it. | Every install, update, removal and undo on this client fails until it is writable, and omaddons never changes permissions itself. |
  | state-dir-not-writable | omaddons' state or cache directory is not writable | omaddons cannot create or rename entries in its state directory, its cache directory, or one of their top-level directories: their permissions, owner or filesystem do not allow it. | Every change command fails: transactions journal under the state directory and downloads stage under the cache. A diagnosis that cannot create its run directory exits 73. |

### 6. README (common rules 11 and 19), in this commit

- The doctor's failure-mode table (E3 created it; follow its columns): rows 26 and 27. Row 27 says that a diagnosis that cannot create its run directory exits 73 naming the path, and that `omaddons doctor explain fm-permissions-state-dir-not-writable` still reports the finding.
- Re-accept the snapshots that list failure modes where A4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`) or E4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4`) has landed (two more rows, and the `permissions` subsystem gains its first rows), and regenerate `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` with `OMADDONS_UPDATE_SKILL=1 cargo test --test skill` where B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`) lists failure modes.

### 7. What not to do

- Never change a permission, a mode or an owner, and never create a directory or a file to test writability (no "try to create a temp file": that is a write).
- No `fsx::`, no `WriteSession`, no `std::fs` write in `src/doctor/detectors/permissions.rs`; no `rustix` write call.
- Do not check `<meta>` (`Interface/.omaddons`) under row 26: the row is AddOns'. A non-writable `Interface/` usually denies both; a separate `<meta>` row is not in the catalog.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Rows `fm-permissions-addons-dir-not-writable` and `fm-permissions-state-dir-not-writable` are in `FAILURE_MODES` with the metadata and texts of Technical Approach §2–§5, `ids` holds both, and E1's invariant test passes.
- [ ] `writable_dir` classifies writable, `EACCES`, `EPERM`, `EROFS`, a non-directory, a dangling symlink, `ENOTDIR`, other errors, and a missing directory under a writable or a non-writable ancestor exactly as Technical Approach §1 says, through `access(2)` with `W_OK | X_OK` and nothing else.
- [ ] Row 26 reports each registered client in scope whose AddOns (or, when it is missing, the nearest existing directory that would hold it) is not writable, skips vanished and unregistered clients, and row 27 reports `<state>`, `<cache>` and each of their non-writable top-level directories, machine-scoped, each with `{path, reason, paths?}` evidence and prose naming no omaddons command.
- [ ] With a one-entry `Budget`, rows 26 and 27 stop after one item and return `incomplete`.
- [ ] `tests/single_writer.rs` passes, and `src/doctor/detectors/permissions.rs` contains no write call of any kind.
- [ ] README's doctor table has rows 26 and 27, in this commit; snapshots that list failure modes are re-accepted where A4 or E4 has landed, and `SKILL.md` regenerated where B1 lists them.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes and `ubs` is clean on the changed files.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

Each table-driven, one name per case; every assertion message names the case and shows the probe's answers and the observation.

- **`src/doctor/detectors/permissions.rs`:**
  - `writable_dir_cases`, over a fake `Probe` answering per path: `writable`, `eacces`, `eperm`, `erofs`, `not_a_directory`, `dangling_symlink`, `enotdir_component`, `eio_from_access` (`Unreadable`), `kind_error` (`Unreadable`), `missing_writable_parent` (`Writable`), `missing_unwritable_parent` (`CannotCreate`, `checked` the parent), `missing_two_levels_up`, `missing_parent_not_a_directory` (`NotADirectory`, `checked` the file), `missing_up_to_floor` (`Missing`): expected `Writability`.
  - `real_probe_on_tempdirs`: a 0755 directory is `Writable`, a 0555 one `PermissionDenied`, a 0600 one `PermissionDenied` (search denied), a missing child of a 0555 one `CannotCreate`, a regular file `NotADirectory`, a dangling symlink `NotADirectory`; the mode cases are skipped as root (`rustix::process::geteuid().is_root()`), the assertion message saying so; modes are restored before the tempdir drops.
  - `addons_rows`, over `DoctorView::preloaded` with a fake probe: one case per reason (instance `@<key>:path=<AddOns>`, label, title, evidence, prose), `missing_addons_under_writable_interface` (none), `missing_addons_under_unwritable_interface` (`cannot_create`, `paths: [<Interface>]`), `vanished_client_skipped`, `unregistered_client_not_checked`, `out_of_scope_skipped`, `shared_addons_two_findings`, `budget_stops_after_one_target` (two denied clients, a one-entry `Budget`: one observation and `incomplete`).
  - `state_rows`: `state_root_denied`, `cache_root_read_only`, `top_level_subdirectory_reported` (`<state>/targets/` denied, `<state>` fine: one finding naming `targets/`), `missing_state_with_writable_parent` (none), `missing_state_with_unwritable_parent` (`cannot_create`), `listing_error_lists_nothing`, `budget_stops_the_listing` (two denied top-level directories, a one-entry `Budget`: one observation and `incomplete`).
  - `texts_name_no_command`: each row's `title`, `description`, `why` and every prose remediation contain no `omaddons <a COMMANDS name>`.
  - `the_detectors_never_write`: the source of `permissions.rs` contains none of `tests/single_writer.rs`'s patterns and no `fsx::` (a unit-level guard beside E3's directory scan).
- **`src/doctor/registry.rs`:** `the_permissions_rows_match_appendix_b`: rows 26 and 27: id, subsystem, severity, tier, `requires`, `online`, `cost_ms`, `fix: None`, `manual: Some`, texts non-empty and single-line; E1's invariant test passes unchanged.
- **Insta snapshots** (`src/doctor/detectors/snapshots/`): one finding JSON per row from fixed synthetic paths.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

None in this part: part 4 adds the two fixtures (with their root rule) and runs the real binary over them; part 5 tests the run-directory interaction of §4.

### Logging

Unit tests only: one name per case; assertion messages name the case and show the path, the fake probe's answers (or the real mode) and the observation.

## Considerations

- **Root.** Mode bits deny nothing to root; the real-tempdir cases skip as root and say so, and the fake probe covers every reason. Part 4's fixtures carry the same rule through the `Fixture` trait.
- **False positives (risk 3):** unregistered clients and vanished ones are not checked; a missing AddOns or `<state>` is judged by what omaddons would actually need (its nearest existing ancestor), so a fresh machine or a never-launched client is not reported.
- **A hung network mount** under a client can block one `access` call beyond the `quick` deadline; discovery already stats the same directories.
- **Hot spots:** `src/doctor/registry.rs` (shared with parts 1 and 2 and the other F leaves: insert by id, rebase); `permissions.rs` is this leaf's. README: only the two rows.
- **Decided defaults** are marked above; confirm or adjust them in the close comment.

## Dependencies

- **Parent:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.4.
- **Before it:** none among the siblings. E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, through the parent's edge) provides the registry, the view, the `Budget` and `list_dir`.
- **Beside it:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.4.1 and omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.4.2 touch other detector files and can run in parallel; all three append to `src/doctor/registry.rs` and README's doctor table, so rebase on whichever lands first.
- **After it:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.4.4 adds the two permission fixtures; omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.4.5 tests the unwritable state directory end to end.

title: Tests: the nine fixtures, their planting helpers and their detection checks
description:
Part 4 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.4 (Configs, userland state and permissions (detection only)). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

**The leaf.** F4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.4`) fills three subsystems of the doctor's catalog with nine failure modes, all detection only (no fixer): `fm-configs-config-parse-error` (P1, `cached`, row 19, registered by E2), `fm-configs-config-unknown-key` (P3, `quick`, row 20), `fm-configs-target-root-missing` (P2, `quick`, row 21), `fm-userland_state-target-vanished` (P2, `cached`, row 22, moved by E1), `fm-userland_state-target-key-duplicate` (P2, `quick`, row 23), `fm-userland_state-target-addons-shared` (P3, `cached`, row 24), `fm-userland_state-shared-record-doubled` (P2, `default`, row 25), `fm-permissions-addons-dir-not-writable` (P1, `quick`, row 26) and `fm-permissions-state-dir-not-writable` (P0, `quick`, row 27). Parts 1–3 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.4.1, omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.4.2, omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.4.3) registered the rows and their detectors with unit tests.

**This part** builds each row's fixture and the first suite that runs the real binary over them. M4-D47: "Each failure mode has a fixture: a Rust type implementing `Fixture` in `tests/doctor/fixtures/<fm_id>.rs`, with `corrupt(&TestEnv)`, deterministic, built on the `tests/common/` builders; `assert_healthy`; `subject() -> Vec<PathBuf>`; a doc comment that is the fixture's README: what breaks, why, the evidence." Common rule 19: a leaf that adds a failure mode adds its fixture. The fixtures are reused by part 5 (cross-command scenarios), by F9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`, the safety harness: repeatability, true positive, no false positive on a clean realistic home, purity, and `status` agreement for every row) and by T4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4`, the slice-3 demo). It is its own step because the planting recipes are shared infrastructure, separate from the detectors, and because each must produce exactly its row's instances and nothing that would make another row fire by accident.

M4-D47's rejected alternative, kept rejected: `corrupt.sh`/`assert.sh` scripts per failure mode (a second test language, and scripts that must clean up after themselves; the house rules ban `rm -rf` even in test scripts).

It serves checkpoint criterion 9: "every detector has a fixture that triggers it and a clean home that does not"; "detectors are repeatable"; and risk 3 (doctor false positives), whose mitigation is "every detector has a no-false-positive test on the realistic home".

**What exists to build on:**

- E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`): `tests/doctor/mod.rs` with the `Fixture` trait (`id()`, `corrupt(&Home)`, `assert_healthy(&Home)`, `subject(&Home) -> Vec<PathBuf>`, `fixer()` default `false`, `run_env()`, `run_args()`; included by test crates as `#[path = "doctor/mod.rs"] mod fixtures;`; extended only additively), `tests/doctor/fixtures/mod.rs` with `pub fn all() -> Vec<Box<dyn Fixture>>`, and `tests/common/doctor.rs` with `check_envelope(stdout, stderr, code)` and `plant::*`, among them `plant::target_vanished(home) -> String` (the vanished client's id). F1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1`) adds a defaulted `remedy(&Home)` to the trait; if F1 has not landed, this part adds it the same way.
- T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`): `tests/common/tlog.rs`: `let log = tlog!();`, `log.step(label)`, `log.note(text)`, `log.json(label, &value)`, `log.run(&home, &argv) -> Ran` (the argv without `omaddons`, used verbatim: pass `--json` yourself), `log.cmd(&home, &argv).env(k, v).spawn()`, `log.tree(label, root)`, `log.assert_unchanged(label, root)`, `log.diff`, `log.case(name)`, and `Ran::{ok, exit, fails, envelope, error_code, warnings, commands, events, assert_private, stdout, stderr}` (`Ran::data()` needs a `data` key, which a doctor envelope does not have: use `envelope()`). A suite that uses the log starts with the crate doc `//! e2e suite: <purpose>`.
- `tests/common/`: `Home::new(&[products])` (`home.rs:25-52`; `client(folder)`, `addons(folder)`, `state()`, `env`), `Home::with_custom(CustomRoot)` (`home.rs:129-142`, runs `targets add`), `CustomRoot::at(dir).build()` (`trees.rs:337-426`: a 3.3.5a custom client with `Interface/AddOns`), the private `copy_dir(from, to)` (`home.rs:269-281`, a plain recursive copy), `common::addons::toc` (TOC text), `common::state::{key_of, record}` (`state.rs:15-33`), `common::procfs::running_as_root()` (`procfs.rs:10-12`), `common::trees::tree_hash`.
- Recipes in today's tests: a doubled record (`tests/shared_addons.rs:23-75` and `:183-219`); a copied install (`tests/registry.rs:188-233`); `config set extra_roots` feeding discovery (`tests/cli_config.rs:318-339`).
- `common::realistic::realistic_home(dir) -> Realistic { home, .. }` (`tests/common/realistic.rs`), added by D8's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8`) part 5: three clients (retail, classic, era), 30 records, 5,040 managed files, built offline. It may not be on `main` yet (D8 is not an edge of this bead).

## Technical Approach

### 1. Planting helpers (`tests/common/doctor.rs`, appended to E3's `plant` module)

Each deterministic, each through the real binary or plain edits, each with a doc comment saying what it breaks and the finding's id, severity and evidence:

| Helper | Recipe |
|---|---|
| `plant::config(home, text)` | writes `home.env.config().join("omaddons/config.toml")` (creating the directory) |
| `plant::extra_roots(home, roots: &[&Path])` | `config set extra_roots <TOML array of roots>` through the binary, expecting exit 0 |
| `plant::manual_client(home, dir, name) -> (String, TargetKey)` | `CustomRoot::at(dir).build()`, then `targets add <dir> --name <name> --json` (exit 0), returning the id and `common::state::key_of` |
| `plant::manual_root_gone(home, name) -> (String, PathBuf)` | `manual_client(home, env.root()/<name>, name)`, then renames the root to `env.root()/aside/<name>`; returns the id and the original root path |
| `plant::copied_install(home) -> (String, PathBuf)` | `manual_client(home, <home>/Games/a-wotlk, "awotlk")`, then `copy_dir` of it to `<home>/Games/b-wotlk` (the marker comes along); returns the owner id and the copy's dir |
| `plant::shared_addons(home)` | for `Home::new(&["wow_classic_era", "wow_anniversary"])`: anniversary's `Interface/AddOns` replaced by a symlink to era's (as `tests/shared_addons.rs`'s `Shared::link`), then `targets add <client _classic_era_>` and `targets add <client _anniversary_>` (each registers exactly that flavor folder) |
| `plant::doubled_record(home) -> String` | `tests/shared_addons.rs`'s recipe: a local addon directory `env.root()/src/Both` (`Both.toc` for interfaces 11509 and 20506, one Lua file), `install <dir> -t era` and `install <dir> -t anniversary` while both AddOns are real directories, then anniversary's AddOns replaced by a symlink to era's; returns `"Both"` |
| `plant::deny_writes(dir)` | `chmod 0555 dir`, recording it in a process-wide list that `plant::restore_modes()` (`chmod 0755`, idempotent) undoes |
| `plant::RestoreModes` | a drop guard each permission case holds, calling `restore_modes()` so a failing case never leaves a directory its tempdir cannot delete |

`tests/common/home.rs`'s `copy_dir` becomes `pub` (no other change). Append to E3's module; F1, F3 and F5 append theirs beside this part's.

### 2. Two additive trait methods (`tests/doctor/mod.rs`)

- `fn remedy(&self, home: &Home) {}`: the manual remedy the finding advises, applied by hand (F1's; add it only if F1 has not).
- `fn unavailable(&self) -> Option<&'static str> { None }`: a reason the fixture cannot run here. The two permission fixtures return `Some("running as root: mode bits do not deny root")` when `common::procfs::running_as_root()`. Every runner of fixtures (this suite, part 5, F9's harness) checks it first, logs the reason with `log.note` naming the fixture, and skips that fixture's positive assertions: never a silent pass, never a failure. Decided while writing this bead; the development machine and the gate never run as root.

### 3. The nine fixtures (`tests/doctor/fixtures/fm_<subsystem>_<slug>.rs`, registered in `fixtures/mod.rs`'s `all()`)

Each a `pub struct` implementing `Fixture`, `fixer()` false, with an inherent `pub fn expected(&self, home: &Home) -> Vec<Expected>` (`Expected { instance: String, severity: &'static str, title: String, evidence: serde_json::Value }`, the exact evidence object) that the suite compares with; `assert_healthy` runs `doctor --json --only <id>` through `home` and asserts exit 0 and no finding of the id. `subject()` is the files `corrupt` changed that the finding is about (for documentation and F9's purity property; with no fixer there is no round trip): `config.toml` for rows 19–21, the denied directories for rows 26–27, empty otherwise.

| Fixture | Home | `corrupt` | `expected` | `remedy` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fm_configs_config_parse_error` | `Home::new(&["wow"])` | `plant::config(home, "default_channel = \"beta\"\ncheck_interval_hours = = 6\n")` | one P1 `fm-configs-config-parse-error@machine:path=<config.toml>`, evidence `{path, line: 2, column, reason: "parse"}` with `column` read from `omaddons::state::config::Config::parse(text, path)`'s error `details` | rewrite line 2 as `check_interval_hours = 6` |
| `fm_configs_config_unknown_key` | `Home::new(&["wow"])` | `plant::config(home, "defualt_target = \"retail\"\n")` | one P3 `…@machine:key=defualt_target`, `{path, key: "defualt_target", expected: "default_target"}` | rewrite it as `default_target = "retail"` |
| `fm_configs_target_root_missing` | `Home::new(&["wow"])` | `CustomRoot::at(env.root()/opt/wotlk).build()`; `plant::extra_roots(home, &[env.root()/mnt/gone, env.root()/opt/wotlk])` (`mnt/gone` never created); `plant::manual_root_gone(home, "pserver")` | two P2: `…@machine:path=<…/mnt/gone>` `{path, key: "extra_roots", paths: [<…/mnt/gone>, <…/opt/wotlk>], reason: "missing"}` with argv `config set extra_roots ["<…/opt/wotlk>"]`; `…@<pserver key>:path=<…/pserver>` `{path, reason: "missing"}` with argv `targets rm pserver` | run the extra root's argv, diagnose again, run the manual root's argv |
| `fm_userland_state_target_vanished` | `Home::new(&["wow", "wow_classic"])` | E3's `plant::target_vanished(home)` | one P2 `…@<key>`, `{path: <client dir>}` | `targets rm <id>` |
| `fm_userland_state_target_key_duplicate` | `Home::new(&["wow"])` | `plant::copied_install(home)` | one P2 `…@<awotlk key>:path=<b-wotlk>`, `{path: <b-wotlk>, paths: [<a-wotlk>]}` | `targets add <b-wotlk> --name bwotlk` (its first registration gives it a key of its own) |
| `fm_userland_state_target_addons_shared` | `Home::new(&["wow_classic_era", "wow_anniversary"])` | `plant::shared_addons(home)` | two P3: `…@<era key>:path=<era AddOns, canonical>` `{path, shared_with: ["anniversary"]}` and the mirror | replace anniversary's symlink with a directory of its own |
| `fm_userland_state_shared_record_doubled` | `Home::new(&["wow_classic_era", "wow_anniversary"])` | `plant::doubled_record(home)` | two P2: `…@<era key>:folder=both` (addon `Both`, folder `Both`, `{path: <era AddOns>/Both, owned_on: [{target: "anniversary", addon: "Both"}]}`) and the mirror | README's procedure on anniversary (move the symlink aside, an empty `AddOns/`, `remove Both -t anniversary`, the symlink back) |
| `fm_permissions_addons_dir_not_writable` | `Home::new(&["wow"])` | install one local addon on retail (registers it), then `plant::deny_writes(home.addons("_retail_"))` | one P1 `…@<retail key>:path=<AddOns>`, `{path, reason: "permission_denied"}` | `plant::restore_modes()` |
| `fm_permissions_state_dir_not_writable` | `Home::new(&["wow"])` | install one local addon (so `<state>/targets/` and `<cache>` exist), `doctor --json` once (so `<state>/doctor/runs/` exists), then `plant::deny_writes` of `<cache>` (`home.env.cache().join("omaddons")`) and of `<state>/targets/` | two P0: `…@machine:path=<cache>` and `…@machine:path=<state>/targets`, each `{path, reason: "permission_denied"}` | `plant::restore_modes()` |

- The two permission fixtures' `unavailable()` returns the root reason (§2).
- Other rows may fire too on these homes (a vanished pserver is row 22 as well; a doubled record is also row 24); `expected` lists only the fixture's own row, and the suite asserts the fixture's row exactly and the others not at all.
- Each fixture's doc comment is its README: what breaks, why, the finding (id, severity, instance, evidence keys) and the remedy.

### 4. `tests/doctor_userland.rs` (new)

First line `//! e2e suite: the configs, userland state and permissions rows of the doctor`. Every scenario is a `TestLog` scenario on its own `Home`, runs commands only through `log.run`/`log.cmd` with `--json` passed explicitly, and checks every doctor envelope with `common::doctor::check_envelope`. These homes create `WTF/` (the Battle.net and custom client builders write `WTF/Config.wtf`), so every `doctor` and `doctor explain` run also passes `--progress json` and asserts `Ran::assert_private()` (common rule 9). The suite constructs the nine fixtures by type.

1. **`every_f4_fixture_is_found_and_cleared`**, one `log.case(<fm id>)` per fixture: `unavailable()` → note and skip; `corrupt`; `doctor --json --only <id>` → exit 1, `state: DONE_FINDINGS`, the findings of that id equal `expected` (instance, severity, title, evidence exactly; `label`, `target` and `remediation` present); `doctor --json` (every row) → the same instances present; each finding's `explain_argv` (without the leading `omaddons`) → exit 0 and its `instances` holds the instance; `remedy`; `assert_healthy`.
2. **`the_variants_of_each_row`**, one case each, asserting the instances and evidence:
   - row 20: two unknown keys (two instances, in order); `[targets.retail]\nlabl = "x"` (`targets.retail.labl`, `expected: targets.retail.label`); `[rules]\nprodcuts = []` (`rules.prodcuts`, `expected: rules.products`); a key with no closest (`frobnicate = 1`, no `expected`);
   - row 21: an extra root that is a regular file (`not_a_directory`); one that is a dangling symlink (`missing`); a Battle.net root added by `targets add` (two manual targets) and then renamed away (two target findings, each `targets rm <its id>`); a relative entry (`config set extra_roots '["games/wow"]'`: no finding);
   - row 24: a three-client group (each `shared_with` the other two, in group order);
   - row 26 (not as root): retail's AddOns removed and `Interface/` denied (`cannot_create`, `paths: [<Interface>]`);
   - row 27 (not as root): `<state>` itself denied while `<state>/doctor/` stays writable (a `<state>` finding, and `doctor` still exits 1, not 73).
3. **`no_f4_row_fires_on_a_clean_home`**: the realistic home (`common::realistic::realistic_home` in a fresh directory under `CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR` if it is on `main`; otherwise `Home::new(&["wow", "wow_classic", "wow_classic_era"])` with five local addons installed on each client, every client registered; decided while writing this bead, and the case logs which home it used): `doctor --json --only <the nine ids>` → exit 0, `DONE_OK`, no finding, none of the nine in `skipped`.
4. **`near_misses_are_not_findings`**, one case per row, each asserting no finding of that row (and logging every finding there is):
   - rows 19 and 20: a valid `config.toml` with comments, `default_channel = "beta"`, `running_policy = "safe"`, `check_interval_hours = 6`, `git_hosts = ["codeberg.org"]`, `[limits] snapshot_max_bytes = "4GiB"`, `[sources.github] enabled = true`, `[targets.retail] label = "Main"`, `[client_rules.mainline] multi_toc = true` (it must pass `Config::parse`, which the case checks first);
   - row 21: `extra_roots` naming an existing empty directory and an existing custom root, and a manual client whose root exists;
   - row 22: every registered client present;
   - row 23: a copy already registered (`plant::copied_install`, then `targets add <copy> --name bwotlk`);
   - row 24: one client's AddOns a symlink to a directory no other client uses;
   - row 25: a shared AddOns where only era records `Both` (anniversary sees it `shared`): row 25 silent while row 24 fires;
   - row 26: a registered client with no `Interface/AddOns` and a writable `Interface/`;
   - row 27: a home where nothing has run (`<cache>` absent, its parent writable).
5. **`the_f4_fixtures_are_registered`**: `fixtures::all()` holds exactly one fixture per row 19–27 (by `id()`), each `fixer() == false`, each id a row of `FAILURE_MODES` with `fix: None`.
6. **`tests/registry.rs::a_copied_install_gets_a_new_key`** (an existing test, extended): also asserts `resolved.duplicates == [KeyDuplicate { client_dir: <copy>, key }]` before the copy's registration and empty after; otherwise unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The nine fixture files exist, each registered in `fixtures::all()`, each with a doc comment that is its README, `fixer() == false`, `expected`, `remedy`, `assert_healthy` and `subject` as Technical Approach §3 says; the permission fixtures report `unavailable()` as root.
- [ ] The `plant::` helpers of §1 exist, each documented and deterministic; `copy_dir` is public; `RestoreModes` restores every denied directory even when a case fails.
- [ ] `every_f4_fixture_is_found_and_cleared` passes: each fixture's row reports exactly its expected instances and evidence, every `explain_argv` exits 0 and lists its instance, and after `remedy` the row reports nothing.
- [ ] `the_variants_of_each_row` passes, including the relative extra root that is not judged and the three-client group.
- [ ] `no_f4_row_fires_on_a_clean_home` and every case of `near_misses_are_not_findings` pass.
- [ ] `the_f4_fixtures_are_registered` passes, and `tests/registry.rs::a_copied_install_gets_a_new_key` asserts `resolved.duplicates`.
- [ ] Every scenario writes its `TestLog` (steps, runs, trees), and every root-guarded skip is a logged note naming the fixture.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes and `ubs` is clean on the changed files.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

None new in `src/`: parts 1–3 own the detectors' unit tests. The planting helpers are checked by the scenarios that use them (each fixture's first assertion is that its row fires).

### Integration and end-to-end tests

The scenarios of Technical Approach §4, in `tests/doctor_userland.rs`, and the one assertion added to `tests/registry.rs`. No failpoint and no network: the HTTP fixtures are not needed (addons are installed from local directories), and `net.log` gains no line in any scenario (asserted in case 1 from `Ran`'s logged `net.log` additions).

### Logging

- Every scenario opens `let log = tlog!();` and names its phases with `log.step`: "home", "plant <row>", "doctor --only", "doctor", "explain each finding", "remedy", "healthy".
- Per fixture or variant: `log.case(<fm id or variant name>)`; `log.json("expected", …)` and `log.json("findings", …)` before every comparison; `log.tree` of `<config>`, `<state>` without `doctor/` (its other top-level entries), `<cache>` and each client dir before the diagnosis and `log.assert_unchanged` after it (a diagnosis writes nothing outside `<state>/doctor/`); `log.note` for each root-guarded skip and for which clean home case 3 used.
- A failing comparison prints the case, the expected and actual findings and the transcript path; T1's guard prints the last 20 steps.

## Considerations

- **Accidental findings.** A fixture that trips another row is harmless (`expected` covers only its own row), but one that trips its own row more often than expected (a stray second instance) fails case 1: that is the check that each recipe plants exactly its state.
- **Root.** The permission fixtures and variants skip as root, logged; the other seven fixtures run as root too. F9 inherits the `unavailable()` rule.
- **Determinism.** Ids are fixed with `--name` where `targets add` would otherwise derive them from a directory name; tempdir paths appear only in `expected` values built from the same `Home`, never in snapshots.
- **Hot spots:** `tests/common/doctor.rs`, `tests/doctor/fixtures/mod.rs`, `tests/doctor/mod.rs` and `tests/common/mod.rs` are shared with E3, F1, F3, F5 and F9: append in order and rebase; trait methods only ever added, with defaults.
- **Speed.** Nine fixtures, a dozen variants and nine near misses, each a small home and a handful of commands; the realistic home is built once per run of case 3. No sleep, no network.

## Dependencies

- **Parent:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.4.
- **Before it:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.4.1, omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.4.2 and omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.4.3 (the rows and detectors these fixtures trigger). It is blocked by T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`) at filing, because it writes a `TestLog` suite.
- **After it:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.4.5, which runs the remediations, the README procedure, `-t`, the broken-config skips and the privacy checks over these fixtures and helpers.

title: E2E: remediations that run, scope, skips, purity and privacy
description:
Part 5 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.4 (Configs, userland state and permissions (detection only)). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

**The leaf.** F4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.4`) fills three subsystems of the doctor's catalog with nine failure modes, all detection only: `fm-configs-config-parse-error` (P1, `cached`), `fm-configs-config-unknown-key` (P3, `quick`), `fm-configs-target-root-missing` (P2, `quick`, remediation argv `omaddons config set extra_roots '<the list without it>'` for an extra root and `omaddons targets rm <id>` for a manual one), `fm-userland_state-target-vanished` (P2, `cached`, `targets rm <id>`), `fm-userland_state-target-key-duplicate` (P2, `quick`), `fm-userland_state-target-addons-shared` (P3, `cached`), `fm-userland_state-shared-record-doubled` (P2, `default`, advice that never says `remove`), `fm-permissions-addons-dir-not-writable` (P1, `quick`) and `fm-permissions-state-dir-not-writable` (P0, `quick`). Parts 1–3 built the rows; part 4 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.4.4) built their fixtures, planting helpers and detection checks in `tests/doctor_userland.rs`.

**This part** proves what the leaf promises across commands, end to end through the real binary:

- every remediation argv not only parses but runs to success on its fixture and clears its finding (the plan's acceptance: "Every remediation argv parses, and on the fixture runs to success: the `config set` one removes the missing root");
- the two pieces of advice that are claims about behaviour are true: a copied install is re-keyed at its first registration, and the README's procedure drops one doubled record without deleting the shared folder (the plan: "`shared-record-doubled`'s advice must not suggest `remove`, which would delete the shared folder for both clients");
- scope, skips, tiers and instance stability: `-t` narrows target rows and keeps machine rows (§6.11), a broken `config.toml` skips what depends on it (M4-D43: "never silently dropped, and never reported as clean"), the `quick` and `default` tiers hold their rows (M4-D29), and `--since` tells two unknown keys apart (M4-D30: two findings of one failure mode "stay two instances");
- an unwritable state directory is still reported although `doctor` cannot always create its run directory (M4-D33: the run directory comes first, exit 73);
- purity, repeatability and privacy: a diagnosis changes nothing outside `<state>/doctor/`, two diagnoses agree, and no output names an account, realm or character.

It is its own step because these scenarios need every row, fixture and helper at once, and because they are the evidence the leaf's closing agent quotes. It serves checkpoint criterion 9 ("Bare `doctor` changes nothing outside `<state>/doctor/`"; "Detectors are repeatable"), G-M4-4 ("each finding carries … an exact remediation") and G-M4-6. It is the last subtask: its closing agent verifies the leaf's acceptance criteria and closes omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.4.

**What exists to build on:**

- Part 4: the nine fixtures (each with `corrupt`, `expected`, `remedy`, `assert_healthy`, `unavailable()`), `plant::{config, extra_roots, manual_client, manual_root_gone, copied_install, shared_addons, doubled_record, deny_writes, restore_modes, RestoreModes}`, and `tests/doctor_userland.rs` (`//! e2e suite: …`), whose homes all create `WTF/`.
- T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`): `tlog!()`, `log.step`, `log.note`, `log.json`, `log.run(&home, &argv) -> Ran` (argv without `omaddons`, verbatim), `log.cmd`, `log.tree`, `log.assert_unchanged`, `log.diff`, `log.case`, `Ran::{exit, fails, envelope, error_code, warnings, assert_private, stdout, stderr}`.
- E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`): `doctor`/`doctor diagnose` with `--only`, `--skip`, `--quick`, `--since <run>`, `-t`; `doctor explain <id | instance>` (no run directory, report keys `failure_mode`, `instances[]`); the volatile keys (`run_id`, `run_dir`, `started_at`, `finished_at`, `duration_ms`, declared in `contract::VOLATILE`); `report.json` in each run directory; exit 73 (`io`, `details.path`) when the run directory cannot be made; `common::doctor::check_envelope`. E2: `skipped[]` entries `{id, reason, target}` with reasons `<layer>_unavailable`.
- `remove` of an addon whose folders are all missing on that client forgets its record only, in an undoable transaction of `record` ops (README "`remove <ADDON>...`").
- `common::wtf::Wtf` (`WTF/` trees for `FAKEACCT` on `FakeRealm` as `FakeChar`) and `common::privacy::assert_private_all`.

## Technical Approach

All scenarios are added to `tests/doctor_userland.rs`. Each is a `TestLog` scenario on its own `Home`, runs commands only through `log.run`/`log.cmd` with `--json` and `--progress json` passed explicitly, checks every doctor envelope with `common::doctor::check_envelope`, asserts `Ran::assert_private()` on every run (the homes create `WTF/`), and holds a `plant::RestoreModes` guard whenever it denies writes. Scenarios that deny writes by mode bits first check `common::procfs::running_as_root()`, and as root log a note naming what they skip and run only their root-independent parts.

**A combined home** (`fn combined_home() -> (Home, Planted)`, local to the suite) plants rows 20–27 together on `Home::new(&["wow", "wow_classic_era", "wow_anniversary"])`: an unknown key in `config.toml` (20), a gone extra root and a gone manual root `pserver` (21, and 22 for `pserver`), a copied custom client under `<home>/Games` (23), era and anniversary sharing AddOns with `Both` recorded on both (24, 25), and, when not running as root, retail's AddOns and `<state>/targets/` denied (26, 27). Row 19 is left out: a broken `config.toml` would skip rows 20–26. `Planted` records the expected instance of each row.

### Scenarios

1. **`remediation_argvs_run_and_clear_their_findings`**:
   - steps "plant" (the root-missing fixture of part 4: `mnt/gone` and `opt/wotlk` in `extra_roots`, `pserver` added and moved away); "diagnose" (`doctor --json --only fm-configs-target-root-missing,fm-userland_state-target-vanished`: three findings, the extra root, the manual root and `pserver` vanished);
   - "extra root": run the extra root's `remediation.argv` (without the leading `omaddons`) → exit 0; `config get extra_roots --json` → exactly `[<…/opt/wotlk>]`; `targets --json` still lists the `opt/wotlk` client with `found_by: extra_root`;
   - "manual root": diagnose again; run the manual root's argv (`targets rm pserver`) → exit 0; the registry no longer holds `pserver`;
   - "healthy": the same `doctor --json --only …` → exit 0, no finding;
   - "vanished": on the target-vanished fixture, its finding's argv (`targets rm <id>`) → exit 0, then no finding;
   - in every step, each finding's `explain_argv` → exit 0 with the instance in `instances`.
2. **`two_gone_roots_converge_one_diagnosis_at_a_time`**: `extra_roots` = `[gone1, gone2, existing]`. Case `one_at_a_time`: diagnose → two findings; run gone1's argv; diagnose → one finding (gone2) whose `evidence.paths` is `[gone2, existing]` and whose argv sets `[existing]`; run it → `config get extra_roots` = `[existing]`; diagnose → none. Case `stale_second_argv` (the documented hazard, pinned so the README's advice stays true): from one diagnosis run gone1's argv, then gone2's → `extra_roots` = `[gone1, existing]` (gone1 is back); the next diagnosis reports gone1 again with a fresh argv.
3. **`a_copy_is_rekeyed_at_its_first_registration`**: `plant::copied_install`; diagnose → the row 23 finding `@<awotlk key>:path=<b-wotlk>`; `targets add <b-wotlk> --name bwotlk --json` → exit 0; diagnose → no row 23 finding; `common::state::key_of(home, "awotlk")` unchanged; the copy's marker (`Interface/.omaddons/target.json`) holds a key different from awotlk's, equal to `key_of(home, "bwotlk")`; `status --json` has no `target_key_duplicate` warning.
4. **`the_documented_procedure_drops_one_doubled_record`**: `plant::doubled_record`; diagnose → two row 25 findings (era and anniversary); `log.tree("shared folder", <era AddOns>/Both)`; the README's three steps on anniversary, as a user does them: rename anniversary's `Interface/AddOns` symlink to `AddOns.shared`, create an empty `Interface/AddOns`; `remove Both -t anniversary --json` → exit 0, its history line's ops all `record` (read with `history --json`), no `target_addons_shared` warning; remove the empty directory and rename the symlink back; `log.assert_unchanged("shared folder", …)`; `doctor --json --only fm-userland_state-shared-record-doubled` → exit 0; `common::state::record(home, "era")` still holds `Both`, anniversary's does not; `undo --dry-run --json` names that transaction (the record could be restored). Then assert, from the first diagnosis, that each row 25 finding's `remediation.argv` is `null` and its `command` contains no `omaddons ` followed by a command name.
5. **`a_broken_config_skips_what_depends_on_it`**: plant a gone manual root, a copy and, when not root, `<cache>` denied; then `plant::config(home, "default_channel = \"beta\"\ncheck_interval_hours = = 6\n")`; `doctor --json` → the row 19 finding (line 2, its column, `reason: parse`); `skipped` holds rows 20, 21, 22, 23, 24, 25 and 26, each `reason: config_unavailable`, `target: null`; row 27 is not in `skipped` and (not as root) its `<cache>` finding is present; no byte of the config file's text appears in stdout, stderr or `report.json` (the test searches for `check_interval_hours = = 6` and `beta`).
6. **`t_narrows_target_rows_and_keeps_machine_rows`**: two manual clients `pserver` and `turtle`, both moved away (rows 21 and 22 on each: root-independent), an unknown key and a gone extra root (machine rows 20 and 21), and, when not root, retail's AddOns denied (26). `doctor -t pserver --json` → pserver's rows 21 and 22 and both machine findings, nothing of turtle's or retail's; `doctor -t turtle --json` the mirror; `doctor -t retail --json` (not as root) retail's row 26 and both machine findings.
7. **`an_unwritable_state_dir_is_still_reported`** (as root: logged and skipped). Case `run_dir_possible`: one local install, one `doctor --json` (so `<state>/doctor/runs/` exists), then deny `<state>` (`home.state()`) → `doctor --json` exits 1 with the P0 instance `…@machine:path=<state>` and a published run. Case `run_dir_impossible`: one local install, no diagnosis yet, deny `<state>` → `doctor --json` exits 73, `error.code: io`, `details.path` under `<state>/doctor/`; `doctor explain fm-permissions-state-dir-not-writable --json` → exit 0, `instances` holds `…@machine:path=<state>`. Both restore the mode before the home drops.
8. **`quick_and_default_tiers_hold_their_rows`**: the combined home: `doctor --quick --json --only <rows 20–27>` → rows 20, 21, 22, 23, 24, 26 and 27 present (26 and 27 not as root), row 25 absent and not in `skipped` (a tier filter neither runs nor skips it); `doctor --json --only <rows 20–27>` → all present.
9. **`since_tells_one_fixed_unknown_key_from_another`**: two unknown keys; `doctor --json` (run A, two row 20 instances); rename one key to its closest; `doctor --json --since <A>` → `since: {run: A, new: [], resolved: [<the fixed key's instance>], unchanged: 1}`.
10. **`diagnoses_are_repeatable_and_write_nothing`**: the combined home; `log.tree` of `<config>`, each top-level entry of `<state>` except `doctor/`, `<cache>`, and each client dir; two `doctor --json` → equal `findings` after removing the declared volatile keys (findings themselves hold none); `log.assert_unchanged` on every recorded tree; no `net.log` line added by either run.
11. **`f4_findings_name_no_account_realm_or_character`**: the combined home with a `common::wtf::Wtf` tree (`FAKEACCT`, `FakeRealm`, `FakeChar`, SavedVariables included) on every client; `doctor --json --progress json`, human `doctor --progress json`, and `doctor explain <id> --json --progress json` for each of the nine ids → `assert_private_all(stdout, stderr)` on each; the newest `report.json` contains none of the three names either.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every remediation argv of rows 21 and 22 runs to success on its fixture and clears its finding: `config set extra_roots` leaves exactly the remaining entries and the other extra-root client still discovered, and `targets rm` removes the client from the registry; every `explain_argv` exits 0 and lists its instance.
- [ ] Two gone extra roots converge when `doctor` is rerun after each change, and the stale-second-argv case behaves as documented.
- [ ] A copied install's finding clears at its first registration, the owner's key is unchanged, and the copy's marker holds its own new key.
- [ ] The README procedure drops anniversary's record of `Both` with a record-only removal, the shared folder is byte-identical before and after, era keeps its record, the row 25 finding clears, and no row 25 remediation carries an argv or names a command.
- [ ] A broken `config.toml` gives the row 19 finding and lists rows 20–26 in `skipped` with `config_unavailable`, row 27 still runs, and no byte of the file's text is in any output.
- [ ] `-t` narrows rows 21 (manual), 22 and 26 to the selected client and keeps the machine findings of rows 20 and 21 (extra roots).
- [ ] An unwritable `<state>` is reported by `doctor` when its run directory can be made, and by `doctor explain` when `doctor` exits 73 naming the path (skipped as root, logged).
- [ ] `--quick` runs rows 20–24, 26 and 27 and not 25; the default run runs all of them; `--since` reports one resolved and one unchanged unknown key.
- [ ] Two diagnoses of the combined home give equal findings, and neither changes any tree outside `<state>/doctor/` or adds a `net.log` line.
- [ ] No output on any channel, nor `report.json`, names `FAKEACCT`, `FakeRealm` or `FakeChar`.
- [ ] Every scenario writes its `TestLog`; every root-guarded skip is a logged note.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes and `ubs` is clean on the changed files.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

None new in `src/`.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

The eleven scenarios above, in `tests/doctor_userland.rs`. No failpoint, no network (addons come from local directories; scenario 10 asserts no `net.log` line), no sleep. Commands per scenario: three to twelve.

### Logging

- Each scenario opens `let log = tlog!();` and names its phases with `log.step` ("plant", "diagnose", "run the remediation", "diagnose again", "README step 1/2/3", "check trees", "privacy"); cases within a scenario use `log.case(<name>)`.
- `log.json` records each findings list, `skipped` list, `since` object and `config get` value before it is compared; `log.tree`/`log.assert_unchanged` cover the shared folder (scenario 4) and every tree of scenario 10; a failing tree comparison names the first differing paths.
- Every run goes through `log.run`/`log.cmd`, so argv, environment overrides, cwd, exit, envelope, stderr events and `net.log` lines are in `steps.jsonl` and `transcript.md`; `log.note` records each root-guarded skip and which parts ran.
- A failing assertion names the step and prints the transcript path; T1's guard prints the last 20 steps.

## Considerations

- **The stale-second-argv case is a test of documented behaviour, not a defect:** `config set` replaces a whole list, and one diagnosis computes each argv from the list as it then is. If this case ever fails because the second argv became idempotent, revisit the README sentence and the row's `why` together.
- **The README procedure** uses plain file operations a user would do (rename a symlink, create and remove an empty directory); the test performs them with `std::fs`, which test code may use.
- **Root:** scenarios 5, 6, 7, 8, 10 and 11 run their permission parts only as a regular user; the rest of each runs as root too.
- **Hot spot:** `tests/doctor_userland.rs` is this leaf's; the combined-home helper stays local to it (F9 builds its own pairs).
- **What the closing agent records:** the close comment of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.4 quotes these scenario names with their results, the wire names of the leaf, the Appendix B lines of rows 19–27, the follow-up bead for non-absolute `extra_roots` entries, and every "Decided while writing this bead" confirmed or adjusted.

## Dependencies

- **Parent:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.4.
- **Before it:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.4.4 (the fixtures, helpers and suite this part extends), and through it omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.4.1, omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.4.2 and omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.4.3. It is blocked by T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`) at filing, because it writes `TestLog` scenarios.
- **After it:** nothing within the leaf; closing it closes omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.4, which unblocks F8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.8`), F9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`) and T4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4`).

- [ ] Two gone extra roots converge when `doctor` is rerun after each change, and the stale-second-argv case behaves as documented.
