title: External artifacts
description:
## How to work this bead

This bead is worked through its 5 subtasks, listed below in work order. Claim a subtask, not this bead (`br ready --parent omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.5` lists the ready ones). The agent that closes the last open subtask then verifies every acceptance criterion of this bead (they are the leaf's, not any one subtask's), and closes this bead with `br close omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.5 --reason "done: <evidence> · found: <ids>"`. Until this bead is closed, every bead it blocks stays blocked.

1. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.5.1 The inventory rows: ownership conflicts, case collisions, wrong-flavor and out-of-date folders: rows 30–33, the subsystem's shared helpers and evidence keys, their unit tests and README rows.
2. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.5.2 Missing dependencies from the catalog, and snapshots kept as a possible only copy: rows 34 and 35, the dependency view over an inventory, retention's shared snapshot rule, the History layer's raw text, unit tests, README rows.
3. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.5.3 `managed-files-modified` bounded by its budget, and its re-hash under `--include-deep`: row 28's bounded drift walk, `Selection.deep`, the deep variant's tier and cost, `explain`'s deep look; row 29 kept as it is.
4. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.5.4 Nested addon folders and the disabled flatten fixer: row 36's detector, `src/doctor/fixers/flatten.rs`, unit tests, README row and Troubleshooting entry.
5. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.5.5 Tests: the nine external-artifacts fixtures and their end-to-end suite (`tests/doctor/fixtures/fm_external_artifacts_*.rs`, `tests/doctor_external.rs`, two contract matrix rows).

s1 and s3 can start at once (different files). s2 and s4 build on s1's helpers and can run in parallel with each other. s5 needs s2, s3 and s4 (and so s1).

This leaf is size M. It is one leaf because its nine rows are one subsystem (`external_artifacts`) whose detectors share one inventory, one target scope and one evidence vocabulary, and because F8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.8`, `status` on the registry) and F9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`, the safety harness) need all of them before they start. The subtasks split the work, not the closure: no bead that F5 blocks starts until every subtask is closed and this leaf is closed.

## Background

**What this is.** The doctor's catalog (Appendix B of the plan, filed on the milestone epic `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`) has nine failure modes in the subsystem `external_artifacts`: the things wrong with what sits in a client's `Interface/AddOns` and in its client-side snapshots. Two of them are published since M3 and already move onto the registry in E1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`, the failure-mode registry and finding model) and onto the tolerant view in E2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.2`, `DoctorView`): `managed-files-modified` and `ownership-transferred`. Seven are new. This bead builds all nine as the plan defines them: their registry rows, detectors, one fixer, evidence, texts, fixtures and README rows. Every row but one is a report with an exact remediation; the one fixer (flattening a nested, hand-installed addon folder) ships **disabled**, because it changes a folder the user put there (M4-D39).

| # | Id (`fm-external_artifacts-…`) | P | Tier | Detected by | Repair | `status` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 28 | `managed-files-modified` (published) | P2 | quick (stat); deep (re-hash) | `drift::check` | none (`install --reinstall`, argv) | plain `status` only |
| 29 | `ownership-transferred` (published) | P2 | cached | degraded records | none (`list -v`, argv) | `--cached` and plain |
| 30 | `ownership-conflict` | P1 | default | two addon records of one client claim one folder key (`inventory`) | none (advice) | — |
| 31 | `case-collision` | P2 | default | case-duplicate folders (`inventory`) | none (advice) | — |
| 32 | `wrong-flavor` | P2 | default | a managed folder's loaded TOC no longer loads on this client | none (`update`, argv) | — |
| 33 | `out-of-date-toc` | P3 | default | a managed folder that loads only out of date | none (`update`, argv) | — |
| 34 | `missing-dependency` | P2 | default | `deps::is_satisfied` over managed TOCs | none (`install <candidate>` or `search`, argv) | — |
| 35 | `orphan-snapshot-only-copy` | P2 | default | a client snapshot retention keeps as a possible only copy | none (advice and the path) | — |
| 36 | `nested-addon-folder` | P3 | default | an unmanaged wrapper whose only addon is one level down | flatten (`enabled: false`; `--only` only; refused while the client runs) | — |

**What is true today** (verified at `c0ab5e9`):

- **Detection exists for most rows; no finding does** (the plan's §2.5).
  - `inventory::inventory_shared` (`src/inventory.rs:160-259`) classifies every entry of `AddOns/` as protected, managed, shared, linked, unmanaged or invalid by its ASCII case-folded key. It sets `ownership_conflict` when more than one addon of the client's **own** record claims the key (`:209`, from `ownership(record)` at `:334-348`), and `case_duplicate` when two entries share a key (`:230-237`). At `Depth::Full` it reads each folder's loaded TOC (`TocSummary`, with the TOC's required `dependencies` as this client reads them, `:374-399`) and its verdict (`:400-407`).
  - The verdict is `toc::Verdict::{Compatible { out_of_date }, WrongFlavor { reason }, NoToc}` (`src/toc/loaded.rs:265-280`), with `WrongFlavorReason::{GameTypeExcluded, NoInterface, InterfaceNotInFamily, BelowClientFloor, TargetInterfaceUnknown, NoLoadableToc, DependencySkipped}` (`:283-307`), computed by `judge` (`:416-497`). Install maps an on-disk `NoToc` to `WrongFlavor { NoLoadableToc }` (`src/engine/inspect.rs:921-927`), and leaves out of an install every folder that does not load (`partition`, `:984-1018`), so every folder an install put in place loaded when it was installed. `TargetInterfaceUnknown` is the verdict for every folder of a client whose own interface is unknown (`loaded.rs:450-452`).
  - `AddonRecord.any_flavor` (`src/model.rs:612-617`) records an `install --any-flavor`: builds the publisher did not make for this client installed anyway, by the user's choice.
  - `resolve::deps::is_satisfied(dep, archive, view)` (`src/resolve/deps.rs:127-152`) decides whether a required folder is satisfied by the client (`Blizzard_*`), the addon's own folders, or a folder present in `AddOns`; `resolve::deps::resolve(missing, target, lookups)` (`:276-342`) finds where to get it: a managed record that lost it (reported, `ManagedFolderMissing`), the catalog, the Tukui index, WoWInterface. Both are pure; today only planning calls them. Install follows only the **needed** folders' requirements (the primary folder and what it requires inside its own archive, `needed_folders`, `:41-57`; `src/engine/plan.rs:4659-4690`) and merely reports the requirements of the other folders, the bridges such as `Masque_Dominos` (`bridge_dependencies`, `deps.rs:59-92`). Its `missing_dependency` warning's fix installs the candidate or runs `omaddons search <folder>` (`plan.rs:1577-1685`).
  - The catalog (`src/resolve/catalog.rs:144-191`, `Catalog::load`) is the embedded `catalog/catalog.toml` plus `<config>/omaddons/catalog.d/*.toml`; it reads files only.
  - Retention's orphan sweep (`src/engine/retention.rs:347-407`) deletes the snapshot directories of transactions that never committed (no history mention in the raw history text, `in_history`, `:331-333`; no journal and no live in-flight lock; older than `ORPHAN_MIN_AGE`), **except** a client snapshot whose `AddOns/` holds an entry or which holds `WTF.previous` (`snapshot_folders`, `:310-323`; the rule at `:397`): "it may be the only copy of an addon". Nothing ever reports or removes such a snapshot.
  - `drift::check` (`src/drift.rs:118-155`) finds managed files that changed: `DriftMode::Stat` trusts a size-and-mtime match outside the racy window (`:343-346`), `DriftMode::Deep` re-hashes every file. Its walk is its own recursion (`list`, `:273-304`), with no budget.
  - **Nested folders and their flattening: nothing detects them** (§2.5).
- **What the blockers provide** (the leaves this bead waits for):
  - E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, `doctor diagnose` and `explain`): the runtime that runs each selected detector under its `Budget` and turns an `incomplete` return into `fm-state_files-check-incomplete`; `doctor::budget::{Budget, list_dir, walk}` (the bounded listing and walker: sorted, no symlink followed, one entry charged per visit); the tier filter (`doctor` runs every tier but `deep`, `--quick` the `cached` and `quick` tiers, `--include-deep` every tier); `doctor explain`, which re-detects one row with `DOCTOR_DETECTOR_DEADLINE`; the static manual pair `{instruction, reason}` per row that `explain` prints; the `Fixture` trait in `tests/doctor/mod.rs` and `tests/common/doctor.rs::plant` with `managed_files_modified`, `ownership_transferred`, `restore_file`; `tests/doctor.rs`.
  - E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`, `doctor fix`): `doctor fix` and `doctor diff`; its grouping (a fixer with `enabled: false` is listed and not run unless `--only` names its id; a subsystem name in `--only` never enables it); the `ClientNotRunning` precondition (a client a fix touches that runs, or whose running state is unknown, is `REFUSING` with `doctor_refused`, `details.reason: client_running`); `fix::remediation_for`, which builds every fixer-backed finding's remediation (`omaddons doctor fix --only <fm> [-t <id>]`, `estimated_actions` from `Fix::primitive_count()`: a flatten is 2, or 3 when the inner name equals the wrapper's); the binding token (`--dry-run` returns a `precondition`; `--if-match` runs exactly that or is `plan_stale`); and, through E5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`, the repair transaction), the lowering of `Fix::Flatten { inner, outer }` into two or three journaled `RenameNoReplace` primitives with the wrapper quarantined under `<meta>/snapshots/<tx>.repair/quarantine/Interface/AddOns/<wrapper>` (M4-D35), refusing an existing destination with `file_exists` before anything moves. E6 also ships the debug-only test fixer `fm-test-flatten`, whose shapes this bead's real detector generalizes.
  - Through E3: E1's `FailureMode`, `FixerSpec`, `Finding`, `Observation`, `Detected { found, incomplete }`, `Subject::target(id, key)` with `.folder(..)`, `.addon(..)`, `.tx(..)`, `.path(..)` (one helper builds `instance` and `label` together), `Evidence` (one struct of optional typed keys), `Remediation`; the seven moved rows, rows 28 and 29 among them, in `src/doctor/detectors/external.rs`. E2's `DoctorView` with its tolerant layers (`world()`, `records()`, `inventory(&DiscoveredTarget)` at `Depth::Full`, `history()`), `Selection` with `-t` scope (`Scope::includes`), and the `skipped` bookkeeping.

**Milestone goals served:**

- **G-M4-4 (diagnosable and repairable):** "`omaddons doctor` names every broken state omaddons can detect in what it owns or manages. Each finding carries concrete evidence and an exact remediation. A check that ran out of budget or entries says so: incomplete coverage is never reported as healthy." And "`status` and `doctor` never disagree about what is wrong." This bead names the nine states of what sits in `AddOns` and in client snapshots, each with evidence and a remediation, and keeps the two published rows identical in `status` and `doctor`.
- **G-M4-6 (no new risk to the engine's guarantees):** "every new write goes through fsx, and every repair is a journaled transaction that recovers like any other"; "the doctor never writes `WTF/`". The detectors only read. The flatten is an engine repair of E5's primitives, refused while the client runs, writing only `Interface/AddOns` and the client's `<meta>`.
- Vision G7 ("`doctor` follows the world-class doctor contract": evidence, an exact remediation, a check never reported as a pass it did not make), and the thesis that omaddons stays the sole, safe, undoable authority over what it manages: the doctor reports what is wrong with folders the user put there, and touches one of them only when asked by id.

**Checkpoint criteria this bead is responsible for (its part of each):**

- **9. The doctor's safety harness:** "Detectors are repeatable: two diagnoses of one state give identical findings"; "bare `doctor` changes nothing outside `<state>/doctor/`"; "`set(fixers) == set(fixtures with a fixer)`, and every detector has a fixture that triggers it and a clean home that does not". This bead supplies the nine fixtures (one with a fixer) and proves each row's true positive and no false positive on the realistic home; F9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`, the safety harness) re-runs them through every property, the flatten's undo round trip and crash recovery included.
- **12. `status` and `doctor` agree:** "`status`'s issues come from the doctor registry's `cached` and `quick` tiers. For every fixture, the issue ids `status` reports equal the doctor findings of those tiers." Rows 28 (`quick`) and 29 (`cached`) are this bead's part; F8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.8`, `status` on the registry) moves `status` onto the registry.
- **10. The doctor's surface (in part):** `doctor capabilities` lists every fixer with `enabled` (M4-D39); this bead's flatten is the one fixer that is `enabled: false` without needing `--force` (F2's, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.2`, set-aside is disabled because it needs force).
- **17 (in part):** "On the development machine, `omaddons doctor --json` reports no finding that is wrong: H6 reviews each one." H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`) is the M4 checkpoint. A real home is exactly where these rows could fire falsely (risk 3), so each has a no-false-positive test on the realistic home.

**The decisions that shape it** (full text in the decision-log comments on the milestone epic `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`):

- **M4-D39, a fixer that changes user content ships disabled.** "`fm-external_artifacts-nested-addon-folder` has a fixer: move the inner addon folder up and quarantine the wrapper. That fixer has `enabled: false`, so `doctor fix` without `--only` lists it as available and does not run it. The only way to run it is `--only fm-external_artifacts-nested-addon-folder`. It refuses while the client runs, and refuses when the destination name exists (`RENAME_NOREPLACE`). `capabilities` lists `enabled` per fixer." Why: the doctor contract's rule for new fixers, applied where it matters: a hand-installed folder is the user's, and the doctor's default fix touches only omaddons' own state. **Rejected:** no fixer at all, because a common manual-install mistake (`Foo-main/Foo/`) would then have a finding and no help.
- **M4-D48, the catalog is pruned to what can actually go wrong.** Report-only, with no fixer: "every finding whose fix is an omaddons command the user should choose (`install --reinstall`, …)" and "every finding with no safe automatic fix: … ownership conflicts, case collisions, wrong-flavor folders, missing dependencies". Dropped from the vision's list: `duplicate-addon` ("no identity rule can detect it without false positives"), `orphan-inflight*` and `orphan-snapshot-dir*` (retention's orphan sweep deletes them after every commit; "the case retention does not cover, an only copy, is row 35"). **Rejected:** shipping the vision's list verbatim, with dead detectors and fixers that pre-empt choices.
- **M4-D29, one registry by tier.** `status --cached` runs `cached` rows; plain `status`, `doctor --quick` and `doctor health` run `cached` and `quick`; `doctor` every tier but `deep`; `doctor --include-deep` every tier. A `quick` row may do "the stat-mode drift check"; `default` adds "`Depth::Full` inventories"; `deep` adds "content hashing (… `--deep` drift)". Rows 28 and 29 keep their published tiers; rows 30–36 are `default` because each needs a full inventory or a listing beyond `status`'s budget. **Rejected:** `status` calling `doctor` as a subprocess; two implementations of each check.
- **M4-D30, instance keys are resource-specific and stable.** `instance = <fm-id>@<target key>[:<discriminator>]`, the discriminator a canonical resource key (`folder=<folder key>`, `addon=<name>`, `tx=<ULID>`, `path=<normalized absolute path>`); a target rename changes `label`, never `instance`.
- **M4-D41:** `confidence` is `high` (observed directly), `medium` (inferred from consistent evidence) or `low` (a heuristic).
- **M4-D42, evidence never holds file content,** and never a path below `WTF/` (account, realm and character names live there; M3-D21). Evidence here holds paths under `Interface/AddOns` and `<meta>/snapshots`, folder and addon names, interface numbers, refs and counts.
- **M4-D43, budgets are enforced, not only estimated.** "Every detector works through a `Budget` handle … that the shared bounded walker and every listing check. A detector that hits its deadline [or] `DOCTOR_SCAN_MAX_ENTRIES` … stops and returns what it found plus an `incomplete` record", which becomes `fm-state_files-check-incomplete`, so the run is never `DONE_OK`. A detector whose required layer failed is in `skipped`, never reported clean. **Rejected:** treating truncation as a warning on a healthy run.
- **M4-D47, fixtures are Rust, in `tests/doctor/`, and coverage is bidirectional.** One `Fixture` per failure mode in `tests/doctor/fixtures/<fm_id>.rs` (`corrupt`, `assert_healthy`, `subject`, a doc comment that is its README). **Rejected:** `corrupt.sh`/`assert.sh` scripts (a second test language, and scripts that must clean up after themselves).
- **M4-D31 and M4-D35 (context, E5's):** a fix is lowered to primitives before anything commits; "a flatten becomes two or three separately journaled renames; no step ever hides more than one rename", and "quarantine never crosses a filesystem": a client victim goes to `<meta>/snapshots/<repair tx>.repair/quarantine/<relative path>`. This bead returns `Fix::Flatten` and adds no lowering or journal code.
- **M4-D44 and M4-D45 (context, E6's):** `doctor fix --dry-run` discloses every primitive and returns a token; `--if-match` runs exactly that or nothing; under the lock the planned detectors are re-run before any repair, so a nested folder that changed or vanished since the preview drops out or stales the bound run.
- **M4-D53 (context, F8's):** `status` issues gain `auto_fixable` and `explain`; this bead's two published rows keep `status`'s output unchanged until F8.
- **§8.1 defaults** applied where the plan is silent: existing codes and keys first (no new error code, warning code or constant is added); additive JSON; stable order (target id, then name, then path); no network on a read path (row 34 consults only the catalog); fail closed on what cannot be read (an unreadable snapshot directory is reported, never read as empty).

**How it serves the vision.** G4 ("the first command an agent guesses works"): every row's remediation is a command that runs or advice that names what to do, and the one repair is a single `--only` away. G7: a check that ran out of budget is `check-incomplete`, never a pass. The thesis: omaddons reports the user's own folders truthfully and changes one only on request, undoably.

## Technical Approach

Leaves this section names: E1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`, the failure-mode registry and finding model), E2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.2`, the tolerant `DoctorView`), E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, `doctor diagnose` and its runtime), E5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`, the repair transaction), E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`, `doctor fix`), F1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1`, the journal detectors), F8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.8`, `status` on the registry) and F9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`, the safety harness).

### 1. The nine rows (`src/doctor/registry.rs`, sorted by id among the existing rows)

| # | Id | P | Tier | `requires` | `cost_ms` | Instance (after `<fm-id>@<key>`) | `folder` / `addon` | Confidence | Remediation | Subtask |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 28 | `managed-files-modified` | P2 | `quick` (deep variant) | `[Discovery, Records]` | 5 (deep 300) | `:addon=<name>` | — / the addon | high | `reinstall_hint(addon, id)` (E1's) | s3 |
| 29 | `ownership-transferred` | P2 | `cached` | `[Records]` | 1 | none | — / — | high | `inspect_hint(id)` (E1's) | s3 (kept) |
| 30 | `ownership-conflict` | P1 | `default` | `[Discovery, Records, Inventory]` | 20 | `:folder=<key>` | the folder / — | high | prose | s1 |
| 31 | `case-collision` | P2 | `default` | `[Discovery, Records, Inventory]` | 20 | `:folder=<key>` | the first spelling / — | high | prose | s1 |
| 32 | `wrong-flavor` | P2 | `default` | `[Discovery, Records, Inventory]` | 20 | `:addon=<name>` | — / the addon | high | `omaddons update <addon> -t <id>` | s1 |
| 33 | `out-of-date-toc` | P3 | `default` | `[Discovery, Records, Inventory]` | 20 | `:addon=<name>` | — / the addon | high | `omaddons update <addon> -t <id>` | s1 |
| 34 | `missing-dependency` | P2 | `default` | `[Discovery, Records, Inventory]` | 30 | `:folder=<missing folder key>` | the missing folder / — | high | `omaddons install <ref> -t <id>`, or `omaddons search <folder> -t <id>` | s2 |
| 35 | `orphan-snapshot-only-copy` | P2 | `default` | `[Discovery, History]` | 10 | `:tx=<ULID>` (`:path=<dir>` for an unreadable listing) | — / — | high (medium, low: §7) | prose naming the path | s2 |

### 8. Row 36: nested addon folders and the flatten (s4)

**The detector** (`external/nested.rs`), per `KeyedClient`, over the inventory's entries of class `Unmanaged` that are not `case_duplicate`, not `unreadable`, and have no loaded TOC (`toc: None`). For each such wrapper `W` (`<A>/W`):

1. `budget::list_dir(<A>/W)` (charged). Its addon children: real directories (not symlinks) with a valid, non-protected `FolderName` and a TOC the client loads (`toc::loaded_toc(&DiskFolder::new(child)?, &target.rules)` is `Some`), each charged one entry.
2. Exactly one addon child `Y`, whose verdict (`toc::judge` with the target's rules, family, interface and the world's `RulesTable`) is `Compatible` (out of date or not). A wrong-flavor inner folder is not reported: flattening it would not make it load.
3. One of two shapes:
   - `single`: `Y` is `W`'s only entry (the plan's "`X/` with no TOC whose single child `Y/` holds `Y.toc`"; `W/W/` is this shape too);
   - `archive`: `W`'s key is `<Y key>-main` or `<Y key>-master` (a GitHub branch archive, the plan's "`X-main/X/`"), `W` holds at least one entry besides `Y`, and every other entry of `W` is not a directory holding a TOC the client loads (README, LICENSE, `.github/`). Decided while writing this bead: the archive shape keeps the repository files that sit beside the addon, which the strict single-child rule would miss in the most common case, while a wrapper with a second addon folder (a multi-addon repository) is never reported, because flattening one of them would be a guess. A wrapper whose only entry is `Y` is `single`, whatever its name.
4. `Y`'s key equals no other `AddOns` entry's key but `W`'s own. Decided while writing this bead: a nested copy whose name is already at the top level is not this failure mode (the top-level folder is what the client loads, and the wrapper is clutter). It also guarantees the flatten never creates a case pair: on a case-sensitive filesystem `RENAME_NOREPLACE` would happily create `AddOns/Foo` beside `AddOns/foo`, which Wine would see as one folder (ownership rule 4, `src/engine/ownership.rs:271-279`).
5. The finding: instance `:folder=<W key>`, `folder` = `W`'s name, evidence `{path: <A>/W, child: Y, toc: <Y's loaded TOC file>, shape}`, confidence medium (decided while writing this bead: the shape is observed directly, the user's intent to install it is inferred). Title "`<Y>` is inside `<W>`, where the client does not load it".

- Per fixture: `log.case(<fm id>)`; `log.json("finding", …)` before asserting it; `log.tree` of `<A>`, `<state>` without `doctor/`, `<cache>` and `<config>` before, and `log.assert_unchanged` after each diagnosis and each refused or stale fix (the first differing paths are logged); for the flatten, `log.tree` of the quarantine directory after the fix.
- A failing assertion prints the case, the expected and actual finding or tree, and the transcript path; T1's guard prints the last 20 steps.
- Unit tests: one name per case; every assertion message names the case and shows the input (entries, record, verdicts, catalog hits, snapshot names) and the observations.

### Checkpoint-only

None owned here. E4's perf test holds each `quick` detector, row 28 included, under 5 ms on the bench home (release); H6's review of `doctor_on_the_real_home` (E6's real-machine test) must find no wrong finding of these rows (risk 3).

## Considerations

Leaves this section names: F8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.8`, `status` on the registry), H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the checkpoint), E1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`), E2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.2`), E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`), E5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`), D1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1`, which touches `src/drift.rs`), D6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.6`, plan retention), F1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1`), F3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.3`), F4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.4`), F6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.6`, caches) and F9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`, the safety harness).

Mitigations here: bridges excluded from row 34; `any_flavor` and `TargetInterfaceUnknown` excluded from row 32; nested shapes reported only when the inner folder would load and the flatten would be unambiguous; row 35 held to retention's own rule; unregistered clients left out; conservative severities (P3 for the noisiest, rows 33 and 36); every row's no-false-positive test on the realistic home; H6 reviews the real home's findings.

- **Hot spots (§10.5 and §6.19):**
  - `src/doctor/**` (every E and F leaf): append rows to `registry.rs` where they sort; this bead owns `detectors/external.rs` and its child modules and `fixers/flatten.rs`; it adds fields to E1's `Evidence` and E2's `Selection` and History layer, and two calls in E3's runtime. Rebase on each.
  - `src/engine/retention.rs` (D6, E5, F6, F1): one function extracted from the sweep's client branch, behaviour unchanged; E5's `.repair` skip and F1's visibility change rebase beside it.

  - README: only the doctor table, `### doctor`'s two sentences and the new Troubleshooting entry.
- **Why size M, and why five parts.** Seven new rows and two kept ones, most of them pure rules over the inventory; the riskiest parts (the shared snapshot rule, the bounded deep walk, the fixer) each get their own subtask so they can be reviewed alone.
- **What could go wrong, and how to notice.**
  - Row 35 and the sweep disagree (a snapshot reported that the sweep would delete, or the reverse): `the_doctor_reports_exactly_the_snapshots_the_sweep_keeps`.
  - The deep variant runs under a quick budget (every `--include-deep` run would report `check-incomplete`): `tier_for_and_cost_for`, scenario 2.

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M4 plan, 2026-10-24).**

**Why this bead.** `Interface/AddOns` is where users and other tools put things omaddons did not, and where a patch day changes what loads. Today the code already sees most of what can go wrong there, but nothing turns it into a finding: the inventory flags ownership conflicts and case pairs (`src/inventory.rs:209`, `:230-237`), the TOC judge knows when a folder no longer loads or loads only out of date (`src/toc/loaded.rs:265-307`), the dependency resolver can tell a missing requirement and where to get it (`src/resolve/deps.rs:127-342`), and retention keeps, forever and silently, a client snapshot that may hold the only copy of an addon (`src/engine/retention.rs:310-323`, `:397`). Nothing detects a nested, hand-unzipped addon folder. This bead builds the `external_artifacts` subsystem of the doctor's catalog (Appendix B rows 28–36): the two published rows in their final form, seven new report rows and one repair, the flatten, which ships disabled because the folder it moves is the user's.

**Decisions applied.**

- **M4-D39:** the flatten fixer has `enabled: false`; `doctor fix` lists it and does not run it; only `--only fm-external_artifacts-nested-addon-folder` runs it; it refuses while the client runs and when the destination exists; `capabilities` lists `enabled`. Rejected: no fixer at all.
- **M4-D48:** every other row is a report with an exact remediation, because each fix is a choice (`install --reinstall`, `update`, which addon owns a folder, which spelling to keep). `duplicate-addon` is not built (no rule without false positives); the only-copy snapshot is the one orphan case retention does not cover.
- **M4-D29:** rows 28 (`quick`) and 29 (`cached`) keep their published tiers, so `status` and `doctor` keep agreeing; rows 30–36 are `default` (full inventories, listings).
- **M4-D30:** instances by folder key, addon, transaction or path, so two findings of one row on one client stay two and a rename moves only the label.
- **M4-D41, M4-D42, M4-D43:** confidence per row; evidence holds names, paths outside `WTF/`, interfaces, refs and counts, never content; every walk and listing charges a `Budget`, and a cut-short check is `check-incomplete`, never clean (row 28's drift walk gains that bound).
- **M4-D47:** one Rust fixture per row in `tests/doctor/fixtures/`.
- **M4-D31, M4-D35, M4-D44, M4-D45 (context):** the flatten is E5's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`, the repair transaction) two or three journaled renames with the wrapper quarantined beside its client, previewed and bound by E6's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`, `doctor fix`) token, re-planned under the lock.

**Alternatives rejected.**

- *Counting every folder's TOC requirements for `missing-dependency`*: install follows only the needed folders' requirements and merely reports bridges, so this would report optional modules on healthy homes.
- *Consulting the cached Tukui and WoWInterface indexes for a candidate*: the plan keeps the diagnosis on the catalog, which needs no request and is not stale.
- *A second implementation of the only-copy rule in the doctor*: the doctor and the orphan sweep now share one function, so what retention keeps and what the doctor reports cannot drift.
- *A second registry row for the deep re-hash*: ids are unique; instead `Selection.deep` and a declared deep variant give row 28 the deep tier's budget under `--include-deep`.
- *Reporting `any_flavor` addons as wrong-flavor, or `TargetInterfaceUnknown` verdicts*: the first is the user's recorded choice, the second says nothing about the folder.
- *Flattening a nested copy whose name is already at the top level*: on a case-sensitive filesystem the rename would create a case pair the client sees as one folder; that shape is not reported.
- *A flatten-specific refusal reason*: M4-D40's closed set has none for an existing destination, and E5's lowering already refuses it with `file_exists` before anything moves.

**Risks and how they are watched.**

- **Risk 3, doctor false positives (M, M):** each row's exclusions (bridges, `any_flavor`, unknown interfaces, ambiguous nests, unregistered clients), conservative severities, the no-false-positive scenario on the realistic home, and H6's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the checkpoint) review of the real home.
- **Risk 4, `status --cached` slows (M, M; F8 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.8`, `status` on the registry):** rows 28 and 29 cost what `status` already pays; row 28's walk is now bounded.
- **A flatten that moves the wrong thing:** only unambiguous shapes are reported, E5's lowering refuses an existing destination or a protected name, the endpoint predicates catch a change after planning, and F9's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`, the safety harness) blast-radius property checks every moved path.

**What it unblocks, and why they wait.**

- F8 (`status` on the registry) takes rows 28 and 29 from the registry, so it needs their final form.
- F9 (the safety harness) runs every fixture and round-trips the flatten (undo, crash recovery at each rename, concurrency).
- T4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4`, the slice-3 demo) runs the harness over these fixtures.

**How it serves the milestone.** G-M4-4's "names every broken state omaddons can detect in what it owns or manages", with evidence and an exact remediation, for everything in `AddOns` and in client snapshots; its "`status` and `doctor` never disagree" for the two published rows; and G-M4-6, because every detector only reads and the one repair is an ordinary engine transaction that never touches `WTF/`. It pre-checks criteria 9 and 12 for its rows.

**Facts verified during planning** (as of `c0ab5e9`): `src/inventory.rs:148-259`, `:334-348`; `src/toc/loaded.rs:265-307`, `:416-497`; `src/engine/inspect.rs:921-927`, `:984-1018`; `src/model.rs:607-668`; `src/resolve/deps.rs:41-92`, `:127-152`, `:276-342`; `src/engine/plan.rs:379-394`, `:1544-1567`, `:1577-1685`, `:4649-4690`, `:5458-5527`; `src/resolve/catalog.rs:144-191`; `src/engine/retention.rs:286-333`, `:347-407`; `src/drift.rs:118-169`, `:273-304`, `:343-346`; `src/app/drift.rs:74-94`; `src/engine/ownership.rs:271-279`; `src/fsx/lock.rs:247-276`; `src/state/history.rs:442-463`; README `:752-760` and `:1890`.

description:
Part 1 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.5 (External artifacts). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

**The leaf.** F5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.5`) builds the doctor's `external_artifacts` subsystem: the nine failure modes of Appendix B rows 28–36 (the doctor's catalog, filed on the milestone epic `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`), about what sits in a client's `Interface/AddOns` and in its client-side snapshots. Two rows are published since M3 (`managed-files-modified`, `ownership-transferred`; E1 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1` moved them onto the registry), seven are new, and one has a fixer (the flatten of a nested folder), shipped disabled (M4-D39). It serves G-M4-4 ("`omaddons doctor` names every broken state omaddons can detect in what it owns or manages. Each finding carries concrete evidence and an exact remediation") and checkpoint criterion 9 ("every detector has a fixture that triggers it and a clean home that does not"; "detectors are repeatable").

**This part** adds the four rows that read nothing but the client's record and its full inventory: row 30 `ownership-conflict` (P1), row 31 `case-collision` (P2), row 32 `wrong-flavor` (P2) and row 33 `out-of-date-toc` (P3), all `default` tier. It also lays down what the subsystem's later parts share: the registered-client helper, the recorded-entry helper, the evidence keys of these rows and the per-folder evidence type. It is its own step because these four rows are pure rules over data the view already holds (no new I/O), and because parts 2 and 4 build on its helpers.

**The decisions this part applies** (full text in the decision-log comments on the milestone epic):

- **M4-D48:** these four are report-only. "Report-only, with no fixer: … every finding with no safe automatic fix: … ownership conflicts, case collisions, wrong-flavor folders, missing dependencies"; and "every finding whose fix is an omaddons command the user should choose". Rejected: an automatic fix where the right action is a choice (which addon owns a folder, which spelling to keep).
- **M4-D29:** tiers. `default` rows run in bare `doctor` and `doctor --include-deep`, never in `status` or `doctor --quick`; the `default` tier may read "`Depth::Full` inventories".
- **M4-D30:** `instance = <fm-id>@<target key>:<discriminator>`; here `folder=<folder key>` (rows 30, 31) and `addon=<name>` (rows 32, 33; E1 added this discriminator for per-addon rows). `label` is the human form and never compared.
- **M4-D41:** `confidence` `high` here: the inventory and the TOC judge observe the state directly.
- **M4-D42:** evidence holds paths under `Interface/AddOns`, names, interface numbers and counts, never file content, never a path below `WTF/`.
- **M4-D43:** a detector that cannot finish within its `Budget` returns what it found and an `incomplete` record (E3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, the doctor runtime, turns it into `fm-state_files-check-incomplete`); a detector whose required layer is unavailable is listed in `skipped`, never run, never clean.
- **§8.1 defaults:** existing keys first, additive JSON, stable order (target id, then name, then path), fail closed.

**What exists to build on** (verified at `c0ab5e9`, plus what the leaf's blockers provide):

- `inventory::inventory_shared` (`src/inventory.rs:160-259`), which E2's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.2`, `DoctorView`) view runs once per discovered client at `Depth::Full` (`view.inventory(&DiscoveredTarget) -> Option<&Inventory>`). Each `FolderEntry` (`:52-75`) has `name`, `key` (ASCII case-folded), `class` (`Protected | Managed | Shared | Linked | Unmanaged | Invalid`), `owners` (the addons of the client's own record that claim the key, sorted), `case_duplicate` (another entry has the key, set at `:230-237`), `ownership_conflict` (`claimed.len() > 1`, `:209`, where `claimed` comes from `ownership(record)`, `:334-348`, over **one** record's addons), `unreadable`, `toc: Option<TocSummary>` (with `file`, `interfaces`, `dependencies`, `:100-125`) and `verdict: Option<VerdictReport>` (from `toc::judge`, `:400-407`).
- `toc::Verdict` (`src/toc/loaded.rs:265-280`): `Compatible { out_of_date }`, `WrongFlavor { reason }`, `NoToc`; `WrongFlavorReason` (`:283-307`): `GameTypeExcluded`, `NoInterface`, `InterfaceNotInFamily { interfaces, family }`, `BelowClientFloor { interfaces, floor }`, `TargetInterfaceUnknown` (every folder's verdict when the client's own interface is unknown and its family has no range, `:450-452`), and two archive-only reasons. Install maps an on-disk `NoToc` to `NoLoadableToc` (`src/engine/inspect.rs:921-927`) and installs only folders that load (`partition`, `:984-1018`). `SkippedFolder { name, reason }.left_out()` (`inspect.rs:952-970`) and `LeftOutFolder::describe` (`src/model.rs:633-668`) word a reason as install does ("DBM-Core (interface 110207, below the client's floor 120000)").
- `AddonRecord` (`src/model.rs:575-618`): `name`, `folders: Vec<FolderName>`, `any_flavor` (an `install --any-flavor`: builds not made for this client installed by the user's choice, `:612-617`).
- `engine::ownership` refuses any change to a key that has two spellings (`case_collision`, `src/engine/ownership.rs:271-279`) and a takeover without `--force` (`ownership_conflict`, `:363-375`); with `--force` it transfers the folder and marks the previous owner degraded (`:391-413`).
- `update` of a pinned addon skips it with `addon_pinned`, whose fix is `omaddons unpin <addon> -t <id>` (`src/engine/plan.rs:379-394`).
- `crate::engine::testing::target(client_dir)` (`src/engine/testing.rs:37-57`, `cfg(test)`): a retail `Target` at interface 120105 for unit tests.
- From E1, through E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`): `src/doctor/registry.rs` (`FailureMode` with `id, subsystem, severity, title, description, why, tier, online, cost_ms, requires, detect, fix, manual`; `FAILURE_MODES` sorted by id; `pub mod ids`; `invariant_violations`), `src/doctor/finding.rs` (`Observation`, `Detected { found, incomplete }`, `Subject::target(id, key).folder(&FolderName)` / `.addon(&str)`, `Evidence` with optional `path, paths, hash, observed, expected, mode, pid, age_s, line, column, tx, count, reason`, `Evidence::is_private_safe`, `Remediation`, `Confidence`), `src/doctor/detectors/external.rs` holding the two moved rows. From E2: `Layer` (`Config, Registry, Discovery, Records, Inventory, …`), `DoctorView::{world, records, inventory, target_ref}`, `Selection` and `Scope::includes`. From E3: `Budget::check`, `budget.incomplete()`, and the static manual pair `{instruction, reason}` per row that `doctor explain` prints (E3 adds it to `FailureMode`; E4 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4` lists it as `manual_remediations`).

## Technical Approach

Leaves this section names: E1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`, the registry and finding model), E2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.2`, the tolerant view), E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, the doctor runtime), E4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4`, `doctor capabilities`) and F3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.3`, state files, which owns `record-folder-missing`).

### 1. The registry rows (`src/doctor/registry.rs`, inserted where they sort)

| # | Id | P | Tier | `requires` | `cost_ms` | Instance | `folder` / `addon` | Confidence | Remediation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 30 | `fm-external_artifacts-ownership-conflict` | P1 | `Default` | `[Discovery, Records, Inventory]` | 20 | `@<key>:folder=<folder key>` | the folder's name / `null` | high | prose |
| 31 | `fm-external_artifacts-case-collision` | P2 | `Default` | `[Discovery, Records, Inventory]` | 20 | `@<key>:folder=<key>` | the first spelling, bytewise / `null` | high | prose |
| 32 | `fm-external_artifacts-wrong-flavor` | P2 | `Default` | `[Discovery, Records, Inventory]` | 20 | `@<key>:addon=<name>` | `null` / the addon | high | argv `omaddons update <addon> -t <id>` |
| 33 | `fm-external_artifacts-out-of-date-toc` | P3 | `Default` | `[Discovery, Records, Inventory]` | 20 | `@<key>:addon=<name>` | `null` / the addon | high | argv `omaddons update <addon> -t <id>` |

- All four: `subsystem: ExternalArtifacts`, `online: false`, `fix: None`, `manual: Some(…)`, a constant in `ids`.
- `cost_ms` 20 is a declared estimate (decided while writing this bead): the first row to ask E2's view for a client's inventory pays for building it, so each declares the cost of one full inventory of a realistic client. It feeds `--budget`'s refusal and shares and E4's `cost_summary`. Adjust it with a measured reason in the close comment if needed.
- `requires` names `Discovery` and `Records` beside `Inventory`, which depends on both (E2), so a broken config or registry skips them with the root cause.

Static texts (titles lowercase; none names a runnable command), and E3's manual pair (`instruction` / `reason`; `<placeholders>` for values only the user has):

| # | `title` | `description` | `why` | `instruction` / `reason` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 30 | a folder is claimed by several addons | Two or more addons in one client's record list the same AddOns folder (by its case-folded name). omaddons never records this itself: it comes from a hand-edited or damaged record. | Removing any of those addons removes the folder for all of them, and an update of one replaces files the others rely on. | decide which addon owns `<folder>`; reinstalling that addon with --force transfers the folder and marks the others degraded / only you know which addon the folder belongs to |
| 31 | folder names differ only in case | AddOns holds two or more entries whose names differ only in case (Foo and foo). The client runs under Wine, which resolves names ignoring case, so it sees one folder under two names. | Which copy the client loads is undefined, and every install, update or removal of that folder is refused with case_collision until one spelling is left. | keep one spelling of `<folder>` and move the others out of AddOns by hand, with the game closed / omaddons never picks a spelling: either may hold your files |
| 32 | a managed addon's folder no longer loads on this client | The TOC this client loads from a folder omaddons installed no longer passes the client's load rules: its interface is outside the client's range or below its floor, a game-type rule excludes the client, or the folder has no TOC the client loads. Usually the client was patched, or the TOC was edited. | The client skips the folder, so the addon, or that part of it, does nothing. A newer build may load; if none exists, the addon is not built for this client and removing it is the other way out. | update `<addon>`; if no build for this client exists, remove it / whether a build for this client exists is the publisher's decision |
| 33 | a managed addon loads only as out of date | The TOC this client loads from a folder omaddons installed targets an older interface than the client's, so the client lists it as out of date. | It loads only with "Load out of date AddOns" enabled, and an addon built for an older patch may misbehave. | update `<addon>`, or enable "Load out of date AddOns" in the client / a newer build may not exist yet |

### 2. The subsystem's shared helpers (`src/doctor/detectors/external.rs`)

```rust
/// A registered client in scope, with what the inventory rows read.
pub(crate) struct KeyedClient<'v> {
    pub target: &'v Target,             // the discovered target: rules, family, interface, client_dir
    pub key: TargetKey,
    pub id: String,                     // E2's TargetRef id: the registry id, else the key's string
    pub record: Option<&'v TargetRecord>,
    pub inventory: Option<&'v Inventory>,
}
/// The discovered clients with a target key, in `-t` scope (`Scope::includes`, as E2's
/// moved rows check it), sorted by id. Their record and inventory come from the view's
/// Records and Inventory layers; an unavailable one is `None` here, and E2's
/// `target_skips` reports it as skipped.
pub(crate) fn keyed_clients<'v>(view: &'v DoctorView, sel: &Selection) -> Vec<KeyedClient<'v>>;

/// The inventory entry of each recorded folder of `addon`: the entry with the folder's
/// key; when the key has several spellings, only the entry spelled as the record spells
/// it (none: that key is row 31's). A folder with no entry is missing (row 13's, F3).
pub(crate) fn recorded_entries<'i>(addon: &AddonRecord, inv: &'i Inventory)
    -> Vec<(&'i FolderEntry, &FolderName)>;
```

- **Registered clients only.** Decided while writing this bead: every row of this subsystem reports only on discovered clients that have a target key. A `Subject` needs the key, and a client omaddons never registered has no record, no managed folder and no snapshot; G-M4-4 limits the doctor to "what it owns or manages".
- Each row's `detect(view, sel, budget)` iterates `keyed_clients`, calls `budget.check()` before each client (stopping with `budget.incomplete()` when it fails), and calls the row's pure function. No row here walks or lists: the inventory is the view's.

### 3. The rules (pure functions, one per row)

```rust
fn ownership_conflicts(c: &ClientRef, addons_dir: &Path, inv: &Inventory) -> Vec<Observation>;   // row 30
fn case_collisions(c: &ClientRef, addons_dir: &Path, inv: &Inventory) -> Vec<Observation>;       // row 31
fn wrong_flavor(c: &ClientRef, target: &Target, record: &TargetRecord, inv: &Inventory) -> Vec<Observation>;   // row 32
fn out_of_date(c: &ClientRef, target: &Target, record: &TargetRecord, inv: &Inventory) -> Vec<Observation>;    // row 33
```

(`ClientRef` is `{id, key}`; `addons_dir` is the client's `Interface/AddOns` as found on disk, `Target::addons_dir`.)

- **Row 30.** Each key some entry of which carries `ownership_conflict` (class `Managed`), once per key whatever its spellings. Subject `.folder(<the entry's FolderName>)`; `folder` = its name. Evidence `{path: <addons dir>/<name>, owners: <entry.owners>}`. Title "`<name>` is claimed by `<n>` addons of this client (`<a>`, `<b>`)" (more than three owners: the first three, then "and `<k>` more"). Remediation prose: "`<a>`, `<b>` on `<id>` all record `<name>`: decide which addon owns it; reinstalling that addon with --force transfers the folder and marks the others degraded, and removing any of them removes the folder for all". This is the plan's "two records claim one folder key": two **addon** records of one client's record. A folder recorded by two sibling clients that share one `AddOns` is F4's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.4`) `shared-record-doubled`, which the inventory marks with `owned_on`, not `ownership_conflict`; its advice must never suggest `remove`, and nothing here suggests it either.
- **Row 31.** Each key whose entries carry `case_duplicate`, any class (a stray file or symlink spelled another way is refused by ownership too). Evidence `{paths: <each spelling's absolute path, sorted bytewise>, count: <spellings>}`; `folder` = the first spelling; instance `:folder=<key>` (built from the first spelling's `FolderName`, whose key is the shared one; an `Invalid` name uses the case-folded name the inventory recorded). Title "`<A>` and `<B>` differ only in case" ("`<A>`, `<B>` and `<C>` differ only in case" for three or more). Remediation prose: "keep one of `<A>`, `<B>` in `<addons dir>` and move the others out by hand, with the game closed; omaddons refuses to change any of them until one spelling is left".
- **Row 32.** For each addon of the record with `any_flavor == false`, its `recorded_entries` that are not `unreadable` and whose verdict is `WrongFlavor { reason }` with any reason but `TargetInterfaceUnknown`, or `NoToc` (reported as `no_loadable_toc`, as install maps it). One observation per addon with at least one such folder: subject `.addon(<record name>)`, `addon` = the record name, evidence `{folders: [FolderEvidence…], expected: "<target.interface>"}`.
  - Decided while writing this bead: `any_flavor` addons are skipped, because `install --any-flavor` records the user's choice to run builds not made for this client, and reporting them on every diagnosis would be a false positive; `TargetInterfaceUnknown` is never a finding, because it is the verdict of every folder on a client whose own interface is unknown and says nothing about the folder.
  - Title through install's wording: `SkippedFolder { name, reason }.left_out().describe()` of the first affected folder (by name): "`<addon>` no longer loads on this client: `<describe>`" ("Foo no longer loads on this client: Foo (interface 110207, below the client's floor 120000)"); two or more folders: "`<addon>`: `<n>` folders no longer load on this client".
  - Remediation argv `omaddons update <addon> -t <id>` (`destructive: false`). Decided while writing this bead: Appendix B's "`update` or `remove`" becomes one argv, the update, because a `Remediation` holds one command, an update may bring a build that loads and changes nothing when none exists, and removal is destructive; the texts name removal as the other way out. A pinned addon's update is skipped with `addon_pinned`, whose fix (`unpin`) is the right next step.
- **Row 33.** For each addon of the record (any_flavor included), its `recorded_entries` whose verdict is `Compatible { out_of_date: true }`. One observation per addon: `.addon(<name>)`, evidence `{folders, expected}`. Title "`<addon>` loads only as out of date on this client" (two or more folders: "… (`<n>` folders)"). Remediation argv `omaddons update <addon> -t <id>`.
- Rows 32 and 33 are disjoint (one verdict per folder). Neither reports a recorded folder that is gone (row 13, F3 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.3`), a left-out folder (never on disk), or a folder of class `Shared` (another client's record).
- Titles hold no timestamp or byte count, so two runs of an unchanged home print the same title.

### 4. Evidence keys added (`src/doctor/finding.rs`, E1's `Evidence`)

Each is `Option`, omitted when `None`, documented optional (M4-D55 rule 2):

| Key | Type | Rows | Value |
|---|---|---|---|
| `owners` | `[string]` | 30 | the record's addon names that claim the folder, sorted |
| `folders` | `[FolderEvidence]` | 32, 33 | one per affected folder, sorted by name |

```rust
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, JsonSchema)]
pub struct FolderEvidence {
    pub name: String,                                   // the folder as on disk
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")] pub toc: Option<String>,        // the loaded TOC's file name
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")] pub reason: Option<&'static str>, // row 32: the closed set below
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Vec::is_empty")]  pub interfaces: Vec<u32>,         // the TOC's ## Interface values as this client reads them
    #[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")] pub floor: Option<u32>,          // below_client_floor: the client's floor
}
```

- `reason` (row 32, per folder): `game_type_excluded`, `no_interface`, `interface_not_in_family`, `below_client_floor`, `no_loadable_toc` (the `WrongFlavorReason` wire names, plus install's mapping of `NoToc`).
- `expected` (existing key): the client's own interface as a string (`"120105"`).
- Existing keys reused: `path` (row 30), `paths` and `count` (row 31).
- `Evidence::is_private_safe` holds for every case (no path below `WTF/`; these paths are under `Interface/AddOns`).

A row 32 finding, as `doctor --json` prints it (paths are absolute in real output):

```json

 "label":"retail/OmniCC","severity":"P2","subsystem":"external_artifacts",

 "remediation":{"command":"omaddons update OmniCC -t retail","argv":["omaddons","update","OmniCC","-t","retail"],
```

(With two folders the title is "OmniCC: 2 folders no longer load on this client"; the example shows the evidence of that case.)

### 5. README (common rules 11 and 19)

The doctor's failure-mode table (E3 created it): four rows, id, severity, tier `default`, meaning and remediation (`advice` for 30 and 31; `omaddons update <addon> -t <id>` for 32 and 33), in this commit.

### 6. Snapshots and registries that list failure modes

If A4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`), E4 or B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`) has landed and lists failure modes, re-accept its snapshot (A4's count, E4's detectors and `manual_remediations`) or regenerate `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` (`OMADDONS_UPDATE_SKILL=1 cargo test --test skill`), reviewing that only these rows changed.

### 7. What not to do

- No I/O in the four rules: they read the inventory and the record only (no `fsx::`, no `WriteSession`, no file read).
- Do not report an unregistered client, an `any_flavor` addon as wrong-flavor, a `TargetInterfaceUnknown` verdict, or a folder of class `Shared`.
- No new error code, warning code, constant, command or flag.

### 8. Files

`src/doctor/registry.rs`, `src/doctor/detectors/external.rs`, `src/doctor/finding.rs`, README's doctor table, and the snapshots of §6 where they exist.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Rows 30–33 are in `FAILURE_MODES` with the ids, severities (P1, P2, P2, P3), tier `default`, `requires`, `cost_ms`, texts, manual pairs and remediations of Technical Approach §1, and `invariant_violations` finds nothing.
- [ ] `keyed_clients` returns only registered, in-scope clients, sorted by id; `recorded_entries` picks the recorded spelling of a key and skips an unrecorded case pair.
- [ ] Row 30 reports one finding per conflicting key with `owners`; row 31 one per case pair with every spelling's path; row 32 one per addon with `folders[]` and `expected`, never for an `any_flavor` addon or a `TargetInterfaceUnknown` verdict; row 33 one per addon whose folders load only out of date (the unit cases of the Test Plan pass).
- [ ] Prose remediations (rows 30, 31) name no runnable omaddons command; rows 32 and 33 give `omaddons update <addon> -t <id>`.
- [ ] Every observation's evidence passes `Evidence::is_private_safe`; `FolderEvidence` derives `Serialize + JsonSchema` and its optional keys are documented.
- [ ] README's doctor table has the four rows; the snapshots of A4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`) and E4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4`) and `SKILL.md` are re-accepted or regenerated where they exist.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes and `ubs` is clean on the changed files; the close comment lists the four ids, `owners`, `folders` (`name`, `toc`, `reason`, `interfaces`, `floor`) with `reason`'s value set, and the "decided" items of this part.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

In `src/doctor/detectors/external.rs`, table-driven over constructed `Inventory` values (`FolderEntry`'s fields are public), `TargetRecord`s and `crate::engine::testing::target(dir)`; one name per case; each assertion names the case and prints the input entries and the observations as JSON:

- `ownership_conflict_cases`: `two_addons_one_folder` (one finding, `owners: [Bar, Foo]`, instance `…:folder=foo`); `three_addons_one_folder` (title lists three); `five_owners_title_is_cut` ("and 2 more"); `conflict_on_a_case_pair_reported_once`; `no_conflict` (nothing); `shared_folder_is_not_a_conflict` (class `Shared` with `owned_on`, nothing).
- `case_collision_cases`: `two_spellings` (paths sorted, `count: 2`, `folder` the bytewise first); `three_spellings`; `managed_and_stray_file`; `link_and_folder`; `invalid_names` (`.git`/`.GIT`); `none`.
- `wrong_flavor_cases`: `game_type_excluded`, `no_interface`, `interface_not_in_family`, `below_client_floor` (with `floor`), `no_toc_is_no_loadable_toc`; `target_interface_unknown_is_no_finding`; `any_flavor_addon_is_skipped`; `compatible_is_no_finding`; `out_of_date_is_not_wrong_flavor`; `unreadable_is_not_judged`; `two_folders_one_finding` (plural title, two `folders`); `case_pair_judged_on_the_recorded_spelling`; `missing_folder_is_left_to_row_13`; each asserts instance, label, title (built through `LeftOutFolder::describe`), `folders[]`, `expected`, remediation argv.
- `out_of_date_cases`: `one_folder`, `two_folders`, `any_flavor_still_reported`, `current_is_no_finding`, `wrong_flavor_is_not_out_of_date`.
- `keyed_clients_cases` (a tempdir home through `Paths::with_roots` and `DoctorView::load_at`): `unregistered_client_is_left_out`, `out_of_scope_client_is_left_out` (`-t classic`), `sorted_by_id`.
- `budget_is_checked_between_clients` (an expired `Budget`: no observation, `incomplete: Some(deadline)`).
- `prose_remediations_name_no_command` (rows 30, 31 through the same rule as `names_a_command`); `update_argv_per_target`.
- `every_case_is_private_safe` (`Evidence::is_private_safe` over every case above).

In `src/doctor/registry.rs`: `the_inventory_rows_match_appendix_b` (id, subsystem, severity, tier, `requires`, `online`, `cost_ms`, `fix: None`, `manual: Some`, texts non-empty, manual pair naming no runnable command).

### Integration and end-to-end tests

None in this part. Part 5 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.5.5) builds these rows' fixtures and runs them through the real binary, including the no-false-positive check on the realistic home.

### Logging

Unit tests only: one name per case; each failure message names the case and shows the entries, record, verdicts and observations as pretty JSON.

## Considerations

- **Risk 3, doctor false positives (M, M).** The exclusions (`any_flavor`, `TargetInterfaceUnknown`, `Shared`, unregistered clients) are each a unit case. Row 33 will report many addons right after a game patch, which is true (P3; `--severity P2` hides it), and its remediation is the fix.
- **Hot spots.** `src/doctor/registry.rs` and `src/doctor/finding.rs` are shared by every E and F leaf: insert rows where they sort and append `Evidence` fields; rebase. `src/doctor/detectors/external.rs` is this leaf's (E1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`, created it with rows 28 and 29; part 3 edits row 28's function in it, so keep the helpers above the row functions and rebase).
- **Compatibility.** Additive: four ids and two evidence keys; `status` is unaffected (`default` rows never run there).
