title: Missing dependencies from the catalog, and snapshots kept as a possible only copy
description:
Part 2 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.5 (External artifacts). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

**The leaf.** F5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.5`) builds the doctor's `external_artifacts` subsystem: Appendix B rows 28–36 (the doctor's catalog, filed on the milestone epic `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`), the failure modes of what sits in a client's `Interface/AddOns` and in its client-side snapshots. All are reports with an exact remediation except one disabled repair (M4-D39). It serves G-M4-4 ("names every broken state omaddons can detect in what it owns or manages. Each finding carries concrete evidence and an exact remediation. A check that ran out of budget or entries says so") and checkpoint criterion 9 (repeatable detectors, a fixture and a clean home for every detector).

**This part** adds two rows that each reuse a rule the engine already has, so that the doctor and the engine can never disagree:

- row 34, `fm-external_artifacts-missing-dependency` (P2, `default`): a folder a managed addon's TOC requires is not installed, with a candidate from the catalog. It reuses the planner's dependency rules (`resolve::deps::is_satisfied`, `needed_folders`, `resolve`) over the client's inventory.
- row 35, `fm-external_artifacts-orphan-snapshot-only-copy` (P2, `default`): a client snapshot of a change that never committed, which retention keeps forever because it may hold the only copy of an addon or of a previous `WTF/`. It reuses retention's orphan-sweep rule, extracted into one shared function.

It is its own step because both rows touch engine files (`src/resolve/deps.rs`, `src/engine/retention.rs`) whose behaviour must stay unchanged, and both need their own careful unit tests. It builds on part 1's helpers.

**The decisions this part applies** (full text in the decision-log comments on the milestone epic):

- **M4-D48:** both rows are reports. Installing a dependency is a choice ("every finding whose fix is an omaddons command the user should choose"), and so is deciding what to do with a crashed change's leftovers. M4-D48 drops the vision's `orphan-inflight*` and `orphan-snapshot-dir*` because "retention's orphan sweep deletes free in-flight locks and dead stages after every commit … The case retention does not cover, an only copy, is row 35".
- **The plan's consideration for row 34:** "`missing-dependency` uses the catalog only, since a diagnosis makes no request without `--online`."
- **M4-D29:** both are `default` tier: never in `status` or `doctor --quick`.
- **M4-D30:** instances `@<target key>:folder=<missing folder key>` (row 34) and `@<target key>:tx=<ULID>` (row 35).
- **M4-D41:** `confidence` `high` where observed directly; row 35's two degraded cases are `medium` and `low` (§3).
- **M4-D42:** evidence holds folder and addon names, refs, snapshot paths and counts, never content, never a path below `WTF/` (a previous `WTF/` is only a boolean).
- **M4-D43:** every listing goes through `doctor::budget::list_dir` and charges the detector's `Budget`; a cut-short listing is `incomplete`, never clean; a layer that failed means `skipped`.
- **M4-D36 (context):** a repair's own client-side half `<meta>/snapshots/<tx>.repair/` is the doctor's, kept until `doctor gc`; it is never a finding of this row.
- **§8.1 defaults:** no network on a read path; fail closed on what cannot be read; existing keys first.

**What exists to build on** (verified at `c0ab5e9`, plus the leaf's blockers and part 1):

- `resolve::deps` (`src/resolve/deps.rs`), pure, with no I/O:
  - `needed_folders(primary, &[FolderVerdict]) -> BTreeSet<FolderName>` (`:41-57`): the primary folder and every folder of the same archive it requires, transitively;
  - `bridge_dependencies` (`:59-92`): the requirements of the other folders, which install only reports;
  - `trait DepView { fn folder(&self, dep) -> Option<ViewFolder> }` and `ViewFolder::{Planned, Present { class, owner }}` (`:94-109`);
  - `is_satisfied(dep, archive, view) -> Option<Satisfier>` (`:127-152`): a `Blizzard_*` folder (the client), a folder of `archive`, or a present folder of any class but `Invalid`;
  - `resolve(missing, target, &DepLookups { managed, released, catalog, tukui, wowi, now }) -> DepResolution` (`:276-342`): a managed record that lists the folder while it is gone → `Missing { ManagedFolderMissing, owner }`; the catalog's entries declaring the family; Tukui; WoWInterface; the catalog's undeclared entries; else `Missing { NoSource }`. `Resolved { r#ref, via, name, undeclared }`, `Ambiguous { candidates, reason }`.
- Planning's view (`PlanView`, `src/engine/plan.rs:1544-1567`) maps a live inventory entry to `Present { class: entry.class, owner: entry.owners.first() }`. Install follows the needed folders' requirements only (`plan.rs:4659-4690`), and names an addon after its primary folder (`:4649-4652`); `primary_by_shape(&[FolderName])` (`plan.rs:5484-5527`) picks it by names alone. Install's `missing_dependency` warning fixes with `omaddons install <ref> -t <id>` or `omaddons search <folder>` (`plan.rs:1577-1685`).
- `FolderVerdict { folder, report, dependencies: DepList { required, optional, unknown_condition }, interface }` (`src/engine/inspect.rs:886-899`, `src/toc.rs:203-211`), all fields public.
- `Catalog::load(paths) -> (Catalog, Vec<Warning>)` (`src/resolve/catalog.rs:144-191`): the embedded catalog plus `catalog.d`, files only; `impl CatalogLookup for Catalog` (`deps.rs:159-163`).
- Retention (`src/engine/retention.rs`): `snapshot_folders(client_snapshot)` counts the entries of its `AddOns/` plus one for `WTF.previous`, and one for an `AddOns/` that cannot be read (`:310-323`, private, unless F1 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1` has made it `pub(crate)`); `in_history(text, tx)` checks the raw history text (`:331-333`); the orphan sweep `orphans(paths, client, now, text)` (`:347-407`) keeps a client snapshot with entries (`:397`) and deletes the others that are named by a transaction id (`tx_named`), not in history, dead (`!InflightLock::is_live` and no `journal::existing`), and older than `ORPHAN_MIN_AGE`, in that order (`:385-402`). `InflightLock::is_live` (`src/fsx/lock.rs:247-276`) opens the lock file read-only and probes its flock; it returns an `io` error on an unreadable file. `journal::existing(paths, tx)` (`src/engine/journal.rs:670`). `paths::tx_named` strips only `.wtf` (`src/state/paths.rs:33-35`), so a `.repair` directory never parses.
- `history::text(paths)` reads the raw history (`src/state/history.rs:448-460`), `history::parse(text, filter)` parses it (`:463`), and `history::read` is the two (`:442-445`).
- From the leaf's blockers: E2's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.2`) History layer holds `history::read`'s `HistoryRead` (`DoctorView::history()`); `Layer::History`; E3's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`) `doctor::budget::list_dir(dir, &mut Budget) -> io::Result<Listing>` (one level, sorted, charged per entry, truncated past its budget); `crate::clock::now()`.
- From part 1 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.5.1): `keyed_clients(view, sel)`, `recorded_entries(addon, inv)`, the row-text conventions, and `Evidence`'s `owners`/`folders` additions.

## Technical Approach

Leaves this section names: E2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.2`, the tolerant view), E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, the doctor runtime), E5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`, the repair transaction) and F1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1`, the journal detectors).

### 1. The registry rows (`src/doctor/registry.rs`, where they sort)

| # | Id | P | Tier | `requires` | `cost_ms` | Instance | Confidence | Remediation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 34 | `fm-external_artifacts-missing-dependency` | P2 | `Default` | `[Discovery, Records, Inventory]` | 30 | `@<key>:folder=<missing folder key>` | high | argv: `omaddons install <ref> -t <id>`, or `omaddons search <folder> -t <id>` |
| 35 | `fm-external_artifacts-orphan-snapshot-only-copy` | P2 | `Default` | `[Discovery, History]` | 10 | `@<key>:tx=<ULID>`, or `@<key>:path=<dir>` for an unlistable snapshots directory | high (medium, low: §3) | prose naming the path |

Both `online: false`, `fix: None`, `manual: Some(…)`, constants in `ids`. `cost_ms` are declared estimates (decided while writing this bead: row 34 covers a full inventory plus the catalog's parse, row 35 a few listings), adjustable with a measured reason in the close comment.

| # | `title` | `description` | `why` | Manual pair: `instruction` / `reason` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 34 | a folder a managed addon requires is not installed | The TOC of a managed addon's own folder lists a required dependency that is not in AddOns, is not one of the addon's own folders, and is not one the client provides. | The client does not load an addon whose required dependency is missing. | install the addon that ships `<folder>` / installing is your choice, and only you can pick among several candidates |
| 35 | a crashed change left folders in a snapshot, possibly their only copy | A client snapshot of a change that never committed, with no journal and no live process, over an hour old, still holds addon folders or a previous WTF/. Retention keeps it forever because it may hold the only copy. | Nothing restores or removes it: undo cannot (the change never committed), and retention keeps it on purpose. Only you can tell whether its contents are still needed. | copy back what you still need from `<path>` with the game closed, then delete the directory / omaddons never deletes what may be the only copy of an addon |

### 2. Row 34: missing dependencies, from the catalog only (`src/doctor/detectors/external/deps.rs`)

1. **The dependency view over an inventory** (`src/resolve/deps.rs`): `impl DepView for Inventory`, `folder(dep)` → the first entry (in the inventory's order) whose key equals `dep.key()` → `ViewFolder::Present { class: entry.class, owner: entry.owners.first().cloned() }`; none → `None`. This is exactly the live half of `PlanView`, which is not edited (`src/engine/plan.rs` is another leaf's hot spot). Decided while writing this bead.
2. **The primary folder at rest.** For each managed addon of the record: the recorded folder whose key equals the addon's name ASCII-lowercased (install names an addon after its primary folder); else `crate::engine::plan::primary_by_shape(&addon.folders)`; else none, and every recorded folder is needed, as planning does without a primary.
3. **Needed folders.** One `FolderVerdict` per entry of `recorded_entries(addon, inv)` with a TOC: `folder` its `FolderName`, `report` its verdict, `dependencies.required` its `TocSummary.dependencies` parsed with `FolderName::new` (names that do not parse are dropped; the TOC reader already drops them), `optional` and `unknown_condition` empty, `interface: None`. Then `deps::needed_folders(primary, &verdicts)`.
   - Decided while writing this bead: only the needed folders' requirements count. Install installs exactly those and only reports a bridge's (`Masque_Dominos` requiring `Masque`), so reporting bridges would flag, on many healthy homes, an optional module the user never asked for (risk 3).
4. **Unsatisfied requirements.** For each needed folder and each of its required dependencies: `deps::is_satisfied(dep, &addon.folders, inventory)`. `None` is missing. Group the missing ones by key across the client's addons: `required_by` (the addon names, sorted, de-duplicated) and the spelling of the first requirer's TOC (by addon name order).
5. **Where to get it, offline.** Load the catalog once per detection, only when something is missing: `Catalog::load(view.paths()).0` (its `catalog_override_invalid` warnings are not repeated by the doctor: decided while writing this bead, they are a configuration report, and `install` and `search` already give them). Then:

   ```rust
   deps::resolve(&dep, target, &DepLookups {
       managed: record, released: &|_| false, catalog: &catalog,
       tukui: None, wowi: None,          // the catalog only: no request, no stale cached index
       now: crate::clock::now(),
   })
   ```

   | Resolution | Finding | Remediation |
   |---|---|---|
   | `Resolved { r#ref, .. }` (unique, declared or undeclared) | `candidate: "<ref>"` | argv `omaddons install <ref> -t <id>` (the form install's own warning uses) |
   | `Ambiguous { candidates, .. }` | `candidates: [<refs>]`, `reason: several_catalog_entries` | argv `omaddons search <folder> -t <id>` |
   | `Missing { NoSource, .. }` | `reason: no_source` | argv `omaddons search <folder> -t <id>` |
   | `Missing { ManagedFolderMissing, .. }` | **no finding** | — |

   - Decided while writing this bead: an ambiguous folder gets `search`, not the first candidate (install's warning installs the top one), because a diagnosis lets the user choose and the evidence lists every candidate.
   - Decided while writing this bead: `ManagedFolderMissing` (another managed addon of this client lists the folder and it is gone) is not reported here, because it is row 13's `record-folder-missing` (F3 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.3`), with its reinstall remediation: one finding per broken thing.
   - `search` consults the catalog offline and the other sources only when online; its argv runs on a test home.
6. **The observation.** Subject `.folder(<missing FolderName>)`; `folder` = its spelling; `addon` `null`. Evidence `{required_by, candidate?, candidates?, reason?}`. Title "`<folder>`, required by `<addon>`, is not installed" ("`<folder>`, required by `<n>` addons, is not installed" for several). Confidence high.
7. **Budget.** `budget.check()` before each client; no listing (the inventory is the view's, the catalog is embedded plus `catalog.d`).

Example (paths absolute in real output):

```json
{"id":"fm-external_artifacts-missing-dependency","instance":"fm-external_artifacts-missing-dependency@01M5ZQ7Y3KJ8V9W2X4C6B0N1RT:folder=testlib",
 "label":"retail/TestLib","severity":"P2","subsystem":"external_artifacts","title":"TestLib, required by Foo, is not installed",
 "confidence":"high","target":{"id":"retail","key":"01M5ZQ7Y3KJ8V9W2X4C6B0N1RT"},"addon":null,"folder":"TestLib",
 "evidence":{"required_by":["Foo"],"candidate":"gh:o/testlib"},
 "remediation":{"command":"omaddons install gh:o/testlib -t retail","argv":["omaddons","install","gh:o/testlib","-t","retail"],
   "explain_command":"omaddons doctor explain fm-external_artifacts-missing-dependency -t retail","explain_argv":["…"],
   "auto_fixable":false,"needs_force":false,"estimated_actions":0,"destructive":false}}
```

### 3. Row 35: snapshots kept as a possible only copy

**One rule with the sweep** (`src/engine/retention.rs`):

```rust
/// What the orphan sweep makes of one entry `name` at `path` in a client's `<meta>/snapshots/`.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum SnapshotFate {
    NotATransaction,                                  // the name is not `<tx>` or `<tx>.wtf` (a `.repair` half, a stray file)
    Recorded,                                         // history's raw text names the transaction
    Live,                                             // its in-flight lock is held, or its journal exists
    Young,                                            // younger than ORPHAN_MIN_AGE
    Sweep,                                            // dead, old and empty: the sweep deletes it
    KeptOnlyCopy { entries: usize, wtf_previous: bool }, // dead and old, but holds AddOns/ entries or WTF.previous
}
pub(crate) fn client_snapshot_fate(paths: &Paths, name: &str, path: &Path, now: Timestamp, history_text: &str)
    -> Result<SnapshotFate>;
```

- It applies today's checks in today's order: `tx_named(name)` (else `NotATransaction`), not `in_history` (else `Recorded`), dead (else `Live`; an `is_live` error is the `Err`), old (else `Young`), then `snapshot_folders(path)`: 0 → `Sweep`, else `KeptOnlyCopy { entries, wtf_previous: <WTF.previous exists> }`.
- `orphans`' client-side branch (`:391-402`) calls it and sweeps exactly `Sweep`, propagating its error with `?` as today; the state-side branch is unchanged. Retention's existing tests pass unchanged.
- Decided while writing this bead: the doctor reports exactly what the sweep keeps, so "what retention keeps as a possible only copy" and "what the doctor calls one" cannot drift; `snapshot_folders` becomes `pub(crate)` if F1 has not already made it so.

**The raw history text** (`src/doctor/view.rs`, E2's History layer): the sweep's "never committed" is judged against the raw text (a torn or merged line still names its transaction), which `HistoryRead` does not keep. Decided while writing this bead: the History layer reads `history::text(paths)` once, parses it with `history::parse(&text, &HistoryFilter::default())`, and keeps both; `DoctorView::history_text(&self) -> Option<&str>` is added beside `history()`, whose type and behaviour are unchanged. No second read of `history.jsonl`.

**The detector** (`src/doctor/detectors/external/snapshots.rs`), per `KeyedClient` (part 1), with `client = ClientPaths::new(target.client_dir)` and `now = crate::clock::now()`:

1. `budget::list_dir(client.meta_dir().join("snapshots"), budget)`:
   - not found → nothing;
   - another error → one observation: subject `.path(<the snapshots dir>)`, evidence `{path, reason: "unreadable"}`, confidence low, title "the snapshots of `<id>` cannot be listed, so an only copy may be hidden there", remediation prose "make `<path>` readable by your user". Decided while writing this bead: fail closed (§8.1), since a silent pass is what M4-D43 forbids;
   - truncated → stop, `incomplete`.
2. For each entry, `client_snapshot_fate(view.paths(), name, path, now, text)`, where `text` is `view.history_text()` (always `Some` here: the row requires the History layer, so it is skipped, never run, when that layer failed):
   - `KeptOnlyCopy { entries, wtf_previous }` → an observation: subject `.tx(<tx>)` (label `<id> · tx <tx>`), evidence `{tx, path: <the snapshot dir>, kept_folders, wtf_previous, count: entries}`, where `kept_folders` is the sorted names of its `AddOns/` from `budget::list_dir` (a truncated listing stops the detector with `incomplete`); confidence high. Title "a crashed change left `<n>` folders in snapshot `<tx>`, possibly their only copy", or, with only `WTF.previous`, "a crashed change left the previous WTF/ in snapshot `<tx>`, possibly its only copy" (both: "… `<n>` folders and the previous WTF/ …").
   - `Err` (the in-flight lock or the journal could not be checked) → when `snapshot_folders(path) > 0`, the same observation with `reason: "liveness_unknown"` and confidence medium. Decided while writing this bead: a possible only copy is reported, not hidden, when its liveness cannot be read; a live transaction over an hour old holding such a snapshot is not a realistic state.
   - Any other fate → nothing.
3. Remediation prose for a kept snapshot: "look in `<path>`: copy back what you still need, with the game closed, then delete the directory; omaddons never deletes it". It names no runnable omaddons command.

Notes:

- A `<tx>.repair` directory (E5's quarantine half) is `NotATransaction`: the doctor's own artifacts are `doctor gc`'s (M4-D36).
- A transaction with a journal is `Live` here, and F1's journal rows report it (with their own `may_hold_only_copy`), so the two subsystems never report one snapshot twice.
- Never list or name anything below `WTF.previous`: `wtf_previous` is a boolean.
- The detector does not call `fsx::` directly; `InflightLock::is_live` is reached through `retention::client_snapshot_fate`, and it only opens the lock file read-only (E3's scan of `src/doctor/detectors/` for `fsx::` and `WriteSession` stays clean).

### 4. Evidence keys added (`src/doctor/finding.rs`)

| Key | Type | Row | Value |
|---|---|---|---|
| `required_by` | `[string]` | 34 | the managed addons whose needed folders require the missing folder, sorted |
| `candidate` | string | 34 | the ref to install, when the catalog has exactly one |
| `candidates` | `[string]` | 34 | several catalog entries' refs, sorted |
| `kept_folders` | `[string]` | 35 | the entry names of the snapshot's `AddOns/`, sorted bytewise |
| `wtf_previous` | bool | 35 | the snapshot holds a previous `WTF/` |

Each `Option`, omitted when `None`, documented optional. `reason` gains the values `several_catalog_entries`, `no_source` (row 34) and `liveness_unknown`, `unreadable` (row 35). Existing `tx`, `path`, `count` are reused. Every case passes `Evidence::is_private_safe` (the snapshot path is `<client dir>/Interface/.omaddons/snapshots/<tx>[.wtf]`, never below `WTF/`).

### 5. README

The doctor's failure-mode table: rows 34 (remediation `omaddons install <candidate> -t <id>`, or `omaddons search <folder> -t <id>`) and 35 (advice, naming the path), in this commit.

### 6. Snapshots and registries that list failure modes

As part 1: re-accept A4's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`) and E4's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4`) snapshots and regenerate `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` where B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`) has landed and lists failure modes.

### 7. What not to do

- Do not pass the Tukui or WoWInterface index to `resolve`, and make no request.
- Do not edit `src/engine/plan.rs`; do not change the sweep's behaviour (every existing retention test and `tests/engine_crash.rs`'s orphan checks pass unchanged).
- Do not report a bridge's requirement, a folder another managed addon lost, a committed transaction's snapshot, a young or live one, or a `.repair` half.
- Do not read `history.jsonl` twice.

### 8. Files

`src/doctor/registry.rs`, `src/doctor/detectors/external.rs` (`mod deps; mod snapshots;`), `src/doctor/detectors/external/deps.rs` and `external/snapshots.rs` (new), `src/resolve/deps.rs`, `src/engine/retention.rs`, `src/doctor/view.rs`, `src/doctor/finding.rs`, README's doctor table.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Rows 34 and 35 are in `FAILURE_MODES` with the ids, severities (P2, P2), tier `default`, `requires`, `cost_ms`, texts, manual pairs and remediations of Technical Approach §1, and `invariant_violations` finds nothing.
- [ ] Row 34 reports a needed folder's missing requirement once per missing folder with `required_by`, and `candidate` (argv `install <ref> -t <id>`), or `candidates`/`reason` (argv `search <folder> -t <id>`); it never reports a bridge's requirement, a requirement satisfied by the client, by the addon's own folders or by any present folder, or a folder another managed addon lost; it consults only the catalog (a recording lookup sees no other source).

title: `managed-files-modified` bounded by its budget, and its re-hash under `--include-deep`
description:
Part 3 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.5 (External artifacts). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

**The leaf.** F5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.5`) builds the doctor's `external_artifacts` subsystem: Appendix B rows 28–36 (the doctor's catalog, filed on the milestone epic `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`), the failure modes of what sits in a client's `Interface/AddOns` and in its client-side snapshots. It serves G-M4-4 ("a check that ran out of budget or entries says so: incomplete coverage is never reported as healthy"; "`status` and `doctor` never disagree about what is wrong") and checkpoint criteria 9 and 12.

**This part** finishes the two published rows of the subsystem, which E1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`, the failure-mode registry) moved onto the registry and E2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.2`, `DoctorView`) onto the tolerant view:

- row 28, `fm-external_artifacts-managed-files-modified` (P2, `quick`): managed files changed on disk. Appendix B gives it two depths: "quick (stat); deep (re-hash)", "by re-hash under `--include-deep`". Today its doctor detector runs `drift::check` in stat mode only, and that walk is unbounded (it is drift's own recursion, not the doctor's bounded walker). This part bounds it by the detector's `Budget` and adds the deep re-hash under `--include-deep` (and in `doctor explain`), while `status` stays exactly as it is.
- row 29, `fm-external_artifacts-ownership-transferred` (P2, `cached`): kept as E1 and E2 left it; no code changes here (its fixture is part 5's, its README row exists).

It is its own step because it touches the doctor runtime's budget plumbing (`Selection`, the tier and cost a detector runs with) and `src/drift.rs`, which no other part touches, and because it must leave `status`'s output byte-identical.

**The decisions this part applies** (full text in the decision-log comments on the milestone epic):

- **M4-D29, one registry by tier.** `status --cached`: `cached`; plain `status`, `doctor --quick`, `doctor health`: `cached` and `quick`; `doctor`: every tier but `deep`; `doctor --include-deep`: every tier. The `quick` tier may run "the stat-mode drift check"; `deep` adds "content hashing (blobs, `--deep` drift)". Row 28 stays a `quick` row (it is published under `status`), with a deep variant. Rejected: `status` calling `doctor`; two implementations of one check.
- **M4-D43, budgets are enforced, not only estimated.** "Every detector works through a `Budget` handle (a deadline and an entry counter) that the shared bounded walker and every listing check. A detector that hits its deadline, `DOCTOR_SCAN_MAX_ENTRIES` or an online request limit stops and returns what it found plus an `incomplete` record", which E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`) turns into `fm-state_files-check-incomplete`, so the run is never `DONE_OK`. Rejected: treating truncation as a warning on a healthy run.
- **M4-D30:** row 28's instance stays `@<target key>:addon=<name>` whichever depth found it, so `--since` compares a stat run and a deep run instance by instance.
- **M4-D42:** evidence holds counts and the check's depth, never a path below `WTF/` or file content.
- **§3.2 criterion 12:** "for every fixture, the issue ids `status` reports equal the doctor findings of those tiers": `status` and `doctor --quick` both use the stat check.
- **§3.2 criterion 10 (context, the perf test of E4, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4`):** "each `quick` detector takes under 5 ms (release build, on the bench home)".

**What exists to build on** (verified at `c0ab5e9`, plus the leaf's blockers):

- `drift::check(target, record, index, mode) -> DriftReport` (`src/drift.rs:118-155`): per addon of the record (in the record's order) and per folder (sorted by key), `walk` → `compare` (`:229-259`, `:320-387`); `list` (`:273-304`) recurses without following symlinks. `DriftMode::{Presence, Stat, Deep}` (`:31-41`, wire `presence`/`stat`/`deep`): `Stat` trusts a size-and-mtime match outside the racy window (`:343-346`), `Deep` re-hashes every file. `Walked { drift, files_checked, files_rehashed }` (`:108-114`). `check_folder` (`:160-169`) re-reads the `AddOns` listing per call. D1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1`) makes `slack` `pub(crate)` in this file; nothing else changes it.
- `app::drift::report(paths, target, record, mode)` (`src/app/drift.rs:74-85`) loads the files index and calls `check`; `reinstall_hint(addon, target)` (`:88-94`).
- From E1 and E2: row 28's per-addon rule (a drift entry of state `Modified` → one observation: `Subject::target(id, key).addon(name)`, title "`<name>`'s files changed on disk (`<n>` file)"/"(`<n>` files)", evidence `count`, remediation `reinstall_hint`), shared with `status`, which feeds it `status`'s own drift report until F8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.8`) moves `status` onto the registry; row 28's doctor detector in `src/doctor/detectors/external.rs`, `requires: [Discovery, Records]`, calling `app::drift::report(.., DriftMode::Stat)` per registered, in-scope discovered client; row 29 there too (`[Records]`, `cached`, degraded addons > 0, `inspect_hint`). `Selection` (`src/doctor/selection.rs`: `target`, `only`, `skip`; `Selection::all()`, `parse`).
- From E3: `Budget { deadline, entries }` with `charge(n) -> Result<(), Exhausted>` (entries first, then the deadline), `check()`, `incomplete()`, `Budget::for_tier(tier)` (`cached`/`quick` → `QUICK_DETECTOR_BUDGET`, 5 ms; `default`/`deep` → `DOCTOR_DETECTOR_DEADLINE`, 2 s; the implicit deadlines ×20 in debug builds; entries `DOCTOR_SCAN_MAX_ENTRIES`, 20,000); the runtime's per-detector start (`src/doctor/runtime.rs`) and the `--budget` refusal and shares from declared `cost_ms` (`src/doctor/mod.rs`, `plan_diagnose`); the tier filter (`--quick`, default, `--include-deep`); `doctor explain` (`src/doctor/explain.rs`), which re-detects one row with `DOCTOR_DETECTOR_DEADLINE` whatever its tier; the `doctor.detector.panic=sleep:<ms>` failpoint (a slow detector, after its clock starts). From E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`): `doctor fix` flattens the same selection flags, `--include-deep` among them (`src/app/doctor.rs`).

## Technical Approach

Leaves this section names: E1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`, the registry), E2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.2`, the tolerant view), E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, the doctor runtime), E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`, `doctor fix`) and F8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.8`, `status` on the registry).

### 1. The bounded drift walk (`src/drift.rs`, `src/app/drift.rs`)

```rust
/// [`check`], calling `between` after each folder with what that folder cost. When
/// `between` returns `false` the walk stops: the report then holds only the addons whose
/// folders were all walked, and the second value is `false` (incomplete).
pub fn check_bounded(
    target: &Target,
    record: &TargetRecord,
    index: Option<&FilesIndex>,
    mode: DriftMode,
    between: &mut dyn FnMut(&Walked) -> bool,
) -> (DriftReport, bool);

pub fn check(target, record, index, mode) -> DriftReport { check_bounded(target, record, index, mode, &mut |_| true).0 }
```

- Same listing, same order, same per-folder `walk`; only the stop is new. An addon whose folders were partly walked when the walk stopped is dropped from the report, so a stop never reports an addon as clean, or as `missing`, from half its folders.
- `src/app/drift.rs` gains `report_bounded(paths, target, record, mode, between) -> (DriftReport, bool)` beside `report`, with the same index rule.
- `status`, `list`, `info` and every existing caller keep calling `check` and `report`, unchanged.
- Decided while writing this bead: the bound is enforced between folders, because the walk is drift's own (`list`'s recursion, `:273-304`) and a folder's drift lists are complete only when its walk is; E3's walker is not used, so `drift` keeps no dependency on the doctor.

### 2. The deep variant (`src/doctor/selection.rs`, `src/doctor/registry.rs`, E3's runtime)

A registry row has one tier (E1), and a detector learns nothing of the run's tier filter from what it is passed. Decided while writing this bead:

- **`Selection` gains `pub deep: bool`**, default `false` (`Selection::all()` and `parse` leave it `false`). It is set to `true`:
  - by `doctor` / `doctor diagnose` when `--include-deep` is given (E3's selection code, `src/app/doctor.rs` or `src/doctor/mod.rs`, where the tier filter is chosen);
  - by `doctor fix` and `doctor diff` from the same flattened flag (E6's `FixArgs`);
  - by `doctor explain`, always: an explain is a deliberate look at one row, E3 already gives it `DOCTOR_DETECTOR_DEADLINE` whatever the tier, and an instance found by a deep run must not read `instances: []` in its explain.
  - `status`, `doctor health`, `doctor --quick` and `--robot-triage` (E4 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4`) never set it.
- **The declared deep variants** (`src/doctor/registry.rs`):

  ```rust
  /// Rows that look deeper under `--include-deep`, with the cost declared for that depth.
  pub const DEEP_VARIANTS: &[(&str, u32)] = &[(ids::MANAGED_FILES_MODIFIED, 300)];
  impl FailureMode {
      /// The tier this row's budget is drawn from in `sel`: `Deep` for a deep variant
      /// when `sel.deep`, else its own tier.
      pub fn tier_for(&self, sel: &Selection) -> Tier;
      /// The declared cost in `sel`: the deep variant's when it applies, else `cost_ms`.
      pub fn cost_for(&self, sel: &Selection) -> u32;
  }
  ```

  `300` ms is a declared estimate for re-hashing a realistic client's managed files (decided while writing this bead; adjust with a measured reason in the close comment).
- **E3's runtime uses them:** each detector's `Budget` starts as `Budget::for_tier(row.tier_for(sel))` (instead of `row.tier`); the `--budget` refusal sums `row.cost_for(sel)`, and each detector's share is computed from `cost_for`. The tier **filter** keeps using `row.tier`, so row 28 runs wherever `quick` rows run and is never excluded by `--quick`.
- **Row 28's detector** uses `DriftMode::Deep` when `sel.deep`, else `DriftMode::Stat`, and adds `evidence.drift_mode` (below).
- **E4's `cost_summary`**, if E4 has landed: `deep_total_ms` counts `cost_for(&Selection { deep: true, ..Selection::all() })` for each row it sums (whichever of E4 and this part lands second makes it so); `quick_total_ms` and `default_total_ms` keep `cost_ms`.
- An invariant (added to E1's `invariant_violations`): every `DEEP_VARIANTS` id names a registered `Cached` or `Quick` row, and its deep cost is at least the row's `cost_ms`.

### 3. Row 28's detector (`src/doctor/detectors/external.rs`)

For each registered, in-scope discovered client with an available record (as E2's version does):

1. `let mode = if sel.deep { DriftMode::Deep } else { DriftMode::Stat };`
2. `app::drift::report_bounded(view.paths(), target, record, mode, &mut |walked| budget.charge(walked.files_checked.max(1)).is_ok())`: one entry per file checked (at least one per folder), and the deadline, between folders.
3. The shared rule turns each `Modified` addon into its observation, unchanged; the detector adds `drift_mode: <mode>` to each observation's evidence.
4. If the walk stopped, stop iterating clients and return `Detected { found: <what was found>, incomplete: budget.incomplete() }`.

`status` keeps its own drift report and the shared rule (E1/E2), so its output does not change: E1's characterization snapshots and `tests/e2e_status_issues.rs` pass unchanged. When F8 moves `status` onto the registry, `status` passes `deep: false` and its quick `Budget`, and F8 decides how `status` shows an `incomplete` (F8's bead owns that, with the `status --cached` budget).

**Evidence key added** (`src/doctor/finding.rs`, E1's `Evidence`): `drift_mode`, type `drift::DriftMode` (`"stat" | "deep"`; `presence` never appears here), `Option`, omitted when `None`, documented optional. Row 28's evidence is `{count, drift_mode}`.

### 4. Row 29

No code change: `[Records]`, `cached`, cost 1, one observation per client with degraded addons > 0, `{count}`, `inspect_hint(id)` (`omaddons list -t <id> -v`, `src/app/status.rs:1207-1209`). Part 5 builds its fixture. Confirm it still has the static manual pair E3 gave the published rows.

### 5. README

- `### doctor`: "`--include-deep` also runs the `deep` checks: it re-hashes every managed file for `fm-external_artifacts-managed-files-modified` (a plain `doctor` and `status` compare sizes and times), and every cached archive (F6 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.6`, once it lands). `doctor explain` looks as deeply."
- The doctor's failure-mode table, row 28: "stat check; every file re-hashed under `--include-deep`".
- `status`'s issue table is unchanged.

### 6. What not to do

- Do not change `check`'s or `report`'s behaviour, or any `status`, `list` or `info` output.
- Do not give row 28 a second registry row or another tier; do not let `--quick` or `status` re-hash.
- Do not cut a folder's walk in half; do not report an addon from a partial walk.

### 7. Files

`src/drift.rs`, `src/app/drift.rs`, `src/doctor/selection.rs`, `src/doctor/registry.rs`, `src/doctor/runtime.rs` and `src/doctor/mod.rs` (the budget's tier and the declared cost), `src/doctor/explain.rs` and `src/app/doctor.rs` (setting `deep`), `src/doctor/detectors/external.rs` (row 28's detector), `src/doctor/finding.rs`, README.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `drift::check_bounded` stops between folders when its callback says so, drops a partly walked addon, and `check` gives exactly today's reports (unit cases); no caller of `check` or `report` changed.
- [ ] `Selection.deep` is `false` for `status`, `doctor health` and `doctor --quick`, `true` for `doctor --include-deep`, `doctor fix --include-deep` and `doctor explain`.
- [ ] `DEEP_VARIANTS` holds row 28 with 300 ms; `tier_for`/`cost_for` give `Deep`/300 for it only when `sel.deep`; E3's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`) runtime starts the row's `Budget` from `tier_for` and sums `cost_for` for `--budget`; the new invariant holds.
- [ ] Row 28 uses the stat check unless `sel.deep`, then re-hashes; its evidence carries `drift_mode`; a walk cut by the budget yields what was found plus `incomplete`, never a clean result.
- [ ] `status`'s output is byte-identical (E1's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`) characterization snapshots and `tests/e2e_status_issues.rs` unchanged); row 29 is unchanged.
- [ ] README describes `--include-deep` and row 28's two depths.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes and `ubs` is clean on the changed files; the close comment lists `drift_mode` (and its values), `Selection.deep`, `DEEP_VARIANTS`, the `--include-deep` meaning, and the "decided" items of this part.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

- **`src/drift.rs`** (on the module's existing tempdir trees and `index` helper):
  - `check_is_check_bounded_unbounded`: for every existing case (clean, modified, deleted, added, racy, unindexed, missing), `check` equals `check_bounded(.., &mut |_| true)` with `complete: true`.
  - `check_bounded_stops_between_folders`: three addons of one folder each; a callback that allows two folders → two addons, `complete: false`; the callback saw exactly two `Walked` values.
  - `a_stopped_walk_drops_the_partial_addon`: one addon of three folders, stopped after the second → the addon is absent from the report.
  - `deep_rehashes_a_kept_mtime_same_size_edit`: a file rewritten with other bytes of the same size and its mtime set back (outside the racy window) → `Stat` reports the addon `Clean`, `Deep` reports `Modified` with that path in `modified`.
- **`src/doctor/registry.rs`**: `tier_for_and_cost_for` (cases `row_28_default_selection` → `Quick`/5, `row_28_deep_selection` → `Deep`/300, `row_29_deep_selection` → `Cached`/1, `a_default_row_deep_selection` → its own); `deep_variants_name_registered_quick_rows` (through `invariant_violations`, with a synthetic bad slice: an unknown id, a `Default` row, a deep cost below `cost_ms`, each named in the violation).
- **`src/doctor/selection.rs`**: `deep_defaults_to_false` (`all()`, `parse(..)`).

title: Nested addon folders and the disabled flatten fixer
description:
Part 4 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.5 (External artifacts). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

**The leaf.** F5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.5`) builds the doctor's `external_artifacts` subsystem: Appendix B rows 28–36 (the doctor's catalog, filed on the milestone epic `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`), the failure modes of what sits in a client's `Interface/AddOns` and in its client-side snapshots. Every row but one is a report; this part builds the one with a repair. It serves G-M4-4 ("every auto-fixable state is repaired by one consented command that backs up verbatim, never deletes, and is proven by a fixture that round-trips") and G-M4-6 ("every repair is a journaled transaction that recovers like any other"; "the doctor never writes `WTF/`").

**This part** adds row 36, `fm-external_artifacts-nested-addon-folder` (P3, `default`), and its fixer, the flatten, in `src/doctor/fixers/flatten.rs`. A user who unzips an addon by hand often ends up with `AddOns/Foo/Foo/Foo.toc` or, from a GitHub "Download ZIP", `AddOns/Foo-main/Foo/Foo.toc`. The client loads only top-level folders whose TOC is named after them, so the addon silently does nothing. Nothing detects this today (the plan's §2.5). The flatten moves the inner folder up and quarantines the emptied wrapper, as an engine repair transaction. It ships **disabled**: it runs only when the user names its failure mode with `--only`, and never while the client runs. It is its own step because it is the subsystem's only write path, and its exclusions decide whether it could ever move the wrong folder.

**The decisions this part applies** (full text in the decision-log comments on the milestone epic):

- **M4-D39, a fixer that changes user content ships disabled.** "`fm-external_artifacts-nested-addon-folder` has a fixer: move the inner addon folder up and quarantine the wrapper. That fixer has `enabled: false`, so `doctor fix` without `--only` lists it as available and does not run it. The only way to run it is `--only fm-external_artifacts-nested-addon-folder`. It refuses while the client runs, and refuses when the destination name exists (`RENAME_NOREPLACE`). `capabilities` lists `enabled` per fixer." Why: "a hand-installed folder is the user's, and the doctor's default fix touches only omaddons' own state." **Rejected:** no fixer at all, because "a common manual-install mistake (`Foo-main/Foo/`) would then have a finding and no help".
- **M4-D31 (context, E5's, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`):** "A flatten becomes two or three separately journaled renames; no step ever hides more than one rename." Each rename has write-ahead `step` lines and endpoint predicates; a crash between them recovers to the whole before state. **Rejected there:** one write-ahead step per presentation-level action (a crash between a flatten's two renames would leave a state matching neither before nor after).
- **M4-D35 (context, E5's):** quarantine never crosses a filesystem: a client victim goes to `<meta>/snapshots/<repair tx>.repair/quarantine/<path relative to the client dir>`; a rename that would cross a mount is refused before anything moves.
- **M4-D44 and M4-D45 (context, E6's, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`):** `doctor fix --dry-run` discloses every primitive and returns a token; `--if-match <token>` runs exactly that or nothing; under the global lock the planned detectors are re-run and the plan rebuilt before any repair, so a nested folder that changed or vanished since the preview drops out or stales the bound run.
- **M4-D36 (context):** the quarantined wrapper is kept until `doctor gc`; retention never touches `.repair` halves.
- **M4-D41:** confidence `medium`: the shape is observed directly, the user's intent to install the inner addon is inferred.
- **M4-D42:** evidence holds the wrapper's path, the inner folder's name, the TOC file name and the shape, never content.
- **Common rule 16 (previews bind):** the flatten's path is `doctor fix`, which binds with E6's token; part 5 tests a change between preview and run.

**What exists to build on** (verified at `c0ab5e9`, plus the leaf's blockers and part 1):

- The inventory (`src/inventory.rs:160-259`), at `Depth::Full` through E2's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.2`) view: each entry's `class` (`Unmanaged` = a real directory with a valid, non-protected name that no record claims), `case_duplicate`, `unreadable`, and `toc` (`None` when the client loads no TOC from it). `FolderName::is_protected` (`src/model.rs:82`).
- `toc::DiskFolder::new(path)` (`src/toc/loaded.rs:38-62`: `InvalidInput` for a name that cannot be a folder name), `toc::loaded_toc(&view, &target.rules) -> io::Result<Option<LoadedToc>>` (`:186-211`: the TOC named after the folder with the most specific suffix the client reads; `None` when there is none), and `toc::judge(folder, loaded, rules, family, interface, table)` (`:416-497`).
- `engine::ownership` refuses a change whose name differs only in case from an existing folder (`case_collision`, never overridable: Wine would see one folder under two names, `src/engine/ownership.rs:271-279`, `:349-362`). On a case-sensitive filesystem `RENAME_NOREPLACE` does not see `AddOns/foo` as `AddOns/Foo`.
- From E5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`, the repair transaction, through E6): the lowering of `Fix::Flatten { inner: <A>/X/Y, outer: <A>/X }` (`<A>` = `Interface/AddOns`): when `Y ≠ X`, `RenameNoReplace <A>/X/Y → <A>/Y`, then `RenameNoReplace <A>/X → <client quarantine>/Interface/AddOns/X`; when `Y = X`, `<A>/X → <A>/.omaddons-flatten-<tx>`, its child back to `<A>/X`, and the emptied wrapper into quarantine under its own name. Lowering refuses, before anything is written, a destination that exists (`file_exists`, "… already exists; it is never replaced"), an inner folder that is not a direct child of the outer one, a protected name, a path outside the client's scope or under `WTF/`, and a mount crossing (`filesystem_mismatch`).
- From E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`, `doctor fix`): the grouping (a fixer with `enabled: false` is listed and not run unless `--only` names its id; a subsystem name in `--only` never enables it; a finding named by id is planned whatever its `auto_fixable`); the static preconditions (`ClientNotRunning`: a client a fix touches that the process scan lists, or whose running state is unknown, is `REFUSING` with `doctor_refused`, `details.reason: client_running`; `SameFs`: E5's mount check; `LockHeld`: by construction); `fix::remediation_for(finding, spec, target_id)`: `omaddons doctor fix --only <fm> [-t <id>]`, `auto_fixable` = enabled and not forced and fixable, `estimated_actions` from `Fix::primitive_count()` (a flatten 2, or 3 when the inner name equals the wrapper's); VERIFYING re-runs the fixed rows' detectors. E6's debug-only test fixer `fm-test-flatten` (`src/doctor/test_fixers.rs`) has the same two shapes for `TestWrap*` folders; this part's real detector generalizes them.
- From E1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`): `FixerSpec { plan: fn(&DoctorView, &Finding) -> Result<Vec<Fix>, Refusal>, writes_to: &[ScopeName], ops: &[FixKind], enabled, needs_force, cardinality, preconditions: &[FixerPrecondition] }`; `ScopeName::{State, Config, Cache, ClientMeta, AddOns, Skill}`; `FixKind::Flatten`; `Fix::Flatten { inner, outer }`; the invariant "a `needs_force` fixer is never `enabled`". From E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`): `doctor::budget::list_dir` (one level, sorted, charged, truncated past the budget). From part 1 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.5.1): `keyed_clients(view, sel)`.

## Technical Approach

Leaves this section names: E1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`, the registry), E2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.2`, the tolerant view), E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, the doctor runtime), E5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`, the repair transaction) and E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`, `doctor fix`).

### 1. The registry row (`src/doctor/registry.rs`, where it sorts)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| `id` | `fm-external_artifacts-nested-addon-folder` |
| `severity`, `tier` | P3, `Default` |
| `requires` | `[Discovery, Records, Inventory]` |
| `cost_ms` | 30 (a declared estimate: one listing and a few TOC reads per candidate wrapper; adjust with a measured reason) |
| `online` | false |
| `fix` | `Some(fixers::flatten::SPEC)` |
| `manual` | `None`: the remediation is E6's `remediation_for` (E1's `remediation()` would otherwise prefer a `manual` builder) |
| title | an addon folder is nested inside another |
| description | An unmanaged folder in AddOns holds no TOC the client loads, and its one addon is a level down (Foo/Foo/, or a GitHub archive's Foo-main/Foo/), so the client never loads it. |
| why | A common mistake when unzipping by hand: the addon silently does nothing. The doctor can move it up, but only when asked by id, because the folder is yours. |
| E3's manual pair | `instruction`: move `<child>` up into AddOns and remove the emptied `<wrapper>`, with the game closed; `reason`: the doctor flattens a folder you put there only when you name its failure mode with --only |

### 2. The detector (`src/doctor/detectors/external/nested.rs`; `external.rs` declares `mod nested;`)

Per `KeyedClient` (registered, in scope), with its inventory and `addons_dir = target.addons_dir()`, over the entries `W` with `class == Unmanaged`, `!case_duplicate`, `!unreadable` and `toc == None`:

1. **List `W`** with `budget::list_dir(addons_dir.join(&W.name), budget)`. A truncated listing stops the detector with `incomplete`; an unreadable one skips `W` (the inventory read it as a folder; a listing error now is a race, and `W` is not reported).
2. **Find its addon children.** An entry is an addon child when it is a real directory (not a symlink), its name is a valid, non-protected `FolderName`, and `toc::loaded_toc(&DiskFolder::new(path)?, &target.rules)?` is `Some`. Each child checked charges one entry (`budget.charge(1)`).
3. **Exactly one addon child `Y`**, and its verdict `toc::judge(Y, Some(&loaded), &target.rules, target.family, target.interface, &world.table)` is `Compatible { .. }` (out of date or not). Decided while writing this bead: a wrong-flavor inner folder is not reported, because flattening it would not make it load.
4. **One of two shapes:**
   - `single`: `Y` is `W`'s only entry (the plan's "`X/` with no TOC whose single child `Y/` holds `Y.toc`"; `W/W/` is this shape too);
   - `archive`: `W`'s key is `<Y key>-main` or `<Y key>-master` (a GitHub branch archive, the plan's "`X-main/X/`"), `W` holds at least one entry besides `Y`, and every other entry of `W` is anything but an addon child (README, LICENSE, `.github/`, `docs/`). A wrapper whose only entry is `Y` is `single`, whatever its name (so `Foo-main/` holding only `Foo/` is `single`).
   Decided while writing this bead: the archive shape keeps the repository files that sit beside the addon in the commonest case, which a strict single-child rule would miss; a wrapper with a second addon child (a multi-addon repository) is never reported, because flattening one of them would be a guess.
5. **`Y`'s key equals no other `AddOns` entry's key** but `W`'s own. Decided while writing this bead: a nested copy whose name is already at the top level is not this failure mode (the top-level folder is what the client loads; the wrapper is clutter), and the rule guarantees the flatten never creates a case pair, which on a case-sensitive filesystem `RENAME_NOREPLACE` would allow (`AddOns/Foo` beside `AddOns/foo`) and Wine would see as one folder. It is also why the fixer needs no refusal of its own for an existing destination (§3).
6. **The observation:** subject `Subject::target(id, key).folder(<W's FolderName>)` (instance `…@<key>:folder=<W key>`, label `<id>/<W>`); `folder` = `W`'s name; `addon` `null`; evidence `{path: <addons dir>/<W>, child: <Y>, toc: <the loaded TOC's file name>, shape: "single" | "archive"}`; confidence medium. Title "`<Y>` is inside `<W>`, where the client does not load it".
7. `budget.check()` before each client; sorted output (E2 sorts findings).

**Never reported:** a managed, shared, linked, protected or invalid entry; a case-duplicate wrapper; a wrapper whose own TOC the client loads; an inner folder that is a symlink, has no TOC the client loads, or is wrong-flavor; a wrapper with two addon children; an inner key already at the top level; anything on an unregistered client.

**Evidence keys added** (`src/doctor/finding.rs`, E1's `Evidence`; each `Option`, omitted when `None`, documented optional):

| Key | Type | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `child` | string | the inner addon folder's name (if E6's test fixer already added `child`, reuse it) |
| `toc` | string | the TOC file the client would load from the inner folder (`Foo.toc`, `Foo_Mainline.toc`) |
| `shape` | `"single" \| "archive"` | which nested shape |

`path` (existing) is the wrapper's absolute path, under `Interface/AddOns`: `Evidence::is_private_safe` holds.

Example:

```json
{"id":"fm-external_artifacts-nested-addon-folder","instance":"fm-external_artifacts-nested-addon-folder@01M5ZQ7Y3KJ8V9W2X4C6B0N1RT:folder=foo-main",
 "label":"retail/Foo-main","severity":"P3","subsystem":"external_artifacts","title":"Foo is inside Foo-main, where the client does not load it",
 "confidence":"medium","target":{"id":"retail","key":"01M5ZQ7Y3KJ8V9W2X4C6B0N1RT"},"addon":null,"folder":"Foo-main",
 "evidence":{"path":"<client dir>/Interface/AddOns/Foo-main","child":"Foo","toc":"Foo.toc","shape":"archive"},
 "remediation":{"command":"omaddons doctor fix --only fm-external_artifacts-nested-addon-folder -t retail",
   "argv":["omaddons","doctor","fix","--only","fm-external_artifacts-nested-addon-folder","-t","retail"],
   "explain_command":"omaddons doctor explain fm-external_artifacts-nested-addon-folder -t retail","explain_argv":["…"],
   "auto_fixable":false,"needs_force":false,"estimated_actions":2,"destructive":false}}
```

### 3. The fixer (`src/doctor/fixers/flatten.rs`)

`src/doctor/fixers/mod.rs` gains `pub mod flatten;` (created, with `src/doctor/mod.rs`'s `pub mod fixers;`, if no fixer leaf has created it yet).

```rust
pub const SPEC: FixerSpec = FixerSpec {
    plan,
    writes_to: &[ScopeName::AddOns, ScopeName::ClientMeta],   // the moved folder; the quarantined wrapper
    ops: &[FixKind::Flatten],
    enabled: false,                                            // M4-D39: runs only with --only <this id>
    needs_force: false,
    cardinality: Cardinality::Low,
    preconditions: &[FixerPrecondition::LockHeld, FixerPrecondition::ClientNotRunning, FixerPrecondition::SameFs],
};

/// The flatten of one nested folder: `Fix::Flatten { inner: <W>/<Y>, outer: <W> }`, from
/// the finding's `evidence.path` (W) and `evidence.child` (Y).
fn plan(view: &DoctorView, finding: &Finding) -> Result<Vec<Fix>, Refusal>;
```

- **What the plan relies on.** E6 calls it with a finding of its fresh, under-lock detection (M4-D45), so the shape still holds when it plans. The detector always sets `path` and `child` (a unit test holds this); the plan returns `Ok(vec![])` if either is missing, which would leave the finding to verification. Decided while writing this bead: the plan adds no `Refusal` of its own, because every way a flatten can be unsafe is refused by the machinery it runs in, and M4-D40's closed set of `doctor_refused` reasons has none for an existing destination:
  - the client runs, or its state is unknown → E6's `ClientNotRunning`: `doctor_refused`, `client_running`, nothing moved (M4-D39's "refuses while the client runs");
  - the destination exists → E5's lowering: `file_exists` before anything is written (M4-D39's "refuses when the destination name exists"); a case-only twin is never reported (§2 rule 5);
  - a protected name, a path outside the client's scope or under `WTF/`, a mount crossing → E5's lowering refusals;
  - the wrapper or child changed after planning → E5's endpoint predicates fail that rename, and the repair rolls back.
- **What it does, through E5:** two renames (`<A>/W/Y → <A>/Y`; `<A>/W → <meta>/snapshots/<tx>.repair/quarantine/Interface/AddOns/W`), or three when `Y` is named like `W`. The wrapper, with any README or LICENSE beside the addon, is kept in quarantine until `doctor gc` (M4-D36), and E7's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7`, undo of repairs) generic inverse of `repairs[]` puts everything back; this part writes no undo code.
- **How it is reached** (E6's rules): `doctor fix` lists the finding as disabled and moves nothing; `doctor fix --only external_artifacts` moves nothing; `doctor fix --only fm-external_artifacts-nested-addon-folder [-t <id>] [--dry-run | --if-match <token>]` plans and runs it, then verifies by re-running this row's detector. Its remediation: `omaddons doctor fix --only fm-external_artifacts-nested-addon-folder -t <id>`, `auto_fixable: false`, `needs_force: false`, `estimated_actions` 2 or 3. The E1 invariant (a `needs_force` fixer is never `enabled`) holds; a disabled, unforced fixer is valid.
- **What it never does:** move a managed, linked, protected or shared folder (only row 36's findings reach it); write `WTF/`; run while the client runs; delete anything.

### 4. README (common rules 11 and 19)

- The doctor's failure-mode table: row 36 (P3, `default`, "an addon folder nested inside another, so the client never loads it", remediation "`omaddons doctor fix --only fm-external_artifacts-nested-addon-folder -t <id>` (off by default)").
- `### doctor`: one sentence: "One fixer touches a folder you put in AddOns: the flatten of a nested addon folder. It is off by default and runs only with `--only fm-external_artifacts-nested-addon-folder`, never while the game runs; the wrapper it empties is kept in the client's `.omaddons/snapshots/<tx>.repair/quarantine/`."
- **Troubleshooting**, a new entry "An addon unzipped by hand does not load": the two shapes (`AddOns/Foo/Foo/` and `AddOns/Foo-main/Foo/`); `omaddons doctor` reports `fm-external_artifacts-nested-addon-folder`; `omaddons doctor fix --only fm-external_artifacts-nested-addon-folder -t <client> --dry-run` shows the two or three moves and a token; the same with `--if-match <token>` (or without `--dry-run`) does them; the moved wrapper stays in quarantine. Add "`omaddons doctor undo` reverses it" only if E7's `doctor undo` exists on `main` when this lands (otherwise E7's README pass covers repair undo).

### 5. Snapshots and registries

- If E4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4`, `doctor capabilities`) has landed, its `fixers[]` gains `{id: "fm-external_artifacts-nested-addon-folder", preconditions: ["lock_held","client_not_running","same_fs"], writes_to: ["addons","client_meta"], ops: ["flatten"], reversible: true, idempotent: true, cardinality: "low", enabled: false, needs_force: false, estimated_cost_ms: 30}`; re-accept its snapshot and add an assertion that this fixer is listed `enabled: false` (whichever of E4 and this part lands second adds it).
- A4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`) and B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`) as in part 1.

### 6. Files

`src/doctor/registry.rs`, `src/doctor/detectors/external.rs` (`mod nested;`), `src/doctor/detectors/external/nested.rs` (new), `src/doctor/fixers/flatten.rs` (new) and `src/doctor/fixers/mod.rs`, `src/doctor/finding.rs`, README.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Row 36 is in `FAILURE_MODES` with Technical Approach §1's fields, `fix: Some(flatten::SPEC)` and `manual: None`, and `invariant_violations` finds nothing.
- [ ] The detector reports the `single` and `archive` shapes with `path`, `child`, `toc`, `shape`, instance `…:folder=<wrapper key>` and confidence medium, and never any shape of §2's "never reported" list (each a unit case).
- [ ] `flatten::SPEC` is `enabled: false`, `needs_force: false`, `writes_to: [AddOns, ClientMeta]`, `ops: [Flatten]`, `preconditions: [LockHeld, ClientNotRunning, SameFs]`; `plan` returns one `Fix::Flatten { inner: <W>/<Y>, outer: <W> }`; E6's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`) `remediation_for` gives the `--only` argv with `estimated_actions` 2 or 3.
- [ ] Every evidence object passes `Evidence::is_private_safe`.
- [ ] README's doctor table, `### doctor` and Troubleshooting describe the row and the disabled flatten; the snapshots of E4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4`), A4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`) and B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`) are re-accepted or regenerated where they exist.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes and `ubs` is clean on the changed files; the close comment lists the id, `child`, `toc`, `shape` and its values, the fixer's capabilities entry, that the fixer path binds through `doctor fix`'s token (common rule 16), and the "decided" items of this part.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

- **`src/doctor/detectors/external/nested.rs`**, tempdir clients built with `crate::engine::testing::target(dir)` and inventories from `inventory::inventory(target, record, &RulesTable::builtin(), Depth::Full)`, TOCs at the target's interface unless the case says otherwise; one name per case; each assertion prints the tempdir tree (a sorted listing of names and kinds, built in the test module) and the observations:
  - reported: `single_child` (`Wrap/Foo/Foo.toc`: `shape: single`, `child: Foo`, `toc: Foo.toc`); `same_name_child` (`Foo/Foo/Foo.toc`); `case_twin_child` (`Foo/foo/foo.toc`: the wrapper's own key is allowed); `archive_main_with_readme` (`Foo-main/{Foo/Foo.toc, README.md, LICENSE}`: `shape: archive`); `archive_master_with_dotgithub` (`Foo-master/{Foo/, .github/workflows/x.yml}`); `main_named_with_only_the_child_is_single` (`Foo-main/Foo/` alone: `shape: single`); `suffixed_toc` (`Wrap/Foo/Foo_Mainline.toc`: `toc: Foo_Mainline.toc`); `out_of_date_inner_is_reported`.
  - not reported: `two_addon_children`; `archive_with_a_second_addon`; `wrapper_with_its_own_toc`; `inner_without_a_toc`; `inner_toc_named_otherwise` (`Wrap/Foo/Bar.toc`); `wrong_flavor_inner`; `inner_name_already_at_top_level` (`Foo-main/Foo` beside `Foo`); `inner_case_twin_at_top_level` (beside `foo`); `managed_wrapper`; `linked_wrapper`; `protected_inner` (`Wrap/Blizzard_X/…`); `symlinked_child`; `case_duplicate_wrapper`; `single_shape_with_a_stray_file` (`Wrap/{Foo/, notes.txt}` without the archive name: not `single`, not `archive`); `empty_wrapper`.
  - `budget_cut_is_incomplete` (a 1-entry budget over two wrappers: at most one observation, `incomplete: Some(entries)`); `detector_sets_path_and_child_always` (every reported case has both); `every_case_is_private_safe`.
- **`src/doctor/fixers/flatten.rs`**: `plan_returns_one_flatten` (inner and outer from a finding built by the detector over `Foo-main/Foo`); `plan_without_child_plans_nothing`; `spec_is_disabled_and_unforced`; `spec_preconditions_and_scopes` (each `ScopeName::scope()` admits `Writer::Doctor`, invariant 9 of E1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`); `primitive_count_two_and_three` (the `Fix::primitive_count` of E6, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`, over `Foo-main/Foo` → 2 and `Foo/Foo` → 3).
- **`src/doctor/registry.rs`**: `the_nested_row_matches_appendix_b` (id, P3, `Default`, `requires`, fixer present and disabled, `manual: None`, manual pair naming no runnable command).

### Integration and end-to-end tests

None in this part. Part 5 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.5.5) runs the fixer through the real binary: only by id, the two- and three-rename cases, the result loading, a second run taking 0 actions, the refusal while the client runs, a preview that goes stale, and the case-pair guarantee.

### Logging

Unit tests only: one name per case; each failure message names the case and prints the tempdir tree (names, kinds, TOC file names), the inventory entries and the observation or `Fix` as JSON.

## Considerations

- **Risk 3, doctor false positives (M, M).** The detector reports only unambiguous shapes whose inner folder would load where the flatten puts it; P3, so `--severity P2` hides it. A user who keeps a disabled addon inside a `_disabled/` wrapper on purpose gets a P3 report and nothing moves unless they ask by id.
- **The fixer's blast radius.** Two or three renames inside one client's `Interface/AddOns` and `<meta>`; F9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`) checks that every `actions.jsonl` path is inside `writes_to`, crashes the repair at each rename, and round-trips undo.
- **For F9's declared pair `nested-addon-folder + case-collision`:** a flatten never creates a case pair (§2 rule 5), and `case-collision` has no fixer, so a planted case pair remains after a fix of the pair.
- **Hot spots.** `src/doctor/fixers/` (F2 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.2`, F3 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.3`, F7 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.7` and F10 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.10` add theirs): add `flatten.rs` and one `pub mod` line; `src/doctor/registry.rs` and `src/doctor/finding.rs`: insert and append, rebase. README: the doctor table, one `### doctor` sentence, one Troubleshooting entry.
- **Compatibility.** Additive: one id, three evidence keys, one disabled fixer.

## Dependencies

- **Parent:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.5.
- **Before it:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.5.1 (`keyed_clients` and the subsystem's conventions).
- **Beside it:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.5.2 and omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.5.3 (different files).
- **After it:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.5.5, which builds the fixture (`fixer() == true`) and runs the flatten end to end.

From E5's lowering (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5.2`, closed), two points where the lowering of `Fix::Flatten` is more precise than this bead's Technical Approach states:

- **"`Y = X`" is equality ignoring ASCII case.** A wrapper whose inner folder carries its name in another case (`Foo/foo`) lowers to the three renames through `<A>/.omaddons-flatten-<tx>`, and the lifted folder keeps the inner folder's own spelling (`<A>/foo`). The fixer's fixtures for the case pair should expect that.
