title: Tests: the nine external-artifacts fixtures and their end-to-end suite
description:
Part 5 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.5 (External artifacts). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

**The leaf.** F5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.5`) builds the doctor's `external_artifacts` subsystem: Appendix B rows 28–36 (the doctor's catalog, filed on the milestone epic `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`), the failure modes of what sits in a client's `Interface/AddOns` and in its client-side snapshots. Parts 1–4 built the rows, the bounded deep drift check and the disabled flatten fixer, each with unit tests:

| # | Id (`fm-external_artifacts-…`) | P | Tier | Remediation | Built in |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 28 | `managed-files-modified` (published) | P2 | quick; re-hash under `--include-deep` | `omaddons install <addon> -t <id> --reinstall` | E1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`) and E2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.2`), bounded and deep in omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.5.3 |
| 29 | `ownership-transferred` (published) | P2 | cached | `omaddons list -t <id> -v` | E1 and E2, kept by omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.5.3 |
| 30 | `ownership-conflict` | P1 | default | advice | omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.5.1 |
| 31 | `case-collision` | P2 | default | advice | omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.5.1 |
| 32 | `wrong-flavor` | P2 | default | `omaddons update <addon> -t <id>` | omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.5.1 |
| 33 | `out-of-date-toc` | P3 | default | `omaddons update <addon> -t <id>` | omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.5.1 |
| 34 | `missing-dependency` | P2 | default | `omaddons install <ref> -t <id>`, or `omaddons search <folder> -t <id>` | omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.5.2 |
| 35 | `orphan-snapshot-only-copy` | P2 | default | advice naming the path | omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.5.2 |
| 36 | `nested-addon-folder` | P3 | default | `omaddons doctor fix --only fm-external_artifacts-nested-addon-folder -t <id>` (fixer `enabled: false`) | omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.5.4 |

**This part** proves the leaf end to end through the real binary. It builds the nine fixtures M4-D47 requires ("each failure mode has a fixture: a Rust type implementing `Fixture` in `tests/doctor/fixtures/<fm_id>.rs`, with `corrupt` deterministic and built on the `tests/common/` builders, `assert_healthy`, `subject`, and a doc comment that is the fixture's README"; rejected: `corrupt.sh`/`assert.sh` scripts), their planting helpers, and the suite `tests/doctor_external.rs`, whose scenarios are the leaf's acceptance: every row's true positive, no false positive on the realistic home, the deep check, the budget cut, the flatten only by id and its result loading, its refusal while the client runs, its binding preview, its case-pair guarantee, the catalog-only dependency check, the remediations running, rows 28 and 29 agreeing with `status`, and purity, repeatability and privacy. The fixtures are reused by F9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`, the safety harness: true positive, no false positive, repeatability, purity for every row; reversibility, idempotence, crash recovery and concurrency for the flatten) and by T4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4`, the slice-3 demo). It is its own step because these scenarios need every part in place.

**The decisions this part checks** (full text in the decision-log comments on the milestone epic):

- **M4-D39:** the flatten fixer is `enabled: false`; `doctor fix` without `--only` lists it and does not run it; only `--only fm-external_artifacts-nested-addon-folder` runs it; it refuses while the client runs and when the destination exists.
- **M4-D29:** rows 28 (`quick`) and 29 (`cached`) reach `status`; rows 30–36 (`default`) never do. **§3.2 criterion 12:** "for every fixture, the issue ids `status` reports equal the doctor findings of those tiers".
- **M4-D43:** a check cut short by its budget is `check-incomplete`, never a pass.
- **M4-D44, M4-D45 (E6's, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`):** a `doctor fix --dry-run` token binds; a change in between is `plan_stale` and moves nothing.
- **M4-D42 and common rule 9:** no output on any channel names an account, realm or character; evidence never holds content.
- **The plan's consideration for row 34:** "uses the catalog only, since a diagnosis makes no request without `--online`".
- **§3.2 criterion 9:** "bare `doctor` changes nothing outside `<state>/doctor/`" (tree hashes of `<state>`, `<cache>`, `<config>` and every client dir); "detectors are repeatable"; "every detector has a fixture that triggers it and a clean home that does not".

**What exists to build on** (verified at `c0ab5e9`, plus the leaf's blockers and the leaves around it):

- T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs): `tests/common/tlog.rs` (`tlog!()`, `log.step`, `log.case`, `log.note`, `log.json`, `log.run(&home, argv) -> Ran` through `Home::std_command`, which sets `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES` and, when `home.proc` is set, `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT`; `log.cmd(&home, argv).env(k, v).failpoints(spec)`; `log.tree(label, root)`, `log.assert_unchanged(label, root)`; `Ran::{ok, exit, fails, envelope, error_code, warnings, commands, assert_private}`; `Ran::data()` needs a `data` key, which a doctor envelope lacks: use `envelope()`). A suite carries the crate-doc marker `//! e2e suite: <purpose>`, which `argc e2e` reads.
- E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`): `tests/doctor/mod.rs` with the `Fixture` trait (`id()`, `corrupt(&Home)`, `assert_healthy(&Home)`, `subject(&Home) -> Vec<PathBuf>`, `fixer() -> bool` default `false`, `run_env()`, `run_args()`; extended only additively; included as `#[path = "doctor/mod.rs"] mod fixtures;`), `tests/doctor/fixtures/mod.rs` with `pub fn all() -> Vec<Box<dyn Fixture>>`, `tests/common/doctor.rs` with `check_envelope(stdout, stderr, code)` and `plant::{managed_files_modified(home, target, addon), ownership_transferred(home, target), restore_file(home, target, addon, rel), runs, latest, …}`, and the failpoint `doctor.detector.panic=sleep:<ms>`. F1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1`) adds the defaulted `fn remedy(&self, home: &Home) {}` to the trait; if F1 has not landed, add it here, additively, with the same doc comment.
- E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`): `doctor fix [--only] [-t] [--dry-run] [--if-match]`; its report keys (`state`, `actions_planned` under `--dry-run` with `<run>`/`<tx>` placeholders, `precondition`, `summary.actions_taken`, the disabled findings listed, not run); `doctor_refused` with `details.reason: client_running`; `plan_stale` (exit 4, `retryable: false`).
- `tests/common/`: `Home::new(&[…])` (`home.rs`; `home.addons("_retail_")`, `home.client(..)`, `home.state()`, `home.retail_running()` for a fake running retail client, `home.nothing_running()`), `common::graph::{release_graph, Node, Folder}` (one GitHub release per node over the HTTP fixtures, TOCs with `## Dependencies`, `tests/common/graph.rs:30-50`), `common::http::{gh_release_v, gh_latest}`, `common::addons::{addon_folder, toc}`, `common::archives::zip_text`, `common::engine::Scene::install_args` (an `install <ref> --file <zip> -t retail --offline` argv), `common::state::{record, key_of, files_index}`, `common::trees::tree_hash` (modes and symlink targets included), `common::wtf::Wtf` (`WTF/` trees for the fake `FAKEACCT`/`FakeRealm`/`FakeChar`), `common::privacy::assert_private_all`. Planting by hand follows `tests/adopt_hints.rs:35-66` (a `catalog.d` entry and an HTTP release graph) and `common::engine::Scene::age_orphan_snapshots` (`tests/common/engine.rs:105-110`: `File::open(dir).set_modified(two hours ago)`).
- `common::realistic_home()`: lifted by D8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8`, its fifth part) in `tests/common/realistic.rs`: three clients, 30 records, 5,040 managed files, installed from local archives. It does not exist at `c0ab5e9`.
- The retail test client's interface is 120105 (12.1.5), with retail 12's floor at 120000; a TOC at `120000` loads out of date, one at `110207` is below the floor (`wrong_flavor`, `below_client_floor`), as `tests/install.rs:2406-2445` shows.

## Technical Approach

Leaves this section names: E1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`, the registry), E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, the doctor runtime and its test helpers), D8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8`, which lifts `common::realistic_home()`), F1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1`), F3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.3`) and F4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.4`), the other catalog leaves, and F9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`, the safety harness).

### 1. The planting helpers (`tests/common/doctor.rs::plant`)

Each is deterministic, documented (what it breaks, the finding's id, severity, instance and evidence) and works through the real binary or plain edits of files the binary wrote (test code may use `std::fs`; only `src/` must go through fsx). `<A>` is retail's `Interface/AddOns`; `<root>/aside/` is a directory under the `Home`'s root, outside every scanned or state directory.

| Helper | Recipe |
|---|---|
| `ownership_conflict(home, target)` | install `Foo` and `Bar` from local archives (`Scene::install_args`-style argv); read `<state>/omaddons/targets/<key>.json`, add `"Foo"` to `Bar`'s `folders`, write it back; return the original bytes |
| `case_collision(home, target)` | install `Foo`; create `<A>/foo/` with one file `x.lua` |
| `wrong_flavor(home, target)` | install `Foo` (TOC at 120105); rewrite `<A>/Foo/Foo.toc`'s `## Interface:` line to `110207`; return the original bytes |
| `out_of_date_toc(home, target)` | serve `gh:o/old` v1 with a TOC at `120000` (`gh_release_v` + `gh_latest`); `install gh:o/old -t retail` (exit 0, an `out_of_date` warning) |
| `missing_dependency(home, target)` | write `<config>/omaddons/catalog.d/50-testlib.toml` (`name = "TestLib"`, `ref = "gh:o/testlib"`, `folders = ["TestLib"]`, `families = ["mainline"]`); `release_graph` with `gh:o/foo` (folder `Foo`, `deps: ["TestLib"]`) and `gh:o/testlib` (folder `TestLib`); `install gh:o/foo -t retail --no-deps` |
| `orphan_snapshot(home, target) -> String` | install any addon (registration and `<meta>`); create `<client dir>/Interface/.omaddons/snapshots/<fresh ULID>/AddOns/Foo/Foo.toc` and `Foo/core.lua`; age the snapshot directory two hours; return the ULID |
| `nested(home, target, wrapper, inner, extra: &[&str])` | install any addon (registration); create `<A>/<wrapper>/<inner>/<inner>.toc` (TOC at 120105) and `<inner>/core.lua`, plus each `extra` file at `<A>/<wrapper>/<extra>` |

Order constraints, documented on each helper as E3's are: `wrong_flavor` edits a managed TOC, so a later change on that addon would repair it; `ownership_conflict` edits a record, so plant it after every change on that client.

### 2. The nine fixtures (`tests/doctor/fixtures/fm_external_artifacts_<slug>.rs`)

One file per row (a module name cannot hold a hyphen), each a `pub struct` implementing `Fixture`, added to `fixtures/mod.rs`'s `all()`. Each targets `retail` on a `Home::new(&["wow", "wow_classic"])`, so they compose in one home. What a fixture keeps for `remedy` (original bytes, the ULID) lives in interior state (`RefCell`), since the trait takes `&self`. The doc comment of each is its README: what breaks, how `corrupt` builds it, the finding (id, severity, instance, evidence), and the remedy.

| Row | `corrupt` | Expected finding | `remedy` | `fixer()` | `subject` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 28 | E3's `plant::managed_files_modified(home, "retail", "Foo")` | `…@<key>:addon=foo`, `count ≥ 1`, `drift_mode: stat` | `install Foo -t retail --reinstall` | false | `<A>/Foo` |
| 29 | E3's `plant::ownership_transferred(home, "retail")` | `…@<key>`, `count: 1` | `remove <the degraded addon> -t retail` | false | the two addons' folders |
| 30 | `plant::ownership_conflict` | `…:folder=foo`, `owners: ["Bar","Foo"]`, `path: <A>/Foo` | write the saved record back | false | the record file |
| 31 | `plant::case_collision` | `…:folder=foo`, `paths: [<A>/Foo, <A>/foo]`, `count: 2` | move `<A>/foo` into `<root>/aside/` | false | `<A>` |
| 32 | `plant::wrong_flavor` | `…:addon=foo`, `folders: [{name: Foo, toc: Foo.toc, reason: below_client_floor, interfaces: [110207], floor: 120000}]`, `expected: "120105"` | write the saved TOC back | false | `<A>/Foo` |
| 33 | `plant::out_of_date_toc` | `…:addon=old`, `folders: [{name: Old, toc: Old.toc, interfaces: [120000]}]`, `expected: "120105"` | serve `gh:o/old` v2 at 120105, then `update Old -t retail` | false | `<A>/Old` |
| 34 | `plant::missing_dependency` | `…:folder=testlib`, `required_by: ["Foo"]`, `candidate: "gh:o/testlib"` | run the finding's remediation argv | false | `<A>` |
| 35 | `plant::orphan_snapshot` | `…:tx=<ULID>`, `kept_folders: ["Foo"]`, `wtf_previous: false`, `count: 1` | move the snapshot directory into `<root>/aside/` | false | `<client dir>/Interface/.omaddons/snapshots` |
| 36 | `plant::nested(home, "retail", "Foo-main", "Foo", &["README.md"])` | `…:folder=foo-main`, `child: Foo`, `toc: Foo.toc`, `shape: archive` | none (a fixer row): the fix is `doctor fix --only fm-external_artifacts-nested-addon-folder -t retail` | **true** | `<A>` |

- `assert_healthy`: `doctor --json --only <id>` reports no finding of the id. Row 36 also asserts `<A>/Foo/Foo.toc` exists, `<A>/Foo-main` does not, and `list -t retail --unmanaged --json` gives `Foo` the verdict `compatible` (its result loads).
- `run_env` and `run_args`: none (row 28's deep case is a scenario, not the fixture).
- `subject` for row 36 is the whole `<A>`, so F9's reversibility property compares exactly what the flatten touched besides the repair's own quarantine root.

### 3. The realistic home

Use `common::realistic_home()` if it is on `main`. Otherwise lift it here as D8's bead describes (`tests/common/realistic.rs`: `Home::at(dir, ..)` with three clients and 30 `install` runs from local archives under `gh:` refs, then an assertion of 30 records and 5,040 managed files) and say so in the close comment; D8 reuses it. Its TOCs must carry each client's own interface (a healthy realistic home has no out-of-date or wrong-flavor addon and no missing requirement); if the builder makes them otherwise, change the builder and record why (decided while writing this bead: the no-false-positive property is about a healthy home).

### 4. The suite (`tests/doctor_external.rs`, new)

First line `//! e2e suite: the external-artifacts detectors and the flatten fixer`. It includes the fixtures with `#[path = "doctor/mod.rs"] mod fixtures;`. Decided while writing this bead: a suite of its own rather than more scenarios in E3's `tests/doctor.rs`, which F1, F3 and F4 also extend. Every scenario is a `TestLog` scenario on its own `Home`, passes `--json` explicitly, and checks each doctor envelope with `check_envelope`:

1. **`every_external_fixture_is_found_and_cleared`**: one `log.case(<id>)` per fixture of the nine, each on a fresh `Home`. "plant": `corrupt`. "doctor --only": `doctor --json --only <id>` → exit 1, `state: DONE_FINDINGS`, exactly one finding, of that id, at its severity, its instance and evidence as §2's table says. "doctor": `doctor --json` → the id is present (for row 28: `doctor --json` runs `quick` rows too). "remedy": `remedy`, or for row 36 `doctor fix --json --only fm-external_artifacts-nested-addon-folder -t retail` → exit 0, `DONE_OK`. "healthy": `assert_healthy`.
2. **`no_external_detector_fires_on_the_realistic_home`**: "doctor deep": `doctor --json --include-deep --only <the nine ids, comma-separated>` → exit 0, `findings: []`, `summary.incomplete: 0`, `skipped: []`. "doctor quick": `doctor --quick --json` → no finding of rows 28 or 29, no `check-incomplete`. `log.json("summary", …)` of each.
3. **`a_kept_mtime_same_size_edit_is_found_only_by_the_deep_check`**: install Foo (local archive); record `Foo/core.lua`'s mtime; rewrite it with other bytes of the same length; set its mtime back. `doctor --json --only fm-external_artifacts-managed-files-modified` → exit 0, no finding. `doctor --json --include-deep --only …` → exit 1, one finding, `drift_mode: deep`, `count: 1`. `doctor explain fm-external_artifacts-managed-files-modified -t retail --json` → exit 0, `instances` holding that finding's instance. `status --json` → no `managed-files-modified` issue (status compares sizes and times; `log.note` says so). Then a plain edit (a different size): every one of the four finds it, `status` included, with one instance key across `doctor` and `doctor --include-deep`.
4. **`the_drift_check_stops_at_its_budget`**: install three addons; `doctor --json --only fm-external_artifacts-managed-files-modified --budget 1ms` with `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS=doctor.detector.panic=sleep:50` → exit 1, `DONE_FINDINGS` (never `DONE_OK`), one `fm-state_files-check-incomplete` naming row 28 with `limit: deadline`.
5. **`the_flatten_runs_only_by_id_and_its_result_loads`**: `plant::nested(…, "Foo-main", "Foo", &["README.md"])` and `plant::nested(…, "Bar", "Bar", &[])`. `log.tree("addons", <A>)`.
   - "default fix": `doctor fix --json` → no action for these findings (listed as disabled), `log.assert_unchanged("addons", <A>)`.
   - "subsystem fix": `doctor fix --json --only external_artifacts` → nothing moved (`assert_unchanged`).
   - "preview": `doctor fix --json --only fm-external_artifacts-nested-addon-folder -t retail --dry-run` → exit 1, `actions_planned` of five `rename_noreplace` steps (two for `Foo-main`, three for `Bar`, the provisional `.omaddons-flatten-<tx>` and the quarantine paths written with `<tx>`/`<run>`), a `precondition`; `assert_unchanged`.
   - "fix": the same with `--if-match <token>` instead of `--dry-run` → exit 0, `state: DONE_OK`, `summary.actions_taken: 5`, a `tx`. `<A>/Foo/Foo.toc` and `<A>/Bar/Bar.toc` exist; `<A>/Foo-main` and no `<A>/.omaddons-flatten-*` remain; `<client dir>/Interface/.omaddons/snapshots/<tx>.repair/quarantine/Interface/AddOns/Foo-main/README.md` and `…/quarantine/Interface/AddOns/Bar` exist; `log.tree("quarantine", …)`.
   - "loads": `list -t retail --unmanaged --json` → `Foo` and `Bar` with verdict `compatible`; `doctor --json --only fm-external_artifacts-nested-addon-folder` → exit 0.
   - "idempotent": `doctor fix --json --only fm-external_artifacts-nested-addon-folder -t retail` → exit 0, `actions_taken: 0`.
   - "history": `history --json` → one line of `kind: repair` naming the run.
6. **`the_flatten_is_refused_while_the_client_runs`**: plant `Foo-main/Foo`; `home.retail_running()`; `doctor fix --json --only fm-external_artifacts-nested-addon-folder -t retail` → exit 4, `state: REFUSING`, `error.code: doctor_refused`, `error.details.reason: client_running`, `error.details.fm` = the id; `<A>` unchanged; no `<state>/omaddons/journal/*.repair.jsonl`. Then `home.nothing_running()` and the same command → exit 0.
7. **`a_flatten_preview_binds`**: plant `Foo-main/Foo`; `--dry-run` → token; add `<A>/Foo-main/Foo/new.lua`; `doctor fix --json --only … -t retail --if-match <token>` → exit 4, `error.code: plan_stale`, `retryable: false`; `<A>` equal to the tree after the added file (nothing moved).
8. **`a_flatten_never_creates_a_case_pair`**: plant `Foo-main/Foo` and an unmanaged `<A>/foo/` (with a TOC): `doctor --json --only fm-external_artifacts-nested-addon-folder` → exit 0 (not reported); `doctor fix --json --only … -t retail` → exit 0, `actions_taken: 0`, `<A>` unchanged. Then a case pair `<A>/Baz`, `<A>/baz` and `plant::nested(…, "Qux-main", "Qux", &[])`: `doctor fix --json --only fm-external_artifacts-nested-addon-folder,fm-external_artifacts-case-collision -t retail` → exit 0, `Qux` flattened, `Baz`/`baz` untouched; `doctor --json --only <both ids>` → exit 1, exactly one finding, the case pair's.
9. **`missing_dependency_reads_only_the_catalog`**: `release_graph` with `gh:o/foo` holding `Foo` (deps `TestLib`, `Blizzard_X`) and `Foo_Masque` (deps `Masque`), `gh:o/testlib`; the `catalog.d` entry for `TestLib`; an unmanaged `<A>/LibBar/` that `Foo` also requires; `install gh:o/foo -t retail --no-deps`. `doctor --json --only fm-external_artifacts-missing-dependency` → exactly one finding (`TestLib`, `candidate: gh:o/testlib`), none for `Masque` (a bridge's), `Blizzard_X` (the client's) or `LibBar` (present); `Ran`'s `net.log` lines for the diagnosis are empty. Run the finding's `remediation.argv` → exit 0; `doctor --json --only …` → exit 0.
10. **`the_remediations_run`**: for each fixture with an argv remediation (rows 28, 29, 32, 33, 34): plant, diagnose, run `remediation.argv` (without its leading `omaddons`, plus `--json`) → exit 0 (row 33's after serving v2). For rows 30, 31 and 35: `remediation.argv` is `null` and `remediation.command` names no runnable omaddons command (the rule of `names_a_command`, `tests/contract/main.rs`). Every finding's `explain_argv` runs → exit 0.
11. **`the_published_rows_agree_with_status`**: plant rows 28 and 29 on one home. `status --json` → issue ids for retail exactly `{managed-files-modified, ownership-transferred}`, each title equal to the doctor finding's title; `status --cached --json` → only `ownership-transferred`; `doctor --quick --json` → findings of exactly those two ids. E1's characterization snapshots and `tests/e2e_status_issues.rs` pass unchanged (run as part of the gate).
12. **`external_findings_are_repeatable_pure_and_private`**: every fixture's `corrupt` on one home (they compose), plus a `Wtf::at(<client dir>)` tree with the fake names. "trees": `log.tree` of `<state>` without `doctor/`, `<cache>`, `<config>` and each client dir. Two `doctor --json --include-deep --progress json` runs → equal `findings` after stripping the declared volatile keys; `log.assert_unchanged` on every tree; `Ran::assert_private` (`assert_private_all(stdout, stderr)`) on both runs; the newest `report.json` contains none of `FAKEACCT`, `FakeRealm`, `FakeChar`.
13. **`the_external_fixtures_are_registered`**: `fixtures::all()` holds exactly one fixture per `FAILURE_MODES` row whose id starts `fm-external_artifacts-`; `fixer()` is true exactly for row 36, whose registry row has a fixer.

### 5. Contract rows (`tests/contract/matrix.rs`)

- `doctor_diagnose_with_external_artifacts`: a home with rows 30, 34 and 36 planted; `doctor --json`; snapshotted and checked by `support::check`'s doctor mode (and, once A3 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3` has landed, validated against the report schema with the new evidence keys).
- `doctor_fix_dry_run_of_a_flatten`: `Foo-main/Foo` planted; `doctor fix --json --only fm-external_artifacts-nested-addon-folder -t retail --dry-run`; snapshotted (run ids and tx ids redacted by `support::stable()`).

### 6. Files

`tests/common/doctor.rs` (`plant::*`), `tests/doctor/mod.rs` (`remedy`, only if F1 has not added it), `tests/doctor/fixtures/fm_external_artifacts_*.rs` (nine) and `fixtures/mod.rs`, `tests/doctor_external.rs` (new), `tests/common/realistic.rs` (only if absent), `tests/contract/matrix.rs` and two snapshots.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The nine fixture files exist, each registered in `fixtures::all()` with a doc comment that is its README; `fixer()` is true only for row 36; `subject` as Technical Approach §2 says.
- [ ] `every_external_fixture_is_found_and_cleared` passes: each `corrupt` yields exactly its row's finding with §2's evidence, and its remedy (row 36: the fix) makes `assert_healthy` hold, row 36's result loading.
- [ ] `no_external_detector_fires_on_the_realistic_home` passes with `--include-deep` and with `--quick`, with no `check-incomplete`.
- [ ] Scenarios 3–13 pass: the deep-only edit, the budget cut, the flatten only by id (both shapes, five actions, quarantine paths, the result loading, idempotence), the refusal while running, the stale preview, the case-pair guarantee, the catalog-only dependency check with no `net.log` line, every remediation and explain argv running, rows 28 and 29 agreeing with `status`, repeatability, purity and privacy, and the fixture registry.
- [ ] The contract rows `doctor_diagnose_with_external_artifacts` and `doctor_fix_dry_run_of_a_flatten` are snapshotted and pass `support::check`.
- [ ] `argc e2e doctor_external` runs the suite with verbose logs.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files; the close comment lists the fixture files and the `plant` helpers (for F9 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9` and T4 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4`), and says whether `common::realistic_home()` was lifted here.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

None in `src/`; parts 1–4 carry them. Each planting helper is checked by its fixture's case in scenario 1: the planted state is the one the finding names, with the expected evidence values.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

The thirteen scenarios of §4 in `tests/doctor_external.rs` and the two contract rows of §5, through the real binary. Failpoints: `doctor.detector.panic=sleep:50` (scenario 4). Environment: `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES` (every `Home` command), `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT` (scenario 6, through `home.retail_running()`).

### Logging

- Every scenario opens `let log = tlog!();` and names its phases with `log.step` ("home", "plant <row>", "doctor --only", "doctor", "default fix", "subsystem fix", "preview", "fix", "loads", "idempotent", "remedy", "healthy", "trees"), so each command's argv, environment overrides, exit, envelope, stderr events, `net.log` lines and failpoints are in `steps.jsonl` and `transcript.md`.
- Per fixture: `log.case(<fm id>)`; `log.json("finding", …)` before asserting it; for the hand edits (the record, the TOC, the kept-mtime file), `log.note` of what changed (the key, the line, the size and mtime), never file content beyond the edited TOC line.
- Trees: `log.tree` before and `log.assert_unchanged` after each diagnosis and each refused or stale fix (the first differing paths are logged); for the flatten, `log.tree` of `<A>` and of the quarantine directory after the fix.
- A failing assertion prints the case, the expected and actual finding or tree, and the transcript path; the guard of T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`) prints the last 20 steps.

### Checkpoint-only

None owned here. H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`) runs E6's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`) `doctor_on_the_real_home` and reviews every finding of these rows (risk 3).

## Considerations

- **Fragility of the recipes.** Row 33's fixture depends on the retail test client's interface (120105) and floor (120000), and row 32's on the floor; if a rules change moves them, the fixtures' TOC values move with them (read the client's interface from `common::trees` where the builder exposes it, rather than repeating the number in several places).
- **Row 35's age.** The snapshot is aged by setting its directory's mtime two hours back, as `Scene::age_orphan_snapshots` does; the doctor's clock is the real one here (no `OMADDONS_NOW` needed).
- **Root.** No scenario depends on file modes (the mode-000 cases are part 2's unit tests, skipped as root there).
- **Privacy.** Scenario 12 plants a `WTF/` with the fake names only; no fixture writes under `WTF/`.
- **Time.** The suite installs from local archives and HTTP fixtures; keep each case's home small (one or two addons) so the suite stays fast, and reuse the realistic home within scenario 2 only.
- **Hot spots.** `tests/common/doctor.rs` and `tests/doctor/fixtures/mod.rs` are shared with E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`), F1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1`), F3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.3`), F4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.4`) and F9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`): append, then rebase. `tests/contract/matrix.rs`: append rows; one snapshot file per row.

## Dependencies

- **Parent:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.5.
- **Before it:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.5.2, omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.5.3 and omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.5.4 (and, through them, omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.5.1): every row, the deep check and the fixer must exist. It is blocked by T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`) at filing, because it writes a `TestLog` suite.
- **After it:** nothing in this leaf; it is the last subtask, and its closing agent verifies the leaf's acceptance criteria and closes omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.5.

title: Caches: verified blob reads and the blob detector
description:
## How to work this bead

This bead is worked through its 4 subtasks, listed below in work order. Claim a subtask, not this bead (`br ready --parent omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.6` lists the ready ones). The agent that closes the last open subtask then verifies every acceptance criterion of this bead (they are the leaf's, not any one subtask's), and closes this bead with `br close omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.6 --reason "done: <evidence> · found: <ids>"`. Until this bead is closed, every bead it blocks stays blocked.

1. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.6.1 Blob verification, and the `fm-caches-blob-hash-mismatch` detector and fixer: `engine::blobs::verify_blob` with its stamp-guarded memo, the registry row, `src/doctor/detectors/caches.rs`, the quarantine fixer, README's doctor table row, and their unit tests.
2. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.6.2 Verified blob reads: `BlobCache::get` re-hashes a blob before it hands it out; a damaged archive is a cache miss, downloaded again online and refused with `hash_mismatch` (`details.blob`) offline; the planner's conversion points, the `DetailSpec`, the meaning, README, and their unit tests. After s1.
3. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.6.3 E2E: the blob detector finds a damaged archive, quarantines it and stays quiet otherwise: the fixture F9 runs, `plant::damaged_blob`, `tests/doctor_caches.rs` and a contract row. After s1.
4. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.6.4 Tests: a damaged cached archive is never staged: `tests/blobs.rs` extended, a locked-sync case in `tests/sync.rs`, a contract row, the perf note and the real-machine step. After s2.

s2 and s3 both need only s1 and touch different files: they can be worked at the same time. s4 needs s2.

**Why s1 comes first.** s2's new error names the fix `omaddons doctor --include-deep`. That fix must find the damage from the first commit in which the error can appear, so the detector lands before the read path that points at it. Both use one verification function, which s1 adds.

**Size M, one closure.** The leaf is two small changes to existing code (the read path of the blob cache, and the planner's handling of a damaged archive) and one `deep` detector whose fixer is a single quarantine rename, all over machinery that E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, the doctor runtime), E5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`, the repair transaction) and E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`, `doctor fix`) already built. The subtasks split the work into commits that each pass the gate; the bead closes only when all four are done, so F9 and H1 never see half of it.

## Background

**The problem.** omaddons keeps every downloaded archive once, in a content-addressed cache: `<cache>/blobs/<sha256>`, where the file name is the SHA-256 of the archive's bytes, in 64 lowercase hex digits (`src/engine/blobs.rs:1-17`, `src/state/paths.rs:374-388`). The cache is what makes reinstalls, `sync --locked`, cross-client installs and a plan applied within its time to live work without downloading again. A download is hashed while it streams and checked against the hash the source publishes (`blobs.rs:513-553`), so a blob is right when it is written. Nothing checks it afterwards. `BlobCache::get` (`blobs.rs:307-326`) builds the path from the name, checks that a regular file is there, marks it used in `<cache>/blobs/index.json`, and returns it. It trusts the name. A blob damaged on disk later (a failing disk, a flipped bit, a truncation, a file another program overwrote) is then handed to planning as the archive its name promises. Depending on the damage, the install fails with a confusing archive error, or it installs bytes that are not the release's: a different, valid archive under the name installs whatever that archive holds. The engine's integrity promise, "a verified archive or nothing", should not depend on the disk.

**What this leaf does** (M4-D52):

1. **Every use re-hashes.** `BlobCache::get` checks a blob's SHA-256 against its name before handing it to staging. A mismatch counts as a cache miss. Online, the archive is downloaded again, verified, and written through fsx to the same content-addressed path: the cache heals itself, and nothing is deleted. Offline, or when the source no longer serves the archive, the command fails with `hash_mismatch`, raised as a first attempt so it says `retryable: true`, with `details.blob` (the damaged blob's name) and the fix `omaddons doctor --include-deep`. It changes nothing.
2. **A deep detector and its fixer.** The failure mode `fm-caches-blob-hash-mismatch` (P2, tier `deep`, subsystem `caches`; Appendix B row 37) hashes every blob against its name. Its fixer quarantines a damaged blob into `<cache>/quarantine/<run id>/blobs/`. A pinned blob (the archive an installed release came from) is quarantined too: its next reinstall downloads it again.

**Milestone goals it serves:**

- **G-M4-4, diagnosable and repairable:** "`omaddons doctor` names every broken state omaddons can detect in what it owns or manages", and "every auto-fixable state is repaired by one consented command that backs up verbatim, never deletes, and is proven by a fixture that round-trips". The damaged blob gets a finding with evidence, a consented, undoable quarantine (a rename, never a deletion), and a fixture F9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`, the safety harness) round-trips.
- **G-M4-6, no new risk to the engine's guarantees:** "every new write goes through fsx, and every repair is a journaled transaction that recovers like any other", and "the global lock is still held only for commit windows". The read path adds no write and never hashes under the lock; the quarantine is one primitive of E5's repair transaction.

**Checkpoint criteria it is responsible for** (§3.2; H6 records them):

- **9, the doctor's safety harness:** "every auto-fixer round-trips: corrupt → `doctor` finds it → `doctor fix` → the fixture asserts healthy → `doctor undo` → the subject tree is byte-identical to the corrupted state", "a second `doctor fix` takes 0 actions", "detectors are repeatable", "bare `doctor` changes nothing outside `<state>/doctor/`", and "`set(fixers) == set(fixtures with a fixer)`, and every detector has a fixture that triggers it and a clean home that does not". This leaf adds the row, its fixer and its fixture; F9 runs the properties over them, including the undo round trip.
- **10, the doctor's surface, in part:** "a check that runs out of its budget or its entry limit yields a `check-incomplete` finding, so the run is never `ok`". The blob detector is the doctor's one content-hashing detector, so it is the one most likely to meet its deadline.
- **17, gate and checkpoint runs, in part:** "On the development machine, `omaddons doctor --json` reports no finding that is wrong." This leaf adds a deep-tier step to the real-machine test `doctor_on_the_real_home`, so H6 reviews this detector on the real cache too.

**The decisions that shape it** (full text in the decision log comments on the milestone epic `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`):

- **M4-D52: cache blobs are verified when used, and corrupt ones are quarantined.** `BlobCache::get` checks a blob's SHA-256 against its name before handing it to staging; the cost is about one hash per install, and a mismatch counts as a cache miss. Online, the archive is downloaded again, verified, and written through fsx to the same content-addressed path, so the cache heals itself with no deletion. Offline, or when the source no longer serves it, the result is `hash_mismatch`, raised as a first attempt so the instance says `retryable: true` (online, a retry heals; the registry lists the code's retryability as conditional), with `details.blob` and the fix `omaddons doctor --include-deep`. `fm-caches-blob-hash-mismatch` (`deep`, P2) hashes every blob proactively and quarantines mismatches into `<cache>/quarantine/<run id>/blobs/`; a pinned blob (an installed release) is quarantined too, and its next reinstall fetches it again. *Why:* a blob damaged on disk is served without a check, and the engine's integrity promise should not depend on the disk. *Rejected:* (i) detection only (a bad blob would still install until someone runs `doctor --include-deep`); (ii) deleting on the read path (reads never prune: only `prune()` deletes, and only retention, cleanup, backups' prune and `doctor gc` call it).
- **M4-D29: one detector registry, by tier.** `status --cached` runs `cached`; `status`, `doctor --quick` and `doctor health` run `cached` and `quick`; `doctor` runs every tier but `deep`; `doctor --include-deep` runs every tier. A `deep` detector may hash content ("plus content hashing (blobs, `--deep` drift)", §6.13) within `DOCTOR_DETECTOR_DEADLINE`. So this detector never runs in `status`, the widget or a plain `doctor`. E3 decided that `--only` without a tier flag runs exactly what it names, whatever its tier, so `doctor --only fm-caches-blob-hash-mismatch` and `doctor fix --only fm-caches-blob-hash-mismatch` run it.
- **M4-D30: instance keys are resource-specific and stable.** `instance = <fm-id>@<target key | machine>[:<discriminator>]`, and the plan names this leaf's discriminator: `blob=<sha256>`. Two damaged blobs are two instances; a finding's human `label` is separate and never compared.
- **M4-D42: evidence never holds file content.** Paths, digests, modes and counts only. A blob finding cites its path, the digest its name promises and the digest its bytes have.
- **M4-D43: budgets are enforced, not only estimated.** Every detector works through a `Budget` (a deadline and an entry counter); one that hits its deadline or `DOCTOR_SCAN_MAX_ENTRIES` stops and returns what it found plus an `incomplete` record, which E3 turns into `fm-state_files-check-incomplete`. *Rejected:* treating truncation as a warning on a healthy run (incomplete coverage would read as a pass).
- **M4-D35: quarantine never crosses a filesystem.** A victim under `<cache>` is renamed (`RENAME_NOREPLACE`) to `<cache>/quarantine/<run id>/<path relative to <cache>>`, which for a blob is `<cache>/quarantine/<run id>/blobs/<sha256>`. A mount mismatch is found before anything moves (E5's `fsx::mount_id` check) and the run is REFUSING (`doctor_refused`, `filesystem_mismatch`). *Rejected:* a copy plus delete across filesystems (a deletion, and not atomic).
- **M4-D36: what a repair keeps is deleted only by `doctor gc`.** Transaction retention, the orphan sweep and blob eviction never touch `<cache>/quarantine/`; `doctor gc` (E8, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.8`) deletes a run's cache quarantine with the run.

**How it serves the vision.** The thesis is that omaddons stays the sole, safe, undoable authority over what it manages. Its own cache is part of that: after this leaf, an archive omaddons installs is the archive its name promises, whatever happened to the disk, and the cache repairs itself without ever deleting. G7, "`doctor` follows the world-class doctor contract": the proactive check is a detector with evidence and an exact remediation, and its repair is consented, journaled and undoable, never a deletion.

## Technical Approach

### 1. One verification function, and its memo (s1)

`src/engine/blobs.rs` gains the read-only verification every caller shares: `BlobCache::get` (s2) and the detector (s1).

```rust
/// What re-hashing a cached blob found.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Verification {
    /// Its bytes hash to its name.
    Matches { size: u64 },
    /// Its bytes hash to `actual` (64 lowercase hex), not to its name.
    Differs { size: u64, actual: String },
    /// A regular file is there and cannot be read: never used, never reported as matching.
    Unreadable { kind: std::io::ErrorKind },
    /// No regular file is at the path (absent, a directory, a symlink, or removed meanwhile).
    Gone,
    /// `stop` asked to stop before the last byte.
    Stopped,
}

/// Re-hashes the blob at `path` against `name` (64 lowercase hex), consulting `stop` after
/// each MiB read. An unchanged, settled stamp seen earlier in this process answers without
/// reading (the process-wide memo).
pub fn verify_blob(path: &Path, name: &str, stop: &mut dyn FnMut() -> bool) -> Verification;

/// What this process already hashed, by path.
pub struct VerifyMemo { /* Mutex<BTreeMap<PathBuf, Seen>>, cap, reads: AtomicU64 */ }
impl VerifyMemo {
    pub const fn new() -> Self;                        // cap DOCTOR_SCAN_MAX_ENTRIES
    #[doc(hidden)] pub const fn with_cap(cap: usize) -> Self;
    pub fn verify(&self, path: &Path, name: &str, stop: &mut dyn FnMut() -> bool, now_ns: i128) -> Verification;
    #[doc(hidden)] pub fn reads(&self) -> u64;         // files opened and hashed: the tests' witness
}
struct Seen { stamp: FileStamp, size: u64, sha256: [u8; 32] }
static MEMO: VerifyMemo = VerifyMemo::new();
```

The algorithm of `VerifyMemo::verify`:

1. `name` not 64 lowercase hex → `Gone` (not a blob). `is_sha256` becomes `pub(crate)` for the detector.
2. `FileStamp::read(path)` (`lstat`, symlinks not followed), and `read_at = now_ns`. `None`, or a stamp that is not a regular file → `Gone`. Any other error → `Unreadable { kind }`.
3. The memo holds this path with an equal stamp → answer from it (`Matches` or `Differs` against `name`), without opening the file.
4. Otherwise open the file (`NotFound` → `Gone`, any other error → `Unreadable`), read it in 64 KiB chunks into SHA-256, and consult `stop()` after each MiB read: `true` → `Stopped` (nothing remembered). A read error → `Unreadable { kind }`.
5. Read the stamp again. When it equals the first, the first was `settled(read_at)`, and the memo holds fewer than its cap, remember `Seen`. Then answer `Matches { size }` when the digest equals `name`, else `Differs { size, actual }`.

**Decided while writing this bead: a process-wide memo guarded by the stat stamp.** Two reasons, both about cost, never about behaviour:

- **One hash per blob per command.** One install can ask for the same blob several times: the reinstall's `local_blob_candidate`, then `fetch_blob`'s cache hits, then the download memo for each further target. Without the memo, a three-client update of a 5 MB archive hashes it three to five times.
- **No hashing under the global lock in `doctor fix`.** E6 re-runs the planned failure modes' detectors under the lock (M4-D45). For this detector that would hash the whole cache (up to `BLOB_CACHE_MAX_BYTES`, 1 GiB) a second time while every other command waits. With the memo, the under-lock pass costs one listing and one `lstat` per blob; only a blob whose stamp moved since the first pass is read again.

It cannot change a verdict: a stamp equal to a settled one proves the bytes did not change in between (the same argument as `predigest`), and an unsettled stamp is never remembered. It is keyed by path, so two homes in one test process never share an entry. It is in memory only. It is capped at `DOCTOR_SCAN_MAX_ENTRIES` entries (the most blobs one detector run visits; past the cap, verification still runs and is not remembered), so it needs no new constant. Decided while writing this bead: `store_checked` does not fill it, because a file just written is never settled. *Rejected:* a memo per `BlobCache` (the doctor's detector has no `BlobCache`, and E6's fresh view under the lock is a new value); a memo carried in the `DoctorView` (it would change E6's and E2's interfaces for a cache of a pure function).

### 3. The detector (s1)

`src/doctor/detectors/caches.rs` (new; §6.10's layout names `detectors/caches.rs`):

```rust
pub fn blob_hash_mismatch(view: &DoctorView, _selection: &Selection, budget: &mut Budget) -> Detected;
```

1. `view.caches()` is `None` only when the layer is unavailable, in which case E3's runner lists this row in `skipped` and never calls it; return `Detected::default()` defensively.
2. For each entry of `caches.blobs` in listing order (sorted by name): skip it unless `kind == File` and its name is a blob name (`is_sha256`: 64 lowercase hex). So `index.json`, fsx temp files (`.omaddons-*`), directories, symlinks and other names are never reported, exactly as eviction ignores them.
3. `budget.charge(1)`; on `Exhausted`, stop and return what was found with `budget.incomplete()`.
4. `blobs::verify_blob(&caches.blobs.dir.join(name), name, &mut || budget.check().is_err())`:
   - `Matches` or `Gone` (evicted between the listing and the read): nothing;
   - `Differs { actual, .. }`: one observation (below);
   - `Unreadable { .. }`: one observation with `reason: "unreadable"`;
   - `Stopped`: stop and return what was found with `budget.incomplete()` (the deadline).
5. After the loop, a listing with `truncated: true` returns `incomplete: Some(Incomplete { limit: IncompleteLimit::Entries })`: the blobs past the cut were never checked.

Each observation (E1's `Observation`): `subject: Subject::machine().blob(<the name's 32 bytes>)`, `confidence: High` (a hash, observed directly), `addon: None`, `folder: None`, and:

| differs | `Cached archive 3f9a1c4e2b7d… is damaged` (the first 12 hex digits) | `{path: "<cache>/blobs/<sha>", expected: "sha256:<name>", observed: "sha256:<actual>"}` |
| unreadable | `Cached archive 3f9a1c4e2b7d… cannot be read` | `{path, expected: "sha256:<name>", reason: "unreadable"}` |

### 4. The fixer (s1)

`src/doctor/fixers/quarantine.rs` (§6.10's layout names `fixers/quarantine.rs`, shared with F3's temp-file fixer, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.3`; whichever of the two leaves lands first creates the file, and the other adds its function beside it):

```rust
/// Quarantines a damaged cached archive into this run's cache quarantine.
pub fn blob(view: &DoctorView, finding: &Finding) -> Result<Vec<Fix>, Refusal>;
```

- The path is `view.paths().blob(<name>)`, the name taken from the finding's `evidence.expected` (`sha256:<name>`), so the fix can only ever name a file directly under `<cache>/blobs/`. A finding whose evidence holds no valid blob name cannot come from this detector; for it the fixer returns no fix (`Ok(vec![])`), and a unit test holds that the detector always provides one.
- It returns `vec![Fix::Quarantine { path, root: QuarantineRoot::Cache }]`. E5 lowers it to one `RenameNoReplace` from `<cache>/blobs/<sha>` to `<cache>/quarantine/<run id>/blobs/<sha>`, with `pre` = `{path: {kind: file, identity}, to: {kind: absent}}` and `post` the reverse, and resources `writes: [<cache>/blobs/<sha>, <cache>/quarantine/<run id>/blobs/<sha>]`. E5 creates `<cache>/quarantine/<run id>/blobs/` before `prepared`, and checks the mounts.
- **It never touches `blobs/index.json`.** A stale index entry is harmless: eviction lists the directory, not the index, and the next `touch` rewrites the index. One primitive per blob keeps the repair, its crash recovery and its undo one rename each.
- **It refuses nothing and consults no pins** (M4-D52: a pinned blob is quarantined too). A blob put right between planning and the commit is caught twice: E6's re-plan under the lock re-detects (the memo re-reads a blob whose stamp moved, finds it matching, and the fix drops out), and the rename's identity predicate fails if a new file took the name after the re-plan.

The token E6 computes for a bound run (`doctor fix --dry-run`, then `--if-match`) holds this step as `{fm, fix, op: "rename_noreplace", path: <cache>/blobs/<sha>, to_rel: "cache/blobs/<sha>"}` and its `pre` predicate: nothing run-specific, so a preview and its confirmation in another process agree.

The undo of this repair is E7's: one `RenameNoReplace` back, after checking that the quarantined file still has the recorded identity and that `<cache>/blobs/<sha>` is absent. F9 round-trips it.

### 5. Verified reads: `BlobCache::get` (s2)

`get` keeps its signature, `get(&self, scopes, sha256) -> Result<Option<BlobRef>>`, so its four callers keep treating `None` as "not cached, fetch it":

1. Lowercase; not 64 hex → `Ok(None)` (as today).
2. `symlink_metadata`: not a regular file → `Ok(None)` (as today).
3. **A blob larger than the effective download cap** (`self.max_download`, the `limits.download_max_bytes` the engine passes) → `Ok(None)` without hashing, and not recorded as damaged. Decided while writing this bead: such a file can only be there if the cap was lowered after it was downloaded (or the file was replaced), the download that would replace it is refused by the same cap (`archive_too_large`), and reading it unbounded would violate common rule 15.
4. `self.memo.verify(&path, &sha256, &mut || false, now_ns())`:
   - `Matches { size }` → `touch` (as today), `Ok(Some(BlobRef { sha256, size, path }))`;
   - `Differs { size, actual }` → remember a `DamagedBlob` in this cache instance, `Ok(None)`, **no** `touch` (a miss is not a use) and no deletion (M4-D52 rejected deleting on the read path);
   - `Unreadable { kind }` → remember it the same way, `Ok(None)`;
   - `Gone` or `Stopped` (impossible with a `stop` that never stops) → `Ok(None)`.

```rust
pub struct DamagedBlob { pub sha256: String, pub path: PathBuf, pub size: u64, pub damage: Damage }
pub enum Damage { Differs { actual: String }, Unreadable { kind: std::io::ErrorKind } }
impl BlobCache {
    /// A blob this cache found damaged during this command, by name.
    pub fn found_damaged(&self, sha256: &str) -> Option<DamagedBlob>;
    #[doc(hidden)] pub fn with_memo(self, memo: &'static VerifyMemo) -> Self;   // tests; default &MEMO
}
/// `error` (a fetch that could not replace `damaged`) as the error the user needs.
pub fn damaged_instead(error: Error, damaged: Option<&DamagedBlob>) -> Error;
```

The damage memory is a `Mutex<BTreeMap<String, DamagedBlob>>` in the `BlobCache`, so it lives exactly as long as the command's cache (one per `engine::tx::run`), and it is not cleared when a later download heals the blob (it records what this command found). `get`'s doc comment says what it now guarantees: a returned blob hashed to its name when it was returned.

**`local_blob_candidate`** (`plan.rs:5341-5376`) drops its own `hash_file_streaming` and uses `blob.size`: `get` now does that check, for every caller. Its behaviour is unchanged, and its unit test `a_cached_blob_is_the_recorded_release_while_it_hashes_to_it` keeps passing.

**`reused_unverified`'s doc comment** (`plan.rs:4913-4924`) says "the cache cannot check it either". After this leaf the cache proves that a blob holds the bytes that were downloaded, not that the download matched a hash its source published, so the `unverified` reason it reports still stands; reword the comment to say exactly that.

### 6. The planner: healing online, `hash_mismatch` offline (s2)

**When a fetch could not replace a damaged blob** (`blobs::damaged_instead`): the error becomes the damaged blob's own error when the fetch failed because the archive cannot be had now:

| The fetch's error | Becomes |
|---|---|
| `offline` | the damage error |
| `not_found` (the source no longer lists the release) | the damage error |
| `http_status` with `details.status` 404 or 410 (the source no longer serves the file) | the damage error |
| anything else (`network`, `rate_limited`, a 5xx `http_status`, `archive_too_large`, a download's own `hash_mismatch`, …) | unchanged |

Decided while writing this bead: M4-D52 says "offline, or when the source no longer serves it"; a transient failure keeps its own, retryable error, because a retry heals it.

**The damage error:**

- `Damage::Differs` → `Error::hash_mismatch(1, message, Suggestion::command(["omaddons", "doctor", "--include-deep"]))` with `details: {"blob": "<64 hex>", "actual": "<64 hex>"}`: exit 1, `retryable: true` (M4-D52: online, a retry downloads it again). The message names both digests by their first 12 hex digits and the reason it could not be replaced, for example: `the cached archive 3f9a1c4e2b7d… is damaged (its bytes hash to 9b0e55a1c3f2…, not to its name), and it cannot be downloaded again: --offline blocked a request`.
- `Damage::Unreadable` → `Error::io(&path, &io::Error::from(kind), Suggestion::command(["omaddons", "doctor", "--include-deep"]))`: today's `io` shape (`details.path`), with the doctor as its fix. Decided while writing this bead: an unreadable file did not "mismatch" anything, so it keeps the code that says what happened; the doctor reports it (Technical Approach §3) and its quarantine clears it.
- `details.actual` reuses the key the download form of `hash_mismatch` already carries; only `blob` is new (Technical Approach §7). Decided while writing this bead.

**Where the planner applies it** (`src/engine/plan.rs`):

1. **`fetch_blob`** (`:4817-4911`): before it downloads, it collects the damaged blobs among the ones its two cache hits asked for (the declared SHA-256, and the remembered fact's), with `ctx.blobs.found_damaged(sha)`. The download's error goes through `damaged_instead` (the `?` on each of the three download arms, and WowAce's assembly). When the download succeeds and a damaged blob was found, the planner adds a `-v` note: `<release id>: the cached archive <sha12>… did not match its name; downloaded it again` (its `notes`, which the commands already log at debug level through `out.log(LogLevel::Debug, …)`). Decided while writing this bead: a note, not a warning code, because the plan adds no warning for this leaf (§7.5 lists exactly three new warnings) and the heal needs no action.
2. **`prepare_install`, for a reinstall and a locked install** (`:3495-3634`): the release set's error at `:3552` and the `PinnedVersionNotFound` refusal at `:3560-3574` go through `damaged_instead` with the damaged blob among the ones this want would have reused: the installed record's `blob_sha256` for a reinstall (`intent.reinstall`), and the locked `cached` hash. When it converts, the result is the damage error; otherwise the error continues as today (through `not_cached` for an offline reinstall of an absent blob, which keeps `offline` with `details.reason: "not_cached"`). A small helper `TargetPlanner::recorded_damage(existing, intent, cached) -> Option<DamagedBlob>` collects them.
3. **`details.tried`.** A conversion inside a candidate's download (point 1) reaches the planner's existing rule for a release whose every candidate failed its published hash (`:3767-3778`), which returns the `hash_mismatch` with `details.tried` added, as for any download mismatch (`tried` is already in the spec). A conversion in `prepare_install` (point 2) returns before any candidate, so its `details` are exactly `{blob, actual}`.
4. **Nothing else changes.** The download memo (`:4806`) re-`get`s a blob it fetched for another target; a damaged one is now a miss, so it falls to `fetch_blob` and the rules above. `check_releases` (`outdated`, `adopt`'s checks) shares `fetch_blob`. Re-judging under the lock never fetches.

**What each path does after this leaf:**

| Situation | Online | Offline |
|---|---|---|
| `install --reinstall`, recorded blob damaged | `local_blob_candidate` declines; the source is asked; `fetch_blob`'s cache hits decline; the download heals `<cache>/blobs/<sha>` (same name when the bytes upstream are the same); installs; one more `asset` line in `net.log`; the `-v` note | `hash_mismatch` (`details.blob`), nothing changed |
| `sync --locked`, locked blob damaged | the same | `hash_mismatch`, whether the memo answers the listing (then `fetch_blob` converts the download's `offline`) or not (then `prepare_install` converts the listing's) |
| `update`, the new release's blob (downloaded by an earlier dry run) damaged | `fetch_blob` declines, downloads, installs | `hash_mismatch` when the release memo answers the listing within its window; else today's `offline` |
| `install` on a second client, the cached blob damaged | `fetch_blob` declines, downloads, installs | `install` revalidates its source, so offline it is `offline`, as today |
| the source now answers the asset URL with 404 | `hash_mismatch` (`fetch_blob` converts the `http_status` 404) | no request is made: as the row of the command that was run |
| the blob is absent | download (as today) | `offline` with `not_cached` (as today) |

Every row changes nothing on failure: no stage, no lock, no commit, the damaged file left in place, and `index.json` untouched by the miss.

**Hashing never happens under the global lock in the engine:** `get` runs only while planning, the commit re-judges without fetching, and eviction (under the lock) lists the directory without calling `get`. The perf test `commits_hold_the_lock_under_50_ms` (`tests/perf.rs:674-722`) keeps holding.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **A blob damaged on disk is never staged.** With the recorded blob of an installed release damaged (a same-size byte flip, a truncation, or another valid archive under its name), `install --reinstall` online downloads it again (one more `asset` line in `net.log`), the installed folder hashes as the release's own, `<cache>/blobs/<sha>` hashes to its name again (healed in place, nothing deleted), and the record's `release_id` and `blob_sha256` are unchanged.
- [ ] **Offline it fails and changes nothing.** The same reinstall with `--offline` fails `hash_mismatch` (exit 1, `retryable: true`, `details.blob` = the damaged blob's name, `details.actual` = what its bytes hash to, `fix_argv` = `["omaddons","doctor","--include-deep"]`), and `<state>`, the client dir and `<cache>/blobs/` (the damaged file and `index.json`) hash as before. Running the fix argv exits 1 and reports the finding.
- [ ] The same holds for `sync --locked` (online heals; offline `hash_mismatch`), for an `update` whose new release's cached blob is damaged (online installs a good copy; offline `hash_mismatch`), for an install on a second client (online, a good copy), and for a source that now answers the asset with 404 (`hash_mismatch`).
- [ ] An absent blob offline still fails `offline` with `details.reason: "not_cached"` (`tests/install.rs`'s existing case passes unchanged), and a transient failure (`network`, a 5xx) keeps its own error.
- [ ] A blob is hashed at most once per process while its stamp is unchanged and settled, never when it is not, never past the effective download cap, and never under the global lock by the engine (unit tests; `commits_hold_the_lock_under_50_ms` still passes).
- [ ] **The detector.** `fm-caches-blob-hash-mismatch` (P2, `deep`, `caches`) reports a damaged blob only under `doctor --include-deep` or `--only fm-caches-blob-hash-mismatch`, never in a plain `doctor`, `doctor --quick`, `doctor health` or `status`. The finding has `instance` `fm-caches-blob-hash-mismatch@machine:blob=<sha>`, `label` `machine · blob <12 hex>`, `confidence: high`, evidence `{path, expected, observed}` (or `reason: "unreadable"` for an unreadable blob), and the remediation `omaddons doctor fix --only fm-caches-blob-hash-mismatch` with `auto_fixable: true`.
- [ ] Two deep diagnoses of one state give equal findings; a diagnosis changes nothing outside `<state>/doctor/` (tree hashes of `<state>` without `doctor/`, `<cache>`, `<config>` and the client dirs); a clean home with a populated cache and non-blob entries in `blobs/` reports nothing; a detector stopped by its budget or a truncated listing reports `check-incomplete`, never a clean run.
- [ ] **The fixer.** `doctor fix --only fm-caches-blob-hash-mismatch` (and `doctor fix --include-deep`) quarantines the blob with one `rename_noreplace` into `<cache>/quarantine/<run id>/blobs/<sha>`, bytes and mode kept, `index.json` untouched, exit 0, after which `doctor --include-deep` reports nothing. A second run takes 0 actions and exits 0. Its dry run discloses that rename and returns a token a later `--if-match` run honours.
- [ ] A pinned blob is quarantined too; the next online reinstall downloads it again, and an offline one fails `offline` (`not_cached`). A blob put right between the preview and the run is never quarantined: a bound run is `plan_stale` (exit 4), and an unbound run paused at `doctor.fix.planned` takes 0 actions.
- [ ] The fixture `tests/doctor/fixtures/fm_caches_blob_hash_mismatch.rs` exists with `fixer() == true`, `subject() == [<cache>/blobs]` and `run_args() == ["--include-deep"]`, its `corrupt` produces the finding and the clean home does not (E3's per-fixture test). F9 round-trips it through `doctor undo`.
- [ ] Re-verification adds under 10 ms per 5 MB blob: `tests/perf.rs::blob_reverification_cost` (release build) prints the median of 21, and the close comment quotes it (a perf note, not a gate budget).
- [ ] `hash_mismatch`'s `DetailSpec` declares `blob` and its meaning names the cached-archive case; the contract rows `reinstall_damaged_blob_offline` and `doctor_deep_damaged_blob` are snapshotted, and A3's validation passes over them.
- [ ] README describes what ships: the doctor table row, "Files and state", the `hash_mismatch` row, the Safety model bullet, the Limitations sentence and the Troubleshooting entry, each in the commit that ships its surface.
- [ ] The snapshots that list failure modes and error meanings are re-accepted with only this row and this code changed; `SKILL.md` is regenerated where its blocks changed (once B1 has landed).
- [ ] `tests/real_machine.rs::doctor_on_the_real_home` also runs `doctor --include-deep --only fm-caches-blob-hash-mismatch --json`, read-only, printing every finding and the run's duration for H6.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files.
- [ ] The close comment lists every new or changed wire name (the failure-mode id `fm-caches-blob-hash-mismatch`, the `details` key `hash_mismatch.blob`, the `hash_mismatch` meaning, the file `<cache>/quarantine/<run id>/blobs/<sha256>`), Appendix B row 37's line, the compatibility note (an offline reinstall or locked sync of a damaged cached archive fails `hash_mismatch` where it failed `offline` "not in the blob cache", and a fallback fetch that used to serve a damaged blob now downloads it again), and every "Decided while writing this bead" item with its outcome.
