title: Tests: the widget and credential fixtures, their detection checks, and the credential repair end to end
description:
Part 4 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.7 (Plugins, secrets and the network). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

**The leaf.** F7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.7`) fills the doctor's `plugins`, `secrets` and `network` subsystems: Appendix B rows 38 (`fm-plugins-widget-version-drift`, P3, cached), 39 (`fm-plugins-widget-invalid`, P2, quick), 41 (`fm-secrets-credential-file-mode`, P2, cached, with the chmod fixer) and 42–44 (the online checks). Part 1 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.7.1) registered the two widget rows and the typed validator; part 2 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.7.2) the credential row, its manual advice and `fixers/chmod.rs`.

**This part** builds the fixtures of rows 38, 39 and 41 (M4-D47: "each failure mode has a fixture: a Rust type implementing `Fixture` in `tests/doctor/fixtures/<fm_id>.rs`, with `corrupt`, deterministic, built on the `tests/common/` builders (E3's trait takes `&Home`); `assert_healthy`; `subject` …; a doc comment that is the fixture's README"), their planting helpers, and the suite that proves, end to end on the real binary: each row's true positive and true negative, repeatability, purity, and the credential repair itself (the plan's acceptance: "The chmod fixer sets 0600 and the verify step passes; `explain` warns that undo restores the exposure (F9 round-trips it to 0644)"). F9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`, the safety harness) reuses the fixtures for its fourteen properties, T4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4`) for the slice-3 demo. It is its own step because fixtures and multi-command scenarios are integration work, separate from the detectors' code and its unit tests.

M4-D47's rejected alternative stays rejected: `corrupt.sh`/`assert.sh` per failure mode (a second test language; scripts that must clean up after themselves; the house rules ban `rm -rf` even in test scripts).

**The decisions it checks:**
- **M4-D50:** both widget rows are manual with the argv `omaddons omarchy install`; the doctor never reinstalls the widget.
- **M4-D51:** the stored token and `{ file = … }` credentials readable by group or others are reported; inside `<config>` the fixer sets 0600; outside, prose advice; undo restores the exposure and `explain` says so.
- **M4-D42:** evidence holds modes and paths, never content; the token is never read for evidence.
- **M4-D44 (E6's):** `doctor fix --dry-run` and a later `doctor fix --if-match <token>` in another process agree, because the token holds nothing run-specific; a change in between is `plan_stale` and changes nothing.

**What exists to build on** (from E3, E5, E6, T1 and the earlier parts; verified against their beads, and against the code at `c0ab5e9` where it already exists):
- T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`): `tests/common/tlog.rs`: `let log = tlog!();`, `log.step(label)`, `log.note(text)`, `log.json(label, &value)`, `log.run(&home, &argv) -> Ran`, `log.cmd(&home, &argv).env(k, v).failpoints(spec).spawn()`, `log.tree(label, root)`, `log.assert_unchanged(label, root)`, `log.case(name)`, and `Ran::{ok, exit, fails, envelope, error_code, warnings, commands, events, stdout, stderr}` (a doctor envelope has no `data` key: use `envelope()`). Environment variables whose names contain `TOKEN`, `SECRET` or `CREDENTIAL` are redacted in the log. A suite carries the crate-doc marker `//! e2e suite: <purpose>`, which `argc e2e` reads.
- E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`): `tests/doctor/mod.rs` with the `Fixture` trait (`id`, `corrupt(&Home)`, `assert_healthy(&Home)`, `subject(&Home) -> Vec<PathBuf>`, `fixer() -> bool`, `run_env`, `run_args`; F1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1`) added the defaulted `remedy(&Home)`), `tests/doctor/fixtures/mod.rs` with `all()`, `tests/common/doctor.rs` with `plant::widget_version_drift(home)` and `common::doctor::check_envelope`, and the pattern `#[path = "doctor/mod.rs"] mod fixtures;` for including them.
- `common::home::Home` (`tests/common/home.rs`): synthetic clients in one Wine prefix; every run sets `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES` to its scenario dir (`:257`), so no request ever leaves the test. `install <ref> --file <zip> -t retail --offline` installs a local archive as one ref's release (`src/app/install.rs:403-409`). `tests/omarchy.rs:24-…` builds a stub Omarchy desk (`Desk`: `<config-omarchy>`, stub `omarchy-shell`, `omarchy-plugin-validate`, `omarchy-bar`, `omarchy-plugin-disable` on a `PATH` holding only the stubs, and `OMARCHY_PATH`), so `omaddons omarchy install` runs without touching this machine's bar.
- The widget: `omarchy install` replaces an installed widget whenever any file differs from its render (`src/omarchy/install.rs:479-…`), while `outdated` reads only the `CONTENT_SHA256` stamp in `Build.js` (`src/omarchy/render.rs:300-306`); so a manifest edit or a planted symlink makes `widget-invalid` fire without drift, and `omarchy install` clears it.
- The credential: `<config>/credentials/github` (`src/state/paths.rs:170-179`); the Config scope row admits the doctor (`src/fsx/scope.rs:108`).
- E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`): `doctor fix` and its report (`state`, `tx`, `summary {findings_before, findings_after, actions_taken, actions_failed, bytes_backed_up, backups_restored}`, `actions[]`, `actions_planned[]` under `--dry-run` with `bytes`, `precondition`, `undo_command`), `--if-match`, `plan_stale` (exit 4 in the doctor dictionary, `details.changed`), and VERIFYING. E5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`): the `kind: repair` history line (`target: null`, `targets: []`, `repairs[]`, `doctor_run_id`).

## Technical Approach

1. **Helpers** (`tests/common/omarchy.rs`, `tests/common/doctor.rs`):
   - `tests/common/omarchy.rs`: lift `Desk`'s stub writer out of `tests/omarchy.rs` (unless E3's `plant::widget_version_drift` already did): `pub fn stub_desk(env: &TestEnv) -> Desk` and `Desk::install(&home)` running `omaddons omarchy install --json` with the stubs' `PATH` and `OMARCHY_PATH`. `tests/omarchy.rs` uses it; its tests pass unchanged.
   - `plant::widget_current(home)`: install this binary's widget through the stub desk.
   - `plant::widget_invalid(home)`: `widget_current`, then in `<plugins>/omaddons/manifest.json` set `barWidget.defaultSection` to `"top"` (parse the JSON, set the key, write it back) and create the symlink `views/link → ../manifest.json` inside the plugin folder; `Build.js` untouched. The finding: row 39, `count: 2`, `rules: ["default_section", "symlink"]`, and no row 38 finding.
   - `plant::credential_file_mode(home) -> PathBuf`: create `<config>/credentials/` mode 0700 and write `github` holding the fixed fake token `ghp_F7FIXTURE000000000000000000000000000` (plain test writes; the binary is not needed), mode 0644. The finding: row 41, `mode: "0644"`, `origin: file`, `source: github`, fixable.
   - `plant::configured_credential(home, path, mode) -> PathBuf`: write a fake key at `path` with `mode`, and add `[sources.github] credential = { file = "<path>" }` to `<config>/config.toml` (plain edit).
   - Each helper's doc comment says what it breaks and which finding, severity and evidence it yields.
2. **Fixtures** (`tests/doctor/fixtures/`, registered in `all()`, each with a doc comment that is its README):
   - `fm_plugins_widget_version_drift.rs`: `corrupt` = `plant::widget_version_drift(home)`; `assert_healthy` = `doctor --json --only fm-plugins-widget-version-drift` reports none; `remedy` = `omaddons omarchy install` on the stub desk; `fixer()` false; `subject()` empty.
   - `fm_plugins_widget_invalid.rs`: `corrupt` = `plant::widget_invalid(home)`; `remedy` = `omaddons omarchy install`; `assert_healthy` = neither widget row; `fixer()` false; `subject()` empty.
   - `fm_secrets_credential_file_mode.rs`: `corrupt` = `plant::credential_file_mode(home)`; `assert_healthy` = the file's mode is 0600 and `doctor --json --only fm-secrets-credential-file-mode` reports none; `fixer()` true; `subject()` = `[<config>/credentials/github]` (F9 compares it, mode included, after its undo).
3. **The suite** `tests/doctor_plugins_secrets.rs` (new), first line `//! e2e suite: the widget and credential failure modes, and the chmod repair`. Every scenario is a `TestLog` scenario on its own `Home::new(&["wow"])` (a second product where a scenario says so), runs commands only through `log.run`/`log.cmd` with `--json` passed explicitly, checks each doctor envelope with `common::doctor::check_envelope`, and states its steps:
   1. **`widget_fixtures_are_found_and_cleared`** — per widget fixture (`log.case(<id>)`): "plant" (`corrupt`); "diagnose" (`doctor --json`): exit 1, `DONE_FINDINGS`, the finding at its severity with the evidence of §1 (`reason: code_differs` for drift; `count`, `rules` for invalid), `remediation.argv == ["omaddons","omarchy","install"]`, `auto_fixable: false`, and no manifest value anywhere in the envelope (the planted `"top"` does not appear); "remedy"; "verify" (`assert_healthy`).
   2. **`a_widget_serving_another_state_gets_prose`** — `plant::widget_invalid`, then rewrite `Build.js`'s `CONTEXT` line to another `HOME` (as `tests/omarchy.rs`'s `restamp` does): the finding is reported with `argv: null` and the prose remediation; drift is not reported (M3-D7).
   3. **`no_widget_finding_on_a_clean_or_current_home`** — `common::realistic_home()` (lifted from `tests/perf.rs`'s bench home by whichever leaf first needed it; lift it here otherwise): `doctor --json --only fm-plugins-widget-version-drift,fm-plugins-widget-invalid` → exit 0 with no `<config-omarchy>`; then `plant::widget_current` → exit 0 again.
   4. **`credential_fixture_is_found_fixed_and_verified`** — "plant" (`plant::credential_file_mode`; `log.tree` of `<config>`, `<state>` without `doctor/`, `<cache>` and the client dir); "diagnose": exit 1, the finding with `instance == "fm-secrets-credential-file-mode@machine:path=<the file>"`, title "The GitHub token file is readable by other users", evidence exactly `{path, mode: "0644", expected: "0600", origin: "file", source: "github"}`, `remediation.argv == ["omaddons","doctor","fix","--only","fm-secrets-credential-file-mode"]`, `auto_fixable: true`, `estimated_actions: 1`; the trees unchanged; "dry run" (`doctor fix --only fm-secrets-credential-file-mode --dry-run --json`): exit 1, one `actions_planned` entry `{op: "chmod", path, mode: "0600", pre: {kind: "file", identity, mode: "0644"}, post: {…, mode: "0600"}, bytes: 0}`, a `precondition`; the file still 0644; "fix" (`doctor fix --only fm-secrets-credential-file-mode --json`): exit 0, `DONE_OK`, `summary.actions_taken: 1`, `bytes_backed_up: 0`, `findings_after: 0`, `tx` set; the file is mode 0600, same inode, same bytes; every other tree unchanged; "history" (`history --json`): the newest line is `kind: repair`, `target: null`, `targets: []`, `repairs[0].op: "chmod"`, `repairs[0].fm`, `pre.mode: "0644"`, `post.mode: "0600"`, `doctor_run_id` equal to the fix's run id; "verify" (`doctor --json --only fm-secrets-credential-file-mode`): exit 0; "again" (a second `doctor fix --only fm-secrets-credential-file-mode`): `actions_taken: 0`, exit 0 (idempotence).
   5. **`explain_warns_that_undo_restores_the_exposure`** — `doctor explain fm-secrets-credential-file-mode --json`: `failure_mode.why` contains "undoing that repair restores the old mode, and with it the exposure"; `failure_mode.fixer` is `{ops: ["chmod"], writes_to: ["config"], enabled: true, needs_force: false, reversible: true}`; writes nothing (`log.assert_unchanged` on `<state>`).
   6. **`the_chmod_preview_binds_across_processes`** — case `unchanged`: `--dry-run`, then `--if-match <token>` in a new process → exit 0, the file 0600. Case `mode_changed`: `--dry-run`, then `chmod 0640` by hand, then `--if-match` → exit 4, `plan_stale`, `details.changed` contains `observed`, the file still 0640. Case `replaced`: `--dry-run`, then the file replaced by a new one (another inode, same bytes, mode 0644) → `--if-match` exit 4, `plan_stale`, nothing chmodded. Case `two_dry_runs`: two dry runs of an unchanged home give equal tokens.
   7. **`credentials_outside_the_scope_are_left_alone`** — cases (`log.case`): `outside` (`plant::configured_credential(home, <root>/elsewhere/gh, 0644)`), `symlink` (`<config>/credentials/github` a symlink to `<root>/elsewhere/gh`, mode 0644), `other_owner` (skipped as non-root, since a test cannot create another user's file: the case runs only when `procfs::running_as_root()`, chowning the file to uid 65534, and logs its skip otherwise). Each: `doctor --json` → the finding with `reason` set, `auto_fixable: false`, the prose remediation (`chmod 600 <path>`, or the symlink and owner texts), `argv: null`; `doctor fix --json` (no `--only`) → `actions_taken: 0`, the finding listed as manual; `doctor fix --only fm-secrets-credential-file-mode --json` → `DONE_FINDINGS`, exit 1, `actions_taken: 0`; the outside file, the link and its target unchanged (mode and bytes).
   8. **`inside_and_outside_in_one_run`** — the stored token (0644) and an outside `{file}` (0644): `doctor fix --only fm-secrets-credential-file-mode` repairs the stored one and leaves the outside one listed as manual (the outside instance is never a residual of the repair).
   9. **`credential_detection_cases`** — one case each: a zero-byte stored file at 0644 (`auth github clear`'s result) → no finding; mode 0600 → none; mode 0602 → "open to other users"; a configured `{file}` inside `<config>` at 0644 → title "The credential file config.toml names for github …", `origin: config`, fixable; the stored token also configured as a `{file}` → one finding; a broken `config.toml` → the row in `skipped` with `config_unavailable` (never a clean result).
   10. **`detection_is_repeatable_and_pure`** — with all three fixtures planted: two `doctor --json` runs give equal `findings`; every tree but `<state>/doctor/` hash-identical across both; no `net.log` line added.
   11. **`the_fake_token_never_appears`** — after scenarios 4 and 6 on one home: the planted token's text appears in no stdout, no stderr, no file under `<state>` (`report.json`, `runtime.jsonl`, `actions.jsonl`, `history.jsonl`, `net.log`) and no file under the test's log directory.
   12. **`status_is_unchanged_by_these_rows`** — with all three planted: `status --json` and `status --cached --json` report the widget drift issue exactly as before (title, remediation) and neither row 39 nor row 41 (F8, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.8`, adds them).
4. **Contract.** No new matrix row (no new command); every envelope goes through `support::check`'s doctor mode in `check_envelope`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The three fixture files exist, registered in `fixtures::all()`, each with a doc comment that is its README; `fm_secrets_credential_file_mode` declares `fixer() == true` and its `subject`; the widget fixtures declare no fixer.
- [ ] `tests/doctor_plugins_secrets.rs` passes in the gate with every scenario of Technical Approach §3, each a `TestLog` scenario.
- [ ] The chmod repair sets 0600 on the same inode with the same bytes, verifies clean, writes one `kind: repair` history line, and a second run takes no action; `explain` says undo restores the exposure.
- [ ] The preview binds across processes, and a mode change or a replaced file between preview and run gives `plan_stale` with nothing chmodded.
- [ ] Credentials outside `<config>`, symlinked, or another user's are reported with prose and never touched.
- [ ] No widget or credential finding on the realistic home; detection is repeatable and writes nothing outside `<state>/doctor/`; the fake token appears nowhere.
- [ ] `tests/omarchy.rs` passes unchanged on the lifted stub desk; `status` output is unchanged.
- [ ] `argc e2e doctor_plugins_secrets` runs the suite with verbose logs; `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean; the close comment lists the fixtures and `plant` helpers (for F9 and T4).

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

None new in this part (the detectors' and the fixer's unit tests landed with them in s1 and s2). The helpers in `tests/common/` carry a small self-check each in `tests/common_selftest.rs`: `plant_widget_invalid_breaks_exactly_two_rules` (in-process `omarchy::validate::check` over the planted folder gives exactly `default_section` and `symlink`), `plant_credential_file_mode_sets_0644`.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

The suite of Technical Approach §3, `tests/doctor_plugins_secrets.rs`. Run: `cargo test --test doctor_plugins_secrets`, or `argc e2e doctor_plugins_secrets` with verbose logs.

### Logging

Every scenario uses `TestLog`: one `log.step` per phase named as in §3 ("plant", "diagnose", "dry run", "fix", "history", "verify", "again", "remedy"); each command through `log.run`/`log.cmd`, so its argv, environment overrides (the stub desk's `PATH`, `OMARCHY_PATH`), exit, envelope, stderr events and `net.log` lines are in `steps.jsonl` and `transcript.md`; `log.tree` before the first command of each scenario for `<config>`, `<state>` without `doctor/`, `<cache>` and each client dir, and `log.assert_unchanged` wherever a tree must not change; the credential's mode, inode and bytes recorded with `log.json("credential", …)` before each assertion on them (the bytes as their SHA-256, never the fake token itself); the evidence and the `actions`/`actions_planned` entries recorded with `log.json` before they are asserted. A failure prints the transcript path and the last 20 steps.

## Considerations

- **The stub desk is mandatory.** A widget test that ran the real `omarchy-*` tools would place the widget on this machine's bar; `Desk` keeps a `PATH` of stubs only, as `tests/omarchy.rs` always has.
- **Root and the owner case.** Tests usually run as a normal user; the other-owner case runs only as root and logs why it skipped otherwise (no `SKIP` rule applies: it is a gate test with an environment-dependent case, and the unit test in s2 covers the rule with a synthetic uid).
- **No undo here.** The chmod's undo is E7's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7`) generic inverse and F9's round trip; F7 is not blocked by E7.
- **Hot spots:** `tests/doctor/fixtures/mod.rs` and `tests/common/doctor.rs` are shared with every catalog leaf: append, rebase.

## Dependencies

- **Parent:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.7.
- **Before it:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.7.1 (the widget rows and the typed validator) and omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.7.2 (the credential row and the chmod fixer). It is blocked by T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`) at filing, because it writes a `TestLog` suite.
- **Beside it:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.7.5 (the online scenarios; other files, except the shared `fixtures/mod.rs` and `tests/common/doctor.rs`).
- **After it:** nothing inside the leaf; F9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`) and T4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4`) reuse these fixtures once the leaf closes.

title: E2E: `doctor --online`, the network fixtures on recorded answers, and the live probe
description:
Part 5 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.7 (Plugins, secrets and the network). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

**The leaf.** F7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.7`) fills the doctor's `plugins`, `secrets` and `network` subsystems (Appendix B rows 38, 39 and 41–44). Part 3 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.7.3) added the `network` rows and the client they share:
- `fm-network-github-rate-limited` (P2): one `GET https://api.github.com/rate_limit` (with the configured token when there is one); a finding when 5 or fewer core requests remain (`GITHUB_REST_RESERVE`), or on a 403/429 with `x-ratelimit-remaining: 0`;
- `fm-network-credential-rejected` (P1): with a credential configured, one `GET /rate_limit` with it; a finding on 401 (`reason: rejected`), or, with no request, when the configured credential cannot be read (`reason: unresolvable`); the remediation is `omaddons auth github clear` for the stored file and prose for the environment or config.toml;
- `fm-network-source-unreachable` (P2): one request per enabled GitHub, WoWInterface, Tukui or WowAce source that an available record uses, for its first project by (target id, addon key); a finding on a 5xx (`server_error`), a 429 (`too_many_requests`) or no HTTP answer (`no_answer`), instance `@machine:source=<id>`.

Each probe is one request on the core network stack (no retry, manual redirects), purpose `doctor-probe`, bounded by its detector's budget; an answer the detector cannot judge, or a failure of omaddons' own (a missing replay fixture, a `net.log` write), is `unanswered`, which the runtime turns into `fm-state_files-check-incomplete` (`limit: unanswered`), never a clean result. Without `--online` the rows are `skipped: online_required`; an online-only `--only` is `online_required` (exit 6).

**This part** proves all of that end to end on the real binary, with recorded HTTP answers, as the plan's test plan says ("Fixtures. `tests/doctor.rs::online_*`") and its acceptance requires ("The network detectors make exactly one request each, allowlisted and logged, with none without `--online`"). It also adds the three network fixtures (M4-D47, common rule 19: "a leaf that adds a failure mode adds … its fixture"), E3's missing exit-6 row ("Exit 6 (`online_required`) has no end-to-end row until F7 adds an online failure mode; the row is added then"), and the checkpoint's live probe (§11.1: "Live probes (`OMADDONS_LIVE=1`) | the checkpoint | `doctor --online` against the real hosts (one request per source)"; every checkpoint test has an owning leaf, §2.6 lesson 2). It is its own step because these scenarios need a recorded-answer harness and touch E3's suite and the live probes, none of which the detectors' commit needs.

**The decisions it checks:** M4-D51 (each online check is one allowlisted, logged `doctor-probe` request; without `--online`, `skipped: online_required`); M4-D40 (`online_required` is doctor exit 6); M4-D43 (a check that could not finish is `check-incomplete`, never a pass); M4-D42 (no token, header or body in evidence); §8.1's default 4 (no network on a read path except `doctor --online` and the other upstream commands).

**What exists to build on** (from T1, E3, s3 and the code at `c0ab5e9`):
- T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`): `TestLog` (`tlog!()`, `step`, `note`, `json`, `run`, `cmd(..).env(..).failpoints(..).spawn()`, `tree`, `assert_unchanged`, `case`) and `Ran` (`ok`, `exit`, `fails`, `envelope`, `error_code`, `warnings`, `commands`, `events`, `stdout`, `stderr`); `log.run` records the `net.log` lines each command added; variables naming a token are redacted.
- E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`): `tests/doctor.rs` (first line `//! e2e suite: …`), its exit table `every_doctor_exit_site_uses_the_doctor_dictionary` (one `log.case` per row `(name, argv, setup, exit, code)`), `common::doctor::check_envelope`, the `Fixture` trait with `run_args` (F1 added `remedy`), `tests/doctor/fixtures/mod.rs` `all()`, and the debug failpoint `doctor.detector.panic` (its `sleep:<ms>` form delays a detector, as E3's deadline scenario uses it).
- `common::home::Home` runs every command with `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES` set to its scenario dir (`tests/common/home.rs:257`), so a request with no fixture is the replay transport's `internal` error (`src/net/replay.rs:158-170`), never a real request; a bare `TestEnv` would use the real transport. Replay matches a request by method and normalized URL (`replay.rs:66-69`) and cannot simulate a transport failure. `tests/common/http.rs::fixture_seq` writes a GET fixture (`:97-127`); `fixture`, `Resp::{ok, status, header}` build answers. `common::netlog::net_log(home)` and `NetLogView::count(host, purpose)` read `net.log` (`tests/common/netlog.rs:15-40`).
- `install <ref> --file <zip> -t retail --offline` installs a local archive as one ref's release (`src/app/install.rs:403-409`), so a record of any source is planted without a request.
- The probes' exact requests (s3): `GET https://api.github.com/rate_limit`; `GET https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/releases/latest`; `GET https://api.mmoui.com/v3/game/WOW/filedetails/<id>.json`; `GET https://api.tukui.org/v1/addons`; `PROPFIND https://repos.wowace.com/wow/<slug>/tags/` (`REPOS` is `https://repos.wowace.com/wow`, `src/sources/wowace.rs:41`).
- Live probes: `tests/live_probes.rs` (`OMADDONS_LIVE=1 cargo test --test live_probes -- --ignored`), each `#[ignore = "live network probe: OMADDONS_LIVE=1"]`, gated by `common::checkpoint::require(test, &["OMADDONS_LIVE"])`, which prints `SKIP <test>: <reason>` and fails unless `OMADDONS_ALLOW_SKIP` names it (`tests/common/checkpoint.rs`). Existing probes use `wowi:5995`, `tukui:elvui` and `wowace:bug-grabber` (`tests/live_probes.rs:430`, `:885`, `:931`).

## Technical Approach

1. **Helpers** (`tests/common/http.rs`, `tests/common/doctor.rs`):
   - `http::fixture_method(scenario, name, method, url, responses)`: `fixture_seq` with the request's method (`fixture_seq` calls it with `"GET"`), so a `PROPFIND` fixture can be written.
   - `plant::records_for_sources(home, sources: &[SourceId])`: for each, `install <ref> --file <a fixture zip> -t retail --offline --json` with the ref `gh:f7probe/Probe`, `wowi:5995`, `tukui:elvui` or `wowace:bug-grabber` (each zip holding one folder with a TOC of the ref's name, from `common::archives`).
   - `pub mod probes` (each writes replay fixtures under `home.http` for exactly the URL and method the detector sends, and documents it):
     - `rate_limit(home, limit, remaining, reset_epoch)`: 200, `content-type: application/json`, the body `{"resources":{"core":{"limit":…,"remaining":…,"reset":…,"used":…,"resource":"core"}},"rate":{…}}`;
     - `rate_limit_status(home, status, headers)`: any status, for 401, 403 with `x-ratelimit-remaining: 0`, 500, or a 200 with the body `not json`;
     - `source(home, source: SourceId, status)`: GitHub (302 with `location: …/releases/tag/v1`, or the status given), WoWInterface (200 `[{"UID":"5995",…}]`, or the status), Tukui (200 `[]`, or the status), WowAce (207 with a minimal multistatus body, or the status), for the refs `records_for_sources` plants;
     - `serve_healthy(home)`: a healthy `/rate_limit` and a healthy answer for every source the home's records use (computed from the records by the same rule the detector uses: the first project by (target id, addon key)).
2. **Fixtures** (`tests/doctor/fixtures/`, registered in `all()`, each `run_args() == ["--online"]`, `fixer() == false`, `subject()` empty, a doc comment that is its README):
   - `fm_network_github_rate_limited.rs`: `corrupt` = `probes::rate_limit(home, 60, 2, 1767225600)`; the finding: P2, `rate_limit {limit: 60, remaining: 2, reset_at: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"}`, `authenticated: false`; `remedy` = `probes::rate_limit(home, 60, 59, 1767225600)`; `assert_healthy` = `doctor --online --json --only fm-network-github-rate-limited` exits 0.
   - `fm_network_credential_rejected.rs`: `corrupt` = the stored fake token `ghp_F7ONLINE00000000000000000000000000000` (mode 0600, plain writes) and `probes::rate_limit_status(home, 401, &[])`; the finding: P1, `reason: rejected`, `http_status: 401`, `origin: file`, remediation argv `["omaddons","auth","github","clear"]`; `remedy` = run that argv; `assert_healthy` = no finding and no request for this row.
   - `fm_network_source_unreachable.rs`: `corrupt` = `plant::records_for_sources(home, &[Github, Wowi])`, `probes::source(home, Github, 302)`, `probes::source(home, Wowi, 503)`; the finding: one instance `fm-network-source-unreachable@machine:source=wowi`, `reason: server_error`, `http_status: 503`, `host: "api.mmoui.com"`; `remedy` = `probes::source(home, Wowi, 200)`; `assert_healthy` = none.
   - Each doc comment notes that under `--online` the run appends `net.log` lines, which F9's comparisons exclude (§6.15).
3. **`tests/doctor.rs::online_*`** (E3's suite; every scenario a `TestLog` scenario on its own `Home::new(&["wow"])`, never a bare `TestEnv`; commands only through `log.run`/`log.cmd` with `--json` explicit; each envelope through `check_envelope`; `net.log` lines read with `common::netlog::net_log` and recorded with `log.json` before they are asserted):
   1. **`online_checks_are_skipped_without_online`** — records for all four sources and a stored token; `doctor --json`: `skipped` holds the three network ids with `reason: online_required`, `summary.online_required: 3`; no `net.log` line added; `doctor -v` (human) says "3 online checks skipped".
   2. **`online_only_selection_is_online_required`** — cases `doctor --only fm-network-github-rate-limited`, `doctor --only fm-network-source-unreachable,fm-network-credential-rejected`, `doctor fix --only fm-network-credential-rejected`: exit 6, `error.code: online_required`, `details.fms` the selected ids, `fix_argv` = the argv plus `--online`, no run directory created, no `net.log` line; then, with healthy probe answers, the `fix_argv` run → exit 0.
   3. **`online_mixed_selection_runs_the_offline_rows`** — `plant::credential_file_mode` (s4's helper) and records; `doctor --json --only fm-secrets-credential-file-mode,fm-network-source-unreachable` (no `--online`): exit 1, the credential finding present, `fm-network-source-unreachable` in `skipped` with `online_required`, no `net.log` line.
   4. **`online_each_check_sends_exactly_one_request`** — records for all four sources, a stored token, `probes::serve_healthy`; cases, each on a fresh copy of the home: `--only fm-network-github-rate-limited` → exactly 1 new `net.log` line (`GET api.github.com /rate_limit`, `purpose: doctor-probe`, `status: 200`); `--only fm-network-credential-rejected` → exactly 1, the same request; `--only fm-network-source-unreachable` → exactly 4, in the order GitHub, WoWInterface, Tukui, WowAce, methods `GET`, `GET`, `GET`, `PROPFIND`, paths `/f7probe/Probe/releases/latest`, `/v3/game/WOW/filedetails/5995.json`, `/v1/addons`, `/wow/bug-grabber/tags/`; plain `doctor --online` → exactly 6 lines, all `doctor-probe`; every line's host is on the always-list (`omaddons::net::allowlist::ALWAYS`); every run exit 0, `DONE_OK`, no finding. A case with no credential: `--only fm-network-credential-rejected` → 0 lines, exit 0. A case with records of no HTTP source (a `file:` ref only): `--only fm-network-source-unreachable` → 0 lines, exit 0.
   5. **`online_rate_limit_is_reported`** — cases: `unauthenticated_nearly_spent` (`rate_limit(60, 2, …)`, no token) → the finding, `authenticated: false`, the remediation prose naming the reset time and "pipe a token to omaddons auth github set"; `authenticated_spent_by_headers` (stored token, `rate_limit_status(403, x-ratelimit-limit 5000, x-ratelimit-remaining 0, x-ratelimit-reset …)`) → the finding, `authenticated: true`, `origin: file`, the prose without the token advice; `healthy` (`rate_limit(60, 59, …)`) → none. Each: exactly one `net.log` line.
   6. **`online_credential_rejected_is_reported_and_cleared`** — case `file`: the stored token answered 401 → the finding (`reason: rejected`, `origin: file`, argv `omaddons auth github clear`); run that argv → exit 0, the stored file now empty; `doctor --online --json --only fm-network-credential-rejected` → no finding and no new `net.log` line. Case `env`: `log.cmd(..).env("OMADDONS_GITHUB_TOKEN", "ghp_F7ENV…")`, 401 → `origin: env`, `argv: null`, prose "replace or unset OMADDONS_GITHUB_TOKEN". Case `unresolvable`: config.toml `[sources.github] credential = { env = "OMADDONS_F7_NO_SUCH_VAR" }` → the finding `reason: unresolvable`, `origin: config`, prose "correct [sources.github] credential in config.toml", and **no** `net.log` line for either GitHub row; `fm-network-github-rate-limited` is a `check-incomplete` finding with `limit: unanswered`.
   7. **`online_unreachable_sources_are_reported_per_source`** — records for all four; GitHub 302, WoWInterface 503, Tukui 429, WowAce 207: exit 1, exactly two findings, `…@machine:source=wowi` (`server_error`, 503, `api.mmoui.com`, confidence `high`, label `machine · WoWInterface`) and `…@machine:source=tukui` (`too_many_requests`, 429); GitHub and WowAce not reported; a GitHub 404 (the project gone) in a second case → not reported; `doctor explain` of `fm-network-source-unreachable@machine:source=wowi` exits 0 with `instances: []` and `incomplete.limit: online_required` and adds no `net.log` line.
   8. **`online_unanswered_is_incomplete_never_clean`** — case `unreadable_rate_limit` (200 with `not json`): a `fm-state_files-check-incomplete` finding with evidence `{detector: "fm-network-github-rate-limited", limit: "unanswered", deadline_ms: null, max_entries: null}`, its remediation argv `omaddons doctor --online --only fm-network-github-rate-limited` (run: exit 1 again, same finding), state `DONE_FINDINGS`, never `DONE_OK`. Case `missing_fixture`: records for GitHub and WoWInterface, a fixture only for GitHub: no `fm-network-source-unreachable` finding for WoWInterface (an `internal` replay error is omaddons' own failure), a `check-incomplete` finding for the row with `limit: unanswered`.
   9. **`online_probe_respects_the_deadline`** — `doctor --online --json --only fm-network-github-rate-limited --budget 500ms` with `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS=doctor.detector.panic=sleep:600`: a `check-incomplete` finding with `limit: deadline`, and no new `net.log` line (an expired budget sends nothing).
   10. **`online_fix_lists_network_findings_as_manual`** — the 401 answer and an exposed stored token (`plant::credential_file_mode`): `doctor fix --online --json`: the credential mode repaired (`actions_taken: 1`), the rejected-token finding listed as manual with its remediation, never acted on; the stored token's bytes unchanged (the doctor chmods, never rewrites).
   11. **`online_token_never_appears`** — after scenarios 6 (`file` and `env`) and 10 on one home: the fake tokens' text appears in no stdout, no stderr, no file under `<state>` (`report.json`, `runtime.jsonl`, `history.jsonl`, `net.log`) and no file under the test's log directory.
   12. **`online_findings_are_repeatable`** — with scenario 7's answers, two `doctor --online --json` runs give equal `findings` after stripping the declared volatile keys.
   13. **`online_no_false_positive_on_the_realistic_home`** — `common::realistic_home()` with `probes::serve_healthy`: `doctor --online --json --only fm-network-github-rate-limited,fm-network-credential-rejected,fm-network-source-unreachable` → exit 0, no finding, exactly one `doctor-probe` line per probed source plus one `/rate_limit` line per GitHub row that had something to check.
   14. **The exit table** (`every_doctor_exit_site_uses_the_doctor_dictionary`) gains the row `online only | doctor --only fm-network-source-unreachable | — | 6 | online_required`, and the doctor diagnose path's `COMMANDS.exits` declares 6.
4. **The live probe** `tests/live_probes.rs::doctor_online_probes_the_real_hosts` (`#[ignore = "live network probe: OMADDONS_LIVE=1"]`): `common::checkpoint::require("doctor_online_probes_the_real_hosts", &["OMADDONS_LIVE"])` first; a fresh `TestEnv` (the real transport: no `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES`) with a synthetic Battle.net retail root (`common::trees::BattlenetRoot`); records planted offline with `install <ref> --file <zip> -t retail --offline` for `gh:WeakAuras/WeakAuras2`, `wowi:5995`, `tukui:elvui` and `wowace:bug-grabber`; no token configured; then `omaddons doctor --online --json --only fm-network-github-rate-limited,fm-network-source-unreachable`. Asserts: exactly 5 new `net.log` lines, all `purpose: doctor-probe`, one to `api.github.com` `/rate_limit` and one per source host, each with a status; no `fm-network-source-unreachable` finding (every source answered); `fm-network-github-rate-limited` either reported or not (the machine's budget varies) but never `check-incomplete`; it prints every finding for H6's review. Command: `OMADDONS_LIVE=1 cargo test --test live_probes -- --ignored doctor_online_probes_the_real_hosts`. It makes five requests, writes only under its tempdir, and never touches the real `HOME`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The three network fixtures exist, registered in `fixtures::all()`, each with `run_args() == ["--online"]`, `fixer() == false` and a doc comment that is its README; their `corrupt` yields exactly their row's finding and their `remedy` makes `assert_healthy` hold.
- [ ] Every `online_*` scenario of Technical Approach §3 passes in the gate: no request without `--online`; `online_required` (exit 6) for an online-only `doctor --only` and `doctor fix --only`, its fix run; exactly one request per check (one per probed source for `source-unreachable`), each `doctor-probe` on an always-allowlisted host; each row's findings from recorded answers; `unanswered` and the deadline as `check-incomplete`, never clean; no false positive on the realistic home.
- [ ] The fake tokens appear in no output, run file, history line, `net.log` line or test log.
- [ ] E3's exit table has the exit-6 row, and every exit seen is declared in its path's `COMMANDS.exits`.
- [ ] `tests/live_probes.rs::doctor_online_probes_the_real_hosts` exists, is ignored, gated by `OMADDONS_LIVE` with the `SKIP` rule, and passes when run with `OMADDONS_LIVE=1` on a machine with network access (run once by this subtask's agent if it has network access, else at the checkpoint; the close comment says which).
- [ ] `argc e2e doctor` runs the suite with verbose logs; `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean; the close comment lists the fixtures and the `probes` helpers (for F9 and T4).

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

None new in this part (s3's unit tests cover the client and the classifiers with a fake transport). `tests/common_selftest.rs` gains `probes_write_the_exact_requests_the_detectors_send` (for each `probes` helper, the replay transport loaded from the scenario answers exactly the URL and method s3's request builders produce, by calling those builders in-process) and `fixture_method_writes_a_propfind_fixture`.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

Technical Approach §3 (`tests/doctor.rs::online_*`, `cargo test --test doctor online_`, or `argc e2e doctor` with verbose logs) and the fixtures of §2.

### Logging

Every scenario uses `TestLog`: one `log.step` per phase ("home", "answers", "diagnose", "fix", "remedy", "verify"); every command through `log.run`/`log.cmd`, so its argv, environment overrides (`OMADDONS_GITHUB_TOKEN` redacted by name, `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS`), exit, envelope, stderr events and the `net.log` lines it added are in `steps.jsonl` and `transcript.md`; the replay fixtures written for each step recorded with `log.json("answers", <method, url, status per fixture>)`; `log.tree` of `<config>`, `<state>` without `doctor/` and `net.log`, and each client dir before the first command, and `log.assert_unchanged` wherever a scenario asserts nothing changed (the `net.log` line count is asserted separately, since `--online` appends to it). The live probe logs each `net.log` line and finding with `log.note`. A failure prints the transcript path and the last 20 steps.

### Checkpoint-only

`OMADDONS_LIVE=1 cargo test --test live_probes -- --ignored doctor_online_probes_the_real_hosts` (H6 runs it within §11.3 step 2.8, `OMADDONS_LIVE=1 cargo test --test live_probes -- --ignored`). Without `OMADDONS_LIVE=1` it prints `SKIP doctor_online_probes_the_real_hosts: OMADDONS_LIVE is not 1` and fails unless `OMADDONS_ALLOW_SKIP` names it; it is not one of §3.2's pre-accepted skips, so a checkpoint `SKIP` of it is an unmet criterion.

## Considerations

- **Never the real network in the gate.** Every online scenario runs on a `Home`; a missing fixture shows up as `unanswered` (an `internal` replay error), which the request-count assertions catch, never as a real request.
- **The deadline scenario sleeps 600 ms** once; it is the only slow scenario here.
- **Two `/rate_limit` requests** in a plain `doctor --online` are by design (each GitHub row sends its own).
- **Hot spots:** `tests/doctor.rs` is E3's suite (append scenarios, edit only the exit table's rows); `tests/doctor/fixtures/mod.rs` and `tests/common/doctor.rs` are shared with every catalog leaf; `tests/common/http.rs` gains one function.
- **The live probe's network:** five requests to public hosts, the same kind the existing live probes make.

## Dependencies

- **Parent:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.7.
- **Before it:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.7.3 (the network rows and the probe client). It is blocked by T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`) at filing, because it writes `TestLog` scenarios.
- **Beside it:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.7.4 (the widget and credential suite; it shares `fixtures/mod.rs`, `tests/common/doctor.rs` and the `plant::credential_file_mode` helper, which this part reuses in scenarios 3 and 10: if s4 has not landed, add that helper here).
- **After it:** nothing inside the leaf; F9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`) and T4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4`) reuse the fixtures, and H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`) runs the live probe.

- [ ] Every `online_*` scenario of Technical Approach §3 passes in the gate: no request without `--online`; `online_required` (exit 6) for an online-only `doctor --only` and `doctor fix --only`, its fix run; exactly one request per check (one per probed source for `source-unreachable`), each `doctor-probe` on an always-allowlisted host; each row's findings from recorded answers; `unanswered` and the deadline as `check-incomplete`, never clean; no false positive on the realistic home.

It was run here once and passed: exactly five `doctor-probe` lines, one each to `api.github.com`, `github.com`, `api.mmoui.com`, `api.tukui.org` and `repos.wowace.com`, every source answered, no findings.

**Decided:**

title: `status` on the registry
description:
## How to work this bead

This bead is worked through its 5 subtasks, listed below in work order. Claim a subtask, not this bead (`br ready --parent omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.8` lists the ready ones). The agent that closes the last open subtask then verifies every acceptance criterion of this bead (they are the leaf's, not any one subtask's), and closes this bead with `br close omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.8 --reason "done: <evidence> · found: <ids>"`. Until this bead is closed, every bead it blocks stays blocked.

1. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.8.1 `status` takes every issue from the registry, through a view seeded with what it already read: the seeded `DoctorView`, the shared detector loop (tiers, budgets, isolation), the drift memo, the assignment of findings to clients and to the machine, the machine issues in the human view, and README's `status` section and doctor-table status column.
2. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.8.2 Issues carry `auto_fixable`, `explain` and the doctor's own remediation: the two new keys, the doctor-fix remediations of fixer-backed findings, the human line of a forced repair, the widget's `--force` guard, and the re-accepted snapshots.
3. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.8.3 `status --check` and `needs_attention` also fail on any P0 or P1 issue: the attention rule, the `--check` fix taken from the most urgent issue, and README's `--check` sentences.
4. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.8.4 E2E: `status` and `doctor` agree on every fixture, and every remediation and explain command runs: the agreement suite, the purity and privacy checks, isolation, `--deep`, the contract rows, `tests/contract/recommendations.rs`, and E8's status case enabled.
5. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.8.5 Tests: `status --cached` stays under 5 ms with the cached tier: the release-build budget on M3's realistic perf home plus a doctor run directory, 200 stored plans and the installed skills, and the per-detector cost report.

s1 comes first. s2 and s5 each need only s1; s3 needs s2 (its `--check` fix and its snapshots carry s2's keys); s4 needs s2 and s3. s5 can run beside s2, s3 and s4; the agent that closes the last subtask runs s5's perf test once more on the final code.

**Size M, one closure.** The five parts split the work so each commit passes the gate on its own; the leaf closes only when all of them are done, so no dependent (G2, H1, F9, T4) ever sees `status` half on the registry.

## Background

**What this is.** `omaddons status` is the first call an agent makes and the only call the bar widget makes (`status --cached -v`, `omarchy/Model.js:100`; `status -v` when the panel opens, `:101`). Its `issues[]` today are computed by `status`'s own code from its attention reasons and drift: seven published failure-mode ids, mapped one by one (`src/app/issues.rs:95-208`). M4's doctor declares every failure mode once, in one registry, with a tier per row (M4-D29). This bead puts `status` on that registry: `status --cached` reports every `cached` row's findings, plain `status` every `cached` and `quick` row's, each mapped to `status`'s `Issue` with two new keys, `auto_fixable` and `explain`, and the doctor's own remediation (`omaddons doctor fix --only <fm> [-t <id>]` for an auto-fixable finding). `status --check` also fails on any P0 or P1 issue. After it, `status` and `doctor` cannot disagree about what is wrong, because there is one implementation of every check, and the widget's Issues view (G2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.2`) can offer a previewed repair for exactly the rows the doctor can fix.

**What is true today** (verified at `c0ab5e9`; E1, F1 and others edit `src/app/status.rs` and `src/app/issues.rs` before this bead, so find the code by name, not by line):

- **`status`'s flow** (`src/app/status.rs:609-952`): the discovery mode (`NoScan` for `--cached`, else `Full`, `:610-614`) and `World::load_with(ctx, mode)?` (`:615`); `journal::pending` and `probe_global` (`:627-628`); a per-client loop that loads the record (`load_record`, fail closed), builds the inventory, computes drift once in the mode of the flags (`Presence` for `--cached`, `Deep` for `--deep`, else `Stat`, `:653-659`; the report `:717-719`), and builds `attention` (`:704-733`); the missing clients' loop (`:839-883`); `issues_for` per client (`:884-892`); the widget read (`:895`) and the machine issues (`:906-909`); recommendations and the `--check` fix (`:911-919`); `needs_attention` (`:926`: attention or an unattributed journal); `summary` (`:927`).
- **Plain `status` writes the discovery cache.** `World::load_with` with `DiscoveryMode::Full` writes `<cache>/discovery.json` through an untracked, derived-data session whenever the cache changed (`src/discover/cache.rs:278-287`, `write_cache` `:300-311`); `NoScan` never writes it (`:282`). `status --cached` relies on that cache (without one it parses only the registered roots and recommends a full `status`, README `:725`). "`status` never writes" has always meant: after the cache is warm, nothing changes (`tests/status.rs:153-214` warms it before hashing `<state>`, `<cache>` and both client dirs).
- **A broken `config.toml` or `registry.json` fails every world** (`src/app/world.rs:1-4`, `load_with` `:65-78`): `Config::load` returns `state_corrupt` with `details {path, line, column}` and the message `<path> line L, column C: <parser message>` for a TOML error (`src/state/config.rs:439-463`, `corrupt` `:772-783`), `state_corrupt` with `details {path, line, column: 1, key}` for an invalid value (`invalid`, `:799-811`), and `io` with `details {path}` for a file it cannot read (`Error::io`, `src/error.rs:574-577`). The widget renders a failed `status` as its reason: "A failed status says why (a broken config.toml, a corrupt state file), never \"no clients found\"" (`omarchy/Service.qml:599-606`).
- **The human view prints no machine issue.** It prints each client's issue lines (`  P2 <title> → <remediation>`, `status.rs:418-424`) and the bar widget's own line (`:442-444`), but never `data.issues` (`:354-465`), so an unattributed journal's P0 issue appears only in JSON.
- **The issue shape** is `Issue {id, severity, title, addon, remediation}` with `Remediation {command: Option<String>, argv: Option<Vec<String>>, destructive}` (`src/app/issues.rs:53-90`), ranked by `(severity, id, addon)` (`:206`). `summary.issues` is a `SeverityCounts` over every client's issues and the machine's (`status.rs:1075-1112`, `issues.rs:211-239`); `summary.state` is `attention` on any P0 or P1 issue (`status.rs:1115-1125`).
- **`status --check`** fails with `check_failed` (exit 6, data kept) exactly when `needs_attention` (`status.rs:341-352`), with the first attention item's message and fix (`attention_fixes`, `:1308-1369`).
- **`status --deep`** re-hashes every managed file, and its `drift[]` and its issues come from that one deep report (`:653-659`, `:717-735`).
- **The widget runs an issue's remediation on Enter** through its argv classifier, a destructive path through the confirm dialog (`omarchy/views/IssuesView.qml:8-10`; `Model.cliAction`, `omarchy/Model.js:679-687`, `issueOf` `:689-700`). The classifier refuses only presentation flags (`WIDGET_FLAGS`, `Model.js:184`); nothing refuses `--force`.
- **`tests/contract/recommendations.rs:304-326`** runs every client issue's remediation argv on a fresh home and asserts it clears its issue (a look excepted); it never runs a machine issue's (`data.issues`) remediation.
- **The perf budget.** `tests/perf.rs:435-669`, `status_cached_stays_under_5_ms_with_a_realistic_memo` (release, ignored): one client with 100 records, a 200-entry release memo, 16 accounts with a 2 MB BugGrabber file each, 200 backups and the bar widget installed; median of 21 runs of the binary under 5 ms, process start included. `QUICK_DETECTOR_BUDGET` is 5 ms (`src/limits.rs:62`).
- **The stable ids.** README calls the seven published ids "stable across releases" (`README.md:750`); `status`'s issue table is `README.md:752-760`.

**Milestone goals served:**

- **G-M4-4 (diagnosable and repairable):** "`status` and `doctor` never disagree about what is wrong." This bead removes the second implementation: `status`'s issues are the registry's findings.
- **G-M4-1 (self-describing):** "An agent with no prior knowledge learns everything it needs from the binary itself, in at most three calls: `omaddons capabilities --json`, `omaddons robot-docs guide`, `omaddons status --json`." Every issue now says whether it can be repaired automatically (`auto_fixable`) and how to read its evidence (`explain`), so the third call leads straight to the doctor.
- **G-M4-6 (no new risk to the engine's guarantees):** `status` still writes nothing, takes no lock and makes no request; it builds no run directory.
- **G-M4-3, indirectly:** the widget never runs a forced repair from an issue row (Technical Approach §9).

**Checkpoint criteria this bead is responsible for:**

- **12. `status` and `doctor` agree, and `status` stays fast.** "`status`'s issues come from the doctor registry's `cached` and `quick` tiers. For every fixture, the issue ids `status` reports equal the doctor findings of those tiers. `status --cached` stays under 5 ms (median of 21, release build, on M3's realistic perf home plus one doctor run directory and 200 stored plans)." All of it is this bead's.
- **9, property 14 (in part):** F9's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`, the safety harness) status-agreement property runs this bead's mapping over every fixture again; this bead makes it pass first.
- **8 (in part):** "The Issues view runs an auto-fixable finding's repair with a preview. It never runs a set-aside, `doctor gc`, or any argv with `--force`." This bead supplies `auto_fixable` and `explain`, and keeps the current widget from running a forced repair until G2 builds the preview.
- **17 (in part):** "The perf budgets (`tests/perf.rs`) pass": this bead's `status --cached` budget is one of them.

**The decisions that shape it** (full text in the decision-log comments on the milestone epic `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`):

- **M4-D29: one detector registry serves `doctor`, `doctor health` and `status`, by tier.** `src/doctor/registry.rs` declares every failure mode once, each with a tier (`cached`, `quick`, `default` or `deep`), `online_required`, `estimated_cost_ms`, `requires` (the view layers it reads), a pure detector, an optional fixer and a manual remediation builder. What runs where: `status --cached` runs `cached`; `status` runs `cached` and `quick`; `doctor --quick` and `doctor health` run `cached` and `quick`; `doctor` every tier but `deep`; `doctor --include-deep` every tier. "`app::issues` keeps its wire shape. Its 7 ids move into the registry unchanged, and `status`'s issues become the registry's findings mapped to `Issue`." Why: two implementations of "is this broken?" would drift; tiers are how `status --cached` keeps its 5 ms: a `cached` detector may read only what `status --cached` reads today plus single-file stats. **Rejected:** (i) `status` calling `doctor` as a subprocess (costly, and recursive for the widget); (ii) keeping `status`'s issue code separate and syncing ids by test (two implementations of every check).
- **M4-D53: `status` issues gain two keys, and the old fixes point at the doctor.** `targets[].issues[]` and `data.issues[]` gain `auto_fixable` (bool) and `explain` (`{command, argv}`), both additive. An auto-fixable finding's remediation becomes `omaddons doctor fix --only <fm> [-t <id>]`; a manual one keeps its command, or prose. `status`'s journal remediation stops promising "any change command" for the manual states (done by F1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1`, journal and lock detectors); kept here). `status --check` keeps failing on every existing attention reason, and also fails on any P0 or P1 issue (additive). `error::internal_fix_for` and `store::status_fix` move to the doctor too, which is E10's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.10`, the old fixes point at the doctor) part of this decision, not this bead's. Why: the vision ("internal errors use `omaddons doctor`"); the widget's Issues view needs to know what it can fix; the manual states' old advice was false. **Rejected:** a new `status` field per finding kind (one `issues[]` list is the shape the widget and agents already read).
- **M4-D43: the doctor loads the world tolerantly and says what it skipped.** Each layer loads separately; a detector whose required layer is unavailable is listed in `skipped`, never silently dropped and never reported clean; every detector runs under a `Budget` (a deadline and an entry counter), and one cut short returns an `incomplete` record that becomes `fm-state_files-check-incomplete`. **Rejected:** (i) running detectors with defaults in place of a broken layer ("it reports findings about a config the user does not have"); (ii) treating truncation as a warning on a healthy run.
- **M4-D30: instance keys are resource-specific and stable; labels are separate.** A finding's `instance` (`<fm-id>@<target key | machine>[:<discriminator>]`) never changes with a rename; `label` is display only. `status`'s `Issue` has no instance key; this bead uses it only as the last sort key, so equal issues keep a stable order.
- **M4-D38 and M4-D39: a forced repair is never auto-fixable, and a fixer that changes user content ships disabled.** The set-aside of the stuck journal states (`needs_force`) runs only with `--only <fm> --force --yes`; "a dialog's Yes is too easy", so the widget never runs one. A disabled fixer runs only with an explicit `--only`. Both are `auto_fixable: false`.
- **M4-D18: determinism per command path, volatile keys declared.** `status`'s output is deterministic for an unchanged home; this bead adds no volatile key.
- **M4-D55: the contract's rules hold from slice 1.** New keys are added, never renamed; every new shape passes A3's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`, schemas and live validation) rule test with no allowlist line.

**Facts this bead relies on** (from the beads that block it, as their bead texts specify; use the names that are on `main`, and where a name differs, adapt the call, not the behaviour):

- From E1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`, the failure-mode registry and finding model): `FAILURE_MODES` (sorted by id), `Tier` (ordered `cached < quick < default < deep`; E3 adds `runtime`, never selected by a tier filter), `Layer`, `FailureMode::finding(obs)` and `FailureMode::remediation`, `Finding {id, instance, label, severity, subsystem, title, confidence, target: Option<{id, key}>, addon, folder, evidence, remediation}`, the doctor's `Remediation {command, argv, explain_command, explain_argv, auto_fixable, needs_force, estimated_actions, destructive}`, `doctor::detect(view, selection, max_tier)`, `issues::issue_of`, `for_target`, `for_machine`, `issues::STATUS_FAILURE_MODES` (the rows `status` runs until this bead), and the status-facts bridge (`src/doctor/facts.rs`, `StatusFacts`, `DoctorView::from_status_facts`) that "F8 removes". E1's s1 characterization snapshots pin `status`'s issue JSON and human lines.
- From E2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.2`, the tolerant view): `DoctorView` with lazily loaded layers (Config, Registry, Discovery, Records, Inventory, Journals, Lock, History, Caches, Widget, Skill, Credentials), `ViewOptions { discovery: Scan | Cached }` (the view's own discovery never writes the cache: `DiscoveryMode::FullNoWrite` or `NoScan`), `view.world()`, `view.records()`, `loaded_layers()`, `Selection::parse(target, only, skip, argv)` with `-t` scope (machine findings always in scope), `partition(view, selection, rows, tiers)`, `target_skips`, `Skipped {id, reason, target}`. ### 3. The seeded view (`src/doctor/view.rs`, s1)

`status` keeps loading its own world with `World::load_with(ctx, mode)` (`Full` writes the discovery cache `status --cached` reads; `NoScan` for `--cached`), and hands the view what it has already read, so nothing is discovered or read twice and `status`'s own fields and its issues come from the same reads:

```rust
// src/doctor/view.rs (F8)
pub struct Seed {
    /// status's world (its discovery: Full or NoScan), shared: the view holds it behind Rc,
    /// so status keeps its own handle.
    pub world: Rc<World>,
    /// F1's Journals::read, as status called it (its own running state for sv_writable).
    pub journals: Journals,
    /// status's probe_global.
    pub lock: LockState,
    /// status's omarchy_status::widget read.
    pub widget: Option<WidgetInfo>,
    /// The drift report status computed per registered client, in its mode.
    pub drift: BTreeMap<TargetKey, (DriftMode, DriftReport)>,
}
impl DoctorView {
    /// A view whose Discovery, Journals, Lock and Widget layers are Available from the
    /// start, holding exactly these values; every other layer loads lazily as `load_at`'s do.
    pub fn seeded(opts: ViewOptions, seed: Seed) -> DoctorView;
    /// The drift report of a registered client in at least `mode`, computed once per
    /// client: a report of a stronger mode answers a weaker request (Presence < Stat < Deep).
    /// `None` when the client is not discovered or its record is unavailable.
    pub fn drift(&self, key: TargetKey, mode: DriftMode) -> Option<Rc<DriftReport>>;
}
```

- **The world behind `Rc`.** E2's Discovery layer holds `Discovered { world, inventories }`; it becomes `Rc<World>` (the view is single-threaded, E2). `view.world()` keeps returning `Option<&World>`. `status` uses `world` through its own `Rc` everywhere it does today. Decided while writing this bead: sharing by `Rc` rather than moving the world into the view, because `status` reads the world in a dozen places after the view exists, and an accessor that cannot fail is not available without `expect`, which the lints forbid.
- **What is not seeded.** Config, Registry and Records load lazily, as E2 built them: each is one bounded read and decode of a file `status` has just read successfully, so they load without failure in practice and cost little next to discovery. Decided while writing this bead: seed only what is costly to repeat (discovery, which for plain `status` is a full scan) or what must equal `status`'s own fields (journals and lock: `data.journal` and attention; the widget: `data.widget`; drift: `drift[]`). If s5's budget is missed, seeding Records from `status`'s loaded records is the first fallback (§Considerations).
- **The GitHub token.** A world from `World::load_with` carries the resolved token (`world.rs:141`), which the view's own world never does (E2). No `cached` or `quick` row makes a request (E1's invariant 6), and no detector may read `world.github_token`; the doc comment of `seeded` says so.
- **The drift memo.** `RefCell<BTreeMap<TargetKey, (DriftMode, Rc<DriftReport>)>>`. A request for mode `m` is served by a stored report of mode `≥ m`; otherwise the view computes `app::drift::report(paths, target, record, m)` from the Discovery and Records layers, stores it (replacing a weaker one) and returns it. `Seed.drift` fills it before any detector runs. `record-folder-missing` asks for `Presence`, `managed-files-modified` for `Stat` (F5's deep re-hash under `--include-deep` asks for `Deep`); if F3 or F5 already memoized drift, use theirs and seed it. Consequences: plain `status` computes each client's drift once (not three times); `status --deep`'s seeded `Deep` report answers `managed-files-modified`, so `--deep`'s issues are deep exactly as today; `drift[]` and the drift issues can never disagree within one run. The memo relies on one fact, held by a unit test: a folder is `Missing` in a stronger mode's report exactly when it is in the `Presence` report.
- **Nothing in the view writes** (E2's rule). Seeding adds no write path; `seeded` takes values, not paths to write.

### 4. The shared detector loop (`src/doctor/mod.rs`, s1)

```rust
pub struct Detection {
    pub findings: Vec<Finding>,   // the rows' findings, plus detector-crashed and check-incomplete
    pub skipped: Vec<Skipped>,    // E2's partition and target_skips
}
pub fn detect(view: &DoctorView, selection: &Selection, tiers: &[Tier]) -> Result<Detection>;
/// The same loop over an explicit row slice (doc-hidden; for synthetic rows in unit tests
/// and for the per-detector timing in tests/perf.rs).
#[doc(hidden)]
pub fn detect_rows(view: &DoctorView, selection: &Selection, rows: &[FailureMode], tiers: &[Tier]) -> Result<Detection>;
```

One loop, used by `status` and by E3's `Runtime::diagnose` (which keeps its run directory, its timing and its report around the call). For each row of `failure_modes()` that `selection.includes` and whose tier is in `tiers`, in registry order (so a failpoint's `@N` counts the same everywhere):

1. `partition` (E2): a row whose `requires` names an unavailable layer is `skipped`, never run and never reported clean;
2. force the row's layers, start `Budget::for_tier(row.tier)`, hit `doctor.detector.panic`, and call the detector inside `catch_unwind(AssertUnwindSafe(…))` (E3's steps 1–5, moved, not rewritten);
3. a panic → one `fm-state_files-detector-crashed` finding (P1, machine, `evidence {detector, location}` from `cli::take_caught_panic()`, payload dropped); an `incomplete` → one `fm-state_files-check-incomplete` finding (P3, machine);
4. each observation → `row.finding(obs)`; for a row with a fixer, the doctor's remediation refinement (E6's `remediation_for`, Technical Approach §6), so every caller of `detect` gets the same remediation;
5. after the loop, `target_skips`.

If E3 already factored this loop into a free function, `detect` is that function. If E6 applies `remediation_for` outside it, move the call inside, so no caller can skip it. Decided while writing this bead: one loop, because two loops (the runtime's and `status`'s) are the second implementation M4-D29 rejects, and the agreement test would then be testing two copies of the same code. `Runtime::diagnose`'s observable behaviour, its tests and E3's snapshots stay unchanged.

**Budgets in `status`.** Each `cached` and `quick` row gets `Budget::for_tier` (5 ms, scaled ×20 in debug builds), never a `--budget` share (`status` has no `--budget`). The per-row budget guards against a runaway walk; the 5 ms total of `status --cached` is s5's perf test, not a run-time limit.

### 5. `status::run`, step by step (s1)

1. Arguments and `World::load_with(ctx, mode)?`, unchanged (its refusals, notes and warnings unchanged); then `let world = Rc::new(world)`.
2. Everything `status` computes per client and for the missing clients, unchanged, except that each registered client's drift report is kept for the seed (`(drift_mode, report)` by key).
3. The widget read moves above the view (E1 already moved it).
4. `let view = DoctorView::seeded(ViewOptions { discovery: if args.cached { Cached } else { Scan }, ..Default::default() }, Seed { world: Rc::clone(&world), journals, lock, widget: widget.clone(), drift })`.
5. `let selection = Selection::parse(ctx.target.as_deref(), &[], &[], &[])?`: `status`'s `-t` becomes the doctor's `-t`, so target-scoped rows run only for the selected client. `status`'s own `world.select_many(ctx)` already ran in step 2, so its refusals (`target_not_found`, `target_ambiguous`, a vanished `-t`) are unchanged and come first.
6. `let found = doctor::detect(&view, &selection, status_tiers(&args))?`, where `status_tiers` is `[Cached]` with `--cached`, else `[Cached, Quick]`.
7. **Assign** (`issues::assign(&found.findings, &listed, scoped)`, replacing `for_target`/`for_machine`'s callers): a finding whose `target.key` is a client `status` lists (a discovered registered client, or a missing one) goes to that client's `issues`; a machine finding (`target: null`) to `data.issues`; a finding on a key `status` does not list goes to `data.issues` without `-t` and is dropped with `-t` (F1's rule, now for every row). Within a list: F1's journal grouping (one issue per client and journal row, the plural title for several), then each other finding its own issue, sorted by `(severity, id, addon)` and then by the first finding's `instance` (decided while writing this bead: the instance key as the last sort key, never on the wire, so two issues of one row and scope, such as two skill directories, keep a stable order, M4-D18).
8. Attention, recommendations, `summary` and `last_change`, as today (journal attention from the findings of rows 1–9, F1). `needs_attention` and the `--check` fix: Technical Approach §7 (s3).
9. **`-v` notes for skipped rows.** Each `Skipped` becomes a debug note `status: <fm id> not checked (<reason>)`, with `on <target id>` for a per-client skip, in `StatusOutcome.notes` (the existing `-v` log lines). Decided while writing this bead: no data key and no issue for a skipped row (the plan's §8.1 rule 2: detail behind `-v`). In `status` a layer can be unavailable only where `status`'s own reads either already refused (a record, the journal directory, the config, the registry) or already say so (a history that cannot be read makes `last_change_state: unknown`), or for a file `status` does not otherwise read (`<cache>/plans/`), and `doctor` lists every skip in `skipped[]`.
10. Delete what the bridge left: `issues::STATUS_FAILURE_MODES`, `src/doctor/facts.rs` (`StatusFacts`, `TargetFacts`, `MachineFacts`, `DoctorView::from_status_facts`), any direct call of a rule function from `status.rs` (E2's form), and E1's `#[cfg(test)] mod legacy` oracle with its differential proptest if they are still there: the oracle describes the seven-row `status` that F1 and this bead replace, and E1's characterization snapshots stay as the regression guard.

**The human view** (decided while writing this bead, following the plan's §4.4 example): after every client's block (its row, issue lines, Lua errors, backups and any-flavor line), each machine issue prints as `  <P> <title> → <remediation>`, in `data.issues`'s order, except `fm-plugins-widget-version-drift`, whose `bar widget: from another omaddons build → omaddons omarchy install` line stays where it is (one line per fact). With no client found, the machine lines follow the "No WoW client found" line. Example:

…                                    (each client's row and lines, as today)

…                                    (drift lines, the widget line, the last change, Next:, as today)

### 6. The issue shape (s2)

```rust
// src/app/issues.rs
pub struct Issue {
    pub id: &'static str,
    pub severity: Severity,
    pub title: String,
    pub addon: Option<String>,
    pub remediation: Remediation,       // {command, argv, destructive}, unchanged shape
    /// `omaddons doctor fix --only <id> [-t <client>]` repairs it, previewed, with no force.
    pub auto_fixable: bool,
    /// The command that shows this issue's evidence and what its repair does.
    pub explain: ExplainCommand,
}
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, JsonSchema)]
pub struct ExplainCommand { pub command: String, pub argv: Vec<String> }
```

Field order is A.11's (deterministic, not contract: M4-D56). `ExplainCommand`'s schema name is distinct from every doctor type (E3's `ExplainReport`, E1's `DoctorRemediation`).

**The mapping rule** (`issue_of(&Finding) -> Issue`): every field comes from the finding the doctor reports for the same state, never from `status`'s own code:

- `remediation` = `{command: Some(r.command), argv: r.argv, destructive: r.destructive}` of the finding's doctor remediation, which for a fixer-backed row is E6's `remediation_for` (Technical Approach §4, step 4). So: an auto-fixable finding → `omaddons doctor fix --only <fm> [-t <id>]` (`-t` with the client's id for a client's finding); a forced one (F2's set-aside) → the same plus `--force --yes`; a manual one → its builder's command (the reinstall hint, `targets rm`, `list -v`, `omarchy install`, …) or its prose, exactly as before.
- `auto_fixable` = the finding's `remediation.auto_fixable` (enabled fixer, no force, and the detector marked the instance fixable).
- `explain` = `{command: r.explain_command, argv: r.explain_argv}`: `omaddons doctor explain <fm> [-t <id>]` (E1's builder, which F1 made omit `-t` for a client neither registered nor with a record).
- **A group of journal findings** (F1's one issue per client and row): `auto_fixable` only when every finding of the group is; `remediation` the first finding's when they are all auto-fixable, else the first non-auto-fixable finding's; `explain` the row's for that client (it lists every instance). Decided while writing this bead: "all", so a one-key Fix never leaves part of what the row shows unrepaired.
- **`status` never calls a fixer's `plan`.** A plan may render the guide (F10's rewrite) or list directories, which the `cached` tier forbids, and `status`'s `Issue` carries no `estimated_actions`. If `remediation_for` plans to count `estimated_actions`, split it: a plan-free part (command, argv, `auto_fixable`, `needs_force`, `destructive`) that `detect` applies, and the count the runtime adds afterwards in its reports. A unit test with a row whose `plan` panics holds this.

### 7. `--check`, `needs_attention` and `summary.issues` (s3)

- **The rule:** `needs_attention` = an existing attention reason on any listed client, or the machine's unattributed journal (both as today), **or any P0 or P1 issue** in any client's `issues` or in `data.issues`. `status --check` fails with `check_failed` (exit 6, data and `partial` kept, `details {}`) exactly when `needs_attention` is true. Decided while writing this bead: widen `needs_attention` itself rather than add a second condition beside it, so the data says why `--check` failed, `needs_attention` agrees with `summary.state: attention`, and `assertion_failure` keeps its one test (`status.rs:341-352`). It is an additive widening of an existing key's meaning (M4-D53 calls the `--check` change additive), recorded in the close comment.
- **New cases** (the attention reasons already cover journals, newer records, missing folders, degraded addons, modified files and missing clients): `fm-permissions-addons-dir-not-writable` (P1), `fm-permissions-state-dir-not-writable` (P0), a newer files index or registry (`state-version-newer` instances not on a record, P0), and a `detector-crashed` finding (P1). P2 and P3 issues alone (`credential-file-mode`, `lock-held-long`, `skill-version-drift`, `orphan-temp-file`, …) never fail `--check`.
- **The `--check` message and fix**: the first attention item's, exactly as today (and F1's journal arm), when there is one; else the machine's unattributed journal's (F1's); else the most urgent P0/P1 issue's, ordered by severity, then the listed clients in `status`'s order with the machine last, then id: message `<client id>: <title>` for a client's issue, `<title>` for a machine one; fix `Suggestion::command(argv)` when the issue's remediation has an argv, else `Suggestion::text(<its prose>)`. Prose remediations already name no runnable omaddons command (common rule 8).
- **`summary.issues`** counts every issue `status` lists, per client and the machine's, each once: a group of journal findings is one issue. No code change beyond the new issues flowing through `summary`; a unit test pins it.

### 8. A broken `config.toml` or `registry.json`: `status` keeps refusing (decided while writing this bead)

`status` keeps refusing a `config.toml` or a `registry.json` it cannot load, with today's error: `state_corrupt` (a parse error or an invalid value), `state_too_new` (a newer registry it cannot decode) or `io` (a file it cannot read), each with `details.path`. A parse error's message and `details {path, line, column}` hold exactly what `fm-configs-config-parse-error`'s evidence holds.

Why: every fact `status` reports beyond its issues is computed from that config and registry (the clients found under `extra_roots` and manual roots, their families after `[targets]` overrides, update staleness from `check_interval_hours`, `auto_backup`, each client's identity). Building them on defaults is exactly what M4-D43 rejected for the doctor ("findings about a config the user does not have"), and the widget already renders a failed `status` as its reason (`omarchy/Service.qml:599-606`). So Appendix B row 19's status column, `C (machine)`, is met by the refusal: `status --cached` and `status` report the broken config, as their error, at the same path, line and column the doctor's finding cites, and the agreement test (§Test Plan) holds `status` to that. README's doctor table writes "refuses" in that row's status column. **Rejected:** (i) a degraded `status` on built-in defaults (M4-D43's (i)); (ii) a `status` with `targets: []` and only machine issues, which the human view and the widget would read as "no clients found"; (iii) carrying `data` on the error, which only `check_failed` may (README `:1806`).

### 13. What not to do

- Do not compute an issue in `status`'s own code: every issue is a registry finding (M4-D29's rejected (ii)).

- Do not run a `default`, `deep`, online or runtime-selected row, and do not call a fixer's `plan` from `status`.
- Do not create a run directory, take the lock, or make a request from `status`.
- Do not show evidence in `status`: `Issue` has no evidence key (M4-D42 keeps evidence content-free; `explain` shows it).

- **Risk 4 (the plan's risk register): `status --cached` slows past 5 ms with the cached tier (likelihood M, impact M; owner: this bead).** Mitigations: the tier contracts (a `cached` row reads only what `status --cached` reads, plus single-file stats and at most `SKILL_DIRS_MAX` skill files); the seeded view (no second discovery, no repeated drift, journals, lock or widget read); the perf test with a doctor run directory, 200 plans and the skills present; `each_cached_detector_reports_its_cost` to find the culprit. **The fallback, in order** (decided while writing this bead): seed Records from `status`'s own loads; then move the costliest `cached` row to `quick` (the plan's fallback: an Appendix B tier change, recorded in the close comment with its Appendix B line, README's doctor-table status column C → Q, and the owning leaf's tests updated); never raise the budget.
- **Risk 3: doctor false positives on real homes erode trust (M, M).** Every cheap finding now reaches the owner's bar, and a P0 or P1 one turns it urgent. Mitigations: each F leaf's no-false-positive test; this bead's agreement on the clean realistic home; H6's review of every real-home finding.
- **The window before G2.** Technical Approach §9's `--force` refusal; auto-fixable repairs may run on Enter until G2 adds the preview, as reinstalls do today, each undoable.
- **Two implementations by the back door.** `status` keeps computing `attention[]` and `drift[]` (the plan keeps them), from the same reads it seeds into the view; scenario 9 and the drift memo keep them in step with the issues.
- **Hot spots** (§10.5 of the plan): `src/app/status.rs` and `src/app/issues.rs` are **E1 → F1 → F8**, then E10 and G1 rebase (if E10 landed first, rebase onto it; G1 decided not to touch `status.rs`). `src/doctor/view.rs`, `mod.rs` and the detectors are shared by E1–E8, F1–F7 and F10: add the seed and the memo, move the loop, do not reorder registry rows. `omarchy/Model.js` is G1 → G2: one rule in `cliAction`. `tests/contract/matrix.rs` and snapshots: append rows. README: only `### status`, the doctor table's status column and the `check_failed` row.
- **Why size M and five parts.** The view and the loop (s1), the shape (s2) and `--check` (s3) are separate surfaces that each pass the gate alone; the agreement suite (s4) and the budget (s5) are separate test work. The detectors themselves are the F leaves', so this bead adds no failure mode.
- **What could go wrong, and how to notice.** A row silently missing from `status` (a tier filter off by one, a skipped layer): `detect_runs_the_rows_of_its_tiers` and the agreement suite. A remediation that differs between `status` and `doctor`: the agreement suite's per-issue comparison. A second discovery creeping back: `a_seeded_view_holds_the_seeded_world`. A `--cached` run touching History, Caches or Inventory: the loaded-layers acceptance item. A detector that plans or walks under `status --cached`: `status_never_plans_a_fixer` and the perf report.
- **Compatibility.** Additive keys; older consumers ignore them. The M3 widget build sees new issues in its list; it does not know the `doctor` paths (its classifier says `unknown_path`), so it runs none of them. `status --check` may now fail where it passed (a P0 or P1 issue without an attention reason): documented, recorded with a compatibility note, as M4-D53 decided. No persisted file changes, so older builds read nothing new.
- **Privacy.** `status` shows titles and argv, never evidence; detectors' titles are content-free (each F leaf's rule); the `WTF/` fixtures are checked with `assert_private_all`.
- **Performance of plain `status`.** No budget; one drift pass per client (the memo), plus the `quick` rows' bounded listings (each under `QUICK_DETECTOR_BUDGET`).
- **Decided defaults (§8.1 of the plan):** existing keys reused (`remediation`, `check_failed`, `needs_attention`); additive JSON; stable order (severity, id, addon, instance); no network; fail closed (a broken config or registry is still refused; a skipped check is never clean); never ask the owner.
