title: Tests: concurrent fixers, cross-failure-mode pairs, the conflicting pair and the lock file
description:
Part 5 of 6 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9 (The safety harness). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

F9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`) is the doctor's safety harness: every real fixture and fixer through fourteen properties in every gate, for §3.2 criterion 9 and G-M4-4. Part 1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9.1`) built the runner (lanes, subject maps, doctor-run helpers, the pool).

**This part** runs the properties where fixers meet each other or the lock: 4 (two concurrent fixers serialize, and a fixer held past the lock timeout exits 5), 12 (the declared cross-failure-mode pairs fix together and undo together; the declared conflicting pair is refused), and 13 (no code path renames or deletes the global lock file). It is its own step because each needs a special home (a pair builder, two processes at once) or a source scan, and none needs parts 2–4.

The decisions it applies, restated:

- **M4-D45: concurrent fixers serialize and re-plan.** `doctor fix` plans without the lock, then takes it (`LOCK_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT`, 5 s, then exit 5 `locked`, the doctor's `concurrency_lost`). Under the lock it loads a fresh view, re-runs the planned failure modes' detectors and rebuilds the complete effect plan (findings resolved meanwhile drop out), compares `--if-match`, and only then runs the disclosed recoveries and the repair's primitives. The harness property: two concurrent fixers never interleave; the second takes 0 actions for what the first fixed, or exits 5 if the first held the lock past the timeout; the final state is healthy. *Why:* the lock is held for milliseconds and a second process waits up to 5 s, so serializing and re-planning is stronger than refusing. *Rejected:* a non-blocking lock in the doctor ("exactly one exits 5"), inconsistent with every other command.
- **M4-D62: fixes whose resource sets conflict are refused together.** A path resource is a file or a directory standing for its whole subtree; two overlap when one is the other or its ancestor; a rename touches its source and its destination; two sets conflict when one's writes overlap the other's reads or writes. Conflicting fixes are refused in PLANNING: `doctor_refused` (exit 4) with `details.reason: "fixer_conflict"`, both fixes in `details.fixes` and the overlapping resources in `details.resources`, including a quarantine of a directory against a write to its child. *Rejected:* exact-path comparison, which misses ancestors, descendants and rename destinations.
- **M4-D37:** a delegation's effect is ordinary recovery's, and `doctor undo` does not revert it.
- **Vision D23, the immutable lock file:** renaming or deleting the lock file would create a second lock on a new inode; only `src/fsx/lock.rs`, `src/fsx/scope.rs` and `src/state/paths.rs` may name it.

## Technical Approach

### Facts this part relies on

- `src/fsx/lock.rs:72` `GlobalLock::acquire(paths, command) -> Result<GlobalLockGuard>`; `tests/status.rs:412` holds the lock from a test process the same way; `common::http::paths(&env)` (`tests/common/http.rs:284`) gives the `Paths`.
- `src/fsx/lock.rs:415-453` `no_code_path_truncates_renames_or_unlinks_the_lock_file`: over `crate::source_scan::sources(src)` (`src/source_scan.rs:63`, every `.rs` under `src/`), production code with literals blanked (`production_code(text, Literals::Blank)`, `:26`) must name `lock_file` only in `src/fsx/lock.rs`, `src/fsx/scope.rs` and `src/state/paths.rs`, and `lock.rs` itself must not truncate, rename or prune. (The plan cites `lock.rs:414-439`; it drifted.) `src/fsx/scope.rs:1028` `the_lock_file_is_never_writable` refuses the lock path to every writer, `Doctor` included.
- `tests/common/pause.rs`: `Pause::new(root)`, `env()`, `reached(name)`, `resume(name)`; T1's `log.cmd(..).failpoints(spec).pause(&p).spawn()`, `Running::{pid, wait}`, `log.reached`, `log.resume`. Any failpoint name accepts `=pause` (`src/fsx/failpoint.rs:1-12`).
- E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`): `doctor.fix.planned`, a pause point at the end of the first PLANNING; `LOCK_LOST` reports exit 5 with `error.code: "locked"` and `details.holder {pid, command, age}`; `fixer_conflict`'s `details {fm, fixes: [{fm, instance}, {fm, instance}], resources}`. E5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`): `doctor.repair.prepared` is hit under the global lock after the `prepared` line.
- The fixtures of the pairs' rows: F1/F2's `fm-concurrency_primitives-journal-pending` (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1`, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.2`), F3's `fm-state_files-orphan-temp-file` (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.3`), F7's `fm-secrets-credential-file-mode` (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.7`), F10's `fm-plugins-skill-version-drift` (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.10`), F5's `fm-external_artifacts-nested-addon-folder` and `fm-external_artifacts-case-collision` (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.5`).
- The runner (part 1): `Lane::{build, build_many, restore}`, `SubjectMap`, `Bookkeeping`, `root_map`, `run::{fix, undo, diagnose, caps, assert_blast_radius, actions, repair_line}`, `lock_identity`, `pool::par_lanes`.

### 1. Concurrency (`tests/doctor/harness/props/concurrency.rs`, one `mod concurrency;` line)

#### 1.1 `two_concurrent_fixers_serialize`

For every fixer fixture (one lane each, restored per case, through the pool):

1. Two `Pause`s, `pa` and `pb`, under the lane directory.
2. Spawn A and B, each `doctor fix --only <id> [--force --yes] --json --progress json` with `failpoints("doctor.fix.planned=pause")` and its own pause (`log.cmd(..).pause(&pa).spawn()`).
3. `log.reached(&pa, "doctor.fix.planned")` and `log.reached(&pb, "doctor.fix.planned")`: both have planned before either takes the lock. Resume both; wait both.
4. Exactly one has `summary.actions_taken > 0` or a non-empty `delegated[]` (the winner); the other (the loser) exits 0, or 1 when only unfixable instances remain, with `actions_taken: 0` and `delegated: []`; neither exits 2, 3, 4 or 5.
5. The winner's `actions.jsonl` and the loser's touch disjoint paths (the loser's has none or does not exist); the winner's lines are in `seq` order with no gap; history holds one repair line (or none for a delegation) naming the winner's `tx`.
6. No `<state>/journal/*.repair.jsonl` remains; `doctor --json --only <id>` exits 0 (healthy); blast radius holds for the winner; the lock identity is unchanged.

#### 1.2 `a_fixer_waiting_past_the_lock_timeout_exits_5` (the forced variant)

For every fixer fixture, all cases started together (each waits about 5 s, so the test costs about 6 s of wall time, not 5 s per fixer):

- **A repair-making fixer:** spawn A with `failpoints("doctor.repair.prepared=pause")` (it pauses under the global lock, after its `prepared` line); `log.reached(&pa, "doctor.repair.prepared")`; spawn B with `doctor.fix.planned=pause`, reach and resume it; wait B: exit 5, `error.code: "locked"`, `state: "LOCK_LOST"`, `details.holder.pid` equal to `A.pid()` and `details.holder.command` the command A's lock records (`doctor fix`), `summary.actions_taken: 0`, no repair journal of B's own (only A's `<tx>.repair.jsonl` exists), B's wait between its resume and its exit at least `LOCK_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT` minus a small margin (logged, not tightly asserted); resume A; wait A: exit 0, repaired; `doctor --json --only <id>` exits 0.
- **A delegate-only fixer** (no repair transaction, so no `doctor.repair.prepared`), decided while writing this bead: the test process takes `GlobalLock::acquire(&paths, "harness")`; B (`doctor fix --only <id> --json`) exits 5 with `details.holder.command: "harness"` and nothing recovered (the planted journal still present, its tree unchanged); drop the guard; a new `doctor fix --only <id>` recovers it and exits 0.

### 2. The pairs (`tests/doctor/harness/pairs.rs` and `props/pairs.rs`, one `mod pairs;` line)

#### 2.1 The pair builders (`pairs.rs`)

```rust
pub struct Pair { pub label: &'static str, pub ids: [&'static str; 2], pub build: fn(&TestLog, &Home) }
pub fn declared() -> Vec<Pair>;
pub fn conflicting() -> Pair;
```

Each builder plants both states so they interact, deterministically, on a `Home::at(<lane>/home, &["wow", "wow_classic"])`, through the fixtures' own `corrupt` and planting helpers where they fit (decided while writing this bead):

| Label | Rows | Planting |
|---|---|---|
| `journal-pending+orphan-temp` | `fm-concurrency_primitives-journal-pending`, `fm-state_files-orphan-temp-file` | the orphan-temp fixture's `corrupt`; one more stale temp file `<retail meta>/.omaddons-pair` (mtime three hours back), outside the stage and snapshot directories; then the journal-pending fixture's `corrupt` **last** (any later change on retail would recover its journal first) |
| `credential-mode+skill-drift` | `fm-secrets-credential-file-mode`, `fm-plugins-skill-version-drift` | both fixtures' `corrupt` (the token at 0644; a drifted skill): one repair with a chmod and a write |
| `nested+case-collision` | `fm-external_artifacts-nested-addon-folder`, `fm-external_artifacts-case-collision` | on retail, `AddOns/Foo-main/Foo/` holding `Foo.toc` (the client's interface) and `Foo.lua`, and `AddOns/foo-main/` holding `README.txt` and `notes.txt` (two files and no TOC, so it is neither an addon nor a wrapper): the wrappers `Foo-main` and `foo-main` collide by case; flattening moves `Foo-main/Foo` to `AddOns/Foo` and quarantines `Foo-main`, which resolves the collision although `case-collision` has no fixer |
| `conflict: quarantine-dir+chmod-child` | `fm-state_files-orphan-temp-file`, `fm-secrets-credential-file-mode` | a directory `<config>/.omaddons-stale/` (mtime three hours back) holding `token` at 0644, and `config.toml` naming it as a `{file = "<config>/.omaddons-stale/token"}` credential |

The conflicting pair, decided while writing this bead, from real fixers: the orphan-temp fixer quarantines the stale directory and the credential fixer chmods its child, a quarantine of a directory against a write into its child. If the real fixers cannot produce the conflict (the orphan-temp walker does not visit `<config>`, or the credential detector does not follow `{file = …}` there), use a set-aside of a planted journal whose `<meta>/stage/<tx>/` holds a stale `.omaddons-` temp file (the set-aside's rename of the stage against the temp fixer's quarantine of its child), and if neither is possible, E6's `fm-test-quarantine` over a directory holding a `fm-test-write` subject with `OMADDONS_TEST_FIXERS=1`; the close comment says which, and why.

#### 2.2 `declared_pairs_fix_together_and_undo_together`

For each declared pair, one lane (`Lane::build_many` with the pair's builder):

1. "start": `S0 = SubjectMap::take(<both fixtures' subjects>, base)`; `doctor --json` (plus `--include-deep` if a row is deep) exits 1 with both ids.
2. "fix": `doctor fix --only a,b` (plus `--force --yes` if either needs it) exits 0 or 1 (logged; 1 is accepted only when the report's remaining findings are none of `a`, `b`).
3. "clean": `doctor --json --only a,b` exits 0.
4. "blast radius and backups": as for single fixers (part 3's checks), over the union of both fixers' `writes_to`.
5. "undo": `doctor undo <run_id>` exits 0 (for the pair with a delegation: the repair half is undone; `undo_tx` set).
6. "compare": the subject map, with bookkeeping for both runs, has the same content as `S0` for every non-delegated subject; for `journal-pending+orphan-temp`, the delegated journal's subjects instead equal ordinary recovery's end state on a separately restored copy (the recovering command, `config set check_interval_hours 6` for this folder journal, then the map; the same command is run once after the fix before comparing), as part 3's delegate rule does (M4-D37: the delegated recovery is never reverted by `doctor undo`). The orphan temp files are back byte for byte with their modes and old mtimes (a rename keeps the mtime), so `doctor --only orphan-temp` finds them again.

#### 2.3 `the_declared_conflicting_pair_is_refused_before_anything_moves`

One lane with the conflicting builder: `root_map` before; `doctor fix --only fm-state_files-orphan-temp-file,fm-secrets-credential-file-mode --json` exits 4 with `error.code: "doctor_refused"`, `details.reason: "fixer_conflict"`, `details.fixes` naming both failure modes, `details.resources` holding both `<config>/.omaddons-stale` and `<config>/.omaddons-stale/token`; a bare `doctor fix --json` refuses the same way; `root_map` after, equal apart from `<state>/doctor/`; no repair journal and no history line was written.

### 3. The lock file

#### 3.1 The source scan (`src/fsx/lock.rs`, test module)

`the_doctor_and_the_repair_engine_never_name_the_lock_file`, beside `no_code_path_truncates_renames_or_unlinks_the_lock_file`:

```rust
let src = Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("src");
let files: Vec<_> = sources(&src).into_iter()
    .filter(|(p, _)| p.starts_with(src.join("doctor")) || p == &src.join("engine/repair.rs")).collect();
// the scan reaches both places, so a file moved out of them cannot escape it
// for each: production_code(text, Literals::Blank) does not contain "lock_file";
//           production_code(text, Literals::Keep) does not contain the literal "\"lock\""
```

Assertions: at least one file under `src/doctor/` and exactly `src/engine/repair.rs` were scanned ("the scan no longer reaches src/doctor/" otherwise); for each offending file, the message names the file and the line. Decided while writing this bead: the existing test already fails any `lock_file` reference outside its three files; the string literal `"lock"` is the only other way to build `<state>/lock`, so scanning for it is what "the existing test's scan, extended to `src/doctor/` and `src/engine/repair.rs`" adds. If a legitimate use of that exact literal appears there, rename it, never weaken the scan.

#### 3.2 The dynamic check

Already part of every harness case (part 1's `lock_identity`, checked at each case's end by parts 3, 4 and this part): the lock file's inode and birth time are the same at a case's end as at its start, and no `actions.jsonl` or `runtime.jsonl` line names `<state>/lock`. This part's tests assert it too, and the close comment states it holds across every test of the harness.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `two_concurrent_fixers_serialize` passes for every fixer: both plan before either locks; one repairs and the other takes 0 actions (exit 0 or 1); no interleaving (disjoint action paths, one repair line); healthy at the end.
- [ ] `a_fixer_waiting_past_the_lock_timeout_exits_5` passes for every fixer: exit 5 `locked` with the holder named, nothing done by the waiting fixer, the holder then completes; the whole test takes about one lock timeout of wall time.
- [ ] `declared_pairs_fix_together_and_undo_together` passes for the three declared pairs: a clean `doctor --only a,b` after one fix, and undo restoring the combined corrupted state (the delegated half ending as ordinary recovery ends).
- [ ] `the_declared_conflicting_pair_is_refused_before_anything_moves` passes: `doctor_refused` with `fixer_conflict`, both fixes and both resources named, nothing moved; the close comment says which construction was used.
- [ ] `the_doctor_and_the_repair_engine_never_name_the_lock_file` passes in `cargo test`, and every case of this part keeps the lock file's identity.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

- `src/fsx/lock.rs`: `the_doctor_and_the_repair_engine_never_name_the_lock_file` (Technical Approach 3.1). Cases inside it: reaches `src/doctor/`; reaches `src/engine/repair.rs`; no `lock_file` (blanked); no `"lock"` literal (kept). Each failure message names the file and line.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

`tests/doctor/harness/props/concurrency.rs` (1.1, 1.2) and `props/pairs.rs` (2.2, 2.3), compiled into `tests/doctor_harness.rs` (debug only). Homes: one lane per fixer or pair. Children: `doctor fix` (with `doctor.fix.planned=pause`, `doctor.repair.prepared=pause`), `doctor`, `doctor undo`, `config set check_interval_hours 6` (the delegated pair's reference). An in-process `GlobalLock` holder for the delegate forced case.

### Logging

- Each test opens `let log = tlog!();`; each fixer or pair is a `log.case(<name>/<serialize | forced | pair | conflict>)`.
- Concurrency steps: "spawn A", "spawn B", "both planned" (`log.reached`, with `waited_ms`), "resume", "wait A", "wait B", "verdict" (`log.json` of both reports' `summary`, `delegated`, `tx`, the action paths of each run, and which one won), "healthy". The forced case logs B's wall time from resume to exit and `details.holder`.
- Pair steps: "plant", "diagnose", "fix", "clean", "undo", "compare", with the pair's `S0`, its end map, the fix's actions and the refusal envelope; a failed comparison logs the first differing paths.
- On failure, T1's guard prints the case's transcript path and last 20 steps; the pool lists every failing case.

## Considerations

- **Flakiness:** the interleavings are forced by `pause` points, never by sleeps; the forced variant's timing is logged, not asserted tightly.
- **A conflict the planner misses** is a defect in E6's conflict check or E13's overlap rule (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.13`): fix there, file it `discovered-from` omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9.
- **The pair builders depend on fixtures written by other leaves:** where a fixture's `corrupt` cannot be reused as is, the builder plants directly with the `tests/common/` builders and says so in its doc comment.
- **`src/fsx/lock.rs` is a hot spot** (§10.5: E13 first, G3 last among the fsx changes): this part touches only its test module; rebase before the gate.

- **Beside it:** parts 2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9.2`), 3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9.3`) and 4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9.4`).
- **After it:** part 6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9.6`), whose exhaustive suite crashes these pairs at every boundary.

title: E2E: the exhaustive suite, the 60 s measurement, README and the leaf's close
description:
Part 6 of 6 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9 (The safety harness). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

F9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`) is the doctor's safety harness: every real fixture and fixer through fourteen properties in every gate, for §3.2 criterion 9 and G-M4-4 and G-M4-6. Parts 1–5 built the runner and the gate's properties: detectors and coverage (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9.2`), round trips (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9.3`), crashes at every primitive boundary (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9.4`), concurrency, pairs and the lock file (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9.5`).

**This part** adds the **exhaustive suite** that the checkpoint runs (`cargo test --test doctor_harness -- --ignored`, §11.3 step 2.6: "crosses boundaries with the declared pairs and repeated-recovery depths"), measures the gate's harness against its 60 s target, adds the harness to README's development section, and closes the leaf. It is the last step because the exhaustive suite reuses part 4's crash machinery and part 5's pairs, and because closing the leaf means verifying every acceptance criterion with evidence.

The rules it keeps, restated: speed comes from reuse (each corrupted home built once and copied per case) and parallelism, **never** from dropping crash positions; every primitive boundary of every action kind keeps a witnessed crash case in the gate; if the gate's harness still runs past 60 s, that is a defect filed `discovered-from` omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9 and fixed by faster fixtures, and H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`) records the time.

## Technical Approach

### Facts this part relies on

- Part 4's `tests/doctor/harness/crash.rs`: `CrashPoint`, `Witness`, `references(log, lane) -> Refs`, `fixed_points(plan)`, `settle(log, lane, refs, point) -> Option<Witness>`, `CrashLedger::assert_complete`, the `Checked` sweep, the recovery-crash sweep from the deepest point. Part 5's `pairs::declared()` (three pairs, each `{label, ids, build}`) and part 3's delegate rule.
- README: `### Tests` with its suite table (`README.md:2619`), `### Milestone checkpoints (not part of the gate)` with its command block (`:2642`).
- T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`): `argc e2e [filter]` runs every suite marked `//! e2e suite:` with `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG=verbose` and prints the log root (`target/tmp/test-logs`).

### 1. The exhaustive suite (`tests/doctor/harness/props/exhaustive.rs`, one `mod exhaustive;` line)

Both tests are `#[ignore = "exhaustive harness, checkpoint: cargo test --test doctor_harness -- --ignored"]`:

1. **`exhaustive_pairs_crashed_at_every_boundary`**: for each declared pair, a lane (`Lane::build_many`, `LANES_PER_FIXER` lanes per pair), the pair's references (the plan from a `doctor.repair.prepared=abort` crash of `doctor fix --only a,b`, before and after with the recovering command), every fixed crash point of the combined run plus the `Checked` sweep, each through `settle` against the pair's references, and a complete ledger per pair. For the pair with a delegation, the delegated journal's subjects always end in the after state (part 4's delegate rule), and the repair half by phase.
2. **`exhaustive_recovery_crashed_at_every_depth`**: for every fixer, every before-`done` crash point (each `RepairStep(k)` and `Mutate(b, k)` with no `done`, and each `Checked(n)` attributed to a primitive), crossed with every recovery-crash depth `j` (`doctor.recover.step=abort@j` until an armed recovery completes), and, for each `j`, a second recovery crash `j'` on the next attempt for every `j'` the remaining inverses allow; then an unarmed recovery and three more; the end state is the before reference every time, every `j` up to the inverse count fired, and the root map is unchanged by the three extra recoveries.

Not timed against a budget; the close comment records its wall time and case counts, and H6 records its own run.

### 2. The 60 s measurement

1. `cargo test --locked --test doctor_harness --no-run` (build first, so the measurement is the run).
2. `time cargo test --locked --test doctor_harness` three times on the development machine, with nothing else heavy running; record the three wall times and the median, and from the logs (`target/tmp/test-logs/doctor_harness/`) each test's logged wall time and the five slowest lanes.
3. Median at or under 60 s: record it. Over 60 s: decided while writing this bead, file a P1 bug `discovered-from` omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9 ("the safety harness runs <median> s in the gate, over its 60 s target"), with the timings and the slowest lanes, to be fixed by faster fixtures, cheaper restores or more lanes, **never** by dropping crash positions; this leaf still closes once every boundary is witnessed (the plan calls 60 s a target and the overrun a defect, and adds no edge for it); H6 records the time.

### 3. README (`README.md`, Development)

- In the `### Tests` table (`:2619`), one row: `tests/doctor_harness.rs` | "The doctor's safety harness: every fixture through fourteen properties (round trip through `doctor undo`, idempotence, a real crash at every primitive boundary of every fixer with recovery crashed too, concurrency, repeatability, no false positive on a 5,040-file home, purity, status agreement, declared write scopes, verbatim backups, cross-failure-mode pairs, the lock file), each corrupted home built once and copied per case".
- In the `### Milestone checkpoints` command block (`:2642`), one line: `cargo test --test doctor_harness -- --ignored           # the exhaustive harness: pairs and recovery depths crossed with every boundary`.
- Nothing else: H4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`) reconciles counts and the rest of README.

### 4. Closing the leaf

The agent closing this part (the last open one) verifies every acceptance criterion of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9 with evidence and closes it:

- run `argc gate` (the harness is in it) and `cargo test --test doctor_harness -- --ignored`;
- run `argc e2e doctor_harness` and keep its summary line and log root;
- gather: each test's name and result; each fixer's `crashes exercised` counts (expected, fired, other) from the logs; the number of crash cases; the gate median and the exhaustive suite's time; every fixture change of parts 1–5 (the four trait methods, `evidence_keys` filled, `name`/`finds` set, `copy_safe(false)` and why, shapes extended, `assert_healthy` made read-only); the conflicting pair's construction; every defect found and its bead id (each `discovered-from` omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9, fixed in the owning leaf's code);
- `br close omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9 --reason "done: <evidence> · found: <ids>"`, with a close comment stating that no wire name changed (tests only).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `exhaustive_pairs_crashed_at_every_boundary` and `exhaustive_recovery_crashed_at_every_depth` exist, are `#[ignore]`d with the checkpoint command in their reason, and pass under `cargo test --test doctor_harness -- --ignored`, with complete ledgers; their wall time and case counts are in the close comment.
- [ ] The gate's harness median wall time over three runs is recorded with the per-test times and the slowest lanes; if over 60 s, the P1 bug is filed `discovered-from` omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9, and no crash position was dropped to shorten it.
- [ ] README's Tests table has the `tests/doctor_harness.rs` row and Milestone checkpoints the exhaustive command line.
- [ ] Every acceptance criterion of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9 is verified with evidence (test names, the commit, the counts, the times, `argc e2e doctor_harness`'s summary and log root) and omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9 is closed with the close comment its body asks for.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files; `br lint` is clean on omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9 and its subtasks.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

None.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

The two ignored tests of Technical Approach item 1, in `tests/doctor/harness/props/exhaustive.rs`, compiled into `tests/doctor_harness.rs` (debug only), run with `cargo test --test doctor_harness -- --ignored`. They reuse every helper of parts 1, 4 and 5; nothing new is planted.

### Logging

- Each test opens `let log = tlog!();`; each pair or fixer is a `log.case(<name>)` and each crossed case a `log.case(<name>/<point>/recover@<j>[/<j'>])`, with part 4's steps ("restore", "crash", "crash state", "reader", "recover", "compare", "nothing left", "accounted", "leftovers", "lock").
- `log.json("crashes exercised", …)` per pair and per fixer; `log.note` of each test's wall time and case count.
- The measurement's three wall times and the slowest lanes go into the close comment, read from the logs; `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG=verbose argc e2e doctor_harness exhaustive -- --ignored` echoes every step live.

### Checkpoint-only tests

`cargo test --test doctor_harness -- --ignored` (debug build), run in this part and by H6 at §11.3 step 2.6. It has no `SKIP` path.

## Considerations

- **The exhaustive suite is large** (every before-`done` point times every recovery depth times a second depth, plus three pairs at every boundary): minutes, not seconds. That is why it is the checkpoint's, not the gate's; never move a gate property into it to save gate time.
- **A failure found here** is a defect in the owning leaf's protocol or fixer (E5 recovery, E7 inverses, E14 order, the fixer's lowering): fix it there, file it `discovered-from` omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9, and rerun.
- **Measurement noise:** run the three timings on an otherwise idle machine; report the median, not the best.
- **README hot spot:** edit only the one row and the one command line; H4 owns the rest.

## Dependencies

- **Parent:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9 (The safety harness).
- **Blocked by:** T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`), by its own edge: the exhaustive tests are `TestLog` scenarios.
- **Before it:** parts 2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9.2`), 3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9.3`), 4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9.4`) and 5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9.5`): the suite reuses part 4's crash machinery and part 5's pairs, and the leaf can close only after every property exists.
- **After it:** nothing in this leaf. Closing omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9 unblocks H4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`, the README final pass) and T4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4`, slice 3 end to end, whose demo item "the harness green at every primitive boundary" runs this suite).

title: Epic: M4 the widget and durability
description:
## Background

Area G is the widget-and-durability area of M4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`, the milestone epic: the agent surface, the doctor and the first tag). Its three leaves share little code. What they share is their place in the graph: each one consumes protocols that other areas build and settle first, and none of them invents a protocol of its own except G3's durability rule.

- G1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1`, the widget previews and applies plans, slice 2): the Omarchy bar widget previews every update, install and destructive action, and runs `omaddons apply <plan_id>` of exactly the plan it previewed. It applies directly only a routine plan whose canonical selection matches the row the user pressed; anything else opens the dialog with each effect named.
- G2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.2`, the Issues view runs doctor repairs, slice 3): Enter on an auto-fixable problem previews the repair, lists every change it would make, and runs exactly that repair bound to its token. Undo last reverts a repair through a stored plan. The widget never runs a set-aside, `doctor gc`, or any argv holding `--force`.
- G3 (`omad-7ccp`, group commit, derived writes and deferred directory fsyncs, slice 3): every commit window stays as durable as today with fewer fsyncs, and where that cannot be tested, it is argued in writing per ordering point. G3 is the existing bead `omad-7ccp`, re-parented here (M4-D59).

The three leaves weigh 7 units (two size-M, one size-L) and are worked through 16 subtasks (5, 4 and 7). The area adds no command, no error code, no warning code and no persisted format. On the CLI's wire it adds three data keys (G1's `list` keys `latest.source`, `latest.release_id` and `latest.asset`). It adds one constant (G3's `DIRTY_DIRS_MAX`, 64). Everything else it adds is internal (fsx types, log message texts) or belongs to the widget, which is not CLI contract.

### Why it matters to the milestone

- **G-M4-3, what was previewed is what runs, target by target.** The milestone goal ends: "The bar widget's Update buttons apply a plan directly only when its selection matches the row the user pressed and it needs no further approval (new dependencies, removals, replaced local edits, a different source). Anything else opens the dialog (M4-D28)." G1 is that sentence. G2 extends it to repairs: a repair runs only bound to the preview the user saw, and its undo only through a stored plan.
- **G-M4-4, diagnosable and repairable.** "Every auto-fixable state is repaired by one consented command that backs up verbatim, never deletes, and is proven by a fixture that round-trips." In the widget the consented command is one key press after a dialog that lists every change. The guarded repairs stay a deliberate terminal command, with the doctor's explanation on screen.
- **G-M4-6, no new risk to the engine's guarantees.** "Every new write goes through fsx", and "the global lock is still held only for commit windows". The widget adds no write path: every check is the CLI's. G3 shortens every commit window on real disks without moving any guarantee that recovery relies on, and keeps today's immediate fsync wherever it cannot argue otherwise.

It also carries promises of the vision bead `omad-vision-8qa`:

- its §5.11: "mutating buttons first fetch a plan and then call `apply <plan_id>` for the plan shown", which M3-D9 deferred (M3's widget runs updates directly);
- its G7: "`doctor` follows the world-class doctor contract", whose consent axiom says a forced repair needs a person who read why;
- its §5.5 step 7, "an fsync'd `actions.jsonl` line", which M4-D54 amends (the line is synced at the transaction's end), the reason `omad-7ccp` was deferred to M4;
- the thesis that omaddons stays the sole, safe, undoable authority over what it manages: even the most casual surface, a bar button, installs or repairs only what it showed, and every guarantee recovery gives still rests on what was durable when the power went.

### What is true today (verified at `c0ab5e9`)

**The widget.**

- **Updates run without a preview, by design** (M3-D9: "updates are undoable and expected"). `Model.updateRequest` (`omarchy/Model.js:1602-1607`) runs `update_all` or `update_target` with no confirmation, and Enter on an Updates row runs the `update_addon` template, `update -t <client> -- <addon>` (`omarchy/Model.js:108`). The command installs whatever is newest at that moment, so a release landing between the badge and the key press installs something nobody saw.
- **Destructive actions preview, and confirm with `--if-match`.** The templates `remove`, `restore`, `restore_addon` and `prune_backup` carry `"confirm": true` (`omarchy/Model.js:110`, `:122-124`). `Service.previewOf` (`omarchy/Service.qml:321-327`) runs the dry run, and Yes runs the real command with the preview's token.
- **A version match is not an approval.** The Updates row says `DBM 12.1.14 → 12.1.15`, but the same version can come from another source or another release asset, and a plan can add a dependency, remove a folder or replace files the user edited. M3's widget never looks at a plan before running it.
- **The Issues view runs any remediation the classifier accepts** (`IssuesView.activate`, `omarchy/views/IssuesView.qml:62-72`). `classifyCliArgv` (`omarchy/Model.js:384-420`) refuses malformed argv, foreign programs, widget-owned flags and unknown paths. It has no rule for `--force`, `--yes` or any particular path. No `doctor` path, template or reducer exists in `omarchy/`.
- **The widget turns read-only against another build** (M3-D42): `Model.compatible` (`omarchy/Model.js:472-477`) requires the stamped tool version and an installed widget that `status` does not call outdated, and "outdated" compares the installed files with the binary's embedded ones.

**Durability.**

- **Every durable write is made durable on its own.** Each tracked `mutate()` appends its audit line to `actions.jsonl` with one fsync per line (`log_action` → `sys::append_durable`, `src/fsx/mutate.rs:863-871`). Every temp-plus-rename write fsyncs the file and its parent directory. Every rename fsyncs both parents (`src/fsx/mutate.rs:843-845`). The history projection `history_tail.json`, a cache rebuilt from `history.jsonl`, is rewritten with full durability inside the window.
- **The measurement** (`omad-7ccp`, comment 1167; release build, btrfs on NVMe): an install that replaced an installed version held the lock 165 ms for 62 fsyncs, about 3.3 ms each. By file: 15 `actions.jsonl` (one per action), 5 the journal, then pairs per temp-plus-rename write (snapshot directory 4, `targets/` record 4, `history_tail` cache 4, trash 3, journal directory 2, stage 2, client snapshot 2–3, files index pieces 4, in-flight 2, `history.jsonl` 1, AddOns 1, state root 1). A whole restore of a 500 MiB `WTF/` held it 134 to 146 ms for 51. The comment estimated about 44 after group-committing the action log and taking the cache writes out of the window.
- **The budgets hide it.** Every lock budget of `tests/perf.rs` is measured on tmpfs, where an fsync costs nothing, so the M1 to M3 checkpoints recorded 0 to 2 ms. A second terminal, an agent and the bar widget wait for the lock up to 5 s (`LOCK_ACQUIRE_TIMEOUT`).
- **The pieces that exist.** `fsx::sys::SyncCounts { fsync, syncfs }` counts this thread's durability calls (`src/fsx/sys.rs:27-53`). `Durability::{Immediate, Deferred}` (`src/fsx/sys.rs:131-140`): `Deferred` promises a later `syncfs` and serves staging only. Nothing groups the audit lines, defers a directory sync or reports a sync count per window.

### The decisions that shape the area

The full decision log is in the decision-log comments on the milestone epic. These are the decisions that shape this area, restated:

- **M4-D28: the widget previews updates, and applies directly only a routine plan that matches the row** (G1, and G2's repair part).
  - The CLI says what an approval covers. Every storable dry run returns `data.approval`, built by D4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`, the plan store): the canonical selection (per item: the client's key, the addon's identity, its source and channel, the release id and asset, the from and to versions), the scope (`dependencies_added`, `folders_removed`, `local_changes_replaced`, `source_changed`, the running-client policy), `reasons[]` from a closed set naming each effect that needs a person's eyes, and `routine`, true only when `reasons[]` is empty.
  - Update, Update all and per-addon updates run the command's `--dry-run` and compare the plan's selection with what the view showed. Equal and routine: run `apply <plan_id>` with no dialog.   1. *Group commit.* A tracked `WriteSession` buffers its audit lines. `WriteSession::sync_actions()` writes and syncs the buffer before the journal line that closes the transaction's changes (a folder journal's `swapped`, a repair's `done` or `rolled_back`), before the history line, and at `WriteSession::finish()`, a new explicit method that returns errors. A tracked session dropped without `finish()` fails a debug assertion. It is safe because recovery reads only the journal, never `actions.jsonl`, and a repair's undo reads the history line's primitives (M4-D46); a crash before the closing line loses at most the audit lines of an attempt that recovery then rolls back. The journal stays write-ahead per step.
  2. *Derived files are not fsynced.* `history_tail.json`, `backups.json` and the doorbell are rebuilt from durable state when missing or stale (M3-D37), so they are written with a new `Durability::Derived`: temp-plus-rename atomicity, no fsync, no later `syncfs`. `Durability::Deferred` promises a later `syncfs`, so it is the wrong contract for them.
  3. *Deferred directory fsyncs through owned handles and explicit barriers.* Syncing a file does not make its directory entry durable (Linux `fsync(2)` requires syncing the directory), so the deferral keeps every directory sync, deduplicated and moved to ordering points. A durability context, `fsx::CommitWindow`, is created with the lock and passed explicitly. Each `mutate()` that changes a directory records an open directory handle (`O_RDONLY | O_DIRECTORY | O_CLOEXEC`), the parent of a write or create and both parents of a rename, deduplicated by `fstat` identity; a handle keeps naming its directory after a rename, and nothing ever reopens a path. At most `DIRTY_DIRS_MAX` (64) handles are held; past that the context syncs them at once. `barrier()` syncs every handle and returns the first error; it runs before every journal phase line and the history line, before every step line that follows a rename, and as a final barrier before success and release. A barrier error fails the command, with the journal and backups kept; `Drop` is defensive cleanup only. File-data fsyncs are not deferred. Where the written argument cannot justify deferring a directory's sync, that directory keeps its immediate fsync.

The further cut of change 3 is reported, not promised. *Power loss:* the written argument is the evidence; a power-loss campaign runs where an unprivileged tool that drops unsynced writes is usable, else README says the ordering is argued and crash-tested, not power-loss-tested.
  - *Why the argument:* a crash matrix cannot prove fsync placement. A failpoint kill keeps the page cache, so every placement passes it.
  - *Rejected:* (i) per-line fsync, the status quo (about 40 ms per install for durability nothing reads); (ii) dropping `actions.jsonl` for engine transactions (the doctor contract's audit trail); (iii) skipping a parent fsync "when the directory is unchanged since its last fsync" (every directory fsync follows a change, and as first written it left a rename's removal non-durable); (iv) promising a halving (no measurement supports it); (v) a per-thread map of inode keys to paths flushed when the lock guard drops (a later rename can invalidate a stored path, and `Drop` cannot return its I/O error); (vi) syncing the action log before every journal append (it keeps one log sync per step).

## Goals

This epic's leaves are each worked through subtasks (claim a subtask, not the leaf; the agent that closes a leaf's last subtask verifies the leaf's acceptance criteria and closes it).

- **G1** `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1` (The widget previews and applies plans, size-M, slice-2): `list`'s `latest` gains `source`, `release_id` and `asset`, so an Updates row carries the release identity it was judged on. The widget's previewed-action runner then previews every update, install and destructive action, applies a routine plan whose canonical selection matches the row with no dialog, and opens the dialog naming each effect otherwise. It turns M4-D28 into the widget's behaviour, so the most casual way to change addons installs exactly what it showed or asks first.
- **G2** `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.2` (The Issues view runs doctor repairs, size-M, slice-3): Enter on an auto-fixable problem previews `doctor fix --only <fm> --dry-run`, the dialog lists every planned change, and Yes runs the same argv bound with `--if-match`; Undo last of a repair previews `undo --dry-run` and applies its stored plan. The classifier refuses a set-aside, `doctor gc`, `doctor undo` and any argv holding `--force` or `--yes`, and a set-aside row shows its explanation and the exact terminal command. It brings the doctor to the bar without turning a consent gate into a key press.
- **G3** `omad-7ccp` (Group commit, derived writes and deferred directory fsyncs (`omad-7ccp`), size-L, slice-3): it counts each commit window's fsyncs and pins them per shape, then group-commits the audit log, writes the derived caches without fsync after the lock, and defers directory fsyncs through owned handles to explicit barriers that return their errors. Its design gate carries one written power-loss argument per ordering point and an adversarial matrix at every barrier. It buys back the lock time real disks cost (62 fsyncs and 165 ms per install on btrfs) without weakening anything recovery reads.

## Success Criteria

When every child of this epic is closed, all of the following are true:

- **The row's identity (G1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1`).** `list --json`'s every addon carries `latest {version, status, source, release_id, asset}`, the three new keys always present and `null` exactly when the status names no release. After `outdated`, they equal `update <addon> --dry-run --json`'s `data.approval.selection[0].{source, release_id, asset}` on a GitHub addon. `outdated --json` is unchanged.
- **Updates preview, and apply only what matches (G1).** In bun and QML tests over envelopes the binary writes:
  - an ordinary matching, routine update proceeds directly: the next launch is `apply <plan_id>` of the preview, and no dialog opens;
  - a dependency added by the preview, locally modified files about to be replaced and an extra removal each open the dialog with that effect named in plain words;
  - equal versions with a changed asset or a changed source open the dialog with "Changed since you looked", and so does a release that moved since the row was read;
  - a row or a plan missing any compared field never matches;
  - Update all compares every update row in the filter: all matching and routine gives one `apply`, and one row missing, added or moved gives the dialog.
- **Destructive actions confirm through `apply` (G1).** `remove`, `restore`, `restore_addon`, `prune_backup`, `reinstall` and Undo last open the dialog starting on No, and Yes runs `apply <plan_id>` of their preview; no previewed action runs its command with `--if-match`. `errors dismiss` keeps its read-bound token, `targets rm` its explicit confirmation, and `pin` and `unpin` run directly.
- **Plan errors re-preview, never re-run (G1).** A refused `apply` (`plan_stale` with each `details.reason` or with `details.changed`, `plan_not_found`, a `stale` target in `outcomes[]`) re-runs the original action's preview and reopens the dialog; a re-preview never auto-applies. A no-op preview refreshes the view. `apply` is classified only from a preview's own `commands[]` with the matching `plan_id`, and every other `apply` argv is refused.
- **Repairs from the Issues view (G2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.2`).** A credential-mode fix (`fm-secrets-credential-file-mode`) is previewed, the dialog lists "chmod 0600 <config>/credentials/github (was 0644)", Yes runs the same argv with `--if-match <token>`, and Undo last reverts it through `undo --run <run> --dry-run` and `apply` of its plan; in the matching Rust scene the file's mode goes 0644, 0600, 0644, and `<config>`'s tree hash returns to the one before the repair. The classifier refuses `doctor gc …`, any argv holding `--force` or `--yes`, and `doctor fix` or `doctor undo` from CLI output, by bun test; security scan 11 catches each planted violation.
- **The widget stays a thin, safe runner (G1, G2).** Every security scan passes on the real source and catches its planted violation: `apply` only from its plan, a preview on every addon-changing template, no decision read from a warning's message, no issue id matched by name, no forced or garbage-collecting path. ## Non-Goals

- **A dialog for every update, or no preview at all** (M4-D28, rejected i and ii). The common case, a routine update the user saw, stays one key press.
- **A version-only match** (M4-D28, rejected iii). A field that is hard to carry opens the dialog; it is never dropped from the comparison.
- **Deciding anything from a warning's text or an issue's id.** The widget reads `approval.reasons[]`, `approval.routine` and `auto_fixable`, never a human message, and matches no failure-mode id by name (M4-D48).
- **A `--if-match` fallback when no plan was stored.** A preview with changes but `plan_id: null` (`plan_not_stored`, a write failure) runs nothing and says why.
- **Running a set-aside, `doctor gc`, `doctor undo`, or any argv holding `--force` or `--yes` from the widget** (M4-D38, M4-D36, M4-D22). Those stay deliberate terminal commands, with the explanation shown. A CLI fix that names `install … --force` or `backup import … --force` becomes text too.
- **`plans show` in the widget.** It is an agent's reconciliation tool (D9); the widget re-previews instead.
- **A new notification kind.** A repair is user-started, and its result follows M3's "result after the panel closed" rule.
- **A new CLI command, error code, warning code, `details` key, event or persisted format.** G1 adds three `list` data keys; G2 and G3 add no wire name.
- **Another UI.** The bar widget stays a thin argv runner over the CLI; M4 builds no GUI, TUI, daemon or MCP server (vision D3).
- **Deferring a file-data fsync, or touching the journal's write-ahead order.** Only the audit log's per-line syncs, the derived files' syncs and the directory syncs move.
- **Deferring recovery's or gc's durability.** Recovery prunes journals right after its renames and a prune is not an ordering point, so recovery keeps immediate durability; gc hands its guard to prune and keeps immediate durability (both decided in G3's bead).
- **Dropping `actions.jsonl`, or promising a halving** (M4-D54, rejected ii and iv). The target is what the counted boundaries give.
- **A real-disk lock budget.** The lock budgets stay on tmpfs; the btrfs figures are reported as measurements in README, not budgets.
- **Downloading or building a power-loss tool, or using one that needs root** (`dm-log-writes` needs device-mapper). The campaign runs only with an already installed LazyFS and FUSE usable without root.
- **Changing any persisted shape.** `actions.jsonl`, the journals, `history.jsonl` and the derived files keep their formats; `history.jsonl` stays append-only (M4-D49).

### How the leaves are worked

Each leaf is worked through its subtasks: G1 through five, G2 through four, G3 through seven. Claim a subtask, not the leaf (`br ready --parent <leaf id>`); the agent that closes a leaf's last subtask verifies the leaf's acceptance criteria and closes it. G3 is size L and **kept as one leaf for closure**: its three changes share one counted table and one written ordering argument, so H4 and T4 never see a commit window whose durability was argued for only part of its writes.

- **G1:** subtask 1 (the `list` keys, Rust) and subtask 2 (the pure decisions in `omarchy/Model.js`, additive) touch different files and run in parallel; subtask 3 is the one switch-over commit (templates gain `preview`, `Service.qml`'s runner, the views, README); subtasks 4 (security scans) and 5 (end to end over binary-written fixtures) follow in parallel.

### Design gates

**G3 is the area's one design gate** (common rule 14: a leaf that changes a durability rule closes only when its own adversarial matrix passes). Its gate has two halves, because a crash matrix cannot prove fsync placement:

- **The written argument, before code.** G3's subtask 1 posts a comment on G3 titled "Design gate: commit-window durability (M4-D54)" with the before tables, the derived target per shape and its arithmetic, and one paragraph per ordering point (folder journal F1–F7, repair journal R1–R7, and the final barrier X): what recovery reads after a power loss there, and why it is consistent. The agent claiming G3's subtask 2 reviews every paragraph in its claim comment ("agreed" or a challenge per point), and the agent claiming subtask 5 re-checks each against the code it changes. A challenged point keeps its immediate fsync until the challenge is answered.
- **The adversarial matrix.** G3's subtask 6: an injected sync failure (`fsx.barrier.sync=error@N`) and a crash (`=abort@N`) at every barrier of every commit window, repeated recovery, the `WTF/` privacy case, the oversized window, and every crash matrix rerun.

The gate is passed only when subtask 1's record has been reviewed and subtask 6 is closed. If the gate changes G3's size or edges, the change is recorded in a comment on the milestone epic and the delivery computation (critical path, slack, lanes) is rerun there. Because G3 is on the critical path, any growth at its gate moves the tag.

G1 and G2 are not design gates. They add no journal shape, recovery rule, binding rule, deletion rule or durability rule: they make the widget a client of the binding protocols D1–D8, E6 and E7 built.

### Risks

- **Risk 8, group commit or deferred directory fsyncs weaken durability somewhere recovery depends on, invisibly** (likelihood low, impact high; owner G3). Failpoint kills keep the page cache, so no crash test can see it. Mitigations: the journal untouched; the action log synced before each transaction's closing line; directories synced through owned handles at explicit barriers that return their errors before success; derived files losing durability only because they are rebuilt from durable state; a written, reviewed argument per ordering point and an immediate fsync wherever the argument fails; a unit test that pins the barrier sequence of a journal, and an injection at every barrier that proves each one exists; every crash matrix rerun; G3 lands last, on settled protocols.
- **Risk 7, widget update previews feel slow** (medium, low; owner G1). A dry run downloads and verifies, as the real run did before; the blobs are then cached, so `apply` downloads nothing. The footer shows progress, and no dialog appears when the plan matches. Each widget update now costs two processes instead of one.
- **Risk 20, the under-lock witness check lengthens the commit window** (medium, low; owner D8). G3's `update_bound` row counts that window, so a later fsync there shows as a diff.
- **Risk 23, guarded reactivation refuses more often than users expect** (medium, low; owners F2, E7). G2 shows the `explain` text, which says so, before anyone consents to a set-aside.
- **Risk 3, doctor false positives erode trust** (medium, medium; owners F*, H6). G2 offers Fix only for `auto_fixable` findings, every repair is undoable, and the dialog lists every change.
- **Risk 5, the pre-freeze audit breaks the widget** (medium, medium; owner H1). If H1 renames a key G1 or G2 consumes, H1 updates the widget in the same commit.
- **Risk 14, the milestone is large** (medium, medium). With area T, G3 is a critical-path leaf and the area's slack is 0 to 2 units; claim each leaf as soon as it is ready, and G2 beside G3, not after it.
- **The row and the plan speak different vocabularies** (G1). An asset path against a file name, or the widget's display source `gh` against the wire's `github`, would make every update open the dialog: safe but annoying. G1's parity test against `approval.selection` and its routine fixture, which must apply directly, catch it.
- **A matching bug auto-applies something not shown** (G1). Guarded by the missing-field rule and its cases (each compared field missing on each side), by never auto-applying a destructive offer or a re-preview, and by a real fixture for each reason.
- **A Fix that runs more than the dialog showed, a forced repair from a button, an Undo that reverts something else** (G2). Guarded by M4-D44's token compared under the lock in a second process, the widget's check that every planned action names the row's failure mode, the template shape (no consent flag can sit in a slot), the classifier's refusals and scan 11, and an Undo shown only after `status` names a repair, its dialog listing the inverse primitives and starting on No.
- **An unguarded interval between F8 or F2 and G2.** After F8, an auto-fixable issue's remediation is `doctor fix --only <fm>` with `destructive: false`, and after E6 adds the `doctor fix` row the widget's classifier accepts it; non-destructive CLI argv run directly. Until G2's subtask 1 lands its refusals, Enter on such a row in a widget built from `main` would run a repair unpreviewed, and after F2 a set-aside's `--force --yes` remediation would be a button. The installed widget turns read-only against a binary whose embedded widget files differ (M3-D42), so the exposure needs a widget installed from a commit inside that interval. **Decided while writing this bead:** nobody runs `omaddons omarchy install` from a commit between F8 (or F2) and G2's subtask 1; G2's subtask 1 is claimed first once G2 is ready; H6 installs the widget after the M4 build.
- **The derived durability target differs from the forecast** (G3). M4-D54's three log sync points each find buffered lines in the folder engine, so G3's bead expects about 46 fsyncs before the directory change, not 44. The gate records the derived figure and criterion 13 follows it; no sync point is dropped to reach 44.
- **Doctor previews accumulate run directories** (G2). Every `doctor fix`, dry run included, makes a run directory; E8's growth finding reports past 200 and `doctor gc` reclaims them. The widget previews a repair only on Enter and never retries a preview by itself.
- **Compatibility.** The widget is stamped for one build and turns read-only against another, so a pre-M4 binary never meets the new runner. Nothing G3 persists changes shape: an older build reads the same `actions.jsonl` lines, journals, history and derived files, so E9's characterization is unaffected.
- **Privacy.** Dialog and result lines come from typed fields, as plain text; G2's path display hides any path below `WTF/`; G3's `-v`/`-vv` lines carry counts and fixed kind names only, and a barrier error's directory is redacted below `WTF/`.
- **Filesystems.** G3's figures are btrfs on NVMe, the development machine's; ext4 or a SATA SSD may differ several-fold. README reports them as measurements.

### What the leaf beads found against the plan

The leaf beads found these differences between the plan and the code at `c0ab5e9`, and each records its adaptation:

- **G1:**
  - the Updates view's rows come from `list -v`, not from `status` (`status` has no per-addon update entries), so the row identity goes on `list`'s `latest` (`src/app/list.rs`) and `src/app/status.rs` is not touched; the H1 edge "the update entries' new keys" therefore means `latest.source`, `latest.release_id` and `latest.asset`;
  - the plan compares the release asset but added only `source` and `release_id`; without an asset no update could ever match, so `latest.asset` is added too;
  - `tests/omarchy_widget.rs`'s `binds` assertion is at `:42-46`, not `:44-48`;
