  - Search results carry no release, so an install from Search always confirms; the Installed, Issues and Search views start updates or installs too.
- **G2:**
  - the classifier has no rule for `--force`, `--yes` or any path, and `doctor gc` classifies as the read path `doctor` until E8 adds its row, so the refusal checks the leading words;
  - the doctor envelope has no `data` and a dry run with findings exits 1, so the widget gets a dedicated bind-preview branch and `Model.doctorResult`;
  - F2 and E8 are not blockers, so the set-aside and gc fixtures may be derived;
  - `install --force` and `backup import --force` exist, so those fixes become text too;
  - `KIND_WORDS` has no `repair` and an undo's text reads "0 folders restored" for a repair; both gain repair branches.
- **G3:**
  - the plan's install forecast of 44 assumes one log sync, but three sync points each find lines, so about 46 is expected before the directory change;
  - a barrier after `prepared` (the journal file's creation) is added to the plan's list of ordering points, for both journal families, at the cost of the one directory fsync it costs today;
  - `barrier` takes `&self`, not `&mut self`, because several sessions of one window record into it;
  - a barrier error is never answered by in-process recovery (the plan says a barrier error before `done` "triggers the in-process rollback"): the journal is left for the next lock-taking command, as after a crash, because the folder engine would otherwise roll forward after `swapped` and report success;
  - recovery and gc keep immediate durability and open no window;
  - the pinned table holds twelve shapes, the plan's five plus the windows its blockers add.
acceptance_criteria:
G1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1`), G2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.2`) and G3 (`omad-7ccp`) and every subtask of them are closed, each leaf having verified its own acceptance criteria, and the following hold on `main`:

- [ ] The row's identity (G1): `list --json`'s every addon carries `latest {version, status, source, release_id, asset}`, the three new keys always present and `null` exactly when the status names no release; after `outdated` they equal `update <addon> --dry-run --json`'s `data.approval.selection[0].{source, release_id, asset}` on a GitHub addon, and `outdated --json` is unchanged.
- [ ] Updates preview, and apply only what matches (G1), in bun and QML tests over envelopes the binary writes: an ordinary matching, routine update launches `apply <plan_id>` of its preview with no dialog; a dependency added, locally modified files about to be replaced and an extra removal each open the dialog with that effect named; equal versions with a changed asset or source, and a release that moved since the row was read, open it with "Changed since you looked"; a row or a plan missing any compared field never matches; Update all applies once only when every row in the filter matches and is routine.
- [ ] Destructive actions confirm through `apply` (G1): `remove`, `restore`, `restore_addon`, `prune_backup`, `reinstall` and Undo last open the dialog starting on No, and Yes runs `apply <plan_id>` of their preview; no previewed action runs its command with `--if-match`; `errors dismiss` keeps its read-bound token, `targets rm` its explicit confirmation, and `pin` and `unpin` run directly.
- [ ] Plan errors re-preview, never re-run (G1): `plan_stale` (each `details.reason`, and `details.changed`), `plan_not_found` and a `stale` target in `outcomes[]` re-run the original preview and reopen the dialog; a re-preview never auto-applies; a no-op preview refreshes the view; `apply` is classified only from a preview's own `commands[]` with the matching `plan_id`.
- [ ] Repairs from the Issues view (G2): the credential-mode fix is previewed (`doctor fix --only fm-secrets-credential-file-mode --dry-run`), its dialog lists "chmod 0600 <config>/credentials/github (was 0644)", Yes runs the same argv with `--if-match <token>`, and Undo last reverts it through `undo --run <run> --dry-run` and `apply` of its plan; the Rust scene sees the mode go 0644, 0600, 0644 and `<config>`'s tree hash return to its value before the repair; a subject changed between preview and Yes runs nothing and the dialog returns with the new preview.
- [ ] Consent stays a person's (G2): a set-aside row offers no Fix, shows the explanation and the exact remediation command (`--force --yes` included) and never launches `doctor fix`; the classifier refuses `doctor gc …`, any argv holding `--force` or `--yes`, and `doctor fix` or `doctor undo` from CLI output (bun test); security scan 11 catches each planted violation.
- [ ] The widget stays a thin, safe runner (G1, G2): every security scan passes on the real source and catches its planted violation; no runtime file under `omarchy/` matches an issue id by name or reads a warning's message to decide anything; the output-cap test bounds the `update_all` preview and its `apply`, the doctor templates and `doctor explain` below `WIDGET_OUTPUT_MAX_BYTES` for 12 clients of 400 addons; no line shown from a repair contains a path below `WTF/`.
- [ ] Counted commit windows (G3): `-v` prints each window's `fsyncs` beside `lock_held_ms` and `-vv` the per-kind attribution, neither naming a path; `tests/engine_durability.rs` pins all twelve shapes in the gate, and every changed row landed in the commit that changed the count, with its reason, none loosened silently.
- [ ] The three changes landed (G3): `actions.jsonl` is synced before `swapped`, `done` or `rolled_back`, before the history line and at `finish()`, the journal still written ahead per step; `history_tail.json`, `backups.json` and the doorbell are written with `Durability::Derived` outside every commit window; every directory a window changes is synced through a handle recorded when it changed, at an explicit barrier at every ordering point and once before the lock is released; a tracked session dropped without `finish()` and a `CommitWindow` dropped without its final barrier each fail a debug assertion.
- [ ] Barriers fail loudly and recover (G3): an injected sync failure and a crash at every barrier of every commit window fail the command (`io` with `details.journal_pending`, or the doctor dictionary's exit with `DONE_FAILED`), keep the journal and the backups recovery needs, and the next lock-taking command recovers to the whole before or whole after state; every crash matrix passes unchanged; a barrier failure below `WTF/` names no account, realm or character.
- [ ] The design gate (G3): the comment "Design gate: commit-window durability (M4-D54)" on G3 holds the before tables, the derived target per shape with its arithmetic and one power-loss paragraph per ordering point (F1–F7, R1–R7, X), reviewed by the agents that claimed subtasks 2 and 5; any point without an argument kept its immediate fsync; the adversarial-matrix subtask is closed.
- [ ] Checkpoint criterion 13 is supported end to end: on btrfs an install's window holds no more fsyncs than the gate's derived target (forecast at most 44, from 62), the whole restore's lock hold is reported, and G3's close comment carries the per-file table before (`omad-7ccp` comment 1167) and after and the deferred directory fsyncs' further cut; the power-loss campaign ran where LazyFS is usable without root, or README says the ordering is argued and crash-tested, not power-loss-tested.
- [ ] Checkpoint criterion 8 is supported end to end: the update, destructive and Issues parts pass in bun and QML, ready for H6's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`) desktop runs through IPC `state()` (`lastPreview`, `lastResult`) and screenshots.
- [ ] The area's share of criteria 6, 14, 17 and 18 holds: the M3 binding of `remove`, `undo`, `backup restore`, `backup prune` and `errors dismiss` is unchanged in the CLI; G1 landed before H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`); `argc gate --all` passes with the widget pipeline's QML step; README describes the widget's previews and repairs and the durability figures.
- [ ] The slice demo items pass as tests: G1's three QML scenarios in `tst_plans.qml`, asserted by name by T3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.3`); G2's three QML scenarios in `tst_repairs.qml` and G3's pinned table, read by T4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4`).
- [ ] README's `### list`, `### omarchy` (Update previews, the routine rule, the confirmation paragraph, the Issues bullet, the Enter row, the rules list), the FAQ entry "Why did the widget ask me about an update?", the `-v` row, Concurrency, the Durability bullet, the transaction diagram, Crash testing and the Tests table were each updated in the commit that shipped their behaviour.
- [ ] `DIRTY_DIRS_MAX` (64) is in `src/limits.rs` with its `REGISTRY` row and `LIMIT_NAMES` entry, and the `limit_registries` snapshot was re-accepted after review.
- [ ] Every leaf's close comment lists its new or changed wire names (G1: `targets[].addons[].latest.source`, `latest.release_id`, `latest.asset`; G2 and G3: none), its widget-side or internal names, and each "Decided while writing this bead" item as confirmed or adjusted. `argc gate` passed for every commit, and `br lint` is clean for every bead of the area.

title: The widget previews and applies plans
description:
## How to work this bead

This bead is worked through its 5 subtasks, listed below in work order. Claim a subtask, not this bead (`br ready --parent omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1` lists the ready ones). The agent that closes the last open subtask then verifies every acceptance criterion of this bead (they are the leaf's, not any one subtask's), and closes this bead with `br close omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1 --reason "done: <evidence> · found: <ids>"`. Until this bead is closed, every bead it blocks stays blocked.

1. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.1 The update entry carries its release identity: `list`'s `latest` gains `source`, `release_id` and `asset`, with a parity test against `update --dry-run`'s `approval.selection`.
2. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.2 The plan runner's pure decisions in `omarchy/Model.js`: `PLAN_PATHS`, `planFrom`, `approvalOf`, `selectionMatches`, `reasonText`, `previewDecision`, `applyResult`, the `apply` classifier rule and the front-queued continuation, all additive and bun-tested.
3. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.3 The widget previews and applies plans: templates gain `preview`, `Service.qml`'s previewed-action runner replaces `previewOf`'s destructive-only path, the views pass what they showed, the dialog names each effect, and README's `omarchy` section says so.
4. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.4 Tests: the security scans hold `apply` to its plan, a preview on every addon-changing template, warnings out of every decision, and no issue id matched by name.
5. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.5 E2E: the plan runner over envelopes the binary writes (bun and QML scenarios, the output cap over preview and `apply` envelopes, the built `apply` argv parsed by clap).

Subtasks 1 and 2 touch different files (Rust in `src/app/list.rs` and `src/resolve/updates.rs`; JavaScript in `omarchy/Model.js` and its bun tests) and can run in parallel. Subtask 3 waits for both: it switches the widget over to the functions of subtask 2 and relies on the row identity of subtask 1. Subtasks 4 and 5 wait for subtask 3 (5 also for 1, whose keys its fixtures read) and touch different test files, so they can run in parallel. Subtasks 1 and 5 write integration tests and wait for T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, the structured test log) as well.

**Not a design gate.** Common rule 14 lists D1, D2, D5, D8, E5, E7, E8, E11, E14 and G3. This leaf adds no journal shape, recovery rule, binding rule, deletion rule or durability rule: it makes the widget a client of the binding protocol D1–D8 built (`apply <plan_id>` of a stored plan, D5), and adds three additive data keys to `list`. Size M: one Rust change of a few dozen lines, and one coordinated widget change across `Model.js`, `Service.qml`, five views and their three test suites.

## Background

The Omarchy bar widget (`omarchy/`) runs omaddons command lines for everything it does. Today its updates and installs run **without a preview**, by design (M3-D9: "updates are undoable and expected"): Enter on an Updates row runs `omaddons update -t <client> -- <addon>`, `u` runs `omaddons update` (or `-t <client>`), and the command installs whatever is newest at that moment. Destructive actions (remove, undo, restore, backup prune) preview with `--dry-run`, show a dialog that starts on No, and confirm with `--if-match <token>`. M4 gives the CLI stored plans: every storable dry run returns a typed approval summary (`data.approval`, D4 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`, the plan store), stores the plan, and offers `omaddons apply <plan_id>` (D5 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`, `omaddons apply`), which executes exactly that plan, target by target, or refuses with `plan_stale`. This leaf makes the widget use them.

**The problem it solves.** A version match is not an approval. The Updates row says `DBM 12.1.14 → 12.1.15`, but the same version can come from another source or another release asset, and a plan can add a dependency the user never saw, remove a folder, or replace files the user edited by hand. M3's widget cannot tell, because it never looks at the plan before running it; a release landing between the badge and the key press installs something nobody saw. After this leaf, every update the widget runs is previewed first; the widget applies the stored plan directly only when the plan's canonical selection is exactly what the row showed and the CLI's typed summary says nothing more needs a person's eyes; otherwise the dialog opens and names each effect. Destructive actions keep their dialog, and its Yes runs `apply <plan_id>` of the preview instead of the command with `--if-match`: one runner path serves every previewed action.

**Milestone goals it serves:**

- **G-M4-3, what was previewed is what runs, target by target.** "The bar widget's Update buttons apply a plan directly only when its selection matches the row the user pressed and it needs no further approval (new dependencies, removals, replaced local edits, a different source). Anything else opens the dialog (M4-D28)." This leaf is that sentence.
- **G-M4-1, self-describing** (in spirit): the policy lives in the CLI's typed summary (`approval.reasons[]` from a closed set, `approval.routine`), so the widget, an agent and a future mod apply the same rule, and none of them parses a human message.
- **G-M4-6, no new risk to the engine's guarantees:** the widget adds no write path; it runs `apply` of a plan the CLI stored, and every check is the CLI's.

**Checkpoint criteria it serves** (the M4 checkpoint list, by number):

- **Criterion 8, the widget applies what it shows: the update and destructive parts.** "The Updates view's Update and Update all preview, then apply the stored plan directly only when the plan's canonical selection (client, addon, source, release and versions) matches what the view showed and its typed approval summary needs nothing more. A changed selection opens the confirmation dialog with 'Changed since you looked'. A matching selection that adds dependencies, removes folders, replaces local edits, changes source or needs a different running-client policy opens the dialog with those effects named. Missing evidence never counts as a match. Destructive actions confirm and run through `apply` of their preview's plan. `errors dismiss` keeps its read-bound token." Checked by bun and QML tests here, and on the desktop by H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the checkpoint) through IPC `state()` and a screenshot. The Issues view's repairs (the rest of criterion 8) are G2's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.2`).
- **Criterion 17, gate and checkpoint runs:** `argc gate --all` passes from a clean checkout, the widget pipeline's QML step included.
- **Criterion 6's last item** (kept): "The M3 binding of `remove`, `undo`, `backup restore`, `backup prune` and `errors dismiss` is unchanged." The CLI keeps it; the widget simply stops using `--if-match` for the four storable ones and keeps it for `errors dismiss`.

**The decisions that shape it** (the full decision log is filed as comments on the milestone epic `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`):

- **M4-D28: the widget previews updates, and applies directly only a routine plan that matches the row.**
  - The CLI says what an approval covers: every storable dry run returns `data.approval`, a typed summary with the canonical selection (per item: the client's key, the addon's identity, its source and channel, the release id and asset, the from and to versions), the scope (`dependencies_added`, `folders_removed`, `local_changes_replaced`, `source_changed`, the running-client policy), `reasons[]` from a closed set naming each effect that needs a person's eyes, and `routine`, true only when `reasons[]` is empty.
  - Update, Update all and per-addon updates run the command's `--dry-run`, then compare the plan's canonical selection with what the view showed. Equal and routine: run `apply <plan_id>` with no dialog. Equal but not routine (a dependency added, a folder removed, local edits replaced, another source, a different running-client policy): the dialog opens with each effect in plain words from `reasons[]`, starting on No; the widget never infers safety by parsing warning text. Different: the dialog opens with "Changed since you looked" and the new plan, starting on No. **Missing evidence is not equality:** a row or a plan without one of the compared fields counts as different. Nothing to do (`plan_id: null` and no changes): refresh the view.
  - Destructive actions keep their dialog, and its Yes now runs `apply <plan_id>` of the preview, not the command with `--if-match`. One runner path serves every previewed action. `errors dismiss` keeps binding to the read (M3-D19, M4-D22).
  - Plan errors: `plan_not_found`, `plan_stale` and an expired plan all re-preview from the original action, never re-run `apply`.
  - Timing: a network preview gets the lane's network deadline (`WIDGET_NETWORK_DEADLINE_SEC`, 600 s of inactivity).
  - Classifier: `CLI_PATHS` gains `apply` (D5 adds the row), which may be classified only from a preview's own `commands[]` with a matching `plan_id`, never from remediation or fix argv.
  - **Why:** vision §5.11 says "mutating buttons first fetch a plan and then call `apply <plan_id>` for the plan shown" (deferred by M3-D9). Matching `{target, name, from_version, to_version}` alone does not establish what the user approves. The rule keeps the common case (a routine update the user saw) to one key press, as in M3, and asks exactly when the world changed or the plan does more than the row said.
  - **Rejected:** (i) a dialog for every update (friction where nothing changed); (ii) keeping updates unpreviewed (a release landing between the badge and the press installs something the user never saw); (iii) a version-only match, which an earlier draft had (it auto-applied plans that did more than the row showed). Do not be tempted by (iii) when a field is hard to carry: a missing field opens the dialog.
  - **Departure:** supersedes M3-D9's "the widget runs commands directly" for updates.
- **M4-D48 (the part this leaf owns):** the published issue id `fm-concurrency_primitives-journal-pending` is narrowed by F1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1`) to "a journal recovery can settle", with six new ids for the stuck states. That is safe for the widget only because the widget matches no issue id by name (it lists `issues[]` generically). This leaf confirms it, permanently, with a scan of `omarchy/` (check 10 below).
- **M4-D22 (context):** the storable commands are `install`, `update`, `pin`, `unpin`, `adopt` (when it adopts), `sync`, `copy`, `remove`, `undo`, `backup restore`, `backup prune`. `errors dismiss`, `doctor fix` and `doctor gc` bind with `--if-match` and store nothing. `apply` neither stores nor binds: it carries its plan's own token and refuses `--if-match`. `targets rm` neither stores nor binds.
- **M4-D23 (context):** `omaddons apply <PLAN_ID>` executes the stored typed intent bound to its stored token; its envelope's `command` is `"apply"`, its exit code is the executed command's, and its `data` is `{plan_id, applied: {command, display_argv}, approved?, result, outcomes[]}`, where `result` is the executed command's own data.
- **M4-D24 and M4-D61 (context):** a dry run that would change nothing stores no plan (`plan_id: null`, an empty `approval.selection`, no `apply` offer); a full store or a write failure returns the preview with `plan_id: null` and the warning `plan_not_stored`, never evicting a live plan. `apply` refuses with `plan_stale` (`details.reason`: `expired`, `binary_changed`, `input_missing`, `already_applied`; or `details.changed` from the re-plan), `plan_not_found` (unknown, unreadable or oversized), or `locked` (5, retryable, `details.lease`) when another applier holds the plan's lease. The guarantee is per target: `outcomes[]` reports each target `committed`, `unchanged`, `stale` or `failed`.
- **M4-D25 (context):** a transaction committed by `apply` records the plan's `display_argv`; `actor` is the applier's and `reason` is `apply`'s own `--reason`, else the plan's. The widget passes `--actor widget --reason "<label> (bar widget)"` to the preview and to `apply` alike.
- **M3 rules this leaf keeps** (vision §5.11 as M3 built it): argv only, from the widget's own template table (`Model.buildArgv`) or from CLI output its classifier accepted (`Model.cliArgv`), never a shell or a string (M3-D2); plain text only (M3-D21); no file writes (M3-D3); every omaddons process under the stamped context `Build.CONTEXT` (M3-D7); the lanes and their scheduler (M3-D11); the widget pipeline with fixtures the binary writes (M3-D41); a binary from another build turns the widget read-only (M3-D42); a token mismatch is the non-retryable `plan_stale` whose fix is the preview again (M3-D46).

**Facts this bead relies on** (as of `c0ab5e9`, each verified in the source; corrections marked):

- The template table `COMMANDS` is `omarchy/Model.js:99-127` (between `// BEGIN COMMANDS` and `// END COMMANDS`). Previews are marked today by `"confirm": true` on `remove`, `restore`, `restore_addon` and `prune_backup` (`:110`, `:122-124`). There is **no `undo` template**: Undo last runs `status.last_change.undo.argv` through `Service.runCliArgv` (`omarchy/PanelView.qml:247-250`), and a result's Undo runs its `commands[]` entry the same way (`PanelView.qml:258-261`, `Model.resultUndo` at `Model.js:2188-2201`).
- `CLI_PATHS` is `Model.js:134-177`, held equal to `app::COMMANDS` by `tests/omarchy_widget.rs:29-51`: the registry equality at `:33`, `mutates` at `:35`, `destructive` against the test's own `DESTRUCTIVE` list (`:561-567`) at `:36-40`, and `binds` against `BINDING_COMMANDS` at `:42-46`. *Correction:* the plan cites `:44-48` for the `binds` rule; at `c0ab5e9` it is `:42-46`.
- "Confirm ⇔ destructive" is held by `tests/omarchy_widget.rs:66-74`, `omarchy/tests/model.test.js:240` and `omarchy/tests/security.test.js:484-495` (the `needing` list at `:486`).
- The preview flow: `Service.run` (`omarchy/Service.qml:331-346`) previews a `confirm` template or a destructive path through `previewOf` (`:321-327`); `runCliArgv` (`:362-380`) previews a destructive CLI argv; `confirmYes` (`:384-398`) runs the real command with the preview's token (binding paths) or `confirmed: true` (`targets rm`); `applyAction`'s preview branch (`:617-631`) builds the dialog from `Model.confirmText` and the token from `data.precondition`; a confirmed run that comes back `plan_stale` previews again (`:650-652`).
- `Model.ifMatchFor` (`Model.js:309-324`) enforces "a destructive run needs its preview's token, or an explicit confirmation where the path does not bind". `updateRequest` (`Model.js:1602-1607`) runs `update_all`/`update_target` "with no confirmation: undoable and expected, M3-D9".
- **The Updates view's rows come from `list -v`, not from `status`.** `Model.updateRows(lists, filter, statusTargets)` (`Model.js:1653-1675`) builds them from `Model.reduceList` (`Model.js:946-982`) of the `list` template (`["list", "-v"]`, `Model.js:102`); `views/UpdatesView.qml:21` binds them. `status` has **no per-addon update entries**: `StatusTarget.updates` is per-target counts (`src/app/status.rs:217-218`, `UpdateCounts` at `:263-277`). The per-addon update entry is `list`'s `ListAddon.latest` (`src/app/list.rs:94-95`), today `Latest {version, status}` (`src/app/list.rs:112-118`), built at `src/app/list.rs:286-297` from the shared evaluator's `UpdateStatus::latest()` (`src/resolve/updates.rs:155-165`). *Correction:* the plan says the row comes from "`status`'s update entries" and that this leaf edits `src/app/status.rs`; the keys go on `list`'s `latest` instead (see the Technical Approach, step 1).
- `list`'s row already carries the target key (`ListTarget.key`, `src/app/list.rs:55`), the addon name, the installed version, the ref and the record's channel (`src/app/list.rs:78-84`). `ReleaseBrief` (`src/resolve/updates.rs:100-114`) carries `version`, `release_id`, `published_at`, `channel`; it has no asset, though the evaluator knows the best candidate's asset (`best.asset.filename`, `src/resolve/updates.rs:234-242`, `:267`; `Candidate.asset: Asset {filename, …}`, `src/model.rs:1304-1315`, `:1157-1167`). *Correction:* the plan compares the asset but adds only `source` and `release_id` to the row; without an asset on the row, no update could ever match.
- `SourceId` serializes snake case (`github`, `git`, `url`, `local`, `wowi`, `tukui`, `curseforge`, `wago`, `wowace`; `src/sources/mod.rs:81-96`, `wire()` at `:125-137`); the approval's `source` uses the same vocabulary (`"source":"github"` in the approval example below). `Model.sourceKind` (`Model.js:1631-1638`) is a different, display-only vocabulary (`gh`, `wowi`, …) and must not be compared with it.
- The plan id is a ULID, `^[0-9A-HJKMNP-TV-Z]{26}$` (the `ulid_id!` macro, `src/model.rs:222-278`, its schema pattern at `:273`; `PlanId` at `:290-294`).
- Search results carry no version, release or asset (`SearchResult`, `src/app/search.rs:76-90`), so an install from Search can never match a plan.
- Three more views start updates or installs: the Installed view's Enter (`views/InstalledView.qml:40`, `Model.rowAction` at `Model.js:1731-1739`), the Issues view's Enter on an erroring addon with an update (`views/IssuesView.qml:65`) and the Search view's install (`views/SearchView.qml:76`). The restore chooser (`RestoreChooser.qml:110-114`) and the Backups view (`views/BackupsView.qml:60`) run the confirm templates.
- The mutation lane has **no deadline** (`Service.qml:1059-1064`); only the local and network lanes do (`:1066-1081`). The network lane's deadline is one of inactivity, reset by every progress line (`Service.qml:959-973`).
- The scheduler lets a newer user mutation replace the queued one (`Model.enqueue`, `Model.js:530-563`). An `apply` enqueued when its preview finishes would therefore replace (silently drop) a change the user queued meanwhile; this leaf front-queues continuations instead.
- The widget pipeline (`scripts/widget-test.sh`): step 1 runs `write_widget_fixtures` (`tests/omarchy_widget.rs:1139-1342`), step 2 `bun test` over `omarchy/tests/model.test.js` and `security.test.js`, which writes `built-argv.json` (`model.test.js:1144-1197`), step 3 `validate_built_argv` (`tests/omarchy_widget.rs:399-545`), and step 4 (with `--qml`, or in the gate whenever `omarchy/` changed) `qmltestrunner` over a copy of the plugin with the fixture `Build.js` (`omarchy/tests/fixtures/Build.js`, whose `TOOL_VERSION` is `0.0.0-fixture`). The QML suites today answer their mock processes with hand-written envelopes (`omarchy/tests/qml/tst_service.qml:77-104`).
- `the_output_cap_bounds_every_template` (`tests/omarchy_widget.rs:296-392`) bounds every template's worst case (12 clients, 400 addons each) below `WIDGET_OUTPUT_MAX_BYTES` (8 MiB, `Model.js:88`).
- No runtime file under `omarchy/` holds a failure-mode id literal (`fm-…`) today (a grep at `c0ab5e9`), and none compares an issue's `id` with a literal.
- The widget reads warning messages only to display them, selected by code: `Model.warningMessages` (`Model.js:1346-1354`, used for `still_required` and `before_restore_skipped`) and `Model.warningsOf` (`Model.js:904-918`).

**How it serves the vision.** The thesis is that omaddons stays the sole, safe, undoable authority over what it manages. A bar button is the most casual way to change addons; after this leaf, even a casual press installs exactly what the row showed or asks first, and never acts on a guess.

## Technical Approach

### 1. The row's identity: `list`'s `latest` names the release it was judged on (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.1)

`selectionMatches` (step 2) compares, per item, eight fields: `target_key`, `addon`, `source`, `channel`, `release_id`, `asset`, `from_version`, `to_version`. The row already has the target key, the addon, the channel and both versions. It gains the other three on `list`'s per-addon `latest` object, the update entry the Updates view reads:

```json
{"name":"Foo","version":"v1","version_confidence":"release","ref":"gh:o/foo","channel":"stable","pinned":false,
 "latest":{"version":"v2","status":"update_available","source":"github","release_id":"gh:o/foo@v2","asset":"Foo.zip"}}
```

- `source`: the `SourceId` wire name of the record's ref (`SourceId::of(&record.r#ref)`), the source whose memo entry the status was judged from.
- `release_id`: the `ReleaseBrief.release_id` the status names.
- `asset`: the file name of the candidate the status was judged on (`best.asset.filename`, the candidate `update` tries first).
- All three are present on every row (rule 2 of M4-D55: a key is always present, `null` when it has no value) and are `null` exactly when the status names no release (`unchecked`, `failed`, `static`, and `pinned` with no newer release known), as `latest.version` already is.
- `asset` travels from the evaluator to `list` on `ReleaseBrief` as a field with `#[serde(skip)]` (and so no schema entry), so `outdated`'s and `info`'s wire is unchanged.
- *Decided while writing this bead:* the keys go on `list` (`src/app/list.rs`), not `status`, because `list -v` is what the Updates view reads and `status` carries no per-addon entries; `src/app/status.rs` (a hot spot of E1 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`, F1 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1`, F8 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.8` and E10 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.10`) is not touched. The third key `asset` is added because the plan's comparison includes the asset and "a missing field is a mismatch": without it, no update could ever be routine, which would contradict the plan's own acceptance ("an ordinary matching update proceeds directly"). Record all three keys in the close comment; H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`) audits them.
- A parity test proves that the row and the plan speak one vocabulary: after `outdated`, `list --json`'s `latest.{source, release_id, asset}` equals `update <addon> --dry-run --json`'s `data.approval.selection[0].{source, release_id, asset}`, and `latest.version` its `to_version`. If D4's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`, the plan store) approval spells any of them differently (an asset path instead of a file name, say), that is a defect: file it `discovered-from` this bead against the side that differs from `Candidate.asset.filename` and `SourceId`, and do not paper over it in the widget.

### 2. `omarchy/Model.js`: the pure decisions (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.2, then omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.3)

All new functions are engine-neutral JavaScript (ES2017 at most, `var`/`function`, no QML globals), exported for bun at the end of the file, and decide nothing from a warning's text.

**2.1 Templates and the plan paths.** Each template that previews gains `"preview": "match"` or `"preview": "confirm"`, and the `"confirm": true` key is removed (subtask 3):

| Template | `preview` | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `update_addon`, `update_target`, `update_all`, `install` | `match` | the row (or rows) say what the user expects; a routine plan that matches applies directly |
| `remove`, `restore`, `restore_addon`, `prune_backup` | `confirm` | destructive: always the dialog |
| `reinstall` | `confirm` | *Decided while writing this bead:* a reinstall replaces files, its approval always carries the `reinstall` reason (never routine), and the Installed row carries no installed release id to compare; `confirm` says that directly |
| `pin`, `unpin` | none | *Decided while writing this bead:* the templates carry no `--version`, so they change only the record's pin flag (`src/app/pin.rs:1-9`), are undoable, and keep M3-D9's direct run |
| `backup_target`, `backup_all`, `backup_auto` | none | not storable (`backup create` changes nothing a preview would describe, M4-D22) |
| `dismiss_errors` | none (`bind`) | keeps its read-bound token (M4-D22) |

`var PLAN_PATHS = [...]` (between `// BEGIN PLAN_PATHS` and `// END PLAN_PATHS`, a JSON literal) lists the CLI paths whose dry runs store plans: `install`, `update`, `pin`, `unpin`, `adopt`, `sync`, `copy`, `remove`, `undo`, `backup restore`, `backup prune`. A Rust test holds it equal to the `app::COMMANDS` rows with `stores_plan: true` (the field of A1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1`, set by D4). `Model.storesPlan(path)` reads it. The runner confirms through `apply` exactly on these paths; a destructive path outside them (`targets rm`) keeps M3's explicit confirmation, and a binding path outside them (`errors dismiss`; `doctor fix` and `doctor gc` once G2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.2`, lands) keeps `--if-match`.

**2.2 `planFrom(env)`: the only source of an `apply` argv.** It returns `{planId, argv, destructive, expiresAt, approval}` or `null`:

- `env` is a compatible envelope with `ok: true` and `data`;
- `data.plan_id` is a string matching `PLAN_ID_PATTERN` (`/^[0-9A-HJKMNP-TV-Z]{26}$/`, the ULID form), so a hostile id (`--json`, `-t`, `../x`, a lower-case or short id) yields `null`;
- `env.commands[]` holds **exactly one** entry with `action === "apply"` whose `argv` is exactly `["omaddons", "apply", data.plan_id]` (three elements; another id, an extra argument, a second offer, or `argv[0]` other than `omaddons` all yield `null`);
- `approvalOf(data.approval)` is not `null`.

**2.3 `approvalOf(raw)`: the typed summary, fail-closed.** `null` unless `raw` is an object with a boolean `routine`, an array `reasons` of strings and an array `selection` of objects. It returns `{routine, reasons, selection, scope}` where `routine` is `raw.routine === true && reasons.length === 0` (a summary that says routine while listing a reason is not routine), each selection item is normalized to `{target_key, target_id, addon, source, channel, release_id, asset, from_version, to_version, op}` (strings or `null`), and `scope` is the object given, or `{}`. The shape it reads is D4's (the plan store's §6.9.2, reproduced here):

```json
"approval":{"routine":false,"reasons":["dependency_added"],
  "selection":[{"target_key":"01M5…","target_id":"era","addon":"weakauras","source":"github","channel":"stable",
                "release_id":"gh:…@v5.22.1","asset":"WeakAuras-5.22.1.zip","from_version":null,
                "to_version":"5.22.1","op":"install"}],
  "scope":{"dependencies_added":["libdeflate"],"folders_removed":[],
           "local_changes_replaced":{"count":0,"folders":[]},"source_changed":[],"while_running":false}}
```

The reason set is closed: `dependency_added`, `folders_removed`, `local_changes_replaced`, `source_changed`, `channel_changed`, `while_running`, `reinstall`, `force`, `downgrade`.

**2.4 What the view showed.** `reduceList` keeps, per addon, `channel`, `latestSource`, `latestReleaseId` and `latestAsset` (beside the existing `latest`, `version`, `ref`, `source`); `updateRows` and `installedRows` rows gain `targetKey`, `channel`, `latestSource`, `latestReleaseId`, `latestAsset` (and `installedRows` gains `latest`).

- `shownOf(row)` returns the canonical item `{target_key, target_id, addon, source, channel, release_id, asset, from_version, to_version}` from a row (`source` from `latestSource`, never from the display `source`).
- `shownForAddon(lists, target, addon)` returns `[shownOf(row)]` for the matching list addon, or `[{target_id, addon}]` (the rest missing, so it never matches) when the lists are not read or name no such addon.
- `updateRequest(filter, rows)` returns `{template, slots, label, shown}` with `shown` = `shownOf` of every row of kind `update` (in the filter); `rowAction(row, "update")` adds `shown: [shownOf(row)]`.

**2.5 `selectionMatches(shown, selection)`**: true only when both are non-empty arrays of the same length, every shown item pairs with exactly one selection item by `target_key` and `addon` (the addon compared ignoring ASCII case, the CLI's own identity rule), no pairing key repeats on either side, and for every pair every field of `MATCH_FIELDS = ["target_key", "addon", "source", "channel", "release_id", "asset", "from_version", "to_version"]` is present on both sides and equal (exact string equality, except `addon`). A field is present only when it is a non-empty string; `null`, `undefined` and `""` are missing. *Decided while writing this bead:* these exact equality rules; a spelling difference opens the dialog, which is safe.

`requestedItems(approval)` returns the selection without the items whose addon (ignoring case) the scope lists in `dependencies_added` (strings, or objects with `addon` or `name`). The comparison runs on `requestedItems`, so a matching update that adds a dependency lands in "equal but not routine" (the dialog names the dependency) rather than "different". *Decided while writing this bead:* whatever D4 puts in the selection for a dependency, it never makes a matching row look changed.

**2.6 The words.** Every text is plain, fixed in `Model.js`, and built only from typed fields:

- `reasonText(reason, scope)` returns lines (decided while writing this bead):

  | Reason | Line(s) |
  |---|---|
  | `dependency_added` | one per entry of `scope.dependencies_added`: "Also installs LibDeflate 1.0.2 (a new dependency)" (the version when the entry or a selection item gives one) |
  | `folders_removed` | one per entry of `scope.folders_removed`: "Removes the folder Foo_Options (kept for undo)" |
  | `local_changes_replaced` | "Replaces 2 files you changed in DBM-Core (kept for undo)" (`count` files, `folders` joined) |
  | `source_changed` | one per entry: "Foo comes from another source now" (with "from wowi" when the entry names it) |
  | `channel_changed` | "Follows another release channel than the one installed" |
  | `while_running` | "Changes files while the game is running (/reload in game afterwards)" |
  | `reinstall` | "Reinstalls over the installed files" |
  | `force` | "Takes over folders another addon owns (--force)" |
  | `downgrade` | "Installs an older version than the one installed" |
  | anything else | "Also: <the reason, underscores as spaces>"; never routine |

- `planItemLines(selection)`: "Update Foo v1 → v2 on retail", "Install WeakAuras 5.22.1 on era", "Remove Baz v1 from retail", "Reinstall Foo v1 on retail", else "<Op> <addon> on <client>"; at most `WIDGET_DIALOG_ITEMS_MAX` (12, a UI constant in `Model.js` beside the other `WIDGET_*` constants) lines, then "(and N more)".
- `changeLines(shown, selection)`: one short phrase per difference: "Foo v3 is now the newest" (`to_version`), "Foo v2 is another release now" (`release_id` only), "Foo v2 comes in another file now (Foo-v2-retail.zip)" (`asset`), "Foo comes from wowi now" (`source`), "Foo follows beta now" (`channel`), "Foo on retail is at v1.1 now" (`from_version`), "Also: Update Bar v1 → v2 on retail (not in the view)" (an added item), "Bar on era is no longer part of it" (a dropped item), "the view did not show Foo's release, asset" (fields missing on the row), "the preview did not say Foo's asset" (fields missing on the plan). The heading is "Changed since you looked: " and the first three phrases joined by "; ", then "; and N more".
- `staleText(env)` (extended): the existing "Changed since you looked: <details.changed joined>. Nothing ran; check the new preview." for `plan_stale` with `details.changed`; for `details.reason`: `expired` → "The plan expired.", `binary_changed` → "omaddons changed since the preview.", `input_missing` → "A file the plan needs is gone.", `already_applied` → "The plan was applied already."; for `plan_not_found` → "The plan is gone (expired or cleared)."; for an `apply` whose `outcomes[]` holds a `stale` target → "Changed since you looked on era." Each ends "Nothing ran<there>; check the new preview."

**2.7 `previewDecision(spec, env)`: the routine rule.** `spec` is `{mode, shown, again}`; it returns `{kind, plan, heading, lines, line, fixText}`:

| Case | `kind` |
|---|---|
| the envelope failed | `failed` (the service shows the error, as today) |
| `approvalOf(data.approval)` is `null` | `refuse`: "The preview did not say what it would change; nothing ran" |
| `plan_id: null` and an empty selection | `refresh`: "Already up to date; the view is refreshed" (`match`) or "Nothing to do; the view is refreshed" (`confirm`) |
| `plan_id: null` and a non-empty selection (the store full, or a write failure) | `refuse`: "The preview could not be kept as a plan; nothing ran", with the `plan_not_stored` warning's `fix` (selected by code) as `fixText` |
| `planFrom(env)` is `null` | `refuse`: "The preview offered no plan to apply; nothing ran" |
| `confirm` | `dialog`: `confirmText(path, env)`'s lines, then the reason lines |
| `match`, `selectionMatches(shown, requestedItems(approval))`, `approval.routine`, the offer not `destructive`, and not `again` | `direct` (apply the plan with no dialog) |
| `match`, equal, not routine (or `again`) | `dialog`: the item lines, then the reason lines; no heading |
| `match`, different, `shown` non-empty | `dialog`: heading "Changed since you looked: …", the item lines, the reason lines |
| `match`, `shown` empty (an install from Search) | `dialog`: the item lines and reason lines, no heading |

Decided while writing this bead:
- *A plan cannot be kept (`plan_id: null` with changes):* nothing runs, and there is no fallback to `--if-match`: one runner path, `apply` only of a stored plan.
- *A re-preview after a refused `apply` (`again`) always opens the dialog,* even when the fresh plan is routine and matches: a person decides after a refusal, and no automatic retry loop can form.
- *An empty `shown` drops the heading:* nothing was shown that could have changed, so "Changed since you looked" would be false; the dialog still starts on No and nothing auto-applies.
- *An offer marked `destructive: true` never applies without the dialog,* whatever the template says.
- *The widget never judges a plan's expiry by its own clock:* `apply` refuses an expired plan and the widget re-previews.

**2.8 Reading an `apply` result.** `applyResult(env)` returns, for an envelope whose `command` is `"apply"` and whose `data` has `applied.command` and `result`, the inner view `{ok, schema_version, tool_version, command: data.applied.command, exit_code, partial, data: data.result, warnings, commands, error, outcomes: data.outcomes}`, else `null`. `resultLine`, `failedItems`, `itemFixes` and `commandResultLine` then read it as the executed command's envelope ("Updated 1 addon · /reload in game", "Removed 1 addon", "Undid update on retail"). `needsPreviewAgain(env)` is true for an `apply` refused with `plan_stale` or `plan_not_found`, and for one whose `outcomes[]` holds a `stale` target; false for `locked`, other failures and success.

**2.9 The classifier and the builders.**

- `classifyCliArgv(argv, plan)`: an `apply` argv is refused with reason `apply_outside_plan` unless `plan` is a `planFrom` result whose `argv` equals it element for element. Every existing caller (`cliAction` for fixes, alternatives, remediations, `commands[]`, `last_change.undo`) passes no plan, so an `apply` from any of them is never a button.
- `cliArgv(argv, opts)`: an `apply` argv builds only with `opts.plan` (as above), never as a preview and never with a token; it gets the standard flags and `--progress json` and nothing else. A token on a plan-storing path is refused with `runs_through_apply` (subtask 3).
- `buildArgv(name, slots, opts)`: a template with `preview` builds only with `opts.preview === true`; otherwise it is refused with `preview_required` (subtask 3).
- **The scheduler:** a request with `continuation: true` (the `apply` that continues a preview, and a re-preview after a refused `apply`) is queued at the front of the mutation lane and replaces nothing; every other rule of `enqueue` and `nextRequest` is unchanged.

### 3. `omarchy/Service.qml`: the previewed-action runner (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.3)

It replaces `previewOf`'s destructive-only path:

```text
run(name, slots, label, shown)              runCliArgv(argv, label)
  template.preview "match" | "confirm"         destructive path → mode "confirm"
        │                                              │
        └─────────────── previewOf(spec{mode, shown}, stale, again) ───────┐
                 mutation lane, --dry-run; "match": the network deadline     │
                 (WIDGET_NETWORK_DEADLINE_SEC of inactivity) and "Preparing…" │
                                                                              ▼
 applyAction(purpose "preview"):  path not in PLAN_PATHS → M3's dialog (token or confirmed), unchanged
                                  else Model.previewDecision(spec, env):
   refresh → lastResult line, changed()          refuse → lastError (line, fixText), nothing runs
   direct  → runPlan(plan)                        dialog  → confirm {text, heading, stale}, pendingConfirm {spec, plan}
                                                                 │ Yes (confirmYes) → runPlan(plan)
 runPlan(plan, spec, generation): mutation {cli: plan.argv, plan, purpose "planned", continuation: true}
   → argvOf → Model.cliArgv(plan.argv, {plan}) → omaddons --json --actor widget --reason "<label> (bar widget)"
                                                  --progress json apply <plan_id>
 applyAction(purpose "planned"): Model.applyResult(env) → lastResult (line, partial, commands, fixes)
   Model.needsPreviewAgain(env) → previewOf(spec, Model.staleText(env), again: true)   (apply is never re-run)
   then the toast rule (panel closed) and changed(), as today
```

- `request()` gains the defaults `"mode": ""`, `"shown": null`, `"again": false`, `"plan": null`, `"continuation": false`, `"deadlineMs": -1`, `"inactivity": false`. `argvOf` passes `"plan": r.plan || null` in its options; its single `return r.cli ? Model.cliArgv(r.cli, opts) : Model.buildArgv(r.template, r.slots, opts)` stays (scan 3 checks it).
- `Lane` gains a per-run deadline: `run(r, argv, env)` sets `runDeadlineMs` to `r.deadlineMs` when it is a number ≥ 0, else the lane's `deadlineMs`, and `runInactivity` likewise; the `deadline` timer and `line()` read them. Only a `match` preview sets them (`networkDeadlineMs`, inactivity); confirm previews and every `apply` keep the mutation lane's no-deadline rule. *Decided while writing this bead:* an `apply` is never killed by a timeout, because killing a commit is never a timeout policy.
- `startAction` shows "Preparing…" for a `match` preview (decided while writing this bead, after §4.5's footer), "Checking what it would do…" for a confirm preview, and progress lines replace it as they come.
- `confirmYes` runs `runPlan(pending.plan, …)` when the pending confirmation has a plan, else M3's mutation with the token or `confirmed: true`, unchanged. A confirmation from another context generation never runs (the existing check in `pump`).
- `stateJson()` gains `"confirm"` (`{heading, planId}` or `null`) and `"lastPreview"` (`{resource, decision, planId}` or `null`, where `decision` is `direct`, `dialog`, `refresh`, `refuse` or `failed`). *Decided while writing this bead:* these two keys, so the desktop check of H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the checkpoint) reads the decision from IPC `state()` beside its screenshot.

### 5. Security scans (`omarchy/tests/security.test.js`, omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.4)

Each new check passes on the real source and catches its planted violation:

- **Rule 3, argv provenance, for `apply`:** the literal `"apply"` appears in runtime code only in Model.js's `CLI_PATHS` block and the bodies of `planFrom`, `classifyCliArgv`, `cliArgv`, `applyResult` and `needsPreviewAgain`, never in a QML file and never in an array literal; in `Service.qml`, a request's `"plan":` value comes only from `Model.previewDecision`'s plan (through `runPlan(decision.plan, …)` and `runPlan(pending.plan, …)`), and `argvOf` passes `r.plan`. Planted: a hand-built `["omaddons", "apply", id]` in `Service.qml`; a `"plan":` built from a literal.
- **Rule 6, previews:** every mutating template whose path is in `PLAN_PATHS` has `preview` (`match` or `confirm`), except `pin` and `unpin`, which must carry no `--version`; every destructive path's template has `preview: "confirm"`; no template keeps a `confirm` key; `run` routes every template with `preview` to `previewOf`, and `runCliArgv` every destructive argv. Planted: `update_addon` without `preview`; a template with `"confirm": true`.
- **Check 9, warnings decide nothing:** in Model.js only `warningsOf` and `warningMessages` read a warning's `message`; no line uses `warningMessages(` in a comparison (`===`, `!==`, `indexOf(`, `.test(`, `.match(`, `includes(`, `some(`, `find(`, `filter(`); `planFrom`, `approvalOf`, `selectionMatches`, `requestedItems`, `previewDecision`, `reasonText` and `changeLines` never mention `warnings` or `message`; no QML line compares a warning's `message`. Planted: `previewDecision` reading `env.warnings[0].message`; a function testing a warning message with `indexOf`.
- **Check 10, no issue id by name (M4-D48):** no runtime file holds a failure-mode id literal (`/["'`]fm-[a-z]/`) or compares an issue's `id` with a string literal. Planted: `if (row.id === "fm-concurrency_primitives-journal-pending")` in `IssuesView.qml`.

### 9. Files

`src/app/list.rs`, `src/resolve/updates.rs`, `tests/list.rs`, `tests/contract/snapshots/contract__matrix__list_ok.snap` (re-accepted), `omarchy/Model.js`, `omarchy/Service.qml`, `omarchy/PanelView.qml`, `omarchy/views/{UpdatesView,InstalledView,IssuesView,SearchView}.qml`, `omarchy/tests/model.test.js`, `omarchy/tests/security.test.js`, `omarchy/tests/qml/{tst_service,tst_panel,tst_views,tst_plans}.qml`, `omarchy/tests/qml_fixtures.js` (new, test-only), `scripts/widget-test.sh`, `tests/omarchy_widget.rs`, `README.md`.

### 10. Wire names for the close comment (common rule 6)

New data keys on `list`: `targets[].addons[].latest.source`, `latest.release_id`, `latest.asset`. No error code, warning, `details` key, action, event or file. The widget's own additions (not CLI contract): IPC `state()` keys `confirm` and `lastPreview`; Model.js refusal reasons `preview_required`, `runs_through_apply`, `apply_outside_plan`. Common rule 16: this leaf adds no mutating command path; the widget's runs are bound through `apply` (M4-D23).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `list --json`'s every addon carries `latest {version, status, source, release_id, asset}`, the three new keys always present and `null` exactly when the status names no release; after `outdated`, they equal `update <addon> --dry-run --json`'s `data.approval.selection[0].{source, release_id, asset}` (and `latest.version` its `to_version`) on a GitHub addon; `outdated --json`'s envelope is unchanged by the new internal field; the `list_ok` contract snapshot is re-accepted with only those keys added.
- [ ] §3.2 criterion 8's update part, in bun and QML tests over envelopes the binary writes: an ordinary matching update proceeds directly (the next launch is `apply <plan_id>` of the preview, and no dialog opens); a dependency added by the preview, locally modified files about to be replaced and an extra removal each open the dialog with that effect named in plain words; equal versions with a changed asset (real fixture) or a changed source (derived) open the dialog with "Changed since you looked"; a release that moved since the row was read opens it with "Changed since you looked: Foo v3 is now the newest"; a row or a plan missing any compared field never matches.
- [ ] Update all compares every update row in the filter: all matching and routine → one `apply`; one row missing, added or moved → the dialog.
- [ ] §3.2 criterion 8's destructive part: `remove`, `restore`, `restore_addon`, `prune_backup`, `reinstall` and Undo last (and a result's Undo) open the dialog starting on No, and Yes runs `apply <plan_id>` of their preview; no previewed action ever runs the command with `--if-match`.
- [ ] A refused `apply` (`plan_stale` with each `details.reason`, `plan_stale` with `details.changed`, `plan_not_found`, or a `stale` target in `outcomes[]`) re-runs the original action's preview and reopens the dialog; `apply` is never re-run, and a re-preview never auto-applies.
- [ ] A preview with `plan_id: null` and nothing to change refreshes the view and runs nothing; one with changes but no stored plan, or without a readable approval, or whose `apply` offer names another id, runs nothing and says why.
- [ ] `apply` is classified only from a preview's own `commands[]` with the matching `plan_id`: an `apply` argv in a fix, an alternative, a remediation, another envelope's `commands[]` or `last_change.undo` is refused (`apply_outside_plan`); `validate_built_argv` parses every `apply` argv bun built from a fixture preview as path `apply` with the widget's flags, no `--dry-run` and no `--if-match`.
- [ ] `errors dismiss` keeps its read-bound `--if-match`; `targets rm` keeps its explicit confirmation; `pin` and `unpin` run directly; non-destructive CLI argv run as in M3.
- [ ] A `match` preview runs under the network lane's inactivity deadline (`WIDGET_NETWORK_DEADLINE_SEC`); an `apply` and a confirm preview run under none; a planned `apply` goes first and replaces no queued change.
- [ ] The security scans (rule 3 for `apply`, rule 6 for `preview`, check 9 for warnings, check 10 for issue ids) pass on the real source and each catches its planted violation; no runtime file under `omarchy/` matches an issue id by name.
- [ ] The output-cap test covers the `update_all` preview and its `apply` envelope (12 clients, 400 addons each) below `WIDGET_OUTPUT_MAX_BYTES`.
- [ ] The QML scenarios `test_a_routine_matching_update_applies_with_no_dialog`, `test_a_matching_update_that_adds_a_dependency_opens_the_dialog_naming_it` and `test_a_moved_release_opens_the_dialog_with_changed_since_you_looked` exist in `omarchy/tests/qml/tst_plans.qml` and pass (T3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.3`, asserts them by name).
- [ ] `argc gate --all` passes, the widget pipeline's QML step included.
- [ ] README's `list` and `omarchy` sections and the FAQ entry describe the behaviour, in the commits that ship it.
- [ ] The close comment lists the three new `list` keys (common rule 6), each "decided" item with its outcome, and the facts corrected against the plan.
- [ ] `br lint omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1 --json` is clean, and so is each subtask's.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

- **`src/app/list.rs`** (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.1): `latest_names_the_release_its_status_was_judged_on`, table-driven over `UpdateStatus` values: `update_available`, `current`, `ahead`, `blocked`, `pinned` with a newer release → `source: "github"`, `release_id`, `asset` filled; `pinned` without one, `unchecked`, `failed`, `static` → all three `null`; a `wowi:` ref → `source: "wowi"`. The existing `the_latest_column_shows_only_a_newer_release` keeps its cases with the new fields.
- **`src/resolve/updates.rs`** (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.1): `brief_keeps_the_best_candidates_asset` (the evaluator's `latest` carries `best.asset.filename`, for a fresh and a looked-back status) and `release_brief_serializes_without_its_asset` (`serde_json::to_value` has no `asset` key).
- **`omarchy/tests/model.test.js`** (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.2; each a table with a name per case, the assertion message naming the case, input and output): `planFrom` (11 cases), `approvalOf` (7), `requestedItems` (4), `selectionMatches` (33: 17 named cases, and one per compared field missing on each side), `changeLines` (11), `reasonText` (every reason and an unknown one), `planItemLines` (6), `previewDecision` (13), `applyResult` (3), `needsPreviewAgain` (9), `staleText` (7), `shownOf`/`shownForAddon`/`updateRequest` (6), the classifier's `apply` rule (6), the scheduler's continuation (3). Cases are listed in omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.2.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

- **`tests/list.rs`** (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.1): `latest_carries_the_release_identity_the_plan_reports`, on `common::home::Home::new(&["wow"])` with `gh:o/foo` v1 installed and v2 published: `outdated` → `list --json` (the keys) → `outdated --json` (its `latest.release.release_id` equal, no `asset` key) → `update foo -t retail --dry-run --json` (parity with `approval.selection[0]`); then a `file:` addon and a never-checked addon (`null`s). Through the `TestLog` of T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`).
- **`tests/omarchy_widget.rs`** (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.2, omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.3, omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.5): `plan_paths_mirror_the_registry`; `every_template_is_a_registry_command_with_safe_slots` with the new invariants (destructive ⇒ `preview: "confirm"`; `match` ⇒ not destructive; `preview` ⇒ the path is in `PLAN_PATHS`; no `confirm` key); `write_widget_fixtures` gains the plan scenes (each fixture listed in omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.5); `the_plan_scenarios_read_only_fixtures_the_binary_writes`; `the_output_cap_bounds_every_template` measures the `update_all` preview and its `apply`; `validate_built_argv` parses the planned `apply` argv and accepts the `apply_outside_plan` refusals.

Names are listed in the subtasks; the three names above are fixed for T3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.3`).
- **Security scans** (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.4): the four checks and their planted violations.

### Logging

- Rust integration scenes use T1's `TestLog` (`let log = tlog!();`): one `log.step` per phase ("install v1", "check", "list", "preview", "apply", …), `log.run(&home, &argv)` for every command (argv, the env overrides, exit, the envelope, stderr events and `net.log` lines recorded), `log.json("<fixture name>", &envelope)` for each fixture written, and `log.json("parity", …)` for the compared field sets. A failure prints `test log: <path>` and the last 20 steps.
- bun tests name every case (`[case, input, output]` in the assertion, as `CLASSIFIER_TABLE` does today); a fixture-driven test names the fixture in its message.
- QML tests use `compare(actual, expected, "<what>")` messages naming the scenario step, and print the launched argv (`words(launch.command)`) on a mismatch.

### Checkpoint-only tests

None owned here. H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the checkpoint) runs the desktop check (the widget's Update on a matching plan, with IPC `state()` showing `lastPreview.decision: "direct"` and a screenshot), a run that approving the plan already authorized (it is one of the checkpoint's listed desktop runs, §3.3), so it waits on nobody; the moved-plan case is recorded from `tst_plans.qml` because no fixture server runs on the live bar.

## Considerations

- **Risk #7, widget update previews feel slow** (likelihood M, impact L; owner: this leaf). A dry run downloads and verifies, as the real run did before; the blobs are then cached, so `apply` downloads nothing (it forces one revalidation probe per ref, usually a cheap answer, and reuses the cached blobs); the footer shows "Preparing…" and then the progress lines; no dialog appears when the plan matches. Each widget update now costs two processes instead of one.
- **New risk: the row and the plan speak different vocabularies** (an asset path against a file name, `gh` against `github`), so every update opens the dialog. Safe but annoying. Watched by subtask 1's parity test and subtask 5's routine fixture, which must apply directly.
- **New risk: a matching bug auto-applies something not shown.** Guarded by the missing-field rule and its 16 cases (each compared field missing on each side), `again` and `destructive` never auto-applying, and the real-fixture scenarios for each reason.
- **Hot spots (§10.5):** `omarchy/Model.js` and `Service.qml`: **G1 → G2** (this bead, then G2 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.2`), and command leaves add only `CLI_PATHS` rows (rebase onto theirs). `src/app/status.rs` (E1 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1` → F1 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1` → F8 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.8`, then E10 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.10` and this bead in the plan's table) is not touched after all. `src/app/list.rs` and `src/resolve/updates.rs` are no other M4 leaf's. `README.md`: edit only the `list` and `omarchy` sections and the one FAQ entry.
- **Commit consistency.** `argc gate` runs the QML step whenever `omarchy/` changed, so a commit that changes the templates or `buildArgv` must change `Service.qml`, the views and the affected tests with it: that is why subtask 2 is additive only and subtask 3 is the one switch-over commit.
- **The widget digest.** Changing `omarchy/` changes the build's widget digest, so an installed widget reports `fm-plugins-widget-version-drift` until `omaddons omarchy install` (H6, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, runs it after the M4 build).
- **Compatibility.** The widget is stamped for one binary (`Build.js`'s `TOOL_VERSION`); a binary from another build turns it read-only (M3-D42), so a pre-M4 binary never meets this runner.
- **Privacy.** Every dialog line is built from typed fields (names, versions, folders, counts), shown as plain text; nothing reads `WTF/`, and a warning's message is never parsed.
- **Performance of the dialog:** at most 12 item lines plus effect lines, whatever Update all covers.
- **Size M** holds: the Rust part is small, and the widget part is one coordinated change whose pieces cannot land separately without breaking the gate.

## Dependencies

- **Parent:** the G epic `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7` (the widget and durability).
- **Blocked by:** D5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`, `omaddons apply`): the command this leaf runs, its `CLI_PATHS` row (`binds: false`), its envelope (`applied`, `result`, `outcomes[]`) and refusals (`plan_stale` with `details.reason`, `plan_not_found`, `locked`); through D5, D4's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`, the plan store) `data.plan_id`, `data.approval` and the `apply` offer in `commands[]`. Subtasks 1 and 5 are also blocked by T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`), whose `TestLog` they use.
- **Unblocks:**
  - G2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.2`, the Issues view runs doctor repairs): it extends this runner in the same files (the doctor reducer, Undo last of a repair through `apply`, the `--if-match` path for `doctor fix`, which this leaf keeps for binding paths that store no plan).
  - H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, the pre-freeze contract audit): the `list` keys `latest.source`, `latest.release_id` and `latest.asset` must exist before the audit sees the whole contract.
  - H4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`, the README final pass): the `list`, `omarchy` and FAQ text to reconcile.
  - T3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.3`, slice 2 end to end): it asserts the QML scenarios named above exist and pass, and quotes the widget pipeline's run in the slice-2 demo.
- **Delivery slice `slice-2`, "Preview, then apply exactly"** (D1–D9, E13, G1). Its exit demo includes "the widget's Update with a routine matching plan (no dialog), one that adds a dependency (dialog) and a moved one (dialog), in QML scenarios"; T3 records it, not this leaf. It pre-checks checkpoint criteria 6, 7 and 8 (updates).
- **Related, not edges:** D4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`, the approval summary and the plan store) and D9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.9`, `plans show`, which the widget does not call); D2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2`) and D3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.3`) (`binds: true` rows); A1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1`, the `stores_plan` field `PLAN_PATHS` mirrors); A3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`, the rule test the new `list` keys pass); F1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1`, the narrowing of `journal-pending` that check 10 makes safe); H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the desktop check).

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M4 plan, 2026-10-24).**

**Why this bead.** Today the bar widget's Update buttons run `omaddons update` directly (M3-D9), so a press installs whatever is newest at that moment: a release that landed after the badge was computed, an asset other than the one the row was judged on, a dependency nobody saw, files the user edited replaced. M4 gives the CLI stored plans with a typed approval summary (D4, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`) and `omaddons apply <plan_id>` (D5, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`). This bead makes the widget their client: every update and destructive action previews; a routine plan whose canonical selection is exactly what the row showed is applied with one key press, as in M3; anything else opens the dialog, starting on No, with "Changed since you looked" or one plain line per effect; a refused `apply` re-previews and never re-runs. It closes the vision's oldest widget promise ("mutating buttons first fetch a plan and then call `apply <plan_id>` for the plan shown", vision §5.11) and keeps the thesis true where changes are most casual: omaddons stays the sole, safe, undoable authority, and a bar button never acts on a guess.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M4-D28:** preview every update; apply directly only an equal and `routine` plan; equal but not routine → the dialog naming each effect from `reasons[]`; different → "Changed since you looked"; missing evidence is not equality; nothing to do → refresh; destructive actions confirm and run `apply` of their preview; `errors dismiss` keeps its read-bound token; `plan_stale`, `plan_not_found` and expiry re-preview; network previews get the network deadline; `apply` is classified only from the preview's own offer.
- **M4-D48 (this leaf's part):** the widget matches no issue id by name, which makes the narrowing of `journal-pending` by F1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1`) safe; confirmed by a permanent scan rather than a one-off grep.
- **M4-D22, M4-D23, M4-D24, M4-D25, M4-D61 (context):** which paths store plans (and so confirm through `apply`), `apply`'s envelope and refusals, the no-op and full-store previews, the applier's actor and reason, per-target outcomes.
- **M3-D2, M3-D3, M3-D7, M3-D11, M3-D21, M3-D41, M3-D42, M3-D46 (kept):** argv provenance, no file writes, the stamped context, the lanes, plain text, the binary-written fixtures, read-only on another build, and "the confirmed run is the previewed one".

**Alternatives rejected that matter here.**
- A dialog for every update (M4-D28 (i)): friction exactly where nothing changed.
- Keeping updates unpreviewed (M4-D28 (ii)): the vision's promise unmet.
- A version-only match (M4-D28 (iii), an earlier draft's): it auto-applies plans that do more than the row showed. When a field is hard to carry, the answer is to carry it (this bead adds `latest.asset`), never to stop comparing it.
- Falling back to `--if-match` when a plan cannot be stored: a second runner path, and an approval the widget did not obtain through a plan; it runs nothing and says why instead.
- Parsing warning text to detect a dependency or a removal: the CLI's typed `reasons[]` exists so that no client does that; a scan now forbids it.
- Re-running `apply` after `plan_stale`: it can only fail again, or apply something nobody saw; the widget re-previews and asks.

**Facts verified while writing the bead, and where the plan disagreed with the code.** As of `c0ab5e9`: the Updates view's rows come from `list -v` (`Model.updateRows` from `Model.reduceList`, `omarchy/Model.js:946-982`, `:1653-1675`), not from `status`, which carries only per-target update counts (`src/app/status.rs:217-218`, `:263-277`); so the release identity goes on `list`'s per-addon `latest` (`src/app/list.rs:112-118`), and `src/app/status.rs` is not touched. The plan compares the asset but adds only `source` and `release_id`; the asset is known only inside the evaluator (`best.asset.filename`, `src/resolve/updates.rs:234-242`), so `latest.asset` is added too, or no update could ever be routine. There is no `undo` template (Undo last runs the CLI's own argv, `omarchy/PanelView.qml:247-250`). `reinstall`, `pin` and `unpin` are on plan-storing paths but not in the plan's template lists (decided: `reinstall` confirms, pins stay direct). The mutation lane has no deadline at all (`omarchy/Service.qml:1059-1064`), so the network deadline for `match` previews is per request. A newer user mutation replaces the queued one (`Model.js:530-563`), which would drop a queued change when an `apply` follows its preview; continuations are front-queued instead. The plan's `tests/omarchy_widget.rs:44-48` is `:42-46` today. Search results carry no release (`src/app/search.rs:76-90`), so an install from Search always confirms.

**Risks and how they are watched.**
- Risk #7, widget update previews feel slow (M, L; owned here): the dry run is the work the real run did before, `apply` downloads nothing the preview cached, the footer shows "Preparing…" and the progress lines, and no dialog appears when the plan matches.
- A vocabulary mismatch between the row and the approval (every update opens the dialog): subtask 1's parity test and subtask 5's routine fixture, which must apply directly.
- A matching bug that auto-applies something unseen: the missing-field rule and its cases, `again` and `destructive` never auto-applying, and one real-fixture scenario per reason.
- A stale-plan loop: impossible, since a re-preview always asks a person.

**What it unblocks, and why they wait.** G2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.2`) extends this runner in the same files (the Issues view's repairs, Undo last of a repair, the doctor reducer) and needs its binding branch for `doctor fix`. H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`) audits the contract only after every leaf that adds a wire shape has landed, and this leaf adds three `list` keys. H4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`) reconciles README after every user-visible leaf, this one's `omarchy`, `list` and FAQ text included. T3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.3`) records the slice-2 demo, whose widget items are this leaf's QML scenarios.

**How it serves the milestone.** G-M4-3 (what was previewed is what runs; the widget applies a plan directly only when it matches the row and needs no further approval) and checkpoint criterion 8's update and destructive parts; criterion 17 (the gate with the QML step); G-M4-6 (no new write path: the widget only runs `apply` of plans the CLI stored).
