title: The update entry carries its release identity: `list`'s `latest` gains `source`, `release_id` and `asset`
description:
Part 1 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1 (The widget previews and applies plans). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1 makes the Omarchy bar widget preview every update, apply the stored plan directly (`omaddons apply <plan_id>`) only when the plan is exactly what the Updates row showed and the CLI's typed approval summary says nothing more needs a person's eyes, and otherwise open the confirmation dialog naming each effect (M4-D28). "Exactly what the row showed" is a comparison of eight fields per item: the client's key, the addon's identity, its source and channel, the release id and asset, and the from and to versions. A field missing on either side counts as a mismatch, never a match, so a row that cannot carry a field makes every update open the dialog.

**This part gives the row the three fields it lacks.** The Updates view's rows are built from `omaddons list -v` (the widget's `list` template, `omarchy/Model.js:102`; `Model.updateRows` from `Model.reduceList`, `Model.js:946-982`, `:1653-1675`). Each `list` addon already carries the target key (`ListTarget.key`, `src/app/list.rs:55`), its name, installed version, ref and channel (`src/app/list.rs:78-84`), and `latest {version, status}` (`src/app/list.rs:94-95`, `:112-118`): the newest release the release memo knows, judged by the shared update evaluator. It lacks the release's source (in the approval's vocabulary), its release id and its asset. This subtask adds `latest.source`, `latest.release_id` and `latest.asset`, and proves with a parity test that they equal what `update --dry-run`'s typed approval reports. It is its own step because it is Rust and a contract addition, independent of the widget code, and it can land (and be audited) before the widget uses it.

**Corrections to the plan, decided while writing this bead:**
- The plan says the row comes from "`status`'s update entries" and that this leaf edits `src/app/status.rs`. `status` has no per-addon update entries (`StatusTarget.updates` is per-target counts, `src/app/status.rs:217-218`, `UpdateCounts` at `:263-277`); the per-addon update entry is `list`'s `latest`. The keys go there, and `src/app/status.rs` is not touched.
- The plan adds only `source` and `release_id`, but compares the asset too. Without an asset on the row no update could ever match, which would contradict the plan's own acceptance ("an ordinary matching update proceeds directly"). This subtask adds `asset` as well. The close comment lists all three keys, and H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, the pre-freeze contract audit) audits them.

## Technical Approach

1. **`src/resolve/updates.rs`.** `ReleaseBrief` (`:100-114`) gains a field that never reaches the wire:

   ```rust
   /// The file name of the candidate the status was judged on (the one `update`
   /// tries first); for `list`'s update entry, never serialized.
   #[serde(skip)]
   pub asset: Option<String>,
   ```

   `brief(best, release)` (`:355-364`) sets it to `Some(best.asset.filename.clone())`; both callers (the fresh status at `:242` and the looked-back one at `:322`) pass the candidate they judged. The test literal at `:1169` gains `asset: None` (or the asset it means). `#[serde(skip)]` keeps `outdated`'s `latest.release` and `info`'s wire unchanged; schemars skips the field too, so no schema changes there.

2. **`src/app/list.rs`.** `Latest` (`:112-118`) becomes:

   ```rust
   /// What the release memo says is newest for an addon, and which release that is.
   #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, JsonSchema)]
   pub struct Latest {
       /// The newest release's version, when the status names one.
       pub version: Option<String>,
       pub status: StatusKind,
       /// The source the status was judged from (the record's ref's), when it names a release.
       pub source: Option<SourceId>,
       /// That release's id, when the status names one.
       pub release_id: Option<String>,
       /// The file of that release the status was judged on, when it names one.
       pub asset: Option<String>,
   }
   ```

   - Replace the closure at `:286-297` with a pure function `fn latest_of(status: Option<&UpdateStatus>, r#ref: &Ref) -> Latest`, so the table test can call it: `version`, `release_id` and `asset` from `UpdateStatus::latest()` (`src/resolve/updates.rs:155-165`), `source: Some(SourceId::of(r#ref))` when `latest()` is `Some`, else `None`; `status` as today (`Unchecked` when no row).
   - Field order is rendering order and not contract (M4-D56); keep `version, status` first.
   - `latest_cell` (`:537-547`) is unchanged; the human table shows nothing new.
   - All three keys are always present (M4-D55 rule 2: a key is present, `null` when it has no value), `null` exactly when the status names no release: `unchecked`, `failed`, `static`, and `pinned` without a newer release known.

   The JSON shape the widget reads:

   ```json
   "latest":{"version":"v2","status":"update_available","source":"github","release_id":"gh:o/foo@v2","asset":"Foo.zip"}
   ```

   `source` is the `SourceId` wire name (`github`, `git`, `url`, `local`, `wowi`, `tukui`, `curseforge`, `wago`, `wowace`; `src/sources/mod.rs:81-96`), the vocabulary of the approval's `source`; it is not the display kind `Model.sourceKind` gives (`gh`).

3. **Contract.** The `list_ok` matrix row (`tests/contract/matrix.rs:98-99`) re-snapshots with the new keys: review the diff for nothing but them, then accept. A3's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`) rule test passes (snake case, a closed enum for `source`, nullable rather than omitted). If A3's strict schema validation runs over the matrix, `list`'s schema (derived) already includes the keys. No volatile key, no error code, no constant. If B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`) has landed, the guide's generated blocks show no data keys, so `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` does not change; if a `robot-docs schema` snapshot exists (A5, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5`), re-accept it.

4. **README `### list`** (`README.md:1349`): "Each addon also carries `latest {version, status, source, release_id, asset}`: the newest release remembered from earlier checks, its status as `outdated` would judge it (…), and which release that is: its source (`github`, `wowi`, `tukui`, `git`, `wowace`, …), its release id and the file `update` would try first, all `null` when the status names no release." Same commit.

5. **What if the approval of D4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`) spells a field differently.** The parity test below compares this row with `update <addon> --dry-run --json`'s `data.approval.selection[0]` (D4, the plan store, computes it). If the test shows a different representation (an asset URL or path rather than a file name, a `gh` source, a differently spelled release id), do not change the widget to compensate: file a bug `discovered-from` omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1 against the side that differs from `Candidate.asset.filename`, `SourceId` and `ReleaseBrief.release_id`, and block omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1 on it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `list --json` gives every addon `latest {version, status, source, release_id, asset}`; the three new keys are always present, filled for `update_available`, `current`, `ahead`, `blocked` and `pinned` with a newer release, and `null` for `unchecked`, `failed`, `static` and `pinned` with none.
- [ ] After `outdated`, a GitHub addon's `latest.source`, `latest.release_id` and `latest.asset` equal `update <addon> -t <client> --dry-run --json`'s `data.approval.selection[0].source`, `.release_id` and `.asset`, and `latest.version` its `to_version`.
- [ ] `outdated --json`'s envelope carries no `asset` key (the field is internal), and its other tests pass unchanged.
- [ ] The `list_ok` contract snapshot is re-accepted with only the three keys added; the rule test of A3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`) passes.
- [ ] README's `list` section names the three keys, in the same commit.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

- `src/app/list.rs`, `latest_names_the_release_its_status_was_judged_on`: a table of `(case, Option<UpdateStatus>, ref, expected Latest)`, one name per case:
  - `update_available` with `ReleaseBrief {version: "v2", release_id: "gh:o/foo@v2", asset: Some("Foo.zip"), …}` and ref `gh:o/foo` → `{version: "v2", status: update_available, source: github, release_id: "gh:o/foo@v2", asset: "Foo.zip"}`;
  - `current`, `ahead`, `blocked`, `pinned_with_newer` → the same three filled;
  - `pinned_without_newer` (`Pinned {latest: None}`), `unchecked`, `failed`, `static`, `no_row` (`None`) → `source`, `release_id`, `asset` all `None`;
  - `wowi_ref` (`wowi:12345`) → `source: wowi`.
  Each assertion message names the case and prints the input and the `Latest` produced.
- `src/app/list.rs`, `the_latest_column_shows_only_a_newer_release` (existing): the literal gains the new fields; its cases are unchanged.
- `src/resolve/updates.rs`, `brief_keeps_the_best_candidates_asset`: `evaluate` on a record one release behind gives `UpdateAvailable` whose `latest.asset` is the first candidate's file name; the looked-back case (an existing look-back fixture in the module's tests) gives the found candidate's.
- `src/resolve/updates.rs`, `release_brief_serializes_without_its_asset`: `serde_json::to_value(&brief)` has exactly the keys it had before (`version`, `release_id`, `published_at`, `channel`, and `revision`/`retagged` when set).

### Integration and end-to-end tests

`tests/list.rs`, `latest_carries_the_release_identity_the_plan_reports` (uses the `TestLog` of T1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`):

1. Builder: `common::home::Home::new(&["wow"])`; `gh_release(&home.http, "https://github.com/o/foo", "v1", …)`, `gh_latest(…, "v1")`; `install gh:o/foo -t retail --json` → exit 0.
2. Publish v2 (`gh_release` and `gh_latest` for `v2`, as `support::Rel`-style assets in `tests/omarchy_widget.rs` do), then `outdated --json` → exit 0.
3. `list -t retail --json` → exit 0; assert Foo's `latest` is `{version: "v2", status: "update_available", source: "github", release_id: "gh:o/foo@v2", asset: "<the v2 asset's file name>"}`.
4. `outdated -t retail --json` → its item's `latest.release.release_id` equals `list`'s; its `latest.release` has no `asset` key.
5. `update foo -t retail --dry-run --json` → exit 0; `data.approval.selection[0]` has `source`, `release_id`, `asset` equal to `list`'s and `to_version` equal to `latest.version`; `from_version` equals `list`'s `version`; `target_key` equals `list`'s target `key`.
6. `install file:<a local zip> -t retail --json`, then `list -t retail --json`: the `file:` addon's `latest` is `{status: "static", source: null, release_id: null, asset: null, version: null}`.
7. A second home where Foo is installed and never checked (the memo emptied with the existing memo helpers): `latest.status: "unchecked"` with the three keys `null`.

### Logging

`let log = tlog!();` with `log.step` per numbered phase above ("install v1", "publish v2 and check", "list", "outdated", "preview", "a static addon", "never checked"), `log.run(&home, &argv)` for every command, and `log.json("parity", &json!({"list": …, "approval": …}))` holding the two compared field sets, so a mismatch shows both sides in the transcript. Unit tests name their case in every assertion message.

## Considerations

- **Wire addition on a surface this leaf owns**, additive (DEC-4): three keys, listed in the close comment.
- **Why a skipped field on `ReleaseBrief`:** the evaluator is the only place that knows which candidate the status was judged on; serializing it would also change `outdated`'s and `info`'s wire, which no leaf asked for. If a reviewer prefers, an equivalent is a small accessor returning the candidate's file name beside `UpdateStatus`; keep the wire as specified either way.
- **Not a hot spot:** `src/app/list.rs` and `src/resolve/updates.rs` are no other M4 leaf's files; `src/app/status.rs` (E1 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1` → F1 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1` → F8 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.8`, then E10 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.10`) is untouched.
- **What could go wrong:** the parity test fails because D4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`) chose another representation. That is the point of the test; the fix belongs to whichever side is not the CLI's existing vocabulary (step 5).
- **Performance:** nothing new is read; `list` already evaluates every addon's status.

## Dependencies

- **Parent:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1 (The widget previews and applies plans).
- **Before it:** nothing inside omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1; the leaf's blocker D5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`, `omaddons apply`) must be closed (through it, the `data.approval` of D4, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`, which the parity test reads), and T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, the structured test log) for its integration test.
- **After it:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.3 (the switch-over relies on rows that carry every compared field) and omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.5 (its fixtures read the keys). omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.2 runs in parallel: it touches only `omarchy/`.

title: The plan runner's pure decisions in `omarchy/Model.js`: `planFrom`, `selectionMatches`, the routine rule, the `apply` classifier rule and the continuation
description:
Part 2 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1 (The widget previews and applies plans). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1 makes the Omarchy bar widget preview every update and destructive action through the CLI's stored plans: it runs the command's `--dry-run`, reads the typed approval summary the CLI returns (`data.approval`), and then either runs `omaddons apply <plan_id>` of that preview directly (a routine plan whose canonical selection is exactly what the row showed), or opens the confirmation dialog naming each effect, or refreshes the view (nothing to do), or runs nothing and says why (M4-D28). The widget's logic lives in `omarchy/Model.js`, a file of pure functions that bun tests against envelopes the real binary writes (M3-D41); `Service.qml` only applies its decisions.

**This part writes those decisions, additively:** every new function, the `PLAN_PATHS` list, the `apply` rule of the classifier and the front-queued continuation in the scheduler, with their bun unit tests and the Rust checks that mirror them. Nothing calls the new functions yet, the templates keep their `confirm` key, and `buildArgv`'s behaviour is unchanged, so the widget behaves exactly as before and this commit passes the gate on its own (the gate runs the QML suites whenever `omarchy/` changes). omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.3 then switches the widget over in one commit.

**The rules these functions implement** (restated from M4-D28 and the plan store's shapes, D4 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4` and D5 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`):
- Every storable dry run that would change something returns `data.plan_id` (a ULID), `data.plan_expires_at`, `data.approval` and, in `commands[]`, the offer `{action: "apply", command: "omaddons apply <id>", argv: ["omaddons", "apply", "<id>"], destructive: <the path's destructive flag>}`. One that would change nothing returns `plan_id: null`, an empty `approval.selection`, and no offer. A full store or a write failure returns `plan_id: null` with the warning `plan_not_stored`, the selection intact.
- `approval` is `{routine, reasons[], selection[], scope}`: `routine` true only when `reasons[]` is empty; `reasons` from the closed set `dependency_added`, `folders_removed`, `local_changes_replaced`, `source_changed`, `channel_changed`, `while_running`, `reinstall`, `force`, `downgrade`; each selection item `{target_key, target_id, addon, source, channel, release_id, asset, from_version, to_version, op}`; `scope` `{dependencies_added[], folders_removed[], local_changes_replaced: {count, folders[]}, source_changed[], while_running}`.
- Compare the plan's canonical selection with what the row showed: equal and routine → apply directly; equal but not routine → the dialog with each effect in plain words; different → the dialog with "Changed since you looked"; **missing evidence is not equality**; nothing to do → refresh. The widget never decides anything from a warning's text.
- `apply`'s envelope: `command: "apply"`, the executed command's exit code, `data: {plan_id, applied: {command, display_argv}, approved?, result, outcomes[]}`, each outcome `{target, key, status: committed | unchanged | stale | failed, tx, error_code}`. Refusals: `plan_stale` (`details.reason` `expired`, `binary_changed`, `input_missing`, `already_applied`, or `details.changed` from the re-plan), `plan_not_found`, `locked` (another applier holds the plan's lease). The widget re-previews after `plan_stale` and `plan_not_found`, never re-runs `apply`.
- An `apply` argv may come only from a preview's own `commands[]` with a matching `plan_id`, never from a fix, an alternative, a remediation or another envelope.

## Technical Approach

All code is engine-neutral JavaScript (no `.pragma`, ES2017 at most, `var`/`function`, no QML globals, as the file's header requires), with each new name added to the guarded `module.exports` at the end. None of it reads a warning's `message`.

### 1. Constants and lists

```js
// The paths whose dry runs store a plan (M4-D22), held equal to app::COMMANDS' stores_plan
// by tests/omarchy_widget.rs. A previewed action on one of them confirms through apply.
// BEGIN PLAN_PATHS
var PLAN_PATHS = ["install", "update", "pin", "unpin", "adopt", "sync", "copy", "remove", "undo", "backup restore", "backup prune"]
// END PLAN_PATHS
var PLAN_ID_PATTERN = /^[0-9A-HJKMNP-TV-Z]{26}$/
// The plan items a dialog lists before "(and N more)"; a plain UI choice.
var WIDGET_DIALOG_ITEMS_MAX = 12
var MATCH_FIELDS = ["target_key", "addon", "source", "channel", "release_id", "asset", "from_version", "to_version"]
function storesPlan(path) { return PLAN_PATHS.indexOf(path) !== -1 }
```

### 2. `approvalOf(raw)` and `planFrom(env)`

- `approvalOf(raw)`: `null` unless `raw` is a non-array object with `typeof routine === "boolean"`, `reasons` an array of strings and `selection` an array of non-null objects. It returns `{routine: raw.routine === true && reasons.length === 0, reasons, selection: items, scope}`: each item normalized to the ten fields above (each a non-empty string or `null`), `scope` the object given or `{}`.
- `planFrom(env)`: `null` unless `envelopeOk(env) && env.ok && env.data` is an object; `data.plan_id` matches `PLAN_ID_PATTERN`; `env.commands` holds exactly one entry with `action === "apply"`, and that entry's `argv` is exactly `["omaddons", "apply", data.plan_id]`; and `approvalOf(data.approval)` is not `null`. It returns `{planId, argv: <a copy>, destructive: offer.destructive === true, expiresAt: str(data.plan_expires_at), approval}`.

### 3. What the view showed

- `reduceList` keeps per addon, beside today's fields: `channel: str(a.channel)`, `latestSource: strOrNull(latest.source)`, `latestReleaseId: strOrNull(latest.release_id)`, `latestAsset: strOrNull(latest.asset)` (the keys omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.1 adds to `list`'s `latest`; `null` until it lands).
- `updateRows` and `installedRows` rows gain `targetKey` (the list target's `key`), `channel`, `latestSource`, `latestReleaseId`, `latestAsset`; `installedRows` rows gain `latest` too. Existing fields are unchanged (`source` stays `sourceKind(ref)`, display only).
- `shownOf(row)` → `{target_key: row.targetKey, target_id: row.target, addon: row.name, source: row.latestSource, channel: row.channel, release_id: row.latestReleaseId, asset: row.latestAsset, from_version: row.version, to_version: row.latest}`, each a non-empty string or `null`.
- `shownForAddon(lists, target, addon)`: the reduced list's addon on `target` whose name equals `addon` ignoring ASCII case, as `[shownOf(<its row>)]`; else `[{target_id: target, addon: addon}]` with every other field `null`.
- `updateRequest(filter, rows)`: as today plus `shown`: `shownOf` of every row of kind `update` (rows from `updateRows(lists, filter, targets)`); `rowAction(row, "update")` adds `shown: [shownOf(row)]`; the other `rowAction`s are unchanged.

### 4. `requestedItems(approval)` and `selectionMatches(shown, selection)`

- `requestedItems(approval)`: `approval.selection` without the items whose `addon` (ignoring ASCII case) `approval.scope.dependencies_added` names, an entry being a string or an object with `addon` or `name`.
- `selectionMatches(shown, selection)`: `false` unless both are arrays, non-empty and of equal length. Pair each shown item with the selection item of the same `target_key` and `addon` (addon ignoring ASCII case); `false` when an item has no partner, when a pairing key repeats on either side, or when any `MATCH_FIELDS` entry of a pair is missing on either side (`null`, `undefined`, `""`) or differs (exact string equality, `addon` ignoring case). Otherwise `true`.

### 5. The words

- `reasonText(reason, scope)` → an array of lines:

  | Reason | Lines |
  |---|---|
  | `dependency_added` | per entry of `scope.dependencies_added`: "Also installs <name>[ <version>] (a new dependency)", the version from an object entry's `version`/`to_version` when present |
  | `folders_removed` | per entry of `scope.folders_removed` (a string, or an object with `folder`): "Removes the folder <folder> (kept for undo)" |
  | `local_changes_replaced` | "Replaces <count> file(s) you changed in <folders joined with `joinNames`> (kept for undo)"; "Replaces files you changed (kept for undo)" when the scope gives no count |
  | `source_changed` | per entry: "<addon> comes from another source now", plus " (<to>)" when an object entry names its new source |
  | `channel_changed` | "Follows another release channel than the one installed" |
  | `while_running` | "Changes files while the game is running (/reload in game afterwards)" |
  | `reinstall` | "Reinstalls over the installed files" |
  | `force` | "Takes over folders another addon owns (--force)" |
  | `downgrade` | "Installs an older version than the one installed" |
  | anything else | "Also: <reason with underscores as spaces>" |

  A reason whose scope list is empty still yields one generic line (for example "Also installs a new dependency"), so no reason is ever silent.
- `planItemLines(selection)`: per item by `op`: `update` → "Update Foo v1 → v2 on retail"; `install` → "Install WeakAuras 5.22.1 on era"; `remove` → "Remove Baz v1 from retail"; `reinstall` → "Reinstall Foo v1 on retail"; else "<Op capitalized> <addon> on <target_id>"; a missing version is left out; at most `WIDGET_DIALOG_ITEMS_MAX` lines, then "(and N more)".
- `changeLines(shown, selection)` → phrases, in shown order, then added items: `to_version` differs → "Foo v3 is now the newest"; versions equal, `release_id` differs → "Foo v2 is another release now"; `asset` differs → "Foo v2 comes in another file now (<asset>)"; `source` differs → "Foo comes from <source> now"; `channel` differs → "Foo follows <channel> now"; `from_version` differs → "Foo on retail is at <from> now"; fields missing on the row → "the view did not show Foo's <fields joined>"; missing on the plan → "the preview did not say Foo's <fields joined>"; a selection item without a partner → "Also: <its planItemLines line> (not in the view)"; a shown item without a partner → "Foo on era is no longer part of it".
- `changeHeading(lines)` → "Changed since you looked: " + the first three joined by "; " + ("; and N more" when longer).
- `staleText(env)` (extend the existing `Model.js:1505-1510`): keep today's text for `details.changed`; for `details.reason`: `expired` → "The plan expired.", `binary_changed` → "omaddons changed since the preview.", `input_missing` → "A file the plan needs is gone.", `already_applied` → "The plan was applied already."; for `plan_not_found` → "The plan is gone (expired or cleared)."; for an `apply` result whose `outcomes[]` holds `stale` targets → "Changed since you looked on <their ids joined>."; each followed by " Nothing ran; check the new preview." ("Nothing ran there" for the outcome case). `boundStaleText` is unchanged.

### 6. `previewDecision(spec, env)`

`spec` is `{mode: "match" | "confirm", shown: [...], again: boolean, path}`. It returns `{kind, plan, heading, lines, line, fixText}`:

1. `!envelopeOk(env) || !env.ok` → `{kind: "failed"}`.
2. `approvalOf(env.data.approval)` is `null` → `{kind: "refuse", line: "The preview did not say what it would change; nothing ran"}`.
3. `env.data.plan_id === null` and the selection is empty → `{kind: "refresh", line: mode === "match" ? "Already up to date; the view is refreshed" : "Nothing to do; the view is refreshed"}`.
4. `env.data.plan_id === null` otherwise → `{kind: "refuse", line: "The preview could not be kept as a plan; nothing ran", fixText: <the fix of the warning whose code is plan_not_stored, or "">}`.
5. `planFrom(env)` is `null` → `{kind: "refuse", line: "The preview offered no plan to apply; nothing ran"}`.
6. `mode === "confirm"` → `{kind: "dialog", plan, heading: "", lines: confirmText(spec.path, env).split("\n") + the reason lines}`.
7. `mode === "match"`: `compared = requestedItems(approval)`; `equal = selectionMatches(spec.shown, compared)`.
   - `equal && approval.routine && !plan.destructive && !spec.again` → `{kind: "direct", plan}` (decided while writing this bead: the kind is `direct`, not `apply`, so the literal `"apply"` stays where scan 3b allows it);
   - `equal`, or `spec.shown` empty → `{kind: "dialog", plan, heading: "", lines: planItemLines(approval.selection) + the reason lines}`;
   - otherwise → `{kind: "dialog", plan, heading: changeHeading(changeLines(spec.shown, compared)), lines: [heading] + planItemLines(...) + the reason lines}`.

The reason lines are `reasonText(r, approval.scope)` for each `r` of `approval.reasons`, in order. `dialogText(decision)` joins `lines` with "\n".

### 7. Reading an `apply` result

- `applyResult(env)`: when `envelopeOk(env)`, `env.command === "apply"`, `env.data.applied.command` is a string and `env.data.result` an object, return `{ok, schema_version, tool_version, command: env.data.applied.command, exit_code, partial, data: env.data.result, warnings, commands, error, outcomes: env.data.outcomes}`; else `null`.
- `needsPreviewAgain(env)`: `true` when `env.command === "apply"` and `!env.ok` with `error.code` `plan_stale` or `plan_not_found`, or when `applyResult(env)` has an `outcomes[]` entry with `status: "stale"`; `false` otherwise (`locked`, other failures, success).

### 8. The classifier's `apply` rule, and the continuation

- `classifyCliArgv(argv, plan)`: after the path is found, if it is `apply` and not (`plan` is an object whose `argv` equals `argv` element for element), return `{ok: false, path: "", reason: "apply_outside_plan", …}`. The existing callers pass no plan, so an `apply` argv from a fix, an alternative, a remediation, a `commands[]` entry or `last_change.undo` is never runnable.
- `cliArgv(argv, opts)`: calls `classifyCliArgv(argv, opts.plan)`; for path `apply` it refuses `opts.preview === true` and any `opts.token` (`apply_outside_plan`), adds no `--dry-run`, and returns the standard flags with `--progress json` followed by `apply <id>`.
- `enqueue(queues, request)`: a mutation-lane request with `continuation === true` is put at the front of the lane's list and replaces nothing (`replaced: null`); every other rule is unchanged. `nextRequest` needs no change (the user request at the front starts first).

### 9. Rust checks in the same commit (`tests/omarchy_widget.rs`)

- `plan_paths_mirror_the_registry`: `support::block(&model_js(), "PLAN_PATHS")` equals the set of `app::COMMANDS` names whose `stores_plan` is true (A1's field, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1`, set by D4, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`), and every entry is a registry path.
- `validate_built_argv`: the refusal reasons it accepts in `classified` gain `apply_outside_plan`, asserted as `leading_path(&argv[1..end]) == Some("apply")`; and a new array `planned` in `built-argv.json` is parsed: for each `{plan_id, argv}`, `parse(&argv)` gives path `apply`, `cli.global.dry_run == false`, no `if_match`, actor `widget`, a reason ending " (bar widget)", and the one positional equals `plan_id`.
- bun's writer (`model.test.js:1144-1197`) adds `planned` entries from a synthetic preview envelope built in the test (a valid ULID, a matching offer), and the classified list gains `["omaddons", "apply", "<that id>"]` (refused, `apply_outside_plan`).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `PLAN_PATHS`, `storesPlan`, `approvalOf`, `planFrom`, `shownOf`, `shownForAddon`, `requestedItems`, `selectionMatches`, `reasonText`, `planItemLines`, `changeLines`, `changeHeading`, `previewDecision`, `dialogText`, `applyResult` and `needsPreviewAgain` exist in `omarchy/Model.js`, are exported, and pass every unit case below; `staleText`, `reduceList`, `updateRows`, `installedRows`, `updateRequest` and `rowAction` carry the additions above without changing an existing field.
- [ ] `classifyCliArgv` refuses an `apply` argv given no matching plan (`apply_outside_plan`); `cliArgv` builds it only with its plan, never as a preview or with a token.
- [ ] A `continuation` request goes to the front of the mutation lane and replaces no queued change.
- [ ] `plan_paths_mirror_the_registry` passes; `validate_built_argv` parses the `planned` argv and accepts the `apply_outside_plan` refusals.
- [ ] The widget's behaviour is unchanged: every existing bun, QML and Rust widget test passes without edits other than additions.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes (the QML step runs: `omarchy/` changed); `ubs` is clean on the changed files.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

All in `omarchy/tests/model.test.js`, each a table `[case, input, expected]` asserted as `expect([case, actual]).toEqual([case, expected])`, so a failure names the case and shows both values (the file's `CLASSIFIER_TABLE` style). Synthetic envelopes use a fixed ULID `01M8Q2ZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZ`-style id and the helpers `env(data, commands, extra)`.

- `describe("approvalOf")`: `well_formed` → normalized; `routine_with_a_reason` → `routine: false`; `routine_not_boolean` → `null`; `reasons_not_array` → `null`; `reason_not_string` → `null`; `selection_item_null` → `null`; `scope_missing` → `scope: {}`.
- `describe("planFrom")`: `offer_matches` → the plan (argv copied, `destructive` from the offer); `plan_id_null` → `null`; `plan_id_hostile` (`--json`, `-t`, `../x`, lower case, 25 characters) → `null` each; `offer_for_another_id` → `null`; `two_offers` → `null`; `offer_with_extra_argument` (`["omaddons", "apply", id, "--dry-run"]`) → `null`; `offer_not_omaddons` (`["/bin/omaddons", "apply", id]`) → `null`; `offer_action_not_apply` → `null`; `envelope_failed` → `null`; `approval_missing` → `null`; `approval_malformed` → `null`.
- `describe("requestedItems")`: `string_dependency_dropped`; `object_dependency_dropped` (`{addon}` and `{name}`); `case_differs_still_dropped`; `no_dependencies_unchanged`.
- `describe("selectionMatches")`: `equal_one_item` → true; `equal_two_items_other_order` → true; `addon_case_differs` → true; `to_version_moved`, `from_version_moved`, `item_added`, `item_dropped`, `another_client_key`, `same_versions_other_source`, `same_versions_other_asset`, `same_versions_other_release_id`, `other_channel`, `duplicate_shown_key`, `duplicate_selection_key`, `empty_shown`, `empty_both`, `not_arrays` → false; and `missing_on_row_<field>` and `missing_on_plan_<field>` for each of the eight `MATCH_FIELDS` (`null`, and `""` for one of them) → false.
- `describe("changeLines")`: one case per phrase of §5 (`to_version`, `release_id`, `asset`, `source`, `channel`, `from_version`, missing on row, missing on plan, added, dropped) and `heading_caps_at_three` ("; and 2 more").
- `describe("reasonText")`: each of the nine reasons with a filled scope → the exact line(s); `dependency_added` with an object entry carrying a version; `local_changes_replaced` with two folders ("in DBM-Core and DBM-GUI"); each with an empty scope → a generic line; `unknown_reason` → "Also: some new thing".

- `describe("previewDecision")`: `failed_envelope` → failed; `no_approval` → refuse; `nothing_to_do_match` and `nothing_to_do_confirm` → refresh with their lines; `not_stored` (a `plan_not_stored` warning with a fix) → refuse with that `fixText`; `offer_mismatch` → refuse; `confirm` → dialog whose lines start with `confirmText`'s; `match_equal_routine` → direct; `match_equal_not_routine` (`dependency_added`) → dialog, no heading, the dependency line present; `match_different` → dialog with the heading; `match_empty_shown` → dialog, no heading; `match_equal_routine_again` → dialog; `match_equal_routine_destructive_offer` → dialog.
- `describe("applyResult and needsPreviewAgain")`: `wrapper_reads_as_its_command` (`resultLine` of it is "Updated 1 addon"); `not_apply` → `null`; `failed_apply` → `null`; `needsPreviewAgain`: `stale_expired`, `stale_binary_changed`, `stale_input_missing`, `stale_already_applied`, `stale_changed_selection`, `not_found`, `outcome_stale` → true; `locked`, `ok` → false.
- `describe("staleText")`: one case per `details.reason`, `details.changed`, `plan_not_found`, the outcome case.
- `describe("what the view showed")`: `shownOf_from_an_update_row`; `shownOf_uses_latestSource_not_the_display_source`; `shownForAddon_found`; `shownForAddon_unknown_addon` (partial item); `shownForAddon_no_lists`; `updateRequest_takes_only_update_rows_in_the_filter` (pinned, blocked and failed rows excluded).

### Integration and end-to-end tests

None in this subtask beyond the Rust checks of §9 (static: `plan_paths_mirror_the_registry`; pipeline step 3: `validate_built_argv`). The scenarios over binary-written envelopes are omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.5's.

### Logging

bun assertions carry `[case, …]` tuples; Rust assertions name the path or argv they check (`"{argv:?}: apply …"`), as the file's existing assertions do.

## Considerations

- **Additive only.** Do not change the templates, `buildArgv`'s refusals, `Service.qml` or a view here: the QML suites run in this commit's gate, and the switch-over must land in one piece (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.3).
- **Hot spot `omarchy/Model.js`:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1 first, then G2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.2`); command leaves add only `CLI_PATHS` rows. Put the new functions in a new section (`// ---- the plan runner (G1)`), so G2 appends its doctor reducer after it without conflicts.
- **Why exact equality, and the addon ignoring case:** the CLI's records are keyed by addon name ignoring case; every other field comes from the same memo on both sides, so a spelling difference means a real difference or a vocabulary bug, and both should open the dialog.
- **Why dependencies are filtered before the comparison:** M4-D28 wants "a dependency added" to be an effect the dialog names, not "the world changed"; whether D4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`) lists the dependency in the selection or only in the scope, the comparison is the same.
- **What could go wrong:** a matching bug that returns `true` for an incomplete pair would auto-apply something the user never saw. The missing-field cases (16) exist for that; keep them exhaustive when a field is ever added to `MATCH_FIELDS`.

## Dependencies

- **After it:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.3, which switches the widget to these functions.

comments.text:
decided: six choices this bead left open, made while implementing it (README is silent on all of them; none changes a promise).
1. reasonText gives the reason `destructive` its own line, "Removes, reverts or replaces something you have now". The binary emits it on remove, undo, backup restore and backup prune (src/app/approval.rs ApprovalReason, README's approval table), and the bead's fallback would show "Also: destructive", which tells the user nothing.
2. updateRequest(filter, rows) adds `shown` only when it is given rows. Called as today (PanelView passes only the filter), it returns exactly what it did, so the existing toEqual test stands unedited. previewDecision treats a missing `shown` as empty: a dialog, never a direct apply.
3. enqueue: a newer user request never replaces a queued continuation. Otherwise a second key press in the instant before the lane starts the continuation would drop the apply the user approved. A continuation still replaces nothing and goes first.
4. changeLines: when to_version differs, the release_id and asset phrases are left out (a new version implies both). The field names in the "did not show" and "did not say" phrases are spoken with spaces for underscores ("release id and asset"). Pairing falls back to target_id when either side lacks a target_key, so a partial item from shownForAddon still pairs; selectionMatches pairs by key only.
5. planItemLines: a missing version drops only its side, so "Update Foo → v2 on retail"; a missing addon or client drops its words.
6. previewDecision: any mode other than "match" takes the confirm path (a dialog), so an unknown mode never applies directly.

Part 3 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1 (The widget previews and applies plans). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1 makes the Omarchy bar widget preview every update and destructive action through the CLI's stored plans (M4-D28). Today (`c0ab5e9`) updates and installs run without a preview (M3-D9), and destructive actions preview with `--dry-run`, open a dialog starting on No, and confirm with `--if-match <token>` (`omarchy/Service.qml:321-398`, `:617-652`; `omarchy/Model.js:305-324`). After this subtask:

- **Update, Update all and per-addon updates** (and an install from Search) run the command's `--dry-run`. When the plan's canonical selection is exactly what the row showed and the typed approval summary is `routine`, the widget runs `omaddons apply <plan_id>` of that preview with no dialog. When it matches but is not routine (a dependency added, a folder removed, local edits replaced, another source or channel, a run while the game runs), the dialog opens with each effect in plain words. When it differs, the dialog opens with "Changed since you looked". Missing evidence never matches. A preview with nothing to do refreshes the view.
- **Destructive actions** (remove, restore, restore one addon, prune a backup, Undo last, a result's Undo) and a reinstall keep their dialog, and Yes runs `apply <plan_id>` of the preview, never the command with `--if-match`. One runner path serves every previewed action.
- **A refused `apply`** (`plan_stale`, `plan_not_found`, a stale target) re-runs the original action's preview and reopens the dialog; `apply` is never re-run.
- `errors dismiss` keeps its read-bound token, `targets rm` its explicit confirmation, and `pin`/`unpin` their direct run.

omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.2 wrote the pure decisions (`Model.previewDecision`, `planFrom`, `selectionMatches`, …) without using them. **This subtask is the switch-over:** the templates' `preview` field, the refusals in `buildArgv` and `cliArgv`, the previewed-action runner in `Service.qml`, the views passing what they showed, the dialog, the tests the switch changes, and README. It is one commit because the gate runs the QML suites whenever `omarchy/` changes: a template change without the runner, or the runner without the views, fails the gate.

## Technical Approach

### 1. `omarchy/Model.js`

- **Templates** (`COMMANDS`, `:99-127`): add `"preview": "match"` to `update_all`, `update_target`, `update_addon`, `install`; replace `"confirm": true` with `"preview": "confirm"` on `remove`, `restore`, `restore_addon`, `prune_backup`; add `"preview": "confirm"` to `reinstall`. `pin`, `unpin`, `backup_*` and `dismiss_errors` get none. Update the table's header comment: "a `preview` template runs only as its dry run; its confirmed run is `apply` of that preview's plan (M4-D28)".
  - *Decided while writing this bead:* `reinstall` is `confirm` (it replaces files, its approval always carries `reinstall`, and the Installed row has no installed release id to compare); `pin`/`unpin` stay direct (their templates have no `--version`, so they change only the record's pin flag and are undoable, M3-D9).
- **`buildArgv`** (`:340-369`): after the slot checks, `if (template.preview && o.preview !== true) throw refuse("preview_required", name + " runs only as its preview; its Yes runs the plan's apply")`. Pass `template.preview === "confirm"` where `ifMatchFor` took `template.confirm === true`.
- **`cliArgv`** (`:425-441`): on a path in `PLAN_PATHS`, a token is refused: `refuse("runs_through_apply", path + " confirms through its preview's apply, never --if-match")`. A destructive plan-storing argv without a preview still refuses with `destructive_without_preview` (unchanged).
- **`updateRequest`** (`:1602-1607`): its comment becomes "`u`: every client's updates, or the selected one's, previewed (M4-D28)"; it takes `(filter, rows)` and returns `shown` (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.2).

### 2. `omarchy/Service.qml`: the previewed-action runner

- **`request()`** (`:177-191`) defaults gain `"mode": ""`, `"shown": null`, `"again": false`, `"plan": null`, `"continuation": false`, `"deadlineMs": -1`, `"inactivity": false`.
- **`run(name, slots, label, shown)`** (`:331-346`): after `trialBuild`, a template with `preview` goes to `previewOf({template, slots, label, priority, mode: template.preview, shown: Array.isArray(shown) ? shown : []}, "", false)`; a destructive path without `preview` cannot exist (the Rust invariant below) but still previews as `confirm`; everything else is a direct mutation, as today.
- **`runCliArgv(argv, label)`** (`:362-380`): a destructive argv previews with `mode: "confirm"`; the rest unchanged.
- **`previewOf(spec, stale, again)`** (`:321-327`): the mutation carries `spec`, `stale`, `again`, and `continuation: again`; for `spec.mode === "match"` also `deadlineMs: networkDeadlineMs` and `inactivity: true`.
- **`startAction`** (`:474-478`): the message is "Preparing…" for a `match` preview, "Checking what it would do…" for a confirm preview, "" otherwise.
- **`applyAction`, purpose `preview`** (`:617-631`), when the outcome is `ok`:
  - the path (`Model.classifyCliArgv(r.cli).path` or `Model.templateShape(r.template, templates).path`) is not in `PLAN_PATHS` → M3's dialog, unchanged (`confirmText`, the token when the path binds, else `confirmed`);
  - else `var decision = Model.previewDecision({mode, shown, again, path}, env)` and set `lastPreview = {resource: r.resource, decision: decision.kind, planId: decision.plan ? decision.plan.planId : null}`:
    - `refresh` → `lastResult = {ok: true, line: decision.line, partial: false, commands: [], fixes: []}` and `changed()` (no toast);
    - `refuse` → `lastError = {message: decision.line, code: "not_previewed", fixes: [], fixText: decision.fixText || ""}` and `changed()`;
    - `direct` → `runPlan(decision.plan, r.spec, r.contextGeneration)`;
    - `dialog` → `confirm = {text: Model.dialogText(decision), heading: decision.heading, stale: r.stale}`, `pendingConfirm = {spec: r.spec, plan: decision.plan, contextGeneration: r.contextGeneration}`.
  - a failed preview keeps today's handling (`failedPreview`, `lastError`).
- **`runPlan(plan, spec, generation)`** (new): `mutation({resource: spec.template || "cli", cli: plan.argv.slice(), plan: plan, label: spec.label, purpose: "planned", spec: spec, continuation: true, contextGeneration: generation})`.
- **`confirmYes`** (`:384-398`): with `pending.plan` → `runPlan(pending.plan, pending.spec, pending.contextGeneration)`; without → today's mutation (token or `confirmed`). A confirmation from another context generation is still dropped by `pump`.
- **`applyAction`, purpose `planned`** (new branch, before the generic one): `var view = Model.applyResult(env) || env`; `lastResult = {ok: outcome === "ok", line: Model.resultLine(view), partial: !!env && env.partial === true, commands: <env.commands classified as today>, fixes: Model.itemFixes(view)}`; `lastError` as today; then `if (Model.needsPreviewAgain(env) && r.spec) previewOf(r.spec, Model.staleText(env), true)`; then the existing toast rule (a change started in the panel that finished with every panel closed) and `changed()`. The generic branch's `plan_stale` re-preview for `confirmed` runs stays for M3's legacy paths.
- **`argvOf`** (`:415-421`): `opts` gains `"plan": r.plan || null`; its single `return r.cli ? Model.cliArgv(r.cli, opts) : Model.buildArgv(r.template, r.slots, opts)` stays as it is.
- **`Lane`** (`:909-1057`): `run(r, argv, env)` sets `runDeadlineMs = (typeof r.deadlineMs === "number" && r.deadlineMs >= 0) ? r.deadlineMs : deadlineMs` and `runInactivity = r.deadlineMs >= 0 ? r.inactivity === true : inactivity`; the `deadline` timer's `interval` and `line()` use them. The mutation lane's own `deadlineMs` stays 0, so an `apply` and a confirm preview run under no deadline (decided while writing this bead: an `apply` is never killed for time).
- **`stateJson()`** (`:796-811`) gains `"confirm": confirm ? {"heading": confirm.heading || "", "planId": pendingConfirm && pendingConfirm.plan ? pendingConfirm.plan.planId : null} : null` and `"lastPreview": lastPreview` (a new property, `null` until the first plan preview).

### 3. The views

- `views/UpdatesView.qml` `run(action)` (`:54-57`): `svc.run(action.template, action.slots, action.label, action.shown)`; its header comment drops "Updates and pins run without a confirmation" for "Updates preview first and apply a routine plan that matches the row (M4-D28); pins run directly".
- `PanelView.qml` `updateAll()` (`:236-240`): `var request = Model.updateRequest(filter, Model.updateRows(svc.lists, filter, targets))` and pass `request.shown`. The dialog (`:917-932`): `message` stays `stale` + "\n\n" + `text`; `text` already starts with the heading when there is one. Nothing else in the dialog changes (it opens on No; only a fresh key press confirms).
- `views/InstalledView.qml` `run(action)` (`:59-62`): passes `action.shown` (the update primary gets `[shownOf(row)]`; reinstall and remove go through `confirm`).
- `views/IssuesView.qml:65`: `svc.run("update_addon", {target, addon}, "Update " + row.addon, Model.shownForAddon(svc.lists, row.target, row.addon))`.
- `views/SearchView.qml:76`: `svc.run("install", {target, ref}, "Install " + row.name, [])`.
- `RestoreChooser.qml` and `views/BackupsView.qml`: unchanged calls.

### 4. Tests this commit must change (the switch breaks them otherwise)

- `tests/omarchy_widget.rs`, `every_template_is_a_registry_command_with_safe_slots` (`:56-119`, the confirm rules at `:66-74`): replace "confirm ⇔ destructive" with: a destructive path's template has `preview == "confirm"`; a `preview == "match"` template is not destructive; a template with `preview` is on a path in `PLAN_PATHS` (read with `support::block`); no template has a `confirm` key; `preview` is `"match"` or `"confirm"` when present.
- `omarchy/tests/model.test.js`: `runOpts` (`:122-127`) builds previewed templates as previews; `buildArgv`'s confirm test (`:150-162`) expects `preview_required` for a previewed template's real run; the shipped-template test (`:235-243`) checks the new invariant; the built-argv writer (`:1159-1168`) records previewed templates only with `{preview: true}` (and their hostile slots likewise) and asserts each real form is refused with `preview_required`; the classifier tests (`:279-302`) expect `runs_through_apply` for a token on `remove` and `backup restore`.
- `omarchy/tests/security.test.js`: `needsPreview` (`:313-317`) reads `t.preview`; check 6's `run` route (`:336`) matches the new `if (template.preview …) { previewOf(`; the mechanism test (`:484-495`) lists the previewed templates (`install`, `prune_backup`, `reinstall`, `remove`, `restore`, `restore_addon`, `update_addon`, `update_all`, `update_target`), each refusing its real form with `preview_required`. (The new rules are omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.4's.)
- `omarchy/tests/qml/tst_service.qml`: the `remove_confirm` fixture template (`:24-27`) uses `"preview": "confirm"`; `test_a_confirmed_run_carries_its_previews_token_and_a_stale_one_previews_again` (`:295-319`) becomes `test_a_confirmed_removal_runs_its_previews_plan_and_a_stale_one_previews_again` (preview envelope with `plan_id`, `approval` and the `apply` offer; Yes launches `apply <id>` with no `--if-match` and no `--dry-run`; answered `plan_stale` → a new `remove --dry-run` launch, `confirm.stale` starting "Changed since you looked"; three `remove` launches and one `apply`); `test_an_action_reports_progress_then_its_result` (`:331-348`), `test_user_mutations_go_before_background_ones` and `test_a_third_user_mutation_replaces_the_queued_one` (`:350-371`) answer the update previews first; `test_state_has_the_documented_shape` (`:590-602`) lists `confirm` and `lastPreview`.
- `omarchy/tests/qml/tst_panel.qml`: `test_u_updates_all_or_the_selected_client` (`:199-214`) records the fourth argument (`shown`).
- `omarchy/tests/qml/tst_views.qml`: `test_enter_updates_one_addon_and_p_pins_by_its_state` (`:203`), `test_installed_rows_carry_their_markers_and_enter_repairs_or_updates` (`:260`), `test_enter_updates_the_likely_source_or_shows_its_stack` (`:389`), `test_search_installs_into_the_filtered_client_when_its_hint_allows` (`:473`) and `test_x_previews_the_removal_and_yes_runs_it_bound` (`:598`, renamed `…_and_yes_runs_its_plan`) record `shown` and the confirm-through-`apply` flow.

### 5. README (`README.md`, `### omarchy`, `:1656-1713`, and the FAQ)

- The Updates bullet (`:1662`): add "Update (Enter), Update all and `u` preview first: the widget runs the update's dry run, and when the plan is exactly what the rows showed (the same client, addon, source, release, file and versions) and needs nothing more, it applies that plan (`omaddons apply <plan_id>`) with no dialog. Otherwise the confirmation opens, starting on No: "Changed since you looked" with what moved, or one line per effect the plan adds (a new dependency, a folder it removes, files you changed that it replaces, kept for undo, another source or channel, a change while the game runs). A preview with nothing to do refreshes the view. Pins run directly."
- The key table: Enter "Updates: preview the update, then apply it" (and Installed: "reinstall after a confirmation"); `u` "Update everything, or the filtered client, previewed".
- The confirmation paragraph (`:1691`): every update, install, reinstall and destructive action (an undo, a removal, a restore, a backup deletion) first runs the command's own dry run, which stores a plan; Yes, or a routine matching update, runs `omaddons apply <plan_id>` of exactly that plan. When the plan went stale, expired or is gone, nothing runs: the widget previews again and the dialog comes back with "Changed since you looked" and the new preview. Dismissing Lua errors still binds to the read the panel showed.
- The rules list (`:1701-1709`): "It runs `omaddons apply` only for the plan of the preview it just ran, never from a fix or a recommendation"; "An update, an install, a reinstall or a destructive action runs only after its preview, and only as that preview's `apply`"; "It decides nothing from a warning's text".
- The IPC paragraph (`:1713`): `state` also says whether a confirmation is open (`confirm`) and what the last preview decided (`lastPreview`: `direct`, `dialog`, `refresh`, `refuse` or `failed`).
- FAQ, new entry: "Why did the widget ask me about an update?": because the plan did more than the row showed (each line in the dialog is one effect from the CLI's approval summary), or the release changed since the row was read, or the view had not shown which release it was (an install from Search). *Decided while writing this bead:* this leaf writes the entry; H4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`) verifies it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every template on a plan-storing path that changes addons (`update_*`, `install`, `reinstall`, `remove`, `restore`, `restore_addon`, `prune_backup`) has `preview`, and `buildArgv` refuses its real form with `preview_required`; no template has a `confirm` key; `pin`, `unpin`, `backup_*` and `dismiss_errors` are unchanged.
- [ ] Enter on an Updates row, `u`, the Update all button, the Installed view's update, the Issues view's update and a Search install each launch the command's `--dry-run` with the rows' `shown` (Search: `[]`), on the mutation lane, under the network deadline, showing "Preparing…".
- [ ] A routine matching preview launches `apply <plan_id>` next (the standard flags, `--progress json`, no `--dry-run`, no `--if-match`), with no dialog; a matching, not-routine preview opens the dialog with one line per effect; a different one opens it with "Changed since you looked"; a no-op preview refreshes; a preview without a readable approval, without a stored plan, or with a mismatched offer runs nothing and says why.
- [ ] A confirm template, Undo last and a result's Undo open the dialog, and Yes launches `apply <plan_id>` of their preview; `targets rm` keeps `confirmed`, `errors dismiss` keeps `--if-match`.
- [ ] A refused `apply` (`plan_stale`, `plan_not_found`, a stale outcome) launches the original preview again (as a continuation) and reopens the dialog; no `apply` is launched twice for one preview; `locked` shows the error without a re-preview.
- [ ] A planned `apply` goes first on the mutation lane and replaces no queued change; an `apply` and a confirm preview run under no deadline.
- [ ] `state()` carries `confirm` and `lastPreview`.
- [ ] The tests listed in §4 pass in their new form, and every other widget test passes unchanged.
- [ ] README's `omarchy` section and the FAQ entry describe the behaviour, in this commit.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes (the QML step runs); `ubs` is clean on the changed files.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

The pure functions are omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.2's. Here, the bun changes of §4 (each existing test in its new form), plus in `model.test.js`:
- `buildArgv refuses a previewed template's real run`: for each previewed template, `reasonOf(() => M.buildArgv(name, benignSlots(name), opts()))` is `preview_required`, and with `opts({preview: true})` the argv contains `--dry-run`.
- `cliArgv keeps tokens off plan paths`: `remove`, `undo`, `backup restore`, `backup prune` argv with a token → `runs_through_apply`; `errors dismiss` with a token builds (unchanged).

### Integration and end-to-end tests

QML, with hand-written envelopes in the file's style (`envelope(command, data, extra)`, `answer(launch, text)`, `runs(word)`, `lastRun(word)`); each step asserts the launched argv with `words(launch.command)` and the model properties. New tests in `omarchy/tests/qml/tst_service.qml`:

- `test_a_match_preview_runs_under_the_network_deadline_and_apply_under_none`: `make({"networkDeadlineMs": 400})`; `run("update_addon", …, shown)` → the preview launch; no progress for 450 ms → its outcome is `timeout` and `lastError.message` ends "timeout"; a second preview emitting a progress line every 200 ms outlives 600 ms; its routine answer → the `apply` launch, silent for 600 ms, is not killed.
- `test_a_planned_apply_goes_first_and_replaces_no_queued_change`: start a preview of `update_addon`; while it runs, `run("update_target", …)` queues ("next: Update era"); answer the preview routine → the next launch is `apply`, and `queues.mutation` still holds the `update_target` request; answer `apply` → the queued preview starts.
- `test_an_apply_offer_for_another_plan_runs_nothing`: the preview's offer argv names another id → no `apply` launch; `lastError.message` "The preview offered no plan to apply; nothing ran".
- `test_a_preview_without_an_approval_runs_nothing`: `data.approval` missing → no launch; the message says so.
- `test_a_full_plan_store_runs_nothing_and_says_so`: `plan_id: null`, a non-empty selection and a `plan_not_stored` warning with a fix → no launch; `lastError.fixText` is the warning's fix.
- `test_a_no_op_preview_refreshes_and_runs_nothing`: `plan_id: null`, empty selection → a `status` launch follows, no `apply`; `lastResult.line` "Already up to date; the view is refreshed".
- `test_targets_rm_keeps_its_explicit_confirmation`: `runCliArgv(["omaddons", "targets", "rm", "retail"])` → preview → dialog → Yes launches `targets rm retail` without `--dry-run`, without `--if-match`, and no `apply`.
- `test_a_dismissal_keeps_its_read_bound_token`: `dismissErrors([{target, token}])` → the launch carries `--if-match <token>`, and no preview.
- `test_locked_apply_shows_the_error_and_does_not_preview_again`: the `apply` answered `locked` (exit 5) → `lastError.code` `locked`, no new preview launch.
- `test_state_reports_the_last_preview`: after a routine preview, `JSON.parse(stateJson()).lastPreview` is `{resource: "update_addon", decision: "direct", planId: <id>}` and `confirm` is `null`; after a dialog preview, `confirm.heading` is the heading and `confirm.planId` the id.

`tst_panel.qml` and `tst_views.qml` as in §4, plus in `tst_views.qml`: `test_enter_on_an_installed_drifted_addon_confirms_the_reinstall` (a `reinstall` preview, mode `confirm`) and `test_search_install_passes_nothing_shown` (the fourth argument is `[]`).

### Logging

Each QML step asserts with a message naming the step (`compare(words(launch.command), […], "the apply of the routine preview")`), and on a wrong launch prints `JSON.stringify(ProcessRegistry.launches.map(l => words(l.command)))` with `console.log` before failing, so the run's output shows every launch in order. bun tests keep the `[case, …]` tuples.

## Considerations

- **Hot spots:** `omarchy/Model.js` and `Service.qml` (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1 first, then G2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.2`; command leaves add `CLI_PATHS` rows only, so rebase onto theirs); `views/IssuesView.qml` is G2's next. Keep the runner's functions together (`previewOf`, `runPlan`, the two `applyAction` branches) so G2 extends them for Undo last of a repair without touching the rest.
- **The legacy branch is load-bearing for G2:** `doctor fix` binds with `--if-match` and stores no plan; G2 previews it through the non-`PLAN_PATHS` branch kept here.
- **What could go wrong:** a view forgets its `shown` (every update then opens the dialog: safe, and the QML tests above catch it); a lane rule kills an `apply` (the deadline test catches it); a re-preview loops (it cannot: `again` never auto-applies).
- **The widget digest** changes with `omarchy/`; an installed widget reports drift until `omaddons omarchy install`.
- **Performance:** two processes per widget update (the dry run, then `apply`); `apply` revalidates each ref once and downloads nothing the dry run cached.

## Dependencies

- **Parent:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1 (The widget previews and applies plans).
- **Before it:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.1 (rows that carry every compared field; without it every update opens the dialog) and omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.2 (the functions this subtask calls).
- **After it:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.4 (the security scans over the final source) and omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.5 (the scenarios over the binary's envelopes), in parallel.

comments.text:
decided: choices and corrections made while implementing this bead.
1. Found and fixed in Service.qml: Lane.terminate() sent SIGTERM and then restarted the kill timer. A child that ends at once finishes the request (which stops the timer) before the timer is restarted, so the stale timer SIGKILLed the lane's next child after killGraceMs. Real children exit asynchronously, so this was latent, but a match preview started right after a timed-out one hit it under the mock. The timer is now armed before the signal; test_a_match_preview_runs_under_the_network_deadline_and_apply_under_none covers it.
2. Tests the switch breaks that §4 does not list, changed in this commit: tst_service's test_an_incompatible_binary_makes_the_widget_read_only and test_a_confirmation_from_another_context_never_runs (their remove previews now carry a plan, else no dialog opens); tst_smoke's test_argv_builds_with_the_stamped_context (builds update_addon as its preview); tst_views' test_under_all_a_chooser_preselects_no_client (the install records shown = []); model.test.js's row-action and `u` tests (previewed templates build as previews).
3. The stale-removal test counts two remove launches (the preview and the preview again) and one apply; §4's "three remove launches" counted the M3 flow's real remove, which no longer runs.
4. The preview handling is one function, applyPreview(r, outcome, env), beside previewOf and runPlan, so G2 extends the runner in one place; applyAction keeps the planned branch inline with the generic one (one result, toast and refresh path).
5. pendingConfirm carries `plan` (decision.plan, or null on the M3 branch). omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.4's provenance scan (rule 3b, part 2) must admit those two values beside `plan`, `pending.plan` and `r.plan || null`; every request's plan still comes only from runPlan(decision.plan, …) or runPlan(pending.plan, …).
6. title: Tests: the security scans hold `apply` to its plan, a preview on every addon-changing template, warnings out of every decision, and no issue id by name
description:
Part 4 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1 (The widget previews and applies plans). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1 makes the Omarchy bar widget preview every update and destructive action through the CLI's stored plans, and apply a plan (`omaddons apply <plan_id>`) only when its preview's canonical selection matches what the row showed and the CLI's typed approval summary is routine; otherwise it opens the dialog (M4-D28). The safety of that rule rests on four mechanisms: an `apply` argv comes only from the preview the widget just ran (`Model.planFrom`), every template that changes addons previews, the decision never reads a warning's text, and the widget matches no issue id by name.

The widget's security scans (`omarchy/tests/security.test.js`, pipeline step 2, in every gate) are text lints over every runtime `.qml` and `.js` under `omarchy/` (tests and a generated `Build.js` aside) that fail when a code path goes around a mechanism; each scan also runs over an in-memory copy with one planted violation, which it must report (`plant(files, name, anchor, insertion)`, `security.test.js:41-47`; the `PLANTED` table at `:434-466`). **This part adds the four guards**, over the source omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.3 switched over. It is its own step because it is tests only, over the final source, and runs beside omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.5.

**What the mechanisms are** (from omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.2 and omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.3):
- `Model.planFrom(env)` returns an `apply` argv only when the envelope's `data.plan_id` is a ULID and `commands[]` holds exactly one `apply` offer with exactly `["omaddons", "apply", data.plan_id]`. `Model.classifyCliArgv(argv, plan)` refuses an `apply` argv (`apply_outside_plan`) unless given that plan; `Model.cliArgv` builds one only with `opts.plan`. `Service.qml` passes the plan `Model.previewDecision` obtained from `Model.planFrom` through the request's `plan` field to `argvOf` (`runPlan(decision.plan, …)` and, on Yes, `runPlan(pending.plan, …)`); the decision kind for a direct apply is `direct`.
- Templates carry `"preview": "match"` (`update_all`, `update_target`, `update_addon`, `install`) or `"preview": "confirm"` (`remove`, `restore`, `restore_addon`, `prune_backup`, `reinstall`); `pin` and `unpin` keep running directly because their templates have no `--version` and change only the record; `Model.PLAN_PATHS` lists the plan-storing paths.
- The decision functions (`planFrom`, `approvalOf`, `requestedItems`, `selectionMatches`, `previewDecision`, `reasonText`, `changeLines`) read only typed fields; `warningsOf` and `warningMessages` read a warning's `message` to display it, selected by code.
- **M4-D48:** F1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1`) narrows the published issue id `fm-concurrency_primitives-journal-pending` (from "every stuck journal, P0, needs manual repair" to "a journal recovery can settle") and adds six ids for the stuck states. That narrowing is safe for the widget only because it lists `issues[]` generically and matches no id by name; the plan asks this leaf to confirm it with a grep of `omarchy/`. *Decided while writing this bead:* the grep is a permanent scan (check 10), so no later change can reintroduce a match by name.

## Technical Approach

Add to `security.test.js`, using its helpers (`lines`, `codeOf`, `calls`, `balanced`, `functionBody`, `violation`, `qmlNames`); register the checks in `CHECKS` (`:406-415`) and the planted cases in `PLANTED`.

### Rule 3 extended: `apply` only from `Model.planFrom` (`checkApplyProvenance`, registered as "3b. apply from its plan")

1. Every match of `/["'`]apply["'`]/` in the code (comments stripped) of every runtime file is a violation, except inside Model.js's `CLI_PATHS` block (between `// BEGIN CLI_PATHS` and `// END CLI_PATHS`) and the bodies (`functionBody`) of `planFrom` and `classifyCliArgv` and `cliArgv` (where the `apply` rule lives) and `applyResult` and `needsPreviewAgain` (which read an envelope's `command`). No QML file may hold it at all, and no array literal anywhere may (`/\[[^\]\n]*["'`]apply["'`]/`): `planFrom` compares the offer element by element. Message: "an apply argv outside Model.planFrom". (The decision kind for a direct apply is `direct`, so the service never needs the word.)
2. In `Service.qml`, every `"plan":` key's value is `plan`, `pending.plan` or `r.plan || null`; a `"plan": plan` must sit in a function whose body contains `var plan = Model.planFrom(` or whose parameter list names `plan` and whose every caller passes `decision.plan` or `pending.plan` (concretely: `runPlan(plan, …)` is called only as `runPlan(decision.plan, …)` and `runPlan(pending.plan, …)`, and `decision` comes from `Model.previewDecision(`). Message: "a plan not from Model.planFrom".
3. `argvOf`'s options carry `"plan": r.plan || null`, and its one `return` stays `Model.cliArgv` or `Model.buildArgv` (the existing check).

Planted:
- "a hand-built apply argv": `Service.qml`, after `  function afterStatus() {\n`, `    mutation({ "resource": "x", "cli": ["omaddons", "apply", "01M8Q2ZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZ"], "label": "x" })\n` → /apply argv outside Model\.planFrom/.
- "a plan from a literal": `Service.qml`, same anchor, `    mutation({ "resource": "x", "plan": { "argv": ["omaddons"] }, "label": "x" })\n` → /plan not from Model\.planFrom/.
- "a fix that offers apply": `Model.js`, after `function fixButtons(env) {\n`, `  var sneaky = ["omaddons", "apply"]\n` → /apply argv outside Model\.planFrom/.

### Rule 6 extended: a preview on every addon-changing template (`checkPreviews`)

Keep the existing route checks (`run`, `runCliArgv`, `runBound`, updated by omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.3) and add, from `tableOf(model)` and `PLAN_PATHS` (parsed from its `// BEGIN PLAN_PATHS` block):
- every template with `mutates: true` whose path (`M.templateShape(name, table).path`) is in `PLAN_PATHS` has `preview` equal to `"match"` or `"confirm"`, unless its name is in `RECORD_ONLY = ["pin", "unpin"]`, whose `argv` must not contain `--version` (a pin with a version installs a release, and then needs a preview too). Message: "<name> changes addons without a preview";
- every template on a destructive path (`M.CLI_PATHS[path].destructive`) has `preview: "confirm"`. Message: "<name> is destructive without preview: confirm";
- no template has a `confirm` key. Message: "<name> keeps the old confirm key";
- `function run(`'s body routes `template.preview` to `previewOf(`, and `function previewOf(` passes the network deadline only for `mode === "match"` (`deadlineMs: networkDeadlineMs` beside a `"match"` test). Message: "run does not preview a previewed template".

Planted:
- "update_addon without its preview": in `Model.js`, replace `, "preview": "match"` after `"update_addon"`'s argv with nothing (a `plant` variant that removes text: add a small `unplant(files, name, text)` helper) → /update_addon changes addons without a preview/.
- "a pin with a version and no preview": add `, "--version", "1"` after `"pin", "-t", "{target}"` in `pin`'s argv → /pin changes addons without a preview/.
- "the old confirm key": add `, "confirm": true` to `remove`'s entry → /keeps the old confirm key/.

### Check 9 (new): warnings decide nothing (`checkWarnings`)

1. In `Model.js`, a function whose body mentions `warnings` may read `.message` only if it is `warningsOf` or `warningMessages`. Message: "<fn> reads a warning's message".
2. No line of any runtime file that calls `warningMessages(` also holds `===`, `!==`, `==`, `indexOf(`, `.test(`, `.match(`, `includes(`, `some(`, `find(`, `filter(` or `startsWith(`. Message: "a warning's text decides something".
3. The bodies of `planFrom`, `approvalOf`, `requestedItems`, `selectionMatches`, `previewDecision`, `reasonText` and `changeLines` contain neither `warnings` nor `.message`, except that `previewDecision` may name the warning *code* `plan_not_stored` to read that warning's `fix` (allowed exactly as `warning.code === "plan_not_stored"` followed by `.fix`). Message: "<fn> reads warnings".
4. No QML line holds both `.message` and `warning` (any case) together with a comparison operator. Message: "a view decides from a warning's text".

Planted:
- "the routine rule reading a warning": `Model.js`, after `function previewDecision(spec, env) {\n`, `  if (env.warnings && env.warnings[0] && env.warnings[0].message) return null\n` → /previewDecision reads warnings/.
- "a helper testing a warning's text": `Model.js`, after `function warningsOf(env) {\n` is not allowed to hold it, so plant a new function after `// -------------------------------------------------------------- the reducers\n`: `function sneaky(env) { return env.warnings[0].message.indexOf("dependency") >= 0 }\n` → /sneaky reads a warning's message/.
- "a service deciding from warning text": `Service.qml`, after `  function afterStatus() {\n`, `    if (Model.warningMessages(env, "x")[0] === "y") refresh()\n` → /a warning's text decides something/.

### Check 10 (new): no issue id by name (M4-D48, `checkIssueIds`)

- No line of any runtime file matches `/["'`]fm-[a-z]/` (a failure-mode id literal). Message: "a literal failure-mode id (the widget lists issues generically, M4-D48)".
- No line compares an issue's id with a literal: `/\b(issue|row|mi|i)\.id\s*[!=]==?\s*["'`]/`. Message: "an issue matched by its id".

Planted:
- "an id literal in the Issues view": `views/IssuesView.qml`, after `Item {\n`, `  readonly property bool planted: !!svc && svc.targets.some(function(t) { return t.issues.some(function(i) { return i.id === "fm-concurrency_primitives-journal-pending" }) })\n` → /literal failure-mode id|issue matched by its id/.

### The mechanism tests (`describe("the mechanisms behind the scans")`)

Add, at run time:
- `apply runs only from its plan`: `M.classifyCliArgv(["omaddons", "apply", ID]).reason === "apply_outside_plan"`; `M.cliArgv(["omaddons", "apply", ID], opts)` throws `apply_outside_plan`; with `{plan: M.planFrom(<a synthetic preview with that offer>)}` it builds, and with a plan for another id it throws.
- `every previewed template refuses its real run`: the list `install`, `prune_backup`, `reinstall`, `remove`, `restore`, `restore_addon`, `update_addon`, `update_all`, `update_target` (sorted, exact), each throwing `preview_required` without `preview: true` and holding `--dry-run` with it.
- `a remediation, a fix, an alternative and a commands[] entry offering apply never become buttons`: `M.reduceStatus` of a status envelope whose issue remediation argv is an `apply` argv → `remediation.runnable === false`; `M.fixButtons` of an error whose `fix_argv` and alternatives are `apply` argv → `[]`; `M.warningsOf` of a warning with an `apply` `fix_argv` → `fix: null`; `M.resultUndo({commands: [{action: "undo", argv: ["omaddons", "apply", ID], runnable: false}]})` → `null`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The checks "3b. apply from its plan", the extended "6. previews", "9. warnings decide nothing" and "10. no issue id by name" pass on the real source (`expect(check(REAL)).toEqual([])`).
- [ ] Each planted violation listed above is reported with its rule (ten planted cases).
- [ ] The three mechanism tests pass.
- [ ] No runtime file under `omarchy/` holds a failure-mode id literal or matches an issue by its id (check 10 on the real source).
- [ ] README's widget rules list (written by omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.3) names exactly the guarantees these checks hold; `security.test.js`'s header comment lists checks 9 and 10.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes (the widget pipeline runs); `ubs` is clean on the changed file.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

The scans are the tests. Each check is a pure function over a `{name: text}` map, run once over `REAL` and once per planted copy, as the file does today.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

None: the runtime behaviour is omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.3's QML tests and omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.5's scenarios.

### Logging

Every violation is `file:line: rule` (the file's `violation` helper), and `expect(check(REAL)).toEqual([])` prints the whole list on failure, so a broken rule names its file and line. Each planted test's name says what was planted ("6. previews: update_addon without its preview").

## Considerations

- **The scans catch accidents, not adversaries.** The guarantees are the mechanisms (`planFrom`, the classifier's `apply` rule, `buildArgv`'s `preview_required`); the scans make sure no code path goes around them by mistake. Keep each regex tight enough that the real source passes without exceptions; when a legitimate use needs one, add it as a named, commented exception in the scan, never by loosening the pattern.
- **Regex drift.** If omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.3 named a function or field differently from this body (say `runPlan`), adjust the scan to the real names in the same commit, and keep every planted case catching.
- **G2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.2`) follows:** it adds the doctor reducer and the Issues view's repairs; check 10 then also guards its rows (it lists findings by their data, never by a literal id), and its classifier rules (`doctor gc`, `--force`) join rule 3's family. Leave the checks easy to extend (one function each).
- **Hot spot:** `security.test.js` is touched by omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1 and G2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.2`) only.

## Dependencies

- **Parent:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1 (The widget previews and applies plans).
- **Before it:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.3 (the source the scans hold: the templates' `preview`, the runner's `plan` field, `runPlan`).
- **After it:** nothing inside omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1; it runs beside omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.5 (different files).
