title: E2E: the plan runner over envelopes the binary writes, in bun and QML, with the output cap and the built `apply` argv
description:
Part 5 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1 (The widget previews and applies plans). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1 makes the Omarchy bar widget preview every update and destructive action through the CLI's stored plans (M4-D28): it runs the command's `--dry-run`; when the plan's canonical selection is exactly what the row showed and the typed approval summary (`data.approval`) is `routine`, it runs `omaddons apply <plan_id>` with no dialog; when it matches but the plan does more (a dependency added, a folder removed, local edits replaced, another source), the dialog names each effect; when it differs, the dialog opens with "Changed since you looked"; missing evidence never matches; a preview with nothing to do refreshes the view; a refused `apply` re-previews and never re-runs. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.1 gave `list`'s rows their release identity (`latest.source`, `latest.release_id`, `latest.asset`), omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.2 wrote the pure decisions, and omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.3 switched the runner over, with QML tests over hand-written envelopes.

**This part proves the whole rule on envelopes the real binary writes.** The widget pipeline (M3-D41) already has the binary write real envelopes (`write_widget_fixtures`, `tests/omarchy_widget.rs:1139-1342`), which bun reads. This subtask adds the plan scenes to it, runs the routine rule over each scene in bun, and, new for the widget, runs the QML scenarios over the same binary-written envelopes (through a generated `Fixtures.js`), so a drift between D4's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`) approval and the widget's reading is caught in the gate. It also extends the output-cap test to the preview and `apply` envelopes and parses the built `apply` argv with clap. It is its own step because it is tests only, after the runner exists, and the slice-2 demo (T3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.3`) asserts its QML scenarios by name.

## Technical Approach

### 1. The plan scenes in `write_widget_fixtures` (`tests/omarchy_widget.rs`)

A new function `plans_fixtures(dir, t)`, called from `write_widget_fixtures` beside `errors_fixtures` and `backups_fixtures`, writes each fixture with `write_fixture(dir, name, &ran.run, code)` (the `Ran.run` of T1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, is a `common::home::Run`) and asserts what the scene must show before writing it. Previews are the templates' argv with `--dry-run` inserted before the command words (as `remove-preview` does today, `tests/omarchy_widget.rs:1190-1192`); applies are `support::standard(true)` + `["apply", <plan_id>]`. Each scene is a fresh `common::home::Home`; `Rel` is the file's release helper (`<Name>.zip` with a TOC and a `core.lua` per tag).

- **Scene A, routine, on `Home::new(&["wow", "wow_classic_era"])`** with Foo and Bar one release behind on retail and era (`home.installed_behind`, as the existing updates scene), then the `check` template:
  - `plan-list`: the `list` template → exit 0; Foo's `latest` carries `source`, `release_id`, `asset`.
  - `plan-update-routine`: `update_addon` (`target: retail`, `addon: Foo`) with `--dry-run` → exit 0; assert `data.approval.routine == true`, `plan_id` a ULID, and exactly one `apply` offer with that id.
  - `plan-update-routine-apply`: `apply <plan_id>` → exit 0; `outcomes[0].status == "committed"`; `data.applied.command == "update"`.
  - `plan-update-noop`: the same preview again → exit 0; `plan_id` null, `approval.selection` empty, no `apply` offer.
  - `plan-list-after`: the `list` template again (Foo current on retail).
  - `plan-update-all`: `update_all` with `--dry-run` → routine, three items (Foo on era, Bar on retail and era).
  - `plan-update-all-apply`: its `apply` → three `committed` outcomes.
  - `plan-undo`: the last change's undo (`status`'s `last_change.undo.argv`, as `undo-preview` is built today) with `--dry-run` → a plan and an `apply` offer marked `destructive: true`.
  - `plan-undo-apply`: its `apply` → exit 0, `data.applied.command == "undo"`.
  - `plan-remove`: `remove` (`retail`, `Bar`) with `--dry-run` → a plan, the offer `destructive: true`.
  - `plan-remove-apply`: its `apply` → exit 0.
- **Scene B, a release that moves, on `Home::new(&["wow"])`**, Foo v1 installed, v2 published, `check`:
  - `plan-moved-list`: the `list` template (the row says v2);
  - publish v3, then `outdated --refresh --json` (the dry run of `update` reuses the memo for 15 minutes, so the scene refreshes it explicitly);
  - `plan-update-moved`: the preview → `to_version` v3;
  - publish v4; `plan-apply-stale`: `apply <the v3 plan>` → exit 1, `plan_stale`, `details.changed` holding `selection` (`apply` revalidates and sees v4);
  - `plan-update-v4`: the preview again (a plan for v4); `plan-apply-expired`: its `apply` run with `OMADDONS_NOW` 25 hours after the preview (T1's `log.cmd(&home, argv).env("OMADDONS_NOW", …)`) → `plan_stale`, `details.reason: "expired"`;
  - `plan-apply-not-found`: `apply 01ZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZ` → exit 3, `plan_not_found`.
- **Scene C, another asset, equal versions:** Foo v1 installed, v2 published with asset `Foo.zip`, `check`, `plan-asset-list`; then v2 published again under the same tag with the asset `Foo-retail.zip`, `outdated --refresh`; `plan-update-asset`: the preview → same `to_version` and `release_id`, `asset` `Foo-retail.zip`. *Decided while writing this bead:* if the CLI cannot see a same-tag re-upload (the memo keeps the old asset after the refresh), write this case as a derived fixture in bun instead (the routine preview with `approval.selection[0].asset` changed, labelled derived), and say so in the close comment.
- **Scene D, a dependency added:** Foo v1 installed with no dependency; v2's TOC requires `LibFoo`, which a `catalog.d` override names as a GitHub release (the `tests/deps.rs` helpers: `common::graph::release_graph` and its `catalog` support), `check`, `plan-dependency-list`; `plan-update-dependency`: the preview → `approval.reasons` holds `dependency_added`, `scope.dependencies_added` names LibFoo, `routine` false.
- **Scene E, local edits replaced:** Foo v1 installed, a file in its folder edited by hand (`core.lua` rewritten), v2 published, `check`, `plan-local-edits-list`; `plan-update-local-edits`: the preview → `local_changes_replaced` with `scope.local_changes_replaced.count >= 1` and `folders` holding `Foo`.
- **Scene F, extra removals:** Foo v1 has the folders `Foo` and `Foo_Options`; v2 ships only `Foo`; `check`, `plan-removal-list`; `plan-update-removal`: the preview → `folders_removed`, `scope.folders_removed` holding `Foo_Options`.
- **Derived in bun, not written by the binary** (decided while writing this bead): "another source" (`approval.selection[0].source` changed on a copy of `plan-update-routine`; the fixture home cannot make `update` switch an addon's source cheaply) and "a full plan store" (a copy with `plan_id: null`, the selection kept and a `plan_not_stored` warning; D4, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`, owns the real quota scenario with 512 plans).

`const PLAN_FIXTURES: &[&str]` in the file's `support` module lists every name above; `plans_fixtures` writes exactly those (asserted at its end by listing the directory).

### 2. bun scenarios (`omarchy/tests/model.test.js`, `describe("plans from the binary")`)

Each test reads its fixtures with `fixture(name)`, builds `shown` from the scene's list fixture exactly as the views do (`M.updateRows(M.reduceList(fixture(<list>)), <filter>, [])` then `M.shownOf`), and runs `M.previewDecision({mode, shown, again: false, path}, fixture(<preview>))`:

- `a routine matching update applies its plan directly`: `plan-list` + `plan-update-routine` → `direct`; `M.cliArgv(decision.plan.argv, opts({plan: decision.plan})).argv` ends `["--progress", "json", "apply", <plan_id>]` and holds no `--dry-run` or `--if-match`.
- `the apply's result reads as the update's`: `M.resultLine(M.applyResult(fixture("plan-update-routine-apply")))` is "Updated 1 addon"; its `commands` carry an `undo` or `undo_run` action (if not, file a bug `discovered-from` omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1 against D5, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`: its `apply` envelope must keep the executed command's `commands[]`; mark this assertion pending on it).
- `nothing to do refreshes`: `plan-update-noop` → `refresh`.
- `update all applies when every row matches`: `plan-list-after` (filter "") + `plan-update-all` → `direct`; with one row removed from `shown` → `dialog` with "Changed since you looked" and an "Also: … (not in the view)" line.
- `a moved release opens the dialog as changed`: `plan-moved-list` + `plan-update-moved` → `dialog`, first line "Changed since you looked: Foo v3 is now the newest".
- `another asset opens the dialog as changed`: `plan-asset-list` + `plan-update-asset` → `dialog`, a line "Foo v2 comes in another file now (Foo-retail.zip)".
- `another source opens the dialog as changed` (derived): → `dialog`, "Foo comes from wowi now".
- `a dependency added opens the dialog naming it`: `plan-dependency-list` + `plan-update-dependency` → `dialog`, no heading, a line starting "Also installs LibFoo" and ending "(a new dependency)".
- `local edits replaced open the dialog`: → a line "Replaces 1 file you changed in Foo (kept for undo)".
- `extra removals open the dialog`: → "Removes the folder Foo_Options (kept for undo)".
- `a full store runs nothing` (derived): → `refuse` with the warning's fix as `fixText`.
- `a stale, an expired and a missing plan preview again`: `needsPreviewAgain` true for `plan-apply-stale`, `plan-apply-expired`, `plan-apply-not-found`; `staleText` gives "Changed since you looked: selection. Nothing ran; check the new preview.", "The plan expired. Nothing ran; check the new preview." and "The plan is gone (expired or cleared). Nothing ran; check the new preview.".
- `a removal and an undo confirm through apply`: `plan-remove` and `plan-undo` in `confirm` mode → `dialog` whose lines start with `confirmText`'s ("Remove Bar v1 from retail (1 folder)", "Undo update on …"); `applyResult` of their `-apply` fixtures read "Removed 1 addon" and "Undid update on …".
- `every planned argv parses`: for each preview fixture with a plan, `built-argv.json`'s `planned` gains `{plan_id, argv}` (the writer of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.2), which `validate_built_argv` parses.

### 3. QML scenarios over the binary's envelopes (`omarchy/tests/qml/tst_plans.qml`)

- **`omarchy/tests/qml_fixtures.js`** (new, test-only; `tests/` is never embedded or scanned as runtime): `bun omarchy/tests/qml_fixtures.js <fixtures dir> <out file>` reads every `plan-*.json`, sets each envelope's `tool_version` to the fixture `Build.js`'s `TOOL_VERSION` (read from `omarchy/tests/fixtures/Build.js`, today `0.0.0-fixture`) so `Model.compatible` accepts them under that `Build.js`, and writes `.pragma library` plus `var TEXT = {"<name>": "<the envelope as one line>", …}` and `function text(name)` (throwing on an unknown name).
- **`scripts/widget-test.sh`**, step 4, after `cp -r omarchy "$plugin"` and the `Build.js` copy: `bun omarchy/tests/qml_fixtures.js "$OMADDONS_WIDGET_OUT/fixtures" "$plugin/tests/qml/Fixtures.js"`. It writes only inside the temporary `$OMADDONS_WIDGET_OUT`, never a tracked or gated file.
- **`tst_plans.qml`** (`TestCase { name: "Plans" }`), with `tst_service.qml`'s helpers (`make`, `ready`, `runs`, `lastRun`, `words`, `answer`; copy them, or move them into a shared `imports/` helper, whichever keeps both files simple) and `import "Fixtures.js" as Fixtures`. Each test sets `service.lists = Model.reduceList(JSON.parse(Fixtures.text(<list>)))`, calls the view's entry point (`service.run(template, slots, label, Model.updateRequest(…).shown)` or `rowAction`), answers the preview launch with `Fixtures.text(<preview>)`, and asserts the next launch and the model:
  1. `test_a_routine_matching_update_applies_with_no_dialog`: the next launch is `apply <plan_id>` (`words` equal `["apply", id]`), `service.confirm === null`; answered with `plan-update-routine-apply` → `lastResult.line` "Updated 1 addon", a `status` launch follows.
  2. `test_a_matching_update_that_adds_a_dependency_opens_the_dialog_naming_it`: no `apply` launch; `confirm.text` holds "Also installs LibFoo"; `confirm.heading === ""`; `confirmYes()` → the `apply` launch.
  3. `test_a_moved_release_opens_the_dialog_with_changed_since_you_looked`: `confirm.text` starts "Changed since you looked: Foo v3 is now the newest"; no `apply` until Yes.
  4. `test_a_matching_update_that_replaces_local_edits_opens_the_dialog`: "Replaces 1 file you changed in Foo (kept for undo)".
  5. `test_a_matching_update_with_extra_removals_opens_the_dialog`: "Removes the folder Foo_Options (kept for undo)".
  6. `test_equal_versions_from_another_asset_open_the_dialog`: the heading and the asset line.
  7. `test_a_stale_apply_previews_again_and_never_reruns_apply`: Yes on the moved dialog → `apply`; answered `plan-apply-stale` → a new `update --dry-run` launch (not `apply`); answered `plan-update-v4` → the dialog with `confirm.stale` starting "Changed since you looked"; exactly one `apply` launch so far.
  8. `test_an_expired_plan_previews_again`: the `apply` answered `plan-apply-expired` → a new preview launch, `confirm.stale` starting "The plan expired."
  9. `test_a_missing_plan_previews_again`: answered `plan-apply-not-found` → a new preview launch, `confirm.stale` starting "The plan is gone".
  10. `test_a_no_op_preview_refreshes_and_runs_nothing`: answered `plan-update-noop` → no `apply`, a `status` launch, `lastResult.line` "Already up to date; the view is refreshed".
  11. `test_update_all_applies_when_every_row_matches`: `updateRequest("", rows)` from `plan-list-after`; answered `plan-update-all` → `apply`; answered `plan-update-all-apply` → "Updated 3 addons on 2 clients".
  12. `test_a_removal_confirms_and_runs_apply_of_its_preview`: `run("remove", …)` answered `plan-remove` → the dialog starts on No (`confirm` set, nothing launched); `confirmYes()` → `apply <id>`; answered `plan-remove-apply` → "Removed 1 addon".
  13. `test_undo_last_confirms_through_apply`: `runCliArgv(<plan-undo's argv without --dry-run>, "Undo")` answered `plan-undo` → dialog; Yes → `apply`; answered `plan-undo-apply` → "Undid update on …".
- The first three names are fixed: T3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.3`) asserts they exist and pass.

### 4. Rust checks (`tests/omarchy_widget.rs`)

- `the_plan_scenarios_read_only_fixtures_the_binary_writes` (always on): every `Fixtures.text("<name>")` in `omarchy/tests/qml/tst_plans.qml` names an entry of `PLAN_FIXTURES`, and every QML test function named in this body exists in the file (a list of the 13 names).
- `the_output_cap_bounds_every_template` (`:296-392`): measure, on its own `behind(n)` home for n = 10 and 30 (so the existing `update_all` measurement is unaffected), the `update_all` template with `--dry-run` (`update_all_preview`) and `apply <its plan_id>` (`apply`); extrapolate as the test does (`base`, `slope`); assert `CLIENTS * (base + ADDONS * slope) < cap` for both. *Decided while writing this bead:* if either reaches the cap, do not raise `WIDGET_OUTPUT_MAX_BYTES` here; file a bug `discovered-from` omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1 with the measurement and block omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1 on it.
- `validate_built_argv`: the `planned` entries now come from the real fixtures too (§2), parsed as in omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.2.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `write_widget_fixtures` writes every `PLAN_FIXTURES` entry, each scene asserting its shape (routine, no-op, Update all, undo and remove through `apply`, moved, stale, expired, not found, asset, dependency, local edits, removal) before it writes.
- [ ] The bun scenarios of §2 pass on those fixtures: the routine and Update all cases decide `direct`; the dependency, local-edits and removal cases open the dialog naming the effect; the moved, asset and (derived) source cases open it with "Changed since you looked"; the no-op refreshes; the full store (derived) refuses; the stale, expired and missing cases re-preview with their texts; removal and undo confirm through `apply`.
- [ ] The 13 QML scenarios of §3 pass in `tst_plans.qml` over the generated `Fixtures.js`, the first three under their fixed names.
- [ ] `the_plan_scenarios_read_only_fixtures_the_binary_writes` passes.
- [ ] The output-cap test covers the `update_all` preview and its `apply` (12 clients, 400 addons each) below `WIDGET_OUTPUT_MAX_BYTES`.
- [ ] `validate_built_argv` parses every planned `apply` argv bun built from a real preview.
- [ ] `argc gate --all` passes (the widget pipeline with its QML step, and `cargo deny`).

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

None new: the pure functions are omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.2's. The bun scenarios here are table-free scenario tests, each naming its fixtures in its assertion messages.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

As §1–§4. The Rust scenes run in pipeline step 1 (`cargo test --locked --test omarchy_widget -- --ignored --exact write_widget_fixtures`), the bun scenarios in step 2, the argv parse in step 3, the QML scenarios in step 4 (`argc gate` runs it whenever `omarchy/` changed; `argc gate --all` always).

### Logging

- The fixture scenes use the `TestLog` of T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`) (`let log = tlog!();` inside `write_widget_fixtures`, or one log per scene function): `log.step("scene A: routine")` and one step per fixture; `log.run(&home, &argv)` for every command (argv, overrides such as `OMADDONS_NOW`, exit, envelope, stderr events, `net.log` lines); `log.json("<fixture name>", &envelope)` for each fixture written; `log.note("…")` for each asserted shape ("approval.routine true", "one apply offer"). A failing scene prints `test log: <path>` and its last 20 steps, so a fixture that stopped matching shows the envelope the binary actually wrote.
- bun: every `expect` carries `[<test>, <fixture>, actual]`.
- QML: every `compare`/`verify` carries a message naming the step, and on a wrong launch the test logs `JSON.stringify(ProcessRegistry.launches.map(function(l) { return words(l.command) }))` before failing.
- `argc e2e widget` is not needed: these run in the widget pipeline, whose output already prints each step (`==> widget n/4: …`).

## Considerations

- **Fixture realism is the point.** If the shapes of D4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`) or D5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`) differ from what omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.2 reads (the approval's field names, the offer's argv, the `apply` envelope), these scenarios fail first: fix the reader if this leaf read the shape wrongly, or file a bug `discovered-from` omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1 against D4 or D5 if the shape breaks its own contract (the offer must carry the full plan id; `apply` must keep its command's `commands[]`).
- **Slow scenes:** six small homes; keep each to the commands listed (the pipeline's step 1 runs once per gate).
- **The `OMADDONS_NOW` expiry** needs the plan's `created_at` from the preview's `plan_expires_at` minus `PLAN_TTL` (24 h); set it 25 hours after the preview's time.
- **`Fixtures.js` is generated per run** into the temporary plugin copy; never commit one, and never write it under `omarchy/` (common rule 17's "no shell redirect writes a gated asset" holds: it writes into `$OMADDONS_WIDGET_OUT`).
- **Hot spots:** `tests/omarchy_widget.rs` (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1, then the doctor fixtures of G2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.2`; append a new function rather than editing the existing scenes), `scripts/widget-test.sh` (one added line in step 4).

## Dependencies

- **Parent:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1 (The widget previews and applies plans).
- **Before it:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.1 (the `list` keys the scenes' rows carry) and omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1.3 (the runner the QML scenarios drive); T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, the structured test log) for the fixture scenes' logging.
- **After it:** nothing inside omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1; T3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.3`, slice 2 end to end) asserts its first three QML scenarios by name once omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1 closes.

title: The Issues view runs doctor repairs
description:
## How to work this bead

This bead is worked through its 4 subtasks, listed below in work order. Claim a subtask, not this bead (`br ready --parent omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.2` lists the ready ones). The agent that closes the last open subtask then verifies every acceptance criterion of this bead (they are the leaf's, not any one subtask's), and closes this bead with `br close omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.2 --reason "done: <evidence> · found: <ids>"`. Until this bead is closed, every bead it blocks stays blocked.

1. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.2.1 The widget's repair decisions in `omarchy/Model.js`: the `doctor_fix` templates and their `{fm}` slot, the classifier's consent rule (`--force`, `--yes`, `doctor gc`, and `doctor fix`/`doctor undo` only through their own flows), the doctor reducers (`doctorResult`, the preview decision, the dialog, result and explanation lines), the repair-undo texts and the result's Undo of a repair, all pure and bun-tested, with the Rust template invariants.
2. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.2.2 The Issues view runs repairs: `Service.qml` previews a repair and runs it bound to its token, reads a row's explanation, and offers a repair's Undo once `status` names it; `IssuesView.qml` and `PanelView.qml` use them; QML tests; README's `omarchy` section.
3. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.2.3 Tests: security scan 11, "consent stays a person's": no template, view or service path can run a forced repair, `doctor gc`, or `doctor fix` outside its bound flow, each with its planted violation.
4. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.2.4 E2E: the repair flow over envelopes the binary writes: the credential repair, its stale case and its undo through a stored plan, the set-aside row and its explanation, in bun and in QML (`tst_repairs.qml`), with the output-cap measurement.

Subtask 1 is pure JavaScript plus the Rust and bun tests that hold the template table, and can start at once. Subtask 2 waits for it: it switches the views over to the functions of subtask 1 in one commit (the gate runs the QML suites whenever `omarchy/` changes). Subtasks 3 and 4 wait for subtask 2 and touch different test files, so they can run in parallel; subtask 4 also writes Rust integration scenes through T1's `TestLog` and so waits for T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, the structured test log) as well.

**Not a design gate.** Common rule 14 lists D1, D2, D5, D8, E5, E7, E8, E11, E14 and G3. This leaf adds no journal shape, recovery rule, binding rule, deletion rule or durability rule, and no CLI wire name: it makes the bar widget a client of the binding protocol `doctor fix` already has (E6) and of the repair undo E7 built. **Size M:** one coordinated widget change across `Model.js`, `Service.qml`, two views and their three test suites, plus fixture scenes in `tests/omarchy_widget.rs`; no Rust product code changes.

## Background

**What this leaf is.** The Omarchy bar widget (`omarchy/`) runs omaddons command lines for everything it does. Its Issues view lists `status`'s problems by severity and runs each one's remediation with Enter when the widget's classifier accepts the argv (`omarchy/views/IssuesView.qml:62-72`). M4 gives omaddons a doctor: `status`'s issues come from the doctor's detector registry (F8 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.8`, `status` on the registry), each carrying `auto_fixable` and an `explain` command; `omaddons doctor fix --only <fm>` repairs one failure mode as one undoable engine transaction, previewed with `--dry-run` and bound with `--if-match <token>` (E6 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`, `doctor fix`); and `omaddons undo` reverts a repair strictly, through a preview that stores a plan and `apply` (E7 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7`, undo of repairs). This leaf makes the Issues view use them: Enter on an auto-fixable problem previews the repair, a dialog lists every change it would make, and Yes runs exactly that repair, bound to the preview. Undo last (and the footer's Undo after a repair) reverts it like any other change, through the stored plan of `undo --dry-run`.

**What the widget never runs.** A set-aside (the guarded repair of a stuck journal, which needs `--only <fm> --force --yes` and is never auto-fixable), `doctor gc` (the only command that deletes what repairs keep), and any argv that holds `--force`. The classifier refuses all three, by test. A row whose repair is a set-aside shows the doctor's explanation and the exact command to run in a terminal, because the force gate exists for consent given by someone who read the explanation, and a dialog's Yes is too easy.

**The problem it solves, concretely.** After F8, an auto-fixable issue's remediation is `omaddons doctor fix --only <fm> [-t <id>]` with `destructive: false`. The classifier at `c0ab5e9` accepts any `omaddons` argv on a known path with no widget-owned flag (`omarchy/Model.js:384-420`), and a non-destructive mutating CLI argv runs **directly, without a preview** (`Service.runCliArgv`, `omarchy/Service.qml:362-380`; G1 keeps that rule for CLI argv). So from F8 until this leaf, Enter on such a row would run a repair nobody saw. Worse, a set-aside row's remediation (`… --force --yes`, F2 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.2`) would be a button too: the classifier has no rule about `--force` today. This leaf closes both, first in its subtask 1.

**Milestone goals it serves:**

- **G-M4-3, what was previewed is what runs:** "every command that changes addons can be previewed with `--dry-run` and then run bound to that preview, by token (`--if-match`) or by stored plan (`apply <plan_id>`)". The widget's repairs run only bound to their preview's token; their undos only through a stored plan.
- **G-M4-4, diagnosable and repairable:** "every auto-fixable state is repaired by one consented command that backs up verbatim, never deletes, and is proven by a fixture that round-trips … The states README calls 'manual repair' today each get a name, an explanation and a guarded repair." In the widget, the consented command is one key press after a dialog that lists every change; the guarded repairs stay a deliberate terminal command, with the explanation on screen.
- **G-M4-6, no new risk to the engine's guarantees:** the widget adds no write path; every check is the CLI's.

**Checkpoint criteria it serves** (the M4 checkpoint list, by number):

- **Criterion 8, the widget applies what it shows: the Issues part.** "The Issues view runs an auto-fixable finding's repair with a preview. It never runs a set-aside, `doctor gc`, or any argv with `--force`: those rows show the explanation and the terminal command. Checked by bun and QML tests and on the desktop, through IPC `state()` plus a screenshot." The update and destructive parts of criterion 8 are G1's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1`).
- **Criterion 17, gate and checkpoint runs:** `argc gate --all` passes from a clean checkout, the widget pipeline's QML step included.
- The checkpoint's desktop run "a doctor repair from Issues (the credential mode), with Undo last" (H6 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the checkpoint, step 3.2) and slice 3's demo item "the credential fix from the Issues view (QML) and Undo last" (recorded by T4 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4`, which asserts this leaf's QML scenarios by name).

**The decisions that shape it** (the full decision log is filed as comments on the milestone epic `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`):

- **M4-D38: the stuck journal states get a guarded "set aside" repair, which needs deliberate consent.** The six stuck journal states (`journal-too-new`, `journal-unreadable`, `journal-unexpected-state`, `journal-step-unrecognized`, `journal-marker-mismatch`, `journal-unattributed`) share a fixer that moves the journal set into quarantine and records a suspension manifest; its undo is a guarded reactivation that refuses once anything it depends on changed. It is `auto_fixable: false`, runs only with `--only <fm> --force --yes`, and is never part of a default `doctor fix`. Its `explain` states what the set holds (counts of folders and files, whether a folder may be the only copy), the attribution, that undo is possible only while nothing on that client has changed, and the safer alternative (for `journal_too_new`, finishing with the newer build). *Why for this leaf:* the repair changes how an interrupted change ends, so consent has to come from someone who read that explanation; a dialog's Yes would turn the force gate into one more key press. *Rejected* (in M4-D38): a default fix for these states, which "changes how an interrupted change ends, which needs explicit consent".
- **M4-D28 (the part this leaf owns):** "Doctor repairs from the Issues view preview with `doctor fix --dry-run` and confirm with `--if-match` (M4-D44)", and "`CLI_PATHS` gains … the doctor paths" (each added by its command's own leaf). The rest of M4-D28 (updates preview and apply a routine matching plan; destructive actions confirm through `apply`; plan errors re-preview, never re-run) is G1's and stands: one runner path serves every previewed action.
- **M4-D44: `doctor fix` binds with `--if-match`, and its dry run discloses everything.** The dry run returns every planned primitive `{seq, fix, fm, op, path, to?, mode?, pre, post, backup?, bytes}`, the delegated recoveries `{tx, family, phase, direction}`, the bytes to back up and a `precondition` token. Nothing run-specific enters the token (no run id, tx id or backup path; only stable predicates), so a preview in one process and the bound run in another agree. `doctor fix --if-match <token>` runs exactly that or nothing; the comparison happens under the lock before any recovery or repair moves anything; a mismatch is `plan_stale`, exit 4, non-retryable, its fix the dry run again. **No plan is stored.**
- **M4-D22: which commands store plans.** `doctor fix` and `doctor gc` bind with `--if-match` but store nothing (their exit codes come from the doctor dictionary, and `apply` reports the general one). `doctor undo` neither stores nor binds: "a convenience that resolves a run to its transaction: its bound form is `omaddons undo <tx> --dry-run` then `apply`". `undo` stores plans. This is why the widget's repair goes through `--if-match` (G1's binding branch for paths outside the plan store) while its repair undo goes through `undo`'s stored plan, and why the widget never runs `doctor undo`.
- **M4-D34 and M4-D40: the doctor envelope and its dictionary.** Every doctor verb prints `{ok, schema_version, tool_version, command, exit_code, <report keys>, error?, warnings, commands, meta}`: the report at the top level and **no `data` key**; `ok` is `exit_code == 0`; `error` is present only for exits 4, 5, 6, 64, 66, 73 and 74. Findings present (1), a partial fix (2) and a rolled-back fix (3) are reports, not errors. The dictionary: 0 healthy, 1 findings present, 2 fix partial, 3 fix failed and rolled back, 4 refused (`doctor_refused`, `plan_stale`), 5 concurrency lost (`locked`), 6 online required, 64 usage, 66 no input, 73 cannot create, 74 I/O. *Consequence here:* the widget's envelope reducers read `data` (`omarchy/Service.qml:621` takes a preview's token from `env.data.precondition`) and its outcome rule calls any `ok: false` envelope "failed" (`Model.outcomeOf`, `omarchy/Model.js:637-647`), while a repair's dry run with something to repair exits 1. Hence the dedicated reducer `Model.doctorResult(env)`.
- **M4-D46: a repair is undone by `omaddons undo`, strictly, as a new repair transaction.** Bare `undo`, `status.last_change` and the widget's Undo last may select a repair ("a repair is the newest change"). The undo's preview (`undo --dry-run`) returns E7's four-part token over the line's targets with generations, the inverse primitives, the live predicates, the backups' digests and the guards, and its stored plan applies through `apply` like any other.
- **M4-D53: `status` issues gain two keys.** `targets[].issues[]` and `data.issues[]` gain `auto_fixable` (bool) and `explain` (`{command, argv}`); an auto-fixable finding's remediation becomes `omaddons doctor fix --only <fm> [-t <id>]`; a manual one keeps its command, or prose. *Why (M4-D53):* "the widget's Issues view needs to know what it can fix."
- **M4-D36 (context):** what a repair keeps is deleted only by `doctor gc`, through a bound, dependency-aware retention plan that reports the undos it makes impossible. Its real run needs `--yes`. The widget never runs it, not even its dry run: deleting what may be an only copy is a terminal decision.
- **M4-D42 (context):** a finding's evidence is typed, never holds file content, and never names a path below `WTF/`. The widget displays evidence as plain text and adds its own guard against a `WTF/` path anyway.
- **M4-D48 (context):** the widget matches no issue id by name; G1 made that a permanent security scan (check 10, no `fm-…` literal in runtime code). This leaf keeps it: the Fix offer is driven by `auto_fixable`, never by an id.

**How it serves the vision.** G7, "`doctor` follows the world-class doctor contract": the widget is one more consumer of its preview-then-bind lifecycle and its top-level report shape, and it honours the contract's consent axiom (a forced repair needs a person who read why). G4, "the first command an agent guesses works", is untouched: the widget only reads what the CLI says. The thesis that omaddons stays the sole, safe, undoable authority over what it manages: the most casual surface, a bar button, can repair only what it showed, bound to what it showed, and undo it the same way.

## Technical Approach

### 1. What each Issues row does

| Row (from `status`'s issues) | Enter | Shown on the row |
|---|---|---|
| `auto_fixable: true` and an id matching `FM_ID_PATTERN` | **previews the repair** (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.2.2): `doctor fix --only <fm> [-t <id>] --dry-run`, a dialog listing every change, then the bound run | severity, title, client; "Enter previews the repair" |
| a remediation the classifier accepts (not a doctor fix, no consent flag), not auto-fixable | runs it, as today (destructive ones preview first, through G1's runner) | "Enter runs the fix" |
| a set-aside: the remediation holds `--force` or `--yes` | toggles the **explanation** (`doctor explain`, a read) | "A deliberate repair: read why (Enter), then run this in a terminal:" and the exact remediation command as text |
| a remediation that is `doctor explain …`, refused, or prose, with an `explain` the classifier accepts | toggles the explanation | the command or prose as text; "Enter explains it" |
| none of these | nothing | the text |

*Decided while writing this bead:* a row whose own remediation is `omaddons doctor explain …` (F1's interim remediation of the stuck journal rows before F2, and every manual row's `explain`) is shown as its explanation inline, never run as a generic action whose result line would only say "Done". The explanation is fetched on Enter, never in the background, because `doctor explain` re-runs a detector under its full deadline.

### 2. The templates and the `{fm}` slot (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.2.1)

Two templates in `COMMANDS` (`Model.js:99-127`; the header comment gains "G2 adds doctor_fix and doctor_fix_target (E6)"):

```js
"doctor_fix":        { "argv": ["doctor", "fix", "--only={fm}"],                   "mutates": true, "preview": "bind" },
"doctor_fix_target": { "argv": ["doctor", "fix", "-t", "{target}", "--only={fm}"], "mutates": true, "preview": "bind" },
```

- **`preview: "bind"`**, a third preview mode beside G1's `match` and `confirm`: the template runs first as its dry run, the dialog shows the dry run, and Yes runs the same argv with `--if-match <the preview's token>`. It is M3's binding confirmation, which G1 keeps for binding paths that store no plan, made explicit in the table. `buildArgv` (`:340-369`): a `match` or `confirm` template still builds only as a preview (G1's `preview_required`); a `bind` template builds as a preview with no token, and as a real run only with a token (`ifMatchFor` gets `needsBinding = template.bind === true || template.preview === "bind"`, so a real run without one is `token_required`, and the path must bind, else `token_not_bound`).
- **The slot `fm`** joins `SLOTS` (`:185`). `checkSlot` (`:265-272`) refuses a value that does not match `FM_ID_PATTERN = /^fm-[a-z0-9_-]+$/` with `bad_fm`. That is M4-D30's `--only` grammar for one id: no comma (one failure mode, never a list), no subsystem name, no upper case, nothing that could become a flag. The `--only={fm}` one-element option form keeps the value a single argv element (M3-D2's slot rule).
- **The label** (`--reason "<label> (bar widget)"`, recorded on the repair's history line): `"Repair: " + <issue title>`, with CR and LF turned into spaces, cut to `LABEL_MAX_CHARS` (120) with "…" when longer (`reasonOf` refuses a longer one).
- **Machine-level issues** use `doctor_fix` (no `-t`), a client's issues `doctor_fix_target` with the row's target id, mirroring M4-D53's remediation `doctor fix --only <fm> [-t <id>]`.
- *Decided while writing this bead:* templates, not the issue's remediation argv. The widget then never depends on the CLI's argv for a mutation it runs: the fixed shape holds no `--force`, no `--yes`, no extra selection flag, and exactly one failure mode, validated by the slot pattern.

`Model.repairRequest(issue, targetId)` returns `{template, slots: {fm, target?}, label}` when `issue.autoFixable === true` and `FM_ID_PATTERN.test(issue.id)`, else `null`.

### 3. The classifier: what the widget never runs (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.2.1)

`classifyCliArgv(argv)` gains three refusals, checked in this order after `malformed`, `not_omaddons` and `widget_flag`, and before `unknown_path` and G1's `apply_outside_plan`:

| Reason | When | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `consent_flag` | any element of the argv (before or after `--`) is `--force` or `--yes`, or starts with `--force=` or `--yes=` (`CONSENT_FLAGS = ["--force", "--yes"]`) | a forced repair, a takeover of another addon's folders and `doctor gc --yes` each need consent given in a terminal by someone who read why (M4-D38); checkpoint criterion 8's rule is "any argv with `--force`", and `--yes` (which only `doctor fix --force` and `doctor gc` take) is refused with it |
| `doctor_gc` | the first two words are `doctor gc`, whether or not `CLI_PATHS` has the row yet | gc deletes what repairs keep and may hold an only copy (M4-D36); the widget never runs it, not even its dry run (E8's growth row remediation `omaddons doctor gc --before 30d --dry-run` is text) |
| `own_flow_only` | the first two words are `doctor fix` or `doctor undo` | a repair runs only from the Issues view's templates, previewed and bound (section 2); a repair undoes only through `undo`'s stored plan (M4-D22: `doctor undo` neither stores nor binds; its bound form is `undo <tx> --dry-run` then `apply`) |

- `cliArgv` refuses the same argv (it classifies first), so a CLI-provided argv with any of them can only be text: `cliAction` (`:679-687`) marks it `runnable: false` and every view already shows a non-runnable action as its command.
- *Decided while writing this bead:* the consent check covers the whole argv, `--` included: the rule is about what a person reads, and an addon named `--force` is not worth an exception; `doctor undo` joins the refusals so the widget has one way to undo a repair, the bound one.
- `validate_built_argv` (`tests/omarchy_widget.rs:524-527`) learns the three reasons and checks each: `consent_flag` ⇒ the argv holds a consent flag; `doctor_gc` ⇒ its leading words are `doctor gc`; `own_flow_only` ⇒ they are `doctor fix` or `doctor undo`.

### 4. The doctor reducers (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.2.1)

All pure, engine-neutral JavaScript (ES2017 at most, `var`/`function`, no QML globals), exported for bun, deciding nothing from a warning's text.

- **`isDoctorEnvelope(env)`**: `envelopeOk(env)`, `env.command` starts with `"doctor "`, `typeof env.state === "string"` or `env.failure_mode` is an object, and no `data` key (M4-D34).
- **`doctorResult(env)`** for a `doctor fix` envelope, else `null`. It reads, defensively (missing values become `null`, `0` or `[]`): `{command, exitCode, state, dryRun, tx, summary: {findingsBefore, findingsAfter, actionsTaken, actionsFailed, bytesToBackUp, bytesBackedUp, backupsRestored, totalFindings}, actions (actions_planned in a dry run, else actions), delegated (delegated_planned or delegated), precondition (only when it matches TOKEN_PATTERN, else ""), findings, undoable (Array.isArray(env.undo_argv)), error (env.error or null), report (no error and exit ∈ {0, 1, 2, 3}), repaired (!dryRun && tx && state ∈ {DONE_OK, DONE_PARTIAL} && actionsTaken > 0)}`. The milestone's widget design sets its minimum: "`Model.doctorResult(env)` reads `state`, `summary`, `undo_command` and `undo_argv`".
- **`displayPath(path, context, targets)`**: the longest matching prefix, on a path-component boundary, among `<config>` (`context.XDG_CONFIG_HOME + "/omaddons"`), `<state>`, `<cache>`, each target's absolute `clientDir` (shown as `<id>:` and the rest without its leading slash, as E6's human output abbreviates) and `context.HOME` (shown as a leading `~`); otherwise the path as given. A path holding a `WTF` component followed by anything (`/WTF/`) becomes "(a path under WTF/, not shown)": the CLI never prints one (M4-D42), and the widget does not trust that alone.
- **`repairActionLine(action, context, targets)`**, one plain line per primitive, built only from typed fields:

  | `op` | Line |
  |---|---|
  | `chmod` | `chmod 0600 <config>/credentials/github (was 0644)` (the `mode`, the path, `pre.mode` when present), plus " (readable by other users again)" when the new mode grants group or other read (`& 0o044`) and the old one did not |
  | `write_file` | `Rewrite <path> (1.2 KiB; the old file is kept for undo)` when it replaces a file (`backup` set or `pre.kind == "file"`); `Create <path> (1.2 KiB)` otherwise; the size from `bytes`, left out when absent (a real run's `actions`) |
  | `rename_noreplace` | `Move <path> to <to>`; with `activation: true` (an undo of a set-aside), `Reactivate the interrupted change's journal (<to>); the next change finishes it` |
  | anything else | the op with underscores as spaces, then the path |

- **`doctorPreviewDecision(spec, env, context, targets)`** returns `{kind, token, heading: "", lines, line, fixText}`, with `kind` one of G1's (`failed`, `refresh`, `refuse`, `dialog`):

  | Case | `kind` |
  |---|---|
  | not a `doctor fix` report, or it carries `error` (`doctor_refused`, `locked`, `usage`, …) | `failed`: the service shows the error card with its fixes, as for any failed preview |
  | `actions` and `delegated` both empty (`DONE_OK`: nothing found now, or nothing the fixer plans) | `refresh`: "Nothing to repair now; the view is refreshed" |
  | any planned action whose `fm` differs from `spec.slots.fm` | `refuse`: "The preview planned more than this repair; nothing ran" |
  | `precondition` missing or not a token | `refuse`: "The preview gave no token to bind; nothing ran" |
  | otherwise | `dialog`, with `token` = the precondition |

  The dialog lines: one `repairActionLine` per planned action, at most `WIDGET_DIALOG_ITEMS_MAX` (G1's constant, 12), then "(and N more)"; one line per delegated recovery, "Also finishes the interrupted change <tx> (<direction, underscores as spaces>)"; "Keeps a copy of <bytesText> first, for undo" when `summary.bytesToBackUp > 0`; and "Undo last reverts it". *Decided while writing this bead:* the `fm` check is a widget-side guard on top of `--only` (the CLI already restricts the plan to it); a repair dialog never gets the "Changed since you looked" heading of its own, because only a stale re-preview carries that (as `confirm.stale`).
- **`doctorResultLine(env, context, targets)`**, used by `resultLine(env, context, targets)` for a `doctor fix` envelope (the two new parameters are optional; without them paths show as given):

  | Report | Line |
  |---|---|
  | `error` | its message |
  | `DONE_OK`, `actions_taken > 0` | "Repaired: " + the first action's line, then " (and N more)" |
  | `DONE_OK` or `DONE_FINDINGS`, `actions_taken == 0` | "Nothing was repaired" + "; N findings remain (see Issues)" when `findings_after > 0` |
  | `DONE_PARTIAL` | "Partly repaired (N changes); M findings remain" |
  | `DONE_FAILED` (exit 3) | "The repair failed and was rolled back; nothing changed" |

- **`explainLines(env, context, targets)`** for a `doctor explain` envelope: the failure mode's `title`; its `description`; "Why it matters: " + `why`; one repair line ("No automatic repair" for `fixer: null`; "Its repair needs your deliberate consent: read this, then run the command below in a terminal" for `needs_force`; "Its repair is off by default: run the command below in a terminal" for `enabled: false`); "By hand: <instruction> (<reason>)" for `manual`; then per instance (at most `WIDGET_EXPLAIN_INSTANCES_MAX`, 5, then "(and N more)"): its `label`, its evidence as "  <key, underscores as spaces>: <value>" lines (keys sorted, at most `WIDGET_EXPLAIN_EVIDENCE_MAX`, 12; strings through `displayPath` when they start with `/`; booleans as yes and no; numbers as they are; arrays of strings joined with ", ", at most five, then "and N more"; objects and other values left out), and "  In a terminal: <the instance's remediation command>"; "No instance found now; it may be resolved" when `instances` is empty; and "The check was cut short (<limit>); this may be incomplete" when `incomplete` is set. *Decided while writing this bead:* these texts and the two limits (widget UI constants beside G1's `WIDGET_DIALOG_ITEMS_MAX`, pinned by bun's UI-constants test), so a set-aside's explanation shows M4-D38's statements (what the set holds, the attribution, when undo is possible, the safer alternative) through the description, the manual line and the evidence F2 fills, never through parsing a message.
- **`explainFor(explanation, row)`**: the lines of `explanation` (`{selection: {key}, lines, failed}`) when its selection is the row's key, else `null` (the pattern of `rawLines`, `Model.js:1902-1922`).
- **`staleText(env)`** (G1's, extended): for `env.command === "doctor fix"`, "Changed since you looked: <parts>. Nothing ran; check the new preview.", with each `details.changed` part in words (`observed` → "the files this repair checks", `selection` → "what it would do", `targets` → "the clients it touches", `command` → "the command"). Other commands keep G1's text.

### 5. Undo of a repair, in the texts and the footer (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.2.1, wired in omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.2.2)

- `KIND_WORDS` (`Model.js:767`) gains `"repair": "repair"`, so `lastChangeOf` labels the control "Undo repair" (and " on <ids>" when the repair touched clients; a home-side repair's `targets` is empty).
- `confirmText(name, env, context, targets)` (the two parameters optional, as above): for an `undo` envelope whose `data.kind === "repair"`, "Undo repair" (or "Redo repair" when `reverted.kind === "undo"`) + " on <ids>" from `reverted.targets` + ": N changes", then one `repairActionLine` per `repairs_reverted[]` entry (at most 12, then "(and N more)"). So the dialog of Undo last reads "Undo repair: 1 change" and "chmod 0644 <config>/credentials/github (was 0600) (readable by other users again)", where M3's text would say "0 folders restored, 0 removed". G1's `previewDecision(spec, env)` forwards `spec.context` and `spec.targets` to it.
- `commandResultLine("undo", data)` for `data.kind === "repair"`: "Undid repair" (or "Redid repair") + " on <ids>" + " (N changes)".
- **The footer's Undo of a repair is Undo last.** `Model.resultUndo(result, lastChange)` (the second parameter new): for a result with `repair: true`, it returns `{action: "undo_run", command, argv, runnable: true}` from `lastChange.undo` only when `result.statusSeen === true`, `lastChange` is known, its `kind` is `repair` and its undo is runnable; otherwise `null`. Any other result keeps today's rule. *Decided while writing this bead:* the fix envelope's own undo hint is `omaddons doctor undo <run>`, which stores no plan and binds nothing, so the footer offers the same bound undo as Undo last (`undo --run <run> --dry-run`, its plan, `apply`), and only once a `status` read after the repair names a repair as the last change (`statusSeen`), so it can never offer to revert some other change under the repair's line. This is the milestone's workflow sentence "the footer then shows 'repaired · Undo'" (§4.4).

The flow, end to end:

```text
Issues: P2 the GitHub token file is readable by other users          (status --cached: auto_fixable: true)
Enter   → buildArgv("doctor_fix", {fm}, {preview: true})
          omaddons --json --actor widget --reason "Repair: … (bar widget)" --progress json --dry-run
                   doctor fix --only=fm-secrets-credential-file-mode          (mutation lane; exit 1, DONE_FINDINGS)
        → doctorPreviewDecision: dialog, token pc1:…
          "chmod 0600 <config>/credentials/github (was 0644)" · "Undo last reverts it"       (starts on No)
Yes     → buildArgv("doctor_fix", {fm}, {token})
          omaddons … --if-match pc1:… doctor fix --only=fm-secrets-credential-file-mode     (a new process; exit 0)
          plan_stale (exit 4) → preview again, "Changed since you looked: the files this repair checks …"
        → footer "Repaired: chmod 0600 <config>/credentials/github" · Undo (after the next status names the repair)
z       → undo --run <run> --dry-run → a stored plan → dialog "Undo repair: 1 change" → Yes → apply <plan_id>
```

## Considerations

- **Risks.** No numbered milestone risk is this leaf's. Related ones: #23, guarded reactivation refuses more often than users expect (owners F2, E7): mitigated here by showing the explanation, which says so, before anyone consents to a set-aside. #3, doctor false positives erode trust (owners F*, H6): the widget offers Fix only for `auto_fixable` findings, every repair is undoable, and the dialog lists every change. New risks this leaf watches: (a) **a Fix that runs more than the dialog showed:** guarded by M4-D44's token (compared under the lock in a second process), the widget's `fm` check on every planned action, and the binary-written stale scene; (b) **a forced repair from a button:** guarded by the template shape (no consent flag can be in a slot), the classifier's `consent_flag`, scan 11 and the set-aside scenario; (c) **an Undo that reverts something else:** the footer's Undo appears only after `status` names a repair, and its dialog lists the inverse primitives, starting on No.
- **Hot spots (§10.5).** `omarchy/Model.js` and `Service.qml`: **G1 → G2** (G1 `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1` first, then this bead); command leaves add only `CLI_PATHS` rows, so rebase onto theirs. `views/IssuesView.qml` (G1 touches its update call at `:65`), `PanelView.qml` (G1's `updateAll`) and `tests/omarchy_widget.rs` (G1's invariants and fixtures): rebase onto G1 and keep each change in its own function. `README.md`: edit only the `omarchy` section's Issues bullet, Enter row and rules list.
- **Commit consistency.** `argc gate` runs the QML step whenever `omarchy/` changed. Subtask 1 is additive in behaviour except the classifier's refusals (a `doctor fix`, `--force` or `doctor gc` argv becomes text, which is safe and needs no view change); subtask 2 is the one switch-over commit for the views.
- **Previews accumulate run directories.** Every `doctor fix` invocation, dry run included, creates a run directory of kind `fix` (M4-D33); E8's `fm-state_files-doctor-runs-accumulated` reports past 200 and `doctor gc` reclaims them. The widget previews a repair only on Enter, never in the background, and never retries a preview by itself, so its share stays one directory per press.
- **The lock.** A bound run waits up to 5 s for the global lock and then exits 5 (`locked`, retryable); the mutation lane has no deadline (G1 keeps it so for every run that may commit), and the error card says another omaddons holds the lock.
- **The widget digest.** Changing `omarchy/` changes the build's widget digest, so an installed widget reports `fm-plugins-widget-version-drift` until `omaddons omarchy install` (H6 runs it after the M4 build).
- **Compatibility.** The widget is stamped for one binary (`Build.js`'s `TOOL_VERSION`); a binary from another build turns it read-only (M3-D42), so a pre-M4 binary never meets these templates.
- **Privacy.** Every line comes from typed fields, as plain text; evidence never holds file content (M4-D42); `displayPath` hides any path below `WTF/`; the `--reason` the widget records is the issue's registry title, which names no account, realm or character.
- **Common rules that do not apply:** 7 (no constant goes to `src/limits.rs`: the two new limits are widget UI constants in `Model.js`, beside G1's), 17 (nothing the guide's generated blocks show changes), 18 (no command or intent hook), 19 (no failure mode).
- **Size M** holds: no product Rust code, one coordinated widget change, its tests and fixture scenes.

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M4 plan, 2026-10-24).**

**Why this bead.** M4's doctor can repair what it finds, previewed and bound (`doctor fix --dry-run`, then `--if-match`), and undo it strictly (`omaddons undo`). The bar widget is where a player first sees a problem, and today its Issues view runs any remediation the classifier accepts. Once F8 puts `omaddons doctor fix --only <fm>` into `status`'s issues, that would mean a repair run without a preview, and a set-aside's `--force --yes` command would be one key press. This bead makes the Issues view a careful client of the doctor: Enter on an auto-fixable problem previews the repair, a dialog lists every change, and Yes runs exactly that repair bound to the preview; a repair that needs deliberate consent shows its explanation and its terminal command instead; Undo last reverts a repair through a stored plan like any other change. It is the user surface of checkpoint criterion 8's last sentence and of slice 3's "the credential fix from the Issues view and Undo last".

**Decisions applied.**
- **M4-D38:** set-asides are never `auto_fixable`, run only with `--only <fm> --force --yes`, and need consent from someone who read the explanation; the widget shows `doctor explain`'s text and the exact command, and never offers the repair.
- **M4-D28 (Issues part):** doctor repairs from the Issues view preview with `doctor fix --dry-run` and confirm with `--if-match`; the classifier knows the doctor paths.
- **M4-D44:** the dry run discloses every primitive, recovery and byte, and its token holds nothing run-specific, so the widget's second process matches it; a stale bound run touches nothing and re-previews.
- **M4-D22:** `doctor fix` binds and stores no plan (so the widget uses G1's binding branch, not `apply`); `doctor undo` neither stores nor binds (so the widget undoes a repair through `undo --dry-run` and `apply`, and never runs `doctor undo`).
- **M4-D34 and M4-D40:** the doctor envelope has no `data`, `ok` is `exit_code == 0`, and exits 1–3 are reports; hence a dedicated reducer, `Model.doctorResult`.
- **M4-D46:** a repair is the newest change, and Undo last may revert it, strictly, as a new repair transaction with E7's token.
- **M4-D53:** `auto_fixable` and `explain` on every issue are what the widget decides from; it never matches an issue id by name (M4-D48, G1's scan 10).
- **M4-D36 (context):** only `doctor gc` deletes what repairs keep; the widget never runs it, not even its dry run.

**Alternatives rejected.**
- *Running the issue's remediation argv as the Fix* (the M3 path): it lets the CLI's argv choose the shape of a mutation the widget runs, and it runs unpreviewed. The widget builds its own `doctor_fix` template from the issue's id instead, with a slot pattern that admits one failure-mode id and nothing else.
- *A dialog for set-asides:* a Yes in a bar panel is not the deliberate consent M4-D38 asks for; the explanation plus a terminal command is.
- *Storing doctor plans and confirming through `apply`* (one runner path for everything): M4-D44 and M4-D22 rejected stored plans for doctor runs, because `apply` reports the general exit dictionary.
- *The fix envelope's `doctor undo <run>` hint as the footer's Undo:* it stores no plan and binds nothing; the footer offers the bound Undo last instead, once `status` names the repair.
- *Refusing only `doctor fix --force`:* checkpoint criterion 8's rule is "any argv with `--force`", which also covers `install --force` takeovers suggested by a fix; `--yes` is refused with it.

**Risks and how they are watched.**
- A Fix that runs more than its dialog showed: M4-D44's token, compared under the lock in a second process; the widget's own check that every planned action belongs to the row's failure mode; the binary-written stale scene.
- A forced repair or a gc from a button: the template shape, the classifier's `consent_flag`, `doctor_gc` and `own_flow_only`, security scan 11 with eight planted violations, and the set-aside QML scenario.
- An Undo that reverts something else: the footer's Undo appears only after a `status` read names a repair as the last change, and its dialog lists the inverse changes, starting on No.
- Related milestone risks: #23 (guarded reactivation refuses more than users expect, owners F2 and E7), mitigated by showing the explanation before consent; #3 (doctor false positives, owners F* and H6), mitigated by offering Fix only for `auto_fixable` findings, each undoable.

**What it unblocks and why they wait.** H4 (the README final pass) reconciles the `omarchy` section's repair text. T4 (slice 3 end to end, added at filing) asserts this bead's three fixed QML scenario names and quotes the widget pipeline's run in the slice-3 demo.

**How it serves the milestone.** G-M4-3: the widget's repairs run only bound to their preview, and their undos only through a stored plan. G-M4-4: every auto-fixable state is one consented key press after a dialog that lists every change, and the guarded repairs keep their explanation and their deliberate terminal command. G-M4-6: the widget adds no write path and no CLI wire name; every check is the CLI's. It may land after H1, since it only consumes existing shapes.

**Facts verified while writing.** At `c0ab5e9` the classifier has no rule for `--force`, `--yes` or any path (`omarchy/Model.js:384-420`); `pathOf` would read `doctor gc …` as the read-only `doctor` while E8's row is missing (`:208-217`); non-destructive CLI argv run directly (`omarchy/Service.qml:362-380`); the preview flow takes its token from `env.data.precondition` (`:621`) and calls an `ok: false` envelope failed (`Model.outcomeOf`, `:637-647`), which a doctor dry run with findings is; `KIND_WORDS` has no `repair` (`:767`); `confirmText` describes every undo in folders (`:1377-1396`). F2 and E8 are not edges of this bead, so its set-aside fixture may be derived until F2 lands, and its gc row is derived in bun.

**Confidence.** High. The bead adds no protocol: it consumes E6's binding and E7's undo, both proven by their own matrices, through G1's runner, and every new decision is a pure function with table-driven tests plus a scenario over envelopes the binary writes.
