title: Tests: the documented workflow cannot bypass the released baseline
description:
Part 4 of 4 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.2 (The golden and the released-baseline mechanism). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

H2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.2`) makes omaddons' contract freeze enforceable: after the first tag, a contract change that does not carry its `schema_version` bump fails the gate, **however the current golden was regenerated**. Subtask 1 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.2.1) landed the gate test `wire_names::contract_compat` (the generated golden `tests/contract/manifest.json` and `tests/contract/wire_names.txt` with a header no comparison reads; comparison 1 with the newest released baseline `tests/contract/released/<version>.json` whenever one exists; comparison 2 with the committed golden; the updater `OMADDONS_UPDATE_WIRE_NAMES=1`, which rewrites the current golden only). Subtask 2 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.2.2) landed the release step `OMADDONS_ADVANCE_RELEASED_BASELINE=<version>`, the only writer of a baseline.

**This part tests the workflow itself** (§6.7 of the plan, and the leaf's plan entry): "with a synthetic baseline in a temporary directory, change the contract, run the documented updater without a version bump, and assert that comparison 1 still fails. Cases: an added output field, a removed one, a field made optional, a field made nullable, an integer turned number, a removed flag, a changed default, a new required positional, and an attempt to unfreeze by editing the current golden's header." With the right bump, each passes. This is the proof the design exists for. M4-D56: in the plan's reviewed draft, the update mode rewrote both the snapshot and the previous contract, so regenerating after a breaking change erased the evidence the gate needed, and unit tests of the pure classifier could not catch that bypass. "No local test can stop someone deliberately rewriting every test and baseline; the guarantee is that the documented workflow cannot silently disable the check." These tests are that guarantee.

**How a test "changes the contract".** Code cannot change while a test runs. Decided while writing this bead: the scenarios change the **manifest** (the semantic record a code change would produce) and run **the same `gate` function `contract_compat` runs**, with the mode, version and workspace as arguments; one scenario also runs **the real test binary as a child process** with the documented variable, so the variable's spelling, its parsing and the file writes are proven in a real process; subtask 3 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.2.3) separately proves that real code changes of each kind change the manifest. Together: code change → manifest change (subtask 3) → regenerated golden still fails against the baseline (this part).

It is the leaf's test subtask, ordered after the parts it tests (1 and 2).

**Goals and criteria served:** G-M4-5 ("one that does not carry its version bump fails the gate, however the current golden was regenerated"); checkpoint criterion 14: "A test exercises the documented updater: a contract change regenerated into the current golden without a version bump still fails against the released baseline, for an addition, a removal, a requiredness change, a removed flag and a changed default. Setting the current golden's header back to `frozen: false` does not disable the comparison." and "reordering keys needs no version bump"; slice 4's demo item "the golden and the updater tests" (recorded by H6, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`); risk #22 (the classifier mislabels a change; owners A10 and H2).

**The rules under test** (M4-D56, restated): additions only (an output field, enum value or variant; an optional field made always present; a narrower output bound; a new flag, alias, value or optional positional) need a higher minor; removals and loosenings (an output field removed, made optional or nullable, moved between variants; integer to number; a wider bound; a removed flag or value; a new requirement or conflict; a required positional; a narrower grammar; a changed default) and anything unclassified need a higher major; a persisted kind's change needs that kind's own version bump, not a wire bump; member order is never compared; comparison 1 depends only on the baseline's existence, never on a header.

**Facts this part relies on** (subtasks 1–2 and A10's API as their beads specify them):

- `tests/contract/wire_names.rs`: `Workspace::at(dir)` (`manifest_json()`, `wire_names_txt()`, `released_dir()`); `Mode { update_golden, advance }`; `golden(current, &header)`, `header(ws, version)`; `Provenance`; `gate(ws, &mode, current, version, &provenance_fn) -> Outcome { notes, failures, written }` (order: mode, release step, header, golden, updater, comparison 1, comparison 2; a release-step refusal is the only failure and writes nothing; the release step forces the updater on); `run_from_env(ws)` (reads `Mode::from_env()`, uses `support::manifest()`, `output::SCHEMA_VERSION` and `real_provenance`).
- Comparison 1's failure text (subtask 1, TA 4): the first line `compared with the released baseline (contract {b}, tag {tag}), this change is {verdict} ({summary}):`, then A10's `Changes::render()`, then the remedy `{an additive|a breaking} change needs schema_version {v}: set output::SCHEMA_VERSION = "{v}", regenerate the current golden` / `(OMADDONS_UPDATE_WIRE_NAMES=1 cargo test --test contract wire_names), and record it in a comment on the vision bead (omad-vision-8qa)`, plus "(schema_version is {x}, which does not satisfy it)" when bumped too little, the unclassified line, and one line per unsatisfied persisted kind. Comparison 2's starts `the current golden is out of date with the code:`; a header-only difference says `the header of <file> says … where the code gives …`.
- A10: `Manifest::parse` (reads `format` and `nodes`, ignores other top-level keys), `Manifest::render(&[…])`, `Manifest.nodes: BTreeMap<String, Node>`, `Node { kind: String, facts: BTreeMap<String, Fact> }`, `Fact::{Bool, Int, Text, List, Ints}`; node kinds `command`, `flag`, `positional`, `output_position`, `output_variant`, `file_kind`, `file_position`, …; facts `types`, `required`, `nullable`, `minimum`, `default`, `grammar`, `arity_min`, `arity_max`, `version`; `ids::parent`.
- `support::manifest()` (subtask 1): the real manifest, built once per process.
- `tests/common/trees.rs:439`: `tree_hash(dir)` (modes and symlink targets included). T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`): `tlog!()`, `log.step`, `log.note`, `log.json`, `log.tree(label, root)`, `log.assert_unchanged(label, root)`, the drop guard, `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG=verbose`, `argc e2e [FILTER]`.
- The contract suite's tests run on parallel threads in one binary (`cargo test --test contract`); `std::env::current_exe()` is that binary; libtest accepts `--ignored --exact <name> --nocapture --test-threads=1`.

## Technical Approach

### 1. The file and its helpers

`tests/contract/wire_names_workflow.rs`, `mod wire_names_workflow;` in `tests/contract/main.rs`. The documented filter `cargo test --test contract wire_names` also selects these tests; none of them reads the mode from the environment (each passes a `Mode` to `gate`), and the child-process test removes both mode variables from every child, so a developer's `OMADDONS_UPDATE_WIRE_NAMES=1` or release command never changes what they test.

Helpers (test code):

- `fn workspace() -> (tempfile::TempDir, Workspace)`.
- `fn fixed(v: SchemaVersion) -> impl Fn() -> Result<Provenance, String>`: returns `{contract_version: v, tag: "v0.1.0", commit: "0" × 40, created_at: "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z"}`; it never calls `git` or the clock.
- `fn update(ws, m, v) -> Outcome` = `gate(ws, &Mode { update_golden: true, advance: None }, m, v, &fixed(v))`; `fn compare(ws, m, v)` with `update_golden: false`; `fn release(ws, m, v)` with `advance: Some(v)` (and `release_at(ws, m, v, contract)` when the requested release and `gate`'s version differ).
- `fn seed(ws, base) `: `update(ws, base, 1.0)` (passes: no baseline), `release(ws, base, 1.0)` (writes `released/1.0.json`, header now `frozen: true`), `compare(ws, base, 1.0)` (passes, no change). Seeding through the real release step means every scenario also exercises it.
- `fn v(s: &str) -> SchemaVersion`.

### 2. The synthetic base manifest

`fn synthetic() -> Manifest`: `Manifest::parse` of a literal canonical text holding a small, realistic contract:

- `command install` (`aliases ["add"]`, `exits [0,1,2,3,4,5,6]`, `dictionary general`, `mutates true`, `binds true`, `stores_plan true`, `network optional`);
- `input install --channel` (kind `flag`, `grammar enum`, `values [alpha, beta, stable]`, `arity_min 1`, `arity_max 1`, `required false`);
- `input install --file` (`grammar path`, `required false`);
- `input install @1` (kind `positional`, `grammar string`, `required true`, `repeat true`, `arity_min 1`);
- `input omaddons --format` (`global true`, `grammar enum`, `values [human, json]`, `default human`);
- `output install data` (root), `output install data.items` (`types [array]`, `required true`, `nullable false`), `output install data.items[]` (`types [object]`, `nullable false`), `output install data.items[].name` (`types [string]`, `required true`, `nullable false`), `output install data.items[].files` (`types [integer]`, `required true`, `nullable false`, `minimum 0`), `output install data.tx` (`types [string]`, `required true`, `nullable true`);
- `error not_found` (`exit 3`, `retryable false`, `doctor_exit 66`) with `error not_found .` and `error not_found code`;
- `file target_record` (`version "1.3"`) with `file target_record .` and `file target_record generation` (`types [integer]`, `required true`, `nullable false`).

Exact text asserted against this base keeps the message tests readable.

### 3. The change kinds

Each case is a function `fn(&mut Manifest)`, with the bump it needs and a fragment its comparison-1 line must contain:

| Case | Change (synthetic base) | Change (real manifest: the node picked by predicate, which must exist) | Needs | Line fragment |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `added_output_field` | add `output install data.items[].size_bytes` (`output_position`, `types [integer]`, `required true`, `nullable false`, `minimum 0`) | add `output install data.added_by_test` (the same facts) under the object root `output install data` | minor | `+ output install data.` |
| `removed_output_field` | remove `output install data.items[].files` | the first leaf `output_position` (no descendants) by id under `output install data`, and its descendants | major | `- output install data.items[].files` |
| `field_made_optional` | `data.items[].name`: `required` → `false` | the first non-root `output_position` with `required: true` | major | `required` |
| `field_made_nullable` | `data.items[].name`: `nullable` → `true` | the first non-root `output_position` with `nullable: false` | major | `nullable` |
| `integer_turned_number` | `data.items[].files`: `types [integer]` → `[number]` | the first `output_position` whose `types` is exactly `[integer]` | major | `integer -> number` |
| `removed_flag` | remove `input install --channel` | remove `input install --channel` | major | `- input install --channel` |
| `changed_default` | `input omaddons --format`: `default human` → `json` | the first `flag` node with a `default` fact that is not `false` or `0`, its value replaced by `"changed"` | major | `default` |
| `new_required_positional` | add `input install @2` (`positional`, `grammar string`, `required true`, `arity_min 1`, `arity_max 1`) | add `input install @<highest index + 1>` the same way | major | `+ input install @` |
| `unclassified_node` | add `frobnicate x` (`kind "frobnicate"`) | the same | major (`breaking or unclassified`) | `unclassified` |
| `persisted_kind_field` | add `file target_record installed_by` (`file_position`, `types [string]`, `required true`) | add the same under the first `file <kind>` | that kind's minor (no wire bump) | `persisted file target_record` |
| `reordered_members` | none: the base re-parsed from a text with every node's facts and the nodes themselves written in reverse order | the real manifest's render with its node lines reversed, re-parsed | none | (no failure) |

For `persisted_kind_field`, "the right bump" is the kind's version raised (`file target_record` `version "1.3"` → `"1.4"`) with the contract version left at 1.0.

### 4. `every_change_kind_regenerated_without_a_bump_still_fails` (synthetic) and `every_change_kind_on_the_real_manifest` (real)

For each case, a fresh workspace and a `TestLog` step per phase:

1. `seed(ws, base)`; `log.tree("released", ws.released_dir())`.
2. `changed = base.clone(); case(&mut changed)`.
3. **Compare without regenerating** at 1.0: two failures (comparison 1 first, containing the fragment and the needed version; comparison 2, `the current golden is out of date`), or none for `reordered_members`.
4. **The documented updater without a bump** at 1.0: the golden files now equal `golden(&changed, &Header { contract: 1.0, frozen: true })` byte for byte; `log.assert_unchanged("released", …)`; the outcome still has **comparison 1's failure** (the same text as in step 3) and no comparison-2 failure. This is the assertion the bead exists for.
5. **Compare again** at 1.0: only comparison 1's failure, byte-identical to step 4's.
6. **The right bump**: `update(ws, &changed, needed)` passes with no failure (`1.1` for minor; `2.0` for major; for the persisted case, the kind's version raised and 1.0 kept). For minor cases also `2.0` passes (a major satisfies a minor). For major cases also `update(…, 1.1)` fails with "(schema_version is 1.1, which does not satisfy it)". `released/` is unchanged throughout.

On the synthetic base the full comparison-1 text of each case is asserted exactly (a literal per case in the test); on the real manifest the fragment, the verdict word and the needed version are asserted.

### 5. `header_edits_never_disable_the_comparison`

Seed the synthetic base, apply `removed_flag`, run the updater at 1.0 (comparison 1 fails; record its text `T`). Then, each from that state:

1. `manifest.json`'s header line edited to `"header": {"contract":"1.0","frozen":false}`;
2. `wire_names.txt`'s second line edited to `# frozen: false`;
3. both;
4. both headers deleted (the `"header"` line removed from `manifest.json`, the two `#` lines from `wire_names.txt`);
5. the `contract` in both headers edited to `2.0`.

For each: `compare(ws, &changed, 1.0)` → comparison 1's failure is byte-identical to `T`, and comparison 2 additionally fails naming the header (`the header of …`) or the difference. Then a final `update` restores the generated headers and only `T` remains. Assert `released/` unchanged after every step.

### 6. `the_release_step_in_sequence`

One workspace, the synthetic base:

1. `update(1.0)`, `release(1.0)`: `released/1.0.json` written; headers `frozen: true`; both comparisons pass.
2. Apply `added_output_field`. `release(1.1)` at contract 1.1 **without regenerating** → refused: "the current golden must match the code"; tree hash unchanged.
3. `update(1.0)` (comparison 1 fails), then `release_at(1.1, contract 1.0)` → refused: "advances to 1.1, but output::SCHEMA_VERSION is 1.0".
4. `update(1.1)` (passes), then `release(1.1)` at contract 1.1 → writes `released/1.1.json`; the next `compare(1.1)` notes the comparison against 1.1 ("no change").
5. `release(1.1)` again → refused: "exists"; tree hash unchanged.
6. `Mode { update_golden: true, advance: Some(1.2) }` → refused: "exclusive"; nothing written.
7. Apply `removed_flag` and `update(1.2)` → comparison 1 (against 1.1, the newest) fails needing `2.0`; `release(1.2)` at 1.2 → refused (the bump is missing).

`log.tree("workspace", …)` before and `log.assert_unchanged("workspace", …)` after every refusal.

### 7. `documented_updater_in_a_child_process`

The real test binary, run as a child, through the same `run_from_env` that `contract_compat` calls:

- **The child entry**, in this file:

  ```rust
  #[test]
  #[ignore = "a child of documented_updater_in_a_child_process"]
  fn workflow_child() {
      let Ok(dir) = std::env::var("CONTRACT_WORKFLOW_WORKSPACE") else { return };
      let out = wire_names::run_from_env(&Workspace::at(Path::new(&dir)));
      for note in &out.notes { println!("{note}"); }
      assert!(out.failures.is_empty(), "{}", out.failures.join("\n\n"));
  }
  ```

  `CONTRACT_WORKFLOW_WORKSPACE` is a private parent-to-child handshake of this test binary (not an `OMADDONS_` name, so no `ENV_VARS` row, as A3's `CONTRACT_DETAILS_OBSERVED` precedent), read **only** here; `contract_compat` never reads it, so no variable can point the real gate elsewhere. Run without it (for example by `cargo test -- --ignored`), the entry does nothing. Decided while writing this bead.
- **The parent** builds a workspace whose `released/1.0.json` is the **real** manifest (`support::manifest()`) **minus one node**: the last `output_position` leaf by id under the first `COMMANDS` row's data, rendered with a fixed provenance. The child builds the real manifest, which has that node, so the contract "added" it: additive, needing 1.1, while `output::SCHEMA_VERSION` is 1.0.
- Each child: `std::process::Command::new(std::env::current_exe()?)`, args `["--ignored", "--exact", "wire_names_workflow::workflow_child", "--nocapture", "--test-threads=1"]`, `env_remove("OMADDONS_UPDATE_WIRE_NAMES")`, `env_remove("OMADDONS_ADVANCE_RELEASED_BASELINE")`, `env("CONTRACT_WORKFLOW_WORKSPACE", dir)`, then the step's own variables:
  1. `OMADDONS_UPDATE_WIRE_NAMES=1` → exit non-zero; the output contains "this change is additive", `+ <the removed node's id>`, "needs schema_version 1.1" and "OMADDONS_UPDATE_WIRE_NAMES=1 cargo test --test contract wire_names"; the workspace's `manifest.json` parses equal to the real manifest and its header says `{"contract":"1.0","frozen":true}`; `released/`'s tree hash is unchanged.
  2. nothing set → exit non-zero with the same comparison-1 text, no "out of date" text; the workspace's tree hash is unchanged (a plain run writes nothing).
  3. `manifest.json`'s header edited to `frozen: false`, nothing set → the same comparison-1 text, plus the header named.
  4. `OMADDONS_UPDATE_WIRE_NAMES=true` → exit non-zero with "must be 1"; tree hash unchanged.
  5. `OMADDONS_ADVANCE_RELEASED_BASELINE=1.0` → refused (the golden is stale after step 3's edit, or the baseline exists); tree hash unchanged.
  6. `released/1.0.json` replaced by the full real manifest, then `OMADDONS_UPDATE_WIRE_NAMES=1` → exit 0 (the child path can pass: no false failure).

  Assert the exit status of each and search the combined output; bound each captured stream to 64 KiB in the log.

### 8. README

The Tests table's `tests/contract/` row (`README.md:2625`) adds "the updater's own tests (a change regenerated without its bump still fails against a released baseline)". Edit only that row.

### 9. What not to do

- Never point any test at `Workspace::repo()` in a writing mode; every writing scenario uses a temporary workspace.
- Never set a mode variable in the parent process (`std::env::set_var` is racy across the suite's threads); modes are arguments, and children get their variables per command.
- Do not weaken a case to make it pass: a wrong label is a classifier defect (A10's surface), filed `--deps discovered-from:omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.2.4` and blocking omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.2.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] For each of the eleven cases of TA 3, on the synthetic base and on the real manifest, the documented updater run at 1.0 without a bump rewrites the golden, leaves `released/` byte-identical, and still fails comparison 1 with the case's line and needed version, and comparing again fails comparison 1 alone; with the right bump each passes (a major also for minor cases; 1.1 fails major cases with "does not satisfy it"); the persisted case needs the kind's version and no wire bump; `reordered_members` needs nothing.
- [ ] The synthetic cases assert comparison 1's full text exactly.
- [ ] `header_edits_never_disable_the_comparison`: each of the five header edits leaves comparison 1's failure byte-identical and adds a comparison-2 failure; regenerating restores the headers.
- [ ] `the_release_step_in_sequence`: the release step writes 1.0 and then 1.1 only when allowed, refuses a stale golden, a wrong version, an existing baseline, the combined modes and a missing bump, and every refusal leaves the workspace's tree hash unchanged; after 1.1 the comparison uses the newest baseline.
- [ ] `documented_updater_in_a_child_process`: the six child runs of TA 7 behave as stated: the real binary with `OMADDONS_UPDATE_WIRE_NAMES=1` fails with the §4.8 message and leaves `released/` unchanged, a plain run writes nothing, a header edit changes nothing in comparison 1, a malformed value and a refused release write nothing, and an unchanged baseline passes.
- [ ] No test of this file writes outside a temporary directory or reads the mode from its own environment; each scenario logs through `TestLog` as the Logging section says.
- [ ] README's Tests table `tests/contract/` row names the updater's own tests, in this commit.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

- `case_table_is_complete`: the case table holds exactly the eight change kinds the plan names (added and removed output field, made optional, made nullable, integer to number, removed flag, changed default, new required positional) plus `unclassified_node`, `persisted_kind_field` and `reordered_members`, each with a needed bump and a fragment.
- `real_manifest_has_a_candidate_for_every_case`: each real-manifest predicate of TA 3 finds a node (a failure names the case: the real contract lacks the shape, so the case's predicate needs updating, never deleting).

### Integration and end-to-end tests

All in `tests/contract/wire_names_workflow.rs`, run by `cargo test --test contract wire_names` and `argc e2e wire_names`:

- `every_change_kind_regenerated_without_a_bump_still_fails` (TA 4, synthetic);
- `every_change_kind_on_the_real_manifest` (TA 4, real);
- `header_edits_never_disable_the_comparison` (TA 5);
- `the_release_step_in_sequence` (TA 6);
- `documented_updater_in_a_child_process` (TA 7), with its ignored entry `workflow_child`.

### Logging

Every scenario uses T1's `TestLog` (`let log = tlog!();`):

- one `log.step` per phase: `seed`, `change <case>`, `compare at 1.0`, `regenerate at 1.0`, `compare again`, `regenerate at <version>`, `header edit <n>`, `release <version>`, `child <n>`;
- after every `gate` call, `log.json("gate", {case, mode, version, notes, failures, written})`;
- `log.tree("released", ws.released_dir())` after seeding and `log.assert_unchanged("released", …)` after every updater run; `log.tree("workspace", …)` before and `log.assert_unchanged("workspace", …)` after every refusal and every plain compare (the first differing paths are logged on a difference);
- for each child: `log.json("child", {argv, env_set, env_removed, exit, stdout, stderr})`, each stream bounded to 64 KiB with a truncation note;
- a failing assertion names the case and step and prints the expected and actual comparison texts in full; T1's drop guard prints `test log: <path>` and the last 20 steps;
- `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG=verbose argc e2e wire_names` echoes every step live.

No checkpoint-only test: nothing here needs the real machine, a release build or the network.

## Considerations

- **Cost.** The real-manifest cases clone a manifest of thousands of nodes eleven times and classify: about a second. The child-process test starts the contract binary six times, each building the manifest: about ten seconds. If the file passes fifteen seconds in a debug build, merge child steps (the state carries over) rather than drop an assertion.
- **The real-manifest predicates depend on the contract's content** (an `install` command with items, a `--channel` flag). They assert a candidate exists and name the case when it does not, so a later contract change updates a predicate deliberately.
- **What a failure here means.** A case that passes without a bump is a bypass: either comparison 1 read something the updater wrote (subtask 1's defect) or the classifier mislabels the change (A10's, risk #22). Fix the cause; never relax the case. A rule found wrong is made more conservative.
- **Parallel threads.** Each scenario has its own temporary workspace; nothing shares state but `support::manifest()`, which is read-only.
- **Hot spots:** `tests/contract/main.rs` (one `mod` line; subtask 3 also edits it); `README.md` (the Tests row only).

## Dependencies

Parent: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.2 (The golden and the released-baseline mechanism), in area omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.

- **Before it:** subtask 1 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.2.1: `gate`, the comparisons, the updater, `support::manifest()`) and subtask 2 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.2.2: the release step, which seeds every scenario and whose refusals TA 6 sequences). Also T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs, and the `argc e2e` runner), whose `TestLog` every scenario uses.
- **After it:** none inside the bead. If it closes last (the usual order), its agent verifies every acceptance criterion of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.2 and closes it, which unblocks H4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`, the README final pass).

title: The determinism audit
description:
## How to work this bead

This bead is worked through its 5 subtasks, listed below in work order. Claim a subtask, not this bead (`br ready --parent omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3` lists the ready ones). The agent that closes the last open subtask then verifies every acceptance criterion of this bead (they are the leaf's, not any one subtask's), and closes this bead with `br close omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3 --reason "done: <evidence> · found: <ids>"`. Until this bead is closed, every bead it blocks stays blocked.

1. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3.1 `contract::VOLATILE` completed: scoped and kinded rows, one path grammar, the plan's rows, the schema check and README's table. The registry that every comparison masks with, and the only one.
2. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3.2 Every matrix row repeated on two fresh copies of its home and compared byte for byte, with the audit pass that declares or fixes each difference. The order-preserving comparison, `Scene::matrix`, and the end of the ad hoc strips.
3. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3.3 The coverage audit: a success and a failure row for every command path, the matrix's conventions, and the missing rows. A child run of the matrix records every row by its invoked path.
4. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3.4 The `HashMap` scan: `tests/determinism.rs` refuses a hash map or set in a serialized type of the output directories (`src/app`, `src/output`, `src/contract`, `src/doctor`).
5. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3.5 E2E: the audit catches what it must, on real runs over copies and over a partial matrix. Reduced tables, identity-bound and content-bound tokens, masked values that reappear, and empty or failed audits.

Subtasks 1, 2 and 3 form a chain: each builds on the code the previous one adds, in the same files (`src/contract/volatile.rs`, `tests/contract/main.rs`, `tests/contract/matrix.rs`). Subtask 4 touches only `tests/determinism.rs` and one README table row, so it can be worked at any time. Subtask 5 tests the machinery of 2 and 3, so it comes last. This is a size-M leaf kept as one bead for closure: H4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`, the README final pass) waits for all of it, because the README's "Volatile keys" table and "Stability" text are only true once every part has landed.

## Background

**What this is.** omaddons promises that one command on one unchanged home prints the same bytes every time, apart from a few keys whose values legitimately change (a new transaction id, a timing). Agents diff outputs, the bar widget compares them, and the contract's golden (H2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.2`, the golden and the released baseline) and the snapshots are only meaningful if the output is a function of the home. This bead is the audit that makes the promise checked, for every command path, by the gate:

1. `contract::VOLATILE` lists every key that may differ, each with its scope, its kind and its reason, and nothing else is ever masked.
2. Every row of the contract matrix runs twice more, each time on a fresh copy of the home it started from, and the two outputs must be byte-identical once the declared keys are masked, member order included.
3. A coverage test fails any command path without a success row and a failure row in the matrix, so "every row" means every command path. The rows missing today are added.
4. A source scan fails a `HashMap` or `HashSet` in a type that derives `Serialize` in the four output directories. Their iteration order is randomized per process (Rust's default `RandomState`), so such a field prints its members in a different order on each run.

**What is true today** (verified at `c0ab5e9`):

- The repeat tests cover a handful of read commands, in place, on one home: `repeated_runs_are_byte_identical` (`tests/contract/special.rs:455-474`: `list`, `status`, `history`, `info nosuchaddon`, `remove Nope`), `m2_outputs_are_byte_identical` (`:478-532`: `outdated`, `status`, `status --deep`, `export`, `search --offline`), and `sync --dry-run` twice (`tests/contract/matrix.rs:127-129`). No real run (an install, an undo, a backup), no doctor command and no plan command is ever repeated.
- They compare `support::without_meta(stdout)` (`tests/contract/main.rs:507-514`), which parses into `serde_json::Value` and serializes it again. `serde_json` is built without `preserve_order` (`Cargo.toml:26`; `cargo tree -e features -i serde_json` shows only `default`, `std`, `alloc`), so `Value` sorts object keys and **member order is never compared**. The tests are called byte-identical but check only sorted equality.
- Every strip is ad hoc. `without_meta` drops `meta`. `support::stable` zeroes `duration_ms`, `elapsed_ms` and `lock_held_ms` wherever they occur (`tests/contract/main.rs:318-333`, the list at `:324`). E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, `doctor diagnose` and the doctor envelope) adds a local `without_volatile` in `special.rs` for the doctor's five run keys. Nothing ties any of them to a declared list.
- The contract matrix (`tests/contract/matrix.rs`, 1,200 lines, 40 `#[test]` functions, 105 snapshots) is not a table of rows. Each test is a scenario whose rows build on the state the earlier rows left (`install`, then `update`, then `undo`), so no row can be re-run on its own.
- Nothing guarantees that every command path has rows. Reading the matrix at `c0ab5e9`, these `app::COMMANDS` paths lack a kind of row (13 rows in all): `backup` (bare) and `targets` (bare) have no failure row; `targets rm` has none of either; `targets rename` has no success row; `targets default` has none of either; `config` (bare) has none of either; `config get` and `config path` have no failure row; `omarchy` (bare) has no failure row; `omarchy status` has no success row (its only success is through bare `omarchy`).
- Nothing stops a `HashMap` field in a serialized type. None exists in the four directories today (`src/app`, `src/output`; `src/contract` and `src/doctor` are created by M4 leaves).

**Goals served.**

- **G-M4-5, frozen and enforced:** "At the first tag the contract is consistent, complete and enforced … Repeated runs print identical bytes." This bead is that last sentence, as a gate test over every command path.
- **G-M4-3, what was previewed is what runs:** "Two dry runs of an unchanged home give equal tokens for every source" (criterion 6). The repeat runs every engine dry run of the matrix on two separate copies of its home, so a token that depends on anything but the home's content and state fails here too.
- **Vision G4, agent ergonomics** ("the first command an agent guesses works"): an agent that runs a command twice can tell from the bytes whether anything changed, because only the documented keys may differ.

**Checkpoint criteria.**

- **14, the contract is frozen, its determinism part.** "JSON member order is deterministic but is not compared as contract (JSON objects are unordered); reordering keys needs no version bump. Repeated runs of every command path print identical bytes, after stripping only the keys the volatile registry declares." H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the checkpoint and the first tag) quotes this bead's tests as the evidence.
- It also supports criterion 6 ("two dry runs of an unchanged home give equal tokens for every source", for the engine commands' rows) and criterion 9 ("detectors are repeatable", for the doctor's rows).

**The decisions that shape it.**

- **M4-D18: determinism is enforced per command path, and volatile keys are declared.**
  - Every path in `app::COMMANDS` has at least one success row and one failure row in the contract matrix, and a coverage test fails a path that lacks one.
  - Every row runs twice, and stdout bytes are compared.
  - Keys whose values legitimately change between runs are declared in `contract::VOLATILE`, each with its reason. The plan names `meta.*`; the doctor's `run_id`, `run_dir`, `started_at`, `finished_at`; stored plans' `plan_id` and `plan_expires_at`; and the existing `duration_ms` and `lock_held_ms`. §6.8 adds `data.**.tx` and `data.**.run` on real runs, `checked_at`-style memo times, and the doctor's `summary.duration_ms`.
  - The repeat test strips only declared keys, and a stripped key that is not declared fails.
  - A source scan fails any `HashMap` or `HashSet` field in a type that derives `Serialize` under `src/app`, `src/output`, `src/contract` or `src/doctor`.
  - Why: the vision put every volatile value in `meta`, but `duration_ms` and `lock_held_ms` already sit in `data`, and the doctor contract puts run identity at the top level. Declaring them is honest; renaming them would be churn. `HashMap` order differs per process, so the repeat test catches one at run time, and the scan catches it before.
  - Rejected: moving every volatile value into `meta`. It breaks the doctor contract's shapes and the existing snapshots, for no consumer's benefit. Do not "fix" a volatile key by moving it.
- **M4-D5: per-command exit codes are declared beside the command and verified.** `CommandEntry.exits` declares each path's exits (A1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1`, per-command facts in `COMMANDS`), and the contract suite records every exit each path produced across the matrix and fails one that is not declared. Rejected: deriving exits from the error codes a command raises (not statically knowable), and declaring 0–6 everywhere (useless to an agent). This bead's part: the coverage test guarantees every path has a success and a failure row, so the cross-check sees every path at least twice, and the audit reports declared exits no row produced (a report, not a failure).
- **M4-D55, the contract's rules hold from slice 1; H1 is their final audit.** H3 may land after H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, the pre-freeze audit) closes, because it adds no wire shape. If the audit finds a fix that is not additive (a field to remove or retype), it is a defect against H1. It is filed, fixed before H2 regenerates the golden for the last time, and recorded on H1's change list, never done quietly here.
- **M4-D56, member order is not contract.** Rendering stays deterministic (declaration order, byte-identical repeats) so diffs are readable. JSON objects are unordered (RFC 8259), so the semantic manifest ignores member order and reordering keys needs no version bump. The repeat therefore compares order, while the golden does not.
- **M3-D46, preview tokens** (context). A precondition token is `pc1:` plus four 64-bit digests of `command`, `targets`, `selection` and `observed`. Some M3 tokens put file stamps in `observed`: `errors dismiss` and the `errors` read's `dismiss.precondition` use `FileStamp::fingerprint()` of each SavedVariables database. `backup restore --addon` uses it for each live SavedVariables file. That fingerprint includes the device, the inode and the change time (`src/fsx/stamp.rs:73-89`). A whole `backup restore` uses `StampDigest` (path, kind, size, mode, mtime: `src/fsx/mutate.rs:196-215`), which an exact copy keeps.
- **M4-D19 and M4-D60, the engine commands' tokens** (context, D1). `observed` holds the approval witness's canonical digest: each witnessed folder's entry digest (each file's path, size and SHA-256, each symlink's target, each directory), absent names, local inputs, dependency choices, the judge digest, the client marker's digest and `build_id`. The witness's stamps are private and excluded. These tokens therefore survive an exact copy of the home, and the repeat checks that they do.

**Facts this bead relies on** (as of `c0ab5e9`; each file:line verified, and later leaves will have moved some lines):

- `app::COMMANDS` (`src/app/mod.rs:121-165`) lists 42 paths. After A1 it holds one row per runnable path, every clap leaf plus every parent whose bare form runs (`backup`, `config`, `errors`, `omarchy`, `targets`), each with `dictionary`, `exits`, `data`, `stores_plan` and `network`. `auth` becomes `auth github`.
- Bare `backup` answers with envelope `command` `backup list`, and bare `omarchy` with `omarchy status` (`src/app/mod.rs:208-211`, `:232-235`). So envelope names alone can never show the `backup` and `omarchy` rows covered.
- `cli::command_path(argv)` (`src/cli.rs:1010-1037`, public) returns the clap subcommand path an argv names (argv including the binary name, flags and their values skipped, aliases resolved to canonical names by `find_subcommand`).
- `support::check(run, code)` (`tests/contract/main.rs:113-225`) asserts the whole contract on one run. A1 adds the per-process exit observation there, A3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`, schemas and live validation) live schema validation, E3 a doctor mode, and H2 an observed-keys check, each in its own block.
- `support::Scene` (`tests/contract/main.rs:366-505`) wraps a `common::home::Home`. `json`, `json_env` and `json_input` push `--json` and call `check`. `Scene::new()` is used 40 times in `matrix.rs`, 17 in `special.rs`, 11 in `recommendations.rs` and 3 in `usage_fixes.rs`.
- A home lives entirely in one `tempfile` directory (`tests/common/env.rs:23-54`): `home/`, `config/`, `state/`, `cache/`, `no-proc/`, the Wine prefix with its clients, the replayed HTTP fixtures (`OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES`, a directory under the root, `tests/common/home.rs:254-266`), the fake `/proc` and the doorbell (`<cache>/doorbell.json`, `src/state/paths.rs:441-443`). State files hold absolute paths (the registry's client directories), so a copy is valid only at the path it was built at. C4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4`, the run-the-fix corpus) and F9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`, the doctor's safety harness) found the same and restore homes in place.
- `tests/common/home.rs:270-281` (`copy_dir`) follows symlinks and keeps neither modes nor mtimes, so it cannot copy a home. C4 adds `trees::copy_tree_exact(from, to)` (bytes, permission bits children-first, symlink targets never followed, file and directory mtimes). `wtf::writable_again(dir)` (`tests/common/wtf.rs:136-150`) makes a tree deletable again.
- A copy of a file is a new inode with a new birth time and a new change time. Whatever binds to identity (the fingerprint above, a journal's recorded `FileId`s, a files index's `TreeStamp`, which includes the change time, `src/fsx/stamp.rs:108-146`) sees a copy as changed.
- `src/source_scan.rs` (the production view of the crate's source: comments and test-only items blanked) is declared `#[cfg(test)] mod source_scan;` (`src/lib.rs:37-38`). It is crate-private and compiled only into the library's own unit tests, so an integration test cannot `use` it (its module doc says so, `src/source_scan.rs:1-10`). Its `pub(crate)` items are `Literals`, `production_code(text, Literals) -> Option<String>` and `sources(dir)` (`:16`, `:26`, `:63`), and it depends only on `std`.
- Many places read the wall clock directly (`Timestamp::now()`: `src/engine/tx.rs:930`, `src/discover/registry.rs:353`, `src/resolve/cache.rs:274`, `src/app/adopt/apply.rs:870`, `src/app/sync.rs:903`, among others). `OMADDONS_NOW` freezes only `clock::now()` (`src/clock.rs:9-11`). So times are declared, not frozen, and the repeat does not set `OMADDONS_NOW` for a row that does not.
- The JSON contract in README: `### Fields` (`README.md:1790-1806`) and `### Stability` (`README.md:1959-1961`, ending "…that repeated runs print identical bytes…"). The Development section's Tests table is at `README.md:2619-2640`. No test reads README today.
- `contract::OPAQUE` (A3) is the precedent for a registry of declared exceptions: `Opaque { scope, path, source, reason }`, paths in A9's syntax (`a.b`, `a[]`, `a{}`), every row proven to match a schema position by walking the published schemas with `contract::schema::walk`. A3's `CONTRACT_DETAILS_OBSERVED` report is the precedent for a contract test that re-runs the suite as a child of `std::env::current_exe()`, because libtest has no "after all tests" hook.

## Technical Approach

Leaves named in this section: A1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1`, per-command facts in `COMMANDS`), A3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`, schemas, the walk and `OPAQUE`), C4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4`, the run-the-fix corpus, which adds `copy_tree_exact`), D4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`, the plan store), D5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`, `omaddons apply`), E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, `doctor diagnose` and the doctor envelope), E4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4`, the doctor's read surface), H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, the pre-freeze audit), H2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.2`, the golden), H4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`, the README final pass), T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs).

```rust
/// Why a key's value differs between two runs that start from the same home.
pub enum VolatileKind {
    /// A duration the run measured (`duration_ms`, `lock_held_ms`).
    Timing,
    /// An instant the run read from the wall clock (`checked_at`, `started_at`).
    Clock,
    /// An identifier the run drew, or a value derived from one (`tx`, `plan_id`, an archive that embeds a new id).
    NewId,
    /// A value derived from file identity (inode, birth time, change time), which no copy of a home keeps.
    Identity,
}
impl VolatileKind { pub const fn word(self) -> &'static str /* "timing", "wall clock", "new id", "file identity" */ }

pub struct Volatile {
    /// `*` for every command, or one `app::COMMANDS` path.
    pub command: &'static str,
    /// A path from the envelope's root, in A9's syntax (`a.b`, `a[]` each item of array `a`, `a{}` any key of map `a`),
    /// plus two segments: `*` (any one key) and `**` (any run of keys and items, none included).
    pub path: &'static str,
    pub kind: VolatileKind,
    /// One sentence, ending with a period.
    pub reason: &'static str,
}
pub const VOLATILE: &[Volatile] = &[ /* sorted by (command, path); `*` sorts first */ ];

/// One step of a concrete path into an envelope.
pub enum Step<'a> { Key(&'a str), Index }
/// Whether `pattern` matches `path`.
pub fn matches(pattern: &str, path: &[Step<'_>]) -> bool;
/// The row of `table` that declares the value at `path` of an envelope of `command` volatile, if any
/// (`declared` uses `VOLATILE`; the table parameter is for tests that drop rows).
pub fn declared_in(table: &'static [Volatile], command: &str, path: &[Step<'_>]) -> Option<&'static Volatile>;
pub fn declared(command: &str, path: &[Step<'_>]) -> Option<&'static Volatile>;
```

**The path grammar and matching.** A pattern is split into segments on `.`; a segment `name[]` is the key `name` followed by one array item, `name{}` the key `name` followed by any key, `*` any one key, `**` any run of steps including none. ### 2. Every matrix row, repeated on fresh copies (subtask 2)

**Why three runs per row** (decided while writing this bead). The plan says each row runs twice "from a fresh copy of its home (so real runs repeat too, not just reads)". Two facts shape how:

- A copy is valid only at the home's own path, because state holds absolute paths. So copies are made at the same path, one at a time, with the original moved aside.
- A copy loses file identity, so it is a faithful starting state for content and state, but not for anything bound to inodes or change times. A run on a copy and a run on the original can then legitimately differ: an identity-bound `--if-match` token taken on the original (`errors dismiss`'s) fingerprints its inodes and is stale on any copy; a journal's recorded identities do not match a copy, so recovery classifies it differently.

So every row runs **three** times:

1. **A** on a fresh copy of the home the row started from;
2. **B** on another fresh copy of the same home;
3. **C** on the original. C is the row's own run: its output is what the test asserts and snapshots, and the scenario continues from its result exactly as today.

A and B are compared. They start from identical content and state, and both lack the original's identities in the same way, so any difference between them is either a value the run itself draws, reads from the clock, or derives from file identity (declared), or nondeterminism (a bug). C is never compared with A or B. Rejected:

- (i) A on the original and B on a copy: every identity-bound row would fail for a reason that is not nondeterminism.
- (ii) The two runs in place, one after the other: a real run cannot repeat on the home it changed, and a read would see the caches the first run warmed.
- (iii) Copies at another path: they would act on the original's clients.

**The procedure for one row** (`Scene::row`, in `tests/contract/main.rs`):

1. `log.step("row <n>: omaddons <argv>")`.
2. A slot: `tempfile::Builder::new().prefix(".omaddons-repeat-").tempdir_in(<root's parent>)`, on the same filesystem as the root, so renames work.
3. `std::fs::rename(<root>, <slot>/original)`. A rename keeps every inode, so the original stays exactly itself.
4. For A, then B: `copy_tree_exact(<slot>/original, <root>)`; run the row's argv, environment and standard input through `log.cmd(&self.home, &argv)` (`.env(k, v)` for each extra variable, `.stdin(bytes)` for `json_input`), keep the exit and stdout; `writable_again(<root>)`; `remove_dir_all(<root>)`.
5. `std::fs::rename(<slot>/original, <root>)`.
6. Compare A and B (below). On a difference, panic before C runs, with the home back in place.
7. Run C through the log and return `check(c.run, code)`, as `json` does today.

`Scene::on_copies(&self, args, env) -> (Ran, Ran)` exposes steps 2–5 alone (A and B, the original restored, nothing compared, no C) for subtask 5's self-tests. Repeats are on for `Scene::matrix` and off when `CONTRACT_REPEAT=off` (the coverage audit's child sets it). `Scene::new()` (used by `special.rs`, `recommendations.rs` and `usage_fixes.rs`) never repeats: those tests hold locks, spawn background holders and arm pauses, which a moved home would break.

**`copy_tree_exact`**: use C4's `trees::copy_tree_exact` when it exists. Otherwise add it to `tests/common/trees.rs` with C4's semantics: `to` must not exist; entries read with `symlink_metadata`, never following a link; symlinks recreated with their target; regular files by content; permission bits set on each entry, a directory's after its children; file and directory mtimes set with `File::set_modified`, a directory's last; panic on a FIFO, socket or device. Add its self-test `copy_tree_exact_keeps_kinds_modes_links_and_mtimes` to `tests/common_selftest.rs` (C4's case list). Whichever of C4 and this bead lands second reuses the first's.

**The comparison** (`tests/contract/repeat.rs`, a new module of the contract crate):

- **An order-preserving tree.** `enum Json { Null, Bool(bool), Number(serde_json::Number), String(String), Array(Vec<Json>), Object(Vec<(String, Json)>) }`, with a `Deserialize` whose map visitor keeps members in document order (duplicates kept as they come) and a `Serialize` that writes them in that order. Never `serde_json::Value`: its map order depends on whether any crate in the test build enables `serde_json/preserve_order`.
- **Round trip.** `to_compact(&parse(stdout)) == stdout` without its trailing newline is asserted for every run compared, so the comparison sees exactly the bytes the binary printed (serde_json prints integers with `itoa` and floats with `ryu`, and `Number` round-trips both). A stdout that is not one JSON document fails with its text.
- **Masking** (`strip_with(stdout, table) -> Stripped`; `strip(stdout)` is `strip_with(stdout, VOLATILE)`): read `command` at the root, walk the tree, and for each value whose path a row declares for that command, replace it with a type-tagged placeholder: `"<volatile string>"`, `"<volatile number>"`, `"<volatile bool>"`, `"<volatile object>"` or `"<volatile array>"`. `null` is kept. The key stays where it was, so presence and member order are still compared, and a key that is `null` in one run and set in the other still fails.
- **Propagation** (decided while writing this bead): every masked string value of at least `PROPAGATE_MIN_LEN = 16` characters (ULIDs, run ids, RFC 3339 times, tokens) is then replaced by `<volatile>` wherever it appears inside any other string and any object key of the same envelope. Integers and short strings never propagate. This covers the run's own ids inside suggestions (`commands[].argv` `["omaddons","undo","<tx>"]`, `commands[].command`), doctor paths that embed the run id (`actions_jsonl_path`, `backups_dir`, `undo_command`, `undo_argv`), messages, and maps keyed by a new id, without a row for each and without masking a deterministic id that merely looks like one.
- **Differences.** `first_differences(a, b, limit)` walks the two masked trees in step: members by position (a different key at one position is reported as an order difference), items by index, scalars by value. It returns the first 10 as `{path, a, b}` with values cut at 80 characters.
- **Exits.** A's and B's exits must be equal too, which equal stdout already implies for `exit_code`; it is asserted first for a clearer message.

### 3. The coverage audit and the missing rows (subtask 3)

**Recording.** `support::check`, in its own block after its assertions, appends one JSON line per checked run when `CONTRACT_MATRIX_ROWS` names a file (through a process-wide `Mutex<File>` opened in append mode):

```json
{"test":"matrix::targets","argv":["targets","rm","pserver","--json"],"path":"targets rm","command":"targets rm",
 "exit":0,"kind":"success","error_code":null}
```

- `test` is the current thread's name (libtest names each test's thread after the test), else `"unknown"`.
- `path` is `cli::command_path(["omaddons", argv…]).join(" ")`. When that is empty (bare `omaddons`, `--bogus`), it is the envelope's `command`.
- `kind` is `success` for exit 0 with `ok: true`; `failure` for an envelope with a non-null `error` object (any exit, `check_failed` included); otherwise `other` (a doctor run that ends with findings, exit 1, without an error).

**The audit** (`tests/contract/coverage.rs`, a new module):

- `fn audit() -> &'static Audit` (a `OnceLock`, so the tests in the module share one run): run `std::env::current_exe()` with the filter `matrix::`, `CONTRACT_MATRIX_ROWS=<fresh tempdir>/rows.jsonl` and `CONTRACT_REPEAT=off`, capture its output, and parse the rows. If the child fails, the audit is `Failed { status, tail }` (the last 60 lines of its output), and every test of the module fails with "the matrix failed in the coverage child; fix the matrix first", printing the tail, without computing coverage from a partial run.
- `fn audit_with(filter: &str) -> Audit`: the same child run over the tests another filter selects, for the self-tests.
- `fn coverage(rows: &[Row], commands: &[&str]) -> Missing { success: Vec<String>, failure: Vec<String> }`: pure. A path not in `commands` (`omaddons`, `version`) is ignored. `path_of(argv, envelope_command)` and `kind_of(exit, envelope)` are the two pure functions the recording uses.
- `every_commands_path_has_a_success_and_a_failure_row`: `coverage(audit rows, COMMANDS names)` is empty. The failure lists each path and the kind it lacks, with "add a row to its test in tests/contract/matrix.rs: `s.json(&[…], <exit>)` and an insta snapshot of `s.stable(&c.envelope)`". An empty row set fails with "no rows: the filter matched no matrix test" instead, so an empty run never reads as a list of gaps or as covered. The messages come from a pure `verdict(audit, commands) -> Result<(), String>`, which the self-tests call too.
- `the_matrix_follows_its_conventions` (static, over the text of `tests/contract/matrix.rs`): no `Scene::new(`; every `#[test]` function body contains `Scene::matrix(matrix_log!())`; no `.spawn(` (a background process would hold files in the home the repeat moves). The failure names the test function.
- The audit also logs, without asserting, `declared exits no matrix row produced` (each path's `entry.exits` minus the exits its rows produced) and `rows per path`, for M4-D5's evidence and H4's counts.

### 4. The `HashMap` scan (subtask 4)

`tests/determinism.rs`, a new test crate with the crate doc `//! The determinism scan (M4-D18): no HashMap or HashSet in a type that derives Serialize in the output directories.`:

```rust
// The crate's own production-source view, the same file the unit-test scans use: one lexer, not a copy.
#[allow(dead_code)]
#[path = "../src/source_scan.rs"]
mod source_scan;

const SCANNED: &[&str] = &["src/app", "src/output", "src/contract", "src/doctor"];

/// One finding: the line (1-based), the item's name and the line's text.
struct Hit { line: usize, item: String, text: String }

/// Each `HashMap<` or `HashSet<` inside the header or body of a `struct` or `enum` whose derive list contains
/// `Serialize`, in code already passed through `production_code(…, Literals::Blank)`.
fn serialized_hash_fields(code: &str) -> Vec<Hit>;
```

Decided while writing this bead: `#[path]` inclusion, because `source_scan` is `#[cfg(test)]` and crate-private (`src/lib.rs:37-38`). An integration test is compiled with `cfg(test)` itself, so the file compiles there, and it depends only on `std`. Its own unit tests then also run in this crate, which is harmless. Rejected: a copy of the lexer (two lexers drift apart), and moving the scan into a unit test of the library (the plan names `tests/determinism.rs`).

The function works on `production_code(text, Literals::Blank)`, so comments, string contents and test-only items are already blanks:

1. Find each `#[derive(` … `)]` (bracket depth counted; brackets inside literals are already gone) whose comma-separated entries include `Serialize` or a path ending `::Serialize`.
2. Skip whitespace and any further attributes `#[…]`, then an optional visibility (`pub`, `pub(crate)`, `pub(super)`, `pub(in …)`), then require `struct` or `enum` and its name. Anything else (a derive on a `union`, a malformed item) is skipped.
3. The item's extent: from the name to the end of its body. That is the matching `}` of the first `{`, or the matching `)` and the `;` for a tuple struct, or the `;` of a unit struct, generics and `where` clauses included (so a default type parameter counts).
4. Report every `HashMap` or `HashSet` token followed by optional whitespace and `<` within that extent, as a word (`std::collections::HashMap<` counts; `MyHashMap<` does not).

`no_serialized_type_holds_a_hash_map_or_set` scans every `.rs` file under the four directories (via `source_scan::sources`, skipping a file whose `production_code` is `None`) and fails listing `file:line item: text` with "use BTreeMap or BTreeSet (DEC-3, M4-D18): a hash map's order differs per process". `the_scanned_directories_exist` asserts all four directories exist: they do once A1 and E3 have landed, and a rename must not silently empty the scan.

## Considerations

- **Gate time.** Each matrix row now runs three times, plus two copies of the home, and the coverage audit runs the matrix once more as a child (without repeats). Expect the contract suite to take roughly three to four times its current wall time, with homes of a few hundred small files each. Measure it before and after (median of 3) and record both in the close comment. If the whole `argc gate` grows by more than 60 seconds, file a follow-up with `--deps discovered-from:omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3` to make it cheaper (parallel A and B, a smaller copy). Never weaken the repeat to save time.
- **Flakiness from time.** Only declared keys may differ, and they are masked, so a second or minute boundary between A and B cannot fail a row. A value derived from a time that is not itself declared (a "3 minutes ago" inside a JSON message) is a real finding: declare the message's key, or better, keep relative times out of JSON.
- **Rows the copies cannot reproduce.** A row bound to the original's identities (an `--if-match` of an identity-bound token, a recovery of a journal whose identities a copy loses) behaves differently on the copies than on the original. A and B are then compared with each other on the path the copies take, and C still runs the real path. That is by design (three runs, not two); do not special-case such rows.
- **What the scan does not see.** Serialized types defined outside the four directories (`src/model.rs`, `src/backup/`, `src/state/`, `src/engine/inspect.rs`'s report types) are outside M4-D18's scan, which names the four. comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M4 plan, 2026-10-24).**

**Why this bead.** omaddons says that one command on one unchanged home prints the same bytes, apart from a few keys that legitimately change. Today that is checked for about a dozen read commands, in place, through a comparison that sorts object keys, and with ad hoc strips that no list governs. No real run, no doctor command and no plan command is ever repeated, and 13 rows of the matrix are missing outright. The freeze (H2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.2`, the golden and the released baseline; H6, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the checkpoint and the first tag) pins a contract whose meaning depends on output being a function of the home: a golden or a snapshot of nondeterministic output pins nothing, and an agent cannot diff two runs it cannot trust. This bead turns the promise into a gate test over every command path: a declared registry of volatile keys, every matrix row repeated on two fresh copies of its home and compared byte for byte, a coverage test that makes "every row" mean every path, and a scan that keeps hash-ordered collections out of serialized types.

**Decisions applied.**

- **M4-D18:** every `COMMANDS` path has a success and a failure row (a coverage test), every row runs twice and compares stdout bytes, volatile keys are declared in `contract::VOLATILE` with reasons and only those are stripped, and a source scan refuses `HashMap`/`HashSet` fields in serialized types under `src/app`, `src/output`, `src/contract` and `src/doctor`. Rejected: moving every volatile value into `meta`.
- **M4-D5:** exits are declared per path and checked against what the matrix produces. The coverage test guarantees every path is seen on success and failure; the audit reports declared exits no row produced.
- **M4-D55 (after H1):** this bead adds no wire shape. A non-additive fix it needs is a defect against H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, the pre-freeze audit), filed and recorded there.
- **M4-D56:** member order is deterministic but not contract. The repeat compares order; the manifest ignores it.
- **M3-D46 and M4-D19/D60 (context):** some M3 tokens fingerprint inodes and change times, while engine tokens hold content digests only. That decides which tokens are declared volatile (file identity) and which the repeat proves equal across copies.

**Decided while writing the bead** (each restated in the bead where it applies):

- **Three runs per row.** A and B on two fresh copies of the row's starting home, compared; C, the row's own run, on the original, which the scenario continues from. A copy is valid only at the home's path (state holds absolute paths) and loses file identity, so comparing a copy with the original would fail every identity-bound row for a reason that is not nondeterminism. Rejected: original against copy; two runs in place; copies at another path.
- **An order-preserving comparison**, with the round trip to the binary's bytes asserted, because `serde_json::Value` sorts keys.
- **Masking:** type-tagged placeholders, `null` kept, presence and order compared. Masked strings of 16 characters or more are also masked where they reappear (the new `tx` inside an `undo` suggestion).
- **The registry's row type** gains a command scope and a kind (timing, wall clock, new id, file identity), because `data.sha256` is volatile for `backup export` only and README explains each key by its kind. The rows D4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`, the plan store), E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, `doctor diagnose` and the doctor envelope) and the F leaves added are migrated.
- **Every row must name a schema position** (the walk of A3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`, schemas and live validation), instead of being observed in the matrix: it catches typos and stale rows without requiring a matrix row for each rare evidence key.
- **README's "Volatile keys" table is held equal to the registry by a test.**
- **The repeat is scoped to the matrix** (`Scene::matrix(matrix_log!())`, enforced by a conventions test), whose scenarios adopt the log of T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs) so a failing repeat is diagnosable.
- **Coverage is computed from a child run** of the contract binary (libtest has no after-all hook, as A1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1`, and A3 found), keyed by the invoked clap path, because bare `backup` and `omarchy` answer under other names.
- **The scan includes `src/source_scan.rs` by `#[path]`**, because that module is `cfg(test)` and crate-private.

**Alternatives rejected that matter here.**

- Freezing the clock and seeding id generation in debug builds so that nothing is volatile: it changes product code (many sites read the clock directly), hides real per-run values from the test, and the plan chose declaration.
- Comparing only sorted JSON: it cannot see an order that changes per process, the most common symptom of a hash map.
- Requiring every volatile row to be observed in the matrix: it would force a matrix row for every doctor evidence key; the schema check is stronger against typos and cheaper.

**Risks and how they are watched.** No plan risk is owned here. The bead's own risks:

- Gate time grows (three runs per row plus a child run of the matrix): measured before and after, with a follow-up filed past 60 seconds.
- The audit finds nondeterminism whose fix is not additive: routed to H1's change list.
- A copy cannot reproduce an identity-bound row: by design, A and B take the copy's path together, and C keeps the real one.
- Two processes writing one test log: the coverage child logs under its own suite.

Risk 19 of the plan (a token that stales for no reason) gains evidence here: every engine dry run of the matrix runs on two copies, and its token must be equal.

**What it unblocks, and why it waits.** H4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`, the README final pass) waits for this bead because it reconciles README's JSON contract (Appendix D's "the volatile keys") and every test count against `main`, and both need this bead's table, its "Stability" sentence and its new suite. H3 itself waits for A1 (the per-path `COMMANDS` rows it covers), D5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`, `omaddons apply`: `apply` and its rows, with the plan store and the engine tokens behind it) and E4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4`, the doctor's read surface, with E3's envelope, doctor mode and volatile rows, and A3's schemas behind it). It starts once the command surface it audits is nearly complete; later command leaves are held to it by the gate.

**How it serves the milestone.** It is G-M4-5's "repeated runs print identical bytes", made true for every command path and enforced from here on. It supports G-M4-3's "two dry runs of an unchanged home give equal tokens", now across copies. And it supports vision G4: an agent can trust that two outputs differ only where README says they may. Checkpoint criterion 14's determinism part is this bead's evidence for H6.

**Confidence.** High for the machinery: each part follows a precedent in the repository: A3's `OPAQUE` registry and child run; the same-path restore that C4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4`, the run-the-fix corpus) and F9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`, the doctor's safety harness) use; and the existing `source_scan` lexer. Medium for the size of the audit pass, whose findings cannot be known before the repeat first runs over every row.
