title: Every matrix row repeated on two fresh copies of its home and compared byte for byte, with the audit pass that declares or fixes each difference
description:
Part 2 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3 (The determinism audit). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

H3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3`, the determinism audit) makes "one command on one unchanged home prints the same bytes, except the declared volatile keys" a gate test over every command path. It serves G-M4-5 ("repeated runs print identical bytes") and checkpoint criterion 14's determinism part: "JSON member order is deterministic but is not compared as contract … Repeated runs of every command path print identical bytes, after stripping only the keys the volatile registry declares." It also lets G-M4-3's "two dry runs of an unchanged home give equal tokens for every source" be checked across copies for every engine dry run in the matrix.

**This part** is the repeat itself, and the audit pass it enables: every row of the contract matrix runs twice more, each on a fresh copy of the home it started from, and the two outputs must be byte-identical once the keys `contract::VOLATILE` declares are masked. It also removes every other way the contract suite masks keys. It is its own step because it rewrites the matrix's runner, which every matrix test goes through, and because the audit's findings (rows to declare, bugs to fix) must land in the same commit as the repeat that finds them, or the gate fails.

**M4-D18, restated.** Every row runs twice and stdout bytes are compared. Keys whose values legitimately change are declared in `contract::VOLATILE` with their reasons, the repeat strips only declared keys, and a stripped key that is not declared fails. Rejected: moving volatile values into `meta`. **M4-D56, restated:** rendering stays deterministic so diffs are readable, but member order is not contract, so this repeat compares order while the manifest ignores it. **M4-D55's after-H1 rule:** this bead may land after H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, the pre-freeze audit) closes and adds no wire shape; a fix that would not be additive is a defect against H1, filed, never made here.

**What `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3.1` left:** `contract::VOLATILE` as `Volatile { command, path, kind, reason }` rows (`command` is `*` or a `COMMANDS` path; `path` is rooted at the envelope, A9's syntax plus `*` and `**`; `kind` is `Timing`, `Clock`, `NewId` or `Identity`), `Step`, `matches`, `declared_in(table, command, path)` and `declared(command, path)`, and README's `### Volatile keys` table held equal to the registry by `readme_lists_every_volatile_row`.

**Facts this part relies on** (as of `c0ab5e9`):

- The matrix (`tests/contract/matrix.rs`, 40 `#[test]` functions) is a set of scenarios whose rows build on each other's state; `Scene::new()` appears 40 times there. Rows go through `support::Scene::{json, json_env, json_input}` (`tests/contract/main.rs:425-492`), which push `--json` and call `support::check(run, code)` (`:113-225`).
- A home is one tempdir (`tests/common/env.rs:23-54`). It holds the clients, `config/`, `state/`, `cache/`, the replayed HTTP fixtures (`OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES`, a directory under the root, `tests/common/home.rs:254-266`), the fake `/proc` and the zips the rows install. State holds absolute paths, so a copy is valid only at the same path. C4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4`, the run-the-fix corpus) and F9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`, the doctor's safety harness) restore their homes in place for the same reason.
- A copied file is a new inode with a new birth and change time. M3 tokens that fingerprint files (`FileStamp::fingerprint()`: device, inode, size, mtime, change time, `src/fsx/stamp.rs:73-89`) differ on a copy: `errors`' `dismiss.precondition` (`src/app/errors_status.rs:215-218`) and `errors dismiss`' `precondition` (`src/app/precondition.rs:419-440`). A whole `backup restore` token uses `StampDigest` (path, kind, size, mode, mtime: `src/fsx/mutate.rs:196-215`), which an exact copy keeps. Engine tokens (D1, M4-D19 and M4-D60) hold content digests, the client marker's digest, generations and `build_id`, with the witness's stamps excluded, so they survive an exact copy.
- `support::without_meta` (`tests/contract/main.rs:507-514`) compares through `serde_json::Value`, which sorts keys (`serde_json` has no `preserve_order` at `c0ab5e9`). Its callers: `special.rs:377-378` (`read_only_commands_ignore_dry_run_and_reason`, where E3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, added a local `without_volatile` for the doctor's five keys), `:418` (`every_json_spelling_prints_the_same_envelope`), `:469-470` (`repeated_runs_are_byte_identical`), `:527-528` (`m2_outputs_are_byte_identical`) and `matrix.rs:128` (`sync --dry-run` twice).
- `support::stable` zeroes `duration_ms`, `elapsed_ms` and `lock_held_ms` wherever they occur (`tests/contract/main.rs:318-333`, the list at `:324`).
- `tests/common/home.rs:270-281`'s `copy_dir` follows symlinks and keeps neither modes nor mtimes. C4 adds `trees::copy_tree_exact`; `wtf::writable_again` exists (`tests/common/wtf.rs:136-150`).
- T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs) provides `TestLog` (`tests/common/tlog.rs`): `TestLog::new(suite, test)`, `tlog!()` (which names a test by its function path inside the crate), `step`, `note`, `json`, `cmd(&runner, &argv)` returning a `Cmd` with `.env(k, v)`, `.stdin(bytes)` and `.run() -> Ran` (`Ran.run` is a `common::home::Run`), with `Home` as a `Runner` through `Home::std_command`.
- Many places read the wall clock directly (`Timestamp::now()`, e.g. `src/engine/tx.rs:930`, `src/discover/registry.rs:353`), so `OMADDONS_NOW` cannot freeze every printed time: times are declared, not frozen.

## Technical Approach

### 1. Three runs per row

Decided while writing this bead, because a copy is valid only at the home's path and loses file identity:

1. **A** runs on a fresh copy of the home the row started from;
2. **B** runs on another fresh copy of the same home;
3. **C** runs on the original. C is the row's own run, whose output the test asserts and snapshots, and the scenario continues from its result exactly as today.

A and B are compared. Both start from identical content and state, and both lack the original's identities in the same way, so a difference between them is a value the run draws, reads from the clock or derives from file identity (declared), or nondeterminism (a bug). C is never compared with them: a row bound to the original's identities (an `--if-match` of an identity-bound token, recovery of a journal whose recorded identities a copy loses) takes a different path on a copy, and that is expected. Rejected:

- (i) A on the original and B on a copy: every identity-bound row would fail for a reason that is not nondeterminism.
- (ii) Two runs in place: a real run cannot repeat on the home it changed, and a read would see what the first run cached.
- (iii) Copies at another path: they would act on the original's clients.

### 2. `Scene::matrix` and the row procedure

In `tests/contract/main.rs` (`support`):

```rust
pub struct Scene { pub home: Home, log: Option<TestLog>, repeat: bool, rows: Cell<usize> }

impl Scene {
    /// A matrix scene: every row runs on two fresh copies of its home, compared, then on the home itself.
    pub fn matrix(log: TestLog) -> Self;        // repeat = CONTRACT_REPEAT != "off"
    pub fn new() -> Self;                       // unchanged: no log, no repeat
    pub fn json(&self, args: &[&str], code: i32) -> Checked;                        // → self.row(…)
    pub fn json_env(&self, args: &[&str], env: &[(&str, &str)], code: i32) -> Checked;
    pub fn json_input(&self, args: &[&str], input: &[u8], code: i32) -> Checked;
}

/// `matrix_log!()`: a log for the calling test, under the suite `contract.matrix`, or `contract.matrix_audit`
/// when `CONTRACT_MATRIX_ROWS` is set (the coverage audit's child), so the two processes never share a log directory.
macro_rules! matrix_log { () => {{ fn here() {} crate::common::tlog::TestLog::new(
    crate::support::matrix_suite(), &crate::support::test_name(std::any::type_name_of_val(&here))) }} }
```

`matrix_suite()` returns `"contract.matrix"` or `"contract.matrix_audit"`. `test_name(type_name)` names the test as T1's `tlog!()` does: the function path inside the crate (`contract::matrix::install::here` → `matrix.install`), the trailing `here` and the crate name dropped, `::` joined as `.`. It goes through `TestLog::new(suite, test)` rather than T1's `from_location`, so the suite can differ from the module path without depending on how `from_location` derives names. Every matrix test's first line becomes `let s = Scene::matrix(matrix_log!());` (`let mut s` where it was `mut`); nothing else in the scenarios changes. `Scene::new()` keeps its meaning for `special.rs`, `recommendations.rs` and `usage_fixes.rs`: those tests hold locks, spawn background holders and arm pauses, which moving a home would break, so they never repeat.

`json`, `json_env` and `json_input` build the argv (with `--json`), the extra variables and the optional standard input, and call one private `row(argv, env, stdin, code)`:

1. Count the row (`n`) and `log.step(format!("row {n}: omaddons {}", shell_words::join(&argv)))`.
2. If `repeat`:
   1. Create a slot: `tempfile::Builder::new().prefix(".omaddons-repeat-").tempdir_in(root.parent())`, on the root's filesystem, so renames work.
   2. `std::fs::rename(root, slot/original)`. A rename keeps every inode: the original is untouched while it is aside.
   3. For `"A (copy 1)"` and then `"B (copy 2)"`: `trees::copy_tree_exact(slot/original, root)`; run through `log.cmd(&self.home, &argv)` with each `.env(k, v)` and the `.stdin(bytes)`; keep the exit and stdout; `wtf::writable_again(root)`; `std::fs::remove_dir_all(root)`.
   4. `std::fs::rename(slot/original, root)`.
   5. Compare A and B (section 4). On a difference, record it and panic now, with the home back in place.
3. Run C through the log (or through `self.home` directly when the scene has no log) and return `check(c.run, code)`.

`pub fn on_copies(&self, args: &[&str], env: &[(&str, &str)]) -> (Ran, Ran)` exposes steps 2.1–2.4 alone (A and B, the original restored, no comparison, no C), for `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3.5`'s self-tests.

`copy_tree_exact`: use C4's `trees::copy_tree_exact` if it exists. Otherwise add it to `tests/common/trees.rs` with C4's semantics (`to` must not exist; `symlink_metadata`, never following a link; a symlink recreated with its target; files by content; permission bits on each entry, a directory's after its children; file and directory mtimes set with `File::set_modified`, a directory's last; panic on a FIFO, socket or device), and its self-test `copy_tree_exact_keeps_kinds_modes_links_and_mtimes` in `tests/common_selftest.rs` (a 0640 file, a 0755 file, a 0500 directory holding a 0400 file, an empty directory, a relative symlink, a symlink to `/`, a dangling symlink, fixed mtimes; `tree_hash` equal, each mtime equal, each link a link with its target, the copy of the link to `/` childless). Whichever of C4 and this part lands second reuses the first's.

### 3. The order-preserving tree

`tests/contract/repeat.rs`, a new module (`mod repeat;` in `tests/contract/main.rs`):

```rust
/// JSON with object members in document order.
pub enum Json { Null, Bool(bool), Number(serde_json::Number), String(String), Array(Vec<Json>), Object(Vec<(String, Json)>) }
impl<'de> Deserialize<'de> for Json { /* deserialize_any; visit_map keeps members in order, duplicates as they come */ }
impl Serialize for Json { /* serialize_map in member order */ }
pub fn parse(text: &str) -> Result<Json, String>;
pub fn to_compact(json: &Json) -> String;   // serde_json::to_string
```

Never `serde_json::Value`: its map order depends on whether any crate in the test build enables `serde_json/preserve_order`. For every run it compares, `row` asserts `to_compact(&parse(stdout)?) == stdout.trim_end_matches('\n')`, so the comparison sees exactly the binary's bytes (serde_json prints integers with `itoa` and floats with `ryu`, which `Number` round-trips). A stdout that is not one JSON document fails with its text.

### 4. Masking and the comparison

```rust
pub const PROPAGATE_MIN_LEN: usize = 16;
pub struct Stripped { pub tree: Json, pub text: String, pub masked: Vec<(String, &'static Volatile)> }
/// Masks, in an envelope printed by `command` (read from its root), every value `table` declares volatile for it.
pub fn strip_with(stdout: &str, table: &'static [Volatile]) -> Result<Stripped, String>;
pub fn strip(stdout: &str) -> Result<Stripped, String> { strip_with(stdout, VOLATILE) }
pub struct Difference { pub path: String, pub a: String, pub b: String }
pub fn first_differences(a: &Json, b: &Json, limit: usize) -> Vec<Difference>;
```

- **Masking.** Walk the tree with the concrete path (`Step::Key`, `Step::Index`). Where `declared_in(table, command, path)` is `Some`, replace a non-null value with `"<volatile string>"`, `"<volatile number>"`, `"<volatile bool>"`, `"<volatile object>"` or `"<volatile array>"`, and keep `null`. The key stays in place, so presence and member order are compared, and a key `null` in one run and set in the other still fails.
- **Propagation** (decided while writing this bead): each masked string value of at least `PROPAGATE_MIN_LEN` characters is then replaced by `<volatile>` wherever it occurs inside any other string and any object key of the same envelope. That covers the run's own ids inside suggestions (`commands[].argv`, `commands[].command`), paths and argv that embed a doctor run id (`actions_jsonl_path`, `backups_dir`, `undo_command`, `undo_argv`), messages, and maps keyed by a new id. Integers and short strings never propagate, so a deterministic number or short word is never masked by accident.
- **Comparison.** `row` compares A's and B's exits, then `strip(a).text == strip(b).text`. On a difference it records `log.json("A masked", &a.text)`, `log.json("B masked", &b.text)` and `log.json("differences", &first_differences(&a.tree, &b.tree, 10))`, and panics:

```text
matrix row `omaddons <argv>` printed different bytes on two fresh copies of its home:
  <path>: A <value>, B <value>
  …
A key whose value legitimately differs between identical runs is declared in contract::VOLATILE
(src/contract/volatile.rs) with its kind and reason; anything else is nondeterminism to fix
(a HashMap, an unsorted directory listing, a timestamp in a sort key).
test log: <transcript path>
```

`first_differences` walks both trees in step: object members by position (a different key at one position is an order difference: "member 3 of data: A `files`, B `bytes`"), array items by index (a length difference reported once), scalars by value. Values are cut at 80 characters, and at most `limit` are returned in document order.

### 5. One way to mask

- Remove `support::without_meta`. Its callers compare `repeat::strip(stdout)?.text` instead: `read_only_commands_ignore_dry_run_and_reason` (and E3's local `without_volatile` goes too, since the doctor's five keys are `VOLATILE` rows), `every_json_spelling_prints_the_same_envelope`, `repeated_runs_are_byte_identical`, `m2_outputs_are_byte_identical`, and the `sync --dry-run` pair at `matrix.rs:128`. The four in-place repeats stay: they repeat reads on one warm, populated home, which the copies do not, and now they compare member order too.
- `support::stable`'s scrubber keeps zeroing `duration_ms`, `elapsed_ms` and `lock_held_ms` for snapshots, but tracks its path and the envelope's `command`, and asserts for each key it zeroes that `volatile::declared(command, path)` is `Some`. Otherwise it panics: "the snapshot scrubber zeroes `<path>` of `<command>`, which contract::VOLATILE does not declare". Its other redactions (the root, ULIDs, RFC 3339 times, tokens) are snapshot normalization and stay.

### 6. The audit pass

With the machinery in, run `cargo test --locked --test contract matrix::` and resolve every failure in this commit:

- **A value the run draws, reads from the clock, or derives from file identity:** add a `Volatile` row with the narrowest command scope and path that covers it, its kind and a one-sentence reason, and its README line. Expected from reading the code (confirm each; add only what a failure or the type inventory justifies):
  - `backup create`: `data.targets[].backup.id` (new id), `data.targets[].backup.created_at` and `data.targets[].backup.captured_at` (wall clock) (`src/app/backup.rs:303-309`, `:766-790`);
  - `backup export`: `data.sha256` and `data.compressed_bytes` (new id: the archive holds an id each export draws anew; `tests/contract/matrix.rs:973-979` already redacts both for its snapshot);
  - `backup import`: `data.backup.id` (new id), `data.backup.created_at` (wall clock) (`src/app/backup.rs:2604-2615`);
  - `errors`: `data.targets[].dismiss.precondition`, and `errors dismiss`: `data.precondition` (file identity);
  - a target's `key` (`data.**.key`, and `data.**.target_key` where D4's approval shows it), for each command whose row is the first to take the lock on a client and so registers it, drawing its key (new id);
  - `doctor fix`: root `tx` (new id), `**.identity` (file identity) and `precondition` (file identity, since its predicates hold identities); `doctor undo`: `undo_tx` (new id).
- **The type inventory** (decided while writing this bead): the matrix freezes the clock in some rows (`OMADDONS_NOW` for `errors`, `errors dismiss`, `backup prune`), so also list every field of an output type under `src/app`, `src/output`, `src/backup` and `src/doctor` typed `Timestamp`, `TxId`, `RunId`, `BackupId`, `PlanId`, `TargetKey` or a doctor run id, and classify each in the close comment as "from state" (a history line's `tx`, a record's `installed_at`: deterministic) or "drawn or read by this run" (declared). Example: `errors dismiss`' dismissal time is the run's own clock in production, so it is declared although the matrix freezes it.
- **Anything else is a determinism bug.** Fix it at its cause (iterate a `BTreeMap`, sort a directory listing, keep timestamps out of sort keys). Add a regression test, a unit test of the ordering function with a planted input whose natural order differs from the sorted one, and list it in the close comment. If the fix changes an array's order in an output, say so: order is not shape, so no wire name changes.
- **A fix that would not be additive** (a field to remove or retype): do not make it here. File a bug with `--deps discovered-from:omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3`, make it block H4 (`br dep add omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4 <bug id>`, H4 being `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`, the README final pass), comment it on H1 for its change list, and meanwhile declare the key with the reason "Until <bug id> is fixed, …".
- **Record** in the close comment every row added (with the row that showed it, or the inventory line), every bug fixed, and the contract suite's wall time before and after this part (`time cargo test --locked --test contract`, median of 3).

### 7. README

- `### Volatile keys`: one line per new row, in the registry's order (`readme_lists_every_volatile_row` holds it).
- `### Stability`: replace "that repeated runs print identical bytes" with: "that every matrix row, run twice more on two fresh copies of its home, prints identical bytes once the keys in [Volatile keys](#volatile-keys) are masked, member order included (order is deterministic, though not part of the contract)". If omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3.4 has landed, the clause also says ", and a source scan keeps hash-ordered maps out of serialized types". H2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.2`, the golden and the released baseline) rewrites the rest of that section; touch only this clause.
- The Tests table's `tests/contract/` row gains "every row repeated on two fresh copies of its home and compared byte for byte, the volatile keys masked".

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every test in `tests/contract/matrix.rs` starts with `Scene::matrix(matrix_log!())`, and every row runs as A and B on fresh same-path copies of its starting home, then as C on the original; A and B must have equal exits and equal stdout after `repeat::strip`, round trip asserted; the whole matrix passes with every existing assertion and snapshot unchanged.
- [ ] `tests/contract/repeat.rs` has the order-preserving `Json` tree, `strip_with`/`strip` (type-tagged placeholders, `null` kept, scope respected, propagation of masked strings of 16 characters or more into other strings and object keys) and `first_differences`, with the unit tests of the Test Plan passing.
- [ ] `support::without_meta` and E3's local `without_volatile` are gone; the five comparisons named in Technical Approach 5 use `repeat::strip`; the snapshot scrubber panics on a zeroed key that `VOLATILE` does not declare.
- [ ] `trees::copy_tree_exact` exists (C4's, or added here with its self-test), and `Scene::on_copies` exists for the self-tests.
- [ ] Every difference the repeat found is resolved: a `Volatile` row with kind and reason and its README line, or a fix at the cause with a regression test; the close comment lists each, the type inventory's classification, and the contract suite's wall time before and after.
- [ ] No wire name is added or changed; any non-additive need is filed `discovered-from` omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3, blocks omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4, is noted on omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1, and its key is declared meanwhile.
- [ ] README's `### Volatile keys`, the `### Stability` clause and the Tests table row are updated in this commit; `readme_lists_every_volatile_row` passes.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `br lint` is clean for this subtask.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

In `tests/contract/repeat.rs` (the contract crate):

- `the_tree_round_trips_the_binary_s_bytes`, one named case each: `nested_objects`, `escapes` (`"a\"b\\c\n\t"`), `non_ascii` (`"é漢"`), `integers` (`0`, `-1`, `18446744073709551615`), `floats` (`1.0`, `0.1`, `1e-7`, each as serde_json prints it), `empty_containers` (`{}`, `[]`), `duplicate_keys_kept` (`{"a":1,"a":2}`): `to_compact(parse(s)) == s`.
- `member_order_is_compared`: `{"a":1,"b":2}` vs `{"b":2,"a":1}` → one difference naming member 0 of the root.
- `declared_values_are_masked_by_type`: `{"command":"install","data":{"tx":"01M5…","target":{"id":"retail"}},"meta":{"elapsed_ms":3,"offline":false}}` → `data.tx` `"<volatile string>"`, `meta.elapsed_ms` `"<volatile number>"`, `meta.offline` `"<volatile bool>"`, `data.target.id` unchanged.
- `null_is_kept`: A `data.tx` `null`, B a ULID → a difference at `data.tx`.
- `presence_is_compared`: `data.tx` in A only → a difference.
- `the_scope_is_respected`: `data.sha256` masked when `command` is `backup export`, kept when it is `install`.
- `propagation_masks_reappearances_only`: A and B each with `data.tx` and `commands[0].argv[2]` holding their own 26-character tx, and an undeclared `data.target.key` equal in both → equal after masking, the key unmasked; a masked 15-character string does not propagate; a masked number does not propagate.
- `propagation_reaches_object_keys`: a map keyed by the masked tx → equal after masking.
- `differences_are_listed_in_order_and_capped`: 12 differing leaves → the first 10, in document order, values cut at 80 characters.
- `a_non_json_stdout_is_reported`: `"oops"` → `Err` naming the text.
- `the_scrubber_refuses_an_undeclared_zeroed_key`: `stable()` over `{"command":"status","data":{"x":{"duration_ms":1}}}` passes (covered by `data.**.duration_ms`); over `{"command":"status","data":{"elapsed_ms":1}}` (an `elapsed_ms` outside `meta`, which no row declares) it panics with the message of Technical Approach 5, caught with `catch_unwind`.

Each assertion message names the case and shows the input and the output.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

- **The matrix** (`tests/contract/matrix.rs`): every existing test, now repeating each row. Pass: all 40 (and every later one) pass with unchanged snapshots. The audit pass's findings are recorded in the close comment.
- **The in-place repeats** (`tests/contract/special.rs`): `repeated_runs_are_byte_identical`, `m2_outputs_are_byte_identical`, `read_only_commands_ignore_dry_run_and_reason` and `every_json_spelling_prints_the_same_envelope`, unchanged in what they run, now comparing `repeat::strip` text (member order included).
- **The self-test of the copy helper** (`tests/common_selftest.rs`, only if this part adds `copy_tree_exact`): `copy_tree_exact_keeps_kinds_modes_links_and_mtimes`, as in Technical Approach 2.

### Logging

- Every matrix test logs through T1's `TestLog` (suite `contract.matrix`). Each row is a `step` named `row <n>: omaddons <argv>`, holding three run records, `A (copy 1)`, `B (copy 2)` and `C (the row)`, each with its argv, extra variables, exit, stdout, stderr and `elapsed_ms`.
- On a difference the step also records `json("A masked")`, `json("B masked")` and `json("differences")`, and the panic message ends with the transcript path.
- On any other panic, T1's guard prints the log path and the last 20 steps, so a failing row's three runs are on screen.
- Unit tests in `repeat.rs` do not use the log; their messages name the case.

## Considerations

- **Gate time.** Each row runs three times plus two copies of a home of a few hundred small files. Expect the matrix's wall time to roughly triple. Record it. If `argc gate` as a whole grows by more than 60 seconds, file a follow-up `discovered-from` omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3 (run A and B in parallel threads on two slots, or copy less); never drop the repeat.
- **Time boundaries cannot flake a row:** only declared keys may differ, and they are masked. A relative time inside an undeclared string ("3 minutes ago" in a JSON message) is a real finding.
- **Rows the copies cannot reproduce** (identity-bound tokens bound with `--if-match`, journals with recorded identities) take the copy's path in both A and B and the real path in C. That is the design; do not special-case such rows.
- **The environment is the row's.** A, B and C run with exactly the row's argv, variables and input; never add `OMADDONS_NOW` or anything else for A and B.
- **A matrix row must not run while a background process holds files in the home** (the repeat moves the home). `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3.3`'s conventions test forbids `.spawn(` in `matrix.rs`; the matrix has none today.
- **Hot spots.** `tests/contract/matrix.rs` is appended by every command leaf: change the 40 constructors in one quick commit right after rebasing, then tell agents in flight (`SendMessage`) to use `Scene::matrix(matrix_log!())`. `tests/contract/main.rs`'s `support::check` is shared (A1, A3, E3, H2 add blocks): this part changes `Scene`, `stable` and removes `without_meta`, and does not touch `check`'s blocks. `tests/common/trees.rs`: append only. README: only the three places of section 7.
- **Later leaves** add rows that this repeat runs: say in the module doc of `repeat.rs` that a new volatile key is declared in `VOLATILE` with its kind and reason and listed in README's table.

## Dependencies

- Parent: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3 (the determinism audit).
- Before it: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3.1, for the `Volatile` rows, `declared_in` and README's table that this part masks with and extends.
- After it: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3.3 adds the coverage audit, which runs the matrix with `CONTRACT_REPEAT=off` and logs under `matrix_log!()`'s audit suite, and the missing rows, which this repeat then runs; omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3.5 uses `Scene::on_copies` and `strip_with`.
- Also blocked by T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs; an edge added at filing): the matrix logs through `TestLog`.

title: The coverage audit: a success and a failure row for every command path, the matrix's conventions, and the missing rows
description:
Part 3 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3 (The determinism audit). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

H3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3`, the determinism audit) makes "one command on one unchanged home prints the same bytes, except the declared volatile keys" a gate test over every command path (G-M4-5; checkpoint criterion 14's determinism part: "Repeated runs of every command path print identical bytes, after stripping only the keys the volatile registry declares"). `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3.2` repeats every matrix row on two fresh copies of its home. That proves the claim for every path only if every path has rows.

**This part** makes "every row" mean "every command path". It adds the coverage audit (every `app::COMMANDS` path has at least one success row and one failure row in `tests/contract/matrix.rs`), the conventions that keep later matrix tests inside the repeat, and the rows missing today. It is its own step because the audit needs `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3.2`'s `Scene::matrix` and its audit log suite, and because the new rows must pass that repeat.

**M4-D18, restated:** every path in `app::COMMANDS` has at least one success row and one failure row in the contract matrix, a coverage test fails a path that lacks one, and every row runs twice. **M4-D5, restated:** `CommandEntry.exits` declares each path's exits (A1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1`, per-command facts in `COMMANDS`), and the contract suite fails an exit a path produced but did not declare. This part guarantees every path is exercised on success and failure, so that cross-check sees every path. It also reports the declared exits no row produced, as evidence, without failing.

**Facts this part relies on** (as of `c0ab5e9`, adjusted for the leaves before H3):

- `app::COMMANDS` (`src/app/mod.rs:121-165`; after A1 one row per runnable path: every clap leaf, plus each parent whose bare form runs: `backup`, `config`, `errors`, `omarchy`, `targets`, and later `doctor`; `auth` becomes `auth github`).
- Bare `backup` answers with envelope `command` `backup list`, and bare `omarchy` with `omarchy status` (`src/app/mod.rs:208-211`, `:232-235`). So coverage keyed by the envelope's name would never count the `backup` and `omarchy` rows. Instead the key is the invoked clap path: `cli::command_path(argv)` (`src/cli.rs:1010-1037`, public; argv including the binary name; flags and their values skipped; aliases resolved to canonical names).
- The contract tests run on parallel threads, and libtest has no hook after the last test. A1 checks its exit observation inline for that reason. A3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`, schemas and live validation) re-runs the suite as a child of `std::env::current_exe()` for its details report (`CONTRACT_DETAILS_OBSERVED`), which is the precedent followed here.
- `support::check(run, code)` (`tests/contract/main.rs:113-225`) is where every contract run is checked. A1, A3, E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, the doctor envelope) and H2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.2`, the golden) each add their own block there.
- `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3.2` gives `Scene::matrix(matrix_log!())`, which repeats each row unless `CONTRACT_REPEAT=off`, and whose log suite is `contract.matrix_audit` when `CONTRACT_MATRIX_ROWS` is set.
- At `c0ab5e9`, reading `tests/contract/matrix.rs` gives 13 missing rows: failure rows for bare `backup`, bare `targets`, `config get` and `config path` and bare `omarchy`; success and failure for `targets rm`, `targets default` and bare `config`; success for `targets rename` and `omarchy status`.

## Technical Approach

### 1. Recording rows

In `support::check`, as its own block after the existing checks: when `CONTRACT_MATRIX_ROWS` names a file, append one JSON line for the run through a process-wide `static ROWS: OnceLock<Mutex<File>>` (opened with `OpenOptions::new().create(true).append(true)`):

```json
{"test":"matrix::targets","argv":["targets","rm","pserver","--json"],"path":"targets rm","command":"targets rm",
 "exit":0,"kind":"success","error_code":null}
```

- `test`: `std::thread::current().name()` (libtest names each test's thread after the test), else `"unknown"`.
- `path`: `omaddons::cli::command_path(&["omaddons", argv…]).join(" ")`; when it is empty (bare `omaddons`, `--bogus`, `-V`), the envelope's `command`.
- `kind`: `success` for exit 0 with `ok: true`; `failure` for an envelope with a non-null `error` object, whatever the exit (`check_failed`, exit 6, included); otherwise `other` (a doctor run that ends with findings, exit 1, without an error).
- `error_code`: `error.code` or `null`.

`path` and `kind` are computed by two pure functions in `tests/contract/coverage.rs`, `pub fn path_of(argv: &[String], envelope_command: &str) -> String` and `pub fn kind_of(exit: i32, envelope: &Value) -> Kind`, which the unit tests below cover. Without the variable, `check` behaves exactly as before.

### 2. The audit

`tests/contract/coverage.rs`, a new module (`mod coverage;` in `tests/contract/main.rs`):

```rust
pub struct Row { pub test: String, pub argv: Vec<String>, pub path: String, pub command: String,
                 pub exit: i32, pub kind: Kind, pub error_code: Option<String> }
pub enum Audit { Done(Vec<Row>), Failed { status: String, tail: String } }
/// The matrix's rows, from one child run of this test binary (shared by every test of the module).
pub fn audit() -> &'static Audit;          // audit_with("matrix::") in a OnceLock
/// The same over the tests a filter selects (for the self-tests).
pub fn audit_with(filter: &str) -> Audit;
pub struct Missing { pub success: Vec<String>, pub failure: Vec<String> }
pub fn coverage(rows: &[Row], commands: &[&str]) -> Missing;   // pure
/// The coverage test's verdict and message: a failed child, an empty run, or the gaps; Ok when every path is covered.
pub fn verdict(audit: &Audit, commands: &[&str]) -> Result<(), String>;   // pure
```

`audit_with(filter)` runs `std::process::Command::new(std::env::current_exe())` with the argument `filter`, `CONTRACT_MATRIX_ROWS=<fresh tempdir>/rows.jsonl` and `CONTRACT_REPEAT=off`, captures stdout and stderr, then reads the rows file. A child that does not exit successfully gives `Failed { status, tail }` (its last 60 output lines). An unreadable rows line is a failure naming the line. The child runs without repeats, so it costs one plain run of the matrix; the parent's own run of the matrix does the repeats.

`coverage` collects, per path, whether a `success` and a `failure` row exist, and lists each `commands` path lacking either, sorted. Paths that are not in `commands` (`omaddons`, `version`) are ignored.

Tests of the module:

- `every_commands_path_has_a_success_and_a_failure_row`: `audit()` must be `Done`, else it fails with "the matrix failed in the coverage child (<status>); fix the matrix first" and the tail. An empty row set fails with "no rows: the filter matched no matrix test", so an empty run never reads as a list of gaps or as covered (the message comes from a pure `fn verdict(audit: &Audit, commands: &[&str]) -> Result<(), String>`, which `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3.5` also calls). Then `coverage(rows, COMMANDS names)` must be empty, else it fails with each path and the kind it lacks, and: "add a row to its test in tests/contract/matrix.rs: `s.json(&[…], <exit>)` and an insta snapshot of `s.stable(&c.envelope)`". It also logs `rows per path` and `declared exits no matrix row produced` (each path's `entry.exits` minus the exits its rows produced), without asserting them.
- `the_matrix_follows_its_conventions` (static, over the text of `tests/contract/matrix.rs` read at run time): no `Scene::new(`; every `#[test]` function's body contains `Scene::matrix(matrix_log!())` (split the file at `#[test]`, take the function name from the following `fn <name>(`); no `.spawn(`, because a background process holding files in the home would break the repeat's move of the home. The checker is a pure `fn convention_violations(text: &str) -> Vec<(String, &'static str)>` (test name, rule broken), so it can be tested on planted texts. The failure names the test function and the rule.

Decided while writing this bead: the child run (libtest has no after-all hook; inline checks cannot know a path will never be reached); the key by invoked path (bare `backup` and `omarchy`); the three kinds (a doctor run with findings is not a failure row: a failure row is an error envelope).

### 3. The missing rows

Run the audit and add every row it names, each in the matrix test of its command, after that test's existing rows so no later row's state changes, each with `insta::assert_json_snapshot!(<name>, s.stable(&c.envelope))` (the `omarchy` rows also redact `data.plugin.binary` and `data.plugin.version`, as that test's other rows do). Prefer a failure the command itself raises (an unknown id). For a parent with none, use an unknown flag: a usage error, exit 2, which also proves the parent's usage error names the parent's row (A1). The 13 rows expected at `c0ab5e9`, with their expected exits (the exit the code gives is the row's, and any that differs is recorded in the close comment):

| Path | Kind | Row, in which test | Exit | Snapshot |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `backup` | failure | `backup --bogus`, in `backup_list` | 2 | `backup_bare_usage` |

title: The `HashMap` scan: `tests/determinism.rs` refuses a hash map or set in a serialized type of the output directories
description:
Part 4 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3 (The determinism audit). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

H3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3`, the determinism audit) makes "one command on one unchanged home prints the same bytes, except the declared volatile keys" a gate test over every command path (G-M4-5; checkpoint criterion 14's determinism part). Its run-time half repeats every contract matrix row on fresh copies of its home. **This part** is its static half: a source scan that fails a `HashMap` or `HashSet` field in a type that derives `Serialize` in the output directories. Rust's `HashMap` and `HashSet` use a randomly seeded hasher (`RandomState`) per process, so a serialized one prints its members in a different order on each run. The repeat catches that at run time, but only on a row whose output holds two or more members. The scan catches it before any run, wherever the type is used. It is its own step because it touches only a new test crate and one README table row, and depends on nothing the other parts add.

**M4-D18, restated:** "A source scan fails any `HashMap` or `HashSet` field in a type that derives `Serialize` under `src/app`, `src/output`, `src/contract` or `src/doctor`." Why: `HashMap` iteration order differs per process; the repeat test catches one at run time, and the scan catches it before. DEC-3 (common rule 5) already says maps in wire shapes are `BTreeMap` and no `HashMap` or `HashSet` appears in a serialized type; this scan enforces it. §6.8 places it in `tests/determinism.rs`, "using `source_scan`".

**Facts this part relies on** (as of `c0ab5e9`):

- `src/source_scan.rs` gives the production view of a source file: comments, test-only items (`#[cfg(test)]` and `cfg(all(test, …))` items, wherever they sit) and, with `Literals::Blank`, the contents of string and char literals all become spaces, newlines kept. Its `pub(crate)` items are `enum Literals { Keep, Blank }` (`:16`), `fn production_code(text: &str, literals: Literals) -> Option<String>` (`:26`, `None` for a file marked `#![cfg(test)]`) and `fn sources(dir: &Path) -> Vec<(PathBuf, String)>` (`:63`, every `.rs` file under `dir`, sorted). It depends only on `std`. Its private helpers (bracket matching, item ends) are not reachable from outside.
- It is declared `#[cfg(test)] mod source_scan;` (`src/lib.rs:37-38`), crate-private and compiled only into the library's own unit tests. Its module doc says the integration test `tests/single_writer.rs` cannot share it, because an integration test does not see the library's `cfg(test)` code. So `tests/determinism.rs` cannot `use omaddons::source_scan`, as the plan's wording implies.
- An integration test crate is itself compiled with `cfg(test)`, so the same file compiles when included into it by `#[path]`. Its unit tests (`src/source_scan.rs:334-415`, one of which reads `include_str!("net/mod.rs")`, resolved relative to `src/source_scan.rs`) then also run in that crate, which is harmless.
- No `Serialize`-deriving type under `src/app` or `src/output` holds a `HashMap` or `HashSet` today. `src/contract` (A1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1`, and A2) and `src/doctor` (E1, E3) exist by the time H3 starts. Elsewhere, `HashMap`s sit only in non-serialized internals (`src/discover/scan.rs:118`, `src/engine/inspect.rs:287`, `src/net/limit.rs:79`, `src/net/replay.rs:101`) and in tests.

## Technical Approach

### 1. The crate

`tests/determinism.rs`:

```rust
//! The determinism scan (M4-D18): no HashMap or HashSet in a type that derives Serialize in the output directories,
//! because a hash map's iteration order differs per process. The run-time half is the contract matrix's repeat.

// The crate's production-source view, the same file the library's unit-test scans use: one lexer, not a copy.
#[allow(dead_code)]
#[path = "../src/source_scan.rs"]
mod source_scan;

use source_scan::{Literals, production_code, sources};

/// The directories M4-D18 names.
const SCANNED: &[&str] = &["src/app", "src/output", "src/contract", "src/doctor"];

/// One finding: the line (1-based), the item's name and the line's text.
#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
struct Hit { line: usize, item: String, text: String }

/// Each `HashMap<` or `HashSet<` within the extent of a `struct` or `enum` whose derive list contains `Serialize`,
/// in `code`, which is already `production_code(…, Literals::Blank)`.
fn serialized_hash_fields(code: &str) -> Vec<Hit>;
```

Decided while writing this bead: include the file by `#[path]`, because the module is crate-private and `cfg(test)`. Rejected: copying the lexer (two lexers drift apart, which `src/source_scan.rs`'s doc warns about), and moving the scan into a library unit test (the plan names `tests/determinism.rs`, and an integration test keeps it beside the other gate scans). `#[allow(dead_code)]` covers `Literals::Keep` and anything else this crate does not use. The test reads no command and runs no binary, so it does not use T1's `TestLog`.

### 2. The scanner

On the blanked code (so brackets and keywords inside literals and comments are already spaces):

1. Find each `#[derive(`, and its matching `)]` by counting parentheses. Split the contents on top-level commas and trim. The derive counts when an entry is `Serialize` or ends with `::Serialize` (`serde::Serialize`).
2. From after the attribute, skip whitespace and every further attribute `#[ … ]` (matched by counting brackets), then an optional visibility: `pub`, `pub(crate)`, `pub(super)`, `pub(self)` or `pub(in <path>)`. Then require the keyword `struct` or `enum` followed by an identifier, the item's name. Anything else (a `union`, a malformed item) is skipped.
3. The item's extent runs from its name to its end, generics and `where` clauses included (so a default type parameter counts): the matching `}` of the first `{` at depth zero, or, for a tuple struct, the matching `)` and then the `;`, or the `;` of a unit struct.
4. Within the extent, report every occurrence of the word `HashMap` or `HashSet` (preceded by a non-identifier character or `::`, so `std::collections::HashMap` counts and `MyHashMap` does not) followed by optional whitespace and `<`. The line is counted from the start of `code`; `text` is that line of the original source, trimmed.

Keep it about 100 lines; it needs no other parsing.

### 3. The tests

- `no_serialized_type_holds_a_hash_map_or_set`: for each directory of `SCANNED` (relative to `env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")`), each `(path, text)` of `sources(dir)`, skip a file whose `production_code(text, Literals::Blank)` is `None`, and collect `serialized_hash_fields`. It fails listing `<repo-relative path>:<line> <item>: <text>` for each hit, then: "use BTreeMap or BTreeSet (DEC-3, M4-D18): a hash map's iteration order differs per process, so the output would differ between runs".
- `the_scanned_directories_exist`: all four directories exist. A rename or move must not silently empty the scan; if a directory is renamed, update `SCANNED` with it.
- `the_scan_finds_what_it_must`: the planted cases of the Test Plan, each run through `production_code(case, Literals::Blank)` then `serialized_hash_fields`.

### 4. README

The Development section's Tests table (`README.md:2623-2638` at `c0ab5e9`) gains a row: `` `tests/determinism.rs` `` | "No `HashMap` or `HashSet` in a type that derives `Serialize` under `src/app`, `src/output`, `src/contract` or `src/doctor` (a scan of the production source; a hash map prints in a different order on each run)". And README's `### Stability` clause on determinism, as `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3.2` and `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3.3` leave it, gains ", and a source scan keeps hash-ordered maps out of serialized types". If this part lands before `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3.2`, add the Tests table row only, and `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3.2` writes the clause with the scan in it.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `tests/determinism.rs` exists with the crate doc above, includes `src/source_scan.rs` by `#[path]` (no copied lexer), and defines `serialized_hash_fields` over the blanked production code.
- [ ] `the_scan_finds_what_it_must` passes every planted case of the Test Plan, each named in its assertion message.
- [ ] `no_serialized_type_holds_a_hash_map_or_set` passes on `main`, and fails, listing file, line, item and text, when a `HashMap<String, u8>` field is added to any `Serialize` struct under `src/app` (checked by hand once and reverted; say so in the close comment).
- [ ] `the_scanned_directories_exist` passes.
- [ ] README's Tests table lists `tests/determinism.rs` (and the Stability clause names the scan once `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3.2` has written it), in this commit.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes (clippy included: no warning from the included module); `br lint` is clean for this subtask.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

`the_scan_finds_what_it_must` in `tests/determinism.rs`, one named case each. "hit" means exactly one `Hit` with the named item, "none" means no hit:

| Case | Input (abridged) | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| `hash_map_field` | `#[derive(Serialize)] struct A { m: HashMap<String, u8> }` | hit `A` |
| `qualified_hash_set` | `#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, JsonSchema)] pub struct A { pub s: std::collections::HashSet<u8> }` | hit `A` |
| `enum_variant_field` | `#[derive(Serialize)] pub enum E { V { m: HashMap<u8, u8> }, W }` | hit `E` |
| `tuple_struct` | `#[derive(Serialize)] pub struct T(pub HashMap<u8, u8>);` | hit `T` |
| `serde_attr_between` | `#[derive(Serialize)]\n#[serde(rename_all = "snake_case")]\npub(crate) struct A { m: Option<HashMap<u8, u8>> }` | hit `A` |
| `generic_default` | `#[derive(Serialize)] struct A<M = HashMap<u8, u8>> { m: M }` | hit `A` |
| `serde_path_derive` | `#[derive(Debug, serde::Serialize)] struct A { m: HashMap<u8, u8> }` | hit `A` |
| `two_hits_one_item` | a `Serialize` struct with a `HashMap` and a `HashSet` field | two hits `A` |
| `btree_map` | `#[derive(Serialize)] struct A { m: BTreeMap<u8, u8> }` | none |
| `debug_only_derive` | `#[derive(Debug)] struct A { m: HashMap<u8, u8> }` | none |
| `deserialize_only` | `#[derive(Deserialize)] struct A { m: HashMap<u8, u8> }` | none |
| `in_a_comment` | `// #[derive(Serialize)] struct A { m: HashMap<u8, u8> }` | none |
| `in_a_string` | `#[derive(Serialize)] struct A { s: &'static str }` then `const X: &str = "HashMap<u8>";` | none |
| `test_only_item` | `#[cfg(test)]\n#[derive(Serialize)] struct A { m: HashMap<u8, u8> }` | none |
| `next_item_not_serialized` | a clean `Serialize` struct, then `struct B { m: HashMap<u8, u8> }` | none |
| `unit_struct_then_other` | `#[derive(Serialize)] struct U;` then `struct B { m: HashMap<u8, u8> }` | none |
| `similar_name` | `#[derive(Serialize)] struct A { m: MyHashMap<u8> }` | none |
| `pub_in_path` | `#[derive(Serialize)] pub(in crate::app) struct A { m: HashSet<u8> }` | hit `A` |

Each assertion message prints the case name, the input and the hits found.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

`no_serialized_type_holds_a_hash_map_or_set` and `the_scanned_directories_exist` scan the real source tree. They run no binary and no command, so they do not use T1's `TestLog`; this part's spec sets `uses_test_log: false`.

### Logging

No `TestLog` (no command runs). The scan's failure message is the log: every hit with repo-relative path, line, item and text, plus the fix. The planted cases' messages name the case.

## Considerations

- **Scope is M4-D18's four directories.** Serialized types defined elsewhere (`src/model.rs`, `src/backup/`, `src/state/`, `src/engine/inspect.rs`'s report types) are outside it. The matrix repeat catches a hash-ordered field there at run time, and none exists today. Widening the scan is a later decision, not this bead's.
- **What it cannot see.** A `Vec` filled by iterating a `HashMap` without sorting, or a `serde_json::Value` object built from one, has no `HashMap` field. The repeat catches those (two processes, two orders).
- **False positives** are unlikely (the planted cases), and a deliberate exception has no allowlist: a serialized type must not hold a hash collection at all.
- **Hot spots:** none. A new crate, plus one README table row.

title: E2E: the audit catches what it must, on real runs over copies and over a partial matrix
description:
Part 5 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3 (The determinism audit). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

H3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3`, the determinism audit) makes "one command on one unchanged home prints the same bytes, except the declared volatile keys" a gate test over every command path. It serves G-M4-5 and checkpoint criterion 14's determinism part: "Repeated runs of every command path print identical bytes, after stripping only the keys the volatile registry declares". `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3.2` repeats every matrix row on two fresh copies of its home and compares them after masking `contract::VOLATILE`'s keys. `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3.3` proves every command path has a success and a failure row.

A check that always passes proves nothing. **This part** proves on real binary runs that the audit catches what it must and masks nothing it should not:

- a reduced registry makes the repeat fail at the right key;
- a token bound to file identity differs between copies, while the engine's content-bound tokens do not;
- propagation masks a new id where it reappears and leaves deterministic ids alone;
- the coverage audit over a partial matrix names every uncovered path, and an empty run never reads as covered.

It is the leaf's test subtask: integration tests of the machinery the earlier parts added, ordered after them.

**What the earlier parts left** (restated so this part needs nothing else):

- `contract::VOLATILE: &[Volatile]` with `Volatile { command, path, kind, reason }`, and `volatile::declared_in(table, command, path)` (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3.1`).
- In `tests/contract/repeat.rs` (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3.2`):
  - `strip_with(stdout, table) -> Result<Stripped, String>`: masks every value `table` declares for the envelope's `command` with a type-tagged placeholder, keeps `null`, and propagates masked strings of 16 characters or more into every other string and object key;
  - `strip(stdout)` (with `VOLATILE`) and `first_differences(a, b, limit) -> Vec<Difference { path, a, b }>`;
  - `support::Scene::on_copies(&self, args, env) -> (Ran, Ran)`: the args with `--json` run as A and B, each on a fresh same-path copy of the scene's home, the original restored, nothing compared.
- In `tests/contract/coverage.rs` (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3.3`): `audit_with(filter) -> Audit` (`Done(rows)` or `Failed { status, tail }`), which runs the contract binary as a child over the tests `filter` selects with `CONTRACT_MATRIX_ROWS` and `CONTRACT_REPEAT=off`, `coverage(rows, commands) -> Missing { success, failure }`, and `verdict(&audit, commands) -> Result<(), String>` (a failed child: "fix the matrix first"; no rows: "no rows: the filter matched no matrix test"; else the gaps).

**Facts this part relies on** (as of `c0ab5e9`):

- `support::Scene::new()` builds a home with a retail and a Mists Classic client, the zips `foo`, `foo2`, `both` and `blizz` under `<root>/dl`, and replayed GitHub releases for WeakAuras, `gh:o/foo` and `gh:o/bar` (`tests/contract/main.rs:366-423`). `install_foo()` installs `foo` into retail (`:494-499`).
- The matrix's `errors_dismiss` test plants a BugGrabber database with `common::buggrabber` (`BugDb::new(Writer::Modern, 10)`, `write_files`) under `OMADDONS_NOW=2026-10-15T18:30:00Z` (`tests/contract/matrix.rs:1110-1158`).
- `errors dismiss`'s token fingerprints each database file with `FileStamp::fingerprint()` (device, inode, size, mtime, change time: `src/fsx/stamp.rs:73-89`; `src/app/precondition.rs:419-440`), so it differs on a copy. `remove`'s token binds target generations and the selection only (`src/app/precondition.rs:243-311`). The engine commands' tokens (D1, M4-D19 and M4-D60) hold content digests, generations and `build_id`, and exclude stamps.

## Technical Approach

`tests/contract/audit_selftest.rs`, a new module (`mod audit_selftest;` in `tests/contract/main.rs`). Each test builds its own `Scene::new()` (never a matrix scene: these tests are not rows, and the coverage audit must not count them) and its own `tlog!()`. A small helper:

```rust
/// `table` without the rows for which `drop` holds, leaked once per test (the masking API takes a `'static` table).
fn without(drop: impl Fn(&Volatile) -> bool) -> &'static [Volatile];
```

### Scenario 1: `a_real_install_differs_only_in_declared_keys`

1. `log.step("install on two copies")`: `s.on_copies(&["install", "gh:o/foo", "--file", <root>/dl/foo.zip, "-t", "retail"], &[])` → A and B both exit 0 (`Ran::ok`).
2. `log.step("masked with VOLATILE")`: `strip(a).text == strip(b).text`.
3. `log.step("masked without data.**.tx")`: with `without(|r| r.path == "data.**.tx")`, `first_differences` includes `data.tx` and `commands[0].argv[2]` (no propagation without the row), and a failure message built as `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3.2`'s `row` builds it names `data.tx`.
4. `log.json` each masked text and difference list.

### Scenario 2: `an_identity_bound_token_differs_between_copies_and_engine_tokens_do_not`

1. `install_foo()`, plant the BugGrabber database and `!BugGrabber` folder as the matrix's `errors_dismiss` test does.
2. `log.step("errors dismiss --dry-run on two copies")` with `OMADDONS_NOW=2026-10-15T18:30:00Z`: under `VOLATILE`, equal. Under `without(|r| r.command == "errors dismiss" && r.path == "data.precondition")`, a difference at `data.precondition`.
3. `log.step("an engine dry run on two copies")`: `install gh:o/foo --file <root>/dl/foo2.zip -t retail --dry-run`. The raw `data.precondition` values (read from `Ran::envelope()`, not masked) are equal, and not null. That is criterion 6's "two dry runs of an unchanged home give equal tokens", across copies.
4. `log.step("remove --dry-run on two copies")`: `remove Foo -t retail --dry-run`. The raw `data.precondition` values are equal: M3's `remove` token survives a copy.

### Scenario 3: `masked_ids_are_masked_where_they_reappear_and_nowhere_else`

1. On the install of scenario 1 (a fresh scene): after `strip`, `commands[0].argv[2]` and the matching part of `commands[0].command` are `<volatile>` in both A and B, while `data.target.id` is `retail` in both.
2. `log.step("info on two copies")`: after `install_foo()` on the scene itself, `s.on_copies(&["info", "Foo"], &[])` → the masked texts are equal, and the masked list (`Stripped.masked`) holds only `meta.*` paths, so a deterministic id that `info` reads from state (the installed record's `tx`) is never masked. If `info`'s data carries that `tx` under a key `data.**.tx` matches, assert instead that it is equal raw in A and B, and log that the row masks it harmlessly.
3. `log.step("history on two copies")`: `s.on_copies(&["history"], &[])` → equal after masking.

### Scenario 4: `the_coverage_audit_names_every_uncovered_path`

1. `log.step("audit over matrix::info")`: `audit_with("matrix::info")` is `Done(rows)`, every row's `test` is `matrix::info`, and `info` has a success and a failure row.
2. `coverage(&rows, COMMANDS names)`: `info` is in neither list; every other `COMMANDS` path is in both. The failure message the coverage test would print names `install` and `doctor diagnose` and not `info`.
3. `log.json("missing", …)`.

### Scenario 5: `an_empty_or_failed_audit_never_reads_as_covered`

1. `log.step("a filter that matches nothing")`: `audit_with("matrix::no_test_has_this_name")` → `Done(rows)` with no rows (libtest exits 0 when a filter matches nothing). `verdict(&audit, COMMANDS names)` is `Err` containing "no rows: the filter matched no matrix test", never `Ok` and never a list of gaps.
2. `log.step("a child that fails")`: `audit_with("--no-such-libtest-flag")` → `Failed { status, tail }`, the status not a success and the tail naming the flag; `verdict` is `Err` containing "fix the matrix first". A failing child is reported as such and never turned into a coverage verdict.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `tests/contract/audit_selftest.rs` holds the five scenarios, each on its own `Scene::new()` with its own `tlog!()`, and all pass.
- [ ] Scenario 1 shows a real install on two copies equal under `VOLATILE` and different at `data.tx` (and `commands[0].argv[2]`) without the `data.**.tx` row.
- [ ] Scenario 2 shows `errors dismiss --dry-run`'s token differing between copies without its row, and the raw tokens of an engine dry run and of `remove --dry-run` equal across copies.
- [ ] Scenario 3 shows propagation masking the new tx inside `commands[]` and masking nothing in `info`'s output but `meta`.
- [ ] Scenarios 4 and 5 show the coverage audit naming every uncovered path over `matrix::info`, an empty run reported as such, and a failing child reported as `Failed`, never as covered.
- [ ] No product code changes; `argc gate` passes; `br lint` is clean for this subtask.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

None new: the pure functions these scenarios drive (`strip_with`, `first_differences`, `coverage`, `verdict`, `path_of`, `kind_of`) carry their unit tests in `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3.2` and `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3.3`.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

The five scenarios above, in `tests/contract/audit_selftest.rs`, run with `cargo test --locked --test contract audit_selftest`. Assertions after each step:

| Scenario | Step | Asserted |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | install on two copies | both exit 0; masked texts equal; without `data.**.tx`, differences include `data.tx` and `commands[0].argv[2]` |
| 2 | `errors dismiss --dry-run` | equal under `VOLATILE`; without its row, a difference at `data.precondition` |
| 2 | `install … foo2.zip --dry-run` | raw `data.precondition` equal and non-null |
| 2 | `remove Foo --dry-run` | raw `data.precondition` equal |
| 3 | install | `commands[0].argv[2]` is `<volatile>` in both; `data.target.id` is `retail` |
| 3 | `info Foo` | equal; `masked` holds only `meta.*` (or a tx equal raw) |
| 3 | `history` | equal after masking |
| 4 | `audit_with("matrix::info")` | rows only from `matrix::info`; `info` covered; every other path missing both kinds |
| 5 | `audit_with(<no match>)` | no rows; every path missing; the "no rows" sentence |
| 5 | `audit_with("--no-such-libtest-flag")` | `Failed`, status not a success, the tail names the flag |

### Logging

- Each scenario uses T1's `tlog!()`: one `step` per row of the table above. `Scene::on_copies` records its A and B runs as `A (copy 1)` and `B (copy 2)` (argv, variables, exit, stdout, stderr, `elapsed_ms`).
- Every comparison logs `json("A masked")`, `json("B masked")` and `json("differences")`. Every reduced table logs `json("dropped rows")`.
- The audit scenarios log `json("rows")` and `json("missing")`, and on a failed child its status and tail.
- A failing assertion names the step, and T1's panic guard prints the transcript path and the last 20 steps.

## Considerations

- **These are not matrix rows.** They use `Scene::new()`, so they are not repeated and the coverage audit never counts them (its child runs `matrix::` only).
- **Cost.** About a dozen binary runs and two child runs of one matrix test each; seconds.
- **If an assertion here fails after a later leaf's change,** the audit machinery has regressed or a token lost a property it had. Read the transcript before changing the scenario.
- **Hot spots:** none (a new module). `tests/contract/main.rs` gains one `mod` line.

## Dependencies

- Parent: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3 (the determinism audit).
- Before it: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3.2 (`strip_with`, `first_differences`, `Scene::on_copies`, and the declared rows the scenarios rely on, such as install's target key and `errors dismiss`'s token) and omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3.3 (`audit_with`, `coverage`).
- After it: none. As the last part, its closer usually verifies the leaf's acceptance criteria and closes omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3.
- Also blocked by T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs; an edge added at filing): every scenario logs through `TestLog`.

- [ ] `tests/contract/audit_selftest.rs` holds the five scenarios, each on its own `Scene::new()` with its own `tlog!()`, and all pass.
- [ ] Scenario 1 shows a real install on two copies equal under `VOLATILE` and different at `data.tx` (and `commands[0].argv[2]`) without the `data.**.tx` row.
- [ ] Scenario 2 shows `errors dismiss --dry-run`'s token differing between copies without its row, and the raw tokens of an engine dry run and of `remove --dry-run` equal across copies.
- [ ] Scenario 3 shows propagation masking the new tx inside `commands[]` and masking nothing in `info`'s output but `meta`.
- [ ] Scenarios 4 and 5 show the coverage audit naming every uncovered path over `matrix::info`, an empty run reported as such, and a failing child reported as `Failed`, never as covered.
- [ ] No product code changes; `argc gate` passes; `br lint` is clean for this subtask.

title: The README final pass
description:
## How to work this bead

This bead is worked through its 4 subtasks, listed below in work order. Claim a subtask, not this bead (`br ready --parent omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4` lists the ready ones). The agent that closes the last open subtask then verifies every acceptance criterion of this bead (they are the leaf's, not any one subtask's), and closes this bead with `br close omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4 --reason "done: <evidence> · found: <ids>"`. Until this bead is closed, every bead it blocks stays blocked.

1. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4.1 README's structure, held by `tests/readme.rs`: shared Markdown helpers, and gate tests that README's contents list, internal links, command sections, every command line it shows, every repository path it names, its code map and the README headings the binary's own messages name all match the repository; plus the README fixes those tests force.
2. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4.2 README's code tables quote the binary: the error and warning tables become `omaddons robot-docs errors -v`, the exit tables `capabilities --json`'s dictionaries, the failure-mode table `doctor capabilities --json`, the volatile-keys table and the environment section their registries; every count README states is checked against the code; the corpus floor runs in the gate; "For coding agents" becomes the skill pointer and the guide's core loop, verbatim.
3. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4.3 The Appendix D walk: every README section brought to what M4 shipped, item by item, including the M3-build characterization re-run and quoted, the new Troubleshooting and FAQ entries, and the sections Appendix D does not list but M4 changed.
4. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4.4 The final pass: `rumdl` against the `c0ab5e9` baseline, the de-slopify pass over every line M4 changed, the stale-tense sweep, the test counts recomputed, the Appendix D ledger with README line numbers, and the exact flip text that H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the checkpoint and the first tag) commits; then this bead's close.

The chain is linear (1 → 2 → 3 → 4) because every subtask edits `README.md` and each builds on the one before: s2 reuses s1's helpers and test file, s3's prose edits are checked by both subtasks' tests, and s4 measures the finished text. **Size M, closed as one leaf:** H5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.5`, the vision comments) reads README after this bead as its second source of truth, so it must never see a half-reconciled README. The subtasks split the work, not the closure.

## Background

Beads this section names: A2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.2`, Registries for actions, events, env vars, features and per-source facts); A4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`, `omaddons capabilities`); A5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5`, `robot-docs schema` and `robot-docs errors`); A9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9`, A meaning and a typed `DetailSpec` for every code); B2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.2`, The guide's content); C4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4`, The run-the-fix corpus); E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, `doctor diagnose` and `explain`: runtime, run directories, the doctor envelope and its exit dictionary); E4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4`, `doctor health`, `ls`, `--robot-triage`, `capabilities` and `robot-docs`); E9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9`, The M3 build against M4 state); E10 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.10`, The old fixes point at the doctor); F8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.8`, `status` on the registry); H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, The pre-freeze contract audit); H2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.2`, The golden and the released-baseline mechanism); H3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3`, The determinism audit); H5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.5`, The vision comments); H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, The M4 checkpoint and the first tag).

`README.md` is the product contract (CLAUDE.md: "README.md is the product contract: where it answers, that is the answer"). During M4 every leaf that shipped a user-visible surface updated its own README section in the same commit (common rule 11). By the time this bead starts, some sixty leaves have edited one file of about 2,800 lines (at `c0ab5e9`), each touching only its own section, over the whole milestone. Nobody has read the whole file against the code since M3's README pass. This bead is the final consistency pass, "not the first mention" (plan §3.5). It reads README against `main` once every surface has landed. It works the plan's README checklist (Appendix D, restated in full in Technical Approach §1). It makes the code tables quote what the binary publishes, so they cannot drift. It matches every count to the code. It replaces the hand-written "For coding agents" block with a pointer to the skill and a verbatim excerpt of it. It lints and de-slops the text. Last, it prepares, for H6, the exact text of the lines that become true only when the tag exists.

It also leaves a guard behind. The plan's test plan for this leaf says "`rumdl`. The tests that read README (if any) pass", and at `c0ab5e9` no test reads README. A one-off reconciliation drifts at the next leaf that adds a code or a command, so this bead adds `tests/readme.rs` to the gate. That test holds README's generated parts (code, exit, failure-mode, volatile-key and environment tables, counts, the agent excerpt) equal to the binary and its registries. It also holds README's structure (contents, links, command coverage, command lines, repository paths, code map) true of the repository. A later README edit or code change that breaks the agreement fails the gate, and the failure prints the expected rows.

**How it serves the milestone's goals.**
- **G-M4-1, self-describing:** "Every fact in those outputs is generated from the code, so it cannot drift from what the code does." README is the human-readable copy of those outputs. After this bead, its tables quote `robot-docs errors`, `capabilities` and `doctor capabilities` instead of restating them, and a test holds them equal (M4-D2: a fact is declared once).
- **G-M4-5, frozen and enforced:** README states the freeze rule exactly as the gate enforces it: the semantic manifest, the released baseline, the bump rule in both directions, member order not being contract.
- **G-M4-6, no new risk to the engine's guarantees:** "A build from before M4 never destroys what M4 wrote: the M3 build is characterized against M4 state, and README states the result." This bead re-runs that characterization and quotes it.
- **G-M4-3 and G-M4-4:** README is where a person learns the per-target preview guarantee and its scope, and what the doctor changes and how a repair is undone. The walk checks that each is stated as the code behaves.
- **The vision's thesis** (omaddons stays the sole, safe, undoable authority over what it manages) holds only if what README promises is what the code does. **G4** ("the first command an agent guesses works"): an agent that reads README instead of the skill must meet the same commands, codes and core loop the binary describes.

**Checkpoint criteria this bead serves** (§3.2 of the plan; H6 records them):
- **18, README and vision:** "README describes exactly what exists, including the frozen contract and its rules." This bead makes that true up to the tag. H6 commits the flips that are true only after the tag, from the text this bead prepares.
- **5, intent inference, its count:** "A corpus of at least 60 wrong invocations covers: misplaced client names before and after the verb, a client name given as an addon, `-t all`, client-id typos, command, flag and value typos, `apply` for `adopt --apply`, and doctor verb typos." The plan's corpus appendix: "H4 checks that the corpus holds at least 60 rows." C4's checkpoint test does the counting; this bead runs it and puts it in the gate.
- **16, older builds against M4 state, its README part:** "README's Limitations quote the result." E9's acceptance: "The table of observations is printed and quoted in README's Known limitations by H4."
- **14, the contract is frozen, its README part:** "JSON member order is deterministic but is not compared as contract (JSON objects are unordered); reordering keys needs no version bump." README's Stability section must say so, and say how the released baseline is compared.

**The decisions README must state correctly.** This bead implements no decision of its own; it makes README describe these as the code implements them. Each is restated because the walk checks README against it:
- **M4-D2, one contract registry feeds every description of the CLI.** A fact clap cannot give is declared once, beside the command or code it describes, and verified by a test. *Rejected:* hand-maintained descriptions, which drift. For README this means: its tables quote the generated outputs; they are not a second source.
- **M4-D7, the guide, `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` and the installed skill are one artifact,** byte-identical in all three places, stamped with a content digest on the line after its frontmatter. README's agent section therefore quotes the committed `SKILL.md` verbatim and never paraphrases it.
- **M4-D8, `install-skill`** writes `SKILL.md` into the default skill directory (`<skills>`, `$HOME/.claude/skills/omaddons`), or anywhere sensible with `--dir`, and records a `skill` history line. Nothing in M4 installs the skill into the real skill directory: that is the owner's choice, made with one command.
- **M4-D21, stored plans live in `<cache>/plans/` (owner-visible):** a dry run now writes one small file under the cache. README's file table says it is safe to delete, and that previewing again recreates it.
- **M4-D56, a semantic manifest pins the contract, and every change is compared with the released baseline (owner-visible):** after the tag, an added JSON key needs a minor `schema_version` bump, and a breaking or unclassified change a major one. The comparison is with `tests/contract/released/<version>.json`, which only the release procedure advances; regenerating the current golden cannot bypass it. Member order is not contract. *Rejected:* a golden that is both the current snapshot and the baseline (it erases its own evidence when regenerated).
- **M4-D57, the first tag is `v0.1.0`, made by the checkpoint (H6).** The crate version stays `0.1.0`. *Rejected:* `v1.0.0`, because the project is pre-alpha and 1.0 implies a public stability the private repository does not offer. So README's pre-alpha badge stays at the tag.
- **M4-D58, the M3 build is characterized against M4 state,** and README's Known limitations quote what it does.
- **M4-D60 and M4-D61, the preview guarantee and its scope:** on each target, a bound run commits exactly the approved operations or none of them. A multi-target run is one transaction per target and reports each target's outcome (`committed`, `unchanged`, `stale`, `failed`); nothing calls it atomic. Other omaddons processes are serialized by the global lock and by one applier per plan (a lease). Every change to a witnessed resource made before the under-lock check is caught; after it, only the identity of what moves is re-checked. *Rejected:* promising an absolute compare-and-swap against arbitrary writers, which no filesystem primitive provides. README states this scope plainly, and the walk checks that it does.
- **M4-D55, the contract's rules held from slice 1, and H1 was the final audit.** This bead renames nothing. A non-additive change found here is a defect against H1, filed as a bug (Technical Approach §8).
- **M4-D18, determinism is enforced per command path, and volatile keys are declared** in `contract::VOLATILE` with their reasons. README's volatile-keys table quotes that registry.
- **M4-D40, the doctor dictionary:** the doctor tree has its own exit codes, and every error code maps to one. README documents both dictionaries.
- **M4-D16 and the non-goals:** completions are static, for five shells. Dynamic completion of client ids and addon names is a non-goal, and README lists it as a known limitation.
- **M4-D35, M4-D36, M4-D38, M4-D62 and M4-D54, the safety model's new parts:** quarantine never crosses a filesystem; only `doctor gc` deletes what a repair keeps, through a bound, reachability-pinned retention plan; the set-aside repairs suspend a stuck journal, and their undo reactivates it only while nothing it depends on has changed; a stuck repair fences only the resources it protects, and one whose journal cannot be read fails closed; `actions.jsonl` is group-committed, derived files are not fsynced, and directory fsyncs are deferred to explicit barriers.
- **The plan's §7.8:** M4 adds no `config.toml` key. The doctor has no configuration, by design, because `doctor capabilities` must describe one behaviour, not a configurable family.

**Facts this bead relies on** (as of `c0ab5e9`; every M4 leaf edits README, so line numbers will have moved when this bead starts: they locate the M3-era text, and the quoted words find it):
- README is 2,804 lines. Its `## Contents` list (`README.md:45-70`) has 24 entries, one per `##` section.
- **No test reads README.** In `tests/` and `src/` the word appears only in comments and in fixture strings (an archive entry named `README.md`).
- **Five runtime messages name a README heading:** "see \"journal_pending that does not clear\" under Troubleshooting in the README" (`src/app/issues.rs:106`, `:134`; `src/app/status.rs:916`; `src/engine/journal.rs:512`, `:1213`). E10 points the recovery stop errors' fixes at the doctor; whatever text remains must name a heading that exists.
- **The error table** (`README.md:1822-1869`) is a `<details>` block whose summary reads "Every error code (41)", with columns Code, Exit, Retryable and When. Its 41 rows match the 41 rows of `error_codes!` (`src/error.rs:150-204`).
- **The warning table** (`README.md:1871-1929`) has the summary "Every warning code (51)" (`:1872`) but 52 rows. `warning_codes!` (`src/error.rs:246-349`) holds 52 codes. A9's subtask 2 corrects the summary to 52; the plan's own count is 52 → 55 (§7.5).
- **The general exit table** (`README.md:1808-1818`: Exit, Name, Meaning) does not match `Exit::meaning()` (`src/error.rs:81-99`), which `help --json` publishes and `capabilities` will publish. For exit 3, README says "Target, ref, addon, backup, run, plan or transaction not found, or ambiguous", and the code says "Target, ref, addon, plan or transaction not found, or ambiguous". For exit 2, README adds "an unreadable `addons.toml` (`desired_state_invalid`)". The other rows differ in wording.
- **The Global options `--if-match` row** (`README.md:705`) names the five M3 binding commands only.
- **"Previews and `--if-match`"** is `README.md:1931-1945`. **"Stability"** is `README.md:1959-1961` and says the contract can change until the first tag (milestone 4).
- **"For coding agents"** (`README.md:2743-2798`) is a hand-written block: a core loop, refs, targets, how to read the envelope, exit codes, rules and the state directories.
- **"What works today"** (`README.md:126-162`): the intro sentence (`:128`) says milestones 1, 2 and 3 are complete; the CLI contract row (`:137`) says "✅ Done (freezes in M4)"; the M4 row (`:161`) is "`capabilities`, `doctor`, `robot-docs`, stored plans, the agent skill, the first tag | 🗓️ Milestone 4".
