### 0. Ground rules for the pass

- **Sources of truth, in order:** the code on `main` together with the close comments of the leaves (each records the decisions its leaf took, including its "Decided while writing this bead" items); then the plan's intent as this bead restates it. README is brought to the code. **The exception:** a README promise that a leaf's acceptance criteria required, and that the code does not keep, is a bug in the code, not a README edit (§8).
- **Every section belongs to the leaf that wrote it.** This pass may edit any section, but it keeps each leaf's recorded decisions. Where a section and its leaf's close comment disagree, the close comment and the code win.
- **No behaviour changes and no wire names.** This bead adds no command, flag, code, key, action, event, env var or constant, and renames nothing. The only code it changes:
  - the tests it adds or extends: `tests/readme.rs`, `tests/common/markdown.rs`, one line in `tests/common/mod.rs`, appended cases in `tests/common_selftest.rs`, and one `#[ignore]` attribute in `tests/contract/intent_corpus.rs`;
  - description texts (the meanings of error, warning and exit codes, fix patterns, detector descriptions, the guide's prose) where README's older text shows them wrong or incomplete (§3.4). Each such change is text only, listed in the close comment, gated, and followed by the `SKILL.md` regeneration and snapshot re-accepts it needs.
- **No script edits README** (CLAUDE.md "No Script-Based Changes"). When a quoted-table test fails, it prints the expected Markdown rows into the test log, and the implementer pastes them in with the editor. No `sed`, and no update-mode variable.
- **Verbatim quotes are never edited in README.** A transcript of the binary's output, and the agent excerpt, are copies. A wording problem in one is fixed at its source (the binary's text, or `src/contract/guide/guide.md` followed by the `SKILL.md` regeneration), and the copy is taken again.
- **Defaults applied** (§8.1 of the plan): prefer what exists (no new name of any kind); stable order (the quoted tables follow registry order, which is the order the binary prints); fail closed (a README line the helpers cannot parse fails the test, it is never skipped); never ask the owner (every open point below is decided, and marked).

### 2. `tests/readme.rs`, part 1: structure (subtask 1)

**Helpers** in a new `tests/common/markdown.rs` (one line, `pub mod markdown;`, in `tests/common/mod.rs`), so `tests/skill.rs` or a later suite can reuse them. If B2 already put a fence or command extractor in `tests/common/`, extend that module instead and record it. The API:

```rust
pub struct Doc { pub lines: Vec<String> }            // the file split on '\n'; reports use 1-based line numbers
pub struct Heading { pub level: u8, pub text: String, pub line: usize, pub anchor: String }
pub struct Fence { pub info: String, pub open: usize, pub body: Vec<(usize, String)> }
pub struct Table { pub line: usize, pub header: Vec<String>, pub rows: Vec<(usize, Vec<String>)> }
pub struct CommandLine { pub line: usize, pub source: String, pub argv: Vec<String> }
pub enum RepoPath { Exact(PathBuf), Glob(PathBuf), Prefix(PathBuf) }

impl Doc {
    pub fn read(path: &Path) -> Doc;
    pub fn headings(&self) -> Vec<Heading>;            // ATX headings outside fences; anchors GitHub-style, "-1", "-2" for repeats
    pub fn fences(&self) -> Vec<Fence>;                // ``` and ```` fences (and ~~~), with the info string
    pub fn unclosed_fence(&self) -> Option<usize>;     // the opening line of a fence that never closes
    pub fn section(&self, heading_text: &str) -> Option<std::ops::Range<usize>>; // to the next heading of the same or a higher level
    pub fn details(&self, summary_prefix: &str) -> Option<std::ops::Range<usize>>; // the <details> block whose <summary> text starts so
    pub fn tables(&self, range: std::ops::Range<usize>) -> Vec<Table>; // GFM tables outside fences; cells trimmed, "\|" unescaped
    pub fn prose(&self, range: std::ops::Range<usize>) -> Vec<(usize, &str)>; // the lines outside fences
    pub fn links(&self) -> Vec<(usize, String)>;       // inline link targets outside fences and code spans
}
pub fn github_slug(text: &str) -> String;              // lowercase; drop all but letters, digits, spaces, '-' and '_'; spaces to '-'
pub fn code_spans(line: &str) -> Vec<String>;          // `x` and ``x`` spans
pub fn command_lines(fence: &Fence) -> Vec<Result<CommandLine, String>>;
pub fn repo_paths(span: &str) -> Vec<RepoPath>;
```

**`command_lines` rules** (decided while writing this bead, so that every command README shows, in a form a reader would copy, is parsed):
- Fences whose info string is `bash`, `sh`, `shell` or `console`: every line is a candidate. `text` fences: only lines starting with `$ `, with the prompt removed (transcripts). Every other fence (`json`, `toml`, `markdown`, none): no commands.
- A line ending in `\` is joined with the next one.
- A `#` comment that starts at a word boundary outside quotes is removed.
- The line is split into segments at unquoted `|`, `||`, `&&` and `;`, and each segment is cut at its first unquoted `>`, `<` or `2>`. Each segment is tokenized with `shell_words::split`, and leading `NAME=value` tokens are dropped. A segment is kept when its first token is `omaddons`. So `echo "$TOKEN" | omaddons auth github set` yields `omaddons auth github set`, and `omaddons doctor health; echo $?` yields `omaddons doctor health`.
- Placeholders: a token that is exactly `<SHELL>` or `<shell>` becomes `bash`, and `<N>` or `<n>` becomes `5`. Every other token, `<id>` and `pc1:…` included, stays as it is: clap parses those as strings, and `--if-match` tokens are validated by the app, not by clap (`src/cli.rs:282-283`, `check_if_match` at `:309`).
- A line that does not tokenize (an unbalanced quote) is an `Err`, reported as a failure, never skipped.

**`repo_paths` rules:** a code span is a repository path when it starts with `src/`, `tests/`, `omarchy/`, `catalog/`, `scripts/`, `fuzz/` or `skills/`, or is exactly one of `build.rs`, `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, `deny.toml`, `rust-toolchain.toml`, `Argcfile.sh`, `clippy.toml`, `rustfmt.toml`, `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md`. A `:<line>` or `:<line>-<line>` suffix is stripped. One `{a,b,…}` group is expanded into several paths. A component holding `<…>` ends the path, and the part before it must be an existing directory (`Prefix`). A last component holding `*` or `?` must match at least one entry (`Glob`). Otherwise the path must exist (`Exact`), and a trailing `/` must be a directory. Home-relative and placeholder paths (`$HOME/…`, `<state>/…`, `Interface/AddOns`) are no repository paths.

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M4 plan, 2026-10-24).**

**Why this bead.** README is omaddons' product contract, and every M4 leaf that shipped a surface updated its own section in the same commit. Some sixty leaves editing one 2,800-line file section by section leave a document that is locally right and globally inconsistent: counts that predate the last code, a code table that paraphrases what `robot-docs errors` publishes, an agent block that duplicates (and drifts from) the skill, "planned for milestone 4" sentences in sections nobody revisited, links to renamed headings. This bead is the one reading of the whole file against `main` once every surface has landed (the plan: "H4 is the final consistency pass, not the first mention"). It works the plan's README checklist (Appendix D, 17 items), makes the tables quote the binary, matches the counts, replaces the agent block with the skill pointer and a verbatim excerpt, lints and de-slops the text, and prepares the exact flip text that H6 commits with the tag. It also leaves `tests/readme.rs` in the gate, so the agreement it establishes survives the next leaf. It serves checkpoint criterion 18 ("README describes exactly what exists, including the frozen contract and its rules"), the count of criterion 5 (the corpus holds at least 60 rows), and the README parts of criteria 14 and 16.

**Decisions applied** (this bead implements none of its own; it makes README state these as the code does):
- **M4-D2:** one registry feeds every description of the CLI, so README's code, exit, failure-mode, volatile-key and environment tables become quotations held equal by a test, not a second source.
- **M4-D7 and M4-D8:** the guide, `SKILL.md` and the installed skill are one artifact, so README quotes the core loop verbatim and points at `robot-docs install-skill` and `robot-docs guide`.
- **M4-D21 and M4-D56 (owner-visible):** README states that dry runs write a small plan file under `<cache>/plans/`, and the freeze rule: the semantic manifest, the released baseline, the bump rule in both directions, member order not contract.
- **M4-D57:** H6 makes the tag, so the lines true only after it are prepared here and committed there; the pre-alpha badge stays.
- **M4-D58:** README's Known limitations quote the M3-build characterization; this bead re-runs it so the quote describes the final M4 state.
- **M4-D60 and M4-D61:** README states the per-target guarantee and its scope, never an absolute compare-and-swap and never an atomic multi-target run.
- **M4-D55:** nothing is renamed here; a wire-name defect found here is a defect against H1, filed as a bug.
- **M4-D18, M4-D40, M4-D16, M4-D35, M4-D36, M4-D38, M4-D62, M4-D54 and the plan's §7.8:** the volatile keys, both exit dictionaries, static completions, the doctor's safety model and durability, and "no new configuration key" are each checked in the walk.
- **The plan's defaults (§8.1):** no new name of any kind, registry order in the quoted tables, fail closed on what cannot be parsed, decide rather than ask.

**Alternatives rejected.**
- **A one-off reconciliation with no test** (the plan's test plan reads "`rumdl`. The tests that read README (if any) pass", and none existed): it would drift at the next code or command. `tests/readme.rs` checks only generated content and structure, never prose, so it costs ordinary edits nothing.
- **An update mode that rewrites README's tables** (an `OMADDONS_UPDATE_README` variable): a new harness name, a generator writing a hand-edited document, and a script-shaped change CLAUDE.md forbids. The test prints the expected rows and the editor pastes them.
- **Keeping README's long "When" texts beside the quoted meanings:** two sources for one fact, which M4-D2 exists to prevent. The fact ledger moves each detail to the meaning, the `details` schema or the owning command's section instead.
- **Dropping the tables for a pointer to `robot-docs errors`:** README is also the human's contract, and a table generated from the binary costs nothing to keep true once tested.
- **Committing the flips here:** they are false until the tag exists; H6 commits them with the baseline in one gated commit (M4-D57).
- **Quoting E9's close comment instead of re-running `compat_m3`:** leaves that landed after E9 (G3 among them) can change the state it runs against.

**Risks and how they are watched.**
- **Facts lost when tables become quotations:** the per-code fact ledger in subtask 2's close comment makes every move reviewable.
- **README-only commits breaking the new test:** the test compares only generated content and structure; its failures print the rows to paste; README's Development section tells editors to run `cargo test --test readme`.
- **Promises the code does not keep, found late:** each becomes a P1 bug `discovered-from` this bead, listed in Known issues and added as a blocker of H6, so the tag cannot pass over it, while this bead closes with README honest about the code.
- **The flip text going stale before H6:** each flip carries the exact current text, so a changed line fails H6's edit loudly.
- **Plan risk #13** (the guide drifts from behaviour): README's agent section is now a tested verbatim excerpt. **Plan risk #14** (the milestone's size and critical path): this bead is on the 25-unit critical path (… → H1 → H2 → H4 → H5 → H6) with no slack; its four subtasks each land on their own.

**What it unblocks, and why that waits.** H5 (the vision comments) reconciles every M4 wire name and departure into vision comments, and its sources of truth are the leaves' close comments with the code, then README after this bead, then the plan. It must read a reconciled README. Through H5, H6 (the checkpoint and the tag) waits too, and commits this bead's flip text.

**How it serves the milestone.** G-M4-1 says every fact an agent reads is generated from the code; after this bead the human-facing copy is generated too, and tested. G-M4-5 says the contract is frozen and enforced; README now states the rule the gate enforces. G-M4-6 says README states what an older build does to M4 state; it quotes a fresh run. And the thesis, omaddons as the sole, safe, undoable authority over what it manages, holds for a reader only if README promises exactly what the code does.

title: README's structure held by tests/readme.rs: contents, links, command sections, command lines, repository paths, the code map and the headings the binary names
description:
Part 1 of 4 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4 (The README final pass). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

H4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`) is M4's README final pass. `README.md` is omaddons' product contract (CLAUDE.md: "README.md is the product contract: where it answers, that is the answer"), and during M4 some sixty leaves each edited their own section of it. H4 reads the whole file against `main` once every surface has landed. It works the plan's README checklist, makes the code tables quote the binary, matches every count to the code, replaces the agent block with the skill, lints and de-slops the text, and prepares the tag's flip text for H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the checkpoint and the first tag). It serves checkpoint criterion 18: "README describes exactly what exists, including the frozen contract and its rules."

**This part** builds the guard that keeps README true of the repository after H4: `tests/readme.rs`, in the gate, with shared Markdown helpers in `tests/common/markdown.rs`. It holds README's **structure**. The contents list matches the sections. Every internal link resolves. Every command in `app::COMMANDS` has a section or an example. Every command line README shows parses. Every repository path README names exists. The code map names every top-level `src/` entry. Every README heading that the binary's own messages name exists. This part also makes the README fixes those tests force. At `c0ab5e9` no test reads README, so nothing would notice if a leaf renamed a section that a message points at, showed a flag that does not exist, or cited a file that moved. It is its own step because subtask 2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4.2`) builds its quoted-table tests on these helpers and this file, and subtask 3's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4.3`) prose edits are then checked by both.

**Facts this part relies on** (as of `c0ab5e9`):
- No file in `tests/` or `src/` reads `README.md`; the word appears only in comments and fixture strings.
- Five runtime messages name a README heading: "see \"journal_pending that does not clear\" under Troubleshooting in the README" (`src/app/issues.rs:106`, `:134`; `src/app/status.rs:916`; `src/engine/journal.rs:512`, `:1213`). E10 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.10`, the old fixes point at the doctor) repoints the recovery stop errors at the doctor; whatever remains must name a heading that exists.
- README's `## Contents` (`README.md:45-70`) lists 24 sections. The links README uses are GitHub heading anchors, such as `#previews-and---if-match` (from "Previews and `--if-match`"), `#choosing-a-target-with--t`, `#undo-tx` and `#a-build-not-made-for-this-client---any-flavor`.
- The fences at `c0ab5e9`: 41 `bash`, 25 `text` (30 lines start with `$ omaddons`), 5 `toml`, 4 `json`. Their 135 bash command lines contain few placeholders (`<folder>`, `<ref>`, `<tx>`, `pc1:…`).
- `omaddons::cli::Cli::try_parse_from` is the parse the contract suite's `parses` helper uses (`tests/contract/main.rs:257-268`): clap's help and version displays count as parsed. `--if-match` is a plain string to clap, and its token is checked by the app after parsing (`src/cli.rs:282-283`, `check_if_match` at `:309`). `omaddons::app::COMMANDS` (`src/app/mod.rs:121`) is public, with one row per command path and its `name` field the canonical path (`targets add`).
- `shell-words` is a normal dependency (`Cargo.toml`), usable from tests. There is no `regex` crate, so the helpers scan strings by hand.
- `tests/common/mod.rs` allows dead code (`:12`), so a new helper module costs the other test binaries nothing. `tests/common_selftest.rs` holds the builders' own table-driven tests.
- The Architecture code map (`README.md:2363-2394`) omits `src/test_exec.rs`, a `#[cfg(test)]` module like the listed `src/source_scan.rs`. `src/snapshots/` holds insta snapshots and is no module.
- H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`) writes `tests/contract/released/1.0.json` in the tag commit, so that directory does not exist while H4 runs.

## Technical Approach

Beads this section names: B2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.2`, The guide's content); E10 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.10`, The old fixes point at the doctor); H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, The M4 checkpoint and the first tag).

### 1. The helpers: `tests/common/markdown.rs`

Add `pub mod markdown;` to `tests/common/mod.rs`. If B2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.2`, the guide's content) already put a fence or command extractor in `tests/common/` for `tests/skill.rs`, extend that module instead, and record it in the close comment.

```rust
pub struct Doc { pub lines: Vec<String> }            // the file split on '\n'; reports use 1-based line numbers
pub struct Heading { pub level: u8, pub text: String, pub line: usize, pub anchor: String }
pub struct Fence { pub info: String, pub open: usize, pub body: Vec<(usize, String)> }
pub struct Table { pub line: usize, pub header: Vec<String>, pub rows: Vec<(usize, Vec<String>)> }
pub struct CommandLine { pub line: usize, pub source: String, pub argv: Vec<String> }
pub enum RepoPath { Exact(PathBuf), Glob(PathBuf), Prefix(PathBuf) }

impl Doc {
    pub fn read(path: &Path) -> Doc;
    pub fn headings(&self) -> Vec<Heading>;            // ATX headings outside fences; GitHub anchors, "-1", "-2" for repeats
    pub fn fences(&self) -> Vec<Fence>;                // ``` and ```` fences (and ~~~), with the info string
    pub fn unclosed_fence(&self) -> Option<usize>;     // the opening line of a fence that never closes
    pub fn section(&self, heading_text: &str) -> Option<std::ops::Range<usize>>; // to the next heading of the same or a higher level
    pub fn details(&self, summary_prefix: &str) -> Option<std::ops::Range<usize>>; // the <details> block whose <summary> text starts so
    pub fn tables(&self, range: std::ops::Range<usize>) -> Vec<Table>; // GFM tables outside fences; cells trimmed, "\|" unescaped
    pub fn prose(&self, range: std::ops::Range<usize>) -> Vec<(usize, &str)>; // the lines outside fences
    pub fn links(&self) -> Vec<(usize, String)>;       // inline link targets outside fences and code spans
}
pub fn github_slug(text: &str) -> String;
pub fn code_spans(line: &str) -> Vec<String>;
pub fn command_lines(fence: &Fence) -> Vec<Result<CommandLine, String>>;
pub fn repo_paths(span: &str) -> Vec<RepoPath>;
```

- **`github_slug`** follows GitHub's rule: lowercase; drop every character that is not a letter, a digit, a space, `-` or `_`; turn each space into `-`. Repeated headings get `-1`, `-2`, … in document order (`headings()` assigns them).
- **`section`** runs from the heading's line to the line before the next heading of the same or a higher level. `details` finds a `<details>` line whose following `<summary>` text (tags stripped) starts with the prefix, and runs to its `</details>`.
- **`tables`** reads GFM pipe tables: the header row, the alignment row (skipped), and each following row, split on unescaped `|`, cells trimmed, `\|` turned into `|`. Tables inside fences are ignored.
- **`command_lines`** (decided while writing this bead, so that every command README shows, in a form a reader would copy, is parsed):
  - fences whose info string is `bash`, `sh`, `shell` or `console`: every line is a candidate; `text` fences: only lines starting with `$ `, with the prompt removed; any other fence (`json`, `toml`, `markdown`, none): no commands;
  - a line ending in `\` is joined with the next;
  - a `#` comment starting at a word boundary outside quotes is removed;
  - the line is split into segments at unquoted `|`, `||`, `&&` and `;`, each segment is cut at its first unquoted `>`, `<` or `2>`, tokenized with `shell_words::split`, and stripped of leading `NAME=value` tokens; a segment is kept when its first token is `omaddons` (so `echo "$TOKEN" | omaddons auth github set` gives `omaddons auth github set`);
  - placeholders: a token that is exactly `<SHELL>` or `<shell>` becomes `bash`, and `<N>` or `<n>` becomes `5`; every other token stays as it is, because clap parses `<id>` or `pc1:…` as strings;
  - a line that does not tokenize (an unbalanced quote) is an `Err` with the line number, never skipped.
- **`repo_paths`**: a code span is a repository path when it starts with `src/`, `tests/`, `omarchy/`, `catalog/`, `scripts/`, `fuzz/` or `skills/`, or is exactly one of `build.rs`, `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, `deny.toml`, `rust-toolchain.toml`, `Argcfile.sh`, `clippy.toml`, `rustfmt.toml`, `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md` or `AGENTS.md`.
  - A `:<line>` or `:<line>-<line>` suffix is stripped, and one `{a,b,…}` group expands into several paths.
  - A component holding `<…>` ends the path, and the part before it must be an existing directory (`Prefix`).
  - A last component holding `*` or `?` must match at least one entry (`Glob`, matched by hand: `*` any run, `?` one character).
  - Otherwise the path must exist (`Exact`), and a trailing `/` must be a directory.
  - Home-relative and placeholder paths (`$HOME/…`, `<state>/…`, `Interface/AddOns`) are not repository paths.

### 2. The tests: `tests/readme.rs` (new)

`mod common;` at the top, then the seven tests. Each reads `concat!(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"), "/README.md")` through `Doc::read`, opens `let log = tlog!();`, collects every failure before asserting (so one run shows all of them), and asserts that the list is empty, with the list in the message. None needs a `TestEnv`, and none runs the binary.

1. **`contents_lists_every_section_in_order`.** The items of `## Contents`, each `- [Text](#anchor)`, equal, in order, the `##` headings after it (the `#` title and "Contents" itself excluded): the same texts, and anchors equal to the headings' anchors.
2. **`every_internal_link_resolves`.** Every link whose target starts with `#` names an anchor of `headings()`. Links to other files and URLs are not checked here.
3. **`every_command_has_a_section`.** For each row of `omaddons::app::COMMANDS`:
   - its top-level word starts a code span in a `###` heading inside `## Command reference` (the one heading for `pin <ADDON>` and `unpin <ADDON>` covers both words);
   - a nested path (two or more words) is covered by a `###` or `####` heading whose code span starts with the path, or by a command line in a fence inside its top-level command's section whose words after `omaddons` start with the path;
   - these paths need a heading (the plan's Appendix D item 5: "new sections for `capabilities`, `robot-docs`, `apply`, `plans show`, `doctor` (each verb), `completions`"): `capabilities`, `robot-docs`, `apply`, `plans show`, `completions`, `doctor`, and every path that starts with `doctor `.

   Decided while writing this bead: a usage example suffices for the other nested paths, as README documented `targets add` or `config get` at `c0ab5e9`.
4. **`readme_commands_parse`.** Every `Ok` from `command_lines`, over every fence, parses with `omaddons::cli::Cli::try_parse_from`, counting clap's `DisplayHelp` and `DisplayVersion` as parsed. Every `Err` is a failure. The exceptions are on `INTENTIONALLY_WRONG: &[&str]`, the exact source text of each line README shows as a mistake on purpose: a misplaced client (`omaddons retail update`), a flag the doctor does not have (`omaddons doctor --fix`), a typo shown with its fix. Each entry must occur in README and must fail to parse, so the list cannot go stale. Keep it as short as README needs; each entry has a comment naming the README section that shows it.
5. **`repository_paths_named_in_readme_exist`.** Every repository path in a code span outside fences, table cells included, holds by its rule. One exception: a path under `tests/contract/released/` may be absent while that directory does not exist, because H6 writes the first released baseline with the tag. Decided while writing this bead, so that H6 need not edit a test in its tag commit.
6. **`code_map_names_every_top_level_module`.** Every top-level entry of `src/` (each `*.rs` file and each directory), except `src/snapshots/`, is named in the Path column of the first table under `## Architecture`: as itself (`src/x.rs`, `src/x/`), or through a path inside it (`src/toc/loaded.rs` names `src/toc/`).
7. **`readme_headings_named_by_the_binary_exist`.** Walk `src/**/*.rs` with `std::fs::read_dir` (no extra crate). For each occurrence of ` in the README` inside a string literal of the form `\"<heading>\" under <Section> in the README`, a heading whose text equals `<heading>` (with code spans' backticks removed) must exist inside the `## <Section>` section. Log how many references were found; zero is a pass, since E10 may have repointed them all.

### 3. The README fixes these tests force

Run the seven tests against README as the M4 leaves left it, and fix README until they pass:
- **Contents:** add or rename entries for any `##` section a leaf added or renamed.
- **Links:** repoint each broken anchor (a leaf renamed a heading, for example "Previews and `--if-match`" rewritten to cover plans) at the heading's new anchor.
- **Command sections:** a missing section or example is written in the leaf's style (synopsis, a `bash` block of examples, what it prints, its errors). It is drawn from the command's `--help`, its leaf's close comment and its contract snapshots, never invented.
- **Command lines:** a line that does not parse is corrected to the command's real syntax, or, if README shows it as a mistake on purpose, added to `INTENTIONALLY_WRONG` with its comment.
- **Repository paths:** a moved or renamed file is corrected.
- **Code map:** add `src/test_exec.rs` ("Test-only: scripts a test writes and runs from a child process, so no descriptor of the test process holds them while they run") and a row for each M4 module a leaf did not add (`src/contract/`, `src/doctor/`, `src/vocabulary.rs`, and any other new top-level entry).
- **Headings named by the binary:** if a message names a heading that no longer exists, restore the heading text in README. Runtime messages are the contract's, and README follows them.

List every fix in the close comment as `README.md:<line>: <before> → <after>`, and why. A fix that would change what README promises (not just its form) belongs to subtask 3's walk; here, change only what the tests require.

### 4. What not to do

- No script edits README; every fix is made by hand in the editor (CLAUDE.md "No Script-Based Changes").
- The tests check structure only, never prose wording, so ordinary edits do not trip them.
- Do not change any code outside `tests/` in this part.
- Do not add an update-mode environment variable: a failing test lists what to fix.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `tests/common/markdown.rs` exists with the helpers above (declared in `tests/common/mod.rs`), and their table-driven tests in `tests/common_selftest.rs` pass.
- [ ] `tests/readme.rs` holds the seven tests (`contents_lists_every_section_in_order`, `every_internal_link_resolves`, `every_command_has_a_section`, `readme_commands_parse`, `repository_paths_named_in_readme_exist`, `code_map_names_every_top_level_module`, `readme_headings_named_by_the_binary_exist`), each using T1's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs) `TestLog`, and all pass on `main`.
- [ ] Each test fails on a planted defect, checked once by hand and recorded in the close comment (not committed): a renamed `##` heading (tests 1 and 2), a removed command section (3), a misspelled flag in a `bash` block (4), a renamed test file named in the Tests table (5), a new empty `src/x.rs` (6), a changed Troubleshooting heading (7).
- [ ] `INTENTIONALLY_WRONG` holds only lines that occur in README and fail to parse, each commented with its section.
- [ ] README's code map names `src/test_exec.rs` and every M4 module, and every README fix these tests forced is listed in the close comment (line, before → after, why).
- [ ] `argc gate` passes, and `ubs` is clean on the changed files.
- [ ] The close comment states that no wire name, code, key, env var or constant was added or changed, and confirms or adjusts each "Decided while writing this bead" item of this part.

## Test Plan

Beads this section names: T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, Structured test logs, and the `argc e2e` runner).

### Unit tests

In `tests/common_selftest.rs`, table-driven, one name per case. Each assertion message names the case and shows the input, the expected and the actual value.
- `markdown_headings_cases`: `atx_levels` (`# A`, `## B`, `### C` give levels 1, 2, 3); `heading_inside_fence_ignored`; `closing_hashes_stripped` (`## A ##` gives `A`); `code_span_kept_in_text`.
- `markdown_fences_cases`: `three_backticks_with_info` (`bash`); `four_backticks_holding_three` (the inner fence is body); `tilde_fence`; `unclosed_fence_reported` (`unclosed_fence()` gives the opening line).
- `github_slug_cases`, from real README headings: `plain` ("Quick start" → `quick-start`); `code_span_flag` ("Previews and `--if-match`" → `previews-and---if-match`); `short_flag` ("Choosing a target with `-t`" → `choosing-a-target-with--t`); `colon_and_commas` ("Concepts: targets, families and load rules" → `concepts-targets-families-and-load-rules`); `parentheses` ("Milestone checkpoints (not part of the gate)" → `milestone-checkpoints-not-part-of-the-gate`); `brackets_and_dots` ("`install <REF>...`" → `install-ref`); `underscore_kept` ("`journal_pending` that does not clear" → `journal_pending-that-does-not-clear`); `repeat_suffix` (two "Tests" headings give `tests` and `tests-1`).
- `table_rows_cases`: `simple`; `escaped_pipe` (`json\|human` → `json|human`); `alignment_row_skipped`; `cells_trimmed`; `table_inside_fence_ignored`.
- `code_spans_cases`: `one_span`; `double_backtick_span` (a span holding a backtick); `no_span`.
- `command_lines_cases`: `bash_line`; `comment_stripped` (`omaddons status            # every client` → `omaddons status`); `hash_inside_quotes_kept` (`--reason "a # b"`); `continuation_joined`; `pipe_cut` (`omaddons capabilities --json | jq .`); `redirect_cut` (`omaddons completions bash > file`); `env_prefix_dropped` (`OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1 omaddons status`); `pipe_into_omaddons` (`echo "$TOKEN" | omaddons auth github set`); `text_prompt_line` (`$ omaddons status`); `text_output_line_ignored` (`omaddons doctor · 6 clients` without a prompt); `not_omaddons` (`cargo install --locked --path .` gives nothing); `shell_placeholder` (`omaddons completions <SHELL>` → `bash`); `semicolon_cut` (`omaddons doctor health; echo $?`); `unbalanced_quote_is_err`.
- `repo_paths_cases`: `file`; `directory_with_slash`; `glob` (`tests/discover_*.rs`); `braces` (`src/app/{update,sync}.rs` gives two paths); `placeholder` (`tests/fixtures/http/<scenario>/` gives the prefix `tests/fixtures/http/`); `line_suffix` (`tests/contract/special.rs:251`); `not_a_repo_path` (`$HOME/.cache/omaddons/`, `<state>/journal/`, `Interface/AddOns` give nothing).

### Integration and end-to-end tests

`tests/readme.rs`, the seven tests of Technical Approach §2. They read the repository only (README, `src/`, `fuzz/`, the clap tree through the library), so they need no `TestEnv` and run no command; each finishes in well under a second. The planted-defect checks of the acceptance criteria are done by hand once, then reverted.

### Logging

- Each test opens `let log = tlog!();` with these steps:
  - `read README`: `log.json("headings", …)` of every heading with its line, level and anchor;
  - `collect`: `log.json` of what the test checks, such as the Contents items, every link, every command line with its line, source, argv and verdict, every repository path, each `COMMANDS` path and how it is covered (the heading line or the example line), or the messages that name README headings;
  - `compare`: `log.json("failures", …)`.
- A failing assertion prints every failure with its README line and both values (expected and found), and T1's guard prints `test log: <path>` and the last 20 steps. `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG=verbose cargo test --test readme -- --nocapture` echoes the steps live.
- Unit-test messages name the case and show the input, the expected and the actual value.

## Considerations

- **A README-only commit can now break the gate.** CLAUDE.md lets commits that touch only README skip the gate. These tests check structure, not wording, so ordinary prose edits never trip them. Subtask 3 adds a sentence to README's Development section saying that `cargo test --test readme` checks README and should be run after editing it.
- **Brittleness.** The helpers parse only the constructs README uses (ATX headings, GFM tables, fenced blocks, inline links). Anything they cannot parse, such as an unclosed fence or an untokenizable line, fails closed with its line number, rather than being skipped.
- **`INTENTIONALLY_WRONG` must stay honest.** Every entry must occur and must fail, so a corrected example or a removed one fails the test until the list follows.
- **Hot spots:** `README.md` (everyone; H4 reconciles: at this point only H5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.5`, the vision comments) and H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`) remain, and neither edits README before H6's flips; rebase onto any reopened leaf's or bug fix's change, never revert it); `tests/common/mod.rs` (one line); `tests/common_selftest.rs` (append only).
- **Privacy:** the tests read only the repository; README's examples use synthetic names.
- **Defaults applied** (§8.1 of the plan): no new name of any kind; fail closed on what cannot be parsed; decide and record.
- **Decided while writing this bead** (confirm or adjust in the close comment): the helpers' module and API; the command-line extraction rules and the two placeholder substitutions; the `INTENTIONALLY_WRONG` mechanism; the coverage rule (headings for Appendix D's new commands and every doctor verb, examples for the rest); the repository-path rules and the released-baseline exception; the code map rule with only `src/snapshots/` exempt; no update-mode variable.

## Dependencies

- **Parent:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4 (The README final pass), under the H epic omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8. The parent's blockers (every surface leaf, the golden and determinism audits, and the three slice-demo suites) have all closed before this part can start.
- **Before it:** nothing; this is the first part.
- **After it:** subtask 2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4.2`, the quoted tables, the counts and the agent section) reuses these helpers and extends `tests/readme.rs`, so it waits for this commit. Subtasks 3 and 4 follow it.
- **T1** (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs and the `argc e2e` runner) provides `tlog!()` and `TestLog`; the filing step adds its edge to this part.
- **Related:** B2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.2`) may already hold a fence extractor in `tests/common/`, to extend rather than duplicate. E10 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.10`) changed the messages test 7 checks. H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`) writes the released baseline that test 5 exempts until it exists.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] `tests/common/markdown.rs` exists with the helpers above (declared in `tests/common/mod.rs`), and their table-driven tests in `tests/common_selftest.rs` pass.
- [ ] `tests/readme.rs` holds the seven tests (`contents_lists_every_section_in_order`, `every_internal_link_resolves`, `every_command_has_a_section`, `readme_commands_parse`, `repository_paths_named_in_readme_exist`, `code_map_names_every_top_level_module`, `readme_headings_named_by_the_binary_exist`), each using T1's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs) `TestLog`, and all pass on `main`.
- [ ] Each test fails on a planted defect, checked once by hand and recorded in the close comment (not committed): a renamed `##` heading (tests 1 and 2), a removed command section (3), a misspelled flag in a `bash` block (4), a renamed test file named in the Tests table (5), a new empty `src/x.rs` (6), a changed Troubleshooting heading (7).
- [ ] `INTENTIONALLY_WRONG` holds only lines that occur in README and fail to parse, each commented with its section.
- [ ] README's code map names `src/test_exec.rs` and every M4 module, and every README fix these tests forced is listed in the close comment (line, before → after, why).
- [ ] `argc gate` passes, and `ubs` is clean on the changed files.
- [ ] The close comment states that no wire name, code, key, env var or constant was added or changed, and confirms or adjusts each "Decided while writing this bead" item of this part.

description:
Part 2 of 4 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4 (The README final pass). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says. ## Background Beads this section names: A2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.2`, Registries for actions, events, env vars, features and per-source facts); A4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`, `omaddons capabilities`); A5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5`, `robot-docs schema` and `robot-docs errors`); A9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9`, A meaning and a typed `DetailSpec` for every code); B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`, The guide renderer and `robot-docs guide`); B2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.2`, The guide's content); C2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.2`, A client named as an addon, and `-t all`); C4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4`, The run-the-fix corpus); D4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`, The plan store); E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, `doctor diagnose` and `explain`: runtime, run directories, the doctor envelope and its exit dictionary); E4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4`, `doctor health`, `ls`, `--robot-triage`, `capabilities` and `robot-docs`); E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`, `doctor fix`); F2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.2`, Journal fixers: the delegation and the set-aside as suspension); F8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.8`, `status` on the registry); G3 (`omad-7ccp`, Group commit, derived writes and deferred directory fsyncs (`omad-7ccp`)); H2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.2`, The golden and the released-baseline mechanism); H3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3`, The determinism audit); H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, The M4 checkpoint and the first tag); T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, Structured test logs, and the `argc e2e` runner). H4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`) is M4's README final pass. `README.md` is omaddons' product contract, and during M4 each leaf edited only its own section. H4 reads the whole file against `main` once every surface has landed, and makes it describe exactly what exists (checkpoint criterion 18: "README describes exactly what exists, including the frozen contract and its rules"). **This part** turns README's code tables from copies into quotations, and holds them with tests in `tests/readme.rs` (which subtask 1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4.1`, created with its Markdown helpers). The tables quoted: - the error and warning tables quote `omaddons robot-docs errors -v`; - the general and doctor exit tables quote `capabilities --json`'s exit dictionaries; - the doctor's failure-mode table quotes `doctor capabilities --json`; - the volatile-keys table and the environment section quote their registries; - the Global options `--if-match` row and the storable-commands sentence quote the per-command facts. It also checks every count README states against the code. It runs C4's corpus-floor test for criterion 5 ("at least 60 rows") and moves it into the gate. And it replaces the hand-written "For coding agents" block with the skill pointer and the guide's core loop, verbatim. The reason is the plan's decision **M4-D2: one contract registry feeds every description of the CLI**. A fact clap cannot give is declared once, beside the command or code it describes, and verified by a test, never written twice. *Rejected:* hand-maintained descriptions, which drift. A9 wrote each code's one-sentence `meaning` "from README's tables, which become the derived copy (H4 checks them)", and the plan says "README's code tables then quote `robot-docs errors`; H4 checks they agree". The guide is the same: **M4-D7** makes the guide, `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` and the installed skill one byte-identical artifact, so README quotes it rather than paraphrasing it. It is its own step because it is the one part that may touch code, namely description texts the comparison shows wrong (§6), and so needs the full gate. Subtask 3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4.3`) then walks the prose against tables that are already settled. **Facts this part relies on** (as of `c0ab5e9`, the README lines located by their M3-era text): - **The error table** (`README.md:1822-1869`): a `
` block whose summary reads "Every error code (41)", with columns Code, Exit, Retryable and When (the "When" cells are long: situations, `details` keys and `reason` values). Its 41 rows match `error_codes!` (`src/error.rs:150-204`). E3 added `online_required` and `doctor_refused` (forecast 43). - **The warning table** (`README.md:1871-1929`): summary "Every warning code (51)" over 52 rows; `warning_codes!` (`src/error.rs:246-349`) has 52. A9 corrected the count to 52; D4, C2 and F2 added `plan_not_stored`, `target_id_reserved` and `delegated_recovery` (forecast 55). - **`robot-docs errors`** (A5, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5`): `--json` gives `{error_codes: [{code, exit, doctor_exit, retryable, meaning, details_schema, fix_pattern}], warning_codes: [{code, meaning, fix_pattern}]}`, in registry order; `retryable` is `true`, `false` or `"conditional"` (for the codes whose instances decide: `plan_stale`, `http_status`, `hash_mismatch`, and, as A5 decided, `network` and `io`). Its human form is a table under "Error codes (N)" (`CODE`, `EXIT`, `DOCTOR`, `RETRYABLE` as `yes`/`no`/`conditional`, `MEANING`) and "Warning codes (N)", and `-v` adds each row's `fix: ` line. `doctor_exit` comes from E3's `doctor::exit_for`, wired by whichever of A5 and E3 landed second. - **The general exit table** (`README.md:1808-1818`: Exit, Name, Meaning) differs from `Exit::meaning()` (`src/error.rs:81-99`), which `help --json` publishes, and `capabilities` publishes as `exit_codes.general: [{code, name, meaning, retryable}]` (A4, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`). The doctor dictionary is `exit_codes.doctor: [{code, name, meaning}]`. For exit 3, README says "Target, ref, addon, backup, run, plan or transaction not found, or ambiguous", and the code says "Target, ref, addon, plan or transaction not found, or ambiguous". For exit 2, README adds "an unreadable `addons.toml` (`desired_state_invalid`)". - **`doctor capabilities --json`** (E4, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4`) is the doctor's report shape, with its keys at the top level of the envelope rather than under `data` (M4-D34). It carries: - `detectors: [{id, subsystem, severity, description, tier, estimated_cost_ms, online_required, requires, depends_on}]`, every failure-mode id exactly once in registry order, the two runtime-raised modes (`fm-state_files-detector-crashed`, `fm-state_files-check-incomplete`) included with `tier: "runtime"`; - `fixers: [{id, preconditions, writes_to, ops, reversible, idempotent, cardinality, enabled, needs_force, estimated_cost_ms}]`; - `manual_remediations: [{id, instruction, reason}]`; - `exit_codes` (code to name). No `fm-test-` id appears unless `OMADDONS_TEST_FIXERS=1` is set in a debug build. `capabilities --json`'s `failure_modes.count` equals the registry's size (forecast 46). - **The doctor's failure-mode table** was created by E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`) under `### doctor`, extended by each F leaf (common rule 19: every failure mode has "its row in README's doctor table"), and given a status column by F8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.8`). The status values follow the plan's catalog: `C` (the `cached` tier, which `status --cached` runs), `Q` (`quick`, which plain `status` adds), `—` (neither), sometimes with "(machine)". One exception: `fm-configs-config-parse-error` reads "refuses", because F8 decided that `status` refuses a broken `config.toml` with the same path, line and column the finding cites. - **`contract::VOLATILE`** (E3 started it, H3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3`, completed it) declares every key whose value changes between identical runs, with its reason (M4-D18), for example `meta.*`, `data.**.duration_ms`, `data.**.plan_id` and the doctor's `run_id`. README has a table of them under the JSON contract. - **`contract::env::ENV_VARS`** (A2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.2`) registers every environment variable the code reads, with a kind (`release`, `debug`, `harness`), held complete by a source scan. README's "Environment variables" (`README.md:2251-2265`) is a table of the release ones plus a paragraph of the debug and harness ones. T1 registered `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG` (harness); H2 `OMADDONS_UPDATE_WIRE_NAMES` and `OMADDONS_ADVANCE_RELEASED_BASELINE` (harness); B1 `OMADDONS_UPDATE_SKILL`; E6 `OMADDONS_TEST_FIXERS`. - **The Global options `--if-match` row** (`README.md:705`) names only the five M3 binding commands. `capabilities --json` gives each command's `binds` and `stores_plan`. The plan's storable set is eleven: `install`, `update`, `pin`, `unpin`, `adopt`, `sync`, `copy`, `remove`, `undo`, `backup restore`, `backup prune` (M4-D22); the binding set is those plus `errors dismiss`, `doctor fix` and `doctor gc`. - **Counts in README at `c0ab5e9`:** "All 34 engine failpoints" (`README.md:2626`); "There are 20 cargo-fuzz targets", with the list (`:2659`). `fuzz/fuzz_targets/` holds 20 files. `engine::FAILPOINTS` (`src/engine/tx.rs:78-113`, re-exported at `src/engine/mod.rs:21`) holds 34. The plan forecasts 21 fuzz targets (the new `journal` target), 11 doctor failpoints (`doctor::FAILPOINTS`) and fsx's new `fsx.barrier.sync` (G3). - **The corpus** (C4, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4`): `tests/contract/intent_corpus.rs` has `the_corpus_meets_checkpoint_criterion_5`, `#[ignore = "checkpoint: H4 and H6 run it once every M4 surface has landed"]`. It asserts at least 60 rows, an empty `PENDING` list and a row in every category of criterion 5, prints the count per kind, and reads only the repository. Criterion 5: "A corpus of at least 60 wrong invocations covers: misplaced client names before and after the verb, a client name given as an addon, `-t all`, client-id typos, command, flag and value typos, `apply` for `adopt --apply`, and doctor verb typos." - **"For coding agents"** (`README.md:2743-2798`) is a hand-written block that starts "omaddons: WoW addon manager for Linux. One JSON envelope per command, typed errors with fixes as argv." The guide (B2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.2`) opens its body with `## The core loop`. Per the plan's outline, step 4 is the reconcile step: "Lost an `apply`'s output? `omaddons plans show --json` says whether it committed, before you preview or change anything again." `tests/skill.rs::skill_md_is_the_guide` holds `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` byte-identical to `omaddons robot-docs guide`. ## Technical Approach Beads this section names: A3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`, Schemas with the serialize contract, declared `details`, and live validation); A5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5`, `robot-docs schema` and `robot-docs errors`); A9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9`, A meaning and a typed `DetailSpec` for every code); C4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4`, The run-the-fix corpus); D2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2`, `--if-match` on `install`, `update`, `sync` and `copy`); D9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.9`, `omaddons plans show`); E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, `doctor diagnose` and `explain`: runtime, run directories, the doctor envelope and its exit dictionary); H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, The pre-freeze contract audit); H3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3`, The determinism audit); H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, The M4 checkpoint and the first tag). All edits are by hand (CLAUDE.md "No Script-Based Changes"). Each quoted-table test, on failure, writes the whole expected Markdown table into the test log (a `log.note` in step `expected`) to be pasted in with the editor. No update-mode variable is added. ### 1. The error and warning tables quote `robot-docs errors -v` Decided while writing this bead: the tables are the `-v` human form as Markdown, because that form is what A5 built for people (the table plus each code's fix pattern). Under "### Exit codes", one sentence before them: "`omaddons robot-docs errors -v` prints these tables from the binary; `--json` adds each error code's `details` schema." ```markdown
Every error code (43) | Code | Exit | Doctor exit | Retryable | Meaning | Fix | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | `usage` | 2 | 64 | no | The command line was not accepted: … | the corrected command line when a correction is close, else `omaddons help ` |
``` - Rows in `error_codes` order. `Code` is a code span. `Exit` and `Doctor exit` are the integers. `Retryable` is `yes`, `no` or `conditional`, from `true`, `false` or `"conditional"`. `Meaning` and `Fix` are `meaning` and `fix_pattern` verbatim, with `|` escaped as `\|`. The summary's number is `error_codes.len()`. - The warning table: `Every warning code (N)`, columns `| Code | Meaning | Fix |`, in `warning_codes` order. - If `doctor_exit` is missing from the JSON, A5's and E3's "whichever lands second" wiring was not done: file a bug (§7) and leave the column out until it lands. - The paragraph **"Declared `details`"** sits beside the tables (A9 or A3 may have written it; verify or write it). Every error's `details` is typed by its code's specification. `omaddons robot-docs errors --json` gives each code's `details_schema`: keys, value types, required or optional, nullable, and the closed sets of `reason` and `changed`. The contract suite validates every observed `details` against it. A consumer tolerates keys and values it does not know, because additions arrive in minor versions. ### 2. The fact ledger: nothing in the old cells is lost The old "When" (errors) and "Meaning" (warnings) cells hold more than the one-sentence meanings. Before replacing each table, list every fact each cell states: the situations that raise the code, its `details` keys and `reason` or `changed` values, its retry behaviour and its fix. Then record where each fact lives afterwards: - `m`: the code's meaning or fix pattern, now in the table; - `d`: its `details_schema`, published by `robot-docs errors --json` and `capabilities --json`; - `s()`: a README command section or Troubleshooting entry that says it, or now says it; - `x()`: not true of the code, so dropped. If a leaf's acceptance criteria required it, it is a bug instead (§7). A fact without a home gets one: a sentence in the section of the command that raises the code, or a corrected meaning when the meaning itself is wrong or incomplete (§6). The ledger goes in this part's close comment, one line per code: `code: fact → m | d | s() | x()`. Example (`desired_state_invalid` at `c0ab5e9`): - "addons.toml cannot be read: broken TOML, a bad value, an unknown family, an entry listed twice, a newer schema" → `m`; - "`details: {path, line, key, reason}`" → `d`; - "`export --write` refuses a file edited since it was written (`reason: "edited"`) or an empty export (`reason: "empty"`)" → `d`, plus `s(...)` for the `export` section; - "`sync --prune` refuses a section for no known client" → `s(...)` for the `sync [FILE]` section. ### 3. The other quoted tables and lists - **Exit tables.** The general table, `| Exit | Name | Meaning |`, quotes `capabilities --json`'s `exit_codes.general` (`code`, `name`, `meaning`) in order. The doctor dictionary's table (E3 wrote it, with the doctor envelope) quotes `exit_codes.doctor` the same way. README's extra explanations stay as prose below the tables: exit 6 keeps `data`; a panic is one `internal` envelope with exit 1, never Rust's 101 (74 in the doctor tree). Decided while writing this bead: the exit tables quote too, although the plan's checklist only says "both exit dictionaries", for M4-D2's reason. Where README's older text was truer than the code's (exit 3's backups and runs, exit 2's `desired_state_invalid`), correct the code's text (§6). - **The failure-mode table** quotes `doctor capabilities --json`'s `detectors[]`. Decided while writing this bead: it moves inside `
Every failure mode (N)`, like the code tables, with columns `| Id | Severity | Tier | Status | Description | Repair |`, in `detectors[]` order: - `Id` (a code span), `Severity`, `Tier` and `Description` are `id`, `severity`, `tier` and `description`, verbatim. - `Status` starts with `C` for tier `cached` and `Q` for `quick`, and is `—` for any other tier, optionally followed by ` (machine)`. Exceptions: `fm-configs-config-parse-error` reads "refuses: `status` fails with the line and column"; the two `runtime` rows take `C`, `Q` or `—` as README explains (they are raised for whichever check stopped), and the test only checks that their cell is one of those. - `Repair`: an id in `fixers[]` names `omaddons doctor fix --only `, adds ` --force --yes` exactly when `needs_force`, and says "(off by default)" exactly when `enabled` is false; it may add a short clause ("delegates to the engine's recovery", "backs up, then rewrites"). An id with no fixer never names `doctor fix`; when `manual_remediations[]` has an entry for it, the cell is that `instruction`, verbatim. - N equals `detectors.len()` and `capabilities --json`'s `failure_modes.count`. - **Volatile keys:** the `| Key pattern | Reason |` table equals `contract::VOLATILE`'s entries in registry order, read through the library (`omaddons::contract::VOLATILE`, or the path H3 gave it). - **Environment section:** the set of variable names in "### Environment variables" (code spans matching `[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*`, optionally followed by `=…`, which is stripped) equals the names in `omaddons::contract::env::ENV_VARS`. Release-kind names appear in the table, debug-kind and harness-kind names only in the prose after it. A name the section mentions that omaddons does not read itself (for example `PATH`, which a spawned process uses) goes on a `MENTIONED_ONLY` list in the test, each entry with its reason. - **Binding and storing:** - The Global options `--if-match` row names, as code spans, exactly the paths `capabilities --json` marks `binds: true`. - "Previews, plans and `--if-match`" (whatever D2–D9 titled the rewritten section) names exactly the paths marked `stores_plan: true`, in one sentence that begins "These commands store a plan:". Decided while writing this bead, as the test's marker. ### 4. The counts Rule, decided while writing this bead: a number README states about the code is either one the test checks, or it is replaced by "every" and a link to the table that lists them. `counts_named_in_readme_match_the_code` scans the prose lines (outside fences; numbers with a thousands comma read as numbers) for a number followed by one of these phrases, plus the three `` lines: | Phrase | Must equal | Forecast | |---|---|---| | "error code(s)", "Every error code (N)" | `omaddons::error::ErrorCode::ALL.len()` | 43 | | "warning code(s)", "Every warning code (N)" | `omaddons::error::WarningCode::ALL.len()` | 55 | | "failure mode(s)", "Every failure mode (N)" | `capabilities --json` `failure_modes.count` | 46 | | "cargo-fuzz target(s)", "fuzz target(s)" | the `*.rs` files in `fuzz/fuzz_targets/` | 21 | | "engine failpoint(s)" | `omaddons::engine::FAILPOINTS.len()` | 34 | | "doctor failpoint(s)" | `omaddons::doctor::FAILPOINTS.len()` | 11 | | "command path(s)" | `omaddons::app::COMMANDS.len()` | about 62 | - The fuzzing sentence also names, as code spans in sorted order, exactly the stems of `fuzz/fuzz_targets/*.rs`. - README names `fsx.barrier.sync` in the durability or crash suite's row. - Numbers written as words are not scanned; subtask 4's sweep catches them. - A count that differs from the forecast is not by itself a defect: README follows the code. If no leaf's close comment explains the difference, it is a bug (§7). ### 5. The corpus floor Run `cargo test --test contract intent_corpus::the_corpus_meets_checkpoint_criterion_5 -- --ignored --exact` and record its output (the count per kind) in the close comment. Then remove its `#[ignore]` attribute and update its doc comment ("runs in the gate since H4: every M4 surface has landed"). Decided while writing this bead: C4 ignored it only until every M4 surface had landed, and this bead is blocked by every surface leaf, so in the gate it now stops a later edit from dropping rows below the floor unnoticed. README's sentence about the corpus says "at least 60" or gives no number, because the corpus lives in another test binary. ### 6. Description texts corrected in code When the ledger or a comparison shows that the code's text is wrong or incomplete (README's older text was true of the code, and the text dropped or misstated it), correct it in place in this commit: - a `meaning` in `error_codes!` or `warning_codes!` (`src/error.rs`); - a fix pattern (A5's `src/error/fix_pattern.rs`); - `Exit::meaning()` (`src/error.rs:81-99` at `c0ab5e9`), or the doctor's exit meanings (E3); - a detector's description (`src/doctor/registry.rs`). Change text only: no code, exit, retryability, key, id or order. Then: - run A9's meaning style test (one sentence, ending with a period) and A5's fix-pattern style test; - regenerate `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` with `OMADDONS_UPDATE_SKILL=1 cargo test --test skill` when the guide's generated tables show the text (common rule 17); - re-accept every snapshot that holds the text (`help --json`, `capabilities`, `robot-docs errors`, `doctor capabilities`), after reviewing that the diff is only that text; - if the semantic manifest records the text, regenerate the current golden with `OMADDONS_UPDATE_WIRE_NAMES=1 cargo test --test contract wire_names`. No released baseline exists before H6's tag, so only the comparison with the current golden runs. List every change in the close comment, before → after. None is a wire name. ### 7. Mismatches - README wrong, code right (as its leaf decided): fix README. - The code breaking a promise a leaf's acceptance criteria required: `br create "…" --type bug --priority 1 --deps discovered-from:omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4.2`, naming the leaf, the README text and the code location; list it under README's "Known issues" with its id; `br dep add omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6 `, so the tag waits for it. This part does not wait for the fix. - A wire-name inconsistency: never renamed here (M4-D55: after H1, a non-additive change is a defect against H1); file it the same way. ### 8. "For coding agents" Replace the block. Keep the heading `## For coding agents` and its Contents entry (the FAQ links to it): `````markdown ## For coding agents Install the skill: `omaddons robot-docs install-skill`. Read it: `omaddons robot-docs guide`. ````markdown ## The core loop ```` ````` - The excerpt runs from the line `## The core loop` of `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` up to, not including, the next line that starts with `## `, with trailing blank lines removed. - It sits in a fence with info string `markdown`, so its heading is not a README heading. The outer fence has four backticks when the excerpt holds a three-backtick line, and three otherwise. - A slop or wording problem in the excerpt is fixed in `src/contract/guide/guide.md`, then `SKILL.md` is regenerated and the excerpt re-copied; the copy is never edited in place. - If the core loop lacks the reconcile step (`plans show` before anything else), that is a bug against B2 (§7), never a README paraphrase. ### 9. Files `tests/readme.rs` (the tests below), `tests/common/markdown.rs` (helper additions, if any), `tests/contract/intent_corpus.rs` (one attribute and its doc comment), `README.md` (the tables, the declared-details paragraph, the counts, the agent section, the facts the ledger moves), and only where §6 applies: `src/error.rs`, `src/error/fix_pattern.rs`, the doctor's exit and registry texts, `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md`, the affected snapshots and the current golden. ## Acceptance Criteria - [ ] README's error and warning tables equal `omaddons robot-docs errors -v` as Markdown tables (registry order; Code, Exit, Doctor exit, Retryable, Meaning, Fix; Code, Meaning, Fix), with summaries "Every error code (N)" and "Every warning code (N)" carrying the lists' lengths, and the sentence saying they are generated; the "Declared `details`" paragraph states the rule. - [ ] The close comment carries the fact ledger, one line per error and warning code, and every fact with no home in the table, the `details` schema or a README section was given one or recorded as untrue of the code. - [ ] Both exit tables quote `capabilities --json`'s `exit_codes`, with README's extra explanations kept as prose. - [ ] The failure-mode table quotes `doctor capabilities --json`'s `detectors[]` inside "Every failure mode (N)", with the Status and Repair rules, and N equals `failure_modes.count`. - [ ] The volatile-keys table equals `contract::VOLATILE`; the environment section names exactly `ENV_VARS` (release in the table, the rest in the prose, `MENTIONED_ONLY` aside); the `--if-match` row and the "These commands store a plan:" sentence name exactly the `binds` and `stores_plan` paths. - [ ] Every count README states is checked by `counts_named_in_readme_match_the_code` and matches the code; the fuzz list names exactly the targets; README names `fsx.barrier.sync`. - [ ] `the_corpus_meets_checkpoint_criterion_5` passed under `--ignored --exact` (output in the close comment), and runs in the gate without `#[ignore]`. - [ ] "For coding agents" holds the pointer line and the guide's core loop verbatim, reconcile step included, and the old block is gone. - [ ] All nine tests of this part pass, each using T1's (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`) `TestLog`; each fails on a planted defect, checked once by hand and recorded in the close comment (a changed meaning, a removed failure-mode row, a wrong count, a changed excerpt line). - [ ] Every description text changed in code is listed (before → after), with `SKILL.md`, the snapshots and, if needed, the current golden regenerated in the same commit; no wire name, code, key, env var or constant was added or changed. - [ ] Every mismatch found is a bug `discovered-from` this part, in Known issues, blocking H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`). - [ ] `argc gate` passes, `ubs` is clean on the changed files, and every "Decided while writing this bead" item of this part is confirmed or adjusted in the close comment. ## Test Plan Beads this section names: A5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5`, `robot-docs schema` and `robot-docs errors`); A9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9`, A meaning and a typed `DetailSpec` for every code); T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, Structured test logs, and the `argc e2e` runner). ### Unit tests None new in `src/`. A changed description text is covered by A9's meaning style test and A5's fix-pattern style test, which run in the gate. If this part adds a helper to `tests/common/markdown.rs` (a `
` table reader, say), its table-driven cases go in `tests/common_selftest.rs`, one name per case, with messages that show the input, the expected and the actual value. ### Integration and end-to-end tests `tests/readme.rs`, nine tests. Each opens `let log = tlog!();`. Each command runs through `log.run(&env, &argv)` on a fresh `TestEnv::new()` (an empty home: these outputs describe the binary, not a machine) and must be `ok()` before its envelope is read. None of these commands makes a request: each test asserts that `Ran`'s recorded `net.log` lines are empty. 1. **`error_table_quotes_robot_docs_errors`.** Steps: `run` (`robot-docs errors --json`; `data.error_codes`); `read README` (the `details` block "Every error code", its table); `compare`. The header is exactly `Code | Exit | Doctor exit | Retryable | Meaning | Fix`; the summary's N equals the length; row i's six cells equal code i's `code` (span), `exit`, `doctor_exit`, retryable word, `meaning` and `fix_pattern` (pipes unescaped). 2. **`warning_table_quotes_robot_docs_errors`.** The same over `warning_codes`, header `Code | Meaning | Fix`. 3. **`exit_tables_quote_the_dictionaries`.** `run` (`capabilities --json`); the general table under "### Exit codes" equals `exit_codes.general` (`code`, `name`, `meaning`); the doctor dictionary's table equals `exit_codes.doctor`. 4. **`doctor_table_quotes_doctor_capabilities`.** `run` (`doctor capabilities --json`, report keys at the top level) and `run` (`capabilities --json`). N equals `detectors.len()` and `failure_modes.count`. `OMADDONS_TEST_FIXERS` is never set. 5. **`binding_and_storing_lists_match_capabilities`.** `run` (`capabilities --json`). The `--if-match` row's command spans equal the `binds: true` paths, as sets. The "These commands store a plan:" sentence's spans equal the `stores_plan: true` paths, as sets. 6. **`volatile_keys_quote_the_registry`.** The library's `VOLATILE` entries equal the README table's rows, in order. 7. **`environment_section_names_every_registered_variable`.** The section's names equal `ENV_VARS`'s, minus `MENTIONED_ONLY`; each release name is in a table row, each debug or harness name in the prose. 8. **`counts_named_in_readme_match_the_code`.** `run` (`capabilities --json`) for `failure_modes.count`; the library for the rest; `std::fs::read_dir("fuzz/fuzz_targets")` for the targets. The section holds the exact pointer line; it has exactly one `markdown` fence; the fence body equals the excerpt; the excerpt contains `plans show`; and the old block's first line occurs nowhere in README. In `tests/contract/intent_corpus.rs`: `the_corpus_meets_checkpoint_criterion_5` runs in the gate from this commit on. ### Logging - Each test logs the steps `run` (each `log.run` records the argv, the environment overrides, the exit, the parsed envelope, stderr and the `net.log` lines added), `read README` (`log.json` of the table or section found, with its line), `compare` (`log.json` of the README rows, the expected rows and the differences) and, on a difference, `expected` (a `log.note` holding the whole expected Markdown table or block, ready to paste). - A failing assertion names the first differing row and column, both values and the README line, and T1's guard prints `test log: ` and the last 20 steps. `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG=verbose cargo test --test readme -- --nocapture` echoes each step live. - The corpus test prints its count per kind; that output is copied into the close comment. ## Considerations Beads this section names: A3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`, Schemas with the serialize contract, declared `details`, and live validation); A9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9`, A meaning and a typed `DetailSpec` for every code); C4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4`, The run-the-fix corpus). - **Losing facts is the main risk.** The ledger makes each loss visible in review, and the close comment is where a reviewer checks it. - **A README-only edit can now fail the gate.** These tests compare generated content only, never prose. Their failure message gives the rows to paste, and subtask 3 adds a sentence to the Development section telling README editors to run `cargo test --test readme`. - **The quoted texts are long.** Meanings and fix patterns are one sentence each. The table is wide, but `
` keeps it out of the way; rumdl's line-length rule is already exempt for README (one line per row). - **Wording in a quotation is fixed at its source** (the code, or the guide's template), never in README, so the next regeneration cannot undo it. - **Hot spots** (§10.5 of the plan): - `src/error.rs`: A9 then A3 own the rows, and later leaves append. Change only meaning strings in place. - `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md`: regenerate after rebasing, never merge by hand. - `tests/contract/matrix.rs` snapshots: re-accept only after reviewing the diff. - `tests/contract/intent_corpus.rs` (C4's): one attribute. - `README.md`: rebase onto any concurrent bug fix's change, never revert it. - **Privacy:** the commands run on empty `TestEnv` homes; nothing reads a `WTF/`. - **Defaults applied** (§8.1 of the plan): no new name of any kind; registry order, which is the binary's order; fail closed (a table the helpers cannot find fails the test). - **Decided while writing this bead** (confirm or adjust in the close comment): the `-v` form and the column sets; the fact ledger and its notation; text corrections in code where README was truer; the exit tables quoted; the failure-mode table in `
` with its columns and the Status and Repair rules; `MENTIONED_ONLY`; the "These commands store a plan:" marker; the counts rule and its phrases; the corpus test un-ignored; the agent section's form, the four-backtick fence and the guide-side fix rule. ## Dependencies - **Parent:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4 (The README final pass), under omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8. Its blockers (every surface leaf, the golden and determinism audits, and the three slice-demo suites) have closed, among them the leaves whose outputs this part quotes: A4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`, `capabilities`), A5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5`, `robot-docs errors`), A9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9`, the meanings), E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`) and E4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4`, the doctor's surface), F8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.8`, the status column), F9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`, the complete catalog), H3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3`, `contract::VOLATILE`) and C4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4`, the corpus). - **Before it:** subtask 1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4.1`), whose `tests/readme.rs` and `tests/common/markdown.rs` this part extends, and whose structural fixes it builds on. - **After it:** subtask 3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4.3`, the Appendix D walk) walks the prose around these settled tables, and subtask 4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4.4`) finishes. - **T1** (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`) provides `TestLog`; the filing step adds its edge. - **Related:** H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`) is blocked by every bug this part files.
