title: The M4 checkpoint and the first tag
description:
## How to work this bead

This bead is worked through its 5 subtasks, listed below in work order. Claim a subtask, not this bead (`br ready --parent omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6` lists the ready ones). The agent that closes the last open subtask then verifies every acceptance criterion of this bead (they are the leaf's, not any one subtask's), and closes this bead with `br close omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6 --reason "done: <evidence> · found: <ids>"`. Until this bead is closed, every bead it blocks stays blocked (it blocks none: it is the sink of the graph, and the milestone epic closes after it).

1. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.1 The freeze check and the gate from a clean checkout, with every criterion's gate evidence named: §11.3 steps 1 and 2.1, the criterion-by-criterion map of the tests that ran in the gate, and slice 4's pre-tag parts; evidence comment 1.
2. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.2 The checkpoint-only runs: perf, bench, fuzz, compatibility, the exhaustive harness, the guide's fixed point, live probes, coverage and the ignored-test inventory, with the plan's runs 2.2 to 2.9 in order, every command of README's checkpoint block, and every ignored test accounted for; evidence comment 2.
3. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.3 The real-machine and desktop runs, and the review of every real-home finding: the real-machine suite, the doctor on the real home reviewed finding by finding, the widget installed from the M4 build, its Update on a matching plan, and a doctor repair from the Issues view undone with Undo last; evidence comment 3.
4. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.4 The freeze commit and the annotated tag `v0.1.0`: the vision comment, README's flips, the first released baseline and the golden's header, then a negative control, `argc gate`, one commit, the tag, and the push.
5. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.5 Closing the milestone: slice 4's demo, the close reason with all eighteen criteria, and the epics, through `br epic close-eligible` until nothing more closes, and the last `.beads/` commit.

The subtasks form one chain, s1 → s2 → s3 → s4 → s5, and none may run beside another. The order is the plan's checkpoint protocol (§11.3, "in this order"), and it is also the cheapest order when something fails: the gate (s1) is the fastest way to find a defect, the timing budgets of s2 need a quiet machine, the real-machine runs of s3 touch the owner's clients only after everything that could force a code change has passed, and the tag (s4) is made only when every criterion is met. Every run of s1 to s3 happens at one commit, the evidence commit `E` (Technical Approach, part 0); a code change after `E` sends the work back to s1 (part 8).

**This bead is never deferred.** A failed criterion files a bug or reopens the owning leaf, and that bead blocks this one (part 8). No step waits on a person: approving the plan was the owner's one involvement in M4, and it is also the go-ahead for every real-machine and desktop run listed below.

## Background

Beads this section names: H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, the pre-freeze contract audit), H2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.2`, the golden and the released-baseline mechanism), H4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`, the README final pass), H5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.5`, the vision comments), E5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`, the repair transaction, which adds the `journal` fuzz target), E9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9`, the M3 build against M4 state), G3 (`omad-7ccp`, group commit and deferred fsyncs, which is `omad-7ccp`), T2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.2`, slice 1 end to end), T3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.3`, slice 2 end to end), T4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4`, slice 3 end to end), the milestone epic (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`), and the vision bead `omad-vision-8qa`.

**What this bead is.** It is the M4 checkpoint: the leaf that proves the milestone, records the proof, freezes the contract and makes the project's first tag. It is the sink of M4's graph (the plan's 60 leaves plus area T's four), so when it starts every other M4 leaf is closed and every feature, test and README section exists. It then does what no other leaf can: it runs every success criterion of the milestone against `main` and the development machine, records the evidence criterion by criterion, writes the vision's "M4 is done" comment, commits README's done flips together with the first released contract baseline and the golden's `frozen: true` header, tags that commit `v0.1.0`, pushes both, records slice 4's demo, and closes the milestone.

**Why it exists.** A milestone is done when its promises are demonstrated, not when its beads are closed. The tag matters beyond the record: from the tag on, the contract is frozen and the gate compares every change with the released baseline this bead writes (M4-D56). M3's checkpoint record (bead `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.7.3`) taught four lessons this bead applies on purpose: slice demos were not recorded as slices landed (here T2–T4 record slices 1–3 as tests, and this bead only checks them); real-machine tests the plan named had no owning leaf (here each has one, and this bead only runs them); the plan's compat command was wrong (`--release` on a debug-only test; here every command is written out and was checked against the code); and the real-machine and desktop steps waited for an owner go-ahead (here approving the plan was that go-ahead).

**What is true today** (at `c0ab5e9`, the commit the plan was verified against): the repository has no tag; the crate says `0.1.0`; there is no golden, no released baseline and no `tests/contract/released/` directory (H2 commits the golden, this bead the first baseline); README says "Nothing is tagged … the JSON contract freezes at the first tag (milestone 4, next)". By the time this bead starts, every M4 leaf will have landed its surfaces, tests and README sections, H4 will have prepared the exact text of README's done flips, and H5 will have written the vision comments.

**The milestone goals it proves** (each restated):

- **G-M4-1 Self-describing:** an agent learns omaddons from the binary in at most three calls (`capabilities --json`, `robot-docs guide`, `status --json`); every fact is generated from the code; every command's output has a published JSON Schema that the contract suite validates real output against.
- **G-M4-2 The first guess works:** a plausible wrong invocation gets a usage error whose fix is the command meant, proven to run, never a different changing command.
- **G-M4-3 What was previewed is what runs, target by target:** every addon-changing command previews and runs bound (`--if-match` or `apply <plan_id>`); per target exactly the approved operations or none; the approval covers what the preview saw and is checked again under the lock; `plans show` reconciles; the widget applies directly only a routine matching plan.
- **G-M4-4 Diagnosable and repairable:** `doctor` names every broken state with evidence and an exact remediation, never calls incomplete coverage healthy; every auto-fixable state is repaired by one consented, verbatim-backed, never-deleting, undoable command; the "manual repair" states get guarded repairs; `status` and `doctor` never disagree.
- **G-M4-5 Frozen and enforced:** at the first tag the contract is consistent (audited), complete (a semantic manifest of every input and output, with a readable names list) and enforced (every later change compared with the released baseline, and one without its version bump fails the gate, however the golden was regenerated); every exit site maps to a published code; repeated runs print identical bytes. **This bead makes the tag and writes the baseline that turns the enforcement on.**
- **G-M4-6 No new risk to the engine's guarantees:** every new write through fsx, every repair a journaled transaction; dry runs leave `<state>` untouched; the lock is held only for commit windows; the doctor never writes `WTF/`; the M3 build never destroys what M4 wrote.

**Checkpoint criteria: all eighteen** (§3.2 of the plan; the full text of each, its owners and where its evidence comes from are in Technical Approach, part 2): 1 capabilities; 2 schemas; 3 the guide and the skill; 4 the eight canonical intents as recipes; 5 intent inference; 6 previews bind on every addon-changing command; 7 stored plans; 8 the widget applies what it shows; 9 the doctor's safety harness; 10 the doctor's surface; 11 stuck states named and repairable; 12 `status` and `doctor` agree and `status` stays fast; 13 durability; 14 the contract is frozen; 15 completions; 16 older builds against M4 state; 17 gate and checkpoint runs; 18 README, the vision and the tag. This bead records each in its close reason as `[x] N <criterion>: <evidence>`, with the commit hash, test names, timings and every `SKIP` line quoted.

**Pre-accepted `SKIP`s, exactly three** (approving the plan accepted them, so this bead never needs an owner decision):

- `keyless_installs_forever`, which M2 and M3 already accept through `OMADDONS_ALLOW_SKIP` while the Forever client's guard (`forever_guard()`) stands;
- the bind-mount and size-limited-tmpfs sandbox tests (`unshare -rm`), where unprivileged user namespaces are unavailable;
- the `zsh -n` and `fish --no-execute` syntax checks of generated completions, where those shells are not installed (bash's check is never skipped).

Any other `SKIP` means the criterion is not met: it is recorded as unmet with its reason, a bug is filed `discovered-from` this bead and added as its blocker, and this bead waits on it. **The compatibility characterizations are never skipped:** an older commit is built with the toolchain it records (`af10e34` and `c0ab5e9` both pin `1.97.1`, which rustup installs on demand), or a provenance-verified binary of it is used; if neither can be had, criterion 16 is unmet ("compiler inconvenience is not evidence that storage is safe").

**Owner involvement (§3.3 of the plan), restated.** M4 needed the owner exactly once: approving the plan. That approval is also the go-ahead for the checkpoint's real-machine and desktop runs, each listed exactly here, each read-only or undone, none touching the Forever client's state:

- the doctor on the real home (`doctor` and `doctor fix --dry-run`, read-only);
- one update previewed and applied on a non-Forever client, then undone;
- the widget's Update preview on the live bar;
- a doctor repair from the Issues view, undone;
- `install-skill --dry-run` against the real home, and a real install into a tempdir only.

Decided by the plan, so nothing waits on a person: nothing in M4 installs the skill into the real `$HOME/.claude/skills/` (a skill there is loaded by every Claude Code session on the machine, which is the owner's call, made with one command whenever they like; the checkpoint proves the default path resolves and the install works); an unexpected `SKIP` is a failed criterion, not a question.

**The decisions that shape it** (the full decision log is filed as comments on the milestone epic `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`):

- **M4-D57: the first tag is `v0.1.0`, made by the checkpoint.** After every criterion passes and README says M4 is done, this bead makes one commit holding the README status flips, the golden's header flip, the first released baseline `tests/contract/released/1.0.json` (with its provenance: `v0.1.0`, the commit it was generated from, the date) and `.beads/`. That commit changes a test fixture, so `argc gate` runs on it before it is made (vision D16), with the baseline in place: the compatibility test then runs its comparison with a released baseline on an unchanged registry, which must pass. Then this bead creates the annotated tag `v0.1.0` on that commit (`git tag -a v0.1.0 -m "omaddons 0.1.0: contract 1.0 frozen"`) and pushes the commit and the tag. ### 0. Ground rules for the whole checkpoint

- **The evidence commit `E`.** Every run of s1 to s3 happens at one commit: `E`, the head of `main` when s1 starts, with every leaf but this one closed, a clean working tree (`git status --porcelain` empty), and `origin/main` equal to it (push first if it is not). The close reason says "every criterion was run at `E`, the last code commit". A commit after `E` that changes only `.beads/` or README does not move `E`. Any other commit (a fix for a failed criterion) makes a new `E`, and part 8's rerun rule applies.
- **Where the runs happen.** *Decided while writing this bead:* a fresh clone of `main` at `E` into a new directory under the repository's own `target/` (git-ignored, and on btrfs on the development machine, which the clone-capable gate tests and the btrfs budgets need; never under `/tmp`, which is tmpfs), cloned from the local repository (`git clone --branch main <repository> <checkout>`), with `git -C <checkout> rev-parse HEAD` equal to `E`. Free space is checked first (at least 60 GiB, because the clone's target dir, the compat builds and the coverage build each take tens of GiB). Every step of s1 to s3 runs in that checkout, except fuzzing, which runs in the main working copy (still at `E`, still clean) so that it reuses the git-ignored `fuzz/corpus/` that earlier runs accumulated.
- **Long runs.** The gate, fuzzing (about four hours), the compat builds and the exhaustive harness run in a background shell whose stdout and stderr are saved to files in the agent's scratch directory (`gate.log`, `perf.log`, `fuzz-<target>.log`, …), so a session break loses no evidence. Each file is quoted from, never pasted whole.
- **What counts as a failure.** A failing test; a `SKIP` that is not one of the three pre-accepted ones; a budget missed (a perf test failing, a `✗` in `argc bench`); a fuzz crash; a compat row that deletes or overwrites what M4 still needs; a real-home finding or a planned fix that is wrong; a named checkpoint test that does not exist; a slice demo comment that is missing; a README statement that is false; a privacy leak in any output or record. Each is handled by part 8, never by deferring, never by `--force`.
- **The privacy scrub.** Everything this bead posts (three evidence comments, the vision comment, the slice demo, the close reason) is public-safe bead text: no absolute or home path (the home directory becomes `<home>`, a client directory `<client dir>` with its target id, omaddons' directories `<config>`, `<state>`, `<cache>`, `<meta>`, `<skills>`), no host name, no user name, no real name, no email, no account, realm or character name, no token, and no screenshot (screenshots and IPC captures stay in the scratch directory and are named only). Before each `br comments add` and the `br close`, the file is checked by a scratch script that greps it for the value of `$HOME`, any absolute path, a tilde path, the machine's host name (`uname -n`), the user name (`id -un`) and every directory name under each client's `WTF/Account/` (read without printing them; the script prints only "clean" or the line numbers that matched). A match is fixed before posting.
- **Nothing here writes code.** This bead adds no test, no command and no wire name. Its only repository changes are README's flip lines, the golden's two header lines (regenerated, never hand-edited), the new `tests/contract/released/1.0.json`, and `.beads/`.

### 2. The eighteen criteria, their owners, and where the evidence comes from

Each criterion is restated in full; *Owners* are the leaves that built and tested it; *Evidence* names which subtask records which part. Test names come from each owner's close comment (the names its bead fixed are given here as examples) and are confirmed present at `E` in `cargo test --locked -- --list` (and `cargo test --locked --release --test perf -- --ignored --list` for the release budgets), saved by s1. A test an owner's close comment names that is absent from the list is a failed criterion.

1. **Capabilities.** `omaddons capabilities --json` carries the six required keys (`version`, `contract_version`, `features`, `commands`, `exit_codes`, `env_vars`) and the extra keys (`build_id`, `guide_digest`, `limits`, `sources`, `families`, `client_rules`, `target_id_forms`, `error_codes`, `warning_codes`, `actions`, `failure_modes`, `schemas_uri`, `robot_docs_uri`, `config_error`; §6.2.2); it round-trips (every command entry, flag and alias parses with `Cli::try_parse_from` and `--help`; every error, warning and action it lists is registered and every registered one listed; failure modes summarized with `count` and `subsystems`, the count equal to the registry's, pointing at `doctor capabilities`); it makes no request and writes nothing (`net.log`, `<state>` and `<cache>` hash-identical); under 20 ms, median of 21, release build. *Owners:* A4 (with A1, A2). *Evidence:* s1, `tests/capabilities.rs` in the gate; s2, `tests/perf.rs::capabilities_answers_in_under_20_ms` (A4's name), with its median.
2. **Schemas.** `robot-docs schema` gives a JSON Schema for every `app::COMMANDS` path, the envelope and every NDJSON event; the contract suite validates every live envelope's `data` (every matrix row, success and failure) and every stderr event strictly (an unknown key fails, except under `OPAQUE` paths), and every envelope snapshot in the repository (the walker); the strict transform is itself tested on `$ref`, maps, tagged unions and composition; `robot-docs errors` lists every code with exit, retryability, meaning and typed `details` specification, and every observed `details` validates against it; `apply`'s data validates as the wrapper variant of its own `applied.command`. *Owners:* A3, A5, A9, D5. *Evidence:* s1, `tests/contract/` and `tests/robot_docs.rs` in the gate.
3. **The guide and the skill.** `robot-docs guide` and `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` are byte-identical; the file opens with YAML frontmatter, and the line after it is `<!-- omaddons guide sha256:<hex> -->`, a digest of the document without that line, with no build id, so regenerate → rebuild → regenerate leaves bytes and digest unchanged; `install-skill` writes the same bytes to `<skills>/SKILL.md` and a second run writes nothing; `doctor` reports an installed skill whose guide digest differs (`fm-plugins-skill-version-drift`), never one differing only by build, and `doctor fix` brings it current, undoably; a hand-edited skill is left to the user; the guide is under 500 lines and 32 KiB. *Owners:* B1, B2, B3, F10. *Evidence:* s1, `tests/skill.rs` (`skill_md_is_the_guide`, `regeneration_is_a_fixed_point`, the size and parse tests), `tests/robot_docs.rs::install_skill_*` and F10's fixture tests in the gate, plus `wc -l -c skills/omaddons/SKILL.md`; s2, the literal fixed point; s3, `install_skill_round_trip` on the real machine.

If the push of `main` is rejected (someone pushed after `E`), delete the local, unpushed tag (`git tag -d v0.1.0`), fetch, and: if the new commits touch only `.beads/` or README, rebase onto them, rerun `argc gate`, recommit and retag; otherwise the evidence is stale (part 8's rerun rule). **A pushed tag is never moved or deleted.**

### 6. Steps 6 and 7 of the protocol: closing the milestone (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.5)

1. **Slice 4's demo**, a comment on the milestone epic titled "**Slice demo 4. Freeze and close**", in the `[x] <item>: <evidence>` style, one item per exit-demo element: the recipes pass (B4's eight tests at `E`, each at most two commands); the audit's change list and the empty allowlist (H1's "**Pre-freeze audit change list**" comment and addenda, the number of entries by disposition, and `tests/contract/rules_allowlist.txt` empty at the tag); the golden and the updater tests (the manifest's section counts from A10's report, the header `frozen: true`, H2's updater test names passing); README (H4's checklist, the flips at the tag commit); the tag (`v0.1.0` → the commit hash, annotated, the `git ls-remote` lines); the released baseline (its provenance quoted, the negative control's three outcomes). It pre-checks criteria 3, 4, 14, 17 and 18.
2. **The close reason** (part 7), assembled from the three evidence comments with criteria 14 and 18 completed by s4's results.
3. `br close omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.5`, then `br close omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6 --reason "$(cat <close reason file>)" --transition-comment "done: all 18 criteria [x] at <E>; v0.1.0 on <tag commit>; slice demo 4 posted · found: <ids>"`, never `--force`.
4. `br epic close-eligible --transition-comment "closed by the M4 checkpoint: every child closed"`, repeated until it closes nothing: AREA-H, then the milestone epic.
5. `br lint` on every bead this bead touched or filed, `br sync --flush-only`, `git add .beads/`, commit `chore(beads): close M4: checkpoint record, slice 4 demo and the epics`, push. `git status` is clean and `git log origin/main..main` is empty.

### 7. The record formats

- **Evidence comments** (one per subtask s1–s3, on this bead): a bold title "**Checkpoint evidence k of 3: <what> (at <E short hash>)**", then for each criterion the subtask covers a block starting `[x] N <criterion name> (<part>):` or `[ ] N … UNMET:`, with commands, test names (`file::name`), counts, medians and p95 where measured, and every `SKIP` line quoted exactly. The block for criterion 17 lists every run of the subtask with its exit and wall time.
- **The close reason**, in M3's form: `done: M4 checkpoint, <date>. Every criterion was run at <E>, the last code commit; <tag commit> adds README, the contract freeze and beads only, and is tagged v0.1.0. Evidence: comments <ids> on this bead; slice demos <ids> on the milestone epic; vision comment <id>.` Then eighteen blocks, `[x] 1 Capabilities: …` to `[x] 18 README, the vision and the tag: …`, each with its evidence from part 2's sources. Then the open follow-ups (part 1), the decided defaults applied (each confirmed or adjusted), a `Contract:` line naming the one new contract file, `tests/contract/released/1.0.json`, and saying no other wire name was added or changed (common rule 6), and `found: <bug and reopened ids, each with its state, or none>`.
- **The slice demo** and **the vision comment** as in parts 5 and 6.

### 8. When a criterion fails

1. Record it in the subtask's evidence comment as `[ ] N … UNMET: <what failed>`, quoting the output.
2. **A missing deliverable** (a named test that does not exist, a slice demo comment that was never posted, a README checkpoint command an owner promised and did not add): reopen the owning leaf, `br reopen <leaf> --reason "M4 checkpoint: <what is missing>"`. **Anything else:** file a bug following the bead-creation conventions (CLAUDE.md), `br create "<what fails>" --type bug --priority 1 --labels m4 --description-file <file> --deps discovered-from:omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, whose description holds the failing command, its quoted output (scrubbed), the criterion, the commit `E` and the log file's name; `br lint` clean.
3. Add the bug or reopened leaf as a blocker of this bead and of the current subtask: `br dep add omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6 <id>` and `br dep add <current subtask id> <id>`. Release the subtask: `br update <current subtask id> --status open --transition-comment "blocked: <id> (criterion N unmet)"`. This bead returns to open and waits; it is never deferred, and nothing is closed with `--force`.
4. **The rerun rule,** when the blocker lands as a code commit (a new `E`): reopen every closed subtask among s1–s3 (`br reopen … --reason "evidence predates <new E>"`) and rerun them in order at the new `E`; their earlier evidence comments stay, and the new ones say which they supersede. *Decided while writing this bead:* the only runs that may be carried over are the fuzz runs, and only when `git diff --stat <old E> <new E>` touches nothing under `src/`, `fuzz/`, `build.rs`, `Cargo.toml` or `Cargo.lock`, recorded as "carried from <old E>".
5. A defect found after the tag was pushed is filed as a bug for the next milestone and named in the close reason; the tag is never moved.

### 9. What this bead never does

It never writes product or test code; never changes the Forever client's state (no install, update, pin, repair or record change there); never writes under any `WTF/`; never installs the skill into the real `$HOME/.claude/skills/`; never quits a running game; never sends text through `wtype` (key names only, `wtype -k`); never hand-edits the golden; never moves, deletes or force-pushes a pushed tag; never closes with `--force`; never defers itself; and never posts a path, host name, user name or account name.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every one of §3.2's eighteen criteria is `[x]` in this bead's close reason, each with its evidence (commit `E`, test names, counts, timings), every `SKIP` line quoted, and no `SKIP` other than the three pre-accepted kinds.
- [ ] The freeze check passed at `E`: every other M4 leaf closed, the slice demo comments of slices 1–3 present on the milestone epic, only the H area epic and the milestone epic open among the epics, and every open P0–P1 bug discovered from M4 work closed.
- [ ] `argc gate --all` passed from a fresh clone of `main` at `E` on btrfs under the repository's `target/` (never tmpfs), with its counts recorded.
- [ ] Every machine-local checkpoint run passed at `E` and is recorded: the perf budgets, `argc bench` (every target ✓), every fuzz target 10 minutes and `journal` 30 more with no crash, `compat_m2` and `compat_m3` with no `SKIP`, the exhaustive harness, the guide's literal fixed point with an empty diff, the live probes, line coverage, every command of README's checkpoint block, and the inventory of ignored tests.
- [ ] The real-machine suite passed with only `keyless_installs_forever`'s pre-accepted `SKIP` (or its recorded exclusion when Forever manages no addons), and every real-home doctor finding and every planned fix action is recorded with a verdict of right.
- [ ] The desktop runs are recorded with IPC `state()` and screenshot names: the widget installed from the M4 build and current, an Update on a matching plan with `lastPreview.decision: "direct"`, and a credential-mode repair from the Issues view undone with Undo last; the Forever guard, every AddOns tree hash, every `WTF/` metadata hash and the `<config>` metadata hash equal their values before.
- [ ] The vision comment "§10 Milestone status: M4 (the agent surface, the doctor and the first tag) is done, <date> (…)" exists on `omad-vision-8qa`, with its departures and limits, and ends with "M5 (accounts and release engineering) is next."
- [ ] One commit holds exactly README's done flips, the golden's regenerated `frozen: true` header lines, the new `tests/contract/released/1.0.json` and `.beads/`, and `argc gate` passed on it before it was made.
- [ ] `tests/contract/released/1.0.json` carries the provenance `contract_version` "1.0", `tag` "v0.1.0", `commit` = `E` (the commit it was generated from), and an RFC 3339 UTC `created_at`, and equals the golden's manifest apart from `provenance` and `header`; the negative control showed the gate reads it.
- [ ] The annotated tag `v0.1.0` (message "omaddons 0.1.0: contract 1.0 frozen") points at that commit, `Cargo.toml` still says `0.1.0`, and both the commit and the tag are on `origin`.
- [ ] Slice 4's demo comment "Slice demo 4. Freeze and close" is on the milestone epic, with the recipes, the audit's change list and the empty allowlist, the golden and the updater tests, README, the tag and the released baseline, each with its evidence.
- [ ] `br epic close-eligible` closed the H area epic and the milestone epic; the final `.beads/` commit is pushed and `git status` is clean.
- [ ] The close reason lists the one new contract file, `tests/contract/released/1.0.json` (the released baseline, with provenance), and states that no other wire name was added or changed (common rule 6).
- [ ] Every comment and the close reason passed the privacy scrub: no path, host name, user name, real name, email, token, or account, realm or character name.
- [ ] `br lint` is clean for this bead, its subtasks and every bead it filed.

## Test Plan

Beads this section names: T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs), T2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.2`), T3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.3`) and T4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4`) (the slice demos as tests), G1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1`, the widget previews and applies plans), G2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.2`, the Issues view runs repairs), H2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.2`, the golden and the released-baseline mechanism).

This bead writes no test. Its test plan is the checkpoint protocol itself: every command below is run as written, at `E`, and its outcome is recorded as evidence.

### Unit tests

None: this bead adds no code. The unit tests of every M4 module run inside the gate (part 3, run 1), and their counts are recorded.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

The runs, in order, with the outcome each must have (the full detail is in the subtasks):

- **The gate from a clean checkout** (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.1): `argc gate --all` exits 0. Every M4 suite runs in it: `tests/capabilities.rs`, `tests/robot_docs.rs`, `tests/skill.rs`, `tests/skill_recipes.rs`, `tests/contract/` (the matrix, strict schema validation, `intent_corpus.rs`, `wire_names.rs` with H2's updater tests, the rule test with an empty allowlist, the repeat and coverage tests), `tests/determinism.rs`, `tests/completions.rs`, `tests/apply.rs`, `tests/plans_show.rs`, `tests/preconditions.rs`, `tests/doctor.rs`, `tests/doctor_harness.rs`, `tests/doctor_repair.rs`, `tests/engine_durability.rs`, `tests/engine_crash.rs`, `tests/journal.rs`, T2–T4's `tests/e2e_slice{1,2,3}.rs`, and the widget pipeline with bun and QML (G1's `tst_plans.qml`, G2's `tst_repairs.qml`).
- **The checkpoint-only runs** (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.2): perf (every budget passes), bench (every target ✓), fuzz (no crash), compat_m2 and compat_m3 (no `SKIP`, every row green), the exhaustive harness, the fixed point (empty diff), live probes, coverage, README's extra checkpoint commands, and the inventory (every ignored test accounted for).
- **The real machine and the desktop** (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.3): the real-machine suite (only the pre-accepted `SKIP`), the finding-by-finding review, the status/doctor comparison on the real home, and the three desktop checks, each followed by hash comparisons that must be equal.
- **The tag commit** (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.4): `argc gate` passes with the baseline in place; the negative control fails twice and passes once as specified; the tag checks pass.

### Logging

- Every run's stdout and stderr go to a file in the agent's scratch directory (`gate.log`, `list-debug.txt`, `list-ignored.txt`, `perf.log`, `bench.log`, `fuzz-<target>.log`, `compat_m2.log`, `compat_m3.log`, `harness.log`, `fixedpoint.log`, `live.log`, `coverage.log`, `real_machine.log`, `doctor-review.md`, `desktop/state-<step>-before.json` and `-after.json`, `desktop/<step>.png`, `hashes-before.txt`, `hashes-after.txt`, `negative-control.log`), named in the evidence comments. Screenshots and IPC captures are never committed or attached.
- Integration suites that T1's `TestLog` covers leave transcripts under `<CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR>/test-logs/<suite>/<test>/`; a failing gate test is diagnosed from the transcript its panic prints (`test log: <path>`), and that path (relative to the checkout) is quoted in the bug.
- Real-machine tests print their evidence through `tests/real_machine.rs`'s `note()` (the home directory shown as `<home>`); T1's log is not used there, because it refuses roots outside a `TestEnv`.
- A failure prints, in its evidence block, the command, the exit code, the last 40 lines of its log and the log's file name.

### Checkpoint-only tests and the `SKIP` rule

The exact commands, in the order they run (README's checkpoint block holds most of them, and any it holds beyond these are run too): `cargo test --release --test perf -- --ignored --skip bench_home --skip live_home --test-threads=1`; `argc bench`; `argc fuzz-all --time 600 --toolchain <nightly ≥ 1.97>` and `argc fuzz journal --time 1800`; `cargo test --test compat_m2 -- --ignored --nocapture`; `cargo test --test compat_m3 -- --ignored --nocapture`; `cargo test --test doctor_harness -- --ignored`; `OMADDONS_UPDATE_SKILL=1 cargo test --test skill`, `cargo build`, again, `git diff --exit-code skills/`; `OMADDONS_LIVE=1 cargo test --test live_probes -- --ignored`; `OMADDONS_LIVE=1 cargo test --locked --lib -- --ignored live_github_request`; `cargo llvm-cov --summary-only`; `OMADDONS_ALLOW_SKIP=zsh_accepts_its_script,fish_accepts_its_script cargo test --test completions -- --ignored`; `OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE=1 OMADDONS_LIVE=1 OMADDONS_ALLOW_SKIP=keyless_installs_forever cargo test --test real_machine -- --ignored --test-threads=1`. **`SKIP` rule:** only `keyless_installs_forever` (while Forever manages addons), the sandbox tests (where user namespaces are unavailable) and `zsh_accepts_its_script`/`fish_accepts_its_script` (where the shell is missing; neither zsh nor fish was installed on the development machine when this bead was written) may print an accepted `SKIP`; any other `SKIP` is an unmet criterion.

## Considerations

Beads this section names: A10 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.10`, the semantic manifest and its classifier), H2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.2`, the golden and the released-baseline mechanism), H4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`, the README final pass), E9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9`, the M3 build against M4 state).

- **Risk #3, doctor false positives on real homes erode trust** (likelihood medium, impact medium; owners the F leaves and this bead). Mitigation here: every real-home finding and every planned action is reviewed and recorded with a verdict; a false one is a bug that blocks the tag. The catalog leaves already hold a no-false-positive test per detector on the realistic home, and severities are conservative.
- **Risk #17, Forever launches mid-milestone (2026-11-04)** (medium, low). The checkpoint may run after the launch. M4 touches no discovery or rules code, and `omad-wez` re-verifies Forever outside M4; if `status_reports_every_client` fails on a changed Forever layout, that is a failed criterion 17 handled by part 8, and the bug names `omad-wez` as related.
- **Risk #22, the classifier mislabels a change** (low, high; owners A10, H2): from this bead's tag on, the classifier guards every commit. The negative control is the last check that the gate reads the real baseline file.
- **Hot spots** (§10.5): `README.md` (everyone edits their own section; H4 reconciled; this bead edits only the flip lines and the sentences the tag makes false); `tests/contract/` (the golden's header is regenerated by the updater, never merged by hand); `.beads/` (commit after `br sync --flush-only`). By the time this bead runs every leaf is closed, but a blocker's fix may be in flight: the freeze commit waits until no peer holds uncommitted work.
- **Why size M, and why five subtasks.** No code is written, but the protocol is long (the fuzz runs alone take about four hours) and each part ends in a separately reviewable record; the subtasks split the work at the points where a failure sends the checkpoint back (part 8), not the closure: this bead closes only when all five are done.
- **What could go wrong, and how to notice.** A checkout on tmpfs (gate tests skip; check the filesystem type first). A stale `SKILL.md` (the fixed point's first regeneration shows a diff). A stale golden (the header flip's diff touches more than the header). A gate that does not read the baseline (the negative control passes when it should fail). A real client launched during s3 (`skip_if_running` prints `SKIP`; wait and rerun). Text typed into the live panel (use `wtype -k` only; after the desktop step, `omaddons history --json` shows no transaction the agent did not intend, and the Forever guard is unchanged).
- **Compatibility.** The tag freezes contract 1.0: after it, an added JSON key needs a minor `schema_version` bump and anything else a major one, compared with `tests/contract/released/1.0.json` on every gate (owner-visible, M4-D56). The crate stays `0.1.0` (M4-D57). Older builds were characterized by E9.
- **Privacy.** The real-machine runs and the desktop read real paths and real clients; nothing of them reaches bead text except through the scrub (part 0). The credential plant holds no secret, and the real token's content is never read.
- **Performance.** The perf budgets need a quiet machine: nothing else runs during s2's perf and bench runs (no fuzzing, no gate, no other agent's build).
- **Decided defaults, recorded here so the closing agent can confirm them in the close reason:** the evidence commit and its rerun rule; the checkout's location; fuzz in the main working copy; README's extra checkpoint commands and the ignored-test inventory; the handling of open follow-ups; the `keyless_installs_forever` exclusion; waiting for a running client; installing the widget first; the Update candidate and its undo; the credential plant; the status/doctor comparison on the real home; the provenance `commit`; the header by the updater; the negative control; the badge; the commit messages; closing this bead after the tag.

## Dependencies

Parent: the H area epic (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8`, freeze and close).

**Blocked by:**

- H5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.5`, the vision comments): the vision comments of Appendix E must exist before this bead writes the last one ("§10 Milestone status"), and through H5 this bead waits for everything: H4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`, the README final pass, which prepared the flip text this bead commits), H2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.2`, the golden and the baseline mechanism this bead's commit uses), H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, the pre-freeze audit whose contract the tag freezes), T2–T4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.2`, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.3`, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4`, whose slice demos this bead checks), and every other M4 leaf.

**Unblocks:** none. This is the sink of M4's graph; when it closes, `br epic close-eligible` closes AREA-H and then the milestone epic (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`).

**Slice:** `slice-4`, "Freeze and close": A6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.6`, bare help's discovery line), B2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.2`, the guide's content), B4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.4`, the recipes end to end), H1, H2, H3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3`, the determinism audit), H4, H5 and this bead. Exit demo, recorded by this bead after the tag exists: the recipes pass; the audit's change list and the empty allowlist; the golden and the updater tests; README; the tag and the released baseline. It pre-checks criteria 3, 4, 14, 17 and 18.

**Related, not edges:** `omad-vision-8qa` (the vision bead, which receives the milestone-status comment); `omad-wez` (Forever after its launch, deferred outside M4) and `omad-claude-mod-explore-0va5` (deferred, owner-led), both left as they are (M4-D59); G3 (`omad-7ccp`, which is `omad-7ccp`); E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`), D7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.7`) and B3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3`), the owners of the three real-machine tests this bead runs; E9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9`, `compat_m3`); F9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`, the exhaustive harness); G1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1`) and G2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.2`), whose desktop checks this bead runs; A7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.7`, the completions checkpoint command); T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, whose logs the evidence quotes). This bead is the last two of the 25 units of M4's critical path (the doctor and its repairs, then the freeze: H1, H2, H4, H5 and this bead), and in the plan's computed six-lane schedule it runs in lane 1 at t = 23–25; nothing runs beside it.

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M4 plan, 2026-10-24).**

**Why this bead.** A milestone is done when its promises are demonstrated on the real machine and recorded so the next agent can check them, not when its beads are closed. This bead runs all eighteen checkpoint criteria against `main` and the development machine, records the evidence criterion by criterion in M2's and M3's `[x] N <criterion>: <evidence>` form, and then does the one thing only the end of M4 can do: it freezes the contract. It writes the first released baseline `tests/contract/released/1.0.json`, flips the golden's header to `frozen: true`, commits README's done flips with them in one commit, and tags that commit `v0.1.0`. From that commit on, every gate compares the contract with the released baseline, so an added JSON key needs a minor `schema_version` bump and anything else a major one. It is the sink of the graph and the last two units of the critical path.

**Decisions applied.**

- **M4-D57** (its own): the first tag is `v0.1.0`, made after every criterion passes and README says M4 is done; one commit holds the README flips, the header flip, the baseline with provenance (`v0.1.0`, the commit it was generated from, the date) and `.beads/`; `argc gate` runs on it first, with the baseline in place; the annotated tag `omaddons 0.1.0: contract 1.0 frozen`; the crate stays 0.1.0.
- **M4-D56** (its Tasks list names this bead for the first baseline): the released baseline is separate from the current golden, written only through `OMADDONS_ADVANCE_RELEASED_BASELINE`, compared on every gate once it exists, whatever any header says; the header is informational.
- **M4-D55:** the tag freezes the post-audit contract; the change list of H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, the pre-freeze audit) and the empty allowlist are slice 4 demo items.
- **M4-D58:** `compat_m3` (and, for M3's state, `compat_m2`) are never skipped.
- **M4-D7:** the guide's fixed point is repeated literally.
- **M4-D59:** `omad-wez` and `omad-claude-mod-explore-0va5` stay deferred outside M4; `omad-7ccp` closes as G3 (`omad-7ccp`, group commit and deferred fsyncs).
- **§3.2's pre-accepted `SKIP`s** (exactly three) and **§3.3's owner involvement** (approving the plan was the go-ahead for exactly the real-machine and desktop runs listed; no skill in the real `$HOME/.claude/skills/`; an unexpected `SKIP` is a failed criterion; no step waits on a person).

**Alternatives rejected that matter here.**

- `v1.0.0` as the first tag (M4-D57): the project is pre-alpha, and 1.0 implies a public stability the private repository does not offer.
- Folding `omad-wez` into this bead (M4-D59): M4's close would wait for a game launch.
- Deferring the checkpoint when a criterion fails or an unexpected `SKIP` appears (M3's way): no bead waits on a person; a failure files a bug or reopens the owning leaf and blocks this bead.
- Writing missing real-machine tests here (M3's checkpoint had to): each has an owning leaf (D7, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.7`, release drift and apply races; E6, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`, `doctor fix`; B3, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3`, `robot-docs install-skill`), and a missing one reopens it.
- Editing the golden's header by hand: the comparison with the current golden demands generated output; the updater writes the header.
- Closing this bead inside the tag commit: its close reason cites the tag, which does not exist until after that commit; the plan's protocol already has a later `.beads/` commit.
- Planting the desktop's credential-mode repair by changing the real token's mode: every widget on the live bar uses the real `<config>`, so a placeholder that holds no secret is planted instead, and removed after.

**Risks and how they are watched.**

- **Risk #3, doctor false positives on real homes** (medium, medium; owners the F leaves and this bead): every real-home finding and planned action is reviewed with a recorded verdict, and a wrong one is a bug that blocks the tag.
- **Risk #17, Forever launches mid-milestone** (medium, low): `omad-wez` re-verifies it outside M4; a real-machine failure from a changed layout is a failed criterion like any other.
- **Risk #22, the classifier mislabels a change** (low, high; owners A10, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.10`, the manifest and its classifier, and H2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.2`, the golden and the released-baseline mechanism): from the tag on it guards every commit; a negative control in a throwaway clone shows the gate reads the real baseline before the tag is pushed.
- **The checkpoint's own hazards**, each with a guard: a checkout on tmpfs (gate tests skip; the clone goes under `target/`, on btrfs); evidence from mixed commits (one evidence commit `E`, and a rerun rule when a fix moves it); a pushed tag on the wrong commit (checks before the push; a pushed tag is never moved); the real Forever client touched by accident (its guard compared before and after; `keyless_installs_forever` excluded when it would install there; keys sent only with `wtype -k`, M3's lesson); a secret or account name in a record (the privacy scrub before every post).

**What it unblocks and why they wait.** Nothing: it is the sink. When it closes, `br epic close-eligible` closes the H area epic and then the milestone epic. It waits for H5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.5`, the vision comments), and through H5 for everything, because it can only prove what exists, and the vision's milestone-status comment comes after H5's comments.

**How it serves the milestone's goals.** It proves G-M4-1 to G-M4-6 with evidence anyone can re-check, and it completes G-M4-5 itself: "at the first tag the contract is … enforced: every later change is compared with the released baseline, and one that does not carry its version bump fails the gate, however the current golden was regenerated." It keeps vision D21 true from the tag on ("contract changes become deliberate, never accidental"), and the thesis that omaddons stays the sole, safe, undoable authority over what it manages is demonstrated on the real machine before it is frozen.

**Confidence.** High for the protocol: every command was checked against the code at `c0ab5e9` and against the beads that own the tests it runs, and M3's record shows the form works. The uncertainty is in what the runs find, which this bead handles by blocking on the owning fix rather than by judgment at close.

#### H6 The M4 checkpoint and the first tag
- **Type** task · **P1** · **size-M** · **slice-4**
- **Blocked by:** H5 (and so, transitively, everything).
- **Unblocks:** none (the sink).
- **Background.** §3.2, §11.3, M4-D57.
- **Technical approach.**

Approving this plan is the go-ahead for its real-machine and desktop runs (§3.3): each is listed in §11.3, read-only or undone, and never touches the `Forever` client's state. The protocol includes the guide's literal fixed-point check (regenerate, `cargo build`, regenerate, `git diff --exit-code skills/`).
  2. Record each criterion in the close reason as `[x] N <criterion>: <evidence>`, quoting every `SKIP` line.

Commit the README flips, the golden's header with `frozen: true`, the first released baseline `tests/contract/released/1.0.json` (written with `OMADDONS_ADVANCE_RELEASED_BASELINE=1.0`, with its provenance: `v0.1.0`, the commit it was generated from, the date), and `.beads/`, in one commit. That commit changes a test fixture, so `argc gate` runs on it first, baseline in place (M4-D57).
  5. `git tag -a v0.1.0 -m "omaddons 0.1.0: contract 1.0 frozen"`, then push the commit and the tag.
  6. Record slice 4's demo on the milestone epic now that the tag exists (§11.3).
  7. Run `br epic close-eligible` until nothing more closes.
- **Acceptance criteria.** Every §3.2 criterion is `[x]` with evidence. The tag exists on the checkpoint commit, and the released baseline is there. Slice 4's demo is recorded.
- **Test plan.** The protocol itself.
- **Considerations.**
  - **A failed criterion.** The owning leaf is reopened, or a bug is filed `discovered-from` H6 and added as H6's blocker. H6 returns to open and waits on that dependency. It is never deferred.
  - **A `SKIP` that §3.2 did not pre-accept** is a failed criterion: it is recorded as unmet, with the reason, and handled as above. No step of this leaf waits on a person.

description:
Part 1 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6 (The M4 checkpoint and the first tag). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

Beads this section names: H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the parent: the M4 checkpoint and the first tag), H4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`, the README final pass), H5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.5`, the vision comments), T2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.2`), T3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.3`) and T4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4`) (slices 1–3 end to end, the slice demos as tests), G3 (`omad-7ccp`, group commit and deferred fsyncs, which is the re-parented `omad-7ccp`), the H area epic (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8`), the milestone epic (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`), and the next part omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.2.

H6 is M4's checkpoint: it runs all eighteen success criteria of the milestone against `main` and the development machine, records the evidence in its close reason as `[x] N <criterion>: <evidence>` (with the commit hash, test names, timings and every `SKIP` line quoted), writes the vision's "M4 is done" comment, commits README's done flips together with the first released contract baseline, tags that commit `v0.1.0` (M4-D57: "the first tag is `v0.1.0`, made by the checkpoint"; the crate already says 0.1.0, and `v1.0.0` was rejected because the project is pre-alpha), and closes the milestone. It is the sink of M4's graph, so every other M4 leaf is closed when it starts.

**This part** is the checkpoint protocol's step 1 (the freeze) and its first machine-local run (`argc gate --all` from a clean checkout), plus the work that turns the gate's output into evidence: the criterion-by-criterion map of which tests ran in the gate, and the pre-tag parts of slice 4's demo. It fixes the **evidence commit `E`** at which every later run of s2 and s3 happens. It is its own step because the gate is the fastest way to find a defect, and every later part is wasted work if it fails.

## Technical Approach

Beads this section names: H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the parent) and its parts omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.1 (this one) and omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.2 to omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.5; the H area epic (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8`) and the milestone epic (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`); A1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.1`, per-command facts), A2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.2`, the registries), A3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`, schemas and live validation), A4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`, `omaddons capabilities`), A5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.5`, `robot-docs schema` and `errors`), A7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.7`, `omaddons completions`), A9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.9`, `DetailSpec`s), A10 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.10`, the semantic manifest), B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`, the guide renderer), B2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.2`, the guide's content), B3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3`, `install-skill`), B4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.4`, the recipes), C1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.1`), C2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.2`), C3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.3`) and C4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4`) (intent inference and the corpus), D1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.1`, the approval witness), D2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.2`) and D3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.3`) (`--if-match` on the engine commands), D4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`, the plan store), D5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`, `apply`), D6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.6`, plan retention), D7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.7`, release drift and apply races), D8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8`, the approval under the lock), D9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.9`, `plans show`), E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, `doctor diagnose`), E4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4`, `doctor health` and friends), E5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`, the repair transaction), E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`, `doctor fix`), E7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7`, undo of repairs), E8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.8`, `doctor gc`), E9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9`, the M3 build against M4 state), E14 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14`, fences and barriers), F1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1`, journal detectors), F2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.2`, journal fixers), F8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.8`, `status` on plans), G2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.2`, the Issues view's repairs), G3 (`omad-7ccp`, durability, `omad-7ccp`), H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, the pre-freeze audit), H2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.2`, the golden and the baseline mechanism), H3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.3`, the determinism audit), H4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`, the README final pass), H5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.5`, the vision comments), T2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.2`), T3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.3`) and T4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4`) (the slice demos as tests).

### 1. The evidence commit and the checkout

- `git status --porcelain` in the main working copy is empty; `git fetch origin`; `main` equals `origin/main` (push `main` first if it is ahead, after confirming no peer is mid-commit with `ListAgents`). Then `E = git rev-parse main`. Record `E` (full and short) and the date.
- *Decided while writing this bead (H6):* the clean checkout is a fresh clone into a new directory under the repository's own `target/` (git-ignored; on btrfs on the development machine), never under `/tmp` (tmpfs: M3's gate ran out of space there with a 22 GiB target dir, and the clone-capable gate tests skip, and so fail, when the test target dir is not on btrfs: `tests/backup_auto.rs:108-117`, `tests/restore.rs:92-101`). Check first: `stat -f -c %T target` prints `btrfs`, and `df` shows at least 60 GiB free (the clone's own target dir, s2's compat builds and the coverage build each take tens of GiB).
- `git clone --branch main <repository> target/<checkpoint dir>`; `git -C <checkout> rev-parse HEAD` equals `E`. Every step of s1, s2 (except fuzzing) and s3 runs in this checkout. Do not delete it until H6 closes: s2 and s3 reuse its build.
- A `.beads/`-only or README-only commit after `E` does not move `E`. Any other commit does, and sends the work back to this part (the rerun rule below).

### 2. The freeze (§11.3 step 1)

1. **Every leaf but H6 is closed.** `br list --label m4 --json` (every status except `closed`) returns exactly H6, its five subtasks, AREA-H and the milestone epic. Also `br show omad-7ccp --json` is `closed` (G3 is `omad-7ccp`, re-parented at filing). Record the number of closed M4 beads.
2. **The epics.** `br epic close-eligible --dry-run --json`; then, for any area epic it lists, `br epic close-eligible --transition-comment "closed by the M4 checkpoint's freeze check: every child closed"`. Afterwards `br epic status --json` shows exactly two open epics: AREA-H (waiting on H6) and the milestone epic (waiting on AREA-H).
3. **Slice demos 1–3** exist on the milestone epic (`br comments list omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm --json`): "**Slice demo 1. Self-describing**" (T2), "**Slice demo 2. Preview, then apply exactly**" (T3) and "**Slice demo 3. Diagnose and repair**" (T4), each in the `[x] <item>: <evidence>` style. Record their comment ids. A missing or unmet one is a T leaf that closed without delivering: reopen it (the failure path below). This part never records a slice demo.
4. **Open work found during M4.** List every open bead with a `discovered-from` edge to an M4 bead (an id starting with the milestone epic's id): `br list --json`, then `br show <id> --json` for each open bead, reading `dependencies` for `dependency_type: "discovered-from"`. *Decided while writing this bead (H6):* an open bug at P0 or P1 blocks the checkpoint (the failure path); every other one is recorded as a known follow-up for the close reason and the vision comment.
5. **H5's and H4's outputs.** `br comments list omad-vision-8qa --json` holds H5's comments 1–11 of the plan's Appendix E (the last an index); `br show omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4 --json` holds, in its close reason or close comment, Appendix D's checklist ticked with README lines, and the exact replacement text for README's done flips (the status line and badge, the "What works today" M4 row and the contract row, the Roadmap's M4 row). Record both comment ids; s4 applies H4's text.

### 3. The gate from a clean checkout (§11.3 step 2.1; criterion 17's first part)

In the checkout, with `OMADDONS_ALLOW_SKIP` unset, in a background shell, output to `gate.log` in the scratch directory:

```bash
argc gate --all
```

Record: the exit code (must be 0), the wall time, each `cargo test` summary line's passed and ignored counts and their totals, the widget pipeline's bun and QML counts (the QML step runs under `--all`), `cargo deny`'s four checks (advisories, bans, licenses, sources), and every line that starts `SKIP `. On the development machine no `SKIP` is expected: the target dir is on btrfs, `/dev/ptmx` exists (`tests/terminal.rs:111-149`), and unprivileged user namespaces are available. If a sandbox test skips (`a_full_disk_leaves_nothing_behind`, `tests/backup_export.rs:494-505`; `an_addons_folder_on_a_mount_of_its_own_is_refused_before_the_swap`, `tests/install.rs:1084-1103`; `what_cannot_be_exchanged_or_is_damaged_is_refused_before_anything_moves`, `tests/restore_addon.rs:633-680`; or an M4 test built on `tests/common/mounts.rs`), that is §3.2's pre-accepted case: rerun the gate with `OMADDONS_ALLOW_SKIP` naming exactly the skipped sandbox tests and record their `SKIP` lines as pre-accepted. Any other `SKIP` or failure is an unmet criterion (the failure path).

Then save, in the checkout: `cargo test --locked -- --list` (to `list-debug.txt`), `cargo test --locked -- --ignored --list` (to `list-ignored.txt`) and `cargo test --locked --release --test perf -- --ignored --list` (to `list-perf.txt`). s2 uses the last two for the ignored-test inventory.

### 4. The criterion map: what the gate proved

For each of the eighteen criteria, from the owning leaves' close comments (the test names they list) confirmed in `list-debug.txt`, and from `gate.log` (passed), write one block `[x] N <criterion> (gate): <evidence>`; a named test absent from the list is a missing deliverable (failure path). The criteria, their owners and their gate evidence:

1. **Capabilities** (A4, with A1 and A2): `tests/capabilities.rs` (the six keys `version`, `contract_version`, `features`, `commands`, `exit_codes`, `env_vars`, and the extras `build_id`, `guide_digest`, `limits`, `sources`, `families`, `client_rules`, `target_id_forms`, `error_codes`, `warning_codes`, `actions`, `failure_modes`, `schemas_uri`, `robot_docs_uri`, `config_error`; every command, flag and alias parses with `--help`; every error, warning and action listed is registered and vice versa; the failure-mode summary's count equals the registry's; no request and no write). The 20 ms budget is s2's.
2. **Schemas** (A3, A5, A9, D5): `tests/contract/` (strict validation of every matrix row's `data` and every stderr event; the envelope-snapshot walker; the strict transform's own tests on `$ref`, maps, tagged unions and composition; every observed `details` against its code's `DetailSpec`; `apply`'s wrapper variants) and `tests/robot_docs.rs` (`robot-docs schema` for every `COMMANDS` path, the envelope and every event; `robot-docs errors` with exit, retryability, meaning and `details` specification).
3. **The guide and the skill** (B1, B2, B3, F10): `tests/skill.rs` (`skill_md_is_the_guide`, `regeneration_is_a_fixed_point`, the frontmatter-then-stamp check, the size and parse-every-command tests), `tests/robot_docs.rs::install_skill_*`, F10's skill-drift fixture tests; plus `wc -l -c skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` in the checkout (under 500 lines and 32,768 bytes). The literal fixed point is s2's; the real-machine install is s3's.
4. **Canonical intents** (B4): the eight recipe tests of `tests/skill_recipes.rs`, each recipe at most two commands.
5. **Intent inference** (C1–C4 and the command leaves' rows): `tests/contract/intent_corpus.rs` and its row count (at least 60), including `remove dbm retail` and `update dbm retail` changing nothing.
6. **Previews bind** (D1, D2, D3, D8): `tests/preconditions.rs` and the D leaves' suites (every change kind between preview and run gives `plan_stale` and changes nothing; the under-lock checks; no-op and dry-run paths check the token; equal tokens for an unchanged home, cache hit included; M3's five bindings unchanged).
7. **Stored plans** (D4, D5, D6, D7, D9): `tests/apply.rs` (D7's `drift_*`, `race_*` and `lease_*`), `tests/plans_show.rs`, and `tests/contract/special.rs`'s "dry runs leave `<state>` untouched".
8. **The widget** (G1, G2): the widget pipeline's bun tests and argv check, and the QML scenarios `test_a_routine_matching_update_applies_with_no_dialog`, `test_a_matching_update_that_adds_a_dependency_opens_the_dialog_naming_it`, `test_a_moved_release_opens_the_dialog_with_changed_since_you_looked` (G1's `tst_plans.qml`) and `test_a_credential_fix_from_issues_is_undone_with_undo_last_through_a_stored_plan`, `test_a_set_aside_row_offers_no_fix_and_shows_its_explanation_and_command` (G2's `tst_repairs.qml`). The moved-plan case is recorded from here, because no fixture server runs on the live bar. The desktop runs are s3's.
9. **The safety harness** (F9, with E5, E6, E7 and the F leaves): `tests/doctor_harness.rs`, with its wall time from `gate.log` (target under 60 s). The exhaustive suite is s2's.
10. **The doctor's surface** (E3, E4, E6, E8): `tests/doctor.rs`, `tests/doctor_repair.rs`, the doctor contract rows (eleven exit codes by name, `doctor robot-docs`'s literal strings, every exit site mapped, previews binding across processes, distinct run ids for a hundred concurrent diagnoses, `check-incomplete`). The budgets are s2's.
11. **Stuck states** (F1, F2, E14, E7): their fixtures and suites (each manual-repair state's finding and title in `status` and `doctor`; set-aside and guarded reactivation; `undo_conflict` after an overlapping change; attribution never by payload path).
12. **`status` and `doctor` agree** (F8): the agreement test over every fixture. The 5 ms budget is s2's; the real-home comparison is s3's.
13. **Durability** (G3): `tests/engine_durability.rs` (the pinned fsync counts for an install, an update, an undo, a whole restore and a repair; the injected barrier failures) and `tests/engine_crash.rs` unchanged; G3's close comment for the written power-loss arguments. The btrfs figures are s2's.
14. **The contract is frozen** (H1, H2, H3, A10): H1's comment "**Pre-freeze audit change list**" (and any addenda) and `tests/contract/rules_allowlist.txt` with no line left; `tests/contract/wire_names.rs` (both comparisons and H2's updater tests: an addition, a removal, a requiredness change, a removed flag and a changed default each still fail against a synthetic released baseline after the documented regeneration, and a `frozen: false` header changes nothing); `tests/determinism.rs` and the repeat and coverage tests. The baseline and the tag are s4's and s5's.
15. **Completions** (A7): `tests/completions.rs` (five shells snapshot-tested, `bash -n`, never skipped, `--json` `{shell, script}`). The zsh and fish checks are s2's.
16. **Older builds** (E9): README's Limitations entry for pre-M4 builds exists (quote its first line). The run is s2's.
17. **Gate and checkpoint runs**: this part's gate run.
18. **README and vision** (H4, H5): H4's checklist and flip text, H5's comments (step 2.5 above). The flips and the tag are s4's and s5's.

### 5. Slice 4's pre-tag parts (§11.3 step 1)

Verify and record, for s5's demo comment: the recipes pass (criterion 4 above); H1's change list exists (count its entries by disposition) and the allowlist is empty; the golden is committed (`tests/contract/manifest.json` with `"header": {"contract": "1.0", "frozen": false}`, `tests/contract/wire_names.txt` starting `# contract 1.0` and `# frozen: false`, and no `tests/contract/released/` directory yet) and its updater tests pass; README is reconciled (H4's checklist).

### 6. The evidence comment

Write `evidence-1.md` in the scratch directory and post it with `br comments add omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6 -f evidence-1.md`, titled "**Checkpoint evidence 1 of 3: the freeze and the gate from a clean checkout (at <E short>)**": the freeze (counts, the epics, the slice demo comment ids, the open follow-ups), the gate (command, wall time, counts, deny, `SKIP` lines), the eighteen gate blocks of section 4, and slice 4's pre-tag parts. **Before posting, run the privacy scrub:** the file contains no absolute or home path (home → `<home>`, client dirs → `<client dir>` with the target id), no host name (`uname -n`), no user name (`id -un`), no account, realm or character name (a scratch script compares the file with the directory names under each client's `WTF/Account/`, printing only "clean" or matching line numbers), no token. Then close this subtask: `br close omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.1 --reason "done: freeze and gate at <E>; evidence comment <id> · found: <ids>"`.

### 7. When something fails here

Record it as `[ ] N … UNMET: <what>` in the evidence file. A missing deliverable (a named test absent, a slice demo comment never posted) reopens its leaf: `br reopen <leaf> --reason "M4 checkpoint: <what is missing>"`. Anything else files a bug: `br create "<what fails>" --type bug --priority 1 --labels m4 --description-file <file> --deps discovered-from:omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6` (the failing command, its scrubbed output, the criterion, `E`, the log's name; `br lint` clean). Then `br dep add omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6 <id>`, `br dep add omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.1 <id>`, and `br update omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.1 --status open --transition-comment "blocked: <id> (criterion N unmet)"`. Never defer, never `--force`. When the blocker lands as a code commit, that commit is the new `E`: start this part again from section 1 in a fresh clone, and post a new evidence comment that says which one it supersedes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `E` is recorded: the head of `main`, equal to `origin/main`, with a clean working tree, and the clean checkout is a fresh clone at `E` on btrfs under the repository's `target/` with at least 60 GiB free.
- [ ] `br list --label m4 --json` lists only H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`), its subtasks, the H area epic and the milestone epic; every area epic but H is closed; G3 (`omad-7ccp`, `omad-7ccp`) is closed.
- [ ] The three slice demo comments of slices 1–3 exist on the milestone epic, and their ids are recorded.
- [ ] Every open bead discovered from M4 work is listed; none is an open P0–P1 bug.
- [ ] The eleven vision comments of H5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.5`) and the checklist of H4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`) with its prepared flip text exist, and their ids are recorded.
- [ ] `argc gate --all` exited 0 in the clean checkout, with its counts, wall time and `cargo deny` result recorded and no `SKIP` other than a pre-accepted sandbox one.
- [ ] `list-debug.txt`, `list-ignored.txt` and `list-perf.txt` are saved for s2.
- [ ] Every criterion's gate part is recorded with the test names that proved it, each confirmed present at `E`.
- [ ] Slice 4's pre-tag parts are verified: the recipes, the change list of H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`) and the empty allowlist, the golden with its `frozen: false` header and passing updater tests, and README's checklist.
- [ ] Evidence comment 1 is posted on H6 after a clean privacy scrub.
- [ ] `br lint` is clean for this subtask and every bead it filed.

## Test Plan

Beads this section names: H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the parent), T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs).

### Unit tests

None: this part writes no code. The gate it runs executes every unit test of the repository; their totals are recorded.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

The run is `argc gate --all` in the clean checkout at `E`: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --locked` (every M4 suite: `tests/capabilities.rs`, `tests/robot_docs.rs`, `tests/skill.rs`, `tests/skill_recipes.rs`, `tests/contract/`, `tests/determinism.rs`, `tests/completions.rs`, `tests/apply.rs`, `tests/plans_show.rs`, `tests/preconditions.rs`, `tests/doctor.rs`, `tests/doctor_harness.rs`, `tests/doctor_repair.rs`, `tests/engine_durability.rs`, `tests/engine_crash.rs`, `tests/journal.rs`, `tests/e2e_slice1.rs`, `tests/e2e_slice2.rs`, `tests/e2e_slice3.rs`, and every M1–M3 suite), the widget pipeline with its QML step, `ubs` (nothing changed, so it runs on nothing) and `cargo deny check`. Expected: exit 0, no `SKIP` line.

### Logging

`gate.log` (the whole gate output), `list-debug.txt`, `list-ignored.txt`, `list-perf.txt` and `evidence-1.md` in the scratch directory. A failing integration test that uses T1's `TestLog` prints `test log: <path>` and its last 20 steps; that path (relative to the checkout) and the transcript's failing step go into the bug. The evidence comment quotes counts and test names, never whole logs.

### Checkpoint-only runs and the `SKIP` rule

This part's run is `argc gate --all`. The `SKIP` rule (`tests/common/checkpoint.rs:1-43`): a test that cannot run prints `SKIP <test>: <reason>` and fails unless `OMADDONS_ALLOW_SKIP` names it. In the gate only the sandbox tests' `SKIP` may be accepted, and only where unprivileged user namespaces are unavailable.

## Considerations

Beads this section names: H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the parent), H4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`, the README final pass).

- **Disk.** The clean clone's target dir is about 22 GiB or more; the space check comes first, and the checkout is kept until H6 closes.
- **A wrong filesystem shows up as `SKIP`s, not as passes:** the clone-capable gate tests skip, and so fail, off btrfs. That is why the checkout's location is fixed.
- **Peers.** By now every leaf is closed, but a blocker's fix may be in flight; `E` is taken only when `main` is pushed and no peer is mid-commit (`ListAgents`, `SendMessage`).
- **Hot spots:** none. This part writes only `.beads/` (the comment, closures and any filed bugs), committed with `br sync --flush-only` and `git add .beads/` before the session ends.
- **Privacy.** The gate runs on synthetic `TestEnv` homes only; its output names no real path, but the scrub runs anyway.
- **Decided defaults** (recorded in the close reason of H6): the checkout's location and the space floor; open P0–P1 bugs block, other follow-ups are listed; H4's flip text is taken from its close reason or close comment.

## Dependencies

Beads this section names: H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the parent), omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.2 (the next part).

- **Parent:** H6, the M4 checkpoint and the first tag.
- **Before it:** nothing inside H6. Through H6's blocker H5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.5`, the vision comments) it waits for every other M4 leaf.
- **After it:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.2 (the checkpoint-only runs), which reuses this part's checkout, `E` and its test lists, and must not start before the gate has passed, because a gate failure moves `E`.
