title: The checkpoint-only runs: perf, bench, fuzz, compatibility, the exhaustive harness, the guide's fixed point, live probes, coverage and the ignored-test inventory
description:
Part 2 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6 (The M4 checkpoint and the first tag). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

Beads this section names: H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the parent: the M4 checkpoint and the first tag), its parts omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.1 (before) and omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.3 (after), E5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`, the repair transaction, which adds the `journal` fuzz target), E9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9`, the M3 build against M4 state), F9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`, the safety harness), A7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.7`, `omaddons completions`).

H6 is M4's checkpoint: it runs all eighteen success criteria of the milestone against `main` and the development machine, records the evidence as `[x] N <criterion>: <evidence>` with the commit hash, test names, timings and every `SKIP` line quoted, then freezes the contract and tags the first release, `v0.1.0` (M4-D57). omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.1 fixed the **evidence commit `E`** (the head of `main`, pushed, with every other M4 leaf closed), made a fresh clone of it on btrfs under the repository's `target/` (the **checkout**), ran `argc gate --all` there, and saved the test lists `list-ignored.txt` (debug) and `list-perf.txt` (release perf) in the scratch directory.

**This part** runs the checkpoint protocol's remaining machine-local runs (§11.3 step 2.2 to 2.9), in the plan's order, at `E`: the perf budgets, `argc bench`, every fuzz target, both compatibility characterizations, the exhaustive harness, the guide's literal fixed point, the live probes and coverage; then every checkpoint command README's block lists that the plan's list lacks; then an inventory proving every ignored test was run or has a reason not to be. These runs are checkpoint-only: they are `#[ignore]`d or slow, never part of the gate. It is its own step because it takes most of a day of wall time and needs a quiet machine (the perf budgets), and because nothing here should touch the real home: that is s3's.

**The rules these runs are judged by**, restated:

- **The `SKIP` rule** (`tests/common/checkpoint.rs:1-43`): a checkpoint test that cannot run prints `SKIP <test>: <reason>` on stderr and **fails**, unless `OMADDONS_ALLOW_SKIP` names it; an accepted skip still prints its line.
- **Pre-accepted `SKIP`s, exactly three** (§3.2): `keyless_installs_forever` while the Forever client's guard stands (s3's); the bind-mount and size-limited-tmpfs sandbox tests where unprivileged user namespaces are unavailable; the `zsh -n` and `fish --no-execute` checks where those shells are not installed (bash's is never skipped). Any other `SKIP` is an unmet criterion.
- **The compatibility characterizations are never skipped** (§3.2, M4-D58): an older commit is built with the toolchain it records (`af10e34` and `c0ab5e9` both pin `1.97.1` in `rust-toolchain.toml`, installed by rustup on demand), or a provenance-verified binary of it is used; if neither can be had, criterion 16 is unmet. "Compiler inconvenience is not evidence that storage is safe."
- **Criterion 17** (gate and checkpoint runs): "every fuzz target runs 10 minutes, and the new `journal` target 30 minutes. The perf budgets (`tests/perf.rs`) pass, the live probes and the real-machine tests pass with every `SKIP` quoted, and line coverage is recorded."

## Technical Approach

Beads this section names: H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the parent) and omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.1; A4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`, `omaddons capabilities`), A7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.7`, completions), B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`, the guide renderer), B4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.4`, the recipes), D8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8`, the approval under the lock), E4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4`, `doctor health`), E5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`, the repair transaction), E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`, `doctor fix`), E9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9`, `compat_m3`), F6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.6`, caches), F7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.7`, the network checks), F8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.8`, `status` on the registry), F9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`, the harness), F10 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.10`, skill drift), G3 (`omad-7ccp`, durability).

**Ground rules.** Every run is at `E`, in the checkout from omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.1 (check `git -C <checkout> rev-parse HEAD` equals `E` and `git -C <checkout> status --porcelain` is empty before each), except fuzzing (step 3). Each long run goes to a background shell with its output saved to a file in the scratch directory, named below. Nothing else runs on the machine during steps 1 and 2 (no fuzzing, no build, no other agent's gate): the budgets need a quiet machine.

### 1. Perf budgets (§11.3 step 2.2; criteria 1, 10, 12, 13, 17)

```bash
cargo test --release --test perf -- --ignored --skip bench_home --skip live_home --test-threads=1   # → perf.log
```

`bench_home`, `live_home` and `coverage_home` are builders that build nothing without their variables (`tests/perf.rs:226-303`). Every budget passes. Record each test's median (and p95 where printed), and quote in particular:

- `capabilities_answers_in_under_20_ms` (A4's name; criterion 1: median of 21 under 20 ms);
- `doctor_health_stays_under_200_ms` and `each_quick_detector_stays_under_5_ms` (E4's; criterion 10);
- `status_cached_stays_under_5_ms_with_the_cached_tier` (F8's; criterion 12: on the realistic perf home plus one doctor run directory and 200 stored plans), beside M3's `status_cached_stays_under_5_ms_with_a_realistic_memo`;
- `release_build_lists_no_test_fixers` (E6's), `skill_drift_detector_stays_within_its_cached_share` (F10's);
- the reports, which are not budgets: `the_approval_check_under_the_lock_costs` (D8's), `blob_reverification_cost` (F6's), and G3's btrfs figures (an install's and a whole restore's lock hold, the install's fsyncs under the lock against the count G3's design gate derived, forecast at most 44 from 62, and the per-file fsync table before and after), measured beside `backups_of_500_mb_meet_their_budgets`.

The btrfs tests skip when `target/` is not on btrfs (`tests/perf.rs:967`, `:1031-1034`); in the checkout under the repository's `target/` it is. A `SKIP` here is an unmet criterion 17.

### 2. `argc bench` (§11.3 step 2.3)

`argc bench` in the checkout (`→ bench.log`; needs `hyperfine` and `jq`). Every row with a target is marked `✓`: `status --cached` under 5 ms, `status (drift)` under 30 ms, `update --all --dry-run warm` under 2,000 ms, `update --all cold` under 10,000 ms (`scripts/bench.sh:85-105`); the script exits non-zero on a missed target or when a warm run added a `net.log` line (`:109-114`). Quote the table and the `net.log` line. A `✗` or a non-zero exit is an unmet criterion 17.

### 3. Fuzzing (§11.3 step 2.4; criterion 17)

*Decided while writing this bead (H6):* in the **main working copy**, at `E` with a clean tree, so that the git-ignored `fuzz/corpus/` accumulated by earlier runs makes these runs deeper (`.gitignore:3-4`). Before: `rustc +<nightly> --version` (a nightly at least the crate's `rust-version`, 1.97, which `_fuzz_check` enforces, `Argcfile.sh:76-95`), the target list (`ls fuzz/fuzz_targets/`: 21 targets, E5's `journal` among them), and the full file listing of `fuzz/artifacts/` (`→ artifacts-before.txt`).

```bash
argc fuzz-all --time 600 --toolchain <nightly>    # every target, 10 minutes each → fuzz-all.log
argc fuzz journal --time 1800 --toolchain <nightly>   # journal, 30 more minutes → fuzz-journal.log
```

After: each target's seconds and run count (libFuzzer's last `#<runs>` line and `Done <n> runs in <s> second(s)`), and the listing of `fuzz/artifacts/` again (`→ artifacts-after.txt`). A file in the second listing that is not in the first is a crash: an unmet criterion 17, whose bug carries the target and the artifact's file name. Run nothing else on the machine while fuzzing if s2's remaining steps can wait; the remaining steps may not start until fuzzing ends (the timing in step 6 and the builds in step 4 compete for the CPU).

### 4. The compatibility characterizations (§11.3 step 2.5; criteria 16, 17)

In the checkout:

```bash
cargo test --test compat_m2 -- --ignored --nocapture   # → compat_m2.log
cargo test --test compat_m3 -- --ignored --nocapture   # → compat_m3.log
```

Debug builds of the tests: **no `--release`**, which M3's plan got wrong (`tests/compat_m2.rs:14` is `#![cfg(debug_assertions)]`, so a release run runs nothing). Each builds its old commit with the toolchain that commit records. `tests/compat_m2.rs` reports a failed build of `af10e34` as a `SKIP` (`:367-373`, `:601-607`, `:689-695`); *decided while writing this bead (H6):* such a `SKIP` is an unmet criterion 17, never accepted, because §3.2 never skips a compatibility characterization. `tests/compat_m3.rs` (E9's) has no skip path at all. Quote both tables, every row's class (E9's `untouched`, `recovered_by_m3` where its family allows it), E9's provenance record (`target/compat/c0ab5e9.provenance.json`: toolchain, `rustc -vV`, binary digest) and each run's wall time. A `fail` row is an unmet criterion 16.

### 5. The exhaustive harness (§11.3 step 2.6; criterion 9)

`cargo test --test doctor_harness -- --ignored` in the checkout (`→ harness.log`): F9's combination suite (primitive boundaries crossed with the declared pairs and repeated-recovery depths). Record passed counts and the wall time.

### 6. The guide's fixed point (§11.3 step 2.7; criterion 3)

In the checkout, literally:

```bash
OMADDONS_UPDATE_SKILL=1 cargo test --test skill
git diff --exit-code skills/
cargo build
OMADDONS_UPDATE_SKILL=1 cargo test --test skill
git diff --exit-code skills/
```

(`→ fixedpoint.log`). Both diffs are empty, and the stamp line (the line after the frontmatter's closing `---`, `<!-- omaddons guide sha256:<hex> -->`) is the same before, between and after; quote it. A non-empty first diff means `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` was not current at `E` (an unmet criterion 3: the skill no longer equals the guide); a non-empty second diff means the guide embeds something the build changes (B1's fixed point is broken). The plan writes the sequence as regenerate, build, regenerate, diff; the extra diff after the first regeneration was decided while writing this bead (H6) to tell those two failures apart. Afterwards `git -C <checkout> status --porcelain` is empty.

### 7. The live probes (§11.3 step 2.8; criterion 17)

```bash
OMADDONS_LIVE=1 cargo test --test live_probes -- --ignored                       # → live.log
OMADDONS_LIVE=1 cargo test --locked --lib -- --ignored live_github_request       # → live-unit.log
```

The first includes F7's `doctor_online_probes_the_real_hosts` (`doctor --online` against the real hosts, one request per source) and the M1–M3 probes (`catalog_matches_declared_flavors` with its addon × client matrix, the WowAce probes). The second is the one live probe that lives in a unit test (`src/net/tests.rs:640-642`, whose ignore reason names `OMADDONS_LIVE=1 cargo test -- --ignored live_github_request`; `--lib` runs the same test from the library's unit-test binary alone). They use throwaway homes, never the real one. Record passed counts, the request counts the probes print, and any mismatch line.

### 8. Coverage (§11.3 step 2.9; criterion 17)

`cargo llvm-cov --summary-only` in the checkout (`→ coverage.log`): lines, functions and regions, quoted beside M3's 95.91% lines. *Decided while writing this bead (H6):* no threshold, because the plan sets none ("line coverage is recorded"). Afterwards no `*.profraw` is left in the checkout (`git status --porcelain --ignored | grep profraw` prints nothing; `.gitignore:6` ignores them).

### 9. README's checkpoint block (decided while writing this bead, H6)

The plan's list predates the leaves that added checkpoint commands to README's "Milestone checkpoints (not part of the gate)" block (`README.md:2642-2652` at `c0ab5e9`). Read that block at `E` and run every command in it that steps 1–8 and s3 do not already run, exactly as README writes it, recording each. One is known: A7's

```bash
OMADDONS_ALLOW_SKIP=zsh_accepts_its_script,fish_accepts_its_script cargo test --test completions -- --ignored   # → completions.log
```

where `zsh_accepts_its_script` and `fish_accepts_its_script` print the pre-accepted `SKIP` when their shell is missing (neither zsh nor fish was installed on the development machine when this bead was written) and must pass where it is installed; quote both lines. E9, F9 or B4 may have added others (B4's recorder test is a recorder, not a checkpoint run: see step 10). The real-machine command is s3's.

### 10. The inventory of ignored tests (decided while writing this bead, H6)

Every `#[ignore]` test in `list-ignored.txt` and `list-perf.txt` (from omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.1) gets exactly one class, recorded as counts per class plus the names in the last two:

- **run** by a command of steps 1–9, or by s3's real-machine command (all of `tests/real_machine.rs`);
- **builder**: `bench_home`, `live_home`, `coverage_home`;
- **child process** of another test (its ignore reason says "child process" or "a child of");
- **recorder** (`OMADDONS_RECORD=1`) or **seed writer** (`OMADDONS_WRITE_SEEDS=1`): never run at a checkpoint, because they rewrite committed fixtures from the live hosts;
- **widget-pipeline helper**: run by the gate's widget pipeline (their reasons say so);
- **not run, with its reason**: `discover_custom::real_custom_client` (a real-machine test outside the runs the plan's approval lists; it needs `OMADDONS_REAL_CUSTOM_ROOT`).

An ignored test whose reason names a checkpoint command that nothing ran is run by that command now; if it cannot be, it is an unmet criterion 17.

### 11. The evidence comment

Write `evidence-2.md` and post it with `br comments add omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6 -f evidence-2.md`, titled "**Checkpoint evidence 2 of 3: the checkpoint-only runs (at <E short>)**": one section per step with its command, exit, wall time, counts, the figures above and every `SKIP` line quoted; then the per-criterion blocks this part completes (`[x] 1 … (budget)`, `[x] 3 … (fixed point)`, `[x] 9 … (exhaustive)`, `[x] 10 … (budgets)`, `[x] 12 … (budget)`, `[x] 13 … (btrfs figures)`, `[x] 15 … (zsh, fish)`, `[x] 16 …`, `[x] 17 … (machine-local runs)`). Run the privacy scrub first (no absolute or home path, host name, user name, account name or token; the live probes print host names of the public sources, such as `api.github.com`, which are not the machine's and may stay). Then `br close omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.2 --reason "done: checkpoint-only runs at <E>; evidence comment <id> · found: <ids>"`.

### 12. When something fails here

Record it as `[ ] N … UNMET: <what>`. A missing deliverable (a checkpoint test an owner's bead names that does not exist) reopens its leaf (`br reopen <leaf> --reason "M4 checkpoint: <what is missing>"`); anything else files a bug: `br create "<what fails>" --type bug --priority 1 --labels m4 --description-file <file> --deps discovered-from:omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6` (the command, its scrubbed output, the criterion, `E`, the log's name; `br lint` clean). Then `br dep add omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6 <id>`, `br dep add omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.2 <id>`, `br update omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.2 --status open --transition-comment "blocked: <id> (criterion N unmet)"`. Never defer, never `--force`. When the fix lands as a code commit, it is the new `E`: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.1 is reopened and rerun first (a fresh clone, the gate), then this part from step 1. *Decided while writing this bead (H6):* only the fuzz runs may be carried over, and only when `git diff --stat <old E> <new E>` touches nothing under `src/`, `fuzz/`, `build.rs`, `Cargo.toml` or `Cargo.lock`, recorded as "carried from <old E>".

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The perf run passed at `E` with every budget met and no `SKIP`, and the medians of the capabilities, `doctor health`, quick-detector, `status --cached`, test-fixer and skill-drift tests, the approval-check and blob re-verification cost reports, and the btrfs lock holds and fsync table are recorded.
- [ ] `argc bench` shows `✓` on every row that has a target, and its table is quoted.
- [ ] Every one of the 21 fuzz targets ran 600 s and `journal` 1,800 s more, with run counts recorded and no new file in `fuzz/artifacts/`.
- [ ] `compat_m2` and `compat_m3` ran as debug test builds with no `SKIP`, every `compat_m3` row green, and both tables and the M3 build's provenance record are quoted.
- [ ] The exhaustive harness passed, with its wall time.
- [ ] The guide's fixed point left `skills/` unchanged after the first regeneration and after the rebuild and second regeneration, with the stamp line quoted.
- [ ] The live probes and `live_github_request` passed, with their request counts.

- [ ] Evidence comment 2 is posted on H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`) after a clean privacy scrub.
- [ ] `br lint` is clean for this subtask and every bead it filed.

## Test Plan

Beads this section names: H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the parent), T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs), E9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9`, `compat_m3`).

### Unit tests

None: this part writes no code.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

The runs of steps 1 to 9, each with its expected outcome: perf (every budget passes), bench (every target ✓), fuzz (no crash), compat (no `SKIP`, every row green), the exhaustive harness (passes), the fixed point (two empty diffs), live probes (pass), coverage (recorded), README's extra commands (pass, with only pre-accepted `SKIP`s). No scenario is written here; each suite's own scenarios are what run.

### Logging

The scratch files `perf.log`, `bench.log`, `artifacts-before.txt`, `artifacts-after.txt`, `fuzz-all.log`, `fuzz-journal.log`, `compat_m2.log`, `compat_m3.log`, `harness.log`, `fixedpoint.log`, `live.log`, `live-unit.log`, `coverage.log`, `completions.log`, `inventory.md` and `evidence-2.md`. `compat_m3` logs its M3 and M4 runs through T1's `TestLog` (E9's suite writes `table.md` in each test's log directory under `<CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR>/test-logs/compat_m3/`); a failing row's transcript path, relative to the checkout, goes into its bug. The evidence comment quotes figures and lines, never whole logs.

### Checkpoint-only runs and the `SKIP` rule

The exact commands are in steps 1 to 9. Accepted `SKIP` lines here: only `zsh_accepts_its_script` and `fish_accepts_its_script` when their shell is missing. Every other `SKIP` (a btrfs budget, a compat build, a live probe) is an unmet criterion.

## Considerations

Beads this section names: H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the parent), E9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9`, `compat_m3`), G3 (`omad-7ccp`, durability).

- **Time.** Fuzzing alone takes about four hours (21 × 10 minutes, plus 30); the compat builds compile two old commits; the exhaustive harness is long. Run each in the background with its log in the scratch directory, and record wall times.
- **Quiet machine.** The perf budgets are medians of 21 runs with tight budgets (`status --cached` under 5 ms); a concurrent build or fuzz run fails them for reasons that are not regressions. If a budget fails once, rerun that test alone (`cargo test --release --test perf -- --ignored --exact <name>`) on an idle machine before calling it unmet, and record both runs.
- **Disk.** The compat builds (`target/compat/` in the checkout) and the coverage build add tens of GiB; s1 checked the space.
- **Measured versus forecast.** G3's install fsync count is pinned by its design gate, not by the plan's forecast of 44; record the measured count and the pinned target, and pass the vision comment (s4) any figure that differs from the plan's forecast.
- **Privacy.** These runs use synthetic homes; the live probes reach public hosts only. The scrub still runs before posting.
- **Hot spots:** none. This part writes only `.beads/` and scratch files.

## Dependencies

Beads this section names: H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the parent), omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.1 (before), omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.3 (after).

- **After it:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.3 (the real machine and the desktop), which runs only when everything that could force a code change has passed, so the owner's clients are touched once.

title: The real-machine and desktop runs, and the review of every real-home finding
description:
Part 3 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6 (The M4 checkpoint and the first tag). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

Beads this section names: H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the parent: the M4 checkpoint and the first tag), its parts omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.1, omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.2 (before) and omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.4 (after), D7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.7`, release drift and apply races), E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`, `doctor fix`), B3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3`, `robot-docs install-skill`), F7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.7`, plugins, secrets and the network), G1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1`, the widget previews and applies plans), G2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.2`, the Issues view runs repairs).

H6 is M4's checkpoint: it runs all eighteen success criteria against `main` and the development machine, records the evidence as `[x] N <criterion>: <evidence>`, then freezes the contract and tags `v0.1.0` (M4-D57). omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.1 fixed the **evidence commit `E`** and a clean **checkout** of it on btrfs under the repository's `target/`, and passed `argc gate --all`; omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.2 passed every machine-local checkpoint run. Nothing that could force a code change is left.

**This part** runs the protocol's step 3 (§11.3), the only part that touches the owner's real home and desktop: the real-machine suite (with M4's three new tests), the review of every finding the doctor reports on the real home, and the desktop checks of the bar widget. It serves criterion 8 (the widget applies what it shows, "checked … on the desktop, through IPC `state()` plus a screenshot"), criterion 3 (the real-machine install of the skill into a tempdir), criterion 7 (one update applied through its stored plan on a real client), criterion 12 (status and doctor agree, here on the real home) and criterion 17 ("the live probes and the real-machine tests pass with every `SKIP` quoted … On the development machine, `omaddons doctor --json` reports no finding that is wrong: H6 reviews each one and records it in the close reason. `omaddons doctor fix --dry-run` plans only actions H6 judges right"). It is risk 3's mitigation (doctor false positives on real homes erode trust).

**The owner's approval** (§3.3 of the plan, restated): approving the plan was the go-ahead for exactly these runs, each read-only or undone, none touching the Forever client's state: the doctor on the real home (`doctor` and `doctor fix --dry-run`, read-only); one update previewed and applied on a non-Forever client, then undone; the widget's Update preview on the live bar; a doctor repair from the Issues view, undone; `install-skill --dry-run` against the real home, and a real install into a tempdir only. Nothing installs the skill into the real `$HOME/.claude/skills/`. No step waits on a person, and no other real-machine run is made.

## Technical Approach

Beads this section names: H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the parent) and omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.1; B3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3`, `install_skill_round_trip`), D7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.7`, `apply_one_update_and_undo`), E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`, `doctor_on_the_real_home`), F7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.7`, the credential-mode detector and its chmod fixer), F8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.8`, `status` on the registry), G1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1`, the widget's Update), G2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.2`, the widget's repairs).

### 0. Preconditions and the before state

- `E` is unchanged: `git -C <checkout> rev-parse HEAD` equals `E`, the tree is clean, omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.2 is closed.
- **Every client is stopped.** `omaddons status --json` shows `running: false` on every target. A running client is never quit by the agent, and a `SKIP` because of it (`skip_if_running`, `tests/real_machine.rs:159-170`) is never accepted: wait, polling `omaddons status --cached --json` every 15 minutes, until every client has stopped. Waiting on a running game is waiting on the machine's state, not on a person's decision.
- **The before state**, recorded in `hashes-before.txt` by two scratch scripts that only read:
  - `treehash.sh <dir>`: every entry's relative path, type, mode and symlink target, and every regular file's SHA-256, sorted (`LC_ALL=C`), hashed;
  - `metahash.sh <dir>`: every entry's relative path, type, mode, size and symlink target, sorted, hashed; no file content is read;
  - for the **Forever client** (its guard, as `forever_guard()` in `tests/real_machine.rs:222-248` records it): the record generation (`<state>/targets/<key>.json`'s `generation`), the managed addons and folders (`omaddons list -t forever --json`), and `treehash.sh` of its `<client dir>/Interface/AddOns`;
  - for every other client: `treehash.sh` of its `<client dir>/Interface/AddOns` and `metahash.sh` of its `<client dir>/WTF` (the hash only; names under `WTF/` are never printed);
  - `metahash.sh <config>` (no content: `<config>` holds credentials);
  - the number of lines of `<state>/history.jsonl`.

### 1. The real-machine suite (§11.3 step 3.1)

In the checkout:

```bash
OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE=1 OMADDONS_LIVE=1 OMADDONS_ALLOW_SKIP=keyless_installs_forever \
  cargo test --test real_machine -- --ignored --test-threads=1        # → real_machine.log
```

M4 adds three tests to the suite, each owned by its leaf, which this part only runs: `doctor_on_the_real_home` (E6: `doctor --json` and `doctor fix --dry-run --json` on the real home, read-only, printing every finding and planned action, asserting no write outside `<state>/doctor/`, no request, and every AddOns and `WTF/` tree and the Forever set unchanged), `apply_one_update_and_undo` (D7: one update on a non-Forever client previewed, applied through its stored plan, checked with `plans show`, and undone, with every AddOns and `WTF/` hash as before; it makes its own update when none exists) and `install_skill_round_trip` (B3: `install-skill --dry-run` against the real `HOME` resolves `<skills>` and writes nothing; `install-skill --dir <tempdir>/omaddons` writes the guide's bytes and a second run is `unchanged`). A missing one is a reopened leaf (the failure path), never something this part writes.

**The one accepted `SKIP`** is `keyless_installs_forever`'s: it skips while the Forever client manages addons (`tests/real_machine.rs:753-762`, the stress-test set), and otherwise installs into the Forever client and undoes it. *Decided while writing this bead (H6):* §3.3 forbids any change to the Forever client's state at this checkpoint, so before the run, if `omaddons list -t forever --json` shows no managed addon, append `--skip keyless_installs_forever` after `--test-threads=1`, and record "`keyless_installs_forever`: not run (the pre-accepted case of §3.2): the Forever client manages no addons, so the test would install into it". Every other `SKIP` (a variable unset, a client running) is an unmet criterion 17. Record the passed count, quote every `SKIP` line exactly, and quote the notes of the three M4 tests (they print the home directory as `<home>`).

### 2. The review of every real-home finding (criterion 17; risk 3)

From `doctor_on_the_real_home`'s notes ("doctor findings" and "doctor fix plan"); if they were cut, run `omaddons doctor --json` and `omaddons doctor fix --dry-run --json` again with the checkout's build (read-only, within the approval). Write `doctor-review.md`:

| Finding | Instance | Severity · confidence | Verdict | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fm-…` | resource key, paths as placeholders | P2 · high | true / **false** | what was checked |

- **A finding is true** only when the state it names really exists, checked independently and read-only (the file, its mode, the journal, the stale widget digest is really there), its severity and confidence are reasonable for that state, and its remediation (the argv or the prose) is what would fix it. Otherwise it is false.
- **For each planned action** of `doctor fix --dry-run`: `seq`, `fm`, `op`, path (placeholder), `bytes`, and a verdict: right only when it repairs a true finding, is the minimal operation for it, stays inside the declared write scope, writes nothing under any `WTF/`, needs no `--force`, and touches the Forever client only if the finding is the Forever client's own (and even then nothing is run here). The dry run's `delegated_planned` recoveries are judged the same way.
- A false finding or a wrong action is a bug (the failure path), P1 when following its remediation would do harm, P2 otherwise; a P2 here still blocks this part, because criterion 17 says no finding is wrong.
- *Decided while writing this bead (H6):* also compare, on the real home, `status`'s issues with the doctor's findings of the same tiers, the rule of criterion 12 that F8's test proves on fixtures: the keys `(id, client key or "machine", addon)` of `omaddons status --json`'s issues (`targets[].issues[]` and `data.issues[]`) must equal those of `omaddons doctor --quick --json`'s findings whose failure modes are of tier `cached` or `quick` (the tiers from `omaddons doctor capabilities --json`). Both commands are read-only. A difference is a bug.

### 3. The desktop (§11.3 step 3.2; criterion 8)

*Decided while writing this bead (H6):* the widget is installed first and its currency confirmed last; the plan lists `omarchy install` last, but an outdated widget is warned about and turns read-only (README's "What works today" widget row, `README.md:160` at `c0ab5e9`), so the checks would otherwise exercise the old widget. Keys are sent only as key names, `wtype -k <Key>`: during M3's checkpoint `wtype Escape` typed the text "Escape" into the live panel, and its `p` pinned addons on the Forever client. `<widget id>` is the widget's IPC id, the constant `WIDGET_ID` (`src/state/paths.rs:22`) that `Paths::omarchy_plugin_id()` returns (`:195-199`). Before and after every step, save `omarchy-shell <widget id> state` to `desktop/state-<step>-before.json` and `-after.json`, and a `grim` screenshot to `desktop/<step>.png`, in the scratch directory; they are named in the evidence, never committed or attached. The panel's keys are those of README's `### omarchy` section.

1. **Install the M4 build.** `cargo install --locked --path <checkout>` (README's documented install, into `$HOME/.cargo/bin`), then `omaddons omarchy install`; `omaddons omarchy status --json` says current and enabled, and IPC `state()` answers.
2. **The widget's Update on a matching plan, with no dialog** (G1). Choose a non-Forever, stopped client and one managed, unpinned addon with an update whose CLI preview, `omaddons update <addon> -t <id> --dry-run --json`, has `data.approval.routine: true` (no dependency added, no folder removed, no local edit replaced, the same source and channel). If no client has one, make one as D7's test does: `omaddons install dominos --version <an older tag> -t <id>` (which pins it), then `omaddons unpin Dominos -t <id>`, recording each transaction id. Open the panel at the Updates view (`omarchy-shell <widget id> show updates`), narrow it to that client with the panel's client filter, select the row (confirm the selection in a screenshot before pressing anything), and press Enter (`wtype -k Return`). Expected: IPC `state()` shows `lastPreview` `{resource: "update_addon", decision: "direct", planId: <id>}` and `confirm: null` (G1's keys), no dialog opened, and the result line names the update; screenshot. Then, with the CLI: undo every transaction this step made, newest first (`omaddons undo <tx>`: the widget's update, then the unpin and the install if they were made), prune the backups this step made (`omaddons backup list -t <id> --json` before and after; `omaddons backup prune <backup id> -t <id>` for each new one, except a client's newest checkpoint, which `backup prune` refuses by design: record it), and check that client's AddOns `treehash.sh` and `WTF/` `metahash.sh` against the before state.
3. **An Update whose plan moved** opens the dialog with "Changed since you looked". No fixture server runs on the live bar, so this case is recorded from G1's QML scenario `test_a_moved_release_opens_the_dialog_with_changed_since_you_looked`, which passed in omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.1's gate; name it in the evidence.
4. **A doctor repair from the Issues view, undone with Undo last** (G2; F7's `fm-secrets-credential-file-mode`, which reports a credential file under `<config>` readable by group or others, from `stat` alone, and whose fixer is `chmod 0600`). *Decided while writing this bead (H6):* every widget on the live bar runs its commands against the real `<config>` (the stamped context carries the real `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `omarchy/Model.js:190`; `OMADDONS_WIDGET_ID` moves only the widget's id and folder, `src/state/paths.rs:49-62`), so the state is planted with a placeholder that holds no secret, never by changing the real token:
   - if `omaddons doctor --only fm-secrets-credential-file-mode --json` already reports an instance, use it and plant nothing (record it as a true real-home finding in the review);
   - otherwise create `<config>/credentials/m4-checkpoint` (and the `credentials` directory, mode 0700, if it does not exist) holding the line `placeholder written by the M4 checkpoint; not a credential`, mode 0640, and confirm the doctor now reports it;
   - if the doctor does not report that file, remove it, and plant instead by setting the stored GitHub token's mode to 0640 when `<config>/credentials/github` exists (recording its mode first; its content is never read), or, with no stored token, by a placeholder at `<config>/credentials/github` that `omaddons auth github clear` removes afterwards.

   Then in the panel: `omarchy-shell <widget id> show issues`; select the credential row; Enter. Expected: IPC `state()` shows `lastPreview` `{resource: "doctor_fix", decision: "dialog"}`, and the dialog, starting on No, lists `chmod 0600 <config>/credentials/<file> (was 0640)` (screenshot). Move to Yes and confirm (key names only). Expected: `lastResult.line` "Repaired: …" and the file's mode 0600 (screenshot). Undo last (the panel's key for it): the dialog reads "Undo repair: 1 change" (screenshot); Yes: the mode is back to 0640. Then remove the plant (or restore the token's recorded mode, or run `omaddons auth github clear`), remove a `credentials` directory the plant created (empty, `rmdir`), and check `metahash.sh <config>` equals the before value and `omaddons doctor --only fm-secrets-credential-file-mode --json` reports what it reported before the plant.
5. **Currency, at the end:** `omaddons omarchy status --json` is still current and enabled. The widget stays installed and enabled.

### 4. The after state

Recompute everything of section 0 into `hashes-after.txt`. Equal: the Forever guard (generation, addons, folders, AddOns hash), every non-Forever client's AddOns tree hash and `WTF/` metadata hash, and `<config>`'s metadata hash. Allowed to differ, by design, and recorded: non-Forever record generations (each undone transaction moves them forward), `<state>/history.jsonl` (the new lines are exactly the transactions this part and the real-machine tests made, each followed by its undo: list them from `omaddons history --json`), `<state>/doctor/runs/` (the run directories of the reviews and the repair), and `<cache>/plans/` (the plans the previews stored, swept after 24 hours). Any other difference is an unmet criterion.

### 5. The evidence comment

Write `evidence-3.md` and post it with `br comments add omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6 -f evidence-3.md`, titled "**Checkpoint evidence 3 of 3: the real machine and the desktop (at <E short>)**": the real-machine command, its passed count and every `SKIP` line; the three M4 tests' notes; the review table and the action table with verdicts; the status/doctor comparison; the desktop steps with their IPC `state()` values (quoted, scrubbed) and screenshot names; the before and after comparison. Then the blocks this part completes: `[x] 3 … (real machine)`, `[x] 7 … (real machine)`, `[x] 8 … (desktop)`, `[x] 12 … (real home)`, `[x] 17 … (real machine and review)`. **The privacy scrub is essential here**: the notes and states come from the real home, so every absolute path becomes a placeholder (`<home>`, `<client dir>` with its id, `<config>`, `<state>`, `<cache>`), and the scratch script that compares the file with the host name, the user name and the directory names under each client's `WTF/Account/` must print "clean". Then `br close omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.3 --reason "done: real machine and desktop at <E>; evidence comment <id> · found: <ids>"`.

### 6. When something fails here

Record it as `[ ] N … UNMET: <what>`. Restore the real home first: undo every transaction the failing step made and remove any plant, so the after state equals the before state. A missing deliverable (one of the three M4 tests absent) reopens its leaf (`br reopen <leaf> --reason "M4 checkpoint: <what is missing>"`); anything else files a bug: `br create "<what fails>" --type bug --priority 1 --labels m4 --description-file <file> --deps discovered-from:omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6` (the command, its scrubbed output, the criterion, `E`, the log's name; `br lint` clean). Then `br dep add omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6 <id>`, `br dep add omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.3 <id>`, `br update omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.3 --status open --transition-comment "blocked: <id> (criterion N unmet)"`. Never defer, never `--force`. A fix that lands as a code commit is a new `E`: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.1 and omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.2 are reopened and rerun first, then this part.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every client was stopped for the whole run, and the before state was recorded.
- [ ] The real-machine suite passed in the checkout at `E`, with `doctor_on_the_real_home`, `apply_one_update_and_undo` and `install_skill_round_trip` among the passed tests and no `SKIP` but the pre-accepted `keyless_installs_forever` (or its recorded exclusion when the Forever client manages no addons).
- [ ] Every real-home finding and every planned fix action is in the review with a verdict of right, and `status` and `doctor` agree on the real home.
- [ ] The widget was installed from the M4 build and is current and enabled at the end.
- [ ] The widget's Update on a matching plan applied with no dialog (`lastPreview.decision: "direct"`), and every transaction it needed was undone.
- [ ] The moved-plan case is recorded from its QML scenario.
- [ ] A credential-mode repair ran from the Issues view with its preview dialog and was undone with Undo last, and the plant was removed.
- [ ] The Forever guard, every AddOns tree hash, every `WTF/` metadata hash and the `<config>` metadata hash equal their before values, and every other difference is one the design allows.
- [ ] Evidence comment 3 is posted on H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`) after a clean privacy scrub.
- [ ] `br lint` is clean for this subtask and every bead it filed.

## Test Plan

Beads this section names: H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the parent), T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs), G1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1`) and G2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.2`), the widget leaves.

### Unit tests

None: this part writes no code.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

- **The real-machine suite** (section 1): every test passes; the expected `SKIP` is `keyless_installs_forever` alone, accepted.
- **The review** (section 2): a manual check, recorded as tables; its pass condition is "every verdict right".
- **The desktop scenarios** (section 3), each with its expected IPC `state()` values: Update → `lastPreview {resource: "update_addon", decision: "direct"}`, `confirm: null`; the repair → `lastPreview {resource: "doctor_fix", decision: "dialog"}`, then `lastResult.line` "Repaired: …", then Undo last's "Undo repair: 1 change". The moved-plan case is G1's QML scenario, run in the gate. The Issues view's QML scenarios (G2's `tst_repairs.qml`) ran in the gate too.
- **The before and after comparison** (sections 0 and 4).

### Logging

The scratch files `real_machine.log`, `doctor-review.md`, `status-vs-doctor.json`, `hashes-before.txt`, `hashes-after.txt`, `desktop/state-<step>-{before,after}.json`, `desktop/<step>.png` and `evidence-3.md`. The real-machine tests print evidence through `tests/real_machine.rs`'s `note()` with the home directory as `<home>`; T1's `TestLog` is not used there, because it refuses roots outside a `TestEnv`. Screenshots and IPC captures are named, never committed or attached.

### Checkpoint-only runs and the `SKIP` rule

`OMADDONS_REAL_MACHINE=1 OMADDONS_LIVE=1 OMADDONS_ALLOW_SKIP=keyless_installs_forever cargo test --test real_machine -- --ignored --test-threads=1` (plus `--skip keyless_installs_forever` when the Forever client manages no addons). Only `keyless_installs_forever`'s `SKIP` is accepted; any other is an unmet criterion 17.

## Considerations

Beads this section names: H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the parent).

- **Risk 3, doctor false positives on real homes** (medium, medium; owners the catalog leaves and H6): this review is its mitigation. Be strict: "true" needs an independent check, not the finding's own evidence restated.
- **The Forever client is never changed.** Its guard is compared before and after; its rows in the widget are never pressed; `keyless_installs_forever` is excluded when it would install there.
- **Text typed into the live panel** is M3's checkpoint accident. Only `wtype -k` key names; after the desktop step, the history check of section 4 shows every transaction was intended.
- **The real token.** The plant never touches the real GitHub token unless the placeholder is not detected, and then only its mode (to 0640, readable by the owner's group alone) for the few minutes of the scenario; its content is never read.
- **State that stays, by design:** history lines of the undone transactions, run directories, stored plans (swept after 24 hours), and a client's newest automatic checkpoint, as M3's real-machine tests leave target markers and their last checkpoint.
- **Forever's launch (risk 17).** If this part runs after the Forever client's 2026-11-04 launch and a real-machine test fails on a changed layout, that is an unmet criterion like any other, and its bug names `omad-wez` (re-verifying Forever after the launch, deferred outside M4) as related.
- **Hot spots:** none in the repository; this part writes only `.beads/` and scratch files. On the machine it writes what the approved runs write.

## Dependencies

Beads this section names: H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the parent), omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.2 (before), omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.4 (after).

- **Parent:** H6, the M4 checkpoint and the first tag.
- **Before it:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.2, so the owner's clients are touched only after every run that could force a code change has passed, and the perf budgets ran on a quiet machine.
- **After it:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.4 (the freeze commit and the tag), which needs every criterion met at `E`.

- [ ] Every real-home finding and every planned fix action is in the review with a verdict of right, and `status` and `doctor` agree on the real home.
- [ ] The widget was installed from the M4 build and is current and enabled at the end.
- [ ] The widget's Update on a matching plan applied with no dialog (`lastPreview.decision: "direct"`), and every transaction it needed was undone.

- [ ] A credential-mode repair ran from the Issues view with its preview dialog and was undone with Undo last, and the plant was removed.
- [ ] The Forever guard, every AddOns tree hash, every `WTF/` metadata hash and the `<config>` metadata hash equal their before values, and every other difference is one the design allows.

title: The freeze commit and the annotated tag `v0.1.0`: the vision comment, README's flips, the first released baseline and the golden's header
description:
Part 4 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6 (The M4 checkpoint and the first tag). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

Beads this section names: H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the parent: the M4 checkpoint and the first tag), its parts omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.1 to omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.3 (before) and omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.5 (after), H2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.2`, the golden and the released-baseline mechanism), H4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`, the README final pass), H5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.5`, the vision comments), the milestone epic (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`).

H6 is M4's checkpoint. Its first three parts ran all eighteen success criteria at the **evidence commit `E`** and posted three evidence comments on H6; every criterion is met. **This part** is the protocol's steps 4 and 5 (§11.3): it records the milestone on the vision bead, applies README's done flips, freezes the contract, and makes the project's first tag. It is its own step because it is the only one that changes the repository, and the one whose result can never be taken back once pushed.

**The decisions it carries out**, restated:

- **M4-D57: the first tag is `v0.1.0`, made by the checkpoint.** After every criterion passes and README says M4 is done, one commit holds the README status flips, the golden's header flip, the first released baseline `tests/contract/released/1.0.json` (with its provenance: `v0.1.0`, the commit it was generated from, the date) and `.beads/`. That commit changes a test fixture, so `argc gate` runs on it before it is made (vision D16, the local gate), with the baseline in place: the compatibility test then compares a released baseline with an unchanged registry, which must pass. Then the annotated tag `v0.1.0` on that commit (`git tag -a v0.1.0 -m "omaddons 0.1.0: contract 1.0 frozen"`), and the commit and the tag pushed. The crate version stays `0.1.0`; M5 owns the version scheme beyond it. *Rejected:* `v1.0.0`, because the project is pre-alpha and 1.0 implies a public stability the private repository does not offer.
- **M4-D56: the released baseline is separate from the current golden.** The current golden is `tests/contract/manifest.json` (the semantic manifest) and `tests/contract/wire_names.txt` (its readable projection), each with an informational header recording the contract version and whether a released baseline exists: `"header": {"contract": "1.0", "frozen": <bool>}` and the first lines `# contract 1.0`, `# frozen: <bool>`. No comparison reads either header. `OMADDONS_UPDATE_WIRE_NAMES=1` regenerates the current golden only. The released baseline `tests/contract/released/<version>.json` is a copy of the released manifest plus its provenance `{contract_version, tag, commit, created_at}`, written only by `OMADDONS_ADVANCE_RELEASED_BASELINE=<version>`, which refuses unless the current golden is at exactly that version and passes the comparison with the previous baseline when there is one (`1.0.json` has none). Once a baseline exists, the gate compares the current manifest with it on every run, whatever a header says: additions only need a higher minor `schema_version`, anything breaking or unclassified a higher major. Both variables are harness variables, never read by the binary. H2 built the mechanism; this part uses it once.
- **Vision D21:** "contract changes become deliberate (`schema_version` bump plus a recorded comment), never accidental". From this part's commit on, the gate enforces it.
- **The vision bead's milestone record:** each milestone ends with a comment "**§10 Milestone status: M<n> … is done (date)**" on `omad-vision-8qa` (M1's, M2's and M3's are there). H5 wrote M4's other comments (the plan's Appendix E: the decomposition and departures, the discovery surfaces, previews and plans, the doctor, the repair transaction, durability, wire names and the freeze, every wire name M4 added, the constants, external facts, and an index); this part adds the last, "with the checkpoint's outcomes, departures and limits, and 'M5 (accounts and release engineering) is next'".

## Technical Approach

Beads this section names: H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the parent) and its parts omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.1 to omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.5; H2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.2`, the baseline mechanism), H4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`, whose close comment holds the flip text), H5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.5`, the vision comments), G3 (`omad-7ccp`, durability, whose measured figures the vision comment may report), A10 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.10`, the manifest's classifier, which the negative control exercises).

### 0. Preconditions

- omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.1, omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.2 and omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.3 are closed, their evidence comments posted, every criterion met at `E`.
- No peer has uncommitted work in the repository: `ListAgents`, and a `SendMessage` to any active session asking it to hold commits until this part's push.
- In the main working copy: `git status --porcelain` is empty; `git fetch origin`; `main` = `origin/main` = `E`, or the commits after `E` touch only `.beads/` or README (then `E` stands, and the work proceeds on the current head).
- No tag exists yet: `git tag -l 'v*'` prints nothing, and `git ls-remote --tags origin` lists none.

### 1. The vision comment (§11.3 step 4)

Write `vision-m4-done.md` in the scratch directory and post it with `br comments add omad-vision-8qa -f vision-m4-done.md`. The house style is M3's (bead `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.7.3` wrote it):

1. The bold first line: "**§10 Milestone status: M4 (the agent surface, the doctor and the first tag) is done, <YYYY-MM-DD> (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6, H6).**", then "[x] M4. This closes the M4 set: H5's comments <first id>–<last id> and their index <id>, then <any fix notes made between H5 and the checkpoint>."
2. **What:** every one of the eighteen criteria (vision §7's M4 checkpoints as amended in the milestone epic's body) passed at `E`, the last code commit, with the pre-accepted `SKIP`s quoted; the evidence is H6's close reason and its comments <three ids>; the slice demos are the milestone epic's comments <ids>; the contract is frozen at `v0.1.0` with the released baseline `tests/contract/released/1.0.json`.
3. **Why it counts as done:** one paragraph: the surfaces exist as README describes them; the machine-local runs (gate from a clean checkout, perf, bench, fuzz, both compat characterizations, the exhaustive harness, the guide's fixed point, live probes, coverage) and the real-machine and desktop runs passed.
4. **Departures and limits,** each recorded where it was decided: what the checkpoint found and fixed (the bugs filed `discovered-from` H6, each closed); measured figures that differ from the plan's forecasts (G3's install fsync count against the forecast of at most 44, lock holds on btrfs, coverage); the open follow-ups s1 listed; that `omad-wez` re-verifies the Forever client after its 2026-11-04 launch, outside M4; that `omad-claude-mod-explore-0va5` stays deferred and owner-led; that nothing installed the skill into the real `$HOME/.claude/skills/`, by decision.
5. **Contract:** "no wire name beyond comment <id> (H5's 'Every wire name M4 added')"; from the tag on, every change is compared with the released baseline, and an added JSON key needs a minor `schema_version` bump, anything else a major one.
6. The last sentence: "M5 (accounts and release engineering) is next."

The tag commit's hash cannot be in this comment (the commit will hold it); H6's close reason and slice 4's demo carry it. Run the privacy scrub (no path, host name, user name, account name or token) before posting.

### 2. README's done flips (§11.3 step 4)

Apply the exact text H4 prepared in its close comment (`br show omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4 --json`), verbatim:

- the status line and badge: M4 is done; the contract is frozen at `v0.1.0`; next is M5 (README `:7` and `:41` at `c0ab5e9`, "Nothing is tagged, the repository is private, and the JSON contract freezes at the first tag (milestone 4, next)");
- "What works today": the M4 row becomes ✅ (`:161` at `c0ab5e9`, "🗓️ Milestone 4"), and the contract row's "(freezes in M4)" becomes "frozen at v0.1.0" (`:137`);
- the Roadmap's M4 row becomes ✅ with the date (`:2588`, "🗓️ Planned").

Then grep README for anything the tag makes false and correct it in the same edit: `Nothing is tagged`, `freezes at the first tag`, `freezes in M4`, `Until the first tag`, `Milestone 4` beside 🗓️, the Roadmap's `Planned` on the M4 row, the intro "Milestones 1 … and 3 … are complete" (`:128`), and any future-tense sentence about the freeze (the "Stability" section, `:1959-1961` at `c0ab5e9`, which H2 rewrote "as it will hold from the tag"). List each extra correction for the close reason. *Decided while writing this bead (H6):* if H4's text leaves the badge open, the `status: pre-alpha` badge stays and no badge is added, because M4-D57 keeps the project pre-alpha (which is why the tag is `v0.1.0`). Run `rumdl check README.md`: no new finding.

### 3. The first released baseline (§11.3 step 5)

```bash
OMADDONS_ADVANCE_RELEASED_BASELINE=1.0 cargo test --locked --test contract <H2's filter>
```

H2's close comment and README's "Stability" section name the exact test filter. It writes `tests/contract/released/1.0.json`. Check:

- the provenance: `contract_version` `"1.0"`; `tag` `"v0.1.0"`; `commit` the full 40-hex hash of `E`; `created_at` an RFC 3339 UTC instant of today. *Decided while writing this bead (H6):* `commit` is `E`, the commit the manifest was generated from, which is the tag commit's parent: a commit cannot record its own hash, and the tag commit changes no code, so the manifest at `E` is the manifest at the tag. If H2's mechanism records anything else, that is H2's defect (section 9);
- the content: `jq -S 'del(.provenance)' tests/contract/released/1.0.json` equals `jq -S 'del(.header)' tests/contract/manifest.json` (the same nodes, the same `format`).

### 4. The golden's header flip

By the documented updater, **never by hand** (the comparison with the current golden requires the committed files to equal generated output):

```bash
OMADDONS_UPDATE_WIRE_NAMES=1 cargo test --locked --test contract <H2's filter>
```

The headers now say `"frozen": true` and `# frozen: true`, because a released baseline exists. Then `git status --porcelain` and `git diff --stat` must show exactly: `README.md`, `tests/contract/manifest.json` and `tests/contract/wire_names.txt` (their header lines only: `git diff -U0` of the two shows one changed line each), and the untracked `tests/contract/released/1.0.json`. A change to any other line of the golden means it was stale at `E` (s1's gate would have failed) or the updater changed more than its header: stop (section 9). If the header still says `false` after the updater ran, the generator does not derive it from the baseline's existence: H2's defect (section 9).

### 5. The negative control (decided while writing this bead, H6)

The gate on this commit compares the baseline with an unchanged registry, which passes even if the comparison never read the file. So, before committing, in a throwaway clone of `E` in the scratch directory (never in the repository):

1. Copy in the four changed files from the working copy.
2. Remove one output node from the copy's `tests/contract/released/1.0.json` (any `output` node of a command's `data`), then run H2's comparison test (`cargo test --locked --test contract <H2's filter>`): it must **fail**, naming that node as an addition and the required version (a higher minor, `1.1`), through A10's classifier.
3. Set the copy's golden header back to `"frozen": false` and `# frozen: false`, and run it again: it must still **fail** (no comparison reads a header).
4. Restore both: it **passes**.

Record the three outcomes and the failure message's first lines in `negative-control.log`. An unexpected pass in 2 or 3 is H2's defect (section 9), and nothing is committed.

### 6. The gate on the tag commit's tree

```bash
br sync --flush-only
git add README.md tests/contract/manifest.json tests/contract/wire_names.txt tests/contract/released/1.0.json .beads/
argc gate
```

The tree changes test fixtures, so the gate is required (vision D16). It runs fmt, clippy, every test (the `wire_names` comparison now against the baseline), the widget pipeline, and `ubs` on the changed files. It must pass. `git diff --cached --stat` shows only the five paths.

### 7. One commit

No attribution lines:

```text
chore(release): freeze contract 1.0 at v0.1.0 and mark M4 done

- README: M4 done, the contract frozen at v0.1.0, M5 next (the flips H4 prepared)
- tests/contract/released/1.0.json: the first released baseline (provenance: v0.1.0, <E>, <date>)
- tests/contract/manifest.json, wire_names.txt: header frozen: true
- .beads: the M4 checkpoint record and the vision's milestone-status comment

Every M4 checkpoint criterion was run at <E> (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6). From this commit
on, the released baseline is compared on every gate.
```

### 8. The tag, and the push

```bash
git tag -a v0.1.0 -m "omaddons 0.1.0: contract 1.0 frozen"
git cat-file -t v0.1.0                    # tag (annotated)
git rev-parse 'v0.1.0^{commit}'            # = git rev-parse HEAD
git describe --exact-match HEAD           # v0.1.0
grep -n '^version' Cargo.toml             # version = "0.1.0"
cargo run --locked --release -- --version # omaddons 0.1.0
git push origin main
git push origin v0.1.0
git ls-remote origin refs/tags/v0.1.0 'refs/tags/v0.1.0^{}'   # the tag object, then the commit
```

The tagger is git's configured identity; never set or change `git config`. Push `main` first, then the tag, never `--tags` (pushes every local tag) and never `--force`. If the push of `main` is rejected because someone pushed after `E`: delete the local, unpushed tag (`git tag -d v0.1.0`), `git fetch`, and if the new commits touch only `.beads/` or README, rebase onto them (`br sync --import-only` first when they touch `.beads/`), rerun section 6's gate, recommit and retag; otherwise the evidence is stale (section 9). **A pushed tag is never moved, deleted or force-pushed.**

Then `br close omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.4 --reason "done: v0.1.0 on <commit>, pushed; baseline 1.0 with provenance <E>; negative control failed twice and passed once; vision comment <id>"`. If omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.5 does not follow in the same session, `br sync --flush-only`, commit `.beads/` and push, as the session protocol requires.

### 9. When something fails here

Before the commit: restore the working copy (`git restore README.md tests/contract/manifest.json tests/contract/wire_names.txt`, and remove the untracked `tests/contract/released/1.0.json`, which this part created), so `main` stays at `E`. File the defect as a bug: `br create "<what fails>" --type bug --priority 1 --labels m4 --description-file <file> --deps discovered-from:omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6` (the command, its scrubbed output, the criterion, `E`; `br lint` clean), then `br dep add omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6 <id>`, `br dep add omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.4 <id>`, `br update omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.4 --status open --transition-comment "blocked: <id>"`. A fix that lands as a code commit is a new `E`: omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.1 to omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.3 are reopened and rerun first. The vision comment already posted stays; a new one replaces it only if its facts changed, and says which comment it supersedes. Never defer, never `--force`. After the push, a defect is filed for the next milestone and named in the close reason; the tag stays.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The vision comment "§10 Milestone status: M4 (the agent surface, the doctor and the first tag) is done, <date> (…)" is on `omad-vision-8qa`, with What, Why it counts as done, Departures and limits, Contract, and the closing "M5 (accounts and release engineering) is next.", after a clean privacy scrub.
- [ ] README carries the flips H4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`) prepared, verbatim, and no sentence the tag makes false; `rumdl check README.md` reports no new finding.
- [ ] `tests/contract/released/1.0.json` was written by `OMADDONS_ADVANCE_RELEASED_BASELINE=1.0`, with provenance `contract_version` "1.0", `tag` "v0.1.0", `commit` = `E`, an RFC 3339 UTC `created_at`, and the golden's nodes.
- [ ] The golden's two header lines say `frozen: true`, written by `OMADDONS_UPDATE_WIRE_NAMES=1`, and no other golden line changed.
- [ ] The negative control failed with a removed baseline node, failed again with the header set back to `frozen: false`, and passed once restored.
- [ ] `argc gate` passed on the staged tree, and the commit holds exactly README, the two golden files, the baseline and `.beads/`, with no attribution lines.
- [ ] The annotated tag `v0.1.0` with the message "omaddons 0.1.0: contract 1.0 frozen" points at that commit, `Cargo.toml` says `0.1.0`, the release build prints `omaddons 0.1.0`, and `main` and the tag are on `origin`.
- [ ] `br lint` is clean for this subtask and every bead it filed.

## Test Plan

Beads this section names: H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the parent), H2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.2`, whose comparison test is run).

### Unit tests

None: this part writes no code.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

- **H2's comparison test** run four times: once to advance the baseline, once to regenerate the golden, three times in the negative control (fail, fail, pass), and inside the gate (pass).
- **`argc gate`** on the staged tree: every suite passes with the released baseline in place.
- **The tag checks** of section 8, each with its expected output.

### Logging

The scratch files `vision-m4-done.md`, `readme-flips.diff` (`git diff README.md`), `baseline-provenance.json` (`jq .provenance`), `golden-header.diff` (`git diff -U0` of the two golden files), `negative-control.log`, `gate-tag.log` and `tag-checks.log`. The close comment of this part quotes the provenance, the three negative-control outcomes, the commit and tag hashes and the `git ls-remote` lines.

### Checkpoint-only runs and the `SKIP` rule

None here: the runs are the gate and H2's comparison test, neither of which may print a `SKIP`.

## Considerations

Beads this section names: H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the parent), H4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`, the README final pass).

- **Irreversible once pushed.** Everything before section 8's push can be undone locally; the push cannot. Every check before it exists so that the pushed tag is right the first time.
- **Hot spots:** `README.md` (H4 reconciled it; edit only the flip lines and the sentences the tag makes false), `tests/contract/` (the golden is regenerated, never merged by hand), `.beads/` (`br sync --flush-only` before `git add`). The commit is made while no peer holds uncommitted work.
- **The installed binary** (from s3, built at `E`) has the tag's code: the tag commit changes no source.
- **Owner-visible from here on** (M4-D56): an added JSON key needs a minor `schema_version` bump, compared with `1.0.json` on every gate.
- **The vision comment's numbers** come from the evidence comments, never from memory; each figure names the run it came from.

## Dependencies

Beads this section names: H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the parent), omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.3 (before), omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.5 (after).

- **Parent:** H6, the M4 checkpoint and the first tag.
- **Before it:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.3 (and through it s1 and s2): the tag is made only when every criterion is met at `E`.
- **After it:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.5, which records slice 4's demo and H6's close reason, both of which cite the tag this part pushes.

- [ ] The vision comment "§10 Milestone status: M4 (the agent surface, the doctor and the first tag) is done, <date> (…)" is on `omad-vision-8qa`, with What, Why it counts as done, Departures and limits, Contract, and the closing "M5 (accounts and release engineering) is next.", after a clean privacy scrub.
- [ ] README carries the flips H4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`) prepared, verbatim, and no sentence the tag makes false; `rumdl check README.md` reports no new finding.
- [ ] `tests/contract/released/1.0.json` was written by `OMADDONS_ADVANCE_RELEASED_BASELINE=1.0`, with provenance `contract_version` "1.0", `tag` "v0.1.0", `commit` = `E`, an RFC 3339 UTC `created_at`, and the golden's nodes.
- [ ] The golden's two header lines say `frozen: true`, written by `OMADDONS_UPDATE_WIRE_NAMES=1`, and no other golden line changed.
- [ ] The negative control failed with a removed baseline node, failed again with the header set back to `frozen: false`, and passed once restored.
- [ ] `argc gate` passed on the staged tree, and the commit holds exactly README, the two golden files, the baseline and `.beads/`, with no attribution lines.
- [ ] The annotated tag `v0.1.0` with the message "omaddons 0.1.0: contract 1.0 frozen" points at that commit, `Cargo.toml` says `0.1.0`, the release build prints `omaddons 0.1.0`, and `main` and the tag are on `origin`.

title: Closing the milestone: slice 4's demo, the close reason with all eighteen criteria, and the epics
description:
Part 5 of 5 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6 (The M4 checkpoint and the first tag). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

Beads this section names: H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the parent: the M4 checkpoint and the first tag), its parts omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.1 to omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.4 (before), H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, the pre-freeze audit), H2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.2`, the golden and the released-baseline mechanism), H4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`, the README final pass), A10 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.10`, the semantic manifest), B4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.4`, the recipes end to end), the H area epic (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8`), the milestone epic (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`).

H6 is M4's checkpoint. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.1 to omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.3 ran all eighteen success criteria at the **evidence commit `E`** and posted three evidence comments on H6; omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.4 posted the vision's "M4 is done" comment, committed README's done flips with the first released baseline `tests/contract/released/1.0.json` and the golden's `frozen: true` header, tagged that commit `v0.1.0`, and pushed both.

**This part** is the protocol's steps 6 and 7 (§11.3), done now that the tag exists: it records **slice 4's demo** on the milestone epic (slice 4, "Freeze and close", contains H6 and its tag, so its demo can only be recorded after the tag: "the recipes, the change list, the golden, README, the tag and the released baseline, each with its evidence"), writes **H6's close reason** with every criterion `[x]` (in M2's and M3's form, `[x] N <criterion>: <evidence>`, with the commit hash, test names, timings and every `SKIP` line quoted), closes this part and H6, runs `br epic close-eligible` until nothing more closes (the H area epic, then the milestone epic), and commits and pushes `.beads/`. *Decided while writing this bead (H6):* H6 closes here, in a commit after the tag, not inside the tag commit, because its close reason cites the tag and the tag's commit, which do not exist until that commit is made; the plan's protocol already has this later `.beads/` commit (§11.3 step 6). It is its own step because it changes only `.beads/` and must follow a pushed tag.

## Technical Approach

Beads this section names: H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the parent) and omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.1 to omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.5; A10 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.10`, the manifest's report), B4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.4`, the recipes), H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, the change list), H2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.2`, the updater tests), H4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`, the README checklist), H5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.5`, the vision comments), T2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.2`), T3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.3`) and T4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4`) (the slice demos of slices 1–3), the H area epic (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8`) and the milestone epic (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`).

### 0. Preconditions

omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.4 is closed; `git ls-remote origin refs/tags/v0.1.0 'refs/tags/v0.1.0^{}'` shows the annotated tag and the tag commit; `git rev-parse 'v0.1.0^{commit}'` is that commit; the tag commit is on `origin/main`.

### 1. Slice 4's demo (§11.3 step 7)

Write `slice-demo-4.md` and post it with `br comments add omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm -f slice-demo-4.md`, titled "**Slice demo 4. Freeze and close**" (the naming of T2's, T3's and T4's "Slice demo 1. Self-describing", "Slice demo 2. Preview, then apply exactly" and "Slice demo 3. Diagnose and repair"), one `[x] <item>: <evidence>` line per item of the exit demo:

- **The recipes pass:** B4's eight recipe tests in `tests/skill_recipes.rs`, passed in s1's gate at `E`, each recipe at most two omaddons commands (names from evidence comment 1).
- **The audit's change list and the empty allowlist:** H1's comment "**Pre-freeze audit change list**" (and any "addendum N"), its entry count by disposition (`fixed`, `narrowed`, `excepted`, `confirmed`, `kept`, `prose`), and `tests/contract/rules_allowlist.txt` with no entry at the tag commit.
- **The golden and the updater tests:** `tests/contract/manifest.json` and `tests/contract/wire_names.txt` at the tag commit, their section counts from A10's report test, their header `frozen: true`; H2's updater tests passed in s1's gate (their names).
- **README:** H4's Appendix D checklist (its comment id) and the done flips at the tag commit (the status line, the "What works today" rows and the Roadmap row, quoted).
- **The tag:** `v0.1.0` → the tag commit's hash, annotated with "omaddons 0.1.0: contract 1.0 frozen", and the two `git ls-remote` lines.
- **The released baseline:** `tests/contract/released/1.0.json`'s provenance quoted (`contract_version`, `tag`, `commit` = `E`, `created_at`), and s4's negative control (failed with a removed node, failed with the header set back to `frozen: false`, passed once restored).

It pre-checks criteria 3, 4, 14, 17 and 18. Run the privacy scrub first (no path, host name, user name, account name or token).

### 2. The close reason

Assemble `close-reason.md` from the three evidence comments, completing criteria 14 and 18 with s4's results. The form is M3's:

```text
done: M4 checkpoint, <YYYY-MM-DD>. Every criterion was run at <E>, the last code commit; <tag commit> adds README, the contract freeze and beads only, and is tagged v0.1.0. Evidence: comments <id1>, <id2>, <id3> on this bead; slice demos <ids> on the milestone epic; vision comment <id>.

[x] 1 Capabilities: …
[x] 2 Schemas: …
…
[x] 18 README, the vision and the tag: …

Open follow-ups (not M4 criteria): <ids from s1, or none>.
Contract: one new file, tests/contract/released/1.0.json (the released baseline, with provenance); no other wire name added or changed.
· found: <every bug filed and leaf reopened during the checkpoint, each with its state, or none>
```

Each block holds that criterion's evidence from every part: s1's gate tests, s2's budgets and runs, s3's real-machine, review and desktop results, s4's baseline and tag. Criterion 14's block ends with the baseline's provenance and the negative control; criterion 17's lists every run with its exit and wall time, and quotes every `SKIP` line (only the pre-accepted kinds); criterion 18's names H4's checklist, the flips at the tag commit, H5's comments and the vision comment, and the tag on the remote. List the decided defaults of H6's body that were applied, each confirmed or adjusted (the evidence commit and its rerun rule, the checkout's location, fuzzing in the main working copy, README's extra checkpoint commands, the ignored-test inventory, the follow-up rule, the `keyless_installs_forever` exclusion if it was used, waiting for a running client, the widget installed first, the Update candidate, the credential plant, the real-home status/doctor comparison, the provenance `commit`, the header by the updater, the negative control, the badge, the commit messages, closing H6 after the tag). Run the privacy scrub.

### 3. Closing (§11.3 step 6)

```bash
br close omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.5 --reason "done: slice demo 4 <comment id>; close reason assembled" --transition-comment "done: slice demo 4 posted after the tag"
br close omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6 --reason "$(cat close-reason.md)" \
  --transition-comment "done: all 18 criteria [x] at <E>; v0.1.0 on <tag commit>; slice demo 4 <id> · found: <ids>"
br epic close-eligible --transition-comment "closed by the M4 checkpoint: every child closed"   # repeat until it closes nothing
```

Never `--force`: if `br close` refuses H6 because a blocker is open, the checkpoint is not done (go back to the blocker's subtask). `br epic close-eligible` closes AREA-H first, then the milestone epic; repeat it until a `--dry-run` lists nothing. Afterwards `br epic status --json` shows no open M4 epic, and `br list --label m4 --json` is empty.

### 4. The last commit

```bash
br lint <H6's id> <every subtask id> <every bead filed during the checkpoint> --json   # clean
br sync --flush-only
git add .beads/
git commit -m "chore(beads): close M4: checkpoint record, slice 4 demo and the epics"
git push origin main
```

No attribution lines; `.beads/` only, so the gate may be skipped (CLAUDE.md). Then `git status` is clean and `git log origin/main..main` is empty. The clean checkout from s1 is a plain clone under the git-ignored `target/`; it is no longer needed and goes with the next `cargo clean`.

### 5. When something fails here

Nothing here should fail: every criterion was met before the tag. If the slice demo or the close reason shows a gap (a criterion block with missing evidence), fill it from the evidence comments and the logs in the scratch directory; never invent a figure. A real defect found now is filed as a bug for the next milestone, named in the close reason's `found:` list, and does not move the tag. Never defer, never `--force`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The comment "Slice demo 4. Freeze and close" is on the milestone epic, with the recipes, the audit's change list and the empty allowlist, the golden and the updater tests, README, the tag and the released baseline, each `[x]` with its evidence.
- [ ] The close reason of H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`) starts "done: M4 checkpoint, <date>. Every criterion was run at <E>", holds the eighteen `[x] N` blocks with their evidence and every `SKIP` line quoted, lists the open follow-ups, the decided defaults applied and the one new contract file (`tests/contract/released/1.0.json`, no other wire name), and ends with the `found:` list.
- [ ] This subtask and H6 are closed without `--force`, and `br epic close-eligible` closed the H area epic and the milestone epic.
- [ ] `br lint` is clean for H6, its subtasks and every bead filed during the checkpoint.
- [ ] The `.beads/` commit is pushed; `git status` is clean and `git log origin/main..main` is empty.
- [ ] The slice demo and the close reason passed the privacy scrub.

## Test Plan

Beads this section names: H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the parent).

### Unit tests

None: this part writes no code.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

None run here: every test ran in s1 to s4 at `E` or on the tag commit's tree. This part's checks are the closing commands' results: `br close` accepts H6 (no open blocker), `br epic close-eligible` closes two epics, `br list --label m4 --json` is empty, and the push succeeds.

### Logging

The scratch files `slice-demo-4.md`, `close-reason.md` and `close.log` (the output of the closing commands). The close reason cites the evidence comments by id and the scratch logs by name.

### Checkpoint-only runs and the `SKIP` rule

None here.

## Considerations

Beads this section names: H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the parent).

- **The close reason is the milestone's record.** It must let a later agent re-check every criterion: commit hashes, test names, counts and timings, never "passed" alone.
- **Order matters:** the slice demo and the close reason cite the tag, so they come after s4's push; the epics close after H6.
- **Hot spots:** `.beads/` only.
- **Privacy.** The close reason quotes the real-machine evidence of s3, already scrubbed; scrub again, because it is assembled anew.

## Dependencies

Beads this section names: H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the parent), omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.4 (before).

- **Parent:** H6, the M4 checkpoint and the first tag. Closing this part's work closes H6, and then the H area epic and the milestone epic.
- **Before it:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6.4, whose pushed tag this part's demo and close reason cite.
- **After it:** nothing. M5 (accounts and release engineering) is next, outside M4.
