title: Epic: M4 test infrastructure and end-to-end scenario suites
description:
## Background

Area T is the test-infrastructure area of M4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`, the milestone epic: the agent surface, the doctor and the first tag). It gives every M4 integration test one structured log and one runner. It also turns the exit demos of slices 1–3 into test suites that run in every gate. It has four leaves:

- T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs, and the `argc e2e` runner): `tests/common/tlog.rs`, its self-test and an `argc` task;
- T2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.2`, slice 1 end to end): `tests/e2e_slice1.rs`, slice 1's demo as a test;
- T3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.3`, slice 2 end to end): `tests/e2e_slice2.rs`, slice 2's demo as a test;
- T4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4`, slice 3 end to end): `tests/e2e_slice3.rs`, slice 3's demo as a test.

All four leaves are size-M, so the area weighs 8 units. It adds no command, no error or warning code, no wire name, no persisted format, no dependency and no `src/limits.rs` constant. Everything it adds is test-only:

- one harness environment variable, `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG`;
- one `argc` task, `e2e`;
- a crate-doc marker for end-to-end suites, `//! e2e suite:`;
- a test-log format (`format: 1`) that only the test suite reads;
- four test crates and their README rows.

It changes no product code. Its only line under `src/` is T1's `ENV_VARS` row for `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG`, and only when A2 lands before T1.

Every leaf is worked through its subtasks: four for T1, three for T2, four for T3 and four for T4. Claim a subtask, not the leaf. The agent that closes a leaf's last subtask verifies the leaf's acceptance criteria and closes the leaf.

### Why the area exists

The area was not in the M4 plan. It was added when the plan was turned into beads, at the owner's request that the beads include comprehensive unit tests and end-to-end test scripts with detailed logging. The aim is that, after implementation, every behaviour can be shown to work and every failure can be diagnosed from its log alone. Filing added area T and changed no decision, edge, size, error code, constant or wire name of the plan.

Two problems make the area necessary:

1. **A failing scenario cannot be diagnosed today.** M4 adds about a dozen integration suites: capabilities, robot-docs, the skill and its recipes, completions, `apply` and stored plans, `plans show`, the doctor and its repair matrices, the safety harness, determinism, durability counts, and the M3 build against M4 state. Their scenarios run five to twenty commands against one synthetic home. They crash child processes at failpoints, pause them to force races, and compare tree hashes. When a scenario fails at its fourteenth command, the developer needs commands 1 to 13: each argv, each envelope and stderr event, each `net.log` line, each failpoint armed, and the paths that differ. Without a shared log, every suite invents its own prints, and the checkpoint can quote nothing beyond a test name.
2. **A slice demo is run once by hand, if at all.** M3 recorded its slice demos only at the end of the milestone, so its checkpoint found out late that halves did not fit (the first lesson of the M3 checkpoint record). A demo run by hand proves the slice on the day it ran. A demo written as a test proves it in every later commit, and a later leaf that breaks the slice's promise fails the gate at once.

### What is true today (verified at `c0ab5e9`)

- `tests/common/` holds 29 files and 5,242 lines of builders (`TestEnv`, `Home`, `Scene`, HTTP fixtures, `pause` failpoints, `tree_hash`). 94 test crates compile it: 93 `mod common;` lines, plus `tests/contract/main.rs:8-9`. No file in `tests/common/` holds a `#[test]`; the builders are tested in `tests/common_selftest.rs`.
- A failing integration test shows the assertion that failed and, at most, the failing run's argv and output (`common::home::Run::context()`, `tests/common/home.rs:327`). Nothing records the steps before it.
- `common::trees::tree_hash` (`tests/common/trees.rs:439`) returns only a digest. It cannot say which paths differ.
- There is no `tests/common/tlog.rs`, no `tests/e2e_*.rs` and no `e2e` task. `Argcfile.sh` has the tasks `gate`, `widget-test`, `bench`, `fmt`, `lint`, `test`, `fuzz` and `fuzz-all`.
- The gate (`argc gate`, `scripts/gate.sh`) runs `cargo test --locked` and the widget pipeline. The pipeline's QML step runs only when something under `omarchy/` changed, or with `--all` (`scripts/gate.sh:35-42`). `argc widget-test` always runs it.
- `src/contract/` does not exist yet. A2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.2`, the registries) creates `src/contract/env.rs` and its `ENV_VARS` registry.
- README's `## Development` section (`README.md:2600`) has a `### Tests` table (`:2619`) with one row per suite.

### Why it matters to the milestone

Area T has no milestone goal of its own. It is how the other areas' goals are shown to hold, and then kept holding:

- **G-M4-1, self-describing:** "an agent with no prior knowledge learns everything it needs from the binary itself, in at most three calls", and every command's output has a published JSON Schema that the contract suite validates against real output. **G-M4-2, the first guess works:** "a plausible wrong invocation yields a usage error whose fix is the command the user meant", and each fix is proven to run. T2's suite runs both end to end.
- **G-M4-3, what was previewed is what runs, target by target.** Every addon-changing command is previewed with `--dry-run` and then run bound to that preview, by token or by stored plan. The approval is checked again under the commit lock, a plan has one applier at a time, and `plans show` reconciles an approval with history. T3's suite runs this.
- **G-M4-4, diagnosable and repairable.** `doctor` names every broken state with its evidence and a remediation. Every auto-fix is consented, backs up verbatim, never deletes, round-trips, and stays undoable until a later change overlaps it. `status` and `doctor` never disagree. T4's suite runs this.
- **G-M4-6, no new risk to the engine's guarantees.** Every new write goes through fsx, and every repair is a journaled transaction. Dry runs leave `<state>` untouched, the doctor never writes `WTF/`, and an older build never destroys what M4 wrote. T3 and T4 assert this around every refusal and every crash.
- **G-M4-5, frozen and enforced:** T2 shows, from slice 1 on, that the semantic manifest builds and reports.
- **The vision's local gate (D16: no CI).** Every test runs on the development machine before each commit, and nobody else sees the output. A failure the developer cannot read in the terminal stalls the work. T1's log makes every failure readable there.

### The decisions that shape the area

The full decision log is in the decision-log comments on the milestone epic. These are the decisions this area applies, restated:

- **Area T, added at filing.** Four leaves, each `parent-child` to this area epic, which is `parent-child` to the milestone epic. Epics carry no blocking edges. The leaves change no product behaviour and add no wire name. Their edges were chosen so that the plan's 25-unit critical path does not grow: T1 is a root, and T2, T3 and T4 finish before H4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`, the README final pass) starts.
- **M4-D47: tests are Rust, not shell.** The plan decided that the doctor's fixtures are Rust types run by `cargo test`. The reasons: the project's tests are Rust (`assert_cmd`, `TestEnv`); Rust fixtures reuse the `tests/common/` builders, run in the gate and are deterministic by construction; and the house rules ban `rm -rf` even in test scripts. Rejected: a `corrupt.sh` and an `assert.sh` per failure mode, "a second test language, and shell scripts that must clean up after themselves". For this area, "end-to-end test scripts" are Rust integration tests that drive the real binary on a synthetic home. The one script added is an `argc` task over `cargo test`, and it deletes nothing.
- **Slice demos become tests (plan §10.6, amended at filing).** The plan gave each slice's demo to the agent who closes the slice's last leaf, recorded on the milestone epic in the `[x] <item>: <evidence>` style. For slices 1–3 that duty moved to T2, T3 and T4. H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the M4 checkpoint and the first tag) still checks that the three demo comments exist before it starts. H6 still records slice 4's demo itself, because slice 4 contains the tag.
- **The test and logging standard (milestone epic, Considerations).** Every M4 integration or end-to-end test that runs more than one command logs through T1's `TestLog`. Each phase of a scenario is a `step`, and every state assertion goes through `log.tree`/`log.assert_unchanged` or logs the values it compares. Unit tests in `src/` do not use the log: they are table-driven, with a name per case and assertion messages that show the input and the output. Every bead that writes such a test carries `uses_test_log`, and filing added a `blocks` edge from T1 to each of them.
- **M4-D6: environment variables get a registry.** `contract::env::ENV_VARS` lists every variable with one of three kinds: `release`, `debug`, or `harness` (read only by the test harness, never by the binary). A source scan fails on any unregistered variable, and `capabilities.env_vars` publishes only the `release` ones. `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG` is a `harness` variable. Whichever of A2 and T1 lands second registers it.
- **What runs where (plan §11.1).** The gate runs the unit tests, the contract suite, the end-to-end suites, the crash matrices, the safety harness and the widget pipeline. Checkpoint-only tests (perf budgets, compat, live probes, the real machine) are `#[ignore]`d and follow the `SKIP` rule: a test that cannot run prints `SKIP <test>: <reason>` and fails, unless `OMADDONS_ALLOW_SKIP` names it. Every T suite runs in the gate. `argc e2e` runs the same tests with the log turned up, and it is never a gate step.
- **The checkpoint protocol (plan §11.3).** H6's freeze step requires the demos of slices 1–3 to be recorded on the milestone epic, and H6 quotes test names, timings and transcripts as evidence. If a demo comment is missing, a closed T leaf did not deliver, and H6 reopens it.
- **Common rules 10 and 12.** Rule 10: real-machine tests and live probes never log through `TestLog`, because the log holds only synthetic homes and never reads the developer's real `HOME`. Rule 12: bead text is public-safe, so demo comments and close comments quote the log root as `target/tmp/test-logs`, never as an absolute path.
- **M4-D55, the contract's rules hold from slice 1 (context).** Area T adds no wire shape, so none of its leaves blocks H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, the pre-freeze audit). If a demo item forces a product fix, that fix is filed as its own bug against the owning leaf and must be additive. A needed change that is not additive is a defect against H1.

### How the area connects to the others

Beads named in this subsection, beyond the area epics and the leaves introduced above: A3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`, schemas and live validation), A4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`, `omaddons capabilities`), A7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.7`, completions), A10 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.10`, the semantic manifest), B3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3`, `install-skill`), C4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4`, the run-the-fix corpus), D4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.4`, the plan store), D7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.7`, release drift and apply races), D9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.9`, `plans show`), G1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1`, the widget's plans), E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, the doctor runtime), E9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9`, the M3 build against M4 state), E11 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.11`, `journal::diagnose`), F1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1`, journal and lock detectors), F2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.2`, journal fixers), G2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.2`, the Issues view's repairs) and G3 (`omad-7ccp`, group commit and deferred fsyncs, `omad-7ccp`). Keys in the leaf lists (A1–A5, D1–D9, …) are written bare; the key → id table in the first comment on the milestone epic resolves them.

- **Every area, through T1.** T1 blocks every bead of the milestone that writes an integration or end-to-end test. That covers the test subtasks of nearly every leaf in areas A–H, the leaves without subtasks that write their own tests (A6, A8, C3, D6 and E10 among them), and the test-writing subtasks of T2, T3 and T4. `br show omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1` lists them all. T1's own subtasks carry no such edge, because an edge from T1 to its own child would deadlock.

## Non-Goals

Beads named in this section: the four leaves T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`), T2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.2`), T3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.3`) and T4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4`); A4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.4`, `omaddons capabilities`), B3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.3`, `install-skill`), D7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.7`, release drift and apply races), E6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`, `doctor fix`), E9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9`, the M3 build against M4 state), F9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`, the safety harness), G1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1`, the widget's plans), G2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.2`, the Issues view's repairs) and H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the checkpoint).

- **Product behaviour.** Area T changes no command, output, error, state file or wire name. A demo item that fails is a defect in the leaf that owns the behaviour, fixed there, never in the T suite.
- **Shell test scripts** (M4-D47). Every scenario is a Rust integration test. The one script is T1's `argc e2e` task, which runs `cargo test` and deletes nothing.
- **A CI service or a hook.** The gate stays local (vision D16), and `argc e2e` is a convenience, never a gate step. The milestone's own non-goal applies in the same way: making the doctor a CI gate or a pre-commit hook is not M4's, and neither is wiring the end-to-end suites into one.
- **Converting the existing suites.** No existing test changes behaviour. An older suite adopts `TestLog` only when a leaf rewrites it for its own reasons.
- **Logging the real machine.** Real-machine tests and live probes never use `TestLog`. The log refuses trees outside the test's synthetic directories and never records the test process's environment.
- **Re-implementing the owning leaves' checks.** T2, T3 and T4 call the helpers their blockers shipped (the round trip, the guide layout, the corpus harness, the landing builders, the fixtures, the harness routine). Where a helper lacks a parameter, it is extended additively, never copied.
- **Replacing a leaf's own matrices.** Each owning leaf proves its own protocol in its own suite: D7's per-source drift matrices, the design-gate leaves' crash matrices, F9's whole harness. The T suites run the demo's composition of those pieces. T4 crashes one fixer, not the catalog, and checks by name that the full harness stays in the gate.
- **Timing budgets.** No T suite asserts a time. The perf budgets are checkpoint tests owned by their leaves (A4's `capabilities` under 20 ms, among others). The T suites only record their wall time, against targets of 30 s (T2, T3) and 60 s (T4) in a debug build.
- **Checkpoint-only tests.** Area T owns none. T4 quotes E9's `tests/compat_m3.rs` run. The real-machine tests belong to D7, E6 and B3, and H6 runs them.
- **Snapshots in the demo suites.** They assert invariants, so later leaves' additions do not move them.
- **QML in every gate.** The QML step of the widget pipeline runs when `omarchy/` changes or with `--all`. The T suites check G1's and G2's QML scenarios by name and by fixture provenance in every gate. Their passing is evidenced by `argc widget-test` in the demo comment.
- **Slice 4's demo.** It contains the tag, so H6 records it.
- **A list file of suites.** A crate is an end-to-end suite because it carries the `//! e2e suite:` marker, which keeps parallel leaves off a shared list.
- **A contract for the log.** `steps.jsonl` (`format: 1`) is internal to the test suite. Its only readers are `argc e2e`'s summary and T1's self-test.
- **Dynamic shell completion.** As for the milestone: T2 checks the static scripts only.

## Considerations

Beads named in this section: the four leaves T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`), T2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.2`), T3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.3`) and T4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4`); A2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.2`, the registries); A3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.3`, schemas and live validation); B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`, the guide renderer); C4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4`, the run-the-fix corpus); D5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5`, `omaddons apply`); D7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.7`, release drift and apply races); D9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.9`, `plans show`); E1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1`, the failure-mode registry); E9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9`, the M3 build against M4 state); F2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.2`, journal fixers); F9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`, the safety harness); G1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.1`, the widget's plans); G2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.2`, the Issues view's repairs); G3 (`omad-7ccp`, group commit and deferred fsyncs, `omad-7ccp`); H1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.1`, the pre-freeze audit); H4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`, the README final pass); H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the checkpoint). Keys that appear only in a chain or a list (the critical path, the slices' leaves, the design gates) are written bare; the key → id table in the first comment on the milestone epic resolves them.

### How the leaves are worked

All four leaves are worked through subtasks, in work order inside each leaf:

- **T1, four subtasks:** the log core, then commands and trees under the log, then two in parallel: the runner, the marker convention, the registry row and README; and the self-test scenarios.
- **T2, three subtasks:** the suite with the self-description items first, then two in parallel: the guide, skill and completions items; and the first-guess items.
- **T3, four subtasks:** the suite with the single-process items first, then two in parallel: the paused and background items; and the widget checks. A fourth subtask runs the demo and records it.
- **T4, four subtasks:** the suite with the stuck-states item first, then three in parallel: set-asides and gc; the fence and the Issues view; and the harness and the fsync table.

Claim a subtask, not the leaf (`br ready --parent <leaf id>`). The agent that closes a leaf's last subtask verifies the leaf's acceptance criteria. For T2–T4, that agent also runs the demo and records it, and then closes the leaf.

### Order of work, and why the edges are where they are

- **T1 first, at once.** It is a root. Its edges exist so that every multi-command test of the milestone logs the same way, and no suite invents its own prints.
  - The edge to each test-writing bead starts at the leaf T1, not at one of its subtasks. A dependent therefore waits for all four of T1's subtasks, the runner and the self-test included.
  - Work T1's third and fourth subtasks in parallel as soon as the second closes.
- **T2, T3 and T4 each wait for T1 and for every leaf of their slice.** A leaf's closure is its unit of delivery, so the demo runs against the finished slice and never against half a leaf. Each suite can call helpers that have already landed under their final names. Each suite's scenarios are `TestLog` scenarios, and `argc e2e slice<N>` is T1's runner.
- **T2, T3 and T4 block H4.** H4 matches README's test counts and Tests table to the code, and describes each slice as what passes, so the three suites and their README rows must exist first. Before area T, the plan's §10.2 already had "everything user-visible → H4 → H5 → H6" and "H1 → H2 → H4". Area T's three edges join H4 beside them, and do not lengthen the 25-unit critical path.
- **No edge among T2, T3 and T4.** Their suites share no file, and each can be recorded as soon as its slice closes.
- **No edge into H1.** Area T adds no wire shape (M4-D55, §10.2: the leaves that may land after H1 are those that add none).
- **The order across slices follows the plan's order of work** (§10.2): correctness protocols first, and durability last against the settled protocols. Slice 1's demo can be recorded first, then slice 2's. Slice 3's comes last, because T4 waits for F9 and for G3, which lands last.
- **Waves** (earliest start, leaf level): T1 at t = 0; T2 at t = 10, after B3; T3 at t = 16, after D7; T4 at t = 18, after F9 and G3; H4 at t = 20.

### Critical path and slack (the milestone's computation with area T)

Filing reran the plan's graph computation with area T's edges (leaf level, S = 1, M = 2, L = 3): 64 leaves and 210 `blocks` edges, the plan's 153 plus area T's 57.

- **The critical path stays 25 units:** E1 → E2 → E3 → E6 → E7 → F2 → H1 → H2 → H4 → H5 → H6.
- **T4 is on it.** Area T adds two more zero-slack chains: E1 → E2 → E3 → E6 → E7 → F2 → F9 → T4 → H4 → H5 → H6, and the same chain with G3 in place of F9. F9 and G3 lost their 2 units of slack to T4. A slip in F9, G3 or T4 now delays the tag. T4 composes finished helpers, so start it the moment F9 and G3 close, and work its three parallel subtasks with three agents.
- **T3 has 2 units of slack.** It starts after D7 (t = 16) and must finish before H4 starts (t = 20). The plans chain ahead of it (D1 → D2 → D4 → D5 → D9 → D7) has only 1 unit of slack up to D9, so a plans slip reaches T3 quickly.
- **T2 has 8 units of slack.** It starts after B3 (t = 10) and must finish by t = 20.
- **T1 has 16 units of slack at leaf level, but it is urgent.** The leaf-level graph counts only T1 → T2, T3 and T4. Every test subtask of every leaf also waits for T1, E1's included, and E1 starts the critical path. E1 cannot close before its test subtask, and that subtask cannot start before T1 closes. Claim T1 at once, beside E1, D1 and E11.
- **Lanes.** The plan's six-lane schedule was computed without area T and reached 25 units. Rerun at filing with the plan's own method (list scheduling by least latest start plus a seeded random offset under 2.5 units, over 1,000 trials), six agents now finish at 27 units, seven at 25 and five at 31. The lane table is guidance for order, not a schedule.
- **These numbers are provisional** until the design-gate leaves pass their gates. A gate that moves a size or an edge is recorded on the milestone epic, and the graph is recomputed there.

### Collision hot spots

Parallel agents share one `main`. Claim with the file list (`br update <id> --claim --transition-comment "claim: <files>"`). Keep commits small, rebase before each gate run, and coordinate through `SendMessage` and `ListAgents`. Treat unrecognized working-tree changes as a peer's work.

| File | Who touches it | Rule for this area |
|---|---|---|
| `tests/common/tlog.rs` | T1 creates it; every test-writing bead of M4 uses it | T1 shapes it. A later bead that needs a new helper adds it additively, in its own commit (the milestone's hot-spot rule). |
| `tests/common/mod.rs` | T1 (`pub mod tlog;`) and several other leaves (C4's corpus home, D7's landing and memo, the plans and doctor helpers) | Append `pub mod` lines; rebase. |
| `tests/common/trees.rs` | T1 adds `tree_entries`, `Entry`, `EntryKind`, `TreeDiff` and `tree_diff`; C4 appends `copy_tree_exact` | Additions only. `tree_hash` never changes: every existing suite and crash matrix relies on what it covers (kinds, modes, bytes, symlink targets). |
| `Argcfile.sh` | T1 (`e2e`) | No other M4 writer. `argc --argc-export Argcfile.sh` succeeds and `shellcheck -x Argcfile.sh` is clean. |
| `src/contract/env.rs` | A2 owns it; T1 adds one row | One `harness` row, only if A2 has landed. Otherwise T1 comments on A2 asking for it, and the second to land adds it. |
| `skills/omaddons/SKILL.md` | every leaf after B1 (common rule 17) | T1 regenerates it only if the guide's environment table lists harness variables: `OMADDONS_UPDATE_SKILL=1 cargo test --test skill` after rebasing, never by hand. |
| `README.md`, `## Development` | T1 (its subsection, the "Other tasks" line, a Tests row, the harness-variable list); T2, T3 and T4 (one Tests row each); every suite leaf | Edit only your own row or subsection. H4 reconciles the counts. |
| `tests/e2e_slice1.rs` | T2 alone | Its second and third subtasks append their own inline modules after the first; rebase. |
| `tests/e2e_slice2.rs` | T3 alone | Its second and third subtasks append after the first; rebase. |
| `tests/e2e_slice3.rs`, `tests/e2e_slice3/` | T4 alone | One module file per subtask, and one `#[path]` `mod` line each in the root; rebase. |
| `tests/contract/snapshot_walk.rs` (and a possible `tests/contract/snapshot_set.rs`) | A3's; T2 may share its snapshot collection | Only a pure move, with the walker's summary line identical before and after. Announce it with `SendMessage` if another agent has a claim open on the file or on `tests/contract/main.rs`. |
| `tests/common/landing.rs` | D7's; T3 may add `Landing::download_tokens(n)` | Pure addition, only if D7 exposed no accessor. |
| `tests/doctor/journal_sets.rs`, `tests/doctor/harness/`, `tests/common/doctor.rs` | F2, F9, E3; T4 includes them by path | Additive, or a pure refactor (F9's per-fixer crash routine factored out). The owner's suite is rerun, and the change is listed in T4's close comment. |
| `tests/engine_durability.rs`, `tests/common/durability.rs` | G3's; T4 may move G3's table and its five window builders | Pure move; G3's test then reads them from `tests/common/`. |

### Design gates

**None of area T's leaves is a design gate.** Common rule 14 lists D1, D2, D5, D8, E5, E7, E8, E11, E14 and G3. Area T adds no journal shape, recovery rule, binding rule, deletion rule or durability rule.

T3 and T4 do demonstrate design-gated protocols end to end: the token and its witness, the under-lock check and the lease in slice 2; the repair journal, fences, undo of repairs, gc's retention plan and group commit in slice 3. They run only after those leaves have closed, so after their gates have passed. A demo never stands in for a gate's matrix: each design-gate leaf closes only when its own adversarial matrix passes, and F9 integrates across fixers but never discovers whether a leaf's own protocol works.

### Slice share and the demos the area records

- `slice-1` (17 leaves): T1 and T2, beside A1–A5, A7–A10, B1, B3 and C1–C4. T2 records its demo.
- `slice-2` (12 leaves): T3, beside D1–D9, E13 and G1. T3 records its demo.
- `slice-3` (26 leaves): T4, beside E1–E12, E14, F1–F10, G2 and G3. T4 records its demo.
- `slice-4` (9 leaves: A6, B2, B4, H1–H6): no leaf of this area. H6 records its demo.

T1 records no demo. It provides the log every demo quotes.

**How each demo is recorded.** The agent that closes the T leaf's last subtask works on a clean, current `main`:

1. Run `argc e2e slice<N>`. It must exit 0, and its summary lines are quoted.
2. Run whatever else the leaf's bead names: the contract suite for slice 1; `argc widget-test` for slices 2 and 3; the full harness through `argc e2e doctor_harness` for slice 3; and the `compat_m3` quote rule for slice 3.
3. Write the comment to a scratch file outside the repository, check it for paths and names, and post it with `br comments add omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm --file <file>`.

A re-recording is a new comment, never an edit. The demo is recorded only from a run in which every item passed: a skipped QML step is not a pass, and a failing compat run is criterion 16 unmet.

**A demo item that fails** is a defect in the leaf that owns the behaviour. The T suite never weakens, ignores or skips the item, and never commits a failing test. Each T leaf's bead governs its own procedure:

- **The default, for all three:** a P1 bug `discovered-from` the T subtask that found it. It names the owning leaf, the failing step, the assertion and the transcript's log root, and blocks that subtask (`br dep add <subtask> <bug>`), so the T leaf and H4 wait for the fix. The fix lands in the bug's own commit, and the scenario stays as its regression test.
- **T2 and T4** also allow reopening the owning leaf, when one of that leaf's own acceptance criteria was never met.
- **T3 never reopens a leaf.** Reopening a closed slice-2 leaf would re-block every bead that leaf blocks; D5 alone blocks seven.
- **A failure in the T suite's own builder** is fixed in place.

### Risks

- **Risk 14, the milestone is large** (likelihood medium, impact medium; all leaves). The plan's mitigation includes "slices demo progress". Area T turns that mitigation into tests, and so carries part of the risk itself: T4 is on the critical path, and T1 gates nearly every leaf's test subtask. Claim T1 at once. Start T4 as soon as F9 and G3 close, and work its subtasks in parallel.
- **Helper drift.** T2, T3 and T4 call helpers named in more than twenty other beads' specifications. If a helper landed under another name or signature, call it as it landed and list the difference in the close comment. Never add a parallel helper. A helper private to another suite is moved into `tests/common/` as a pure move, never copied.
- **A demo that passes for the wrong reason,** for example a refused run that never got far enough to be refused for the reason asserted. Every refusal asserts its exact code and its `details` part. Paused runs assert that they reached, or never reached, the named failpoint. Every state claim goes through a tree hash or a logged comparison.
- **Gate time.**
  - T1 must stay cheap: a passing test writes two small files, hashes trees only when asked, and never fsyncs. If its overhead shows in F9's 60 s harness, that is a defect filed `discovered-from` T1, fixed by making the log cheaper, never by dropping crash positions.
  - The demo suites' targets are 30 s (T2, T3) and 60 s (T4) in a debug build, measured and recorded in the close comment. A suite past its target is a defect, fixed by faster setup, never by dropping a demo item.
- **The QML step is not in every gate.** The gate runs `qmltestrunner` only when `omarchy/` changes or with `--all`, and the T leaves change nothing under `omarchy/`. The QML scenarios are therefore checked by name and fixture provenance in every gate, and passing in `argc widget-test` at record time. A missing `qmltestrunner` is not a skip.
- **Criterion 16 is checkpoint-only.** `compat_m3` builds `c0ab5e9` with toolchain 1.97.1 and takes minutes. T4 quotes E9's last run, unless `src/engine`, `src/fsx`, `src/state` or `src/doctor` changed after it, in which case T4 reruns it. A failing or unbuildable run is criterion 16 unmet, never a `SKIP`.
- **The composed stuck home (T4).** Eight stuck states on one home depend on recovery's machine-wide reach and on where each failpoint sits. The planting order is derived from the code, and each planting step reruns `doctor`, so a disturbance fails at the step that caused it. If a later engine change makes two states incompatible on one home, T4 moves one to its own client and never drops one.
- **Privacy of transcripts.** A transcript is exactly what someone pastes into a bead comment. The log redacts variables whose names contain `TOKEN`, `SECRET` or `CREDENTIAL`, scrubs values registered with `log.secret`, records stdin as a byte count only, never records the test process's environment, and rewrites paths to placeholders. Homes with a `WTF/` use the fake account, realm and character names, and runs there assert privacy on both streams.
- **libtest or the standard library changes underneath the log.** If libtest changes how it captures output, or `type_name_of_val` changes its format (it is documented as not guaranteed), T1's child-process self-tests fail first, and `TestLog::new` with explicit names keeps working.
- **The plan's risks the demo suites watch:**
  - T2: #2 (live validation finds many mismatches; a snapshot the published schemas reject is A3's bug), #12 (misplaced-client fixes misfire), #13 (the guide drifts from behaviour) and #15 (`jsonschema` and `deny.toml`; T2 adds no dependency).
  - T3: #19 (a token stales for no reason: a deferred release whose `apply` hits the cache must not be stale) and #7 (widget previews feel slow: the `apply` after a preview downloads nothing).
  - T4: #1 (a recovery bug in the repair journal), #3 (doctor false positives), #8 (durability weakened invisibly), #9 (the M3 build destroys M4 artifacts), #21 (fences scoped wrong) and #23 (guarded reactivation refuses more than expected).

### What the leaf beads found against the plan

The leaf beads checked area T's entries against the code at `c0ab5e9`. Each kept the intent and recorded how it adapted:

- **T1:**
  - unit tests of the log's helpers go in `tests/tlog_selftest.rs`, not in `tests/common/tlog.rs`, because 94 crates compile `tests/common/` and a test there would run 94 times;
  - `log.run` builds a `std::process::Command` with exactly `TestEnv`'s environment, through a `Runner` trait for `TestEnv`, `Home` and `Scene`, instead of `TestEnv::command()`'s `assert_cmd::Command`, which cannot run in the background or report the variables it set;
  - `tree_entries` and `tree_diff` are added beside an unchanged `tree_hash`, which returns only a digest;
  - the live echo writes directly to the stderr handle, so it needs no `--nocapture`;
  - `ENV_VARS` does not exist yet, so the "whichever lands second" rule applies;
  - A2's harness scan is read as covering reads in `src/`, because the name must also appear in `Argcfile.sh` and README.
- **T2:**
  - the matrix's live validation and the corpus live in the contract test binary, which another crate cannot call. T2 proves that the published schemas equal the generated ones, validates every envelope snapshot directly, runs the demo's intent rows itself, and guards by name that the matrix validation and the corpus stay in the gate. The demo comment quotes the contract suite's run;
  - `TestEnv` holds no client, so the scenarios use `Home` and C4's `IntentHome`;
  - snapshots are redacted, which M4-D9 gave as a reason not to validate them, so they validate after A3's typed-sample substitution, shared with A3's walker.
- **T3:**
  - a fixture sequence restarts in every process, so a release landing is D7's second scenario directory (`common::landing`), not `fixture_seq`;
  - no QML test read a binary-written envelope at `c0ab5e9`, so the currency of G1's generated fixtures is asserted structurally;
  - with the lease, the second applier never reaches the commit loop, so it is armed with sentinel failpoints that must never fire;
  - a single-target bound run refused under the lock surfaces as the whole command's error with `details.items`, so T3 asserts membership in `details.changed`;
  - the QML step does not run in every gate, so its passing is evidenced by `argc widget-test`.
- **T4:**
  - the scenario modules live under `tests/e2e_slice3/` and are included with `#[path]`, because a plain `mod stuck;` would resolve to `tests/stuck.rs`, which cargo would also build as its own test crate;
  - the crate is debug-only, because its plantings arm failpoints;
  - recovery is machine-wide, so the planting order of the stuck home follows from the code;
  - one fixer is crashed in the suite, plus a by-name check of the whole harness, rather than a second full harness run.
- **Against the milestone epic's own summary:**
  - the epic says the verbose echo runs "with `--nocapture`" (T1 needs none);
  - it says each demo item runs "on a fresh `TestEnv`" (each runs on a home of its own: a `TestEnv`, a `Home` or an `IntentHome`);
  - it says the T suite asserts that the widget's fixtures "are current" (they are checked structurally).

  The leaves' text governs.
acceptance_criteria:
T1 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1), T2 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.2), T3 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.3) and T4 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4) and every subtask of them are closed, each leaf having verified its own acceptance criteria, and the following hold on `main`:

- [ ] Structured test logs (T1): `tests/common/tlog.rs` exists, is declared in `tests/common/mod.rs`, and provides `TestLog::new`, `tlog!()`, `step`, `note`, `json`, `run`, `cmd`, `tree`, `assert_unchanged`, `diff`, `case` and `Ran::{ok, exit, envelope, data, error_code, warnings, commands}`, plus the additions T1 decided.
- [ ] A scenario of several commands writes `target/tmp/test-logs/<suite>/<test>/steps.jsonl` and `transcript.md`. Every run record carries the sequence number, the step, the argv, the environment overrides with secrets redacted, the working directory, the start time, `elapsed_ms`, the exit code (and signal), stdout parsed as the envelope, the stderr events parsed, the `net.log` lines the run added and the failpoints armed. A rerun replaces the directory.
- [ ] Captures are bounded by `STREAM_CAP_BYTES` (1 MiB per stream per record) and `TEST_CAP_BYTES` (64 MiB per test), and a truncation or a cap is recorded, never silent. A passing three-run scenario writes under 64 KiB.
- [ ] A failing `Ran` assertion names the step, the expected and actual exit, the error code and the transcript path. A panicking test prints `test log: <path>` and its last 20 records. `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG=verbose` echoes every record live. Both are proved in child processes.
- [ ] A planted `OMADDONS_GITHUB_TOKEN` never appears in either file. Paths are rewritten to placeholders. `log.tree` refuses a root outside the test's synthetic directories. `log.assert_unchanged` and `log.diff` name the first 20 differing paths and what changed, and `tree_hash` is unchanged.
- [ ] `argc e2e [FILTER] [ARGS…]` runs every crate marked `//! e2e suite:` with `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG=verbose`. It prints the logs written, the panicked and incomplete ones and the log root `target/tmp/test-logs`, exits with cargo's status, and deletes nothing; an unmatched filter exits 2 naming the suites. The convention test keeps the marker, the `TestLog` users and `Argcfile.sh`'s pattern in step.
- [ ] `ENV_VARS` lists `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG` as `harness`. No existing test changes behaviour, and no crate is added.
- [ ] Slice 1's demo (T2): `tests/e2e_slice1.rs` carries the marker, and each of its nine demo items passes in the gate. `capabilities --json` round-trips and writes nothing. The published schemas equal the generated ones, and at least 100 envelope snapshots (at least 30 with `details`) validate strictly against them, while five planted faults fail. The manifest's report prints, with 0 breaking and 0 unclassified changes. `robot-docs guide` is byte-identical to `SKILL.md`, frontmatter first. `install-skill` into a throwaway `HOME` writes once and then nothing. `omaddons retail update` fixes to `update -t retail` and changes nothing. `remove dbm retail` and `update dbm retail` change nothing, with DBM also on `era`. The corpus's twelve per-kind tests stay in the gate and pass. `completions bash` passes `bash -n`.
- [ ] Slice 2's demo (T3): `tests/e2e_slice2.rs` carries the marker, and each Rust demo item passes in the gate. Preview, then apply, commits exactly the previewed release with no asset request. A release landing in between gives `plan_stale` (`["selection"]`), and the re-preview shows it. A late hand edit is caught under the lock and kept, and an undo restores it byte for byte. A second `apply` is `already_applied`, also after expiry. Two appliers never split a plan. `plans show` reconciles a lost output, and still answers with the plan file gone. A Tukui plan applies from the cache with no token stored anywhere.
- [ ] The widget's three QML Update scenarios (routine and matching: no dialog; a dependency added: the dialog; a moved release: the dialog) exist by name, read only fixtures the binary writes, and pass in `argc widget-test`.
- [ ] Slice 3's demo (T4): `tests/e2e_slice3.rs` carries the marker, is debug-only, and each Rust demo item passes in the gate.
  - The eight stuck states of criterion 11 are planted on one home, named alike by `doctor`, `status` and `status --cached`, and nothing changes outside `<state>/doctor/`.
  - A set-aside with `--force --yes` is reactivated byte-identical by bare `doctor undo`. After a later install on that client, the undo is `undo_conflict` and nothing moves.
  - A stuck repair fences only its own resources.
  - A bound `doctor gc` refuses a changed plan and deletes exactly its preview.
  - The Issues view's credential repair is undone by Undo last, and its three QML scenarios exist by name and pass in `argc widget-test`.
  - The demo's repair is green at every primitive boundary through F9's routine, and the full harness is asserted to be in the gate.
  - The five pinned windows' fsync counts equal G3's pins.
  - Criterion 16 is quoted from a passing `compat_m3` run.
  - The suite runs in under 60 s in a debug build.
- [ ] The comments "**Slice demo 1. Self-describing**", "**Slice demo 2. Preview, then apply exactly**" and "**Slice demo 3. Diagnose and repair**" are on the milestone epic (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm). Each has one `[x] <item>: <evidence>` line per demo item, quoting the test names, the commit, the `argc e2e slice<N>` summary and the log root `target/tmp/test-logs`, with no absolute path, host name or user name. H6 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6) finds all three before its freeze step.
- [ ] Through the demos, the area pre-checks checkpoint criteria 1, 2, 3 (in part), 5 and 15 (T2), 6, 7 and 8 for updates (T3), and 8 for the doctor, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13 and 16 (T4), and keeps them checked in every gate. It serves criteria 17 and 18 in part: `argc gate --all` runs every T suite, and README describes the logs, `argc e2e` and the suites.

title: Structured test logs, and the `argc e2e` runner
description:
## How to work this bead

This bead is worked through its 4 subtasks, listed below in work order. Claim a subtask, not this bead (`br ready --parent omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1` lists the ready ones). The agent that closes the last open subtask then verifies every acceptance criterion of this bead (they are the leaf's, not any one subtask's), and closes this bead with `br close omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1 --reason "done: <evidence> · found: <ids>"`. Until this bead is closed, every bead it blocks stays blocked.

## Background

### Why this bead exists

M4 (the milestone this bead belongs to; epic `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`) adds about a dozen new integration suites: capabilities, robot-docs, the skill and its recipes, completions, `apply` and stored plans, the doctor and its repair matrices, the safety harness, determinism, durability counts and the M3 build against M4 state. Their scenarios run five to twenty commands against one synthetic home, crash child processes at failpoints, pause them at named steps to force a race, and compare tree hashes before and after. When such a scenario fails at its fourteenth command today, `cargo test` shows only the assertion that failed. The developer needs steps 1 to 13: each argv, each envelope, each stderr event, each `net.log` line, each failpoint armed, each tree hash. Without one shared log, every suite invents its own ad-hoc prints, and none of them can be read the same way.

This bead adds that shared log, `tests/common/tlog.rs`, and a runner, `argc e2e`, that runs the end-to-end suites with the log turned up. After it, a failing M4 scenario can be diagnosed from its log alone, and the M4 checkpoint can quote evidence beyond a test name.

It was not in the M4 plan. It was added when the plan was turned into beads, at the owner's request that the beads include comprehensive unit tests and end-to-end test scripts with detailed logging, so that after implementation every behaviour can be shown to work and every failure can be diagnosed from its log. Area T (this bead and T2–T4) changes no product behaviour and adds no wire name.

"End-to-end test scripts" in this repository means Rust integration tests that drive the real `omaddons` binary through a scenario on a synthetic home (`tests/*.rs`, `TestEnv`), not shell scripts. The project's tests are Rust, and M4-D47 rejected shell fixture scripts. The one script this bead adds is an `argc` task that runs the Rust suites with logging turned up.

### What it serves

- **The slice demos become tests.** The plan's four delivery slices each end with a demo. M3 recorded its slice demos only at the end of the milestone, so problems surfaced late (the M3 checkpoint record's first lesson). In M4 the demos of slices 1–3 are tests owned by T2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.2`, slice 1 end to end), T3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.3`, slice 2 end to end) and T4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4`, slice 3 end to end), which run in every gate once their slice lands. Each of them is a suite of `TestLog` scenarios, and each records its demo on the milestone epic quoting this bead's log root.
- **The checkpoint can quote evidence.** H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the M4 checkpoint and the first tag) records every success criterion as `[x] N <criterion>: <evidence>` with test names and timings. With this bead, the evidence for an end-to-end criterion is a test name plus a transcript any reader can open.
- **The milestone goals that most depend on multi-command scenarios:**
  - G-M4-3, "what was previewed is what runs, target by target": its proofs are races between a preview and a bound run, staged with `pause` failpoints; a failing race is undiagnosable without the interleaving written down, which `log.reached`/`log.resume` and the run records provide.
  - G-M4-4, "diagnosable and repairable": the doctor's safety harness runs every fixer through corrupt, diagnose, fix, verify, undo and a crash at every primitive boundary; one failing case among hundreds needs its own log, which `log.case` gives.
  - G-M4-6, "no new risk to the engine's guarantees": every crash matrix compares whole trees; `log.tree` and `log.assert_unchanged` say which paths differ, not only that a hash moved.
- **The vision's local gate (D16: no CI).** Every test runs on the development machine before each commit, and nobody else sees the output. A failure that the developer cannot diagnose from the terminal is a failure that stalls the work.

Checkpoint criteria: this bead pre-checks none itself. It makes the evidence of criteria 5 (the intent corpus), 6 and 7 (previews and stored plans), 9 (the safety harness), 11 (stuck states) and 17 (gate and checkpoint runs) quotable, because the suites that prove them log through it.

### The decisions that shape it

- **M4-D47: fixtures are Rust, not shell.** Each doctor failure mode gets a Rust `Fixture` (in `tests/doctor/fixtures/<fm_id>.rs`, with `corrupt`, `assert_healthy`, `subject` and a doc comment), and `tests/doctor_harness.rs` runs them all. Why: the project's tests are Rust (`TestEnv`), Rust fixtures reuse the `tests/common/` builders, run in `cargo test` (so in the gate) and are deterministic by construction, and the house rules ban `rm -rf` even in test scripts. Rejected: `corrupt.sh`/`assert.sh` per failure mode, "a second test language, and shell scripts that must clean up after themselves". For this bead it means: the end-to-end "scripts" are Rust tests; the runner is a thin `argc` task over `cargo test`; and the runner deletes nothing (each test replaces its own log directory).
- **M4-D6: environment variables get a registry.** `contract::env::ENV_VARS` lists every environment variable, each with a name, a kind, a description and the flag it mirrors. The kinds: `release` (read by every build), `debug` (read by debug builds only: failpoints, fixtures, clocks) and `harness` (read only by the test harness, never by the binary). A scan of `src/` fails on any unregistered `env::var`/`var_os` literal, and a second scan checks that every `harness` name appears only in test code. `capabilities.env_vars` publishes only the `release` ones; publishing debug or harness variables was rejected because release builds ignore them and listing them would mislead. `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG` is a `harness` variable. A2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.2`, the registries) creates the registry; whichever of A2 and this bead lands second registers the variable.
- **Slice demos (plan §10.6, as amended at filing).** The plan said the agent closing a slice's last leaf records the slice's demo on the milestone epic in the `[x] <item>: <evidence>` style. At filing, that duty moved to T2–T4 for slices 1–3 (their demos are tests now); H6 still checks that the three demos exist and still records slice 4's, because slice 4 includes the tag. This bead records no demo.
- **What runs where (plan §11.1).** The gate (`argc gate`: fmt, clippy, `cargo test`, the widget pipeline, `ubs`, `cargo deny` on dependency changes) runs unit tests, the contract suite, the end-to-end suites, the crash matrices and the safety harness. Checkpoint-only tests (perf budgets, compat, live probes, the real machine) are `#[ignore]`d and follow the `SKIP` rule. `argc e2e` runs the same tests the gate's `cargo test` runs, with the log turned up; it is a convenience, never a gate step.
- **The checkpoint protocol (plan §11.3).** H6 runs every checkpoint command written out exactly, from a clean checkout, and quotes the results. Bead text and comments never contain absolute or home paths, so the demo and checkpoint comments quote this bead's log root in its repo-relative form, `target/tmp/test-logs`.
- **Common rule 10, the real machine.** Real-machine tests run against the developer's real home, never change the Forever client, and undo every change. This bead's log holds only synthetic homes: it never runs a command outside a `TestEnv`, and `log.tree` refuses a root outside the test's synthetic directories. Real-machine tests and live probes therefore do not log through it.

### 2. The log's layout and lifetime

- The log root is `<CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR>/test-logs` (`target/tmp/test-logs` by default). A test's directory is `<root>/<suite>/<test>/`, holding `steps.jsonl` (one JSON object per record) and `transcript.md` (the same records, readable). A case sub-log (Technical Approach 6) lives at `<test dir>/cases/<case>/`.
- `TestLog::new(suite, test)` removes the directory if it exists and recreates it: a rerun replaces it. Nothing else ever deletes logs; `cargo clean` removes them with `target/`, and nothing is committed.
- `let log = tlog!();` takes the suite from `module_path!()` (its first segment, which is the test crate's name) and the test name from the enclosing function: the macro defines a nested `fn __tlog_here() {}` and reads `std::any::type_name_of_val(&__tlog_here)` (stable since Rust 1.76; the toolchain is 1.97.1). From that path it drops the crate segment, the final `__tlog_here` segment and every `{{closure}}` segment, and joins the rest with `.`: `fn x` at the crate root is `x`; `fn x` in `mod scenarios` is `scenarios.x`. Joining with `.` rather than `/` keeps one test's directory from nesting inside another's (a rerun of test `x` would otherwise delete `x/y`). Every component is sanitized to `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]`: anything else becomes `_`, and an empty component or one made only of dots becomes `_`.
- The macro is defined with `macro_rules! tlog` in `tests/common/tlog.rs` and re-exported with `pub(crate) use tlog;`, so a test writes `use common::tlog::{tlog, TestLog};`. Both items carry `#[allow(unused_macros)]`/`#[allow(unused_imports)]` as needed, because 94 crates compile the module and most never use it (clippy runs with `-D warnings`). Decided while writing this bead: the re-export pattern rather than `#[macro_export]`, because it keeps the macro addressable by module path, like every other builder.
- One `TestLog` per test function. A table-driven or parallel test uses `log.case(name)` for each case.
- Call `tlog!()` in the test function itself. Inside a helper, it would name the helper; pass names explicitly with `TestLog::new(suite, test)` there.

### 3. The API

All of it in `tests/common/tlog.rs`. `TestLog` is `Send + Sync` (its state is behind one `Mutex`), so scoped threads may share it.

**Constants** (named, in `tests/common/tlog.rs`; these are test-harness constants, not the binary's, so they do not go in `src/limits.rs` and need no `REGISTRY` row):

| Constant | Value | Bounds |

| `STREAM_CAP_BYTES` | `1 << 20` (1 MiB) | each stream (stdout, stderr) of each run record, each note's text, each JSON value's serialization |
| `TEST_CAP_BYTES` | `64 << 20` (64 MiB) | both files of one test together, its case sub-logs included |
| `LAST_STEPS_SHOWN` | 20 | the records the panic guard prints |

| `SCRUB_MIN_LEN` | 8 | the shortest secret value scrubbed from text |

The plan fixes 1 MiB per stream per step, 64 MiB per test and the last 20 steps. Decided while writing this bead: `DIFF_PATHS_SHOWN` 20 (as many as the guard shows), `RUN_TIMEOUT` 300 s (five times a failpoint pause's 60 s maximum, so a paused child always resumes first, and far above any single debug-build command on the realistic home), and `SCRUB_MIN_LEN` 8 (Technical Approach 5).

Decided while writing this bead: the `Runner` trait over `std::process::Command`, rather than `TestEnv::command()`'s `assert_cmd::Command`, because a background run, a timeout and reading back the variables a scenario set (`Command::get_envs`) all need the standard type, and because scenarios with HTTP fixtures or a fake `/proc` already build their command with `Home::std_command`. The environment is exactly the one `TestEnv::command()` applies: both go through the same `vars()`, `SETTINGS` and `removed()` (`tests/common/env.rs:97-146`).

`argv` passed to `run` does not include the binary name; the log records it as `["omaddons", …]`. Nothing is appended: unlike `Home::run`, `log.run` does not add `--json`, so the argv logged is exactly the argv that ran.

A failing `Ran` assertion first appends a `failure` record, then panics with:

```text
tlog: run #7 in step "apply the stored plan": expected exit 0, got 4
  error: game_running: the retail client is running
  argv: omaddons apply 01M6T… --json
  transcript: <absolute path of transcript.md>
```

(the error line is present when stdout is an envelope with an `error`; the absolute path is printed on the developer's terminal only, never written into a log file). `log.assert_eq` records an `assert` record with both values and, on a mismatch, panics with the label, both values, the step and the transcript path.

**Decided while writing this bead** (the plan names only `run`, `step`, `note`, `json`, `tree`, `assert_unchanged` and `Ran::{ok, exit, envelope, data, error_code, warnings, commands}`): the additions `cmd`/`Cmd`/`Running` (background runs, extra variables, stdin, timeouts), `reached`/`resume`, `diff`, `case`, `env`, `secret`, `assert_eq`, `Ran::{fails, aborted, events, assert_private, stdout, stderr}`, and `Ran.run` as a `common::home::Run`, because the M4 suites need races, crash children, stdin-fed commands (credentials) and privacy checks, and each of those would otherwise bypass the log.

### 4. What a run records

`log.run`/`Cmd::run`/`Running::wait` build the command through `Runner::command`, add the `Cmd`'s variables, stdin (`Stdio::null()` when none, as `Command::output()` does) and working directory, spawn it with piped stdout and stderr read by two threads, and poll `try_wait` every 5 ms until it exits or the timeout passes (then `kill`, `wait`, record `timed_out: true` and panic naming the step and the timeout). It then records one `run` record:

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| `seq` | the record's number, assigned when the run starts (a background run's record is written when it ends, so it may follow later records) |
| `step` | the current phase label |
| `env` | the label of the `TestEnv` root it ran in (`<root>`, `<root2>`, …) |
| `argv` | `["omaddons", …]`, paths rewritten (Technical Approach 5) |
| `cwd` | the working directory set, else the inherited one (the test process runs in the package root, recorded as `<repo>`) |
| `overrides` | every variable set on the command whose value differs from that `TestEnv`'s base (read back with `std::process::Command::get_envs`; removals are not listed), secrets redacted (Technical Approach 5), paths rewritten |
| `failpoints` | `{"spec": <OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS>, "pause_dir": <OMADDONS_FAILPOINT_DIR>}` when either is set, else `null` |
| `stdin_bytes` | the length of the stdin given, else `null`; stdin content is never recorded (it may be a credential) |
| `background` | whether it was spawned with `spawn()` |
| `started_at`, `elapsed_ms` | wall clock (RFC 3339, UTC) and duration |
| `exit`, `signal`, `timed_out` | the exit code (`-1` when killed by a signal), the signal number, whether the timeout killed it |
| `stdout` | `{"form": "envelope", "value": <parsed>}` when stdout is exactly one line that parses as a JSON object; `{"form": "text", "text": …}` otherwise; `{"form": "empty"}`; plus `bytes` and `truncated` |
| `stderr` | `{"lines": [...]}`: each line parsed as JSON when it parses (an NDJSON event), else the raw string, in order; plus `bytes` and `truncated` |
| `net_log` | `{"added": [...], "rotated": bool}`: the `net.log` lines this run appended, each parsed as JSON (raw string when it does not parse) |
| `scrubbed` | the names of the secret variables whose values were scrubbed from this record |

Decided while writing this bead: `net.log` is read raw (no `omaddons` library type, so a malformed line never breaks the log and the log does not depend on `NetLogEntry`'s shape) from `<state>/omaddons/net.log.1` and `net.log` before and after the run: when the before-lines are a prefix of the after-lines, the rest is what the run added; otherwise the log rotated, and every line of the current `net.log` is recorded with `rotated: true`. Two runs in parallel on one home both see each other's lines; the record says so only implicitly, which is acceptable for a diagnostic.

The first run on a `TestEnv` (or `log.env`) also writes an `env` record with that environment's base variables (the six paths and the three settings, rewritten), so each `run` record lists only what the scenario changed. A `Running` dropped without `wait` kills its child and writes its record with a `failure` record after it, so no child outlives its test.

`Ran.run` holds the raw stdout and stderr (absolute paths, nothing scrubbed): assertions run against what the binary printed; only the log is rewritten.

### 5. Privacy: secrets and paths

- **Secret names.** A variable whose name contains `TOKEN`, `SECRET` or `CREDENTIAL`, ignoring case, is recorded as `"<redacted>"` (so `OMADDONS_GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `api_token`, `MY_SECRET`, `SOME_CREDENTIAL_FILE`). Over-redaction is harmless.
- **Secret values.** Each such value of at least `SCRUB_MIN_LEN` (8) bytes, and every value given to `log.secret`, is replaced by `<redacted>` in every record written after it is learned (argv, stdout, stderr, `net.log` lines, notes, JSON values, failure messages), longest value first. A shorter value is still redacted where it is the variable's value, but not scrubbed from text, where it would destroy unrelated output. The run record's `scrubbed` lists the variable names. A test that plants a credential in a file or feeds one on stdin calls `log.secret(value)` first.
- **What is never recorded:** the test process's own environment (only the variables a run set), stdin content, and file content other than the binary's output and `net.log` (`log.tree` records digests, never bytes).
- The plan fixes the three name fragments. Decided while writing this bead: matching ignores case, values are also scrubbed from text (so a value the binary echoed, or one a test planted in a file, cannot reach the log either), `log.secret` registers more, and stdin is recorded as a length only.
- **Paths.** Every recorded string has these prefixes rewritten, longest first: each `TestEnv` root seen → `<root>`, `<root2>`, … (in order of first use); `CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR` → `<target-tmp>`; `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` → `<repo>`. Logs of two runs then diff cleanly, and a transcript pasted into a bead comment carries no absolute path. The plan says "paths are printed relative to the `TestEnv` root"; decided while writing this bead: the named placeholders, because a test may use several homes and paths under the target directory or the repository. The rewrite applies to the raw text before JSON parsing (it replaces a path by a placeholder without quotes or backslashes, so valid JSON stays valid).
- **Synthetic homes only.** `log.run` always applies a `TestEnv`'s environment, so it can never run against the developer's real home. `log.tree`, `assert_unchanged` and `diff` refuse (panic, before reading anything) a root that is not under a `TestEnv` root this log has seen (at its first run there, or through `log.env`), `CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR` or `std::env::temp_dir()`. Decided while writing this bead, because the plan states the rule ("it never reads the developer's real `HOME`") without a mechanism.

### 6. Trees and cases

- `common::trees` gains (subtask 2), beside `tree_hash`, which does not change:

  ```rust
  pub enum EntryKind { File, Dir, Symlink }
  pub struct Entry { pub kind: EntryKind, pub mode: u32, pub len: u64, pub sha256: Option<String>, pub target: Option<String> }
  pub fn tree_entries(dir: &Path) -> BTreeMap<String, Entry>; // relative path → entry; same walk, kinds and modes as tree_hash
  pub struct TreeDiff { pub added: Vec<String>, pub removed: Vec<String>, pub changed: Vec<(String, String)>, pub total: usize }
  pub fn tree_diff(before: &BTreeMap<String, Entry>, after: &BTreeMap<String, Entry>) -> TreeDiff;
  impl TreeDiff { pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool; pub fn first(&self, n: usize) -> Vec<String>; }
  ```

  `changed` names what changed, joined with `+` in this order: `kind`, `content` (length or digest), `target` (a symlink's), `mode`. `first(n)` gives the first `n` differing paths in path order, each as `+ <path>`, `- <path>` or `~ <path> (<what>)`.
- `log.tree(label, root)` computes `tree_hash(root)` (the authoritative comparison, the function every other suite uses) and `tree_entries(root)` (for diffs; kept in memory under the label), and records `{label, root, exists, hash, entries}`. A missing root records `exists: false` and `hash: null`. Decided while writing this bead: hash with `tree_hash` and diff with a second walk, rather than changing `tree_hash`, so no existing suite's comparison changes.
- `log.assert_unchanged(label, root)` re-reads the tree, compares it with the last `tree` of that label (a label never recorded is a panic naming it), records a `tree_check` with `expected`, `actual`, `equal` and, when they differ, `diff: {total, first}` with the first `DIFF_PATHS_SHOWN` paths, and panics with the same paths, the step and the transcript path. `log.diff` records the same and returns the `TreeDiff` for the test to assert on ("only `Interface/AddOns/Foo` changed").
- `log.case(name)` creates `<test dir>/cases/<name>/` with its own two files and its own guard, writes a `case` record in the parent, and shares the parent's `TEST_CAP_BYTES` budget (an `Arc`'d counter). The doctor harness's hundreds of (fixer, failpoint) cases each get a short, readable log, and a failing case's guard points at its own transcript.

### 7. The records

`steps.jsonl` holds one compact JSON object per line, written with one `write_all` and no buffering as each record completes, so a test that is killed still leaves everything up to that point. Each record is a `#[derive(Serialize)]` struct with `kind` first and `seq` second. The format is internal to the test suite (not part of the omaddons contract; DEC-4 does not apply), versioned by the header's `format: 1`.

| `kind` | Fields after `kind`, `seq` |
|---|---|
| `header` | `format: 1`, `suite`, `test`, `started_at`, `mode` (`files`/`verbose`), `caps: {stream_bytes, test_bytes}`, `parent` (the parent's `<suite>/<test>` for a case, else `null`) |
| `env` | `name` (`<root>`, …), `vars` (the base variables) |
| `step` | `index` (1, 2, …), `label`, `at_ms` (since the log was created) |
| `note` | `step`, `text`, `truncated` |
| `json` | `step`, `label`, `value` (or `null` with `text` holding the kept prefix of its serialization when truncated), `truncated` |
| `run` | Technical Approach 4 |
| `pause` | `step`, `action` (`waiting`/`reached`/`resumed`), `name`, `dir`, `waited_ms` |
| `tree` | `step`, `label`, `root`, `exists`, `hash`, `entries` |
| `tree_check` | `step`, `label`, `root`, `check` (`unchanged`/`diff`), `expected`, `actual`, `equal`, `diff` |
| `assert` | `step`, `label`, `actual`, `expected`, `equal` |
| `case` | `step`, `name`, `dir` (`cases/<name>`) |
| `failure` | `step`, `message` |
| `capped` | `test_bytes` (written once) |
| `end` | `outcome` (`passed`/`panicked`), `records` (the records in the file, this one included), `runs`, `bytes`, `dropped`, `elapsed_ms` |

`truncated` is `null` or `{"kept": <bytes>, "total": <bytes>}`.

`transcript.md` renders the same records:

````text
# tlog_selftest :: scenarios.a_passing_scenario_writes_both_files

- started 2026-10-24T20:00:00.123Z · mode files · steps.jsonl beside this file
- env `<root>`: HOME=<root>/home XDG_CONFIG_HOME=<root>/config XDG_STATE_HOME=<root>/state XDG_CACHE_HOME=<root>/cache XDG_DATA_HOME=(HOME)/.local/share OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT=<root>/no-proc TZ=UTC OMADDONS_FS_CLONE=no OMADDONS_FS_FREE_MB=65536

## 1. help, then a usage error

### #3 run `omaddons help --json` → exit 0 (41 ms)

- cwd `<repo>` · overrides none · failpoints none · stdin none · net.log +0

stdout (envelope):

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "schema_version": "1.0",
  …
}
```

stderr: empty

### #4 run `omaddons frobnicate --json` → exit 2 (12 ms)

- …

stderr (1 line):

```json
{"event":"error","code":"usage","message":"unrecognized subcommand 'frobnicate'",…}
```

### #5 tree `state` = 3f2a9c1d… (12 entries)

### #6 tree check `state`: unchanged

---

end: passed · 8 records · 2 runs · 9,812 bytes · 0.3 s
````

Envelopes are pretty-printed in the transcript; stderr events stay one per line.

### 8. Bounds

- Per record, each stream, note text and JSON serialization is cut at `STREAM_CAP_BYTES` on a UTF-8 character boundary; the record keeps the prefix and `truncated: {kept, total}`, and the transcript says "truncated: kept N of M bytes". A truncated stdout is recorded as `form: "text"` (the prefix is no longer a parseable envelope).
- Per test, the bytes of both files (cases included) are counted against `TEST_CAP_BYTES`. The record that would pass it is replaced by one `capped` record; after that nothing more is written except the final `end` record, whose `dropped` counts the records not written. The in-memory ring of the last 20 summaries keeps working, so the panic guard still prints them. Decided while writing this bead: stop writing entirely rather than keep writing headers, so the bound is real.
- `Ran` keeps each stream whole in memory, as `Home::exec_with` does today; `RUN_TIMEOUT` bounds how long a child can print.
- Cost: a passing test writes two small files (a header, its records and an end record); there is no per-run tree hashing unless the test asks for it, and no fsync.

### 9. Modes, the live echo and the panic guard

- `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG` is read once per test process (`OnceLock`) by `parse_mode`: unset or empty → `files` (write both files); `verbose` → files plus a live echo; any other value → the first `TestLog` panics with "OMADDONS_TEST_LOG=<value> is not a log mode: use `verbose`, or leave it unset". Decided while writing this bead: a typo fails loudly rather than silently logging nothing extra.
- **The live echo** (`verbose`): every record's one-line summary is written straight to the stderr handle (`writeln!(std::io::stderr().lock(), …)`), prefixed `[tlog <suite>::<test> #<seq>]`, so parallel tests stay attributable. It bypasses libtest's capture, so it streams without `--nocapture`. Decided while writing this bead: the plan said "run with `--nocapture`"; a direct write makes that unnecessary, as `common::checkpoint::skip` already relies on.
- **The panic guard** (`Drop for TestLog`): it always writes the `end` record. When `std::thread::panicking()`, it prints, with `eprintln!`, `test log: <absolute path of transcript.md>` and `last 20 of N records:` followed by the last 20 one-line summaries (N counts the records written before `end`, the header included). `eprintln!` output is captured by libtest and shown in the failing test's `---- <test> stdout ----` section, right after the panic message, which is where a developer reading a failure looks. It carries `#[allow(clippy::print_stderr, reason = "the guard's lines belong in libtest's captured output of the failing test, beside its panic message")]`, because `clippy.toml`'s `allow-print-in-tests` does not reach helper modules. Decided while writing this bead: captured for the guard, direct for the echo.
- **Write failures** of the log (a full disk) print one `test log: cannot write <file>: <error>` line and disable that log's writes; they never fail the test, because the log is a diagnostic. The guard never panics (a panic during unwinding aborts the process).

### 10. The runner: `argc e2e [FILTER] [ARGS…]` (subtask 3)

- **Which suites.** A test crate is an end-to-end suite when its root file (`tests/<name>.rs`, or `tests/<name>/main.rs`) has a crate-doc line that starts with `//! e2e suite:` (`E2E_MARKER`), followed by a short purpose. A convention test keeps the marker honest: a crate whose files (its root file, and for a directory crate every `.rs` in its directory) call `tlog!(` or `TestLog::` on a non-comment line carries the marker, and a marked crate does call them; every `tests/e2e_*.rs` is marked; and `Argcfile.sh`'s pattern equals `E2E_MARKER`. So every suite that uses the log runs under `argc e2e`, and nothing has to keep a list. Decided while writing this bead: a marker in the suite rather than a list in `Argcfile.sh` or a text file, because many leaves add suites in parallel and a shared list is a merge hot spot.
- **The task:**

  ```bash
  # @cmd Run the end-to-end suites (each test crate marked `//! e2e suite:`) with verbose test logs, then print where the logs are
  # @arg filter  Only the suites whose name contains this; `all` or nothing runs every suite
  # @arg args~   Passed to the test binaries after `--` (a test name, --exact, --test-threads=1, --nocapture)
  e2e() {
      # 1. suites: grep -l '^//! e2e suite:' tests/*.rs tests/*/main.rs, sorted; name = file minus tests/ and .rs or /main.rs
      # 2. filter: `all`/absent keeps every suite, else those whose name contains it;
      #    none kept → "e2e: no end-to-end suite matches '<f>'. The suites: <list>. To pass test arguments to every suite: argc e2e all <args>" on stderr, exit 2
      # 3. root: target_directory from `cargo metadata --format-version 1 --no-deps` (read with sed, no jq) + /tmp/test-logs
      # 4. start=$(date +%s); OMADDONS_TEST_LOG=verbose cargo test --locked --test <s>… -- ${argc_args[@]+"${argc_args[@]}"} || status=$?
      # 5. summary: for each selected suite's dir, find steps.jsonl files newer than start (find -newermt "@$start");
      #    a file with "outcome":"panicked" is panicked; one without "kind":"end" is incomplete (the test was killed)
      # 6. print: "==> e2e: N test log(s) written, P panicked, I without an end record", one line per panicked or
      #    incomplete transcript, then "==> test logs: target/tmp/test-logs" (repo-relative when under the repo)
      # 7. exit with cargo's status
  }
  ```

  Under `set -euo pipefail`, counters use `n=$((n + 1))` (never `((n++))`, which returns 1 at zero), `grep` with no match is guarded with `|| true`, and unset arrays are expanded with `${a[@]+"${a[@]}"}`. The task deletes nothing (no `rm`): each test replaces its own directory, and the summary looks only at logs written since it started.
- Selftest children write under the suite directory `tlog_selftest_child`, which is not a suite, so the runner never summarizes their deliberate failures.
- `argc e2e` is a convenience. The gate's `cargo test` runs the same tests; the runner adds the live echo and the summary.

### 11. The conventions (written once, in `tests/common/tlog.rs`'s module doc and README's Development section)

1. Every M4 integration or end-to-end test that runs more than one command logs through `TestLog`, and its crate carries `//! e2e suite: <purpose>`.
2. Each phase of a scenario is a `log.step`.
3. Every state assertion goes through `log.tree`/`log.assert_unchanged`/`log.diff`, or `log.assert_eq`, or logs the values it compares with `log.json` before asserting.
4. Unit tests are table-driven, with a name per case and assertion messages that name the case and show the input and the output. They do not use `TestLog`.
5. An older suite adopts the log when a leaf rewrites it; nothing is converted for its own sake.
6. Real-machine tests and live probes never use `TestLog` (Technical Approach 5).
7. Bead comments quote the log root as `target/tmp/test-logs`, never as an absolute path.
