  - `secret_values_are_scrubbed_longest_first`: a value twice in one text; at the start and the end; two secrets where one contains the other (the longer replaced whole); an empty value (ignored); a 7-byte value (not scrubbed from text); an 8-byte value (scrubbed).
  - `text_is_capped_on_a_char_boundary`: under the cap (no `truncated`); exactly the cap; one byte over; a 3-byte character straddling the cap (cut before it); each with the expected `{kept, total}`.
  - `the_test_budget_stops_writing_at_the_cap`: a `Budget` with a small cap admits records until the next would pass it, then refuses every later one and counts them as dropped.
  - `function_paths_split_into_suite_and_test`: `tlog_selftest::x::__tlog_here` → (`tlog_selftest`, `x`); `contract::matrix::row::__tlog_here` → (`contract`, `matrix.row`); a path with `{{closure}}` segments → those dropped.
  - `path_components_are_sanitized`: `a b` → `a_b`; `a/b` → `a_b`; `..` → `_`; `.` → `_`; empty → `_`; `ok-name.1` unchanged.
  - `paths_are_rewritten_to_placeholders`: an env root → `<root>`; a second root → `<root2>`; a root under `CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR` (a `tempdir_in` home) → `<root>`, not `<target-tmp>/…` (longest first); `CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR` alone → `<target-tmp>`; `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` → `<repo>`; an unrelated path unchanged.
  - `log_modes_parse`: `None` → files; `""` → files; `"verbose"` → verbose; `"verbos"` → an error naming `verbose`.
  - In-process log tests (no binary): `notes_and_json_write_both_files` (header first, `step`/`note`/`json` records in order, `end` with `outcome: passed` after drop; the transcript has the step heading and the note); `a_rerun_replaces_the_directory` (a planted extra file is gone after `TestLog::new` again); `the_macro_names_the_suite_and_the_test` (`tlog!()` in `core_units::the_macro_names_the_suite_and_the_test` gives `…/tlog_selftest/core_units.the_macro_names_the_suite_and_the_test`); `an_oversized_json_value_is_truncated_and_says_so`; `the_cap_writes_one_capped_record` (`with_caps` with a 4 KiB test budget); `a_registered_secret_is_scrubbed_from_notes`; `assert_eq_failure_names_the_step_and_the_transcript` (caught with `catch_unwind`; the `failure` record exists).
- **`run_units` (subtask 2):**
  - `stdout_is_classified`: one JSON object line → envelope; a JSON line plus a second line → text; plain text → text; empty → empty; a JSON array → text.
  - `stderr_lines_parse_one_by_one`: mixed NDJSON and text lines keep their order and kinds.
  - `net_log_additions_are_the_new_suffix`: before a prefix of after → the suffix; no file before → every line; equal → none; rotated (before not a prefix) → the current file with `rotated: true`; an unparsable line → kept as a string.
  - `overrides_exclude_the_base_and_redact_secrets`: the base variables unchanged → absent; `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT` changed by `Home` → present; `OMADDONS_GITHUB_TOKEN` → `<redacted>`; a path value → rewritten.
  - `tree_entries_cover_kind_mode_content_and_target` and `tree_diff_names_what_changed`: added file; removed file; same-size content change; mode change; file replaced by a directory; symlink retargeted; an empty directory added; 25 changed paths → `total: 25`, `first(20)` in path order. `tree_hash_and_tree_entries_agree`: for each case, `tree_hash` differs exactly when `tree_entries` differs.
  - `tree_roots_outside_the_test_are_refused`: a path under a registered env root → allowed; under `CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR` → allowed; `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR/src` → refused.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

`tests/tlog_selftest.rs`, module `scenarios` (subtask 4), each scenario logging itself with `tlog!()` and inspecting a subject log created with `TestLog::new("tlog_selftest_child", <scenario>)` (or `with_caps`), dropped before its files are read:

- `a_passing_scenario_writes_both_files`: `TestEnv::new()`; subject steps `help, then a usage error` and `status`; runs `help --json` (exit 0), `frobnicate --json` (exit 2, `fails(2, "usage")`), `status --json` (exit 0); `tree("state", env.state())` then `assert_unchanged` after a `config get check_interval_hours --json`. Asserts the record kinds in order, every run field of Technical Approach 4 present with the right values (`exit`, `stdout.form: envelope`, the stderr `error` event parsed, `net_log.added: []`, `failpoints: null`, `cwd: <repo>`), the `end` record, the transcript's headings and fenced envelope, and both files together under 64 KiB.
- `net_log_lines_are_recorded`: `Home::new(&["wow"])` with `gh_release(&home.http, "https://github.com/o/foo", "v1", …)`; `install gh:o/foo -t retail --json` → the run's `net_log.added` has the same entries, in order, as `common::netlog::read_net_log` (`release-latest`, `release-json`, `asset` purposes); a following `status --cached --json` adds none.
- `failpoints_and_pauses_are_recorded`: a `Scene` install spawned with `.failpoints("engine.plan.done=pause").pause(&pause)` (paused before the lock, so a reader runs freely); `log.reached`, a `status --json` meanwhile, `log.resume`, `wait()` → the run record's `failpoints`, three `pause` records, `background: true`, and the `seq` of the background run lower than the `status` run's although its record comes later.
- `an_aborted_child_is_recorded_with_its_signal`: `.failpoints("engine.journal.prepared=abort")` → `exit: -1`, `signal: 6`, `Ran::aborted()` passes, `Ran::ok()` fails with the step in its message.
- `a_hung_child_is_killed_at_its_timeout`: paused at a failpoint never resumed, `.timeout(300 ms)` → the run panics (caught) naming the timeout, the record has `timed_out: true`, and the child process no longer exists.
- `a_planted_token_never_reaches_the_files`: `OMADDONS_GITHUB_TOKEN=tlogSelftestToken-0123456789abcdef` (a fake) on `status --json`; another value via `log.secret` printed in a note → neither value appears in either file; `"<redacted>"` and `scrubbed: ["OMADDONS_GITHUB_TOKEN"]` do.
- `truncation_and_capping_are_recorded`: `with_caps(stream 256 B, test 8 KiB)`; `help --json` → `stdout.form: text`, `truncated.kept: 256`; repeated runs until the cap → exactly one `capped` record, later runs absent, `end.dropped` equal to the runs after the cap, and the transcript says so.
- `tree_differences_name_the_paths`: a tree under the env root; a content edit, a `chmod`, a retargeted symlink → `assert_unchanged` panics (caught) listing the three `~` paths with `content`, `mode`, `target`; `diff()` returns the same; an unchanged tree passes.
- `ran_assertions_name_the_step_and_the_transcript`: `exit(0)` on the exit-2 run → the message has the step label, `expected exit 0, got 2`, `usage` and the transcript path.
- `cases_have_their_own_files_and_share_the_budget`: two cases from two scoped threads, each with a run → both case directories have both files, the parent has two `case` records, and the bytes count against the parent's cap.
- `paths_are_relative_in_both_files`: neither file contains the env root's absolute path, `CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR` or `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`.

Module `child` holds the `#[ignore = "run by a parent test as a child process"]` children, each returning at once unless `TLOG_SELFTEST_CHILD=1` (a private handshake of this crate, not an `OMADDONS_` variable, so it needs no registry row and `TestEnv` does not strip it). Their parents in `scenarios` run `std::env::current_exe()` with `--ignored --exact child::<name> --test-threads=1`, setting or removing `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG` explicitly. Decided while writing this bead: child processes of the test binary itself, because the panic guard's output and the log mode are per process (a test cannot set its own environment in edition 2024 without `unsafe`, which the crate forbids), and because the realistic check is libtest's own failure output. The children write under the suite directory `tlog_selftest_child`, which `argc e2e` never summarizes:

- `a_failing_test_prints_its_log_and_last_steps`: the child writes 25 notes (`note 01` … `note 25`) and fails a `Ran` assertion on a `frobnicate --json` run (29 records before `end`: header, 25 notes, `env`, `run`, `failure`); the parent asserts a non-zero exit, the assertion message, then `test log: …/tlog_selftest_child/fails_after_twenty_five_notes/transcript.md` and `last 20 of 29 records:`, with `note 09` … `note 25`, the run and the failure present and `note 08` absent, and the child's `steps.jsonl` ending with a `failure` record and `outcome: panicked`.
- `verbose_echoes_every_record_live`: the child runs three steps with `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG=verbose` and without `--nocapture` → its stderr has the `[tlog tlog_selftest_child::…]` lines in order; with the variable removed → none.
- `an_unknown_log_mode_fails_the_test`: `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG=verbos` → the child fails with the message naming `verbose`.

Module `convention` (subtask 3): `every_test_log_suite_carries_the_e2e_marker` and `the_runner_uses_the_marker` (Technical Approach 10).

### Logging

- The scenarios log themselves through `tlog!()`: one `step` per phase (build the subject, run it, read its files, check), `log.json("subject records", …)` with the subject's record kinds and counts (not its whole content), and `log.note` with the subject transcript's path before each file assertion, so a failing self-test shows what it inspected.
- Unit tests name each case in their assertion messages and show the input and the output; they do not use `TestLog`.
- `argc e2e tlog` runs the whole self-test with the live echo; its summary is quoted in the close comment.

### Checkpoint-only tests

None. Nothing here needs a real machine, the network or a release build, and nothing is `#[ignore]`d except the child-process helpers, which pass trivially when run directly.

## Considerations

- **Cost.** 94 crates compile `tests/common/`, so `tlog.rs` adds compile time to each (expected a few seconds in total for a debug build); keep it free of heavy generics and new dependencies. At run time it writes two small files per test and reads `net.log` twice per run; it hashes trees only when asked. The doctor harness (F9, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`) has a 60 s target in the gate with hundreds of child runs; if the log's per-run overhead shows up there, that is a defect filed `discovered-from` this bead, fixed by making the log cheaper, never by dropping crash positions.
- **It never changes how existing tests behave.** Existing suites keep their own runners (`Home::run`, `Scene::run`); `tree_hash` is untouched; M4's new suites adopt the log, and an older suite adopts it only when a leaf rewrites it.
- **Privacy.** The log holds only synthetic homes, secrets are redacted and scrubbed, stdin and the test process's environment are never recorded, and paths are rewritten, because a transcript is exactly what someone pastes into a bead comment. Real-machine tests and live probes do not use it.
- **What could go wrong.**
  - libtest changes how it captures output: the child-process tests fail first, and the guard or the echo switches between `eprintln!` and a direct write.
  - `type_name_of_val`'s format changes (it is documented as not guaranteed): `the_macro_names_the_suite_and_the_test` fails first; `TestLog::new` with explicit names keeps working.
  - Flaky child-process tests under a loaded gate: every wait is bounded (`Pause` 30 s, failpoint pauses 60 s, `RUN_TIMEOUT` 300 s), and the hung-child test uses its own 300 ms timeout on a child that is certainly paused.
  - A test that runs two scenarios against one home in parallel sees both runs' `net.log` lines in each record: acceptable for a diagnostic, and documented in the module doc.
- **Collision rules.** `tests/common/mod.rs` gains `pub mod` lines from several M4 leaves (`intent_home`, `realistic_home`, the doctor helpers, `plans::age_plan`): append, rebase. README: edit only the Development subsection, the "Other tasks" line, the Tests row and the harness list; H4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`, the README final pass) reconciles counts. `src/contract/env.rs` belongs to A2; add the one row only. `Argcfile.sh` has no other M4 writer.
- **Why size M, four subtasks.** The log core, the binary runner with trees, the runner script with docs, and the self-test suite are separable commits that each pass the gate; together about 1,200 lines including tests.
- **Compatibility.** No product behaviour, no wire name, no state file. The log format is internal (`format: 1`); its only readers are `argc e2e`'s summary greps (`"kind":"end"`, `"outcome":"panicked"`), which the self-test exercises.
- **Decided defaults, collected** (each "Decided while writing this bead" above; confirm or adjust in the close comment): unit tests in `tests/tlog_selftest.rs`; the `Runner` trait over `std::process::Command`; the API additions; the redaction rules and `SCRUB_MIN_LEN`; path placeholders; refusing tree roots outside the test; `tree_entries` beside an unchanged `tree_hash`; stop writing at the test cap; `RUN_TIMEOUT` 300 s; the live echo written directly and the guard captured; strict `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG` values; the `.`-joined test directory names; the marker convention; the runner's `all`, exit 2 and summary; child processes through the test binary with `TLOG_SELFTEST_CHILD`; the A2 coordination.

## Dependencies

Parent: AREA-T (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9`, "Epic: M4 test infrastructure and end-to-end scenario suites"), which is `parent-child` to the milestone epic `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`.

**Blocked by:** none (a root). It can start at once and should, because every bead that writes an integration test waits for it.

**Unblocks:**
- T2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.2`, Slice 1 end to end: self-describing): its `tests/e2e_slice1.rs` scenarios are `TestLog` scenarios, and its demo comment quotes the log root.
- T3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.3`, Slice 2 end to end: preview, then apply exactly): the same for `tests/e2e_slice2.rs`, whose races need `cmd().spawn()`, `reached` and `resume`.
- T4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4`, Slice 3 end to end: diagnose and repair): the same for `tests/e2e_slice3.rs`, over the doctor fixtures.
- Every bead (leaf or subtask) whose spec says it writes integration or end-to-end tests: the filing step adds a `blocks` edge from this bead to each, so `br show omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1` lists them as dependents. They need the log to exist before their first scenario is written, so no suite invents its own.

**Slice:** `slice-1` (self-describing). Its demo is recorded by T2 as a test; this bead records no demo.

**Related, not edges:**
- A2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.2`): the `ENV_VARS` registry; whichever of A2 and this bead lands second registers `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG`.
- B1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.2.1`): if its guide lists harness variables, the guide is regenerated (common rule 17).
- F9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`, the safety harness): the heaviest user, through `log.case`; its 60 s target is where the log's cost would show.
- C4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.3.4`, the run-the-fix corpus) and D7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.7`, release drift and apply races): multi-command suites that log through it.
- H4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`): reconciles README's test counts. H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`): quotes test names and transcripts as checkpoint evidence, and checks that T2–T4 recorded their demos.

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M4 plan, 2026-10-24).**

**Why this bead.** M4 adds about a dozen integration suites whose scenarios run five to twenty commands against one synthetic home, crash children at failpoints, pause them to force races, and compare tree hashes. Today a failing scenario prints only its last assertion, so a failure at step 14 says nothing about steps 1 to 13, and every suite would invent its own prints. This bead adds one structured step log (`tests/common/tlog.rs`: `steps.jsonl` and `transcript.md` per test, every argv, envelope, stderr event, `net.log` line, failpoint and tree hash recorded, secrets redacted, paths rewritten, bounded) and one runner (`argc e2e`). After it, a failing M4 scenario is diagnosable from its log alone, the slice demos of T2–T4 are tests whose evidence is a transcript, and the checkpoint (H6) can quote more than a test name. It was added at bead filing, at the owner's request for comprehensive end-to-end tests with detailed logging; it changes no product behaviour and adds no wire name.

**Decisions applied.**
- **M4-D47: tests are Rust, never shell.** The end-to-end "scripts" are Rust integration tests driving the real binary on synthetic homes; the runner is a thin `argc` task over `cargo test` that deletes nothing. Rejected: shell scripts per scenario ("a second test language, and shell scripts that must clean up after themselves"; the house rules ban `rm -rf` even in tests).
- **M4-D6: `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG` is a `harness` variable** in `contract::env::ENV_VARS`, read only by test code, never by the binary, and not published in `capabilities` (which lists `release` variables only). Whichever of A2 and this bead lands second registers it.
- **§10.6 as amended at filing:** the demos of slices 1–3 are recorded by T2–T4 as tests, not by whoever closes a slice's last leaf; this bead records none.
- **§11.1 and §11.3:** `argc e2e` runs the same tests as the gate's `cargo test`, only with the live echo and a summary; checkpoint commands stay as the plan writes them, and comments quote the log root repo-relative (`target/tmp/test-logs`).
- **Common rule 10:** the log holds only synthetic homes; real-machine tests and live probes do not use it, and `log.tree` refuses roots outside the test's synthetic directories.

**Alternatives rejected here.**
- Per-suite ad-hoc printing: unreadable across suites, and lost by libtest's capture unless every test runs with `--nocapture`.
- `assert_cmd::Command` (`TestEnv::command()`) as the runner: it cannot spawn in the background or report the variables a scenario set; the log builds a `std::process::Command` with the same environment (`TestEnv::apply_to`, `Home::std_command`).
- Unit tests inside `tests/common/tlog.rs`: 94 crates compile that directory, so each `#[test]` would run 94 times; they go in `tests/tlog_selftest.rs`, as the builders' own tests go in `tests/common_selftest.rs`.
- A list of end-to-end suites in `Argcfile.sh` or a text file: a merge hot spot for every leaf that adds a suite; a marker line in the suite, enforced by a test, needs no list.
- Changing `tree_hash` to produce per-path output: every existing suite compares with it; `tree_entries` and `tree_diff` are added beside it instead.

**Risks and how they are watched.**
- The log slows the gate, most visibly the doctor harness's 60 s target (F9): two small files per test, `net.log` read twice per run, trees hashed only on request, no fsync; a measurable slowdown is a defect filed `discovered-from` this bead and fixed in the log.
- A log leaks a secret or a real path: name-based redaction plus value scrubbing, stdin and the process environment never recorded, path placeholders, tree roots confined to synthetic directories, each with a self-test.
- libtest's capture behaviour or `type_name_of_val`'s format changes: the child-process tests and the macro test fail first.
- Flaky child-process tests: every wait is bounded (`Pause` 30 s, failpoint pauses 60 s, `RUN_TIMEOUT` 300 s).

**What it unblocks, and why they wait.** T2, T3 and T4 (the slice demos as tests) are suites of `TestLog` scenarios. Every bead whose spec writes an integration or end-to-end test gets a `blocks` edge from this bead at filing, so no suite is written before the shared log exists and none invents its own. This bead is a root and small (size M, four subtasks), so it adds nothing to the critical path.

**How it serves the milestone's goals.** Indirectly, all six: the proofs of G-M4-3 (previews bind, target by target) are races staged with `pause` failpoints, whose interleavings the log records; G-M4-4's safety harness runs hundreds of fixer and crash cases, each with its own case log; G-M4-6's crash matrices compare whole trees, and the log names the differing paths. And the vision's local gate (D16, no CI) only works if the developer at the terminal can diagnose what failed.

**Confidence.** High. It is self-contained test code over existing builders (`TestEnv`, `Home`, `Scene`, `Pause`, `tree_hash`), with no product change beyond one registry row, and its every promise is checked by its own self-test, including the failure output in a child process.

comments.text:
**The M4 plan's entry for T1, verbatim (M4 plan, 2026-10-24).** This is area T's entry, added at bead filing, kept as provenance. The description above is the authoritative, elaborated version; where they differ, the description was decided while filing and says why.

#### T1 Structured test logs, and the `argc e2e` runner
- **Type** task · **P1** · **size-M** · **slice-1**
- **Blocked by:** none (a root).
- **Unblocks:** T2, T3, T4, and every bead (leaf or subtask) that writes an integration or end-to-end test: each such bead carries its own `blocks` edge from T1, added at filing from the bead's `uses_test_log` flag.
- **Background.** The repository has about 5,200 lines of DEC-8 builders in `tests/common/` (`TestEnv`, synthetic trees, HTTP fixtures, `pause` failpoints, tree hashes), but an integration test that fails today prints only the assertion that failed. M4 adds about a dozen new integration suites (capabilities, robot-docs, skill and recipes, apply and plans, the doctor and its repair matrices, the harness, durability, compat_m3) whose scenarios run five to twenty commands each against one home, crash children at failpoints, and compare tree hashes. When one of those fails at step 14, the developer needs to see steps 1 to 13: each argv, each envelope, each stderr event, each `net.log` line, each tree hash. Without a shared log, every suite invents its own `eprintln!`s, and the checkpoint (H6) cannot quote evidence beyond a test name.
- **Technical approach.**
  1. `tests/common/tlog.rs`, a structured step log for integration tests:
     - `TestLog::new(suite, test)` (and a `tlog!()` macro that takes the suite from `module_path!()` and the test name from the enclosing function) creates `<CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR>/test-logs/<suite>/<test>/`, with `steps.jsonl` (one JSON object per step) and `transcript.md` (the same, readable). A rerun replaces the directory.
     - `log.step(label)` opens a named phase; `log.note(text)`; `log.json(label, &value)`.
     - `log.run(&env, argv) -> Ran`: runs the real binary through `TestEnv::command()`, and records: the sequence number, the phase label, the argv, the environment overrides the test set (any variable whose name contains `TOKEN`, `SECRET` or `CREDENTIAL` redacted), the working directory, the start time, `elapsed_ms`, the exit code, stdout (parsed as the JSON envelope when it is one and pretty-printed in the transcript, else the raw text), stderr (each NDJSON event parsed, else raw lines), the `net.log` lines this run added, and the failpoints armed (`OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS`). Captures are bounded by named constants in `tests/common/tlog.rs` (1 MiB per stream per step, 64 MiB per test), and a truncation is logged, never silent.
     - `Ran` helpers: `ok()`, `exit(n)`, `envelope()`, `data()`, `error_code()`, `warnings()`, `commands()`. A failing `Ran` assertion panics with the step, the expected and actual exit, the error code and message, and the transcript path.
     - `log.tree(label, root)`: the tree hash (`common` already computes one that covers modes and symlink targets; reuse it) and entry count, recorded; `log.assert_unchanged(label, root)` compares with an earlier `tree` of the same label and, on a difference, logs the first differing paths.
     - A drop guard: when the test panics, it prints `test log: <path>` and the last 20 steps to stderr, so `cargo test` output always points at the log. With `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG=verbose` every step is also echoed to stderr as it happens (run with `--nocapture`).
     - Privacy: the log holds only synthetic `TestEnv` homes; it never reads the developer's real `HOME`. Paths are printed relative to the `TestEnv` root.
  2. `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG` is a harness variable. It is registered in `contract::env::ENV_VARS` with kind `harness` (A2's registry; whichever of A2 and T1 lands second registers it, and A2's scan requires harness names to appear only under `tests/`).
  3. **The runner.** An `argc e2e [FILTER]` task in `Argcfile.sh` runs the M4 end-to-end suites (`tests/e2e_*.rs` and the suites each leaf marks end to end) with `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG=verbose`, and prints the log root at the end. It is a convenience: the gate's `cargo test` runs the same tests.
  4. **Conventions, written once in `tests/common/tlog.rs`'s module doc and in README's Development section:** every M4 integration test that runs more than one command uses `TestLog`; each phase of a scenario is a `step`; every state assertion goes through `log.tree`/`assert_unchanged` or logs the values it compares; unit tests are table-driven, with a name per case and assertion messages that name the case and show the input and output.
  5. A self-test, `tests/tlog_selftest.rs`: a scenario that passes writes both files with the expected steps; a child test that fails (run as a subprocess) prints the transcript path; redaction hides a planted token; truncation is recorded.
- **Acceptance criteria.**
  - `TestLog` writes `steps.jsonl` and `transcript.md` for a scenario of several commands, with every field above.
  - A failing assertion prints the log path and the last steps; `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG=verbose` echoes steps live.
  - A planted `OMADDONS_GITHUB_TOKEN` value never appears in either file.
  - `argc e2e` runs the suites and prints the log root.
  - The env-var registry lists `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG` as `harness` (once A2 has landed).
  - README's Development section documents the logs and `argc e2e`.
- **Test plan.** `tests/tlog_selftest.rs` as above; unit tests of the redaction and the truncation inside `tests/common/tlog.rs`.
- **Considerations.** It must stay cheap: a passing test writes two small files. It never changes how existing tests behave; M4's new suites adopt it, and an older suite may adopt it when a leaf rewrites it. The log directory is under `CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR`, so `cargo clean` removes it and nothing is committed.

title: The test log core: `TestLog`, `tlog!`, the two files, redaction, bounds and the panic guard
description:
Part 1 of 4 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1 (Structured test logs, and the `argc e2e` runner). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`) gives every M4 integration and end-to-end test one structured step log, so a scenario that fails at its fourteenth command can be diagnosed from the record of the thirteen before it: each argv, envelope, stderr event, `net.log` line, failpoint and tree hash. M4 adds about a dozen suites of such scenarios (capabilities, robot-docs, the skill, `apply` and plans, the doctor and its repair matrices, the safety harness, durability), and its slice demos (T2–T4) are tests built on this log. Today a failing integration test prints only its last assertion, and nothing is shared. The bead was added when the M4 plan was filed as beads, at the owner's request for end-to-end tests with detailed logging; it changes no product behaviour and adds no wire name.

This part builds the log itself: the `TestLog` object and the `tlog!()` macro, the two files and their record format, redaction of secrets, rewriting of paths, the bounds, the log modes, the live echo and the panic guard, plus the unit tests of all of it. It is its own step because it runs no binary: it can be built and proved in isolation, and part 2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1.2`) then adds running the binary and recording trees on top of a log whose format, bounds and privacy rules are already settled.

## Technical Approach

### Files

- `tests/common/tlog.rs` (new): everything below, with the module doc of "Conventions".
- `tests/common/mod.rs`: `pub mod tlog;` (keep the list alphabetical: between `targets` and `trees`) and the words "a structured step log (`tlog`)" in the module doc's list of builders.
- `tests/tlog_selftest.rs` (new test crate, `mod common;` at its root): the crate doc (one paragraph: what it proves) and `mod core_units` with this part's unit tests. Later parts add `run_units` (part 2), `convention` (part 3), `scenarios` and `child` (part 4); keep this part's tests inside `core_units` so those modules never collide.

Facts this part relies on (as of `c0ab5e9`):
- `tests/common/mod.rs:12-13` allows `dead_code`, `unwrap_used` and `expect_used` for every module under `tests/common/`. No file there has a `#[test]`, and 94 test crates compile the directory (93 `mod common;` lines plus `tests/contract/main.rs:8-9`), so any `#[test]` placed there would run 94 times. Builders are tested in a self-test crate (`tests/common_selftest.rs`). The plan put "unit tests of the redaction and the truncation inside `tests/common/tlog.rs`"; decided while writing this bead: they go in `tests/tlog_selftest.rs`, and the helpers they call are `pub`.
- `Cargo.toml` `[lints.clippy]` denies `print_stdout`, `print_stderr`, `unwrap_used`, `expect_used`, `dbg_macro`; `[lints.rust]` forbids `unsafe_code`. `clippy.toml`'s `allow-print-in-tests` reaches only `#[test]` functions and `#[cfg(test)]` items, not helper modules, so a print in `tests/common/tlog.rs` needs a local `#[allow(clippy::print_stderr, reason = "…")]`.
- libtest captures only the `print!`/`eprint!` family and panic messages; a direct write to the stderr handle is not captured (`tests/common/checkpoint.rs:19-26` writes its `SKIP` lines that way on purpose).
- Edition 2024: `std::env::set_var` is `unsafe`, which the crate forbids, so a test cannot change its own environment; anything depending on `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG` in the test process is tested in a child process (part 4).
- `TestEnv` (`tests/common/env.rs`) removes every `OMADDONS_*` variable of the test process from the binary's environment (`:133-146`), so `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG` never reaches the binary.
- `CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR` (`<target dir>/tmp`, `target/tmp` by default) is a compile-time variable of integration tests, already used by `tests/backup_create.rs:422`; `target/` is ignored by git.
- `serde` (derive), `serde_json`, `jiff` and `sha2` are dependencies already; no crate is added.

### Constants (named, in `tests/common/tlog.rs`)

These bound test-harness behaviour, not the binary's, so they do not go in `src/limits.rs` and need no `REGISTRY` row.

| Constant | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `STREAM_CAP_BYTES: usize` | `1 << 20` (1 MiB) | the most bytes a record keeps of one stream (stdout, stderr), one note's text or one JSON value's serialization |
| `TEST_CAP_BYTES: u64` | `64 << 20` (64 MiB) | the most bytes one test writes to both files together, case sub-logs included |
| `LAST_STEPS_SHOWN: usize` | 20 | records the panic guard prints |
| `DIFF_PATHS_SHOWN: usize` | 20 | differing paths a tree check logs (used by part 2) |
| `RUN_TIMEOUT: Duration` | 300 s | the longest one run may take (used by part 2) |
| `SCRUB_MIN_LEN: usize` | 8 | the shortest secret value scrubbed from text |
| `LOG_MODE_VAR: &str` | `"OMADDONS_TEST_LOG"` | the mode variable |

The plan fixes 1 MiB, 64 MiB and 20 steps; decided while writing this bead: the other values (`RUN_TIMEOUT` is five times a failpoint pause's 60 s maximum, so a paused child always resumes first).

### The log's layout

- `pub fn log_root() -> PathBuf` = `Path::new(env!("CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR")).join("test-logs")`.
- A test's directory is `<log root>/<suite>/<test>/` with `steps.jsonl` and `transcript.md`. `TestLog::new` removes that directory if it exists (`std::fs::remove_dir_all`; test code may use `std::fs`, `tests/single_writer.rs` scans `src/` only) and recreates it: a rerun replaces it. Nothing else deletes logs; `cargo clean` removes them, nothing is committed.
- Names: `pub fn sanitize_component(s: &str) -> String` maps every character outside `[A-Za-z0-9_.-]` to `_`, and an empty component or one made only of dots to `_`.

### The API of this part

```rust
pub enum Mode { Files, Verbose }
pub fn parse_mode(value: Option<&str>) -> Result<Mode, String>;
pub struct Caps { pub stream_bytes: usize, pub test_bytes: u64 }   // Default: STREAM_CAP_BYTES, TEST_CAP_BYTES

pub struct TestLog { /* Arc<Mutex<Inner>> plus the paths; Send + Sync */ }
impl TestLog {
    pub fn new(suite: &str, test: &str) -> Self;
    pub fn with_caps(suite: &str, test: &str, caps: Caps) -> Self;
    #[doc(hidden)] pub fn from_location(module_path: &str, fn_type_name: &str) -> Self;
    pub fn dir(&self) -> &Path;
    pub fn steps_path(&self) -> PathBuf;
    pub fn transcript_path(&self) -> PathBuf;
    pub fn step(&self, label: &str);
    pub fn note(&self, text: impl AsRef<str>);
    pub fn json(&self, label: &str, value: &impl Serialize);
    pub fn secret(&self, value: &str);
    pub fn assert_eq<T: Serialize + PartialEq + Debug>(&self, label: &str, actual: &T, expected: &T);
}
impl Drop for TestLog { /* the end record, and the panic guard */ }
```

Plus the pure helpers, `pub` for the unit tests: `is_secret_name`, `Scrubber` (`new`, `add`, `scrub`), `Relativizer` (`new`, `add_root(&Path) -> String`, `rewrite(&str) -> String`), `cap_text(&str, usize) -> (&str, Option<Truncated>)`, `Budget` (`new(cap)`, `admit(bytes) -> bool`, `dropped()`), `split_location(module_path, fn_type_name) -> (String, String)` and `sanitize_component`.

Part 2 adds `run`, `cmd`, `reached`, `resume`, `tree`, `assert_unchanged`, `diff` and `case` to the same type, so design `Inner` for them now: a record writer that every kind goes through, a current step label, a sequence counter, the set of known `TestEnv` roots, the secrets, the budget (an `Arc` so a case can share it) and the ring of the last 20 summaries.

### The macro

```rust
macro_rules! tlog {
    () => {{
        fn __tlog_here() {}
        $crate::common::tlog::TestLog::from_location(module_path!(), ::std::any::type_name_of_val(&__tlog_here))
    }};
}
#[allow(unused_imports)]
pub(crate) use tlog;
```

- `type_name_of_val` is stable since Rust 1.76 (toolchain 1.97.1). For `fn x` in `mod core_units` of crate `tlog_selftest`, it gives `tlog_selftest::core_units::x::__tlog_here`.
- `split_location` takes the suite from `module_path!()`'s first segment (the crate name, which equals the test target's name), drops that segment, the final `__tlog_here` and every `{{closure}}` segment from the function path, and joins the rest with `.`: `core_units.x`. A `.` rather than `/` keeps one test's directory from nesting inside another's (rerunning `x` would otherwise delete `x/y`).
- `$crate::common` resolves because every test crate declares `mod common` at its root.
- `#[allow(unused_macros)]` on the `macro_rules!` and `#[allow(unused_imports)]` on the re-export, because most of the 94 crates never use it and clippy runs with `-D warnings`. Confirm with `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`.
- Decided while writing this bead: the `pub(crate) use` re-export rather than `#[macro_export]`, so tests import it by path like every other builder (`use common::tlog::{tlog, TestLog};`).
- Call `tlog!()` in the test function itself; a helper should call `TestLog::new` with explicit names. One `TestLog` per test; a table-driven or parallel test uses part 2's `log.case`.

### Records

`steps.jsonl` holds one compact JSON object per line. Each record is a `#[derive(Serialize)]` struct with `kind` first and `seq` second, written with a single `write_all` on an unbuffered `File` opened for appending, as soon as the record is complete (no fsync), so a killed test still leaves everything written so far. The format is internal to the test suite, not part of the omaddons contract (DEC-4 does not apply), versioned by the header's `format: 1`. The kinds this part writes:

| `kind` | Fields after `kind`, `seq` |
|---|---|
| `header` | `format: 1`, `suite`, `test`, `started_at` (RFC 3339 UTC, `jiff::Timestamp::now()`), `mode` (`files`/`verbose`), `caps: {stream_bytes, test_bytes}`, `parent` (`null`; part 2 sets it for a case) |
| `step` | `index` (1, 2, …), `label`, `at_ms` (milliseconds since the log was created) |
| `note` | `step` (the current label, `null` before the first step), `text`, `truncated` |
| `json` | `step`, `label`, `value` (or `null`, with `text` holding the kept prefix of its serialization, when truncated), `truncated` |
| `assert` | `step`, `label`, `actual`, `expected`, `equal` |
| `failure` | `step`, `message` |
| `capped` | `test_bytes` |
| `end` | `outcome` (`passed`/`panicked`), `records` (the records in the file, this one included), `runs` (0 until part 2), `bytes`, `dropped`, `elapsed_ms` |

`truncated` is `null` or `{"kept": <bytes>, "total": <bytes>}`. Part 2 adds `env`, `run`, `pause`, `tree`, `tree_check` and `case`.

`transcript.md` renders the same records as they are written:

````text
# tlog_selftest :: core_units.notes_and_json_write_both_files

- started 2026-10-24T20:00:00.123Z · mode files · steps.jsonl beside this file

## 1. first phase

note: the first note

### json `sample`

```json
{
  "a": 1
}
```

### assert `count`: equal (3)

---

end: passed · 6 records · 0 runs · 1,234 bytes · 0.0 s
````

Each record also has a one-line summary (`step 1: first phase`, `note: the first note`, `json sample`, `assert count: equal`), kept in a ring of the last `LAST_STEPS_SHOWN` and used by the live echo and the panic guard.

### Privacy

- **Secret names.** `pub fn is_secret_name(name: &str) -> bool`: the name contains `TOKEN`, `SECRET` or `CREDENTIAL`, ignoring case. The plan fixes the three fragments; decided while writing this bead: ignoring case.
- **Secret values.** `Scrubber` holds every secret value (part 2 adds the values of secret-named variables a run sets; `log.secret(value)` adds any other) and replaces each occurrence with `<redacted>` in every record written after it is learned, longest value first. A value shorter than `SCRUB_MIN_LEN` is not scrubbed from text (a value like `1` would destroy unrelated output); part 2 still records it as `<redacted>` where it is a variable's value. Decided while writing this bead: value scrubbing and `log.secret`, so a value the binary echoed or a test planted in a file cannot reach the log.
- **Paths.** `Relativizer` rewrites, longest prefix first: each `TestEnv` root added (part 2 adds them as runs use them) → `<root>`, `<root2>`, … in order of addition; `CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR` → `<target-tmp>`; `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` → `<repo>`. A home built with `tempdir_in(CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR)` is therefore `<root>`, not `<target-tmp>/…`. It applies to every recorded string (labels, notes, JSON values' strings, and in part 2 argv, output and paths). The plan says "paths are printed relative to the `TestEnv` root"; decided while writing this bead: named placeholders, because a test may use several homes and paths under the target directory or the repository, and because a transcript pasted into a bead comment must carry no absolute path.
- The log never records the test process's environment, and never reads the developer's real home.

### Bounds

- `cap_text(text, cap)` keeps at most `cap` bytes, cut on a UTF-8 character boundary (never inside a character), and returns `Truncated {kept, total}` when it cut. Every note text and every JSON serialization goes through it with `Caps::stream_bytes`; the transcript says "truncated: kept N of M bytes".
- `Budget` counts the bytes written to both files. The record that would pass `Caps::test_bytes` is replaced by one `capped` record; after that nothing more is written except the final `end` record, whose `dropped` counts the records not written. The transcript renders the `capped` record as `log capped at <N> bytes: the records after this one are not written`. The ring of summaries keeps working. Decided while writing this bead: stop writing entirely (rather than keep writing headers) so the bound is real.

### Modes and the live echo

- `parse_mode`: `None` or `Some("")` → `Files`; `Some("verbose")` → `Verbose`; anything else → an `Err` whose text is "OMADDONS_TEST_LOG=<value> is not a log mode: use `verbose`, or leave it unset". The process reads `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG` once (`OnceLock`); the first `TestLog` created with an invalid value panics with that message. Decided while writing this bead: a typo fails loudly.
- `Verbose`: each record's summary is also written straight to the stderr handle (`writeln!(std::io::stderr().lock(), "[tlog {suite}::{test} #{seq}] {summary}")`, write errors ignored), bypassing libtest's capture, so it streams live without `--nocapture` and stays attributable when tests run in parallel. The plan said "run with `--nocapture`"; decided while writing this bead: the direct write makes that unnecessary.

### The panic guard and failures

- `Drop for TestLog` always writes the `end` record (`outcome: "panicked"` when `std::thread::panicking()`, else `"passed"`). When panicking, it also prints with `eprintln!` (inside a function marked `#[allow(clippy::print_stderr, reason = "the guard's lines belong in libtest's captured output of the failing test, beside its panic message")]`):

  ```text
  test log: <absolute path of transcript.md>
  last 20 of 26 records:
    #6 note: note 06
    …
    #25 note: note 25
  ```

  N counts the records written before `end`, the header included (here a header and 25 notes); `end` is never part of the ring. `eprintln!` output is captured by libtest and printed in the failing test's `---- <test> stdout ----` section right after the panic message. Decided while writing this bead: captured for the guard (it belongs beside the failure), direct for the echo (it must stream).
- The guard never panics: a panic while unwinding aborts the whole test binary. Every write in `Drop` ignores errors.
- A write failure of the log (a full disk) prints one `test log: cannot write <file>: <error>` line (`eprintln!`, same allow) and disables that log's writes; it never fails the test, because the log is a diagnostic.
- `log.assert_eq(label, actual, expected)` writes an `assert` record with both values (scrubbed, rewritten, capped) and, when they differ, a `failure` record, then panics with `tlog: assert "<label>" in step "<step>": expected <expected:?>, got <actual:?>` and `  transcript: <absolute path>`. The absolute path is printed on the terminal, never written into a log file.

### The module doc ("Conventions", written once here and in README by part 3)

`tests/common/tlog.rs`'s `//!` doc explains what the log writes and where, how a failure points at it, the two modes, the privacy rules, and these conventions:

1. Every M4 integration or end-to-end test that runs more than one command logs through `TestLog`, and its crate carries a `//! e2e suite: <purpose>` line (part 3 adds the runner and the check).
2. Each phase of a scenario is a `log.step`.
3. Every state assertion goes through `log.tree`/`log.assert_unchanged`/`log.diff` (part 2), or `log.assert_eq`, or logs the values it compares with `log.json` before asserting.
4. Unit tests are table-driven, with a name per case and assertion messages that name the case and show the input and the output; they do not use `TestLog`.
5. An older suite adopts the log when a leaf rewrites it.
6. Real-machine tests and live probes never use `TestLog`.
7. Bead comments quote the log root as `target/tmp/test-logs`, never an absolute path.

Part 2 extends the doc with the run and tree API.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `tests/common/tlog.rs` exists with the constants, `log_root`, `Mode`, `parse_mode`, `Caps`, `TestLog::{new, with_caps, from_location, dir, steps_path, transcript_path, step, note, json, secret, assert_eq}`, `Drop`, the `tlog!` macro re-exported as `common::tlog::tlog`, and the pure helpers named above; `tests/common/mod.rs` declares it.
- [ ] A `TestLog` writes `<CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR>/test-logs/<suite>/<test>/steps.jsonl` (header first, one compact record per line, `kind` then `seq`, `end` last) and `transcript.md` (the same records, readable); a rerun replaces the directory.
- [ ] `tlog!()` in `fn x` of `mod m` names the directory `<suite>/m.x`.
- [ ] Note texts and JSON values are capped at `STREAM_CAP_BYTES` with `truncated: {kept, total}`; the test budget writes one `capped` record and counts `dropped` in `end`.
- [ ] Secret values given to `log.secret` (8 bytes or more) never appear in either file; `TestEnv` roots, `CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR` and `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR` are rewritten to their placeholders.
- [ ] A panicking test's guard prints `test log: <path>` and the last 20 summaries through `eprintln!`, and the `end` record says `panicked`; `OMADDONS_TEST_LOG=verbose` echoes each summary with a direct stderr write; an unknown value panics naming `verbose`. (Proved end to end in child processes by part 4; here by the unit tests of `parse_mode` and by reading the code.)
- [ ] The unit tests of the Test Plan pass; every crate that compiles `tests/common/` stays warning-free under `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`.
- [ ] No other file under `tests/` changes; no crate is added.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

In `tests/tlog_selftest.rs`, `mod core_units`. Table-driven with a `name` per case; each assertion message is `"{name}: input {input:?} gave {output:?}"`.

- `the_macro_names_the_suite_and_the_test`: `tlog!()` here → `dir()` ends with `tlog_selftest/core_units.the_macro_names_the_suite_and_the_test`.
- `an_oversized_json_value_is_truncated_and_says_so`: `with_caps(stream 64 B, test 64 KiB)`, a 1 KiB string value → the `json` record has `value: null`, a 64-byte `text`, `truncated: {kept: 64, total: …}`.
- `the_cap_writes_one_capped_record`: `with_caps(stream 1 KiB, test 4 KiB)`, 200 notes → exactly one `capped` record, both files together at most 4 KiB plus the `end` record, `end.dropped` equal to the notes not written.
- `a_registered_secret_is_scrubbed_from_notes`: `secret("tlogSelftestValue-0123")`, then a note containing it twice → neither file contains the value; the note says `<redacted>` twice.
- `assert_eq_failure_names_the_step_and_the_transcript`: `assert_eq("count", &2, &3)` under `std::panic::catch_unwind(AssertUnwindSafe(…))` → the payload contains `count`, the step label and `transcript:`; `steps.jsonl` has an `assert` record with `equal: false` and a `failure` record.

### Integration and end-to-end tests

None in this part. Part 4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1.4`) proves the guard's output, the live echo and the mode error in child processes, because they depend on per-process state and libtest's capture.

### Logging

Unit tests name each case and show the input and the output. The in-process tests write their subject logs under the suite directory `tlog_selftest_child` (never a real suite, so `argc e2e` never summarizes them) and print the subject transcript's path in every assertion message.

## Considerations

- **Cost.** The module compiles into 94 crates: keep it free of heavy generics and new dependencies. A passing test writes two small files and nothing else.
- **No behaviour change.** No existing test uses the module yet; adding `pub mod tlog;` must not add a warning in any crate.
- **Thread safety.** One `Mutex` around the writer state; the summary ring and the budget live there too. Keep the lock short (format the record outside it where possible).
- **What could go wrong.** `type_name_of_val`'s output format is not guaranteed by Rust; `the_macro_names_the_suite_and_the_test` catches a change, and `TestLog::new` with explicit names keeps working. A guard that panics would abort the test binary: every operation in `Drop` swallows its errors.
- **Hot spot.** `tests/common/mod.rs` also gains `pub mod` lines from other M4 leaves (`intent_home`, `realistic_home`, the doctor helpers, `plans::age_plan`): append in order and rebase.

## Dependencies

- Parent: T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, Structured test logs, and the `argc e2e` runner).
- Before it: nothing; this is the first part.
- After it: part 2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1.2`, commands and trees under the log), which adds runs, trees and cases to this `TestLog` and reuses its writer, redaction, paths and bounds. Parts 3 and 4 follow part 2.

title: Commands and trees under the log: `log.run`, `Ran`, `net.log` and failpoint capture, tree checks and cases
description:
Part 2 of 4 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1 (Structured test logs, and the `argc e2e` runner). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`) gives every M4 integration and end-to-end test one structured step log, so a scenario that fails at its fourteenth command can be diagnosed from the record of the thirteen before it. M4's new suites (capabilities, robot-docs, the skill, `apply` and plans, the doctor and its repair matrices, the safety harness, durability) run five to twenty commands against one synthetic home, crash children at failpoints, pause them to force races, and compare tree hashes; the slice demos (T2–T4) are built on the same log. The bead changes no product behaviour and adds no wire name.

Part 1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1.1`) built the log object (`TestLog`, `tlog!`, the two files `steps.jsonl` and `transcript.md`, redaction, path placeholders, bounds, modes, the live echo and the panic guard). This part makes it record what M4's scenarios actually do: run the real `omaddons` binary (in the foreground or the background, with extra variables, stdin, failpoints and a timeout) and capture everything about each run, synchronize with `pause` failpoints, hash trees and name the paths that differ, and give each case of a table-driven or parallel test its own sub-log. It is its own step because it is the part that touches the existing builders (`TestEnv`, `Home`, `Scene`, `Pause`, `trees`) and the binary, and it rests on part 1's settled format, privacy and bounds.

## Technical Approach

### Facts this part relies on (as of `c0ab5e9`)

- `TestEnv::command()` (`tests/common/env.rs:97-108`) returns an `assert_cmd::Command`, which cannot be spawned in the background or report the variables set on it. `TestEnv::apply_to(&mut std::process::Command)` (`:110-116`) applies exactly the same environment: `HOME`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME`, `XDG_CACHE_HOME`, `XDG_DATA_HOME` and `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT` inside the tempdir (`vars()`, `:118-130`), `TZ=UTC`, `OMADDONS_FS_CLONE=no`, `OMADDONS_FS_FREE_MB=65536` (`SETTINGS`, `:17-21`), and removal of `CI`, `NO_COLOR`, `TERM`, `XDG_DATA_DIRS`, `XDG_CONFIG_DIRS` and every other `OMADDONS_*` of the test process (`removed()`, `:133-146`).
- `Home` (`tests/common/home.rs:17-23`, fields `env`, `root`, `prefix`, `http`, `proc`). `Home::std_command(args, extra)` (`:254-266`) = `Command::new(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_omaddons"))` + `env.apply_to` + `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES` + `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT` when set + `extra` + args. `Home::exec_with` (`:209-217`) reports a signal death as code `-1`. `common::home::Run` (`:295-333`) is `{argv, code, stdout, stderr}` with `envelope()`, `expect()`, `context()`.
- `common::engine::Scene` (`tests/common/engine.rs:51-54`) holds `pub home: Home`.
- `common::pause::Pause` (`tests/common/pause.rs:13-48`): `env()` → `("OMADDONS_FAILPOINT_DIR", dir)`; `reached(name)` waits up to 30 s and asserts; `resume(name)`.
- Failpoints: `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS=<name>[=abort|=error|=sleep:<ms>|=panic|=pause][@N][,…]` (`src/fsx/failpoint.rs:3-12`); a pause waits at most 60 s (`:25`); `abort` dies by `SIGABRT` (`:33-37`).
- `common::trees::tree_hash(dir)` (`tests/common/trees.rs:439-475`): SHA-256 over sorted relative paths, each entry's kind and permission bits (`mode & 0o7777`), file bytes (with length) and symlink targets, symlinks not followed; it panics on an unreadable directory. It returns only the digest. No test pins a literal value.
- `net.log` is `<XDG_STATE_HOME>/omaddons/net.log`, rotated above 10 MiB to `net.log.1` (`src/net/log.rs:1-6`, `src/state/paths.rs:353-360`); one JSON object per line (`NetLogEntry`, `src/net/log.rs:29-52`). `common::netlog::read_net_log(paths)` (`tests/common/netlog.rs:10-12`) parses it with the library.
- `std::process::Command::get_envs()` returns the variables explicitly set or removed (`None`) on the command, last value per key.
- `common::privacy::assert_private_all(stdout, stderr)` (`tests/common/privacy.rs:40-43`).

### Running the binary

```rust
pub trait Runner {
    fn test_env(&self) -> &TestEnv;
    fn command(&self, argv: &[String]) -> std::process::Command;
}
impl Runner for TestEnv { /* let mut c = Command::new(env!("CARGO_BIN_EXE_omaddons")); self.apply_to(&mut c); c.args(argv); c */ }
impl Runner for Home    { fn test_env(&self) -> &TestEnv { &self.env } /* command: self.std_command(argv, &[]) */ }
impl Runner for Scene   { /* delegates to self.home */ }
```

The plan says the log runs the binary "through `TestEnv::command()`". Decided while writing this bead: the `Runner` trait over `std::process::Command`, with the same environment, because background runs, timeouts and reading back the variables a scenario set need the standard type, and because scenarios with HTTP fixtures or a fake `/proc` already build their command with `Home::std_command`. Builders that later leaves add (`intent_home()`, `realistic_home()`) implement `Runner` when they wrap a `Home` or a `TestEnv`.

```rust
impl TestLog {
    pub fn run<A: AsRef<str>>(&self, on: &impl Runner, argv: &[A]) -> Ran { self.cmd(on, argv).run() }
    pub fn cmd<A: AsRef<str>>(&self, on: &impl Runner, argv: &[A]) -> Cmd<'_>;
}
impl Cmd<'_> {
    pub fn env(self, key: &str, value: impl AsRef<OsStr>) -> Self;
    pub fn cwd(self, dir: &Path) -> Self;
    pub fn stdin(self, bytes: impl Into<Vec<u8>>) -> Self;
    pub fn failpoints(self, spec: &str) -> Self;   // sets OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS
    pub fn pause(self, pause: &Pause) -> Self;     // sets OMADDONS_FAILPOINT_DIR from pause.env()
    pub fn timeout(self, limit: Duration) -> Self; // default RUN_TIMEOUT (300 s)
    pub fn run(self) -> Ran;
    pub fn spawn(self) -> Running;
}
impl Running { pub fn pid(&self) -> u32; pub fn wait(self) -> Ran; }
```

- `argv` excludes the binary name and is used verbatim: nothing is appended (unlike `Home::run`, which adds `--json`), so the logged argv is exactly what ran. The record shows `["omaddons", …]`.
- The sequence number is taken when the run starts, after the `env` record of a first run on that `TestEnv` (below) has been written. `run()` = `spawn().wait()`.
- `spawn`: `Runner::command(argv)`, then the `Cmd`'s variables, working directory and stdin (`Stdio::piped()` when given, written then closed by a writer thread; else `Stdio::null()`, as `Command::output()` does), stdout and stderr piped, each read to the end by its own thread into a `Vec<u8>`.
- `wait`: poll `try_wait` every 5 ms until the child exits or the deadline passes. At the deadline: `kill`, `wait`, join the readers, write the record with `timed_out: true`, and panic: `tlog: run #<seq> in step "<step>" timed out after <ms> ms and was killed` plus the argv and the transcript path. A hung child therefore fails its test with a log instead of hanging the gate.
- The first run on a `TestEnv` writes an `env` record: `{"kind":"env","seq":n,"name":"<root>","vars":{…}}` with that environment's base variables (the six paths and three settings, rewritten), and adds the root to the log's path placeholders (part 1's `Relativizer`: `<root>`, `<root2>`, … in order of first use). The root is also what `log.tree` accepts (below).

### The `run` record

| Field | Content |
|---|---|
| `seq`, `step`, `env` | the number, the current phase label, the `TestEnv`'s placeholder |
| `argv` | `["omaddons", …]`, rewritten, scrubbed |
| `cwd` | the directory set, else the inherited one (the test process runs in the package root, so usually `<repo>`) |
| `overrides` | from `get_envs()`: every variable set whose value differs from the `env` record's base value or that the base lacks; removals are not listed; a secret-named variable (part 1's `is_secret_name`) as `"<redacted>"`; values rewritten |
| `failpoints` | `{"spec": …, "pause_dir": …}` from `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS` and `OMADDONS_FAILPOINT_DIR` when either is set, else `null` |
| `stdin_bytes` | the length of the stdin given, else `null`; its content is never recorded (it may be a credential) |
| `background` | whether `spawn()` was called by the test (rather than through `run()`) |
| `started_at`, `elapsed_ms` | RFC 3339 UTC; duration |
| `exit`, `signal`, `timed_out` | `status.code()` or `-1`; `ExitStatusExt::signal()`; the timeout flag |
| `stdout` | `{"form":"envelope","value":…}` when stdout is exactly one line (trailing newline allowed) that parses as a JSON object; `{"form":"text","text":…}` otherwise; `{"form":"empty"}`; plus `bytes` and `truncated` |
| `stderr` | `{"lines":[…]}`: each line parsed as JSON when it parses, else the raw string, in order; plus `bytes` and `truncated` |
| `net_log` | `{"added":[…],"rotated":bool}` |
| `scrubbed` | the names of the secret-named variables whose values were scrubbed from this record |

- Before the record is built, each secret-named variable's value is added to part 1's `Scrubber` (values under `SCRUB_MIN_LEN` stay redacted in `overrides` but are not scrubbed from text). The rewrite and the scrub apply to the raw text before parsing (a path replaced by a placeholder keeps JSON valid).
- Each stream is cut at `Caps::stream_bytes` on a character boundary (part 1's `cap_text`); a truncated stdout is recorded as `form: "text"` with the kept prefix.
- `net_log` (decided while writing this bead: read raw, so a malformed line never breaks the log and nothing depends on `NetLogEntry`'s shape): read the lines of `<state>/omaddons/net.log.1` then `net.log` (missing files are empty) before spawning and after the exit; when the before-lines are a prefix of the after-lines, the rest is what the run added; otherwise the log rotated, and every line of the current `net.log` is recorded with `rotated: true`. Each line parsed as JSON, else kept as a string. Two runs in parallel on one home see each other's lines; the module doc says so.
- `Ran.run` (a `common::home::Run`) holds the raw output (absolute paths, nothing scrubbed): assertions check what the binary printed; only the log is rewritten.

### `Ran`

```rust
pub struct Ran {
    pub run: Run, pub seq: u64, pub step: String, pub elapsed_ms: u64,
    pub signal: Option<i32>, pub timed_out: bool,
    /* transcript path; envelope parsed once (Option<Value>); a Weak handle to the log for failure records */
}
pub struct Suggested { pub action: String, pub command: String, pub argv: Vec<String>, pub destructive: bool }
```

| Method | Asserts or returns |
|---|---|
| `ok()` | exit 0, and `envelope.ok == true` when stdout is an envelope |
| `exit(n)` | exit `n` |
| `fails(n, code)` | exit `n` and `error.code == code` |
| `aborted()` | killed by `SIGABRT` (an `abort` failpoint) |
| `envelope()` | stdout is exactly one JSON object line (else a failure naming the step) |
| `data()` | `envelope()["data"]`, which must exist |
| `error_code()` | `envelope()["error"]["code"]` as `Option<&str>` |
| `warnings()` | the codes of `envelope()["warnings"]`, in order |
| `commands()` | `envelope()["commands"]` as `Vec<Suggested>` |
| `events()` | every stderr line, each of which must parse as JSON |
| `assert_private()` | `common::privacy::assert_private_all(stdout, stderr)`, with the step in the message |
| `stdout()`, `stderr()` | the raw text |

The assertion methods return `&Self` for chaining within one statement (`log.run(&home, &["status", "--json"]).ok();`); a test that keeps the data binds the `Ran` first (`let ran = log.run(…); let data = ran.ok().data();`), because a reference into a temporary `Ran` does not outlive the statement. A failing one appends a `failure` record (when the log still exists) and panics with:

```text
tlog: run #7 in step "apply the stored plan": expected exit 0, got 4
  error: game_running: the retail client is running
  argv: omaddons apply 01M6T… --json
  transcript: <absolute path of transcript.md>
```

(`error:` only when stdout is an envelope with an `error`; before the first `log.step`, `in step "…"` reads `before any step`). A run killed by a signal reads `expected exit 0, killed by signal 6`; `aborted()` on a run that exited reads `expected to be killed by SIGABRT, got exit 0`; a timed-out run has already panicked in `wait`. `Ran.run` is a `common::home::Run` so every existing helper that takes `&Run` (`common::engine::lock_held_ms`, …) works on `&ran.run`. Decided while writing this bead: `fails`, `aborted`, `events`, `assert_private`, `stdout` and `stderr` beyond the plan's `ok`, `exit`, `envelope`, `data`, `error_code`, `warnings`, `commands`.

### Pauses

```rust
impl TestLog {
    pub fn reached(&self, pause: &Pause, name: &str); // record "waiting", Pause::reached(name), record "reached" with waited_ms
    pub fn resume(&self, pause: &Pause, name: &str);  // Pause::resume(name), record "resumed"
}
```

Record: `{"kind":"pause","seq":n,"step":…,"action":"waiting"|"reached"|"resumed","name":…,"dir":<rewritten>,"waited_ms":…|null}`. When `Pause::reached` times out, its own assertion panics; the `waiting` record already shows what the test was waiting for.

### Trees

In `tests/common/trees.rs`, beside `tree_hash`, which does not change:

```rust
pub enum EntryKind { File, Dir, Symlink }
pub struct Entry { pub kind: EntryKind, pub mode: u32, pub len: u64, pub sha256: Option<String>, pub target: Option<String> }
pub fn tree_entries(dir: &Path) -> BTreeMap<String, Entry>; // the same walk, kinds and `mode & 0o7777` as tree_hash
pub struct TreeDiff { pub added: Vec<String>, pub removed: Vec<String>, pub changed: Vec<(String, String)>, pub total: usize }
pub fn tree_diff(before: &BTreeMap<String, Entry>, after: &BTreeMap<String, Entry>) -> TreeDiff;
impl TreeDiff { pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool; pub fn first(&self, n: usize) -> Vec<String>; }
```

- Keys are the relative paths as `tree_hash` encodes them (`strip_prefix(dir)`, displayed). `sha256` is set for files, `target` for symlinks.
- `changed`'s second element names what changed, joined with `+` in this order: `kind`, `content` (length or digest), `target`, `mode`. `first(n)` merges the three lists in path order, as `+ <path>`, `- <path>`, `~ <path> (<what>)`.
- Decided while writing this bead: a second walk beside `tree_hash` rather than changing it, so no existing suite's comparison moves. The plan said to reuse `tree_hash`, which covers modes and symlink targets but cannot name a path.

In `tests/common/tlog.rs`:

```rust
impl TestLog {
    pub fn tree(&self, label: &str, root: &Path) -> Option<String>;
    pub fn assert_unchanged(&self, label: &str, root: &Path);
    pub fn diff(&self, label: &str, root: &Path) -> TreeDiff;
}
```

- **Allowed roots.** Each refuses (panics, before reading anything) a root that is not under a `TestEnv` root this log has seen, `CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR` or `std::env::temp_dir()`: `tlog: <root> is outside this test's synthetic directories; the test log never reads the developer's files`. A log sees a `TestEnv` root at its first run there, or through `pub fn env(&self, on: &impl Runner)`, which writes the `env` record without running anything (for a test that hashes a tree before its first command). Decided while writing this bead: the rule (the plan states "it never reads the developer's real `HOME`" without a mechanism) and `log.env`.
- `tree`: `tree_hash(root)` (the authoritative value) and `tree_entries(root)` (kept in memory under the label, replacing an earlier one of the same label); records `{"kind":"tree","seq":n,"step":…,"label":…,"root":<rewritten>,"exists":bool,"hash":…|null,"entries":n}`. A missing root records `exists: false`, `hash: null`, `entries: 0` and returns `None`.
- `assert_unchanged`: re-reads the tree and compares with the label's last `tree` (a label never recorded is a panic naming it); records `{"kind":"tree_check",…,"check":"unchanged","expected":…,"actual":…,"equal":bool,"diff":null|{"total":n,"first":[…]}}` with the first `DIFF_PATHS_SHOWN` (20) paths, and on a difference panics with those paths, the step and the transcript path.
- `diff`: the same record with `"check":"diff"`, never panics, returns the `TreeDiff` so the test can assert what changed ("only `Interface/AddOns/Foo` changed").
- Cost: each call walks and hashes the tree twice; the realistic home (5,040 files) takes well under a second in a debug build. No tree is hashed unless the test asks.

### Cases

```rust
impl TestLog { pub fn case(&self, name: &str) -> TestLog; }
```

- Creates `<test dir>/cases/<sanitized name>/` with its own `steps.jsonl` and `transcript.md` (replacing an earlier one), its own header (`parent: "<suite>/<test>"`), its own guard and summary ring, and the parent's secrets and path placeholders (copied at creation). It shares the parent's byte budget (the `Arc`'d `Budget` of part 1), so a test and all its cases together stay within `TEST_CAP_BYTES`.
- The parent writes `{"kind":"case","seq":n,"step":…,"name":…,"dir":"cases/<name>"}`.
- The safety harness (F9) and other parallel tests create one case per (fixer, failpoint) or per row, possibly from scoped threads; a failing case's guard points at its own transcript.

### Transcript rendering of these records

````text
### #3 run `omaddons install gh:o/foo -t retail --json` → exit 0 (312 ms)

- cwd `<repo>` · overrides OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES=<root>/http · failpoints none · stdin none · net.log +3

stdout (envelope):

```json
{ …pretty… }
```

stderr (2 lines):

```json
{"event":"progress",…}
{"event":"progress",…}
```

net.log (+3):

```json
{"time":"…","method":"GET","host":"github.com","path":"/o/foo/releases/latest","status":302,…,"purpose":"release-latest",…}
…
```

### #4 pause `engine.plan.done`: reached after 41 ms

### #5 tree `retail` = 3f2a9c1d… (41 entries)

### #6 tree check `retail`: changed (3 paths)

- `~ Interface/AddOns/Foo/Foo.toc (content)`
- `+ Interface/AddOns/Foo/new.lua`
- `- WTF/Config.wtf`
````

One-line summaries for the ring and the echo: `run omaddons install … → exit 0 (312 ms)`, `pause engine.plan.done: reached (41 ms)`, `tree retail: 3f2a9c1d (41 entries)`, `tree check retail: changed, 3 paths`, `case <name>`.

### The module doc

Extend part 1's doc with the run, pause, tree and case API, the `Runner` implementations, the record fields, and the note that parallel runs on one home see each other's `net.log` lines.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `Runner` is implemented for `TestEnv`, `Home` and `Scene`, and `TestLog::{run, cmd, env, reached, resume, tree, assert_unchanged, diff, case}`, `Cmd::{env, cwd, stdin, failpoints, pause, timeout, run, spawn}`, `Running::{pid, wait}`, `Ran` with the methods above and `Suggested` exist in `tests/common/tlog.rs`.
- [ ] A run record carries every field of the table above: `seq`, `step`, `env`, `argv`, `cwd`, `overrides` (base excluded, secrets redacted), `failpoints`, `stdin_bytes`, `background`, `started_at`, `elapsed_ms`, `exit`, `signal`, `timed_out`, `stdout` (envelope parsed, else text), `stderr` (each line parsed), `net_log.added` and `scrubbed`.
- [ ] A run past its timeout is killed, recorded with `timed_out: true`, and panics naming the step.
- [ ] A failing `Ran` assertion writes a `failure` record and panics with the step, the expected and actual exit, the error code and message (when there is an envelope), the argv and the transcript path.
- [ ] `tests/common/trees.rs` has `tree_entries`, `Entry`, `EntryKind`, `TreeDiff` and `tree_diff`; `tree_hash` is byte-for-byte unchanged.
- [ ] `log.tree` records `tree_hash` and the entry count; `log.assert_unchanged` and `log.diff` record and report the first 20 differing paths with what changed; all three refuse a root outside the test's synthetic directories before reading it.
- [ ] `log.case` writes its own two files under `cases/<name>/`, a `case` record in the parent, and counts against the parent's budget.
- [ ] The unit tests of the Test Plan pass; the crates that compile `tests/common/` stay warning-free under clippy with `-D warnings`.
- [ ] No existing test or builder changes behaviour (only additions to `tests/common/trees.rs` and `tests/common/tlog.rs`); no crate is added.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

In `tests/tlog_selftest.rs`, `mod run_units`. Table-driven with a `name` per case; each assertion message is `"{name}: input {input:?} gave {output:?}"`. The classification helpers are `pub` in `tests/common/tlog.rs` (`classify_stdout`, `parse_stderr`, `net_log_added`, `overrides`).

| Test | Cases (name: input → expected) |
|---|---|
| `stdout_is_classified` | `envelope`: `{"ok":true}\n` → envelope; `two_lines`: a JSON line then `x` → text; `plain`: `omaddons 0.1.0\n` → text; `empty`: `` → empty; `array`: `[1]` → text; `no_newline`: `{"ok":false}` → envelope |
| `stderr_lines_parse_one_by_one` | `mixed`: an event line, a text line, an event line → JSON, string, JSON in order; `empty`: `` → no lines; `blank_line`: an empty line between events → kept as `""` |
| `net_log_additions_are_the_new_suffix` | `appended`: before `[a]`, after `[a, b, c]` → `[b, c]`, `rotated: false`; `first_run`: no file before → every line; `nothing`: equal → `[]`; `rotation_kept`: before `.1` empty and current `[a, b]`, after `.1=[a, b]` and current `[c]` (concatenations `[a, b]` and `[a, b, c]`) → `[c]`, `rotated: false`; `rotation_dropped`: before `.1=[x]` and current `[y]`, after `.1=[y]` and current `[z]` (`[x, y]` is no prefix of `[y, z]`) → the current file's `[z]`, `rotated: true`; `garbage`: an unparsable line → kept as a string |
| `overrides_exclude_the_base_and_redact_secrets` | `base_only`: the base variables unchanged → none; `proc_root_changed`: `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT` set by `Home` to another dir → present, rewritten; `fixtures`: `OMADDONS_HTTP_FIXTURES` → present; `token`: `OMADDONS_GITHUB_TOKEN` → `"<redacted>"`; `removed`: an `env_remove` → absent |
| `tree_entries_cover_kind_mode_content_and_target` | a file, a directory, a symlink and a `0o600` file → their kinds, modes, lengths, digests and target |
| `tree_diff_names_what_changed` | `added`: a new file → `+`; `removed`: → `-`; `same_size_edit`: one byte flipped → `~ (content)`; `chmod`: `0o644` → `0o600` → `~ (mode)`; `file_to_dir`: → `~ (kind)`; `retarget`: a symlink's target changed → `~ (target)`; `empty_dir`: an empty directory added → `+`; `many`: 25 files changed → `total: 25`, `first(20)` the first 20 in path order |
| `tree_hash_and_tree_entries_agree` | for each `tree_diff_names_what_changed` case, `tree_hash` before and after differ exactly when `tree_diff` is not empty |
| `tree_roots_outside_the_test_are_refused` | `env_root`: a path under a registered env root → allowed; `target_tmp`: under `CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR` → allowed; `repo`: `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR/src` → refused (the check runs before any read) |

### Integration and end-to-end tests

None in this part: part 4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1.4`) runs the real binary through every path above (envelopes, `net.log`, pauses, aborts, timeouts, redaction, truncation, trees, cases, assertion messages).

### Logging

Unit tests name each case and show the input and the output. Tree tests build their trees under a `TestEnv` root and print `common::trees::listing(dir)` in their failure messages.

## Considerations

- **Reading back the environment.** `get_envs()` gives every variable the command set, including `TestEnv`'s base; the `env` record holds the base once, and `overrides` lists only differences, so a record stays short and a scenario's own changes stand out.
- **Background runs.** The record of a spawned run is written when it is waited for, so `steps.jsonl` is in completion order while `seq` is in start order; the transcript shows `#seq`, which is what the interleaving needs. A `Running` dropped without `wait` kills its child and writes the record with a `failure` note, so no child outlives its test.
- **Cost.** Each run reads `net.log` twice (small in tests) and spawns two reader threads; no fsync, no tree hashing unless asked. The safety harness (F9) runs hundreds of children against a 60 s gate target; if this shows up there, it is a defect filed `discovered-from` T1 and fixed here.
- **Privacy.** Only synthetic homes: `log.run` always applies a `TestEnv`'s environment, and tree roots are confined. Secret-named variables are redacted and their values scrubbed; stdin is recorded as a length only.
- **Hot spots.** `tests/common/trees.rs` is shared by many suites: additions only, below `tree_hash`. `tests/common/home.rs` and `engine.rs` do not change (the `Runner` impls live in `tlog.rs`).

## Dependencies

- Parent: T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, Structured test logs, and the `argc e2e` runner).
- Before it: part 1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1.1`, the test log core), whose writer, record format, `Scrubber`, `Relativizer`, `cap_text` and `Budget` this part uses.
- After it: part 3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1.3`, the `argc e2e` runner and README), which documents this API, and part 4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1.4`, the self-test scenarios), which proves it over the real binary. Both wait only for this part.
