title: Slice 3 end to end: diagnose and repair
description:
## How to work this bead

This bead is worked through its 4 subtasks, listed below in work order. Claim a subtask, not this bead (`br ready --parent omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4` lists the ready ones). The agent that closes the last open subtask then verifies every acceptance criterion of this bead (they are the leaf's, not any one subtask's), runs and records the slice demo as Technical Approach §9 says, and closes this bead with `br close omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4 --reason "done: <evidence> · found: <ids>"`. Until this bead is closed, every bead it blocks stays blocked.

1. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4.1 E2E: the slice-3 suite, and every stuck state named on one home: the crate, its shared support module with its unit tests, and the first demo item (the eight stuck states planted together, named alike by `status` and `doctor`).
2. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4.2 E2E: a set-aside undone, a set-aside whose undo a later install refuses, and a bound gc: demo items 2, 3 and 5.
3. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4.3 E2E: a stuck repair fences only its own resources, and the Issues view's credential repair undone by Undo last: demo items 4 and 6, and the by-name check of the three QML scenarios.
4. omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4.4 E2E: the harness at every primitive boundary, and the fsync counts table: demo items 7 and 8.

Subtasks 2, 3 and 4 each wait only for subtask 1 and can be worked in parallel: each adds its own module files under `tests/e2e_slice3/` and one `mod` line per file to `tests/e2e_slice3.rs`, so a rebase resolves any overlap.

A demo item that fails is a defect in the leaf that owns the behaviour, never something to work around in this suite: reopen that leaf, or file a bug `--deps discovered-from:omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4` naming the failing step and its transcript, and make the bug a blocker of the subtask that found it.

## Background

### Why this bead exists

M4 (epic `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`) is delivered in four slices, each with an exit demo that shows the slice working end to end. Slice 3, "Diagnose and repair", is the doctor: its catalog of failure modes, its repairs, their undo, the fences a stuck repair puts up, `doctor gc`, the widget's Issues view and the durability work. Its exit demo, as the plan's §10.6 states it:

> `doctor` on a home with each §2.3 stuck state planted; a set-aside with `--force --yes`, then `doctor undo`; a set-aside, a later install, and the refused undo; a stuck repair that fences only its own resources; a bound gc; the credential fix from the Issues view (QML) and Undo last; the harness green at every primitive boundary; the fsync counts table.

M3 recorded its slice demos only at the end of the milestone, so the problems they would have shown surfaced late (the M3 checkpoint record's first lesson, plan §2.6). M4 makes each demo a test: this bead turns slice 3's demo into `tests/e2e_slice3.rs`, a suite of `TestLog` scenarios that run in every gate once the slice has landed, and records the demo on the milestone epic as a comment, "**Slice demo 3. Diagnose and repair**", whose evidence is the suite's test names and transcripts. It was not in the M4 plan: it was added when the plan was turned into beads (area T, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9`), at the owner's request that the beads include comprehensive end-to-end test scripts with detailed logging, so that after implementation every behaviour can be shown to work and every failure diagnosed from its log. It changes no product behaviour and adds no wire name.

"End-to-end test scripts" here means Rust integration tests that drive the real `omaddons` binary through a scenario on a synthetic home, never shell scripts. M4-D47 decided that for the doctor's fixtures (each failure mode's fixture is a Rust type in `tests/doctor/fixtures/<fm_id>.rs` with `corrupt`, `assert_healthy`, `subject` and a doc comment that is its README; rejected: `corrupt.sh`/`assert.sh` per failure mode, "a second test language, and shell scripts that must clean up after themselves", while the house rules ban `rm -rf` even in test scripts). This suite follows the same rule and reuses those fixtures.

The demo is the evidence for the slice's share of the M4 checkpoint. A demo that passes in every gate is a regression test of the slice's promises taken together: each owning leaf proves its own piece in its own suite; this suite proves that the pieces compose into what the demo states, on the same homes, in the order a user meets them.

### Milestone goals it serves

- **G-M4-4 Diagnosable and repairable:** "`omaddons doctor` names every broken state omaddons can detect … Every auto-fixable state is repaired by one consented command that backs up verbatim, never deletes, and is proven by a fixture that round-trips. A repair can be undone byte for byte as long as no later change overlaps what it touched; once one does, undo refuses before moving anything, and the kept bytes stay inspectable. The states README calls 'manual repair' today each get a name, an explanation and a guarded repair. `status` and `doctor` never disagree about what is wrong." Demo items 1 to 7 are this goal, end to end.
- **G-M4-6 No new risk to the engine's guarantees:** "every repair is a journaled transaction that recovers like any other … the doctor never writes `WTF/` … a build from before M4 never destroys what M4 wrote." Demo items 4, 7 and 8, and the quote of criterion 16's run.

And through them the vision's G7, "`doctor` follows the world-class doctor contract", and its thesis that omaddons stays the sole, safe, undoable authority over what it manages: the demo shows a stuck client unblocked without deleting a byte, the repair undone, and the undo refused once it would no longer be safe.

### Checkpoint criteria it pre-checks

The slice table lists criteria 8 (the doctor part), 9, 10, 11, 12, 13 and 16. This bead pre-checks them; H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`, the M4 checkpoint) still runs every criterion. Restated:

- **8 (doctor part):** "The Issues view runs an auto-fixable finding's repair with a preview. It never runs a set-aside, `doctor gc`, or any argv with `--force`: those rows show the explanation and the terminal command."
- **9, the safety harness, in every gate:** bare `doctor` changes nothing outside `<state>/doctor/` (tree hashes of `<state>`, `<cache>`, `<config>` and every client dir); every auto-fixer round-trips (corrupt, find, fix, healthy, `doctor undo`, subject byte-identical with modes and symlinks); a second fix takes 0 actions; a real `abort` at every repair-journal failpoint and every primitive boundary of every fixer is recovered by the next lock-taking command to the whole before or whole after state, never a mixture, with recovery itself crashed at every inverse and repeated three times, and every boundary actually fired; concurrent fixers serialize; detectors are repeatable; every write in a declared scope; `set(fixers) == set(fixtures with a fixer)`.
- **10, the doctor's surface:** among its items, `doctor health` prints one line whose first token is `ok`, `findings`, `unsafe` or `concurrency`; `doctor fix --dry-run` and a later `doctor fix --if-match <token>` in another process agree; `doctor gc --dry-run` returns the exact deletion set, the kept candidates with their pin reasons, the undos that would be lost, and a token that `doctor gc --if-match` honours.
- **11, stuck states are named and repairable:** every manual-repair state (`journal_too_new`, `journal_unreadable`, marker mismatch, a step in neither state, `unexpected_state`, `preservation_incomplete`, a journal with no readable target, and a restore journal waiting for the game) has a finding with a correct title in both `status` and `doctor`; the force-gated repairs suspend the journal set and unblock the client; while nothing overlapping has changed, `doctor undo` reactivates it byte-identical and recovery then behaves exactly as before; after an overlapping change (a later install on that client), `doctor undo` refuses with `undo_conflict` before moving anything and the set stays inspectable in quarantine.
- **12, `status` and `doctor` agree:** `status`'s issues come from the registry's `cached` and `quick` tiers, and for every fixture the issue ids `status` reports equal the doctor's findings of those tiers.
- **13, durability:** the number of fsyncs inside each commit window is pinned by a gate test for an install, an update, an undo, a whole restore and a repair.
- **16, older builds against M4 state:** `tests/compat_m3.rs` builds `c0ab5e9` with its recorded toolchain and runs it against homes holding M4's artifacts; it must never delete or overwrite anything M4 still needs. It is checkpoint-only (ignored, never a pre-accepted `SKIP`), so the demo quotes its last run (Technical Approach §8).

### The decisions that shape it

- **The slice demos are tests (area T, at filing; plan §10.6 amended).** The plan had the agent who closes a slice's last leaf run the demo and record it on the milestone epic in the `[x] <item>: <evidence>` style. For slices 1–3 that duty moved to T2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.2`, slice 1), T3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.3`, slice 2) and this bead (slice 3), whose demos are suites in the gate. H6 still checks that the three demo comments exist before it starts, and still records slice 4's demo itself, because slice 4 contains the tag.
- **M4-D47: fixtures are Rust, in `tests/doctor/`, and coverage is bidirectional.** This suite plants every state through the fixtures and planting helpers the catalog leaves wrote (`fixtures::all()`, `common::doctor::plant`), never through a second planter, so a fixture that drifts from what it claims fails here as well as in its own suite.
- **M4-D38: the stuck journal states get a guarded set-aside.** One fixer for rows 3–8 of the catalog suspends the journal set (journal file, in-flight lock, state snapshot half, client stage and snapshot halves), one `RenameNoReplace` per artifact into its own filesystem's quarantine root, journal last, nothing copied or deleted. It runs only with `--only <fm> --force --yes` and is never part of a default fix. Its suspension manifest (the target's generation, the marker's digest, the epochs of the resources the journal would recover) is recorded as `guards`; `doctor undo` reactivates the set only while every guard still holds, else `undo_conflict` with `details.reason: "changed_since_suspension"` and `details.changed`, moving nothing. Rejected there: an unconditional restore (it would activate stale instructions after later work), deleting the journal, guessing a direction.
- **M4-D62: fences.** A stuck, readable repair journal refuses only the mutations whose write sets overlap its protected resources; every other command, client and path keeps working. The refusal is the fencing journal's own stop error with `details.tx` and `details.resource`, and the fix `omaddons doctor explain <fm>`. Rejected: blocking the whole machine for any stuck repair.
- **M4-D36: `doctor gc` is a bound, dependency-aware retention plan.** `--before` makes runs eligible; the plan pins by reachability (`active_run`, `unfinished_journal`, `active_undo`, `recovery_dependency`, the last for a set-aside's quarantined set while its manifest is reachable), lists `undo_lost[]` and `may_hold_only_copy`, and binds: `--dry-run` returns a `precondition`, and `--if-match` refuses a changed deletion set with `plan_stale`, deleting nothing. Rejected: age-only deletion (it deletes recovery inputs).
- **M4-D44 and M4-D45: `doctor fix` binds across processes, and fixes serialize.** The dry run's token holds nothing run-specific (no run id, tx id or backup path), so a bound run in a new process matches it; under the lock the doctor re-plans and compares the token before the first recovery or repair mutation.
- **M4-D46: a repair is undone strictly, as a new repair transaction.** `omaddons undo` (and `doctor undo [<run>]`, which resolves to it) inverts the history line's primitives with their own predicates and guards; bare `doctor undo` selects the newest committed, not yet undone `fix` run, so it survives an intervening diagnose; undoing an undone run is a no-op with exit 0. The widget's Undo last may select a repair, previewed with `undo --dry-run` and applied through its stored plan.
- **M4-D40: the doctor exit dictionary** (`0 healthy`, `1 findings_present`, `2 fix_partial`, `3 fix_failed_rolled_back`, `4 refused_unsafe`, `5 concurrency_lost`, `6 online_required`, `64`, `66`, `73`, `74`); `plan_stale`, `undo_conflict` and `doctor_refused` are 4 there; a command outside the doctor tree keeps the general dictionary.
- **M4-D54: durability.** The action log is group-committed once per transaction, derived files are not fsynced, directory fsyncs are deferred to explicit barriers; `-v` prints `lock_held_ms` and `fsyncs` per commit window; `tests/engine_durability.rs` pins the counts per shape (install, update, undo, whole restore, repair), and "a change shows as a diff". The counts are regression evidence, never a reason for an unsafe boundary.
- **M4-D58: the M3 build is characterized against M4 state** by `tests/compat_m3.rs` (E9, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.9`, the M3 build against M4 state), checkpoint-only and never skipped.
- **M4-D42 and common rule 9: privacy.** Doctor evidence never holds file content, and no output names an account, realm or character; every scenario with a `WTF/` runs `--progress json` and asserts `assert_private_all` over stdout and stderr.

The full decision log is filed as comments on the milestone epic `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`; the restatements above are what this bead needs.

### Facts this bead relies on (as of `c0ab5e9`, verified while writing this bead)

- `tests/e2e_slice3.rs`, `tests/doctor/` and `tests/engine_durability.rs` do not exist yet; the blockers create the last two. `tests/common/` holds 28 builder modules (`tests/common/mod.rs:15-42`), with `#![allow(dead_code)]` and the unwrap and expect allowances for the whole tree (`:12-13`).
- `Home::new(products)` (`tests/common/home.rs:27`) builds one Battle.net root with the given product codes. The codes and their default target ids (`src/rules.rs:1050-1063`): `wow` → `retail` (`_retail_`, `WoW.exe`), `wow_classic` → `classic` (`_classic_`), `wow_classic_era` → `era` (`_classic_era_`), `wow_anniversary` → `anniversary` (`_anniversary_`), the last three running `WoWClassic.exe`.
- `Home.proc`, when set, is passed to every child as `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT` by `Home::std_command` (`home.rs:254-266`); `Home::client_running(folder, exe)` (`:175-187`) builds a fake `/proc` in which that client runs. Without it, `TestEnv` points `OMADDONS_PROC_ROOT` at an empty `<root>/no-proc` (`tests/common/env.rs:51`, `:118-130`), which lists no process (`src/discover/running.rs:313-319`): no client counts as running.
- **Recovery is machine-wide.** Every lock-taking command's `recover_all` (`src/engine/journal.rs:811-848`) re-attempts every leftover journal whose in-flight lock is free, on every target; a failure on another target only warns (`journal_pending`), and a journal with no readable target fails the caller. A `WTF/` journal with a step waits while its client runs or may run (`journal.rs:1037-1046`). So on a home holding several planted states, a stable stop (too new, unreadable, marker mismatch, step unrecognized, unexpected state) stays stopped however often recovery tries it, while a recoverable journal, a restore waiting for a game that is not running, or a resumable preservation is changed by the next lock-taking command anywhere. The order in which this suite plants states (Technical Approach §3.1) follows from that.
- Under `-v`, a commit's lock release is logged as the debug event `lock released: tx <tx>, lock_held_ms <ms>` (`src/app/mod.rs:306-313`), which `common::engine::lock_held_ms(&Run)` reads from stderr (`tests/common/engine.rs:516-527`). `fsx::sys::SyncCounts` counts fsyncs per thread (`src/fsx/sys.rs:27-46`). G3 (`omad-7ccp`, group commit and deferred directory fsyncs) adds the window's fsync count to that event and pins the counts.
- Failpoints are read by debug builds only; the crash suites are debug-only crates (`#![cfg(debug_assertions)]`, `tests/engine_crash.rs:24`).
- The gate (`argc gate`, `scripts/gate.sh`) runs `cargo test --locked` (`:32-33`) and the widget pipeline; the pipeline's QML step runs only when `omarchy/` changed or with `--all` (`:35-40`). `argc widget-test` (`Argcfile.sh:20-21`) runs `scripts/widget-test.sh --qml`, whose step 4 runs `qmltestrunner -input <plugin copy>/tests/qml`, so every `tst_*.qml` there (`scripts/widget-test.sh:60-68`). Seven QML files exist today: `tst_bar`, `tst_chooser`, `tst_panel`, `tst_service`, `tst_signals`, `tst_smoke`, `tst_views`.
- `common::trees::tree_hash(dir)` covers kinds, modes, file bytes and symlink targets (`tests/common/trees.rs:439-475`); `common::privacy::{PRIVATE, assert_private, assert_private_all}` (`tests/common/privacy.rs:19-43`); `common::pause::Pause` (`tests/common/pause.rs:13-48`); `common::archives::zip_text(entries) -> Vec<u8>` (`tests/common/archives.rs:26`); `common::checkpoint::skip` and its rule (a test that cannot run prints `SKIP` and fails unless `OMADDONS_ALLOW_SKIP` names it, `tests/common/checkpoint.rs:1-41`).
- README's `## Development` (`README.md:2600`) has a `### Tests` table (`:2619`) listing the suites.

**What the blockers deliver, which this suite calls** (named as their beads specify them; where one landed with another name or signature, call it as it landed and say so in the close comment; never re-implement it):

- T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, structured test logs): `tests/common/tlog.rs` (`tlog!()`, `log.step`, `log.note`, `log.json`, `log.secret`, `log.run(&runner, argv) -> Ran`, `log.cmd(..).env(..).stdin(..).failpoints(..).pause(..).run()/.spawn()`, `log.reached`/`log.resume`, `log.tree`/`log.assert_unchanged`/`log.diff`, `log.case`, `log.assert_eq`; `Ran::{ok, exit, fails, aborted, envelope, data, error_code, warnings, commands, events, assert_private, stdout, stderr}` and `Ran.run` a `common::home::Run`); the crate-doc marker `//! e2e suite: <purpose>` that `argc e2e [FILTER] [ARGS…]` uses; the log root `target/tmp/test-logs`.
- E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, the doctor runtime): `tests/doctor/mod.rs` (the `Fixture` trait, included by a test crate as `#[path = "doctor/mod.rs"] mod fixtures;`), `tests/doctor/fixtures/mod.rs` (`all()`), `tests/common/doctor.rs` (`check_envelope(stdout, stderr, code)`, `plant`), the doctor envelope (report keys at the top level: `run_id`, `run_dir`, `state`, `summary`, `findings[]`, `skipped[]`, `commands[]`), `doctor explain`.
- F1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1`, journal and lock detectors): the ten `fm-concurrency_primitives-…` rows and fixtures, and `plant::{journal_waits_for_game, journal_too_new, journal_unreadable, journal_unexpected_state, journal_step_unrecognized, journal_marker_mismatch, journal_unattributed, journal_preservation_incomplete, journals, copy_journal}`.
- F2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.2`, journal fixers): the set-aside and the delegation, and `tests/doctor/journal_sets.rs` (`Stuck`, `plant(row, env)`, `set_hashes`, `set_aside`, `preview`, `undo`, `quarantine_of`, `change_on`, `stuck_state`), written for this suite's reuse.
- F7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.7`): `fm-secrets-credential-file-mode`, its chmod fixer and its fixture.

### 2. Conventions every scenario follows

- **One `TestLog` per test** (`let log = tlog!();`), one `log.step` per phase, every command through `log.run`/`log.cmd` (so each argv, override, failpoint, exit, envelope, stderr event and `net.log` line is recorded), `--json --progress json` passed explicitly on every run whose envelope is read, and every doctor envelope checked with `common::doctor::check_envelope(stdout, stderr, code)`.
- **State assertions go through the log**: `log.tree` before and `log.assert_unchanged`/`log.diff` after, or `log.assert_eq`, or `log.json` of the compared values before asserting.
- **"Outside `<state>/doctor/`"** is the set of trees `support::Trees::outside_doctor(&home)` returns: each child of `<state>/omaddons` except `doctor`, plus `<config>`, `<cache>` and every client dir, each recorded under its own label.
- **Privacy:** every run passes `--progress json` and calls `Ran::assert_private()`; a scenario whose home has a `WTF/` also checks the text of the run's `report.json` with `common::privacy::assert_private`.
- **Planted transactions are found by difference:** a planting helper's transaction is the entry `plant::journals(&home)` gains across the call (`support::planted(before, after)`), never a position in the list.
- **Frozen time** (`OMADDONS_NOW`, RFC 3339) only where expiry or age matters (the gc demo); `TZ=UTC` comes from `TestEnv`.
- **Helpers are called, not copied.** Where a blocker's helper is missing a parameter this suite needs (a target, leaving `home.proc` alone), extend it additively in the subtask's commit, run its owner's suite again, and list the change in the close comment.

## Considerations

- **It owns no feature code.** A demo item that fails is a defect in the leaf that owns the behaviour; fix it there and file it `discovered-from` this bead (How to work this bead). Weakening an assertion here would make the demo lie.
- **Fragility of the composed home** (item 1). Eight states on one home depend on recovery's machine-wide reach and on where each failpoint sits. The planting order is derived from the code (Background, facts), and each step re-runs `doctor` so a disturbance fails at the step that caused it, with both journal lists logged. If a later engine change makes two states incompatible on one home, keep the eight states and move the conflicting one to its own client; never drop one.
- **Risks (plan §11.4), as they meet this suite:** #1 (a recovery bug in the repair journal): the fence and harness items exercise real crashed repairs; #3 (doctor false positives): every finding outside the planted rows is logged and quoted, and must agree with `status`; #8 (durability weakened invisibly): item 8 re-reads the pinned counts, while the ordering argument stays the evidence of G3 (`omad-7ccp`); #9 (the M3 build destroys M4 artifacts): criterion 16's quote; #14 (a large milestone): the slice demo shows progress as it lands; #21 (fences scoped wrong): item 4 checks both sides, refused overlap and unrelated work proceeding; #23 (guarded reactivation refuses more than expected): item 3 shows the refusal naming what changed and the set kept.
- **Hot spots** (plan §10.5 and the blockers' notes): `tests/common/mod.rs` and `tests/common/doctor.rs` (append only, rebase); `tests/doctor/journal_sets.rs` and `tests/doctor/harness/crash.rs` (owned by F2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.2`, and F9, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`; additive or a pure refactor); `tests/engine_durability.rs` (G3's; a pure move of its table); README's Tests table (one row; H4, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`, the README final pass, reconciles counts).
- **Why size M, four subtasks:** about 1,200 lines of tests in four separable commits; each passes the gate alone, and three can be worked in parallel.
- **Run time.** Roughly 200 debug-build runs, most of them in the harness demo's crash cases and the stuck home's plantings, spread over parallel tests. The target is under 60 s on the development machine; each test logs its wall time.
- **Privacy.** Synthetic homes only; the fake account, realm and character names in every `WTF/`; canaries redacted from the logs; the demo comment carries no absolute path.
- **Compatibility.** No product behaviour, wire name or state file changes; nothing here can affect an older build.
- **Decided defaults, collected** (each marked where it is made): the eight states of criterion 11 on one four-client home and their planting order; a `doctor` confirmation after each planting; the real crashed `doctor fix` for the fence; bare `doctor undo` after a diagnose, then `already_undone`; the gc home with one invalidated and one reactivatable set-aside and a 40-day clock; the `#[path]` module layout and the debug-only crate; QML by name in the gate and by `argc widget-test` at close; one fixer crashed here plus the by-name harness check; the shared fsync table; the compat quote rule; the demo recorded by the last subtask's closer; the README row; the 60 s target.

comments.text:
**Planning rationale (M4 plan, 2026-10-24).**

**Why this bead.** Slice 3 is the doctor: twenty-five leaves (E1–E12, E14, F1–F10, G2, G3) that each prove their own piece in their own suite. Nothing yet proves that the pieces compose into what the slice promises: a home with every stuck state named alike by `status` and `doctor`; a client unblocked by a consented set-aside and restored byte-identical by `doctor undo`; that undo refused, moving nothing, once a later install made it unsafe; a stuck repair that blocks only what it touched; a gc bound to its preview that keeps what an undo still needs; the widget's credential repair undone by Undo last; the harness green at every boundary; the durability counts pinned. M3 recorded its slice demos only at the end of the milestone, and their problems surfaced late. This bead makes slice 3's demo a suite in the gate, `tests/e2e_slice3.rs`, and records it on the milestone epic as "**Slice demo 3. Diagnose and repair**", with test names, transcripts and the commit as evidence. It was added at bead filing (area T), at the owner's request for comprehensive end-to-end tests with detailed logging; it changes no product behaviour and adds no wire name.

**Decisions applied.**
- **Area T, at filing (amending §10.6):** the demos of slices 1–3 are tests owned by T2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.2`), T3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.3`) and this bead, not a duty of whoever closes a slice's last leaf; H6 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.6`) checks the three demo comments exist and still records slice 4's.
- **M4-D47:** every state is planted through the catalog leaves' own Rust fixtures and planting helpers, never a second planter, never shell. Rejected there: `corrupt.sh`/`assert.sh`.
- **M4-D38:** the set-aside runs only with `--only <fm> --force --yes`, suspends the whole journal set, and is reactivated only while its guards hold (`changed_since_suspension` otherwise). Rejected there: unconditional restore.
- **M4-D62:** a stuck readable repair refuses only overlapping writes; everything else proceeds. Rejected there: blocking the machine.
- **M4-D36:** gc is a bound retention plan with reachability pins. Rejected there: age-only deletion.
- **M4-D44, M4-D45, M4-D46:** doctor previews bind across processes; fixes serialize and re-plan under the lock; repair undo is strict, `doctor undo` selects the newest committed fix run and is idempotent.
- **M4-D40:** the doctor exit dictionary (`undo_conflict`, `plan_stale` and `doctor_refused` are 4 there).
- **M4-D54 and M4-D58:** the fsync counts are pinned per window; the M3 build's characterization is checkpoint-only and never skipped, so the demo quotes its run.
- **M4-D42 and common rule 9:** no evidence holds file content, and no output names an account, realm or character.

**Alternatives rejected here.**
- One home per stuck state: F1's suite already does that; the demo says "a home", and a home with every stuck state at once is the case no per-fixture suite covers. The planting order is derived from recovery's machine-wide reach (`recover_all` re-attempts every target's journals), and a `doctor` after each planting step catches any disturbance where it happens.
- E14's synthetic crashed child for the fence: the real `doctor fix`, crashed after its chmod, makes the demo end to end.
- Re-running the whole safety harness inside this suite: it would double the gate cost of F9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`) for no new evidence. One fixer (the demo's own) is crashed at every boundary through F9's routine, a by-name check keeps the full harness from being dropped or ignored, and its run is quoted.
- Copying G3's pinned counts into this suite: the table is read from one shared place, so a re-pin cannot leave two copies disagreeing.
- Recording the QML items from an ordinary gate run: its QML step runs only when `omarchy/` changed; the names are checked in every gate and the scenarios' passing is quoted from `argc widget-test`, which always runs them.
- A separate subtask for recording the demo: it has no code commit; the agent closing the last subtask records it.

**Risks and how they are watched.**
- The composed home is fragile against engine changes (recovery's reach, failpoint placement): per-step confirmation with both journal lists logged; a conflicting state moves to its own client rather than being dropped.
- A demo item fails: it is a defect in the owning leaf, fixed there and filed `discovered-from` this bead; this suite never weakens an assertion.
- Doctor false positives (plan risk #3): every finding outside the planted rows is logged, quoted and must agree with `status`.
- Run time: about 200 debug-build runs over parallel tests, a 60 s target, wall time logged per test.
- A demo comment leaking a path: the comment uses placeholders and the repo-relative log root only.

**What it unblocks, and why it waits.** H4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.4`), the README final pass, which matches README's test counts and descriptions to the code; it waits for the three slice demos so that both include these suites (an edge chosen so the plan's critical path, 25 units, does not grow). This bead waits for T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`), because its scenarios are `TestLog` scenarios, and for every slice-3 leaf, because a demo of a slice that has not landed would prove nothing.

**How it serves the milestone's goals.** G-M4-4 (diagnosable and repairable) end to end: stuck states named, repaired with consent, undone, refused when unsafe, `status` and `doctor` agreeing. G-M4-6 (no new risk to the engine's guarantees): real crashed repairs recovered or fenced, the harness at every boundary, the fsync counts, the M3 build's characterization quoted. Through them the vision's G7 (the doctor contract) and its thesis: omaddons stays the sole, safe, undoable authority over what it manages. It pre-checks checkpoint criteria 8 (doctor), 9, 10, 11, 12, 13 and 16.

**Confidence.** Medium-high. The suite owns no protocol and calls only helpers its blockers deliver; the risk is in composing eight stuck states on one home, which the per-step confirmation turns from a silent failure into a diagnosed one.

description:
Part 2 of 4 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4 (Slice 3 end to end: diagnose and repair). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

**The leaf.** T4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4`) turns the exit demo of M4's slice 3, "Diagnose and repair", into `tests/e2e_slice3.rs`, a suite of `TestLog` scenarios in the gate, and records it on the milestone epic (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`) as "**Slice demo 3. Diagnose and repair**". It owns no feature code and adds no wire name; it drives the real binary on synthetic homes through the helpers the slice's leaves wrote, and a demo item that fails is a defect in the leaf that owns the behaviour, fixed there and filed `discovered-from` omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4. Part 1 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4.1) created the crate root, `tests/e2e_slice3/support.rs` and the first item.

**This part** adds three demo items: "a set-aside with `--force --yes`, then `doctor undo`", "a set-aside, a later install, and the refused undo", and "a bound gc". They are one step because they share their subject (a suspended journal set, its guards and what `doctor gc` may delete of it) and their helpers (`tests/doctor/journal_sets.rs`, by F2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.2`, the journal fixers), and the gc item's home is built from the second item's steps. They pre-check checkpoint criterion 11's repair half: "The guarded repairs of the force-gated states suspend the journal set and unblock the client. While nothing that overlaps the suspended set has changed, `doctor undo` reactivates it byte-identical, after which recovery behaves exactly as before the repair. After an overlapping change (a later install on that client, say), `doctor undo` refuses with `undo_conflict` before moving anything, and the set stays inspectable in quarantine"; and criterion 10's gc item: "`doctor gc --dry-run` returns the exact deletion set, the candidates it keeps with their pin reasons, the undos that would be lost, and a token that `doctor gc --if-match` honours".

**The decisions these items show, restated:**

- **M4-D38, the set-aside as suspension.** The six stuck journal states (catalog rows 3–8: `journal-too-new`, `journal-unreadable`, `journal-unexpected-state`, `journal-step-unrecognized`, `journal-marker-mismatch`, `journal-unattributed`) share one fixer that moves the journal set into quarantine, one `RenameNoReplace` per artifact (the journal file, its in-flight lock, its state snapshot half, its client stage and snapshot halves), each into the quarantine root on its own filesystem, journal last; nothing is copied or deleted. It is `auto_fixable: false`, runs only with `--only <fm> --force --yes`, and is never part of a default fix. Its suspension manifest (each artifact's identity and stamp, the target's key, the marker's digest, the target's record generation, the epochs of the resources the journal would recover) is recorded as the primitives' `guards`. **Reactivation is guarded:** `doctor undo` checks every guard under the lock before moving anything; a moved generation (a later install), a changed marker or a changed epoch is `undo_conflict` with `details.reason: "changed_since_suspension"` and `details.changed`, and nothing moves; the bytes stay in quarantine. The undo restores the journal under a provisional name (`<tx>.reactivating.jsonl`) and activates it last, so no crash lets ordinary recovery run it ahead of the undo. Rejected there: an unconditional restore ("it activates stale instructions after later work"), deleting the journal, guessing a direction.
- **M4-D46, strict undo of repairs.** `doctor undo [<run>]` resolves to the same code as `omaddons undo <tx>`. Without a run it selects the newest run of kind `fix` whose repair is committed and not yet undone (the newest run is usually a diagnose, which has nothing to undo); undoing an undone run is a no-op with exit 0 (`already_undone: true`); the undo writes its own run directory of kind `undo` with `reverted_run`.
- **M4-D44, the bound fix.** `doctor fix --dry-run` returns `actions_planned` and a `precondition` holding nothing run-specific; `doctor fix --if-match <token>` in another process runs exactly that or nothing.
- **M4-D36, `doctor gc` is a bound, dependency-aware retention plan.** `--before <date | age>` (`30d` parsed by `history::parse_since`) makes runs eligible; the plan excludes active runs and pins by reachability: `active_run`, `unfinished_journal`, `active_undo`, and `recovery_dependency` for a set-aside's suspended set while its manifest is still reachable (it can still be reactivated). It lists `deletions[]` (`{kind, run_id, target, tx, path, bytes, may_hold_only_copy}`), `excluded[]` with `pin`, `undo_lost[]` (the undos each deletion makes impossible) and `latest {from, to}`. `--dry-run` returns a `precondition`; a real run needs `--yes`, takes the global lock, recomputes the plan from a fresh view and honours `--if-match`: a changed deletion set is `plan_stale` and deletes nothing. `latest` is retargeted to the newest retained terminal run before its target is deleted, or removed when none remains, never left dangling. Rejected there: age-only gc ("deletes recovery inputs").
- **M4-D40, the doctor exit dictionary:** `0 healthy`, `1 findings_present`, `2 fix_partial`, `3 fix_failed_rolled_back`, `4 refused_unsafe` (`doctor_refused`, `undo_conflict`, `plan_stale`), `5 concurrency_lost`, `6 online_required`, `64 usage_error`, `66`, `73`, `74`.

## Technical Approach

### Facts and helpers this part relies on

- Part 1's crate (`tests/e2e_slice3.rs`, debug-only, with `mod common;`, the fixtures included as `#[path = "doctor/mod.rs"] mod fixtures;`, and `support.rs` with `Trees::outside_doctor`, `planted`, `strip_volatile`).
- T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`): `tlog!()`, `log.step`, `log.json`, `log.run`, `log.cmd(..).env(..).run()`, `log.tree`, `log.assert_unchanged`, `log.diff`, `log.assert_eq`; `Ran::{ok, exit, fails, envelope, error_code, assert_private}`.
- F2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.2`): `tests/doctor/journal_sets.rs`, written for this suite's reuse: `Stuck { fm, row, tx, target_id, artifacts, clients }`, `plant(row, env) -> Stuck` (rows 3–8, on retail, through the fixtures of F1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1`), `set_hashes(paths) -> BTreeMap<PathBuf, Option<String>>` (a file's mode and SHA-256, a directory's `tree_hash`, `None` when absent), `set_aside(log, env, stuck, extra) -> Ran` (`doctor fix --only <fm> [-t <id>] --force --yes --json` plus `extra`), `preview(…)` (the same with `--dry-run`), `undo(log, env, run_id) -> Ran`, `quarantine_of(ran) -> Vec<(PathBuf, PathBuf)>` (each primitive's `(path, to)` from `actions[]`), `change_on(log, env, client) -> Ran` (an install of a local archive on that client, `install <name> --file <zip> -t <id> --offline --json`), `stuck_state(log, env, client)` (the code, reason and `journal_pending` warnings a change and `config set check_interval_hours 6` report). Include it in this crate the way `tests/doctor_repair.rs` does (by path, with `#[allow(dead_code, unused_imports)]`). F2's bead gives `plant` an `&TestEnv`; call each helper with the home type it landed with.
- F1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1`): `common::doctor::plant::journal_too_new(home, target)` (an install crashed at `engine.journal.prepared=abort`, its `prepared` line's `schema_version` then set to `"9.0"`).
- E3/E4/E6/E7/E8 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.4`, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.6`, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.7`, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.8`): `common::doctor::check_envelope`, `doctor ls --json` (`runs[]` with `run_id`, `kind`, `undo_complete`), `doctor fix`, `doctor undo`, `doctor gc`.
- E12 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.12`): `history --json` renders repair lines (`kind: "repair"`, `target: null`, `targets`, `doctor_run_id`) and undo lines (`kind: "undo"`, `reverts`).
- `OMADDONS_NOW` (an RFC 3339 time, debug builds) freezes the binary's clock; `TestEnv` sets `TZ=UTC`.

### 1. `tests/e2e_slice3/set_aside.rs` (new; one `#[path]` line in the crate root)

#### 1.1 `a_set_aside_with_force_yes_is_reactivated_by_doctor_undo`

Home: `Home::new(&["wow"])`; the id is `fm-concurrency_primitives-journal-too-new` (`<fm>`).

| Step (`log.step`) | Command or action | Assert |
|---|---|---|
| `plant` | `stuck = journal_sets::plant(3, …)`; `before = set_hashes(&stuck.artifacts)` | `log.json("set before", before)`; every artifact present |
| `stuck before` | `journal_sets::stuck_state(&log, …, "retail")` | the change refused with `state_too_new`, `details.reason: "journal_too_new"`; recorded as `state_before` |
| `diagnose` | `doctor --json --progress json` | exit 1; the `<fm>` finding on retail with `remediation.needs_force: true`, `auto_fixable: false`, `argv` `["omaddons","doctor","fix","--only",<fm>,"-t","retail","--force","--yes"]`, `evidence.attribution: "complete"`; its `instance` recorded as `instance_before` |
| `no consent` | `doctor fix --only <fm> -t retail --json --progress json` | exit 4, `error.code: "doctor_refused"`, `details.reason: "force_required"`, `details.fm: <fm>`, a `fix_argv` that runs (exit 0) |
| | `doctor fix --only <fm> -t retail --force --json --progress json` | exit 64, `error.code: "usage"`, `details.flag: "--force"` |
| | after each | `set_hashes(&stuck.artifacts) == before` |
| `preview` | `journal_sets::preview(…)` (`… --force --yes --dry-run --json`) | exit 1, `dry_run: true`; `actions_planned` is one `rename_noreplace` per artifact, the journal file's last, each `to` under `<run>/quarantine/state/` or `<meta>/snapshots/<repair tx>.repair/quarantine/`; `precondition` matches `^pc1:[0-9a-f]{64}$`; `Trees::outside_doctor` unchanged across it |
| `set aside` | `journal_sets::set_aside(&log, …, &stuck, &["--if-match", <token>])` (a new process) | exit 0, `state: "DONE_OK"`; `quarantine_of(&ran)` equals the preview's `(path, to)` pairs in order; each source absent; each `to` hashes as its source did in `before`; `undo_argv` set; `run_id` recorded as `aside_run` |
| `unblocked` | `status --json --progress json` | no `<fm>` issue on retail; `last_change.kind: "repair"` |
| `diagnose between` | `doctor --json --progress json` | no `<fm>` finding |
| `undo` | bare `doctor undo --json --progress json` | exit 0; `reverted_run == aside_run`, `already_undone: false`; `set_hashes(&stuck.artifacts) == before` (bytes, modes, kinds); no `<state>/journal/*.reactivating.jsonl`; every quarantine `to` absent |
| `as before` | `stuck_state(&log, …, "retail")`; `doctor --json` | equal to `state_before` (the same code and reason; the `journal_pending` texts equal after removing ULIDs and run ids); the `<fm>` finding's `instance == instance_before` |
| `undo again` | `doctor undo <aside_run> --json --progress json` | exit 0, `already_undone: true`; `set_hashes` unchanged |
| `history` | `history --json` | a line with `kind: "repair"`, `target: null`, `doctor_run_id == aside_run`; then one with `kind: "undo"` whose `reverts` names the repair's tx |

Decided while writing this bead: the undo is bare `doctor undo`, after an intervening diagnose, because that is what an agent or a person types and what M4-D46's selection rule exists for; `doctor undo <run>` is then run once more to show idempotence.

#### 1.2 `a_set_aside_then_a_later_install_refuses_the_undo`

Home: `Home::new(&["wow"])`; the id is `fm-concurrency_primitives-journal-step-unrecognized` (`<fm>`).

Factor steps 1–3 into `pub fn set_aside_then_install(log: &TestLog, home: &Home, target: &str) -> SetAsideThenInstall { stuck, aside_run, repair_tx, quarantine: Vec<(PathBuf, PathBuf)>, quarantine_hashes, addons_after }`, which the gc item reuses on retail.

| Step | Command or action | Assert |
|---|---|---|
| `plant` | `stuck = journal_sets::plant(6, …)` | |
| `blocked` | `journal_sets::change_on(&log, …, "retail")` | `Ran::fails(1, "internal")`, `details.reason: "step_unrecognized"` |
| `set aside` | `doctor fix --only <fm> -t retail --force --yes --json --progress json` | exit 0; `quarantine = quarantine_of(&ran)`; `quarantine_hashes = set_hashes(<every to>)`; `aside_run`, `repair_tx` (the report's `tx`) recorded |
| `a later install` | `change_on(&log, …, "retail")` | exit 0 (the client is unblocked); `log.tree("addons", <retail>/Interface/AddOns)` |
| `refused undo` | bare `doctor undo --json --progress json` | exit 4, `error.code: "undo_conflict"`, `details.reason: "changed_since_suspension"`, `details.changed` contains `"generation"`, `details.target` is retail's key; `set_hashes(<every to>) == quarantine_hashes`; every original path still absent; `log.assert_unchanged("addons", …)` (the installed addon stays) |
| `kept` | `doctor ls --json`; `doctor explain <fm> --json --progress json` | the `aside_run` entry has `kind: "fix"`, `undo_complete: false`; explain exits 0 |

### 2. `tests/e2e_slice3/gc.rs` (new; one `#[path]` line)

#### `a_bound_gc_deletes_exactly_its_preview_and_keeps_the_pinned_set`

Home: `Home::new(&["wow", "wow_classic"])`.

**Setup, at the real clock:**

1. `set A on retail`: `a = set_aside::set_aside_then_install(&log, &home, "retail")`. A's suspended set can no longer be reactivated (retail's generation moved).
2. `set B on classic`: `plant::journal_too_new(&home, "classic")`; the preview `doctor fix --only fm-concurrency_primitives-journal-too-new -t classic --force --yes --dry-run --json --progress json` (exit 1) names B's artifacts as the `path` of each `actions_planned[]` entry; `b_hashes = set_hashes(<those paths>)` (`log.json`); then the same command without `--dry-run` → exit 0, its `run_id` recorded as `b_run`. Nothing changes on classic afterwards, so B stays reactivatable.
3. `diagnoses`: two `doctor --json` runs.
4. `listing before`: `gc_listing(&home)`: every entry of `<state>/omaddons/doctor/runs/`, every `*.repair` entry of each client's `<meta>/snapshots/` and every entry of `<cache>/omaddons/quarantine/`, as absolute canonical paths (`log.json`). Decided while writing this bead: a helper in `gc.rs`, because these are exactly the places M4-D36 lets gc delete from.

**Then every command with `OMADDONS_NOW` = the real time at step 4 plus 40 days** (`log.cmd(..).env("OMADDONS_NOW", t).run()`):

| Step | Command | Assert |
|---|---|---|
| `preview` | `doctor gc --before 30d --dry-run --json --progress json` | exit 0, `dry_run: true`; `deletions[]` holds A's run directory and its `<meta>/snapshots/<a.repair_tx>.repair` half, the latter (or the run's entry, as E8 marks it) with `may_hold_only_copy: true`, and the old diagnose runs; `excluded[]` holds B's quarantined set with `pin: "recovery_dependency"`; `undo_lost` contains `a.repair_tx`; `precondition` set; `log.json("plan", …)` |
| `the world changes` | `doctor --json --progress json` | a young diagnose run, which moves `latest` |
| `stale` | `doctor gc --before 30d --yes --if-match <token> --json --progress json` | exit 4, `error.code: "plan_stale"`, `retryable: false`, `details.changed` contains `"selection"`, `fix_argv` the same command with `--dry-run` in place of `--yes --if-match <token>`; `gc_listing` unchanged, and `log.tree` of `<state>/omaddons/doctor`, `<state>/omaddons/journal`, each client's `<meta>/snapshots` and `<cache>/omaddons/quarantine` unchanged across it (nothing deleted, nothing recovered) |
| `preview again` | the dry run again | a new token |
| `bound gc` | `gc_listing` taken just before it; then `doctor gc --before 30d --yes --if-match <token 2> --json --progress json` | exit 0; that listing minus `gc_listing` after it equals the set of `deletions[].path` of the second preview; every `excluded[].path` exists; `<state>/omaddons/doctor/latest`, when present, resolves to an existing run directory (read the link, check the target) |
| `the pin held` | `doctor undo <b_run> --json --progress json` | exit 0; B's artifacts hash as `b_hashes` (byte-identical, modes included): gc kept exactly what an undo still needed |

Every run passes `Ran::assert_private()`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `set_aside::a_set_aside_with_force_yes_is_reactivated_by_doctor_undo` passes every step of §1.1: refused without consent (4, `force_required`; 64 without `--yes`) with nothing moved; the preview's token binds a run in a new process whose actions equal the preview's; the client is unblocked; bare `doctor undo` after a diagnose reactivates the set byte-identical; recovery then reports exactly the state it reported before; the second undo is `already_undone`; `history` shows the repair and its undo.
- [ ] `set_aside::a_set_aside_then_a_later_install_refuses_the_undo` passes: after the later install, `doctor undo` is exit 4 `undo_conflict` with `changed_since_suspension` naming `generation` and retail's key; the quarantine and the installed addon are unchanged and the originals stay absent.
- [ ] `gc::a_bound_gc_deletes_exactly_its_preview_and_keeps_the_pinned_set` passes: the preview lists A for deletion with `may_hold_only_copy` and `undo_lost`, and B as `recovery_dependency`; the stale token is refused with `plan_stale` and nothing is deleted or recovered; the bound run deletes exactly the second preview's paths; `latest` never dangles; B's undo then restores its set byte-identical.
- [ ] Every run is private (`Ran::assert_private()`), and every doctor envelope passes `check_envelope`.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

None new: `gc_listing` and `set_aside_then_install` are scenario helpers, exercised by the three tests. (Part 1's `support.rs` holds the suite's unit-tested pure helpers.)

### Integration and end-to-end tests

The three tests of Technical Approach §1 and §2, in `tests/e2e_slice3/set_aside.rs` and `tests/e2e_slice3/gc.rs`, each on its own `Home`, through the real binary, with the commands in the order of their tables. Failpoints only inside the planting helpers of F1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1`) and F2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.2`) (`engine.journal.prepared=abort`, `engine.swap.before_rename=abort`); environment `OMADDONS_NOW` for every gc-phase command.

### Logging

- `let log = tlog!();` per test; one `log.step` per table row, with the labels shown.
- Every command through `log.run`/`log.cmd` (the frozen time is in each gc-phase run record's overrides).
- `log.json` of `before`, every `set_hashes` result, the preview's `actions_planned` and the run's `actions`, every `quarantine_of` result, each error's `details`, both gc plans, both `gc_listing`s and their difference, and the history lines.
- `log.tree`/`log.assert_unchanged` for retail's `Interface/AddOns`, the trees outside `<state>/doctor/` around the preview, and the five gc trees around the stale run.
- Each test logs its wall time; a failure prints the transcript path and the last 20 records.

## Considerations

- **Plan risk #23** (guarded reactivation refuses more often than users expect): §1.2 shows the intended behaviour, the refusal naming what changed and the set kept; the gc item shows what happens next (the set is listed as a possible only copy and its undo as lost).
- **Why a reactivatable set-aside in the gc home:** a gc demo without a pin would not show that it is dependency-aware; B is the pin M4-D36 adds for set-asides, and its successful undo after the gc is the proof.
- **The stale step** uses a young diagnose moving `latest`, the one change that alters the plan without touching any repair (E8, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.8`, covers the other changes in its own suite: grown, shrunk, identity, `undo_lost`).
- **`details.changed` is a closed set** (`generation`, `marker`, `epochs` for a guard; `selection`, `observed` for a token): assert the expected member and log the whole value.
- **Hot spots:** `tests/doctor/journal_sets.rs` (owned by F2, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.2`: extend additively only if a helper lacks a target parameter, rerun `cargo test --test doctor_repair`, list it in the close comment); the crate root's `mod` lines (rebase).
- **Run time:** about 45 runs over the three tests.

title: E2E: a stuck repair fences only its own resources, and the Issues view's credential repair undone by Undo last
description:
Part 3 of 4 of omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4 (Slice 3 end to end: diagnose and repair). If this is the last open subtask of that bead, verify its acceptance criteria and close it as its body says.

## Background

**The leaf.** T4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4`) turns the exit demo of M4's slice 3, "Diagnose and repair", into `tests/e2e_slice3.rs`, a suite of `TestLog` scenarios in the gate, and records it on the milestone epic (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm`) as "**Slice demo 3. Diagnose and repair**". It owns no feature code and adds no wire name; it drives the real binary on synthetic homes through the helpers the slice's leaves wrote, and a demo item that fails is a defect in the leaf that owns the behaviour, fixed there and filed `discovered-from` omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4. Part 1 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4.1) created the crate root and `tests/e2e_slice3/support.rs`.

**This part** adds two demo items, "a stuck repair that fences only its own resources" and "the credential fix from the Issues view (QML) and Undo last", plus the in-gate check that the item's QML scenarios exist. They are one step because both are built on the same failure mode and repair, `fm-secrets-credential-file-mode` and its chmod fixer (F7, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.7`, plugins, secrets and the network), seen from two sides: the repair stuck halfway, and the repair as the widget runs and undoes it.

**The decisions these items show, restated:**

- **M4-D62, fences.** A doctor repair is a target-less transaction of its own journal family; one that recovery cannot settle stays on disk. A stuck, readable repair journal refuses only the mutations whose write sets overlap its protected resources (its primitives' writes and the backups its rollback reads); every other command, client and path keeps working. The refusal is the fencing journal's own stop error (the code and `details.reason` its state has) plus `details.tx` and `details.resource`, with the fix `omaddons doctor explain <fm>`, and every command gets one `journal_pending` warning per stuck repair. Fences are enforced at the one writer: each command loads them once from `journal::diagnose`'s verdicts into its scope table and `mutate()` refuses an overlapping operation. Rejected there: blocking the whole machine for any stuck repair ("one stuck chmod would block every client").
- **M4-D31 and M4-D45, write-ahead primitives and the fixed order.** A repair is lowered into primitives, each one filesystem operation with its own `step` line written before it runs, and `pre`/`post` endpoint predicates; recovery decides whether a primitive ran by matching the live path against them, and when it matches neither, it stops (`step_unrecognized`).
- **M4-D44, `doctor fix` binds across processes:** its dry run's `precondition` holds nothing run-specific, so `doctor fix --if-match <token>` in a new process runs exactly the preview or nothing.
- **M4-D46, repair undo:** `omaddons undo --run <run>` (what the widget's Undo last runs) inverts the repair strictly; `--dry-run` stores a plan, and `apply <plan_id>` applies exactly it.
- **M4-D28 and criterion 8 (doctor part):** "The Issues view runs an auto-fixable finding's repair with a preview. It never runs a set-aside, `doctor gc`, or any argv with `--force`: those rows show the explanation and the terminal command." G2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.2`) built that in the widget, with QML scenarios over envelopes the binary writes; three of their names were fixed for this bead.

## Technical Approach

### Facts and helpers this part relies on

- Part 1's crate and `support.rs` (`rust_test_fns`, `qml_test_fns`, `Trees`).
- T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`): `tlog!()`, `log.step`, `log.note`, `log.json`, `log.secret`, `log.run`, `log.cmd(..).env(..).stdin(..).failpoints(..).run()`, `log.tree`, `log.assert_unchanged`; `Ran::{ok, exit, fails, aborted, envelope, data, warnings, commands, assert_private}`.
- E3 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.3`): the fixtures (`fixtures::all()`, each with `id()`/`name()`, `corrupt(&home)`, `subject(&home)`), `common::doctor::check_envelope`.
- F7 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.7`): the fixture `fm-secrets-credential-file-mode` (plants the stored GitHub token, `<config>/credentials/github`, at mode 0644) and its chmod fixer (one `chmod` primitive to 0600).
- E5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`): the repair's tracked session runs its primitives and nothing else, so the first hit of `fsx.mutate.executed` in a `doctor fix` process is the first primitive (the doctor's own run-directory writes are untracked and hit only `fsx.mutate.checked`); the journal is `<state>/journal/<tx>.repair.jsonl` with lines `prepared`, `step k`, `done`, `committed`.
- E14 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.14`): fences, the refusal's shape, and the `journal_pending` warning text holding the tx and one parenthesized reason.
- E11 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.11`): `tests/common/differential.rs`: `predict(log, label, paths, clients, running) -> Prediction`, `observe_envelope(envelope, prediction, journals_after, caller)`, `assert_agrees(log, prediction, observed, caller)`.
- F1 and F2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.1`, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.2`): a repair journal that recovery cannot settle reports as `fm-concurrency_primitives-journal-step-unrecognized` with `evidence.family: "repair"` and its protected resources in the evidence.
- G2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.2`): the widget's argv (`status --cached -v` for status; `doctor fix --only <fm> --dry-run`, then `--if-match <token>`, for a repair; `undo --run <run> --dry-run`, then `apply <plan_id>`, for Undo last of a repair), `omarchy/tests/qml/tst_repairs.qml` (`TestCase { name: "Repairs" }`), and in `tests/omarchy_widget.rs` the always-on guard `the_repair_scenarios_read_only_fixtures_the_binary_writes`.
- At `c0ab5e9`: the gate's QML step runs only when `omarchy/` changed or with `--all` (`scripts/gate.sh:35-40`); `argc widget-test` (`Argcfile.sh:20-21`) runs `scripts/widget-test.sh --qml`, whose step 4 runs `qmltestrunner` over every `tst_*.qml` in `omarchy/tests/qml` (`scripts/widget-test.sh:60-68`); seven QML files exist today, none named `tst_repairs.qml`.

### 1. `tests/e2e_slice3/fence.rs` (new; one `#[path]` line in the crate root)

#### `a_stuck_repair_fences_only_its_own_resources`

Home: `Home::new(&["wow", "wow_classic_era"])` (targets `retail` and `era`); two local archives built with `common::archives::zip_text` (`Bar/Bar.toc`, `Bar/Bar.lua`; `Baz/Baz.toc`, `Baz/Baz.lua`), written under the home's root.

Decided while writing this bead: the stuck repair is made by the real `doctor fix`, crashed after its chmod, then disturbed, rather than by E14's synthetic child (`common::repairs::stuck`), because the demo is end to end: the journal that fences is one the binary's own repair wrote.

| Step (`log.step`) | Command or action | Assert |
|---|---|---|
| `plant` | the `fm-secrets-credential-file-mode` fixture from `fixtures::all()`: `corrupt(&home)`; `log.secret(<the token's value>)` | the token file exists at mode 0644 |
| `crash the repair` | `doctor fix --only fm-secrets-credential-file-mode --json --progress json`, `.failpoints("fsx.mutate.executed=abort@1")` | `Ran::aborted()`; the token's mode is 0600 (the chmod ran); `<state>/journal/<tx>.repair.jsonl` exists, its complete lines exactly `prepared` and `step 1` (`log.json` of the lines); `tx` recorded |
| `disturb` | test code: write the token's bytes to a sibling temp file, set its mode to 0644, rename it over the token | a new inode at the path; `pre` (old identity, 0644) and `post` (old identity, 0600) both fail to match, so recovery will stop at step 1 |
| `status` | `status --json --progress json` | exit 0; exactly one `journal_pending` warning whose message holds `tx` and `(step_unrecognized)`; `log.tree("credentials", <config>/credentials)` |
| `doctor` | `doctor --json --progress json` | a `fm-concurrency_primitives-journal-step-unrecognized` finding with `evidence.tx == tx`, `evidence.family: "repair"`, its protected resources naming the token's path; `check_envelope` passes |
| `the fenced write` | `auth github set --json --progress json` with a second canary token on stdin (`log.secret` it first) | `Ran::fails(1, "internal")`; `details.reason: "step_unrecognized"`, `details.tx == tx`, `details.resource` the token's path; a fix naming `doctor explain`; `log.assert_unchanged("credentials", …)` |
| `unrelated work proceeds` | `install bar --file <Bar zip> -t retail --offline --json --progress json` | exit 0, one `journal_pending` warning naming `tx`; `credentials` unchanged |
| | `install baz --file <Baz zip> -t era --offline --json --progress json` | exit 0; `credentials` unchanged |
| | `config set check_interval_hours 6 --json --progress json` | exit 0 (`config.toml` is a sibling of `credentials/`); `credentials` unchanged |
| `prediction` | around each of the four lock-taking commands above: `differential::predict(&log, <label>, &paths, &<client dirs>, &[])` before, `observe_envelope` + `assert_agrees` after | the repair stays stopped at `step_unrecognized` each time; no other journal exists |
| `explain` | the finding's `remediation.explain_argv` with `--json --progress json` | exit 0; the instance's evidence lists the token's path |
| `no canary leaked` | read both of this test's log files | neither canary value appears; every run passed `Ran::assert_private()` |

### 2. `tests/e2e_slice3/issues_view.rs` (new; one `#[path]` line)

#### 2.1 `the_credential_repair_the_issues_view_runs_is_undone_by_undo_last`

Home: `Home::new(&["wow"])`; F7's fixture `corrupt(&home)`; every argv is the one the widget builds (G2), with `--json --progress json`.

| Step | Command | Assert |
|---|---|---|
| `plant` | | `log.tree("config", <config>)` (modes included) |
| `status` | `status --cached -v --json --progress json` | the issue `fm-secrets-credential-file-mode` with `auto_fixable: true`, `remediation.argv` exactly `["omaddons","doctor","fix","--only","fm-secrets-credential-file-mode"]`, `explain.argv` `["omaddons","doctor","explain","fm-secrets-credential-file-mode"]` |
| `preview` | `doctor fix --only fm-secrets-credential-file-mode --dry-run --json --progress json` | exit 1, `dry_run: true`, `state: "DONE_FINDINGS"`, `actions_planned` one `chmod` with `mode: "0600"` and `pre.mode: "0644"`, `precondition` matching `^pc1:[0-9a-f]{64}$`, `tx: null`; `log.assert_unchanged("config", …)` |
| `bound run, a new process` | `doctor fix --only fm-secrets-credential-file-mode --if-match <precondition> --json --progress json` | exit 0, `state: "DONE_OK"`, `tx` set, `actions[0].ok`; the token's mode is 0600; `run_id` recorded |
| `status after` | `status --json --progress json` | no credential issue; `last_change.kind: "repair"`; `last_change.undo.argv` `["omaddons","undo","--run",<run_id>]` |
| `Undo last: preview` | `undo --run <run_id> --dry-run --json --progress json` | exit 0, `data.kind: "repair"`, `data.plan_id` a ULID, exactly one `apply` action in `commands[]` |
| `Undo last: apply` | `apply <plan_id> --json --progress json` | exit 0; the token's mode is 0644; `log.assert_unchanged("config", …)` against the `plant` tree, modes included |

#### 2.2 `the_issues_view_qml_scenarios_exist_by_name`

A source check, logged (`let log = tlog!();`, `log.json` of every name found):

1. `omarchy/tests/qml/tst_repairs.qml` exists and contains `TestCase` with `name: "Repairs"`.
2. `support::qml_test_fns` of it contains each of these exactly once:
   - `test_a_credential_fix_from_issues_is_undone_with_undo_last_through_a_stored_plan`
   - `test_a_set_aside_row_offers_no_fix_and_shows_its_explanation_and_command`
   - `test_undo_last_reverts_a_repair_through_its_stored_plan`
3. `support::rust_test_fns` of `tests/omarchy_widget.rs` contains `the_repair_scenarios_read_only_fixtures_the_binary_writes`, not ignored, so in every pipeline run the QML scenarios read only fixtures the binary has just written.
4. No file named `Fixtures.js` exists under `omarchy/` in the working tree (it is generated per run into a temporary plugin copy, never committed).

Decided while writing this bead: the names are checked in every gate here, and the scenarios' passing is shown at the leaf's close by `argc widget-test`, which always runs the QML step, because the gate's QML step runs only when `omarchy/` changed or with `--all`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `fence::a_stuck_repair_fences_only_its_own_resources` passes: the real `doctor fix` crashed after its chmod and disturbed leaves a repair journal recovery cannot settle; `status` warns once naming it; `doctor` reports it as `journal-step-unrecognized` with `family: "repair"` and the token among its protected resources; `auth github set` is refused with `internal`/`step_unrecognized`, `details.tx` and `details.resource`, `<config>/credentials` unchanged; installs on retail and era and `config set` succeed; the prediction of E11 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.11`) agrees around each lock-taking command; no canary appears in any output or log.
- [ ] `issues_view::the_credential_repair_the_issues_view_runs_is_undone_by_undo_last` passes: the issue is auto-fixable with the doctor's argv; the preview writes nothing; the bound run in a new process repairs; `status` names the repair as the last change with its `undo --run` argv; the undo's preview stores a plan and `apply` restores `<config>` exactly, modes included.
- [ ] `issues_view::the_issues_view_qml_scenarios_exist_by_name` passes: the three named scenarios exist once each in `tst_repairs.qml`, the fixture guard of G2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.7.2`) is an always-on test, and no `Fixtures.js` is committed.
- [ ] Every run is private (`Ran::assert_private()`); every doctor envelope passes `check_envelope`.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files.

## Test Plan

### Unit tests

None new (the name scanners are part 1's, unit-tested in `support.rs`).

### Integration and end-to-end tests

The three tests of Technical Approach §1 and §2, in `tests/e2e_slice3/fence.rs` and `tests/e2e_slice3/issues_view.rs`, each on its own `Home` (the source check needs none), through the real binary, commands in table order. Failpoint: `fsx.mutate.executed=abort@1` (the fence). Stdin: the canary tokens of `auth github set`, registered with `log.secret` first.

### Logging

- `let log = tlog!();` per test; one `log.step` per table row, with the labels shown.
- Every command through `log.run`/`log.cmd`: the crashed child's record holds its failpoint and `signal: 6`; stdin is recorded as a length only.
- `log.json` of the repair journal's lines after the crash, of the finding's evidence, of each refusal's `details`, of every prediction and observation (the helper of E11, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.11`, logs them), of the preview's `actions_planned` and the run's `actions`, of the undo's `data`, and of the QML and Rust names found.
- `log.tree`/`log.assert_unchanged` for `<config>/credentials` around every command of §1, and for `<config>` across §2.1.
- Each test logs its wall time; a failure prints the transcript path and the last 20 records.

## Considerations

- **Plan risk #21** (fences scoped wrong): §1 checks both sides at once, the overlapping write refused and three unrelated changes on two clients allowed.
- **Plan risk #1** (a recovery bug in the repair journal): §1 exercises a real crashed repair and its stop; the matrices of E5 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.5`) and F9 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.9`) remain the proof of recovery itself.
- **If `fsx.mutate.executed@1` is not the chmod** (a later change adds a tracked write before the primitives), the `crash the repair` step fails with the journal's lines logged; arm `doctor.repair.step=abort@1` plus a check that the chmod did not run, and adapt `disturb` (the identity change alone then matches neither predicate), recording the change in the close comment.
- **Hot spots:** `tests/omarchy_widget.rs` and `omarchy/tests/qml/` are read, never written, here.
- **Privacy:** the canaries never reach a log (T1, `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`, scrubs registered secrets) or an output; no `WTF/` exists on these homes, and every run is still checked.
- **Run time:** about 20 runs.

## Dependencies

- **Parent:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4 (Slice 3 end to end: diagnose and repair). Also blocked by T1 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.1`) through its own edge, because it writes `TestLog` scenarios.
- **Before it:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4.1, for the crate root and `support.rs`.
- **Beside it:** omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4.2 and omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.9.4.4, which touch other files.
- **After it:** none; if it is the last open subtask, its closer runs the leaf's close (the demo comment).
