title: doctor fix exits 0 when findings it does not repair remain after a repair
description:
## Background

README's `### doctor fix` promises: "It exits 0 when nothing is left, 1 when a dry run plans something or findings remain that it does not repair". E6's runtime (`src/doctor/fix_runtime.rs`, the terminal-state match in `state_of`) does not do that for a real run that repaired something. When the repaired instances verify (`verification.remaining == 0`) and every delegated recovery settled, the run is `DONE_OK`, exit 0, even when `findings` still lists findings of other failure modes that it did not repair (manual ones, or ones only a forced or disabled fixer repairs). Only a run that planned nothing ends `DONE_FINDINGS` (exit 1) when findings exist.

So an agent or the widget reading `exit_code: 0` from `doctor fix` concludes the machine is healthy, while the report's `findings` holds, for example, `fm-network-credential-rejected`, which no fixer repairs. This contradicts M4-D43's spirit that a run with something left is never reported as healthy.

Found while writing omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.7.5's scenario `online_fix_lists_network_findings_as_manual`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. A home with an exposed stored GitHub token (`<config>/omaddons/credentials/github` at mode 0644), and `/rate_limit` answering 401 (the replay fixtures `common::doctor::probes::rate_limit_status(home, 401, &[], None)` and `plant::credential_file_mode`).
2. `omaddons doctor fix --online --json`.
3. Observed: the chmod is repaired (`actions_taken: 1`), `findings` holds `fm-network-credential-rejected` (manual) and a `check-incomplete` for the rate-limit row, and `state: DONE_OK`, `exit_code: 0`. README says exit 1.

## Technical Approach

- In `fix_runtime.rs`'s terminal-state decision, a `Done` with a verification that left nothing of the repaired modes, but with findings in the final report (the run's `final_findings`) that are not the repaired instances, is `DONE_FINDINGS` (exit 1), not `DONE_OK`. `DONE_PARTIAL` (exit 2) stays reserved for a repaired mode still found.
- Decide, and record in README, whether runtime findings (`check-incomplete`, `detector-crashed`) count as "left". Following M4-D43, they should.
- Update README's `### doctor fix` sentence if the decision refines it, and E6's state-table tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `doctor fix` that repairs everything it planned, with other findings remaining, ends `DONE_FINDINGS`, exit 1; with no findings remaining, `DONE_OK`, exit 0; with a repaired mode still found, `DONE_PARTIAL`, exit 2.
- E6's unit table of terminal states covers the new row; `tests/doctor.rs::online_fix_lists_network_findings_as_manual` asserts exit 1.
- README's exit sentence and the code agree; `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit: the terminal-state table in `fix_runtime.rs` (repaired with leftovers, repaired with none, partial).
- E2E: `tests/doctor.rs::online_fix_lists_network_findings_as_manual` tightened to `exit(1)`; a fixer-only scenario (the chmod alone) stays exit 0.

## Considerations

- The widget's Issues view reads `doctor fix`'s exit through the envelope; check `omarchy/Model.js` treats exit 1 after a fix as "done, with findings left", not as a failure.
- This changes a wire exit code before the freeze, which is allowed until the first tag; note it in the close comment (M4-D55).
acceptance_criteria: doctor fix that repairs everything it planned with other findings remaining ends DONE_FINDINGS (exit 1); none remaining DONE_OK (exit 0); a repaired mode still found DONE_PARTIAL (exit 2). E6's terminal-state unit table covers it; tests/doctor.rs::online_fix_lists_network_findings_as_manual asserts exit 1. README and code agree; argc gate passes.
close_reason: doctor fix now ends DONE_FINDINGS (exit 1) when its repairs verify but findings remain, with verification re-checking every offline mode found so a settled state is not misreported.

comments.author: FrostyJasper
comments.text: claim: src/doctor/fix_runtime.rs (terminal state), README doctor fix exits, tests/doctor.rs online_fix_lists_network_findings_as_manual, tests/doctor_plugins_secrets.rs inside_and_outside_in_one_run

comments.text: decided: (1) Runtime findings count as left: a committed run whose report still holds check-incomplete or detector-crashed ends DONE_FINDINGS (exit 1), following M4-D43; the Done arm is now partial (a planned instance still found, or a recovery unsettled) → findings left → OK. (2) The exit alone was not enough: final findings used to keep the pre-repair findings of every mode the run did not repair, so a delegated roll-forward that settled another mode (the half-swapped update's managed-files-modified) still reported it, and with the new exit it would have read as exit 1 on a healthy home (tests/doctor_repair/delegate.rs caught it). Verification now re-checks the repaired modes and every other offline mode the diagnosis found or could not finish checking (RealEffects::rechecked_modes), the runtime's findings about those checks included; an online finding stands as found (a local repair cannot change a remote state, and re-probing would double the requests). README's doctor fix section says both.

Verification re-checks the repaired modes and every other offline mode the diagnosis found (rechecked_modes, detect_modes with the runtime's findings about those checks); online findings stand as found. The widget never runs doctor fix (Model.js lists it in CLI_PATHS only), so nothing there reads the new exit. · found: none

title: update's command-level error drops a failed item's details: hash_mismatch.blob never reaches the envelope
description:
## Background

M4-D52 promises that a damaged cached archive which cannot be downloaded again fails with `hash_mismatch` carrying `details.blob` (the archive's name) and `details.actual`, so an agent knows which blob to look at. F6 part 2 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.6.2`) raises exactly that error inside the planner (`engine::blobs::damaged_instead`), and `install` delivers it whole.

`update`, and every other command whose envelope is assembled by `TargetsData::all_failed` (`src/app/outcome.rs`), does not. When every item failed, the command's error is the first failed item's `ItemError` rebuilt with `.error()`, and an item's error keeps no `details` (the code says so: "A target's own error keeps its form, which an item's error keeps none of"). So the command-level error of an offline `update` whose new release's cached archive is damaged has the right code, message, retryability and fix, but `details` is only `{items: [...]}`, and the items' errors have no `details` either. `details.blob` and `details.actual` never reach the envelope. Neither does a planner's `details.tried` for a `hash_mismatch` (a `no_compatible_release`'s `tried` is special-cased in `src/app/update.rs`).

Found by F6 part 4 (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.6.6.4`), whose `tests/blobs.rs::an_update_never_installs_a_damaged_cached_archive` asserts what holds today and points here.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On a test home, install `gh:o/foo` v1 on retail from an HTTP fixture, then serve v2 (`gh_release`).
2. `omaddons update --dry-run --refresh --json`: v2's archive is cached.
3. Flip one byte of v2's blob in `<cache>/omaddons/blobs/<sha>`.
4. `omaddons update --offline --json`: exit 1, `error.code: "hash_mismatch"`, `retryable: true`, `fix_argv: ["omaddons","doctor","--include-deep"]`, but `error.details` is `{"items": [{"target", "request", "error": {code, message, fix, fix_argv}}]}`, with no `blob` and no `actual`.

## Technical Approach

- Keep the failed item's original `Error` beside its `ItemError` in `ItemResult`, not serialized (`PlanFailure` already carries it as `cause`). In `TargetsData::all_failed`, when no target error applies, build the command's error from that original error, so its `details` keep their keys, and add `items` as today. This is what `install::all_failed` already does.
- Check every caller of `TargetsData::all_failed` (update, remove, pin, unpin, sync, copy and others). Their top-level `details` gain the first failed item's own keys, which their `DetailSpec`s must already declare (A3's live validation checks them).
- Do not add `details` to the per-item `error` objects: that is a wire change to every items list, not needed for this.
- Re-accept the contract snapshots whose command-level `details` gain keys, reviewing each.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An offline `update` of a damaged cached archive fails with `details.blob` and `details.actual` at the command level, beside `items`.
- Every command assembled by `TargetsData::all_failed` keeps its first failed item's `details` keys at the command level; no per-item `error` gains a key.
- `tests/blobs.rs::an_update_never_installs_a_damaged_cached_archive` asserts `details.blob` (replacing its message check), and passes.
- The changed contract snapshots are re-accepted with only command-level `details` keys added.
- `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files.

## Test Plan

- Unit (`src/app/outcome.rs`): `all_failed` keeps a failed item's `details` (a `hash_mismatch` with `{blob, actual}`, a `no_compatible_release` with `tried`), plus `items`; a target's own error still wins, as today.
- E2E: `tests/blobs.rs`'s update scenario asserts `details.blob`; the contract matrix rows that cover an all-failed `update` or `remove` show the kept keys.

## Considerations

- A wire change on an error path: command-level `details` gain keys that their specs already declare. Record it in the close comment (common rule 6).
- Risk: a command whose first failed item's `details` hold a key its own spec does not declare. A3's live validation catches that in the gate.
- Privacy: details hold digests, refs and paths under omaddons' own folders, never below `WTF/`.
acceptance_criteria:
- An offline `update` of a damaged cached archive fails with `details.blob` and `details.actual` at the command level, beside `items`.
- Every command assembled by `TargetsData::all_failed` keeps its first failed item's `details` keys at the command level; no per-item `error` gains a key.
- `tests/blobs.rs::an_update_never_installs_a_damaged_cached_archive` asserts `details.blob` (replacing its message check), and passes.
- The changed contract snapshots are re-accepted with only command-level `details` keys added.
- `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files.

title: Doctor finding: two targets sharing one AddOns directory (target-addons-shared)
description:
## Background

Some players symlink one `Interface/AddOns` directory between Classic clients (for example Classic Era and Anniversary), so both clients load the same folders. omaddons keeps one record and one files index per target and never compares targets' AddOns paths. With a shared directory, each target's records are its own: an addon installed through one target shows up on the other as unmanaged folders, `status` there recommends looking at them, and `adopt` on the other target would record the same folders a second time. Two records owning one physical folder can then disagree, and an update through one target silently changes what the other's record claims.

M2 does not special-case this (recorded as a known limitation in README and on the vision bead, comment 606). The vision gives such machine-shape checks to M4's `doctor`.

## Technical Approach

- A doctor finding `target-addons-shared`: after discovery, canonicalize each target's `Interface/AddOns` (resolving symlinks) and group targets whose resolved directories are equal, or where one is inside another.
- Report each group once, naming the targets and the resolved path, with a fix that is advice, not a command: keep one target managing the directory (`omaddons targets rm <id>` for the other is the argv alternative), or stop sharing it.
- `status` may surface the same condition as an attention item; decide in this bead whether that is in scope (the finding is the minimum).
- No mutation: the finding only reports.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Two discovered targets whose AddOns directories resolve to the same directory produce exactly one `target-addons-shared` finding naming both targets.
- A target whose AddOns is not shared produces no finding; a symlink to a directory outside every target produces no finding.
- The finding's fix is a valid text fix or argv per the JSON contract, and the contract suite covers it.

## Test Plan

- Unit test over a synthetic layout: two Battle.net product folders whose `Interface/AddOns` is a symlink to one directory, and a control layout without the link.
- A contract row for the doctor command once it exists (M4).

## Considerations

- Discovered in the M2 documentation pass; belongs to M4 (the doctor). Not a blocker for any M2 or M3 bead.
- Resolving symlinks must not follow links out of the user's home in unexpected ways; reuse discovery's existing path rules.
close_reason: Shared AddOns directories are detected; status warns target_addons_shared

comments.author: CrimsonJasper
comments.text: done: discover::shared::shared_addons(targets) canonicalizes each target's Interface/AddOns (read-only) and groups targets whose directories are equal or nested (outermost path; a missing AddOns shares nothing; a link to a directory no other target uses is no group). decided: with no doctor yet (M4 is not decomposed), status is the surface now: one target_addons_shared warning per group that includes a selected target, message naming the targets and the resolved path, fix a text instruction (manage those addons from one client, -t <first>, do not adopt them on the others, or stop sharing) since targets rm only unregisters and discovery would find the client again. M4's doctor reuses shared_addons for its finding and contract row (to note when M4 is decomposed). Tests: unit a_symlinked_addons_dir_is_one_group_and_the_rest_share_nothing, an_addons_dir_inside_another_is_shared; status clients_sharing_one_addons_directory_are_warned_once (era+anniversary symlinked, retail control; -t retail none; -t anniversary one). Real machine: status shows no such warning (nothing shared here). README: warnings table row; the Known-limitations line now says detected but not managed together. Gate green (1288).

title: Retail 12.x: a mainline TOC below 120000 is called out of date, but the client never loads it
description:
## Background

Patch 12.0.0 changed retail's load rules: "Mainline addons that don't have an interface version of 120000 or higher are not allowed to load in 12.0.0+ builds at all" (warcraft.wiki.gg, Patch 12.0.0/API changes/notes, beta 1 and beta 2 notes). "Load out of date AddOns" does not lift this.

omaddons does not know about it:

- The Mainline family range is `NumRange::at_least(60_000)` (`src/rules.rs:1145`), so on a 12.x client a TOC at 110207 counts as in family.
- `judge` (`src/toc/loaded.rs:409`) then returns `Compatible { out_of_date: true }`, with the warning "…it loads only with out-of-date addons enabled" and the fix "update the addon, or enable "Load out of date AddOns" in the client".
- Installs succeed, and `status` and `outdated` call the addon out of date.

The keyless-coverage study (omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.7, comment 868) counted 38 of the WoWInterface top 100 as "installs, out of date" on mainline. Those below 120000 never load.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. A retail client at 12.1.5 (interface 120105).
2. `Foo.zip` holding `Foo/Foo.toc` with `## Interface: 110207`.
3. `omaddons install ./Foo.zip -t retail --json`.
4. Today: exit 0, `Foo` added, and an `out_of_date` warning whose fix suggests enabling "Load out of date AddOns".
5. Expected: `wrong_flavor`, saying that retail 12.0 and later never loads an interface below 120000, with nothing written.

## Technical Approach

- **Put the floor in the rules data** (`src/rules.rs`), the one place for load rules, patchable through `[client_rules]` as rows are. For the mainline family, when the client's own interface is 120000 or higher, TOC interfaces below 120000 do not count.
- **Key it on the client's interface, not on the row.** The `mainline-12.0.7` row covers 9.1.0 to 12.1.4 builds, and PTR, XPTR and beta builds are 12.x.
- **`best_in_family` and `judge`** (`src/toc/loaded.rs`): on such a client, values below the floor are out of range. When only such values remain, the verdict is `WrongFlavor` with a new reason. Its wire name is something like `below_client_floor`, and it carries the floor.
- **Messages.** Refusals and `info` say "retail 12.0 and later never loads addons below interface 120000". The `out_of_date` warning and its "Load out of date AddOns" fix never appear for such a folder.
- **Folders on disk.** Wherever a load verdict is shown (`status --unmanaged`, update status, `adopt`), such a folder reads as not loading, not as out of date.
- **With the evidence rule** (omad-mixed-archive-single-file-skk1), a side folder below the floor is left out like any folder built for other clients.
- **README:** step 4 of "How omaddons decides what loads", the rows table, the `out_of_date` warning row, and the new reason in the error details.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The steps above give `wrong_flavor` naming the floor, and nothing is written.
- On a 120105 client, 120000 is still `out_of_date`.
- A custom retail client below 12.0 (interface 110207) still treats 100207 as `out_of_date`.
- An installed addon whose TOC is below 120000 shows as not loading in `status` and update status.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

The companion test bead covers judge units, TOC-matrix rows, an install refusal, the on-disk verdict and the PTR, beta and `mainline-12.0.7` rows.

## Considerations

- Forever reads `_Mainline` TOCs, but its range is 15000 to 19999, so mainline interfaces never count there. A Forever floor, if one exists, is out of scope.
- Many installed retail addons will flip from out of date to not loading. Update status must still offer an update when a newer release loads.
- The new reason's wire name joins the output contract (vision D21).
acceptance_criteria: On a client at interface 120000 or higher, a mainline TOC below 120000 is WrongFlavor with a new floor reason (rules data in src/rules.rs, keyed on the client's interface), installs are refused naming the floor, on-disk folders read as not loading, the 'Load out of date AddOns' fix never appears for them; 120000 on 120105 stays out_of_date and pre-12 custom retail clients are unchanged; README updated; argc gate passes
close_reason: Retail 12.x refuses Mainline TOCs below 120000: interface_floor rules field on the 12.x mainline rows, below_client_floor verdict, refusal messages naming the floor, README and catalog updated

comments.author: CobaltOak
comments.text:
What landed, and the decisions taken where the bead left a choice.

**Source.** warcraft.wiki.gg `Patch_12.0.0/API_changes/notes`, "Forced interface matching for 12.0.0" (fetched 2026-10-24): "Mainline addons that don't have an interface version of 120000 or higher are not allowed to load in 12.0.0+ builds at all (with no player override)", in the Week 6, Beta 1 and Beta 2 notes. It is cited at `MAINLINE_INTERFACE_FLOOR` in `src/rules.rs` and in README step 5.

**Rules data.** `ClientRules.interface_floor: Option<u32>` (serde default `None`), with `ClientRules::floor_for(client_interface)`, which returns the floor only once the client's own interface has reached it. It is set to 120000 on `mainline`, `mainline-12.0.7` and `mainline-10.2.7`, the three rows a 12.x build can fall in. 12.0.0 to 12.0.6 share `mainline-10.2.7` with 11.x, so it binds by interface, not by row. `mainline-9.1` and every other row have none. It can be patched as `[client_rules.<row>] interface_floor = N`, where 0 removes it and a new row gets none (`RULES_FIELDS` in `src/state/config.rs`, README Rules overrides).

**Verdict.** There is a new `WrongFlavorReason::BelowClientFloor {interfaces, floor}`. Its wire form is `{"verdict":"wrong_flavor","reason":"below_client_floor","interfaces":[...],"floor":120000}`. `judge` checks the floor after the family range: no in-family value gives `interface_not_in_family` as before, and in-family values all below the floor give `below_client_floor`, never `out_of_date`, so the "Load out of date AddOns" fix never appears for such a folder. `best_in_family` and `primary_interface` take the rules and return `None` below the floor.

**Decided: a side folder below the floor rules itself out.** `accepts` (`src/engine/inspect.rs`) lists `BelowClientFloor` with game-type gates and other-client TOCs, so the addon installs and the folder is `folders.skipped` with the reason. Why: such a folder is an old build of this client's own family, not evidence of another client's build. Refusing the whole archive would be a new tightening the bead did not ask for, while installing it puts in a folder the client never loads. The addon's own folder below the floor still refuses the archive.

**Messages.** `wrong_flavor` (url/file/--file) and `no_compatible_release` add `retail never loads an addon whose interface is below 120000, whatever the player enables` when a candidate's own folder fell below the floor. `try_candidate` now returns a small `Refusal {reason, floor}` instead of a bare string. `info` has no per-reason text: its hint comes from verdict facts (`blocked` once a plan proved it), so there was no out-of-date claim there to change.

**Decided: catalog families.** OmniCC 11.2.8, Quartz 3.7.17, Rarity r751, OmniBar v34, Cell r274 (release.json declares mainline at 110207 or 110200) and Tukui 20.463 (Mainline TOC 110207) no longer list `mainline`. Their notes say why, and README's catalog intro now says a family whose live client never loads the declared build is left out. Why: `families` drive `search`'s yes/no and `info`'s hint, which would otherwise say "retail: yes" for a build retail refuses. The live probe's `declared_family` (`tests/live_probes.rs`) likewise reads a declared interface below its family's current floor as declaring no client.

**On disk.** `list --unmanaged` shows such a folder as `wrong_flavor`. `status` shows no load verdict for managed addons, so it has nothing to change. For update statuses: an adopted (TOC-versioned) build below the floor has no installed primary interface, so M2-D42's floor does not hold back a newer release that loads. A newer release below the floor is `blocked` (`verified_not_loading`) once a plan has downloaded it.

**Tests.** Judge units, including the floor patched away, are in `src/toc/loaded.rs`. Row data and the override are in `src/rules.rs`. The matrix has a new group `interface_floor` with 12 cases (12.1.5, 12.1.0, 12.0.5, 12.0.1, custom 12.1.5, pre-12 11.2.7 Battle.net and custom, and Forever), and the old "previous expansion is out of date" case now runs on an 11.2.7 client. `tests/install.rs` covers the refusal and the skipped side folder, `tests/update.rs` a release below the floor being blocked, and `tests/list.rs` the on-disk verdict. Tests that used 11.x interfaces on 12.x clients to mean "out of date" now use 120000. Setting the builtin floor to `None` fails 7 tests across `--lib`, `toc_matrix` and `install`.

**Found:** omad-ycev (a gate flake: ETXTBSY on a freshly written test stub) and omad-fxma (memo verdict facts made before this change still say such an asset loads, until it is downloaded again).

title: `undo --last-by <typo>` usage fix drops every other argument and suggests a real undo by another actor
description:
## Background

The closing check of the post-M2 audit (omad-m2-audit-yegz) found a usage-error fix that hands the user a different command that changes addons.

README's usage-fix rule ("Command reference"): "A mistyped command, flag or value is a usage error. Its fix is the corrected command when that command only reads, and `omaddons help <command>` when the closest command changes something: a typo never hands you a different command that changes addons. A mistyped flag or value of the command you typed is corrected in place (`--channel betaa` → `--channel beta`). Every suggested command parses."

`undo --last-by` breaks it. `--last-by` is a plain `Option<String>` (src/app/undo.rs:40-42) parsed inside `undo::run` (src/app/undo.rs:268-280). Any value other than human, agent or widget is a usage error whose fix is always the fixed argv `["omaddons", "undo", "--last-by", "agent"]`:

- every other argument the user typed is dropped: `-t <id>`, `--dry-run`, `--saved-variables`, `--reason`;
- the value is not the closest match: `humna` is "corrected" to `agent`, not `human`.

So `omaddons undo --last-by humna -t retail --dry-run` (a preview of undoing the human's last run on one client) suggests `omaddons undo --last-by agent`, which really undoes the agent's last run on every client. An agent that follows `fix_argv`, as the contract invites, changes addons the user never asked to touch, and possibly SavedVariables too.

Compare `--saved-variables`, which uses a clap `value_parser` (src/app/undo.rs:46-49) and goes through the general clap invalid-value correction: `undo --saved-variables restor -t retail --dry-run` suggests `omaddons undo --saved-variables restore -t retail --dry-run`, every argument kept.

The global `--actor` flag has a smaller version of the same defect. `Context::new` (src/cli.rs:245-253) answers an invalid `--actor` value with `fix_argv(&without_flag(argv, "--actor"))`: the flag is dropped instead of corrected in place. The suggested command is the one the user typed, so it changes the same addons, but it runs under a different actor: with no flag, the actor falls back to `OMADDONS_ACTOR`, then to human when stdin is a terminal and agent otherwise (src/model.rs:338-356). `omaddons install weakauras -t retail --actor humna` from a script suggests `omaddons install weakauras -t retail`, which would be recorded as `agent`, so a later `undo --last-by human` would not find it. That is not a different command on addons, but it is a mistyped value not corrected in place, and it changes what `undo --last-by` and `history` see. It is included here because the fix is the same.

tests/contract/usage_fixes.rs only checks that a fix runs the command path the user typed (`never_another_mutating_command`), so `undo --last-by agent` for a typo in `undo` passes it today.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Fresh HOME with one synthetic retail client, `OMADDONS_OFFLINE=1`.
2. `omaddons undo --last-by humna -t retail --dry-run --json`: exit 2, `error.fix_argv` = `["omaddons","undo","--last-by","agent"]` (no `-t`, no `--dry-run`, wrong value).
3. `omaddons undo --last-by xyzzy -t retail --dry-run --json`: the same fix.
4. `omaddons undo --saved-variables restor -t retail --dry-run --json`: fix `["omaddons","undo","--saved-variables","restore","-t","retail","--dry-run"]` (correct behaviour, for contrast).
5. `omaddons install weakauras -t retail --actor humna --json`: fix `["omaddons","install","weakauras","-t","retail"]` (the flag dropped, not corrected).

## Technical Approach

- `--last-by`: give the clap arg `value_parser = ["human", "agent", "widget"]` (as `--saved-variables` and `--channel` have), so a bad value goes through the existing clap invalid-value path that corrects the value in place and keeps every argument. Keep parsing the accepted string into `Actor` in `run`; the hand-built usage error there becomes unreachable and can be removed (or kept as an internal guard).
- If the clap path cannot be used (e.g. it must stay a free string for some reason), build the fix with the existing helper `with_flag_value(argv, "--last-by", <closest>)` (src/cli.rs:1060), choosing the closest of human/agent/widget by the same distance `suggest` uses; when nothing is close, the fix is `omaddons help undo` (a read), never a guessed value.
- `--actor`: correct the value in place the same way: `fix_argv(&with_flag_value(argv, "--actor", <closest>))` when a value is close, otherwise `omaddons help <command>` or a prose fix ("--actor is human, agent or widget"). A clap `value_parser` on the global flag would also work, but the env-variable path (`OMADDONS_ACTOR`) keeps its prose fix either way.
- Add the cases to the usage-fix corpus in tests/contract/usage_fixes.rs, and add an assertion there (or a new test beside it) that for a mistyped flag value the fix keeps every other argument: the fix argv equals the typed argv with only that value replaced.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `undo --last-by humna -t retail --dry-run` suggests `omaddons undo --last-by human -t retail --dry-run`.
- `undo --last-by agnet ...` suggests `agent` with every other argument kept.
- A `--last-by` value with no close match suggests `omaddons help undo` (or a prose fix), never an `undo` that runs.
- A mistyped `--actor` value is corrected in place with every other argument kept, or answered with help/prose when nothing is close; the flag is never silently dropped.
- The usage-fix corpus covers both flags and fails if a value fix drops an argument.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Contract (tests/contract/usage_fixes.rs): corpus entries `["undo", "--last-by", "humna", "-t", "retail", "--dry-run"]`, `["undo", "--last-by", "xyzzy"]`, `["install", "x", "-t", "retail", "--actor", "humna"]`; assert the exact `fix_argv` for the first and third.
- Contract: a property over the value-typo corpus entries: the fix argv differs from the typed argv only at the mistyped value's position.
- Unit (src/cli.rs tests): `Context::new` with `--actor humna` yields a fix with `--actor human`; with `OMADDONS_ACTOR=humna` the prose fix is unchanged.
- E2E: `undo --last-by humna --dry-run` exits 2 and nothing in the client changes.

## Considerations

- README already states the rule; no README change is needed for this fix.
- `undo` is the most dangerous command to guess for: it can restore SavedVariables. Any fallback must prefer help over a guessed actor.
- clap's value-parser error text for `--last-by` will change the message wording; update any snapshot that pins the old message ("--last-by is human, agent or widget, not ...").
acceptance_criteria: undo --last-by humna -t retail --dry-run suggests undo --last-by human -t retail --dry-run; no close match suggests help undo or prose, never a running undo; a bad --actor value is corrected in place or answered with help/prose, never dropped; usage-fix corpus covers both and fails if a value fix drops an argument; argc gate passes
close_reason: --last-by goes through clap's in-place value fix; --actor is corrected in place or answered with help

comments.author: DapperDelta
comments.text: claim: src/app/undo.rs (--last-by value_parser), src/cli.rs (--actor fix in place), tests/contract/usage_fixes.rs

comments.text: done: undo --last-by humna -t retail --dry-run suggests --last-by human with every argument kept; xyzzy suggests omaddons help undo; --actor humna is corrected in place, robot gets omaddons help <command>, OMADDONS_ACTOR keeps its prose fix; new contract test a_mistyped_value_is_corrected_in_place_with_every_argument_kept over 7 value typos; argc gate exit 0 · found: none

title: TLS crates rustls-webpki 0.103.15 and webpki-roots 1.0.9 fail cargo deny (RUSTSEC-2026-0381, -0382)
description:
## Background

`argc gate --all` runs `cargo deny`. On 2026-10-21 it fails on two new RustSec advisories against the TLS stack that every omaddons request goes through (ureq 3.4.2 with rustls):

- RUSTSEC-2026-0382: `rustls-webpki` 0.103.15 may accept certificate paths through distrusted emSign intermediates, whose private keys are now public. Fixed in 0.103.16.
- RUSTSEC-2026-0381: `webpki-roots` 1.0.9 bundles `emSign ECC Root CA - G3`, which allows the same paths. Fixed in 1.0.10, which removes that root.

README "Network and privacy" promises TLS through rustls with the bundled Mozilla root store (webpki-roots). With the affected versions, a certificate chaining through a distrusted emSign intermediate could be accepted for an allowlisted host. The plain `argc gate` runs `cargo deny` only when `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` or `deny.toml` change, so it still passes at HEAD and hides the advisories. The post-M2 audit epic (omad-m2-audit-yegz) needs the gate to pass at its closing commit.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. At be0e16f, run `argc gate --all`.
2. The fmt, clippy and test stages pass. `cargo deny` reports `advisories FAILED` with RUSTSEC-2026-0381 and RUSTSEC-2026-0382, and the gate exits 1.

## Technical Approach

- `cargo update -p rustls-webpki -p webpki-roots`, which changes only `Cargo.lock`: rustls-webpki 0.103.15 to 0.103.16, webpki-roots 1.0.9 to 1.0.10. Both are semver-compatible patch releases, and no other crate moves.
- No `Cargo.toml` change and no code change. Do not ignore the advisories in `deny.toml`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `Cargo.lock` pins rustls-webpki 0.103.16 or newer and webpki-roots 1.0.10 or newer, and nothing else changes.
- `argc gate --all` passes, with `cargo deny` reporting advisories ok.

## Test Plan

- `argc gate --all`: the full test suite, including the recorded-HTTP replay tests, and cargo deny.
- No new test. The certificate path validation is the crates' own; the suite proves nothing else moved.

## Considerations

- Release builds embed the root store, so binaries built before this commit keep the affected roots until they are rebuilt.
- If a later advisory lands with no patched release, a `deny.toml` exception needs its own decision; it is not part of this fix.
acceptance_criteria: Cargo.lock pins rustls-webpki >= 0.103.16 and webpki-roots >= 1.0.10 with no other change; argc gate --all passes with cargo deny advisories ok
close_reason: Cargo.lock now pins rustls-webpki 0.103.16 and webpki-roots 1.0.10 (cargo update -p for both, nothing else moved). argc gate --all passes: 1592 tests passed, 0 failed, 53 ignored; cargo deny advisories ok, bans ok, licenses ok, sources ok.

comments.text: claim: Cargo.lock only (cargo update -p rustls-webpki -p webpki-roots), then argc gate --all

title: Scaffold the Cargo package, toolchain pin, lint config, deny.toml and local gate
description:
## Background

The vision bead (omad-vision-8qa, §5.12 and §7 M1 "Project and contract core") fixes the shape of the repository: a single Cargo package with a library and an `omaddons` binary, a pinned stable toolchain, strict lints, `deny.toml`, and one local command that runs the full quality gate (D16: no CI; every commit that changes code runs the gate first). Nothing else in M1 can start until the crate compiles and the gate exists, so this bead lands first and every other M1 bead depends on it.

## Technical Approach

- `Cargo.toml`: package `omaddons`, edition 2024, `publish = false`, `rust-version` equal to the pinned toolchain. `[lib]` plus `[[bin]] name = "omaddons"`.
- Lints in `[lints]`: `unsafe_code = "forbid"`; clippy `unwrap_used`, `expect_used`, `dbg_macro`, `print_stdout`, `print_stderr` denied. `clippy.toml` allows unwrap/expect inside `#[test]` code. Integration test crates that need unwrap in helpers add a crate-level `#![allow(...)]`. `print_stdout`/`print_stderr` enforce "commands never print": rendering goes through `src/output/` writing to locked handles via `std::io::Write`.
- Dependencies: every M1 crate from the §5.12 crate table is declared up front with the features the vision names (clap derive/env/wrap_help; serde; serde_json; toml; toml_edit; shell-words; ureq with rustls on the ring provider only; zip with deflate only; sha2; pelite; etcetera; fs4; rustix fs; reflink-copy; tempfile; ulid; jiff; thiserror; schemars). Dev-dependencies: insta, assert_cmd, predicates, proptest. Decided: declaring them once avoids parallel agents fighting over `Cargo.toml` and lets `cargo deny` vet the whole tree in one pass. Crates for later milestones (tar, zstd, sha1, md-5, clap_complete, clap_mangen) are added by the milestone that needs them.
- `rust-toolchain.toml`: pinned to an installed stable release with rustfmt and clippy. Decided: a pinned version instead of the floating `stable` channel so every agent builds with the same compiler.
- `rustfmt.toml` (style edition 2024) and `clippy.toml`.
- `deny.toml`: advisories, a permissive license allowlist (tuned until `cargo deny check` passes), crates.io as the only source, and bans that enforce D9 and the crate table: `openssl-sys`, `native-tls`, `aws-lc-rs`, `aws-lc-sys`, `reqwest`, `tokio`.
- Module skeleton: `src/lib.rs` declares the M1 modules from the §5.12 layout, each file holding only a `//!` doc comment stating its responsibility. Decided: declaring them now keeps parallel beads from colliding on `lib.rs`. `src/net/` is a directory rather than the single `net.rs` the layout shows, because it holds the Http trait, the ureq implementation, the allowlist, net.log, validators, retry and record/replay. Folder classification gets its own `src/inventory.rs`, which the layout does not list.
- The local gate: `Argcfile.sh` recipe `argc gate` calls `scripts/gate.sh`, which runs `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --locked`, `ubs` on changed files (staged, unstaged and untracked relative to HEAD, excluding `.beads/`), and `cargo deny check` only when `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock` or `deny.toml` changed (`--all` forces it).
- `.gitignore` for `target/`, fuzz outputs and coverage files.
- README.md v1 describing exactly what exists: the goal, the pre-alpha status, how to build, the gate, the layout, and where the plan lives.
- A "This Project" section in CLAUDE.md with the gate rule and the crate-level rules (fsx single writer, no printing outside `output`, no unwrap outside tests).

## Acceptance Criteria

- `cargo build` produces `target/debug/omaddons`, and running it exits 0.
- `argc gate --all` passes: fmt, clippy with `-D warnings`, tests, ubs and cargo deny.
- `cargo tree -i aws-lc-rs`, `cargo tree -i openssl-sys` and `cargo tree -i tokio` find nothing.
- `rust-toolchain.toml` pins an installed stable toolchain; `cargo --version` inside the repository reports it.
- README.md describes only what exists, and CLAUDE.md has a "This Project" section.
- No `.github/` directory exists (D16).

## Test Plan

- Unit: none (no logic yet).
- E2E: `tests/smoke.rs` runs the built binary with `assert_cmd` and asserts exit 0. The CLI skeleton bead replaces it with the bare-help contract test.
- Gate: run `argc gate --all` and record the output in the close reason.

## Considerations

- ureq's default features may pull in a crypto provider other than ring. Verify with `cargo tree` and disable default features where needed.
- The deny license allowlist must be the minimum the tree actually needs; widen it only in response to a concrete `cargo deny` rejection.
- `cargo deny check` fetches the advisory database over the network; the gate runs it only when dependency files change.
acceptance_criteria: cargo build produces target/debug/omaddons and running it exits 0; argc gate --all passes (fmt, clippy -D warnings, tests, ubs, cargo deny); cargo tree finds no aws-lc-rs, openssl-sys or tokio; rust-toolchain.toml pins an installed stable toolchain; README.md describes only what exists and CLAUDE.md has a This Project section; no .github/ directory exists
close_reason: Crate scaffold landed: lib + bin, toolchain pinned to 1.97.1, lints, deny.toml with D9 bans, M1 crates declared, module skeleton, argc gate, README v1, CLAUDE.md This Project section

title: update --all with names: the usage fix drops the first name
description:
## Background

`update`'s usage error for `--all` with addon names (`src/app/update.rs`, `check_args`) builds its fix with `crate::cli::without_flag(&fix_argv(&ctx.argv), "--all")`. `without_flag` is for flags that take a value: it also drops the token after the flag. `--all` is a boolean, so `omaddons update --all Foo` gets the fix `omaddons update`, which drops `Foo` and updates everything: the opposite of naming addons. `omaddons update Foo --all` gets the right fix, `omaddons update Foo`. Found while writing `adopt --apply <folder>`'s usage fix, which filters the boolean flag out instead.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install any addon on a client (`omaddons install gh:o/foo -t retail`).
2. Run `omaddons update --all Foo --json`.
3. The error is `usage`, and its `fix_argv` is `["omaddons", "update"]`: the name is gone. With `update Foo --all` it is `["omaddons", "update", "Foo"]`.

## Technical Approach

Add `crate::cli::without_switch(argv, flag)`, which drops only the flag token (and `--flag=` forms are not valid for a switch), next to `without_flag` in `src/cli.rs`. Use it in `update::check_args` and in `adopt`'s `Mode::of` (`src/app/adopt/apply.rs`), which filters `--apply` by hand today. Grep for other `without_flag` calls on boolean flags and switch them too.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `omaddons update --all Foo` fails `usage` with `fix_argv` `["omaddons", "update", "Foo"]`; `omaddons update Foo --all` gives the same.
- `adopt --apply Foo` keeps its fix `["omaddons", "adopt", "Foo"]`.
- `without_flag` keeps its meaning for valued flags (`--channel beta`).

## Test Plan

A unit test of `without_switch` in `src/cli.rs` (switch first, last, between names); an e2e assertion in `tests/update.rs` for both argument orders.
close_reason: update --all with names now suggests the names without --all

comments.author: CrimsonJasper
comments.text: done: cli::without_switch removes a valueless flag only (without_flag removed --all and the word after it, the first name); update's check_args uses it. Unit test in cli.rs; contract row update_all_with_names shows fix_argv [omaddons, update, weakauras]. Found by the M2 contract audit (omad-m2-updates-adoption-2hp.8.1).

title: Library unit tests do not compile in release: with_spec callers are not debug-gated
description:
## Background

`fsx::with_spec` (the in-process failpoint override) exists only in debug builds (`src/fsx/mod.rs` re-exports it under `cfg(debug_assertions)`, as every failpoint). Unit tests that call it are not gated the same way, so the library's unit tests do not compile in a release build. Nothing in the gate builds them in release, and the checkpoint builds only `--test perf` in release, so nothing fails today; but `cargo test --release` as a whole (or any future release-built unit test) cannot run.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `cargo test --release --lib --no-run`
2. It fails with `unresolved import crate::fsx::with_spec` in `src/engine/repair/commit.rs` (test module), `src/engine/repair/recover.rs` (test module) and `cannot find function with_spec` in `src/doctor/fix_runtime.rs` (`real_flow_rolls_back_on_a_step_error`).

## Technical Approach

Gate each test (or each test module's failpoint-dependent tests) that calls `with_spec` with `#[cfg(debug_assertions)]`, matching how the failpoint machinery itself is compiled. Prefer gating the individual tests, so the rest of each module still runs in release. Grep `src/` for every `with_spec` caller, not only the three above.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `cargo test --release --lib --no-run` compiles.
- Every test that uses `with_spec` still runs in the gate (debug build); none is deleted.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- Unit: no new tests; the existing failpoint tests keep running in debug.
- Build check: `cargo test --release --lib --no-run` exits 0.

## Considerations

- Do not make `with_spec` available in release: failpoints are debug-only by design.
- The checkpoint command (`cargo test --release --test perf -- --ignored …`) is unaffected either way.
acceptance_criteria: cargo test --release --lib --no-run compiles; every with_spec test still runs in the debug gate; argc gate passes

title: Test: retail 12.x refuses mainline TOCs below 120000
description:
## Background

This is the test companion of omad-retail-12-floor-e5a0: on a retail client at interface 120000 or higher, a mainline TOC below 120000 never loads, and omaddons must say so instead of calling it out of date. The floor is keyed on the client's interface across several rows (`mainline`, `mainline-12.0.7`, PTR, XPTR, beta), so the tests cover each edge.

## Technical Approach

- Unit tests on `judge` and `best_in_family` in the `src/toc/loaded.rs` test module.
- TOC-matrix rows in `tests/fixtures/toc/matrix/cases.toml`.
- Integration tests for install and for the on-disk verdict.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each case below is a test.
- Removing the floor fails the 110207-on-120105 case.

## Test Plan

- **`judge`:**
  - 110207 on a 120105 client: `WrongFlavor` with the floor reason;
  - 120000 on 120105: `out_of_date`;
  - `110207, 120105` on 120105: compatible;
  - 110207 on a 12.0.5 client (`mainline-12.0.7` row) and on 12.x PTR and beta clients: the floor applies;
  - 110207 on an 11.2 client (`mainline-10.2.7` row) and on a custom 11.x client: `out_of_date`, as today.
- **Install:** `omaddons install ./Foo.zip -t retail` with 110207 gives `wrong_flavor` naming the floor, and nothing is written.
- **On disk:**
  - a managed addon whose TOC is below the floor reads as not loading in `status` and update status;
  - an unmanaged one reads the same in `status --unmanaged`;
  - neither carries the "Load out of date AddOns" fix.
- **TOC matrix:** rows for each case above.

## Considerations

- The client interfaces come from the rows' version data (`src/rules.rs` test table, around line 1589). Reuse those values rather than inventing new ones.
acceptance_criteria: judge and TOC-matrix tests cover 110207, 120000 and a mixed list on 120105, the mainline-12.0.7, PTR and beta rows, and pre-12 clients unchanged; an install refusal naming the floor with nothing written; on-disk verdicts in status, update status and status --unmanaged without the out-of-date fix; removing the floor fails the 110207 case
close_reason: Every case of the test plan is a test: judge units, interface_floor matrix group (12 cases), install refusal with nothing written, skipped side folder, blocked update, list --unmanaged verdict without the out-of-date fix

title: In-source scanners stop at the first #[cfg(test)], as single_writer did
description:
## Background

omad-m2-audit-yegz.2.8 fixed tests/single_writer.rs, which stopped scanning a file at its first column-0 #[cfg(test)] and so never scanned src/net/mod.rs past its early `#[cfg(test)] mod tests;` (line 20). Five unit tests inside src/ scan source text the same way, with `text.split("#[cfg(test)]").next()`:

- src/engine/tx.rs (~1829): every failpoint::hit("engine.…") name across src/engine/.
- src/state/store.rs (~345): every `impl Versioned for` across src/.
- src/fsx/lock.rs (~362, ~384): lock_file references across src/, and forbidden calls in lock.rs itself.
- src/resolve/select.rs (~642): banned std::fs/std::net use in select.rs itself.
- src/state/paths.rs (~650): create_dir/canonicalize calls in paths.rs itself.

They also match inside comments and string literals, and a `#[cfg(test)]` written in a string (as these very scanners do) cuts the scan short. No miss exists today: the only file with production code after its first #[cfg(test)] is src/net/mod.rs, which holds no engine failpoint, no Versioned impl and no lock_file reference.

## Technical Approach

Give these scanners the production view single_writer now has: a small shared helper under src/ (cfg(test), e.g. src/testing/source.rs) with the lexer (comments dropped, literals blanked across lines) and test-item skipping, ported from tests/single_writer.rs (code_lines, production_code), used by all five. Alternative if the helper is judged too heavy: move src/net/mod.rs's `mod tests;` to the end of the file and add a guard test that no src file has production code after its first column-0 #[cfg(test)].

## Acceptance Criteria

- Each of the five scanners sees production code after an early `mod tests;` (a self-test with an in-memory probe, as single_writer's net/mod.rs test does).
- argc gate passes.
close_reason: The five in-source scanners read a production view of the source (comments dropped, test items blanked wherever they sit), so code after an early mod tests; is seen.

comments.author: CosmicKettle
comments.text: claim: shared cfg(test) source helper in src/, five in-source scanners (tx.rs, store.rs, lock.rs x2, select.rs, paths.rs)

comments.author: CosmicKettle
comments.text: done: src/source_scan.rs (#![cfg(test)], declared in lib.rs under cfg(test)): char-aligned lexer ported from tests/single_writer.rs, test-only items found on the literal-blanked view and blanked in either view, production_code(text, Literals::Keep|Blank) and sources(dir). Converted: engine/tx.rs failpoints_list_every_engine_failpoint (Keep, it reads the failpoint names in literals), state/store.rs versioned_impls, fsx/lock.rs lock_file references and forbidden calls, resolve/select.rs selection_does_no_io, state/paths.rs this_module_never_touches_the_filesystem (Blank). Probe tests: code_after_an_early_mod_tests_is_production (an early #[cfg(test)] mod tests;, a commented and a test-only failpoint, #[cfg(test)] inside a string, raw strings, char literals, line count and char count preserved), a_test_only_file_has_no_production_code, src_net_mod_rs_is_scanned_past_its_mod_tests (the real file). All five scanners pass unchanged results. decided: the shared helper (the bead's first approach) rather than moving net/mod.rs's mod tests; tests/single_writer.rs keeps its own copy, since an integration test cannot see cfg(test) code. argc gate passes. · found: none

title: Archive ratio guard rejects real textures just past the 1 MiB floor (Plater)
description:
## Background

The M1 checkpoint's live keyless install of Plater (gh:Tercioo/Plater-Nameplates, Plater-v660.zip) into retail failed with unsafe_archive: "Plater/images/transparent.tga expands 1048594 bytes from 1046, past the 200:1 compression ratio". The file is a legitimate 512x512 RGBA TGA (1 MiB of pixels plus an 18-byte header) that is almost entirely transparent, so it deflates about 1000:1. ARCHIVE_RATIO_FLOOR (1 MiB) exempts only entries up to exactly 1 MiB, so ordinary textures trip the zip-bomb guard.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. omaddons install plater -t retail --dry-run --json
2. error.details.tried[0].reason is unsafe_archive for Plater/images/transparent.tga.

## Technical Approach

Raise ARCHIVE_RATIO_FLOOR in src/limits.rs to 32 MiB: large enough for a 2048x2048 RGBA texture with its header, the largest texture an addon realistically ships uncompressed. Bombs stay bounded by ARCHIVE_MAX_UNCOMPRESSED (1 GiB total, counted while decompressing) and ARCHIVE_MAX_ENTRIES; the ratio still catches a bomb entry once it passes 32 MiB. Update the ratio-bomb fixture in tests/inspect.rs to expand past the new floor, and the limits registry snapshot.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An archive holding a 1 MiB + 18 byte highly compressible texture inspects cleanly.
- A deflated entry of zeros larger than 32 MiB is still refused with unsafe_archive (ratio).
- Plater installs into the development machine's retail target.

## Test Plan

- Regression test in tests/inspect.rs with the Plater-shaped texture.
- The ratio bomb case in hostile_entries_are_refused uses 40 MiB of zeros.
- Unit test ratios_apply_past_the_floor follows the constant.

## Considerations

- A higher floor lets a single bomb entry expand to 32 MiB before the ratio stops it; that is within every other bound.
acceptance_criteria: A 1 MiB + 18 byte compressible texture inspects cleanly; a deflated zero entry past 32 MiB is still unsafe_archive; Plater installs into the development machine's retail target
close_reason: ARCHIVE_RATIO_FLOOR raised to 32 MiB so real textures pass; bombs stay bounded

comments.author: BoldKettle
comments.text: claim: src/limits.rs, tests/inspect.rs, limits snapshot

comments.author: BoldKettle
comments.text: done: argc gate passes; tests/inspect.rs a_compressible_texture_is_not_a_bomb (1 MiB + 18 byte texture) passes, the 40 MiB ratio bombs in tests/inspect.rs and tests/engine_fallbacks.rs are still unsafe_archive; live: Plater-v660 installs into the development machine's retail target and a synthetic Forever target · found: none

title: Wire the failure-mode registry into the semantic manifest
description:
## Background

The semantic contract manifest (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.1.10, M4-D56) records every registry a consumer may switch on, as nodes in `src/contract/manifest/registries.rs`. §6.7 of the M4 plan lists the doctor's failure-mode ids among them. Section `fm <id>`, kind `failure_mode`, carries no facts: the id itself is the contract.

When A10 closed, E1 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1, which adds the `FAILURE_MODES` registry) was not on `main`. So the `fm` section is absent, and a golden committed without it would freeze a contract that lacks every failure-mode id. This task wires it, and H2 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.2) is blocked on it.

## Technical Approach

- In `registries::collect`, add one node per `FAILURE_MODES` id: `ids::registry(section::FAILURE_MODE, id)`, `NodeKind::FailureMode`, no facts.
- The classifier (`src/contract/manifest/classify.rs`) already labels a `failure_mode` added as additive and removed as breaking, and `wire::names` prints `fm <id>`. Neither changes.
- Remove `fm <id>` from the "not recorded yet" note in `registries.rs`'s module doc.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Every `FAILURE_MODES` id has an `fm <id>` node of kind `failure_mode`.
- `registries.rs` gains `failure_modes_are_recorded`.
- `tests/contract/manifest_report.rs` asserts the `fm` section's count equals `FAILURE_MODES.len()`.
- `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files.

## Test Plan

- **Unit:** `failure_modes_are_recorded` checks the ids and kinds against `FAILURE_MODES`.
- **Integration:** `manifest_report`'s count check gains the `fm` section, against its registry.
- **E2E:** none of its own. The manifest's end-to-end suite (`tests/e2e_manifest.rs`) is unaffected: registry nodes are not located from envelopes.

## Considerations

- Blocked by E1 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.5.1); blocks H2 (omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.8.2).
- The report test's previous-run comparison shows the new nodes as additive. That is the expected diff for this change.
acceptance_criteria: Every FAILURE_MODES id has an fm <id> node of kind failure_mode; failure_modes_are_recorded is added; manifest_report counts the fm section against FAILURE_MODES; argc gate passes and ubs is clean

title: Discovery offers Warcraft III (product w3) in the Battle.net prefix as a WoW target, warning unknown_flavor on every command
description:
## Background

On the development machine (2026-10-20), the Battle.net prefix also holds Warcraft III: Reforged, at `drive_c/Program Files (x86)/Warcraft III/` (it has its own `.build.info` and a `_retail_` flavor folder whose `.flavor.info` names product `w3`). Discovery's scan treats it as a WoW install. Every command then lists an unregistered target `retail@battlenet`:
- `product: "w3"`, `version: "3.0.1.24371"`, `interface: 30001`, `family: "unknown"`, `found_by: "scan"`, label "retail (battlenet)";
- every command, `status` and `list -t <other>` included, emits `unknown_flavor`: "retail@battlenet: flavor folder _retail_ runs version 3.0.1.24371, which no family covers; it is usable with permissive modern rules", with a fix suggesting `config set targets.retail@battlenet.family <family>`.

That warning is noise on every run. Worse, its fix invites the user to give a Warcraft III folder a WoW family, after which omaddons would install addons into it. README's first line promises omaddons manages addons "for every client"; a non-WoW Blizzard game is not a client.

The cause: `src/discover/battlenet.rs:30-60`. `is_battlenet_root` accepts any directory with a `.build.info`, and `discover_root` makes a target of every flavor folder, whatever its product. A product unknown to the rules table still becomes a target, which is deliberate for future WoW products (a new `wow_*` code), but it also admits other Blizzard games.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. In a Battle.net prefix with WoW, install another Blizzard game that uses the `_retail_` layout (Warcraft III: Reforged; also likely Diablo IV, Hearthstone, Overwatch).
2. Run `omaddons targets --json`: a `retail@battlenet` entry with that game's product code (`w3`) appears, `registered: false`.
3. Run any command: `unknown_flavor` is warned for it.

Unit-level: a fake prefix with `Program Files (x86)/Warcraft III/.build.info` and `_retail_/.flavor.info` naming `w3` yields a discovered target today.

## Technical Approach

- In `discover_root`, skip a flavor folder whose product is known and is not a WoW product. Define "WoW product" in one place: a code in the rules table's product list, or matching the `wow` prefix (`wow`, `wow_classic`, `wow_classic_era`, `wow_anniversary`, `wowt`, `wowf`, ...). `w3`, `fenris`, `hs_beta`, `pro`, `osi` and the like are skipped.
- A folder with no readable product (no `.flavor.info`, no hint) keeps today's behaviour, so an unusual WoW layout is still found.
- Alternatively, or in addition, require a WoW executable (`Wow.exe`, `WowClassic.exe`, `WowT.exe`, ...; the table's exe names) in the flavor folder. Prefer the product check: it reads only the file discovery already reads.
- Skip silently: no warning for a non-WoW game.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A Battle.net root whose flavor folders all name non-WoW products produces no target and no warning.
- A WoW root next to it is discovered exactly as before.
- A flavor folder with an unknown `wow*` product still becomes a target (with `unknown_flavor`), as today.
- On the development machine, `omaddons targets` no longer lists `retail@battlenet`, and `status` emits no `unknown_flavor`.

## Test Plan

- `tests/discover_*.rs`: a fake prefix with `World of Warcraft/` (`_retail_`, product `wow`) and `Warcraft III/` (`_retail_`, product `w3`): only the WoW target is discovered, no warning.
- Unknown `wow_future` product: still discovered, `unknown_flavor` warned.
- Unit test for the WoW-product predicate.
- The "nothing written" discovery assertions stay green.

## Considerations

- A user may already have run the suggested `config set targets.retail@battlenet.family …`. A registered or configured target must not vanish silently: if config names it, keep it and let the user remove it (or warn once that it is not a WoW product).
- The discovery cache may hold the stale target; check it is re-scanned.
- No personal data: product codes and folder names only.
acceptance_criteria: a Battle.net flavor folder whose product is known and not a WoW product yields no target and no warning; WoW roots beside it are discovered as before; unknown wow* products still become targets; configured targets do not vanish silently; discovery tests cover it
close_reason: discover_root skips a flavor folder whose readable product is not WoW's (RulesTable::is_wow_product: in the rules table, or a wow* code), silently; unreadable products stay targets; registered ones surface as target_missing; discovery cache PARSE_REVISION 3; README says so.

comments.author: ScarletThistle
comments.text: claim: src/rules.rs (WoW-product predicate), src/discover/battlenet.rs (skip non-WoW flavor folders), src/discover/cache.rs (PARSE_REVISION), tests/discover_*.rs

comments.author: ScarletThistle
comments.text: decided: skip by product, silently, in discover_root (src/discover/battlenet.rs), with the predicate in one place (RulesTable::is_wow_product: a product in the rules table, or any wow* code). What and why: a flavor folder whose product is readable and not WoW's is no client; a folder with no readable product stays a target, and a [rules] products entry can admit any code. How the bead's 'must not vanish silently' consideration is met: a target registered there by an earlier build is no longer discovered, so the registry keeps it and status raises target_missing with 'targets rm' as the fix (existing behaviour, tests/status.rs); a never-registered one only had a config family override at stake, and nothing installs without registering, so its override simply goes unused (no warning: README promises none for an unused override). Found while testing: on a fresh machine Warcraft III sorts before World of Warcraft and took the bare id retail, leaving WoW as retail@battlenet, so -t retail selected Warcraft III; the fix removes that too. Risk: a future WoW product whose code does not start with wow and is not in the table is skipped until a [rules] products entry or a release adds it. Discovery cache PARSE_REVISION bumped to 3 so cached w3 targets are re-parsed. README 'Where discovery looks' says so.

comments.author: ScarletThistle
comments.text: done: src/rules.rs is_wow_product (+ unit cases), src/discover/battlenet.rs, src/discover/cache.rs, README 'Where discovery looks'; tests/discover_matrix.rs another_blizzard_game_in_the_prefix_is_no_client failed before (Warcraft III took the bare id retail, WoW became retail@battlenet) and passes; unknown wow* products still targets (an_unknown_flavor_folder_is_a_usable_unknown_target green); on the development machine targets lists only the six WoW clients and status has no warnings; argc gate passed (1534 tests) · found: none

title: A committed install drops the out_of_date and toc_comma_on_legacy warnings its dry run reports
description:
## Background

README "Interface" rule (step 4 of the load rules) promises: "An older one gets an `out_of_date` warning, because the client loads it only with "Load out of date AddOns" enabled". The warning table lists `out_of_date` and `toc_comma_on_legacy` as install warnings.

During the omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.2 real-client load check (2026-10-20), OmniCC 11.2.8 was installed into the retail client (12.1.5, interface 120105). Its TOCs carry `## Interface: 110207, 50503, 38000, 20505, 11508`, so the retail client treats it as out of date. The client did not load it: Bartender4 and DBM, installed in the same transaction, wrote their SavedVariables at logout, and OmniCC wrote no `OmniCC.lua`. `checkAddonVersion` was at its default (not in `Config.wtf`).

The dry run warned, the committed install did not:
- `omaddons install omnicc -t retail --dry-run --json` emits two `out_of_date` warnings (OmniCC, OmniCC_Config).
- `omaddons install omnicc -t retail --json` (same plan, committed) emits none; its envelope and stderr events hold only unrelated warnings.
- The same happened with `toc_comma_on_legacy` on a 3.3.5a install of a TOC with `## Interface: 30300, 30400` (omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.6): the dry run warned, the commit did not.

So a user who installs without `--dry-run` is never told an addon will not load. After the install, `status`, `list` and `info` show nothing either (`state: ok`, no attention). README does not promise those do, so this bead is about the install output only.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On a mainline 12.x target with OmniCC not installed: `omaddons install omnicc -t retail --dry-run --json 2>&1 >/dev/null | jq -c .code` prints `out_of_date` twice.
2. `omaddons install omnicc -t retail --json 2>&1 >/dev/null | jq -c .code` prints no `out_of_date`, and `jq '[.. | objects | .code?] '` over stdout has none either.
3. `omaddons undo <tx>` to clean up.

## Technical Approach

Likely cause: the commit path in `src/engine/tx.rs` (around `:760-840`, the revalidation loop) seeds `warnings` from `tp.unchanged_warnings` and adds each `rejudge` result's `p.warnings`. `rejudge` replans with `downloads: &no_downloads` and `indexes: None`. The planner's `judge` (`src/engine/plan.rs:3860`) returns only ownership and running-policy warnings, so the TOC verdict warnings that `inspect::verify` attached at plan time (`src/toc/loaded.rs:388-424`) to changed works are not carried over. The dry-run outcome (`src/engine/tx.rs:~456`) returns `tp.warnings` whole, which is why it differs.

Fix: carry the plan-time verdict warnings of every work that still commits into the commit outcome (de-duplicated with `push_new`), or have `rejudge` re-derive them from the staged folders. Prefer the first: the folders committed are the ones that were judged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A committed install, update, sync or copy reports the same `out_of_date` and `toc_comma_on_legacy` warnings as its dry run, for every folder it adds or replaces.
- Text output shows them too (the warnings render as they do for the dry run).
- A work dropped at revalidation (a concurrent transaction did it) does not report its plan-time warnings.

## Test Plan

- Integration (`tests/install_*.rs` or the existing TOC-warning tests): install a fixture addon whose TOC interface is older than the target's, once with `--dry-run` and once committed; assert both envelopes carry `out_of_date` for each folder.
- Same for a legacy target and a comma-list TOC (`toc_comma_on_legacy`).
- Update path: an update to an out-of-date build warns when committed.
- Existing dry-run warning tests stay green.

## Considerations

- De-duplicate: a warning present in both `tp.unchanged_warnings` and a work's plan warnings must appear once.
- `--strict` semantics: check whether warnings affect `partial` or exit 6; they should behave the same as in the dry run.
- The catalog note for OmniCC ("out of date on 12.x") was added in the same session; it does not replace the warning.
acceptance_criteria: a committed install, update, sync or copy reports the same out_of_date and toc_comma_on_legacy warnings as its dry run for every folder it adds or replaces, in JSON and text; works dropped at revalidation report none; integration tests cover install and update, modern and legacy
close_reason: The commit carries every warning checking the archive gave at plan time: FolderWork.unverified became archive_warnings (TOC verdicts out_of_date and toc_comma_on_legacy, plus download_unverified), set in build and passed by rejudge to build_install exactly as planning did, so a committed install, update, sync or copy reports them in the same order as its dry run; a work dropped at revalidation reports none.

comments.author: ScarletThistle
comments.text: claim: src/engine/tx.rs (commit-path warnings), src/engine/plan.rs, tests for out_of_date / toc_comma_on_legacy on committed installs

comments.author: ScarletThistle
comments.text: done: src/engine/plan.rs (FolderWork.archive_warnings, build, rejudge); tests/install.rs a_committed_install_warns_out_of_date_as_its_dry_run_does (JSON and human stderr events) and a_committed_legacy_install_warns_toc_comma_on_legacy_as_its_dry_run_does (3.3.5a); tests/update.rs an_update_warns_what_its_new_tocs_say_as_its_dry_run_does (retail and 3.3.5a in one run); tests/engine_concurrency.rs a_work_dropped_at_revalidation_reports_none_of_its_plan_warnings; all four failed before the fix; argc gate passed (1532 tests). Note: across several targets a dry run reports warnings in plan order and commits in key order (tx.rs commit ordering), unchanged and not promised by README · found: none

title: omaddons vision, architecture and milestone roadmap (M1–M5)
description:
# omaddons — vision, architecture, milestone roadmap

Living document. Body revision 2, 2026-10-14. This revision incorporates:
- the decisions recorded as comments: D16 (no CI, local gate) and D17–D22 (CLI contract, exit codes, discovery surfaces, doctor, wire-name pinning, politeness constants);
- revision set 2: 28 changes, logged in §11.

Comments added after this revision supersede the body where they conflict. External facts were verified on 2026-10-14 unless marked UNVERIFIED.

## 1. Thesis

`omaddons` is a single Rust binary that is the sole authority over every World of Warcraft client on a Linux machine. That covers:
- Battle.net under Wine/Proton/umu (Omarchy's default);
- Steam, Lutris, Heroic and Bottles prefixes;
- custom private-server clients: 1.12.1, 2.4.3, 3.3.5a (AzerothCore), 4.3.4 and 5.4.8.

It discovers every client and manages addons per client (a "target") through one journaled transaction engine. Everything is exposed through a stable, machine-readable CLI contract. Coding agents drive the CLI directly. Humans use a thin Omarchy bar widget that renders CLI output and holds no logic of its own.

Every mutation is a transaction: install, update, remove, adopt, sync, backup restore and doctor repair. Each one is snapshotted, attributed to an actor, and reversible with `omaddons undo`.

Framing: **the CLI is the product, the widget is a view, the agent skill is the manual.**

## 2. Goals and non-goals

Goals:
- **G1 Multi-target.** All installed flavors are managed simultaneously: retail, progression Classic, Classic Era, Anniversary, Forever, PTR/XPTR/beta. Custom and legacy clients are first-class targets with stable identities.
- **G2 Zero-config, keyless by default.** Discovery needs no setup. The most-used addons install and update without any account. CurseForge and Wago are optional bring-your-own-credential sources; nothing depends on them.
- **G3 Reliability.**
  - No operation can leave an addon half-installed.
  - Crashes recover, and only a process that provably holds the lock repairs anything.
  - Widget, terminal and agent can mutate concurrently, because the lock is held only for milliseconds.
  - Upstream schema drift yields typed errors, never crashes or unparseable output.
- **G4 Agent-first ergonomics.**
  - The first command an agent guesses works.
  - Under `--json`, stdout carries exactly one envelope, success or failure.
  - Every error carries an executable fix (a display string plus `argv`).
  - Plans are stored: a dry run can be applied exactly.
  - Every change is attributed to an actor.
  - Discovery via `capabilities`, `doctor` and `robot-docs`.
  - The skill is installed where agents look. Output is token-frugal.
- **G5 Verifiable privacy.** Hard host allowlist (redirects included), a local request log that also covers git subprocesses, `--offline`, no telemetry, no CurseForge or Wago data persisted.
- **G6 Correct by the game's rules.** Client capabilities (`ClientRules`) are applied to the actual archive contents. Folder identity is case-insensitive, matching Wine.
- **G7 Diagnostics and recovery.**
  - `doctor` follows the world-class doctor contract.
  - Lua errors captured by BugGrabber are attributed to addons.
  - Required dependencies are resolved.
  - `WTF/` can be backed up and restored.
- **G8 Omarchy-native widget** following the house plugin pattern, always version-locked to the binary.

Non-goals:
- No standalone GUI or TUI, no daemon, no MCP server in v1. The command layer returns typed results, so an MCP adapter would be a thin later addition.
- No WeakAuras/Wago string management, no ElvUI profile management, no SavedVariables editing.
  - Whole-`WTF/` backup and restore is in scope; backups never parse or edit contents.
  - `errors` reads BugGrabber's SavedVariables file read-only.
- No Windows or macOS support. Code may stay portable but is untested and unsupported.
- No CurseForge proxy, no bundled API keys.
- No addon authoring or packaging.
- No CI, public distribution or public installer while the repository is private (D16).

## 3. Reference project audit

Reference: https://github.com/BabaStardust/Omarchy-WoW-Addons-Plugin at commit 5c35a8f (v1.1.1, MIT). It is an Omarchy bar widget (`Panel.qml`, ~1000 lines of QML) plus `bin/wowaddons` (750 lines of stdlib Python) calling CurseForge API v1 with a user-supplied key.

The audit found no telemetry or malicious behavior. Network traffic is limited to api.curseforge.com, the CurseForge CDN, and xdg-open of user-clicked links.

Ideas worth keeping:
- argv-only process invocation (no shell);
- the API key passed via stdin and stored mode 0600 with atomic writes;
- zip path-traversal checks and checksum verification;
- honoring `allowModDistribution=false` with a manual-download flow;
- `Text.PlainText` rendering of all API strings in QML.

Defects this design must fix (line references into `bin/wowaddons` / `Panel.qml` at 5c35a8f):

| R1 | One AddOns dir resolved by glob plus a folder-name guess; only `*forever*`/`*classic_beta*` folders are auto-picked (`resolve()`, l.132-149). A comment promises a classic fallback that is not implemented | A retail-only install resolves to `no-flavor`. Custom layouts (`drive_c/WoW`) are never detected | Discovery from `product.db`, `.build.info`, `.flavor.info`, drive mappings, launcher configs and PE version; many targets with stable keys (§5.2) |

A JSONDecodeError surfaces as "Invalid argument" | Typed error model; one stdout envelope under `--json` even on panic (§5.9) |
| R4 | Read-modify-write of `installed.json` without a lock, using a fixed `.tmp` name (`write_json`, l.99-105) | A concurrent widget and CLI/agent can lose updates or clobber the temp file | The fsx single writer; flock held for the commit window only; per-target generations; unique temp + rename for every write |
| R5 | Zip top-level directories used verbatim (l.331) | `Foo-main/` and `Foo-main/Foo/` layouts install broken | Addon-root detection by TOC; name normalization |
| R6 | File choice = max fileId per gameVersionTypeId; default releaseType 3 = alpha (l.47, l.237-247) | Alpha builds by default; no check that the client will load the file | Pure selection + TOC verification against `ClientRules`; stable channel by default |
| R7 | CurseForge-only with a mandatory key; caches CurseForge search results (l.436-495) | Useless without a CF console key. CF terms forbid caching API data, and say non-developer console accounts may be deleted | Keyless-first; CF opt-in; CF/Wago archives and responses never cached |

| R9 | Unmanaged addons are only listed. `Blizzard_*` folders in custom clients appear as unmanaged | No adoption; protected folders exposed to mutation | Tiered adoption; `Blizzard_*` protected by a case-insensitive key at the type level |

Language note: most improvements come from design, not language. Rust is chosen for:
- a self-contained binary with no interpreter dependency;
- ~1–2 ms startup for the high-frequency widget and agent calls;
- type-level enforcement of safety invariants: folder keys that cannot escape AddOns or name protected folders, a closed filesystem `Op` enum, exhaustive error mapping;
- simple bounded concurrency.

## 4. Verified external facts

### 4.1 Battle.net installs

- **Omarchy's install.** Omarchy installs Battle.net via umu-launcher + GE-Proton into `WINEPREFIX=~/Games/battlenet` (`omarchy-install-gaming-battlenet`) and launches it with `omarchy-launch-battlenet`. The WoW root is `~/Games/battlenet/drive_c/Program Files (x86)/World of Warcraft/`.
- **`product.db`.** The Battle.net Agent keeps a protobuf database at `<prefix>/drive_c/ProgramData/Battle.net/Agent/product.db`.
  - On the development machine it contains the install path `C:/Program Files (x86)/World of Warcraft`, the flavor `_retail_` and the version `12.1.0.69933`.
  - The field layout follows WowUp's reader and is UNVERIFIED. A tolerant wire-format reader is sufficient.
- **Drive letters.** `<prefix>/dosdevices/<letter>:` symlinks map Windows drive letters to Linux paths. The development machine has `c: → ../drive_c`, `s: → /home`, `w: → /mnt`, `x: → ~`, `z: → /`. A game installed on another letter lives outside `drive_c`.
- **`<root>/.build.info`** is BPSV: one header row of pipe-separated `Name!TYPE:size` columns, then one row per installed product.
  - Columns have changed over the years (KeyService, KeyRing and Product were added later), so **parse by header name, never by position**.
  - Relevant columns: `Product`, `Version` (e.g. `12.1.5.70391`), `Active` (`1`), `Branch` (`us`/`eu`), `Tags` (contains spaces, `?` and `:`).
  - Example header: `Branch!STRING:0|Active!DEC:1|Build Key!HEX:16|CDN Key!HEX:16|Install Key!HEX:16|IM Size!DEC:4|CDN Path!STRING:0|CDN Hosts!STRING:0|CDN Servers!STRING:0|Tags!STRING:0|Armadillo!STRING:0|Last Activated!STRING:0|Version!STRING:0|KeyRing!HEX:16|Product!STRING:0`.
  - Format reference: https://wowdev.wiki/TACT
- **`.flavor.info`.** Each flavor folder `<root>/_<x>_/` contains `.flavor.info` (BPSV header `Product Flavor!STRING:0`, value = product code). It is the authoritative folder → product mapping.
- **Products.** From Blizzard productconfig `shared_container_default_subfolder`, mirrored at https://github.com/Arctium/bnet-tact-channel-configs. Prior art: instawow `wow_installations.py`, WowUp `warcraft-platform.linux.ts`.
