comments.author: CosmicKettle
comments.text: §5.5 Retention (omad-m2-audit-yegz.6.5 item 22): blobs are pinned for installed releases only (src/engine/retention.rs, as README Retention promises); undo uses snapshots, never blobs, so retained transactions need no blob pin, and the LRU already evicts their blobs last. Plans are M4. This departs from the body's 'Blobs referenced by retained transactions, installed records or unexpired plans are pinned' on purpose: pinning retained transactions' blobs would let heavy setups exceed the 1 GiB cache cap by far, for the sole benefit of skipping a re-download on an explicit install --version <old>.

comments.author: SunnyLynx
comments.text:
Real-client observations, 2026-10-20 (omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.2 and omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.6). Supersedes the UNVERIFIED notes named below; the body is not edited.

**§4.4/§8, AddOns.txt (modern format).** Retail 12.1.5, Classic Era 1.15.9, Anniversary 2.5.6 and Mists 5.5.4 keep `WTF/Account/<account>/<realm>/<character>/AddOns.txt` as plain `<Folder>: enabled` (or `disabled`) lines, no header or other structure. The client does not add a newly installed addon to it: after installs and a logged-in session on three clients, no AddOns.txt was rewritten. The 3.3.5a client had no AddOns.txt at all. So AddOns.txt records only toggles made in the AddOns screen. It is neither load evidence nor a list of installed addons. The SavedVariables files are the load evidence.

**§4.4/§8, "Load out of date AddOns".** `checkAddonVersion` and `lastAddonVersion` appear in neither `WTF/Config.wtf` nor any `config-cache.wtf` on retail, Era, Anniversary or 3.3.5a, with the checkbox never touched. On 3.3.5a, `GetCVar("checkAddonVersion")` returned `"1"` in game: the CVar exists and is written only when it differs from the default. Where a modern client stores a non-default value stays not located (UNVERIFIED).

**§4.2/§4.4, legacy reload (3.3.5a only).** A new addon folder is not seen until the client restarts: a probe installed while the game ran never loaded across three `/reload`s. A loaded addon's TOC *is* re-read on `/reload`: a replacement adding a Lua file to the TOC ran after one `/reload`. The `safe` policy's "refuse every legacy change" is therefore stricter than needed for replacements (follow-up omad-ht23). Other legacy builds remain unobserved.

**§8, comma Interface lists on legacy.** 3.3.5a loaded a TOC with `## Interface: 30300, 30400`, with `checkAddonVersion` on (`GetAddOnInfo` reason nil). omaddons' reading (leading integer, `toc_comma_on_legacy` warning, not a refusal) is confirmed for 3.3.5a.

**TOC-verified installs load** on retail (Bartender4, DBM), Classic Era and Anniversary (Bartender4, Questie, DBM) and 3.3.5a (GroupBulletinBoard): each wrote its declared SavedVariables at logout. OmniCC 11.2.8 (Interface 110207) did not load on retail 12.1.5. That is the out-of-date case the rules predict, but the committed install dropped the `out_of_date` warning its dry run reports (omad-vaeg). Mists Classic and Forever are still unobserved: their realms were unavailable that night.

comments.author: SunnyLynx
comments.text:
§4.8/§8: Wine process naming observed under umu-launcher and GE-Proton 11-11 (pressure-vessel) on 2026-10-20, one client at a time (omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.1). Supersedes "UNVERIFIED under Proton/umu".

- **The client's `comm` is its exe name, spelled as the exe:** `WoW.exe` (retail), `WoWClassic.exe` (Era, Anniversary, Mists Classic), `Wow.exe` (3.3.5a). No loader name, no rename after startup: sampled at +30 s and +120 s, and every 2 s for 6 min on Mists. The 15-byte cap is real: `WowVoiceProxy.exe` shows as `WowVoiceProxy.e`. `/proc/<pid>/exe` is `wine64-preloader` (`wine-preloader` for 32-bit 3.3.5a), so only `comm` and `cmdline` identify the game.
- **argv[0] is the Windows exe path** (`C:\Program Files (x86)\World of Warcraft\_retail_\WoW.exe -launcherlogin -uid wow`, `C:\WoW\Wow.exe`), and it maps through `dosdevices` to the exact client dir. Era and Anniversary were attributed exactly despite sharing `WoWClassic.exe` and one prefix (`ExePath`, never `PrefixOnly`).
- **`WINEPREFIX` is `<prefix>/pfx/`:** umu creates `pfx -> .` in the prefix, and sets it with a trailing slash. umu-run itself carries `<prefix>`. The process route now canonicalizes it. Before the fix, a running client made discovery scan its own prefix a second time, qualified `pfx`.
- **Same PID namespace and root as the host:** pressure-vessel does not containerize `/proc`, and host paths are valid.
- **The Battle.net app runs as `CrBrowserMain`/`CrGpuMain`/`CrUtilityMain`/`CrRendererMain`** (Chromium thread names), not `Battle.net.exe` (omad-c8ni). `Agent.exe` keeps its name; its argv[0] uses forward slashes.
- **Wine pads `cmdline`** of its processes with many trailing empty arguments.
- **3.3.5a runs under umu in its own prefix** (`~/Games/wow-335`, `pfx` symlink alike), not a separate Wine runner.

comments.author: ScarletThistle
comments.text: §5.5 running policy, revised by omad-ht23 (DEC-4; supersedes 'safe refuses every legacy change'). What: ClientRules gains reload_rereads_toc (whether a running client re-reads a loaded addon's TOC and files on /reload): true for every modern row and fallback-battlenet, and for wrath-legacy; false for vanilla-legacy, tbc-legacy, cata-legacy, mists-legacy and fallback-custom. It is a [client_rules.<row>] field like the others (config key list and README updated). Under safe, an op lands while the client runs when it drops no loaded TOC and is a replacement on a row that re-reads TOCs, or an add or a remove on a row that is not legacy. So modern clients are unchanged; on a running 3.3.5a client a replacement keeping its loaded TOC now lands with reload_required reload, while an add or remove is refused as legacy_client ('this client needs a restart to see a new addon folder (…); a replacement that keeps its loaded TOC needs only /reload') and a dropped loaded TOC as loaded_toc; the other legacy rows refuse every change with legacy_client as before. Under allow or --while-running, a 3.3.5a replacement reports reload instead of restart. Why: the real 3.3.5a client (12340) ran a loaded addon's new Lua file after one /reload and saw a new folder only after a restart (omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.6, 2026-10-20). Risks: observed on one stock build and one server; a patched Wow.exe could differ (a [client_rules.wrath-legacy] reload_rereads_toc = false override restores the old rule); other legacy builds stay strict until observed (omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.5). Tests: src/engine/running.rs the_policy_table (modern, legacy and 3.3.5a rows) and a_legacy_refusal_says_what_needs_the_restart; tests/install.rs a_running_3_3_5a_client_takes_a_replacement_on_reload_but_not_a_new_addon; tests/update.rs running_clients_follow_the_running_policy (retail and 3.3.5a update with reload, 1.12.1 refused).

comments.author: CobaltZephyr
comments.text:
Real-client observations, 2026-10-21 (omad-classic-forever-gaps-xud.6 and omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.2). These complete comment 898, which left Mists Classic and Forever unobserved; the body is not edited.

**TOC-verified installs load** on Mists Classic 5.5.4.70531 (Bartender4, Questie, DBM) and on the Forever stress-test client 1.60.1.70532, interface 16001 (Bartender4, BigWigs, DBM, Plater, Questie). Every addon wrote its declared SavedVariables at logout, account-wide and per character. That makes every Battle.net client on the development machine, plus 3.3.5a, observed loading omaddons installs.

**§4.3, Forever TOC suffix.** The real Forever client reads _Camelot:
- Plater's SavedVariables carry 'Plater-v661-Forever', the ## Version of Plater_Camelot.toc; its plain TOC is the retail one.
- Questie loaded although its plain Questie.toc says Interface 00000.
- Still unobserved: _Forever alone, and the client's order when an addon ships both. QuestieDB's _Forever and _Camelot TOCs are byte-identical, so its load says nothing about the order.
- The forever rules row stays as it is ([Forever, Camelot]).

**§4.4, AddOns.txt, refining comment 898.** On Forever, WTF/ did not exist before the session. The client created AddOns.txt on that first login, and it listed every installed folder (12 lines, '<Folder>: enabled', no header). So a client lists all present addons when it creates the file. After that it records only toggles: on Mists Classic, an AddOns.txt written before the install was not rewritten. Neither case is load evidence; the SavedVariables files are.

**§4.4/§8, Load out of date AddOns.** There is no checkAddonVersion or lastAddonVersion line in Config.wtf or config-cache.wtf on Mists Classic or Forever either. On Forever, WTF/SavedVariables/Blizzard_AddOnList.lua holds only g_addonCategoriesCollapsed. Storage stays not located (UNVERIFIED).

comments.author: CobaltZephyr
comments.text:
**Addenda and corrections to earlier comments, from the close of the post-M2 audit (omad-m2-audit-yegz).**

- Comment 701 (omad-m2-audit-yegz.2.1): the undo `state_corrupt` refusal carries `details.tx` and `details.reason: "snapshot_mismatch"`, with fix `omaddons undo <tx> --saved-variables keep`. README's error table states it.
- Comment 744: `FolderWork.unverified` was renamed `archive_warnings` by omad-vaeg (commit 75eac6a). A committed install, update, sync or copy now reports `out_of_date`, `toc_comma_on_legacy` and `download_unverified` as its dry run does.
- Comment 696: the "silently ignored until yegz.4.9" note is superseded; see the `[rules]` validation comment.
- Comment 898: omad-vaeg, listed there as open, is fixed (75eac6a).
- Comment 903: omad-c8ni is fixed (c216600); see the discovery comment.

comments.author: CobaltZephyr
comments.text:
**Pasted GitHub links (omad-m2-audit-yegz.3.2 and omad-m2-audit-yegz.3.10).** DEC-4 contract addition, before the M4 freeze; adds to §5.4's ref forms. Recorded at the close of the post-M2 audit (omad-m2-audit-yegz), which found it missing.

- What: each path segment of a github.com link is percent-decoded once. A tag spans every segment after `releases/tag`, or every segment but the file after `releases/download`, so `/` and `+` in tags work as GitHub writes them. A tag the GitHub source would refuse, a bad file name, or a download link with no file is `ref_invalid` before any request.
- A github.com link that names no repository (`https://github.com/o`) is `ref_invalid` (exit 2, fix `omaddons help install`). It used to become a `url:` ref that downloaded an HTML page.
- README "Sources and refs" documents both (commit 7f42a14).

comments.author: CobaltZephyr
comments.text:
**`[rules]` validation (omad-m2-audit-yegz.4.9).** DEC-4 behaviour change; adds to §5.6 config.toml and completes comment 696, which said the removed keys were "silently ignored until yegz.4.9".

- What: every unknown key under `[rules]` and `[client_rules]` warns `config_unknown_key`, with a did-you-mean from the same table. Array elements are named by index (`rules.products[0].nmae`). The removed ClientRules fields `game` and `path_variables` now warn instead of being ignored.
- No new code or key (commit 2a15df9). README "Rules overrides (advanced)" documents it.

comments.author: CobaltZephyr
comments.text:
**§5.2 discovery: non-WoW Battle.net products and the Battle.net app's agent (omad-v1u0, omad-c8ni).** DEC-4 behaviour; completes comment 903, which recorded the c8ni observation but not the rule.

- Non-WoW products (v1u0, commit 0349bc9): a Battle.net flavor folder whose readable product is not WoW's is skipped without a warning. A product is WoW's when the rules table lists it or its code starts with `wow`. Warcraft III: Reforged's `_retail_` (product `w3`) is the case found. A folder whose product cannot be read stays a target, and a registered one whose product turns out not to be WoW's surfaces as `target_missing`. The discovery cache's parse revision is 3.
- The Battle.net app (c8ni, commit c216600): the app runs as `CrBrowserMain` under Wine, so the process route also counts `Agent.exe` whose argv[0] lies under `ProgramData/Battle.net/Agent/`. A prefix found that way is remembered (`found_by: remembered`).
- Observed 2026-10-21 under umu with GE-Proton 11-11, with the app alone open: the agent's environment carries `WINEPREFIX`, set to the umu `pfx` path, which is a link to the prefix root. The route's assumption holds. The prefix path must be canonicalized, which omad-9p2l already does. README "Known limitations" now states this.

comments.author: CobaltZephyr
comments.text:
**§5.5 journal warnings describe the end state (omad-m2-audit-yegz.1.12).** DEC-4 behaviour; completes comment 680's note.

- What: a command's journal warnings describe the state when it finishes. A journal it recovered appears only as `journal_recovered`, never also as `journal_pending`. One it could not recover, or one a dry run or read command saw, stays `journal_pending` (`tx_in_progress` while another process holds the global lock).
- No new code (commit ec32c64). README "Safety model, Interrupted runs" documents it.

comments.author: CobaltZephyr
comments.text:
**§5.9 fixes for refs that name nothing installable (omad-install-unknown-name-search-jw4i, omad-github-no-releases-message-wvw1).** DEC-4 behaviour; adds to comments 827 and 832. No new codes.

- Unknown name (jw4i, commit 7730b9a): a bare name that is neither installed nor in the catalog stays `not_found`, now with fix_argv `omaddons search <name>` (no request is sent) and alternative `omaddons help install`.
- GitHub with no stable release (wvw1, commit a4d851c): when `releases/latest` redirects to the release list, the error is `no_compatible_release` "has no stable release (only prereleases, or none published)", with fix `--channel beta` and the repository's `git:` ref as alternative. When it answers 404, the error is `not_found` "has no GitHub releases (or the repository does not exist)", with the `git:` ref as fix. An empty REST release list is `no_compatible_release` "has no published releases", with the `git:` ref as fix.
- README "Sources and refs" (Channels) and the error table document these.

comments.author: CobaltZephyr
comments.text:
**§5.9 global flags: `--dry-run` and `--reason` everywhere (omad-m2-audit-yegz.5.18).** DEC-4 contract change; supersedes the synopsis' "--dry-run (mutating)".

- What: every command accepts `--dry-run` and `--reason`. A command that changes nothing ignores both, so an agent can pass them uniformly. The help text says so (commit c19c4d5).
- The contract suite checks every read-only command accepts and ignores them. README "Global options" documents it.

comments.author: FierceWren
comments.text: D13 (DEC-4) amended by omad-ck0h: the HTTP and git allowlists are now disjoint by enforcement, not only by construction. config validation refuses a git_hosts entry that is any HTTP host (the always-list and every optional source's hosts, enabled or not, in any case): config set is a usage error, and a hand-edited config.toml that lists one fails to load (state_corrupt naming the host, line and key; fix: remove it). GitHosts::new also drops such hosts, so a config that bypassed validation never lets git reach one. A git: ref to an HTTP host is still host_blocked, and its fix is prose (use a gh:, url:, wowi: or tukui: ref), never a config set git_hosts that would list it.

comments.author: FierceWren
comments.text:
**§5.11 Omarchy widget, as shipped in M3 (omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.5.1 to omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.5.4, E1 to E4; omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.1 to omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.10, F1 to F9 and the spike F0).** Supersedes §5.11, and the house-plugin notes of §4.6 where they differ; the body is not edited. The departures M3-D2 (argv sources), M3-D4 (the doorbell), M3-D8 (enable by default), M3-D9 with M3-D46 (previews bind) and M3-D10 (settings) are stated in the M3 decomposition comment; this comment gives the widget's whole shipped design. The Omarchy and Quickshell facts behind it were observed by F0 (omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.10) on Omarchy 4.0.6, Quickshell 0.3.2 and Hyprland 0.56.2.

**What.** An Omarchy plugin, id `a44.omaddons`, embedded in the binary and installed by `omaddons omarchy install`. One gamepad button on every monitor's bar shows the pending updates and turns urgent for problems and new Lua errors; a keyboard panel holds five views. The widget renders `--json` envelopes and runs omaddons command lines, so each change it makes is an ordinary CLI change with `--actor widget`, in history and undoable. It holds no product logic and writes no file (M3-D3). Its sources are in `omarchy/`: `manifest.json`, `Service.qml`, `BarWidget.qml`, `PanelView.qml`, `RestoreChooser.qml`, `PlainLabel.qml`, `Model.js` (every decision that is not drawing, tested with bun), `Store.js` and `views/{Updates,Installed,Issues,Backups,Search}View.qml`; `src/omarchy/assets.rs` embeds them, and install adds a generated `Build.js`. §5.11's `Panel.qml` does not exist.

**The service kind and the two-monitor finding (M3-D5).**
- The manifest declares `kinds: ["service", "bar-widget"]` with `entryPoints` `{"service": "Service.qml", "barWidget": "BarWidget.qml"}`, `allowMultiple: false` and `defaultSection: "right"`, and leaves `keepLoaded` out (false).
- Omarchy mounts a service once per shell and a bar widget once per monitor; the development machine has two monitors. Only one `IpcHandler` per target works (a second logs "Handler was registered but will not be used"). So the service owns every process, timer and watcher, the Hyprland connection, the notifications and the IPC target, and each bar copy owns nothing (`manageIpc: false`). F0 saw one service and one working handler with two monitors.
- Binding: the service is created before the widgets, but `bar.shell.serviceFor(Build.PLUGIN_ID)` is still null in a copy's `Component.onCompleted`. A copy therefore takes `Store.get()` first (`Store.js`, a `.pragma library` the service sets on completion and clears on destruction), rebinds through `serviceFor` on `barChanged`, and retries every 200 ms while unbound. Services receive no settings, so each copy pushes its `settings` and its panel's open state into the service.
- Hot reload (F0): any file event under `<plugins>` reloads every plugin widget. A reload SIGKILLs the service's children (their own children survive, orphaned), and children share the shell's process group, so the widget signals a pid, never a group. A reload never recompiles code whose file URL is unchanged, and `.pragma` modules keep their state; that is why install puts the code at new URLs (below). With `keepLoaded: true`, a reinstall would run new widgets against the old service until a shell restart.

**Inert manifest defaults, and the settings.** Omarchy 4.0.6 neither renders nor applies `barWidget.defaults` or `barWidget.schema`. Enabling writes only `{"id": …}` into `<config-omarchy>/shell.json`, and disabling deletes the entry with any settings in it. So `Model.js` holds `DEFAULT_SETTINGS`, which a bun test keeps equal to the manifest's defaults, and `Model.setting` checks every value against `SETTING_RULES`, replacing a missing, wrong-typed or out-of-range one with its default. The six settings are `binary` (`""` runs the stamped binary; otherwise an absolute path), `panelWidth` (400 to 800, 540), `autoCheck` (On), `notifyUpdates` (Off), `notifyErrors` (On) and `refreshIntervalSec` (30 to 3600, 300). They are set with `omarchy bar set a44.omaddons <key> <value>`; the widget never writes `shell.json`. `omarchy remove` reports `settings_dropped` when Omarchy deleted them with the entry.

**The panel and the reserved keys.**
- The panel is a `qs.Ui` `KeyboardPanel` with a `PanelKeyCatcher`, `panelWidth` wide and at most 720 units tall. The catcher reserves `h`/`j`/`k`/`l` and the arrows (`moveRequested`), Enter, Space, `x` (and `X`, both `deleteRequested`), Esc (`closeRequested`) and Tab/Shift-Tab (`tabRequested`, Omarchy's move to the neighbouring bar panel); other letters arrive as `textKey`. F0 found that Enter emits `returnRequested` and then `activateRequested`, so the frame acts on `activateRequested` alone; and that the catcher consumes moves, so the frame scrolls the cursor row into view itself.
- The key map fits around them: `h`/`l` and `1` to `5` switch views (Tab stays Omarchy's), `j`/`k` move, Enter is the row's primary action, `x` removes an addon or deletes a backup after a confirmation. The letters: `u` update all or the filtered client, `c` check now, `z` undo or redo the last change after a confirmation, `o` open the filtered client's `Interface/AddOns`, `t` cycle the client filter (All, then each client), `/` search, `b` back up, `d` dismiss new Lua errors, `r` restore settings, `s` raw error details, `i` release notes, `p` pin or unpin.
- The views, in switcher order: Updates, Installed, Issues, Backups, Search. The hero holds the summary ("2 clients · 3 updates · 1 issue", the oldest check, which client runs) with Check now, Undo last and Open AddOns; the footer shows the running change's NDJSON progress, the queued one ("next: …"), the last result with its Undo, and a failure with its Fix buttons or its prose fix. This replaces §5.11's target switcher, tab list and header actions.
- Updates groups what is behind per client ("then /reload" while that client runs), then pinned, blocked and failed checks. Installed lists managed addons with their source and markers (`dep`, `orphan`, `pinned`, `modified`, `missing`) and an adopt hint for unmanaged folders. Issues holds `status`'s problems by severity with their remediation (Enter runs it when the classifier accepts it, a destructive one previews first, others show as text), each client's Lua errors in strict text with the likely source and its confidence, a BugGrabber install where it is missing, and the last status's warnings. Backups lists each client's backups and its automatic-backup state with the free space. Search covers every client or the filtered one, and installs only where the compatibility hint is `yes` or `likely`; under All it asks which client.
- A confirmation takes the keyboard (the catcher is blocked) and starts on No. `y`, or `h`/`l` to Yes then Enter, confirms; `n` or Esc cancels; a held key's auto-repeat never confirms a fresh preview.
- Opening the panel or switching views reads only local commands (`status -v`, `list -v`, `errors --limit 10`, `backup list --limit 50`). Release notes (`info --changelog`) and search reach the network only when asked.

**The bar.** The badge is `summary.updates.available` (hidden at 0, `99+` above 99). The button is urgent when `summary.state` is `attention` (a P0 or P1 issue) or `errors` (new local Lua errors), dimmed when there is no answer or no client, and shows a turning sync glyph while a user change runs. The tooltip gives updates per client, the first urgent issue, new errors, running clients ("updates land, then /reload"), a due check, an outdated widget and the oldest check's age. Left click toggles the panel, right click checks now, middle click opens it on Issues.

**The binary, the context and the content-hash stamp (M3-D7); the folder name kept (M3-D6).**
- `omarchy install` renders `Build.js` (`.pragma library`, one `var` per line, each a JSON literal): `BINARY` (the canonical `current_exe`), `TOOL_VERSION`, `PLUGIN_ID`, `CONTEXT` (the installing run's absolute `HOME`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME`, `XDG_CACHE_HOME` and `XDG_DATA_HOME`, defaults written out: exactly what `Paths::from_env` reads), `CACHE_DIR` (`<cache>`, for the watcher) and `CONTENT_SHA256`. The manifest's `version` is stamped with the tool version and its `id` with the plugin id.
- The content hash covers the tool version, the five context paths, a build-time digest of the embedded runtime files (`build.rs`) and the stamped manifest; `BINARY` is left out, so another path to the same build is the same widget. `status` and `omarchy status` recompute what this binary would stamp for the installed context (read from the installed `Build.js`, which they find through the manifest's `entryPoints.service`, within `WIDGET_READBACK_MAX_BYTES`, 64 KiB) and compare. `outdated` therefore means another build or other assets, never merely another binary path or context; a missing or unreadable `Build.js` is outdated with `context_matches: null`. This replaces §5.11's version comparison.
- The code folder (decided on E1 after F0): every code file and `Build.js` go into `<plugins>/omaddons/r-<16 hex>/`, named for a SHA-256 over those files, `Build.js` included; `manifest.json` stays at the plugin root with its `entryPoints` stamped to `r-<16 hex>/Service.qml` and `r-<16 hex>/BarWidget.qml`. Any byte change, a moved binary included, gives new file URLs, so the hot reload after a swap loads the new service, widgets and `.pragma` modules and keeps the bar placement (verified live with an exchange swap). The repository's `omarchy/manifest.json` keeps the plain entry points.
- The plugin folder stays `<plugins>/omaddons/` with id `a44.omaddons`, the house convention and the existing scope rows. Omarchy's `omarchy plugin remove` assumes folder = id and cannot remove it; `omaddons omarchy remove` is the supported way.
- Every omaddons process the widget starts (reads, mutations, the previews behind confirmations, the self-reinstall) gets `Build.CONTEXT` overlaid on its environment through `Process.environment`. It runs `settings.binary` when set, else `Build.BINARY`. The desktop tools keep the plain desktop environment. A change of binary bumps a context generation; no answer or confirmation from before the change applies or runs after it.
- `status` reports `data.widget` `{omarchy, installed, enabled, version, outdated, context_matches}` (`null` without `<config-omarchy>`), from file reads only. It raises the warning `widget_outdated`, the P3 issue `fm-plugins-widget-version-drift` in the machine-level `data.issues`, the recommendation `reinstall_widget` and `summary.widget_outdated` only when `omarchy && installed && outdated && context_matches != false`. Run under another known context, it recommends nothing: reinstalling from there would point the widget at that run's state.

**Install and remove** (E2 omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.5.2, E3 omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.5.3). Install stages in its own hidden `<plugins>/.omaddons.stage-<ulid>` under an in-flight lock (Omarchy's registry and hot reload ignore dot names), validates with omaddons' port of `omarchy-plugin-validate` and with the real tool when it is on `PATH`, and publishes under the global lock with one `RENAME_EXCHANGE` (`RENAME_NOREPLACE` for a first install; a two-rename fallback warns `atomic_swap_unavailable`). It appends a `widget` history line, rings the doorbell, asks the shell to rescan, and places the widget on the bar (M3-D8). Unchanged rendered bytes write nothing. Remove takes the widget off the bar when it is placed (`omarchy-plugin-disable`, else the shell's `setPluginEnabled <id> false`), parks `<plugins>/omaddons` as `.omaddons.old-<ulid>` under the global lock, appends a `widget` line and prunes it. Omarchy's tools run with the user's environment inherited, so both commands belong in the desktop session. The scope rows are in the §5.5 write-scope comment.

**IPC.** One `IpcHandler` in the service, target `Build.PLUGIN_ID` (`a44.omaddons`), called as `omarchy-shell a44.omaddons <function> [arg]`:
- `state()`: JSON `{phase, bar, summary, action, lastResult: {ok, line}, panelOpen, binary, toolVersion, widgetVersion, contextGeneration, lanes, lastRefreshMs}`, where `lanes` holds `mutation`, `local` and `network`, each `{running, queued}`;
- `refresh()`: queue a `status`;
- `check()`: queue the update check (Check now);
- `show(view)`: set the requested view, then open the panel on the focused monitor through the service's `shell.summon(id, "")`, falling back to `omarchy-shell shell summon <id> {}`. `summon` opens and never toggles; for bar widgets the shell drops the payload, which is why the view is set first.

It is a desktop integration surface, not part of the CLI's JSON contract.

**The scheduler (M3-D11).** Every omaddons run is a request `{id, contextGeneration, target, resource, kind, priority, selection}` in one of three lanes, each running one fresh `Process` at a time. Which request starts next and which answer applies are pure `Model.js` functions with bun tests.
- Mutation lane: every command that mutates, the silent `backup_auto` included. User requests start before background ones, and nothing preempts a running change. At most one user change waits ("next: …"; a newer one replaces it), and one background change per (template, client). While a user change runs, mutating keys and buttons are off and say why. A silent change shows no progress, never locks the panel, and says nothing unless it fails.
- Local read lane: `status`, `list`, `errors`, `backup list`. One queued request per (resource, client), the newest replacing the older; `status` jumps the queue; a queued full `status` is never downgraded to a cached one.
- Network read lane: `outdated`, `search`, `info --changelog`. A newer search replaces a queued one, and at most 4 requests wait (`NETWORK_QUEUE_MAX`).
- Applying answers: every answer needs the current context generation. A data answer applies when its request id is newer than the last one applied for its key, even while a newer request still waits, so a busy lane never starves the bar. A view-bound answer (search, release notes, raw error details, the chooser's `backup list -v`) applies only while the view still shows the selection it was asked for.
- Deadlines: a local read gets `WIDGET_LOCAL_DEADLINE_SEC` = 20 s from its start; a network read gets `WIDGET_NETWORK_DEADLINE_SEC` = 600 s of inactivity, reset by each NDJSON progress line (a Rust test holds it at least as long as the longest polite request: 4 attempts of 30 s and 3 waits of 60 s, 300 s); a mutation has none. On a deadline or cancel the lane sends `signal(15)` to the pid, then `signal(9)` after `WIDGET_KILL_GRACE_SEC` = 5 s, and stays occupied until the child has really exited.
- Completion: `exited`, the end of stdout and `running` false, in either order; a killed run whose stdout stays open (a surviving `git`) completes `WIDGET_STREAM_GRACE_SEC` = 2 s after exit. A finished process's late signals are ignored. Outcomes: `ok`, `failed` (an envelope with `ok: false`), `timeout`, `cancelled`, `missing` (it never started: a missing binary emits no `exited`), `incompatible`, `malformed` (no envelope) and `oversized` (stdout above `WIDGET_OUTPUT_MAX_BYTES`, 8 MiB). stderr keeps its last 20 lines, each cut to 512 characters.
- Output is bounded on the CLI side, because Quickshell cannot cap a single line as it arrives: `search --limit 20`, `errors --limit 10` (at most `ERRORS_SHOWN_PER_ADDON` = 10 errors per addon, added for this), `backup list --limit 50`. A Rust test holds every template's worst case under 8 MiB (12 clients, 400 addons each).
- Freshness: the doorbell watcher (M3-D4: `inotifywait -m -q -e moved_to --format %f <cache>`, 150 ms debounce), behind a fallback poll of `refreshIntervalSec`, 15 s while a panel is open and at most 30 s while a client runs. A view re-reads its data when it is older than 10 s or a doorbell rang.

**The read-only incompatible state (M3-D42).** Every envelope is checked: schema major 1, `tool_version` equal to `Build.TOOL_VERSION`, and `data.widget.outdated` not true. A mismatch puts the service in phase `incompatible`: the last numbers stay, dimmed and marked stale; the open confirmation, the queued changes and the pending dismissals are dropped; no new change starts, and automatic work (checkpoints, error reads, update checks) and notifications stop. The panel offers only Retry and Reinstall widget. Just before any mutation starts, the service rechecks that it is compatible and that the request was made in the current context generation, so a confirmation given before a binary change never runs after it. The other phases are `starting`, `ok`, `missing` (no binary: the bar dims and the panel shows the two commands that bring it back) and `unreachable` (no envelope from `status`). Reinstall widget runs `[binary, "--actor", "widget", "--reason", "reinstall from the bar widget", "omarchy", "install"]` in a `Process` with `environment` set to `Build.CONTEXT` and `startDetached()`. It is detached because the reload kills the service's children, and it is a `Process` because `Quickshell.execDetached` cannot set an environment. This replaces §5.11's `Quickshell.execDetached` reinstall.

**Desktop triggers (M3-D12, M3-D13).**
- Hyprland `rawEvent`s `openwindow` and `closewindow`, with no class filter (a Proton game window's class names its launcher, not the game), restart a 500 ms debounce, then `status --cached` runs. A window closing while a client runs is followed by refreshes 2, 5 and 15 s later, because the game outlives its window.
- After each compatible status, a client that went from running to stopped gets its post-session checkpoint (`backup create --auto -t <id>`, silent, mutation lane), then its errors read (`errors --limit 10 -t <id>`, background). The first status of each context generation queues the checkpoint for every client known to be stopped; the CLI skips an unchanged one, so a session played with the bar off is still covered. A client whose `errors.state` is `stale` or `unchecked` is read again; a `partial` one is not. An unknown running state is no transition and gets no catch-up.
- Update checks: with `autoCheck` On, when `summary.check_due` is true and the last automatic check started 15 minutes ago or more, `outdated` runs in the network lane, judged on each status and by a 15-minute timer. Check now runs regardless. This replaces §5.11's `checkIntervalHours` timer: `config.toml`'s `check_interval_hours` decides when a check is due.

**The notification tool (M3-D14), with names and counts only.** Toasts are argv, run with `Quickshell.execDetached`: `omarchy-notification-send --app-name omaddons -g <U+F0297> -u <urgency> <title> <body> --exec omarchy-shell shell summon a44.omaddons {}`. The shell is the notification daemon; a click opens the panel on the focused monitor and leaves an open one open.
- Errors (`notifyErrors`, On, `-u normal`): when `summary.errors.new` rose since the previous compatible status. Title "Lua errors in your last session on <clients>", body "<addon> <count>" pairs from `status`'s per-client `errors.top`. `Model.errorToastArgv` reads only `{names, counts, targets}` from `Model.errorFacts`, so no message, location, stack, locals, path or folder can reach a toast, and toasts persist in the notification center. Received reports never count (the CLI excludes them).
- Updates (`notifyUpdates`, Off, `-u low`): when `summary.updates.available` rose.
- Results (`-u low`): a change started in the panel that finished after every panel closed.
- Nothing fires on the first status of a context generation, or while the widget is incompatible or the binary is missing. With one shared service, two monitors never send two toasts. §7 M3 listed only optional update notifications.

**The restore chooser** (F9, omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.9). A panel overlay with its own keys, which decides no folder, file or version itself: the CLI's dry run does.
- From an addon row (`r` in Installed, or on an erroring addon in Issues): choose a backup, restorable ones only, newest first, each showing the version of that addon that wrote its settings (from the view-bound `backup list -v -t <id> --limit 50`); then the scope. From a Backups row (Enter or `r`): the scope, then the addon for "One addon's settings…".
- The scopes always come in this order: the addon's settings first (template `restore_addon`, `backup restore -t {target} --addon={addon} -- {backup}`), then "Whole WTF/" (template `restore`), labelled "also restores keybindings, macros, chat settings and every other addon's settings".
- Choosing runs the dry run, and the confirmation shows the CLI's preview: the files that change, "settings written by <addon> <captured version>; installed now: <version>", what is not in the backup, and that a whole restore keeps the current `WTF/` as a backup. Yes runs with `--if-match`. A `ref_ambiguous` refusal (a capture-time folder another addon owns now) shows one button per folder, which reruns `restore_addon` with `--addon=folder:<F>` through the same preview, plus the backup's own folder as text for a copy by hand.
- Restores are off while the client runs or its running state is unknown ("quit the game first"). Esc steps back, then closes.
- `b`, anywhere in the panel, backs up the filtered client or every client (`backup create`). In the Backups view, `x` deletes exactly the backup under the cursor after a bound confirmation (template `prune_backup`), never one in use. Export, import and verify are CLI only.

**The security scans** (F7, omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.7). `omarchy/tests/security.test.js` runs in every gate (pipeline step 2) over every runtime QML and JS file; the scanned set must equal the embedded asset table less `manifest.json`, so a new file cannot escape. Each of the eight checks must also report a violation planted in an in-memory copy (15 plants, each named by file, line and rule):
1. Rendering: CLI strings reach the screen only through `PlainLabel` (plain text, no `textFormat` exposed) or qs.Ui's plain-text sinks, and every raw `Text`, `Label`, `TextEdit` or `TextInput` sets `textFormat: Text.PlainText`.
2. Launching: no shell, no string-form launch; `execDetached` takes an argv literal or a named `Model` argv builder; every omaddons `Process` carries `environment: Build.CONTEXT`.
3. Argv provenance: every argv comes from `Model.buildArgv`, `Model.cliArgv` (the classifier) or one of the four tools, each builder returning only its own tool's argv; the summon fallback and the self-reinstall are allowed as whole literal strings.
4. Files and URLs: no file writes (`FileView.setText` included); a browser opens only behind `Model.isSafeUrl` (`https:`, github.com, www.wowinterface.com, www.tukui.org or www.wowace.com, no credentials, no port).
5. Slots: `{query}`, the user's typing, fills read-only templates only.
6. Previews: outside `Service.qml` nothing calls the lane internals, and no direct mutation names a confirm template (`remove`, `restore`, `restore_addon`, `prune_backup`) or a destructive path.
7. Notifications: the error toast's builders read only names, counts and clients.
8. The plugin id: every use derives from `Build.PLUGIN_ID`; a Rust test also requires the literal `a44.omaddons` to appear only in the manifest.

At run time, every confirm template and destructive `CLI_PATHS` row refuses to build without its preview, and every template builds with the stamped context.

**Tests (M3-D41).** `scripts/widget-test.sh` runs after `cargo test` in every gate, over one fresh temporary directory: (1) the real binary writes the envelopes the reducers read (`write_widget_fixtures`); (2) bun tests `Model.js` over them and writes the argv it builds; (3) Rust parses exactly those argv (`validate_built_argv`); (4) when `omarchy/` changed, or with `--all`, Qt 6's `qmltestrunner` runs the QML tests over a copy of the plugin with a fixture `Build.js`. At the README pass: 108 bun tests (81 model, 27 security) and 116 QML tests.
