comments.text:
**§5.9 CLI contract, §5.6 files and §5.11 widget: every wire name M3 added, as shipped (DEC-4, D21) (omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.1 to .1.5 (A1–A5), .2.3 to .2.8 (B3–B8), .3.1 to .3.3 (C1–C3), .4.1 to .4.14 and .4.16 (D1–D14, D16), .5.1 to .5.4 (E1–E4), .6.1 to .6.9 (F1–F9)).** Adds to §5.9's command table, data shapes and code dictionaries, to §5.6's file table and to §5.11; supersedes the plan's checklist (the milestone epic's "Contract additions, part 1" and "part 2") where they differ, as listed at the end. The body is not edited. A short id `.4.16` means `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.16`; plan keys (A1 … F9) resolve through the key → id map, the milestone epic's first comment. Until the M4 golden file (D21), this comment is the record of M3's wire names. Everything is additive: `schema_version` stays "1.0", and no key, code or value was renamed or removed.

**How this was reconciled.** Mechanically against `af10e34` (the M3 baseline), then against every M3 leaf's close comment (common rule 6): the `error_codes!` and `warning_codes!` tables in `src/error.rs` (39 → 41 errors, 41 → 49 warnings), `app::COMMANDS` (28 → 42 paths), the clap structs, `store::KINDS` (+9 rows), every `CommandHint::new` action name in `src/` (+7), `TxKind` (+2), `FolderOp` (+2), `output::Phase` (+1), the engine's `FAILPOINTS` (27 → 34), `src/state/config.rs`, the environment variables the binary reads, the contract snapshots in `tests/contract/snapshots/`, and `omarchy/Model.js`. Constants are comment 8.

### Commands and flags
- New paths in `app::COMMANDS` (group, `mutates`):
  - `errors` (Look, false; writes only the derived `<cache>/errors.json`), `errors dismiss` (Look, true);
  - `backup` (Change, true; bare = `backup list`, envelope `command` "backup list"), `backup list` (false), `backup create`, `backup restore`, `backup prune`, `backup export`, `backup import`, `backup verify` (all true; `export` writes a file, `verify` records integrity);
  - `omarchy` (Setup, true; bare = `omarchy status`, envelope `command` "omarchy status"), `omarchy status` (false), `omarchy install`, `omarchy remove` (true).
- No new verb aliases. Bare help: `errors` joins Look, `backup` Change, `omarchy` Setup.
- Flags, by command:
  - `errors [--since WHEN] [--addon ADDON] [--limit N] [--received] [--raw-details] [--check]`. `WHEN` is `30m`, `12h`, `1d`, `2w` or RFC 3339; `--limit` defaults to 10 addons per client and 0 is `usage`; `--check` exits 6 (`check_failed`). `args_conflicts_with_subcommands`, so `errors dismiss` takes none of these.
  - `errors dismiss`: no flags of its own (`-t`, `--dry-run`, `--if-match`, `--reason`, `--actor`).
  - `backup list [ID] [--limit N]`: `ID` is an id or a prefix of 8 or more characters; bare `backup` takes only the global flags.
  - `backup create [--verify] [--auto]` (the two conflict).
  - `backup restore <ID> [--addon ADDON]…`: `ADDON` is a name, a ref, a folder, or `folder:<F>` (one folder alone); `--addon=<v>` and an `ID` after `--` parse.
  - `backup prune [ID…] [--keep N] [--older-than D]`: `D` takes `history --since`'s forms, RFC 3339 included; `--keep` and `--older-than` conflict with named ids.
  - `backup export <ID> <FILE>`; `backup import <FILE> [--force]` (`-t` required: `usage`, fix `omaddons targets`); `backup verify <ID>…`.
  - `omarchy install [--no-enable] [--section left|center|right]` (default `right`).
- Global flag `--if-match <TOKEN>` (A4, M3-D46). Accepted by the paths in `app::precondition::BINDING_COMMANDS`: `remove`, `undo`, `backup restore`, `backup prune`, `errors dismiss`. Elsewhere it is `usage` (fix: `omaddons help <command>` for a command that changes something, the argv without the flag for one that reads). A malformed token is `usage` with the `--dry-run` argv as fix. The token is `pc1:` and 64 lowercase hex: four 16-hex fields over the parts `command`, `targets`, `selection`, `observed`. `--dry-run` with `--if-match` previews afresh and returns a new token.

### Data keys on existing commands
- `status` (A2, B7, D11, E4), every key after the existing ones:
  - `data.summary {targets, running[], updates{available, targets[]}, issues{p0, p1, p2, p3}, errors{new, targets[]}, check_due, widget_outdated, state}`; `state` is `attention | errors | updates | idle`.
  - `data.last_change {run, kind, at, actor, reason, targets[], changes{added, replaced, removed, recorded, restored}, undo{command, argv}}` or `null`, and `data.last_change_state` `ok | unknown`.
  - `data.widget {omarchy, installed, enabled, version, outdated, context_matches}`, `null` without `<config-omarchy>`; `context_matches` is `null` when `Build.js` cannot say.
  - `data.issues[]`: issues of no client (today only the widget's), same shape as a target's.
  - `targets[].issues[] {id, severity, title, addon, remediation{command, argv, destructive}}`; `severity` `P0`–`P3`; `argv` `null` means prose.
  - `targets[].errors {capture, state, coverage, new, total, addons, received, top[{addon, folder, new, count}], last_session_at, dismissed_at}`; `capture` `buggrabber | none`; `state` `ok | stale | unchecked | partial | unreadable`; `coverage` `complete | truncated`; `top` holds at most 5.
  - `targets[].backups {count, stale, latest{id, captured_at, kind, trigger}, latest_qualifying{id, captured_at}, auto{mode, capability, last{at, result}}, bytes, snapshot_bytes, free_bytes}`, `null` for a missing client; `bytes` and `snapshot_bytes` are `null` without the inventory projection.
- `remove`, `undo`: `data.precondition` (a token under `--dry-run`, `null` on a real run) (A4). `undo`: `data.changed_since` (a count, or `null` when it cannot be counted), present only for an undo of a whole restore (D6).
- `history` (D2, D5, B8): `entries[].backup {id, kind, files, bytes}` on `backup` lines, `entries[].dismissed {databases, errors}` on `dismiss` lines, `changes.restored`; with `-v`, the new ops below.
- `info` (C3): `data.catalog.variant` (omitted for a name without variants) and `data.catalog.variants[{variant, families}]` (omitted when empty).
- `outdated`, `update` (C2): `latest.revision` (omitted when absent) and `latest.retagged: true` (omitted when false); human `v12.1.1 (re-tagged upstream)`.

### `errors` data (B3–B8, C3, F6)
- `data {raw_details, targets[], summary{targets, new, addons, uncertain, received}}`.
- Per target: `target{id, key}`, `capture` (`buggrabber | none`), `capture_note` (omitted unless no BugGrabber build is known for the client), `coverage` (`complete | truncated`), `files{read, accounts, partial, skipped{symlinked, two_spellings}}`, `databases[]`, `summary`, `addons[]`, `dismiss{precondition, databases}`, `dismissed` (newest valid acknowledgement time, or `null`).
- `databases[] {id, account, provider, shape, session, state, baseline, acknowledged, path}`: `id` is opaque (`db-1`), `account` the label `account N`, `shape` `modern | legacy`, `state` `complete | partial | over_budget | unreadable`, `acknowledged` the dismissed session or `null`, `path` only with `-v` (relative to the client, the account replaced).
- `summary {entries, occurrences, addons, new, matched, shown, uncertain, no_time, received}`.
- `addons[] {addon, managed, folders, kind, origin, version, latest{version, status}, count, new, entries, last_seen, errors[]}`; `kind` `addon | library | blizzard | unknown`; `origin` `local | received`.
- `errors[] {fingerprint, database, origin, message_kind, message, message_chars, location, attribution{method, confidence}, stack, count, sessions, new, last_seen, type, raw}`:
  - `fingerprint` is `e:` and 16 hex; `message_kind` `lua_runtime | blizzard | custom` (for `custom`, `message` is `null` and `message_chars` gives its length; `message_chars` is omitted otherwise);
  - `method` `protected_call | first_addon_frame | library_frame | blizzard_only | none`; `confidence` `high | medium | low`;
  - `last_seen {at, meaning, tz}` or `null`: `meaning` `last | first_or_last | unknown`, `tz` `explicit | system_assumed`;
  - `type` `error | event | warning`;
  - `raw {message, stack, locals, chunks}` only with `--raw-details`.
- `errors dismiss` data: `{dry_run, targets[{target, acknowledged[{database, session}], skipped[{database, reason}], errors}], precondition}`; `skipped.reason` is a database `state`; `precondition` appears only under `--dry-run`; `partial: true` when anything was skipped (exit 0).

### `backup` data (D1–D4, D7–D11, D13)
- `backup list`: `targets[] {target, auto{mode, capability, last}, backups[], bytes, snapshot_bytes, free_bytes, shown, total}`; each backup `{id, created_at, captured_at, kind, trigger, actor, reason, files, bytes, reflinked, client_running, unsettled, consistency, integrity, verified_at, baseline, restorable, qualifying, busy}`, its metadata fields `null` when `backup.json` does not read; `-v` adds `addons[{name, folders, version}]`.
  - `auto.mode` `off | daily | daily-copy`; `auto.capability` `unknown | supported | unsupported`; `auto.last.result` `created | failed` or a skip reason.
  - `kind` `manual | auto | before_restore | imported | recovered`; `trigger` `pre_change | post_session`; `reflinked` `all | some | none`; `consistency` `stable | best_effort`; `integrity` `metadata_only | verified | damaged`; `baseline` `capture | import | later`.
- `backup create`: `{dry_run, run, targets[{target, backup, tx, skipped, error, would}]}`; `skipped {reason}` with `off | no_wtf | running | unchanged | no_reflink | space_low | in_progress` (`done_today` is a pre-change outcome only); `would {files, bytes, copy, free_bytes}` only under `--dry-run`, `copy` `copy_on_write | byte_copy`.
- `backup restore`: `{dry_run, target, tx, kind: "restore", mode, backup{id, captured_at, kind, integrity}, files{restored, differed, created_since, unchanged}, before_restore{id}, reload_required, precondition, exchange, addons}`.
  - `mode` `whole | addons`; `exchange` `verified | unverified` (a dry run writes no probe); `reload_required` `restart` (whole) or `none` (`--addon`).
  - With `--addon`: `files` and `before_restore` are `null`, and `addons[] {addon, folders, folders_from, captured_version, installed_version, not_in_backup, files{replaced, restored, created_since}}`, `folders_from` `backup | installed | folder`. A whole restore has `addons: null`.
  - `commands`: `undo` (`omaddons undo <tx>`).
- `backup prune`: `{dry_run, targets[{target, pruned[{id, kind, bytes}], busy[{id}], kept, reclaimed_for_space, error}], precondition}`.
- `backup export`: `{dry_run, target, backup, file, files, bytes, compressed_bytes, sha256, verified_against}`; `compressed_bytes` and `sha256` (the archive's own) are `null` in a dry run; `verified_against` `capture | import | later | computed_at_export`.
- `backup import`: `{dry_run, target, backup, source{id, target_id, family, created_at, captured_at, tool_version}, files, bytes}`; `backup` is `null` in a dry run.
- `backup verify`: `{dry_run, targets[{target, backups[{id, integrity, baseline, files, checked, mismatched, note}]}]}`; `partial: true` when a backup is `damaged` (exit 0).

### `omarchy` data (E2, E3)
- `omarchy status`: `{omarchy{present, shell_running, validator}, plugin, validation{ok, errors[]}}`; `validation` is `null` when nothing is installed.
- `plugin` (also in `install`): `{installed, path, id, version, binary, outdated, enabled, section, context_matches}`; `section` `left | center | right | null`.
- `omarchy install`: `{dry_run, installed, enabled, section, plugin}`; `installed` `fresh | replaced | unchanged`; `enabled` `yes | already | skipped | failed`.
- `omarchy remove`: `{dry_run, removed, disabled, settings_dropped}`.

### Error codes
- New (registry 39 → 41), both exit 4, not retryable:
  - `filesystem_unsupported` (D5): `details.reason` `wtf_is_mount_point | stage_cross_mount | no_rename_exchange`, `details.backup_dir`; prose fix.
  - `file_exists` (D9): `details.file`; prose fix.
- Reused, with new details:
  - `plan_stale` under `--if-match`: not retryable, `details.changed` ⊆ `command | targets | selection | observed`, `fix_argv` the `--dry-run` form.
  - `state_too_new`: up front, before staging (A3); with `details {journal_pending, reason: "journal_too_new", target}` for a journal from a newer build.
  - `state_corrupt`: `details.reason` `journal_unreadable` (A3) or `preservation_incomplete` (D5, D14), with `journal_pending` and `target`; also an unreadable `backup.json`, manifest or `errors_ack.json`, and a restore of a backup marked `damaged`.
  - `internal`: `details.reason` `unexpected_state` (D5), or `plugin_invalid` with `details.problems` (E2).
  - `game_running`: `details.reason: "saved_variables"` for a restore, and for a waiting restore journal (with `journal_pending`, `target`).
  - `scope_denied`: `details.reason: "wtf_symlinked"` (with `backup_dir`); an export destination inside a client, a Wine prefix or omaddons' own dirs.
  - `undo_conflict`: `details.reason: "history_unreadable"` with `details.lines` (A3); rules 1 to 3 for restores (D6, D7), fix `omaddons undo <newest>`.
  - `not_found`: `details.reason` `omarchy_missing` (E2) and `widget_not_installed` (E3); an unknown backup id (`details {prefix, target, newest}`, `newest` the three newest ids); another client's backup (`details {id, target, owner}`); an `--addon` that names nothing (`details {addon, target}` or `{addons, target}`); `errors --addon` where no client captures errors; a client no BugGrabber variant covers (`details {name, family}`).
  - `ref_ambiguous`: a backup id prefix (one alternative per candidate); an `--addon` whose capture-time folder another addon owns now (`details {addon, candidates, owned_now[{folder, owner}], target}`, alternatives `--addon folder:<F>`), or that names several addons (`details {candidates, target}`).
  - `usage`: an id prefix under 8 characters; naming the newest checkpoint in `backup prune` (`details {id, target}`); a partial backup restored whole (`details {id, partial: true}`); `--saved-variables keep` on an undo of a restore.
  - `check_failed` from `errors --check`: `details {reason: new_errors | incomplete, target}`.
  - `hash_mismatch`: a restore's or export's file against its recorded hash, not retryable, `details.backup`.
  - `wrong_flavor`: `backup import` of another family (fix: the import into a client of that family, alternative `--force`).
  - `unsafe_archive` (`details.reason` `unsupported_entry | bad_name | duplicate_name | duplicate_metadata | missing_metadata | manifest_mismatch | symlink_escape`, plus `path`), `bad_archive` (`decoder_window | corrupt | truncated | metadata_unreadable | changed` for imports; `tree_collision` with `path`, `not_a_listing`, `bad_name` for WowAce trees), `archive_too_large` (import and `WTF/` walk bounds: `details {limit: <constant name>, max}`; WowAce tree bounds: `details {limit: <value>, constant: <name>}`; the tree's bytes reuse `download_max_bytes`).

### Warning codes (registry 41 → 49)
- New: `backup_copied`, `backup_unsettled`, `backup_space_low` (D2); `auto_backup_failed` (D3, fix `omaddons backup create -t <id>`); `before_restore_skipped` (D8); `restore_rolled_back` (D14, fix `omaddons backup restore <id> -t <target>`, with `--addon <F>` per folder for a partial one); `errors_partial` (B6, fix `omaddons errors -t <id>`); `omarchy_shell_unreachable` (E2, fix `omaddons omarchy install`; prose from `remove`).
- `widget_outdated`: reserved before M3, now emitted by `status` (E4), fix `omaddons omarchy install`.
- `journal_pending` names new reasons in its message text: `journal_too_new`, `journal_unreadable`, `saved_variables` (waits for the game), `preservation_incomplete`, `unexpected_state`. Warnings carry no `details` on the wire.
- Reused: `atomic_swap_unavailable` (the widget's two-rename fallback), `retention_failed` (now also after `backup create` and a restore, fix `omaddons backup prune -t <target>`), `saved_variables_out_of_scope` (a partial restore), `history_not_recorded` (a backup that stands without its line).

### Recommendation actions (`commands[].action`)
- New: `check_errors` (`omaddons errors`, from `status --cached` when a client's errors are `stale` or `unchecked`), `dismiss_errors` (`omaddons errors dismiss -t <id>`), `install_buggrabber` (`omaddons install buggrabber -t <id>`, only where a variant covers the family), `backup_create` (`omaddons backup create -t <id>`, from `backup list` and `status`), `refresh_backups` (`omaddons backup list -t <id>`), `reinstall_widget` and `enable_widget` (both `omaddons omarchy install`).
- Existing names in new places: `update` from `errors`; `undo` from `backup restore`.
- Issue ids (`app::issues::ids`, the D20 table the M4 doctor imports): `fm-concurrency_primitives-journal-pending` (P0), `fm-schemas-state-version-newer` (P0), `fm-state_files-record-folder-missing` (P1), `fm-external_artifacts-managed-files-modified` (P2), `fm-external_artifacts-ownership-transferred` (P2), `fm-userland_state-target-vanished` (P2), `fm-plugins-widget-version-drift` (P3, in `data.issues`).

### History, journal and on-disk formats
- `TxKind`: `dismiss` and `widget` are new settings kinds (never undone); `restore` and `backup` are now written.
- History ops: `op` values `wtf` (`folder` the literal `WTF`, `addon` empty) and `saved_variables` (one per addon folder); optional op keys `backup`, `from` (`backup | snapshot`), `files`, omitted when unset.
- History lines: optional `backup {id, kind, files, bytes}`, `sv_restored` (every M3 undo line of folders or SavedVariables carries it, 0 included; the undo of a whole restore does not, its `wtf` op standing for every file), `dismissed {databases, errors}`.
- Journal version 1.1. `prepared` gains optional `writes_wtf`, `staged_stamp` (`stamp:sha256:<hex>`), `staged_files[{rel, stamp}]`, `source_backup {id, dir{dev, ino, born_ns}}`, `client {target_id, family, version}`. New line kinds `preserve {id, items[{path, identity{dev, ino, born_ns}, rel}], assembly}` and `preserved {id}`. The digest kind `stamp:sha256:` appears in `actions.jsonl` for whole-tree renames.
- Persisted kinds (`store::KINDS`, each 1.0): `doorbell`, `history_tail`, `errors_memo`, `errors_ack`, `backup`, `backup_manifest`, `backup_addons`, `backup_inventory`, `backup_export` (only inside an export archive).
- `backup.json`: `{id, target, target_id, family, created_at, captured_at, kind, trigger, actor, reason, client_version, client_running, files, dirs, symlinks, skipped, bytes, reflinked, unsettled, consistency, integrity, verified_at, baseline, tool_version, source, partial, wtf_outside_client}`; `source` is `{restore_tx}` for `recovered`, or the import shape.
- `manifest.json`: `entries[{path, kind: file | dir | symlink, size, mode, mtime_ns, link, sha256}]`. `addons.json`: `addons[{name, folders, version, source{kind, ref, release_id}}]`.
- Export archive: zstd(tar), `backup.json` (kind `backup_export`: the backup's fields plus `verified_against`), `addons.json`, `WTF/…` in path order (uid/gid 0, recorded modes), `manifest.json` last with every `sha256` filled.
- Cache and state shapes: `doorbell.json {at, command, actor}` (`command` is the envelope's, or `recovery`); `errors_ack.json {targets{<key or id>: {databases{<16 hex of the path's SHA-256>: {acked_session, acked_at}}}}}`; `history_tail.json {covers{from, bytes}, partial[], dropped_at, lines[]}`; `backups.json {targets{<key>: {covers{backups[], wtf_previous[]}, counts_by_kind, bytes, snapshot_bytes, latest, latest_qualifying, auto{capability, last}}}}`; `errors.json` per target `{capture, coverage{truncated, accounts, files}, listings[{account, fingerprint}], received, databases[{path, account, provider, stamp, written_at, state, session, baseline, sessions{<n>: {entries, occurrences, newest}}, entries, occurrences, addons[{addon, managed, kind, sessions, folders}]}]}`.

### Progress, sources, network
- Progress phase `copy` (new): file counts under a fixed label, never a path: `WTF/ files` (create, restore staging), `exporting`, `importing`. Phase `verify` also carries backup hashing under the label `verifying`. A multi-client `backup create` reports one run-wide count (D15, .4.15).
- Source id `wowace` (`SourceId::Wowace`, `RefKind` wire `wowace`), registered by C2; config `[sources.wowace]`.
- Ref grammar: `wowace:<slug>` (slug `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]{0,63}$`), `#<tag>` (1 to 64 of letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `+`, `-`), `#r<rev>` (trunk at that revision), and `#r<rev>:<directory>` (a directory outside `trunk/` and `tags/`, 1 to 8 segments). Links: `repos.wowace.com/wow/<slug>/…` (`trunk/`, `tags/<tag>/`, `!svn/bc/<rev>/…`) and `www.wowace.com/projects/<slug>`; `http://` is `ref_invalid` with the https form as fix.
- Release id `wowace:<slug>@<tag>`, `@r<rev>` or `@r<rev>:<directory>`; asset location `wowace_tree {base, revision}` (release memo only); `revision` on releases, candidates, addon records (`targets/<key>.json`) and `addons.toml` entries.
- `no_compatible_release` `tried[].reason` `packaging_unsupported: <each item named>`. No `download_unverified` for WowAce downloads.
- `net.log`: method `PROPFIND`; purposes `wowace-tags`, `wowace-tree`, `wowace-file`. Host `repos.wowace.com` is always allowed for HTTP (so `url:` refs reach it too) and never for git.
- Catalog: key `variant` (letters, digits, `.`, `_`, `-`); an entry's identity is `name` or `name#variant`. BugGrabber ships variants `modern`, `r152`, `r130`, `r43`. `catalog_override_invalid` gains reasons for overlapping families, a missing or repeated variant, an empty family list, and one name given twice in a file.

### Files
- `<cache>/doorbell.json`, `<cache>/errors.json`, `<cache>/history_tail.json`, `<cache>/backups.json`; `<state>/errors_ack.json`.
- `<state>/journal/<tx>.wtf.jsonl`: the journal of a transaction that puts settings back (a restore, an `--addon` restore, an undo of either), named so pre-M3 builds never list it (D16, .4.16).
- `<meta>/backups/` (0700) and `<meta>/backups/<id>/` (0700) with `backup.json` (0600), `manifest.json`, `addons.json`, `WTF/`.
- `<meta>/snapshots/<tx>/WTF.previous/`: the tree a whole restore replaced.
- `<meta>/stage/<tx>.wtf/` with `WTF/` (the staged copy), `probe/` (the exchange probe) and `recovered/<id>/` (a preservation being assembled, published into `backups/`).
- `<plugins>/omaddons/`: `manifest.json` (stamped `version`, `id`, `entryPoints`) and the code in `r-<16 hex>/`, whose `Build.js` holds `BINARY`, `TOOL_VERSION`, `PLUGIN_ID`, `CONTEXT`, `CACHE_DIR`, `CONTENT_SHA256` (one `var` per line; content hash scheme "omaddons widget content 2").
- `<plugins>/.omaddons.stage-<ulid>/` (one install's stage), `.omaddons.old-<ulid>/` (a parked old widget), `.omaddons.trash/` (removed once empty).
- `backup export` writes only its destination and a hidden temporary sibling, published without replacing anything (`RENAME_NOREPLACE`, or a hard link where that flag is missing).

### Config and environment
- `auto_backup` gains the value `daily-copy` and its default becomes `daily` (was `off`, M3-D30).
- New keys: `limits.backup_min_free_mb` (2048, 0 to 1,048,576, 0 disables), `limits.backup_copy_max_mb` (4096, same range, `daily-copy` only), `limits.backup_auto_keep_days` (7, 1 to 100), `sources.wowace.enabled` (true).
- Environment read in every build: `OMARCHY_PATH` (Omarchy's shell at `$OMARCHY_PATH/shell` when `omarchy-shell` is not on `PATH`).
- Debug builds only: `OMADDONS_NOW` (RFC 3339 clock), `OMADDONS_FS_CLONE` (the clone hint), `OMADDONS_FS_FREE_MB` (free space), `OMADDONS_WIDGET_ID` (`[a-z0-9-]{1,32}`: plugin id `a44.omaddons-<suffix>` in `<plugins>/omaddons-<suffix>`).
- Debug failpoints: engine `FAILPOINTS` 27 → 34 (`engine.restore.staged`, `engine.restore.exchanged`, `engine.restore.snapshotted`, `engine.preserve.intent`, `engine.preserve.moved`, `engine.preserve.published`, `engine.autobackup`); outside that list, `backup.capture.copied.<n>`, `backup.capture.done.<n>`, `omarchy.staged`, `omarchy.swap`, `omarchy.parked`, `omarchy.invalid`, `omarchy.removing`.

### The widget's own names (F1–F9, E1–E4)
- Plugin id `a44.omaddons` (`paths::WIDGET_ID`), kinds `service` and `bar-widget`, `defaultSection` `right`, no `keepLoaded`. The repository's `omarchy/manifest.json` keeps plain `entryPoints`; install stamps `r-<16 hex>/Service.qml` and `r-<16 hex>/BarWidget.qml`.
- Settings (manifest `defaults`, also `Model.DEFAULT_SETTINGS`): `binary` (path, `""`), `panelWidth` (400–800, 540), `autoCheck` (`On | Off`, On), `notifyUpdates` (Off), `notifyErrors` (On), `refreshIntervalSec` (30–3600, 300).
- IPC target `Build.PLUGIN_ID`, functions `state()`, `refresh()`, `check()`, `show(view)`; `state()` returns `{phase, bar, summary, action, lastResult{ok, line}, panelOpen, binary, toolVersion, widgetVersion, contextGeneration, lanes{mutation, local, network: {running, queued}}, lastRefreshMs}`; `phase` `starting | ok | missing | unreachable | incompatible`; views `updates | installed | issues | backups | search`.
- Templates (`Model.COMMANDS`, 27, every argv parsed by the binary's clap in the gate): `status`, `status_full`, `list`, `changelog`, `search`, `search_all`, `check`, `update_all`, `update_target`, `update_addon`, `reinstall`, `remove` (confirm), `pin`, `unpin`, `install`, `errors` (`--limit 10`), `errors_raw`, `errors_target`, `dismiss_errors` (bind), `backups` (`backup list --limit 50`), `backups_detail`, `backup_target`, `backup_all`, `backup_auto` (silent), `restore` (confirm), `restore_addon` (`--addon={addon}`, confirm), `prune_backup` (confirm). Slots: `target`, `addon`, `ref`, `backup`, `query` (never in a mutating template).
- `CLI_PATHS`: one row per `app::COMMANDS` path (42) with `mutates`, `destructive`, `binds`; destructive: `remove`, `undo`, `targets rm`, `backup restore`, `backup prune`. Widget-owned flags a classified argv may not carry: `--json`, `--robot`, `--format`, `--actor`, `--reason`, `--progress`, `--if-match`.
- Every run: `<binary> --json --actor widget --reason "<label> (bar widget)"`, plus `--progress json` for a mutation or `check`, `--dry-run` for a preview, `--if-match <token>` for a bound run, under `Build.CONTEXT` (`HOME`, `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, `XDG_STATE_HOME`, `XDG_CACHE_HOME`, `XDG_DATA_HOME`).
- Toasts: `omarchy-notification-send --app-name omaddons -g <glyph> -u <urgency> <title> <body> --exec omarchy-shell shell summon <id> {}`; the doorbell watcher `inotifywait -m -q -e moved_to --format %f <cache>`.
- Omarchy tools the binary runs (`src/omarchy/shell.rs`): `omarchy-plugin-validate <dir>`, `omarchy-shell -q shell rescanPlugins`, `omarchy-bar put <id> --section <s>`, `omarchy-shell shell ping`, `omarchy-plugin-disable <id>` (fallback `omarchy-shell shell setPluginEnabled <id> false`).

### Added in the same window outside the M3 epic
- Action `search` (omad-zwl3): `install`'s hint for a bridge requirement nothing resolves; every hint is now labelled by the verb its argv runs.
- `undo --last-by` takes only `human | agent | widget`, and a mistyped value or `--actor` is corrected in place (omad-rnk8); `download_failed` for a commit the server refuses is not retryable (omad-peud).

### Planned but not shipped, or shipped differently
- Bare `backup` takes only the global flags (the plan's synopsis gave it `--limit`); `backup list` also takes an optional `ID` (D1).
- `status` gained `data.issues` for the machine's own issues; the widget issue lives there at P3, not under a client (E4; A2's handoff suggested P2).
- `errors` gained `capture_note`, `addons[].origin` and `databases[].path`; `errors[]` per addon is capped at 10 by `ERRORS_SHOWN_PER_ADDON` (F6).
- `errors dismiss` data gained `dry_run` and `targets[].errors`; its `precondition` is omitted on real runs, where `remove`, `undo`, `backup restore` and `backup prune` emit `null` (`omad-q585`, open).
- `backup create` gained `would`; `backup prune` gained `targets[].error`; `backup export` and `backup import` gained `dry_run` and `target`, import also `files` and `bytes`; `backup restore` puts `addons` last and adds `folders_from`.
- `verified_against` gained `computed_at_export`. `unsafe_archive` also uses `bad_name`, `duplicate_name` and `missing_metadata`; `bad_archive` also `corrupt`, `truncated`, `metadata_unreadable`, `changed`.
- `archive_too_large` details differ by origin: M2 and WowAce use `details.limit` for the value (with `config_key`, or `constant` naming a WowAce bound), while the `WTF/` walk and `backup import` put the constant's name in `details.limit` and the value in `details.max` (`omad-36gn`, open: one shape before the M4 freeze).
- `hash_mismatch` from a restore, an `--addon` restore or an export keeps the fix `omaddons backup list`; D8 asked D13 to point it at `omaddons backup verify <id> -t <target>`, and that did not happen (`omad-mc1i`, open).
- `journal_pending`: planned as `details.reason`; warnings have no `details`, so the reason travels in the message, and the errors raised for the own target carry `details.reason`.
- `HistoryEntry` also gained `dismissed`; `prepared` also gained `client` (D14).
- Files: the restore stage and preservation assembly are `<meta>/stage/<tx>.wtf/…`, not `<meta>/stage/<tx>/…`, and restore journals `<tx>.wtf.jsonl` (D16). `Build.js` lives at `<plugins>/omaddons/r-<16 hex>/Build.js`, not the plugin root (E1, after F0); `.omaddons.old-<ulid>/` and `.omaddons.trash/` were not in the plan.
- Ref grammar: the slug is bounded to 64 characters, and `#r<rev>:<directory>` was added after the plan (omad-xork, BugGrabber for 1.12.1).
- Progress: hashing reports under `verify` (`verifying`), not `copy` (D2, D13).
- Catalog `variant` and `info`'s `catalog.variant`/`variants` were not in the plan's contract list (C3).

comments.text:
**§7 M3, as decomposed and shipped: the M3 decomposition record and every departure from this body (omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx).** Supersedes §7 M3's scope list and, where a departure below says so, §5.6, §5.8 and §5.11; also supersedes comment 606's list of BugGrabber options. The body is not edited. Recorded against `main` at `41e4b33`, after the README final pass (omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.7.1, G1). The checkpoint and "M3 is done" are recorded by G3 (omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.7.3).

**Planning.** The M3 plan was written on 2026-10-21 against `main` at `af10e34`, after five read-only investigations: the CLI and contract layer; the engine and fsx; tests, gate and bead conventions; the Omarchy and Quickshell plugin system on the live desktop; BugGrabber's sources and schemas. It went through three review rounds before decomposition: an internal review (42 findings, 3 blockers), a second internal review (20 findings, 1 blocker) and an external review of 23 proposed revisions (19 adopted, 4 adapted, none rejected outright). Two consistency reviews followed (41 findings, then 17), all fixed. It was decomposed into beads the same day.

**The tree.** The milestone epic `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx` has seven area epics:
- A `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1`: contract foundations (the doorbell, `status` triage and the history projection, fail-closed formats, preview tokens, the privacy redactor);
- B `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2`: Lua errors (the SavedVariables parser, BugGrabber decoders, attribution, `errors`, `errors dismiss`, errors in `status`);
- C `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.3`: keyless BugGrabber (the `wowace:` source, catalog variants);
- D `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4`: backups and restore (the store, `create`, automatic checkpoints, retention and `prune`, the restore engine and its undo, `--addon`, `export`, `import`, `verify`, preservation, integration evidence);
- E `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.5`: widget packaging (embedded assets, `omarchy install`, `status` and `remove`, the widget in `status`);
- F `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6`: the widget (the Quickshell spike, the model, the service, the bar button, the panel and its views, desktop triggers, security scans);
- G `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.7`: README, these vision comments, the checkpoint.

The plan filed 47 leaves (7 S, 34 M, 6 L; 35 features, 10 tasks, 2 docs) with 102 `blocks` edges: the plan's 101 plus D6 ← A4, added at filing. Leaf ids follow the area epic and the plan key (A1 is `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.1`, D14 is `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.14`), except the spike F0, which is `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.10`. **The key → id map is the first comment on the milestone epic.** The epic's other comments hold the decision log (parts 1 to 5), the ground truth at `af10e34`, the architecture, the workflows, delivery (critical paths, lanes, slices), risks and the checkpoint protocol, rationale, the planned contract additions (parts 1 and 2), the file map, the planning record, and F0's amendments to M3-D4 to M3-D7 (2026-10-22).

Changes to the tree during M3:
- Two leaves were added under the D epic: `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.15` (run-wide progress counts for a multi-client `backup create`, found by D2) and `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.16` (journals and stages that put settings back are named `<tx>.wtf`, so a pre-M3 build never sees them; found by D12, and G3 depends on it).
- Three edges were added: F9 ← F5 and F9 ← F6 (F9 edits their view files) and G3 ← `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.16`. The tree now has 49 leaves and 105 `blocks` edges.
- Work found during M3 and filed with `discovered-from`: `omad-exlw` (filed under the B epic, closed as not worth the risk), `omad-5vdb`, `omad-7o7e` and `omad-hrf5` (fixed), `omad-xork` (closed: a BugGrabber build for 1.12.1), and open follow-ups: `omad-7ccp` (on btrfs a restore's or an install's commit window holds the lock 130 to 180 ms, about 50 fsyncs) and `omad-7jwk` (`status --cached` with a 20 MB history runs within 0.2 ms of its 5 ms budget). G2's reconciliation of these comments with the code filed seven more: `omad-k2ns` (the pre-change automatic backup runs no backup retention, against M3-D32), `omad-aepa` (a pre-M3 build's orphan sweep after a restore crashed past its first rename), `omad-mc1i` (`hash_mismatch`'s fix and a damaged backup left looking verified), `omad-in4u` (`errors -v` account numbering), `omad-09iu` (a timed-out Omarchy tool's children), `omad-36gn` (`archive_too_large` details shapes) and `omad-q585` (small registry and text inconsistencies).

**The four delivery slices** (each leaf carries its slice label; the plan asked for a demo comment on the milestone epic when each slice's last leaf closed):
- `slice-1` See and update from the bar: A1, A2, A4, F0 to F5, E1 to E4. Demo: `omarchy install` on the desktop; the badge follows a terminal `update` within 1 s; update one addon from the panel and undo it; a stale `remove` preview gives `plan_stale`; a reinstall swaps atomically.
- `slice-2` Capture and diagnose: A5, B1 to B8, C1 to C3, D1 to D4, D11, D13, F6, F8. Demo: `errors` on every client, read-only; `install buggrabber` keyless on retail and the 3.3.5a client; automatic checkpoints before a change and after a session, coalesced; `backup verify`; the Issues view with strict output, received reports and a bound dismissal.
- `slice-3` Recover: A3, D5, D6, D14, D8, D7, F9. Demo: whole and `--addon` restores from the CLI and from the bar's chooser, each undone; the crash matrices of D5, D6, D7 and D14.
- `slice-4` Portability and close: D9, D10, D12, F7, G1, G2, G3. Demo: export, import, restore byte-identical; integration scenes; the `af10e34` characterization; perf; the gate from a clean checkout; README.

No slice demo comment was recorded on the milestone epic. The suites and CLI scenes behind each demo closed with their leaves; the live desktop parts (install on both bars, doorbell latency, updates, restores and dismissals from the panel) were left to G3's checkpoint run. The 14 success criteria in the milestone epic body amend §7's M3 checkpoint list (criterion 1 amended for enable-by-default and two monitors, criterion 2 for update checks and `backup` commands; criteria 7, 13 and 14 added). G3 records each outcome.

**Decisions.** The plan made 48 decisions, M3-D1 to M3-D48, numbered by when they were made (M3-D43 and M3-D44 before the third review, M3-D45 to M3-D48 during it). Each has its reasons and rejected alternatives in the decision log on the milestone epic. As shipped, one line each; the topic comments of this M3 set carry the detail:
- Scope and shape. M3-D1: M3 is the vision's M3 plus the doorbell, the `status` triage blocks and the `wowace:` source (*departure*). M3-D2: the widget runs argv arrays only, from its template table or from CLI output its classifier accepts (*departure*). M3-D3: the widget writes no file. M3-D4: `<cache>/doorbell.json` replaces `status.json` as the widget's signal (*departure*). M3-D5: one shared `service` per shell beside the per-monitor bar widgets. M3-D6: the plugin folder stays `<plugins>/omaddons/`, id `a44.omaddons`. M3-D7: `Build.js` stamps the binary, the data context and a content hash; after F0's finding, the code lives in a content-addressed folder `r-<16 hex>/`. M3-D8: `omarchy install` enables by default (*departure*). M3-D9: stored plans stay in M4; destructive widget actions preview and bind (*departure*, with M3-D46). M3-D10: six widget settings (*departure*). M3-D11: one scheduler with a mutation lane and two read lanes. M3-D12: background update checks follow `status`'s `check_due`. M3-D13: Hyprland window events are a doorbell, with a startup catch-up. M3-D14: notifications carry names and counts only. (The §5.11 widget comment.)
- Lua errors. M3-D15: BugGrabber comes from WowAce's SVN through `wowace:` (*departure*). M3-D16: same-name catalog variants select by disjoint client families. M3-D17: the bounded, fuzzed SavedVariables parser `src/lua.rs`. M3-D18: attribution with its evidence (`method`, `confidence`), worded "likely source". M3-D19: "new" is per-database session watermarks; `errors dismiss` writes durable user state (*departure*). M3-D20: the errors memo `<cache>/errors.json` is derived; `status` stays write-free. M3-D21: privacy is a contract on kinds of text, on every channel; free text needs `--raw-details`. M3-D22: `errors` exits 0; `--check` exits 6 on new errors or an incomplete read. M3-D44: where `BugGrabberDB` is looked for, within bounds. (The §5.8 errors comment.)
- Backups and restore. M3-D23: what a backup is (`<meta>/backups/<id>/` with `backup.json`, `manifest.json`, `addons.json` and `WTF/`; five kinds; `stable` or `best_effort`). M3-D24: a whole restore is one journaled `RENAME_EXCHANGE` of `WTF`; recovery waits for the game and preserves displaced versions. M3-D25: whole-tree renames record `stamp:sha256:` digests. M3-D26: a whole restore first makes a `before_restore` backup. M3-D27: `backup restore --addon` is a SavedVariables-only transaction in undo's layout. M3-D28: undo and restores conflict where they would overwrite each other. M3-D29: restores never run while the client runs, or while that is unknown. M3-D30: `auto_backup` defaults to `daily` (*departure*, owner-visible). M3-D31: two automatic triggers, qualifying captures, coalescing. M3-D32: automatic backups are thinned by local day. M3-D33: each backup is a `backup` history line. M3-D34: `backup export` streams a new `.tar.zst` and never replaces a file. M3-D35: `backup import`, exact archives only (*departure*). M3-D36: the `tar` and `zstd` crates, both with default features off, the only crates M3 added. M3-D43: `backup create` without `-t` backs up every live client that has a `WTF/`. M3-D47: backup integrity is explicit; `backup verify` (*departure*). M3-D48: a free-space guard, a byte-copy budget, a per-target scheduling lock and reader reservations. (The §5.5 write-scope, §5.5 journal and recovery, and §5.8 backup comments.)
- Triage and contract. M3-D37: `status` gains `summary`, `issues[]`, `last_change`, `errors`, `backups` and `widget`, read under `--cached` from two small projections (`history_tail.json`, `backups.json`). M3-D38: widget installs and removals are `widget` history lines, each install with its own stage. M3-D39: help gains `errors` (Look), `backup` (Change) and `omarchy` (Setup). M3-D40: the progress phase `copy` (hashing reports under `verify`). M3-D41: the widget's ordered test pipeline runs in every gate. M3-D42: the widget turns read-only when it does not match the binary. (The §5.11 widget comment and the contract additions comment.)
- Safety contracts. M3-D45: persisted formats fail closed (*a strict change from M2*). M3-D46: destructive previews bind through `--if-match` precondition tokens (*departure*, with M3-D9).

**Departures from this body, each as shipped.** Each changes what the body or a later vision comment says.

- **M3-D1, additions only** (the beads named below).
  - The vision said: §7 M3 is the widget, `--progress json`, `errors` and `backup`.
  - M3 does: it also ships (1) the doorbell `<cache>/doorbell.json` (omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.1, A1); (2) the `status` triage blocks: `summary`, `targets[].issues[]` with the doctor's `fm-…` ids and P0 to P3 severities, and `last_change` with its `undo --run <run>` argv (omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.2, A2), `targets[].errors` (omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.7, B7), `targets[].backups` (omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.11, D11), `widget` and a machine-level `issues` list (omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.5.4, E4); (3) the `wowace:` source and BugGrabber's catalog variants (omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.3.1 to omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.3.3, C1 to C3). `--progress json` itself had landed in M2 (M2-D26); M3 added the phase `copy`. The doctor was not pulled forward: `issues[]` uses its ids, so M4 extends it.
  - Why: each is the smallest change that makes a listed deliverable work on a real machine. `status.json` misses update checks; the bar needs severity, error counts and "last change" in one cheap call; BugGrabber has no keyless release anywhere else.
- **M3-D2, argv templates and the CLI argv classifier** (omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.1 F1, omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.2 F2, omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.7 F7).
  - The vision said (§5.11): actions run as `Process` argv arrays with `--json --progress json --actor widget`, and only argv entries from CLI output are executed.
  - M3 does: the widget never runs a shell string, and every omaddons argv comes from one of two sources.
    - CLI output (`error.fix_argv`, `alternatives[].argv`, `warnings[].fix_argv`, `commands[].argv`, `issues[].remediation.argv`, `last_change.undo.argv`), when `Model.classifyCliArgv` accepts it: `argv[0]` is `omaddons`; the leading command words form a path in `CLI_PATHS` (42 rows in `omarchy/Model.js`, each with `mutates`, `destructive` and `binds`, held equal to `app::COMMANDS` by `tests/omarchy_widget.rs`); and no flag the widget owns (`--json`, `--robot`, `--format`, `--actor`, `--reason`, `--progress`, `--if-match`) appears before `--`. A refused argv is shown as text, never as a button.
    - The template table `COMMANDS` in `omarchy/Model.js` (27 templates): literal argv with typed slots `{target}` (must match `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._@-]*$`), `{addon}`, `{ref}`, `{backup}`, and `{query}`, which only read-only templates may hold. Positional slots follow `--`; an option slot is one element, `--opt={slot}`.
    - The widget puts its standard flags right after the binary, before the command words: `--json --actor widget --reason "<button label> (bar widget)"`, then `--progress json` for mutations and the update check, `--dry-run` for a preview, and `--if-match <token>` for a confirmed binding run. Appended after `--`, clap would read them as positionals.
    - A destructive path (`remove`, `undo`, `backup restore`, `backup prune`, `targets rm`) and the four `confirm` templates refuse to build without their preview (`destructive_without_preview`).
    - Besides omaddons the widget runs four tools with literal argv: `inotifywait`, `omarchy-notification-send`, `xdg-open` and `omarchy-launch-browser` (only for an `https:` link to github.com, www.wowinterface.com, www.tukui.org or www.wowace.com). Two more argv are allowed exactly as written: the summon fallback and the self-reinstall.
    - Every gate builds every template's argv in bun, for benign and hostile slot values (spaces, `!`, `$(…)`, `;`, a leading `-`, non-ASCII), and Rust parses exactly those argv with `Cli::try_parse_from`. Rust never fills a slot itself.
  - Why: taken literally, §5.11 needs per-row argv arrays in `list`, `search` and `backup list`, which is contract weight with no safety gain. The property behind §5.11 is "nothing is shell-parsed, and nothing the user did not see runs", and argv arrays holding identifiers the CLI returned keep it. A prefix check proves which program runs, not what the command does, so a classifier decides.
- **M3-D4, the doorbell replaces `status.json` as the widget's signal** (omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.1 A1, omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.2 F2, omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.10 F0).
  - The vision said (§5.11, §5.6): the widget's doorbell is `FileView { watchChanges: true }` on `status.json`.
  - M3 does: `<cache>/doorbell.json` (kind `doorbell` 1.0, body `{at, command, actor}`) is rewritten through fsx after every write that can change `status --cached`: each commit window (undo's too), a recovery that rolled a journal back or forward, a write of the release memo, the errors memo, the backup inventory or the history projection that changed it, each backup's history line, a `backup prune` that deleted something, a recorded `backup verify`, every settings command (`errors dismiss` included), and `omarchy install` and `remove`. `status` never rings it, and a read rings it only when it rewrote one of those derived files. The service watches `<cache>` with `inotifywait -m -q -e moved_to --format %f <cache>`, filters for `doorbell.json`, debounces 150 ms and reads `status --cached`; it retries the watcher after 5 s, or 30 s when the directory is missing, behind a fallback poll (`refreshIntervalSec`). F0 changed the watched events from the planned `close_write,moved_to`, which rang twice per fsx write. `status.json` is unchanged: a derived summary written after commits, no longer anyone's signal. Measured live: 20 of 20 rings answered, median 159 ms, p95 161 ms.
  - Why: `status.json` is never written by `outdated`, settings commands or recovery, and it lives in `<state>`, which read-like commands must not touch. A directory watch survives fsx's temp-file-then-rename writes.
- **M3-D8, enable by default** (omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.5.2 E2, omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.5.3 E3).
  - The vision said (§5.11): `omaddons omarchy install [--enable] [--section right]`, then `omarchy-shell shell rescanPlugins` and `omarchy-plugin-enable`, enabling only on request.
  - M3 does: `omaddons omarchy install [--no-enable] [--section left|center|right]` (default `right`) installs and enables. After the swap it asks the shell to rescan (best effort). Then, unless the widget is already in a section of `bar.layout` in `<config-omarchy>/shell.json` (read only, bounded by `OMARCHY_SHELL_JSON_MAX_BYTES`, 4 MiB), it runs Omarchy's own `omarchy-bar put a44.omaddons --section <s>`, up to 5 attempts 200 ms apart while it answers `is not a known widget`. Only the stdout `a44.omaddons is on the bar` counts as success, because the tool exits 0 when the shell is not running. Anything else gives `enabled: failed` and the warning `omarchy_shell_unreachable`, with the files installed. A reinstall keeps the owner's placement, omaddons never writes `shell.json`, and bare `omaddons omarchy` is `omarchy status`.
  - Why: the first guessed command should work (D17). A bar widget installed invisible behind a flag is a trap, and removal is one command. `omarchy-bar put` places the widget without racing the shell's asynchronous rescan.
- **M3-D9 with M3-D46, stored plans stay in M4; previews bind through precondition tokens** (omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.4 A4, omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.4 D4, omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.8 D8, omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.8 B8, omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.2 F2).
  - The vision said (§5.11): mutating buttons first fetch a plan and then call `apply <plan_id>` for the plan shown (§5.9 stored plans).
  - M3 does: stored plans (`plan_id`, `apply`, `PLAN_TTL`) stay in M4. A new global flag `--if-match <TOKEN>` is accepted by exactly five commands, `remove`, `undo`, `backup restore`, `backup prune` and `errors dismiss`; elsewhere it is a usage error.
    - The `--dry-run` data of those five carries `precondition`: `pc1:` and four 16-hex fields, each the first 64 bits of a SHA-256 over one canonical part: the command path, the targets (keys with generations; keys only for `errors dismiss`), the selection and the observed state (for example the live `WTF/` stamp digest of a whole restore, or each BugGrabber file's stamp and session). `app::precondition` computes it from the plan the command executes. The `errors` read returns `targets[].dismiss.precondition` for the observation it shows.
    - With `--if-match`, the real run recomputes the token before staging anything. A difference refuses with `plan_stale`, not retryable, with `details.changed` drawn from `command`, `targets`, `selection` and `observed`, and `fix_argv` the same command with `--dry-run` in place of the token. Nothing changes. `--dry-run` with `--if-match` previews afresh. Without the flag every command behaves as before.
    - The widget runs a destructive action's `--dry-run` first and shows the CLI's preview in a dialog that starts on No; Yes runs the same argv with `--if-match`, and a `plan_stale` reopens the dialog with the fresh preview ("Changed since you looked") instead of running again. `errors dismiss` binds the token of the read the Issues view showed, without a dialog. `targets rm`, destructive but not binding, is confirmed from its dry run and runs without a token.
  - Why: the race that matters is a concurrent change between preview and confirm (a prune selecting other backups, a session ending before a dismissal), not a new release. Generations alone miss the game's own writes to `WTF/` and BugGrabber files, so the token covers observed files too. A stateless token is the part of stored plans a dialog needs, and M4's `plan_id` can embed it.
- **M3-D10, widget settings trimmed** (omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.1).
  - The vision said (§5.11): `checkIntervalHours`, `notifyUpdates`, `defaultTarget`, `binary` (default `omaddons`), `panelWidth`.
  - M3 does: six settings in `omarchy/manifest.json`: `binary` (path, default `""`, which runs the binary stamped at install; a non-empty value must be absolute), `panelWidth` (400 to 800, step 20, default 540), `autoCheck` (On), `notifyUpdates` (Off), `notifyErrors` (On), `refreshIntervalSec` (30 to 3600, step 30, default 300). `checkIntervalHours` is dropped: `config.toml`'s `check_interval_hours` owns the interval, and the widget follows `status`'s `check_due` (M3-D12). `defaultTarget` is dropped: `default_target` and `targets default` own it. Omarchy 4.0.6 ignores manifest defaults, so `Model.js` holds the same defaults (a bun test keeps them equal) and replaces any invalid value with its default. Settings are set with `omarchy bar set a44.omaddons <key> <value>`.
  - Why: §5.11's own rule, "product configuration stays in config.toml". Two knobs for one interval would disagree.
- **M3-D15, BugGrabber from WowAce, pinned, with a narrow packaging subset** (omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.3.1 C1, omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.3.2 C2, omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.3.3 C3, omad-xork).
  - The vision said (comment 606): M3 must choose a documented git mirror, CurseForge in M5, or a manual `--file` install.
  - M3 does: a fourth option, a keyless `wowace:` source over WowAce's public Subversion repository. Host `repos.wowace.com` joins the always-allowed list for HTTP, never for git; `sources.wowace.enabled` defaults to true.
    - Refs: `wowace:<slug>` (the newest stable tag), `wowace:<slug>#<tag>`, `wowace:<slug>#r<rev>` (trunk at that revision), `wowace:<slug>#r<rev>:<directory>` (another directory of the project at that revision, added by `omad-xork` for BugGrabber's 1.12-era tree), and pasted `repos.wowace.com` and `www.wowace.com/projects/` links.
    - One `PROPFIND` (`Depth: 1`) of `tags/` gives every tag's last-changed revision. Every listing and file of a tag is then fetched under `!svn/bc/<rev>/…`, so a tag edited mid-fetch cannot mix revisions. The release id is `wowace:<slug>@<tag>` (`@r<rev>` for a revision ref), and the revision is recorded beside it in the release memo, the addon record and `addons.toml`, and in the asset name the download cache keys on; a moved tag is an update ("re-tagged upstream"), an unrelated commit never is, and a locked or exact reinstall fetches the recorded revision.
    - The tree is assembled as the packager would build a project that needs only `package-as` and `@project-version@` (replaced by the tag in TOCs), dotfiles left out and metadata-only `.pkgmeta` keys ignored, into a deterministic zip in the blob cache. Then archive inspection and TOC verification run unchanged. Any other packaging step (`externals`, `ignore`, `move-folders`, other keywords, `--@debug@`-style blocks) refuses the release with `packaging_unsupported` in `no_compatible_release`'s `tried[]`. No `download_unverified` warning is given (TLS and the TOCs are the check).
    - The catalog's BugGrabber has four variants with disjoint families (M3-D16): `modern` (`wowace:bug-grabber`: mainline, vanilla, tbc, wrath, titan, cata, mists, forever), `r152` (wrath-legacy, 3.3.5a), `r130` (tbc-legacy, 2.4.3) and `r43` (`wowace:bug-grabber#r43:tmp/trunk/!BugGrabber`, vanilla-legacy, 1.12.1). The plan named only `modern` and `r152`; the others were added after their TOCs were verified live. cata-legacy and mists-legacy have no build: every 4.3.4 and 5.4.8 revision needs the packager's `@localization` keywords.
  - Why: keyless, official and pinned. `hippuli/BugGrabber` builds only for bcc since v11.2.7; `curseforge-mirror/bug-grabber` re-tags several times a day (phantom updates) and needs REST to list assets; CurseForge's website API is a terms risk; modern BugGrabber is "All Rights Reserved", so it cannot be bundled. Refusing unsupported packaging by name keeps the source from installing an unbuilt tree that happens to load.
- **M3-D19, dismissal as a subcommand and durable user state** (omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.6 B6, omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.8 B8, omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.7 B7).
  - The vision said (§5.8): `errors` groups and reports errors; it said nothing about which errors are new or how to dismiss them.
  - M3 does: `errors dismiss [-t T]` is a subcommand (`mutates: true`, group Look). It reads each selected target's BugGrabber databases afresh and checks the token, then, under the global lock (recovering first), re-checks any database that moved and writes `<state>/errors_ack.json` (kind `errors_ack` 1.0: per target and per database key, the first 16 hex digits of a SHA-256 of the file's client-relative path, `{acked_session, acked_at}`, with no path and no error text). It appends a settings history line of kind `dismiss`, rings the doorbell and cannot be undone; the errors stay listed, only the "new" mark goes. A database read incompletely is skipped (`partial: true`). `--if-match` binds a dismissal to each database's file stamp and session as the read the user saw them. "New" is decided per database: the file was written within `ERRORS_NEW_MAX_AGE` (7 days) at the time of the read, and the entry's session is above both the first-read baseline (kept in the errors memo) and the acknowledged session, or that session's newest time evidence is at or after `acked_at`. A mark above the database's current session is void (a reset or replaced file). Received reports are never new.
  - Why: mutation is classified per command path, so a dismissal cannot be a flag on a read. `<cache>` is documented as safe to delete, so a user's decision must not live there. BugGrabber writes only when a UI session ends, and the next session is numbered higher, so per-database session watermarks are exact and need no per-message state.
- **M3-D30, `auto_backup` defaults to `daily`** (owner-visible; omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.3 D3, omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.11 D11).
  - The vision said (§5.6, §5.8): `auto_backup` is `off` or `daily`, default `off`; `daily` backs up before the day's first mutation of a target.
  - M3 does: `auto_backup` takes `off`, `daily` or `daily-copy`, default `daily`. `daily` clones only (`ClonePolicy::Required`: a filesystem that cannot reflink costs zero copied bytes and writes nothing; `statfs` makes btrfs and xfs eligible for an attempt). `daily-copy` also byte-copies, within `limits.backup_copy_max_mb` (4,096 MiB). There are two triggers: a pre-change checkpoint at most once per local day, and a post-session checkpoint (`backup create --auto`) after play. `status` and `backup list` report the configured mode and the observed capability apart, as `backups.auto` `{mode, capability: unknown|supported|unsupported, last: {at, result}}`. README states the change ("before milestone 3 this README said `off`"); plan approval approved it.
  - Why: defaults decide outcomes, and with `off` almost nobody gets the protection. On btrfs, which Omarchy installs, a backup costs milliseconds when made. Byte copies on ext4 need an opt-in.
- **M3-D35, `backup import`** (omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.10).
  - The vision said (§5.8): `backup [create | list | restore <id> | export <id> <file.tar.zst> | prune]`.
  - M3 does: it adds `backup import <FILE> -t T [--force]` (and `backup verify`, M3-D47). Import accepts only an archive shaped exactly as omaddons' exporter writes it. A first pass, before any write, checks entry types, names, the bounds, the metadata objects, an exact bijection between manifest and payload with every file's SHA-256, every entry's parent and the symlink graph. A second pass stages, re-hashes as it writes, creates links last and publishes a backup of kind `imported` with `integrity: verified`, `baseline: import` and `qualifying: false`. Another family is `wrong_flavor` unless `--force`. The rules and refusal reasons are in the §5.8 backup comment.
  - Why: an export that only `tar -x` can restore bypasses undo and the running guard. A hash match alone would still let an unlisted file, a second metadata object or a symlink parent put bytes where they do not belong.
- **M3-D47, backup integrity and `backup verify`** (omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.1 D1, omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.2 D2, omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.8 D8, omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.13 D13).
  - The vision said (§5.8): nothing on integrity; output shows counts and sizes only.
  - M3 does: every backup carries `integrity` (`metadata_only`, `verified` or `damaged`), `verified_at` and `baseline` (`capture`, `import` or `later`). `restorable` stays and now means structurally restorable and not damaged. `backup verify <ID>… [-t T]` hashes each backup under a reader reservation: with recorded hashes it compares; without, it records a `later` baseline and says that this cannot prove the capture was intact. A damaged backup makes the run `partial: true` with exit 0; `--dry-run` records nothing; no history line is written. `backup create --verify` records a `capture` baseline. A restore checks staged files against recorded hashes (`hash_mismatch`) and refuses a damaged backup (`state_corrupt`).
  - Why: a label that overstates its evidence is worse than none. Hashing every capture would break the 1 s budget for a 500 MB `WTF/`, so it is opt-in where it costs time and automatic where hashes exist.

**The strict change from M2: M3-D45, persisted formats fail closed** (omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.3 A3, omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.12 D12, omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.16).
- M2 did: the journal's `schema_version` was never compared, and a journal whose `prepared` line did not decode counted as `Unprepared`, so recovery pruned it with its snapshots.
- M3 does: journals are version 1.1, and the version is checked. A newer major is never recovered (a `journal_pending` warning that says `journal_too_new`; the target's own command fails `state_too_new` with `details.reason: "journal_too_new"`); a newer minor is, ignoring unknown fields. `parse` counts a torn last line (tolerated, as in M2) apart from complete lines it cannot decode. Any such line, or complete lines with no `prepared` line, leaves the journal, its in-flight lock, its stage and its snapshots in place (`journal_unreadable`; the target's own command fails `state_corrupt`), which is M2's manual-repair state. Undo's conflict analysis assumes an unreadable history line on the target touches everything it might (`undo_conflict`, `details.reason: "history_unreadable"`). Before staging, every engine transaction and undo refuses a newer target record, files index or registry with `state_too_new`, and checks again under the lock. One M2 behaviour changes: a journal with an undecodable complete line used to be pruned and is now kept and reported.
- What M3 cannot fix: an M2 build refuses only after its side effects, so no barrier it honours exists, and M3 claims none. `tests/compat_m2.rs` characterizes the `af10e34` build: it skips every M3 history line, and its `undo` of an install older than a restore puts that install's SavedVariables copies back over the restored ones with no conflict. Since `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.16`, journals that put settings back are written as `journal/<tx>.wtf.jsonl` with stages `stage/<tx>.wtf`, which `af10e34` never lists, so a restore interrupted right after its `prepared` line survives an M2 change and the next M3 change recovers it; M2 still recovers M3 install-type journals as its own. A restore interrupted past its first rename is not yet covered: `af10e34`'s orphan sweep can delete its undo snapshot an hour later (`omad-aepa`, open). README Limitations says not to change M3 state with a pre-M3 build (reading with one is safe).
- Why: the M2 behaviour was a latent hazard that deleted a transaction's journal and snapshots. M3's widget stamps one binary path, which makes mixed binaries more likely.

Other body changes M3 made are recorded in their topic comments rather than here: the `Wtf` root accepting `Rename` from `BackupRestore`, `History` admitting `Omarchy` and the Omarchy stage, old and trash rows (the §5.5 write-scope comment); `stamp:sha256:` digests for whole-tree renames, which change what the doctor contract's `before_hash` can hold, and `WTF.previous` kept outside `SNAPSHOT_MAX_BYTES` and reported in `snapshot_bytes` (the §5.5 journal and recovery comment).
