comments.text:
**§4.4, §4.6, §4.8, §5.11 and §8: external facts observed during M3 (omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.10, omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.2, omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.3.2, omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.3.3, omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.5, omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.12, omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.16).** Supersedes the statements named under each heading below; the body is not edited.

What: facts M3 observed on the development machine, in upstream sources and on live servers, each with its date and bead. The first were checked while planning and recorded in the milestone epic's ground-truth comment (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx`, §2, 2026-10-21, cited below as "plan §2.x"). The rest come from the spike F0 and the feature beads, all on 2026-10-22. None of the body's UNVERIFIED notes is among what they supersede: §4.6 carries none, and §8's were taken up before M3 (comments 710, 835, 898, 903 and 1008; where a modern client stores `checkAddonVersion` stays unlocated). What they supersede are statements the body makes without the mark, comment 606's BugGrabber note, and two UNVERIFIED notes of the M3 plan (§2.5: `FileView` across renames, and the window class of a game).

Why: §4 is the vision's record of verified external facts, dated 2026-10-14. The widget, `errors` and restore designs rest on the facts below, and several differ from what the body or the plan assumed.

**Omarchy 4.0.6 and Quickshell 0.3.2 plugins.** Observed on the live desktop on 2026-10-22 by `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.10` (F0): Hyprland 0.56.2, Qt 6.12.0, two monitors. A throwaway plugin (`service` + `bar-widget`) was copied into `<plugins>` for the session only, every omaddons run used a throwaway `HOME` and XDG directories, and `<config-omarchy>/shell.json` was byte-identical afterwards. Supersedes §4.6 "Saving a file under the plugins directory hot-reloads plugin code", §4.6 "Settings come from manifest `barWidget.defaults` + `barWidget.schema`" and §5.11's reinstall "detached (`Quickshell.execDetached`)". Refines §4.6's `FileView` line, and adds placement to its non-git install line.

- **Hot reload.** Any file event under `<plugins>` (top-level dot entries and `.git` aside), or a `rescanPlugins`, destroys and recreates every plugin's service and widgets, built-ins included (plan §2.5, from the shell's `inotifywait -m -r` watcher; F0 saw new instances on every reload). The shell debounces it 150 ms: two back-to-back renames gave one reload.
- **A hot reload never loads changed code at an unchanged file URL.** An in-place edit, a rename swap of the whole folder and an explicit `rescanPlugins` each brought back the previously compiled QML and `.pragma library` JS, with the library's state (a `Store.js` counter ran 1→5 across reloads). New code loaded only after `omarchy restart shell`, or from new file URLs: a new folder name, or a fixed folder whose `manifest.json` points `entryPoints` into a new subfolder (`h1/Service.qml`, then `h2/Service.qml`). That last shape, swapped with `RENAME_EXCHANGE`, brought up the new service, both widgets and fresh `.pragma` modules, kept the bar placement and needed no restart. `omarchy-plugin-validate` accepts such entry points.
- **`keepLoaded: true`** keeps the service, and its running child, across reloads. A reinstall to new URLs then runs new widgets against the old service until a shell restart, each side on its own `Store.js`.
- **A reload SIGKILLs every child of the service** within about 330 ms; no SIGTERM arrives. A child's own child survives, reparented to the user's systemd manager. Children run in the shell's process group, so a group signal would hit the shell.
- **Hidden entries stay invisible**, as §4.6 says: `PluginRegistry.localPluginIdForPath` drops every path whose first component starts with `.` (read again by `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.5.2` (E2) on 2026-10-22), so a dot-named stage triggers no reload.
- **`Process.environment` overlays the inherited environment:** one variable set, the other 187 identical to the shell's. `startDetached()` applies it the same way. From Quickshell's source (plan §2.5): `startDetached()` also applies the working directory, sends stdio to the null device and returns no pid or exit status; `Quickshell.execDetached([...])` takes an argv and no environment.
- **`running = false` sends SIGTERM and nothing more.** A child that traps it was alive 3 s later, with `running` still true and no `runningChanged`. `signal(9)` kills the pid, not its group: `exited(9, 1)` (the exit code is the signal number, status 1 is CrashExit), then `runningChanged(false)` in the same millisecond.
- **A missing binary** gives `runningChanged(false)` about 4 ms after start, `processId` null, and neither `started` nor `exited`.
- **The collectors are unbounded.** `StdioCollector` appends to one buffer, and `SplitParser` grows until its delimiter arrives (plan §2.5, from the source). 1 MiB of multi-line stdout and a 4 MiB single line each arrived whole. `streamFinished` fired before `exited` in 17 of 17 runs (10 B to 4 MiB, 0 to 10 ms apart). NDJSON lines on stderr reached a `SplitParser` within 1 ms of being written.
- **One `service` instance serves every monitor**, created before the widgets. In a widget's `Component.onCompleted`, `bar` is still null, so `bar.shell.serviceFor(id)` answers nothing; a 500 ms poll bound it on its first tick. Only one `IpcHandler` per target works: the service-owned handler logged no "Handler was registered but will not be used" line, while each of 16 other targets with a handler in a bar widget logged one per load. `omarchy-shell <target> <function>` reaches it, and `omarchy-shell shell ping` answers `ok` (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.5.3` (E3)).
- **Manifest `barWidget.defaults` and `schema` are inert** in 4.0.6: nothing renders or applies them, and a `service` receives no settings. `omarchy plugin enable` writes only `{ "id": "<id>" }` into `<config-omarchy>/shell.json`. Disabling (`PluginRegistry.setEnabled(id, false)`) removes the whole layout entry, inline settings included (plan §2.5; E3 read the same in the source).
- **Placement.** `omarchy-bar put <id> --section right` run 16 ms after the files landed: exit 1, empty stdout, stderr `omarchy-bar: <id> is not a known widget; run 'omarchy plugin list'`. The next try: exit 0, stdout exactly `<id> is on the bar`, the same on repeat. After a fresh copy the shell answers `unknown` for about 390 ms, then `not ready` for about 670 ms (which `omarchy-bar` retries itself), then places it. With no shell: exit 0 after about 3.3 s, empty stdout, stderr `omarchy-shell is not running; <id> was not put on the bar`.
- **Toasts and `summon`.** The shell is the notification daemon (plan §2.5: no mako, dunst or swaync). `omarchy-notification-send --app-name <app> -g <glyph> -u low "<title>" "<body>" --exec omarchy-shell shell summon <id> {}` shows a toast at the top right of the focused monitor. Clicked with the panel closed, it opened the focused monitor's copy. With the panel open, the toast is drawn above it and the panel stayed open; a `toggle` toast closed it. For bar widgets the shell drops the payload, and `summon <id>` without one fills in `{}`. From the service, `shell.summon(id, "")` returned true and opened the focused copy, and returned true again without closing an open one; `shell.hide(id)` closed it.
- **`FileView { watchChanges: true }` survives renames** (5 renames gave 5 `fileChanged`, each followed by `loaded` with the new bytes), in-place writes, and delete-then-recreate (`fileChanged` + `loadFailed(2)`, then `fileChanged` + `loaded`). A missing file is picked up once created if its directory exists, never when the directory itself appears later. This resolves the plan's UNVERIFIED note.
- **`inotifywait` on fsx writes.** `-m -q -e close_write,moved_to` printed two lines per write (`MOVED_TO`, then `CLOSE_WRITE,CLOSE`), because fsx closes its temp file after the rename. `-e moved_to` alone printed one, about 2 ms after the write. On a missing directory it starts and exits 1 at once.
- **`PanelKeyCatcher`** (a `KeyboardPanel` around a 40-row `Flickable`, keys sent by `wtype`): Enter emits `returnRequested` and then `activateRequested`; Space only `activateRequested`; `x` and `X` both `deleteRequested`; `h`/`l`/`j`/`k` and the arrows `moveRequested(dx, dy)`, consumed so the `Flickable` did not scroll; Tab and Shift-Tab `tabRequested(1)` and `tabRequested(-1)`; Esc `closeRequested`; other letters `textKey`. A summoned panel took keyboard focus with no click.
- **Found while testing on 2026-10-22.** Plugin files resolve sibling types (`PlainLabel`) only when loaded by `file://` URL, as Omarchy loads them, not under a `qs` root's own `qs:` scheme (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.4` (F4)). A `var` signal argument turns a JS array into a Qt sequence that `Array.isArray` rejects (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.2` (F2)). In a windowless `qs` on the live display, `running` false arrived after `exited`, late enough to reach the lane's next process (F2).

The shipped widget's use of these is in the §5.11 widget comment: the doorbell watches `moved_to` only (M3-D4), `keepLoaded` stays false (M3-D5), the code lives in `<plugins>/omaddons/r-<code hash>/` (M3-D6 and M3-D7 as amended by F0), the reinstall is `Process.startDetached()` under `Build.CONTEXT`, a stop is `signal(15)` then `signal(9)` after 5 s with the lane held until the child exits, and stdout over `WIDGET_OUTPUT_MAX_BYTES` (8 MiB) is discarded after collection, so the CLI bounds its own output.

**The window of a Wine game on Hyprland.** F0 on 2026-10-22, applied by `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.6.8` (F8). Resolves the plan's UNVERIFIED note on a game window's class and complements comment 903 (§8, Wine process naming). §4.6's line on Hyprland raw events stands, with this data format.

- `rawEvent` gives `openwindow` with data `<address without 0x>,<workspace>,<class>,<title>`, and `closewindow` with `<address>`.
- An agent can launch the 3.3.5a client through its desktop launcher (umu with GE-Proton, local realm). The window opened after about 5 s at the login screen, under XWayland, with class `steam_app_wow335` and title `World of Warcraft`. The class comes from the launcher's umu `GAMEID`, not from the exe, and the launcher's `StartupWMClass` (`wow.exe`) does not match it. A class names the launcher, not the game.
- The game outlives its window. In the one timed close, `closewindow` arrived 24.4 s after the close request, and `Wow.exe` exited 451 ms after `closewindow`.
- Not observed: a Battle.net client's game window. Omarchy's window rule that gives every window of the Battle.net prefix the class `steam_app_battlenet` (plan §2.5) stays unchecked for game windows.
- So the widget filters no class: every `openwindow` and `closewindow` asks for `status --cached` after a 500 ms debounce, and a close while a client runs is followed up at +2, +5 and +15 s.

**SavedVariables file formats.** Adds to §4.4, which names paths but no format. Measured on the development machine: the structure of 79 files (plan §2.6, 2026-10-21), then byte by byte the 18 SavedVariables files of the 3.3.5a client (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.2` (B2), 2026-10-22).

- The modern clients write no indentation and no `-- [n]` comments. 3.3.5a writes tab indentation and `-- [n]` after positional fields (12 of the 18 files indented, 6 with `-- [1]`).
- Both write CRLF line endings and a leading blank line: 18 of 18 3.3.5a files start with CRLF and use CRLF only. The plan had named CRLF for modern clients alone. The two writers differ only in tabs and `-- [n]`, so a reader must not tell them apart by line endings.
- Both use only bracketed keys, a trailing comma after every field, and double-quoted strings that escape only `\\`, `\"` and the newline (`\n`). Every other byte is written raw: UTF-8, and control bytes (0x01 to 0x03 appear unescaped in a public 2026 sample).
- Not observed: which client build first wrote the modern form.
- `src/lua.rs` reads both with one grammar; the `savedvariables` fuzz seeds include `modern-crlf` and `legacy-tabs`.

**BugGrabber and BugSack.** Supersedes §4.4's BugGrabber bullet where they differ (its mirror, the v12.x `time`, the r152 chunk bound, the stack-frame form) and comment 606's "BugGrabber has no verified keyless source". From WowAce's SVN and BugGrabber's and BugSack's sources (plan §2.6, 2026-10-21), and from live requests by `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.3.2` (C2), `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.3.3` (C3) and `omad-xork` (2026-10-22).

- **Where it lives.** BugGrabber's upstream is WowAce SVN, `https://repos.wowace.com/wow/bug-grabber/` (Apache 2.4.18, Subversion 1.9.3, mod_dav_svn). §4.4's GitHub `hippuli/BugGrabber` is a mirror, byte-identical to v12.1.0 (trunk r401) on 2026-10-21. BugSack's GitHub release does not bundle `!BugGrabber`, WoWInterface lists it only as discontinued (comment 606 found no listing), and Tukui does not have it.
- **The server over plain HTTP.** GET works; HEAD returns 401. `PROPFIND` with `Depth: 1` on `tags/` returns every tag with its `version-name`, the tag directory's last-changed revision, in one 207 response of about 32 KB. `GET …/!svn/bc/<rev>/<path>` serves a file or a directory listing as of that revision and never changes, while a tag is an ordinary directory that can be edited or re-created. `OPTIONS` with an `activity-collection-set` body returns `svn-youngest-rev`.
- **Tags.** 98 on 2026-10-21, the newest stable v12.1.0 at r401. On 2026-10-22 the newest stable was v12.1.1 at r403, with v12.1.0 still at r401 (C2). v12.1.1's TOC lists interfaces 11508, 11509, 16001, 20505, 20506, 30405, 38002, 40402, 50503, 50504, 120100, 120105 and 120007 (C3).
- **Legacy builds**, from a walk of the trunk log (C3, about 45 sequential requests). r130 is the last trunk revision declaring Interface 20400, for 2.4.3 (r131 says 30000); its tree commits its libraries and has no externals. For 3.3.5a, r152: r153 and r154 still say 30300 but begin the 4.0 port, and r155 says 40000. For 4.3.4, r184 to r186 say 40300 (r187: 50001); for 5.4.8 the last 50400 revision is r203 (r204: 60000); both carry `@localization(…)@` keywords in `locales.lua`. For 1.12.1, trunk has no build (it starts at r122); the 1.12-era tree is `tmp/trunk/!BugGrabber/`, whose last revision declaring 11200 is r43 (r44 says 20000): two files, no `.pkgmeta`, no keywords (omad-xork).
- **Packaging.** `.pkgmeta` in tags and trunk, unchanged since r134, is only `package-as: "!BugGrabber"`. The only keyword is the TOC's `## Version: @project-version@`, and `BugGrabber.lua` and `load.xml` contain no `@`, so there are no debug or alpha blocks. C2's live probe assembled v12.1.1 at r403 within that subset, in six requests.
- **Modern schema** (the v12.1.0 source). `MAX_BUGGRABBER_ERRORS = 500`. An entry is `{message, session, time = time(), counter, stack?, locals?}`; a repeat bumps `counter`, moves `time` to the latest occurrence, updates `session` and moves the entry to the end. DB keys: `session` (+1 per UI load, reset to 1 by `/bugsack reset`), `errors`, `lastSanitation`, `stopnag`; older DBs may still hold `save`, `limit` and `throttle`. C2's live probe found v12.1.1 still building `message =`, `session =`, `time = time()` and `counter = 1`.
- **`time` has four meanings in two types**, with no version field: a local-time string of the first capture (v10.1 to v12.0.2), a string of the last occurrence (v12.0.3 to v12.0.9), a unix integer of the last occurrence (v12.0.11 on), and in r152 a string of the first capture in the session. §4.4's `time=unix_epoch_int` holds only from v12.0.11.
- **r152** (2010, Interface 30300, GPL v2+). `message` is a string or an array of at most 7 chunks of at most 980 bytes, plus `type` (`error` or `event`). There is no `stack` or `locals` key: both follow `"\nLocals:|r\n"` inside `message`, which ends in `"\n  ---"`. Paths drop `Interface\AddOns\`; an addon shows as `Folder-version\`, a library as `Major-Minor (Folder)`. Duplicates merge only within a session. The DB has `limit=50`, `save` and `throttle`.
- **Stack lines come in three eras:** `Interface\AddOns\X\f.lua:12:` (3.3.5a and old retail), `[string "@Interface/AddOns/X/f.lua"]:12:` (about 2020 to 2025) and `[Interface/AddOns/X/f.lua]:12:` (retail 11.1.5 and later, current Classic clients). The message's location is cut to about 57 characters with a leading `...`. §4.4's `Interface\AddOns\<Folder>\…` is the first era only.
- **BugSack's received reports.** `OnBugComm` in BugSack's `core.lua` stores an error another player sends over the addon channel in `BugGrabberDB.errors`. It sets `source` to the sender and `session` to the current local session, keeps the sender's `time` and `counter`, and checks for no duplicate. BugGrabber never sets `source`. So by session a received report looks like a new local error; only `source` tells it apart. `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.3` (B3) takes an entry's origin from `source`'s presence, and `errors` counts received reports apart and never as new (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.2.6` (B6), on fixtures).
- **Limits of the evidence.** No BugGrabber data exists on the development machine (2026-10-21). Every decoder test runs on synthetic files built from this structure in both writer formats (B2), and `errors` has not yet read a capture from a real play session (README Known limitations).

**Rename and mount semantics.** Adds to §4.8's `renameat2(2)` line and to §8's "`RENAME_EXCHANGE` and reflink are unavailable on some filesystems". Observed in a bind-mount sandbox during the plan's review (plan §2.4 item 16, 2026-10-21). M3's tests then exercise the refusals built on it (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.5` (D5), `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.7` (D7) and `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.9` (D9), 2026-10-22); none of them asserts the errno itself.

- A rename across two mount points fails with `EXDEV`, even when both mounts show the same filesystem: two bind mounts of one filesystem share a device number. A device comparison therefore cannot prove a rename will work; the mount id (`statx` `STATX_MNT_ID`, Linux 5.8 and later) can.
- Renaming a mount point fails with `EBUSY`.
- So a capable filesystem is not enough for an atomic `WTF/` exchange: `WTF/` must not be a mount point, and `<meta>/stage/` must be on the client's mount. `fsx::mount_id` and an exchange probe (two empty files exchanged in the transaction's own stage; `EINVAL` or `ENOSYS` means unsupported, while `EXDEV` stays an I/O error) check this before a restore copies anything, and the mount ids again under the lock.
- The development machine lets an unprivileged process bind-mount in a user and mount namespace (`unshare -rm`), so these tests use real bind mounts. A `WTF/` mounted over itself is refused `filesystem_unsupported` with `wtf_is_mount_point`, and an `Interface/.omaddons` on its own mount with `stage_cross_mount` (D5). A SavedVariables folder on its own mount is refused `stage_cross_mount` for that file (D7). D9 ran a disk-full export in a 64 KiB tmpfs inside the same kind of namespace. Where namespaces are not allowed, the scenes print `SKIP`.

**The last M2 build against M3 state (af10e34).** Observed by `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.12` (D12) on 2026-10-22, and again after `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.16` the same day, with `tests/compat_m2.rs`. That test is ignored by default: it builds af10e34's release binary into `target/compat/` and runs it on homes a debug build of the current binary prepared. Supersedes nothing in the body. It replaces the plan's expectation (§2.3) that an M2 binary recovering an M3 restore journal is stopped by `Scope::Wtf` at its first `WTF/` rename: it never gets that far. M3-D45, the fail-closed rule from M3 on, is in the §5.5 journal and recovery comment.

- **An interrupted restore, first observation (D12).** af10e34 cannot parse an M3 restore's `prepared` line, so to it the journal is unprepared, and its recovery prunes the journal and the in-flight lock unread. After an interrupted whole or `--addon` restore (`engine.restore.exchanged=abort`) and an af10e34 `install`: exit 0, `WTF/` untouched, the journal deleted, the stage kept with the pre-restore tree or file, and only the client half of the snapshot left. The next M3 change: exit 0, no warning. An hour on, M3's orphan sweep deleted that stage.
- **After .4.16.** af10e34 lists only `journal/<tx>.jsonl` and sweeps only `stage/<tx>` whose name parses as a ULID. Journals whose `prepared` line puts settings back (`writes_wtf`, or any `wtf` or `saved_variables` history op) are now `journal/<tx>.wtf.jsonl`, and restore stages are `stage/<tx>.wtf`. In `every_m3_journal_is_recovered_by_m2_or_left_for_m3` (each shape crashed right after `prepared`, then an af10e34 `install`), af10e34 recovered an M3 install and an undo of an install as its own. It never saw a whole restore, an `--addon` restore or the undo of either (that last undo has `writes_wtf` false but `saved_variables` ops), and left `WTF/` alone. The next M3 change recovered each (`journal_recovered`, rolled back), at once and with everything aged two hours. af10e34's orphan sweep still removes the transaction's snapshot folders after an hour, since their names did not change; M3 recovered regardless, because at that crash point they were still empty. Past the first rename they hold the tree the restore replaced, which that sweep can delete (`omad-aepa`, open).
- **A committed whole or `--addon` restore, then af10e34's `undo` of an older install:** exit 0, warnings `history_lines_skipped` and `snapshot_only_copy`. It put the install-time `Foo.lua` back over the restored one with no conflict reported, left no journal, and kept both halves of the restore's snapshot. M3's `status` afterwards: exit 0, no warning.
- **M3 `dismiss` and `widget` history lines, then af10e34's `history` and bare `undo`:** `history` warns `history_lines_skipped`; the undo reverted the newest line it could read, the older install, and put its SavedVariables back blindly.
- af10e34's `status`, `list` and `history` leave an interrupted restore's journal and `WTF/` alone (asserted).
- From its source (plan §2.9, 2026-10-21): `Prepared.schema_version` is written and never compared, and a newer record refuses it only at `store::save`, after its folders moved.
- README Known limitations quotes these: do not change M3 state with a pre-M3 build; reading with it is safe.

Contract: none. These facts add no wire name; the designs built on them are recorded in the §5.5, §5.8 and §5.11 comments.

comments.text:
**§5.13 politeness and safety constants, as shipped in M3 (D22) (omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.1.2 (A2), .1.5 (A5), .2.1 (B1), .2.3 (B3), .2.5 (B5), .2.6 (B6), .3.1 (C1), .3.2 (C2), .4.1 (D1), .4.2 (D2), .4.3 (D3), .4.4 (D4), .4.10 (D10), .5.1 (E1), .5.2 (E2), .5.3 (E3), .6.1 (F1), .6.2 (F2), .6.6 (F6), .6.8 (F8), .6.9 (F9)).** Adds to §5.13's tables; supersedes the plan's constants table (the milestone epic's "Contract additions, part 2", §7.11) where it differs, as listed at the end. The body is not edited. A short id `.4.10` means `omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.4.10`; plan keys (A1 … F9) resolve through the key → id map, the milestone epic's first comment.

**What.** M3 adds 40 constants to `src/limits.rs` and none to `src/politeness.rs`. Each new limit has a `REGISTRY` row and a `LIMIT_NAMES` entry, and the `limit_registries` snapshot (politeness and limits registries together) grew from 55 to 95 rows: exactly these 40. The widget's own limits live in `omarchy/Model.js`, because QML cannot read `limits.rs`; two of them are held to Rust-side values by `tests/omarchy_widget.rs`.

**Why.** D22: behaviour toward upstream hosts and the user's machine is auditable in one place. Common rule 15 made every untrusted or user-sized input M3 reads (SavedVariables, BugGrabber files, WowAce listings, backup trees, import archives, history, Omarchy's files) bounded by a named constant, with exhaustion reported as truncated or incomplete, never as a clean result.

**How to read the list.** `NAME` = value (registry unit; config key when `config.toml` can change it): what it bounds. Bead in parentheses. Durations are registered in milliseconds, so 7 days reads 604,800,000 ms in the registry.

### `src/limits.rs`: privacy and history
- `REDACTOR_MAX_NAMES` = 4,096 (count): account, realm and character names the privacy redactor learns per client or archive; any other maps to `account ?`, `realm ?` or `character ?` (A5).
- `HISTORY_TAIL_RUNS` = 16 (count): runs with an undoable entry the history projection keeps whole; backup and settings runs never count (A2).
- `HISTORY_TAIL_MAX_BYTES` = 1 MiB (bytes): the projection's size cap; a run cut by it is marked partial (A2).

### `src/limits.rs`: SavedVariables parser
- `LUA_MAX_DEPTH` = 64 (count): table nesting followed, building or skipping; the 65th level records `DepthLimit` and resynchronizes (B1).
- `LUA_MAX_NODES` = 2,000,000 (count): values built per parse, tables included; skipped globals build none (B1).
- `LUA_MAX_ISSUES` = 64 (count): issues recorded per parse; past it only a count (B1).

### `src/limits.rs`: Lua errors
- `BUGGRABBER_MAX_ENTRIES` = 5,000 (count): entries decoded per database, newest first; BugGrabber itself keeps 500 (B3).
- `ERRORS_MAX_ACCOUNTS` = 32 (count): account folders examined per client; past it, `coverage: truncated` (B5).
- `ERRORS_MAX_FILES` = 64 (count): candidate BugGrabber files parsed per client (B5).
- `ERRORS_MESSAGE_MAX_CHARS` = 300 (chars): a message's first line with `--raw-details` (B5).
- `ERRORS_STACK_LINES` = 6 (count): frames shown by default (B5).
- `ERRORS_STACK_LINES_VERBOSE` = 40 (count): frames with `-v` or `--raw-details` (B5).
- `ERRORS_LOCALS_MAX_CHARS` = 4,096 (chars): locals with `--raw-details` (B5).
- `ERRORS_CHUNK_MAX_CHARS` = 40 (chars): `[string "…"]` chunk contents with `--raw-details` (B5).
- `ERRORS_MAX_TOTAL_BYTES` = 256 MiB (bytes): BugGrabber bytes one `errors` run reads, every client together; a file past it is `over_budget` (B6).
- `ERRORS_NEW_MAX_AGE` = 7 days (ms): a BugGrabber file last written longer ago has no new errors (B6).
- `ERRORS_SHOWN_PER_ADDON` = 10 (count): errors one addon lists in `errors`' output, new first, then the most frequent; `entries` and `count` still count all. Added so the widget's `errors --limit 10` read stays under `WIDGET_OUTPUT_MAX_BYTES` (F6).

### `src/limits.rs`: WowAce trees
- `WOWACE_TREE_MAX_FILES` = 2,000 (count): entries one listing or tag list names, and files one tree holds; past it, `too_many_entries` (C1).
- `WOWACE_TREE_MAX_DIRS` = 200 (count): directory listings one tree fetches (C2).
- `WOWACE_TREE_MAX_DEPTH` = 8 (count): directory depth below the tree's root (C2).
- `WOWACE_TREE_MAX_REQUESTS` = 2,500 (count): requests one tree costs, retries included (C2).
- Every directory is listed before any file is fetched, so the directory, depth and file bounds fail with nothing downloaded; each is `archive_too_large` naming the constant.

### `src/limits.rs`: backups
- `BACKUP_TREE_MAX_ENTRIES` = 200,000 (count): entries walked in one `WTF/` a backup copies; then `archive_too_large` (D1).
- `BACKUP_TREE_MAX_DEPTH` = 16 (count): depth walked, applied to every entry (D1).
- `BACKUP_CAPTURE_ATTEMPTS` = 2 (count): captures tried before one that changed while copied is published `best_effort` (D2).
- `BACKUP_MIN_FREE` = 2,048 MiB (bytes; registry key `backup_min_free`, set in `config.toml` as `limits.backup_min_free_mb`, 0 to 1,048,576 MiB, 0 turns it off): free space beside a client's backups below which a manual backup warns `backup_space_low` and automatic ones reclaim, then skip (D2, D3).
- `BACKUP_COPY_MAX` = 4,096 MiB (bytes; registry key `backup_copy_max`, `limits.backup_copy_max_mb`, same range, 0 turns it off): apparent bytes of a client's automatic byte-copy backups, `daily-copy` only; past it, eligible ones are reclaimed oldest first, or the capture is skipped (D3).
- `BACKUP_STALE_AFTER` = 7 days (ms): a client whose newest qualifying capture is older (or that has none) is offered `backup create` by `backup list` and `status`. Defined by D2 under D11's name and value; D11 adds no second constant.
- `BACKUP_AUTO_KEEP_DAYS` = 7 (count; `limits.backup_auto_keep_days`, 1 to 100): local days of automatic backups kept per client (D4).
- `BACKUP_AUTO_KEEP_DAYS_MAX` = 100 (count): the most that key accepts (D4).
- `BACKUP_MIN_AGE` = 24 h (ms): no backup younger is pruned automatically, nor by `--keep` or `--older-than`; `created_at` decides it (D4).

### `src/limits.rs`: backup import
- `BACKUP_IMPORT_MAX_ENTRIES` = 200,000 (count): entries in an imported archive (D10).
- `BACKUP_IMPORT_MAX_BYTES` = 8 GiB (bytes): what an import may expand to (D10).
- `BACKUP_IMPORT_MAX_PATH` = 4,096 (bytes): one entry's path (D10).
- `BACKUP_IMPORT_MAX_META_BYTES` = 64 KiB (bytes): one entry's PAX or long-name records, checked before the body is read (D10).
- `BACKUP_IMPORT_MAX_MANIFEST_BYTES` = 128,000,000 (bytes): the archive's `manifest.json`, defined as `BACKUP_IMPORT_MAX_ENTRIES` × 640, nearly three times a real entry, so the entry cap is what binds; `backup.json` and `addons.json` keep `DISCOVERY_FILE_MAX_BYTES` (1 MiB) (D10).
- `BACKUP_IMPORT_MAX_WINDOW_LOG` = 24 (count): the zstd decoder window an import allows, 16 MiB, refused before it is allocated (D10).
- Existing limits an import also applies: `ARCHIVE_MAX_RATIO` (200:1, once the expansion passes `ARCHIVE_RATIO_FLOOR`, 32 MiB) and `DISCOVERY_FILE_MAX_BYTES` (1 MiB).

### `src/limits.rs`: the widget and Omarchy
- `WIDGET_READBACK_MAX_BYTES` = 64 KiB (bytes): an installed widget's `manifest.json` or `Build.js` read back; a larger one is not one omaddons wrote (E1).
- `OMARCHY_COMMAND_TIMEOUT` = 10 s (ms): each run of an Omarchy tool (`omarchy-plugin-validate`, `omarchy-shell`, `omarchy-bar`, `omarchy-plugin-disable`) is killed after it (E2).
- `OMARCHY_SHELL_JSON_MAX_BYTES` = 4 MiB (bytes): Omarchy's `shell.json` read for the widget's place on the bar; past it the widget counts as not placed (E2).
- `OMARCHY_PING_TIMEOUT` = 2 s (ms): `omarchy status`'s `omarchy-shell shell ping`; a shell that has not answered `ok` by then is not running (E3).

### `src/politeness.rs`
- Unchanged since `af10e34`. The WowAce source goes through the shared HTTP stack: `MAX_CONCURRENT_PER_HOST` = 3 (a tree is fetched one request at a time in any case), `MAX_RETRIES` = 3 with `BACKOFF_BASE` 500 ms, `BACKOFF_MAX` 8 s and `RETRY_AFTER_CAP` 60 s, `API_READ_TIMEOUT` 30 s, `DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT` 300 s, `SOURCE_RECHECK_MIN_INTERVAL` 15 min.
- Byte caps WowAce shares, from `limits.rs`: listings and `.pkgmeta` are API responses under `API_RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES` (64 MiB); a tree's files together are under `DOWNLOAD_MAX_BYTES` (512 MiB, `limits.download_max_bytes`).

### `omarchy/Model.js`: the widget's limits
- `WIDGET_LOCAL_DEADLINE_SEC` = 20: a local read's deadline from its start; a UI choice, pinned by `model.test.js` (F1).
- `WIDGET_NETWORK_DEADLINE_SEC` = 600: a network read's inactivity deadline, reset by every progress line. `tests/omarchy_widget.rs` holds it at or above the longest request `politeness.rs` allows: (`MAX_RETRIES` + 1) × `API_READ_TIMEOUT` + `MAX_RETRIES` × `RETRY_AFTER_CAP` = 300 s (F1).
- `WIDGET_KILL_GRACE_SEC` = 5: SIGTERM, then `signal(9)` this much later; F0 confirmed a SIGTERM-trapping child outlives `running = false` (F1).
- `WIDGET_OUTPUT_MAX_BYTES` = 8 MiB: stdout above it is discarded as `oversized`. The output-cap test in `tests/omarchy_widget.rs` holds every template's worst case under it (12 clients × 400 addons for the list-shaped outputs; search and changelog by their own limits) (F1, F6, F9).
- `WIDGET_STREAM_GRACE_SEC` = 2: how long stdout may stay open after `exited` before the run completes anyway, since a killed omaddons can leave a child holding the pipe; pinned by `model.test.js` (F2, not in the plan).

### Values outside the registries (local choices, not safety limits)
- Rust:
  - `errors --limit` defaults to 10 addons per client (`app::errors::DEFAULT_LIMIT`; 0 is `usage`).
  - `status`' `errors.top` holds at most 5 (`TOP_MAX`).
  - Backup ids resolve from a prefix of 8 or more characters (`backup::ID_PREFIX_MIN`).
  - Prune retries a busy victim once after 50 ms (`backup::prune::PROBE_RETRY`).
  - `omarchy-bar put` is tried 5 times, 200 ms apart (`PUT_ATTEMPTS`, `PUT_RETRY`), covering the shell's `unknown` window after a fresh install.
  - The widget's code folder is `r-` and 16 hex of its code hash (`CODE_HASH_HEX`); a precondition token is four 16-hex fields.
  - Export: zstd level 3, 256 KiB chunks, 8 in flight, archive mode 0600; backups are stored 0700 (dirs) and 0600 (`backup.json`).
- Widget, `Model.js`: `AUTO_CHECK_INTERVAL_MS` 15 min (F8), `NETWORK_QUEUE_MAX` 4 queued network reads, `LABEL_MAX_CHARS` 120 (a `--reason` label), `NOTES_MAX_CHARS` 400 (release notes shown).
- Widget, `Service.qml` timing: doorbell debounce 150 ms, watcher retry 5 s (30 s while `<cache>` is missing), fallback poll 15 s with a panel open and at most 30 s while a client runs (else `refreshIntervalSec`), window-event debounce 500 ms, follow-up refreshes 2, 5 and 15 s after a window closes while a client runs, a view's data re-read when older than 10 s; `BarWidget.qml` retries binding its service every 200 ms.
- Widget settings bounds (manifest and `Model.SETTING_RULES`): `panelWidth` 400–800 (540), `refreshIntervalSec` 30–3600 (300).
- Templates pass `--limit 50` to `backup list`, `--limit 10` to `errors` and `--limit 20` to `search`.

### Planned but not shipped, or shipped differently
- Five constants were not in the plan: `ERRORS_SHOWN_PER_ADDON` (F6), `BACKUP_AUTO_KEEP_DAYS_MAX` (D4), `BACKUP_IMPORT_MAX_MANIFEST_BYTES` (D10, a spec defect: a 1 MiB manifest bound would refuse to import any `WTF/` over about 4,600 entries), `WIDGET_READBACK_MAX_BYTES` (E1) and `OMARCHY_SHELL_JSON_MAX_BYTES` (E2). Every planned constant exists under its planned name and value.
- The registry's config key for `BACKUP_MIN_FREE` and `BACKUP_COPY_MAX` is `backup_min_free` and `backup_copy_max` (bytes), because the registry requires `config_key` to be the lowercase name; `config.toml` takes MiB under `limits.backup_min_free_mb` and `limits.backup_copy_max_mb`, as planned.
- `BACKUP_STALE_AFTER` came with D2, not D11.
- The plan placed `API_RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES` among the politeness values; it is a `limits.rs` constant (64 MiB).
- `Model.js` gained `WIDGET_STREAM_GRACE_SEC` (F2).

comments.author: FierceWren
comments.text: **§5.8 backup retention after the pre-change backup (omad-k2ns).** Completes comment 1237, which recorded the gap as open. The automatic backup taken before the day's first change now runs backup retention (M3-D32) like every other backup: in `engine::tx::pre_change`, after the backup is published, outside the lock, the new backup pinned; a failure is only `retention_failed` (fix `omaddons backup prune -t <target>`) and the change goes ahead. `tests/backup_auto.rs` `pre_change_backups_are_thinned_by_day_as_they_are_made`: nine days of one change a day keep the newest seven days' backups (all nine before the fix), and a pass that cannot delete leaves the change committed with `retention_failed`. No wire name changes; README's Known issues entry is removed.

comments.author: FierceWren
comments.text:
**§5.5 journal and recovery: a settings transaction's snapshots are named `<tx>.wtf` (omad-aepa).** Completes comments 1236 and 1242 (the `af10e34` characterization), which recorded this as open.

What: a restore, a `--addon` restore and the undo of either now keep both halves of their undo snapshot as `<meta>/snapshots/<tx>.wtf/` and `<state>/snapshots/<tx>.wtf/`, like their journal (`journal/<tx>.wtf.jsonl`) and their stage (`stage/<tx>.wtf`). Every other transaction keeps the bare names, which `af10e34` recovers as its own.

Why: `af10e34`'s orphan sweep removes a snapshot folder named by a bare id once it is an hour old, if no journal it can list and no history line names its transaction, and its `AddOns/` is empty. A restore crashed past its first rename keeps the replaced `WTF/` in `WTF.previous`. That is the only copy when the filesystem cannot clone, since no `before_restore` backup is made there. The sweep deleted it, and M3's recovery then stopped with `unexpected_state`. The new compat test reproduces this on the unfixed engine.

How:
- One predicate names all three: `history::puts_settings_back(ops)` (any `wtf` or `saved_variables` op), which `Prepared::puts_settings_back` combines with `writes_wtf`.
- Writers choose the name: `SnapshotRoots::for_wtf_tx`, `ClientPaths::snapshots_wtf` and `Paths::state_snapshot_wtf`. The undo of a partial restore decides from its planned ops, as its journal will.
- Readers find a transaction's snapshot under either name, `.wtf` first (`engine::retention::snapshot_of`, `state_snapshot_of`). So restores committed before the change stay undoable.
- Retention, the orphan sweep, `dead_snapshots`, `fsx::prune`'s locations and the backup inventory's `WTF.previous` count treat both names alike.
- Recovery needed nothing new, because journal steps record absolute paths.
- `state/paths.rs` stays free of filesystem calls; the by-existence lookups live in `engine::retention` and `backup::inventory`.

Tests:
- `tests/compat_m2.rs` `every_interrupted_settings_change_survives_m2_two_hours_on`: 4 shapes, each crashed at every step (28 cases: after `prepared`, around each journaled rename, after `swapped`, the record and the history line). In every case, with everything aged two hours, an `af10e34` install leaves both halves. M3 recovers the transaction, and `WTF/` equals the pre-command tree, rolled back or rolled forward and then undone. On the unfixed engine it fails with `unexpected_state`.
- The `engine_crash.rs` restore oracles now require the `.wtf` halves and no bare ones.
- Unit and integration tests cover the names and old-name reads (`restore.rs`, `tests/restore_addon.rs`), retention and the sweep (`retention.rs`), and the inventory.

Contract: no JSON wire name changes. The on-disk layout adds `snapshots/<tx>.wtf/` on both sides; README's Transactions section and file table say so. README's Known limitations now quotes the extended test, and the Known issues entry is gone.

comments.author: FierceWren
comments.text:
**§5.8 backup: a restore or export that finds a damaged backup records it (omad-mc1i).** Completes comment 1237 and M3-D47; supersedes D8's `hash_mismatch` fix (`backup list`).

What: when `backup restore` (whole or `--addon`) or `backup export` reads a backup file that differs from its recorded hash, it still fails `hash_mismatch` ("backup … is damaged", not retryable, `details.backup`). Two things are new:
- The error's fix is `omaddons backup verify <id> -t <target>`.
- Before returning, the command records `integrity: damaged` in the backup's `backup.json`, so `backup list` stops calling it verified and restorable. It also rings the doorbell.

Why: M3-D47 says a label that overstates evidence is worse than none. After a refused restore, the backup still read `verified (…)` and `restorable: true` until someone ran `backup verify`. The restore and the export read the backup's own bytes: a clone of them, a copy of them, or a stream of them. A mismatch there is the same evidence `backup verify` has, so recording it does not overstate anything.

How:
- One constructor builds the error at the three sites: `backup::verify::mismatch`.
- One handler, `backup::verify::damage_found`, runs on the failure path. It writes the description through fsx (`Writer::Backup`, untracked, as `verify`'s own `record` does) under the backup reservation the command already holds, so a prune still finds the backup busy. Recording is best effort: the `hash_mismatch` stands either way.
- `backup verify` remains the authority. Run as the fix, it re-hashes and records what it finds, `verified` again if the bytes were put back.

Tests: `tests/restore.rs`, `tests/restore_addon.rs` and `tests/backup_export.rs` assert the fix argv and that `backup list` shows `integrity: damaged`, `restorable: false` after the refusal. The whole-restore test runs the fix, which reports `damaged`. The export test puts the bytes back and runs the fix, which finds the backup whole.

Contract: no new wire name. The `hash_mismatch` fix argv for backups changes. README's error table and `backup restore` text say so.

comments.author: FierceWren
comments.text:
**§5.11 Omarchy tools run in their own process group (omad-09iu).** Completes comment 1239 (the widget as shipped) and adds one constant to comment 1241.

What: `src/omarchy/shell.rs` starts each Omarchy tool (`omarchy-plugin-validate`, `omarchy-shell`, `omarchy-bar`, `omarchy-plugin-disable`) in its own process group, with the user's environment inherited unchanged (M3-D6). A tool that times out (`OMARCHY_COMMAND_TIMEOUT`, the ping `OMARCHY_PING_TIMEOUT`) is stopped with its whole group: SIGTERM, then SIGKILL after `OMARCHY_KILL_GRACE` (200 ms, new in `limits.rs`), then reaped. The child is not reaped before the SIGKILL, so the group's id cannot pass to another process in between.

Why: these tools are shell scripts that start children (`jq`, `find`, `hyprctl`). Killing only the script left a hung child running, as the git runner (`src/sources/git_hosts.rs`) already avoided by killing its group.

Tests: `tests/omarchy.rs` `a_timed_out_tool_leaves_no_process_of_its_own_behind` (a stub that backgrounds a child and hangs: the child is gone once omaddons returns; on the unfixed code it still runs), and the existing ping scenes, still bounded at 2 s.

Contract: none; the limits registry adds `OMARCHY_KILL_GRACE` (snapshot updated).

comments.author: FierceWren
comments.text:
**DEC-4 contract: one shape for `archive_too_large` details (omad-36gn).** A pre-freeze correction to comment 1240 (every wire name M3 added), made before the contract freezes at the first tag (M4).

What: every `archive_too_large` now carries `details.limit` as the numeric bound. It also names the bound one of two ways: `details.config_key` when `config.toml` can raise it (archives, downloads, `git:` checkouts, an indexed folder), else `details.constant`, the fixed bound's name in `limits.rs`. The fixed bounds are a `WTF/` tree a backup copies, a `backup import` archive, a WowAce tree, and an API response (`API_RESPONSE_MAX_BYTES`).

Why: three shapes existed. For a `WTF/` copy and `backup import`, `details.limit` held the constant's name and `details.max` the number. For WowAce, `limit` held the number and `constant` the name. For M2's bounds, `limit` held the number and `config_key` the setting. An agent reading `details.limit` got a number from one command and a string from another.

How: `src/backup/tree.rs` and `src/backup/import.rs` move to `{limit: <number>, constant: <name>}` (`details.max` is gone). `src/net/guard.rs`'s API-response bound adds `constant`. The WowAce bound already had this shape, and the M2 sites keep theirs.

Contract: a value changed type (`details.limit` for the two backup bounds), allowed before the freeze and recorded here. A contract-matrix row (`backup_import_archive_too_large`) pins the shape. README's error table says so, and its Known issues entry is gone.

comments.author: FierceWren
comments.text:
**§5.11 `status --cached` on every widget refresh: two costs removed (omad-7jwk).** Completes comment 1239 and G2's note on milestone criterion 10 (the 5 ms median budget, which the 20 MB-history case met within 0.2 ms).

What and why, measured on the perf test's fixture home (release build, medians of 21 runs):
- Before: heavy home 4.46–4.60 ms; with a 20 MB history 4.74–4.99 ms (p95 up to 5.29 ms).
- After, three consecutive runs: heavy home 4.04–4.12 ms; with a 20 MB history 4.23, 4.23 and 4.27 ms (p95 4.33–4.43 ms).

The 20 MB case's own cost was the history projection. Its 71 lines (80 KB, the newest sixteen undoable runs, interleaved) were all read whole, ops included, to find one run. A 12-line projection on the same home ran 0.35 ms faster.

How:
- `HistoryTail::answer` finds the newest undoable line by each line's facts (kind, run, tx; ops skipped) and reads only that run's lines whole. A line whose facts read but which does not read whole is skipped, as reading every line skips it; a unit test pins that case. The existing randomized test, which checks the projection selects what the whole history does over 1,000 interleavings, passes unchanged.
- `store::load` decodes a document at its current version straight from its bytes. It no longer builds a `serde_json::Value` first and then converts it. Every state file `status` reads benefits, the 440 KB release memo most. Any other document (another version, duplicate keys, anything that does not decode) takes the general path, so results and errors are unchanged. A unit test checks the two paths agree and that the fast one steps aside.

Contract: none. `--cached` still writes nothing, makes no request, and says `unknown` rather than guess. `tests/status.rs` and the contract snapshots pass unchanged.

comments.author: FierceWren
comments.text:
**§10 Milestone status: M3 (the Omarchy widget, Lua errors and `WTF/` backups) is done, 2026-10-23 (omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.7.3, G3).** [x] M3. This closes the M3 set: G2's comments 1234–1242 and their index 1243, then the fix notes 1247–1264 made between G2 and the checkpoint.

What: every one of the checkpoint's fourteen criteria (§7's M3 checkpoints as amended in G3's body) passed at 87aee9a, the last code commit, with one pre-accepted `SKIP` (`keyless_installs_forever`, the Forever stress-test set still installed). The set is as it was (5 addons, 12 folders, AddOns hash identical, nothing pinned); its record generation went 8 → 28. Separately, the widget's start-up catch-up made Forever an automatic `post_session` backup, as README describes for every stopped client; it writes only `<meta>/backups/`.
- **Found and fixed at the checkpoint:** `omad-ljl9` (an undo's and a dismissal's result lines, a stale error card, the no-clients tooltip), `omad-ex9m` (backup times in UTC), `omad-est4` (failpoint aborts dumped core: 28,238 dumps in 12 hours, and a desktop notification each), and the bench script's reading of hyperfine 2.0 (df59536). Before it, G2's findings `omad-k2ns`, `omad-aepa`, `omad-mc1i`, `omad-in4u`, `omad-09iu`, `omad-36gn` and `omad-q585`.

comments.author: PlushDelta
comments.text:
**§5.8 errors: a dismissal that reads again reports only that read's warnings (omad-he63, omad-0jrj).** Completes the §5.8 errors comment's `errors dismiss` paragraph and the review pass's "dismiss reports the read it binds to"; adds one debug failpoint to the list outside `FAILPOINTS` in the M3 wire-names comment.

What: when a BugGrabber file moves between a dismissal's first read and the global lock, the dismissal reads again under the lock and binds to that read. Its warnings are now the second read's alone, in the envelope and on stderr. Before, the first read's warnings stayed: `observe` notes every read's warnings in the run's notes, which `output::emit_to` merges first, so a database the game was still writing at the first look (`errors_partial`) and finished before the lock was acknowledged whole while the envelope still said it could not be read.

How: `RunNotes::withdraw` takes back warnings a step found and then superseded. `dismiss` withdraws the first read's own (not those the run had found before it, from `World::load`), truncates its list, then reads again. A failure before the second read (the lock timing out, a stale `--if-match` at the first check) still reports the first read's warnings, which then describe the read made.

Failpoint: `errors.dismiss.observed` (debug builds), between the first read with its `--if-match` check and the lock, so a test can change a file while the dismissal waits.

Tests: `tests/errors_dismiss.rs` `a_database_finished_while_a_dismissal_waits_is_acknowledged_without_a_stale_warning` (fails on the unfixed code, and with either the withdrawal or the truncate removed) and `a_session_ending_while_a_dismissal_waits_is_read_again` (a first-read token refused as `plan_stale`, then a dismissal bound to the rewritten file, 3 new errors where the first look had 2, a second account's partial database warned about once). Unit: `output::notes` `a_withdrawn_warning_leaves_the_others_in_order`.

Contract: no wire name changes; the envelope now matches README's `errors dismiss`.

comments.author: PlushDelta
comments.text:
**§5.9 stderr events: human progress on a real terminal (omad-1afl, omad-aco1).** Completes the third review pass's "progress fits the terminal width" and "a progress line left by a dropped reporter is cleared" (c9f6a33), which landed without a test because human progress draws only on a terminal.

What: a human progress line is now cut to the terminal's width (`columns - 1` characters, `…` where cut) on every run. The pass gave the cut only to `Reporter::stderr`, which serves help, usage errors and the panic path, none of which draw progress; the run's own reporter (`output::shared_stderr`, the one every `ProgressSink` draws through) was built unmeasured, so a long line (a local zip's path, `gh:…@… on retail`) wrapped on a narrow terminal and left rows behind when erased. `shared_stderr` now measures the terminal too. Where stderr is no terminal, `tcgetwinsize` fails and nothing is cut, so `--progress human` into a pipe is unchanged; NDJSON and JSON are untouched.

Tests: `tests/terminal.rs` runs the binary with stderr on a pseudo-terminal (rustix's `pty` feature, a dev-dependency only; the binary opens none) and stdout on a pipe:
- `progress_lines_fit_the_terminal`: an install on a 40-column terminal; every progress line is at most 39 characters and the too-wide one is cut. It failed on the unfixed code with 100-character lines.
- `a_panic_after_progress_starts_on_a_cleared_line` (debug builds): `engine.lock.acquired=panic` after the stage progress drew; the clear sequence comes right before `error[internal]`. With `Reporter::stderr` starting from `false` instead of `PROGRESS_ON_SCREEN`, it reads `stage: retail 1/1error[internal]: …` and fails.
Both skip through `common::checkpoint::skip` where `/dev/ptmx` cannot be opened.

Contract: none; README's "on a terminal in human mode, progress is one line that is rewritten in place" now also holds on a narrow terminal.

comments.author: CobaltOak
comments.text:
**§5.3 Compatibility verdict: retail 12's interface floor (omad-retail-12-floor-e5a0, omad-test-retail-12-floor-3cvk).** Completes §5.3's "the interface is not below the family floor (out-of-date loads are allowed, with a warning)". This is a pre-freeze addition to the contract (D21), made before the first tag (M4).

What: retail 12.0 and later load no Mainline TOC below 120000, with no player override (warcraft.wiki.gg `Patch_12.0.0/API_changes/notes`, "Forced interface matching for 12.0.0", fetched 2026-10-24).
- **Rules data:** a new client-rules row field `interface_floor` (`Option<u32>`), set to 120000 on `mainline`, `mainline-12.0.7` and `mainline-10.2.7`, and binding by the client's own interface (`ClientRules::floor_for`). It can be patched as `[client_rules.<row>] interface_floor`, where 0 removes it. No client version is special-cased in code: the number is table data.
- **New wire name:** `WrongFlavorReason` `below_client_floor` `{interfaces, floor}`. It appears in `list --unmanaged`'s underlying verdicts, in `folders.skipped`, and in `error.details.tried[].reason`. Below the floor a folder is `wrong_flavor`, never `out_of_date`.
- **The archive rule:** a side folder below the floor rules itself out (it is skipped). The addon's own folder below it refuses the archive.

Why: before this, omaddons installed 11.x builds on 12.x clients and suggested enabling "Load out of date AddOns", which cannot load them. The coverage study (omad-m2-audit-yegz.7.7, comment 868) counted 38 of the WoWInterface top 100 as "installs, out of date" on mainline.

Also: six catalog entries whose only mainline build is below the floor no longer list `mainline` (OmniCC, Quartz, Rarity, OmniBar, Cell, Tukui).

Follow-up: omad-fxma. Verdict facts remembered before a judging change are still believed until they are re-verified.

comments.author: CobaltOak
comments.text: **§5.3 Compatibility verdict: a game type naming the client admits an off-range interface (omad-author-built-loading-5po6.1, .7).** The first landed child of the epic omad-author-built-loading-5po6. What: on a modern row, a folder with no Interface value in the client's family range is no longer another client's when its effective AllowLoadGameType names one of the row's own game_types (never the family names classic or mainline): it is compatible, out_of_date, and its warning lists its interfaces. The retail interface floor still wins (below_client_floor), an ExcludeLoadGameType naming the client still wins, and legacy rows still ignore game types. Why: the author's own game-type line says the folder is built for this client, and the client lists such a folder as out of date (warcraft.wiki.gg TOC format); Titan Panel 9.3.5, refused on Anniversary because TitanAmmo declares 205056 (a typo) under AllowLoadGameType tbc, now installs there (checked live 2026-10-24), and the catalog lists tbc for it. Shared game types admit on each row: a Titan build gated to wrath is out of date on Wrath Classic. No wire name changed.

comments.author: CobaltOak
comments.text: **§5.4 Selection: file-name flavor words and the evidence view (omad-author-built-loading-5po6.2, .8).** Second landed child of omad-author-built-loading-5po6. What: name_hints also reads burningcrusade and tbcc (bcc), cataclysm and catac (cata), pandaria and mopc (mists) and camelot (forever), the words real per-flavor releases use (Pawn, VuhDo); a new evidence view (github_rest::evidence_hints) drops every word of the addon's own folder and repository names, and select::name_evidence reads it per client, with a bare classic against mainline and Forever only. Ranking still uses the raw hints. Why: the evidence rule of omad-mixed-archive-single-file-skk1 will refuse a file whose name names only other clients, so a hint must never come from the addon's own name (Foo_Classic, Titan). No wire name changed; the new words only re-rank files that carry them.

comments.author: CobaltOak
comments.text: **§5.4 Selection: downloads chosen by evidence (omad-mixed-archive-single-file-skk1, omad-author-built-loading-5po6.9).** Third landed child of omad-author-built-loading-5po6; replaces README's 'a folder that merely lists another client's interface refuses the archive'. What: each candidate is graded Clean (declared, or every skip ruled out by its own TOCs), LeftOut (the addon's own folder loads; the other skips list only other clients' interfaces, read none, or lie below the floor) or Refused. A candidate whose release.json entries name no client of the family (by interface range, else flavor; only where a release.json can name the client), or whose GitHub REST asset name names only other clients (evidence_hints, own names excluded), is refused even when clean. Install and the update check take the first Clean candidate, else the first LeftOut one; a rankless cached archive wins only Clean. Refusal messages name what decided the best-ranked candidate. title: plan_not_found's published fix pattern says prose, but apply's resolve fixes it with omaddons help apply
description:
## Background

`ErrorCode::fix_pattern` (`src/error/fix_pattern.rs`) publishes, for every error code, the form its fix takes; `omaddons robot-docs errors` prints it as `fix_pattern`, and agents read it to know whether a code's fix is runnable. The module's own rule is that a pattern is "true of every construction site", and a pattern that starts with `prose: ` means "no site gives a command".

`plan_not_found`'s pattern is `prose: preview the change again with its command's --dry-run`. That was true when D4 (the plan store) added the code, but D5's `apply` (`omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5.4`) added a site whose fix is a command: `apply::resolve` (`src/app/apply.rs`) refuses an unknown id or prefix with fix `omaddons help apply` (and alternative `omaddons adopt --apply`). The other two sites keep prose fixes: `apply::reload` (a plan removed while `apply` waited for its lease) and `state::plans::load` (an unreadable plan file). So the published pattern tells an agent that no `plan_not_found` fix is runnable, while the most common one is.

Found while closing `omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.5.5` (the `apply` and `adopt --apply` hints), which made `resolve`'s fix the subject of its own snapshots.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On any home, run `omaddons apply 01ZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZZ --json`: `error.code` is `plan_not_found` and `error.fix_argv` is `["omaddons","help","apply"]` (a command).
2. Run `omaddons robot-docs errors --json`: the `plan_not_found` entry's `fix_pattern` is `prose: preview the change again with its command's --dry-run`, which says no site gives a command.

## Technical Approach

- Change `Self::PlanNotFound`'s arm in `src/error/fix_pattern.rs` to name both forms, in the style of its neighbours: "`omaddons help apply`, or prose: preview the change again with its command's `--dry-run`".
- Check whether any snapshot or the generated guide (`skills/omaddons/SKILL.md`, regenerated with `OMADDONS_UPDATE_SKILL=1 cargo test --test skill`) carries the pattern text; today a search finds it only in `fix_pattern.rs`, so nothing else should change. Re-accept any snapshot that does, after review.
- No wire name changes: `fix_pattern` is documentation text, not a key or a value an agent matches on.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `omaddons robot-docs errors --json` gives `plan_not_found` a `fix_pattern` that names `omaddons help apply` and the prose fix, and no longer starts with `prose: `.
- Every `plan_not_found` construction site (`apply::resolve`, `apply::reload`, `plans::load`) gives a fix of a form the pattern names.
- `tests/robot_docs.rs` passes; any changed snapshot or the regenerated `SKILL.md` differs only by this phrase.
- `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed file.

## Test Plan

- Unit: none new; the pattern is a constant, covered by `tests/robot_docs.rs`'s catalog checks (every code listed with its pattern).
- Contract: the existing `apply_plan_not_found` and `apply_folder_hint` snapshots already pin `resolve`'s `omaddons help apply` fix, which the new pattern now describes.

## Considerations

- If a later site gives `plan_not_found` another command fix (D9's `plans show`, say), that leaf extends the pattern in the same commit, as the module's rule requires.
- Size S: one line, plus whatever the guide or a snapshot echoes of it.
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] omaddons robot-docs errors --json gives plan_not_found a fix_pattern that names omaddons help apply and the prose fix, and no longer starts with prose:
- [ ] Every plan_not_found construction site (apply::resolve, apply::reload, plans::load) gives a fix of a form the pattern names.
- [ ] tests/robot_docs.rs passes; any changed snapshot or the regenerated SKILL.md differs only by this phrase.
- [ ] argc gate passes; ubs is clean on the changed file.
close_reason: done: plan_not_found's fix_pattern names omaddons help apply and the prose fix; argc gate passed

title: Re-verify Forever keyless installs and launch layout after the 2026-11-04 launch
description:
## Background

The M1 checkpoint (omad-m1-working-slice-ejl.7.10) ran the five keyless publishers against a synthetic WoW: Forever target (`wowf`, `_forever_`, 1.60.x) before Forever launched on 2026-11-04. Plater and Bartender4 installed; WeakAuras, DBM and BigWigs were refused with `no_compatible_release` because none of them had published a `forever` build yet. That refusal is correct behavior, but it means the Forever path was proven only for two publishers, and Forever's launch layout (product code `wowf`, folder `_forever_`, interface 1.60.x, TOC suffixes `_Forever`/`_Camelot`) was taken from pre-launch data.

## Technical Approach

- After launch, re-run `OMADDONS_LIVE=1 cargo test --test live_probes keyless_installs_into_a_synthetic_forever_target -- --ignored` and record which publishers now install.
- Check the launch layout against the vision tables (D15, data not code): Battle.net product code and folder for Forever and its beta, `.build.info` version and interface number, and the TOC suffixes publishers actually ship (inspect each installed archive's TOC names and `release.json` flavor values).
- If any of these changed, update `src/rules.rs` tables, the discovery and TOC fixtures (`tests/discover_matrix.rs`, `tests/toc_matrix.rs`) and snapshots, and add a vision comment recording the change.
- If a publisher ships a Forever build that the TOC rules reject, treat it as a bug in the rules (file a bug bead with the archive's TOC lines as the repro).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The live Forever probe has been run after 2026-11-04 and its per-publisher result is recorded in the close reason.
- Every publisher that ships a `forever` build installs and verifies; none installs a non-Forever build.
- Discovery and TOC tables match the shipped launch layout, with fixtures updated if anything changed.
- `argc gate` passes for any code or fixture change.

## Test Plan

- Live: `live_probes::keyless_installs_into_a_synthetic_forever_target` with `OMADDONS_LIVE=1`.
- Unit/E2E (only if tables change): `tests/discover_matrix.rs`, `tests/toc_matrix.rs`, contract snapshots.

## Considerations

- Publishers may lag the launch by days; if most still ship no Forever build, record that and defer again with `--until`.
- The synthetic target is built from fixtures; a real Forever install is not needed (and not available to agents).
acceptance_criteria: The live Forever probe has been run after 2026-11-04 and its per-publisher result is recorded; every publisher that ships a forever build installs and verifies and none installs a non-Forever build; discovery and TOC tables match the shipped launch layout with fixtures updated if anything changed; argc gate passes for any code or fixture change

title: Folder-mutating engine APIs take FolderName, not MutableFolderName (D14 type invariant unbuilt)
description:
## Background

`src/model.rs` defines `MutableFolderName`, a folder name that is not `blizzard_*`, constructed only by `FolderName::into_mutable`. Its doc (and the model module doc) promised that every API that creates, replaces, renames or removes an AddOns folder takes this type, so a protected folder cannot reach one at compile time (D14, D27). No API takes it: the engine's folder operations (stage/swap/undo/prune paths in `src/engine/` and `src/fsx/`) take `FolderName` or paths. The protection that exists is the ownership check's rule 1 (`src/engine/ownership.rs`): a `blizzard_*` key is `protected_folder`, never overridable, judged at plan time and again under the lock.

Found by the doc audit omad-khsy, which corrected the docs to say so.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `grep -rn MutableFolderName src/` lists only `src/model.rs`.
2. Expected: the engine's folder-changing functions take it. Actual: they take `FolderName` (or paths), so nothing at compile time keeps a `blizzard_*` name out of them.

## Technical Approach

- Change the folder-mutating engine APIs (the swap's add/replace/remove of AddOns folders, undo's restore, adoption's handover) to take `MutableFolderName`, converting with `into_mutable` where the ownership check has already allowed the change; a protected name there is an internal error.
- Keep the ownership check as the user-facing refusal; the type is defense in depth.

## Acceptance Criteria

- No engine or fsx function that changes an AddOns folder accepts a bare `FolderName` for the folder it changes.
- The model.rs docs again state the invariant, now true.
- `argc gate` passes; no behavior change.

## Test Plan

- Existing ownership and protected-folder tests pass unchanged.
- A compile-time check is the point; a unit test that `into_mutable` refuses `Blizzard_*` (any case) exists or is added.

## Considerations

- Touches the engine's hot path signatures; keep the change mechanical and reviewable.
acceptance_criteria: no engine or fsx function that changes an AddOns folder accepts a bare FolderName for that folder; model.rs docs state the invariant; argc gate passes with no behavior change
close_reason: The swap takes MutableFolderName for every folder it changes

The ownership check is where a name becomes mutable: rule 1 is now into_mutable(), refusing a client folder as protected_folder exactly as before; the live spelling converts likewise (same key). Undo converts history's folders and a live respelling with into_mutable, refusing an entry that names a client folder as protected_folder before anything moves. Readers (plan's claim/release/handover, local-changes check, policy ops, summaries, history ops, index changes) use as_folder()/key(). snapshot_saved_variables keeps FolderName: it copies SavedVariables and changes no AddOns folder. model.rs docs state the invariant again. title: BugGrabber for 1.12.1 clients (and why 4.3.4 and 5.4.8 have no build)
description:
## Background

C3 (`omad-m3-widget-errors-backups-7qmx.3.3`) gave BugGrabber catalog variants for every modern family, 3.3.5a (`wowace:bug-grabber#r152`) and 2.4.3 (`wowace:bug-grabber#r130`). Three legacy families get "no BugGrabber build for this client is known" from `errors` and `not_found` from `install buggrabber`, so `omaddons errors` cannot become actionable there (goal G-M3-3 says "every client"):

- **1.12.1 (vanilla-legacy).** The repository's 1.12-era code exists, but outside trunk: under `tmp/trunk/!BugGrabber/`, where trunk's TOC at r30 reads `## Interface: 11200` (r10: 11000, r20: 11100, r45: 20000). Trunk itself only starts at r122 (Interface 20400). The `wowace:` ref grammar (C1) addresses `tags/<tag>/` and `trunk/` (`#r<rev>`), so no ref can name that tree.
- **4.3.4 (cata-legacy) and 5.4.8 (mists-legacy).** Every 4.3 revision (r184 to r186) and every 5.4 revision (last: r203) has `--@localization(locale="…", format="lua_additive_table", …)@` keywords in `locales.lua`, which C2's packaging subset refuses (`packaging_unsupported`), correctly: those keywords are filled in by the packager from the CurseForge localization service.

The facts above were found by the one-off trunk walk C3 ran on 2026-10-22, and the live probe `live_probes::wowace_bug_grabber_legacy_revisions` re-checks the 4.3/5.4 refusals.

## Technical Approach

1.12.1 is the reachable one:
1. Extend the `wowace:` ref grammar with a pinned path form, for example `wowace:bug-grabber#r44:tmp/trunk/!BugGrabber` (revision plus a repository path under the project root). Parse it in `src/model.rs` (`WowAceRev` gains the path, or a new variant), accept it in `src/sources/refs.rs` links if useful, and build `AssetLocation::WowAceTree` with base `…/!svn/bc/<rev>/<path>/` in `src/sources/wowace.rs` (`pinned()` must accept and check the new shape). The tree's root is the `!BugGrabber` directory itself, so `package-as` falls back to the folder name rather than the slug.
2. Find the last `tmp/trunk/!BugGrabber/` revision whose TOC declares 11200 (between r30 and r44) and whose tree passes the packaging subset.
3. Add `variant = "r<rev>"` with `families = ["vanilla-legacy"]` to `catalog/catalog.toml`, record the fixture with the WowAce recorder, and extend the live probes.

4.3.4 and 5.4.8 need the packager's localization step. Do not build it keylessly: record that they stay without a variant unless a CurseForge source (M5) offers packaged files for those eras.

Decide while doing: whether the path form is worth a grammar change for one addon, or whether a catalog-only pinned location (no user-facing grammar) is enough. README describes `wowace:` refs, so a grammar change is a README change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `omaddons install buggrabber -t <1.12.1 client>` installs the 1.12-era BugGrabber at a pinned revision, verified by its TOC (Interface 11200), replayed from recorded fixtures.
- `errors` on a 1.12.1 client without BugGrabber offers `omaddons install buggrabber -t <id>` instead of the "no build known" prose.
- The new variant's families are disjoint from the others; the shipped catalog loads; `catalog_matches_declared_flavors` covers it.
- 4.3.4 and 5.4.8 stay without a variant, with the reason recorded in the catalog header and README.
- README's Sources row and catalog section describe whatever ref form is added.

## Test Plan

- Unit: the new ref form parses and round-trips; `pinned()` accepts the pinned path base and refuses a live one.
- E2E (`tests/catalog.rs`, replayed): install on a synthetic 1.12.1 client; `errors` hint on it.
- Live: extend `wowace_bug_grabber_legacy_revisions` with the 1.12 revision's TOC.

## Considerations

- The `tmp/` tree is an import of the project's pre-SVN-migration history; check its packaging (externals, keywords) before committing to it.
- A ref grammar addition is additive but user-visible; keep `#r<rev>` meaning trunk.
- Low priority: 1.12.1 private-server players are a small audience, and `--file` with a hand-downloaded build works today.
acceptance_criteria: install buggrabber on a 1.12.1 client installs the 1.12-era BugGrabber at a pinned revision, TOC-verified (Interface 11200), replayed; errors on a 1.12.1 client without BugGrabber offers the install argv instead of the no-build prose; the new variant's families are disjoint, the shipped catalog loads, and catalog_matches_declared_flavors covers it; 4.3.4 and 5.4.8 stay without a variant with the reason recorded in the catalog header and README; README describes any new ref form
close_reason: BugGrabber installs on 1.12.1 from the 1.12-era tree (wowace:bug-grabber#r43:tmp/trunk/!BugGrabber); 4.3.4 and 5.4.8 stay without a build, with the reason recorded

comments.text: done: decided: a grammar change, not a catalog-only location, because a record re-resolves from its ref string alone (update, sync --locked), and #r43 alone would mean trunk, which starts at r122. New wire forms (DEC-4): ref wowace:<slug>#r<rev>:<directory> (directory not under trunk/ or tags/, 1-8 segments of [A-Za-z0-9._+-!]), its links …/!svn/bc/<rev>/<directory>/, release id wowace:<slug>@r<rev>:<directory>, version r<rev>; catalog variant r43 (vanilla-legacy). Found live: r43 is the last tmp/trunk/!BugGrabber revision declaring 11200 (r44 declares 20000; the bead guessed r44), two files, no .pkgmeta, no keywords. pinned() accepts the directory shape (trunk/x and .. still refused), the folder is the directory's last segment, recorded_candidate honours the ref's pin. title: Release-mode unit tests do not compile: failpoint tests call the debug-only with_spec
description:
## Background

`cargo test --release --lib` does not compile: 30 `E0425` errors, all calls to `failpoint::with_spec`. That function exists only in debug builds (DEC-7: test hooks are debug-only). Its unit-test callers are in:
- `src/fsx/failpoint.rs` (15)
- `src/engine/tx.rs` (11)
- `src/engine/undo.rs` (3)
- `src/engine/swap.rs` (3)
- one each in `src/engine/journal.rs`, `retention.rs`, `stage.rs`, `src/fsx/mutate.rs` and `prune.rs`

`argc gate` builds tests in debug only, so nothing catches this. It bites anyone who runs release-mode unit tests, for example to time a proptest or check optimised behaviour; integration tests (`cargo test --release --test perf`) build fine.

Found while doing 4.5 (a release-mode proptest run).

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `cargo test --release --lib`
2. The build fails with `cannot find function with_spec in module failpoint`.

## Technical Approach

Gate the failpoint-driven unit tests on `#[cfg(debug_assertions)]`, per test or per test module, so release builds skip them and keep the rest. Alternatively, give release builds a `with_spec` that panics with a clear message. The cfg gate is preferable: it keeps DEC-7's rule that hooks do not exist in release builds.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `cargo test --release --lib` compiles and passes.
- Debug runs still execute every failpoint test (same count as before).
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

Run `cargo test --release --lib` and `cargo test --lib`, and compare the test counts: release runs fewer, by exactly the gated failpoint tests.

title: Tests that run a stub they just wrote can fail with Text file busy (ETXTBSY)
description:
## Background

The gate failed once (2026-10-24) on a test unrelated to the change being gated:

```
---- omarchy::shell::tests::only_the_exact_answer_places_the_widget stdout ----
assertion `left == right` failed
  left: Unreachable("omarchy-bar could not run: Text file busy (os error 26)")
 right: Yes
```

The next gate run passed unchanged. The test's `stub` helper (`src/omarchy/shell.rs`, test module) writes a shell script with `std::fs::write`, makes it executable and runs it at once. `cargo test` runs tests on several threads. When another test thread forks a child between this thread's `open` and `close` of the stub, the child inherits the write descriptor until its own `exec` closes it (`O_CLOEXEC` closes it only at exec). If the stub is exec'd during that window, the kernel refuses with `ETXTBSY`. This is the known Linux race between writing an executable and running it in a multi-threaded process; no code in the repository handles it today (`grep -rn ETXTBSY src tests` finds nothing).

A flaky gate costs a full rerun (about 1.5 to 4 minutes) and teaches agents to rerun failures blindly.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. `cargo test --locked --lib` repeatedly, or `argc gate`, on a loaded machine.
2. Now and then `omarchy::shell::tests::only_the_exact_answer_places_the_widget` (or another test that execs a freshly written stub) fails with `Text file busy (os error 26)`.

## Technical Approach

- Find every test that writes an executable and runs it: the `stub` helpers in `src/omarchy/shell.rs`, the stub Omarchy tools of `tests/omarchy.rs` and `tests/omarchy_widget.rs`, and any git or credential-command stub (`grep -rn "from_mode(0o7" src tests`).
- Fix it in the shared test helpers, not in production code: production omaddons never writes an executable it then runs.
  - Preferred: write the stub through a short-lived child (`sh -c 'cat > "$1" && chmod 755 "$1"'`), so this process never holds a write descriptor that a sibling fork could inherit.
  - Or retry the spawn a few times when it fails with `ErrorKind::ExecutableFileBusy`, in the test helper that runs the stub.
- Keep each stub's behaviour exactly as it is.

## Acceptance Criteria

- No test that runs a stub it wrote can fail with `ETXTBSY`: the stubs are written outside the test process, or their spawns retry `ExecutableFileBusy`.
- `cargo test --locked --lib omarchy::shell` passes 200 times in a row under `--test-threads=16`.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- A loop of 200 runs of the `omarchy::shell` tests at 16 threads, before and after (record the failure count before).
- The full gate.

## Considerations

- Retrying hides the race rather than removing it; writing through a child removes it. Prefer the latter where the helper allows.
- The QML and bun widget tests run their own processes and are not affected.
acceptance_criteria: No test that runs a stub it wrote can fail with ETXTBSY (stubs written outside the test process, or spawns retry ExecutableFileBusy); the omarchy::shell tests pass 200 times in a row at 16 threads; argc gate passes
close_reason: Every test that writes a script and runs it now writes it through a child sh (src/test_exec.rs for unit tests, tests/common/exec.rs for integration tests), so no descriptor of the multi-threaded test process can be inherited by a sibling fork
