title: An unbound remove whose forget no longer applies reports not_managed for an addon still managed
description:
## Background

`remove` of an addon whose folders were all deleted by hand plans a forget: a records-only change that moves no folder (README, `remove`). Under the commit lock, `engine::plan::rejudge_records` checks the forget's guard again (`RecordGuard::check` in `src/engine/edit.rs`): every planned folder must still be absent. When a folder is back and the target's generation has not moved, the work is dropped without an error (`Err(_) => Ok(Planned::nothing())`), so the transaction has nothing to commit.

`app::remove::item` (`src/app/remove.rs`, the `None` branch after `done.outcomes`) then reads the missing change as "Removed by someone else between planning and the lock" and reports `not_managed` with "Foo is no longer managed in retail". That is false: Foo is still recorded and its folder is in AddOns again. README's `not_managed` row says the code means "a name no managed addon answers to", so the code differs from the contract.

A bound run (`--if-match`) is right: the re-judged operations differ from the approved ones, and it is refused as `plan_stale` with `details.changed: ["selection"]` (D8, omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8). Only the unbound report is wrong. Nothing on disk changes either way.

Found while writing omad-m4-agent-surface-doctor-c6cm.4.8.3: `tests/preconditions.rs::a_bound_remove_whose_forget_no_longer_applies_changes_nothing` drives this race and asserts only that nothing changed, not the report.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. A debug build, and a retail client with Foo installed from a local archive (two folders, `Foo` and `FooOld`; the `common::engine::Scene` fixture `v1`).
2. Delete both folders by hand.
3. Run `omaddons remove Foo -t retail --json` with `OMADDONS_FAILPOINTS=engine.snapshot.prestaged=pause` and `OMADDONS_FAILPOINT_DIR=<dir>`.
4. When `<dir>/engine.snapshot.prestaged.reached` appears, create `AddOns/Foo/Foo.toc`, then create `<dir>/engine.snapshot.prestaged.resume`.
5. The run exits 3 with `not_managed`, "Foo is no longer managed in retail", fix `omaddons list -t retail`. `omaddons list -t retail` still lists Foo.

## Technical Approach

Report the real reason: the forget no longer applies because a folder is back, and running `remove` again now would remove that folder.

- Recommended: in `rejudge_records`, a failed absent-folder check (a forget whose folder is back) is a retryable `plan_stale` carrying the guard's cause ("FooOld is in AddOns again, so Foo is not forgotten"), as `super::tx::stale` builds it. The output boundary already turns a retryable `plan_stale`'s fix into a rerun of the same command (`app::Out::boundary_fix`). Other guard failures on an unchanged generation keep today's silent drop.
- Then `remove::item`'s `None` branch is reached only when the addon really dropped out; check the current record before saying "no longer managed", and say "unchanged" (or the existing wording for a no-op) when the addon is still recorded.
- Decide and record in the close comment whether `pin`/`unpin`/`adopt` records-only works need the same treatment (their guards are `recorded` and `release`, which an unchanged generation cannot fail, so probably not).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The unbound race above fails with `plan_stale`, `retryable: true`, a message naming the folder that is back, and `fix_argv` `["omaddons", "remove", "Foo", "-t", "retail"]`; running that fix removes Foo's folder in a normal remove transaction, undoable.
- [ ] Nothing changes in the refused run: AddOns, the record, the generation and `history.jsonl` are as the hand edit left them.
- [ ] A remove whose addon another process really removed between plan and lock still reports `not_managed` "no longer managed" (a test drives that race).
- [ ] The bound race still refuses with `["selection"]`, not retryable, its preview as `fix_argv`.
- [ ] `tests/preconditions.rs::a_bound_remove_whose_forget_no_longer_applies_changes_nothing` asserts the unbound outcome; README's Known issues entry for this bead is removed.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files.

## Test Plan

- Unit (`src/engine/plan.rs`): `rejudge_records` over a forget whose folder is back on an unchanged generation is a retryable `plan_stale` naming the folder; on a moved generation it keeps today's error; a forget still valid commits.
- Unit (`src/app/remove.rs`): `item` with no change for a still-recorded addon does not claim it is no longer managed.
- E2E (`tests/preconditions.rs`, `TestLog`): the unbound race (pause at `engine.snapshot.prestaged`, folder put back), its refusal, and its fix run end to end; the real concurrent remove still `not_managed`.

## Considerations

- A millisecond race: someone restores a folder by hand while a forget waits for the lock. The impact is a misleading message, never lost data.
- Keep the silent drop for guards whose failure means "someone else already did it", so a concurrent identical change stays a no-op rather than an error.
- `plan_stale` is an existing code; no new wire name is needed. If the message or `details` change, list them in the close comment (DEC-4).
acceptance_criteria:
- [ ] The unbound race above fails with `plan_stale`, `retryable: true`, a message naming the folder that is back, and `fix_argv` `["omaddons", "remove", "Foo", "-t", "retail"]`; running that fix removes Foo's folder in a normal remove transaction, undoable.
- [ ] Nothing changes in the refused run: AddOns, the record, the generation and `history.jsonl` are as the hand edit left them.
- [ ] A remove whose addon another process really removed between plan and lock still reports `not_managed` "no longer managed" (a test drives that race).
- [ ] The bound race still refuses with `["selection"]`, not retryable, its preview as `fix_argv`.
- [ ] `tests/preconditions.rs::a_bound_remove_whose_forget_no_longer_applies_changes_nothing` asserts the unbound outcome; README's Known issues entry for this bead is removed.
- [ ] `argc gate` passes; `ubs` is clean on the changed files.

title: `install` labels a bridge requirement's `omaddons search` hint as action `install`
description:
## Background

The closing check of the post-M2 audit (omad-m2-audit-yegz) found that `install`'s `commands` can hold a `search` command labelled with action `install`.

`install_hints` (src/app/install.rs:1168-1194) builds at most three hints, all labelled `CommandHint::new("install", argv, false)`: the candidates of unresolved requirements, then "what each `bridge_dependency` warning's fix installs". For the bridge part it copies the warning's `fix_argv` as is.

The `bridge_dependency` warning's fix is built in src/engine/plan.rs:2042-2059: `omaddons install <name> -t <id>` when the catalog names the requirement, `omaddons install <ref> -t <id>` when the dependency resolver finds a ref, and otherwise `Suggestion::command(["omaddons", "search", requires])`. In that last case `commands` carries `{"action": "install", "command": "omaddons search <folder>", ...}`.

The `action` field is how an agent or the widget decides what a hint does without parsing argv. README's Fields table lists `commands` as "suggested next steps: `{action, command, argv, destructive}`", and README's `install` section says "`commands` offers at most three `omaddons install <candidate> -t <id>` hints (action `install`): unresolved candidates in item order, then bridge requirements". README's warning table already says the `bridge_dependency` fix "searches for it (`omaddons search <folder>`) when no keyless source ships it", so the search fix itself is intended; only its label in `commands` is wrong. A consumer that trusts `action: install` (e.g. offers an "Install" button, or counts install hints) is told a search is an install.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install an addon whose archive ships a second folder (a bridge or plugin, like `Masque_Dominos`) whose `## Dependencies` names an addon that is not installed and that neither the catalog, the managed record nor the Tukui/WoWInterface indexes resolve; e.g. the `gh:o/plug` scenario in tests/contract/matrix.rs with the requirement's catalog entry and index rows removed.
2. The `bridge_dependency` warning's `fix_argv` is `["omaddons","search","<folder>"]`.
3. The envelope's `commands` holds `{"action":"install","command":"omaddons search <folder>",...}`.

(Code path verified by reading at 7fb0a2c; the existing matrix test only exercises a bridge that resolves, so it never sees the `search` fix.)

## Technical Approach

- In `install_hints`, label each hint by what its argv runs: `install` for an `omaddons install …` argv and `search` for an `omaddons search …` argv. Derive it from `argv[1]` (the verb) rather than from where the hint came from, so a future fix shape cannot mislabel again.
- Keep the cap (`INSTALL_HINTS_MAX`, 3) over all of them, and keep the order (unresolved candidates, then bridge requirements).
- Check that nothing in tests/contract/ restricts `commands[].action` to a fixed list; at 7fb0a2c `action` is a free `String` on `CommandHint` (src/error.rs:405-410) and the contract checks only its type, so `search` is accepted.
- README's action list (Fields table, and the `install` section's "(action `install`)") will be updated separately to name `search`; this bead does not edit README.md.

## Acceptance Criteria

- No `commands` entry has action `install` unless its argv runs `omaddons install`.
- A bridge requirement that nothing resolves yields a hint with action `search` and argv `omaddons search <folder>`.
- Resolvable bridge requirements and unresolved candidates keep action `install`.
- `argc gate` passes.

## Test Plan

- E2E (tests/deps.rs or tests/contract/matrix.rs): a bridge scenario whose requirement resolves nowhere; assert the `bridge_dependency` fix is `search`, and the matching `commands` entry has action `search`.
- Contract: a general check over every envelope the matrix produces that a hint's action matches its argv verb for `install` and `search` hints.
- The existing `gh:o/plug` matrix case still runs every `install` hint successfully.

## Considerations

- Skipping the `search` hint instead of relabelling it is the alternative; relabelling is chosen because the search is the useful next step and the warning already carries it.
- The same mislabel cannot happen for unresolved candidates: those argvs are built as `install` directly.
acceptance_criteria: no commands entry has action install unless its argv runs omaddons install; an unresolvable bridge requirement yields action search with argv omaddons search <folder>; resolvable bridges and unresolved candidates keep action install; argc gate passes
close_reason: install's hints are labelled by the verb their argv runs: a bridge requirement nothing resolves gives action search
